title: v0.34.0
summary: # v0.34.0 **1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).** Thank you! ## TL;DR - **10 new models** (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!) - **Extensible KV cache is on by default:** vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now **remove `gpu_memory_utilization`** from your configs. - **Model Runner V1 is gone.** Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner. - **Big speedups** on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3). - **Upgrade check:** default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` is required. See [Before you upgrade](#before-you-upgrade). ## Before you upgrade > [!IMPORTANT] > These changes can break existing setups. | Change | What to do | PR | |---|---|---| | Model Runner V1 removed | Remove `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`; it now fails at startup. Port V1 logits processors to `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor`. | #63373 | | Default `--block-size` is 64 (was 16) | Pass `--block-size 16` to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16. | #63231 | | Extensible KV cache on by default; `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 | **In most cases it's now best to not set `gpu_memory_utilization`**. This should provide maximum kv cache capacity while avoiding runtime OOMs. Use it to share a GPU with other processes or when extensible kv cache is disabled. | #56492 | | ROCm 7.2 artifac

title: [Benchmark] Separate native and custom activation paths
summary: ## Overview Add an eager `forward_native` baseline to the activation kernel benchmark and call the CUDA implementation explicitly for the Custom OP series. This makes it possible to separate PyTorch eager, the vLLM custom operator, and `torch.compile` performance. This addresses the activation benchmark request in #19817. ## Claims - `benchmark_activation.py` now reports `PyTorch (eager)`, `Custom OP`, and `Compiled` providers. - The Custom OP series directly measures `forward_cuda` instead of depending on the active CustomOp dispatch configuration. - The benchmark documentation describes the three providers and the timing scope. ## Validation - On an NVIDIA H200 NVL with PyTorch `2.14.0+cu130`, the old path recorded 0 `_C::silu_and_mul` calls and compiled native/Triton events; the changed path recorded 289 `_C::silu_and_mul` calls. - The changed benchmark completed 486 real CUDA invocations across 9 activations, 3 dtypes, 2 representative shapes, 3 providers, and 3 repeats. All results were finite and positive. - Native and CUDA outputs matched for all 27 activation/dtype cases within dtype-appropriate tolerances. - The CLI completed successfully: `python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_activation.py --func-name silu_and_mul --dtype bfloat16` and printed all 45 shape rows with all three provider columns. - `pytest tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py::test_act_and_mul tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py::test_activation -q` — 198 passed. - `SKIP=actionlint pre-commit run --files benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_activation.py docs/benchmarking/README.md` — passed. Actionlint wa

title: [Core][PP] Admit new requests past idle empty steps, and size prefill microbatches from the backlog
summary: ## Overview Two scheduling changes for pipeline parallelism with async scheduling, both active only with PP > 1 (admission also requires DP == 1). The original optimization and first implementation are by @gau-nernst (the first two commits). The later commits rework them onto the existing wait-for-output input handling, simplify them, and cut the per-step CPU cost. - **Admission:** don't let empty steps fill the batch queue and hold back newly arrived requests. - **PP microbatch cap:** split the outstanding prefill backlog into roughly `pp_size` chunks so a light prefill load fills every stage instead of crossing them one stage at a time. ## Claims MiniMax-M2.7 (FP8), PP4 × TP1 on one 4×GB200 node, prefill-only traffic (180k-token prompts: 161,984 cached prefix + 18,016 new tokens, 1 output token): - Mean TTFT at 31% of capacity: **−60%** (5.1 s → 2.06 s); −42 to −47% at 51–66%; −14 to −22% at 82–99%. - Closed loop: c=1 TTFT halves (3.25 s → 1.62 s); c=2 throughput 0.31 → 0.97 req/s. - Saturated throughput unchanged (~0.98–1.0 req/s); p90 near capacity about equal. - No decode regression (2k in / 256 out); decode throughput at c=4/c=16 is 13–18% higher with the cap. - No behaviour change without PP. ## Validation ### Unit tests Run on `9ff0cd87561` (this branch's head), CPU only: ``` pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_batch_queue_pp_admission.py tests/v1/engine/test_inputs_during_step.py 361 passed, 18 warnings in 68.18s ``` New/changed tests (`-k "pp_microbatch or decode_awaiting or admission or stop_on_add"`

title: [Bugfix] Reject unsupported feature strides in rotary_embedding
summary: ## Overview Reject query/key tensors with a non-unit last-dimension stride in `rotary_embedding` before launching the CUDA kernel. These views previously produced incorrect results silently. Fixes #67401. ## Claims - Validate query and optional key independently before either tensor can be modified. - Preserve support for row/head padding with unit feature stride. - Add six regression cases covering transposed 2D and feature-strided 3D views, including query-only calls and a valid query with an invalid key. ## Validation RTX 3090, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu126, CUDA toolkit 12.8, GCC 13.4. title: [Bugfix][GLM] Preserve kpool history at unaligned prefill boundaries
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fix GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer cache writes when a prefill chunk starts inside a pool. Recover missing members from the request's existing tail before reseeding it. Fixes #63168. ## Claims - Write complete pools at all chunk-start residues, including chunks shorter than a pool and a request following another prefill in the batch. - Preserve the existing compression, Hadamard/FP8 quantization, cache layout, scheduler and decode writers. - Share the strided gather between CUDA/ROCm and register compile-only startup warmup; metadata offset views do not add a new runtime-JIT variant. ## Validation [Public evidence bundle](https://gist.github.com/Loken-Lau/520b35aa7201bd528e1f6da7752820a1): reproduction scripts, original/fixed logs, benchmark samples, controlled output diagnostics and profiler traces. The source patch contains seven files; experimental sorting/forcing hooks are outside the patch. **2026-11-08 refresh:** rebased to main `7a90549f7e1e40a6fd61854812bdd90b5dc290f1`, head `752502497352692127403de62aded539ca7ddc5b`. title: [Core][PP] Chunk a lone long prefill under pipeline parallelism
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `long_prefill_token_threshold` is not applied when only one request is eligible (#57951): there is nobody to starve, so the lone prompt may use the whole budget. With pipeline parallelism that is the wrong trade-off: the lone prompt crosses every stage as one chunk, so its TTFT is the sum of all stages, and the later stages idle while the first one works. This PR keeps applying the threshold to a lone prefill when `pipeline_parallel_size > 1`. The chunks of that prompt then overlap across the stages. With `long_prefill_token_threshold_adaptive`, the fair-share floor (the whole budget for one request) is skipped in that case as well, otherwise it would undo the cap. Requests whose multimodal items must not be split (`disable_chunked_mm_input`) keep the old behavior: a cap smaller than such an item would end every chunk inside it, and the encoder check would roll the chunk back to zero forever. No new option: behavior only changes with PP **and** `long_prefill_token_threshold > 0`, i.e. when the user already asked for chunks of that size; `long_prefill_token_threshold=0` still turns the cap off. Related: #57951, #58459. ## Claims MI355X, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (Quark MXFP4), prefill-only engine, agentic prefill load (100k cached prefix + ~10k new tokens, 1 output token), `--long-prefill-token-threshold 4096`, before / after this change: | P layout | metric | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | 2 x (PP2 x TP1), 4 GPUs | TTFT p50 at 0.5 / 1 / 2 req/s | 478 / 480 / 483 ms | 417 / 352 / 391 ms | | 2 x (PP2 x TP1) | TTFT p50 at 3-7 req/s | |

title: [KV Connector][UMBP] Support pipeline-parallel prefill producers
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `UMBPStoreConnector` raises `NotImplementedError` for `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` in every mode. This PR lets a pipeline-parallel engine (e.g. a PP prefill producer in a P/D deployment) use UMBP in **standalone** mode: all PP stages agree on one key namespace, and the scheduler accepts handshake metadata from every stage. Embedded mode keeps rejecting PP. A layout where some stage holds no layers of a cache group (vLLM projects such groups to empty ones under PP, e.g. an indexer group only on the last stage) is not supported yet: saving, restoring and key lookup all assume every stage holds every group. Workers now refuse it at startup with a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of failing on the first save; only groups UMBP actually stores (`prefix_cacheable_group_ids`) count, so scratch or non-cacheable groups do not block startup. MiniMax-M3.1 is not affected: with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` it has one cache group, held by every stage (measured: PP0 60 layers, PP1 65 incl. the DSpark draft layers). Whether a group's KV is identical on every TP rank (and can be stored once) is now decided from the group's global specs (`group.distinct_specs`, kept through the PP projection), not from the layers one stage happens to hold. Otherwise a group with only replicated layers on PP0 and only sharded layers on PP1 made the stages report different replicated groups, and the scheduler handshake failed. With `MultiConnector(MoRIIO, UMBP)` no MoRIIO change is needed on current main: #67174 hands each sub-connector only its own handshake

title: [KV Connector][MoRIIO] Prefer the LBHNC KV cache layout for non-MLA models
summary: ## Overview `MoRIIOConnector` now asks for the `LBHNC` KV cache layout (head-major blocks) on non-MLA models, as `NixlConnector` does. Without it, heterogeneous-TP WRITE transfers of an all-sparse-attention model (MiniMax-M3.1) fill the RDMA send queue and the decode request never gets its KV. ## Claims - On non-MLA models, `get_kv_connector_cache_layout()` returns `LBHNC` with MoRIIO (it returned `None`). MLA models are unchanged (`None`). - Fixes `SQ full (batch): depth=32767` write failures and the resulting stuck `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests for MiniMax-M3.1 1P1D (prefill TP4 → decode TP1) with long prompts. ## Validation Unit test (`tests/distributed/test_kvlayout.py`, real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig`/`KVTransferConfig`, CPU device): ``` # base (bde6bff65) E AssertionError: assert None == 'LBHNC' FAILED tests/distributed/test_kvlayout.py::test_get_kv_connector_cache_layout_with_moriio_connector 1 failed, 4 passed # this PR 5 passed ``` End to end, MI355X, MiniMax-M3.1 1P1D (prefill PP2×TP4, decode DP8×TP1 + EP8, MoRIIO WRITE), AgentX traces with prompts up to 256k tokens, concurrency 48: | KV layout | Result | |---|---| | default (LBNHC, picked by the sparse attention backend) | `SQ full` on prompts of a few ten thousand tokens; those requests never finish | | `LBHNC` (set with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC` on P and D) | 1 h run with no transfer error | The rows above forced the layout with the environment variable. A rerun with this change and **no** `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` (same deployment, same nodes) shows the connector's choice taking effect, against LBNHC force

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Fix heterogeneous-TP WRITE of NVFP4 KV pages and replicated indexer caches
summary: ## Overview MoRIIO's heterogeneous-TP WRITE (prefill TP != decode TP) cannot serve MiniMax-M3 today, for two independent reasons. This PR fixes both: 1. **NVFP4 KV pages** (`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on ROCm): the WRITE cuts the page into per-head slots as if each KV head's bytes were contiguous, but the ROCm page stores all heads' FP4 data before all heads' block scales on each K/V side. A decode instance with a smaller TP than prefill (e.g. TP4 -> TP1) receives scrambled KV and generates garbage. This PR slices those pages by their real layout, and refuses any other packed NVFP4 page instead of mis-slicing it. 2. **Replicated indexer key cache**: MiniMax-M3's lightning-indexer keys live in an MLA-type cache (one vector per token, identical on every TP rank) inside a GQA model. The per-layer WRITE mapping sizes it by the model's KV heads, so with prefill TP > decode TP (and fewer prefill ranks than KV heads, e.g. TP4 -> TP2) it tries to slice it by head and every request fails with `MoRIIOError: Heterogeneous-TP WRITE of layer ...indexer... needs a KV head layout on both sides`. This PR maps such a layer like an MLA latent: copied whole, by one prefill rank per decode rank on fan-in and to every decode rank on fan-out. ## Claims - Prefill TP != decode TP over MoRIIO WRITE with an NVFP4 KV cache on ROCm (MiniMax-M3) now lands every KV byte where the decode kernels read it; before, the decoder output was garbage. - A packed NVFP4 page MoRIIO cannot slice (e.g. laid out by KV head, `kv_head_major_slots=True`) now fails with a clear `ValueError` instead of silently writing the w

title: [Bugfix][Multiproc] Fail fast when a worker hits a fatal RPC failure
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview When a worker fails an RPC that already fails the engine, the worker now exits. The executor's existing worker monitor then shuts down the other ranks, instead of leaving them blocked in a collective with the failed one. Fixes #60928. #61558 (@olivierzach) builds on this PR to cover workers on other nodes. ## Claims - A rank that fails a step no longer runs later steps. Before, a rank that doesn't send the reply logged the error and took the next RPC, so its collectives could pair with its peers' collectives from the previous step (#60928). - A fatal RPC failure on any rank now fails the engine within seconds. Before, a failed startup RPC hung forever, because those RPCs have no timeout. A failed step RPC waited up to `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s by default). - A rank that replies flushes its FAILURE reply before it exits, so the engine can still report the root cause. - Recoverable RPC failures keep the current behavior: the failure is only returned to the caller. An example is loading an invalid LoRA adapter. `--enable-fault-tolerance` also keeps the current behavior. ## Validation CPU unit tests: ```bash pytest tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor_fail_fast.py \ tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py \ tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor_timeout.py ``` - 26 passed with this branch merged into current main (`bf39457294`). - `test_multiproc_executor_fail_fast.py` runs the real failure path in a forked worker that has a real `MessageQueue`. It covers sync and async scheduling, and ranks that do and do

title: [ROCm][PP] MoRI-IO pipeline-parallel transport backend
summary: ## Purpose Add `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=mori_io`: a pipeline-parallel transport backend for ROCm, in the `vllm/distributed/pp_transport` framework (#65896, #66677, #65658), that hands a stage's intermediate tensors to the next stage with MoRI-IO writes into receive slots pre-registered on the next stage. On MI355X, the RCCL hand-off is costly on PP prefill instances: - PP2×DEP2: RCCL costs 16% throughput at TTFT-p50 = 2 s compared with MoRI-IO. - PP4: RCCL collapses to 2.3 req/s, against 7.78 req/s with MoRI-IO. The ROCm SDMA copy-engine path (#65658, now `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=copy_engine` on gfx950) solves this on one node. This backend complements it: - **Coexistence with MoRI EP AsyncLL.** The SDMA hand-off and MoRI EP AsyncLL both use SDMA engines. On PP2×DEP2 with MoRI EPv2 AsyncLL + DBO, the SDMA hand-off saturated at 4.45 req/s, against 7.89 req/s with MoRI-IO (see Test Result). The suspected cause, not proven, is that the SDMA hand-off and AsyncLL both use the SDMA engines. - **Multi-node PP stages.** A chain that spans nodes uses MoRI's RDMA backend. This path is experimental and not yet validated (see Test Plan). - **Independent of the copy-engine feature set.** It needs neither gfx950 nor particular free SDMA engines. It is opt-in only. `auto` never selects it, and nothing changes when it is not selected. **Not a duplicate:** no open PR adds a MoRI-IO PP transport. Searched with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "mori pp transport"` / `"MoRI-IO pipeline parallel"`. #64693 is about PP for the MoRI-IO *KV connector* (prefill instance KV layout), not the stage ha

title: [Bugfix] Save sharded state before weight post-processing
summary: ## Overview Fixes #67416. Adds `--save-sharded-state-path` so that each worker saves its shard right after `load_weights()`, before weight post-processing. A `load_format=sharded_state` reload then rebuilds the same checkpoint layout and post-processes it once, the same way as a normal load. The offline example now uses this option. This replaces #51496, which takes the same approach but is stale, conflicts with main, and breaks tied word embeddings (details below). ## Claims - Sharded checkpoints now round-trip for models whose post-processing repacks weights (FP8 via Marlin, FusedMoE layouts, ...). On current main the reload fails with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (...) must match the size of tensor b (...)`. - Tied word embeddings round-trip: the save happens after `maybe_retie_word_embeddings`. - Online quantization is rejected, since its weights are not final before post-processing. Speculative draft models are not saved. ## Validation 8x A100-80GB (sm80; FP8 runs through Marlin, whose post-processing repacks weights). title: [Kernel][MoE] Run Kimi-K3.1 SiTU routed experts in SM90 DeepGEMM Mega MoE
summary: ## Overview `MEGA_MOE_MXFP4_SM90` advertised only SwiGLU, so `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on Hopper rejected Kimi K3.1's SiTU activation while constructing the experts: ``` NotImplementedError: DeepGEMM MegaMoE mxfp4 experts support ['swiglu'], not 'situ'. ``` SM100's `MEGA_MOE_MXFP4` already accepts `situ`, and the only thing that makes the SM90 variant distinct is its hidden-state staging (FP8 with one FP32 scale per 128, versus SM100's packed per-32 UE8M0). That staging is a property of the dispatch path and is independent of the L1 epilogue activation. Accept SiTU there too. The second half of this change is a capability probe. SM90 SiTU support lives in the DeepGEMM kernel, not in vLLM, so simply widening the frozenset would move the failure downstream: an installed DeepGEMM without the SM90 SiTU branch rejects it in its C++ host code (`DG_HOST_ASSERT(activation != "situ")`), which surfaces as an opaque launch error. `deep_gemm_supports_sm90_situ()` probes for the `situ_beta` parameter that [DeepGEMM#62](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/62) adds to `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, following the same signature-probing pattern this file already uses in `_kernel_fuses_shared_experts`. The probe is false on the DeepGEMM revision pinned in `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` today, so construction raises a clear `NotImplementedError` naming the missing kernel. **This PR does not change behavior on the current pin**; it takes effect once DeepGEMM#62 is merged and the pin is bumped. Depends on: https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/62 ## Not duplicating exi

title: Triton backend rejects fp8_per_token_head KV cache on SM 8.x: the guard is one dtype predicate too wide
summary: Two items from running vLLM 0.33 with quantized KV caches on an RTX 3090 (`sm_86`) under Windows. They are independent; the first comes with a patch, the second is a question. ## 1. `fp8_per_token_head` KV cache cannot start on SM 8.x **File:** `vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py:517` on `main` (525 in 0.33), `TritonAttentionImpl.__init__`. ```python if self.kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8") and not ( current_platform.has_device_capability(89) ): suggested = ( "float16" if (cap is None or cap.to_int() < 80) else "bfloat16" ) raise ValueError( f"FP8 KV cache is not supported by the Triton attention backend " ``` With `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype fp8_per_token_head` on a 3090 this raises at startup, before any weight is loaded. **Why the guard does not apply to this dtype.** The guard protects the native `fp8e4nv` path, where the kernel performs the scaled dot product in fp8 and therefore needs SM89 tensor-core support. `fp8_per_token_head` is not that: the cache is stored as `torch.uint8`, viewed as `float8_e4m3fn`, and dequantized inside the Triton kernel with an explicit per-head, per-token scale — the same arithmetic `int8_per_token_head` already uses, and which already runs on the same card through the same backend. The condition is one dtype predicate too wide. **Suggested change:** ```python if ( self.kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8") and not self.kv_cache_dtype.endswith("per_token_head") and not (current_platform.has_device_capability(89)) ): ``` **What it buys, stated honestly:** nothing in speed. title: [CI][ROCm] Match the AMD steps to the mirror declarations they carry
summary: Fixes [#57956](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57956). `mirror.amd` blocks in `.buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml` declare, per suite, the label tier it carries in the AMD pipeline and the device class it runs on; `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` carries the steps, their `mirror_hardwares` selector tags and their `agent_pool`. title: [Core] Persistent state: model hooks for CUDA graph capture, warmup, shutdown and memory contributors
summary: ## Overview This PR gives a persistent-state model control over its own startup and shutdown ([RFC #65543](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65543)). A model can allocate execution memory that the KV cache budget counts, capture its own CUDA graphs over its state pools, run work after warmup, release resources at shutdown, and name the options that drive its memory use when memory runs out. **Depends on [#67375](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67375)**, which depends on [#67374](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67374). This branch is stacked on both, so the diff also shows their commits. Review only the last two commits: `[Doc]` and `[Core]`. This is the third of three PRs that split [#65544](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65544): #67374 adds the state lifetime, #67375 adds admission and the `AsyncLLM` integration, and this PR adds the model hooks. Models without persistent state keep their current behavior: every hook defaults to a no-op, and the capture predicate defaults to `False`. ## Claims - `ModelState` gains six hooks: `needs_cudagraph_capture` (default `False`), `capture_cudagraphs`, `clear_cudagraphs`, `prepare_execution_memory`, `post_warmup` and `shutdown` (each a no-op by default). - **Execution memory.** The GPU worker calls `prepare_execution_memory` once, inside the memory-profiling window, so what the model allocates there is subtracted from the KV cache budget. - **Model-state graph capture.** When the model state's predicate returns `True`, `capture_model` calls `capture_cudagraphs` after the decoder, encoder and sp

title: [rust][server] Add generative scoring route

title: [Core] Persistent state: state pool, scheduling and release fence
summary: ## Overview This PR adds the lifetime of persistent state ([RFC #65543](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65543)): a fixed pool of per-request state slots on the GPU, scheduling that binds one slot to a request across steps and across the inputs of a streaming-input request, and a release fence that returns a slot to the pool only after the worker has finished every write to it. It is the first of three PRs that split [#65544](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65544). #67375 adds stream admission and the `AsyncLLM` integration on top of this one. #67583 adds model hooks for CUDA graph capture and memory contributors. A search of open PRs for `65543` in the body and for "persistent state" in the title returns only #65544, so this PR does not duplicate other open work. title: [Perf][Kernel] Tune the SM80 FP32-state tile for packed GDN decode
summary: ## Summary On SM80, the packed GDN decode path still uses the default BV=32. With FP32 recurrent state, we observed the largest gains at small batch sizes. This PR picks BV=8 for SM80, FP32 state, and K=V=128, keeping 1 warp and 3 stages. Other architectures, state dtypes, and head dimensions keep the existing dispatch. This is in the same spirit as the SM90/SM100 tuning in #61355 and #63864. title: [Bugfix][RL] Fail a weight update without taking the engine down
summary: ## Purpose A weight-update session (`start_weight_update` → `update_weights` × N → `finish_weight_update`) has two ways to end without completing, and today both leave the engine dead rather than just failing the request. They are fixed together here because they meet at the same point in the worker: the code that drops a session that will not finish. ### 1. The weights are asleep Sleep mode unmaps the weight allocations (level 1 offloads them to host memory, level 2 discards the parameters), and nothing checked that they were mapped again before a weight update wrote into them. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `_qsa_mqa_paged_kernel` scores every row against the full page-table width (max_model_len / 4 = 65,600 columns), regardless of how many are visible. For decode with one query row per request (no MTP, no prefill) the 16-row tile is mostly padding. At 262K context with one row it took 9.4 us against 6.3 us for the old one-row kernel (scoring kernel only). On gfx942, batches of at most 32 such rows now use the old one-row kernel plus the same skip of invisible column blocks. ## Dispatch `qsa_mqa_paged(..., single_row_decode=True)` uses the one-row kernel when all of these hold: - the caller sets `single_row_decode`. `QSAIndexer._select` sets it from `QSAForwardMetadata`: `num_prefills == 0 and decode_query_len == 1`. The crossover against the tiled kernel on MI325X is about 32 rows at 32K to 98K context. - the platform is gfx942 (`get_cdna_version() == 3`). title: [Core][Spec Decode] Give the DFlash/DSpark drafter's KV its own block pool
summary: ## Purpose **Stacked on #64109 (DFlash/DSpark drafter KV backs only its tail) and #64628 (`--max-num-inflight-kv-loads`)**, and builds on #63416 (NIXL pairs KV regions by layer, now merged). The branch merges #64109 and #64628; the rest of the diff is this PR. This PR adds `--draft-kv-pool`, which gives a DFlash or DSpark drafter's sliding-window KV its own block pool. With the hybrid KV cache manager every group draws from one pool, and every block is as large as the widest group's. A drafter group of a few sliding-window layers therefore pays a target-sized block for each of its blocks. RFC #59117 measures what this costs on a GDN target with a 5-layer DFlash drafter: 3-11x less KV capacity. In its own pool, a drafter block is as large as the drafter's layers. The pool is sized for the window each request keeps under #64109. ## Changes **Config:** `--draft-kv-pool` and `--draft-kv-pool-cache-fraction` (default 0.5). **Planning** (`kv_cache_planning.py`): - `get_global_kv_cache_groups` groups the drafter's `DFlashSlidingWindowSpec` layers on their own, in pool 1 (`KVCacheGroupSpec.pool_id`). - The pool holds the null block plus `(max_num_seqs + max_num_inflight_kv_loads) × (1 + cache_fraction)` requests at their admission cap. An async KV load holds drafter blocks without counting toward `max_num_seqs`, and #64628 caps those loads, so this bounds every request that holds drafter blocks. A KV consumer with the pool must therefore set `--max-num-inflight-kv-loads`; startup fails without it. The pool is sized from the specs alone, so every worker and the scheduler agree on it

title: [Feature][Core] Size prefill chunks from a step-time budget.

title: [Bug]: With TP>1, `vllm:num_requests_waiting` briefly includes requests the scheduler hasn't seen yet (since #65466)
summary: ### Your current environment Not the full `collect_env.py` output: the behavior follows from the engine-core code path described below and does not depend on the hardware. We can add it if needed. - vLLM v0.34.0, official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.34.0` image (amd64) - 4x NVIDIA A100, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` (multiprocessing executor) - `--max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MTP speculative decoding (3 tokens) - Before the upgrade: nightly build `0.32.1rc1.dev36+ge68efc685` (does not contain #65466) ### 🐛 Describe the bug After upgrading to v0.34.0, our gateway started throttling clients on a server that was mostly idle. We traced it to a side effect of #65466 on the waiting gauge: with TP>1, a request that arrives while a step is running is counted in `vllm:num_requests_waiting` (as `reason="capacity"`) at the end of that step, before any scheduling pass has looked at it. title: [RFC] feat(scheduler): implement Shortest Remaining Prefill First (SRPF) policy with starvation aging
summary: ### Summary Implements Shortest Remaining Prefill First (SRPF) scheduling with dynamic starvation aging in the v1 engine core. In mixed workloads, heavy prompt ingestion (e.g. multi-turn context or RAG prompts with 7k+ tokens) causes head-of-line (HoL) blocking under FCFS: long prefills are chunked across consecutive iterations, forcing short interactive requests arriving behind them to queue for seconds. SRPF reorders the `running` and `waiting` queues by remaining prefill work (`num_prompt_tokens - num_computed_tokens`), while an aging clock tracks scheduler ticks since each request was last scheduled. When a request exceeds `VLLM_SRPF_STARVATION_THRESHOLD`, it is temporarily elevated ahead of non-starved requests to guarantee compute progression, preventing starvation. --- ### Mechanics - **Activation**: Gated by `VLLM_ENABLE_SRPF=1` under `SchedulingPolicy.FCFS`. - **Sort Key**: `(not is_starved, remaining_prefill, arrival_time)`. - **Aging & Cadence**: - `srpf_starvation_clock` increments on unpaused scheduler steps. - A request is considered starved when `starvation_ticks > VLLM_SRPF_STARVATION_THRESHOLD` (default `3`). - Upon receiving a prefill chunk, `last_scheduled_clock` updates and `frozen_starvation_clock` resets to 0. - Slicing behavior: a tight threshold (`3`) enforces frequent round-robin interleaving between heavy prefill chunks and incoming short bursts, keeping short request queue wait times low without stalling long completions. --- ### Benchmark Results (Independent Hardware Sweep) Evaluated by @lkhun9311 on a dedicated AWS A10G instance with seeded ran

title: [Bugfix][Compile] Preserve control dependencies during defunctionalization
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #56041. `FixFunctionalizationPass` rewrites `getitem` users before removing an `auto_functionalized` node. A `control_deps` ordering edge can still reference that node, causing FX to abort compilation when removing it. Redirect the ordering edge to the replacement operation and its mutated arguments, preserving unrelated dependencies. The buffer dependencies retain scheduling constraints for operators returning `None`; flattening the dependency sequence also makes them visible to PyTorch 2.12 lowering. Extend the existing functionalization suite with returned-tensor and mutation-only regressions. Inputs follow the current platform so the tests run on CPU and CUDA. GPU fusion imports move into their existing GPU test to allow CPU collection. Before modifying a wrapper, retain it if a user cannot be rewritten: this includes returning the whole wrapper or passing it as a `control_deps` data argument. Supported dependency-list users still take the optimized path. The full-pass regression covers these boundaries, multiple control users, and mixed graphs where ordinary wrappers should still be optimized. The fallback is computed before graph edits and propagated through data descendants, including views and successive consumers. This prevents downstream reinplacing from overwriting retained outputs. Pure scheduling dependencies do not propagate protection. summary: ## Overview On SM90+, four Triton kernels on the decode path still use ordinary launches, so each one starts about 0.45 us after its predecessor finishes, even inside a CUDA graph: the Qwen GDN packed recurrent decode (`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`), the Qwen3.5 gated RMS norm (`fused_gdn_gated_rms_norm`), the attention output gate (`fused_sigmoid_gate_mul`) and the Triton fused-MoE expert GEMM (`fused_moe_kernel`, two launches per MoE layer). This PR launches them with programmatic dependent launch (PDL), the same way `causal_conv1d_update` and the LoRA Triton ops already do: `launch_pdl=current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()` at the launch and `gdc_wait()` before the first load. The kernels do not trigger their dependents early (no `gdc_launch_dependents()`): the trigger happens implicitly when the grid completes, which hides the launch latency without letting the next grid take SM slots while this one is still running. Off SM90, and on other platforms, `launch_pdl` is False and the code is unchanged. PDL changes no math: every kernel still waits for its predecessor to complete and flush before it reads, so outputs are bitwise identical. ## Claims - **`Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, H200 TP1:** median TPOT −3.2% at concurrency 1 (3.890 → 3.765 ms) and −1.1% at concurrency 8; output throughput +3.3% and +1.3%. At concurrency 32 TPOT is within the main run-to-run spread (+0.4%, throughput +0.9%). - **`Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` (dense, no MoE):** median TPOT −0.5% / −0.4% / −0.6% at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. title: [Core][Feature] Add opt-in per-request prefix-cache miss attribution
summary: ## Overview Implements the opt-in per-request prefix-cache miss attribution proposed in #60044. vLLM now reports what it **observed** for the first block after the longest prefix-cache hit (`evicted` / `no_match` / `lookup_limit`), plus the names of extra hash keys. Disabled by default. Related: #60044 (open feature request), #43711 (lower-level debug event at the same lookup point; closed for inactivity, no implementation). ## Claims - Distinguishes a recently evicted block from a genuine no-match, and from the intentional lookup cap used to recompute the last prompt token for logits. - Reports only extra-key **kinds** (`cache_salt`, `lora`, `mm`, `prompt_embeds`), never values, so salts, adapter paths and multimodal identifiers cannot leak through the diagnostic. - Addresses all three acceptance cases raised in the issue discussion: identical tokens with a different `cache_salt`, the 16/17/32/33-token lookup-cap controls, and the maintainer's "how can vLLM know the cause?" objection (labels state observations, not inferred causes). - Off by default: no history is allocated and no attribution is computed. title: [Bugfix][Core] Refuse /resume while the engine is asleep
summary: ## Overview `POST /resume` while the engine is asleep (`POST /sleep?level=1`, before `/wake_up`) currently returns `{"status": "resumed"}`, and the next request then executes a step against offloaded (CPU) model memory. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix TRITON_MLA NaN logits under CUDA graphs at batch>=3
summary: ## Summary Fixes #57017 DeepSeek-V2-Lite with online FP8 on sm_89 GPUs returned NaN logits once ≥3 sequences decoded in one CUDA-graph batch. Eager mode and `cudagraph_mode=NONE` were unaffected. ### Root Cause The MLA split-KV decode logits scratch (`Att_Out` in `triton_mla.forward_mqa`, shape `[B, q_num_heads, num_kv_splits, kv_lora_rank+1]`) was served from the shared `WorkspaceManager` scratch pool via `get_simultaneous`, which returns **offset-0 slices that alias across MLA layers and other scratch users**. Under CUDA-graph replay at the size-4+ capture bucket (default `cudagraph_capture_sizes=[1,2,4,8,...]` → 3 sequences pad to size-4), this created a **read-after-write hazard** that corrupted `attn_logits` → NaN attention output → NaN logits. The online-FP8 MoE per-tensor dynamic scale then propagates one row's NaN to every request in the batch. ### Fix Replace the shared `get_simultaneous` workspace acquisition with a **persistent per-impl `_attn_logits_buf`** (helper method `_get_attn_logits`): - Sized to the worst case (`max_num_seqs × max_decode_query_len × num_heads × max_splits × (kv_lora_rank+1)`) at first use, so it never grows under CUDA-graph capture. - Each `TritonMLAImpl` instance (per MLA layer) owns its own buffer — no aliasing across layers. - Sliced per call to the actual needed shape. - Falls back to per-call `torch.empty` when no full `VllmConfig`/`num_heads` is present (unit-test stubs built via `object.__new__`). Memory footprint: same order as the working `torch.empty` fallback (`num_layers × max_workspace`), not a regression. ### Relationship to

title: [ROCm][CI] Enable AITER on for Qwen3-8-Flash-Next-FP8 Accuracy Eval
summary: ## Overview With AITER on, the Qwen3-8-Flash-Next-FP8 Accuracy Eval (tests/evals/qwen4_exp/test_accuracy.py) will fail: 1. AITER FP8 MoE kernel supports only (128, 128) quantization block size. Since TP=4, the size for each rank is 640/4=160, not a multiple of 128, so padding is needed. But: I) padding is not equal for all 4 ranks (pad=0, 0, 128, 256, respectively); II) pad value is set to 0 and scale to 1; so AITER MoE kernel could treat padding as real value, and I just explicitly set intermediate_pad = 0; 2. AITER custom all-reduce doesn't supports FP8 dtype but the selection logic didn't check this when selecting all-reduce kernels. title: [Refactor][KV Cache] Remove EAGLE block dropping and default to lookahead hashes
summary: ## Purpose Lookahead block hashes are now used by core prefix caching and by every hash-keyed in-tree KV connector. With them, an EAGLE, EAGLE3 or MTP prefix hit already proves that the draft KV at the block boundary is reusable. The legacy approach drops the last matched block and compensates for it everywhere else. It is no longer needed, so this PR removes the drop and makes lookahead hashes the only behavior. #65448 (merged) enabled lookahead hashes for the remaining in-tree connectors. `supports_lookahead_block_hashes` now only marks connectors whose external hits ignore hash lookahead: Example, HF3FS, LMCache and FlexKV match by token IDs and report False. Core keeps lookahead hashes for them, and vLLM logs that spec decode acceptance may drop. More details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FaPogNcsjkYNgUORg1Scctj-9RDx7NTV3ZG6Gv84UdY/edit?tab=t.0 ## Implementation The drop changed what a hit length means. Every piece of code that predicts where a later request will hit therefore had to compensate: - lookup, with proof margins and convergence guards; - registration, with an extra proof block and wider SWA retention; - Mamba checkpoints, which back off one block; - a draft-group tagging chain; - and a copy of these rules in each connector. Lookahead puts the next L tokens into each block's hash, so a matched block already proves the boundary. With that, all of these compensations go away. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Serialize batch queue for spec decode + PP
summary: ## Overview With speculative decoding + pipeline parallelism + async scheduling disabled, the PP batch queue schedules step N+1 before step N's output is processed; the plain scheduler lacks the overlap compensation AsyncScheduler has, so the worker asserts (`num_scheduled_tokens_np >= num_logits`) and the PP0 worker dies mid-step (PP1+ hang in NCCL irecv). title: [KV Connector][NIXL][Mooncake] Report completed KV loads before the next model output
summary: ## Overview Report completed KV loads before the next model output, so the engine can schedule the request sooner. Set `"enable_early_recv": true` in `--kv-transfer-config` on the engine that loads KV (a NIXL decoder, or a Mooncake Store consumer); disabled by default. ## Claims Supports `uni` and single-node `mp`, TP, sync/async scheduling, with NixlConnector (pull) or MooncakeStoreConnector, directly or inside MultiConnector. NIXL pull requires PP=1; Mooncake Store also works with PP>1 (Mooncake Store support is from xsxszab). Existing threads do the polling. Successful loads share the normal all-worker quorum. A load with an error on any rank (a failure, or Mooncake Store invalid blocks) completes through step outputs, after the output that carries the error. NIXL early reporting is now restricted to direct receives with matching block sizes and physical block layouts, without permutation, heterogeneous-attention conversion, padding zeroing, or host-buffer staging. Other receives remain entirely on the ordinary step path, even when early receive is enabled. ## Validation **2026-11-10 correctness scope reduction:** addresses apex-mochen's review by excluding heterogeneous-block/post-processing receives from early reporting. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Break the online acceptance estimator's separation feedback loop with a circuit breaker
summary: ## Overview Follow-up to #52228 (added the online acceptance estimator for adaptive verification) and complementary to #65229 (fixes catastrophic cancellation in the estimator's *feature* computation, merged separately). This fixes a different failure in the same estimator: once a draft position's own Fisher information collapses toward zero under separation, its refit has no way to recognize that and keeps taking increasingly large, wrong-direction Newton steps forever. ## Claims - Fixes unbounded coefficient divergence in `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator`'s refit, caused by **separation** in the online logistic regression (Albert & Anderson, 1984): once a draft position's samples within a refit window become (quasi-)perfectly predictable, its own Fisher information collapses to exactly `0.0`, despite a real, substantial sample count — and the resulting Newton step divides a non-vanishing gradient by a near-zero denominator. - Adds a floor + clip safety net (Levenberg-Marquardt-style damping) so a single refit can't take an arbitrarily large step, plus a **circuit breaker**: track, per position and separately for the shared slope, how many *consecutive* refits its raw (pre-floor) Fisher information has sat below a small threshold; after 3 consecutive such refits, discard the computed step and reset that one coefficient to its own existing cold-start default instead. - Reproduced with a **fully public, dataset-free** repro (three generic prompts asking for a long, maximally repetitive completion — no internal data, no benchmark dependency): unpatched, the intercept reaches **-107

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Do not schedule ahead of an uncapped lone prefill chunk
summary: ## Overview Fixes #60476. Since #57951 a lone long prefill runs uncapped chunks of `max_num_batched_tokens`, and with async scheduling (or `max_concurrent_batches > 1`) the next chunk is scheduled while the current one is still executing. A request that arrives mid-prefill therefore sits through up to two full uncapped steps before `long_prefill_token_threshold` can engage again. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Pack the decode sparse-MLA ragged top-k in one launch from the MXFP4 indexer's row bounds
summary: ## Overview On gfx950 with the MXFP4 sparse indexer and no `--monokernel`, every DeepSeek-V4.1 index layer converts its decode top-k into the ragged form sparse MLA reads: global slot ids, indptr and lengths. Main builds it in 4 launches per index layer: a count kernel, a zero fill, a cumsum and a pack. This PR builds it in 1. Each row's length is `min(topk, row_len)`, where `row_len` is the bound the indexer's top-k already ran over, so the count and the scan are not needed. Over the 8 index layers this removes 24 of the 32 launches per decode step, with identical output. It runs on the layouts that decode without `--monokernel`: DEP8 (C128 and up), 2x TP4+EP4 (C64), and TP2 steps of more than 48 rows (C32). Since #66047, a TP>1 decode step of 64 or more rows narrows the indexer's `decode_row_lens` to the rank's own shard. The PR therefore keeps the whole step's bounds in `decode_step_row_lens`, set before the narrowing. Every rank's top-k rows are all-gathered before the pack runs, so the bounds of the whole step are the right ones. Part of a series that trims the DSv4.1 sparse-indexer launch overhead on MI355X, after #63888: #67363, #67364, #67366, #67367 and #67368. This PR is independent of the others. ## Performance vs main Setup: - Base: stock `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2`, AITER 0.1.29. Every file this PR touches, and the indexer ops it reads, is identical to main 2c1fc9b3d3 (this PR's base). The md5s inside the containers matched. - This PR: the same image with the PR's two Python files mounted over it. - Hardware and model: MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1

title: [Performance]: FA2 prefill uses a tile that fits one CTA/SM on 100 KB-smem GPUs (SM86/89/12x); num_splits=1 is 5-60% faster
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance For prefill batches (more tokens than the largest CUDA graph), `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` passes `max_num_splits = 0`. On FA2, the paged-KV varlen path ignores the split heuristic. The `num_splits` value only picks the kernel tile in `run_mha_fwd_splitkv_dispatch` (vllm-project/flash-attention, `flash_fwd_launch_template.h`): | head dim | `num_splits=0` (today) | `num_splits=1` ("align" path) | |---|---|---| | 64 | 64x256 tile, 72 KB smem | 64x128 tile, 40 KB smem | | 128 | 64x128 tile, 80 KB smem | 64x64 tile, 48 KB smem | | 256 | 64x64 tile, 96 KB smem | same tile | SM86, SM89 and SM12x have 100 KB of shared memory per SM. There, the `num_splits=0` tile fits **1 CTA/SM** and the `num_splits=1` tile fits **2**. On A100 (164 KB) the counts are 2 and 3, and the bigger tile still wins on long sequences. summary: ## Overview Add `--async-scheduling-depth` (`SchedulerConfig.async_scheduling_depth`, default 2): how many steps Model Runner V2 keeps in flight with async scheduling. title: [Bugfix][CPU] Stop VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE from overriding kv_cache_memory_bytes
summary: Fixes #67033 The legacy `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` env var applied any non-empty value, including `0` and negative values, and silently replaced an explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`: 1. `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=0` produced a 0-byte KV cache and startup failed with `ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks`, although the docs say 0 means vLLM does not override the KV cache size through this variable. 2. With `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1` and `kv_cache_memory_bytes=50_000_000`, the engine silently used 1 GiB instead of the explicit 50 MB. Now the env var is applied only when it holds a positive size and no explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes` was given: - a positive value without explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` sets the KV cache size (unchanged behavior); - `0` (the documented default) and an unset or empty variable leave automatic sizing in place, silently; - a negative value is ignored with a warning; - an explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` always takes precedence, with a warning that the env var was ignored. **Test plan**: run on `c4f1f36b71` (macOS, CPU platform), `pytest tests/platforms/test_cpu.py tests/models/language/generation/test_cpu_kv_cache_space.py` → `25 passed, 16 warnings in 18.11s`. - `tests/platforms/test_cpu.py::test_cpu_kv_cache_space_env_var` covers unset/empty/zero/negative/positive and explicit-bytes-wins, asserting the KV cache bytes and the warning text for each case. title: [Structured Outputs] Resolve special tokens when validating Lark grammars

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Insert the compressed KV cache inside the compression launch
summary: ## Overview **TL;DR (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1 decode):** the compression launch now writes the compressed-cache record itself. - At the 4 kv-source layers, the compress + insert chain drops from 8 launches to 4, and from 21.78 to 14.26 us per C1 decode step (**-34.5%**; -23% to -25% for 14-336-row graphs). - Cache bytes equal main's. - NVIDIA is unaffected: nothing on CUDA takes the fused path, unit tests pass on GB300, and the kernels compile to the same instructions. - GSM8K and RULER at 32K / 64K / 128K are unchanged on both changed paths (every McNemar p >= 0.1). - End to end, the saving is about 0.17% of a 4.30 ms C1 step. That is below the noise between serving runs, so serving ITL shows no measurable change. **Today.** On ROCm, every DeepSeek-V4.1 decode step compresses the KV at the 4 kv-source layers (L2, L8 and L14 at compress ratio 2, L20 at ratio 1). A second Triton launch, `_rope_quant_insert_kernel`, then reads the BF16 latent back and writes its 584-B fp8_ds_mla record into the paged compressed cache. **With this PR.** `fused_save_compress_norm` writes that record from the row it has just produced. Two ROCm decode call sites switch to the fused form: - the TP `--monokernel` decode (`amd/mono_decode._select`); - the CSA aux-stream chain of FULL-graph decode (`amd/rocm.py` `_forward_csa2_full`). These keep the separate insert: NVIDIA, ROCm prefill and mixed steps, PCP, and the plain-row caches. **Series.** This PR is part of a series that trims the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-indexer launch floor on MI355X, after #63888 (merged). title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep developer messages in place for templates without the role
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Follow-up to #65294, which fixed this in the Rust frontend and named the Python port as a follow-up. This PR is that port. When a chat template does not name the `developer` role, the Python HF renderer renames every developer message to `system` and merges every system message into one at position 0 (`_consolidate_system_messages`, from #43590). Codex sends its base prompt as a leading developer message and adds developer updates mid-conversation. Each update is moved ahead of all earlier turns, so the prompt changes from the system message onward on every update and prefix caching misses from there. The caller's own mid-conversation system messages move too, and non-text parts in a moved message are dropped. ## Claims - Templates that name `developer` are unchanged. - Developer messages in the leading run of system messages are merged into one `system` message, as before. Later ones stay in place: as a `system` message when the template renders a later system message (Qwen3), otherwise joined to the adjacent user turn (Qwen3.5, Llama 2, Ministral 3). The template is probed once per template (and per set of template variables) and the result cached. - The caller's own system messages are left to the template, and merged content keeps its parts (images) in order. - On the Rust test cases ported here, Python now renders the same prompts as the Rust frontend. title: [RFC]: Bounded, retryable NCCL weight updates
summary: ### Motivation. An NCCL weight update is a collective between the trainer engine (`NCCLTrainerWeightTransferEngine`, `M2NTrainerWeightTransferEngine`) and the worker engine (`NCCLWeightTransferEngine`, `M2NWeightTransferEngine`). If one side stops partway, the other blocks forever, and there is no supported way to retry. Based on `main` at `e10ef091ba`. Following are the resulting failure modes we have hit in production RL runs, with a trainer streaming weights over NCCL into a fleet of vLLM replicas. Both ended with the job torn down. **A worker dies or is preempted.** The communicator is created once at init and reused for every update, so this hurts whether it happens during an update or between two. A worker lost between updates is not noticed until the next one, when everyone else enters the broadcast and waits for a rank that is gone. A death between updates can be worked around by re-initializing the communicator at the update boundary when we see the fleet has changed. A death mid-update has no clear solution today. Either way the trainer and the surviving workers stay blocked in the collective, and from the trainer this looks like a fabric hang. With this RFC, the trainer is unblocked as soon as update_weights reports the failure, or at the deadline otherwise. The survivors abort and roll back to idle, and the trainer re-initializes against them and retries. **The update_weights RPC never reaches some workers.** They never join the broadcast, so everyone else waits for them indefinitely while health checks stay green. title: [BUG] Fix async EPLB worker shutdown ordering
summary: ## 1. Root cause The async EPLB transfer thread is started as a daemon, but has no explicit shutdown lifecycle. `Worker.shutdown()` cleans up the model runner and other resources without stopping or joining that thread. A daemon thread exits when its process exits, not when `Worker.shutdown()` returns. It can therefore remain blocked on `rearrange_event` or on a pending layer result while worker cleanup proceeds. ## 2. Fix Add `EplbState.stop_async_loop()` and call it at the beginning of `Worker.shutdown()`, before resource cleanup: 1. Drain any in-flight async EPLB results using the existing `drain_async()`. Acknowledge each result without applying its transferred weights, allowing the background thread to finish the current cycle. 2. Set a stop event and record `rearrange_event` to wake the thread. 3. Check the stop event after waking, exit instead of starting another cycle, and join the thread before continuing cleanup. Clear the stop event when starting a new async worker. If no async worker exists, stopping is a no-op. ## 3. Behavior without the fix With async EPLB enabled, calling worker shutdown does not terminate the EPLB thread. If the worker process remains alive, the thread can retain references to the EPLB state and model resources after model-runner cleanup. If shutdown happens during a rebalance, the thread can still be transferring experts or waiting for the main thread to consume a layer result. Subsequent distributed teardown can then overlap with unfinished EPLB work. Normal process exit eventually terminates the daemon thread and reclaims process resource

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reclaim resident pages before allocating the next prefill chunk
summary: ## Overview HiSparse chunked prefill can stall under GPU KV cache pressure when a request needs to transition from resident history to a hot buffer. The scheduler can reject the next chunk even though allocating the hot buffer first would let it reclaim enough resident blocks to proceed. ## Problem and reproduction Resident history stays pinned until the request has a hot buffer that can read its Host copies. The hot buffer and the next prefill chunk use the same GPU block pool. Checking their combined demand before allocating the hot buffer can defer the request indefinitely, because the resident pages remain pinned until that allocation succeeds. The reporter observed timeouts at concurrency 25. One reported allocation had about 2,800 free GPU blocks, while the hot buffer needed 1,680 blocks and the next chunk needed another 1,386 blocks for the other KV groups, including the indexer. The combined 3,066-block check failed. Allocating the hot buffer first would leave about 1,120 free blocks, so reclaiming about 266 eligible resident blocks would let the next chunk fit. ### Two-request CPU reproduction of the async KV admission issue I reproduced the reservation issue from [Matthew's review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67185#discussion_r4621436158) on `2cfdee310435`. The probe uses the real scheduler and KV block allocator. It seeds A after its first prefill chunk and simulates the external KV match and Host writeback acknowledgments. title: [ROCm][DSv41] MegaMoE improvements for DEP8
summary: ## Motivation AITER MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has scope for improvement: - **No overlap between dispatch and GEMM1.** A rank cannot tell whether more tokens will arrive for an expert, so it waits for every rank's dispatch to finish before computing. - **No overlap between GEMM1 and GEMM2.** The two run as separate stages. - **Kernel selection.** A4W4 ran generic configs that are not tuned for this shape. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reset multi-module MTP cache on slot admission (fixes #66886)
summary: ## Overview Stop `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` from re-prefilling a previous request's cached draft inputs when a request slot is reused. Fixes #66886. ## Claims - Admitting a request into a slot resets that slot's count of valid cache entries (`add_request`). - Each cache write records how many entries it wrote. The re-prefill count is clamped to that value in both the token-id kernel and the hidden-state/embedding kernel. - A reused slot can no longer feed another request's token ids or hidden states into the draft model at negative positions. ## Validation - Not run in CI yet: CI is gated on a maintainer label (`ready`/`verified`) or `/ci run`. - No tests were executed locally for this PR. The kernels are Triton kernels and have not been executed. - Reproduction: the POC in #66886 runs the speculator's Triton kernels on CPU with `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`. Before this change it prints foreign token `9005` in request B's draft input and a draft position of `-1`. - Expected after this change: no foreign token ids and no negative draft positions for request B. ## Details - **Root cause:** three things combine. (1) Slot reuse does not clear the cache, since `add_request` is the base no-op. (2) A query shorter than `S-1` tokens only rewrites the tail of the window, so head slots keep the previous occupant's entries. (3) The re-prefill reads `R = num_rejected - 1` entries without checking how many were written for the current request. - **Design:** `cached_num_valid` (int32, per request slot) is written by `_cache_inputs_kernel` as the number of entries written in the current step. title: [MRV2][Sampler] Warm up seeded native top-k/top-p without PP deadlock (#54425, #62129)
summary: ### Purpose Fixes #54425. Addresses the remaining seeded native sampling warmup gap from #54425 while aligning with #62129 to prevent pipeline parallel deadlocks. ### Problem 1. **Unwarmed Fallback Kernels (#54425)**: Under V1 with fused sampling enabled (`sampler.use_flashinfer` or `sampler.use_xpu_sampler`), `warmup_kernels()` only exercises default unseeded `SamplingParams`. Requests with an explicit `seed` bypass fused sampling (`fused_sampler_eligible` is False) and fall back to PyTorch-native top-k/top-p and Gumbel sampling. This causes JIT compilation and memory allocation latency spikes on the first seeded request. 2. **PP Rank Asymmetry (#62129)**: Under pipeline parallelism (`PP > 1`), `self.sampler` is initialized strictly on the last PP rank. Non-last ranks have `self.sampler = None`. Gating the warmup pass purely on rank-local `sampler is not None` causes non-last ranks to skip the pass while the last rank attempts to receive activations, deadlocking the engine on startup. ### Solution - **Symmetric Warmup Pass**: Add a dedicated `seeded=True` warmup pass in `warmup_kernels()` that gates on `flashinfer_sampler_supported()` / `xpu_sampler_supported()` when `sampler is None`. All PP ranks execute the same forward passes in lockstep, eliminating startup deadlocks. Unfused configurations skip this pass with zero overhead. - **Tests**: - `tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py`: Parameterized across `is_last_pp_rank: [False, True]` and `fused_backend: ["flashinfer", "xpu", None]` to assert all PP ranks stay in sync. - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`:

title: [ROCm][Muse Spark] Support EPLB with FP8 and BF16 experts
summary: ## Overview Lets Muse Spark run with `--enable-eplb` on ROCm with Triton FP8 and BF16 experts, where it currently fails at init (`Muse Spark FP8 on ROCm does not support EPLB`). This is enablement work, not a speedup: on 8× MI300X, EPLB gives +2.2–6.5% throughput at 8k–16k input and concurrency 32–64, within ±2% at lower concurrency, and 3.5–5.2% slower at 1k input. title: [RFC]: Eager-mode Sequence Parallelism (SP) with Collective+GEMM Overlap (Async-TP)
summary: ### Motivation. [#42770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42770) moves vLLM away from full-graph `torch.compile` fusion passes toward fusions expressed directly in eager/model code. [#43224](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43224) tracks the concrete porting work for that effort and leaves two explicit open questions unanswered: 1. **Sequence Parallelism (SP)** — "We should decide whether to keep an SP path at all in the manual-fusion world." 2. **Async-TP** — "Not sure if this is possible to port to manual fusion." [#60517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60517) has since removed the `torch.compile`-based SP and Async-TP passes entirely, so today there is no SP and no Async-TP in the compile-free world. This RFC proposes an eager-mode answer to both open questions: - **Yes, keep SP** — expressed as a property of the model's own forward pass, not a compiler pass. - **Yes, Async-TP is portable** — as an opportunistic behavior of the same mechanism, which degrades gracefully to plain SP when it isn't available. **RFC Draft design:** https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yKH678I3_rcm6_IQzEbbMaGOwdDPS7Ri9YGLlutP5Bs/edit?tab=t.0 ### Proposed Change. ### Why SP needs a communication/GEMM boundary TP duplicates token-wise work like norms and residual adds. SP removes that duplication by sharding tokens between boundaries, so communication changes from all-reduce to gather/scatter while keeping results the same. ### Let the model define the boundaries Instead of relying on compiler pattern matching, the model declares which spans can run on sharded tok

summary: ## Overview Move Qwen3.5 models and MTP on XPU to the eager, breakable-graph design introduced by [vLLM #51012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51012). title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode for DEP2/4/8 on B300
summary: ## Overview This PR adds **DEP-specific fused EP communication for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on B300**: routing/quantization writes directly into dispatch buffers, expert finalize publishes directly to request owners, and owner reduction fuses the local shared-expert add with mHC. TP ranks work on the same request rows; DEP ranks own different rows. This path returns each expert contribution to the request's DP owner and adds only that owner's shared-expert result. It supports DEP2/4/8 at TP1, with one GPU per DP rank. The attention/indexer, Engram prefetch and executor structure reuse #61868 and #63921. Main's TRTLLM W13/W2 GEMMs remain unchanged; the new work is the DEP data movement and fused ownership-aware boundaries around them. The diff now includes DEP2/4/8 and the EP communication fusion. The integrated DEP8 path completed full-model GSM8K: **1,180 / 1,319 (89.46%)**. The path is opt-in; choose 2, 4 or 8 with `--data-parallel-size`: ```bash --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized_dep"}' ``` It runs the target and DSpark draft through the specialized executor on FULL decode graphs with up to 128 token rows per rank. Prefill, mixed batches and larger batches keep the stock path. The default backend is unchanged. ## Claims - Reuse the specialized attention/indexer and Engram prefetch for DEP, with local mHC and fused routing/quantization before expert dispatch. - Keep main's TRTLLM W13/W2 GEMMs. Fuse dispatch-buffer writes, expert finalize/owner publication, and owner reduction + shared add + mHC. Ineligible batches keep the standard expert collectives.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Seed the fast detokenizer with a prompt tail, not the full prompt
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` seeds `DecodeStream` with the whole prompt, so each request's first output token decodes the entire prompt on the output-processing loop, stalling every other stream (17 ms at 100k tokens, ~40 ms with byte-fallback tokenizers). After its first emitted chunk `DecodeStream` keeps only the new ids, so the seed only shapes the first delta. This PR seeds it with a short prompt tail that reproduces that delta exactly: - the tail holds 5 tokens (`INITIAL_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZATION_OFFSET`) that decode to text on their own, since Metaspace, WordPiece and leading-`Strip` decoders treat the start of the text specially; - if the tail's text ends in U+FFFD (it starts inside the prompt's last character), it is extended by up to 3 tokens; if the prompt itself ends in U+FFFD, or the walk exceeds 256 tokens, the full prompt is used. No new config or env var. ## Results First output token (`FastIncrementalDetokenizer` construction + first `decode_next`), 100k-token prompt, median of 21, one core of an EPYC 9575F: | tokenizer | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (byte-level BPE) | 17.2-17.5 ms | 0.005 ms | | `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf` (byte fallback) | 39.4-41.6 ms | 0.007 ms | | `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` (served below) | 18.6-18.7 ms | 0.005 ms | Run from the repo root on each branch: ```bash python - Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 <<'EOF' import glob, statistics, sys, time from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.sampling_para

title: [CPU] Warm up the remaining sampling kernels before serving
summary: ## Purpose On CPU with Model Runner V2, one to three Triton kernels still compile inside the first requests after a server start, adding ~1.5 s to their TTFT. The penalty is a fixed *count* of requests per start, not a fraction of traffic, so it breaches p95 or p99 at small request counts while the median never moves. Two independent causes: 1. **The JIT warmup registry never runs on CPU.** `CPUWorker` overrides `compile_or_warm_up_model` without calling `kernel_warmup()`, so `jit_warmup_registry.warmup()` never fires and the top-k/top-p variants the registry already declares are never built. Registering them alone is not enough for this reason. 2. **`idx_mapping` inherits numpy's alignment.** The CPU `async_tensor_h2d` hands back `torch.from_numpy(...)` unchanged when the dtype already matches, and `idx_mapping_np` is already int64, so `_prepare_prefill_inputs_kernel` and `_gumbel_sample_kernel` see a pointer that is 16-byte aligned during warmup and 8 mod 16 on a real batch. Triton specializes on pointer alignment, so that is a recompile warmup cannot predict. Copying numpy inputs into a torch allocation keeps the pointer aligned and keeps the aligned specialization. ## Test Result ### Serving `vllm bench serve`, Qwen3.5-9B, 32 cores, concurrency 2, 512-token prompts, `--ignore-eos`. Same wheel, same pod, arms interleaved per request count, nothing else on the cluster. title: [MoE][Kernel] Quantize MXFP8 in the DeepEP low-latency dispatch (VLLM_DEEPEPLL_MXFP8_DISPATCH)
summary: ## Overview Add `VLLM_DEEPEPLL_MXFP8_DISPATCH` (default off), the MXFP8 counterpart of `VLLM_DEEPEPLL_NVFP4_DISPATCH`. With it, the DeepEP low-latency dispatch kernel quantizes the tokens to MXFP8 while it sends them, and `FlashInferCuteDSLBatchedExperts` runs on them directly. Without it, the tokens are dispatched in bf16 and the experts quantize them in a separate pass. - Stacked on #66456; only the last two commits are new. - Needs a DeepEP build with deepseek-ai/DeepEP#823 (`use_mxfp8` in `Buffer.low_latency_dispatch`, `hybrid-ep` branch). - Also fixes the startup of `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` with a `hybrid-ep` DeepEP, which either fused dispatch flag needs. - Related: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3362. ## Claims - With the flag, a dispatched token carries `hidden + hidden / 32` bytes instead of `2 * hidden`, and the experts no longer run `mxfp8_grouped_quantize`. - The MoE output is bit-identical to the bf16 dispatch, and GSM8K stays within run-to-run noise. - Serving Qwen3-30B-A3B MXFP8 on 4 GB200 GPUs (DP=EP=4), median TPOT is 2.5% to 3.2% lower at concurrency 16, 64 and 256. - The flag is opt-in. summary: ## Overview Enable KV cache reuse through Mooncake Store between vLLM instances with different pipeline-parallel (PP) sizes or layer partitions. title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip masked-out context tiles for sliding-window models in Triton prefix-prefill
summary: ## Overview On sliding-window layers the Triton prefix-prefill kernel walks the whole cached context, then masks almost all of it to `-inf`, so a 32k-token prompt with a 512-token window reads 62x more KV than it uses. title: [ROCm] Warm the AITER FA extend kernels from the attention backend

A chunked continuation or prefix-cache hit runs `extend_forward`, which makes a causal call for the new tokens and a noncausal call per gathered context chunk, both returning the LSE. AITER builds each of those modules on first use, so the first request that takes the extend path stalls for about 45 s per module. summary: ## Purpose `memory_profiling()` derives `total_consumed` (weights + non-torch overhead, the base of the KV cache budget) from the device-wide free-memory delta between the worker's init snapshot and the end of the profile run. Anything another process allocates or releases on the same device in that window is charged to, or credited against, this instance: two instances started at the same time on one GPU shrink each other's KV cache or fail with `No available memory for the cache blocks` or `To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len ...`. Since #56492, the KV cache on CUDA and ROCm with the V2 model runner is extensible by default. title: [Bugfix][MLA] Drop PCP padding-only rows from FlashMLA sparse FP8 decode metadata
summary: ## Overview With `--prefill-context-parallel-size > 1` (PCP) and the FlashMLA sparse FP8 KV cache (`fp8_ds_mla`), a decode step can crash and deadlock the engine when at least one PCP rank owns no decode request. PCP decode sharding assigns each decode request to a single PCP rank; the other ranks keep a zero-token collective placeholder row. The local batch is padded to the largest rank's token count, so on a FULL-cudagraph replay `num_actual_tokens` is the padded count (e.g. 1) while `query_start_loc` is all zeros. The FP8 separate prefill/decode metadata builder then computes `decode_query_len = 0` and `num_decode_tokens = 1`, and the pre-fix code fails at `assert decode_query_len > 0` (or divides by zero) on those ranks. The rank that owns the decode keeps going and enters the PCP collectives, so the workers deadlock and the engine core dies after the RPC timeout. The fix drops decode metadata for a batch whose rows carry no query token, and makes the FP8 forward return zeros for padding-only rows so every PCP rank still reaches the collectives. ## Claims ## Validation ## Details --- <details> <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary> - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Allow replicated MoE with --monokernel
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview #67569 removes the MoE all-gather and reduce-scatter of the ROCm Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) under `--enable-hc-sp` by replacing each rank's TP2 expert shards with whole experts. It has to refuse `--monokernel`: #65188's specialized decode reads the TP2 shards in place and sums the two ranks' outputs, so whole experts would be summed twice. This PR makes the two work together. With `--monokernel` and `--enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe`, every step the specialized decode does not run (prefill, mixed steps, decode widths it does not plan) runs the whole experts on the rank's own rows, without the MoE collectives. What the specialized decode reads is `--hc-sp-replicated-moe-decode-layout`: - `copy` (the default): each decoder layer also keeps the TP2 shards, which the specialized decode reads in place as without the flag. Each rank holds its shard on top of the whole experts. - `shares`: no second copy; the specialized decode reads the rank's TP2 share of the whole experts in place. Each rank holds the weights #67569 holds. Without `--monokernel`, the flag keeps #67569's single layout, and setting the decode layout is refused. **Which configuration to run** (each pair on one image; Validation): - `--monokernel` with `copy` against #67569 alone (the flag without `--monokernel`), for 36.5 GiB more a rank: - output tok/s +2.3 to +8.6 % at the prefill-heavy points, +36 to +70 % at 1024 / 1024; - most of that gain is #65188's specialized decode, which only `--monokernel` runs (median ITL −33 to −42 %); this PR's own gain is the flag-off vs fl

title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add --enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With TP=2 and `--enable-hc-sp` (sequence parallelism for the HyperConnection (HC) computation), each rank of a ROCm Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model keeps only its own rows between layers, but the MoE experts are TP-sharded. So every MoE layer all-gathers its input from both ranks and reduce-scatters the partial outputs back. These collectives cost more than the expert GEMMs. One profiled 8192-token prefill step, without → with the flag (Validation): - step: 472.7 → 417.7 ms; - collective kernels: 85.4 → 45.9 ms (the MoE all-gather and reduce-scatter of all 48 layers go away); - MoE expert GEMMs: 28.1 → 16.0 ms (whole experts on the rank's own rows instead of shards on all rows; AITER also has tuned rows for the whole-expert shape and none for the shard; the two effects are not separated). The opt-in `--enable-hc-sp-replicated-moe` (off by default) keeps every routed expert and the fused shared expert whole on each rank. Each rank then computes complete MoE outputs for its own rows, so the MoE all-gather and reduce-scatter go away. The attention keeps its all-gather and reduce-scatter. **Memory.** Whole experts add 24.0 GiB of weights a rank for this model (measured 42.25 → 66.26 GiB). At a fixed `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.85 in the A/B below), the KV cache shrinks by the same amount: - MI355X has 288 GiB of HBM a GPU; the KV cache keeps 175 GiB a rank (199 GiB without the flag). - vLLM's KV cache size: 13.8 M tokens (15.7 M without the flag, −12 %). - vLLM's maximum concurrency at the full 262,144-token context: 52.6 requests

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix handshake metadata key collision across PCP ranks
summary: ## Overview Fix KV connector handshake failures when using `MultiConnector` with PCP > 1 and DCP = 1. Workers with the same PP and TP ranks report metadata under the same key, so one PCP rank’s report can overwrite another’s before `MultiConnector` distributes the metadata to its sub-connectors. This can discard NIXL’s handshake metadata and cause P/D requests to fail. This PR preserves each worker’s metadata using `(pp_rank, pcp_rank, tp_rank)` keys, then splits the reports by sub-connector before converting them to the existing handshake keys. This prevents metadata loss while preserving existing connector interfaces and rank mappings. ## Claims - A P instance with PCP2 / DCP1 and `MultiConnector(NixlConnector, <connector that reports handshake metadata on every rank, such as UMBPStoreConnector>)` serves P/D requests. On main, P starts but D's first NIXL handshake fails and every request returns 500. - Connectors that implement `set_xfer_handshake_metadata` or `set_xfer_handshake_metadata_pp_aware`, including `NixlConnector`, receive the same `(pp_rank, tp_rank)` keys as on main. When PCP ranks that share such a key report different metadata, startup fails instead of keeping the last report. - D outputs are unchanged: output token IDs and top-5 logprobs match main exactly on 36/36 prompts, for NIXL alone and for NIXL with a second connector. ## Validation **Unit tests** (commit b90d837a81) ```bash pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k "handshake or overrides_all_base_methods" p

title: [Model Loader] Load plan: plan copy-time casts and setitem writes as direct; faster overlap check
summary: ## Purpose Part of the weight-update speed work for #54477 (direct reload with `use_load_plan`). The load plan decides, for each checkpoint tensor, whether an update writes it straight into its destination or falls back to the model's `load_weights`. Fallbacks run per tensor in Python and dominated update time on several flagships. Two common loader patterns were fallbacks and are now direct writes: - **A copy across dtypes** is the loader's own `copy_` conversion. The write records the destination dtype (`Write.dtype`), the destination is viewed in it, and the copy replays the same conversion. Integer casts of equal width keep every bit, so they stay plain byte copies: an int8 MXFP4 checkpoint into a uint8 parameter, for example. - **`param[...] = weight`** with a traced value is recorded as `param[...].copy_(weight)` when the index selects a view; an advanced index makes a copy and is still dispatched. `load_planned` also batches its direct copies into one `torch._foreach_copy_` per ~2 GiB of source instead of one `copy_` per tensor; the flush bounds how many streamed source tensors stay alive. The overlap check also sweeps each copy's byte span first and expands only intersecting copies into runs. The result is the same. ## Results (GB200, steady-state update) | Model | Before | After | |---|---|---| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash (int8 → uint8 experts) | 7.4 s | 2.6 s | | Qwen3.8 TP2+EP (bf16 → fp32 casts) | 7.7 s | 1.9 s | | MiniMax-M3.1 (setitem; with the FP4 prep PR) | 5.3 s | 1.1 s | | Beam (setitem; with the FP4 prep PR) | 8.8 s | 1.4 s | | DSv4.1 first-update plan trace | 99
