title: [RFC]: Load plan — an engine-neutral API for sharded weight transfer
summary: # Motivation. Weight transfer engines that move sharded bytes themselves (`nccl_m2n`, sharded RDT/NIXL) need to know, for every tensor the trainer sends, **which part this rank needs** and **where in live memory it goes**. `load_weights` can't tell them: it takes full tensors and shards them internally. Today each engine works this out on its own by reaching into reload internals: - **NCCL M2N** (#51520, #60934, #62853, #60949, #63216) matches parameter names (`resolve_parameter_destinations`) and uses a hand-written hook for experts (`resolve_sharded_weight_target`). Anything else is a full tensor through `load_weights`. - **Sharded RDT** (#43375) bakes an op chain with `FakeRDTTensor` in a layerwise meta dry run and scatters on background threads. The dry run keeps it off direct reload (#64336). Two merged or in-flight pieces make one shared answer possible: - **#63215 / #63256**: every `WeightSource` declares its tensors once in `ParamMeta` (HF name, dtype, shape, owners, placements), identically on every trainer rank. - **#54477** (direct reload): each update views every tensor back to its checkpoint layout in its own storage, `load_weights` writes in place, and post-load processing (PWAL) reruns at finish. Storage never moves. **Goals.** One `plan_loads(model, metadata)` for every engine; the model's loaders stay the only source of truth for sharding; results equal a cold start, checked byte for byte in CI; anything the plan can't express falls back to `load_weights`. **Non-goals for now.** Online quantization, EPLB, per-update subsets of names, rollback, staging buffe

title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Add connector checkpoint hooks and restore NIXL P/D workers independently
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Lets KV connectors take part in the process checkpoint lifecycle added in #62570, and implements it for NIXL so prefill and decode instances can be checkpointed and restored independently, with several replicas restored from one checkpoint. Two commits: the connector hooks and checkpoint gate, then the identity refresh with the NIXL implementation. ## Claims - KV connectors get `checkpoint_prepare()` and `checkpoint_restore()`, which do nothing by default. `MultiConnector` forwards them. Preparing calls them once the engine has drained and released its KV cache: first the scheduler-side instance, then every worker-side instance, before the device communicators. Restoring calls them on every worker-side instance after the device communicators, then on the scheduler-side instance, before the KV cache wakes. - An engine with a KV connector prepares only if the connector supports process checkpoints with its config. `supports_checkpoint(vllm_config)` is False by default, so `/checkpoint/prepare` returns 400 and `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` fails at startup for other connectors. A `MultiConnector` needs every child to support them. - Each restore gives the instance a new identity. The engine draws a restore ID and passes it to its workers. `VllmConfig.refresh_identity` appends it to the KV engine id on both sides, and `MultiConnector` refreshes the config copy of each connector it wraps. NIXL re-reads it on restore, so peers handshake again instead of reusing metadata cached under the old engine id. - NIXL supports process checkpoin

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Push: stop WRITE submission stalls and early block release; lock the NIXL agent
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes for NIXL push mode (P/D disaggregation) under sustained load, plus locking for the NIXL agent in both modes: 1. **Push: no UCX thread pool.** Push posts WRITEs from its writer thread. With `num_threads=4`, a large WRITE waits on the UCX backend's posting threads; push now defaults to `num_threads=0`. 2. **A locking NIXL agent, in both modes.** The agent is created with `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW`. Without a sync mode NIXL's agent lock is a no-op, yet push calls the agent from three threads and pull from two (the handshake executor loads remote agents while the engine thread posts and polls transfers). 3. **Push: no block release while a WRITE is in flight.** A send lease could expire, and its blocks be freed, while their WRITE was still being submitted or running. The lease reaper now keeps such requests until their WRITEs end. The pull-mode lost-connection fix that was originally part of this PR is now #68047. Locking the agent in pull mode builds on #59877 by Maroon Ayoub (co-author here), which diagnosed the unlocked agent and reproduced its crashes and hangs; this PR uses `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW` instead of `STRICT` (see "Agent locking"). ## Claims - A push-mode worker creates its NIXL agent with `num_threads=0` unless `num_threads` is set in `kv_connector_extra_config`. summary: > **Stacked on #64062.** Only the last 2 commits are new in this PR; the commits before them are #64062. ## Overview Client stop strings (`stop`, `stop_sequences`) are matched against the whole output text, including reasoning and tool call arguments. title: [Bug] Sync scheduler loses decode-filled blocks in Mamba align mode with spec decode (K ≥ 2)
summary: I ran into this while running a hybrid (Mamba-style + attention) model with prefix caching in `mamba_cache_mode="align"` and MTP with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2`, using the synchronous scheduler (vLLM 0.32.0). **What happens:** blocks that the decode fills never make it into the prefix cache. A follow-up request that shares the generated text only gets a hit up to the end of the prompt. **Why, as far as I can tell:** the sync `Scheduler` only caches blocks inside `KVCacheManager.allocate_slots()`, and that call runs `remove_skipped_blocks()` first. In align mode, `MambaManager.get_num_skipped_tokens()` returns `num_computed_tokens - 1`, so any recurrent block that ends one or more tokens before the computed count gets freed. With K ≥ 2, one verify step can commit 2+ tokens past a block end. The next `allocate_slots()` frees that block before it caches it. The state in the page was fine, it just never gets cached. K = 1 doesn't hit this, because a step only moves 1–2 tokens. The async scheduler doesn't either, because it caches the committed tokens when the output arrives. **Repro:** hybrid model, block size 512, `--prefix-match-unit 128`, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 512`, MTP K = 2, sync scheduling. 1. Send a prompt and let the decode fill at least one block. 2. Send prompt + generated text + 1 token. You'd expect the hit to include the decode-filled block, but it stops at the last prompt block. K = 0 and K = 1 give the full hit. **A fix that works for us:** do what `AsyncScheduler` does, and cache the committed tokens when the output arrives, only in align mode wi

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix Qwen3-VL M-RoPE input positions after a pruned video
summary: ## Overview With `--video-pruning-rate`, the Qwen3-VL processor puts the retained tokens of every frame of a video into the first frame's slot. `_get_mrope_input_positions` advanced the position counter only by the frame grids those tokens fill. Everything after the video got positions that are too early, and a video that keeps fewer tokens than one frame got a whole frame grid, so the result had more columns than the prompt has tokens. `MultiModalPruner.recompute` overwrites these positions when the video is encoded. It does not run when the video is a prefix cache hit, so on those requests the model reads the text after the video at the wrong positions. With this PR every frame advances the counter by one grid, as it does without pruning. Fixes #68269. #67190 makes the same kind of fix for Qwen2.5-VL and leaves Qwen3-VL out of scope. ## Claims For Qwen3-VL with `--video-pruning-rate` (EVS or VidCom2): - The text and media after a pruned video, and the first generated token, get the positions they have without pruning. These are also the positions `_recompute_mrope_positions` gives them, so a request whose video is a prefix cache hit now uses the same positions as one where the video is encoded. Before, they were early by (T − ⌊n/P⌋)·max(h, w) − part(n mod P) positions (defined under Details). That is 120 positions for a 16-frame 960x544 video at rate 0.5 with the `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` processor. - A video that keeps fewer tokens than one frame (VidCom2 at high rates or on short videos) gets one position per prompt token. Before, it got a whole frame grid. - Nothing

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep model-dtype query without a TRTLLM-GEN kernel
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #68523. On SM100/SM103 with a quantized KV cache, `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.get_q_data_type()` selected an FP8 query for every group, regardless of whether that group can run a kernel which consumes FP8 queries. This produces two failures: 1. **Default flags.** `use_trtllm_attention()` forces the TRTLLM prefill path whenever the query is FP8. Gemma 4's `head_dim=512` full-attention layers are then routed to the TRTLLM-GEN *context* kernel, which has no cubin for d512, so warm-up dies with `Missing TRTLLM-GEN kernel (context)`. 2. **`--attention-config.use_trtllm_attention=0`.** The prefill kernel selection honors the flag and falls back to native FlashInfer, but the query is still quantized to FP8, and FlashInfer's native `paged_run` asserts `assert not is_float8(q)`. The FlashAttention backend cannot take these layers either: on Blackwell, FA4 is limited to `head_size <= 128` (plus 256/256 and 192/128) because of TMEM capacity, and d512 is downgraded to FA2, which has no FP8-KV kernel. The only viable path for d512 + FP8 KV is therefore native FlashInfer with a model-dtype query. This PR keeps the query in the model dtype when TRT-LLM attention is explicitly disabled, or when the group's head dim has no TRTLLM-GEN kernel, and skips query pre-quantization / fused output quantization for those groups. | Config (B300, FP8 KV) | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | default | crash: `Missing TRTLLM-GEN kernel (context)` | prefill: native FlashInfer (BF16 Q); decode: TRTLLM-GEN | | `use_trtllm_attention: false` | crash: `assert not is_float8(q)` | native Flas

title: [RFC]: Direct Weight Reload for RL Training
summary: > **Revision 2 (2026-10-27).** Rewritten after validating direct reload on 17 flagship families. > > Rev 1 classified the 88 PWAL implementations so that most modules would skip post-load processing on reload. That skip caused silent errors: MLA absorbed weights went stale, and loaders that bypass tracking were missed. Rev 2 drops the skip, so every module reruns cold-start post-load processing. > > Rev 1 is in the edit history. #59502 was closed in favor of this design. > > **Update (2026-10-27, later).** The work is split into PRs and the PR stack is validated on DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-M3.1, Muse Spark and gpt-oss (Validation → PR stack). Derived tensors now go through `refill_derived` instead of widening `replace_parameter`, so F6 is dropped. ## TL;DR After a weight update, the engine must serve exactly what a cold start on the new checkpoint would serve, and the cold-start CUDA graphs must stay valid. `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` does this with three rules: 1. **View back.** At begin, each tensor is reinterpreted in its own storage as its checkpoint layout: the shape, stride and dtype recorded at cold start. Nothing is allocated. 2. **Rerun cold start.** The model's own `load_weights` writes the new bytes in place. At finish, every module reruns its cold-start post-load processing (PWAL), then the model-level hooks run. Nothing is skipped, so correctness equals cold start by construction. 3. **Derived state stays at its address.** Some tensors that a kernel or CUDA graph reads are derived from the weights: kernel constants, `1/a_scale`, absorbed MLA weights, decode copies.

summary: ## Overview With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs`, a greedy request's logprobs change in the last bits when it shares a batch with a request whose logits need processing (penalties, temperature, min_p, logit bias, structured output). `Sampler.apply_sampling_params` returns the raw BF16 logits when no request in the batch needs processing, and an FP32 copy otherwise, and the logprob kernel rounds the two inputs differently. Under the flag, this PR returns FP32 logits in both cases. Related: #68446 (top logprobs also depended on the batch, through `torch.topk`). ## Claims - **Bug:** `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` says "Batch invariance ensures that the output of a model is deterministic and independent of the batch size or the order of requests in a batch." With processed logprobs on `main`, a greedy request's logprobs change next to a request with `repetition_penalty`. Tokens are unchanged. title: [Spec Decode] Fix Dspark adaptive verification cost model
summary: ## Summary Adaptive verification picks, every step, the draft budget `b` that maximises ``` expected accepted tokens(b) / step cost(b) step cost(b) = drafter cost + base + (price of b draft slots) ``` The argmax depends only on how the slot price compares with the base. The current cost model gets both wrong, because it reads everything off a single profiled curve. This PR profiles the two separately and prices the base from the batch's real shape and context. On Qwen3-4B with DSpark at batch size 256 (TP1, H100), this gives **+2.7% output throughput on SPEED-Bench throughput_1k** and **+8.4% on MT-Bench**. The fixed model won all 10 paired runs. ## The bug `batches_to_profile` ran one family of dummy batches: *n* requests, one token each, every request carrying `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN` (default 8192) tokens of fabricated KV context. That produced `verify_cost_ms[n]`, whose index means *n sequences, each reading 8k tokens of KV*. `get_num_tokens` then priced every budget as ```python costs = draft_cost_ms[num_reqs] + verify_cost_ms[num_non_draft_tokens : num_non_draft_tokens + max_draft_budget + 1] ``` That one lookup has three errors. 1. **A draft slot is priced as another whole sequence with 8k of context.** Walking `b` steps along `verify_cost_ms` charges each draft token as one more request reading 8k of KV. A draft slot is really one more query token on a sequence already in the batch, so it reads no new KV. 2. **The base always assumes 8k of context per request.** Workloads with short contexts, such as MT-Bench, carry a few hundred tokens, so m

title: [Quantization] Keep E8M0 scale bytes when loading into uint8 params
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item L6). Builds on #65235 (P1, load plan). MX scale parameters (compressed-tensors MXFP4/MXFP8, ModelOpt MXFP8, Quark OCP-MX, INC MXFP4/MXFP8) are `uint8`, and their loaders end in `copy_weight_`. When the source is `float8_e8m0fnu`, `copy_` converts it by value (2^(b-127) cast to an integer), which stores wrong scales. Under the load plan the same copy is a cast, so the name falls back, and the fallback stores the same wrong bytes. With this PR, `copy_weight_` copies between any two different **byte containers** as bytes (`src.view(dst.dtype)`). The parameter then holds the sent bytes, and because the load plan sees a view, the names are direct. The load plan also makes copy-time casts between real value formats direct (for example a BF16 checkpoint into an FP32 or `float8_e4m3fn` parameter): the planned copy replays the loader's by-value conversion into a destination in the parameter's dtype. Same-width integer casts (`int8` ↔ `uint8`) are byte copies there. This part is taken from #67836 by @aoshen02 and co-authored. - **Byte containers:** `uint8`, `int8`, `float8_e8m0fnu`, `float4_e2m1fn_x2`. They hold raw bytes, scales or packed data, so the bytes are the value. - **Covered pairs include:** - E8M0 scales into `uint8` params, and the reverse (a U8 checkpoint into Fp8's `float8_e8m0fnu` block scales); - `int8` ↔ `uint8`, e.g. DeepSeek-V4/V4.1-Flash I8 routed experts into Mxfp4MoEMethod's `uint8` params. `copy_` already gave the same bytes. title: [ROCm] wvSplitK: keep bf16 N=5 at YTILE 2 on wave64 to avoid VGPR spills
summary: co-author with @whatghost ## Overview On wave64, bf16 `wvSplitK` at N=5 spills registers on the `YTILE=3` and `YTILE=4` rows of the generic tile table, which `out_dim > 32 * CUs` (8192 on MI355X) takes when the activations fit in LDS. title: [CPU] Fix int32 overflow in MLA decode buffer-size and offset computation
summary: ## Overview Fix signed int32 overflow in `mla_decode_kvcache` (`csrc/cpu/mla_decode.cpp`). Scratch-buffer sizes and per-sequence pointer offsets were computed in `int32_t`, so for large head counts the byte count `num_heads * V_HEAD_DIM * sizeof(float)` wraps before `std::aligned_alloc`, under-allocating the scratchpad (heap out-of-bounds write) or sign-extending into a huge `size_t` (worker crash). ## Claims - Widen the scratch-buffer sizes (`acc_out_nbytes`, `q_f32_nbytes`) to `int64_t` and the accumulator vector size to `size_t`. - Widen the pointer-offset arithmetic (`thread_id * num_heads * V_HEAD_DIM`, `seq_idx * stride`, `head_idx * V_HEAD_DIM`, `physical_block_idx * kv_stride`) to `int64_t`. - Add a `num_heads > 0` guard at the public entry point. - No behavioral change for in-range inputs (identical arithmetic, wider type). ## Validation Trigger configs (ASan+UBSan, single thread): - MODE A `num_heads=2,097,153`: `acc_out_nbytes` wraps to 2,048, so `std::fill` at `mla_decode.cpp:289` writes ~4 GiB past a 2 KiB buffer (ASan `heap-buffer-overflow` WRITE over the `aligned_alloc` at `:266`). - MODE B `num_heads=1,864,136`: the int32 product wraps negative and `aligned_alloc` receives `0xffffffffe38e4000` (ASan `allocation-size-too-big` at `:266`). - CONTROL `num_heads=16`: clean. After the fix, the file compiles and CONTROL runs clean (exit 0); the size computations are `int64_t` and cannot wrap for these sizes (3.8–4.3 GiB ≪ 2^63). title: [Bugfix][Perf] Exclude draft-only buckets from min_num_layers in KV cache grouping
summary: ## Overview When `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` groups KV cache specs by `(is_draft, type_id, page_size_bytes)`, it previously computed `min_num_layers` across **all** buckets—including draft-only buckets (`spec.is_draft=True`). When a hybrid target model (such as `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` / Qwen3.5-4B with 24 Mamba GDN layers and 8 FullAttention layers) is paired with a speculative decoding drafter whose attention bucket has only 1 layer (e.g., a 6-layer hybrid DFlash drafter with 5 Mamba layers + 1 FullAttention layer, or a 1-layer EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafter), the 1-layer draft bucket causes `min_num_layers` to collapse to `1`. As a result, `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits every target bucket into 1-layer KV cache groups (`[1] * 38` = 38 KV cache groups instead of `6` groups of `[8, 8, 8, 8, 5, 1]`), inflating per-step KV cache coordinator/manager iteration, block-table slicing, and attention metadata construction across 38 groups on every prefill and decode step. This PR computes `min_num_layers` and `max_num_layers` over **target-model buckets** (`not all(spec.is_draft for spec in specs)`) when any non-draft bucket is present, and suppresses the false-positive layer-padding warning for draft-only buckets that have fewer layers than `min_num_layers`. ## Claims - Reduces KV cache group count on hybrid target + draft models (`Qwen3.5-4B` + `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash`) from **38 groups (`[1]*38`) to 6 groups (`[8, 8, 8, 8, 5, 1]`)**. - On NVIDIA H100 NVL (512-query production JSON benchmark, $k=8$, concurrency 1), reduces **p95 E2E latency by 31.44

summary: ## Overview Fix signed int32 overflow in `cpu_fused_moe_int8`'s scratchpad-size computation. summary: ## Overview Fixes #61490. title: [HY4 Flash][Performance] Fuse LatentMoE TP all-reduces via reduce_commutative
summary: ## Purpose Reuse the existing `reduce_commutative` mechanism to eliminate a redundant TP all-reduce in HY4 Flash LatentMoE. On 8×H200 with TP8, this change improves output token throughput by up to **5.74%** and reduces TPOT by up to **3.42%** in end-to-end serving benchmarks. Follow-up to [#68296](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68296). The optimization is limited to a single commit in `vllm/models/hy_v4_flash/nvidia/moe.py`. Hy4-flash-FP8 keeps `routed_expert_up_proj` unquantized and bias-free. MoERunner already supports `reduce_commutative` for Nemotron-H (see [#52301](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52301)). Marking the latent up projection as commutative lets vLLM fuse routed and shared expert TP all-reduces after the up matmul instead of reducing the routed latent partial sum first. ```text Baseline: reduce(routed_partial) -> up_proj -> add(reduce(shared_partial)) This PR: reduce(up_proj(routed_partial) + shared_partial) ``` For a bias-free, unquantized linear projection, `W @ sum(x_i) = sum(W @ x_i)` in real arithmetic. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Derive the namespace cache dtype from the KV cache specs
summary: Closes #56894 ## What The native offloading secondary-tier namespace identity is built from `cache_config.cache_dtype` on the scheduler side. Sparse MLA workers normalize that field in place (`fp8` -> `fp8_ds_mla`) inside `MLAAttention` construction, which runs in the worker process. With the default `uni` executor the worker shares the EngineCore process so the scheduler sees the rewrite; with `mp` it never leaves the worker. The same model then writes to two different namespaces depending on the executor, cross-engine hits drop to zero, and a TP1 engine that later gains `--distributed-executor-backend mp` can no longer see the blocks it wrote before restart. ## How The KV cache specs travel from the workers at registration, so `MLAAttentionSpec.cache_dtype_str` carries the normalized dtype string under both executors. `build_offloading_config` now derives the model identity dtype from the specs when they agree on one, and keeps the config knob when they do not or carry no string (non-MLA specs leave `cache_dtype_str` at its `None` default, so nothing changes for everyone else). A literal `auto` in either the knob or a spec resolves to the actual model dtype before it enters the namespace identity, so FP16 and BF16 cannot collapse into an `auto` namespace. title: [ROCm][Kernel] Tune the GatedDeltaNet Triton prefill kernels on gfx942
summary: ## Purpose The Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill walks each sequence's chunks in order, so the kernel grid and the MFMA tile shape are all that decide how much of the GPU its five Triton kernels fill. title: [Bugfix][Executor] Size response rings for in-flight batches
summary: ## Problem With Model Runner V2 async scheduling and a KV output aggregator, every worker rank must send a response so the aggregator can observe connector state. title: [Bugfix][Model] Don't carry realtime context into single-turn prompt models
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #51374. Fixes #51376. `/v1/realtime` runs one resumable request per session, and `Scheduler._update_request_as_session()` appends the previous chunk's output tokens to the next chunk's prompt. That is right for models whose realtime prompt is a running conversation and which consume `input_stream`. It is wrong for Qwen3-ASR: `buffer_realtime_audio()` emits a fresh single-turn ChatML prompt per 5 s segment and never reads `input_stream`, so the generic carry-over turns the session into a growing fake conversation whose assistant turns are the model's own transcripts. When a segment's acoustic evidence is weak, the decoder reproduces that history. Segment N+1's prompt today: ``` [segment N prompt] + [segment N output tokens] + [segment N+1 single-turn prompt] ``` This change lets the model class declare whether earlier segments belong in its context, and rebuilds the session from the new chunk alone when they do not. Text, multimodal features, KV and block hashes move together, which is the invariant asked for in #51376. The session also gives up its model-runner slot, as a preempted request does, because it then waits behind newer requests like a new one. ## Measurements vLLM at 144e79c, Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one session per row, `temperature=0`. title: [Metrics][Frontend] Pluggable KV connector metrics on the Rust frontend via connector metrics descriptor
summary: ## Purpose Today the Rust frontend's `/metrics` can only export KV connector metrics for Nixl and Mooncake, because each of them has dedicated Rust code. Stats from every other connector (Offloading, HF3FS, HiSparse, and out-of-tree connectors) do reach the Rust process, but are silently dropped, so these metrics disappear as soon as `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` is set. This PR lets a connector describe its own metrics, so the Rust frontend can export them without any per-connector Rust code. Design discussion: RFC: #58562. ## Changes How it works: 1. On the Rust frontend, the first time a connector reports stats, it also sends a short description of its metrics: name, type, help text, histogram buckets, and where each value sits in its stats. The description rides the existing scheduler stats message; there is no new RPC. 2. When the Rust frontend sees a description, it registers those metrics. After that, every stats tick carries values only, and Rust updates the metrics from them. 3. On the Python frontend nothing changes: no description is sent, and the existing Prometheus metrics stay as they are. 4. With MultiConnector, each child sends its own description and is exported separately. Nixl and Mooncake keep their existing Rust code paths. Key pieces: - **`maybe_attach_metrics_descriptor()`** (Python): attaches the description once, and only when the Rust frontend is on. title: [Feature][Scheduler] Opt-in kv_load_failure_policy="repair" for selective KV recovery
summary: > This PR is stacked on [#68139](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68139). Please review that PR first. This change adds the scheduler-side recovery lifecycle on top of the structured failure-reporting interface. ## Summary This PR introduces the opt-in `kv_load_failure_policy="repair"` policy, implementing the scheduler-side part of selective KV recovery proposed in [RFC #65172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65172). Instead of discarding an entire external KV cache claim when a load partially fails, the scheduler can now authorize a bounded repair of the affected region while preserving independently verified cached state. Recovery is only admitted when the failure report and per-rank transfer attestations provide sufficient evidence. The scheduler notifies the selected connector through `KVConnectorBase_V1.note_transfer_attempt()`, and subsequent reports and attestations carry the corresponding generation. This allows the scheduler to distinguish evidence belonging to the current transfer from delayed reports belonging to an earlier attempt. title: [Core] Add worker-side execution for KV cache repair
summary: ## Summary This PR implements the worker-side execution of selective KV cache recovery proposed in [RFC #65172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65172). A partial KV transfer failure currently costs the whole cached prefix: the request rolls back and recomputes everything above the failed region even when the surrounding cache is healthy and independently verified. The goal of the repair policy is to recover only what is actually damaged: identify the affected region from the structured report, re-execute just the failed span through the layers that observed the failure, and keep the verified cache on both sides of it. The stack splits as follows: - [#68139](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68139) - connectors emit structured `KVLoadFailureReport`s (spans, rollback boundary, failed layers, content certification) instead of a flat failure flag. - [#68140](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68140) - the scheduler-side lifecycle: recovery planning, admission bounds and budget, rollback, untrusted-block invalidation, evidence aggregation, and the opt-in `kv_load_failure_policy="repair"` policy. It also owns the init-time refusals for PP>1, DP>1 and multi-KV-cache-group setups. - **This PR - the worker side.** The scheduler admits a `RepairWork` on an exclusive repair-only step; this PR executes it, proves that what it wrote is what was authorized, and reports the verdict the scheduler commits against. ## What the worker does on a repair step `execute_repair_only()` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/repair_executor.py) runs inside the live forward context of an eage

summary: ## Overview Let a KV connector request and receive each step's intermediate (EAGLE-3 auxiliary) and final hidden states after sampling without storing them in the KV cache. title: [Model][Engram] Share Engram via RDMA to reduce DRAM redundancy cross instances
summary: ## Summary Share DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's immutable Engram tables across independently launched vLLM instances on different hosts. Each instance fetches the rows it needs from a shared host table using GPU-initiated RDMA GET. The existing local-table path remains the default. ```text Ordinary 1P1D: two local table copies (~377.66 GiB total) P instance --> local host Engram table (~188.83 GiB) D instance --> local host Engram table (~188.83 GiB) Shared 1P1D: one table backing (~188.83 GiB total) P instance -- GPU-initiated RDMA GET --+ +--> shared host Engram table D instance -- GPU-initiated RDMA GET --+ Shared 3P1D: four instances, one table backing (~188.83 GiB total) P1 --+ P2 --+-- GPU-initiated RDMA GET --> shared host Engram table P3 --+ D --+ ``` For 3P1D, sharing one table instead of four local copies reduces the estimated table extent from ~755.32 GiB to ~188.83 GiB, avoiding ~566.49 GiB of duplicate table storage. These figures describe table extent rather than measured total RSS or HBM savings. KV transfer continues through the configured P/D connector. This scale-out path complements the scale-up shared-address proposal in [RFC #64002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64002) and [#64082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64082). ## Implementation - The checkpoint-backed owner keeps the table in pinned host memory and registers it for remote access. The reader validates checkpoint metadata and sampled rows, then manages its buffers, ordering, and owner lease. Owner metadata contains memory keys and requires a trusted network. - A reusable provider

title: [Perf][Core] Keep Voxtral Realtime sessions resident across audio chunks
summary: ## Overview Voxtral realtime sends each audio chunk as a streaming-input update. Today, every chunk waits for the previous sampled token to round-trip through the frontend, then re-enters the waiting queue and is re-sent to the workers with its full token history and feature list. That per-chunk cost grows with the session's length. This PR keeps realtime sessions resident in the running batch: the engine keeps the last sampled token, Voxtral realtime stops feeding tokens back, and the workers receive only the new audio features. Follow-up (not in this PR): applying a queued chunk at schedule time under async scheduling, so that resident sessions decode every step instead of every other step. ## Claims - **Streaming chunks without tokens.** A continuation chunk with no prompt tokens now continues from the token sampled for the previous chunk instead of discarding it, and its multimodal data is placed at that token. Such chunks were rejected before (empty prompt), so existing clients are unaffected. Chunks with prompt tokens behave as before. - **Voxtral realtime uses it.** The frontend no longer feeds output tokens back through `input_stream`, and continuation chunks carry only audio. - **In-place resume.** A chunk without tokens resumes its session in place. The session is not re-admitted through the waiting queue, `NewRequestData` is not re-sent, and the workers get only the chunk's features through `CachedRequestData.new_mm_features`. Per-chunk scheduler and worker work no longer depends on the session's length. - **More real-time streams.** On 1×H100, with every stream

title: [RFC]: Adaptive admission for RL rollout batches under KV pressure
summary: ### Motivation. This is a concrete design for [automatic admission #64460](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64460), aimed at finite RL rollout batches under the [vLLM × RL roadmap #58990](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58990). A synchronous rollout batch finishes when its last sample does. Too much concurrency causes repeated preemption and recomputation; too little leaves KV capacity idle. The right level shifts with output lengths and cache pressure, so a static setting tuned on one workload can be off on the next. We propose an engine-local controller that adjusts admission from observed preemptions. The [watermark #44594](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44594) benchmark shows the trade-off on one workload (Qwen2.5-7B, prefix caching off): watermark 0.05 cut preemptions from 1,065 to 187 and raised output throughput 5.1% at the cost of higher TTFT, and by 0.15 the throughput gain had shrunk to 0.5%. A tuned static setting is the baseline to beat. We expect the largest effect on hybrid models, whose large KV blocks make free memory run out in big jumps. Phase A checks whether one calibrated static setting holds up as lengths, output-cap slack and KV pressure change. ### Proposed Change. Add an opt-in admission cap `C` under the hard limit `H` (`max_num_active_seqs`, or `max_num_seqs` when unset). `C` starts at `H` and stays within `[1, H]`. The target is preemption that repeats across scheduling steps; the scheduler already skips admission in a step that preempts. Lowering `C` only gates new admissions and never evicts running requests. title: [RFC]: Reuse-Prioritized LRU for Sparse KV Offloading
summary: ### Motivation. This RFC proposes Reuse-Prioritized LRU (RPLRU), a cache eviction policy for sparse key-value (KV) offloading. RPLRU gives entries with observed reuse stronger retention priority than newly loaded entries. Each valid entry maintains an integer age. A cache hit resets the age to zero. A newly loaded entry starts at a configurable age `P`. At each decoding step, resident entries without a hit increase their age by 1, up to the maximum age. When space is required, the policy uses free slots first, then evicts entries with the largest ages among those absent from the current selection. The objective is to improve cache hit rate and reduce repeated transfers from DRAM to HBM at a fixed cache capacity. ##### Background In sparse KV offloading, DRAM stores the complete KV state, while HBM maintains a cache with fixed capacity. At each decoding step, a Top-k selection identifies the required KV entries. The system reuses entries already in HBM and loads only cache misses from DRAM. Related work in vLLM includes the [RFC on layerwise and sparse KV cache offloading (#48203)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48203). The [HiSparse implementation (#53781)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781) retains KV in HBM when capacity permits and offloads pages to DRAM under memory pressure. Its decode path reuses selected KV from resident pages or a per-request hot buffer and gathers missing rows from DRAM. The hot buffer uses LRU replacement. RPLRU focuses on improving retention in this type of hot buffer by assigning different initial priorities to cache h

title: [Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs for faster Gated DeltaNet standard decode
summary: Supersedes [#48792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48792), closed when the source fork was deleted. ## Background This is the second sub-PR split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576), which presents the full ReplaySSM design across Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet for both standard and speculative decode. The first sub-PR, Mamba2 standard decode ([#48018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48018)), landed as `866fea2b9`, so this is a plain diff against main. It lands the next stage: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) standard decode. ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs instead of writing the recurrent state back to HBM on every step. It is a collaboration between Dao AI Lab and NVIDIA, and the full derivation and figures are in the [blog post](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/). AI assistance was used for parts of this work, and the authors have reviewed every changed line. ## Core concept GDN decode is memory-bound. Each step loads and stores the delta-rule recurrent state (a `head_v x head_k` matrix per value head), and that per-step state store dominates HBM traffic. ReplaySSM keeps a small ring buffer of recent per-step inputs (the key `k`, the corrected value `d`, and the scalar gate `g`) together with a periodic checkpoint state. On most steps it reconstructs the state and reads the output from the checkpoint plus the buffer, and it writes the full state back only on periodic flushes, once every `L` steps, where `L` is the buffer length. title: [Bugfix][DeepEPv2] Fix ElasticBuffer over-allocated by sp_size× under sequence parallelism
summary: ## Overview With sequence parallelism (TP>1, DP>1, EP), each EP rank only dispatches a `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, sp_size)` shard. Despite that, the DeepEP v2 `ElasticBuffer` is sized for the full `max_num_batched_tokens`, so it is over-allocated by `sp_size`×. This PR sizes the buffer for the shard. It also caps the per-step dispatch bound at the buffer capacity. Follows #57210, which bounded the dispatch by `sp_size` but left the buffer sizing unchanged. Related: #57440. ## Claims - Frees **~2.7 GiB per GPU** (ElasticBuffer 3.56 → 0.89 GiB) for KV cache on Kimi-K3 TP4×DP4×EP16 (B200). The saving is `(1 − 1/sp_size)` of the buffer and grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`. - Fixes a latent overflow. The power-of-2 dispatch bound could exceed a non-power-of-2 buffer capacity and trip DeepEP's host assert. Example: mnbt 10240 with sp 4 gives capacity 2560 and bound 4096. The same holds for sp 1 with mnbt 10240. - No numerics change. With real weights, 12/12 greedy prompts were identical, including top-20 logprobs. ## Validation **End-to-end setup**: Kimi-K3, TP4×DP4×EP16 (`sp_size=4`) on 2× a4-highgpu-8g (16× B200), stock `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-ac9126e5` (DeepEP d4f41e4). `main` and the PR differ only in the edited files. ```bash vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --max-num-batched-tokens $MNBT --max-num-seqs $SEQS \ --gpu-memory-utilization $GMU --max-model-len 32768 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --load-format {dummy|safetensors}

title: [Model Loader] Prefetch the node's share when the checkpoint exceeds RAM
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview **Stacked on #68351**: the first commit is #68351's; review only the second ([this PR's own diff](https://github.com/anish-shanbhag/vllm/compare/fix-prefetch-node-local-split...prefetch-ep-aware)). Auto-prefetch skips any checkpoint that does not fit in 90 % of available RAM. Under expert parallelism with the EP weight filter (on by default with #68491), a node reads only the shared tensors plus its own ranks' experts, often a fraction of the checkpoint. DeepSeek-V4-Pro is 805 GiB, and on nodes with ~800 GiB free it gets no prefetch at all, even though a TEP8 node reads 439 GiB of it and a DEP16 node 256 GiB. This PR gates on what the node reads when whole shards do not fit, and then prefetches just those bytes. Checkpoints that fit keep #68351's whole-shard prefetch unchanged. ## Claims - Model loading on the slowest node, **stock → this PR** (median of cold starts), deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro (805 GiB), auto mode: - TEP8, 2 nodes: **181.7 s → 57.4 s (−68%)** - DEP16, 4 nodes: **164.2 s → 44.9 s (−73%)** Stock logs "checkpoint total size (805.33 GiB) exceeds 90% of available RAM ... Skipping auto-prefetch". - No change when whole shards fit. The NVFP4 and FP8 timings below match #68351. - No new flag. title: [Mamba] Add INT8/FP8 Mamba2 SSM cache dtypes for FlashInfer ReplaySSM
summary: ## Overview Adds `int8` and `fp8` to `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype`. With either value, the Mamba2 SSM state is stored in 8 bits with one FP32 scale per `(head, head_dim)` row, and recurrence and readout share that one checkpoint. Only FlashInfer ReplaySSM decode (with Triton prefill) supports it today. Builds on #55688 (merged). The separate-checkpoint CuTeDSL variant is in draft #65660. Following review, 8-bit state is now an SSM cache dtype instead of a ReplaySSM-only `--replayssm-state-dtype` flag: - The scale page is part of the generic Mamba2 state: `(conv, ssm, ssm_scale)`. ReplaySSM appends its three rings after it, so code reads them as the last three states. - Each Mamba decode and prefill backend declares the SSM dtypes it supports (`decode_backend_ssm_dtypes`, `prefill_backend_ssm_dtypes` in `vllm/config/mamba.py`). One validator rejects any other combination with a single error that names the backend and lists what it supports. ```diff Mamba2 cache, per layer conv state BF16 - SSM state FP32 | BF16 | FP16 + SSM state FP32 | BF16 | FP16 | INT8 | FP8 E4M3FN + SSM scales FP32, (heads, head_dim) # only for int8/fp8 ReplaySSM rings ×3 unchanged, always last ``` [Diff against main](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/compare/a01451befc...f67b48a06c): 27 files, +1053/−87. ## Claims - With a fixed 160 GiB cache, both 8-bit formats admit **63.9% more requests** than FP16 (2,001 vs 1,221) on one GB300. - That does not raise throughput. At those admission limits, decode TPS changes by +0.25% for FP8 and −3.64% for INT8. - GSM8K stays within 1 point of BF16. FP8 averages 90.4% agai

title: [Model Loader] Enable the EP weight filter by default
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Enable the EP weight filter (`--enable-ep-weight-filter`) by default; `--no-enable-ep-weight-filter` turns it off. Under expert parallelism each rank only needs its own experts. Without the filter, every rank still creates a tensor for every expert weight in the checkpoint and passes it through the model's `load_weights`, only for `FusedMoE` to discard the non-local ones. The filter skips them up front. **History.** The filter landed on by default in #37136 and was made opt-in two days later (#37351), alongside #37322, which fixed its two accuracy bugs: - **EPLB:** redundant expert slots were starved, and GSM8K dropped to ~0.08. #37322 disabled the filter under EPLB; #64187 later made it EPLB-aware using the initial placement. - **NVFP4:** global activation scales were computed over uninitialized slots (~2 % loss). #37322 fixed this by skipping only `.weight` / `.weight_packed` tensors and always loading scales. With both fixed (and the filter covered by `test_ep_weight_filter.py` and the EPLB end-to-end test from #64187), keeping it opt-in only leaves the load-time win on the table. **Precedent.** TensorRT-LLM loads only a rank's own experts by default, with no option: its MoE weight loading iterates `module.initial_local_expert_ids` and looks each one up by name, so other ranks' expert tensors are never created. SGLang currently creates them all and drops the non-local ones afterwards, as vLLM does today; sgl-project/sglang#51314 proposes the same default skip there. Related: #68351 and #68490 (multi-node prefetch, including EP-aw

title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Prefetch the whole checkpoint into every node's page cache
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Safetensors prefetch (`--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`, or the automatic prefetch on NFS/Lustre) splits the checkpoint shards by **global** rank. The page cache is per node, so on a multi-node deployment each node warms only `1/num_nodes` of the shards, and its ranks then read the rest cold through the loader. This PR splits the shards among the ranks of **each node**, so every node prefetches the whole checkpoint. This affects any deployment whose world group spans nodes with prefetch active: - TP or PP across nodes (`--nnodes`, or Ray); - DP/EP across nodes, because `init_distributed_environment` folds the DP rank into the global rank. Related: #51339 (extends auto-prefetch to VirtioFS), #49324 (prefetch in the multi-thread loader; it calls `_prefetch_all_checkpoints`, so it inherits this fix), #57973, and the earlier prefetch and read-order work in #40068, #41499, #42837. Follow-ups: #68490 (stacked on this PR: EP-aware prefetch plus a per-node RAM gate) and #68491 (enable the EP weight filter by default). ## Claims - Each node now prefetches every shard. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds an opt-in snapshot endpoint to the ZMQ KV event publisher. A cache-aware router that starts late, restarts or misses events loads a rank's current cache state from it, then follows the live stream with no gap. Related: #50134 solves the same problem differently (compared under Details). title: [RFC]: PLE Connector for Disaggregated Embedding Serving
summary: ## Motivation Qwen models use large N-gram embedding tables: the open-weight [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) includes **51B** embedding parameters, and [Qwen4-Max](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen4-max) reports **328B** ([launch text](https://m.sohu.com/a/1102096678_384789)). This RFC uses PLE (per-layer embedding) for this lookup path. Assuming FP8 storage (one byte per parameter), these tables would occupy approximately **51 GB and 328 GB**, respectively, excluding quantization scales, metadata and runtime buffers. Replicating these tables across prefill instances multiplies storage costs, even when offloaded to host memory. At scale, lookup failures should have limited impact, and recovery should not require restarting inference workers. We propose a **PLE Connector** that connects vLLM prefill instances to a shared lookup service and prepares embedding rows asynchronously before prefill execution. ## Proposed Change This RFC targets prefill instances in disaggregated prefill/decode deployments. ### Shared lookup service A dedicated service owns a versioned, immutable PLE table and performs sparse row lookups for multiple prefill instances. It may shard or replicate the table and scale independently of inference compute. Within vLLM, the PLE Connector uses a provider interface for local or remote lookup and manages preparation, retries and a bounded result pool. Providers return raw rows in the requested row-ID order. Model-specific hashing, dequantization, projection and gating remain in vLLM. For remote lookup, prefill instances retain

title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Engram pool: split Engram tables across engines over NVLink or RDMA
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds `vllm/distributed/engram_pool/`, a pool of read-only tables split by rows over every GPU of a group of engines. Rows move over NVLink, or over RDMA from HBM or host memory. DeepSeek V4.1's cross-engine peer group (#66552) now runs on it and gains `peer_group_transport: nvlink | rdma`. Same goal as RFC #64002, #64395, #57023 and #64082 (one copy of the Engram tables shared across engines), different approach: no owner host or process, no native dependency (verbs through ctypes), NVLink and RDMA from HBM or host memory, and fetches fully capturable in CUDA graphs. Tracking issue: #57448. ## Design - **NVLink:** every GPU maps every shard (cuMem FABRIC); a fetch is one gather kernel. - **RDMA:** the owner's NIC gathers rows, ~15 rows (one packet) per RDMA WRITE, so fetches are not bound by the NIC's READ message rate. The requester's GPU writes the WRs and posts the request itself (mlx5 WQE + doorbell); a per-GPU owner proxy process posts them on its NIC. Each QP's last chain ends with a READ and a fenced flag WRITE, and the consumer kernel waits on the flags. A fetch is 2 kernels, with no host sync. - **Engines sharing NICs:** another engine's prefill could fill every owner QP and delay decode fetches (P/D in one group). `peer_group_rdma_inflight` (default 8) bounds prefill-sized gathers in flight per NIC. Prefill and decode engines can share one group (each GPU holds less) or use one group each (no interference, a full copy per group). The DP ranks of one engine step together, so the bound does not matter within one engine. ## V

summary: ## Overview In Tiered Offloading, the CPU block allocation for Secondary -> Primary transfer happens in tiering/manager.py. Under load, this leads to, reserving / locking the CPU cache space for long periods of time unnecessarily. For example, when the FS tier has only N threads, we'd only need to allocate space for N jobs for active use. This behavior on `main` makes "Promotion Allocation Failure" a function of input requests load. ## Claims This PR adds a Lazy CPU block allocation technique, by which the FS tier allocates CPU blocks only when it needs it. With this "Promotion Allocation Failure" becomes a function of the number of FS read/write threads. Users can tune their FS read/write threads value based on their CPU KV cache size. Note : With Thread Pool batching https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58404 "Promotion Allocation Failure" will further be decoupled from RW thread count. With batching, there is only a small constant number of jobs that are actively promoting at any given time. ## Validation [bench.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33185797/bench.sh) Benchmarking Setup: Model : gptoss120b GPU : H100 x 2 CPU KV Cache size : 25GB GPU mem util : 0.7 Benchmark : Guidellm - Multiturn conversations - 5 Turns, 20K prefix, 4K subsequent ISL . title: [RFC]: Add Time-to-Live (TTL) / Idle Eviction for GPU Prefix Cache
summary: ### Motivation. Currently, vLLM's GPU prefix cache only evicts cached KV blocks under memory pressure following an LRU eviction policy. However, major LLM serving providers associate an idle Time-To-Live (TTL) with cached prefixes and evict blocks once they remain unused past their TTL, even though GPU memory is not full. For example, OpenAI retains cached prefixes for GPT-5.6 for up to 30 minutes after their most recent read or write ([source](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime-gpt-5-6-and-later)). While users have previously asked for prefix-cache timeouts ([discussion](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/how-to-adjust-prefix-caching-timeout/1663), [#8333](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8333)), vLLM does not currently support general TTL-based prefix cache eviction. The closest existing setting is `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` ([docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease/#bidirectional-kv-transfer)), which is specific to decode-node KV blocks in disaggregated prefill/decode setups. Note that this issue is different from the RFCs [#37003](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37003) and [#51428](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51428). Those RFCs introduce priority/retention hints (`RetentionDirective` / `KvHint`) to protect high-value blocks from premature LRU eviction under memory pressure (e.g., during agent tool-call pauses); once their retention window expires, the blocks revert to normal LRU priority and remain cached if HBM is available. In contrast, this RFC proposes a hard idle expiration

title: [Feature]: TTL-based Eviction for KV Cache Blocks
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch As you may know, major LLM providers apply a retention period to stored KV cache. For example, OpenAI retains the KV cache for GPT-5.6 and later models for 30 minutes after its most recent read or write ([source](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime-gpt-5-6-and-later)). vLLM has only limited support for this. The only relevant option I could find is `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` ([source](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease/#bidirectional-kv-transfer)), which sets time-based eviction for KV cache stored on the GPUs of the decode stage in PD disaggregation. Beyond that, based on [this discussion](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/how-to-adjust-prefix-caching-timeout/1663) and [this GitHub issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8333), vLLM doesn’t support TTL-based prefix cache eviction. Note that what I have in mind is simpler than memory pinning, as discussed in GitHub issues #51428 and #37003. vLLM would keep its existing LRU eviction as is, but [`KVCacheBlock`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/624a5ddafd96df23fe2b9f6d4b8f52a08b9fe9ea/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L154) would gain an `expires_at` field, and a block would be lazily evicted after expiration time is passed. So my question is: would this feature be useful for vLLM? I’ve already implemented the eviction method described above and would like to open a PR. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview PR 1 of RFC #66344 (word timestamps for speech models). title: [Kernel] SM 12.x FP8 scaled_mm: swizzle the CTA raster for prefill-sized GEMMs

Once both the weight and the activation slab outgrow the L2, the default CTA raster re-streams an operand from DRAM. For example, Llama-3.1-8B `gate_up` (28672×4096) runs at about 180 TFLOPS at M=4096 and drops to about 52 at M=8192. This hits every FP8 (W8A8) dense model served on these parts with long prompts or large prefill batches. #55180 fixed the same problem in the SM 12.x blockwise FP8 kernel with the tile scheduler's `max_swizzle_size`. title: [MoE] Use sorted fused-MoE path on integrated GPUs for multi-token batches (#63943)
summary: ## Summary Triton fused MoE currently engages the low-latency unpermuted "naive block assignment" path when `num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= global_num_experts`, bypassing `moe_align_block_size`. - **On discrete HBM GPUs (A100, H100, B200):** This yields a ~12–19% decode speedup at `M=2..4` by eliminating the fixed CUDA launch overhead of the alignment kernel. - **On integrated/unified-memory GPUs (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark with UMA LPDDR5x):** Multiple tokens routing to identical experts cause redundant weight reads over shared memory bandwidth, leading to an 8% to 52% decode regression (#63943). This PR introduces an adaptive, architecture-aware threshold: 1. **Integrated / UMA GPUs (`current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()`):** Restricts naive assignment strictly to `num_tokens == 1` where expert collision is impossible, routing multi-token batches (`M >= 2`) through the sorted `moe_align_block_size` path. 2. **Discrete GPUs:** Preserves the existing `num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= global_num_experts` heuristic. > **Hardware Scope:** Measured on NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark) only; other integrated GPUs such as Jetson Thor take the same path but are unmeasured. Fixes #63943. ## Test Plan 1. **Unit tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py`:** - `test_integrated_gpu_expert_assignment`: Parameterized across `M in [1, 2, 4, 8]` for both integrated and discrete GPUs, verifying integrated GPUs take sorted path at `M >= 2` while taking naive path at `M=1`, and discrete GPUs preserve naive path at `M <= 4`. - `test_host_resident_weights_take_sorted_path`: Verifies zero regression on host-resident weigh

title: [Bugfix] Nemotron diffusion: per-request reveal-time logprobs
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Stacked on #58387 (base model support); the diff against main includes it. Tracking: #60283. This PR fixes how Nemotron masked diffusion returns logprobs. The batch's largest `logprobs` setting decided the score path for every request. When one request asked for top-k, the other requests' scores came from the converged step instead of the step each token was revealed at, and scores could be lost when that neighbour finished. ## Changes - **Per-request reveal-time scores.** The compiled step captures each position's sampled-token logprob and rank when the position is revealed. With `logprobs=k` it also captures the top-k of that same distribution, using one top-k over all decode rows. The values go into per-slot GPU buffers sized by `max_logprobs`. A request that asks for top-k no longer changes the other requests' scores. - **No host syncs on the logprobs path.** Every request's rows are emitted at fixed offsets with one gather, and the output processor keeps the first `num_sampled`. This removes the per-request Python loop, the per-slot stash and the host read of the commit flags. Request add and remove reset their state with in-place device fills, so the sampler passes `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. - **Admission checks owned by the model.** The model config registers a validator that rejects `logprob_token_ids`, and masked diffusion requires `--max-logprobs >= 0`. - **Configuration.** Pipeline parallelism is rejected in diffusion mode. - **SM100 workaround.** The graph break after the stochastic argmax only runs on SM100. title: [Bug]: Hybrid-model prefix caching silently drops to 0% when the align-mode Mamba checkpoint lands in request-unique tokens

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Store the chunks that fit when a request exceeds the CPU tier
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #66696. A request with more unstored chunks than the CPU offload tier can hold was never offloaded: the whole store was rejected and retried unchanged on every step. title: [RFC]: Optional weight staging and trainer-managed pause for weight transfer engines
summary: ### Motivation. Some weight sync strategies need more from the weight transfer API than it offers today. They split an update into **fetching** the new weights (slow, safe while serving) and **applying** them (faster, needs a pause): - **ModelExpress** already splits its client into `stage_weight()` (NIXL pull from trainer GPUs, or S3 delta replay) and `apply_weight()`. Its vLLM backend has to call both inside `update_weights`, while paused. - **vime disk-delta** patches vLLM with a `pull_weights` worker RPC so it can fetch to local NVMe before pausing. - **CoreWeave's RL rollouts** (built on ModelExpress S3-delta) run a separate background prefetcher process for the same reason. - **humans&** (on SGLang) reports a ~220 ms pause out of a ~4 s sync by decoding into pinned host memory while rollout continues. vLLM can't express this today. Pause/resume is entirely up to the caller, and no engine-side call is promised to be safe while serving: every weight-sync RPC runs inline on the EngineCore busy loop and each worker's main loop, so even an "unpaused" call stalls generation. The in-tree engines don't need the split, since their transfers are fast enough to fit inside the pause. This RFC proposes one optional, engine-side staging step that is guaranteed to overlap with generation, and moving pause/resume into the trainer-side `send_weights` so each backend pauses only for the apply. title: [Bugfix] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 loading: map fused_qkv_a_proj
summary: ## Overview `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` fails to load on main since #66118: ```text KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.kv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight_scale' ``` - #66118 builds the MLA projections with `bf16_linear(build, quant_config)`: a projection keeps its FP8 checkpoint weight only when the quant config resolves it to an FP8 scheme. - Quark resolves a fused module through `packed_modules_mapping`. This PR maps `fused_qkv_a_proj` to `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, as DeepSeek-V2 does. #56176 had fixed loading of these `weight_scale` tensors in the old loader-side dequant; #66118 removed that loader and its test. ## Claims - `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` loads and serves again, with and without the MTP draft. After loading, its MLA weights (target and draft, both TP ranks) equal, bit for bit, those of main with #66118 reverted. - Scope: `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the architecture of every published GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint. Its text model and MTP draft share its quant config and define no mapping of their own, so they resolve with this one. Across 13 published quantized GLM-5.3-Flash configs, only `fused_qkv_a_proj` resolves differently: - amd Quark MXFP4: block FP8, its shards' scheme (was MXFP4: the KeyError); - nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local (ModelOpt): its shards' `FP8_PB_WO`, dequantized like its `q_b_proj`

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Hoist tensor-descriptor construction out of unified-attention TD loop
summary: ## Summary Part of the TD adoption strategy proposed in #42545. `USE_TD`'s K/V tile loader rebuilt the tensor descriptor every tile iteration, since the descriptor base baked in the per-tile physical block index. This forced a `tensormap_create` per iteration, which the pipeliner could not predicate. - With Triton 3.8.0, the loop-local path failed to compile with a `tensormap_create` pipeliner error on all tested CUDA architectures (SM90, SM100, SM103, and SM120). ## Fix The loop-invariant `kv_head_idx` is now part of the descriptor base. One descriptor is built per K/V cache before the tile loop, and the per-tile physical block is supplied through the `load()` coordinate. This makes the descriptor loop-invariant and restores pipelined compilation. The hoisted 3D descriptor also requires a registered scratch allocator on the tested CUDA architectures. The PR wires up `set_triton_allocator()`, cached per device to avoid repeated registration on every forward pass. Q/output TD remains disabled for CUDA query lengths up to `MAX_3D_QUERY_LEN`; K/V TD remains enabled. TD remains opt-in, and the raw-pointer default is unchanged. ## Final validation Across the tested workloads, this PR's TD path improves on or remains near parity with vLLM main's TD path. The default path passes the same `1,627` tests before and after the change. With Triton 3.8.0, vLLM main's TD path fails to compile on all four tested architectures. title: [ROCm][Perf][MRV2] Context-length-bounded decode graphs (RFC #63757)
summary: ## Overview Reference implementation for RFC #63757, which covers the design, the alternatives and the interaction with #62749; design feedback is best placed there. title: [Attention] Support NVFP4 KV cache at head_dim 512 (Gemma 4) on SM100
summary: ## Summary Adds NVFP4 KV cache support for Gemma 4 on SM100/SM103 (via FlashInfer backend), including MTP with full CUDA graphs. - **Zero new KV blocks when NVFP4 KV groups share a pool.** The head_dim 256 and 512 groups use different NVFP4 page layouts. All FlashInfer dependencies are in flashinfer-python 0.7.4, which `main` pins: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6445 (NVFP4-to-FP8 materializer), flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5720 (PrimTS NVFP4 decode at head_dim 512), flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6925 (PrimTS runtime split-KV), flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8078 (shared PrimTS workspace) and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8057 (materializer API). The path is enabled only with `flashinfer-python>=0.7.4`. ## Results Gemma-4-31B-IT, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER --block-size 64`, MTP with `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant`. The baseline is FP8 KV. **Test cases** - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` passes. - Pre-commit is clean. - No NaN or degenerate

title: [ROCm][Model][Perf] Fold the k_out dequant and fp8 query quant into the QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache fusion for ROCM_AITER_FA, ROCM_ATTN, and ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
summary: ## Overview This PR depends on: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6808, which has already made it into the most recently pinned aiter release for vLLM (0.1.29). When this fusion and FP8 KV-Cache are active, there's an extra dequantize op (shown below) after the fused kernel to convert `k_out` from FP8 back to BF16 so the downstream attn pieces (ROCM_ATTN & ROCM_AITER_FA) can consume it properly. ```bash def convert_fp8( output: torch.Tensor, input: torch.Tensor, scale: float = 1.0, kv_dtype: str = "fp8" ) -> None: torch.ops._C_cache_ops.convert_fp8(output, input, scale, kv_dtype) ``` This extra small op launch overhead can be saved by folding the conversion portion back into the fused kernel, as it already has an option to output k_out in BF16 when FP8 KV Cache is active. We take `k_out` via `k_out_unquantized`. As for the FP8 query quant, it follows the same idea; we fold the FP8 quantization portion back into the fused kernel. `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` consumes quantized q_out_fp8; we're only able to fold the extra quantize op if the method is `per_tensor` and one corner case of `per-head` (if we have only one local KV head, we'd only need 1 scale). If we have more than 1 local KV head, it falls back to an extra ` static_scaled_fp8_quant` launch to take care of the quantization. To be able to fold all query quantization cases back into the fused kernel, this requires further kernel-side changes within AITER; it needs to take in a scale tensor of size [num_kv_heads] and have the kernel pick the scale for each Q head. title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Decode monokernel TP4: EP buddy expert copies for HM
summary: ## Overview Stacked on #65748 (decode monokernel TP4 EP4), which stacks on #65747. The PR targets main, so review only the last commit. At TP 4 the 24-64-row decode steps run HA + HM + HB a layer. HM (the routed experts) lasts as long as the rank with the most used experts, and HB waits for it. With `VLLM_MUSE_MONO_EP_BUDDY=1` (off by default): - At attach, every rank receives copies of K experts a layer of rank r + 1 (`VLLM_MUSE_MONO_EP_BUDDY_K`, default 6, 1-7) through a P2P ring on the TP group. That costs 26.7 MB an expert a layer, so **9.6 GB a rank at K = 6**. The copies are allocated with the weights, before the KV cache is sized. - Each HM launch plans, from the step's top-8 ids alone and so identically on every CTA and rank, how many of rank r + 1's used and copied experts rank r runs. The plan minimizes the largest per-rank expert count. It is exact for K <= 7, which is why K is capped at 7. - A moved expert's picks are summed into the executing rank's EP partial, and HB already sums every rank's partial. HA, HB and the K3 builds (8 / 16 rows) are unchanged. - Flag off: every new kernel line is behind `const_expr(BUDDY)` or `rep is None`. On the development copy, the flag-off HM ELFs and the K3 ELF were byte-identical to the base. ## Why the table is built in The experts to copy are the first K of a per-layer, per-rank priority table. I considered two options. 1. **Ship a generator.** The table comes from counting which experts each 64-row decode launch uses. That needs a MoE id-capture hook plus an offline reader, and the user has to run a serving workload first.

title: [Quantization] Report the resolved kernel per layer in model inspection
summary: ## Overview Model inspection now reports the quantization kernel or backend that was actually selected for each layer, instead of only the quant method class name. The load time log moved out of `create_model` to the end of `load_model`, after `process_weights_after_loading`. That step is where `moe_kernel` gets assigned, because it starts as `None` in `fused_moe/fused_moe_method_base.py:33`. Before this change every MoE layer printed no kernel while linear layers printed one, so the output was inconsistent. - Works with the full set of kernel attribute names used across quant methods (`moe_kernel`, `fp8_linear`, `linear_kernel`, `ocp_mx_linear`, `kernel`, `experts_cls`), and with the compressed-tensors `module.scheme`. title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Optional replicated input embedding
summary: ## Overview `VLLM_MUSE_REPLICATED_EMBED=1` keeps the full input embedding table on every TP rank (`VocabParallelEmbedding(disable_tp=True)`), so the embedding lookup issues no all-reduce. title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] DSpark: Markov sampling on each rank's vocabulary shard
summary: ## Overview `VLLM_MUSE_DSPARK_MARKOV_VOCAB_SHARD=1` (off by default) applies to the Muse Spark DSpark draft on ROCm with TP > 1. It installs a model-level `sample_sequential` hook that runs the sequential Markov chain on each rank's vocabulary shard of the draft lm_head. vLLM's loop instead all-gathers the draft logits and then reads the whole replicated `markov_w2` (207 MB) on every rank for every draft position. No shared runner or speculator code changes: the hook is the existing `DSparkSpeculator` contract that #66051 uses. ## Claims - **Per draft position:** the bias comes from the rank's rows of `markov_w2` (1/tp of the bytes). One Triton launch does the bias add, Muse's output transform, the cache-dtype store and each 1024-token block's Gumbel (or greedy) max. Then comes an all-gather of the (token id, score) keys (`R x 2 x blocks` fp64), and one launch that picks the winner and gathers the next Markov embedding. The base logits come from the lm_head shard, so the draft logits all-gather goes away. For probabilistic drafts, the staged shards are all-gathered once and copied into the draft logits cache. - **Same draws as vLLM's loop.** The Gumbel noise is keyed by the global token id, and the winner is the lowest-index maximum in either block partition. Only a NaN logit can choose differently, because the block boundaries move. - **Coexists with #66051.** The hook is installed *ahead of* the `--monokernel` Markov rounds when those are present, and the steps it declines go to them (or to vLLM's loop). title: [Bugfix][Core] Profile and validate kv_cache_memory_bytes instead of skipping the profile
summary: ## Purpose `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` never checked the size it was handed. The branch returned before `memory_profiling` ran, logged "skipped memory profiling", and passed the number straight through. Nothing compared it against what the model needs for itself, so a size that is too large starts fine, serves short requests, and then OOMs in the middle of one once traffic reaches the activation peak. The same measurement gap exists under `gpu_memory_utilization`, but it stays hidden there: the KV size is derived from a budget that is only a fraction of the device, so whatever the profile missed lands in the part the utilization fraction left unallocated. A pinned size has no such slack — the operator sized it to use what was free — so the pinned cache and the unprofiled activation peak compete for the same free memory. There is a second half to it. Even when the profile does run, it forwards with `skip_attn=True`, because there is no KV cache yet to attend against. The attention activations, and the device memory those kernels take the first time they launch, are simply not in the figure. Harmless where slack absorbs it; not harmless when the cache was pinned to that figure. ## What this changes Run the profile for a pinned size too, and check the value against the result. If it does not fit, fail at startup and report the largest size admitted by this profile. Refusing rather than quietly capping is deliberate: a pinned size is an explicit capacity decision, and silently reducing it hides the one number this option exists to control. title: [Qwen3.5] FP16 partial sums for the deferred row-parallel all-reduces
summary: ## Overview This is a follow-up to #61888 and is stacked on it: the diff specific to this PR is 28e9e006 plus the `main` merges (through #61888's branch) and the docstring commit on top of it, and I'll rebase once #61888 lands. #61888 adds an opt-in flag (`VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS`) that makes tensor-parallel row-parallel layers exchange their partial sums in FP16 instead of BF16, so the result is rounded once, as on a single GPU. Since #64723, Qwen3.5 on NVIDIA no longer all-reduces inside those layers: it defers the all-reduce to the next norm. The flag therefore never reaches them. On Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 at TP=2, flag on and flag off give identical logprobs. This PR makes the deferred path carry FP16 partial sums too, on GPUs where that all-reduce isn't fused into the norm by FlashInfer (anything but SM90/SM100-class). The norm that receives the sum undoes the 2^-k prescale itself. For the quantized case this happens inside the existing Triton norm kernel, so there's no extra launch, and the result is bit-identical to unscaling first. On the 27B, decode at batch 1 is 0.7% slower with the flag. A simpler version that kept the all-reduce in the layers cost 3.3%, because this path runs without torch.compile and the unscale became a separate kernel in every layer. With the flag off, or on SM90/SM100, nothing changes. <details> <summary>How it works, tests and numbers</summary> **Change** - `deferred_fp16_partial_sums()` (context manager in `linear.py`): row-parallel layers built inside it with `reduce_results=False` write FP16 partial sums when their kernel can, under the sam

title: [Distributed] Opt-in FP16 partial sums for tensor-parallel row-parallel layers
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With tensor parallelism every row-parallel layer (`o_proj`, `down_proj`, linear-attention `out_proj`) rounds its per-rank partial sum to BF16 before the all-reduce, while a single GPU rounds the full sum once. The extra rounding is small on average but explodes where the two halves cancel, which is frequent: on real Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-14B activations at TP=2, outputs whose error exceeds 1% of the row's RMS occur **4.75x / 5.53x as often as on one GPU**. Converting the BF16 partials to FP32 before the all-reduce (#50972) cannot help at TP=2: the rounding has already happened, and the result is bit-identical. This PR adds `VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS=1` (off by default): the row-parallel GEMM writes its partial sum in FP16 (8x finer than BF16, same bytes on the wire), the all-reduce runs in FP16, and the output is rounded to BF16 once, after the sum, as on one GPU; an exact power-of-two prescale (2^-2 by default) keeps partial sums far from the FP16 range limit. The large-error events return to the single-GPU level, and the BF16 output gets measurably closer to an FP32 reference than both TP=2 today and TP=1. The cost is up to ~1% in throughput, plus a higher activation peak in the unquantized path (see Tradeoffs). **Not a duplicate of #50972.** That PR upcasts the BF16 partial sums to FP32 before the all-reduce; at TP=2 this is bit-identical to today (`bf16(a) + bf16(b)` is exact in FP32), because the extra rounding happens earlier, when each rank's GEMM writes BF16. This PR changes the precision of the partial sums themselves. Related:

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Synthetic acceptance: verify from the target argmax without full-vocab logits
summary: ## Overview With `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"`, acceptance comes from fixed per-position rates, but MRV2 verification still gathers full-vocabulary target logits, copies them to FP32 in `apply_sampling_params`, and runs the four rejection kernels. The kernel draws the same acceptance stream and writes the argmax as the recovery/bonus token. ## Claims - Synthetic-acceptance verification no longer builds `[num_logits, vocab]` logits when nothing needs them. title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Gather only the sampled rows after a token-sharded step
summary: ## Overview On a token-sharded step (#63085, #63254) Muse Spark all-gathers the final hidden states of every token, but the runner reads only the rows at `logits_indices`. With this PR, Muse Spark provides its own Model Runner V2 state (`get_model_state_cls`). That state passes `logits_indices` to steps that may shard, and `TokenShard.gather_rows` all-gathers only those rows. There is no flag. The model runner is not changed. ## Claims - On a token-sharded step the final all-gather moves `world * num_sampled` rows instead of `num_tokens` rows. `num_sampled` is the number of sampled rows: one per request, plus the draft tokens being verified. - The sampled rows are bitwise those of the full gather. The other rows are zero, and nothing reads them. - The full gather is kept when something reads the other rows: - a request in the batch asks for prompt logprobs (`prompt_logprobs` or `prompt_logprob_token_ids`); - the drafter reads the final hidden states (a speculator without aux hidden states); - microbatching (`use_ubatching`) is on. - Decode and CUDA graph steps are unchanged. title: [Frontend] Report time to first content token in per-request metrics
summary: ## Summary Adds the optional `time_to_first_content_token_ms` field to the existing `PerRequestMetrics` response object for Chat Completions, Completions, and Responses. ## Motivation For reasoning workloads, TTFT measures the first generated output, which may be reasoning or control output rather than final-answer content. It therefore does not indicate when the answer starts. `time_to_first_content_token_ms` supports per-request monitoring and diagnosis: identifying requests that exceed answer-start latency targets, evaluating the impact of prompts and reasoning effort, and comparing models and deployment configurations. Aggregate timing and token counts cannot reliably reconstruct this boundary. Streaming clients can measure content arrival, but that includes transport and buffering; non-streaming clients cannot observe the boundary directly. Returning this optional metric provides consistent server-side visibility without requiring each client to implement separate instrumentation. ## Behavior - With a response parser, the new field measures from scheduling until the first engine output batch in which the parser emits final-answer content. - Timing has engine output-batch resolution. - Without a response parser, it equals `time_to_first_token_ms`. - It is `null` when the parser emits no final content or the boundary cannot be determined. - Chat Completions streaming reports metrics only on the final usage chunk, which requires `stream_options.include_usage` or `--enable-force-include-usage`. - Responses streaming reports metrics only on `response.completed`. - Existing
