title: [Bugfix][Muse Spark] Keep the FP32 RoPE tables in FP32
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `RotaryEmbedding.forward_cuda` and the AITER branch of `forward_hip` call `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype`, which replaces an FP32 cos/sin table with a copy in the query's dtype (eager), or casts the whole table on every call or uses a BF16 copy (compiled). Muse Spark builds FP32 RoPE tables, so its DSpark context-key precompute and the unfused attention branch of the AMD and NVIDIA attention rotated BF16 Q/K with a BF16 table. The CUDA/HIP `rotary_embedding` op and the AITER Triton RoPE kernel take the table dtype and the Q/K dtype independently, compute in FP32, and write Q/K-dtype outputs. This PR passes `self.cos_sin_cache` as is in those two paths when it is on the query's device, and keeps the helper for an actual device mismatch. AITER's paired op needs a key, so calls with `key=None` go through `forward_cuda`. The Muse Spark attention already calls `self.rotary_emb.forward_cuda(positions, q, k)`. The DSpark context-key precompute (`amd/dspark.py` and `nvidia/dspark.py`) called the module, which dispatches to `forward_native` when the RoPE custom op is disabled (the default for compiled models, e.g. ROCm without breakable CUDA graphs), and `forward_native` still replaces the table. It now calls `self._rotary_emb.forward_cuda(positions, k, None)` in the same way, so the table stays FP32 in every configuration. It still goes through the module's own method and table, not the op directly. This follows @mawong-amd's review and his validation branch ([ROCm/vllm@c43b68aa](https://github.com/ROCm/vllm/commit/c43b68aa02bfc049649928d0f567

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Re-save the block that straddles a chunked-prefill boundary in host-buffer mode
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview In NIXL host-buffer mode (TPU, or `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`), a chunked prefill that ends inside a block leaves that block for the next chunk to finish, but the block is never copied to the host buffer again. The decode instance (D) then reads stale KV for up to `block_size - 1` tokens per chunk boundary, with no error. This PR makes `_build_save_meta` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`) select blocks by token position, in the block table the scheduler resolves for each scheduled request (#54853), so the straddling block is copied again once it is complete. ## Claims - Each chunk copies the blocks covering `[saved, num_computed + num_scheduled)`. A block that straddles a chunk boundary falls in both ranges, so it is copied again once complete. Example (block size 16, budget 24, 40-token prompt): on main, step 1 copies b0 and b1 with b1 half written, and step 2 copies only b2, so tokens 24-31 never reach the host buffer; with this PR, step 2 copies b1 and b2. - Spec-decode lookahead blocks are copied only once written (ovidiusm's review). - A first chunk after a local prefix-cache hit still copies the cached blocks. - A preempted request starts over when it comes back. It arrives with its whole block table (`is_full_table`, from #60810), so its save starts again at token 0. - Chunked local attention groups are saved by position too (xuechendi's review). A `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group needs nothing extra: `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` gives the scheduler one of its layer specs, which already takes this path. - SSM state with `mamba_ca

summary: ## Overview Stacked on #66742 (which stacks on #66741). Adds a FlyDSL causal extend kernel for `ROCM_AITER_FA` on gfx950. It reads the paged fp8 e4m3 KV cache directly and covers both full-attention and sliding-window layers with head size 64, 8 query heads per KV head and 16-token blocks. title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: FP8 rows on the token-sharded all-gathers
summary: ## Overview On token-sharded steps (#63085), `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_TSP_FP8_AG=1` sends the attention input and the pooled expert input through the TP all-gather as FP8 rows with one fp32 scale per row. This halves the bytes of the two largest gathers. The gathered rows have a relative error of 0.027 against BF16. - The quantization adds no kernel on the attention side: the residual-boundary kernel that already computes the pre-attention norm also writes the FP8 rows and their scales. title: [MoE] Add VLLM_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE to opt out of FlashInfer fused finalize
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #66904. FlashInfer's CUTLASS MoE (`cutlass_fused_moe`) takes `use_fused_finalize`, defaulting to `True`: GEMM2 may reduce the top-k expert outputs with atomics in its epilogue, which FlashInfer documents as not run-to-run deterministic, with `False` selecting the deterministic finalize path. `FlashInferExperts` never passed the argument, so vLLM users could not opt out. This PR adds `VLLM_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE`: - unset (default): the argument is not passed, so FlashInfer's own default applies (including newer FlashInfer policies that derive it from `torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()`); no behavior change; - `0`: pass `use_fused_finalize=False` (deterministic finalize); - `1`: pass `use_fused_finalize=True`. The value is read once in `FlashInferExperts.__init__`. FlashInfer already includes the flag in its MoE runner and autotune cache keys, so tuned tactics for the two settings do not mix. The pinned `flashinfer-python==0.7.3` accepts the argument (present since 0.7.0). ## Test Plan - `tests/test_envs.py::test_flashinfer_moe_fused_finalize_tristate`: unset → `None`, `0` → `False`, `1` → `True`. - Import check of the patched module against the FlashInfer in a vLLM image: `use_fused_finalize` is in `cutlass_fused_moe`'s signature. - End-to-end on DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B NVFP4, with an equivalent local patch (see #66904): two independently built autotune caches per setting, 4 restarts each, greedy 32-token completion compared. ## Test Result - Unit test passes. - With `use_fused_finalize=False`, all 8 restar

title: [RFC][Prototype] Snapshot post-processed model weights to skip checkpoint loading on restart
summary: ## [RFC][Prototype] Snapshot post-processed model weights to skip checkpoint loading on restart ### Purpose On restart, vLLM re-reads the safetensors checkpoint and re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` even when nothing changed. This draft adds an opt-in snapshot of the post-processed model state. The first start saves it; later starts build the model with dummy weights (same structure) and copy the saved bytes back with O_DIRECT reads, skipping checkpoint parsing and weight conversion. ### Usage | Env var | Meaning | |---|---| | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_DIR` | Enables the feature; one snapshot file per rank in this directory. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_AUDIT=1` | After a restore, log live CUDA storages the snapshot did not cover (state a model keeps outside module attributes). | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_SKIP_FUNCS` | Comma-separated `module:function` list of pure, expensive weight-preparation functions whose output the snapshot overwrites; skipped on restore (see below). Empty by default. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_CLEAR=1` | Delete this rank's snapshot files in the directory (all keys) and load normally without saving. One-shot: applies on every start while set. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_REBUILD=1` | Delete this rank's snapshot for the current key, load normally and save a fresh one. One-shot like CLEAR; mutually exclusive with it. | The file key is built from the settings that shape the post-processed weights: checkpoint identity (HF `repo@commit` plus a `config.json` digest, or weight file names/sizes for local directories), dtype, quantization, hf_overrides, KV cache dtyp

title: [HiSparse] Stage only top-k host rows; gather resident rows in one kernel
summary: ## Purpose When a HiSparse batch has any prefill context that isn't fully on GPU, every prefill layer stages **every block of every prefill context**: resident rows are copied device-to-device, and host rows are read over PCIe. That cost scales with context length, not chunk length. On the proxy below, a 24-token chunk staged 36K context tokens. This PR: 1. **Stages host rows by top-k.** A prefill reads host rows only for the blocks its top-k references. A fused Triton kernel marks the referenced blocks. It returns immediately on device when the plan has no host rows. Resident rows are always copied, because marking costs more than copying them when the top-k is spread out. 2. **Gathers resident rows faster.** One Triton kernel replaces the indexed-copy path on CUDA: about 1.4 TB/s vs about 160 GB/s. That's 0.578 → 0.111 ms per layer at 128K context and 2.16 → 0.31 ms at 512K. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py ``` New or extended tests: - `test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows[mask_blocks]`: host rows of unreferenced blocks are not read. - `test_hisparse_prefill_stages_only_topk_referenced_blocks` - `test_hisparse_cuda_resident_gather_copies_rows_and_skips_misses` **End-to-end (4× B200).** - Model and server: GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 128`. title: [Performance][EPLB] Skip unchanged layers in async transfer cycles
summary: ## Summary - Skip async EPLB weight transfers for layers whose physical-to-logical expert mapping is unchanged. - Mark the final changed layer explicitly so a cycle no longer depends on the model's physical last layer. - Publish a no-transfer completion result when every layer is unchanged, preserving the existing cross-rank/main-thread acknowledgement path. Fixes #51791. ## Root cause and impact The async worker previously iterated over every MoE layer after rebalancing. Even when a layer's mapping was unchanged, it still performed the coordinated stop check, entered `transfer_layer()`, synchronized the CUDA stream, published a result, and waited for acknowledgement. Sparse mapping changes therefore cost `O(L)` layer handshakes instead of `O(K)`, where `K` is the number of changed layers. ## Performance Host-side control-flow benchmark: 64 MoE layers, 5,000 cycles, nine repeats. | Changed layers | Transfers before → after | Median cycle before → after | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 0 | 64 → 0 | 77.44 → 5.23 µs | | 1 | 64 → 1 | 77.71 → 6.04 µs | | 4 | 64 → 4 | 78.16 → 9.79 µs | | 64 | 64 → 64 | 77.99 → 84.83 µs | The benchmark executes the production worker control flow with counting CPU fakes. It verifies operation counts but does not measure CUDA, NCCL/Gloo/NIXL, or end-to-end serving throughput. ## Correctness and tests The regression test compares the optimized path with the legacy all-layer reference using exact expert-weight tensors and physical-to-logical maps (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`). title: [Feature]: vllm.Inference: retryable KV and EC load errors
summary: ### The feature, motivation and pitch Gateways that tokenize once at ingress render each request in a `vllm-rs render` sidecar (#65503). They then call `encode`, `prefill`, and `decode` workers over `vllm.Inference` with token IDs. KV and EC load failures look like engine failures in that flow. When a KV load fails (`kv_load_failure_policy: fail`) or the EC connector cannot obtain an encoder input, the scheduler finishes the request with an error. That error carries no `retryable` flag. `vllm.Inference` maps only `retryable` errors to `UNAVAILABLE` (`rust/src/server/src/grpc/convert.rs`), so these failures return `INTERNAL`. A gateway cannot tell when to run `encode` or `prefill` again. **Moved to other issues:** this issue first listed two more items. #66093 tracks metadata-only and mixed media sources on `vllm.Inference`. #67653 tracks the render fingerprint check. **Proposal:** - Set `error.retryable = true` in the scheduler for KV load failures and unavailable EC inputs. `vllm.Inference` then returns `UNAVAILABLE` for them. - The error that #66928 adds for an uncovered metadata-only item needs the same flag. PRs: #67604 (open draft) sets the flag for KV load failures and unavailable EC inputs. ### Alternatives - Retry every `INTERNAL` error in the gateway. Engine bugs then run again as often as transient transfer failures. ### Additional context - **Split from:** #65503. - **Consumers:** `llm-d` Coordinator (`Coord-Text-Tok`, `Coord-Tok-Tok`) and `pd-sidecar` (llm-d/llm-d-router#3992, llm-d/llm-d-router#3993). - **Related:** #66093, #66928, #67653, #40978, #41929. ### B

title: [Perf][KV Connector] Serve Mooncake store lookups from a separate process
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Mooncake store prefix lookups run on a thread in worker rank 0 and hold the GIL for the whole lookup, including inside the native `batch_is_exist` RPC, so long prompts stall rank 0's GPU launches. This PR serves them from a separate process with its own lookup-only store client, so a lookup never takes the worker's GIL. Related: #65702 makes the in-worker lookup ~3.5x cheaper; it still runs in the worker, and reports the lookup thread holding the GIL for 18% of the P workers' wall time on GLM-5.3-Flash 2P1D. This PR is complementary: it moves the remaining work (the Python key building and the native RPC, which #65702 cannot remove) off the worker. The two compose; whichever lands second needs a small rebase. ## Claims - A launch-bound worker thread is no longer stalled by lookups: with 30K keys per lookup at 20 lookups/s, the in-worker path cuts its throughput by 35% with stalls up to 30 ms; the lookup process removes this entirely (0 stalls > 2 ms). - End to end, on a lookup-heavy agentic workload (long prompts, 15 KV cache groups, 64-token blocks; TP4 on GB200), output throughput rises 9-14% and mean ITL drops 7-14%: the GPU-step stall and the slowed scheduler steps from rank 0's GIL both go away. - Same lookup results: identical code (moved, not changed), verified by an end-to-end shadow comparison on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (388 lookups, 0 mismatches) and a new integration test against a real Mooncake master. - No user-facing config changes. title: [Kernel] Cap fused 4-bit GPTQ split-K fan-in
summary: ## Overview Cap the fused 4-bit GPTQ kernel's split-K launch at four blocks and make each block stride over multiple 128-row K tiles. At `K=4096`, this reduces output atomic fan-in from 32 blocks to four. This also includes the lazy `temp_dq` allocation change. This is a draft for design review. Four is not yet a tuned cap, and no performance claim is made. ## Claims - Each 4-bit block reinitializes its packed weights, scales, zero-points, and activation pointers for every assigned K tile. - FP32 accumulators persist across tiles, and each block emits its output atomic once after its strided walk. - Threads without output columns (partial 512-wide N blocks) stay in the K-tile loop because they own shared activation preload slots and must reach every barrier; their global loads and output stores are predicated on `n < size_n`. - Other bit widths and the reconstruct path are unchanged. - No latency or throughput claim is made. ## Validation Hardware: RTX 5060 Laptop (`sm_120`), CUDA 13.2, torch 2.14. - Nine direct numerical guards cover group sizes 32/64/128/256, `K=4096`, nine K tiles at `K=1152`, a ragged final 32-row tile at `K=1056`, and a partial 512-wide N block at `N=896` (fused path, both sides of `M=50`). The original also passes these guards; this is a performance change, not a wrong-output fix. - Full suite: ```bash .venv/bin/python -P -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_gptq.py -q # 26 passed ``` - The base allocation cases pass for 4-bit Exllama, 8-bit Exllama, and the alternate GPTQ path, including their original fail-before evidence. - A separate 20-case

title: [Kernel] Lower the 4-bit GPTQ reconstruct cutoff to 32 on sm_120
summary: ## Overview On sm_120 (consumer Blackwell), lower the 4-bit GPTQ fused→reconstruct row cutoff from `MAX_Q_GEMM_ROWS = 50` to 32. summary: ## Overview `gptq_gemm` allocates a full `K x N` fp16 reconstruction buffer on every call, including fused Exllama calls that never read it. title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Peer prefix lookup-and-pin (RFC 65967)
summary: ## Overview Implements RFC https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65967 (compute-free prefix KV lookup-and-pin for router-driven peer KV reuse), proposed by @briefgaming. The consumer (B) asks the producer (A) over the NIXL side channel to pin the longest cached run of a prefix by block hash. A pins it under a lease and replies with the block ids without computing anything, and B pulls the blocks and computes the rest. This is the engine counterpart to https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/509, which routes a prompt to a less busy engine that fetches the prefix from the engine holding it. The design page is `docs/design/nixl_peer_lookup_pin.md`, linked from the NIXL connector usage guide. The lease and expired-read fix from `vllm-project/vllm#66011` (commit c8e43bb, by Hugo Abonizio) is the first commit here, because the peer pins reuse its lease. This PR targets `main`, so the diff includes that commit. ## Claims - A router can have an idle engine (B) fetch a prefix from the engine that holds it (A) instead of recomputing it, and B's output after a pull matches its own recompute. - The lookup does not compute anything on A, so A's GPU is not spent on a request it did not receive. - A pull is faster than recomputing the prefix on an idle B, and a fetched request under load beats the same request with fetching off in most cases (numbers under Validation). - Nothing changes when `peer_lookup` is off. title: [Bug]: Model Runner V2 dies with cudaErrorContained when the GPU cannot read large pinned host buffers via UVA (M-RoPE prefill positions)
summary: vLLM 0.32.0 (docker vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0), Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, one H100 NVL passed through to a KVM VM, driver 580.159.03. With the default Model Runner V2 the engine dies at the first real request with cudaErrorContained ("Invalid access of peer GPU memory over nvlink or a hardware error", Xid 94 on the host). With CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 the failing kernel is _prepare_rope_positions_kernel, launched from RopeState.prepare_positions (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/rope.py:106). Without CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING the error surfaces in unrelated later kernels (vision encoder profiling, the GDN input projection, cuBLAS), which made it hard to trace. RopeState keeps prefill_positions as a StagedWriteTensor with uva_instead_of_gpu=True, so the kernel reads a (max_num_reqs * 3, max_model_len) int32 buffer, about 200 MB here, directly from pinned host memory. On this machine GPU kernels can read pinned host memory through UVA only for small buffers: a standalone test with get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor reads 4 KB and 4 MB fine and fails with the same cudaErrorContained at 256 MB, while DMA copies from pinned memory work. So the trigger is our VM/IOMMU setup, but MRV2 has no way around it, since is_uva_available() only checks for pinned memory. VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 works around it and the model then runs fine. A switch to disable UVA buffers (the NonUvaBuffer path already exists), or a fallback for buffers this large, would help, and so would a hint in the docs. title: [Core] Add --kv-cache-host-pinned: host-pinned KV cache on integrated GPUs (GB10, Thor)
summary: ## Overview Related: #60844. Add `--kv-cache-host-pinned` (`CacheConfig.kv_cache_host_pinned`): on integrated (unified-memory) GPUs such as GB10 / DGX Spark it is not possible to register buffers for zero-copy RDMA. The switch adds the capability to back the KV cache with host-pinned memory (`cudaHostAlloc`, mapped and write-combined), so the NIXL connector can register it for RDMA (`ibv_reg_mr`) and UCX moves it zero-copy. On 2× DGX Spark this makes the prefill→decode KV transfer **33× faster** at batch 1 (553 → 16.8 ms for 255.9 MB) and cuts TTFT by **39% / 43% / 83%** at batch 1 / 8 / 32. Gated on `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()`, refused everywhere else. ## Claims - On GB10 the KV cache in device memory **cannot be registered for RDMA**: no `nvidia-peermem`, `cuMemGetHandleForAddressRange(DMA_BUF)` returns `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` (`DMA_BUF_SUPPORTED=0`, `GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_SUPPORTED=0`), `ibv_reg_mr` fails with `EFAULT`, and ODP registers lazily but the first transfer hangs. title: [Perf][HiSparse] Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Background I did HiSparse + prefill work on DSv4.1 Flash before, so I had a rough expectation for what prefill should cost with host-backed KV. When I first ran GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 with HiSparse on 8xH20, the prefill numbers looked abnormal to me: much slower than the same model with HiSparse off, and slower than what I expected from the DSv4.1 Flash work. That is why I went through the profile and the sparse-MLA code path instead of accepting it as the price of host-backed KV. The short version is that HiSparse was disabling both attention-level ShardQ and model-level sequence parallelism, so prefill fell back to the split-KV decode-shaped kernel and the indexer scored every token on every rank. This PR fixes that. Along the way I hit a separate precision problem; it is not caused by this change and is fixed in #67882, which is merged. I want to be upfront about coverage: I only validated on H20 + GLM-5.3-W4AFP8. The code path is shared by other HiSparse sparse-MLA models (DeepSeek V3.2 shares this model implementation) and `sparse_mla_shard_q` defaults to true, so the blast radius is larger than what I actually ran. Dense models, FlashInfer sparse and non-HiSparse runs are unchanged; GLM-5.3-Flash uses a separate implementation and is out of scope; I did not validate other hardware, other quantization settings, or multi-node performance; I did add a final-tree serving matrix (44K c1-c16 and 128K c1/c4) and one mixed 1024-output check below, but they cover only the configurations described there, not the full space. title: [Usage]: Whisper large-v3, lower concurrent transcription throughput on H100 than A100 80GB

title: [Bugfix] TP ranks agree on the sampler backend and refuse mismatched sampling config
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #66912. Every TP rank samples on the all-gathered logits and feeds **its own** sampled tokens into the next step; only TP rank 0's tokens reach the user, and nothing compares the ranks. So if ranks sample differently they silently continue on different tokens: rank 1 writes KV for a token the user never sees, and its head shard keeps feeding the all-reduce. #66912 reproduces two ways to get there with no error: a rank falling back from the FlashInfer top-k/top-p sampler (e.g. FlashInfer JIT failing on one node) and a `--headless` node started with a different `--seed`. This PR makes both impossible, with no per-step cost: - **Collective sampler choice.** A fused sampler (FlashInfer, XPU) is used only if every TP rank can use it: a MIN all-reduce on the TP CPU group when the `Sampler` is built. A rank that can use it but whose peer cannot logs a warning and falls back with the others. A rank whose explicit opt-in (`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`) cannot be honoured still raises as before, but only after voting, so its peers do not wait on it. - **Startup consistency check.** The TP ranks all-gather the sampling-relevant settings (`seed`, data-parallel index, logprobs mode, fp64 Gumbel, the chosen backends) and refuse to start if they differ, naming the field and the per-rank values. Both are one-time collectives at `Sampler` construction, which happens on every rank of the last PP stage's TP group. Nothing is added per step. title: [Determinism] Canonical sparse-indexer top-k: deterministic set and order behind VLLM_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK
summary: ## Purpose **How to review.** The kernel is one file, `vllm/model_executor/layers/canonical_topk.py` (about 200 lines: three Triton kernels, threshold / counts / ordered write, no host synchronization). Wiring: the decode top-k in `indexer_topk.py` (39 lines), the shared prefill in `sparse_attn_indexer.py` (17), the fused-MQA eligibility rule (7), the GLM-5.x-Next and Qwen4Exp indexers (12), the env var. Tests: `tests/kernels/test_canonical_topk.py`. Off by default; part of the series in #66873, independent of #66526. The radix top-k kernels behind the sparse-attention indexer (`persistent_topk`, `cooperative_topk`, the filtered path; used by DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1, GLM-5.x, Kimi-K3, Qwen4Exp QSA and others) take output slots with `atomicAdd`. So the **order** of the selected indices depends on thread scheduling, and so does the **set** when several scores tie with the k-th one: the last pass keeps whichever tied candidates reach the remaining slots first (`csrc/persistent_topk.cuh`, `atomicAdd(&shared_final_k, -1)`; same pattern in the filtered path and in `cooperative_topk`'s `counter_eq`). The sparse attention then sums over the selected indices in that order. This PR adds an opt-in canonical form, `VLLM_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK=1` (also on with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`): after the top-k, a Triton post-pass rewrites the result so that it depends only on the scores. It keeps every candidate scoring above the k-th score, then the **lowest-index** candidates that tie with it, all in **ascending index order**. Scores are compared by value: -0.0 ties with +0.0 and every NaN ranks

title: [Perf][Sampling] Gather vocab-parallel logits into their final layout in one pass
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With a vocab-parallel LM head (TP > 1), every sampled step moves the logits three times: 1. `LogitsProcessor` gathers them with a last-dim all-gather. NCCL fills a rank-major `[world, rows, vocab/world]` buffer. 2. `movedim` + `reshape` copies that into the vocab-major `[rows, vocab]` layout, which is a slow strided copy, and the vocab padding is sliced off. 3. In Model Runner V2, the sampler copies the logits once more into a new FP32 tensor before applying temperature, top-k/top-p and logits processors. For a 200k vocabulary at 256 rows (DSpark K=7 verify at concurrency 32), that is 102 MB gathered, 205 MB re-laid out and 307 MB copied to FP32 on every rank, per step. This PR changes this only for models that opt in (MiniMax-M3 / M3.1), and only in Model Runner V2's target logits. Every other model, every draft head and Model Runner V1 keep main's gather and the samplers' FP32 copy unchanged. - **`all_gather_vocab_parallel_logits`** (`logits_processor.py`) gathers along rows, which needs no copy, then writes the final `[rows, vocab]` layout with one Triton kernel. That kernel also cuts off the padding and casts to the requested dtype. The kernel is compiled once per output dtype (not per row count), and the gather stays off the dim-0 symmetric-memory route (`VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM`), which would add a scratch buffer and a full-size clone. - **The request travels in the forward context, not on the model.** `ForwardContext` gets one field, `logits_gather_dtype`. `LogitsProcessor` uses the fused gather on CUDA only when that field is

title: [RFC]: Replicate selected blocks across TP ranks for tensor parallelism over slow inter-node links
summary: ### Motivation Tensor parallelism across nodes linked by commodity Ethernet (25 GbE RoCE between workstations or DGX Spark-class boxes) pays one all-reduce per block per step. At decode batch sizes that all-reduce is latency-bound: we measured about 66 us for TP4 and 36-40 us for TP2 over 25 GbE at batch 1 (inside a CUDA graph), against 2-3 us on one PCIe node. That is the same order as reading a mixer's weights from HBM, so for some blocks it is cheaper to keep the block whole on every rank (replicate it) and skip its all-reduce than to shard it. Replicating a block costs each rank (1 - 1/TP) x W extra bytes of resident weights and of reads per step, and saves one all-reduce. With weight bandwidth BW and all-reduce time t_AR(T) for a step of T tokens, it pays when (1 - 1/TP) x W / BW < t_AR(T). Prefill matters: under steady load each prompt is prefilled inside other requests' decode steps, and those steps carry multi-MB all-reduces, which is why replication gains most at high concurrency. ### Proposal 1. **Per-model opt-in replication of selected blocks** (attention, linear-attention/Mamba mixers, FFN), built on `disable_tp=True` for the block's linear layers and skipping the block's all-reduce. Each model declares which blocks can be replicated; MoE experts, embeddings and lm_head stay sharded. title: [Bugfix][Batch Invariance] Keep top logprobs independent of other requests' logprobs
summary: ## Overview With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a request's top logprobs depend on how many logprobs the other requests in its batch ask for. The sampler takes one `torch.topk` over the batch with `k` set to the largest `logprobs` in it, and `torch.topk` orders tied logits differently for different `k`. When two tokens tie for a rank, the token reported at that rank changes between "alone" and "batched". The sampled tokens and logprob values are unchanged. Ties are common with bf16 logits. Running the existing `alone vs. batched` check with one target at `logprobs=1` and neighbours at `logprobs=5` (L4, nightly `092b7aaa6`), 4 of 7 configurations differ: Qwen3-0.6B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-1B-FP8-dynamic and Qwen2.5-0.5B compiled. This PR re-sorts the top-k when batch invariance is on: by token id, then stably by logit descending. Tied logits then come out lowest id first for every `k`. ## Claims - With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a request's top logprobs no longer depend on the other requests' `logprobs`. Tied tokens are listed lowest id first. - Nothing changes when batch invariance is off. - Cost: two sorts over a `[batch, k]` tensor. Measured `topk(20)` on L4 at vocab 151936: 0.105 → 0.240 ms (B=1), 0.297 → 0.332 ms (B=64), 3.218 → 3.263 ms (B=256). A full stable sort of the vocab would also be correct, but it costs 31.7 ms and an extra 1.2 GiB at B=256. - `torch.topk` already keeps the lowest ids among values tied at the k-th position. Only the order inside the top-k depends on `k`. On logits rounded to create many ties (including at the k-th value), sorting the top-k this way

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Default the Mamba ssm state cache to float32
summary: ## Overview With `--mamba-cache-dtype` and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` both on `auto`, Mamba layers keep their ssm state in the model dtype, which is bfloat16 for most checkpoints. Decode rounds the state to that dtype on every token, so the log-probs it reports drift from the ones the same engine computes when it prefills the same tokens, and the drift grows with the sequence. This PR makes float32 the default for the ssm state of Mamba layers, the default NemotronH already gets per architecture (#39032, #63218). Fixes #68338. Not a duplicate: I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype`, "ssm state float32", "mamba state dtype", "recurrent state dtype", "Falcon-H1" and "decode prefill mismatch mamba". Related work that does something else: #39032 and #63218 set this default for NemotronH only. RFC #55524 and #55627 keep the Mamba2 state in fp32 under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, where decode replays the chunk to be bit-identical with prefill; the RFC's kernel-level evidence already notes that a bf16 state adds an error that grows with position. This PR changes the default outside that mode and does not aim at bit-identity. #54123 rejects unsupported explicit Mamba1 combinations; #61245 and #66686 make KDA honour the option; #54146 fixes the GDN readout for an fp32 state. ## Claims - **New default.** With both options on `auto`, Mamba layers store the ssm state in float32. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep the most likely candidate's logprob when /v1/completions top_logprobs keys collide
summary: ## Overview `/v1/completions` keys `top_logprobs` by decoded string, so when candidates decode to the same string (byte fragments all decode to `""`), the last one in engine order overwrites the sampled token's entry and `top_logprobs[i][tokens[i]] != token_logprobs[i]`. This PR keeps the highest logprob among the candidates that share a string in both `/v1/completions` and `/v1/completions/derender`. A tie keeps the earlier candidate, which is the sampled token. Fixes #65726 ## Claims - In `/v1/completions` (streaming and non-streaming, including echoed prompt positions), `top_logprobs[i][tokens[i]] == token_logprobs[i]` now holds whenever the token at that position is the most likely of the candidates that share its string. That includes every greedy position, so it covers every case in #65726. On main it breaks when a later candidate shares the token's string. - `max(top_logprobs[i].values())` is now the logprob of the most likely returned candidate wherever `top_logprobs[i]` is not `None`, so a greedy check that reads it (as lm-evaluation-harness does) sees the text of the most likely returned candidate. - Barring exact ties between different candidates, no position is worse than on main for either check. Main keeps the token's own entry only when no other candidate shares its string, and then this PR keeps it too. - `/v1/completions/derender` returns the same `top_logprobs` as the coupled endpoint for these positions. - Only the value of a colliding key changes. Keys, key order, entry count, `tokens` and `text_offset` are the same as before in all cases. ## Validation

title: [Core] KV cache: block-range eviction for live requests
summary: ## Purpose Add a primitive to free a block-aligned range of KV cache from a request that is still running. Today blocks are only freed when a request finishes; a long-running streaming-input session (#28973) therefore grows its KV without bound. This PR adds the missing operation, with no policy attached and no consumer yet in-tree — the retention policy that uses it follows in the next PR of this series (RFC #51948). I split it out because it is the only part that touches the KV-cache managers, so it can be reviewed on its own. Three layers, matching the existing KV stack: - `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.evict_blocks_for_request(request_id, block_ids) -> int`: removes the given blocks from a live request's block table, returns them to the free pool, and removes them from the prefix-cache index so their old content can never be matched by another request. Keeps `num_cached_block` consistent. Returns how many blocks were actually reclaimed — a block still shared with another request is dropped from this request's table but not counted, since its memory is not free. - `KVCacheCoordinator.evict_blocks_for_request`: fan-out per group, same as the other coordinator methods. - `KVCacheManager.evict_token_range_for_request(request_id, start, end) -> (aligned_start, aligned_end, num_freed)`: the caller-facing form. Callers think in tokens, memory lives in blocks, so the range is rounded INWARD to whole blocks and the function returns the range it actually freed. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Decline remote prefill reads after the producer's KV lease expired
summary: ## Overview In P/D disaggregation with `NixlConnector`, the decode (consumer) could issue the NIXL read of a request whose KV blocks the prefill (producer) had already released and recycled because its lease ran out. The read succeeds and silently loads other requests' KV cache and SSM state. This reuses the deadline gate that already protects the bidirectional turn-2 readback and applies it to every remote-prefill read, with an exact model of the lease renewals the consumer's own heartbeats cause. Fixes #66009. ## Claims - A consumer never reads KV blocks past the producer's lease deadline (minus a safety margin of `min(5 s, kv_lease_duration / 6)`). The read is declined, counted in the new consumer-side counter `vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads`, reported as `failed_recving`, and the request follows `kv_load_failure_policy`: with the default `fail` it finishes with an error, with `recompute` it is prefilled locally. Before this change such a read loaded recycled memory with no error at all. - Requests that waited inside the consumer's scheduler keep working: the consumer keeps an exact model of the producer's lease as renewed by the heartbeats it sent (the scheduler ships the exported deadline and `remote_lease_extension` with each heartbeat batch, and the worker applies the producer's own renewal rule to it), so reads after long but heartbeated waits are not declined. A request is heartbeated at the first scheduler step after D starts tracking it rather than at the next periodic round, since a router may already have held it for most of its lease. title: [Bugfix] Don't re-append default custom ops on every `replace()`
summary: Update: a second commit (1a21913) widens the fix after a review pass. It adds `CompilationConfig.enable_custom_op_by_default()`, uses it for the `quant_fp8` default and in the ROCm platform defaults, which had the same problem, and deletes the duplicate `quant_fp8` block in `__post_init__`. The sections below describe both commits. ## Overview `VllmConfig.__post_init__` writes default custom ops into `compilation_config.custom_ops`, and `replace()` re-runs it on a copy that shares the same `CompilationConfig`. Those writes weren't idempotent. The blocked-FP8 `+quant_fp8` default was appended on every run, from two identical blocks, and on ROCm `apply_config_platform_defaults` appended `+sparse_attn_indexer` (and, depending on the AITER and batch-invariance settings, `+quant_fp8` and `+rms_norm`) again on every run. So the compile hash of a config changed every time it was copied. This PR adds `CompilationConfig.enable_custom_op_by_default(op)`, which enables `op` unless `custom_ops` already enables or disables it. The `quant_fp8` default and all five ROCm defaults use it, and the second `quant_fp8` block is gone. ## Claims - For a blocked-FP8 config, `compile_factors()` is the same before and after `replace()`, for the copy and for the original. - `flashinfer_autotune_cache_hash` returns the same name every time it is called on a runner. - The same holds on ROCm, where the platform defaults now go through the same method. This one is from reading the code; I haven't run it on ROCm. ## Validation Test `test_replace_keeps_compile_factors_with_blocked_fp8_weights`, CPU, offlin

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Split decodes off the AITER FlashKDA prefill on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 has 34 KDA layers. On MI355X (gfx950) at TP4, `main` runs their prefill through vLLM's Triton chunk path and their decode through a chain of Triton kernels. This PR is stacked on #63568, which routes the prefill recurrence to AITER FlashKDA, and #63612, which runs plain decode steps as one AITER kernel. It carries both and adds three changes on top. FlashKDA counts each decode in a mixed step as a sequence when it plans its recurrence, so with four or more decodes it stops segmenting the prefill's recurrence (A). `f_b` and `g_b` run as two small GEMMs (B). Those compiles hit mostly this PR's arm: with A, FlashKDA gets views of the state indices that start after the step's decodes. Each compile stalls the whole engine step, for every request in it. title: [ROCm][Quantization] Add int8 lm_head quantization (per-channel and per-group-32) for RDNA (gfx11/gfx12)
summary: Follows #62708 (merged), which added online lm_head quantization with `int4_per_group_32_asym`. This PR adds two int8 weight-only lm_head formats: - `int8_per_channel_static`: symmetric int8 with one scale per output channel. - `int8_per_group_32`: symmetric int8 with one scale per 32 input channels. ```bash vllm serve <model> --quantization-config '{"targets": {"re:.*lm_head$": {"weight": "int8_per_channel_static"}}}' vllm serve <model> --quantization-config '{"targets": {"re:.*lm_head$": {"weight": "int8_per_group_32"}}}' ``` The regex target also matches multimodal wrappers, whose head is `language_model.lm_head` (e.g. Qwen3.6, Gemma-4); a bare `"lm_head"` target only matches a module named exactly `lm_head`. Many 4-bit checkpoints leave the lm_head in fp16/bf16. Decode reads the whole head on every step, so on bandwidth-bound GPUs it is often one of the largest per-token costs. Int8 halves that read. Int4 (#62708) cuts it further, but int8 keeps the logits at the bf16 level, which lets users trade speed against accuracy. `int8_per_group_32` gives up 0.1–1.6 % of TPOT against `int8_per_channel_static` for 38 % fewer flipped top-1 tokens. **Hardware:** all testing, benchmarks and evals below were run on gfx1151 (Strix Halo) only. The kernel is enabled for gfx11/gfx12 like #62708's int4 path, but has not been validated on other RDNA GPUs. ## Design This follows #62708: the format code is hardware-agnostic and the kernel is chosen by `choose_mp_linear_kernel`. - **Formats** (`online/int8.py`): `Int8PerChannelLMHeadMethod` and `Int8PerGroup32LMHeadMethod` subclass `OnlineLMH

title: [RFC]: [KV Offload] Request-level KV promotions: decide at promotion time, pin until load
summary: ### Problem A hit is decided at lookup time, but secondary tiers allocate CPU slots later, at `materialize()`, possibly several steps later. That gap causes stale budgets, over-commit, lifetime bans after a failed promotion, promotions that evict their own or each other's hits, and over-size hits that cannot be partially loaded (#62931). This RFC replaces the v3–v5 sketches in #62932. ### Goals 1. **No wasted promotions.** A promotion never evicts chunks another request has pinned. 2. **Decide at promotion time.** Resolve promoted keys against the live tiers when the transfer starts. 3. **All or nothing per request.** A request pins and allocates its whole hit in one step, or none. 4. **Clean layering.** The connector knows KV groups; the manager knows tiers and capacity. 5. **Never worse than recompute.** A hit that cannot be served prefills. 6. **One policy** for promotion admission and retries. ### Non-goals - Shrinking an over-size hit (#62931); optional follow-up. - Changing tier I/O paths, store eviction, or cascade scheduling. - The prefetch and retry policies themselves. ### Design **Poll (scheduler thread).** The connector computes the longest group-consistent candidate. The manager classifies each key with `lookup()`, which checks the primary tier and then the allowed secondary tiers: - primary `HIT` → resident; - primary `HIT_PENDING` → present, not readable (a primary write or promotion in flight); - primary `MISS` → ask the allowed secondary tiers: a `HIT` there is a secondary copy (also reported as `HIT_PENDING`), a `RETRY` defers the walk, and no copy is a `M

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: fix the gfx1151 bf16 tile cliff at decode-sized M (up to +44% decode throughput)
summary: ## Summary On gfx1151, bf16 W4A16 Triton layers have a tile cliff at decode-sized M. The existing prefill-tuned tiles are especially slow at M=33..64 for wide-N layers and at M=65..128 for g32 tall-K layers. This PR adds gfx1151 bf16 decode-sized-M tile selection for M=9..128. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] Fix the decode glue crash with preshuffled MXFP8 weights
summary: ## Overview #67072 broke MiniMax-M3.1 on MI355X at TP4. The server crashes at startup. This PR fixes it. ## Cause #65479 added `AiterFlyDSLMxfp8LinearKernel`. This kernel shuffles each MXFP8 linear weight in place (16x16 layout) and views its scales as E8M0. The M3.1 decode glue from #67072 still reads these weights as row-major: 1. `fp8_rows()` builds the glue's shared-expert copies from the shuffled weight. 2. Above 72 rows, `shared_decode()` gives the shuffled weight and the E8M0 scales to vLLM's Triton `dot_scaled` GEMM. Triton fails at the 192-row warmup: ``` File ".../minimax_m3/amd/glue/shared.py", line 196, in shared_decode return _mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm(a_q, a_s, dn.weight, dn.weight_scale, OUT_DTYPE) KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu' ``` ## Fix 1. `fp8_rows()` reads the weight through `row_major_weight()`, as the DSpark drafter already does. 2. The glue uses the Triton down GEMM only when the layer's weight is row-major with uint8 scales. Otherwise it uses the AITER GEMM on its own copy. ## Validation MI355X, TP4, `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, DSpark 7, AITER v0.1.29, GSM8K through `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --apply_chat_template`: | Code | Server start | GSM8K (flexible / strict) | | -- | -- | -- | | main 748f1ab35 | crash (`KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu'`) | - | | main 748f1ab35 + this PR | OK, decode glue on at 24-192 rows | 0.8332 / 0.8180 | `glue/shared.py` is the same on the current main. summary: ## Overview GLM-5.3-Flash builds its attention projections (KDA, MLA, DSA indexer) with `quant_config=None`, so online quantization requested with `--quantization-config '{"targets": ...}'` silently skips them. This PR passes the model's quant config to these modules, so they follow the checkpoint's own skip list and the online targets, as other models do. The one special case is the MLA projections of FP8 / Quark checkpoints, which the model already dequantizes to BF16 at load. Related: #59833, #55741 (see Details). ## Claims - **Online quantization now reaches the BF16 attention projections** when `--quantization-config` names them. title: [Core] Session-based retention and lookup for the prefix cache
summary: ## Overview Requests that carry a `session_id` have the cached blocks they use evicted after all other cached blocks, and the session's next turn finds those blocks without a cache lookup per block. On by default with a 600 s TTL (`--session-cache-ttl`, `0` disables). Requests without a `session_id` are unaffected. - **Retention** is a timestamp on the block, set when a session request hits or caches it. Nothing is pinned and capacity is unchanged. It covers every KV cache group, so hybrid models keep their Mamba checkpoints. - **Lookup**: the session table records where the previous turn's blocks are. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] All gather in FP4 in TP configs
summary: ## Overview In prefill, all ranks did the same norm, router and shared-expert work on all tokens, and the all-reduce sent bf16 data. Now each rank does this work on a quarter of the tokens and sends FP4 data. Steps spend less time in communication. ## Claims Speed up prefill by reducing comms time in the all gather phase of the all reduce operation. ## Validation MoE half of a layer vs stock: 1024 tokens −9%; 2343 −20%; 14394 −33%. Fused combine + reduce-scatter on top: 2343 189.6→170.3 µs; 5857 469.8→366.0; 14394 1145→853. Eval | With our changes | Baseline (stock main) -- | -- | -- GSM8K (flexible / strict) | 0.846 / 0.831 | 0.844 / 0.826 GPQA-Diamond | 84.09% | 82.68% ## Details Prefill TP4 all reduce comms are bandwidth bound. Currently, we (typically) do a two shot all reduce with RS in bf16 and AG in bf16, preceded by rmsnorm and residual add, and followed by router, topk/sort and quant. This changes the order so we do reduce scatter first. Then on the quarter of the rows held in each GPU we do the rmsnorm and residual add, followed by the router, shared experts and the sorting for MoE and quantizing the activations to fp4. This is followed by an all gather in fp4 of the activations, and the metadata. The shared expert activations remain on the owner ranks. they are added after the subsequent reduce scatter before moving to the next attention layer. This allows us to keep the shared expert output local and not paying the price of all gathering that. Requires AITER #7771. --- <details> <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary> - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skil

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Split-K BF16 router GEMM for gfx950 decode batches
summary: ## Overview On gfx950, GateLinear's tier 6 now runs the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash router GEMM (bf16 [M, 5120] × [384, 5120]ᵀ → fp32) on a split-K Triton kernel for 22 ≤ M ≤ 256, instead of hipBLASLt. title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fail only the request when an adapter cannot be loaded
summary: ## Overview A LoRA adapter that was evicted from the CPU cache is read from disk again inside `execute_model`. If that read fails, for example because the adapter's files are gone, the exception leaves the step and the engine dies, taking every in-flight request with it. This change loads the adapter when its request is admitted instead, so a failed load ends only that request, and it stops loads from evicting an adapter that a running request is using. Related work, none of it a duplicate: - #54839 (issue): `/v1/unload_lora_adapter` never removes the adapter from the engine. Same lifecycle area, different problem. - #67459: keeps an in-place reload across an eviction. It edits `vllm/lora/worker_manager.py` near this change, so one of us will need a small rebase. - #65361 (draft): opt-in group-wide admission and residency for the MoE DP path. It also loads before admitting, as a feature for that path; this PR is a fix on the default path and adds no option. - #67714: an independent fix of mine for LoRA slot starvation, in the same part of `scheduler.py`. The two branches merge cleanly with each other, and I ran the scheduler tests on the merged result. ## Claims - A request whose adapter cannot be loaded gets an HTTP 500 for that request. The engine keeps serving. On main the engine dies. - Loading an adapter, through `/v1/load_lora_adapter`, a resolver, or admission, no longer evicts an adapter that a running request uses. On main it can, and the next step then reads that adapter from disk again. - If the only way to make room in the CPU cache is to evict an adapter in use

title: [Bugfix][Core] Stop starving a request that waits for a LoRA slot
summary: ## Overview With more LoRA adapters in demand than `--max-loras`, a request for an adapter without a slot can wait indefinitely: the scheduler skips it, then keeps admitting later requests for the adapters that already hold the slots, so under steady traffic those slots never free. This change bounds that wait. Related, not a duplicate: #65795 touches the same gate to make skipping blocked requests cheaper, and states that its scheduling decisions match main. It leaves the starvation in place. The two will conflict textually in that block, and I am happy to rebase onto whichever lands first. Also related: #67715 (load LoRA adapters at admission) is an independent fix of mine in the same part of `scheduler.py`. The two branches merge cleanly with each other, and I ran the scheduler tests and the simulation below on the merged result. ## Claims - A request waiting for a LoRA slot now gets one once the running requests of one slot-holding adapter finish, instead of waiting for as long as traffic on the other adapters continues. - Only one adapter is held back while a request waits: the one that has held its slot longest. The other adapters keep batching as before. - In a scheduler-level simulation of three adapters on two slots, all three adapters are served at every load tested, where main serves two and starves the third. Where main already serves all three, the totals are unchanged. - No behavior change when the adapters in demand fit in `--max-loras`, or for requests without an adapter. ## Validation Environment: WSL2, AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, one RTX 4080 SUPER, Python 3.12.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Compose ShardQ with the candidate-only indexer prefill
summary: I measured the candidate-path deployment (#65656) on 8xH20 with TP8: it takes 82.9 s at 1M tokens, and adding the V4.1 ShardQ prefill takes it to 49.9 s (-39.8%). Dense scoring with ShardQ is 51.5 s, so the combination keeps the candidate default and is 3.0% faster at 1M. ## Overview #65656 made the candidate-only indexer the SM90 default: the indexer scores candidate blocks instead of dense logits. It is faster, but at 1M tokens the indexer MQA logits are still 40.5% of GPU kernel time, and candidate-only is only 1.6% faster than dense-only prefill (82.9 vs 84.3 s), so the long-context prefill bottleneck remains. ShardQ token-shards the V4.1 sparse-MLA prefill: each TP rank takes a zigzag slice of the step's prefill tokens and runs the indexer and the sparse attention for those rows with all heads, with all-to-alls moving Q in and the output out. On the dense path it gives -38.9% at 1M, but it did not compose with the merged candidate path: the candidate source layer publishes top-k blocks for its consumers in batch order. This PR is that integration. Layers at and after the candidate source (20 here) keep the full-batch candidate plan and stay head-sharded; the layers below take the split. One eligibility hook is shared by the indexer and both attention builders, so the indexer compacts exactly the rows the attention reads. I looked at a full-coverage variant and left it out: the candidate layers still spend about 1.3 s in the indexer at 1M, so even a perfect split saves about 1 s (2% of the 46.3 s kernel time), and it would need a replay-batch ShardQ path and a compact p

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Make the RoPE + KV-cache fusion reachable by explicit request and through its documented opt-ins
summary: On ROCm with AITER the RoPE + KV-cache fusion cannot be turned on: an explicit `fuse_rope_kvcache=True` is silently reset because the KV-cache update op it rewrites is split out of the graph, and the documented opt-ins (`-O2` with graph partition or `splitting_ops: []`) never resolve it because the resolver requires the `rotary_embedding` op that only the fusion appends; this PR keeps that op in the graph when a fusion asks for it and makes the custom-op requirement an opt-out. The fusion stays opt-in: stock `-O0` to `-O3` resolve as on `main` (one unread difference, below). `unified_kv_cache_update` is split out for Inductor graph reuse (#33267), which breaks only while `layer_name` is a string constant: keeping it takes `torch.compile` from 5.15 to 5.35 s (Llama-3.1-8B) with `_USE_LAYERNAME` and to 12.8x without, so there the request is still refused with a warning. QK-norm and MLA variants: same; a dropped fusion leaves no 256-token compile-range endpoint. Limits: the opt-ins resolve the fusion only with ROCm AITER; an explicit request keeps the op in the graph with AITER off too (config only). The plain pattern matches Llama-3.1 and Mixtral, not Qwen3; the QK-norm variant (Qwen3-8B, 36 layers; greedy output identical on 2 prompts) and `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla` (Kimi-K2.7 MLA layers, dummy weights) now fuse too, unbenchmarked. With the fusion on, RoPE above 256 tokens runs the custom op, up to 5 % slower than native (#36716); the fused op loses at 128–256 tokens, so the threshold may want lowering. Supersedes #57349; #49142 and #60326 overlap only the MLA hunk. ## Vali

title: [Kernel] Add opt-in NVFP4 activations for long prefills to b12x NVFP4 W4A16 linears
summary: ## Overview Builds on #64766 ([this PR's own change](https://github.com/puririshi98/vllm/compare/562e4289cadfd62ce2ae69ad36a5065eb8d7e4de...9065e934c263f27101c2c1d3b3c7a27185e110b8)). NVFP4 W4A16 checkpoints run every linear with BF16 activations. Long prefills are compute-bound, and there b12x's FP4 GEMM is 3.3–4.7× faster at 4K–8K rows. This PR adds an opt-in `--kernel-config '{"b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens": N}'`: linear inputs with more than N rows are quantized to NVFP4 with a per-call scale, and smaller inputs, including every CUDA graph replay, stay BF16. It is lossy, so it is off by default. ## Claims - **Faster long prefills:** at N=1024, Bolt's 2K / 8K TTFT drops 1.40× / 1.38× on an RTX 6000D. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Muse: start structured outputs at the answer channel
summary: ## Overview With `--reasoning-parser muse`, `response_format` (`json_object`, `json_schema`) is never applied to an answer: the grammar waits for `is_reasoning_end`, which the Muse parser reports only when a tool channel opens. This PR starts the grammar at the `to=user` answer and leaves the reasoning unconstrained. Related: #68319 addresses the same behavior on the parser-engine port in #62728, together with chat-template and Rust-frontend changes. title: [Mamba] Store ReplaySSM ring trackers in the Mamba page; put the dt ring last
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview The goal of this PR is to make ReplaySSM code simpler and more contained. It moves the ReplaySSM ring trackers `(ring_start, num_committed)` from off-page tensors into the Mamba page, and puts the dt ring after the B ring, which removes `MambaSpec.state_alignment`. Every tracker user on main reads the in-page copy: FlashInfer ReplaySSM, the Triton decode planner and the Triton speculative-decoding kernel (#66318). Needs FlashInfer 0.7.4 for strided trackers ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8548](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8548)), which main pins. ## Claims - The trackers are a sixth Mamba state. Block copies, the align pre-copy and KV cache accounting cover them, so the off-page tracker allocation, binding, block-copy tensors and cleanup are removed from the model runner, the extensible KV cache and the worker utils. - The Triton speculative-decoding kernel and the Triton decode planner take page-strided trackers; FlashInfer takes them as of 0.7.4. - The page order is conv, ssm, x, B, dt, trackers. FlashInfer's 16-byte-sensitive states (ssm, x, B) start aligned without per-state padding, so `MambaSpec.state_alignment` is removed. With FlashInfer ReplaySSM, a one-time check raises a clear error if a layout would misalign them. - On Nemotron-3.5 Lightning NVFP4, GSM8K accuracy, MTP acceptance and prefix-cache hits match main for both FlashInfer and Triton ReplaySSM. - Serving throughput matches main: on a dedicated node, the change is within ±0.3% at every concurrency from 1 to 64 for both backends, with 95% confidence

title: [ROCm][JIT] Warm the sparse MLA split-K decode kernels at every split count
summary: ## Overview The rope-free sparse MLA decode on ROCm (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with a bf16 or `mxfp4_mla` KV cache, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) runs a split-K partial and combine kernel pair whose split count is a `tl.constexpr`. The count follows the decode batch and its selected KV length, so whenever attention runs outside a FULL CUDA graph, each new count a batch reaches compiles both kernels during serving. This PR registers every count the split heuristic can return when the layer's KV cache is bound, through the decode warm-up hook #65349 added for `TritonMLAImpl`, so the JIT warm-up compiles them before serving. The partial kernel is registered for both pointer classes the KV cache can take once the extensible KV cache re-binds it, and no longer specializes on the KV row count, which the re-bind also changes (Details, Keys). ## Claims - Cost: startup compiles 93 more keys on gfx950 (the partial kernel at 31 split counts in each of 2 KV pointer classes, the combine at 31; 45 keys on other archs), serially, as the parallel warm-up pool is CUDA-only. Serving GLM-5.3-Flash at TP2 with the default `cudagraph_mode`, the JIT warm-up grows from 244 to 337 keys and from 46.9 s to 75.1 s (+28.1 s); with `cudagraph_mode` PIECEWISE, from 45.8 s to 73.5 s (+27.7 s). The 31 partial keys of the small pointer class go unused on this model, whose KV cache view stays above 2 GB. - With the default `cudagraph_mode`, which vLLM resolves to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` for GLM-5.3-Flash, decode graphs are captured at the longest selected length and reach 10 of the 31 counts at TP2. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview #67710 adds bidirectional attention spans to the engine and to offline `TokensPrompt`s, but the OpenAI-compatible APIs have no field for them yet. title: [Perf][Attention] Cache FlashAttention KV cache transpose+split views
summary: ## Overview Cache the `kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, dim=-1)` result in `FlashAttentionImpl` keyed on `data_ptr()`, avoiding redundant view operations on every `forward()` and `do_kv_cache_update()` call. ## Claims - Eliminates redundant `transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, dim=-1)` calls in the FlashAttention hot path - Applies to both `FlashAttentionImpl` and `FlashAttentionDiffKVImpl` - Clears cached views during profiling cleanup to avoid stale references ## Validation - GPU correctness test on RTX 5090 (CUDA 13.0): verified cache hit returns same views, rebind triggers recompute, cached views match fresh computation, writes to kv_cache reflected in cached views - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: all passed - Existing `test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py` tests: 10 CPU tests passed ## Details The KV cache tensor is bound once via `bind_kv_cache()` and never reallocated during serving, making its `data_ptr()` stable. This allows caching the transpose+split views and reusing them across calls. `_get_kv_cache_views()` checks `data_ptr()` on each call. On the first call (or after a rebind with a new tensor), it computes and stores the views. Subsequent calls return the cached views directly. `FlashAttentionDiffKVImpl` inherits this method. Its `forward()` uses the same `split(self.head_size)` pattern, so the cached views work correctly. Its `do_kv_cache_update()` uses only `transpose(1, 2)` without split (passes to `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv`), so it does not use the cached views. Also added cleanup of `_kv_cache_view_cache` in `_cleanup_prof

title: [Model] Mamba2: low-rank projection slices with a per-slice rank
summary: Stacked on #68464: only the second commit is new here. ## Summary A Mamba2 projection slice (z, x, B, C, dt of `in_proj`, or `out_proj`) can now be stored as two factors, the way DeepSeek stores `q_a_proj`/`q_b_proj` under `q_lora_rank`. The rank comes from the model config, per slice. Each factor is a normal linear, so each can use its own quantization format. ```text config.mamba_<slice>_rank = r # slice in z, x, B, C, dt, out; None = full rank in_proj slice -> <slice>_a_proj: ReplicatedLinear(hidden -> r) <slice>_b_proj: ColumnParallelLinear(r -> slice rows) out_proj -> out_a_proj: RowParallelLinear(intermediate -> r) # all-reduce at rank r out_b_proj: ReplicatedLinear(r -> hidden) ``` A low-rank `in_proj` slice turns on the per-slice `in_proj` from #68464. A low-rank `out_proj` alone keeps the fused `in_proj`. Invalid slice names or ranks raise at construction. ## Evidence - **Before:** a checkpoint with `x_a_proj`/`x_b_proj` or `out_a_proj`/`out_b_proj` tensors has no matching parameters. **After:** `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_projection_slices.py` (GB10, 5 passed): for `{x: 8}` and `{z: 8, dt: 2, out: 16}`, every factor resolves its own quant method by prefix, and `_project_in` / `_project_out` equal the dense product `b @ a` stacked in slice order. Invalid ranks raise. - End to end on GB10, the 40-Mamba-layer NVFP4 NemotronH checkpoint with `out_proj` replaced by full-rank (4096) BF16 SVD factors gives the same answers as the original. At rank 1024 without fine-tuning it loads and runs, but the output is not usable; that is expected for an untrained truncation.

title: [Model] Mamba2: per-slice in_proj so each slice can use its own quantization
summary: ## Summary Mamba2's `in_proj` packs five output slices (z, x, B, C, dt) into one fused GEMM, so a checkpoint cannot give the slices different quantization formats. Like `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`, a checkpoint can now store the slices as separate tensors. Each slice then resolves its own quant method by its own prefix: one can be NVFP4, another FP8 or BF16, and an out-of-tree quant method can claim a single slice. The fused `in_proj` stays the default. ```diff MambaMixer2(..., split_in_proj=False) # NemotronH: config.mamba_split_in_proj - in_proj = MergedColumnParallelLinear([z, x, B, C, dt]) + if split_in_proj: + z_proj, x_proj, B_proj, C_proj, dt_proj = ColumnParallelLinear(...) # prefix <mixer>.<slice>_proj + else: + in_proj = MergedColumnParallelLinear([z, x, B, C, dt]) # unchanged forward - projected_states = in_proj(h) + projected_states = cat(slice(h) for slice in slices) if split_in_proj else in_proj(h) ``` Per-slice mode runs five GEMMs plus one concat instead of one GEMM. Use it only when the slices really differ. It requires the TP size to divide `n_groups` (the same layout as the fused path). Module names are resolved at forward time, so LoRA wrappers on the slice attributes still apply. ## Evidence - **Before:** a per-slice checkpoint cannot load: there is no `z_proj`/`x_proj`/... parameter, and ModelOpt rejects mixed formats inside one fused layer ("All shards must use the same quantization"). **After:** `tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_projection_slices.py` (GB10): each slice calls `get_quant_method` with its own prefix; per-slice weights copied from a fused

title: [Feat] [AMD] ultraquant: Add MTP verify decode
summary: ## Purpose UltraQuant decode already ships. MTP verification did not reach it: on current `main` the TurboQuant metadata builder opts out of spec-as-decode, so a k-token verify is classified as a prefill and never enters the UltraQuant decode kernel. This PR keeps an MTP verify on the UltraQuant decode path and scores it with the shipping FlyDSL kernel. - Width 1 is today's single-token decode. - Widths 2–8 are the same kernel family with the four-wave schedule. One read of each KV tile scores the verify. Qwen3.8-27B is query group size 6, head size 256, MTP k=5, so a verify step is 6 tokens. - A width outside 2–8, or a batch that is not eligible, falls back to one single-token launch per verify token. There is no environment variable and no second kernel name. The wide path is the default when the query length is in 2–8, the same kind of condition KV8 uses. The 4-bit cache format is unchanged: FP4 E2M1 codes, UE8M0 per-group scales, Hadamard-rotated keys. See [UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20474). ## Design - `UltraQuantMetadataBuilder` subclasses `TurboQuantMetadataBuilder` and opts into spec-as-decode. A pure verify batch stays a decode: `is_prefill` is set from whether any request is a prefill, not from `max_query_len > 1`. - `num_verify_tokens` comes from `max_query_len`. A ragged batch such as `[2, 4]` is not collapsed to one width. Each request is masked with `query_start_loc`. - Width 1 compiles the single-wave kernel in `ultraquant_decode_hd256.py`. Widths 2–8 compile the four-wave schedule in `ultraquant_decode_h

summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Triton unified attention (`TRITON_ATTN`) JIT-compiles `kernel_unified_attention` and `reduce_segments` during serving. title: [KV Offload] Mirror CPU offload region slots across nodes
summary: ## Overview Fixes `TieringOffloadingSpec` secondary tiers when the engine's workers span nodes (the bug half of #54415). The scheduler and its secondary tiers read one CPU region, on the head node; workers on other nodes now move their KV straight between their GPU blocks and their slot of that region with one-sided NIXL transfers (GPUDirect RDMA). ```text other node head node +---------------------+ +----------------------------------+ | worker r | | worker 0 engine core | | GPU KV blocks <---+-- RDMA ---+-> CPU region (scheduler, | +---------------------+ (NIXL) | chunk: [w0|..|wr|..] tiers) | +----------------------------------+ ``` Builds on #52838 (failed offloading transfers are reported instead of asserting) and #62930 (which rejects these engines at startup; this PR lifts that), both now in `main`. Their original commits still appear here through two merge commits; this PR's own changes are the non-merge commits from `6070c79aad` on, and the other merge commits only bring the branch up to date with `main`. ## What changes - **Where the KV lives:** the head node's region holds every worker's slot of each chunk and is the only copy. Workers on other nodes allocate no CPU region: their copy plan addresses their slot of the head region directly. - **Stores and loads:** a remote worker writes its GPU blocks to its slot (RDMA WRITE) and reads them back (RDMA READ), in transfers of about 256 MiB; loads go ahead of stores, so a load waits for at most one transfer of a large store. title: [RFC]: Large-page KV cache allocator: one KV cache group per spec
summary: **Status:** draft · **Implementation:** two stacked PRs to follow (PR1 opt-in, PR2 large pages only) · **Related:** [#62100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62100) (pluggable KV cache planning) ## TL;DR vLLM requires every KV cache group to have the same page size in bytes. For hybrid models, this one rule is the source of most of the grouping complexity in core: layer-count grouping, page padding, raised block sizes, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, and a second hash granularity (`hash_block_size`). Each new hybrid model, drafter or cache precision tends to need another special case. This RFC proposes to remove the rule. The KV cache pool becomes a set of equal **large pages**. A page belongs to one KV cache group at a time, and the group cuts it into blocks of its own size. Then grouping becomes trivial: **one group per `KVCacheSpec`**, with one block size for every prefix-cacheable group. Block ids stay affine (block `b` is kernel row `b * R`), so attention kernels and slot mapping keep their upstream form. KV cache capacity stays within 1% of main on the models we checked. The motivation is simpler code, not memory. ## 1. Background Main stores the KV cache of each group in per-layer tensors that several groups share. A block id `b` addresses page `b` of every layer in its group, and one tensor can back one layer from each group. This sharing works only if all groups have the same page size in bytes. summary: ## Overview The DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode kernels (`--monokernel`, ROCm gfx950) now also run over a plain fp8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`: 512 B e4m3 rows with one per-tensor scale), not only over the default `fp8_ds_mla` records (584 B with block scales). The default KV format is unchanged: the same kernels, the same vector/memory code, the same speed. ## Claims - `--monokernel` works with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. At TP2, against plain fp8 without mono, it gives +42.5 % output tok/s at C=1, +19.3 % at C=4 and +3.5 % at C=8. On `fp8_ds_mla` it gives +43.5 %, +20.3 % and +6.1 %. - Accuracy over plain fp8 matches `fp8_ds_mla`. NIAH is 100 % from 8K to 256K, and GSM8K, MMLU and GPQA are all within run-to-run noise. - Plain fp8 holds 13.6 % more tokens in the same KV memory. With mono it matches `fp8_ds_mla` throughput (within 0.5 % at C ≤ 8) and is 2.6 % faster at C=16. - The default `fp8_ds_mla` path is unchanged: - **Codegen:** across the 150 compiled kernels, every MFMA and memory instruction is identical to `main`. Only scalar code changes, plus one kernel's SGPR spill lanes. - **Throughput:** equal to `main` within 0.8 %, inside the repeat spread. ## Validation **Setup:** - **Hardware and software:** MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP2. - **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens: 5`, so every decode step carries 1 + 5 = 6 rows per request. - The mono kernels take decode-only steps of up to 48 rows. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Keep few-row gfx950 top-512 calls in one block up to 36K
summary: ## Overview On gfx950 (MI355X), `top_k_per_row_decode` with topK = 512 and at most 32 rows splits every row longer than 16K positions into 8 blocks (more above 128K) and merges their candidates in a second kernel. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode at low concurrency takes this path on every step: DSpark k=6 gives 7 rows per request, and indexer layers 2/8/14/20 each make one full-width top-512 call per step (rows of about half the context for layers 2/8/14, the full context for layer 20). For rows of up to about 36K, the split plus merge is slower than one block. This PR keeps rows of 16K-36K in one block when no row of the call is longer than 36K. A call with any longer row splits exactly as on main. - **Device:** the split kernel and the merge kernel make the same decision from the same inputs. Each lane loads one row end of the call (at most 32), and a wave ballot checks them against the limit. The merge returns at once for one-block rows. - **Host:** a call of at most 32 rows that is no wider than 36K gets no workspace and no merge launch. - **CUDA graphs:** grid and workspace still depend only on shape, so FULL graphs replay correctly at any context length. ## Performance vs main All numbers are MEASURED on MI355X with the ROCm nightly `nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2ed`. Its `csrc/sampler.cu` is identical to that of main 2c1fc9b3d3, which this PR is rebased on. Both arms run the same image with a `_C_stable_libtorch` built in one tree with the same flags: main's (control) or main + this PR (change). title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Fold the consumer remap into top-512; skip the -1 fill on all decode rows
summary: ## Overview On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 sparse indexer has 4 candidate-consumer index layers (24/28/32/36). Each picks the top-512 from the candidate pool's compact scores, then a second Triton launch, `_remap_compact_topk`, maps each picked pool slot to its context position. This PR adds a ROCm op, `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode_remap`: the existing gfx950 top-512 kernel with an index map in its final store, so it writes the context positions directly. The consumers use it when k = 512 and the step has fewer than 128 decode rows (a prefill launch goes by its own rows), which removes 4 launches per decode step. It also skips the `-1` fill on all decode rows, whichever top-k kernel runs. #63888 skipped it only where vLLM's top-k runs (fewer than 128 decode rows in the step, k < 2048), so at 128 or more step rows and at k >= 2048 this removes the remaining fills (one launch per index layer, 8 per DeepSeek-V4.1 step) unless prefill or padding rows follow the decode rows. Both halves are exact: the fused op stores the same index sets, and every top-k path writes every slot. On TP-sharded steps both decisions follow #66047's step rows (the whole step's decode rows, not the rank's slice), so all ranks and FULL-graph replays take the same branch. ROCm/gfx950-only. End to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP8 and TP4), that saving (4.7-5.0 us per C1 step in the microbench, about 0.11% of the 4.3 ms TP8 C1 step) is below the server-to-server noise: no step-time change is resolved in either direction, and long-context accuracy is unchanged. ## Performance vs main Setup: MI355X (gf

title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] READ mode restore the cached recurrent state for hybrid prefixes that end on a block
summary: ## Overview In MoRIIO READ mode serving a hybrid model with P/D disaggregation, a prompt whose first N-1 tokens end at a block boundary leaves the Mamba state block that decode caches for it unwritten, so a later request with the same prompt resumes from stale state and generates different text. title: [HiSparse] Batch owner bookkeeping when unpinning pages
summary: ## Purpose Cut the HiSparse coordinator's per-block Python work when a request's resident pages are unpinned. Importing a long multi-turn prefix in P/D, as in #65888, adopts the GPU copies of about 1,250 pages × 20 resident groups, then unpins them on the next step. Unpinning built one owner `set` and one `(request, page)` tuple per block, about 50k long-lived objects per import. On 8×B200 with #65888, that's about 12 ms of a 17.7 ms `schedule()` step, plus full-GC spikes of up to 76 ms. Changes, all in `vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`: - `_owners` maps a block to a tuple of owners. A page's blocks share one 1-tuple, so a single-owner block (the common case) costs no allocation. - `_unpin_pages` finds null pages once per column and updates page state once per page. Release order is unchanged: page-major, tail first. - The block-reuse watcher is bound once. Each unpin used to pass a new bound method, which `BlockPool` keeps per block. - `_discard_owner` replaces the per-call `set.discard` in `_lose_page` and `free`. No behaviour change. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py ``` CPU micro-benchmark at real size (1,250 pages × 20 resident groups, real coordinator and block pool), this PR vs `main`. summary: ## Overview Add opt-in native Rust gRPC scheduler-retirement acknowledgements for explicit Abort and frontend stop-string completion. summary: ## Overview Part of item 2 of RFC #66782 (item 1 before the RFC's v2 renumbering). The offloading connector's lookup moves behind `SchedulerView.lookup_request()`, which returns the keys a load would read. The first commit is that refactor, with no behaviour change. The second fixes lookups for chunked local attention (Llama 4), where comparing the lookup's keys with the load's showed they disagree. title: [RFC] Adaptive spin grace + bounded arch waits (aarch64 WFET, x86 WAITPKG) for shm_broadcast
summary: ## Problem `SpinCondition` in `shm_broadcast.py` busy-loops with `sched_yield` for a fixed grace period after each successful read before a reader transitions to the poll/sleep path. Two problems follow: 1. The grace is a compile-time constant (`busy_loop_s=1` at `SpinCondition.__init__`). Real message cadence in serving varies over ~4 orders of magnitude (sub-ms during decode, multi-second when idle), so no single fixed value is right. 2. On aarch64, the optional `spinloop` native extension degrades to a plain `yield` busy-poll — the x86 path has MONITORX/MWAITX (AMD) but there is no aarch64 equivalent, and x86 Intel parts have WAITPKG (UMONITOR/UMWAIT) with no equivalent wired either. The consequence on integrated CPU+GPU packages (e.g. DGX Spark-class GB10, or any SoC where the CPU and GPU share a thermal/power envelope): during idle-adjacent decode the mp executor's shm_broadcast readers pin performance cores at 100% for the duration of the fixed grace on every poll cycle, heating the SoC and stealing power/thermal headroom from the GPU. The same class of issue applies to the writer side: `acquire_write` yields in a tight loop while waiting for ALL readers to consume a block. ## Proposed change Draft implementation: #52917 1. **Adaptive spin grace (readers and writers, Python).** Derive the spin grace from an exponential moving average of observed inter-event intervals: `grace = clamp(B*B/T_ema, MIN_GRACE, MAX_GRACE)` where `B` is a latency budget (default 1ms).
