title: [ROCm][BugFix] Trim MoE GEMM input to valid token prefix
summary: ## Purpose AITER's ROCm `fused_moe` (`AiterExperts`) silently corrupts its own output (returns all-zero rows) when the allocated input buffer is much larger than the real number of valid tokens it's asked to process. This is the normal case for EP dispatchers like MoRI, which pre-allocate a worst-case buffer (`max_num_batched_tokens * world_size`) while real per-step token counts are usually a handful per rank. `AiterExperts.apply()` passed the full buffer straight to `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()` even though `num_local_tokens` identifies the real valid prefix. Confirmed independent of any EP dispatcher via a standalone microbenchmark calling AITER's `fused_moe()` directly against a from-scratch reference GEMM: AITER zeros the valid rows whenever the buffer-to-valid-token ratio is large enough, regardless of routing pattern. **Fix:** in `AiterExperts.apply()`, slice `hidden_states`/`topk_weights`/ `topk_ids`/`a1q_scale` down to the valid prefix before calling `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()`, then scatter the result into a zero-initialized output buffer of the original shape (padding rows are never read downstream). Applied unconditionally — no feature flag, since this is a correctness fix, not an opt-in behavior change. Under CUDA-graph capture, a live `.item()` read of `num_local_tokens` is illegal, so the bound is instead a static worst-case value (`graph_bs * topk * dispatch_group_size`) under full-graph capture with a uniform batch, or trimming is skipped entirely when no safe bound exists (e.g. piecewise cudagraphs). ## Test Plan Hy3-preview (192 experts, top-8, BF16) depl

title: [Security] Widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
summary: ## Summary - Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32` - Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension - Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels ## Affected kernels | Kernel | File | Risk | |---|---|---| | `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC | | `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path | | `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High | | `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate | | AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) | ## Root cause CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens. ## Fix pattern ```cpp // Before (32-bit overflow) scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size; // After (64-bit safe) const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x; scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size; ``` For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change. ## Test plan - [x] Pr

title: [Feature][Multimodal] Name every uncached item in the cache-miss error
summary: ## Overview Closes #68428. When a request skips the media data of some items and relies on their UUIDs hitting the processor cache, the processor rejects the request at the first item that missed. By then it has already found every missed item, but the error names only the first one. A client that resends that one item then meets the next miss, so it needs one more round trip for each missing item. This PR names all of them in one error. ## Claims - The cache-miss error for items sent without data now names every such item, by modality and index, in one error. - A request with a single missed item gets exactly the same message as before. - The error is the same `ValueError`, raised before the cache is updated, so it is still an HTTP 400 and nothing else changes. ## Validation The new test `test_omitted_media_cache_miss_names_every_item` in `tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_video.py` sends two videos and one image with only a UUID, none of them cached, through the OpenAI-compatible server, and checks the error message. summary: ## Purpose On DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), an MTP drafter that shares an unquantized BF16 lm_head now uses the NVFP4 copy from `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973) by default. title: [Bugfix] Guard Conch W4A16 preconditions and pad non-tile-multiple outputs
summary: ## Overview `--linear-backend conch` dies at the first forward pass on `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16`: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x30a2bea0) on address 0x7e69a4600000. Reason: Unknown. ``` 48 of the model's layers are fused `in_proj_ba` projections with `N=96`. Conch's W4A16 kernel loads the weight block and the per-group scales in 64-column tiles with no bounds mask, so the second tile covers columns 96-127: **128 B of packed weight and 64 B of scales per row past the end of the buffer**. This PR handles those shapes in vLLM's Conch wrapper: a `K` the kernel cannot address is refused, and `N` is padded up to the kernel's tile width. All 48 layers then load and run - decode TPOT **-31.7% / -29.4% / -22.5%** vs the default Triton kernel at c=1/8/32 (8k-in / 1k-out). Selection is untouched: Triton stays the default, Conch stays opt-in, and conch itself is not patched. The change is shape arithmetic in the wrapper rather than anything platform-specific, so it should hold for any conch-enabled target; validated on `gfx950` (MI355X). ## Claims * **Refuse the K side.** Every kernel implements `can_implement`, the hook vLLM calls to ask "can you run this layer?". `ConchLinearKernel.can_implement` now says no when the input dimension `K` is not a multiple of the kernel's 64-wide tile, or not a multiple of the quantization group size; channelwise layers (`group_size == -1`, one scale per output column) are checked as if the group size were `K`. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Probe where chat templates place Anthropic inline system messages
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Since v2.1.154 (#44000), Claude Code sends its per-turn reminders as inline `role: system` messages in `/v1/messages`. `AnthropicServingMessages` checks the chat template at startup to decide whether to keep those messages in place, which is good for the prefix cache, or merge them into the leading system prompt. title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
summary: # [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950 ## Purpose Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4). HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and pulls back only the indexer-selected rows just in time, so long-context agentic sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only. ## Changes **Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel.** HiSparse points attention at a view over the *whole multi-layer KV slab*, so emitted row indices scale with total block count: max row index is 33 off HiSparse and 7.5M on. AITER's decode kernel computes `row_index * row_width` in int32, so on GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above row 3,728,270 and returns approximately zero — no NaN, no assert. Force Triton kernel for HiSparse for time being. **ROCm backend wiring.** CUDA HiSparse backends consume a dense `[tokens, topk]` tensor; AITER's decode kernel consumes a ragged list plus indptr. Bridging that is most of the diff: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` registers with an `index_group_builder` (which is what makes `mla_attention.py` pick up `hisparse_cache`), decode converts dense physical top-k to ragged and attends against the hot buffer, and prefill stages host rows via `stage_prefill_rows` when the context is not fully resident. One new Triton kernel, `compact_topk_to_ragged_triton` — `fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable because a mid-row `-1` must drop out rather than displace a valid entry. title: [RFC]: Bring vLLM's development cost back to linear: a small core with owned, independently tested components
summary: ### Motivation. Every new model, kernel, platform or quantization method in vLLM lands in the same tree, the same review queue and the same CI. Because components import each other directly, the cost of a change grows with the number of pairs that can interact, not with the number of components: development cost grows much faster than the codebase. The symptoms are already tracked separately: review backlog (#58253, #59665), stalled kernel packaging split and multi-hour builds (#17419), unversioned extension points that break out-of-tree code (#57566, #62187). The goal of this RFC is to bring that cost back to linear: each component is owned, reviewed, tested and built on its own, against a small core with stable contracts, so adding the N+1-th model or backend costs the same as the first. Measured coupling today (pruning upstream down to 8 models, CUDA sm_12x only, no LoRA): - 230 modules we wanted to drop had to be restored because the core imports them unconditionally. - Engine entry points statically reach 65% of all modules, including model-specific packages (e.g. the speculative proposer base imports `deepseek_v4` and `minimax_m3`; sparse MLA backends import `deepseek_v2`). - The pruned build crashed at startup because `get_quantization_config` imports every quantization method eagerly. ### Proposed Change. Split vLLM into a small engine core plus independent components (models, kernels, platforms, quantization, KV transfer, speculative decoding, serving), as separate repos or at least as independently owned and tested modules. Kubernetes did this with SIGs, OWNERS fi

title: [Bugfix] Raise a clear error when weights leave no room for sampler state
summary: ## Overview Startup dies with a raw PyTorch out-of-memory error when the weights almost fill the GPU, because the sampler allocates its penalty tables before KV-cache planning can explain that nothing is left. Fixes #68316. ## Claims - A device that cannot hold `PenaltiesState` now raises `ValueError` with the weight size, the free memory, and the buffer size, instead of `torch.OutOfMemoryError` from `output_bin_counts`. - The byte count matches the two int32 tables `PenaltiesState` allocates: `output_bin_counts` and `prompt_bin_mask`. ## Validation Unit test, no GPU. From `eca61f52c1` plus this commit: ```bash PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_sampler_memory.py -q --noconftest ``` ```text ... [100%] 3 passed, 1 warning in 1.23s ``` The warning is `Failed to read commit hash: No module named 'vllm._version'` from importing the worktree without a generated version module. title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: undo parameter renames before rerunning post-load processing
summary: ## Overview A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) reruns post-load processing on checkpoint-layout bytes. This rerun has to see the same parameters cold start saw. `begin` restored each tensor's checkpoint layout and loader metadata, but it did not restore the names post-load processing changed: - `move_parameter` registers a checkpoint tensor under a runtime name as well (Humming: `w13_weight_scale_inv` is also `w13_weight_scale`) and sets `runtime_name`, which `kernel_parameters` reports; - `retire_parameter` marks a tensor that no kernel reads, which `kernel_parameters` and `get_live_param` skip. Tensors that processing itself created can be retired too, such as an online NVFP4 `weight_global_scale`. Humming looks its inputs up by name through `kernel_parameters`, so its rerun took a different path than cold start: | Humming case | Reload on main | |---|---| | MoE, block FP8 (`moe_backend="humming"`) | fails: `weight_scale is required by humming` | | MoE, block FP8 requantized from NVFP4 | fails: the stand-in `w13_weight_scale` was replaced by the runtime alias | | Linear, NVFP4 weight-only (`linear_backend="humming"`) | fails: `KeyError: 'weight_global_scale'` (retired) | Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477). It is a prerequisite for making direct reload the default (#68041), so that Humming kernels keep reloading as they do with layerwise reload. ## Change `begin_direct_reload` undoes what `move_parameter` and `retire_parameter` (#62407) add, from the cold-start record it already keeps (#64336), with no new bookkeeping: - a parameter name

title: [MRV2][BugFix] Don't expose P/D step output before drafter KV writes complete
summary: In MRV2, the async output copy is started before the speculator's propose() so that the D2H copy can overlap with drafting. Its copy event therefore only covers the target model's work, and the scheduler can see a step's output while the drafter is still writing its KV for those blocks. On a P/D producer this lets a finished request's blocks be sent before its draft KV is complete: the scheduler finishes the request and the KV connector transfers its blocks (e.g. NIXL READ/WRITE, Mooncake, MoRI-IO) without any further GPU sync. Outputs are unaffected since draft tokens are verified, but D's drafter attends over stale draft KV for the prompt for the rest of the request, and via D's prefix cache for later requests sharing that prefix, lowering acceptance. When the KV connector requires_kv_delivery and spec decoding is enabled, re-record the output copy event after the drafter so that output readiness implies the drafter's KV writes are done. The D2H copies are still issued early. Best-effort caches (offloading connectors) opt out of requires_kv_delivery and their copies are already stream-ordered after compute, so they are unaffected.

title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE positions stride assertion in compile_sizes graphs
summary: ## Overview Fixes #50046. When `compile_sizes` is set, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with TP=4 dies at start-up, during CUDA-graph memory profiling, with `AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0`. The cause is `create_concrete_args` in `vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py`. It set every symbol, stride symbols included, to the compile size. With this fix, a symbol that Dynamo created only for an input's stride or storage offset keeps its traced value. Compared with #50445, this fix: - Also fixes the stride where the graph takes the stride symbol as a SymInt input. With vLLM's `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` at compile size 16, [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) gives output that differs from eager (`Tensor-likes are not close!`), and this fix matches eager. - Does not break a case that works today. Take a tensor with no token dim whose stride is the token count, passed across a split: with [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) the size-16 graph fails with `stride 16==64`, and the old code and this fix both pass. - Adds a test that catches the bug. title: [RFC]: Compute-free prefix KV lookup-and-pin for router-driven peer KV reuse
summary: ### Motivation. KV-aware routers such as the vLLM router (`kv_aware` policy) keep an index of which worker holds which prefix blocks, built from KV events. When the worker with the best prefix hit (A) is busy, the router would like to send the request to a less loaded worker (B) and have B reuse A's cached prefix over NIXL instead of recomputing it. Issue https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/424 and PR https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/509 seeks to have worker B transfer kv from worker A. Doing this with stock vLLM is a 3-request flow: 1. Router → A: the prefix only, `kv_transfer_params: {do_remote_decode: true}`, `max_tokens=1`. A keeps the blocks under a lease (`kv_lease_duration`, 30 s by default) and returns their ids. 2. Router → B: the prefix plus A's params, `do_remote_prefill: true`, `max_tokens=1`. B pulls the blocks and caches them. 3. Router → B: the real request, which hits B's local prefix cache. This works, but it has two problems the router can't fix. **Problem 1: A computes on a miss, and nothing can stop it.** The router's index is eventually consistent. A can evict the prefix just before step 1 arrives, while its `BlockRemoved` event is still in flight. Step 1 then becomes a normal prefill on A: the busy worker we were trying to unload recomputes the prefix, just to export it. No request option says "serve this only from the prefix cache, otherwise refuse", and `cached_tokens` in the response arrives after the work is done. **Problem 2: The pull is all-or-nothing.** The NIXL connector pulls blocks for B's whole prompt (`nixl/pull_schedul

summary: ## Overview Adds an opt-in FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-gather/reduce-scatter path for uniform expert-parallel MoE collectives. title: [XPU] Add VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY to control FP8 query in flash attention
summary: ## Purpose On XPU, `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` always returns False, so the FA backend never quantizes the query to FP8 even with an FP8 KV cache. Xe3p kernels in vllm-xpu-kernels (>= 0.1.17) can run full-FP8 attention (FP8 Q/K/V, `q_scale` fused in the kernel), while Xe2 kernels cannot. This PR adds `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` (`bool | None`, default unset) to control it: | `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` | Device | FP8 query | |---|---|---| | `1` | any XPU | on | | `0` | any XPU | off | | unset | Xe3p (`torch.ops._xpu_C.is_xe3p_arch()`) | on | | unset | other XPU (e.g. BMG), or op missing | off (unchanged) | Implementation: `XPUPlatform.support_fp8_query()` resolves the value, and `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` calls it on XPU. Other platforms are unchanged (still True). Limitation: the Xe3p full-FP8 kernels currently only support head_size 128 (and Q/K/V of the same FP8 type), so models with another head size fail on Xe3p when the FP8 KV cache is on; set `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0` for those until the kernels are extended. ## Test Plan On an Xe3p GPU, serve a model with FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) and check the query is quantized; compare with `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0`. On a non-Xe3p XPU the default stays off. Not yet run on hardware.

title: [Roadmap] Rust Frontend Feature Parity
summary: ## Motivation The Rust frontend has landed in the vLLM repository as a drop-in alternative to the Python API server process. It is enabled through `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and uses the existing vLLM engine/core boundary. The Rust frontend is still experimental and not yet feature-complete relative to the Python frontend. This issue tracks the roadmap for the remaining gaps in feature parity and provides community contributors with a place to find scoped work. This roadmap prioritizes user value and the Rust frontend's architectural goals over blanket 1:1 parity with the Python frontend. In particular, we may skip: - Features / endpoints / options that are not commonly used in production - Options that mainly reflect Python frontend implementation details or Python-side workarounds - Features whose Python implementation has accumulated enough complexity that redesigning or removing them may be better than porting them directly **For items marked with 🧭:** Please start with a design discussion before implementation, covering the intended API/architecture, co-design with the engine if needed, and the testing plan. Related context: - Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40846 - Integration PRs * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40848 * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43283 ## Current status - [x] Rust code lives in the main vLLM repository under `rust/` - [x] `vllm-rs` integrates with `vllm serve` as a Python-supervised frontend subprocess - [x] Core `/v1/chat/completions` support (streaming & non-streaming) - [x] Core `/v1/completions`

title: [RFC]: Shared Context Parallelism: peer-addressable GPU objects for PCP and DCP
summary: # [RFC]: Shared Context Parallelism: peer-addressable GPU objects for PCP and DCP ## Motivation. ### Problem vLLM's context-parallel paths frequently cross a rank boundary by first materializing an operation-specific communication result. This is a good general default, but it does not always match the physical placement required by the next consumer. Several recent PCP and DCP PRs instead treat the exchanged data as a logical cross-rank GPU object: - a producer can write directly into a replicated consumer layout; - a consumer can read directly from an owner-sharded layout; - a producer can publish only a compact transient result needed by a later consumer. These PRs currently duplicate peer allocation, mapping, publication, and lifecycle code. They also use different names for closely related data semantics. The duplicated infrastructure makes each feature larger and makes it difficult to review synchronization, failure behavior, and capability requirements consistently. ### Goal Define **Shared Context Parallelism (Shared-CP)** as a common semantic model for peer-addressable GPU objects used inside existing PCP and DCP execution. A Shared-CP object is a logical cross-rank GPU object with: 1. explicit physical ownership and placement; 2. stable local and peer views; 3. a consumer-specific physical layout; 4. an explicit publication and reuse protocol; 5. a bounded lifetime and deterministic teardown contract. **Shared-PCP** and **Shared-DCP** are applications of this model. Shared-CP is not a new context-parallel algorithm and does not redefine PCP or DCP rank topology. #

title: [Bugfix] Keep warmup block IDs within each KV block pool
summary: ## Purpose V2 warmup numbers the fake block IDs it hands to synthetic requests from one counter across all KV cache groups, capped by the device pool. Groups that index a separate pool, such as HiSparse host-resident groups, get IDs past the end of that pool. summary: Stacked on #67306 (two commits) and #67380 (two commits) — review only this PR's two commits, "Online fp8_per_channel dense linears on tuned FP8 kernels" and "Run the FP8 dense linears on generic FP8 kernels". ## Purpose Muse Spark's dense decoder GEMMs (the fused QKV + output-gate projection, and the MoE pooler and unpooler around the experts) are BF16 in the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint and take a large share of the decode step at low concurrency. This PR lets the standard online quantization config turn them into FP8 W8A8 on ROCm gfx950: ```bash vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 ... \ --quantization-config '{"linear": "fp8_per_channel", "ignore": ["*o_proj"]}' ``` (or the `targets` form, `'{"targets": {"re:.*\\.(qkv_proj|pooler|unpooler)$": "fp8_per_channel"}}'`). As in the [online quantization docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/quantization/online/)' Quark example, the checkpoint's own method keeps its quantized experts, and the online target applies to the layers it left in BF16. The loader's online-quantization summary reports them as usual (`Quantizing 186 layers of types: feed_forward.pooler: 62 ...; feed_forward.unpooler: 62 ...; self_attn.qkv_proj: 62 (from linear: fp8_per_channel_static)`). Muse resolves the online method on these layers with `resolve_quant_method`. The pooler and unpooler are BF16 in the checkpoint, so they take only the online part of the config. The layers keep the standard `fp8_per_channel` method and vLLM's FP8 kernel selection: - **GEMMs:** `AiterPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` now also covers AITER's Triton per-tok

title: [ROCm][Muse Spark] Ulysses sequence parallelism for TEP prefill
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> Stacked on #67306 — review only the last two commits. ## Purpose #63085 keeps the Muse Spark residual stream token-sharded across the TP group (`TokenShard`) on large steps: attention all-gathers the hidden states and reduce-scatters the O projection, and the MoE all-gathers its pooled rows. Its gain comes from de-duplicating the replicated pooler, unpooler and norms; the collectives cost more than the all-reduce they replace. This PR adds an opt-in Ulysses mode on that stream for its large eager steps, which cuts that communication: - **Attention.** Every rank projects its token shard with the full QKV-gate weight (all-gathered once at load and kept as per-channel FP8). One all-to-all gives every rank all tokens of its own heads, which is the TP layout, so KV insert and the attention backend are unchanged. A second all-to-all returns all heads for the rank's tokens, which are gated locally and projected by the full FP8 O weight with no reduction. - **MoE input.** The pre-expert-normed pooled rows are quantized to MXFP4 on the shard and gathered as FP4 bytes + E8M0 scales, a quarter of the BF16 bytes. The rows travel to the experts attached to the placeholder input tensor; a mismatch raises. - **MoE experts.** With EP, the gathered rows stay one pre-quantized row per token and run on #67306's native-routes experts (`moe_sorting` over the `[T, 8]` routes, `mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd` on the T-row scales, FlyDSL stages, masked finalize). Without EP the experts repeat the rows per route themselves, as they do with an AITER that lacks `mxfp4_moe_sort_fwd`

title: [KV Offload][P2P] Bulk import of a peer's CPU-tier KV cache
summary: ## Purpose A new vLLM instance starts with an empty KV cache. During a rolling upgrade every new replica therefore recomputes its users' prefixes, and the hit rate drops until it warms up. This PR lets a starting instance copy a running peer's whole CPU-tier cache over the existing P2P tier, once, before it takes traffic: POST /v1/kv_connector/rpc {"op": "import_from_peer", "host": "<peer-ip>", "port": <peer-base-p2p-port>} POST /v1/kv_connector/rpc {"op": "import_status", "import_id": "..."} Depends on #68331 (generic connector RPC, RFC #51639): `OffloadingConnector.on_rpc` handles these two ops. This PR builds and tests on its own; the import is reachable over HTTP once #68331 merges. How it works: - A new `ListKeysMsg`/`ListKeysRespMsg` pair lists the peer's primary-tier keys in pages, most recently used first. Only the key copy runs under the manager lock; ordering runs on a background thread. - The importer moves keys through the existing lookup, promotion and fetch path, in batches of at most 1 GiB (4 in flight), coldest first, so the peer's LRU order carries over. - Each DP rank imports from the peer rank with the same index (`port + dp_index`). - Import lookups are excluded from prefix-cache hit metrics. - A failed import (incompatible peer, peer lost, timeout) leaves the instance serving with what it already has; at worst it starts cold. `import_status` reports the reason, e.g. `session to peer closed before the handshake completed: block_len mismatch ...`. title: [Bugfix] Fix crash with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True set and custom_allreduce enabled
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Fixes #42609. Launching vLLM with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` while custom allreduce is active (tensor or data parallelism) crashes at startup during CUDA graph capture / memory profiling: ``` Profiling CUDA graph memory: PIECEWISE=2 (largest=2), FULL=1 (largest=1) Failed: Cuda error csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'invalid argument' ``` ## Root cause Custom allreduce shares its CUDA graph buffers across tensor-parallel ranks by exporting them with cudaIpcGetMemHandle (custom_all_reduce.cuh:455), which only accepts cudaMalloc memory. PyTorch's CUDA caching allocator parses PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF when it initializes. With expandable_segments:True, every device allocation it serves — including the graph buffers allocated during CUDA graph capture — comes from a VMM-backed expandable segment (CUDA virtual memory management) instead of a conventional cudaMalloc allocation. So when custom allreduce exports those buffers, cudaIpcGetMemHandle rejects the VMM-backed pointers with invalid argument. VMM memory is shareable only via cuMemExportToShareableHandle, not the legacy IPC path this kernel uses. ## Fix Temporarily disable `expandable_segments` only while custom allreduce captures its CUDA graph buffers, then restore the user's setting: ```python @contextmanager def _disable_expandable_segments_for_cuda_ipc(active: bool): conf = os.environ.get("PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF", "") should_disable = ( active and current_platform.is_cuda() and "expandable_segments:True" in conf ) if should_disable: logger.info_once( "Tempora

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Backport Qwen3-ASR/Omni audio-encoder host-side bookkeeping to v0.23.0 (#68099)
summary: ## Purpose Backports the Qwen3-ASR / Qwen3-Omni audio-encoder changes from **#68099** (merged on `main` as `7a1d2818b`) to `releases/v0.23.0`. `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder.forward` synchronises with the accelerator several times per call on this branch: - `feature_lens_after_cnn.max().item()` on a device tensor, - `chunk_lengths.tolist()` and `aftercnn_lens.tolist()` on device tensors, - `padded_embed[padded_mask_after_cnn]`, a boolean-mask gather whose output size has to be read back before the kernel can be issued. The change is therefore applied by hand and scoped to the audio encoder; the `lfm3_omni`, `qwen2_5_omni_thinker` and `Qwen3Omni_VisionTransformer` parts of #68099 are left out. summary: ## Summary The Python serving layer already rejects `cache_salt` values longer than 128 characters or containing `@`, `/`, `\`, or NUL. title: [Model Loader] Direct reload reruns post-load processing on the cold-start modules (LoRA)
summary: ## Overview A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) reruns post-load processing (PWAL) over `model.named_modules()` as the model is at reload time. LoRA wraps layers after cold start (`ColumnParallelLinear` → `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, the original layer kept as `base_layer`), and the wrappers forward their base layer's `quant_method`. The rerun therefore visits both the wrapper and the base layer and processes the same weights twice, so direct reload refuses LoRA today. Layerwise reload does not have this problem because it reruns processing only on modules recorded at cold start. This PR gives direct reload the same rule instead of special-casing LoRA. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477): LoRA is one of the setups F7 (removing layerwise reload) needs in direct mode, and one of the refusals #68041 carries. ## Change - `record_checkpoint_layout` (cold start, right before PWAL) records `model._ckpt_modules`, the modules cold-start PWAL runs over. - `process_weights_after_loading` iterates `_ckpt_modules` when recorded, else `named_modules()`. At cold start both are the same list; on a reload, modules added after cold start are left out. A LoRA base layer is the same object under its wrapper, so it is still processed once. - Drop the LoRA refusal from `VllmConfig._verify_direct_reload_compat`. - `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe` runs in both reload modes. LoRA adapter weights are not touched by a reload; only base weights are updated, as with layerwise reload. ## Validation GB200, nightly image with this tree's Python files overlaid: `test

title: [RFC] [DSV4.1] [Engram]: Share immutable host-backed Engram tables across independent instances
summary: ## Motivation: Engram host offload alone is not enough. * Engram host offload saves accelerator memory, but independently launched serving instances can still keep separate copies of the same large immutable tables. * This is particularly expensive for prefill/decode deployments with different TP layouts. Sharing inside one instance's DP group does not eliminate these cross-instance copies. * Additionally, when deployed with KVcache Pool (such as Mooncake), DRAM fragments will lead to engine OOM. We propose separating **table ownership and physical placement** from **the instances that perform lookups**. A persistent owner publishes one table generation. Independent workers attach the head ranges they need and run lookup kernels against device-accessible mappings of that backing. Selected rows and model activations remain local to each worker. ## Related PRs ### vLLM - [#64082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64082), cross-instance shared host tables. - [#64395](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64395), GPU-initiated RDMA GET for Engram sharing. - [#66552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66552), cross-engine GPU table sharding. - [#67539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67539), Engram pool over NVLink or RDMA. ### vLLM-Ascend - [#21246](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21246), shared host-table sharding across owners. - [#21623](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21623), local host VMM for shared A3 tables. - [#21638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21638), shared backends for Qwen PLE tabl

summary: ## Overview This PR enables Octave KV (`ROCM_OCTAVE`) on gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA3.5). title: [AMD][DSV4.1][DEP] Opt in switch for mori EP combine to FP4
summary: ## Motivation MoRI's intra-node combine sends each expert output back to the token's owning rank as BF16 and reduces the top-k copies there. MoRI also ships a packed-FP4 (E2M1) blockwise codec for exactly that transport — `QuantType::Fp4BlockwiseQuant`, the quantize/dequantize device primitives, the half-sized staging slots, and the registered `EpCombineIntraNodeKernel_bf16_nop2p_fp4_blockwise*` kernels are all already there. Nothing in vLLM selects it. `MoriAll2AllManager._make_all2all_kwargs` never passes `quant_type` when it builds the handle, so the config always lands on the `"none"` default and the combine always moves BF16. Turning the codec on cuts combine traffic substantially. Per token at hidden 5120, top-k 6, no combine weights: | transport | bytes/token | | --- | --- | | BF16 | `5120 x 2` = 10240 B | | FP4 | `5120 / 2 + 40 scales x 4 B` = 2720 B | That is 3.76x less data on the MoE residual path. The codec is lossy, so it is strictly opt-in and off by default. Companion mori PR: [ROCm/mori#891](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/pull/891). ## Summary of changes - **`vllm/envs.py`**: add `VLLM_MORI_FP4_COMBINE` (bool, default `0`), alongside the DeepEP combine knobs. - **`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py`**: when the flag is set, `MoriAll2AllManager._make_all2all_kwargs` passes `quant_type="fp4_blockwise"` instead of letting it default to `"none"`. The sending rank then quantizes each token to packed FP4 (E2M1) with one fp32 scale per `MORI_FP8_COMBINE_SCALE_DIM`-element block, and the receiving rank dequantizes back to BF16 as it reduces the top-k cop

summary: ## Overview OpenAI's `tool_choice: {"type": "allowed_tools", ...}` lets a client keep one stable tool list and change only which tools the model may call in a given turn, so the prompt (and the prompt cache) stays the same across turns. title: [Perf][Multimodal] Fuse dynamic FP8 Q/K/V quantization for padded ViT attention
summary: **Stacked on #64928**: this branch includes #64928's commits; review only the last three commits until #64928 merges. ## Overview With dynamic FP8 scales and a head_dim that needs padding (80 padded to 128 for AITER's asm FP8 attention on ROCm, 72 padded to 80 for FlashInfer cuDNN on Blackwell), every ViT attention layer runs about 24 small kernels to record the Q, K and V amax, update three scales, and quantize and pad each tensor. title: [Feature][KV Connector][Mooncake] Support HiSparse host-pool imports
summary: ## Summary Support Mooncake KV imports from an ordinary sparse-MLA prefiller into a HiSparse decoder. The prefiller may store source KV and indexer KV in one cache group, while the decoder stores source KV in host memory and indexer KV on the GPU. Each decoder group imports its uncached suffix. For a shared host pool, only decoder TP rank 0 registers and requests host writes; every rank retains its GPU-indexer transfer and completion obligation. Different P/D TP sizes use the existing replicated-MLA sender selection and completion counting. Enabling this only removes the equal-TP restriction from the new import path. No transfer metadata fields, kernels, or completion-aggregator changes are added. ## Supported scope Sparse MLA, PP=1, matching token block sizes, and unsplit physical pages. Asymmetric TP follows Mooncake's existing divisible-size requirement, for example TP2 → TP4 or TP4 → TP2. Page pairing requires each decoder group's missing pages to be a contiguous logical suffix: P supplies its last N blocks for D's N requested blocks. Groups may have different prefix-hit lengths. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] Fuse DBO SDMA all-reduce + add + RMSNorm + MXFP8 quant
summary: **Stacked on #64930**: this branch includes #64930's commits; review only the last two commits until #64930 merges. ## Overview With DBO at TP2 on ROCm (`--enable-dbo`, `VLLM_DBO_TP_DMA_AR=1`), #64930 runs each microbatch's TP all-reduce as an SDMA push of INT4 messages plus a dequantize-add kernel on the comm stream, and MiniMax-M3's post-attention residual add + Gemma RMSNorm + MXFP8 quant then runs on the bf16 sum. Today the dequantize-add writes that sum (12.3 KB per row at hidden size 6144) and the norm reads it again. With `VLLM_DBO_TP_DMA_AR_FUSED_NORM=1` the push stays on the comm stream and one Triton kernel on the compute stream reads both ranks' INT4 messages and the residual and writes the MXFP8 values, E8M0 scales and new residual (plus the bf16 normed rows on MoE layers), with the residual and scales bit-identical to the unfused chain. **Perf (MI350X, TP2): the fused kernel takes 0.63-0.70x the time of the chain it replaces and a 16k / 32k-token DBO prefill step is 1.1% / 1.4% faster; end to end, this change plus a deferred MoE all-reduce (not in this PR) measured +1.6% on 4 image rows, 0.5 points above the 1.14-point A/A gap. There is no end-to-end number for this change alone.** ## Claims - Kernel (MI350X, hidden size 6144): 0.63-0.70x the time of dequantize-add + norm at 2k-16k rows. Residual and E8M0 scales are bit-identical to the chain; 3-35 of 12.6-100M FP8 values and 49-472 bf16 normed values differ by one step (variance summation order); the error against fp64 is the same on both paths. - Prefill step (MI350X, TP2, 16k / 32k tokens): 1.1% / 1.4% faste

title: [Distributed][Multimodal] Add --shm-tensor-arena-slots and --shm-tensor-arena-slot-mb
summary: ## Overview The shared-memory tensor arena (`--enable-shm-tensor-arena`) has a fixed size of 8 slots x 256 MiB. Each large CPU tensor (at least 8 MiB, such as one image's `pixel_values`) takes one slot until every worker has dropped it, so tensors beyond the slot count, or larger than a slot, take the copying pickle path. This PR makes the slot count and slot size configurable (`--shm-tensor-arena-slots`, `--shm-tensor-arena-slot-mb`), validates them, and keeps today's defaults (related: #65017, which adds the arena memory note and logs). **Perf: none claimed.** At the default sizes, 67-72% of the large image tensors of one MiniMax-M3 TP2 run took the fallback path (MI355X). title: [ROCm][DBO] SDMA INT4 all-reduce and a dedicated comm-stream queue for pure-TP microbatches
summary: ## Overview With pure tensor parallelism, dual batch overlap (DBO) runs each microbatch's TP all-reduce on a comm stream while the other microbatch computes, but RCCL, QuickReduce and the custom all-reduce move data with CU kernels that contend with the other microbatch's GEMMs, so little of the all-reduce is hidden. title: [Core][DP] Add a DP-global prefill gate for prefill_schedule_interval
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Draft, to settle the mechanism first. This overlaps draft #51199 (adaptive prefill delayer for DP serving), which targets the same lockstep problem with per-rank delay budgets and acknowledgments; we would like maintainers to pick one approach before either is reviewed in detail. It builds on #54627 (`prefill_schedule_interval` outside DP). With `--prefill-schedule-interval N` (PSI), DP ranks admit new prefills only every N steps, except that a rank whose last release could not drain its queue (`prefill_capacity_bound`) releases on every step. Under sustained load that exception sets the step shape: a backlogged rank runs a long mixed step on most off-cadence steps while the other ranks, with nothing to prefill, run decode and then wait for it in the lockstep EP collectives. On DP8/EP8 + MTP1, 8x MI355X, PSI 8, chat-like 8k-class prompts at c=1024, 82% of wall time was in mixed steps (median 720 ms vs 81 ms decode-only), and 12-13% of all rank-time was spent waiting on another rank's prefill. ## Claims - New `SchedulerConfig.prefill_release_min_dp_ranks` / `--prefill-release-min-dp-ranks K` (default 0 = off). With PSI > 1 and K > 0, off-cadence steps release prefills on every rank if at least K DP ranks have prefill work, and defer them on every rank otherwise, including capacity-bound ranks. Cadence steps are unchanged. - The count is one CPU `SUM` all-reduce of an int32 over the DP group per step, in `_has_global_unfinished_reqs`. title: [Perf][Core] Hash prompt-embeds blocks in parallel for prefix caching
summary:
## Overview With prefix caching, the engine sha256-hashes every `prompt_embeds` block on each request. This PR instead hashes the embeds of a request's new full blocks on a small, lazily created thread pool (`hashlib` releases the GIL), slicing one `memoryview` of the tensor instead of running torch ops per block so the threads don't serialize on the GIL. The digests land in the request's existing per-block cache, so block hashes are byte-identical for every prefix-caching hash algo. ## Claims At 262k tokens x 4096 bf16: 1.17 s --> 0.22 s At 262k tokens x 8192 bf16: 2.21 s --> 0.35 s. ## Validation Unit test validate that hashing prompt embeds on the thread pool does not change any block hash, including blocks hashed later as the request grows. ---

title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Reduce the shared expert for MegaMoE without sequence parallelism
summary: ## Purpose Kimi-K3 with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel` and `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` serves garbage: no crash, normal throughput, wrong tokens. `KimiMoE` builds the shared expert with `reduce_results=False`, and the MegaMoE branch of `forward` adds its output locally through the replicated up-projection, with no collective. That is correct under sequence parallelism, where the shared expert is replicated (or does its own reduce-scatter). With PP > 1 sequence parallelism is off (`pipeline_parallel_size == 1` in `use_sequence_parallel`), so the shared expert is TP-sharded and its partial outputs are never reduced: each rank continues with a different, incomplete hidden state. This PR lets the shared expert reduce its own output in that case. Sequence-parallel and non-MegaMoE paths are unchanged. DeepSeek-V4 already does the same (`reduce_results=self.use_native_mega_moe`). Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue covers this. #54347 enables sequence parallelism under PP for Kimi-K3, which would avoid this path, but it is a feature PR and does not fix the fallback; this fix is still needed while SP is off under PP. ## Test Plan 4x GB200 nodes (16 GPUs), `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`, aggregated serving. summary: ## Overview After decoder preemption or a partial promotion caused by a full CPU primary tier, the KV Offload P2P tier still reports PD cache hits that trigger an unsatisfiable second fetch and wait for the 30-second timeout. title: [Bug][Quantization] MXFP8 linear kernel selection ignores the requested activation scheme — weight-only (W8A16) checkpoints silently run W8A8
summary: ### Summary `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` selects an MXFP8 linear kernel from `(N, K)` weight shape and compute capability alone. Unlike the sibling `init_mxfp4_linear_kernel` / `init_mxfp6_linear_kernel`, it has **no `activation_quant_key` parameter**, and `Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig` has no activation field — so selection cannot express or enforce the activation precision the checkpoint asked for. On Blackwell (SM100), a **weight-only (W8A16)** MXFP8 checkpoint is therefore routed to the W8A8 FlashInfer kernel, which quantizes the BF16 activations to FP8 (E4M3). The accuracy loss is applied **silently** — no warning, no error. Two open PRs (#59460, #63378) independently call this exact dense-linear path out as a known gap they are leaving for a follow-up, because the activation key never reaches `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel`. ### Mechanism (all on `main` @ 7ff608a03) The MXFP4/MXFP6 selectors thread the activation key and gate on it: - `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:1050` `init_mxfp4_linear_kernel(..., activation_quant_key=None)` → `:1054` `_resolve_linear_activation_key(...)` → `:1082` `kernel_cls._supports_quant_scheme(kMxfp4Static, activation_quant_key)` gate. The MXFP8 selector does not: - `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:961` `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel(*, weight_shape, bmm_batch_size=None)` — no activation parameter. - `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/Mxfp8LinearKernel.py:13` `Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig` carries only `weight_shape` + `bmm_batch_size`. - Selection loop (`__init__.py:~988-1012`) runs only `is_supported()` (compute capability)

title: [Bugfix][XPU] Forward num_splits to the XPU flash attention kernel
summary: ## Purpose The XPU flash attention shim in `vllm/_xpu_ops.py` accepts `num_splits` and then drops it: it is listed in the "not used in xpu kernel currently" block and never forwarded to `vllm_xpu_kernels.flash_attn_interface.flash_attn_varlen_func`. So the `max_num_splits = 1` that `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` sets in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py` never reaches the kernel, which keeps choosing its own split count via `get_num_splits()`. This PR forwards it as `num_splits_kv` and moves the parameter out of the stale comment block that made the omission look deliberate. The determinism suite could not catch this. `_random_prompt(10, 50)` in `tests/v1/determinism/utils.py` only pads when the target exceeds 50 words, so it returns roughly 16 tokens: the KV of every request fits inside a single kernel block and no backend has a split to be inconsistent about. This PR adds `_prompt_with_tokens(target_tokens)`, which tokenizes with the test model to hit an exact token count, and uses ~2k-token prompts in the bs=1 vs bs=N test. A residual violation survives this fix and is a **separate** defect, not addressed here: the XPU kernel serves decode (`max_seqlen_q == 1`) from `cutlass_paged_decode_interface` and prefill from `cutlass_chunk_prefill_interface`, and those two reduce over KV differently (the decode path has its own FP32 `max_logits`/`exp_sums` and a cross-sub-group SLM epilogue). title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Report failed pulls per request with several KV cache groups
summary: ## Overview On a model with several KV cache groups whose transfer groups are all full attention, one failed NIXL KV pull stops the decode engine. HiSparse decode is such a model: it adds KV cache groups that take no part in the transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`). The worker reports the failed request's block IDs in `invalid_block_ids`, and `Scheduler._handle_invalid_blocks` raises for any model with more than one KV cache group. This reports those failures through `failed_recving` only, so the request fails (or is recomputed) and the engine keeps serving. Related: #53779 (transfer groups), #53781 (HiSparse host-resident groups), #52232 (HMA receive failures). ## Claims - With more than one KV cache group, a failed pull is reported only in `failed_recving`. `invalid_block_ids` stays empty, so the scheduler no longer raises, and the request ends as `FINISHED_ERROR` (or is recomputed under `kv_load_failure_policy: recompute`). - With one KV cache group nothing changes: the request's block IDs are still reported. - HMA layouts are unchanged; they already skip `invalid_block_ids`. ## Validation **Unit, CPU.** `test_transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished` gains a case with a second KV cache group outside the transfer, the shape HiSparse adds. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview > **Merge order:** #66569 → #67402 → #67403 → #67404 → #67405. This is part 1 of 5; merge each only after the previous one. summary: ### Your current environment ### Question What is the intended support scope for layerwise external KV cache loading in vLLM? The connector API exposes `start_load_kv()` and `wait_for_layer_load(layer_name)`, which appear to allow cache transfer to overlap with model execution. However, it is unclear which model paths and execution modes provide the synchronization points required to use this safely. We would appreciate clarification on whether layerwise loading is a supported integration pattern with defined requirements, or whether connectors must implement model-specific handling. ### Background We are integrating UCM with vLLM for external KV cache loading. Our deployment uses: - vLLM 0.27.1 - GLM-5.2 - Two H100 nodes - Layerwise external KV cache loading - `--enforce-eager` We observed accuracy degradation on long-context evaluation workloads. During investigation, we found that indexer computation could consume cache data before the corresponding attention-layer load wait. This raised a broader question about the synchronization contract for layerwise loading. ### Our understanding of the API A typical layerwise connector would: 1. Submit initial cache loads in `start_load_kv()`. 2. Return while some transfers remain in flight. 3. Wait for a layer's cache in `wait_for_layer_load(layer_name)`. 4. Overlap subsequent transfers with computation. For this to be safe, every relevant cache consumer needs a synchronization point before its first read. title: [RFC]: Near-Native Deterministic Serving on Hopper via Native Dispatch, Length-Keyed Split-KV, and KV Obligation Admission
summary: ### Motivation Enabling `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on Hopper (`SM90`) in upstream vLLM currently sacrifices substantial throughput and tail latency across three layers: 1. **Linear / MoE / Compilation Fallback:** Hopper currently disables `torch.compile` and routes BF16 GEMMs and MoE layers through slow batch-invariant Triton fallbacks (`~20–25%` dense slowdown; `>2×` MoE slowdown). 2. **Unsplit Attention Bottleneck at Long Context:** `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` forces single-split FA3 (`num_splits=1`), adding `+32–35%` single-stream decode latency at `8k–16k` context. 3. **Capacity-Preemption Phase Drift:** When KV blocks exhaust under load, recompute preemption replays already-decoded tokens through prefill, breaking bitwise equivalence whenever decode uses split-KV (`num_splits > 1`) while prefill uses single-split attention. ### Proposed Change We propose closing all three gaps via **three cleanly separable PRs** (plus one small companion PR in `vllm-project/flash-attention`): - **Companion FlashAttention PR:** https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/224 — per-request split counts (`num_splits_per_request`), external split accumulators (`split_workspace`), fixed MMA warpgroups, and fixed `stride_LSE_partial` for reusable large-capacity workspaces. - **Layer 1 (`PR 1`):** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68361 — Hopper Native Linear & MoE Dispatch - **Layer 2 (`PR 2`, Draft awaiting FA3 pin bump):** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68362 — Length-Keyed FA3 Split-KV & Dual CUDA Graphs - **Layer 3 (`PR 3`, standalone on `main`):** https://github.c

title: [CI][ROCm] Transcendental, reduction and MFMA bounds for specialized decode (T1 of #68016)
summary: ## Purpose Completes the primitive tier (T1) of #68016 for the AMD monokernels. #67135 checked the device helpers that have a closed form — roundings, packings, scale codes, data movement — and asserted them bit-exact. This adds the helpers that cannot be bit-exact: the hardware transcendentals, the wave reductions and the MFMAs. The point of the series is that comparing a monokernel against vLLM's own ops cannot localise a bug, because both sides reach for the same helpers and a shared bug cancels. The same argument applies to tolerances: a tolerance measured from the kernel it checks proves nothing. **Every bound here is derived a priori** — from AMD's documented instruction accuracy, from the helper's own source, or from the arithmetic of the accumulator — and is written next to the assertion that uses it. T1 stays a debugging aid, not the numerical contract. The contract is `DecodeNumerics` (T2), at the decoder layer's public entry point, and it lands next per #68016. title: [Frontend] Bound structured-output compilation with the existing timeout
summary: ## Purpose `vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py` already ships a compile timeout, and its docstring states exactly what it defends against: ``` Prevents ReDoS attacks where adversarial regex patterns (e.g. nested quantifiers like `(a+)+b`) cause exponential DFA state-space explosion, hanging the inference worker indefinitely. ``` But `backend_xgrammar.py` applies it to one of five constraint types. `JSON`, `GRAMMAR`, `CHOICE` and `STRUCTURAL_TAG` all carry client input from the same request field and call the compiler directly. This PR applies the existing timeout to those four paths. No new configuration variables, no behaviour change for the `REGEX` path or for inputs that compile quickly. ## Why the JSON path needs it A JSON schema of an object with N **optional** properties forces the compiler to track which subset has been emitted, so the work follows the number of subsets rather than the input size. Measured on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0` (RTX A6000, 20 vCPU host, default config): | schema | body | compile time | |---|---:|---:| | 1,000 optional properties | 31 KB | 3.7 s | | 2,000 optional properties | 57 KB | 28.7 s | | 10,000 optional properties | 319 KB | > 500 s | | 2,000 **required** properties | 74 KB | 0.2 s | | 20,000 **required** properties | 788 KB | 6.1 s | Two thousand optional properties cost more than twenty thousand required ones in a body thirteen times larger, and `choice` / EBNF grammars don't show the effect. That points at the power set over optional members. Compilation runs in a pool of `(cpu_count + 1) // 2` workers, and `_create_compiler` sets `

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Preserve WRITE receive mappings after consumer abort
summary: ## Overview Fix a KV block leak on the MoRIIO WRITE consumer (D) when a request is aborted while waiting for remote KV. Related: #56089 fixes scheduler-side transfer accounting. summary: ## Summary AITER's custom all-reduce IPC buffer is hardcoded to `8192 * 1024 * 8 * 2` == 128 MiB (`effective_max_size()` returns 64 MiB). title: Add Mooncake EP all-to-all backend

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Map adapter keys back through Transformers' reversed WeightRenamings
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Transformers v5 renames some checkpoint weights at load time (the `WeightRenaming`s in its `conversion_mapping`), and PEFT saves adapters under those renamed module names. Native vLLM models name their modules after the checkpoint, so LoRA weights on renamed modules match nothing and get dropped without a warning. This PR catches those adapter keys at load time and maps them back through the reversed renames, using the mappings Transformers already ships. This is the generalised version of #60131, which hard-codes the rename for GLM-5.3-Flash only. The idea comes from @hmellor, who pointed at how the Transformers modeling backend reuses `WeightRenaming` ([base.py#L318-L320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4ed4c4433b87e45d72f401f27f1b56c932c90071/vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py#L318-L320)). Root-cause discussion is in huggingface/peft#3896. #60666 is the bigger version of this, which applies the renames to the checkpoint itself. This one is LoRA-only and can land on its own. ## Claims - GLM-5.3-Flash LoRA on `f_b_proj` (saved as `self_attn.forget_gate.f_b_proj`) is applied, without any model-specific change. With #56327, `f_a_proj` is applied as well. - Mixtral router LoRA (saved as `mlp.gate`, vLLM has `block_sparse_moe.gate`) is applied. On `main` it is silently dropped. - Adapter keys that resolve to a module on `main` are mapped exactly as before, so nothing that works today changes. ## Validation Tested on `main` at d80ddaac73 (the base of this branch), 1x H100, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`. **Log-probs.**

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Backoff last prompt token for sliding window in P/D (#65550)
summary: ## Motivation In P/D disaggregated serving, the decoder recomputes the last prompt token ($N - 1$) to sample the first output token. When all $N$ tokens are transferred, the sliding window group is laid out for position $N$, dropping the block holding position ```math $N - W , whenever (N - W + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{\text{block\_size}} ``` Consequently, FlashAttention's sliding window query at $N - 1$ reads position $N - W$ from `null_block` (#65550). ## Proposed Changes Scope `_prefill_backoff` to sliding window attention models (`SlidingWindowSpec`) in both NIXL (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`) and Mooncake (`mooncake_connector.py`), following the precedent already established for **Mamba** and **DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay**: 1. Prefiller computes $N - 1$ tokens, keeping position $N - W$ within the active sliding window on the sender. 2. Connector transfers $N - 1$ tokens to the decoder. 3. Decoder loads $N - 1$ tokens and natively recomputes token $N - 1$ with its full sliding window intact. 4. Pure full-attention models (Llama, etc.) remain untouched with 0 backoff, avoiding the multimodal boundary splitting and prompt-logprob complexities that stalled #59330. Fixes #65550. ## Relationship to Prior Work - **#59330** (@ivanium): Proposed universal backoff across all models, but encountered blockers around multimodal inputs and prompt logprobs. This PR restricts the backoff strictly to `SlidingWindowSpec` (mirroring Mamba and DSV4.1), serving as a clean, low-risk bridge fix. - **#60545** (@njhill): Proposes transferring hidden states in KV cache padding so decode never recomputes

title: [ROCm][Perf] Avoid materializing padded bf16 in the ViT fp8 attention path
summary: ## Purpose `_vit_fp8_asm_segment` quantizes q/k/v for the padded-head fp8 assembly FMHA. For each of the three tensors it currently: 1. materializes a padded BF16 tensor (head_dim → 128), 2. takes `abs().amax()` over that **padded** tensor, 3. builds an FP32 copy of the padded tensor, converts to fp8, then copies again for `.contiguous()`. Steps 1 and 3 are avoidable, and step 2 reads `128/72` of the data it needs — the pad is zeros, so `abs().amax()` is identical whether taken before or after padding. This takes the amax on the unpadded tensor and allocates the padded buffer directly in fp8, filling only the real lanes. The FP32 intermediate then covers only the real head_dim, no padded BF16 tensor is created, and the result is contiguous by construction. **Numerically identical**: amax is unchanged by zero padding, and the padded lanes end up zero either way (`0 / scale → 0 → fp8 0`). Profiling Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B on MI355X attributed **0.557 s of a 13.7 s window** to this glue — one fp8 convert, one amax reduction and one layout copy per ViT attention call (1620 of each per window = 135 calls × 12 iterations). That cost is also what forces the fp8 path to sit behind a large minimum segment length: lowering that cutoff so every segment uses fp8 measured **−4.8%** before this change, because each extra segment paid the glue. ## Test Plan Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (MXFP4), 8x MI355X, TP1 x 8 data-parallel replicas, offline max-throughput, 20000 samples per arm, same node and config, repeated runs averaged. ## Test Result | build | relative throughput | n | |---|---|---| | without t

title: [ROCm][Perf] Pad sub-128 vision head_dim to the aiter ASM FMHA tile
summary: ## Purpose aiter's assembly FMHA for gfx950 ships code objects for head_dim **128, 192 and 256 only**. A vision tower with a smaller head cannot reach it and falls back to `ck_tile`. Qwen3-VL uses head_dim 72, so that fallback is its default path today. Profiling Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B on MI355X: | path | head_dim at kernel | useful TFLOP/s | |---|---|---| | `ck_tile` (current) | 72 native | 409 | | aiter ASM, head zero-padded | 128 | **1101** | The padded kernel does `128/72` = **1.78x** the matrix work and is still **2.7x better per useful FLOP**. Zero-padding is safe: `softmax_scale` stays `1/sqrt(head_dim)` and the padded lanes are zero, so they contribute nothing to Q·K or to amax. Padding only pays on large segments, so the varlen batch is partitioned — segments at or above a length threshold go individually through the padded ASM kernel (the longest additionally use the fp8 variant, which pays for its quantize pass), and everything else stays on a single batched `ck_tile` call. **When no segment is large enough, the original path is taken unchanged**, so smaller vision inputs are unaffected. fp8 descales are computed per call from the segment's own amax rather than a running history: vLLM feeds zero-filled dummy inputs during profiling and cuda-graph warmup, and a history would collapse toward zero, after which real activations overflow fp8. Non-ROCm and non-aiter paths are untouched. ## Test Plan Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (MXFP4), 8x MI355X, TP1 x 8 data-parallel replicas behind one router, offline max-throughput, 20000 samples per arm, identical config and node across arms. title: [RFC]: First-Class, Orchestrator-Agnostic KV Hint Envelope for Agentic Workloads
summary: > [!NOTE] Please review alongside companion PR #53423 . > ## Motivation RFC #51428 proposes a router-initiated “KvHint” surface as a first-class construct for e2e programmatic KV management between vLLM and an orchestrator (such as Dynamo). This RFC proposes a concrete implementation of this hint protocol, such that it is extensible, expressive, and durable: the protocol is compatible with various orchestrators, enables semantics-free expression of various types of hints (e.g. fetch, share, …), and guarantees durability via typing and versioning. Today, integrations (such as [Dynamo PR #13134](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13134)) prototype vLLM KV hints via indirect, untyped plumbings, such as `SamplingParams.extra_args` and `kv_transfer_params`. KvHints instead provides a typed, versioned request contract within vLLM which can be accessed by routers, schedulers, cache managers, and KV connectors: ``` Router / control plane -> KvHintsEnvelope -> vLLM request ingress -> EngineCoreRequest.kv_hints -> Request.kv_hints -> scheduler-visible metadata ``` ## Proposed API ### Canonical Types The canonical transport types – `KvHintsEnvelope`, `KvHintAction` – should be broadly accessible and live outside any specific cache manager or connector: ``` vllm/v1/kv_hints/ __init__.py protocol.py KvHintsEnvelope KvHintAction ``` ### Typed Envelope Contents A `KvHintsEnvelope` requires: 1. A `protocol_version` 2. A `message_id` 3. A list of `KvHintAction` objects Each `KvHintAction` contains: 1. `action_id` 2. `action_version` 3. `action_type` 4. An action-specific JSON payload

summary: ## Overview `SlidingWindowMLASpec.merge` is the only attention `merge` that does not compare the fields declared on `AttentionSpec`. `FullAttentionSpec.merge`, `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` and `SinkFullAttentionSpec.merge` each end with the same loop over `fields(AttentionSpec)`, and `RSWASpec.merge` delegates to the full-attention one; the sliding-window MLA version compares nine hand-picked fields and takes `specs[0]` for everything else, including `head_size`, `dtype`, `num_kv_heads`, `block_size` and `page_size_padded`. `is_kv_cache_spec_uniform()` decides whether a model's layers can share one KV cache group by calling `merge()` and catching `AssertionError`, so layers that disagreed on one of those fields were reported as uniform: they were grouped together and the cache was sized from the first layer's spec instead of failing. The comparison now lives in `_assert_uniform_attention_fields` and is used by all four merges, since a fourth copy of the loop is how the gap appeared. No open PR makes this comparison. #55187 converts the same `assert`s to explicit raises so they survive `python -O`, but it keeps the same hand-picked field set and is currently conflicting with main; this change adds the missing comparison, so the two touch the same lines and whichever lands second needs a rebase. #63411 fixes `bounded_replay` in the spec-promotion path and adds a test elsewhere in the same file. title: [KVConnector] Add generic control RPC channel (RFC #51639)
summary: ## Overview Implements [RFC #51639](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51639): a single, generic, connector-defined control channel. title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3.1] Fuse the DSA decode prologue
summary: ## Purpose On ROCm, a Kimi-K3.1 DSA layer (MXFP4 indexer, `fp8_ds_mla` cache, DCP8) runs 37 kernels per decode step. Most of the prologue is small launches. title: [Bug][KV Offload] FS tier reports EIO instead of ENOSPC when the disk fills
summary:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text main @ 1648fef, Linux, C extension (fs_io_C) and Python fallback both affected. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug When the filesystem behind the `fs` offload tier fills up partway through a block, the store fails with EIO (C path) or an OSError with errno=None(Python fallback). It should fail with ENOSPC. write(2) returns a short count when space runs out mid-block; only the next write returns ENOSPC. `_store_block` in csrc/fs_io.cpp maps the short count to EIO, and `_store_block` in tiering/fs/io.py raises `OSError("Short write ...")` without an errno. A full tier can't be told apart from a failing disk, in logs or in code (#54363 item 4 needs the errno). Reproducer, 512 KiB tmpfs, 192 KiB blocks, 4 stores: C ['ok', 'ok', 'EIO', 'EIO'] Python ['ok', 'ok', 'errno=None', 'errno=None'] Expected: ENOSPC for stores 3 and 4. Quotas (EDQUOT) and RLIMIT_FSIZE (EFBIG) go through the same path. I have a fix and will open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

summary: <!-- Title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3.1] DSA layers in the AMD specialized decode --> <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Runs Kimi-K3.1's 24 DSA layers inside the AMD K3 specialized decode (`decode_backend=latency_specialized`, #60683, #61498). title: [KV Offload] Bound PUT staging and schedule aligned batches
summary: ## Overview Add opt-in bounded PUT staging and group-correct batching for tiered KV offload. When both a primary tier and a secondary tier (e.g., KVCR) are configured but the primary tier is small (for instance, KVCR Guard owns secondary tier memory), offloading from the primary tier to the secondary tier can be slow without batched staging. For instance, a 5,384-chunk offer cannot fit an approximately 873-slot host pool even when a much larger secondary cache is free. ### Illustrative Example Run KVCR as a secondary tier. The primary tier's host pool of 873 chunks sits in front of the large secondary tier. A long request offers 5,384 chunks in one step. - **Before:** the primary tier must allocate all 5,384 chunks at once. However, it can't, so the whole offer is rejected, and that repeats every step. Nothing reaches the secondary tier, even though it has room. - **After (with this PR)** (`put_batch_chunks=256`, `put_max_inflight_chunks=512`, `put_get_reserve_chunks=128`), the offer is split into aligned batches of up to 256 chunks: - At most 512 chunks are staged at a time, and 128 primary chunks always stay free for loads (GETs). - When a batch has been copied into the primary tier and cascaded to the secondary tier, its credit is freed and the next batch goes. - The request reaches the secondary tier in about 21 batches instead of never. - If the request finishes first, it offers all of its remaining chunks in its final store pass, because its GPU blocks are freed right after. ## Claims - **Bounded batches:** running requests offer whole aligned multi-group units, cappe

title: [XPU] Flatten N-D input in XPU W8A16 FP8 linear kernel
summary: `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel.apply_weights` overrides `apply_weights` directly instead of `apply_scaled_mm`, so it bypasses the base class's 2D flatten / output-unflatten logic that the other FP8 linear kernels in this file rely on (see `FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` in `ScaledMMLinearKernel.py`, and `XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel.apply_scaled_mm` which does `output.view(*output_shape)`). This mirrors the same class of bug fixed for the XPU MXFP8 linear kernel in #66494 ("Flatten N-D input in XPU MXFP8 linear kernel"). Apply the same fix here: reshape the input to 2D before calling the op and restore the leading dims on the output. ### Root cause (why this only reproduces under torch.compile) The real oneDNN `fp8_gemm_w8a16` kernel (`vllm-xpu-kernels/csrc/xpu/onednn/onednn_matmul.cpp::check_and_create_output_tensor`) actually supports both 2D and 3D input and *preserves* the leading (batch) dim in its output: 2D in -> 2D out, 3D in -> 3D out. So under plain eager execution, calling this op with a 3D activation happens to work, because the real kernel tolerates it. However, the `register_fake` meta implementation registered for this op in `vllm/_xpu_ops.py` (`_fp8_gemm_w8a16_fake`) always collapsed its output shape down to 2D `(M, N)`, regardless of input rank: ```python input_2d = input.view(-1, input.shape[-1]) M = input_2d.size(0) N = q_weight.size(1) return torch.empty((M, N), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device) ``` Under `torch.compile`, Dynamo/AOTAutograd use this fake kernel to infer shapes while tracing, not the real kernel. So a 3D input traces to a 2D fake output

title: [Kernel][XPU] Tensor-descriptor Q loads in Triton MLA decode attention
summary: ## Overview On Intel XPU, `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (TRITON_MLA decode) now loads its Q and Q-PE tiles through tensor descriptors instead of masked pointer loads, for the 576-wide MLA tile (`kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64) only. The K/V loop and the math are unchanged. The KV gather stays on pointer loads: this is a Q-tile change, not a descriptor path for the paged gather. Context: RFC vllm-project/vllm#42545 recorded that this kernel could not use descriptors because of its paged KV gather. That still holds for K/V; the change here covers only the Q tile, which is a plain strided 2D tile, and only on XPU. Scope: the gain applies to XPU runs that use `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` explicitly, or that reach it as the fallback when `XPUFlashAttnMLABackend` rejects a config (`vllm/platforms/xpu.py`). The default XPU MLA backend (FlashAttnMLA) is faster than TRITON_MLA even with this change, and it is not affected. End-to-end numbers are on one model (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat); most are with `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` forced, plus one real fallback configuration (`--block-size 16`, where FlashAttnMLA rejects the config). Fp8 KV was not measured end to end. CUDA and ROCm launch the unchanged kernel. Not a duplicate: no open PR adds tensor descriptors to this kernel. 18 other open PRs touch `triton_decode_attention.py` or its test file. Those that change the same code: - vllm-project/vllm#51861 (draft) rewrites the Q-PE load; after it lands the descriptors here (`shape=[q_head_num, Lk]`) must be rebuilt for the split Q / Q-PE layout. - vllm-project/vllm#51685

This measures table extent, not total RSS or HBM. title: [RL][Weight Transfer] PP-stage broadcast groups: each stage receives only its weights, in parallel
summary: ## Purpose Part of #54477. **Stacked on #67840.** The diff includes it until it merges. Opt-in: `engine.stage_groups = True`, with `use_load_plan`. With pipeline parallelism, a broadcast still delivers every byte to every inference rank, so each PP stage takes in the other stage's weights too. With stage groups, each stage receives only its own weights, and the stages receive in parallel. **Setup (`_stage_handshake`, once, at the first update, right after its start has built the workers' load plan):** - Every rank all-gathers its PP rank and a mask over the planned names. A name is needed unless the plan writes nothing of it on that rank; fallbacks count as needed. A stage needs the union of its workers' masks. - A stage's sub-communicator is its workers plus the trainer ranks that send it the most bytes, so no trainer rank sits on two rings (that would halve both). **Per update:** - One RPC carries every stage's rounds (one per trainer rank on its ring) and the tail. - Each stage runs its rounds back to back on its ring. - The tail holds what a rank owns for a stage whose ring it is not on, such as the stage-boundary layer or vision weights. It then goes in main-group turns. ## Results (GB200, Kimi-K3 TP8×PP2, 1.56 TB, 12 sender ranks, real start) | | Per update | GSM8K before → after | |---|---|---| | Every rank receives all weights (#67840) | 3.5 s | | | Stage groups | **1.67–1.73 s** | 0.952 → 0.949 | Each stage takes in ~780 GB; at the ~630 GB/s measured for a broadcast, the wire floor is ~1.2 s. A two-group NCCL benchmark on the same 7 nodes reaches 626–640 GB/s per g

title: [RL][Weight Transfer] Packed NCCL: planned receive into the model
summary: ## Purpose Part of #54477, 3 of 3 for packed NCCL transfer. **Stacked on #67839.** The diff includes it until it merges. With a load plan, the worker knows ahead of time where every received byte goes, yet the packed receive still unpacked each tensor in Python and loaded it through `load_weights`. Planned receive builds, once per update metadata, the copies from each received chunk into the model: - Copies of the same role (the name without its indices) that are evenly spaced in source and destination are coalesced into one strided copy (DSv4.1: 8,180 → 933 copies per turn). Data moves in whole words, not byte by byte. - Each chunk then costs one broadcast and one `_foreach_copy_`. - Fallback names load once per turn. - Pieces at an offset their dtype cannot view are realigned. A split tensor whose writes need it whole is joined. - Metadata reused from an earlier call is not checked against the manifest again. - **Receive buffers:** every sender shares the device's `slot_buffers`, which are released at finish because the KV cache wakes into that memory under sleep mode. Before, each sender's buffers were held until finish; on Kimi-K3 that alone was ~24 GiB per GPU. ## Results (GB200, steady-state update, real start, sleep level 2 around each update) | Model | Before | After | GSM8K before → after | |---|---|---|---| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 2.7 s | 0.62 s | 0.947 → 0.948 | | DeepSeek-V4.1 | | 0.9–1.1 s | 0.911 → 0.908 | | Muse-Spark | | 1.45 s | 0.955 → 0.953 | | Qwen3.8 TP2+EP | | 1.87 s | 0.951 → 0.952 (chat) | "Before" is #67839 with #67836 (generic packed receive with the

title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct reload: check that an update loaded every parameter
summary: ## Overview A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) now checks at `finish_weight_update` that the update loaded every parameter cold start loaded. If any is missing, `finish` raises and names it, before post-load processing runs. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F2). On main, a parameter the update leaves out keeps its runtime bytes. `begin` views them as checkpoint bytes, and `finish` reruns post-load processing over them. That is silent corruption whenever the processing changes the layout or isn't idempotent (transposes, requantization, packing). Padded MoE parameters are worse: `begin` zero-fills them (`padding_fill_params`), so leaving one out serves zeros. ## Design - **Required:** the parameter names cold start's `model.load_weights` returned (`track_loaded_params`, recorded by `record_checkpoint_layout`). - **Delivered:** the names this update's `load_weights` calls returned between `begin` and `finish`, plus the tensors written without `load_weights`: - M2N's in-place writes; - the load plan's direct copies (`load_planned`, #65235). Both report through `mark_loaded`. The load plan's trace of `load_weights` loads nothing, so it is kept out of the record. - Names are resolved to parameter objects before comparing, so a tied parameter counts under either name. Fused and per-expert checkpoint names both count, because `load_weights` reports parameter names. - **Exempt:** parameters matching `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`. Level 2 sleep keeps exactly the tensors an update doesn't rewrite, so they are the ones an update may leave out

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS storage rank derivation with pipeline parallelism
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `HF3FSKVConnector` uses the TP rank alone as its storage rank. With pipeline parallelism, workers of different stages that share a TP rank write the same data file (`hf3fs_vllm_data_file_<rank>`) and register as the same metadata rank, although they hold different layers. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Dequantize ModelOpt 4-D FP8 block scales in DequantLinearMethod
summary: ## Overview `DequantLinearMethod` (#66118) runs a projection that the checkpoint stores in FP8 in BF16. title: [CI][ROCm] float64 reference + specialized decode format primitives (T1 of #68016)
summary: ## Purpose An AMD monokernel fuses most of a decoder layer into a single launch. When one comes out wrong, the symptom shows up far from the cause, and the checks we have today cannot localise it: they compare the monokernel against vLLM's own ops, and both sides reach for the same rounding and packing helpers. title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Reduce retained arena and encoder-cache memory
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Multimodal inference can retain a large allocation while using only a small part of it. This PR limits SHM arena registration to each slot's used prefix and compacts excess backing storage behind cached GPU encoder outputs. It builds on #51207 and the already merged #57368; savings from #57368 are not attributed to this follow-up. ## Claims - **CPU arena registration:** register an 8 MiB-rounded prefix per slot, growing geometrically to the slot capacity. Eight slots containing 13.5 MiB tensors register 128 MiB per reader instead of the default 2048 MiB. Shared pages must not be multiplied by TP size. Slot reuse still waits for all readers and H2D completion. Failed unregistration falls back to an owned pageable copy; registration errors are cleared before fallback. Prefixes remain available for reuse and can eventually grow to full capacity. - **GPU encoder storage:** after applying an eviction batch, group retained outputs by storage and copy a group only when potentially reclaimed bytes are at least the bytes copied. Publish replacements only after all copies succeed; OOM preserves the originals. With an EC connector, isolate shared views at insertion and disable subsequent relocation to preserve registered addresses. Logical cache contents and embedding values are preserved. Copies add temporary allocation pressure and cost; failed compaction does not provide a hard memory bound. Allocator-reserved memory need not fall. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Claude Code's `ToolSearch` returns `tool_reference` blocks, which hold tool names only. vLLM passes them to the chat template as `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` parts.
