title: [CI][Test] Give seeded MTP sharded sampling its measured divergence bound
summary: ## Purpose `(L4) Distributed DP Basic` intermittently fails on main in `test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence`. It failed both attempts of [103590](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103590), which made that main build red. It also failed first attempts in 103334, 103404, 103549, 103675 and 103676, and 6 times between Nov 2 and Nov 5 (99322–100126). Every failure is the **seeded** comparison, never greedy: ``` AssertionError: seeded: 4/20 prompts diverged at [12, 13, 17, 18], beyond near-tie noise AssertionError: seeded: 5/20 prompts diverged at [12, 13, 16, 17, 18], beyond near-tie noise ``` Across all 14 failures the divergent set is always 4 or 5 prompts drawn from {12, 13, 16, 17, 18}. Those are GSM8K prompts. The low-entropy "repeat the word" prompts (0–9) never diverge. The seeded pass samples at temperature 1.0, so any small logit difference between the replicated and sharded boots can push a draw across a CDF boundary. Greedy only flips on true near-ties. A sharding or per-request seed bug would hit the repeat prompts too and diverge across most of the batch. So this is noise just above a shared bound of 3, which was calibrated mostly on greedy. The fix gives the seeded pass its own bound of 6/20 and keeps greedy at 3/20. The DSpark test still uses 3. Test-only change. ## Test Plan - CI: `(L4) Distributed DP Basic`. - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`. ## Test Result - Ruff passes. Not run locally (needs 2 GPUs). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [RFC]: CPU offloading cache lifecycle metrics
summary: Expose CPU offloading cache retention and eviction pressure through chunk lifecycle metrics. | Metric | Type | Definition | |---|---|---| | `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_chunk_idle_before_evict_seconds` | Histogram | Time from the last demand access to capacity eviction; measured from readiness if never accessed | | `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_chunk_lifetime_seconds` | Histogram | Time from successful store or promotion completion to capacity eviction | | `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_chunk_evictions_total` | Counter | Number of chunks evicted to reclaim capacity, split by `reused` | Common labels: `model_name` and `engine`. The eviction counter additionally has a `reused` label. Each observation represents one **chunk residency**. A chunk may contain multiple GPU blocks. Reinserting a key or reusing a slot starts a new residency. A demand access includes a scheduled CPU-to-GPU load, an explicit peer read, or a request offering an already-cached chunk. Count once per request per residency. Lookup probes, background cascades, and pin releases do not refresh the access timestamp. `reused="true"` means at least one successful CPU-to-GPU or peer read during the residency, excluding background cascades. Record histograms only at capacity eviction. Failed writes and cache resets produce no eviction observations.

title: [Scheduler][RFC] Opt-in adaptive prefill time budget
summary: ## Summary Related to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62574 and the [design discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62574#issuecomment-6900973564). This is a **draft experimental implementation**, requesting feedback on scope and scheduler integration. title: [Performance]: `--prefix-match-unit` recovers hybrid-model prefix hits on multi-turn and agent traces, but on the Triton/FLA GDN backend it costs about 30 ms of TTFT on almost every request
summary: ### Misc discussion on performance #### Summary I measured prefix caching for a hybrid model (Qwen3.5-4B, GDN + full attention) against a full-attention model of the same size (Qwen3-4B) on replayed multi-turn chat and coding-agent traces. The GPU is one L40, so GDN prefill runs on the Triton/FLA backend. Four results came out that I could not find reported for real multi-turn workloads: 1. With default flags, the hybrid model recomputes 1.6–1.7× as many prompt tokens per turn as the full-attention model on the same conversations. On chat the hit rate is 56% against 71%. 2. `--prefix-match-unit 16` closes that gap. The hit-rate difference drops below 1 percentage point and the recompute ratio to 0.88–1.08. 3. With that flag, TTFT gets about 30 ms worse on about 96% of requests, although the same requests recompute 176–288 fewer tokens. For a 4B model the flag is a net loss on this backend. 4. The cost is the extra prefill stop at `floor((P - 1) / unit) * unit` that `_mamba_block_aligned_split` adds when the backend has no internal prefill checkpoints. A profiler timeline shows that the extra step is mostly host time: the GPU is busy for about one third of it. #65186 looks like the change that removes this stop on Triton/FLA, and #61779 / #61952 target the host time of GDN prefill steps. title: [Bugfix] Use 64-bit row offsets in the block-FP8 Triton GEMM
summary: ## Overview `_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` forms its A-row and C-row offsets (`offs_am * stride_am`, `offs_cm * stride_cm`) in int32, so once `M * K` or `M * N` passes 2**31, rows past that bound read A from, and write C to, the wrong address. This casts `pid_m` to int64 where both row offsets are formed, the same fix #63054 and #64614 made in the W4A16 Triton kernels, and adds a past-the-bound test in #63054's style. This change was prepared with AI assistance. I found no open PR for this kernel's offsets; #52577 edits this kernel's launcher in the same file for a different issue (the K tile); the two diffs touch different lines and apply together cleanly. ## Claims - Block-FP8 Triton GEMMs with `M * K` or `M * N` past 2**31 now compute the right rows. On main the `M * K` case returns NaN in the last rows and the `M * N` case hits an illegal memory access. - The per-row A scale offsets also become int64, since they are built from `offs_am`. The B offsets stay int32, so a single block-FP8 weight with `N * K` past 2**31 (over 2 GiB in FP8) would still wrap; this PR does not cover that case. ## Validation New test `test_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_rows_past_int32_offsets`, two cases, on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with Triton 3.8.0: | Case | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | K=17408, N=256 (`M * K` past 2**31) | fails, `rel_diff` is NaN | passes | | K=256, N=34816 (`M * N` past 2**31) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` | passes | The main column is this branch with only `fp8_utils.py` reverted to its base, 6c15c6cc5, and each case ran in its own pytest proces

title: [RFC]: Exact-end Mamba states and whole-state eviction for hybrid prefix caching
summary: ### Motivation. With prefix caching in Mamba `align` mode, a hybrid model caches its recurrent state only at block boundaries inside the prompt. Those blocks are big (4,352 tokens on GLM-5.3-Flash), and in agent traffic each turn's prompt is the previous prompt plus its output plus new content. So the next turn resumes at the last block boundary of the previous prompt and prefills the rest of that prompt and the whole previous output again. For example turn 1 is 10,000 prompt + 500 output tokens and turn 2 is 10,800 tokens: the cached state is at 8,704, so turn 2 prefills 2,096 tokens and 1,796 of them were computed before. Under load, blocks go back to the free queue one by one in LRU order, so a state can be evicted while the KV pages it needs stay cached (or the other way), and the request falls back to an earlier state anyway. The FlashState paper (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate) studies this on coding-agent traces and proposes two pieces. This RFC is about upstreaming them. ### Proposed Change. Everything is off by default, and a setup that isn't supported yet is refused at startup with the missing requirement named. The plan is four milestones, each its own PR or a short stack. Milestones 3 and 4 lift milestone 1's refusals of speculative decoding and KV cache events. **Milestone 1: exact-end states and whole-state eviction** (#66881) - [ ] `--mamba-frontier-checkpoint`: when a request finishes, its running state and its last partial KV page are cached under a key for its exact processed length, in all groups or none. title: Feat/invariant with prefix cache
summary: ## Purpose This PR makes prefix caching compatible with batch-invariant inference, as part of the batch-invariant work tracked in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433#issuecomment-4624935971. Prefix caching is an important performance path for real workloads with shared long prefixes, but it introduces a new source of variation: the same prompt can resume from different prefix-cache hit lengths depending on cache state. In batch-invariant mode, those different hit lengths should not cause the remaining prefill work to be scheduled with arbitrary chunk boundaries, because that makes the effective prefill shape depend on cache state rather than on a stable canonical policy. This PR fixes that by using a shared canonical chunk-block policy for both: - the prefix-cache hit length accepted by the KV cache manager, and - the prefill chunks scheduled after the cache hit. With this, batch-invariant prefix-cache requests resume from stable block boundaries, and the remaining prefill work is chunked consistently even when the raw cache-hit length differs across runs or batch compositions. The core behavior is: - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT_CANONICAL_PREFILL_CHUNK_BLOCKS=0` means auto. - When batch-invariant prefix caching needs canonical prefill chunking, auto resolves to the current default of 8 scheduler blocks. - Explicit positive values continue to select a fixed chunk size in scheduler blocks. - Prefix-cache hit canonicalization and scheduler prefill chunking now use the same chunk-block policy. This keeps the high-cache-hit prefix-caching path useful under `VLLM_BATCH_IN

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix fp8 KV cache prefill query quantization selection for Kimi-K3
summary: # Issue #50056 — `kimi-k3 --kv-cache-dtype fp8` fails despite `use_prefill_query_quantization` Reported error: ``` Worker failed with error 'Kimi-K3 fp8 KV cache requires an fp8 prefill query; enable --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'.' ``` …while the reporter already passed both `--attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization":true}'` and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. ## 1. Root cause The flag was being silently dropped by MLA prefill backend selection. `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.determine_prefill_query_data_type()` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`) only returns the FP8 query dtype when **all three** of these hold: 1. the KV cache is quantized, 2. `attention_config.use_prefill_query_quantization` is set, 3. the *already selected* MLA prefill backend can consume an FP8 query (`FLASHINFER`, `TRTLLM_RAGGED`, `TOKENSPEED_MLA` — not `FLASH_ATTN`). title: [XPU] Prefer W8A8 FP8 linear kernel on Xe3p XPUs with native FP8
summary: ## Purpose On XPU, FP8 linear layers always run weight-only (W8A16), even on GPUs with native FP8. Today the only way to get it is `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`. This PR makes `init_fp8_linear_kernel` prefer W8A8 on Xe3p, using a new `XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel.has_native_fp8()` (wraps `torch.ops._xpu_C.is_xe3p_arch()` from vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.17, False if the op is missing). Only XPU code is touched. The kernel list order is unchanged. summary: ## Overview Muse Spark normalizes each expert's output before the top-k weighted sum, so its MoE must return the unweighted per-route outputs `[T, top_k, H]`. On ROCm the MXFP4 experts get them by repeating the normed input `top_k` (8) times and calling AITER `fused_moe` with one route per row, and at TP > 1 every route's partial sums over all `H` columns are then reduce-scattered before the norm. This PR runs the experts through AITER's two-stage MoE API (ROCm/aiter#7135): - **Native routes.** One input row per token, on the `[T, top_k]` routes; stage 2 writes each route to its own row (`per_slot`). The kernels are the ones AITER selects for today's repeated-input call (`config_shape`), so the route outputs are bitwise identical. - **Column-sharded stage 2 at TP prefill.** For eager batches of ≥ 1024 tokens, the MXFP4 stage-1 output and its scales are all-gathered along the intermediate dim and stage 2 runs against this rank's `H / tp` output rows of `w2`. The norm then needs only a `[T, top_k]` sum-of-squares all-reduce and an all-gather of the finalized columns, instead of a `[T, top_k, H]` reduce-scatter. It replaces #63290 (native routes) and #63263 (column-sharded down projection), which reached into AITER internals (`_fused_moe_impl` with `_metadata_transform` and `_stage2_override`) and could not be combined. With the public API both are one code path. #63290 and #63263 are closed in favour of this PR. **Dependency.** Needs ROCm/aiter#7135. summary: ## Purpose Two flaky tests on main between Nov 14 and Nov 16. Each test asserts something that isn't guaranteed. - **`distributed/test_cpu_all_reduce.py::test_cpu_all_reduce[12]`** (MI300 Distributed Comm Ops, 1 of 22 runs): `EADDRINUSE` on the stateless TCPStore. - The stateless group's port was picked before spawning the workers, but bound only after the default gloo group had opened its full mesh of ephemeral sockets (66 pairs at 12 ranks). title: [Quantization][ROCm] Fix symmetric GPTQ loading and optimize RDNA INT4 repacking
summary: ## Purpose This PR fixes redundant zero-point handling during symmetric GPTQ loading and reduces the cost of RDNA hybrid INT4 weight preparation. **GPTQ loader fix.** Symmetric GPTQ `uint4b8` uses a fixed zero point of 8, but checkpoints may still contain packed `qzeros`. Passing these redundant checkpoint zero points to RDNAHybrid can fail during startup, for example: ```text Zero points must be [320, 16] but got [16, 320] ``` The cleanup lives in `AutoGPTQLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()`. GPTQ still registers and loads `qzeros` normally; after loading, the loader removes the checkpoint tensor when the selected kernel has `zero_points=False`, before backend preprocessing. This handles the mismatch at the shared loader boundary. Only the tensor is removed: `kernel.w_zp_name` stays intact. Symmetric CPU W4A16 can leave zero points unset, while CPU W4A8 can use the retained name to create its required fake zero point. ExLlama and Marlin can likewise create their runtime zero points or placeholders. Explicit-zero-point processing is preserved. **RDNA loading optimization.** The hybrid preprocessing introduced in #40977 expands every packed INT4 value to INT32, then repacks it into ExLlama order. Reuse the existing `gptq_shuffle` on a contiguous packed clone instead, followed by the transpose into the existing runtime layout. The clone protects checkpoint storage from the in-place shuffle; inference kernels and dispatch are unchanged. title: [Core][Scheduler] Add opt-in prefill chunk backoff for steps that would idle
summary: ## Overview Stacked on #66725. GitHub will show that accounting fix in this diff until it merges; please review only `2275216942`. Adds `SchedulerConfig.prefill_chunk_backoff` (`--prefill-chunk-backoff`, **off by default**). On a step that would otherwise schedule nothing, because nothing is running and the head of the waiting queue cannot allocate its next prefill chunk, the head is retried with halved, block-aligned chunks. The full-sequence check stays on, evaluated at the smaller chunk, and the resulting cap sticks until the request's KV is freed. This does not fix the null-padding undercount in #66724. It is a separate liveness backstop for KV held outside those reservations, for example finished prefill KV waiting on a slow decode pull. Related to #66724. ## Claims - With the flag off, scheduling is unchanged. The new test compares per-step token traces with the flag on and off for workloads that are not idle. - With the flag on, an idle head that cannot fit a full chunk but can fit a half chunk is admitted once, with no preemption. The cap is cleared when its blocks are freed. - The tighter cap goes through the same early return as #66725 (`min(uncapped, cap - recyclable)`), via `admission_cap_overrides`. ## Validation New CPU tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_prefill_chunk_backoff.py`: - `test_prefill_chunk_backoff_when_idle`: a finished P/D producer holds blocks until decode pulls them. Flag off schedules 0 tokens for 20 steps. Flag on finishes at a half chunk, 0 preemptions, exactly one backoff. - `test_prefill_chunk_backoff_noop_when_not_idle`: mixed work

title: [Bug][KVEvents]: Use effective block size in DCP full KV cache report
summary: When decode context parallelism is enabled, the full KV cache report path used the raw physical page size from the cache spec instead of the DCP-effective block size from the manager. This caused an assertion failure in resolve_block_hashes() when a client set kv_cache_report_mode to "full" and a prefix cache hit existed, terminating the EngineCore. Use manager.block_size (which includes DCP scaling) when emitting BlockStored events for cached prefix blocks in the full-report path.

title: [Quantization][RL] Online quantization under direct reload: keep the online method where quantize-on-load can't apply; reload mode in the compile cache key
summary: ## Overview Fixes for online quantization under direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, from #65802), split out of #68041, which makes direct reload the default. Part of #54477. ## Why this is needed (for #68041) Some online-quantized configurations can't be updated by direct reload: - online schemes with no checkpoint counterpart; - gpt-oss; - FP8 block layers whose TP shards aren't 128-aligned. Today direct mode refuses them **at model construction**. That's the right behavior while direct mode is opt-in: the user asked for direct reload, and these can't do it. #68041 makes direct reload the **default**. A refusal at construction would then mean these configurations can't **start** at all, for every user of them, including the many who never update weights. Today, in the default layerwise mode, they start and serve fine. So the refusal has to move from "can't start" to "can't reload": - **this PR** lets them build: each such layer keeps its online method, which serves exactly as it does in layerwise mode today; - **#68041** refuses them when a reload is attempted (at weight-transfer engine init and at every `start_reload`). Nothing new becomes reloadable; these configurations are still refused. What changes is that they can still be served. | Configuration | Today, default (layerwise) | Today, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` | This PR + #68041 (direct by default) | |---|---|---|---| | gpt-oss + online quantization | starts, serves | fails at construction | starts and serves as today; reload refused | | FP8 block layer with shards not 128-aligned | starts, serves | fail

title: [Bugfix][Prefix Caching] Keep hybrid evictions on a prefix every KV cache group can hit
summary: ## Overview A hybrid prefix hit needs every KV cache group, but a finished request's blocks enter the LRU free queue one group at a time, so pool pressure evicts one group's head while the other groups' blocks stay cached and can never be hit. This PR frees a request's blocks by token position across all groups and uncaches the blocks no lookup can reach. Related: RFC #57111, #48532, #61282, #63808 (see "Why this is not a duplicate"). ## Claims - After a hybrid request is freed, pool pressure evicts its tail token positions first in every group, so its remaining blocks always form a prefix that every group can hit. Before, a full-attention group could lose its head (hit drops to 0) while the Mamba or sliding-window blocks of the same request stayed cached. - The immediate (`KVCacheManager.free`) and deferred (`pop_blocks_for_free`, used with async scheduling + KV connector consumers) free paths now produce the same order. - Full-attention blocks past the last position every group can resume from (for example the last cached Mamba state under sparse retention, or decode tokens) lose their hashes when the request is freed, so they are reused before other requests' older, still-hittable cache. - Outputs cannot change: only free order and cache membership of unreachable blocks change. Default behavior for dense (single-group) models is unchanged. - Scheduler-side cost on hybrid models: about +5% scheduler KV time per request in the benchmark below (one cache-hit lookup per freed request). No GPU work, no synchronization. ## Validation **Unit tests, failing before and passing af

title: [Core][Mamba] Retain decode-crossed Mamba boundary states under sparse retention
summary: ## Update: hold the latest decode state and cache it on free (design by @ZJY0516) The implementation was reworked; the new design is by @ZJY0516, implemented with AI assistance (Claude Code). The goal is unchanged: under sparse retention, a follow-up turn that replays the output should resume near its end. What changed is how the decode state is retained. A request now caches exactly one decode state, the latest decode-crossed boundary, and caches it once, when the request is freed. ### Why the previous version was reworked The previous version hashed each decode-crossed boundary block as it was crossed, then evicted the previous one on the next crossing. Align mode frees a boundary state block one step after the crossing, so by that point the previous block was already back in the free queue. That required: - a per-request side table, plus a hash-equality guard against the block having been reallocated; - calls to the private `BlockPool._maybe_evict_cached_block`; - injecting the decode boundary through `replay_boundaries`. It also leaked one cached entry per preemption. ### How it works now - **Hold.** Align mode already writes the exact state at each crossed boundary into its own block: the copy source of the crossing step. Under sparse retention, `MambaManager.remove_skipped_blocks` keeps the block at the latest decode-crossed boundary instead of freeing it one step later. That block is released unhashed once the next boundary is crossed. - **Cache on free.** When the request is freed (finish or preemption), `MambaManager.cache_blocks_on_free` hashes that one block. title: Add a debug tool to detect non-explicitly returned outputs under BCG
summary: ## Purpose BCG records a sequence of CUDA graphs broken apart by eager functions that can't be CUDA graphed. At each eager break, we copy the tensors returned by the eager function in a static buffer that the next graph consumes. This leaves room for developer errors that could be very difficult to debug: if an eager function allocates a new tensor that wasn't returned explicitly but survives outside of the eager call (like assigning to an instance variable if the eager function was a class method), the new tensor won't be copied to the next CUDA graph, causing a potential silent correctness issue. ``check_non_explicit_outputs`` detects this at capture time and returns a list of tensors that were not returned explicitly. ## Test Plan Tests added for the new debug tool. Run with: ``` python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph_debug.py -v ``` ## Test Result N/A --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

title: [Bugfix] Hybrid Mamba + KV connector: reconcile diverged per-group prefix hits instead of `max()`/trim
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #46453 the hybrid (full-attention + Mamba) prefix-cache-hit divergence bug described: - On `main` #44243, `num_new_local_computed_tokens = max(per_group_hits)` over-reports the local prefix when a request's FA prefix is evicted but a deeper Mamba state block survives, crashing the engine (or leaving dirty KV). - PR #45804 switches to the dense `min` but trims the sparse Mamba per-group list, which drops the state block (silent correctness bug) and still crashes for some external-hit lengths. This PR takes the spine (full-attention) `min` as the local hit and **reconciles the divergence after the external length is known**, choosing the correct operation per case. title: [Scheduler] Fix KeyError in PP2 when last stage finishes request via tool-call parser
summary: ## Summary In pipeline parallelism (PP≥2), the last PP stage can finish a request — for example via a tool-call or stop-string parser — before the master scheduler (rank 0) has processed the step output. When this happens the request ID is present in `num_scheduled_tokens` but absent from `model_runner_output.req_id_to_index`, causing an unguarded dict access to raise `KeyError`. **Root cause:** The existing guard at the top of the output-processing loop only covers `request is None` and `request.is_finished()`. It does not cover the case where the request is still in `self.running` but was silently removed from the model runner's output batch by the last PP stage. ## Fix Add a `req_id not in model_runner_output.req_id_to_index` guard immediately after the existing check. When triggered: 1. Set `request.status = RequestStatus.FINISHED_STOPPED` 2. Call `_free_request(request)` — reclaims KV cache blocks 3. Add to `stopped_running_reqs` — removes from `self.running` after the loop 4. Emit an `EngineCoreOutput` with `finish_reason` — gives the API server a proper finish signal 5. `continue` past the rest of the per-request processing A bare `continue` is **not** sufficient: it leaks KV cache blocks and leaves the request in `self.running` indefinitely, which causes scheduling deadlocks under sustained load. ## Reproduction PP2 + TP8, `--enable-auto-tool-choice`, `--no-async-scheduling`, AMD MI355X (ROCm 7.2.3). Observed as `KeyError: '<req_id>'` in `scheduler.py` during tool-call responses. ## Test plan - [ ] PP2 + tool calling smoke test: request completes without `KeyError`

title: [Feature]: Skip unused last-layer FFN computation during prefill while preserving mathematical equivalence
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Background and motivation In ordinary autoregressive generation, prefill processes the entire input sequence, but predicting the first output token only requires the final hidden state of the last input token in each request. The model still executes the final-layer FFN for every input position, although the FFN outputs at earlier positions are not used by subsequent generation. This computation can be removed without changing model weights, retraining, or sacrificing the model's mathematical expressiveness. The goal is to accelerate prefill by eliminating unused computation while preserving the mathematical equivalence of the required outputs. ## Principle A Transformer FFN operates independently on each token; it does not exchange information between tokens. After the final-layer attention operation, evaluating the FFN only for the last input position of each request is sufficient to produce the hidden state needed for next-token prediction. Earlier positions have no subsequent decoder layer consuming their FFN outputs, so those computations can be skipped. All attention computation and KV-cache writes remain unchanged, allowing subsequent decode steps to access the complete historical keys and values. The mathematical expression of the required outputs is preserved. The principle applies to multiple Transformer architectures with token-wise FFNs, rather than being specific to Qwen. Tasks requiring outputs at every input position, such as prompt logprobs, are outside this last-position-only case. ## Proposed changes After the fin

title: [Bugfix][V1] Retain the EAGLE hit blocks below a sliding window across a KV connector import
summary: ## Purpose Related: #57610 / #57613 (same all-or-nothing miss from a different trigger), RFC #54661. With the hybrid KV cache manager, an EAGLE-family drafter whose layers use sliding-window attention (DFlash, window 2048, block 64) and prefix caching, a prefix-cache hit on the draft group needs `cdiv(window - 1, block) + 1 = 33` contiguous cached blocks (`SlidingWindowManager._contiguous_blocks_for_hit`): one more than the window spans, because EAGLE matches one block past the boundary and drops it. The hybrid lookup reconciles to the shortest group, so a 0 draft hit zeroes the target's hit too. On a decode engine in P/D disaggregation that run never exists. A KV connector import allocates only the blocks inside the window (`get_num_skipped_tokens(P) = P - window + 1 - extra_retained_tokens`), NIXL ships only those, and `cache_blocks` after the load hashes only those: 32 blocks. Every later request whose prompt is longer than the window misses on all layers; the fallback only accepts a run reaching block 0. Prefill engines are unaffected, because local compute hashes the block before `remove_skipped_blocks` nulls it, which is why this only shows on the decode side. Fix: for an EAGLE group (annotated, or every group when none is, mirroring the coordinator), widen `SlidingWindowSpec.extra_retained_tokens` by `(cdiv(window - 1, block) + 1) * block - (window - 1)` (65 tokens here), so `get_num_skipped_tokens` lands exactly that many whole blocks below the last full-block boundary for every prompt length. This includes groups packed as `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` by block-outermo

See Known limitations (b). - **The decision is made before post-load processing.** It is made at construction, which is before post-load processing rewrites `moe_config`, as the snapshot was. title: [Perf][MoE] Backport triton#10875 to the bundled triton_kernels v3.5.1
summary: ## Overview The `triton_kernels` v3.5.1 that CUDA builds bundle declares the bitmatrix strides of `_topk_forward` and `_sum_bitmatrix_rows` `tl.constexpr`. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Drain sub-connector KV cache events in MultiConnector (fixes worker memory leak)
summary: ## Overview `MultiConnector` never forwarded `get_kv_connector_kv_cache_events()` to its sub-connectors. title: [Performance]: Long-prefill decode starvation survives prefill/decode interleaving — head-to-head from two stacks on 2× GB10, plus a 4×98k-prefill OOM boundary
summary: ## Summary We run DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (MoE + sparse MLA) on a **2× DGX Spark GB10 pair** (TP=2 over a 200 Gb RoCE fabric, one 128 GB unified-memory node per rank) as a small-office shared service. Long-document ingestion (one user pastes a 100k-token document) repeatedly starves concurrent short chat requests. We already reported the raw phenomenon and the `--prefill-schedule-interval` mitigation in #54919 (that fix works for the *Qwen* model we tested: 1.2 → 22.6 tok/s on the short stream). This issue is different: we ran a **controlled head-to-head between two complete stacks** — one stock fork build, one heavily patched community recipe — and the conclusion is that the patched recipe does **not** fix starvation, it only changes its shape. We also hit a hard memory boundary at 4 concurrent long prefills that looks like #50298. Posting because we would like to know what upstream considers the sanctioned path here. ## Setup Hardware: 2× DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified memory each), 200 Gb RoCE v2 (`GID_INDEX=5`), TP=2 + EP across nodes. Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, fp8 checkpoint, 156 GB / 48 shards, ~79 GB per rank. Workload, identical for both stacks (same script, same weights): - long request: 560,000 chars of English filler (~**98,620 prompt tokens**) + a Chinese instruction, `max_tokens=8` - short request: an 11-token prompt, `max_tokens=128` - short requests are launched 3 s after the long ones start - a random 16-byte hex prefix is prepended to every long doc so prefix caching cannot mask the prefill - 3 short-chat concurrency runs: 8 and 1

title: [MoE][RL] MegaMoE NVFP4: load each scale on its own, combine after loading
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (load plan), item L2 (closes RFC item X5 for MegaMoE). - P1's loader is called with a meta tensor for every name the load plan copies direct. `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` skipped its `_record_global_scale` bookkeeping on meta, so after a planned update `l2_activation_scale` kept its old value. - This PR moves that bookkeeping out of the loader. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> <!-- Author-review draft. Suggested title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add Hybrid KV Backend with bounded SSD streaming --> ## Insight SimpleCPU's disk backend (#49644) streams KV through one/two buffers per direction, but has no CPU hot cache. Native tiering retains CPU caching, but requiring an SSD prefix to fit in CPU memory limits restoration under capacity pressure (#62931). #62932 addresses that limitation by bounding promotion to CPU capacity and recomputing the remainder. **Hybrid KV Backend combines a CPU hot cache with bounded SSD streaming:** keep SimpleCPU's small default pools, borrow additional hot-cache rows when SSD work grows, and copy CPU hits during storage-read gaps. The accepted prefix can exceed host-cache capacity as long as GPU admission succeeds. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Required KV prefix] --> H[CPU hot hits] P --> S[SSD misses] H -->|Bounded H2D batches| G[Final GPU allocation] S -->|O_DIRECT reads| B[Default slots + leased hot rows] B -->|H2D; reuse after completion| G ``` The benefit has two parts: hot hits **avoid SSD reads**, and their H2D copies can occupy otherwise idle transfer time. Dynamic slots increase read concurrency within the same host budget, trading some hot-cache capacity for more I/O in flight. Opting into `kv_offload_backend="hybrid"` on `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` retains its scheduler, logical disk slots and completion protocol, extending its disk backend with hot copies and bounded read concurrency. ### Dynamic Staging Accounting ```text Fixed host KV budget +--------------------+--------------------

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Shard the kpool indexer prefill across TP
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On ROCm, every tensor-parallel rank of GLM-5.3-Flash runs the k-pool indexer over all prefill rows, so the indexer work is replicated TP times. This reuses the existing ShardQ token split for the indexer only: each rank scores its own tokens and the ranks all-gather the selected pool ids, while the sparse attention itself stays head-sharded. Pool ids are what makes this cheap. A row selects `index_topk / index_kpool` = 512 pools and expands them to 2051 token ids, so exchanging pools instead of tokens moves a quarter of the data; narrowing them to int16 where they fit moves an eighth. The exchange becomes small enough that halving or quartering the scoring is worth it. Supersedes #60601, which implemented the same idea on the indexer row-sharding helpers (`PrefillRowShard`, `balanced_prefill_row_shard`) that #63956 removed in favour of ShardQ. title: [RFC]: Word-level timestamps for speech models from per-request encoder outputs
summary: ### Motivation. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` accepts OpenAI's `timestamp_granularities[]=word`, but no model returns `words`. The serving code never reads the field, and `verbose_json` works only for models whose decoder writes segment timestamps as tokens (Whisper, FunASR, FireRedASR2). Word timestamps are a common need for captions, search and editing (#39735 asks for them in `/v1/realtime`). Many speech LLMs can produce word timestamps from the audio encoder. For example, an auxiliary CTC head on the encoder gives frame-level label scores, and a forced alignment of the final transcript against them gives each word's start and end. The head depends only on the audio, so it can run inside the encoder pass. Only the alignment needs the transcript, and it is CPU work after generation. vLLM has no path for this. Two pieces are missing: 1. **A way to return a per-request tensor computed in `embed_multimodal`.** Encoder outputs go only to the encoder cache. 2. **A transcription hook that sees more than text.** `post_process_output` and `parse_diarized_transcript` receive only the generated text. So projects align beside the engine. The NeMo vLLM plugin keeps encoder states in the worker, runs its head after generation and adds the timestamps in middleware. FunASR runs its encoder outside vLLM. Qwen3-ASR runs a separate aligner model next to `vllm.LLM`. The in-tree attempt for Whisper (#47664) captures cross-attention in every decode step; by its author's benchmark this costs about 39% of throughput even for requests that do not ask. title: [Attention] Decide the sparse MLA prefill route once in the metadata builder
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview A sparse MLA prefill runs one of three ways: dense MHA, masked MHA, or sparse MQA (the top-k kernel that decodes use). Today three places each decide part of that choice: - the metadata builder (`use_dense_mha`); - `MLAAttention._use_sparse_mha`, at every layer call; - `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mha` (`prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`). Seven other places read or re-derive it. This PR makes the metadata builder decide once per metadata build and store the result in `SparseMLAPrefillMetadata.route`. Every consumer reads that field. Serving behavior does not change. ## Background: the three prefill routes For causal, sink-free sparse MLA, all three compute the same attention in exact arithmetic: each query attends only to its top-k keys chosen by the indexer. They differ in the kernel, and in rounding and query quantization (sparse MQA can take an fp8 query). Models with learnable sinks (HY-V4) need sparse MQA and force it. | Route | Kernel | Keys per query | When | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `SPARSE_MQA` | Absorbed MLA: q is projected into the latent space and one shared latent KV is gathered by top-k index (the kernel decodes use). Reads the compressed, possibly fp8, cache. | its top-k | The fallback when no other route applies, and always for decodes. | | `DENSE_MHA` | KV is decompressed per head with `kv_b_proj`, then causal MHA with no top-k mask. | all causal keys | Every prefill in the step has `seq_len <= top-k`, so the top-k already contains every causal key and no mask is needed. | | `MASKED_MHA` | Same decompressed MH

title: [Bugfix][Benchmarks] Count tokens, not chunks, in peak output throughput
summary: ## Purpose `vllm bench serve` reports a **peak output token throughput far below the average output token throughput**, which is impossible by definition. With speculative decoding enabled: ``` Output token throughput (tok/s): 410.61 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 113.00 <-- 28% of the average ``` The two metrics count different units. `output_throughput` uses the token counts the server reports in `usage.completion_tokens`. The peak metric instead rebuilds a token timeline from `output.itl` and adds **one token per entry**: ```python for itl_value in output.itl: current_time += itl_value token_times.append(current_time) ... tokens_per_second[second_bucket] += 1 ``` The OpenAI endpoint request functions append one `itl` entry per SSE chunk (`endpoint_request_func.py:240`, `:412`, `:528`), and a chunk can bundle several tokens — which is exactly what speculative decoding produces. `calculate_metrics` already accounts for this when deriving `output_len` ("multiple output tokens may be bundled together", `serve.py:595-599`), but the peak metric does not, so it measures chunks per second rather than tokens per second. This PR weights each chunk by the request's tokens per chunk, so the per-second buckets sum to the reported output token count instead of the chunk count. Limitation. The weight is the request's mean tokens per chunk, because the OpenAI streaming protocol reports token counts only once at the end of the stream, never per chunk. title: [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models
summary: # [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models ## Overview Hybrid-state (mamba + full-attention) models running MTP speculative decoding keep every request's speculative window allocated even when the dynamic spec-tier table resolves the step to K=0 at high batch counts — at a c32 crossing that is most of the pinned KV. This PR releases running rows' idle windows back to the pool at the K=0 crossing, admits waiting rows at the K=0 tier (the window born as null row slots), and promotes released rows back — priced against the formed-batch fit verdict plus the watermark — when the batch drains and the tier rises. On a public Qwen3-Next checkpoint the PR as submitted holds bench parity and converts the crossing's pool-exhaustion crash into graceful preemption; on a tuned stack the same mechanism measures +110% at the crossing (labeled below). Worker-side, the mamba metadata builders route draft-less decode rows through the align fold — released rows park at K=0 without a kernel premium. The release arm can exhaust the shared pool mid-call at the crossing — the PR ships the guard: `--kv-cache-valve-threshold` (default off) preempts the running tail when a waiting admission stalled on a relievable block shortage (optionally when usage crosses the fraction). The valve is general-purpose — it fires on any waiting-admission stall for any workload, and its tests run plain full-attention schedulers; it ships in this PR because the release arm needs it. title: [Feature][Attention] Add NIXL GPU Device API for MLA DCP A2A

title: [Kernel][Attention] Segment sliding windows in split-K; split-K for non-causal speculative rows
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Changes to the split-K (3D) path of the Triton `unified_attention`: 1. **With a pruned sliding window, the segments split the window instead of the whole sequence.** - Before, segment `i` covered tiles `[i * tiles_per_segment, (i + 1) * tiles_per_segment)` of `[0, seq_len)`. - At long context, most segments therefore fall before the window and return immediately, so the whole window was walked by one or two programs. - This applies to every sliding-window model on `TRITON_ATTN` (decode and spec verify). 2. **Non-causal speculative rows take the 3D launch.** - Multi-query rows of up to `MAX_3D_QUERY_LEN` tokens already use split-K when causal (#56148). Non-causal rows, i.e. the DFlash drafter's query block, were excluded. - The softmax reduction does not depend on the mask, so `reduce_segments` applies unchanged. 3. **Non-causal rows use fewer, fuller segments when the batch is larger.** - Each non-causal program carries a whole query block, so at short context a one-tile segment is mostly fixed cost (Q load, partial store, reduction). - Non-causal 3D launches therefore require at least `min(next_power_of_2(num_seqs), 8)` tiles per segment. - The kernel and `reduce_segments` take this as the same constexpr, so they agree on the segment count. ## Claims - **Gemma-4-26B-A4B on one MI355X, end to end.** 25 of its 30 layers are sliding window (1024). On ROCm, Gemma-4 is forced to `TRITON_ATTN`, so this is its default path. - Output throughput with 16k-token prompts: **+35% at concurrency 1, +28% at c=4, +5% at c=16**. - With 4k-token pro

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Stream DeepSeek DSML tool-call names and arguments like Python
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With the Rust frontend, a DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 tool call reaches the client as a single delta after its last token: the DSML tool parser buffers each `invoke` until its closing marker. The Python parser emits the function name when the `invoke` opens and streams the arguments (#58780). This makes the Rust parser stream the same way. #56334 by @thuanpham582002 fixes the same problem in the same way, and this PR builds on its approach. It was written before four changes to this parser (#56271, #62874, #62875 and #65375) and has had merge conflicts since September. This version differs in three ways: - It works on the current parser, keeping #62875's token-aware matching of the `calls` and `invoke` markers rather than searching the text for them. - It merges each chunk's fragments into one delta per call, as Python does, rather than sending several. - It adds end-to-end validation (below). ## Claims - The function name is emitted when the `invoke` header arrives. A string argument streams as it decodes; any other argument is emitted when its parameter closes, after the same schema conversion as before. - Final arguments are byte-identical to `main` for every input `main` accepts, except a repeated parameter name. title: [RFC]: LoRA adapter support for DFlash speculative decoding draft models
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM supports serving many LoRA adapters over a single base target model, but speculative decoding still requires a separate, fully-trained draft model per domain. When serving many domains, this is expensive: each domain needs its own drafter (e.g. 0.8B) held in memory, with corresponding I/O cost to load and swap. This RFC proposes applying LoRA adapters to the DFlash drafter, so a single base drafter can be specialized per-domain via small adapters instead of full drafters. In our experiments an R64 adapter is ~28x smaller than the 0.8B drafter it replaces, substantially reducing memory footprint and I/O latency when serving many domains, while keeping drafter quality within ~2% of a fully-trained per-domain drafter (measured by acceptance length behavior). This mirrors the efficiency win vLLM already provides for target-model LoRA, extended to the speculative-decoding drafter. ### Proposed Change. Allow a LoRA adapter to be applied to the DFlash drafter, independent of the target model: - The adapter wraps all drafter layers except `lm_head` and `embed_tokens`, loaded from a stage-2-trained LoRA checkpoint. - The drafter LoRA is specified via additional arguments in the speculative config, distinct from any target-model adapter. - The correct adapter is routed to the drafter and applied along its forward path. Initial support targets DFlash drafters specifically (tested with a GPT-OSS-120B target and a 0.8B DFlash drafter). This is distinct from target-side multi-adapter work (#49705, #48297) and from prior Eagle-style draft-model attempts. **Prior art /

title: [Bug]: Without the extensible KV cache, CUDA graph memory profiling allocates one KV block per request and OOMs at startup
summary: ### Your current environment RTX 4070 Laptop (SM89, 7.62 GiB), torch 2.14.0+cu132, vLLM main `b7e43db256`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug When the KV cache is sized from profiling estimates (`enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, or wherever the extensible cache is unavailable), Model Runner V2 runs `profile_cudagraph_memory`. That function first builds a throwaway KV cache in `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling` with `min(max_num_reqs, max_cudagraph_capture_size)` blocks, one per request. With 64-token blocks this is large. For Qwen3-1.7B plus a Qwen3-0.6B draft (56 attention layers) it is 256 blocks = 3.5 GiB, or 16k tokens per layer, before the real KV cache is even sized. ```python from vllm import LLM LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B", max_model_len=2048, enable_extensible_kv_cache=False, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, speculative_config={"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}) ``` ``` File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", in _init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling File ".../vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", in allocate_kv_cache torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.50 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 7.62 GiB of which 2.86 GiB is free. ``` Capture runs with zeroed dummy block tables (`BlockTables.get_dummy_block_tables`), so every request reads and writes block 0, and one block is enough. With a one-block profiling cache the same config starts. On 6 configs the CUDA graph estimates and greedy outputs were identical to the per-request cache. This issue was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); I ran and checked all results above.

title: [Bugfix][PP] Use the same hybrid KV cache block size on all pipeline stages
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Under pipeline parallelism, a stage of a hybrid Mamba model that holds no attention layer keeps the default KV cache block size, while the other stages align it to the Mamba page size. With prefix caching, this moves prefix-cache hits inside the other stages' Mamba blocks, and Nemotron-H models then give wrong outputs. This PR shares the block sizes chosen by the stages with attention layers across the pipeline-parallel group. Fixes #51752. Credit to @taking-lying-flat, who found the mismatch and proposed the same fix in #51764; credited as co-author. ## Claims - Every pipeline stage of a hybrid model uses the same KV cache block sizes as PP=1, also a stage without attention layers. - With prefix caching, Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 at PP=4 (default split; stages 0 and 3 hold no attention layer) gives the same greedy outputs as with prefix caching off, within the batch noise seen at PP=1 and PP=2. On main, 38 of 64 batched requests differ. - Prefix-cache hits at PP=4 land on the same block boundaries as at PP=1. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged. ## Validation ### Regression test `test_pipeline_parallel_mamba_only_stage_prefix_caching` runs `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview` at PP=1 and PP=2 with `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=5,35`, so the first stage holds only Mamba layers. title: [Bugfix] Force spawn when the CUDA driver was initialized outside torch
summary: ## Purpose vLLM switches the engine-core start method from `fork` to `spawn` when CUDA is already initialized in the parent process, but the check (`cuda_is_initialized()`) only sees torch's own lazy initialization. If the host process initialized the CUDA driver *outside* torch — another library or a C extension calling `cuInit`, or simply `ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1").cuInit(0)` — vLLM still forks, and the forked `EngineCore` dies with the misleading ``` RuntimeError: CUDA driver initialization failed, you might not have a CUDA gpu. RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. ``` `cuInit` is process-wide state and is not fork-safe, so no child can recover from it; the only fix is to spawn. This is the same failure shape as #46996 (where Triton's `is_active()` called `cuInit` at import), seen there from a different trigger. This PR adds `cuda_driver_is_initialized()`: a side-effect-free probe using `cuDeviceGetCount`, which returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED` until `cuInit` has run in the process and `CUDA_SUCCESS` afterwards. `_maybe_force_spawn()` now treats a driver initialized outside torch as a reason to spawn, with its own reason string. `cuda_is_initialized()` itself is unchanged, so `cuda_get_device_properties()` keeps its current behaviour. Duplicate check: searched issues/PRs for "CUDA driver initialization failed", `cuda_is_initialized`, `cuInit` + fork; no existing fix for the external-`cuInit` case. ## Test Plan - `tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py`: - `test_external_cuda_driver_init_forces_spawn[True/False]` — `_maybe_force_spawn` p

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Re-handshake a pull peer whose connection NIXL reports lost
summary: ## Overview In pull mode, invalidate a remote engine as soon as one of its transfers fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, so the existing drain, backoff and re-handshake path from #55471 reconnects it. Today the dead peer is kept, because its NIXL metadata stays loaded, and every later read to it fails until a restart. This is the pull-mode fix from #66795 (by Yongye Zhu, co-author here), split out so it can be reviewed apart from that PR's push-mode changes. It is an alternative trigger to #61500. Related: #59971 (production report), #66011 (see "Interplay with #66011"). ## Claims - A pull that fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (NIXL's `nixlRemoteDisconnectError`) invalidates its remote engine on the next `_cleanup_remote_engines`, even though the engine's metadata is still loaded. Its agents are removed once in-flight reads drain, and the next read re-handshakes. - Other transfer errors are unchanged: they invalidate the engine only when the metadata probe reports it missing (#55471). - Push mode is unchanged. ## Validation **Unit test.** `TestPeerReplacement::test_lost_connection_invalidates_peer_with_metadata`: a read fails with a remote disconnect while the peer's metadata stays loaded. `[True]` fails without the fix (the dead peer is kept) and passes with it. `[False]` checks that another error still keeps the peer. **End to end** (from #66795, run with an earlier version of this change that matched the error by name instead of `isinstance`; equivalent for NIXL's real exception). title: [Perf][CPU][DiffusionGemma] Run one-step DiffusionGemma reads in a single forward pass
summary: ## Overview This PR runs DiffusionGemma one-step reads in a single forward pass on the CPU backend. It adds `DiffusionConfig.single_pass_reads`, off by default. It is split out of #60527 and holds only the single-pass part. A one-step read sets `diffusion_read_only` and `diffusion_max_steps=1`. It is the default structured read in examples/features/structured_diffusion. Today it takes two engine steps. The first prefills the prompt and emits nothing. The second runs the canvas. With the flag on, the canvas runs in the step that finishes the prompt. No other open PR or issue covers this. I searched open PRs for single_pass_reads, single pass diffusion, DiffusionGemma one-step and DiffusionGemma CPU. I used Claude Code to help with this PR. OpenAI Codex was used for the rebase and validation below. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below. ## Claims - On a 44 vCPU Xeon with AMX, one-step reads are **21 to 25% faster for 188-token prompts and 12 to 13% faster for 1250-token prompts**. Reads with a cached prompt prefix are 21% faster. - Bursts of 4 reads are faster in all 8 shapes when comparing the fastest of 3 bursts per arm: 11 to 14% for 188-token prompts and 3 to 5% for 1250-token prompts. Medians of 3 bursts are noisier, see Validation. - Constrained reads (`diffusion_constrained`) fuse too, with the same gains. - Each read takes one engine step instead of two. Over 144 timed calls, engine steps fell from 312 to 168. - With the flag off, single reads are bit-identical to main. - With the flag on, outputs are close but not bit-identical. No label decision flip

title: [Feature]: Support NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming (nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b)
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch NVIDIA recently released **Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming** ([nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b)), a 600M-parameter multilingual streaming ASR model under the OpenMDW-1.1 license. Key features: - **Native streaming architecture** with Cache-Aware FastConformer-RNNT, supporting configurable chunk sizes from 80ms to 1120ms - **35 languages** (19 transcription-ready + 13 broad-coverage + 8 adaptation-ready), including German, English, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, etc. - **Automatic language detection** via `target_lang=auto` - **Punctuation & capitalization** built-in - On a single H100: **240 concurrent streams at 80ms chunk**, ~17x more than Parakeet RNNT 1.1B This would be a great addition to vLLM's supported ASR models, complementing the existing Voxtral Realtime and Qwen3-ASR support. The model is already available in HuggingFace Transformers (`AutoModelForRNNT`) and NVIDIA NeMo. ### Alternatives Currently, the only open-source streaming ASR options in vLLM are: - **Voxtral Realtime (4B)** — high VRAM due to persistent encoder KV-cache, limiting concurrent streams - **Qwen3-ASR (0.6B/1.7B)** — segment-based (5s chunks), higher latency Nemotron 3.5 would fill the gap for a lightweight, truly native streaming model with low latency and high throughput. ### Additional context - HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b - Architecture: FastConformer-CacheAware-RNNT with language-ID prompt conditioning - Primary framework: NeMo, with Transform

title: [RL] Support partitioned trainer source groups for NCCL M2N
summary: # [RL] Support partitioned trainer source groups for NCCL M2N ## Summary This PR builds directly on `main`, which includes merged [#60934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60934), and addresses [#59840](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59840). It lets a trainer-side producer partition the parameter manifest across disjoint source rank groups while preserving the per-parameter mesh and placement contract. [#60949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60949) is now stacked above this PR; it is not a prerequisite. This supports pipeline-parallel and other partitioned trainers where different trainer ranks own different parameters. It removes the requirement for a producer to gather or replicate pipeline-owned parameters across one common trainer group before calling NCCL M2N. A parameter's declared layout may still require collectives within its owning source group. Each parameter selects one canonical source group, and vLLM creates one NCCL M2N transfer communicator for that source group plus all inference workers. Before this PR, every parameter had to use the same participating trainer-rank set, even though each parameter could describe a different mesh factorization over those ranks: ```text all trainers + all inference workers -> one M2N communicator ``` After this PR, the source declares ordered, disjoint trainer groups and assigns each parameter to exactly one group: ```text all trainers + all inference workers -> one metadata/control group source group 0 + all inference workers -> transfer route 0 source group 1 + all inference workers -> trans

title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Select the whole-layer mono decode with --monokernel and remove mono/envs.py
summary: ## Purpose The ROCm MiniMax-M3 mono decode (#64111) and DSpark drafter kernels (#65386) were switched on by model-specific env vars in `mono/envs.py` (this envs file was added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64111). Every other monokernel uses `--monokernel`, including the MiniMax-M3 FFN-only. This removes `envs.py` from the model directory. `--monokernel` now runs every MiniMax-M3 monokernel the deployment fits: - Decode: the whole-layer mono decode if it fits (it needs MXFP8 attention, as in M3.1), otherwise the FFN-only decode (BF16 attention, as in M3). - Draft: the DSpark drafter kernels (7-token DSpark, TP4). - If none fit, startup fails and lists every reason. To run only some of them, name them in `additional_config`, e.g. `--additional-config '{"minimax_m3_monokernel": ["drafter"]}'`. Startup then fails only if none of the named kernels fit. The M3.1-Flash recipe now uses `--monokernel` (AgentX c1–c32 and the 1P2D preset; c64's 3-token draft fits no kernel). This PR also removes the `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO_CHECK` debug path (`mono/check.py`). ## Usage Env vars: `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO` and `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO_DRAFTER` are removed; `--monokernel` replaces both. title: [Feature] Enable triton autotuning for config reliant kernels
summary: ## Purpose Adds `--enable-triton-autotune` (equivalent to `--kernel-config.enable_triton_autotune`). When enabled, vLLM tunes Triton kernels that read launch configs from JSON tables during kernel warmup, before CUDA graph capture, and only for model shapes that have no config yet. Mamba `selective_state_update` (SSU) is the first kernel to use it. I will built on top of this PR and extend this to the other three families of kernels, namely: `fused_moe`, `w8a8 block fp8 gemm`, `lora`. Further information can be found in my proposal #58751. - **Off by default** at every optimization level (`-O0` to `-O3`). - **Generic:** a kernel opts in by implementing `TunableConfigTable` (`pending_items`, `tune`, `commit`) in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/triton_autotune.py`. - **Safe with multiple GPUs:** ranks gather the union of the work they need, split it deterministically, gather the results, and every rank saves the same configs. Every rank reaches every collective, so if one rank's tuning fails, startup logs a warning instead of hanging. - **Cached:** results are written to `$VLLM_TRITON_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` (default `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/triton_autotune/triton=<version>/<table>`). Later startups reuse them, even with the flag off. - **Validated:** candidates are timed with the same method as `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_selective_state_update.py`. A winner is only saved if its output matches the default config's. Re-scoped based on the reviews in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48980. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Honor the activation scheme in MXFP8 linear kernel selection
summary: ## Summary `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` dropped the activation quant key, so a weight-only (W8A16) MXFP8 checkpoint could select a kernel that quantizes activations to FP8 (the FlashInfer W8A8 kernels on SM100), silently clipping BF16 activations to E4M3 with no warning. The sibling MXFP4/MXFP6 selectors already thread the activation key and gate on it; MXFP8 did not. This threads an optional `activation_quant_key` through `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` and adds a permissive `_supports_quant_scheme` classmethod on the kernel base. The self-quantizing kernels (FlashInfer CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL, ROCm dot-scaled, and torch-native on CUDA) override it to decline a weight-only request, so it falls through to the W8A16 Marlin kernel. The parameter defaults to a sentinel, so callers that do not declare a scheme keep the historical selection (no gating); only the Quark OCP-MX caller is migrated here. compressed-tensors/modelopt (both W8A8) and the online path can follow up, and this aligns with #59460's `executed_activation_key()` direction. Fixes #65193 ## Testing `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py` — 45 passed (CPU-only). Added cases: a weight-only request on SM100/103 now selects `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`; an explicit W8A8 (`kMxfp8Dynamic`) request still selects the FlashInfer kernel; an unspecified request keeps the historical selection. Verified the new weight-only test fails without the gate (selects the W8A8 FlashInfer kernel) and passes with it. `pre-commit` clean (ruff, ruff-format, mypy). ## Duplicate check `gh pr list --state open --search "activation

title: [ROCm] Bound DeepSeek V4 steady-state memory on gfx1151
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fix gfx1151 / Strix Halo ROCm long-run instability for DeepSeek V4 DSpark `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` serving. The final reproduced failure was a TP logits all-gather stall/watchdog at the vocab-parallel logits gather boundary: ```text LogitsProcessor._gather_logits -> tensor_model_parallel_all_gather -> DeviceCommunicatorBase.all_gather -> torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor -> _ALLGATHER_BASE 64640 -> 129280 ``` This PR keeps the load-bearing memory fixes that bound paged-MQA/MXFP4 profiling workspace size and keep the gfx1151 expandable-segments lifecycle stable, then adds the narrow ROCm synchronization needed at the logits gather boundary. It does not change model weights, DSpark acceptance logic, graph mode, capture-size policy, quantization, RoPE, TP behavior, or GEMM kernels. ## Claims - Bounds ROCm paged-MQA/MXFP4 decode workspace sizing during profiling for the 100k-context DeepSeek V4 DSpark target. - Carries active `VllmConfig` through `ForwardContext`, allowing low-level ROCm profiling helpers to use scheduler/speculative limits instead of falling back to `max_num_batched_tokens`. - Keeps PyTorch expandable segments available during startup, profiling, graph capture, and remaining warmup, then disables them once for steady-state gfx1151 ROCm serving when they were initially enabled. - Keeps the conservative post-collective completion guard after the steady-state allocator transition. - Adds a ROCm-only current-stream synchronization before logits TP all-gather outside graph capture. - Does not add a new environment variab

title: [Frontend] Add serve warmup for completions, chat, and embeddings
summary: ## Summary This PR adds a pre-serve warmup feature for `vllm serve` that runs real requests against the async engine before the HTTP server starts accepting traffic. This avoids the first served request paying the lazy kernel compilation cost. ### What changed - `vllm/entrypoints/warmup.py` (new): adds `WarmupConfig`, `WarmupPrompt`, `load_warmup_config()`, and `warmup_engine()`. - `vllm/entrypoints/common/cli_args.py`: adds `--warmup-config` to `FrontendArgs` (serve only; not accepted by `run-batch`) and validates it in `validate_api_server_args` before the engine starts. The parsed config is passed to every API server worker via `args`. - `vllm/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/entry.py`: runs warmup in `build_and_serve` after the app state is initialized and before `serve_http()` starts accepting traffic. - `docs/serving/warmup.md` (new): documents the config format and serve startup behavior. Behavior: - At each concurrency level, every prompt runs: `max(concurrency, num_items)` requests are issued with at most `concurrency` in flight. - `prompt` and `messages` are rendered through the server's `OnlineRenderer`, the same path as `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`, so `--chat-template`, `--chat-template-content-format`, and `--default-chat-template-kwargs` apply. - Embedding warmup uses `PoolingParams(task="embed")` like `/v1/embeddings`, and sends one request per string of a list-valued `input`. ### Why this is not duplicating existing work I checked the existing issue and PR space for warmup-related work. title: [Deepseek] Warm the SM90 indexer decode schedule metadata for every batch size
summary: ## Overview Part of #64824; follow-up to #64827. On SM90, DeepGEMM compiles the DSA indexer's decode schedule-metadata kernel once per decode batch size rounded up to 32. With speculative decoding (DSpark/MTP verify `1 + k` rows per request) most of those sizes were never warmed, so they compiled on the request path after `/health`. This warms every bucket the indexer builder can produce, for the target and the drafter. ## Claims DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 + DSpark (k=5), H100 TP8, fresh JIT cache, CUDA graphs on, this PR vs `main` measured on the same pod (3 vs 3 runs, median): - **Cold-start TTFT p99 24.8 s → 3.6 s** over the first 1000 requests after `/health`. - **Cold-start output throughput 1067 → 1248 tok/s.** - **Runtime DeepGEMM compiles after `/health`: 28 → 0.** The main benefit is that it will no longer trigger these compilation in production serving, thus to make the service more stable. - No startup cost on H100: time-to-ready 998 s → 1003 s. Steady-state throughput 1384 → 1366 tok/s. - GB200 (SM100): 0 runtime compiles before and after, latency and throughput unchanged; fresh-cache time-to-ready +11 s (1769 s → 1780 s, consistent across 3 pairs: the metadata sweep is launches only on SM100), warm restarts unchanged. ## Validation **End-to-end cold start**, same harness for both arms: empty `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`/`TRITON_CACHE_DIR`/TileLang/FlashInfer/inductor caches, start the server, then send the same 1000 streaming requests twice — the first pass is the cold window, the second is steady state. title: [Core][Spec Decode] Back only the tail of DFlash/DSpark sliding-window drafter KV
summary: ## Purpose A DFlash or DSpark drafter's sliding-window layers are managed by the plain `SlidingWindowManager`, like a target SWA layer: - every prefill chunk allocates drafter blocks for the whole chunk; - the per-request reservation (`max_admission_blocks`, which also sizes the startup check) grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`; - a prefix hit at `h` needs the drafter's window before `h` cached. None of that is needed for these drafters. Their context KV at a position is a projection of the target's hidden state at that position, and draft attention only runs past the last target token. So: - an allocation whose target tokens end at `T` only needs drafter blocks from `T - tail_tokens` on. `T` counts drafts still in flight, which is what the margin over the window is for; - once nothing is in flight (processed tokens, a prefix hit), the window is enough, as for plain sliding window; - a hit at `h` for a request of `L` tokens only needs cached drafter blocks in `[L - sliding_window + 1, h)`. Lower blocks are never read, and the target prefill from `h` rewrites the drafter context KV for the rest. Related: RFC #59117 reports the pool collapse a DFlash drafter causes on hybrid models. This PR addresses one of the effects it measures, the per-request drafter block demand. It does not change grouping or page padding, and needs no separate pool. ## Changes Since #61452, allocation policy lives on the KV cache manager as a frozen `Params` dataclass, and a layer returns `Manager.layer_config(spec, **params)`. This PR follows that design. - **`DFlashSlidingWindowManager(SlidingWindo

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't let later image requests overtake a request deferred for encoder limits
summary: ## Overview Fixes #67292. With chunked prefill off and async scheduling, a multimodal request that the scheduler defers whole for encoder cache or budget limits (#65399) can be skipped indefinitely, while later requests with fewer images take the encoder cache space it needs. With this PR, once the scheduler defers a request this way, it admits no later request that needs encoder output in that step, as long as the deferred request's images fit the configured encoder cache at once. In the issue's repro, the 4-image request is then scheduled whole at step 2, where before it was not scheduled in 50 steps. ## Claims - Under FCFS, with chunked prefill off and async scheduling or pipeline parallelism, a request deferred for encoder limits is no longer overtaken by later requests that need encoder output, provided the embeddings of all its images add up to no more than the configured encoder cache size. It is scheduled whole once the steps in flight at the deferral have been processed, with one exception described in Details. - In the scheduler-only repro from #67292, with `AsyncScheduler` and chunked prefill off, the 4-image request is scheduled whole at step 2. Before this change it was not scheduled in 50 steps. - On `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` served with chunked prefill off and async scheduling under a sustained one-image load, base completed none of the 4-image requests within 30 s in any of its saturated runs, and the first version of this change completed all of them, with a median time to first token of 0.45 to 1.36 s. title: [watermarking] Support block verification with dual_key_gumbel watermarking
summary: ## Purpose This PR allows `rejection_sample_method="block"` together with `dual_key_gumbel` watermarking, and keeps block verification unbiased under watermark context deduplication. Enablement: block verification already draws its accept/reject uniforms from the request seed, and it resamples the block residual through the same key-B Philox draw as standard verification. The config check now accepts `"block"` next to `"standard"`, and still rejects `"synthetic"` and `"fly"`. A new chi-square test checks the joint law of the full block against a product target, with a residual-skipping negative control. The existing distribution test only checked the first token of each block. Context deduplication needs one more change. With block verification, the number of accepted drafts τ depends on all K drafts, including drafts τ+2..K. The draft key (key A) noise used to sample those later drafts is observed by the verifier but never committed. If the same context shows up again, the drafter reuses the same key A noise. The proposal then depends on a draw that block verification already looked at, and the output distribution is no longer the target distribution. The fix has three parts: - Each request slot keeps a ring of the contexts that block verification observed but did not commit. The contexts of drafts τ+2..K of each block are recorded. The context of draft τ+1 is committed with the recovered token, so the existing history dedup already covers it. - The drafter samples with stock noise at a recorded context, in the same way it already does at a committed context. title: [Hybrid] Decoupling block_size from allocation block size
summary: ## Purpose **Note: This is a draft PR and needs testing & verification.** Hybrid models often comprise attention layers with relatively small KVcache states and other layer types (e.g. Mamba, GDN) with relatively large cache states. Current vLLM implementation sets the `block_size` in a way to keep the KVcache allocation unit of block the same for both attention and hybrid cache. This typically involves considerably increasing the `block_size` of attention, resulting in lower cache hit chances. This PR separates the `block_size` setting from the size of hybrid cache entries by allowing different sizes of block allocations for attention and SSM layers. summary: ## Purpose `--ignore-eos-mode mask` cuts the [AA-AgentPerf-Local](https://github.com/ArtificialAnalysis/aa-agentperf-local) replay of Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + DFlash2 on one DGX Spark from 15.48 to 12.59 min (-18.7%), with the same output token count. A request with `ignore_eos` samples the EOS token and keeps generating past it. [AA-AgentPerf-Local](https://github.com/ArtificialAnalysis/aa-agentperf-local) ([launch article](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/aa-agentperf-local)) replays 168 recorded agent turns. Its default `exact` output policy sends `ignore_eos` with `max_tokens` = the recorded length, and fails any turn that does not end with `length`. When the model's answer ends early, vLLM then measures the model free-running after its answer has ended (`<|im_start|>user ...` loops). That text is not what a user would get, and speculative decoding accepts far fewer of its tokens. llama.cpp and TensorRT Edge-LLM instead forbid EOS for these requests. This adds `--ignore-eos-mode {continue,mask}`: - `continue` (default) keeps the current behavior. - `mask` gives an `ignore_eos` request a `-inf` logit bias on the model's EOS ids (tokenizer EOS plus generation config `eos_token_id`), through the existing per-request `logit_bias` path. The model keeps writing its answer until `max_tokens`. `stop`, `stop_token_ids` and requests without `ignore_eos` are unchanged. Clients can already get this per request with `min_tokens` = `max_tokens`. The flag is for clients that only send `ignore_eos`: AgentPerf's `exact` policy has no option to send `min_tokens`. title: [Model][ROCm][Inkling]: Add support for Lamport P2P(hip kernels) collective on ROCm/AMD
summary: ## Overview Add Lamport P2P Collective support back on ROCm with hip kernels and ipc buffers. ## Claims Previous Lamport P2P code used triton kernels and pytorch symmetric memory. However, that stack didn't have proper support for memory semantics required by Lamport P2P and caused deadlocks. The PR adds support back using hip kernels and ipc buffers without any deadlocks while preserving the accuracy. ## Details Enabling lamport P2P is a critical optimization for Inkling model. It reduces decode time. Note: this is already enabled by default on Nvidia side, but the original implementation didn't work on AMD/RoCm If Lamport P2P collective isn't used, then RCCL library kernels are used. Inkling model involves collective communication post attention and moe op. The pipeline is this ReduceScatter -> sconv(short convolution) on shards -> AllGather -> fused add(+rmsnorm). With RCCL calls, this results in two collective ops Reduce Scatter and AllGather. By using Lamport P2P collective mechanism the overall time of this pipeline is reduced. It still involves 4 kernels, but relies on spin-wait mechanism between GPU peers and uses a sentinel value as part of data payload for synchronization. The following traces from a decode step show the perf. improvement. **Lamport-OFF** **Lamport-ON**

title: [Feature][Kernel] Triton autotune block fp8
summary: ## Purpose Depends on #59492. Builds on the generic Triton autotune warmup (`--kernel-config.enable_triton_autotune`) and its block-FP8 table. The earlier version swept the full ~1,280-config grid per M bucket, which was too slow to use at startup. Its search space also copied the grid that produced the bundled tables. This PR replaces the sweep with a bounded search that does not read any bundled or user tables. It stays useful on new GPUs and models that have no shipped configs. cc @vanshbhatia-amd Changes: - **Bounded search.** At most 48 configs are timed per M bucket. The search starts from the default config, 8 random configs and up to 2 nearby-M winners, then expands neighbors of the fastest config that hasn't been expanded yet. - **Backend-derived search space.** Launch options (`waves_per_eu`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, `kpack`) and the shared-memory limit come from the installed Triton backend. Nothing is keyed on GPU name. Configs that spill across a quant block are rejected, and `GROUP_SIZE_M` is collapsed when M fits one tile. - **Correctness and noise guard.** A winner must match the default config's output. It must also beat the default by at least 2% in a side-by-side re-timing, otherwise the default is kept. - **Nearby-bucket seeding.** Winners tuned on the same rank seed later buckets. This matters under TP, where ranks split the work and the neighboring bucket is often tuned elsewhere. - **Partial-cache resume.** Only missing M buckets are tuned. Shapes with a user or bundled table are skipped unless `VLLM_TRITON_AUTOTUNE_FORCE=1`. - **Config lookup cleanup

title: [Bugfix][Core] Deliver abort outputs of a pause to an in-process caller, and finish pooling requests ended without a pooler output
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Requests aborted by a sleep or pause were not finished correctly in two cases: - In process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), their final outputs never came back, so `LLMEngine.has_unfinished_requests()` stayed `True` and a loop stepping until it is false never ended. - For pooling requests (e.g. embedding), the engine's abort output carries no pooler output and tripped `assert req_state.detokenizer is not None` in `OutputProcessor`. Fixes #66700. ## Claims - In process, requests aborted by `sleep()` or a pause in `abort` mode finish with `finish_reason="abort"` on the next `step()`, as in multiprocess mode. - A pooling request the engine ends without a pooler output (aborted, or failed before it ran) finishes as a `PoolingRequestOutput` with an empty tensor, as frontend aborts already do.
