title: [Spec Decode] Exclude invalid draft logits from the acceptance estimator
summary: ## Overview The online acceptance estimator behind adaptive verification now flags draft rows whose distribution is undefined (a NaN or +inf logit, or every logit -inf), hardening the training logic. These rows get zero confidence, so adaptive verification trims them, and they stay out of the estimator's IRLS calibration. Related: #68164, #66673, #57533 (see Details). ## Claims - A draft row with a NaN logit, a +inf logit after temperature scaling, or all logits -inf gets confidence 0 and adds nothing to the IRLS statistics (`info`, `grad`, `counts`). The slot's next valid draft trains as usual. - Valid rows are scored as before, including one-hot rows that saturate at `+MAX_LOG_ODDS`. - No host syncs. The cost is one `[max_num_reqs, num_speculative_steps]` bool buffer and +32 lines in `acceptance_estimator.py`. ## Validation New tests: - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_invalid_logits_use_fallback_and_do_not_train` covers all-masked, NaN, +inf and temperature-overflow rows, with single-block and multi-block vocabularies. An invalid row replaces the slot's earlier prediction with confidence 0 and is flagged invalid. Its round leaves `info`, `grad` and `counts` bit-identical to an estimator that never saw the row, and the slot trains again once its logits are valid. In the multi-block NaN case, the NaN shares its vocab block only with -inf, which `tl.max` would silently drop. - `test_one_hot_logits_remain_valid_across_empty_blocks`: a one-hot row beside empty or partial vocab blocks stays valid, saturates at `+MAX_LOG_ODDS`, and is counted in the fit.

title: [Bugfix][FA4] Warm the SplitKV combine kernel for the layer's query heads
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview vLLM's dense JIT warmup for FlashAttention 4 (FA4), registered for Gemma 4 checkpoints, compiles the SplitKV combine kernel of the SM90 head-size-512 forward for one query head. This PR adds the layer's query heads to the warmup's compile key and compiles the combine for them. title: [CPU] Count reclaimable page cache as available under a cgroup limit
summary: ## Overview Inside a memory-limited container, the CPU worker counts page cache as used memory, so right after loading a large model it can reject a KV cache that fits. This PR counts the cgroup's reclaimable page cache and slab as available in `get_memory_node_info()` and `get_available_memory()`, the same way the NUMA meminfo path already does. Related open PRs: #60520 edits the neighbouring `if` in `get_memory_node_info` (always clamp the total to the cgroup limit). It's compatible with this change, but whichever lands second needs a small rebase. #64104 adds an opt-in way to read limits from the process's own cgroup path. If it lands, `memory.stat` should be read from that same path. ## Claims - Under `docker run --memory 24g`, Qwen2.5-7B with `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4` now starts and serves, where before it stopped with "Available memory on node 0 (0.56/24.0 GiB) ... less than requested memory for kv (4.0 GiB)". - Available memory under a cgroup limit is `limit - usage + reclaimable`, where reclaimable is `active_file + inactive_file + slab_reclaimable` (cgroup v2) or `total_active_file + total_inactive_file` (cgroup v1). If `memory.stat` can't be read, the result is the same as before. - Nothing changes without a cgroup memory limit. ## Validation **End to end** on AWS c7i.4xlarge (Xeon, 16 vCPU, 30 GiB), image `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.33.0-x86_64`. `get_memory_node_info()` is identical on v0.33.0 and `main` (27a441ca4). title: [CPU] Size CPU worker memory per worker under a shared cgroup limit
summary: ## Overview Two fixes to how `CPUWorker` sizes its memory when there is more than one worker or the CPU's NUMA id isn't a memory node: 1. Inside a memory-limited container, each local worker reserves `gpu_memory_utilization` × the whole cgroup limit, so N workers together reserve N times that fraction of the limit. This PR gives each local worker an equal share of the limit. 2. `__init__` falls back to a valid memory node when the CPU's group id isn't one (s390x book ids), but `determine_available_memory()` read the original id again. This PR keeps the node chosen in `__init__` and uses it in both places. ## Claims - With a cgroup memory limit and `local_world_size > 1`, each worker's reservation is `gpu_memory_utilization × min(node total, limit // local_world_size)`. Example: TP=2 on two 96 GiB NUMA nodes in a 64 GiB container reserves 2 × 28.8 GiB = 57.6 GiB instead of 2 × 57.6 GiB = 115.2 GiB. - With one local worker, or no cgroup limit, the reservation is unchanged. - The KV budget check and its log and error messages use the same memory node as the reservation. ## Validation **Unit tests only.** I don't have a multi-socket machine, so there is no end-to-end run. summary: ## Summary - fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44575 The SWA/chunked-attention KV-tile loop floor-rounds its start to a tile boundary, so a misaligned window can span one extra `TILE_SIZE` tile. Adds an opt-in `SHIFT_TILE_BASE` that starts the loop exactly at the window's first allowed key instead — 2D decode/prefill only; `USE_TD` and 3D decode keep the old bounds, and the two other callers of `compute_tile_loop_bounds` are unaffected by default. This idea was initially proposed by #44584 (@almogtavor), but it was closed — because H100 numbers were near the noise floor for realistic windows. This PR carries the fix forward (adapted for `USE_TD`/Gemma4 additions since) with new B200 evidence below. ## Test Plan ### A. summary: ## Overview Follow-up to #60418. Three decode changes in `triton_unified_attention.py`; other arches are unaffected and segment counts don't change anywhere. 1. **gfx1201: drop the halved decode threshold.** The launcher halved the 2D/3D threshold for 16-bit pure decode on gfx1201 (64 programs instead of vLLM's 128). gfx1201 now uses vLLM's default, which the metadata builder already snaps to a CUDA graph capture size, so every batch takes the same kernel as its CUDA graph. Re-tuning with mixed context lengths showed the halving doesn't pay off: split-KV keeps the GPU busy when a few long requests would otherwise leave most of it idle in the 2D kernel. 2. **gfx1201 head size 512: tuned split-KV launch.** Head 512 keeps vLLM's 16 segments and gets the (16, 4, 1) launch instead of the default one. 3. **gfx1100: tuned split-KV launch at the default segment count.** Full-attention layers use the tuned `_GFX1100_3D_CONFIGS` launch also when the segment rule keeps 16 segments (before: only when it raised the count). Sliding-window layers are unchanged. ## Performance Kernel sweep on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), 16-bit decode, heads 64–512, GQA 4–16, KV heads 1–8, 1–512 requests, uniform and mixed context lengths, every output checked against an fp32 reference: - **Threshold, heads 64 / 128 / 256:** mixed context lengths +8–11%, uniform lengths within 1% (−0.5 to −0.8%). - **Head 512 launch:** ~10% faster split-KV decode (0.90–1.84× per batch).

title: [Perf][Attention] Split only the sliding window into Triton split-K decode segments
summary: ## Overview In the Triton split-K (3D) decode path of `kernel_unified_attention`, the segments split the whole sequence, so with a sliding window only 1-2 segments overlap the window once `seq_len >> window`, and they walk it serially. This PR splits only the window's tiles into the segments. Sliding-window decode then costs the same at any context length instead of growing linearly. Complementary to #60418 (now merged), which made TRITON_ATTN the default on RDNA and raised the gfx1201 split-K segment count; interacts with #56148 (multi-query split-K), see Details. ## Claims - **Per sliding-window layer, decode on TRITON_ATTN:** the cost no longer grows with context. title: [ROCm][RDNA][Perf] W4A16: fused scale/zero-point carrier for Triton prefill
summary: ## Overview For asymmetric fp16 W4A16 layers on gfx1151 (Strix Halo), `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` now trades a little weight memory for faster prefill. At load time, each per-group scale and zero-point is packed into one int32 "carrier". The packed fp16 Triton prefill dequant (#60644) then does one load per (n, group) and a single `v_pk_fma_f16` per pair. Before, it did a scale load, a packed zero-point gather, and a subtract-then-multiply. With the cheaper dequant, asymmetric layers take the packed path from M > 192 (M > 128 when N ≥ 4K) instead of M > 256. Builds on #60644. Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a scale/zero-point carrier or changes the asymmetric prefill cutoff. #61193 also speeds up gfx1151 prefill, but at M ≥ 4096 by dequantizing to a dense matmul; the two are complementary but touch the same file. ## Claims - **Batch-1 prefill up to 18% faster end to end.** Qwen3-8B (asymmetric g128): −18.4% at 224 prompt tokens, −17.3% at 256. Qwen3-1.7B (asymmetric g64): −12.1% at 224, −12.4% at 256. No change at 128 tokens, and within ±1.8% from 320 tokens up. - **No regression at batch 128 and 256** (outputs 1 and 128): Qwen3-8B is 3–11% faster, Qwen3-1.7B 1–5%. - **Kernel** (geomean over 12 Qwen3 shapes, g128 and g64): 15–18% faster at M 193–256, 4–5% at M 129–192, 1–3% at M 257–4096. At M = 8192, summed over each model's four layers: 12% faster on Qwen3-8B, 5% on Qwen3-1.7B. - **Memory cost:** 8/G of the int4 weight bytes (6.25% at g128, 12.5% at g64). summary: ## Purpose `save_sharded_state` serializes each worker's in-memory `state_dict()`, i.e. the weights *after* `process_weights_after_loading`. title: [Doc] Sleep mode: free a KV connector's host memory with Mooncake standalone-store
summary: ## Purpose Document how to free a KV connector's host memory while a colocated engine sleeps. Resetting the connector's cache does not return its host memory: `MooncakeStoreConnector` in its default `embedded` mode keeps its pool share inside each rank for the engine's lifetime. With `standalone-store`, the pool lives in the external `mooncake_client`, which can be stopped while vLLM sleeps and started again before serving resumes. The section sits in the sleep mode docs next to "Keep the KV connector cache" and notes that the pool's KV cache is lost, so later lookups miss and recompute. The Mooncake store docs link to it. ## Test Plan Docs only. Checked the documented steps on one GB300 GPU (vLLM nightly 153dc0464, Mooncake 0.3.14, RDMA, Qwen3-0.6B, `standalone-store`, default connector options): 1. Sleep (level 1), stop `mooncake_client`: vLLM stays up, `/health` 200. 2. Start `mooncake_client` at the same address, wake, send a prompt that hit the store before: HTTP 200, `external_prefix_cache_hits` unchanged (miss, recomputed), no errors. 3. Requests while `mooncake_client` is down: HTTP 200 as misses; store puts only log warnings. 4. summary: Stacked on #66369 and #66371; review only the last commit. ## Overview Follow-up to #66369 and #66371, stacked on them. A hot set fixed at boot goes stale when the traffic changes: after a switch from prose to code, the step reads the experts code routes to over PCIe. This adds `--cpu-offload-expert-swap`: the route counters of #66371 also drive an asynchronous exchange of hot and cold experts while serving. The copies run on a side stream through spare cold rows, and the expert maps are rewritten in place between steps, so captured graphs are kept and no step waits on a copy. ## Claims - Every expert stays routable with complete bytes at every step; no host synchronization on the forward path; each copy phase moves at most 256 MiB per runner step. - Off by default; without the option nothing changes. ## Validation | Check | Result | |---|---| | `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_xpu_expert_swap.py`, CPU, with a simulated side stream whose copies poison their destination and land only when the test lets them: every expert routable and read from complete bytes at every step while copies land at random, with each cold block staged first as `--cpu-offload-stage-min-tokens` does; the hot set following a shift in traffic; host mirrors, owners and device maps agreeing; maps rewritten in place (same pointers); bytes per step within the budget; no swap while capturing; a staged copy taken while a spare row is in flight never read through a map (and the check catching it when a map is pointed there early); swap off on a hot/cold layout mismatch; spare rows zeroed and counted by the cold

title: [XPU][Offload] Learn the expert rankings while serving
summary: Stacked on #66369; review only the last commit. ## Overview Follow-up to #66369, stacked on it. Per-expert placement needs a rankings file, recorded per checkpoint before the first boot. This adds `--cpu-offload-expert-state <file>`: the server counts its own routes per expert and keeps the order in that file, in the rankings format, so the next boot places by this host's traffic. title: [Kernel][Triton] Allow an fp8_e5m2 KV cache on SM80-SM88
summary: ## Overview Allow `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` with `TRITON_ATTN` on SM80–SM88 (Ampere) by storing it as e5m2. Today every FP8 cache dtype is refused below SM89, and the writer stores e4m3 even when e5m2 is requested. The change also clamps the KV tile for FP8 caches with head size > 256 on SM8x, where a 32-wide tile exceeds shared memory. Related open work, and how this differs: - **#50882** (draft, last updated 2026-08-28): relaxes the same `triton_attn.py` guard for MiniMax-M3, and plans to route writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash`. This PR keeps the Triton writer and makes it store e5m2. - **#54341**: observes that the Triton writer stores e4m3 for `fp8_e5m2`, and stops advertising `fp8_e5m2`. This PR fixes the writer on CUDA instead. ROCm and XPU, which #54341 also covers, are left unchanged here. - **#49077** (draft): e4m3 on SM75–SM88 through software conversion in CUDA bitcode. That is complementary: this PR only enables the format Triton already converts. - **#60317**: tunes head_dim 512 for 16-bit KV. The tile clamp here only applies to 1-byte KV on SM8x. ## Claims - **New on SM80–SM88:** `fp8_e5m2` KV cache on `TRITON_ATTN`. title: [Bugfix] Package the SM90 DeepGEMM mHC register lifetime fix
summary: ## Purpose Package the SM90 mHC prenorm GEMM register-lifetime fix from [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/448), authored by jason (leevan). In a multi-stage K loop, the next iteration can overwrite register A operands before the previous asynchronous WGMMA has finished. Repeated calls with identical inputs can therefore produce different outputs. The upstream fix waits immediately after committing the WGMMA batch. This integrates that existing fix into vLLM's packaged JIT header until the pinned DeepGEMM dependency contains it; it is not a new kernel implementation. DeepGEMM #448 is currently open. There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair. ## Changes - Generate a patched header during CMake configuration and install it without modifying a supplied `DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR`. title: [RFC]: Native Text Watermarking Support
summary: # Motivation Text watermarking for LLMs is a process by which we perturb the output of a model in such a way that is detectable after generation. This process allows us to test whether a sequence of text is consistent with a watermarked generation process after the fact. Watermarking is a necessary functionality in vLLM, because: - It has become an important part of responsible LLM deployment - It has become required by regulation by certain entities, to support provenance and transparency requirements (see [EU AI Act, Article 50(2)](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/50/) and [California SB 942](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB942)) - It is a modification of the sampling process, which cannot be modified by downstream consumers Watermarking cannot be left as an out-of-tree functionality (such as `CustomLogitsProcessor`) because: - Not all watermarking schemes are simple "logit biasers": some (such as gumbel-max) require adjust the sampling process itself - Some schemes require access to the final output distribution of the model (after top-p, temperature...) and this is not currently possible with a `CustomLogitsProcessor` - Production-ready implementations of watermarking will require support for speculative-decoding, which will potentially require adjustments to rejection sampling and other core behaviours of vLLM - Watermarking will only become more ingrained with the generation process as techniques evolve and complexify # Proposed Change We propose the implementation of native vLLM watermarking during sampling,

summary: ## Overview Enable vLLM's existing custom all-reduce on AMD RDNA4 (gfx1200/gfx1201) GPUs connected by PCIe peer-to-peer, such as Radeon AI PRO R9700 workstations. title: [Doc] Routed experts: row storage, replica affinity, sizing and cache resets
summary: ## Purpose Bring `docs/training/routed_experts.md` in line with what `main` does today, for RL users running routed experts return without the session object store: - **Row storage**: rows live in the host memory of each engine's first TP worker, keyed by KV block hash, and last as long as their KV. - **Replica affinity**: later turns hit only on the engine holding the prefix; route sessions with consistent hashing and use `routed_experts_prompt_start`. - **Sizing `max_bytes`**: a smaller value does not save memory; size the KV cache for the sessions instead. - **Requirements**: drop the KV connector rejection list, which `main` does not enforce; explain what a prefill/decode deployment actually does. - **Weight updates and cache resets**: any prefix-cache reset drops all rows; `reset_connector` decides whether the KV connector tier survives, and how to keep reusing it via `routed_experts_prompt_start`. ## Test Plan Docs only. title: [Frontend] Add generative box answers for multimodal models on /v1/systemone
summary: ## Overview Add generated bounding-box answers to `/v1/systemone` for text-described targets in images. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Avoid Humming's fused-E8M0 path for MXFP4 layers it would round
summary: ## Overview Fixes #66074. With FP8 activations (the default for compressed-tensors MXFP4 checkpoints on Hopper), Humming runs MXFP4 linear layers on its fused-E8M0 path. That path keeps only 11 binades of E8M0 scales below the largest scale of the layer's fused weight tensor and silently rounds or zeroes the weights of blocks further down. This PR checks each Humming MXFP4 linear layer once at load time. A layer that would lose weights runs with 16-bit activations instead, which decode the checkpoint exactly, and vLLM logs one warning naming it. Every other layer is unchanged. ## Claims - Humming MXFP4 linear layers now use exactly the checkpoint's weights. On `ibm-granite/granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4`, main decodes 28,000,270 weights wrongly (14,154,257 of them as 0); with this PR, 0. The issue's reproducer goes from 69 wrong weights to 0, and its N-padded case from 524,288 of 524,288 (all 0) to 0. - Layers whose scales fit the range keep FP8 activations and the same kernel configuration as on main: 253 of the 256 MXFP4 layers of Granite-4.2-30B, and every layer of Granite-4.2-8B and 3B. On 8B and 3B, the prompt log-probs are bit-identical to main. - Cost: only the layers that switch get slower. Per GEMM, 16-bit activations take 1.0 to 1.2x the FP8 time at M ≤ 16 and 1.8 to 1.9x at M ≥ 256 (still faster than Marlin). On Granite-4.2-30B, where 3 of 256 layers switch, end-to-end throughput is unchanged within run-to-run noise (3,852 vs 3,863 tokens/s, 2 runs each). The load-time check adds 0.2 to 0.4 ms per MXFP4 layer. ## Validation Setup: one NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), TP 1, torch 2.1

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Size FlexAttention request buffers for local-attention virtual batches
summary: ## Overview With `attention_config={"backend": "FLEX_ATTENTION"}`, models that use chunked local attention (Llama 4) crash at engine startup or during prefill when a step's local-attention split produces more virtual requests than `max_num_seqs`. `make_local_attention_virtual_batches` splits each request at window boundaries, but `FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder` sizes its per-request persistent buffers (offsets, `query_start_loc`, `seq_lens`, and the lazily created physical-to-logical block table) with `max_num_seqs`. No kernel or scheduler change. ## Validation DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), `main` at 29c6cfc457 (both touched files are unchanged on current `main`), torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0. title: [ROCm][Spec Decode][Muse Spark] Fuse the DSpark Markov sampling steps
summary: ## Purpose Draft PR on top of #66051; it stays a draft until #66051 merges, then is rebased onto main (this commit applies as is). `DSparkSpeculator._sample_markov_chain` runs about 16 small kernels per draft step besides the Markov bias GEMM: bias add, output transform, cache cast and copy, Gumbel kernel, block argmax, gathers and copies. Each is a 4-6 µs launch on a few MB. On ROCm gfx950, without `--monokernel` or batch-sharded sampling, the Muse Spark DSpark draft now installs a `sample_sequential` hook that runs each step as the model's own `markov_bias` GEMM plus one Triton launch over (row, 1024-token block). The reduction keeps the first of equal maxima, as the loop does, and the token stays in the vocabulary. Scratch buffers are sized for `max_num_reqs`, so the launches are CUDA-graph safe at any row count. In rows without NaN, each token is sampled from exactly the value written to the draft-logits cache, so verification sees the draft's distribution. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose With an FP8 KV cache, `ROCM_AITER_FA` computes extend attention (chunked prefill over a cached prefix) by gathering and dequantizing the prefix to BF16 in chunks, running CK per chunk and merging by LSE. title: [Feature]: Add a synchronization hook for indexer cache loading before sparse top-k execution
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Motivation We encountered accuracy degradation on long-context evaluation datasets when serving **GLM-5.2 with vLLM 0.27.1 on two H100 nodes**, using UCM layerwise external KV cache loading. Our investigation indicated that the indexer could consume its cache before loading had completed. Moving cache loading and completion waits one layer earlier in the connector restored accuracy on the affected workload. This motivates a supported synchronization point before indexer cache consumption, allowing connectors to wait when the data is actually needed. ### Current limitation The KV connector API exposes `wait_for_layer_load(layer_name)`, which is invoked from attention-layer execution through `maybe_transfer_kv_layer`. In the sparse-attention path we investigated, indexer computation and top-k selection occur **before the corresponding attention-layer wait hook**. Waiting at that hook therefore does not protect earlier indexer cache reads. The execution order can be: ```text Submit the cache load for layer L ↓ Layer L's indexer reads its cache and computes top-k ↓ Attention hook calls wait_for_layer_load(L) ↓ Attention executes ``` If loading has not completed when the indexer reads its cache, the attention-layer wait is too late. Registering an indexer cache as an `AttentionLayerBase` does not itself provide a runtime wait point. title: [Frontend] Add low-overhead /ready GPU health check
summary: ## Purpose Fix #36960 Add a `/ready` readiness endpoint that checks whether the engine can serve requests. The existing `/health` endpoint stays as the cheap liveness check. `/ready` calls `EngineClient.check_health_gpu()`. In `AsyncLLM` it does three things: 1. Runs the existing `check_health()` liveness check. A dead engine returns 503. 2. Sends one EngineCore utility call, `check_ready()`, which runs on the engine-core thread between steps: - If the engine is sleeping or paused (`EngineCore.is_sleeping()`), it returns not ready and runs nothing. - If no request from any API server is in flight (`scheduler.has_requests()` is false and `batch_queue` is empty), it runs `execute_dummy_batch()` to confirm a forward pass still works. - Otherwise it returns ready without adding GPU work. 3. Waits at most `VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 20). A timeout or an exception returns 503. This borrows the low-overhead idea from SGLang's health generation path. Instead of routing a synthetic request through the scheduler, it uses vLLM's existing utility-call dummy batch. ### Behaviour details - **MoE with DP (`DPEngineCoreProc`)**: `check_ready()` is overridden and never runs the dummy batch. title: [Bugfix] Fit speculative draft pages to TurboQuant targets
summary: ## Summary FP8 draft KV caches can require larger physical pages than an already aligned TurboQuant/Mamba hybrid target cache. title: warn when an FT-adjacent timeout is not shorter than the recovery timeout
summary: ## Overview With `--enable-fault-tolerance`, `engine_recovery_timeout_sec` (120 s by default) bounds how long an engine waits for recovery instructions after a fault. Several timeouts on the fault path default to values at or above that, so a fault surfaced only through one of them is observed after the recovery window has expired. This adds a config-time warning that lists them. No related issue exists. ## Claims - Under FT, vLLM warns when an applicable timeout is at least `engine_recovery_timeout_sec`: - All2all kernel timeout: 130 s for `deepep_low_latency` (DeepEP `NUM_TIMEOUT_CYCLES`, 200e9 cycles), 30 s for `nixl_ep` (NIXL EP `timeout_ms` default) - CPU distributed group timeout (`--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds`, else the gloo default read from `torch.distributed.constants.default_pg_timeout`) - `execute_model` RPC timeout (300 s, `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) - The `execute_model` checks apply whenever the deployment uses the multiprocessing executor, which includes DP > 1 with TP = 1. - vLLM warns when the `execute_model` RPC timeout is not longer than the kernel and CPU group timeouts inside the step, since the RPC then fails before the peer fault is reported. - vLLM warns when EPLB uses an NCCL communicator (`torch_nccl`, `pynccl`); the NCCL watchdog aborts the process on a failed collective, so FT cannot recover the rank. - Warn-only: no exception, no new flag, no change to runtime behavior. Every check reads the resolved config, so the same config gives the same result on any rank. ## Validation - `pytest tests/config/test_fault_tolerance_config.py`

title: [Bugfix] Enable quant_fp8 CUDA op for online fp8_per_block
summary: ## Purpose This is the config-level fix behind #68130. #68130 stays open as the NaN guard for `QuantFP8.forward_native`. `VllmConfig` turns on the `quant_fp8` CUDA op (`+quant_fp8`) only when the quant config reports blocked weights, through `weight_block_size` or `has_blocked_weights()`. Block FP8 checkpoints and ModelOpt already do this. `OnlineQuantizationConfig` reported neither, so online `--quantization fp8_per_block` behaved differently: - `custom_ops` stayed `['none']`, so `QuantFP8` ran `forward_native`. - The DeepGEMM block linear (`DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`) therefore received **fp32** activation scales. Measured on GB200 with an instrumented `fp8_gemm_nt`: - `custom_ops=['+quant_fp8', 'none', '+quant_fp8']`. - `QuantFP8` dispatches to `forward_cuda`. - The activation scales are **int32**, already packed to UE8M0 by `per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm`. DeepGEMM never runs the runtime packing. - 12/12 prompts, 32/32 burst, GSM8K 0.9219. This PR makes `OnlineQuantizationConfig.has_blocked_weights()` return `True` whenever any linear, MoE, or `targets` spec uses 128x128 block FP8. title: [KV Offload] Add an external evictor to bound the FS tier's root_dir ( #64239 )
summary: ## Overview The filesystem (FS) KV offload tier has no size limit: every stored block stays on disk forever, so `root_dir` grows until the disk or shared volume fills up. This PR adds a small standalone evictor that keeps `root_dir` under a byte budget, for a single engine or many engines sharing one directory. Refs RFC #64237, which asks for a cluster-wide quota and coherent eviction for an FS tier shared by many engines. This PR is the smallest useful piece of that: a working size bound with no engine changes. **Not a duplicate:** #52784 (an in-engine capacity bound) was closed unmerged, and no open PR bounds the FS tier. This PR takes a different, out-of-engine approach. ## Claims - `python -m vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.fs.evict <root_dir> --max-bytes 500G` keeps the FS tier's disk usage under the budget, whether one engine or many write to the directory. - Cleans up `.tmp` files left behind by writers that crashed mid-store, which today are never removed. - No changes to the engine, the FS tier, or any config. Users who don't run the evictor see no difference. ## Validation - New test `test_evict_removes_oldest_blocks_and_stale_tmp` checks that the oldest blocks are evicted down to the low watermark, a stale `.tmp` is removed, a live `.tmp` is kept, and a second pass deletes nothing. I confirmed the test fails if the eviction order is reversed. ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py -q # 36 passed, 11 skipped ``` - The engine side of a concurrent delete is already covered by the existing `test_failed_load_missing_file`: a block removed after lookup l

title: [Perf][Core] Add encoder length bucketing for padded audio encoders
summary: ## Overview Padded audio encoders pad every mel either to a fixed window (1000–3000 frames) or to the batch maximum, so a mixed-length batch computes every item at full length. This PR adds an opt-in bucketing layer that regroups a batch by true item length into discrete rungs, so short clips stop paying for the padding of long clips. All bucket-2 (mask-aware) and bucket-3 (mask-less attention) models are adapted — seven in total: Qwen2-Audio, Canary, FireRed-ASR2, Cohere-ASR, FunASR/SenseVoice, GLM-ASR and Granite-Speech — and each is net-positive or parity with the feature enabled at its recommended setting. This **complements, not replaces**, the existing packed-varlen path (`MMEncoderAttention` + `cu_seqlens`): varlen packs items losslessly where the encoder function is unchanged by packing, while bucketing recovers the padding waste where packing does not apply. ## Mechanism 1. **Bucketing** (`additional_config.audio_bucket_seconds`) — a model-agnostic encoder-length bucketing layer (rung grouping + per-batch waste gate + whitelist gate + fixed-window shim registry, driven from `EncoderRunner.execute_mm_encoder` before the CUDA-graph decision) that regroups a padded batch by true item length into fixed-length rungs, so short clips stop computing over the padding of long clips. Each rung is a fixed-shape sub-batch, keeping the CUDA-graph path intact; the waste gate guarantees a batch never computes more than the untouched forward. 2. **Compute-budget merging** (`additional_config.audio_bucket_budget`, off by default) — keeps each encoder call's compute (items × padded f

title: [MoE] Support llm-compressor MoNE checkpoints with compact expert execution
summary: ## Overview Add support for llm-compressor MoNE checkpoints, which replace selected MoE experts with learned constant vectors called novices. Routing still considers all logical experts, while vLLM stores and executes only the retained expert MLPs. This continues #62978 with the original author's agreement to hand over the work. The original commits and authorship are preserved. Duplicate-work checks found the predecessor and related #61460; this is the agreed continuation of #62978, while #61460 primarily adds REAP (`method: "prune"`) and legacy MoNE-format support. This PR targets llm-compressor's `method: "novice"` format and compact decomposed/monolithic execution. AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, review, and preparation of this PR. ## Claims - Load llm-compressor MoNE checkpoints with compact retained-expert weights and separate novice vectors, including supported compressed-tensors quantization formats. - Preserve novices' routing weights, normalization, and scaling. This intentionally replaces the existing MoNE checkpoint format. title: [Bugfix][Parser] Add flint parser
summary: ## Overview and claims Flint assistant turns may not generate `<think></think>` blocks at all, particularly on swe trajectories. This breaks existing parsers. The current recipe's glm47 parser (#62938) starts every reply in reasoning, so a reply without `<think>` would have its content/tool calls populate the reasoning field. Forcing `<think>` every turn would probably be ok, but the model was not trained this way. We implement a fix by subclassing the glm47 parser, rather than a minimal patch that adds flags to make the think block optional in glm47. Only flint would use those flags, which is a waste of API space. This PR used AI, and the remainder of this PR description is AI-generated. ## Validation **Real Flint output** (one B200, `vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint` with the recipe's flags). The table shows an answer after a tool result where Flint skipped `<think>`: | raw output | `glm47` | `flint` | |---|---|---| | `The current weather in Paris is 18°C with clear skies. It's a pleasant day!` | `reasoning=<whole answer>`, `content=''` | `content=<whole answer>` | **The new tests fail with today's recipe parsers.** With `glm47` in place of `flint` in `test_flint.py`'s `_parser`: ``` $ sed -i 's/_parser_name="flint"/_parser_name="glm47"/' tests/parser/engine/test_flint.py $ pytest tests/parser/engine/test_flint.py E AssertionError: assert ('391', None) == (None, '391') # [no-think]: the answer is returned as reasoning E AssertionError: assert (None, 'Easy.391') == ('Easy.', '391') # [think-enable_thinking_false] E AssertionError: assert ('Checking.', '') == ('', 'Checking.')

title: [ROCm] RDNA4: enable SiLU-and-mul + block FP8 quant fusion and fix the fused kernel's gfx12 slow paths
summary: ## Overview `SiluMulBlockQuantPattern` is registered only on CUDA. #39387 added that guard because `per_token_group_fp8_quant` was not built for ROCm at the time (#39377). The op is now built for ROCm, so the guard is stale. With the default compilation config, block-FP8 models on RDNA4 still run SiLU-and-mul and the group quant as two kernels. This PR does two things: 1. It registers the pattern on RDNA4 (`on_rdna4()`: gfx1200/gfx1201). 2. It fixes two gfx12-specific slow paths in `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant`. Without these fixes the fused kernel was slower than the unfused pair at some batch sizes on gfx1201. ## Claims - With the default compilation config, block-FP8 models on RDNA4 now use `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant`. - Measured on R9700 (gfx1201): - Kernel: the fused kernel is at least 1.68x faster than the unfused pair at all 44 measured shapes (intermediate 3072 and 12288, M = 1..8192). - Qwen3-8B-FP8: TTFT is 1.3-2.4 % lower and TPOT is 0.5-3.8 % lower. - gsm8k: the difference from main is within about one stderr. - Other targets are unaffected: - The pattern registration is limited to RDNA4. - The kernel changes are under `__gfx1200__`/`__gfx1201__` guards, and the host-side arch check is `constexpr false` on CUDA. - The compiled ISA for gfx1100 and gfx942 is identical to main. - CUDA was not built or run. ## Validation AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 7.14, PyTorch 2.11, main 48e1b8830. - Tests: `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py` and `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_fusion.py` give 443 passed and 16 failed. - The 16 failure

summary:
### What does this PR do? cc: @hmellor → **This PR makes the Transformers modeling backend serve Omni models, with audio, image, and video supported in a single request.** I've tried to scope the work as much as I could, but there are a lot of edge cases, such as which audio a fused `use_audio_in_video` span should pair with, bidirectional encoders sitting inside multimodal configs, and one quantity carrying three different names across the Qwen family, that we need to handle to fully cover these models. title: [RFC]: Holemiss: Selective Recovery of Partially Lost LLM Cache State
summary: > **Implementation status (November 2026)** > > A working v1 prototype is available for architectural review. It implements the scheduler recovery lifecycle and worker-side selective replay, with model-scale validation on Qwen3-32B (TP=2, Ascend 910C). > > The implementation is provided as a reference, not as a merge-ready proposal. We would particularly appreciate feedback on report transport, executor placement, recovery admission, and capability discovery. ## Summary External KV-cache storage makes long-context inference cheaper by reusing previously computed prefixes. But a cached prefix is not always fully retrievable. A rare storage or transfer failure can make one or several blocks unavailable even though the rest of a long prefix is still valid — a damaged SSD object is the canonical case: retrying the read cannot recover bytes that no longer exist. The safe fallback is to fail the request or recompute. Existing vLLM handling rewinds the request to the failed region (or to zero) and recomputes. Holemiss explores an optional, more selective alternative: **locate the missing state, replay only the computation needed to reconstruct it, and preserve independently valid cached state.** It should coexist with — and always be able to fall back to — the conservative policies. What has changed since this RFC was opened: 1. **The lifecycle exists as code.** A Scheduler–Worker contract is implemented on top of vLLM's existing skip-quarantine: structured failure reports from a connector, a scheduler-admitted repair-only step, a worker replay executor with an independent write-a

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Support device adapters and typed TP state views
summary: ## Overview `MooncakeStoreConnector` currently hardcodes `MooncakeStoreWorker`, CUDA save events, and single-allocation packed Mamba views (`(num_blocks, 1, 1, state_bytes)`). Hardware plugins that allocate convolution and recurrent states in separate tensors, or that require backend-specific Store setup, worker-thread device binding, and fail-safe close handling, would otherwise have to duplicate connector and worker orchestration downstream. This PR adds narrow lifecycle hooks on `MooncakeStoreConnector` and `MooncakeStoreWorker` (4 production files, +151/-29 lines) along with `MambaStoreLayout.register_state_views`, enabling device plugins such as [vllm-project/vllm-ascend#20755](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20755) to reuse upstream Store lookup, queues, key rotation, capacity handling, and block lifetimes directly. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Core["vLLM Core (#64096 + #66294)"] Coord["Store Scheduler & Coordinator (lookup, lookahead, block refs)"] Conn["MooncakeStoreConnector (_create_worker)"] Wkr["MooncakeStoreWorker (queues, key rotation, capacity)"] Layout["MambaStoreLayout (register_kv_caches / register_state_views)"] end subgraph Plugin["Device Plugin (e.g. vllm-ascend #20755)"] SubW["Plugin Worker Subclass (_setup_store, _record_save_event, _close_store)"] Views["Separate or Padded Allocations (conv + recurrent, K/V planes)"] end Coord --> Conn --> Wkr Conn -. title: fix(rocm): drain GPU during MLA fp8 BMM load warmup
summary: Sync and periodically empty the caching allocator while pre-compiling fp8 BMM batch sizes 1..1024. ## Overview Fixes ROCm model **load** failures when Aiter Triton fp8 BMM warmup is enabled (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1`). MLA layers pre-compile batch sizes 1..1024 in `process_weights_after_loading`; without draining the caching allocator after async Triton launches, memory use can peak to OOM on MLA-heavy models before load finishes. Forward/inference behavior is unchanged. **Scope:** `is_aiter_triton_fp8_bmm_enabled` only (ROCm + Aiter fp8 BMM). Default upstream env keeps fp8 BMM off; this path is used by ROCm recipes and deployments that enable it. ## Claims - **Bug fix:** Reduces load-time GPU OOM (`HIPCachingAllocator` / `free: 0`, worker init failure) during `[Aiter Triton] Pre-compiling fp8 BMM kernel`. - **No forward change:** Same 1..1024 precompile coverage; kernels and MLA math unchanged. - **Minimal diff:** Only the existing fp8 BMM warmup loop in `mla_attention.py`; uses `torch.accelerator.*` (not `torch.cuda.*`). - **Tunable drain cadence:** `_FP8_BMM_WARMUP_CACHE_DRAIN_INTERVAL = 32` for periodic `empty_cache` (batch-size loop cadence, not kernel tile size). ## Validation **Reproduce (ROCm, fp8 BMM on)** 1. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=1`. 2. title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Prefer Transformers' class over custom code, as the registry does
summary: ## Overview With `--trust-remote-code`, the Transformers modeling backend built a checkpoint's custom `AutoModel` code instead of Transformers' implementation of its architecture. Since #66821 serves Qwen2 with the backend, this breaks `Alibaba-NLP/gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct`: its `modeling_qwen.py` can't take vLLM's attention and fails with `KeyError: 'vllm'`. This PR makes the backend choose between Transformers' class and custom code the same way the model registry does. Fixes `test_non_causal_models[half-Alibaba-NLP/gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct]` in the Extended Pooling jobs (e.g. [build 102826](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102826#01a1db82-3c35-4a85-b52e-43ebf45ece91)). #67716 works around the same failure in the test by loading the model with `trust_remote_code=False`; with this PR, users who pass `--trust-remote-code` (as gte-Qwen2's model card does) no longer hit it, and the test passes unchanged. Related: #67003. ## Claims - gte-Qwen2 serves again with `--trust-remote-code`, under both `--model-impl auto` and `--model-impl transformers`. Both fail on main. - Its embeddings with this PR are identical to vLLM's native Qwen2 before #66821 (cosine 1.0 on every input tested). - Checkpoints with custom code for an architecture Transformers doesn't have (e.g. `vllm-project/Ilama-3.2-1B`) still use their custom code, unchanged. ## Validation GB200, Python 3.12, Transformers 5.23.0. main = `5e51c0ca1`; PR = main + this change. **The failing CI test.** ```bash pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_auto_prefix_cache_support.py::test_non_causal_models ``` ``` # main File ".

title: [ROCm][Warmup] Warm attention over cached context before serving
summary: ## Summary Calls the existing `run_context_prefill_warmup` at the end of `warmup_kernels` for ROCm decoder models. The warmup runs a prefill over cached tokens during startup, so the attention kernels that path uses are built before serving instead of on the first request that reaches them. ## Motivation `warmup_kernels` schedules only fresh prompts (`num_computed_tokens = 0`). On ROCm with `ROCM_AITER_FA`, a prefill over cached tokens, such as a chunked-prefill continuation or a prefix-cache hit, takes the extend path. That path needs a causal+LSE varlen kernel, `mha_varlen_fwd_..._mask_lse_...`, which a fresh prompt never selects. AITER compiles it on first use, so the first such request stalls for roughly 30 s while the server is already taking traffic. The kernel-by-kernel breakdown is in #68022: which modules each ROCm attention backend builds, which ones the current warmup misses, and where a warmup can be registered. This PR is one of two fixes proposed there. ## Changes - Call `run_context_prefill_warmup` at the end of `warmup_kernels`, after the adaptive-verification and acceptance-estimator warmups. - Gate the call on `current_platform.is_rocm()`. Encoder-decoder models are skipped: this step has no encoder input, and the existing warmup already covers cross-attention with a dummy encoder. - Add `test_warmup_kernels_prefills_over_cached_context`, which checks that the cached-context step runs on ROCm and nowhere else. ## Trade-offs - Every ROCm decoder pays one extra forward at startup. title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Size the ERNIE-4.5-VL image budget from the processor's pixel limits

title: [Spec Decode] Per-position acceptance rate over the drafts that reached each position
summary: ## Overview The per-position acceptance rate divides the accepted tokens at position `i` by the number of drafts. When drafts are shorter than `num_speculative_tokens`, for example under dynamic speculative decoding, that under-reports every later position, and a position no draft reached shows `0.000`. This PR divides by the drafted tokens at each position everywhere the rate is computed, and exports the counter that makes it computable from `/metrics`. A second commit seeds the dummy prompts of `vllm bench latency`, whose run-to-run variance hid this kind of change in A/B runs. Follow-up to #64156 (drafted / verified / accepted counts, RFC #64099), whose per-position verified counter this mirrors. ## Claims - The periodic `SpecDecoding metrics` log (Python and Rust frontends), `vllm bench serve`, the Rust bench and `examples/features/speculative_decoding/spec_decode_offline.py` report accepted / drafted at each position; a position no draft reached reports `nan`. With fixed-length drafts nothing changes: drafted per position equals the number of drafts (checked on a real engine below). - New counter `vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_per_pos` (label `position`) in both frontends; the PromQL recipe and `docs/features/speculative_decoding/acceptance_metrics.md` use it. `vllm bench serve` and the Rust bench fall back to `num_drafts` against servers without it. - `vllm bench latency` draws its prompts from `np.random.default_rng(args.seed)`: the engine seeds only its own process, so the prompts, and with speculative decoding the acceptance and latency, changed between runs. #

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix sparse-MLA query-head padding for Kimi-K3.1-Pro on SM120
summary: ## Summary `trtllm_gen_query_heads()` claims to pad query heads to a width the trtllm-gen sparse MLA kernels instantiate, but it only handles `64 < h < 128`. Every other count is passed through unchanged and finds no kernel. ## Impact 96-head models hit this on every usable TP: | layout | heads/rank | instantiated | |---|---|---| | TP32 | 3 | no | | TP16 | 6 | no | | TP8 | 12 | no | | TP4 | 24 | no | | TP2 | 48 | no | (TP12/6/3 would give 8/16/32, but they do not divide the 163840 vocab.) The failure is raised while vLLM sizes the KV cache, so the engine cannot start with `--max-num-batched-tokens` above the 64-token decode budget: ```text ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=8192, num_heads=3, topk=2048, d_qk=576, page_block_size=64, model_type=dsv3_2 ``` ## Change Two files: 1. `trtllm_gen_query_heads()` rounds up to the next instantiated width, keeps the 128 cap, and leaves counts above 128 alone. 2. The SM120 sparse runner pads the query to that width and slices the padded rows off the output. ```python kernel_heads = trtllm_gen_query_heads(num_heads) if kernel_heads != num_heads: q = _pad_query_heads(q, kernel_heads) ... if kernel_heads != num_heads: out = out[:, :num_heads] ``` ### Why this is safe - Padded heads attend the same shared latent KV; the kept rows are bitwise equal to a native-width run with random filler. - The KV cache is unaffected: MLA stores one latent per token, independent of the query head count. - The extra FLOPs are attention-only and measured to be in the noise (see below). ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Fix packed hybrid block sizes for Kimi-K3.1-Pro on SM120
summary: ## Summary `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size()` picks the KV cache block size for hybrid (linear-attention + sparse-MLA) models but never checks that the attention backends can execute it. On SM12x that makes such a model unable to start: - The **packed** hybrid block size is used verbatim, even when no kernel accepts it. - The backends' kernel block sizes are treated only as a **floor**, never a cap. ## The failure ```text ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=8192, num_heads=3, topk=2048, d_qk=576, page_block_size=64, model_type=dsv3_2 ``` and, with pipeline parallelism: ```text ValueError: DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER needs 64-token kernel blocks, which packed 1536-token KV cache blocks cannot be split into. ``` ## Change `vllm/platforms/interface.py` only: 1. **Clamp the packed size to what every backend can execute.** New helper `_largest_common_kernel_block_size(backends, desired)`: | backends report | packed | result | |---|---|---| | `[MultipleOf(64)]` + `[64]` | 256 | **64** | | `[64, 128]` and `[64]` | 256 | 64 | | `[64, 128]` | 256 | 128 | | `[MultipleOf(64)]` only | 256 | 256 | | `[MultipleOf(16)]` only | 544 | 544 | | `[32]` | 256 | 32 | 2. **Log the decision once per worker**, so a rank that resolves it differently is visible in the logs instead of surfacing as a deep assertion. ### Why the generic path is untouched Only the packed branch is clamped. title: [ROCm][MoRIIO] Support DCP for decode instance in PD disaggregated serving with MoRI WRITE mode
summary: ## Overview In WRITE mode, `MoRIIOConnector` copies prefill block `i` straight into decode block `i`, so when the two instances store tokens differerntly, like a decode instance with DCP and a prefill instance without DCP, ends up with its tokens on the wrong ranks. This PR makes each prefill rank write each decode rank exactly the tokens that rank holds for MLA models and at any interleave that divides the block size. ## Claims - A prefill instance without DCP can now feed a DCP decode instance for MLA models, including hybrid MLA + linear-attention models, and every token is written once per DCP group instead of once per decode rank. - On DeepSeek-R1 (8x MI355X), prefill TP4 and decode TP4+DCP4 gives the decode side 3.9x the KV cache of a TP4 decode instance. Under a decode-heavy load it completes all 640 requests with 19% more output per GPU, where TP4 prefill and TP4 decode loses 214 of them to decode-block timeouts. Interleave 1 and 64 perform the same. - On Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (MLA + KDA), prefill TP2 with decode TP2+DCP2 gives the decode instance 1.54x the KV cache of a TP2 one, completes every request with exact-length outputs matching the prefill server, and GSM8K scores are unchanged. - Instances with the same DCP size keep main's rank-to-rank writes, in READ and WRITE mode and for hybrid models, and main's hybrid DCP unit tests pass unchanged. - Layouts the connector can't transfer are refused at the handshake. The affected requests fail with an error and both instances keep serving, where before the request would hang or the decode engine would stop. ##

title: [Bugfix] Stop weak_ref_tensor from keeping the base of 0-size views alive
summary: ## Overview With `qk_rope_head_dim=0` (GLM-5.3-Flash), MLA passes a 0-size view of `qkv_lora` to every eager break of a breakable CUDA graph. `weak_ref_tensor` returned 0-size tensors unchanged, so the replay closures kept one `qkv_lora` per capture size and MLA layer alive in the CUDA graph pool. This PR makes `weak_ref_tensor` return a new empty tensor with the same size, stride, dtype, and device instead. #25954 added the 0-size exemption. #63427 fixed a similar leak for nested graph outputs. ## Claims - `weak_ref_tensor` no longer keeps the base of a 0-size view alive. The returned tensor has the same size, stride, dtype, and device as the input. - On GLM-5.3-Flash (TP8 + EP, 8x H100, default capture sizes), CUDA graph memory drops from 1.89 to 1.40 GiB per GPU, and the KV cache grows from 2,270,520 to 2,311,189 tokens (+1.8%). Larger `max_cudagraph_capture_size` values free more memory. - Accuracy and latency do not regress. GSM8K accuracy is 0.917 on main and 0.918 with this PR, and mean TPOT at concurrency 1 is 6.62 and 6.63 ms. ## Validation All runs use the post-merge CI image of 821851eab0 (`public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:821851eab038d2ec1bcdcb8c7da32a3728f71358`). title: [Perf][DCP] DeepSeek-V3.2: skip other ranks' top-k slots in FP8 sparse attention on Hopper
summary: ## Overview Fixes #58980. Under DCP, each rank owns about 2048/dcp slots of the indexer's 2048-wide top-k row, but `_forward_fp8_kv_mixed_batch` kept the other ranks' slots as `-1` and ran FlashMLA on the full width, so ~(dcp-1)/dcp of every rank's sparse attention went to masked slots, for decode and prefill rows alike. This PR packs the rank's slots into a prefix and passes their count to FlashMLA as `topk_length`. title: [Bugfix] Ignore NaN in QuantFP8 native group quant scale
summary: ## Purpose Serving a BF16 checkpoint with online `--quantization fp8_per_block` on Blackwell (e.g. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 on GB200) crashes during CUDA graph replay with `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED` (719). This needs both the DeepGEMM block FP8 linear kernel and CUDA graphs. Eager mode does not crash. **Root cause** - With torch.compile and `custom_ops=["none"]`, `QuantFP8` takes `forward_native` → `_quantize_group_native`. - There, `x.abs().amax()` passes NaN through, `clamp(min=...)` keeps it, and `exp2(ceil(log2(NaN)))` makes the per-group activation scale NaN. - CUDA graph padding rows (rows ≥ the real token count) can contain stale garbage, including NaN. I observed it first in the attention output that feeds `o_proj`, and it then spreads through the residual stream. - DeepGEMM's `pack_fp32_into_ue8m0` checks that every scale is a positive power of two (`(bits & 0x807fffff) == 0`). A NaN scale trips the device assert, which aborts the graph. - The CUDA `per_token_group_quant` kernel ignores NaN (`fmaxf` with eps), which is why only the native path is affected. I confirmed this with compute-sanitizer and an instrumented `fp8_gemm_nt`: - Every non-UE8M0 activation scale came from a padding row, together with NaN in the FP8 activations. - Masking those scales, or forcing `+quant_fp8` (the CUDA kernel), made the crash go away. **Fix** One line in `_quantize_group_native`: `absmax = torch.nan_to_num(absmax, nan=0.0)`. A NaN group then gets the minimum scale, the same way the CUDA kernel handles it. Results for valid rows do not change. ## Test Plan - New unit test `test_

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Context Aware Sparse LM Head for MTP (BF16 rows)
summary: ## Purpose Part of #67220. Stacked on #67222 (the `DraftVocab` helper); this PR's own changes: https://github.com/stecasta/vllm/compare/draft-vocab-helper...sparse-lm-head-bf16 An MTP drafter reads the target's full lm_head for every draft token: 248,320 x 2,560 in BF16 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, about 1.27 GB. On bandwidth-bound GPUs such as DGX Spark this is 20 to 30% of the decode step. With `draft_token_map` the drafter computes exact logits only for a static list of frequent tokens, and with `draft_token_map_dynamic_rows` also for the rows outside the list that a rank-256 projection of the lm_head scores highest for the current hidden state. The target still verifies with its full head, so outputs are unchanged; only the acceptance length can move. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3), 1x DGX Spark, SPEED-Bench qualitative, 32k list + 16k dynamic BF16 rows: **+13.8% decode at c=1, +7.7% at c=4**, average AL +0.1%, multilingual AL -4.7%. A static list alone loses 5.7% average AL and 33% on multilingual. On top of an already NVFP4 draft head, the sparse head with NVFP4 rows adds +5.5 to 7.9% on Flash-Next, +8.0 to 13.7% on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and +5.5 to 12.2% on Qwen3.8-27B at c=1 across MTP k=3 to 8 (quantized rows are #67238). These runs include the fused scatter of #67223; more results, including the gain on top of NVFP4 heads, are in #67220.

title: [Core] Pack execute_model SchedulerOutput for multiproc RPC
summary: On TP>1, MultiprocExecutor broadcasts `execute_model(SchedulerOutput)` to every worker on each scheduling step. The default `collective_rpc` path pickles the full dataclass object graph, which carries per-field metadata and nested object overhead on this hot path. This PR uses a fixed positional tuple wire format with `array('i')` for int lists so pickle/unpickle operates on a flat schema instead of serializing the dataclass object graph. ## Purpose When `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, `execute_model(SchedulerOutput)` is broadcast to every TP worker on every scheduling step. The generic RPC path pickles the full `SchedulerOutput` dataclass graph through MessageQueue, which adds noticeable Python serialize/deserialize overhead on large scheduler payloads (e.g. steady-state decode with many concurrent requests). This PR: - Packs `SchedulerOutput` into a fixed tuple schema before enqueue - Converts large int lists to `array('i')` for faster pickle/unpickle - Sends a 3-tuple `(EXECUTE_MODEL_FAST_PATH_TAG, packed_payload, output_rank)` for `execute_model` instead of the generic 4-tuple RPC message - Leaves all other RPCs on the existing generic 4-tuple pickle path ## Scope / non-goals - Only applies to `method == "execute_model"` with a single `SchedulerOutput` argument and no kwargs - Does not change model semantics, scheduling logic, or CUDA/ROCm kernels - Does not replace generic RPC pickle; complements tensor-oriented MQ optimizations such as [Perf] Zero-copy torch.Tensor pickling in shm_broadcast MessageQueue #48442 ## Test Plan **New tests** - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_schedu

title: [watermarking] Add SBW (Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking) algorithm
summary: ## Purpose Adds SBW (Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking) as a second watermarking algorithm alongside the existing Gumbel-max scheme introduced in #54053 and extended in #56122. Reference: Ceppi & Sanchez, "Flip, Don't Shuffle: Watermarking LLMs at the Speed of Inference", EMNLP 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03844 SBW is a KGW-family (Kirchenbauer et al.) logit-bias watermark. Like KGW, it derives a pseudorandom green list from the token context and adds a bias `+delta` to green token logits before sampling. Unlike KGW, green-list membership is determined per token independently via a single counter-based PRF call (Philox 4x32-10), with no vocabulary partitioning or hash list. This makes the scheme stateless and O(1) per (token, context) pair. The detector re-derives the same green lists from context and runs a z-score test over the fraction of green tokens in the output. The Philox 4x32-10 PRF is implemented from scratch over int32 to match the paper's integer-domain greenness test exactly (`CBRNG(v, seed_t) < gamma * INT31_MAX`). The same implementation is used in both the sampler and the detector, ensuring bit-identical results across devices and releases. Detection requires only the output token IDs and the watermark parameters; no model weights are needed. Two seeding schemes are supported via `sbw_scheme`: - `selfhash` (default): anchored minhash PRF, seed depends on context and the candidate token. More robust to substitution attacks. Default `context_width=4`. - `lefthash`: additive PRF, one seed per context row. Faster. Default `context_width=1`. Key parameters: `

title: [Discussion] Separate Mamba state pool from the paged KV pool for hybrid models (directional proposal)
summary: # [Discussion] Separate Mamba state pool from the paged KV pool for hybrid models (directional proposal) ## Context #55533 (and its reproductions, e.g. #68081) established why MTP on hybrid GDN models collapses concurrency: **all device groups — including Mamba state and full-attention KV — draw block ids from one shared pool** (per the docstring in `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config`), and speculative decoding inflates per-sequence Mamba residency (`2 + num_speculative_blocks + num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks`, `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1728`), so the scheduler can only afford ~3 resident sequences at decode time. Real numbers from our 4090D TP2 box (Qwen3.8-27B AWQ, v0.33, `max_model_len=262144`, kv fp8, MTP k=1): ``` shared pool: 227 blocks per-request: 9 mamba blocks (3 groups × 3) + 166 full-attn blocks (256K @ 1580 tok/block) → worst-case concurrency = 1.30; startup itself fails against default max_num_seqs=256 ``` ## Observation Mamba state and attention KV are fundamentally different resources: | | Mamba state | attention KV | |---|---|---| | size | fixed per sequence (slot-like) | grows with context (paged) | | lifetime | whole sequence, non-preemptable | dynamic, preemptable | | spec-decode impact | ×(1+k) inflation | none | Sharing one block-id pool means a fixed-size, non-preemptable resource competes with an elastic paged one — the elastic side starves the fixed side under pressure, which is exactly the #55533 signature. For reference, SGLang's hybrid path keeps the (mamba/linear) state pool separate from the paged KV pool for these models. ## Direct

title: [Speculative] Warm standalone AR prefill block sizes at startup
summary: ## Overview Warm the power-of-two `BLOCK_SIZE` ladder for the standalone-AR draft prefill kernel, and stop specializing `max_num_reqs` and `max_model_len`. A draft-model server compiled a wider kernel on the first long chunk than startup had built. Details are in #68022. The target-dependent AR kernel hardcodes `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` and is not part of this change. Ngram speculation did not miss this kernel. No open PR warms this ladder. ## Claims - The ladder is `4, 8, ..., min(512, next_power_of_2(max_num_batched_tokens + 2))`, which is the launch rule in `prepare_prefill_inputs` (`min(512, next_power_of_2(max(query_lens) + 2))`). A one-token query is the smallest real case, so the ladder starts at 4. - For `max_num_batched_tokens=64` the keys are 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. title: [Bugfix] Restore exact division in per-token-group FP8 quantization for non-UE8M0 scales
summary: ## Why #61343 switched `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (and the fused `norm_and_quant`) from per-element division by the group scale to a per-group reciprocal + per-element multiply. For UE8M0 (power-of-two) scales `x * (1/y_s)` is exact, but for plain FP32 scales the second rounding differs from `div.rn` exactly on e4m3 tie boundaries and moves quantized codes across the 8-bit boundary. The pre-change code carried a comment warning about precisely this, deleted by the same commit. Kernel-level measurements in #65906: ~0.05% of elements flip on real bf16 activations (177/327,680 at the embedding layer), 93.8% of them upward — a directional bias concentrated in early layers, matching the small accuracy drop reported there on FP32-scale blockwise FP8 models (e.g. Qwen3.5-*-FP8). ## What - `QuantizeGroup` (smem schedule): new `USE_RECIP` template parameter; division unless the scale is UE8M0 (call sites pass `SCALE_UE8M0`, so the multiply folds away at compile time — no runtime branch). - register-resident schedule: restore `SCALE_UE8M0 ? v * inv_y : v / y_s` (the exact pre-#61343 form). - fused `norm_and_quant`: revert `mul_by_recip`; the fp32 scale there is never a power of two, so the reciprocal is never exact on this path. - UE8M0 paths (incl. the packed-register kernel) are untouched and keep the reciprocal fast path, where it is exact. ## Cost Measured on GB200 against the same kernel using the reciprocal: | shape (rows × cols) | div | recip | ratio | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 × 4096 | 6.41 µs | 5.35 µs | 1.20× | | 4096 × 4096 | 20.83 µs | 17.33 µs | 1.20× | | 8192 × 8192 |

title: [RFC]: Let replicas read each other's GPU KV cache (L1 sharing)
summary: > [!NOTE] > This RFC is at an early stage and under active development. We will keep updating the design and results as the work progresses, and feedback is very welcome. Terms: **L1** = a replica's GPU KV cache; **L2** = host-DRAM KV tier; **L3** = SSD or remote KV store. ### Motivation. Each model replica's GPU KV cache is private: another replica can reuse a block only after it is offloaded to L2/L3. As a result: - **Most KV cannot be shared.** Only offloaded KV can be shared: on a 72-GPU rack, the KV in tens of TB of HBM is invisible to other replicas, and each shared block is stored many times (on every GPU that uses it, plus L2/L3). - **Cache affinity vs. load balance.** Pinning sessions to the replica that holds their prefix keeps hits high but leaves replicas unevenly loaded, while balancing load sends requests to replicas without the prefix, turning hits into L2/L3 reloads or recompute. **Rack-scale systems such as AMD Helios and NVIDIA NVL72 put 72 GPUs in one scale-up domain. Pooling their HBM (e.g. 72 × 432 GB ≈ 31 TB on a Helios rack of MI455X GPUs) turns 72 private KV caches into one shared cache**, which brings several benefits: 1. **Larger effective KV capacity (the main benefit).** Sharing no longer requires offloading, L2/L3 hold only blocks no GPU holds, and duplicate GPU copies can be evicted first. Capacity grows from "L2/L3" towards "GPU pool + L2/L3". 2. **Load balancing without losing hits.** A hit no longer depends on landing on the replica that holds the prefix: the router can pick the least-loaded replica, and a prefix held by another GPU is copie

title: [ROCm] Cached-context attention warmup: which kernels are missed
summary: ## Problem `warmup_kernels` schedules fresh prompts (`num_computed_tokens = 0`). A step that already has cached tokens can run a different attention kernel, and that kernel is then built on the first serving request. The expensive case is `ROCM_AITER_FA`. `AiterFlashAttentionImpl.extend_forward` asks AITER for two varlen modules that a fresh prompt never asks for. On gfx950 each one takes about 47 s to build. A chunked continuation or a prefix-cache hit is what reaches them. Head dim 128 on gfx950 usually takes `module_fmha_v3_varlen_fwd` instead, and that assembly kernel serves both the fresh call and the extend calls, so the stall shows up at head dims such as 64 and 256. This is the path gemma-2 and Muse Spark hit in #67083. At concurrency 32 a 1024-token prompt no longer fits in the 8192-token step, the later piece has cached tokens, and the server log shows `mha_varlen_fwd_bf16_…_mask_lse_…` building while requests are waiting (about 26 s on gemma, about 30 s on Muse). title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: column-shard the MoE pooler/unpooler over TP
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, the Muse Spark MoE pooler (8192 → 4096) and unpooler (4096 → 8192) are `ReplicatedLinear`, so at TP8 every rank reads both full BF16 weights on every step: 134 MB per layer, about 8.3 GB per forward over the 62 layers. This PR makes both projections `ColumnParallelLinear` and all-gathers their output columns over TP. Each output column is still computed from the full reduction on one rank; the gather only moves data. See Details. - **Accuracy:** GSM8K unchanged (paired exact McNemar p = 0.86). Outputs are not bit-identical, because the GEMM summation order changes. - **Default on** when every TP rank sees the same tokens (TP > 1, no sequence-parallel MoE, DP = 1, not `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`), with the same config switches as the CUDA path. title: [ROCm] Fuse Muse Spark's attention boundary into FlyDSL QuickReduce
summary: ## Summary - The attention all-reduce and `_norm_residual_norm` stay two kernels today. This runs both inside AITER FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce (`QuickAllReduceInt4.allreduce_norm_residual_norm`, ROCm/aiter#7761): the same bf16 all-reduce a plain QuickReduce would store, then `new_stream = alpha * stream + beta * post_norm(reduced)` and `out = pre_norm(new_stream)`. The reduced branch is overwritten. - It fires only when that o_proj partial would already take FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce. There is no new environment variable. That path is removed. The kernel lives in AITER. vLLM only decides to call it. - Not a measured speedup. The multi-GPU check is the AITER test, which compares the fused outputs to plain QuickReduce followed by the same boundary. ## Test plan - [ ] AITER: `python op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_flydsl_quick_allreduce_int4_boundary.py` on gfx942 or gfx950 - [ ] Muse Spark, MI355X, TP8, with FlyDSL QuickReduce enabled: a prefill or mixed step whose o_proj partial is large enough for INT4 matches the unfused QuickReduce plus `_norm_residual_norm` - [ ] A step below the QuickReduce size floor still all-reduces and norms as before - [ ] With an AITER build that does not have `allreduce_norm_residual_norm`, the boundary stays on the unfused path

title: [Perf][MoE] Select full-warp top-k rows with redux.sync and keep selections in registers (SM80+)
summary: ## Overview `topkGating` (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu`) gives each row to one full warp when the row is wide enough (512 experts, 256 experts with 16-bit logits, 128-512 experts with fp32 logits). For each of the k selections it runs a 5-stage shuffle butterfly with 3 dependent shuffles per stage, then lane 0 stores the selection and later re-reads the weights to scale them. For those rows, without a correction bias, this PR selects each expert with two `redux.sync` reductions (`__reduce_max_sync` on the score key, then `__reduce_min_sync` on the expert among the lanes that hold the max), keeps selection i in the registers of lane i, rescans only in the winning lane, and writes the row once at the end. The output is bitwise equal to `main`: the same experts, the same order, the same lowest-index tie rule and the same weight bits. The register-resident output path is from @Gin-Sin (#64731, co-author); the SM80+ `redux.sync` selection scope is from this PR. #64731 will be closed in favour of this PR. ## Claims - **Same output:** bitwise equal to `main` (ids, weights as bits, token-expert indices) in every case run on A100, including tie-heavy, all-equal and NaN/Inf rows. - **Faster on SM80+:** E 512 top-10 softmax on A100: 0.59-0.68x of `main`'s time at 1-256 tokens, 0.71-0.76x at 1,024-4,096 tokens. summary: Supersedes #54342 (closed): the same branch, rebased on current main. ## Overview `HF3FSKVConnector` keys its external cache on `md5(prompt token ids)`. title: [Bugfix] Stop advertising fp8_e5m2 where the KV writer stores e4m3
summary: Supersedes #54341 (closed): the same branch, rebased on current main. ## Overview `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` stores an e4m3 variant for every fp8 cache dtype, yet `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN` advertise `fp8_e5m2`. On ROCm, `ROCM_ATTN` decodes that cache as `torch.float8_e5m2`, so the model returns garbage with no error. On CUDA, `TRITON_ATTN` loads the model and then fails its first forward pass with a bare `AssertionError`. This PR stops advertising `fp8_e5m2` on both backends and refuses it in the writer, so the request fails at backend selection with a clear message. ## Claims - **Bug, ROCm:** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` on `ROCM_ATTN` with block sizes other than 16/32 stores e4m3 bits and reads them back as e5m2. The output is garbage and no error is raised. With block size 16/32 the C++ writer refuses e5m2 with a `RuntimeError`, so the result depends only on the block size. - **Bug, CUDA:** on `TRITON_ATTN` (L4, SM89) the same flag loads the model and then fails in `Attention.forward` with a bare `AssertionError` (`attention.py:543`). - **Root cause:** the writer stores `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`, which is `float8_e4m3fn` or `float8_e4m3fnuz` on every platform. `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py` and `prefix_prefill.py`, which `ROCM_ATTN` uses, decode `fp8_e5m2` as `torch.float8_e5m2`. - **Fix:** remove `fp8_e5m2` from `TritonAttentionBackend` and `RocmAttentionBackend` `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`, return `False` for it in `_is_supported_kv_cache_dtype`, and drop the RDNA exception that kept `ROCM_ATTN` for it. `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3` are unchanged. ## Validation

summary: ## Summary - Recognize Quark online Hadamard rotations on routed MXFP4 experts (`input_rotation` for w1/w2/w3 of the same layer) and pass a `rotation_size` to the MoE method. - Rotate MoE activations before both GEMMs. When the oracle selects `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` and the installed AITER `fused_moe` accepts `inter_hadamard`, the fused kernel is kept: vLLM rotates the hidden states before the first GEMM, and AITER rotates the SwiGLU output before the second. Online Hadamard checkpoints store expert weights already rotated along K by an orthonormal Sylvester matrix of size 128. Activations must be rotated by the same block Hadamard before quantization, so `(xH)(wH)^T = x w^T`. Shared experts are not rotated. The checkpoint conversion script that renames the 21888 expert `input_rotation` tensors into the vLLM layout lives outside this repo and is not part of this PR. `inter_hadamard` is not in upstream AITER yet. This PR only passes it when the installed `aiter.fused_moe` accepts the argument; a stock AITER build takes the emulation fallback, which is the previous behavior. ## Relation to #62750 and #65398 This is not a duplicate of those PRs. title: [Multimodal] Preprocess multimodal inputs in parallel when the processor cache is off
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview The API server renders every multimodal request (chat template, media load, HF processor) before it reaches the engine, on a single thread, because with the processor cache on the frontend cache must stay ordered with the engine-core cache (#38418). With the cache off (`--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`) there is no order to keep, yet a burst of requests is still preprocessed one at a time, and numba-based processors abort the process if two threads enter a `parallel=True` region. This PR serializes numba's workqueue threading layer behind a process-wide lock (commit 1) and then preprocesses on `--renderer-num-workers` threads when the cache is off (commit 2); the cache-on default is unchanged. **Perf: API-server CPU time -45 to -68%, render time -15 to -66% per request (MI350X: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP2 and three TP1 models); end to end neutral on GPU-bound runs, +4% tok/s on Qwen2.5-VL-7B (MI350X); InternVL3-8B: see Claims.** ## Claims - Bug fix (commit 1): concurrent numba `parallel=True` regions no longer abort the process with SIGABRT (`Concurrent access has been detected`). On `main` this is reachable only once preprocessing is multi-threaded (commit 2). - Feature (commit 2): any multimodal model served with `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --renderer-num-workers N` (N > 1) preprocesses N requests at a time instead of one, halving the API server's CPU time per request. title: [Core] Opt-in time-bounded prefill hold in the v1 scheduler
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview The v1 scheduler admits each new request in the next step after it arrives, so while decodes run, a stream of arrivals is prefilled one or two requests per step and every step that carries a prefill slows all running decodes. Under independent arrivals near capacity this keeps TPOT high, and today there is no way to trade a small, bounded TTFT increase for it (`--prefill-schedule-interval`, #54627, counts steps and also defers chunks of admitted prompts). This PR adds an opt-in hold: while decodes run, new requests wait until the oldest waiting one has waited `--prefill-hold-ms`, so nearby arrivals are prefilled together; the added TTFT is at most the hold and admitted prompts are never deferred. **Perf (opt-in, 50 ms): Poisson arrivals at 90% of capacity, median TPOT -24%, goodput +142%, median TTFT and throughput unchanged (MI355X, MiniMax-M3 TP4). Default off: no change.** ## Claims - A model-agnostic knob for any model on the v1 scheduler; `--prefill-hold-ms 0` (default) changes nothing. title: [Bug]: FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce workspace is allocated after KV cache sizing
summary: ### Your current environment ```text 4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, 97,887 MiB), PCIe only: GPUs 0-1 and 2-3 behind one PCIe switch each (PIX), SYS between the pairs, P2P OK on all pairs Driver 615.71.09 vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f5d93296c8ec82b7e7dabdb308d24d43cb1907bf (sha256:902b49de0568...) vLLM 0.34.0rc1.dev206+gf5d93296c, torch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.3, Triton 3.8.0 ``` (Summary, not `collect_env.py` output.) ### Describe the bug With `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER_PCIE_IPC=1`, the FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce allocates its workspace in `FlashInferPcieIpcAllReduce.setup()`, which `kernel_warmup` calls from `compile_or_warm_up_model`. title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Read the hot cache as flat rows in FlashMLA FP8 decode
summary: ## Purpose FLASHMLA_SPARSE with HiSparse crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access in the FP8 sparse decode kernel. Before the crash, decode attention reads the wrong KV rows. HiSparse resolves top-k to flat-row indices over the hot cache: `block * block_stride_rows + offset`. With `fp8_ds_mla`, hot blocks interleave with other layers' rows, so the stride is 271 rows rather than 64. `_host_backed_fp8_decode` passed the strided cache to FlashMLA as 64-token pages, and FlashMLA decodes an index as `page * 64 + offset`. Most indices pointed at the wrong row, and high blocks pointed past the end of the cache. The fix reads the hot cache as flat rows (`[rows, 1, row_bytes]`). This is the same view the BF16 HiSparse path and the other sparse MLA backends already use. With the V32 layout that HiSparse uses here, each row carries its own scales, so FlashMLA sparse decode addresses a page size of 1 row by row. ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse`. The decode test now uses an interleaved hot cache and checks that each index reaches the row HiSparse resolved. - FlashMLA FP8 sparse decode on the same interleaved cache, run once as 64-row pages and once as flat rows (B=60, h_q=64, topk=2048), on 1×B200. SM90 takes the same path but was not run. - GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP8, 8×B200: `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 18432 --max-num-seqs 256`, with HiSparse `host_pool_gib=128`. lm_eval GSM8K, 5-shot, `num_concurrent=64`. title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Register custom AR graph buffers only after a capture that did not raise
summary: ## Overview `CustomAllreduce.capture()` calls `register_graph_buffers()` in its `finally` block, so the call also runs while an exception from the capture propagates. `register_graph_buffers()` is a cross-rank collective (`dist.broadcast_object_list` on the CPU group). When one rank raises during CUDA graph capture (for example CUDA out of memory), the other ranks do not join this collective. The failing rank then waits until the gloo timeout (30 min by default) and does not report the original error. This PR registers the graph buffers only after a capture that did not raise. ## Claims - An exception inside `CustomAllreduce.capture()` reaches the caller at once with its original message. Before this PR, it hung in the registration collective until the gloo timeout. - A capture that succeeds is unchanged: it registers the graph buffers once at exit, as before. - `_IS_CAPTURING` is reset on every exit path, as before. ## Validation **CPU reproduction** (2 processes, gloo CPU group with a 20 s timeout, the real `CustomAllreduce.capture()` with `register_graph_buffers` replaced by the same broadcast loop without the CUDA IPC calls). Rank 0 raises inside `capture()`. Rank 1 waits in another collective, as a rank does when it waits for rank 0 in a GPU collective. | Code | Rank 0 result | |---|---| | `main` (5be4266f5) | `RuntimeError: ...
