title: [Bugfix][FP8][MoE] Propagate use_deep_gemm=False denylist into MoE backend selector
summary: ## Summary When `VllmConfig._verify_quantization` sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm=False` for model types excluded from DeepGEMM support (e.g., `qwen3_5_text`, `qwen3_5_moe_text`), this correctly gates the **linear-layer** path, but `Fp8MoEMethod.__init__` called `select_fp8_moe_backend()` without passing that signal. As a result, the **MoE path** still selected `DEEPGEMM`/`BATCHED_DEEPGEMM` backends on hardware where they would be invalid for those model types. ## Changes 1. Added a `force_disable_deep_gemm` parameter to `select_fp8_moe_backend()` that unconditionally removes `DEEPGEMM` and `BATCHED_DEEPGEMM` from the `AVAILABLE_BACKENDS` list **before** any environment-variable checks. This ensures that a denylisted model cannot be re-enabled via `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`. 2. Modified `Fp8MoEMethod.__init__` to pass `force_disable_deep_gemm=(self.quant_config.use_deep_gemm is False)` to propagate the per-model-type denylist decision into MoE backend selection. ## Rationale - The denylist in `VllmConfig._verify_quantization` already prevents DeepGEMM from being used for incompatible model types on the linear-layer path. - Without this fix, the MoE path could still select DeepGEMM backends, leading to runtime failures or incorrect behavior on affected hardware. - This fix ensures consistent behavior across both linear and MoE paths. title: [Kernel] Exact top-p cutoffs and kept log-sum-exps for bf16 logits
summary: ## Overview Adds `topp_cutoffs_lse`, a CUDA op (SM90 and datacenter Blackwell) that turns each bf16 logit row into its exact top-p cutoff, keeping every token tied at the cutoff, and the fp64 log-sum-exp of `x / T` over the kept tokens, in one launch. Nothing calls it yet; #65102 uses it to apply top-p to speculative-decoding verification rows as the rejection kernels load them. Part of #61024; 2/4 of a stack (see the end). **Update (2026-11-02):** the second commit reworks the kernel after an ncu pass. It picks the cluster size per batch, halves the histogram's cost and adds a fixed-point tier ahead of the fp64 fallback. It gives the same cutoffs bit for bit and is 2.4× faster than the first commit from 128 rows up. The third makes every CTA of a cluster start before a peer writes its shared memory (found by racecheck). **Fix (2026-11-03):** the op now reads `expanded_idx_mapping` as int64, the dtype Model Runner V2 has built its index mappings in since #60736. It accepted only int32, so with #65102 the first verification chunk that took the top-p path raised `expanded_idx_mapping must be int32` and took EngineCore down. The tests and the benchmark built int32 mappings, so they missed it; it was found by an end-to-end serving test of the stack, and #65102 now adds an `LLM` test that runs the op on the model runner's own mappings. ## Claims - One launch replaces what verification runs for top-p rows today: an fp32 copy of the target logits, the temperature kernel and the Triton top-k/top-p mask. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Check pointer alignment before vectorizing activation kernels
summary: ## Overview The activation launchers in `csrc/activation_kernels.cu` (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`, `fatrelu_and_mul`, `gelu_fast`, ...) pick the 128/256-bit vector path from the row width alone. A contiguous input or output whose data pointer is not vector-aligned, such as a view at an odd storage offset, passes that check and then fails with `CUDA error: misaligned address`, which leaves the CUDA context unusable. This PR also checks both data pointers and falls back to the existing scalar path when either is unaligned. ## Claims - Inputs or outputs at an unaligned storage offset now produce correct results instead of a sticky CUDA error, for all ops built on the three launch macros. - Aligned tensors take the same vector path as before: on Qwen3-8B, GSM8K scores match main, and serving throughput is similar across the measured runs (raw output below). ## Validation H100 80GB HBM3, main `3a104103ac` wheel. The e2e runs force `silu_and_mul` to the CUDA kernel with `--compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["+silu_and_mul"]}'`; with `torch.compile` the default uses the native op. ```text $ cd tests && python -m pytest kernels/core/test_activation.py -k misaligned_data_ptr -v -x # main E torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: misaligned address FAILED kernels/core/test_activation.py::test_activation_misaligne

title: [KV Cache] Add layer-sharded MLA cache with NCCL broadcast (KVPP)
summary: ## Summary Add opt-in `--enable-kvpp` for replicated MLA KV caches on NVIDIA GPUs. Each layer bundle has one persistent owner within a **PCP × TP** replica group; other ranks materialize it in two reusable scratch slots. NCCL broadcast prefetches the next bundle before the current attention, with CUDA events protecting cache writes and buffer reuse. The intended workload is multi-prefix serving where limited KV memory causes cache eviction. Layer ownership increases cache capacity while preserving ordinary attention tensor views. ## Integration and usage - Reuse the existing logical block, prefix-cache, scheduler, and KV config construction flows. Account for owner storage and scratch in capacity calculation, then apply physical placement after the common block count is finalized. - Share one storage plan between allocation, broadcast, and owner-only `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` registration. - Manage the KVPP communicator in `parallel_state`, scoped to each DP replica and PP stage. Reuse PCP's existing KV gathering with DCP=1. Requires Model Runner V2 and PCP × TP ≥ 2. Use `--enforce-eager`, or: ```text --enable-kvpp -cc.mode=3 -cc.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=false ``` Keep the default attention/KV-update splitting ops. FULL graphs and GPU MRV1 are unsupported. PCP MoE also requires `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`. See [design and compatibility limits](https://github.com/pisceskkk/vllm/blob/codex/kvpp-attn-prefetch-bcast/docs/design/kv_cache_layer_sharding.md) for other combinations. ## Accuracy and correctness **DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, 4×H100, TP2 ×

title: [RFC]: Session-Aware KV Cache Hints for Agentic Workloads
summary: ### Motivation. Agentic applications often know more about future KV cache reuse than the inference engine: - a child agent is waiting for a tool and will probably resume soon; - several agents share a long system/tool prefix; - a branch has completed and its KV cache can be released; - an offloaded branch will be resumed and can be prefetched. Today, after a request finishes, these prefixes are ordinary free cached blocks managed by the same replacement policy. vLLM cannot distinguish a temporarily idle but valuable agent context from a prefix that will never be used again. This RFC proposes optional `agent_hint` metadata so an application can communicate session identity, a short retention TTL, and explicit cache management operations. The goal is to improve prefix-cache hit rate and TTFT for multi-turn and multi-agent workloads. The proposal addresses an information gap rather than replacing vLLM's cache policy. An agent runtime knows when a tool call is outstanding, a sub-agent has finished, a conversation has been suspended, or a checkpoint is about to be resumed. vLLM knows which KV blocks are resident and when capacity is needed. Neither side can make the best decision with only its own information. Hints provide a narrow, best-effort contract between those two layers. ### Workload scenarios and expected value The largest opportunity is not generic chat traffic, but workloads with long prefixes and explicit lifecycle transitions: | Application event | Hint/action | Expected system value | | --- | --- | --- | | A long-running agent waits for a tool or user response |

title: [Bugfix] Swap ipc_cache tensors into meta placeholders in place
summary: ## Summary `--load-format ipc_cache` left MoE routers on **meta** placeholders. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` used to `pop` + `register_parameter` a *new* `nn.Parameter`, so objects that captured the placeholder during construction (e.g. routers holding `gate.e_score_correction_bias`) kept pointing at the meta tensor → illegal memory access / meta-tensor errors at runtime. title: [RFC]: Keep agent KV in the CPU offload tier across tool calls, using client hints
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **TL;DR:** Agent sessions spend most of their life waiting on tools. When a tool call takes minutes, the session's KV often falls out of vLLM's CPU offload tier, and its whole prefix is recomputed when it comes back. Several open RFCs (#52113, #51428, #57103) propose ways for clients to describe these waits and lifecycles. We built a CPU-offload eviction policy driven by that kind of advice and measured it. In an exploratory, adaptive campaign on one GPU, the combined advice policy cut recomputed prefix tokens on hinting sessions' returns from 7.8% (best tested server-only hold) to 1.5% at a 3 GiB CPU pool, on 5 of 5 seeds. We are not proposing a new hint API. This RFC offers the policy's rules, the evidence, a reference implementation, and questions about which interface should carry the advice. ## Context With CPU offloading on, vLLM copies computed KV blocks into a pinned host pool. When the pool fills, a `CachePolicy` picks what to evict: LRU by default, ARC, or an out-of-tree policy via `cache_policy_module_path`. A new request looks up its prefix in the GPU prefix cache first, then in the CPU pool; anything missing is recomputed. An agent session alternates a model turn with a tool call, and its context grows every turn (here from about 3k to 16k tokens). In agent traces we captured, most waits are short (median 0.24 s), but about 1% run past 30 s: builds, test suites, web research, a human approving a step. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview A MoE Gemma 4 target cannot start with its MTP assistant when expert parallelism is on. summary: ## Overview #57924 moved Nemotron VL's rescale and normalization to the GPU, but images and video frames are still resized on the CPU. That `uint8` bicubic resize is now the largest CPU cost in Nemotron's preprocessing: ~350 ms per Perception Test video on one Grace core. The primary win of this change is an upwards of 40-50% reduction in TTFT for image and video workloads. This PR moves that resize to the GPU for `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2`, which serves Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, and video for Nemotron Nano VL v2. The API server sends the decoded `uint8` pixels at their source resolution, and the model resizes them on the GPU with [CV-CUDA](https://github.com/CVCUDA/CV-CUDA), which is an actively developed, maintained, and optimized near-SOL image processing and CV library from NVIDIA (Disclosure: I am a member of the team that supports this library). title: [Core] Add prefill_schedule_backlog_interval to bound prefill bursts
summary: ## Purpose `prefill_schedule_interval=N` defers prefill to every Nth engine step, so decode-only steps sit between prefill chunks. Today, a prefill step that leaves requests waiting sets `prefill_capacity_bound`, and the throttle then stays off until the queue drains. In a burst of long uncached prompts, prefill chunks run back to back. Every decoding request stalls for the whole burst, and that becomes a fat inter-token-latency tail. This PR adds `--prefill-schedule-backlog-interval M` (default 1, the current behavior). While the backlog lifts the throttle, prefill is admitted on every Mth throttled step instead of on every step. The release still drains the backlog, but decode-only steps stay between the prefill chunks. - The engine-core cadence, the `schedule(throttle_prefills)` interface, and the DP alignment of the regular cadence are unchanged. The backlog release was never rank-aligned. - The new field is excluded from the compile hash, like `prefill_schedule_interval`. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_throttle_capacity_bound_backlog_interval[1|3]` builds a capacity-bound backlog and checks which throttled steps admit prefill: every step for M=1, `[no, no, yes, no, no, yes]` for M=3. The M=3 case fails on the current scheduler. The existing throttle and gating tests still pass. - End to end: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash NVFP4 on 1×B300 node, TP2, DSpark speculative decoding, CPU KV offload. title: [Model][DSv4.1] Token-shard sparse-MLA prefill under TP (ShardQ)
summary: Enable ShardQ for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. On 8xH20 with TP8, the final gated build takes 1M-token prefill from 83.1 s to 50.0 s (-39.9%, 1.66x). ## Overview #63956 added token-sharded prefill for the V3.2/GLM `MLAAttention` path, but V4.1 runs its own `DeepseekV4Attention`/`FlashMLA` path, so its prefill indexer still scores every token on every TP rank. That scan is what dominates long prompts. This PR enables the same idea for V4.1-Flash. Each rank takes a zigzag slice of the step's tokens, runs the indexer and the compressed-KV/SWA attention for those rows with all heads, and two all-to-alls move the Q in and the output out. The decision is one hook on the model, shared by the indexer and the attention builders, so a step is either sharded on every rank or head-sharded on every rank. I also added a size gate. The main path needs at least 3072 prefill tokens in the step and at least 2048 in every request; the long-context tail exception keeps a step sharded when its own long-context requests (32K+ context) contribute at least 1024 tokens. Both numbers are measured on this model; the data behind them is below. Related work: #63956 (ShardQ for V3.2/GLM), #66041 (model-owned split hints for the same generic split; my keyword-only `eligibility` hook composes with its positional `sequence_parallel`), #65555 (ROCm-only V4.1 indexer slicing, CUDA unchanged), #66052 (a pre-existing race in the shared indexer upload path that this PR exercises). ## Claims - Final gated build, 8xH20 TP8, 1M prefill: 83.133 s with `sparse_mla_shard_q=false`, 49.995 s with it on, -39.9% (1.66x). 256K: 1

title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Expire write_done notifications no request matches
summary: ## Overview Bound the MoRIIO WRITE consumer's buffer of `write_done` notifications that arrive before their transfer is mapped: an entry no request ever matches is now dropped after 60 s (and the buffer is capped at 4096), instead of being kept and rescanned every step forever. Tracked in ROCm/mori#759. ## Claims - Fixes an unbounded leak on the decode worker: a `write_done` for a request that already finished (e.g. a client abort while the request waits for its KV) stayed in `_unmatched_write_completions` for the life of the process, and the whole buffer was rescanned twice per scheduler step. - An early `write_done` (one that races ahead of `start_load_kv`) still matches as before; only entries still unmatched after 60 s are dropped, counted in a warning; entries dropped at the cap are counted in an error. - No new config, no change outside the MoRIIO connector and its usage doc. ## Validation **End to end** (1P1D Qwen3-8B TP1, MoRIIO WRITE over RDMA, 2 x MI355X nodes with AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI NICs, MoRI 1.2.3.post1 from the `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` image; prefill on vLLM 76c6f3f, decode on vLLM be47189f3 with this PR's connector change applied for the PR arm). `defer_timeout=20`, to show that the retention no longer follows it. Send a request to decode, abort it client-side while it waits for KV (decode unmaps its transfer), then serve the same transfer on prefill, which writes and sends `write_done`. Repeated 4 times, then 15 normal P/D requests over 75 s. Buffer size from a logging-only probe (not part of this PR): | | after the 4 aborted transfers | 75 s

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: serve deep-K skinny GEMM shapes with the chunked HIP kernel on gfx12
summary: ## Summary On gfx12 (RDNA4), W4A16 `down_proj`-like layers (large K) at batch 3-5 fall off the fast HIP skinny int4 kernel onto the Triton fallback, because the HIP path is gated by an LDS size check. The HIP kernel already has a `CHUNKED` variant that walks K in LDS-sized chunks and removes that limit; it is compiled for all gfx1x but only enabled on gfx115x. **This PR enables the existing chunked kernel on gfx12.** No new kernel, no new op, no weight-layout change - only the dispatch rule changes. title: [Core][DBO] Allow dual batch overlap with pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Overview Allow dual batch overlap (DBO) with pipeline parallelism in Model Runner V2. Each pipeline stage microbatches its own forward pass and the stages keep exchanging whole batches. Stacked on #65128 (MORI EPv2 with DBO, native and AsyncLL). Only the last commit is new here; this PR stays a draft until #65128 lands. Related: #64350 (tracked in #64334) is a draft that allows PP + DBO for one narrower combination (NIXL EP, TP=1, synchronous scheduling, no CUDA graphs) together with a refactor of the microbatch runner, and has only CPU validation so far. This PR is the minimal change for the V2 runner as it is on main: it only drops the config check, covers MORI EPv2 (native and AsyncLL), and brings GPU accuracy and throughput data. If the reviewers prefer to land the scope through #64350, the data below can be used there instead, and I am happy to close this one. ## Claims - `--enable-dbo` can be combined with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` on the V2 runner. The only change to runtime code is removing the config check that rejected the combination; the V2 runner already slices `intermediate_tensors` per microbatch (`slice_model_inputs`) and merges `IntermediateTensors` outputs back into one batch (`merge_ubatch_outputs`). - On a single 8x MI355X node with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, PP2 x DP4 (EP4 per stage) with MORI EPv2 gains +21.9% prefill throughput (AsyncLL) and +15.4% (native) from DBO, close to the gain DBO gives a DEP8 layout on the same node (+23.9% / +19.3%). gsm8k matches the runs without DBO and the DEP8 reference. ## Validation Hardware and stack: 8x MI355X (ROCm)

title: [Model] Enable sequence-parallel MoE with pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Motivation SP-MoE (`use_sequence_parallel_moe`) currently hard-disables itself when `pipeline_parallel_size > 1`, with a TODO in `deepseek_v2.py`: *"enable SP MoE with PP after the PP boundary logic can safely send/receive sequence-parallel hidden_states across stages."* This PR implements that boundary logic and removes the guards. ## Changes 1. **PP boundary gather** (`qwen3_next.py`, `deepseek_v2.py`): non-last stages packed the sequence-sharded `hidden_states`/`residual` into `IntermediateTensors` as-is. Now they are gathered first (same cat → all-gather → trim → split pattern already used at the last-rank exit). The gather is driven by an explicit SP flag, not a shape check: after SP padding, a shard can equal `full_num_tokens` on decode steps (T=1, tp=2), which silently skips the gather and leaks a pad row across the boundary. 2. **Runtime downgrade for small batches** (`qwen3_next.py`): with fewer tokens than TP ranks, SP pads rows up to the TP size; pad rows propagate through norm/experts and produce NaN that then spreads through every subsequent gather (observed: decode outputs collapse to a flat distribution; per-rank probes show NaN). Steps with `num_tokens < tp_size` now take the replicated path. Because `o_proj` is built with `reduce_results=False` under SP, the downgraded step reduces partial sums with an explicit all-reduce. title: [Feature][EPLB] Expose cached EP rank-to-node topology
summary: ## Overview Expose `EplbState.get_rank_node_ids()` so node-aware EPLB integrations can obtain the actual EP rank-to-node assignment instead of inferring it from a node count. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Report async EPLB worker failures to fault tolerance instead of stalling
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #66144. With `--enable-fault-tolerance`, an async EPLB worker exception is now reported to fault tolerance (FT) instead of silently stopping EPLB. ## Claims - Under FT, an exception in the async EPLB worker makes `step()` raise on every rank, through the #62009 path. Before, it raised nowhere: EPLB stopped for good and the engine stayed HEALTHY. - The worker thread still stays alive, so a `retry` can resume EPLB. `scale_down` redistributes the experts and then disables rebalancing (`eep_eplb_suppressed`). If no recovery arrives, the engine raises the original error and exits after `engine_recovery_timeout_sec` (existing FT behavior, not run end to end here). - `reset_eplb_async_state()` first waits for the worker to finish the cycle it is in, then clears the error, so recovery never resets the state or rebuilds the groups under a running cycle. A peer's worker blocked in a collective ends within `cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`; if the wait times out, the `retry` fails and can be sent again. The reset clears `rebalanced` before it changes the reset epoch, so a cycle that starts during the reset transfers nothing. - Docs: the fault-tolerance section of `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md` says an async EPLB worker error is a fault, and that `retry` resumes rebalancing unless an earlier `scale_down` disabled it. ## Validation - Unit tests in `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`. title: [RFC]: Allow the DSA Indexer to Use Context Parallelism Independently
summary: ### Motivation. > **RFC scope.** This RFC requests architectural feedback on allowing the DSA Indexer and Sparse MLA to use different parallel contexts. It does not propose a complete scheduling policy or optimized cross-rank communication system. The first implementation would exercise this capability only through a fixed Indexer-CP configuration while preserving the existing Sparse MLA execution path and today's default behavior. DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) has two sequential stages: 1. The Indexer scans the history-wide index cache and selects global Top-K token positions. 2. Sparse MLA reads only those positions from the latent KV cache. vLLM currently derives both stages' parallel rank, group, and world size from the same Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) configuration. Enabling DCP for the Indexer therefore also enables it for Sparse MLA. The two stages do not benefit equally from this coupling. The Indexer scans a compact cache over the full history, so its work grows with history length and can be divided across ranks. Sparse MLA reads a fixed Top-K from a much larger latent KV cache, so using more ranks adds partial-output/LSE merging and consumes ranks that could otherwise serve independent requests. Our preliminary operator benchmarks on 2x NVIDIA H20 report CP2 latency speedup as `T(DCP=1) / T(DCP=2)`. Each panel fixes batch size and query length; the x-axis is history length. The Indexer obtains substantially higher CP2 speedup than Sparse MLA across most long-context `Q>1` shapes, while both stages regress at `Q=1` because communication and launch overheads

title: [ROCm] Fuse output proj to MoE topk and sort for M3.1 decode
summary: ## Overview In decode, the all-reduces and the small ops around the MoE are many short launches, and their latency adds up in each layer. One launch now goes from the o_proj output to the MoE inputs, and one launch does the all-reduce and norm after the MoE. ## Claims Fusing these small ops results in substantial improvement in ITL ## Validation Pre-MoE launch vs the stock chain, µs per layer: 1 row 22.0→11.9; 8 rows 25.0→13.1; 16 rows 28.5→13.7; 64 rows 39.2→17.5; 128 rows 49.2→24.3; 192 rows 59.5→33.7. Post-MoE AR + norm + MXFP8: 24 rows 11.0→9.0; 192 rows 29.4→27.1. MoE half of a layer: 1 row 58.3→43.7; 8 rows 93.9→71.8; 64 rows 203→177; 192 rows 270→244. At larger request sizes, the MoE kernels require more workgroups active to keep HBM busy. A monokernel style persistent 256 or 512 CTA grid doesn't scale. However, the size of th eother ops' grid does not scale this way. This effectively leverages the monokernel's advantages where possible and the separate ones' elsewhere. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Share one NIXL agent per worker across elastic EP reconfigurations, enable MI355 scaling test
summary: ## Overview `NixlEplbCommunicator` created its own NIXL agent and registered the expert weights with it. A reconfiguration builds the replacement communicator while the old one is still alive, so a worker ended up holding several agents with the same expert pages registered. On MI355 the extra IPC export is refused and the test fails. This hands the replacement communicator the agent it is replacing, so the pages are registered once. Two things follow from sharing an agent and are part of this change: the agent runs in strict thread sync mode, and the replacement communicator disconnects from the ranks that scaling down removed. title: [Bugfix][CPU] Use CPU fallback for Mamba batch_memcpy without Triton
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #46693. On macOS/CPU, hybrid Mamba models such as Qwen3.5 crash in `mamba_utils.batch_memcpy` when Triton is unavailable. `batch_memcpy` always launched `@triton.jit batch_memcpy_kernel` with `[grid]` syntax. Without Triton that name is a dummy Python function, so the launch raises `TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable`. `CPUModelRunner` later monkeypatches `batch_memcpy_kernel` to `cpu_triton_utils.batch_memcpy_kernel`, but that is too late and is skipped when the GPU runner path is used (as in the issue traceback). This PR makes `batch_memcpy` itself fall back to the existing CPU `_batch_memcpy_impl` (`ctypes.memmove`) when `HAS_TRITON` is false or the kernel is not launchable. The GPU/Triton launch path is unchanged when Triton is available. The same issue also reports that `python -m vllm.collect_env` crashes on macOS because `get_pkg_version()` asserts `get_platform() == "linux"`. That helper now returns `None` off Linux so IGC/XPU package queries stay Linux-only without aborting the report. ## Why this is not a duplicate - No open PR references #46693. - #46697 (`[Bugfix] Add CPU fallback for mamba batch memcpy`) attempted a similar fix but is **closed** (merge conflicts). That PR inlined a new `ctypes.memmove` loop; this one reuses the existing `cpu_triton_utils._batch_memcpy_impl` and does not depend on the `CPUModelRunner` monkeypatch. - #48354 only fixes the `collect_env` non-Linux assert. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Ignore KV cache dtype for encoder-only backend selection
summary: ## Purpose Fix embedding / encoder-only serving when a global `--kv-cache-dtype` is set (e.g. `bfloat16`). `EncoderOnlyAttention` does not allocate a KV cache (`get_kv_cache_spec` returns `None`), but it still passed `cache_config.cache_dtype` into `get_attn_backend()`. CUDA backends then filter on that unused dtype and can raise: ``` ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda ``` instead of serving the embedding model (or failing with a clear config error). This PR selects the encoder-only backend with `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`. `cache_config` is still forwarded to `Attention` for anything that actually needs it. Fixes #55046 ## Why this is not a duplicate - Open PRs mentioning #55046: none. - [#55150](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55150) rejects *quantized* KV cache for encoder-only models during `VllmConfig` validation. This change is backend *selection* for encoder-only layers when a global (including non-quantized) `cache_dtype` is set. It does not add or move quantized-KV validation. - [#55159](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55159) / [#55160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55160) are about prefix caching on encoder models, not backend selection. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py::test_encoder_only_attention_ignores_kv_cache_dtype tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py::test_encoder_only_backend_selected_with_global_cache_dtype -v ``` ## Test Result ``` tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py::test_encoder_only_attention_ignores_kv_cache_dt

title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Tune sparse GQA prefill profile on gfx942 and gfx950
summary: ## Overview On CDNA3 (gfx942) and CDNA4 (gfx950), the prefill launch profile of `qsa_sparse_paged_attention` (more than 512 programs) now uses one warp per program, except BF16 K/V with `BLOCK_M >= 16` on gfx942, which uses `BLOCK_N=32`. This makes Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's prefill sparse attention 1.2-2.2x faster, and long-prompt serving 2-3% faster at TP2, with unchanged accuracy. Co-authored with @eppaneamd: the gfx950 one-warp rule comes from his #65341, which was closed and folded into this PR. Not a duplicate: draft #65474 is stacked on this PR and retunes the same branch further, and #57969 changes `BLOCK_M` on gfx11 only. ## Claims - Kernel: 1.6-2.2x at TP1/TP2 and 1.2-1.8x at TP4/TP8 at 8,192 rows, on MI325X and MI355X, for BF16 and FP8 K/V. No measured cell is slower than main. - Outputs are bitwise equal to main, except gfx942 BF16 at TP1/TP2 (`BLOCK_N=32`). title: [Feature] Report per-request prefill progress over gRPC
summary: ## Overview A router that prices a prefill worker needs to know how much prefill work that worker still owes. This PR reports that value per request, over the gRPC stream that already carries the request's output, so a consumer can price a running request exactly instead of estimating it at admission. Closes #63140. Consumed by Router [#469](https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/469). ## Why per request rather than an aggregate We implemented the aggregate first and measured it. Two results decided the shape of this PR. An aggregate cannot price queued work. Counting queued prompts at their prompt length over-counts them, because they may hit the prefix cache; in a clean A/B on 2P+2D the router lost 35.8% on TTFT p99 when it consumed that value. Excluding queued work instead leaves a blind spot that is arithmetic rather than noise: a request admitted before a sample and still queued contributes to neither the sample nor a delta, for as long as it stays queued. Per-request progress closes that gap with one number per request and no new delivery path. Numbers from earlier comments that compared aggregate variants are retracted: they were single runs, the baseline itself drifts between 4.13 and 5.02 s mean TTFT, and one A/B was invalid because the build had lost the consumer. ## Design ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Scheduler participant F as Rust frontend participant R as Router S->>F: EngineCoreOutput(prefill_progress) F->>R: GenerateStream frame (prefill_progress) Note over S: each scheduled chunk, then a final zero ``` The scheduler reports from the sche

title: [Core] Hit prefix cache on the hash unit when an attention block is coarser than Mamba's
summary: ## Purpose This PR lets a hybrid Mamba/GDN model hit the prefix cache at the Mamba block when another attention group's block is coarser. A resent prompt then reuses almost all of its cached prefix, where today it recomputes up to one coarse block. The case comes up when a drafter stores more KV per token than the target. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B has 2 KV heads and the public EAGLE-3 head `jiapingW/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Eagle3-Specforge` has 16, so the shared page makes the target's attention block a multiple of the Mamba block. The hash unit is then the Mamba block, `partial_hash_hits_enabled()` returns False, and a hit has to end on a coarse attention boundary. The prefill split checkpoints Mamba state on the Mamba block, so the hit falls back to the last coarse boundary that has a Mamba state, or to zero when there is none. `partial_hash_hits_enabled()` now also turns on fine-grained hits when the Mamba block equals the hash unit and some prefix-cacheable group's block (after DCP scaling) is coarser. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Pass device pointers of host-registered CPU KV memory to batched copies
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #61052. CPU KV offload faults (Xid 31 / illegal memory access) on platforms where host memory pinned with `cudaHostRegister` is mapped at a device address that differs from its host address: NVIDIA vGPU and WSL2. Both connectors pin pageable host memory with `cudaHostRegister` (`OffloadingConnector`: the mmap region in `pin_mmap_region`; `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`: the CPU KV tensors) and then use `tensor.data_ptr()`, the host address, as the copy pointer. `cudaMemcpyAsync` translates such addresses itself, but `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` and the Triton swap kernel use them as given. This covers the direct and canonical layouts and both the batched-copy and Triton paths. - `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`: `build_params` uses the device address of each CPU tensor. - Nothing changes where the two addresses are equal, for pageable (unregistered) memory, or on ROCm and XPU. title: [Bugfix] Reject prompts that cannot be scheduled without chunked prefill
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Chunked prefill can be turned off after the token budget was validated with it on: HRM-Text's model config hook disables it (non-causal prefill), and `EngineCore` disables it for models without KV cache, such as a decoder served with `hf_overrides={"is_causal": false}`. summary: ## Overview NVFP4 BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-R write the FFN's GELU output in 16 bits and read it back to quantize it for the down projection. The block max now takes |x|, since GELU can be negative; ReLU2's output never is, so its results are unchanged. - BERT's FFN fuses GELU + NVFP4 quant only when the down projection takes NVFP4 input, so FP16 and FP8 are unchanged. - `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 on an RTX PRO 6000 with `--linear-backend cutlass`: 18-21% less GPU time, with scores bitwise identical to main. title: [Feature]: Quantize MoE experts one at a time during loading for every online quantization scheme
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **Problem.** Online MoE quantization materializes a layer's full-precision experts, then quantizes the whole layer in `process_weights_after_loading`. Peak device memory during loading is therefore one full BF16 MoE layer plus its quantized copy. For large MoE models that peak decides whether the model fits: Muse Spark Open's two BF16 MoE layers are 24 GiB each. **Current workarounds, each scoped to one case:** - #67136 stages the BF16 experts on the CPU for `nvfp4_per_token` when `--cpu-offload-gb` offloads them, then quantizes one expert at a time on the GPU. That makes quantization depend on offloading, which reviewers found odd ([thread](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67136#discussion_r4545423553)). - #64315 requantizes per expert unconditionally, for Qwen4Exp's MegaMoE path. - #64378 chunks NVFP4 → MXFP4 requantization. **Proposal.** Make per-expert (or chunked) quantization the default for online MoE methods, for every scheme. Then peak memory during loading is the quantized layer plus one full-precision expert, whatever the offloading setup. Two possible shapes: 1. **Quantize as experts arrive.** The online method quantizes expert `e` once its `w13`/`w2` shards are loaded, and never holds the whole full-precision layer. The closed RFC #53192 (streaming quantization units for weight reload) describes the completion tracking this needs. 2. **Quantize per expert after loading.** Experts are materialized on the CPU, or in a chunked buffer, and each `_quantize_*` helper takes one expert at a time. title: [Feature] Segment attention layout for one-pass multi-candidate scoring
summary: ## Overview Some scoring workloads read one shared prefix against many candidates: a cross-encoder or listwise reranker scoring one query against N documents, or a decision model answering N questions about one state. Today each candidate is a separate request, so the prefix is encoded N times. For encoder-only (non-causal) models prefix caching cannot help, because bidirectional keys depend on the whole prompt. This PR adds an opt-in **segment attention layout** for encoder-only models. The prompt is the prefix followed by the candidates, read in one forward: - the prefix attends to itself; - each candidate attends to the prefix and to itself, never to another candidate; - each candidate's positions restart right after the prefix, so it sees the positions it would see in a `prefix + candidate` prompt; - the output has one row per candidate (the mean of its contextual token states). Request it with a pooling parameter on the `token_embed` task: ```python from vllm import LLM, PoolingParams from vllm.pooling_params import SegmentLayoutParams llm = LLM( model, runner="pooling", pooler_config={"task": "token_embed"}, attention_backend="FLEX_ATTENTION", ) ids = prefix_ids + [t for c in candidate_ids for t in c] out = llm.encode( [{"prompt_token_ids": ids}], pooling_params=PoolingParams( segment_layout_params=SegmentLayoutParams( [len(prefix_ids)] + [len(c) for c in candidate_ids] ), ), pooling_task="token_embed", ) # out[0].outputs.data: [num_candidates, hidden_size] ``` The online `token_embed` request takes the same field (`"segment_layout_params": {"segment_lengths": [...]}`

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Enable Engram disk offload for memory-constrained nodes
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's Engram tables are about 197 GB, so they fit neither in GPU memory nor, with `cpu_offload`, in host memory on a 128 GB node. At TP=4, each rank owns about 50 GB of table rows on top of about 78 GB of weights. On an APU (Strix Halo, DGX Spark), host and GPU memory are the same RAM. This PR extends `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'` (added for Qwen4Exp in #59958) to DeepSeek V4.1. The tables stay in the checkpoint's safetensors files: - After loading, each rank memory-maps only its own row range, located through the safetensors header. - Each step it gathers the distinct rows it needs through the page cache and copies them into fixed GPU buffers. - The existing `_engram_lookup_kernel` (SORTED mode) runs over that compact table, so results are bit-identical to the in-memory table. The gather needs the hash ids on the host, so the lookup is an `@eager_break_during_capture` segment. It runs with `--enforce-eager`, or with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 -cc.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`. Startup rejects other graph modes and the host-memory options. Qwen4Exp stays CUDA-only and unchanged. DeepSeek V4.1 also rejects `embedding_across_dp`, since each rank reads only its own rows. The change is in the shared Engram code and is not tied to a platform. It was tested on gfx1151 and should equally serve CUDA unified-memory machines such as DGX Spark (not tested there). ## Duplicate-work check - #59958 (merged) / #58815 / #58439: file-backed PLE tables for Qwen4Exp. title: [RFC]: A standard for Specialized (MonoKernels) Decodes in vllm/models
summary: ### Motivation. A **Specialized Decode** implementation is one where most/all operations in a model’s forward pass are manually implemented in a way that optimizes for the model’s specific shapes and execution patterns on certain hardware. Typically, these include heavy kernel fusions and overlap for low-latency execution, and custom kernels that tune exact grid sizes for certain batch sizes. These implementations can reach tens of thousands of lines of code, and present a major challenge in managing their complexity. This RFC proposes a standard way to modularize and integrate these runtimes into vLLM under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`. #### Why Specialized Decodes like MonoKernels? At low concurrency, decode is bound by launch overhead and weight reads, and a MonoKernel removes most of both. On 8× MI350X a graph-mode GLM-5.2 decode step issues ~2,459 kernels in vLLM. With the MonoKernel it issues ~210: 75 MonoKernel launches plus ~135 for dense layers 0–2, input prep and the head. | GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (#60889), TP8, MI350X, ~3k-token context | vLLM | MonoKernel | Speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Time per token, batch 1 / 8, defaults (BF16 attention) | 13.70 / 17.33 ms | 5.92 / 11.44 ms | 2.31× / 1.51× | | Time per token, batch 1, FP8 attention opt-in | 13.70 ms | 4.80 ms | 2.85× | | MoE layer w/o indexer (57 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 178.8 / 189.6 µs | 69.1 / 100.6 µs | 2.59× / 1.88× | | MoE layer with indexer (18 of 75), batch 4 / 8, FP8 | 214.9 / 227.6 µs | 88.5 / 123.4 µs | 2.43× / 1.84× | | AgentX time between tokens, 1 / 8 users (3,600 s/point), FP8 | 15.0 / 20.4

title: [ROCM][KVConnector][MoRIIO] Add WRITE-mode consumer timeout
summary: ## Purpose Fixes the consumer half of ROCm/mori#655 and the hang in #59114. **The #59114 hang is only fixed when `write_recv_timeout` is set below the client timeout.** With the 540s default and that report's ~400s client, the client gives up first, and its abort stops the timer. In MoRIIO WRITE mode the consumer parks a request in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until the producer's `write_done` arrives. If the producer dies that never happens: the request waits until the client gives up, nothing is logged, and `/health` stays 200. This adds a per-request receive timer on the consumer scheduler; at the deadline the request is failed instead of wedging. It complements ROCm/mori#670 (merged), which fails the producer-side transfer on a QP error but still tells decode nothing. Config: `kv_connector_extra_config["write_recv_timeout"]` (seconds, default 540, finite and > 0, validated at startup) and `write_recv_max_timeout` (default 3 x `write_recv_timeout`, not below it). Documented in `docs/features/moriio_connector_usage.md`. Not a duplicate: the other open MoRIIO timeout PRs cover the prefill side (#51301, #56465) or the handshake (#63856). ## Scope: this fails the request, it does not free the blocks RDMA writes are one-sided, so a passed deadline does not prove the producer's NIC has stopped; releasing a block could let a late write corrupt another request. Blocks stay held until a real `finished_recving` (lifecycle split in #59382): a timed-out request keeps its transfer mapping, so a late `write_done` (a slow producer) still frees its blocks. title: [Bugfix][V1] Preserve per-group eviction order in deferred block free
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #48489. The deferred block-free path returns a finished request's blocks to the block pool in a different **eviction order** than the immediate-free path, for **multi-group (hybrid) KV cache** configs (e.g. sliding-window + full attention, or Mamba/GDN hybrids such as Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5). The deferred path (`defer_block_free`) is enabled when a KV connector is configured in a **consumer** role and `max_concurrent_batches > 1` — async scheduling or pipeline parallelism (`scheduler.py`, `Scheduler.__init__`). It is not enabled by async scheduling on its own. ### Root cause The immediate path (`KVCacheCoordinator.free`) frees each single-type manager's blocks in its **own** reversed `block_pool.free_blocks()` call, so each group is evicted tail-first *within its own group*: ```python for manager in self.single_type_managers: manager.free(request_id) # free_blocks(reversed(group_i)) — one call per group ``` The deferred path instead flattened every group into one list (`KVCacheCoordinator.pop_blocks_for_free`) and reversed it **once**: ```python self.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.free_blocks(reversed(blocks)) # single flattened call ``` Reversing a concatenation `[groupA..., groupB...]` does not reproduce per-group tail-first ordering — it emits all of group B before group A. For two groups allocated `A=[1,2,3]`, `B=[4,5,6]`: - immediate path → eviction order `[3, 2, 1, 6, 5, 4]` - old deferred path → `[6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]` There is **no correctness/data-safety impact** (ref-count bookkeeping and block validity are unchanged); it is an eviction-quality regression

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix ROCM_AITER_FA extend/prefill split bug
summary: ## Overview split_decodes_prefills_and_extends assumed extends precede new prompts (MRV1's behavior), which MRV2 does not guarantee (it only puts decodes first). An extend that followed a new prompt was classified as a prefill and attended without its KV cache context. This will silently downgrade the output quality. In some of my tests, the PPL could increase 8%+. Only the leading decodes and the trailing run of requests without context are now separated; everything in between goes through the extend path, which handles zero-context rows correctly. The extend context workspace is split only among requests that actually have context, so interleaved new prompts do not inflate the number of context chunks. This fix is compatible with MRV1. ---

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Extend skinny gemm N=5 to N=8 cases on GFX12 (RDNA4) using SWMMAC optimization
summary: ## Purpose This PR adds an optimized ROCm GFX12 (RDNA4) SWMMAC-based skinny GEMM path. The new path targets serving workloads with low max concurrency, matching the benchmarked decode GEMM range of N=5-8. The implementation uses sparse wave matrix multiply-accumulate instructions on GFX12 (RDNA4) to improve throughput for these skinny GEMM cases, while keeping the existing fallback path for unsupported cases. Skinny GEMMs can be important for ROCm/GFX12 (RDNA4) serving performance, which is often used in local or small-scale serving setups. In these deployments, the server is expected to handle single users, or a small number of users with a relatively lower request rate, so the active decode batch can remain small instead of being filled to a large batch size. This optimization follows the same general direction described in the Hugging Face technical blog, [*Creating custom kernels for the AMD MI300*](https://huggingface.co/blog/mi300kernels). The blog discusses custom kernels for AMD MI300X vLLM serving and describes a skinny GEMM optimization for inputs with 8 or fewer rows. The key idea is to map each logical skinny A row into two adjacent SWMMAC sparse rows. The first sparse row selects one set of 16-bit pairs from `A[n, :]`, and the second sparse row selects the complementary pairs from the same logical row. Both sparse rows multiply with the same normal `B[32 x 16]` fragment, producing two partial accumulator rows. The epilogue then adds the adjacent partial rows back together to recover the final logical output row. This interleaved sparse-row layout lets the kerne

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Guard cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous
summary: ## Purpose Cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous is safe only when every rank belongs to the same NVLink fabric. Without a topology check, unsupported groups can hang or fail during CUDA memory import. This affects generic symmetric-memory all-reduce as well as Direct DCP, custom all-reduce, Async TP, GEMM RS/AR, and the Kimi K3 latent-MoE tail fusion. This change: - classifies groups as `INTRA_NODE`, `CROSS_NODE_NVLINK`, or `UNSUPPORTED`; - reads the fabric UUID and clique ID through vLLM's vendored NVML V2 API (`c_nvmlGpuFabricInfoV_t` and `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfoV`), without spawning `nvidia-smi`; - fails closed when fabric metadata is absent, invalid, or differs across ranks; - applies the topology guard before entering symmetric-memory rendezvous; and - prevents forced Direct DCP settings from bypassing topology safety. The legacy `nvmlDeviceGetGpuFabricInfo` structure is not compatible with the GB300 driver used for validation: it exposed zero clique/state fields. The versioned V2 call returns correct UUID and clique. title: [Perf][MoE] OCP MX emulation: dequantize only the routed experts
summary: ## Overview On GPUs without native OCP MX support (e.g. MI250X), MXFP4/MXFP6 MoE layers run through `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`, which dequantizes every local expert to bf16/fp16 on every forward. A decode batch usually routes to a small fraction of the experts, so this PR dequantizes only the routed ones when they are at most a quarter of the local experts. Related, touching the same class but not this path: #43983 (oracle test coverage), #52868 (`a2_scale` forwarding). Credit: @ekuznetsov139 had the same idea earlier in #40055 (single-token decode; on MI325 it took Qwen3-235B from about 4 to 21 tok/s). Its capturable single-token path is folded in here (5a4baceea, co-authored by him). ## Claims - When a batch routes to at most a quarter of the local experts, `apply` gathers the routed experts' packed weights and scales, dequantizes only those, and renumbers `topk_ids` onto the gathered set. For multi-token batches this uses `torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True)`. For a single token (from #40055) it uses a sort of the token's ids and an argsort, so shapes are static and the path also runs under CUDA-graph capture. - The output is unchanged when both paths select the same Triton tile config: each token is multiplied by the same dequantized expert weights. Tuned config files are keyed by expert count, and the routed path looks up the gathered count, so on a GPU with a tuned file for the full shape the full path may use a tuned tile while the routed path uses the default one, and the outputs can then differ by rounding. vLLM has no tuned configs for MI250X, s

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Select batch-invariant MXFP8/MXFP4 linear kernels under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
summary: ## Overview Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the MXFP8 and MXFP4 linear kernel selectors could pick Marlin (or FlashInfer on Blackwell), whose output for a row changes with the batch size. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Decode each streaming-input chunk after its own prompt
summary: ## Overview With streaming input, the frontend detokenizer only ever sees the first chunk's prompt. Each later chunk's output gets decoded straight after the previous chunk's output, so when a chunk stops partway through a character (max_tokens landing on a byte token), the next chunk's text starts with U+FFFD. This PR feeds each new chunk's prompt to the detokenizer as context, the same way the scheduler builds the model's context. ## Claims - After a chunk that ends partway through a multi-byte character, the next chunk's text no longer starts with U+FFFD. That holds for DELTA and CUMULATIVE output, and for both the fast and the slow detokenizer. - Voxtral realtime is unchanged. It re-sends each chunk's last token as the next prompt, and a character split across two chunks still comes out once, whole. - Chunk boundaries that don't cut a character give the same text as before. ## Validation The new test, on main and on this branch: ``` pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k chunk_text_follows_its_prompt ``` main: ``` E AssertionError: assert '� ok' == ' ok' FAILED tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_streaming_input_chunk_text_follows_its_prompt[False] 1 failed, 1 passed, 60 deselected ``` This PR: ``` PASSED tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_streaming_input_chunk_text_follows_its_prompt[False] PASSED tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_streaming_input_chunk_text_follows_its_prompt[True] 2 passed, 60 deselected ``` `[True]` is the Voxtral realtime pattern. title: [Quantization][RL] Buffered online quantization; direct reload of online-quantized layers
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Online quantization loads each layer into a short-lived BF16 buffer and runs the layer's existing `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) when its last shard arrives. Cold start and weight updates share that path. Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`) now supports online-quantized models, and online quantization no longer uses the layerwise reload machinery. Part of the direct weight reload RFC (#54477). This supersedes #65802 (same author), which staged online layers through the layerwise machinery, so it doesn't duplicate an open PR. All three parts are in one PR so the whole change can be reviewed in one place. It can be split for merging: (A) buffered loading for cold start, (B) direct reload of online layers, (C) removing online quantization's use of layerwise code. ## Claims - **Cold start is unchanged.** For every online scheme tested, every parameter and buffer is bit-identical to main. - **Direct reload of online-quantized models works.** After a reload of checkpoint B, every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh cold start on B. Reloading back to A restores every tensor exactly, and no tensor changes address, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid. - **Layerwise reload of online models** goes through the same buffers, with the same results. - **Online layers process when their last shard arrives**, detected from shard keys, so element counting, buffered argument replay and meta materialization are gone for online quantization. - **Unsupported cases are refused** with a clear error: see *Refused* below. ## Validation **E

title: [Refactor] Encoder cache extension hooks for MRV2
summary: ## Purpose This PR ports the encoder cache extension hooks introduced for the V1 GPU model runner in #48218 to ModelRunner V2, so platform plugins can customize encoder cache behavior under `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` without changing the default vLLM path. In ModelRunner V2, all encoder-cache reads and writes are inline dictionary operations on `EncoderCache.encoder_outputs` spread across `model_states/interface.py`, `mm/encoder_runner.py` and `model_runner.py`. There is no overridable seam, so vllm-ascend (e.g., its Ascend score-based encoder cache) cannot integrate with V2 at all. Copying large parts of the V2 runner into a plugin would be difficult to maintain and would quickly diverge from upstream — exactly the problem #48218 solved for V1. Concretely, this PR: - Reroutes the post-encode store in `ModelState.execute_mm_encoder` through the runner-level `cache_encoder_outputs` hook. - Adds four overridable cache hooks on `EncoderRunner` (`cache_encoder_outputs` / `_cache_encoder_output` /`_has_cached_encoder_output` / `_get_encoder_output_from_cache`) whose default bodies are the original inline dictionary operations. - Reroutes the cached-output checks in `prepare_mm_inputs` and `gather_mm_embeddings` through the new hooks. - Extracts the `free_encoder_mm_hashes` release loop in `ModelRunner.free_states` into an overridable `_process_encoder_cache_scheduler_output` hook. - Adds a no-op `_on_request_state_removed` hook for request-scoped cleanup. title: [Feature][Kernel] Triton autotune lora
summary: ## Purpose Depends on #59492. Builds on the generic Triton autotune warmup (`--kernel-config.enable_triton_autotune`) and adds a LoRA table for the `lora_shrink` and `lora_expand` Triton kernels. LoRA ships no tuned configs, so without a user file in `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` every shape uses the heuristic default. With this PR, each GPU and model can tune its own launch configs at startup. cc @vanshbhatia-amd Changes: - **Shapes from the LoRA weights.** Shrink and expand shapes are read from the allocated `lora_a_stacked` / `lora_b_stacked` of every `BaseLinearLayerWithLoRA` and of `lm_head` (`LogitsProcessorWithLoRA`). No adapter has to be loaded. Linear layers are tuned up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, and `lm_head` up to `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)`. - **M buckets.** 1, 16, 32, …, 4096, up to the first bucket at or above each shape's token limit. - **Bounded search.** At most 12 configs are timed per M bucket. The search starts from the default config plus up to 2 winners from the nearest M buckets already tuned on the same rank (same op and slice count). All starting points are snapped to the search grid. It then expands one-step neighbors of the fastest config that hasn't been expanded yet. - **Search space.** - Shrink: `block_m` 16–128, `block_n` 16 plus a rank-sized tile, `block_k` 64/128, `split_k` 2–32. - Expand: `block_m` 16–64, `block_n` 32–256, `num_warps` 2/4/8. - `block_m` is capped by M, and shrink configs whose `block_k × split_k` exceeds K are rejected. - **Timing.** CUDA graph replays of 10 launches. title: [Quantization] Online weight-only NVFP4 for dense linear layers
summary: ## Purpose Add `nvfp4_weight_only`, online NVFP4 weight-only quantization for dense linear layers: FP16/BF16 weights are quantized at load time and run on the existing W4A16 kernel selector, with no NVFP4 checkpoint needed. MoE layers are unchanged. It is selected like the other online methods: the whole model (`--quantization nvfp4_weight_only`), chosen layers (`quantization_config.targets`), or only the drafter (`"quantization": "nvfp4_weight_only"` in `--speculative-config`). The main use is a BF16 spec-decode drafter on bandwidth-bound GPUs: **+13.1% decode on DGX Spark and +14.1% on RTX PRO 6000 at c=1** for Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + DFlash2, with acceptance length unchanged. title: [Bugfix] PCP: replicate prefills too short for every rank, also without DCP
summary: # [Bugfix] PCP: replicate prefills too short for every rank, also without DCP ## Purpose With PCP-only execution (`PCP > 1`, `DCP == 1`), a prefill step that is too short to give every PCP rank its DualChunkSwap chunks is still split. With PCP=8, a 1-2 token prefill step leaves 6-7 of the 8 ranks with no row of that prefill. That happens in practice when a KV connector (for example LMCache) loads every prompt token except the last one, so the step schedules a single-token prefill. On v0.31.0 this hangs the engine. The workers log `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds`, then EngineCore dies after the 300 s execute timeout (`TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`). ## Root cause `PCPManager.replicated_requests` replicates prefills that cannot fill all `2 * PCP` chunks (`(2*PCP - 1) * ceil(q / 2*PCP) >= q`), but only when `dcp_world_size > 1`. #56157 added the rule so that every rank holds the same number of rows per region, which the PCP+DCP gathered KV layout depends on. PCP-only execution needs the same invariant: - `_iter_rank_chunks` gives rank `r` chunks `r` and `2*PCP-1-r`, each of size `ceil(q / 2*PCP)`. For `q <= PCP - 1`, some ranks get no tokens of the prefill. - On v0.31.0, `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs` returns early on a rank whose rows are all decodes (`num_decode_tokens == local_num_tokens`). That rank skips the PCP all-gather of the prefill KV, while the ranks that do hold prefill rows enter it. The collective never completes. title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Fail pulls from a lost prefill worker
summary: ## Overview When a prefill worker dies, the Mooncake decoder does not notice. Its pull waits up to `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT + 60` = 540 s for P's reply while holding the request's KV blocks, because ZMQ reconnects silently instead of reporting the lost peer. D also keeps the dead worker's address cached, so the requests queued behind send their pulls there and wait another 540 s. Under load, D's KV stays full of requests that can never finish. This PR fails a pull as soon as its connection is lost, and makes D look P up again. It is the decoder-side counterpart of #64193. ## Claims - **P process dies:** the requests waiting on it fail within 2–4 s, instead of after 545 s plus a second 540 s wave. - **P frozen or unreachable:** they fail once heartbeats or the existing timeouts expire, all within 102 s. - No change for a live P and no new option. Failures follow `kv_load_failure_policy`. ## Validation **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake*.py` → 750 passed, 5 skipped. 4 more cases hit Hugging Face Hub fetch errors and pass on rerun. - The new test runs a ZMQ ROUTER in a subprocess that takes the pull and never answers. The ROUTER is then killed, frozen with `SIGSTOP`, or never listening. All three cases time out on main and pass in about 1 s with this PR. - This PR also fixes `test_mooncake_stats.py::test_expired_request_bumps_counter`, which has been broken since #64193. `pre-commit` passes. **End to end:** - Setup: 2× A800, DeepSeek-MoE-16B, TP=1 per side, `kv_lease_duration=30`. - Load: 128 requests at 2.4× D's KV capacity. - Failure

title: [Feature]: Close the remaining DeepGEMM (and other kernel-library) runtime-JIT gaps in kernel warmup
summary: ### Closing Remaining Gap of Deepgemm kernel The main issue and motivation for this is we found **Silent JIT compile** during production workloads, and for VLLM users, there are no easy way to tell if kernel cache is missed or not. The common failure we saw in the real time is related to the "shared memory broadcast" where the system is doing the JIT compilation, taking really long time. it's about **external kernel libraries that JIT-compile in their own runtime, DeepGEMM first.** Their kernels are only partly covered by warmup and not visible to `jit_monitor`. Any model that reaches one of those uncovered entry points can still compile on live requests, even if it passes `--jit-monitor-mode error`. **Goals:** 1. Every DeepGEMM entry point vLLM calls is either warmed, or its JIT compiles are visible to `jit_monitor`. 2. The same treatment for other libraries that JIT outside the hooks `jit_monitor` already has. **Related Impacts.** DeepGEMM compiles a new kernel with nvcc whenever it meets an M (tokens per step) that maps to a tile config it hasn't built yet, and it logs nothing while doing so. Two things make this worse: - **Under DP + EP every rank waits for the rank that is compiling.** - **A step with enough compile time exceeds `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s).** The engine logs `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`, then `EngineDeadError`, and the server exits. `/health` still returns 200, so traffic keeps routing to the stuck pod. This issues is hardware dependent. In different network setting/ hardware setting, the impact will be different. **Production

title: [KV Offload] Set the CPU tier up in the background under async_init
summary: ## Purpose Milestone 1 of #66570. Builds on #66391; only the last two commits are new. With `"async_init": true`, workers map the CPU region and return right away. A background thread then pre-faults and pins it, while the engine serves without offloading. Offloading turns on once every worker reports ready. - The setup thread switches itself to relaxed capture mode, so pinning can't invalidate a CUDA graph capture. That race is what reverted #45850. If the mode can't be set, setup fails and offloading stays off. - It pins one small call at a time (a worker slot, or whole rows up to 8 MiB) and sleeps `async_init_pin_pace` (default 2.0) times each call's duration after it. Back-to-back registrations hold a driver lock and stall serving. - Readiness goes through the connector's existing worker metadata, so nothing outside the offloading connector changes. Once #62337 lands, this gate moves to the core. - If setup fails, offloading stays off and the engine keeps serving. - CUDA only; other platforms set up synchronously. Off by default. This covers `CPUOffloadingSpec`. `TieringOffloadingSpec` ignores the option with a warning until the follow-up. #54578 proposes the same key with a different design; the two need to be reconciled. ## Results Startup to `/health` OK, with the Tiering follow-up on top: | Setup | Sync | async_init | |---|---|---| | GLM-5.3, 16 H100 (4 pods), 280 GiB/rank | 439 s | 334 s | | Qwen3-8B (dummy weights), TP=4, 1,250 GiB | 241.5 s | 57-61 s | On GLM, pre-fault (117 s) and pinning (12 s) leave the critical path. title: [RFC / Performance] How LLM Agent Context Compaction Collapses Automatic Prefix Caching (APC)
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Many long-horizon LLM Agent frameworks perform context compaction (summarization) to prevent context window overflow. In our production runs (~81k context), we observed that compaction caused a severe prefill stall (TTFT stalled at 206.9s), collapsing vLLM's Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) hit rate down to 10.1%. Root Cause: Agent frameworks often strip older archive checkpoints from the prompt to "keep the window lean". This drops an early message and shifts all subsequent tokens, causing APC prefix matching to fail right after the system prompt (token 8,886). 73k tokens had to undergo full re-prefill. The Proposal & Benchmark: By ensuring the compaction request's message prefix is token-identical to normal conversation turns, APC hit rate immediately recovered to 99.6%: - Cache Hit Rate: 10.1% -> 99.6% - Cached Tokens: 8,192 -> 144,165 - Re-prefilled Tokens: 72,986 -> 627 (116x reduction) - TTFT: 206.9s -> 3.1s (66x faster) We propose adding guidelines/warnings in vLLM docs regarding APC-friendly prompt construction for Agent builders. ### Alternatives Explicit cache control breakpoints can help, but keeping the prefix token-identical in the request builder is the cleanest, zero-overhead solution. ### Additional context Full methodology, de-identified logs, and 2-second model-free reproduction script: https://github.com/yansu202511/cache-alignment-findings ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](h

This makes the `amd_ci_fast_exit` plugin also dump the stacks and kernel wait channels of every child process when a test outlives `faulthandler_timeout`. ## Claims - When an AMD CI test runs past `faulthandler_timeout` (1500 s), the log now shows each descendant process (including `VLLM::EngineCore` grandchildren): pid/ppid/state/cmdline, per-thread kernel wait channels, and a `py-spy dump --native` stack (gdb fallback). - Best-effort and bounded (16 processes, 60 s per tool call, 10 min total, 64 KiB per process). It never changes a test result. - Only affects AMD CI: the plugin is loaded only via `-p amd_ci_fast_exit` in `run-amd-test.sh`. title: [ROCm][Model] Run Qwen3.5 on the eager breakable-graph model on MI355X
summary: ## Overview Adds a ROCm variant of the eager Qwen3.5 model (`vllm/models/qwen3_5/amd/`), uses it with breakable CUDA graphs by default on ROCm, and adds an MI355 mirror for the B200 `Qwen3.5` step. ## Claims - `qwen3_5/amd/model.py`, `amd/mtp.py`: copy of the NVIDIA model with the ROCm counterparts of its fusions: Triton Gemma RMSNorm, the row-parallel all-reduce deferred into AITER's fused all-reduce + Gemma RMSNorm (when AITER custom all-reduce is on), the strided-z GDN gated norm, and the fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernel. Keeps AITER fused shared-expert weight rerouting like the legacy ROCm model. - `qwen3_5/__init__.py`, `config/vllm.py`: ROCm picks the AMD model and adds the Qwen3.5 archs to the ROCm breakable-graph default, on every arch. summary: ## Purpose Gemma 4 dense variants get the V2 model runner through the `not is_moe` branch of `_is_default_v2_model_runner_model`, but the MoE variant (26B A4B) falls back to V1. title: [Model][DSv4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1 on A100 (SM80) and H100 (SM90)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash does not run on A100 today: its attention, indexer and cache codecs need FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and FP8/FP4 conversion instructions that SM80 lacks; on H100, `main` runs it on its stock kernels. This PR serves the model on one 8×A100 or 8×H100 node with decode kernels written in CuTe DSL, all under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`; other GPUs keep their current path. Accuracy is on par with `main` on GB300, and in AgentX H100 reaches 1.5–1.7× the P90 interactivity of InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. ![DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash AgentX on 8×H100 and 8×A100, this PR against InferenceX's H100 vLLM line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/19f66703fce5da5fc12b706a6525d3adb2040fcc/sm80_sm90_agentx.png) ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves on 8×A100 (SM80) at TP8, with DSpark speculative decoding. - On 8×H100 (SM90), the decode path reaches 489 P90 tok/s per user at one request in AgentX, against 324 for InferenceX's H100 vLLM line. - Accuracy on both matches `main` on GB300 (GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME25, RULER NIAH up to 256K). ## Validation ### Accuracy Stock vLLM does not run DeepSeek-V4.1 on A100, so the reference is `main` on one GB300 tray as measured for #63921 (same checkpoint, tasks and sampling). title: [RFC]: Bidirectional attention spans, set per request
summary: ### Motivation. Several decoder models are now trained with a PrefixLM-style mask such that some token ranges of the prompt attend to each other in both directions, and the rest of the prompt is causal. vLLM applies such ranges today to images and videos (`mm_req_doc_ranges` in `CommonAttentionMetadata`; FlashAttention 4 support with #42175, FlexAttention with #27938; since #65996, per request in `DefaultModelState.mm_prefix_ranges`). Models that need ranges over text, or over a whole state that holds images, build them out of tree or model by model, including the following: - #66722, which carries #62584, serves Decision 3.0 `prefix_bidir` (vllm-sr/d3-turbo, a Qwen3.5 hybrid). A prompt is a state block, media included, and a question block, each bidirectional within itself on the full-attention layers. `D3Strategy` sends the state block's size in `PoolingParams.extra_kwargs`, and a model state writes the two blocks into `mm_prefix_ranges`. Chunked prefill and prefix caching stay off. - #63114 serves Base Labs mammoth-1 and elephant-1 (Qwen3.5) with a block-bidirectional mask, two ranges per request, with its own `PrefixLMScheduler` (cache hits capped at the prefix end, the rest of the prompt prefilled in one step, client salts moved into a prefix namespace). - RFC #64267 builds a state cache for Decision 3.0 on top of both. - #63033 makes PaliGemma's whole prompt one bidirectional block, with chunked prefill and prefix caching off. - #65268 (draft) reads a shared prefix and several candidates in one forward, for encoder-only models. - Strands Decider's Gemma 4 decision mod

title: [Performance]: FA4 on SM90 under-splits the keys of varlen calls whose rows differ in length
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance FlashAttention 4's automatic split-KV count on SM90 (vllm-project/flash-attention, `flash_attn/cute/config.py` at vLLM's pin `8dd9eaea`) sizes a varlen call as if every row of the batch were as long as the longest one: ```python num_m_blocks = ceil_div(packed_seqlen_q, q_stage * tile_m) # from max_seqlen_q total_mblocks = batch_size * num_heads_kv * heads_per_m_block * num_m_blocks num_splits = num_splits_heuristic(total_mblocks, num_sms, num_n_blocks, 128) # = max(1, min(num_sms // total_mblocks, 128, num_n_blocks)), or 1 for 4 key blocks or fewer ``` A call whose rows differ widely in length therefore gets far fewer splits than its work needs. A vLLM PR (#67983, part of RFC #67334) makes such calls when it runs a PrefixLM step as varlen rows: a new question about a cached state becomes two rows of one request, the uncached tail of the state's last bidirectional range (a few tokens) and the question (a few hundred), over thousands of cached keys. With head size 512, 8 query heads and 1 KV head (packed GQA, 64-row tiles), rows of 20 and 300 tokens count as 2 × ceil(300 × 8 / 64) = 76 m-blocks, so a 132-SM H100 gets 132 // 76 = 1 split. The call holds 3 + 38 = 41 m-blocks of work. The same 320 query tokens as one row count as 40 m-blocks and get 3 splits. On Gemma 4 12B's full-attention layers (16 query heads over 1 KV head), the engine's next question has rows of 192 and 64 tokens: they count as 2 × ceil(192 × 16 / 64) = 96 m-blocks and get one split, while one 256-token row counts as 64 and gets 2. `FwdHeuristicInputs` already carries `t

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode on Hopper (H200 TP4)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds a Hopper (SM90) backend to DeepSeek-V4.1's specialized decode executor (#61868), for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on H100/H200 with DSpark. It is opt-in, as on GB300: `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'`. FULL-graph pure-decode steps of up to 192 rows run in the executor, under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/hopper/`. Prefill, larger steps and anything else it does not serve run the stock path on the same weights. The executor runs the target model only; the DSpark draft keeps main's stock path. The PR is based on `main` and depends on no open PR. It runs no DeepGEMM mHC kernel: the executor computes the mHC coefficients itself, with a CuTe DSL TF32 mixes kernel and the stock epilogue, on its own side stream. So the SM90 DeepGEMM prenorm GEMM and its register-lifetime race (#59129) are not on its path. Main's stock SM90 decode does call that GEMM, at every boundary above 32 tokens and a few times per step at c1 (nsys kernel counts in the details below). This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which was stacked on #61869 and #64892 and included a Hopper drafter. Those parts move to follow-ups (listed below). ## Claims Median ITL on H200 TP4, DSpark k=5, real prompts, temperature 0.7, fixed output length, against `main` without the executor (two runs per build, ABBA; the A / B values are in the table below): - **1.58× at c1**, 1.52× at c2, 1.38× at c4, **1.29× at c8**, 1.18× at c16, 1.03× at c32. - **1.54× at 64K c1** and 1.23× at 64K c8. - Quality is unchanged within noise: 12

title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
summary: ### Motivation. Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side. Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models. ### Proposed Change. **Model Integration:** - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35963 @b-mu - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41736 @johncalesp - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40830 @johncalesp - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38061 @shen-shanshan - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42151 @shen-shanshan - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44720 @harsha20032020 - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42224 @JisoLya - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Fall back to torch.distributed when pynccl is disabled
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview I hit a silent precision failure in model-level sequence parallelism: when pynccl is disabled (for example, when the installed NCCL is older than 2.29.7 and lacks `ncclCommSuspend`), `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` still allocates its output with `torch.empty` and calls a disabled `PyNcclCommunicator.reduce_scatter`, which returns without writing anything. The caller gets uninitialized memory. This PR falls back to the base-class `torch.distributed` reduce-scatter when pynccl is unavailable, and logs a one-time warning at communicator construction so the silent performance downgrade and the upgrade path are visible. ## Claims - `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` now returns a correct result when pynccl is `None` or `disabled`: it falls back to `DeviceCommunicatorBase.reduce_scatter` (`torch.distributed.reduce_scatter_tensor`), matching the reference bit-for-bit in the reproducer below. - The pynccl fast path is unchanged when pynccl is healthy; this only affects the unavailable/disabled case. - `PyNcclCommunicator.__init__` logs a one-time warning when it disables itself, including the original exception and the "upgrade to NCCL >= 2.29.7 if this is due to an old NCCL" hint. The warning is at startup, not on the `reduce_scatter` hot path. - Added `test_reduce_scatter_falls_back_when_pynccl_disabled`, which mocks the base-class method and asserts the fallback is used with the right arguments. - This does not loosen the NCCL version requirement: CUDA still needs NCCL >= 2.29.7 for pynccl, and `ncclCommSuspend` remains required. title: [Perf][Kernel] Use FlashInfer cute-dsl NVFP4 linear for decode on SM120
summary: ## Purpose On SM120, use FlashInfer's cute-dsl NVFP4 GEMM for decode-sized inputs. `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel` heads `_POSSIBLE_NVFP4_KERNELS` but is gated to sm_10x, even though FlashInfer's cute-dsl FP4 backend gained an SM12x runner in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5100 (included in the pinned 0.7.4). On SM120 that runner is faster than FlashInfer CUTLASS (today's default) up to 64 tokens and slower above, so this: - allows the kernel on SM120 when FlashInfer has the SM12x runner (`has_flashinfer_sm12x_cutedsl_fp4_gemm()`); - on SM120 dispatches per call inside a custom op (`sm120_cutedsl_nvfp4_mm`): cute-dsl when M <= 64 and the output is BF16 (the SM12x runner only writes BF16), FlashInfer CUTLASS otherwise. Both take the same swizzled + padded operands, so the weight layout is unchanged; - compiles the cute-dsl kernels for M = 1..64 once per weight shape at load time. cute-dsl compiles one kernel per token-count bucket on first use (0.3-0.5 s each); without this, eagerly run layers such as `lm_head` on the sampled tokens compiled while serving and raised median TTFT by 14% at concurrency 32. SM100/103 behavior is unchanged. SM121 (GB10) is not measured and keeps its current selection. Not a duplicate: no open PR enables cute-dsl NVFP4 linear on SM12x (searched "cutedsl sm120", "FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel", "sm12x_cute"). Related: #67202 reorders b12x ahead of FlashInfer CUTLASS on SM120. cute-dsl was also faster than b12x for M <= 64 in the measurements below, and this PR leaves the order of the remaining kernels as is. ## Test Plan Hardware: RTX PRO 6000
