title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Resolve the kernel block split per KV cache group
summary: ## Overview The Mooncake connector resolves a single physical-kernel-block split for the whole model and applies it to every KV cache group. When two groups need different splits — two attention groups with different logical block sizes, or attention alongside Mamba state — the block id mapping is wrong for at least one of them, so transferred KV pages land at the wrong offsets. This PR resolves the split per transfer group, using the same decision the caches were registered with. ## Claims - The logical-to-kernel block split becomes `list[int]`, one entry per `transfer_groups` element, instead of a single `int` shared by all groups. - Each group's kernel block size is resolved with the same rules `vllm.v1.worker.utils.prepare_kernel_block_sizes()` applied at registration: keep the group whole when it holds no layer views, when block-outermost packing interleaves other layers' pages, when the spec is not an attention spec, or when the pipeline stage owns none of the group's layers; otherwise call `select_common_block_size()` with only that group's backends, specs, and layer names. - The three consumers of the split — block id expansion, the registered pool capacity, and the per-layer transfer length — read their own group's entry, which now matches the block id index space the connector works in. - `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/utils.py` is untouched, so `NixlConnector` keeps its scalar path and the shared helpers keep their signatures. ## Validation Static checks on the four touched files: `ruff check` passes, `ruff format --check` reports no changes, `py_comp

title: [RFC]: UltraQuant: the scale constant c = 0.156 is MSE-optimal before the UE8M0 snap, not after; c ≈ 0.2 cuts KV-quantization KL by 40–56% at no cost
summary: ### Motivation. `ultraquant_4bit` picks each group's UE8M0 scale as ``` s_raw = c * absmax(group) # c = 0.156 (DEFAULT_CONSTANT_C, vllm/v1/attention/ops/ultraquant/format.py) s = 2^round(log2(s_raw)) # UE8M0 snap ``` The constant is documented as "MSE-optimal; `s_raw = c * absmax`, then UE8M0-snapped". That holds before the snap. c = 0.156 minimizes the E2M1 reconstruction error for a **continuous** scale s = c·absmax. But the stored scale is the snapped power of two. Snapping moves absmax/s anywhere within a factor √2, and erring toward clipping costs more than erring toward coarseness. So for the snapped scale the MSE optimum moves up, to **c ≈ 0.19–0.20**. At c = 0.156, about a third more reconstruction error is left on the table, on synthetic data and on real K/V alike. For reference, the OCP MX rule 2^(floor(log2 absmax) − 2) is the same family with c = 1/(4√2) ≈ 0.177. **Reconstruction error (relative MSE, groups of 32, E2M1 grid).** Real K/V are from Llama-3.1-8B: all 32 layers, post-RoPE, one 4096-token wikitext-2 window. | c | Gaussian, continuous s | Gaussian, snapped s | Llama K (Hadamard-rotated), snapped s | Llama V, snapped s | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.156 (current) | **0.0104** (≈ min) | 0.0178 | 0.0162 | 0.0183 | | 0.166 | 0.0102 | 0.0149 | 0.0140 | 0.0160 | | 0.177 (≈ OCP MX) | 0.0114 | 0.0132 | 0.0129 | 0.0143 | | 0.19 | 0.0143 | 0.0125 | **0.0123** | **0.0136** | | 0.20 | 0.0175 | **0.0125** | **0.0123** | **0.0136** | On the same real K/V, the continuous-scale optimum is c = 0.166 in all four cases (K, rotated K, V, rotated V), where 0.156 is within 2–5

title: [Metrics] Size vector metric values per label set in reader
summary: ## Purpose In `vllm/v1/metrics/reader.py`, `_digest_num_accepted_by_pos_samples(samples)` converts position-indexed Prometheus samples (`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos{position="...", ...}`) into `Vector(name=..., labels=..., values=[...])` metrics grouped by their non-position label set. Previously, `_digest_num_accepted_by_pos_samples` tracked a single global `max_pos` across all samples in the metric family and allocated `values = [0] * (max_pos + 1)` for every label set. When multiple engines or models in the same Prometheus registry have different speculative decoding position counts (e.g., engine `0` with 2 positions `0..1` and engine `1` with 4 positions `0..3`), any label set with fewer positions had its `Vector.values` padded with trailing `0` entries up to the global `max_pos + 1` (`[8, 4, 0, 0]` instead of `[8, 4]`). title: [Feature]: Add GetLoad RPC to the Rust frontend gRPC Control service
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch vLLM's gRPC interface (`Control` service) covers discovery and lifecycle but has no way to query a server's current load — anyone building a router, sidecar, autoscaler, or placement scheduler in front of vLLM workers today has to scrape HTTP `/metrics` and hand-parse Prometheus text to learn how busy a worker is. I'd like `Control` to expose a small, typed load snapshot: aggregate running/waiting requests and used/total KV blocks, plus an optional per-DP-rank breakdown. The data already flows to the frontend — the engine reports scheduler stats every step, and `GetServerInfo` already serves the static capacity — so this is a typed read-out of existing state with no engine-side change. ### Alternatives Keep polling `/metrics`: works but fragile — text parsing, no schema, and Prometheus is a metrics/telemetry surface, not a control API. ### Additional context - Field names and semantics follow the precedent set by TensorRT-LLM and SGLang's `GetLoad`, so existing gRPC-native control planes can treat vLLM like the other engines. - One concrete consumer today: NVIDIA Dynamo's sidecar architecture needs `kv_used_blocks` per worker for busy detection, and currently polls the vLLM sidecar's `/metrics` as a workaround ([ai-dynamo/dynamo#16468](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/16468)). - Verified on vLLM v0.30.0: the gRPC `Control` service has no dynamic-load RPC, while `/metrics` exposes `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` and `vllm:num_requests_running/waiting` with an `engine` label. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you

title: [Mooncake] Route KV transfers through a backend interface
summary: ## Purpose `MooncakeConnectorWorker` creates `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`, asks it for its RPC port, registers KV memory with it, and runs both transfer directions against it, so the connector is bound to one engine implementation. This PR puts that role behind an interface and wraps the Transfer Engine in an adapter, and the connector stops touching `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`. Behaviour is unchanged: same status text, same per-request failure fan-out, no new configuration key, no wire change. What the interface covers: - `register_regions` / `unregister_regions`: pin and release KV memory. - `submit(peer, op, ranges)`: start one request; every range carries an id. - `poll()`: terminal outcome per range. `TransferEngineBackend` implements it with the same blocking batch call the connector made before, and reports the batch status for every range of the request. The Transfer Engine settles a request inside the call, so the events of a submission come back to the submitting thread; the adapter keeps them per thread so concurrent sender workers never read each other's results. ## Why per-range events The engine answers with one status per batch today. Keeping that status as per-range events keeps a failure attached to the blocks it happened on, and gives an engine that reports finer outcomes a place to put them without another change in the connector. ## Duplicate work No open PR puts an interface in front of the engine usage in the Mooncake connector. #61974 adds the pull-mode connector and edits `mooncake_connector.py`; it keeps calling `mooncake.engine.TransferEng

summary: # [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas ## Summary Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in `cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes. The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool. title: [ROCm][DSV4.1] Honor the multi-stream GEMM token threshold in the CSA attention path
summary: ## Purpose `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention.forward` forks the CSA input chains (Q/KV projections, compressor, indexer inputs) onto the aux streams for **every** batch. The shared path it parallels, `DeepseekV4Attention._run_parallel_input_projections`, only overlaps its input GEMMs while ```python hidden_states.shape[0] <= envs.VLLM_MULTI_STREAM_GEMM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD ``` This PR applies the same condition to the ROCm CSA fork while a graph is being captured. Above the threshold, the layer takes its existing sequential fallback. The eager profile run still forks at any size. That run is the first time the aux streams execute hipBLASLt GEMMs (`torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` in the compressor chain), so it creates their hipBLASLt handles and accounts their memory. If the profile run skipped the fork, the first fork would happen inside a graph capture. `hipblasLtCreate` deadlocks there, and server startup hangs. **Behavior change with default settings:** the threshold defaults to 1024 tokens. Decode CUDA graphs wider than that stop forking here, the same as `_run_parallel_input_projections` already does for them. For example, 256 requests with 6 speculative tokens make 1792 tokens. Smaller graphs are unchanged. ## Why it matters Inside HIP graphs, every fork/join becomes a cross-stream edge. At large decode batches those edges cost more than the overlapped GEMMs save. Deployments that set `VLLM_MULTI_STREAM_GEMM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=0` to turn the overlap off still paid for it in this layer. title: [Perf][Kimi-K3] Index KDA metadata with device row ids instead of CPU bool masks
summary: ## Overview When spec-decode requests share a step with non-spec requests (for example, a prefill chunk scheduled next to DSpark/MTP decodes), `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder.build` indexes six device tensors with host bool masks. Items 5-7 (bind-scope env vars, firewall requirements, log indicator) are not covered and need separate verification. title: [Core] Priority scheduling: hold lower-priority prefill for first tokens
summary: ## Overview Builds on #65282: the first commit here is #65282's, and this PR's change is the second. With priority scheduling, a high-priority request's first tokens share every step with lower-priority prefill chunks, which make those steps long. This PR adds `--priority-prefill-budget-cap` (off by default): until a higher-priority request has its first `--priority-prefill-budget-cap-tokens` output tokens (16 by default), lower-priority prefills are held back. ## Claims - With the cap on, prefills of a strictly lower priority, running or waiting, sit out the steps in which a higher-priority request awaits its first `--priority-prefill-budget-cap-tokens` output tokens, with or without async scheduling: from the step in which it fits (a free running slot and KV cache room for its whole sequence) or, with a running slot free, its KV connector load is done. - A request scheduled nothing, running or waiting, its KV load done or not, or a KV load still in flight, holds prefill back for at most that many steps in a row, and a lower-priority request that holds KV blocks sits out only while a request of its priority or a lower one runs, which preemption takes first. - Decodes are never held, nor is a request with one token left to compute, nor a prefill midway through an encoder input while a request it is held for needs encoder cache space. - Off by default, and off it changes no schedule: 2,496 traced configurations schedule as #65282 does, step for step. - Counters, `vllm:priority_prefill_held_steps` and `vllm:priority_prefill_held_tokens`, registered only with the cap on. - On

title: [Core] Priority scheduling: preempt lower-priority requests for KV cache space
summary: ## Overview With `--scheduling-policy priority`, a waiting request never preempts running requests for KV cache space, so a high-priority request that finds the KV cache full waits behind lower-priority ones: the KV cache case of #40004. This PR adds `--max-priority-preemptions-per-step N` (default `0`, off): at the start of a step, the highest-priority waiting request may preempt up to `N` lower-priority running requests, but only if that makes room for it. #65283 builds on it. ## Claims - With `N > 0`, the highest-priority waiting request preempts up to `N` running requests of a strictly lower priority when the KV cache lacks room for its whole sequence: in the running loop's order (lowest priority, then latest arrival), as few as make room, and none if `N` would not. - The room is net of the request's prefix cache hit, bounded as the waiting loop bounds it. It counts a shared block as freed only once all its holders are preempted, and it counts the blocks the running decodes take until the victims' blocks are freed. - In the step room is made, neither a victim nor a lower-priority request that holds KV blocks without a reservation, such as a streaming session's next chunk, takes the room. - A request waiting to start an async KV load (#65319's queue, with `--max-num-inflight-kv-loads`) counts as a waiting request: room is made for it as for any other. - Off by default, and off it changes no schedule: 416 traced configurations schedule as main does, step for step. - A counter, `vllm:num_priority_preemptions`, registered only when `N > 0`; `vllm:num_preemptions` counts the

title: [Feature]: Production evidence for restoring concurrent partial prefill limits (max_num_partial_prefills / max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Motivation We operate a production vLLM deployment (GLM-based MoE model, TP=4, 4x NVIDIA B200, V1 engine) serving a workload dominated by very long prompts (RAG/long-context, median ~100k-180k prompt tokens per request, generation typically <1k tokens). Under this workload we consistently observe severe TTFT tail latency caused by head-of-line blocking in prefill scheduling, and we believe this is a strong real-world case for reviving #49075 / #55256. ## Problem With `--enable-chunked-prefill` and `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to a reasonably high value (tested 8192 and 16384), a single long-prompt request still needs many scheduler iterations to complete its prefill (prompt_tokens / max_num_batched_tokens ≈ 7-12 iterations for our 100k-180k token prompts). Because the V1 scheduler currently has **no cap on concurrent partial prefills**, any request queued behind one of these long prefills must wait for it to fully finish before its own prefill can start — there is no way to interleave multiple partial prefills to give newer/shorter requests a fair share of the per-step token budget. We attempted to mitigate this with `--max-num-partial-prefills 4` (docs suggest this exists as a `SchedulerConfig` field), which immediately fails: vllm: error: unrecognized arguments: --max-num-partial-prefills 4 Digging into this, we found the flag was intentionally removed from `vllm/config/scheduler.py` in #49244 (V0 cleanup, July 2026) as "dead config" because it had no V1 consumer, and issue #39737 confirms the same failure mode on an earlier vL

summary: ## Purpose Fixes #46460. title: [Feature]: Support n > 1 multi-choice sampling in vllm.Inference
summary: ### The feature, motivation and pitch OpenAI Chat (`/v1/chat/completions`) and Completions (`/v1/completions`) accept `n > 1` to generate multiple choices from one shared prompt prefill. In `rust/proto/inference.proto`, `vllm.Inference/{Generate,GenerateStream}` rejects `num_sequences > 1` (`n > 1`). Non-streaming `GenerateResponse` also carries a single `SequenceOutput` rather than an indexed choice list. Gateways that tokenize once at ingress call workers over `vllm.Inference` (llm-d/llm-d-router#3758, llm-d/llm-d-router#3993). Without `n > 1` support on `vllm.Inference`, gateways cannot serve multi-choice requests from one prefill. **Proposal:** - Support `num_sequences > 1` in `vllm.Inference/GenerateStream` with per-candidate `index` on streamed chunks and `FinishInfo` (#66078). - Support `num_sequences > 1` in non-streaming `vllm.Inference/Generate` with indexed outputs per candidate. - When a client disconnects or a stream fails, cancel all unfinished candidates. ### Alternatives - Fan out `n` separate `GenerateStream` calls in the gateway. That duplicates prefill computation and breaks single-request disaggregated KV cache transfer. ### Additional context - **Consumers:** `llm-d` Coordinator (`Coord-Text-Text`, `Coord-Text-Tok`, `Coord-Tok-Tok`) and direct `vllm.Inference` gRPC clients (llm-d/llm-d-router#3992, llm-d/llm-d-router#3993, llm-d/llm-d-router#3758). - **Split items:** Multimodal kwargs moved to #66426, and worker `output_mode: derender` moved to #66427. - **P/D:** With `kv_transfer_params`, the `n` sequences read the KV blocks of one prefill request. #67

title: [Model] Kimi-K3: all requests degenerate to a repeated token after long-context prefill (NaN logits; packed KDA prefill suspected)
summary: # Summary Serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` at long context reproducibly degenerates: once a large-context request (~240K tokens, well inside the model's 1M-token spec) is processed, the deployment begins returning a **single repeated degenerate token on every step for every subsequent request**, never samples EOS, and every request runs to `max_tokens`. In the observed incident the state persisted ~19 hours and the set of corrupted requests grew over time (2 → 8 concurrent), i.e. the corruption **spreads between requests and is permanent per request** until process restart. We have proven the logits go NaN (see below); what remains open is *where* the NaN originates. This issue is filed as an investigation-in-progress with the evidence, two ready-to-run repro tests, and a concrete suspect code path — AI assistance was used in the investigation and in preparing this report. # Proven mechanism (established from the live system, not inferred) - The emitted token id is **0** every step. `KimiK3Config` sets `pad_token_id = 0`; chat deltas render empty (special token skipped) while `/v1/completions` renders ` @`. - Constant index-0 output means `greedy_sample` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:240`) returned argmax over NaN logits (argmax over NaN resolves to index 0). - Confirming evidence: while debugging, a logprobs request against this deployment killed the (Rust) frontend with `token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs`. The rank is computed as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)`; that count can only be 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN (all IEEE-754 comparisons ag

title: [Bugfix] Fix KV cache pages for hybrid models with draft layers
summary: ## Overview This PR fixes how vLLM picks KV cache pages when a model mixes layer types, which is what speculative decoding with a draft model on a hybrid (attention plus linear-attention) target does. FlashInfer now chooses kernel pages per layer, padded manager pages can split into kernel pages, and hybrid block alignment counts the drafter's KV. It is independent of #62961, #62962, #62963 and #62964, and of #63279, which carries the FA4 dense warmup coverage that started in this PR. ## Claims - FlashInfer kernel pages follow each attention group's own head counts, with query heads from its layers and KV heads from its spec. An MHA draft layer next to a GQA target otherwise gets the target's large pages, and its metadata builder rejects them at startup. `AttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes_for_layers(kv_cache_spec, layer_names)` carries this and defaults to `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`. The model runner and the NIXL and Mooncake connectors pass each group's layer names, so P/D transfer uses the same kernel blocks as the runner. - A padded manager page splits into uniformly strided kernel pages, and manager-page boundaries are kept. Interleaved layers and non-divisible padding still fail with a clear error. - Hybrid block alignment includes the drafter's KV bytes per token. When a draft has more KV per token than the target, it sets the common page size, and every recurrent-state page is padded up to it. For a 64-layer Qwen3.5-style GDN model with a one-layer draft that is a 5.2x padding, and the KV pool holds about 61 concurrent requests of 2.5k tokens.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Skip the FlashMLA sparse bf16 prefill workspace on the fp8 mixed-batch path
summary: ## Purpose `FlashMLASparseImpl` reserves the bf16 prefill KV workspace even when the fp8 mixed-batch path is selected and never reads it. Gate the `max_model_len`-sized reservation with the same path condition used by the metadata builder. Keep the three `max_num_batched_tokens` q/out buffers: the staging implementation in #60220 uses them. After #61023 the prefill factor is 2 above 256K context. At `max_model_len=786432`, the unused bf16 buffer is 1.6875 GiB per rank. The net saving depends on the other users of the shared workspace; the earlier 4.22 GiB figure no longer describes main. The separate prefill/decode, HiSparse and PCP+DCP gather reservations remain covered by the constructor test. The redundant truth-table test was removed following review. title: Feature request: a documented, supported pattern for fast weight synchronization between an RL trainer and vLLM rollout workers
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Use case In RL post-training loops (e.g. GRPO-style training), rollout generation runs on vLLM while a separate trainer process updates the policy. Every training step then needs the updated weights moved from the trainer into the vLLM workers. Today each RL framework (verl, TRL, OpenRLHF, Miles, etc.) implements this weight transfer on its own — via NCCL broadcast, shared memory, or checkpoint reload — with different performance characteristics and different failure modes. For long runs this sync can become a visible fraction of step time, and when something goes wrong it is hard to tell whether the problem is in the framework's sync code or in vLLM. ### Proposed feature A documented, supported pattern (or API) in vLLM for externally-driven weight updates, aimed at RL rollout deployments: - A recommended mechanism for pushing updated weights into running vLLM workers (in-place update vs. reload), with expected performance characteristics. - Documentation of how this interacts with CUDA graphs, KV cache invalidation, and ongoing requests. - Ideally, a small reference example of a trainer <-> rollout weight-sync loop. ### Why it matters RL post-training is becoming one of the main serving workloads for inference engines, and weight sync is the seam where the training and inference stacks meet. A first-class, documented pattern would reduce duplicated effort across RL frameworks and make performance problems at that seam much easier to diagnose. ### About me I'm a master's student working on RL (including RL-based sequential decisio

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Engine crash when a request hands over several partial-tail boundaries
summary: ## Purpose `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs` asserts that a request hands over exactly one boundary state. The producer does not guarantee that: `cache_blocks` deliberately offers *every* retained boundary it holds, so one step can deliver several for the same request. A partial-tail store job records a single shared block index for all groups, so such a hand-off cannot be represented — and the `assert` turns that into an engine crash instead of a dropped optimization. Fix: skip the ambiguous hand-off with a one-shot warning. The state is recomputable from the request, so the only loss is that offload's cache hit. Observed in production: 16 replicas of an MTP (K=3) model with `--kv-offloading-size` set, two engine crashes within two hours. `AssertionError` from this function, container exit code 0, no container OOM. ## Trigger conditions The `assert` was introduced with partial-tail reuse in #50507 and the producer has always offered every retained boundary (#52832). Both must hold for a crash: - **Partial-tail storage is enabled** — an offloading connector configured with a store tier (`--kv-offloading-size`) and `supports_partial_tail`. Without that, `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs` returns before reaching the loop. - **Speculative decoding with EAGLE/MTP groups** — added by #61019. Only then can a request retain more than one non-aligned boundary across consecutive steps. Non-speculative models collapse to a single retained boundary, so the set is always a singleton and the assert always passes. title: [RFC]: R3 as a KV cache layer: where routed-experts rows of prefix-cached blocks live
summary: Companion to #64380 (delivery protocol) and #61291 (payload format). Umbrella: #45221. Compares #57968 (Mooncake store keyed by block hash) with storing R3 as one more layer of the KV cache (prototype; PR to follow). Related: #58328, #57966, #62056 / #45419, #61897, #62920, #49555 / #62915. ## Motivation `--enable-return-routed-experts` (R3) returns, for every position of a request, the top-k experts each MoE layer selected. RL trainers replay these routes so the trainer computes the same experts as the rollout. A row is produced by the forward pass that computes that position's KV. On a prefix-cache hit that forward pass does not run, so the rows of hit blocks must be kept from an earlier request. R3 data therefore has two lifetimes: | Segment | Must live while | Lifetime decided by | Typical length | |---|---|---|---| | **Cache segment** | the block's KV can still be hit (GPU, CPU offload, KV store, P→D) | KV eviction (block manager + connectors) | ms to hours | | **Delivery segment** | after the request finishes, until the trainer has consumed the rows | trainer consumption | seconds to one RL step | If the cache segment dies before the KV does, a hit must either recompute, return missing rows, or fail. Aux outputs defined only at sampled positions (e.g. top-k logprobs) have no cache segment and are a pure delivery problem. Aux outputs defined at all positions (R3, indexer replay #49555 / #62915) need both. This RFC decides **who owns the cache segment**. The delivery segment is specified separately in #64380; nothing below depends on it except where noted. ## The two de

summary: ## Motivation - **What:** `SchedulerConfig.encoder_cache_size` is derived from `max_num_batched_tokens` and is `Field(init=False)` with a standing `# TODO (ywang96): Make this configurable.` This adds `--encoder-cache-size`. `None` keeps today's derivation, so **no behaviour change unless it is set**. - **Why:** they are different quantities. `max_num_encoder_input_tokens` is a per-step **compute** budget; `encoder_cache_size` is a **capacity** for keeping encoder output resident *across requests*, so a later request on the same image can skip the encoder (`EncoderCacheManager.check_and_update_cache`). - **Cost today:** cross-request reuse is capped at `max_num_batched_tokens / tokens_per_item` items and cannot be raised on its own. title: [Feature]: Support online linear re-quantization from FP8 checkpoints (Fp8LinearMethod.dequantize_weight)
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch When using vLLM's online quantization API (`--quantization-config '{"linear": ...}'`) on a pre-quantized FP8 checkpoint (`"quant_method": "fp8"`, such as `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8`), vLLM raises `NotImplementedError` because `Fp8LinearMethod` does not implement `dequantize_weight`: ```python from vllm import LLM llm = LLM( model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8", quantization_config={"linear": "mxfp8"}, ) ``` NotImplementedError: The quantization method <class 'vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8.Fp8LinearMethod'> does not implement dequantize_weight, so re-quantization from this checkpoint is not supported. Please open an issue. title: Deadlock: workers that disagree on enable_extensible_kv_cache hang in initialize_from_config
summary: ## Symptom `initialize_from_config()` branches on `enable_extensible_kv_cache`, and only one branch enters a world-group all-reduce: ```python if self.cache_config.enable_extensible_kv_cache: ... kv_cache.warmup_committable_blocks = _min_across_ranks( kv_cache.committable_blocks() ) else: self.model_runner.initialize_kv_cache(...) ``` A worker that resolved the flag differently takes the other branch and waits there forever. The engine hangs **after weight loading** with no error and no progress. Observed on vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev206` (4 nodes x 8x RTX PRO 6000, TP32 + EP32, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, prefix caching on), where the workers did not run byte-identical vLLM builds and therefore resolved different defaults for the flag: * the head rank printed `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds.` every minute indefinitely; * `py-spy dump` showed the head workers blocked in `all_reduce_int()` -> `_min_across_ranks()` -> `initialize_from_config()`, while the other ranks were already idle in `WorkerProc.worker_busy_loop()`; * no timeout fires, so the only external signal is the shm_broadcast warning. The existing `extensible_kv_cache_unsupported_reason()` already all-reduces for exactly this reason -- "Every rank must reach the same decision: one that keeps the feature would wait in the block-count all-reduces for one that dropped it" -- but only over *capability* (VMM availability), not over the resolved value of the flag itself. ## Proposal Require agreement on the value before branching, mirroring the existing capability check: reduce the flag with `MIN` and `MAX`

title: [Perf] Rotate q/k as a packed zero-copy view in Qwen-VL vision attention
summary: ## Purpose `Qwen2_5_VisionAttention` materialized a contiguous copy of q+k before applying rotary embeddings: `rearrange` to `(two*b, s, head, head_dim)` followed by `.contiguous()`, then an out-of-place rotation into a second buffer. The q and k heads are already adjacent in the fused qkv projection output, so flattening `(two, head)` is a zero-copy stride merge (verified: same `data_ptr`, 0 MiB allocated) — and the flash-attn Triton rotary kernel takes strided inputs natively; feeding it the strided view instead of a contiguous buffer costs +0.13% on average (measured below). Layout note: this moves the rope path's q/k from contiguous to strided; last-dimension stride remains 1. The FlashInfer/cuDNN wrapper explicitly materializes contiguous q/k, so performance on that backend has not been established by these measurements. The mm encoder runs eager by default (`compile_mm_encoder=False`), so the copy is real per-layer work Inductor never sees. The attention class is shared by the Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE and Qwen3-Omni vision towers. ## Warmup follow-up (2026-11-02) Updated to main `0e5b2ba11` and addressed the warmup feedback in `6d18a371`. Vision warmup now constructs sequence-major QKV and takes the same packed, strided `(1, S, 2H, D)` Q/K view as runtime. The existing vision test uses a real small Qwen3 vision transformer to check shape and stride equality, full-tower exclusion, and CPU-offload skipping. The cuDNN wrapper's outdated contiguity comment is removed. Validation on Colab Tesla T4 (SM75), FP16, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, T

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Reserve the sparse indexer's DCP top-k merge scratch through the workspace manager
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #59317. The sparse indexer's NCCL top-k merge allocates packed candidates and the rank-major all-gather output per call. The profile branch never executes that merge, so its scratch is absent from the KV budget. With 8192 rows, top-k 2048 and DCP4, those two tensors require 0.625 GiB per rank on top of the logits. Merge at most 1024 rows per step through workspace-manager buffers. The scratch is bounded at `(1 + dcp) * 8 * 1024 * topk` bytes (80 MiB for DCP4/top-k 2048). Gather into the destination buffer in place and let the selector read its rank-major prefix. Pass the existing `score_bits` and `id_bits` through unchanged. The prefill path takes merge scratch in the same workspace request as gathered K, which stays live across chunks. The GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer reserves the same scratch using pool-granular top-k; a separate workspace request would alias K needed by a later `skip_kv_gather` chunk. Both profile branches reserve their merge specs. The rebase preserves main's direct symmetric-memory DCP merge for eligible small batches. Only the remaining gathered-candidate path uses the bounded scratch. A CPU regression checks that the direct route still dispatches to its workspace. Related work: #47348 optimizes selector/exchange kernels; #50010 and #66027 add alternative bounded or packed routes and retain an existing merge for other shapes. This PR bounds and profiles that common gathered-candidate scratch. #59535 moves FlashInfer attention-kernel workspace, which is a different allocation. ## Test Plan Focused CPU tests cover the scratch bound, chun

title: [Bugfix] Fix MiniMax-M3 attention warmup deadlock under PP>1 (#60791)
summary: Follow-up to #64338 and resolves Item 8 in #60791. ### Root Cause & Context MiniMax-M3 is a hybrid model architecture: early layers (layers 0–2) use dense attention + standard MLPs, while subsequent layers (layers 3+) use MiniMax-M3 Sparse Attention (MSA) + MoE. When partitioned across pipeline stages under `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` (e.g. PP=2 where stage 0 only hosts layers 0–2): 1. **Asymmetric MSA Gate:** Stage 0 detects no `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` modules in its local layer partition and returns early from `minimax_m3_msa_warmup`. Later stages (hosting layers 3+) proceed into `mixed_batch_attention_warmup(worker)`, invoking `worker.execute_model`. Because model execution participates in pipeline activation send/recv and broadcasts across stages, later stages hang indefinitely waiting for Stage 0 until the NCCL watchdog timeout fires. 2. **Asymmetric KV Block Capacity Check:** In `v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py:run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup`, if non-uniform KV block allocations cause one PP stage to have fewer committable blocks than `required_blocks`, that rank early-exits while other ranks enter `model_runner.execute_model`, resulting in the identical PP hang. ### Solution 1. In `minimax_m3_msa_warmup`: All-reduce MSA module eligibility across the pipeline group via `pp_group.cpu_all_reduce_` (following the pattern established in #64338 for FlashInfer and #62129 for speculative warmup). Every PP rank makes a symmetric warmup execution decision: - Rank-local kernel compilation (`_msa_prebuild_kwargs` / `fmha_sm100.warmup`) only runs on ranks that host sparse modules on

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Zero-init dense attention output buffers to prevent CUDA-graph padding corruption (#65734)
summary: ## Summary When running under CUDA graphs with padded batch sizes (e.g. graph captured with batch size 512, active request has 4 tokens), unused padding rows are skipped by attention kernels, leaving uninitialized GPU memory in the output buffer. Under dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization, `o_proj` calculates its dynamic activation scale across the entire tensor (`abs().max() / 448`). Uninitialized large values or NaNs in padding rows artificially inflate this scale factor, shrinking real token activations toward zero and producing runaway garbage tokens under concurrency. This extends the fix in #37442 (which zero-initialized MLA output buffers) to generic dense attention by allocating the attention output tensor with `torch.zeros` instead of `torch.empty`. Fixes #65734. ## Test Plan - [x] Pre-commit hooks (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, SPDX header checks) pass clean. - [x] Verified against the reproducer in #65734 (confirming zero-initialized attention output eliminates padded-row scale contamination). <details> <summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary> - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and follows established precedent in #37442. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Verified against the reported reproducer in #65734. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Clean, surgical one-line change; passes all ruff and mypy checks. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Follows contributing guidelines and references related issues. </details>

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Pass packed rows to the sm90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM
summary: ## Overview Fixes wrong results from the SM90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM (`flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90`) when the activation is not row-contiguous. The kernel binding takes only a data pointer and assumes rows of exactly K elements, but the dynamic FP8 block-scaled linear kernel forwards every M < 32 batch as-is, so a strided input (e.g. a column slice) is read from the wrong memory for every row after the first. The fix passes packed (contiguous) rows in both wrappers and adds a regression test. ## Claims - **Bugfix:** the sm90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM no longer misreads strided activations. Previously, rows 1..M-1 of a non-contiguous input were computed from the wrong memory; they now match the packed-row result bit-exactly. - **Scope:** only the small-batch (M < 32) FlashInfer path is affected; M >= 32 already goes through DeepGEMM, which honours strides. Already-contiguous inputs are untouched (`Tensor.contiguous()` is a no-op), so there is no overhead in the common case and no host synchronization is added. ## Validation - New regression test `test_flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm_strided_input` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py` (parametrized over M in {2, 31}): feeds the wrapper a column slice whose row stride is larger than K and asserts the result is bit-exact against the packed copy. It executes on SM90 + FlashInfer and skips elsewhere. - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "strided_input or flashinfer"`: validated on an H200 by the original author — 42 passed, 5 skipped. title: [ROCm][PP] Stage hand-off on SDMA copy engines (--pp-sdma-handoff)
summary: ## Overview With pipeline parallelism, each step's intermediate tensors go from one stage to the next over NCCL send / recv. On ROCm that peer copy runs as a blit kernel on the sender's CUs, so it slows whatever the sender computes next to it: an 8192^3 bf16 GEMM on the sender runs 5.1x slower while a 201 MiB tensor is copied to the next GPU (table below). In a TP1 x PP2 prefill of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, a 16384-token step hands off several such tensors on both stages' compute path. This PR adds an opt-in hand-off on SDMA copy engines, `--pp-sdma-handoff` (`ParallelConfig.pp_sdma_handoff`, off by default). It applies to PP2 x TP1 on gfx950 (MI355X), eager (`cudagraph_mode` NONE), both stages on one node; with the flag set and any of these unmet, the worker raises at init. - The receiving stage allocates 3 slots and shares them with the sender over CUDA IPC. - A sender thread waits for the step's event, then copies each tensor into the step's slot on two SDMA engines (no CUs). - The stages sync slot reuse through two counters in `/dev/shm`: `ready` (sender) and `freed` (receiver, once the step that read the slot has run on its GPU). Shapes and non-tensor entries still go through the PP group's object send; those sends are reaped against `freed` (a gloo isend `Work` reports `is_completed()` False until `wait()`). Eager only, because a CUDA graph replay reuses its output buffers while the copy may still read them. PP2 only, because a middle stage would relay tensors that alias its receive slots. title: [RFC]: Async CPU tier setup for OffloadingConnector
summary: ## Motivation. With a large CPU tier, startup waits for every worker to pre-fault and pin its share of `/dev/shm` before the engine can serve. Two examples from our experiments: - GLM-5.3 with 16 H100s (DP16/EP, 4 pods), a 280 GiB tier per rank. Pre-fault takes 117 s and pinning 12 s, all of it on the startup critical path. - Qwen3-8B (dummy weights) with TP=4 and a 1,250 GiB tier on one H100 node. Startup is 241.5 s, and most of that is the CPU tier. #62337 adds a core ready state for connectors. #54578 adds async init to OffloadingConnector with the same `async_init` option, and #42632 and #54792 cover SimpleCPUOffloadConnector. This RFC covers what OffloadingConnector needed on top at these sizes: a graph-capture guard, paced pinning, and Tiering support, which #54578 rejects. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Report only written blocks from fs tier store jobs
summary: ## Overview Block files in the `fs` tier are named by content hash, so when a prefix that is already on disk gets stored again, `_store_block` skips the write. This PR makes the tier report only the blocks it actually wrote. ## Claims - `transfer_bytes` now counts written blocks only, and is `0` when every block was already on disk. `BackpressureDetector.update` already ignores `num_bytes <= 0`, so these jobs stop feeding the EMA. - Nothing else changes: same bytes on disk, same job success, same lookup verdicts and KV events. title: [Rust Frontend] Support n > 1 on /inference/v1/generate
summary: ## Purpose The Rust frontend's token-in/token-out route, `/inference/v1/generate`, rejects `sampling_params.n > 1` with `Only n=1 is supported.`, while the Python route returns one choice per sample. Clients that need several samples per prompt (for example RL rollouts) have to send `n` separate requests, which repeats prompt handling and multimodal preprocessing for every sample. This PR adds `n > 1` to the route by reusing the parallel-sampling path the OpenAI routes already use on the Rust frontend. ## Changes - **Fan-out:** the prompt and any media are prepared once, then submitted as `n` child engine requests through the shared `generate_prepared_n` path. Like Python's `ParentRequest`, child IDs are `{index}_{request_id}`, and a seeded request gives each child `seed + index` (wrapping), so samples differ but stay reproducible. A seed of `-1` stays unseeded. - **Non-streaming:** all choices are collected concurrently and returned in index order in one response. Prompt-level fields come from the first choice, usage counts the prompt once and sums completion tokens, and per-request metrics are reported only for `n = 1`. - **Streaming:** per-choice chunk streams are interleaved with their `index` set. title: [ROCm] MXFP8 dispatch for AITER MXFP4 MoE under data parallelism
summary: ## Overview With data parallelism and the default `allgather_reducescatter` all2all backend, AITER MXFP4 MoE experts (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X) all-gather BF16 hidden states, then quantize the gathered batch to MXFP8 inside AITER. On CDNA4 (gfx950), this PR runs that same MXFP8 quantization on the local rows before the all-gather. The all-gather then moves FP8 rows plus E8M0 scales (about half the bytes), and AITER's MXFP8 passthrough ([ROCm/aiter#4954](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4954), in the pinned `v0.1.28.post1`) only sorts the scales. The end-to-end numbers below were taken on AITER `v0.1.28.post1`; the unit tests also pass on `v0.1.29`, the current pin. ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP4 on 4x MI355X, prefill at `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`: 64 x 8k-token prompts take **4.31 s instead of 4.62 s (-7%)** (median of 3). - Same operands reach the experts: the dispatch only runs where AITER would itself call `per_1x32_mx_quant_hip` (unshuffled scales) on the gathered batch. The decision uses AITER's own `resolve_activation_dtype` and the fused-quant cut-over, so behaviour follows AITER. It does not consult AITER's tuned configs: in `v0.1.29` the only configs that quantize BF16 inside the first GEMM (`_f16in`) are A4W4 at 512 tokens or fewer, which this path excludes. - Accuracy unchanged: GSM8K (lm_eval, 5-shot, all 1319 questions) 0.923 -> 0.929, within the standard error of about 0.007, and `niah_single_2` stays at 1.0 at 32k and 64k. - On by default, with no new env var. Other GPUs (the experts' hook returns None unless `get_cdna_version() == 4`)

title: [KVConnector] S1 variant B: P/D keep pause without scheduler changes (RFC #66231, alt. to #67737)
summary: ## Overview Variant B of RFC #66231 (collapsed section "Variant B (glue)"): the same goal as #67737, `pause(mode="keep", clear_cache=False)` on every P and D in any order, but with no changes under `vllm/v1/core/`. Opened as a draft so that the two designs can be reviewed side by side; the RFC recommends A. The branch is based on main 5cdeea9b1 to match the RFC data, so it conflicts with current main. ## Claims Terms used below: - An **export** is a finished request whose KV blocks P keeps until D has read them. - A **lease** bounds how long P keeps an export (30 s here). D's heartbeats extend it, and P frees the blocks when it expires. **B1: P's keep pause stops waiting for D's reads.** - On main, a pause completes only once the engine has no work at all. Retained exports count as work, so P's `pause(mode="keep", clear_cache=False)` waits until D reads them or the lease expires (31 s on NIXL). - With B1, a keep pause without clear completes as soon as nothing is computing, because it does not free those blocks. The check is repeated after every engine step. If `resume` arrives before the pause completed, that pause call fails. - Code: `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`. The changes are in `pause_scheduler`, `_pause_complete` and `resume_scheduler`. New helpers: `_keep_pause_ready` and `_maybe_finish_keep_pause`, called from `_process_engine_step` and `_process_input_queue`. `_has_compute_work` ignores zero-token batches. **B2: a paused D keeps renewing P's leases.** - On main, D's heartbeats are sent from the scheduler step. title: [Security] Add hash collision defense for prefix cache with non-crypto hashes
summary: When using non-cryptographic hash algorithms (xxhash/xxhash_cbor) for prefix caching, hash collisions can cause cache poisoning where a request receives incorrect KV cache data from an unrelated prompt. Add insertion-time content verification that stores a token fingerprint alongside each cached block and rejects colliding insertions with a warning. The defense is automatically enabled when the configured hash algorithm is xxhash or xxhash_cbor, with zero overhead on the default sha256 path.

title: [KV Offload] Carry request provenance and emit chunk-key removals
summary: ## Purpose Emit self-describing KV-offload events without retaining a full payload per offloaded chunk. For a locally initiated store or promotion, the raw event carries the original `ReqContext`; when the asynchronous store completes, the tracker uses its `Request` and KV-group geometry to build `BlockStored` (block hashes, tokens, parent hash, block size, and per-block `extra_keys`). A removal needs only its `OffloadKey`. ## Changes - Carry the exact `ReqContext` through CPU, FS, OBJ, cascade, and promotion completion. Resolve full chunks and partial tails lazily at stored-event translation time; use context identity rather than request ID for stale completions. - Keep promotion hit-source attribution scoped to `ReqContext` identity, so a delayed old request cannot erase a newer request using the same ID. - Generate aligned per-block `extra_keys` for offload events in the existing KV-event format (LoRA name, multimodal identifier/offset pairs, cache salt, and prompt-embedding digests). Explicit unsalted blocks carry `[None, ...]`, distinct from absent `extra_keys`. - Emit chunk-key `BlockRemoved`: one tail block hash per offloaded chunk, grouped by KV group, with the original medium, locality, and ownership. Remove the long-lived metadata/residency map and the lookup/store-time recording hooks. - Keep placeholder stored payloads for external work, unsupported cache shapes, and unsafe token-mutating requests. Preserve queued removal events across cache reset. `OffloadKey` remains `(block_hash, group_idx)`; store admission/batching and worker transfer metadata are unchanged

title: [Bugfix] Keep metadata of a delayed BlockStored when an OffloadKey is reused

The event is then sent as a placeholder (`token_ids=[]`, `block_size=0`). With this fix the tracker counts, per key, the old primary removals that a new recorded store has replaced. The old `BlockRemoved` then no longer drops the metadata that the new store still needs. Compared with #52103 and #63129, this fix: - Is much smaller. It is about 30 lines in `events.py` and keeps the existing metadata map and the `record_*` hooks. [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103) touches 11 source files and removes the map and the hooks. [#63129](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63129) replaces the map with a dict subclass that overrides `__setitem__`, `pop` and `clear`, and adds a deque of generations per key. Compared with #52103, this fix: - Also fixes resumable requests. With the reported order on [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103)'s head, the delayed `BlockStored` of a resumable request is still `block_hashes=[49] token_ids=[] block_size=0`. Its first store is also a placeholder, and that store has full metadata on the current code. - Keeps the current event output. [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103) changes `BlockRemoved` to carry only the chunk key (`[49]` instead of `[48, 49]` for a two-block c

title: [Perf][Core] Restore compact prefix-cache entries after duplicate eviction
summary: ## Purpose When a prefix-cache hash has multiple physical copies, `BlockHashToBlockMap` promotes its value to a dictionary. Eviction currently retains that dictionary even when only one copy remains. Subsequent lookups can repeatedly scan its deleted entries, and its allocation remains live. Restore the existing direct `KVCacheBlock` representation when eviction leaves one copy. Extend the existing mapping test to cover re-insertion, an unknown block ID and final removal, and update the pool-eviction expectations. Block identity, reference counts, cache contents and KV-event behavior are preserved. The state is reachable through repeated `prompt_logprobs` requests followed by cache pressure. summary: ## Purpose Fixes #52715. On ROCm, AutoGPTQ MoE layers that cannot use GPTQMoeMarlin fall back to the Triton WNA16 backend. title: [Attention][CPU] Run Zen CPU decoder prefill on zentorch SDPA
summary: ## Purpose Route **decoder prefill / extend** on the vLLM CPU backend through `zentorch_sdpa` on Zen CPUs, instead of always using the paged `cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` kernel. title: [Bugfix] Pad sub-block FP8 tensor-parallel shards
summary: ## Purpose Serving `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` on one H100 node with tensor parallelism 8 fails during model initialization. Tensor parallelism produces a rank-local shared-expert width of 64, while the checkpoint uses 128-element FP8 quantization blocks: ```text ValueError: Weight input_size_per_partition = 64 is not divisible by weight quantization block_k = 128. ``` Padding only the row-parallel K shard exposes the corresponding merged-column N problem. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Harden handshake listener against bad requests
summary: ## Purpose The prefill-side NIXL handshake listener (`_nixl_handshake_listener` in `base_scheduler.py`) is a single background thread for each engine. It lives for the whole process and answers metadata queries from every decode worker that pulls KV cache from this engine. It handled only the idle-poll timeout. Any bad request killed the thread silently, and nothing restarted or reported it. A bad request is anything on the side-channel port that is not a well-formed request from a real `REQ` client: a peer that does not send the `REQ`/`ROUTER` envelope (e.g., a bare `DEALER` socket, which sends 2 frames instead of 3), malformed or deeply nested msgpack, or a request for a pp/tp rank that this engine does not serve. After the thread dies, every handshake against this engine times out for every decode worker until the process restarts. Thus, one bad request causes a silent denial of service (DoS) for the full engine. No issue is filed for this. We found it in production and reproduced it locally. I searched the issues, the PRs and the current `main` of `vllm-project/vllm`, and found no work on the exception handling of this listener. The nearest related work, vllm-project/vllm#48633 and vllm-project/vllm#49238 / vllm-project/vllm#50047, is about different NIXL reliability gaps (push-mode handshake latency, stale peer state after a restart). ## Changes - `base_scheduler.py`: validate each request before the listener uses it, as suggested in review: - Check that the request has 3 frames. - Decode the message with `msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(tuple[bytes, int, int])`. title: [Core] Add platform-scoped per-request speculative fallback
summary: ## Summary Add a default-false platform capability that lets a backend with homogeneous per-request decode lanes defer globally unsupported speculative sampling controls to its ordinary lane. The existing behavior remains unchanged for every platform that does not opt in. A platform may return `true` only when it can preserve the requested sampling semantics outside speculative decode. This is the small vLLM-side extension needed by the TT model-owned speculative contract. It allows `min_p` and `logit_bias` requests to use the TT ordinary lane instead of making speculative decoding reject the whole server configuration. ## Safety - The capability defaults to `false`. - Existing global rejection remains the default. - The exception is limited to sampling controls that the opted-in platform routes to a semantics-preserving ordinary path. - No request parameter is dropped or rewritten. ## Tests - `tests/test_sampling_params.py`: 65 passed on Python 3.12. - The TT integration candidate passed its ordinary fallback matrix for seeded sampling, penalties, logprobs, structured output, allowed and bad tokens, logit bias, `min_p`, and `n=2`. ## Related work - TT plugin PR: tenstorrent/vllm-tt-plugin#161, homogeneous speculative and ordinary lanes plus dynamic draft caps. - tt-transformers PR: tenstorrent/tt-transformers#47, Qwen3.8 model-owned speculative contract implementation.

This lets disaggregated decode workers opt in without changing prefill workers. When disabled, or when the device, collective, dtype, parallel layout, or tensor shape is unsupported, the runner keeps its existing schedule. Shapes already handled by K3 latent-tail fusion also keep that path. The reusable `LowSMAllReduce` implementation is a bounded BF16 NVLS collective for NVIDIA SM100/SM103. It derives TP size, payload capacity, doorbell storage, and result-slot count at runtime; rank-validates the contract; uses one single-flight slot per ubatch; and falls back collectively if symmetric-memory or NVLS resources are unavailable. title: [Bugfix] Fix logprobs Triton kernel JIT-compiling mid-request for uncommon topk widths
summary: ## What's going on here `_topk_log_softmax_kernel` (the Triton kernel behind logprobs scoring) recompiles mid-request the first time it sees a new `num_logprobs` value — even one that should reuse an already-warmed variant. I tracked it down to `topk` being a plain kernel argument that Triton auto-specializes on 16-byte alignment: a request with `logprobs=31` (topk=32, aligned) and one with `logprobs=32` (topk=33, unaligned) both want `TOPK_BLOCK_SIZE=64`, but Triton compiles them as two different kernels anyway. Since `num_logprobs` is whatever a client sends, there's no way to warm every possible value up front — you're always one odd request away from paying the compile cost live. Two changes fix this: 1. `_topk_log_softmax_kernel` now passes `do_not_specialize_on_alignment=["topk"]`, so Triton stops caring about alignment for that argument and only specializes on the thing that actually matters (`TOPK_BLOCK_SIZE`, 11 possible values). 2. A new startup warmup (`logprob_triton_warmup`, wired into `kernel_warmup()` for the V2 runner) precompiles all 11 buckets using the model's real vocab size and both its compute dtype and fp32, since `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` computes logits in fp32 independent of the model's compute dtype. ## About #55577 This closes #55577, and I checked there's no other open PR against it. But I'm *not* using that issue's proposed fix. title: [Bugfix][Parser] Coerce nested strings in decoded XML arguments
summary: ## Purpose The XML tool parser decodes an object or array parameter from a string, but `ParserEngine._coerce_value` immediately returns that container without applying the existing `properties`/`items` recursion. For an inline schema declaring an array of integers, `<parameter=limits>["10", "20", "30"]</parameter>` therefore produces string elements. Nested numeric, boolean and nullable fields have the same problem, including in streaming responses. Clients expecting the declared argument types can reject these tool calls. After a string successfully converts to a dict or list, recurse through its `properties`/`items` and coerce nested strings. An internal `coerce_native_scalars` flag keeps the decoded container's existing JSON numbers, booleans and nulls unchanged. Without that distinction, the existing fallback to `string` for untyped schemas would turn `{"n": 1}` into `{"n": "1"}` under `properties: {n: {}}`, introducing a regression. Existing native scalar coercion remains enabled by default for native JSON input. Stringified container children in such input also gain the new recursion. String conversion, union precedence and best-effort failure behavior are unchanged. This is a nested-string correction, not full schema normalization: a decoded native `1` still remains `1` even if its schema requests `string`, as it did before. No JSON Schema keyword support is added. Extend the existing Qwen3 parser tests to cover both native JSON values and string values requiring nested conversion. title: Add live scheduler knobs and in-place KV pool reinit via a dev route
summary: ## Purpose Scheduler settings in vLLM are read once at startup. Changing a concurrency cap, a token budget, or a prefill threshold means killing the process and reloading the weights, which costs one to seven minutes on the machines below. Those values are plain scheduler state that the event loop re-reads every step, so nothing on the GPU is allocated when they change. This adds two things behind the existing dev-mode gate: - **Hot knobs.** `EngineCore.trimtab_set_knobs` / `trimtab_get_knobs`, reached through the utility RPC, with `POST /trimtab/set_knobs` and `GET /trimtab/knobs` under `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`, the same gate as the other dev routes. Knobs: `max_num_seqs`, `max_num_batched_tokens`, `long_prefill_token_threshold`, `log_level`, each validated against the value allocated at boot. - **Warm KV pool reinit.** `trimtab_reinit` frees the KV pool and the captured CUDA graphs, reprofiles, and rebuilds pools, attention groups, graphs and the scheduler at the new size, with the weights resident throughout. Requires `--enable-sleep-mode` and an idle engine. Lowering `max_num_seqs` below current occupancy would trip the per-step assertion `len(running) <= max_num_running_reqs`, so it is applied as a target: admissions stop immediately and the enforced cap tightens as requests finish. The read-back reports both. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/engine/test_trimtab_knobs.py`, new in this PR: applied values, every rejected shape, the occupancy floor, a case-insensitive log level, and the reinit validator. No GPU and no KV allocation, so it runs in the default lane. - Hardware runs

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Derive draft KV slots from absolute position on M-RoPE models
summary: # [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Derive draft KV slots from absolute position on M-RoPE models ## Purpose Fixes #54498. On M-RoPE models the V1 draft loop fed `positions[0]` — the M-RoPE temporal coordinate — to both the RoPE recurrence and the KV slot computation. Those are two different coordinate systems. An `H x W` patch grid occupies `H*W` KV slots but advances the M-RoPE coordinate by only `max(t, h, w)`, so on any prompt containing an image the temporal dim falls below the absolute token index and the drafted token is written to a slot that belongs to the prompt. Attention still reads the full span per `seq_lens`, so the corrupted entry is read back as context: acceptance length drops, and the drop compounds with the number of draft steps. ### Changes 1. `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` allocates a `_slot_positions` buffer for M-RoPE and derives the slot coordinate from `seq_lens - 1`, which counts real tokens. No new data source is needed and the non-M-RoPE paths are untouched. 2. All three M-RoPE dims advance together with the kernel's clamp semantics (`>= max_model_len -> 0`) mirrored in torch, instead of the spatial dims being overwritten by the temporal one. 3. `Step3p5MTPProposer` recomputes the secondary KV cache groups' slots from the same absolute position the parent used, capturing the out-of-bounds condition *before* delegating, because the parent advances `seq_lens` in place. 4. `eagle_step_update_slot_mapping_and_metadata` documents `positions_1d` as an absolute sequence position at both the kernel comment and the wrapper docstring. title: [ROCm][Perf] Sparse MLA: build pure-decode indptr on the host and skip the NoPE q copy
summary: ## Purpose Two small per-step cuts on the ROCm AITER sparse MLA decode path. Split out of the draft #59739. Independent of the MXFP4 KV cache work (#60321). 1. **Host-built decode indptr.** On a pure-decode step (`num_prefills == 0`, `max_query_len == 1`) with no speculative decoding, `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is exact. So `paged_kv_indptr = cumsum(min(seq_len, topk))` is computed on the host into a pinned buffer and uploaded with one non-blocking copy. This replaces the `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` launch, the device cumsum, and the tail fill. A `torch.Event` guards reuse of the pinned buffer. `req_id_per_token` is `0..n-1` on pure decode, so it is only rewritten when the decode batch grows past what the buffer already holds. Mixed and prefill batches, and any run with a speculative config, keep the existing device path unchanged. 2. **Skip the NoPE query copy.** When `qk_rope_head_dim == 0`, the MQA bmm output is already the token-major query. `forward` uses it directly instead of copying it into `q_concat_buffer`, provided it is contiguous and the dtype matches. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_sparse_host_decode_indptr.py` (new): checks that the host `cumsum(min(seq_len, topk))` matches `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` for topk 2048 and 64. - `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`: - The builder fixture gains the new attributes. - New `test_pure_decode_builds_indptr_on_the_host` asserts the device seqlen kernel is not launched, and checks the resulting `paged_kv_indptr` and `req_id_per_token`. - Existing ROCm sparse MLA suit

title: [Bugfix][Core] Time out requests stuck in WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #53130. A resumable request that finishes generating with no queued next chunk enters `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and can only leave that status through an external `add_request()` or `finish_requests()` call for the same request id. If a client, or a proxy in front of it, drops the connection without that signal ever arriving, the request stays parked forever and keeps holding its `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` slot, eventually blocking admission for the whole engine even with free KV cache. Gives it a deadline (`VLLM_STREAMING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 600s) and aborts it once that passes, instead of re-skipping it on every scheduling pass. ## Test Plan Added `test_streaming_request_timeout_aborts` and `test_streaming_request_no_timeout_before_deadline` to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`. ## Test Result `pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v`: 10/10 passed, including both new tests and all pre-existing streaming tests (no regressions).

summary: ## Overview This pull request significantly optimizes `DiffusionGemma` (`vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py`) by replacing eager PyTorch operations in `DiffusionGemmaSelfConditioning` with custom fused Triton kernels and eliminating CPU serialization in `DiffusionGemmaModelState._apply_self_conditioning`. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview When two vLLM instances use the same NIXL side-channel port on one host, the second engine can hang during startup. Separate inference groups hit this in SkyRL. [SkyRL #1926](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/1926) ## Claims - If the listener exits before it is ready, the error reports the host and port and points to `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT`. - A successful bind wakes the scheduler immediately. The listener continues to serve updates to the shared handshake metadata. ## Validation With the scheduler from main `56e5608d0f`, the occupied-port regression stopped at `ready_event.wait()` with `Failed: Timeout (>60.0s) from pytest-timeout.` On this branch, the scheduler and in-process `LLM` regressions both raised the expected `RuntimeError` on ARM64 CPU. title: [Attention][DSv4.1] Build indexer prefill chunk metadata once per request range
summary: ## Overview The DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 indexer builds prefill chunk metadata once per request range instead of once per query sub-chunk. Its sub-chunks share all KV-side metadata; only their row bounds differ. ## Claims - Less host work per prefill step. On GB200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP4 AgentX serving (c256): | metric, steady-state prefill steps | before | after | |---|---|---| | `build_prefill_chunk_metadata` calls per step | 46 | 18 | | indexer metadata builder (p50) | 12.4 ms | 6.6 ms | | model-state `prepare_attn` (p50) | 27.0 ms | 16.8 ms | - Identical metadata: each sliced sub-chunk equals a direct build, field for field. - No end-to-end change at c256 (throughput / TTFT / ITL within run-to-run spread). title: [Performance]: Gemma 4 full-attention layers run the Triton kernel for the whole prefill whenever the batch carries image/video spans
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance With `use_bidirectional_attention == "vision"`, Gemma 4 applies the bidirectional image/frame mask only on sliding-window layers; its full-attention layers are plain causal. vLLM already encodes this: `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration._clear_mm_prefix_for_full_attn_layers` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py`) nulls `mm_prefix_range` on those layers at forward time. But the composite backend picks the child kernel earlier. `MMPrefixAttentionRouting.select` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/composite.py`) only asks whether the *batch* carries spans (`requires_mm_prefix`), not whether the *layers of this KV-cache group* will use them. So for every request with media, the group of full-attention layers (head_dim 512 on Gemma 4 31B, the O(n²) share of prefill) runs the Triton unified kernel instead of the causal child (FlashAttention on Hopper, FlashInfer on Blackwell), and the forward-time clearing only makes that Triton call causal. On a long video prompt this is most of the remaining prefill time once the per-span scan is gone (#65505). ### Measured `vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, one H100, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.33.0rc1.dev573+g40941f2c4, backend `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`), one request of 66 × 32-frame 640×360 clips = 158,418 prompt tokens, 16 output tokens, greedy; a fresh server per row: | | TTFT | server prefill | 8 clips / 19,276 tokens TTFT | |---|---|---|---| | stock | 390.3 s | 378.6 s | 12.4 s | | + #65505 (binary-search mm_prefix spans) | 163.2 s | 152.9 s | 8.5 s | | + routing full-attentio

title: [Model][MiniMax-M3] SM120 Blackwell NVFP4 KV cache Triton reader
summary: ## What / Why Enables `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` for **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash** on **SM120** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SE 96 GB), where the SM100 MSA CUTLASS backend (`tcgen05`/TMEM) does not exist and the nvfp4 KV path currently fails. The change is **pure Python/Triton** (no CUDA C++ added): - the existing SM80+ NVFP4 writer (`fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert`) already writes valid pages on SM120; - this PR adds the missing **reader**: packed `E2M1 + E4M3` scale tile loads for prefill and split-K decode in `ops/sparse_attn.py` (`USE_NVFP4`), plus backend wiring in `sparse_attention.py` (`MiniMaxM3SparseBackend` / impl for `kv_cache_dtype=nvfp4`, LBHNC layout, `2 * num_kv_heads` slots of 72 bytes). K scales are addressed linear (`8192 + t*8 + h`), V scales with the 4-token cell swizzle (`8192 + (t//4*4 + h//2)*8 + (h%2)*4 + (t%4)`). ## Numerical validation Cosine similarity vs an exact PyTorch NVFP4 dequantization reference, on-device (`test_sm120_nvfp4_triton.py`, ~50 MB VRAM, loads `./patched/sparse_attn.py`): | kernel | gqa=16 (TP4) | gqa=8 (TP8) | |---|---|---| | prefill | 0.997738 (0.9999987 in FP32) | 0.997692 | | decode qlen=1 | 0.997195 | 0.996711 | | decode qlen=8 (MTP) | 0.995720 | 0.997168 | ## Performance (8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SE, TP=4 EP=4) Strict A/B: same pod, same node, `only --kv-cache-dtype` changes; `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, LMCache disabled for symmetry. | metric | fp8 | nvfp4 |

title: [Security] Validate Mooncake and MoRI-IO transfer requests before scheduling
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Malformed client-supplied `kv_transfer_params` can raise uncaught exceptions in Mooncake and MoRIIO scheduler paths and terminate `EngineCoreProc`, disrupting other requests served by that engine. This PR validates transfer metadata before scheduler admission: invalid inference requests receive request-scoped HTTP 400 errors, and cancellation markers are validated before cleanup. ## Claims - **Mooncake role mismatches:** reject `do_remote_prefill` on a producer and `do_remote_decode` on a consumer before they reach scheduler assertions. - **Mooncake cancellation cleanup:** require non-empty `transfer_id`, `remote_engine_id`, and `remote_bootstrap_addr` for remote prefill, including abort markers, so cleanup metadata construction cannot fail on missing peer fields. Remote decode requires `transfer_id`. - **MoRIIO DP fields:** validate `remote_dp_size`, `remote_dp_size_local`, and `remote_dp_rank` before scheduler conversion. Absent/`None` values retain defaults, and valid numeric strings remain accepted. - **MoRIIO WRITE notification:** reject missing or malformed producer notification addresses before allocation can leave a request waiting for remote KV. Preserve encoded-request-ID and explicit host/port precedence for allocation and cleanup. - A pure connector validation hook covers the shared engine admission path and delegates through MultiConnector. Connector docs describe the requirements; public-server regressions check HTTP 400 followed by successful ordinary inference. ## Validation Local connector tests: **26 Mooncake cases

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Protect the step's reported HITs from promotion eviction
summary: ## Purpose Fix an fs→RAM promotion race in `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU primary tier + secondary tier) that crashes the engine under load: ``` AssertionError: Chunk ... not found in cache (vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py, prepare_load) ``` ## Root cause `lookup()` reports primary-tier chunks as HIT for the current scheduler step, but the scheduler only *pins* them later in the step. Between the two, a secondary→primary **promotion** calls `prepare_write()` on the CPU manager, whose eviction policy may pick exactly those HIT chunks as victims (they look idle). When `prepare_load()` later runs for the reported HITs, the chunk is gone → assert. Observed in production on v0.32.0 under sustained multi-tenant load: **5 engine crashes in one day** (each `docker logs` shows the assert above from the scheduler's `update_state_after_alloc`). Reported in #60729 (case 2) and #54914; also discussed on #62615. ## Fix - The tiering manager records the keys its own lookups reported HIT during the current step (`_step_hit_keys`) and passes them as `extra_protected` to the promotion's `prepare_write()`, so the CPU policy cannot evict them. Cleared at `on_schedule_end()`. - If protecting them leaves no room, the promotion returns `None` and the chunk degrades to a **MISS that the scheduler recomputes** — the pre-existing slow path, never a crash. - `prepare_write()` gains the optional `extra_protected` argument, applied as a union *view* (no copy of the protected set). The manager's own input keys keep their existing protection. ## Test plan - New `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_step_hit_

title: [ROCm][Perf] Dispatch MTP eh_proj to wvSplitK, 1.1-1.85x kernel
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview The DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 MTP drafter on ROCm runs `eh_proj`, a bf16 GEMM, once per draft step at M of 1-5 rows, where it is purely weight-bandwidth bound. It is declared as a plain `nn.Linear`, so it never reaches `dispatch_unquantized_gemm` and the `wvSplitK` skinny kernel that its sibling projections already use. This PR declares it as a `ReplicatedLinear(quant_config=None)`, which keeps the bf16 weight, its name and loading unchanged. On MI300X: 1.23x / 1.15x at M=1. - No end-to-end serving change is claimed: every serving delta is inside the spread between two runs of the same arm (the layer is ~0.3% of a draft step). - GSM8K and MTP acceptance length are unchanged on both models. - At M >= 8 `wvSplitK` rejects the shape and dispatch falls back to `F.linear` (1.00x). ROCm-only file; no shared or CUDA code changes. ## Validation **Setup:** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly `3966924d`, 4x MI325X, TP=4. Before is the same container with `eh_proj` left as `nn.Linear`. title: [Bugfix] Omit inactive CP checkpointing kwargs in FlashInfer GDN prefill
summary: ## Overview In `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` unconditionally passes context-parallel (CP) checkpointing keyword arguments (`state_checkpoints`, `checkpoint_cu_starts`, `checkpoint_every_n_tokens`, `use_cp`, `backend="flashinfer"`) to `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule(...)`. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][MoRIIO] WRITE: keep the RDMA completion wait off the forward thread and fail only the affected request
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview In MoRIIO WRITE mode, the prefill can wait for a request's RDMA completion on the model forward thread (`wait_for_save` → `seal_pending_transfers` → `_finalize_if_complete`). A transfer timeout there raises `TransferError` out of `execute_model` on one rank, and the engine dies. This PR moves that wait to the existing write-worker thread. A failed or timed-out transfer now sends `write_failed` to decode, so only that request fails. ## Claims - A WRITE transfer that fails or times out no longer kills the prefill engine. It fails only its own request: decode reports it in `failed_recving`, and `kv_load_failure_policy` applies. - The forward thread never blocks on RDMA completion. Previously it could stall prefill for every other request for up to `transfer_timeout` (30 s by default). - On the write-worker path, the same failure now notifies decode. Previously the prefill freed its blocks and the decode request hung in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. ## Validation **Setup.** GLM-5.3-FP8 on MI300X, MoRIIO WRITE, PD disaggregation. **On `main`.** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly built from `00b6c4c565` (HIP 7.15, AITER 0.1.26); `moriio_engine.py` there is byte-identical to this PR's base. "With fix" is the same image with this PR's files copied in (together with #63878 and #63879, which do not touch this path). title: [Feat][BI][1/N] add batch-invariant DeepSeek V4 support (top-k order)
summary: When VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is enabled, sort the sparse attention indexer's selected KV indices before attention. This avoids reduction-order differences when top-k returns the same tokens in a different order, while keeping -1 padding at the end. The default path is unchanged, and ties at the top-k cutoff are still not resolved. Adds tests for ordering, padding, buffer preservation, and native prefill/decode top-k outputs.

title: [Bugfix] Inherit target --revision/--code-revision for MTP draft; readable error for n_predict=0
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61197: with `method="mtp"` and no explicit draft model, the draft is the target checkpoint itself, but the draft `ModelConfig` was built with the speculative config's own (unset) `revision`/`code_revision`, so config and weights resolved from the repo's default branch instead of the target's `--revision`. This PR inherits both from `target_model_config` (unless explicitly overridden), mirroring the existing `model`/`quantization` inheritance. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Apply draft overrides atomically and name all2all conflicts
summary: ## Overview `SpeculativeConfig.apply_draft_overrides` rebuilds the target's `VllmConfig` once per draft override. Each rebuild runs `VllmConfig.__post_init__` and therefore `KernelConfig.set_platform_defaults()`, which resolves and validates `parallel_config.all2all_backend` against the MoE backend of that partially overridden config. When the target's MoE backend dispatches and combines its own experts (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`), the target binds `all2all_backend="passthrough"`. title: [Attention][Spec Decode] Capture varlen graphs at the split-K request bound
summary: ## Overview Adaptive verification's varlen decode CUDA graphs are captured with one request per token, so the Triton split-K gate sees a request count up to K+1x the real one and small verification batches replay the 2D kernel. This captures each varlen token size a second time at the largest request count the attention builders still admit to split-K, and dispatch prefers that graph when the real batch fits. Fixes #66557. ## Claims - Qwen3-8B + DFlash2 K=7, c8, `TRITON_ATTN`, H200: attention 2,050 -> 1,022 us/step (`reduce_segments` restored, 0 -> 215 us), step 8,648 -> 7,970 us, unprofiled 30 s reference throughput 2,675 -> 2,869 tok/s. Fixed K=7 measures 2,936 tok/s and 1,026 us/step. - Gemma4-31B-it + DFlash2 K=7, c8: attention 3.21 -> 2.51 ms/step, matching the fixed-K kernel (2.49 ms). - Gemma4-31B serve A/B, 3x60 s per point, c1/c8/c16: AV vs fixed at c8 improves from -2.8% to -0.6%, with overlapping run ranges. - Fixed-K capture, non-AV paths and the speculator graph managers are unchanged. The target graph set grows 28 -> 40 (+12, only token sizes below the bound times the query length), capture 0.85 s -> 1.2 s. ## Validation Unit tests: ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py -q 40 passed .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py -q -k "splitk or geometry or threshold or scratch" 5 passed ``` Kernel evidence, Qwen3-8B + DFlash2 K=7 at c8 with `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, one nsys pass per arm, throughput from the 30 s unprofiled AIPerf reference inside that pass: | | fixed K=7 | AV before | AV
