title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Settle decoder pull preparation failures
summary: ## Overview Mooncake decode now reports pull-preparation failures through the existing KV load failure path, instead of leaving the request waiting for a transfer that never started. ## Claims - Topology, rank-map, empty-worker, and pull-metadata encoding errors are reported with `_handle_failed_recv` before any producer I/O. The scheduler then applies the existing `kv_load_failure_policy` (default `"fail"`, or `"recompute"`). - One peer's preparation failure does not finish a request while another peer is still running, and does not release that peer's destination blocks early. - Cancelling a receiver before the pull is sent fails the request. Cancelling it after the pull is sent logs the error and keeps the destination blocks; that is not treated as remote write completion. - This does not duplicate #65575. That PR fails a pull that was already sent when the prefill worker is lost. This PR covers failures before the pull is sent. ## Validation Recorded on the parent commit, same new tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py -k 'decode_preparation_failure or decode_metadata_encoding_failure or decode_cancelled or decode_cancellation_after' -q ``` Result on the parent: **9 failed, 1 passed**. Failures were the real `AssertionError: Remote tensor parallel size 3 is not divisible by local tensor parallel size 2`, `KeyError: 0`, and `UnicodeEncodeError`, plus `Task exception was never retrieved`. The requests waited until timeout. The existing per-peer socket preparation error still passed and still does not release blocks

title: [Perf] Keep H2D transfers dense in fused-MoE weight loading
summary: ## Purpose Fix the root cause of #31624: ModelOpt Llama-4 (Scout/Maverick FP8) checkpoints take 68s-495s to load depending on hardware, dominated by H2D copies from non-contiguous CPU tensors. These checkpoints store expert weights fused as `[num_experts, hidden_in, hidden_out]`. `Llama4Model.load_moe_expert_weights` transposes to the runtime orientation with a stride-only view, so `RoutedExperts._load_w13`/`_load_w2` end up calling `expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)` with a non-contiguous CPU source. ATen materializes `src.contiguous()` on the CPU first, and for fp8 that gather has no vectorized path, so it costs 3-4s per expert tensor. That is where the load time goes. Per https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31624#issuecomment-3706297841, the fix should keep the CPU weights contiguous rather than move checkpoint tensors to the GPU. This PR does that by flipping the strided side of the copy to the destination: ```python expert_data.transpose(-1, -2).copy_(loaded_weight.transpose(-1, -2)) ``` `loaded_weight.transpose(-1, -2)` undoes the earlier view and recovers the contiguous on-disk slab at zero cost, so the H2D transfer is dense. The layout transform runs as a strided device-side write into the existing parameter storage. No copy of `loaded_weight` is retained in GPU memory at any point; ATen's transient staging buffer is allocator-managed inside the copy op. TP-narrowed slabs (unit inner stride, padded row pitch) degrade to host row-run memcpys instead of an elementwise gather and then take the same dense path. title: [Kernel] Fuse the elementwise chain around get_top_tokens' all-gather
summary: ## Overview Speculative decoding picks each draft token with an argmax over the vocabulary, and `use_local_argmax_reduction` shards that argmax so the all-gather carries `[batch, 2]` instead of `[batch, vocab]`. The sharded path then spends the saving on eight elementwise kernels that pack and unpack the gathered pairs, which made it slower than a full-vocab argmax below ~26 rows. This PR replaces that chain with one Triton kernel on each side of the all-gather. **8x MI325X: 1.26-1.33x at 1-128 rows, never slower. Beats a full-vocab argmax at every size (1.11-3.35x). Bit-identical.** **4x MI300X, TP=4: 1.11-1.27x at 1-128 rows, worst 1.02x. Beats a full-vocab argmax at every size (1.04-3.14x). Best of 4 recorded passes. Bit-identical.** ## Claims - 8x MI325X: 1.26-1.33x vs the old chain from 1 to 128 rows (worst 1.00x); 1.11-3.35x vs a full-vocab argmax. - 4x MI300X, TP=4, best of 4 recorded passes: 1.11-1.27x vs the old chain from 1 to 128 rows (worst 1.02x); 1.04-3.14x vs a full-vocab argmax. - Output is bit-identical to the ops removed, at all 9 sizes, on both machines. ## Validation ```bash # 8x MI325X docker run -it --rm --network host --ipc host --group-add video \ --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505 bash torchrun --nproc-per-node=8 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_local_argmax.py --breakdown pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_local_argmax_kernels.py ``` `before` is the pre-change body of `get_top_tokens`, run in the same process. ``` rows f

title: Optimize sliding window prefix cache hit search
summary: ## Summary Optimize `find_longest_cache_hit` in `SlidingWindowManager` to reduce lookup complexity from O(max_num_blocks) to O(max_num_blocks / stride) for low cache hit rate scenarios. ## Motivation The current implementation scans every block from right to left, costing up to `max_num_blocks` `BlockPool.get_cached_block` lookups even when the cache is cold. For a 128K-token request with a 4K window, this performs ~8192 lookups (block_size=16) although a hit only needs `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) = 256` contiguous blocks. ## Changes - **Stride-based probing**: Probe every `stride = sliding_window_contiguous_blocks` blocks from the right - **Right expansion on hit**: On a probe hit, expand right (at most `stride - 1` blocks) to verify - **Aligned jumps on miss**: After a miss at `idx`, resume at the next aligned edge below `idx - 1` - **Direct cached-prefix fallback**: Compute the cached-prefix fallback directly instead of full scan ## Performance From issue #62336 benchmarks: | pattern | main lookups | proposed lookups | main time | proposed time | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | cold cache | 8192 | 33 | 4.49 ms | 0.021 ms | | 1% random cached | 8192 | 33 | 4.61 ms | 0.021 ms | | tail hit / full cache | 256 | 257 | 0.23 ms | 0.23 ms | | adversarial (cached blocks on probe lattice) | 8192 | 128 | 4.63 ms | 0.11 ms | The worst case remains O(max_num_blocks), but the common low-hit-rate case becomes O(max_num_blocks / stride). ## Testing - Syntax verified with `python3 -m py_compile` - Existing tests should pass (will be verified in CI) --- <a href="https://app.blacksmi

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep cache-registered Mamba states out of retirement
summary: ## Purpose In `mamba_cache_mode=align`, state retirement currently also retires the boundary state that the prefix cache serves hits from. A later request can then match a long prefix with the attention groups and find no recurrent state to resume from, so the match is dropped and the prefix is recomputed. `MambaManager.remove_skipped_blocks` reaches `_remove_blocks_in_range(request_id, 0, num_skipped_blocks)`, and `MambaManager.get_num_skipped_tokens` returns `num_computed_tokens - 1`, so the range covers nearly every block of the request. For the sliding-window managers that the base method was written for, a block below the window can never serve that request again, so retiring it is safe. Mamba differs: "skipped" means *this request's next forward pass* does not need the state, and a later request that shares the prefix resumes from exactly those blocks. Concretely, with the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, `reachable_block_mask` hashes the replay boundary at `(num_prompt_tokens - 1) // block_size`. Once decode passes the prompt length, `num_computed_tokens - 1` exceeds `num_prompt_tokens - 1`, so that block falls inside the retired range. It is released and replaced by `null_block` in the owning request's table, and under load the pool reclaims it before a later request can resume from it. This PR keeps retirement and skips only the states registered while the prompt was still being processed: ```python hashed_at = block.block_hash_num_tokens return hashed_at is not None and hashed_at <= num_prompt_tokens ``` Anything wider would fight `prefix_cache_retenti

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Port cross-layer index top-k sharing to the NVIDIA path
summary: ## Summary Adds opt-in **cross-layer sharing** of the lightning-indexer top-k selection to the NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 path, porting #47269 (AMD-only until now). When `use_index_cache` is set, only 1 of every `index_topk_freq` sparse-attention layers recomputes the indexer score + top-k; the rest reuse the selection the preceding compute layer wrote into the shared `topk_indices_buffer` in the same forward pass. Adjacent sparse layers pick nearly the same blocks, so this cuts the indexer cost ~`freq`×. The skip decision is computed once per layer at construction (static → cudagraph-capture-safe). **Disabled by default.** Enable via: ``` --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}}' ``` (`text_config` nesting because MiniMax-M3.1-Flash is a VL config; a top-level `use_index_cache` is rejected by the config guard.) ## Why this isn't a duplicate #47269's notes explicitly invite this NVIDIA follow-up ("The NVIDIA twin can take the same change as a follow-up"); no open PR implements it (re-checked 2026-11-05 across `index_topk_freq` / `use_index_cache` / minimax top-k / #47269 cross-refs). The NVIDIA-side top-k reuse PRs that do exist target a different model (GLM-5.2 #53562 / #49678). ## Test plan / results `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (NVFP4), 8xH200, TP=4, marlin MoE backend, `index_topk_freq=4`, offline `LLM` with random-token prompts (1 warmup + 3 timed reps, greedy, `ignore_eos`): - **Perf (decode TPOT)** — −5.3% to −8.4% across ISL 2k-32k; a second independent boot per side (real KV + prefix caching) reproduces −5.3/−5.4/−5.8/−6.4% on the same four v

title: [RFC]: Scheduler-owned persistent state, initially for cache-aware streaming RNN-T ASR
summary: ## Motivation. This RFC proposes support for stateful, cache-aware streaming RNN-T models such as [NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 ASR](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b), requested in [Issue #47455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47455). These models process potentially indefinite audio streams, so they need to carry acoustic and decoder state between chunks without letting memory grow with the recording. That state includes encoder attention and convolution caches, predictor state, and decoding progress. To support these models, vLLM needs to preserve each session’s GPU state while batching computation across ready sessions and returning incremental results through its existing serving system. We propose scheduler-owned persistent state, with Nemotron as the first consumer through an extension of the [existing Nemotron plugin](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59827). The scheduler in vLLM core would allocate a state buffer to each session, keep it assigned between chunks, and release it after the session ends and its outstanding GPU writes finish; the plugin would compute the state updates. ### RFC suite: from engine state to a complete deployment We have three related RFCs for a full implementation of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR with a Riva gRPC frontend: | RFC | Responsibility | Associated implementation | |---|---|---| | [1 — Persistent session state #65543](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65543) | Core owns state allocation, admission, and safe release; Nemotron starts as a model plugin. | [vLLM #67374](https://github.co

summary: ## Overview This makes the saturation escape of `--prefill-schedule-interval` (#44558) DP-global. Today a capacity-bound rank prefills on every step and sets the lockstep step time for all ranks, while the other ranks keep their own prefill deferred. With this change, every rank releases prefills on those steps. Fixes #67688, which has the root cause and the measurements. title: [Performance]: DP prefill cadence: a capacity-bound rank prefills alone while its lockstep peers keep deferring
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance **Problem.** With `--prefill-schedule-interval N` on a data-parallel MoE engine, the cadence is aligned across ranks (`step_counter` is identical on every rank), but the saturation escape from #44558 is not. A rank whose last prefill step left requests waiting (`Scheduler.prefill_capacity_bound`) stops deferring and prefills on every step. DP ranks step in lockstep through the MoE collectives, so that rank's mixed steps set the step time for every rank. The other ranks keep their own waiting requests and started prompt chunks deferred until the next cadence step, so they wait out the long steps without getting their prefill done. Under bursty long-context load, at least one rank is capacity-bound on most off-cadence steps. #62901 describes the same lockstep effect and proposes the opposite remedy: between cadence steps, hold every rank unless at least K ranks have prefill work, overriding the per-rank escape (with a fail-open after 8 backlogged releases). #61834 (closed) described it too. **Proposal (minimal).** Keep the stock guard and the cadence, and make the escape DP-global. Once per step, OR each rank's `prefill_capacity_bound` over the DP group. Between cadence steps, all ranks release prefills when any rank is capacity-bound. A rank that is already paying for a long mixed step then does its own prefill in it. title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep dummy-run requests within max_model_len
summary: ## Overview `_dummy_run` can build dummy requests longer than `max_model_len`. Attention then reads block ids past the end of the block table row during warmup, which can crash engine startup. This PR caps the dummy batch at `num_reqs * max_model_len` tokens. It follows up on #49751. ## Claims - Warmup dummy runs no longer read past the block table when `max_num_batched_tokens > max_num_seqs * max_model_len`. - This fixes a startup crash with, for example, `--max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, and the latent out-of-bounds read behind `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `FlashAttnFwdSm90` in `test_auto_fit_max_model_len_rejects_oversized_input`. - Configs where the cap does not apply run the same dummy batches as before. ## Validation All GPU runs on one H200, `JackFram/llama-160m`, main at 379a8487a. Minimal reproducer (no auto-fit involved): ```python from vllm import LLM if __name__ == "__main__": llm = LLM( "JackFram/llama-160m", max_model_len=2048, max_num_seqs=1, max_num_batched_tokens=8192, ) print(llm.generate("Hello")[0].outputs[0].text) ``` vLLM accepts this config with a warning. title: [Bugfix][Compilation] Remove AllReduceFusionPass.__del__ destroying shared workspace
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #67629. `AllReduceFusionPass.__del__` in `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py` unconditionally called `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()` when a pass instance was garbage-collected. summary: ### The feature, motivation and pitch Reasoning models can enter an exact repeating token cycle inside a reasoning section and run to `max_tokens`. The existing `SamplingParams.repetition_detection` finishes the whole request, losing the answer; `thinking_token_budget` limits the length but spends the budget before intervening. It matches the existing `RepetitionDetectionParams` / `check_sequence_repetition` semantics. - Work is bounded to `loop_break_max_pattern_size * loop_break_min_count` tokens, after `loop_break_min_reasoning_tokens` and at `loop_break_check_interval` accepted-token intervals. - Server configuration uses `loop_break_*` fields on `ReasoningConfig`, via `--reasoning-config`. It is disabled by default. `thinking_loop_break: false` opts a request out; `"force"` and `"ramp"` select the release when the server has enabled the feature. - `force` writes `reasoning_end_str` through V2's budget-forcing path. title: [Core] Route by exact in-flight count when a single client owns the DP engines
summary: ## Overview With one API server, `DPLBAsyncMPClient` routes by `max(inflight, waiting + running)`, where the second term is the coordinator's step-boundary snapshot. The snapshot lags the client's exact in-flight count, so the engine that just freed a slot ties with the full engines, and the rotating tie-break sends the replacement to a full engine (DP-1)/DP of the time. Under closed-loop load one engine then runs one request over and one engine one under for a whole round, and lockstep DP+EP decode waits for the fuller one. Related: #43279 (power-of-two choices, open), #59017 (session affinity, merged), #49204 (exact in-flight counts). #58070 (open, with #61386 as its plumbing stage) changes the same score with result-metric penalties and a superlinear in-flight term behind an env flag; whichever lands second will need a rebase, and this PR changes only the single-client case. ## Claims - When `client_count == 1`, engines are scored by `inflight` plus the unchanged KV-pressure waiting penalty; the snapshot's `waiting + running` only breaks ties between equal in-flight counts, and the rotating scan start stays the final tie-break. - With several API servers the score is unchanged. Explicit `data_parallel_rank`, late-interaction stickiness and session affinity are untouched. - On DP8/EP8 MI355X with uniform 8k/1k requests: +2.2% throughput at c256 on main, neutral at c1024. Not a win on every workload (chat-like prompts are flat, see below). ## Validation Imbalance before the change, DP8/EP8, 8k/1k random, closed loop: share of steps with some rank above ceil(c/8) was 56% at

summary: ## Overview With `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs, Inkling on ROCm can hit a GPU memory fault in `fused_moe_kernel` once a few requests decode concurrently (`--enforce-eager` avoids it). Decode graphs are replayed at fixed batch sizes, so 3 live requests run in the batch-4 graph with one padding row. That row has `cache_seqlens` 0 and belongs to no request, but its attention output flows through the residual into the MoE gate, and two paths can leave NaN there. A NaN gate logit can make top-k return an index past the routed experts. Related: #61413 (open) moves this code to `inkling/common/`; both bugs are still in its version, and we are happy to rebase onto it or have it fold this in. ## Claims - Split-KV decode: `_split_kv_stage2` combines zero splits for an empty row and stores `acc / row_sum` = 0 / 0. title: [Bugfix] Reject shape mismatches in ShardedStateLoader instead of partially loading (fixes #61681 mechanism)
summary: ## Purpose Fixes the silent wrong-output mechanism behind #61681. `ShardedStateLoader.load_weights` loads a saved tensor that is smaller than its parameter into a narrowed view of the parameter, and only logs a warning. The code comment says this is for LoRA padding. The rest of the parameter keeps whatever was in memory, and nothing raises. That happens whenever a `sharded_state` checkpoint is loaded with a different parallel layout than it was saved with. One concrete case is `--mm-encoder-tp-mode`. With `weights` (the default), the vision tower is TP-sharded. With `data`, every rank holds the full tower. A checkpoint saved from a `weights`-mode engine and served with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` therefore gets a vision tower that is half real weights and half uninitialized memory. Requests succeed, the text side is fine, and image answers are wrong. That matches #61681. This PR makes the loader raise a `ValueError` on any shape mismatch, naming the tensor, both shapes, and the likely cause. Tensors larger than the parameter already failed in `copy_`. They now fail with the same clear message. **Why dropping the narrowing is safe:** LoRA no longer pads parameters (there is no `lora_vocab_padding_size` on main; vocab padding is `DEFAULT_VOCAB_PADDING_SIZE` with or without LoRA). I also checked it directly. Saving a sharded checkpoint without LoRA and loading it with `enable_lora=True` takes zero narrowing paths, and greedy output is identical to `--load-format auto`. That is the same scenario as `test_sharded_state_loader[enable_lora=True]`, run on Qwen3-0.6B at TP=2, v0.31

title: [Perf] Enable cadence-aligned prefills for DEP
summary: ## Overview In data-parallel expert-parallel (DP+EP) serving, ranks share MoE execution and advance in lockstep. A rank that continues prefill work on a throttled step can delay decode progress on its EP peers, including when its local queue is full or it has no local decode request. When prefill throttling is active and both DP and EP are enabled, defer prefills on every off-cadence step. This keeps the prefill cadence aligned across ranks and lets peers make decode progress. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: fold per-shard weight global scales of merged layers into the block scales
summary: ### Purpose When vLLM merges linear layers (q/k/v, gate/up, or a model-specific merge such as Kimi-Linear's `in_proj_qkvgfab` or the Qwen3.5 GDN `in_proj_qkvz`/`in_proj_ba`), an NVFP4 checkpoint still has one weight global scale per original layer, but the kernels take a single one. The compressed-tensors, ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4 linear schemes keep the `max()` of the shard scales and log a warning. Every shard whose own scale differs is then dequantized with the wrong global scale, and its output is off by a constant factor. This PR folds each shard's global scale into its FP8 block scales at load time: - The rows of `weight_scale` that belong to a shard (found through `output_partition_sizes`) are multiplied by a factor <= 1, so that one common global scale gives the same dequantized values. The FP4 payload is untouched. - Because every factor is <= 1, the E4M3 block scales cannot overflow. The cost is one extra E4M3 rounding of each rescaled block scale, paid once at load time. On the checkpoints below, the result matches an exact per-shard output rescale. - If the rows do not line up with `output_partition_sizes`, or a scale is not finite and positive, the layer keeps the old `max()` and the old warning. This is the policy vLLM already uses for FP8 per-tensor scales (`requantize_with_max_scale`). It is also the approach #55073 takes for the MoE w1/w3 case (#54974). This PR covers the linear schemes, which #55073 does not touch; the two change different code paths. ### Where this happens - **Kimi-Linear (regression since #50000, v0.27.0).** #50000 merged `q/k/v/b/f_a_pr

title: [Tracking] Replace Marlin with Humming across NVIDIA architectures
summary: ### Motivation. Humming now covers the quantization formats Marlin serves (INT4/INT8 GPTQ/AWQ, FP8, MXFP8, MXFP4, NVFP4, MXFP6, plus INT8/FP8 activations) for both dense and MoE layers. Marlin is an SM80-era kernel: it has no architecture-specific paths for Hopper or Blackwell, and each new format or feature has to be added to it separately. The long-term goal is to make Humming the default weight-only / mixed-precision backend on every NVIDIA architecture, including Ampere, then remove Marlin features piece by piece and eventually Marlin itself. This happens gradually. Each step either flips a default where Humming is proven faster or equal, or removes a low-usage Marlin feature that Humming already covers. ### Proposed Change. **Phase 1: Humming default on SM90** - [x] #56997 Prefer Humming before Marlin backends on SM90 - [ ] #63265 Prefer Humming before Machete for 4-bit weights on SM90 **Phase 2: Humming default on SM100/SM103/SM110 and SM120/SM121**, per format where it is benchmarked faster or equal - [ ] #63561 Prefer Humming over Marlin for int4 g128 on SM100 - [ ] #63777 Prefer Humming over Marlin for MXFP8 MoE on SM12x - [ ] #65077 Honor FP8 activations for Humming linear on SM100/SM110 - [ ] Extend `_HUMMING_PREFERRED_CAPABILITIES` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/humming/priority.py`) to SM10x/SM12x once each format has perf data (dense + MoE, decode and prefill shapes) **Phase 3: Humming default on SM75/SM80/SM86/SM89 (Turing, Ampere, Ada)** - [ ] Benchmark Humming vs Marlin per format on A100/A10/L4/L40S/RTX 4090/T4, dense and MoE - [ ] Flip de

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Repeat-last default padding for `cu_seqlens` in multimodal CG
summary: ## Overview Follow-up to #64984. When an encoder CUDA graph replay has fewer sequences than the capture, the manager's default copy zero-fills the end of `cu_seqlens`. A zero after the real total offset makes the padded sequences negative-length. FlashAttn and the other non-FlashInfer ViT backends then produce wrong encoder output for the real items. This PR: - Changes the manager default for cumulative keys (`cu_seqlens`, `cu_window_seqlens`) so it repeats the last value (suggested by @Pb314314). Other buffers are still zero-filled. - Moves the FlashInfer `cu_seqlens` padding helper to `MMEncoderAttention.get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics`, next to `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, which builds that layout. It uses the same OOT dispatch as `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, so an OOT attention that changes the layout can also override the padding. ## Claims - Models fixed by the new default: - GLM-4.1V/4.5V and the models that inherit its config (GLM-OCR, GLM-5.3-Flash). - Qwen2-VL, when `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch` is set. - In both cases, video-enabled capture pads `cu_seqlens` to `max_frames_per_batch`, while image replays pad only to `max_batch_size`. - FlashInfer backend: the packed two-section layout still needs its own padding. These models now get it from `MMEncoderAttention.get_cu_seqlens_padding_logics`: - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, which previously registered `_pad_flashinfer_cu_seqlens_buffer` themselves. - GLM-4.1V. title: [Perf] Allow EPLB with modular TRT-LLM FP8 block-scale MoE
summary: ## Purpose `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular._supports_parallel_config` rejects `enable_eplb`. The gate came in with the MoE refactor vllm-project/vllm#32564 ("[MoE Refactor] Create MK for TRTLLM Kernels"). It has no comment, issue or error report. It matches the monolithic class, which routes inside the kernel and so only supports naive DP/EP and TP. The modular class does not route itself: it takes the router's EPLB-mapped physical expert ids, with `num_experts` / `local_expert_offset` in physical units. Its BlockMajorK weights and block scales stay expert-major, so EPLB's per-expert dim-0 moves are valid. This PR drops the EPLB rejection from the modular class. The monolithic class keeps its rejection. ## Test Plan - GLM-5.3 FP8, DEP8 on 2x4 GB300, `--all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `--enable-eplb` with the sync pynccl communicator, 16 or 32 redundant experts. - Agentic rollout benchmark: ~30k input / 6k output tokens, 24 turns, GRPO n=8, 65k context, 64 groups. - Correctness: GSM8K (n=123, greedy) before and after a KV-cache flood. ## Test Result | arm | tok/s/GPU | EPLB balancedness | |---|---|---| | no EPLB | 722 | 0.58 | | EPLB, 32 redundant | 804-806 (+11.6%) | ~0.95 | | EPLB, 16 redundant | 804 | ~0.95 | - The gain held across 16 and 32 redundant experts and across rebalance step intervals of 1000 and 3000. - GSM8K stayed within run-to-run noise (.90-.95). - Async EPLB over NIXL hung cross-node in our setup, so these runs used the sync pynccl communicator. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Perf][Core] Hash prompt-embeds blocks in parallel for prefix caching
summary: With prefix caching on, the engine hashes every `prompt_embeds` row into the block keys with SHA-256, one block at a time, on every request. Cached blocks still have to be hashed to be found, so a long prompt pays the full cost each turn: 2 GB of embeds at 262k tokens takes about 1.2 s. That time sits between `add_request` and scheduling. - `request_block_hasher` now hashes the embeds rows of all new full prompt blocks up front on a small thread pool, into the request's existing per-block cache. - hashlib releases the GIL for large buffers, so this scales with threads. The digests are the same SHA-256 bytes in the same order, so block hashes and prefix-cache keys are unchanged. >[!note] Full-context request (252,043 x 4096 bf16, 238 hash blocks of 1,056 tokens), median of 5: 1.20 s --> 0.21 s

title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Size the routed-experts row cache from one source
summary: ## Purpose The routed-experts row cache is sized in two places that disagree: - The scheduler (`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector._capacity`) keeps `num_blocks` KV blocks of rows, doubled when a KV connector is configured, and ignores `aux_output_config.max_bytes`. - The worker store (`initialize_output_storage`) uses `max_bytes` when set, otherwise `num_blocks * hashes_per_kv_block` objects, with no KV-connector doubling. So setting `max_bytes` only changed the worker: the scheduler still retained (and kept serving prefix hits for) as many blocks as the KV cache, and the worker store grew past `max_bytes` to hold them. With a KV connector and no `max_bytes`, the scheduler retained twice what the worker allocated. This PR adds `retained_objects(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)` as the single source for both sides. The scheduler capacity and the worker `max_bytes` are both derived from it. The routed-experts dtype and bytes-per-token computation are also shared (`get_routed_experts_bytes_per_token`), so the worker and the capacity computation cannot drift. Behavior changes: - `max_bytes` set: the scheduler now retains at most `max_bytes // object_nbytes` hash-block objects (at least one). - No `max_bytes`, KV connector configured: the worker store now matches the scheduler's 2x. - No `max_bytes`, no KV connector: unchanged. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py ``` `test_retained_objects_follow_max_by

title: perf: read checkpoint shards with one pinned buffer per IO thread
summary: ## Summary Draft. Reworks the `streaming` safetensors loader so that it reads a checkpoint the way a network filesystem wants to be read, and so that it reads only the bytes the rank needs. The loader used to read a whole shard into one pinned buffer, with the IO threads filling it in blocks, and filter the expert weights afterwards. Three things were wrong with that. **Pinning cost.** `cudaHostAlloc` pins pages at about 1.4 GB/s on an A100 - 22 ms for a 32 MiB buffer. Pinning a multi-gigabyte shard therefore cost seconds, once per shard, before a single byte was read. Now each IO thread owns one buffer, created once and reused for every shard, so the pages are pinned once for the whole load. **Read amplification.** The loader read the whole shard and filtered it afterwards, so under expert parallelism every rank paid for every byte of the shard: with 8 ranks, 8x. The tensors are now filtered before they are read, so the storage only moves the bytes the rank needs. **The reader's own choice.** A tensor is now read with a single `pread` straight into the thread's buffer, so the bytes are touched once instead of being paid for twice. ## What the measurements say All on a test deployment of an all-flash distributed file system, with the loader's own access pattern (many tensors, each read once, spread across the file). The absolute numbers are specific to that deployment; it is the ratios the change is based on. ### preadv beats mmap by 6x 8 files of 2 GiB each, one never-before-read file set per run: | strategy | throughput | |---|---| | mmap, 8 files concurrently | 231.58 Mi

title: [Quantization][MoE] Keep MXFP4 expert scales compressed on B12X
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview This PR adds an opt-in kernel config option to the b12x MoE backend: `b12x_moe_mxfp4_compressed_scales`. With it, eligible W4A8 MXFP4 layers keep their E8M0 block scales in a compressed scale format (CSF) in GPU memory. On GLM-5.3-Flash with TP2, each rank uses 3.53 GiB less memory, and the KV cache holds 30.6% more tokens. Depends on #65233. The first commit is that PR. Review only the last commit. This follows #64753, which keeps NVFP4 CSF checkpoint scales compressed. This PR reuses its CSF support and adds the MXFP4 part. ## Claims - Enable it with `--moe-backend b12x --kernel-config '{"b12x_moe_mxfp4_compressed_scales": true}'`. - When the option is off, vLLM does not change. - The mode uses the FlashInfer version that vLLM pins (`flashinfer-python==0.7.4`). title: [Perf]FA2: split-KV decode for sliding-window layers and spec-decode verify
summary: > PR description is generated by AI tool <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose FA2 `mha_varlen_fwd` splits KV only when it can swap the GQA group into the query rows: `max_seqlen_q == 1`, no sliding window, no ALiBi ([flash_api.cpp](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/af5422c5c24e2f464d394295c5b2f659f9332217/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp#L757-L766)). Sliding-window layers and spec-decode verify (`q_len = 1 + k`) miss this, so a small batch runs one CTA per (request, head): 10-20 CTAs on 108 SMs. Example: EXAONE-4.5-33B (window 4096 on 48/64 layers), TP4, MTP 3, 1 request at 128K: 3.0 ms per full-attention layer, 117 us per sliding-window layer, ~50 ms of a 70 ms step in attention. This PR sends small uniform decode batches to `fwd_kvcache`, the split-KV paged kernel in the same FA2 build. - Eligible: FA2, FULL CUDA graph, no DCP, causal, uniform `q_len <= 1 + num_speculative_tokens`, `num_reqs * num_q_heads < num_SMs`. - Global layers: `q_len > 1`, or `q_len == 1` for MHA/ALiBi (no GQA swap). Decided per layer. - Sliding-window groups: block table cut to the blocks the window can reach, lengths shifted to match. Fixed width, so the split count is the same at capture and replay. Refilled in `build()` and `update_draft_decode_metadata()`. - Only during graph capture: outside capture `fwd_kvcache` reads `max(seqlens_k)` on the host. - Off with adaptive verification and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. Related: vllm-project/flash-attention#176, #190 (#51320) add varlen split for `q_len > 1` in the kernel; they need an FA bump and do not cover sliding-window decode. #

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix pipeline-parallel loading and generation for LongCat-Flash-Lite
summary: ## Overview Serving the native LongCat-Flash-Lite model with `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` can fail before the first token. Only the first stage owns its n-gram embedding. During checkpoint loading, later stages pass the embedding weights to the generic LongCat loader. With dummy weights they get further, but still try to prepare token embeddings before the runner switches to intermediate tensors. This was found by auditing the native implementation introduced in #47857. The proposed Transformers backend migration in #53811 remains open. Searches for LongCat PP, the model state class and the observed exception did not turn up another fix for the native path. There is no dedicated tracking issue known. ## Claims - Later stages skip the first stage's n-gram checkpoint entries and use the default model state for intermediate tensors. - The first stage keeps its n-gram weight loader, history and input preparation. ## Validation **Review the two PP boundaries:** [checkpoint loading](https://github.com/tgghzyh/vllm/blob/72a3df415a8f3f970de24e9280505fdf09b9349e/vllm/model_executor/models/longcat_flash_ngram.py#L181) and [model state selection](https://github.com/tgghzyh/vllm/blob/72a3df415a8f3f970de24e9280505fdf09b9349e/vllm/model_executor/models/longcat_flash_ngram.py#L241). title: [Bugfix][Core] Reject KV cache block sizes smaller than tokens_per_state
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #67631. A `--block-size` smaller than a layer's `tokens_per_state` gave that layer a zero-byte KV page, and KV cache planning then divided by it. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Name the differing fields on a NIXL compatibility hash mismatch
summary: Refs #60124. Implements suggestion 1 from the issue: a NIXL compatibility hash mismatch now names the fields that disagree. Suggestion 2 (docs) is covered by #60176; suggestion 3 (a hint next to the "Turning off hybrid kv cache manager" warning) is left out on purpose, since it can only guess at the remote's config while the factor diff reports the actual disagreement at the point of failure. ## Overview The mismatch error used to print two bare hashes plus a generic list of things that might differ. When the divergence is implicit, like the issue's MultiConnector-prefill case that silently turns the hybrid KV cache manager off on one side, finding it meant diffing two full deployment configs by hand. The handshake payload now carries the compatibility factors alongside the hash, and the mismatch path diffs them and reports each disagreeing field, e.g.: ``` NIXL compatibility hash mismatch. Local: ac9aa5b3..., Remote: d6e05114.... Differing factors (local vs remote): is_hma_enabled: local=True, remote=False. Prefill and decode instances have incompatible configurations. ... ``` ## Compatibility - `compatibility_factors` is an optional payload field and msgspec ignores unknown keys, so mixed-version peers handshake fine in both directions: old decoders ignore the field, new decoders default it to `None`, and the error falls back to the previous message when a peer sends none. - Hash inputs are unchanged: `auxiliary_layer_ids` canonicalizes tuple to list, and `json.dumps` (the `hash_factors` serializer) renders both identically, so same-config peers produce the same hash acro

title: [Perf][Bugfix][RL] Fix sparse NCCL update OOM and improve performance
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Problems with `sparse_nccl` on main: - **Memory:** a worker keeps every patch on the GPU until the last one arrives, 6 bytes per changed element on every rank whatever the TP size. On the default config the extensible KV cache leaves about 3 GiB free, so a one-shot `send_weights` on Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 fails at 1.25% of elements changed, after some weights are already written. - **Time:** each tensor costs two allocations and two broadcasts, 37,734 per update on this model, and the `empty_cache` at the end of the update then releases thousands of cached blocks. At 3% changed these take 2.2 s of a 4.3 s update. - **Non-contiguous patch tensors** are broadcast as they are, so the wrong bytes are sent. This PR sends the update in batches of at most 512 MiB. Both ends cut it at the same patches with one `batches()` over the update's metadata, and a patch above the limit forms its own batch. - **Memory:** the worker applies each batch before receiving the next, so patch memory is bounded by the batch size instead of the update size. - **Time:** a batch is one broadcast of all its indices plus one of its values per dtype. The worker receives each into one buffer and splits it into per-patch views, so an update takes a few allocations and broadcasts instead of two per tensor, and leaves few cached blocks for `empty_cache`. - **Non-contiguous tensors:** the trainer concatenates each batch before sending it, so the wire always carries contiguous bytes. Since a batch is applied before the rest arrive, a worker whose batch fails to validate o

title: [Quantization][MoE] Keep NVFP4 expert scales CSF-compressed on the GPU with B12X
summary: ## Purpose Keeps the CSF-compressed routed-expert block scales of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` compressed on the GPU when the NVFP4 MoE backend is B12X: -2.57 GiB of weights, +18.7% KV cache on one RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, +2.4 GiB free memory on DGX Spark, GSM8K unchanged. Builds on #64312, which decodes CSF scales at load. Loading the checkpoint from the Hub also needs #64739 (shards under `tensors/`). At load, B12X re-encodes each rank's decoded scales with FlashInfer's `encode_csf_scales` and hands them to b12x as `CsfScalePlanes`; b12x expands only the routed experts' scales per call into one scratch per layer shape. Re-encoding the rank's slice needs no loader change and works for any TP size. The encoder uses the same base rule as the checkpoint, so the streams are as small as the checkpoint's. - Only B12X with NVFP4 activations keeps scales compressed, and only for layers with `weight_scale_encoding: csf`. Other backends, W4A16 and `csf_32x2_v1` keep #64312's decode at load. - On by default for `csf` checkpoints, which target memory-bound local devices. `--kernel-config '{"b12x_moe_uncompressed_scales": true}'` restores decode at load with the same kernels. - Not supported: expert parallelism (B12X is TP-only) and weight reloading of compressed layers (`NotImplementedError`, captured graphs read the first load's storage). ## Results Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local, MTP-3, B12X, base = main + #64739. | | DGX Spark (GB10) | RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W) | |---|---|---| | model weights (GiB) | 72.08 -> 69.51 | 72.06 -> 69.49 | | KV cache | fixed 8 GiB; MemAvailable +2.42

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Accept split KV blocks in the b12x backend
summary: ## Overview Hybrid attention/mamba models cannot use `--attention-backend b12x`: hybrid page alignment raises the KV block size above 128 (2176 in #62320), and b12x only accepted exactly 64 or 128. The worker already splits large manager blocks into the kernel page sizes a backend declares, and b12x declares 64 and 128, so this drops b12x's exact-size override and lets the standard split apply. title: [Bug]: FlashInfer metadata builder races under async scheduling for non-speculative models since #57214 (CUDA illegal memory access / GPU hang)
summary: ### Describe the bug Since #57214 (0376f8153, "Avoid blocking seq_lens GPU-to-CPU copy for pooling in FlashInfer metadata builder"), `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build()` skips the blocking `common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu()` whenever `num_speculative_tokens == 0`, and uses `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` instead: ```python if ( self._num_speculative_tokens == 0 and common_attn_metadata.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound is not None ): seq_lens_cpu = common_attn_metadata.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound else: with gpu_sync_allowed(): seq_lens_cpu = common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu() ``` The values are fine (the upper bound is exact without speculation). The problem is that the removed copy was also the only per-step host/device barrier on this path. `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan()` passes the wrapper's persistent `_pin_memory_int_workspace_buffer` to the planner, which fills it on the host and enqueues an async H2D copy into `_int_workspace_buffer`. With async scheduling, the CPU builds step N+1's metadata while the GPU has not yet reached step N's queued copy. Without the barrier, `plan()` for step N+1 rewrites the pinned workspace before step N's copy executes, so step N's attention kernels run with another step's plan. The gate is "no speculative tokens", not "pooling model". Pooling models default to async scheduling off (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), so they are safe. A generative model without speculative decoding, with async scheduling on (the default), is exposed. ### Symptoms - `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, reported asynchronously

title: [Bug] XPU qnorm/rope kernel: int32 overflow in the address computation past 2^31 q elements
summary: **File:** `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py`, lines 40-41 and 57 **Confirmed present in v0.27.1** (tag `6e448d0ea9bf`) and on `main`. ## Summary `tl.program_id` is left as int32: ```python token_idx = tl.program_id(0) # int32 head_idx = tl.program_id(1) ... q_base = q_ptr + token_idx * num_heads * HEAD_DIM + head_idx * HEAD_DIM ``` so `token_idx * num_heads * HEAD_DIM` is computed in 32 bits and wraps once `q` exceeds 2^31 elements. ## Evidence The boundary matches the arithmetic to within one token. `(num_tokens - 1) * num_heads * 512` versus 2^31 = 2,147,483,648, against what we observed on MUSA: | shape | max offset | | observed | |---|---|---|---| | 65536 × 64 | 2,147,450,880 | fits, by 32768 | **works** | | 65536 × 128 | 4,294,901,760 | overflows | fails | | 98304 × 64 | 3,221,192,704 | overflows | fails | | 98304 × 128 | 6,442,385,408 | overflows | fails | | 131072 × 64 | 4,294,934,528 | overflows | fails | | 131072 × 128 | 8,589,869,056 | overflows | fails | Failure surfaces as `RuntimeError: MUSA error: unknown error`. FlagGems' kernel runs correctly at every one of these shapes because it casts the program id. ## Fix ```python token_idx = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) head_idx = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64) ``` ## Note Not backend-specific — a 32-bit wrap will corrupt or crash anywhere. 131072 tokens × 128 heads is an ordinary prefill size for this model, so we suspect the implementation was only exercised at small shapes. The same is true of VLLM-1: both defects are invisible below a few thousand tokens.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Key dynamic-SD tier on the running batch, not per-step scheduled count
summary: ## Overview Dynamic speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`, #32374) expresses each tier's K as a function of batch concurrency, but the scheduler indexes the tier table with `len(num_scheduled_tokens)` — the number of requests scheduled in the *current step*. During a chunked-prefill ramp of a large wave, a step schedules only the newest request's prefill (1-2 requests) while the running batch is already large, so the lookup reads a tiny count and holds the whole wave at the K=max tier until the ramp completes. This change keys the table on `len(self.running)` — the formed batch the schedule is documented against. ## Claims - Tier selection becomes `dynamic_sd_lookup[len(self.running)]`: the K the schedule documents for a given concurrency is what the batch actually runs at, at every step, including ramps. - On the per-step key, the two counts diverge whenever a step schedules few requests against a large formed batch (chunked-prefill ramps, staggered arrivals); the batch then runs the K=max tier for the ramp's duration regardless of the configured table. - Regression test: a PP=2 staggered ramp whose running batch crosses the K=0 band while a step schedules only one prefill fails on base (K=3 emitted at running=5) and passes with the fix. ## Duplicate work check Searched open PRs for "dynamic speculative decoding", "num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size", "DSD tier": no open PR changes the tier keying. Related but orthogonal: #48944 (adds a context-length axis to the table), #54748 (schedule observability), #52087 (constant effective-K semantics). ##

title: [Bug][Perf]: flashinfer_autotune / _dummy_run never calls compute_logits, leaving FP8 LM-head GEMM un-autotuned
summary: ### Describe the bug During startup warmup, `_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs` in `vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py` (lines 453–495 on `main`) wraps `runner._dummy_run(...)` in `with fi_utils.autotune(...)`: ```python with fi_utils.autotune(tuning_buckets=tuning_buckets, round_up=True): runner._dummy_run( num_tokens=num_tokens, skip_eplb=True, is_profile=True, randomize_inputs=True, **dummy_run_kwargs, ) autotune_indexer_wq_b(runner.get_model(), max_tuning_tokens) ``` However, `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, lines 884–1036 on `main`) returns `(hidden_states, sample_hidden_states)` without calling `self.model.compute_logits(...)` (which is only invoked in `_dummy_sampler_run` at line 1044). `_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs` discards the returned `sample_hidden_states` and never calls `compute_logits` or `_dummy_sampler_run`. ### Observed impact For FP8 models using FlashInfer autotune (observed on vLLM 0.31.0): - The FP8 LM-head GEMM (e.g., `4096 x 131072`) is never autotuned during startup. - Serving logs 8 FlashInfer fallback warnings at runtime and falls back to the default CUTLASS kernel (~117 µs vs ~77 µs at `M=1` when autotuned). ### Suggested fix Run `compute_logits` (or `_dummy_sampler_run`) on `sample_hidden_states` inside the `with fi_utils.autotune(...)` block in `_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs` (when `sample_hidden_states is not None` / `runner.is_last_pp_rank`).

title: [Bug]: AllReduceFusionPass.__del__ destroys process-global FlashInfer all-reduce workspace while CUDA graphs / communicators still use it
summary: ### Describe the bug `AllReduceFusionPass.__del__` in `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py` (lines 1143–1147 on `main`) unconditionally calls `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()`: ```python def __del__(self) -> None: if getattr(self, "disabled", True): return with contextlib.suppress(Exception): destroy_fi_ar_workspace() ``` However, the FlashInfer all-reduce workspace is **process-global** (shared across compiled callables, captured CUDA graphs, and `FlashInferAllReduce` communicators). If an `AllReduceFusionPass` instance is garbage-collected while any compiled forward, CUDA graph, or communicator is still alive (for example, when dropping/rebuilding a compiled model or reloading AOT artifacts), `__del__` frees the process-global workspace out from under live CUDA graphs. ### Observed symptom On TP=2/4 with FlashInfer all-reduce fusion enabled, dropping and rebuilding the compiled forward while CUDA graphs are active causes an illegal GPU memory access on the next request. ### Expected behavior `AllReduceFusionPass.__del__` should not destroy the process-global FlashInfer all-reduce workspace; workspace lifetime should be owned by the communicator / process shutdown rather than an individual compiler pass instance.

summary: ## Overview This adds opt-in group-wide LoRA admission and residency for MRV2's internal MoE DP path. It follows the draft proposal in #65209. Stacked on #61714 and #63077. Other adapters wait; free slots can be reused while unrelated requests continue. - Register group-wide IDs so separate frontend counters cannot alias different adapters. - Load through the existing managers, retire GPU readers before replacement, and publish readiness only after every worker acknowledges matching source fingerprints. - Keep coordination out of the per-layer path and preserve existing adapter-buffer addresses. The feature is off by default. - Roll back rejected updates from retained CPU objects, restoring cache order and pins before admission resumes. Lost workers or failed restoration still fail closed. This does not duplicate the idle-preservation, residency-reporting, or slot-update work: it coordinates admission and eviction across engines rather than only managing each worker's local state. ## Validation Real OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct with four distinguishable expert-LoRA variant

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use the Triton fp32 router GEMM up to 128 tokens for small routers on gfx950
summary: **AI assistance:** this change was developed with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5.5); the tests and benchmarks below were run on MI355X (gfx950). ## Purpose On gfx950 the fp32 router logits are computed by `_rocm_fp32_router_gemm_kernel` for `num_tokens <= 32` (`_MAX_TOKENS`, also the cap in `fp32_router_gemm_dispatch_impl` and `rocm_bf16x3_router_gemm_dispatch_impl`). Above that the dispatchers fall back to `F.linear(x.float(), w)`, i.e. three kernels per MoE layer: a bf16->fp32 cast, a hipBLASLt split-K GEMM and its split-K reduce. MiniMax-M3.1 decode with speculative decoding sends 8 query tokens per request, so 5 or more concurrent requests (40..192 tokens/step) fall off the Triton path on every MoE layer (57 layers). Profiled at N=5 (40 tokens), rank 0, median of 60 decode steps: | router logits kernels, per layer | before | after | |---|---|---| | bf16->fp32 cast | 5.3 us | - | | hipBLASLt GEMM (`Cijk_..._MT32x32x32`) | 7.1 us | - | | hipBLASLt split-K reduce (`PostGSU16`) | 4.9 us | - | | `_rocm_fp32_router_gemm_kernel` | - | 7.7 us | | **total** | **17.3 us** | **7.7 us** | The router sits at the head of the routed-expert chain (topk -> sort -> GEMM1 -> GEMM2) that is the critical path of a decode layer, so the 9.6 us/layer (0.55 ms/step) shows up in the step time. This PR lets routers with at most `6144 x 128` weight elements (6144x128, 3072x256, 4096x192, 2880x128, 5120x16, ...) use the Triton kernel up to 128 tokens and adds a launch config for 33..128 tokens. title: [Bug]: Rejected LoRA reload replaces cached weights when all slots are pinned
summary: ### Your current environment - Main: `5ec99956ad4253e70a56c8c0179c5af14fef377d`. - Apple M1, 8 GB RAM, macOS 26.1; CPU, single rank. - Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.19.0. - Main Python sources with existing `0.32.0+cpu` native binaries. - `collect_env.py` fails in `get_pkg_version`: `assert get_platform() == "linux"`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug An in-place LoRA reload can raise `All items are pinned` but still replace the cached weights. Later activation uses the rejected replacement. This affects applications that call `LLMEngine.pin_lora` or `AsyncLLM.pin_lora`. Ordinary HTTP serving has no pin route. Ranran suggested reporting this upstream in [vllm-metal#1316](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-metal/pull/1316). Reproduction: 1. Set `max_loras=1`, `max_cpu_loras=2`. 2. The worker removes A and caches its replacement before activation checks whether a slot can be evicted. summary: ## Overview This PR adds five optional hooks to Model Runner V2's `BaseSpeculator`, so a speculator can verify drafts that are not a chain (a tree, for example), choose how many drafts each request verifies, and stop drafting when speculation stops paying off at large batch sizes. Each hook defaults to today's behavior, and the runner calls a per-step hook only when the speculator overrides it, so built-in speculators run as before. Model Runner V2 verifies drafts as a chain, and only built-in adaptive verification can change how many drafts a step verifies. A tree verifier needs to rewrite positions and attention inputs before the target forward, supply its own rejection sampler, and move the accepted path's KV and recurrent state afterwards. A speculator that finds drafting no longer helps needs a way back to plain decode. The hooks sit at points where the runner already branches. Builds on #62962; review the last 4 commits. Together the two let an out-of-tree speculator run tree verification on hybrid models. ## Claims - `make_rejection_sampler(sampler)` lets the speculator supply the verifier. The default keeps the chain `RejectionSampler`, and `ModelState.custom_sampler` still takes precedence. - `prepare_verify_inputs(input_batch, model_inputs, *, dummy_run)` runs before the target forward (in capture and dummy runs too), after positions, slot mappings and attention metadata exist. A tree verifier rewrites positions in place and stages what its attention backend reads. - `post_accept(input_batch, sampler_output, num_sampled, num_rejected)` runs after sampling, before

title: [Spec Decode] Add a registry for out-of-tree speculative methods and a linear-attention verify extension
summary: ## Overview This PR lets a plugin add a speculative decoding method to vLLM without a fork. A package registers the method from a `vllm.general_plugins` entry point, users select it by name in `--speculative-config`, and Model Runner V2 builds its speculator. On hybrid models, a registered method can also verify drafts that are not a chain (a tree, for example) in the GDN and Mamba2 layers, through a data-only `LinearAttnVerifyExtension`. **With no method registered, no new code path runs.** ```python from vllm.v1.spec_decode.registry import SpeculativeMethodSpec, register_speculative_method def register(): # a vllm.general_plugins entry point register_speculative_method( "my_method", SpeculativeMethodSpec(speculator_cls="my_pkg.spec:MySpeculator") ) ``` ```bash vllm serve <target> --speculative-config '{"method": "my_method", "model": "<draft>", "method_config": {"depth": 4}}' ``` A method vLLM does not ship needs a fork today, because `SpeculativeConfig.method` is a closed `Literal`, `SpeculativeConfig` forbids extra fields, and Model Runner V2 picks the speculator in a closed if/elif chain. On hybrid models the GDN and Mamba2 layers verify speculative rows as a chain, so a tree method cannot verify there either. This PR applies to `main` on its own. #62963 builds on it and adds the Model Runner V2 calls that a non-chain verifier also needs (a custom rejection sampler, verify-input and accepted-path hooks). ## Claims - `register_speculative_method(name, SpeculativeMethodSpec)` makes `method=<name>` valid. title: [Spec Decode] Verify tree-shaped drafts and size each step's drafts
summary: ## Overview vLLM verifies drafts as one chain per request. This PR lets any custom speculator from #63205 hand vLLM a tree of candidates instead, on the V2 model runner. vLLM verifies the tree, checks the accepted path on the GPU and commits it. The scheduler also asks the speculator how many drafts to run each step, so it can draft more at low load and less at high load. This works for every speculator, not one draft model. A plugin can turn MTP, DFlash or DSpark drafts into trees and size them per step, and it can run EAGLE-4, which drafts trees natively. vLLM ships no tree kernel. It keeps the state it already owns and checks what the plugin returns, and the plugin computes everything tree-shaped, the same way KV connectors move bytes in a cache vLLM describes. Builds on #63205. Replaces #62962 and #62963. ## Claims - A speculator plugin can verify trees through four optional parts of the contract: a per-step candidate budget (`candidate_budget`), a verify plan (`plan`), the accept walk (`tree_accept`) and keyed commit kernels (`spec_kernels`). Layers that verify trees come from the plugin too: an attention backend whose `tree_decline_reason` returns None, or a recurrent layer swapped in with `PluggableLayer.register_oot`. The docs page `round_contract.md` describes each part. - vLLM keeps the parts it owns: the scheduler's row budget, positions at tree depth, a `PagedKVLayout` description of each KV cache group, sampling the target's token at every row, and a device-side check, with no host sync, that the accepted path is a path of the plan. title: [MM][CG] Support ViT full CUDA graph for Intern-S1
summary: ## Overview Add ViT full CUDA graph support for Intern-S1 (`InternS1ForConditionalGeneration`) through `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`, for images and videos. Part of #38175. It follows the InternVL integration in #41759. HF-format InternVL3 checkpoints (`InternVLForConditionalGeneration`) are registered to the same class, so they get the encoder graph too. I ran the same parity and logprobs tests on `OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B-hf`, and both pass. So I added a docs row for it as well. ## Claims - Intern-S1 now captures and replays encoder CUDA graphs for images and videos when `cudagraph_mm_encoder` is on. Before this change, the graph manager was never built for Intern-S1, so its encoder always ran eagerly, with no warning. - Graph output is bit-identical to eager output on the same padded batch. I checked 6 cases on Model Runner V2 and on V1. - Accuracy is not lower. MMStar is 64.87% with the graph and 64.00% without, and 96.9% of answers are identical. Two eager runs that differ only in `max_num_seqs` both score 64.00%, but they still disagree on 26 answers. So the gap is noise. - Speed on one L40S is mixed: - Encoder replay is 1.68× faster for a 1-tile image and 1.24× faster for 2 tiles. Intern-S1-mini sends one tile per image by default. - From 4 tiles up, the vision tower is compute-bound. The graph is neutral there (0.99–1.02×). - A tile count between two budgets is padded up to the next budget. That costs 25–30% (0.68–0.76×). - In the offline `vllm bench mm-processor` run, the default power-of-two budgets make the encoder 18% slower at 1 image per request, and 7% slower at 4

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Size the MOSS-Audio profiling dummy to its audio budget
summary: ## Overview MOSS-Audio's profiling dummy is a 1 s clip, while its per-item audio budget is a 30 s clip (`DEFAULT_MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS`), so startup profiles 13 audio tokens per item instead of 375. title: [Docs] Document kv_load_failure_policy in MooncakeStoreConnector guide
summary: Closes #62866 ### What this does The MooncakeStoreConnector documentation doesn't mention `kv_load_failure_policy`. When running Mooncake as a shared prefix cache (or with single-node disk offloading), the default `"fail"` policy can cause requests to terminate silently with an empty response if a store node drops or a disk read times out. This PR adds documentation for `kv_load_failure_policy` and provides an example using `"recompute"` so vLLM recovers by computing missing blocks locally. It also adds a quick note clarifying that `MC_RPC_*` timeout variables are read by Mooncake rather than vLLM. ### Motivation & Scope I kept this change minimal (+19 lines) and placed it directly under `## KV Transfer Config` where users look for `--kv-transfer-config` options, keeping everything in one place without duplicating notes. ### Testing - Verified markdown rendering and header hierarchy. - Checked CLI syntax for `--kv-transfer-config`. *(Prepared with AI assistance and manually reviewed by me)*

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] SIGTERM only the managed engine's launcher so in-flight requests drain
summary: ## Overview On shutdown, `vllm-rs serve` sends SIGTERM to the managed engine's whole process group. The GPU worker processes exit on SIGTERM, so in-flight requests fail a few seconds after the signal instead of draining for `--shutdown-timeout`. This PR sends SIGTERM to the Python launcher only, which already drains and then stops the engine cores and workers in order. It keeps the process-group SIGKILL as the timeout fallback. ## Claims - On SIGTERM, `vllm-rs serve` drains in-flight requests for up to `--shutdown-timeout`, as `vllm serve --headless` does, instead of killing them when the workers exit. - A launcher that does not exit in time is still SIGKILLed with its whole process group, and the group is SIGKILLed once more after the launcher exits, to catch stragglers. - With the API server, `vllm-rs serve` now drains the API server first while the engine keeps serving, and stops the engine afterwards with the remaining budget, as `vllm serve` does. ## Validation Unit tests in `vllm-managed-engine`, with a shell-script launcher whose process tree stands in for the engine: - `shutdown_signals_only_launcher_and_reaps_process_group`: the launcher gets SIGTERM, its child does not, and the child is gone after shutdown. title: [Core][Spec Decode] Skip draft tokens instead of preempting under KV pressure
summary: ## Overview Under KV cache pressure, the V1 scheduler preempts another running request to make room for a decode's speculative draft tokens. When a decode's verified token fits in its existing blocks and only its drafts need a new block, this PR schedules that decode without drafts for the step. Preemption is now a last resort for when the verified token itself does not fit. ## Claims - A running request is no longer preempted just to make room for another request's unverified draft tokens. Preemption frees the victim's KV cache, so its work usually has to be recomputed later. - In the pipelined async-scheduler simulator from `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` (PP=3, 3 spec tokens, KV pressure), preemptions drop by 18% across a 48-scenario sweep on current `main`: 931 → 762 (1058 → 785 on the original base). - End to end (Qwen3-0.6B, ngram spec decode with k=4, KV pool sized below peak demand, measured on the original base): preemptions drop 25% (72.5 → 54.0 mean) and output throughput rises 3.1% (783 → 807 tok/s). The run ranges don't overlap. - Outputs are unchanged in the checks below. Spec decode stays lossless; the change only alters which draft tokens get verified in a given step. ## Validation Developed and benchmarked on `90c4a1a73`, now rebased onto `cfee9bc62b` (2026-11-13). Commits merged in between touched `scheduler.py`, but not the `allocate_slots` retry loop this PR edits; that loop is identical on both bases. title: [ROCm] Keep the extensible KV cache for fd-exporting KV connectors
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` rejects every connector whose `kv_cache_access` needs a single physical chunk, including `EXPORTS_FD`. The stated reason (UCX/RDMA cannot register driver-mapped memory) only applies to `REGISTERS`. This narrows the ROCm check to `REGISTERS`, so connectors that import the KV cache in another process through POSIX fds (e.g. `LMCacheMPConnector` in VMM mode) keep the extensible KV cache on ROCm instead of failing at startup. title: [RFC]: add chunked push for NixlPushConnector
summary: ### Motivation. With `NixlPushConnector`, the prefill instance (P) writes a request's KV cache to the decode instance (D) once the request finishes prefill. D then waits for the whole transfer before it can produce the first token. For long prompts under chunked prefill, most of the KV cache is ready several steps before the request finishes, but none of it is sent until the end. Chunked prefill push sends each step's newly completed prompt blocks while the request is still running, so most of the transfer overlaps with the remaining prefill steps. The gap between P finishing and D producing the first token shrinks accordingly. At fixed request rates on H100 (Qwen3-8B, TP1, 16K and 32K prompts), the p50 of this gap drops from 282–377 ms to 79–102 ms, and TTFT p50 by 6–14% against whole-request push. ### Proposed Change. #### Design principle: an optional optimization of whole-request push Chunked push changes **only when** blocks are written to D. Everything else is whole-request push: - **What is sent**: the same blocks as whole-request push. Full-attention blocks are mapped onto D's uncached suffix by the same tail alignment, and state blocks (later phases) use the same clipping and pairing helpers. - **Block lifetimes**: unchanged. A running request owns its blocks; preemption and abort free them as usual; a finished request holds them under the existing KV lease. No blocks are pinned. - **Completion**: D decodes only after the normal completion notification. That notification rides on the WRITE of the request's last blocks, which is submitted only after every earlier WR

This profiles the longest clip the default encoder cache admits and keeps every encoder call within one profiled dummy clip: clips are encoded in length-sorted groups that fit it, and longer clips in windows that reproduce the full-clip output. ## Claims - Fixes OOMs on main, one L4, default process layout with the extensible KV cache on, `max_model_len=32768`: at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, one 10-minute clip, 160 concurrent 5 s clips, and one 10-minute clip with 40 concurrent 5 s clips; at 16384 with `max_num_seqs=1`, one 27-minute clip. title: [Attention][KV Connector] FlashInfer: optional separate K/V head slots for unquantized KV
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds an opt-in `--attention-config.flashinfer_separate_kv_head_slots`. With it, FlashInfer stores an unquantized (fp16/bf16) KV cache with K and V as **separate head slots** (`num_head_slots = 2 * num_kv_heads`, content = `head_size`), instead of packing K|V in the content dim. This is the same split the NVFP4 KV cache already uses, and the same idea as ROCm attention and b12x. Under LBHNC, each page becomes `[K heads (H, N, D) | V heads (H, N, D)]`. The NIXL worker registers the K half and the V half of each page as two regions that step by the full page. A remote engine that keeps K and V in **separate per-layer slabs** then maps onto it region for region, with no post-transfer permute and no extra copy. ## Claims - New flag, off by default. Nothing changes when it is unset: the spec, layouts, kernels, NIXL regions, compat hash and the KV-update bypass are all as before. - With the flag on, a single engine resolves a block-contiguous layout (LBHNC). Before the worker fix below, the engine core collected layouts outside any config context and resolved LBNHC. - With the flag on, FlashInfer decode, prefill and mixed batches match the SDPA reference for bf16 and fp16 under LBHNC and BLHNC, including the KV write path. - Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, H100, `--enforce-eager`: the flag gives **bit-identical** logprobs (512/512 tokens over 8 prompts). With CUDA graphs and torch.compile, greedy text is identical (8/8) when both runs use the same KV layout. Against the default packed run, which resolves LBNHC instead of LBHNC, it is 7/8: the one d

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Mooncake: heterogeneous-TP support for hybrid GDN/Mamba models
summary: ### What Fix `MooncakeConnector` for **heterogeneous-TP** disaggregated prefill/decode (e.g. PP2TP2 prefill → TP4 decode) on **hybrid GDN/Mamba + full-attention** models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next family). Without these changes, het-TP transfer on hybrid models either fails region validation or silently corrupts the mamba/GDN state on the consumer side. ### Changes 1. **Register every mamba state with its real, unpadded byte length** (`register_kv_caches`). Because the conv state only influences the first `kernel-1` decoded tokens, the corruption shows up as a moderate accuracy drop with occasional empty generations rather than a hard failure. Falls back to a single conv region under the SD layout (homogeneous-TP whole-region copies are unaffected by layout). 3. **Whole-region copy when the consumer TP exceeds the KV-head count** (`consumer_kv_replicated`). title: [Bugfix] Fast-fail DFlash2 FP16 speculative decoding
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #55250. DFlash2 drafts inherit the target dtype. title: [Bugfix][MoE] Swizzle mxfp8 activation scales after DP/EP dispatch for FlashInfer CUTLASS
summary: FIX #42118 ## Purpose `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8` returns NaN logits for every request when `data_parallel_size > 1`. The failure is silent: the server stays healthy and generates at full speed, but completions decode to empty strings and GSM8K scores 0.000. The quickest check is a completions request with `"logprobs"`, which fails with HTTP 400 ("Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan"). The CUTLASS kernel expects mxfp8 activation scales in the swizzled 128x4 layout. The DP/EP prepare paths quantize with row-major scales so they can ride the a2a next to the hidden states, then swizzle afterwards, but that step only handled nvfp4. So mxfp8 scales reached the kernel row-major and it read wrong e8m0 block exponents. With dp=1 the scales are quantized directly into the swizzled layout, which is why the existing tests never caught this. The same gap exists in `naive_dp_ep.py` and in both `flashinfer_nvlink` prepare/finalize backends. This PR moves the nvfp4-only restore logic into a shared `restore_dispatched_scale_layout()` in `fused_moe/utils.py`, routes all three backends through it, and enables it for mxfp8 using the same fused `block_scale_interleave` kernel the nvfp4 path already used (bit-identical to quantizing directly into the swizzled layout, covered by the new test). Backends that take row-major scales (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`) pass through unchanged, and nvfp4 behavior is unchanged. title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Opt-in whole-row regions for GQA caches under block-outermost layouts
summary: ## Overview With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), every layer's page of a block sits in one contiguous row, but NixlConnector still registers one region per layer for full-attention (GQA) caches. A layer's consecutive blocks are then a whole row apart, so NIXL cannot merge them, and an 8k-token Llama-3.1-8B transfer is always 16,384 descriptors (32 layers x 512 blocks), however the blocks are laid out. This adds an opt-in, `kv_connector_extra_config={"whole_row_gqa": true}`, that registers one region whose block is the whole row (every layer's page), as packed MLA rows already are (#61074), so each block moves as one descriptor and adjacent blocks merge again. It is related to the "restrict to MLA" TODO in `register_kv_caches` but does not resolve it: there is no TP head slicing, and a whole-row decoder accepts only prefillers with identical rows. Not a duplicate: #60851 (open) coalesces MLA layer views, #60564 (closed) was an opt-in whole-row change for MLA/replicated layers that left non-MLA models alone, and #61074 (merged) packs MLA rows. This covers head-sharded full-attention rows at matching sharding. ## Claims - With BLHNC, the opt-in cuts an 8k Llama-3.1-8B transfer from 16,384 descriptors to at most 512 (one per run of adjacent blocks). - On one A100 with a fragmented free-block pool, against main with the same BLHNC layout: the median 8k transfer went from 72.3 ms to 5.5 ms (13.1x [12.7, 13.5]), and median TTFT was 70.0 ms lower [65.0, 72.3]. - In pull mode, a whole-row decoder rejects a prefiller whose rows differ (per-layer regi

title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Give Wide-EP headless nodes the KV config
summary: ## Purpose Wide-EP headless nodes are started without `--kv-transfer-config`, so no KV connector is created on them. - MoRIIO: ranks 8–15 never open their handshake and notify ports. title: fix(v1): keep spec-decode draft padding out of input_ids under async scheduling
summary: ## Overview Under `--async-scheduling`, the scheduler speculatively schedules step N+1 before step N's output exists (batch queue), so per-request draft counts come from placeholder bookkeeping rather than from step N's actual proposal. Draft rows carry `-1` padding beyond their valid prefix whenever a step schedules fewer draft tokens than the maximum, and `_combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens_kernel` writes the scheduled draft positions of `input_ids` from those rows unmasked — whenever the scheduled count exceeds the row's valid prefix, `-1` token ids land in `input_ids` and the embedding gather trips ATen's `vectorized_gather_kernel` device-side assert, killing the engine. Sync scheduling clamps draft counts to the actual proposal each step, so the assert fires only with `--async-scheduling`. Fix: the kernel substitutes the request's last sampled token (always a valid id) for any negative draft-row load, so padding can never reach `input_ids`. The substituted positions are desync artifacts that would otherwise crash the engine; committed tokens still come from the drafter's valid prefix and the sampler. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Verify pull reads against producer lease slots
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61229: a pull-mode decoder could decode another request's KV when the producer's lease lapsed before or during the READ. The producer now exports a per-request lease slot that the decoder reads after the transfer, and the KV is used only if the producer still held the blocks. Also fixes a second path to the same result: when a request id is reused on the producer (request id randomization disabled and the router retries with the same id), a late read notification for the earlier attempt was counted against the retry and released its blocks while the retry's decoder had not read them yet. Read notifications now carry the lease nonce, and the producer ignores those of an earlier lease. ## Claims - A pull whose producer released the KV blocks before the READ completed fails the KV load (`kv_load_failure_policy` applies) instead of returning another request's tokens. This covers a read that starts after the lease lapsed and a lease that lapses mid-read; the check uses no clocks or heartbeat accounting. - The producer ignores read notifications that carry the lease nonce of an earlier request with the same id, so a late reader can no longer release blocks that the current reader still needs. - With `kv_lease_verification` on (the default), a pull that cannot be verified fails as well (no lease fields in `kv_transfer_params`, slot READ failed), and an instance that cannot register its lease slots in DRAM fails to start. `kv_lease_verification=false` restores the old behavior. - TTFT and ITL unchanged at concurrency 1; at concurrency 16 median TTFT +1.3 ms (abou

title: [Bugfix] Keep DP dummy runs from writing Mamba/linear-attention state into live requests' blocks
summary: ## Purpose With a hybrid model (Mamba-style / linear-attention layers), prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`), FULL CUDA graphs and data parallelism, a DP dummy run can write linear-attention state into KV-cache blocks owned by other live requests. Those requests then read corrupted K/V and produce NaN logits. **When it happens.** An engine runs dummy batches (`execute_dummy_batch`) while its persistent batch still holds live requests. The usual trigger is `pause_generation(mode="keep")` with DP: until all DP ranks agree to pause, the paused ranks keep stepping dummy batches. RL frameworks use this for in-flight weight updates. In our runs that meant 2–56 dummy steps per pause, with every running request still in the batch. **Root cause.** In `GPUModelRunner._dummy_run` (FULL mode): - It commits the live block table to the GPU with `commit_block_table(num_reqs_padded)`, then builds attention metadata from it. - It calls `_build_attention_metadata(num_reqs=num_reqs_padded, ...)` without a separate `num_reqs_padded`, so the "fill unused rows with `NULL_BLOCK_ID`" range in `_get_block_table` is empty. Every dummy row keeps a live request's block IDs. - Dummy `seq_lens` are 1. In align mode `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` picks block index `(seq_len - 1) // block_size = 0` of each row's mamba block list. For a long request, entry 0 is an old state block that the allocator has since freed and reused, often as another request's attention block. - Attention KV writes are disabled for dummy runs (`slot_mapping = -1`), but the mamba/GDN kernels have no such guard. title: [Bugfix][Core] Set TRITON_CACHE_DIR at worker startup to stop Triton kernels rebuilding on every start
summary: ## Overview vLLM now sets `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` when a worker starts, so Triton's JIT kernels are cached under `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` instead of `~/.triton/cache`. Run the same `vllm serve` command three times: | | AOT compile cache | Triton JIT cache | | --- | --- | --- | | first run | miss, writes under `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` | miss, writes under `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` | | second run | **hit** | **miss**, falls back to `~/.triton/cache` | | third run | hit | hit | The first run compiles, which constructs an Inductor autotuner, and torch exports `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` as a side effect of that constructor. The second run hits the AOT cache, constructs no autotuner, and so nothing exports the variable. In most deployments this costs one extra Triton compile and then stops mattering, because the third run is warm. It becomes permanent when a container runs `vllm serve` once and that environment is then sealed into an image. The image carries `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` but not `~/.triton`, so every container started from it is a second run, and pays the Triton compile again. ## Claims - The second time vLLM starts against a warm compile cache, it rebuilds its own Triton kernels from scratch. It no longer does. On Qwen3.5-2B that was 172 kernels and 69 s. - Setting `TRITON_CACHE_DIR yourself still works: vLLM only fills it in when it is unset. - Inference is untouched: the call runs once when a worker starts, and the same prompt gives the same completion. ## Validation Qwen3.5-2B on an AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), running the same command three times in one environment: | second run | wall time | kernels comp
