summary: ## Overview The P2P producer released store pins, and sent `AbortAck` to the consumer, while its NIXL WRITEs could still be running. Neither cancelling the handle nor removing the remote peer stops a running WRITE with the UCX backend. This PR keeps the pins, and holds back `AbortAck`, until NIXL reports each transfer terminal. Addresses #59569 and the review on this PR. The consumer-side counterpart is tracked in #61532. ## Claims - `NixlTransport.cancel(mode="wait")` releases only transfers that are no longer `PROC`/`PEND`. Previously it reported running WRITEs as cancelled, because `release_xfer_handle` never fails for an in-progress UCX request. - A round whose store timed out, or which the consumer aborted, fails its jobs but keeps the pins of jobs that inflight transfers still read, until those transfers are terminal. Late completions settle each job exactly once, and new supply cannot restart such a round. - The abort drain no longer falls back to `cancel(mode="immediate")` + `AbortAck` after `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`. Past the timeout it logs once and keeps retrying. `AbortAck` is sent only when no transfer of the round can still write to the consumer. - Wait-mode cancel retries are paced to one attempt per round per 100 ms, shared by the store-timeout sweep and the abort drain. - When one transfer of a round fails, the round's other transfers are no longer cancelled with `mode="immediate"`. title: [Perf][ROCm] AWQ: keep awq_gemm for decode under torch.compile
summary: ## Overview Under `torch.compile`, the AWQ token-count heuristic in `AutoAWQLinearMethod.apply()` (`num_tokens >= 256` → dequantize + matmul, else `awq_gemm`) is specialized once at compile time and reused for every batch size. As a result, decode (M=1) also takes the dequantize + matmul path. This PR moves the dispatch into a registered custom op (`torch.ops.vllm.awq_linear`), so the heuristic is evaluated per call at runtime. ## Claims - Decode now uses the fused `awq_gemm` kernel again, instead of `awq_dequantize` (which writes the full fp16 weight to memory) followed by a large GEMM. - Decode throughput for Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-AWQ on an RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2.4): **9.5 → 29.8 tok/s** (~3.1x). - Prefill (M >= 256) and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` keep the existing dequantize + matmul path. Numerics are unchanged, since the same kernels are called. ## Validation - **Throughput:** `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-AWQ --max-model-len 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8` with default compilation (CUDA graphs on). title: [Startup UX]: Serial per-process Python imports across the API server → EngineCore → worker tree add significant startup time
summary: ## Summary One of the contributors to vLLM's cold-start time, beyond necessary warmup, is **Python imports that run one process tier after another**. `vllm serve` forces `spawn`, so the API server, then EngineCore, then the workers each start a fresh interpreter and re-import torch, inductor, transformers and most of vLLM (~10s per tier). Each tier waits for the one above it before it can start. A rough prototype that forks EngineCore and the workers from a pre-imported forkserver cut time-to-ready from **~50s to ~29s** on a toy config. This issue collects the measurements, the specific offenders, and a proposed direction. Related: #48193 (Cold Start roadmap). ## Setup - `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B -tp 2 --enforce-eager`, 2x H100, torch 2.13, transformers 5.17, Python 3.12, main @ c37f86e57. - Eager mode and a small model mean almost no real GPU work, so this isolates the overhead. - Each case was run twice, back to back. title: [Bugfix][SpecDecode] Honor scheduled K in the suffix speculator under dynamic speculative decoding
summary: ## Purpose The suffix speculator ignores the runtime `num_speculative_tokens` passed to `propose()` by dynamic speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`), and always drafts with the configured max K (`self.num_speculative_steps`). Dynamic SD schedules a per-batch-size K that can be smaller than max. The model runner already handles a smaller K correctly on the consumer side (`draft_tokens[:, num_spec_tokens:] = -1` in `gpu/model_runner.py`), but the suffix speculator still pays full-K compute on those steps: - `_corpus_draft` walks `tl.static_range(K)` voting chains per candidate slot, so the finalize kernel cost scales with K even when only k < K slots are consumed; - `_suffix_observe_kernel` / adaptive-verification confidence stats are recorded with `K=self.num_speculative_steps`, so per-position acceptance statistics are bucketed against full-K positions that were never drafted. Honor the scheduled K: mask the kernels by the runtime value (`K=k`, `K_PO2=next_power_of_2(k)`) instead of the configured max. Buffers stay allocated at max K (no re-allocation), and out-of-range slots are still dropped by the existing masks/fill, so only the first k draft slots are emitted. Also assert the value is in `[0, max]`, which turns silent misconfiguration into an immediate error instead of garbage drafts. ## Test Plan Correctness: existing `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py` passes untouched (K defaults to max when `num_speculative_tokens is None`, so the default path is unchanged). `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py`. summary: ## Summary vLLM has no launch configuration for the 2D unified-attention path on ROCm, so it falls back on defaults. On gfx1151 (Strix Halo) that leaves long prefill an order of magnitude below the hardware's bf16 peak. This series gives gfx1151 a 2D KV tile that matches the paged-cache block, a launch configuration for the 2D path, a wider query block for long prefill, and ranks `TRITON_ATTN` above `ROCM_ATTN` on gfx1151 so the tuned kernel is what gfx1151 actually runs. End to end on gfx1151 against `upstream/main`, TTFT improves in 20 of 21 model/prompt-length cells (−1.4% to −34.4%). The remaining cell, Gemma-2B-AWQ at 128 tokens, is flat (+0.2%). title: [RFC]: Clarify AMD target and architecture semantics across vLLM
summary: ### Motivation. This proposal grew out of preparing gfx1200 support for the [Octave RFC (#59773)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59773). While separating Octave's common dispatch from RDNA/CDNA implementations locally and reviewing the [gfx1151 enablement experiment (#65696)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65696), I needed to coordinate Python backend selection, C++ dispatch, and device compilation guards. title: [RFC]: DWDP: Distributed Weight Data Parallelism for MoE Prefill
summary: ### Motivation. **Central question: Can Distributed Weight Data Parallelism achieve higher sustainable prefill request throughput under strict TTFT SLAs than the best existing EP-based approaches on high-bandwidth scale-up systems?** MoE prefill commonly distributes expert weights across GPUs and dispatches token activations to expert owners. Efficient EP backends reduce communication costs, but dispatch/combine and coordination across ranks remain in the execution path. Unequal prompt lengths, prefix-cache hits, and request arrivals can leave ranks with different amounts of work. DWDP separates expert-weight ownership from request execution: expert weights remain distributed, while each GPU runs its own prefill batch and fetches peer weights for local MoE computation. High-bandwidth scale-up systems make this trade-off worth evaluating. There is relevant prior work in [TensorRT-LLM's DWDP design and implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/docs/source/blogs/tech_blog/blog19_DWDP_Distributed_Weight_Data_Parallelism_for_High_Performance_LLM_Inference_on_NVL72.md), the [TokenSpeed Kimi K3 AgentX report](https://lightseek.org/blog/tokenspeed-kimi-k3-agentx.html), and [SGLang's DWDP implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778). TokenSpeed's AgentX report evaluates a complete prefill/decode system with shared caching; its output-throughput gains do not establish an isolated prefill improvement at a matched TTFT SLA. summary: ## Purpose Fixes #52525. `moe_align_block_size()` guarantees expert grouping but does not guarantee the ordering of routed token IDs within an expert. title: [CPU] Support heterogeneous memory (DDR + HBM) NUMA nodes via hwloc
summary: ## Purpose Follow up to #65677, On CPUs with heterogeneous memory, vLLM currently recognizes only one NUMA node per CPU core, which can be selected with `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND`. On CPUs configured with SNC4 (sub-NUMA clustering) and containing two memory tiers DDR and HBM (Intel Xeon Max, SiPearl's Rhea1), the DDR nodes are attached to CPU cores, while the HBM nodes are CPU-less and have no cores assigned. `lscpu` does not report this layout, so it is only visible through `lstopo`/`hwloc-ls`. As a result, vLLM CPU workers cannot be placed on HBM memory nodes, and users cannot benefit from the higher memory bandwidth of HBM. This PR adds an hwloc-based topology path that: - parses `hwloc-ls --of xml` and maps each core to every NUMA node attached to it, including CPU-less HBM nodes, instead of a single node per core - lets users assign their own memory nodes to each vLLM CPU worker via `<CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODE>`, including HBM nodes - falls back to the existing `lscpu` path, which stays the default. hwloc is used only when the env var is set and `hwloc-ls` is installed, so there is no behavior change otherwise - works with `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` set to either `auto` or explicit core lists - picks an alternative memory node for a core when its default node is not in the allowed set, and stores the chosen node on the worker. Memory availability checks, error messages and KV cache sizing now use the node actually selected rather than the core's default node `hwloc-ls` becomes an optional dependency, needed only for this feature. ## Test Plan - Manual runs on <CPU mode

title: [Bugfix] Keep a 3 GiB extensible KV cache margin floor on CUDA
summary: ## Purpose With the extensible KV cache on by default (#56492), `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` on 8×H200 (`--tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel`, other settings default) runs out of memory on the first full 8192-token step. It fails on v0.34.0rc0, rc1 and rc2 (perf-eval `qwen3_5-h200`; it passed on v0.33.0) and on main's nightly perf-eval. ``` Memory after warmup: 87.15 GiB free, 0.03 GiB committed to the KV cache, 1.59 GiB kept for transient activations; 10240 KV cache blocks (84.38 GiB) fit within the requested 139.8 GiB. Torch may reserve up to 50.66 GiB. ... MemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.26 GiB. GPU 2 has a total capacity of 139.80 GiB of which 1.29 GiB is free. ... 50.66 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 48.37 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, ... and 1.50 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. ``` The failing allocation is FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE's per-call workspace (`FusedMoeRunner::getWorkspaceInfo` → torch allocator). The measured allocated peak (1.59 GiB) already includes that workspace. What the margin doesn't cover is fragmentation: on the first real step, 1.50 GiB ends up reserved but unallocated. With a 1 GiB floor, torch may grow by only about `1.19 + 1.59 − 0.5 ≈ 2.27 GiB` after the KV cache extends, but the step needs about 2.77 GiB. This raises the CUDA margin floor to the 3 GiB that ROCm already uses. #60570 (reusing the CUTLASS MoE workspace across layers) would remove this particular transient, and it's complementary. ## Test Plan / Results 8×H200, v0.34.0rc2 release image (`8eda4909`), `vllm bench serve --data

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add spec config to shorten drafts on prefill-heavy steps
summary: ## Overview Add a new speculative decoding config, `num_speculative_tokens_under_prefill_load`, that shortens the draft length during prefill-heavy decode iterations, reducing TTFT and E2EL while incurring minimal (or even negative) TPOT degradation ## Claims By temporarily shortening the draft length of speculative decoding requests during prefill-heavy scheduling steps, more of the token budget is freed up for prefill. This reduces TTFT and E2E latency. If configured appropriately, the impact on speculative decoding TPOT is minimal, since prefill is compute-bound and draft tokens are frequently discarded. This feature has the greatest effect when `max_num_batched_tokens ≈ num_decoding_requests * (num_spec_tokens + 1)` within a scheduling step. As the relative gap between the two sides of that equality grows, the prefill budget gained from shortening the draft diminishes. ### Benchmarks * Model: [Qwen/Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) * GPU: RTX 6000 Ada Generation * The benchmark configurations set the relation between the max number of batched tokens and max number of speculative decoding tokens as ` 0.5 * max_num_batched_tokens = max_num_seq * (num_spec_tokens + 1)`. title: [RFC]: int8-key / int4-value per-token-head KV cache dtype (between int8 and int4)
summary: ### Motivation. The per-token-head family has `fp8`, `int8` and `int4`. Keys and values do not tolerate 4 bits equally: the attention scores depend on the keys, while the values average out over many tokens. An int4 cache loses most of its quality in the keys. Storing the keys as int8 and keeping the values at 4 bits recovers most of it for 392 bytes per (token, KV head) at head size 256, against 264 (int4) and 520 (int8, fp8). Measured KL divergence of the next-token distribution against a bf16 cache, Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune (hybrid, 16 full-attention layers, head size 256), 250k-token context, the K/V codec applied exactly as each format stores it: | format | KLD | bytes per (token, KV head), head size 256 | |---|---|---| | `int8_per_token_head` | 0.0011 | 520 | | `fp8_per_token_head` | 0.0023 | 520 | | int8 keys + int4 values (this proposal) | 0.0032 | 392 | | `turboquant_k8v4` | 0.0065 | n/a | | `int4_per_token_head` | 0.0093 | 264 | One model and one corpus, so treat the ratios, not the digits, as the result. KV capacity at equal memory on the same setup: 745k tokens for `turboquant_k8v4` and 650k for this format, so it costs about 13 % of capacity against turboquant for half the KLD. I searched the issues and PRs before writing this (queries on `int4_per_token_head`, `k8v4`, mixed key/value dtypes, the dtype registry): nothing proposes it. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] DSV4 Sparse MLA Optimization
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA on gfx1250, on aiter's packed-fp8 kernels over a 640 B aligned KV record, with every sparse-attention index list built once per step instead of once per layer. Index lists built once per step, no merge kernel.** All of a layer's caches are views into one allocation of 640 B records. title: [RFC]: Draft Window KV: Dual-Boundary Recovery and Sparse P/D Page Fill
summary: ### Motivation. Main attention requires the full reusable history, while a sliding-window Draft model reads only the most recent `W` tokens. In the original shared-pool design, Main KV and Draft KV share the same physical block pool, cache-hit boundary, and lifetime. This forces Draft to retain history outside its window. When Draft cache state diverges from Main, it can also trigger unnecessary target-forward replay, block allocation, and Main KV writes. The shared cache-hit boundary also couples Main reuse to Draft availability. A missing Draft page may move the combined hit boundary backward, preventing the system from reusing otherwise valid Main KV and causing unnecessary replay, block allocation, and Main KV writes. In a prefill/decode-disaggregated deployment, P and D may hold different Draft pages for the same request. Transferring the full Draft history or a coarse-grained contiguous range wastes bandwidth when D needs only a small set of logical pages. An internal production implementation validates the feasibility and potential benefits of this design. For the recovery requests that entered window replay, the actual replay range was reduced from 75.00M to 3.94M tokens, a 94.75% reduction. Under equivalent throughput, TTFT P50/P95 improved by 31.7%/47.9%, while the observed TTFT capacity knee moved outward by at least 7.7% in offered load. ### Proposed Change. This RFC proposes a Draft Window KV protocol that separates Main and Draft cache lifetimes and defines recovery when their cache states diverge. The proposed changes are: 1. **Independent Main and Draft cach

title: [Bugfix] Stop draft-only spec decode queries under PP and clamp the EAGLE sample index
summary: ## Overview With pipeline parallelism (PP > 1) and speculative decoding, the scheduler can schedule a request with only its draft tokens, with no bonus-token row in front of them. The code after the scheduler expects `num_draft_tokens + 1` rows per request. When all drafts are rejected, `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel` then returns `token_indices_to_sample[i] = query_start_loc[i] - 1`. That is -1 for request 0, and a row of the previous request for every later request. The target model's verification (`_calc_spec_decode_metadata`) reads the wrong rows too. This PR fixes the scheduler so it no longer builds that query. If a request's drafts follow a token that is still in flight, the request waits one step. It is then scheduled with that token and its drafts together. The PR also clamps the kernel's index to the request's first row, as the issue asks. Fixes vllm-project/vllm issue 60897 Compared with #60898, this fix: - Removes the draft-only query in the scheduler, where it starts. [60898](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60898) only clamps the kernel. On its tree, a PP=2 scheduler simulation still builds `{'0': 2, '1': 2}` with no bonus row, and target verification still reads `logits_indices [-1, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3]`. The new scheduler test in this PR fails on [60898](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60898)'s tree. - Gives the drafter the right row, not only an in-range row. With [60898](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60898)'s clamp alone, the index lands on a draft row of the same request, not on the row of the token the drafter must follow. W

title: [Bugfix][Core] Reserve only the blocks a spec decode step adds when admitting async KV loads
summary: ## Purpose With a KV connector doing async loads (P/D decode side, offloading) and spec decode enabled, a request whose remote-hit prompt needs exactly the free KV blocks is never admitted: the scheduler reserves a flat extra block for its first spec step even when that step fits in the block the request already has. The request spins at the head of `waiting` forever with no error. Follow-up to #57104 / #59880, found while testing the scheduler (not a production incident). ### Example - block_size 32, 4 usable blocks, `num_speculative_tokens=1`, max_model_len 128 - 1 request A: 126-token prompt, full remote hit (needs 4 blocks); nothing else running #### Step 1 — A arrives `allocate_slots(A, num_new_tokens=126, ..., reserved_blocks=0 inflight + 1 spec margin)` - A needs `cdiv(126, 32) = 4` blocks - free = 4, minus 1 reserved = 3 < 4 → `allocate_slots` returns None → `break` - result: ``` waiting = [A] A.status = WAITING (never reaches WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS) ``` #### Step 2 onward — Same cycle Nothing is running, so no block is ever freed. Peek `waiting` → A → same allocation → fails → `break`. Spin forever, and every request behind A waits too (FCFS). But A did not need the extra block: after the load, its spec step grows it from 126 to 128 tokens, which is still 4 blocks (2 free slots in the last block). The same happens for any prompt already at `max_model_len` (`allocate_slots` caps the slots, so the step adds nothing). ## Root Cause #57104 fixed the opposite mismatch (reserve too little → promoted request can't get its spec block). title: [Security] Fall back to eager when encoder CUDA graph replay exceeds capture
summary: ## Summary When encoder CUDA graphs are enabled, replay copies into fixed-size capture buffers. A legal video (or other multimodal) batch whose leading buffer dimension exceeds that capacity previously raised in the padded copy path and terminated the shared engine. Detect oversize replay tensors before the copy and fall back to eager encoder execution for that batch. ## Changes - `vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py`: add `_replay_exceeds_capture`; return `None` from `_run_budget_graph` when replay does not fit; fall back to `encoder_eager_forward` instead of asserting. - `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: unit coverage for the capacity check; GPU regression that oversized replay falls back to eager without crashing. ## Codepath coverage - All encoder CUDA-graph execute paths go through `_execute_local` → `_run_budget_graph` (including DP sharding and multi-path budgets). The guard sits on that shared sink. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open/merged PRs for `encoder_cudagraph`, `max_frames_per_batch`, `cu_seqlens`, and eager video fallback. Open draft #43403 proposes a related per-item `T > frames_per_item` fallback against an older single-path manager; it does not apply to the current multi-path `_execute_local`. This PR closes the sink model-agnostically on current `main` by comparing replay vs capture buffer shapes. ## Tests - `TestReplayExceedsCapture` (fits / exceeds / scalars-and-missing) - `test_eager_fallback_when_replay_buffer_exceeds_capture` (GPU; oversized captured buffer → eager) - Commands: - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_

title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE position preparation with PCP
summary: ## Summary Prepare M-RoPE coordinates from the global token positions carried by the current input batch. This allows the existing position preparation path to handle both standard execution and PCP-local fragments. The original kernel assumes each batch row contains contiguous tokens starting at the request’s `num_computed_tokens`. Under PCP, multiple fragments can share the same request index while starting at different global positions, so this assumption no longer holds. For example, fragments containing token positions `[0, 1]` and `[3, 4]` could both read columns `[0, 1]` when the request’s computed-token count is zero. Using `input_batch.positions` provides the correct global token positions directly from GPU memory, allowing the same kernel to handle both standard batches and PCP fragments. ## Changes - Pass `input_batch.positions` to `RopeState.prepare_positions`. - Use each token’s global position to gather prefill coordinates or compute decode coordinates as `position + delta`. - Determine the prefill/decode stage from each row’s first token position, with a masked load for empty rows. - Limit kernel launches to active request rows. - Preserve the existing output buffer and `get_positions()` interface. Each row is still expected to contain tokens from a single stage: prefill or decode. ## Testing Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on MMMU. **Atlas A3 (2 devices, max output 8192):** | Configuration | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | | TP2 baseline | 58% | | PCP2 before fix | ~34.33% | | PCP2 with fix | 58.2% | **H20 (2 GPUs per run, TP2/PCP1, validation: 900 samples):** | Revision | C

summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Targets #61024 (SIG Spec Decode: kernel fusion for rejection sampling). title: [Bugfix][Core] Count only held blocks against the sliding window admission cap
summary: ## Purpose Fixes a scheduler deadlock with asynchronous KV loads (KV connectors) on models that have sliding-window or chunked-local KV cache groups. `_request_remaining_blocks` (#44560) reserves, for every request whose KV is still loading, the blocks it will need to resume prefill, so that further loads are not admitted into that space. For recycling-aware groups the reservation is capped by `max_admission_blocks_per_request`, but the cap was compared with `len(req_to_blocks)`, and that list pads the positions outside the window with null blocks. For a request with a long computed prefix the length far exceeds the cap, the subtraction comes out negative, and the sliding-window reservation becomes zero, even though every prefill chunk still needs one slot per token in those groups. The non-fast path has the same problem through `num_skipped_blocks`. With the reservation undercounted, loads keep being admitted until the free pool is smaller than one prefill chunk of the queue head. The head cannot allocate, `schedule()` breaks on it, and because nothing is running there is nothing to preempt: the engine sits at `Running: 0` forever. **Observed in serving.** DeepSeek-V4-Flash (full-attention plus sliding-window KV groups with block sizes 4 and 8) served with pipeline parallelism, the CPU `OffloadingConnector` and DSpark speculative decoding, with contexts up to 1M tokens. While serving, the engine stopped at `Running: 0, Waiting: 20` and never recovered. title: perf: Optimize sliding window cache hit search time complexity to O(N/K) from O(N)
summary: ## Purpose This PR implements an outstanding TODO in find_longest_cache_hit for the sliding window manager, reducing the worst-case time complexity of cache miss searches from $O(N)$ to $O(N/K)$ (where $N$ is max_num_blocks and $K$ is sliding_window_contiguous_blocks). Previously, searching for a contiguous cache sequence scanned backward block-by-block. In low cache-hit rate scenarios, this resulted in an **O(N)** linear scan overhead. By replacing the sequential for loop with a while loop, this PR introduces a Boyer-Moore-style lookahead: we now probe the beginning of the required contiguous window (i - K + 1) before evaluating the rest of the sequence. If the boundary block is a cache miss, we can conclusively skip the entire window, aggressively pruning the search space. ## Test Plan 1. Correctness: Ran the v1 core test suite to ensure the jump logic does not break block alignment or drop_eagle_block behavior. pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py -vv pytest tests/v1/core/ -vv 2. Performance: Created a localized micro-benchmark script using mock vLLM objects to simulate cache hit/miss scenarios without full engine initialization overhead. Tested on a local RTX 3070 Ti. ## Test Result The optimization eliminates severe CPU blocking delays during large context misses, speeding up worst-case scenarios by ~15x to ~45x. As expected, the jump logic introduces a negligible constant-factor overhead (1-37µs) in highly fragmented cache scenarios due to occasional double-lookups, which is a highly favorable trade-off for flattening the O(N) scaling. title: [Bugfix] Bill hidden-state extraction at its own KV cache group width
summary: ## Purpose Fix KV-cache admission for `extract_hidden_states` on hybrid Mamba/MLA models. The 1-layer hidden-state group was charged at the width of the widest peer group (e.g. 24 MLA layers), so a ~5.4 GiB extraction cache was billed as ~130 GiB and startup failed. Fixes #56774. This is not a duplicate of #53074: that PR isolates hidden-state specs from DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA packing. This bug is on the uniform-page-size grouping path used by hybrid Mamba/MLA. ## Details Hidden-state layers are filtered out of target grouping and appended as a singleton with the common page. The shared pool still sizes every block to `max(group width)`, and admission is `bytes_per_block * total_blocks`. The extraction group needs many blocks (small tokens/block), so it pays for unused MLA slots on every block. Changing only the admission formula would still allocate overlay blocks at that wide width. When a hidden-state group is appended, split every group to one layer so the pool width is one page and extraction is billed at its own width. This only runs with `extract_hidden_states`; models without a hidden-state cache keep the original grouping. The block-outermost packed path is unchanged. title: [Feature][KV Offload] Support joint GPU/CPU prefix cache lookup
summary: ## Purpose ### Background We deploy DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp with vLLM Ascend v0.27 in our internal network, with Simple CPU Offload enabled. During operation, we observed a cache miss rate exceeding 10%. Investigation showed that some reusable cache entries were not being retrieved due to the unimplemented TODO in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`: the existing API only matches a CPU suffix following the GPU prefix, rather than searching for a complete valid prefix across both pools. After implementing joint lookup, we ported the change to the v0.27 branch in our fork and redeployed it in the same environment. The deployment has been running for five days, with normal operation and successful retrieval of cache entries previously affected by this limitation. This PR targets upstream main. The deployment observations above come from the v0.27 backport in our fork. ### Changes Support valid prefixes composed of interleaved GPU and CPU cache blocks, replacing the limitation of matching a GPU prefix followed by a CPU suffix. For example, given a `GPU → CPU → GPU` cache layout, reuse both GPU blocks directly and allocate and load a target block only for the middle CPU block. When both pools contain a required block, prefer the GPU copy. title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Cut P/D loads at the Mamba prefix-cache checkpoint
summary: ## The Problem ## Purpose With Mamba `align` prefix caching under P/D, the decoder never holds a prefix-cacheable state for the prompt. P computes N-1 tokens and sends the running state at N-1, which is off the block grid. Retention keeps only the prompt checkpoint C (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, the default). C lives on P, so the next D-local turn of the conversation (a short follow-up, routed straight to D by conditional P/D) recomputes the whole history. #63610 measured this on Qwen3.5-9B (block 576, GSM8K multi-turn): **0 / 123,032 prompt tokens hit on D**, and 59.4% once D got the checkpoint state. This PR makes P stop its prefill **at C** and lets D recompute the tail `[C, N)` itself: - **P** (`_num_prefill_backoff_tokens`): truncates the prompt to the checkpoint a local prefill would cache. It reuses core's `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position` (exposed as `KVCacheManager.get_state_checkpoint_tokens`), so the hash lookahead and the EAGLE/MTP block drop are honoured. P's running state at C *is* the checkpoint. - **D** (`_get_remote_prefill_token_count`): mirrors P's cut. Push mode needs this, because D registers its blocks before P finishes and has no `remote_num_tokens`. In pull mode, P's `remote_num_tokens` wins on a mismatch: a heterogeneous P, or a P without this change that stops at N-1. A mismatch only costs the prefix-cache entry, never correctness. summary: ## Overview The first two items of milestone 3 in RFC #66844, part of #26201: Mamba frontier checkpoints under speculative decoding. Stacked on #66881; only the last commit is new here. #66881 refuses speculative decoding, and GLM-5.3-Flash's recipe runs MTP with 5 draft tokens by default. Under speculative decoding a finished request's computed-token count doesn't say where its exact state is: a verify step writes one Mamba state column per draft position, a stop can land inside the accepted drafts, and with async scheduling one more step can be in flight when the request finishes. This PR handles those cases. - `speculative_config.truncate_acceptance_at_stop` (off by default): the rejection sampler stops accepting at the request's stop (its EOS unless `ignore_eos`, a stop token id, or its length limit), the same rules as the scheduler's `check_stop`. Outputs don't change, since the scheduler drops the tokens after a stop anyway, but the GPU state then ends at the request's last token. - The scheduler keeps each request's last completed step and, when the request finishes, resolves the step and draft column that hold its exact state. A step in flight puts it in that step's first column, after the request's last token. - A state in a later draft column is folded into the first column on the GPU before the next step reads it, with the existing `align`-mode pre-copy kernel: the recurrent state is copied in and the conv window shifted left. title: [KDA][Spec Decode] RecoverSSM: replay the accepted tokens in the next verify
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview The Triton KDA RecoverSSM verify replays each request's accepted tokens of its last verify into its checkpoint, so the commit after sampling only records the count (deferred). title: [Core][KV Events] KV cache events for recovery units and frontier keys in hybrid prefix caching
summary: ## Overview The first item of milestone 4 in RFC #66844, part of #26201: KV cache events with Mamba frontier checkpoints. Stacked on #66881; only the last commit is new here. It doesn't depend on #67045. #66881 refuses KV cache events. A frontier's key isn't a hash of its token range, so a consumer that rebuilds an instance's prefix tree from `BlockStored` events can't place it. And for a hybrid model a `BlockStored` doesn't say whether the instance can resume there at all, since that also needs a recurrent state at exactly that position. This adds `kv_events_config.recovery_unit_events`, off by default. With it, frontier checkpoints run with KV cache events, and the scheduler also publishes: - `RecoveryUnitStored` and `RecoveryUnitRemoved`: a position the instance can resume from, a block-boundary state or a frontier, with its length and session id. A removal also has its cause and the leaf-last tier the unit was last ranked in, and a unit that leaves in the eviction that chose it has the number of blocks freed with it. A block-boundary unit's hash is the block hash its Mamba groups' `BlockStored` events carry. - Each frontier key as a `BlockStored` per group, with `kv_cache_spec_kind="frontier"`, empty `token_ids`, the frontier's length in tokens as `block_size`, and the request's block hash at the last hash-unit boundary before it as parent, plus its `BlockRemoved`. - A `cause` on every `BlockRemoved` from the GPU block pool, one of `REMOVAL_CAUSES`: evicted by GreedyDual-Size (by tier), an orphan page, superseded by the session's newer state, a frontier that lost one of

title: [Core][DP] Add an opt-in cross-DP prefill delayer scheduling policy
summary: ## Overview Adds an opt-in `--prefill-schedule-policy delayer` for MoE data parallelism. On every step the DP ranks exchange their prefill state and take the same decision. They hold prefill while they decode, then release it on all ranks in the same step once it is aligned and well filled, within bounded waits. Supersedes #61834. ## Claims - New option `--prefill-schedule-policy {cadence,delayer}`. The default `cadence` is the existing `--prefill-schedule-interval` behavior, unchanged on every platform. - With `delayer`, `--prefill-schedule-interval N` sets the minimum spacing of prefill steps: the `N - 1` steps after a prefill decode only. The only new knob is `--prefill-max-wait-ms`, which releases held prefill, including during those steps, once the oldest waiting request has queued that long. - No new collective. summary: ## Overview Adds a per-request `SamplingParams.return_aux_outputs` flag (default `true`). A request that sets it to `false` gets no RL auxiliary outputs: its routed experts are neither recorded nor returned, and it gets no sampling mask and no sample `logprobs` or `logprob_token_ids`. `prompt_logprobs` and the `top_k` sampling parameter are unaffected. **Why:** RL inference servers record these outputs for every request, but some requests never use them, such as online evals that run next to the rollouts. title: [Feature][Kernel] Triton autotune fused MoE
summary: ## Purpose Depends on #59492. Builds on the generic Triton autotune warmup (`--kernel-config.enable_triton_autotune`) and adds a fused MoE table. A GPU or model with no bundled `fused_moe/configs/*.json` can now tune its own launch configs at startup instead of falling back to the heuristic default. The search does not read any bundled or user tables, so it works the same on new hardware as on hardware with shipped configs. cc @vanshbhatia-amd Changes: - **Bounded search.** At most 48 configs are timed per M bucket. The search starts from the default config, 8 random configs and up to 2 nearby-M winners, then expands neighbors of the fastest config that hasn't been expanded yet. The M buckets are the same 18-bucket grid as `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py`, clipped to `max_num_batched_tokens`. - **Backend-derived search space.** Launch options (`waves_per_eu`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, `kpack`), the warp size and the shared-memory limit come from the installed Triton backend. Nothing is keyed on GPU name. Configs that exceed registers or shared memory are skipped. Block FP8 configs are clamped or rejected so tiles align with the quant block. `BLOCK_SIZE_M` is capped by the rows per expert. - **Routing-robust timing.** Timing runs in a CUDA graph and cycles through 10 routing draws. At small M the number of active experts changes which config is fastest, and a single draw can crown a config that is usually slow. - **Correctness and noise guard.** A winner must match the default config's output (rtol 1e-2). summary: ## Overview FLy's entropy gate now renormalizes the top-k target scores and divides by `log(k)`, so `fly_entropy_threshold` is a `[0, 1]` value with the same meaning for every `fly_entropy_top_k`. title: [RFC]: Multimodal Asynchronous Collaborative Architecture Sidecar
summary: ### Motivation. Motivation In multimodal inference on hardware accelerators, the vLLM API Server process is conventionally responsible for both: 1. **Serving inference requests** (HTTP I/O, scheduling, tokenization, streaming) 2. **Image preprocessing** (network download, PIL decode, HF `processor()`, grid_thw extraction, pixel_values tensor construction) These two responsibilities are architecturally in conflict: - Image preprocessing is **CPU-bound, synchronous, and variable-latency** — network download alone is unbounded, and HF transforms scale with image resolution. - The API Server is **event-loop-driven, async, latency-sensitive** — it must serve many concurrent HTTP requests with sub-millisecond scheduling overhead. - When preprocessing runs inside the API Server process, it competes for the **same event loop, the same GIL, and the same CPU cores** as the inference serving path. The symptom is a **super-linear TTFT inflation under concurrency**: a single-image request pays the full preprocess cost, while N concurrent requests pay it N times serialized through the event loop, plus the gather-callback queueing overhead that emerges when many coroutines compete for the same loop. At high concurrency, the wait for `grid_thw` (the shape tensor needed before accelerator prefill can start) becomes the dominant tail-latency contributor. title: [RFC]: Decoder Append-Prefill for Multi-Turn Workloads in P/D Disaggregated Serving
summary: ### Motivation. Multi-turn agentic workloads often combine long, growing conversation histories with relatively short outputs. In Prefill/Decode (P/D) disaggregated serving, these workloads can concentrate pressure on Prefiller instances, especially during request bursts. The Decoder that served the previous turn may still hold a substantial reusable prefix in its local KV cache, including tokens generated during that turn. Sending the next request through the Prefiller can introduce queueing, additional prefill computation, and KV transfer, even when the Decoder could reuse its local prefix and compute the remaining suffix. We propose **Decoder Append-Prefill**: an opt-in path that allows a follow-up request to reuse KV on its previous Decoder and perform the remaining prefill locally. When the required local cache is unavailable, the request falls back to ordinary P/D. The target is a workload where Prefiller pressure is high, Decoder capacity is available, and the uncached suffix is relatively short. The design must account for the effect of additional prefill work on ongoing decode requests. ### Proposed Change. **1. Request flow** 1. The first turn follows the ordinary P/D path. 2. The router records the Decoder endpoint and data-parallel rank that served the session. 3. For an eligible follow-up turn, the router sends the complete request directly to that Decoder and rank, requesting local-cache admission. 4. The Scheduler checks the actual reusable local KV prefix. summary: > contact: @amdrajeevp1 @amd-adichatt ## Motivation We propose an optional interface allowing a quantized linear kernel to combine its base computation with the LoRA update. The initial implementation targets compressed-tensors W4A16 dense linear layers on AMD gfx1151. Today, these layers use separate logical operations for the quantized base GEMM, LoRA shrink, and LoRA expand. For small activation batches, the separate expand operation adds launch overhead and reads and writes the base output again. Our prototype retains the standard Punica shrink operation and incorporates expand into the W4A16 GEMM epilogue. This reduces output memory traffic and removes the standalone expand operation for supported calls. title: [Performance]: Resize video frames while decoding to skip full-resolution copies
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance **TL;DR:** Resize video frames right after decoding instead of in the HF processor. For Qwen3-VL on 1080p video: 10–60× smaller frame arrays, 35–46% less decode + processor time, 1.8–2.5× throughput when preprocessing-bound, and `pixel_values_videos` stays bit-identical. **Problem.** vLLM's video loaders keep every sampled frame at full resolution; the HF processor then copies and resizes them. Most video processors downscale (Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, GLM-4.xV, LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL, ...). For Qwen3-VL, a 5-min 1080p video at 2 fps is 600 frames ≈ 3.5 GiB per request, resized down to 256×128 (W×H). **Proposal.** Resize each frame right after decoding, using the same op and target size as the HF processor (Qwen3-VL: torchvision bicubic + antialias on uint8, size from `smart_resize`). The processor then computes the same target size from the already-resized frames, so its resize changes nothing and `pixel_values_videos` is bit-identical. That holds for common aspect ratios but not always (e.g. 480×1920 with ≥258 frames shrinks one more step), so the loader checks it and otherwise keeps the current path. The resize is generic; each model only supplies its target size. Starting with Qwen3-VL, the only one measured so far. **Results** (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, Big Buck Bunny 1080p h264, RTX 4090 + 16 vCPU EPYC 7542; OpenCV decode backend, fps=2; bit-identical on both clips): | Video | Frame array (MiB) | Decode + processor (s) | req/s, c=4 | req/s, c=8 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 60 s (120 frames) | 712 → 67 | 3.84 → 2.51 | 0.37 → 0.68 | 0.33 → 0.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: merge K2(l) and K1(l + 1) into one launch at TP8
summary: ## Overview At TP8 on MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode (`--monokernel`) launches K2 of layer l and K1 of layer l + 1 as one persistent kernel. This covers 34 of the 39 target layer boundaries and both DSpark draft boundaries. Each merged boundary saves the launch gap and K1's start-up. ## Results - **Bit-exact.** Merged and separate launches give identical outputs on every rank in FULL-graph replays. The CI test below passes on MI355X on this branch. - **Accuracy unchanged** (table below). - **Perf.** Conc 1, 1 × TP8, DSpark k = 6: −96.8 µs per step (−2.21%), 4 ABBA pairs, SE 4.3 µs. The layer bench gives −1.71 to −2.08 µs per merged layer boundary. These perf numbers were measured before #63893, #64152, #64883 and #64153 merged; - **Scope.** TP8 only. TP2, TP4 and gfx942 builds, and the standalone K1, K2 and FFN builds, are byte-identical to main. There is no new env var. **Accuracy, main vs this PR** - Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1 × TP8, `--monokernel`, DSpark k = 6 with real (block) acceptance, greedy. - Every request runs at concurrency 1, so every decode step merges: about 150k target steps per PR session. - ABBA order, 4 server sessions. Each arm's number is its two runs pooled. - Both arms run the same nightly image. Main uses main's versions of the 8 files this PR changes. | Task | main | PR | p | |---|---|---|---| | GSM8K (1319, 8-shot) | 91.24 | 91.85 | 0.22 | | MATH-500 (4-shot) | 84.20 | 82.70 | 0.20 | | RULER niah_multikey_3 / variable tracking, 4k–512k | 100 / 100 | 100 / 100 | – | | RULER niah_single_2 / niah_multivalue, 4k–128k | 100 / 99.97 | 100

title: [Perf][Kernel] Add opt-in BF16 gated projection fusion for SM89 prefills
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds an opt-in Triton kernel that fuses the MLP gate/up GEMM with SiLU-and-mul for BF16 dense prefill on SM89 (RTX 4090), wired into `Qwen2MoeMLP`, the dense MLP of Qwen3.5-4B. Defaults are unchanged. Related: [RFC #52776](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52776) proposes a general epilogue interface; this PR is one narrow, measured instance and does not implement that interface. An open-PR search on 2026-11-03 (`swiglu gemm`, `silu fusion`, `dense MLP`, `52776`) found no equivalent dense BF16 gate/up + SiLU fusion for SM89; [#60846](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60846) targets SM120 tiny-batch decode (shared-expert scalar gate and reduction), not the gate/up GEMM. ## Claims - **End to end:** Qwen3.5-4B on one RTX 4090, 16K-token prompt, `vllm serve` default `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`: TTFT **−3.0%** (mean per-pair change, 95% CI −3.3% to −2.8%; median 1,143.5 → 1,108.2 ms over 12 request pairs, all 12 faster). - **Per MLP call (isolated op):** gate/up GEMM + SiLU-and-mul takes **10–11% less time** for 768–4,096 rows (1,090.1 → 966.2 µs, −11.4%, at 1,584 rows). - **Opt-in and contained:** nothing changes unless `+gated_linear_silu` is set. When it is set, steps outside 768–4,096 rows run the same cuBLAS GEMM and `silu_and_mul` kernels as before (bit-exact in the fallback tests), and no weight copy is made. GSM8K: 1,019 → 1,022 of 1,319 correct, difference not significant. ## Validation **Why this kernel.** In a 16K-token prefill before this PR, GEMMs take 73% of GPU kernel time and the MLP gate/up GEMM alone

title: [KV Connector] Per-connector "enable_kv_events" switch for KV cache events
summary: ## Overview `--kv-events-config` currently turns on the engine's GPU prefix-cache events and every KV connector's events together. This PR adds a per-connector opt-out: `"enable_kv_events": false` in a connector's `kv_connector_extra_config`. With it, a deployment can publish GPU events without, for example, a shared MooncakeStore's events. ## Claims - New `kv_connector_extra_config` key `enable_kv_events`, default `true`, so existing behavior is unchanged. When set to `false`, that connector's events are left out of the published `KVEventBatch`; the engine's own GPU events are still published. - Applies to every connector without per-connector code: - The scheduler applies the switch to the configured connector. - `MultiConnector` applies each child's own setting. - So the key can be set on a single child, or once on the `MultiConnector` to cover all of its children. - Connectors that opt out are still drained every step, so their buffered events do not accumulate. - `MooncakeStoreConnector` checks the switch at startup. When it is off, it skips building store events, including tracking prompt token IDs for them. ## Validation Rebased onto `main` at 2abde627d9. Unit tests ran on Linux (aarch64, NVIDIA GB200, Python 3.12), with `main` at the same commit as the baseline. Results are identical apart from the 2 new tests. | Suite | This PR | Baseline (`main`) | | --- | --- | --- | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` | 31 passed, 3 failed\* | 29 passed, 3 failed\* | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_{connector,scheduler,worker,coordinator}.py`

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Report Mooncake Store reset failures
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` returns `True` even when Mooncake fails to clear the Store. ## Root cause The worker's RESET handler calls `store.remove_all(force=True)` and always replies ACK. The SDK reports failure by returning a negative `ErrorCode` rather than raising, so the result was dropped. title: [Bugfix][KV Transfer] Allow DMA-only connectors with expandable_segments:True
summary: ## Summary PR #41237 added a blanket rejection of **all** KV connectors when `expandable_segments:True` is set in `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`. This is correct for RDMA-based connectors (`NixlConnector`, `MooncakeConnectorV1`) whose registered memory regions become stale after CUDA VMM remaps virtual addresses. However, it's a false positive for DMA-only connectors like `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, which transfer data via `torch.cat`/tensor slicing — operations that are transparent to VMM remapping. This PR introduces a `SupportsVmmSafeTransfers` marker class that connectors opt into by inheriting. The config validation checks this marker before rejecting, allowing DMA-only connectors to work with `expandable_segments` without requiring sleep mode. ### End-to-end validation on hardware **Setup:** 3× NVIDIA RTX 3060 12GB, AMD EPYC 7551P 32-Core, 260 GB RAM **Model:** `groxaxo/Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-Pro-4bit` (GPTQ-Pro 4-bit, Marlin kernels, ~21 GB weights, 64-layer hybrid: 16 full attention + 48 linear attention) **Config:** ``` --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --max-model-len 252000 --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 1568 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True ``` Without the PR, you cannot use both **PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF** and **--kv-offloading-***. title: [Kernel] Coalesce reshape_and_cache stores by taking a KV block at a time
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `reshape_and_cache`, the paged KV-cache writer behind `ROCM_ATTN`, launches one block per token, so the `block_size` tokens that share each cache line of the paged layout are stored from `block_size` different blocks. Once a launch is large enough, this gives each block one head of a KV block's worth of consecutive tokens instead, so those stores coalesce. Smaller launches run the existing code unchanged. ## Claims - **1.9-5.5x on the kernel for prefill-sized launches** on MI355X (bf16, head_size 128, block_size 16, 1-8 KV heads): 4.4-4.9x at 8192 tokens and 4.9-5.5x at 16384 tokens with 8 KV heads, for one request, several aligned requests, misaligned requests, mid-block starts and masked slots alike; 3.0-3.6x with an fp8 KV cache. - **3.1x in situ on Llama-3.1-8B and 2.5-3.5x on Qwen3-30B-A3B**: in an 8 x 8192-token prefill run, the kernel's device time drops from 33.8 ms to 10.7 ms and from 26-36 ms to 10.4 ms. - **No change on decode-sized launches**: below the threshold the existing kernel runs as before (0.99-1.01x in every such case measured, 1-8 KV heads). - **Bit-identical output** to the current kernel in 4,467 cases, including `kv_cache_dtype="fp8"` and `interleaved_v`. - +53/-21 in `csrc/cache_kernels.cu`, +2/-1 in the test; no API or caller change. - **End-to-end throughput was not measured.** The kernel was 0.9-2.0% of device time in the prefill-heavy run above and drops to 0.4-0.6%, so the step-level gain is bounded at about 1.3%. ## Validation **In-tree test.** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k "test_r

title: [ROCm][Attention] Use AITER as fallback for flash_attn_varlen_func
summary: ## Summary On ROCm, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py` imports `flash_attn_varlen_func` from upstream `flash_attn`. That package isn't shipped in the ROCm prebuilt wheels and a from-source build of Composable Kernel takes 30-60 minutes (FMHA emits thousands of kernel variants). On environments that don't ship `flash_attn` preinstalled (e.g., the AMD Developer Cloud images), the existing fallback is a stub that raises `ImportError` at call time. Callers that import `flash_attn_varlen_func` directly from this module then either fail at runtime or fall through into a `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention` path, which materialises an O(N²) attention matrix and OOMs at 32K context. This PR adds a second-level fallback to AITER's `flash_attn_varlen_func` (already integrated in vLLM via `vllm._aiter_ops.rocm_aiter_ops`). AITER is an existing optional dep on ROCm — no new dependency surface. Detection order on ROCm: 1. upstream `flash_attn` (preferred, unchanged) 2. AITER (new fallback when upstream is missing) 3. `ImportError` stub at call time (only when neither is installed) ## Why this matters - The ROCm `FLASH_ATTN` backend itself is not affected here — when `flash_attn` is missing the platform selector rejects it via `ImportError` and falls back to `ROCM_AITER_FA` or `TRITON_ATTN`, both of which already work. So users running stock vLLM on ROCm aren't OOMing today. - The fallback primarily helps third-party / custom attention backends and code paths that import `flash_attn_varlen_func` from `fa_utils` directly (e.g., custom long-context KV-cache backends), w

title: rocm_attn: fix paged attention for custom KV cache layouts
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #41472 — the ROCm custom paged-attention kernel (`paged_attention_ll4mi_QKV_mfma{4,16}`) produces wrong outputs for models whose KV cache layout does not match the standard contiguous formula `physical_slot = block_table[s, i // BS] * BS + (i % BS)`. The LFM2 family (LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M, LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B) is the reported repro; the same kernel path is taken for any model on ROCm that falls through `RocmAttentionImpl` → `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` → `ops.paged_attention_rocm`. ## Root cause The kernel computed both the physical block number *and* the in-block offset from the local/global token index, baking the contiguous-layout assumption into the kernel itself. Models with mixed (hybrid) KV layouts cannot express their real per-token slot positions through `block_table` alone, so the kernel read from the wrong slots and silently corrupted attention outputs. ## Fix Move KV-slot resolution out of the kernel and into a caller- supplied flat `slot_mapping` tensor of length `sum(seq_lens)`, indexed per context token. The kernel now computes `physical_block = slot / BLOCK_SIZE` and `in_block_offset = slot % BLOCK_SIZE` from this tensor. - For standard contiguous-layout models, the tensor is derived once per step inside `chunked_prefill_paged_decode` from `block_table` + `seq_lens` — exactly the formula the old kernel was implicitly evaluating, hoisted out. Behavior is unchanged. - For models with non-standard layouts, a new optional `context_slot_mapping` field on `RocmAttentionMetadata` lets the model's metadata builder express the real layout, and the

title: [RFC]: Per-Layer Parallelism Policy
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## 1. Motivation PR #36287 introduced TPA (tensor-parallel-size-attention) to vLLM, and review feedback from Lucas Wilkinson — *"the design shouldn't be attention-specific"* — pointed to a more general need: a per-layer parallelism policy that lets layers declare what they are and have the framework resolve their plan. ## 2. The idea A single function, owned by the framework, that turns a layer's identity into its parallelism plan: ``` ┌─────────────────────────────┐ (layer instance, prefix) ──▶ │ framework-owned resolver │──▶ plan │ (consults config + layer) │ └─────────────────────────────┘ ``` Layers consult the resolver in `__init__` instead of reading global TP accessors. A *plan* is whatever the layer needs to make local decisions — its TP width, its rank within that group, its communication backend, etc. The plan schema is open-ended; the call shape stays the same as new fields are added. The plan being a function of the layer is what makes the design non-attention-specific. The resolver doesn't know it's an attention layer — it knows it's *this* layer at *this* prefix and consults config to decide. New strategies (Q-replication, hybrid attention, MTP, future ideas) become resolver-and-config changes, not N-model changes. ## 3. How the policy expresses different models The mechanism in §2 is one resolver and one plan dataclass. The breadth comes from what the policy declares for which layers. title: [Core] Per-layer parallelism policy + TPA-GQA on FlashAttention
summary: ## Purpose Implements the per-layer parallelism policy proposed in RFC #42659, with TPA-GQA on FlashAttention as the first concrete realization. Supersedes #36287, addressing review feedback (Lucas Wilkinson: _"the design shouldn't be attention-specific"_) by introducing a framework-owned resolver that lets layers declare what they are and have the framework resolve their parallelism plan. **Mechanism.** A single module-level function — `get_layer_parallel_config(layer, prefix)` — owned by the framework, turns a layer's identity into its parallelism plan. Shared layer code (`QKVParallelLinear`, attention, weight loaders) consults the resolver in `__init__` instead of reading global TP accessors. A default `LayerParallelConfig` (all fields `None`) means "fall back to the global TP world" — non-adopting layers and the no-TPA case behave bit-identically to today. **First feature: TPA-GQA on FlashAttention.** `--tensor-parallel-size-attention K` (alias `-tpa K`) decouples attention head parallelism from FFN tensor parallelism, enabling higher DCP ratios for GQA models. Standard DCP requires `TP / DCP >= num_kv_heads`; for Nemotron-49B (8 KV heads) on 16 GPUs that caps DCP at 2. TPA shards attention heads independently (`attention_tp = TP / DCP`), so DCP=4 with TPA=4 becomes possible. **Backward compatibility.** Two properties enforce BC by construction: - *Sentinel-fallback at every consult site* — the resolver returns a "no policy active" plan by default; unmigrated layers and the no-TPA case fall back to today's global TP accessors and behave bit-identically. - *Per-strategy

title: [KVConnector][P/D][Tests] Add tests for KV transfer completion during shutdown
summary: Relates to #24885, partially based on an earlier version of #32420 by @wseaton During shutdown with a configured timeout, we want to allow in-flight KV transfers to complete before terminating worker processes. This was implemented by #43433, extending the existing shutdown timeout mechanism to coordinate with async KV transfer completion in disaggregated prefill/decode deployments. Finished requests remain in Scheduler.requests only when waiting for async KV transfer (`delay_free_blocks=True`) and so, during shutdown, the `has_finished_requests()` check ensures the engine continues stepping to poll `get_finished()`. Add integration tests and test utilities to verify this behavior. Tests use a `DelayedKVConnector` that simulates async KV transfers by delaying the completion signal for a configurable duration, exercising three scenarios: - `shutdown_timeout > delay`: transfers complete within the timeout - `shutdown_timeout < delay`: server exits after timeout expires - `shutdown_timeout == 0`: server exits immediately, no transfer wait

title: [Perf] Eliminate two GPU→CPU syncs in make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata
summary: ## Summary Implements the `TODO(perf)` left by the original author in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` (lines 415–420). **Problem**: `make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata()` called `.max().item()` and `.sum().item()` on a GPU tensor (`num_decode_tokens`) to compute two scalar values. Each `.item()` forces a GPU stream synchronization — the CPU blocks until the CUDA reduction kernel completes. **Fix**: Transfer the already-computed `decode_query_start_loc` cumsum tensor to CPU once (one sync), then derive both scalars from CPU-only arithmetic: - `decode_query_start_loc_cpu[-1]` → total decode token count (was `.sum().item()`) - adjacent differences → `.max()` → max query length (was `.max().item()`) The CPU tensor is then passed directly to `CommonAttentionMetadata` (eliminating the subsequent `non_blocking` transfer as well). **Net effect**: 2 GPU→CPU sync points → 1 per mixed prefill+decode step in the KV-sharing fast-prefill code path. ## Tests ```bash # Unit tests (CPU-only, no GPU required) .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py -v # Results (32 tests total): # test_make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_pure_decode_shortcircuit PASSED # test_make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_scalar_values[query_lens0-...-6-3] PASSED # test_make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_scalar_values[query_lens1-...-2-1] PASSED # test_make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_scalar_values[query_lens2-...-4-4] PASSED # test_make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_query_start_loc_consistent PASSED # ... 27 pre-existing tests PASSED # Lint pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/v1/attention/b

title: [DSv4][Performance][MoE] Optimize pack_bitmatrix Triton kernel for CDNA GPUs
summary: ## Purpose This PR improves the performance of DSv4 Pro by replacing the naive pack_bitmatrix Triton kernel with an optimized implementation that: - Uses tighter K_PAD heuristic (next_power_of_2 of n_expts_act) to cut memory traffic vs fixed BLOCK_SIZE_K=32 - Reduces warp count to 2 (launch-bound kernel benefits from higher occupancy) - Adds a Python-level wrapper with torch.compile compatibility - Provides a vectorized uint32 packing path for CDNA architectures - Includes a hand-written HIP kernel fast-path that eliminates Triton per-launch dispatch overhead on ROCm co-authored with @heachary. This fix was suggested by Claude. ## Test Result ## Performance Benchmarked on AMD MI355X with DeepSeek-V4-Pro (256 experts, top-8), `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graph mode, these are the e2e results: | Metric | Baseline | + pack_bitmatrix opt | Delta | |--------|----------|---------------------|-------| | Throughput (tok/s) | 154.87 | 163.2 | **+5.4%** | | Median ITL (ms) | 48.8 | 46.4 | -4.9% | | Median TTFT (ms) | 312.2 | 303.7 | -2.7% | | Accuracy (lm_eval) | 95.3% | 95.0% | -0.3% (noise) | <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

title: [Bug]: EngineCore crash — assert req_id in self.requests in _update_from_kv_xfer_finished when an async KV connector reports a finished transfer for an aborted/freed request
summary: ### 🐛 Describe the bug `Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished` asserts that every connector-reported finished transfer still belongs to a live request: ```python # vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py (present on main as of 2026-05-20) for req_id in kv_connector_output.finished_recving or (): logger.debug("Finished recving KV transfer for request %s", req_id) assert req_id in self.requests # <-- crashes the EngineCore req = self.requests[req_id] ... for req_id in kv_connector_output.finished_sending or (): logger.debug("Finished sending KV transfer for request %s", req_id) assert req_id in self.requests # <-- same self._free_blocks(self.requests[req_id]) ``` With an **asynchronous KV connector** (KV transfer completion is reported some steps after it is initiated), a request can be **aborted/finished and freed by the scheduler while a store/recv transfer for it is still in flight**. When that transfer later completes, the connector's `get_finished()` reports the now-unknown `req_id`, the assertion fails, and the **entire EngineCore dies** with `EngineDeadError` — taking down the server, not just the one request. ``` File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line ~2124, in _update_from_kv_xfer_finished assert req_id in self.requests AssertionError -> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError ``` This is the classic "abort races an in-flight async KV transfer" double-free/stale-id scenario. ### Why #33377 does not fully fix this PR #33377 ("avoid vllm-side double free during async scheduling + request abort + async KV cache transfer", merged 2026-02-03) addressed exactly this

title: [Kernel] Add fused CUDA kernels for MoE non-gated activations

For `RELU2_NO_MUL` specifically, the old code also mutated the input tensor in-place as a side effect. title: fix(turboquant): use SDPA prefill fallback on pre-Ampere GPUs
summary: Closes #43576 ## Summary - Fix `RuntimeError: FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer` when running TurboQuant on T4/Turing (SM75) - The SDPA fallback path already exists in the TQ backend but is unreachable on CUDA because `is_flash_attn_varlen_func_available()` unconditionally returns `True` - Add a compute capability check: if SM < 8.0, set `_HAS_FLASH_ATTN = False` so prefill routes through `F.scaled_dot_product_attention()` ## Root cause `is_flash_attn_varlen_func_available()` (in `fa_utils.py`) returns `True` on all CUDA platforms — it checks that the function exists in the flash_attn package, not that the hardware can actually execute FA2 kernels. FA2 requires SM >= 8.0 (Ampere). On T4 (SM75/Turing), the CUDA kernel launch crashes at runtime. The TQ backend already has a complete SDPA fallback path gated behind `if not _HAS_FLASH_ATTN` (used for CPU/non-CUDA). This path works correctly on SM75 — it just never executes because the flag is always True on CUDA. ## Changes **`vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py`** (8 lines): After `_HAS_FLASH_ATTN = is_flash_attn_varlen_func_available()`, add a compute capability check. If SM < 8.0 (Turing/Volta), override to `False`. The existing `if _HAS_FLASH_ATTN: from ... import flash_attn_varlen_func` conditional import remains correct — it just won't trigger on pre-Ampere. ## Test plan - [x] Tested on Kaggle T4 (SM75) with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` + `turboquant_4bit_nc`: - Engine boots successfully (FlashInfer JIT + Triton decode kernel compile) - Prefill routes through SDPA (`_HAS_FLASH_ATTN = False` confirmed) - Dec

summary: ## Summary Stacked on top of #43328. summary: ### Your current environment ## Environment - **Hardware:** NVIDIA GB10 Spark (4 hosts, identical config) - **Kernel:** `6.17.0-1018-nvidia` (Ubuntu nvidia driver kernel) - **NVIDIA driver:** `580.159.03`, CUDA 13.0 - **Container image:** `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f023269abe06db3a1a7cd9e170a0f5bd2b333a19ef9cb99ed8df97a70345bc25` (vLLM v0.21.0) - **Model:** `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` (dense, Gated-DeltaNet hybrid attention, 262K native context, FP8 weights) - **vLLM args:** ``` --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.60 --port 8000 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --max-log-len 200 --max-num-seqs 6 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary `vllm-qwen36` containers running **Qwen3.6-27B-FP8** on **NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)** hosts occasionally enter a **stuck CUDA stream** state under sustained inference load: the EngineCore process spin-loops at 99% CPU in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py::get_output()` waiting for a GPU forward-pass result that never arrives. `/v1/models` keeps answering (parent API process) but `/v1/chat/completions` hangs. `nvidia-smi` reports GPU-Util pinned at 96% with abnormally low power draw (19 W vs 36 W on a healthy peer at the same utilization) — i.e. utilization counter pinned on a stuck kernel doing no real work. We have mitigations in place that keep this from being user-visible (wedge-recovery watchdog auto-restarts in ~5 min, sub-cap concurrency limit `--max-num-seqs 6` reduces incidence). This issue is to **track the upstream cause** so we can either fix it permanently or quantify the residual

title: [Kernel] Use FlashInfer CUDA BGMV MoE Kernel for Multi-LoRA MoE dispatch
summary: Co-authored-by: Claude ## Purpose This PR connects vLLM's MoE LoRA dispatch path to FlashInfer's BGMV MoE CUDA kernel (merged in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3249). When FlashInfer with BGMV MoE support is installed, vLLM uses it via the `flashinfer.fused_moe` API. The Triton SGMV kernel remains as a fallback, selectable via environment variables. This is the recommended integration path: kernel lives in FlashInfer, vLLM consumes it through the existing FlashInfer interface. ## Changes * **flashinfer.py**: Add `has_flashinfer_bgmv_moe()` detection and lazy wrappers for `bgmv_moe_shrink` / `bgmv_moe_expand` * **punica_gpu.py**: * Add CUDA/Triton backend selection via `VLLM_MOE_LORA_BACKEND` env vars (default: CUDA) * Add pre-allocated GPU buffer infrastructure (`_init_moe_bgmv_buffers`) for zero-allocation kernel calls * Add `add_lora_fused_moe_cuda` method that dispatches to FlashInfer's `bgmv_moe_shrink` / `bgmv_moe_expand` * Add cudagraph capture skip (MoE LoRA ops are not capture-safe) * Route `add_lora_fused_moe` between CUDA (FlashInfer) and Triton paths based on backend config * Add FP8->bf16 input cast in `add_lora_fused_moe` for FP8 quantized models (neither CUDA BGMV nor Triton MoE LoRA kernels support FP8 activations directly) * Add stream synchronization after expand to prevent race condition with shared buffer reuse across layers ## Related PRs * https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40670 - Original PR with kernel implementation directly in vLLM (superseded by this approach) * https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3249 - Flash

title: [RFC]: Semantic KV Cache Reuse Interface
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM's exact prefix cache is the right primitive when requests share the same token prefix. Many long-context workloads have a nearby but different shape: the expensive reusable content is present, but the request starts with a different instruction, chat wrapper, retrieval order, or paraphrased lead-in. Exact prefix caching correctly misses in those cases. This potentially leaves a lot of potential optimization on the table. This proposal is about exposing the engine-side controls needed for that class of reuse without putting a semantic search algorithm in vLLM. External systems can discover donors; vLLM should continue to own scheduling, paged KV allocation, block lifetime, failure recovery, and exact prefix-cache semantics. - semantic lookup is an optional external policy decision, - reporting external tokens to vLLM is a materialization promise, - exact prefix-cache writes must remain exact, - any approximate or request-only reuse needs explicit cache-commit semantics before it can be enabled safely with prefix caching. ### Proposed Change. # Semantic KV Cache Connector Interface for vLLM ## Summary vLLM already has most of the control points needed for semantic KV cache reuse. `KVConnectorBase_V1` separates scheduler-side external match discovery from worker-side KV materialization, the scheduler already has an explicit `num_external_computed_tokens` path, and the worker/model-runner path already lets connectors load KV into vLLM-owned paged KV slots before attention reads them. This proposal defines a conservative semantic-KV connector strategy on top

title: [Feature]: Improving NVFP4 Quantization via Fast and Accurate Sweep on FP8 Block Scale
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch I propose ScaleSweep to improve NVFP4 quantization. The core idea of ScaleSweep is to select an FP8 E4M3 scale by sweeping a small analytically derived range around the base scale, rather than searching over all FP8 scales. ### Alternatives A preliminary implementation and corresponding tests are available here: https://github.com/efsotr/nvfp4quant_test On an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, `ScaleSweep_MSE_round` shows comparable speed to the current vLLM default operator `vllm._custom_ops.scaled_fp4_quant` on an 8192×8192 speed test: about `1.0064×` latency. In a preliminary error test on Gaussian-distributed inputs, it reduces MSE from `0.0171616` to `0.0135951`. Currently, I only have preliminary Triton implementations of the `ScaleSweep*` kernels, and the tests have only been run on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU. I would appreciate further help from the vLLM community to refine these kernels and integrate ScaleSweep into vLLM's NVFP4 quantization path as production-level operators. @potatosalad @tmm1 @wpc @jefp @mgoin, @Isotr0py, @yewentao256 ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm] Add tuned MoE configs for Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
summary: ## Summary Add Triton fused_moe kernel configs for **E=256, N=512** on the AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU, gfx1151). These configs were produced by an 11-hour `benchmark_moe.py` sweep and validated in production serving **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4**. - Two config files added: - `E=256,N=512,device_name=Radeon_8060S_Graphics,dtype=int4_w4a16.json` - `E=256,N=512,device_name=Radeon_8060S_Graphics.json` (dtype-agnostic fallback) ### Key findings - **num_warps=1** is optimal for gfx1151 at small batch sizes (1-64 tokens), consistent with RDNA 3.5 single-CU wave occupancy - BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 preferred over 64 or 256 for the E=256 shape - Without these configs, vLLM autotuning adds ~90s to cold starts and selects suboptimal parameters ### Not a duplicate - No existing PR adds Radeon 8060S MoE configs - TheTom/vllm-turboquant has an E=128,N=768 config for 8060S (different model shape); this PR covers E=256,N=512 (Qwen3.6 MoE) ## Test plan - [x] Benchmarked against autotuned baseline: equivalent throughput, eliminates cold-start tuning delay - [x] Validated with `vllm serve` + Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 on Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128GB UMA, ROCm 7.14) - [x] Production-validated at ~38 tok/s sustained over 5+ restarts **AI assistance was used** (Claude) for benchmarking automation and config generation. All results validated by human on physical hardware. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [ROCm] Fix get_device_name crash with TheRock/MagicMock amdsmi stub
summary: ## Summary TheRock-based Docker builds stub `amdsmi` with `unittest.mock.MagicMock`. When `get_device_name()` calls `amdsmi_get_gpu_asic_info()`, it gets MagicMock objects instead of strings for `device_id` and `market_name`. These mock objects pass the `in` membership test against the device ID map (`MagicMock.__eq__` returns a truthy MagicMock), causing downstream code to receive mock objects where it expects device name strings. This breaks: - MoE config file resolution (filename includes device_name) - Any code path that uses the device name as a string ### Fix Add `isinstance(str)` checks on amdsmi return values and fall back to `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` when they fail. The torch.cuda path always returns a real string regardless of amdsmi availability. ### Not a duplicate - PR #40963 addresses APU VRAM reporting (different problem in the same file) - This fix addresses the MagicMock stub behavior specific to TheRock builds, which #40963 does not cover ## Test plan - [x] Validated on Strix Halo APU (gfx1151) with TheRock vLLM Docker image (v0.22.0) - [x] Confirmed `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` returns correct "Radeon 8060S Graphics" when amdsmi is mocked - [x] MoE config file resolution works correctly after fix (previously got MagicMock in filename) - [x] Production-validated at ~38 tok/s serving Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 **AI assistance was used** (Claude) for debugging and patch development. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fp8 family: match modules_to_not_convert by substring
summary: ## Purpose Fix #21669: FP8 quantized models with short-pattern `modules_to_not_convert` (e.g. `["linear_attn.in_proj_qkv"]`) silently load ignored layers as FP8 because `Fp8Config.get_quant_method` calls `is_layer_skipped` with the default `skip_with_substr=False`, which performs exact `prefix in ignored_layers` match. The vLLM runtime prefix is the full path (e.g. `language_model.model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkv`), so the short pattern from the checkpoint never matches → the layer is fp8-quantized despite missing `weight_scale`, and the model outputs gibberish. This is the FP8 counterpart of: - #26909 (AWQ) — introduced `skip_with_substr=True` opt-in - #27416 (AWQ-Marlin) - #29774 (IPEX-AWQ) The FP8 family (`Fp8Config`, `FBGEMMFp8Config`, `ModelOptQuantConfigBase`, `Mxfp4Config`, `DeepseekV4FP8Config`) was the only group still on the exact-match default. This PR opts FP8 in to the same behaviour. **Affected user-visible behaviour**: FP8 checkpoints exported by `llm-compressor` / `AutoFP8` with HuggingFace-style short patterns now correctly skip layers that were previously force-quantized. **Backwards compatibility**: substring match is a superset of exact match, so users who already wrote full paths in `modules_to_not_convert` still hit. No regression to existing fp8 / modelopt deployments. ## Test Plan New unit test file `tests/quantization/test_layer_skipped.py` (no GPU required) covering: - exact match (legacy default) — full path hit + short pattern miss (the bug) - substring match (new fp8 default) — short pattern hit + full path hit + unrelated miss - fused map
