title: [Model] Optimize Qwen3-VL image preprocessing with compact patches
summary: ## Purpose This PR optimizes the Qwen3-VL still-image preprocessing subpath used by text+image requests. For Qwen3-VL still-image inputs, the original processor path materializes duplicated temporal image patches: ```text pixel_values [N, C*T*P*P] ``` For still images, the temporal frames are duplicates. This PR introduces a compact image-patch representation: ```text pixel_values [N, C*P*P] ``` `Qwen3_VisionPatchEmbed.forward()` handles this compact image representation by summing the temporal dimension of the Conv3D kernel weights: ```text sum_t W[:, :, t, :, :] * image_patch + bias ``` This is mathematically equivalent to applying the original Conv3D to duplicated temporal image patches. The PR also adds a fused compact preprocessing helper for the guarded fast path: ```text uint8 BCHW -> fused normalize + compact patchify -> float32 compact patches [num_patches, C*P*P] ``` This avoids materializing the full intermediate normalized BCHW tensor before compact patchification. The fast path is guarded to still-image preprocessing inputs and falls back for video inputs, unsupported inputs, or unsupported processor kwargs. Tokenizer-only kwargs such as `truncation=False` are not forwarded to the direct image-processor path, including fallback cases where the compact fast path is not used. Related issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44688 Duplicate-work check: I searched open PRs for `44688 in:body` and `Qwen3 VL compact image preprocessing`; I did not find an existing open PR covering this change. AI assistance was used while preparing and validating this chang

title: [KVConnector] Add prefix-length threshold for lazy SimpleCPUOffloadConnector
summary: ## Purpose This PR adds an optional prefix-length threshold for lazy CPU KV offload in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. This is an incremental enhancement to the existing `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` lazy offload mode; it does not change eager offload behavior or introduce a new connector. When `lazy_offload_min_prefix_tokens` is set in `kv_connector_extra_config`, the scheduler records block hashes from requests whose full-attention prefix length reaches the threshold. The lazy scanner then offloads only those candidate hashes. This lets lazy CPU offload prioritize blocks from longer prefixes that are more likely to be reused. The default behavior is unchanged: - `lazy_offload_min_prefix_tokens` defaults to `0`. - With the default value, lazy offload scans and stores eligible hashed GPU blocks as before. - The new filtering is only active when a positive threshold is configured. Implementation notes: - The threshold is token-based. - The prefix length is computed using the full-attention KV group's block size, rather than assuming `scheduler_block_size == hash_block_size`. - The lazy offload candidate hash set is bounded to avoid unbounded growth in long-running serving processes. - This PR does not add JSONL stats or new metrics output. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -q python -m ruff check --no-cache \ vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \ vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \ tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/vllm-pycompile python -m py_compile \

title: [Feature]: Avoid duplicate KV block allocation for shared external-prefix hits
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Please add a vLLM core mechanism to let concurrent KVConnector requests share one local GPU KV materialization for the same exact external prefix. Today the external-hit path reports `num_external_computed_tokens`, and vLLM allocates recipient-owned GPU KV blocks for each request. For concurrent requests `x+a` and `x+b`, where `x` is the same exact external KV-cache hit, there is no generic way for both requests to reference one local materialization of `x`. Connector-level alternatives are all trade-offs: duplicate loads waste IO/GPU KV space, delaying followers can create request convoys, and returning a miss recomputes known external hits. See related work: #29087, #44294, #44295, #44223, #38474. Desired behavior: the first request hitting exact external prefix `x` allocates/materializes local blocks once; later requests with the same exact external prefix attach their prefix block table to the same blocks and increment refcounts, similar to a local prefix-cache hit. If the entry is still loading, followers wait on the same materialization without issuing another load or allocating another copy. A first scope could be exact, contiguous, block-aligned prefix reuse only. This likely needs scheduler, `KVCacheManager`/`BlockPool`, and `KVConnectorBase_V1` support because connector metadata alone is too late: block allocation happens before `update_state_after_alloc()`. ### Alternatives 1. Duplicate per-request external loads: preserves concurrency but wastes IO and GPU KV space. 2. Connector-side in-flight gating: saves IO/space but ca

title: fix(multimodal): support gemma4 QAT configs by adding safe num_soft_t…
summary: ## Purpose Hey everyone! I was trying to serve the official Gemma 4 quantized model (`google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct`) using vLLM on a cloud pod, but the server immediately panicked and crashed with a fatal exception: `AttributeError: 'Gemma4UnifiedVisionConfig' object has no attribute 'num_soft_tokens'` inside `encoder_budget.py` via `gemma4_unified.py`. To figure out why, I dug into the code and compared the `config.json` metadata files of both the standard unquantized base model and this quantized variant. I found out that the non-quantized model explicitly contains the `num_soft_tokens` attribute inside its `vision_config` block, but the serialized QAT export completely drops it. Because vLLM currently relies on a strict dot-property lookup, the missing key instantly brings down the engine. I noticed someone else ran into a very similar brick wall in an issue raised here: #45039. ### 🛠️ Proposed Solution I figured a safe fallback approach would prevent this crash entirely. This PR switches out the strict dot-property lookup inside `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py` with a safe Python `getattr()` lookup. If the attribute is missing (like in the QAT checkpoint), it gracefully falls back to Gemma 4's architecture standard of `280` tokens. I'm going to keep looking at it on my end, but I thought this quick patch would be a solid way to bridge the gap for now. If there's anything else I am missing or if you'd prefer a different architecture fallback pattern, please do let me know—all learning here! 😊

title: [Kernel] NVIDIA-tuned tile configs + PID swizzling for triton_scaled_mm (up to 1.6x on H800, 2.0x on L20)
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #44998. `triton_scaled_mm` selects tile sizes with a fixed heuristic introduced in #11698 ("avg 2.8x speedup for **int8** models"), tuned on AMD: it keys only on `M` (four buckets), ignores `N`, and never tunes `num_warps`/`num_stages`. On NVIDIA this leaves substantial performance unused (data in #44998). This PR: - adds **per-architecture tuned tile tables** for sm_89 (Ada) and sm_90 (Hopper), derived from an offline sweep of (tile, num_warps, num_stages, group ordering) over representative W8A8 linear shapes; - adds **L2-friendly grouped program ordering** (PID swizzling) to the kernel. `GROUP_SIZE_M=1` reduces exactly to the original row-major order (`pid_m = pid // num_pid_n`), which is what non-tuned paths use; - is **compile/cudagraph-safe by construction**: config selection is a cached pure-Python dict lookup (same class as the existing heuristic) — no `@triton.autotune`, no runtime benchmarking (cf. #26993); - **leaves AMD and unknown architectures untouched**: non-CUDA platforms and CUDA capabilities without a tuned table fall back to the existing heuristic with `GROUP_SIZE_M=1` and default `num_warps`/`num_stages`, i.e. byte-identical launch behavior. Where the sweep found nothing beating the default (sm_89, M-bucket 128 with small N), the table keeps the default config explicitly. - Bonus: `use_heuristic=False` previously crashed with `NameError` (`tile_shape` undefined); it now respects the `block_size_*` arguments. **Not a duplicate**: #20163 (NVIDIA AOT autotuning + PID swizzle, Draft) was closed unmerged when the author's fork was deleted —

title: [RFC]: Forward ReqContext from CPUOffloadingManager to CachePolicy for session-aware KV eviction
summary: ### Motivation. This is a follow-up to the KV Offloading Roadmap (#33689), which already lists "Add request ID to RequestContext" (done in #42507) and "Create an offloading policy abstraction" among its items. Since #42507, `ReqContext` carries `req_id` and is available to `OffloadingManager` API calls; vLLM also has request-level offloading semantics via `OffloadPolicy.REQUEST_LEVEL` ([source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1ae1051b4bf6e7e98d61b15527040f63eda73a0b/vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py#L60-L63)). However, for the native CPU backend this context currently stops at `CPUOffloadingManager`: `touch(keys, req_context)` calls `CachePolicy.touch(keys)`, and `prepare_store(keys, req_context)` performs policy get/evict/insert operations without exposing `req_context` or store-batch boundaries to the policy ([source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1ae1051b4bf6e7e98d61b15527040f63eda73a0b/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py#L141-L203)). The missing boundary is specifically manager → policy. This matters for multi-turn serving. The value of offloaded prefix KV is *chain-shaped*: a lookup recovers only a contiguous leading run of a request's blocks, so isolated blocks are worthless without their predecessors. Block-centric policies cannot see this structure. In controlled multi-turn experiments on a capacity-constrained CPU tier (details below), we observed: - **LRU and ARC deliver zero recoveries.** Across 3 runs each on a cyclic-revisit workload (6 sessions, ~2K-token prefixes, tier sized to ~2 complete prefixes), neither policy served a single load; their sto

title: [Tokenizer] Add batch_split_message tokenizer mode for lossless segmented encoding
summary: ## Motivation In multi-turn / long-conversation serving, the tokenization stage takes a non-trivial slice of TTFT: the prompt grows long, the HF fast tokenizer encodes a single long sequence on one thread, and tokenization cost grows linearly with prompt length. This PR introduces a lossless segmented parallel-encoding scheme, plus a cache for long, highly-reusable segments, substantially cutting the tokenization latency in multi-turn / long-sequence serving. `batch_split_message` cuts tokenization latency in two independent ways: - **Parallelism:** split the text on a special-token delimiter (default: eos) and encode the segments in a single `encode_batch`, which the underlying Rust tokenizer parallelizes across segments — so the tokenization cost drops from encoding the whole prompt to encoding the longest single segment. - **Segment reuse (optional cache):** in many deployments the system prompt and tool definitions are a large, fixed share of the prompt and are fully reusable across requests, while the user message is far smaller than these segments. With those long segments cached, the tokenizer only needs to encode the user segment. It is lossless: when the delimiter is a registered special token (a hard BPE boundary), the produced token ids are byte-for-byte identical to a single `encode()`. ## What it does - `encode(text)` → split on delimiter → `encode_batch(segments)` (parallel) → concat with the delimiter ids in between. - **Lossless guard:** for tokenizers that inject specials on encode (`num_special_tokens_to_add() > 0`), the completion path (`add_special_token

title: Turboquant native fp8 v4 store
summary: Related to #40069. Add a native CUDA store path for TurboQuant `turboquant_k8v4` FP8-key / 4-bit-value KV cache storage on Hopper+ GPUs. The existing Triton store path remains the fallback. The native path is only selected when the request matches the supported contract: - FP8 key path - 4-bit value quantization - CUDA device using Hopper+ E4M3 FP8 - contiguous int32 `slot_mapping` - native op is built and available This also adds a kill-switch through `VLLM_DISABLE_TURBOQUANT_NATIVE_STORE` and validation guards in the C++ wrapper. ## Test Plan - Add byte-parity coverage comparing the native CUDA store against the existing Triton store. - Cover fp16 and bf16 inputs. - Cover `D=127`, `D=128`, and `D=256`. - Cover FP8 saturation with large key values. - Cover negative slot mappings. - Add an H100 Buildkite lane for the native store parity test so it does not silently skip on non-Hopper CI workers. ## Test Result Local static checks passed: ```bash git diff --check main...HEAD python3 -m py_compile \ vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_turboquant_store.py \ vllm/_custom_ops.py \ vllm/envs.py \ tests/quantization/test_turboquant.py uvx ruff check \ vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_turboquant_store.py \ vllm/_custom_ops.py \ vllm/envs.py \ tests/quantization/test_turboquant.py uvx ruff format --check \ vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_turboquant_store.py \ vllm/_custom_ops.py \ vllm/envs.py \ tests/quantization/test_turboquant.py I could not run the CUDA parity test locally because this machine does not have a CUDA/Hopper environment. title: [Feature]: Add a 2-bit KV-cache quantisation backend from Together AI
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Purpose Integrate a new INT2 KV-cache quantisation backend. Paper:**OSCAR** ([arXiv:2605.17757](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17757)). Code: https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/OSCAR (500+ stars, proved to be working on Qwen3-32B, GLM-4.7-FP8.) Website: https://oscar-quantize.github.io/ vLLM already has TurboQuant, a data-free Hadamard-rotation KV-cache quantizer. Oscar is similar, but has better accuracy. If we apply the most aggresive quantisation method in TurboQuant, (`turboquant_3bit_nc`), the accuracy will drop by 20%. But with Oscar, for Qwen3-32B and GLM-4.7-FP8 respectively, the mean gap to BF16 is −0.02, and +0.27 points while reducing KV memory by ~8× and increasing large-batch throughput by up to ~7×. The main idea is, before applying clipped INT2 scalar quantization, we first apply a per-layer covariance-aware orthogonal rotation to distribute the values evenly, so they can be later de-quantised with higher precision. To use this feature, just need to load the original model checkpoints, and download a small per-layer rotation file (`[head_dim, head_dim]` orthogonal matrices, a few MB), published in the [OSCAR RotationZoo](https://huggingface.co/Zhongzhu/OSCAR-RotationZoo). ## CC List Paper author: @zzz0906 vLLM maintainer: @mgoin, @robertgshaw2-redhat ## Implementation Details - We stored rotation matrix for K and V. - Then, we use the same fp16 `(scale, zero)` parameter for each vector. title: [Quantization] Align online fp8_ptpc/block_fp8/mxfp8 weight quantization with llm-compressor (compressed-tensors) export
summary: ## Purpose vLLM's online (quantize-at-load) FP8 paths produced weights that did **not** numerically match the offline llm-compressor / compressed-tensors checkpoints for the same recipe. The divergences came from vLLM's own quant helpers using different scale math, clamping, and rounding than compressed-tensors: - **Block FP8** (`per_block_cast_to_fp8`): fp32 reciprocal-multiply scale and a `1e-4` amax floor. - **PTPC / channel FP8** (`scaled_fp8_quant`): different scale dtype handling. - **MXFP8** (`mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` / FlashInfer): E8M0 exponent calculation disagrees with compressed-tensors. This PR ports the numeric steps used by compressed-tensors' offline export into a small in-tree helper (`online/quant_utils.py`) so the online path stays **numerically equivalent** (and byte-for-byte identical for the weight quant) without importing compressed-tensors APIs from the online quantize-at-load path: - Add `_quantize_fp8_blockwise`, `_quantize_fp8_channelwise`, and a shared `_quantize_fp8_symmetric` (via local `_symmetric_fp8_scale` / `_quantize_fp8`) for `online/fp8.py`, replacing `per_block_cast_to_fp8` and `scaled_fp8_quant` in both the linear and MoE paths. - Add `_quantize_mxfp8` (via local `_generate_mx_scales` / `_round_to_uint8` / `_quantize_fp8`) for `online/mxfp8.py`, replacing `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` for the linear and MoE paths. - Add `OnlineQuantizationConfig.apply_vllm_mapper` so the `ignore` list is remapped from HF to vLLM module naming (mirroring `CompressedTensorsConfig.apply_vllm_mapper`); without it the online path would quantize layers the offline check

title: [CPU] Add hierarchical all-reduce with RDMA for multi-node tensor parallelism
summary: ## Purpose This PR adds an opt-in **Hierarchical All-Reduce (HAR)** path to the CPU backend to make **multi-node tensor parallelism** practical on Arm Grace (and other CPU) clusters. Today the CPU backend reduces activations with a flat gloo/TCP ring all-reduce. On a 2-node setup this crosses the slow inter-node link on every collective (~96 collectives/token for Qwen2.5-14B), so decode becomes network-bound and throughput collapses (5.47 tok/s at TP=4). A flat ring is also topology-blind and, at TP=4, fails to make cross-node TP usable. HAR replaces the flat ring with a two-level collective: - **Intra-node:** shared-memory (SHM) reduce — no syscalls, no NIC. - **Inter-node:** a single **RDMA Write-with-Immediate** hop over libibverbs (kernel-bypass, zero-copy), with each rank owning its own queue pair (4-way direct exchange, no leader relay). The PR also includes two related changes: - **Topology-aware logits all-reduce:** the per-token vocab-wide logits gather (the last collective still on gloo/TCP) is re-routed onto the HAR/RDMA path when ranks span nodes; single-node deployments keep the original fast SHM reduce. - **Dynamic RDMA buffer sizing:** the registered RDMA region is right-sized to the model (≈148 MB vs a 256 MB static default for Qwen2.5-14B) to stay resident in the NIC's MTT cache and avoid an address-translation thrashing regression. The entire RDMA path is gated behind a CMake build option **`VLLM_CPU_RDMA_HAR` (default `OFF`)**. title: [Core] Add scheduler-orchestrated worker transfers for multi-node KV cache tiering
summary: ## Summary This PR enables multi-node TP CPU-offloaded KV cache to write to and read back from a shared filesystem via a scheduler-orchestrated, worker-executed secondary-transfer path. In the existing single-node offloading design, CPU KV cache shards are locally visible through the shared mmap region. In multi-node TP, each worker owns a rank-local CPU mmap slice, and the scheduler cannot directly access remote-node CPU shards. This PR extends tiering offload so the scheduler still owns policy, lookup, promotion, and lifecycle, while workers only execute typed transfer specs for rank-local CPU-shard <-> shared-filesystem copies. It also hardens the multi-node path around explicit global-rank selection, worker-transfer failure propagation, partial-store cleanup, MoE/MTP canonical tensor layout handling, and compatibility with upstream #46713's filesystem C batch lookup. ## Design **Scheduler owns policy and lifecycle.** `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` continues to decide when to offload, which blocks move to secondary tiers, and how lookup, promotion, eviction, reset, and completion are handled. **Worker only executes transfer specs.** Workers receive typed `TransferSpec`s through connector metadata, execute data movement, and report completion/failure. A worker does not own a secondary tier, eviction policy, lookup policy, or promotion policy. **Eager write-through is preserved.** The GPU -> CPU primary-store path remains eager. title: docs: add note on bitsandbytes batch size dependency
summary: ## Summary This PR adds a note to the `bitsandbytes` quantization documentation regarding the throughput impact at small batch sizes. As discussed in issue #14526 (hypothetical reference based on community findings), `bitsandbytes` INT8/INT4 weight-only quantization involves a dequantization step before matrix multiplication. While this reduces memory usage, it introduces significant overhead for memory-bandwidth-bound workloads when batch sizes are small (e.g., batch=1). This overhead is typically amortized at batch sizes of 8 or greater. ## Changes - Added a "Note on Batch Size Dependency" section to `docs/features/quantization/bnb.md`. - Recommended benchmarking INT8 vs FP16 on target hardware for single-request serving scenarios. This clarification helps users avoid unexpected performance regressions in production latency-sensitive endpoints.

title: [RFC]: KVarN: a calibration-free, variance-normalized sub-8-bit KV-cache quantization backend
summary: ### Motivation. KV cache is the dominant memory cost for long-context and high-concurrency serving. vLLM already supports fp8 KV cache (~2x capacity) and, as of [#38479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38479), a sub-4-bit rotation-based backend (**TurboQuant**). But sub-4-bit KV quantization is still rarely turned on in production, for one reason: **it costs throughput and accuracy.** As vLLM's own [TurboQuant blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-05-11-turboquant) reports, existing sub-4-bit methods buy 2.3 to 3.7x capacity but give up **40 to 52% of throughput**, and aggressive low-bit quant also tends to cost accuracy. Losing both speed and quality is why the feature stays off. **KVarN** ([arXiv:2606.03458](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03458)) is a variance-normalized KV-cache quantization scheme built to keep all three at once: capacity, throughput, and accuracy. - **~3.2 to 3.4x measured KV-cache capacity** at int4-K / int2-V. - **Throughput at or above FP16/baseline in the memory-bound regime**, *uniquely* among KV-quant backends (measured +9% at 14B, rising to +18% at ~106B), not the throughput regression every other sub-4-bit method pays. - **FP16-level accuracy**, calibration-free, no model changes, one flag (measured lossless on Qwen3-14B/30B and GLM-4.5-Air). It also covers models TurboQuant cannot: it supports MLA, and it runs on hybrid and sliding-window models. TurboQuant supports full-attention and uniform sliding-window only. title: [Frontend] Add idle timeout for /v1/realtime audio sessions
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #46815. On `/v1/realtime`, a client can hold engine resources indefinitely by keeping the websocket open and never sending more audio or a `final` commit. Once a non-final commit starts generation, `_run_generation` reads from `audio_stream_generator`, which blocks on the audio queue when the client stops sending chunks. The `engine.generate()` request stays alive and its KV cache is never released, so a few stale clients can push KV cache usage to 100% and require restarting the server. This adds an idle watchdog to `RealtimeConnection`: - New env var `VLLM_REALTIME_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (default `30`, set `0` to disable). - The timer only resets on real activity: a valid `input_audio_buffer.append`, or a non-final `commit` that actually starts generation. Repeated no-op commits do not reset it. - On timeout it sends an `idle_timeout` error event, enqueues the `None` sentinel so in-flight generation finishes and releases its KV cache, force-cancels after a short grace period if it does not stop, then closes the socket. The existing `cleanup()` path handles the rest. Clients that stream audio and send `final=True` behave exactly as before. Setting the env var to `0` restores the old behavior. ## Test Plan New unit tests, no GPU or model needed: ``` pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/test_realtime_idle_timeout.py -v ``` They cover the idle close path, activity resetting the timer, graceful finalize on the sentinel, force-cancel of a stuck generation, and the `0` disable switch. ## Test Result ``` 5 passed in 1.10s ``` `ruff check` and `ruff format --

title: Fix plain FP8 MLA KV cache page size
summary: ## Summary This PR is for the bug #46985 Fix plain FP8 MLA KV cache page-size accounting for `MLAAttentionSpec` and `SlidingWindowMLASpec`. Plain FP8 MLA cache formats (`fp8`, `fp8_e4m3`, `fp8_e5m2`) store one combined MLA KV vector per token using one byte per FP8 element. The per-tensor scales are stored outside the KV cache tensor, so they should not be included in the KV page-size calculation. Previously, these formats fell through to the generic dtype-based formula. That can overestimate KV cache memory when the semantic/cache dtype is not already a 1-byte dtype, causing vLLM to reserve fewer usable blocks or mis-size memory for plain FP8 MLA variants. ## Changes - Add explicit plain FP8 MLA handling in: - `MLAAttentionSpec.real_page_size_bytes` - `SlidingWindowMLASpec.real_page_size_bytes` - Preserve existing `fp8_ds_mla` custom-layout handling. - Add regression coverage for plain FP8 MLA and sliding-window MLA page sizing. ## Tests Passed: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m py_compile vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py git diff --check .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ``` Also passed via commit hooks: - ruff check - ruff format - typos - mypy - SPDX header check - forbidden imports check - torch.cuda API check - config validation - Attention backend documentation check - sign-off commit hook Blocked: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/test_kv_cache_interface.py -v ``` The existing `.ven

title: [RFC]: Qwen3-ASR pseudo-streaming can repeat or miss segments
summary: ### Motivation. I have been experimenting with Qwen3-ASR pseudo-streaming based on the `response_prefix` / prefix-feedback approach discussed in: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35908 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36018 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35894 Thanks to the contributors of these discussions and PRs. They provide a useful path for REST/realtime pseudo-streaming ASR. In my local tests, this approach works well for English. After normalizing punctuation and whitespace, English content similarity between full-audio transcription and batched pseudo-streaming transcription can reach around `0.99`. However, for Arabic/Thai and some Chinese cases, pseudo-streaming can enter repeated generation loops or miss transcript segments after repeated rounds are filtered. Based on these experiments, using `response_prefix` as the main mechanism for carrying streaming context does not seem robust enough for production multilingual ASR. ## Observations The pseudo-streaming loop I tested is: text ``` 1. Split audio into chunks. 2. Send a sliding audio window to /v1/audio/transcriptions. 3. Keep stable transcript text locally. 4. Send stable text back as response_prefix. 5. Merge the new response into the final transcript. ``` For long audio, around 120 seconds, with 10-second chunks and a 30-second sliding window, I observed: - English: content-normalized result is very close to full-audio transcription. - Arabic/Thai: some windows can generate thousands of repeated words/tokens. - Chinese: some windows can enter repeated short-phrase loops.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Surface out-of-range token ids as a clear per-request error
summary: ## Purpose An out-of-range token id coming from the model (e.g. NaN/overflow in the forward pass yields a garbage sampled id) is currently handled poorly by the fast (Rust `DecodeStream`) detokenizer path: - It is passed straight to `tokenizers.DecodeStream.step`, which raises a cryptic `TypeError: argument 'id': StreamInput must be either an integer or a list of integers`. - The existing `except (OverflowError, TypeError)` handler — added in #24351 / #26445 for the rare **in-range** overflow in #21951 — logs a **full traceback per token** and returns an empty token. So when the model produces *systematically* corrupt ids, you get thousands of stack traces plus a silently empty / garbage completion, with no clear signal of the real problem. Seen in the wild on ROCm gfx950 serving DeepSeek-R1 with an fp8 KV cache, where a metadata bug (since fixed by #46997) corrupted decode output into out-of-range (negative) token ids: ~19k tracebacks followed by engine death, and on well-formed prompts a silent accuracy collapse. ## Change - `FastIncrementalDetokenizer`: validate `0 <= token_id < vocab_size` **before** the `DecodeStream` step and raise a clear `InvalidTokenIDError` naming the id and valid range. This is also stricter than the Rust binding, which silently accepts any `u32` (so an in-`u32`-range but out-of-vocab id would otherwise be mis-decoded rather than flagged). - `OutputProcessor`: catch `InvalidTokenIDError` and abort **only that request** (`FinishReason.ABORT`) with a single clear log line; the server and other in-flight requests keep running. - In-range step overfl

title: [LoRA] Add DoRA support for serving and linear layers
summary: ## Purpose #10849 This PR adds initial DoRA support for vLLM LoRA serving. The supported scope is the dense linear path, runtime adapter loading, mixed LoRA/DoRA batches,tensor parallel dense linear layers, and common packed linear layers such as QKV and gate-up projections. The implementation follows PEFT DoRA semantics by loading `lora_magnitude_vector`, precomputing the per-output DoRA scale from `magnitude / ||W + BA||`, and applying that scale only to requests using a DoRA adapter. Bias handling is kept consistent with DoRA: the scale is applied to the weight path, not to the added bias. Unsupported paths fail closed instead of silently producing incorrect outputs. This includes quantized layers, embeddings, logits processor, fused MoE LoRA, and fully sharded LoRA paths.Follow-up PRs can add quantized backends, MoE/EP support, and Punica/Triton fusion with benchmarks once the supported correctness path is in place. ## Test Plan Added focused coverage for DoRA checkpoint loading, magnitude-vector validation,DoRA scale computation, PEFT parity, bias handling, mixed base/LoRA/DoRA batches, TP=2 row/column linear paths, and packed QKV/gate-up projections. Also added serving tests for static and runtime-loaded DoRA adapters, concurrent base/LoRA/DoRA requests, unload/reload/replace behavior, and failed adapter loads that should not corrupt existing adapters. ## Test Result All tests passed. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_peft_helper.py tests/lora/test_lora_checkpoints.py tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_layers.py tests/lora/test_dora_mixed

title: [Bugfix] Load per-shard per-tensor FP8 scales for fused GDN in_proj (Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next)
summary: ## Purpose Loading a **ModelOpt per-tensor FP8** checkpoint for **Qwen3.5** (and, by extension, other Gated-Delta-Net models such as **Qwen3-Next**) currently crashes at weight-load time: ``` AssertionError: assert loaded_weight.shape[0] == 1 (vllm/model_executor/parameter.py, PerTensorScaleParameter._load_into_shard_id) ``` ### Root cause The GDN input projection fuses q/k/v into a single on-disk `in_proj_qkv` weight, which maps to shards `(0, 1, 2)` of the `in_proj_qkvz` `MergedColumnParallelLinear`. A ModelOpt per-tensor FP8 checkpoint stores **one scale per q/k/v shard** — a length-3 vector. `MergedColumnParallelLinear.weight_loader_v2` only handled the "single shared scalar, broadcast to every shard" case for tuple shard ids, so it passed the whole `[3]` scale to each shard and tripped the `assert loaded_weight.shape[0] == 1` check in `PerTensorScaleParameter`. ### Fix When a fused per-tensor scale has exactly one element per shard (`shape == [len(shard_id)]`), slice it per shard; otherwise keep the existing broadcast behavior. This matches the `PerTensorScaleParameter` contract ("N scales for N logical matrices") and mirrors how the fused weight tensor itself is already split. Fully backward compatible (blockwise FP8 and single-scalar per-tensor paths are unchanged). ## Test Plan - Added `tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_5_quantization.py`: - `test_per_tensor_scale_tuple_shard_slices_per_shard` — a `[1,2,3]` scale with tuple shard id `(0,1,2)` lands as `[1,2,3,0]`. - `test_per_tensor_scale_tuple_shard_broadcasts_single_scalar` — a scalar `5.0` with tuple `(0,1)` broadc

summary: Fixes #42593. ### Purpose `--enable-return-routed-experts` is only valid for MoE models. On dense models, vLLM previously accepted the flag and failed later during routed experts capturer initialization with an internal `AttributeError` after model loading and KV cache setup. ### What changed - Added an early config validation check that rejects `--enable-return-routed-experts` when the selected model is not a MoE model. - Kept the existing pipeline-parallelism and KV connector incompatibility checks in the same validation path. - Added focused config tests for dense-model rejection and MoE-model acceptance. ### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR I checked the issue comments and searched open PRs for `#42593`, `enable-return-routed-experts`, `routed experts`, `non-MoE`, and `num_experts_per_tok`. title: [RFC]: ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs instead of state for faster standard and speculative decode (Mamba2 + GDN)
summary: ### Motivation. ## Summary [ReplaySSM](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) is a memory-bandwidth optimization for the decode kernels of state space model (SSM) and linear attention layers. It is a collaboration between Dao AI Lab and NVIDIA; a concurrent cross-framework implementation is in the [TensorRT-LLM PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/14203). SSM decode is memory-bound: today each step reads and writes back the full recurrent state. ReplaySSM instead caches recent inputs, reconstructing the state only when needed and otherwise computing the output directly from the cache. This keeps most steps read-only and writes the full state back only once every L steps. ReplaySSM provides three benefits: 1. Memory-traffic reduction in a bandwidth-bound kernel: the per-step state write is replaced by a small input append. 2. Cheap rollback for speculative decoding: caching recent SSM inputs makes rollback a buffer pointer move, avoiding the separate per-draft-token state the current implementation keeps. 3. Parallel verification for speculative decoding: on non-flush steps the output is read directly without materializing the state, so a draft window is verified in one shot instead of by a serial recurrence. Implementation: we have opened a draft PR (#47576) implementing ReplaySSM in vLLM, based on the [ReplaySSM reference repository](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM). We are aware of the existing feature request #46187, which tracks ReplaySSM in vLLM and is assigned to us as the ReplaySSM authors. This RFC and the accompanying draft PR are the upstream

title: [RFC]: Opt-in incremental prompt encoding for multi-turn chat
summary: ## Motivation vLLM's frontend re-tokenizes the **entire** prompt on every request. In multi-turn chat this is almost pure waste: each request re-sends the whole conversation, so the rendered prompt of turn `N` is (in the overwhelmingly common case) a strict string prefix of the prompt of turn `N+1`. Tokenization cost is linear in conversation length, so per-turn TTFT degrades linearly with history size even when the KV cache has a 100% prefix hit: - For a ~200K-token history, a single full encode costs ~0.5 s on a typical host CPU — often *more* than the prefill itself once prefix caching kicks in. - The cost is paid on the API-server CPU, so under concurrent load it also competes with detokenization, chat-template rendering, and multimodal preprocessing for renderer threads (#39590 tracks frontend tokenization overhead more broadly). We ship this optimization in production on a DeepSeek-V4-Flash 2×DGX-Spark deployment (agentic coding workload, long conversations): **median multi-turn TTFT dropped from 0.92 s to 0.47 s**, with encode itself ~35× faster at the median, and token-exact output verified on every request (30/30 sampled turns exact; the always-on overlap verifier never had to fall back incorrectly). ### Relationship to existing work - **PR #45514 (segment-parallel tokenization / segment cache)** is adjacent but different: it splits a single large prompt into segments to tokenize them in parallel and/or cache segment encodings keyed by content. title: [Bug]: `vllm bench sweep serve_workload` crashes with "non-positive request rate" when max throughput < 1 req/s (integer floor/ceil of rate anchors)
summary: ### Environment Not environment-specific — this is a pure control-flow bug in the `vllm bench sweep serve_workload` CLI, so `collect_env.py` output is not relevant. Verified present on current `main` (permalinks below reference commit 9226613043573137, whose `vllm/benchmarks/sweep/serve_workload.py` is identical to `main`'s). Observed and reproduced twice on an RTX 4090 (24 GB) serving an 8K-token-input long-prompt workload, where batch throughput measures ≈ 0.425 req/s. ### 🐛 Describe the bug `vllm bench sweep serve_workload` (with the default `--workload-var request_rate`) deterministically crashes whenever the benchmarked deployment's maximum throughput is below 1 req/s — e.g. long-prompt workloads on a single consumer GPU. **Mechanism** After running the two anchor benchmarks (serial: `max_concurrency=1`; batch: `max_concurrency=num_prompts`), the measured throughputs are converted to `request_rate` sweep endpoints with integer rounding: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/922661304357313700340e787cfe19d58b8c0a2f/vllm/benchmarks/sweep/serve_workload.py#L155-L170 With serial ≈ 0.21 req/s and batch ≈ 0.425 req/s: 1. `serial_workload_value = math.ceil(0.21)` → `1` (L155) 2. `batch_workload_value = math.floor(0.425)` → `0` (L160) 3. `np.linspace(1, 0, workload_iters)[1:-1]` rounded to integers → intermediate levels `[0, 1]` (L167–L170) 4. The `request_rate=0` level is injected into the bench command (L69), and `vllm bench serve --request-rate 0` fails its rate validation while precomputing request intervals: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/922661304357313700

title: [Models] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP with GPTQ/AWQ quantization
summary: ## Summary MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) decoder layers in Qwen3.5 use **unquantized bf16 weights**, but when the main model is GPTQ/AWQ-quantized, the global `vllm_config.quant_config` propagates into `FusedMoE.__init__()` (via `get_current_vllm_config()`), causing shape mismatches and initialization failures. This patch: - Detects GPTQ/AWQ quantization in `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` - Temporarily overrides `vllm_config` with `quant_config=None` when constructing MTP decoder layers - Uses `object.__setattr__` + `set_current_vllm_config` context manager (because `dataclasses.replace` re-resolves quant_config in `__post_init__`) - Main model layers remain fully quantized ### Motivation Qwen3.5-35B-A3B models with GPTQ-Int4 quantization fail to load when MTP (speculative decoding) is enabled. The MTP layers in the checkpoint are stored as bf16, but vLLM applies the main model's GPTQ quantization config to them. ### Tested with - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4` with `--num-speculative-tokens 1` - Hardware: AMD Z13 Strix Halo APU (gfx1151, 128GB UMA) with ROCm 6.4 - Verified: MTP layers load as bf16, main model layers remain GPTQ-quantized Supersedes #44333 (closed due to branch deletion during rebase). ## Test plan - [x] Model loads successfully with `--num-speculative-tokens 1` - [x] MTP layers initialized as bf16 (confirmed via log output) - [x] Main model layers remain GPTQ-Int4 quantized - [x] Inference produces correct output - [ ] CI tests pass

title: V1 multiprocess engine: sporadic 0.7-2s frozen engine step once per generate batch (absent with VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0)
summary: ## Summary On vLLM **0.24.0** (V1 engine, default multiprocess topology), we observe a sporadic **0.7–2.0 s frozen engine step** — a single `llm_engine.step()` call whose wall time is 100–300× the surrounding steps — occurring roughly **once per generate batch** at a varying step index, with the freeze duration **growing over process lifetime**. title: [KV Offload] Prefetch secondary lookups on request admission
summary: ## Overview Start eligible secondary-tier metadata lookups when a request is admitted, so the lookup can overlap an already-running model step. With the EngineCore behavior from [#65466](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65466), an `ADD` can be handled while EngineCore waits for the current worker output; this lets admission submit the probe before that step completes. The normal scheduler lookup still decides the hit boundary and starts promotion. ## Claims - Avoid waiting for the next `on_schedule_end()` to submit eligible FS/OBJ probes. - Reuse the async lookup state at scheduler lookup time, so a probe is not submitted twice for the same key. - Filter admission candidates against the current GPU/CPU cache snapshot and bound candidate count and outstanding prefetch batches. - Keep promotion and primary-tier slot allocation on the normal lookup path. This follows the request-arrival lookup timing used by the merged [Mooncake #61292](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61292), adapted to `OffloadingConnector`'s tiered metadata lookup. Mooncake caches an async RPC result in its connector lookup client; this change reuses the FS/OBJ async lookup manager and filters GPU/CPU-resident chunks before probing secondary storage. It does not change the scheduler's final cache boundary or promotion decisions. Related work has a different scope: [#58198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58198) proposes a request-free CPU-to-GPU data load primitive, while this PR only starts secondary metadata probes for an admitted request. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fall back from InstantTensor for PP-local draft models
summary: ## Overview With pipeline parallelism, a speculative-decoding draft model that lives only on the last PP stage deadlocks at load time when the target uses `--load-format instanttensor`. title: [Bugfix][Elastic EP] Release a prepared reconfiguration when scaling fails
summary: A failed prepare or drain leaves `eep_scaling_state` active, so subsequent scales are rejected until the engine restarts. Release the prepared engine state and standby groups when prepare or drain fails, including external-LB peers waiting for drain completion. Preserve failure handling once the topology commit starts. ## Tests - Revision `37ce4eae3f`: seven CPU control-path regressions with injected failures passed. The same tests with the current main implementation failed all seven cases. Coverage includes prepare/drain failures, external peer failure, and preserving a committing state. - `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py::test_elastic_ep_releases_prepared_state_before_commit tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_abort_prepared_elastic_ep_preserves_committing_state tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py::test_external_elastic_ep_releases_state_when_peer_drain_fails -q` - Pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed for all changed files. Historical GPU validation, before the current main merge: **2× H200**, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, externally launched DP/EP ranks, TP=1, EPLB enabled. A single-rank scale request reproduced the stuck state; the fix released it and accepted a new reconfiguration. DP2 → DP3 still committed in about 33 seconds. This GPU scenario was not rerun on the current revision. A failed scale-up still requires recreating the joining rank before retrying because abort tears down its handshake.

title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add mamba_aware_lru CPU-tier eviction policy for hybrid models
summary: ## Overview Adds `mamba_aware_lru`, an opt-in eviction policy for the CPU offload tier of hybrid models (attention plus Mamba or other state-space layers). Under `lru`, a turn that loads a Mamba state from the tier also refreshes that state's rank, so states that the session's later turns no longer need outlive the cached context of idle sessions. `mamba_aware_lru` evicts those states first. On an AgentX replay (agentic coding traces) with Nemotron 3.5 Super, it cut recomputed prompt tokens per request by 18% and raised throughput by 3–6% over `lru`. #63808 applies the same rule to the GPU prefix cache, for serving without a CPU tier or with one smaller than the GPU cache. Related work, none of which changes how the CPU tier orders Mamba states: #50422 (session-aware eviction, model-agnostic), and #61282 and #50551 (keep more Mamba states in the GPU prefix cache). ## Claims - New built-in `"eviction_policy": "mamba_aware_lru"` for `CPUOffloadingSpec` and `TieringOffloadingSpec`. The default stays `lru`. - When a request finishes, each Mamba state it superseded moves to the eviction end (it is demoted). A state is superseded when an earlier request stored it as its deepest state (its tip), and this request's prefix passes it and holds a deeper cached state. Attention chunks, the deepest state, and states stored below their writer's tip, such as shared-prefix junctions (where prompts that share a prefix diverge), keep their LRU order. On models without Mamba groups, the policy evicts exactly like `lru`. - Outputs do not change: the policy only reorders evictions, and the load

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Use the group's own DCP factor for the SWA store mask
summary: ## Purpose The offloading scheduler passes the global `decode_context_parallel_size` to `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask` for every KV-cache group, and that mask scales the spec's block size by the factor it is given. A DCP-replicated sliding-window group (`dcp_sharded=False`, e.g. a non-DCP DSpark drafter next to a DCP target since #56723) therefore had its block span inflated by the DCP size. Under the default semantic-only retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`) the retained window tail ending at the replay boundary was stored at block index `aligned // (block_size * dcp)` instead of `aligned // block_size`, so the stored SWA chunks never formed a full window at any boundary a later request looks up. Every request then missed in the drafter group, and hence overall. Pass the group's effective DCP factor, matching how the GPU-side `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` and the offload `tokens_per_block` resolution already treat `dcp_sharded`. ## Test Plan - New unit test `test_dcp_replicated_swa_tail_store_then_lookup` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, run with the draft group replicated and DCP-sharded: checks which blocks are stored, then that a longer request sharing the prompt hits up to the DCP-aligned boundary. The replicated case fails without this change. - GPU: GLM-5.3 + `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-speculator.dspark` (window 2048) on a PCP8×DCP8×EP8 H200 prefiller with `OffloadingConnector` (TieringOffloadingSpec, 512 GiB), behind NIXL P/D. title: [RFC]: Prefix caching of Decision 3.0 `prefix_bidir` state blocks (hit cap, in-block checkpoints, CPU offload)
summary: ### Motivation. A Decision 3.0 `prefix_bidir` request (vllm-sr/d3-turbo, a Qwen3.5 hybrid: 48 Gated DeltaNet + 16 attention layers) asks many questions about one long *state* block. Each question is a separate prompt `state + question`. The state is read bidirectionally and the question causally. Today every question re-prefills the whole state, so a page of 26 questions over a 40–60K-token state spends most of its compute re-reading the same tokens. The state is a shared prefix. Caching it is not plain prefix caching, for four reasons: - a hit must stop where the bidirectional part ends, never inside it; - the Gated DeltaNet state has to be saved at that position, which is usually inside a Mamba block; - a hit inside a block must not write the block back to the cache under a key it doesn't match; - under memory pressure the saved state should come back from CPU memory rather than be recomputed. ### Proposed Change. On top of the PrefixLM schedulers from #63114 and the `prefix_bidir` support from #62584: 1. **Per-request prefix-cache hit cap**: `Request.max_cache_hit_length`. The scheduler sets it for PrefixLM requests (the end of the bidirectional part, minus one token for a whole-prompt state). Every lookup honours it: the local prefix cache and KV connectors (the native OffloadingConnector). 2. **Mamba prefill checkpoints at the cap.** The Gated DeltaNet state is saved inside the step at the cap's last multiple of a **prefix match unit** finer than the block: 16 tokens with the Triton/FLA prefill, 64 with FlashInfer. This builds on the internal prefill checkpoints of #52

title: [Feature][Frontend] Add local output resume support to run-batch
summary: ## Overview Add `vllm run-batch --resume` for local output files. Completed successful requests are skipped; failed and missing requests run again and append results instead of truncating the output. Fixes #60184. ## Claims - Match successful HTTP 200 responses without an error by `custom_id`. - Preserve existing complete records and recover an incomplete final JSONL record. - Reject duplicate input IDs and incompatible/corrupt output before model loading or output modification. - Avoid loading a model when every input request already succeeded. ## Validation Linux ARM64 CPU, real `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` weights: - Before: the new end-to-end test completes its first inference run, then fails because `--resume` is unrecognized. - After: 27 selected tests pass, including a real first run, recovery from successful/failed/partial output, and a completed-batch rerun that leaves output unchanged without loading a model. - Existing dispatcher/writer/validation coverage and new corrupt-record, partial-UTF8, URL, duplicate-ID, and skip-completed cases pass. ```bash VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \ -k "resume or validate_batch or dispatch or output_writer or unwritable" -q ``` Pre-commit and MkDocs build passed. The existing launcher Buildkite step includes this test file. Initial validation used Python sources on base `db3b0f0fae4b` and CPU native extensions from wheel commit `8e2beaa3bff5`; CUDA was not exercised. On 2026-10-29, merged `main` at `a0e31b7353cc` in `1aa17ed7`.

title: [Bugfix] Keep the MiniCPM-V-4.6 vision tower unquantized for GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints
summary: ## Overview Fixes #58943. The official MiniCPM-V-4.6 GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints store the vision tower unquantized, but vLLM built it as quantized, so the server crashed at startup. With this PR, vLLM builds these layers unquantized, which matches the checkpoints. ## Claims - `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6-Thinking-GPTQ` now loads and serves. Before, it failed during weight loading with `AttributeError: 'QKVParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'`. - `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6-AWQ` now loads and serves. Before, it failed while building the vision MLP with `ValueError: The input size is not aligned with the quantized weight shape`. - `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6-GPTQ` and `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6-Thinking-AWQ` have the same quantization config as the two above (read from the Hub). title: [Perf][Core] Skip idle KV cache groups in per-step allocation
summary: ## Overview Scheduler CPU per step scales with running requests × KV cache groups, because `allocate_slots` calls each single-type manager's `remove_skipped_blocks`, `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, `allocate_new_blocks` and `cache_blocks` for every request on every step, even though most steps cross no block boundary in most groups. DeepSeek-V4 with HiSparse has 27 groups, so at c=160 the scheduler accounts for much of the TPOT. This PR skips a group's per-step calls until the request reaches a token count where they could do something. Related: #63934 skips the whole allocation pass for a request, but only for FullAttention/SlidingWindow groups whose block size equals the hash block size. That rules out mixed-block-size layouts such as DSv4. ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4-Flash + HiSparse, TP4 B200, 8k/1k, c=160: mean TPOT 28.4 → 23.9 ms (−16%), output throughput +13%. - GLM-5.3-NVFP4 + HiSparse (42 groups, all block size 64), 8k/1k, c=16/160/256: no change. That workload appears GPU-bound. - gpt-oss-120b (full + sliding window), 1k/1k, c=512: no change. - Scheduler state is unchanged. Per-step digests of block tables, free/cached block counts, preemptions and prefix hits match main bit for bit across 16 configurations. ## Validation **E2E, B200.** DSv4 and gpt-oss runs are applied onto #53592 head `b03827c63b`. title: [Perf][HiSparse] Batch the coordinator's per-page residency bookkeeping
summary: ## Purpose The HiSparse coordinator updated residency one page and one resident group at a time, with a block-pool call per block. When a request's whole context is GPU-resident (~1.3k pages × 20 groups), one `schedule()` spends tens of ms in Python and stalls every running request. #65888 promotes completed P/D imports into GPU-resident pages, which makes that the common case on decoders. This PR batches each operation (adopt, unpin, writeback planning and completion, copy recording, free) into one pass per request and one block-pool call: for a fully resident request (~1.3k pages × 20 groups), each operation goes from ~26k single-block pool calls and residency lookups to one pool call and one lookup per group. `HiSparseResidentManager` gains `get_residency_pages`, `adopt_resident_pages` and `drop_resident_pages`, which touch only the requested pages, so per-step cost does not grow with context length. Behavior is unchanged, including the order blocks return to the free queue; two new tests pin that order. Not a duplicate: no open PR touches these loops. ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` - GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, concurrency 128) with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 2G` to force host offload. - Non-P/D and P/D host landing: 8×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, multi-turn agentic dataset (80K-token first turn,

title: [HiSparse] Add DeepSeek V4 support
summary: ## Summary HiSparse host offload for DeepSeek V4. Only the indexed C4 compressed KV goes to host. C128, SWA, indexer and compressor-state caches stay on GPU. - **Compressed rows:** a C4 row holds 4 tokens. Row slot mappings and row mirrors are derived from token slot mappings and spans. - **Split `fp8_ds_mla` rows:** a 576 B value plane, then an 8 B scale plane. Gather kernels, prefill staging and row DMA copy each plane. Host pages are packed. - **FlashMLA DSv4:** decode swaps top-k rows into the hot buffer. Prefill stages non-resident context per chunk, with one staging plan per chunk per step. - **Host mirroring:** C4 layers arm their host mirror from the connector. The model runner passes attention metadata to the connector only on full cudagraph replay, so on eager and piecewise steps `start_load_kv` reads it from the forward context. - **GPU block size:** packed GPU groups all pay the widest group's block bytes. C128 shares the indexer group, the block is sized to that group (~225 KB), and the other device groups are split to fit. This keeps the C4 compressor state (~0.9 MB/block) from setting the width. Overlap: #59209 (QSA) and #61243 (GLM-5.3-Flash) touch `vllm/v1/hisparse/{layout,runtime,binding}.py` but add neither DSv4 nor split rows. ## Validation DeepSeek-V4-Flash (rev 60d8d70), 4x B200, TP4, FlashMLA, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256`. title: [HiSparse] GLM-5.3-Flash support
summary: ## Purpose HiSparse didn't work on GLM-5.3-Flash. This PR makes it start, serve correctly, and fit 3.4–4.8× more concurrent long requests than serving without HiSparse. Fixes #59176. Flash is the first hybrid model on HiSparse: 11 of its 45 layers use sparse MLA, the rest use KDA (linear attention). ## Changes **Getting Flash to start and serve** - Read the top-k setting from the text config (Flash's top-level config is multimodal). - Fix a hang during CUDA graph capture. - One line in the GPU model runner: piecewise CUDA graph steps now give the HiSparse connector the attention metadata, as full-graph steps already do. Without it, Flash overflows a buffer once pages live on the host. - Fix a crash in `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` on Hopper caused by gaps in the indexer's top-k output. - Attention backends now declare whether they support HiSparse. FlashInfer on Hopper (wrong results on prefix-cache hits) and on SM120 (unvalidated) opt out. **Using GPU memory efficiently** All KV cache groups share one GPU pool whose blocks are sized for the biggest group. On Flash that's a ~1.1 MB KDA state, much bigger than what HiSparse's own groups need, so most of each block was wasted. Now HiSparse groups fill those blocks: - Hot-cache layers are packed together into each block (22 groups become 4). - Each indexer block holds several kernel pages instead of one. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Pass attention metadata to the connector on piecewise steps
summary: ## Overview MRv2 passes `attn_metadata` to the KV connector's `pre_forward` only on FULL CUDA graph steps. On piecewise and eager steps the HiSparse connector gets `None`, so `prepare_forward` skips its per-forward setup. That setup resets the swap-row step counter and binds the batch's decode/prefill state. DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM hide this because their attention layers call `prepare_for_batch` themselves. Kimi-K3.1's fused DSA path doesn't, so the step counter keeps growing across mixed steps until the worker raises: ``` ValueError: HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity: stop=76, capacity=64. ``` A probe showed one layer's `swap_in` handling 28 rows in one forward and 59 in the next, with no reset in between. The fix passes the same `attn_metadata` on both branches. The only connector that reads this kwarg is HiSparse, so no other connector sees a change. ## Validation HiSparse args for every run: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 20480 --max-num-seqs 64 --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":<N>}}'`. GSM8K: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8123 [--max-concurrency 64]` (1319 questions, 5-shot). Host traffic comes from `vllm:hisparse_cache_misses_total` and `vllm:hisparse_host_to_device_bytes_total`. | Model | Hardware | Revision | GSM8K | Host misses / H2D | |---|---|---|---|---| | Kimi-K3.1-Pro-pruned75, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`, pool 64 GiB | 4x B200

title: [Kernel][Perf] Optimize NVFP4 MoE CUTLASS quant on Blackwell
summary: ## Overview Speeds up the NVFP4 MoE experts quant kernels (`scaled_fp4_experts_quant`, `silu_and_mul_scaled_fp4_experts_quant`) on B200. With many experts, the per-row expert lookup makes these ops compute-bound on B200. This PR makes the lookup cheaper and cuts the instructions each thread executes. Each thread now handles one 16-element vector, which needs CUDA ≥ 12.9. Expert offsets are looked up with a bisect over a shared-memory copy of the expert tables when there are enough experts. At large expert counts, `scaled_fp4_experts_quant` gallops forward from the previous row's expert instead. One kernel now covers every token count, replacing `main`'s separate low-latency kernel. ## Claims - **`scaled_fp4_experts_quant` on B200:** 2.4–2.7× faster at 16384 tokens and 1.7–1.8× at 1024 tokens. - **`silu_and_mul_scaled_fp4_experts_quant` on B200:** 3.8–3.9× faster at 16384 tokens and 2.1–2.2× at 1024 tokens. - **End-to-end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (B200):** in vllm bench serve (1000 prompts, 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64), output throughput is 2.7% higher, mean TTFT 6.5% lower and mean TPOT 1.7% lower. - **One kernel for all sizes:** removes `main`'s separate low-latency kernel for small token counts; the new kernel is at least as fast at every measured size (1.35–3.0× at 1–16 tokens, on par at 64). - **New correctness tests** for both ops: `tests/kernels/moe/test_nvfp4_moe.py` - **New benchmarks** for both ops and various expert and token sizes: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_nvfp4_moe_quant.py` ## Validation **Correctness:** new tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_nvfp4_

title: [Performance]: Best practices for preventing GPU OOM in production
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance We are using vLLM to serve large language models in a production environment. Our primary requirement is **production stability and avoiding GPU OOM**, rather than maximizing GPU utilization or throughput. We would like to ask the vLLM community and maintainers: **What are the recommended best practices for configuring vLLM to minimize or prevent GPU OOM in production?** In particular, we would appreciate guidance on: * How to choose a safe `--gpu-memory-utilization` * How to balance `--max-model-len`, `--max-num-seqs`, and `--max-num-batched-tokens` * How much GPU memory safety margin should typically be reserved * Whether `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` is recommended for production deployments * How to account for GPU memory used by CUDA Graphs, activations, NCCL, workspaces, and other runtime components * How to perform stress testing to validate that a configuration is safe before deploying it to production We understand that there may be no configuration that can mathematically guarantee zero OOM under completely unbounded workloads. Our goal is to establish a **systematic and reproducible production-sizing methodology** so that, given a fixed model, GPU configuration, `max-model-len`, and expected workload, we can determine a sufficiently safe vLLM configuration. Any recommended production deployment guidelines, sizing formulas, profiling tools, or real-world best practices would be greatly appreciated. Thank you! ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance _No response_ ### Your current environm

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Fail fast on SM120 when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes
summary: ## Purpose Narrows this PR after review feedback (thanks @lucifer1004). Related to #56461 and #59203. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197 makes FlashInfer's SM120 sparse-MLA page sizes a runtime argument, so DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM120 no longer needs vLLM to switch to 64-token pages. #59846 serves V4.1 on SM120 with the existing 128-token kernel blocks and 32-token SWA pages. The geometry change this PR originally proposed is dropped. What remains is a startup guard. #5197 is in FlashInfer 0.7.1rc1/rc2 but not in the pinned 0.7.0.post1, whose SM120 decode kernels are instantiated only for 64-token pages. On such a build, V4.1 on SM120 currently fails with an error that does not name the cause. This PR checks for runtime page sizes when `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention` is constructed and raises: ``` FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 on SM120 requires FlashInfer >= 0.7.1 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197). ... ``` The probe uses FlashInfer's public `supported_sparse_mla_sm120_configs()` and reads `page_block_size_is_runtime` on the `dsv4` entry. That field exists only in builds that contain #5197, so the probe needs no version parse and works with dev builds. It sits next to the existing `has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_config` probe and runs only on the SM120 path. SM90 and SM100 behavior is unchanged. Once vLLM pins FlashInfer >= 0.7.1, the guard always passes on supported installs and only catches stale environments. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py -q ``` The new tests stub FlashInfer, so they run without an SM120 GPU. title: fix(sampler): ensure deterministic index ordering in top_k_per_row_prefill
summary: fixes #67192 `top_k_per_row_prefill` selects top-k elements across histogram passes, with bins strictly below the threshold bin written directly to `smemOutput` via `atomicAdd` slot reservation. because threads win atomic reservations in non-deterministic arrival order, the returned row indices are permuted across runs with identical inputs. downstream flashinfer sparse attention accumulates in output index order, causing bf16 numerical drift across layers. this sorts `smemOutput` by index prior to writing out to global memory when `!multipleBlocksPerRow` (prefill and merged decode passes), guaranteeing bit-exact deterministic ordering and monotonic memory access in downstream attention kernels. also adds an assertion verifying monotonic ordering in `test_top_k_per_row`.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Pack DSpark verify positions into one FlashMLA head tile on SM90
summary: ## Overview On SM90, packs each request's DSpark verify positions (1 + K tokens) into one 64-row FlashMLA head tile, instead of padding every position to 64 rows. This targets DeepSeek-V4.1 at TP8, where each rank has 8 heads. It sits behind `VLLM_DSV41_PACK_SPEC_DECODE=1`, off by default. Depends on vllm-project/FlashMLA#34 (per-row slot masks); FlashMLA is temporarily pinned to that branch. ## Claims - On H20, at DeepSeek-V4.1 TP8 c1-layer shapes with DSpark K=3 (98 requests × 4 positions, SWA 128 + top-k 512), the per-layer sparse-MLA decode cost goes from 334 µs to 147–282 µs, i.e. 1.12–2.29× faster. This includes all overheads: the packed kernel, the Q/O repack, and the amortized key-union build. The spread comes from how much the 4 positions' top-k lists overlap. - Output is the same as the unpacked path up to bf16 rounding: each position still sees exactly its own keys and attention sink. - *Projected, not yet measured:* +4–7% end-to-end decode throughput at the current production load (~39 running requests per TP8 replica), and +8–11% at c100–128. The basis: sparse MLA decode is 11 ms of a ~55 ms DSpark cycle at c98 in a production trace. ## Validation **Done (1× H20):** | Check | Result | |---|---| | Packed vs unpacked, same inputs. 2/4 slots, unequal per-slot lengths, overlap 0–1, random sink (`test_packed_spec_decode_matches_unpacked`) | max abs err 0.0039 | | FlashMLA SM90 sparse decode suite with the vllm-project/FlashMLA#34 build (no masks) | 4748/4748 | | pre-commit (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering) | pass | Kernel timing, CUDA graph, 50 iterations, K=3. summary: ## Overview In Mamba prefix-caching (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`) mode, intermediate prefill chunks end on the block grid. With the large blocks hybrid models get after page-size alignment, a sizeable part of `--max-num-batched-tokens` can silently stay idle on every prefill step. title: [Bugfix] build with param.dtype when one is not specified
summary: ## Purpose The Transformers modeling backend materializes meta parameters in the model dtype, discarding the dtype the modeling declared. A modeling that stores weights as fp8 with fp32 scales therefore gets them in bf16: the weights take twice the memory and the scales are rounded. Parameters declared without a dtype get the model dtype, and those declared with one keep it. So on `meta`, shapes and dtypes are as the modeling declares them. `init_parameters` then materializes every meta parameter in `model_config.dtype` ([here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/94febce7563ae2d67a062dc0f8ab408cd817f66c/vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py#L814-L826)), discarding the declared dtype. `from_pretrained` keeps it instead ([here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5b99c07c047ae2af90bafe66bb91650e5b06989f/src/transformers/core_model_loading.py#L1745-L1752)). title: Migrate from `mypy` to `ty`
summary: Depends on: - [ ] vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533 - [ ] Replace all `mypy` references with `ty` - [ ] #67295 --- `pre-commit` setup: - Use the official hook from [`astral-sh/ty-pre-commit`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty-pre-commit) with `--no-project`, so that `uv check` doesn't build vLLM to resolve its dynamic dependencies - Only run on the lower bound Python version instead of testing all supported versions. `ty` infers it from `requires-python` in `pyproject.toml`, and the official hook can't target other versions - Set `TY_OUTPUT_FORMAT=github` in CI so that `ty` emits GitHub annotations directly, so the `mypy` matcher can be deleted - Keep a `[tool.mypy]` config in `pyproject.toml` that mirrors the `ty` rules below, so contributors who run `mypy` locally get equivalent results (it is not run in CI) `ty` rules: - We don't want to install the full vLLM environment for type checking so we ignore any unresolved imports and attributes of those imports - In `tests/`, ignore `invalid-argument-type` and `invalid-assignment` because tests deliberately pass mocks and stand-ins where real types are expected (e.g. `SimpleNamespace` for `VllmConfig`) - In `tests/`, also ignore `missing-union-attribute` because accessing an attribute on an unexpected `None` fails the test anyway --- Progress: | Date | `ty` version | Errors | | - | - | - | | Dec 18, 2025 | 0.0.2 | 3900 | | Mar 24, 2026 | 0.0.2 | 3200 | | Sep 30, 2026 | 0.0.84 | 2146 | | Nov 12, 2026 | 0.0.101 | 2748 |

title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Refuse batch-invariant mode on the sparse indexer
summary: ## Summary `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` looks like it works on DSA / sparse-indexer models. It does not: the indexer's top-k has no batch-invariant backend, so which keys a row attends to can change with the rest of the batch. Every path is batch-dependent: | backend | what makes it batch-dependent | | --- | --- | | `auto` | switches kernels at `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS` (64) rows — `indexer_topk.py:_resolve_auto` | | `per_row` | picks among three algorithms from the **padded column count**, i.e. the batch's longest sequence (`sampler.cu`, `kSortingAlgorithmThreshold` / `kSplitWorkThreshold`); on gfx950 it also splits a row across blocks by row count | | `persistent` | sizes its cooperative launch from occupancy and the batch's max sequence length, and falls back to `per_row` when the launch does not fit (`topk.cu`) | | `cooperative` | only applicable under the 64-row cap, so it is by definition batch-conditional | None of this changes the logits. It changes tie-breaking and therefore the selection — and a different sparse selection is a different forward pass, not a rounding difference. The failure mode is silent: output drifts with concurrency instead of raising, which is exactly what #53257 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash non-deterministic at temperature=0, rate scales with concurrency) and #54521 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next greedy decoding non-deterministic from `persistent_topk`) describe. This PR refuses at construction, naming the batch-dependent inputs, instead of serving results the flag promises are batch-invariant. ## Why this matters beyond a debug flag The GLM-5 tech report attributes

title: [Performance]: Mamba1 packed prefill sizes the selective scan launch from the total packed length, so many short prompts prefill about 10x slower
summary:
Proposal to improve performance

I found this while working on my own project, a Mamba-based video deepfake detector that processes short clips (about 30 frames each). I benchmarked a scan kernel for it against vLLM's selective scan kernel on the same short-clip shapes, run as padded batches. In a follow-up comparison of packed and padded inputs, vLLM's kernel turned out to be much slower when the sequences were packed (varlen) than when the same tokens were given as a padded batch. I traced the gap to how the launch configuration is chosen, described below. Mamba1 prefill in vLLM shows the same slowdown when one step contains many short prompts.

The cause seems to be in csrc/mamba/selective_scan_fwd.cu. For packed (varlen) input, the kernel picks its launch configuration (threads per block and items per thread) from params.seqlen, which is the total number of tokens in the step, not the length of each sequence. Each sequence still gets its own block, so 64 prompts of 30 tokens each run with the largest configuration (2,048 time slots per block) when 128 would be enough. The results are correct; the extra slots are just wasted work.

Proposed fix: the Mamba metadata builder already knows the longest prefill length on the CPU (from query_start_loc_cpu), so it can pass that to the op as a new max_seqlen argument, defaulting to 0, which keeps the current behaviour. The kernel then picks the configuration from the longest sequence instead of the total.

summary: ## Overview Fixes #67227. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Evict invalid blocks of requests aborted mid-step
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61768. A request aborted in the same step its synchronous KV load fails leaves the scheduler before the failure report is processed, so its never-loaded blocks stay prefix-cache hits. This keeps the departing request's block ids until its in-flight outputs arrive, and evicts them when a late failure report names them. ## Claims - After a sync KV load failure whose owner was aborted in the same step, the invalid block and every block after it are evicted, under both `kv_load_failure_policy` values and with sync and async scheduling. With async scheduling or PP this relies on deferred freeing, which is on for a top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`; see Tradeoffs and limits for a top-level producer whose connector loads. - A later identical prompt recomputes instead of decoding from never-loaded KV (GPU: r2 cached 1904 → 0, output matches the full-recompute baseline). - An abort whose load succeeded keeps its valid cached KV (unchanged behavior). ## Validation **Tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`). title: [Bugfix] Do not initialize CUDA when importing vendored FLA

summary: ## Purpose On SM12x (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, sm_120), MXFP8 linear layers go through `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel`, i.e. `flashinfer.mm_mxfp8(..., backend="cutlass")`. The existing `--linear-backend b12x` selects `B12xMxfp8LinearKernel`, which is the native b12x library, a different code path. In a kernel microbenchmark it was not faster than CUTLASS on the shapes below, but end to end it matches this PR (see Test Result). title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Carry the PLE short-conv state from the last computed block in align mode
summary: > **Relation to #61601.** #61601 fixed the *write* side of the PLE state in align mode: the boundary checkpoints of the PLE group are now written, so the blocks stored in the prefix cache, offloaded to CPU/disk or sent over PD hold the correct conv state. This PR fixes the *read* side, which is still broken on `main`: when a request resumes from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector load or PD transfer), the PLE reads its initial conv state from the wrong block and never sees the state that was loaded. The original version of this PR fixed both halves; after rebasing on #61601 only the read-side fix remains. ## Purpose Fix the PLE (per-layer n-gram embedding) short-conv state handling of `qwen4_exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, so that a request resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD) reads the conv state that was loaded for it. Part of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tracking issue #55922 (KV offload section). Same component as #59642 (PD side of the PLE state). Possibly related symptoms: #55357 (episodic 0% MTP acceptance with prefix caching on), #53912. ## Root cause In align mode the PLE metadata builder (`short_conv_attn.py`) takes `block_table[:, 0]` of the align-gathered block table, i.e. the block of the last *scheduled* token, and uses it both to read the initial conv state and to write the final one. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Transfer the whole PLE short-conv page in disaggregated P/D
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #59642 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 0% MTP acceptance in disaggregated P/D serving with `NixlConnector`). The NIXL worker folds every KV cache layer that reports the same base address into one region (`register_kv_caches`, `if base_addr in seen_base_addresses`). In the block-outer HMA layout every cache group places its first page at byte 0 of the shared allocation, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the PLE short-conv state (`Qwen4ExpPLELayer`, a tp-replicated `MambaSpec`, page = `channels × (conv_state_len + num_spec_tokens)` = 245760 B) lands in the same region as layer-0 GDN, the layer-3 QSA ring and the layer-3 MLA indexer cache, and that region keeps the MLA page length (204800 B). The PLE descriptors built from `block_len_per_layer[_ple_region_index]` therefore transfer only 204800/245760 bytes of each PLE slot: 8534 of 10240 channels arrive on the decode worker, the rest is whatever the block held before (never zeroed: the block is exempt from zeroing because an async load is expected to overwrite it). With `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` the spec-decode short conv reads those stale columns, the layer-1 hidden state becomes NaN, the target logits are NaN and the rejection sampler rejects every draft (the generated tokens are garbage too, not just slow). This PR records the PLE page length at registration (`_ple_block_len`) and uses it for the PLE descriptors on both sides of the transfer (`_build_mamba_local` / `_build_mamba_remote`), exchanging it through `NixlAgentMetadata.ple_block_len` (optional, backward compatible) so the existing P/D geometry check still compare

title: [MoE] Release cached allocator blocks before mapping MegaMoE symmetric memory
summary: ## Overview With expert parallelism (EP > 1), DeepGEMM allocates the MegaMoE symmetric buffer through `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory`, which maps it with the CUDA driver, outside the PyTorch caching allocator. After the profile run, the allocator can hold most of the GPU in cached free blocks, and the driver allocation then fails with `CUDA driver error: out of memory` although that memory is free. With a single EP rank, DeepGEMM uses a plain `torch` allocation, which reuses the cached blocks, so it is not affected. `get_symm_buffer` now calls `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` before it creates a buffer. title: [Attention] Run SM90 FP8-KV attention on FA4 native FP8
