title: [Spec Decode] Fix EAGLE3 MRoPE decode-step position computation to use per-request delta
summary: ## Purpose In the EAGLE3 proposer, `_update_positions_dependent_metadata` computes MRoPE decode-step positions by replicating dimension 0 into dims 1 and 2: ```python self.mrope_positions[1:, :batch_size] = self.mrope_positions[0, :batch_size] ``` The target model uses a per-request `mrope_position_delta` in `MRotaryEmbedding.get_next_input_positions_tensor` to compute decode positions as `delta + context_len`, writing the same value to all 3 dims. For standard text decode tokens this is numerically equivalent to dim-replication, so acceptance rate is unaffected in the common case. However, when multimodal pruning is enabled, `recompute_mrope_positions` can update `req_state.mrope_position_delta` mid-request. `_gather_mm_embeddings` is called from within the speculative decode path, so a pruning event during spec decode causes the proposer's positions to advance from a stale base rather than the updated delta — a mismatch with the target model. This fix maintains a persistent pinned CPU buffer of per-request deltas in `GPUModelRunner`, kept current by `_update_states` (on batch changes) and `_gather_mm_embeddings` (on pruning events). A dirty flag gates a CPU→GPU copy at the start of each `propose()` call, so steady-state decode steps pay no allocation or copy cost. The `[batch_size]` delta slice is passed into `_update_positions_dependent_metadata`, computing all 3 dims as: ``` decode_pos = delta + seq_lens_after_kernel - 1 = delta + context_len ``` This matches the target model's formula and remains correct after any delta update. summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch With `--scheduling-policy priority`, the Completions, Chat Completions and Responses APIs take a `priority` body field and the `X-Vllm-Priority` header, which overrides the body. The speech-to-text endpoints take neither. Every transcription and translation request is scheduled at priority 0. Nothing tells the caller that the header was dropped. Priority scheduling lets one engine serve latency-sensitive and lower-priority traffic together, and the engine scheduler is the right place to enforce it, because it decides which chunks join each batch. The audio endpoints can't take part in that today. **Where it's missing (v0.33.0; the same on `main` today):** - `SpeechToTextBaseServing` submits each audio chunk without a priority: [`speech_to_text/base/serving.py` L560-L566](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.33.0/vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py#L560-L566) ```python generator = self.engine_client.generate( engine_input, sampling_params, request_id_item, lora_request=lora_request, trace_headers=trace_headers, ) ``` The beam-search branch just above it doesn't pass priority either. - Automatic language detection also submits without a priority: [L235-L239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.33.0/vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py#L235-L239). So a high-priority request that relies on detection waits behind lower-priority work for that step. - `TranscriptionRequest` and `TranslationRequest` have no `priority` field: [`transcription/protocol.py` L52](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Publish KV cache events immediately after prefix cache reset
summary: ## Purpose `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache()` clears the block pool immediately, but the resulting `AllBlocksCleared` event was only drained by `_publish_kv_cache_events()` at the end of the next `update_from_output()`. On an engine that goes idle after the reset, no scheduler step runs, so the event can be delayed indefinitely and a downstream router can keep routing to cache locations that no longer exist. This is a liveness fix for the event path, not a change to the reset semantics. ## Change - Extract the existing event collection/publish block from `update_from_output()` into `Scheduler._publish_kv_cache_events()`. - Call it immediately after a **successful local** `kv_cache_manager.reset_prefix_cache()`. - If the local reset fails, no event is published. - If the connector reset fails after a successful local reset, the local `AllBlocksCleared` is still published (the local cache really was cleared); the method's return value remains `False`. - No event is published when `kv_event_publisher` is `None`. ## Tests New CPU tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: - `test_reset_prefix_cache_publishes_pending_events` - `test_failed_reset_prefix_cache_does_not_publish` - `test_local_reset_still_publishes_when_connector_reset_fails` Run: ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \ PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q \ -k "reset_prefix_cache_publishes_pending_events or failed_reset_prefix_cache_does_not_publish or local_reset_still_publishes" # 3 passed ``` Existing reset coverage: ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLIN

summary: ## Overview Load already-compressed compressed-tensors LUT-B MoE weights and run them through the LUT-B kernels, including the emulation path on Hopper. Builds on the emulation kernel merged in [#62759](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62759). This uses the normal `QuantizationArgs` model with `QuantizationType.CODEBOOK`. This PR requires a new compressed-tensors version with LUT-B (`codebook`) support, and vLLM must pin that version for this support to land. title: [Bugfix] Honor X-Vllm-Priority in scale-out generate.
summary: ## Overview In scale-out serving, `/inference/v1/generate` schedules a request with header `X-Vllm-Priority: -10` at its body priority, with no error, while coupled `/v1/completions` lets the header override the body; `ServingTokens.serve_tokens` passes `request.priority` to the engine and never reads the header. It now resolves priority with `GenerateBaseServing._get_priority`, as the coupled Completions, Chat Completions and Responses APIs do, and, as asked in review, the header and the body `priority` of these four APIs share the Rust frontend's int32 range `[-2**31, 2**31 - 1]`, outside which a request returns 400. Fixes #67007 ## Claims - `/inference/v1/generate` with header `X-Vllm-Priority: -10` on a priority-scheduling engine finishes before a queued priority-0 request, as coupled `/v1/completions` does, instead of after it. - With header and body both set, the header wins (header `-1` over body 1) instead of the body. - A `priority` outside `[-2**31, 2**31 - 1]`, by header or by body, returns 400 on `/inference/v1/generate`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`; a value between the int32 and int64 limits returned 200. - No change for a request without the header or with a non-integer header: the body `priority` is used. ## Validation Environment: vLLM main `fcc1015e33` (2026-11-11) and this branch at `7cdd50193b`, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cu132, 1x RTX A6000, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Record the load window by logical expert
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #60685. EPLB records load per physical expert. When step_interval < window_size, part of the window still holds load recorded under the old map, and the next rearrange counts it for the expert that now sits at that physical index. This PR records load by logical expert instead. `eplb_map_and_record` already has the logical id, so the `atomic_add` now goes to the logical id rather than the physical index. `expert_load_pass` and the window have logical width, so old steps stay with the right expert after the map changes, and rearrange only sums the window. No extra kernel or scatter is added. The PR also removes `expert_load_pass_buffer`, `last_expert_load` and `use_last_expert_load`. The number of logical experts does not change when Elastic EP scales, so the window stays valid across a scale and the scale rearrange uses it directly. `log_balancedness` needs per rank load, so the same kernel also records physical counts into a new `physical_load_pass` when `log_balancedness` is on. The window never reads these counts, and they are cleared in the same `step` as the logical pass, so each logged value comes from one forward under one map. With `log_balancedness` off the buffer is not allocated and Triton compiles the second `atomic_add` out. The MegaMoE kernels share this helper, so they get the same recording. No open PR fixes this. #49700 only clears the window on an elastic EP topology change, and #64485 changes when rearrangements run, not how the window is recorded. ## Test Plan All runs are on H100, on main at `24a49203ee` with this PR on top. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Start the async rearrangement interval after the last layer commits
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Async EPLB resets the rearrangement counter only when a cycle starts. A cycle longer than `step_interval` therefore logs a negative "steps until the next rearrangement" and starts the next rearrangement in the same step its last layer commits. This PR counts the interval from the last layer's commit and logs in-flight progress instead. If a cycle overruns, a warning names the slowest EP ranks; when the ranks wait for each other inside a transfer, it names all of them. Related: #57883 (stall that shows the negative count), #60685 / #60686 (load window credited to the wrong experts), #57905. ## Claims - Async rearrangements no longer run back-to-back. The next interval starts when the last layer of the last in-flight model commits. - With `step_interval >= window_size` (default 3000 / 1000), every window row that the next rearrangement uses is recorded after that commit, however long the cycle ran. - On main, a cycle longer than `step_interval - window_size` leaves pre-commit rows in the window. #60685 notes that async EPLB has its problem per layer. This also hits the defaults (3000 / 1000) once a cycle runs past 2000 steps, which #60685 does not cover. - The `step_interval < window_size` case of #60685 is not fixed here. Nor are ranks that ran dummy steps (see Limitations). - No more negative step counts. - While a cycle is in flight, the balancedness log shows `async rearrangement in progress: k/L layers committed`. - Every `step_interval` steps while a cycle is still running, rank 0 warns. title: fix(metrics): capture num_preemptions before _reset() clears it in log()
summary: ## Summary `LoggingStatLogger.log()` called `_update_stats()` before formatting the periodic log. `_update_stats()` calls `_reset()`, which cleared two accumulated counters before they were read: - `num_preemptions`: the non-zero guard always saw `0`, so `Preemptions:` was never logged. - `num_corrupted_reqs`: the periodic log always reported `0` corrupted requests. Snapshot both counters before `_update_stats()` and use the snapshots when constructing the log message. This preserves the existing reset interval and all current logging behavior. The bug was independently reproduced on v0.29.0 and current `main`: `/metrics` reported 258 preemptions and KV cache usage reached 100%, while no periodic log line contained `Preemptions:`. See [this confirmation and repro](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38452#issuecomment-5796052413). ## Why this is not a duplicate This follows up on #28522, which introduced preemption logging and has already been merged. #28522 does not contain this reset-order correction; this PR fixes a defect in that merged implementation. This is also the existing PR for this bug being refreshed rather than a second PR for the same fix. ## Tests Added focused unit coverage in `tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py` for: - logging the exact preemption count when it is non-zero; - omitting `Preemptions:` when the count is zero; - logging the exact corrupted-request count when `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` is enabled. Refreshed against current MRV2 warmup on main; this PR changes measurement configuration, while #66681 separately expands managed-cache eligibility to distributed deployments. ## Claims - `KernelConfig.flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode` accepts `auto` (existing per-operation defaults), `eager` (include recurring host cost), and `cuda_graph` (captured replay). **`auto` does not infer vLLM's execution mode.** - Forward explicit `MeasurementPolicy` through generic and sparse-MLA warmup. Reject explicit modes when autotuning is disabled or the managed-cache path is ineligible. - Preserve the default policy and current-main single-rank gate. Explicit policies use separate FlashInfer cache namespaces, reused after warmup without per-token dispatch or synchronization additions. This is one objective for the entire warmup. It does not change runtime CUDA Graph configuration or choose separate winners for graph and eager regions. ## Validation **November 9 refresh:** head `17c38e9670b8`, main base `7c9a2fa2b3c9`. Standard changed-file pre-commit, mypy, test-wiring checks and merge-commit hooks passed. On B200, **112 warmup/lifecycle tests and 2 configuration-rejection tests passed**. **Actual single-rank `LLM` validation:** Qwen3-8B-FP8, eager/cuda_graph policies, cold/warm processes, graph serving enabled, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. All four cases passed through the new KernelConfig field without an eligibility override or policy-context monkeypatch. Each cold process profiled 1,98

title: [Feature] Add batch invariance support to GDN_ATTN backend
summary: Fixes #42960 Enable batch-invariant inference for GDN (Gated-Delta-Net) attention backend used by Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 multimodal models. ## Problem Setting `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with Qwen3.5/3.6 multimodal models raises: ``` RuntimeError: VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN. ``` These models use `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` which inherits `mamba_type = GDN_ATTN` from the base class. PR #49827 adds `QWEN_GDN_ATTN` with batch invariance but doesn't cover these multimodal architectures — they continue routing to the base `GDNAttentionBackend`, which had no `supports_batch_invariance()` override. ## Solution 1. **`GDNAttentionBackend.supports_batch_invariance() → True`** — unblocks the selector check for all GDN_ATTN users 2. **Per-sequence loops in `_forward_core`** — when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, each sequence is dispatched independently through `chunk_gated_delta_rule` (prefill) and `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` (decode), with fresh `cu_seqlens=[0, seq_len]` per sequence. The FLA/Triton kernel's chunking depends on batch geometry; per-sequence dispatch guarantees bit-identical outputs regardless of batch size. 3. **Test coverage** — detect Qwen3.5/3.6 and restrict to `["GDN_ATTN"]` backend in the batch invariance test suite. ## Why this is not a duplicate of #49827 PR #49827 adds `QwenGDNAttentionBackend` (enum `QWEN_GDN_ATTN`) via a new text-only model path. title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Stop declaring the MXFP4 MoE intermediate padding to AITER
summary: ## Purpose The AMD CI job `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` goes red intermittently with ``` AssertionError: (0, 1, (973, 973), 'residual', nan) ``` (e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94971). The NaN comes from AITER, on vLLM's ordinary MoE path, not from the mono kernels the test compares against. AITER's a8w4 MoE (FP8 activations x MXFP4 weights) allocates several scratch buffers with `torch.empty`, sized for the padded sorted length, and reads them where the producing kernel never wrote. In FP8/E8M0 a garbage `0xFF` byte is NaN, so a whole token row of the output comes back NaN. It only happens with a non-zero `intermediate_pad`, at decode-sized batches, after larger calls have run in the same process — which is why it shows up as a flaky decode failure. Root cause, a standalone repro and a fix are filed upstream: - https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/6565 - https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6568 ## This change Stop declaring `intermediate_pad` to AITER on the MXFP4 path. It is redundant there, and dropping it keeps the call off the buggy AITER path. Why it is redundant — the padded region is zero at the point AITER sees it, and stays zero through every step between allocation and the kernel call: | step | padded region | where | |---|---|---| | allocation | `torch.zeros` for `w13`/`w2`, their scales and `w13_bias`/`w2_bias`, at the **padded** intermediate size | `Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` | | checkpoint load | the destination is narrowed to the loaded shard before the copy, so the padded rows are never written — this is deliberate, the helper is named for

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Stop AITER FA from skipping 1-token prompts in prefill/extend
summary: ## Overview The ROCm AITER FA backend passes `min_seqlen_q=1` to aiter's `flash_attn_varlen_func`. On aiter's CK path that is a skip threshold, not a hint: every sequence with `seqlen_q <= 1` gets no output. This passes 0 instead. Upstream root cause: [ROCm/aiter#2229](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2229), fixed in [ROCm/aiter#7473](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7473). ## Claims - Fixes garbage output for a 1-token prompt batched behind a longer prefill on the V1 model runner, whenever the prefill/extend call runs on CK (fp16, head size 64, sinks or sliding window). - `test_aiter_mha_decode_single_token[float16]` passes without its xfail. - No accuracy or throughput change on Qwen3-0.6B fp16 or gpt-oss-20b. ## Validation MI350X, aiter 0.1.27, built from `main` 2a777ce26e. - Reproducer: fp16 Qwen3-0.6B with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA` and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Create the shared region reservation memfd via libc
summary: ## Purpose `SharedOffloadRegion` reserves address space for segmented regions with `os.memfd_create`. Python builds made against old glibc headers do not have that function. One example is uv-managed python-build-standalone, which is what any `uv venv --managed-python` uses. On those builds, every segmented region fails, so HiSparse with TP>1 fails at KV cache init: ``` AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'memfd_create' ``` The fix calls libc `memfd_create` through ctypes, the same way this file already calls libc `mmap`. The reservation itself stays the same: an anonymous sparse memfd mapping that needs no writable temp directory and is not commit-charged (see #61680). An anonymous `mmap(-1, MAP_SHARED|MAP_NORESERVE)` was considered and rejected. It is still charged under `vm.overcommit_memory=2`, and python-build-standalone does not expose `mmap.MAP_NORESERVE` either. ## Repro on `main` In a uv-managed Python 3.12.12 venv on x86_64 Linux: ``` $ python -c "import os; print(hasattr(os, 'memfd_create'))" False ``` A Kimi K3.1 HiSparse server with TP=4 on 4×B200 failed at startup with the `AttributeError` above, raised from `shared_offload_region.py`. The same failure reproduces directly with a segmented region: ```python SharedOffloadRegion(engine_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, num_chunks=1, rank=0, kv_bytes_per_chunk=4 << 30, cpu_page_size=4 << 30, num_segments=REGION_SEGMENTS, populate=False) ``` On `main` this raises the `AttributeError`. With this PR, it maps 4 segments and cleans them up. ## Test `test_segmented_region_maps_files_back_to_back` now removes `os.memfd_creat

title: [Kernel] Dynamic NVFP4 W4A4/W4A16 selection with shared weights
summary: ## Purpose Add opt-in dynamic NVFP4 W4A4/W4A16 selection on SM120/SM121. Both paths share canonical packed weights and scales, without additional weight preparation or a second weight copy. Selection happens before activation quantization, so small decode calls can use W4A16 while larger batches and prefill use W4A4. The default pair is **FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A4 and native CuTe W4A16**, removing the dependency on the open W4A4 PR #5100. Compatible CUTLASS, b12x, cuDNN and CuTe W4A4 providers use explicit adapters; providers requiring a different weight layout are rejected. The ordinary-linear and fused-SiLU cutoffs are independently configurable from 0 to 16. ```bash vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --dtype bfloat16 \ --kernel-config '{"linear_backend":"nvfp4_dynamic","nvfp4_dynamic_max_tokens":16,"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' ``` `nvfp4_dynamic_w4a4_backend` and `nvfp4_dynamic_w4a16_backend` select providers. `nvfp4_dynamic_silu_max_tokens` optionally overrides the fused-down cutoff. Automatic backend selection is unchanged. Native W4A16 was merged in [FlashInfer #5242](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5242). The Spark CI lane pins its merged commit `2f3bc5ac` because FlashInfer 0.7.0 predates it. This updates the existing precision-switching proposal; fixed-precision backend selection does not provide this behavior. ## Performance On RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (300 W), NVIDIA Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, the measured CuTe W4A4/native-W4A16 pair reduced time per output token by **6.6% to 7.2%** and request latency by **6.1% to 6.8%** at concurrency 1, selecting W4A1

title: [Quantization] Support nvfp4_per_token MoE activation override for compressed-tensors
summary: ## Purpose `--quantization-config.moe.activation=nvfp4_per_token` (#56740) only takes effect for ModelOpt checkpoints. For compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE checkpoints the option is accepted but never reaches `CompressedTensorsConfig`, so the MoE silently keeps using the checkpoint's static input scale. This PR passes the override through to `CompressedTensorsConfig` and on to `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod` as its `activation_key`, the same way ModelOpt does. Without the flag nothing changes, and the checkpoint format is untouched. Same restrictions as the ModelOpt path: W4A4 checkpoints only, and a MoE backend that supports per-token activations (tested on FlashInfer TRT-LLM). The checkpoint's input global scales are ignored when the flag is set. ## Test Plan ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 --quantization-config.moe.activation nvfp4_per_token python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 ``` Unit tests added in `tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py` and an init test in `tests/quantization/test_blackwell_moe.py`. ## Test Result GB200, GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions: | Config | static input scale | `nvfp4_per_token` | |---|---|---| | TP1 | 0.886 | 0.879 | | TP4 + EP | 0.889 | 0.886 | With the flag, all 48 MoE layers report `per_token_activation=True`; without it, `False`. `test_compressed_tensors.py`, `test_modelopt.py` and `test_quantization_config_args.py`: 204 passed. title: [Perf] Make DeepEP high-throughput SM count configurable
summary: ## Purpose `DeepEPHTAll2AllManager` only calls `deep_ep.Buffer.set_num_sms()` from the DBO micro-batching path (`set_num_sms`, via `ubatch_utils`). Without DBO, DeepEP high-throughput dispatch/combine always run on DeepEP's default of 20 SMs, and the manager's `num_sms` cap is hard-coded to 20, so there is no way to give them more. This adds `VLLM_DEEPEP_HIGH_THROUGHPUT_NUM_SMS` (default `20`, so behaviour is unchanged unless set) and applies it to the DeepEP buffer when the handle is created. Under DBO, the per-micro-batch `set_num_sms` call still applies and is capped by this value as before. Larger values need more NVLink buffer: on 8 ranks, 96 SMs fails DeepEP's buffer-size assertion with the default `VLLM_DEEPEP_BUFFER_SIZE_MB=1024` and works with 2048. ## Test Plan 8x B300 (SM103, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130), one node, GLM-5.3 FP8 (DeepSeek-V3.2-style MoE, 256 experts, top-8), prefill-only engine: `--prefill-context-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, DeepEP `d4f41e4e` built for `10.3a`. Closed-loop real-prompt prefill load (`max_tokens=1`, prompt mix 1k-200k tokens, 12 and 24 requests in flight, 240 s), every prompt with a unique per-run prefix; `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` was 0 for every request in every run. The runs used vLLM v0.31.0 with the equivalent change applied at startup (`deep_ep.Buffer.set_num_sms(N)` next to the `num_sms` cap), not this exact branch. ## Test Result Served prompt tokens/s: | DeepEP SMs | `VLLM_DEEPEP_BUFFER_SIZE_MB` | 12 in flight | 24 in flight |

title: [Attention] Support FlashInfer attention sinks on SM8x
summary: ## Purpose The FlashInfer backend serves attention sinks only where XQA (SM90, SM12x) or trtllm-gen (SM100) handles decode, so on SM8x a sink model such as gpt-oss cannot use it. On SM8x this leaves gpt-oss on TRITON_ATTN, and an FP8 KV cache has no backend at all, since Triton's FP8 KV cache needs SM89+. This routes every layer with sinks through FlashInfer's fa2 sink wrappers for causal and non-causal prefill and for decode, and `supports_sink()` returns True on SM8x. As a result, on SM8x: - gpt-oss with an FP8 KV cache now runs. - gpt-oss with a BF16 KV cache now selects FLASHINFER instead of TRITON_ATTN, by backend priority. Measurements are below. The fa2 paths take the query scale from `get_q_scale()`, so a bf16 query ignores the layer `q_scale`, as elsewhere since #64329. The SDPA reference test for sink prefill, `test_flashinfer_native_prefill_with_sinks`, now also runs on SM8x. This depends on [FlashInfer #6021](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6021), which adds `BatchDecodeWithAttentionSinkWrapper`, the decode counterpart of `BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper`. That PR shipped in FlashInfer 0.7.3, which main has pinned since #65930. The open draft #37949 would instead keep sink models on TRITON_ATTN on SM8x. With that policy, this PR still gives FP8 KV caches a backend on SM80 and SM86. I used Codex and Claude while implementing and preparing this PR. title: [Kernel] Separate what the GDN prefill selector can run from what it prefers
summary: ## Overview `--gdn-prefill-backend` uses one capability list both to resolve `auto` and to veto an explicit choice, so asking for `flashinfer` on a device the list doesn't name logs a warning and runs Triton anyway. This splits "can it run here" from "should `auto` pick it", and passes FlashInfer the prefill lengths it needs once it does run. The SM8x path comes from [FlashInfer #5109](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5109), which shipped in FlashInfer 0.7.3, the version main has pinned since #65930. ## Claims - A named backend runs where it can and fails at startup where it can't, instead of quietly running something else. When the selector refuses it, the message names the device, `head_k_dim` and the alternative. - `auto` makes the same choice as before on every platform. - SM8x with `head_k_dim == 128` is allowed by the selector, but not preferred. Running it needs FlashInfer 0.7.3 or later. - The prefill gets the longest prefill length and a host copy of the prefill `cu_seqlens` without a device-to-host sync. With that FlashInfer PR on sm_80 (2048 tokens, 48 value heads), passing the length takes peak prefill memory from 159.0 MiB to 132.0 MiB. ## Validation sm_80, main (`32551991b9`) plus this PR, with FlashInfer built from the [FlashInfer #5109](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5109) branch: ```text pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_backend_selection.py # 13 passed pytest tests/kernels/mamba/ -k gdn # 36 passed, 21 skipped pytest tests/v1/attention -k gdn # 78 passed, 10 skipped ``` `test_gdn_prefill_backend_selection.py` is

title: [Bugfix][PCP] Run the MTP draft prefill eagerly under prefill context parallel
summary: ## Purpose Engine start fails with prefill context parallel, MTP and prefill CUDA graphs together, for example: - `--prefill-context-parallel-size 8 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` - `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE",...}'` The failure is in the speculator's `capture()` (now `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.capture()` in `spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`, used by `TargetDependentARSpeculator`), while it captures the draft model's prefill graphs: - The capture runs `_prefill` on generic dummy inputs. - Under PCP, the draft prefill instead reads the inputs that the PCP manager prepares (`prepare_draft_prefill` / `draft_prefill_batch`). - For DSA models the sparse indexer then fails during capture: ``` File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 723, in sparse_attn_indexer File ".../vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py", line 635, in mqa_logits_mx_inputs torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument ``` The fix adds an `AutoRegressiveSpeculator._capture_prefill_graphs()` hook (default `True`) around the draft prefill capture; `TargetDependentARSpeculator` returns `False` when a PCP manager is present. Dispatch then finds no prefill graph for the draft and runs it eagerly, while the target model keeps its prefill graphs. Without PCP, and for other speculators, nothing changes. _Rebased onto current `main` (2026-11-12): the capture code moved to the shared autoregressive base, so the guard is now a hook there instead of a branch in the target-dependent speculator._ ## Test Plan GLM-5.3 FP8 and NVFP4 on 8×B300 (SM103): - `--prefi

title: [Performance]: Inconsistent speculative decoding acceptance metrics between vLLM and SpecForge on Qwen3-32B baselines
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance _No response_ ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance I am benchmarking speculative decoding baselines in vLLM and observed inconsistent acceptance metrics compared with SpecForge. I would like to understand whether this difference is expected due to different metric definitions, verification logic, benchmark prompt formatting, or whether it may indicate a configuration mismatch or a potential issue in the vLLM speculative decoding benchmark path. The target model is Qwen3-32B. I tested two speculative decoding baselines: Qwen3-32B with Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh, and Qwen3-32B with Qwen3-0.6B as a standalone draft model. title: [RFC]: Attention Backend Test Suites
summary: ### Motivation. Attention backends are where kernels, the metadata builder, the model runner, the KV-cache manager and the backend selector meet. Most backend bugs come from the contracts between those parts, not from inside a kernel: - a declared feature that the kernel silently ignores; - a batch order the builder does not expect; - a KV dtype the selector accepts but the cache write rejects; - a layout or CUDA graph mode that nobody exercises. Today each backend's tests are written ad hoc. They mostly compare outputs on a few shapes, so a fallback kernel or a dropped feature still passes. Coverage also can't be compared from one backend to another, and reviewers have no shared bar for what a backend PR should prove. Trying the standard on one backend showed the gap. ROCM_AITER_FA had no failing tests, yet a suite built to the standard found seven backend defects that tests did not catch: - wrong results under model runner v2; - logits soft cap, sinks and ALiBi dropped in prefill/extend; - shuffle-layout configs that crash at the first decode; - non-causal fp8 decode raising an error; - a declared KV dtype that the cache write rejects; - an unusable KV layout listed as supported; - a capability flag that went stale after an env change. It also found an AITER kernel addressing bug. ### Proposed Change. Adopt a written test standard for attention backends, kept in two forms: a document for people, and an agent skill (`.agents/skills/attention-backend-testing/`) that authors and reviewers can follow. The full text is in the Google Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/11AU

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep activations MXFP8 between DeepGEMM kernels
summary: ## Purpose DeepGEMM's DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels can hand FP8 activations to each other, but vLLM re-quantized their BF16 outputs before every dense projection: 127 standalone MXFP8 quantize launches per decode step at C1 (TP4), plus the quantize half of the Mega-MoE input staging. This PR wires the FP8 outputs DeepGEMM already provides to the consumers, and runs those consumers on DeepGEMM. title: [MRV2][Perf] Screened lm_head
summary: ## Purpose Opt-in `--screened-lm-head`: when sampling only reads the top-k logits (greedy, or temperature with top-k <= 32 and optional top-p, e.g. Qwen's default `temperature=1.0, top_k=20, top_p=0.95`), compute them from an FP8 screen of the lm_head plus exact logits for the few rows the screen cannot rule out. Same tokens for the same seed, about half the lm_head bytes. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on DGX Spark: +7.7% decode greedy, +6.2% at Qwen's default sampling (c=1, no speculative decoding). - An FP8 copy of the lm_head scores every row, with a rigorous per-row error bound (FP8 error plus fp32 accumulation error of both GEMMs, computed in fp64 at load). - A row more than one output ulp below the k-th best lower bound can neither enter nor tie the full head's top k. The rest (greedy: 15 rows per token on Flash-Next, top-20: about 1,200) get exact BF16 logits, the others `-inf`. - Three Triton kernels, no host sync. Other batches (logprobs, penalties, logit bias, min-p, structured outputs, top-k > 32) use the full head. Unsupported setups (quantized or TP-sharded lm_head, LoRA, custom samplers, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, pre-SM89) raise at load. **Scope:** the gain needs the lm_head to be a large share of the step (DGX Spark, Jetson Thor, RTX). On GB200/GB300 it is neutral to slightly negative, so it is opt-in. ## Results Flash-Next NVFP4, SPEED-Bench (11 domains, 352 prompts, 256 tokens), same-node stock/screened pairs, both arm orders: ``` GPU sampling config c=1 c=4 GSM8K stock / ours GB10 greedy plain decode +8.0% / +7.4% +5.9% / +5.8% 98.5 / 98.5 GB10 greedy MTP k=3 +3.9% / +

title: [Model Runner][Multimodal] Add exact-budget encoder CUDA graphs for Cosmos3-Edge
summary: ## Purpose This PR adds image-encoder CUDA Graph support for the recently added `nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge` model. Cosmos3-Edge has a 27-layer SigLIP2 vision encoder. A 64-token image launches 281 CUDA kernels in eager mode on the RTX PRO 6000 setup below, making the encoder strongly launch-bound. The graph path precomputes dynamic metadata outside capture and records only the tensor-only vision forward: - patch projection and packed positional embeddings; - packed `cu_seqlens` and `max_seqlen`; - the 27-layer SigLIP2 encoder; - the patch-merge gather and Cosmos projector. Cosmos image shapes are highly dynamic. Padding an input into the next larger graph can be slower than eager and, depending on the platform and capture shape, can also change BF16 values. This PR therefore adds an opt-in per-path `require_exact_token_budget_match` policy to the generic encoder CUDA Graph manager. Cosmos enables it, defaults to one 64-token image per replay, and sends inputs between captured budgets through the existing eager fallback. Fixed-resolution deployments can add their exact merged-token counts with `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`. The graph path is intentionally limited to raw-pixel images and one image per replay. Video and precomputed image embeddings continue to use eager execution. ## Rebase validation (2026-11-12) Rebased onto main `8a36f080e2a28a91137d86ef503eab6e37d0a9d4`; validated PR head is `268a902fb447e38c08a560a4b4a657397436f030`. - Preserved upstream MRV1 removal and the new whole-batch encoder dispatch. Exact-budget matching is checked when choosing the batch's graph.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Enable partial-tail offload for hybrid models under DCP
summary: ## Purpose Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 2 of 2): the DCP store guard and per-group addressing, with the `-1` squashed in and `alignment_tokens` reused. `supports_partial_tail` required `len(group_block_sizes) == 1` **and** `decode_context_parallel_size == 1`. Under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp ×` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8 — attention groups are scaled in `build_offloading_config` / `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size`, `MambaManager.__init__` undoes the scaling for recurrent state). Both conditions fail, so the feature is off for every hybrid model under DCP. The store path also addressed every group with one shared physical block index (`boundary // self._partial_tail_block_size`), which is wrong once block sizes differ, and read that block size from `kv_group_configs[0]`, which need not be the full-attention group. Fix: - Gate partial tails on core's resolved hit alignment, `cache_hit_alignment_tokens < alignment_tokens` (per review), instead of `len(group_block_sizes) == 1` and `dcp == 1`. Mixed block sizes are allowed when every recurrent block divides the full-attention block and is hash-aligned, and hash boundaries split evenly across DCP ranks. The window a tail can lie in is the full-attention offload block, which `SchedulerOffloadConfig.alignment_tokens` already holds — no new field. - Address each group's source block in its own block size, as the block that *ends* at the boundary: `(boundary - 1) // tokens_per_block`. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Clear partial-tail pending state on a required group miss
summary: ## Overview When a partial-tail boundary requires KV from multiple groups, any required group returning `MISS` makes that boundary unusable. The lookup currently retains a pending result observed from an earlier group. The baseline deferred that request; the fix allowed recomputation. This confirms the behavior is reachable. summary: ## Overview With tensor parallelism and no expert parallelism, every MiniMax-M3 layer all-reduces two TP-partial activations. At an 8192-token step that is two 100 MB NCCL all-reduces per layer (121 per step, about 28% of the GPU time on GB300 TP4). The residual add, Gemma RMSNorm and MXFP8 quantization that follow each one run on every token on every rank. For batches of 4096 tokens or more, this PR keeps the residual stream sharded by token across the TP ranks, reusing the sequence-parallel path that MegaMoE already has. The tensor-parallel experts see the all-gathered BF16 batch. 2. **Fused MoE tail** (`ops/finalize_reduce_scatter.py`). A sharded MoE layer stops the TRTLLM-Gen experts after GEMM2. A Triton kernel sums each token's routed rows and shared-expert row and stores the TP-partial row straight into its owner rank's symmetric-memory mailbox. After a symmetric-memory barrier, a second Triton kernel sums the TP slots of each owned row in rank order, adds the residual and writes the Gemma RMSNorm as MXFP8 (BF16 for the final norm). summary: ## Purpose When grouped Triton MLA uses one KV split, its second-stage reduction has one input and is mathematically an identity. title: [XPU] Move weight transfer to torch.distributed where NCCL is absent
summary: ## Purpose The `nccl` weight-transfer backend reaches NCCL through `PyNcclCommunicator`, which loads `libnccl` itself. On any accelerator that has no NCCL the communicator sets `available = False, disabled = True` and every collective early-returns, so a full RL weight-update round reports success while moving nothing and the workers keep serving the weights they started with. #57022 turns that silence into an error; this PR gives those platforms a transport that actually works. The backend does not need NCCL itself — the engines only ever ask their communicator to `broadcast`, and every accelerator torch supports already has a collective library behind `torch.distributed` (`xccl` on XPU). So keep the backend named `nccl` and choose the transport by platform. That distinction matters because the RL control plane lives in the *trainer*: TRL and similar frameworks select `backend="nccl"`, name NCCL in their config schemas, and call `packed_nccl_broadcast_producer` directly. A new backend *name* would have to be taught to each of them; a transport chosen by the platform works with the trainers that exist today. `TorchDistTransport` wears the same shape as `PyNcclCommunicator` (`broadcast`, `rank`/`world_size`, `available`/`disabled`, `group`) over a stateless `torch.distributed` group on the platform's own `dist_backend`. The group is stateless for the same reason the NCCL engine's is: the trainer is a separate process and not a member of the workers' tensor- or pipeline-parallel groups, so broadcasts address the sender by its rank *within the transfer group* (`group_src`). title: [Feature]: EC events: publish encoder cache presence and eviction from the EC connector
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **Motivation** KV events let external components (routers, indexers, cache-aware orchestrators such as llm-d) track which KV blocks each instance holds and route requests accordingly. The EC connector has no equivalent. A router can't tell which instances already hold the encoder output for multimodal objects, so a repeated multimodal input is re-encoded or fetched again when it could have been routed to an instance that already has it. This matters most in E-PD disaggregation. **Proposal** Add EC events that mirror KV events in format, transport and configuration, keyed by `mm_hash` instead of block hash. Event types, alongside the KV event types in `vllm/distributed/ec_events.py`: ```python class ECCacheEvent(msgspec.Struct, omit_defaults=True, gc=False, tag=True): """Base class for all EC cache-related events.""" class ECStored(ECCacheEvent): mm_hashes: list[str] medium: str | None class ECRemoved(ECCacheEvent): mm_hashes: list[str] medium: str | None class AllECCleared(ECCacheEvent): pass class ECEventBatch(EventBatch): events: list[ECStored | ECRemoved | AllECCleared] ``` Connector API, same shape as `KVConnectorBase_V1.take_events()`: ```python class ECConnectorBase: def take_events(self) -> Iterable["ECCacheEvent"]: """Return EC events collected since the last call.""" return () ``` Scheduler: on each step, collect `ec_connector.take_events()` and publish an `ECEventBatch` through the existing `EventPublisherFactory` / `ZmqEventPublisher`, the same way `KVEventBatch` is published. title: [Bug][KV Connector] Permanent stall: parked async KV loads exhaust the GPU pool and none can allocate its tail (OffloadingConnector, spec decode on, 0.31-0.33)
summary: ### Summary With `OffloadingConnector` (CPU offload, async loads) and a small GPU KV pool relative to the load, the engine stops forever: `running` = 0, every step schedules nothing, GPU KV ~90 % used, all of it held by requests whose async load has **completed** but that never run. This is not the head-of-queue stranding fixed by #58947 / #57104: the completed loads ARE visited and promoted; each one fails `allocate_slots` for its un-cached tail because the parked loads themselves hold the pool, and parked/loaded requests cannot be preempted (`_preempt_request` asserts `RUNNING`). Nothing ever frees a block. Reproduced 3 times (vLLM 0.31.0, 0.32.0; the 0.33.0 scheduler has the same paths). Speculative decoding is ON (DSpark k=5), so #57104's spec margin is in effect and does not prevent it. ### Environment - vLLM 0.31.0 / 0.32.0 (via NVIDIA Dynamo 1.6 / 1.7-dev), 4x H100 80GB, TP4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MoE, MXFP4) - `--kv-transfer-config {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":429496729600}}` - `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `max_num_seqs` 64, GPU KV pool ~1.19-1.24 M tokens - Workload: agentic multi-turn traces (AgentX, 64 concurrent sessions, mean ISL ~83k, 92 % of prompt tokens hit the CPU tier) ### Evidence Engine log at the stall (repeats every step until the client times out): ``` running 0, KV fetch: 1 waiting to start, 33 completed waiting, GPU KV 89.8 % ``` `vllm:generation_tokens_total` flat for > 10 min with `num_requests_waiting` > 0. title: [Feature]: Super Prefill: keep generating on the prefill instance while the KV cache transfers (P/D, opt-in)
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch In disaggregated prefill/decode (P/D) serving, the client waits for the KV transfer. The prefill instance stops after one token, the decode instance pulls the KV cache, and only then do tokens flow. That wait sits on the critical path of every request: it adds to time to first token and to end-to-end latency. The KV cache is append-only, so the prefill instance can keep generating the same request while the decode instance copies the prompt blocks. Once the copy is done, the decode instance continues from the prompt plus the tokens already sent, and recomputes only those tokens in one step. The client sees one continuous stream with a short pause at the switch. Measured with a proxy-only prototype on stock v0.33.0: two nodes with one L4 each, `NixlConnector` pull over UCX/TCP at 0.57 GB/s, Qwen3-0.6B, greedy, 1024 output tokens, concurrency 1, 12 requests per point, medians: | Prompt tokens | TTFT: single / P/D today / Super Prefill | End-to-end: single / P/D today / Super Prefill | Longest pause | |---:|---|---|---:| | 512 | 19 / 133 / 21 ms | 6462 / 6503 / 6456 ms | 19 ms | | 2048 | 59 / 487 / 58 ms | 7222 / 7592 / 7191 ms | 20 ms | | 8192 | 363 / 2026 / 349 ms | 10336 / 11907 / 10253 ms | 42 ms | | 16384 | 1015 / 4274 / 987 ms | 14818 / 17844 / 14607 ms | 70 ms | Costs: the prefill instance does decode work (26 to 396 tokens per request above), and the transfer ran 1.5 to 1.6x slower while it decoded. title: [KV Connector][LMCache] Forward failed KV loads to the LMCache scheduler side
summary: ## Purpose `LMCacheConnectorV1.update_connector_output` only consumes KV events from `KVConnectorOutput`, so LMCache's scheduler side never learns which blocks failed to load. With LMCache CPU offload under GPU KV-cache pressure (200k-token prompts, 13 concurrent requests, one TP8 replica), a preempted request is resumed, promised the same LMCache chunk, gets 0 tokens back, and is promised the same chunk again on the next resume. One request repeated this 136 times and the engine stalled while its health check stayed green. This change passes `KVConnectorOutput.invalid_block_ids` to the LMCache engine's `record_load_failures` when it exists ([LMCache/LMCache#5443](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5443)), so those requests recompute instead of loading again. Older LMCache versions without the method are unaffected (`getattr` guard). For the failed blocks to be recomputed rather than failing the request, use `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"` in `kv_transfer_config` (the default `fail` errors the request). ## Test Plan ``` pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_lmcache_connector.py -k "UpdateConnectorOutput or LoadFailureForwarding" ``` New `TestLoadFailureForwarding`: forwards `invalid_block_ids`; no call without them; no error with an LMCache engine that lacks `record_load_failures`. ## Test Result ``` 10 passed, 17 deselected ``` (vLLM 0.28.0 with the same change.) title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Promote rejection sampler's global logsumexp to fp64
summary: ## Overview Fixes a precision bug deferred from #61383: the rejection sampler's global logsumexp silently collapses a real near-1.0 probability to exactly 1.0 under fp32 rounding. ## Claims - `_compute_global_logsumexp` combined per-block max/sumexp arrays in fp32. At a typical confident logit magnitude (~25), fp32 ULP (~3e-6) rounds away the correction term whenever a runner-up token trails the max by more than ~14 in logit-space. - Fix: promote the per-block terms to fp64 before summing (summing in fp32 first reintroduces a smaller version of the same loss), and carry `target_rejected_logsumexp`/ `draft_rejected_logsumexp` as fp64 through their downstream call sites. - O(1) cost per block/request — not O(vocab_size) — so the fp64 promotion is free. ## Validation ``` CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py -q # 89 passed, 1 failed -- the 1 failure is a CUDA OOM from a concurrent process on a shared GPU # (confirmed unrelated: fails in isolation too, with "61.29 GiB memory in use" by another PID). CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py::test_global_logsumexp_keeps_near_max_correction -v # PASSED. Stashed the fix and reran: FAILED with `25.0 == 25.0` -- reproduces the exact bug. ``` New test constructs a synthetic 2-block vocab (max logit 25.0, runner-up 11.0, i.e. gap=14) and calls `_compute_global_logsumexp` directly through a minimal probe kernel, asserting the result against the closed-form `max + log1p(exp(-14))` rather than exactly `max`. ##

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Take the INT4 value zero-point sum on the rounded P
summary: ## Purpose `_attn_packed` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/int4_per_token_head.py`) computes `acc += tl.dot(P_v, V) - sum(P_v * v_zp)`. Both operands of the dot are fp32, which Triton rounds to TF32, but the zero-point sum is taken on the unrounded `P_v`. The rounding error is multiplied by a zero point of about 8 and does not cancel, so the output drifts away from the true attention and gets worse with the context length. Relative error against an fp64 attention over the very same cache (Qwen3.8-27B full-attention shape: 24 query / 4 KV heads, head size 256, random bf16 K/V, query lengths 1, 4 and 256; the errors do not depend on the query length): | context | main | this change | |---|---|---| | 4,096 | 3.8 % | 0.40 % | | 32,768 | 10.9 % | 0.41 % | | 131,072 | 21.3 % | 0.41 % | | 229,000 | 28.0 % | 0.40 % | (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server; the A40 gives the same numbers within 1 point.) The change passes `P_v` and the value nibbles to the dot in the query dtype (the nibbles 0..15 are exact in bf16/fp16) and takes the zero-point sum on that same rounded `P_v`: 5 changed lines, no new arguments. The key side is untouched: query and key nibbles are already exact in TF32 for bf16 queries, and quantizing the key operands as well gave identical errors. title: [Perf][KV Offload] Split the shared Tiering region and skip the scheduler pre-fault
summary: ## Purpose Tiering keeps one shared CPU region per engine so its secondary tiers can address it. At large sizes it is slow to set up: - The region is one `/dev/shm` file, so every worker pre-faults into the same file and page-cache inserts serialize. - The scheduler then maps the whole region and pre-faults every page again, on one thread. This splits the region across `REGION_SEGMENTS` files, as `CPUOffloadingSpec` already does (#59546), and maps the scheduler side without pre-faulting. Secondary tiers still see one contiguous range. #45693 (hugetlbfs) is a separate, opt-in backend. ## Results CPU tier setup only (worker pre-fault and pinning, scheduler mapping, P2P registration), timed with a script that runs those steps through vLLM's own classes. One H100 node, 8 worker processes sharing one GPU, P2P tier, GLM-5.3-sized rows (8 x 3.8 MB slots): | Tier | Before | After | |---|---|---| | 512 GiB | 167-175 s | 59 s | | 1,250 GiB | 397-460 s | 135-138 s | At 1,250 GiB, worker pre-fault drops from 255-317 s to 55 s and the 59-140 s scheduler pre-fault is gone. Pinning goes up from 15-35 s to 42 s; P2P registration stays at ~40 s.

title: [RFC]: Add Watchdog for Engine and Worker Monitoring
summary: # Add Watchdog for Engine and Worker Monitoring # Motivation Hangs and deadlocks in vLLM V1 are notoriously hard to diagnose. When the engine core process or a worker process stops making progress — for example due to a deadlock in collective communication (NCCL), an infinite wait on a synchronization primitive, a stuck device kernel, or a scheduler bug — the process usually stays alive but silent: no exception, no traceback, no signal. Operators are left with an opaque production incident; diagnosing it requires reproducing the hang, attaching a debugger (e.g. `py-spy`), or sending a signal manually, none of which is always possible in production. There is no automatic mechanism to capture what every thread is doing *at the moment* progress stops. A watchdog that detects "no progress for N seconds" and automatically dumps all-thread stack traces would turn a previously opaque hang into an actionable diagnostic artifact (e.g. "the engine has been stuck in `all_reduce` for 10 minutes"). This RFC proposes adding such a watchdog to vLLM V1, integrated at the two places where hangs are most commonly observed: the engine core process and the worker processes. # Proposed Change ## 1. New `vllm/utils/watch_dog.py` — `WatchDog` class hierarchy A lightweight watchdog implemented as one background daemon thread per process, split into an abstract base and two concrete implementations: - **`WatchDog` (ABC).** Defines the contract: `feed()`, `disable()`, `handle_failure(reason)`. - **`NoopWatchDog`.** Zero-cost placeholder returned by default (and used when the watchdog is disabled via

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix prompt_logprobs corruption from CUDA graph output buffer reuse by padded drafter
summary: ## Purpose FIX #53488 When speculative decoding runs a padded GPU drafter (MTP/EAGLE-style), `prompt_logprobs` are silently corrupted for requests executed through piecewise CUDA graphs, while the same server without `--speculative-config` scores every request correctly. ### Root cause In the V1 GPU model runner, the padded GPU drafter runs **before** `_bookkeeping_sync()`: ```text target model forward -> hidden_states backed by a reusable CUDA graph output buffer sample padded drafter forward -> reuses/overwrites that graph output buffer bookkeeping -> _get_prompt_logprobs_dict() computes prompt logits from the already-overwritten hidden_states ``` All CUDA graphs share one global memory pool, so the drafter's forward can reclaim the memory backing the target model's graph output. Prompt logprobs are then computed from draft-model output instead of the target hidden states. This exactly explains the sharp boundary reported in #53488: - Prompts at or below the CUDA graph capture limit (PIECEWISE) are corrupted. - Prompts immediately above the limit (cudagraph_mode NONE, eager output) are correct. - Generation is unaffected, since sampling consumes logits before the drafter runs. I reproduced this on different hardware from the reporter (RTX 5880 Ada, x86_64, vs. their aarch64 GB10) with one of their exact checkpoints, confirming DEBUG-log `cudagraph_mode` flips PIECEWISE→NONE precisely at the corruption boundary (512→513 tokens with `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`). ### Fix Add `_get_bookkeeping_hidden_states()`: only when (1) a GPU model drafter will run before bookkeep

title: [KV Offload] Track the outcome of promoted chunks
summary: ## Overview With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a secondary-tier hit is first promoted (copied) into the CPU primary tier and only then loaded into the GPU. The tiering metrics count promotions and their bytes, but not whether a promoted chunk was ever used. This PR records, for each chunk a promotion lands, exactly one outcome: `loaded`, `served_peer`, `evicted_unloaded` or `reset`. It also records the time from landing to that outcome, the chunks still waiting for one, and promotions started again for chunks that were evicted unread. It is observability only: no cache, eviction, scheduling or transfer behavior changes. Related: - #49902 and RFC #66782 describe promotions that are evicted before they are loaded. - #50014 and #62932 propose behavior fixes for that problem. These metrics measure the problem; they do not fix it. **Not a duplicate.** I searched open and merged PRs for promotion outcome, re-promotion, time-to-outcome, failed-load and tiering-metrics work, and found none that adds outcome accounting for promoted chunks. - #53910 (merged) added the promotion latency histogram. This PR complements it: latency until a chunk lands, versus what happens to the chunk after it lands. - #50014, #62932 and #66782 change or propose promotion behavior; they add no metrics of this kind. ## Claims New metrics, each labeled by the source `tier`: | Metric | Type | Extra label | |---|---|---| | `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promoted_chunk_outcomes` | Counter | `outcome` | | `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promoted_chunk_time_to_outcome_seconds` | Histogram | `outcome` | | `vllm:kv_offload_tiering

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fold the MXFP4 dense activation quant into SiLU-mul and RMSNorm with AITER
summary: On ROCm with AITER the MXFP4 dense linear (Triton afp4wfp4 path) quantizes its bf16 input inside `gemm_with_dynamic_quant`, so the quant is invisible to the fusion passes and every down_proj and qkv/gate_up input costs a separate `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` launch. This PR emits that quant as its own op when a fold is enabled and adds two patterns to the AITER fusion passes: - SiLU-mul + MXFP4 quant -> `fused_reduce_act_mul_and_mxfp4_quant` (in `RocmAiterSiluMulFp8GroupQuantFusionPass`), runs with `fuse_act_quant`. On ROCm with AITER linear `+quant_fp8` is enabled, so that is on by default at -O1 and up. - RMSNorm (with and without the residual add) + MXFP4 quant -> `fused_rms_mxfp4_quant` (in `RocmAiterRMSNormQuantFusionPass`). Opt-in via the new `PassConfig.fuse_norm_mxfp4_quant`, off at every -O level, and only applies together with `fuse_norm_quant`. The quant is only split out of `gemm_with_dynamic_quant` when the model is compiled and one of the folds is on, so enforce_eager and -O0 keep the single call. Depends on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6024. The SiLU fold needs `round_to_input_dtype` so it rounds silu(a)*b to bf16 once, like the compiled native silu_and_mul, and `transpose_scale` so the scales come out column-major like `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` (the layout the afp4wfp4 configs are tuned for). Both are added in that AITER PR. A probe checks the AITER signature, and on an AITER without them neither pattern registers and nothing changes. With them the SiLU fold is bit exact: output matches the unfused path byte for byte. Against `+silu_and_mul` it can be one fp4 cod

title: [Perf][Attention] FA2: split mixed prefill/decode batches into two calls
summary: ## Purpose On FA2 GPUs (SM8x: A100/A800/A10/A40/L4/RTX 30xx/40xx), `FLASH_ATTN` runs every mixed prefill+decode batch as one `flash_attn_varlen_func` call. FA2 has no tile scheduler; its grid is `ceil(max_seqlen_q / 64) × batch × heads`, so with chunked prefill each decode request launches `max_seqlen_q / 64` CTAs, all but one empty. The decodes also miss FA2's `max_seqlen_q == 1` path (packed GQA + split-KV), which only activates when the whole call is decode. This PR splits FA2 mixed batches into a decode call (`max_seqlen_q=1`) and a prefill call. Decodes already lead the batch under MRv2 (`sort_batch_req_ids`); for the V1 runner the builder now sets `reorder_batch_threshold=1` when splitting. FA3/FA4 (tile-scheduled) and DCP are untouched. - Only active when `fa_version == 2`, DCP is off, `max_query_len > 1`, no cascade, and both parts are non-empty. - CUDA graphs are unaffected: FA2 full graphs are only captured for uniform batches, which never split; mixed batches already run attention outside the graph. - Spec decode: verify requests (q_len > 1) sort first, so `split_decodes_and_prefills` finds no leading decodes and the path is not taken. Not a duplicate: I searched open/closed PRs and issues for FA2 mixed-batch/decode-prefill splitting. The closest are #51320 (FA2 `num_splits > 1` for spec decode, kernel-side, blocked on vllm-project/flash-attention#176) and #57709 (opt-in FlashInfer paged prefill, FlashInfer backend only); neither changes how `FLASH_ATTN` issues FA2 calls. ## Test Plan All on 1× A800 80GB PCIe (SM80), torch 2.13.0+cu130, `main` @ 3df4ae153, `--att

title: [Feature]: Quantization support (AWQ / GPTQ / FP8) for mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch I am currently deploying the new `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` model using the vLLM V1 Engine. Because it is a realtime multimodal audio model, the memory footprint is extremely high. On a standard mid-tier GPU like the RTX 5060 Ti (16GB VRAM), the `bf16` weights consume around 8.4GB. This leaves very little room for the `encoder_cache` and standard KV cache. As a result, the `max-model-len` has to be severely restricted (around ~4300 tokens), which is barely enough for a short audio session, and it completely prevents running multiple concurrent streams due to `encoder_cache_usage` hitting 100%. It would be incredibly helpful to have quantization support for the `VoxtralRealtimeGeneration` architecture. Specifically: 1. **Weight Quantization:** Support for loading AWQ, GPTQ, or bitsandbytes (int8/int4) formats for this specific model type. 2. **KV Cache Quantization:** Support for FP8 KV cache for Voxtral to further reduce the memory required for long audio streams. Reducing the weight footprint by half (e.g., to ~4GB using 8-bit) would drastically increase the viable audio context window and allow continuous batching of multiple sessions on 16GB and 24GB consumer GPUs. Currently, the only alternative is to limit `max-model-len` to minimal values or use expensive multi-GPU setups / A100s, which makes testing and local deployment of Realtime audio models inaccessible for many developers. ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already sear

title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Set token budgets for the MiniMax-M3 wide-EP cells
summary: ## Purpose The MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 wide-EP cells are very slow. The 2P2D EP16 GSM8K eval takes about 1h37 in CI and the 1P1D EP8 one about an hour. The AITER MXFP8 MoE kernel runs over a padded buffer sized by `--max-num-batched-tokens`, 131072 rows at the default, so every prefill and decode step pays for the whole buffer. Small token budgets shrink it. title: kv offload: invalidate cached absent verdicts after a successful store
summary: ## Overview A block that a secondary KV-offload tier previously probed as **absent** keeps serving that stale "absent" verdict even after the block is later **stored** into the tier. `AsyncLookupManager` only corrects a cached negative verdict on a *failed load* (`mark_miss`); there was no path to correct it when the block was later *written* to the tier, so the scheduler kept skipping a block that was actually on disk. This PR adds `AsyncLookupManager.invalidate()` and calls it from `FileSystemTierManager.get_finished_jobs()` when a store job succeeds, so freshly stored blocks are re-probed instead of served as a stale miss. ## Claims - Fixes a correctness bug: a block stored into a secondary tier after its absence was cached is still served as absent (the cached negative is never invalidated on a successful store). - `invalidate()` is conservative: it drops **only** resolved-absent (`result is False`) entries. title: [Feature]: Expose startup status and health endpoint before model engine is ready
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch vLLM currently exposes its HTTP API only after the model engine has completed initialization. For models with expensive startup phases, this can leave the service unreachable for a long time even though the process is alive and making progress. For example, startup may include: Loading model checkpoints Compiling execution paths Allocating KV cache FlashInfer or backend autotuning CUDA graph capture Model-specific kernel warmup With large or hybrid models, these phases can take many minutes. During that period, an external orchestrator or monitoring system cannot distinguish between: Normal initialization A stalled startup An out-of-memory condition A crashed worker A restart loop A process that is alive but not yet ready to serve inference I would like vLLM to expose a lightweight management or health endpoint before the model engine is ready. A possible design would separate process liveness, startup state, and inference readiness: ``` GET /livez GET /readyz GET /startupz ``` Example startup response: ``` { "state": "starting", "phase": "model_warmup", "detail": "mamba2_ssd_kernel_warmup", "elapsed_seconds": 842 } ``` A minimal implementation does not need an estimated completion time or exact percentage. Even a stable state and phase enum would be useful: ``` PROCESS_STARTED LOADING_MODEL COMPILING ALLOCATING_KV_CACHE AUTOTUNING_KERNELS CAPTURING_GRAPHS WARMING_UP READY FAILED ``` The management endpoint should be served by a lightweight component that starts before engine initialization and remains available if model initializatio

summary: ## feat(serve): Add `/readiness/stages` endpoint for model-ready autoscaling ### Summary This PR adds `GET /readiness/stages` to vLLM's serve instrumentator, exposing the engine's current readiness sub-stage, estimated residual delay to model-ready state, and available HBM for KV-cache allocation. ### Motivation Existing autoscalers assume **resource-ready ≈ service-ready**. For LLM serving this is structurally wrong: - A 7B model replica takes **~40 seconds** after GPU allocation before serving SLO-compliant tokens - A 72B TP=4 replica takes **~17 minutes** This causes **elasticity loss** — requests arrive but cannot be served. Two problems require model-aware information from vLLM: **Pillar 1 (readiness delay):** The autoscaler needs `residual_delay_s` to decide whether to pre-warm replicas. Without it, it systematically underestimates how early to start. **Pillar 2 (KV-cache memory):** Even a model-ready replica fails if `hbm_available_gib < M_KV(tokens)`. We observed 100/1801 requests fail with KV-cache OOM at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.875` with 3 warm replicas — giving λ=0.338, **worse than compute-ready** (λ=0.335) despite 3× the GPU cost. Related: #6073 ### Changes - `vllm/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/health.py`: Added `ReadinessStageResponse` model and `GET /readiness/stages` route - `docs/source/features/readiness_stages.md`: Documentation with usage examples and autoscaler integration guide ### Example Response **During startup (7B, weight loading):** ```json { "stage": "loading_weights", "model_ready": false, "residual_delay_s": 50.0, "hbm_available_gib": nul

title: [Bugfix][Prefix] Retain the SWA window block that lookahead hashing costs
summary: ## Purpose With block-hash lookahead on, a 16384-token shared prefix is served only 8192 tokens from the cache to every request after the first. The sliding-window lookup misses even though the blocks it needs are in the cache — all but one of them. This keeps that one. This is the second, independent cut reported in #64808; the trailing-block drop is carried by #64875 and this change does not touch it. ## TL;DR for review - Root cause: lookahead makes the last block of the shared prefix request-specific, so the shared ceiling drops one block; the EAGLE pop drops another. The resulting hit needs one block below the retained tail, the lookup misses, and it answers from the retention segment. - Fix: ask for one extra retained block per retained boundary, but only when the pool hashes with lookahead. Default configs are untouched. - Before: `0 / 8192 / 8192 / 8192` (37.50%). After: `0 / 16352 / 16352 / 16352` (74.85%). Measured through the real `KVCacheManager` on CPU, no GPU. - The regression test asserts the hit length **and** that no fallback boundary is pinned, because the fallback is what produced the 8192. ## Cause `_resolve_num_hash_lookahead_tokens` returns `num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` whenever the drafter may look ahead, and `block_pool.py` extends each block's hash range by it. The hash of a block therefore covers the tokens *past* its end. title: [ROCm][Attention] Add an mxfp4_mla KV cache for rope-free sparse MLA (read/write path)
summary: ## Overview Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache. This is the first of the smaller PRs split out of #59739, as requested there. It contains the cache format, the write path, and a Triton read path for both the ragged kernel and the split-K decode kernel from #58584. Everything is Triton or Python: no HIP or C++ sources, and no new environment variables. ## Claims - **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token). - **Correctness:** attention over the packed cache is bit-identical to attention over the same dequantized values stored as bf16. - **No change for other KV dtypes.** The only shared-kernel change is a branch on the cache pointer's element type, which Triton resolves at compile time, so the bf16 and FP8 specializations compile to the same code as before. - **Same serving speed as bf16, no speedup claimed.** The Triton read path unpacks to bf16 before both dots, so the gain is capacity, not arithmetic. title: Fix/dsv4 sm8x o proj
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek V4 sends scaled NVIDIA output-projection weights through the fused FP8 DeepGEMM path. On A100 the first projection fails before generation while converting the inverse-RoPE output: ```text ValueError: type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture ``` DeepGEMM is unavailable throughout SM8x, so replacing only that conversion would move the failure into `fp8_einsum`. [#44847](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44847) already provides a BF16 grouped output-projection helper when scale metadata is absent. This PR is stacked on #44847 and selects that helper whenever the platform does not support DeepGEMM, including when the weights carry scale metadata. Scaled weights must still pass through `wo_a` so its quantization backend applies their scales. The helper therefore calls `wo_a` for scaled weights, reshapes its output by group, and selects the per-group diagonal. It retains #44847’s direct einsum for unscaled BF16 weights and retains the fused FP8 path on DeepGEMM-capable GPUs. The alternatives were to duplicate the BF16 inverse-RoPE projection or extend only the FP8 conversion. Reusing #44847 avoids a second implementation, while extending only the conversion would still fail at DeepGEMM. Calling the existing linear module for scaled weights preserves its quantization contract instead of reading raw FP8 weights without their scales. ## Test Plan Use a direct import of the production output-projection module, extend #44847’s existing test with a scaled-weight case, and run the complete module. title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4 K-cache gather for strided block tables
summary: ## Purpose `_dequantize_and_gather_k_kernel` accepts `block_table` tensor views but advances between rows using `block_table.shape[-1]`. A narrowed view of a fixed-width backing table retains the backing table's larger `stride(0)`, so requests after the first read incorrect physical block IDs and can access memory outside the K-cache allocation. Two fixes were considered: 1. Materialize the view with `block_table.contiguous()` before launching the kernel. 2. Pass `block_table.stride(0)` to the kernel and use the physical row stride for address calculation. We chose the stride argument because the kernel already accepts tensor views and already uses physical strides for `out` and `k_cache`. Calling `contiguous()` would repair the addressing indirectly by allocating temporary storage and copying the active block table on every invocation of this inference-path operation. Passing one scalar stride fixes the incorrect assumption at its source without adding GPU work, memory traffic, or allocator pressure. For contiguous block tables, `stride(0) == shape[-1]`, so the generated addresses remain unchanged. For narrowed views, the kernel now advances by the backing table's actual row layout. ## Test Plan Run the existing platform-dispatch test and the new direct Triton test: ```bash python3 -m pytest -v \ tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_dequantize_and_gather_k_cache \ tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_triton ``` Run the direct Triton test under Compute Sanitizer: ```bash compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck \ python3 -m pytes

title: [Kernel] Add portable Triton FP8 E4M3 conversions
summary: ## Purpose Triton kernels that cast `tl.float8e4nv` directly cannot compile those conversions for SM80 and SM86, which blocks otherwise portable attention and DeepSeek V4 kernels with `ValueError: type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture`. Provide one reusable pair of dtype-dispatched Triton helpers backed by always-inline CUDA conversion routines linked from portable SM75 LLVM bitcode. This keeps conversion semantics in one implementation, supports FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs, preserves direct FP32 rounding, and lets consumers retain native conversion paths where the architecture supports them. The alternatives were to duplicate conversion code in every consumer or wait for every supported Triton version to lower these casts on pre-SM89 GPUs. A shared helper is smaller across the full call graph, gives every consumer identical saturating round-to-nearest-even behavior, and can be removed cleanly when native lowering covers the supported architectures. This extracts the conversion layer from Michael's existing #49077 so attention and DeepSeek V4 changes can consume one prerequisite rather than carry private copies. ## Test Plan Run the focused reproducer on a physical RTX 4090 (compute capability 8.9). The unforced test uses native SM89 code generation; the other three runs force Triton to compile SM75, SM80, and SM86 targets on the same GPU: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_fp8e4nv_conversion.py -q TRITON_OVERRIDE_ARCH=sm75 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_fp8e4nv_conversion.py -q TRITON_OVERRIDE_ARCH=sm80 \ .v

title: [KVConnector] Allocate the extensible KV cache exportable for EXPORTS_FD (LMCache MP)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Implements `KVCacheAccess.EXPORTS_FD` from #66605: when a KV connector reports it, the extensible KV cache is allocated exportable as POSIX file descriptors. title: [RFC]: Reduced sampling for tensor-parallel decoding
summary: ### Motivation. Tensor-parallel vocabulary projection produces one vocabulary shard per TP rank. The current sampling path gathers all shards before selecting the next token, resulting in `O(B × V)` communication per sampling step. This is unnecessary for several common workloads: - Greedy decoding only needs the global argmax. - Bounded top-k sampling only needs the global top-k candidate set. - Greedy speculative verification only needs one target argmax per position. This RFC proposes a generic reduced sampling path that avoids full-vocabulary communication when possible and safely falls back otherwise. ### Proposed Change. Add an opt-in flag: ```text --enable-reduced-sampling ``` The feature is disabled by default and initially requires: - Model Runner V2. - Tensor parallel size greater than one. - Standard vocab-parallel logits heads. - The built-in sampler. ### Local-logits capture While `model.compute_logits()` runs, the common `LogitsProcessor` may skip the TP gather and expose: - Shard-local logits. - Global vocabulary size. - The shard's starting global token ID. - Local padded vocabulary size. Local logits are accepted only when exactly one standard projection is captured and the returned Tensor matches the captured result. Models with missing metadata, added vocabulary, multiple projections, or unsupported postprocessing use the normal full-logits path. This avoids adding `compute_logits_local()` to individual model files. ### Greedy sampling Each rank computes its local maximum and global token ID. The ranks gather only these candidate pairs and select the glob

title: [Bugfix] Profile the forward again after a profiling pass that compiled
summary: ## Purpose On a cold compile cache, `torch.compile` runs inside the first `profile_run()` of `determine_available_memory()`, and its allocator peak is charged as `transient_peak_headroom`. The KV cache is then sized smaller than on a warm boot of the same arguments. Related: #54122 (the same effect reported on CUDA), #49064 (the hybrid Mamba `max_num_seqs` check that this made flaky on ROCm). This PR profiles the forward again, after resetting the allocator peak, when the first pass compiled (`compilation_counter.num_backend_compilations` changed during the pass). Warm boots do not compile and keep a single pass. The change is 8 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py` plus a test. ### Relation to #54209 #54209 addresses the same term by dropping the allocator peak when the AOT compile block ends. This PR is not meant to replace it, and I found no open PR that does the same (searches on `transient_peak_headroom`, compile peak and `profile_run` list only #54209 as related): the difference is that this one measures the forward again instead of discarding the compile peak, so it also covers compile paths where compile and the first forward share one block (`VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE=0`, models with `_allow_aot_compile=False`), which #54209 leaves unchanged (`discard_peak=False`). It touches neither `monitor.py` nor `mem_utils.py` and adds no module state. The cost is one extra profile pass on a boot that compiled. If #54209 merges first, the extra pass stays useful for the non-AOT paths and is redundant on cold AOT boots; I am happy to restrict it to the non-AOT case or rebase onto

The output is also deterministic, with ties at the k-th score keeping the smallest key index. This issue proposes making the fused prefill top-k kernel a selectable backend, with FlashTopK as a second backend next to the native kernel. summary: ## Overview Cut the ROCM_AITER_FA sliding-window decode-table trim (`_build_swa_decode_tables`, q == 1 decodes) from 10 GPU ops to 7 per call, with byte-identical results. The trim runs eagerly on every decode step for each sliding-window KV-cache group, and it is launch-bound, so this saves about 16 us of host time per call (about 28%). This PR started as an opt-in trim of the block table for spec-decode verify (q > 1), which only paid off with a window-bounded AITER split. AITER instead merged a window-aware split, ROCm/aiter#6889 (`b6c376cfa6`). title: [Misc] Warn when gpu_memory_utilization withholds memory from the extensible KV cache
summary: ## Overview With the extensible KV cache, an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization` is a hard cap on everything the engine uses, and the KV cache gets what is left inside it. Values just under 1.0, such as a 0.9 carried over from estimate-based sizing, therefore leave free device memory unused, and nothing says so. This PR adds a startup warning for that case and fixes the out-of-memory error, which blamed the device when the cap was the limit (#66192, #66193). ## Claims - A startup warning, logged once per node, fires when an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization` above 0.8 and below 1.0 keeps at least 1 GiB of measured free memory out of the extensible KV cache. It states the amount and suggests leaving the setting unset unless other processes share the GPU. - No warning when the setting is left unset, set to 1.0 or set to 0.8 or below, or when another process already holds the memory above the cap. - When `gpu_memory_utilization` is below 1.0, the KV cache memory error names it and its 1.0 default, instead of claiming the cache "already takes all device memory". After warmup, it also names CUDA graphs and points at the capture sizes. ## Validation GB200, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `max_model_len=4096`, one run each: | `gpu_memory_utilization` | Warning | KV cache | |---|---|---| | 0.9 | "caps this instance at 165.88 GiB, keeping 15.03 GiB of free device memory out of the KV cache" | 23920 blocks (157.68 GiB) | | unset (1.0) | none | 26200 blocks (172.71 GiB) | The 15.03 GiB in the warning is exactly the difference between the two KV caches.
