title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Run store prefix lookups concurrently over DEALER/ROUTER
summary: ## Purpose Mooncake store prefix lookups go from the scheduler to worker rank 0 over a ZMQ REQ/REP pair, so they run one at a time on both ends: a single-worker executor on the scheduler, and a single loop thread on rank 0. A few slow master RPCs back up every lookup queued behind them, and with the timeout and breaker from #65939 those queued lookups come back as cache misses. This switches the channel to DEALER (scheduler) ↔ ROUTER (rank 0) so lookups run concurrently: - **Wire format.** Each request carries a request id and the time the client will wait (`budget_ms`). Replies carry the id and a status (`RESP_OK` / `RESP_ERR` / `RESP_EXPIRED`), so they can come back in any order. Replies to requests the client has given up on are dropped. - **Rank 0** runs lookups on `lookup_server_threads` daemon worker threads (new option, default 4), so a stuck master call can't block process exit. Upstream Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` and `batch_probe_key` bindings release the GIL (`py::gil_scoped_release`), and its `MasterClient` sends calls through an `RpcClientPool`, so lookups overlap during the master round trip. Most of `MooncakeStoreWorker.lookup()` only reads state set at init and builds its cache-hit pool fresh on every call. Stats are already recorded under a lock. - **Threading.** ZMQ sockets aren't thread-safe, so on each side one I/O thread owns (and closes) the socket and other threads hand it outgoing messages over an `inproc` PUSH/PULL pipe (`_SocketLoop`). - **Expiry.** Rank 0's I/O thread answers `RESP_EXPIRED` for a lookup still queued shortly before the client stops

title: [Bugfix][V1] Restore hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding
summary: ## Purpose On **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B** with MTP speculative decoding, a replay of a cached prompt never reaches the depth the prefix cache could give it, and prompts whose length is a multiple of the hash unit get **no hit at all**. Measured live before this change, with a 1072-token GDN page and `--prefix-match-unit 67`: | prompt | cached tokens on replay | ceiling | |---|---|---| | 1072 | **0** | 938 | | 2000 | **0** | 1876 | | 2144 | **0** | 2010 | | 3000 | 1072 | 2881 | | 3500 | 2144 | 3417 | ### Root cause Three rules compose badly. A lookup caps at `prompt_len - 1`, because the last token must be recomputed for logits. The MTP/EAGLE drafter then rewinds the hit one hash unit (67) further. But the producer publishes the GDN state at the prompt's own tail boundary, `prompt_len // 67 * 67`, which is at or above the cap — so the recurrent group cannot resume where the rewind lands, and the coordinator intersects the two groups down to the previous full page (or to zero). The same cap breaks the full-attention side whenever `prompt_len` is a multiple of 67 — and every page multiple is, since `1072 = 16 × 67`. Its partial-tail entry is registered at `prompt_len // 67 * 67 == prompt_len`, which the `- 1` cap excludes, so full attention itself matches nothing below the page boundary and the hybrid hit collapses to 0. That is the `1072 → 0`, `2144 → 0` row above. ### Fix Write-side only, all of it gated on MTP/EAGLE plus fine-grained hashing being active: - `mamba_state_cache_position(num_tokens, block_size, hash_block_size)` in `kv_cache_utils.py`: `unit = min(hash_block_size, b

title: HybridKVCacheCoordinator: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's ephemeral content incorrectly vetoes GPU-tier prefix cache reuse
summary: ## Summary `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`) requires every KV-cache group of a hybrid model to independently report a nonzero hit before confirming any prefix reuse for a request, on the GPU tier, independent of any KV connector. When serving DeepSeek-V4 with DSpark speculative decoding, the draft-model KV-cache group can never satisfy this, so it incorrectly vetoes reuse of the target model's own KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) even when those groups genuinely still hold valid, resident GPU blocks for a matching prefix. Concretely, this means: a follow-up request sharing a prefix with GPU blocks still resident from a previous request (shared system prompt, multi-turn conversation), or a request resumed after preemption, gets treated as having zero reusable prefix and is fully recomputed from scratch, even though the target model's real cache groups could have served part or all of that prefix. ## Root cause Same underlying issue as #47890, at a different layer. `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._lookup()` and `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` independently reimplement the same iterative AND-convergence lookup algorithm, one for the RAM-tier offloading path, one for the GPU tier. #47890 covers the RAM-tier symptom (`external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stuck at 0). This issue is the same defect on the GPU-tier side of that same algorithm. `find_longest_cache_hit()`'s per-group loop calls `manager_cls.find_longest_cache_hit(...)` for every group and treats any group's `0`-block result

title: Support partial fused MoE LoRA adapters
summary: ## Summary Hey! This fixes loading PEFT-format fused MoE adapters that target only one of the two fused projections. ### 🐛 Describe the bug When running models with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) enabled under W8A8 (or similar) quantization, severe silent precision loss occurs. title: [Bug][Spec Decode] Drafter attention backend auto-selection picks FlashInfer on SM90 for a sliding-window drafter, hitting the guard crash
summary: ### Environment Same as #48494 (v0.25.0, single H100 NVL 94GB SM90, Gemma4 MTP drafter with 3 sliding-attention layers + 1 full-attention layer), **without** `--attention-backend`. ### Behavior - Target model backend selection: `Using TRITON_ATTN attention backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON_ATTN']` — fine (heterogeneous head dims exclude others). - Drafter selection: `Using FLASHINFER attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER', 'TRITON_ATTN']` — then engine init crashes: ``` File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 757, in __init__ raise NotImplementedError( NotImplementedError: FlashInfer backend on SM90 currently crashes with sliding-window attention layers. Use the default attention backend. ``` ### Expected The auto-selector should exclude FlashInfer for a draft model containing sliding-window layers on SM90, instead of selecting it and failing at `create_metadata_builders`. The constraint is already documented in-code — the guard at `flashinfer.py:757` cites `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3578`; the selector just doesn't consult it. title: [RFC]: KV offload event path refactor — provenance-carrying events and key-only removals
summary: ### Motivation. > Code references are pinned to `main` at > `3d204dfdaaf09d67d49c7855630ef949754e0f8f`; implementation starts from > current `main`. [#48679](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48679) added self-describing KV-offload events as an initial implementation. This RFC finishes the event-path refactor in two PRs. Today, `OffloadKey` contains only `(block_hash, group_idx)` ([base.py:23-41](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d204dfdaaf09d67d49c7855630ef949754e0f8f/vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py#L23-L41)), and a raw `OffloadingEvent` has no request context ([base.py:153-159](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d204dfdaaf09d67d49c7855630ef949754e0f8f/vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py#L153-L159)). title: [RFC]: Generic Control RPC for KV Connectors
summary: ### Motivation. For KV migration, a user needs to tell a KV connector which set of blocks to transfer to a remote destination. Today the only connector-facing control surface from outside the engine is reset_connector_cache (scheduler.py), which calls a fixed, argument-less reset_cache() on the scheduler-side connector and returns a bool. Anything richer requires adding a new bespoke endpoint, engine method, and RPC wrapper per operation, and baking each operation's schema into vLLM core. This RFC proposes a single, generic, connector-defined control channel: an external caller sends a request payload to the scheduler-side KV connector and receives a response payload. The payload is opaque to vLLM — carried as raw bytes end-to-end — so the connector owns all (de)serialization and semantics. vLLM provides one stable transport, and each connector defines whatever request/response protocol it needs on top of the byte payload. New connector operations then require no changes to vLLM core. ### Proposed Change. # Overview The motivating use case: a migration controller needs to tell a KV connector *which blocks to transfer to a remote destination*. The connector already knows how to move blocks; what it lacks is a runtime channel to receive such an instruction and report the result. This RFC adds one generic channel for exactly that — and for any other connector-specific control operation. A caller issues a single HTTP request whose body is the connector-defined request payload (raw bytes; vLLM never parses it): ```http POST /v1/kv_connector/rpc Content-Type: application/octet-st

title: [RFC]: Per-request activation of multiple LoRA adapters with static scales
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM's multi-LoRA serving currently routes each request to exactly one adapter: `LoRARequest` holds a single `lora_name`/`lora_int_id`, and the Punica metadata maps each token to one LoRA index. There is no way to apply two or more already-loaded adapters to the same request. This blocks several practical workflows: 1. **Composed / incrementally-trained adapters.** A common pattern is training `adapter_1` on top of a frozen `adapter_0` (continual or staged fine-tuning). Serving the result requires both deltas active at once: `y = Wx + s_0·B_0A_0x + s_1·B_1A_1x`. 2. **Combinatorial merge explosion.** The current workaround is merging adapters offline (e.g. PEFT `add_weighted_adapter(combination_type="cat")`). With N adapters and per-request combinations, this requires materializing and loading up to N-choose-k merged artifacts, versus keeping only N adapters loaded with runtime composition. 3. **Per-request scaling.** Requests that weight the same adapters differently (`0.7·style + 0.5·domain`) cannot be served by any finite set of offline merges. Related work: - vllm-project/vllm-omni#2149 proposes exactly this capability for diffusion models, where multi-LoRA composition with independent scales is a standard workflow (Diffusers `set_adapters(names, weights)`). This RFC is the LLM-side counterpart. - vllm-project/vllm#49705 proposes router-driven adapter mixtures (X-LoRA/MixLoRA-style), where gate weights are computed per-token/per-layer by a learned router. This RFC is deliberately narrower: the adapter set and scales are **static per request and supplied b

title: [Core] Add configurable load-balancing strategy to EPLB
summary: ## Purpose EPLB currently selects hierarchical or global rebalancing implicitly and leaves a TODO in `EplbState.rearrange` to treat prefill and decode nodes differently. The [DeepSeek EPLB documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/EPLB) recommends hierarchical load balancing for prefill deployments with smaller expert-parallel groups and global load balancing for decode deployments with larger expert-parallel groups. This configuration flag was also discussed when EPLB was introduced in [#18343](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/18343#issuecomment-2918047879). This PR adds `load_balancing_strategy` to `EPLBConfig`: - `"auto"` is the default and preserves the existing topology-selection behavior; - `"hierarchical"` preserves expert-group locality across detected nodes and rejects incompatible group/node or rank/node topologies; - `"global"` passes a single global group and node to the existing EPLB policy. The strategy is selected explicitly by each deployment. It is not inferred from `KVTransferConfig.kv_role`, because disaggregated deployments may set `kv_role="kv_both"` on both the prefill and decode instances. The existing load window, policy implementation, expert transfer, and map commit paths are unchanged. Duplicate-work checks were run on 2026-08-12: ```bash gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \ --search 'EPLB load_balancing_strategy' gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \ --search 'EPLB hierarchical global' gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \ --search 'prefill decode EPLB' gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --

title: [Feature]: split local/external prefix-cache hits in `prompt_tokens_details`
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Background With distributed prefix caching (KV connectors such as Mooncake / lmcache), cache hits in a single prefill can come from two different sources: - **local**: hits on this instance's GPU prefix cache; - **external**: hits fetched from a remote KV store / another instance via the KV connector. The scheduler already tracks `num_local_cached_tokens` / `num_external_cached_tokens` separately in `PrefillStats`, but `OutputProcessor` only forwards their sum (`num_cached_tokens`), so the breakdown is lost before it reaches the OpenAI serving layer — users cannot tell, per request, where cache hits came from. Exposing this information per-request may also be handy for pricing purposes. ## Current behavior With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` enabled, the response currently looks like: ```json "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 3627, "created_cache_tokens": 0, "multimodal_tokens": null } ``` ## Expected behavior Add two optional keys, `local_cached_tokens` / `external_cached_tokens`, alongside the existing fields: ```json "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 2320, "created_cache_tokens": 0, "multimodal_tokens": null, "local_cached_tokens": 1216, "external_cached_tokens": 1104 } ``` Invariant: `cached_tokens == local_cached_tokens + external_cached_tokens`. ## Requirements - Strictly additive change: existing fields (`cached_tokens` / `created_cache_tokens` / `multimodal_tokens`) must be preserved untouched; - New fields default to `None` and must not affect existing output when the flag is off or the values carry n

title: [RFC]: fp8_ds_mla KV cache on pre-SM89 (Ampere) GPUs via software-dequant TritonMLA decode
summary: ### Motivation MLA models (DeepSeek family, Kimi-K3) on Ampere fleets (RTX 3090 / A100) can only run bf16 KV today: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8*` is rejected below SM89. The `fp8_ds_mla` packed layout (656 B/token/layer vs 1152 bf16) is storage-only — the query stays bf16 — so it does not need native fp8 arithmetic at all. Enabling it on Ampere is **1.75× context per card**. ### What already works upstream (verified on sm_86) - the CUDA cache writer (`*_ds_mla_insert`) is ungated in CMake, and its PDL blocks are no-ops below SM90; - chunked-prefill dequant (`cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`) is ungated, and `_compute_prefill_context` already dispatches on `fp8_ds_mla`; - `MLAAttentionSpec.real_page_size_bytes` already returns 656 for this layout. ### The one gap TritonMLA decode reads a contiguous 576-wide bf16 row and does not list `fp8_ds_mla` in its supported cache dtypes. ### Proposal 1. A Triton decode path reading the packed 656-byte row with in-kernel fp8e4m3→fp16 bit-math dequant (~220-line kernel, no new CUDA). 2. Carve `fp8_ds_mla` out of the SM89 kv-cache-dtype gate **for TritonMLA only**. No Hopper/Blackwell path changes. ### Evidence in hand - kernel test suite 12/12, CPU-runnable via `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` (CI-friendly); - cosine vs bf16: 0.9999967; - greedy outputs identical to bf16, including under pipeline parallelism (PP=2); - measured end-to-end on RTX 3090. ### Alternatives considered - Status quo: bf16-only KV on Ampere — the 1.75× context stays on the table. - Enabling the plain-fp8 KV path below SM89: rejected — that path genuinely needs native fp8 query

title: Fix missing q_scale fallback for FP8 KV cache
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fix the missing `q_scale` fallback for quantized KV caches when a checkpoint provides `k_scale` and `v_scale` but omits `q_scale`. ## Claims - Preserve the `k_scale` fallback through the final query-scale assignment. - Give an explicit checkpoint `q_scale` precedence over the fallback. - Use the already-adjusted fallback on FNUZ platforms without applying the scaling adjustment twice. ## Details `process_weights_after_loading()` writes the fallback directly to `layer._q_scale`, then later recomputes the query scale from the still-invalid `layer.q_scale` parameter and overwrites it with `1.0`. This change retains `k_scale` in a local fallback variable and applies it during the final assignment to `layer._q_scale` and `layer._q_scale_float`. For example, a checkpoint with `k_scale=0.25` and no `q_scale` keeps a query scale of `0.25` on non-FNUZ platforms. On FNUZ platforms, `k_scale` has already received its scaling adjustment before becoming the fallback. Keeping the fallback in a separate branch avoids applying that adjustment again. title: [RFC] Bounded, restart-safe capacity management for the filesystem KV offload tier
summary: ﻿### Motivation. The current filesystem KV offload tier (`type: "fs"`, `TieringOffloadingSpec`) has no configurable disk capacity limit. Persisted KV blocks accumulate indefinitely and may exhaust the backing disk in long-running deployments. The existing configuration also cannot express the following requirement: > Within a given disk budget, preferentially retain prefixes with high reuse > value and high recomputation cost, and safely evict low-value cache entries. This RFC proposes optional bounded, restart-safe capacity management for the FS tier, including: - a `max_bytes` capacity limit per FS tier storage instance; - cache admission and eviction; - recovery of cache files and policy metadata after restart; - in-flight read/write protection; - optional `cache_namespace` isolation; - capacity, admission, eviction, and hit-related metrics. When `max_bytes` is unset or `null`, the current unbounded behavior is preserved for backward compatibility. ### Relationship to related work This RFC focuses on capacity management, admission, and eviction policy within the existing FS tier. Related work: - #54777: worker-side GDS transport and the `FSOffloadingWorker` abstraction. Its scope is explicitly restricted to the worker side ("changes are restricted to the worker - we avoid making changes in the scheduler or to the multi-tier logic"), so it is complementary to this RFC, which operates on the scheduler-side tiering layer. It also absorbs the scope of #48504. The admission/eviction policy proposed here is transport-agnostic and remains valid over any `FSOffloadingWorker` bac

title: [Bugfix][Model] Route Gemma 4 per-layer embeddings through the CPU weight offloader
summary: ## Overview Gemma 4 E2B/E4B build their per-layer embedding (PLE) table (`embed_tokens_per_layer`, 4.4 GiB / 5.25 GiB in bf16) outside `make_layers`, so it never reaches the weight offloader. title: [Bugfix] Use realistic top_k in _dummy_sampler_run to avoid SM120 startup hang
summary: Purpose Fixes #42987. On RTX 5090 (SM120), vllm serve hangs indefinitely during engine startup. As diagnosed in the issue with py-spy, the hang is in _dummy_sampler_run (profile_run → _initialize_kv_caches): it builds dummy SamplingMetadata with top_k = logits.size(1) - 1 (i.e. vocab_size - 1), and the top-k masking kernel never returns for that value on SM120. The issue reports the same hang in both the Triton path (apply_top_k_top_p_triton) and the FlashInfer path (top_k_mask_logits). _dummy_sampler_run exists only to warm up / memory-profile the sampler for KV-cache sizing. Its inputs are already entirely synthetic (torch.rand_like hidden states, dummy temperature/top_p/penalties), and its output is discarded. The vocab_size - 1 value is an arbitrary "max-ish" placeholder — nothing depends on it, and the top-k masking operates on the full [num_reqs, vocab_size] logits tensor regardless, so the memory footprint is independent of top_k. This PR substitutes a realistic top_k (50, within the typical production range of ≤100) in the dummy run. This avoids the buggy SM120 kernel codegen path with no functional change and an identical memory-profiling footprint. title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashInfer plan buffer race causing illegal memory access with PP
summary: ## Overview Fixes #63505. `FlashInferMetadataBuilder` could call FlashInfer `plan()` again before the GPU had copied the previous plan out of the wrapper's page-locked buffer. The earlier step's attention kernel then ran with the later step's plan and read out of bounds. This PR makes the builder wait for that copy before it plans again. The race became reachable with #57214. ## Claims - Fixes the `illegal memory access` that kills the engine on the first long cold prefill with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, `--pipeline-parallel-size=3`, chunked prefill and prefix caching. - The wait covers every `plan()` call in `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build()`: prefill, DCP prefill and decode (`fast_plan_decode`, which also plans the CUDA-graph decode wrappers). The TRTLLM/XQA paths do not call `plan()`, so they neither wait nor record. - The host waits only when it is more than one plan ahead of the GPU. On one GPU with async scheduling it never blocked (0 of 2000 builds). - New test `test_flashinfer_plan_waits_for_previous_plan_copy` (prefill and decode cases) fails without the fix and passes with it. ## Validation **Setup:** 3 x NVIDIA A10 (23 GB, sm_86). vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`, built from source at `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b`, with and without this commit. title: [Bugfix] Replace non-deterministic index_add_ with scatter-then-sum in TopKWeightAndReduceNaiveBatched
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #53430. `TopKWeightAndReduceNaiveBatched.apply` used `output.index_add_(0, t_idx, gathered)` to scatter weighted expert outputs back to their source tokens. When multiple experts route to the same token (the common case with `top_k > 1`), `torch.index_add_` on CUDA performs **atomic floating-point adds** whose order of accumulation is non-deterministic across runs. Because floating-point addition is not associative, repeated calls can differ in the low bits, and those differences can propagate far enough to change a greedy argmax token and break determinism for `temperature=0` / fixed-seed inference. ## Root cause `torch.index_add_` on CUDA uses atomic operations when multiple source indices map to the same destination. The order of atomic adds is non-deterministic, and since BF16 has limited precision, different accumulation orders produce slightly different results — enough to flip a greedy `argmax` at near-tie logits. ## Fix Replace the atomic scatter-add with a deterministic two-step approach: 1. **Scatter** gathered expert outputs into a `(T, topk, K)` buffer where each `(token, topk-slot)` position is written at most once (no atomics, no races). 2. **Reduce** with `ops.moe_sum` — the same kernel already used by `TopKWeightAndReduceContiguous`, which accumulates in fixed top-k order with an FP32 accumulator. This keeps the single vectorized `nonzero`/gather path and does not restore the old per-expert Python loop. The tradeoff is one temporary `(T, topk, K)` tensor. ## Related work #53442 is an overlapping proposal for #53430. This existing PR includes

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] attention: Improve the DSA prefill kernel with LiteTopK (FP8, GLM-5.x / DeepSeek) on SM100
summary: ## Motivation DSA-style sparse attention (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4.1) selects the top-k keys for each prefill row from indexer scores over all visible keys. In the dense baseline evaluated here, DeepGEMM `mqa_logits` materializes the full `[rows, keys]` logits, then a separate top-k reads them back. At long context, both the logits traffic and selection work grow with `rows x keys`. The logits-memory budget also forces large prefills into smaller scoring calls. This PR replaces the kernel behind `fused_mqa_topk` with the sampled-threshold path of [LiteTopK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976), continuing [vLLM #48726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726) and [#60618](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60618). In particular, we retain the **sample-filter-select framework for fused sparse-indexer scoring and top-k**, which was first proposed in [LiteTopK (#48726)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726). The details of each stage: 1. **Sample.** We sample keys across the visible context randomly, then predict a per-row threshold from a conservative quantile of the sampled scores. title: [RFC] Report per-request prefill progress over gRPC
summary: ## Motivation and scope A KV-aware router prices a prefill worker from its own estimate of the work that worker still owes. Two kinds of error make that estimate wrong. Work the worker has already computed, reused from cache, or recomputed after preemption is invisible to the router. Work that is queued but not yet scheduled is visible neither to the router nor to a worker-level aggregate without a guess: counting queued prompts at their prompt length over-counts them, because they may hit the prefix cache. We implemented the aggregate variant first. In a clean A/B on 2P+2D, a router that consumed the aggregate (queued prompts counted at prompt length) lost 35.8% on TTFT p99 versus pricing from its own admission estimate. Excluding queued work instead produces a blind spot that is arithmetic rather than noise: a request admitted before a sample and still queued contributes to neither the sample nor the router's delta, for as long as it stays queued. Earlier per-variant comparisons posted on the PR are retracted: single run per arm, a baseline that drifts between 4.13 and 5.02 s mean TTFT, and one A/B that was invalid because the build had lost the consumer. Scope: report the remaining prefill work per request, on the stream that already carries that request's output, and let the consumer price a running request exactly. - The scheduler reports one update per scheduled chunk, throttled to a quarter of the remaining work and capped per request; the final zero is always sent. - The update travels as an ordinary engine output, so the existing per-request routing carries it; the

summary: ## Summary Enables adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. title: [Core][Scheduler] Add shortest_prefill_first scheduling policy
summary: ## Overview Adds `--scheduling-policy shortest_prefill_first`. Before each scheduling step, requests whose remaining prefill length is known are ordered shortest first within each scheduler queue. Nothing else in the scheduler changes: token budget, chunking, KV connector lookups and loads, block allocation and preemption all run as under `fcfs`. The target is prefill instances serving multi-turn, prefix-heavy traffic (e.g. agentic coding with an external KV cache tier such as Mooncake), where uncached tokens per request are heavy-tailed and a few long prefills ahead in the queue set the TTFT of many short ones. ## Ordering rules Key: remaining prefill tokens, smallest first; ties keep their current order. | queue | requests that are ordered | key | |---|---|---| | `running` | prefill chunks | prompt tokens not yet computed | | `kv_holding_waiting` | all (their external hit is final, e.g. a KV connector load in flight or done) | tokens not yet computed | | `waiting`, `async_kv_waiting` (first 64) | requests whose KV connector lookup has finished, including a hit of 0 | tokens not in that hit | A request whose remaining length is not known keeps its exact position: a decode, a waiting request with no or an unfinished external lookup, or one that skips external KV reads. Known requests are permuted only among the positions they already hold, so nothing moves past an unordered request. title: [Perf][Kernel] Adopt PTX 9.4 `ldmatrix.s8.s4` (hardware INT4→INT8 expanding load) in W4A8-INT8 paths
summary: ## Summary PTX ISA 9.4 (CUDA 13.4.0 Developer Preview) exposes a new `ldmatrix` variant that performs **in-flight sign extension of packed INT4 to INT8 during the shared-memory matrix load**: ``` ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n16.{x1,x2,x4}{.shared{::cta}}.s8.s4 r, [p]; ``` Source data is densely packed signed 4-bit elements; the hardware expands them to signed 8-bit values in the destination fragment. This can eliminate the register-level INT4→INT8 unpack sequences (`lop3`/`prmt` bit tricks and PRMT LUTs) in our W4A8-INT8 kernels, and potentially the dequant-oriented weight interleaving in repack. Doc: PTX ISA 9.4, §9.7.16.5.15 (`ldmatrix`), https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/developer-preview/13.4/parallel-thread-execution/index.html ## Hardware verification (already done) Verified with `ptxas`/`nvdisasm` from CUDA 13.4.0 preview (`V13.4.46`), no GPU required: - `ptxas` accepts the instruction for **sm_90a, sm_100a/f, sm_103a, sm_107a/f, sm_110f, sm_120f, sm_121a** (PTX targets per doc: `sm_90a, sm_100f, sm_110f, sm_120f`). - SASS is a **single LDSM instruction** on every architecture — no unpack sequence is generated. The encoding is bit-identical across all seven targets (opcode `0x783b` = LDSM, modifier `0x9000/0x9100/0x9200` for x1/x2/x4; cf. `LDSM.16.M88` = `0x0000`, `LDSM.U4x16P64TO8.M816` = `0xa800`, `LDSM.U6x16P32TO8.M816` = `0xb000`). - Notably **Hopper (sm_90a) is supported** — the datapath appears to have existed in silicon since GH100; PTX 9.4 merely exposes it. Existing H100/H200 fleets benefit immediately. - `nvdisasm` 13.4 does not yet print a mnemonic for this modifie

title: [Bugfix] Apply the layer q_scale only to FP8 queries in FlashInfer
summary: ## Overview Fixes #63043. When the query that reaches FlashInfer is BF16/FP16, `FlashInferImpl.forward` still passed the layer's FP8 query scale (`layer._q_scale_float`) to the kernel. title: [CI][Bugfix][ROCm] Seed each MLA backend correctness case; allow one bf16 ULP for ROCm glm
summary: - `test_mla_backends.py`: seed each case at the start of `_run_backend_correctness`, so its random inputs no longer depend on which tests ran before it - `test_mla_backends.py`: on ROCm with a bf16 KV cache and `v_head_dim=256` (glm), allow one bf16 ULP of the largest reference value as `atol` `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness[False-trtllm-gen-auto-glm-…ROCM_AITER_FA]` fails on both `TRITON_MLA` and `ROCM_AITER_MLA` in every 4-shard run of "(MI355 DPX) V1 Attention" (e.g. https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97849), while it passed under the old `--shard-id` layout. No code change caused it: `_run_backend_correctness` draws all inputs from `torch.randn` without reseeding, so the inputs depend on the tests that ran earlier in the process, and the runtime shard plugin changed that order. Swept on an MI300X with the main wheel, the case passes for some seeds and fails for others, and the old and new code give identical results seed for seed. In all 17 seeds the largest diff from the SDPA reference is exactly one bf16 ULP of the largest reference value (0.03125, with max |ref| between 4.0 and 4.75). That is above the `1e-2` atol, so elements near zero fail (#55609, #55611). The new `atol` is that one ULP, computed from each reference rather than a fixed number, and only for the ROCm glm bf16 combination. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Register host-backed KV pages over their full stride span
summary: ## Overview `NixlConnector` rejects host-resident KV pools whose pages are padded to a kernel/packing alignment. Registration uses `cache.nbytes`, which stops short of the last page's stride, while the descriptor path addresses `num_blocks * block_stride`. This patch registers the full stride span for `is_host_resident` groups. ## Claims - Fixes the startup failure `KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions ...` for host-resident, padded KV pages. - Device-resident groups and unpadded host pages register exactly the same range as before; only padded host-resident groups change. - A host-resident KV group can now register at all. The host-backed P/D transfer path is a separate change and is not part of this PR. ## Validation New unit test: `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py::test_host_resident_padded_page_registers_its_stride_span` (extends `_register_overlaid_mla_worker` with `host_resident=True`). On `main` it fails with the exact production assertion: ``` AssertionError: KV cache view cannot be partitioned into NIXL regions cache_nbytes=96, num_blocks=4, block_stride=64, physical_page_size=32 ``` With the fix it passes, and the registered range and descriptors are asserted to be `(allocation.data_ptr(), num_blocks * block_stride, 0, "")`. Regression (CPU-only NIXL suites): ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \ tests/v1/

title: [Bug]: NixlConnector: with n > 1, prefill releases KV blocks after the first decode child's read, later children can decode from reused blocks
summary: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ```text vLLM: 0.32.0 (docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0), unmodified image Model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, --enforce-eager, --gpu-memory-utilization=0.5, --max-model-len=8192 KV transfer: --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' on both pods NIXL over UCX, UCX_TLS=cuda_ipc,cuda_copy,tcp Topology: 1 prefill pod + 1 decode pod, 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB each, on separate nodes (OpenShift) ``` `collect_env.py` was not run inside the pods; the image is the unmodified release image. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug With `NixlConnector` in pull mode, a decode request with `n > 1` makes `n` child requests read the KV of one prefill request, but the prefill worker releases that request's blocks after the first child's read notification. Children whose reads finish later can read blocks that another prefill request has already reallocated and written, and then decode from that request's KV. The client gets wrong output with HTTP 200. The only signal is one prefill-side log line per late child: `Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request ... were retrieved by a decode worker. They may have expired.` This was first reported privately (GHSA-grjf-r4cj-w3ch). The vulnerability management team classified it as out of scope for security and asked for a public issue as a correctness bug. #### Cause - `AsyncLLM.add_request` splits `n > 1` into `n` child `EngineCoreRequest`s, each with a copy of the same `kv_transfer_params`, so all children pull from the same `remote_request_id

title: [Perf][DSpark] lossless improve DSpark throughput by W2 matrix topk pruned
summary: ## Purpose Reduce DSpark draft latency with opt-in candidate pruning of the Markov projection. At each position, candidates are the union of the top-k backbone logits and the top-m precomputed Markov-bias entries. The sequential walk evaluates and samples within that union. `markov_topk=0` keeps the full-vocabulary path. This changes the draft proposal distribution. Correct probabilistic rejection sampling must use exactly the truncated distribution used to draw the draft tokens; draft quality and acceptance length can change. Target-distribution preservation therefore depends on sampler/cache correctness and is not established by throughput measurements alone. ## Implementation and compatibility - Use a fused Triton walk over base-logit and optional static Markov candidates. - Cache the candidate proposal logits for probabilistic rejection sampling. - Preserve draft-to-target vocabulary mapping. - Keep pruning disabled by default; unsupported quantized or sharded Markov heads use the dense path. - Use the existing platform-aware top-k dispatcher so importing DSpark does not unconditionally require FlashInfer. - Use the maximum score for overlapping candidate IDs, matching token-keyed Gumbel sampling; synchronize cache clearing before updates. - Fall back to dense drafting when online acceptance estimation or draft watermarking is enabled. title: [Quantization] Diagnose CUDA driver too old for Marlin PTX JIT across all Marlin users
summary: ## Summary Detect a CUDA driver that is too old to JIT-compile Marlin's PTX once, at the shared Marlin op layer, and log a single actionable warning that tells the user how to keep using Marlin. This replaces the earlier AWQ-only fallback. Kernel selection is unchanged for every quantization method. In #36235 that was torch/vLLM cu129 on an H20 with a 12.8 driver. title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Wire Gemma-4 MoE layers into EPLB
summary: ## Purpose `--enable-eplb` has no effect on Gemma-4 MoE models (for example `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`). The server starts, but EPLB logs `avg_tokens=0.00, max_tokens=0, balancedness=0.0000` at every step and never rearranges experts. There are three causes: 1. `Gemma4DecoderLayer` builds its MoE layer without `enable_eplb` or `num_redundant_experts`, so the router has no `EplbLayerState` and records no expert load. 2. `Gemma4ForCausalLM` reports `num_physical_experts = num_local_physical_experts = num_experts` and `num_redundant_experts = 0`, so EPLB sees every expert as local to every rank. 3. Gemma-4 checkpoints store experts as fused `[num_experts, ...]` tensors. The fused branch of `RoutedExperts.load_weights` loads only the logical experts, so with `num_redundant_experts > 0` the redundant physical experts would keep uninitialized weights. This PR: - passes `enable_eplb` and `num_redundant_experts` from the parallel config to Gemma-4's `FusedMoEFactory`, as `qwen3_moe.py` does; - takes the physical and local expert counts from the first MoE layer's `moe_config`; - in the fused branch of `RoutedExperts.load_weights`, also loads each redundant physical expert `i` from logical expert `i % num_logical_experts`. title: [Feature]: Add opt-in in-flight request deduplication for chat completions
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Problem An agent gateway can retry a chat completion while the original request is still running. This can happen when the gateway's timeout expires before the upstream connection is closed or the engine has finished cancelling the original generation. vLLM may end up processing both attempts independently. Prefix caching can help with repeated prefill work, but it doesn't prevent the second request from entering the scheduler and consuming decode capacity. For a gateway that retries requests automatically, this can waste GPU time on generations that represent the same logical operation. Could the OpenAI-compatible API support an opt-in guard that rejects duplicate requests while the original generation is still active? ### Proposed behavior I'd limit the initial implementation to non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` requests within a single API server process. The caller supplies a stable operation key across retries, separate from the existing `request_id` and `X-Request-Id` mechanisms. For example, a proposed request header could look like: ```http POST /v1/chat/completions Content-Type: application/json X-Inference-Operation-Key: agent-step-42 { "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the deployment status."} ], "temperature": 0.2, "stream": false } ``` The header is only an example of the proposed contract, not an existing vLLM parameter. When enabled, the API server would atomically claim the operation key before submitting generation to the engine. - The first request claims the key

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Enable FlashInfer mm-prefix attention
summary: ## Purpose This keeps multimodal PrefixLM batches on the native FlashInfer backend. It is the vLLM adapter for FlashInfer's mm-prefix batch-prefill wrapper: it builds per-query `[start, end]` rows from request metadata, decides when the path is eligible, and calls the wrapper, whose attention variant evaluates `(causal AND sliding_window) OR mm_prefix` on every KV tile. No `O(qo_len * kv_len)` mask is materialized; the ranges are one `int32 (N, 2)` buffer sized by scheduled tokens, 128 KiB at 16384 tokens. The prefill still traverses the full rectangle, so the gain is memory, not FLOPs. The wrapper comes from [FlashInfer #5189](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5189) and has shipped since 0.7.1, so main's pin already has it. FlashInfer builds the variant's JIT module when the wrapper is constructed. The mm-prefix wrapper is planned beside the regular prefill path rather than replacing it, so text-only batches, decodes and layers whose ranges are cleared at forward time (Gemma 4 full-attention groups) keep trtllm-gen or FA3 with main's query dtype and scales. On the SM100 family `TRITON_FLASHINFER` stays the automatic choice; an explicitly selected `FLASHINFER` serves the ranges natively and does not advertise large pages. An SM100 NVFP4 cache keeps its V scale factors in the trtllm-gen swizzle, so native mm-prefix accepts it only when FlashInfer's wrapper takes `v_sf_swizzled` and rejects it otherwise. title: [Bugfix][Core] Reclaim KV blocks from idle streaming-input sessions under KV pressure
summary: ## Purpose Under KV pressure, resumable streaming-input sessions that are paused (`WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`) or resumed-but-unscheduled retain their KV blocks indefinitely, which can deadlock the engine: sessions park holding blocks, resume with continuations that no longer fit, and every `schedule()` breaks out of the waiting loop with nothing scheduled, while preemption only reclaims from `running` (which is empty). This PR reclaims those retained blocks at the waiting loop's allocation-failure point. Victims are, in order: (1) paused sessions — idle with no pending work, zero-cost victims; (2) WAITING resumable sessions still holding blocks — picking the newest/lowest-priority victim, mirroring the running loop's preemption choice. Victims are found by their resource fact (`_holds_kv_blocks`) across all waiting containers, not by queue membership, so the search is robust to the scan loop's step-local bookkeeping. The victim is freed exactly like a preemption (blocks, encoder cache, inflight-prefill tracking, `num_computed_tokens = 0`, PREEMPTED event, `reset_preempted_req_ids`) but keeps its status and its `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` accounting; it moves out of the kv-holding queues and recomputes from scratch when resumed. Each reclaim strictly shrinks the candidate set, so the retry provably terminates. Reclaim is skipped when the victim's blocks can only be freed lazily (deferred frees can't help this step's allocation), matching the running loop's discipline. ## Relationship to other PRs - Supersedes/extends #49439 (whose approach — reclaim from a WAITING res

title: [Model Loader] Run model-level post-load finalization from the loader hook
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview **`load_weights` must not assume all weights arrive in one call.** RL weight updates call it once per bucket: verl sends 512 MB buckets tensor by tensor, and the NCCL engine calls it once per tensor (inside `disable_mtp_completeness_check()`). So a weight and its scale, or the two halves of a merged tensor, can land in different calls. Any post-load work inside `load_weights` then runs on partial weights, once per bucket. Context: RFC #54477, tracker #50079. The PR has three parts: 1. **One finish step for every load.** `finalize_model_weights(model)` runs once after a full load and once at the end of every reload, and calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. There are no per-model opt-ins. This mirrors SGLang, which post-processes once at `end_weight_update`. 2. **Split merged tensors written through the weight loader.** Molmo/Molmo2 embedding halves and Llama4 DP-vision q/k/v are written straight into their rows, so any split or order of calls works. Nothing is parked across calls. 3. **Post-load work moves out of `load_weights` into the hook.** That includes the blocks that used to rebuild derived state on every call. Coverage: an AST script enumerated every `def load_weights` in `vllm/` (447), and each was checked in source. That covers multimodal wrappers, MTP/EAGLE/DSpark/DFlash drafters, adapters, `AutoWeightsLoader`, layer-level loaders, model loaders and the `vllm/models/*` platform variants. Every model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` was also checked for whether it is safe to re-run on new weights. ##

title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Keep image bidirectional attention within the sliding window on the V2 model runner
summary: ## Purpose #47217 fixed Gemma4 vision models silently falling back to **causal-only** image attention whenever a single image's soft-token span exceeded the text sliding window (e.g. ~1120 soft tokens at `max_soft_tokens=1120` vs `sliding_window=1024`). The runner was dropping the *entire* bidirectional `mm_prefix` range for such an image; the fix gated that skip on a model capability flag, `mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window`, so models that bound `mm_prefix` **in-kernel** keep the full range and let the kernel clamp it per-query — matching HF's `(causal OR blockwise) AND sliding_window` on local layers. That fix only landed in the **V1** `GPUModelRunner`. The V2 model runner has its own copy of the range-building logic in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py::compute_mm_prefix_ranges`, which still drops oversized ranges unconditionally: ```python for r in mm_feature.mm_position.extract_embeds_range(): if sliding_window is not None and (r[1] - r[0] + 1) > sliding_window: continue # <- no opt-out, unlike V1 ``` So the original defect is still reachable today on `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. This matters more than it did at the time of #47217, because V2 is no longer opt-in for these configs — `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` force-enables V2 for DSpark speculative decoding and for hybrid DFlash drafters, both of which are used with Gemma4. A user who serves Gemma4 with images and DSpark drafting gets the degraded mask with no warning and no error. title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Spec Decode][DCP] Align ranks before DFlash speculator graph capture
summary: ## Purpose **Fixes a boot blocker for decode context parallelism (DCP) combined with speculative decoding: the DFlash/DSpark speculator faults during CUDA graph capture.** When the DFlash/DSpark draft is **DCP-sharded**, the graph captured by `DFlashSpeculator.capture()` contains a context-parallel collective. Graph capture is only safe when every rank enters it aligned: a rank still finishing earlier work can have its collective recorded into a peer's graph, which faults. Nothing currently quiesces or aligns the ranks before `capture()` runs. Symptom: every rank dies in `Capturing model for DSpark speculator...` with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N ... Reason: Unknown`, at a **fresh fault address each time**, with a clean teardown. **It is a race, not an out-of-bounds access.** The decisive evidence is that booting the same configuration with `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` **succeeds**: a configuration that only fails when kernels overlap is a race by construction. The logs show ranks entering `capture()` staggered by ~1 s. ### Why this has not been reported before The precondition is a **sharded** draft. The replicated draft of #51705 ran at `dcp=1`, so its captured graph contained no collective and there was nothing to race. That changed with **#55472** (merged 2026-09-08), which rebuilds the draft's `ParallelConfig` from the target's and therefore preserves `decode_context_parallel_size`, so a `--decode-context-parallel-size N` run with a DSpark draft now gets a draft at `dcp=N`. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Avoid NaN from empty seq_len in Triton MLA decode (CUDA graph pad)
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #57017 DeepSeek-V2-Lite with `--quantization fp8` on sm89 (`TRITON_MLA`) returns NaN logits for every request once three or more sequences share one CUDA-graph decode batch. Eager / `cudagraph_mode: NONE` are fine; `--max-num-seqs 2` sidesteps it. ### Root cause 1. Default CUDA-graph capture sizes are `[1, 2, 4, 8, ...]`, so a 3-sequence decode batch is padded to 4. Inactive pad slots get `seq_lens=0` (and `NULL_BLOCK_ID` in the block table). 2. `triton_decode_attention` stage2 always did `acc / e_sum`. For `seq_len=0`, stage1 writes nothing and `e_sum` stays 0, so the pad row becomes `0/0 = NaN`. 3. Online FP8 MoE (`Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod`) quantizes expert activations with a **per-tensor** dynamic scale (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. `amax` over the whole batch. One pad NaN makes the scale NaN and poisons every co-batched request. Dense Cutlass FP8 linears use per-token scales, so they would not amplify a pad NaN the same way; the MoE path is what turns a pad-slot NaN into batch-wide NaN logits. ## Softcap PR #56579 (Triton softcap overflow) is unrelated; DeepSeek MLA does not use `logits_soft_cap` on this backend. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py -k zero_seq_len_pad_no_nan -v ``` New test: batch of 3 active rows + 1 `seq_len=0` pad (MLA / GQA / MHA). title: [Core] Add --independent-data-parallel to run MoE DP ranks as independent replicas
summary: # [Core] Add `--independent-data-parallel` to run MoE DP ranks as independent replicas ## Purpose With `--data-parallel-size N`, a MoE model's DP ranks are never independent. Without `--enable-expert-parallel`, the expert layers are tensor-parallel across all `DP × TP` GPUs. With it, they are expert-parallel across the same GPUs. In both cases every MoE layer runs collectives across the DP ranks, and the ranks step in lockstep, with dummy forward passes on idle ranks. Dense models instead run each DP rank as an independent replica behind one endpoint. This PR adds that mode for MoE models. With `--independent-data-parallel`, each DP rank holds the full model, sharded only by its own TP size. Its expert layers never communicate with other ranks, and it schedules and steps on its own, exactly like a dense DP rank. This suits models that fit on one GPU or TP group. Co-located ranks still share one CPU-offloaded n-gram (PLE) table, as lockstep DP ranks do since #60390. Running separate engines instead would pin one table per GPU (48 GiB each for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). Motivating cases: - **Prefill-only workers in disaggregated serving.** Prefill is compute-bound, so the natural unit is one GPU per prefill worker. Each worker then runs as soon as it has a request, with no expert collectives and no waiting on other ranks. Today the choice is between lockstep DP, which couples the workers in every MoE layer, and separate single-GPU engines, which each pin their own PLE table. With this flag, `-dp N --independent-data-parallel` gives N independent 1-GPU prefill workers on a node that

title: [Feature]: EC events: publish encoder cache presence and eviction from the EC connector
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **Motivation** KV events let external components (routers, indexers, cache-aware orchestrators such as llm-d) track which KV blocks each instance holds and route requests accordingly. The EC connector has no equivalent. A router can't tell which instances already hold the encoder output for multimodal objects, so a repeated multimodal input is re-encoded or fetched again when it could have been routed to an instance that already has it. This matters most in E-PD disaggregation. **Proposal** Add EC events that mirror KV events in format, transport and configuration, keyed by `mm_hash` instead of block hash. title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Fix garbled outputs and streaming reasoning parser on NVFP4 MoE backends for SM 12.0a (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell)
summary: ## Summary This PR fixes three bugs in the MiniMax M3 tool parser and streaming reasoning parser on SM 12.0a (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) with NVFP4 MoE backends. **Fix 1 — Streaming reasoning tokens going to `content` instead of `reasoning`** `is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)` returned `True` at prompt evaluation time because the M3 system prompt contains `<mm:think></mm:think>` as instruction text at positions 84–85. The `end(85) > start(84)` check evaluated to `True` → `state.reasoning_ended = True` before generation began. Fix: tail-check — only return `True` if the end token appears within the last few positions of `input_ids`. **Fix 2 — Tool calls dropped on `max_tokens` truncation** `parser.finish()` raises `"incomplete MiniMax M3 tool call"` when generation is cut off before the closing tag. This was inside the same `try/except` as `parse_into`, so both failed together → `None` → raw XML leaked as content. Fix: split into two separate `try/except` blocks; `finish()` failure falls back to the partial parse from `parse_into`. **Fix 3 — Tool calls dropped when model omits `]<]minimax[>[` NS prefix on inner tags** The model intermittently generates `<invoke name="...">` or `</param>` without the namespace prefix. `parse_into` throws a blank `ValueError` on such output. Fix: `MinimaxM3ToolParser._parse_complete` override: on Rust failure, run `_normalise_ns()` to add missing prefixes to all tags inside the `tool_call` block, then retry once. **Fix 4 — Tool calls dropped when model omits closing param tag before `</invoke>`** Root cause identified via binary analysis + targ

title: [RFC]: Source Identity and Semantic Metadata for KV Cache Events
summary: ### Motivation. External KV-cache indexers and routers need to know which component produced an event, which storage resource it describes, and how its advertised cache units can be retrieved. vLLM currently combines local cache-manager and connector events into a common stream, but does not explicitly identify each event's logical producer. `MultiConnector` also combines events from its children. This creates two related interpretation problems. ### Storage medium does not determine sharing scope | Producer and configuration | Reported medium | Resource represented | | --- | --- | --- | | Native `OffloadingConnector`, primary CPU tier | `CPU` | The instance's local DRAM offload cache. | | Native `OffloadingConnector`, local filesystem tier | `STORAGE`, with `locality=LOCAL` when declared | Local filesystem storage used by the offloader. | | `MooncakeStoreConnector`, shared DRAM pool | `cpu` in the inspected implementation | DRAM in a shared KV pool, accessible to compatible instances connected to that pool. | The CPU cases correspond to `cpu_local` and `cpu_share` in Mooncake Conductor. A write reported by instance A may therefore describe cache that instance B can also access. Attributing every CPU event to A's local cache would misrepresent availability. Locality and sharing are independent: a shared pool can include memory on the publishing host. Conversely, `STORAGE` alone does not imply local disk; native filesystem and object-storage tiers both use it with configurable locality. The table describes the stated configurations; Mooncake's current `cpu` label does not id

title: [Model][Core] Share the PLE table between separate engine processes on one node
summary: ## Details **How it works.** Each ETP shard of each PLE layer is one file in `shared_host_table_dir`, named by a hash of its identity: model, revision, layer, shape, dtype, ETP rank, ETP size and vocabulary range. Equal-sized shards therefore never map each other's rows, and the identity is stamped into a `<file>.ready` mark that every reader checks. The loader holds an exclusive `flock` on `<file>.lock` from before it sizes the file until after it publishes `.ready` (from `process_weights_after_loading`). The kernel drops the lock when the process exits, so: - a file with no ready mark and no lock holder was left by a loader that died, and the next process to take the lock loads it again; exactly one can; - waiters probe the lock with `LOCK_SH`, which only an exclusive holder refuses, and fail at once with the reason when the loader is gone, rather than waiting out the hour-long timeout; - the file is never truncated below its size, so waiters that already mapped and registered its pages see the reload in place. Every process maps the file `MAP_SHARED` and registers it with `cudaHostRegister` for the unchanged UVA lookup (as `dp_shared_memory` does). Only the table is shared; NVFP4 block scales and the global scale stay per process. **Code.** `Qwen4ExpPLEFileSharedHostEmbedding` (a `Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding`) and its lock helpers in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ngram_embedding.py`; selection in `nvidia/ngram_embedding.py` only where the private pinned table would otherwise be used; the option and its validation in `vllm/config/engram.py`; docs in `docs/features/engr

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Engram: 128-row lookup tiles; split GPU tables across engines
summary: ## Overview Two Engram changes for DeepSeek-V4.1: 1. **128-row lookup tiles.** Large Engram lookups are latency bound on their reads. Once the rows fill the persistent grid with 128-row tiles, the lookup now uses them (with 8 warps) instead of 16-row tiles, so each program keeps 8x the reads in flight. Packed rows are copied 8 bytes per load instead of a byte, with both loads issued before the stores. Smaller lookups keep 16-row tiles. The rows read and written are unchanged. 2. **GPU tables split across engines.** Engines in one NVLink domain, such as the prefill engines of a disaggregated deployment, can now split each Engram GPU table's rows over all of their GPUs: ```bash --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false, "peer_group_size": 8, "peer_group_store": "/shared/job-dir/engram-peers"}' ``` Each GPU holds 1/`peer_group_size` of every table, and lookups read the other rows from their owner's HBM through the existing peer-read path (#62091), so no engine's step waits on another's. This frees the host memory of a CPU-offloaded copy per engine (188.8 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's two tables), e.g. for a host KV cache tier, without a whole table on any GPU. Related: #64609 (closed) used 128-row tiles for sorted host lookups only; this keys the tile size on the row count instead, which also covers unsorted lookups from THP host tables (`use_thp`) and HBM tables. #64082 (draft) shares *host* tables across independent instances through a persistent owner process with leases; this PR instead splits *GPU* tables peer to peer, with no extra process and no coordination after startup.

title: [UMBP][9/10] Add lazy GPU cache offloading
summary: This PR is split from the original full PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58568 Select reusable prefix blocks from the GPU free queue for optional lazy offload. Close full-attention prefix chains before a lazy store is submitted, and keep source blocks pinned until the transfer finishes. Scan the free queue only when its eviction end may have moved, plus a recheck once a second. Between rechecks, skip lookups for keys already confirmed resident and skip blocks whose keys and prefix chain are all confirmed. Return completed lazy blocks the scan found behind the empty blocks at the front of the free queue, in their original order, and free prefix blocks it pulled in from elsewhere normally. Report a rank the scheduler cannot reach as unavailable (`None`) instead of a miss, and back off failed lazy lookups and stores instead of retrying every step. Implementation only, apart from existing UMBP handle test assertions that expected `False` when the server could not be asked and now expect `None`. `lazy_offload` defaults to false, and the umbrella serving tables use that default. Lazy stores include blocks produced by decoding, so `save_decode_cache` does not apply with `lazy_offload`; the docs say so. Lazy offload tests are in the next PR (#61798). title: [RFC]: Async EPLB: one owner for all state, worker runs self-contained jobs
summary: ### Motivation. **One owner for all async EPLB state: the main thread. The worker thread only runs self-contained jobs.** Today the main thread and the async EPLB worker hand work to each other through seven pieces of shared mutable state. Fault recovery has to patch that state while the worker keeps running. In this proposal the worker thread runs one job per MoE layer. A job takes all its inputs as arguments and returns a result or raises. The main thread keeps each cycle as a plain list of layers still to do, and takes the next one once every EP rank has finished the same job. The goal is to simplify the hand-off and change as little observable behaviour as possible. Every chart below compares main with the proposal. "Main" here means main plus the fix for the fault-tolerance silent stall (#66144, PR #66146). The few visible differences are listed in "Visible changes". - Draft PR: #67020. title: [RFC]: KV Trace monitoring
summary: ## Summary **KV Trace monitoring** connects request scheduling, KV-block lifetimes, and model-runner address plans. A developer should be able to start with a request or block and inspect its history across these boundaries. > **Status:** Seeking agreement on the problem and first implementation scope. No upstream acceptance is recorded yet. > **Reference implementation:** My [vllm-ascend PR #17833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17833), head `a0d8bef0b2ef`. Evidence and CI status below were checked on **2026-11-11**. ## 1. Problem and evidence ### The missing debugging view An allocated block can still be the wrong token destination. For example, A and B own blocks 1 and 2, but their write slots are swapped. Allocation logs alone cannot identify the mismatch. This is an illustrative failure, not measured production incidence. Diagnosing such behavior requires connecting three views: - **Request history:** scheduled ranges, block bindings, preemption/resume, and completion. - **Block history:** allocation, reference changes, sharing, and reuse across allocation generations. - **Execution plan:** request/row order, block tables, slot mappings, and read lengths. Repeated text alone does not prove a KV fault; conclusions need trace evidence, with missing observations identified. ### Evidence available today The linked PR's [guide at the referenced commit](https://github.com/Tjh-UKN/vllm-ascend/blob/a0d8bef0b2efb7ed9da31ba683671e462e8e3080/docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_guard.md) documents scheduler-to-metadata checks and their supported paths.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix Qwen3-VL EVS M-RoPE positions for the outer vision marker and chunked prefill
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #62937 and #62969. #62975 is folded into this PR, as requested in review. After a short prefix this crashed EngineCore on the first prefill step. title: [Rust][Benchmark] Align vllm-bench result files and requests with Python
summary: ## Overview Align the Rust `vllm-bench` result files and request payloads with Python `vllm bench serve`, and stop sweeps and `--num-runs` from dropping or overwriting results. These are the remaining parity gaps that no open PR covers. title: [Transformers backend] Fuse the GLU activation with the down projection's input quant
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Let the Transformers modeling backend fuse a GLU activation with its down projection's input quantization, as native Llama does with `maybe_fused_act_quant`. This closes the NVFP4 throughput gap listed in #66547 (serving Llama with the backend). ## Claims - The GLU fuser rewrites `down(act(gate_up(x)))` to `down(act(gate_up(x), down))` when the activation feeds the down projection directly, and wraps the activation in `ActAndMulQuant`, which calls `maybe_fused_act_quant(act, x, down)`. For HF's `LlamaMLP`: ```python down_proj = self.down_proj(self.act_fn(self.gate_up_proj(x), self.down_proj)) ``` - NVFP4 Llama on the backend uses the fused SiLU-and-mul + NVFP4 quant kernel, and its throughput matches native (it was 1.8% slower). - No change without a fused kernel: `maybe_fused_act_quant` falls back to the plain activation. ## Validation B200, `RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4`, 1024 in / 256 out, 1000 prompts, mean of 4 runs (2 GPUs × 2 rounds, alternating): | | req/s | vs native | |---|---|---| | Native | 74.44 | | | Backend, `main` | 73.10 | -1.8% | | Backend, this PR | 74.85 | +0.6% | Prompt logprobs over 1577 tokens: mean NLL native 2.1295, backend `main` 2.1301, this PR 2.1268; mean |Δlogprob| vs native is 0.2011 for backend `main` and 0.2046 for this PR, so the fused path is as close to native as the unfused one. GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy): native 0.689, backend `main` 0.688, this PR 0.673. Given the matching logprobs, I read the GSM8K gap as greedy paths diverging under NVFP4 rather than a numerical regression

summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch On the Rust frontend, gRPC encoder/PD serving still reprocesses multimodal inputs. HTTP EPD already skips that second pass. The Rust frontend and its inference proto do not carry the fields the HTTP path uses, and two media flags the Python server accepts are still rejected. What HTTP already sends, and gRPC needs to carry the same way: - The encoder's expanded placeholder ranges: modality, content hash, offset, length, which positions take embeddings, and the encoder-cache identifier. Today a gRPC encoder reply has the expanded ids and no ranges. - The placeholder metadata JSON that an HTTP `image_embeds` / `video_embeds` / `audio_embeds` body already carries. That is the grid (`image_grid_thw`, `video_grid_thw`), video timestamps, audio feature lengths, and token counts. It is not the pixel tensors. When the encoder-cache handle names the embedding, the MessagePack kwargs blob can be omitted. A caller-supplied embed still needs a place for its `.npy` tensors. - The per-item options on an OpenAI content part: image `detail` (`auto` / `low` / `high`), video `fps`, and `max_long_side_pixel`. A raw item mixed with already-featured items also needs the prompt offset of its single placeholder marker, so PD expands that item in place. - Request-level `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs.video.num_frames`. title: [draft][XPU]add kernel nightly pipeline
summary: # Intel XPU Kernel Nightly This workflow builds a wheel from the vLLM XPU kernel repository, uses it to build a vLLM XPU test image, and runs the Intel XPU tests with that image. It is intended for nightly or manually triggered integration testing. It does not publish the wheel to PyPI or public storage. ## Workflow When enabled, the pipeline: 1. Checks out the configured kernel repository and ref (by default, `main`). 2. Builds the kernel wheel in the builder image specified by the kernel repository's `wheel-per-commit.yaml` workflow. 3. Uploads the wheel, checksum, and build information as Buildkite artifacts. 4. Builds the regular vLLM XPU image, installs the wheel into it, and commits the result as a uniquely tagged image. 5. Runs the Intel XPU tests with the image produced by the image-build step. The wheel artifact is stored by Buildkite. Its availability and retention depend on the Buildkite artifact settings; it is not a public wheel download URL. ## Enable the workflow Set these variables in the Buildkite pipeline environment: ```yaml env: VLLM_XPU_KERNEL_NIGHTLY: "1" RUN_ALL: "1" NIGHTLY: "1" MAX_JOBS: "8" ``` `VLLM_XPU_KERNEL_NIGHTLY` must be set to `1` for both the XPU image-build job and Intel test jobs. `RUN_ALL` and `NIGHTLY` are used by the pipeline generator to select the full nightly test suite. If the pipeline is generated in a bootstrap step, make sure these variables are also present in the generated pipeline; variables exported only in the bootstrap shell do not automatically carry over to other Buildkite jobs. The image-build job needs Docker with Bui

title: [EPD] Metadata-only image and video inputs for GLM-5.3-Flash

The encoder publishes `image_grid_thw`, and for video `video_grid_thw` plus one timestamp per temporal patch. title: [Bugfix][Step5] Fix FP32 residual truncation at pipeline boundaries
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fix silent FP32-to-BF16 rounding at Step5 pipeline boundaries by allocating the NVIDIA implementation's intermediate buffer in FP32 when `fp32_residual_connection` is enabled. Add a one-time MRV2 check of the tensors each non-first PP stage receives against its persistent receive buffers. ## Claims - In the tested Step5 PP2 configuration, prompt logprobs match PP1 exactly at all 418 scored positions, and greedy outputs match on all 53 prompts, up from 10 before the fix. - MRV2 no longer copies mismatched PP tensors silently. A missing tensor or a different per-token shape fails on the first step; a received tensor without a buffer, or a buffer with lower precision or range, is logged with the tensor's name. - PP communication volume is unchanged. The FP32 buffer adds 128 MiB per non-first-stage worker at 16,384 batched tokens and hidden size 4,096. ## Validation **Setup:** `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview`, B300, TP4 + EP + MegaMoE with sequence parallelism, MRV2. Compared PP2 before and after the fix against PP1. **Prompt logprobs:** six fixed prompts via `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0`, covering 418 scored positions. | Configuration | Mean absolute logprob difference from PP1 | Maximum absolute difference | |---|---:|---:| | PP1, repeat run | 0 | 0 | | PP2, main | 0.036 | 1.59 | | PP2, this PR | 0 | 0 | **Greedy outputs:** 53 sequential requests comprising 48 GSM8K questions and five long prompts of 2K–25K tokens, generating up to 256 tokens each. | Configuration | Outputs identical to PP1 | |---|---:| | PP1, repeat run | 53

title: [Core][Scheduler] Bound the context a prefill step attends over
summary: ## Overview Adds `--max-num-batched-context-tokens`, an opt-in bound on the context that one step's prefill chunks attend over. Each chunk counts its request's already-computed tokens plus the tokens it prefills, summed over the step. `max_num_batched_tokens` bounds only the new tokens, so it does not bound the step time of long-context prefill. ## Claims - New `SchedulerConfig.max_num_batched_context_tokens` (default `None`: no change in behavior). - When set, a prefill chunk that does not fit is shortened, or left for a later step. The step's first prefill chunk is always scheduled, so every prefill keeps making progress. Decode tokens do not count. - This bounds the cost of a prefill step when several chunks deep into long prompts land in it. With data-parallel MoE, it also bounds how long the other ranks wait for that step. ## Validation - New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: - chunks deep into long prompts are shortened, then deferred, while the first chunk of each step still runs; - decodes do not use the budget. - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` (CPU, offline): 272 passed on this branch and 270 on main, the difference being the 2 new tests. The same 81 tests fail on both, because their Hugging Face models are not cached on the test node. - `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. - End-to-end benchmark: **pending**. The plan is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill instances (DEP4, B200) under the AgentX trace, comparing step-time distribution and TTFT p50/p99 with and without the bound. Results will be added here before

title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Detect shared-prefix junctions in the MooncakeStore lookup
summary: ## Overview Stacked on #62278; review only the last commit. The MooncakeStore lookup now detects shared-prefix junctions, and the store keeps the SWA tails at those junctions under sparse retention. Without this, a fresh instance (or one that evicted the prefix locally) gets 0 hits from the store for siblings that share a prefix, because store retention keeps only each request's own replay tails. ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP + MooncakeStore, local prefix cache reset before every request: siblings get 3584 / 3840 hit tokens from the store (d = 8 / 160 past an aligned 3840-token prefix). On main they get 0 in both cases. - Shared-prefix GSM8K (200 questions, local cache reset before each): 194 questions hit 3584 tokens and 4 hit 3840 from the store, with accuracy 0.975. On main every question gets 0 hits, with accuracy 0.97. - No dense SWA retention in the store: the store keeps only the tails at junction positions, in addition to the existing replay tails. ## Validation **End to end** (GB200, 4 GPUs, base 83c9a547bf): the same serve command as #62278, plus `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}'`. Before every request after the first, the client calls `/reset_prefix_cache`, so all hits come from the store. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | junction probe C, D (d = 8) | 0, 0 | 3584, 3584 | | junction probe C, D (d = 160) | 0, 0 | 3840, 3840 | | A replayed (own prompt, store sanity) | 4864 / 5120 | 4864 / 5120 | | GSM8K accuracy (200) | 0.97 | 0.975 | | GSM8K store hit rate (`external_prefix_cache_hits / queries`) | 0% |

title: [KVConnector][Core] Add MultiConnector opt-in to only load from first matching connector
summary: ## Overview `MultiConnector.get_num_new_matched_tokens` queries every sub-connector even after one reports a hit, although only the first matching connector is ever used to load. This PR adds an opt-in `quick_load_from_first_only` flag to stop the lookup at the first hit. ## Claims - New `quick_load_from_first_only` key in MultiConnector's `kv_connector_extra_config` (default `False`, so behaviour is unchanged). - When enabled, connectors after the first hit are not looked up for that request. E.g. NixlConnector + MooncakeStoreConnector on a P/D decoder no longer pays for a store lookup when NIXL already has the KV cache. - Connectors that were not chosen still receive `update_state_after_alloc(request, blocks, 0)`, as before (#18632). ```json {"kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "quick_load_from_first_only": true, "connectors": [{"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both"}, {"kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both"}]}} ``` ## Validation New unit test `test_quick_load_from_first_only` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py`, covering flag on/off × first connector hit/miss. It checks the returned tokens, the chosen connector, whether the second connector is looked up, and the `update_state_after_alloc` calls. ## Details The loop over all connectors was introduced in #18632. Short-circuiting unconditionally is not safe, because some connectors rely on their `get_num_new_matched_tokens` call: - `LMCacheMPConnector` only creates its per-request tracker there and asserts on it later (AssertionError). title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Drop a DeepSeek DSML tool-call opener cut after its DSML token
summary:
<!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Follow-up to #65375. Since #65375, a DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1 output that ends inside a DSML tool-call block is dropped at finish instead of being returned as `content`. An output that ends inside the tool-call opener, after its `｜DSML｜` token, still leaks: a V4.1 output `Checking.

<｜DSML｜ calls` (cut before `>`) returns `content: "Checking.

<｜DSML｜ calls"`. This PR reports that tail as `IncompleteToolCall` too, so `UnifiedParserState::finish` drops it like any other unfinished tool call. This PR is now rebased onto #65375 and reduced to that one case. Its earlier revision added its own `IncompleteToolCall` and dropped the buffer only at `max_tokens`; #65375 does that in general (every parser family, every finish reason), so that part is gone, and the title and description are rewritten. ## Claims - An output that ends inside a DSML opener after its `｜DSML｜` token (` calls>` for V4.1, `tool_calls>` for V4, `function_calls>` for V3.2) no longer returns the half-written opener as `content`. The text before it is kept (the `

` that frames the opener is dropped with it, as it is for a complete tool call). As in #65375, this holds for every finish reason. It is the rule the Python parser engine pins for a cut inside a tool-call opener (`TestTruncatedToolOpenerStreamParity`, with `qwen3_coder`); I did not check the Python DeepSeek parser for this case. - Trailing text is still returned as text: a partial `<｜DS` spelling, an opener spelled with ordinary tokens, and a held-back tail without `<｜`. - Code change: `deepseek_dsml/mod.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Treat a shared-prefix junction as a set of positions under EAGLE
summary: ## Overview Fixes the shared-prefix junction under per-group EAGLE flags (#61455): with a dropping EAGLE group in the lookup, siblings that share a prefix get 0 prefix-cache hits under sparse retention (default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`). The junction becomes a set of positions, `{J - A, J}`, computed in one place (`junction_boundaries()`) and used by every junction consumer. This is an alternative to #62206, which keeps an extra SWA tail at `J - block_size` inside the SWA mask only. The MooncakeStore side (store lookup as a junction source, `store_mask` as a consumer) is a follow-up PR stacked on this one: #62400. ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (retention 0): siblings that diverge 8 tokens past an aligned shared prefix of 3840 tokens get 0 hit tokens on main and 3584 with this PR. Siblings that diverge 160 tokens past it get 3840 on both. - Shared-prefix GSM8K (1319 questions): the prefix-cache hit rate goes from 4.7% to 82.1%, and accuracy does not change (0.943 → 0.945). - One helper produces the junction; all consumers read it: SWA and Mamba retention masks, the Mamba junction checkpoint, the scheduler's chunk stops (one per position) and `OffloadingConnector`. - No behavior change without EAGLE, or when no dropping (non-Mamba) EAGLE group takes part in the lookup. ## Validation **End to end** (GB200, 4 GPUs, base 83c9a547bf): ``` vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \ --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}
