title: [Core][Mamba] Keep align-mode Mamba state in fixed block-table slots on MRV2
summary: ## Overview In Mamba "align" prefix caching, a block-table column is two things at once: column `p` holds the state after `(p + 1) * block_size` tokens, and it is the physical slot a kernel reads or writes. A prefill over `[s, e)` can only use columns `(s - 1) // B` to `(e - 1) // B`, yet it needs a fixed set of slots: initial state, running state, internal checkpoint, speculative-decode slots. A prefill spanning fewer than about two Mamba blocks does not get enough columns, and the roles collide: | Columns | Result | Current workaround | | --- | --- | --- | | checkpoint column = initial-state column (a shared hit block) | no internal checkpoint | split at the block boundary and at the prompt tail: 3 forward steps | | checkpoint column < initial-state column | no internal checkpoint | split at the prompt tail: 2 steps | | prompt within one block (`checkpoint column < 0`) | no internal checkpoint | 2 steps | | running column = hit column | the running state would overwrite a shared block | copy-on-write on partial hits | | a chunk starting mid-block crosses the boundary | the slot holds the initial state but would be published under the full-block hash | block-aligned split / publish masks | With `--prefix-match-unit` below the Mamba block size, this is the common case for multi-turn chat: every turn hits inside a block and appends a few hundred tokens. This PR gives Model Runner V2 a layout where these collisions cannot happen: **fixed state slots**. A request's Mamba row is `[running, spec_1..spec_n, checkpoint, boundary]` for its whole lifetime, the same running/speculati

title: [Feature] Switch EP groups between prefill and decode
summary: Related to #56133 and #43807. Adds opt-in switching of a running EP group between prefill and decode. The router stops new assignments; vLLM drains accepted work and retained KV, commits the role on every core, then publishes readiness at the next epoch. Workers, weights, communicators, and CUDA graphs stay resident while other groups keep serving. The initial scope is NIXL pull transfer, one Python frontend, and internal DP load balancing. EP membership and the communication backend remain fixed. ## Tests - Revision `bd4f411812`: `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_pd_role.py tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_pd_role.py tests/entrypoints/common/test_cli_args.py -q` — **91 passed** on CPU after merging current main. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed. - Historical GPU prototype, before the current main merge: **6× H100 80GB**, three EP2 groups, OLMoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and Qwen3-30B-A3B. All 60 switches and 3,060 requests passed with matching reference outputs and unchanged process, graph, and communication identities. Held-KV timeout recovery and stale-epoch rejection passed. This GPU scenario was not rerun on the current revision. [Validation and commands](https://github.com/Etelis/vllm/blob/ff89426a0d23b0d5509e50d0bfa69a36d0174459/VALIDATION.md) distinguish the historical control checks from the GPU build, which includes a separate unmerged Triton MoE fix. EP16 and multi-node operation remain untested.

title: [KV Connector][Offloading] Certify per-token-head KV quant in the canonical layout
summary: Stacked on #51690. The packed per-token-head form pads each (token, head) row so its fp32 scale sits inline, making rows self-contained shard-portable units. Size regions against `unpadded_page_size_bytes`, which covers the scale carve and matches the worker's offload refs; split forms cannot carry scales per row and keep falling to the opaque fallback. Unlocks TP-agnostic offload for per-token-head KV cache dtypes (`int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`, `int4_per_token_head`) on GQA models. ## Test plan `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py` (no GPU): padded-row certification, tiling across ranks, gate coverage. E2E on 2x H200: Qwen3-4B-FP8 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_per_token_head` tp2 and canonical_layout: all layers certified portable, CPU load bytes equal store bytes.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix DeepSeek/GLM PP inputs for DFlash2
summary: ## Overview Fix DFlash2 pipeline-parallel startup and auxiliary inputs for generic DeepSeek-V2/V3 targets and the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 backbone used by GLM-5. title: [Model][DSV4.1] Support MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables
summary: ## Overview Support DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints with MXFP4 Engram tables: two E2M1 values per byte with UE8M0 block-32 scales. Checkpoint metadata selects the layout; existing FP8 checkpoints retain their default format. ## Claims - Packed Engram tables load through GPU, peer-HBM, pinned host, huge-page, and DP-shared storage paths. Allocation and host-memory eligibility use the actual packed row width. - MXFP4 reduces table storage from 264 to 136 bytes per 256-element row, including scales (48.5% less). - Unsupported checkpoint block sizes, scale formats, and partial layer lists fail before table allocation. Existing workers now cover both formats, including peer and non-peer GPU reads, host offload, cuMem success/fallback, sharding, loading, and graph replay. - Targeted reversions demonstrate failures without metadata validation, packed meta allocation, the packed-output guard, and packed shared-memory sizing. - Matched GSM8K: FP8 95.91%,

title: [Bugfix] Fix ExllamaLinearKernel wrong output for group sizes such as 16 and 96

title: [Perf][Core] Reserve step budget for waiting requests with cached KV
summary: ## Overview A chunked prefill that is already on the running list spends the whole per-step token budget on every step, so the waiting loop only runs once that prefill finishes. A queued request whose KV is already cached (prefix cache or a KV connector's async load) needs only the tokens the cache did not serve, yet it waits for the entire prefill. This reserves the budget the waiting queue needs to be admitted, and lets the running loop use only the remainder. Found while investigating LMCache/LMCache#5440; the fix is independent of LMCache: any chunked prefill on the running list starves the waiting queue, so plain prefix caching is affected as well. ## Claims - A queued cache-hit request is admitted mid-prefill instead of after it: on 1x A100-PCIE with Qwen3-14B + LMCache MP, 4 requests whose 39,497-token prefix is resident plus 4 cold 14,465-token requests, the hit requests' TTFT drops 13.95 s -> 5.00 s (-64%). - Group wall is unchanged: 14.769 s -> 14.813 s (+0.3%, same run). The budget comes out of the running prefill's step, and every queued request is capped at one fair share so the running batch keeps its own share. - No new configuration, env var or default. The scheduler change is 52 added lines (+52/-6), plus 99 lines of unit tests. ## Validation Hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100-PCIE-80GB (SM80), vLLM 0.32.0 container, Qwen3-14B, LMCache 0.5.6 MP connector (engine_driven, SHM), `max_num_seqs=8`, `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`. title: [Feature]: [KV Connector] Configure Mooncake Mamba snapshot write intervals
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch For Kimi-K3.1-Pro and other hybrid models, Mooncake Store writes the exact Mamba boundary states handed off by core. Frequent handoffs can produce many large state writes. GPU prefix-cache retention does not independently control these writes. Add an opt-in Store write interval in scheduler blocks, with optional retention of the prompt's reusable checkpoint. For 16-token blocks and handoffs at 16, 32, …, 128, interval 4 selects states at 64 and 128. This selects available states; it does not create missing checkpoints. Default interval 1 preserves current writes. ### Alternatives #46906 separates Store and GPU retention; #65917 deletes superseded prompt-end states. This proposal filters Mamba states before writing them. Unlike the broader checkpoint-generation/backfill proposal in #53041, it only selects exact states already handed off by core. ### Additional context CPU validation on main `595b1514e837`: 35 new cases passed; all Mooncake Store suites: 607 passed, 5 existing skips. Tests cover complete multi-shard bytes, irregular boundaries, prompt/lookahead alignment, Store failures and request-ID reuse. Only the external Store is mocked; CUDA initialization is prohibited. Sparser external states can reduce cache hits and increase recomputation. Real Store/RDMA, GPU state lifetime, model accuracy and serving performance are not yet validated; no speedup is claimed. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and PRs and consulted the vLLM documentation assistant through its public MCP search interface.

title: [RFC]: Faster Engram / PLE `disk_offload`: io_uring + O_DIRECT row reader and read/compute overlap
summary: ### Motivation. `EngramConfig.disk_offload` keeps the n-gram tables on storage instead of GPU or host memory: - Qwen4Exp PLE: merged in #59958. - DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram: open in #62238. Both read paths go through the page cache and run synchronously before the forward: - #59958 does `WILLNEED` + one `preadv` per row from Python, with a stream sync before staging. - #62238 gathers rows through an mmap. That is fine at low concurrency. It becomes the bottleneck once prompts get long or several requests prefill at once: - A 32K-token prefill touches millions of random rows of 160–264 B. - The page cache turns each of those rows into a 4 KiB+ read. - The GPU waits for every one of them. The review of #59958 pointed in the same direction (bypassing the page cache with `O_DIRECT`, prompt-side prefetch, removing the per-step sync), and its own future-work list asks for batched reads. We measured upstream `disk_offload` against two of our changes on the same nightly and the same checkpoint (Qwen PLE, 9-cell grid, median of 3 runs): - **PR 1 alone**, which replaces only the row read of #59958 with a batched `O_DIRECT` io_uring reader: - TTFT is **1.65–2.15× lower** than upstream `disk_offload`. - Decode at concurrency 16 is 6–53% higher. - The page cache stays empty. Upstream fills it with 47.5 GiB, almost the whole table. - **With read/compute overlap (PR 2) and the small follow-ups on top:** - TTFT is 1.02–1.71× that of `cpu_offload` (pinned host memory). Upstream `disk_offload` is 2.7–3.4×. - Decode is 85–89% of `cpu_offload`. Upstream is 43–93%, and 43–74% at concurrency 16. This

summary: On gfx950 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `CudaCommunicator` builds no vLLM `CustomAllreduce`, so AITER's custom all-reduce serves every TP all-reduce, including sizes where AITER's one-stage kernel is slower than vLLM's. title: [Quantization] Route batch-invariant GPTQ linear through Humming when selection picks it
summary: ## Summary Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `AutoGPTQLinearMethod` ignores kernel selection entirely and runs `gptq_linear_batch_invariant`: it unpacks and rescales the full `[K, N]` weight **on every forward call**, then calls the Triton persistent matmul. This addresses the batch-invariance item of the coverage-gap checklist in #65560 (Replace Marlin with Humming). This PR makes batch-invariant mode follow the normal kernel selection when it resolves to `HummingLinearKernel` — the one mixed-precision WNA16 kernel that honors `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` itself (its compute config forwards the flag) — for **4-bit weights only**; W8A16 stays on the fallback until its Humming-side correctness is validated. Any other selection (Machete, Marlin, ...) keeps the dequant fallback, since those kernels pick their tiling from the token count. No Humming-side change, no new flags, no behavior change with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` unset. For 4-bit GPTQ on SM90, selection resolves to Humming today for shapes Machete rejects (`N % 128 != 0`, `group_size=32`, ...) — no env tweaks needed — and everywhere once #63265 (open) prefers Humming over Machete; until then `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=MacheteLinearKernel` selects it explicitly. NVFP4 W4A16 already routes batch-invariant mode to Humming (`init_nvfp4_linear_kernel`); this gives INT4 the same behavior by following the oracle instead of forcing a kernel. ## How to try it ```bash # SM90, any sym GPTQ-Int4 model (g128); Machete disabled as in #63265's # A/B recipe (not needed on Machete-rejected shapes, or after #63265): VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_DISA

title: [Frontend] Support cross-machine snapshot (step 1: portable attachments)
summary: # Purpose This PR extends the snapshot feature ([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51360](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51360)) from inplace checkpoint/restore to cross-machine checkpoint/restore. The goal is fast startup for auto-scaling scenarios. ## WHAT Making snapshots work across machines requires solving at least the following problems: * Package all intermediate files generated during vllm startup, such as the triton jit cache. Some of these files are currently open/mapped by vllm; others may be used later. They must be carried over to the new machine, so the process can still find them after restore. * Support cuda device map. GPU device uuids change on the new container, so we need to tell cuda-checkpoint how the old uuids map to the new ones. * Handle ip changes. The new container gets a different ip. Any TCP connections recorded in the snapshot must be re-established on the new ip, and any connections vllm makes afterwards must use the new ip as well. * Avoid pid conflicts. In the new container, running the vllm snapshot restore cli imports libraries such as cuBLAS, which can start threads before criu restore runs. Those threads may occupy pids that criu restore needs. Nothing currently prevents this conflict; a solution is needed, for example setting `kernel.ns_last_pid`. This PR is the first step: it packages the intermediate files so they can travel with the snapshot, and introduces the following: 1. A new `--portable` flag. It marks the snapshot as portable, i.e. for cross-machine use. Making this explicit keeps inplace checkpoint/restore

title: [ROCm][Perf] Pick the GDN chunk-state V tile from the batch, not the first autotune
summary: On ROCm, the Triton GDN and KDA prefill runs the chunk-state kernel `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` with the V tile and launch config that the 64-token profile warmup (#36599) autotuned, because the autotune key `["H", "K", "V", "BT"]` has no batch dimension. This PR sizes the tile from the batch and the CU count at every launch and gives each tile a fixed launch config, so small prefill batches fill the GPU. CUDA is unchanged. The kernel is sequential over chunks, so its grid `(cdiv(V, BV), N * H)` is all its parallelism. On MI355X the warmup leaves `BV = 64` on some models, `BV = 32` on others; at `BV = 64` a single-sequence prefill with `H = 32` launches 64 programs on 256 CUs. `BV` is now the widest power-of-two tile whose grid still covers the CUs, clamped to `[16, 64]`, with a fixed `(num_warps, num_stages)`: `16: (4, 3)`, `32: (2, 3)`, `64: (4, 2)`, inside the space `main` autotunes on ROCm. Fixed, since the warmup's one chunk cannot rank them and tuning a new tile mid-serving stalls that step. title: [Bugfix][XPU] Keep MoE expert weights offloaded during weight post-processing
summary: **Description** When serving a CPU-offloaded MoE model on Intel XPU (e.g. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with --cpu-offload-gb), the server OOMs at load time — during process_weights_after_loading, before KV-cache profiling. **Root cause.** UVAOffloader offloads expert weights as UVA views: they report device=xpu but their storage lives in host RAM, and the parameter is stamped _vllm_is_uva_offloaded=True. The XPU branch of UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading then runs: ``` w13.data = w13.transpose(-1, -2).contiguous() w2.data = w2.transpose(-1, -2).contiguous() ``` .contiguous() on a UVA view materializes a real on-device copy, silently de-offloading every expert. For a large MoE the per-layer stacked expert tensors are big enough that this transient device allocation exhausts the card and OOMs. **Fix.** For offloaded weights, transpose on the host and rebuild the UVA view so the weight stays off-device; resident (non-offloaded) weights keep the original device path and are numerically unchanged. Because _setup_kernel → replace_parameter registers a fresh Parameter and drops the old one's Python attributes, the _vllm_is_uva_offloaded marker is re-asserted afterward so a later reload (e.g. RL weight update) still takes the host-transpose path. This also lets the existing device_loading_context re-offload safety net skip a redundant copy. The change is scoped strictly to UnquantizedMoeBackend.XPU: - Non-XPU platforms never enter the branch (the import is inside it too). - Non-offloaded XPU MoE takes the else branch, byte-identical to the previous code. - Numerically i

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Generalize cache registration and payload layouts
summary: ## Overview Generalize MooncakeStore's rank-local cache registration to describe logical tensor components instead of relying on their allocation layout. Skip empty components and remove covered aliases without copying neighboring components or padding. - Preserve component order and coalesce adjacent regions only when their strides and registered storage bounds match and the combined span fits within a block stride. - Use one registration path for device and host-resident groups, register each backing storage once, and stop startup if registration fails. - Use `torch.Event` and extensible configuration/setup methods; support documented environment overrides for the Store master and segment size. Neither gathers the index keys across DCP ranks. ## Claims With DCP > 1 on ROCm, the base indexer prefill in #65685 scores each rank's key shard and merges the per-rank top-k candidates. This PR adds: - **Global-key prefill** (`VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_GLOBAL_KEY_PREFILL`, default 1): all-gather every rank's FP8 index keys once per prefill chunk (`gather_global_indexer_keys`) and take the top-k over the whole context, so no candidate merge is needed. - **Row-sharded scoring** (`VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_ROWSHARD_PREFILL`, default 1): each rank scores 1/dcp of the chunk's query rows, and the selections are all-gathered once per layer. They are only built on ROCm with DCP > 1 and no PCP. - `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_PAD_KEY_GATHER` (default 0) pads the key all-gather to a 16-byte multiple for the AITER IP

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix extract_hidden_states to use last valid token for multi-token outputs
summary: The `ExtractHiddenStatesProposer.prepare_next_token_ids_padded()` method incorrectly read only the first column of `sampled_token_ids` when determining the next token to use for continuation. During speculative decoding with `num_speculative_tokens >= 1`, the sampled token tensor can have shape `[batch_size, num_speculative_tokens + 1]`, containing multiple valid tokens per row. The old implementation always used column 0, causing it to report different progress and a different continuation token from what was actually committed to the output. This manifested as reproducible duplicated digits and punctuation in generated answers. The fix replaces the simple column-0 slicing with the same `eagle_prepare_next_token_padded_kernel` used by EAGLE proposer. This kernel correctly iterates through all columns, counts valid tokens, and extracts the last valid token in each row. For a row `[15, 18]` with both tokens valid, the corrected method now reports `valid_count=2, next_token_id=18` instead of the incorrect `valid_count=1, next_token_id=15`. A regression test `test_prepare_next_token_ids_padded_multi_token` has been added to verify correct behavior with multi-token outputs, including cases with mixed valid/invalid tokens and discarded requests. Fixes #56417

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Optimize draft_token_ids assembly in NgramProposer from O(N^2) to O(N)
summary: ## Purpose In `NgramProposer.batch_propose()`, `valid_ngram_requests` is a `list[int]`. The previous implementation iterated through `range(num_requests)` and performed `if i in valid_ngram_requests`, which executes an $O(N)$ linear scan for each request index in pure Python. For large batch sizes (e.g., $N=512$), this executes up to $O(N^2)$ (~130,000) membership comparisons during every drafting step. This PR optimizes the result assembly to $O(N)$ by: 1. Pre-allocating `draft_token_ids = [[] for _ in range(num_requests)]`. 2. Iterating directly through `valid_ngram_requests` and populating `draft_token_ids[i]` by index. Thread capping logic is left unchanged. ## Duplicate Work Check Checked open issues and PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `ngram_proposer` and `valid_ngram_requests`; no duplicate PRs or issues exist. ## Test Plan Ran unit tests for N-gram speculative decoding: ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram.py -v ``` ## Test Result ```text ============================= test session starts ============================== platform darwin -- Python 3.12.14, pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.6.0 collected 2 items tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram.py::test_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens PASSED [ 50%] tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram.py::test_ngram_proposer PASSED [100%] ======================== 2 passed, 6 warnings in 2.80s ========================= ``` All `ruff check` and `ruff format` checks pass cleanly. ## Attribution AI assistance was used to analyze complexity and prepare the patch.

title: [RFC]: Tree speculative decoding in vLLM
summary: ### Motivation. Recent work has made tree-based drafting a major direction in speculative decoding. By proposing multiple continuations per step, a draft tree can increase the number of tokens accepted in one target verification pass. [PCTree](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02123), [DARTree](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13524), [PRESTO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22634) This RFC builds on [vLLM RFC #65813](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65813) and details how vLLM schedules, verifies, and commits draft trees, drawing on the Ascend prototype. [vLLM-Ascend RFC #18797](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18797) ### Proposed Change. ### Execution flow | Stage | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | Propose | Produce a bounded tree of candidate continuations. Publish flattened candidate token IDs and retain their topology with the matching worker request state. | | Schedule and prepare inputs | Account for the candidate rows and their KV slots. When trimming a tree to fit, retain an ancestor-closed subset. Keep the flat candidates and topology associated with the same request and draft step. | | Verify | Assign position IDs by depth and distinct temporary KV slots by node. Each query can attend to the committed prefix and its own path through the tree, including itself. | | Select a path | Starting from the root, match each token selected by the target to a child. Stop at a missing match or a leaf and emit the target token, subject to normal stop and length handling. | | Commit | Keep the root and commit the accepted nodes in path order. title: [Multimodal] Add keyframe-aware sampling to PyNvVideoCodec backend
summary: # [MM] Add keyframe-aware video sampling to PyNvVideoCodec ## Overview Uniform video sampling picks frame positions without regard to the stream's GOP structure, so reaching most sampled frames means decoding the intermediate frames back to the previous keyframe. On long videos, that decode work is significant. The primary win of this change is a 34% reduction in video decode time across all 900 VideoMME videos, and 56% on long videos. This PR adds a `keyframe_sampling="nearest"` option to the PyNvVideoCodec video backend. It moves the frame positions chosen by the existing loader to nearby keyframes, which decode without walking their GOP: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \ --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"backend": "pynvvideocodec", "keyframe_sampling": "nearest"}}' ``` ## Claims - **Decode time, VideoMME:** −34% across all 900 videos; −36% on N150, and −56% on its long videos. - **Serving, VideoMME N150 at 8 concurrent requests:** mean TTFT −60%, API-server CPU time per request −49%, request rate +58%. - **Accuracy is unchanged:** VideoMME N150 +0.23 pp [−2.13, +2.70]; Perception Test −0.31 pp [−1.04, +0.43]. - **Same frame count:** every video gets the requested number of frames. A video with fewer keyframes than samples keeps its uniform frames. - **Off by default:** with the option unset, nothing changes. Other video backends reject the option. ## Validation Unit tests, in `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` (PyNvVideoCodec 2.0.4): ```bash python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py ``` The new tests check that:

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
summary: This carries #56831 by @CedricHwong forward to current main. That PR has been idle since 09-14 and no longer passes CI after the rebase. Cedric's commit is kept unchanged, with his authorship. The two commits on top address the review comments on that PR. Adaptive verification (DSpark) picks the per-step draft budget on the host from rank-local stale confidences, then picks which slots to keep on the device from rank-local live confidences. If TP ranks disagree on either one, they run different batch layouts: different token counts, or equal totals with different request boundaries. That breaks the collectives that follow and can hang them (#54011). This PR makes TP rank 0 authoritative: 1. `get_num_tokens`: `draft_budget` is broadcast with `broadcast_object` (shm MessageQueue, host only). 2. `reallocate_drafts`: on steps that trim, the per-request `capacities` are broadcast from rank 0 before `cu_num_logits` / `query_start_loc` are built. Both conditions around (2), `draft_budget == 0` and `draft_budget < scheduled drafts`, depend only on the broadcast budget and scheduler-provided counts. Every TP rank therefore takes the same branch, and the collective cannot be entered unevenly. ### Changes vs #56831 - **Test updates for current main.** #56888 renamed `async_copy_to_gpu` to `async_tensor_h2d`; the old monkeypatch no longer resolved, giving 12 failures, and `cpu.yaml` runs `-x`. #58466 made `reallocate_drafts` also return the admitted draft counts. #63421 replaced the compiled budget assignment with a Triton kernel; the CPU test stands in for it with its global top-k ref

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Count pinned adapters against max_loras when scheduling
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #63924. `pin_lora` keeps an adapter in one of the `max_loras` GPU slots, but the scheduler doesn't know about pins and still admits up to `max_loras` other adapters per step. With `max_loras=2` and one pinned adapter, a batch using two other adapters makes the worker evict one that the batch needs, and building the LoRA mapping raises `KeyError` in `convert_mapping`, which kills EngineCore. This makes the scheduler count pinned adapters toward `max_loras`. ## Claims - The scheduler admits at most `max_loras` distinct adapters per step including pinned ones; a request for a pinned adapter doesn't need a new slot. - `EngineCore.pin_lora` / `remove_lora` keep the scheduler's set of pinned adapters up to date. - If a batch still cannot fit next to the pinned adapters (for example after pinning while requests are already running), the worker raises a clear `RuntimeError` instead of evicting an adapter the batch uses and failing with `KeyError`. - Reloading a pinned adapter with `load_inplace=True` keeps it pinned (it was silently unpinned). ## Validation New tests: `test_max_loras_counts_pinned_adapters` (`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`), `test_pinned_lora_counts_toward_gpu_slots` and `test_load_inplace_keeps_lora_pinned` (`tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py`). macOS, CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. title: [KV Offload] Avoid quadratic event polling
summary: ## What changed `SimpleCPUOffloadWorker` previously drained completed transfer events with repeated `list.pop(0)` and scanned every pending event ID on every engine step. title: [Model][DCP] Support Qwen4Exp QSA
summary: ## Purpose Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Qwen4Exp QSA. Each rank reads its own shard of the main KV cache. The QSA selector and its side caches stay replicated on every rank. The ranks then combine their partial results with the base-2 log-sum-exp convention that QSA uses. Five further changes make this work: - The selector and the main KV cache share one block table. In separate groups the selector takes most of the blocks that a request needs, and DCP loses capacity instead of gaining it. - A packed compressed cache binds one whole manager block. Its kernel blocks are mapped afterwards through the stride between manager blocks. Without this the server stops at startup, because a packed block cannot be cut into evenly spaced kernel blocks. - The QSA side caches skip their stores when the block table points at the null block. - Every attention metadata builder in a group takes the block table row width that the runner allocated. A replicated layer in a DCP-sharded group has a larger block than the group, so a builder that derives the width from its own layer spec sizes its kernel block table too small. The mapping now rejects a row that does not fit instead of writing past it. - QSA marks its compression work inactive while CUDA graphs are captured. A capture batch has no real history behind its blocks, so an active work item reads positions that were never written. Without this, full graph capture fails when DCP and speculative decoding are both on. An empty DCP batch now returns both an output tensor and a log-sum-exp tensor. Draft #61242 covers the same fea

title: [Debug] Add native tensor dumping for eager Model Runner V2
summary: ## Purpose Add an opt-in tensor dumper for eager Model Runner V2, using native module hooks and the existing Python serving HTTP/collective-RPC infrastructure. It captures module inputs/outputs and explicit `dump(name, value)` calls, with name/rank/layer and batch-phase filters, a delayed and bounded capture budget, batch metadata and independent CPU snapshots. This simplifies the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate. The generic training/gradient plugins, source patching, grafting, standalone HTTP/ZMQ transport and bundled comparison framework are removed. SGLang format compatibility is not a requirement. ## Design and usage ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve MODEL --enforce-eager \ --tensor-dump-config '{"output_dir":"/tmp/vllm-dumps","patterns":["*self_attn*"],"max_steps":2}' ``` - Native `TensorDumpConfig` travels through `EngineArgs` and `VllmConfig`, like other engine configuration. No dumper-specific environment variables. - Hooks are registered **after worker warmup**. V4.1 runs sparse-MLA warmup through ordinary scheduler requests; registering at model load consumed the dump budget before user requests. The lifecycle change fixes this without request-name filters or an extra readiness flag. - Capture is scoped to actual forwards; snapshots are detached, compact CPU copies. A small `tensor_dumper_capture` helper owns the dummy-run/dumper checks; the eager branch only enters that context and calls the model. - `start_step` counts real forwards independently of the capture budget. `layers` selects `layers.N` module paths; `phase` uses native MRV2 req

title: feat(metrics): add per-step copy-on-write KV block counter
summary: ## Summary Add a per-step copy-on-write (CoW) KV block counter to the scheduler metrics. The scheduler issues KV cache block copies (copy-on-write) when a forked sequence gets a partial prefix cache hit that ends mid-block: the shared block is duplicated into a fresh destination block. Today this work is invisible in metrics. This change exposes it as: - `SchedulerStats.num_cow_blocks` — the number of CoW block copies issued in the most recent `schedule()` step (a per-step delta, mirroring how `prefix_cache_stats` counts per-step). - A Prometheus counter `vllm:num_cow_blocks` — the cumulative number of CoW block copies from the engine (the logger accumulates the per-step delta into a monotonic counter). This gives operators visibility into how often sequences fork with partial cache hits, which is a direct cost driver of KV cache usage (each CoW copy duplicates a block and temporarily holds both endpoints). ## Details - **`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`**: track the per-step CoW count in `Scheduler._last_step_cow_blocks`, set unconditionally after `take_kv_cache_block_copies()` (so a step with no copy resets to 0). Surfaced via `make_stats()`. - **`vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py`**: add `SchedulerStats.num_cow_blocks` field. - **`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`**: aggregate the per-engine count and register `vllm:num_cow_blocks` Prometheus counter, incrementing by the per-step delta. - **`tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`**: add `test_cow_blocks_stats_per_step_delta` verifying the stat is a per-step delta (0 → 1 → 0 across steps) rather than a cumulative total. ## Test pla

title: [KVConnector] Add priority-aware transfer ordering
summary: ## Purpose In disaggregated prefill/decode deployments, P-to-D KV transfer is on the TTFT critical path. It may share the same NIC with background Store or offload traffic, especially when `MultiConnector` combines connectors such as NIXL and `OffloadingConnector`. Priority is currently lost at two points: - `Request.priority` affects scheduler ordering, but is not propagated to connector workers. NIXL workers therefore process requests in metadata insertion order. - `MultiConnector` invokes child connectors in config order. A background connector listed before a P/D connector is submitted first. This PR adds priority-aware ordering at both levels: - NIXL request metadata carries `Request.priority`, and save and receive work is ordered using the scheduler convention: lower values run first. - Connectors expose a default `TransferPriority`. NIXL, Mooncake, and MoRIIO use `CRITICAL`; other connectors use `BACKGROUND` by default. - `MultiConnector` uses this priority when calling `start_load_kv` and `save_kv_layer`. Connectors with equal priority keep their config order. - The transfer order is computed once during initialization to avoid sorting in the per-layer forward path. - The default priority can be overridden through `kv_connector_extra_config`. The original connector list is not reordered because its config order is used for metadata mapping and load selection. Existing behavior is preserved when all connectors have the same priority, and request priority defaults to zero. This changes transfer submission order only. title: [Perf][LoRA] Compute kernel metadata on the CPU to remove per-step GPU syncs
summary: ## Purpose The per-step LoRA metadata path is slow on the CPU and blocks on the GPU: - `convert_mapping` loops over every token in Python (tuple of numpy scalars -> list -> tensor). - `LoRAKernelMeta.prepare_tensors` runs `sort` / `unique` on the GPU and does `if torch.all(...)`, which syncs the CPU with the GPU. This runs twice per step (token mapping and sampler mapping). See the existing `# TODO avoid gpu<->cpu sync here` in `punica_gpu.py`. title: [Bugfix] Make PyTorch top-k tie-breaking deterministic
summary: ## Overview Make the PyTorch top-k/top-p fallback resolve exact ties by lower token ID. Top-k filtering retains exactly k finite candidates when available, before any subsequent top-p filtering. This follows up on closed, unmerged #50979 and the sampling consistency work in #42259. **Draft for discussion of the semantic change and CPU cost:** CPU top-k-only took **1.924x** the original implementation's time on captured model inputs and **2.684x** on BF16-quantized synthetic inputs. These are CPU tensor microbenchmarks, not serving throughput. ## Claims - Both PyTorch paths select the same deterministic top-k support, including cutoff ties, without mutating the caller's k/p tensors or perturbing retained logits. - The sorting path keeps the ascending cumulative-probability calculation, resolves top-p ties consistently, and preserves disabled p=1 rows even when softmax tails underflow. - Restore exact top-k comparison against Triton for ordinary inputs, with explicit mask, fixed-noise sampling, and parameter-preservation regressions. title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Keep the AttnRes block bank in a persistent workspace
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Kimi-K3 on ROCm allocates two ~1.8 GB buffers on every prefill step, each sized by the step's token count. The caching allocator keeps the slightly-too-small leftovers, so its cache grows while serving until something fails. What fails depends on how vLLM sizes the KV cache: - **Extensible KV cache off** (the V1 model runner, which DBO uses, ROCm KV connectors such as MoRIIO/NIXL/Mooncake, or an explicit KV size): ROCr can't get scratch memory and aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. Every request fails. - **Extensible KV cache on** (vllm#56492, the default with the V2 runner): torch's allocator is capped, so the leftovers turn into allocator OOM-and-retry cycles and a larger warmup reserve that costs KV cache. Under TP4 x PP2 the capped pool runs out and requests fail. This PR fixes one of the two buffers: the AttnRes block bank in `KimiLinearModel` now comes from the workspace manager as one persistent buffer, sized for `max_num_batched_tokens`, instead of a fresh allocation per forward. The other buffer is AITER's MoE stage-2 target, fixed by ROCm/aiter#7363. Both are needed, and on current vLLM they have to land together (see [Merge order](#merge-order)). SGLang has the same bank and fixes it in sgl-project/sglang#48164. ## Claims - With ROCm/aiter#7363, Kimi-K3 serves in the configurations where stock fails: extensible KV cache off (stock fails every request) and TP4 x PP2 (stock fails the 1k conc 64 and 128 benchmarks). - On the default TP8 path, 2 allocator retries instead of 10 over the benchmark sequence, a 1.61

title: [Attention][TurboQuant] Optimize 4-bit GQA decode for group size 4
summary: ## Summary Optimize the TurboQuant MSE-key, 4-bit-value decode path for models with a GQA group size of 4. title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek MoE sequence-parallel layout tracking
summary: ## Purpose `deepseek_v2.py` decides whether `hidden_states` are sequence-parallel by comparing the first dimension against the full token count. That inference is ambiguous, and single-token decode is exactly where it breaks. With TP=2 and one decode token, `ceil(1 / 2) == 1`, so a full input and a padded local shard both have one row: | Value | First dimension | Data represented | | --- | ---: | --- | | Full decode input | 1 | Real token | | TP rank 0 local shard | 1 | Real token | | TP rank 1 local shard | 1 | Padding row | When the check misfires, the layer skips its entry all-gather. Each TP rank then runs attention on a different row — rank > 0 holds padding — and the following `reduce_scatter` sums misaligned partials, so decode output is corrupted. This is the same root cause as #50681 / #50685, which fix `qwen3_next.py`. `deepseek_v2.py` carries an independent copy of the pattern, introduced earlier by #46635, so #50685 does not cover it. This PR mirrors that fix so the two read the same way. ### Sites fixed All four shape comparisons on `main` (`63e78ce`): 1. Layer-entry inference — [`deepseek_v2.py#L1300-L1304`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/63e78ce3652f4f94e9f484f40db71ca4cf019f21/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py#L1300-L1304) 2. title: [Performance][EPLB] Skip unchanged layers in async transfer cycles
summary: ## Proposal to improve performance Async EPLB currently runs the full per-layer transfer/commit handshake for every MoE layer, even when a layer's new physical-to-logical mapping is identical to its current mapping. In `transfer_run_periodically()`, every layer unconditionally goes through: 1. the cross-rank `rebalanced` coordination, 2. `transfer_layer()`, 3. a stream synchronization, 4. publication of an `AsyncEplbLayerResult`, and 5. main-thread consumption and map commit. `move_to_buffer()` avoids copying locally unchanged expert rows, but a fully unchanged layer still pays the surrounding Python, communicator, stream, and main-thread handshake costs. For a model with `L` MoE layers and only `K` changed layers, the async pipeline therefore performs `L` layer handshakes instead of `K`. There is also a lifecycle constraint that prevents simply skipping unchanged layers: `_move_to_workspace()` currently completes an async cycle only when it consumes a result whose `layer_idx` is the model's physical last MoE layer. If the last changed layer occurs earlier, or if the whole cycle is unchanged, a naive skip leaves no final result for the main thread to consume and the cycle can remain in progress indefinitely. ## Proposed change Make transfer selection and cycle completion separate concepts: - Compute the changed layer indices from the old and new global mappings. - Call `transfer_layer()` only for changed layers. - Make the last real transfer explicitly complete the cycle, regardless of its physical layer index. - For an entirely unchanged cycle, publish an explicit no-trans

title: [RFC]: Report characters/second alongside tokens/second in vllm bench serve
summary: ## Motivation `BenchmarkMetrics` (`vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`) reports `output_throughput` and `total_token_throughput` and nothing per-character. For English that distinction rarely matters. For scripts whose tokenizers are less efficient it inverts the ranking: **tokens/s flatters exactly the models that make the reader wait longest.** Measured on one machine, one protocol, chat-scenario decode, Thai output (characters counted in U+0E00–U+0E7F only): | served model | Thai chars per output token | |---|---| | Qwen-SEA-LION-v4.5-27B | 3.18 | | WangchanLION-v3-8B | 2.15 | | OpenThaiGPT-1.6-72B | 1.85 | | Typhoon-2.5-Qwen3-4B | 1.75 | | OpenThaiGPT-ThaiLLM-8B | 1.36 | That is a **2.3x spread across models a user might reasonably compare**. Two models at the same tok/s can differ by more than a factor of two in delivered text; a benchmark table that shows only tok/s reports the faster-reading model as the slower one. The effect is not Thai-specific — it applies to any language whose tokenizer coverage is weaker than English, which is most of them. ## Proposal Add character-level counterparts to the existing throughput fields: - `output_char_throughput` and `mean_chars_per_token` in `BenchmarkMetrics`, computed from the decoded output text already available in the benchmark path. - Optional `--charset-range` (or a named preset) to count only codepoints in a range, so mixed-language output can be scored on the target script rather than on incidental Latin/punctuation. title: [Bugfix] Remap ModelOpt q_scale to attn.q_scale
summary: ## Purpose vLLM's checkpoint scale-name remapping has dedicated rules for `k_scale`/`v_scale` in the ModelOpt per-projection and fused-QKV layouts, but no rule for `q_scale`. Checkpoints that quantize the query in addition to the KV cache — NVFP4 W4A4 exports ship `self_attn.q_proj.q_scale` right alongside `k_scale`/`v_scale` — therefore lose the query scale. Two code paths are affected: - **`QuantizationConfig.get_cache_scale_mapper()`** — `WeightsMapper._map_name_with_shard` applies *every* matching regex cumulatively rather than stopping at the first hit. With no ModelOpt rule for `q`, the name falls through to the generic `(?<!\.attn)\.([qkv])_scale$` catch-all and is rewritten to `...self_attn.q_proj.attn.q_scale` — a module path that does not exist. The scale is silently dropped. - **`maybe_remap_kv_scale_name()`** — the `.q_scale` suffix passes the `endswith` guard, but the ModelOpt and `qkv_proj` patterns are `[kv]`-only, so the same catch-all produces a name that isn't in `params_dict`. That path warns and returns `None`, so the scale is not loaded. The fix widens `[kv]` to `[qkv]` in the ModelOpt per-projection and fused-QKV patterns in both places, making `q` symmetric with `k` and `v`. In the mapper, the catch-all's `(?<!\.attn)` lookbehind then correctly declines to fire a second time, so the result stays idempotent. No behavior change for existing checkpoints: before this patch the `q_scale` path produced a name that matches no module, so nothing can be depending on it. summary: ## Purpose On UMA GPUs (GB10 / DGX Spark), MTP spec-decode logs a **negative** CUDA-graph memory estimate (e.g. `-35.69 GiB`). It is then *subtracted* in `determine_available_memory`, so a negative **inflates** the KV budget → OOM (silently, since the warning is gated on `estimate > 0`). Issue #44740. If the reviewer agrees & merges this PR, we can close #44745 #44740 ## Background (skip this if you are familiar with vllm memory budget) At startup vLLM decides how much memory to give the KV cache. Part of that is reserving room for CUDA graphs (captured replayable kernel sequences). The activation runs as `act_and_mul` + `per_token_group_quant` instead. title: [Perf][DSpark] Compute windowed draft context for trailing rows only
summary: ## Purpose A DFlash/DSpark drafter whose KV groups are all sliding-window only ever reads each request's last `window` context positions, but `DFlashSpeculator.propose` runs `combine_hidden_states` (DSpark's `main_proj`) and the per-layer context K/V precompute over every target row. On a 16K-token DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill step that is ~2.6 ms of GPU work, almost all of it for rows the drafter never reads. This PR projects and stores only each request's trailing rows. - **Gate.** Trimming is on when every draft KV group is sliding-window with a window larger than `num_speculative_steps`, the dropped rows cannot be served later, and the drafter has no context anchor (LiLiCorr reads `hidden_states` by target row). Dropped rows could only be served through a prefix-cache hit or a hash-addressed KV store, and both use prefix-cacheable groups only (`KVConnectorBase.get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids` defaults to them). So trimming needs either no draft group to be prefix-cacheable (DSv4.1's SWA bounded replay), or prefix caching off and no KV connector. A P/D transfer connector restores the request's own blocks; the decode side reads the trailing window, which is always among the kept rows. Other drafters are unchanged. - **Threshold.** Only steps that drop at least 2048 context rows trim, since the row gathers cost a few fixed launches; decode steps only pay one integer compare. - **Rows.** Each request keeps its last `window + num_query_per_req` rows (the query block can shift the window when clamped at `max_model_len`), counted back from the device `query_start_loc`, which adaptive v

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Drain and validate HF3FS save writers
summary: ## Overview Wait for every submitted HF3FS save writer before releasing its staging buffers, and require complete allocation/write results before confirming cache keys. Connect the existing cleanup to the engine's `shutdown()` lifecycle so active I/O finishes before the worker releases its GPU cache. ## Changes An early failed writer no longer short-circuits waiting for later writers. A submission exception also drains every writer already accepted. Each batch must return exactly one non-Boolean integer full-page result per submitted page; empty, truncated and malformed responses fail. Allocation replies must match the requested keys and provide distinct nonnegative integer pages before gathering starts. Failed saves retain raw page indices because the current protocol does not distinguish newly reserved pages from existing live pages. **This can leak newly allocated capacity on failure.** The ownership protocol needs a separate fix. During the refresh, real in-process `LLM` execution exposed a second lifecycle gap: the engine calls `shutdown()`, but HF3FS only implemented `close()` and inherited the base no-op hook. The five-line hook now invokes that existing cleanup and unregisters its exit handler. It finishes active I/O; it does not promise to persist saves that have not started. An I/O operation that never completes can still block cleanup. ## Validation 2026-11-10 local GPU run against main at `75be5c3919b6`, with this patch. title: [Bugfix][CPU] Compute beta in float32 in the GDN decode kernel
summary: ## Overview The CPU Gated DeltaNet decode kernel computes the gate `beta = sigmoid(b)` in bf16, while the CPU spec-decode kernel and the Triton GPU kernel compute it in float32. title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][Perf] Support BF16 MLA projections in specialized decode
summary:
## Overview

Part of the Kimi-K3 ROCm decode optimization series. This BF16 MLA PR can merge independently.

Change | Status / dependency -- | -- BF16 fused MLA | This PR Persistent DSpark backbone | Planned; builds on #64031’s sharded sampler

Related: #66172 enables ordinary MLA fallback at DCP1 when fusion is unavailable. It complements this PR and is not a dependency.

The full-stack results below include additional prototype routing, prefetch and scheduling optimizations. They are not the measured result of this PR alone; its end-to-end benchmark is still pending.

Main’s fused MLA requires MXFP4 projections. Keeping the checkpoint’s BF16 weights falls back to separate MLA operations at DCP8, adding kernel boundaries and intermediate memory traffic across 24 layers. At DCP1, specialized decode rejects BF16 projections. This PR lets the fused kernels read BF16 `W_UK_T` and `W_UV` directly at both DCP settings, without a packed weight copy. title: [Feature]: Map unsupported reasoning_effort values to the nearest level the chat template accepts
summary: ## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Some chat templates accept only a subset of the reasoning effort ladder and raise a Jinja error on anything else. For example, the official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` template validates `reasoning_effort` directly against `('xhigh', 'medium', 'low')`, so a request with `high` returns HTTP 400: `Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.` Meanwhile the `ChatCompletionRequest.reasoning_effort` field accepts the full ladder (`none`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`), and OpenAI-compatible clients — agent harnesses especially — routinely send `high` or `minimal`. The request validates at the API layer, then fails at template render time. Today the only ways around this are patching vLLM, forking the chat template, or rewriting requests in a fronting proxy. Proposal: let the operator declare the levels the served model's template accepts, and have vLLM remap any other requested value to the nearest supported level: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh \ --reasoning-effort-rounding down ``` Semantics (on the ladder `minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max`): - `--reasoning-effort-rounding down` (default): highest supported level at or below the requested one; if nothing is at or below, the lowest supported level. With the set above: `high` → `medium`, `minimal` → `low`. - `--reasoning-effort-rounding up`: lowest supported level at or above the requested one; if nothing is at or above, the highest supported level. It writes them into the draft tokens and looks up the selector codebooks with them. Only rows where `d2t` is non-zero come out wrong. Pruned vocabularies usually keep the most frequent (lowest) ids, so `d2t` is the identity over a prefix and it's the rarer tokens past that prefix that break. title: [Bugfix] Use one stage in Triton MLA decode on GPUs with <128 KiB shared memory
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #60172. On sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090), `TRITON_MLA` is the only MLA backend, and the first decode fails with: ```text out of resource: shared memory, Required: 102400, Hardware limit: 101376 ``` `_decode_grouped_att_m_fwd` launches the MLA shape (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=32`, `BLOCK_H=16`) with `num_stages=2`, which needs 102,400 bytes. These GPUs allow 101,376 bytes per block. The existing one-stage fallback only triggers when `BLOCK_DMODEL >= 1024`, so MLA (latent width 512) never gets it. This PR also uses one stage when the device's `max_shared_mem` is below 128 KiB. It reads the value from the Triton driver, cached per device. GPUs with large shared memory (Hopper, datacenter Blackwell) keep two stages, so their behavior is unchanged. ## Test Plan - The standalone reproduction in #60172 (`decode_attention_fwd`, `is_mla=True`, Lk=576, 32 heads, FP8 KV cache, page size 16, 1,000-token sequences) on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (CC 12.0), comparing the output against a PyTorch reference. - End to end: `sarvamai/sarvam-105b-fp8` on 2x RTX PRO 6000, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, vLLM 0.31.0. title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Add prefill_context_kv_only for P/D prefill instances
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On a P/D prefill instance, a DFlash-based drafter (DFlash, DSpark, DFlash2, XPress, ...) only needs to store the context K/V that the decode instance reads. This PR adds `prefill_context_kv_only` to the speculative config. Set on the prefill instance, it makes the drafter schedule no drafts, reserve no lookahead KV slots, capture no draft CUDA graphs and, for draft models that name their context K/V modules, free the draft weights that only drafting reads. Requests that decode on that instance run without speculation. It follows #62784 (per-step K=0) and takes its lookahead and speculator-flag handling from #56957. The option is set explicitly because `kv_role` does not identify a prefill instance: one that also loads from or offloads to a KV store through `MultiConnector` has the `kv_both` role. Related: #62923 does the same for Qwen3 DSpark, behind an opt-in flag with a separate model class. #56957 adds a DSpark prefill-only mode for PP > 1 with non-NIXL connectors and the DeepSeek-V4 draft. This PR keeps `num_speculative_tokens` unchanged, because it also sizes state the decode instance loads (e.g. the Mamba state). Since this PR takes similar approaches, the authors of #56957 (@lucifer1004) and #62923 (@LLLZeSheng) are added as co-authors, as is @njhill, whose simplification of the weight-freeing opt-in is squashed in. ## Design - `SpeculatorConfig.supports_prefill_context_kv_only` declares support: `DFlashSpeculatorConfig` and its subclasses; other speculators reject the option. title: [Bugfix] Add unsplit warmup when dbo enabled
summary: ## Overview Fixes #65106. With `--enable-dbo`, a step that runs without being split into micro-batches can need more workspace than warmup allocated. Because the workspace is locked after CUDA graph capture, the step crashes with `AssertionError: Workspace is locked`. This PR also warms up an unsplit step when micro-batching is enabled, so the workspace is large enough before it locks. ## Validation **End to end**: the serve and bench commands from #65106 (random dataset, 8192 in / 1024 out, 512 prompts, concurrency 128). **Unit tests**: ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py ``` Without the fix: only the new test `test_profile_run_sizes_unsplit_step_under_microbatching[True]` fails. The new test checks that `profile_run` adds the unsplit pass only when micro-batching is enabled. ## Details **Root cause.** Under DBO the workspace manager keeps one slot per micro-batch. `profile_run` only ran the micro-batched dummy step, so each slot was sized for half of `max_num_batched_tokens`. At runtime a step still runs unsplit when any DP rank declines to split: the `_allow_microbatching` prefix veto, a rank below the DBO token threshold, or DP imbalance (one rank with half or fewer of the other's tokens). B200: 885 passed, 45 skipped. RTX PRO 6000: 400 passed, with the same 198 failures on both, from `cooperative_topk` failing to launch on SM12x and from bf16 cases that need 128 KiB of shared memory. - Fault injection: a test-only build makes every guarded scatter claim extra slots (`>` → `>=`, or keeping every tie in `sampled_topk`).

title: [RFC]: Classify GPU faults in fault-tolerance status and mark sticky CUDA errors dead
summary: ### Motivation. I work on GPU device health in Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA): resource health status in kubelet ([KEP-4680](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4680)) and the device health monitor for the NVIDIA DRA driver ([kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu#1525](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1525)). That monitor decides whether a GPU is healthy from the [NVML recovery action](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/latest/api/group__nvmlFieldValueEnums.html#c.NVML_FI_DEV_GET_GPU_RECOVERY_ACTION). One class of faults is invisible there, and only the inference engine can report it. The fault-tolerance framework from [#44428](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44428) and [#46370](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46370) is the natural place to do so. **Faults caused by the application leave the GPU healthy but the process unusable.** - **CUDA:** for `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700), the [CUDA runtime documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#_CPPv4N9cudaError23cudaErrorIllegalAddressE) says it "leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched." [`cudaErrorAssert`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#_CPPv4N9cudaError15cudaErrorAssertE) (710) says "The device cannot be used again" and requires the same relaunch. - **Device:** NVIDIA's [Xid catalog](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/analyzing-xi

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Bound copy descriptors submitted per step for CPU->GPU loads
summary: ## Overview A large CPU->GPU KV offload load submits all of its copy descriptors in one `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` call. When the call has more descriptors than the GPU command queue holds, it blocks the worker thread for most of the copy, and the next step's kernels are not launched. This PR caps the descriptors a regular async load submits per step and submits the rest in later steps. Fixes #65515 ## Claims - Regular async loads no longer block the worker thread for the length of the copy. - GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=8, 8x B200, CPU tier on, AgentX c=32: 859 vs 706 output tok/s, TTFT avg 17.4 s vs 23.8 s. - Stores and expedited loads are unchanged. `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_LOAD_SUBMIT_DESCRIPTORS=0` restores the old behavior. ## Validation **Root cause.** One B200, 6.6 GB per load, same bytes in each row (GLM-5.2 TP=8 uses 40 KB descriptors): | Descriptors per call | CPU time inside the call | DMA time | | --- | --- | --- | | 161k (40 KB) | 110 ms | 123 ms | | 40k (160 KB) | 52 ms | ~123 ms | | 10k (640 KB) | 3.1 ms | ~123 ms | In a torch profiler trace of the TP=8 server, all 8 ranks enter the call in the same step and the compute stream launches nothing during it. **End to end.** `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=8 on 8x B200, `OffloadingConnector` with an 880 GB CPU tier, AgentX (`aiperf --scenario agentx`), concurrency 32, KV tiers emptied before each run. `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` with and without this change backported to `gpu_worker.py`. | Run (30 min) | Engine steps | Output tok/s | TTFT avg / p50 / p90 (s) | ITL avg / p50 (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Baseline | 62,253 | 706

title: [Feature]: Integrate CFT counted-write MoE all-to-all kernel
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Summary Integrate the CFT counted-write MoE all-to-all kernel introduced in [TensorRT-LLM PR #17647](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17647) into vLLM through FlashInfer. ## Background The kernel adds a Compute Fabric Transport (CFT) path for MoE dispatch and combine communication. It uses CUDA Logical Endpoints and `fabric.try_put.counted` operations to write directly into peer receive buffers over the NVLink fabric. A Logical Endpoint is a CUDA transport object representing a resource reachable over the NVLink fabric. Peers address its bound memory using an endpoint ID and offset rather than a mapped remote pointer. ## What is a counted write? A counted write transfers data to a remote Logical Endpoint while atomically incrementing a destination-side counter by the number of bytes delivered. The receiver waits until the counter reaches the expected byte count before consuming the data. This combines data transfer and arrival notification to reduce nvlink latency, avoiding a separate fence-and-flag handshake between the sender and receiver. In throughput cases, because the counter adds to bytes transferred, it could lead to perf regressions. ## Integration plan 1. @bobboli will first integrate the kernel into [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer). 2. After the kernel is available through FlashInfer, vLLM should integrate it through the FlashInfer backend. 3. vLLM should detect the required capabilities at runtime and fall back to the existing MoE all-to-all path when they are unavailable. ## Requirem

summary: ## Problem: Operators running multi-tenant vLLM deployments (behind a gateway, router, or fairness layer) can't attribute server-side metrics to the tenant that generated them. title: [KV Connector] Support piecewise prefix loading in MultiConnector
summary: ## Purpose `MultiConnector` currently queries all configured connectors for cache availability but loads a request from only the first connector with a hit. It cannot combine a cached prefix from one connector with a later contiguous range from another connector. This prevents piecewise prompt KV loading in P/D + offloading deployments. For an external Store hit `[0, S)` and a prompt `[0, N)`, Decode cannot load the cached prefix from Store while receiving `[S, N)` from the P/D connector. Instead, the complete prompt KV must come from a single source, so the cached prefix may take an extra network hop and the two available transfer paths cannot progress concurrently. This PR adds an opt-in `range_aware` policy and a generic range-load API to `MultiConnector`. With the policy enabled, `MultiConnector` queries every child and assigns contiguous, non-overlapping prompt ranges in configured connector order. A connector can advertise support for explicit range assignment and its required range-start alignment. For a Store hit `[0, S)` followed by a P/D hit `[0, N)`, the framework can therefore assign `[0, S)` to the Store connector and `[S, N)` to the P/D connector. The request resumes only after all asynchronous contributors finish. The default first-hit policy remains unchanged. No production connector adopts the range-load API in this PR; a following PR implements it for the Mooncake Store and P/D connectors and adds model-output and RDMA E2E validation. ## Test Plan ### Unit and static checks ```bash pre-commit run --files \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Decline CUTLASS int8 w8a8 on SM100+ so Triton fallback is reachable
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #54311. `CutlassInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported()` takes `compute_capability` but ignores it and always returns `True` on CUDA. So CUTLASS claims every int8 w8a8 layer — but the SM100/SM120 dispatchers wire the int8 func as `nullptr` (`scaled_mm_c3x_sm120.cu`: `nullptr, // int8 not supported on SM120`, same on `sm100`), so the C++ hard-errors at runtime: ``` Int8 not supported on SM121. Use FP8 quantization instead, or run on older arch (SM < 100). ``` The working `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel` — next in `_POSSIBLE_INT8_KERNELS[CUDA]` — never gets a chance. ## Fix Decline in `is_supported()` when `compute_capability >= 100` (SM100/SM120/SM121 Blackwell; CUTLASS int8 is only wired for SM < 100), mirroring the sibling `AiterInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel`'s capability guard. Kernel selection then falls through to `TritonInt8`, which overrides `is_supported()` and supports these arches. FP8 is unaffected (SM120 wires the fp8 func). ## Verified on a GB10 (sm_121) ``` CutlassInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported(121) -> (False, 'CUTLASS int8 w8a8 is not supported on SM100+ (Blackwell); use the Triton int8 kernel.') TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported(121) -> (True, None) _POSSIBLE_INT8_KERNELS[CUDA] == [Cutlass, Triton, Humming] # Triton now reachable ``` ## Tests Device-free (`tests/model_executor/kernels/test_cutlass_int8_sm_gate.py`): declines on SM100/120/121, stays supported on SM90/89/80/75, and `compute_capability=None` stays supported (back-compat).

A power-saving governor or deep C-states on the pinned cores (see the existing `--numa-bind`/`--numa-bind-cpus` docs just above this section) undermines that design, adding latency jitter that's easy to misattribute to the GPU or network. - **`vm.swappiness` / `vm.overcommit_memory`**: hosts using CPU KV offloading (`docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`) have the offloaded tier competing with the page cache and other host memory. title: [Bugfix] Exclude the compilation peak from memory profiling
summary: ## Purpose Closes #54122. On a cold start `torch.compile` and Inductor autotuning run inside `profile_run()`, which sits inside the `memory_profiling()` window. With AOT compile, `decorators.py` already splits the two phases into separate `with` blocks, and `monitor_profiling_run()` asserts compilation is finished before the profiling forward begins, but nothing clears the allocator high-water mark between them. Compilation's temporaries are freed before that forward, so `transient_peak_headroom` counts them as activation memory and the KV cache shrinks until the compile cache is warm. This drops the high-water mark when compilation finishes. Clearing the counter alone would also discard a peak recorded earlier in the same window, since `profile_run()` runs the multimodal encoder before the backbone compiles, so the pre-compilation value is carried over and folded back in. Without AOT (`VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE=0` or `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`) the compile and the first profiling forward run in the same `monitor_torch_compile` block, so the two peaks can't be told apart there. That block passes `discard_peak=False` and keeps the current behavior. ## Test plan 1x H100 80GB, `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, nightly wheel `3b33a845c` with the patch overlaid. title: [RFC]: Data integrity and I/O liveness for the filesystem KV offload tier
summary: ### Motivation. The filesystem secondary tier (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/`) is a data path with no integrity verification and no bound on how long a single I/O operation may take. #49328 established the partial-keep contract this builds on: a failed load marks its own cached lookup verdict a miss and reports how many blocks loaded before the failure, so earlier blocks survive. Two gaps remain on top of that: 1. **No data integrity verification.** Block contents written to the filesystem tier are never checksummed. `_load_block` detects a file shorter than `block_size` and deletes it, so truncation is caught. What is not caught is content that is the right length and the wrong bytes: bit rot on the storage device, a partially rewritten file, or a block written by an instance whose layout differs in a way the `FileMapper` path hash does not capture. Such a block is copied into the primary tier and consumed as attention KV, producing wrong logits with no error signal anywhere in the system. 2. **No deadline on filesystem I/O.** `batch_store_block` and `batch_load_block` run as a single pool task per job with no deadline. A stalled NFS mount, hung FUSE filesystem, or a device in error recovery blocks that pool thread indefinitely. The pool is bounded at `n_read_threads` + `n_write_threads` (16 + 16 by default), and read-priority threads fall back to the store queue and vice versa, so ~32 stuck operations stall all tiering traffic in both directions. This is the tier-side half of the problem reported in #49829: that issue bounds how long the scheduler waits on a `HIT_PENDIN

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve confirmed junction after lookup retry
summary: ## Overview Preserve a confirmed full-attention junction when offload lookup convergence excludes an in-flight chunk. Related to #63565 and its fix #63566. ## Claims - A deferred full-attention lookup can become confirmed after a sparse group shortens the lookup range, even when the pending chunk itself remains pending. Record the confirmed boundary if a later sparse group shortens the hit again. - Never record a junction from a full-attention group that has not been confirmed, even if another group has reset the convergence loop's deferred flag. - This changes junction retention, not the converged hit length or the manager's lookup semantics. ## Validation - Real `CPUOffloadingManager`, real requests and scheduler: both new regression tests fail on the base revision and pass with the fix. The first returns a 16-token hit and changes the junction from 0 to 32; the second prevents an unconfirmed 16-token junction. - Full `test_scheduler.py`: **507 passed**, 15 warnings. title: [RFC]: extract_hidden_states — stream hidden states to CPU pages with token-hash prefix backfill
summary: Implementation PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66785 ## Motivation The `extract_hidden_states` speculative-decoding method caches target-model hidden states so they can be exported as training data. Today those hidden states live in the **device KV cache pool** via `HiddenStateCacheSpec` and are gathered from device at request completion. This creates two problems: 1. **The hidden-state pool competes with attention KV for the same HBM.** On MLA / hybrid-attention models its footprint is on the same order as the attention KV itself — about **72 KiB/token** for a GLM-style config with 6 extracted layers × hidden 6144 (bf16). At 64k–128k context this materially reduces achievable concurrency; small-memory devices (RTX 4090, Ascend 910C) have no headroom for it at all. 2. **The data is destined for host disk anyway.** Hidden states are exported to `.safetensors` for offline training consumption, so holding the full working set in HBM for a request's entire lifetime provides no compute benefit — it is pure residency cost. Host RAM (typically 128–512 GiB) is far larger than device memory and is the natural place for a data-extraction pipeline. Measured impact on Qwen3-8B / RTX 4090 48 GiB (`--max-model-len 8192`, 4 extracted layers, HS ≈ 32 KiB/token ≈ 18% of the device KV+HS pool): moving hidden states off-device raises GPU KV cache capacity from 151,872 to 189,600 tokens (**+24.8%**), i.e. maximum 8k concurrency from 18.54x to 23.14x, with element-wise identical exported files. ### Problem statement We need an opt-in storage path for `extract_hidden_states` that (

summary: ## Overview Let `--enable-ep-weight-filter` work with `--enable-eplb`. Since #37322 the loader turns the filter off whenever EPLB is enabled, so every rank of an EPLB deployment reads every expert weight. This derives the experts each rank needs from EPLB's initial placement instead. Follow-up to #37136, #37351 and #37322. ## Claims - With EPLB, each rank reads only the experts its physical slots hold in the initial placement, including redundant replicas. DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2 with DEP8 and 32 redundant experts: **105.2 GiB per rank instead of 384.9 GiB** (the plain EP filter without EPLB reads 100.1 GiB). - Outputs match EPLB without the filter within run-to-run noise, across 32-33 rebalancing steps: GSM8K 0.9636 vs 0.9621 (A/A 0.9629), and the same final answer on 97.4% of questions, equal to the A/A agreement. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Widen the lazy SimpleCPUOffload walk to cover CPU loads
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview In lazy mode, `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` evicts cached GPU blocks with no CPU copy whenever a step's async CPU loads take more blocks than the lazy walk covers. This PR widens the walk by a decaying peak of recent load allocations. It keeps the behavior of #59383 (stores return to the eviction end) and #65237 (the walk starts at the head, bounded by `_target_free`). ## Claims - **Bug.** `_target_free = 2 × cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, block_size)` bounds the blocks one step takes for scheduled tokens. A CPU-hit load, however, allocates all its destination blocks at admission, outside that budget. One 100k-token prefix with block size 128 is about 800 blocks against a 512-block window. Cached blocks past the window are evicted uncopied and recomputed on their next hit. - **Fix.** `update_state_after_alloc` counts the destination blocks loads take between walks. The walk covers `_target_free + 2 × peak`, where the peak decays by ⌈peak/128⌉ per walk. Without loads, the walk is exactly as before, and eager mode is unchanged. - **End-to-end.** In the deployment that surfaced this (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP2 on 2×B300, lazy offload, agentic trace replay), moving from an older build to `c18fd7e` nearly doubled recomputed prompt tokens, 4.3% → 8.2%. Throughput fell 100.3k → 91.9k tok/s/GPU, and p90 interactivity 107 → 72 tok/s. With this patch, the top TP2 point (c48) is back at the older build's accepted numbers: 135.5k tok/s/GPU and p90 85.3, against 111.0k and 55.6 for the unpatched build (see Validation). - **Cost.** In a simulated contend

title: [ROCm] Route DSv4 sparse decode to the aiter v4 nm ASM kernel
summary: ## Summary The DeepSeek V4 sparse decode on ROCm always runs the Triton `_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_partial` kernel. aiter ships an ASM decode for this exact shape, `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm` (loaded as `mla_a8w8_qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_nm`), but it takes a single packed KV buffer while the V4 decode reads two caches: the SWA window and the compressed region. Both stacks already encode a token identically — 448 OCP E4M3 FP8 NoPE values, 64 BF16 RoPE values, and seven UE8M0 scale bytes of `ceil(log2(absmax / 448)) + 127`. Only the placement differs: | | vLLM record | aiter / packed row | |---|---|---| | NoPE | 448 FP8 at offset 0 | 448 FP8 at offset 0 | | Scales | 8 bytes/token in a block-tail scale row, 7 real + 1 pad | inline at `[448, 462)`, each of the 7 duplicated twice, then pad to 512 | | RoPE | 64 BF16 inline at offset 448, giving a 576-byte token record | separate parallel `[pages, 64]` BF16 buffer | So a fused Triton gather repacks the selected pages of both caches into one unified two-buffer allocation **without requantizing anything**, and a single ASM call serves the whole step. Compressed rows take the head of each query's slice and the SWA window takes the tail, which is how a single-source kernel covers a two-source decode. Opt-in with `VLLM_ROCM_V4_ASM_DECODE=1`. Unset reproduces the Triton path exactly: the flag is the first, short-circuiting condition in the dispatch. ## Status: the kernel wins, the path still loses Draft because this is not yet a net gain. title: [KV Connector] Preserve divergent hybrid hits with mixed connectors
summary: ## Overview Fixes #62862. A mixed `MultiConnector` now preserves divergent local hybrid prefix hits when a capable child such as NIXL can restore the missing recurrent state. An incapable child cannot be selected at that divergent boundary. ## Claims - Advertise divergent-hit support when any child supports it, and route divergent lookups only to capable children. If none matches, the scheduler falls back to the shared local cache boundary. - Add scheduler regressions for both child-selection outcomes and a real P/D serving regression using NIXL plus offloading on Qwen3.5-0.8B. ## Validation | Configuration | Decode local hits on second request | NIXL bytes, first request | NIXL bytes, second request | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Original `MultiConnector` capability check | 0 | 33,693,696 | 33,693,696 | | This change | 576 | 33,693,696 | 26,615,808 | The serving check sent the same 601-token prompt twice through 1P1D servers sharing one RTX 5050 Laptop GPU (8 GB), with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, greedy decoding, `max_tokens=4`, 128 MiB KV cache per server, `max_model_len=768`, and block size 16. Both outputs matched. This is a functional and transfer-volume check, not a throughput or RDMA benchmark. The new serving test failed with the original capability check (`0` local hits, unchanged transfer bytes) and passed with the fix (`576` local hits, fewer transfer bytes). title: [ROCm][AITER] Add GDN long-prefill split-QKV fast path
summary: ## Motivation ROCm/aiter#4299 adds a channel-last HIP path for `causal_conv1d_fwd_split_qkv`, which can consume Qwen3.5's contiguous `[T, D]` projection through its logical `[D, T]` transpose without materializing a copy. vLLM already fuses its packed post-conv split, normalization, and gating, so dispatching the AITER op unconditionally regresses short prompts. title: Enhance engine snapshot management and API lifecycle
summary: ## Purpose Add an opt-in Engine Snapshot deep-sleep path that keeps the API frontend, HTTP listener, and launcher alive while snapshotting and exiting the `EngineCoreProc` subtree. On wake, vLLM validates the snapshot and runtime environment, restores the EngineCore and CUDA state, adopts the restored process, reconnects the frontend, and reopens request admission only after health and semantic checks pass. Design, roadmap, compatibility constraints, and complete experimental results are documented in [RFC #52125: vLLM Native Reusable Engine Snapshot Sleep (L3)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52125). This work overlaps with #51360 in its use of CRIU and CUDA Checkpoint/Restore for an initialized engine. The snapshot boundary and user-facing lifecycle differ: - #51360 captures the complete initialized service process tree before the HTTP listener is bound and restores it during instance startup. - This PR implements runtime deep sleep. The frontend and HTTP listener remain available for status and wake requests while only the EngineCore subtree is captured, terminated, restored, and reattached. ## Change Summary - Add the Engine Snapshot lifecycle: `READY → DRAINING → PREPARING → SNAPSHOTTING → HIBERNATED` and `HIBERNATED → RESTORING → ATTACHING → VERIFYING → READY`. - Add idle-only request admission control and readiness handling around snapshot transitions. - Add EngineCore detach, expected-exit handling, restored-process adoption, and frontend reconnection. - Add `fake` and `criu_cuda` snapshot providers. - Add atomic snapshot artifact commit, manifest valida
