title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM120 sparse-MLA prefill IMA with DSpark speculative decoding (#56771)
summary: When running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 with DSpark speculative decoding, long-prompt prefill chunks triggered an Illegal Memory Access (IMA) in FlashInfer's sparse-MLA backend. This PR fixes the underlying memory aliasing, stride mismatch, and out-of-bounds loads. ## Root Cause 1. Workspace memory aliasing under CUDA graphs: With DSpark speculative decoding, decode verification is captured inside CUDA graphs while prefill chunks run eagerly. Both paths were sharing a single 128MB workspace buffer from `_flashinfer_dsv4_workspace_by_device`. Eager prefill chunks overwrote scratchpad memory that the active decode graph expected to remain valid, corrupting memory during graph execution. 2. Index tensor geometry mismatch: FlashInfer's sparse MLA decode kernel expects a 3D coordinate layout `(num_tokens, 1, topk)`. The decode path already reshapes its indices to 3D, but `_forward_prefill` passed a 2D tensor `(num_prefill_tokens, topk)`. FlashInfer accessed this buffer using 3D stride assumptions, which caused pointer calculations to index out of bounds on longer prompts. 3. Unbounded block table loads and uninitialized memory: In `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel`, loads from `block_table_ptr` lacked upper-bound checks against `block_table_stride`. Large local indices read past the request row in the block table. In addition, outputs in `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` were allocated using `torch.empty`, leaving uninitialized garbage when reusing memory from CUDA caching pools. ## Changes - Workspace isolation: Separated prefill workspace allocation using `i

title: [KV Offload][KVCR] Demote the CPU-tier copies of chunks served to a peer
summary: ## Overview This PR adds an opt-in `demote_served_chunks` option to the KVCR secondary tier. When a peer fetches chunks from this instance through KVCR, the peer stores its own copy. The local CPU-tier copy keeps its place in the eviction order, because the serve path pins it without recording an access. With the option on, the tier demotes those local copies right after pinning them, so they are evicted first once the transfer releases them. They are demoted, not dropped: a later local reuse restores their rank. To support it: - `CachePolicy` gains an optional `demote(keys)` hint. It is a no-op by default, and `lru` implements it. - `CPUOffloadingManager` gains `demote(keys, pins_held)`. - Secondary tiers reach it through a new optional `ParentManager.demote(keys)`. ## Claims - **New option:** the KVCR tier option `demote_served_chunks`, default `false`. Nothing changes unless it is set. - **Behavior with `lru`:** served chunks move to the evict-first end, tail first and oldest demotion first. - A chunk that another local request is reading keeps its place. - A later local request-scoped access restores normal recency. - **Compatibility:** `arc` and existing out-of-tree policies ignore the hint. Other secondary tiers are unaffected, because `ParentManager.demote()` demotes nothing by default. - **Outputs cannot change:** the option only reorders CPU-tier evictions. - **Performance:** in a disaggregated deployment of a hybrid model (4 prefill and 4 decode instances with KVCR, under agentic traffic), compared with the option off: - at 320 concurrent sessions: 10.3% more requ

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] CuTe DSL mHC boundary for decode batches up to 336 tokens
summary: ## Overview DeepSeek-V4.1 decode spends ~80 Mega mHC launches per step on the shifted mHC boundary (residual update, next sublayer's pre-mix, Sinkhorn, collapse and RMSNorm). summary: ## Summary Fixes #64572. `TritonAttentionImpl` re-derives K/V cache views (`transpose(1, 2).split` + optional FP8 `view`) on every attention call across `forward`, `do_kv_cache_update`, and `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update`, even though these views depend only on the `kv_cache` tensor's storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is allocated. title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support KDA RecoverSSM (--use-replayssm)
summary: ## Overview Let GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA layers use the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM verify/commit path (`--use-replayssm`) during speculative decoding, so each request holds one KDA state block per group instead of `2 + num_speculative_tokens`. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] MonoKernel: fetch the shared expert's up/gate weights before the top-8 (on #64245)
summary: ## Overview In the MonoKernel's expert up/gate stage, half of the 256 CTAs also compute one 8-column chunk of the shared expert. Those CTAs ran up/gate about 2 µs longer than the rest, and the slowest of them set when the down stage could start. The shared expert needs no routing, yet its weights were fetched only after the top-8 selection. This PR issues those weight loads before the routing wait, so the bytes stream while the CTA would otherwise sit idle in the top-8. The units, the MFMA order and the reduction are unchanged, so outputs are bit-identical. **Stacked on #64245** (and through it on #64225 and #61662), which has not landed, so the diff against main includes them. This PR's own change is the last commit, `dc17d297ba` (`mono/ffn/kernel.py` only): [compare against #64245](https://github.com/amd-dlimpus/vllm/compare/aff9dc4a91...dc17d297ba). `dc17d297ba` has the same tree as `acc8087d86`, which the numbers below were measured on; only a missing Signed-off-by was added. **Independent of the KV cache dtype**: the change is in the MoE stage, after attention. ## The change `ug8_units` moves out of the round loop and takes its 8-column chunk explicitly. Each CTA's shared-expert units, always in its first round, are issued right at the start of the stage, before `dn_route`. A unit only loads weights when it is built; it reads the activations from LDS later, in `mma_units`. So the early loads need nothing from the routing or the activation staging. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] MonoKernel: quantize routed expert mid to MXFP8 once, in up/gate (on #61662)
summary: ## Overview The MonoKernel's expert-down stage spent 5.6 µs of every width-4 launch re-quantizing the expert intermediate (`mid`) to MXFP8, and every one of the 256 CTAs did the same work on the same 36,864 values. This PR quantizes the routed experts' `mid` once, in the up/gate CTAs that produce it, and publishes MXFP8 words and E8M0 scales instead of f32. The down stage then polls a quarter of the bytes and copies them into LDS. The LDS words and scales are unchanged, so launch outputs are bit-identical. **Stacked on #64225**, which is stacked on #61662. Neither has landed, so the diff against main includes both. This PR's own change is the last commit, `aff9dc4a91` (`mono/ffn/kernel.py` and `mono/ffn/layout.py`): [compare against #64225](https://github.com/amd-dlimpus/vllm/compare/269796ffc2...aff9dc4a91). `aff9dc4a91` has the same tree as `0fb606374d`, which the numbers below were measured on; only a missing Signed-off-by was added. It touches different code from #64207 and stacks cleanly with it. **Independent of the KV cache dtype**: the change is in the MoE stages, after attention. ## Where the time went From a traced width-4 launch (TP2, FP8 KV, 2,048-token context), with all waves synchronized before each mark. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] MonoKernel: pad a narrow step's inputs once, not every layer (on #61662)
summary: ## Overview When a decode step has fewer tokens than the MonoKernel's width (one request on width 2, three on width 4), the runtime copied the four mHC inputs into padding buffers before each of the 41 kernel layers. This PR pads once, at the first kernel layer, and chains each layer's padded outputs straight into the next. At concurrency 1 it cuts median ITL by about 5%, and it doesn't change the kernels at all. **Stacked on #61662**, which has not landed, so the diff against main includes it. This PR's own change is the last commit, `269796ffc2` (+73 / −6: `runtime/layers.py` plus tests). It is independent of #64207 (the Sinkhorn change, a different file), and the two stack cleanly. I'll rebase when #61662 lands. **Independent of the KV cache dtype**: the change is in the runtime's per-layer glue, before any attention. ## The change `FlashLayer.finish` slices each launch's width-S outputs down to the step's n rows for vLLM's layer interface, and `_pad` then copied them back into width-S buffers for the next launch. That is 4 device copies per kernel layer, 164 per step, each about 4 µs and serialized on the stream. `FlashLayer.inputs` now recognises the previous kernel layer's row slices (an identity check) and passes that layer's padded buffers on as they are. Anything else, such as the step's first kernel layer fed by vLLM's layer, is still padded. The padding rows then carry the previous layer's padding outputs instead of fresh zeros. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] MonoKernel: take the mHC Sinkhorn off the gate's critical path (on #61662)
summary: ## Overview Takes the mHC Sinkhorn off the critical path of the GLM-5.3-Flash MonoKernel's gate. Median decode ITL drops 6.7% at concurrency 1 and 6.9% at concurrency 4 (TP2, MI355X, real-text prompts), with bit-identical outputs. **Stacked on #61662**, which has not landed, so the diff against main includes it. This PR's own change is the last commit, `bcba53a68f` (+72 / −66, one file: `mono/ffn/kernel.py`, `run_gate`). I'll rebase when #61662 lands. **Independent of the KV cache dtype.** The gate runs before attention in every MonoKernel launch (the attention gate before qkv, the FFN gate before the router) and touches no KV state, so the gain carries over unchanged to the e4m3 KV path, bf16 KV, and the `mxfp4_mla` KV of #64121. ## The change Each gate computes `pre`, `post`, and a 4×4 `comb` matrix normalised by 20 Sinkhorn iterations. Before this PR, thread 0 did all of it serially and only then wrote the layer input row, which the rest of the launch waits on. Traced at TP2 (S=2, 2,048 context), the Sinkhorn alone took 5.0–6.9 µs per gate, twice per launch. - **16 lanes.** The Sinkhorn now runs on 16 lanes of wave 0, with lane `4i + j` holding `comb[i][j]`. Row and column sums come from lane shuffles, added in the sequential loop's order, so every `comb` value is bit-identical to before. - **After the row.** Only a later seam reads `comb`, so the layer row is written first and the Sinkhorn runs after it, off the critical path. - **Smaller moves.** `pre` and `post` move to 8 lanes, and the scale and base loads are issued before the mailbox wait. ## Performance A/B on thi

title: [RFC]: Explicit row layouts for routed-expert capture
summary: ## Motivation Routed-expert capture (R3, `enable_return_routed_experts`) records the logical expert IDs selected for each token on the current DP rank. The router computes `topk_ids` and invokes `capture_fn` before EPLB maps logical IDs to physical experts. The current `RoutedExpertsCapturer.capture(layer_id, topk_ids)` then infers which rows belong to this DP rank from the tensor's row count and `dp_metadata`. That inference works for the layouts currently encoded in the capturer, but an out-of-tree MoE backend can split, gather, and pad `hidden_states` and `router_logits` **before routing**. The resulting `topk_ids` inherits that physical row layout. Row count alone does not describe the ownership, ordering, or padding of those rows. In particular, different TP ranks can see different row counts in the same forward, so inferring whether to enter a collective from each rank's local shape is unsafe. vLLM-Ascend currently [replaces the entire capturer method](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_routed_experts_capture.py) to handle its communication layouts. This duplicates upstream capture logic and couples it to Ascend communication modes. A previous [padded all-gather fix, #43737](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43737), addressed one layout by adding another shape branch; the broader issue is that the component which knows the row arrangement cannot communicate it to the capturer. ### Concrete Ascend layouts These are **routing-input layouts before expert dispatch**, not the later EP all-to-all exchange of token ac

title: [Test][KV Events] Check a reference consumer against a real engine

title: [RFC]: Switch Rust regex engine for response parsing
summary: ### Motivation. Hi! Matt from the Transformers team at HF here. I see there's a Rust implementation of the response parsing feature (in `rust/src/parser/src/unified/hf/`), but it uses the standard `regex` crate which doesn't support lookaround. However, a lot of regexes in response parsing do use lookarounds, and they're quite hard to avoid, and this makes it hard to add templates to models because the model owners don't want to break vLLM support ([example](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/discussions/68)) Note that this only applies to Rust, the Python code uses Python's `regex` which does support lookarounds! ### Proposed Change. Could we move the regex engine to something else? For example, I think `PCRE2` supports lookarounds and partial matching. Regexes might need a couple of changes to work in `PCRE2` but we these can be implemented fairly straightforwardly. Of course, if anyone has other ideas, I'm open to suggestions! ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Opt in to lifecycle-aware KV admission (#64460)

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Seed both-XD-RoPE drafting from the xdrope positions buffer
summary: Fixes #54555. ## Purpose The both-XD-RoPE config (target model `uses_xdrope_dim > 0` and draft model `uses_xdrope_dim > 0`) allocates `xdrope_positions` instead of the 1D `positions` buffer, but the draft loop seeds `positions` from `self.positions` for anything that is not `uses_mrope`, so the first both-XD-RoPE drafter with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2` raises `AttributeError` on its first speculative step. title: [Bug]: ModelOpt Llama-4 Checkpoints Take 5+ minutes to load
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch In working on some MoE refactors, I discovered that L4 for ModelOpt takes 5+minutes to load weights even from CPU page cache. - https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8 The root cause is basically this hack logic to load the state dict that ModelOpt uses - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/llama4.py#L439-L523 [modelopt is the fused case] What happens is that the CPU tensor (loaded weight) that we are going to load into the GPU tensor (param) becomes non-contiguous due to this logic. As a result, when we eventually call `_copy()` from CPU->GPU we are calling this on a non-contiguous cpu tensor which takes 3-4s per weight. To hack around this for local R&D, I simply immediately move the loaded_weight to the GPU. This makes the gather happen on the GPU which accelerates things a lot. This isn't reasonable as an actual solution though We should investigate where the logic in the weight loader can avoid creating non-contiguous CPU tensors ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Make fused MoE expert weights contiguous before GPU copy in Llama-4
summary: Fixes #31624. ## Summary In `load_moe_expert_weights`, a sliced/transposed fused MoE expert weight view is passed to `weight_loader()` and copied to GPU while still non-contiguous. A non-contiguous CPU tensor's DMA transfer to GPU is dramatically slower than a contiguous one. Adds `.contiguous()` right before the `weight_loader()` call, on the already-sliced piece — not upfront on the whole weight, since a prior attempt at this fix (#32081, auto-closed by staleness, not rejected) found that naive blanket `.contiguous()` can regress smaller tensors. ## Scope note A synthetic benchmark on H100 NVL (the real Llama-4 checkpoints, 109B-400B, don't fit on one GPU) tested three locations that could have the same issue. Only the fused MoE expert weight path (this PR) showed an unambiguous, large improvement — FP8 block-scale and Q/K rotary permute tensors were *slower* with `.contiguous()` added at their (smaller) sizes in isolation. Since MoE expert weights dominate total checkpoint bytes, this is the change with validated, measured benefit; the other two locations are deliberately excluded pending more precise real-world sizing data. ## Validation ``` torch 2.6.0a0+df5bbc09d1.nv24.11 | GPU: NVIDIA H100 NVL === fused MoE expert weight, basic-indexed view after transpose(-1,-2), shape [64,4096,1024] === non-contiguous transfer: mean=574.401ms min=536.849ms max=585.899ms contiguous() transfer: mean=28.911ms min=24.788ms max=103.387ms speedup: 19.87x ``` (A first run on the same shape measured 22.35x; 19.87x on a clean isolated re-run — consistent within normal GPU/CPU scheduling noi

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][BatchInvariant] Use a fixed AttnRes tiling under batch invariance
summary: Part of #66163. ### Purpose Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a token's output must not depend on the other tokens that share its step. The Kimi-K3 ROCm AttnRes op (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/attn_res.py`) picks its launch tiling from the batch size: ```python # Source tiling helps decode, while one-source tiles scale better for prefill. if num_tokens >= 256 or num_blocks <= 1: block_l, num_warps = 1, 4 else: block_l, num_warps = 4, 8 ``` `BLOCK_L` sets how many source blocks each online-softmax step combines, and `num_warps` sets the reduction layout. Both change the FP32 rounding of a row. When more than one AttnRes block is valid, a decode token run alone (`num_tokens < 256`, tiling (4, 8)) and the same token in a step with prefill chunks (`num_tokens >= 256`, tiling (1, 4)) therefore get different results. Why this is easy to miss: - Layers before the first AttnRes block boundary always have `num_blocks <= 1`, so they always take (1, 4) and are invariant. - The difference first appears at the first boundary, layer `attn_res_block_size`. A small test model with fewer layers never reaches it. - In the full Kimi-K3.1 model (TP8 + EP8, every other batch-invariant component in place), prompt logprobs were bitwise equal alone vs batched. Decode logprobs differed by up to 7e-4 when a decode token shared a step with other requests' prefill chunks. The first diverging tensor was the MoE input of the first AttnRes boundary layer. title: [Kernel] Harden top_k_per_row against NaN and under-filled output
summary: ## Purpose Addresses the kernel-hardening portion of #49896: prevent `top_k_per_row_prefill` (and the shared `topKPerRowJob` used by the decode/split variants) from emitting uninitialized or invalid indices when NaN values leave fewer than `top_k` selectable candidates. Root cause in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`: `extractBinIdx` bins positive-NaN bit patterns above +inf, so NaN-dominated rows place the histogram threshold bin on a NaN bin; the insertion-sort final pass's NaN comparisons all evaluate false, so every threshold-bin element writes slot 0 and the remaining `smemOutput` slots keep uninitialized dynamic shared memory, which the unconditional final store loop emits as indices. With fewer than `top_k` non-NaN candidates, `smemThresholdBinIdx` is additionally read unset. Downstream gathers with the garbage indices then hit device-side asserts / illegal memory access. Changes (kernel `+42/−1`, tests `+209`): - `isNaNLogit()` bit-pattern test (robust under `--use_fast_math`, HIP-compatible via `__float_as_uint`); - NaN exclusion in both `distributeToBins` and `processBins`, kept consistent so histogram counts match prefix sums; - well-defined fallback when fewer than `top_k` candidates exist (`smemThresholdBinIdx = kNumBins`, `smemFinalBinSize = 0`); - `smemOutput` pre-filled with `-1` (multi-block variant also `-FLT_MAX` logit halves), `finalIndices[ii] = -1` init in the radix path, and a `-1`-preserving rebase in the strided final store — under-filled rows now return `-1` padding like the short-row path instead of garbage. title: [Bugfix][MoE] Dynamic per-group BLOCK_M for SM120 DeepGEMM contiguous-grouped MoE
summary: ## Why On SM120 (RTX 6000D / RTX PRO 6000), the vendored DeepGEMM reports a fixed contiguous-group alignment of 128, so every routed expert in a MoE batch is padded to 128-row multiples and the grouped GEMM runs BLOCK_M=128 tiles. At decode-time token counts (per-expert M is often 1-6), most of each tile is padding — the whole MoE chain runs ~2x slower than it needs to. The SM120 kernels support BLOCK_M in {64, 128}; nv_dev's DeepGEMM fork already applies a per-group policy on SM120. This PR ports that policy into the vLLM glue layer as a **shape-dynamic** cap. ## What this PR does When `ceil(num_tokens * num_topk / local_num_experts) <= 64`, cap the alignment at 64 instead of 128. Deterministic per token-count shape, so cudagraph capture/replay stay consistent. Applied at the three call sites that must agree (permute, both apply variants, warmup planning). ## Validation (8x RTX 6000D 84G SM120, DSV4.1-Flash-1017, TP8+EP8, DSpark k=7) | tier | stock (128) | dynamic | delta | |---|---|---|---| | 1K c1 | 252.4 tok/s | 284.0 | +12.5% | | 1K c32 | 973.5 tok/s | 1094.3 | +12.4% | | 8K c8 | 546.1 tok/s | 826.1 | +51.3% | Quality probes (17*19=323 / 9.11-vs-9.9 / factual zh / tool call) all correct on both legs. title: [Perf][KV Offload] Lazy SimpleCPUOffload: offload before every GPU eviction, evict CPU copies of loaded blocks first
summary: ## Overview With `lazy_offload`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` stores a cached GPU block only when it nears eviction. The walk that does this misses blocks the GPU then evicts with no CPU copy, and the CPU tier spends a quarter of its capacity on copies of blocks the GPU already holds. This PR closes the gaps and evicts those copies first. Related: #65683 sizes the walk target for sliding-window groups, #65561 orders eager CPU frees; neither covers these cases. ## Claims - Scheduler-level replay of an agentic multi-turn workload: prefill tokens per request fall by 6.4% (CPU tier = 1x GPU), 14.3% (2x) and 51.1% (4x) against main, 3 seeds each. - E2E, Qwen3-8B on one GB200 with a lazy CPU tier: prefill tokens computed fall by 10-12% with a CPU tier of 2x the GPU KV cache and by 58-59% at 4x; throughput rises 1.1-5.0% and TPOT falls 3.6-5.1%. At 4x, mean TTFT falls 1.7-4.4% and p90 4.7-7.0%; at 2x, mean TTFT is flat and p90 rises 2.5-5.4% (see Tradeoffs). - No numerics change: GSM8K 5-shot strict-match is 0.8976 with prompts computed and 0.9037 with 69% of prompt tokens read back from the CPU tier. ## Validation E2E: Qwen3-8B, TP1 on one GB200 GPU, GPU KV cache 4096 blocks of 16 tokens (65K tokens), `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048, lazy `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with `num_cpu_blocks` 8192 or 16384. Workload: `benchmarks/multi_turn` with 12 clients over 24 active conversations, 2400 requests, 150 output tokens. Main and this PR ran at the same time on the two Grace sockets of one node (GPU0 and GPU2, memory bound to the local NUMA node), swapping GPUs in the second round. Compute

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Only divide shared expert output in FP16 for models that compensate
summary: ## Overview Fixes #65533. Since #35949, the MoE runner divides the shared expert output by `routed_scaling_factor` in FP16 (instead of scaling the routed output) whenever a model sets `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True`. That is only correct for models whose decoder layers compensate (DeepseekV2-style). GLM-4 MoE does not, so FP16 GLM-4.7 produces degenerate output on v0.20.0+. This makes the divide-shared path opt-in. ## Claims - FP16 GLM-4.7-AWQ (`routed_scaling_factor=2.5`, one shared expert) generates correct output again; it loops on v0.20.0–v0.31.0 without this fix. - Models that set `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True` without FP16 compensation (glm4_moe, bailing_moe_linear, laguna, nemotron_h) now get `routed * scale + shared` in FP16, matching BF16. - No behavior change for models that compensate: `DeepseekV2MoE` (deepseek_v2, deepseek_v32, unlimited_ocr), AXK1 and OpenPangu opt in. - No change for BF16/FP32, for layers without shared experts, or for the fused-shared-expert path (`shared_output` is `None` there). ## Validation **Unit test** (new, `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py`): real `FusedMoEFactory` layers with shared experts and `routed_scaling_factor=2.5`, compared against a routed-only layer with the same weights; FP16/BF16 × opt-in on/off. Run on CPU (macOS); CI runs it in `:nvidia: (L4) MoE Kernels`. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py -v ``` | Source | FP16, no opt-in | BF16, no opt-in | FP16, opt-in | BF16, opt-in | |---|---|---|---|---| | `main` (`1ab4476ac9`) | **FAILED** | pass

title: [Model][Quantization] Muse Spark: online FP8 routed experts (fp8_per_channel) on Hopper
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Let Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA quantize only its routed experts to FP8 at load time (`quantization="online"`, `quantization_config={"moe": "fp8_per_channel"}`), so the BF16 checkpoint fits on Hopper. Builds on the Muse Spark support in #61879. ## Claims - **New usage:** the BF16 Muse Spark Open checkpoint runs with online FP8 routed experts on Hopper. Before this PR, Muse Spark's NVIDIA path accepted only ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints. At TP16 the BF16 experts are about 93 GiB per GPU and do not fit an 80 GB H100. - **Routed experts:** this PR validates FP8 for the routed experts only, with attention, dense layers, the router and `lm_head` in BF16. `linear` and `targets` are accepted as for other models, but the linear path is not validated on Muse Spark. The experts accept only `fp8_per_channel`, and `ignore` can keep individual expert layers in BF16. - **Generic online path:** loading, quantization and layerwise reload are the stock `Fp8PtpcOnlineMoEMethod` ones. title: [ROCm][gfx1250] Kimi-K3: run the W_UK/W_UV bmms and the latent up-pro…
summary: …jection on aiter Gluon GEMMs On gfx1250 three Kimi-K3 bf16 GEMMs still go to hipBLASLt because they call torch directly instead of the linear-layer dispatch: - W_UK absorb and W_UV up-projection in MLA decode (torch.bmm). title: [Distributed][MoonEP] Sharded symmetric-memory expert weights and MoonEP release pin
summary: ## Purpose Sharded symmetric-memory expert weight ownership for the MoonEP backend (RFC #52095 item 5), together with the MoonEP build/commit pin in `tools/ep_kernels` (RFC item 2, supersedes #54147). MoonEP's 2026-09-26 public release (MoonshotAI/MoonEP@33327eb) replaced the weight contract that #52101 was written against. The replicated `[E+B, ...]` full-weight tensors and the `B` prefetch-slot count are gone. `prefetch_weight` now takes each projection as this rank's local experts `[epn, ...]` (`epn = E / R`) plus an all-rank symmetric prefetch pool `[R, epn, ...]`, and the expert GEMM consumes a compact `[2 * epn]` view: the local experts followed by this rank's prefetch slice. `cu_seqlens` is `[2 * epn]` accordingly. This is exactly the sharded ownership the RFC scheduled as a follow-up, so this PR does the API migration and the memory fix in one step. What changes: - `MoonEPExpertWeightPools` (owned by `MoonEPAll2AllManager`): one process-global VMM prefetch pool per projection, created collectively on first use and shared by every MoE layer, so the extra memory per rank is `epn` expert weights per projection in total rather than per layer. At load time each layer's local experts are copied into a VMM chunk that is mapped right in front of this rank's prefetch chunk, which yields the contiguous `[2 * epn, ...]` compute view `torch._grouped_mm` needs with no per-layer prefetch copies and no replication. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Lets a streaming-input session run past `max_model_len` on sliding-window RoPE models, behind `--enable-unbounded-streaming-input`. Experimental, off by default. Builds on #45022 (merged, in v0.32.0). Updated 2026-11-10: merged main. #63373 removed the V1 model runner, so its hook and test cases are gone; the V2 hook is unchanged. #63231 made 64 the default block size, which makes the Voxtral KV block 512 tokens: the parity test pins `block_size=16` and the docs give the figures for both sizes. It ran the live captions of Wikimania 2026 on one L40S at `--max-model-len 8192`, where a session would otherwise stop after 11 min: 6 concurrent streams translated into 5 languages, multi-hour sessions, all week. A throughput bench on the same card, without translation, kept up in real time with 17 streams. ## Claims - A Voxtral realtime session no longer stops at `max_model_len`. Its KV usage stays constant, since the windows already bound it. - The shift is model-agnostic: each attention layer is rotated with its own RoPE, read from the model at startup. title: [Perf][MoE] Skip grouped_topk group selection when every group is selected
summary: ## Purpose `grouped_topk` builds and applies a group mask even when `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, where the mask is all ones and the work is a no-op; this skips it. title: [Core] Add max_async_kv_loads_per_step to cap new async KV loads per step
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds `--max-async-kv-loads-per-step` (default `None`), which limits how many async KV loads one `schedule()` may start. #65319 (merged) bounds how many loads are held at once; this bounds how fast they start. The two solve different problems on a DP decode instance, where every rank waits for the slowest rank's step. Tested at `f3cd063ede` (main at `226104db52`, 2026-11-04). The limit shares its gate with the in-flight cap. Following review, async-load requests wait in `async_kv_waiting` whenever either limit is set, so a limited load no longer holds back local requests (fix from @ivanium). The option is marked experimental. ## Claims - **Hard bound per step.** With the cap alone, one step can start up to `cap - held` loads. On one real `schedule()` with 140K-token requests, that is 42.7 ms at cap 16 and 174.3 ms at cap 64, against 5.8 ms at cap 64 with a limit of 2. - **No cap value does both jobs.** The cap must exceed rate x load time or requests fall behind. At the highest load tested, caps 16 and 32 wait 20 s and 8 s, while caps of 64 and above keep up and still start 32 loads in one step. - **The limit fixes that without falling behind.** In the same high-load case, the slowest rank's `schedule()` goes from 28.7 / 48.2 ms (mean / p99) at cap 64 to 14.6 / 14.6 ms at limit 4 and 9.0 / 9.0 ms at limit 2, while the wait before a load starts goes from 0.05 s to 0.07 s and 0.17 s. - **The limit has its own range.** It must stay above the arrival rate and at or below the typical burst. title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Avoid unused index caches in MiniMax-M3 sharing layers
summary: ## Overview Avoid allocating an unused index-key cache for MiniMax-M3 layers that reuse top-k indices on ROCm. This fixes resource registration for the existing opt-in sharing mode introduced in #47269. ## Claims - Layers that reuse top-k indices no longer construct an indexer or register its side cache, except on the NVFP4 K/V path, where fused cache insertion still requires it. Main K/V caches, trained parameters and the sharing policy are unchanged. - Default settings and `index_topk_freq=1` retain the existing behavior. This is a cache-capacity fix, not a throughput claim. ## Validation MI355X base/head validation reproduced the four unwanted cache registrations and confirmed their removal, with matching lifecycle outputs and BF16 eager generation results. The recorded runs below used BF16 main K/V on 2026-10-30: base `dbd49af222355`, head `eab3ee8b05a2`. title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Avoid runtime JIT for offset combine_topk_swa_indices inputs
summary: ## Purpose The chunked sparse prefill passes `query_start_loc`, `seq_lens` and `gather_lens` to `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` as views at `num_decodes` and `chunk_start` offsets, so each of these int32 pointers lands on any 4-byte offset. Triton specializes on that alignment, and the three warmed alignment variants miss reachable combinations: every DeepSeek-V4.1 server compiles the kernel 6 more times during serving (2 alignments x 3 compress ratios), and the JIT monitor reports `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` once multi-request prefills arrive. Each program reads one value from these tensors, so their alignment does not enable vectorized loads. Stop specializing on it (`do_not_specialize`, as #57667 does for `end_ptr`) and warm only the `topk_indices` alignments. This drops the warmup from 3 to 2 variants per compress ratio. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_deepseek_v41_combine_topk_swa_warmup.py pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/cache_utils.py \ tests/kernels/attention/test_deepseek_v41_combine_topk_swa_warmup.py ``` The test warms the kernel, then calls `combine_topk_swa_indices` for compress ratios 0/1/2 with the offset views the chunked prefill passes (`num_decodes = chunk_start = 1`: `query_start_loc` and ROCm's `seq_lens` at offset 2, `gather_lens` at offset 1) under a Triton post-compile hook, and asserts nothing compiles. title: [RFC]: Improving MooncakeConnector
summary: # [RFC]: Improving MooncakeConnector MooncakeConnector is the built-in P/D disaggregation KV direct-transfer connector in vLLM. Its underlying Mooncake TransferEngine supports pluggable transports (RDMA/TCP/Ascend direct, etc.), making it **the primary path for P/D disaggregation on non-CUDA platforms**. Its engineering quality directly determines the usability of P/D disaggregation on those platforms. There are currently 20+ open issues in the vLLM repo pointing directly at MooncakeConnector, with crash/hang/leak and data-corruption reports making up the largest share. ## Motivation. <details> **Transfer and protocol** 1. **Single transfer mode**: push only — no pull path and no mode configuration; the decode side cannot pull on demand at its own scheduling pace. 2. **Redundant metadata**: the full KV region table of the decode node is rebuilt and re-sent with every request batch, and the prefill side re-aligns it every time — layout information that never changes during the engine lifetime sits on the per-request critical path. 3. **Fragile discovery**: the HTTP bootstrap server runs inside a prefill-side worker process and is affected by that process's GIL; the query side has a hard-coded timeout with no retry, the register side once blocked producer startup indefinitely, and under external DP LB all workers register as dp_rank 0. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview In MoRIIO WRITE mode with more than one decode instance (xPyD, y ≥ 2), the prefill can start writing a request's KV to a decode instance whose DP ranks are not all handshaked yet. title: [Bugfix] Surface TorchCodec video decode failures as client errors
summary: ## Purpose TorchCodec raises `RuntimeError` when decoding user-supplied video bytes fails. That exception type has no handler in the exception-handler registry (`ValueError`/`VLLMError` map to 400; raw `RuntimeError` falls through to the safety net), so the server returns **HTTP 500 with an ASGI traceback** for what is a client-input problem. The most common user-triggerable case: `seek_mode="approximate"` on a file whose container metadata overstates the decodable frame count — e.g. any stream-copied cut (`ffmpeg -c copy`). Frame sampling targets an index past the real end and torchcodec raises `Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode.` Reproduced end-to-end on a Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 server: request → 500. This PR converts `RuntimeError` from the torchcodec branch of `VideoBackend.load_bytes` to `ValueError` (chained with `from exc`), exactly mirroring the existing pattern in the `pynvvideocodec` backend (`raise ValueError("Invalid or unsupported video file.") from exc`). When `seek_mode="approximate"` is in effect, the message additionally tells the user to retry with `"exact"`: ``` HTTP 400 Failed to decode video with the torchcodec backend: Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode. This can happen with seek_mode='approximate' when the file's container metadata overstates the decodable frame count; retry with seek_mode='exact'. ``` Bundled docs: the "Video Decoding Backend" section gains operational guidance for the two TorchCodec knobs — when `num_ffmpeg_threads=0` (default) beats `1` and vice versa, with measured numbers

title: [ROCm] Run SiluAndMulWithClamp through AITER's fused clamped SwiGLU
summary: ## Purpose On ROCm, `SiluAndMulWithClamp.forward_hip` uses the `_C` `silu_and_mul_with_clamp` kernel for the default `alpha=1, beta=0` configuration, and the native implementation otherwise. The `_C` restriction exists because that kernel rounds its SiLU intermediate to the activation dtype (the precision loss MiniMax hit). With AITER enabled on gfx942 or gfx950, this PR routes the default configuration to AITER's fused clamped SwiGLU, `aiter.ops.triton.fusions.fused_clamp_act_mul`, which has been in ROCm/aiter since v0.1.27 (the version `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins). - The AITER kernel keeps clamp, SiLU and the product in FP32 and rounds only the output. - It applies only where it computes the same function: `alpha == 1`, `beta == 0`, and a half width that is a positive multiple of 128 (the kernel tiles whole 128-column rows). That width check is `rocm_aiter_ops.clamp_act_mul_supported(n_half)`, next to `clamp_act_mul`, so other callers of the kernel can share it. - Everything else keeps the current routing unchanged. That includes AITER being disabled and gfx1250, where AITER runs a separate Gluon kernel that has not been validated here. The op is registered in `_aiter_ops` like the other AITER custom ops (`rocm_aiter_clamp_act_mul`, with a fake impl), so it works under `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs. ## Accuracy and speed MI355X (gfx950), BF16 input scaled to exercise the clamp (limit 10). title: [Doc] Clarify that max_num_batched_tokens also shrinks the KV cache pool
summary: ## Purpose `docs/configuration/optimization.md` recommends raising `max_num_batched_tokens` for better TTFT, but doesn't mention that a larger startup value also enlarges the dummy batch used for startup memory profiling, which reduces the memory left for the KV cache pool (`gpu_memory_utilization` bounds weights + activation peak + KV cache together). On memory-constrained GPUs with cache-sensitive (e.g. multi-turn/agentic) workloads whose working set sits near the pool's capacity, this can erase the intended TTFT benefit: in one measurement (RTX 4090 24GB, Qwen3-8B bf16, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`), raising the startup `max_num_batched_tokens` from 2048 to 8192 shrank the KV cache pool by 10% (40,464 -> 36,720 tokens), which increased p99 TTFT by 71% (23.9s -> 40.8s) and dropped goodput from 54.7% to 46.2% on a multi-turn workload, with no change in total throughput (6062 vs 6055 tok/s). This adds a note pointing readers at the "GPU KV cache size: ... tokens" startup log line so they can check the actual pool impact before/after tuning this value. This is a documentation-only change; no code paths are modified. **Not a duplicate:** - #27951 is an RFC about memory-profiling *accuracy* in general (imbalanced MoE / CUDA graph estimation), with no proposed fix and no docs change; it doesn't cover this `max_num_batched_tokens` <-> KV-cache-pool tradeoff. - #46307 is an unrelated GB10 unified-memory OOM/host-hang bug during profiling, not a documentation gap. - Searched `gh issue list`/`gh pr list --search` across several keyword combinations (`max_num_batched_tokens kv cache

title: [Bug]: Explicit VLLM_CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE selection silently produces empty completions on SM_120
summary: ### Summary On SM_120 (RTX 5090 Laptop), serving an NVFP4 MoE checkpoint with `--moe-backend cutlass` (which resolves to `VLLM_CUTLASS`) makes the server consume the entire `max_tokens` budget and return `content: null` with `finish_reason: "length"` for certain inputs. There is no exception, no warning, and the response is HTTP 200. Switching **only** `--moe-backend` to `marlin` serves the identical requests correctly. **Severity is bounded, and I want to be upfront about it rather than have you discover it:** `--moe-backend auto` does *not* select this backend on my machine (it selects `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`), so nobody lands here by default. Reaching this state requires explicitly passing `--moe-backend cutlass`. This is a config footgun rather than silent corruption in default deployments. The checkpoint [model card](https://huggingface.co/bg-digitalservices/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4) explicitly says that `--moe-backend marlin` is required for correct MoE computation. I therefore see two possible resolutions: if `VLLM_CUTLASS` is expected to support this checkpoint layout, this is an output-correctness bug; if it is incompatible by design, vLLM should reject the explicit selection or emit a prominent startup warning rather than accept it and silently return corrupted output. It still seems worth fixing, for two reasons: the opt-in is a plausible one (see the selector note at the bottom), and once taken, the failure is invisible — a short smoke prompt passes, throughput looks normal, and a system prompt fails at 49 tokens. title: [Bug][KV Offload] EAGLE volatile-tail boundary can collapse hybrid SWA replay to zero hits
summary: ## Summary With hybrid EAGLE/MTP plus smaller sliding-window groups, CPU KV offload can restore **zero external tokens** when the EAGLE volatile-tail pop moves the shared replay boundary below the full-attention alignment boundary. ## Reproduction geometry Using the current offloading scheduler/manager path with five groups: - full attention: 256 tokens/chunk - SWA: 64 tokens/chunk - EAGLE/MTP SWA: 64 tokens/chunk - C4 SWA: 4 tokens/chunk - C128-style SWA: 8 tokens/chunk A 30,208-token prompt stores successfully. On a matching replay, the EAGLE volatile-tail pop tightens the shared boundary to 30,144 tokens. The C4 group needs chunks 7,534 and 7,535 to verify its boundary-relative window, but the ordinary per-segment store retained only the prompt-end tail at 7,550 and 7,551. Lookup then cascades through lower boundaries and returns 0 external tokens. Control: the aligned 30,272-token prompt restores 30,208 tokens correctly. This was reproduced through the real `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._build_store_jobs` -> `CPUOffloadingManager.prepare_store` / `complete_store` -> `_lookup` / manager `lookup` path, without downstream-only store modes. ## Fix concept proven in production At the prompt-final store step, compute the tightest boundary produced by EAGLE/MTP volatile-tail removal. For each non-EAGLE sliding-window group, additionally retain only the missing sliding-window tail immediately below that boundary, deduplicated against the ordinary per-segment store keys and bounded to valid/storable chunks. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> **Human note**: This PR adds copy engine option for PP handoff from one rank to the next. The copy is one-sided by nature (sender sets a flag after sending the data, receiver releases a flag once finished consuming it). Selected by `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT`: - `auto` (default): copy engines if every PP rank supports them, NCCL otherwise. title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Replay one row for prefill chunks far from the prompt end
summary: ## Overview With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end. A 124K prompt in 16K chunks now skips 7 of its 8 replay tails. The same idea is DeepSeek DeepInfer's `clip_prefix` rule. The rule isn't gated on CUDA, so it covers ROCm too. @frida-andersson tested it on 4x MI325X ([numbers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62817#issuecomment-6370899321)) and is co-author. Her #61682 does the ROCm side of this and she'll close it once this lands. ## Claims - A prefill chunk that ends at least `decoder_replay_trim_threshold + window` (768 + 128) tokens before its prompt's end replays only its last row, which reads only itself. Chunks within that reach keep the 128-row replay. - The prompt's last window is computed as before. Greedy outputs on 3 prompts of ~98.6K tokens are identical with and without this change. - No step reads replay-layer KV that a one-row chunk skipped. Every later chunk whose window still reaches back past a one-row chunk starts its replay window after it and takes the replay batch. title: [RFC]: Opt-in return of the last hidden state at sampled positions, per request (Model Runner V2)
summary: ### Motivation. A growing class of deployments puts a small trained head on top of a served model: a linear probe, a per-task classifier over a fixed label set, a calibration layer. Such a head needs two things from one forward pass: the model's scores for a few tokens, and the hidden state those scores were computed from. vLLM returns the first (logprobs, `logprob_token_ids`) but not the second. Today there are two ways to get it, and both are costly: 1. **A second engine in pooling mode** (`LLM.encode` with last-token pooling). It holds a second copy of the weights, and it runs a different runner and kernels, so its hidden state is not the one the generate engine's scores came from. In our deployment (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, FP8, RTX PRO 6000), the label readout computed from the pooling engine's state picked the same top label as the generate engine's own readout on 97.3% of 150 Banking77 items (100% of 100 CLINC items), with a median largest probability difference of 0.016. 2. **A model class that overwrites reserved logit columns with the hidden state**, read back through `allowed_token_ids` and logprobs (`h_j = lp_j - lp_0`). It works, but it is a workaround: the sampler allows at most 1,024 ids per request, so a 2,048-dimensional state takes three requests sent one at a time (identical requests batched together are not the same forward on FP8 MoE stacks), which costs a median 113 ms per question, against 35 ms for one request that returns the labels and the state with this change (RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q). title: [Perf][MoE] Skip DP padding rows in TRT-LLM monolithic MoE with vLLM's top-k
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## 1. Why this change Under data parallelism (DP), every DP rank pads its batch to the largest batch on any rank. The FlashInfer TRT-LLM **monolithic** MoE kernels are the default on Blackwell for block-FP8 and MXFP8 checkpoints. They route from the router logits themselves, so padded rows pick experts like real tokens, and the kernel loads and computes those experts. `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` (on by default) cannot help here. It works by having vLLM's routers write expert id -1 for padded rows, and the monolithic kernels never call vLLM's routers. Padding under DP is large: - In decode steps with up to 32 rows per rank, 34-65% of rows are padding. - In mixed (prefill + decode) steps, 37-84% of rows are padding, because every rank pads to the rank running prefill. ## 2. What this PR changes Under DP, the runner routes with vLLM's top-k, where padded rows get -1, and then calls the kernel's precomputed-routing op (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`), which skips those rows. There is no new option: the existing `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns it off (its doc comment now says so). - `FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic.apply_precomputed_routing` and `supports_precomputed_routing`, implemented for TRT-LLM block FP8 and MXFP8 (`TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`). The kwargs shared with the logits call move to one helper. - `prepare_routed` for the NaiveDPEP monolithic prepare/finalize: it all-gathers top-k ids and weights instead of logits. - `MoERunner` takes the routed path under DP. - Routers that do not mask padding themselves (`masks_padding` False, e.g. groupe

title: [Bugfix][Model] Size RoPE cos/sin cache to max_model_len for unscaled RoPE
summary: ## Purpose When `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN` sets `max_model_len` above the model's native `max_position_embeddings`, the RoPE cos/sin cache is still sized from the native limit. title: [LoRA][BatchInvariant] Match an fp32-add LoRA reference: round the expand epilogue once under batch invariance
summary: Part of #66163. ### Purpose Batch-invariant mode is used to make inference reproduce another implementation's numerics exactly, for example a trainer's forward pass in RL with on-policy logprob checks. For LoRA layers, the punica expand kernel already gives deterministic, batch-invariant results. It just rounds differently from the usual training-side LoRA forward. The expand epilogue (`do_expand_kernel`, used by `lora_expand` with `add_inputs=True`) computes: ``` tiled_c = accumulator.to(bf16) # delta rounded to bf16 tiled_c += tl.load(out) # added to the base and rounded again ``` That is `bf16(bf16(delta) + base)`. A reference that computes `base + x @ A.T @ B.T` with the add in fp32 and a single cast, as training frameworks' LoRA forwards typically do, gets `bf16(delta + base)`. The two differ in the last bit wherever rounding the delta first changes the final rounding. The difference is systematic, on every LoRA layer, so a batch-invariant engine cannot match such a trainer bitwise. For example, the zero-mismatch RL recipe for Kimi K3.1 ([Inferact/zero-mismatch-rl](https://github.com/Inferact/zero-mismatch-rl), branch `vllm/kimi-k3.1`, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/k31_bi_gemm.py` `lora_f32add`) gets this single rounding with a model-specific GEMM epilogue that bypasses the punica ops. This PR makes it available in vLLM's general LoRA path. To be clear about scope, this PR is not a determinism or batch-invariance fix. The current kernel is already deterministic and batch-invariant. title: [6/N] HiSparse: support direct GPU landing for P/D transfers
summary: ## Why HiSparse P/D imports always land in the host tier today. That costs a host round trip even when the decoder has room to keep the whole prefix on GPU. This PR lands a NIXL import directly in resident GPU pages when it fits, and falls back to the host tier otherwise. ## Design - **Landing choice:** `HiSparseCoordinator` tries GPU landing first. If that admission fails, the retry uses the host tier and keeps it. There is no length threshold, and the generic KV cache manager is unaware of the choice. - **NIXL alias regions:** NIXL registers each source layer's resident pages as a local-only *alias region* of that layer's host source region. Aliases are not advertised in the handshake. - A GPU import sends its resident blocks as `ReqMeta.alias_block_ids`. The existing region-mapped pull then writes those regions into their aliases, and the mixed DRAM/VRAM split still applies. - A host import is unchanged from `main`. - **Review follow-up:** this replaces `HiSparseNixlDestination`, which re-implemented NIXL's host registration, descriptor mapping and read submission ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#pullrequestreview-5190836165)). NIXL no longer has a second host path, and it has no HiSparse logic: it sees a generic `KVImportLanding` hook (HiSparse's is `vllm/v1/hisparse/landing.py`) and the generic `KVCacheConfig.transfer_aliases` layer map. - **Not supported with aliases** (each raises `NotImplementedError`): host staging buffers, Mamba, layer-name routing, kernel block size ≠ logical block size, DCP, and more than one source rank. ## Validation C

title: [Engine Core][LoRA] Report loaded LoRA adapters to frontends and Prometheus
summary: Reports which LoRA adapters each engine holds, and how long loads take, to the frontends and Prometheus, so LoRA-aware routers (llm-d-router#2792) can send a request to a replica that already has its adapter. Workers snapshot their adapter caches as a `LoRALoadEvent` (GPU, CPU and pinned adapters, ranks, load/activate times since the last snapshot). No RPC is added: the snapshot rides on replies the engine core already waits for. - **Steps:** the output rank sets `ModelRunnerOutput.lora_load_event`. The first commit activates adapters in id order, so every rank holds the same caches and one rank's reply is enough. - **`add_lora` / `remove_lora` / `pin_lora`:** each rank returns its snapshot with the result (`WorkerBase.run_lora_rpc`, which wraps the existing methods, so out-of-tree workers keep working) and the executor keeps the output rank's. An idle engine reports changes without waiting for a step. - **Batch queue** (async scheduling, PP): steps still queued during an adapter RPC took their snapshots before it, so the engine core sends only their timings, with the RPC's adapters. - **Several API servers:** every API server gets the adapters; only client 0 gets the timings, so each load is counted once in the shared registry. Each server serves `vllm:lora_adapter_loaded` from its own state, because a multiprocess registry cannot remove an evicted adapter's series. title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip the seq_lens D2H sync in the AITER sparse MLA metadata key
summary: ## Purpose This is the ROCm counterpart of #58684, which has the background. On every build of `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with persistent metadata (the default for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x sparse MLA), `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` runs, decode steps included. That is a blocking D2H copy, and under async scheduling it stalls the CPU until the GPU catches up. The copy only feeds the cache key that decides whether to re-run `get_mla_metadata_v1`, which was added in #42982. The metadata itself is already built on device from `paged_kv_indptr`. The key only looks at seq_lens and context lens clamped to `index_topk`, so exact values usually aren't needed. This PR builds the key from `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` whenever that gives the same key: - **No spec decode:** the upper bound is exact, so it's always used. - **Spec decode:** the bound can overshoot by up to `num_speculative_tokens`. It's used once every request's `context_ub - num_speculative_tokens >= index_topk`. Past that point both lens clamp to `index_topk`, so the key is identical to the exact one. That's the steady state for long-context decode, the same regime #42982 targeted. - **Otherwise:** it falls back to the current D2H copy. Unlike #58684, no device fixup is needed, since AITER already plans on device. Not changed here: - The `synchronize()` after a metadata recompute (#47404) is untouched. summary: ## Overview Fixes a GPU memory fault in EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding with async scheduling: the drafter's backup next-token ids live in one pinned host buffer that the CPU refills for step N+1 before step N's non-blocking upload has run, so the drafter can embed the async-scheduling placeholder `-1`. title: [RL][Model Loader] Load plan: stacked (transformers v5) routed experts as per-expert views
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item L1). Builds on #65235 (P1, load plan), now merged. Hub checkpoints store routed experts per expert (`experts.E.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight`). transformers v5 models hold them stacked: `experts.gate_up_proj` `[E, 2I, H]` (gate rows, then up rows) and `experts.down_proj` `[E, H, I]`, under the checkpoint's own module paths. This PR lets a trainer send that stacked form (for example, one built on v5 models) without converting it to per-expert names. Today many MoE models only load the per-expert form: the ~50 model and MTP files that hand-roll a `make_expert_params_mapping` loop only match per-expert names. A small wrapper turns each stacked tensor into per-expert views under the per-expert names and feeds them to the model's unchanged `load_weights`. The bake traces each per-expert copy back to a box of the stacked tensor and merges them into one write per run of local experts, so a stacked name is direct with a single destination, like a per-expert name. **The split is a bridge.** #48972 moves every model's `load_weights` onto `AutoWeightsLoader`, so routed experts load through `MoERunner.load_weights` → `RoutedExperts.load_weights`, whose fused mapping already takes 3-D stacked tensors (#65904 does this for MiniMax-M3). title: [ROCm][BatchInvariant] Add gfx950 tuned tile table for the persistent matmul
summary: Part of #66163 (BI matmul: gfx950 tile table for `batch_invariant`). ### Purpose With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on ROCm, every BF16 `mm`/`addmm`/`matmul`/`linear` goes through `matmul_persistent`. Today the tuned-config table is only resolved on CUDA, so on gfx950 (MI355X) every call uses the default 128x128x64 tile. At decode-sized M, most of each 128-row tile is padding, and the persistent grid launches only `cdiv(M, 128) * cdiv(N, 128)` programs. Large-K shapes are then limited by how fast those few CUs can stream the weight. M > 256 (prefill) keeps the default: the last bucket of every shape is `128x128, nw8, st3`. There is no new flag. title: [Kernel] Allow steering the unquantized linear backend independently
summary: ## Purpose `--linear-backend` is consumed by two selectors: the quantized kernel picker in `model_executor/kernels/linear`, and `dispatch_unquantized_gemm` for unquantized layers. Setting it to reach the second also redirects the first, which on a mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint was a net loss in our measurements even though the unquantized layers themselves improved. ## Changes Adds `--unquantized-linear-backend` / `KernelConfig.unquantized_linear_backend`, which overrides the backend for `UnquantizedLinearMethod` only. Defaults to `"auto"`, which applies `linear_backend` as before — no behavior change unless the new flag is set. This is separate from (and complements) `linear_backend_per_quant`, which overrides backend selection for the *quantized* kernel picker keyed by quantization scheme. That mechanism doesn't reach `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, since unquantized layers don't go through `select_linear_kernel`/`QuantKey` scheme lookup. ## Test plan - `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('vllm/config/kernel.py').read())"` and same for `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py` — all parse cleanly. - Default behavior verified unchanged: `unquantized_linear_backend` defaults to `"auto"`, in which case `UnquantizedLinearMethod` falls back to `linear_backend` exactly as before this change. ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and this description.

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add fused MoE FP8 config for DeepSeek-V2-Lite on RTX 5090
summary: ## Overview Add a tuned Triton fused MoE config for `E=64,N=1408` with FP8 W8A8 on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (SM120). This is the MoE shape of DeepSeek-V2-Lite / DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite at TP=1. There are currently no fused MoE config files for the RTX 5090 on `main` (see #48732), so this shape falls back to `get_default_config()`. Config-only change: no code or numerics changes. ## Claims - Kernel level: tuned matches default up to M=64 (within ±1%). It's 2–5% faster at M=96–1024 and 7–19% faster at M=1536–4096 (largest at M=1536: 829 → 700 µs). - End to end, on the workloads below, the change is neutral: within ±1.1%. Decode at these batch sizes is memory-bandwidth-bound, so the default config is already close to optimal there. - M=1 deliberately keeps the default config (see Details). - No accuracy change: GSM8K 0.783 tuned vs 0.776 default. ## Validation Environment: RTX 5090 (driver 610.57.04), torch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, `nm-testing/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` (FP8 channel-wise weights, dynamic per-token activations). GPU temperature, clocks and throttle reasons were logged during every run (max 65 °C, no thermal throttling), and no other GPU jobs ran concurrently. **Kernel time.** The tuner's winner and `get_default_config()` were re-timed back to back in the same process for each M, with 100 iterations of CUDA-graph replays (10 calls each): | M | Default (µs) | Tuned (µs) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 24.2 | 24.2 (default kept) | 1.000× | | 2 | 45.9 | 44.3 | 1.034× | | 4 | 127.3 | 128.4 | 0.992× | | 8 | 201.9 | 200.4 | 1.008× | | 16 | 2

title: [DCP] Add FlashInfer fused A2A backend for decode context parallelism
summary: ## Summary Adds FlashInfer's fused MNNVL all-to-all (LL128) kernel as an alternative backend for the DCP **a2a-reduce** exchange, on top of the merged packed-NCCL a2a path (`--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, #41160). The kernel replaces the two `dist.all_to_all_single` exchanges of the packed path with a single fused `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall`. The backend defaults to **automatic selection by hardware** (`--dcp-a2a-backend auto`), with an opt-in override: - **Blackwell (sm_100+)** → FlashInfer fused LL128 A2A (captured under CUDA graph, where it beats the NCCL pack → `all_to_all` → unpack chain). - **Everything else** → NCCL packed (unchanged behavior). In eager / non-Blackwell, FlashInfer's per-call overhead makes it ~3–5% slower, so it is not used there. - **`--dcp-a2a-backend {auto,nccl,flashinfer}`** (default `auto`) lets users force the kernel. `nccl`/`flashinfer` override the auto choice; forced `flashinfer` still falls back to NCCL if the MNNVL workspace can't initialize (never crashes). Ignored unless `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`. The FlashInfer MNNVL workspace is allocated lazily the first time an attention backend selects the A2A combine path (before CUDA-graph capture); if that fails (no NVL fabric / IMEX, e.g. non-NVL72 cross-node) it logs a warning and **falls back to NCCL packed** — no user action, no crash. **Files (7 changed):** - `vllm/distributed/dcp_alltoall_flashinfer.py` (new): MNNVL workspace manager (alloc + init + CPU barrier; `enable_pdl=False` to match TRT-LLM), cached per CP group. - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp_alltoall.py`: dispatcher routes `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce`

title: [HiSparse] Alternative to #55398: land P/D imports in resident pages through a generic transfer view
summary: Second alternative to #55398 (see also #65888): NIXL lands HiSparse P/D imports straight in resident GPU pages, with no HiSparse-specific NIXL code. HiSparse makes its resident pages the transfer target of its sparse MLA layers. Two new generic `KVCacheGroupSpec` fields, `transfer_layer_names` and `transfer_kv_cache_spec`, say how the peer knows those layers. Imported pages are written back to the host tier like a locally computed prefix. The NIXL changes are generic. Each group's pull starts after the blocks already covered locally (null blocks included), and a group that transfers under other names keeps its own regions. The NIXL and KV-cache unit tests pass. Some HiSparse unit tests still assert host landing and are not updated yet. Imports now need GPU room for the whole prompt; there is no host fallback. **Results.** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 1P1D on 2×GB300 nodes (TP4 each). The decoder runs `MultiConnector[NixlConnector, HiSparseConnector]`, with NIXL over RDMA. All three variants ran on the same nodes. | | `main` | #55398 | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | Multi-turn 64K (8 conversations, C=8), ITL p50 | 11.34 ms | 10.46 ms | 10.35 ms | | Multi-turn TTFT p50 | 1437 ms | 1827 ms | 1970 ms | | GSM8K 5-shot: accuracy / wall time | 0.914 / 56.4 s | 0.914 / 43.4 s | 0.911 / 42.9 s | | NIXL bytes for the same imports | 1× | 3.4× | 3.4× | Needle retrieval at 8K–100K was correct in every run.

title: [Config] Hash MambaConfig in the compile cache identity
summary: ## Overview The compile cache identity built from `VllmConfig.compile_factors()` omits `mamba_config`, so two configs that differ only in Mamba settings can collapse to one AOT/compile cache key and reuse each other's compiled artifact. This folds `MambaConfig` into the cache identity. ## Claims - Bug fix: configs differing only in `mamba_config` now produce distinct compile cache hashes instead of colliding. - Covers the Mamba settings that change the compiled mixer: `backend`, `enable_stochastic_rounding`, `stochastic_rounding_philox_rounds`, `ssu_algorithm`. - No change to model behavior; only the cache identity is corrected. ## Validation Current head: `3969258ed91fc0315eecc1fbd9295393537f5a8a`, merged with upstream/main `d1879210a4b10773d22a2a659152beca0d35d007`. title: [Bugfix][Model] Make Glm5NextMoE.forward rank-agnostic
summary: ## Purpose `Glm5NextMoE.forward` starts with: ```python num_tokens, hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape ... return final_hidden_states.view(num_tokens, hidden_dim) ``` which only works for the rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` layout. Model runners that pass bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` in every MoE layer. The fix flattens on the way in and restores the caller's leading dims on the way out. It deliberately does not broadcast: `sequence_parallel_chunk`, `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` and the `[:num_tokens]` slice inside the block all require tokens to live on dim 0. The flatten sits before the MegaMoE branch added in #60895, whose `fused_topk_bias` also unpacks a rank-2 size (`M, _ = hidden_states.size()`), so both paths are covered. No-op for rank-2 input. Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2. ## Test Plan `tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py`, CPU-only, no model weights needed. Exercises the block's shape contract for rank-2 and rank-3 input: the experts must see a rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` view, and the caller must get its original shape back. The test reads `Glm5NextMoE.forward` via `inspect.getsource` and asserts the flattening is present, so it tracks the implementation instead of silently drifting from a copy. ```bash pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py ``` ## Test Result With the fix: ``` 3 passed ``` Against the unpatched code the same tests fail. title: [Quant] LUT-B MoE with MXFP8 activations: native Rubin kernel + emulation
summary: <!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"mgoin"} --> ## Overview Adds `--quantization lut_b_moe`: online LUT-B quantization of routed MoE experts with MXFP8 activations. On Rubin (SM 10.7) it runs a new native grouped GEMM built on `tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.decompress::lut::b`; every other GPU emulates the same numerics so accuracy can be checked without Rubin hardware. This reworks #51880 on current main. That PR emulated LUT-B weights with BF16 activations, which Rubin cannot run natively (the LUT-B tensor core forms only take FP8/FP6/FP4 A), and it needed a fused Triton decode GEMM plus a dequantize fallback. This PR replaces it; #51880 can be closed. No other open PR touches LUT-B. ## Claims - New `lut_b_moe` online scheme (MoE only, dense layers unquantized): 3-bit indices into an E4M3 codebook plus a UE8M0 exponent per 8x64 weight tile (3.14 bits/weight logical), MXFP8 activations (E4M3, UE8M0 per 1x32). - Native Rubin path (`LutBSm107Experts` + `ops.lut_b_moe_gemm`): weights stay packed in memory and are decoded by the tensor core (`UTCQMMA.LUTB` in SASS). A deliberately simple kernel, not tuned for peak throughput. - Emulation path (`LutBEmulationTritonExperts`): dequantize weights once at load, MXFP8 quantize-dequantize activations before each GEMM, run the existing BF16 `TritonExperts`. Selected automatically off Rubin, or with `--moe-backend emulation`. - GLM-4.7-Flash on Rubin: GSM8K for native (0.839) and emulated (0.843) LUT-B agree within one standard error and sit about 1.5 points below BF16 (0.857). title: [Bugfix] Re-probe the tier for new requests instead of reusing a cached miss in tiering AsyncLookupManager
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61658. In KV offload tiering, `AsyncLookupManager` gave a resolved "absent" verdict to every later request for that key, as long as any request still held the key. On a shared tier (fs `root_dir`, obj), this meant the instance missed blocks that another instance wrote after the first probe. With this change, a new request that finds a cached miss starts a fresh probe. Requests that already have a verdict keep it. ## Claims - A new request no longer inherits a resolved miss. It probes the tier again. This fixes the fs tier (`FsAsyncLookupManager`) and the obj tier (`ObjAsyncLookupManager`), which both use this class. - Present verdicts, pending probes and in-flight probes are still shared across requests. Several new requests in one step share one new probe. - A request keeps the verdict it already got. This includes a `mark_miss` after a failed load, so the failed-load livelock [#49176](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49176) does not come back. - New test: `test_new_request_reprobes_cached_miss`, with two cases (the miss came from a probe, or from `mark_miss`). ## Validation Reproducer from the issue. title: [Core] Simplify `prefill_schedule_interval` outside data parallelism
summary: #54627 applied `prefill_schedule_interval` to non-DP engines with a separate gate and timing state in the scheduler. Replace that with the mechanism DP already uses: the engine core computes the cadence and passes it to `schedule()` as `throttle_prefills`. The base EngineCore now uses `num_executed_steps % N`, while `DPEngineCoreProc` keeps its override that is aligned across ranks. Empty `schedule()` calls don't advance the counter, so they can't expire the hold early. Non-DP engines don't run dummy batches, unlike DP ranks, where every loop iteration is a forward pass. This changes behaviour: the interval now follows a fixed grid instead of being measured from the last prefill step, so a prefill arriving after a decode-only stretch can wait up to N-1 executed steps. As a separate cleanup, this also moves `_checkpoint_state`, `_checkpoint_error` and `_kv_cache_reclaimable` from class attributes into `EngineCore.__init__`. They were only initialized at class level so that tests could build an `EngineCore` with `object.__new__`, even though production code relies on them; the tests that reach them now set them explicitly.

title: [Performance]: DFlash drafts the full block under dynamic speculative decoding, so a small runtime K still pays max-K drafter cost
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance Ideally the dynamic schedule matches the best static K at each concurrency. With `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`, a dense DFlash2 setup on H100 gets most of the way back from the large-batch slowdown, but it still trails static K=3 at concurrency 64 and static K=1 at concurrency 128. The gap is the drafter: `DFlashSpeculator.propose` always runs the full `num_speculative_tokens + 1` query block. The runtime K only changes how many tokens the target verifies. The only special case is K=0, which skips the query pass (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`, `if num_speculative_tokens == 0`). **Proposal:** when the runtime K is smaller than the configured maximum, run the DFlash query pass with `K + 1` positions per request. This means capturing FULL graphs per query width (the schedule only uses a few widths) and passing that width to `prepare_dflash_inputs` and the attention metadata build. This is complementary to #52559. That PR picks K adaptively, and its docs say that lowering a nonzero K "reduces target verification work but not draft-model work". This proposal reduces the draft work for any K-selection policy, including the existing static schedule. #### Measurements - Target: Qwen/Qwen3-8B. Draft: RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.dflash2 (DFlash2, block size 8, 5 sliding-window layers). - 1x H100 80GB, MRV2, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, FlashInfer kernels installed. - Workload: `vllm bench serve` on `philschmid/mt-bench`, 512 output tokens, temperature 0, prefix caching off, `max_num_seqs=128`. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Propagate dictionary hf-overrides to speculative draft models
summary: ## What this PR does Ensures dictionary-based `--hf-overrides` (e.g. CLI JSON for YaRN RoPE scaling) are recursively merged into speculative **draft** model configs. `SpeculativeConfig.compose_draft_hf_overrides` only handled the *callable* form of `target_hf_overrides`. When `--hf-overrides` is passed as JSON via the CLI (the common case), the parsed dict was silently dropped for the draft model — so the draft keeps the native RoPE/context config while the target runs with scaled positions. **Before:** draft model ignores dict `--hf-overrides` → RoPE scaling (e.g. `yarn`, `factor`, `mrope_section`) never reaches the draft → context-length mismatch and illegal memory access when serving past the draft's native window. **After:** dict overrides are recursively merged into the draft config, matching the callable path's behavior. ## Why we need it Repro: ```bash vllm serve <model> \ --hf-overrides '{"rope_parameters":{"rope_type":"yarn","factor":2.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":262144}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \ --max-model-len 418000 ``` Without this fix the MTP draft runs at native (unscaled) RoPE and fails/degrades past the native window. ## Test Plan - New unit tests: `tests/config/test_speculative_dict_hf_overrides.py` (dict merge, nested merge, callable-path regression) - Hardware validation: DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8 Flash Next + MTP (K=5) at 418K YaRN context (524K window) ## Test Result - 96.9–99.2% spec-decode acceptance across the full 524K window (was failing/degrading without the fix) - 30-stage enterprise eval s

title: [Perf] Warm up JIT kernels that only long prefills, eager drafters and constrained decoding reach
summary: ## Overview Warm up JIT kernels that are currently compiled lazily, on live traffic: the FA4 MLA split-KV combine, the DCP all-to-all fallback pack/unpack kernels, and Triton MLA decode for eager-only (e.g. draft) layers. title: [Security] Drop NixlPush WRITEs after the producer request ends
summary: ## Summary When `NixlPushConnector` waits on a P→D handshake, the completion callback captured the original logical block ids and later submitted a WRITE even if `get_finished` had already reported the producer request done (lease expiry or completed push). Those source blocks can already belong to another request, so the still-live decode request can generate from the wrong KV while the API returns HTTP 200. This change marks finished/expired requests abandoned on the engine thread and refuses the WRITE at the handshake callback, the deferred-inbox drain, and the transfer sink. A follow-up on the same branch closes two remaining holes: abandoned ids with an in-flight handshake callback are not forgotten after the 300s tombstone TTL, and dropping the WRITE notifies decode (`PUSH_FAIL`) so the request fails instead of waiting out the lease. This is not a duplicate of open NixlPush work: #50754 reports NIXL WRITEs that failed to post, and #54757 hardens the handshake listener. Neither invalidates a deferred WRITE after the producer lease ends. title: [Security] Skip target-only sampling observations in the acceptance estimator
summary: ## Summary When adaptive verification uses the online acceptance estimator, draft sampling copies only temperature and seed. Request-specific transforms such as `allowed_token_ids`, penalties, and `bad_words` are applied on the target but not on the draft, so accept/reject labels from those requests were pooled into worker-wide estimator coefficients used to size verification for later unrelated requests. This change drops those observations from estimator updates. Requests without those transforms still train the estimator as before. ## Changes - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py`: add `target_only_sampling_transforms()` for the draft-ignored sampling fields. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py`: drop masked rows before `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator.step`. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: pass the mask from the sampler into `observe_verification`. ## Codepath coverage - All OpenAI-compatible and SageMaker/gRPC inference entry points reach this sink through `GPUModelRunner` → `DraftModelSpeculator.observe_verification`. The skip is applied at that sink. - DSpark with a confidence head does not construct the estimator (`acceptance_estimator is None`), so it is unchanged. - Offline `LLM.generate` uses the same worker path. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open/merged PRs for "acceptance estimator", "adaptive verification", "observe_verification", and "draft sampling parameters". - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56724 applies draft-side top-k/top-p for acceptance rate; it does not isolate estimator updates and does not cover `allowed_token_ids`.

title: [Security] Bound unread engine output queued per request
summary: ## Summary The Rust frontend buffers each request's engine outputs in an unbounded channel and the dispatcher `send`s without waiting for the HTTP consumer. title: [Bug]: MoE w2_bias is added tp_size times under tensor parallelism
summary: ### Your current environment vLLM 0.32.0 (release CPU wheel), PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, fp32, gloo between processes. The affected code is unchanged on main (40837c5d0e). ### 🐛 Describe the bug `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` copies the full checkpoint `w2_bias` onto every TP rank. Its `"bias" in weight_name` / `shard_id == "w2"` branch has no `tp_rank` handling, while `w13_bias` right below it is sharded through `_load_w13`. `w2` is row-parallel: each rank adds the bias to its partial output and `MoERunner` all-reduces afterwards, so the output carries `tp_size × w2_bias` instead of `w2_bias`. gpt-oss is not affected, because its own loader zeroes `w2_bias` on `tp_rank != 0`. The generic loader is used by the Transformers modelling backend, which sets `has_bias=True` when the HF experts module has a bias (per-expert `ModuleList` experts).
