title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Name the layer when a MoE expert weight is unquantized
summary: ## Purpose A ModelOpt checkpoint can store a MoE submodule unquantized while leaving it out of the quantization exclude list. The layer is then built for packed low-precision weights and the weight loader is handed a floating point tensor of the logical width, so the load dies inside `Tensor.copy_` with a message that names neither the layer nor the cause: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` The two numbers differ by exactly 2, which is the FP4 packing factor, but it reads like a tensor-parallel sharding bug. The ratio is identical at every TP size, so the obvious experiment (change `--tensor-parallel-size`) costs a full model load and proves nothing. The traceback ends in a generic loader and names no module, so there is nothing to grep for. This PR raises a targeted error instead. The check only fires where `copy_` would already fail, so no configuration that loads today changes behaviour. ### The checkpoint that prompted it `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` has `num_hidden_layers: 45` and `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, so layer 45 is the MTP layer. Reading the safetensors headers, layer 45 is unquantized and layer 44 is not: | tensor | layer 44 | layer 45 | | --- | --- | --- | | `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight` | `U8 (2048, 2048)` | `BF16 (2048, 4096)` | | `mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight_scale` | `F8_E4M3 (2048, 256)` | absent | | whole-layer dtypes | 864 `U8` + 864 `F8_E4M3` | 888 `BF16` + 1 `F32` | `quantization_config.ignore` has 132 entries covering layers 0 to 44 and nothing matching layer 45

title: [Security] Drop leftover NIXL empty-recv metadata
summary: ## Summary When a decode-side request is rejected before scheduling, NIXL still enqueues an empty recv so the prefiller can be released. The push worker stored that recv in `_recving_metadata` even though no WRITE will ever complete, so `get_finished` never popped the entry and the dict grew without bound. title: Fix unbounded series accumulation in vllm:lora_requests_info
summary: ## vllm:lora_requests_info leaks a series per observed adapter-set state I run 8×TP2 pods serving 200 LoRA adapters and noticed the llm-d router (the downstream metrics consumer) intermittently dropping healthy pods from its scheduling pool during benchmarks. Chasing that led here. The gauge encodes the current running/waiting adapter sets in its *labels*: ```python self.gauge_lora_info.labels(**lora_info_labels).set_to_current_time() ``` prometheus_client keeps every distinct label combination exposed forever, and nothing ever removes the previous child. So every time a request starts or finishes and the in-flight set changes, that exact (running, waiting) pair becomes a permanent series in /metrics. With 200 adapters the churn is combinatorial. From the Prometheus data I collected during a 5 minute benchmark on v0.31.0: ``` t= 0s: 1 series t= 60s: 291 series t= 140s: 1352 series after 5 min: 4451 series # for this one gauge ``` The exposition grows until scrapes slow down enough that the router (1s refresh, 2s staleness threshold) starts considering pods stale and filters them out of the candidate set. While all 8 pods were healthy and Ready: ``` candidate sizes: {1: 26, 2: 20, 4: 15, 5: 6, 8: 24} # 91 requests ``` 74% of requests were scheduled against a shrunken pool, which is what broke the adapter-affinity routing (session bindings kept migrating as their bound pod flapped in and out). ## The fix Remember the last label values per engine and `remove()` the previous child when the set changes, so the exposition holds only the current state. title: [Perf][Sampling] Use FlashInfer top-k selection for top-k/top-p masking
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview This PR masks top-k/top-p logits with FlashInfer's top-k selection instead of the Triton kernel, whenever every row of the batch has an active top-k ≤ 256. FlashInfer selects the `top_k_max` largest logits per row, and a small Triton kernel orders those candidates, cuts them at each row's k and p, and scatters them back into the logits. On B300 the masking op is 58% faster on average than the Triton kernel (21% to 89%, in all 160 cases of `benchmarks/benchmark_topk_topp.py`). - **Where it runs:** MRV2's `apply_top_k_top_p` callers that need dense masked logits: speculative verification, and sampling that doesn't take the fused FlashInfer sampler (processed logprobs, per-request seeds, mixed greedy batches, watermarking). - **Eligible batches:** vocab ≥ 65536 and `1 <= top_k_min <= top_k_max <= 256` on every row. Everything else (top-p-only rows, k > 256, MRV1, CPU, XPU) keeps the Triton kernel. - **Output:** exactly k tokens by logit, then the smallest prefix whose mass reaches p, with ties broken by the lowest index at both cutoffs. ## Claims - **Kernel speed, B300:** ≥10% faster than the Triton kernel in every pass of all 160 cases (top-k 20 and 100, with and without top-p, V65536 to V248320, batch 1 to 2048). title: fix(mooncake): reject duplicate transfer_id to prevent KV-cache leak
summary: A client-controlled transfer_id reused across multiple do_remote_decode requests caused metadata overwrites in the producer's reqs_need_send dictionary. title: [Feature][Whisper] Native word-level timestamps (cross-attention + DTW)
summary: Whisper accepts `timestamp_granularities[]=word` today, but `words` always comes back `null`. This fills it in. ```bash vllm serve openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo --enable-word-timestamps curl localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F file=@mary_had_lamb.ogg -F model=openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo \ -F response_format=verbose_json -F 'timestamp_granularities[]=word' ``` **Before** ```json { "text": " The first words I spoke in the original phonograph...", "words": null } ``` **After** ```json { "text": " The first words I spoke in the original phonograph...", "words": [ {"word": "The", "start": 0.52, "end": 0.88}, {"word": "first", "start": 0.88, "end": 1.60}, {"word": "words", "start": 1.60, "end": 2.02}, {"word": "I", "start": 2.02, "end": 2.26}, {"word": "spoke", "start": 2.26, "end": 2.66} ] } ``` Off by default; nothing runs without `--enable-word-timestamps`. ## How Whisper never emits word boundaries as tokens — they live in the decoder's cross-attention. Instead of asking a fused backend for its attention probabilities, this records **Q** (and the encoder **K** at prefill) just before the fused call, then recomputes `softmax(Q·Kᵀ)` for the `alignment_heads` only, median-filters it and runs a DTW. Same method as OpenAI Whisper and WhisperX. No second model, no second forward pass, no attention-backend change, and it runs with CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` on. The recording is a registered custom op writing into static buffers, so it stays opaque to Dynamo and safe under graph replay. title: [ROCm][MoRIIO] Support PP for prefill instance in PD disaggregated serving with MoRI WRITE mode
summary: ## Overview In WRITE mode, `MoRIIOConnector` assumes one prefill rank per TP index that writes every layer. With pipeline parallelism, the index is shared for the stages, so the stages collide on ports and the later ones fail to start. Each stage also numbers its layers from zero, so a stage that does write puts them on the decode instance's first layers. This PR lets a prefill instance under MoRIIO's WRITE mode use pipeline parallelism, with each stage writing the layers it holds to the decode addresses of those same layers and a decode rank finishing the transfer only after every stage has reported. ## Claims - A prefill instance can now run with pipeline parallelism in WRITE mode. Each stage writes its own layers, and decoding starts only after every stage has reported. - For MLA models the main gain is prefill capacity. On GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (8 × MI355X), a TP1 × PP4 prefill instance holds about 4× the KV cache of a TP4 one (4.12× and 4.02×) and serves 41.9 % and 27.1 % more tokens per GPU on 32K-token prompts at 16 concurrent requests, with TTFT p50 down 42 % and 30 %. - The peer's layer addresses are now looked up by layer name. This also fixes a case without pipeline parallelism where a decode instance with an MTP layer is fed by a prefill instance without MTP. - Combinations the connector don't support fail at startup with an error that articulates the setting. ## Validation ### Unit tests The new tests added are CPU tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_pipeline_parallel.py` (21 cases, `cpu_test`), ROCm + MoRI cases in `test_moriio_connector.py` (per-st

title: [Feature]: Support simultaneous Tool Calling and Structured Output via Grammar Union / Prefix Tree
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Currently, when a request specifies both tools and a structured output constraint (response_format / guided_json), vLLM strictly enforces the structured output schema, completely suppressing the model's ability to trigger tool calls. In agentic workflows, an agent should be able to either: Call one or more registered tools to fetch external context, or Emit the final answer directly, formatted according to the user's structured JSON schema. Right now, developers are forced to make an unconstrained preliminary call (or two separate requests), wasting latency and tokens, because guided decoding cannot branch between tool calls and final structured outputs. Describe the solution you'd like Support unified guided decoding that constructs a combined search space (prefix tree / grammar union) covering both: All declared tool definitions (formatted according to the chat template / tool call format). The user-provided response_format schema (final response). Deterministic Prefix Traversal: As long as all candidates share a common prefix (e.g., identical opening syntax or delimiters), the engine follows that shared path. title: [Core] Count KV connector hits in cache-aware admission

title: [Performance]: Hybrid models with prefix caching prefill chunks above the default cudagraph capture ceiling eagerly
summary: ### Summary Serving a Qwen3.5-MoE fine-tune (40 layers, 30 GDN linear-attention + 10 full attention) on one B200 I chased a flat prefill penalty that showed up for every cold prompt above ~1.1k tokens: ~104 ms of engine prefill regardless of size, from 1.2k to 5.7k tokens, while prompts under the threshold prefilled in ~39 ms. It amortizes under concurrency so it is easy to misattribute to the workload. Root cause, end to end: 1. With prefix caching on, vLLM puts hybrid models in mamba cache mode "align", so prefill chunk ends are governed by mamba block boundaries (1088 tokens on this model, set from the state page size). 2. `_mamba_block_aligned_split` has an internal-checkpoint path: when every mamba group exports prefill checkpoints and the validity holds, a chunk runs to completion and the GDN kernel writes the checkpoint mid-chunk. For a fresh request the condition reduces to `cdiv(N, block) - 2 > (0-1)//block`, and with Python floor division `(0-1)//1088 = -1`, so any prompt over one block prefills as ONE chunk covering the whole prompt. I verified this at runtime with logging in the split: 1877-token prompts went through as a single chunk with `use_internal_checkpoint=True`, no multi-pass split. (Worth flagging because the floor division is easy to misread as C-style truncation, which makes it look like the split should fire.) 3. The default piecewise cudagraph capture ceiling is `2 * max_num_seqs`, capped at 512, or 1024 on Blackwell (see #60264). A chunk above the ceiling cannot replay a captured graph, so the same compiled pieces run kernel by kernel through the

title: [Bugfix][Model] Cap Voxtral Realtime transcription at audio boundary
summary: ## Purpose fix #52926. Voxtral Realtime requires decoding positions to stay aligned with audio embedding positions. At each position, the model may generate a text token, a blank token (ID 32), or EOS. For some audio inputs, the model does not generate EOS before the available audio embeddings are exhausted. Previously, offline `/v1/audio/transcriptions` used the generic request or model context length as the generation limit. title: [Performance]: Adaptive verification's varlen decode graphs lose Triton split-KV at small batches
summary: ### Summary Small decode batches under adaptive verification (AV) run the 2D Triton unified-attention kernel, while the same batch without AV runs the 3D split-KV kernel. On Gemma4-31B + DFlash2 (K=7) at c8 that makes AV 2.8% slower than a fixed budget, even though AV keeps the full budget. On Qwen3-8B + DFlash2 (K=7) at c8 the same comparison is 8.9% slower. Neither model is special. The cause is in how AV captures its decode CUDA graphs, and it applies to any target whose attention runs the Triton unified attention with AV and a verify width of at most 8 (K <= 7). ### Cause AV enables `varlen_decode`, so decode batches replay token-keyed graphs that are captured with `num_reqs=min(num_tokens, max_num_reqs)`, i.e. one request per token: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8db73f26c16afa748e9796e37d60f2e266ec281d/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L313-L330 The 2D/3D choice is fixed at capture time by `num_seqs * cdiv(max_seqlen_q, BLOCK_Q) > seq_threshold_3D`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8db73f26c16afa748e9796e37d60f2e266ec281d/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1221-L1239 So the 64-token graph is captured as 64 requests and takes the 2D path, and every replay keeps it, including a batch of 8 requests x 8 query tokens. Without AV, the uniform-decode graph for that batch is captured with 8 requests and takes the 3D path. The gate is evaluated at a request count up to `K+1` times too high. This is a missed improvement rather than an AV regression. In v0.31.0 the Triton 3D path required `max_seqlen_q == 1`, so K=7 verify batches ran 2D w

title: [Feature]: Cache-aware waiting QoS with optional cooperative prefill preemption
summary: #### Summary Add an opt-in V1 scheduling policy that improves time-to-first-token (TTFT) for cache-warm continuations under long-context contention: 1. **Cache-aware waiting admission/order**: within a bounded window, prefer a waiting request when its *estimated remaining service cost* is materially lower because a local or external KV prefix is already available. 2. **Optional cooperative prefill preemption (later phase)**: at an ordinary chunked-prefill scheduling boundary, checkpoint and pause a cold running prefill only when doing so is predicted to let a warm request reach its first streamed token significantly sooner, without losing the victim's completed work. This issue is intended to track one concrete policy/use case. It is compatible with the scheduler extension framework proposed in #51608 rather than a duplicate of that framework. #### Motivating workload A single engine may serve many concurrent, long-lived agent sessions with distinct 100k–500k-token histories. Under load, one or more uncached chunked prefills can occupy the running set while a continuation with hundreds of thousands of tokens already present in local APC or an external KV cache remains waiting. FCFS is fair by arrival time, but it can produce poor interactive latency in this case: the warm continuation may need only a cache transfer, a short uncached suffix, and one decode step, while a cold request ahead of it still has a very large prefill remaining. This is a QoS/tail-latency proposal, not a claim that cache affinity universally improves throughput. The corrected experiment reported in #4

title: [RFC]: Define an Optional In-Tree Integration Path for Hardware Backends
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM's hardware plugin system enables independent backend development. However, an optional in-tree path could improve coordination during upstream refactors for vendors willing to provide sustained maintenance and hardware CI. Two examples illustrate the adaptation work involved: 1. KV cache spec refactoring ([#51704](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51704)): Introduced backend-published packing through customize_spec() and fields such as state_content_bytes, moving format-specific sizing out of spec subclasses. Downstream backends need to align their custom cache specifications and packing logic with this contract. 2. Memory profiling changes ([#49208](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49208)): Added torch_allocated, total_consumed, and transient_peak_headroom, and changed how non-KV memory is calculated and consumed by the worker. Backends maintaining their own profiling utilities need to update both data structures and accounting semantics. These changes improve vLLM, but adapting out-of-tree implementations can require a separate cross-repository update and validation cycle. In-tree implementations are more readily included in repository-wide impact analysis, maintainer review, and coordinated updates within the same PR. With vendor-provided CI, affected backends could be validated before merging. Out-of-tree plugins can also participate in upstream PR testing, but coordinated fixes still span repositories. title: [Feature]: Add RDMA-capable NIXL OBJ support for KV offload secondary tier
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch vLLM already supports an object-store secondary tier for KV offloading through the NIXL OBJ backend and OffloadingConnector (RFC for this: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38260). The existing JSON shape should remain the same: users configure an OBJ secondary tier with `type: "obj"` and provide object-store parameters through `store_config`. I would like vLLM to extend this existing OBJ tier so it can use accelerated NIXL OBJ backends that support CPU DRAM registration and RDMA-capable object transfers. They should be allowed to come from the AWS SDK default credential/config provider chain, including environment variables, AWS profiles, credential files, IAM roles, or workload identity. title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add RDMA-capable OBJ tier (#55855)
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #55855. Lets the KV offload OBJ secondary tier use NIXL's accelerated (S3-over-RDMA) object-store engines, pinned to NIXL 1.5.2. - Accelerated NIXL OBJ options (`accelerated`, `type`, `use_virtual_addressing`, `req_checksum`, `resp_checksum`) are passed through `store_config.backend_params`. No new `ObjStoreConfig` fields. Connection fields and `num_threads` stay reserved and cannot be overridden. Bool values are normalized to `"true"`/`"false"`. - The primary CPU DRAM pool is registered in chunks of at most `4 GiB - 64 KiB`. cuObject-based engines reject larger registrations: `CUOBJ_MAX_MEMORY_REG_SIZE` is 4 GiB in the CUDA 13.2 header and 4 GiB - 64 KiB in 13.3. Without this, a CPU tier above 4 GiB fails at startup. A single block larger than the limit raises a clear `ValueError`. - Docs: `backend_params` row and an accelerated example in `kv_offloading_usage.md`. Not duplicating #65956: that PR is about <fill in the actual scope>. This one only adds the `backend_params` passthrough and the chunked DRAM registration, which that PR does not touch. <Confirm before posting.> Scope note: NIXL 1.5.2 ships only a vendor engine (`type: dell`). With `accelerated: true` and no `type`, it initializes an accelerated client that still transfers over plain S3. The generic S3-RDMA engine is on NIXL main / 1.6 and is not covered here. ## Test Plan Unit tests: ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -v ``` End to end on 1x L40S (Qwen2.5-0.5B, `TieringOffloadingSpec`, `block_size` 64, 40 distinct prompts of about 3.5k tokens, FlashBlade

title: [ROCm][KV Offload] SimpleCPUOffload: batch copies on SDMA with hipMemcpyFlagExtPreferCE (HIP 7.16+)
summary: ## Overview vLLM's ROCm image now ships the HIP 7.16 runtime (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` 25e14349f2). summary: ## Overview Async KV load admission (#44560) checks each new load against the blocks every in-flight prefill still needs. To get that total it calls `_request_remaining_blocks` for every in-flight request, and it does so again on every admission. A P/D decode instance under a burst parks thousands of loads, so one `schedule()` makes (loads admitted) × (loads parked) calls. This PR caches each parked load's reservation and keeps a running total, so an admission computes only its own. ## Claims - For one `schedule()` that admits k async loads while M are parked, `_request_remaining_blocks` is called about k·M times on main and about M + k times with #64379. With this PR it is called k + p + k·s times, where p loads are promoted and s of them are scheduled in that step. It no longer depends on M. - With 4096 loads parked, a `schedule()` that admits 8 more takes 47.2 ms on main, 12.7 ms with #64379 and 5.4 ms with this PR. A per-step cap (#61725) turns a burst into many steps like this one. A single uncapped burst of 4096 loads takes 8.05 s on main, 77 ms with #64379 and 63 ms with this PR. - Admission decisions do not change. A load that is scheduled stays counted until the step ends, as on main. The stress test below compares every step with main and found no difference. - A cached reservation only needs refreshing at promotion. A parked load keeps its blocks until then, and the count follows the blocks it holds, not `num_computed_tokens`. So a failed load or invalid blocks do not change it until promotion frees the blocks. The stress test below checks cached == recomputed af

title: [Bug]: FlashInfer pinned planner workspace reuse corrupts async prefill/decode; fixes tracked upstream
summary: ## Root cause identified; combined source patches verified in an isolated environment This was an AI-assisted investigation. Earlier statements attributing the fault to vLLM's block-table assembly, a head-dimension argument, or an SM120-specific kernel dispatch defect were not established and are withdrawn. ### Actual ownership failure FlashInfer's native planners serialize scheduling metadata into a reusable pinned host integer workspace and enqueue a raw asynchronous H2D copy. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail a dead peer's sibling ports on the same host at once (opt-in)
summary: ## Overview Fixes 1 and 3 of #56828. A P2P peer is identified by `host:port` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py:128-133`), and each DP rank binds its own port (`manager.py:344-348`). So a source pod with 8 DP ranks is 8 unrelated sessions on the consumer. When one rank's session dies, `_reap_dead_sessions` reaps only that `peer_id` (`manager.py:872`, `:878`). The sessions to the pod's other ranks stay up, and so do their loads. With the new P2P tier option `group_peers_by_host`, a dead peer also takes down the sessions to the other ports on its host, and that host gets no new outbound sessions for 10 s. The option is off by default. Separately, the load-timeout warning now prints the job id and the seconds since submit. ## Claims - With `group_peers_by_host: true`, when a session dies, every other session to the same host is closed in the same reap, through the same teardown. Their in-flight loads fail at once. Their kv_request_ids go into `_failed_req_ids`, so `lookup()` returns MISS (`manager.py:427`) and the requests prefill locally. - For the next 10 s, `_get_or_create_session` returns None for any port on that host. `on_new_request` then marks the request failed (`manager.py:473-475`), so a new request naming that host prefills locally instead of opening a session. - Sessions to other hosts are untouched. - With the option off (the default), nothing changes: the reap is per peer, as on main. - The warning at `session/client.py:527` now reads `P2PSession <peer>: <req> round=0 job_id=7 timed out 10.0s after submit, sending abort`. title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Keep the residual stream token-sharded between layers under EP
summary: ## Overview Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63722; this branch is stacked on it. That PR runs the MoE block's router, pooler, norm and unpooler on each rank's \(T/8\) token slice, then all-gathers the block output so the rest of the layer sees all tokens. Everything outside the block still runs replicated: the FP32 residual adds, the gated post-norms, the pre-QKV and pre-FFN norms, and the `o_proj` all-reduce. With `--enable-expert-parallel`, EP over the whole TP group and DP1, this PR keeps the residual stream split over tokens through all layers (Megatron-style sequence parallelism) for batches of 256 or more tokens: 1. `MuseSpark1xModel.forward` takes each rank's slice of the embeddings (`sequence_parallel_chunk`). 2. Each decoder layer norms its slice, all-gathers the BF16 attention input, runs attention on all tokens, and reduce-scatters `o_proj` (built with `reduce_results=False`). 3. The post-attention norm, residual add and pre-FFN norm run on the slice. The MoE block runs its token-sharded path on the slice (`forward_local_tokens`) and skips the final all-gather. 4. The final norm runs on the slice and its output is all-gathered once. Below 256 tokens (decode), the model takes the existing path, and attention all-reduces `o_proj` itself. The path is off for DSpark draft layers, under PP, and when aux hidden states are requested (EAGLE-style drafters). ## Claims - Serving PTPC-FP8, TP8 + EP on 8× MI300X, on top of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63722: +2.5–3.6% total throughput at 8k input and +4.9–6.4% at 16k input for concurrency 16

title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Shard the MoE block's dense ops over tokens under EP
summary: ## Overview Each Muse Spark MoE layer wraps the routed experts in dense work: an FP32 router, a BF16 pooler (8192 → 4096), a pre-expert RMSNorm and a BF16 unpooler (4096 → 8192). With TP8 + EP and DP1, every rank runs all of it on all tokens and then all-reduces the expert output. In an 8,192-token prefill step on MI300X that is about 2.3 ms per layer, 7/8 of it duplicated across ranks. vLLM's sequence-parallel MoE branch (`sequence_parallel_chunk` + all-gather) would avoid this, but `use_sequence_parallel_moe` requires DP > 1 and an all2all backend. With `--enable-expert-parallel`, EP over the whole TP group, DP1 and no sequence-parallel MoE (the EP group is TP-sized even without EP, so the flag is checked explicitly), this PR makes the block reduce the expert output itself (`reduce_results=False`). For 256 or more tokens each rank: 1. runs the router, pooler and pre-expert norm on its \(T/8\) token slice; 2. all-gathers the router logits and the pooled activations, so the experts still see all tokens; 3. reduce-scatters the expert output, which moves the same bytes as the all-reduce it replaces; 4. runs the unpooler on its slice and all-gathers the `[T, 8192]` result. Below 256 tokens the block keeps one all-reduce. For AITER MXFP4 experts, which take one input row per route, the norm-and-expand runs after the gather. `_validate_tp_post_norm_deployment` rejected any unreduced MoE output. It now rejects it only when the experts are TP-sharded (`needs_pre_norm_all_reduce`), the case where the reduction must run before the per-route post-expert norm. The fail-closed test cas

title: enable_gqa=True can be 2.59x slower than materializing the KV cache - silent MATH-backend fallback at decode
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance Profiling a Llama-3.2-1B-shaped decoder (2048 hidden, 16 layers, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, 2048-token context) at decode time, I found a counterintuitive result and wanted to check it against this community's experience. At batch 32, context 2048: materialize KV with repeat_interleave then einsum: fastest materialize then SDPA: 1.03x slower enable_gqa=True (no materialization): 2.59x slower Moving ~8x fewer bytes (34.36 GB/step down to the 4.29 GB logical cache) made it slower, because on this build no fused kernel accepts the grouped-query shape: flash-attn not compiled, mem-efficient and cuDNN attention runtime-disabled, so enable_gqa=True silently falls back to the MATH reference path. At decode the query length is 1, so attention is matrix-vector and the fused kernels that win at prefill either lose their edge or fail to qualify and fall back. Is this expected on current builds, and is there a recommended way to detect the silent fallback programmatically? Measurement harness and numbers available. ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance _No response_ ### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary) ```text The output of `python collect_env.py` ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix DP vision encoder hang: type an empty rank's output with the vision tower's output dtype
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes a startup hang of `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` at TP >= 2 when a vision tower's first parameter has a different dtype from the embeddings it returns. Since #64111, MiniMax-M3's tower keeps its patch embedding (its first parameter) in fp32 and returns bf16. In `run_dp_sharded_mrope_vision_model`, a rank with no images typed its empty output with the first parameter's dtype, so it joined the all-gather with fp32 while the other ranks sent bf16, and the collective never completed. Follows up on #56872, where this dtype choice was discussed. ## Claims - A rank without images now uses `vision_model.dtype` when the tower defines it, else the first parameter's dtype (the old rule). MiniMax-M3 already declares `dtype = bf16`. For every other in-tree caller, `dtype` equals the first parameter's dtype, so nothing changes for them. - With TP > 1, a rank that ran the tower raises `ValueError` before its all-gather if its output dtype differs from that empty-rank dtype. This is a host-side dtype comparison: no sync and no extra collective. - Behaviour change for non-conforming towers (e.g. out-of-tree): a tower that breaks this rule used to work on batches with at least TP images and hang on smaller ones. It now fails on every call, which in practice means at startup, in the encoder profile run. ## Validation Repro on `main` (MiniMax-M3; the encoder profile run encodes one dummy item on TP ranks, so one rank is always empty): ```bash # CUDA, 4x B200, main at 76c6f3f2 vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --mm-encoder-t

title: [Bugfix] Map compressed-tensors KV-cache scale names for GPT-J
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #65945. LLM Compressor stores GPT-J's FP8 KV-cache scales on the HF attention module, as `transformer.h.<i>.attn.{k,v}_scale`. In vLLM that module's `Attention` layer is its child, also named `attn`. The default cache-scale rule skips names that already end in `.attn.k_scale`, so these scales are never placed. They are then dropped with only a DEBUG message, and attention runs with 1.0. This PR adds a GPT-J-specific rule to `GPTJForCausalLM.hf_to_vllm_mapper`. It maps `.attn.{q,k,v}_scale` and the `*_zero_point` variants to `.attn.attn.<suffix>`. The rule leaves alone names already in vLLM form, and the deprecated `.attn.kv_scale`, which the generic rule already handles. Only GPT-J changes. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -k "KvCacheScaleMapper" ``` plus the self-contained repro script from #65945. ## Test Result - **New test:** 4 of its 7 cases fail before the change; all 7 pass after. - **Nearby suites:** 79 passed, and `ruff` reports no problems. - **Repro:** the attention layers now apply the checkpoint scales (layer 0: 0.5 / 0.25; layer 1: 0.75 / 0.375) instead of 1.0 / 1.0. - **ModelOpt-named checkpoints:** they still fail loudly, as described in the issue; this is unchanged. **Why this is not a duplicate.** No open PR references #65945, and `gh pr list --state open --search` for "gptj kv scale" and "gpt_j k_scale" finds no PR that changes GPT-J's KV-cache scale names. Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed and tested by the author. <details> <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary> - [ ]

title: [Attention] Opt-in FA3 split cap for length-homogeneous decode batches
summary: # [Attention] Opt-in FA3 split cap for length-homogeneous decode batches ## Purpose FA3 splits a request's KV range across `num_splits` partitions so that more CTAs can work on one long sequence, and vLLM passes a flat upper bound — `flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph`, default **32** — when capturing decode CUDA graphs. The per-request split count is then chosen on device by `prepare_varlen_num_blocks`: ``` num_splits = ceil(n_blocks / ceil(total_blocks * 1.1 * kv_heads / num_sms)) ``` **Both ceilings round up, so `kv_heads * num_reqs * num_splits` overshoots the SM count for some batch sizes.** The hdim-256 decode kernel occupies ~227 KB of shared memory on Hopper, i.e. at most **one CTA per SM**, and each (request, kv-head, split) triple is a persistent work item that streams its KV range serially. Once the item count exceeds the SM count, the surplus items form a second wave that runs with only a handful of CTAs resident. This PR caps the budget to `max(2, num_sms // (kv_heads * num_reqs))`. ## Measured effect (H20, 78 SMs, 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, fp8 KV, 16 full-attn layers) Isolated FA3 decode, b=7 @ 42,608 context, GPU exclusive + SM clock locked: | `num_splits` | per layer | bandwidth | executed TFLOPS | |---|---|---|---| | 3 (what the heuristic picks today) | **1.506 ms** | 406 GB/s | 36.2% | | **2 (this PR)** | **1.133 ms** | 539 GB/s | 48.6% | **1.33x on the attention kernel**, which is 52% of the decode step for this model. Two more batch sizes where the heuristic overshoots: b=4 (**capture size 4**) **1.53x** (0.854 → 0.559 ms, two runs per arm) and b=8

title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Read fp8_ds_mla tile scales as arbitrary fp32
summary: ## Purpose The read format has to match the write format. The vLLM writers used with this backend store each tile scale as raw fp32 amax / 448 (concat_and_cache_ds_mla and the DeepSeek-V3.2 fused Triton path). However, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` asked FlashInfer for `pow2_fp32`, which extracts the exponent and reconstructs `2^floor(log2(scale))`. For a non-power-of-two scale written by vLLM, that is smaller by a factor in `(0.5, 1]`. The format was chosen from a `model_type` allowlist that only sent `glm*` to the correct reader, so every other sparse model landing here reads its scales wrong: DeepSeek-V3.2 today, and HY V4 as soon as it can select this backend (it needs the sink support in the stacked follow-up, since `learnable_sink` defaults to on). https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54434 FlashInfer supports both scale conventions for the same 656-byte physical layout, but vLLM's writer contract currently always stores arbitrary fp32 scales. Kimi-K3 demonstrates that this convention is not tied to the model label: its dense MLA path writes the same layout even though it never reaches this sparse backend. This backend accepts no other layout (it raises unless `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_ds_mla"`), so its reader format becomes a constant. DeepSeek-V4 is not a counterexample. It reuses the `fp8_ds_mla` string for a different footer-scale layout: 576 bytes of per-token data plus 8 bytes of UE8M0 `2^(u8-127)` scales in the page footer, or 584 logical bytes per token. title: [Bug]: fused_recurrent_kda silently ignores num_accepted_tokens
summary: ### Your current environment `main`. This is argument plumbing in the vendored FLA wrapper and visible in the source, so no GPU or model run is involved; I've left out `collect-env`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug `fused_recurrent_kda` in [`vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/kda.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/kda.py#L109) accepts `**kwargs` and then hardcodes `num_accepted_tokens=None` when it calls `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd`: ```python o, final_state = fused_recurrent_kda_fwd( ... ssm_state_indices=ssm_state_indices, num_accepted_tokens=None, ... ) ``` `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` just above it [forwards that argument to the kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/kda.py#L83), so a caller that supplies an accepted-token count gets no error, and the count has no effect. In the kernel, when `ssm_state_indices` is also supplied, the count picks which column of the request's row holds the slot id to resume from: a count of 2 [should pick column 1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_recurrent.py#L104-L121), `None` picks column 0. If those columns point at different prefix states, the step resumes from the wrong one. The line has been there since KDA landed in #27654. I ran into this while wiring up KDA speculative rollback in an out-of-tree integration, and worked around it by calling `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` directly on the speculative path while leaving plain decode on the wrapper. title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable fused multi-step draft decode for ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
summary: ## Overview #46849 runs all MRV2 autoregressive draft decode steps from one metadata build in one CUDA graph when every draft attention backend sets `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`. `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` does not, so EAGLE and MTP drafters on it log ``` Attention backend(s) ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly. ``` and rebuild the metadata on the host and replay one draft graph for each of the k−1 draft decode steps. Its metadata holds only views of buffers the fused loop keeps current plus step-invariant values, so this PR opts it in with a no-op `update_draft_decode_metadata`, as the Triton backend and FlashInfer trtllm-gen (#58371) do. ## Claims - With `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, multi-step drafters run the fused draft decode loop, and the fallback line is no longer logged. - On MI355X the draft decode loop, timed in isolation, takes 16–19% less time at k=3 (571 → 463 µs at batch 1, 697 → 585 µs at batch 8, 678 → 559 µs at batch 32) and 6–8% less at k=7 (1197 → 1108 µs, 1623 → 1530 µs, 1559 → 1464 µs). The saving per loop, 90–120 µs, does not grow with k. - No end-to-end throughput gain is claimed. At k=3 serving throughput moves by +0.1% and +0.2% at concurrency 1 and 8, and by −0.6% at concurrency 32 (see Details for what the profiler shows there); at k=7 by +1.9%, −0.1% and −0.2%, within the variation between server instances. - Output quality is unchanged: GSM8K accuracy at k=3 and k=7, GPQA accuracy of gpt-oss-20b at k=4, and acceptance length match main within run-to-r

title: [RFC]: Packed-weight INT4 GEMM (W4A16 / W4A8) for RDNA4 (gfx1200/gfx1201)
summary: ### Motivation. On RDNA4 (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), W4A16 decode runs on `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` (#40977): `wvSplitK_int4_g` for up to 5 rows, Triton above. #62708 extends it to an INT4 `lm_head`, and #63562 retunes the gfx12 Triton tiles for small M. I have a set of RDNA4 kernels (HIP, opt-in, gfx1200/gfx1201 only). Against current main + #63562, with the model's numerics unchanged (W4A16), my branch decodes RedHatAI's Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 1.12× faster at batch 1, 1.65× at batch 16 and 1.51× at batch 64. It decodes Muse-Glimmer-30B-INT4 at the same speed at batch 1 and 1.71× faster at batch 16 and 64. An opt-in W4A8 mode raises batch 64 to 1.84× (Qwen) and 2.30× (Muse). The branch sits on an Oct 16 base, so these are not yet like-for-like; numbers on main will come with PR 1. I'd like to agree on how to upstream them without duplicating or conflicting with the PRs above. The core idea differs from the existing path. Weights are repacked once at load time into WMMA fragment order, with each group's scales and zero points interleaved in the same stream. One HIP decode kernel family then covers 1–448 tokens, with variants chosen by M. Above 448 tokens the weights are dequantized into a packed BF16 prefill GEMM. The existing path reads the GPTQ/AWQ layout directly instead, using `wvSplitK` for M ≤ 5 and Triton for everything else. **Setup:** 1× R9700 (32 GB) capped at 250 W to reduce run-to-run variance, ROCm 7.2.1. Models: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4` and `RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-INT4` (compressed-tensors, symmetric INT4, group 128). FP8 KV cache, 1024-token prompts,

title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Add stream-ordered same-host CUDA IPC pulls
summary: ## Overview Add an opt-in same-host CUDA IPC pull path to `NixlConnector`. Decode admits the request in the compute batch, copies the producer's cache with `swap_blocks_batch`, and waits on a CUDA event before consuming it, avoiding the normal receive-completion scheduler round trip. Related design discussion: #50913. This targets direct device-memory pulls on one host; the NIXL handshake, descriptor mapping and completion notifications are retained. ## Claims - `kv_connector_extra_config.enable_local_fastpath=true` enables direct CUDA IPC imports and batched device-to-device copies for matching P/D TP and cache geometry. The default is off; cross-host peers use ordinary NIXL pulls. - Adjacent and aliased ranges are merged only when their source-to-destination byte mappings agree. Conflicting overlapping destinations and descriptors crossing an exported allocation are rejected. - The copy stream waits for destination initialization. A completion event gates the compute stream before KV/SSM state preprocessing, while CPU input preparation can overlap the copy. Producer completion notifications remain gated on the copy event. ## Validation ### H20 serving observations from the downstream port The human submitter provided and confirmed a serving-profile report collected on **2026-11-04**. These measurements are from an internal downstream adaptation, rather than a GPU run of this upstream branch. The upstream patch includes the same allocation-bound checks, alias coalescing and copy-stream initialization fence. Configuration: **8×H20, P/D TP4/4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, attention K

title: [Performance]: Startup sizing of FlashInfer workspace to recover KV-cache capacity
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance I tested startup workspace sizing for FlashInfer in vLLM with Qwen2.5-1.5B BF16 on an RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89). Reducing the workspace from **394 to 32 MiB** increased KV-cache capacity by **21.27%** under the same memory budget. With four concurrent requests, each with 16K input and 128 output tokens, batch completion time improved by **5.38% and 6.25%** in two separate rounds. First-request completion was about **2.24s slower** in the second round. This builds on [FlashInfer #5236](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5236) and relates to #40383 and #46883. Would this fit the current workspace lifecycle, and which sizing API/integration point would you recommend? [Detailed proposal, results and reproduction prerequisites](https://github.com/lktr-wq/flashinfer-workspace-study/blob/main/PROPOSAL.md). The prototype and analysis were AI-assisted; support conditions, quality comparisons and trade-offs are documented in the repository. ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance _No response_ ### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary) ```text The output of `python collect_env.py` ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bugfix] Avoid O(n) strip_covered_mm_data work per realtime step
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #58324. Realtime (`/v1/realtime`) sessions re-enter the scheduler as new requests on every engine step. `NewRequestData.from_request` called `strip_covered_mm_data` over **all** accumulated multimodal features and `dataclasses.replace`'d every already-covered item. Per-step EngineCore time grew linearly with session age (~3 ms per minute of audio; quadratic over the session). A late-session profile put ~55% of EngineCore time in this path. Covered features only grow, and `mm_features` are ordered by offset. This change: 1. Memoizes the stripped copy on each `MultiModalFeatureSpec`, so `dataclasses.replace` runs once per feature. 2. Keeps a covered prefix cache on `Request` (`_mm_stripped_prefix`) so later steps only examine newly covered features (O(new features), not O(all features)). The scheduler-side `Request` still keeps the full payloads. Originals are not mutated. Preempt (`num_computed_tokens == 0`) clears the prefix cache so a later prefix-cache hit can re-strip from the originals. **Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for `#58324`, `strip_covered_mm_data`, and realtime scheduler mm-feature stripping. Issue #58324 is open with no linked PRs. `#52041` introduced the function; `#54994` only preserved SHM address items. AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. The submitting human reviewed the diff. This does not change model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior — only scheduler CPU work for already-covered mm payloads. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_output.py -v --noconftest ``` CPU-only unit te

title: [Feature]: KV-pool-saturated admission retries inflate decode TPOT ~2.3x: request automatic admission backoff
summary: ### Describe the feature you'd like to see **Environment** - vllm 0.30.0 (main, Oct 2026), Ascend backend (vllm-ascend main), decode instance of a P/D-disaggregated deployment — but the mechanism is in the V1 scheduler and platform-independent - TP8, 8 × Ascend 910B; KV pool ≈ 32k tokens ⇒ ~22 concurrent sequences fit for this workload (avg input ~400 tokens, fixed output 1000) - Offered load: 120 concurrent requests **Observation** With `max_num_seqs` (96) above what the KV pool can sustainably hold (~22), decode TPOT collapses while throughput barely moves: | config | TPOT | output tok/s | |---|---|---| | max_num_seqs=96 | 120.6–120.7 ms | 347‒360 | | max_num_seqs=20 (≤ pool capacity) | 48.5–54.4 ms | 378–411 | Capping admission to pool capacity improves TPOT ~2.3x and throughput +10–14% with the same engine. While the pool is saturated, every scheduler step re-scans ~90 waiting requests for admission (plus preempt/readmit churn as sequences grow into the pool), which appears to add O(100 ms) per step. Two consequences: 1. title: [LoRA] Keep loaded adapters across idle dummy batches
summary: With data parallelism on an MoE model, idle ranks run `execute_dummy_batch` between steps to keep the expert collectives in lockstep. The dummy run went through the same LoRA setup as warmup. It registered `max_loras` dummy adapters with ids `1..max_loras`, which evicted real adapters from the CPU cache and reused real adapters whose ids matched. On exit it called `remove_all_adapters()`. Any engine serving LoRA traffic in that configuration dropped every adapter whenever it went idle, so the next request for any adapter reloaded it from disk. Dummy LoRAs exist only so the dummy batch can select them. When a dummy run selects none (`num_active_loras=0`), they are no longer added or removed, and the punica mapping is still set to "no LoRA" for every token. The runtime dummy batch now selects none on both model runners. The V1 runner already passed 0. V2 hardcoded `max_loras`, so its `_dummy_run` now takes `num_active_loras` and keeps `max_loras` as the default for profiling and warmup. `num_active_loras` needs no agreement across DP ranks (`dp_utils.py`). The same change fixes the V1 runner's external launcher + DP path, which calls `_dummy_run(1)` at runtime. ## Test - `pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -k dummy_run_without_active_loras`: a dummy run with no active LoRAs keeps adapters 1 and 3 resident and in the same GPU slots, with and without `remove_lora`. Warmup with active dummy LoRAs behaves as before. Fails on main (`{1, 2, 3} != {1, 3}`, then flushed). - `pytest tests/lora/test_lora_functions.py -k dummy_batch_keeps_loras`: end to end, `execute_dummy_batch` on

title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Run MoE LoRA on tokens gathered from other DP ranks
summary: ## Purpose Part of #61453. With DP > 1 and no EP, the MoE layer runs on tokens gathered from all DP ranks, and the token to LoRA slot mapping is gathered with them. But the MoE LoRA path still returned early on this rank's own `no_lora_flag`, and only aligned this rank's own active LoRA ids. So a rank with only base model requests added no expert LoRA delta for the LoRA tokens of its peers. This PR: - In `PunicaWrapperGPU`, when a gathered mapping is passed in, skips the local early return and aligns over all slots. Rows are already masked by the mapping, and disabled slots exit on `adapter_enabled`. - In `LoRAKernelMeta.prepare_tensors`, copies the mapping before the `no_lora` early return. Before this, a rank whose batch was all base sent its stale mapping from an older step to the other ranks. - Does the same for the `_batch_has_no_lora` fast path in the TRT-LLM LoRA experts. What this does not fix is a fully idle peer. Its dummy step activates a zero weight warmup adapter, and it never loaded the real adapter in the first place. That needs the slots to be consistent across DP ranks, which is the second point in the issue and a bigger change. No open PR touches this. ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py`. `test_add_lora_fused_moe_early_exit` now also checks that the mapping is copied when all ids are -1, and that a gathered mapping with LoRA tokens still runs the kernel. - E2E on 4xH100: `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct` with `-dp 2 -tp 2 --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 8`, adapter `jeeejeee/olmoe-instruct-text2sql-spider` (has expert LoRA).

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Bound draft max_model_len by the target before logging
summary: Fixes #29945 ## The bug With MTP or any other in-checkpoint drafter, startup prints two different max model lengths for the same run: ``` [model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration [model.py:1684] Using max model len 131072 [model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP [model.py:1684] Using max model len 262144 ``` Users read the second line as the drafter being sized for a longer context than the target and reasonably conclude that KV cache is being over-allocated. The issue has collected repeat reports on Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and GLM-4.5-Air since December, including cases where an explicit `--max-model-len 8192` still printed `Using max model len 262144` for the draft. @benchislett investigated twice and confirmed there is no over-allocation, since `SpeculativeConfig._maybe_override_draft_max_model_len` clamps the draft to the target immediately after the model config is built, and invited a PR to fix the log. ## Root cause `ModelConfig` for the draft is constructed with `spec_target_max_model_len=target_model_config.max_model_len`, but `_get_and_verify_max_len` only consults that argument inside the `derived_max_model_len == inf` branch, which is the fallback for checkpoints that declare no length key at all. Every real MTP or EAGLE checkpoint does declare one, so the argument is dead in practice and the draft resolves to its own declared length, logs it, and is only corrected one step later by the clamp in `SpeculativeConfig`. So the bound exists twice, in two different places, and the value that gets logged is the one from before the bound

title: [Spec Decode][PP] Centralize auxiliary hidden-state relay

This enables gpt-oss, Qwen3-VL-MoE and Gemma 4 with pipeline parallelism, fixes Qwen3-VL's PP startup failure, and removes repeated upstream-state collection from target models. ## Claims - **Enable gpt-oss + EAGLE3 with PP.** Previously rejected at startup; now runs with PP=2, PP=4 and TP=2 × PP=2, with acceptance length comparable to PP=1. - **Fix Qwen3-VL + EAGLE3 startup at PP=2.** Previously failed with `mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (16384x2560 and 7680x2560)`; now starts and achieves acceptance length comparable to PP=1. - **Enable Qwen3-VL-MoE + EAGLE3 and Gemma 4 + EAGLE3 / DFlash with PP.** Previously rejected at startup; now run at PP=2 with acceptance length comparable to PP=1. - **Preserve global layer order across stages.** Capture each stage-boundary tap once, place upstream states before local states, and deliver the complete list even when the last stage captures no aux hidden states itself. - **Detect missing aux states at the sending stage.** `PPHandler` checks the expected local `IntermediateTensors` keys and reports which states the model failed to pack. - **Detect an incomplete aux-state list on the last stage.** Before passing the list to the drafter, `PPHandler` checks that its length matches the requested layer count. This catches missing taps caused by a model forward using stage-local rather than global layer indices. ## Validation Local B300 runs used 64 prompts × 128 generated

title: [Hybrid] Round the attention block size up to prefix_match_unit
summary: ## Overview For hybrid attention/mamba models, round the block size derived from the mamba state up to a multiple of `--prefix-match-unit` instead of failing at startup. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR; I reviewed every changed line. ## Claims - The derived size is often divisor-poor (2112 tokens for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with fp8 KV), so most units failed: ``` ValueError: Invalid prefix_match_unit=256; prefix-cacheable KV cache group block sizes must be divisible by prefix_match_unit. Got group block sizes=[2112, 2112, 2112, 2112], ... ``` - Units that already divide it are unchanged. ## Validation ``` $ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k rounds_up_to_prefix_match_unit 3 passed # this PR (CPU and GB300) 1 failed, 2 passed # main E AssertionError: assert 400 == 512 ``` GB300, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, fp8 KV, `prefix_match_unit=256`: starts with this PR (block size 2112 → 2304), fails on `main`. ## Details The step is `lcm(kernel alignment, backend alignment, prefix_match_unit)`. The mamba page is padded to the attention page anyway; this adds a little more padding, and a warning is logged when it grows the block by more than 10%. title: [Perf][KV Events] Batch BlockRemoved events per allocation
summary: ## Overview Emit one `BlockRemoved` per KV cache group per allocation instead of one per evicted block. When most of a prompt comes from an external KV store (P/D prefill with Mooncake), every allocated block evicts a cached one, and building these events costs the scheduler a few percent of its time. ## Claims - `BlockPool.get_new_blocks` with KV events on, every allocated block evicting a cached one: 1,613 -> 717 ns per evicted block; events off unchanged (468 ns). - `BlockRemoved` events for 10,240 evictions in 40 allocations over 4 KV cache groups: 10,240 -> 160. title: [Bug] MTP draft model does not inherit --hf-overrides (YaRN): length gate + dummy-0 drafts silently kill speculative acceptance beyond the draft's max_model_len
summary: # [Bug] MTP draft model does not inherit `--hf-overrides` (YaRN): length gate + dummy-0 drafts silently kill speculative acceptance beyond the draft's `max_model_len` ## Summary When a model's context is extended with `--hf-overrides` **as a dict** (e.g. YaRN ×4), the MTP draft model's `model_config` is **not** given the override — `compose_draft_hf_overrides()` documents dict overrides as "target-specific key patches and are not applied to the draft". The draft therefore keeps the model's native `max_position_embeddings` as its `max_model_len`. That length feeds the drafter's input gate in `gpu_model_runner` (`_input_fits_in_drafter`): once the batch's longest sequence + `num_spec_tokens` exceeds the **draft's** `max_model_len`, vLLM **skips draft proposal entirely and substitutes dummy token 0 for every request in the batch**. Since `rejection_sampler` reserves only `-1` as placeholder, token 0 is an ordinary token and is "accepted" only when the target happens to sample 0 — ≈0%. Result: engine-wide MTP acceptance collapses to ~0 (per-position 0.000/0.000) for as long as any sequence is past the boundary, each decode step still pays the target-side cost of verifying the dummies, and the only signal is the spec-decode metrics. Target output stays correct; nothing is logged. Note (correction to earlier text in this issue): the RoPE objects themselves are **not** what diverges — the MTP layer builds its rope from the target's config (`initialize_model` never forwards the draft `model_config` to the model class, and `qwen3_5_mtp` reads `vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config

title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Inkling NVIDIA sconv cache block-size mismatch
summary: ## Purpose While benchmarking Inkling-Small on Blackwell I ran into a bug when tuning the KV cache block size: with `--block-size 64`, `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` enlarges the sconv conv group's block size to match the attention page (4 -> 8 here), but every NVIDIA call site still indexed the cache with the static kernel window size W=4. Slot mappings use the enlarged size, so this landed conv reads/writes in the wrong pages: greedy generation degenerates into garbage within a few tokens. AMD already handles this correctly via `InklingConvState.cache_block_size` (#48841). This ports that property to NVIDIA and switches all call sites to it. Tagging @WoosukKwon (who contributed these call sites in #48799) and @tjtanaa (AMD implementation which handles this correctly). AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter. ## Test Plan pytest tests/models/inkling/test_sconv_cache_layout.py -v E2E: Inkling-Small-NVFP4, TP=4, `--block-size 64`, greedy completion of "The capital of France is Paris. The capital of Germany is", before/after on top of nightly main. ## Test Result Unit: fails on main (no `cache_block_size` accessor), passes with the fix. E2E: unpatched output collapses into a `they they they...` loop; patched output is coherent: "Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Spain is Madrid...".

title: [Bugfix] Fix incorrect --kv-cache-memory flag name in optimization docs
summary: The actual CLI flag is --kv-cache-memory-bytes (defined in vllm/engine/arg_utils.py). title: [Core][KV Connector] Add VLLM_KV_SCRAMBLE_BLOCKS to test and benchmark with a fragmented KV pool
summary: TL;DR: PD disagg benchmarks tend to be overly optimistic due to how blocks allocated to rquests are initally (in the lifespan of a server) contiguous; this can also hide some correctness (ie eval accuracy drop might only show up on 3rd/4th run during dev). This PR adds a dev option to assign a random free block and mimic worst-case/equilibrium scenario that a server reaches after some time. ## Purpose A fresh `BlockPool` hands out block ids in order, so on a new server, requests get physically contiguous KV blocks. On a server that has been running for a while, the free lists are fragmented and every request gets scattered blocks. This difference matters in two ways: - **Hidden bugs.** Code that maps block ids to KV memory (KV connectors, transfer descriptors, kernels) can look correct while every request's blocks are contiguous and in order, and only break once they are not. Short CI runs on a fresh server almost never reach that state. - **Misleading benchmarks.** With NIXL, contiguous blocks are merged into a single descriptor. Early requests therefore transfer with very few descriptors and little CPU overhead, and a short benchmark measures a best case that a long-running server does not see. This PR adds a dev-only env var, `VLLM_KV_SCRAMBLE_BLOCKS=<seed>`. It shuffles the initial free-block order once, when the `BlockPool` is built, so every request sees fragmented blocks from the first allocation. `0` (the default) leaves behavior unchanged. Block 0 stays first, because it is popped as the null block, and `BlockPool.blocks` stays indexable by block id. The PR also en

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] SM120: decode DeepSeek-V4.1's own KV records with FlashInfer's DSv4.1 sparse MLA
summary: ## Overview On SM120/SM121, DeepSeek-V4.1 writes the V4 KV record and decodes it with FlashInfer's V4 sparse MLA kernels, and `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` is rejected. FlashInfer's SM120 sparse MLA also decodes V4.1's own records (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5197). This PR writes the V4.1 record on SM120 and lets the KV cache option select the matching FlashInfer kernel. It is the base for further SM120 DSv4.1 work. **Depends on FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.1:** the `fp8_dsv41` / `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca` formats are in 0.7.1rc2 but not in the pinned 0.7.0.post1, so this needs the FlashInfer pin bump before it merges. ## Claims - `fp8_ds_mla` on SM120 writes the 528 B V4.1 record (all 512 dims MXFP8) instead of the 584 B V4 record, and decodes it with FlashInfer's `fp8_dsv41` kernels: +8.7% KV tokens at TP4. - `nvfp4_ds_mla` works on SM120 (previously rejected): MXFP8 sliding window plus an NVFP4 compressed cache, decoded with `fp8_dsv41_fp4_ca`: +31% KV tokens over `fp8_ds_mla`. - GSM8K accuracy and fixed 8K/1K serving throughput are unchanged. ## Validation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), FlashInfer built from main with #5197, one run per configuration. ```bash vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype {fp8,nvfp4_ds_mla} --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \ --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` | KV cache | FlashInfer format | KV tokens | GSM8K (chat, flexible-extract) | |---|--

title: [Perf][MoE] Grouped W8A16 skinny GEMM for block-FP8 routed experts at small token counts (SM90)
summary: ## Overview Builds on #64980 (W8A16 skinny GEMM for the dense block-FP8 linear layers). At 1-4 tokens the Triton fused MoE on SM90 is far from memory bound: on `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (256 experts, top-8, 128x128 block FP8) the first expert GEMM reads 16 MB of weights in 10.7 us (1.5 TB/s) and the second 8 MB in 5.8 us, and the layer quantizes its activations twice (before each GEMM). Whole expert path per layer at one token, measured in isolation: 27.7 us. title: [Perf][MoE] Skip the token-count load on the low-latency fused-MoE path
summary: ## Overview The Triton fused MoE has a low-latency path for small batches (`num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= num_experts`, #29354 / #39016): it skips `moe_align_block_size` and launches exactly one program per (token, expert) pair. On that path the `num_tokens_post_padded` early exit in `fused_moe_kernel` can never fire (the grid is exact), yet `_prepare_expert_assignment` still materialized the count with `torch.full` on every call. Under CUDA graphs that fill is captured and replays as a ~1.9 us `FillFunctor<int>` kernel on the MoE stream, right before the first `fused_moe_kernel`, in every MoE layer of every decode step. This PR makes `fused_moe_kernel` skip the load on the low-latency path (its `naive_block_assignment` constexpr already selects the token mapping; the LoRA MoE kernels already guard the load the same way) and has `_prepare_expert_assignment` hand it a one-element view of the ids in place of the count. No fill kernel, no new allocation, and the helper stays traceable: `fused_mova_impl` (K2-Horizon) calls it directly under `torch.compile`, so a Python-side cache keyed by the token count would have specialized on the batch size. ## Claims - **Trace, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` on H200 TP=1, one request:** 40 `FillFunctor<int>` kernels per decode step removed (1194 -> 1154 kernels/step), 1.7-1.9 us each plus the launch gap, all on the MoE stream, which is the critical stream of the layer at this batch size (the shared expert on the main stream finishes earlier). - **E2E, same model:** median TPOT -2.8% at one request (3.880 -> 3.775 ms), -0.9% at 2, -1.3% at 4, -1.2%

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Apply expert biases in BatchedTritonExperts
summary: ## Purpose `BatchedTritonExperts` never consumed `quant_config.w1_bias` or `quant_config.w2_bias`. Both of its GEMM calls ignore them, yet the unquantized backend selector happily accepts `has_bias=True` together with `moe_backend="batched_triton"`. This applies the w1 bias to the first GEMM output before the fused activation, and the w2 bias to the down-projection output, matching what `TritonExperts` does. That keeps the change contained to `apply()`, leaves the quantization kernels untouched, and is exact for the FP8/INT8 paths too, since the bias is not quantized and must be applied after dequantization. title: [Core] Count V2's KV cache init memory against the KV cache budget
summary: ## Purpose The V2 CUDA graph memory profile runs the real KV cache init on a minimal cache and then measures only the capture. What that init allocates beside the KV cache, such as FlashInfer's float workspace, is torn down with the profiling state and allocated again after the KV cache is sized. Nothing counts it, so with FlashInfer the engine can start above `gpu_memory_utilization`. This change measures the drop in free device memory across the minimal init, subtracts each KV cache storage once (layers that share a cache share one storage), and counts the rest as consumed memory: it comes out of the KV cache budget and goes into the consumed total used to calculate the startup-plan KV budget, while the profiling result itself is left as measured. It is kept apart from the CUDA graph estimate, so `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0` does not drop it, and it is added after the ROCm fallback. The startup plan schema is bumped so plans recorded without it are not reused. When and in which memory pool the init allocates is unchanged. Scope: V2 with CUDA graphs. Eager mode runs no such profile and is unchanged. Backends that allocate nothing new at init (FlashAttention in the runs below) get the same KV cache size as before. ## Test Plan - Unit tests: the init cost is measured apart from the graph estimate with a shared KV cache excluded once; the worker counts it once with the graph estimate on or off and after the ROCm fallback, and leaves the profiling result as measured. - GPU runs on one sm_80 GPU comparing the baseline and this change for Gemma 4, Llama and Qwen,

title: [Bugfix] Name the cause when a compile cache dir cannot be created
summary: ## The problem An unwritable cache root ends engine startup with a bare `PermissionError` from `os.makedirs()`. What the user sees is: ``` RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. title: [Doc]: Docs use CLI flag names that `vllm serve` does not register
summary: ### The doc issue Several pages document `vllm serve` options with the underscore spelling (e.g. `--hf_overrides`) while the options are registered under the dash-separated spelling (e.g. `--hf-overrides`). `vllm serve` parses its arguments with `FlexibleArgumentParser`, which rewrites underscores in long option names to dashes before the options are looked up, so both spellings are accepted: ``` --hf_overrides == --hf-overrides --tokenizer_mode == --tokenizer-mode --config_format == --config-format --load_format == --load-format ``` The underscore spellings were therefore not broken commands. The issue is that they are inconsistent with the rest of the docs and with the option names that `vllm serve --help` prints and that the generated CLI reference lists. Affected pages on `main`: | Page | Spelling used in the docs | Spelling the option is registered as | | --- | --- | --- | | `docs/models/pooling_models/scoring.md` | `--hf_overrides` (5x) | `--hf-overrides` | | `docs/features/tool_calling.md` | `--tokenizer_mode`, `--config_format`, `--load_format` (10x) | `--tokenizer-mode`, `--config-format`, `--load-format` | | `docs/design/torch_compile.md` | `--compilation_config` | `--compilation-config` | | `docs/design/debug_vllm_compile.md` | `--compilation_config` | `--compilation-config` | | `docs/design/custom_op.md` | `--compilation_config.custom_ops` (6x) | `--compilation-config` | | `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md` | `--compilation_config` | `--compilation-config` | | `docs/features/custom_logitsprocs.md` | `--logits_processors` (2x) | `--logits-processors` |

title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix Mamba prefix cache EAGLE hit
summary: ## Purpose Fix an unsafe prefix-cache hit for hybrid full-attention + Mamba/GDN models when EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding is enabled. Prefix caching should be behavior-preserving, but with Qwen3.5-style multi-turn agent prompts we observed prefix-cache-on can diverge from prefix-cache-off. This is related to the hybrid prefix-caching work tracked in #26201, and to Mamba/GDN prefix-caching + speculative-decoding reports such as #38182, #39809, #39273, and #34361. This PR fixes the concrete cache-hit boundary bug shown below; it does not claim to resolve all startup/kernel/rollback issues discussed in those reports. ### Root Cause The hybrid coordinator computes a common reusable prefix across KV cache groups, but the current code can let a later/sparse group increase that common prefix. Also, dense KV cache can safely match one EAGLE/MTP lookahead block and then drop the final block. Mamba/GDN stores recurrent boundary states, so it cannot safely match a lookahead boundary and then rewind to an earlier state. title: [Bugfix] MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit ignores drop_eagle_block, silent corruption with prefix caching + MTP/EAGLE
summary: <!-- AI-assisted PR: drafted and tested with Claude (Anthropic) assistance, reviewed and submitted by the author. --> ## Purpose `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`) accepts `drop_eagle_block` as a parameter but never acts on it. When native MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding is combined with `--enable-prefix-caching` on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model, a matched block containing recurrent state written over rejected draft positions stays reachable through the prefix cache and gets reused by later requests sharing that prefix. title: [Core][KV Events] Emit skipped ancestry for partial cache events
summary: ## Purpose This draft is a follow-up stacked on #44488. When a physical cache block is larger than `hash_block_size`, `cache_partial_block()` registers only the final hash boundary. Its `BlockStored` event uses the immediately preceding fine-grained hash as `parent_block_hash`, even when that intermediate boundary was neither registered nor emitted. A content-keyed consumer therefore cannot reconstruct the emitted block's prefix chain. For example: ```text resident full block: H1536 omitted boundary: H1664 resident partial: H1792 primary event: H1664 -> H1792, tokens[1664:1792] skipped ancestry: H1536 + tokens[1536:1664] ``` This change preserves final-boundary-only cache residency while populating the optional `skipped_parent_block_hash`, `skipped_token_ids`, and `skipped_extra_keys` metadata introduced by #44488. Consumers can reconstruct `H1664` without treating it as a resident cache entry. ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate the existing related work: - #44451 / #44488 address gaps caused by null or masked logical blocks in `cache_full_blocks()`; this change covers skipped fine-grained boundaries in `cache_partial_block()`. - #57339 centralizes partial-event construction through `_build_block_stored_event`, but does not populate the missing ancestry. - #43258 uses a separate hybrid-model sub-block emission path; it does not fix the current `cache_partial_block()` event contract. - #49125 / #52972 address stale partial hashes after full-block promotion, not missing parent context during event emission. - #57358 addresses sparse cache hits in `kv_cache_report

title: [RFC]: Dual Batch Overlap (DBO) for Model Runner V2
summary: ### Motivation. Dual Batch Overlap hides all-to-all communication latency in DP+EP deployments by splitting a step's batch into two microbatches and interleaving their compute and comm phases across two CUDA streams. Today it exists only in the V1 model runner (`gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py` / `ubatching.py`), wired in as a `UBatchWrapper` that wraps the whole model and rebuilds attention metadata per microbatch after the fact. Model Runner V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`) is meant to eventually replace V1, but it has no DBO path. `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features()` currently raises if `--enable-dbo` is combined with V2, so **DP+EP deployments that depend on DBO for throughput cannot move to V2**. That's a real migration blocker for exactly the multi-node MoE serving configurations V2 is aimed at. Porting V1's implementation directly doesn't fit. V1's DBO is architecturally opportunistic: `split_attn_metadata` slices *already-built* full-batch attention metadata after the fact, allocating fresh tensors per microbatch per step. That's fine for V1's dynamic-shape eager/graph-per-shape model, but it's hostile to V2's core design — V2 dispatches per `BatchExecutionDescriptor` against a graph registry and reuses **persistent** input buffers across replays so tensor addresses stay stable. Naively porting V1's post-hoc splitting would mean allocating inside the hot path on every microbatched step, undermining the reason V2 exists. title: [RFC]: Using Backend-Owned KV Cache Runtime Shapes
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM currently has three descriptions of KV cache layout (from refactor proposed in #42082 and its follow-up PRs): 1. `KVCacheSpec` specifies the KV cache format of one layer: block size, page geometry, dtype, quantization, and related layout fields. 2. `KVCacheTensor` describes where layers and manager blocks live. 3. `compute_layer_kv_cache_shape_bytes()` and `compute_layout_strides()` create one generic `[B, H, N, C]` view based on `KVCacheLayout`. The third step assumes every backend uses one tensor shape given the same spec and kv_cache_tensor inputs, with all components packed into trailing `C`. However, that is no longer true when: - Some attention backends on different platforms may require block-level K/V packing rather than separate components inside `C`. - Quantization may introduce additional components such as scales, with a different dtype, shape, and placement from the data. - Hybrid recurrent layers may expose convolution and SSM state as separate components. Three concrete examples in current `main` branch show the split responsibility: 1. **Mamba-style layers.** `MambaBase.bind_kv_cache()` receives one generic `[B, 1, 1, C]` page and performs a second block-internal view. It slices conv and SSM state bytes, reinterprets each state with its own dtype, and reshapes it to `get_state_shape()`. summary: ## Purpose A batch-wide no-LoRA check cannot skip work when a request uses an adapter but the current layer has no weights for that adapter. title: LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6)
summary: ## LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6) Just wanted to give a heads-up here because I've seen a few issues pop up about LMCache + PP not working, and I've put up a fix on the LMCache side that unblocks it. ### What was broken If you tried to run vLLM with LMCache in multi-server MP mode with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`, the connector would refuse to start with: ``` ValueError: LMCacheMPConnector multi-server mode only supports tensor parallelism (TP), not pipeline parallelism (PP). Got pp_size=2. ``` This hit especially hard for MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.5/4.6) because those are exactly the workloads where you want both PP (to fit a large model across nodes) and LMCache (to cut TTFT on long-context agentic workloads). ### Why it was blocked The guard existed because of a subtle read-lock refcounting bug. `compute_extra_count` in LMCache inferred whether a model used MLA by checking `tp > world_size`. That heuristic is correct when PP=1 but breaks under PP>1 — PP inflates `world_size` to `tp × pp`, so the inference produces `extra_count = 0` when it should be `tp_size - 1`. Result: the server under-locks, multiple workers race on the same KV chunk, and you get premature eviction. ### The fix I opened [LMCache PR #4082](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4082) that: 1. Carries an explicit `use_mla` flag in the cache key (instead of inferring it) — backward-compatible on the wire 2. Fixes `kv_tp_size` and `is_kv_writer` in `ParallelStrategy` to account for the fact that server blocks align with PP stages, not TP groups 3. P

summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `VllmConfig._verify_kv_transfer_compat` rejects **every** KV connector when `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` is set (unless `enable_cumem_allocator` is on). The rationale is sound for connectors that pin/register KV cache memory (NixlConnector via `ibv_reg_mr`, MooncakeConnector): CUDA VMM physical remaps invalidate their registrations. The check's own comment acknowledges it is conservative: *"We can't enumerate every in-tree and out-of-tree connector that pins memory, so we conservatively reject the combination whenever any KV connector is configured."* However, copy-based connectors are unaffected by remaps: they move KV with CUDA kernels or `cudaMemcpy` at transfer time, dereferencing (stable) virtual addresses on every call. Example: LMCache's connectors — `lmcache`'s transfer kernels take per-call pointer-array tensors of virtual device addresses, stage into lmcache-owned pinned **host** buffers, and never register vLLM's KV pages with RDMA/GDS/IPC (verified in lmcache 0.5.1: the only `cudaHostRegister`/`pin_memory` usage is on lmcache-owned host staging buffers; `ibv_*`/`cuFile*` symbols are absent from the classic-path native ops). title: [Core] Add operator opt-out for the expandable_segments KV-connector rejection
summary: ## Purpose FIX #48242 `_verify_kv_transfer_compat` conservatively rejects every KV connector under `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. That is correct for connectors that pin/register KV cache memory (NIXL `ibv_reg_mr`, Mooncake), but copy-based connectors (CUDA kernels / `cudaMemcpy` at transfer time, e.g. the LMCache connectors) dereference virtual addresses on every transfer and are unaffected by VMM physical remaps. Both sanctioned escapes are harmful on unified-memory platforms (GB10/DGX Spark): dropping `expandable_segments` costs the anti-fragmentation margin (CUDA OOM at previously-working `gpu_memory_utilization`), and `enable_cumem_allocator` routes the weights load through the CuMem pool too (`gpu_worker.py` wraps both `tag="weights"` and `tag="kv_cache"`), which pins ~weights-sized RM sysmem and hard-crashed both nodes mid weight-load (`NVRM: NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` from `nv_alloc_system_pages`). Details and evidence in the linked issue. This PR adds `KVTransferConfig.kv_connector_supports_expandable_segments` (default `False` — behavior unchanged): an explicit operator assertion that the configured connector never pins/registers KV cache device memory, which skips the rejection.
