title: [ROCm][AITER] Port FlyDSL int4 MoE integration to AITER fused_moe API
summary: ## Motivation The current [`fused_flydsl_moe.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_flydsl_moe.py) directly calls AITER internals: `aiter.fused_moe.moe_sorting` and `aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.moe_gemm_2stage.compile_moe_gemm1/2`. This makes vLLM own routing buffers, pointer ABI adaptation, JIT caches, two-stage launches, and a duplicate tile-config table. These low-level compiler interfaces may change and bypass AITER’s end-to-end tuned dispatch. ## Proposal Port this path to AITER’s supported `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe` API. Let AITER own sorting, quantization handling, kernel/backend selection, stage dispatch, and tuned/model-specific configs (`AITER_CONFIG_FMOE`). Remove direct imports of `moe_sorting` and `compile_moe_gemm1/2`, plus duplicate launch/cache/config plumbing where possible. ## Benefits - Stable framework-facing integration instead of internal codegen APIs - AITER tuned configs and better-performing kernel dispatch - Easier adoption of improved CK/FlyDSL/Opus and quantization-specific paths - Less duplicated code and one source of truth for sorting/dispatch correctness ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] No direct imports of `moe_sorting` or `compile_moe_gemm1/2` - [ ] Uses AITER’s end-to-end fused MoE interface - [ ] Existing int4/bf16 configurations remain correct - [ ] AITER tuned/model-specific configs are honored - [ ] Representative prefill/decode benchmarks are reported - [ ] Add a capability guard/fallback for older AITER versions if needed Related architectural context: #31578.

summary: ## Purpose This PR upstreams work from the patch set of the MiMo recipe we deploy — Diffbot's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL FP8KV/W4A8 recipe (Hugging Face: diffbot/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-FP8KV-W4A8-2x-RTX-PRO-6000, built by Mike Tung), itself porting parts from the local-inference-lab/vllm fork: the idea and the original implementation belong to the recipe's authors, not to us. Their version of this change is tracked in local-inference-lab/vllm#848; we re-derived the diff against upstream main, wrote or extended the tests, and ran the checks. ### Motivation The Triton DiffKV backend handles mixed batches poorly in two ways: 1. **Cudagraphs.** The DiffKV metadata builder inherited `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` from `TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder`, so cudagraphs were captured and replayed for mixed batches too — a graph may only replay for batches whose call structure matches the one it was traced on. title: fix(warmup): cover all C128A extra_topk widths in sparse-MLA autotune
summary: Fixes #53600 ## Description The FlashInfer sparse-MLA warmup for DeepSeek-V4-Flash only exercises `extra_topk=128` during startup. At runtime, C128A compressed cache dynamically selects wider widths — `256` for sequences 16,512–32,895 and `384` for sequences 32,896–33,792 (when `max_model_len=33,792`). Each width is an independent FlashInfer autotune cache key; a 128-width tactic cannot cover 256 or 384. This causes `SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1` fallback at runtime, degrading decode performance. In the motivating environment, this resulted in **944 `tactic=-1` warnings** during CUDA Graph capture across 4 TP workers, covering 4 unique batch shapes (all with `extra_topk=384`). ## Root Cause The warmup path in `flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py` uses `_SPARSE_MLA_MIXED_WARMUP_TOKENS = 16`, which creates a mixed batch (`create_mixed_batch=True`) where decode tokens have `seq_lens=[1]` (`gpu_model_runner.py:6131`). With `seq_len=1`, the C128A width computation yields `active_topk_width=128`. The warmup never simulates a decode request with `seq_len ≥ 16,512`, so `extra_topk=256` and `384` are never autotuned. The root cause is that the warmup conflates two concerns into a single dummy run: 1. **JIT compilation warmup** — ensuring kernels are compiled and loaded (a `seq_len=1` run achieves this). 2. **FlashInfer autotune shape coverage** — generating cache entries for every runtime-reachable shape (requires multiple `seq_len` values). title: [SpecDecode] Fall back to text-only drafting on encoder cache miss (#38551)
summary: With MTP + multimodal inputs under sustained load, the encoder cache can evict an entry the draft proposer still needs; `_gather_mm_embeddings` then raises `Encoder cache miss` inside `propose_draft_token_ids` and the whole engine dies, dropping every in-flight request (#38551). Unlike the target forward pass, a miss during *drafting* is not an invariant violation: every draft is verified by the target model, so drafting without the mm embeddings can only lower acceptance for that step, never corrupt output. Catch the miss at the draft call site (target-pass misses still raise), log a warning, and draft without mm embeddings. Fixes #38551.

title: [ROCm] DeepEP: configurable dispatch timeouts, deferred legacy annotations
summary: ## Summary Two small changes needed to serve over a DeepEP build that does not include the legacy backend. **Dispatch timeouts.** A data-parallel rank that holds no request still joins every MoE collective through a dummy batch. On the first real forward the rank that does hold the request spends minutes JIT-compiling attention and MoE kernels, and the waiting ranks abort a healthy collective on DeepEP's stock 100 s GPU and 300 s CPU limits. Both now come from `VLLM_DEEPEP_TIMEOUT_SECS`, default 1800 s. **Import under a `deep_ep` without the legacy backend.** Such a build has no `Config` or `Buffer`, which `deepep_ht.py` evaluates in annotations at import time, so `import vllm` fails before serving starts. `from __future__ import annotations` defers that evaluation; the module still imports its own symbols normally. ## Test DeepSeek-R1 FP8 on 8x MI350X, `TP=1 / DP=8 / EP=8` over DeepEP. Without the timeout change the first request aborts the collective partway through JIT compilation; with it the request completes and later ones are unaffected. Without the annotations change the server does not start at all against a `deep_ep` built without the legacy backend. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: [Bugfix][V1] Chunk prompt-logprobs logits to bound the activation peak
summary: ## Purpose `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict` materializes the full `[num_scheduled_tokens, vocab_size]` logits tensor in one shot and then upcasts it to float32 via `log_softmax`. Both tensors are live simultaneously, so the transient peak is roughly: ``` num_scheduled_tokens * vocab_size * (2 bytes bf16 + 4 bytes fp32) ``` At 8192 scheduled tokens and a 152k vocabulary that is **~7.5 GiB**. That peak is never observed by memory profiling. `profile_run` calls `_dummy_sampler_run`, which constructs its `SamplingMetadata` with: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L6362 ```python max_num_logprobs=None, ``` so the logprobs path is not exercised and the float32 score tensor is never allocated during profiling. KV cache capacity is sized against a peak that excludes prompt logprobs, and the allocation has to come out of whatever is left at serving time. This is exactly the mechanism @robertgshaw2-redhat described in #5907: > When determining the KV cache size, we calculate peak memory running a long prefill *without logprobs*. If a prompt requests many logprobs, however, this is an additional source of memory usage which is not considered during warmup and can cause OOM because we have nothing in scheduler to prevent this. ## Approach Rather than restructure profiling, this bounds the allocation directly — the "chunked logits processing" approach proposed by @tjohnson31415 in #5907 and endorsed in that thread as "the ideal solution". `compute_logits` and the score computation now run over row chunks of `VLLM_PROMPT_LOGPROBS_CHUNK_SIZE` (def

title: [ROCm] Fix APU unified-memory accounting across GTT and host pressure
summary: ## Summary `RocmPlatform` does not override `is_integrated_gpu()`, so vLLM treats AMD APUs like discrete GPUs and trusts `hipMemGetInfo()` as-is. On APUs that allocate from GTT (system RAM mapped for the GPU — the default on Strix Halo and the configuration AMD recommends), that is wrong in two ways: - **free** is KFD's static system limit minus KFD's own allocations, so it ignores memory used by everything else on the host. With 60 GiB held by a CPU process, HIP still reports 100 GiB free while ~59 GiB is actually available. vLLM then sizes the KV cache for memory that does not exist and, without swap, ends in the OOM killer instead of a clean startup error. - **total** is the TTM/GTT limit, which can exceed the RAM the OS sees (e.g. after enlarging the BIOS carve-out without retuning `ttm.pages_limit`). With a 64 GiB carve-out and a 100 GiB GTT limit, HIP reports 100 GiB total with ~60 GiB of RAM, so the default `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9` cannot start. This PR: - Detects ROCm APUs via HIP's `is_integrated` device property. - Adds a `Platform.get_integrated_gpu_memory_info()` hook, called from `device_memory_info()` (#65413), so both `MemorySnapshot` and the extensible KV cache use it. The default implementation keeps the existing NVIDIA UMA behavior (free from `psutil`) unchanged. - On ROCm, determines which pool HIP allocates from by comparing the pool size HIP reports with the amdgpu sysfs sizes (`mem_info_vram_total`, `mem_info_gtt_total`, located via the PCI address HIP reports for the device): - **GTT-backed:** `free = min(hip_free, MemAvailable)`, `total = min(hip

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Size the extensible KV cache from exact VRAM use, not 2 MB-rounded free memory
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, `hipMemGetInfo` counts every allocation as at least 2 MB, so after warmup the extensible KV cache (#56492) sizes itself from free memory that looks a few GB smaller than it is. This PR adds that memory back once, at the final sizing, using amdgpu's exact VRAM count. Only unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPUs are affected. **Root cause.** The amdgpu driver rounds each allocation up to 2 MB in the free memory it reports, on purpose (commit 1ac354beecfd, "drm/amdgpu: Pessimistic availability based on rounded up allocations"), unless the GPU's memory is kept in system memory (`apu_prefer_gtt`). Its own allocation check uses exact sizes. The many small kernel code objects loaded during warmup therefore hide a few GB. The sysfs counter `mem_info_vram_used` counts exact sizes for the whole device. ## Claims - On an unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPU, the extensible KV cache sizes itself from exact device memory use. On Llama 3.1 8B / R9700 the KV cache went from 51,712 to 76,288 tokens, with no OOM and no failed requests (one run per config). - The correction is never more than what is physically free and never negative. Other processes' allocations are not added back. - Integrated GPUs, partitioned GPUs, a missing or mismatched sysfs count, and all non-ROCm platforms keep the current behaviour (no-op platform hooks). ## Validation Unit tests (the sysfs lookup and correction arithmetic need no GPU; the GPU tests skip off ROCm): ```bash pytest tests/utils_/test_rocm_vram_lookup.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/w

title: [RFC]: Single Batch Overlap (down GEMM ↔ combine) for DeepEP LL
summary: ### Motivation. **I (@algebra-MCX) propose to integrate Single Batch Overlap (SBO) for the DeepEP low-latency path, once the required kernel arguments exist upstream, and would be glad to work on the vLLM-side implementation and validation if maintainers are open to it.** This revisits [#34963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34963) (closed as stale) and the prototype [#29211](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29211) (closed as abandoned because it depended on two unmerged forks). This issue records what has changed, what is still blocking, and a vLLM-side plan that does not pin a fork. SBO targets decode batches that are too small for DBO to pay off (the crossover studied in [#64100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64100)). With one batch there is no second microbatch to hide the all-to-all. title: [Bugfix][Metrics][MFU] Bill linear-attention layers of hybrid models separately
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #58597. `AttentionMetrics` bills every layer of hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5) as full attention. `SlidingWindowAttentionParser` only reads `layer_types` when `sliding_window` is set and only counts `"sliding"` entries, so the `"linear_attention"` (Gated DeltaNet) layers are never subtracted. title: [Spec Decode] Remove the one-chunk cap on adaptive verification
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> > **Paused.** This PR is on hold and not ready for review; I will update it here before resuming. ## Overview Adaptive verification (AV) caps its per-step draft budget so that all verified logits fit in one rejection-sampling chunk: 2^30 / (vocab × 4) rows, which is 2,076 rows for a 129k vocab and 1,081 rows for a 248k vocab. The cap applies per engine (per DP rank), and all TP ranks of an engine verify the same rows, so a TP deployment with high per-engine concurrency hits it first. At high concurrency this cap, not AV's cost model, sets how many drafts get verified. For example, at 2,048 requests with a 129k vocab, it leaves ~28 drafts per step, and raising concurrency past 1,024 lowers throughput. This PR removes the cap: - Steps that make no FP32 copy of the logits (greedy, or temperature 1 with no top-k/top-p/min-p, and no logprobs) verify in one call without chunking. - Other steps chunk at request boundaries. When AV trims drafts, the admitted draft counts are copied to the host (the path batch-sharded sampling already uses), and the host rebuilds the compacted layout from them. ## Claims All on main `b43366fa4b`, whose decode CUDA graphs reach 2,048 requests / 8,192 tokens (#63406), TP4 on one GB200 node: - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark K=7 + AV, 1M context: +19% (greedy) / +16% (sampled) output tokens/s at 2,048 requests, +5–7% at 1,536, within ±2% at 1,024. title: [Refactor] Simplify GLM sparse indexer decode grouping with gather
summary: ## Overview This follows up on [@tomasruizt’s review comment on #60229](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60229#discussion_r4379617970), which suggested replacing the GLM sparse indexer’s scatter-based token grouping with a simpler gather-based implementation. For nonuniform decode rows, the sparse indexer needs to turn the flattened token list into a padded `[request, position]` layout. The existing implementation scattered tokens into that layout and used a dummy request to absorb CUDA graph padding. This PR instead builds the source indices and validity mask, then gathers each tensor directly into the desired layout. The uniform path does not change. ## Claims - Removes the dummy request used to absorb CUDA graph padding. - Replaces the scatter, `repeat_interleave`, and discard-row machinery with a reusable gather mapping. - Reuses the same gather indices for keys, gates, slot mappings, positions, and sequence lengths. - Keeps the NVIDIA and AMD sparse indexer implementations aligned. - Preserves support for nonuniform adaptive-verification rows and CUDA graph replay with a smaller live token budget. - This is a structural simplification rather than a performance claim. ## Validation - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` - `10 passed` - Built this exact branch and loaded `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on 2×B300 with TP2/EP, MTP `k=5`, block verification, and CUDA graphs enabled. - Tested adaptive verification both enabled and disabled at concurrency 1, 16, and 96. - Tested short and approximately 8K-token prompts with varied output lengths and mi

title: [Kernel][PCP] Publish direct-final KV into ExtensibleKVCache storage
summary: ## Overview Publish replicated PCP KV updates directly into ExtensibleKVCache-owned storage. The fused producer writes final cache rows into each PCP peer's replica, then a device publication barrier makes those writes visible to the local Indexer and attention consumers. ```text ASIS Norm/RoPE -> update tensors -> PCP collectives -> cache insertion -> attention PR ExtensibleKVCache -> export/import physical handles -> stable peer mappings Norm/RoPE + quantization -> final peer cache stores -> publication -> attention ``` Rebased onto main `ebac032b92`, including merged #56492 and #65225. The diff now contains the peer extension and direct-publication consumer; it no longer carries an allocator prerequisite snapshot. Related design: #50127. #52863 contains the earlier SymmetricMemory-backed implementation; this version borrows the native VMM allocation and coordinates its growth/remapping instead of allocating KV through SymmetricMemory. ## Claims - Preserve native padded/unequal KV segments and allocation ownership. Peer virtual addresses and pointer tables stay stable across physical growth and remapping. - Replace KV-update collectives with final peer stores and one system-scope publication barrier. Preserve the replicated cache layout/capacity and existing output collectives. - Qualify eager and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` execution on current MRV2, including actual graph replay after post-capture cache growth. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep MuseGlimmer tool call arguments valid JSON for non-finite values
summary: ## Summary The MuseGlimmer tool parser can emit a tool call whose `arguments` string is not valid JSON, so a strict client cannot parse the call at all. `_decode_value` JSON-decodes each `<atem:parameter>` value and falls back to the raw string when decoding fails: ```python try: return json.loads(raw) except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): return raw ``` `json.loads` accepts the `NaN` / `Infinity` / `-Infinity` extension, and it overflows large exponents such as `1e999` to `inf`. None of those raise, so they are kept as floats. `_parse_tool_calls` then serializes the dict with `json.dumps`, which writes them back as bare `NaN` / `Infinity` tokens — not valid JSON under RFC 8259. ## Reproduction Model output: ``` <atem:invoke name="set_temp"><atem:parameter name="value">NaN</atem:parameter></atem:invoke> ``` Emitted arguments, on `main` (`40824284bc`): ``` {"value": NaN} ``` JavaScript `JSON.parse`, Go `encoding/json` and Rust `serde_json` all reject that. Seven inputs hit it, including ones that are perfectly valid JSON on the way in and only become non-finite while decoding: | parameter value | decoded | emitted `arguments` | |---|---|---| | `NaN` | `nan` | `{"x": NaN}` | | `Infinity` | `inf` | `{"x": Infinity}` | | `-Infinity` | `-inf` | `{"x": -Infinity}` | | `1e999` | `inf` | `{"x": Infinity}` | | `-1e999` | `-inf` | `{"x": -Infinity}` | | `[1e999]` | `[inf]` | `{"x": [Infinity]}` | | `{"a": 1e999}` | `{'a': inf}` | `{"x": {"a": Infinity}}` | ## Not a duplicate `muse_glimmer` has several PRs in flight, so per `AGENTS.md` I checked the overlapping ones. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Save chunked host-buffer prefills after their final chunk
summary: # [Bugfix][NIXL] Save chunked host-buffer prefills after their final chunk ## Overview With `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`, the NIXL prefiller copies each request's blocks to the host buffer one step at a time and copies only the blocks newly allocated in that step. A chunked prefill of a hybrid Mamba/GDN model therefore copies its SSM state after the first chunk only, and the decoder starts from that stale state. This PR saves a chunked prefill once, in the step that completes it, with all of its blocks. ## Claims - With a host buffer, a chunked prefill of a hybrid model transfers its final SSM state. title: [ROCm][Misc] Write GDN prefill output in place for the Triton and FlyDSL backends
summary: ## Overview `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward_core` passes no output buffer to the GDN prefill kernel, so the kernel allocates its own output and the layer copies it into `core_attn_out` (after a `torch.cat` in mixed decode/prefill batches). The Triton/FLA kernel already writes into a passed `core_attn_out`, and AITER's FlyDSL kernel (#57560) takes an `o` argument that `rocm_aiter_ops.gdn_flydsl_prefill` did not forward. This hands both backends their slice of `core_attn_out` so the prefill writes in place. ## Claims - Removes one full-size output copy per GDN layer per prefill step on the Triton/FLA backend (the ROCm default, and the CUDA fallback when FlashInfer is unavailable) and on `aiter_flydsl`, plus the decode/prefill `torch.cat` in mixed batches. The effect is small: about 37 µs per GDN layer at a 32K-token step with 16 value heads per rank on MI355X, roughly 0.1% of TTFT. As such, the end-to-end impact is small. - No numerics change, no new host-device sync. Spec-decode batches and the FlashInfer and CuteDSL backends are unchanged. - Related, not a duplicate: #57039 does the same for the FlashInfer backend (and the gated-norm `z` clone), with the same `_forward_core` structure, so the two conflict textually. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] MXFP4 mode for the fused norm / RoPE / KV insert
summary: Replaces #64359, which GitHub closed when its base branch `minimax-m31-flash` was deleted after #64111 merged into main. ## Overview Adds an MXFP4 mode to MiniMax-M3's fused FlyDSL norm / RoPE / KV insert on ROCm (gfx950). The same launch that writes NVFP4 pages can write K, V and index-K as MXFP4 pages: E2M1 data with one E8M0 scale per 32 dims and no global scale. That takes 68 B per token and head, against NVFP4's 72. **Stacked on #64358** (the `mxfp4` KV dtype; its two commits come first here). Review the writer commit, `425d35ac5`; the rest is #64358 and merges of main. ## Changes - `norm_rope_nvfp4_insert/kernel.py`: `compile_norm_rope_insert(..., mx=True)` swaps the scale step and the scale addresses. Norm, RoPE, the E2M1 data layout, V's octet runs and the index-q output are unchanged. - The scale is 2^ceil(log2(amax / 6)) from the fp32 quotient's exponent bits, clamped at 2^-126, and 2^0 for an all-zero group. It reduces over 8 lanes (32 dims) instead of 4. - Elements are scaled by the exact power of two, then converted with the RNE `cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32` the NVFP4 path already uses. - Scale layout: K and index-K `[token][4]`, V `[group][token]`; per head and page, 8192 B of data plus 512 B of scales. - `host.py`: `mxfp4=` keyword. The slot width comes from `mxfp4_kv_cache_full_dim` / `nvfp4_kv_cache_full_dim`, and `k_scale` / `v_scale` are ignored in MXFP4 mode. - The NVFP4 path compiles to the same code as before (`mx=False`). The readers (sparse decode / prefill and the index kernels on scaled MFMA) and the backend's `customize_spec` follow in later PRs. Noth

title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Native gfx950 sparse decode for mxfp4_mla rows (on #64121)
summary: ## Overview At TP2 with more than 4 decode rows, the MonoKernel steps aside and GLM-5.3-Flash runs the regular sparse MLA decode. With the `mxfp4_mla` KV cache (#64121), that decode is the bf16 split-K kernel, which unpacks every selected row to bf16 before the dot products. In a C64 trace it takes 140.1 µs per call against 23.5 µs for the FP8 kernel. Over 11 calls per step that is 1541 µs against 259 µs, and the step goes from 23.50 ms (FP8 KV) to 24.98 ms. This PR adds a gfx950 decode that reads the packed rows on the scaled MFMA instead, with no bf16 or FP8 copy of the cache. **Stacked on #64121** (and through it on #61662 and #60321), which has not landed, so the diff against main includes them. title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse the latent-MoE tail allreduce and RMSNorm
summary: ## Purpose The Kimi-K3 latent-MoE tail ran a custom all-reduce and then a separate RMSNorm on every MoE layer. On ROCm, batches of at most 80 tokens now use AITER's one-stage CustomAR kernel, which does the all-reduce, a zero residual add, and RMSNorm together. Prefill stays on the unfused path. The zero residual is one persistent buffer per dtype, device, and hidden size, sliced per batch, so decode graph capture does not allocate. On MI355X Kimi-K3 FP4 TP8 conc-1, 100k x 256, without the profiler, 10 requests per arm on the same node: ITL median 6.100 -> 6.057 ms. The one-stage kernel is about 12 µs per layer, against 15.6 µs for the all-reduce plus RMSNorm pair it replaces. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_latent_moe_runner.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py ``` Those tests compare the latent-MoE tail with the unfused all-reduce plus RMSNorm reference, including batches at and below the 80-token one-stage limit. ## Test Result The ITL comparison above is from that MI355X run. The pytest command was not re-run on this host; it has no PyTorch. title: [Perf] Faster BF16x3 router GEMM at large batch sizes on SM100
summary: ## Overview Add a large-M path to the SM100 BF16x3 router GEMM. title: [Perf][Attention][DCP] Gather the MLA DCP context rows by index instead of reorg_kvcache
summary: ## Overview Under DCP, the MLA chunked-context loop un-shards the all-gathered context rows with `reorg_kvcache`: a host loop that slices the latent and rope rows of each (request, rank), then two `torch.cat` calls, for every chunk in every MLA layer. This PR builds the row indices once per batch with the chunk metadata (`ContextChunk.context_row_indices`) and replaces `reorg_kvcache` with one Triton row-gather launch per chunk and layer. Split out of #63935 (fp8 DCP context), which builds on this PR. ## Claims - Per chunk and MLA layer, in the five chunks below: GPU time 21.8–397.0 us → 7.1–29.4 us, host time 104.5–3,458.7 us → 47.2–49.4 us. - Cost: 214–376 us more host time per batch in `build_mla_chunked_context_metadata`, under DCP only, once per batch (not per layer), with no device sync. - `kv_b_proj` and the prefill backend get bit-identical inputs (same rows, order, dtype, shapes, contiguity). Kimi K3 prompt logprobs match main bit for bit. - End to end on Kimi K3 with a 129K-token cached prefix, latency matches main within run-to-run noise. The other end-to-end runs below are up to 3.6% lower in throughput and up to 3.0% higher in median TTFT than main, one run per arm and node pair. The saving per chunk is largest for chunks of many requests (host time 3,458.7 → 48.2 us per chunk and layer at 64 requests). - `reorg_kvcache` is removed; nothing else called it. ## Validation **Per chunk and MLA layer.** One GB300 GPU, DCP 8, bf16 rows of 512 + 64 values, chunks from `build_mla_chunked_context_metadata`. title: [Bugfix][CPU] Resolve the process cgroup when reading the memory limit
summary: ## Issue `get_cgroup_memory_limit()` and `get_cgroup_memory_usage()` read `/sys/fs/cgroup` only. They miss a limit on the process cgroup or on a parent. The CPU backend then sizes the KV cache and the SHM buffers from host RAM. Fixes #64103. ## Fix - Read `/proc/self/cgroup`. Walk from the process cgroup up to the root. - `get_cgroup_memory_limit()` returns the smallest limit on that path. - `get_cgroup_memory_usage()` returns usage such that `limit - usage` is the smallest free headroom of all limited cgroups. A parent limit also counts its other children. The callers do not change. - Find the cgroup mount in `/proc/self/mountinfo`. Of the mounts that contain the process cgroup, use the one with the shortest root, so every parent limit is visible. - Off by default. `RESOLVE_PROCESS_CGROUP_BY_DEFAULT = False` sets the default in one line. `VLLM_RESOLVE_PROCESS_CGROUP=1` or `=0` overrides it. Its comment in `vllm/envs.py` generates the docs. ## Effect Three callers read these two functions. With `VLLM_RESOLVE_PROCESS_CGROUP=1` they see the limit of the process cgroup instead of the root: - `get_memory_node_info()`: the CPU worker's KV-cache budget (`total_memory × gpu_memory_utilization`) and its available-memory check; also `CpuPlatform.get_device_total_memory()` and the CPU `mem_get_info` stand-in. - `_get_available_ram_bytes()` in `weight_utils.py`: whether the checkpoint fits in 90% of available RAM, which decides safetensors prefetch on a network filesystem. - `check_cgroup_memory_available()`: the SHM preflight log. With the variable unset, every caller gets the values

title: [Perf][Attention][DCP] Gather the MLA chunked prefill context in fp8 under decode context parallelism
summary: ## Overview Stacked on #64548, which replaces `reorg_kvcache` with an index-based row gather; please review that one first. Until it merges, this PR also shows its two commits. This PR adds the last three: - `[Attention][DCP] Dequantize fp8 rows in the MLA DCP context row gather` - `[Attention][DCP] Keep the MLA DCP context in fp8 through the all-gather` - `[ROCm][DCP] Take the AITER MLA DCP context rows from the chunk metadata` (not fp8; can be dropped, see Details) With decode context parallelism (DCP), a plain fp8 KV cache and an fp8 prefill query, the MLA chunked-context loop dequantizes each rank's cached rows into a bf16 (or fp16) workspace and all-gathers those rows across the DCP group. This PR keeps the rows in fp8 as stored through the local gather and the all-gather, and dequantizes them with the layer's `k_scale` in #64548's row-gather kernel. Everything after the gather (`kv_b_proj`, the K/V pack, attention, LSE merge) gets the same tensors as before. ## Claims - Half the DCP context all-gather bytes (576 B per row instead of 1,152 B) and half the DCP context workspace. - The prefill K/V are bit-identical to the default path whenever this path is on. The kernel dequantizes like `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` (fp32 product, rounded to nearest even), and every DCP rank holds the same `k_scale`, so dequantizing after the all-gather gives the same values as dequantizing before it. This holds for any `k_scale`; the previous revision of this PR required `k_scale == 1.0`. - Off unless the backend opts in (`supports_fp8_dcp_context`, set only for `TOKENSPEED_MLA`), D

title: [Feature][Model][Kernel] Inkling: fp8 e4m3 KV cache with per-tensor scales on SM100
summary: > Depends on vllm-project/tml-fa4#4 (fp8 kernel port with the `rescale_threshold` fix). Draft until that merges and the pin is bumped; see the dependency section. title: [Core] Release DeepEP all2all buffers on sleep with comm suspend
summary: ## Purpose Part of RFC #59055 (release more GPU memory in sleep mode). With `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, sleep mode now also releases the DeepEP all2all buffers of `deepep_high_throughput` and `deepep_low_latency`. Before this change those buffers (the NVL IPC buffer, plus the NVSHMEM heap for low-latency) stayed on the GPU while the engine was asleep. How it works: - `All2AllManagerBase` gets two no-op hooks, `suspend()` and `resume()`. `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` / `resume()`, which `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` already calls on every group from `Worker.sleep()` / `wake_up()`, now call them. - `DeepEPAll2AllManagerBase.suspend()` calls `Buffer.destroy()` on every cached buffer. vLLM already creates the buffers with `explicitly_destroy=True`. - `resume()` re-runs `Buffer.__init__()` on the same Python object with its cached kwargs. The prepare/finalize objects keep a reference to that object, so they stay valid, and the handle cache still finds it. - One flag, `_suspended`, records that the buffers are destroyed. While it is set, `destroy()` (shutdown) skips them, so shutting the engine down while asleep is clean. - Both steps are collective over the EP group, like `ncclCommSuspend`: `destroy()` has GPU barriers and `__init__()` exchanges handles with `all_gather_object`. As with NCCL suspend, the engine must be idle. - With `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, `NVSHMEM_DISABLE_NCCL=1` becomes the default (a value the user sets wins). NVSHMEM otherwise builds NCCL communicators for its default teams on every init, which DeepEP never uses; they cost ~1.6 GiB/GPU while awake, ~4 s

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support FP8 KV cache for NoPE sparse MLA
summary: ## Summary - Route rope-free (NoPE) sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton kernels for every KV-cache dtype. Routing now depends only on geometry (`head_size == kv_lora_rank`) and workload, not on `kv_cache_dtype`. - Add per-tensor-scaled FP8 KV support to both Triton kernels: the ragged prefill kernel, and the split-K decode kernel from #58584. KV is upcast through BF16 in registers. K and V are the same latent row, so the scale is folded in once into the QK scale and once into the accumulator, never per tile. - Keep Q in model dtype on the Triton route. The AITER asm route and the `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` opt-in still quantize Q to FP8. - Use 64-bit query-row offsets in the ragged prefill kernel, so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic. - Preserve custom MLA geometry and the FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness. ## Problem AITER's precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. On main, FP8 NoPE requests reach the AITER path, whose 576-element assumption can read past the cache row and cause a ROCm GPU memory fault, so GLM-5.3-Flash cannot serve with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. The Triton ragged and split-K paths already handle the NoPE geometry for BF16. This PR makes their routing geometry-based, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and skips FP8-quantizing Q on that path. ## Duplicate-work check No open PR addresses ROCm NoPE FP8 sparse-attention KV rows. #39168 overlaps the ROCm ops file but changes t

summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Non-streaming tool-call parsing in `ParserEngine` runs the streaming argument-delta computation and then discards the result. summary: ## Summary - select the Marlin MoE M tile through a shared helper - let batched Marlin estimate per-expert load from the current token assignments instead of the padded capacity - retain the capacity-based fallback for direct callers DeepEP low-latency uses a capacity-padded batched expert layout. Selecting `block_size_m` from that capacity can choose a 64-row tile even when the current request has very few valid assignments per expert, adding substantial padding work. `topk_ids.numel()` is shape metadata and does not introduce a device-to-host synchronization. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs for `batched Marlin tile`, `Marlin block_size_m token load`, and `BatchedMarlinExperts padding`. - #56493 changes dense block-FP8 Marlin kernels on SM89. - #46639 pins the tile only when batch-invariant mode is enabled; its default path is unchanged. - #53875 concerns Triton FP8 activation/quantization fusion. - #51217 generalized masked activation and is complementary to this change. title: [Kernel] Support batch invariance for WNA16 Marlin MoE
summary: ## Overview Makes the WNA16 Marlin MoE GEMM (`moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`) batch-invariant under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, so quantized MoE models that run on Marlin (AWQ-INT4, GPTQ-INT4/INT8, MXFP4, NVFP4) can be served in batch-invariant mode. title: [Model] Add AnyModel: generic support for NAS-optimized heterogeneous architectures
summary: ## Summary This PR adds `AnyModel`, a generic model wrapper that enables vLLM to serve **heterogeneous, NAS-optimized models** -- models where each decoder layer can have a different configuration (varying KV heads, intermediate sizes, MoE expert counts, or entirely skipped attention/MLP blocks). This contribution comes directly from **NVIDIA**, where we produce these architectures via the [Puzzle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19146) neural architecture search framework and need first-class vLLM support to deploy them efficiently at scale. ### Motivation Modern NAS and model compression pipelines (Puzzle, Nemotron Elastic) produce models that are no longer "homogeneous" -- layers can differ in width, depth, and structure. Examples include: - **Llama-3.1-Nemotron-51B-Instruct**: a 70B Llama pruned to 51B with per-layer KV head and FFN dimension variations, fitting on a single H100 with 2.17x throughput speedup. - **gpt-oss-puzzle-88B**: a 120B MoE reasoning model compressed to 88B with heterogeneous expert pruning and selective window attention, achieving up to 2.82x throughput on a single H100. - **Nemotron Elastic** nested submodels: multiple deployment-optimized models extracted zero-shot from a single parent. Today, vLLM assumes all decoder layers share one global config. AnyModel is the **first implementation in any major serving framework** to support truly heterogeneous layer configurations. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] GDN readout: honor fp32 SSM state precision to avoid fp16 overflow → NaN
summary: ## Purpose Closes #54308. On non-Blackwell GPUs, gated-delta-net (Qwen3-Next / GDN) decode degenerates to a single infinitely-repeated token when the SSM state cache is fp32 (`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`). Once the recurrent state grows large over long context, greedy/low-temperature decoding emits one token (e.g. `!!!!…`) forever. ## Root cause `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` accumulates the readout `o = state @ q` in fp32 (`b_o` is `tl.float32`) but materialized the output tensor in the input/activation dtype: ```python o = q.new_empty(NK, *v.shape) # inherits q's dtype, e.g. fp16 ``` The GDN recurrent state is an *unnormalized* accumulator: it grows over long, low-decay context and is normalized only at the readout by `RMSNormGated`. With an fp32 state cache the readout exceeds fp16's 65504 range and overflows to `±inf` at the store; `RMSNormGated` then produces `inf / inf = NaN`, and decode collapses to a single repeated token. Blackwell does not hit this because its `fi` / `cutedsl` GDN backends run the readout in fp32; the Triton path here is the one every non-Blackwell GPU takes. ## Fix Materialize the output in the state's precision — fp32 when `initial_state` is fp32, unchanged otherwise. The fp16 path is byte-for-byte identical, so tensor-core / NVIDIA behavior is unaffected by construction. That alone only moves the overflow one line down, because the caller stores the readout into `core_attn_out`, allocated in the activation dtype (thanks @JartX for spotting this). summary: Running Qwen3-Next (GDN) on 4x MI50 (gfx906, ROCm) with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`, decode eventually collapses to a single token repeated forever (`!!!!!!...`) once a conversation gets long enough. title: Decode optimizations for NVIDIA confidential computing
summary: ## Background Confidential Computing (CC) is a feature of NVIDIA GPUs (Hopper and later) that protects workloads running in a confidential VM from infrastructure operators. It implements a range of security features on the GPU, including encrypted data transfers over PCIe and between GPUs. CC is designed to require no code changes for existing applications, albeit often at a performance penalty. Running vLLM under CC, we measured a significant degradation in both prefill and decode performance relative to non-CC operation. We traced the decode degradation to CUDA async memcpy behavior under CC's bounce-buffer encryption: a host<->device `cudaMemcpyAsync` on pinned memory becomes **host-synchronous** — the issuing thread blocks until the copy *and everything already queued on its stream* completes. This hurts the engine in two ways: 1. **H2D input copies** issued on the compute stream during `_prepare_inputs` block the scheduler thread for the duration of the in-flight forward pass (~one full step per copy), starving the GPU of work. 2. **The per-step D2H token readback** blocks the thread that issues it, delaying the next step's CUDA graph launch by roughly one decode step. ## Changes All changes are gated on CC detection and are no-ops otherwise; the non-CC code paths are untouched. - **CC detection** (`Platform.is_confidential_compute()`): auto-detected once via NVML, with a `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0/1` env override for testing and for hosts without NVML. - **Staged H2D input copies** (`StagedH2DCopier`, `prep_stream_ctx` in `vllm/v1/conf_compute_utils.py`): the H2D la

title: [Kimi K3][Kernel] Enable residual skinny GEMM on SM100
summary: ## Summary This PR connects Kimi-K3's existing residual skinny-GEMM API to the production latent-MoE output transform and adds measured SM100 configurations for the local `BF16[M, 3584] @ BF16[7168, 3584].T + residual` routed up-projection. For supported decode token counts, the CuTeDSL kernel performs the GEMM and residual add in one epilogue; unsupported token counts, layouts, dtypes, and devices retain the existing in-place `residual.addmm_` fallback. This extends #53534 rather than duplicating it: #53534 installed SM100 low-latency methods for ordinary linear calls, but the SM100 residual table was empty and `KimiRoutedOutputTransform` called `addmm_` directly, so `apply_with_residual` had no production caller. #54151 optimizes SP communication around the latent tail and does not cover this residual up-projection. This change has no DeepGEMM dependency and is independent of shared-expert fusion. The dispatch is intentionally local to `KimiRoutedOutputTransform`. Existing whole-tail fusion may bypass this transform for some TP8/PP2 small-batch configurations; this PR accelerates paths that reach the native/fallback latent output transform. ## Performance Measured on one NVIDIA B200 GPU with CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.13.0. Each point is the median of 31 measurements, each measurement replays a CUDA Graph 200 times, and eight weight/residual pairs rotate over more than 3x L2 capacity. | Local tokens `M` | cuBLAS `addmm` | CuTe residual GEMM | Latency change | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 12.533 us | 9.395 us | **-25.03%** | | 2 | 12.928 us | 10.386 us | **-19.66%** |

title: [Quantization] Support tensor parallelism for block-diagonal compressed-tensors Hadamard transforms
summary: ## Overview Allow compressed-tensors online Hadamard transforms to run with tensor parallelism. Previously, any online transform with TP > 1 raised `NotImplementedError`. ## Claims - **Block-diagonal transforms (`head_dim` set, e.g. QuIP):** `HadamardTransform` accepts TP > 1 when `head_dim` divides the per-rank size the transform acts on. That size is the input partition for input transforms and `output_partition_sizes[i]` for output transforms. Otherwise it raises `NotImplementedError`, naming the layer, the scheme and the sizes. - **Full-width transforms (no `head_dim`):** supported on dimensions that are not split across ranks, i.e. the input of column-parallel layers and the output of row-parallel layers. On a split dimension, the replicated checkpoint matrix is larger than the per-rank partition, so loading fails on the shape check. - **Loading:** `SharedWeightParameter` partitions are replicated on every rank. Each loader copies the full matrix with `BasevLLMParameter._assert_and_load` instead of sharding it. The shape check is kept, so a malformed or mis-sharded matrix fails at load instead of being broadcast. - **Docs:** documented TP support and its limits in `docs/features/quantization/README.md` (Hadamard Input Transforms section). ## Validation ### `test_compressed_tensors_transforms_perplexity` (threshold 150) | Model | Transform | TP | 2× RTX 5060 Ti (SM120) | 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) | |---|---|---:|---|---| | `spinquantR1R2R4-w4a16` | full width + `head_dim=64` | 1 | passed, 110.37 | passed | | `quip-w4a16` | full width | 1 | passed, 134.49 | passed | | `

This draft extracts the measured implementation onto current main; GPU validation of this rebased PR head is pending. ## Claims - `additional_config.gdn_norm_quant_decode=true` selects the fused producer only for eligible physical decode batches of 1 or 2. title: [Bugfix] Await the accepted-token copy before moving batch rows
summary: ## Purpose Fixes silent output corruption on hybrid (Mamba/GDN) models running speculative decoding with `--enable-prefix-caching`, which forces `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, and async scheduling. Step N copies the accepted-token counts D2H non-blocking into the pinned `input_batch.num_accepted_tokens_cpu_tensor`, in step N's row order. Step N+1's `_update_states` permutes that same buffer on the host - `add_request`, `swap_states`, `condense` - without waiting on the event, and `_prepare_inputs` only syncs afterwards, then applies the `prev_positions` gather. The gather is therefore correct only when the DMA lands after the row moves. Under host load the GPU runs ahead, the copy lands early, `condense()` has already mapped the values into current order, and the gather permutes them a second time. The request gets another request's count, which becomes its conv-window shift and its GDN snapshot selector, and the wrongly gated state is written back into the SSM cache, so it does not self-correct. Nothing is raised. The non-align async path is already excluded from reading these counts for this reason, but align is the one mode that needs them on the CPU. Wait on the event in `_update_states` before the first row move, and drop the gather, which is redundant once the copy has landed first. Both halves are needed: the wait alone is worse (7.6% vs 4.3% baseline), because it guarantees the early landing that triggers the double permute. ## Test Plan Standalone repro, stdlib only: send one ~59k-token document repeatedly, each time asking for a different labelled six-digit code insi

summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Encoder (ViT) CUDA graphs only help while eager is bound by host launch time. This PR applies one rule to every model, in the style of the LLM's CUDA graphs: - **One replay per batch.** A batch replays the smallest budget that holds it; anything else runs as one eager forward. - **A finer budget grid up to one global maximum.** The new `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (default 5120) works like the LLM's maximum capture size. summary: Fixes #60981 ## Purpose In `vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer_gpu.py:340`, `NgramProposerGPU.propose` hardcodes `assert num_speculative_tokens == self.k`. title: [Feature] Restore concurrent partial prefill limit (max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler
summary: Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413. As detailed in #57413, without a cap on concurrent partial prefills, long-context RAG workloads (e.g. 100k+ tokens) completely stall V1's scheduling queue. Short requests are forced to wait for many iterations until massive partial prefills finish. This reintroduces `max_concurrent_prefills` directly into the V1 scheduler's `WAITING` loop. By bounding how many requests can simultaneously hold partial prefill state, we allow interleaving and dramatically reduce tail TTFT (as validated by the community on 4x B200 / GLM-5.3-Flash). Original patch credit to @fululi12 in #55256. Rebased and verified against main. Fixes #57413.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fix prompt_logprobs=0 bypassing admission guards and chat echo

title: [Bugfix][Kernel][MoE] Zero-expert identity kernel silently drops output for hidden_dim not a multiple of 256
summary: ## Purpose **Bug: the zero-expert (identity) MoE kernel silently returns wrong output whenever `hidden_dim` is not a multiple of 256.** `zero_experts_compute_triton` / `compute_identity_kernel` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py` compute, per token, `out[t] = hidden_states[t] * sum_k(zero_expert_scales[t, k])`. The kernel is launched on a **floor-division** grid: ```python grid = lambda meta: (num_tokens * (hidden_dim // meta["BLOCK_SIZE"]),) # BLOCK_SIZE = 256 ``` and the kernel recovers `(batch_id, dim_offset)` from that same floor division. So: - For `hidden_dim` **not** a multiple of 256, the **tail block is never launched**. Those elements are returned as `0` instead of a scaled hidden value. The output looks plausible — there is no error, no NaN, just a silently truncated row. It is masked today only because the output happens to be allocated with `torch.zeros_like`. - For `hidden_dim < 256`, the grid is `num_tokens * 0 = 0`: the kernel **never runs at all** and the entire output is zeros. The bug is currently baked into the test suite as an assumption (`hidden_size must be >= 256 ... BLOCK_SIZE=256 causes grid=0 when hidden_dim<256`) rather than being fixed. This path is reachable in-tree: `FusedMoEFactory` wires it through `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/zero_expert_router.py` (`ZeroExpertRouter._compute_routing`) for `zero_expert_type="identity"` models such as LongCat-Flash / DeepSeek-style MoE. ### Fix Launch a **2-D ceil-div grid** `(num_tokens, triton.cdiv(hidden_dim, BLOCK_SIZE))` — axis 0 is the token row, axis 1 a `BLOCK_SIZE`

title: [Core][Scheduler] Add opt-in aging to cache-aware admission
summary: ## Overview `--cache-aware-admission-window` (#54625) lets waiting requests with a cached prefix go ahead of requests that would have to compute theirs. Nothing limits how often a request can be passed, so an older request with no cached prefix can be bypassed again and again by newer cache-warm requests for as long as they keep arriving. This PR adds the optional `--cache-aware-admission-max-wait-ms`. It defaults to `0` (disabled), which keeps current scheduling behavior. With a positive value, a request in the window that has waited that long can no longer be passed by cached peers, and expired requests are admitted in the order the scheduler received them. Related: #54625 (merged; introduced the window), #53277 (cache-aware waiting QoS). This PR is independent of #66331 (see Details). ## Claims - **Opt-in bound on cache-based bypass.** With `window > 0` and `max_wait_ms > 0`, no reorder pass moves a younger request ahead of one that has waited `max_wait_ms`. Expired requests go first, in scheduler receive order. - **Default unchanged.** With `window = 0`, FCFS is untouched. With `window > 0` and `max_wait_ms = 0`, ordering is behaviorally equivalent to #54625. - **No admission guarantee.** The setting only stops cached peers from passing a request. It does not admit a request when KV cache space or a running slot is unavailable, and it is not a TTFT guarantee. - **Small.** +52/−3 production lines and one config field with its CLI flag. No changes to `Request`, `RequestQueue`, `KVCacheManager` or connectors. ## Validation > **Who ran what.** Every test result in this sect

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clamp token_indices_to_sample to the request's first query row
summary: ## [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Clamp token_indices_to_sample to the request's first query row Fixes #60897 ## Purpose `eagle_prepare_inputs_padded_kernel` (vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py) computes `index_to_sample = q_last_tok_idx - num_rejected_tokens` without a lower bound. When a request's query carries fewer rows than the rejection count assumes, the index underflows past the start of the request: - For the first request, the index is negative → out-of-bounds gather. - For any later request, the index lands inside the **previous request's** rows → silently cross-wired sampled tokens and corrupted drafting. The underflow is reachable when the query has no bonus-token row. With PP > 1, the scheduler can schedule only the draft tokens (`num_scheduled_tokens == num_draft_tokens`), while `valid_sampled_tokens_count` still assumes the bonus row is present (`num_rejected_tokens = num_draft_tokens + 1 - valid_count`). The same unclamped formula exists in the CPU implementation (csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp), so both backends are affected. Downstream, `token_indices_to_sample` is consumed by `drafter.propose(...)` to select per-request sampled tokens (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py), so an out-of-range index corrupts every subsequent decode step. ## Reproducer Unit-level, hermetic (no network, no gated models). Runs on any CUDA GPU (e.g., an RTX 3090 24GB) — the kernel is pure integer index arithmetic, so the bug is hardware-independent: ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_prepare_inputs_padded_index_stays_within_request_rows -x -q ``` Two requests, 2

title: [Multimodal] Refactor encoder cuda graph to support share graph buffer reuse
summary: <!-- vLLM PR description format: Purpose / Test Plan / Test Result --> ## Purpose Encoder CUDA graphs are captured once per token budget, and every captured graph allocates its own full set of I/O buffers sized by that budget. That per-budget O(budget) memory cost is the only reason the default budget table is a coarse power-of-2 ladder — which forces ~33% average padding waste (round-up to the next power of two). This PR removes the memory cost **generically, with zero model changes**, following the decoder's `input_ids[:num_tokens]` pattern: 1. **Universal shared capture buffers.** At capture time the manager keeps the first (largest) budget's buffers per (path, axis) as the shared allocation; for every later budget it probes shapes via the model's unmodified `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs()` and, per buffer key, checks prefix compatibility (same ndim/trailing dims/dtype, rows fit). Compatible keys capture into a prefix view of the shared buffer (probe content is copied in so the capture-time forward sees correct metadata); incompatible keys silently keep their per-budget allocation. Scalars are shared by identity. This works because all encoder buffers are packed-contiguous row buffers and replay only ever writes `buf[:real_rows]`. Output buffers are shared the same way. No protocol changes, no model changes, no config knobs. 2. **Subdivided default budget table.** With extra graphs costing ~zero buffer memory, the auto-inferred default becomes a subdivided table (4 steps per octave up to 1024, 2 above; 64→16384 = 25 tiers, expected padding waste ~10% vs ~33%

title: [Perf] TurboQuant: run spec-decode verify batches as decodes with FULL cudagraphs
summary: ## Purpose Performance follow-up to #53406 (the correctness fix for #52475). That fix stopped FULL cudagraph capture of spec-decode verify batches because the TurboQuant path serving them (the per-request Python prefill loop) is not graph-capturable. Correct, but expensive: with MTP enabled, every verify step runs the attention eagerly with per-layer Python iteration and CPU-resident metadata, and measured decode throughput dropped well below the fp8 KV baseline. This PR teaches the backend spec-as-decode so verify batches run as decode batches and FULL cudagraphs come back: 1. title: [Core][KVConnector] Keep the offloaded KV tier across pause/sleep
summary: ## Summary `pause`/`sleep` exist to hand GPU memory back. An external KV connector tier (CPU/SSD offload) is the one cache that *survives* that handover, and the pause/sleep cascade evicts it. For an RL rollout that time-shares the GPU (`sleep(1)` → train → `wake_up()`), that tier is what makes resumption cheap: without it the resume re-prefills every in-flight sample. Whether the tier is still valid depends on the caller replacing the weights, which the engine cannot know at pause time. Block hashes do not cover the weights, so the default stays "evict" and this adds an opt-out: ```python llm.sleep(level=1, clear_connector_cache=False) # same weights on wake-up ``` Threaded through `pause_scheduler`/`sleep` to `_reset_caches(reset_connector=)`, the Python and Rust clients, and `/pause` and `/sleep`. Default `True` everywhere, so nothing changes unless a caller opts out. The Rust client sends the argument only when opting out, so a new frontend still drives an older engine. ## Measured 2x GB200, slurm job 30001, on the nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.29.1rc1.dev422`), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this branch's files bind-mounted over the image one by one (mounting the whole package would hide the compiled `_C` that ships in it). title: [Core] Add cache_salt_start_idx for divergence-point prefix-cache salting
summary: ## [Core] Divergence-point prefix-cache salting: `cache_salt_start_idx` ### Motivation `cache_salt` today is all-or-nothing. A salted request isolates its **entire** block-hash chain, so two tenants on the same deployment never share a single cached block — even when their prompts begin with the same thousands of tokens (shared system prompts, RAG preambles, agent scaffolds). That is the all-or-nothing tradeoff documented in "Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference" ([arXiv:2608.09225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09225)), which proposes salting only from the point where prompts diverge. The timing side channel that motivates isolation is real and measured: "The Early Bird Catches the Leak" ([arXiv:2409.20002](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20002)) recovered other tenants' prompts through response-time differences, and an audit of 17 API providers ([arXiv:2502.07776](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07776), ICML 2025) found cross-tenant cache sharing at 7 of them. On this engine the membership oracle gap measured **5.3x** (79 ms cached vs 414 ms one-character-off, Qwen2.5-0.5B, CPU) with full secret recovery in 12 probes. This PR adds an optional `cache_salt_start_idx` so a deployment can keep the shared, public part of its prompts cached across tenants while keeping the private part tenant-isolated. ### Design - `Request`/`EngineCoreRequest` gain `cache_salt_start_idx: int | None`. - `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` applies the salt to blocks whose start token index is `>= cache_salt_start_idx`. title: [Bugfix][MRV1] Stage consistent FULL dummy metadata
summary: ## Purpose The V1 model runner's FULL CUDA-graph profiling can stage a long dummy sequence length without staging matching absolute token positions. MiniMax-M3's MSA indexer derives causal page counts from those positions, while sparse decode derives the number of entries to consume from sequence lengths. Specifically, `MiniMaxM3IndexerMSAMetadataBuilder.build()` computes `num_valid_pages = positions // 128 + 1` and supplies it to `sparse_topk_select`, which pads out-of-range selections with `-1`. Sparse decode instead consumes `min(topk, ceil(kv_len / 128))` entries based on `seq_lens`. Stale short positions paired with long dummy sequence lengths therefore leave sentinels inside that consumed range. Stage the same length/position invariants used by real batches: - `seq_len == num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens` - `positions == num_computed_tokens[req_indices] + query_pos` Also clear scheduled/computed lengths for padded request rows and positions for padded tokens. title: [RFC]: Confident Decoding — entropy-guided intermediate-layer logits selection
summary: # [RFC]: Confident Decoding — entropy-guided intermediate-layer logits selection ## Summary We propose adding **Confident Decoding** to vLLM: a training-free decoding strategy that dynamically selects logits from near-final intermediate layers instead of always using the final layer. Layer selection is guided by prediction entropy (conservative backward search for the first entropy valley closest to the final layer). This is the inference implementation accompanying our paper: > **Deeper is Not Always Better: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Confident Layer Decoding** > Xuanming Zhang, Sining Zhoubian, Yuxuan Chen, et al. > arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21906 The paper shows consistent gains on challenging reasoning benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, Omni-MATH, HLE) across dense and MoE LLMs, with zero memory overhead and <2% latency increase. ## Motivation Standard autoregressive decoding always uses logits from the **final** transformer layer. Our work reveals a recurring **Guess-Refine-Perturb** dynamic: early layers form coarse guesses, intermediate layers refine reasoning-relevant semantics, and final layers can perturb refined predictions toward generic or alignment-preferred tokens. Confident Decoding bypasses harmful final-layer perturbations by selecting the most confident near-final layer at each token position. ## Proposed API Enabled via `--additional-config` (no recompilation required): ```bash vllm serve /path/to/model \ --additional-config '{ "enable_multi_layer_entropy_selection": true, "select_method": "trough", "p": 1.0, "trough_max_backtrack_layers": 10 }' ```

title: [RFC]: Optimizing Asynchronous Stream Serialization in OpenAI API Entrypoint
summary: ### Motivation. Currently, vLLM’s OpenAI-compatible API server processes incoming HTTP requests and handles request streaming on a unified FastAPI event loop. While this architecture performs exceptionally well for text-only inputs, it introduces severe performance regressions under concurrent multimodal workloads (e.g., high-resolution Vision-Language Models or video input processing). When a request containing large base64-encoded images or video frames hits the /v1/chat/completions endpoint, the payload validation (via Pydantic), base64 decoding, and initial tensor formatting happen in a way that blocks the main asynchronous event loop. During local profiling under a simulated load of 50 concurrent connections, processing a request with multiple high-res image inputs blocks the FastAPI event loop for up to 42ms to 65ms. Because the AsyncLLMEngine scheduling loop relies on this same event loop to fetch tokens and step the engine, this starvation directly causes severe spikes in Inter-Token Latency (ITL) and Time-to-First-Token (TTFB) across all concurrent requests on the instance, completely neutralizing continuous batching efficiency. ### Proposed Change. I propose decoupling the heavy ingress payload ingestion from the critical engine scheduling path by refactoring the vllm/entrypoints/openai layer: **Offloaded Ingress Processing:** Move base64 decoding, multimodal payload parsing, and structural validation entirely off the main FastAPI event loop into an asynchronous worker pool using a configured ProcessPoolExecutor or dedicated CPU ingress threads. **Zero-Copy Shared

title: [RFC]: Remove Group Activation Ordering (actorder=group) Support from vLLM and Compression Libraries
summary: ## Motivation This RFC proposes the removal of runtime group activation ordering (actorder) support from vLLM, compressed-tensors, and llm-compressor. This affects GPTQ quantized models (W4A16, W8A16, and other WNA16 variants) that use `actorder=group` during quantization. **Key motivations:** 1. **Limited kernel support**: Modern high-performance kernels (Humming, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer) do not support `g_idx`-based runtime reordering. title: [RFC]: Support router-driven mixtures of multiple LoRA adapters
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM currently supports serving one LoRA adapter per request and supports LoRA weights for MoE base-model experts. It does not support router-driven mixtures of multiple LoRA adapters within one request, token, or layer. This blocks inference for adapter-MoE approaches such as X-LoRA ([Buehler and Buehler, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07148)), MixLoRA ([Li et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15159)), and Riemannian MoE-LoRA ([Sun et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15828)) where the serving-time forward form is: $$\text{base}(x) + \sum_i \text{gate}_i(x) \times \text{LoRA}_i(x)$$ The goal is to add serving support for multiple active LoRA adapters whose contributions are selected or weighted by a router. ## Current Behavior Today, `LoRARequest` represents a single adapter, and runtime LoRA metadata maps tokens to one LoRA id. Existing fused MoE LoRA support is for applying LoRA to MoE model experts, not for treating LoRA adapters themselves as routed experts. ### Proposed Change. Add an experimental multi-adapter LoRA routing path with these stages: 1. Add internal data structures for representing multiple active LoRA adapters for one request. 2. Add a reference implementation that computes weighted adapter mixtures in PyTorch for correctness. 3. Add optimized kernels / Punica integration after the semantics are validated. 4. Add docs, examples, and benchmarks. Initial supported mode: - Inference only. - Same base model. - Multiple already-loaded LoRA adapters. - Per-token or per-layer routing weights supplied by an internal router interface. -

title: No capability flag declares which KV-cache kinds may be peeked past a candidate boundary — each margin implementation excludes Mamba by hand
summary: **Related:** #43559 · #50188 · #38182 · #50438 (RFC) · #48375 · #48970 · #50021 ## Summary vLLM's EAGLE-style prefix-cache path grants a lookahead margin of one cache unit past the candidate hit length, then relies on each cache manager to drop it again. Full-attention and sliding-window managers honour that drop. `MambaManager` does not: `find_longest_cache_hit` takes `drop_eagle_block` and never reads it (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1280-1357` — the identifier appears once, in the signature). `ChunkedLocalAttentionManager` handles the same situation by asserting the flag is `False`, which is the safe pattern. The user-visible failure is silent output corruption — in #43559, an accuracy drop of roughly twenty points with no crash, no warning and no log line; the same family's tail includes null completions and degenerate token loops. That asymmetry is not itself the interesting part — it is now masked by caller-side carve-outs. The interesting part is that **nothing in the tree declares the property**. `supports_eagle_cache_peek`, or any equivalent, returns zero hits repo-wide. Because no manager announces "this cache kind cannot be rewound," every **margin implementation** — a place that computes the lookahead margin — has to know about Mamba by hand. There are four; three needed the identical carve-out and received it at three different times, and the fourth never needed one only because its author independently restricted the peek to sliding-window groups: | Margin implementation | Carve-out landed | |---|---| | `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` |

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] MRV2 AutoRegressiveSpeculator ignores dynamic K from scheduler — DSD non-functional on MRV2
summary: ## Summary When using `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (MRV2) with dynamic speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`), the `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` ignores the scheduler's per-step dynamic K selection and always runs the full static-K draft pipeline. At K=0 batch sizes, the speculator runs full draft prefill + multi-step decode — producing draft tokens that are immediately rejected because the scheduler allocated 0 spec slots. title: [Perf] Sample in log space in TopKTopPSampler.forward_native, skipping the full-vocab softmax
summary: ## Purpose `TopKTopPSampler.forward_native` computes `probs = logits.softmax(-1)` only to feed the exponential-noise Gumbel trick, `argmax(probs / q)`. The softmax normalizer is constant per row and exp is monotonic, so `argmax(logits - log q)` selects the same token — the full-vocab softmax kernel is unnecessary. The MRV2 sampler's Triton gumbel kernel already samples straight from logits; this brings the V1 sampler in line (still the live path for hybrid/GDN models and any non-MRV2 deployment). Merged precedent for the same idea on another path: #32852 (skip softmax for all-greedy rejection sampling). `forward_native` is what actually runs whenever FlashInfer bails: per-request generators (seeded sampling), `use_fp64_gumbel`, processed logprobs modes, or FlashInfer unavailable. In a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 batch-16 seeded decode profile the softmax was ~93 µs/step on top of the top-k/top-p kernel. One measured exception stays on the old path: **fully-seeded batches**. There `random_sample` skips the bulk noise fill, the launch-bound per-row generator loop dominates, and the softmax hides completely under it — while log-space would serialize an extra full-vocab pass after the loop (+8.5% at B=256 all-seeded, stable across 3 repeats). Mixed and unseeded batches draw bulk noise, where the softmax is on the critical path and skipping it wins. ## Results RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), V=151936, k=20/p=0.95, median of 80 pristine-input iters (inputs restored outside the timing window — the masking is in-place, so naive loops feed `-inf`-heavy rows back in and measure the wrong work): | B |

title: [Spec Decode] Batch invariance: speculative_config.batch_invariant lets the drafter skip batch-invariant MoE kernels
summary: ## Overview Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `--speculative-config '{..., "batch_invariant": false}'` lets the speculative drafter select MoE kernels that are not batch invariant. The drafter only proposes tokens; the batch-invariant target verifies them and decides every output token and logprob. This lets speculative decoding use faster drafter kernels while batch invariance is kept for train-inference consistency (e.g. RL rollouts). Leaving the field unset (default `None`) keeps today's behavior; without `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` the field has no effect. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FA sliding window active under batch invariance
summary: ## Overview With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, keep FlashAttention's sliding window active in every step, so Gemma-2 outputs on H100 (FA3) no longer depend on which requests share the batch. Fixes #65587 ## Claims - Fixes #65587: under batch invariance, a sliding-window request on FA3 gives the same tokens and bitwise-equal logprobs alone as when it decodes next to other requests' prefill chunks. - A 9-line change in `FlashAttentionImpl.forward`. It only runs with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on layers that have a sliding window; every other configuration is unchanged. - Adds `test_sliding_window_logprobs_bitwise_alone_vs_mixed_batch` to `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`, which the existing H100 and B200 batch invariance CI jobs already run. ## Validation [@imthomp ran the fix on an H100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65627#issuecomment-6634783966) (vLLM nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev454 plus this diff): the issue reproducer went from 5/20 differing prompts to 0/20. title: [Core] Reserve FlashInfer's persistent workspace before KV cache sizing
summary: ## Purpose FlashInfer builds its wrappers lazily. Each wrapper owns an int workspace allocated when it is constructed, and the shared float arena grows on first use, so on a fresh engine none of it exists while `determine_available_memory()` runs. The closing measurement of `memory_profiling` never sees it, and the KV cache is sized as if that memory were free. It is taken back on the first real request. This PR builds that workspace inside the profiling window instead, holds it until the closing measurement has read it, and locks the shared arena once the last warmup that could still grow it has run. ## What changed since the last review The core diff is down from ~900 added lines to ~550, and the mechanism it replaces was unsound. The earlier revision let each builder take the arena as it went and rebound the wrappers afterwards. That does not hold: FlashInfer's prefill wrapper records its float workspace size in `__init__` and `reset_workspace_buffer()` does not refresh it, so a wrapper built against a small arena and rebound to a larger one keeps handing the kernel the old size. So the order is inverted. One pass over every builder sizes the float arena and the module-global trtllm buffer; a second pass builds the wrappers against the arena that is now final. The weakref registry, the rebind hook and the reset bookkeeping are gone with it. Two smaller corrections came out of the same pass. summary: ## Background Issue #64853 requested a new behavior for `reset_prefix_cache` that clears the prefix cache without preempting running requests. The endpoint currently offers two behaviors while requests are running: - **Default mode**: the reset fails (`success: false`) while any block is held by running requests. Under sustained load, the window where nothing is in flight can be vanishingly small or absent entirely. - **`reset_running_requests=true`**: the reset succeeds, but every running request is preempted and restarts from scratch, adding repeated prefill work on top of the cache-loss shock. Neither mode lets operators separate the effect of losing the cache from the effect of restarting all running requests. ## Problem There was no way to invalidate all prefix-cache hashes while keeping in-flight requests undisturbed. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: apply each fused shard's own global scale
summary: ## Purpose The NVFP4 linear kernels take one global weight scale per layer. For a fused layer (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) whose shards store different ones, the ModelOpt scheme (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16) kept the largest and the compressed-tensors scheme kept the smallest, and both only warned. Every other shard was then dequantized with the wrong scale. ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often differ. title: [Bugfix] Reject shape-aliased prefills in uniform-decode classification
summary: ## Purpose FIX #53051 (same root cause as #49918) With spec decode enabled, `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` classifies batches by shape only. A prefill whose scheduled tokens equal `uniform_decode_query_len (= 1 + num_spec_tokens)` per request — e.g. a single (k+1)-token prompt — aliases the uniform-decode shape and is dispatched into the FULL cudagraph captured for spec decode. For attention backends with persistent metadata buffers (e.g. GDN / hybrid recurrent models), those buffers are only refreshed on the decode path, so the replay uses stale capture-time state indices (NULL block 0); the kernels' null-block guards silently skip all recurrent-state writes, the request's state stays zero forever, and output is deterministic garbage (details and measured evidence in #53051). This PR makes `_is_uniform_decode` additionally require that every request in the batch is already past its prompt (`num_computed_tokens >= num_prompt_tokens`), so any batch still containing prefill tokens falls back to the mixed prefill-decode path. The `force_uniform_decode` override used for cudagraph capture is preserved unchanged. **Relationship to #47123:** that PR addresses the same root cause by computing `force_uniform_decode=False` in `execute_model` when a hybrid model's batch contains context requests. This PR is an alternative that fixes the classification at its source instead: the diff is smaller (no new caller-side state), it applies to all models rather than only `is_hybrid` (the q_len==1 aliasing of 1-token prompts exists without spec decode too), and the per-request check also

title: [RFC]: Limit the use of envvars in vLLM
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM's envvars are on the edge of getting out of control. There are many envvars should instead be configs. Like the attention backend, all2all kernel backend, and even there is a flag to control KV cache layout. envvars are evil because: 1. It is equivalent of using global variables everywhere in the code, which is a bad programming practice. 2. envvars have no advanced structure like, hierarchy, typechecks, etc. In summary, I think envvars are the kind of thing that is very easy to add so people tend to add envvars as the shortest path to implement their feature, but this can quickly becomes unmanageable and makes the project very hard to use. ### Proposed Change. I think we should: 1. Spend some effort on reviewing the current envvars and move many of them to configs. 2. Have very strict bar on what can be an envvar and question every new envvars in vllm. ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Core] Add collective_rpc_per_engine to return every data-parallel engine's worker results
summary: With data parallelism, `EngineClient.collective_rpc` reaches every engine but returns only the first engine's worker results (`DPLBAsyncMPClient.call_utility_async`), so a caller cannot see what the other engines' workers returned. RL integrations that drive weight updates from the API server need every worker's answer, for example to know whether every worker could prepare an update before any applies it, and today they reach into `engine_core.call_utility_all_async` the way `compute_weight_checksums` does internally. This adds `collective_rpc_per_engine` to `EngineClient` and `AsyncLLM`, which returns each engine's worker results in engine order; `collective_rpc` is unchanged. Tested with a unit test next to the existing DPLB checksum test, which checks that a two-engine client returns both engines' results and that `collective_rpc_async` still returns the first engine's. The same call path drives in-place weight updates in a prime-rl run on 3 servers of 4 data-parallel engines with tensor parallel 2 and expert parallel.

The scores are bitwise identical to the unsplit plan. ## Claims - **Bitwise identical scores.** Split and unsplit scores are equal by construction. This is checked with `torch.equal` in the new SM100 test. - **No change to the default output path.** The split defaults to off. The sync-free metadata produces the same plan inputs and the same page table as before; only how they are computed changes. - **Fewer GPU stalls on prefill steps.** The metadata build no longer calls `seq_lens.cpu()` or does a boolean-mask gather, so it does not wait for the GPU queue to drain. - **Faster deep-context prefill scoring (split on).** Before this change, a short chunk at 200k context ran the index score on 11 of 148 CTAs. That score took 37% of the step in a B300 trace (see Validation). On an older nightly, end-to-end gains were +4.8% to +8.0% p90 tok/s/user and +1.6% to +3.0% tok/s/GPU (see Validation for caveats). ## Validation **Unit tests (CPU).** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_ind
