title: [Bug]: NCCL symmetric all-reduce uses the wrong group when TP and ETP differ
summary: ## Your current environment Linux, four RTX 6000D GPUs on one host, NVIDIA driver 595.71.05, Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, and the official CUDA wheel for vLLM `f98575ec133dce6a759d1d0f27667eb246fc3123`. ## Describe the bug With `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1`, an Engram embedding tensor parallel (ETP) all-reduce can return sums for the tensor parallel (TP) subgroup when TP and ETP have different memberships. In a four-rank reproduction with TP=2, DP=2, and ETP=4, a tiny Qwen4Exp checkpoint loaded through eager `LLM.generate` hit `ETP_WRONG_GROUP_TP2`. Both observed ETP all-reduces differed from the four-rank reference and matched each rank's own TP2 reference. The independent four-rank NCCL window control returned the correct sum of 15 on all ranks. The regression creates its checkpoint locally. See https://gist.github.com/jackLei0901/9885b172cf0465111bc6c28efc461181 for the test-only patch, the exact pytest node and the redacted traceback. The process-wide custom op is registered once with a closure over the first PyNCCL communicator. Later calls pass the tensor without the calling group's identity, so an ETP call can reuse the TP communicator.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Use promised max_query_len for encoder-only FULL CUDA graphs
summary: ## Overview With the V2 model runner, models whose attention is encoder-only (non-causal, no KV cache) produce wrong outputs when they are served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL`. A FULL CUDA graph for mixed batches is captured on a dummy batch that spreads its tokens over many requests (down to one token each), but it may later replay a batch with one long prompt. `DefaultModelState` already builds the captured attention metadata from the batch's promised `max_query_len` for this reason. `EncoderOnlyModelState` instead used the dummy batch's actual largest query length, so the encoder attention kernels in the graph kept a very short `max_seqlen_q` / `max_seqlen_k`. Prompts that replay such a graph are then computed incorrectly. There is no error. The fix applies the same rule as `DefaultModelState`: use `input_batch.max_query_len` when the batch sets it, and fall back to the largest scheduled query length otherwise. ```python max_query_len = input_batch.max_query_len if max_query_len is None: max_query_len = int(input_batch.num_scheduled_tokens.max()) ``` One file changed (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py`), plus a regression test. ## Claims - Encoder-only models served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL` give the same outputs as eager execution. - No change for `PIECEWISE` or `NONE`, for decoder models, or for batches without FULL graphs. - With the fix, FULL graphs are a correct option for these models: slightly faster single-request reads than PIECEWISE, about equal under load (table below). ## Validation | test | hardware | main | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `tests/

title: [Performance]: ~1.4 s gpt-oss serving stalls from per-batch-size recompiles of the bundled triton_kernels v3.5.1 routing kernels
summary: ### Report of performance regression Serving `gpt-oss-120b` with the default Triton MXFP4 MoE path, every step whose token count is above the CUDA graph capture range (1024) and falls into a 32-token bucket the process has not seen before takes 1.3 to 1.5 s regardless of its size, several times what the same step costs once the kernels are compiled. Mixed prefill/decode steps hit this constantly, and it does not settle quickly: with long prompts at concurrency 64 to 128 we still saw 10 to 19 of these stalls per benchmark window in a third repeat, 7 to 9 minutes and 1,700 to 2,500 requests into the server's life. ITL p99 sits at ~1.5 s in every configuration (with and without spec decode), which is the length of one stall. **Root cause.** CUDA builds fetch `triton_kernels` at `v3.5.1` (`cmake/external_projects/triton_kernels.cmake`, pinned in #43135). In that version `_topk_forward` (`stride_rm`, `stride_rn`) and `_sum_bitmatrix_rows` (`stride_bm`, `stride_bn`) declare the bitmatrix strides `tl.constexpr`, and `topk_forward` allocates the bitmatrix with `stride(1) = cdiv(n_rows, 32) * 32`. Every new 32-row bucket is therefore a new specialization, and both kernels compile on the request path. Upstream Triton fixed exactly this in triton-lang/triton#10875 (reported in triton-lang/triton#10872 as recurring ~1 s TTFT stalls on gpt-oss-120b), but `v3.5.1` predates it. title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix padding isolation in FunASR adaptor attention
summary: ## Purpose `FunASRForConditionalGeneration` uses an audio adaptor to downsample and project audio-encoder features before the LLM consumes them. The adaptor pads each row to the longest feature sequence in the scheduled batch. However, `EncoderLayer.forward` currently calls adaptor self-attention without length metadata: ```python self.self_attn(hidden_states, None, None) ``` A short request's valid frames can therefore attend to its right-padding positions introduced by longer batch-mates. Its transcription can change depending on the other requests in the batch. The reference FunASR adaptor (`funasr/models/llm_asr/adaptor.py`) does not have this issue because it builds a padding mask from the real feature lengths and passes it through every block. This PR derives the length metadata from the adaptor's post-downsampling output lengths and routes the three representations expected by `MMEncoderAttention` through every adaptor block: `cu_seqlens` stores the cumulative boundaries of the packed segments, `max_seqlen` stores the longest segment length for kernels that need it, and `sequence_lengths` stores each individual segment length for backends that consume explicit lengths. Carrying all three lets `MMEncoderAttention` select the representation required by its active backend without reconstructing or losing the padding boundaries. - Each padded row contributes a valid-prefix segment and, when present, a padding-tail segment. title: [Bugfix][Parser] Gemma4: keep tool-call flush beside a partial thought prefix
summary: [Bugfix][Parser] Gemma4: keep tool-call flush beside a partial thought prefix ## Overview `Gemma4Parser._events_to_delta` drops the **whole** delta while the `thought\n` reasoning prefix is incomplete. When one streaming step holds both the end of a tool call (`<tool_call|>`, which flushes the argument tail the parser held back) and `<|channel>thought` without its `\n`, the flushed `"}` is discarded. The client then receives `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with arguments that are not valid JSON. This PR drops only the reasoning in that branch, as the branch above it already does. ## Claims - Streamed Gemma 4 tool-call arguments are complete when the call's end and a partial `<|channel>thought` share a step. - No other step changes: a delta that carries only the partial prefix is still held back (`None`), and the prefix is still stripped from reasoning. ## Validation New regression test in `tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py`. title: [Draft][CPU][GLM5Next] Add sparse MLA / KeyPool backend
summary: ## Summary This PR adds a correctness-first CPU sparse MLA / KeyPool execution path for GLM5Next for #57345. The implementation keeps the common GLM5Next model graph and adds only the GLM-local CPU indexer, KeyPool lifecycle, metadata, and sparse MLA adapters required for execution. It is independent of the CPU KDA work in #57496. ## Self-review / Implementation notes ### Why a GLM-specific path The existing dense CPU MLA backend does not match the GLM5Next sparse contract. The DeepSeek CPU implementations were useful structural references, but GLM5Next has distinct KeyPool compression, gate-score pooling, pool-level top-k, pool-to-token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, index-cache representation, and request-local pool boundaries. For that reason this PR does not copy a complete DeepSeek attention object graph and does not introduce a generic sparse framework. The feature-local flow is: ```text GLM5Next common attention -> CPU indexer metadata -> KeyPool compression/tail/cache lifecycle -> selected-row sparse MLA -> existing latent/value/output projections ``` I intentionally did not add `glm5next/cpu/model.py`. The existing model hierarchy remains usable; only sparse indexer/MLA execution and the minimum platform/backend injection differ on CPU. ### KeyPool lifecycle For complete pools, the CPU path preserves the intended sequence of pooling, BF16 round-trip, Hadamard transform, FP8 quantization, and index-cache write. title: [Bugfix][CPU] Fail fast when MLA head dimensions are not supported by the CPU decode kernel
summary: ## Purpose Partial implementation of **option B** from #52008: fail fast with a clear error when an MLA model's head dimensions are not supported by the CPU MLA decode kernel, instead of crashing deep inside kernel dispatch after a confusing chain of contradictory mamba / prefix-caching validation errors. The CPU MLA decode kernel (`csrc/cpu/mla_decode.cpp`) only compiles for the DeepSeek-V2/V3 cache layout (`head_dim=576, v_head_dim=512, block_size=16`). Models with different MLA head dimensions — e.g. the `inference-optimization/Kimi-K3-0.40B` tiny variant (`head_dim=160, v_head_dim=64`) — cannot run on the CPU backend at all, but previously only failed deep in kernel dispatch with an unrelated-looking error. Now `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config` validates the dimensions at startup and raises: ``` ValueError: The CPU MLA decode kernel only supports head_dim=576, v_head_dim=512 (block_size=16); got head_dim=160, v_head_dim=64. Model <model> cannot run on the CPU backend. ``` DeepSeek-V2/V3 standard dimensions still pass the guard and keep running; the existing MLA handling (forcing chunked prefill and prefix caching off) is unchanged. This PR does **not** implement option A (CPU MLA prefix caching / chunked prefill) or option C (honoring `--hf-overrides {"use_mla": false}`). This is deliberately more precise than the architecture-level fail-fast suggested in #52008: only models whose MLA head dimensions the CPU decode kernel cannot run are rejected, so DeepSeek-V2/V3 with standard dimensions remain supported on CPU. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Serve --kv-cache-dtype mxfp4 on gfx942
summary: ## Summary Adds MXFP4 main K/V cache support for MiniMax-M3 on gfx942 (MI325X/MI308X/MI300X). Uses the same 8704 B MXFP4 page layout as gfx950. title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Emit the o_proj MXFP8 input from the NVFP4 sparse decode kernel
summary: ## Purpose On ROCm, every MiniMax-M3.1 decode layer runs the NVFP4 sparse decode attention, then a separate `_kernel` launch (the MXFP8 activation quant of its bf16 output, K = 2048 per TP4 rank), then the `o_proj` GEMM. In the profile of a real decode step (rank-0 profile windows at N=4 and N=16) that quant is 60 launches per step, ~4.4-4.6 us each (profiled, inflated ~1.6x). This PR adds an `fp8_out` variant of the FlyDSL sparse decode kernel (`m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode_*_q8`) whose final store writes E4M3 values and row-major E8M0 scales instead of bf16, and hands them to `o_proj` as a `QuantizedActivation` (same mechanism as #63637 for `qkv_proj` and the FFN fusion in #65478). ## How it works - Output layout: in the final store a lane owns head `n`, dims `32g..32g+31`, i.e. exactly one 32-element MX block, so the quantization needs no cross-lane exchange. With split-K (`splits > 1`) the last workgroup of a row merges the partials and stores O; the quant runs there on the merged O, so every 32-block sees the final values. - Arithmetic: it quantizes the *bf16-rounded* values the bf16 store would have written (`pk_bf16`), computes the block amax on their integer bit patterns and the E8M0 byte as `clamp(exponent_field - 8 + (mantissa > 0.75), 0, 254)` (448 = 1.75 x 2^8, so this is `ceil(log2(amax/448)) + 127` exactly, no log2/division), scales by the exact power of two `2^(127-sb)` and converts with `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32` (RNE). title: [ROCm][Perf] Two-level all-reduce for TP=8 across two XGMI islands (8x MI210)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On 8x MI210 the GPUs form two fully connected 4-GPU XGMI islands joined only by PCIe. The flat custom all-reduce needs every GPU linked to every other, so at TP=8 it turns itself off and every all-reduce goes through RCCL's ring, which crosses PCIe on every step. This PR adds an `ISLAND` backend that reduces inside each island first, then across GPU pairs: - below 2.25 MiB: the existing custom all-reduce inside each island, then across the GPU pair at the same island position; - from 2.25 MiB: RCCL reduce-scatter inside the island, all-reduce of the quarter-size shard across the four pairs, all-gather inside the island. It adds no kernels (it reuses `CustomAllreduce` and `PyNcclCommunicator`), and both paths also run inside CUDA graphs. Fully connected gfx90a groups (MI210 TP=2/4, MI250X TP=8) are handled by #63226; the two PRs don't overlap. ## Claims - TP=8, Qwen2.5-72B on 8x MI210, 1k/1k and 8k/1k vs main on the 2026-11-05 nightly: TPOT −11% to −26%, output throughput +13% to +34% (table below). - On automatically on gfx90a when the GPUs form two islands, with no env vars; everything else keeps its current backend. ## Validation 8x MI210 (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7 are the islands). summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` return 500 (`IndexError: list index out of range`) when a finished output has fewer logprob positions than tokens (#63751). With this PR, an output whose logprob positions and tokens differ in length (shorter, as reported, or longer) is returned without logprobs instead of failing the request, and each occurrence is logged with both lengths. It does **not** fix the upstream mismatch. That fix is #61219: with `logprob_token_ids` and speculative decoding on the V2 model runner, the rejection sampler drops the token-id logprobs on every step that has draft tokens. This PR is a backstop, so a mismatch like that, from this path or another, can't fail the whole request. It addresses the 500s in #63751 without closing it. **Relation to other work:** #61219 fixes the root cause in the rejection sampler (@kfirtoledo traced #63751 to it). This PR only touches the serving layer, so the two don't overlap and can land in either order. @MarinaMackay, who had planned to work on #63751, stepped back once #61219 was found. No other open PR touches these loops. ## Claims - When an output has fewer or more logprob positions than tokens, the four logprobs builders (chat, completions, and the tokens endpoint's text and generate shapes) return it without logprobs instead of raising, wherever the positions are missing or extra (end or middle). Every token gets the builder's existing no-logprob entry: `-9999.0` for chat and tokens, `null` for completions. - No logprob is attributed to the wrong tok

title: [Model][Core] Register every persistent device tensor as a parameter or buffer
summary: ## Overview Sleep mode level 2 discards the weights memory pool. On wake, only `model.named_buffers()` are restored in place, and parameters come back through the weight update. A device tensor that is built at load and kept as a plain attribute is therefore garbage after sleep level 2 + wake. This PR fixes each such tensor at its own site. Most fixes are `register_buffer(name, t, persistent=False)` with the same tensor object, so addresses do not change. It adds no walker, no exemption table and no CI scan. Context: #54477, #50079. ## Fixed (one site each) - NVFP4 linear emulation: the layer holds the E2M1 lookup table as a buffer. - Humming linear (MXFP4/6/8, NVFP4, mixed precision, FP8/INT8 scaled-mm, `HummingLinearMethod`): `locks` is a layer buffer. - `Attention`: `_k_scale_cpu`/`_v_scale_cpu` are created on CPU explicitly. ALiBi slopes / fp32 sinks (impl-derived state) moved to #62634 (runtime cuMem pool, as in #62358). - `_k_scale_cpu`/`_v_scale_cpu` are created on CPU. They were built under the target-device context, so on main they landed on the GPU. - DSv4.1 mega attention: the three `permute_on_load` permutations are built on CPU. They are used only at load time: the weight-loader closures keep them and apply them on every (re)load, and `forward` never reads them. Built on GPU they landed in the weights pool, so after level-2 sleep a `reload_weights()` permuted with garbage indices; `gather` already moves them to the parameter device. - DSv4.1 fused mHC all-reduce: `_stage_state` is a model buffer. - Model constants are buffers: GraniteSpeech `attention_dists`, P

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 decode logprobs drift after a prefix-cache hit with swa_bounded_replay (default)
summary: ### Your current environment - vLLM 0.32.0, model runner V2, CUDA graphs on - 8x B200 (TP=8), `attention_backend="FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41"` - Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, text-only, BF16 (converted from the released checkpoint) - `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `logprobs_mode="raw_logprobs"` ### 🐛 Describe the bug With prefix caching on, DeepSeek-V4.1 decode-time logprobs disagree with a prefill re-score of the same tokens noticeably more often when requests share a prompt prefix. Turning off `swa_bounded_replay` (on by default) brings the mismatch back down to the level we see with prefix caching disabled. `CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay` keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching and "rebuild[s] it after a prefix hit by recomputing the hit's last window". A replay of only the last W tokens cannot reproduce the sliding-window KV a full prefill computes for those positions in layers after the first: the first replayed tokens cannot attend to the window before them, so their hidden states, and the sliding-window KV derived from them, differ. #62365 describes the exact replay length as W + L(W-1) tokens, but makes the replay exact only under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. In the default mode the rebuilt window is approximate, and the first decode tokens after the prompt (which attend over exactly that window) get shifted logprobs. We hit this in RL: rollouts sample 12 responses per prompt, so 11 of them take the prefix-hit path. The affected tokens show up as rollout-vs-trainer logprob outliers clustered by prompt group, often at the first response token. ### Measurement The sam

title: [Bug]: Scheduler livelock with multi-module MTP + Mamba align prefix caching when prompt_len % block_size < num_speculative_tokens
summary: ### Your current environment Reproduced on CPU at main `a2fb482732`, using the scheduler and KV cache manager directly with no model forward, so the GPU and driver are irrelevant. I have not run it on a GPU with a real checkpoint (see "Reachability" below). ### 🐛 Describe the bug With `mamba_cache_mode="align"` and multi-module MTP (`num_prefill_lookahead` = `num_speculative_tokens` = L ≥ 2), a request whose prompt length satisfies `1 <= prompt_len % block_size <= L - 1` stops making progress after its first chunk. From then on the scheduler gives it 0 tokens on every step and never finishes or errors. It does not need chunked prefill: it happens with a 512-token budget and a 49-token prompt. Two clamps in `Scheduler.schedule()` disagree about the same position: 1. `_mamba_block_aligned_split` ends the chunk at the last block boundary before the end of the prompt (48 for a 49-token prompt, block size 16), so that the Mamba state there can be cached. 2. `_reserve_prefill_lookahead` then sees `remaining = 1 < L` and moves the end back by `L - remaining`, to 46. That end is no longer block-aligned. 3. On the next step the request starts at 46. The Mamba split stops it at the boundary 48, the look-ahead reservation takes away 2 more tokens, `num_new_tokens == 0`, and the request is skipped. This repeats on every step. Minimal repro, run from the repo root: ```python from tests.v1.core.test_prefix_caching import make_kv_cache_config_hybrid_model from tests.v1.core.utils import create_requests, create_scheduler from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput BLOCK = 16 base = creat

title: [Bugfix] Keep attention impl state in the runtime pool under sleep mode
summary: ## Purpose Part of #59055 (sleep-mode memory). Same pattern as #62358 (LoRA). Attention backend impls derive device tensors from their inputs/weights, e.g. ALiBi slopes (built in `__init__`) and the FlashInfer/B12x fp32 sinks copy (built in `process_weights_after_loading`). With `enable_sleep_mode`, model construction runs inside the `weights` cuMem pool, so these tensors land there too. Level-2 sleep discards that pool, and they are not parameters or buffers, so nothing restores them: after wake-up the model generates garbage even though the weights are correct. This PR builds the impl, and runs the impl's `process_weights_after_loading`, inside the `runtime` pool when sleep mode is on. Sleep offloads and restores the `runtime` pool at every level, so the impl state survives. No backend changes; nothing changes without sleep mode or on non-CUDA-alike platforms. Split out of #60009. ## Test Plan `sleep_ab.py`: greedy baseline, then 3 x (sleep(level=2) -> wake -> regenerate, compare tokens), GSM8K before/after. `inplace` = `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["*"]`; `reload` = wake weights, `reload_weights()`, wake KV cache. title: [Bugfix][Offload] Re-offload UVA params whose data replace_parameter rebound
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #66264. `replace_parameter` keeps the existing `Parameter` object (and its `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded` marker) and rebinds `.data` to the new device tensor when a repacked weight does not fit the old storage. `device_loading_context` only re-offloaded when the marker was missing, so these weights silently stayed resident on the device after `process_weights_after_loading`. summary: ## Why `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass` on **SM120/SM121** serves silently corrupted output. title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Isolate probe generation length from workload extra_body (#66246)
summary: ## Overview Fixes #66246. In `vllm bench serve`, prevents generation-length overrides in `extra_body` from leaking into single-token probe requests. ## Claims - Probes generated by `vllm bench serve --probe-request-rate` strictly maintain a one-token generation limit (`output_len=1`), even when the main workload configures token limits via `--extra-body` (e.g. `max_completion_tokens`, `max_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `min_tokens`). - Non-generation fields in `extra_body` continue to be preserved for probes. ## Validation - Added automated unit test in `tests/benchmarks/test_probe_overrides.py` verifying `completions`, `chat/completions`, and `responses` endpoints against mock server. - Verified test suite passes locally (`3 passed in 4.60s`). - Verified code passes `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`. ## Details In `vllm/benchmarks/serve.py`, `probe_loop` generates single-token requests to measure queueing and scheduling interference. However, `probe_input` was created via `replace(test_input, prompt="Hi", prompt_len=1, output_len=1, ...)` without replacing `extra_body`. Because `_update_payload_common` applies `payload.update(request_func_input.extra_body)`, any token length limits specified in `extra_body` overwritten `payload[key] = 1`, turning lightweight probes into multi-token generation requests and skewing interference latency measurements. We filter out generation length keys (`max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `max_new_tokens`, `min_tokens`, `min_completion_tokens`) when constructing `probe_extra_body`, ensuring probes stay single-tok

title: [Core] WhisperEncoder support `torch.compile`
summary: ## Overview This PR enables compiling of WhisperEncoder. This is particular important when running Whisper as the encoder execution time is independent of the input sequence/audio length (spectogram gets padded/truncated). As Encoder-Decoder models move closer to MM abstractions, the compilation introduced here follows the same approach proposed for MM models here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23207, wherein compilation is turned on a model by model basis. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] SimpleCPUOffload: remove the disk tier's file on graceful shutdown
summary: ## Purpose `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` does not override `shutdown()`, and `SimpleCPUOffloadWorker` has no `shutdown()`, so `DiskBackend.shutdown()` never runs outside unit tests. Each worker's slot file, `<disk_path>.rank_<N>`, outlives every exit. It holds prompt-derived KV (mode `0600`) and is only removed when the next start on that node reuses the path. `docs/usage/metrics.md` already describes the file as "unlinked at startup and shutdown". This PR wires the shutdown through and makes it safe to call on the teardown path: - `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector.shutdown()` calls `SimpleCPUOffloadWorker.shutdown()`, which shuts down the `DiskBackend`. The scheduler role opens no files, and the CPU backend is unchanged. - `DiskBackend.shutdown()`: - **Unlinks first**, before waiting for the IO threads, so a kill during the wait still leaves no file. - **Removes only its own file.** `init()` records the `(st_dev, st_ino)` of the file it created; shutdown unlinks `disk_path` only if it still refers to that inode. A file another process has since created at the same path (e.g. the next start) is left alone. - **Drops queued transfers** and stops between blocks of a running one. It still waits for the DMAs it already issued, so no copy into a staging buffer is in flight when its thread exits. - **Bounds the wait:** one 2 s budget for both IO threads (previously up to 10 s each). - **Then releases resources:** once both threads have exited, it closes the fd and unregisters the pinned staging buffers (`cudaHostUnregister`, new `unpin_tensor()`). title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep FlashInfer BF16 MoE correct across load_weights refits

title: [Spec Decode] Add FlashInfer CuteDSL non-causal decode path for DFlash
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose On SM100, FlashInfer serves non-causal DFlash draft queries through `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(causal=False)` because the decode/TRTLLM paths cannot express non-causal attention. FlashInfer's CuteDSL paged decode wrapper can (`q_len_per_req > 1`, dense mask), and it fits the DFlash decode shape exactly (uniform `1 + num_speculative_tokens` queries per request). This PR adds a `CuteDSLDecode` dispatch mode to the FlashInfer backend (tracker #46105 item): - `VLLM_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_DECODE`, default off. - Static gate: SM100, full attention (no SWA / soft cap / sinks), `kv_data_type == q_data_type`, page size in {8, 16, 32, 64}. - Per-batch gate: non-causal with uniform query length; otherwise the existing non-causal prefill path. - CUDA graphs are already excluded for this case by `get_cudagraph_support()` (non-causal on SM100 reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`), so no extra gate is needed. title: [Perf][KV Offload] Vectorize direct-layout descriptor fill across layers
summary: ## Overview `_fill_direct_ops` builds the (src, dst, size) copy descriptors for every GPU<->CPU KV transfer in the `OffloadingConnector`. This PR fills all refs in one numpy broadcast. ## Claims - Same descriptors, same order. title: [Core][V1] Add residual-aware SJF scheduling policy
summary: ## Summary Sort waiting prefill requests by remaining local prefill cost (num_tokens minus local cached tokens) instead of raw prompt length, so cache-warm long prompts are not misclassified as expensive. Recovery requests stay first; max-wait aging promotes stragglers in FCFS order. Residual cost is quantized to KV blocks so requests with the same remaining block count tie-break by arrival time, stabilizing decode arrivals and TPOT variance. Add `residual_sjf_max_wait_ms` to configure the aging threshold. Raw-length cost mode is kept as an uncommitted test-only ablation switch and is not part of this change. This PR is the main-branch port of the same change previously developed on a v0.23.0-based branch, cherry-picked onto current `main` (commit `3378b45b4`). The only adaptation: the local cache-hit lookup now consumes the coordinator's 3-tuple return (blocks, hit length, uncached shared-prefix boundary) introduced by the sparse-retention (Mamba/APC) work; scheduler semantics are unchanged. ## Why This Is Not a Duplicate - RFC #29406 proposed SJF, and PR #29366 (closed) implemented raw-length SJF at the RequestQueue level; EWSJF (PR #33392) sorts by raw prompt length with dynamic partitioning. None of them is cache-aware: a cache-warm long prompt is still treated as expensive. This change sorts by exact local residual prefill, which no existing open PR covers. - Checked open PRs for "sjf" / "shortest job first" before opening; no open PR implements residual/cache-aware SJF. The CacheAffinityScheduler RFC (#42185) is complementary (cache affinity as an inner ordering key)

title: [RFC] guard-gated sparse MLA topology index policy
summary: ## Summary This RFC is intended to supersede the broad topology-aware KV cache compression framing in #38725 with a narrower, falsifiable vLLM integration target: a disabled-by-default topology policy for sparse MLA logical-token index selection. The goal is not to introduce a new KV cache compression stack. The goal is to test whether topology-aware replacement of a bounded tail of an existing learned sparse-MLA `topk_indices_buffer` can improve sparse attention quality under the same budget, while preserving vLLM's current sparse MLA coordinate contracts and fail-closed behavior. ## Why this is materially different from #38725 #38725 proposes a broad topology-aware KV cache compression framework with lifecycle compression, directional pruning, NPU-oriented matrix operations, and expected memory/FLOPs gains. This RFC narrows the surface to sparse MLA index policy only: - topology object: sparse MLA logical request-local token indices, shape `[num_tokens, topk]` - invariant: learned-token retention plus segment/witness coverage, optional barrier and diversity terms - implementation rule: preserve a learned prefix and replace only a bounded tail with topology witnesses - baseline: existing sparse MLA learned/top-k indices unchanged - null models: same-budget random, locality, and learned-tail selectors - fallback: disabled or unsupported paths return the original learned indices unchanged - hot path: no Python loops or CPU sync in CUDA runtime paths without a separate benchmark gate ## Proposed contract A topology index policy should satisfy these constraints before runtime

title: [RFC]: Composite Attention Backends
summary: ### Motivation. In certain scenarios, it would be beneficial to use different attention backends for prefill and decode requests. For example: - **Performance:** some kernels perform better at either prefill or decode, so mixing backends will improve overall performance. - **Feature compatibility:** in the case of `mm_prefix`, the backend must support bidirectional attention for the image prefix, which restricts the set of compatible backends. This is only necessary for prefills, though, so we could use a different (and potentially faster) backend for decodes. There are two scenarios in which we already do this: 1. **MLA:** MLA has entirely different pipelines for prefill and decode, and uses different backends for each. MLAPrefillBackend is already a formalized object since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32623 2. **FlashInfer:** The standard FlashInfer GQA backend routes prefills and decodes to different kernels, and there's an intra-FlashInfer selector mechanism distinct from the vLLM-level backend selector. ### Proposed Change. Establish composite attention backends, which use different backends for prefill and decode. These will be able to be specified by `--attention-config.prefill_backend/--attention-prefill-backend` and `--attention-config.decode_backend/--attention-decode-backend` (mutually exclusive with `--attention-config.backend/--attention-backend`). The automatic backend selector will now select prefill and decode selectors independently. **Draft PRs / plan:** - 1/N: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48024 - 2/N: Unify FlashInfer under this

title: [Performance]: Marlin MoE block_size_m heuristic over-selects a large M-tile for expert-parallel decode (up to ~30% TPOT on gpt-oss)
summary: ## Summary The Marlin MoE M-tile heuristic in `fused_marlin_moe` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/marlin_moe.py`) selects `block_size_m` from `M * topk / E`, where `E = w1.size(0)` is the number of **local** experts. Under expert parallelism (EP) `E` shrinks (e.g. gpt-oss-120b at EP=8 → `E = 128/8 = 16`), which drives the heuristic to saturate at `block_size_m = 64`. On Hopper this instantiates a Marlin variant using **255 registers/thread (near the HW cap) and 112 KB dynamic shared memory** → low SM occupancy. For **decode**, that large tile is slower than a smaller one: forcing `block_size_m` to 16/32/48 recovers **9–30 % of decode TPOT** on gpt-oss-120b (DP8, `vllm serve`). The selection loop already carries `# TODO: tune this further for specific models`, and — unlike the Triton fused-MoE path — Marlin is not covered by vLLM's device-aware autotuned-config mechanism, so it cannot be tuned per hardware. This issue reports the problem and proposes a fix path. ## Where `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/marlin_moe.py`, `fused_marlin_moe()`: ```python M, K = hidden_states.size() E = w1.size(0) # local experts: 128 (no EP) vs 16 (EP=8) topk = topk_ids.size(1) # M block size selection logic # TODO: tune this further for specific models for block_size_m in [8, 16, 32, 48, 64]: if M * topk / E / block_size_m < 0.9: # small E -> large ratio -> saturates at 64 break ``` (Identical in v0.18 … current `main`; the file was `fused_moe/fused_marlin_moe.py` before v0.23.) ## Evidence **End-to-end (gpt-oss-120b, MXFP4, MARLIN MoE backend), 8×H200, `vllm serve --

title: [Bugfix] Wire up weight offloader in V2 Model Runner (`--cpu-offload-gb` was silently a no-op)
summary: ## Purpose `--cpu-offload-gb` (and `--offload-group-size`) silently has **no effect** whenever the engine selects the V2 Model Runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`), which is the default for most generate models. The global offloader singleton never gets set to anything other than `NoopOffloader`, so every decoder layer is fully constructed on the accelerator regardless of the configured offload budget. There is no error, warning, or log line indicating this — it just looks like an unrelated OOM. Root cause: `set_offloader(create_offloader(offload_config))` is only called from the legacy V1 Model Runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:451,921`, inside `__init__`, guarded by the comment "Make sure this is called before any get_offloader call"). The V2 Model Runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) never calls it at all — `self.offload_config` isn't even assigned there. Both runners share the same underlying `make_layers()` → `get_offloader().wrap_modules(...)` path in `vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py`, so the offloading mechanism itself works identically once it's actually wired up; V2 just never flips the switch. ## Fix Add the same `set_offloader(create_offloader(...))` call to `GPUModelRunner.load_model()` in the V2 runner, immediately before model construction begins (matching the "before any get_offloader call" ordering requirement from the V1 implementation). title: [Bug]: kernel_warmup() has no inter-rank synchronization between stages that issue real TP/EP collectives, causing startup hangs on multi-node deployments
summary: ## Summary `kernel_warmup()` (`vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`) runs a sequence of ~10 warmup stages, several of which internally call `runner._dummy_run(...)` and thereby issue real cross-rank TP/EP collectives (all-reduce, all-gather, etc.) against the model. There is no inter-rank synchronization between these stage calls. If one rank finishes a stage and moves on to the next (which issues a *different* collective sequence) before its peer has finished the earlier stage, the ranks can permanently desync — once two ranks disagree on the sequence/count of collective calls they've issued, they can never rendezvous again, so every subsequent step (including real inference later) blocks forever instead of erroring. This is distinct from — but can compound with — live-JIT-during-inference hangs (e.g. #45198, #43009): it's a startup-time ordering bug, not a compilation bug, and can happen even when every kernel is already warmed. ## Why I believe this is real, not just theoretical `flashinfer_autotune()`, defined in the same file just below `kernel_warmup()`, already guards against exactly this: it explicitly calls `get_world_group().barrier()` after its own `runner._dummy_run(...)` calls (kernel_warmup.py:266 and :311) specifically because tuning is distributed and needs rank sync. That shows the failure mode is already known and handled *for that one function* — but the barrier isn't applied anywhere else in `kernel_warmup()`'s outer sequence. None of `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`, `deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup`, `sparse_mla_triton_warmup_if_needed`, `flashinfer_sparse

title: [Bugfix] Demote FlashInfer CUTLASS unquantized MoE when intermediate size is not 128-aligned
summary: ## Purpose Serving Gemma 4 26B A4B on SM100 (B200) hangs during engine initialization. The last log line is `torch.compile took N s in total`; `Initial profiling/warmup run` is never reached, and the EngineCore process spins at ~56% CPU indefinitely with no traceback or error. Root cause: `_get_priority_backends` ranks `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` ahead of `TRITON` on CUDA. `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` declines non-128-aligned intermediate sizes (the `% 128` check in `_trtllm_bf16_lora_supported`), but `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` has no equivalent guard, so the oracle selects it and the kernel hangs. Gemma 4 26B A4B has `moe_intermediate_size=704`, and `704 % 128 == 64`. This patch demotes `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` when the per-partition intermediate size is not a multiple of 128, following the existing demotion pattern in the same function (the Qwen3.5/dp_size and SWIGLUOAI hacks). It does not attempt to fix the kernel itself — happy to move the check into `FlashInferExperts.is_supported_config` instead if that is preferred. ## Test Plan Hardware: NVIDIA B200 (SM100), 183 GB, vLLM 0.26.0, CUDA 13.0 ``` vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --max-model-len 131072 ``` Then a 400-token decode, repeated 3x: ``` curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the HAZOP procedure in 3 steps."}], "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 400, "seed": 3407 }' ``` Also verified that the existing workaround `--kernel-config.moe_backend=trito

title: MooncakeConnector P/D: NVLink fallback transfer fails "Requested address not found" (fp8 MLA, v0.25.0)
summary: ### Summary Same-node P/D disaggregation of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with the MooncakeConnector fails at the first KV transfer on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`, on an 8x B200 SXM node, in every configuration tested; each transport fails differently, and none fails at startup. title: deepseek_v4: decode runs unfused (breakable CUDA graph) — DeepseekV4ForCausalLM lacks @support_torch_compile; fullgraph capture blocked by inline deep_gemm/tilelang pybinds
summary: ### Summary `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` (nvidia backend) does not carry `@support_torch_compile`, so vLLM auto-enables `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` and runs decode as **unfused eager kernels wrapped in a breakable CUDA graph** (`compilation mode=NONE`). torch.compile/inductor fusion never runs for DS4. ### Why it can't just be turned on Adding `@support_torch_compile` makes Dynamo `fullgraph=True` capture fail, because several DS4 forward paths call raw `deep_gemm`/tilelang pybind extensions inline (Dynamo cannot trace pybind calls). We verified, in sequence, that wrapping each as a torch custom op advances capture: 1. `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` (+ the 4 sibling MHC ops need their plain names rebound to `torch.ops.vllm.*`, not just registered) — cleared. 2. `fp8_einsum` (nvidia/ops/o_proj.py → utils/deep_gemm.py) — cleared with a boundary wrap. Capture then reaches upstream-scale blockers in the DSA lightning-indexer path: `has_cutedsl()`→`importlib.util.find_spec` called inside `forward` (fused_indexer_q.py), the multi-stream lambda orchestration (`execute_in_parallel`/`maybe_execute_in_parallel`), and `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` taking a cached **non-tensor** `symm_buffer` (can't be a custom-op arg without unpacking). ### Honest note on payoff On GB10/sm_121a we measured DS4 C=1 decode at **99.9% GPU-busy** (host-gap ~0.1%) — it's bandwidth/kernel-bound, so inductor fusion upside is ~0 here. This is filed as an **enablement/correctness** report (the breakable-graph fallback is a real architectural gap), not a perf claim; on higher-bandwidth GPUs the fusion win could matter. ###

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Force Triton MXFP4 for 96-row ASM scale tiles
summary: ## Purpose On ROCm gfx950, AITER ASM MXFP4 (`gemm_a4w4`) is selected when weight-scale tiles have `rows % 32 == 0` and `cols % 8 == 0`. Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN `in_proj_ba` uses **96×160** scales, which pass that layout check, but ASM is numerically wrong for **M ≤ 64** (error ratio ~0.83–0.92; ~22–24 µs broken ASM vs ~7.6–8.9 µs Triton). This PR forces 96-row scales onto Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4`. Other legal tiles (e.g. 128×160) stay on ASM. TP2/TP4 BA (`N=48/24`) already fail the row-%-32 check and were Triton via #55213. ## Test Plan - Unit: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_asm_fp4_scale_swizzle_supported_shape_rules` - `(96, 160) -> False` (Triton) - `(128, 160) -> True` (ASM unchanged) - gfx950 TP1 Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 serve: GDN `in_proj_ba` should log Triton, not ASM, at decode M≤64. ## Test Result Dispatch unit cases added. Numerical mismatch for 96-row ASM at M=8/16/32/64 was measured on MI355X. Full e2e accuracy vs Triton path still to be attached from the TP1 patched serve.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fix Triton block-FP8 scalar scale indexing
summary: ## Overview Fixes #66195. Triton 3.9 rejects rank-0 `b_scale` values indexed as `b_scale[None, :]` or `b_scale[:, None]` in the block-FP8 fused MoE kernel. This causes engine warmup to fail before serving for affected Triton configurations. ## Claims - Keep the scalar block-scale optimization introduced by #64760. - Avoid invalid rank-0 indexing when `group_n` is divisible by `BLOCK_SIZE_N`. - Preserve the existing vector-scale path for all other configurations. - Add regression coverage for the small-batch scalar block-scale path. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k scalar_b_scale -q` - Collected successfully; skipped locally because this environment has no CUDA device. - `git diff --check` passed. The issue reporter validated the same change on 4x GB200 with Triton 3.9: the engine started, the Triton FP8 MoE kernel compiled, and the benchmark completed. I could not reproduce that GPU run locally. ## Details The scalar `offs_bsn` branch is compile-time specialized. Its `tl.load` therefore returns a rank-0 `b_scale`, but the old accumulation code always applied two-dimensional indexing. Triton 3.8 accepted the extra indices; Triton 3.9 rejects them. The fix adds a matching compile-time branch in the accumulation step. It multiplies by scalar `b_scale` directly in the scalar case and retains the existing broadcast indexing in the vector case. The change is limited to the Triton block-FP8 kernel and does not alter tensor shapes, launch configuration, or steady-state synchronization. This is not a duplicate PR: no existing open PR

title: [Bugfix][Core] Do not double-count CUDAGraph memory in --kv-cache-memory suggestion
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #57936 `--kv-cache-memory` suggestions double-count CUDAGraph memory whenever `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1` (the default). `peak_activation_memory` included the graph estimate from `determine_available_memory`, and `compile_or_warm_up_model` then added the actual captured pool. For large graph pools both suggested values go negative, so they cannot be copied back and the startup-plan guard rejects them. This is a regression of #37426, reintroduced by the accounting rewrite in #49208. The allocation path is unchanged: it already subtracts the graph estimate once. This PR restores `peak_activation_memory` to transient activation headroom only, matching #37426, and extracts the suggestion arithmetic so a CPU test can pin the invariant. `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` was saving that printed suggestion. The suggestion also subtracts the captured CUDAGraph pool and a 150 MiB buffer, so the next boot allocated fewer KV tokens than the profiled boot (reported by @GodRishUniverse). The plan now persists `available_kv_cache_memory_bytes`, the budget this boot allocated. The printed suggestion is unchanged. On current main, extensible KV warmup reads `peak_activation_memory` as reserved activation headroom. Leaving the graph estimate out of that field matches that use. The captured pool is still subtracted once in the KV budget and once in the printed suggestion. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py::test_kv_cache_suggestion_does_not_double_count_cudagraph tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py::test_startup_plan_saves_allocated_kv_b

summary: ## Overview With `data_parallel_size > 1`, a `NixlConnector` and `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`, every engine fails the DP configuration check at READY since #62330. The READY message now carries the hash of the parallel config the engine was started with, which is the config the front-end compares it against (#26218). ## Claims - Fixes the startup failure `Configuration mismatch detected for engine N ... Worker hash: ..., Expected hash: ...` for DP > 1 deployments that rely on the automatic `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` resolve (NIXL + DCP). The set of compared fields is unchanged, only the moment of hashing moves. - One file, +12/-4, no new configuration and no user-visible behaviour change. ## Validation - Root cause reproduced on a live deployment at `44965a1097` (2026-11-03): an MLA MoE model (GLM-5.3 shape), one engine per node, `--data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 1 --data-parallel-rank N --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --block-size 64 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", ...}'`. title: [Perf] Vectorize silu_and_mul_per_block_quant for large inputs
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` launches one 128-thread block per (token, group). Each thread issues one 2-byte load, and the group max is a shared-memory tree reduction. At prefill sizes the kernel runs at ~0.9 TB/s on H200. It is therefore 1.3-2.2x *slower* than the unfused `silu_and_mul` + `per_token_group_quant_fp8` pair it replaces. This PR adds a vectorized variant (16B loads, warp-shuffle reduction, 8B stores) for large inputs. The existing kernel stays for small inputs, where it has lower latency. Both produce bitwise-identical results. ## Claims - At >= 16k rows the fused kernel is 2.0-2.45x faster than before, and now 8-53% faster than the unfused pair. At <= 64 rows (decode) it is unchanged. See the table below. - Paths that use the fused kernel today get faster prefill: - the Triton FP8 MoE with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0`; - the `SiluMul+BlockQuant` compile fusion, where it matches. - Prerequisite for #65794, which enables the fused path by default (superseding #64906 and #43399). With the old kernel, that change costs -3.8% prefill on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8. ## Validation **Kernel:** H200, bf16 in, fp8 out, group 128, CUDA-graph timed, p10 µs. | 2I | rows | unfused (silu_and_mul + group quant) | fused, main | fused, this PR | vs main | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 512 | 8 | 3.80 | 1.87 | **1.84** | 1.02x | | 512 | 64 | 4.02 | 2.17 | **2.00** | 1.08x | | 512 | 512 | 4.51 | 2.70 | **2.53** | 1.07x | | 512 | 4096 | 7.49 | 7.54 | **4.63** | 1.63x | | 512 | 16384 | 18.77 | 23.88 | **12.04** | 1.98x | | 512 | 65536 | 64.88 |

Since #56492 (extensible KV cache), MRV2's `profile_cudagraph_memory()` returns 0 when the extensible cache is on. title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Unlink shared mmap by inode after all ranks map
summary: Fixes a /dev/shm region leak in TieringOffloadingSpec, and a stale-generation unlink that could delete a live engine's file. ## Purpose `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap` is unlinked once every process has mapped it, so a hard kill can't leak the region. Two gaps: 1. **`TieringOffloadingSpec` never dropped the name.** It maps the region in the workers *and* the scheduler, and the scheduler maps last, so nothing was positioned to unlink. The file survived every restart. 2. **Unlink targeted the path, not the file.** A stale generation shutting down late could delete the file belonging to the engine that replaced it. Fix: `SharedOffloadRegion.unlink()` records `(st_dev, st_ino)` at map time and removes the pathname only if it still names that inode. All four unlink sites route through it. `get_manager()` calls `scheduler_mmap.unlink()` once the scheduler-side mapping exists — EngineCore builds it only after the synchronous worker `initialize_from_config` RPCs return, so every TP worker has already mapped. Single-generation behavior is unchanged; the guard only turns a wrong unlink into a no-op. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py -v ``` Two existing tests extended, both of which fail on `main`: - `test_joiner_flag_not_set` — a joiner (the scheduler mapping) can drop the pathname; all mappings stay valid and coherent. - `test_backing_file_unlinked_after_barrier` — a stale generation's `unlink()` returns `False` and leaves the replacement's inode at the path. ## Test Result ``` 92 p

title: [Perf][Kimi] Run one packed prefill convolution
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Kimi K3's KDA prefill path split the packed q|k|v projection into three views and ran one causal convolution per view, then materialized dense Q/K/V for FlashKDA. The convolution weights and the conv state are already stored packed, so run a single convolution over the packed input and pass the resulting row-strided views straight to FlashKDA (vllm-project/FlashKDA#15), which consumes them without copies. This turns three prefill convolution launches per KDA layer into one and removes the three `.contiguous()` calls. Decode is untouched, and the raw projection is still available for the conv-state checkpoint export. The FlashKDA pin bump this originally needed is already in `main` via #61614, so this PR now only contains the Kimi K3 call-site change. The merged-convolution path is taken only when `kda_prefill_backend == "flashkda"`; the triton and flashinfer backends keep three dense convolutions. ## Claims - One `causal_conv1d_fn` per KDA layer per prefill step instead of three, with lower total convolution GPU time. - Prefill output is bit-identical to the previous path. - No change to the FlashKDA operator, the convolution weight/state layout, or decode. ## Validation Model-level A/B on 8×H200 (SM90), TP8, `mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75` (the CI K3 checkpoint: 93 layers, 69 of them KDA, MXFP4 experts), vLLM at this PR's head. title: [Bugfix] Close the early-PDL completion race for small FlashInfer one-shot all-reduce calls on the trtllm IPC backend
summary: ## Overview Correctness hardening of the FlashInfer all-reduce integration: calls with `num_tokens <= PDL_ADVANCE_LAUNCH_TOKENS` that are dispatched to the one-shot Lamport kernel via FlashInfer's AUTO strategy currently run with `trigger_completion_at_end=False` — the early-PDL completion mode that both vLLM's own code comment and FlashInfer's API documentation describe as conditionally safe. Related: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#1223 (one-shot instability), flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2887 (the perf rationale for the early-completion mode). ## Scope The behavioral change is confined to FlashInfer's **`trtllm` (single-node IPC) workspace backend**. On MNNVL workspaces the argument is ignored by FlashInfer — its API documentation states: "`trigger_completion_at_end` : bool — TRT-LLM only. Controls when PDL completion is signaled. `True` (default) signals after the kernel finishes (safe, no overlap). `False` signals early, allowing the next PDL-aware kernel to overlap with this one. Only safe when the next kernel also calls `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()`. **Ignored by the MNNVL backend.**" (`flashinfer/comm/allreduce.py`, unchanged from 0.6.16.post3 through current main; the MNNVL kernels hard-code their own completion points and do not take the parameter.) Multi-node / MNNVL serves are therefore unaffected by this PR; the race window it closes exists only where the flag is live, i.e. single-node IPC workspaces. ## Claims - Removes a documented race window on the `trtllm` backend: the existing comment in `allreduce_rms_fusion.py` states — "The one-shot Lamport all-reduce signals

title: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters
summary: ## Overview Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. title: [RFC]: Bring-Your-Own-GPU (BYOG) reproducible evals and benchmarks for PRs
summary: ### Motivation. Reviewing performance- and accuracy-sensitive PRs is frequently bottlenecked on evidence and regression testing. Reviewers routinely ask "can you please provide e2e performance data?", "can you please provide eval results?", or "can you show 8k1k numbers on H100?". Not only are these requests often vague, leaving the submitter unsure exactly how to run the benchmark or eval, but the answers also arrive as screenshots, hand-run `vllm bench` output, or not at all. On the flip side, running a broad eval + benchmark matrix on vLLM-funded CI for PRs does not scale, especially as the volume of AI-generated PRs grows. AI tools have made producing a PR nearly free, but reviewing one costs as much as or more than it ever did. Maintainer attention is now the scarce resource, and AI generation of PRs is skewing more of the cost of a PR onto the reviewer, who frequently has to validate the PR manually or validate it on other hardware. Asking for evidence that costs GPU time to produce moves some of that cost back to whoever wants the PR merged. It doesn't close the gap, and spending compute doesn't make a PR good, but it pushes in the right direction in two ways: - the evidence gives the reviewer more confidence, making the PR easier to review; - spending it signals that someone values the PR. At the same time, the community has more datacenter hardware than vLLM CI, and more kinds of it (GB300, MI355X, older Hopper/Ampere fleets, and so on). Some of it may be free to help with evals for specific, important PRs, even if its owners aren't ready to commit it to vLLM CI fu

title: AOT compile cache key ignores the LoRA module tree, loading an incompatible artifact (`KeyError: 'weight'`)
summary: **Repo:** vllm-project/vllm **Version:** vLLM 0.26.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, `VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE=1` ## Problem The AOT compilation artifact path does not account for whether LoRA wrappers are present in the module tree. Two runs with identical `VllmConfig` but different LoRA wrapping resolve to the **same** cache key, so vLLM loads a graph compiled against the wrong parameter names. When a layer is LoRA-wrapped, its weight moves from `<prefix>.weight` to `<prefix>.base_layer.weight`. A graph compiled before wrapping still looks up `weight`, and the load path (`decorators.py:311`, "Directly load AOT compilation from path ...") does not detect the mismatch — `disable_guard_check()` is applied when `evaluate_guards` is off, so nothing catches it. The failure surfaces during `profile_run` as a bare: ``` KeyError: 'weight' ``` with a traceback that ends inside the compiled function and names no module, which makes it very hard to attribute. ## Reproduction The cache-key collision is directly observable without needing the crash. Run the same model twice with LoRA enabled and the same cache root, differing only in whether one layer gets wrapped (hook `vllm.lora.model_manager.from_layer` and return the layer unchanged to suppress wrapping): ``` run A (layer left unwrapped): saves .../torch_aot_compile/c3d50e52.../rank_0_0/model run B (layer wrapped): attempts to load .../torch_aot_compile/c3d50e52.../rank_0_0/model ``` Identical hash, materially different module tree. title: [RFC]: [Draft] Split FusedMoEQuantConfig into static schema and runtime state
summary: # Fused MoE Static and Runtime Quantization Configs **Status:** Proposal / RFC **Date:** 2026-11-03 ## Summary Split `FusedMoEQuantConfig` into two objects with different lifetimes: * `FusedMoEQuantSchema` is an immutable, tensor-free description of the quantization scheme owned by a quantization method. It contains the loaded weights, scales, zero points, biases, and other tensor-valued parameters. During the compatibility stages it also holds temporary references to static metadata; those references are removed once they are no longer needed. The existing external interface is preserved through properties. Callers keep using the current names such as `quant_dtype`, `block_shape`, `a1_scale`, and `w1_bias`; they do not read dataclass fields, `_a1`/`_w1` descriptors, or the new static reference directly. `FusedMoEQuantSchema` is the only static quantization type. Selection consumes only the schema's role keys; after choosing the backend, the quantization method finalizes the backend ABI fields (`is_scale_swizzled`, `is_scale_transposed`, and `mx_alignment`) by constructing a new immutable schema value for kernel construction. title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Fix mixed draft-model warmup token budget
summary: ## Overview Draft-model initialization with speculative decoding can fail during mixed prefill/decode warmup: ``` AssertionError: Shape: 2050 out of considered ranges: [(1, 2048)] ``` The warmup creates one synthetic decode request and one synthetic prefill request, but builds the scheduler inputs directly and bypasses the scheduler's correction-slot reservation. title: [CPU] Support 2D (batched) weights in rms_norm, fixing DFlash acceptance on CPU
summary: ## Overview The CPU `rms_norm` kernel ignores the row dimension of a 2D (batched) weight and applies row 0 to every token. title: [Spec Decode] Treat standalone draft model prefill as decode
summary: ## Purpose Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its draft prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds the correction token sampled by the target. `max_decode_query_len()` returns `1 + num_speculative_tokens`, so every spec-as-decode attention builder sets its reorder threshold one token short. Each draft-prefill request is classified as a **prefill**, and the FULL graph captures the backend's prefill path. That has two consequences: - **Correctness:** `UNIFORM_BATCH` backends only promise FULL-graph safety for uniform *decode* batches. FlashInfer's TRTLLM prefill path was not graph-safe, which caused the GB200 crash reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731. #65598 fixed that specific allocation, but the prefill path is still outside what `UNIFORM_BATCH` covers. - **Performance:** the draft prefill runs the prefill attention kernel even though it is decode-shaped. On model runner V2, this PR makes `max_decode_query_len()` add `speculative_config.max_num_new_slots_for_drafting`, the extra per-request slots the drafter adds. The scheduler already reserves this same quantity in its input budget. It is 1 for the standalone draft model and 0 for every other V2 method. V2 rejects `parallel_drafting` for everything except DFlash and DSpark, which report 0. summary: ## Overview Fix FP8 attention metadata in both Pixtral vision towers so FlashInfer uses correct buffer offsets for batches containing multiple images. ## Claims - Pass the FP8 padded hidden size through Pixtral’s packed sequence metadata generation. - Use matching Q/K/V offsets for separately quantized FP8 buffers, avoiding out-of-bounds V reads. - Preserve the existing non-FP8 metadata behavior. ## Validation Needs Blackwell (SM 100+); FP8 ViT attention isn't supported on Hopper. ```bash vllm serve mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409 --tokenizer-mode mistral \ --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER --mm-encoder-attn-dtype fp8 \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' --max-model-len 8192 ``` Then send ~16 concurrent chat requests, each with a different 1024x768 image (a single request may not trigger it). - Before: the engine core crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`; the in-flight and subsequent requests return 500 (`EngineDeadError`). - After: all requests return 200. ## Details FlashInfer FP8 attention quantizes Q/K/V into separate contiguous buffers. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Keep Q and P in BF16 in the AITER sparse paged attention
summary: - sparse_pa.py: call AITER's Gluon paged attention with `compute_type=q.dtype` on an FP8 KV cache, so Q and the softmax weights stay in BF16 and only K/V are upcast from FP8. - test_minimax_m3.py: first numerical test of the AITER sparse attention path on an FP8 cache, against fp32 attention on the dequantized cache with an error bound derived from the BF16 roundings. With an FP8 KV cache the MiniMax-M3 ROCm sparse attention asked AITER for FP8 compute without a query scale, so the kernel rounded the BF16 query and the softmax weights to e4m3. Q's range is not the problem (on gsm8k traffic |q| stays under 14, far below 448, and a per-token query scale changes nothing); e4m3's 3-bit mantissa is. Rounding Q alone moves the attention output by 2% (median head) to 7% (median worst head per token) against an fp32 reference on the same cache. With BF16 compute the error drops to 0.2-0.3%. The kernel is 2-7% slower below about 4K rows and as fast above, which does not show end to end, and gsm8k does not move, so this improves precision and does not fix an accuracy regression. MI355X, MiniMax-M3 at TP4 (16 query heads and 1 KV head per rank), FP8 KV cache. Before forces `compute_type` back to FP8; after is this PR. Both arms run on identical inputs. Attention output error against fp32 attention on the dequantized cache. Inputs match MiniMax-M3's statistics (Q RMS 1.5 from the per-head QK norm, logits spread over about +-10); 64 rows x 16 heads per case: | keys attended | before: median / worst head / p99 | after: median / worst head / p99 | |---|---|---| | 512 | 4.96% / 11.3% / 13.

title: [Perf][KDA] Use views for spec rows that lead the batch on mixed MTP steps
summary: _Requested by **Simon**_ ## Overview On mixed speculative-decoding (MTP) steps, the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer splits spec and non-spec tokens with 6 `index_select` gathers and merges the outputs back with 2 `index_copy_` calls. In the usual case the spec rows already lead the batch. The GDN metadata builder now detects this and sets `num_leading_spec_tokens`, and KDA then takes views instead of gathers and skips the merge. The recurrent kernel and FlashKDA prefill write straight into the output buffer; Triton prefill has no output argument, so it keeps one copy into the non-spec rows. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph pr["This PR, spec rows lead"] direction LR b1[inputs] -->|slices| b2[views] --> b3[kernels] -->|"in place, Triton: 1 copy"| b4[core_attn_out] end subgraph stock["Stock, mixed step"] direction LR a1[inputs] -->|"6x index_select"| a2[copies] --> a3[kernels] --> a4[scratch outputs] -->|"2x index_copy_"| a5[core_attn_out] end ``` Only mixed steps with speculative decoding are affected. Pure decode, pure spec verify, pure prefill and steps whose spec rows are not a prefix run the existing code. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 state "Spec rows?" as spec state "Non-spec rows?" as other state "Spec rows first?" as first state "Existing path" as stock state "lead = spec tokens" as lead state "Take views" as views state "Kernels write into core_attn_out" as write state "Merge skipped" as skip [*] --> spec spec --> other : yes spec --> stock : no other --> first : yes other --> stock : no first --> lead : yes first --> stock : no lead --> views views --> write write --> skip not

title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Re-fit `--max-model-len auto` after the extensible KV cache shrinks
summary: ## Overview With the extensible KV cache (default on CUDA/ROCm with model runner V2, #56492), `--max-model-len auto` is fitted at planning time, against a budget that leaves out CUDA graphs and warmup on purpose: the KV cache is committed later, from the memory measured after warmup. When that measurement can no longer hold the fitted length, `finalize_extensible_kv_cache` only checks it and startup fails, even though the user never asked for that length. This PR fits the length again to the measured capacity, for `auto` only. ## Claims - `--max-model-len auto` no longer fails at startup when CUDA graphs and warmup leave less KV cache than the planning-time fit assumed. title: [Kernel][Perf] Fused GDN MTP: Support DSpark K=8 and use idle SMs at small batch sizes
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview This PR makes two changes to the fused GDN MTP decode kernel: 1. **K=8 support:** DSpark K=8 (9 tokens per request) fell back to the slower Triton path. The kernel now handles 9 tokens. Overlaps with #53070. 2. **Split-V:** at small batch sizes, each value head is split over a cluster of 2 or 4 thread blocks to use idle SMs (SM90+). title: [Bug][v0.32.0 release] No working block size on the release tag (both 64 and 128 fail); fix tracked in #60762
summary: ### Your current environment - Hardware: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB), single node TP8 - vLLM: 0.30.1rc1.dev327+g9af952c55 (nightly, pip) - FlashInfer: 0.7.0 (flashinfer-python + flashinfer-cubin + flashinfer-jit-cache sm120f+cu130, all three packages installed) - Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (official 476GiB mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint) - Config: TP8, `--language-model-only`, `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41` ### 🐛 Describe the bug DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fails to start on SM120 with: ``` ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=8, num_heads=8, topk=128, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=dsv4, extra_topk=0. ``` ### Root cause analysis V4.1's two-tier sparse attention gives each layer a `compress_ratio` (this checkpoint: `[0,0,2,2,...,2,1,1,1,1,1]`). vLLM computes the compressed-layer KV page block size as `attn_metadata.block_size // compress_ratio`, so ratio-2 layers get pbs = 64//2 = **32**. FlashInfer's SM120 dispatch planner (`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120_plan.py`) hard-codes `_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64` and instantiates the dsv4 decode kernels **only** at pbs=64 (the error message itself lists `page_block_size=32` as unsupported). There is **no single global block size that works**: - global block_size=64 → ratio-2 compressed layers compute pbs=32 → this crash - global block_size=128 → vLLM reports "No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; ...)" because the SM120 kernel set has no pbs=128 dsv4 instantiation either (only 64)

title: [Bugfix] Register the aten::mm out_dtype overloads for batch invariance
summary: ## Overview With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and an fp32 lm_head (`--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'`, which `ModelConfig` documents as "required for RL training-inference consistency"), the head runs `torch.mm(x, w, out_dtype=torch.float32)`. That call dispatches to `aten::mm.dtype`, a separate overload from `aten::mm`, so on CUDA SM8x, where batch-invariant mode installs the Triton matmul overrides, it stays on cuBLAS. Whether the result then depends on the batch size depends on the shape: on an A40, Mistral-7B-v0.1 (vocab 32000) shows it and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (vocab 151936) do not. This PR registers `aten::mm.dtype` and `aten::mm.dtype_out` next to `aten::mm`. ## Claims - **Bug:** on `main`, Mistral-7B-v0.1 with an fp32 head gives different logprobs at batch size 1 and 32 for 32 of 32 prompts on an A40. title: [RFC]: Text sessions on /v1/realtime with streaming-input prefill
summary: ### Motivation. `/v1/realtime` is transcription only today. It accepts `input_audio_buffer.*` events and works only for models that implement `SupportsRealtime`. Voice agents that run ASR separately and use a text LLM can't use it. These agents get the user's words incrementally while the user is still speaking. With streaming input (`StreamingInput`, resumable requests), the engine can prefill those words before the turn ends. When the turn is committed, only the last few tokens are left to prefill before decoding starts. vLLM has this engine support, but the server has no text API for it. Today a client has to write its own websocket server around `AsyncLLM`, or run another serving layer. This RFC proposes text sessions on `/v1/realtime` in `vllm serve`. vLLM-Omni tracked streaming input for Qwen3-Omni in [vllm-project/vllm-omni#1951](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/1951). This RFC covers text LLMs in vLLM itself. ### Proposed Change. Add text sessions to `/v1/realtime` for generative text models. Audio transcription keeps its current behavior. **Protocol.** These are OpenAI Realtime events, except `input_text.*`, which mirrors `input_audio_buffer.*` because the OpenAI protocol has no text buffer. - Client: - `session.update` (`instructions`, `tools`, `tool_choice`) - `conversation.item.create` (`message`, `function_call_output`) - `conversation.item.delete` - `input_text.append`, `input_text.commit`, `input_text.clear` - `response.create`, `response.cancel` - Server: - `session.updated` - `conversation.item.added`, `conversation.item.done`, `conversation

title: [Bugfix] Stop baking NVFP4 weight_scale_2 into b12x MoE block scales
summary: ## Purpose The SM12x b12x MoE path (RTX Pro 6000 / DGX Spark) distorts NVFP4 weights at load time: - The FlashInfer kernel's `w1_alpha` does two jobs: FC1 activation-quant global scale and post-GEMM multiplier. The checkpoint's per-expert weight scale (`weight_scale_2`, ~2e-5) would wreck activation quantization if passed as `w1_alpha`, so the b12x experts class bakes it into the e4m3 weight block scales instead. - The bake pushes nearly all block-scale bytes into the 3-bit e4m3 subnormal range and noticeably perturbs the dequantized weights. Marlin applies the same scale in full precision and is unaffected. FlashInfer added a separate `input_global_scale` argument for the activation-quant job (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3932, shipped in v0.6.17). With it, this PR: - Skips the bake and keeps the checkpoint's block scales as loaded. `weight_scale_2` reaches the kernel as an exact fp32 multiplier; no extra wiring is needed because `g1_alphas`/`g2_alphas` already alias the scale_2 parameters. - Passes `input_global_scale=1.0` so FC1 activation quantization behaves exactly as before. Depends on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3932, which shipped in FlashInfer v0.6.17 — the version vLLM pins on main since #52681. The kernel call passes `input_global_scale` unconditionally; a FlashInfer build without it rejects the argument loudly at call time rather than producing wrong results. ## Test Plan - End-to-end accuracy and token-efficiency evals on GB10 (SM121) with an NVFP4 MoE checkpoint, against the Marlin backend as baseline, identical serving settings across configs. - Weight-parity check

title: [Bugfix] Fall back from DeepGEMM when nvcc is older than 12.9
summary: ## Overview DeepGEMM compiles its kernels at runtime and aborts the engine when nvcc is missing or older than 12.9. vLLM only checks the GPU architecture and that DeepGEMM is installed, so on Hopper with an older toolkit, block-FP8 models crash on load. This PR adds the nvcc check, so vLLM warns and falls back to its other FP8 kernels. To find nvcc, it reuses FlashInfer's existing lookup, moved unchanged to `find_nvcc()` in `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py`. ## Claims - Block-FP8 models load on Hopper with nvcc 12.8 or no nvcc, instead of aborting with `NVCC version must be at least 12.9`. - The fallback logs one warning naming the nvcc version it found and where it looked. - No change when nvcc is 12.9 or newer, or with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`. - No change to FlashInfer: `has_flashinfer` finds the same nvcc as before, and its existing tests pass unchanged apart from the patched module. ## Validation H100 NVL, CUDA 12.8.1 toolkit (`nvcc` 12.8), driver for CUDA 13, vLLM `528772a4b` (precompiled; `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` is identical on current main), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8`, offline `LLM.generate` with two prompts: | | kernel selected | result | |---|---|---| | main | `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel` | `RuntimeError: ... NVCC version must be at least 12.9`, then `Engine core initialization failed` | | this PR | `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | warning below, then `'The capital of France is' -> ' Paris. ...'` | ``` WARNING DeepGEMM kernels are disabled: its JIT needs nvcc 12.9 or newer (DG_JIT_NVCC_COMPILER, CUDA_HOME, CUDA_PATH, PATH or /usr/local/cuda), found 12.8.

title: [Bugfix][Worker] Apply the startup plan on every rank or on none
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` each rank decides alone whether to apply its saved plan. If the ranks disagree, startup can hang. This PR has the ranks vote first: all apply or none do. ## Claims - A rank applies its plan only if every rank in the world group can. - A rank that skips an applicable plan logs why. ## Validation - New test `test_startup_plan_applies_on_every_rank_or_none` runs two gloo ranks through three rounds. It fails on main (rank 0 applies while rank 1 cannot) and passes with this PR. CI runs it in "V1 Executor + Worker". - GPUs: Qwen3-0.6B with TP=2 across two L40S nodes. Before the third boot rank 1's plan is made unusable. With `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` main hangs (no `/health` after 600 s) and this PR comes up healthy. With defaults both come up healthy. ## Details Applying a plan sets `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, which makes `determine_available_memory` skip `profile_cudagraph_memory()`. Its graph captures run collectives. A rank that profiles alone waits forever. The V2 runner skips the capture when the extensible KV cache is on (its CUDA default). The V1 runner and V2 with that cache off still capture. Ranks split most easily under DP. DP ranks with the same TP/PP rank share one plan file. One rank's free-memory baseline can then fail another's gate. We hit this on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with DP8. The vote is one `cpu_all_reduce_` over the world group. Related: #60143, #57983, #63388 and #60228. None changes how ranks agree. **AI assistance:** Claude helped write the code, tests and this description. --

title: [Perf] Bypass DispatchPooler grouping for homogeneous tasks
summary: ## Overview When all requests use the same pooling task, `DispatchPooler` still slices metadata and hidden states, calls the sub-pooler, and converts its dense output into individual row tensors. Bypass grouping for homogeneous tasks and return the sub-pooler's output directly, allowing MRv2's existing dense output path to issue one D2H copy for a fully finished batch. ## Claims - Improve short-query embedding throughput by **3.8% at concurrency 64** and **10.3% at concurrency 128** on the GH200 workload below. The gain comes from doing less CPU work per request on the EngineCore busy loop, which is the bottleneck in this scenario: one batched device-to-host copy per step instead of one copy, one pinned-memory allocation and one pinned free (with their CUDA event bookkeeping) per request. - Avoid redundant pooling metadata operations and per-row D2H copies when the sub-pooler returns a dense batch. Ragged outputs and the mixed-task fallback remain supported. ## Validation ### Benchmark Embedding throughput for short text queries on one NVIDIA GH200 (144 GB). title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Respect disabled chunked prefill for multimodal requests
summary: ## Overview Fix partial prefill of multimodal pooling requests when chunked prefill is disabled. Bidirectional MEAN-pooling models can crash under async encoder-cache pressure or an explicit long-prefill threshold. ## Claims - Defer the whole request when encoder limits would force partial prefill, releasing acquired cache references and restoring the compute budget. - Ignore `long_prefill_token_threshold` when chunked prefill is disabled. - Add scheduler and real-model regression coverage for both triggers. ## Validation Reproduced with real weights for `nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2`, using Model Runner V2. Both cases queue two distinct images with chunked prefill disabled: - **Encoder-cache pressure:** async scheduling, a 384-token budget/cache, and 256 tokens per image. The second request fits the next step's token budget while the first image still occupies the encoder cache. - **Prefill threshold:** synchronous scheduling with `long_prefill_token_threshold=128`, which incorrectly splits the queued prompts. With the unchanged upstream scheduler (`c7a7607519`), both cases raise `RuntimeError: partial prefill is not supported with MEAN pooling`. With this fix, both complete and every batched embedding matches its individually processed reference with cosine similarity ≥0.999. summary: ### Report of performance regression Since #56876 moved DeepGEMM to vllm-project/DeepGEMM `e1f418c2`, `get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` returns 128 on SM12x. DeepGEMM 2.6.1 (`8b1392b9`) returned 64 when each expert gets at most 64 rows. The fork's SM120 port (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#4) left that rule unwired. vLLM pads the contiguous MoE layout with this alignment, so decode pads twice as many rows and the grouped GEMMs run with `BLOCK_M=128`. DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, DFlash (7 speculative tokens), TP1, vLLM main 70fc359d (official cu130 aarch64 wheel).
