title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL issues up to ~112k KV descriptors per rank-transfer, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**. The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's. Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below. ### Measurements GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion. | Transport | Descriptors / transfer | Post mean | Total mean | Movement remainder | Payload / remainder | Post share | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | RoCE `rc_x`, 1 rail | 91,262 | 32.1 ms | 517.4 ms | 485.2 ms | 6.45 GB/s | 6.2% | | MNNVL `cuda_ipc` | 112,092 | **455.9 ms** | 800.8 ms | 345.0 ms | 14.16 GB/s | **56.9%** | | Native IB `rc_x`, 4 rails | 119,984 |

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Bound expert_map gathers on data-derived expert ids
summary: ## Summary Four MoE kernels index `expert_map` with an expert id taken from `topk_ids`, guarding the gather with a sign check only (`expert_id >= 0` / `expert_id < 0`). `topk_ids` is data, not a loop bound: the routers allocate it with `torch.empty` and do not always overwrite every slot, so a stale slot can hold an arbitrary positive value. When that happens the gather reads far past the end of `expert_map` and the context dies with a Warp MMU fault on **every** rank. `get_local_expert_id()` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu` already applies exactly the missing bound: ```cpp int expert_id = topk_ids[idx]; if (expert_id >= num_experts || expert_id < 0) { return -1; } ``` This PR bounds the other four consumers the same way. **Updated after review:** an id at or past `expert_map`'s length is a producer bug, so instead of skipping the slot the kernels stop with a clear message (CUDA `printf` + trap; the Triton kernels use a predicated PTX trap, since `tl.device_assert` is compiled out outside Triton debug mode, and fall back to `tl.device_assert` on other platforms). `-1` remains the not-routed sentinel, and the loads stay bounded, so the map is never read out of bounds even before the trap fires. ## Relationship to the root cause These gathers were the *victims*, not the cause. The garbage expert ids originated upstream: the sampler could emit a token id equal to `vocab_size`, and DeepSeek-V4's hash-MoE router turned that into a garbage expert id by gathering past its lookup table. Both are fixed separately in #50843 (sampler) and #50844 (DSv4 hash router

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Keep per-shard weight global scales in compressed-tensors NVFP4 linears
summary: ## Purpose `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.process_weights_after_loading` runs a fused NVFP4 linear (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, Qwen3.5's `in_proj_qkvz` / `in_proj_ba`, ...) with the largest `weight_global_scale` divisor of its shards and only logs a warning when they differ. Every shard with a smaller divisor is then dequantized `gs_shard / gs_max` times too small. llm-compressor gives each checkpoint tensor its own global scale unless it fuses them. For example, `sakamakismile/Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-NVFP4` (Qwen3.5 architecture) has different scales for `in_proj_qkv` / `in_proj_z` and `in_proj_b` / `in_proj_a` in all 48 Gated DeltaNet layers. In every layer, one side of each pair is dequantized x0.36 to x0.99 too small. That changes z (output gate), b (beta) and a (decay) relative to the rest; these are used without normalization. Generation stays coherent, which is why this is easy to miss. ## Changes - Keep the GEMM exactly as today (the largest divisor). Record the column ranges of the shards whose divisor differs, with the factor `gs_max / gs_shard`, and multiply those output columns in place in `apply_weights`, before adding the bias. Adjacent shards with the same factor are merged into one range (e.g. q/k/v of `in_proj_qkvz`). - It works for any number of partitions and with every NVFP4 linear kernel, because it wraps `kernel.apply_weights`. The factors are applied as fp32 scalars. - Layers with a shared global scale take the unchanged path. - The warning for mismatched *weight* global scales is removed, because they are now handled. title: [Kernel][Sampler] Replace Gaussian pivot with order statistic in combined top-k/top-p Triton kernel
summary: Fixes #61998 ## Overview The zeroth pass of `_topk_topp_kernel` picks the gather pivot with a Gaussian quantile (`avg + std * sigma`) fitted to the **first 8192 logits only**. On real logits (MiMo-V2.6 measurements in the issue) the head of the row carries systematically higher values, and skewed rows break the Gaussian fit entirely; the gather then returns fewer than `k` candidates and the row falls back to a full-vocab ternary search, 3-6x slower per row, stalling every other row in the batch. This PR replaces the Gaussian estimate with an **order statistic of a strided sample taken across the whole row**: - Sample `S = BLOCK_SIZE / 4` logits uniformly across the row (one lane every `NUM_TILES * 4` vocab entries), so head bias cannot skew the estimate. - Target `m = max(8, ceil(4 * k * S / V))` — the m-th largest sample value, found with a 12-step in-register binary search (no extra global memory traffic). The 4x margin over `k` keeps the gathered set small (a few hundred entries at V=152576) while reliably covering `k`. - When the sample holds no finite logits (grammar bitmask hiding most of the vocab), the pivot degenerates to `+inf` (gather nothing) and the existing full-row fallback search runs with its finite, well-scaled bounds. A sentinel like `-1e30` would instead poison the buffer-search range and never converge (found via a fuzz case, fixed in `test_topk_pivot_all_masked_sample`). - The Gaussian path, both sigma tables and the table upload, are removed. ## Claims - Rows whose gather previously failed no longer take the full-vocab fallback: **3-6x lower latency p

I ran MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL (mxfp4, 309B/15B MoE) on 4x MI210 with that flag for several days without incident, so the kernel path itself is in good shape on CDNA2. title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 vision crash with online FP8 quantization
summary: ## Overview Fixes #63732. With `--quantization fp8`, an image request to Gemma 4 returns HTTP 500 and kills the engine core. The transformers patch embedder casts the pixel values to `input_proj.weight.dtype`. Once vLLM quantizes that layer, this dtype is `float8_e4m3fn`, so the FP8 linear gets an FP8 input. title: [Bugfix] Partition HF3FS external cache keys by multimodal and LoRA identity
summary: ## Overview `HF3FSKVConnector` keys its external cache on `md5(prompt token ids)`. title: [Bugfix] Stop advertising fp8_e5m2 where the KV writer stores e4m3
summary: ## Overview `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` stores an e4m3 variant for every fp8 cache dtype, but `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN` advertise `fp8_e5m2`, and the readers decode that cache as `torch.float8_e5m2`. The cache therefore holds e4m3 bits read back as e5m2, and the model produces garbage with no error. This PR stops advertising `fp8_e5m2` on those two backends and refuses it in the writer. ## Claims - **Bug:** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` on `TRITON_ATTN` (any block size) and on `ROCM_ATTN` (block sizes other than 16/32) silently stores e4m3 bits. title: [RFC]: ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs instead of state for faster standard and speculative decode (Mamba2 + GDN)
summary: ### Motivation. > This RFC also serves as the tracking hub for ReplaySSM across vLLM, FlashInfer, and TensorRT-LLM. Status tables are kept live as work lands; PRs are linked rather than duplicated. It supersedes [RFC #47572](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47572) [ReplaySSM](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/) ([vllm#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576)) is a memory-bandwidth optimization for the decode kernels of state space model (SSM) and linear-attention layers. It was developed concurrently and independently by @Johnny-Liou at Dao AI Lab and @hnover-nv at NVIDIA. A concurrent cross-framework implementation is in [TensorRT-LLM (#14203)](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/14203), developed by @hnover-nv. SSM decode is memory-bound: today each step reads and writes back the full recurrent state. ReplaySSM instead keeps a single checkpoint state and caches recent SSM inputs in a ring buffer. It reconstructs the state only when needed, computing the output directly from the checkpoint plus cached inputs on every other step, and writes the full state back only once every `L` steps. This helps two cases: 1. **Standard decode.** Writing the state back once every `L` steps instead of every step roughly halves the dominant memory traffic in the bandwidth-bound SSM kernel. 2. **Speculative decode.** The SSM state update is irreversible, so today's implementation keeps a separate recurrent state per draft token (~`(1 + num_spec)×` the state). title: [Feature]: Fast Start For vLLM
summary: ## Overview Fast Start reduces vLLM startup time by avoiding repeated checkpoint loading, weight processing, and kernel autotuning during engine restarts and scaling events. The core design uses a persistent per-GPU weight daemon. The daemon loads and processes model weights once, keeps sharded weights in GPU memory, and exposes them to new vLLM engines through CUDA IPC or a multi-node transport. When a compatible cache is unavailable, vLLM falls back to the existing checkpoint loader. ## Design Goals - Reuse processed GPU weights across engine instances. - Support TP, PP, EP, multi-node deployments, and MTP. - Support quantized formats including FP8 and FP4. - Cache autotune results with hardware- and version-aware keys. - Preserve correctness through strict cache validation. - Provide a reliable fallback path for cache misses and failures. ## Cache Validation Cache entries are identified using model and checkpoint identity, quantization configuration, parallelism settings, GPU architecture, vLLM protocol version, and other relevant runtime metadata. Incompatible entries must never be silently reused. Cache misses, stale daemon connections, and validation failures produce diagnostics and fall back to the normal loading path when enabled. ## Roadmap ### Weight Daemon (core) - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54921 - [ ] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56047 - [ ] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60086 ### Parallelism - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57386 - [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55477 - [x] https://githu

title: [Performance]: Avoid extra logits passes for temperature-only sampling
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance Hi, I noticed that MRV2 still copies logits to FP32 and runs a separate temperature-scaling kernel for plain temperature-only sampling. The existing Gumbel kernel can apply temperature while loading the logits, so these extra passes appear unnecessary when no filters, penalties, or processed-logit consumers are active. I have a small CUDA patch that reuses that kernel and registers its variants for compile-only startup warmup. [Patch available for review](https://github.com/TwilightTechie/vllm/commit/fe073514e0178c44bc4f457349536331442e4ad8). ### Measurements On one Modal H100 with Qwen3-0.6B BF16, batch 32, temperature 0.8, 128-token inputs and 256-token outputs, the before/after run of the updated patch measured: | Metric | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | Full-generation output tokens/s | 10,957 | 11,218 | | Inferred decode output tokens/s | 11,799 | 12,316 | This was one fresh process per arm, with eight timed runs at each output length. A separate earlier prototype experiment used A/B/B/A order and showed 3–4% higher generation throughput. Clocks were not locked; smaller-batch results drifted, so I would not generalize this result. The patch passes 72 sampler tests. The 70 parity cases also pass on baseline; the two added warmup-coverage tests fail on baseline and pass with the patch. A real-weight startup check also passed with runtime JIT compilation forbidden. title: [Bugfix] Reject a KV cache dtype that silently reinterprets the model's bits
summary: ## Overview `--kv-cache-dtype float16` on a bfloat16 model (or `bfloat16` on a float16 model) is accepted at config time. The C++ cache writers then store the model dtype's bits in a cache that is read back as the requested dtype. On the MLA path this produces fluent nonsense with no error on v0.30.0 (measured below); v0.31.0 has the same `kAuto` mapping and no config check. This PR rejects that pair at config time. Related: #38922, #43330. ## Claims - **Bug:** with an explicit unquantized cache dtype that differs from the model dtype, every C++ `DISPATCH_BY_KV_CACHE_DTYPE` write copies raw bits instead of converting. Reachable silently on stock vLLM through `concat_and_cache_mla` (measured on ROCm), and through `reshape_and_cache_flash` on CUDA by the same macro (#38922's traceback shows the CUDA flash backend entering it; not measured here). - **Root cause:** `get_fp8_kv_cache_data_type` maps `auto`, `float16` and `bfloat16` to `kAuto`, and the `kAuto` arm instantiates only same-type pairs (`FN(uint16_t, uint16_t)`, `FN(__nv_bfloat16, __nv_bfloat16)`), identically in `amd/` and `nvidia/quant_utils.cuh`. The cache tensor is allocated at the requested dtype, so writer and reader disagree. - **Fix:** `VllmConfig._verify_unquantized_kv_cache_dtype()` raises a `ValueError` that names both dtypes. `auto`, a cache dtype equal to the model dtype, and every quantized dtype are unchanged. ## Validation All runs below: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0`, MI250 (gfx90a). title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Honor and normalize explicit VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT

summary: ## Overview A media cache entry evicted between its metadata check and read can be recreated as an empty file, causing image decoding to fail. title: [Perf][DiffusionGemma] Canvas packing + canvas swap: up to 10x lower short-request latency under load
summary: ## Overview Every DiffusionGemma request gets the full served canvas (256 tokens, about two paragraphs). Each denoising step computes and budgets all 256 positions, whether the reply is 14 tokens or 250, so under load short replies queue behind work that is mostly padding. When the scheduler preempts a request mid-block, the half-denoised canvas is discarded and the block restarts from noise. This PR adds two opt-in mechanisms to the MRV2 runner. Both are off by default. - **Canvas packing** (`VLLM_DIFFUSION_PACK_SPANS`): two requests share one canvas. A per-sequence span mask in Triton unified attention keeps each request's queries off the other's keys. A per-request RoPE remap gives each request the positions it would have if served alone. - **Canvas swap** (`VLLM_DIFFUSION_CANVAS_SWAP`, `VLLM_DIFFUSION_CANVAS_SWAP_CAP`): on preemption, the request's in-flight block (canvas, step, stability history, self-conditioning embeds, pending logprobs) is stashed in a bounded host-RAM FIFO. It is restored after the re-prefill, so the block resumes where it stopped. **Not a duplicate.** No open PR or issue covers canvas packing or preemption-safe canvas state (searched `diffusion canvas`, `DiffusionGemma preempt`, `DiffusionGemma packing`, `span mask triton`, `diffusion_canvas_length`). #60663 fuses self-conditioning kernels. #57250 and #59107 added client-chosen per-request canvas widths, which need the reply length up front; packing does not (see Details). ## Claims - **Up to 10x lower short-request latency on real traffic shapes.** On Azure code traces, short-request p50 is 10.0-

title: [RFC]: TokenGate integration into vLLM
summary: ### Motivation. I’m working on integrating [TokenGate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26754) into vLLM, starting with Qwen3 and Qwen3.5. TokenGate adapts pretrained language models to perform learned token pruning during prefill. A trained gate scores the prunable input tokens at an intermediate layer and selects a subset to retain, alongside all non-prunable tokens. Subsequent layers process this shorter sequence, reducing prefill computation and KV-cache storage in the full-attention layers above the gate. We evaluated Qwen3-1.7B on RepoBench-P, 2WikiMultihopQA, MultiNews, BioDEX, and needle-in-a-haystack retrieval. TokenGate achieves 1.4-11.3× faster TTFT and 1.5-3.4× lower peak prefill memory at matched accuracy against fine-tuned full-context baselines. On Qwen3.5-2B, TokenGate achieves 3.8× faster TTFT on 32K needle-in-a-haystack retrieval without losing accuracy. We’d like to make this available through vLLM’s existing Python and serving APIs. ### Proposed Change. A user would load a TokenGate-adapted checkpoint, specify the input span eligible for pruning, and choose a retained-token budget. Training would happen outside vLLM. We’d reuse the existing Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 implementations. The main changes would be: 1. Add an optional gate that selects prunable input tokens while preserving all non-prunable tokens and the original position IDs of retained tokens. 2. Apply TokenGate’s learned attention bias and scaling in the full-attention layers above the gate. 3. Let the runner and cache manager handle different sequence lengths before and after pruning. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Use 64-bit row offsets in the persistent and cooperative top-k kernels
summary: ## Overview `persistent_topk` and `cooperative_topk` compute each row's start in the logits tensor as a 32-bit product. Once one call's logits exceed 2^32 elements, the product wraps and every later row selects its top-k from the wrong row. This widens those products to 64 bits, matching `sampled_topk` and `top_k_per_row_decode`, which already use 64-bit row offsets. ## Claims - Fixes wrong sparse-attention indices for decode top-k calls with more than 2^32 logits elements. With the default decode logits budget from #64806 (2048 MiB), every call stays below 2^32 elements. The bug is still reachable when `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_DECODE_LOGITS_MB` is 0 (no chunking), or at least 8192 with BF16 indexer logits (16384 with FP32, see #64580), and on decode paths that do not chunk. - No measurable kernel time change (table below). ## Validation **Kernel check, Baseline vs After PR.** The Baseline is main `2a777ce26e`; After PR is this PR on the same commit. summary: ## Overview NVFP4 linears add the bias in a separate kernel after the GEMM. When the output goes straight to the attention custom op (the QKV projection of BERT/XLM-R and Qwen2-style models), Inductor cannot fuse that add, and on large prefills it costs more than the GEMM. This PR adds an optional `bias` to `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm`, applied in the SM120 epilogue (CUTLASS `LinCombPerColBias`) as the FP8 CUTLASS path already does, and passes it from `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`. ## Claims - The SM120 epilogue add costs 0.007 ms on an 81920 x 3072 x 1024 GEMM, vs 0.749 ms for a separate `out + bias`. - `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` passes the bias to the GEMM on SM12x unless N is padded. - `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 with `linear_backend="cutlass"`: 12-13% less GPU time per batch on an RTX PRO 6000. ## Validation RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130. - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`: 28 passed, 14 of them with a bias. bge-reranker-v2-m3 (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, classifier excluded), `linear_backend="cutlass"`, GPU kernel time of one `classify` call on 128 sequences; two alternating rounds per arm agree within 0.1 ms: | | 128 x 640 tokens | 128 x 320 tokens | |---|---|---| | main (separate bias add) | 135.1 ms | 60.4 ms | | this PR | **119.1 ms** | **52.5 ms** | The QKV bias kernels (16.1 ms at 640 tokens) disappear and the GEMMs take 0.4 ms longer; Inductor already fuses the other bias adds into the next LayerNorm or GELU kernel. Recall@10 on 60 questions each of Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko: 0.898 / 0.941 v

title: [Bug]: NixlConnector: KV blocks released on lease expiry while remote READ in flight, decode silently consumes overwritten KV
summary: ### Your current environment **Env:** vLLM 0.30.0 (aed92ba5), NixlConnector 1P1D on one host, UCX (`UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`), Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 2048`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary:** With the pull flow, the producer releases a request's KV blocks when `kv_lease_duration` expires, unconditionally — it does not matter whether a consumer read is still pending or about to be issued. The consumer side has no content/identity binding on the block descriptors it received earlier, so it reads whatever bytes now occupy those slots (they may belong to a newer request that reused them) and feeds them to the model with no error or warning. Output is silently wrong. **Repro (deterministic, no code changes):** 1. Start P (`kv_role=kv_producer`) and D (`kv_role=kv_consumer`). 2. Send a completion to P with `kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": true, ...}` (max_tokens=1). Record the returned `kv_transfer_params` (remote_block_ids / remote_request_id). 3. Stall the decode engine for > `kv_lease_duration` (default 30 s). We used `SIGSTOP` on the decode processes to simulate an engine pause (GC / long step / scheduler stall); ~33.6 s total. 4. During the stall, P logs: `Releasing expired KV blocks for request <id> which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired.` 5. Send new completions to P (same total token length) so the freed slots are reused and overwritten with different content. 6. title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: reset MoE expert padding at begin
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview At the start of a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336), zero MoE expert padding, so that post-load processing reruns over the same bytes as a cold start. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477). MoE expert parameters are often larger than the checkpoint tensors loaded into them: DeepEP rounds the hidden size up, MXFP4 / TRT-LLM / AITER backends round the intermediate size, and block-aligned FP8 TP pads shards. Loaders copy only the checkpoint part. On a direct reload the padding then holds the previous post-processed bytes, which post-load processing processes again. After a `load_format=dummy` cold start (the usual RL setup) it holds random values. ## Claims - **gpt-oss-20b (TP2, MXFP4), direct reload through IPC weight transfer:** every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh start, both after 3 same-weight syncs and after a dummy start plus one sync. On main, 168 expert tensors differ after every sync and drift from one sync to the next. After a dummy start, 288 differ and GSM8K drops about 2 points. - Cold start and layerwise reload are unchanged. - No loader changes: whether to fill is decided from `moe_config` when the checkpoint layout is recorded at cold start, so it also covers dummy and other cold starts that skip loaders, and the load plan (#64418) that bypasses them. ## Validation **This PR's head (`1e25cc87e2`) with #66010 (`84ab98b6d8`) applied, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 1319 questions, 3 updates; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid). title: [Perf][Attention] FA4 sparse MLA: grouped prefill with an FP8 KV cache
summary: ## Status On main with ShardQ (#63956, on by default under TP), the default FP8 backend prefills faster than this PR, so I don't propose it for merging as is. ShardQ gives each rank a slice of the tokens that spans requests, while this path stages one request's KV at a time, so with an FP8 cache ShardQ steps stay on trtllm-gen here. With ShardQ off, this path groups again, but main's FP8 backend with ShardQ is still faster (table below), because it keeps the KV and the math in FP8 while this path computes in BF16. A native FP8 grouped kernel, as in LiteDSA, would be the way to combine both. The branch is merged with main and tested so that it stays a correct reference. ## Overview Lets `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4` serve an FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` / `fp8_e4m3`). Decode runs on trtllm-gen's FP8 kernel, as `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` does, and the grouped prefill of #63104 reads a BF16 copy of each prefill request's KV. Stacked on #63104, which depends on vllm-project/flash-attention#205. Default backend selection does not change: for a quantized cache the SM100 sparse priority list stays `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, so this path is opt-in with `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4`. Related work: LiteDSA (arXiv 2607.11976) groups neighbouring queries in the same way for the FP8 sparse MLA path, on a vendored FlashMLA SM100 FP8 kernel. It was proposed in #48726 and removed from it in a later commit, so #48726 now carries only the LiteTopk indexer. #60806 (draft) would let the FA4 masked-MHA prefill serve an FP8 cache when the prefill query is BF

title: [RL][Model Loader] Load plan: plan_loads and TraceTensor
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item P1). Builds on #64336 (direct reload). Engines that move sharded bytes themselves (sharded RDT, NCCL M2N) need to know, for each checkpoint tensor, which part this rank needs and where in live memory it goes. This PR adds the engine-neutral answer from RFC §3/§4: - `plan_loads(model, metadata)` traces the model's own `load_weights` once, between `start_reload` and `finish_reload`, on the tensors direct reload just viewed back; - it returns a `LoadPlan` with `get_boxes(name)` (what this rank needs) and `get_dest(name)` (where it goes); `load_planned` applies it to full tensors. The NCCL broadcast engine can opt in (`use_load_plan`, off by default), which exercises the plan end to end. Sharded RDT (E1) and NCCL M2N (E2) move onto it in follow-ups and are the users of `get_boxes`. Cold start and the existing reload paths are unchanged. Not a duplicate: no open PR implements `plan_loads` or `TraceTensor`. The M0 prototype on #64418 is a measurement tool and is not proposed for merge. ## Assumptions The plan relies on these and does not check them. A problem that only arises when one is broken is out of scope here (RFC §1, §5, §6). **Loaders** (the target models' `load_weights`): - Each name is handled as it arrives, on its own: no holding a tensor for another name and no deferring, within a call or across calls. - Parameters are written only with `copy_`; a loader never replaces a parameter or buffer. - State a loader sets is harmless or needed, and nothing that post-load processing or the forward reads. title: [Model Loader] One finish for every update path; drop refresh_derived_weights
summary: ## Overview Every load and weight-update path now finishes through `finalize_model_weights`, and weight-derived state has one hook again: each module's own `process_weights_after_loading()`. Before this PR the paths finished differently: | path | quant methods | attention-like layers | other modules' hooks | |---|---|---|---| | cold start, direct reload (`process_weights_after_loading`) | yes | yes (loader pass) | yes | | layerwise reload | yes (per layer) | yes (`_finalize_attention_layer`) | yes | | sparse NCCL finish | — | **no** | yes | | kernel-format `reload_weights` | — | **no** | **no** | #64886 covered the two gaps with a second per-module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, and a walker. Kimi-K3 ROCm's KDA layer is a `MambaBase`, hence attention-like, so `finalize_model_weights` skipped its hook and its decode copies stayed stale after a sparse update or a kernel-format reload. This PR closes both gaps without a second hook: - `finalize_model_weights` runs every module's hook in one children-first traversal, attention-like layers included (those under `device_loading_context` when given a target device). Attention hooks need the quant pass done, which the loader does first, and must precede their ancestors' hooks, which children-first gives; no hook reads attention-derived state from a non-ancestor, so there is no separate attention pass. Quant methods and the submodules of quantized layers are still skipped. - The loader's own attention pass and the hook call in layerwise `_finalize_attention_layer` are removed, so every hook runs once per load, from one place. -

title: [Perf][Core] Reduce per-block CPU cost of KV block allocation and caching
summary: ## Overview Reduces the per-block Python work on the scheduler's main thread when an async KV load starts, is promoted to running, and finishes. These costs grow linearly with prompt length, and on a DP decode instance a slow `schedule()` on one rank holds up the per-step all-reduce. Related: #61725 limits load starts per step to contain this cost; this makes each load cheaper. #64379 and #65285 target the repeated reservation sum, which is a separate cost. ## Claims - For a 140K-token request, start + promote + finish CPU time drops about 50% on a DeepSeek-V4.1-shaped KV layout (2.66 to 1.34 ms) and about 45% with one group at block size 16 (10.55 to 5.79 ms). - Source changes are net neutral in size (+51/-49 lines), and two properties are removed. - No behaviour change intended. These paths are shared by all requests, so non-P/D traffic benefits too. **Not yet shown:** an end-to-end improvement. These are scheduler-only numbers, with no real P/D run, so the effect on `schedule()` time and GPU wait in serving is unmeasured. ## Validation ### Timing Real `Scheduler` and NIXL scheduler connector, with no GPU or transfer. GB200 host (aarch64), Python 3.12, 32 requests per run. Each value is the median of 3 rounds, each round being the median of 5 runs, interleaved with the baseline on one node. title: [ROCm][Kernel] Follow-ups to the gfx942 MLA Triton verify kernel
summary: - Run `test_decode_attention_fwd_verify_int64_page_offset` at 128 heads too, so the 64-row QSPLIT path is checked past 2 GiB, and free cached memory before its free-memory gate. - `verify_num_kv_splits` takes the launch config from `select_verify_config` itself instead of from the caller. - Replace `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG` with a private base config that holds only the values both launch configs share. - Cite ROCm/aiter#6732 in the FP8 V-scale probe and use `_ASM_PADDED_MAX_PS_QLEN` for its qlen bound. - Fix the `_forward_triton_verify` docstring (only a varlen tail comes back as zeros) and a stale test comment. These are the non-blocking follow-ups from the review of #62725, plus a few cleanups found by re-reading the merged code. The int64 test used to run only at 16 heads, which always picks the small-tile config, so the QSPLIT path's own page loads were never tested past 2 GiB. With the 128-head case, truncating one QSPLIT page offset to int32 causes an illegal memory access, while the 16-head case still passes. The test's memory gate also counted memory held by the caching allocator as used, so it could skip silently on a busy shard. On the kernel side, `VERIFY_DEFAULT_CONFIG`'s `BLOCK_H`, `BLOCK_N`, `num_warps` and `MIN_SPLIT_LEN` were always overridden, and `verify_num_kv_splits` defaulted to a split length the kernel never uses. Having it read the real launch config means the workspace reservation can't drift from the launch. title: [Bugfix] Exclude cudagraph padding rows from the per-tensor FP8 MoE amax
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #62124. With a dynamic per-tensor FP8 activation scale, the Triton fused-MoE path computes the amax over every row of the batch the model runner hands it. Under CUDA graphs that batch is padded to the capture size, and the padding rows hold whatever the previous step left there: stale hidden states, or, once the router skips padding (`VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1`, the default), workspace rows that the first GEMM never wrote. So the scale used for a request's own rows, and with it the request's output, depends on the request that ran before it. The reporter's script shows the first generated token changing with the previous request; `--enforce-eager` is clean because nothing is padded. Two quantizations see the padding rows: the expert input (`a1`, in `MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEP.prepare`) and the post-activation intermediate (`intermediate_cache2`, in `TritonExperts.apply`). This PR computes both per-tensor scales over the non-padding rows only, with `masked_amax_scale` and the `is_padding` mask the model runner already keeps for the router. The V2 model runner only filled that mask under `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`; it now fills it always (as the V1 runner does), so the fix does not depend on that flag. Nothing changes for static or per-token/block activation scales, and without padding rows the masked input scale is bitwise the dynamic one. summary: ## Summary Prefill fastpath for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on gfx950 (MI355X): fold the shared expert into the routed MoE grouped GEMM as one appended slot (E 384→385, topk 6→7), keeping its native FP8 block-32 weights — no requant, fused/stock outputs match bit-for-bit. title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Retune the MXFP8 dot_scaled GEMM tiles for M=17-256
summary: ## What `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (Triton `tl.dot_scaled`) picks its tile in `_select_cfg`. This adds a shape-scoped tile table (`_M31_TP4_TILES`, keyed by the local `(N, K)`) for M <= 256 covering the fused qkv, o_proj, shared-expert gate_up / down, dense gate_up / down and the DSpark qkv. Decode and verify batches are M = 8 x requests, so M = 8..256 spans c1..c32. Everything else is unchanged: M <= 16 for qkv / gate_up / shared down keeps its tile, M > 256 and every other shape use the existing selection, every other arch is untouched (the tile table is gated on CDNA4, `get_cdna_version() == 4`, i.e. gfx95x where it was tuned). ## Why These GEMMs read each weight byte once and are weight-bandwidth bound (FLOPs are under 10% of the time at M=32, about 40% at M=128). title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Pick the NVFP4 sparse decode splits per XCD, not per CU
summary: ## Purpose The NVFP4 sparse decode kernel of MiniMax-M3.1 (`ops/nvfp4_sparse_decode`, ROCm gfx950, XCD-aware grid) picks its number of splits with `decode_splits`, a cost model that spreads the work over all CUs of the device (256 on MI355X). The XCD-aware grid does not do that: it places a request's rows and all of its splits on **one XCD (32 CUs)**. The model therefore mispredicts: at 5 concurrent requests (DSpark 7: 8 rows per request) it picks **6 splits (the `s6` variant, 15.4-15.7 us per layer)** where 4 splits take 11.9 us, and at 1-4 requests it picks 8 splits (12.4-13.3 us) where 4 splits take 11.2-12.4 us. `s6` appears only at exactly 5 requests, which is a common decode batch in the AgentX c16 workload (about 15% of request decode time). This PR adds `_xcd_splits`, used only when the heuristic would otherwise run (explicit `splits=` and the `splits == 1` large-grid path are unchanged), for the shape it was measured on (top-k 16, 8 rows per request = DSpark 7); every other shape keeps `decode_splits`: - up to 3 requests per XCD, i.e. up to 8 requests on 4 XCDs and 17-24 requests: 4 splits; - 2 requests per XCD (9-16 requests): 2 splits. summary: ### Environment - vLLM 0.32.0 built from the sdist for sm_70 (Tesla V100 PCIe 32 GB, driver 580.196.07, CUDA 12.9), torch 2.13.0+cu126. title: [RFC]: Internal Process-level Fault Tolerance for vLLM
summary: ### Motivation. Modern sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model service like DeepSeek use hybrid parallelism (e.g., DP+EP) across multiple GPUs and nodes for high-throughput inference, but this tight coupling makes them highly fault-sensitive — a single GPU or network failure can halt the entire instance. **vLLM currently follows a fail-stop recovery model**, where any fault terminates the whole instance, causing minute-long recovery delays and request interruptions — **an overly rigid approach for transient or localized issues such as short communication drops or single-GPU errors**. To address these challenges, we propose to introduce internal process-level fault tolerance mechanisms. These mechanisms aim to handle local faults efficiently while minimizing service interruption from minutes to seconds. Based on publicly reported hardware failure statistics[[1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21783),[2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.09343v1),[3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.16293)], we estimate that approximately 70% of failures can be mitigated by the proposed process-level fault tolerance mechanism. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf2161ae-d037-4066-9dba-b1651aa41c37) ### Proposed Change. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16a687ca-49f2-4f0a-b7d0-eabf9c2f37ad) In typical industrial deployments, vLLM serves as the engine while the upper-layer framework (e.g., AIBrix) is responsible for system-wide monitoring, diagnosis, and recovery decisions. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid catastrophic cancellation in the acceptance estimator
summary: ## Overview Follow-up to #52228, which added the estimator to do adaptive verification without a confidence head. The adaptive-verification acceptance feature loses its entire signal to catastrophic cancellation whenever the drafter is confident. Every draft row more confident than `1 - 6e-8` reports the same acceptance feature, `40.0`, whatever its true confidence is. The feature is specified as a log-odds, `logit(q(m*))`, but it recovers the complement mass by subtracting 1 from a sum that includes the max's own unit term, which in fp32 destroys the quantity being measured — no NaN, no warning, just the clamp. **Headline:** at temperature 0.5 on source code, **11.5% of draft positions** had their confidence score destroyed and replaced with a constant. The failing positions are not exotic or adversarial — the single worst case in the sample is completing `tl.int64` from `tl.int6` (see the `Details` section for the error analysis). This PR computes the complement directly instead fixing completely the numerical issue. ## Claims - The feature is accurate to fp32 relative precision across the full range it is clamped to. Previously it saturated to the `_MAX_LOG_ODDS` clamp for any row more confident than `1 - 6e-8`, collapsing a ~23-nat span of distinct confidences onto a single value. - No change to the feature's definition, the fit, the trimming policy, or any buffer layout the rest of adaptive verification reads. - One extra fp32 partial per (token, vocab block): 0.1% of the kernel's memory traffic (311 KiB against 311 MiB of logit reads at 1024 tokens and a 152k vocab).

title: [Perf][Frontend] Render plain completion stream deltas from a template
summary: Working with smaller models I've noticed I pay "high tax" on format in every stream response. `completion_stream_generator` builds a `CompletionStreamResponse` and a `CompletionResponseStreamChoice` per streamed chunk and dumps them with `model_dump_json`. title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Allow push with DCP when both instances shard identically
summary: ## Purpose `NixlPushConnector` refuses decode context parallelism outright, so no P/D-disaggregated topology with DCP can use the WRITE path: ``` NixlPushConnector does not support decode_context_parallel_size > 1. ``` #50611 added DCP to the NIXL **pull** path and, being scoped to READ, guarded the other two cases with blanket refusals: `NixlPushConnector.__init__` rejects `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`, and `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.__init__` rejects hybrid MLA+Mamba with `dcp_size > 1`. Push does not need the general solution the pull path needed. A WRITE goes rank to rank and never slices a block across ranks, and for equal TP and DCP on both sides `dcp_source_ranks(8, 8)` reduces to `[local_dcp_rank]` with `dcp_consumer_count == 1` — the identity mapping. What push actually requires is that the two instances shard the KV cache the same way. So this PR replaces the two refusals with one precondition, checked where the two configurations first meet: - `NixlPushConnector.__init__`: drop the DCP refusal. - `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.__init__`: keep the hybrid+DCP refusal for the pull path (`self._TRANSFER_MODE != "push"`), where prefix-cache-aware DCP slicing for the Mamba group really is unimplemented. - `_validate_remote_parallel_config`: refuse push when `local_dcp_size != remote_dcp_size`, with a message that names both sides. Net effect: symmetric DCP works over push; asymmetric DCP is rejected at handshake instead of at construction; the pull path is untouched. title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Emit FunctionGemma tool calls that arrive in a single streaming delta
summary: ## Purpose `FunctionGemmaToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` dropped a tool call entirely when the whole `<start_function_call>call:name{...}<end_function_call>` block arrived inside one streaming delta, which happens with speculative decoding, multi-token prediction or `stream_interval > 1`. A tool call was only opened in the branch guarded by `start_count > prev_start_count and start_count > end_count`. When a complete block lands in a single delta, `start_count == end_count` for that step, so the call was never opened and `current_tool_id` stayed at `-1`. The "call just ended" branch did run, but it found no call to close and returned `None`. The client got nothing: no name, no arguments, no error, even though non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` parses the same text correctly. This fix moves the completion handling into `_flush_completed_calls`, which opens any completed call that was never started (advancing `current_tool_id` and the `streamed_args_for_tool` / `prev_tool_call_arr` bookkeeping) and emits its name and arguments. A call that was already started is finished through the existing `_stream_arguments`, which replaces `_close_tool_call`. The helper is called both when a call ends and when a delta closes one call while opening the next, so trailing arguments of an in-flight call are not lost when a new `<start_function_call>` shows up in the same delta. A delta that carries several calls now reports all of them in one update. title: [ROCm][DSV4.1] Quantize the shared query once with AITER's fused dual RMSNorm
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek V4.1 normalizes the q-lora and kv halves of the fused down-projection together. Where both query projections (`wq_b` and the indexer's `wq_b`) take MXFP8 input, it quantizes the normalized Q **once** and hands both projections the same `QuantizedActivation` (`fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` / `can_fuse_query_quant`). That path is CUDA-only. On ROCm, each projection quantizes the same Q again, so a decode-sized batch runs the RMSNorm, two activation quantizations and two GEMMs. This PR brings the shared quantization to ROCm: - **`_aiter_ops`** registers AITER's `fused_dual_rmsnorm_mxfp8_quant` (in ROCm/aiter since v0.1.27, the version `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` pins) as `fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_mxfp8_quant`, with a fake impl, next to the existing per-token and group-quant dual RMSNorm ops. It normalizes both halves in one launch and quantizes Q to e4m3 with row-major `[M, K / 32]` E8M0 scales. - **`fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant`** calls it on ROCm. Those scales are the layout `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` reads (`input_quant_key` notes it differs from FlashInfer's swizzled scales). - **`can_fuse_query_quant`** accepts ROCm consumers when AITER is enabled, the AITER function is importable, and every consumer is `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` and `supports_quantized_input` (it reads the activation as is, never dequantizing it back). Anything else keeps the current unfused path. ## Accuracy AITER's MXFP8 is not bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`: about 3% of the e4m3 bytes and 0.2% of the scales differ, because the two kernels round differently. title: [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support
summary: # [XPU] Add Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) model architecture support Adds the `xpu/` sibling to the existing `amd/` and `nvidia/` implementations under `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/`, routed through the existing platform dispatch. It reuses `Qwen3NextAttention`, `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`, so it is much smaller than the other two backends. **Changes outside the model package** - `speculator.py` / `llm_base_proposer.py` - the MTP hidden buffer was widened via `hc_mult` (the DeepSeek-V4 spelling). Qwen4Exp calls it `hc_count`, so the `getattr` fell back to 1 and the MTP head got an un-widened buffer. Both names now accepted. - `inc_wna16_linear.py` - guard the `qzeros` copy, which can be empty or mismatched under symmetric group quantization and crashed weight load on the 512 routed experts. **`layer_types`** - Transformers v5.18 renames `full_attention` to `indexed_attention`; all three spellings map to the dense GQA block here. This does not branch on `indexer_n_heads` like `amd/`/`nvidia/` do: on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` that field is set (`4`) but the checkpoint ships no indexer tensors, so keying off it would pick a QSA path the weights cannot feed. **Known limitations** - no QSA/indexer path on XPU (such checkpoints fail at weight load rather than silently running dense attention); TP=4 needs `--enable-expert-parallel` (`moe_intermediate_size=640 / 4 = 160` is not divisible by `group_size=128` - checkpoint arithmetic, not an XPU limit); requires `transformers >= 5.16.1`, same as the other backends; TP=4 validated with `--enforce-eager` only.

title: [Core][Perf] Evict superseded Mamba align states first
summary: Draft for early review. No blocking issues. ## Overview With Mamba `align` prefix caching, each turn of a multi-turn conversation resumes from the previous turn's Mamba state and caches a deeper one. The old state is then dead for the conversation, but `BlockPool.free_blocks` queues it at the most-recently-used end, so under pool pressure it outlives live conversations' prefixes. This adds an opt-in `--evict-superseded-mamba-states` that frees such states to the front of the free queue, hashes kept. ## Claims - With the flag, a finished request's Mamba states that it resumed from, and that a deeper cached state on its own tokens supersedes, move to the front of the free queue, or go there when their last reference is freed. They stay hashed until handed out, so a branch can still hit them. - Nothing changes for preempted requests, turns that cache no deeper state, states up to a shared-prefix junction, or with the flag off. - Off by default: a branch, retry or shared system prompt that resumes from a superseded state misses once the block is handed out, which is the next allocation, since the front of the queue is ahead of never-used blocks. - Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, 88 concurrent agentic sessions with the prefill pool near capacity: +2.1% tok/s/GPU, mean TTFT 8.90 to 7.64 s. summary: ### Summary MiniMax-M3's speculative-decode **verify** step runs through the block-sparse **decode** kernel ("verify-as-decode": `_init_reorder_batch_threshold(1, supports_spec_as_decode=True)` in [`common/sparse_attention.py#L186`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9fde043f5452b2aa49c90ddeb4848e0834aa32eb/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/sparse_attention.py#L186), with `decode_query_len = 1 + num_speculative_tokens`). title: [RFC]: vLLM gRPC server API for downstream integrations
summary: ## Motivation Today, integrations that need more than OpenAI-compatible HTTP often depend on private engine objects, Python wrappers, monkey patches, or version-specific behavior. That is fragile for both vLLM and downstream users. Instead, vLLM should expose a supported gRPC runtime API that lets downstream systems and users drive a stock `vllm serve` process with explicit discovery, readiness, abort/drain, load/capacity, and KV/disaggregation surfaces. ## Goals - Allow downstream systems and users to integrate with stock vLLM images. - Keep vLLM’s native CLI, flags, scheduler, and feature behavior intact. - Provide enough runtime information for: - streaming generation, - model and capability discovery, - health/readiness, - request cancellation, - graceful drain, - load/capacity reporting, - KV-aware routing, - prefill/decode handoff. - Support local and Kubernetes deployments. - Keep the API additive and capability-driven so vLLM can expose features incrementally. ## Non-goals - Replacing vLLM’s OpenAI-compatible HTTP server. - Moving routing policy into vLLM. - Making vLLM implement downstream orchestration logic. - Requiring every vLLM feature to be available through gRPC in the first PR. - Changing vLLM’s scheduler, KV manager, or internal execution model. ## Proposed Change Promote the vLLM gRPC server into a supported runtime API and extend it beyond generation. summary: ## Purpose Fix three Hunyuan3 (Hy3) compatibility issues on Ascend NPU when MTP and/or quantization are enabled: 1. **Replace boolean mask indexing with `torch.where`**: `inputs_embeds[positions == 0] = 0` triggers unsupported `aclnnNonzeroV2` on Ascend. summary: ## Purpose SwiGLU-OAI NVFP4 checkpoints — e.g. `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`, which declares `swiglu_alpha=1.702`, `swiglu_beta=1.0`, `swiglu_limit=7.0` — generate degenerate output at temperature 0 (repeated `</`-style tokens) on every fused-MoE backend that reads its activation parameters from `FusedMoEQuantConfig`. ### Root cause `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.get_fused_moe_quant_config` forwards only `swiglu_limit`. `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_beta` are never set, so the experts fall back to `alpha=1.0, beta=0.0` and `apply_moe_activation` runs clamped plain SiLU instead of SwiGLU-OAI in every MoE layer. title: [Performance]: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration) BF16 GDN backbone isn't quantized — ~80% of per-step reads, caps decode
summary: ## Summary On `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` (arch `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`, a Mamba-2/GDN hybrid MoE), the always-active **BF16 dense backbone** (GDN in/out_proj, attention, FFN, router) is read every decode step and — by our per-step audit — is **~80% of per-step weight traffic (~2.95 GB of ~3.7 GB)**, dwarfing the NVFP4/FP8 MoE experts (~0.75 GB). Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, so this backbone caps throughput. The root cause: the GDN / linear-attention layers **don't route through the compressed-tensors quant path**, so the backbone stays BF16 even with an FP8/NVFP4 checkpoint. Attempting to requant the backbone to FP8 failed with `MergedColumnParallelLinear has no attribute data` — the GDN layers aren't handled by `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod`. ## Why it matters Quantizing the backbone BF16→FP8 is the single biggest bytes/token lever for this arch. Measured on GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121a): vLLM tops out ~42 tok/s no-spec on this model, while a different engine (atlas) that runs the *backbone* quantized reaches ~90 tok/s on the same checkpoint. The ~2× gap is essentially the un-quantized backbone. ## Ask Is this known / already addressed on main, or is there a supported way to quantize the GDN backbone of these hybrids? If not, treating the linear-attn/GDN projections as quantizable (or documenting that they aren't) would help. ## Environment / caveat Measured on vLLM **0.26.0**, GB10 / sm_121a. We have **not** re-verified against current `main` — filing to ask whether it's known or fixed. Related but distinct: #44688 (same model, low decode throughput, focused on

title: [RFC]: Hybrid KV Backend: Eliminating Disk Restore Pipeline Bubbles Without CPU Memory Bloat
summary: ## Insight While SimpleCPU ( #49644 ) already uses dedicated 2-buffer double-buffering for pure disk-to-GPU streaming, it operates in a single tier that completely discards CPU DRAM caching. Conversely, Native Tiering preserves CPU L 1 caching but suffers from an all-or-nothing staging design: it attempts to materialize the entire secondary SSD prefix into host DRAM prior to GPU transfer, directly causing memory exhaustion ( #62931 ) and forcing destructive capacity truncation ( #62932 ) . My core architectural insight is that **with maintained CPU DRAM caching, tiered restoration can be fully pipelined to eliminate transmission bubbles without dedicating extra memory or materializing secondary prefixes in CPU DRAM**: 1. **Zero-Expansion Staging via Ephemeral Credit Leases:** Instead of allocating dedicated persistent staging buffers (as in SimpleCPU) or expanding host memory to hold multi-gigabyte prefixes (as in Native Tiering) , this design dynamically borrows a tiny sliver of existing rows from `SharedOffloadRegion` on-the-fly . Leased slots are recycled immediately across waves and returned to the shared pool, allowing arbitrarily large SSD prefixes to be restored without increasing host DRAM footprint . 2. **Absorbing the Initial SSD Bubble with L 1 Hits:** Due to physical bandwidth asymmetry ($B_{\text{H2D}} \gg B_{\text{SSD}}$), initiating the first SSD read introduces a multi-hundred-millisecond latency bubble where the GPU H 2 D engine sits completely idle . title: [ROCm] MXFP8 block32 GEMM: add TP1 tuned configs for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DP8+EP8

title: [CI][XPU] Raise memory utilization for Granite4Vision mixed-tile test
summary: ## Purpose `models/multimodal/generation/test_granite4_vision.py::test_mixed_tile_counts_across_requests` fails on the 16 GiB Intel BMG CI card (intel-ci build 16725): ``` Model loading took 7.78 GiB Available KV cache memory: -5.86 GiB ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks. ``` The test hard-codes `gpu_memory_utilization=0.4`. Weights (7.78 GiB) plus encoder profiling (~2.2 GiB peak) and ~0.5 GiB of startup non-torch memory need ~11 GiB, which is more than 0.4 of 15.13 GiB. The engine is in-process, so its failed init leaks memory and the six following tests fail with `Memory of devices ... not free`. Use 0.85 on XPU only; other platforms keep 0.4. Not a duplicate: searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for Granite4Vision/XPU memory fixes; none found. ## Test Plan / Result ``` VLLM_TEST_DEVICE=xpu pytest -q models/multimodal/generation/test_granite4_vision.py ``` I only had a 22.7 GiB Arc Pro B60, so I emulated the CI card's budget (0.85 × 15.13 GiB ≈ 12.9 GiB) with 0.566 on this device: `1 passed`, available KV cache 2.0 GiB / 2.6 GiB for the two engines. With the 0.4-equivalent budget the same test hit the failure above. ## AI assistance Written with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI); I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix] Fix startup illegal memory access from unaligned extensible KV cache segments
summary: ## Overview Fix a startup illegal memory access in FlashMLA sparse prefill with the extensible KV cache (#56492), reproduced with DeepSeek-V3.2 on B300. FlashInfer autotuning runs FlashMLA before warmup expands the cache. When a sparse gather includes an invalid (padding) index, FlashMLA reads past the selected rows. With only the null block committed, those reads can reach unmapped memory inside the layer's reserved KV view. Settings: `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=64`, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`. title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Emit BlockRemoved only after the last physical copy is evicted
summary: ## Purpose A prefix-cache block hash can map to multiple physical KV cache blocks. For example, when an identical block-aligned prompt is served repeatedly, vLLM may reuse earlier prefix blocks but recompute the final prompt block to obtain next-token logits. The recomputed blocks have the same hash while retaining different physical block IDs. Previously, evicting any one of these physical copies emitted a `BlockRemoved` event. An external KV event consumer could therefore invalidate the hash even though another physical copy was still resident and available for prefix-cache lookup. For example, consider two cached requests: ```text Request A: H1 -> H2 -> H3 Request B: H1 -> H2 -> H3 -> H4 -> H5 -> H6 -> H7 ``` Suppose `H3` is backed by two physical blocks, `P3-A` and `P3-B`. Evicting `P3-A` previously emitted `BlockRemoved(H3)` even though `P3-B` remained resident. The external cache view could then appear as: ```text H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, H7 ``` Because block hashes form a prefix chain, a new request matching `H1 -> ... -> H7` would be scored as a two-block cache hit rather than the seven-block hit actually available in the engine. A prefix-aware router could consequently choose the wrong engine, or trigger unnecessary recomputation or remote loading of `H3` through `H7`. This PR makes `BlockRemoved` a logical cache-key disappearance event: - Remove the requested physical block from `BlockHashToBlockMap` and determine how many copies remain under the same `BlockHashWithGroupId` key. - Suppress `BlockRemoved` while at least one same-hash physical copy remains. - Emit the ex

title: [Bugfix] Compute NIXL EP per-tensor FP8 scale over valid rows only
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #64456. Thank you to @fangyuchu for the detailed report and for pinpointing the root cause so precisely. With `--all2all-backend nixl_ep` and `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, the dynamic per-tensor FP8 scale was computed over the entire fixed-capacity NIXL receive buffer, including stale rows past each expert's `expert_num_tokens`. Those leftover values inflated the scale and corrupted the quantized valid rows (the reporter measured 0/32 on the first 32 GSM8K questions with DP=2 + NIXL EP + FP8, vs 19/32 single-GPU FP8). This PR threads `expert_num_tokens` from `NixlEPPrepareAndFinalize._receiver` into `_do_quant`, which now computes the dynamic per-tensor scale over valid rows only (a masked absmax, matching the kernel's `absmax / quant_max` formula). The quantized output keeps its full buffer shape; only the scale changes. Deliberately untouched, since their scales never mix rows or are fixed: - per-token quantization and block quantization; - static per-tensor scales (`a1_scale is not None`); - the fp8-dispatch paths (the block-128 early return, and dequant-then-requant, which now also benefits from the valid-rows scale); - NVFP4/MXFP formats (not dynamic per-tensor FP8/INT8). The masked scale computation adds no host sync and keeps all shapes static (one extra elementwise pass over the receive buffer, only for dynamic per-tensor quantization). **Why this is not a duplicate:** no open PR references #64456, and the issue timeline shows no competing fix. summary: ## Overview Fixes #57017. With `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` (the default), CUDA-graph padding tokens are routed to expert −1, so `TritonExperts`' first GEMM never writes their workspace rows. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On Hopper with DeepGEMM installed, `is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` is true by default for every layer. It also covers interactions those PRs predate: the sorted-A TMA path from #64760, the batched Triton experts, and the compile fusion. **Depends on #65791:** the first commit here is #65791, which fixes the fused kernel's prefill performance. title: [MoE][DeepEPV2] Add PaddedStandard activation format
summary: ## Motivation `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize` hands the experts an activation tensor whose **row count is an upper bound rather than the exact token count**, so some rows are inactive padding. The shape is still 2D `(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` — the padding is in the token dimension; nothing is padded along `E`. It arises because the number of tokens a rank receives after dispatch is data-dependent and not knowable on the host without a device sync, from two sources: - **decode / cudagraph mode** — the recv buffer is sized to the worst case (`R * num_max_tokens_per_rank`); only the `[0, num_recv_tokens)` prefix is written and the tail is left **uninitialized**. - **prefill mode** — tokens are grouped per-expert and each expert's block is padded up to `expert_alignment`; those gaps are zeroed. Inactive rows are signalled by setting all of their `topk_ids` slots to `-1`, and `ExpertTokensMetadata.psum_recv_per_rank` carries the real/padding boundary on device (reading it host-side would break CUDA-graph capture). Previously this was hidden behind the generic `Standard` activation format, so experts had no way to know their input might contain such rows. Kernels that *can* skip padding couldn't opt in, and kernels that *can't* handle it had no way to reject the layout. That is a correctness issue, not just a missed optimization: the decode-mode tail is uninitialized, so an expert that builds routing by scanning every row can read garbage that aliases a valid expert id and corrupt real tokens. title: [Performance]: extract_hidden_states loses ~38% throughput to a decode draft that is almost never accepted
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance `extract_hidden_states` schedules one draft token per request on every decode step, and it is almost never accepted (about 0.03%). On an L4 this costs 37% to 39% of saturation throughput. Setting `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size=[[1, 1, 0]]` removes the drafts and recovers nearly all of it, and extracted states match an offline reference about as well as the default's do. Details and measurements are below. Stop drafting on decode steps for the `extract_hidden_states` method, either by default or using a flag, and make the sync-scheduling path respect K=0 (currently it falls back silently). Questions 1. Should zero decode drafts be the default for `extract_hidden_states`? Do the drafts serve any purpose for this method? 2. If not the default, would a dedicated flag (e.g. `extract_hidden_states_decode_drafts=False`) be preferred over a dynamic SD schedule? Either way, the sync-scheduling path should respect K=0, or at least warn when it can't. 3. Related: #56417 (V1 bug that only accepted drafts can trigger) and #48743 (inline return built on this path, which would inherit this cost). ### Report of performance regression I haven't measured a regression from before v0.30.0, this situation is measured solely on v0.30.0 ### Misc discussion on performance #### Cost One L4 run (20261102T130854Z), 4 rounds, each arm against plain serving: | Config | Saturation throughput loss | p99 TPOT change | Bench drafts, per round (rounds 1 to 3) | Accepted | Drafts per score stage | Accepted | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Default extract_hidden_st

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graph: cap each graph's frame slots at its token budget

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Don't sync when building sparse-attention prefill metadata
summary: ## Overview `MiniMaxM3SparseMetadataBuilder.build` zeroes the first prefill `cu_seqlens_k` entry with `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[0] = 0` on CUDA. Assigning a Python scalar to an element of a CUDA tensor is a pageable host-to-device copy, so the host waits for all queued GPU work. The metadata is built while the previous step is still running on the GPU, so every step that contains a prefill stalls the host until the GPU drains. This PR zeroes the element with `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[:1].zero_()`, which ROCm already uses. ## Claims - **No host sync when building MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention metadata.** Before this PR it is the only synchronizing call in a MiniMax-M3.1 Flash step (torch sync-debug mode, GB300, TP4). It is also why M3.1 cannot run under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on `main`: every request fails at this line. - **The stall is gone.** Host time of the metadata build with GPU work still queued (GB300): | queued GPU work | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | 5 ms | 5.41 ms | 1.34 ms | | 20 ms | 20.48 ms | 1.31 ms | | 60 ms | 60.43 ms | 1.16 ms | With no queued work both take about 1.3 ms, so the difference is the wait. - **In serving** (MiniMax-M3.1 Flash, GB300, TP4, DSpark K=7, AgentX agentic workload, 1 h per run, 2 runs per arm): host time of the attention-metadata build on steps with a prefill, p90, goes from 3.9–4.2 to about 1.5 ms at concurrency 16 and from 4.5–4.8 to 1.6–1.7 ms at concurrency 32. title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Fix PP rank derivation when prefill context parallelism is enabled
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fix PP rank calculation when pipeline parallelism (PP) and prefill context parallelism (PCP) are enabled together. The current calculation ignores the PCP dimension, causing incorrect MooncakeStoreConnector keys, model layer metadata, and Ray actor names. Workers follow a PP × PCP × TP layout, so each PP stage contains `tp_size * pcp_size` workers. This PR replaces `rank // tp_size % pp_size` with `rank // (tp_size * pcp_size) % pp_size` in all three affected locations. This PR also includes a small PP fix that I don't think warrants a separate PR: rejecting negative layer counts in VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION, such as "-1,5", instead of allowing invalid layer ranges. ## Claims - MooncakeStoreConnector uses the correct PP stage in store keys, restoring external prefix cache hits in the tested PP2 × PCP2 configuration. - `ModelConfig.get_layers_start_end_indices` returns the correct stage's layer range, including the layer count used by KV connectors and EAGLE drafters for uneven partitions. - Ray actor names report the correct PP and PCP indices. - Negative custom layer counts fail validation at startup. PP rank calculation is unchanged when PCP = 1. ## Validation ### End-to-end - Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (MLA, 27 layers, split 14/13). - Hardware and parallelism: 4 × B300, PP2 × PCP2 × TP1. - Connector: `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `kv_both`, standalone store, asynchronous loading. - Workload: GSM8K 5-shot, run twice against the same server so the second pass can reuse stored prompt KV. title: [Guard] Assert no prefill in FULL decode-cudagraph replay (#53051)
summary: ## What Defense-in-depth guard for #53051 (the "second latent half" from @allenzz-dev's addendum): assert that a FULL decode-cudagraph replay never contains a prefill. A FULL graph is only dispatched for uniform-decode batches (`CudagraphDispatcher` builds FULL keys exclusively with `uniform=True` descriptors). For backends with persistent capture-time buffers (e.g. GDN), `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` refreshes those buffers only in the `num_prefills == 0` branch, so a prefill reaching a FULL replay would reuse stale capture-time state indices and the null-block guards would silently drop the prefill state writes, producing garbage output. This guard turns that into an immediate, debuggable assertion on the real replay path (`execute_model`, where the dispatch has already chosen FULL). The check is a no-op on the correct path: FULL ⇒ uniform decode ⇒ every request is past its prompt. It complements the dispatch-side fix in `_is_uniform_decode` (#53059) and holds regardless of whether that lands. ## Why this is not a duplicate - #53059 fixes the **dispatch side** (shape-aliased prefills no longer classified as uniform decode). This adds the **replay-side** assertion it does not include — the one explicitly requested in the issue's addendum ("add a builder- or replay-side guard"). - #51508 fixes a different mechanism (stale `num_accepted_tokens=0` → index -1 under async scheduling), not the prefill-into-FULL path. - #54361 covers the breakable-cudagraph path, not standard FULL_AND_PIECEWISE dispatch. ## Tests - `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` on the changed files

title: [Attention] Derive Triton split-KV decode threshold from the KV cache group's head count
summary: ## Purpose `TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` derives the split-KV ("3D") decode threshold from the model-wide KV-head count: ```python self.num_heads_kv = model_config.get_num_kv_heads(vllm_config.parallel_config) self.seq_threshold_3D = MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D // self.num_heads_kv ``` but the 2D launch grid the bound reasons about, `(num_q_blocks, num_heads_kv)`, is built from the KV cache group's own per-rank head count (`num_kv_heads = k.shape[2]` in `triton_unified_attention.py`). On hybrid models whose full-attention layers have fewer KV heads than the model-wide count (e.g. Gemma4 with `attention_k_eq_v`), the full-attention group's threshold is underestimated: Gemma-4-31B at TP4 has 1 global KV head per rank against a model-wide 4, so the threshold lands on 32 instead of 128, and a 36-request 220K-token decode batch walks each global layer as 36 serial scans — decode turns latency-bound and ITL roughly doubles. Fix: read `kv_cache_spec.num_kv_heads`, the count the launch grid actually uses (the group's KV cache is allocated from that same spec). `FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` already does exactly this. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] DSv4 router: compute sqrt(softplus) with log1p
summary: ## Overview The DeepSeek-V4 `sqrtsoftplus` routers compute softplus(x) as log(1 + exp(x)) in fp32. For x below about -16.64, 1 + exp(x) rounds to 1, so the expert's score is exactly 0. Up to about x = -10 the score is off by more than 1e-3 relative (77% at x = -16.6 in the CUDA kernels). This PR computes log1p(exp(x)) instead, in the Triton `dsv4_topk` kernel and in the CUDA `topk_softplus_sqrt` kernels. It makes the same change in the GB300 CuTe DSL MoE front, which must match `dsv4_topk` bit for bit. Related: #49927. ## Claims - Max relative error of sqrt(softplus(x)) for x in [-30, -5], main vs this PR: - Triton `dsv4_topk`: 1.0 -> 9.15e-7 - CUDA hash kernel: 1.0 -> 2.18e-7 - CUDA generic kernel: 1.0 -> 1.43e-7 - On main, a token whose selected experts all have logits <= -16.64 gets all-zero routing weights (sum 0.0 instead of `routed_scaling_factor`), so it gets no routed expert output. With this PR its weights match the `F.softplus(x).sqrt()` reference. - The GB300 specialized-decode front still matches `dsv4_topk` bit for bit. title: [ROCm][Kernel] Wave64 topk_softplus_sqrt fast path for DeepSeek-V4 routing
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 routing calls `topk_softplus_sqrt` once per MoE layer per step (40 times per decode step on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). On ROCm it runs the generic `topkGatingSoftplusSqrt<6,384,4,8,64,...>` kernel, which keeps its row in a dynamically indexed private array (32 B/lane of scratch) and reduces each argmax round through LDS shuffles. The CUDA build already has a specialized DSv4 kernel (`launchDsv4HashTopk`, hash layers only); ROCm has none. This adds a ROCm-only fast path inside `topkGatingSoftplusSqrtKernelLauncher` for fp32 gating output, `topk == 6`, 256/384/512 experts, wave64: - one wave64 per row, 2 or more scores per lane via `float2` loads; - the k loop is unrolled and nothing is dynamically indexed (0 scratch, 35 VGPRs); - the argmax is a DPP reduction (quad_perm, row_half_mirror, row_mirror, row_bcast:15/31) into lane 63 plus `readlane`, so the winner is wave-uniform; - hash rows, `bias_vl` image rows, `is_padding` rows, `renormalize` and the routed scaling factor follow the generic kernel, and so do the output bits: the weight is `(score + bias) - bias`, decoded from the argmax key, and the renormalize sum runs in the generic fp32 launch's order (k order on thread 0 for score rows; per owner thread, then a 64-lane XOR butterfly, for hash rows). It launches only on gfx950 (a runtime `gcnArchName` check), where it was measured; other wave64 GPUs keep the generic kernel. title: [Feature] Chi-squared and perplexity watermarking
summary: ## Overview Adds the chi-squared watermark and the two perplexity watermarks, `ppl_hard` and `ppl_soft`, from [Gloaguen et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06754). The implementation is built on top of the watermarking infrastructure introduced in #53916 / #54053. ## Claims - `--watermark-config '{"algorithm": "chi_squared", "key": 42}'` samples from `q = p * w`, where `p` is the unwatermarked distribution, and `q` maximizes the expected watermark score minus a chi-squared distance from `p` (Theorem D.6 of the [Gloaguen et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06754)). Each token score is Binomial(30, 1/2), computed using the Philox PRF from the key and the last `context_width` tokens (default 4). The variable `delta` (default 1.0) sets the strength of the watermark. - `"algorithm": "ppl_hard"` and `"ppl_soft"` use the same scores, but bound the expected surprisal `-log p` of the watermarked token above the model's entropy. The variable `epsilon` (default 0) is that budget in nats, met for every key (`ppl_hard`) or on average over keys (`ppl_soft`). - `BinomialScoreWatermarkDetector` returns a one-sided binomial p-value for all three. - All three reject speculative decoding, also with `allow_target_only_watermarking: true`. ## Validation Tests: `tests/watermarking/test_chi_squared.py`, `test_perplexity.py` and `test_binomial.py` (new), the new golden candidates (`tests/watermarking/golden_candidates.py`, `watermarking_goldens.json`), `tests/watermarking/test_watermarking_e2e.py`, `test_watermarking.py`, `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sam

title: [ROCm][Build][4/5] Speed up ROCm build: instantiate the int4 skinny GEMM per output width
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Disclosure AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually. ## Overview **Splits the int4 skinny GEMM translation unit on one item - `N_in` (output width, 1-5), from the dispatch tower #40977 landed and #57199 widened.** `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` holds the whole int4 skinny GEMM (`wvSplitK_int4_g`): a single host entry whose macro tower expands per output width `N_in` (1-5) x 2 activation dtypes x 3 group sizes, so all of the op's device code is emitted by one translation unit. On a 9-arch build that unit is the longest compile of the entire build - 1232 s of a 1234 s ninja span, i.e. the build waits on one core while the other 63 job slots sit idle. This PR instantiates one unit per `N_in` instead: the kernels live in an include-only `skinny_gemms_int4.cuh` whose entry is a `template <int N>`, each unit is two lines (`#include` + `VLLM_SKINNY_INT4_INSTANTIATE(N)`), and a small `skinny_gemms_int4_api.cu` keeps the public symbol and dispatches on `in_b.size(0)`, with `extern template` keeping the device code in the five units. Same kernels, same dispatch rules, same numerics: the only change is which translation unit generates which `N_in`, plus the runtime forward in the API unit. At 1 arch the file is not the build's tail, so the single-arch wall is unchanged. The single-arch rows are `pip install -e .` on MI350 (gfx950); the 9-arch row is the `setup.py bdist_wheel` described under *Validation*. title: [Bug]: Requests queued during level-2 sleep run before `reload_weights` and return wrong output with HTTP 200
summary: ### Your current environment - vLLM 0.33.0 (pip wheel) and main (9a519c058, 97c198cd4), torch 2.14.0+cu130 - NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), driver 610.43.02 - `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --enable-sleep-mode --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2g --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` ### 🐛 Describe the bug With level-2 sleep, a request that arrives while the engine is asleep waits. But `POST /wake_up` without tags resumes scheduling immediately, so the queued request is executed before `POST /collective_rpc {"method": "reload_weights"}` has restored the discarded weights. The request completes with HTTP 200 and output computed from the discarded weights, unrelated to the prompt. Requests sent after the reload are correct. Related to #29341, which was closed because the weights were not reloaded. Here they are reloaded; the queued request runs in the window between `wake_up` and `reload_weights`. This affects deployments that sleep idle engines while they can still receive requests. Waking in steps avoids it: `wake_up?tags=weights` (returns `"status": "sleeping"`, the queued request keeps waiting) → `reload_weights` → `wake_up?tags=kv_cache`. The queued request then returns the correct output. ### Reproduction ```bash export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --port 8000 --enable-sleep-mode --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2g --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15 & # wait for /health req='{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B","prompt":"Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0}' curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: ap

title: [Perf][DSA] Shard the decode indexer rows across TP ranks
summary: ## Purpose On CUDA, every tensor-parallel rank runs the sparse-attention (DSA) indexer on every decode row: paged MQA logits, DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate selection or mask, and top-k. Every rank ends up with the same indices. At long context this is a large part of the decode step. This PR adds an opt-in, `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1`, that splits the decode rows across TP ranks: - **Row assignment:** rank `r` scores the rows of requests `r, r + tp, r + 2·tp, …`. All of a request's rows stay on one rank, because the varlen `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` reads a request's KV once for all of its rows. - **Metadata builder:** gathers each rank's rows, block-table rows and context lengths into persistent buffers and builds that rank's DeepGEMM schedule. The plan depends only on the padded row count, so CUDA graphs replay with the same buffers. - **Indexer op:** scores the local rows, keeps DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate blocks rank-local, all-gathers the int32 top-k indices across TP ranks, and restores request order in `topk_indices_buffer`. - **When it applies:** uniform decode batches with at least `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD_MIN_REQS` requests (default 8), on the varlen paged-logits path, without DCP/PCP or the sparse-logits indexer. ## Test Plan **Serve.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200. The only difference between main and this PR is `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD`: `0` behaves exactly like main, `1` is this PR. ```bash VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1 \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \ VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXP

summary: ## Overview Adds a tuned fused-MoE Triton config for `E=256,N=512,dtype=int4_w4a16` on the AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4). Without it, int4 W4A16 MoE models of this shape (for example Qwen3.5/3.6-35B-A3B GPTQ Int4 at TP=1) log `Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal!`. Config file only; no code change.
