title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Keep whole-chunk max_load_tokens caps with sliding window groups
summary: ## Overview With sliding window groups, the OffloadingConnector applied its prompt-end `-1` after the `max_load_tokens` / `max_num_new_tokens` caps, so a whole-chunk cap lost a chunk (a one-chunk cap loaded nothing). Follow-up to #55885. ## Claims - With sliding window groups (and no partial-tail support, e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 2/3), `max_load_tokens = k * tokens_per_chunk` now loads `k` chunks instead of `k - 1`. - The same lost chunk is fixed for `max_num_new_tokens` (the bound from groups the connector does not offload). - No change when there is no cap: the hit still stops before the last prompt token. ## Validation New test `test_max_load_tokens_preserves_aligned_sliding_window_chunk` (16-token chunks, 65-token prompt, mixed full/sliding-window groups): | Cap | Before | After | |---|---|---| | 16 tokens | 0 | 16 | | 32 tokens | 16 | 32 | | none | 64 | 64 | ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \ -k "max_load_tokens or sliding" # 132 passed pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector ``` ## Details `_lookup_complete_chunks` computed `min(num_tokens, computed + cap) - 1`. The `-1` exists so a sliding-window hit stops before the last prompt token, which must be recomputed. When a cap ends earlier, it is already a supported boundary, but the `-1` moved it one token below, and the per-group `round_down` then dropped a whole chunk. The fix applies the `-1` to the prompt-end ceiling only: `min(num_tokens - 1, computed + cap)`. This matches the partial-tail path, which already uses `num_prompt_tokens - 1` with uncapped limits.

title: [KV Offload] Publish block extra keys in self-describing offload events
summary: ## Purpose With `self_describing_kv_events`, offload `BlockStored` events carry each block's parent, tokens and LoRA, but `extra_keys` is always `None` (`_OffloadEventMetadata` marked it deferred). The GPU block pool publishes each block's LoRA, multimodal, cache-salt and prompt-embeds keys. A consumer that keys blocks by tokens and extra keys therefore gives an offloaded LoRA, multimodal or salted block a different key from its GPU copy, so prefix-cache routing misses the CPU copy. This builds each block's extra keys with `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` while the request is available. It seeks the first multimodal input overlapping the chunk with `get_mm_features_in_window`, as `request_block_hasher` does, and carries the index across the chunk's blocks as the block pool does. Full chunks use the group's block size and partial recurrent tails the hash block size, matching the `block_size` each event already reports. Events for blocks without extra keys now publish `[None]` per block, as GPU events do. Raised in review of #57789 (KV event snapshots), where a snapshot recorder has to reconcile GPU and offload stores of the same hash. #43468 introduced self-describing offload events and deferred extra keys; #52068 and #57453 keep that metadata alive until removal. #52103 (draft) rewrites the tracker to build stored payloads from the request carried by each store event and to emit key-only removals, and since its Oct 13 revision also generates per-block extra keys with the same helper. summary: ## Summary Fixes #65385. `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel`'s Triton autotune configs with `BK < 128 and num_warps >= 4` miscompile on Hopper (loop-carried WGMMA accumulator), producing wrong, run-to-run non-deterministic GDN prefill output. title: [Bug]: NixlConnector silently corrupts NVFP4 KV cache when the prefill block size is smaller than decode's
summary: ## Environment - vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175`). - One node, 2x H100. summary: ### Motivation. vLLM transfers KV between engines over NIXL (prefill to decode) and the P2P offload tier (engine to engine). Each checks compatibility once per peer connection. P2P compares the block length, the hash seed and a fingerprint of the offload run config: model path, KV dtype, parallel sizes, KV groups ([session.py#L647-L654](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/39dbf51839/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/session.py#L647-L654), [file_mapper.py#L64-L73](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/39dbf51839/vllm/v1/kv_offload/file_mapper.py#L64-L73)); the page layout joins only with `canonical_layout`, off by default. Quantization and `hf_overrides` are not checked, and on P2P neither are the model dtype and page layout. The code identity is the whole `vllm_version`, which changes with every commit (2,036 in the 30 days to 2026-11-03), or on P2P nothing. A passing check uses the received pages silently. title: [Bugfix] Gate the FA4 masked-MHA sparse prefill on prefill-query quantization, not KV cache dtype
summary: ## Description `_is_masked_mha_available` rejects the FA4 masked-MHA sparse prefill whenever the KV cache is quantized: `fa_version == 4 and not is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)`. That conflates the KV cache dtype with the prefill query dtype. The masked path never reads FP8 KV as FP8: context rows go through the same `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` the dense path already uses, and the suffix K/V are the current step's bf16 projections. An FP8 prefill query is what the kernel cannot consume, and for NoPE-dims models like GLM-5.3-Flash it is unreachable anyway: no prefill backend supports the `(256, 0, 256)` dims for prefill query quantization, so the query is always bf16. summary: ### Motivation In MRV2, `CudaGraphManager._init_candidates()` interleaves decode-only and prefill/mixed descriptor generation with candidate indexing. title: [Security] Use weights_only=True for EPLB all_gather_object collectives
summary: ## Purpose Harden the EPLB object collectives against untrusted deserialization. `NixlEplbCommunicator` and `SymmMemEplbCommunicator` exchange agent and expert-weight metadata through `torch.distributed.all_gather_object` (`vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py`), which deserializes peer-contributed data with pickle and no `weights_only` guard. On elastic-EP / fault-tolerant deployments these collectives run over rebuilt groups whose membership and coordination store are unauthenticated, so they are the remaining ungated pickle sinks in the distributed layer — every other deserialization path in vLLM is already guarded (`weights_only=True` for prompt_embeds/adapters; `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION` for the RLHF ipc-handles and serial_utils paths). Discussed privately in GHSA-v8vv-h2j8-g9mx; agreed there to land this as hardening. ## Change Add `weights_only=True` to the three EPLB `all_gather_object` call sites (`_init_remote_agents`, `_exchange_remote_send_meta`, and the SymmMem NVLink check). The gathered payloads are plain data — nixl agent-metadata bytes and `dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]` of ints — so the restricted loader accepts them unchanged. ## Why this is safe / no functional change - `weights_only=True` restricts only the load side; senders still pickle normally. The payloads contain no custom classes or `__reduce__` objects, so the restricted unpickler loads them identically. - `torch==2.14.0` (already required by this path) supports `weights_only` on the object collectives; default is `False`. ## Scope note This intentionally does **not*

title: [Attention] Portable Triton sparse-MLA fallback for SM12x (consumer Blackwell)
summary: ## Purpose DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels (`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x). This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton** implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has that content). title: [Bugfix] Restore engine memory budget after IPC fallback
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview When `ipc_cache` falls back to disk (e.g. the daemon is reachable but its weights do not match the engine config), the worker keeps charging the daemon's weights against its memory budget even though it no longer maps them, so the KV cache is smaller than with a direct disk load by the daemon's weight size. This removes the charge of each model that falls back, so a fallback is sized exactly like a direct disk load. Follow-up to #62583. ## Claims - After an IPC disk fallback, the engine budget and KV cache size match a direct disk load (Qwen3-4B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`: KV cache 10.82 → 18.34 GiB, equal to the direct load). - Only the charge of the model (target or draft) that fell back is removed; models still mapped from the daemon keep theirs. ## Validation Setup: NVIDIA B300, TP1, eager, `max_model_len=1024`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `max_num_seqs=1`, FlashInfer autotune off. The daemon (`vllm preload --dtype bfloat16`) and the engine (`dtype="float16"`, `load_format="ipc_cache"`, `fallback=True`) differ in dtype, so the engine logs `Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dtype']); falling back to disk loading`. Direct-load baselines use `load_format="auto"` with the same daemon running. Outputs are greedy, 8 tokens, for "The capital of France is". The `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1` runs shared the GPU with an unrelated workload. **Regression test** (`test_ipc_fallback_restores_memory_budget`, Qwen3-0.6B, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.1`): | Model runner | upstream main (`c126ebf159`) | This PR | |---|

title: fix(mamba): stop a mid-block resume at the block boundary
summary: ## Summary - Fixes #65264. - In align mode, a prefill that resumes inside a Mamba block and has a valid internal checkpoint dropped the stop at the next block boundary. The chunk ran past that boundary, and `cache_blocks` still keyed the copy-on-write block there even though no chunk ended at that token. - A mid-block start now stops at the next block boundary whether or not the internal checkpoint is valid. title: [Core][MLA] Cross-layer KV cache sharing for attention layers
summary: ## Overview Model-agnostic enablement for MLA models in two areas: cross-layer KV sharing and PCP+DCP decode handling. No behavior change for existing models; each piece is opt-in or additive. Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for KV-sharing / MLA enablement / PCP+DCP work — the open items cover KV-sharing prefill perf for a specific model family (#60445), DSv4.1 pipeline partitions (#63106), and compressed-MLA offloading (#63586); none generalize cross-layer KV sharing over `AttentionLayerBase` or move the PCP+DCP LSE merge into the base MLA forward. ## Claims - **Cross-layer KV sharing:** `kv_sharing_target_layer_name` is declared on `AttentionLayerBase` and plumbed through `MLAAttention`. A layer that shares another layer's KV cache skips its own cache write, and the V2 runner resolves consumers to the sharing target's KV cache spec (`get_shared_kv_cache_layers` now walks `AttentionLayerBase`). - **Sparse MLA only, with forced MQA:** KV sharing is supported by sparse MLA backends, and a sharing layer requires `sparse_mla_force_mqa`. The sparse MHA prefill paths attend over the layer's own new latent KV rather than the cache, and a sharing layer has no latent of its own, so the model must opt into the MQA path; otherwise initialization raises a `ValueError`. Dense MLA still rejects sharing, since its prefill always uses the layer's own latent. - **PCP+DCP:** the decode-only LSE merge moved into the base `MLAAttention` forward (as DeepSeek-V3.2 does in its own forward), so MLA models opt in with `supports_pcp_dcp` instead of overriding `forward`. ## Validation Unit tests

title: [Core] Change default --block-size from 16 to 64
summary: ## Overview Changes the default `--block-size` for `vllm serve` / `EngineArgs` from 16 to 64, via `CacheConfig.DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE`. Also teaches `RocmAttentionBackend` to prefer 16-token blocks for default-sized runs, keeping ROCm on its native paged-attention kernel. ## Claims - `CacheConfig()` (and therefore `vllm serve` without `--block-size`) now resolves to `block_size=64`; an explicit `--block-size` still sets `user_specified_block_size=True` and takes precedence. - Platforms/attention backends that declare a preferred or restricted block size continue to override the default exactly as before: `update_block_size_for_backend` only consults `DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE` when the user did not specify `--block-size`. - ROCm runs without an explicit `--block-size` keep the native C++ paged-attention kernel (block sizes 16/32) instead of silently falling back to the slower Triton path that any other multiple of 16 routes to. ## Validation - Full Buildkite CI build [#97300](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97300) passed (171 jobs), including the suites that caught regressions in the first run (#96922): H200/MI355 KV connector offload, MI250 PyTorch fullgraph cudagraph compatibility, and model executor. - First CI run (#96922, default alone) failed exactly where 16-token assumptions were baked in: offloading-connector chunk sizes (48/16 vs the 64 GPU block), shared-storage connector hash-count expectations, an autotune cache-key test using 64 as a "non-default" control, and a 25-minute MI250 hang in RocmAttn with 64-token blocks (engine never returned from a step). title: [KV Cache] Size packed groups by pooled bytes per request, not layer padding

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 1M context this takes the KV pool from 1.88x to 3.16x concurrency with the pool size unchanged; a second commit batches the sliding-window metadata build so the higher group count does not add host time per step. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has no `MambaSpec` at all (its caches are `CircularBufferSpec` and `MLASpec`), so the two builds are identical and the `bytes_per_request` comparison is never reached — a no-op for this model by construction. - **#58207** rewrites t

title: [Bugfix] Widen the QSA raw-key ring instead of asserting divisibility
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #54552. `QSAKeyStateCache.get_kv_cache_spec` asserts that the raw-key ring capacity divides the attention block size. The safety property in the comment above the assert is one-sided: the ring must be **at least** `span` rows; wider is slack. With `compress_ratio = 4`, `num_speculative_tokens` 5..8 (and 13..16) need a 12-row (20-row) ring, and neither the power-of-two block sizes nor the hybrid LCM sizes 848/1616 have the factor, so those depths fail at engine init: ``` QSA ring capacity 12 must divide the attention block size 848 ``` The change factors the arithmetic into `qsa_ring_capacity()`, which returns the smallest whole-group ring `>= span` that divides the block size, logs once when it widens, and raises a `ValueError` with the numbers when no such size exists. Every previously legal depth keeps its ring size, so the change is a no-op for existing configurations. ## Test Plan - New unit tests in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py`: for block sizes 848 and 1616 and `num_speculative_tokens` 0..16 the ring is `>= span`, a multiple of `compress_ratio`, divides the block size, and equals the old value wherever the old value was legal; plus the concrete cases `(4, 5, 848) -> 16`, `(4, 8, 1616) -> 16`, `(4, 5, 16) -> 16`, and `(4, 13, 16)` raises. - End-to-end on a GB10 (DGX Spark), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=5`, attention block size 1616: previously a hard init failure; with this change the engine starts, logs `QSA ring widened from 12 to 16 rows ...`, serves, and passes a needle-in-a-haystack retrieval check 5/5 at ~20k co

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Use a 32-wide KV tile for FP8 queries in grouped DiffKV launches
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview In v0.33.0, MiMo-V2 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` crashes on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): with MTP the engine fails to start (default CUDA graph settings), and without speculative decoding it dies on the first short prompt. title: [Perf][Multimodal] Add `mm_tensor_ipc="cuda_ipc_pool"`: TP-aware GPU transport
summary: ## Summary This PR continues [#49462](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49462), co-authored by me, @SangChengC (who opened it), and @wendadawen, rebased onto current main. Adds `cuda_ipc_pool`, a persistent CUDA IPC pool that sends GPU-preprocessed multimodal features to TP workers over D2D / P2P without a host round trip. Unlike `torch_shm`, it supports TP > 1. For an EPD encoder with TP > 1, `direct_rpc` was previously the only transport. `auto` therefore kept preprocessing on CPU; explicitly selecting GPU still copied the output back to host. `cuda_ipc_pool` lets `auto` use GPU preprocessing and keeps the data on device. On Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct with E TP4, 10 random 1920x1080 images per request, and concurrency 16, GPU preprocessing + `cuda_ipc_pool` achieves a 2.33x speedup in p50 E-stage latency over CPU + `direct_rpc`; holding preprocessing on GPU, the transport-path comparison is 2.01x. ## Changes from #49462 - Rename `cuda_ipc` to `cuda_ipc_pool` to distinguish the persistent pool from `torch_shm`, which also uses CUDA IPC handles. - Add a separate `--mm-cuda-ipc-pool-gb` budget; `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb` remains the frontend decode admission budget. - Reject PP > 1, DP > 1, TP > 16, `nnodes > 1`, and `--api-server-count > 1` during config validation. - Fix slice leaks on encoder-cache, prefix-cache, and EC hits, duplicate items, and queued aborts; disable the processor cache because cached items could outlive their slices. - Let EPD encoder-only instances select GPU preprocessing in `auto` mode. ## How it works - **Frontend:** allocate one persistent pool

title: [ROCm] Fixing GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4 on gfx942 and gfx950
summary: * An in-tree Triton paged MQA kernel. It is required unconditionally for DeepSeek V4 (Flash and Pro): V4 shares KV-cache blocks between the indexer and the main MLA cache, so its indexer cache is a non-contiguous strided slice of a larger per-block record written in plain pos-major layout, whereas aiter assumes a contiguous 16×16-preshuffled cache. It is also required when speculative decoding is enabled, because the current AITER implementation of paged_mqa_logits does not work correctly in these cases (the exact cause is yet to be determined). * Periodically synchronizing the device during FP8-BMM precompilation. title: [Core] Fix EngineDeadError on late KV transfer completion
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #49089. This PR addresses a critical fault-tolerance issue in the `Scheduler` where a delayed or crashing external KV server (e.g., LMCacheMPConnector) could kill the entire vLLM engine. Previously, `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` used strict `assert req_id in self.requests` statements. If a request failed and was removed before the KV transfer finished, this triggered an `AssertionError` leading to an `EngineDeadError`. This PR replaces those assertions with guarded `.get()` lookups and logs warnings, allowing the engine to gracefully ignore orphaned transfer completions. ## Test Plan 1. Created a unit test `tests/v1/core/test_kv_xfer_failure.py` simulating late KV transfer completions for already-deleted requests. 2. Verified the scheduler logs the appropriate warnings and bypasses the error. Test command: `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_xfer_failure.py -v` ## Test Result **Before Fix:** `AssertionError` leading to engine crash. **After Fix:**

title: [Perf][Core] Add mamba_aware_lru GPU prefix-cache eviction policy for hybrid models
summary: ## Overview Adds `--prefix-cache-eviction-policy mamba_aware_lru`, an opt-in eviction order for the GPU prefix cache of hybrid models in Mamba `align` mode. Under `lru`, the hit that resumes a conversation from a Mamba state also refreshes that state's LRU position, so states that the conversation's later turns no longer need outlive the cached context of idle conversations. `mamba_aware_lru` evicts those states first. On a 1-hour AgentX replay (agentic coding traces) with Nemotron 3.5 Super, it served 5.4% more requests per hour than `lru` and recomputed 15% fewer prompt tokens. This is the GPU counterpart of #63578, which applies the same rule to the CPU offload tier. Use this one without KV offloading, or with a CPU tier smaller than the GPU cache: a tier at least as large already holds a copy of almost every block the GPU evicts. Related work: #61282, #40270, #55403, #50551 and RFC #57111 (see "Why this is not a duplicate"). ## Claims - New option `--prefix-cache-eviction-policy {lru,mamba_aware_lru}` (`CacheConfig.prefix_cache_eviction_policy`). The default, `lru`, keeps the current behavior. - With `mamba_aware_lru`, when a request finishes, the Mamba states it superseded move to the front of the free queue (they are demoted). A state is superseded when an earlier request left it as its deepest cached state (its tip), and this request resumed from or passed it and then cached a deeper state. All other blocks keep LRU order, including the request's shared-prefix junction, the state where prompts that share a prefix diverge. - Outputs do not change: the policy only reor

title: [Bugfix] Migrate Olmo3 reasoning parser to the streaming parser engine
summary: ## Purpose Fix content being silently dropped by the Olmo3 reasoning parser when a single streaming delta carries the closing `</think>` together with the content after it (stream interval > 1, chunked prefill), by migrating the parser onto the streaming parser engine as suggested in review. The legacy buffer parser processed at most one `<think>`/`</think>` transition per delta: `process_buffer()` emitted the reasoning and left the trailing content in the buffer, where it was never flushed. The first revision of this PR patched the buffer with an unconditional drain, which (as review pointed out) broke 4 existing tests by flushing text the buffer was intentionally holding back. This revision does the migration instead, following the qwen3/gemma4/nemotron_v3 pattern: - `vllm/parser/olmo3.py` — declarative `ParserEngineConfig`: initial state REASONING, optional leading `<think>`, text-lexed terminals (the Olmo3 markers are ordinary text split across multiple vocabulary tokens, so there are no `token_id_terminals`), `strip_trailing_reasoning_whitespace=False` to keep reasoning verbatim. title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Force two-shot MNNVL fused all-reduce+RMSNorm for fp16 (flashinfer#6817)
summary: ## Why the old behavior is bad Any fp16 model served with TP > 1 and the default compilation config on MNNVL hardware (e.g. a GB200 NVL tray) generates garbage: the FlashInfer MNNVL **one-shot** fused all-reduce + RMSNorm kernel squares activations in the *input dtype* (`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh`: `threadSum += toFloat<T>(x * x)`). For fp16, any activation |x| > 256 overflows to `inf`, `rsqrt(inf) == 0`, and the token's entire norm output is silently zeroed. fp16 models with large activation outliers (e.g. Qwen2/Qwen2.5 backbones) hit this on decode-sized batches, so completions degenerate to repeated token id 0 (`!!!!!`) and greedy decoding is nondeterministic. Eager mode is unaffected because the fusion is a compile-time pass. Upstream root cause: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6817, fixed by flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6818 (fp32 square), first released in flashinfer **v0.7.3** (2026-11-04) — but vLLM still pins 0.7.2.post1, which has the buggy line. ## What changed In the registered custom op `vllm::flashinfer_trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm` (`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py`), force `use_oneshot=False` when the workspace backend is `mnnvl` and the input dtype is fp16, but only while the installed flashinfer is older than v0.7.3 (the guard self-disables once the fixed kernel is available). The MNNVL *two-shot* kernel converts to fp32 before squaring and is correct; bf16 cannot overflow and is untouched, as is the `trtllm` backend. title: [Fix] dsv41: Build MegaGate row masks inside the decoder replay-tail graph capture
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51478. With MegaGate on and EPLB off, the decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs inside a serving forward, after two eager warm-ups of the same layers on a copy of the same batch. The per-forward row-mask cache from #46071 hands the warm-ups' eager masks to the capture, so the mask build is never recorded in the graph. Every replay then reads a valid-row mask computed for the step that captured the graph. Real rows past that count are routed as padding in the tail layers, and prompts whose tail runs from a graph (≤ 2048 tokens here) drift. ## Modifications - `layers/moe/mega_gate.py::_gate_row_masks`: the cache key gains `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`. A capture builds its own masks inside the graph, and the layers it captures still share them; eager forwards behave as before. The query runs only when the per-forward cache is active. - `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: a CPU test that runs an eager build and a capturing build in one forward scope and checks that the capture does not reuse the eager mask. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on 2× GB300, upstream `34dfaccc57` (the code path is unchanged on current `main`); config and method in #51478. Top-1 agreement with a MegaGate-off reference over 50 real text prompts, at positions where the reference's top-1 margin is above 1 nat: | arm | all prompts | ≤ 2048 tokens | > 2048 tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:| | MegaGate on, 3 independent boots | 96.64% / 96.77% / 96.78% | 69.7% | 99.4% | | MegaGate on + fix | 99.41% | 99.3% |

title: [Bug] sgl-deep-gemm PyPI wheels are built with CUDA 13.0, which compiles out DeepGEMM's CUDA >= 13.4 paths (in-CTA-norm Mega mHC on Rubin)
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The PyPI `sgl-deep-gemm` wheels are built with CUDA 13.0 ([release-whl-deepgemm.yml#L52](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/33a03ba42ee4c6036d75c22e71b9bb8600c79355/.github/workflows/release-whl-deepgemm.yml#L52)). Several DeepGEMM host paths are gated on `CUDA_VERSION >= 13040` at compile time, so these wheels compile them out. One of them is the in-CTA-norm Mega mHC template (sgl-project/DeepGEMM#141), which is selected only on CC 10.7: [`csrc/apis/mega_mhc.hpp#L257`](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e3f6b84093dab1213f50cd1865d847365697ef23/csrc/apis/mega_mhc.hpp#L257) (v0.2.8): ```cpp bool in_cta_norm = CUDA_VERSION >= 13040 and is_shifted and SM107ArchSpec::is_current() and (in_cta_norm_env >= 0 ? in_cta_norm_env != 0 : ...); ``` `CUDA_VERSION` is a compile-time constant of the host build, and it is tested before `DG_MHC_IN_CTA_NORM`, so the env override cannot turn the path back on. The other paths behind the same gate in v0.2.8 are the Mega mHC and MegaMoE oversized-shared-memory settings and the native locality-domain allocator. On Rubin (VR200), the 0.2.8 aarch64 wheel therefore always runs the slower Mega mHC template for large prefill calls. ### How to confirm The same compile-time test backs `uses_native_locality_domains()` ([`csrc/apis/locality_domain.hpp#L31-L33`](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e3f6b84093dab1213f50cd1865d847365697ef23/csrc

summary: **Stacked on #51312**: review only the last commit ([this PR's own diff](https://github.com/anish-shanbhag/sglang/compare/prefetch-node-reads...skip-unread-tensors), +188/-27 lines). **Precedent** - **TensorRT-LLM** loads only each rank's local experts, by default and with no option ([`fused_moe_triton.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/662d6908de2f92deda2c63436bba679d69a25167/tensorrt_llm/_torch/moe/fused_moe/fused_moe_triton.py#L628-L629) iterates `module.initial_local_expert_ids`). - **vLLM** has the same skip as `--enable-ep-weight-filter`: vllm-project/vllm#37136, made EPLB-aware in vllm-project/vllm#64187, scale tensors always loaded since vllm-project/vllm#37322. vllm-project/vllm#68491 proposes enabling it by default. - **SGLang** already ignores non-local experts: `FusedMoE.weight_loader` returns before copying them. summary: ## Motivation When one attention-DP rank goes idle, aggregate step and synchronization metrics identify the imbalance. They cannot tell whether that scheduler exhausted its request slots, stopped at its pass budget, or walked past a request waiting for a storage prefetch. summary: ## Motivation When `SGLANG_PORT` is set, local SHM-broadcast XPUB writers currently compete for the same eight loopback ports. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Snapshot host memory before any rank builds explicit-size HiCache pools
summary: ## Motivation With an explicit `--hicache-size` or `--hicache-ratio`, each HiCache host pool checks its allocation against the host memory free when that pool is built, divided by the number of ranks on the host (`host_memory_budget_plain_hugetlb`). The ranks on a host build their pools at the same time. A rank that reaches its check after its node mates have allocated therefore gets a share that their pools have already shrunk. Whether startup succeeds depends on the order the ranks run in, not on how much memory the host has. Example: a node runs 4 ranks, and each rank builds KV (60 GB), Mamba (72 GB) and DSA indexer (14 GB) host pools. That is ~146 GB per rank and ~583 GB per node, on nodes with ~699 GiB available. In one launch, a rank reached its Mamba check after its node mates had built most of their pools. It saw 240 GiB free, got a (240 - 10) GiB / 4 = 57.5 GiB (61.7 GB) share, below its 72 GB Mamba pool, and failed with `Not enough host memory available`, although the node had room. The same config passed in a launch where all 4 ranks checked before any of them had allocated. The auto-size path (neither flag set) does not have this race. It samples the budget, runs an all-reduce over the world group before building any pool, and books every pool against that one snapshot through `host_memory_budget_scope`. ## Modifications - `auto_size_hicache`: for explicit sizes, sample the budget, call a barrier on the world CPU group so no rank allocates before every rank has sampled, then book the rank's pools against that snapshot. T-HEAD SAIL ships its own DeepGEMM build (`deep_gemm>=1.1.0`), DeepEP and a set of fused JIT kernels, but none of them are reachable through the shared code paths: - The DeepGEMM wrapper only knows the community call surface. SAIL's library exposes a `nopad` grouped-GEMM interface, dispatches int8 / bf16 / fp4 / int4 kernel types, and needs the kernel configs supplied by an offline autotuner. - `DeepGemmRunnerCore` covers blockwise FP8, MXFP4 and INT4. SAIL's expert-parallel path additionally needs per-channel FP8 and INT8 grouped GEMMs, plus a different MXFP4 / INT4 weight layout, and it fuses the SiLU-mul with the activation quantization. - The quantization methods (`fp8`, `mxfp4`, `w8a8_int8`, `unquant`, `compressed_tensors`) never resolve to `MoeRunnerBackend.DEEP_GEMM`, so the runner is unreachable from the model side. - The DeepEP dispatcher probes FABRIC assuming a CUDA-version-specific layout, and the masked SAIL kernels consume int64 top-k ids. This PR makes DeepSeek / Kimi / DSpark models run on SAIL with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, for both TP (`--moe-a2a-backend none`) and EP (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep`), including the DSpark speculative path. SAIL behavior is gated behind `is_sail()` and kept in new modules; the shared runners keep their existing behavior. ## Modifications ### 1. summary: ## Motivation The packed HiCache target/draft layout assumes compatible physical MLA rows. title: [Feat] pd: Add input-only prefix retention on decode
summary: ## Motivation In PD serving with NEXTN/EAGLE, a long conversation can return to a decode rank that still holds its previous input. Some deployments want to reuse those input pages without retaining the generated tail as part of the reusable prefix. Upstream main already accepts speculative decoding with decode radix caching. This PR proposes an optional **input-only retention policy**; it does not change speculative sampling or enable a new draft model. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_PD_DECODE_CACHE_INPUT_ONLY` (default `false`). On decode, cap the reusable token span at the original input length before the existing EAGLE bigram and page-alignment logic. Generated slots remain request-owned until normal release. - Limit the first version to the Python unified FULL-only device cache, NEXTN/EAGLE, Mooncake and PP/CP/DCP=1. Reject decode HiCache/offload, external KV stores, session radix tracking and unsupported tree layouts. Prefill is unchanged. - This is a deliberate behavioral opt-in: subsequent turns may need to transfer pages containing previous **output** again. It is not a universal performance improvement. This PR does not add the separate Ascend INT8 KV enablement required by the GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 deployment. ## Accuracy Tests **Current code, CPU:** on base `bf20186739060dadf3e1f4a9e8772917e710ff14`, the new regression and the existing server-arguments suite passed: **360 tests, 228 subtests**. The regression uses an actual Python tree and a 128-token paged CPU allocator. It covers page/bigram boundaries, duplicate insertion, divergent suffixes, a locked in-flight prefi

title: [Fix] gemm: Use int64 row offsets in block-scaled FP8/INT8 matmuls
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51098. The block-scaled FP8 and INT8 Triton matmuls compute `offs_am * stride_am` and `stride_cm * offs_cm` with int32 row offsets. Once `M * K` (A) or `M * N` (C) reaches 2^31 elements, the offsets wrap and the kernels read A and write C out of bounds. Example reach from the issue: Qwen3-32B-FP8 at TP1, gate_up projection (N = 51,200), from about 41.9k tokens in one forward. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py` and `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/int8_kernel.py`: `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, its Hopper and gfx1250 variants, and `_w8a8_block_int8_matmul` take a `USE_INT64_OFFSETS` constexpr that promotes `offs_am` and `offs_cm` to int64. The launchers set it only when A or C has at least 2^31 elements, so every other shape compiles the original int32 kernel unchanged. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: the same for the group offset in `_per_token_group_quant_int8` (the FP8 quantizers already use int64 here), set only when the input has at least 2^31 elements. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_block_matmul_large_m.py`: regression tests with M = 2^15 + 1 and a 2^16-wide dimension, so the last row starts past 2^31 elements: FP8 with rows of A past 2^31, FP8 with rows of C past 2^31, and INT8 through `apply_w8a8_block_int8_linear` (quantization plus matmul). Inputs use exact encodings. ## Accuracy Tests Run on an NVIDIA L4 on top of the `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image, with this branch's `python/` on `PYTHONPATH`: | Test | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | FP8, rows of A past 2^31 | error | pass | | F

summary: ## Motivation RL trainers correct for the policy that generated a rollout with each sampled token's probability under the sampler's distribution: after temperature and top-k/top-p/min-p, renormalized. `output_token_logprobs` is the temperature-scaled softmax before filtering, so under top-k/top-p it is not that probability. title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Exchange K/V over device IPC instead of two NCCL all-gathers in 2-rank K/V-gather SP
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** `USPAttention._forward_with_kv_gather` calls `_gather_sharded_sequence` twice per attention layer, once for K and once for V. Those two `all_gather_into_tensor` calls are the only collectives in a FLUX.2 denoising step, and they are slow out of proportion to the bytes they move: on a gfx1250 socket a 25 MB/rank all-gather takes 446 us, an effective 56 GB/s, while a device copy of the same bytes takes 9.8 us. In a 2-step FLUX.2 trace the 432 RCCL kernels account for 219 ms of 1183 ms of GPU time, 18.5% of the step, to move data between two ranks that already have peer access to each other's memory. **Where it shows up** Any two-rank K/V-gather SP group pays this, on any device where the collective is slower than a peer-to-peer copy, and for any model that takes that path -- it is a property of the SP mode, not of FLUX.2. It is most visible when the two ranks are partitions of one socket, because the collective is then moving bytes that never had to leave the device. It reproduces on FLUX.2-dev at 720p with `--num-gpus 2` (`sp_degree=2`, `kv_gather_degree=2`) on two gfx1250 partitions; a single-GPU run has no SP group and is unaffected. The fix below is gated to ROCm and off by default, so no other platform changes behavior. **How to fix** Exchange the bytes the way the hardware already allows, and use a collective only for the ordering it is actually needed for: each rank copies K and V into a staging buffer the peer has mapped over device IPC, a one-element `all_gather_into_tensor` orders the two streams, and each rank reads the peer's half

title: [Perf] [NPU] dllm: Stop materializing fp32 logits in the denoise step
summary: ## Motivation A dLLM denoise step needs exactly two things per position: the argmax token, and the softmax probability of that same token — the confidence it compares against the unmask threshold. Both are reductions over the vocab. The logits path hands the algorithms a full fp32 `[tokens, vocab]` tensor to compute them from, and both algorithms then build a second full-width tensor for the softmax. At LLaDA2's vocab of 157184 that is **2.1 GiB per copy at 112 blocks** — this, not the KV pool, is what caps the dLLM batch size, and it is pure waste: nothing downstream needs the full matrix. ## Modifications Add `argmax_and_softmax_prob()` in `dllm/algorithm/base.py` and route both denoise algorithms through it. It has three implementations of the same quantity and picks by what the caller already paid for: 1. **`sgl_kernel_npu.sample.argmax_softmax_prob`**, when that kernel is installed. It reads each logit once, carries `(max, argmax, sumexp)` in registers via the online-softmax recurrence, and returns `(argmax, 1/sumexp)` — the argmax token's logit *is* the running max, so its shifted exponent is exactly 1 and its probability is the reciprocal of the denominator. Optional dependency; without it the branches below give the same answer. 2. **`argmax` + `softmax` + `gather`** when the logits are already fp32 — the pre-existing formulation, bitwise unchanged. 3. **Otherwise** a max reduction plus a vocab-chunked exp-sum, whose transients are `[tokens, vocab_chunk]` rather than `[tokens, vocab]`. title: [Fix] [Intel] disaggregation: Compute Mooncake transfer addresses in uint64
summary: [Fix] [Intel] disaggregation: Compute Mooncake transfer addresses in uint64 ## Motivation On Intel XPU, two Mooncake transfer paths kill the prefill transfer thread the first time they run: ``` File ".../disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py", line 2036, in process_layer_tp_aware src_page_base_addrs = src_layer_ptr + prefill_page_indices * src_kv_item_len OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long RuntimeError: Transfer thread failed because of Python int too large to convert to C long. Prefill instance with bootstrap_port=21500 is dead. ``` Both add page or row offsets to a layer base pointer in int64 numpy arrays. Level Zero device pointers have bit 63 set (for example `torch.empty(..., device="xpu").data_ptr() == 0xffff80ac0bc00000`), so they don't fit in int64. CUDA pointers do fit, which is why this only shows on XPU. The two paths: - `send_kvcache_slice`, the heterogeneous-TP head-slice path. It runs when prefill and decode split KV heads differently, e.g. GQA prefill CP (attention TP 1) into decode TP 2. Hit on 4x Arc Pro B60. - `send_kvcache_dcp`, the sliced draft-KV path (`process_sliced_draft`). It runs for decode context parallel with a draft model. Reproduced in a unit test. ## Modifications - Compute the addresses in both paths in `np.uint64`: page and row indices, per-token and head-slice offsets, and layer base pointers. The NIXL connector already does the same for this reason (`nixl/conn.py`, `_pack_stride_descs`). - Every operand is non-negative and the result is a device address, so the values are unchanged on CUDA. - Add `test_sliced_draft_address

title: [Feat] Dspark: Support PP decode with stage-local draft owners
summary: Co-authored-by:@zhangxiaolei123456 ## Tracking - Roadmap: #43885 - PP × speculative decoding tracking: #39634 - Supersedes: #38702 This PR implements the DSpark-specific PP decode path with stage-local draft ownership and bubble-aware scheduling. ## Motivation Pipeline-parallel target verification can reduce cross-node MoE communication for DeepSeek-V4 deployments. However, running all DSpark draft work on the last pipeline stage creates an additional bottleneck and leaves bubbles on other stages. This PR supersedes #38702 and updates the implementation against the current `main`. It introduces an experimental PP2 DSpark mode where: - Each PP stage hosts a complete TP draft model replica. - Every request is assigned to one stable stage-local draft owner. - Draft work is distributed across PP stages instead of duplicated on every stage. - Draft generation for one microbatch can overlap with target verification of another microbatch. - Only projected target context and draft proposals are transferred between stages. - DSpark state is preserved across PD-disaggregated Prefill and Decode servers. ### Individual runs Policy | Run | Duration | Output throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Mean E2E -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- tail | 1 | 204.32 s | 7,517.54 tok/s | 4,203.11 ms | 26.97 ms | 44,636.74 ms tail | 2 | 201.39 s | 7,627.00 tok/s | 4,162.39 ms | 26.69 ms | 44,176.98 ms tail | 3 | 198.08 s | 7,754.25 tok/s | 4,069.90 ms | 26.85 ms | 44,319.53 ms bubble | 1 | 186.68 s | 8,227.76 tok/s | 4,686.25 ms | 25.02 ms | 42,197.61 ms bubble | 2 | 180.96 s | 8,488.27 tok/s | 3,956.3

title: [Fix] dsa: Attend the sharded indexer's local slots in trtllm / prims_ts DCP decode
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1 under decode context parallelism produces garbage with `--dsa-decode-backend prims_ts` or `trtllm`: GSM8K drops from ~0.97 to ~0.03 and answers mix in other requests' content. `flashmla_kv` (the default) is unaffected, so `test_kimi_k31_b300.py` stays green. The InferenceX Kimi-K3.1 GB300 recipes serve with `prims_ts`, so every disagg point broke when moving from the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 image to a main nightly (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261118-ecd3d75a`). Root cause: a semantic merge conflict between two PRs that are each correct on their own base. They touch different lines, so they merged cleanly. - sgl-project/sglang#49106 (opened before the next PR merged) added sharded DCP decode (`dcp_partial`) to `_forward_trtllm`, which both `trtllm` and `prims_ts` go through. On its base the indexer returned global slots (`dcp_global_topk`), so it localized them with `localize_dcp_page_table`. That remap treats its input as interleaved global slots, keeps `slot % dcp_size == dcp_rank`, and maps those to `slot // dcp_size`. - sgl-project/sglang#48895 merged first and moved localization into the indexer: `dcp_local_topk` returns this rank's compacted local KV slots and writes their counts to `metadata.dcp_topk_length`. It updated the only consumer that existed then, `flashmla_kv`, to take them as-is. After both merged, `_forward_trtllm` localizes slots that are already local. That keeps about 1/dcp_size of the selected keys and points them at unrelated KV entries. The Day-0 branch localized only once, with `dcp_localize_compact` at this point in the back

title: [Perf] sampling: Re-derive top-p and min-p flags when filtering a batch
summary: ## Motivation `SamplingBatchInfo` keeps batch-wide flags that select the sampling path. #50400 re-derived the five `top_k` flags after `ScheduleBatch.filter_batch` drops rows, but the two adjacent flags derived from request parameters are still left unchanged: - `need_top_p_sampling = any(top_p != 1.0)` - `need_min_p_sampling = any(min_p > 0)` Both flags are conservative when stale, but sticky. For example, after the only `min_p > 0` request finishes, the remaining batch still has `need_min_p_sampling = True`. On the FlashInfer and Intel XPU paths, every later decode step then keeps launching `top_p_renorm_prob`, `top_k_renorm_prob`, and `min_p_sampling_from_probs` instead of leaving the min-p path. Likewise, stale top-p or min-p flags keep an otherwise plain-temperature batch out of `simple_sampling_case`, including the deterministic log-softmax fast path. The filtered batch should select exactly the same sampling path as a batch built directly from the kept requests. ## Modifications - Add `_sampling_flags(top_ps, top_ks, min_ps)` as the single derivation point for all request-parameter sampling flags. It reuses the existing `_top_k_flags` helper. - Use `_sampling_flags` in `SamplingBatchInfo.from_schedule_batch`. - Generalize `refresh_top_k_flags` to `refresh_sampling_flags`, and have `ScheduleBatch.filter_batch` pass the kept requests' top-p, top-k, and min-p values. - Add a derived-property regression test covering the cases where the kept row needs top-p, needs min-p, or needs neither. In every case, the refreshed flags must equal a freshly constructed batch's flags.

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Fuse the MLA decode query and latent KV cache write

title: [Fix] dllm: Cap and capacity-gate the staging token budget
summary: ## Motivation One device-agnostic dLLM scheduling-budget fix found while running LLaDA2 FDFO at large batch sizes, plus regression tests pinning an abort-path KV reclaim that upstream has since fixed independently. Reproduces on any backend (no device-specific branches involved). ### Bug 1: KV leak when aborting FDFO requests with unresolved blocks `RadixCache.cache_finished_req` slices `req_to_token` by `len(origin_input_ids + output_ids)`, but an FDFO request's unresolved denoise block exists only in `dllm_incomplete_ids` — its committed KV slots lie **beyond** that length. The tail free never sees those slots, so every aborted incomplete request orphans one block of KV, and the pool never recovers. **How to reproduce** (radix cache on, i.e. default): ```bash # 1. Launch a dLLM server; strict idle check turns the leak warning into a hard error. # --dllm-algorithm is the only required dLLM flag (FDFO and radix cache are on by # default; the attention backend is auto-resolved per platform). SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_IDLE=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini --trust-remote-code \ --dllm-algorithm LowConfidence # 2. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Opt-in single-pass Triton top-k for long-context decode rows
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, DSA decode and MTP verify run their top-2048 + page transform through the top-k v2 kernel. At long contexts with 72 or more rows per rank, v2 takes 113 to 127 us per call on MI355X. This PR adds a single-pass Triton/Gluon selector that takes 58 to 82 us there, 1.5x to 1.9x faster. It is opt-in via `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON=1` because it is slower than v2 at short contexts; see the table below. ## Modifications - **New `kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_topk_transform.py`**: three launches whose shape depends only on the row count (CUDA-graph safe). - `est`: per row, samples about 8192 logits and bit-searches a threshold that leaves about 2 x topk elements above it. Rounding down admits more candidates, but a biased sample can still overestimate the full-row threshold; the selector handles candidate underflow explicitly. - `collect`: one pass over the logits on a persistent grid; keys at or above the threshold go to a per-row candidate buffer of 8192 entries. - `select`: the exact k-th largest key among the candidates, then exactly min(L, topk) slots through the compact page table (`real_page_table`, page_size 64). This is the table the v2 decode graph keeps, so it needs no page_size=1 table. - **Exact fallback.** If a row has fewer than min(L, topk) candidates or overflows the 8192-entry buffer, `select` takes the k-th largest key over the whole row and emits from it. This path is slow and rare, but it keeps the result an exact top-k for any input. - **Dispatch** (`dsa_topk_backend.topk_transform`): this path is used, instead of v2, for decode-shaped PAG

summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51395. The regular DSA `sgl-kernel` TopK path uses radix-selection kernels that collect selected indices in `atomicAdd` arrival order. On an RTX 5090, a model-independent fixed-random-input repro launched 20 fresh processes. All processes received bitwise-identical scores and selected the same set, but all 20 raw-order hashes were different. Passing two permutations through the actual `triton_sparse_mla_prefill` kernel changed 13,960 BF16 output elements across all 32 tested rows. summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51104. `_per_token_quant_int8` computed `row_id * stride_x` and `row_id * stride_xq` from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`, and `_per_token_group_quant_int8` did the same with `g_id * y_stride`. For inputs with at least 2^31 elements the product wraps to a negative offset and the kernels read and write before the tensors. It asserts the per-row scales equal `value / 127` and that the last 16 rows, which sit past 2^31 elements, quantize exactly like the early rows with the same value. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Route the DCP prefill by its wire bytes
summary: ## Motivation A DSA DCP prefill can be served two ways: **owned** all-gathers Q, attends the slots this rank owns, and LSE-merges the head partials back through an a2a; **gathered** all-gathers the cached prefix KV latents once and attends them with this rank's local heads, with no merge. Neither wins everywhere. Owned pays per extend token and head, gathered pays per cached prefix token, and the crossing between them is a property of the data layout, not of the model. This PR derives it from the running configuration and routes each extend batch accordingly. Builds on #47180 (Q replication + project-before-merge) and #44322, both merged. ## Modifications Per extend token and gathered head, owned puts a partial plus its packed LSE on the wire. Per cached prefix token, gathered puts one latent on the wire. Both collectives move the same `(W-1)/W` of their volume over the same fabric, so the group width and the bandwidth cancel: ``` crossover = (partial_width + lse_pack) * itemsize(partial_dtype) / (latent * itemsize(kv_dtype)) gathered when sum(extend_prefix_lens) < crossover * gathered_heads * extend_num_tokens ``` `latent = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`; `partial_width` is `v_head_dim` when the partials are projected before the merge, `kv_lora_rank` otherwise. A query all-gather adds one latent in the KV dtype to the numerator, which is exactly the denominator — so **not replicating `q_b_proj` adds exactly 1.0, for every model and dtype.** `dcp_gathered_prefill_crossover()` evaluates this once at backend construction and logs it. title: [Fix] model_loader: Split checkpoint prefetch among each node's own ranks
summary: ## Motivation `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` splits the checkpoint's shards among a node's ranks, so that the node reads each shard once and the ranks' mmap loads hit the page cache. On multiple nodes, the split is wrong: - The split strides by `world_group.local_size or launch_world_size`. - On GPU, `LOCAL_SIZE` is never set, so the stride is the whole world size (`tp * pp`), while the offset `local_rank` is the GPU index. - With 4 nodes of 4 GPUs, every node prefetches the shards whose index `i` satisfies `i % 16 < 4`: the same quarter on every node. - The other three quarters are never prefetched on any node and are read through page faults during loading. ## Modifications The split now uses the number of ranks per node, `launch_world_size // nnodes` when `LOCAL_SIZE` is unset, and this rank's position on its node, `rank % ranks_per_node`. Ranks are numbered node by node. No option is added. Prefetch itself stays opt-in; #50342 (on by default) and #37806 (automatic on network filesystems) propose enabling it, and either would hit this bug on every multi-node run. ## Accuracy Tests Prefetch never changes which weights are loaded. title: [Fix] kernels/lora: Use int64 token row offsets in the csgmv shrink and expand kernels
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51099. The chunked-SGMV (csgmv) LoRA kernels load each token's physical row from the int32 `permutation` and multiply it by the row stride: `s_offset_physical * x_stride_0` / `* output_stride_0` in the shrink kernel (plain and split-K) and `* output_stride_0` in the expand kernel. When `row * stride >= 2^31` the int32 product wraps, so the kernels read (shrink) and read/write (expand) before the tensors. The Triton LoRA backend already widens the same index to int64 in `kernel_utils.py`. One forward of about `2^31 / K` tokens reaches this, e.g. a long unchunked prefill. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_shrink.py` and `chunked_sgmv_expand.py`: widen `s_offset_physical` to int64 right after the `tl.load` (three kernels: shrink, split-K shrink, expand). - `test/registered/kernels/ops/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph.py`: three CUDA regression tests, skipped below about 10 GB of free GPU memory. The shrink test (with and without `split_k=2`) uses the shape from the issue, `x` of 65538 x 32768 fp16 with the last physical row at offset 2,147,516,416, and expects the last row to be 16 values of 32.0. The expand test writes into a 65538 x 32768 fp16 base output and expects the last row to be all 1.0. They are added to the existing csgmv test file in the same subsystem. ## Accuracy Tests No model output changes for inputs below 2^31 elements: the offset arithmetic is unchanged there. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA L4, 24 GB (compute capability 8.9, sm89), driver 595.112.07 (CUDA 13.2) | | Host | RunPod container, Ubuntu 24.

title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Score decode rows with a grouped Triton kernel on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, the QSA indexer of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores the compressed keys of every decode, target-verify and draft-extend row with `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode`. It reads the keys at about 0.5 TB/s, for two reasons: - Each draft row of a request reads the request's compressed keys again, although a request's rows share its page-table row and differ only in length, so a verify step moves 4x the key bytes it needs. - ROCm MFMA needs a 16-wide N dimension, so the 4 index heads are padded with 12 zero heads (`head_alignment = 16 if is_hip()`) and three quarters of the MFMA work multiplies zeros. ## Modifications Scope: ROCm only. title: [Feat] model-loader: cap the bytes the multithreaded loader keeps in flight
summary: ## Motivation `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` bounds its sliding window by a shard **count**: `num_threads + 1` shards are in flight, so peak host RAM is about `(num_threads + 2) x shard size`. With `--weight-loader-disable-mmap`, every in-flight shard is held in memory as bytes and then as tensors, so loads on RAM-limited hosts can be OOM-killed partway through. ## Modifications - `model_loader/weight_utils.py`: `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` takes `max_inflight_bytes`. summary: Any feedback is highly welcome! I'm a PhD student working on serving performance, but I'm new to contributing to sglang and open-source repositories in general. Please let me know if I've missed anything obvious! ## Motivation Paged Experts copies every missing expert into its GPU slot before the MoE kernel starts. That makes every expert wait for every transfer: resident experts cannot start until all copies finish, and each missing expert waits for the others to arrive. Fusing the host reads into the MoE kernel removes that dependency, so the GPU pipelines computation with transfers. This matters more as CPU-GPU interconnects get faster, as with NVLink-C2C on GH200, GB200/GB300 and (upcoming) Vera Rubin. ## Design Our goal is to extend the existing MoE kernels (Triton and Marlin) to pipeline loading missing experts alongside computing resident experts, without unnecessary dependencies between them. The host copies are variants of the existing Triton `fused_moe_kernel` and Marlin MoE kernel, chosen through their existing entry points; no other implementation in SGLang pages experts in from inside a MoE kernel. The kernel has to use as much of the interconnect bandwidth as it can for the whole launch, without taking every SM, so resident experts keep progressing. - How the kernel knows which experts to read from host memory: each layer has K GPU slots, and routed entries normally carry a slot id 0 to K − 1. title: [Fix] disaggregation: wait for the prefill forward before sending KV chunks under PP
summary: ## Motivation On a disaggregated prefill server with pipeline parallelism, `process_prefill_chunk` sends the KV of a chunked request's non-final chunk at the start of the next scheduler iteration. At that point the chunk's forward has only been launched on `forward_stream`, and the PP event loop does not wait for it before the page indices are handed to the KV sender. With the default PP comm path and the default `--pp-async-batch-depth 0`, this happens to be safe. After launching a batch, each stage issues a P2P send for it (proxy tensors on non-last stages, outputs on the last stage) that makes the schedule stream wait on that forward's event. The page-index copy in `send_kv_chunk` is issued on that stream after the wait, so it completes only after the forward: v0.5.22 blocks on it with `.cpu()`, and on main the Mooncake transfer worker synchronizes on its `indices_event`. Three settings break this ordering: - `--pp-async-batch-depth N` with N > 0: the last stage sends the outputs of the micro-batch launched N iterations earlier, before it launches the current one, so what holds its scheduler back now refers to that older forward. The last stage hands each non-final chunk to the KV sender while the chunk's forward is still running. - `SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP=1`: the wait is issued on the dedicated PP comm stream instead, so on the non-last stages nothing orders the KV read after the forward anymore. - `SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1`: the last stage skips the output send for a batch that holds a single non-final chunk, and the wait goes with it. #47074 reports t

title: [Perf] [H20] fp8-gemm: Take the swapAB kernel for small-M block FP8 GEMM on H20
summary: ## Motivation On SM90, `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` resolves to plain DeepGEMM (`_dispatch_auto_backend` → `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`). DeepGEMM's default kernel is shaped for large M, but in decode the M dimension *is* the batch size: every decode step runs 60+ block-FP8 GEMMs with `1 <= M <= 32`, and that kernel leaves most of its tile empty at those sizes. Whether that empty tile **costs** anything depends on how much compute the part has per byte of weights it streams, and on H20 it costs a lot. H20 is Hopper silicon cut down to 78 SMs against 132 on H100/H200, so it has roughly a third of their compute while giving up only ~15% of their bandwidth. Narrow-M block-FP8 GEMM on H20 is therefore compute-bound: the redundant MMA work, not the ~27 GB weight stream, is what sets the inter-token time. That is the part this PR targets, and the measurement below shows the effect is absent on an H200 — so the change is scoped to H20 rather than to SM90 as a whole. `flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` is one entry point over **two** DeepGEMM kernels — `fp8_gemm_kernel_swapAB` for `M < 32` and `fp8_gemm_kernel` above it. #32843 already confined `flashinfer_deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` to exactly the `1 <= M < 32` band and delegates every other M (including `M == 0` on idle ranks) back to DeepGEMM, so that callable is a strict superset of what `auto` selects today. It is reachable only by naming `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` explicitly, which leaves the single-request decode of a mainstream FP8 model at roughly 60% of what it reaches

title: rust-server: /generate hidden_states for the prefill step is one flat row, Python returns one row per token
summary: ## Summary With `--return-hidden-states-mode full` and `"return_hidden_states": true`, the first item of `meta_info.hidden_states` has a different shape on the two frontends: - Python frontend: one row per prefill token, `[n, hidden_size]`. - Rust frontend: one flat row of `n × hidden_size` numbers. In the three requests below, the values are the same. The Rust response does not keep the token boundaries, so a client has to know the hidden size to split the row, and needs different code for each frontend. In the requests below, `n` = `prompt_tokens − cached_tokens`, so the length of the flat row also changes with the prefix cache. ## Reproduce ```bash # Python frontend python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 31000 --return-hidden-states-mode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1 --skip-server-warmup # Rust frontend SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 31001 --return-hidden-states-mode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1 --skip-server-warmup ``` `--skip-server-warmup` matters: the warmup request would put a prefix in the cache before the first request. I ran one server at a time. Send these three requests, in this order, to a fresh server. The last line prints `prompt_tokens`, `cached_tokens` and the shape of each item: ```bash PORT=31000 # 31001 for the Rust frontend P1='The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the quiet river bank today' P2="$P1 and then it slept under an old oak tree" for P in "$P1" "$P1" "$P2"; do curl -s localhost:$PORT/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"tex

summary: ## Motivation A native `api.v1` Abort ACK means cancellation was requested. In disaggregated serving, a Decode worker may still hold KV pages and a metadata slot while a Prefill peer can still write to them. The caller needs a receipt tied to the original request that confirms those resources were released. ## Dependency and merge order 1. #50617 provides the scheduler-side retirement proof for an exact request instance. 2. #50042 exposes the proof through `api.v1` Abort for unified, single-rank text serving and binds retries to the original request instance. 3. #51460 extends that receipt to Decode-side KV receive and drain in single-rank text P/D. [Focused diff against the integrated #50042 revision](https://github.com/andrewzyxing/sglang/compare/17e83beeb0c1c61e088984b78cf0751237c572f7...59877d20bd51b7fab05eaccbd22351d0bcf0b942). ## Implemented - The existing Decode attention TP collective distinguishes pending, timed out, and drained transfers. A timed-out peer cannot be reported as drained. - The scheduler targets the exact Decode request while receiving KV, or observes it if it is already in the deferred-release queue. The receipt requires a nonempty set of Prefill drain ACKs for the receiver's abort generation and successful local KV, metadata and receiver cleanup. title: [Fix] metrics: Add MLA/MoE-aware FLOPs and fix device-timer prefill TFLOPS estimation in the MFU estimator
summary: ## Motivation `_init_estimated_perf_constants()` in `metrics_reporter.py` applied the generic dense/GQA linear-layer formula to every model, regardless of architecture. Two gaps this causes: - **MLA models** (DeepSeek-V2/V3, MiniCPM3, DeepSeek-VL2, Kimi-VL) have a structurally different attention shape: Q is optionally low-rank compressed (`q_lora_rank`), and K/V are jointly down-projected into one shared latent per token (`kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`) rather than per-head K/V like GQA. Reusing the generic formula (with the padded kernel-layout `head_dim`, e.g. 256) overstates both linear-projection FLOPs and, especially, KV-cache/weight-read bytes -- directly undercutting the bandwidth-bound regime MLA is designed to shrink. - **MoE models** were charged dense `intermediate_size` FFN cost per token, not scaled by how many experts actually activate (`num_experts_per_tok` + shared experts), understating MLP FLOPs/bytes by roughly that multiplier. This is depended on by `fix/hybrid-mamba-mfu-flops-overcount` (#48326)'s `num_attn_layers`/`num_mlp_layers` layer-type split, so this PR is stacked on that one and should be reviewed/merged after it (or rebased if it lands first). A second, smaller fix in the same file: `query_forward_active` (which drives the `forward_overlap` label on `scheduler_stage_seconds_total`) was gated on `self.scheduler.device == "cuda"`, silently disabling it on every non-CUDA backend even though `DeviceTimer`/`_TimingInterval` only use `torch.get_device_module()` + `Event.query()`, both device-agnostic. ### `est. prefill TFLOPS/s` can report physic

summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51096. On a sliding-window layer, `_fwd_kernel_unified` read the speculative tree mask with the rail length as the row stride and the rail index as the column. title: [Perf] [NPU] dllm: Cut per-step host overhead in the extend path
summary: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Name the hybrid state cache in the KV OOM message
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51175's diagnostic request. When the hybrid state cache exhausts the KV budget, startup fails with: ``` ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=0.9. Raise --mem-fraction-static above 0.778 (minimum viable = 1 - available/pre = 0.7771). ... ``` That suggestion only prices the weights against free memory. The state cache is charged *after* the fraction's slack, so `--mem-fraction-static` does not shrink it — in the reported case the advice was to raise the fraction above `0.778` while it was already `0.90`/`0.92`. The overflowing term is never named, and the actual unblock was `--max-mamba-cache-size`. ## Modifications - Extract the message into `kv_cache_oom_message()` and record the budget just before and just after `_handle_max_mamba_cache()` in `_profile_available_bytes()`. - Only when that charge — and not the weights — crosses zero, append: the charge in GB, the fact that `--mem-fraction-static` does not reduce it, and the knobs that do: - `--max-mamba-cache-size` (with its current value, or the auto-sized/`--max-running-requests` guidance when unset); - `--speculative-num-draft-tokens` when speculation is on and the value is known; - `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` is named explicitly as part of the charge. - The weights-only failure and the non-overflowing path keep the original message byte-for-byte, so no existing expectation changes. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_oom_message.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`) covers: - weights crossing zero before the state cache → original m

title: [Fix] [AMD] JIT: Port per-token group FP8 quantization v2 to ROCm
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fails to start on gfx942 with ROCm. During decode CUDA graph capture, it calls `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2`. title: [Perf] moe: Faster loading for MoE models using TP
summary: ## Motivation TL;DR Loading expert weights with TP is very unfriendly to disk reads. Kimi-K3 at TP8 on two GB300 nodes over NFS loads slower than 70 minutes, but with this PR it loads in about 7 minutes. To use, add ``` --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"load_tp_by_experts": true, "enable_multithread_load": true}' ``` The high level idea is to load expert weights in a disk friendly order (which is the same as EP), then perform an all-to-all on device to restore TP weights layout. Loading a large MoE checkpoint with pure tensor parallelism (TP) is slow when the checkpoint is read from network storage and does not fit in host memory. A safetensors checkpoint stores each expert as its own tensors, but a TP rank needs a slice of every expert, so every rank reads from every expert tensor, and in a multi-node TP group every node reads from the whole checkpoint. `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` hides this by staging the checkpoint in the page cache first, which works only while the checkpoint fits in host memory. With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"load_tp_by_experts": true}'`, each TP rank instead loads whole experts, as EP would: rank `r` reads only its `1/tp` share of the experts, so a node reads only the experts its ranks own, as whole contiguous tensors. After loading, every MoE layer is converted to the normal TP layout with one `all_to_all` per parameter over the TP ranks. The served model is unchanged: same weights, same TP layout, same kernels. The flag alone fixes what is read, not how fast. The loader still reads a tensor's page

The kernel returns routing-weighted BF16 outputs per expert. The caller owns expert reduction, routed scaling and TP communication. title: [Perf] qwen4: pin the offloaded PLE table at its exact size
summary: ## Motivation With `--ple-offload-embedding` (the default for BF16 Qwen4-Exp on CUDA, and what the RTX PRO 6000 cookbook cells use), the PLE n-gram table lives in pinned host memory: `torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True)`. torch's caching host allocator rounds every block up to a power of two. For Qwen3.8-Flash-Next the FP8 table is 51,200,245,760 bytes (47.68 GiB), so the process pins **64 GiB**: 16.32 GiB of page-locked host RAM that holds nothing. The cookbook's RTX PRO 6000 notes accordingly require "≥ 64 GB of free RAM for the locked table". On hosts that run several engines per node, or that are RAM-limited, those 16 GiB per engine are the difference between fitting and not. ## Modifications - `models/qwen4_exp_ple_table.py`: on CUDA builds the `pinned` backend allocates the table with `cudaHostAlloc`: same call and flags (`cudaHostAllocDefault`) as torch's pinned allocator, exact size. It is freed with `cudaFreeHost` when the table's storage is released. Non-CUDA builds keep `torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True)`. The `file` backend is unchanged. - `mem_cache/pool_host/common.py`: the ownership logic of the ROCm host-pool allocator (`torch.frombuffer` over the raw allocation, free with the last view) becomes `alloc_owned_host_tensor(dims, dtype, alloc, free)`, shared by `_alloc_hip_host_tensor` and the PLE table. - `distributed/device_communicators/cuda_wrapper.py`: `CudaRTLibrary` gains `cudaHostAlloc` / `cudaFreeHost`. - Cookbook (`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.mdx` and the deployment-panel config): the RTX PRO 6000 cells need ≥ 52 GB of free host RAM for the locked table, not ≥ 64

title: [Fix] pd: Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots
summary: ## Motivation On the PD **decode** side, `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` sizes the hybrid Mamba / linear-attention **speculative** intermediate scratch (`intermediate_ssm`, `intermediate_conv_window`) by `size + pre_alloc_size`, where `pre_alloc_size = disaggregation_decode_extra_slots` reserves extra `req_to_token` slots for in-transfer (being-received-from-prefill) requests. Those in-transfer slots never need the speculative scratch: it is indexed **positionally by running-batch slot** (`build_verify_intermediate_state_indices` is seeded from `req_to_token_pool.size`, which is `size`, not `_alloc_size`), and in-transfer requests are not in the running batch, so they never enter `target_verify`. The extra rows are never touched. They are not budgeted either. By default a decode server runs with the radix cache disabled, and `_handle_max_mamba_cache` then reserves verify scratch for `max_running_requests // attn_dp_size + 1` rows, while the pool allocates `size + pre_alloc_size + 1`. The difference comes out of the memory left for CUDA graphs and NCCL: in the run below the KV pool is 1,072,640 tokens on main and on this branch alike, and only the free memory after startup changes. The scratch is `[num_layers, spec_state_size + 1, draft_tokens, ...]` fp32. With MTP on GLM-5.3-Flash (34 KDA layers, TP8) the default `disaggregation_decode_extra_slots` (2x the per-worker running batch for small batches) roughly triples it: `max_running_requests=64`, per-worker `size=8`, `extra_slots=16`, so `spec_state_size=24` instead of `8`, and `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` is **19.9 GB**

title: [Perf] dspark: Fold the static verify epilogue's commits into the accept tail and trim the verify-to-draft glue
summary: ## Motivation At batch 1, a DSpark decode step on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash replays two CUDA graphs, the target verify and then the draft, with a little eager work between them. Several small launches on that path sit on the critical path. All of them run whatever the sampling temperature: - **The static verify graph's epilogue.** The verify graph always records the greedy epilogue. On a sampled step it runs with its commit gate at 0, before the sampling-accept graph replays the real accept and commits. The second one, for the bonus tokens, runs on the forward stream behind the previous step's draft. All three changes copy the same integer values that the separate launches copy, so the results are bitwise identical. None of them adds a switch: each is gated only by the feature it builds on. ## Modifications - **Commit tail in the fused accept tail.** When the fused greedy accept tail serves the batch size, `run_static` passes the relay scatter, the engram history commit and the deferred draft KV staging to that tail. `static_accept_tail` takes the relay tables and a `CommitTai

summary: ## Motivation Refs #45563. With a NIXL file plugin and O_DIRECT on (the default), every transfer's address and length must be whole 4 KiB blocks. title: [Fix] hicache: Preserve storage prefetch results through admission
summary: ## Motivation HiCache cache-mode storage hits can be lost at two admission boundaries: 1. A capacity-limited prefetch has no active operation yet, so admission may treat the deferred lookup as a miss and cancel it. 2. A completed L3 read inserts pages into L2 without retaining them until admission. A subsequent allocation can make the loaded span unusable before load-back (`cache_admission_shortfall`). The original TP2 reproduction used independent 45,056-token L3 prefixes, 50,000-token inputs and 1,000-token outputs. A same-request trace showed capacity rejection, no-operation admission, retry cancellation and zero cached tokens with zero prefetch wait. A regression fails on upstream base `9304abb5321dcf27b28235d53060ecc1438df0f5`. ## Changes and provenance - Preserve pre-query capacity deferrals as explicit waiters, with retry/cancellation and rank-agreed timeout handling. - Retain completed host-cache spans until admission hands ownership to load-back, including abort and teardown cleanup. - Keep pending storage hits under allocation backpressure and account for admission capacity, including PD prefill wait-cycle handling. - Complete PD decode storage lookup before advertising a reusable prefix to prefill, rematch before admission, and transfer/release host references during restore and cancellation. - Settle pending decode prefetches before FIFO admission can stop on a capacity-constrained queue head, then recompute current capacity budgets. - Adapt the dependency stack to the current request-list ownership API. title: [Fix] [Intel] quant: Serve compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE on XPU with sgl-kernel-xpu's INT4 GEMM
summary: ## Motivation A weight-only group-packed compressed-tensors MoE checkpoint (W4A16) cannot load on Intel XPU. In `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_moe_scheme`, the WNA16 branch has a ROCm case and an NPU case and otherwise returns the Marlin scheme, whose repack kernel has no XPU build: ``` RuntimeError: Failed to build JIT module sgl_kernel_jit_gptq_marlin_repack ``` First hit on Intel Arc Pro B60 with `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (INT4, group 32, symmetric), served through SGLang-Omni. ## Modifications - On XPU, `get_moe_scheme` returns a new `XPUCompressedTensorsWNA16MoE`, which runs the experts on sgl-kernel-xpu's native INT4 grouped GEMM, `fused_experts(use_int4_w4a16=True)`. `--moe-runner-backend triton` selects `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` instead. - The new scheme subclasses the Triton one and keeps its post-load layout, which is what the native kernel takes: [E, N, K//2] uint8 weights and [E, N, K//group] scales. Only the nibble encoding differs. With no zero-point the kernel reads signed INT4, but compressed-tensors stores symmetric codes as code + 8. The packed weights are XORed with 0x88 once after loading, so no zero-point tensor is kept. The scheme does not build the Triton `MoeRunner`. - `FusedMoE`'s weight loader transposes w13/w2 only for the scheme names in two lists. The new class is added to both. - XPU has no Marlin to fall back to. Under either backend, a layout that hasn't been validated (asymmetric, channel, group size other than 32 or 128, actorder, int8) raises a `ValueError` instead of being routed to a kernel.
