title: [Fix] mamba: Fix PP speculative intermediate-state row indexing
summary:
Motivation

Fixes #51107.

During pipeline-parallel speculative decoding with stable request rows (SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1), the Qwen4 fused short-conv, Mamba2, and LFM2 verify paths wrote intermediate states using batch-local row indices, while delayed commit read them using stable request-pool indices.

For example, requests at batch positions [0, 1] with request-pool rows [4, 2] would write intermediate states to rows [0, 1], but commit would read rows [4, 2]. This mismatch could cause stale or zero states to be committed, particularly when requests were reordered or multiple microbatches were in flight.

This PR aligns intermediate-state indexing between verify and commit while preserving the existing behavior when PP stable rows are disabled.

Modifications

  • Qwen4 fused short-conv

    • Add optional intermediate_state_indices support to the fused verify kernel.

    • Use stable request-pool rows for intermediate-state writes while keeping batch-local input indexing and persistent-state indexing unchanged.

    • Mask invalid writes to prevent padded requests from overwriting live requests' intermediate states.

title: [Feat] [AMD] linear-attn: Add FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
summary: ## Motivation AITER ships fused FlyDSL implementations of the GDN prepare stages and the K5 state scan for AMD gfx95. Qwen3.5-397B has 45 Gated DeltaNet layers, and at TP4 each rank runs them with 4 key heads, 16 value heads and K=V=128. On those shapes the FlyDSL path runs a prefill batch 1.4-1.74x faster than SGLang's Triton GDN prefill. This PR exposes that path as an opt-in prefill backend: ```bash --linear-attn-prefill-backend flydsl ``` Decode and speculative verification stay on Triton. The backend requires gfx95 and is rejected with deterministic inference or multi-item scoring. It also serves batches that track Mamba state for the radix cache, so it stays active with radix cache on (e.g. AgentX). It falls back to Triton for unsupported input/state shapes, mixed batches, and graph-planned paths. ## Modifications - Register `flydsl` in the linear-attention backend enum and CLI choices. - Add `FlyDSLGDNKernel`, which runs AITER's FlyDSL prepare, FlyDSL K5 state scan, and output stages. - Calls the stages directly instead of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk`, which only returns `(o, final_state)`. Radix-cache Mamba tracking needs the per-chunk states `h`, so the adapter keeps them. - Uses SGLang's native `[N, H, V, K]` state pool with indexed in-place updates, reuses the caller-provided output buffer, and remaps DP-attention padding indices to the pool's padding slot once per batch. - `use_exp2=True` (FlyDSL's fused prepare owns the gate cumsum). Recurrent state follows `--mamba-ssm-dtype`; per-chunk snapshots are bf16. - Requires AITER with the `gated_delta_net` module

title: [Feat] tracing: Record detokenizer time on root spans
summary: ## Motivation Time spent in the detokenizer is invisible in traces. It sits between the scheduler's spans and the tokenizer's, so it shows up as unexplained latency between them. ## Modifications - With tracing on (`--enable-trace`), `DetokenizerManager.handle_batch_token_id_out` times each batch it handles, from the start of decoding (beam-search and standard) until the output is built, and sends the duration in a new `BatchStrOutput.detokenize_duration` field. The field is `None` when tracing is off. - `TokenizerManager._handle_batch_output` adds the duration to every request in the batch, and `set_finished_time` puts two attributes on the root span: - `detokenize.total_seconds`: summed time of the batches that carried the request (each request waits for its whole batch); - `detokenize.batches`: number of those batches. - Multi-tokenizer routing copies the per-batch duration into every sub-batch: `detokenize_duration` is in `_NOT_SPLIT_FIELDS`, and `_handle_output_by_index` and `_handle_output_by_indices` copy it explicitly; the generic split would otherwise call `len()` on the float and fail. Root-span attributes rather than a span per batch keep the span count unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling With tracing off, the duration isn't sent, so the cost is one `perf_counter` read and a few branches. Measured with `timeit` (Xeon 8375C, Python 3.11): | Where | Cost, tracing off | | --- | --- | | Detokenizer, per batch | ~55 ns | | Tokenizer, per batch | ~30-70 ns | | Tokenizer, per request | ~3 ns

title: [Fix] lora: Keep TRT-LLM virtual-expert fallback tiles power-of-two
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #51100. The stock virtual-experts path caps a tile at the LoRA rank, and for ranks such as 24, 40 or 48 that leaves a non-power-of-two `BLOCK_SIZE_N`/`BLOCK_SIZE_K`; Triton rejects a non-power-of-two `tl.arange` range at compile time. #51136 fixes that path. The experimental TRT-LLM mirror at `python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/moe/trtllm_lora_temp/virtual_experts.py` keeps its own `_get_stage_config` fallback with the same expressions, and it was not part of that PR. Its two stages see the rank on opposite sides: - shrink weight `(slots * experts, rank, hidden)`: `N_dim` is the rank; - expand weight `(slots * experts, width, rank)`: `K_dim` is the rank, and the default expand path (`use_direct_expand_add=False`) passes this config to the generic Triton kernel, whose `tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_K)` then fails. ## Modifications - Round `N_dim` and `K_dim` up before applying the 16/64/256 caps, so every tile the fallback emits is a power of two. The kernels already mask or wrap the padded rows/columns (the shrink kernel wraps `offs_bn` modulo `N` and masks the store), so the extra lanes do not change results. - Add `test/registered/kernels/ops/lora/test_virtual_experts_trtllm_fallback.py`, a CUDA regression that forces this fallback by making tuning raise (the same technique the stock path's test uses) and runs the public mirror entry point for ranks 12, 16, 24, 40 and 48. On the unmodified fallback the expand tile is the raw rank and the kernel fails to compile for the non-power-of-two ranks. The mirror's shrink launcher and direct expand kernel already d

title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Serve group32 FP8 dense linears from a BF16 weight expansion on gfx942
summary: **End to end** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8x MI300X, InferenceX AgentX trace replay, concurrency 32): P50 E2E-normalized interactivity +41.0%, P90 +37.2%, output throughput per GPU +18.8%; GSM8K unchanged. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores its dense linears as `[32, 32]` ue8m0 block FP8. On gfx942 (MI300X / MI325X) nothing but Triton serves that layout: `dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` sends every non-128 block to `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`, and `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul` loads one weight scale and one activation scale per K tile, so `BLOCK_K` is capped at 32. A K=5120 projection runs 160 serial K iterations and takes about 105 us whatever its N; at decode sizes the kernel reads weights at roughly 26 GB/s. In a decode profile of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x MI300X (TP8/EP8, DSpark, AgentX concurrency 32), this kernel is the largest single item: 17.25 ms of a 61.9 ms step (27.9%), plus 1.14 ms of group32 activation quantization. Hopper already avoids the same bound with `SGLANG_OPT_HOPPER_BLOCK_FP8_BF16` (#41251): at load it caches an exact BF16 expansion of these weights, which is exact because ue8m0 scales are powers of two, and runs the GEMM in BF16. That path is gated to `_is_cuda and is_sm90`, and its exactness range assumes OCP `float8_e4m3fn` weights, while gfx942 normalizes them to `float8_e4m3fnuz`. This PR enables the same cache on gfx942 and runs those linears in BF16 through hipBLASLt. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`: the BF16 cache condition becomes Hopper (unchanged) or gfx942 with `float8_e4m3fnuz` weights, with the existing

summary: ## Summary On MI355X with aiter, GLM-5.3-Flash picks MoE experts with a rounded bias. The checkpoint stores each layer's 288 expert correction biases in fp32, within a band about 0.4 wide. title: [Feature] Treat max_tokens as an upper bound when the prompt fits the context
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation SGLang rejects a request when `input + max_new_tokens > context_len`, even when the prompt alone fits. The exact token count depends on the server's tokenizer and chat template, so a client usually cannot compute it exactly. A client that estimates the prompt length can still exceed the remaining window, whether it sends a fixed cap or calculates one. The cap is an upper bound, not a reservation of the whole window. OpenAI defines both `max_tokens` and `max_completion_tokens` that way. The scheduler already treats it as an upper bound. `init_req_max_new_tokens` clamps `max_new_tokens` to `max_req_len - input_len - 1`, then to the KV budget. A request that does not send a cap already relies on that clamp, because the frontend check only runs when `max_new_tokens` is set. The 400 comes from `_validate_one_request` in `tokenizer_manager.py`, before the scheduler sees the request. The only switch that changes this is `--allow-auto-truncate`, and it cannot be used here because it also truncates the input. When the prompt exceeds the context, SGLang truncates it to exactly `context_len`, then clamps `max_new_tokens` to 0: the client gets HTTP 200 with an empty message and `finish_reason: length`. If the prompt alone does not fit, that should stay a 400. Measured on 0.5.22 with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` and `--context-length

title: [Fix] gemma4: Refold the router scale when it is reloaded
summary: ## Motivation `Gemma4Router` folds `scale * root_size` into `norm.weight` on its first forward and sets `_scale_fused`, and nothing ever clears that flag. So after an online weight update (`update_weights_from_distributed`, `update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_disk`) loads a new `scale`, the router keeps routing with the old one, with no error or warning. We hit this while adding Gemma 4 to the SGLang weight sync in [Halo](https://github.com/whitecircle/halo), which carries a local patch for now. It's the same kind of bug as #35883 (GLM gate). ## Modifications - `scale` gets its own weight loader that writes the parameter and refolds it into `norm.weight` in place, so CUDA graph replays see the new value too. Only clearing the flag wouldn't fix replays, because a replay doesn't run the `_scale_fused` check in `forward`. - `fuse_scale` moves `scale` to the buffers' device first. With `--cpu-offload-gb`, `scale` is still on the CPU at load time while `root_size` is on the GPU. - `forward` keeps its lazy fold for loads that skip `load_weights` (e.g. `--load-format dummy`). - `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` and `gemma4_diffusion.py` load `scale` through the parameter's own loader, so they're fixed too. - Not covered: `update_weights_from_tensor(load_format="direct")` skips parameter loaders, so the fold still goes stale there, as it does for any parameter with a custom loader. ## Accuracy Tests The first load folds the same value as before, just at load time instead of on the first forward. title: [Fix] [AMD] dflash: Keep the draft KV on full-attention slots under PD disaggregation
summary: On PD prefill and decode servers, keep the DFLASH draft KV pool on full-attention slots instead of the target's sliding-window ids, which the KV transfer does not address. ## Motivation On ROCm, `SGLANG_ROCM_ENABLE_DFLASH_SWA_DRAFT_KV` (on by default) sizes a compact DFLASH draft pool per sliding-window token and indexes it with the target's SWA ids. PD prefill and decode append that pool to the KV entries of the target's full-attention pool, and the transfer applies one plan, built from the full-attention page indices, to every entry. A draft pool on SWA ids is then addressed at the wrong rows, and past its end once a page index exceeds the smaller pool, so with the default setting PD requests of a full + SWA model with DFLASH fail at KV transfer. ## Modifications - `dflash_draft_kv_follows_target_swa` returns `False` when `disaggregation_mode` is `prefill` or `decode`, alongside the other cases where the switch is ignored (one startup warning). The draft pool is then sized per full-attention token, as with the switch set to 0. Aggregated servers are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests One 8x MI355X node (ROCm 10), `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, single-node PD (TP4 prefill + TP4 decode, MoRI transfer), DFLASH, `SGLANG_ROCM_ENABLE_DFLASH_SWA_DRAFT_KV` left unset: - Without this change both roles size the draft pool per sliding-window token (prefill 52,352 rows for a 262,144-token full pool, decode 30,336 rows for 11.9M), and 3 of 3 requests fail (`KVTransferError: KV transfer failed: length out of range`; mori `Engine batch write error 11 message length out of range`

title: [Fix] diffusion: Reserve mmap and activation headroom in host pin budget (#51188)
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Closes #51188 On memory-constrained hosts or containers (e.g., an RTX 4090 24 GB GPU in a container capped at 32 GiB host RAM via cgroup v2), running diffusion models with layerwise offload (such as `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`) causes the scheduler worker process to be OOM-killed during synthetic server warmup. ### Root Causes 1. **Aggressive Host Pin Budget Over-allocates Pinned Storage**: In `host_memory_budget.py`, `HOST_RESERVE_FRACTION` was set to `0.05` (5%) with `MIN_HOST_RESERVE_BYTES = 2 * GIB_BYTES`. Following PR #48418 (which counted reclaimable page cache as available memory under a cgroup cap), `HostPinBudget` calculated ~15.48 GiB of spendable budget in a 32 GiB cgroup and pinned 12 of 50 DiT layers (~14.43 GiB) into unevictable `memfd`/shmem (`sglang-pinned-store`). Because unpinned components stream from disk via `mmap` (DiT ~37.5 GB, text encoder ~46.9 GB, plus VAE), converting all available memory into unevictable shmem left zero page cache headroom for `mmap` page faults and dynamic activations, triggering an unrecoverable cgroup `oom_kill 1`. 2. **Server Fails Open on Worker Death**: In `http_server.py`, when synthetic warmup failed due to the scheduler worker being SIGKILLed by the cgroup OOM killer, the server logged `"Synthetic server warmup failed; continuing startup"`, set `warmup_done`

title: [Perf] [AMD] Qwen3.8: Serve QSA decode with AITER's fused FlyDSL sparse decode on gfx950

title: [Perf] disaggregation: Add the just_in_time decode allocation policy
summary: > Depends on #45337. This PR's own change is its last commit, `[PD] Add the just_in_time decode allocation policy`. ## Motivation TL;DR Instead of allocating decode memory immediately under policy early (which wastes decode memory), or waiting until prefill completes under policy prefill_complete (which adds latency to kv-transfer), we should allocate decode memory precisely such that it aligns with kv-transfer start. This PR does so with policy just_in_time. `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` (#40703) makes decode reserve a request's KV slots only after prefill finishes, so a request does not hold decode memory while it waits for and runs prefill. The cost is that decode's reservation handshake runs after prefill instead of overlapping it: prefill signals readiness, decode admits the request and allocates, and decode's destination indices travel back (under PP, through the stage-0 consensus poll) before prefill may write the KV. `early` overlaps that handshake with prefill but reserves decode memory for the whole prefill. `just_in_time` keeps the deferred reservation but starts the handshake while the request still prefills, timed so that decode's destination arrives about when prefill finishes: decode memory is reserved for roughly one handshake longer than under `prefill_complete`, and the handshake no longer adds to TTFT (time to first token). On a GLM-5.2 deployment at 0.8 req/s, with #45337 applied, `prefill_complete` still trails `early` by 0.12-0.15 s of mean TTFT with a PP4 prefill. `just_in_time` closes that gap, and with a DEP4 prefill i

summary: ## Motivation TL;DR This PR enables prefill_complete in #40703 for PP prefill as well. For a high throughput GLM5.2 server, prefill_complete on PP scheduler reduces ~70% of reserved requests on decode. Furthermore, we change how we send the kv-transfer completion signal under prefill_complete, improving TTFT by 1 to 2 iterations of prefill model forwards. This improves prefill_complete for overlap scheduler slightly, and is quite crucial for prefill_complete for PP scheduler to be useful. `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` (#40703) makes PD (prefill/decode) disaggregated decode reserve a request's KV (key-value cache) slots only after prefill finishes, instead of at bootstrap. It helps most when prefills are long, and long-context prefill is often served with PP (pipeline parallelism). This PR lets the policy run with a PP prefill, and removes the TTFT (time to first token) cost that releasing a request through the PP stages would otherwise add. **PP prefill.** Today the policy cannot start on a PP prefill: 1. `_validate_prefill_complete` rejects `pp_size != 1` on both roles. 2. `handle_other_validations` resolves `--optimistic-prefill-attempts` to 0 whenever `pp_size > 1`, and `prefill_complete` requires optimistic prefill. 3. The decode receiver fails any room whose prefill peer has `pp_size != 1`. Removing these checks is not enough. Each PP stage runs its own scheduler, and the stages must make identical scheduling decisions. summary: ## Motivation #43463 launches the QSA indexer's decode MQA-logits TileLang kernel with a fixed number of CTAs per row, each striding over the row's 64-key groups. title: [Fix] dsa: Make metadata kernel batch size a runtime arg to avoid per-bs Triton recompiles
summary: ## Motivation Three Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py` declare the batch size as `bs: tl.constexpr`. The batch size changes from one step to the next: - `_fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata_kernel` Because `bs` is a `tl.constexpr`, Triton specializes on it and compiles and caches a separate kernel for every batch size it sees. These kernels are not called during CUDA-graph capture. They run when a graph's metadata is filled on replay, with `bs` set to the padded graph batch size. So on main, the first decode step at each new padded batch size JIT-compiles up to three kernels inside the serving loop, and the Triton cache gets one entry per kernel per captured size. These kernels only use `bs` as a runtime bound: `offs_b < bs`, `row < bs`, `tl.range(0, bs)`, and `expanded_size = bs * next_n`. The compile-time tile shapes already come from `BLOCK_BS = next_power_of_2(bs)` and `BLOCK_EXPANDED`, so `bs` itself does not need to be a `constexpr`. For the same reason, `bs` is also added to each kernel's existing `do_not_specialize` list. Otherwise Triton's divisible-by-16 integer specialization would still compile a separate variant for batch sizes like 16, 32 or 48. This is the same bug as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33506, which @amd-mvarjoka fixed in another file. This PR applies that fix to the file below. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py`: removed `tl.constexpr` from `bs` in all three kernels. `bs` stays in e

title: [Fix] bench: open a fresh HTTP connection per request
summary: ## Motivation `sglang-bench` (the Rust client) intermittently records `error sending request` under high concurrency. Printing the error source chain shows the connection dies while the request is in flight: error sending request for url (...) <- client error (SendRequest) <- connection closed before message completed error sending request for url (...) <- client error (SendRequest) <- connection error <- Connection reset by peer (os error 104) The client keeps an idle connection for 90 s (reqwest's default). SGLang's HTTP server closes an idle keep-alive connection 5 s after a response completes (`SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`, the timer uvicorn arms in `on_response_complete`). A request written on a pooled connection after the server has closed it is lost. This is HTTP/1.1 keep-alive behaviour, not a server defect: a separate reproduction against the same protocol stack SGLang serves with (h11, uvloop) shows that a request reaching the server before its deadline is never lost (29,400 requests with a 60 s keep-alive all succeeded; with a 200 ms keep-alive only requests written after the deadline failed), and uvicorn upstream (main a99c1b7) has no related fix. The client is the side that must not write on a connection the server has already closed. ## Modifications - `http_client()` (new helper that builds the HTTP client) sets `pool_max_idle_per_host(0)`: no connection is kept idle between requests, so a request is never written on a connection the server is closing. In-flight concurrency is unaffected; it was never governed by the idle pool. Applies to all HTTP backends; gRP

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Transfer the draft's DSA indexer cache for hybrid DSA models
summary: ## Motivation For hybrid DSA pools (`HybridLinearKVPool` with `use_dsa`, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash: KDA + DSA layers) `setup_state_kv_args` registers `StateType.DSA` / `DSA_TAIL` from the target's `full_kv_pool` only. An EAGLE/NEXTN draft on such a model owns a single-layer DSA pool whose indexer cache is never transferred, so after a PD handoff the decode-side draft runs its top-k over an all-zero index for every prompt position. Prompts up to `index_topk` are unaffected; above it MTP acceptance drops and per-user decode speed on PD falls well below aggregated serving. The pure-DSA branch (`DSATokenToKVPool` target, DeepSeek-V3.2 / V4 NEXTN) already ships the draft's indexer cache; the hybrid branch does not. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py`: in the hybrid branch, after the target's DSA components, register the draft's index cache and kpool tail as `StateType.DSA` / `DSA_TAIL` components of their own, with the draft layer ids remapped above `num_hidden_layers` (`_remap_draft_layer_ids`). The target's components are untouched, so `slice_dsa_tail_dst_ptrs_for_pp` keeps its equal key/score halves per component and a peer without a draft simply registers fewer trailing components. A draft pool whose page / kpool / tail geometry differs from the target's is skipped with a warning. title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] kvcache: Gate fused FP8 prefix-valid commit kernel on SM89+
summary: Motivation set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8 (added by #40785) fuses FP8 KV-cache quantization into the prefix-valid commit kernel used by DFLASH speculative decoding. It compiles fp8e4nv inside a Triton kernel, which only works on SM89+ (Ada / Hopper). On SM86 (Ampere, e.g. RTX 3090) the Triton codegen rejects fp8e4nv: ValueError: type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5'). The dispatch in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid only checks the KV cache dtype and the resolved K/V scales — it does not inspect the compute capability — so an SM86 box is sent straight into the fused kernel and crashes on startup. The pre-#40785 eager path (PyTorch-layer quantization + the generic byte-copy Triton kernel) is left untouched below the fused branch, so the fix is to fall back to it on pre-SM89 GPUs. This is the prefix-valid writer specifically. #31652 gates the ordinary set_kv_buffer FP8 stores on SM89+ but leaves the prefix-valid dispatch ungated, and #42982 (SM89 NaN-saturation) does not add a capability guard either. Modifications - Add a module-level _FP8_FUSED_OK that is True only on CUDA SM89+ (torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (8, 9)). - Add and _FP8_FUSED_OK to the fused-branch condition in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid, so pre-SM89 GPUs take the existing eager-quantization fallback (the pre-#40785 path) instead of the fused fp8e4nv kernel. SM89+ keeps the fused fast path unchanged; SM86 / SM80 and other pre-SM89 arches fall back to eager quantization, which is exactly what worked before #407

title: [Fix] dsa: Refuse the trtllm backend at launch outside SM100/SM103/SM107
summary: ## Motivation On CUDA capability >= 10, `_dsa_split_backend_resolution` defaults the `trtllm` DSA backend (FP8 KV on both phases, BF16 KV on decode). summary: ## Motivation The weight cache builds a model on the meta device and replaces its parameters and buffers with tensors imported from the daemon. title: [Fix] disaggregation: fix HiSparse spec PD transfer on PP>1 prefill
summary: ## Bug HiSparse + speculative decoding + PD disaggregation on a `--pp-size > 1` prefill fails on the first request: every non-last pipeline stage raises ``` ValueError: HiSparse spec PD transfer requires an appended device-only draft KV buffer ``` inside `send_kvcache` (mooncake), killing that stage's transfer thread. All subsequent PD requests hang at 0 completions while `/health` stays 200. ## When it happens Mooncake PD with a spec-decoding decode engine and hisparse. Only the last prefill PP stage owns a draft runner, so non-last stages register `num_draft_entries = 0`; `send_kvcache` derives the host-backed vs device-only boundary in the receiver's `dst_kv_ptrs` from the local stage count and raises when it is 0. Any model whose weights exceed one node's HBM at the target TP forces PP>1 on the prefill (GLM-5.3 FP8 at TP8: 88.5 GB/GPU > 80 GB HBM), so production-shaped topologies hit this on the first request. The current CI does not reach this path (the hisparse PD test runs PP=1 with a dense prefill and no spec), and this is the destination-side boundary suggested during #37771 review. ## Fix The decode receiver ships its registered draft-entry count over the mooncake registration wire (one field appended after `dst_draft_rows_dcp_collapsed`, i.e. frame `msg[22]`; absent for peers that predate it), and `send_kvcache` takes the host-backed/device-only boundary from the destination's registration, falling back to the local count when the field is absent. summary: ## Summary When several requests reach an idle server together, the overlap scheduler admits the first request alone. title: [Fix] attention: Fix KDA prefill overflow past 2**31 token offsets
summary: _Produced by Hyperloom._ ## Motivation Three KDA prefill kernels build per-sequence row offsets entirely in int32. Once a sequence in a packed prefill starts past `2**31 / (H * K)` tokens, `bos * H * K` wraps. With H=32, K=128 per rank that is about 524k tokens (262k with H=64), which is reachable with a large or disabled `chunked_prefill_size`: - `chunk_local_cumsum_vector_kernel` (`cumsum.py`) and `kda_gate_chunk_cumsum_vector_kernel` (`kda.py`) load `bos` from `cu_seqlens` as int32, and `i_bh` is an int32 program id, so `(bos * H + i_h) * S` is int32. On MI300X both raise `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`. This is the first kernel `chunk_kda` runs, so the whole KDA prefill crashes. - `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_intra_token_parallel` (`chunk_intra_token_parallel.py`) computes `bos * H * K` in int32. It does not fault at this size; it reads and writes the wrong rows of `q/k/g/Aqk/Akk`. The other FLA prefill kernels also load `cu_seqlens` as int32, but there `i_h` comes from `tl.program_id(...).to(tl.int64)`, so `(bos * H + i_h) * K` is already promoted to int64 before the large multiply. This includes the rest of `kda.py`, `chunk_o.py`, `wy_fast.py`, `chunk_fwd.py` and `chunk_intra.py`. With the same packing, `chunk_gated_delta_rule` returns a bitwise-identical second sequence with or without this change. That corrects the note in #49803, which expected those kernels to overflow at about twice its threshold. ## Modifications - In the three kernels above, load `bos`/`eos` from `cu_seqlens` as int64, as upstream flash-linear-attention does. - Widen the program ids that feed the non-

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] DSA: Fix BF16 TileLang shared memory overflow on SM120
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50749. On RTX 5090 (SM120), BF16 TileLang DSA decode with `d_v=512` and a 64-wide RoPE tail crashes on the first decode step: ```text tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 170048 ``` The device allows 101376 bytes (99 KiB) of shared memory per block. The v2 kernel's two 64-row KV buffers alone need `2 * 64 * (512 + 64) * 2 = 147456` bytes (144 KiB), before Q and scratch buffers. Reducing the KV tile to 32 rows also requires fixing the cooperative loads: both producer loops hardcode four 16-row copies, so they still write 64 rows and cause illegal memory accesses. Q storage must also be bounded; reducing only the KV tile does not fit larger head counts. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/tilelang_kernel.py`: replace both fixed KV-loading loop bounds with `BI // 16` and require `block_I` to be a multiple of 16. Each block uses at most 18 KiB for Q and 72 KiB for KV, leaving room for scratch and barriers within the 99 KiB limit. Heads are split across blocks automatically, including a partial final tile, rather than selecting from a head-count whitelist. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_tilelang_dsa_bf16_small_tile.py`: cover the 32-row loader and public dispatch with partial head tiles, multiple query tokens and different topk values. summary: Co-authored-by: @HanHan009527 ## Summary **TL;DR: This PR lets the CUDA TileLang FP8 sparse decode split each query's top-k tiles into groups of any size that divides the tile count, not only halvings of it, as long as the GPU stays busy. For GLM-5.3-Flash, whose 2051-wide top-k pads to 66 tiles, attention DP8 decode with MTP 1/1/2 at 128 concurrent requests now splits each query into 6 groups instead of 33.** Fewer groups mean fewer partial results to write and merge. With one request at a time, the step time is the same or 0.7% lower, and TTFT stays within 1% of main. At 128 concurrent requests with MTP 1/1/2, the sparse decode attention kernels take **27% less GPU time** per call (1.36× faster). Per kernel call, across 8 to 64 heads per GPU and 4 to 200 query rows, this PR takes **8–27% less time** wherever it changes the split, and never more. With TP8 attention and MTP 5/1/6, the step time is up to 1.2% lower at 2 to 8 concurrent requests. title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Stop the schedulers only after every tokenizer worker drains
summary: ## Motivation With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, SIGTERM drops in-flight streams. Each tokenizer worker runs `sigterm_watchdog`, drains only its own `rid_to_state`, and then sends `ShutdownReq`. The schedulers are shared, so the first worker with nothing left to drain stops them, and the streams held by the other workers stop producing tokens. Their connections stay open until the process is SIGKILLed at the end of the termination grace period, so a rolling restart cuts every in-flight stream without `[DONE]`. ## Modifications - In multi-tokenizer mode, a tokenizer worker drains its own requests and exits without sending `ShutdownReq`. - The main process sends `ShutdownReq` (via `MultiTokenizerRouter.dispatch_to_scheduler`) after the uvicorn/granian supervisor returns, which happens once every worker has drained and exited, then waits for the schedulers and cleans up as the single-worker path does. - The process that holds the subprocess watchdog stops it, then sends `ShutdownReq` and waits for the schedulers; a process without one sends it only when it is a single-worker server (`tokenizer_ipc_name is None`). So single-worker servers and `Engine`/`RayEngine` parents (including Ray actors, which are not child processes) stop the schedulers, while HTTP tokenizer workers and `Engine.attach_tokenizer_worker()` processes only drain. - The router sends this `ShutdownReq` with `zmq.NOBLOCK`, so a main process whose schedulers are already gone does not block before cleanup. - Each uvicorn tokenizer worker gets a server stop hook (its `uvicorn.Server`, read from the SIGTERM handler

title: [Perf] HiSparse: Reduce redundant DSA index-K memory to increase decode capacity
summary: ## Motivation HiSparse currently reserves index-K memory for every DSA layer, including layers that reuse another layer’s top-k selection. This PR removes the redundant allocation, freeing GPU memory to support more concurrent decode requests. For GLM-5.2, **index-K storage layers decrease from 78 → 21. Consider a 8 RTX PRO 6000 D, total index-K memory across eight GPUs decreases from 160.88 → 43.31 GiB (−73.1%); MLA KV is unchanged.** Removing redundant index-K allocations raises the theoretical capacity for 256K-token resident contexts to the CPU KV budget limit of 145 requests, as shown below.

title: [Feat] scheduler: Share prompt KV among requests of one prefill batch
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48963 (same-forward sharing, the approach proposed there). SGLang inserts a request's KV into the radix tree only after its prefill result is processed, so requests admitted to one prefill batch with a common prompt each compute the whole prompt. RL rollouts hit this all the time: a GRPO group is N samples of one prompt, sent as N requests. So does any client that fans out samples as separate requests. `lpm`'s in-batch prefix caching only reorders the queue, and priority scheduling rules `lpm` out entirely. ``` 8 samples of one 1K-token prompt, admitted together main: one prefill batch, 8 x 1024 prompt tokens computed, cached_tokens = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] PR: one prefill batch, 1024 + 7 x (last page) computed, cached_tokens = [0, 960, 960, ...] (64-token pages) ``` #49147 holds duplicates until the first request's KV is cached instead. That costs the followers an extra forward. This PR shares within the same forward, which is what vLLM does by registering blocks at schedule time. ## Modifications New opt-in flag `--enable-in-batch-prefix-sharing`. Most of the logic lives in the new `mem_cache/in_batch_prefix_sharing.py`. 1. **Plan at admission** (`PrefixSharePlanner`, called around `PrefillAdder.add_one_req`). Before PrefillAdder prices a request, the planner looks for an already admitted request in the same namespace (`extra_key`, `cache_salt`, LoRA) that computes, in this forward, at least one full page past the request's own radix match. title: [Feat] dp-controller: Keep a routing key on one DP rank (--load-balance-method follow_routing_key)
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention each DP rank keeps its own prefix cache. A front door that sees only the engine, not its ranks (sgl-router's `sticky` policy, or a generic load balancer), keeps a session on one engine, but inside it the DP controller spreads the session's turns over every rank, so most turns miss their own history. The request already carries the key: the `x-sgl-routing-key` header becomes `routing_key` on the chat, completions and embeddings endpoints, and `/generate` takes `routing_key` in the body. The scheduler's routing-key policy reads it; the DP controller does not. ## Modifications - `--load-balance-method follow_routing_key`: a routing key's first request goes to the DP rank `total_requests` would choose, and every later request with that key goes to the same rank. - A request without a key, or with an empty one, is balanced like `total_requests`, and `routed_dp_rank` still takes precedence. A key whose rank has gone inactive is placed again, as a new key would be. - `GenerateReqInput` and `EmbeddingReqInput` copy `routing_key` into each item, so batched and `n > 1` requests keep their key, as the Rust server already does. - The controller remembers the 65,536 most recently used keys, by hash, so the bound also holds memory for long keys; a forgotten key's next request is balanced anew. - `server_arguments.mdx` lists the method and says what it does. ## Accuracy Tests No change to the model or to any other load-balance method. `test_data_parallel_controller.py` adds `TestFollowRoutingKeyScheduler`: - `test_a_new_key_goes_to_the_least_loaded_rank_and

title: [Feat] api.v1: Add opt-in administrative Shutdown RPC
summary: ## Motivation A separate runtime sidecar using native `api.v1` needs to request engine shutdown without a shared PID namespace. #38075 tracks this operability gap. A closed Generate stream or an RPC acknowledgement must not be mistaken for scheduler retirement or process exit. **A central part of this PR is adding P/D support to the existing native Rust graceful-drain path.** The Shutdown RPC reuses the existing SIGTERM lifecycle. For supported P/D configurations, a normal drain additionally waits for frontend pipeline work, every scheduler request queue, and owned KV-transfer work to settle. This is why the change touches the Rust request/drain core, Python Scheduler, and KV-transfer lifecycle. ## Changes - Implement `SglangService.Shutdown` and generate the Rust/Python bindings with the repository generator; bump `sglang-api-types` to 0.3.0. - Require explicit `SGLANG_ENABLE_NATIVE_SHUTDOWN_RPC=1`, a nonempty `--admin-api-key` bearer credential, and the expected `GetServerInfo.instance_id`. The inference key does not grant this administrative operation. - Enter the existing native SIGTERM drain, including listener close, parent-supervisor notification and scheduler teardown. Refuse before mutation unless the launcher installed that ownership path. Keep unified single-node, single-DP serving without DP attention, and add per-engine prefill/decode shutdown for the bounded P/D configuration below. - Authenticate the listener-close notification with Linux `SCM_CREDENTIALS` and the launcher's registered listener PID list. title: [Fix] deps: Raise fastokens floor to >=0.3.5 to avoid an HTTP-process deadlock
summary: ## Motivation With `--tokenizer-backend fastokens`, the HTTP server can deadlock and never recover (#45310). fastokens 0.3.3 and 0.3.4 have a GIL / lock-order inversion: `encode_batch` takes the GIL back while still holding the tokenizer's state read lock, and `enable_padding` / `no_padding` / `enable_truncation` wait for the write lock with the GIL held (crusoecloud/fastokens#84). SGLang hits both sides on one tokenizer: a text request encodes on an executor thread while a multimodal request runs the HF processor with `padding=True` on the event loop. `/health` then stops answering until the process is restarted. fastokens 0.3.5 fixes it (crusoecloud/fastokens#85). The floor is `>=0.3.2`, so whatever was newest when an image was built gets installed; v0.5.22 images ship 0.3.4. This PR raises the floor to `>=0.3.5`. #45312 removes the SGLang-side write for the multimodal path. This floor covers every caller, including the truncation writer reported in crusoecloud/fastokens#84. ## Modifications - `python/pyproject.toml`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`: `fastokens>=0.3.2` → `fastokens>=0.3.5` (lower bound only, as before). ## Accuracy Tests - Deadlock repro on CPU, Gemma 4 31B-it tokenizer: one thread loops `encode` on ~100 KB of text while the main thread loops the HF processor (image + text). 0.3.4 hangs on the first iteration with the stacks from #45310; 0.3.6 runs 180 s clean (89k encodes). Same with padding/truncation changes in place of the processor call: 2.4M calls, no hang. - Serving: Gemma 4 31B-it FP8 on 2×H200 (TP2), v0.5.22, fastokens 0.3.4, mixed image + long-tex

title: [Feat] weight-cache: Use IPC only for the speculative target
summary: ## [Feat] Use Weight Cache only for the target model during speculative decoding ### Motivation and changes The Weight Cache Daemon publishes target weights, but its configuration applies to the whole service. If a draft runner inherits the target’s IPC configuration, it connects to the same owner and requests draft weights that the owner never published. SGLang previously rejected the combination of Weight Cache and speculative decoding at startup. This PR makes the loading decision per runner and enables target-only Weight Cache for **EAGLE, EAGLE3, DSpark, STANDALONE, NGRAM, and DFLASH**. - **Target and draft loading.** The target runner attaches to the owner’s prepared weights through IPC. Each draft runner uses its configured checkpoint loader with cache mode `off` and no cache socket. IPC loader selection and weight CPU-backup policy both follow the runner-local configuration. - **Native weight sharing.** EAGLE-family drafts retain their existing target embedding and LM-head bindings. STANDALONE keeps its own draft weights. NGRAM uses only the target runner. - **DFLASH write isolation.** When `mask_embedding.pt` supplies a trained mask embedding, each rank that owns the target row takes a private copy of its local IPC storage before applying the update. Tied embedding and LM-head weights retain their `Parameter` identity. The owner and other clients continue to see the original weights. Startup without a mask attachment incurs no copy. - **Tied parameter slots.** If two exported names resolve to one tied parameter slot, they must describe the same storage view. ### Wh

title: [Feat] diffusion: [sglang-miles] Roll out the LTX-2 audio stream as a named extra stream
summary: ## Motivation A rollout applies the RL transition (SDE/CPS/ODE step, per-step log-probs, noisy-latent trajectory) to one latent stream: the one the denoise loop iterates. Joint models denoise more streams in the same loop (LTX-2: video + audio), and those streams could not be rolled out. This PR lets a rollout request name extra streams to roll out, with the LTX-2 audio stream as the first one: ```json {"rollout": true, "rollout_extra_streams": ["audio"], "rollout_return_dit_trajectory": true} ``` It is based on https://github.com/JingwenGu0829/sglang/pull/6 by JingwenGu0829 (the LTX-2 audio commit of this PR is authored by her), rebased onto `sglang-miles` and reworked so that the rollout request, hooks and data are generic over streams; only the LTX-2 modules roll out audio. title: SGLang 1.0 Release Tracker
summary: SGLang 1.0 is a stability release. The work focuses on hardening existing functionality, replacing silent configuration changes with errors that name the setting, and defining a compatibility policy for the 1.x series. Upgrading from 0.5.x may require changes; see [Upgrade notes](#upgrade-notes). This issue tracks progress toward the release, and the sections below are kept current. ## What SGLang offers These capabilities are available in 0.5.x. 1.0 makes them more reliable; apart from the models under New model support, it does not add new ones. ### Performance - Overlap scheduling and multi-stream execution - CUDA graph support, including breakable and full-graph capture - Rust implementations of the radix tree, the router, and an experimental frontend server - A runtime built around prefix sharing - Speculative decoding ### Production serving - Aggregated and prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated serving - Parallelism support: TP, DP, EP, PP, DCP, PCP, and SP - HiCache, Linker, and HiSparse - Unified memory ### Multimodal generation - SGLang Diffusion in the same package and CLI, with native pipelines for image, video, 3D, world, and action models - Composable multi-GPU parallelism: CFG, TP, sequence parallelism, and DP - Request-level quality tiers - Component residency and layerwise offload, from consumer GPUs to multi-GPU servers - OpenAI-compatible image and video API, a Python SDK, and a ComfyUI plugin ### Multiple platform support - NVIDIA (Hopper, Blackwell, Grace Blackwell, Vera Rubin), AMD Instinct, Intel Xeon and XPU, Ascend NPU, PPU, and MUSA ## Release principle

title: [Feat] sgl-router: Route DeepSeek image chats by prefix cache
summary: > **Depends on #46562.** This uses `ChatFormatter::encode_multimodal_request` from that PR, so it builds only on top of it. It is a draft until #46562 merges; then I will rebase, and the diff stays as it is now (`sgl-router/` only). ## Motivation Cache-aware routing finds a prompt's cached prefix by hashing the router's own tokenization of the request and matching it against the block hashes engines publish as KV events. For DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1, the router renders chats through `sglang-processor`, whose text-only path refuses images (`image input is not supported for this model`). The router then falls back to hashing the raw message text. Those hashes never match the engine's blocks, so every chat that carries an image is routed as if nothing were cached. In agent workloads an image (a screenshot, a `read_image` result) stays in the history for the rest of the conversation, so all its later turns scatter across workers and re-prefill context that another worker already holds. #46562 lets `sglang-processor` render DeepSeek image chats (`encode_multimodal_request`), for the Rust server. Two things are still missing on the routing side: 1. **The router never uses it.** `encode_chat` calls `encode_request`, which still refuses images. 2. **Rendering alone stops at the first image.** The engine turns each image into token ids derived from its preprocessed pixels (`pad_value`), which the router does not reproduce. title: [Fix] [AMD] GLM-5.3-Flash: Let breakable prefill graphs replay cached-prefix extends
summary: ## Summary On MI355X, GLM-5.3-Flash with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` never replays a prefill graph for an extend with a cached prefix, which is almost every agentic turn. Those extends run eager. Off CUDA, the prefill graph runner sends any extend with a prefix to eager unless the attention backend is DSA, because DSA stays on sparse MLA inside the graph. It is read only off CUDA (`not is_cuda()`), so CUDA keeps current behaviour. Only models whose hybrid backend wraps DSA change, and of those only GLM-5.3-Flash did not already replay. The KDA extend kernel inside the graph is main's (#51000 captures the gfx950 HIP `kda_prefill_gfx950` with padded rows); this PR does not touch it. title: [Fix] speculative: Reject non-greedy requests DFLASH would verify greedily
summary: ## Motivation DFLASH verifies non-greedy requests by greedy argmax when it cannot verify them by sampling, after a one-time warning. The client asked for `temperature > 0` and silently gets greedy output. Reject these requests with an error that names the setting instead, as requested by the predictable-configuration item in #50045. Refs #50045 (DFLASH verifies requests with temperature > 0 greedily when non-greedy verification is unavailable on the device). Related: #42828 adds an opt-in `SGLANG_SPEC_REQUIRE_EXACT_SAMPLING` that raises at the same fallback point for DFLASH and EAGLE. This PR rejects at admission by default instead, per the 1.0 rule; the EAGLE part of #42828 is unaffected. ## Modifications - Add `DFlashWorkerV2.supports_sampling_verify()`, false exactly when `_accept_block` verifies non-greedy rows by argmax: a selector draft with selector sampling off (Ascend), or a draft with no sampled head on a device without the sampling verify kernel. A Domino draft proposes by greedy rollout and never uses a selector or LiLiCorr head, so it counts as supported only with the kernel. - The scheduler caches `dflash_greedy_verify_only` after building the draft worker and returns 400 at admission for a request with `top_k > 1`: `This DFLASH server only supports greedy sampling (temperature=0 or top_k=1), got temperature=1.0.` A PD prefill server skips the check: it never verifies, and its non-last PP stages hold no draft. - `_validate_phase1_sampling_support` keeps its one-time warning for batches that still reach the fallback, using the same predicate. - `validate_spec_s

title: [Fix] scheduler: Count the unprefilled part of a chunked request in total_tokens load
summary: ## Motivation With `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the smallest `num_total_tokens`. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens", but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill. That request holds KV only for the chunks it has already run, and it is in neither the running batch nor the waiting queue. So a rank that has just started a 64K-token prompt reports only about one chunk of load, and new requests keep going to it. We saw this on 2×H20 with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP=2, `--attn-dp-size 2`, FA3, FP8 KV, and `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` (4096 per rank). The traffic was 30 short requests (1024 in / 96 out) plus one 32K and one 64K prompt. When the 32K prompt arrived first, both long prompts went to different ranks as expected. The rank prefilling the 64K prompt then also received 24 of the 30 short requests, which gave a 38,912 / 90,112 input-token split. When the 64K prompt arrived first, the bug was not triggered and the split was 68,608 / 60,416. `SchedulerLoadInquirer._get_num_pending_tokens()` already adds the chunked request's `seqlen - prefix_len`; `num_total_tokens` did not. ## Modifications - `load_inquirer.py`: add the chunked request's remaining tokens (`seqlen - prefix_len`) to `num_total_tokens`, and so also to `num_active_tokens`. The prefix it has already run is counted in `num_used_tokens`, as before. - `test_load_inquirer.py`: two unit tests for `get_loads()`, with and without a chunked request. The new chunked case fails on main (`300 != 340`) and passes with this

title: [Perf] dllm: Run several denoise forwards per scheduled FDFO round
summary: ## Motivation Under FDFO, one scheduler round is one denoise forward. Everything the round does around that forward — committing resolved blocks, admitting waiting requests, processing results, rebuilding the batch — is paid once per forward. dLLM also disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so that host work is exposed directly as device idle rather than hidden behind the next forward. At large batch this is a real share of the step: the forward itself is the only part that scales with the model, while the round overhead is roughly fixed. ## Modifications `SGLANG_DLLM_FDFO_STEPS_PER_ROUND` (new, default `1` = today's behavior) makes a round issue N denoise forwards instead of one. The batch is frozen for the inner steps: rows that resolve mid-round freeze themselves inside the step, and commits, admissions and result processing all happen once at the end of the round. The per-round host work is therefore amortized over N forwards. Two hooks are added to `DllmAlgorithm` so an algorithm can keep its per-request state in batched device tensors for the whole round (`fdfo_batched_begin` / `fdfo_batched_step` / `fdfo_batched_all_finished`), which is what makes an inner step cost no host gather/scatter. `JointThreshold` implements them; an algorithm that returns `None` from `fdfo_batched_begin` gets a plain loop with the same semantics, which is the path non-NPU dLLM runs today. The round still exits early once every row has resolved, so a short round does not issue no-op forwards. That probe costs one scalar s

title: [Perf] dllm: Schedule prefill and decode rows into one mixed round
summary: ## Motivation The dLLM scheduler builds every round from a single phase. `_process_dllm_batches` takes every prefill-phase row it can find, and only when there are none does it fall back to decode-phase rows: ```python prefill_reqs = self.dllm_manager.get_prefill_requests() if prefill_reqs: ... # prefill-phase rows only else: ... # decode-phase rows only ``` So a round is all prompt chunks or all denoise blocks, never both. A round's row budget is `--max-running-requests` blocks; when the phase that wins a round cannot fill that budget, the rest of it goes unused and the other phase's rows wait a whole round for their next forward — even though the batch had room for them and they are the same shape. Whether that costs anything depends entirely on the **arrival pattern**, and the honest summary is that it is sometimes nothing and sometimes very large: - when every request arrives at once, all of them march through the phases in lockstep, there is nothing to mix, and this change does nothing; - under continuous arrival with prompts long enough to span many block-size chunks, some rows are always in a prefill phase while others are in a decode phase, and the either/or scheduler spends most of its rounds on batches it cannot fill. Arrival pattern is not observable at scheduling time, so there is no threshold that could pick between the two. The change is therefore opt-in, behind an env var that defaults to today's behavior. ## Modifications All of it is in `dllm/mixin/scheduler.py`, behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_DLLM_MIXED_BATCH` (default off). `_process_dllm_batches` gains one branch

title: [Feat] hicache: Add unified Engram store and support Qwen4-Exp
summary: ## Motivation Add a **unified Engram store abstraction to HiCache**, and support **Qwen4-Exp as its first model integration**. HiCache provides a common interface for storing and looking up immutable Engram tables. Models supply row IDs and interpret the returned bytes, while storage backends handle table ownership and data access. This separates model computation from the storage implementation and gives Engram integrations a shared storage contract. This PR introduces the HiCache abstraction, implements a local backend using [Mooncake EngramStore](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4701), and connects Qwen4-Exp PLE N-gram tables to it. The storage interface is model-independent; Qwen4-Exp is the only model integrated and validated in this PR. This supersedes #44521. ## Modifications - **Add the HiCache Engram store interface.** `HiCacheEngramStorage` defines `initialize(rows)`, `lookup(ids)`, and `close()` for immutable byte-row tables. It is defined at the end of `hicache_storage.py`, with row-based semantics independent of the existing KV interface. `sglang.srt.mem_cache.engram.create_storage` creates row storage within the Engram module, independently of a KV cache or host KV pool. - **Add the Mooncake backend.** `MooncakeEngramStorage` implements the HiCache interface over Mooncake EngramStore, including owned local snapshots and CUDA stream-ordered lookup. The embedding adapter uses the HiCache storage contract. - **Support Qwen4-Exp.** Route its PLE N-gram embedding construction through the shared adapter. title: [Feat] [NPU] DSV4.1: Support DeepSeek-V4.1 on Ascend A5
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 changes the KV pipeline relative to V4 in every layer: compression runs at ratios 1/2 (instead of 4/128), the indexer becomes two-level (level-1 block candidates, level-2 QSLI rescore within them), cache rows switch to two quantized formats (window FP8 E4M3 g32, compressed packed FP4 E2M1 g16), and mHC residual mixing moves into fused ops. The NPU backend only served V4: ratio 4/128, one indexer level, and the 584-byte A5 row. title: [Feat] [AMD] moe: Fuse GLM-5.2 routing with the AITER MoE sort
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, every GLM-5.2 MoE layer runs four small kernels between the router GEMM and the first expert GEMM: upcast the bf16 logits to fp32, aiter `biased_grouped_topk`, append the fused shared expert, and aiter `moe_sorting` (which also zeroes the `fused_moe` output). At decode and MTP-verify sizes these take about 21 µs per layer, and they run in all 78 target layers plus every draft step. This PR does all of that in one JIT kernel, `glm_route_sort`. It routes, appends the shared expert, writes the exact sort `fused_moe` would compute under the EP expert mask, and zeroes the output buffer. The sort is handed to aiter's `fused_moe` as a presort, so it skips `moe_sorting`. Per call, this drops from 21.1 µs to 7.7 µs. **Result** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4/EP4, MI355X, AgentX; baseline = same stack with the env off): | Conc | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | P90 TTFT (s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 158.7 → **173.4** (+9.3%) | 6,845 → 6,794 (−0.7%) | 0.794 → 0.805 | 5.28 → **4.88** (−7.5%) | | 8 | 113.9 → **117.6** (+3.2%) | 11,734 → 11,857 (+1.0%) | 0.744 → 0.750 | 6.84 → **6.24** (−8.8%) | Decode gets 7–9% faster at both concurrencies. Throughput and TTFT move within run-to-run noise (about 3%), as expected for a decode-only change at low concurrency. Depends on sgl-project/sglang#43126 (`aiter_presort`) and the companion aiter PR (plain-layout presort for `fused_moe`). ## New environment variables | Variable | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_GLM_ROUTE_SORT` | `false` | Turns on the fused GLM route+sort on

title: [Bug] `extend_attention_fwd_unified` reads the wrong tree-mask bits on sliding-window layers
summary: ### Describe the bug `extend_attention_fwd_unified` is the extend kernel that the Triton backend uses for all extend batches when deterministic inference is on ([triton_backend.py#L1913-L1915](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1913-L1915)). In target-verify batches it gets the speculative tree mask (`custom_mask`). Each mask row has `seq_len + num_draft` columns. On a sliding-window layer the KV rail holds only the last `min(seq_len, W)` prefix keys, from column `seq_len - W`. The kernel reads the mask as `custom_mask[row * cur_seq_kv_len + n]`, where `cur_seq_kv_len` is the rail length plus the drafts ([extend_attention.py#L1376-L1384](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py#L1376-L1384)). It has no window-offset input, and `_forward_extend_unified` passes the full mask ([triton_backend.py#L2412-L2419](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L2412-L2419)). For `seq_len > W`, both the row stride and the column origin are wrong: prefix bits (all True) are read as draft-to-draft bits, so drafts attend to drafts that are not their ancestors. For `seq_len <= W` the result is correct. `_fwd_kernel` handles the same case with `window_kv_offsets` ([extend_attention.py#L555-L560](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/op

title: [Feat] http_server: Compress response bodies for clients that accept zstd
summary: ## Motivation Responses that carry routed experts, sampling masks or top logprobs run to megabytes per request. A client in another region, or behind a proxy that bills egress per byte, pays for every one. SGLang decompresses zstd request bodies (`SGLANG_ENABLE_REQUEST_DECOMPRESSION`) but never compresses a response. This adds the standard HTTP negotiation for responses: the client lists `zstd` in `Accept-Encoding` and the server answers with `Content-Encoding: zstd` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, which curl, httpx, aiohttp and requests decode on their own when their zstd support is installed. It is the zstd counterpart of Starlette's `GZipMiddleware`, opt-in like request decompression, since clients on the same host that advertise zstd would otherwise have every large response compressed for nothing. ## Modifications - `http_response_compression.py`: `ResponseCompressionMiddleware`, a pure-ASGI middleware beside `RequestDecompressionMiddleware`. It compresses a response body when the request's `Accept-Encoding` lists zstd (`q=0` refuses it), the body arrives whole in one message of at least 64 KiB, and the response has no `Content-Encoding` yet. Streamed responses and small bodies pass through. It sets `Content-Encoding`, `Content-Length` and `Vary`, and compresses in the executor, off the event loop. - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_ENABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION`, default off, next to `SGLANG_ENABLE_REQUEST_DECOMPRESSION`. - `http_server.py`: mounts the middleware when the variable is set, as it does request decompression. The Rust server can follow in its own PR, as request decompres

title: [Perf] [AMD] frontend: Encode long Qwen3.5-family chat prompts in parallel
summary: ## Motivation `parallel_prompt_encode` (#41259) cuts a long rendered chat prompt at added tokens and, for the GLM / Llama-3 pre-tokenizer only, at pre-token boundaries inside long gaps, then encodes the pieces with `encode_batch`. Qwen3.5-family tokenizers (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8: NFC normalizer + the Qwen3.5 split regex) get neither benefit for a single long message: - the intra-gap cuts are refused (different regex, and a normalizer is present), so a 100k-token message is one piece; - these models are multimodal, and SGLang sets `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` for them, so `encode_batch` runs serially anyway and the CPU-time probe switches the helper off for the process. On a 100k-200k token chat request, tokenization alone then takes 0.15-0.32 s on the request path before prefill starts. Related: #44392 (open) extends the intra-gap cuts to the Qwen2 / Qwen3, Qwen3.5, o200k and DeepSeek-V3 pre-tokenizers under NFC, with the same regex and the same NFC argument as the first item below. It does not have the thread pool, so on Qwen3.5-family models (multimodal, `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false`) the pieces are still encoded one after the other. The measured gain needs both parts: the cuts make the pieces and the pool encodes them in parallel. If #44392 lands first, I'll rebase this PR onto it and keep only the thread pool. ## Modifications - Accept the Qwen3.5 split regex (letter runs include combining marks, single digits) and an NFC normalizer for the intra-gap cuts. summary: Part of #49944 ("Support priority-based request preemption" under Correctness and Robustness). ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory`, the scheduler turned priority preemption off (the `TODO(ch-wan)` in `Scheduler.init_schedule_policy`). `PrefillAdder.preempt_to_schedule` picked victims by `rem_total_tokens`, and a unified budget has no remaining token count: `ChainPrefillBudget._available_and_evictable` raises on it. title: [Feat] elastic-ep: Runtime scale-down that retires EP ranks via Mooncake deactivate_ranks
summary: ## Motivation Elastic EP today grows a serving deployment and recovers a rank that has dropped out. This PR adds the third direction: **retiring live ranks from a deployment that keeps serving**. Both directions are expressed on the same `active_ranks` bitmask, so a shrink and a later grow are the same mask operation viewed from opposite ends, and a deployment can move freely between widths under an orchestrator's control. The driving use case is a Kubernetes reconciler reclaiming GPUs from an underloaded deployment (Dynamo DEP #13121, RFC #35376, raised by @julienmancuso). That needs three things from a shrink: in flight requests finish, the interruption is small enough not to read as an outage, and the orchestrator gets a positive "this rank may now be terminated" signal rather than having to infer it from a process exit. title: [Feat] model-loader: Add model-aware checkpoint shard selection for Qwen MTP
summary: ## Motivation Closes #43196. A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside `load_weights`, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files. On whole-file paths, an unnecessary shard may already have been read into memory before the model discards its tensors. Following [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152), this PR extracts existing model-owned selection rules into a reusable interface and excludes wholly unused shards before weight-payload reads and prefetch. This avoids unnecessary reads, memory copies, and tensor iteration. The same need arose in [ModelExpress #805](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/issues/805). Keeping the rules in SGLang lets native loaders and downstream integrations share one implementation, instead of requiring MX to duplicate architecture-specific checkpoint naming rules and keep them synchronized with upstream changes. ## Modifications 1. **Model-owned weight selection.** Add an optional `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` hook. It receives a raw checkpoint tensor name and returns `True` when the model does not use that weight. Pre-read selection and `load_weights` share the same rule, preserving shared weights and pipeline-parallel embedding requirements. 2. **Select files before Default Loader reads.** Pass the rule through `Source.is_unused_weight`, inspect safetensors headers, and retain a shard whenever it contains at least one required tensor. summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` routes **every plain extend (prefill)** through the Triton `unified_attention` kernel: ```python if self.use_triton_unified_attention: # unified_attention has no head_dim cap; route extend through it # so Gemma-4's 512-wide full-attention layers don't hit the CK # `head dimension at most 256` assert. return self._forward_extend_unified(...) ``` The comment says the route exists for Gemma-4's 512-wide heads, but the condition does not check the head dim. title: [Perf] pp: Defer steady decode output packing until after forward submission
summary: ## Motivation In pipeline-parallel disaggregated decode, collecting and sending the previous microbatch's token output can delay submission of the next forward. This draft moves steady-state token-delta packing and IPC behind that submission, while keeping request cursor updates on the scheduler thread. Base: `d89bc5b57477d89ab1411264599b153b6e34e78d`. Candidate: `f96f7e2f3f88b75aea73a88aae0b625bc432d367`. This is a port of an archived experiment to the current output protocol. It is not the archived patch applied verbatim. Current upstream already sends headers and request statistics only when needed and uses a flat token buffer, so its remaining opportunity is smaller. **The archived performance numbers below are not benchmarks of this PR against main.** ## Modifications - For ordinary, nonterminal decode batches with headers and statistics already delivered, advance streaming cursors and retain owned token slices and scalar counts. Pack them through the existing accumulator and wire-payload builder after the next forward submission. - Keep at most one deferred output per sender. Immediate outputs, including terminal messages and detokenizer-state releases, drain it first to preserve FIFO order. The PP loop also drains it on idle, paused and prebuilt iterations, before output exchange can block. - Enable this internal scheduling path only in PP disaggregated decode with asynchronous batch depth zero. First outputs, finishes, retractions, grammar, beam search, speculative decoding, auxiliary/custom outputs, the Rust frontend and skip-tokenizer mode keep their existing path

summary: ## Motivation Under DP attention every DP rank publishes its own `ForwardPassMetrics` (FPM) stream, one message per step, and a consumer (the Dynamo planner) combines the ranks of one worker. Nothing in a message says which step it belongs to: `counter_id` is a per-rank publisher sequence that also advances on heartbeats. A consumer that reads "the latest message of each rank" can therefore combine rows of different steps, or a measured row with an idle heartbeat. In the validation runs below, that latest-per-rank view held rows of different steps for 2.6% to 8.9% of busy time with 2 DP ranks and 7.9% to 16.5% with 4 (the ranks' messages for one step arrive 0.06 to 2 ms apart at p50 and up to 66 ms apart at worst). This PR adds an optional `iteration_id` to `ForwardPassMetrics`. For a step that the attention-DP ranks launch together, every rank's message carries the same id, so a consumer can group messages by `(worker_id, iteration_id)` and use a set once every rank reported it. ## Modifications - `ForwardPassMetrics.iteration_id: Optional[int] = None`, appended last. `FPM_VERSION` stays 1: a message is a msgpack map keyed by field name (the struct sets neither `array_like` nor `forbid_unknown_fields`), so a consumer built before the field ignores it. The docstring said "positional encoding", which is not what the struct selects; corrected. - The id comes from the per-step MLP-sync gather, which already makes all attention-DP ranks agree on whether a step launches. title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM-5.3-Flash: Small-M MoE kernel and sort-fused MXFP4 quant for decode
summary: ## Summary At small decode batches, the routed experts of a GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 MoE layer take **five** kernels. A sort groups tokens by expert, and each of the two expert GEMMs needs an FP4 quant first. The sort and the two quants cost half as much as the GEMMs. Both changes are on by default: 1. SGLang already has a gfx950 small-batch MoE kernel. It reads BF16 activations directly, so it needs no sort and no quant. GLM-5.3-Flash now uses it. 2. For somewhat larger batches, the sort also writes the first FP4 quant, bit-exact with aiter. This removes one quant kernel. | Routed MoE, decode batch 4 | baseline (µs) | this PR (µs) | | --- | --- | --- | | sort | 4.40 `_moe_sorting_small_kernel` | — | | stage-1 + stage-2 FP4 quant | 3.88 + 3.88 `fused_mx_quant_moe_sort_kernel` | — | | gate/up + SiLU | 15.38 moe1 | 14.78 `smallm_p1_i512_c16` | | down | 7.98 moe2 | 10.26 `smallm_p2_i512_s8` | | **per layer (×42)** | **5 kernels, 35.52** | **2 kernels, 25.04** | ## Scope gfx950 MXFP4 MoE on the aiter runner, decode only. CUDA and other AMD GPUs do not change. The small-batch kernel adds one shape: per-GPU intermediate 512 with 8 or 9 top-k slots (top-8, plus the fused shared expert), up to decode batch 16. Larger batches and other shapes stay on aiter. The sort change needs batch × top-k ≤ 256 and a hidden size divisible by 2048: batch 17 to 28 with 9 slots, 17 to 32 with 8. It covers any MXFP4 MoE with SiLU or GELU and separate gate/up. `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0` still turns off the small-batch kernel. ## Test plan Baseline `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x-20260928` (sglang `0318

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] cuda-graph: Prefill CUDA graphs for FlashInfer CuTe DSL MoE and MegaMoE
summary: ## Motivation The FlashInfer CuTe DSL MoE (`flashinfer_cutedsl`, NVFP4 W4A4 and W4A16) and FlashInfer MegaMoE W4A16 (`flashinfer_megamoe`) integrations (#28354, #35120, #43789, #44036) were validated with prefill CUDA graphs disabled: their e2e tests passed `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, and the CuTe DSL tests never ran the full-model EXTEND autotune pass. This PR runs those tests with breakable prefill CUDA graphs (BCG; the default backend, passed explicitly for the Nemotron-H classes), runs the CuTe DSL GSM8K tests with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND=1`, and fixes the gaps that blocked, broke, or silently disabled either one. ## Modifications - **MegaMoE prefill graphs:** add `flashinfer_megamoe` to the BCG a2a allowlist in `disable_breakable_cudagraph_if_incompatible`. Before, any server using it fell back to eager prefill ("unvalidated a2a backend"). MegaMoE keeps the generic DP contract: a DP prefill graph batch is padded to one shared MAX_LEN bucket on every rank (an idle rank runs a dummy extend of that bucket), so every rank's captured MegaMoE call uses the same workspace profile; the per-rank SUM_LEN replay in `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len` stays DeepGEMM-`megamoe`-only. - **BCG under the memory saver:** `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` raised `NotImplementedError` with `--enable-memory-saver` + `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, which is why the RL reload test disabled prefill graphs. `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` now takes an optional `segment_capture` context factory that captures each segment; in memory-saver mode it is `torch_memory_saver`'s pauseab

title: [Feat] glm5_next: Support LayerNorm sequence parallelism
summary: ## Motivation With TP attention every rank runs GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC (`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`, `mhc_post`, the `hc_prenorm` GEMM) on all token rows, since the residual stream is replicated. On the 8x H200 TP8 proxy below that is 81 ms of rank 0's 651 ms of GPU time for a 128K cold prefill, the same work on all 8 ranks. `--enable-layernorm-sp` already keeps the residual on 1/tp of the rows for Qwen3, Qwen4Exp and Muse. mHC only mixes the `hc_mult` streams of one token, and `residual/mhc.py` declares the same update facts as the gated residual Qwen4Exp runs under SP, so the boundary needs no change. What's missing is the GLM decoder layer running attention and the FFN on gathered rows. I also tried `--enable-attn-tp-input-scattered`, since GLM's forward goes through `maybe_input_scattered`. With the default breakable prefill graphs it doesn't change the mHC work: on a 2x H200 TP2 proxy (main 424fa3c8b7), 32K cold prefill, mHC was 20.14 ms by default and 20.09 ms with it, GPU busy 296.4 / 296.8 ms. This is for the TP-attention cells. With DP attention each rank already does mHC only for its own requests; I didn't compare against DP attention. ## Modifications - `Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward`: under SP, attention (KDA and MLA/DSA) and the FFN run through `run_replicated_token_rows` on the gathered rows and hand back this rank's rows. KDA, the DSA indexer and the MoE see exactly the sequence rows (`total_rows=positions.shape[-1]`). - MLA reads its QKV latent from the attention inputs the boundary cached on this rank's rows, so the SP closure points them at the gathered rows.

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Read the KV layout of the pool wrapped by HybridLinearKVPool
summary: _Produced by Hyperloom._ ## Motivation With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, a hybrid linear attention model (Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next) fails on its first prefill on the aiter backend: ``` File ".../hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 1567, in forward_extend return self.full_attn_backend.forward_extend( File ".../aiter_backend.py", line 5489, in forward_extend o = mha_batch_prefill_func( ... RuntimeError: if page_block_size > 1, must pass kv_last_page_lens to kernel ``` `MHATokenToKVPool` allocates the full-attention KV in the 5D layout, but `AiterAttnBackend` decides the layout through `_kv_cache_is_vectorized_5d(model_runner.token_to_kv_pool)`. For these models that pool is the `HybridLinearKVPool` composite. The helper only resolves the wrapped view when the router has a sliding-window sub-pool. `HybridLinearKVPool` routes its full-attention layers to a single FULL sub-pool, so the helper reads `kv_cache_layout` off the composite, which does not have one, and falls back to `"nhd"`. The backend then runs the NHD prefill and decode paths on a 5D pool. ## Modifications - `_kv_cache_is_vectorized_5d` reads the FULL view's layout whenever the router has a FULL sub-pool, not only when it also has a window sub-pool. A plain pool's FULL view is the pool itself, and pools with a window sub-pool resolve the same view as before. - `test/registered/amd/test_aiter_vectorized_5d_decode.py`: add `TestAiterVectorized5DHybridLinearDecode`, the existing 5D GSM8K test on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`. The model scores about 0.2 (MI355X) to 0.33 (MI300X) on the default NHD

title: [Perf] [AMD] spec: Sort-free top-p and many-row softmax for HIP verify
summary: ## Summary On ROCm, EAGLE with topk=1 turns on rejection sampling by default. Each verify step then runs a temperature softmax and a top-p renorm over `bs × num_draft_tokens` target rows. For GLM-5.3-Flash (vocab 154880, 6 draft tokens) at concurrency 64 that is 384 rows, and both steps were slow: 1. Top-p found the cutoff with a full `torch.sort` and `cumsum`. It now bisects on the fp32 bit patterns, which order like int32 for non-negative values: 10 passes, no sort. 2. The split softmax stopped at 32 rows and fell back to `torch.softmax`. It now covers any row count. | Kernel (µs), rows × 154880 | 48 rows base | this PR | 384 rows base | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | top-p renorm | 927 | **116** | 4426 | **739** | | temperature softmax | 75 | **19** | 261 | **129** | ## Scope HIP only; CUDA is unchanged. Top-p keeps the same rule (keep every token at or above the pivot, ties included) and can differ from the sort by one token only when the cutoff is within fp32 rounding; the denominator sums the kept tokens, so rows sum to 1 even for tiny top_p. Top-k still sorts. The softmax block is capped at 4096 to avoid register spills; other vocab sizes do not regress (softmax time, this PR / base, MI355X, CUDA graph): | Vocab | Model | 1–32 rows | 33–1024 rows (base = `torch.softmax`) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 129280 | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 0.77–0.86 | 0.26–0.56 | | 151936 | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 0.70–0.86 | 0.22–0.55 | | 154880 | GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash | 0.70–0.86 | 0.22–0.54 | | 163840 | Kimi-K3 | 0.71–0.86 | 0.23–0.54 | | 200064 | MiniMax-M3 | 0

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv41: Sparse attention on aiter opus for the V41_NEW KV layout (4/5)
summary: ## Motivation On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse attention runs the triton `_sparse_mla` kernel. aiter's opus `mla_sparse_prefill_v41` is faster for both decode and prefill, but it needs the token-interleaved V4.1 KV layout. ## Modifications - With `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT=v41_new SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESSED_KV_LAYOUT=fp8`, HIP accepts the token-interleaved V4.1 caches (528 B rows). Every `aiter_sparse` attention call then goes to aiter `mla_sparse_prefill_v41`: MXFP8 q, the compressed cache as prefix source, the SWA cache as extend source, and CSR row lists, with the SWA CSR built once a forward. - aiter dependency: `aiter.ops.mla_sparse_prefill.mla_sparse_prefill_v41` from ROCm/aiter #6675 (954f8f95d). #7124 (553db8b17) adds the a8w4 kernel for the NVFP4 prefix of `v41_fp4_new`, and #6831 (32b18c869) speeds up the unsplit CSR prefill. aiter 581579ab5, the gfx950 / gfx942 image pin, has all three. The `-rocm720` image flavors are still pinned at 285579b62, which has none of them; there `v41_new` fails at startup with an ImportError. title: [Perf] [AMD] scheduler: DP prefill coalescer mode for the prefill delayer (1/5)
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, the prefill delayer lets one rank prefill while the others decode, so the gathered MoE runs unbalanced prefill steps. A coalescer mode holds prefill until all ranks have work and enough tokens to fill the chunk. ## Modifications - New `--prefill-delayer-mode coalesce` (default `legacy`, unchanged). It negotiates once per scheduler pass with one 6-int all_gather, after the waiting queue is ranked. - After any DP rank prefilled, hold prefill for `--prefill-decode-interval` passes while decode exists. Then wait until every rank has prefill work and the group's pending tokens fill `--prefill-delayer-fill-ratio` of the chunk, bounded by stall / TTFT / partial-prefill / KV-pressure releases. - The decision is a pure function with unit tests (`test_prefill_delayer_coalesce.py`). - Fix `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_GATHER_FP8` on ROCm: quantize with the triton group-quant kernel.
