title: [Perf] [AMD] minimax-m3: Default page_size to the 128-token sparse block on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, MiniMax-M3 is the only platform branch of `_minimax_m3_overrides` that leaves `page_size` at the default of 1, so the sparse attention kernels look up `req_to_token` once per token of every selected block; this PR defaults it to the model's 128-token sparse block, as the SM100 and SM90 branches already do. With `page_size == 128` a selected sparse block is exactly one allocator page. The sparse prefill attention then derives each block's slots from one base slot (`PER_PAGE_SLOTS` in `flash_with_topk_idx.py`), and the decode sparse kernel reads the block as one contiguous page (`PAGED_CONTIG` in `topk_sparse.py`), instead of looking up 128 `req_to_token` entries. The Triton backend ROCm uses here accepts any page size, so the only thing that changes is which addressing path the kernels take. ## Modifications - `_minimax_m3_overrides`, ROCm branch: when `--page-size` is unset, set it to 128, as the SM100/SM90 branches do. An explicit `--page-size` is kept. - The M3.1 NVFP4 path already sets 128 on gfx950 and is untouched; CUDA is untouched. - `test_model_overrides.py`: a ROCm case for the default and for an explicit page size. It fails on main (`KeyError: 'page_size'`), and it also fails on a variant that overrides an explicit `--page-size`. What a 128-token page also changes, as it already does on NVIDIA: the radix cache shares prefixes at page granularity, and each request's KV allocation rounds up to a whole page (at most 127 slots). The runs below have the radix cache off. Related: #36283 speeds up the sparse KV page lookups for any page size; it co

title: [Fix] [AMD] all-reduce: Check quick reduce before custom AR so ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION takes effect
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, setting `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` builds and enables a `QuickAllReduce` that is never called, because `_resolve_outplace_all_reduce_method` asks custom AR first and custom AR accepts every size quick reduce was tuned for; this PR checks quick reduce first. `dispatch_custom_allreduce` returns AITER's `CustomAllreduce` by default (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_AR`), whose `max_size` is 1 GiB. Every entry of `QuickAllReduce._QR_MIN_SIZE`, the kernel-tested quick-reduce/custom-AR crossover (1–2 MiB at world size 2), sits far below that, so with the order `ca -> pcie_ipc -> qr` the opt-in has no effect. MI355X, TP=2, `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8`, a harness that logs the decision and counts the kernel entered: ``` 2 MiB: should_ca=True should_qr=True -> resolved=ca ran_qr=False 32 MiB: should_ca=True should_qr=True -> resolved=ca ran_qr=False total quick_all_reduce kernel calls: 0 ``` ## Modifications - `_resolve_outplace_all_reduce_method`: check `qr` before `ca`. The order is now `qr -> ca -> pcie_ipc -> pymscclpp -> torch_symm_mem -> pynccl`; nothing else moves and no predicate changes, so `should_quick_allreduce`'s per-dtype, per-world-size `_QR_MIN_SIZE` still decides the crossover. Sizes below it still go to custom AR. - The same function backs the eager path and the runtime `"auto"` resolver used under graphs, so one edit covers both. - Opt-in only: `qr_comm` is `None` or `disabled` unless `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` names a codec on gfx94x/gfx95x. CUDA, and ROCm without the variable, resolve exactly as before. After the change the same harn

title: [Fix] cuda_graph: Capture full prefill CUDA graphs of linear attention backends on static forward metadata
summary: ## Motivation Partially addresses #48593: this enables full prefill CUDA graphs for linear attention backends that read only static forward metadata (TorchTitan's GDN/KDA). SGLang's native GDN/KDA backends are left for a follow-up and now fail at capture with a clear `ValueError`. With `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full`, models on `HybridLinearAttnBackend` crash at capture: ``` MambaAttnBackendBase._replay_metadata: self.state_indices_list[bs - 1] IndexError: list index out of range ``` `MambaAttnBackendBase.init_forward_metadata_out_graph` only knows the decode graph path. Its per-batch-size buffers are sized by the decode runner and cover decode/verify only. ## Modifications Following the full-attention backends (FlashAttention's `_init_full_cg_prefill_metadata`), `MambaAttnBackendBase.init_forward_metadata_out_graph` now handles EXTEND/MIXED, which only the full prefill graph runner passes: - A backend opts in with `supports_full_cuda_graph_prefill = True`. This means its extend reads the batch only through `forward_metadata.mamba_cache_indices` / `query_start_loc` and static request buffers, on grids fixed by the token count (e.g. TorchTitan's GDN/KDA backends). - On the first capture, it allocates `[R]` state slots and `[R+1]` query offsets (`R = full_prefill_max_req`). Before every capture and replay, it refills them in place: sentinel rows get `PAD_SLOT_ID` and become empty sequences. - Other backends, and the `extra_buffer` prefix cache, raise a `ValueError` pointing to breakable graphs. ## Behavior changes | Configuration | Before | After | |---|---|---| | full pr

title: [Feat] metrics: expose scheduler-to-router delivery latency
summary: ## Motivation Part of #43304: router CPU and processing-time metrics cannot show how long an output waits between the scheduler's send and the detokenizer router's receive. title: [Fix] weight_update: Keep weight loads out of the draft in a target-only session
summary: A full Engine refit of a server with an EAGLE3 draft kills the server, and `begin_weight_update(selector="target")` cannot prevent it: tensor, distributed and plugin loads read their own request `selector`, which defaults to `"all"` and which the `Engine` update calls never set, so target tensors keep reaching the draft. title: [Perf] diffusion/flux3: Keep static streams across steps under CFG parallel
summary: ## Motivation A FLUX.3 request reuses the work of the streams whose tokens and timestep stay fixed across denoising steps (text and reference tokens: input embedding, the mode blocks, their modulation and position tables) through `Packed.static`. With `--enable-cfg-parallel` that reuse never happened: - the gate in `Flux3ImageDenoiseStage` excluded `enable_cfg_parallel`, and - `_CFGParallelModel` slices its branch out of the packed CFG pair on every step, so even with the gate open the DiT would get a fresh, empty `StaticStreams` each step. So on two GPUs every step recomputed the text stream on both ranks. ## Modifications - `_CFGParallelModel` keeps one `StaticStreams` per branch for the request (the wrapper is built per request) and attaches it to the per-step slice. - The static-stream gate no longer excludes CFG parallel. The other conditions (no flow map, no CUDA graph, no compile, no layerwise offload, no sequential CFG, `can_reuse_mode_blocks()`) are unchanged. ## Accuracy Reuse is the same computation done once instead of every step. title: [Fix] ray: Fail requests and report health when a scheduler actor dies or hangs
summary: ## Motivation `RayEngine` runs schedulers as Ray actors, which the subprocess watchdog cannot see. When a scheduler actor dies, or hangs (for example in a collective), requests wait forever and nothing tells the host to restart the engine. Ray Serve LLM serves SGLang through `RayEngine`, so its replicas stay healthy with a dead or stuck backend. ## Modifications - **Dead scheduler:** a `RayEngine` thread waits on the schedulers' `run_event_loop` refs (`ray.wait(num_returns=1)`). When one resolves, pending and new requests fail with 503. Exits caused by `shutdown()` are ignored. - **Hung scheduler:** new `async RayEngine.check_health(timeout_s=20)` raises if a scheduler exited, or if a one-token probe, as in `/health_generate`, gets no scheduler output within `timeout_s`. Follow-up in Ray: `SGLangServer.check_health()` will await `RayEngine.check_health()`. ## Tests - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestSchedulerExit` (CPU CI): a pending request fails with 503 and a new request is rejected with 503. Both fail on `main`. - `test/manual/test_ray_engine_scheduler_exit.py` (real Ray, no GPU; the CPU CI image has no Ray): a killed actor among running ones, a crashed loop, a returned loop, no report after shutdown, and a probe that is answered or times out. - GPU (A100, SGLang 0.5.23 + this patch, which applies cleanly), with a long streaming and a long non-streaming request in flight: - Killed scheduler (`ray.kill`; TP1 rank 0, TP2 rank 1): both requests failed with 503 within 3 ms, a new request got 503, and `check_health()` raised. title: [Fix] constrained: bound the compiled-grammar cache by host memory (LRU) to stop RSS growth with per-request schemas
summary: ## Motivation `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` is a plain `dict` that is never evicted. Each compiled grammar (xgrammar / outlines / llguidance) holds per-vocabulary token tables; with a 150k-token vocabulary we measured **+250–380 MB of scheduler RSS per previously-unseen `json_schema`**. Agent frameworks commonly embed per-call values (enums, defaults, descriptions) inside the schema, so every request is a cache miss and the scheduler grows until the host runs out of RAM. In production (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, `--dp-size 4`, 4× H100 NVL, 128 GB RAM + 61 GB swap, SGLang 0.5.10.post1) one client with ~1,250 distinct schemas/day drove each scheduler from 3.5 GB to 35 GB in 11 days; RAM and swap filled and the server stalled for 25 minutes. `/flush_cache` clears the cache but is refused unless the server is fully idle, so it is not a mitigation under load. The cache code is unchanged on `main`. Fixes #45077. ## Changes - `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` becomes an LRU `OrderedDict` bounded by a fixed host-memory budget, `BaseGrammarBackend.DEFAULT_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES` (1 GiB). There is no server flag for it (review feedback: the bound is an implementation detail); backends and tests can still pass `cache_limit_bytes` to the constructor, and `<= 0` there disables the bound. Each entry is charged `BaseGrammarObject.memory_size_bytes()` plus the UTF-8 length of its key: xgrammar reports `CompiledGrammar.memory_size_bytes`, `InvalidGrammarObject` is charged the length of its error message (failed compilations stay cached but cannot accumulate for free), and backends without a size API (outlines,

title: [Fix] json-schema: Add depth and state bounds validation
summary: This fix addresses the security vulnerability where deeply nested or complex JSON schemas could cause CPU thread hanging and DoS via unbounded DFA/NFA state compilation. Changes: 1. Added validate_schema_depth() and validate_schema_bounds() functions in json_schema_validation.py 2. Added JSONSchemaDepthExceeded and JSONSchemaStateExplosion exception classes 3. Integrated validation into all three grammar backends (xgrammar, outlines, llguidance) 4. Added comprehensive unit tests for the new validation The validation enforces: - Maximum schema nesting depth of 16 - Maximum estimated DFA states of 10,000 This prevents adversarial schemas from causing DoS by state space explosion. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This PR addresses a security vulnerability (Issue #39125) where deeply nested or cyclically referencing JSON schemas (depth > 16 or high branching factor) could cause the Grammar DFA/NFA state compiler to attempt unbounded state space compilation. This leads to severe CPU thread starvation, blocking the inference engine loop for multiple minutes and causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition on the server instance. The root cause was the absence of validation capping schema nesting depth or maximum DFA transition states before constructing the regex/grammar parsing table in the schema-to-grammar FSM transformation pipeline. ## Modi

summary: ## Motivation [#36267](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36267) removed Qwen3.5 GDN prefill projection unpack copies on CUDA by keeping Q/K/V/Z/B/A as strided views, and [#41683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41683) brought those views to ROCm. Profiling then showed that the recurrent `chunk_h`/`chunk_o` kernels dominated the remaining GDN time. Their fixed launch geometry under-filled MI355X, while NVIDIA can route GDN prefill through specialized FlashInfer/CuTeDSL backends. This PR therefore adds gfx95-aware Triton launch selection while preserving the original configuration for other platforms, KDA, and unsupported shapes. The norm fusion differs from [#33290](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33290) and closed [#28361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28361): those reduce two norm launches to one; this PR reduces them to zero by normalizing while Q/K are already in registers. [#37113](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37113) is the complementary decode projection/Conv1D fusion; its decode branch is mutually exclusive with this prefill path. ## Modifications - Add `fused_gdn_prefill_prepare`, a thin HIP wrapper over the shared `_prepare_gdn_prefill` kernel for the equal-Q/K-head extend path, which: - splits strided post-conv Q/K/V, - L

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: One decode graph variant on every attention-DP rank, one verify graph
summary: ## Motivation On HIP, DSA models (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V3.2) capture two decode graphs per batch size: dense (the indexer only writes K when every sequence fits in `index_topk`) and sparse (`DsaGraphVariants`). Each rank picks its variant from its own longest sequence, and an idle rank always picks sparse. Under DP attention the ranks replay their graphs in lockstep, and the collectives captured inside them pair up across ranks. Some of these collectives register their graph's input buffers (aiter all-gather / reduce-scatter / custom all-reduce). When two ranks replay different variants in the same step, a rank reads its peer's buffers from the other graph: stale data. On GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X, PD decode TP4 + DP4 attention with the MoE gather / combine inside the graphs, 26 of 200 GSM8K prompts came back garbled. Pinning every rank to one variant removed all of them, which confirmed the cause. It also shows up with only the custom all-reduce in the graph (first token right, then noise: `Theutzer1-case55500The $500 + 800 = 1300 ...`): on current `main` with the stock image's defaults, aggregated TP4 / DP4 attention with MTP returns 153 of 1,200 GSM8K prompts garbled (Accuracy Tests). Two further observations from the code: - The dense variant only changes the decode / idle indexer (`_should_skip_logits_computation()`); a target-verify capture runs the full indexer in both, so MTP deployments capture the verify graphs twice for nothing. - On the verify path `select()` has no host lengths and syncs `seq_lens.max()` to the host before every replay. ## Modifications - `graph_varia

title: [Feat] mem_cache: Evict a Mamba state together with the KV only it serves (unit eviction)
summary: ## Motivation On a hybrid model (Mamba, gated delta rule), a cached prefix can be resumed only at a node that holds a recurrent state. The radix cache evicts states and KV separately by LRU, so under memory pressure it keeps full-attention KV that no state can serve and evicts states that the next turn of a conversation resumes from. This PR adds unit eviction from FlashStates ([paper](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate), [code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashStates), [project page](https://flashstates.ai)), the "Unit eviction" item of the roadmap #50700. ## Modifications `--enable-mamba-unit-eviction` (off by default): - A cached Mamba state and the full-attention KV that only it can serve form a unit: when the state is evicted, that KV is freed with it. - KV that no state can serve is evicted before any other KV. - The bookkeeping lives in `unified_cache/unit_eviction.py`: per-node counts of the states at or below each node, updated when a state appears or goes, so no eviction decision walks a subtree. With the flag off, the cache behaves exactly as on `main`. With it on, the Python radix-tree core is used (selected automatically). The flag is refused with `--disable-radix-cache`, a registered `--radix-cache-backend`, `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (for now) and on a model without Mamba states. The flag is documented in `server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests Unit eviction changes which cached prefixes stay on the GPU, not what the model computes. - GSM8K on every benchmark server below, on a boot with the same server arguments just before each run: 200

title: [Feat] diffusion: share the layerwise pinned weight stores across co-resident instances
summary: ## Motivation Several `sglang serve` processes on one host each materialize the **same** layerwise pinned host store. For MiniMax-H3 fl2va that store is 108.5 GiB of page-locked host memory (transformer 62.28 GB + text encoder 46.18 GB), while each server uses only ~10 GiB of a 96 GiB card — so the host, not VRAM, is what limits how many can run. Part of that duplication is already handled: `main`'s read-only checkpoint mapping shares page-cache pages across processes (36.7 GiB per instance at N=2 in the run below). What cannot be shared that way is the **pinned** store, because `cudaHostRegister` refuses a read-only file mapping, a writable one breaks copy-on-write per process, and `_shared_storage` is an anonymous memfd that peers cannot open. Measured on `main` with sharing off, one server per GPU started one at a time, on an otherwise idle 498 GiB host (build and its one caveat in *Speed Tests* below): the first server costs 126 GiB of host memory and **every further one costs another ~123 GiB**. title: [Roadmap] Unified weight snapshot loading: weight cache, R-Fork and stores
summary: ## Motivation @zanes-ops @galletas1712 @whybeyoung @ShangmingCai @Fridge003 @alphabetc1 @ispobock @alexnails SGLang loads weights from a weight-cache daemon on the same GPU, from another running instance (R-Fork), from a store that holds post-processed state (`presharded`, `sharded_state`, Redis `remote`), or from a raw checkpoint (disk, HF Hub, or streamed by `runai_streamer`). Every path except the raw ones has the same three problems today: - **Each path decides by itself what to copy and what to recompute.** `sharded_state`, `presharded` and Redis run quant post-processing on the empty model, before the bytes arrive. `sharded_state` and Redis then re-run `post_load_weights` on the received weights. R-Fork over NCCL or the transfer engine never runs quant post-processing and re-runs `post_load_weights`. The weight cache runs neither. - **Checks stop at tensors** (names, shapes, dtypes). Only `presharded` carries derived tensors kept as plain attributes, with an opt-in checksum. Nothing checks non-tensor attributes, flags kept on tensors, or the expert map. - **Each rank decides alone** between a snapshot-like source and a fallback, so one rank can load from the cache while its peer loads from disk. Three bugs show the pattern, and the rest of this issue calls them the three motivating bugs: the expert map is not carried (a fork of a rebalanced seed routes to the wrong experts); the FP8 scale-format flags are not carried (a cache hit fails, and a store load quietly runs a slower kernel); MLA `w_kc`/`w_vc` are not carried or are re-derived from already-processed weights. <

summary: On H100, `update_weights_from_disk` kills the server on every per-tensor FP8 and INT8 checkpoint we tried, and so does a `begin_weight_update` session. This PR makes both work on all five. title: [Fix] deepseek-v3.1: Parse coalesced streaming tool calls
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek V3.1 streaming tool calls depend on how the output is chunked. With two complete calls in one increment, the greedy name match spans both calls. With the first header delivered separately, the second call's arguments can instead be attached to the first tool. A complete single call can lose its arguments as well. For example, `weather({"city":"Tokyo"})` followed by `search({"query":"cafes"})` parses correctly when headers and arguments arrive separately, but not when the calls share one increment. The serving layer's final argument flush does not recover the lost/wrongly attributed arguments. The first-chunk argument issue was previously reported in the closed, unmerged #18236; credit to @momaek. This change also fixes the coalesced multi-call case and adds regressions. ## Modifications - Bound the function name at the first tool separator. - Process arguments in the same increment that emits the name. - Drain completed calls in order; retain a JSON-complete call until its end marker arrives so the next call cannot inherit its state. - Add nine CPU-registered tests covering coalesced calls, partial arguments, repeated names, delayed end markers, empty arguments, and existing sequential/non-streaming behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Local native Windows CPU component validation: - Nine added regression tests pass, including every internal split of the second call's argument JSON. The unchanged detector fails this test set. - Five source-bound wrapper/final-SSE-flush probes pass after the fix; only the sequential control passes before it. - Ruff 0.15.1 check

Dictionary conversion and defaults are unchanged. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The regular DSA `sgl-kernel` TopK path can return the same selected indices in a different order in two fresh processes, even when its FP32 score input is bitwise identical. The selected set is correct, but `triton_sparse_mla` consumes the indices in the returned order. summary: ## Problem For Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 native in-checkpoint MTP (EAGLE/STANDALONE speculative decoding with **no** `--speculative-draft-model-path`), the target worker never learns the draft layer count: `eagle_draft_num_layers` stays `None` because it is only resolved from the external draft model config. The draft KV pool is then **not budgeted into the target cell size**, so on a 32 GB card the draft pool allocation overruns the static memory envelope and OOMs during initialization. ## Correct accounting The native MTP draft physically allocates one full-context draft K/V layer. With the current FP8 geometry: - target: 16 full-attention layers (64 layers, full attention every 4) × 2048 B/token = **32,768 B/token** - native MTP draft: 1 layer × 2048 B/token = **2,048 B/token** - **total = 34,816 B/token (34 KiB/token)** ## Change `resolve_spec_aux_hidden_state_config` now passes the target `model_config` into `_resolve_eagle_aux_hidden_state`. title: feat(metrics): count waiting-queue request rejections
summary: The scheduler drops requests from the waiting queue in three places without recording anything: a full queue, a preemption by a higher-priority request, and a waiting timeout. None are observable. The tokenizer-side sglang:num_aborted_requests_total counter does not cover them, because its only increment site counts aborts the frontend initiates, and these travel the opposite direction. HTTP status codes do not cover them either for streaming requests: the 200 is committed at http.response.start before the scheduler can reject, so the client receives 200 plus an SSE error chunk and the rejection never appears in any status-code metric. Rejected requests also return before set_wait_queue_entry_time(), so they are absent from queue_time_seconds, per_stage_req_latency, TTFT, and e2e_request_latency. On a production deployment running --max-queued-requests, this hid roughly 6% of offered load behind zero recorded 503s. Add sglang:num_queue_rejected_requests_total, labelled by reason. It inherits the SchedulerMetricsCollector label set, so it carries dp_rank and attributes rejections to the individual rank whose queue filled, which matters when a load-balance method concentrates a shared prefix on one rank. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! title: [PD] Stage MLA DCP=8 relayout before Mooncake RDMA for KIMI K3
summary: ## Motivation When Prefill uses DCP size 1 and Decode uses DCP size greater than 1, each Decode rank owns a strided subset of the Prefill KV tokens. The existing Mooncake DCP relayout path builds transfer blocks only when both source and destination token addresses are contiguous. The destination offsets are packed, but the source offsets advance by `dcp_size`. As a result, the source is noncontiguous and the transfer is split into one RDMA block per token and KV layer. For Kimi K3 MLA FP8 KV cache, one token row is approximately: ```text (kv_lora_rank 512 + rope dimension 64) × 1 byte = 576 bytes ``` In a 56K-token, DCP=8, 24-MLA-layer deployment, this produces approximately 168K small transfer descriptors per Decode rank. The observed aggregate P-to-D bandwidth was about 1.23 GB/s across eight RDMA devices, despite the available link bandwidth being much higher. This PR adds an opt-in GPU staging path that gathers each Decode rank's strided token rows into contiguous registered memory before issuing Mooncake transfers. ```text Legacy: strided source tokens -> one descriptor per token and layer -> approximately 576-byte RDMA writes Staged: strided source tokens -> Triton byte-preserving gather -> contiguous layer-major staging buffer -> normally one descriptor per layer and destination page -> 64 × 576 bytes = 36 KiB writes for Kimi K3 ``` For the example above, the descriptor count is expected to decrease from approxim

title: [ROCm] Use the AITER sparse-MLA kernel for DSA prefill and decode
summary: Enable with `--dsa-prefill-backend aiter --dsa-decode-backend aiter` (both flags are required; passing only one skips the ROCm default path). The default is unchanged. ## What this does On ROCm, DSA attention currently runs on TileLang for both prefill and decode. This PR adds an `aiter` backend that routes both phases to the AITER sparse-MLA kernel `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen1_gqaratio16_ps` with fp8 Q and fp8 KV. Sparse DSA prefill is structurally a very wide decode: the chunk is handed to `mla_decode_fwd` as `num_tokens` sequences of length 1 (`max_seqlen_q = 1`), so one kernel serves both phases and no separate prefill kernel is needed. Notable details: - Q must be fp8, or AITER dispatches `mla_a16w8_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1_ps` instead, which is 4.2x slower. fp8 Q comes from `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, whose gate in `forward_mla.py` previously tested `dsa_backend == "tilelang"` literally. It is now a set of backends that want fp8 Q. - CUDA-only DSA backends now fall back to `tilelang` on ROCm with a warning instead of raising `ImportError: flashmla_ops`. The ROCm default is only applied when *both* backend flags are unset, so passing one previously made the other fall through to `flashmla_kv`. ## Results GLM-5.2 FP4, MI355X (gfx950) TP4, 8192 in / 1024 out, concurrency 64. title: [Speculative] Fix DSpark base logits for quantized target lm_head
summary: ## Motivation Serving a **quantized** target model with a DSpark draft fails at startup (both eager and CUDA-graph capture) with: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (7x5120 and 2560x248320) ``` Reproduced on `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` drafting `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (RTX 5090, sglang 0.5.17 and current main). **Root cause**: DSpark dense drafts share the target's `lm_head` (`attach_shared_modules`). When the target is quantized, `lm_head.weight` is stored in a packed layout — e.g. NVFP4 stores `[vocab, 2560]` for a 5120-hidden target (5120 × 4 bit = 2560 bytes/row, with separate per-block `weight_scale`). `compute_base_logits` performs a raw `torch.matmul(hidden, weight.T)` against the packed layout, which is invalid for any quantized packing. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/dspark.py` — `DSparkDraftMixin.compute_base_logits`: - When `weight.shape[1] != hidden.shape[-1]` (packed layout), route through `lm_head.quant_method.apply(lm_head, hidden, bias)` — mirroring `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head` so the quant method's dequantize path applies. - Raise a clear `ValueError` when the lm_head is packed but carries no applicable quant method. - Unquantized targets keep the existing dense matmul path unchanged. ## Tests New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/models/test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py` (3 cases, all passing locally): 1. packed weight routes through `quant_method.apply` (call verified via mock, returns expected logits) 2. unquantized weight still uses the dense matmul path 3. packed weight without a quant method raises `V

title: [Bugfix] Kimi-K3: fix vision-DP rank-local indexing into global grid_thws_host
summary: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3 with vision-DP sharding (observed on `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8` with DSPARK speculative decoding, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`), the first `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries **two or more images with different geometries** kills the scheduler: ``` ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids ``` The request returns 500 and the server never recovers — every subsequent request fails until the container is restarted. Single-image requests, and multi-image requests whose images share one NaViT grid, are unaffected — which is how this survives typical smoke tests. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`, `materialize_item_features(image_indices)` receives the **global** image indices assigned to this vision-DP rank, but the deferred-preprocessing block indexes `grid_thws_host` — a global tensor with one row per image in the batch — with the rank-**local** enumerate positions: ```python expected_grids = grid_thws_host[indices] # local idx into global tensor ... patch_counts = [int(grid_thws_host[index].prod().item()) for index in indices] # same bug ``` On any rank whose assigned images are not the global prefix `[0..k)`, the expected grids and patch split counts are read from the wrong rows. If the wrongly-read row happens to hold a different grid, the `torch.equal` sanity check fires and raises, taking the scheduler down. (The non-DP path passes `list(range(len(items)))`, where local == global, so it never triggers.) ## Fix Translate the local enumerate positions through the closure's `im

title: [Feature] Support Kimi-K3 FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE on SM120
summary: > Draft: depends on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4460. The dependency is not > vendored or pinned by this PR, and the default MoE backend is unchanged. ## Motivation SGLang already supports the FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP4 MoE path for GPT-OSS on SM120, but Kimi-K3 needs additional model-specific integration: - Kimi stores gate and up projections as contiguous halves, while the CUTLASS kernel consumes the opposite half order. This differs from GPT-OSS's pair-interleaved layout. - Kimi-K3 uses SiTU with independent parameters `situ_beta=4.0` and `situ_linear_beta=25.0`. - Chunked Prefill can pass non-contiguous hidden states to the MXFP8 quantizer. - RTX 6000D (SM120) must not enter the tcgen05 fused attention-residual path intended for GB100/GB200/GB300-class architectures. FlashInfer PR #4460 owns the public CUTLASS SiTU kernel and API. This PR only adds the SGLang-side Kimi-K3 integration and should remain Draft until #4460 is available in an official RC or release. ## Modifications - Detect the public FlashInfer CUTLASS SiTU capability without making the new enum or function parameters mandatory at SGLang import time. - Dispatch Kimi-K3 MXFP8-activation-by-MXFP4-weight MoE to FlashInfer CUTLASS on SM120 only when `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` is selected. - Convert Kimi's contiguous `[gate; up]` weight and scale halves to CUTLASS's `[up; gate]` order while preserving the existing GPT-OSS interleaved path. - Forward `situ_beta` and `situ_linear_beta` independently through the FlashInfer #4460 API. - Materialize non-contiguous hidden states immediately before MXFP8 quant

title: [AMD] Enable staged HiCache write-back for DeepSeek V4
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 hybrid HiCache uses specialized paged, compress-state, and DSA indexer host pools. Their staged page-first write-back remained gated to native CUDA even though the shared JIT kernel supports HIP. Simply opening that gate is not sufficient on ROCm: on MI355X with ROCm 7.2.26015, mmap-backed memory registered with HIP has a device alias different from its CPU `data_ptr()`, so the existing PF-to-LF GPU load kernel faults while dereferencing the CPU virtual address. ## Modifications - Enable staged write-back on ROCm for `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool`, `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool`, and `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. - Use HIP runtime H2D copies for page-first loads from registered host storage, allowing the runtime to resolve the GPU-visible host alias. CUDA retains the existing AOT kernel path. - Cache converted CPU page-row indices across the layers of one L2 load, with tensor identity/version invalidation. - Validate ROCm HiCache host-pool capabilities during controller construction and dynamic sidecar registration. `kernel + page_first` now fails at startup if any pool lacks staged JIT write-back, and `kernel + layer_first` is rejected because its GPU kernel dereferences host CPU virtual addresses. The existing runtime checks remain as defense in depth. - Add byte-exact D2H/H2D round-trip coverage for C4/C128-style paged rows, compress-state ring rows, and DSA indexer rows, including in-place index mutation. ### Scope and index routing This PR supports the DeepSeek-V4 `kernel + page_first` host pools listed above; it is not an allocator-wide fix for every kernel th

title: feat(dsa): add SM80 Torch fallbacks and Triton paged-MQA indexer
summary: ## Motivation The current CUDA DSA path cannot run end-to-end on NVIDIA A100/SM80: 1. The paged-MQA indexer depends on a DeepGEMM FP8 path targeting newer architectures. 2. Sparse MLA attention uses an FA3 configuration with asymmetric head dimensions (`QK=576`, `V=512`) that is unsupported on SM80. This PR establishes an explicit SM80 DSA path in two steps: - Correctness-first Torch backends for paged-MQA logits and sparse-MLA attention. - An optimized native Triton paged-MQA indexer for A100. The attention path remains on the Torch fallback in this PR. Triton sparse-MLA attention is intentionally left for a follow-up. All new backends are explicit opt-in and existing automatic backend selection remains unchanged. ## Modifications ### Torch correctness backends Add a general Torch paged-MQA implementation for the packed DSA index cache: - Query: `[T, H, 128]` E4M3FN - Packed page: `[64 * 128 FP8 key bytes][64 FP32 scales]` - Output: `[T, max_seq_len]` FP32 - Query/page chunking avoids gathering the complete cache. - Invalid pages and positions outside the sequence length produce deterministic `0.0`. Add a Torch sparse-MLA implementation: - BF16 query and KV cache - FP32 score computation and online softmax state - Query and Top-K chunking - Correct handling of `-1` sparse indices - No complete `[T, H, K, 576]` intermediate tensor These implementations provide the correctness reference and fallback for the optimized SM80 path. ### SM80 Triton paged-MQA indexer Add a native Triton paged-MQA logits kernel for NVIDIA A100: - Fixed grid: `(query row, logical KV page)` - One pro

title: [AMD] Serve Kimi-K3 on gfx942: moonmath MLA multi-query verify, MXFP4 MoE, chunked prefix KV
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 cannot be served on CDNA3 (MI300X / MI325X) today, and MLA models more generally lose speculative decoding there. Four independent blockers, each of which aborts or OOMs rather than degrading: 1. **`SituAndMul` does not build on ROCm.** `forward_cuda` JIT-builds `kimi_k3/situ_and_mul.cuh`, which includes `<cuda_fp8.h>` unguarded. Under hipcc the build fails *inside* CUDA-graph capture, so it surfaces only as `Capture cuda graph failed: ninja exited with status 1`. 2. **MXFP4 MoE aborts.** `aiter.fused_moe` has no gfx942 a4w4 path and dies in the activation quantiser with `fused_dynamic_mx_quant_moe_sort_hip: not support output type: fp4x2`. 3. **aiter's asm MLA has no kernel for 12 query heads** (Kimi-K3 at TP8 is 96/8 = 12; aiter requires 4, 8, or a multiple of 16 in [16, 128]) and none past `qseqlen` 4, so a speculative draft window larger than 4 calls `abort()` during cuda-graph capture. 4. **Long-context prefill runs out of VRAM.** With a cached prefix the aiter MHA extend path re-gathers and up-projects the *entire* prefix through `kv_b_proj` in one shot. `AttnForwardMethod.MHA_CHUNKED_KV` already bounds this, but it was unreachable on ROCm: `maybe_disable_chunked_prefix_cache()` force-sets `disable_chunked_prefix_cache=True` for any backend absent from `CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_SUPPORTED_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`. This PR closes all four. It is stacked on #<PR1> (the single-query moonmath MLA decode backend); the first commit here is that PR's commit rebased onto current main. ## Modifications **New attention backend — `--attention-backend moonmath_mla`**

title: [Feat] weight_cache: Add the vmm_fd transport
summary: Co-authored with @Shunkangz and @mohammedabdulwahhab. ## Motivation The weight cache daemon (#27139) shares weights with engines through `torch_ipc`, which uses CUDA IPC handles. The `vmm_fd` backend in `weight_cache/transport.py` is still a placeholder that raises `NotImplementedError`; #33522 and #27310 (§4.2, phase 1) both plan it. With CUDA VMM, the engine reserves its own virtual address range and maps the daemon's allocations into it. With `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`, the caller cannot choose the address. That difference gives: 1. **In this PR:** a daemon exit no longer kills the engine. CUDA frees a `cuMemCreate` allocation only after every mapping and handle to it is released, so an attached engine keeps valid weights, and the SIGKILL watchdog is only needed for `torch_ipc`. 2. **Follow-ups:** release the weights and map them back later at the same addresses, so that pointers captured in CUDA graphs stay valid. This would allow weight release/resume with the cache on (rejected today by `_assert_weight_cache_inactive`), the roadmap's epoch handoff, and engine snapshots that re-attach the node's resident weights instead of reading them from the checkpoint (#43965, #40736; a proposed design, not tested here). In this PR the engine maps once and does not re-map. The KV cache needs no new transport: with `--enable-memory-saver`, torch_memory_saver already allocates it with CUDA VMM and keeps its addresses across pause and resume. ## Modifications - `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}`, the flag named in #33522. On the daemon, `auto` keeps `torch_ipc` for now; on

title: [Feat] disaggregation: Let PD decode servers prefill short requests locally, routed by sgl-router
summary: ## Motivation Today a PD decode server never runs a prefill forward: every request arrives through a prefill server, a bootstrap handshake and a KV transfer, even when the decode server's radix cache already holds almost the whole prompt. In multi-turn and agentic traffic that is the common case: the decode server that served turn N holds turn N's prompt and output, so turn N+1 needs only a short prefill, and the fixed PD cost dominates its TTFT. This PR lets a decode server prefill such requests itself, in the same running batch as its PD requests, and lets `sgl-router` decide when to send a request there. It is RFC #45416 (PPD) with both phases in one change: the engine side ports #45423 (by @alphabetc1, 1685 commits behind main and conflicting in 11 files) onto the current request-list and retirer abstractions, and the router side is new. ## Modifications ### Engine (`--disaggregation-decode-enable-local-prefill`) - **Request field.** `disagg_local_prefill: bool` on `/generate` and the OpenAI endpoints, carried as a defaulted tail field of `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`. A marked request needs no bootstrap fields. A server without the flag (or a prefill server) rejects it with 400. - **Queues.** With the flag on, transferred requests wait in a new `ListKind.PD_PREBUILT` list (`Scheduler.disagg_decode_prebuilt_queue`, registered through `request_lists()` so abort, idle checks, invariants and load reporting see it) and `waiting_queue` holds only the requests this server prefills, so the aggregated prefill path keeps its meaning. title: [Fix] [CPU] Fix: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 quantization rule failure and accuracy degradation
summary: ## Motivation - When attempting to load the `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4` model, we discovered that a projection layer (`in_proj_ba`)—which should have been excluded from quantization—was incorrectly identified by the CPU execution path as being quantized via GPTQ. - Furthermore, the dequantization process follows an outdated GPTQ convention by erroneously adding 1 to the model's symmetric zero-points, which leads to accuracy issues. ## Modifications - Modified `gptq.py` at line 238. title: [Perf] MiniMax-M3: overlap the shared expert with MegaMoE under CUDA graph
summary: ## Motivation In `MiniMaxM3MoE.forward_mega_moe`, the shared expert (MXFP8 gate_up, SwiGLU, down) runs on the main stream before the router and MegaMoE: about 23 µs per layer, about 1.3 ms per decode step across the model, all on the critical path. DeepSeek's `forward_mega_moe` already forks its shared expert onto `alt_stream` under CUDA-graph capture; MiniMax-M3 does not. Fusing the shared expert into MegaMoE, as DeepSeek V4 does, is not possible here without changing precision: with FP4 routed activations, sgl-deep-gemm's MegaMoE kernel also takes the shared expert in FP4, while the MiniMax-M3 checkpoint ships it in MXFP8. ## Modifications `models/minimax_m3.py`: - Under CUDA-graph capture, with an `alt_stream` and a shared expert, the shared expert runs on `alt_stream` (after `wait_stream` on the current stream) beside the router and MegaMoE. - `_add_shared` joins the streams before the add, on both the MegaMoE and the TRT-LLM decode paths. - Eager steps keep running it inline. ## Accuracy Tests Same operations on the same inputs, only on another stream. title: [Feat] hicache: Forward request-scoped KV hints to storage backends
summary: ## Motivation #38891 added a versioned `kv_hints` envelope to generation requests. `GenerateReqInput` documents that it is "passed through untouched to the HiCache storage backends", but today it stops at `Req.kv_hints`: no storage backend can see it. This PR completes that path, so a HiCache storage backend can use an orchestrator's hint when it looks up and reads pages. For example, an orchestrator that routes a request to one worker can tell that worker's storage backend which of the request's blocks another worker has already published, so the backend can fetch those blocks instead of the worker recomputing them. The first consumer is the KVCR storage backend in #45647, which will be rebased onto this API. No in-tree backend uses hints yet, and the hook is opt-in, so nothing changes for existing backends. Hints are stated in terms of the block hashes that SGLang publishes in KV events. For requests isolated by `cache_salt` or by an `extra_key` such as a LoRA adapter, those event IDs differ from the HiCache storage keys. A backend cannot convert between them without reproducing the scheduler's hash chain, so this PR also gives the backend that mapping. ## Modifications A storage backend opts in by overriding `HiCacheStorage.consumes_kv_hints()` to return `True`. For such a backend, HiCache storage lookups (`batch_exists`, `batch_exists_v2`) and reads (`batch_get_v1`, `batch_get_v2`) for a request whose `kv_hints` contains at least one action receive one or two entries in `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info`: - `kv_hints`: the request's `KvHintsEnvelope`. - `storage_key_t

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1: capture the vision encoder in CUDA graphs per image grid
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 runs its 32-layer ViT + aligner replicated on every TP rank. The encoder is host-bound (hundreds of small launches, per-call host-to-device copies of the rotary tables and `cu_seqlens`, four host-syncing mask writes to build the image span), so host jitter on one rank shows up as collective wait on the other ranks in the first LM layer. In a TP4 trace of a 768x1024 image, rank 0 waited about 30 ms in that all-reduce, longer than the encoder itself. This PR replays tower + aligner + span assembly as one CUDA graph per `(n_vit_h, n_vit_w)` grid, with a sync-free span builder and per-grid cached rotary/metadata. **Perf: image rows, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4, MI355X: TTFT p50 -15 to -19%, output tok/s +9 to +14% at 1k text (c16/c64); neutral at 8k text (+2.3% TTFT p50, +0.7% tok/s, unclear). title: [Fix] [AMD] distributed: Fix custom AR capture for DSA DP dual graphs
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #36071. On ROCm, DSA with DP attention allows different DP lanes to replay different decode graphs concurrently. Custom all-reduce direct graph-input registration assumes something stronger: every rank in the communicator replays the same captured graph and custom-AR call ordinal in lockstep. During capture, each custom-AR call embeds a `RankData` slot. Registration then fills that slot with peer pointers belonging to the same captured-call ordinal. At replay there is no runtime graph-id handshake. If TP2 lane pairs select different graphs, each pair reads graph-local buffers that are inactive on the other ranks. The resulting all-reduce is incomplete and can turn GLM-5.2 logits into NaN, followed by repeated token ID 0. This supersedes the earlier shared-memory-pool address-collision hypothesis. Instrumentation found no pointer-registration ordering, IPC-handle, offset, or capture-to-registration drift. ## Modifications - Use the communicator's stable pre-registered copy-in buffer during graph capture when DSA DP attention is enabled. - Apply the policy to both AITER and legacy SGLang custom all-reduce. - Preserve direct graph-input registration for non-DP DSA and other attention backends. - Add unit coverage for the graph-capture policy. title: [RFC] A Unified KV-Cache Sparsity Framework for Post-Hoc Sparse Attention
summary: ## Motivation An increasing number of KV-cache sparsification methods can be applied to existing dense-attention checkpoints without training a model-native sparse indexer. Examples include fixed-pattern selection, KV-derived selection, and current-query-aware retrieval. We refer to this family as **post-hoc or non-native KV sparsity**: - the model was not trained with a native sparse-attention architecture; - the sparse policy is attached at inference time; - the policy decides which cached KV entries are visible to an existing attention backend; - the same framework can potentially support many dense MHA/GQA model families. This scope is broader than a model-specific sparse implementation. A unified framework would make it possible to: - experiment with new sparse methods on existing dense checkpoints; - share request, decode-step, and layer lifecycle hooks; - reuse logical-to-physical KV translation; - reuse attention-backend integration and CUDA Graph support; - compare methods under the same serving conditions; - add a new method without modifying the model runner and attention backend again. Today, SGLang does not yet provide a complete runtime framework for this use case. Some abstractions have been merged, and several Quest/HiSparse efforts are in progress, but the common interface and serving integration remain incomplete or method-specific. ## Current State ### Existing `mem_cache/sparsity` interfaces SGLang `main` already contains a sparse algorithm skeleton under: ```text python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/sparsity/ ├── algorithms/ │ ├── base_algorithm.py │ ├── quest_a

title: [Bug / Security] Potential DFA state explosion and CPU thread hanging in JSON Schema grammar compilation under deeply nested schemas
summary: ### Bug / Issue Description During formal analysis of the structured decoding compiler pipeline in `sglang/srt/constrained/`, an issue regarding unbounded recursive schema compilation was identified. When a client submits an untrusted, deeply nested, or cyclically referencing JSON schema (depth > 16 or high branching factor), the Grammar DFA/NFA state compiler attempts to unroll the entire state space without recursion depth or state count limits. This causes severe CPU thread starvation, blocking the inference engine loop for multiple minutes and causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition on the server instance. ### 🔬 Root Cause Analysis In the schema-to-grammar FSM transformation, there is no validation capping the schema nesting depth or maximum allowed DFA transition states before constructing the regex/grammar parsing table. ### 🛡️ Remediation / Suggested Fix Introduce an explicit depth and state boundary validator before compiling the grammar automaton: ```python def validate_schema_depth(schema, current_depth=0, max_depth=16): if current_depth > max_depth: raise ValueError(f"JSON schema nesting depth exceeds allowable limit of {max_depth}") if isinstance(schema, dict): for key, value in schema.items(): if isinstance(value, (dict, list)): validate_schema_depth(value, current_depth + 1, max_depth) elif isinstance(schema, list): for item in schema: if isinstance(item, (dict, list)): validate_schema_depth(item, current_depth + 1, max_depth) Enforcing this gate at the HTTP/gRPC request entry point prevents uncontrolled state space explosion. summary: ## Motivation Hybrid prefix-cache users that publish only prompt checkpoints still prepare decode tracking masks and indices, capture checkpoint-save work, and update checkpoint-boundary bookkeeping. title: [Fix] pd: Keep a transfer Success terminal when a client abort lands late
summary: ## Motivation A client abort in the prefill transfer queue can land after the transfer worker wrote `Success` but before the scheduler polled. `update_status` wrote `Failed` over the `Success`, and `abort()` set its own result to `Failed`. Under `prefill_complete`, decode had not been told `Success` yet, so it received `Failed` for KV that had already landed. Under early, prefill released the KV without caching it and the client got a 500. ## Modifications `Success` is terminal like `Failed`, `update_status` checks and writes under the lock, and `abort()` returns early when the room is already `Success`. An abort after the transfer finished is the router's cancel, not a failed transfer. `conclude_transfer` takes `counts_self`, so a chunk the worker has not yet uncounted does not make its own Success provisional. Mooncake passes it; Mori passes it under deferred release; NIXL uncounts first and needs nothing. For review: - On prefill, `Success` is final once no chunk is pending; a `Failed` from an outstanding deferred chunk still replaces it. Decode keeps main's rule and accepts a late `Failed` from prefill, since only prefill knows whether chunks are outstanding. - Traced and tested on Mooncake staging; Mori counts the concluding chunk only under deferred release; NIXL uncounts before it concludes. title: [Feat] tracing: Record why requests failed, and mark only server faults as errors
summary: ## Motivation Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors: - A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal request. - Every `trace_ctx.abort(abort_info=...)` sets the thread span's status to ERROR, whether the request hit a server fault, was rejected as invalid, or was aborted by its caller. A sampler or alert that keys on error spans counts every bad request and every client disconnect as a server failure. - A request that fails in the tokenizer before reaching the scheduler (invalid input, a LoRA or encoder error) never has its trace ended. With sync tracing its root span is never exported, so rejected requests don't appear in traces at all. ## Modifications 1. **Thread spans are errors only for server faults.** Each abort that has an HTTP status passes it in `abort_info["status_code"]`, matching the status the client gets: - scheduler: 400 for a missing bootstrap room or a bad sampling mask, 503 when the queue is full, and the `FINISH_ABORT`'s own status when retiring an unadmitted or chunked request; - PD prefill: 400 over KV capacity, 500 on KV transfer or bootstrap failure, and the sampling-mask reason's status; - EPD encoder: 504 on timeout, otherwise `MMError.code` or the worker's error code, falling back to 500. An aborted thread span is marked ERROR only for a 5xx, as the OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions do for server spans. Attributes whose value is None are left out instead of being exported as empty

summary: ## Motivation `EPLBManager` waits `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations` passes before every rebalance, including the first one. summary: Fixes #42364. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 does not start on SM12x. `make_candidate_indexer` sends every GPU with compute capability >= 10 down the SM100 branch, and that branch requires DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits. I hit it on four DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) nodes running TP4. Hopper already has what SM12x needs. title: [Fix] mamba: isolate one sequence's non-finite input from others in the same chunk
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51108. The SSD chunk-state and chunk-scan kernels zero out another sequence's contribution to a dot product by multiplying it by a clean 0.0. But `0 * inf` (and `0 * nan`) is still `nan` under IEEE 754, regardless of which operand supplied the zero. If one sequence's x or B tensor has a non-finite value, it silently leaks through `tl.dot` into every other sequence sharing the chunk — including their cached SSM state, which then stays wrong for all later decode steps. ## Modifications Sanitize x and B right after loading in both `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` and `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, replacing non-finite elements with 0 before they reach any multiply or dot. `v - v` is 0 for finite v and nan for +-inf/nan — the same idiom already used in this codebase's `fla/route.py` for nan handling. This only changes behavior when a non-finite value is present; output is bit-identical for ordinary finite inputs (checked with and without `seq_idx` batching). Added a regression test (`test_mamba_chunk_scan_isolates_nonfinite_request`) via the public `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` API, reproducing the issue exactly. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on an RTX 4090: - New test fails on unpatched code (30/30 non-finite outputs, non-finite final state) and passes with this fix. - Full existing `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` suite (371 cases) still passes. - Bit-identical output and final state on normal finite inputs, patched vs. unpatched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `mamba_chunk_scan_combined`, median ms/iter over 50 iters, warmed up, RTX 4090: | config | unpatched | patched | delta | |---

summary: ## Motivation This PR ports and refines the dLLM TP-local vocab-state optimization from #29970 onto the current SGLang main branch. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Let a memory-parked chunked continuation outrank external-linker prefetch
summary: ## Motivation With the unified-cache external linker in `load_mode: prefetch`, every queued request that hits the external store starts a LOAD on arrival (`UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.prefetch`). `FullComponent.build_external_linker_transfer(LOAD)` evicts the radix cache and takes free full-KV slots for the whole hit prefix, and nothing bounds the total. Under a burst of queued long-prefix requests, in-flight prefetch reads can own the entire full-KV pool while a chunked prefill is mid-flight. - Before #44823, the continuation was forced through and failed in `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend` with `Prefill out of memory ... Available full tokens: 0`. This was observed in a PD prefill run with DP attention: every radix node was locked, and prefetch owned about 93% of the pool. - Since #44823, the continuation parks instead. But arrival-time prefetch runs before every scheduling pass and can take each slot that frees up, so the parked continuation, and the admission pass it closes, can wait indefinitely. An earlier revision of this PR capped prefetch-owned slots at a fixed share of the pool. That limits prefetch even when nothing contends for memory, and it still cannot guarantee progress when locked KV exceeds the rest of the pool. title: [Fix] triton: Size the per-request indptr buffers for graph buckets past the req pool
summary: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3.1-Pro with PCP8 + EP8 MegaMoE + BCG and an SWA DFLASH2 MLA draft (`K31-DFlash2-MLA5-Preview1027-SWA1024`) crashes while the draft verify CUDA graph is being captured: ``` File ".../layers/attention/triton_backend.py", line 603, in _update_target_verify_buffers qo_indptr[: bs + 1] = torch.arange( RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (4) must match the existing size (9) at non-singleton dimension 0. ``` An SWA MLA draft has to use the `triton` draft backend. `TritonAttnBackend` sizes `kv_indptr`, `window_kv_indptr`, `qo_indptr` and `mask_indptr` from `req_to_token_pool.size`. `get_batch_sizes_to_capture`, however, pads the largest bucket up to the attention TP/CP alignment. In this run the mamba state cache caps `max_running_requests` at 3 (`max_mamba_cache_size=17`, 5 slots per request), while PCP8 aligns the buckets to 8. The target verify graph captures bs 1–8 without trouble, but the triton draft runs out of rows at bs=8. ## Modifications `TritonAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state` now grows the per-request indptr buffers the backend owns to `max_bs + 1`. A `kv_indptr_buf` that a multi-step backend passes in is shared, so it keeps the size its owner chose. Every reader takes these buffers through the attribute at use time, so no stale view survives the swap. ## Validation On 8× B300 (`kitkat-blackwell`), with `--tp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --attn-cp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --moe-runner-backend megamoe --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-attention-backend triton

title: [Fix] [AMD] qwen4_exp: Split the PLE prefill short conv under the int32 limit
summary: ## Motivation Serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on ROCm, a prefill batch that holds many short requests next to one long request kills the scheduler on both TP ranks: ```text RuntimeError: Expected canUse32BitIndexMath(input) && canUse32BitIndexMath(output) File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py", in _short_conv conv_output = F.conv1d( ``` The PLE short conv pads every request in the batch to the longest one: - conv input: `[num_requests, 10240, longest_extend + 9]` (10240 = `hidden_size × hc_count`, 9 = conv state length) - PyTorch does not send dilated grouped convs to MIOpen, so on ROCm `F.conv1d` runs the native depthwise kernel, which requires fewer than 2**31 − 1 elements in its input and output. - The limit is passed once `num_requests × (longest_extend + 9) ≥ 209,716`. A batch of fresh 8k prompts never gets there (the default 16,384-token chunk holds at most 3 of them). Prefix-cache hits do: 94 requests of which one extends 2,223 tokens are enough, and so are 42 requests of which one extends 4,985 tokens. - `bench_serving --warmup-requests 128` produces such batches: it sends 128 copies of one prompt, which then hit the radix cache. Observed: `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`, TP2, MI355X, random 8k-in/1k-out at concurrency 128 crashes in the bench warmup on the unmodified image with the commands below. The crashing batch logs no "Prefill batch" line, because prefill stats are logged after the forward. Scope: - Models: `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints). The MTP draft has no PLE layers. - Code path: ordinary prefill/extend and target-v

title: [Perf] tokenizer_manager: Drop the prompt token list once a single request is dispatched
summary: ## Motivation `GenerateReqInput.input_ids` stays a Python `list[int]` for the whole request, because `ReqState.obj` holds the request until it finishes. With long agentic prompts (0.5-1M tokens) at high concurrency, the tokenizer manager process holds tens of millions of list elements in the young GC generations. Every gen0/gen1 collection walks all of them, about 8-9 ns per element, so the process stalls for 0.2-0.5 s per collection. Clients see these stalls as mid-stream gaps in the token stream. A PD decode gateway hits this hardest: it serves the full prompt of every in-flight request for the whole length of its decode. ## Modifications - `TokenizerManager.generate_request`, single-request path: after `_send_one_request`, a list `obj.input_ids` is swapped for the `array('q')` copy the tokenized request already carries. - The GC does not track an array, and the swap allocates nothing. - Nothing in the tokenizer manager reads `obj.input_ids` after dispatch except the finished-request log and the request dumps. - The request logger renders an array the same as a list, in both the text and JSON formats. - `scripts/playground/replay_request_dump.py` converts an array `input_ids` back to a list before posting a dumped request. A companion Dynamo change drops the handler's own references to the same list in disaggregated decode: ai-dynamo/dynamo#18895. The prompt list is freed by refcount right after dispatch only when the caller drops it too. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs: the scheduler already receives the `array('q')` copy. ## Speed Tests and Profiling DeepSe

title: [Perf] eplb: Vectorize the greedy loop of balanced_packing over layers
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation Every EPLB rebalance runs `balanced_packing` on every rank. Its greedy assignment is a per-layer Python loop: for each item it scans all packs with a generator and `min()`. At a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shape, 40 layers × 416 physical experts into 32 GPUs, that is ~530k generator steps per rebalance, and all ranks wait on it. ## Modifications - Step all layers together with numpy. At each sorted position, each layer picks the lightest pack that still has room. `argmin` keeps the first minimum, as `min()` does over ascending pack ids. - Weights accumulate in float64 in the same order as the old Python sums. The output is therefore identical, including ties and integer token-count weights. - The Python loop runs `num_groups` times instead of `num_layers × num_groups × num_packs` generator steps. - The `groups_per_pack == 1` fast path and the CPU int64 outputs are unchanged. - Add `test_matches_reference_greedy`. It compares the new code with the original loop, copied into the test, on random, tied, all-zero and int64 weights. The cases include a 40 × 416 shape, with 2, 4 and 8 packs. ## Accuracy Tests The output is bit-identical to the previous implementation; the new test checks this. All 61 tests under `test/registered/unit/eplb/` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In a 32-rank DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode deployment on Vera Rubin, `balanced_packing` took 4.2 ms per rebalance with this change. summary: # Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution for this reproduction. Related reports are linked below. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Environment information and a minimal reproducible example are included. - [x] This reports a reproducible numerical behavior with a concrete decision impact. - [x] This report is in English. Tested on SGLang **0.5.21**. I have not verified today's latest main or enabled deterministic inference. # Describe the bug On one NVIDIA H20-3e, Qwen3.8-27B returns different scores for **identical token IDs** when the number of copies in a batch changes. With the FP8 checkpoint and the default BF16 LM head, `P(positive)` changes from **0.500000 to 0.622459**. Under first-option tie breaking, this changes the decision from `negative` to `positive`. The difference is repeatable for each tested batch shape, not run-to-run randomness. Cache is flushed before each request, and server logs show zero cached tokens and no splitting of the tested batches. The example generates no tokens. title: [Perf] scheduler: Add SGLANG_DISABLE_THP to turn off transparent huge pages
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With transparent huge pages (THP) on, two kernel paths can stop a thread for a long time: - The first write into an eligible region allocates and zeroes a whole huge page in the faulting thread. - khugepaged collapses small pages into huge ones while it holds the process's mmap lock for writing. Every page fault in the process waits behind it. On kernels with 64K base pages, as on Arm servers such as NVIDIA Vera, a PMD huge page is 512 MB, so either path takes tens of milliseconds. With DP attention, every rank then waits at the next gather. We hit this in decode schedulers serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PD disaggregation on Vera Rubin. Decode ran on 32 attention-DP ranks, on a 64K-page 7.0 kernel with THP `enabled=madvise`, `defrag=madvise`. - Every decode scheduler held four 1 GB `MAP_NORESERVE` anonymous regions marked `MADV_HUGEPAGE`, from a native allocator in the process that we did not identify. Each rank had 0.5-2.5 GB of `AnonHugePages`, growing during the run. - A stack sampler caught scheduler main threads asleep ~30 ms in `lock_mm_and_find_vma`, i.e. a page fault waiting on the mmap lock. - All 32 ranks then waited at the next gather: 10-13 all-rank stalls of ~57 ms per minute. The kernel setting is the system-wide fix, but it needs root and also changes every other process on the node. `prctl(PR_SET_THP_DISABLE)` is per process, needs no privileges, and also covers regions marked `MADV_HUGEPAGE`. ## Modifications - New `SGLANG_DISABLE_THP` (default `false`). title: [Perf] gc: Add --gc-dp-lockstep-steps to collect in lockstep across DP-attention ranks
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With DP attention, every scheduler gathers with all the others once per step (the MLP-sync gather), so a pause on any one rank stalls every rank at the next gather. CPython's full (generation-2) garbage collection is such a pause, and each rank's collector starts one on its own allocation counts: the ranks pause one after another, so a collection cycle costs up to one pause per rank instead of one. We measured this serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PD disaggregation on Vera Rubin, with decode on 32 attention-DP ranks (DEP32), Python 3.12, launched through `sgl.Engine`, which does not run the HTTP server's post-warmup `/freeze_gc` (#49412 proposes that separately). Over one hour of steady load, a per-rank stall tracer showed: - Every ~9.3 minutes, each decode rank ran one automatic full collection of 240-350 ms, scanning ~1.3M long-lived objects (375 were frozen). - The 32 collections landed one after another in a 30-72 s window. That is ~8.5 s of all-rank stall per cycle, ~1.5% of decode time, concentrated in ~10% of the run. - Removing those stalls from each request's timeline (time-uniform sample of ~105k requests) raises per-user decode speed (1000 / TPOT p90) by 3.0%. `--gc-freeze-on-idle-secs` (#50883) freezes only after idle periods, which a continuously loaded decode server does not have, and does not line ranks up. ## Modifications - New `--gc-dp-lockstep-steps N` (default `0`, off). - `SchedulerDPAttnAdapter.before_gather`: an optional callback that `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` runs before every MLP-sync gather. summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation DeepSelect's bf16 top-k sends a batch to a cluster kernel only when the batch fits in one wave of some cluster tier. A larger batch goes to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. That kernel runs every row at once, so its time is set by the longest row in the batch. The DeepSeek-V4.1 decode indexer hits this case. With DSpark (6 verify rows per request) and 40 requests per rank, each index layer runs a top-512 over 240 rows. On a Vera Rubin GPU (SM107, 212 SMs) the widest one-wave tier is the 2-CTA cluster with 106 rows, so all 240 rows go to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. Agentic decode batches mix very different context lengths: in the samples below, the longest row is 2.6-6.3x the mean row. The cluster kernel already launches one cluster per row, and the hardware starts the next row's cluster as an earlier one retires. summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation At decode, the target lm_head is a `[rows, hidden] x [hidden, vocab]` BF16 GEMM with few rows and a large vocabulary, so it streams the weight. title: [Perf] disaggregation: Admit DSpark PD-decode batches without waiting for the in-flight forward
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With the overlap scheduler, a PD decode server admits newly transferred requests in `get_new_prebuilt_batch`. Unless `_nonblocking_admit_in_scope()` holds, the schedule stream first waits for the whole in-flight forward (`schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)`). The admission work (seed, filter, merge, KV allocation: a few dozen small kernels and copies) then sits between that forward and the next one. The non-blocking path already exists: the seed runs on the forward stream after the in-flight forward, and the rest runs on the schedule stream without the wait. Today only EAGLE takes it, under the megakernel runtime switches. Under DP attention, one rank's admission delays all ranks. We profiled 8 ranks of a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP32 PD decode on Vera Rubin (DSpark, 40 running requests per rank). On those ranks, a step that admits requests runs about 45 small serialized ops (about 1% of the step) before the draft forward. Every other rank then waits for it at the draft's first MoE all-to-all. Each rank admits on about a quarter of steps, so at 32 ranks nearly every step has an admitting rank. That costs every rank about 1% of the step. DSpark's seed (`build_dspark_disagg_draft_input`) builds the draft input from the last token and the seq lens, and writes both into the FutureMap. It reads nothing back to the host. It uses neither hidden states nor DSA top-k indices, the two inputs that keep some EAGLE requests on the blocking path. title: [Fix] scheduler: Publish load on every idle batch result under DP attention
summary: ## Motivation The help text of `--load-snapshot-publish-interval` says the load snapshot is published "every N decode iterations. Prefill and idle always publish immediately." That holds for a scheduler that is idle by itself: its loop calls `on_idle`, which publishes right away. It does not hold for an idle rank under DP attention. With `--enable-dp-attention` and more than one DP rank, a rank with nothing of its own to run still steps an idle batch whenever a peer rank has work, so that it takes part in the group's collectives. Its loop then goes through `process_batch_result` and never reaches `on_idle`. `process_batch_result` forced a publish only for extend results, so an idle batch result was throttled like a decode step and the rank's load was refreshed once per publish interval. Until the next refresh, a change in that rank's queues, or the completion of its last request, was missing from both sinks: the load snapshot that DP balancing reads, and the load publisher's socket. ## Modifications - `Scheduler.process_batch_result` forces the publish for idle batch results as well as extend results, for both `publish_load_snapshot` and `load_publisher.publish_load_stat`. Decode results keep the publish interval. - An idle batch is built only when there is more than one DP rank, so an engine without DP attention publishes exactly as before. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_on_idle_load.py` gains `TestBatchResultPublish`. title: [Feat] disaggregation: Report a full decode host pool and landed host-staged transfers in /v1/loads
summary: ## Motivation With decode host receive (`--disaggregation-decode-host-receive-threshold` below 1), a decode engine first receives a transfer's KV into the host pool and moves it to the device later. Two states of that path cannot be seen in `/v1/loads` today: - When the host pool is full, the prealloc admission pass stops without an error. The snapshot then shows ready requests that are not admitted (`queues.prealloc_ready > 0`), which is also what a decode engine with a full device KV pool or no free request slot shows. A reader of `/v1/loads` cannot tell which pool is the limit. - A host-staged transfer whose KV has already landed, and that only waits for the device to admit it, stays in `decode_transfer_queue_reqs` together with transfers still in flight. ## Modifications - `DecodePreallocQueue.host_pool_blocked` is cleared at the start of each `move_preallocated` pass and set when `_pre_alloc_host` stops it. - `DecodeTransferQueue.num_host_staged_landed` is the number of host-staged transfers whose KV landed but that `allocate_host_staged` did not admit on the last `move_transferred` pass. It is reset when the queue is empty. - `DisaggregationMetrics` gains two fields, read by the load inquirer on decode engines: - `decode_host_pool_blocked`: 1 while the last admission pass stopped on a full host pool and at least one ready request is still waiting, else 0. title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Run the Quark FP8 KDA in-proj and MLA absorb on FP8 kernels
summary: ## Motivation - Kimi-K3 decode on MI355X is latency-bound, and with the Quark `AttnFP8` checkpoint the KDA input projection is a large part of each step. - Today the Quark per-channel FP8 KDA in-proj runs as one wide `[q,k,v,g]` GEMM plus separate small GEMMs for `f_a` and `b`. The BF16 in-proj merge (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ`) does not apply, because a raw row concat would drop the FP8 channel scales. - The MLA absorb dequantizes the per-channel FP8 `kv_b_proj` to BF16, so on gfx950 it runs a BF16 BMM even though AITER has an a8w8 BMM for it. - The KDA switch names do not follow the `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_*` env var convention. ## Modifications - **KDA input projection (Quark FP8):** `fused_qkvg_proj` reserves `[f_a | b | pad]` rows at init (192 rows per rank at TP8, so N % 64 == 0 keeps AITER's preshuffled FP8 GEMM). After load, those rows and their channel scales are filled in place, so every batch size runs one FP8 GEMM. Filling in place avoids a post-load realloc that would fragment about 1 GB per GPU. - `kimi_k3.py` asks the ROCm module on every platform, with no new platform branch: `k3_kda_inproj_fp8_tail_rows` (in `kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py`) returns 0 off ROCm, the layer merges only where a tail was reserved (`_merge_kda_inproj_fp8`), and the merged path's f_b GEMM comes from `k3_kda_inproj_fp8_f_b` (AITER's tuned GEMM on gfx95x, the tiny GEMM elsewhere). Main's BF16 merged in-proj block is unchanged. - **MLA absorb (opt-in):** with `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_MLA_ABSORB_FP8=1` on gfx950 with AITER, `kv_b_proj` is requantized to per-tensor FP8 so the absorb BMMs run AITER's a8

title: [Feat] tracing: Stable span names and full rid
summary: ## Motivation A request's trace is hard to find and hard to group: - Root spans are named `Req <first 8 chars of rid>`, and thread spans `Scheduler [TP 0] (host:<id> | pid:<pid>)`. With a per-request or per-process ID in the name, every span gets a unique name, which breaks grouping and aggregation by span name in tracing backends. The IDs are already recorded as attributes. - The `rid` attribute is the rid split on `_`, to drop a worker-ID prefix that multi-tokenizer added to rids (#8964; the split came with #9962). #11295 removed that prefix, so the split now only truncates rids that contain `_`: `req_abc_123` is recorded as `123`, so a request can't be found by its rid. ## Modifications 1. **Create root spans in one function.** `start_root_span` replaces the identical root-span code in `TraceReqContext` and `TraceReqContextAsync`, so the change below applies to both sync and async tracing. Pure refactor, no behavior change. 2. **Stable span names; `rid` recorded as is.** - Root spans are named `Req`, or `prefill Req` / `decode Req` under PD disaggregation. - Thread spans are named `<label> [TP n] [PP n] [DP n]`; `host_id` and `pid` stay attributes. - The `rid` attribute is the full rid. Docs: new "Span Names" section in `production_request_trace.mdx`. ### Behavior changes for existing tracing users | What | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Root span name | `Req 6f97ea7f`, `decode Req 6f97ea7f` | `Req`, `decode Req` | | Thread span name | `Scheduler [TP 0] (host:1a2b3c4d \| pid:123)` | `Scheduler [TP 0]` (`host_id`, `pid` still attributes) | | `rid` attribute | last

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Reserve the decode workspace in the automatic mem_fraction_static
summary: ## What On ROCm with the aiter attention backend, the KV cache budget now leaves room for aiter's decode workspace. The reserve is computed in `KVCacheConfigurator._resolve_memory_pool_config`, after the request pool is resolved, so it sees the final `max_running_requests`, the speculative settings and whether the sliding-window pool is on. - It counts every `AiterAttnBackend` that allocates `workspace_buffer` on the shared request pool: - the target backend, or three with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` (a primary plus two children); - under EAGLE/standalone, the draft runner's own backend, `steps - 1` multi-step decode backends and one draft-extend backend (the draft-extend backend follows `--speculative-attention-mode`); multi-layer EAGLE builds one runner backend and one draft-extend backend per step; frozen-KV MTP only its runner's backend. title: [Fix] benchmark: Handle empty retokenized chunks
summary: ## Motivation and modifications When an emitted text chunk normalizes to no tokens under the reporting tokenizer, speculative-decode ITL accounting divides by zero and loses the complete benchmark report. Carry elapsed time over zero-token chunks until the next token-bearing chunk, then reset the accumulator. Keep trailing zero-token time in end-to-end latency and reset at each request boundary. The regression verifies the accumulated gap, ordinary subsequent gaps, and isolation between two requests. ## Accuracy Tests The regression fails on the original implementation and passes with this change. The complete registered CPU test file passes (3 tests). The final test output is retained locally with the exact branch head.
