title: [Feat] diffusion: Add expert parallelism for MoE DiTs
summary: ## Motivation MoE DiTs are growing, and SP shards activations but not experts: every rank still stores all routed experts. This PR adds expert parallelism (EP) to SGLang Diffusion, with LingBot-Video MoE (128 routed experts) as the first supported model. On 2×H100, EP2 cuts peak memory by 26.2 GB/GPU (43%) for 12% more latency. ## Modifications Two commits: 1. **Fix LingBot SP.** LingBot under SP produced wrong output before this PR (RoPE positions restarted at zero on every rank, and replicated text was gathered as distinct shards). It now shards video tokens inside the DiT, slices global RoPE positions per rank, and passes text as `num_replicated_suffix`. 81 frames are no longer rounded to 85. EP depends on this. 2. **Add EP.** `--ep-size`, a per-pipeline capability gate, expert-sharded checkpoint loading, and a fixed-capacity dispatcher. **Design decision: EP reuses the SP group (`ep_size == sp_degree`).** SP already gives every rank the same token count, so dispatch is one equal-split all-to-all with static shapes and no host sync. Non-local routes carry a `-1` expert ID and are masked; partials are reduced in FP32 by the existing `moe_fused_mul_sum`. | Alternative considered | Result | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | Replicated tokens (no SP) | 1711 vs 1245 ms/step | Keep SP; replication duplicates attention | | Variable-split Torch dispatcher | 1133 vs 1051 ms/step, ~20× more variance | Fixed capacity; no per-block host sync | | Eager / compiled reducer | 3.64 / 1.07 vs 0.211 ms | Reuse `moe_fused_mul_sum` | ## Scope and scaling - Qualified: EP2/SP2, single-node CUDA

summary: ## Motivation `EPLBManager` waits `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations` passes before every rebalance, including the first one. Each rebalance pauses serving, so large EP deployments set a long interval. That makes the first rebalance wait just as long, and until then the server runs on the initial (by default trivial) expert layout, which hurts tail latency early on. This PR adds a separate setting for the first rebalance, so it can come early while later rebalances keep the long interval. title: [Fix] hyperconnection: Refresh derived mix-weight caches on online weight updates
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50835. On SM100, `GatedResidual.mix` builds `self._mix_up_weight_padded` once via `permute_pad_up_weight(...)` on the first batch of at most 24 tokens, and captured CUDA graphs keep that pointer. `permute_pad_up_weight` allocates a new tensor, so the padded copy is a snapshot of the launch weights. `update_weights_from_tensor` writes the live `input_mix_weight_up.weight` and never touches the copy, so after an online weight update small batches keep reading the launch weights while larger batches read the new ones. The update returns 200 and nothing logs. The FlyDSL path has the same hole: `_mix_flydsl_weights` is cached under `weight_cache_key(down, up)` = `(data_ptr, version)`, and in-place loader writes (`param.data.copy_`) change neither, so the packed weights are never re-packed either (inference tensors have no version counter at all). ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/hyperconnection.py`: - Attach a `weight_loader` to `input_mix_weight_down.weight` and `input_mix_weight_up.weight` (`set_weight_attrs`, same pattern as the DSV4 compressor norm weight). The loader copies the weight in place and then refreshes the derived caches: the padded copy is rewritten with `copy_` so captured CUDA graphs keep working through the same storage, and the FlyDSL key is dropped so the next `mix()` re-packs from the new weights. - Set `_direct_weight_update_error` while a derived mix-weight cache can exist (JIT path active, or FlyDSL shapes on a ROCm build), because `load_format='direct'` bypasses `load_weights` and these loaders entirely. title: [Bug] `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` varlen: a non-finite value in one sequence makes the other sequences in the same chunk NaN
summary: ### Describe the bug In a packed (varlen) prefill, the SSD kernels remove the tokens of other sequences by multiplying them with 0 before the dot product. In `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`: `scale = where(seq_idx_k == seq_idx_last, exp(...) * dt_k, 0.0)`, `b *= scale` ([ssd_chunk_state.py#L338-L343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/triton_ops/ssd_chunk_state.py#L338-L343)). The chunk scan relies on `cb = 0` for other sequences and then computes `dot(cb, x)` ([ssd_chunk_scan.py#L475-L489](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/triton_ops/ssd_chunk_scan.py#L475-L489)). If one sequence has an `inf` in x, B or dt, then `inf * 0 = NaN`, and the NaN enters the result of every other sequence in the same chunk. An `inf` in dt also gives `exp(-inf - (-inf)) = NaN` through the chunk cumsum, which is not split by sequence ([ssd_chunk_state.py#L119-L120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/triton_ops/ssd_chunk_state.py#L119-L120)). The NaN final state goes to the SSM state cache, so the other request stays wrong in all later steps. In the script, one `inf` in request 0 (5 tokens) makes all 30 outputs and the final state of request 1 NaN. The expected output of request 1 is finite (8 ... 240). title: [Feat] scheduler: Keep a reserve of KV and state slots for cached prefixes (--prefill-cache-reserve)
summary: ## Motivation On multi-turn agent traffic the prefix cache collapses once the sessions' contexts no longer fit next to the running requests. GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2x B200 (TP2, the 0.9 split that was its default before #50018: 2,969,600 KV tokens, 419 state slots) with coding-agent sessions of about 75K tokens, `lru`: the hit rate is 0.91 at 16 sessions, 0.43 at 40 and 0 at 64. At 64 sessions 58 running requests hold 98% of the KV pool. A session that steps out for a tool call leaves its KV evictable, the next prefill takes it, and the session comes back to a full recompute. The extra prefill keeps decode waiting, so requests hold their KV longer and the next round loses more. The eviction order can't fix this: on the same setup (runs on #49430's branch, where `lru` is main's policy and the policy was still called `gds`; #49430 was reverted in #50118 and is now the opt-in `state_cost` in #50122) `lru` and `gds` both had a 0 hit rate at 64 sessions, since almost nothing is left to choose from. `--enable-session-radix-cache` (#29173) only evicts unreferenced KV first; with every session still open all of it is referenced, so I did not expect it to help and did not measure it. Admission can: a request that reuses little of the cache should wait for running requests to finish rather than take the room other sessions are about to come back to. This adds `--prefill-cache-reserve R` (off by default). title: [Feature] Add per-request skip_detokenize option to sglang.api.v1.GenerateRequest
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation In `rust/sglang-server`, `--skip-tokenizer-init` controls server detokenization globally at startup (`DetokenizerBackend::Skip` vs `Dynamo`). On a standard pool, `sglang.api.v1.SglangService/Generate` detokenizes every output chunk into `text` alongside `output_ids`. Token clients consume `output_ids` only, so server detokenization wastes CPU for them. Conversely, a `--skip-tokenizer-init` pool cannot serve text-output requests, which forces operators to maintain separate worker pools. Even on dedicated token-output pools, `--skip-tokenizer-init` disables scheduler features that depend on the vocabulary. Without a loaded tokenizer, the scheduler leaves `grammar_backend` unset and aborts `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` requests with `400`. It also rejects `min_new_tokens > 0` and omits tokenizer EOS and `additional_stop_token_ids`. Per-request `skip_detokenize` keeps vocabulary-dependent generation active on standard pools and skips output and logprob UTF-8 decoding. **Proposal:** - Add `bool skip_detokenize` to `GenerateRequest` in `proto/sglang/api/v1/generate.proto` (to match Python `return_text` and vLLM `ResponseOptions.output_text`). - When `skip_detokenize` is `true`, skip output and logprob UTF-8 decoding for that request and emit `output_ids` and `meta_info` only. ### Related resources - #492

title: [Fix] marlin: Prevent scale underflow in NVFP4 fallback on SM80-SM90 (#44998)
summary: fixes #44998 when running nvfp4 on pre-blackwell gpus with marlin, checkpoints that have small block scales (like weight_scale_2 = 1.0 from modelopt, probec, or llm-compressor) underflow during bf16 dequantization. the marlin packing does `(scales * 2^7).view(int16) << 1` which assumes `scales * 2^7 >= 2`. with small scales, the top bit is unset and bf16 exponent widening causes the weights to dequantize to zero, corrupting output. ported the fix from vllm #34577: - added `_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor` to upscale small block scales by a power of 2 so `scales * 2^7 >= 2` - clamped subnormals (`scales < 2`) to zero to prevent bit corruptions - compensated by dividing `weight_global_scale` by `scale_factor` - unified the scale factor across experts in `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin` - added unit tests covering scale factor computation, dense/moe scale adjustment, and underflow prevention <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #44382539357](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/44382539357)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #44382539143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/44382539143)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->⊘ **Skipped** -- add the `run-ci` label to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end --> > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Perf] diffusion: fix 5 quantization-layer overheads (NVFP4 scale conversion, BnB, Nunchaku)
summary: Fixes #46302. Five independent, minimal fixes to real overheads in the diffusion (`multimodal_gen`) quantization layer. Each is its own commit. Tests are folded into the closest existing test file for each change (no new test files), reusing existing fixtures/imports wherever one already fit, plus a GPU benchmark for the NVFP4 scale conversion fix. ## Commits 1. **NVFP4 scale TMA conversion: avoid GPU->CPU->GPU round trip.** `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` built the padded TMA scale buffer with a device-less `torch.zeros(...)`, forcing scales off and back onto the GPU on every load. Calls the existing on-device `_linear_nvfp4_scales_to_tma` helper instead. 2. **Dynamic NVFP4: cache `weight_scale_2.max()` at load.** It's fixed after loading; stop reducing the tensor on every forward. 3. **Comfy full-precision NVFP4: unswizzle scales once at load**, not on every forward. Scoped under its own attribute (`_weight_scale_linear`) since the sibling dynamic-activation-quant method still needs `weight_scale` swizzled. 4. **BnB 4-bit: skip the output-buffer copy for a single unfused shard.** Calls `matmul_4bit` directly in the common (non-fused) case. 5. **Nunchaku: lazily read only the needed scale tensors** via `safetensors.safe_open` instead of deserializing the entire checkpoint (including the bulk int4 weights) with `load_file`. ## Benchmark (Modal T4, torch 2.14.1+cu130, transformers 5.19.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10+cu130, CUDA 13.0) **Fix 1 - NVFP4 scale TMA conversion** (scales shape 3072x256, 200 iters): | | ms/call | |---|---| | old (CPU round trip) | 1.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] cosmos3: Fix multi-node execution
summary: # [Fix] diffusion/cosmos3: Fix multi-node CFG-parallel FSDP desyncs and auto_tune GPU probing ## Motivation Serving a Cosmos3 checkpoint that only fits with FSDP sharded across nodes (`--use-fsdp-inference --cfg-parallel-size 2 --ulysses-degree 4 --nnodes 2`) hits three independent bugs: 1. **Startup fails on multi-node launches.** `auto_tune` probes `num_gpus` device ids on every node, but `num_gpus` is the total across nodes: `AssertionError: Invalid device id`. 2. **T2I returns a corrupted image, then the server hangs.** The default T2I `guidance_interval` turns CFG off partway through the request. During CFG-split steps each CFG rank caches only its own UND K/V entry, so at the first no-CFG step one rank misses its cache and reruns the UND layers. Under FSDP that issues all-gathers the other ranks never match: the collectives pair the wrong layers (equal shard sizes, so NCCL does not error), one node returns an image built from mixed-layer weights, and the other node hangs until the NCCL watchdog fires. Every later request then hangs as well. 3. **Transfer with control-CFG + text CFG desyncs the same way.** Three CFG branches on two ranks give one rank two forwards and the other one, so the ranks issue different numbers of FSDP all-gathers. ## Modifications - `auto_tune.py`: probe `num_gpus // nnodes` local GPUs. - `Cosmos3DenoisingStage._denoise_once`: track each step's CFG split mode (`"control"`, `"text"` or none) and call `transformer.reset_cache()` on every rank when it changes, so all ranks recompute the UND prefix in the same step. summary: ## TL;DR - **Bug:** requests accepted at the advertised context boundary can return two fewer tokens than requested. - **Cause:** a legacy output-token reserve introduced by #1748 remains in the scheduler even though exact-boundary requests are now valid (#22546) and page-aware KV admission is enforced separately (#25126). - **Fix:** use `max_req_len - input_len + 1`, while leaving the separate global KV memory clamp (now `max_new_tokens_for_memory`) unchanged. - **Safety:** generating `N` tokens forwards the prompt and only the first `N - 1` generated tokens; the final token is sampled and returned without another decode step. - **Validation:** focused scheduler tests (re-run after merging current `main`), end-to-end boundary tests on Qwen3/Qwen3.5, speculative-decoding coverage, and an independent behavior cross-check against Mini-SGLang. ## Motivation Requests that fit the advertised context length are silently clipped by two tokens in the scheduler. SGLang's public validation permits requests whose total length is exactly the model context length: ```text input_len + max_new_tokens <= context_len ``` This boundary was explicitly adopted in #22546 after the same behavior was reported in discussion #16020. title: [Fix] dsa: Read paged MQA logits schedule after griddepcontrol_wait
summary: ## Motivation `FP8MQALogitsKernel` (`cutedsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.py`) is launched with PDL by default (`enable_pdl=True`). Its prologue reads two inputs before `cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()`: - `mScheduleMeta[(sm_idx, 0..1)]` and `mScheduleMeta[(sm_idx + 1, 0..1)]` - `mContextLens[start_q_clamped]` Both tensors are produced on the same stream by earlier kernels: the schedule metadata by `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`, and the context lens by the kernels that update the sequence lengths for the current step. Under programmatic dependent launch, a dependent grid may start before its primary grid finishes. Only `griddepcontrol.wait` guarantees that the primary grid has completed and its memory writes are visible. Loads issued before the wait therefore race with the producing kernel and can observe values from the previous launch. The race matters most in CUDA-graph decode, where the same buffers are rewritten on every replay. A stale schedule entry or context length gives a CTA the wrong work range or KV length. The kernel then walks block-table entries that belong to a different request, or that lie past the valid range of its own request. ## Modifications - Move the schedule-metadata and context-lens loads, and the scheduler values derived from them, to just after `griddepcontrol_wait()`. - Keep the TMA descriptor prefetch, SMEM allocation and pipeline initialisation before the wait. They depend only on kernel parameters, so they still overlap with the tail of the primary grid. - No change when PDL is disabled, and no change to the kernel's arithmetic. ## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] detokenizer: Keep generated text after a mid-character prompt end with byte-fallback tokenizers
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51308. When a token-id prompt ends inside a UTF-8 character that the output completes, `DetokenizeState.step` slices `read_text` at `len(surr_text)`. Byte-fallback decoders (SentencePiece `<0xNN>` pieces, e.g. Gemma-4) emit one U+FFFD per dangling byte, so the slice skips up to three generated characters, in streaming and non-streaming output. Byte-level BPE emits one U+FFFD for the whole incomplete sequence and is not affected. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/managers/incremental_detokenize.py`: - `_new_text_start(surr_text, read_text)` returns `len(surr_text)` unless `surr_text` ends in U+FFFD and the new ids rewrite those U+FFFDs. In that case it skips the U+FFFDs that stayed invalid, then the characters made entirely of the dangling bytes, plus the one straddling character. That is the text main already returns for byte-level tokenizers, which always get the same slice as before. - When a streaming step completes such a split character, `surr_offset` is kept for that one commit. Otherwise the next window starts inside the byte run, and a byte-fallback run that continues past the boundary decodes as U+FFFD (`'ฃ��� ok'` instead of `'ฃฦ ok'`). The straddling character itself is still dropped, as it is for byte-level tokenizers today. Emitting it instead would be a one-character change (`pos` instead of `pos + 1`). Not changed: when the 5-token prompt tail itself starts inside a byte-fallback run, that run still decodes as U+FFFD, as on main. title: [Feat] kimi-k3: DWDP for KDA and shared-expert weights on PD prefill
summary: **Motivation.** Under attention DP, every Kimi-K3 PD prefill rank holds every KDA layer's `[q,k,v,g]` in-projection and `o_proj` (60.8 GB BF16 per rank at attention TP 1), plus 24 GB of replicated shared experts under an EP all-to-all backend. ADP8 then barely fits on 8 x GB300. **Change.** `--kda-dwdp-size N` (DWDP for the KDA projection and shared-expert weights; opt-in, `--disaggregation-mode prefill` only) shards those weights across N attention-DP ranks, and gathers the next layer into the other of two rotating slots on a copy stream while the current layer computes. - **Head-aligned layout:** rank r stores exactly tensor-parallel rank r's slice (heads/N rows of each of q / k / v / g, the matching o_proj columns), so with N == TP the shard is byte-identical to KDA TP rank r's weights. N may be any divisor of the attention-DP size that splits the heads. - **Gather:** copy-engine peer pulls from a cuMem shard mapped on every group rank with `cuda_vmm_utils` (one copy per in-proj block, one `cuMemcpy2DAsync` per o_proj column slice). It uses no SMs, no collective and no replica. The slot is the replicated layout, so prefill outputs are bitwise identical to replicated weights. - **Gates:** prefill role only; refuses PP, attention CP, full CUDA graphs, loaders that skip `load_weights`, the weight cache, quantized sharded weights, a second K3 model, online weight updates, and non-Kimi-K3 models. **Results** (Kimi-K3 truncated to 40 layers, GB300:4, EP4 MegaMoE with #50838, aggregated prefill proxy): | Input | ADP4 TTFT / batch-4 tok/s | ADP4 + DWDP4 | TP4 (reference) | |---|

title: [Perf] hicache: optional minimum tokens per write_back allocation-driven eviction
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache `write_back`, an allocation-driven device eviction waits once for the forward running on the device (the write fence) before its victims' copies to the host pool complete. The allocator asks only for its shortfall, so a busy prefill server evicts many small batches and pays that wait each time. On post-#46930 `main`, @xiezhq-hermann measured the remaining single wait per walk as most of the eviction time (28% of scheduler wall time at 80 req/s, 46% at saturation, 87-91% of it that wait; see the review below). ## Modifications - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_HICACHE_WRITE_BACK_MIN_EVICT_TOKENS` (`EnvInt`, default 0 = off): the minimum Full KV tokens one write_back allocation-driven eviction frees. - `unified_radix_cache.py` `evict_pool_shortfalls` (where prefill and decode capacity, HiCache load-back and PD decode preallocation evictions converge since #48012): under write_back, when `0 < token shortfall < value`, the token shortfall is raised to the value and the token entry of the `demand` handed to `_evict` by the same amount. Raising the demand matters: the walk stops at the first victim after which its pool can serve the demand, so raising only the token count would free nothing extra. `_write_back_batch_tokens` then takes the whole floor as one batch behind one wait. The cheap shortfall check runs before reading `is_write_back`, so a disabled floor never reaches it. - Scope: Full KV only. Window and state shortfalls, explicit `evict()` / `evict_until()`, `--enable-unified-memory` (`reclaim_jointly`) and non-write_back policies are unchanged. - `docs/

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add opt-in reasoning-effort KV budgets
summary: ## Motivation Running requests currently share the scheduler's new-token ratio regardless of reasoning effort. This adds an opt-in way to use effort tiers when budgeting their future decode growth during prefill admission. Related to #42915. This PR implements a separate **KV admission-budget** capability; it does not implement the RFC's DP routing or retraction-victim policies and should not close that RFC. ## Modifications Add `--reasoning-effort-kv-budget {off,scaled,adaptive}`, defaulting to `off`: - **off:** retain existing admission behavior. - **scaled:** multiply the initial reservation by a tier-specific factor and divide the accumulated global ratio decay by that factor. Higher tiers reserve more and decay more slowly; lower tiers reserve less and decay faster. Simply multiplying the current ratio would not provide the intended decay behavior. - **adaptive:** use the mean of recent completed output lengths for the request's tier. The difference between that mean (capped by the request limit) and generated length scales the accumulated decay. Normalization uses the existing clipped admission demand, so large `max_new_tokens` values do not collapse all tiers onto the same fastest-decay setting. Requests that outlive the mean recover a ratio of 1 rather than losing their reservation. Chat Completions forwards recognized effort metadata after template/default normalization. Native `/generate` accepts `reasoning_effort_hint` as scheduling-only metadata. Batch splitting, parallel sampling and tokenizer-to-scheduler IPC preserve the hint; new positional fields are append

title: [Refactor] [AMD] mxfp8-moe: Remove redundant output zero-fill
summary: ## Motivation The gfx950 native MXFP8 MoE grouped GEMM zero-initializes an output that its kernel overwrites completely. This adds redundant work on the native Triton path, including two grouped GEMMs per MoE call. EP-filtered routes are retained by `moe_align_block_size`. Their invalid expert IDs mask the weight loads to zero, but the final store still writes those route rows. Padding token IDs fail the store mask and do not correspond to output rows. ## Modifications - Replace this output's `torch.zeros` allocation with `torch.empty`; keep the kernel and routing unchanged. - Extend the existing MoE tests with a small-route, large-K shape (`T * top_k = 8`, `K = 3072`) and NaN-poisoned EP output allocation. Check both combined and per-route output, including exact zeros for filtered routes. ## Accuracy Tests Tested against base `063d9d4af835c0a2bf250e8ed4b9ae0b239cc227` on one AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0 / HIP 7.15.26333: ```bash python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_minimax_m3_mxfp8.py -k native_moe ``` With the same test overlay, base and head each passed all 7 selected cases, with zero errors or skips. The existing reference tolerance is unchanged. As a sensitivity control, adding `valid_expert` to the kernel's final store mask deliberately leaves filtered rows unwritten; both poisoned EP cases then fail at the finite-output assertion. The three benchmark fixtures also produced bitwise-identical base/head outputs. These are native-kernel/wrapper correctness checks; no model-level accuracy result is claime

title: [Perf] Foundry: adding the adapter of foundry to enable fast CUDA graph save/load
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation [Foundry](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry) persists CUDA graphs across restarts. The first start (`save`) archives the captured graphs, their kernels and the device-memory layout. Later starts (`load`) rebuild the graphs from the archive instead of capturing them, so an engine that spends 40-120 s capturing 128 decode graphs per rank is serving within a few seconds of the eager engine. Foundry hooks the CUDA driver (an `LD_PRELOAD` library, like `torch_memory_saver`) and needs SGLang to call it at a few points of the engine bring-up. This PR adds it the way SGLang integrates `torch_memory_saver`: an optional dependency behind an adapter that is a no-op unless the feature is enabled, a server argument, and explicit one-line call sites. The call sites pass only the values Foundry needs (the loaded model, the draft-worker flag, the resolved pool config, the prefill request slots), never a runner or backend object. It replaces the plugin approach of #41791, which maintainers considered unsuitable for an extension that needs runtime call sites. Outside the configurations Foundry supports, the engine starts natively and says why (see Modifications, 3). ## Modifications Eleven commits on `main` (`cbbc6b67f4`), 37 files, +1863 / -51. This assumes weight N and K dimensions are always multiples of the block size. When they are not, the transpose guards fail to fire and the subsequent shape assertions raise an `AssertionError` on load. title: [Fix] openai: Answer a stream refused before its first chunk with its status
summary: ## Motivation With `--max-queued-requests` (or a waiting timeout), the scheduler refuses a request it cannot queue with an abort that carries a status: 503 `The request queue is full.`. A non-streaming request gets HTTP 503. A streaming `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/completions` request gets HTTP 200 with `data: {"error": {..., "code": 503}}` and `data: [DONE]` as its body. A router or load balancer in front of several workers sees the 200 as a success, so a refused stream is never retried on a worker with room. We hit this with sgl-model-gateway in front of SGLang workers. When one worker was full, non-streaming requests were retried on the free worker. Streaming requests came back as 200 from the full worker, carrying only the error. The streaming handlers already read the first chunk before sending the status line ("Kick-start the generator to trigger validation before HTTP 200 is sent"), and a `ValueError` raised there already becomes a 400. An error abort that arrives at that point is streamed in-band instead. #28175 and #43779 (draft, conflicts with main) address the same problem. This PR is a smaller change on current main. ## Modifications - `serving_base.py`: `raise_error_abort(finish_reason)` raises what `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason` raises for a non-streaming request: a `ValueError` for a 400, an `HTTPException` for any other 4xx/5xx. - `serving_chat.py`, `serving_completions.py`: an error abort that arrives before the first chunk is raised through it, and `handle_request` answers it as it answers the non-streaming request. title: [Fix] hicache: Look up L3 below a device-only anchor under write-back
summary: ## Motivation `Scheduler._prefetch_kvcache` looks up L3 only from a backed-up anchor or the root (plus buffer mode), assuming an unbacked anchor means a storage miss. That holds for write-through, whose host copy is contiguous from the root, but not for `write_back`: a prefix stays on device with no host copy while another writer, e.g. a PD decode offloading its output KV, has stored the continuation. The prefill never looks it up and recomputes it. End to end (PD with decode KV offload and a `write_back` prefill, window 512, page 128), the second turn's prefill reuse of the 256 tokens the decode wrote: **0 before, 256 after**. Run on a fork carrying this change. ## Modifications The tree already keeps a host-only suffix below a device-only anchor under `write_back`, so the lookup opens there: ```diff or ( - buffer_mode + (buffer_mode or tree_cache.is_write_back) and tree_cache.get_last_hash_value(last_host_node) is not None ) ``` Cost: one existence query for a `write_back` request whose deepest match is device-only and whose rest reaches the prefetch threshold. Write-through and buffer mode are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests No kernel or forward change. | test | before | after | |---|---|---| | `test_write_back_prefetch_looks_up_storage_below_a_device_anchor` (new; drives `Scheduler._prefetch_kvcache` on a real `write_back` tree) | fails in every HiCache config (no prefetch issued) | passes | `test_unified_radix_cache_storage.py`: 227 passed, 0 failed. Related: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46934, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46935, https://github

title: [Feat] inkling2: Let MegaMoE take only this rank's tokens
summary: ## Motivation `Inkling2MegaMoE` (#51048) takes the full batch on every rank and slices out the tokens the rank dispatches. sgl-project/sglang#50899 computes the MoE input (AttnRes, `mlp_norm`, router, top-k) only for those rows, so its caller already holds the slice. The op on main needs to take that slice directly, so that the model wiring can use #50899's change once the Inkling2 model is on main. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/inkling2_mega_moe.py`: - `Inkling2MegaMoE.token_slice(num_tokens)` returns the `(start, count)` of the tokens this rank dispatches. Same split as before. - `Inkling2MegaMoE.__call__(x, topk_weights, topk_ids, num_tokens=None)`: with `num_tokens`, the inputs hold only this rank's `token_slice(num_tokens)` rows. The output still covers all `num_tokens` tokens. Without it, the behavior is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not committed: the check needs 4 GPUs and DeepGEMM MegaMoE. B300, EP4, sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.9, 64 experts, top-8, hidden 4096, intermediate 1536, random weights. On every rank the output with the pre-sliced input is bitwise equal to the full-batch call, for MXFP8 and NVFP4 at 3 tokens (ranks with no tokens), 1028, 4099 (the last rank gets a shorter slice) and 8192 tokens. Two full-batch calls are also bitwise equal to each other. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel change. #50899 measured the model-side gain: +9.1% prefill throughput and −9% mean TTFT at TP4 / EP4 on Vera Rubin. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-tes

title: [Perf] [AMD] gdn: ReplaySSM verify q/k prep kernel and layer-loop commit
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` and MTP (4 draft tokens, the default ring of 16), every verify step runs `gdn_replayssm_spec_decode` once per GDN layer and `commit_gdn_replayssm_circular` once for all of them. On gfx950 two parts of that work repeat: - The verify grid is (V tiles, requests, value heads). Each program L2-normalizes its key head's q and k, splits k into BF16 high and low parts and forms `k @ k^T` and `k @ q^T`, which depend only on the request and the key head. The kernel takes 262 VGPRs (64-wide V tile) or 334 (128-wide), one wave per SIMD, so MI355X runs 1,024 of its programs at a time; at 16 key and 48 value heads a step of 11 requests needs a second round. - The commit grid is (V tiles, requests, value heads x layers). With track rows, which the radix cache passes, the kernel takes 168 VGPRs (3 waves per SIMD; 6 without track rows), and every program reloads its request's slot, cursors and track entry to fold one layer. This PR computes the q/k part once per (request, key head) in a new kernel, which brings the verify kernel to 144 VGPRs (3 waves per SIMD), and folds all layers of a (V tile, request, value head) in one program. The arithmetic and its order are unchanged, so outputs, rings and checkpoints are bitwise those of `main`. On one MI355X at 16 key and 48 value heads and 36 GDN layers (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at TP1), the GDN verify and commit of a step take 8.8 to 25.4 % less from 11 to 128 requests; at six other head and layer counts, 8.3 to 26.9 % less where the new launches run. title: [Feat] [AMD] kv-shard: Support KV cache sharding with aiter and MoRI

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Restore request padding after KV resume
summary: ## Motivation `req_to_token` maps request/token positions to KV-cache locations. Row 0 is initialized to zero and reserved for dummy requests used to pad a CUDA graph batch; real requests use the other rows. With memory saver enabled, releasing `kv_cache` unbacks this table along with the KV allocations. Resuming remaps the memory without preserving its previous contents, but the padding row is not initialized again. Newly admitted real requests populate their own rows, while row 0 can remain uninitialized. A subsequent padded graph replay can read that row while building the attention page table, even though the padded request's output is discarded. An uninitialized entry can point to an unrelated or out-of-range KV page. For example, in the FlashMLA page-table builder with page size 64, an entry of 6400 would select page 100 instead of the reserved padding page 0. Depending on the backend and the resulting index, this can cause a device memory access error or incorrect inference output; it may also appear to work if the remapped bytes happen to be zero. A targeted H20 test detected uninitialized reads after resume, even though the remapped bytes happened to be zero. Separate model inference did not show incorrect output. The test configuration and fix validation are described below. ## Modifications Restore the padding row to zero after KV memory resumes. Add a CPU regression test that simulates nonzero data after resume and checks that real request rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - CPU: `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_sched

title: Perf [AMD] all-reduce tuner for graph and eager mode
summary: ## Motivation This is a significant modification of [#34838](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34838), which introduced `python/sglang/auto_tune/allreduce_tuner.py` as item 4 of the auto-tuner roadmap ([#13363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13363)). That PR established the idea and the file: time the all-reduce backends and write the best one per message size to a JSON table. It kept to four backends, derived the sizes from the model config, timed eager calls only, and ran from a `--allreduce` flag on the auto-tune main flow. What is kept from it is the shape of the output and the place in the tree. What is new here is a second timing mode for CUDA graphs, a selection file that names who competes, cross-rank agreement before entering any collective, and the synchronisation needed to keep eight ranks from wedging in a timing loop. The entry point is a standalone torchrun module that starts no server and loads no model. Which all-reduce backend is fastest depends on the message size, the hardware, and whether the call is replayed from a CUDA graph. New all-reduce implementations keep landing (another custom all-reduce, another QuickReduce codec, FlyDSL INT4), and the only way to know where each one wins is to time them against each other on the machine before a model is started. The tuner is the tool for that: it opens the kernels the selection names, times them at the sizes you list, and writes the winner per size. ## Workflow Commands, example output for each mode, and the stack-dump guide are in `python/sglang/auto_tune/README.md`. summary: ## Motivation LFM3 interleaves gated short-conv layers with full-attention and 256-token sliding-window layers, which is exactly the shape the hybrid SWA KV cache path exists for. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Scale int8 mamba checkpoints per value channel for scalar-gate models
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint` stores cached recurrent states as int8 with one scale per (head, k-channel): `amax(dim=-2)` over `S [H, d_v, d_k]`. The docstring motivates that axis with the per-k-channel decay `diag(alpha)`. That is KDA's gate. GDN and Mamba2 decay a head with one scalar, and for them the per-k axis costs accuracy on every cache hit. On Qwen3.5-9B, moving the scale to the value axis removes most of the extra divergence of an int8 cache hit, at the same bytes and the same store/load cost (numbers below). Why the axis matters, from `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`: - `S` is only read contracted over k: the readout `b_o = sum(b_h * b_q[None, :], 1)` and the erase `b_v -= sum(b_h * b_k[None, :], 1)`. The rounding error of row `v` therefore lands in output channel `v` and no other. - Row `v` is written by value channel `v` (`b_h += b_v[:, None] * b_k[None, :]`), so the rows inherit the magnitudes of the value channels. - One scale per k-column rounds every row with the step of that column's largest row. Value channels with small rows keep only a few of the 8 bits. - KDA is different: `b_h *= exp(b_gk[None, :])` decays each column on its own, which is what the per-k scale was designed around. GDN has `b_h *= exp(b_g)`, one scalar per head. `test_int8_mamba_checkpoint_e2e.py` already records the symptom on a GDN model: its int8 thresholds sit about 10x above the bf16/fp8 reuse tests, with the comment that "int8 is a lossy codec". title: [Perf] scheduler: Skip SWA admission only during global capacity exhaustion
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid SWA admission needs to retry as running decode releases capacity. Retrying when the full KV pool is globally exhausted repeats queue matching and external-cache lookups that cannot admit any candidate. ## Modifications Cache an admission refusal only for non-CP budgets with no remaining current full-pool capacity. Poll storage-prefetch completions before this gate. Resume admission as soon as capacity becomes positive. Candidate-specific refusals (including window pressure and future-token reservations), CP padding, and joint-pool budgets retry every round. Priority preemption, an empty running batch, and chunk continuation retain their progress paths. This deliberately narrows the optimization: a shorter request, a better prefix hit, or reduced decode reservations may permit admission without physical capacity growth, so those cases must not reuse a capacity-only refusal. ## Validation - CPU checks executing the actual scheduler gate and budget methods passed: reservation improvement, candidate replacement/prefix changes, global exhaustion/release, completion polling, CP/joint-pool fallback, preemption, chunk continuation, and empty batches. - Updated the existing prefill-adder regression to distinguish candidate-specific refusals from global exhaustion. - Full registered tests and GPU/model validation were not run locally because the required runtime dependencies are unavailable. - No new performance measurements are claimed. Earlier measurements of the broader gate do not establish performance of this narrowed implementation. <!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [Perf] all_reduce_fusion: Compile the cluster-size variants in parallel
summary: ## Motivation The fused MoE-finalize / all-reduce / RMSNorm kernels are compiled once per `cluster_size`. The launch geometry chooses the cluster size from the token count, so CUDA graph capture hits each size at a different batch and stalls on one nvcc compile after another. MiniMax-M3.1 (TP4, hidden 6144) needs 3 cluster sizes for each of 2 modules, about 6 s per compile, all paid serially inside target-verify capture when the JIT cache is empty. ## Modifications - When `_jit_module` is first called for a `(world_size, hidden_dim, top_k, weight_dtype)`, it compiles every cluster size the launch geometry can select (the default plus the two-shot table entries that are valid for this hidden size), in parallel threads, and waits for all of them before returning. - The compiles still happen at first use, in eager execution and never during capture. With a warm cache this is a few cache loads. - Kernel code and the kernels that get selected are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests No kernel change. `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_all_reduce_residual_norm.py` (4 GPUs) passes on main and on this PR: 7 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4 + DSPARK on B200, with an empty sglang JIT cache and every other cache warm. title: [Fix] diffusion: keep TP/Ulysses head shards on the unsharded torch SDPA kernel
summary: ## Motivation PyTorch's flash SDPA forward picks split-KV when `batch * heads * ceil(query_len / 128)` is below 80% of the SM count (`num_splits_heuristic` in ATen's `flash_api.cpp`). Split-KV reorders the softmax sums. Tensor parallelism and Ulysses both reduce the number of heads each rank attends over. At short sequence lengths, that can push a head shard onto the split kernel while the unsharded layer stays unsplit. The result is that `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` runs differ between parallel and single-GPU execution even at the attention-operator level. The default backends do not depend on the head count, and are unaffected: - sm100: cuDNN SDPA. Measured on B200: head shards are bit-identical. - sm90: sgl FA3, which runs with `num_splits=1`. Affected setups: - explicit `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`; - sm120, where torch SDPA is the default; - head dims that fall back to torch SDPA. This came up while validating Ovis-Image (#43152), which carries a model-local version of this fix. ## Modifications - **`SDPAImpl`** pads query rows past the split threshold when all of the following hold: - the request asks for `quality="exact"`; - the call is a non-causal, unmasked fp16/bf16 CUDA call, without dropout and with head_dim ≤ 256; - the local head count would split, but the unsharded layer's would not. Query rows attend independently, so the real rows match the unsharded kernel bit for bit. The padding is sliced off afterwards. - **Gated on `exact`**: under the quality tiers, the default `lossless` tier already allows rounding-order changes. It keeps the faster split ke

title: [Fix] attention: Bound FP8 KV-cache reads in FlashInfer MLA prefill and decode
summary: ## Motivation Addresses the FlashInfer MLA portion of [#35291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35291). Paged prefill and decode cast the entire per-layer FP8 KV pool to the query dtype on every forward, including unused slots. Conversion work and temporary memory therefore scale with allocated pool capacity. This change reads the rows referenced by the attention plan when that reduces the temporary allocation. The separate FA3 path remains outside this PR's scope. ## Modifications - Eager paged prefill/decode gather referenced rows as bytes, convert the compact copy, and plan FlashInfer over consecutive compact IDs. This accounts for both the FP8 gather and its BF16/FP16 output. A fixed-grid Triton kernel reads the live row count from device metadata, so replay follows updated indices and sequence lengths. - Share the shadow across layers and the primary/child TBO backends, whose attention calls execute serially on the compute stream. Each backend retains its own attention metadata. - Preserve the existing E4M3 graph path below SM89, and the existing paths for non-FP8 caches, speculative decoding/verification, DCP and ragged prefill. title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3.1: Exchange DCP8 attention partials in one IPC kernel and row-shard the MoE tail at decode
summary: ## Motivation In a Kimi-K3.1-Pro decode trace on MI355X (TP8 / DCP8, DFLASH verify at about 435 rows), the DCP8 attention exchange (pack kernel + RCCL `all_to_all`) costs 62-66 µs per DSA layer, 29 calls a step. title: [Bug] dsv41: Candidate graph variants can differ across attention-DP ranks (decode and DSpark verify)
summary: ## Problem Under DP attention the ranks replay their CUDA/HIP graphs in lockstep, and some collectives captured in them (custom all-reduce, aiter all-gather / reduce-scatter) register that graph's input buffers. If two ranks replay different graph variants in the same step, a rank reads its peer's buffer from the other graph, which holds stale data. `Dsv41CandidateGraphVariants` (DeepSeek-V4.1, SM100+ and gfx95) still selects from each rank's own lengths: - Decode: ranks holding different requests can pick different candidates; an idle rank has no lengths and takes `candidate_filtered`. - DSpark target verify: busy ranks select from their committed lengths plus `verify_extra_tokens`. An idle rank stays `IDLE` (no ragged layout) or runs `TARGET_VERIFY` with all-ones lengths (ragged layout), so it can pick a different variant. `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_METADATA_EARLY` is off under DP attention (`_wants_early_verify_metadata()`), so verify does not need its own lengths for early staging there. #48302 fixes the same issue for `DsaGraphVariants` and `SeqLenBucketGraphVariants`: an upper bound of each rank's longest decode sequence rides the existing MLP-sync all-gather (`dp_decode_graph_max_seq_len`), and those classes select from the maximum over ranks in decode / idle. DSV4.1 was left out of that PR (review: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48302#discussion_r4595135900). ## Proposed fix - Under DP attention, select DSV4.1 candidates from the global bound in decode, idle and target verify alike (`select_for_max_seq_len(bound)`, which adds `verify_extra_tokens`), includ

title: [Fix] grpc: Allow --tokenizer-worker-num > 1 with --grpc-port in Rust-server mode
summary: ## Context (TL;DR) - **Report:** a Dynamo deployment of SGLang behind Dynamo's gRPC sidecar could not raise `--tokenizer-worker-num` above 1, because `--grpc-port` refuses it. At high throughput the single TokenizerManager then caps the engine. With token-in requests the sidecar has already tokenized, but every request and output chunk still goes through that one process: request state, conversion, and pickled IPC to the scheduler (`SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC` defaults on). - **Why the Python path can't simply scale:** the native gRPC server (`sglang.runtime.v1`) runs in the single-tokenizer process and calls `TokenizerManager` through PyO3. With N tokenizer workers, the main process holds only `MultiTokenizerRouter`, so there is no TokenizerManager to attach the bridge to. - **The fix on the Dynamo side is to move to `sglang.api.v1` on SGLang's Rust server (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`).** The Rust server replaces the Python TokenizerManager and DetokenizerManager with Rust threads inside the scheduler process: msgpack over in-process channels, no pickle, no GIL hop per request. Dynamo's sidecar port to `api.v1` is in review: - ai-dynamo/dynamo#17219: replace `runtime.v1` with `sglang.api.v1` - ai-dynamo/dynamo#17368: move the SGLang mocker and sidecar testkit to `api.v1` - ai-dynamo/dynamo#17431: run the launch scripts and deploys on SGLang's Rust server - ai-dynamo/dynamo#17610 and ai-dynamo/dynamo#17612: one sidecar per node for DP - **Gap this PR closes:** the same `--grpc-port` check also fires in Rust-server mode, where it doesn't apply. title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Score relative prefill rows with one stage on gfx95
summary: ## Motivation On gfx95, `tilelang_qsa_mqa_prefill_relative`, which scores the QSA indexer's extend rows against their request's compressed keys, runs the kernel's default three K-tile pipeline stages. A CTA holds a 128 x 128 Q tile (32 KB in bf16) and a 64 x 128 K tile per stage (16 KB): 80 KB with three stages, so two CTAs fit in a CU's 160 KB of LDS. With one stage a CTA needs 48 KB and three fit. This PR launches the kernel with one stage on gfx95. The scores are the same, bit for bit. On one MI355X, for a 16,384-token extend chunk on an 83,968-token prefix, one layer's scoring kernel takes 19.6 % less time (1,819.3 to 1,462.8 µs) and the layer's whole prefill selection 9.5 % less (3,528.7 to 3,194.4 µs), medians of three runs. There the indexer scores 1,312 rows at a time, 656 CTAs a launch (41 row blocks x 16 key splits) for 256 CUs. Limits: - gfx95 only. Other platforms keep three stages. - Without a prefix it is slower: 16,384 rows on 0 cached tokens (4,096 blocks a row) take 3.6 % longer in the kernel and 0.5 % longer in the whole selection. There the indexer scores 8,192 rows at a time, 512 CTAs a launch, two a CU, which fit with three stages too. - Served end-to-end throughput has not been measured on its own. - Timed with bf16 scoring, which the checkpoint below uses. With fp8 Q and K the kernel needs 24 KB a CTA instead of 40 KB; that path is covered by the bit-identity test, not timed. - The absolute-layout prefill kernel (`tilelang_qsa_mqa_prefill`, used when the host lengths are missing) keeps three stages; the GSM8K runs below never called it. summary: ## Motivation Disaggregated decode admits prebuilt requests using the request-pool size and global `max_running_requests`, but does not apply `pp_max_micro_batch_size`. title: [Perf] pp: Send decode activations before CPU result processing
summary: ## Motivation In disaggregated PP decode, the scheduler posts the current microbatch's activation only after waiting for and processing the next slot's CPU results. This delays work that the next stage could already receive. Ordinary non-speculative decode also records a copy-stream event without actually copying token IDs. The later `.tolist()` reads the device tensor on the scheduler stream, where subsequent PP sends can introduce an unrelated forward dependency. An 8 KB readback was observed waiting about 13 ms on the CPU while the GPU copy itself took about 3–4 us. ## Modifications - Post the existing request/retraction/preallocation/transfer messages and current activation before next-slot CPU postprocessing in the disaggregated decode loop. Preserve their relative ordering, consensus handling and CUDA Graph proxy-send fences. - In the common PP output-receive path, use the existing `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu` for CUDA-tensor, non-speculative decode IDs on the existing copy stream. Preserve the device tensors used for output relay and `future_map`; consumers still wait for `copy_done`. - Extend the existing PP output-exchange regression suite. No new environment variables, streams, worker threads or public options. Both changes apply automatically in the described paths. This does not enable `SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP`; its setting is unchanged. title: [Fix] deterministic: Keep the GDN output tile fixed for varlen prefill
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid Gated DeltaNet (GDN) models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and later) are not batch-invariant for short prompts under `--enable-deterministic-inference`: the same prompt gives different log-probabilities depending on what it is batched with. The cause is one line in `chunk_fwd_o`, the last kernel of the GDN chunked prefill: ```python BT = min(chunk_size, max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(T))) ``` For varlen input (`cu_seqlens`), `T` is the token count of the whole batch, not of one sequence. A 9-token prompt prefilled alone gets a 16-token tile; the same prompt prefilled together with others gets a 32- or 64-token tile. The output is reduced over a different tile, so the last bits change. Every other stage of the GDN prefill (L2 norm, gate cumsum, the intra-chunk solve, the chunk states) gave bitwise-identical results in our tests. We found it on MI350X with Qwen3.8-27B. The bitwise check below sends the same short prompt 1 to 50 times in one request and compares every response with the batch-size-1 one: token IDs were always identical, but log-probabilities matched in only 33-48 of 1,275 responses at TP2 (triton attention, AITER off; 8 runs), and 50-51 of 1,275 at TP1 with AITER on. The first token's log-probability already differs. Disabling the radix cache, CUDA graphs, or the overlap scheduler, or forcing RCCL for the all-reduce, did not change that. The same Triton kernels run on NVIDIA in deterministic mode (FlashInfer GDN prefill is refused there), so this is not specific to ROCm. ## Modifications - `chunk_fwd_o`: use the full chunk size (64) as the tile for

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dp-attention: Route the padding rows of the TP-MoE gather to no expert
summary: ## Motivation With attention DP and TP MoE on CUDA, the MoE input of a decode step is a MAX_LEN gather: every DP rank contributes a slot of the same length, and the rows past its real requests are padding. The decode CUDA graph always uses this layout, and an idle rank still replays one fabricated row. The router sends the padding rows to experts like real tokens, so every MoE layer loads those experts' weights. Since #46225 this costs more on hybrid models. Before it, the unpacked KDA/GDN decode left the padding rows' output unwritten. On GLM-5.3-Flash, six or seven of the seven padding rows of a one-request step then selected exactly experts 0-7 in every MoE layer, which is what the router does with NaN scores (it ranks NaN as -1e30 and breaks ties toward the lowest id). #46225 zeroes that output, which is the right fix for correctness, and the padding rows now route like real tokens. With one request on 8×H20 (attention DP8, main 552e16968b), the expert-distribution recorder counts 64 selections and 35 distinct experts per MoE layer per decode step; with this PR, the real row's 8. On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 zeroes the padding rows before the gather (#43077). Zeroed rows still route, to the experts with the largest correction bias. This PR keeps them out of routing on CUDA. `SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE` (#31888, off by default) drops the same rows from the dispatch, but only with EP: it runs in the standard dispatcher after the local expert mapping, which exists only when `moe_ep_size > 1`. title: [Feat] scheduler: early reject on predicted prefill-side TTFT
summary: ## Motivation > Detailed design, measurements and known issues: see the design note: [飞书](https://my.feishu.cn/docx/GbcXdBbYvoj93sxJMrdcHBIinBb?from=from_copylink) or [google docs](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gz_r6QljscBkFleBVsoRZhyjzSRCpAZbpUUpvMWLeus/edit?usp=sharing) Under overload a prefill server keeps admitting requests that will miss their TTFT SLA. Each of them still spends prefill compute before it times out on the client, and every request queued behind it waits longer. Rejecting such a request on arrival costs no GPU time; letting it time out costs a full prefill. This PR adds an opt-in admission check on prefill and PD prefill servers. A request is answered with HTTP 503 on arrival when draining the prefill queue ahead of it, itself included, is predicted to take longer than `SGLANG_EARLY_REJECT_THRESHOLD` seconds. When the feature is off nothing changes: no hook runs and no collective is issued. **Scope of the prediction.** The model predicts prefill compute and the queueing it causes; the CPU gap between batches is learned as well. It does not predict what happens before the request reaches the scheduler (HTTP, tokenization, IPC) or after prefill (KV transfer, the first decode step, detokenization). These are small and fairly stable, so the threshold should leave a margin for them below the client SLA. In PD, sglang's TTFT also includes the bootstrap wait for decode-side KV preallocation, which prefill cannot see; it is predicted and rejected separately by a decode-side predictor (follow-up PR). **Only effective when prefill compute is the bottleneck.*

summary: ## Motivation Z-Image folds RoPE into its QK-norm call only on CUDA, or on any platform when the RoPE table is the batched 3D form that carries explicit positions. On ROCm every attention in those configurations therefore runs QK-norm over Q and K and then a separate `RotaryEmbedding` call, one extra kernel per step per block for each of the image, caption, and unified streams. The two-step path is worse on ROCm than the kernel count alone suggests, because the separate QK-norm step has no kernel to call there. #40585 repairs part of this by removing the call site for Z-Image altogether by folding the norm and the rotation into one kernel. The two changes are complementary and neither subsumes the other, and the measurements below report this change both against current main and on top of #40585. ## Modifications - Add the `_is_rocm` platform constant next to the existing `_is_cuda` one in the Z-Image DiT. - Let a 2D cos/sin table reach `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` on ROCm as well as CUDA. title: [Fix] Z-Image: Correct and optimize Ulysses sequence layout
summary: ## Motivation Z-Image has 30 attention heads, which do not divide evenly across Ulysses degree 8. Its spatial SP planner also rounds each local image shard to a multiple of 32, even when the complete image already meets the model's 32-token alignment. At 1088x1920 this adds 32 attention-visible image tokens that the single-device reference does not require. The main transformer stack additionally treats caption tokens as a replicated suffix in every block. This PR adds model-local head padding, a guarded global-alignment path, and joint image/caption sequence sharding for native eager Ulysses inference. It preserves existing spatial token ownership and reconstruction while avoiding per-block replicated-caption handling on eligible requests. ## Modifications - Pad Q/K/V with zero-valued heads when the head count does not divide the Ulysses group size, and remove them again before the output projection. Z-Image has 30 heads, so Ulysses degree 8 otherwise fails at the first all-to-all. Only the layers that really exchange heads pad: the context refiner attends over replicated caption tokens on one rank, and a run that selects the K/V-gather exchange keeps every head local, so neither of them pays for padding. - Shard the caption together with the image instead of replicating it. The refined image rows and the refined caption rows form one sequence that is split evenly over the Ulysses ranks, so each rank holds its share of the caption instead of a full copy, and no block has to treat the caption as a replicated suffix. title: [Perf] [AMD] rope: Use the fused rotary kernel for DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation This is a ROCm performance change: `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding` stops pinning itself to `forward_native` on HIP and uses the fused in-place `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding` that the base `RotaryEmbedding` already uses there, worth **-14% to -19% median TPOT** (+5.5% to +18.5% output tok/s) on Mistral-Large-4 MXFP4, MI355X TP4, random ISL 60k / OSL 600, concurrency 1 to 16. On HIP the eager path is a gather from the cos/sin table, repeats, muls, a neg, cats and casts: about 16 kernels per call, 42-46 us per call inside a CUDA graph at decode sizes. The override goes back to the dispatch refactor in #6745, which kept an older `forward_hip -> forward_native` and gave no reason for it. title: [Feat] quantization: Route named layers to a second online quantization format
summary: ## Motivation `--quantization` picks one format for every linear in a transformer. The only per-layer control today is `--quantization-ignored-layers`, which chooses between that one format and BF16. Models whose quality falls off unevenly across the stack have no way to say "run most of this narrow, but keep these layers wide", so the choice is a uniformly narrow model that loses quality or a uniformly wide one that gives back the speedup. MiniMax-H3 is a clear case. Measured on 8x MI355X, Ulysses 8, 50 steps, seed 42, 1344x768 5s T2VA, against the BF16 output as reference: | Run | Warmed-up request | vs BF16 | Video PSNR | Video SSIM | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `bf16` | 27.49 s | — | — | — | | `--quantization fp8` | 24.16 s | -12.1% | 17.59 dB | 0.701 | | `--quantization mxfp4` | 22.40 s | -18.5% | 14.95 dB | 0.702 | | `--quantization mxfp4` + overrides | 23.71 s | -13.7% | 19.96 dB | 0.779 | Uniform MXFP4 is visibly broken on this model. title: [Fix] hicache: Book explicitly sized host pools against one host memory snapshot
summary: ## Motivation - With an explicit `--hicache-size` or `--hicache-ratio`, every HiCache host pool checks itself against a fresh `psutil` sample of free host memory, divided by the number of local ranks. - Ranks build and pin their pools at different times. title: [Perf] dsv41-flash: Add FP8 DeepGEMM prefill scoring on Hopper
summary: ## Motivation and changes #50719 enables Hopper FP8 scoring for full top-k layers and candidate sources. This PR extends its shared indexer implementation to prefill candidate consumers and replaces source block selection with the existing ragged top-k operators. - Reuse `score_tiles`, FP4-to-FP8 widening, per-vector scales, and the `fp8_mqa_logits` integration introduced by #50719. - Score bounded compact candidate batches by packing the published K ranges per query. Carry causal lengths and padding through ragged top-k and map the selected columns back to request positions and pool slots. - Reuse `amax8_varlen` and ragged top-k for source block selection through a helper shared with the sparse-table backend. - Bound the repeated compact K to 65,536 vectors per batch. Larger compact batches use the existing Torch scorer. Full-width candidates use the batched FP8 scorer. Enable these additions with `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SM90_DEEPGEMM_PREFILL=1`. The flag defaults to off and is resolved when constructing the backend. Full/source FP8 scoring comes from #50719. title: [Refactor] graph: Decouple eager_on_graph from CUDA capture (2/3)
summary: ## Motivation SGLang's breakable graph path captures a model forward as a sequence of device graph segments separated by operations that must run eagerly. Model and attention code marks those boundaries with `@eager_on_graph`. At each boundary, SGLang finishes the current captured segment, preserves the eager call's inputs and outputs, records the callback for replay, and starts the next segment. Today, `eager_on_graph` performs those steps by reaching directly into private `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` state. It calls CUDA/XPU-specific segment methods, appends callbacks through `capture.cuda_graph._break_fns`, and applies the current CUDA/XPU tensor-retention policy itself. This coupling blocks an out-of-tree platform even after it implements the breakable graph backend lifecycle: the existing decorators still expect a `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` object and cannot record breaks through the platform's device-specific capture implementation. The platform would have to inherit from or patch the CUDA implementation instead of supplying a clean device backend. This PR separates graph-break recording from CUDA/XPU capture mechanics through a small device-neutral recorder contract. The existing CUDA/XPU implementation adopts that contract without changing behavior; later platform backends can provide the same operations for their capture runtime. This is PR 2 of 3 and is stacked on [PR 1: Introduce device-neutral graph backend bases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49402), which introduces the `BaseGraphBackend` and `BaseBreakableGraphBackend` contracts. ## Modifications

title: [Fix] [AMD] moe: Stop declaring zero-filled A8W4 intermediate padding
summary: ## Motivation On AMD GPUs, some MoE (mixture-of-experts) models can produce NaN (not-a-number) outputs. SGLang adds a few empty rows to each expert so that the sizes line up for the kernel, and then tells the kernel to skip those rows. The kernel skips writing them but later reads them, so it can read garbage. This PR stops telling the kernel to skip them; the rows are already zeros, so computing them is safe. For native AITER FP4 experts, `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading_block_quant()` pads the per-rank intermediate size to a multiple of 128 (for example 576 to 640) and declares the 64 padded rows through `intermediate_pad`. On AITER's A8W4 path, that declaration shrinks the stage-1 launch grid, so the matching scratch columns are not written, while a tile-K128 stage-2 kernel cannot skip a 64-column tail (`64 // 128 == 0`) and can read them; garbage FP8 or E8M0 bytes can become NaN. The physical tails are already allocated with `torch.zeros`, so computing the full width makes stage 1 write exact zeros there. ## Modifications - Set `layer.intermediate_pad` to zero for the native AITER FP4-expert path. The physical weight and scale padding stays, zero-filled. - Add a CPU regression test for the 576-to-640 case: no intermediate pad is declared, and the padded `w13` and `w2` weight tails stay zero. - `hidden_pad` and all other quantization paths are unchanged. - Related: vllm-project/vllm#61816 merged the same workaround in vLLM; ROCm/aiter#6598 fixes the unwritten columns inside the kernel, and ROCm/aiter#6170 adds `AITER_MOE_SKIP_INTER_PAD` with the same effect in

summary: ## Motivation When several GPUs run one model, they often add up their partial results with a step called an all-reduce. On AMD GPUs, SGLang has two kernels for this and always tries the same one first, even when the other one, QuickReduce, is faster for that size. This PR adds an opt-in size from which QuickReduce goes first. It is off by default. title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Reuse the attention-residual bank across forward passes
summary: # [Fix] kimi-k3: Reuse the attention-residual bank across forward passes ## Motivation On MI350X or MI355X, a TP8 Kimi-K3 server ends a long benchmark with 15.0–16.6 GiB more memory in use on each GPU than right after startup, and the amount differs by up to 1.6 GiB between GPUs. At `--mem-fraction-static` 0.91 and 0.93 the server ran out of memory during an ~8K-token prefill, each time on a different set of GPUs. The difference between GPUs comes from timing. Every rank runs the same steps, but each one keeps a slightly different set of large cached segments, depending on which step sizes it saw and when its buffers were freed. A GPU that holds a few more segments has less memory left for allocations outside PyTorch, such as RCCL kernel scratch, and PyTorch cannot free its cache to make room for those. So a server with a few GiB of headroom per GPU can run out of memory on some GPUs while others still have room. The cache grows because of two buffers that are sized by each step's token count and allocated fresh on every step. The caching allocator reuses a free segment only if it is large enough and never merges segments, so every new, larger size leaves another segment behind, and nothing calls `empty_cache()` while serving. The two buffers are: 1. The MoE stage-2 reduce target in aiter's `_flydsl_v2_stage2_wrapper` (112 KiB per token, 1.75 GiB at 16,384 tokens). [ROCm/aiter#7363](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7363) fixes it there. 2. The attention-residual (AttnRes) bank in SGLang, which this pull request fixes. `AttnResidual.__init__` allocates the `[num_tokens, bl

title: [Perf] scheduler: Copy decode top logprobs to the host once per step
summary: ## Summary While training RL model I noticed that score centering which relies on next_token_top_logprobs_val is much slower for small-medium models, one of the reasons is that logprobs are copied separately for each entry in the batch which creates cpu bubbles (can be seen on torch profiles at the end of the post). I propose to fix this by first copying the logprobs into one buffer on gpu and then doing the copy to cpu. ## Motivation With `top_logprobs_num` (or `token_ids_logprob`) set, a decode step moves its top-logprob values and ids to the host one request at a time. With 128 running requests and `top_logprobs_num=128` that is 258 device-to-host copies a step instead of 2, in both scheduler modes: - **Overlap scheduling (default).** `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu` calls `_async_d2h` per request and list. Each copy allocates its own pinned host tensor, and the decode loop waits on all of them. While the batch is small this hides under the GPU step; as it grows it becomes the bottleneck. - **`--disable-overlap-schedule`.** The rows are still on the device when the result processor calls `.tolist()` on each of them, a blocking copy every time, and nothing runs in parallel with it. ## Modifications - `_async_d2h_rows` in `managers/utils.py`: the rows of a list are concatenated on the device and copied with one `_async_d2h` call, then split into per-row host views. title: [Fix] [AMD] engine: Default hipBLASLt's workspace to 128 MiB on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill with the AMD monokernel computes `wo_a` as a bf16 batched einsum (`o [T, 4, 4096] @ wo_a [4, 1024, 4096]`). For every T from 1201 to 1266, `hipblasLtMatmul` returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` and torch falls back to hipBLAS: ``` bgemm_internal_cublaslt error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR when calling hipblasLtMatmul with transpose_mat1 t transpose_mat2 n m 1024 n 1264 k 4096 lda 4096 ldb 16384 ldc 1024 ... ``` In a 1-hour InferenceX AgentX run (TP2, concurrency 32) each rank logs this for 26-28 chunk lengths. The failure depends on the workspace torch passes to hipBLASLt. torch 2.11 passes 76 MiB. Calling hipBLASLt directly for T = 1220, the heuristic returns one solution with `workspaceSize = 0` at every limit, yet `hipblasLtMatmul` fails when given 32-80 MiB and succeeds with 0-16 MiB (slow path) or with 80 MiB and more. pytorch/pytorch#197201 raised torch's default to 80 MiB for the same error on fp8 shapes, but torch 2.11 does not include it. ## Modifications `_set_envs_and_config` now calls `_set_rocm_blas_envs()`, which sets `HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=131072` (128 MiB, in KiB) on ROCm when neither `HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE` nor `CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE` is set. title: [Feat] scheduler: Report where an ignore_eos request's first stop token would have ended it
summary: ## Motivation With `ignore_eos`, the scheduler keeps decoding past every stop token and the response never says where the reply would have ended. A client that wants the valid prefix of a fixed-length generation has to rebuild the stop set itself (EOS, the tokenizer's additional stop tokens, `stop_token_ids`), and that copy can drift from what the scheduler actually checks. This PR makes the scheduler record where the first stop token would have ended the request, and reports it on every length finish as `meta_info.finish_reason.ignored_stop`. Example, `max_new_tokens=64, ignore_eos=true`, EOS sampled as the second output token: ```json "finish_reason": {"type": "length", "length": 64, "ignored_stop": {"position": 2}} ``` The same request without a stop token at or before `max_new_tokens` reports `"ignored_stop": null`. Other finish types never carry the key. ## Modifications - **Scheduler** (`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`, `req_types.py`, `dllm/mixin/scheduler.py`): under `ignore_eos` the stop-token check in `Req._check_token_based_finish` now runs too. Its first match records `Req.ignored_stop_token_len`, the output length at which the same request without `ignore_eos` would have stopped; nothing else changes, decoding continues to `max_new_tokens` and the output keeps every token. Every `FINISH_LENGTH` (the dLLM context-limit one included) passes the value on, and `to_json()` emits `ignored_stop` as `{"position": L}` or `null`. Retraction clears it only where it also clears the output (input-embeds requests). `finished_len` is not reused: it trims the emi

title: [Perf][mem_cache] Persistent lazy eviction heap for the UnifiedRadixCache Full component (bit-identical order)
summary: ## Motivation `FullComponent._evict_device_start` rebuilds a heap over **every** evictable device leaf on **every** eviction call (`[(key(n), n) for n in evictable_device_leaves]` + `heapify`), and `_evict_device_end` throws it away; `drive_host_eviction` does the same over `evictable_host_leaves`. The call sits on the decode path: once the KV pool is full, `check_decode_capacity -> evict_from_tree_cache -> evict_for_alloc -> _evict -> _evict_components` runs on every step that needs to free the shortfall, so the per-call cost is O(#evictable leaves) of pure Python plus O(#leaves) tuple garbage, independent of how few tokens are actually evicted. The Python `UnifiedTreeCore` is the default backend (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND="python"`); the Rust core (`rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/full.rs`) has the same per-call rebuild and is left untouched here (see Follow-ups). Measured on CPU (Apple M3 Pro) with the real `UnifiedRadixCache` (Python core, decode-shaped loop: pool full, `evict(64 tokens)` then insert one 64-token sequence per step, 300 steps, gc disabled, machine idle, min-of-3 p50; `--chunk-len 128 --kv-size 4000000`, `--num-seqs 5000/20000/50000`; "heap rebuild" = time inside `_evict_device_start`, the O(L) `_evict_device_end` list drop is the rest of the removed share): | evictable leaves | `evict()` p50 before | of which heap rebuild + drop | `evict()` p50 after | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | ~3.5K | 326 us | 273 us (84%) | 30 us | 10.9x | | ~14K | 1,426 us | 1,262 us (89%) | 32 us | 44.6x | | ~35K | 4,907 us | 4,300 us (88%) | 33 us | 149x

title: [Perf] lfm3: Enable hybrid SWA KV cache for the LFM3 family
summary: ## Motivation LFM3 interleaves gated short-conv layers with full-attention and 256-token sliding-window layers, which is exactly the shape the hybrid SWA KV cache path exists for. title: [Fix] deterministic: Align chunked prefill to the Gated DeltaNet block size
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid Gated DeltaNet models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and later) are not batch-invariant under `--enable-deterministic-inference` when chunked prefill splits a prompt: the Gated DeltaNet prefill kernels process each chunk in 64-token blocks counted from the chunk's start, and the split point depends on what else is in the batch, so the same prompt can get different block boundaries and slightly different outputs. This PR removes that effect by ending every prefill chunk of these models on an absolute 64-token position in deterministic mode, also after a radix-cache hit and for continuation chunks. No change outside deterministic mode; no measurable speed change. Full attention does not have this problem. We measured it on MI350X with Qwen3.8-27B. A 3,000-token prompt with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048` was sent alone, then together with one other prompt of 100 to 3,500 tokens: - when the split point moved off a multiple of 64, its output differed from the solo run in 21 of 24 calls (log-probabilities from the first token, and token IDs when the other prompt was 1,000+ tokens); - when the split stayed on a multiple of 64, 12 of 12 calls matched; - without splitting, 24 of 24 matched; - Qwen3-8B (full attention only) matched 24 of 24 either way. In the end-to-end determinism tests this shows up as occasional `prefix` and `prefix --return-logprob` failures (one or two extra distinct outputs in ~300 samples, and log-probability mismatches). title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Treat actorder aliases like their canonical form in WNA16 MoE
summary: ## Motivation compressed-tensors defines `"weight"` as an alias of `"static"` and `"dynamic"` as an alias of `"group"` (`ActivationOrdering.get_aliases()`). `QuantizationArgs` stores the actorder as the string the config wrote, so the enum's alias-aware equality never runs: with compressed-tensors 0.18.0 (the pinned version), `"weight" != "static"` is `True`. `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoE` compares `self.actorder` with the raw strings `"static"` and `"group"`: - **`actorder: "weight"` is treated as dynamic actorder.** Checkpoints that record it, e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-quantized.w4a16`, carry no `g_idx`. At `moe_tp_size > 1` the scheme still sets `load_full_w2`, so every rank loads the full, unsharded w2 scale. The Marlin wrapper then derives the group as rank K / total groups (256 / 8 = 32 instead of 128 at `moe_intermediate_size=1024`, TP4) and every rank computes wrong output without an error. On CUDA these checkpoints always run on Marlin, because `_is_wna16_triton_moe_supported` rejects any actorder. Found by reading the code; the GPU check below does not exercise it. ## Modifications - Normalize the aliases once, when the scheme stores `actorder`: `"weight"` becomes `"static"` and `"dynamic"` becomes `"group"`. title: [Feat] scheduler: Allow lpm with priority scheduling
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-priority-scheduling` only works with `--schedule-policy fcfs` or `lof`; startup rejects every other policy. A deployment that serves several priority classes therefore has to give up prefix-cache-aware ordering. That costs the most when many requests of the same class wait at once, for example agentic multi-turn sessions with 100k-token contexts. FCFS then admits requests of one class in arrival order, they evict each other's prefixes, and every miss is paid back as recomputed prefill. This PR allows `lpm` with priority scheduling. Requests are ordered by priority first, then by longest cached prefix within a priority. ## Modifications - `validation_hook.py`: `lpm` is accepted with `--enable-priority-scheduling`. - `SchedulePolicy._sort_lpm_with_priority`: - sorts the queue by (priority, arrival); - prefix-matches only the first `WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX` (128) requests in that order and re-sorts them by (priority, in-batch duplicate, longest prefix); - leaves the tail in (priority, arrival) order. Plain `lpm` drops to unsorted FCFS above 128 waiting requests, but with priority the class order holds for the whole queue. - The tail gets the same handling as the tail of a bounded batch: a fast-match init, and the FCFS prefix refresh before the head is matched. - Bounded LPM (#48409) is turned off when priority scheduling is on. Its fixed batch commits the head of the queue, so a new higher-priority request could wait behind committed lower-priority members. Making the bounded batch priority-aware can follow separately. - Requests without a priori
