title: [Feat] api.v1: Add native RGB shared-memory ingress
summary: ## Motivation A runtime sidecar may already hold decoded RGB images. Re-encoding those pixels only for the engine to decode them again adds CPU work and copies; putting tens or hundreds of MiB inline also enlarges gRPC requests. This adds an optional same-host api.v1 input carrying small references to shared RGB storage, while keeping model preprocessing in the existing native engine pipeline. **Earlier cleanup of shared media.** The existing `file://` input can keep large media out of gRPC, but it provides no explicit read-completion signal. This PR returns `sglang-decoded-media-consumed: true` in the initial gRPC response metadata once the receiving engine owns a complete copy of the input. The producer can then unlink its object before the first token or request completion, shortening the time large payloads occupy the shared volume. Each receipt covers one engine. The producer retains cleanup responsibility for objects with outstanding readers or missing receipts. ## Design question for review: `file://` or a decoded-media input A main design question, is `file://` the intended long-term `api.v1` path for a trusted sidecar and engine sharing a volume? The current API already accepts local media files, and both paths keep the large payload off the gRPC wire. If `file://` is the recommended contract and meets the needs below, we can use it and reassess whether the decoded-media API is worth adding. **Request and object identity.** Both paths use `Generate.rid` for the inference request. summary: Serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 at plain TP4 on Hopper, where Marlin fails at startup, and prefills the clamped GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 1.25x faster than Marlin on four H100s. | H100, Marlin → this PR | prefill tok/s, 16K prompts | batch-1 decode tok/s | GSM8K | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 | 17,961 → 22,463 (1.25x) | 178.0 → 161.2 | 0.971 → 0.972 | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP2 | 21,591 → 23,760 (1.10x) | 145.3 → 128.2 | 0.973 → 0.979 | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP4 | fails at startup → 19,957 | fails → 138.9 | not run | The runner from #50801 needed each GPU's slice of an expert to be a multiple of 128 columns, and it refused models that clamp SwiGLU. title: [Perf] spec: Derive the speculative max_running_requests default from the decode CUDA-graph ladder
summary: ## Summary ### The problem Turning on speculative decoding silently replaces this server's admission limit with a hardcoded `48` — on every device, whatever the hardware can actually run. Five per-algorithm handlers in `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` each do: ```python if server_args.max_running_requests is None: server_args.max_running_requests = 48 ``` Because the field is non-`None` afterwards, `resolve_max_num_reqs` then takes its "the user asked for this" branch, so **the KV-capacity estimator that sizes every non-speculative server never runs.** The sharpest way to see it: on the *same GPU, same model, same flags*, adding `--speculative-algorithm` moves the resolved limit from **4096 to 48**. It gets worse on multi-GPU deployments, because `max_running_requests` is a *global* figure that `resolve_max_num_reqs` divides per attention-DP worker: a `dp_size=8` server ends up admitting **6 requests per worker**. ### What this PR does Replace the five hardcoded `48`s with **one value derived from a bound sglang already computes from measured device memory** — the decode CUDA-graph ladder (`cuda_graph_config[decode].max_bs x attn_dp_size`) — floored at `48`. title: [Fix] [NPU] memory-saver: Drain device before sleep unmap and preserve runtime tensor attrs
summary: ## Motivation In RL-colocated serving (slime / verl), the rollout engine loops `release_memory_occupation -> training -> resume_memory_occupation -> update_weights_from_disk` on every iteration. On Ascend NPU (910B A3) with `--enable-memory-saver`, this loop deterministically corrupted the model: after `sleep -> resume -> update_weights_from_disk(correct weights)` the engine emitted stable garbage outputs for **every** request, and further weight updates never recovered it. Two independent defects combine here: 1. `release_memory_occupation` synchronized the device only **after** all unmaps, so the TMS unmap raced in-flight async work (kernels, D2H copies), corrupting pages behind stable virtual addresses that captured graphs happily replay. 2. Plain tensor attributes (neither parameters nor buffers) held by modules or by non-Module helper objects (MoE dispatchers, quant methods) are not covered by `_export/_import_static_state` — anything they carry across sleep is silently lost (the "virtual address stability ≠ value preservation" failure class of vLLM RFC #53343; vllm-ascend #13352 fixed the same class case-by-case). ## Modifications - `weight_updater.py`: synchronize the device **before** the first pause (covers every unmap, including `kv_cache`) and again after the weights export D2H copies, before unmapping `weights`. - new `utils/sleep_state_utils.py`: generically export/restore every persistent device tensor reachable as a plain module attribute (containers and non-Module helper objects included; CPU snapshots so the export does not inflate device memory). title: [Fix] [XPU] graph: make sgl-kernel scratchpads graph-safe with shared workspace and dual compatibility
summary: ## Motivation On XPU, `sgl_kernel` internal scratchpad allocators (MoE's `_get_moe_ws` and GDN's `_get_gdn_workspace`) use module-level dictionary caches. When capturing an XPU Graph at smaller batch sizes, the device memory pointers of these initial buffers become baked into the captured command lists. If a subsequent eager or larger forward pass triggers buffer expansion, the references to older buffers are dropped, allowing PyTorch's caching allocator to recycle their physical memory for other active tensors. Subsequent graph replays then overwrite those newly allocated buffers, causing silent memory corruption. This PR introduces a robust, capture-aware, and dual-compatible scratchpad buffer management layer for Intel XPU: 1. **Graph Capture Mode**: All captured graphs (Decode Full, Prefill Breakable/Full) and layers share dedicated static graph workspaces via narrow slicing, keeping physical device pointers immutable and completely isolated from eager execution. Retired buffers from in-graph reallocations are retained for the graph lifetime. 2. **Zero-Break `torch.compile` Integration**: Custom ops (`sgl_xpu::get_moe_ws_op` and `sgl_xpu::get_gdn_ws_op`) support dynamic shapes (`SymInt[]` / `SymInt`) without graph breaks when models combine `torch.compile` and XPU Graph. 3. **Lifecycle & GC Safety**: Tracks active graph owners with `weakref.finalize` reference counting so scratchpads are safely released when all runners exit, without leaking memory or invalidating co-existing backends. 4. **Dual Compatibility**: Automatically bypasses patching if `sgl-kernel-xpu` define

title: [Fix] attention: Fix fp16 MHA decode NaN when a q*k product overflows
summary: ## Motivation For MHA models (`kv_group_num == 1`), `decode_attention_fwd` runs `_fwd_kernel_stage1`, which computes the scores as `tl.sum((q[None, :] * k).to(tl.float32), 1)`. The elementwise product `q * k` is formed in the input dtype and cast to fp32 only afterwards. In fp16, a single product above 65504 overflows to `inf`, the softmax then computes `exp(inf - inf)`, and every output of the head becomes NaN — while the same token gives a finite result in prefill, because the grouped and extend kernels use `tl.dot` with fp32 accumulation. Any fp16 model served on the Triton attention backend can hit this silently: one large `q_i * k_i` pair (e.g. 256 * 256) is enough to NaN a whole head's decode output. Fixes #51095 ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py` (`_fwd_kernel_stage1` only): when the `q*k` product itself would be formed in fp16 (either operand is fp16 — Triton also promotes an fp16 Q with an fp8 K to fp16), cast `q` and `k` to fp32 **before** the multiply. Otherwise keep the original form exactly. ```python # Cast the product, not q and k, to avoid a fp32 [BLOCK_N, D] tile -- # except when the product itself would be formed in fp16: ... if q.dtype == tl.float16 or k.dtype == tl.float16: qk = tl.sum(q[None, :].to(tl.float32) * k.to(tl.float32), 1) else: qk = tl.sum((q[None, :] * k).to(tl.float32), 1) ``` Why this shape, and not a blanket cast: - The existing comment deliberately avoids a fp32 `[BLOCK_N, D]` tile. title: Allow runtime schedule_policy switching via /set_internal_state
summary: ## Motivation We run mixed traffic on single SGLang instances: high-throughput batch jobs and low-latency realtime requests for the same model. The right waiting-queue policy differs by mode and by time of day, but `--schedule-policy` is fixed at boot — changing it costs a full engine reload (minutes of weight loading plus radix-cache re-warm), which is too disruptive to do on a live server. We'd like to toggle the scheduling mode at runtime, and eventually automate the toggle on load signals. ## The concrete issue that motivated this Serving GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on 8x B300 with production traffic (~115K-token mean input, agentic workload, ~96% radix cache hit rate under `slru` eviction), we compared `fcfs` and `lpm`: - **`lpm`** delivers excellent median TTFT (~0.7s — warm-prefix requests are scheduled onto their cached prefixes), but it **systematically starves cache-miss requests**: a cold request with zero prefix match sorts last on every scheduling pass, and at high hit rates fresh warm-prefix arrivals keep jumping the queue indefinitely. Our TTFT histogram showed a 20–60s tail (~5% of requests) contributing ~75% of total accumulated TTFT. - **`fcfs`** bounds the tail (fair ordering) but gives up lpm's cache-locality preference, which is measurably valuable in quiet periods. Neither policy is right all day. Since `SchedulePolicy` is pure CPU-side state — no CUDA graphs or memory layouts depend on it (unlike e.g. speculative tiers) — switching it live is safe and cheap. ## What this PR does Adds `schedule_policy` to the `set_internal_state` allowlist: ```bash curl -s -X POST h

title: [Inkling] Fix inkling gate renorm nan
summary: ## Motivation Inkling's fused gate can produce NaN routing weights from finite logits. Expert selection uses `sigmoid(raw_logit) + expert_bias`, but normalization uses the unbiased raw logits of the six selected routed experts and two shared experts. A large selection bias can therefore select an expert whose sigmoid weight is tiny; top-k selection does not guarantee a nonzero normalization denominator. The CUDA gate evaluates sigmoid as `1 / (1 + exp(-x))`. At `x = -100`, the intermediate `exp(100)` overflows FP32 and the computed sigmoid becomes zero. If this happens for all eight active experts, normalization divides by zero and produces NaNs. Adding `1e-20` to the denominator avoids the NaNs but changes the model's output: eight equal finite logits should always receive equal normalized weights, not zero weights. Even before overflow, the epsilon attenuates the total weight by `S / (S + 1e-20)`, where `S` is the sigmoid sum. With eight logits equal to `-50`, the unscaled weights sum to about `0.1337` instead of `1`. The non-fused path has a separate cancellation issue. Reconstructing `max_log_prob + log(sum_exp)` loses the normalization term when the maximum is very negative, such as `-1e8`. Eight equal logits can then receive unscaled weights of `1` each instead of `1/8`. This work was prompted by an Inkling request that reached sampling with an invalid row and triggered a device-side assert in `torch.multinomial`. Disabling the overlap scheduler did not resolve that failure. The gate defect is reproducible independently, but the sampling logs alone do not establish it

title: [Fix] [AMD] qwen3_5: Rotate the online MXFP4 GDN projections by Hadamard-32
summary: ## Motivation This ROCm accuracy fix rotates the online MXFP4 GDN `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` of #43839 (merged) by a 32-point block Hadamard matrix, because plain MXFP4 there makes Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 write **11% more tokens** than BF16 on thinking-on GSM8K. With the rotation, the answers are 2% to 5% longer than BF16, and the median TPOT is within 0.6% of plain MXFP4 (+0.0% and +0.4% without MTP, +0.1% and +0.6% with NEXTN, geomean over 12 serving shapes in two runs, 8x MI355X, TP8). The extra length repeats in every run. Against BF16, the per-question geomean of plain MXFP4 is 1.071, 1.070 and 1.073 in our three runs, and 1.073 in [vllm#62750](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62750). With the rotation, it is 1.017, 1.021, 1.016 and 1.022. The accuracy drop of plain MXFP4 does not always repeat. It is 0.9641 to 0.9597 in our first run (McNemar p = 0.0017), 0.9638 to 0.9606 in our third run (p = 0.023) and 0.9630 to 0.9586 in [vllm#62750](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62750) (p = 0.0027), but 0.9628 to 0.9626 in our second run (p = 0.94). With the rotation, no run shows an accuracy change against BF16 (p = 0.62, 0.73 and 0.73 here, 0.79 over 8 reps and 0.057 over 12 reps in vLLM). The extra tokens cost decode time. At almost the same TPOT, the rotation gives 7.8%, 5.4% and 9.1% fewer tokens per thinking answer than plain MXFP4 in our three runs. The rotation needs [Rocm/aiter6734](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6734) (merged), which adds `hadamard_rotate` to `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`. title: [Fix] scheduler: keep chunked prefill within allocatable KV under memory pressure
summary: ## Motivation Under overload on Kimi-K3 (MI355X, TP8, chunked prefill + hybrid KDA/MLA), the scheduler could stall or fail allocations: - A continuing chunk was sized only by the token budget, so it could ask `alloc_extend` for more KV than is free. - A second unfinished chunked request could be admitted under policies other than shortest-prefill-first, even though only one can be tracked (assert crash). - A latched `batch_is_full` was cleared only when the running batch shrank, so the waiting queue stalled. - On the aiter backend, an over-capacity extend inside graph context could leave the chunked-KV path. ## Modifications - `available_chunk_tokens` caps a continuing chunk by free + evictable KV, less the page `alloc_extend` over-asks. When that leaves nothing, the continuation is parked (as upstream #44823 does for the decode-headroom budget). - The one-chunked-request guard applies under every schedule policy. - `batch_is_full` is re-evaluated every scheduling step; `PrefillAdder` still enforces the real limits. - Over-capacity aiter extends stay on the chunked-KV path. ## Accuracy Tests New unit tests (`test_prefill_memory_budget.py`, `test_prefill_adder.py`, `test_scheduler_batch_is_full_latch.py`, `test_aiter_attention_backend_handler.py`): all 5 new cases fail on `main` and pass with this PR (76 passed). End to end, the Kimi-K3 MI355X production build includes these fixes. On a 40-min overload soak (48 concurrent requests against 12 slots), 901/901 completed requests returned 200, the queue peaked at 37, and there were 0 OOM, HSA or assert errors. ## Speed Tests and

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi_k3: Row-shard the latent MoE up_proj over TP8 in prefill
summary: ## Motivation On the fused front's single-collective path, `KimiK3MoE` all-reduces the flat `[latent | shared]` buffer once, and then every rank runs the full latent `up_proj` (`[7168, 3584]`, bf16). Under TP8 the same GEMM runs redundantly on all ranks: at 14336 tokens it costs about 1.1 ms per layer on MI350X, across 92 MoE layers. ## Modifications For prefill batches of at least 1024 tokens on ROCm at TP8, on the single-collective path only (not when the K3 AR fusion is active): 1. All-reduce the latent and apply the latent norm (`_reduce_latent`, as the unfused front does). 2. Add this rank's `7168 / tp_size` rows of `up_proj(latent)` into its shared partial sum, in place. 3. All-reduce the shared sum (`_reduce_shared`) and add `prefix_sum`. The bytes on the wire are unchanged; each rank runs 1/tp_size of the GEMM, at the cost of one extra collective launch. - New pure helpers in `kimi_k3.py`: `_sharded_up_proj_eligible`, `_tp_row_slice`, `_sharded_up_proj_tail`. Eligibility and the row slice are computed once in `__init__`. - Eligible only for ROCm at TP8 and a bf16 `up_proj` weight whose rows divide by TP. Quantized or packed weights, other TP sizes, smaller batches and other platforms keep the existing path. - The sharded GEMM uses `_k3_bf16_gemm` on a row slice of the weight (ROCm does not shuffle linear weights, so the slice is valid). - New CPU test: `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_sharded_up_proj.py`. ## Accuracy Tests - Unit tests (CPU, simulated 8-rank sums): the sharded tail matches the replicated tail exactly in float64 and adds the prefix sum once,

title: [NPU] [Roadmap] SGLang Diffusion Integration with MindIE-SD
summary: ## Background SGLang Diffusion already supports RainFusion, adaptive block sparse, and Laser attention on Ascend. Extending sparse attention and quantized FA requires ongoing kernel development, integration, and maintenance. Maintaining these paths ourselves means bringing the required kernels and bindings into `sgl-kernel-npu`, as is currently done with the `attentions` module, and keeping them compatible with new CANN releases and Ascend devices. This duplicates work across inference frameworks and increases the effort needed to adopt new optimizations and fixes. [MindIE-SD](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD) is a diffusion acceleration framework that provides optimized attention implementations and public APIs for sparse and quantized execution. Reusing these APIs can reduce duplicated kernel maintenance and shorten the path to adopting performance improvements in SGLang. vLLM-Omni also integrates MindIE-SD, providing a precedent for sharing this acceleration layer across inference frameworks. This roadmap starts with attention backends, with potential extensions to other MindIE-SD optimizations. SGLang remains responsible for model execution, scheduling, and parallelism; MindIE-SD supplies optimized execution APIs. The integration boundary and configuration design are discussed in [RFC #48582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48582). ## Motivation Provide a maintainable way to adopt MindIE-SD optimizations in SGLang Diffusion, reducing duplicated kernel development and enabling faster adoption of performance improvements on Ascend. title: [Fix] moe: Make biased top-k symbolic-shape safe
summary: The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic. For routing scores shaped `[T, E]` and a shared correction bias shaped `[E]`, the intended operation is: ```text [T, E] + [1, E] ``` The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic expert width: `correction_bias.view(-1, num_experts)` When `num_experts` is symbolic, Dynamo represents the inferred leading dimension as `correction_bias.numel() // num_experts`. Fake-tensor tracing cannot always prove that this expression is 1, causing a shape assertion or broadcasting failure before inference starts. This affects the generic PyTorch fallback and is not specific to a particular hardware backend. The same pattern exists in both `biased_topk_impl` and `biased_grouped_topk_impl`. The helpers also support per-token correction biases shaped `[T, E]`, so always reshaping the bias to `[1, E]` would not be correct. ## Modifications - Add a private _add_correction_bias helper that preserves both supported bias layouts: - Shared bias [E] is explicitly expanded to [1, E]. - Per-token bias [T, E] remains unchanged. - Use the helper in both biased_topk_impl and biased_grouped_topk_impl. - Add a CPU regression test that: - Marks the routing dimensions as unbacked. - Keeps the model correction-bias width static. - Compiles both helpers with backend="eager", dynamic=True, and fullgraph=True. - Compares compiled outputs against eager outputs, including expert IDs, weights, dtypes, and normalization. summary: ## Motivation On gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA 3.5, 20 CU) a bs=1 decode step is almost entirely single-row GEMV (`x[1,K] @ W[N,K].T`). rocBLAS serves that as a tiled GEMM with a 96-row tile, so the number of CTAs that can be resident is pinned by `N/96`: 32-64 CTAs for the dense projections of a 0.6B-9B model. On 20 compute units that is not enough to cover memory latency, and the measured read bandwidth is 45-93 GB/s, i.e. 20-40% of what the part can reach. Splitting K gives every k-chunk its own CTA group. At M=1 the fp32 partials are `N * 4 B * split_k`, 0.2-0.4% of the weight bytes, so the extra traffic is negligible next to the 2-4x occupancy gain. Two kernels: one CTA per (32-wide n-tile, 512-wide k-chunk) accumulating in fp32 and storing partials, then a reduce kernel with a static order that stores bf16. `tl.dot` is deliberately not used — at M=1 it requires 16 rows and spends 15/16 of the loaded weight tile on padding (76 GB/s vs 202 GB/s on `4096x1024`). ## Modifications | File | Change | |---|---| | `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/rdna_small_m_gemv.py` (new) | split-K kernel (`BN=32` / `BK=512` / fp32 partials) + fixed-order reduce + gate (incl. summary: ## Motivation This PR bundles two independent, hardware-validated fixes found during P1 perf/accuracy CI triage, both in the MFU/MBU analytical estimator. **1. MFU/MBU estimator overcounts read bandwidth.** With `--enable-metrics --enable-mfu-metrics`, the estimated decode read-bandwidth (and therefore any peak-bandwidth-normalized MBU%) comes out several times too high once concurrency is above a handful of requests. This inflates the estimated prefill TFLOPS by roughly an order of magnitude for mostly-Mamba stacks. title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Fuse prefill indexer scoring with the top-k on gfx95
summary: ## Motivation Builds on #50871 (draft) and contains its commits until it merges; the last commit is this PR. On gfx95, #50871 selects each QSA prefill row's 512 blocks with `topk_v2` over request-relative fp32 scores. For a 16,384-token extend chunk on an 83,968-token prefix, one layer writes and reads back 16,384 × 25,088 scores (1.6 GB) in 13 row chunks. title: [Fix] GDN: Take prefix-cache checkpoints from the fp32 state in the Triton kernel
summary: ## Motivation For hybrid Gated DeltaNet (GDN) models with the mamba radix cache, a request that reuses a cached prefix gets slightly different results than the same prompt computed without the cache. Under `--enable-deterministic-inference` this breaks the guarantee: whether a request hits the cache depends on scheduling and timing, so its log-probabilities change from run to run. Cause: when a prefill crosses a radix-cache checkpoint, `GDNAttnBackend` asks the extend kernel for an fp32 snapshot of the recurrent state at that chunk boundary (`track_state` / `track_chunk_idx`). `TritonGDNKernel` does not declare `supports_track_state_snapshot`, so the backend falls back to the per-chunk states `h`, which `chunk_gated_delta_rule` stores in the activation dtype (bf16) - the fallback's docstring says so ("already rounded to the activation dtype"). A request resuming from that checkpoint starts from a rounded state; its prefill output can still match (the output kernel reads the same rounded `h`), but the state it then decodes from differs, so the first decode step changes. The shared chunk kernel (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`) already writes the fp32 snapshot; KDA's Triton kernel uses it. Only the GDN path does not pass it through. title: [Bug] `chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_forward` / `chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_forward`: token row offset wraps for >= 2^31 elements
summary: ### Describe the bug The csgmv LoRA backend (the default LoRA backend) maps tokens through an int32 `permutation` ([chunked_backend.py#L237](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/chunked_backend.py#L237)). The shrink kernel computes `x + s_offset_physical * x_stride_0` ([chunked_sgmv_shrink.py#L84-L92](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_shrink.py#L84-L92); split-K variant [chunked_sgmv_shrink.py#L184-L194](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_shrink.py#L184-L194)), and the expand kernel computes `output + s_offset_physical * output_stride_0` ([chunked_sgmv_expand.py#L126-L128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_expand.py#L126-L128), [chunked_sgmv_expand.py#L168-L176](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_expand.py#L168-L176)). `s_offset_physical` is int32, so the product wraps when `row * stride >= 2^31`. The shrink then reads before `x`; the expand reads and writes before `output`. The Triton LoRA backend casts the same index to int64 ([kernel_utils.py#L15-L19](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/lora/dense/kernel_utils.py#L15-L19)). title: [Feat] dp: Add shape-aware DP load balancing method
summary: ## Motivation `total_tokens` balancing treats prefill-heavy and decode-heavy load as the same quantity, so a rank owing a lot of prefill can look equivalent to one owing a lot of decode. This adds a `shape_aware` DP load-balance method that tracks the two separately. Reference: the same policy was implemented and merged in SGL-JAX as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-jax/pull/1435. ### Why this score Currently, DP scheduling doesn't distinguish FLOP-bound (prefill) from HBM-bound (decode) requests. The score is inspired by cluster (k8s) scheduling, which balances CPU and RAM pressure per device: ``` max(FLOPs Util, HBM Util) ``` Input tokens stand in for FLOPs pressure and output tokens for HBM pressure. Ideally each would be normalized or weighted: ``` max(input token / prefill capacity, output token / decode capacity) ``` For now prefill and decode capacity are assumed equal, so the score is `max(input_load + req_input, output_load + req_output)`. The `max` keeps whichever resource is binding on each rank lowest, so a prefill-heavy request is drawn toward a decode-heavy rank and vice versa. Weights can be tuned later, using cost factors or real FLOPs / HBM GB estimates. ### When it helps Shape-aware routing matters when compute is stranded: long outputs, low concurrency and a saturated KV pool, where a small decode batch is memory-bandwidth-bound and FLOPs sit idle (long-generation / reasoning serving). On ordinary high-concurrency traffic there is little imbalance to exploit, and it should be close to `total_tokens`. In SGL-JAX (TPU v6e-4, Qwen3-8B, dp=4, bimodal wor

title: SGLang-Diffusion Roadmap (2026 Q4)
summary: Center Q4 on MiniMax-H3 as the stress test; most of the work is model-agnostic. - Lossless performance: overlap TP/Ulysses communication with compute, fuse kernels under the bit-exact contract, and ship validated GB200/GB300 recipes. - Lossy `high` tier: extend the quality gate to all Blackwell GPUs and to substituted (LoRA) weights, then combine sparse attention, few-step distillation (PDD, Turbo LoRA, on top of FastH3 V2) and FP8/NVFP4 for at least 2x over `exact`. - Community H3 variants: run at least 90% of the top-50 Hugging Face derivatives (GGUF, quantized, LoRA, component repos) with a plain `sglang serve`, fail before downloading otherwise, and keep distilled LoRAs effective when merged. - Serving and platforms: batching for audio-video outputs and disaggregated serving; ROCm, NPU, DGX Spark, Apple MPS and consumer GPUs. - Consumer GPUs (RTX 4090, RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000): default commands that run without OOM on 24–32 GB of VRAM and 32–64 GB of host memory, with weight residency planned from measured memory (layerwise streaming, decode-scoped VAE, evicting idle encoders) and faster weight streaming from host memory and disk; FP8/NVFP4 GEMMs, FP8 attention and INT8 W8A8 on SM89/SM120; at least ComfyUI's speed with the same weights.

title: [Feat] [NPU] eplb: Add experimental asynchronous expert migration
summary: ## What this adds `--eplb-async-rebalance` moves NPU EPLB CPU placement planning and remote expert READs off the forward thread onto one worker, then installs one completed layer at a target-forward boundary. The synchronous path stays the default. ## Why NPU EPLB transfers expert weights on the forward thread. Splitting a rebalance into one-layer chunks bounds each pause, but the transfer for that layer still delays the next forward. Same-host measurements: sync versus async gave **+5.86%** output throughput and **-4.84%** mean TPOT, with **+9.19%** p99 TTFT. Peer batching alone gave **+2.52%** pooled throughput against serial-peer async across two reverse-order pairs. The two comparisons are independent and must not be added. Related discussion: #45282 and #8529. ## How a layer moves `EPLBManager` takes the statistics snapshot on the inference stream and starts one rebalance. The coordinator owns its epoch, phase and current layer. A single executor runs the planner and HIXL work, so two rebalances cannot reuse the staging buffer at once. ```mermaid flowchart TB M["EPLBManager: statistics snapshot"] --> C["Coordinator: one active rebalance"] C -->|"submit Future"| W["Worker: CPU placement, then HIXL READs"] C -->|"vote at target-forward boundary"| G["Gloo control group: all EP ranks"] W -->|"remote expert bytes"| S["One-layer staging buffer"] G -->|"all ready, no error"| I["Forward owner: install layer and metadata"] S -->|"copy on owning inference stream"| I I --> L["Live expert storage: addresses unchanged"] L --> F["Subsequent forward / captured graph"] ``` The diagram

title: [Fix] cuda_graph/breakable: Derive MHA capture state from recorded attention breaks
summary: ## Motivation Under the breakable prefill graph, each attention call is an eager break. At replay only the break reruns. It reads three `ForwardBatch` fields, `mha_one_shot`, `mha_return_lse` and `attn_attend_prefix_cache`, but the model code that set them sits inside a captured segment and does not rerun. So the runner has to know what the breaks were captured with. `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` currently decides this with `not is_cuda()`. When that is true, and the model has `attn_mha` companion layers (every DeepSeek-family model does), the runner: 1. rejects replay for batches with a cached prefix; 2. forces `mha_one_shot=True, mha_return_lse=False, attn_attend_prefix_cache=False` onto the replay batch. The platform does not decide which attention path gets captured; the attention backend's DeepSeek dispatch handler does (`deepseek_common/attention_backend_handler.py`): Mainstream CUDA works because its default backends pin MLA. MLA breaks read none of the three fields, and both the capture and the replay batch leave them `None`. MLA-pinned backends off CUDA get MHA state forced onto an MLA graph. fa3, flashinfer, flashmla, triton and trtllm_mla all return MLA when breakable capture is active ## Modifications Replace the platform guess with what capture actually did. While capturing, each eager attention break records the batch's three fields and the layer that broke. - **Replay** restores exactly the recorded state. MLA captures record all `None`, so nothing changes for them. - **Prefix replay** is rejected only if an `attn_mha` companion layer broke. DSA needs no special c

title: [Fix] trtllm_mha: Pack a graph-built page table for eager reads
summary: **Stack:** [#47644 → #47703 (this PR)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/stack/51142). The base branch is #47644's, so the diff shows only this change; once #47644 merges, the base goes back to `main`. The code does not depend on #47644, but under attention DP the workload below hits both crashes, so the GPU check needs both. ## Motivation With unified memory, every reader in an iteration shares one plan's page table, built by the first reader that asks. A CUDA-graph reader builds it in place in its static buffer as `into[:rows, :width]`. `width` is the pages the batch's host lengths need, usually far narrower than the buffer's `max_num_pages`, so with 2+ rows the table is a strided view. A later eager trtllm_mha read of the same plan asking for no more rows gets that view. XQA and fmha_v2 take a table's row length from its width and ignore its strides, so #42930 added an assert for this case, which "no known configuration produces": ```text AssertionError: trtllm_mha reads its page tables as packed rows, but the plan's table is a strided view of a wider buffer ``` Main reaches it since #48414, which captures the DFlash draft CUDA graph under attention DP. The draft graph is keyed by the rank-local batch and the target verify by the DP-wide max. In a round where the draft replays but the verify overflows the captured graph and runs eager, the draft builds the table in place and the verify reads the strided view. Under skewed DP load (one rank past the graph max, 2+ requests on the others) the scheduler dies on the first decode rounds. Default launches do not hit this: t

title: [Fix] dflash: Stage the draft sampler only for batches its buffers hold
summary: **Stack:** [#47644 (this PR) → #47703](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/stack/51142). #47703 fixes the second crash the same workload hits under attention DP. Merge this one first. ## Motivation With a DFlash2 draft (candidate selector) or a LiLiCorr head, the draft sampler is folded into the draft CUDA graph. Its static buffers are sized to the largest captured decode bucket, but every decode step staged its sampling params into them. When a decode batch is larger than the decode graph max, the scheduler crashes: ```text File ".../speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py", line 423, in stage_sampling_params self.greedy_mask[:bs].copy_( RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (4) must match the size of tensor b (8) at non-singleton dimension 0 ``` That step's draft cannot replay (no captured bucket covers the batch). It runs the eager head, which reads none of the sampler's buffers, so the staging is not needed. Default launches do not hit this: the decode graph max defaults to the running-request cap (up to 512 on B200/GB300), so every batch has a bucket. It happens when `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` is set below the running-request cap, or with more than 512 running requests per rank. Since #48414, which captures the DFlash draft graph under attention DP, it also happens under DP when one rank's batch exceeds the graph max. ## Modifications - `DFlashWorkerV2._stage_draft_sampler` stages the folded sampler only when the batch fits its buffers (`bs <= max_bs`). - `_SelectorDraftSampler` records its `max_bs`; `LiLiCorrDraftSampler` already does. - The NVIDIA megakernel selector head (

title: [Fix] dp_attention: Feed real per-rank counts to the pad-row MoE mask in decode graphs
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention and MAX_LEN padding, every rank pads its decode batch to the size of the busiest rank, and the MoE runs on the gathered buffer of `num_dp_ranks * max_len` rows. `SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE` exists to drop those pad rows from MoE dispatch (`mask_dp_pad_moe_topk_ids` sets their `topk_ids` to -1). In decode CUDA graphs the switch currently has no effect: - `mask_dp_pad_moe_topk_ids` reads the per-rank counts from `_DpGatheredBufferWrapper.get_dp_global_num_tokens_gpu()` and returns early when that is `None`. - `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` calls `set_dp_buffer_len(...)` without the `global_num_tokens_gpu` argument, so it is `None` while the graph is captured and no mask kernel ends up in the graph. - The registry slot `global_num_tokens_gpu` could not serve as the source anyway: on replay it is filled with the padded count, which masks nothing. So when the ranks are unevenly loaded, pad rows are routed to real experts and cost as much as real rows. Kernel timing on v0.5.23 (8-GPU node, tp 8 / dp 8 / ep 8, W4A8 grouped-GEMM MoE path, decode graphs for batch 1..32), grouped GEMM time per decode step on one rank: | rows on this rank | grouped GEMM per step | |---|---| | 1 real, every rank has 1 | 5.5 ms | | 1 real + 7 pad (another rank has 8) | 11.7 ms | | 8 real | 11.6 ms | ## Modifications - `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` keeps a `[num_dp_ranks]` int64 tensor with each rank's real token count. title: [Perf] multi-item-scoring: avoid host syncs in label-logprob readback and embed overrides
summary: ## Motivation Multi-item scoring (`enable_mis`, `/v1/score`, `Engine.score`) runs prefill without CUDA graphs or chunked prefill, so throughput depends on the overlap scheduler keeping the GPU fed. On a pointwise yes/no scoring workload the scheduler blocked on the GPU several times per batch. Each block was either a device tensor read on the host or a host-to-device copy from pageable memory, and in both cases it waited for the next batch's forward, which the overlap scheduler had already launched. CPU and GPU then ran one after the other: SM utilisation was 60-67% on H200. This PR removes two of those syncs, one per commit. The math is unchanged; only the way data moves between host and device changes. ## Modifications 1. **Label-token logprobs are read back with one async pinned copy per batch** (`logits_processor.py`). - Before: for multi-item scoring the label logprobs at each delimiter stayed on the device as one tensor per request, and the scheduler read each with a blocking `.tolist()`. - Now: `_multi_item_token_ids_logprobs_to_host` gathers the requested token ids for the whole batch and starts an `async_d2h` into pinned memory. When every scored request asks for the same label ids (the normal score API case) this is one H2D of the ids, one gather and one D2H; with different ids of the same count, per-request gathers and one D2H; with ragged counts, one D2H per request. - It records `input_logprobs_copy_done`, and the readers already call `finalize_input_logprobs()`, which waits on that event and flattens the pinned spans into rows. title: [Perf] gdn: Add an opt-in lazy ReplaySSM fold for 16-bit checkpoints
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, a GDN layer verifies its drafts from the request's checkpoint plus a ring of the request's accepted (update, key, decay) entries. An fp32 checkpoint folds the ring into the checkpoint only when the next draft window would not fit. A 16-bit one (`--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`) folds after every verify (`fold_every_commit` in `spec_utils.py`), so each decode step's commit reads and writes every request's full state: 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.6 ms of a 2.1 / 2.6 / 3.1 ms verify + commit step at 40 / 52 / 64 requests (MI355X, the 36 GDN layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). This PR adds an opt-in, `SGLANG_OPT_GDN_REPLAYSSM_LAZY_FOLD=1`, that gives a 16-bit checkpoint the fp32 rule in verify batches of at least 34 × 48 request states per layer (requests × value heads: 34 requests at TP1 of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 68 at TP2). There it takes 6-17 % (TP1) and 3-25 % (TP2) off the step at mean accept lengths 1.74-3.34. Smaller batches fold every commit, each request with whatever history it still holds. The verify then reads ring history. `main`'s 16-bit history read drops the ring's low parts and rounds its products to bf16; under the opt-in the verify adds the low parts and splits the products into 16-bit high and low parts. Against fp64, its outputs' max and mean error in steps 2-10 are then 0.81-0.85x and 0.73-0.78x those of folding every commit (`main`'s history read: 1.06-1.38x and 0.87-0.91x; an fp32 checkpoint: 0.81-0.83x and 0.54-0.58x). title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Run extend attention on AITER's FlyDSL sparse prefill
summary: ## Motivation On gfx950, `QwenSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend` runs QSA extend attention on Triton: `sparse_gqa_fwd_interface_triton` for an extend without a prefix, `sparse_gqa_fwd_interface_triton_ck` on the packed K/V over a prefix. title: [Perf] spec: Size the MHA accepted-token KV move by chunk area, not tile width
summary: <!-- PR title: [mem_cache][Spec] Size the MHA accepted-token KV move by chunk area, not tile width --> ## Summary **TL;DR: the accepted-token KV move already chunks itself to keep the Triton specialization small; this PR derives that chunk bound from the compiled area instead of the tile width, so all three tile widths `MHATokenToKVPool` ships compile the same small kernel.** The bound reaches the compiler as a product -- `chunk_upper * bytes_per_tile`, the chunk area in bytes -- because `chunk_upper` becomes the kernel's `num_locs_upper` `tl.constexpr` and every distinct value compiles its own kernel. Branching on the width alone leaves that product free, and all three shipped widths land where the register allocator stops holding the working set in registers. Deriving the bound from a target area instead fixes the product at 16384 B and lets the row count follow the model: caps of 32 / 64 / 128 rows for the 512 / 256 / 128 B tiles, against 128 / 256 / 256 today. **It needs nothing set: no new flag, no tuning, no opt-in.** The derivation is guarded by `is_sm90_supported()`, so every other architecture keeps today's expression byte for byte, and MLA pools are untouched. - **Performance** (8xH200, SM90; `bench_serving --dataset-name random`, 512-token prompts, 128-token outputs, `--max-running-requests 256`, `--page-size 1`; median of `n` independent pairs, each pair restarting both servers; higher is better): - End-to-end output-token throughput is **higher on all 31 models measured, from 9 vendors**. summary: ## Motivation `response_format` (`json_schema` / `json_object`) misbehaves for Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open. summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #47546, covering its "Not covered" case (`tokenizer_worker_num > 1`) and the same gap with a single tokenizer worker. `/abort_request` is a point-in-time, rid-addressed message: the process it lands on aborts what it holds at that moment. The generate and the abort are independent HTTP requests, so the abort can arrive before the request reaches the scheduler: - with several tokenizer workers it usually lands on a worker that does not hold the rid, while the owner is still preprocessing it (pause gate, tokenization, multimodal feature publication); - it can arrive before any worker has registered the rid; - with one tokenizer worker it can arrive before that worker has registered the rid, where an unknown-rid abort is a no-op. The scheduler drops an abort for a rid it has not received, so the request is dispatched afterwards and runs to completion. As in #47546, on a PD decode server it holds its preallocated KV meanwhile. A client that disconnects is still caught by the disconnect poll a few seconds after dispatch; a caller that keeps the connection open and cancels through `/abort_request` has no other signal. ## Modifications - A tokenizer worker that sends an abort for a rid it does not hold marks the `AbortReq` with a new `forward: bool` field. The scheduler does not read it. - New `PendingAbortTable` (`managers/pending_abort_table.py`): rids whose abort arrived before the request, each consumed once, expiring after 30 s. title: [Perf] kimi-k3.1: Sequence-parallel layer tail for large eager prefill batches
summary: ## Motivation Original design and implementation by @nvpohanh. On a Kimi-K3.1 prefill with plain-TP attention (no attention DP or CP) and no EP all-to-all MoE backend, every TP rank repeats the row-wise part of each layer on all rows of the batch: the attention-residual bank reads, the residual adds, the latent RMSNorm, the latent up_proj and the tail add. The o_proj and MoE sums are full all-reduces. ## Modifications A sequence-parallel layer tail for large eager prefill batches. From the first MoE layer on, each TP rank keeps only its 1/tp of the rows (the batch is padded to a multiple of 2 * tp; pad rows are zero and dropped by every gather). Per layer: - bank read for the attention input on the local rows, then an all-gather of the normed attention input; - attention (MLA with DCP, or KDA), unchanged; - reduce-scatter of o_proj's TP partial with the residual add fused; - bank read for the FFN input on the local rows, then an all-gather for the MoE; - the fused MoE front and the routed experts, unchanged; the shared experts on the side stream end in a reduce-scatter instead of an all-reduce; - reduce-scatter of the routed latent sum, then the latent RMSNorm, up_proj and tail add on the local rows. DFLASH aux-hidden-state captures and the final norm run on the local rows and are gathered into owned storage. The collectives are K3's NVLS pull reduce-scatter and multicast direct all-gather on the TP group's CustomAllReduceV2, in BF16, with an NCCL fallback. title: [Fix] scheduler: reserve SPF capacity against both token budgets
summary: ## Motivation Shortest-prefill-first (SPF) can reserve room in the chunk budget while exhausting the separate input budget. In `get_new_batch_prefill` / `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` (`scheduler.py`) the chunked-request reservation was sized from `adder.rem_chunk_tokens` alone: with 4096 chunk tokens, 2048 input tokens and a 256-token waiter, the old arithmetic admits a 3840-token continuation and the waiting loop stops, its input budget spent. With `chunked_prefill_size > max_prefill_tokens` and every waiter longer than the continuation, `shortest_prefill_chunk_limit` returns `None`; the continuation then spends the whole input budget and the loop breaks on every pass (head-of-line stall). Tracks #48626. ## Modifications - `scheduler.py`: extract `_admit_chunked_req(self, adder, resumed_req)`, passing `resumed_req` explicitly (the helper previously read it out of scope, an undefined name on the admission path). It sizes the reservation against `min(rem_chunk_tokens or 0, max(adder.rem_input_tokens, 0))` (1792 in the example, 256 left for the waiter), calls `shortest_prefill_chunk_limit` and `add_chunked_req`, and moves the request to `prefill_launched_reqs` on its last chunk. title: [Fix] diffusion: Fall back to the cached snapshot when the Hub API lookup of weights fails
summary: ## Why the test broke `flux2_modelopt_nvfp4_t2i` in the B200 diffusion suite failed three times in four days with `429 ... api/models/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev-NVFP4 ... quota of 3000 api requests per 5 minutes`. The weights were already in the local Hugging Face cache, but `--transformer-weights-path` resolves its weight set through `resolve_weight_inventory`, which always calls `HfApi().model_info()` and has no fallback. A rate limit on a shared account therefore fails the run even though nothing needs downloading. #46679 skipped the API only for an exactly named weight file; a repo or subfolder reference still depends on the live call. ## Changes - `resolve_weight_inventory` (`runtime/weights/source.py`) still calls `model_info` first. When the call fails with a 429, a 5xx, or a transport error (connection, timeout), it falls back to the cached snapshot of the same revision (`_cached_hub_inventory`) and logs a warning. If no snapshot is cached, the original error is raised. - 401, 403, 404 and other client errors (missing repo, missing revision, no access) are raised as before, so the cache never masks a wrong reference. - When the API answers, behavior is unchanged: the inventory still comes from the Hub and is pinned to the commit it returns. Why fall back instead of skipping the API whenever a snapshot is cached: the cached listing holds only the files fetched so far, so choosing among candidates from it could resolve differently from the full listing (a missing index, a newer file on the branch). Using it only when the Hub cannot answer keeps every successful look

[Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Reduce TP groups over RCCL on gfx1250, where the custom all-reduce returns wrong sums
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** On ROCm, diffusion TP groups reduce through the srt `CustomAllreduce`, and on gfx1250 that kernel returns wrong sums: against RCCL `all_reduce` on the same bf16 inputs, the relative error is 0.38 to 0.77 for 0.7 to 15.7 MB tensors, which looks like the peer rank's contribution is missing. No error is raised, so a TP run finishes with silently wrong activations. **Where it shows up** Any diffusion model run with `--tp-size > 1` on gfx1250 (MI450) can hit it; other ROCm architectures and CUDA are not affected by this change. It reproduces on FLUX.2-dev with `--num-gpus 2 --tp-size 2`: the Mistral text encoder is TP-sharded, every row-parallel all-reduce in it is under the 16 MB custom all-reduce cap, so `prompt_embeds` come out at cosine 0.57 against TP1 and the image loses the prompt (the dog and the cake disappear). The DiT's own all-reduces are about 50 MB, above the cap, so they already went to RCCL. The same run with `--num-gpus 2` (sequence parallel, no TP all-reduce) is correct. **How to fix** Skip the srt custom all-reduce for diffusion TP groups on ROCm gfx1250, so every TP all-reduce there goes to RCCL; CUDA and other ROCm architectures keep the custom all-reduce. ## Modifications - `runtime/distributed/group_coordinator.py`: add `_srt_custom_allreduce_supported()`, which returns False on ROCm when `is_gfx1250_supported()` and otherwise keeps the previous `is_cuda_alike()` check. `GroupCoordinator.__init__` uses it to decide whether to build `srt_custom_allreduce`. With it unset, the eager path calls `torch.distributed.all_reduce`,

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsv4: use T.And for the dual-cache phase-1 guard in the TileLang FlashMLA kernel
summary: ## Motivation ROCM-30721: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 on MI350X aborts during decode CUDA-graph capture while TileLang compiles `dpsk_v4_fp8_partial_kernel`: ``` [ThreadSync] Cannot lower a required shared-memory sync ... not warp-uniform ... Condition: thread_binding < 448 ``` - In the dual-cache path, phase 1 is guarded with a Python bitwise `&`: `if (group_i < n_groups_1) & (group_i < actual_n_groups_1):`. Inside it, a 448-wide parallel loop on 512 threads needs a barrier for `thread_binding < 448`. That is 7 full waves, so it really is warp-uniform. - TileLang >= 0.1.14 checks barrier uniformity (tile-ai/tilelang#3085) and cannot prove it under the bitwise `&` (tile-ai/tilelang#3653, filed against this kernel). - The TileLang pinned in current images (`a55a823`) compiles it, so the bug is latent today. Any TileLang bump brings it back, and RDNA support needs one (ROCM-34286). ## Modifications `&` → `T.And(...)` for that guard: the same condition expressed as a logical and, which TileLang can prove uniform. One line. ## Accuracy Tests gfx950 dual-cache config (BI=64, 512 threads, H=64, topk 128/512): | TileLang | without this PR | with this PR | |---|---|---| | 0.1.15 | compile fails with the QA message | compiles | | a55a823 (image) | compiles | compiles; output and LSE **bitwise identical** to without | A wider static compile matrix (H=32/64/128, single and dual cache, several inner-iter splits) also compiles on a55a823, 0.1.14 and 0.1.15 with the change. No unit test: CI's TileLang is a55a823, which compiles either way, so a test would not fail without this change. ## Speed

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsv4: fix TileLang FlashMLA on gfx942 (pipeline crash + fnuz KV decode)
summary: ## Motivation ROCM-33500: DeepSeek-V4 Pro and Flash (FP8) fail on gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) in the TileLang FlashMLA kernel `dpsk_v4_fp8_partial_kernel`. It has two independent bugs: 1. **Compile crash.** The non-gfx95 dispatch uses `num_stages=1`. TileLang's `PipelinePlanning` (at the pinned `a55a823`) reorders the statement that writes `page_idx_shared` after the indirect K gather that reads it, and `InjectSoftwarePipeline` then aborts: `Check failed: src_info.order < dst_info.order (6 vs. 4)`. This is arch-independent: gfx950 fails the same way when forced to `num_stages>=1`, and only passes because it uses `num_stages=0`. TileLang main compiles it, but the bump isn't in any TileLang release yet. 2. **Wrong results once it compiles.** On fnuz platforms the KV writers store `float8_e4m3fnuz` (exponent bias 8), but the kernel's software FP8 decode hard-codes the OCP e4m3fn bias of 7, so every dequantized K/V element is 2x too large. This is why QA's `num_stages=0` workaround scored GSM8K 0.015. The Triton FlashMLA and other kernels in the same file already handle fnuz; this kernel was the outlier. ## Modifications - `dpsk_v4_fp8_attention_fwd`: `num_stages=0` for the non-gfx95 tile config too. The pipelined loop only runs `inner_iter` (typically 1-4) iterations. - `dpsk_v4_fp8_partial_kernel`: new JIT parameter `fp8_exp_bias` (default 7); the dispatcher passes `8 if _is_fp8_fnuz else 7`. gfx950 generates the same code. - Regression test `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_tilelang_fp8_fnuz.py`. It runs on any ROCm GPU, writes the cache with the production writer

title: [Perf] hicache: Faster unified page-envelope host pool — per-pool shared reclaim, hole-filling compaction, row-granular host↔device copies
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory --enable-hierarchical-cache`, the full-attention and window host pools of a hybrid-SWA model can share one page-envelope host backing. Under sustained multi-turn load, three costs in that host tier stall the scheduler: 1. **Compaction sorts every live page.** `_compact_side` gathers and sorts all live pages of a side and moves them into a packed prefix on the scheduler thread, even when only a few holes exist. With large host caches this produces multi-second stalls. 2. **Shared-domain reclaim always drains windows first.** When a shared allocation fails, `_alloc_shared_host_requests_with_reclaim` asks each requested pool to free the whole shortfall in order. The window pool is drained first every time, so the host window share shrinks one-way and hit rates fall. 3. **Whole-page kernel copies.** Host↔device copies for the envelope move one page per work item, which leaves the copy kernel under-occupied for large transfers. This addresses the roadmap item "Optimize compaction and data movement" in #49944. ## Modifications - `mem_cache/kv/memory/host_backing.py` (**platform-generic**): compaction fills holes from the side's high-water mark inward instead of sorting all live pages. The result has the same packed layout invariant and logical↔physical mapping, with far fewer moved pages. Call sites and the external interface are unchanged. - `mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py` (**CUDA only**): in the shared page-envelope domain, each requested pool first reclaims its proportional share of the remaining byte shortfall (a

title: [Doc] linear-attn: Document the extra_buffer contract for registered linear attention backends
summary: ## Motivation Addresses #48463. Linear attention models registered from outside SGLang (`register_linear_attn_model`) get the mamba radix cache. With `mamba_radix_cache_strategy=auto`, SGLang picks between two strategies: - `extra_buffer`, when the spec sets `support_mamba_cache_extra_buffer`. - `no_buffer` otherwise, which turns overlap scheduling off. `no_buffer` cannot run with overlap scheduling. It copies (or donates) the request's own state slot while processing batch N's results. By then, batch N+1 may hold the same request and be advancing that slot in place, so the cache would store a later state under an earlier key. We reproduced this by forcing `no_buffer` with overlap on in TorchTitan's GDN parity tests: decode after a cached prefix differed from the trainer (max delta about 2e-3). With the radix cache disabled and overlap on, the results were bitwise equal. For an external backend, `extra_buffer` is the way to keep overlap scheduling. But what the backend has to do is undocumented. It is also easy to get wrong silently: a backend that declares support but does not fill the track slots puts stale states in the cache. title: [Perf] hicache: Space out write_back eviction waits with a bounded reserve
summary: ## Motivation With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, a device eviction backs its victims up to host and blocks on that copy (`writing_check(write_back=True)` -> `ack.finish_event.synchronize()`). The D2H stream is fenced on the forward stream (#44800), so every eviction pass waits for the whole in-flight forward. On a saturated prefill instance the device pool is full, so nearly every scheduling step evicts exactly its shortfall and pays that wait. The scheduler loses its one-step lookahead every step. Under DP attention the peer rank waits for it in the DP-attention all-gather, and the GPU idles between forwards. In a PD prefill trace this was 14-15% GPU idle, almost all of it between forwards. #46884 removed an earlier form of this wait (the coarse WAR barrier behind the write-back index copy). The eviction ack wait remains. #41690 adds a reserve at some allocator call sites. This PR instead puts the reserve inside `UnifiedRadixCache.evict()` and the per-pool shortfall eviction of `evict_for_alloc()` (`evict_pool_shortfalls`), which stay exact-shortfall today. Those are reached by the paged allocator's eviction, HiCache load-back and the linker LOAD path. ## Modifications - New opt-in `SGLANG_OPT_HICACHE_WRITE_BACK_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS` (default 0: unchanged). - Under write_back, `UnifiedRadixCache.evict()` and `evict_pool_shortfalls()` grow a nonzero token / window shortfall by the reserve, capped by the evictable size. title: [Perf] hicache: Fence write_back eviction copies on the forward stream instead of blocking the scheduler
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache `write_back`, the device eviction walk backs its victims up to host and then blocks the scheduler on `Event.synchronize()` for those D2H copies before it demotes the victims. The copies are fenced behind the in-flight forward (`write_fence_stream`), so on a busy prefill server the scheduler cannot finish building the next batch until the current forward ends. On DSv4.1-Flash disaggregated prefill this wait was 50-56% of scheduler time, and the GPU sat idle while the next batch was prepared and launched. ## Modifications `_demote_backed_up` no longer waits on the host. It submits the queued copies and makes the forward stream `wait_event` on each copy's finish event, then finishes the acks and demotes the victims at once. Without overlap scheduling the forward runs on the current stream, so the current stream waits as well; the scheduler tells the cache controller which case applies. Ordering: - The copy still waits for the in-flight forward (unchanged `write_fence_stream` fence), so it reads complete KV. - The next forward waits for the copy. With overlap scheduling it runs on the forward stream. Without overlap it runs on the current stream, which then also waits, and so do current-stream writers such as a Mamba state copy into a freshly allocated slot (Mamba `no_buffer` turns overlap off). - With overlap the current (schedule) stream does not wait: making it wait would serialize the scheduler's GPU work behind the in-flight forward and the copy, which cancelled the gain in measurement (below). - Every later load-back waits for the copy, because

summary: ## Motivation Plain tensor parallelism scales prefill poorly on this model. summary: ### Describe the bug For MHA models (`kv_group_num == 1`), `decode_attention_fwd` runs `_fwd_kernel_stage1`. The element product `q * k` is formed in the input dtype and is cast to fp32 only after that. In fp16, one product above 65504 becomes `inf`. The softmax then computes `exp(inf - inf)`, and all outputs of the head become NaN. The grouped kernel (`_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`, [decode_attention.py#L689-L691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py#L689-L691)) and the extend/prefill kernels use `tl.dot` with fp32 accumulation and give finite results on the same data. So the same token gives a finite result in prefill and NaN in decode. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Prefill CP today **replicates** at-rest KV storage: every CP rank allgathers the full chunk's K/V and writes all of it into its own pool, so a CP group of size N stores each cached page N times — group-aggregate *unique* cache capacity stays at 1×. MLA has the same redundancy on a second axis: the latent KV is computed by a replicated projection, so every attention-TP rank stores an identical copy. On the prefill workers of a PD-disaggregated deployment, this replication directly caps radix-cache hit rate — and therefore TTFT — for long-context and multi-turn workloads. This PR introduces `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, which stores each KV page **exactly once per shard group** (~N× unique cache capacity at unchanged per-rank HBM) around a single abstraction: the **logical page** — N consecutive, N-aligned physical pages, one per rank. The allocator's index space is widened ×N (the landed DCP configuration, generalized to page granularity), the radix-tree quantum follows the allocator page, and page ownership is pure arithmetic (`owner(loc) = (loc % N·ps) // ps`) — so the tree, allocator, `req_to_token`, and scheduler keep running identical SPMD code on identical state, with no ownership metadata, directory, or cross-rank consensus anywhere. title: [Perf] disaggregation: Stream a PD decode request's first token with its first decode output
summary: ## Motivation A PD decode server streams the prefill-sampled first token as soon as the request is admitted (`process_batch_result_prebuilt`). Under the overlap scheduler, that request's first decode forward is queued behind the forward already in flight, so its next tokens arrive about two decode steps later. Client TPOT is computed as (e2e - TTFT) / (osl - 1), so this gap is charged to every request's TPOT. On DeepSeek-V4.1 with DEP32 decode, the time to the second token was ~104 ms, against ~92 ms for a steady 32-token chunk. A decode server that samples the first token in its own first decode step has no such gap. ## Modifications At admission, the decode server now streams only requests that have already finished, for example `max_new_tokens=1`. A running request's prefill token goes out with its first decode output, which the output streamer sends at once because `send_token_offset == 0`. This applies to PD decode only. Non-disaggregated serving is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Output tokens are unchanged; only the time at which the first token is sent changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Setup: - Hardware: GB300. - Model: DeepSeek-V4.1 with MTP. - Deployment: PD disaggregation; the prefill worker count and the decode size vary by point (below). - Workload: agentic multi-turn, 3600 s per run. | point | run | throughput / GPU (tok/s) | p50 / p90 TPOT (ms) | 1 / p90 TPOT | p50 / p90 TTFT (s) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 10 prefill + DEP32 decode, concurrency 4000 | base | 620.4k | 2.87 / 3.05 | 327.9 | 1.92 / 6.25 | | | this PR | 618.5k (-0.3%) | 2.82 / 2.95 | **339.0

title: [Perf] moonvit: Pool video frames before reordering spatial blocks
summary: ## Motivation Kimi K3 and K2.5 use the same MoonViT temporal pooling helper. For each video group it materializes a tensor of all frames in spatial-block order, then averages those frames into a single output grid. title: [Feat] [NPU] hicache: Support modelslim MLA fp8 kv and GQA mxfp8 kv for L2 Hicache
summary: ## Motivation SGLang supports ModelSlim FP8 MLA and MXFP8 GQA KV caches on NPUs. Previously, HiCache did not support ModelSlim FP8 MLA and MXFP8 GQA KV caches. Reusing an evicted prefix through L2 HiCache requires preserving each format’s full cache state. MLA stores its compressed KV latent in FP8 and its RoPE key in BF16. GQA stores dynamic K scales alongside its MXFP8 K/V data. This PR enables both formats to round-trip through CPU memory so that prefill can reuse the restored prefix. ## Modifications - **MLA FP8 KV:** Allocate the split host buffers using the device dtype of each component. Account for the FP8 latent and BF16 RoPE key separately when sizing the host pool and reserving memory. - **GQA MXFP8 KV:** Add an L2 host pool for `QK_MXFP8_DYNAMIC_V_MXFP8_PER_CHANNEL`. It uses the existing Ascend transfer path to back up and restore K/V pages together with their dynamic K scales. Static per-channel V scales are initialized from the checkpoint and stay on the NPU. - **Manual NPU tests:** Add L2 round-trip tests for DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus (TP8) and Qwen3.6-27B (TP2). The tests force L1 eviction, verify a host-cache hit, and compare generated token IDs and log probabilities against an L1-resident reference. The suites also include GSM8K and GPQA Diamond accuracy checks, respectively. ## Accuracy Tests GPQA-Diamond test (qwen3.6-27B with modelslim gqa mxfp8 kvcache) 0.864 200 gsm8k tests (dsv3 with modelslim mla fp8 kvcache): 0.98

title: [Perf] hicache: rank finished sub-agent sessions first for host eviction (Qwen3.8 Perf 17/18)
summary: Split out of #50156 (reverted in #50703) as its own change, measured against `main`. ## Motivation Agentic clients such as coding agents spawn sub-agents. A sub-agent is a short session that starts from its own prompt, runs a few turns, and returns a result to the session that spawned it. Under HiCache `write_back`, a finished sub-agent's prefixes stay in the host tier and compete for host capacity with the contexts of live sessions. Host eviction is LRU. Sub-agents that have just finished are more recent than the contexts of other agents that sit idle while they wait for their own sub-agents, so host eviction drops those live contexts first, and they are recomputed when their agents resume. This PR lets a client say which session spawned a request, and, behind an opt-in switch, ranks the nodes of finished sub-agent sessions first for host eviction. ## Modifications **Request field (no output change).** `parent_session_id: Optional[str]` names the session that spawned this one. - `GenerateReqInput`: keyword-only field, declared like `session_id`; each item of a batch inherits it. - `Engine.generate` / `Engine.async_generate`: keyword-only argument, declared like `cache_salt`. - `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`: a defaulted tail field, so older IPC senders still decode. - `Req`: stored for the cache. - It reaches `/generate` and the `Engine` API. title: [Fix] Handle overflowing TopK v2 threshold buckets exactly
summary: ## Motivation TopK v2 can silently select incorrect values when more than 2,048 candidates occupy the threshold bucket. FP32 scores in a coarse bucket need not be equal, so selecting from an arbitrary retained subset can discard required high-score members even when all returned indices are valid. ## Modifications - Preserve the true bucket population while keeping candidate-buffer copies capacity-bounded. - Recover overflowing buckets from the valid input using four byte-wise radix passes and a final scan, retaining all higher keys and only the required cutoff ties. - Apply recovery to register, streaming, and cluster selection. Cluster recovery runs in rank 0; no additional kernel launch or host synchronization is introduced. - Add strict regressions for overflow boundaries, output modes, negative scores, partial ties, infinities, ragged/odd lengths, small K, and changing CUDA Graph inputs. Public APIs and dispatch remain unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests H20 (78 SMs), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: - **155 strict added regressions passed**, including 55 additional boundary/Graph cases. - Full test file: **443 passed, 18 ROCm-only skipped**. The strict regressions are included in the 443; existing general tests retain upstream tolerances. - The same 4,096-candidate negative control fails the selected-value oracle upstream and passes with the fix. - Memcheck, racecheck, and synccheck each passed the same 55 new cases with zero errors; racecheck also reported zero warnings. - The historical frozen failure passed eager and CUDA Graph checks with the unchanged CUDA implementatio

title: [AMD][Kimi-K3] Take the aiter fused cat+cache path on NoPE MLA layers on gfx95
summary: # [AMD][Kimi-K3] Take the aiter fused cat+cache path on NoPE MLA layers on gfx95 [sgl-project/sglang#41844](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41844) > **Depends on** the matching AITER change: `fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla`, a NoPE variant of `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, [ROCm/aiter#5980](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5980). It's safe to merge either way: with an aiter that lacks the op, NoPE layers stay on the existing unfused path. It only pays off once the aiter change is in. ## Motivation On MI355X the aiter MLA absorb decode path spends four launches per layer on layout and cast work — the absorbed-q concat, the K concat, the BF16→FP8 KV cast, and the paged scatter. That is ~20.5 us per layer and it is entirely dispatch-bound, so batch size barely moves it. `forward_mla_rocm.py` already has the fix and already calls it: aiter's `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` does all four in a single launch. But it was reachable only for layers carrying a rotary embedding, because the wrapper unconditionally read `attn.rotary_emb.cos_cache`. Kimi-K3's MLA is NoPE, so every layer fell back to the four-launch path. ## Modifications aiter now has a NoPE entry point, `fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla`. It copies the PE halves through unrotated and keeps the q concat, the k concat, the `k_scale` quantization and the paged write in one launch. This PR routes NoPE layers to it. **`_fused_rope_cat_and_cache`**: when `attn.rotary_emb is None`, call `fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla` with the same q/k tensors, KV buffer, `out_cache_loc`, `k_scale` and `q_out_dtype`, and no rope argument

title: [AMD][Kimi-K3] Update GEMM dispatch to route the fused MoE front GEMM through Aiter
summary: # [AMD][Kimi-K3] Update GEMM dispatch to route the fused MoE front GEMM through Aiter ## Motivation On ROCm, Kimi-K3's fused MoE front GEMM calls torch.mm directly and lands on hipBLASLt, even when SGLANG_USE_AITER is set and aiter already has tuned kernels for these shapes. This pull request routes that GEMM through aiter's tgemm, saving about 0.5–0.7 ms of decode time per token on MI355X while leaving the shared down projection and every non-ROCm path unchanged. More specifically, module-level GEMMs reach aiter's tuned `tgemm` through `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, but Kimi-K3's fused-front path does not: the merged MoE front GEMM — `hidden_states @ [H, gate_up + E + latent]` — goes through `_k3_bf16_gemm`, which calls `F.linear` / `torch.mm` directly on the raw merged weight, so it lands on hipBLASLt regardless of `SGLANG_USE_AITER`. title: [Fix] Coordinate multi-tokenizer controls with broadcast_and_wait
summary: ## Motivation With multiple Python tokenizer workers, an instance-wide control request can complete before sibling workers have applied the required state change. For example, `/update_weights_from_tensor` can update the backend and the receiving worker's configuration while a sibling still reports the previous version through `/model_info`. Sibling workers can also admit requests during an update's local drain. Pause/continue already have router-side broadcast support, but completion is tracked by the initiating worker rather than an acknowledgement from every worker. Abort can miss a request that is still tokenizing or publishing multimodal features when the scheduler processes cancellation. This PR gives these operations a shared completion mechanism while retaining the current Python worker processes and backend dispatch. Related: [#24462](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24462) introduced pause/continue fan-out; [#33700](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33700) and [#33701](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33701) address overlapping completion-state races. This change also preserves the scheduler-owned per-token version tracking from [#35926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35926). ## Modifications - Compose a `ControlCoordinator`, `ControlRpc`, and `WorkerBroadcast` into the existing managers. `broadcast_and_wait(action)` snapshots participating tokenizer workers and collects distinct ACKs for that action. - Coordinate pause/continue, the existing disk/tensor/distributed/checkpoint-engine IPC weight updates, version updates, and

title: model_loader: only open the MTP-head shards for a NextN/MTP draft load
summary: ## Motivation An EAGLE/MTP **NextN draft** is loaded from the **same combined checkpoint** as the target, so `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` hands it **every shard in the safetensors index** — the whole checkpoint — even though the draft consumes only the appended NextN layer: - `embed_tokens` / `shared_head.head` are **shared from the already-resident target** (`deepseek_weight_loader` skips them: `if "shared_head.head" in name or "embed_tokens" in name: continue`), not read from disk; - every other tensor is skipped by the NextN weight loader (`if not name.startswith(layer_prefix): continue`) **after** the iterator has already opened the file. title: [Bugfix] Prevent hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk decode over-admission
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk scheduling admits new prefill tokens while an existing decode batch is executed in the same forward pass. The mixed-chunk path does not perform the regular decode memory check before admission. However, the existing decode batch still requires SWA KV pages immediately after admission. Since `PrefillAdder` did not reserve this SWA demand, prefill admission could consume pages required by decode. This can cause decode allocation failure under SWA memory pressure. ## Root Cause For a running batch, `new_tokens_required_next_decode()` returns the page-aligned token demand for the next decode step. The mixed-chunk admission path previously ignored this demand and initialized the SWA reservation offset to zero. The composite SWA allocator had a second issue: full-attention pages were allocated before SWA pages. If the SWA allocation failed, the full allocator had already consumed pages, leaving a partial allocation state. ## Fix Reserve the current decode batch's SWA demand during mixed-chunk admission: ```python mixed_decode_swa_tokens = ( running_batch.new_tokens_required_next_decode() if self.is_mixed_chunk and self.tree_cache.supports_swa() else 0 ) ``` Pass this value to `PrefillAdder` as the initial SWA reservation. Make hybrid SWA decode allocation preflight both underlying allocators before performing either allocation: ```python num_new_pages = get_num_new_pages( seq_lens=seq_lens_cpu, page_size=self.page_size, decode=True, ) if not self.new_pages_available(num_new_pages, num_new_pages): return None ``` This prevents full-KV pages fro

summary: ## Summary > **Supersedes [#31435](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31435).** This PR continues its GLM-5.2 Prefill CP Shared KV work and replaces it with a unified mixed Prefill/Decode implementation, adding Demand Cache, optional Shared Indexer, and EAGLE support. title: [spec] Reject trtllm_mha for DFlash drafts with non-causal sliding layers
summary: ## Motivation trtllm's spec-decode kernel is causal in-window. `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` therefore serves an `ENCODER_ONLY` layer by expanding the verify block into `bs*L` single-query decode rows, and those rows share one `cache_seqlens`. A decode row is understood to sit at the end of its sequence, so every query in the block is placed at the block's last position and they all get the same window, too narrow by up to `block_size - 1` keys for the earlier ones. Nothing errors. Measured on B200 against masks computed in fp32 over the same q/k/v, the multi-query verify call (`q_len_per_req = block`) matches a per-query window to 0.0012 in bf16, while the expanded path matches the anchored mask instead, which sits 0.365 away. The probe needs `block < window < prefix` to separate them at all -- at a shipped window of 2047 against a 16-token block the two masks differ by at most 15 keys out of 2047, at the oldest end of the window, which is why this went unnoticed. The gate meant to prevent this admitted exactly that shape. It kept `trtllm_mha` when the layers were *all* sliding **or** the draft was *all* causal, treating all-sliding as a reason to permit; a published DFlash draft is all-sliding with `is_causal: false`, so it took the one path the backend cannot represent. ## Modifications Gate on the pairing that actually breaks -- a layer that both slides and is not causal -- instead of on two whole-draft shapes. `is_causal` is three-valued to the model, so the check reads it that way. title: Prevent Qwen3.5 MTP draft from inheriting GPTQ quantization
summary: ## Motivation On RTX Pro 6000 with Qwen3.5 speculative NEXTN serving, using the model from [Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4), I launched the server with: ```bash SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ~/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4/ \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --quantization moe_wna16 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path ~/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4/ \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --dtype float16 ``` Before the fix, the draft path still inherited the target checkpoint quantization: ```text Load weight end. elapsed=4.86 s, type=Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP, quant=gptq, bits=4 ``` So `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant` was not taking effect for the Qwen3.5 MTP draft model, and the draft path could still inherit GPTQ quantization instead of staying unquantized. This can hurt MTP quality directly. On GSM8K with speculative MTP enabled at `steps=3`, the expected accept length is around 3.5, but with this bug the observed accept length drops below 3, which means the draft model is losing a large part of its speculative benefit. ## Modifications - Preserve explicit draft quantization intent through `ServerArgs` / `ModelConfig`. - Prevent draft-model quantization auto-detection when `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant` is explicitly set.

title: [AMD] Avoid padded Q for unified DSV4 prefill
summary: Reduce DeepSeek V4 prefill latency by eliminating unnecessary Q-head padding and the resulting contiguous copy in the unified-KV attention path. ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 TP prefill currently allocates a decode-oriented 64-head padded Q tensor, then passes the local-head slice to the unified-KV attention backend.
