title: [LMCache] Support MLA/DSA dual-buffer KV cache in LMCache connector
summary: ## Summary The LMCache connector (`LMCRadixCache`) hardcoded access to `k_buffer` / `v_buffer`, which only exists on MHA-style KV pools. MLA and DSA models use a fused `kv_buffer` instead, so LMCache could not be initialized for these architectures. This PR adds automatic KV buffer detection and DSA indexer support. ## Changes ### 1. KV buffer detection (MLA/DSA vs MHA) `__init__` now inspects the KV pool type and builds a flat `kv_caches` list: - **MLA / DSA** (`kv_buffer` present): fused single-buffer per layer, `use_mla=True`, `kv_cache_dim` inferred from the buffer shape. - **DSA indexer** (`index_k_with_scale_buffer` present): the indexer buffers are appended to `kv_caches` so both DSA layer groups are registered with LMCache. title: [Fix] moe: Pad NVFP4 trtllm hidden size to a multiple of 256
summary: ## Motivation On SM100, SGLang serves `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` with wrong MoE outputs. The cookbook launch command scores **17% on GSM8K**, against 90% for BF16. The TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE kernels need a hidden size that is a multiple of 256. Nano's hidden size, 2688, is a multiple of 128 but not of 256, and at that size the kernels run but return wrong results with no error. FlashInfer 0.7.4 documents the requirement (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8401), and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9333 reports the per-token case. `trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment` pads the hidden size only for the per-token non-gated variant, to 512. It leaves every other variant unpadded, including the static-scale ModelOpt NVFP4 path that the NemotronH override selects by default on SM100. vLLM's function of the same name pads those variants to 256. #39199, which added the padding, validated Nemotron 3 Super, whose hidden size of 4096 is already aligned. ## Modifications - `trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment` returns 256 instead of 1. Hidden sizes that are already multiples of 256 are unchanged, so only Nano-shaped checkpoints get padded: 2688 becomes 2816. This uses the existing padded path, which pads the weights at load, pads the activations, and slices the output, as the per-token variant already does. - FP4 dispatch: the padded path needs BF16 activations, because the dispatcher would quantize them at the unpadded size. `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` now leaves NVFP4 dispatch off when the TRT-LLM backend will pad the hidden size. title: [Feat] debug_utils: Tag non-intrusive dumps with an optional tags dict
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50087. Under DSPARK speculative decoding, the draft model's block forward borrows `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY` to reuse the verify-style attention metadata and the decode CUDA graph. The target model's verify forward uses the same mode. So when the non-intrusive dumper is on, draft and target dumps carry identical tags and cannot be told apart, and dumps of the same tensor from the two runners collide in the comparator. Which model a forward belongs to is a property of the runner, not of the forward, so `forward_mode` is the wrong place to encode it. ## Modifications - `register_non_intrusive_dumper(model, *, tags=None)` accepts an optional dict of tags and attaches it to every dump the hooks emit (both core fields and, in `all` mode, the prefixed module dumps). The tags are bound at registration, so two models in one process keep their own tags even when their forwards interleave. - `ModelRunner` passes `{"runner": "draft"}` or `{"runner": "target"}` (from `is_draft_worker`) only when speculative decoding is on. Without speculative decoding, and when no tags are given, dump names are unchanged. - The dumper itself stays unaware of speculative decoding: the tags are an opaque dict. - `register_non_intrusive_dumper` now has a docstring describing `tags`. Dumped files carry the tag in their name, for example `...___runner=draft.pt` and `...___runner=target.pt`. This overlaps with #50066, which covers the same three files with a `spec_role` string. This takes a generic `tags` dict instead, following the discussion on the issue. Either design works for me. #

title: [Perf] weight_checker: Avoid per-chunk host syncs and redundant FP32 casts in compare_weights
summary: ## Motivation Self-discovered performance and portability improvements in `sglang/srt/utils/weight_checker_comparator.py`: 1. **Fast-path native-dtype equality check before FP32 upcast**: - `compare_weights` previously executed `abs_diff = (actual_dq.float() - expect_dq.float()).abs()` on every chunk before checking if the chunk matched. For a `CHUNK_NUMEL = 64M` chunk of BF16/FP8 weights, upcasting both sides and materializing `abs_diff` allocates **3 $\times$ 256 MB = 768 MB** of temporary FP32 buffers even when expected and actual weights are bitwise identical (the common case during weight verification). - Checking `if torch.equal(expect_dq, actual_dq) and torch.isfinite(expect_dq).all(): continue` compares in the native dtype without allocating temporary FP32 tensors. 2. **Eliminate per-chunk GPU-to-CPU scalar synchronizations**: - When chunks differ, `compare_weights` previously triggered three separate device-to-host scalar transfers on every chunk (`abs_diff.max().cpu()`, `abs_diff.sum().item()`, and `int((~(abs_diff <= tol)).sum())`). - Accumulating `max_abs_err`, `sum_abs_err` (`float64`), and `num_exceed` (`int64`) on-device across chunks and synchronizing once after the loop completes eliminates per-chunk host stalls while preserving exact `float64` sum precision and `NaN` tolerance semantics. 3. **Guard `.cuda()` in `RawComparable.iter_chunks` and `Fp8BlockComparable.iter_chunks`**: - Guard `.cuda()` with `torch.cuda.is_available()` so `RawComparable` and `compare_weights` also work cleanly on CPU-only environments and unit tests. ### Attribution & Prior Work C

title: [ROCm][QuickReduce] Q8 BF16→FP16 low-amplitude scale saturation attenuates all-reduce output
summary: ## Summary With `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT8` and `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=1`, the ROCm two-shot `CodecQ8<half>` path can **strongly attenuate finite BF16 all-reduce inputs whose 32-value block maxima are below ~2e-3**. On an MI350X TP4/EP4 GLM-5.3 long-context run, this produced numerically wrong all-reduce tensors and an incoherent completion. Disabling the cast while retaining INT8 repaired the tested long-context continuation. This is the **low-amplitude reciprocal-scale cliff**, distinct from the high-end FP16 overflow in #34473 / #34484. The current [native source comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h#L35-L46) already describes the cliff; this report adds same-input operator and end-to-end causal evidence that real model activations cross it at `S=1`. ## Mechanism For each interleaved 32-value Q8 block, `CodecQ8<half>` stores `decoding_scale ≈ block_max / 128` in FP16 and computes `encoding_scale ≈ reciprocal(decoding_scale)` in FP16 ([implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce.cuh#L355-L497)). When `block_max` falls below roughly `128 / 65504 ≈ 0.001954`, the reciprocal cannot reach the value needed to map the maximum to Q8's full range and saturates at FP16's 65504. Encode/decode are no longer reciprocal: the whole block is attenuated. The two-shot collective can apply this twice. The existing [BF16 range test](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/kernels/test

summary: ## Motivation AI-assisted experimental prototype extending the existing prefill/decode cadence controls. summary: ## Motivation QSA's block selection picks each row's 512 blocks with `fast_topk`, which stages at most 4,096 members of a row's threshold bin and drops the rest, so a row with more drops members of its true top 512 (#36807 reports the same overflow in `fast_topk_v2`). On unpatched main, four rows of 8,192 scores in one threshold bin leave 239 to 263 of each row's 512 selected scores below the true 512th largest in two runs (`fast_topk` against `torch.topk`; repro in the details). This PR picks the blocks on gfx95 with `topk_v2` (#47960), which is exact in its default mode, for extend and for decode, target-verify and draft-extend batches. In extend, `topk_v2` reads only the order of the scores, so they stay unscaled and the division pass goes away. On one MI355X, one layer's selection takes 24.6 % less time for a 16,384-token extend chunk on an 83,968-token prefix, and 57.8 % less for a verify step of 60 requests (0.50 ms per decode step). Most of the extend gain is the division pass, which #48274 removes too; `topk_v2` alone saves 4.6 % to 11.0 %. title: [Feat] hicache: Forward request-scoped KV hints to storage backends
summary: ## Motivation #38891 added a versioned `kv_hints` envelope to generation requests. `GenerateReqInput` documents that it is "passed through untouched to the HiCache storage backends", but today it stops at `Req.kv_hints`: no storage backend can see it. This PR completes that path, so a HiCache storage backend can use an orchestrator's hint when it looks up and reads pages. Hints are stated in terms of the block hashes that SGLang publishes in KV events. For requests isolated by `cache_salt` or by an `extra_key` such as a LoRA adapter, those event IDs differ from the HiCache storage keys. A backend cannot convert between them without reproducing the scheduler's hash chain, so this PR also gives the backend that mapping. ## Modifications When a request carries `kv_hints`, HiCache storage lookups and reads for that request receive two entries in `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info`: - `kv_hints`: the request's `KvHintsEnvelope`. - `storage_key_to_event_hash`: only for namespaced requests (with a `cache_salt` or `extra_key`). summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On a PD decode server, once a request has been retracted under KV pressure, `process_decode_queue` returns before it polls the transfer queue, for as long as the retracted queue is not empty: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f76ac26543deb2149c2da9173b59b3adce16df0f/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py#L4545-L4548 ```python self.disagg_decode_prealloc_queue.move_resumed(self.waiting_queue) if len(self.disagg_decode_prealloc_queue.retracted_queue) > 0: # if there are still retracted requests, we do not allocate new requests return False ``` The return skips `_preallocate_new_requests`, and also `move_transferred` a few lines below. Requests that are already preallocated and sit in the transfer queue stay there after their KV has arrived: they never run and never free their pages. Each of them still counts one `num_reserved_decode_tokens` against the resume budget of the retracted request (`_active_req_count` counts the transfer queue). When the free space is below what that budget needs, the retracted request never fits again, its queue never empties, and the transfer queue is never polled

title: [Feat] CP: Prefill context parallelism for Kimi K3
summary: ## Motivation K3 = 93 layers: 69 KDA (linear attention, chunked delta rule) + 24 MLA (softmax attention). Every layer except the dense layer 0 is followed by a latent MoE (896 NVFP4 experts, top-16, latent width 3584, two bf16 shared experts, SiTU activation). Hidden size 7168, 96 attention heads, attention projections in FP8 (DeepGEMM), MoE front/back projections in bf16. The branch's prefill CP is "full-sequence CP": only the MLA layers see a token shard (zigzag, balanced causal work) with attention TP width A = tp / cp; KDA and MoE run the full sequence on every rank with the usual TP8 collectives. CP8 means A = 1: every rank holds all 96 MLA heads for its N/8 query rows and the MLA o_proj all-reduce disappears. Structurally, CP cannot reduce attention, KDA or expert FLOPs per rank (heads × queries is conserved) and it does not touch the KDA/MoE collectives, so on its own it can only trade the MLA all-reduce against the cost of replicating the K/V expansion. Two things had to change for CP8 to win. ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests

summary: Split out of #50156 (reverted in #50703) as its own change, measured against `main`. ## Motivation With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, `UnifiedRadixCache` copies a node to host when it is evicted from the device. The eviction walk queues the D->H copies of its victims, then calls `writing_check(write_back=True)`, which blocks the scheduler thread on every copy's finish event, and only then frees the victims' device pages. The copies are queued behind the write fence (the forward stream), so the wait lasts as long as the forward still running plus the copy itself. Under overlap scheduling this sits on the extend round's host critical path: the scheduler cannot prepare and launch the next forward until the previous one has finished and the copy has landed. The wait exists only to keep the freed pages (and their host copies) from being reused before the copy has read them. That ordering can be expressed on the GPU instead. ## Modifications - New opt-in switch `SGLANG_OPT_HICACHE_WRITE_BACK_ORDERED_DEMOTE` (`EnvBool`, default off). summary: Split out of #50156 (reverted in #50703) as its own change, measured against `main`. ## Motivation On a HiCache hit, the KV pages come back to the device one layer at a time through the JIT per-layer kernel, which runs on a fixed CTA quota: 4 CTAs for the TMA kernel, 2 for the register kernel. title: [Perf] attention: Parallelize MLA chunked-prefix KV index construction
summary: ## Motivation MLA chunked prefill builds cached-prefix KV indices with one Triton program per request, copying the row serially in 512-token tiles. At batch size 1, a single program handles the entire prefix. Parallelize the copy over token blocks. On B200, a 131,072-token prefix improves from **49.381 us to 1.832 us** (**27x faster; 96.3% lower kernel latency**). ## Modifications - Add `create_chunked_prefix_cache_kv_indices_2d` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/kv_indices.py` and register it in the attention kernel namespace. Each program copies one 1,024-token block, with an early return for inactive blocks and a masked tail. - Update the direct request-to-token table branch in `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_deepseek_mha_mixin.py` to launch `(batch_size, cdiv(max_chunk_len, 1024))`, using the existing CPU-side maximum chunk length. - Retain the 1D kernel for its other callers, including the separate prefill CUDA-graph and DCP-planner paths. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Insert the prompt end in the same checkpoint as an SWA branch point
summary: ## Motivation In multi-turn workloads on SWA models, some conversations lose their prefix cache on every turn after the first miss. When a request matches Full KV past its last live SWA window, the post-prefill checkpoint inserts only up to the SWA branching point. The SWA window at the prompt end stays request-owned. Decode retires it once the request passes one window, because `cache_protected_len` is still the branching point. The finish insert then stores the prompt end as an SWA tombstone. The next turn of the conversation again matches only up to the branching point, branches again, and the misses chain from turn to turn. Only single-chunk prefills whose decode passes one window are affected. A multi-chunk prefill already inserts the branch window and the prompt-end window on its next chunk. ## Modifications - `UnifiedRadixCache.checkpoint_into_tree`: after a branch insert in the checkpoint that covers the whole prompt, insert the rest of the forward in the same checkpoint. The request then protects and locks the prompt end before decode starts, the same path a multi-chunk prefill takes on its next chunk. Earlier chunks, including the non-final KV sends of disaggregated prefill, still stop at the branch point. - Tests in `test_unified_radix_cache_core.py` cover page-aligned and partial last pages, a multi-chunk prefill, and `cache_protected_len` right after each checkpoint. The single-chunk cases fail without the fix on both the Python and the Rust TreeCore; the multi-chunk case guards the existing next-chunk path. ## Accuracy Tests The change affects only which KV en

summary: > **Stacked on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50929.** This branch contains both commits. Only the last commit, `[Perf] dsa: Skip Triton divisibility specialization ...`, is new here. I'll rebase onto `main` once #50929 merges. ## Motivation #50929 makes `bs` a runtime argument of the three DSA metadata kernels, so Triton no longer compiles a variant per batch size. These lists already hold `max_len`, `max_seqlen_k`, `total_len` and the page-table strides for the same reason. title: [Fix] unified_cache: Restore Inkling MTP draft state in the direct external linker
summary: ## Motivation #40223 restores every Inkling MTP draft head's KV and recurrent state on a HiCache hit, but the direct external linker never picked those pools up: the FULL + SWA + MAMBA linker group ignores `mtp_draft_device_pools` and `mtp_draft_mamba_pools` without an error. Target outputs stay correct (verification rejects bad drafts), but the accept length drops. ## Modifications - Pack draft KV into the linker pages: full-attention drafts and SWA drafts addressed by full-token ids ride the KV entry (a linker page may mix head geometries, so no separate draft sidecar is needed); SWA drafts that share the target's SWA indices ride the SWA entry. - Pack the separate draft Mamba conv/temporal state into the MAMBA entry, addressed by the target's slot indices. - Draft buffers attach to each entry's last transfer layer, since drafts read only after the whole target forward. - Small HiCache refactor in the same area: a sidecar draft with both full and SWA sub-pools now registers a `DRAFT` sidecar for its full sub-pool next to `DRAFT_SWA`, instead of only mirroring the SWA sub-pool (`build_hicache_draft_sidecars`, plus staging sizing in `prepare_hicache_staging`). title: [Perf] QSA: build the extend row map from the host lengths instead of reading its size back
summary: ## Motivation `QwenSparseAttnBackend._metadata_from_forward_batch` maps every extend row to its request with `torch.repeat_interleave(arange(bs), extend_seq_lens)`. Without `output_size`, `repeat_interleave` reads the total length back from the device, which synchronizes the stream. For the draft model's extend after a long prefill, that sync waits behind the whole queued target prefill, so the scheduler cannot prepare the next step ahead of the GPU. With 16k-token prefill chunks, it held the scheduler thread for about 90 ms per long-prefill extend round while the GPU drained its queue. ## Modifications - `qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`: a small helper, `_extend_token_to_batch_idx`, builds the row map. The device lengths are copied from `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens_cpu`, so their sum is known on the host. When the host lengths line up with the device tensor and no CUDA graph is being captured, the helper passes `output_size` from them; otherwise it reads the size back as before. - The resulting row map is identical in both cases. - `test_qsa.py`: one new case. The map built with host lengths equals the map built without them and raises no sync under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`; host lengths that do not line up keep the device read. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model outputs: the row map is the same tensor, value for value (asserted in the new test). The forward and the attention kernels are untouched. `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa.py` on an NVIDIA Rubin GPU: 301 passed, 1 skipped, including the new case. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - O

title: [Fix] [XPU] spec: Sample EAGLE verification on XPU instead of forcing argmax
summary: ## Motivation EAGLE verification on XPU always commits the target model's argmax, because XPU has no `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` kernel (`_verify_uses_greedy` returns True for every XPU batch). With speculative decoding on, sampled requests (temperature, top-p, top-k) are therefore silently decoded greedily, and the output distribution differs from the same request without speculation. `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is not a way out for most EAGLE3 drafts. Rejection sampling needs a draft distribution over the target vocab, and reduced-vocab drafts (e.g. 32000 of 151936 tokens for the Qwen3 EAGLE3 drafts) do not have one. ## Modifications The fix rests on one observation: a top-1 EAGLE draft is deterministic, so it is a point-mass proposal. Classic speculative sampling against a one-hot proposal is exactly target-only verification: accept the draft token `t` with probability `p(t)`, and on rejection resample from `p` with `t` removed. That needs no draft distribution. - `kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py`: - A `ONE_HOT_DRAFT` mode of the existing Triton `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel`. In this mode `q` is 1 for the proposed token and the residual removes only the rejected token. `DraftProbs` is never read and no draft distribution is materialized. - New `chain_speculative_sampling_target_only_triton`, with the `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` signature, so it plugs in where CUDA uses the sgl-kernel op. - It supports exact verification only, and raises if accept thresholds other than 1.0 are set. - `kernels/ops/speculative/verify_sam

title: [Fix] rust-server: Seed detokenizer decode stream with prompt tail
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51029. With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, generated text dropped the leading space of the first output token for Llama-2-style (SentencePiece) tokenizers: the Rust detokenizer minted each request's `DecodeStream` with an empty prompt context, so the decoder's `Strip(" ", 1, 0)` removed the space from the first token decoded alone ("▁Paris" → "Paris"). title: [Feat] kv-cache: 4-over-6 block-scale search for the NVFP4 KV cache
summary: # [Feat] kv-cache: 4-over-6 block-scale search for the NVFP4 KV cache ## Motivation The NVFP4 KV cache stores each 16-value block as E2M1 codes with one FP8 block scale, chosen so that the block's largest magnitude maps to 6, the largest E2M1 value. E2M1's grid is coarse at the top (4 → 6), so for some blocks a scale that maps the maximum to 4 reconstructs the block with lower error, because more of its values land on the finer part of the grid. This PR adds that search as an opt-in flag, `--nvfp4-kv-scale-search 4over6`. vLLM ships the same rule as `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_4over6` ("selects between max/6 and max/4 scales per 16 values by minimizing squared reconstruction error"). The cache layout, KV capacity and attention kernels stay the same, and the default path is untouched. ## Modifications - **New Triton kernel `quantization.nvfp4_kv_quantize_triton`** (`sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/nvfp4_kv_4over6.py`). It writes the same packed FP4 data and linear FP8 block scales as FlashInfer's `nvfp4_kv_quantize`. With `four_over_six=True` it builds both the max/6 and the max/4 block scale for each 16-value block, rounds each to FP8, measures the squared reconstruction error with the rounded scale, and keeps the lower one. With `four_over_six=False` it matches FlashInfer bit for bit. - **New flag `--nvfp4-kv-scale-search {default,4over6}`** (default `default`). `NVFP4KVCacheMethod` reads it and passes it to every K and V store through `NVFP4KVQuantizeUtil.quantize`, which calls the Triton kernel only for `4over6`. The default never runs the new kernel. - **Validation:** the f

title: [Fix] jit: Build four JIT kernels with CUDA 13.5 and 12.x nvcc
summary: ## Motivation Four JIT kernels fail to build with some CUDA toolkits. There are two independent causes. **Missing `<cassert>`.** `include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh` and `csrc/gemm/awq_dequantize.cuh` call `assert` without including `<cassert>`. With the CUDA 13.0–13.4 headers they still build, because `assert.h` comes in transitively: `sgl_kernel/type.cuh` → `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh` → `cuda_fp8.h` → `cuda_fp8.hpp` → `assert.h`. CUDA 13.5 removed that include from `cuda_fp8.hpp` (lines 80–88 in 13.4), and CUDA 12.2 never had it. With either toolkit, both files fail with `identifier "assert" is undefined`. The Docker images currently pin CUDA 13.0.3 and 13.4.1, so CI does not hit this yet. A 13.5 toolkit or image will. **`#pragma unroll` on a host-side range-for.** `csrc/elementwise/kvcache.cuh` and `csrc/elementwise/set_mla_kv_buffer.cuh` put `#pragma unroll` on the host-side lambda that picks a warp count from `{1, 2, 4}`. nvcc 12.2 hits an internal compiler error there (`Internal Compiler Error (codegen): "Parsing unroll count failed!"`). nvcc 13.0–13.5 accept it. summary: ## Motivation The GDN fused decode projection + Conv1D path is gated on `_is_cuda`, so ROCm never takes it — although every prerequisite is already satisfied on HIP: - `TritonGDNKernel.supports_packed_decode` is `not is_cpu() and not is_npu()`, i.e. true on HIP. Without the fusion, ROCm decode runs `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous` and then a separate `_causal_conv1d_update`. title: [Perf] [AMD] batch-invariant: Faster small-M launch for the segmented bf16 matmul on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode on gfx950, bf16 linear layers run through the segmented batch-invariant matmul (#45599). At decode batch sizes (M up to 64) its launch uses narrow 64-column tiles with 2 pipeline stages, and its final reduction (the step that adds the K segments) uses 4,096-element blocks. At these sizes that leaves much of an MI350X idle, and decode GEMMs are still one of the largest costs of deterministic mode. This PR tunes only the launch for M <= 64: 128-column tiles with 3 stages, and 1,024-element reduction blocks. Launch parameters cannot change the result: the K segments and the order in which they are added are fixed, so every launch gives the same bits. **Impact** - Deterministic-mode throughput on MI350X, 1k/1k, single request: Qwen3-8B +9.9% (TP1) and +10.5% (TP4), phi-4 +9.3%, Qwen3.8-27B +6.3%. At concurrency 16-64: +1.4% to +10.8% (tables below). - Outputs are bitwise the same as before this PR: the same tokens and log-probabilities. - Only `--enable-deterministic-inference` on gfx950 with bf16 linears at M <= 64 and N >= 1,024 changes. Normal mode, other GPUs, larger M and N < 1,024 are unchanged. ## Modifications - `batch_invariant_ops.py`, `_segmented_matmul_launch(M, N)`, for every N >= 1,024: - M <= 32: 32 x 128 tiles, 4 warps, 3 stages (was 32 x 64, 4 warps, 2 stages); - M <= 64: 64 x 128 tiles, 8 warps, 3 stages (was 64 x 64, 4 warps, 2 stages). Chosen from 10 candidate launches timed on MI350X over 22 bf16 linear shapes (Qwen3-8B, phi-4, Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, gpt-oss-20b, Llama 3.1 8B, a 24B Mistral model and the Qwen3-8B LM

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen: Fuse decode FP8 quant into GDN norm and output gate
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, a Quark per-channel FP8 linear with per-token activations (`QuarkW8A8Fp8`) quantizes its BF16 input in its own launch inside `apply_fp8_linear`. #41134 (@chuyeh) added two producers that write the `(fp8, scale)` pair in the launch of the op before the linear: the gated RMSNorm before the GDN `out_proj` (`_layer_norm_fwd(quant_heads=...)`) and the attention output gate before `o_proj` (`fused_sigmoid_mul(quant=True)`). They run only where the gfx950 small-M GEMM takes the shape (Qwen3.5-397B at TP2 and TP4, up to 40 and 36 tokens). `Qwen4ExpAttentionDecoderLayer` has no such branch, and the norm's launch cannot take a head count that is not a power of two: Qwen3.8's 48 GDN heads (24 at TP2) fail with `AssertionError: num_warps must be a power of 2`. This PR runs both producers for these linears at up to 256 tokens, Qwen4-exp's attention gate included. The linear receives the codes and scales its own quant would have computed, bit for bit: from 22 tokens, the 36 GDN and 12 attention layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next make 48 quant launches fewer per pass. title: [Feat] [CPU] numa: Add support for CPU-less HBM/NUMA node binding
summary: ## Motivation This PR adds support for explicit HBM/NUMA node binding in SGLang, specifically targeting systems with **CPU-less (memory-only) HBM nodes**. Previously, memory node binding relied entirely on auto-detection via `numa_node_of_cpu(...)` mapped from the assigned OpenMP CPU cores. On hardware architectures featuring CPU-less HBM nodes, this auto-detection fails or cannot target the memory nodes directly because no CPUs are attached to them. By introducing the `SGLANG_CPU_MEM_BIND` environment variable, you can now explicitly bind parallel execution ranks and migrate memory pages directly to specific NUMA/HBM nodes regardless of CPU topology. Examples: ```bash # With TP=1, the worker allocates from node 8. export SGLANG_CPU_MEM_BIND=8 # Global worker indices 0–3 allocate from nodes 8–11. export SGLANG_CPU_MEM_BIND=8,9,10,11 ``` ## Modifications - **`numa_utils.cpp`**: - Added the `node_mem_bind` argument to `init_cpu_threads_env`. - Updated memory node selection logic: when `node_mem_bind >= 0`, it overrides the automatic `numa_node_of_cpu` lookup, enabling manual targeting of CPU-less HBM nodes for `numa_migrate_pages` and `numa_set_membind`. - **`bootstrap.py`**: - Implemented parsing for `SGLANG_CPU_MEM_BIND` inside `_init_cpu_threads_env`. - For single-machine CPU runs (`dp_size=1`, `pp_size=1`), requires exactly one distinct NUMA memory node per TP worker. - Passes the resolved `node_mem_bind` integer down to the C++ extension layer. - **`torch_extension_cpu.cpp`**: - Updated function signatures and PyTorch bindings to accept the new `node_mem_bind` parameter.

title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Do not fuse a shared expert that the ignore list keeps unquantized
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49372. Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and the DeepSeek family fuse the shared expert into the routed experts' `FusedMoE` unless the quantization config's `can_fuse_shared_expert()` says no. `ModelOptConfig` (#40628) and `QuarkConfig` (#46800) keep a shared expert that they exclude from quantization out of the fused slot; `CompressedTensorsConfig` has no such method, so a compressed-tensors checkpoint that keeps `mlp.shared_expert.*` in BF16 through its `ignore` list is fused anyway. Its BF16 shared-expert weights are then routed to a quantized expert slot that has no `weight` parameter, and `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` fails to load (`KeyError: 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight'`). ## Modifications - `CompressedTensorsConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert()`: return `False` when an `ignore` entry (plain or `re:`) names the shared expert, as `ModelOptConfig` does; `shared_expert_gate` is a separate linear and does not block fusion. Both callers (`qwen2_moe.can_fuse_shared_expert` and `deepseek_common.utils.quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion`) already consult it. - New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_shared_expert_fusion.py`: an `ignore` list without the shared expert, with only `shared_expert_gate`, with the three shared-expert projections, and with a DeepSeek-style `re:.*shared_experts.*` entry. - `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` (GLM-5.3-Flash) also returns a reason when `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config)` holds, as the DeepSeek models' gate does. title: [Fix] models: map checkpoint KV-cache scale names in more model loaders
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48911. Part of #39942: it also covers the loaders listed in the comment there (GLM-4, GLM-4V, GLM-OCR and its NextN draft, Phi, OPT, Starcoder2, Persimmon, Grok-1, Zaya, Spark2.5, LocateAnything, Cohere2-MoE). The attention of these models has `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters, but their loaders never map a checkpoint's KV-cache scale names to them, so an FP8 KV cache runs with a scale of 1.0. The compressed-tensors name `<attn>.k_scale` is skipped as unknown, and the ModelOpt name `<attn>.k_proj.k_scale` is renamed to `qkv_proj.k_scale` by the stacked mapping and then skipped (OPT, Starcoder2, Qwen2.5-VL and the Gemma 3n multimodal model raise `KeyError` on it). A few loaders have a rule that misses one naming, and the shared helper only knows ModelOpt names under `self_attn` and `mixer`. The Qwen2, Mixtral (with GraniteMoe) and Qwen3-MoE loaders are left to #39943; its `weight_utils.py` change still applies on top of this one. ## Modifications - Call `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` before the q/k/v_proj -> qkv_proj rename, as `llama.py` does, in `glm4`, `glm4v`, `glm_ocr`, `opt`, `starcoder2`, `persimmon`, `grok`, `zaya`, `spark2_5`, `locate_anything`, `cohere2_moe`, `afmoe`, `bailing_moe_linear`, `qwen2_moe`, `qwen2_5_vl`, `mixtral_quant`, `gemma4_unified` and `embedding_gemma2`. `phi.py` walks the model's parameters, so it maps the checkpoint names first. `gemma3n_causal.py` and `gemma3n_mm.py` called the helper after the rename; the call moves before it. - `qwen3_next.py` (also used by `Qwen3NextForCausalLMMTP`) and `qwen4_exp.py` mapped only the ModelOpt

title: [Fix] ModelOpt: Refuse layers whose quant_algo SGLang cannot build
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49395. `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for a linear layer whose per-layer `quant_algo` has no branch, and `None` (unquantized) for such a fused MoE. The checkpoint's quantized tensors then load without an error: FP8 codes are copied in as BF16 values and the scales are skipped (only a `not found in params_dict` log line). `AEON-7/Qwen3.8-27B-AEON-ULTIMATE-UNCENSORED-NVFP4-MIXED` (about 10k downloads last month) stores 232 projections as `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN`, and all of them are built this way. #31827 hit the same fallback for MXFP8 layers before they got a branch. ## Modifications - `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method`: a linear or fused-MoE layer whose resolved `quant_algo` is not one the config builds now raises `ValueError` naming the layer and the algorithm. A layer the checkpoint does not list (`quant_algo` is `None`) stays unquantized, as before. The check runs per built layer, so an unsupported algorithm on a layer SGLang does not build (for example a draft head that is not loaded) does not block loading. - New test in `TestModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` (`test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py`): an `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` linear layer and fused MoE are rejected; an `NVFP4` layer and an unlisted layer are built as before. Supporting `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` itself (a per-channel FP8 weight with per-token dynamic activations) would be a separate change; this one only turns the silent load into an error. ## Accuracy Tests Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0

title: [RFC] [NPU] MoE expert offloading through Paged Experts
summary: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation # - **Status:** Proposed - **Roadmap:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/50795 - **Scope:** SGLang runtime on Ascend NPUs ## Summary We propose adding MoE expert offloading on Ascend NPUs by extending SGLang's existing **Paged Experts** implementation, not by writing a separate Ascend offloader. Paged Experts keeps all `E` routed experts in pinned host memory and only `K` expert slots per MoE layer on the device. It copies routed-but-missing experts into those slots and rewrites logical expert IDs to physical slot IDs. Routing and expert computation still run on the device. The first delivery will be a correctness-focused, single-NPU, eager implementation for unquantized experts. Later stages will add Ascend-native formats, asynchronous transfers, graphs, tensor parallelism, and trace-driven prefetch. Each stage will be independently validated and leave CUDA behavior unchanged. We plan to support the implementation, NPU validation, documentation, and benchmark publication for this roadmap item. ## Motivation and goals Routed experts account for much of the weight memory of large MoE models, but each token selects only a small subset. Keeping every expert on device can prevent a model from fitting or leave too little memory for the KV cache. Generic CPU offload transfers weights at module or layer granularity.

title: [Bugfix] Defer beam initialization until request admission
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `BeamCoordinator.validate_and_init()` does more than validate a request. On success, it creates device-backed `BeamGroup` state, replaces the leader sampling parameters, and increments the live-group count. The scheduler previously called it immediately after constructing `Req`, before multimodal prompt expansion, generation-budget clipping, prompt-length validation, and the remaining request checks. Rejected requests could therefore leave an initialized group behind, while valid multimodal or truncated requests could initialize the group using a stale prompt length or generation budget. In addition, `is_beam` was computed only in the normal-request branch. Legacy `session_params` requests therefore bypassed beam validation even though beam search does not support sessions. ## Modifications - Compute `is_beam` before request and session routing. - Move `BeamCoordinator.validate_and_init()` to the final request-admission boundary, after prompt processing and request validation but before grammar processing and queue insertion. - Preserve the existing `BAD_REQUEST` response for invalid or unsupported beam requests. - Add CPU regression tests that verify: - beam initialization uses the finalized prompt and generation budget; - invalid prompts do not initialize a beam group; - legacy session requests do not by

title: [Roadmap] Prefill-Decode Disaggregation Roadmap (2026 Q4)
summary: ## Motivation Prefill-Decode Disaggregation is now the default way people run SGLang at scale, and over the last two quarters we have made it work with almost every model family, every parallel strategy (TP/PP/CP/DCP/DP-attention), HiCache, and speculative decoding (see the Q2 roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21703 for the history). The cost of that is visible in the code: three transfer backends that each carry their own copy of the protocol, a KVCache lifecycle that is only correct because of a long list of patches, and a decode side that still reserves every destination slot in HBM up front. So for Q4 the theme is less "support one more combination" and more "make the thing we already have correct, memory-efficient, and better coordinated with the router": 1. One protocol layer, per-backend transport (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510). 2. KVCache liveness as an invariant, not a patch series. 3. Pre-allocate decode KV slots in HiCache / host memory instead of VRAM, and move the KV into VRAM once the transfer is done. 4. Router/engine coordination for agentic prefix reuse. ## Shared-protocol unification Tracker: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510, RFC: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861 @jambow0320 @livingshade Mooncake / NIXL / Mori each implement bootstrap, room lifecycle, chunk orchestration, timeout, heartbeat, abort, and failure handling in their own `conn.py`. title: [Fix] tokenizer: Isolate and offload regular fast tokenization
summary: ## Problem Long regular HF fast-tokenizer calls in `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts()` block the asyncio event loop and delay handlers such as `/ping`. Moving the call to a worker is insufficient if loop-side callers still share its native backend: a padding/truncation update can wait on the worker's encode. Addresses the regular HF fast-tokenizer case in #30770. OpenAI conversion is already offloaded by merged #39771; this PR leaves that implementation in place. ## Changes - Use one worker with a separate native backend, cloned once at startup, for regular HF fast-tokenizer work that needs offloading. Pass the tokenizer explicitly to the worker. - Encode regular single strings of up to 256 characters inline to avoid executor handoff on short requests. - Shallow-copy the wrapper per call so later wrapper settings are reflected without copying the vocabulary on the request path. Propagate request contextvars. - Preserve synchronous behavior for slow/custom tokenizers and a tokenizer whose backend has been replaced. Preserve the dynamic-batch branch, cross-encoder/result handling and existing OpenAI conversion parallelism. - Add registered CPU coverage for loop and real ASGI `/generate` + `/ping` responsiveness, backend separation, current wrapper settings, fallback behavior, serialization and context propagation. HTTP tests substitute model execution. The backend-isolation direction follows @chromecast56's work and @hnyls2002's [shared-tokenizer review on #39716](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39716#discussion_r4150104467). #39716 and @JianWang97's #44502 both b

title: [Perf] DFLASH: Verify top-k sampled batches on the all-gathered top-k support (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation This continues #46080 by @nbommi19, rebased onto current main with the review feedback on that PR applied. The original commits are kept. With TP > 1 and a softcapped lm_head, DFLASH verify finishes the logits all-gather in the worker. For a sampled batch it all-gathers the full fp32 logits of every verify row (`[bs * block, vocab]`), runs a top-k over the whole vocabulary, scatters the target p and the draft selector's q into vocab-sized tensors, and runs the chain sampler over the whole vocabulary. When requests sample with a top-k (Muse-Spark-Open's generation config uses top_k 64), only the top-k tokens of a row carry target mass. With `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_SPARSE_VERIFY` on, such a batch is verified on the top-k support alone: - each rank takes the top `next_power_of_2(max_top_k + 16)` logits of its vocab shard; the 16 spare slots hold logits tied with the k-th one; - the ranks all-gather those (value, id) pairs instead of their shards (at TP8 and a 202K vocabulary, 1 KB per row from each rank instead of 101 KB); - one Triton kernel softcaps and merges the candidates into each row's exact top-k and argmax, with the softcap formula of the dense gather; - one Triton kernel runs the chain accept and the residual resample on that support, with the dense path's two uniform draws in the same order. A batch the support cannot reproduce keeps the dense path: max top_k above 64 (top_k -1 included), top-p, min-p, any logit adjustment (penalties, logit bias, custom logit processor, grammar), logprobs, sampling-mask capture, block verification and padded vocab shards. title: [Feat] spec/dflash: keep an all-sliding-window DFLASH draft's KV on the target's SWA slots
summary: ## Motivation The DFLASH draft for Muse-Spark-Open (`RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2`) has 5 layers, all sliding-window (window 2048). Today it still gets its own per-token KV pool, sized like the target's full-attention pool, so most of that memory is never read: on GB300 TP4 the draft pool takes 18.89 GB. In PD disaggregation the whole draft KV history is also transferred, although decode only reads the last window. This PR builds on the core approach of #46116: the draft KV lives on the target's SWA slots, the target's budget charges the draft per SWA token, trtllm_mha reads the draft through the SWA page table, and HiCache keeps a draft sidecar of the SWA host pool. On top of that it: - turns on automatically at launch when every condition holds, instead of through an env var, and logs the reason when it stays off; - supports PD disaggregation, transferring only the last draft window; - supports the fa4 draft backend as well as trtllm_mha. ## Modifications - **Placement.** When the draft is all sliding-window MHA and the target is a plain hybrid-SWA MHA model, the draft KV is stored on the target's SWA slots and follows the target's SWA allocation and eviction (`speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py`, `mem_cache/swa_memory_pool.py`, `configs/model_config.py`). The trtllm_mha draft backend reads it through the SWA page table (`layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`). title: [Fix] mem_cache: Hybrid SWA HiCache fixes and --hicache-swa-host-ratio
summary: ## Motivation A model with full-attention and sliding-window layers (here Muse Spark: 16 full-attention and 46 sliding-window layers, window 2048) has three problems on current main, one in the device KV pool and two in HiCache: 1. `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` cannot serve on the hybrid SWA pool. The plain-MHA branch of the KV pool builder creates an FP4 quant method, the hybrid-SWA branch does not, so both `SWAKVPool` sub-pools fall back to `UnquantizedKVCacheMethod` over a `float4_e2m1fn_x2` buffer and the first KV write fails. 2. A large `--hicache-size` fails on some ranks ("Not enough host memory available"). Ranks build their host pools concurrently and each pool's preflight re-samples free host memory, so a rank that samples after its peers have pinned theirs sees only part of its share. 3. The host SWA tier is sized by the device ratio `--swa-full-tokens-ratio`. A prefix hit needs the trailing sliding window on the device or on the host, so a small device ratio caps prefix hits on exactly the sequences the host tier keeps. ## Modifications - `_build_hybrid_swa_kv_pool` builds the KV quant method itself (signature unchanged, same page-major assertion as the plain branch) and passes it through `SWAKVPool` to both sub-pools; `post_capture_active` turns off when a quant method is present. `SWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer` also passes the layer, so a quantized sub-pool reads the scale of the global layer id rather than the one at the sub-pool-local index (callers that go through `KVLayerRouter` already passed it). title: [Fix] scheduler: Fix final chunked-prefill abort commit race
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #34149. Related prior report: #34112. An abort can arrive after final chunked prefill launches but before its result is committed. The pending result can still append the first output token, and overlap scheduling can admit the request to another decode step before applying the abort. This PR proposes discarding that uncommitted final-prefill output. Normal decode keeps its existing in-flight-token semantics. Whether final-prefill cancellation should differ from decode cancellation remains a scheduler semantics decision for review. ## Changes - Mark an aborted, in-flight final-prefill request with `Req.request_discard(req.to_finish)` only in the non-PD, non-beam path. - Reuse `_reqs_finishing_inflight()` to exclude discard-marked requests from subsequent decode when overlap enables the existing finishing-request gate. - Reuse main's prefill result discard and `RequestRetirer` cleanup paths. They drop the token and its metadata while advancing packed hidden-state/logprob offsets for following live requests. - Skip discarded rows in the extend grammar barrier, so a dropped token cannot advance grammar state. - Discard cleanup uses `checkpoint=False`: the aborted request's newly computed prefix is not added to the cache. ## Validation Synced with `main` at `703e763d5f3af75ea3587275d79155c28d3c5d4f`. Local CPU validation: ```text PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_bat

title: [Feat] moe: Integrate EvenMoE and retire native Waterfill/LPLB
summary: ## Motivation Move Waterfill, LPLB, and the other placement/routing algorithms behind [EvenMoE](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/evenmoe). SGLang selects a pipeline with `--moe-load-balancer-algorithm` and consumes its capabilities; EvenMoE owns algorithm selection and composition. SGLang retains ownership of committed placement, weight movement, dispatch, and collectives. ## Changes - Replace the native Waterfill/LPLB implementations and their algorithm-specific configuration paths with the EvenMoE integration. Existing configurations need to migrate to `--moe-load-balancer-algorithm waterfill`, `lplb`, or compositions such as `lplb+waterfill`. - Pass contiguous routed-only logical Top-K IDs and weights to EvenMoE before shared-expert layout materialization. Use the returned physical IDs without a second native remap. Preserve padding, empty batches, scaling, and expert statistics across TopK and HashTopK. - Keep native shared-expert fusion available for replica routing; do not force `disable_shared_experts_fusion=True`. When the selected pipeline itself routes the shared expert, EvenMoE appends that slot and SGLang avoids appending it twice. - Consume `supported_a2a_backends` from EvenMoE through `evenmoe.adapters.sglang` (`resolve_sglang_a2a_backend`, `a2a_backend_from_sglang`), since the tuple holds EvenMoE backend names rather than SGLang flag values. Preserve an explicit supported backend, including MegaMoE for Waterfill, and fall back to the first declared backend SGLang has for unsupported choices. title: [Bug] fused_hc_mix can hang on repeated calls from separate CUDA streams
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Repeated concurrent calls to fused_hc_mix from two CUDA streams on the same device can stop making progress. The same inputs and weights complete when called serially. In several runs, the first concurrent pair completed and a later pair stopped inside torch.cuda.synchronize() for at least 35 seconds, and up to 90 seconds in some runs; the GPU remained at 99% utilization until the process was terminated. On another run, the first concurrent pair itself did not complete. ### Expected behavior Independent invocations submitted to different CUDA streams should complete correctly without interfering with each other's synchronization state. If concurrent invocations are not supported, the restriction should be enforced explicitly (for example with a clear error or a serialization mechanism), rather than producing an indefinite GPU hang. I reproduced this using both SGLang 0.5.23 (revision 297e54fd105e974cdf401e5b4d20253a22c16f90) and source from main commit cf1ab1bd65baaa80f0a476d973f29642d24cbf50. title: [Bug] [NPU] Seeded sampling produces incorrect MurmurHash32 integers
summary: ### Describe the bug This issue takes over follow-up tracking for [PR #43825](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43825). The patch and regression test remain available there as implementation evidence; moving the work to an issue does not mean the defect is fixed. On the evaluated Ascend NPU Triton path, `murmur_hash32(seed, position, columns)` returns integers that differ from an independent unsigned-32-bit reference. These values are used by seeded sampling, so the error changes the sampling inputs for the same seed, generation position, and candidate column. No model weights or server are needed to expose the integer mismatch. **Current source check, 2026-11-17:** official main `703e763d5f3af75ea3587275d79155c28d3c5d4f` still has the same [MurmurHash implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/703e763d5f3af75ea3587275d79155c28d3c5d4f/python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/murmur_hash.py). Its Git blob is `1c3c6ce9f9eaff21617579984d7fc874e74d9048`, identical to the historical tested main. [Seeded sampling still calls it](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/703e763d5f3af75ea3587275d79155c28d3c5d4f/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L985-L1010), and the wrapper's non-CPU path launches the Triton kernel. This is a source check, not a fresh hardware run on today's main/toolchain. ### Minimal reproduction Run on an Ascend NPU with the unpatched implementation: ```python import torch import torch_npu from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.murmur_hash import murmur_hash32 torch.npu.set_device(0) seed = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.uint64, device="npu") posi

title: [Fix] [NPU] Correct MurmurHash values used by seeded sampling
summary: ## Motivation This PR restores the intended integer computation used by seeded sampling on NPU. The sampler hashes the request seed, generation position, and candidate column to produce the pseudorandom values used to select the next token. On the evaluated NPU Triton path, these hashes differ from the algorithm's unsigned 32-bit reference, changing the sampling inputs for the same seed and position. The error occurs in `rotl32`, the shared MurmurHash rotation helper. It widens the input to `uint64` before combining left and right shifts. In the observed NPU execution, the widened value contains extra high bits; the right shift moves them into the low 32 bits. The existing output mask cannot remove those bits once they have entered the result. ## Modifications In `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/murmur_hash.py`, mask the widened input before either shift so that only the intended 32 bits participate in the rotation: ```diff - x = x.to(tl.uint64) + x = x.to(tl.uint64) & 0xFFFFFFFF return ((x << r) | (x >> (32 - r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF ``` This restores the existing MurmurHash computation at the point where the incorrect values originate. The helper is shared by the Triton device path, so the change also applies to GPU callers. Add an NPU regression test comparing 16 candidate-column hashes against fixed values from an independent unsigned 32-bit reference. The inputs exercise the high-bit case that exposes the rotation error. ## Validation Existing NPU validation compared eight seed/position pairs across 16 columns, including seeds with nonzero upper 32 bits: | Implementation |

title: [Feat] [AMD] dsv4: Dispatch Mega-mHC prefill to aiter on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL` already selects single-pass Mega-mHC prefill on SM100 (DeepGEMM). On gfx950 that flag did nothing: `is_sm100` is false, and the fused HIP mHC boundary (`hc_boundary_fused`) owns the same seam. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on MI355X therefore never called aiter's Mega-mHC kernel from [ROCm/aiter#6179](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6179) (`flydsl_mega_mhc`). ## Modifications Opt-in, default off. CUDA behavior is unchanged. - `_can_use_mega_mhc` accepts gfx950 when the flag is set, `hc_mult == 4`, and `hidden == 5120`. Context-parallel prefill stays excluded. - On HIP, `_post_fusion` calls `flydsl_mega_mhc` with `out_dtype="bf16"` and packs the next `(pre, post, comb)` the same way DeepGEMM does. - With the flag set, prefill steps take Mega-mHC (`forward_hc_pre_from_prev`) and every other step takes the fused boundary, never both, so the post is not applied twice. Since #46088, `_post_fusion` takes Mega-mHC on prefill only, so decode and verify steps keep the fused boundary, with or without `--enable-amd-monokernel`. The monokernel refuses layers without `hc_boundary_fused`, so `hc_boundary_fused` stays as on main. - The AMD layers build their mHC boundaries once, on the first forward, and #46088's `extend` field stayed `False` there, so Mega-mHC never ran on gfx950. Each layer now also keeps an `extend` copy of its two boundaries and hands those to `_post_fusion` on prefill steps. title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA: a verify window crossing a 4-token group overwrites the pending index-key ring (MTP 1-3 affected)
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues and found none (closest: #45864, which is about PD retraction, not this). - [x] The bug persists in the latest release I tested (v0.5.23). ### Describe the bug With Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, QSA sparse attention, compress ratio 4) and speculative decoding (MTP / EAGLE, topk 1), the QSA indexer builds compressed index keys from **overwritten** members of the per-request pending ring whenever a target-verify (or draft-extend) window crosses a 4-token group boundary. This happens with the supported settings: `speculative_num_draft_tokens` 2-4 (MTP 1-3), not only above the cap. **Mechanism.** The pending ring holds `ratio` slots per request, addressed `req_pool_idx * ratio + position % ratio` (`build_pending_ring_slots` / `build_group_ring_slots` in `qsa/metadata.py`, and the same formula in the graph-metadata Triton kernel in `qsa/graph_metadata.py`). In one forward, `QSAIndexer.project_qk` first stores the keys of **all** tokens of the window into the ring; then `update_key_state_and_compress` compresses each group completed in the window by reading its members back from the ring. If the window starts at position `p` and `(p % ratio) + W > ratio`, the tokens after the group end are written into the slots of that group's earlier members before the group is compressed. Example, W = 2, `p % 4 == 3`: position `p` completes the group `[p-3 .. p]`, but position `p+1` was already written to slot `(p+1) % 4 == 0`, which held `p-3`. The compressed key of that group is built from `[p+1, p-2, p-1, p]`. The comme

title: [Fix] hicache: Evict pass-through Mamba host checkpoints before path tails
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #45400. On a hybrid GDN model with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, host-tier hits drop to zero once the evicted working set is a few long prefixes larger than the device pool. The KV pages are still on host, but identical requests get `cached_tokens: 0` and a full recompute. A host prefix hit ends at the deepest node on the matched path that still has a Mamba state (device or host). Host Mamba eviction (`drive_host_eviction`) is plain LRU, and a long prefill backs up many chunk checkpoints along one path. With few host Mamba slots, newer intermediate checkpoints evict the tail states of earlier documents, so their host KV is left with no usable Mamba state. `--mamba-max-states-per-path` doesn't help, because it only trims device states after they've been backed up. ## Modifications - `unified_cache/components/mamba.py` and `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/mamba.rs`: host Mamba eviction now runs in two LRU passes. The first pass evicts only pass-through checkpoints (a node with one child that holds its own Mamba state on host). A device-only child doesn't count, because it can leave the device without a host copy (`write_through_selective` before its threshold, or a backup that finds no host slot). The second pass, which runs only if the first one didn't free enough, is the existing LRU order. Path tails, forks, and states whose child has no host state are kept until no pass-through checkpoint is left, so each path keeps the state its host hit ends at. This matches what `_evict_excess_path_states` already preserves on device. - The Python and Rust co

title: [Perf] [NPU] DeepSeek-V4: remove blocking H2D copies and fuse DSPARK verify compressor-position metadata into one triton kernel
summary: ## Motivation On Ascend NPU, `Tensor.to(device[, dtype])` from pageable CPU memory (and any cross-dtype copy with `non_blocking=False`, the default) is executed by torch_npu as `aclrtSynchronizeStream` + `MemCopySync`: the host blocks until the **entire compute queue** drains, not just until the copy itself could run. The DSPARK spec-decode verify/draft metadata path had six such uploads per step (per-req seq-lens in `_build_dsv4_graph_replay_ctx` / `_refresh_graph_seq_metadata`, and gather indices in `_fill_verify_positions_cmp_padding_one` / its ragged variant): - Pure decode steps: ~2.5ms/step of host stall (queue holds the just-enqueued metadata rebuild kernels) - Mixed prefill+decode phases: the queue can hold an entire prefill chunk (hundreds of ms to seconds with long shared prefixes). Each blocking copy pins the host until the chunk completes, serializing all subsequent launches and starving the device — observed as multi-second ITL outliers After the blocking copies are gone, profiling shows the remaining bottleneck on this path is **launch-bound**: ~1759 device kernels per step (99.7% under 20us, avg 15.8us). The largest single offender is the verify compressor-position fill: the graph-replay refresh ran DSPARK through the **eager CPU reference chain** (`zero_ → arange → mask → nonzero (D2H sync count readback) → pinned index upload → gather → copy_`, ~15 host ops, twice per step for ratio 4/128) even though an equivalent fixed-shape device variant already existed upstream for EAGLE — and even the device variant was itself a chain of ~15 small aten kernels. ## Mod

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Support the EP expert mask in the small MoE sort
summary: ## Motivation Under expert parallelism, every decode step hands the MoE sort and the stage-1 MXFP8 quant back to aiter, because the small MoE sort turns itself off whenever aiter passes an expert mask, and EP always passes one. This PR lets the small sort take the mask, which lowers MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL's median decode time per token by 2.0 to 3.3 % at 4 to 32 users with 8k input (TP8/EP8, MI355X). In detail: #44004 and #42498 replace aiter's MoE sort and the separate stage-1 MXFP8 quant with one small Triton launch, but `_small_sort_supported` returns False when `expert_mask` is set. MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL at EP8 splits its 384 experts 48 per rank, so each of its 69 MoE layers pays aiter's masked sort plus a separate quant in every decode step. With this PR the sort maps global expert ids to this rank's local ids in-kernel, drops pairs routed to other ranks, and matches aiter's masked `moe_sorting` bitwise. Related PRs: this PR requires #42498 (open) and nothing else; #42498 itself applies on main. The sort kernels are from #44004 (originally #41900 by @AMD-yanfeiwang) and the fused quant from #42498 by @amd-pedghazi. ## Modifications - `moe_sorting_small.py`: - `_localize_experts` maps a global expert id to its local id, the number of this rank's experts below it, which is the numbering aiter's masked `moe_sorting` emits. Pairs routed to another rank become the kernel's sentinel and drop out of the sort. - The compact kernel (up to 64 pairs) and the bitonic kernel (33 to 256 pairs) take a `HAS_MASK` constexpr. title: [Perf] [AMD] aiter: Opt unified verify out of the host seq_lens mirror for spec-v2 overlap
summary: ## Motivation #44405 added a stream-ordered, GPU-only length resolve for spec-v2 overlap on HIP: when no attention backend needs the host `seq_lens` mirror (`needs_cpu_seq_lens=False`), the scheduler resolves lengths on the forward stream instead of waiting for the previous verify on the host. No AMD attention backend opts out today, so on MI355X with `--attention-backend aiter` that path never runs. The host still blocks every decode cycle, which caps run-ahead at low and medium concurrency. Profiling MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL with DFLASH (TP8/EP8, aiter target, triton draft) on MI355X found two blocking calls per decode cycle that remain on `main`: 1. The event wait behind the host `seq_lens` mirror, which the aiter backend always requests. 2. An implicit `.item()` in `update_sliding_window_buffer`: the eager draft's target-verify path sizes its window buffer with `torch.empty(window_kv_indptr[-1])`. That value depends on what the previous verify accepted, so the host waits for it. A third one, the host-built `num_token_non_padded` in the DFLASH draft, is already fixed on `main`. With all three removed, the profiled decode cycle becomes GPU-bound and output throughput rises up to 18.5 % at low concurrency, with no change at high concurrency. ## Modifications - `aiter_backend.py`, `environ.py`: new `SGLANG_AITER_SYNC_FREE_VERIFY` (default off). When unified verify is active (`_use_unified_verify`), it sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False`, which turns on #44405's GPU-only resolve. Unified verify already sizes from its page table and `max_context_len`, and handles a missing `seq_lens_cpu`

title: [Perf] SM90 decode regression v0.5.22 → v0.5.23: +33~45% per-step at concurrency 12 (8K–64K), and `use_deep_select_decode` costs acceptance on Hopper
summary: ### Summary On 8x H20-3e (SM90) running `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with DSPARK speculative decoding, upgrading from **v0.5.22 (`baa9befa38`)** to **v0.5.23 (`297e54fd10`)** costs **33–45% of per-step decode time at concurrency 12**, at every context length we tested (8K / 16K / 32K / 64K), while concurrency 1 is unchanged. So the fixed per-step cost is flat and the **per-request marginal cost** roughly doubled. While narrowing it we found something we did not expect and that I could not find documented: on SM90, `full_topk.py` computes `use_deep_select_decode = not use_deep_gemm_decode and is_deep_select_supported()`, and `use_deep_gemm_decode` is `is_sm100_or_newer()` — so on Hopper this is **always True** and every decode step goes through DeepSelect (`topk_page_transform`) instead of the topk-v2 `select_decode`. Forcing it to `False` (one line, same image, same patches) **recovers 21–24% throughput — but the recovery is entirely in `tokens_per_step` (acceptance), not in `step_ms`** (which moves only −3~−4%). That is the part I would like help understanding. Two questions come out of it: 1. Is DeepSelect expected to be **acceptance-neutral** on Hopper? On our box it is not: disabling it raises `tokens_per_step` from 3.59→4.22 (8K) and 3.99→4.66 (64K) with identical draft/verify config. Since SM90 index logits are fp32 (`index_logits.py`) and DeepSelect's cluster tier is precompiled for bf16, I suspect SM90 falls into a non-cluster fallback whose tie/ordering behaviour differs from topk-v2 (`#46798` reported ordering/ties issues on SM90 FullTopK — is this the same thing?) 2. title: [Refactor] [NPU] dsa: Resolve the DSA KV cache layout from a startup capability
summary: Part of #41866 (Phase 0). ## Motivation Groundwork for the INT8 KV cache for DSA models on Ascend A2 proposed in #41866. It adds no new KV dtype and no new flag. The Ascend DSA KV path picks its layout from separate `is_arch35` and `dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn` checks in the configurator, the device pool, the attention backend and the indexer. Two of them are wrong today: - **B1.** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (or `mxfp8`, or `auto` with an FP8 checkpoint) on a non-arch35 NPU builds an unpacked FP8 DSA pool with no error, while the sparse attention path still branches on the FP8 dtype and expects the arch35 packed record. - **B2.** `NPUMLATokenToKVPool.get_kv_layer_ids()` assumes one K and one V entry per layer, then the indexer entries. With the packed record the zero-width V buffers are not transferred, so the ids no longer line up with `get_contiguous_buf_infos()` (for example 10 ids for 7 buffers). ## Modifications **1. Capability.** New `hardware_backend/npu/kv_capability.py`: a frozen `msgspec.Struct` `PackedQuantKvCapability` (main KV packed or not, main KV scale dtype, indexer quantized or not, indexer dtype and scale dtype, unsupported reason), produced by a pure `resolve_kv_capability(kv_cache_dtype, is_arch35, soc_name)` and its runtime wrapper. It describes the DSA layout only; dense MLA and ModelSlim KV pools keep their own layouts. | Request | arch35 | other NPUs | |---|---|---| | `float8_e4m3fn` | packed record, FP32 tile scales, FP8 indexer + FP32 scale (today's layout) | rejected (B1) | | anything else | unpacked, indexer in the KV dtype (today's layout) |

title: Support page_first_kv_split in MLA HiCache L3 flat page I/O
summary: ## Purpose On Ascend NPU, MLA HiCache is forced onto `kernel_ascend` + `page_first_kv_split` (separate host `k_buffer` / `v_buffer` / indexer buffers). L1↔L2 transfer already works on that layout, but the generic L3 path (`file`, and any backend that goes through `_generic_page_set` / `_generic_page_get`) calls `get_data_page` / `set_from_flat_data_page`, which only handle `layer_first` / `page_first` / `page_first_direct`. Enabling `--hicache-storage-backend file` therefore crashes on the first L3 write with: ```text ValueError: Unsupported layout: page_first_kv_split ``` This PR teaches `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` how to flatten one kv_split logical page into a contiguous uint8 blob (and restore it), so generic L3 backends can round-trip NPU MLA pages without depending on Ascend MemCache zero-copy. Related but not duplicate: Ascend MemCache L3 work ([#26043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26043), [#36188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36188), [RFC #35620](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35620)) targets a different I/O path. title: [Perf] deterministic: Launch a fixed number of Triton decode blocks for large split budgets
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode, Triton decode attention gets much slower than in normal mode as the batch grows: on MI350X, gpt-oss-20b reaches 0.33x of normal-mode throughput at 64 concurrent requests and 0.21x at 256. The cause is the split budget. For batch invariance, deterministic mode fixes the decode split size at 256 tokens and sizes the budget for the longest possible request (512 splits for gpt-oss's 131k context). The kernels launch one block per split of that budget, so for a 1k-2k-token request about 99% of the blocks do no work, and the waste grows with the batch. This PR lets the grouped decode kernel run fewer blocks than splits, each block looping over the request's own splits: enough blocks to cover the GPU, and at least 32 per request and head tile. In deterministic mode the merge also stops at the request's split count instead of walking the empty tail. Every split is computed and merged in the same order as before. **Impact** - Deterministic gpt-oss-20b: 0.33x / 0.21x -> 0.63x / 0.50x of normal mode at 64 / 256 requests; gpt-oss-120b +63% / 2.1x. Any model on Triton decode attention in deterministic mode benefits, more with a longer context limit. - Normal mode is bitwise unchanged, including MLA with its core-count-sized split budget: checked against main on MI350X for MLA and GQA shapes at batch 1-64, at 0.98-1.05x main's kernel time. In deterministic mode GQA results are bitwise the same as today; on MLA shapes the merge's early stop can move them by a few ULP, and they stay batch-invariant. ## Modifications - `decode_attention.py`, `_fwd_groupe

summary: # [Perf] [AMD] GDN: optional FlyDSL packed decode On ROCm, GDN packed decode can call AITER's `flydsl_gdr_decode` instead of the Triton packed kernel. Any other value, including the default `triton`, keeps the Triton packed decode. - The hook is inside `TritonGDNKernel.packed_decode`. ReplaySSM decode stays on Triton. - Q, K, and V are strided views of the post-conv `mixed_qkv` row. Nothing is copied into separate Q/K/V tensors. - A launch the kernel does not cover logs once and falls back to Triton. The adapter also stays on Triton when `flydsl_gdr_decode` is missing or does not zero padding rows. Graph replay pads with a negative cache index, and those rows have to come back as zeros. - The two kernels are not bit-identical. Triton rounds beta to the activation dtype. title: [Perf] [AMD] muse-spark: Faster FP8 joint router/pooler GEMM for decode and verify
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X, `_joint_fp8_partial` (the FP8 joint router/pooler front in `router_pooler_topk.py`) runs once per MoE layer in every Muse Spark decode / verify step. Each call reads about 42 MB of weights from HBM (FP8 pooler `[4096, 8192]` plus the BF16 high / low router rows `[512, 8192]`), and it reached about 2 TB/s at 40 rows. At TP8 / concurrency 28 that is about 60 calls x ~21 us per verify step. ## Modifications The kernel change is confined to `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/router_pooler_topk.py`: `_joint_fp8_partial`, its `FP8_JOINT` launch table, and the launch in `joint_router_pooler_topk_fp8`. The products (FP8 x FP8 and BF16 x BF16), the FP32 accumulation and the SK = 4 split are unchanged. - **Wider pooler tiles.** 128 output columns per program, so the activation is re-staged fewer times. Above 128 rows the M tile is 256 rows, so no weight is streamed twice per call. - **Separate router tile.** The BF16 router rows get their own narrower tile (`BN_R`), plus an `R_MS` row split above 128 rows, so router programs no longer finish last. - **XCD-aware program-id remap.** Each of the 8 XCDs gets one or two K slices instead of all four, which cuts per-XCD L2 traffic for the activation. The remap is a bijection onto `(pn, pk)`, so the partials are bitwise identical to the current kernel. - **Rules over M.** Row buckets plus `_xcd_map(m)` thresholds; nothing is keyed to specific row counts. summary: ## Summary Keep existing ranks serving while joining ranks prepare for elastic EP scale-up. With decode CUDA graph reuse enabled, only joiners capture graphs; existing ranks retain theirs. title: [CI] [AMD] ci: Name AMD suites, jobs and runners as CUDA does
summary: ## Motivation CUDA suites are `{stage}-test-{runner_config}` (`base-b-test-1-gpu-small`), registered with `register_cuda_ci(stage=..., runner_config=...)`, and its stage checks are named after the suite they run. AMD's suites follow a different scheme: - Most AMD tests register with a legacy `suite=` string. - The names differ from CUDA's: `stage-a/b/c` vs `base-a/b/c`, `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` vs `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-*`. - Nothing validates AMD suite names (`run_suite.py` skips AMD), so a stale or misspelled `suite=` merges green and never runs. This PR mirrors CUDA's naming for AMD. Commits 1, 3 and 5 change names and structure only, not which tests run or on which runner; commits 2 and 4 move tests between tiers to match CUDA. title: [Perf] hicache: Add an opt-in O_DIRECT path to the fast_file backend
summary: ## Motivation `fast_file` moves KV pages between page-first host pools and page files with `readv`/`writev`, but every byte still passes through the page cache: the kernel copies it once more on each side, prefetch and backup fill the page cache with data that already lives in pinned host memory, and a completed buffered write only means the kernel accepted it. This PR adds an opt-in `o_direct` mode to the backend. At startup it checks once that direct I/O works under the storage directory, opens page files with `O_DIRECT` for every pool whose page segments are 4 KiB-aligned, and falls back to buffered I/O everywhere else: pools with unaligned segments, the staged (non zero-copy) path, kernels or filesystems that reject the flag, and any later `EINVAL`. The file format does not change, so pages written in either mode read back in the other and processes with and without the knob can share a namespace. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/fast_file/direct_io.py` (new): `probe_direct_io()` opens an unnamed file in the namespace directory with `O_TMPFILE` (a named file unlinked at once where the filesystem has no `O_TMPFILE`), turns the flag on with `fcntl(F_SETFL)`, then writes one 4 KiB page from page-aligned memory and reads it back through `preadv` into another page-aligned, pre-faulted page. A filesystem that rejects the flag or fails the write disables the mode; with `O_TMPFILE` the probe file never has a name, so nothing can be left behind even if the process dies mid-probe. title: [Fix] multimodal: bound image preprocessing GPU memory; reject decompression bombs
summary: ## Motivation Kimi GPU image preprocessing runs in the tokenizer process on GPU 0, alongside TP rank 0's static pools. - A many-image request batched every same-size image into one fp32 tensor. A 48-image request exhausted GPU 0 and returned a 500 CUDA OOM. - The tokenizer's caching allocator kept that peak reserved on GPU 0 after the request finished. - PIL's `DecompressionBombError` surfaced as a 500. ## Modifications - Each NaViT size group is processed in sub-batches of at most 512 MiB (`_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES`). - Tokenizer-side Kimi preprocessing releases the GPU cache only when reserved memory exceeds 1 GiB, so small requests skip it. Model-side deferred preprocessing does not release. - Sources above 4096x4096 are resized on the CPU with the same antialiased bicubic kernel. `max_gpu_resize_pixels` is a required keyword argument, so every caller states its cap. - On a tokenizer-side GPU OOM, Kimi-K3 serves the request through its CPU processor. - `DecompressionBombError` maps to the existing "Could not decode image" `ValueError`, which returns a 400. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_kimi_k3_gpu_preprocess.py` and `test_mm_process_config.py` pass on CPU. The 2 `midashenglm` failures in the same suite also fail on `main`. - On MI355X, `test_kimi_gpu_resize_parity.py` passes: the CPU fallback stays within 1 pixel level of the GPU resize. - 48-image requests on MI355X give the same output chunked and unchunked: | Images | Unchunked peak | Chunked peak | |---|---|---| | 48 x 3024x4032 | 10.85 GiB | 5.40 GiB | | 48 x 4000x6000 | 18.68 GiB | 5.22 GiB | - Reserved memory on GP

title: [RFC] Session-Aware KV Cache Orchestration for SGLang Router and HiCache
summary: # [RFC] Session-Aware KV Cache Orchestration for SGLang Router and HiCache ## Summary This RFC proposes a session-aware KV cache orchestrator in SGLang Router. It combines application-provided information about sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls with replica locations observed by the existing KV index to issue `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN` hints to engines. Engines use extensible execution interfaces to invoke existing HiCache and storage backend capabilities, then report actual cache changes and action outcomes. The orchestrator is organized as a sibling crate (`sgl-kv-orchestrator`) alongside `sgl-kv-indexer` under `sgl-router`. The indexer provides cache location queries; the orchestrator maintains session-to-prefix associations, collects agent and tool lifecycle statistics, produces cache control intent, and tracks outcomes. In the initial deployment, the orchestrator runs inside the Router process off the synchronous routing path, while keeping module boundaries clean for standalone deployment in the future. The proposal aligns with the [Agentic Cache Scheduling Roadmap #43098](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/43098) and the [Distributed KVCache Roadmap #21846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21846). It covers the three foundational actions, orchestrator functionality, engine execution integration, and event feedback.
