title: [Feat] benchmark: add rerank benchmark client
summary: This PR adds a standalone, closed-loop benchmark client for the cross-encoder /v1/rerank API. Unlike generation benchmarks, it sends query–document pairs and validates relevance scores rather than requesting generated tokens. ### Key features: Configurable concurrency, request count, warmup count, query length, total pair length, and documents per request. Uses SGLang’s tokenizer-loading utility to match server-side tokenization. Pair length includes the query, document, and special tokens. Validates response counts, document indices, finite scores, and server-reported input token counts. Reports successful requests/s, query–document pairs/s, input tokens/s, and mean/P50/P90/P95/P99 end-to-end latency. Excludes input preparation and warmup from measurement, supports JSON result export, and returns a nonzero exit code on request failures. The benchmark uses repeated synthetic text and measures serving performance, not ranking accuracy. Server-side prefix caching should be disabled. title: [Feat] mem_cache: Add programmable KV cache control and composable policies
summary: ## Motivation Agentic workloads need to identify useful task prefixes during tool waits, move cached state between tiers, and restore it before a continuation is admitted. This implements the initial single-owner profile of [RFC #45189: Programmable KV Cache: Composable Policies for Agentic Serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45189). Programmable control is disabled by default. Enabling it executes explicit commands; local policies require separate configuration. ## Modifications - Add versioned native priority, copy, move, task-association, task-finish and signal actions through request-attached hints, HTTP, typed scheduler IPC and Python Engine APIs. - Resolve token/content/session targets against immutable history. Track bounded replay/results, task incarnations and independent cancellation interests; bind `request_cached` only after successful request completion and cache checkpointing. - Apply copy-scoped soft priorities with independent revisions and TTLs. Explicit claims precede local-policy claims and session eviction preferences. Hits do not renew TTLs, eviction ends claims, and active request/transfer references remain protected. - Execute FULL-prefix HiCache transfers across GPU, persistent host memory and file storage. Publish readiness after DMA/backend completion, drain worker access during cancellation, and reclaim MOVE sources only after destination publication and eligibility checks. - Compose optional retention, borrowable quota and cost-aware tool-wait policies. Restored prefixes retain internal references until native prefill admission

summary: <!-- Title: [debug_utils] Dump module tensors under CUDA graph in the non-intrusive dumper --> <!-- base: sgl-project/sglang:main <- compare: ShawnZL/sglang:feat/cuda-graph-tensor-dump-v2 --> ## Motivation The non-intrusive dumper (`DUMPER_ENABLE=1 DUMPER_TARGET_MODULES=...`) registers `nn.Module` forward hooks that call `dumper.dump(...)` inline. That works in eager mode. Under CUDA graph it does not: a replay re-runs only the *recorded device kernels*, so the Python hook body never executes again. **Every module that lives inside a captured region silently stops producing frames** — nothing warns, no error is raised, the dump directory is simply missing them. A user comparing a graph-mode run against a reference sees a partial dump and no indication that it is partial. The existing escape hatch makes the gap worse rather than better: `--debug-tensor-dump-output-folder` force-disables CUDA graph (`ServingArgs`/`CudaGraphArgs` hook). So today you can dump tensors, or you can reproduce graph-mode numerics — never both. That is precisely the configuration where graph-specific numeric bugs live: capture-time address baking, padding tails that survive from the previous replay, piecewise recompilation boundaries. This PR makes the **existing** `DUMPER_*` path produce correct data with graphs enabled, for all three graph backends, without changing any model or kernel code and without adding a single server arg. ## Modifications ### Idea: split "take the value" from "write the file" * **take the value** — during capture the hook issues `buffer.copy_(tensor)`. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> The FlyDSL norm kernels use a single fixed workgroup, `_BLOCK = 640`, so the tile is `BLOCK * VEC` = 5120 and the dispatch asserts `D % 5120 == 0`. title: [Fix] [AMD] kvcache: Write V with its own head size in reshape_and_cache_flash
summary: ## Motivation `reshape_and_cache_flash` assumes K and V have the same head size: the launcher takes `head_size = key.shape[2]` and the kernel uses that size and `BLOCK_D` for the V load, the V store and the V mask. When V is narrower than K, every V write reads past the token's V row and writes past the cache slot's V row. MiMo-V2 (`MiMoV2ForCausalLM`) has K head size 192 and V head size 128, so every token reads 64 elements too many from the source and writes 64 elements past its V row into the cache. On ROCm with `--attention-backend aiter`, the hybrid SWA memory pool is on by default for MiMo-V2. In that mode the aiter backend forces `use_triton_unified_attention` and writes every layer's KV through `launch_reshape_and_cache_flash`, passing `full_to_swa_index_mapping` for the sliding-window layers. The result is garbage output from the first request, and then an illegal memory access that kills the scheduler. Reproduced on MI355X, TP8/EP8, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.23-rocm10-mi35x-20261106` (c06e39c6) with default server arguments plus `--attention-backend aiter`: ``` SHORT FAIL want='Paris' got=' the? the the the the the the the the the..0 the the the ...' SHORT FAIL want='12' got=':, , 00000000000' NEEDLE-4k FAIL got=' 1 ' ... CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered Subprocess scheduler_0 crashed with exit code -6. ``` The same failure occurs with CUDA graphs off. The full-to-SWA slot translation itself is correct: a bounds hook on the launcher saw every translated slot inside the SWA pool and matching `SWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa`.

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Raise the small MoE sort's pair limit from 256 to 1024
summary: ## Motivation The small MoE sort (#36559, #44004, #42498) is limited to 256 (token, expert) pairs, so it turns off at 32 decode tokens with top 8. Speculative decoding reaches that limit quickly. A DFLASH verify step has 8 tokens per request, so at top 8 it covers only 4 requests (256 pairs); 8 requests need 512 pairs and 16 requests 1024. Past the limit every MoE layer goes back to aiter's two-kernel sort followed by a separate stage-1 quant launch. The 256 limit was set in #36559 without a stated reason, and #41900/#44004 benchmarked only up to 256 pairs. Measured above it, the sort is still faster than aiter's sort plus quant at every point up to 1024 pairs, and slower from 1536 on (tables below). This PR raises the limit to 1024. On one MI355X, the MoE layer gets 2 to 5 % faster between 257 and about 900 pairs, and is unchanged at and above 1024. In serving MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL with DFLASH, throughput rises 1.3 % with 8 concurrent requests and is unchanged with 16 (same-node A/B below). Why the crossover sits there: the sort (the bitonic kernel from #44004, with #42498's fused quant) runs in one CTA over `next_pow2(pairs)` lanes, so its time steps up at each power of two: 5.3 us up to 256 pairs, 7.3 to 7.6 us up to 512, and 10 us up to 1024. At 1536 pairs it pads to 2048 lanes and takes 18 us. aiter's sort plus quant grows only from 9.5 to 11.7 us between 256 and 1024 pairs (masked, block 32). title: [Fix] lora: Reject partial TP adapter loads and preserve cleanup IDs
summary: ## Motivation **An adapter can be acknowledged as loaded even though a TP worker never installed it.** If the I/O rank succeeds and a non-I/O rank fails, the frontend registers the adapter and permits new requests to select an incomplete installation. If the I/O rank is the one that fails, the frontend can instead lose the ID needed to clean up the adapter left on a successful peer. This affects dynamic adapter refreshes and multi-adapter serving under tensor parallelism. Merging frontend replies does not catch the failure: non-I/O TP ranks do not send those replies. ## Before/after evidence Matching **two-process CPU Gloo runs of the actual scheduler handlers** demonstrate the hidden load/unload outcomes below. The registered CPU regressions also exercise the actual tokenizer control methods and registry, including explicit cleanup and unload retry. Worker loading and GPU execution are replaced by controlled boundary outcomes. | Fault injected | Upstream | This PR | |---|---|---| | Rank 1 fails to load; rank 0 installs the adapter | **I/O reply succeeds**; the frontend registers an adapter missing on rank 1 | **Load fails**; no frontend registration; the new ID is retained for cleanup | | Rank 0 fails to load; rank 1 installs the adapter | Failure reply has an **empty resident-adapter snapshot**; the frontend loses the new cleanup ID | Failure reply exposes the peer's resident adapter; the frontend retains the ID and explicit unload cleans it up | | Rank 1 fails to unload after rank 0 removes its copy | **I/O reply succeeds**, hiding the adapter still resident on rank 1 |

title: [Fix] hicache: Fail storage attach when the native hash extension cannot build
summary: ## Motivation HiCache L3 lookups hash with the JIT-built `hicache_hash_cpp` extension, which needs OpenSSL headers. Where it cannot build, the server starts normally, every storage query fails per request (`HiCache storage query failed`), and backups keep writing pages that are never read. Seen on a DGX Spark (GB10) arm64 image: 0 L3 hits, ~2.6 GB written. Images have been patched one at a time so far (#31064, #34767, #38796). ## Modifications - `attach_storage_backend` builds/loads the native hash before any backend exists, so a missing toolchain fails at startup instead of silently. - The load error names the missing package (`libssl-dev`). ## Tests On DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, `--hicache-storage-backend file`: - New case in `test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py` fails on main (`RuntimeError not raised`); the whole file passes with the fix (6/6). - Image without libssl-dev: the server now exits at startup with the new message and writes no L3 pages (before: it started, with 0 L3 hits). - With libssl-dev: starts normally; after `/flush_cache`, a repeated 8.7k-token prompt is served from L3 (`storage: 8640`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Feat] [NPU] graph: Compile decode graphs with npugraph_ex and optional static kernels
summary: ## Motivation **npugraph_ex** is the graph-mode compilation backend of torch_npu: it exposes a `torch.compile` backend for the NPU through `torch._dynamo`. Compared with TorchAir, it can compile static-shape kernels for the decode buckets SGLang actually captures, moving runtime tiling and kernel selection to startup. [#13410](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13410) already brought `torch.compile` to the NPU: the model forward is compiled by TorchAir, the device graph is captured and replayed by SGLang's ACLGraph, and GSM8K accuracy plus throughput regression tests were added. Its Advanced Features list mentions static shape kernel compilation, but there is no switch for it on the SGLang side. Today `get_compiler_backend("npugraph_ex")` carries that name but still returns the TorchAir backend: ```python compiler_config = CompilerConfig() # torchair's compiler_config.mode = "max-autotune" if mode == "npugraph_ex": compiler_config.mode = "reduce-overhead" compiler_config.debug.run_eagerly = True npu_backend = torchair.get_npu_backend(compiler_config=compiler_config) ``` That path does not work on current main and has no test coverage. Three concrete problems: **1. Full-graph tracing fails.** `fullgraph=True` raises while tracing the construction of the `msgspec.Struct` state objects (`Contribution`, `ExitDecision`): ``` TypeError: object.__new__(Contribution) is not safe, use Contribution.__new__() ``` **2. Decode graph capture cannot finish.** The capture context sets `skip_guard_eval_unsafe`. Under that stance Dynamo skips guard evaluation and refuses to recompile

title: [Perf] KDA ReplaySSM: commit a one-token verify in place
summary: ## Motivation With `--speculative-adaptive` and `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, high batch sizes run at `steps=0`: the verify carries one token per request, and that token is always accepted. On the KDA ReplaySSM path that verify still writes the ring and leaves `temporal` untouched, then the commit folds the ring back into `temporal`. Each step reads the fp32 SSM state in the verify, then reads and writes it again in the fold. A plain decode reads and writes it once. On GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 (TP4, B300), this made a `steps=0` step 7–16% slower than a decode step without speculative decoding at the same batch size. It removed most of the reason to fall back to `steps=0` at high load. ## Modifications - `TritonKDAKernel.target_verify(inplace_single_step=True)` runs a one-token verify as a decode step: it updates `temporal` in place and writes no ring. - `commit_kda_replayssm_after_verify(ssm_committed_in_verify=True)` skips the fold. It still snapshots the extra_buffer track slot (new `_snapshot_step0_track` kernel) and still runs the conv rollback. - `kda_replayssm_verify_commits_in_place()` is the one predicate both sides read. It is true for a one-token verify from an EAGLE-family worker only. Other workers commit through `update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify`, which always folds, so they keep the ring path. - The track snapshot copies slot to slot inside `temporal`. It does not reuse `fused_mamba_state_scatter_with_mask`, because that kernel requires a contiguous source and `temporal` can be a strided arena view. ## Accuracy Tests New GPU test `test_one_token_inplace_veri

title: [Fix] [MUSA] kvcache: reuse public Triton store path
summary: ## Summary Route the MUSA KV-cache store through SGLang's existing public Triton cache-copy kernel. This removes the need for model-wide `torch.no_grad()` during graph capture without introducing a new kernel or a MUSA-specific source bundle. ## Root Cause CUDA, ROCm, XPU, and CPU use fused cache-store paths that do not expose their in-place cache updates to PyTorch autograd. title: [Feat] speculative: Build adaptive spec states within an opt-in memory budget
summary: ## Motivation Roadmap #23705, Reliability: "Memory-aware state management / lazy init" (the memory-aware half; lazy init is left for a follow-up, see below). With `--speculative-adaptive`, `AdaptiveController.init_states()` builds a runtime state (CUDA graphs and attention backends) for every candidate step at startup. On a tight `--mem-fraction-static` the optional states can OOM the server at startup even though the policy may never switch to them. ## Modifications - New opt-in flag `--speculative-adaptive-memory-budget-gb`. Unset keeps today's behavior. - States the policy can activate without feedback are always built and not charged to the budget: the initial step and every BS slot's start step (`AdaptiveSpeculativeParams.start_steps`). The first batch routed to a slot activates its start step through `activate_step_by_batch`, so these cannot be skipped. - The other candidates are built in priority order (`prebuild_order()`: nearest hop from a slot's start step first) while the spent cost is below the budget. The cost of a state is only known after capture, so the total may exceed the budget by one state. There is no cost estimator: the cost of a state depends on the step count, on the batch sizes captured for it (`cuda_graph_bs_for_step` captures a step's graphs only for the batch sizes whose slot can reach it) and on the attention backend, so no ordering between steps is assumed; the log reports each built state's measured cost. - Candidates that were not built are removed from every slot for this launch (`restrict_candidates()`); the policy never selects them and `_

title: [Perf] scheduler: Reserve a chunked request's unfinished tail under shortest-prefill-first
summary: ## Motivation With `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first`, short requests run beside a long request that is prefilled in chunks. `PrefillAdder` charges the memory budget only for the chunk being run, so requests admitted beside it can take the KV that the chunk's uncomputed tail still needs. Since #44823 the continuation then parks instead of overcommitting the pool (before, `Prefill out of memory`), and can stall for whole passes. The admission paths already pass the unfinished part of the request to `memory_budget.reserve()` (`unfinished_input_len`, `deferred_max_new_tokens`), but only `ChainPrefillBudget` charges it; `PrefillBudget` and `SWAPrefillBudget` drop it. #47308 bounds SPF's compute budget, not KV, so the two compose. ## Modifications - `PrefillBudget.reserve_unfinished_tail`: when set, `reserve()` adds the page-ceiled unfinished tail plus the deferred decode headroom to `total_offset` only (later passes allocate it, so `current_offset` is unchanged). `SWAPrefillBudget.reserve` forwards the tail arguments; the tail is charged to the full-attention budget only; the SWA partition is not reserved for it (a sliding window needs at most its window of the tail). - `PrefillAdder(reserve_chunked_tail=...)` sets it. The scheduler computes it once at init: shortest-prefill-first and `SGLANG_SPF_RESERVE_CHUNKED_TAIL=1`. - **Default off.** In the serving A/B below it removes parked continuations but does not improve TTFT beyond noise, and p50 TTFT is worse in two of four cells. - A later candidate that would break the reservation gets `NO_TOKEN` with its prefix pinned,

title: [Feat] kimi-k31: Support PCP KV sharding with HiCache and DFlash
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1 PCP currently replicates persistent DSA KV across ranks. Store each logical KV page and packed index page on its owner rank, then assemble the working prefix for TRTLLM DSA attention. This extends the existing page-sharded KV infrastructure to Kimi's hybrid attention, HiCache L2 and DFlash paths. This PR targets `kimi-k3.1-day-0`, the branch of #48414. ## Modifications - Add `--kv-cache-sharding-scratch-size` (GiB per GPU, default 10) to bound the two prefix-assembly buffers. title: [Perf] mem_cache: Let the per-path Mamba state cap count host copies
summary: ## Motivation The per-path Mamba state cap counts only device copies. With HiCache, each capped state keeps its host copy, so the host Mamba pool fills with superseded states of paths that are still live; host eviction then drops host KV to make room and the prefix hit rate falls. Under pipeline parallelism each stage has its own host Mamba pool and hits the same problem. Since #49886, `--hybrid-cache-checkpoints-level 2` (one state per path) is the default, so this applies to every hybrid model with HiCache by default. ## Modifications - Host copies count toward the per-path cap, and a capped state also loses its host copy, unless that copy is host-locked or has a backup or load-back in flight. The tail, forks, device-locked nodes and device leaves are kept as before. - Implemented in both tree cores (Python `components/mamba.py`, Rust `components/mamba.rs`); the Rust binding gains `set_mamba_path_cap_counts_host`. - `UnifiedRadixCache` enables it at HiCache init only when there is a per-path cap and a host tier in cache mode (not `buffer_only`). On by default; `SGLANG_MAMBA_PATH_CAP_COUNTS_HOST=0` restores device-only counting, identical to main. - #47339 (open) addresses host Mamba pressure through host eviction order; it touches different functions and composes with this. ## Accuracy Tests Only which cached states stay on host changes; a state that loses its host copy is recomputed on next use, like any miss. Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN hybrid), 1 GPU, Rust tree core, HiCache `write_through`, a small host pool (97 Mamba states), `--mamba-max-states-per-path 1`, temperature 0, seq

title: [Feat] scheduler: Balance decode requests across pipeline microbatches
summary: ## Motivation Requests in a pipeline microbatch can have very different output lengths. As short requests finish, one slot can still have many active requests while other slots have little or no work. ## Modifications Add an opt-in `--enable-pp-auto-balance` flag for colocated autoregressive PP inference. After a slot processes its output, it can donate rows to less populated slots. Each destination consumes its incoming rows when it retires its previous forward. The scheduler preserves request and KV pool indices, sampling history, and the per-microbatch size cap. Outstanding prefills reserve capacity on their destination. Pending transfers participate in abort, pause/retract, idle, and ownership checks. The default remains off. ## Accuracy Tests CPU tests cover all 1,296 four-slot populations with sizes from zero through five, preserve row ownership and accumulated frequency penalties, and exercise PP output ordering and chunked prefill scheduling. ```bash python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/{test_pp_auto_balance,test_pp_war_barrier,test_pp_output_exchange_order,test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate}.py ``` 12 passed, 2 skipped, 11 subtests passed on macOS. title: [Fix] scheduler: Wait for the launched forward before writing weights
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50716. After `pause_generation(mode="in_place")`, the step launched before the pause can still be running on `forward_stream` when a weight update writes parameters on `schedule_stream`. Nothing orders the write after that step's model layers: the WAR barrier after a launch waits only for the step's shared-read event when it published one, and that event marks the end of the input reads, before the layers. The in-flight step can then compute with the new weights, and its token, logprob and KV are kept without an error. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: new `wait_for_launched_forward()`, which makes `schedule_stream` wait for `forward_stream` under the overlap scheduler or pipeline parallelism. title: [Feat] platforms: Let OOT platforms provide breakable graph backends (3/3)
summary: ## Motivation SGLang lets users choose a graph backend independently for decode and prefill. Both phases can select `breakable`, where one model forward is captured as multiple device-graph segments separated by operations that run eagerly. Today, selecting `breakable` always constructs SGLang's built-in `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`. An out-of-tree platform can provide a full decode graph backend, but it has no equivalent way to provide its own breakable graph implementation. The platform must patch SGLang or inherit CUDA-specific code, even when it already supports segmented graph capture on its device. This is the final PR in a three-part series: 1. [PR 1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49402) introduced the device-neutral `BaseGraphBackend` and `BaseBreakableGraphBackend` contracts. 2. [PR 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49457) decouples `eager_on_graph` from private CUDA/XPU capture state through a device-neutral recorder contract. 3. This PR adds the platform hook and resolver routing that allow an OOT platform to supply a breakable backend for decode, prefill, or both. Together, the three changes separate responsibilities cleanly: core SGLang owns graph policy and runner behavior, while the platform owns device-specific graph capture and replay. ## Behavior changes Built-in platform behavior does not change. The new hook returns `None` by default, which keeps the existing `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` path. An OOT platform may now return a `BaseBreakableGraphBackend` subclass for either phase. title: [Perf] disagg: Send each PP prefill stage's last KV chunk when its forward ends
summary: **Draft: waits for a PP4/PP8 A/B (≥3 runs per arm) on main before review.** ## Motivation With PD disaggregation and a PP prefill server, a stage sends a request's last KV chunk only when it processes that request's result. Results travel the PP output ring, so the result reaches a stage `pp_size - 1` micro-batches after the stage's own forward. The stage's KV (and Mamba/DSA state) is already final when that forward ends. Until the ring catches up, every stage keeps the request's KV locked, and the decode hand-off waits for the ring as well. ## Modifications The new env flag `SGLANG_PP_PD_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND` is off by default. It applies to `event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill` with the Mooncake backend and PP > 1. - **Non-last stages.** Right after launching a micro-batch, the stage hands the last chunk of every request that finishes in it to the transfer worker. The forward's launch event rides on the sender (`_early_send_wait_event`), and the worker waits on it before reading. These stages send without aux: `send(..., send_aux=False)` leaves the aux index out, and the Mooncake worker skips `send_aux` for that chunk. The wire format does not change. - **Last stage.** This stage samples the first token. It copies the sampled tokens to the host (`async_d2h` plus an event) and sends the last chunk with aux once the copy has landed. It polls after each launch and forces any pending sends before it processes a result. title: [Fix] pd: Agree on PP prefill release and abort-vs-error outcome via PP0 decision
summary: ## Motivation With a pipeline-parallel prefill server in PD disaggregation, every PP stage must release an inflight request at the same step and in the same way. Main does this with a ring consensus over the PP group (#47045 made the concluded outcome agree across stages). #45085 (WIP, @stepinto) replaces the ring with a simpler scheme: PP0 reads every stage's transfer status through `PPConsensusStore` and forwards its decision. One gap remains in both versions: the *classification* of a failed transfer is still decided locally. When a request is aborted (client `AbortReq` or a decode-side abort), only the rank that saw the abort records an abort reason. A stage that finished its own transfer has no failure reason, so it concludes the same request as a transfer error and returns a 500 for a request the client aborted, while other stages finish it as an abort. This PR builds on #45085 (its commit is included with authorship preserved; happy to rebase onto it if it lands first) and adds an agreed abort-vs-error classification. ## Modifications - Commit 1 (from #45085, rebased onto current main): PP0 polls every stage's status via `PPConsensusStore` and forwards the decision, replacing the ring consensus for releasing inflight requests. A transfer that failed on any stage stays Failed (min over stages), which keeps the behavior of #47045. title: [Feat] hicache: Scale the host Mamba-state pool independently of the KV host pool
summary: ## Motivation The host Mamba-state pool is sized like the KV host pool: `hicache_ratio × device Mamba pool`, or the device-size share of `--hicache-size`. How many host states a hybrid model needs depends on how they are retained, not on the KV ratio: - **Without a per-path state cap**, the small state pool thrashes first. On Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 (GB300, PD, AgentX trace), scaling it 1.0 → 1.25 raised the L2 host hit rate from 89.5% to 91.9% (#39856). - **When the per-path cap also counts host copies**, superseded states are freed from host. The state pool then needs less than its share, and the KV host pool, which carries the prefix hit rate, needs more. On Kimi-K3.1-Pro FP4 (VR200, 2×PP8 prefill, `--hicache-size`), scaling 0.80 → 0.65 gave +2.2% output tok/s/GPU at −1.1% tok/s/user, one run per arm. Same-config replicates differ by about 1.2%, so the Pareto effect is near noise; the value here is a knob that can move bytes in either direction. So one knob is needed that works in both directions and on both sizing paths. ## Modifications - `SGLANG_HICACHE_MAMBA_HOST_RATIO_SCALE` (default 1.0, a no-op). summary: ## Motivation With DP (`--dp-size`) or DP attention (`--attn-dp-size`), each DP rank has its own radix cache, so a request only hits the cache if it lands on the rank that already served its prefix. title: [Fix] kda: Align unfused safe-gate diagonal normalization anchor
summary: ## Motivation KDA's safe-gate diagonal kernels use different normalization anchors: the fused path uses the first token of each 16-token subchunk, while the unfused path uses its midpoint. The anchor cancels algebraically, but changes finite-precision rounding. The grid-size heuristic can therefore change a sequence's output when other sequences join its prefill batch. KDA selects fused diagonal/recompute kernels only when `B * NT * H <= 256`; larger grids use the unfused path to avoid register-pressure spills. For packed variable-length prefill, `B=1` and `NT=sum(ceil(sequence_length / 64))`, so the trigger depends on total prefill chunks and heads, not request count alone. In our captured Ming ASR case (`H=16`), individual requests used 2-3 chunks (grid 32-48, fused); packing eight requests produced 21 chunks (grid 336, unfused). Concurrent requests can therefore cross this threshold when grouped into a larger prefill batch. Async decode changes scheduling and can change that grouping; the same switch also occurs on the synchronous baseline. This surfaced while investigating Ming-3.0-ASR-tiny transcription differences in [sglang-omni#3564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/3564). With identical first-layer inputs and zero initial states, switching only diagonal fusion reproduced the output discrepancy; switching only recompute fusion did not. ## Modifications Use the subchunk-start gate in both gather and direct-load variants of the unfused safe-gate diagonal kernel, matching the existing fused path. Keep the fusion heuristic and batched prefill enabled. Thi

title: [Perf] tokenizer_manager: Poll client disconnects once per wait timeout, not per streamed chunk
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation Fixes #50722. #46586 (c81230bffe) made `TokenizerManager._stream_one_response` call `await request.is_disconnected()` before **every streamed chunk**; before it, only non-streaming outputs ran that check. Since then, high-concurrency streaming throughput has dropped 10-25% across models and platforms. On gpt-oss-120b TP4 / GB200 at 8k-in/1k-out, concurrency 256, the drop is -22% at c81230bffe and -23% on today's `main`. Bisecting nightly CI landed on c81230bffe. This PR removes the cost while keeping the abort-on-disconnect behaviour #46586 added. ### Root cause: what one `is_disconnected()` call costs `Request.is_disconnected()` does not just read a flag. Starlette implements it as a `receive()` inside an already-cancelled anyio `CancelScope`: ```python with anyio.CancelScope() as cs: cs.cancel() message = await self._receive() ``` Under uvicorn that `receive()` waits on `message_event`. Each call therefore: 1. Suspends the stream's task. 2. Waits one full event-loop pass for anyio's `call_soon` to deliver `Task.cancel()`. 3. Unwinds a `CancelledError` through `receive -> is_disconnected -> CancelScope.__exit__`. The default `stream_interval` is 1, so this runs once per token per stream. It all lands on the single TokenizerManager event loop, which also serves HTTP, tokenizes 8k-token prompts and fans out outputs. In a FastAPI/uvicorn microbenchmark (256 SSE streams fed by one shared decode-step ticker, server pinned to one GB200 Grace core): - Server CPU per chunk rises from 14 to 42 us. - The highest sustainable chunk rate drops from ~68k/s

title: [Feat] scheduler: UniBoost decode time-slicing for first-token-starved waiters
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #48078. Under KV-memory pressure, the queue-wait tail is set by memory rather than by queue order. In 12 earlier GLM-5.3 runs of the workload below (6 scheduling configurations x 2, same seed), per-rank queues were shallow: only 9-18% of batch logs had two or more waiting requests. Requests that hit the host cache at admission (their prefix had been evicted from device) were 28-33% of all requests but accounted for 76-83% of total queue-wait seconds. They sat at the head of the queue, waiting for enough free device KV to load the prefix back. Meanwhile the device KV was held by long-running decodes that nothing can interrupt: the 10% of requests with the longest outputs held 55-58% of the decode phase's KV x time. No ordering policy can move that tail. This PR adds decode time-slicing on top of the UniBoost order: when a first-token waiter has starved for `wait_s` and does not fit, the scheduler releases the longest-running decodes into the radix cache, admits the waiter first, and lets the released decodes resume from their cached KV. This mechanism is ours, not the paper's. **UniBoost series** (each PR builds on the previous one; review in order): 1. #48076: the policy (`--schedule-policy uniboost`) 2. #48077: adaptive gamma from the response-time tail 3. #48078: bounded waits for requests that share a prefix 4. #48079: decode time-slicing for first-token-starved waiters All four target `main`, so #48077 to #48079 also carry the commits of the PRs before them; each PR's own change is its last commit. ## Modifications - `managers/decode_preemptio

title: [Feat] scheduler: Bound UniBoost waits of requests that share a prefix
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #48077. Agentic traffic sends many requests that share a long prefix: turns of one session, or sessions forked from one system prompt. Two interactions with prefix sharing break UniBoost's wait bound, and this PR fixes both. 1. **Dedup followers have no bound.** In-batch prefix dedup marks a waiting request whose prefix another queued request will insert (its *leader*) as a follower, and the cache-aware policies sort followers last. A follower behind the whole queue also sits behind every later arrival, so its wait is unbounded under sustained load. 2. **Admitting just before a sibling's commit recomputes it.** When an earlier extender (the in-flight chunked prefill, or a waiting request that sorts first) is about to commit tokens past a request's matched prefix, admitting that request in the same pass prefills those tokens uncached, and the sibling's commit lands a moment later. On agentic contexts of 100k tokens or more, that duplicates the prefill of the whole shared span. **UniBoost series** (each PR builds on the previous one; review in order): 1. #48076: the policy (`--schedule-policy uniboost`) 2. #48077: adaptive gamma from the response-time tail 3. #48078: bounded waits for requests that share a prefix 4. #48079: decode time-slicing for first-token-starved waiters All four target `main`, so #48077 to #48079 also carry the commits of the PRs before them; each PR's own change is its last commit. ## Modifications - **Leader-relative followers**: `_compute_prefix_matches` can report each follower's leader. title: [Feat] scheduler: Adapt the UniBoost gamma online from the response-time tail
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #48076 (the UniBoost policy). The right `gamma` depends on the load: it sets how far a short request may jump a long one, and a fixed value is either too timid at low load or starves large requests under overload. The paper's gamma-Ada estimator (Eq. 9) tracks it online from the response-time tail: `gamma_hat = ln(5) / (t99 - t95)`. This PR adds it as `--uniboost-adaptive-gamma`. **UniBoost series** (each PR builds on the previous one; review in order): 1. #48076: the policy (`--schedule-policy uniboost`) 2. #48077: adaptive gamma from the response-time tail 3. #48078: bounded waits for requests that share a prefix 4. #48079: decode time-slicing for first-token-starved waiters All four target `main`, so #48077 to #48079 also carry the commits of the PRs before them; each PR's own change is its last commit. ## Modifications - `managers/uniboost.py`: `AdaptiveGamma`. It fits `gamma_hat = ln(5) / (t99 - t95)` over the response times (scheduler receive to completion, wall seconds) of the last 128 completed requests, starting after 32. Each fit is folded into an EMA with weight 0.2 and clipped to [1e-3, 15] 1/s. Two additions to the paper's estimator: - **Max-jump floor** (`--uniboost-adaptive-max-jump-s`, default 60): `gamma` is floored so that the largest boost, `b_gamma(k / rate)`, stays within J wall seconds; the floor is the root of a monotone function, found by bisection. That bounds how long a newcomer can delay a waiting request regardless of the service rate. A raw `gamma` floor would give a bound that scales with the rate. - **Size-aware fit*

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add the UniBoost schedule policy
summary: ## Motivation UniBoost (*Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026, [project page](https://yl3469.github.io/uniboost-icml26/#cite), [arXiv:2606.18431](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18431)) is a prediction-free, tail-aware schedule policy. A waiting request `r` is served in ascending ``` phi(r) = A(r) - b_gamma(q(u(r))) b_gamma(w) = -ln(1 - exp(-gamma * w)) / gamma ``` where `A(r)` is its arrival stamp, `u(r)` its uncached prefill work and `q()` a geometric quantization at bin size `k`. Small work gets a large boost and large work almost none, and no boost exceeds `b_gamma(k)`. So a newcomer can only overtake requests that arrived less than `b_gamma(k)` earlier: large `gamma` converges to FCFS, small `gamma` to shortest-uncached-work-first, and every request's wait has a bound. The existing policies sit at the two ends. `fcfs` bounds waits but ignores work; `lpm` and `shortest-prefill-first` favor cheap requests with no starvation bound; `hrrn` ages by waited tokens. UniBoost interpolates between them with one knob and an explicit bound. This PR adds the policy as `--schedule-policy uniboost` with a fixed `gamma`. The follow-ups below add the paper's adaptive gamma and two serving-side extensions. summary: ## Motivation This PR implements **sub-feature 1, "Platform hooks"** — step 1 of the delivery plan in #49799. summary: Fixes #47205 ## Problem When `split_special_tokens=True`, `tokenizer.encode()` splits a special-added marker like `<|end|>` into ordinary ids (`[27, 91, 419, 91, 29]`) instead of returning the native id (`200007`). title: [Perf] dsv41: Share Engram tables across servers with replication group_shards
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables are ~189 GiB for V4.1-Flash, and every server keeps its own full copy, split only across its own TP group. Disaggregated deployments run many small prefill servers (for example DEP2), so the copies add up quickly: - With `{"placement": "cpu"}`, a GB300 node running two DEP2 prefill servers pins ~378 GiB of host DRAM for the same immutable tables. That caps the HiCache host pool at ~1.2x the device pool, and it is full at every mid-curve point we measured. - With `{"placement": "gpu"}`, a TP2 server holds 94 GiB of table per GPU, which does not fit next to the KV pool. - `replication: per_node` shares one copy only inside one server's TP group, so it frees nothing here. This PR adds a way for many servers to share one table, following vLLM #62091, which splits the prefill Engram table over all prefill GPUs as one peer group. ## Design A new `--engram-config` value, `replication: group_shards`. The default placement is unchanged. ```bash # group_size: GPUs across all servers in the group # group_store: a directory visible to all of them, empty per deployment sglang serve ... --engram-config '{"placement": "cpu", "replication": "group_shards", "group_size": 28, "group_store": "/shared/engram-run1"}' ``` - Each table is split by rows over the `group_size` GPUs of every server in the group. The group can span nodes in one NVLink domain. - `placement` picks where each GPU's slice lives: - `gpu`: in its HBM (as in vLLM #62091). - `cpu`: in host-NUMA cuMem on that GPU's own socket. This costs no HBM, and the table is spread over every socke

title: [Apple Silicon][MPS] Cap memory reporting to Metal's recommended working set
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #21443. On Apple Silicon the GPU shares unified memory with the CPU, but Metal can only keep [`recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtldevice/2369280-recommendedmaxworkingsetsize) resident on the GPU (roughly 65-75% of RAM; 17.76 GiB on the 24 GB machine used below). The MPS code paths reported plain `psutil.virtual_memory()` numbers, so memory planning could size budgets against RAM the GPU subsystem can never safely use. Overcommitting the working set causes GPU paging and driver instability, and in the worst case the IOGPUFamily kernel panic and machine reboot discussed in #21443 and diagnosed in #29439. The MLX serving backend already caps its own pool sizing to the working set and calls `mx.set_wired_limit()` (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py`), so this PR closes the remaining torch-MPS reporting paths named in the issue. ## Modifications **Unified Apple Silicon memory abstraction** (suggested by @yeahdongcn): the new `python/sglang/_apple_silicon_memory.py` module is the single dispatch point for Apple Silicon GPU memory queries. `use_mlx()` routes working-set / allocated / available / total-memory queries to MLX APIs (`mx.device_info()`, `mx.get_active_memory() + mx.get_cache_memory()`, `mx.clear_cache()`); otherwise they are answered by torch-MPS (`torch.mps.recommended_max_memory()`, `driver_allocated_memory()`, `empty_cache()`). title: [Fix] sampler: Use non-zero temperature in warmup requests to trigger flashinfer JIT compilation
summary: ## Motivation Warmup requests are supposed to fully heat-start the serving path so that the first real request does not pay compilation or lazy-initialization costs. However, the warmup request in `_execute_server_warmup` sets `temperature=0`, which causes a chain of effects that prevent flashinfer'''s sampling kernels from being JIT-compiled during warmup: 1. `SamplingParams.__post_init__` converts `temperature=0` to `top_k=1` (greedy sampling): `if 0 <= self.temperature < _SAMPLING_EPS: self.temperature = 1.0; self.top_k = 1` 2. `SamplingBatchInfo.from_schedule_batch` computes `is_all_greedy = all(k <= 1 for k in top_ks)`, which is `True` when every row has `top_k=1`. 3. `Sampler.forward` checks `if sampling_info.is_all_greedy:` and takes the `sampler_argmax(logits)` fast path, completely bypassing the `else` branch where flashinfer'''s `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs` and `min_p_sampling_from_probs` are called. Both flashinfer sampling functions are `LazyImport` — they are only imported and JIT-compiled on first invocation. Since warmup never invokes them, the JIT compilation is deferred to the first real request that uses non-greedy sampling (e.g. `temperature > 0`), causing a latency spike on that request. This affects all NVIDIA GPU deployments using the flashinfer sampling backend (the default), since every server warmup runs through this code path. ## Modifications - Change the warmup request `temperature` from `0` to `0.1` in `_execute_server_warmup` (`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`). title: [Perf] quantization: Fuse FP8 row-padding zero fills into group quantization
summary: ## Motivation For a row count that needs padding, `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8_row_padded` launches quantization followed by separate FP8 and scale zero-fill kernels. These launches repeat in small-batch block-FP8 inference. Folding the tail stores into quantization removes two launches while preserving the padded GEMM shapes and quantized values. ## Modifications - Extend the existing flat quant kernel so the last real row also initializes its groups in the padded rows. Quantization arithmetic and GEMM dispatch are unchanged. - Accept caller-provided padded FP8 outputs with column-major FP32 scales, validating dimensions, strides, vector alignment and overflow. title: [Perf] rust-server: Avoid raw state materialization for default /server_info
summary: Addresses item 8 of #49055. ## Motivation #48818 let an embedding package register scheduler `internal_state` fields for `/server_info`. To support that, `CoreHandle::internal_states()` changed from decoding each DP rank's reply directly into the typed `InternalState` to decoding it into an `rmpv::Value` tree and converting it with `InternalState::from_scheduler`. The scheduler's `internal_state` carries its full launch configuration, about 550 `ServerArgs` fields, next to the runtime metrics. With the dynamic decode, every one of those fields is materialized as an `rmpv::Value` and then dropped, even when `server_info_state_keys` is empty, which is the default. That is avoidable CPU work on every `/server_info` call, per DP rank. #49055 measured it at 8.82 -> 30.62 µs per rank. ## Modifications All changes are in `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/handlers/info.rs`. - **No registered keys** (default): `internal_states()` decodes each rank's reply with `Replies::decode::<InternalStateEnvelope>`, whose `internal_state` field is the typed `InternalState`. Unknown fields are skipped by serde instead of being built. - **Registered keys**: the existing `Replies::decode_with` + `InternalState::from_scheduler` path is unchanged. title: [Feat] qwen4-exp: Support GR and PLE sequence parallelism
summary: ## Summary This PR extends the existing LayerNorm sequence-parallel path to Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. During prefill, Gated Residual (GR/HC) and PLE activations are sharded along the token dimension across the tensor-parallel group. GDN, QSA/attention, and TP-MoE keep their existing full-token computation semantics through an output-aware fallback: ```text all-gather token rows -> full-row computation -> TP-partial output: reduce-scatter with SUM complete output: local token-row shard ``` The output contract is explicit at each call site. GDN and attention return TP-partial outputs and therefore use SUM reduce-scatter. MoE selects between SUM reduce-scatter and local sharding through SGLang's existing `post_experts_output_is_complete()` semantics, preventing already-combined FlashInfer/PPLX/MegaMoE outputs from being summed twice. The feature reuses the existing `--enable-layernorm-sp` option. It does not introduce a Qwen4Exp-specific environment variable, and the default path remains unchanged when the flag is not enabled. ## Motivation Qwen4Exp applies Gated Residual projections to all token rows in every decoder layer. PLE adds another replicated token-row projection. Under tensor parallelism, these operations are duplicated on every TP rank. Sharding their token dimension removes the replicated computation while preserving the existing tensor-parallel layout and reduction semantics of attention, GDN/QSA, and MoE. ## Design The implementation: - keeps GR and PLE activations sequence-sharded during prefill; - gathers full token rows before GDN, QSA/attention, or MoE;

title: [Feature] fused MoE tuner: tuned configs can regress at the batch sizes between tuned keys
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` picks the fastest config at each tuned batch size (the JSON keys: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, ...). At runtime, `try_get_optimal_moe_config` serves every other batch size from the nearest key, and when M is equally far from two keys it uses the smaller one. Nothing checks the chosen config at the batch sizes it actually covers, so a config that wins at its key can lose a lot just above it. Those in-between batch sizes are not rare. The default decode CUDA-graph sizes are `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12] + range(16, 257, 8) + ...`, so 12, 40, 56, 72, 80, ... all fall between tuned keys. With speculative decoding the list also includes 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 14, 18, 20, .... **Data.** H20-3e, Triton 3.8.0, GLM-5.3 MoE shape (`E=257,N=256`, fp8 block [128, 128], TP8). The table compares freshly tuned up configs against the existing `triton_3_5_1` ones. Configs were picked by the tuner with #50734 applied, so the down config pairing matches serving. Timing used a server-equivalent harness: no override, configs come from the file lookup, cold L2 before every call, CUDA-graph replay, 32 routings per M, 2 alternating rounds. Each cell is GLM-5.3 (hidden 6144) / DeepSeek-V3 (hidden 7168); both share this config file. | Key | Change at the key | Change at the M it also serves | |---|---|---| | 16 | **-7.0% / -7.5%*

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fused_moe: Add H20-3e Triton 3.8.0 config for E=257,N=256, tuned with real routing
summary: ## Motivation On Triton 3.8.0 there is no H20-3e config for `E=257,N=256,fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128]`, so the server warns and falls back to `triton_3_5_1`. This shape is GLM-5.3 at TP8 (hidden 6144). DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 at TP8 (hidden 7168) loads the same file, because hidden size is not in the filename. This replaces #50762, which I closed. Its config was tuned and validated with uniform random routing. Under real routing, the same config made `fused_moe_kernel` 8.3% slower on the server. Details are in #50761. ## Modifications Adds `triton_3_8_0/E=257,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_H20-3e,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json` and its `_down.json`. Both files are copies of `triton_3_5_1` with one entry changed in each: | File | Key | `triton_3_5_1` | This PR | |---|---|---|---| | up | 1536 | `M32 N64 K128 G1 w4 s3` | `M32 N128 K128 G64 w4 s3` | | down | 256 | `M16 N128 K64 G64 w4 s2 TMA` | `M16 N256 K64 G64 w4 s3 TMA` | The other 16 keys are unchanged, so behavior at those keys is the same as today's fallback. How the two entries were picked: 1. I captured real `topk_ids` from GLM-5.3 serving replayed production chat traffic: 75 MoE layers x 10 batches, with the shared expert fused in. 2. I ran `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py --topk-ids-dir` on them to tune all 18 keys. 3. I re-measured old vs new configs per key, and kept only the keys that were faster on re-measurement and in a server A/B. At several keys the tuned config was slower when measured again, for example 1024 (+4.0%) and 2048 (+3.4%), so those keep the old config. Key 8 looked fine offline but was 4% slower

title: [Fix] hisparse: state-preserving retraction and recovery for DSV4
summary: ## Motivation Current upstream recovers DSV4 / HiSparse decode retractions by asking prefill to recompute the prefix. This PR adds local recovery for non-speculative DSV4 PD serving, retaining HiSparse's existing C4 host state and snapshotting the remaining native page-owned state. The original NotImplementedError is already covered by upstream's recomputation fallback; avoiding recomputation is the remaining motivation. ## Behavior - Settle pending overlap outputs before snapshotting, then flush any committed C4 tail that eager backup has not persisted yet. - Retain the request row, C4 host row, and request-private state. Gate resumed admission on both logical capacity and physical HiSparse buffer capacity. - Restore native pages into newly allocated slots and recover C4 from the retained host row. Short contexts preload; longer contexts begin with an all-miss cache. - Release retained rows and CPU snapshots on abort/retirement. Ordinary retraction callbacks keep their existing signature. - Speculative DSV4 and other HiSparse models retain the upstream recovery path. ## Validation Final verified PR head: `20329099f8391d62bb17890dac74637f9514c30c`. title: [Feature] Prune unused final-layer FFN computation for next-token generation
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Motivation Ordinary next-token generation only needs the final decoder layer’s hidden state for the last input token. After that layer has completed attention and written the KV cache for every token, its FFN and final normalization still process earlier input tokens whose outputs are discarded. This offers a **mathematically equivalent computation pruning opportunity with no approximation of the model**. Unlike approximate pruning that removes weights, tokens, or required layers, this optimization removes only computations that cannot affect the requested output or future KV state. It requires no retraining, calibration dataset, or accuracy/performance tradeoff parameter. The proposed implementation: 1. Preserve all layers' attention and all token KV-cache writes. 2. Select the hidden state and residual operand for each request's last input token immediately before the final decoder FFN. 3. Run the final FFN and normalization on those rows, then compute next-token logits. 4. Support breakable Prefill CUDA Graph with fixed selected-row variants and live request indices. 5. Keep the ordinary path whenever additional rows are required, including prompt logprobs, hidden-state output, and intermediate prefill chunks. title: [Bug] HiCache load-back aborts scheduler with 'must commit all promised FULL tokens or none' on a valid partial load-back (hybrid SWA, regression from #39283)
summary: > Cc @xiezhq-hermann — this assert was added in #39283 (`7f5dd19`), which is where I first bisected it to. Filing here for tracking, and commenting on that PR as well. ### Describe the bug With HiCache enabled on a hybrid-SWA model, a host-hit that includes KV already resident on the device (only blocked by a host-only window/state entry) makes the load-back page in fewer rows than `req.host_hit_length`, and the safety check in `SchedulePolicy.add_one_req` aborts the whole scheduler: ``` RuntimeError: HiCache load-back must commit all promised FULL tokens or none: req=... promised=136192 loaded=41728 ``` This is not a real data-integrity failure: `loaded` is exactly the number of tokens that `build_hicache_transfers(LOAD_BACK)` asked to copy, which is the same value the load-back budget above was reserved with. The assert just compares two different quantities, so a legitimate partial load-back (partial because part of the hit is already on device) kills every TP rank and drops all in-flight requests. ### Environment - 2× NVIDIA L20 (48 GB), PCIe Gen4 x16, no NVLink, single node, 2 NUMA nodes - `sglang` built from source on `sgl-project/sglang` main (2026-11-16), Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9 - Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (hybrid SWA + MoE, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`), fp8 KV, `page_size=256` - Flags: ``` --tensor-parallel-size 2 --context-length 262144 --max-total-tokens 262144 --mem-fraction-static 0.94 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --schedule-policy lpm --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --sp

title: [Feat] debug_utils: Tag non-intrusive dumps with an optional tags dict
summary: ## Motivation Under DSPARK speculative decoding, the draft model's block forward borrows `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY` to reuse the verify-style attention metadata and the decode CUDA graph. The target model's verify forward uses the same mode. So when the non-intrusive dumper is on, the draft and target dumps carry identical tags and cannot be told apart, and dumps of the same tensor from the two runners collide in the comparator. Which model a forward belongs to is a property of the runner, not of the forward, so `forward_mode` is the wrong place to encode it. ## Modifications - `register_non_intrusive_dumper(model, *, tags=None)` accepts an optional dict of tags and attaches it to every dump the hooks emit (both core fields and, in `all` mode, the prefixed module dumps). Without speculative decoding, and when no tags are given, dump names are unchanged. - The dumper itself stays unaware of speculative decoding: the tags are an opaque dict. Dumped files carry the tag in their name, for example `...___runner=draft.pt` and `...___runner=target.pt`. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model outputs. title: [Feat] hisparse: Share prompt prefixes on the decode host-tier radix cache
summary: Share prompt prefixes on the HiSparse decode engine through the host tier of the decode radix tree, and size the HiSparse host pool independently of the logical pool, so decode concurrency is no longer capped by host memory. Depends on #47221 (index-K elision under HiSparse decode). ## Motivation HiSparse previously required `--disable-radix-cache` on the decode engine, so every request kept a private host copy of its whole sequence. Requests that share a long prompt prefix (system prompt, RAG context, multi-turn history) stored, transferred and backed up that prefix once per request. With index-K elision (#47221), the device cost of a logical row drops from `51,168 + 78 × 132 × r` to `51,168 + 21 × 132 × r` bytes, so `max_total_num_tokens` (S) roughly doubles. The default HiSparse host pool has one slot per logical row, `S × r × 51,168` bytes, and grows with it. At a large `host_to_device_ratio` (r) it no longer fits in host memory, which is 259.65 GB per rank on the test node. With elision on, the uncapped pool would need about 315 GB per rank at r=16 and about 353 GB at r=20 (estimated from the formula). So the elided pool has to be capped with `--max-total-tokens`: the GPU memory that elision reclaims goes unused, and the running batch stays capped by host memory whatever the ratio. ## Modifications **Host-tier radix on the HiSparse decode engine** - `arg_groups/hisparse_hook.py`, `pd_disaggregation_hook.py`: allow `--enable-hisparse` with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` on a DSA decode engine. summary: Allow DSA index-K elision under HiSparse decode to reclaim GPU memory and raise batch size. ## Motivation DeepSeek-DSA's IndexShare lets most layers share a single top-k selection: these "shared" layers reuse a preceding producer layer's top-k and never read or write their own index-K. GLM-5.2 has 78 layers, of which only 21 are producers and 57 are shared. The device pool already allocates 0 index-K pages for the shared layers via `skip_topk_layers`, but `_should_elide_dsa_index_k()` still refused elision under HiSparse on a PD decode engine, so the 57 shared layers held device buffers for nothing. title: [Perf] scheduler: Opt-in NO_TOKEN admission lookahead with head-prefix pinning
summary: ## Motivation Closes #38478 `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw` walks the waiting queue in FCFS order and `break`s at the first `AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN`. When the head is a large request whose KV budget does not fit, nothing behind it is considered, even when a smaller request, or one with a long prefix hit that needs almost no new KV, would fit right now. The pass ends with an empty or tiny prefill batch and the head is retried next pass. On a prefill-only node under long-prefix multi-turn load this was ~45 % of all idle scheduler rounds. This PR adds `SGLANG_PREFILL_NO_TOKEN_LOOKAHEAD` (default 0, off). With it set to `N`, after the head's `NO_TOKEN` the loop keeps scanning up to `N` further requests in the same pass. A candidate still goes through `add_one_req`'s ordinary budget (free + evictable), so every existing gate (SWA, Mamba, chunked prefill, DP-attention prefill negotiation) applies unchanged and nothing is over-committed. Three guards make the out-of-order admission safe; the design and the alternatives that were tried are in the issue. With the env var unset the admission loop takes exactly the current decisions (`lookahead_on` never latches, so the first `NO_TOKEN` still breaks) and the lock object is never constructed. ## Modifications **Rebased onto current main (2026-11-10).** The premise still holds: on `AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN` the loop in `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` breaks and considers nothing behind the rejected request. title: [Fix] [AMD] qsa: Handle unaligned extend prefixes from chunk-cache tails
summary: ## Motivation Compressed QSA's extend write plan assumed every cached prefix length was a multiple of `compress_ratio` (4). That holds for a radix-matched prefix because QSA pages are 64 tokens, but `UnifiedRadixCache.cache_unfinished_req` can concatenate a private chunk-cache tail onto `prefix_indices`. The resulting `prefix_lens = seq_len - extend_len` is then not ratio-aligned. Under high concurrency with `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`, a mixed EXTEND batch can therefore hit `torch._assert_async((prefix_lens % ratio == 0).all())`. On ROCm this surfaces as `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION 0x1016` / scheduler `-6`; on CUDA it is a device-side assert (often reported at a later sync point). Reproduced values: `prefix_lens=842`, `842 % 4 != 0`. This is not the same as `--enable-mixed-chunk` injecting `extend_len == 1` decode rows (`ForwardMode.MIXED`). That path is a real trigger and is what #38180 guards against, but the chunk-cache tail also breaks ordinary `ForwardMode.EXTEND`. Disabling mixed-chunk does not fix this crash. ### Why this shows up on MI355 more than MI300 / B200 The QSA grouping bug is platform-agnostic. The usual trigger is gfx950 **exact chunk fill**, which leaves an unfinished chunk-cache tail that is not a multiple of `compress_ratio`. Upstream scheduler: ```python def _use_exact_chunk_fill(): return SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL and is_gfx95_supported() ``` `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` defaults to `True`, but `is_gfx95_supported()` is only true on gfx950 (MI355). Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Since #47944, the Gated DeltaNet chunk prefill kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/`) are 2.3-2.9x slower on Intel XPU, and `recompute_w_u` leaves part of `u` unwritten when the key and value head dims differ (K != V), so those elements hold uninitialized memory: NaN and values up to about 1e38. Cause: #47944 replaced `tl.make_block_ptr` with masked pointer loads, because upstream Triton removed block pointers (triton-lang/triton#10833). In the compiled kernels, `Subgroup2DBlockLoad` calls drop to 0 in `chunk_fwd_kernel_o`, `recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel` and `kkt_solve`. The unwritten `u` comes from the masked-store version of `recompute_w_u` on XPU (`u` is allocated with `torch.empty_like`); the same source is correct on A100. title: [RoadMap] [NPU] NPU Backend Refactor Roadmap
summary: # Background ### From Working to Evolvable SGLang’s support for Ascend NPU began in July 2025 and advanced rapidly through community collaboration over the following year. By August 2025, SGLang could already run end-to-end inference for mainstream models such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi on Ascend, with support for core acceleration features including PD disaggregation, large-scale EP, and the overlap scheduler. Through 2026, NPU backend iteration accelerated further: the quantization stack expanded from W8A8 to W4A8 and W4A4 mixed precision, attention backends began adapting to multiple hardware generations (A3 / 950), and NPU CI coverage gradually widened. In terms of feature coverage and performance, the NPU backend has moved past the stage of “not existing” to “being runnable.” This rapid progress, however, has relied primarily on an **inline adaptation** model: extensive `is_npu()` branches in shared code paths, and hardware-specific logic embedded directly into model and runtime layers. During the feature-catch-up phase, this was a pragmatic choice — it allowed NPU support to reach users in the shortest possible time without waiting for a mature abstraction layer. But as the NPU backend takes on more functionality, its structural costs are becoming apparent. Hardware differences are scattered across multiple layers — ModelExecutor, TPWorker, ModelRunner, Attention Backend, and quantization loading and execution — and backend-specific logic is deeply entangled with shared logic. title: [Fix] scheduler: Dedupe shared prefixes in shortest-first order under SPF
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` (SPF), a short new request can wait minutes, although SPF is meant to run it first. The cause is the in-batch prefix dedupe in `SchedulePolicy._compute_prefix_matches`. It walks the waiting queue in queue order and checks each "cold" request (at most 32 tokens already in the KV cache) against the earlier cold ones. A request that shares at least 32 tokens with one of them is held (deprioritized), so the shared prefix is computed only once, and SPF sorts held requests behind all others. When the earlier request is a long one, SPF itself runs it last, so the short request waits as long as the long one. This PR runs the dedupe in shortest-first order under SPF: in each shared-prefix group the shortest request now runs and the longer ones wait for it, so the shared prefix is still computed once. The dedupe also matches each request on its first 32 tokens only, the most that can decide a match. LPM, DFS-weight and HRRN keep queue order and hold the same requests as before. No request computes anything different; only the order of admission changes. - **Accuracy:** GSM8K-200 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4x B200, SPF, real DSpark speculative decoding: TP4 main 98.0 / 98.0%, this PR 97.5 / 98.0%; DEP4 with HiCache, 2 servers x 8 runs per tree: main 97.5-98.5%, this PR 97.0-98.5% (runs that answered all 200 questions). - **Performance, live server** (4x B200, TP4, SPF): a 432-token request that shares 32 tokens with a queued 150K-token request gets its first token after 9.10-9.21 s on main and 0.22-0.27 s with

summary: ## Motivation The JIT build invokes ninja as a bare command name, so it only works when the active environment's `bin/` directory happens to be on `$PATH`. title: [Fix] logging: Import logging.config before applying custom config
summary: ## Motivation During SGLang engine startup, the detokenizer can fail to apply a valid `SGLANG_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` even when the engine parent and scheduler have no trouble applying it. I hit this with the Dynamo SGLang backend, which [generates the JSON config and exports the path](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/bindings/python/src/dynamo/runtime/logging.py#L218-L252) during worker startup. SGLang creates the detokenizer with multiprocessing's [`spawn` start method](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/multiprocessing.html#contexts-and-start-methods). The new interpreter inherits the environment variable, but not the parent's imported modules. In the failing `python -m dynamo.sglang` launch, [CPython also skips replaying the package's `__main__.py`](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.16/Lib/multiprocessing/spawn.py#L230-L237). The process target is `run_detokenizer_process` in the detokenizer module, so importing the Engine in the parent does not load Engine's dependencies in that child. The detokenizer calls `configure_logger()` before creating its manager. Reading and parsing the file succeeds; accessing `logging.config` then raises the error below because that submodule has not been imported in the child: ```text run_detokenizer_process -> configure_logger logging.config.dictConfig(custom_config) AttributeError: module 'logging' has no attribute 'config' ``` The child exits with code 1, and the watchdog shuts down the engine. The condition is a nonempty `SGLANG_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` **and** no prior import of `logging.config` in the process r

title: [Fix] scheduler: Reserve encoder-replay rows in the shortest-prefill-first chunk reservation
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` (SPF), while a long prompt is prefilled over several chunks, SPF shortens that prompt's chunk so that shorter waiting requests can run in the same step: it reserves room for each of them, charging its uncached tokens rounded up to a page (`SchedulePolicy.shortest_prefill_chunk_limit`). With `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay` (DeepSeek-V4.1), a cache hit that starts a new sliding-window (SWA) state (it has no request slot yet, or was retracted) also recomputes up to 128 of its cached tokens ("replay rows"), and admission charges those rows to the chunk as well (`PrefillAdder._replay_len`). The reservation did not count them, so it came up to 128 tokens short per hit. The last reserved hit then no longer fits; SPF cannot split it (only one request may be mid-chunk), so it waits and the room reserved for it stays empty. The next step computes the same reservation, so the hit keeps waiting until the long prompt's last chunk. This PR adds each reserved hit's replay rows to the reservation, through the same helper admission uses. Nothing changes with encoder replay off, for cache misses, or for hits that keep their slot, and a request computes exactly the same tokens as before; only the step in which it is prefilled changes. SPF and its chunk reservation come from #40024 (@Oasis-Git); the replay-row charge at admission from #45040 and #45047 (@hnyls2002). #46022, another SPF fix, edits the same two files; the two merge cleanly. - **Performance:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x B200, the published Inferen

title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4: Fill a run of identity prefill requests in one batched write
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 low-ratio indexer writes the rows of identity prefill requests one request at a time, about eight tiny device ops each, so its launch count grows with the batch; this PR writes a whole run of identity requests with a fixed number of launches. A prefill request whose compressed context fits `index_topk` selects all of its visible compressed positions, so `fill_identity_requests` writes its rows without scoring. Each `_fill_identity_request` call launches an `arange`, a broadcast compare, a `where`, a cast and a slice-assign, then the same again for `raw_indices`. On a 63-request DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill batch that is ~3.7 ms of almost pure launch overhead per index-source layer. ## Modifications - `_fill_identity_rows_batched`: one `[num_reqs, width]` gather into `k_slots`, one `index_select` to expand it to rows, and one masked `where` into `page_indices` (and `raw_indices`). The per-request host vectors `(lc_per_req, starts, extend_lens)` are uploaded once per forward next to `k_slots` as a single `[3, num_reqs]` tensor. - Same values as the loop: column `j` of a row of request `b` holds compressed position `j` while `j < min(lens_row, lc_b)` and `-1` otherwise. Only columns `[0, max(lc))` are written; the rest is already the `-1` the caller pre-fills. - A run of a single request keeps the existing per-request call, which is already one fill. No new flag. title: [Perf] io_struct: Validate an input_embeds body against one union member
summary: Pydantic walks both members of the `input_embeds` union: a 4,950 × 2048 request spends 6.3 s of its 9.1 s to first token in validation, and one bad value in it costs minutes and a 3.3 GB response. A discriminator on the first value walks one member: 2.8 s, and 1 s with 589 bytes. ## Motivation `GenerateReqInput.input_embeds` is `Union[3D, 2D]` in smart mode. A 2D body, the documented single-request shape, first fails the 3D member once per float, about 10 million errors at 4,950 × 2048, and only then matches the 2D member. FastAPI validates on the event loop, so for those 6.3 s the worker does nothing else: the request waits, and so do the tokens of every stream it serves. A 3D body does not pay this. A body with one bad value matches neither member, so FastAPI keeps all of those errors and `validation_exception_handler` renders them. At 4,950 × 2048: 163 s and 399 s in two launches, 22.6 GB of RSS, a 3.26 GB HTTP 400, and a short request sent meanwhile waits as long. Reordering the union is not enough: smart mode stops early only on an exact match, so one int in the body walks the 3D member again. `union_mode="left_to_right"` with 2D first gives the same speed for a good body, but a bad value still walks both members. A `PlainValidator` as `input_ids` has needs its own shape and coercion rules (pydantic takes numeric strings here); a discriminator leaves pydantic's behaviour on a good body as it is. #20206 took on the same cost with `SkipValidation` and was closed as idle without review; this keeps validation and int coercion. ## Modifications - `io_struct.py`: a callable

title: [Feat] spec-decoding: Add context-aware adaptive routing
summary: ## Motivation Adaptive speculative decoding currently routes by batch size. title: [Feat] [NPU] prefill: breakable prefill graph for DSV4 and ascend_ops MoE
summary: ## Motivation Prefill on Ascend NPU is host-bound at small per-rank chunks: a step launches hundreds of kernels and rebuilds attention / MoE metadata on the host, and the existing graph paths only cover decode. title: [Fix] model_loader: Refuse state-dict checkpoints that would silently drop MXFP4 triton_kernels expert weights
summary: ## Motivation Part of #34448: the fail-loud part. The issue stays open for the full round-trip. The reporter saw a 4.0 GB export for a 13 GB gpt-oss-20b checkpoint. - Loading any such checkpoint copies nothing into the wrappers, which were built from freshly initialized weights. The `Missing keys` check doesn't fire, because the keys are absent from both the checkpoint and the model. Every expert runs on garbage with no error or warning. title: [Fix] modelopt: reject incompatible mixed-precision shared-expert fusion
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-NVFP4 with `--quantization modelopt_mixed` fails during weight loading when shared-expert fusion is enabled. Its routed experts are NVFP4, while its shared experts remain BF16. Fusion copies the BF16 shared weights into NVFP4-packed routed-expert buffers and fails with a 6144-versus-3072 dimension mismatch. `ModelOptFp4Config` already provides a fusion veto, but `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` does not. The earlier Hopper fix in #37325 covers `modelopt_fp4`, not this path. ## Modifications Add `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert()` using the existing fusion hook. Compare the shared and routed quantization formats in every affected layer, including exclusions applied to packed gate/up projections. Preserve fusion when they match, supporting both `shared_expert` and `shared_experts` names. Extend the existing CPU tests with mixed-precision, exclusion and multi-layer cases. No launcher flags or model-specific workaround are added. ## Accuracy Tests CPU tests on this branch: ``` PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4.py # 9 passed, 9 subtests passed PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py # 50 passed, 13 subtests passed ``` The original GLM guard was also tested on SGLang 0.5.23, H200 TP8: target and NextN weights loaded on all eight ranks, and five functional checks passed with real output. That predates the main-based port and its additional compatibility cases; no fresh GPU or GPQA run was performed for this branch. #

title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Use 64-bit token offsets in the Triton sparse MLA kernels
summary: # [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Use 64-bit token offsets in the Triton sparse MLA kernels ## Motivation The four kernels of `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_sparse_mla.py` (`_sparse_mla_fwd_split_dim_kernel`, `_sparse_mla_fused_kernel`, `_sparse_mla_split_k_kernel`, `_sparse_mla_reduce_kernel`) take the token index from `tl.program_id(0)`, 32-bit, and address q, the indices, the output and the split-K partials as `token * stride`. Past 2^31 elements the offset wraps. Depending on where the wrapped address lands: - **wrong output, no error**: the single-pass kernel read other memory for every token past the limit (see Accuracy Tests); or - a GPU memory access fault that stops the server (the split-K / fused kernel, and the single-pass kernel in a server). SGLang hands these kernels q as two views of one `[tokens, H, 576]` buffer (`_row_strides`), so the q row stride is `H x 576`, and the first offset to wrap is q's: `(tokens - 1) x H x 576 > 2^31 - 1`. **Who hits it.** Any model served with `--dsa-prefill-backend triton`, which SGLang on ROCm also picks by itself for an FP8 KV cache ("Set DSA backends for fp8_e4m3 KV Cache: prefill=triton, decode=triton"): **GLM-5.x** (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-MXFP4) and **DeepSeek-V3.2**. Tokens are the extend batch, up to `--chunked-prefill-size`. | heads a rank | e.g. | wrong past (tokens in one chunk) | |---|---|---| | 64 | GLM-5.x TP1; DeepSeek-V3.2 TP2 | 58,254 | | 32 | GLM-5.x **TP2**; DeepSeek-V3.2 TP4 | 116,508 | | 16 | GLM-5.x TP4; DeepSeek-V3.2 TP8 | 233,016 | | 8 | GLM-5.x TP8 | 466,033 | With the sgl-amd-mono GLM-5.3 recipes'

summary: ## Motivation Fixes #22117. `natfii/Qwen3.6-27B-VLM-NVFP4-MTP` fails during TP=2 checkpoint loading with a shape assertion: ```text AssertionError: param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape ``` This checkpoint uses ModelOpt FP4/NVFP4 quantization and contains packed weights and scale parameters in Qwen GDN and attention submodules. title: [Scheduler] Concurrent chunked prefill via --long-prefill-token-threshold
summary: ## Motivation SGLang can have at most **one** request mid-prefill at a time. A long prompt therefore monopolizes the prefill batch for its entire prefill, and every queued request — however small, however long it has waited — waits it out. **Measured in production** (Sference fleet, SGLang backends): - **Kimi-K3** (`chunked_prefill_size=8192`): with 642K–912K-token prompts in flight, **10.35% of requests exceeded 60 s TTFT**, vs 0.23–0.56% in adjacent hours without long prompts. p50 was unaffected — a pure tail/QoS failure. - **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (`chunked_prefill_size=4096`): 458K-token prompts ⇒ ~112 consecutive scheduler rounds in which no other request can prefill. Rolling TTFT p99 of 12–14 s, spiking to 27.7 s. **This is a missing mechanism, not a tuning gap.** Driving the stock `PrefillAdder` (this branch's base) with three 500K-token requests, KV headroom pinned so it can never bind: | config | per-request chunks | requests concurrently mid-prefill | |---|---|---| | `chunked_prefill_size=8192`, `max_prefill_tokens=16384` | `[8192, 0, 0]` | **1** | | `chunked_prefill_size=8192`, `max_prefill_tokens=131072` | `[8192, 0, 0]` | **1** | | `chunked_prefill_size=2048`, `max_prefill_tokens=1000000` | `[2048, 0, 0]` | **1** | Requests 2 and 3 get zero tokens in every configuration. title: [DeepEP] Use static FP8 communication for W4AFP8 normal dispatch
summary: ## Motivation For W4AFP8 MoE on the DeepEP normal-dispatch path, the dispatcher previously sent BF16 hidden states over the all-to-all and re-quantized them on the receiving side using the checkpoint's static activation scale. This doubles the communication volume (BF16 instead of FP8) and re-does a quantization that the weights were already calibrated against.
