title: [Fix] Route text before the opening think token by position, not by index 0
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #35083. `BaseReasoningFormatDetector` enters a reasoning block on `think_start_token in text` (anywhere) but strips the marker with `startswith` (index 0 only). Anything in front of the opening marker — a single space or newline is enough — falls into the gap, and the streaming path has the mirror-image gap: it only recognises a partial opening marker when the whole buffer is a prefix of it. Same string, four answers on `main` (`--reasoning-parser qwen3`, `"Sure.<think>checking</think>Done."`): | path | `reasoning_content` | `content` | |---|---|---| | non-streaming | `'Sure.<think>checking'` | `'Done.'` | | streaming, marker whole in one chunk | `'checking'` | `'Sure.Done.'` | | streaming, chunk ends inside `<think>` | `''` | `'Sure.<think>checking</think>Done.'` | | streaming, whole turn in one chunk | `'Sure.checking'` | `'Done.'` | Row 3 streams the whole reasoning block, markers included, to the client as assistant content. It needs a chunk carrying content plus a strict prefix of the marker, which a multi-token decode step produces: `--stream-interval > 1`, `sampling_params.stream_interval`, speculative decoding, or the detokenizer releasing several tokens after an incomplete UTF-8 sequence. Rows 1, 2 and 4 need no such condition. #34458 already named this case and pinned it: ```python def test_text_before_think_token_is_chunk_dependent(self): """Accepted divergence, inherited from main: text before `<think>` lands in reasoning or content depending on where the chunk boundary falls.""" ``` This PR closes that exception instead of pinning it. ## Mod

title: [Disagg] Layer-pipelined KV transfer: overlap RDMA with GPU compute
summary: ## Motivation In PD disaggregation mode, KV cache transfer happens **after** full prefill computation completes. For long prompts (≥1K tokens), this creates a significant TTFT bottleneck — the decode side must wait for all layers to be computed and then transferred sequentially. This PR implements **layer-pipelined KV transfer**: instead of computing all layers then transferring all KV at once, we split layers into groups and transfer each group incrementally. title: [Fix] scheduler: Reserve encoder replay rows in the SPF chunk reservation
summary: ## Motivation Under `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first`, while a long request is being chunked, `SchedulePolicy.shortest_prefill_chunk_limit` caps the continuation chunk so the shorter waiting requests fit in the same prefill. It reserves `ceil(work / page_size) * page_size` per waiting request. With `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`, admission (`PrefillAdder._select_prefill_admission`) also charges the replay rows of every request that starts a new SWA window: `chunk_limit -= replay_len(prefix_len)`, i.e. up to 128 extra rows. New requests always qualify (`resets_swa_window`: no `req_pool_idx` yet). So a reserved request needs up to 128 more tokens than were reserved. It misses the chunk fit (`chunk_fit_tokens > chunk_tokens_limit`). Under SPF with a chunked request in flight, that returns `AddReqResult.OTHER`, and the scheduler's admission loop breaks. The continuation was already shortened, so the whole reservation goes unused, and the pass runs as a lone, under-filled continuation chunk. ## Modifications - `shortest_prefill_chunk_limit` adds `encoder_swa_replay.replay_len(prefix)` to each reserved request's charge when encoder replay is on and `resets_swa_window(req)`. This matches what admission charges. `prefix` is the request's length minus `_shortest_prefill_work(req)`, so it uses the same notion of cached tokens as the work estimate, including a staged storage prefix. The replay flag is read only once the `exec` config is published, so a policy built before that, as in unit tests, reserves without replay rows. - New unit test `test_shortest_prefill_reser

title: Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids)
summary: # Retracted input_embeds requests silently splice two generations into one successful response (send_token_offset survives the discard of output_ids) ## Summary When the KV cache pool runs out of memory, the scheduler retracts running decode requests and requeues them. For requests that supplied `input_embeds`, `Req.reset_for_retract()` deliberately discards `output_ids` and restarts generation from scratch (the fix for the shape-mismatch crash in #14109, PR #14110), but it does not reset `send_token_offset` (nor the sibling output-stream cursors). The output streamer slices the restarted generation with that surviving offset, so the first N tokens of the new generation are silently dropped and the client's assembled response becomes a splice of generation A's already-streamed prefix and generation B's tail. The request then finishes normally with a success finish reason. Affected code (at commit b510881157b8f12b98387340c7fbfc266dbbb35e): - `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1928-1932`, the input_embeds branch of `reset_for_retract`: ```python if self.input_embeds is not None: self.output_ids = array("q") self.weight_version_events = truncate_weight_version_events( self.weight_version_events, num_kept_tokens=self.send_token_offset ) ``` `output_ids` is cleared, `weight_version_events` is truncated using `send_token_offset`, but `send_token_offset` itself is never reset. title: fix(moe): Nemotron-H fix, honor is_gated=False and support relu2 in native MoE
summary: ## Motivation Nemotron-H's routed experts are non-gated relu2 with `routed_scaling_factor` 2.5. Under `--enable-torch-compile`, single-token decode replaces the MoE runner with `fused_moe_forward_native`, which had two problems: - It always split `w13` into gate and up halves, and neither native path accepted relu2, so non-gated relu2 experts failed with an einsum shape mismatch. - It never applied `routed_scaling_factor`, so routed outputs were 2.5x too small, at batch size 1 only. ## Modifications - Non-gated experts use `w13` as the full up-projection with an elementwise activation (relu2, silu, gelu), and `moe_forward_native` accepts relu2. title: [Feat] speculative: Insert bounded prompt tail on extend in NGRAMWorker
summary: ## Motivation Part of the N-gram Speculative Decoding Roadmap (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21052). Currently, `NGRAMWorker._update_ngram_corpus` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`) is only called after `TARGET_VERIFY` steps and carries a `FIXME`: ```python # FIXME: Whether to insert 'extend' into the cache or not, after testing, # there is not much difference, so we will not insert it for now. ``` As a result, when a new request completes its prefill (`EXTEND`) phase and enters its first `DECODE` step, the N-gram Trie has **zero tokens from the current request's prompt** (except the last `max_trie_depth = 18` query suffix). In long-context chat, RAG, summarization, and structured JSON planning workloads, entities, identifiers, and schema keys that appear earlier in the prompt cannot be drafted until they have already been generated once by the model. Inserting an entire 32k–64k prompt into the Trie on `EXTEND` would incur O(L * max_trie_depth) CPU insertion overhead. However, inserting a **bounded tail window** (`NGRAM_EXTEND_PROMPT_WINDOW = 1024` tokens) of `req.origin_input_ids` asynchronously during `EXTEND` takes `< 0.15 ms` on the background C++ `insertWorker` thread (completely hidden behind the GPU extend forward pass) while capturing the most relevant recent context, instructions, and entity names for immediate drafting on step 1. summary: ## Motivation With `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, the prefill runner refuses graph replay for every Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4-Exp) batch that carries multimodal inputs, so image prefills always run eager. **Scope:** this enables graph replay for image prefills in deployments without speculative decoding. With speculative decoding enabled (any algorithm, including NGRAM), behavior is unchanged. - The refusal came with #41729, which added breakable prefill graphs for this model with text-only scope. - Multimodal `input_embeds` already replay under breakable graphs (#31391): the eager outer forward builds the merged text and vision embeddings, and replay copies them into the captured static slot, as for text batches. - With speculative decoding, the draft runner still refuses image batches, and the target must refuse with it: under DP attention the replay vote consults only the target runner and the draft follows it, so a draft-only refusal could split ranks between replay and eager. This PR keys the refusal on whether speculative decoding is enabled, a launch-time property identical on every rank. Without speculative decoding, image batches become replay-eligible; with any speculative algorithm (including NGRAM), behavior is unchanged. No new flag, environment variable or API. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py` (+8/-4): replace `_qwen_bcg_mtp_draft` (no other reader) with `_qwen_bcg_multimodal_eager = qwen_bcg and model_runner.spec_algorithm.is_speculative()`, and gate multimodal batches on it. - `test/register

title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Pass the EP-wide token count to MegaMoE under attention DP
summary: Independent of the KDA PRs. **Problem.** Kimi-K3 with attention DP + `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` hangs when DP ranks prefill different lengths in the same step. Every EP rank but one then prints `DeepGEMM combine peers timeout` and the server aborts. `KimiK3MoE._forward_mega_experts` calls `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_mega_moe` without `global_num_tokens`, so each rank picks BLOCK_M from its own rows. At K3 shapes on EP4, `get_block_m_for_mega_moe` gives 16 / 64 / 128 / 192 / 240 for 0 / 64 / 1K / 2K / 8K rows. With unequal rows, the ranks launch different tiles and the combine never completes. The generic path (`layers/moe/mega_moe.py`) passes `_mega_moe_global_tokens_hint`. Only the K3 path omits it. **Change.** - `_forward_mega_experts` passes `global_num_tokens=_mega_moe_global_tokens_hint(buf)`. Every rank then picks the same tile (192 for the counts above). - `_mega_moe_global_tokens_hint` also covers attention TP inside DP groups (e.g. DP4 x attention TP2 on EP8). It used to return None unless the EP size equalled the DP count, so those ranks still diverged. EP a2a MoE runs on each rank's attention-TP slice (K3's SP-MoE; the generic path scatters the same way), and `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads each DP count to an attention-TP multiple, so the counts' sum is still the EP-wide row count. The hint now needs the EP size to be a multiple of the DP count. summary: ## Motivation On Hopper, Inkling-2-Small decode returns garbage once requests are batched, unless the server runs with a page size that is a multiple of the decode tile (the cookbook's `--page-size 128`). [concurrency 16] The user wants ★★★ The user response follows.The user wants coral 0The ocean covers about the ocean is ... ``` Nothing warns or fails. A lone request usually gets contiguous slots. title: [Fix] scheduler: Honor earliest stop in speculative token blocks
summary: ## Motivation Speculative decoding can commit several tokens at once. If more than one stop string or regex matched the block, request finishing chose the first match in configuration order rather than the earliest stopping position. A later text stop could also override an earlier EOS token, returning tokens after generation should have stopped. For example, with stops `["END", "STOP"]`, a block containing `A → STOP → B → END` must finish at `STOP`, regardless of the order of the configured strings. ## Modifications Compare the finish positions of matching strings and regexes, then honor an earlier EOS/stop token. Preserve text-stop priority on ties, transient end-anchored regex matches, and the generation-length cap. Keep the abort finish reason when the defensive runtime check catches a malformed regex. ## Tests Added regressions for stop-list permutations, mixed string/regex stops, earlier EOS, length caps, and malformed regexes. The regressions reproduce the failure on the parent revision. The stop-string, finish-length, grammar-stop, and detokenizer-trimming suites pass with the patched finishing methods: **34 tests and eight subtests**. title: [Fix] batch_invariant_ops: Do not choose the matmul kernel by a.is_contiguous()
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. title: [Feat] dflash: Confidence-scheduled compact verify for DFlash2 on Kimi K3.1
summary: ## Motivation Enable confidence-scheduled compact verification for DFlash2 on Kimi K3.1’s sparse MLA and hybrid attention target. DFlash2 already runs on this model; this change connects its selector draft to the existing verification planner and makes the target attention metadata understand variable verification lengths. It builds on current main’s MLA draft support, native-head FlashMLA handling, and per-request draft KV rings. Two assumptions currently prevent that combination: 1. **DFLASH verifies a fixed block without using the confidence planner.** DFlash2 exposes candidate-selector scores but does not have the trained confidence head used by other speculative configurations. Those scores need to become acceptance estimates before the planner can choose a verification budget. 2. **Sparse MLA metadata assumes a uniform query width per request.** Compact verification packs different numbers of query tokens from each request. For example, lengths `[2, 5, 1]` produce eight query rows with request boundaries `[0, 2, 7, 8]`. Reshaping those rows as a uniform `[requests, next_n]` batch loses their request ownership and causal KV lengths. The intended behavior is to verify a planned prefix of each draft block, execute the packed queries through supported target backends, and commit only tokens covered by real target verification. CUDA-graph padding must remain separate from real queries and recurrent-state updates. ## Modifications ### 1. Connect DFlash2 to the existing confidence planner - Reuse `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator`, `DSparkVerifyPlanner`, and `TargetVerifyExecutor`.

FlashInfer's wrapper takes it in both quant modes (W4A4, W4A16) and clamps the same way, in dequantized units. Without a limit nothing is passed and the wrapper keeps its default (no clamp). - The DeepEP low-latency path (`fused_experts_deepep_to_flashinfer_cutedsl_fp4`) refuses a `swiglu_limit`, next to its activation check: its masked GEMM and fused SiLU-and-quantize kernels take no clamp. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_moe_backends.py` gains `test_flashinfer_cutedsl_swiglu_limit`: the real FusedMoE path with `swiglu_limit=0.1` against the dequantized torch reference, which clamps the same way. title: [Fix] mm: encode a multimodal item once per request in chunked prefill
summary: Fixes repeated video encoding in chunked prefill. A long video went through the vision encoder once per chunk, so two or three times per request. Now it is encoded once. ## Motivation When a prompt is longer than `chunked_prefill_size`, prefill runs in chunks. Each chunk looks for the encoder output in the embedding cache. If it is not there, the chunk runs the encoder again on the whole video, not only on the part it needs. For a long video it is usually not there: - The cache is 100 MiB by default. The encoder output of a long video is bigger than that, so it is never stored. - Qwen3-VL on a Hopper GPU with 60 GiB or more runs with the cache off. - An entry can be evicted between two chunks of the same request. So a request with 3 chunks runs the encoder 3 times. A large image or an audio clip cut by a chunk boundary has the same problem. `EarlyEmbeddings` (#47196) works around it for Unlimited-OCR windows; this fixes it in the shared paths. ## Reproduction One H200, upstream `9d547e19ff`, 1280x720 synthetic clips, one at a time, 16 output tokens, greedy, 6 requests per cell (3 clips, each again after a flush). A forward hook on `visual` counts the encoder's passes. | Model | Clip | Prompt tokens | Cache | Passes per request, main → this PR | Same text | Logprob difference | Median total, main → this PR | |---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 33.5 s | 23,788 | off | 3 → 1 | 6 of 6 | 0 | 3.66 → 2.25 s | | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` | 33.5 s | 23,788 | default | 3 → 1 | 6 of 6 | 0 | 3.59 → 2.25 s | | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` | 16.5 s

title: [Perf] [AMD] minimax: Let decode and verify steps run without host seq_lens on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, the overlap scheduler synchronizes the host before each spec-v2 decode or verify step. It does this when an attention backend asks for the host copy of `seq_lens` (`FutureMap.resolve_seq_lens_cpu`, "Temporary workaround: Event.wait() regresses TPOT on AMD MI355"). When no backend asks for the copy, `run_batch` resolves the lengths in stream order on the forward stream, and the host runs ahead (`gpu_only_lens`). The MiniMax sparse and hybrid backends do not declare `needs_cpu_seq_lens`. Thus they ask for the copy. With MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and DSpark on MI355X, the host waits for each step to end and then builds the next step. The GPU idles during that time. py-spy on the TP0 scheduler (one request, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with sgl-amd-mono's monokernels) shows 70 % of the event loop in this `Event.synchronize`. The GPU idles about 0.7 ms of a 6.5 ms step. With linear verify, a decode or verify step reads `seq_lens_cpu` at one place only: the out-of-graph `max_seqlen` bound. A replayed graph does not use it, because the capture already bounds it by `max_context_len`. ## Modifications - `MiniMaxSparseAttnBackend` declares `needs_cpu_seq_lens = False` on ROCm with linear verify. A step without `seq_lens_cpu` takes the capture's bound, `max_context_len`. Only an eager step reads the bound. Its result does not change, and its scan is longer. Eager decode and verify steps are rare, because graphs cover the decode batch sizes. - `MiniMaxHybridAttnBackend` asks for the host copy when its sparse backend asks for it. title: [Fix] dspark: Stop compact verify from counting padding rows as accepted drafts
summary: ## Motivation In `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_verify.py`, compact ragged verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`) runs the target model on only `verify_len` rows per request. The rest of the block is filled with padding: candidate id `0` and all-zero logits. Every accept kernel (greedy, chain sampling, block verification, blockwise rejection) still scans the whole padded block and caps the accepted count afterwards. So `cap_trim_lens`, the count of drafts the target would have accepted past the cutoff, gets inflated in three ways: - The in-graph epilogue (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue.__call__`) compared padding id `0` against the argmax of a zero row, which is also `0`, so the whole padding tail was counted. - That same comparison missed real accepts of the first draft past the cutoff. - Even with real drafts as candidates, a draft whose token id is `0`, or a sampled draft against a uniform padding row, matched rows the target never scored. This corrupts `block_accept_lens` / `spec_num_block_accept_tokens` (API `meta_info`) and the block-accept estimate recorder. Generated output is unaffected, because `cap_trim_lens` never feeds `commit_lens`, `new_seq_lens` or the bonus token. ## Modifications - `build_accept_outs` takes a new `scored_lens` argument: the number of target rows per request that carry real logits. Row `j` verifies draft `j + 1`, so `cap_trim_lens` is bounded by `scored_lens − correct_len` (at most 1 in compact mode). The bound sits where every accept path, graph and eager, meets. - The compact epilogue passes `scored_lens=verify_lens`

summary: ## Motivation With `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, PyTorch allocates GPU memory that `hipIpcGetMemHandle` cannot share with other GPUs. This affects runs that use `CustomAllreduce` instead of AITER's all-reduce: deterministic inference, `SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_AR=0`, or no AITER installed. title: [Perf] Engine: freeze GC after startup, as the HTTP server does
summary: ## Motivation Offline `sgl.Engine` throughput on multi-item scoring (`enable_mis`, `Engine.score` / `async_score`) is limited by the host, not the GPU: on 1x H200 the GPU is only 63-67% busy on main. Three changes, one per commit, remove the main host-side stalls. Together they give 1.53x on this workload (36.5k -> 55.6k scores/s with token ids, 27.4k -> 41.8k with embed overrides). The math is unchanged. 1. **The offline Engine never freezes the garbage collector.** `sglang serve` freezes GC in the tokenizer manager, the scheduler and the detokenizer after its warmup request; `sgl.Engine` never does. Its processes keep the whole startup heap (imported modules, functions, model config and tokenizer objects) in the collected generations, and every gen-2 pass rescans it while collecting nothing. On 1x H200 with Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, right after `sgl.Engine(...)` starts, the main process tracks about 871k objects and a full `gc.collect(2)` takes 350-365 ms. Under a steady request stream these passes stall the tokenizer manager and the scheduler. Users can call `engine.freeze_gc()` after warmup, but few do. 2. **MIS reads label-token logprobs back with a blocking copy per request.** Multi-item scoring runs prefill without CUDA graphs or chunked prefill, so throughput depends on the overlap scheduler keeping the GPU fed. summary: ## Motivation Under MLP sync (DP attention, or a gathered MoE buffer at TP>1), `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads each rank's token count to a multiple of `attn_tp_size`. The first client request with a new prompt length triggers a dynamic-shape recompile, and that recompile fails. All four klein cases (4B/9B × t2i/TI2I) fail with `--enable-torch-compile`. It still reproduces on today's `main` (`de26bb16a9`). **Mechanism** (from `TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks,recompiles,graph_code`, #41944 vs its parent): 1. `_as_fa_input`'s `view.data_ptr() % 16 == 0` can't be traced. Dynamo raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for %: 'int' and 'int'` internally, logs a graph break there (16×), and falls back to eager for the enclosing frames (21× vs 5× on the parent). 2. Dynamo then compiles helpers as separate frames, among them `_flux2_single_qk_rope`. That frame's q/k inputs are views of one fused-projection buffer, and `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` mutates them in place. AOTAutograd therefore builds a synthetic base (`merge_view_inputs`). 3. The static warmup compile works. The first dynamic recompile (4624 → 4608 tokens) hits a symbolic storage size in the synthetic base's `set_()`, giving the error above. Bisected to #41944. Skipping only the `data_ptr()` clause, with the zero-copy views kept, also fixes it, so the untraceable pointer check is the trigger, not the views. ## Modifications - `xpu_backend.py`: under `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`, `_as_fa_input` re

title: [Fix] rust-server: Refuse return_hidden_states above the server's mode
summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` and `--return-hidden-states-mode last`, one `/generate` request with `"return_hidden_states": true` takes down the whole server: ```bash SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 31001 --return-hidden-states-mode last --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1 --skip-server-warmup curl -s localhost:31001/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"hi","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":4},"return_hidden_states":true}' ``` The last two flags only shorten startup. The scheduler raises `RuntimeError: The runtime hidden-state mode exceeds the fixed CUDA graph capture mode (LAST).` and the server exits. The Python frontend returns 400 for the same request. The Rust frontend only receives the resolved `enable_return_hidden_states` bool, which is `True` under `last`, so it can't tell that `true` (`full`) is above the server's mode. This is the `return_hidden_states_mode` entry in `RUST_SERVER_KNOWN_GAPS`. ## Modifications - `rust_server/config.py`: pass `sa.return_hidden_states_mode` to the Rust server, read directly so the parity scanner sees it. - `message/config.rs`: add `HiddenStatesMode { Null, Last, Full }` and `ServerArgs::hidden_states_mode()`, resolved the same way as `get_server_return_hidden_states_mode` in `forward_batch_info.py`. - `Limits` carries the mode instead of the bool. `validate()` refuses a request above it with the two messages from `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request`. - `parity.py`: remove the known-gap entry. - Two visible side effects: - The message for a server

title: [Test] rust-server: Pin that a closed connection aborts an admitted unary prefill request
summary: ## Motivation In prefill/decode disaggregation, a client such as a router can lose its connection to a prefill server before any response byte arrives. The prefill server should then stop work on the request it already admitted, so the client needs no abort of its own for it. The Rust frontend already behaves this way: when the connection closes, the server drops the request's handler, and the generation's guard (`impl Drop for Generation` in `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/handlers/generate.rs`) sends the scheduler `AbortSource::Guard(rid)` for a request intake has accepted. No test in the native API tests closes a real connection on an admitted unary request, so nothing pins that a closed TCP connection actually reaches that guard. ## Modifications Test only, one file: `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/native_api.rs`. New test `closed_connection_aborts_admitted_unary_prefill`: - builds a disaggregation `CoreHandle` and serves `routes()` with `axum::serve` on a `127.0.0.1:0` TCP listener; - writes a unary prefill `POST /generate` (with `bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, `bootstrap_room`) over a raw HTTP/1.1 socket and accepts it at intake; - checks that no response byte arrives while the request is admitted, then closes the socket; - requires the scheduler's abort channel to receive `AbortSource::Guard` naming the request's rid within five seconds, and nothing after it. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: no change outside the test module. Locally on this head: - `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server`: 544 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, the new test included. - Mutat

title: [Perf] dsa: Run Kimi-K3.1's 65-128-head FlashMLA decode on the head128 kernel
summary: ## Motivation Under DCP decode, each Kimi-K3.1 attention call sees 96 q heads over a V3.2-layout KV cache (`d_qk` 576, 656 B/token). On SM100 this runs on the legacy FlashMLA kernels as head64 over two head blocks, so each block gathers and dequantizes the whole KV. sgl-project/FlashMLA#36 adds V3.2 to the current API's 2-CTA head128 decode kernel, which serves 128 heads (96 of them real, the rest padding) with one KV gather. ## Modifications - `dsa_backend.py`: - **Routing:** when the cache is V32, the call has 65–128 q heads and the GPU is SM100, `_flashmla_kv_padded_heads` returns 128, so q is padded to 128 heads. - **Decode call:** `_forward_flashmla_kv` calls `_flashmla_head128_decode`, which runs `use_legacy=False` with a fresh `FlashMLASchedMeta` each call. It skips the legacy DCP schedule. - **LSE:** viewed by the padded head count, because the current kernels return `[T, 1, H]` while the legacy kernels return `[T, H, 1]`. - `deepseek_v4_backend.py`: `_maybe_precompute_flashmla_sched_meta(head128=True)` fills the split-KV schedule for the head128 kernel, with one SM part per 2-CTA pair and a fixed overhead of 3 blocks. Without it, FlashMLA would add its own `<<<1, 32>>>` scheduling kernel to every call. - `test_flashmla_sched_meta.py`: the routing assertion now expects 96 V32 heads to pad to 128. Other head counts and formats keep their current paths. ## Accuracy Tests Not yet run end to end. At kernel level, FlashMLA#36's V3.2 tests pass (448/448), and its output agrees with the legacy head64 kernel on the same cache. ## Benchmarking and Profiling Kernel-level only

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Retire request-owned SWA after skipped no-buffer checkpoint
summary: ## Motivation When an unfinished no-buffer request cannot allocate an optional Mamba checkpoint, `prepare_for_caching_req` returns zero. The insertion key is then empty, so request-owned SWA retirement also stops. Old window rows remain allocated even though the live recurrent state has advanced and no older tracked snapshot needs them. This addresses one no-buffer pressure case related to #49944, not the general recurrent-checkpoint demand problem. #42412 proposed prefill state reservations; this change instead preserves request-local window retirement when donation is skipped. No code from that proposal is incorporated. The existing optional-checkpoint skip behavior is retained, rather than reimplemented. ## Modifications - Record failure of the ordinary no-buffer checkpoint allocation separately from tracked-buffer deferral. - Use the processed token frontier for request-owned window retirement after that failure, while preserving tree-owned prefix protection. - Leave insertion skipped. A later successful checkpoint uses the existing SWA tombstone mechanism. - Add real allocator/cache regression tests for pressure, recovery, retained payload, prefix matching and cancellation. ## Accuracy Tests On upstream `48e35583bd0ebf251637d5b670a615145ce85564`, CPU Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu (not the repository's 2.14.1 pin): ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:test/registered/unit/mem_cache python -m unittest \ test.registered.unit.mem_cache.test_unified_capacity_decisions \ test.registered.unit.mem_cache.test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.TestMambaDonatedAllocRatio \ test.registered.unit.me

title: [Perf] [AMD] rotary_embedding: tile fused RoPE and KV write for large T on gfx1250
summary: This PR tiles the fused RoPE + KV write on gfx1250 once T is at least 256. The existing kernel launches one 1-warp program per token per query head. ## Motivation On gfx1250 that per-(token, head) launch sits around 0.6 TB/s for a prefill-sized T. gpt-oss-120b, TP1, T=16384: 586 us. The tiled launch covers 16 tokens and 8 query heads per program, plus one program per 16 tokens for the K rope and the KV cache write. Same shape: 135 us. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache.py`. For a large enough T the call uses `_fused_qk_rope_cache_tiled_kernel`. Every other call keeps the existing kernel. - The tiled path runs when `SGLANG_FUSED_ROPE_KV_TILED` is left on (the default), the device is gfx1250, T >= 256, the slot count equals T, cos/sin is fp32, q and k are bf16, fp16, or fp32, the rotary layout is NeoX, the cache layout is flash, freqs cover D/2, `zeros_out` is absent, the KV head count is a power of two, the query head count is a multiple of the KV head count, and q, k, v, the outputs, the cache, and cos/sin are unit-stride on the last dim. - The head block is 8 when the query head count divides by 8, and the KV head count otherwise. 4 warps. The cos term is an fma, the same form the existing kernel compiles to, so the two outputs match bit for bit. - `SGLANG_FUSED_ROPE_KV_TILED=false` keeps the original kernel. The tile is fixed at 16 tokens, 8 query heads, and 4 warps, from T >= 256. A bad value warns and keeps the default. It does not stop the server. ## Accuracy Tests Bit-equal to the existing kernel on the shapes check

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] GDN: Prevent NaNs in Qwen3.5 long-context prefill
summary: Fixes [Issue #50037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/50037) ## Motivation The Blackwell CuTe DSL GDN prefill kernel uses three Newton–Schulz iterations to approximate the inverse of the diagonal blocks of `I + A`. Although the persistent inverse iterate is stored in FP32, both operands of the Newton–Schulz MMAs are converted to BF16. For ill-conditioned blocks, this repeated truncation can introduce a large inverse error. The gated recurrent update can amplify and propagate the error across long Qwen3.5 prefills, eventually producing non-finite states or outputs. ## Modifications This PR updates: ```text python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/linear/gdn_blackwell/kernel_kkt_inv_uw.py ``` The Newton–Schulz operands are represented with compensated BF16x2 limbs: ```text Ai ≈ Ai_hi + Ai_lo P ≈ P_hi + P_lo ``` For the first product, the kernel computes: ```text Ai @ (-M) ≈ Ai_hi @ (-M) + Ai_lo @ (-M) ``[]` For the second product, it computes: ```text P @ Ai ≈ P_hi @ Ai_hi + P_hi @ Ai_lo + P_lo @ Ai_hi ``` The second-order low-limb product is omitted. All products accumulate into FP32. The final inverse is converted to BF16 only after the three Newton–Schulz rounds, preserving the existing representation used by the off-diagonal substitution and U/W stages. The existing `sAi` shared-memory storage is reused as temporary low-limb scratch during the iterations. It is not consumed by the downstream code until the loop completes. This change is limited to the SM10x CuTe DSL GDN prefill kernel. It does not change decode or the Triton/FlashInfer backends. ## Accuracy Tests #

title: [Perf] [AMD] smallm_moe_gfx950: MXFP4 kernels at 128 columns per rank
summary: ## Motivation SGLang's gfx950 small-M MoE kernel (`smallm_moe_gfx950`) serves MXFP4 only at 256 intermediate columns per rank (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B at TP4). This PR adds 128, the TP8 shard. 128-column MXFP4 shards reach the kernel in two ways: - #49852 pads Quark W4A4 MXFP4 MoE to 128 for AITER FlyDSL. Its small-M clause keeps 256 for this shape while this kernel lacks a 128 entry; whichever of the two lands second removes that clause. - `SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1` on `main` drops the Quark scheme's padding. Its TP8 calls of up to 56 rows run on AITER today; with this PR they run on this kernel (bf16 activations instead of MXFP4). At 128 columns, on routing captured from a serving run, AITER's `fused_moe` (no tuned rows at 128) takes 1.04–2.5x this kernel's time at 1–56 rows and 0.97–1.02x at 64, so the kernel serves up to 56. On the 256-padded shard, this kernel takes 1.2–1.8x its time at 128 (Speed Tests). title: [RFC] pd: Let decode compute the prompt tail and sample the first token, for any model
summary: ## TL;DR In PD mode the prefill worker must sample the first output token and hand it to decode, along with its logprobs and, under speculative decoding, the draft proposal and hidden states. Decode never runs a forward over the prompt. This RFC adds an opt-in mode in which prefill transfers KV only for `[0, N - W)` and decode runs a real extend over the last `W` prompt tokens, `W >= 1`, then samples the first token itself. It generalizes the decode-side replay that #39963 / #40874 build for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash to any model and any transfer backend. ## Why - **Prefill engines that produce only KV.** Some prefill deployments have no LM head or sampler at all: a prefill engine on different hardware that only produces KV for a GPU decode pool, or a prefill replica that drops late layers and the LM head to save memory, as #39963 does for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash. They cannot be paired with an SGLang decode today, because decode requires the sampled token in the metadata buffer. - **Sampling state already lives on decode.** Grammar, penalties, logprob settings and the speculative drafter all run on decode. Today prefill has to reproduce them for one token: a grammar-constrained request whose handoff token the grammar rejects is aborted in `process_prebuilt`, and EAGLE/MTP decode builds its first draft input from prefill's `output_topk_p`, `output_topk_index`, `hidden_states_tensor` and, for DSA models, `output_dsa_topk_indices` (`speculative/eagle_disaggregation.py`). - **The mechanism already exists for one model.** #40874 has decode "reuse its preallocated slots for a real `[S, N)`

title: [Fix] scheduler: Keep the new-token ratio at its floor after a KV-full retraction
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #46495. With `max_tokens` unset (the OpenAI chat default), `max_new_tokens` is about the context length minus the prompt. After a KV-full retraction the scheduler sets the new-token ratio to `retract_decode`'s estimate, which divides by the survivors' unclipped `max_new_tokens` (`new_token_ratio_tracker.py:41-49`). So it lands far below `NewTokenRatioTracker.min`, which every other writer of the ratio (init, `decay_step`, `reset`) keeps. Admission multiplies the ratio by each running request's remainder clipped to 4096 (`schedule_policy.py:756-765`). So right after the pool ran out it reserves much less decode headroom and admits more prefill work, until the next decode step puts the ratio back at the floor. The issue has the CPU repro and its output on main: the ratio goes 0.0980 -> 0.0117, the survivors' decode reservation drops from 15254 to 1819 tokens, and two fresh 2000-token requests are admitted with 20000 tokens free (none at the floor). ## Modifications `update_running_batch` clamps the estimate to the tracker's floor (`scheduler.py:4471`, one line plus a comment). Above the floor the estimate is used as before: with `max_tokens=2048` it is 0.7422, and a later retraction can still lower the ratio toward the floor. The issue lists two other forms: the estimate in clipped units, or on the clipped remainder. Both change the estimate itself, and `add_one_req_ignore_eos` (`schedule_policy.py:1217-1223`) multiplies the ratio by unclipped `max_new_tokens`: with `max_tokens` unset either would reserve about 47k tokens per running request there, against

title: [Feat] profiler: Emit the forward step span as an NVTX range
summary: ## Motivation SGLang labels every forward pass with a descriptive span, `step[EXTEND bs=8 toks=4096]`, `step[DECODE bs=48]`, `step[VERIFY bs=48]`, `step[DRAFT bs=1]`, built by `build_step_span_name`. title: [Perf] dsv4: Verify-merged mixed step for DSPARK, deterministic C4 top-k ties, and eager ragged indexer
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-mixed-chunk` (#36933), running DSPARK requests are folded into prefill steps, but there each running request only decodes its pending token: 1 token per step instead of the ~4.8 a normal DSPARK verify step yields. Agentic traffic prefills almost constantly (long multi-turn contexts, tool outputs), so running requests spend much of their time at 1 token/step. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 7.0 req/s, ITL p99 is 118 ms with `main`'s mixed chunk vs 37 ms with this PR. ``` One prefill step. P = new request's prompt chunk; r1..r3 = requests already decoding. main: forward: [ P P P P P P P P P P P P | r1 | r2 | r3 ] 1 token each result: r1..r3 advance 1 token this PR: draft: r1..r3 each get W-1 draft tokens forward: [ P P P P P P P P | r1 x W | r2 x W | r3 x W ] pending token + drafts, verified here result: r1..r3 advance ~4.8 tokens each; MoE weights read once for both populations ``` The PR also fixes non-deterministic tie handling in the DSV4 C4 indexer top-k, extends `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_EXTEND` to speculative target workers, and adds an eager ragged indexer path for breakable prefill graphs. ## Modifications Six commits, meant to be reviewed commit by commit. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation LPM falls back to FCFS when the waiting queue exceeds 128 requests to limit prefix matching and sorting cost. This bounds the number of requests considered for cache-aware ordering, not total scheduler work or maximum waiting time. It is opt-in because larger windows can increase scheduling overhead and cold-request waiting time. I have implemented a prototype and tested K=16/32/64/128 on an RTX 4090 with Qwen3-4B. A 45-run sensitivity study used three repetitions of the same 512-request synthetic burst, a running-request limit of 32, output length 16, and three scenarios: constrained cache, sufficient cache, and no prefix reuse. title: [Fix] [NPU] quantization: restore ModelSlim W4A8 MoE TP accuracy
summary: ## Motivation ModelSlim W4A8 MoE initializes its scheme without a TP-size argument, leaving the default at 1. The down-projection compensation buffer consequently retains all 16 checkpoint partials on every TP rank. Its per-channel metadata makes the loader copy those partials without rank slicing, so the subsequent TP reduction repeats compensation. summary: ## Motivation `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors W4A16) has `intermediate_size = 8608`, which is not a multiple of the 64-column tile used by `gptq_marlin_repack` and the Marlin GEMM. title: [Fix] scheduler: keep auto-truncated prompts schedulable
summary: ## Motivation A prompt longer than the KV pool, sent with `--allow-auto-truncate`, is cut to `max_req_input_len` by the scheduler. Two bugs make that request either generate nothing or never run: 1. **max_new_tokens is clipped against the untruncated prompt.** `handle_generate_request` calls `init_req_max_new_tokens(req)` *before* `validate_input_length` truncates the prompt. When the original prompt exceeds the pool, `max_new_tokens` is clipped to 0 and stays 0 after truncation, so the request finishes with `length` and no output. 2. **With `page_size > 1` the truncated request is never admitted.** - `max_req_input_len = max_req_len - 5` ignores page rounding. - `max_new_tokens_for_memory` clips `max_new_tokens` to `capacity - ceil_page(prompt) - page_size - 1`, which is 0 within a page of the pool size. - `PrefillAdder` still needs `prompt + max_new_tokens + page_size < capacity`. - The request stays at the head of the FCFS queue forever and every later request waits behind it. - The same happens without auto-truncate for an untruncated prompt in that last page (e.g. 4080 tokens in a 4096-token pool with page size 16): it passes validation and then never runs. Repro: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, `--max-total-tokens 4096 --allow-auto-truncate --page-size P`. One 8192-token prompt (`max_new_tokens=16`), then a short prompt 3 s later. title: [Fix] hicache: carry routed-experts rows through the host tier
summary: ## Motivation The routed-experts capturer (`--enable-return-routed-experts`) keeps one row per device KV slot, and `get_topk` reads a request's rows through `req_to_token`. With `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, a prefix that comes back from the host tier is loaded into new device slots, but its rows are not. The prefix rows of every host-tier hit therefore come from whatever request used those slots before. Nothing fails; the client just receives wrong routing for the cached part of the prompt. title: [Perf] hisparse: Keep long requests resident in HBM, add an elastic device pool and faster swap-in
summary: ## Summary With a long prompt, HiSparse keeps a 4K-8K token hot buffer per request and swaps the rest in from host every decode step, even when the device pool has room for the whole request. This PR adds faster swap-in kernels and, behind opt-in switches, per-request residency (a long request keeps its whole KV in the device pool while it fits), residency under speculative decoding, an elastic device pool, an exclusive mode in which resident requests keep no host copy (so the host pool can be smaller than the logical pool), and an opt-in fast top-k route with an all-resident decode graph. Apart from the swap-in kernel changes, all new behaviour is behind env switches that default to stock. On GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with 128K-token prompts on 4xGB300, the full set raises decode throughput at B 108 from 744 to 882 tok/s per GPU (+18.5%) and holds batches up to B 148 (1,092 tok/s per GPU), measured before the port to main. ## Changes 1. **Faster swap-in: batched host->device copies and a one-scan plan phase.** - Plan phase: all hit-pass loads are issued up front, and each pass does counts -> one scan -> scatter. Hot buffers that are not a whole number of warps keep the stock plan phase. A differential test found the new plan bitwise equal to stock. - Generic MLA misses are copied block-wide with four 16-byte loads in flight per thread (the stock per-warp copy does one load and its store per lane per round trip). - The skip-layer replay (`copy_cache_planned_kernel`) copies over one flat (request, miss, 16-byte chunk) index. - Opt-in knobs: prefetch-copy grid, wide anchor copy, hit-rate

title: [Perf] hisparse: Remove the per-step host syncs from the scheduler-side swap-in bookkeeping
summary: ## Summary The overlap scheduler prepares decode step N+1 while forward N runs, but with HiSparse the scheduler thread blocked every step on host syncs in the swap-in bookkeeping. The CPU therefore waited for the whole forward graph, then did ~2 ms of batch preparation, and only then launched forward N+1, leaving a 1.5-2.5 ms GPU idle gap per decode step on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4. This PR removes the remaining per-step host syncs so the scheduler overlaps with the GPU again. There is no kernel, policy or stream-ordering change. ## Changes - DeepSeek-V4 branch of `map_last_loc_to_buffer`: the reserved-slot update is computed over all requests with masked writes instead of a `torch.any` early-out and boolean-mask indexing (2-4 syncs per step). title: [Perf] hisparse: Split swap-in host-to-device copies into a wide copy_misses_kernel
summary: ## Summary Kernel-only change to the HiSparse swap-in path. `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` (one 1024-thread block per request and layer) used to copy every missed KV item from the pinned host pool itself, with one miss per warp, so at most 30 dependent host reads were in flight per request while the rest of the GPU idled. On GLM-5.2-FP8 that launch took ~52 us per layer, or 4.1 ms of a 23 ms decode step over 78 layers. The scan kernel now only emits a per-request miss list, and a new `copy_misses_kernel` spreads the copies over many blocks. The Python API, the LRU hit/miss policy, the stream ordering and the device-buffer layout are unchanged; the diff is the single file `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/kvcacheio/hisparse.cuh`. ## Changes - `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` keeps the scan, the LRU update and the `top_k_device_locs` output as before, but writes one `(src host loc, dst device loc)` int64 pair per miss to `miss_list[bid]` and the miss count to `miss_count[bid]` instead of copying. The early-return paths (padded request, warm buffer) write `miss_count[bid] = 0`. This also covers the block-top-k mode (via `NUM_TOP_K_TOKENS`). - New `copy_misses_kernel<BLOCK_SIZE, IsMLA, IsDsv4Layout>`: grid `bs x min(64, ceil(top_k / 8))`, 256 threads. Each warp copies one listed item at a time through main's shared `copy_miss_item` (generic linear layout or the DSv4 page-padded C4 layout, CUDA and ROCm paths), and resolves a late-bound host pool (`host_binding`: host base and row stride) on device. title: [Fix] AITER: take unified-attention decode KV lengths from the spec page table
summary: # [Fix] AITER: take unified-attention decode KV lengths from the spec page table ## Motivation **This makes speculative decoding more effective on the AITER unified-attention path.** EAGLE/EAGLE3 draft decode currently proposes every draft token from the committed prefix alone — the draft never sees a token the draft chain produced, not even its own key. Giving the kernel the real row lengths restores that context, so drafts are accepted more often and each verify step lands more tokens, which is the point of the feature. Generated text is unaffected either way, because the target verify path computes its own lengths: the defect costs throughput, not correctness. Reached on ROCm with `--attention-backend aiter`, a non-MLA model, the Triton unified-attention decode path (always on for a sliding-window KV pool, otherwise `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`), and `speculative_num_steps >= 2` — a one-step draft loop runs no decode forward at all. `init_forward_metadata` builds the decode page table from `spec_info`, then sets `kv_indptr = None` — discarding the only record of how long each row is. `forward_decode` falls back to `forward_batch.seq_lens`, which the draft loop never advances; it bumps `forward_batch.positions` only. The page table for draft backend `i` holds `seq_lens + i + 1` tokens, so the mask cuts away every token the draft chain appended. With `topk > 1` the same mismatch is an out-of-bounds read: the page table has `topk * num_seqs` rows while `seq_lens` has only `num_seqs`. The size of the acceptance gain is not measured. title: [Bug] HiCache `write_back`: prefill admits device KV that eviction cannot free, and the scheduler dies with "Prefill out of memory"
summary: ### Describe the bug With `--hicache-write-policy write_back` and a full host pool, `evictable_size()` can count device KV that eviction cannot free. An unlocked device chain is evictable only through its leaf. When that leaf's device-to-host backup fails and its drop is declined, because a host-only descendant is host-locked (a storage prefetch or backup, a load-back), the whole chain stays on the device. `PrefillAdder` still budgets against available + evictable ([prefill_budget.py#L144-L153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8cb94fcc3f097a5b547dca352131a0b6a05d9ca7/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/prefill_budget.py#L144-L153)), admits the batch, and `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend` raises. The eviction walk logs the declined drops right before ([unified_radix_cache.py#L1320-L1334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8cb94fcc3f097a5b547dca352131a0b6a05d9ca7/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py#L1320-L1334)). The scheduler exits and the server goes down. We first hit it on multi-node PD prefill workers with an L3 tier. title: [Perf] scheduler: Send a finished request's last output before its prefix-cache insert and free its prompt ids after the next dispatch
summary: ## Motivation At the end of every streamed response, two pieces of host work that grow with the prompt length run between the request's last output token and the end of its response stream: 1. **Scheduler: the prefix-cache insert runs before the final chunk is sent.** `process_batch_result_decode` releases a request that finishes in the step (`request_retirer.release` -> `release_kv_cache`, which checkpoints the whole sequence into the radix tree) inside its per-request loop, and only then calls `stream_output`. So the final chunk of every response waits for the insert. 2. **TokenizerManager: the prompt's token-id list is freed before the stream ends.** A prompt given as token ids (the chat-completions path, `/generate` with `input_ids`, or a frontend that tokenizes itself) is a Python list holding one int object per token. Its last references are the request's generator frames, so it is freed when `generate_request` returns: after the final output was yielded, but before the caller ends its response. That costs about 10 ns per token. title: [Feat] eplb: Add ring-buddy expert replication (--ep-dispatch-algorithm ring) for Muse Spark
summary: ## Motivation Muse Spark Open (`MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration`, 256 routed experts, top-8) runs its MoE on every TP rank with the same batch and an all-reduce (EP = TP). At small decode batches the step time is set by the EP rank that holds the most active experts, and routing concentrates on a few ranks often enough that this rank is busy while others idle. This PR adds a fixed redundant-expert placement for that path, selected only through the existing generic expert-location arguments: ``` --ep-num-redundant-experts 256 --init-expert-location ring --ep-dispatch-algorithm ring ``` Each EP rank keeps its home experts (32 at EP8) and also holds the home experts of the next rank ("buddy" copy). For every non-SP forward of up to 256 tokens (decode and DFlash verify), a deterministic pick sends each active expert to its home or buddy copy so that the largest number of active experts on any rank is minimised; larger batches and SP prefill use the home copies. Because routing is identical on every TP rank, every rank computes the same pick and each (token, slot) pair is still computed exactly once; no extra communication is needed. Without these arguments nothing changes, for Muse or any other model. The ring currently supports only the NVFP4 checkpoint with the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernels (SM10x); other Muse checkpoint formats (BF16, INT4) and the Marlin path on Hopper are rejected at startup when the ring is requested. The quantization-excluded BF16 expert layers of the NVFP4 checkpoint are replicated too. ### How the pick balances the load At small batches each MoE lay

title: [Feat] weights: let a custom weight loader reject a tensor update cleanly
summary: ## Motivation A `--custom-weight-loader` used with `update_weights_from_tensor` sometimes receives an update it cannot apply: a tensor for a parameter it keeps frozen, or the same tensor twice in one session. Today the loader has no way to refuse. Any exception it raises propagates out of `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor`, through the scheduler's request dispatcher (which does not catch handler exceptions), and stops the scheduler. The server goes down and every in-flight request is lost. Measured on upstream main (`8d4e1ce4c7`): a custom loader that raises `ValueError` during `update_weights_from_tensor` logs `Scheduler hit an exception: ... ValueError`, the scheduler sends SIGQUIT and the whole engine process is killed (1x H100). ## Modifications - `model_loader/utils.py`: new `WeightUpdateRejected(ValueError)`. A custom loader raises it before it writes any weight. - `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor`: a custom loader that raises `WeightUpdateRejected` makes the call return `success=False` with `"<load_format> rejected the update: <message>"`. The scheduler does not advance the weight version, skips the cache flush if no runner on any rank applied the update, and keeps serving. The weight-update session stays open. Any other exception from a custom loader propagates as before. With pipeline parallelism (`--pp-size` > 1), `WeightUpdateRejected` also propagates as before: each stage handles the request before forwarding it to the next, and only the first stage reports to the caller, so the stages cannot agree on the outcome and a rejection on a later stage

title: [Fix] disagg: Skip PD decode linker writes to window pools prefill never reads
summary: ## Motivation With PD disaggregation, a decode server that has the external cache linker enabled writes its output KV to the shared store, so a later turn's prefill can reuse it. The decode linker's pool group can contain window pools that prefill never reads. DeepSeek-V4 is one example: decode pages its SWA pool, while prefill with encoder SWA bounded replay has no SWA pool in its linker group. Decode still uploads every SWA page, and since prefill never loads them, those writes only fill the store and evict pages prefill does need. ## Modifications - Prefill reports the pools its linker reads (`linker_pools`) when it registers with the bootstrap server. Both the Python and Rust bootstrap servers forward the field to decode. - Decode stores the list on each request. `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.skip_offload_prefix(..., reader_pools=...)` drops every window pool that is not in the list, the same way windows missing from the local linker are already skipped. title: [Perf] gemm: Opt-in table of pinned bit-identical cuBLASLt algorithms for BF16 linears
summary: ## Motivation At decode batch sizes, cuBLAS's heuristic often picks a BF16 GEMM kernel whose grid leaves most SMs idle. When cuBLAS runs a GEMM without split-K, each output element is one fp32 accumulator over K, rounded once to BF16. Other split-K-free cuBLASLt algorithms of the same library build that accumulate K in **the same order** produce the same bits while using the GPU better. This PR lets a deployment pin such algorithms per `(N, K, M)`: an opt-in JSON table, built offline by a tuner for one GPU model and one cuBLASLt version, that unquantized BF16 linears and the BF16 `lm_head` consult before calling `torch.mm`. The tuner keeps an algorithm only if it gives `torch.mm`'s bits on inputs built so that another accumulation order differs with overwhelming probability, and marks the table as checked. A plain random-input comparison is not enough for this: an algorithm that adds K in another order rounds to the same BF16 as `torch.mm` in nearly every output on normal inputs, yet differs on about one output in 10^4 on real activations, which is enough to change greedy text. Per-GPU tables are deliberately not shipped. A `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` is only valid for the cuBLASLt build and GPU it was recorded on, so in-tree tables would go stale with every torch/CUDA bump. The table is generated per deployment, the same way the fused-MoE Triton configs are tuned per device (`benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`), and complements the hand-tuned per-GPU tactic tables already in `unquant.py` (`_BF16_SPLITK_TUNED_TACTICS`, `_BF16_WARP_SPLITK_TUNED_TACTICS

summary: > (auto generated by Claude) ## What A push phase owns `kNumGPU` slots: rank dst's workspace is `[phase][src][slot_bytes]`, and `PushEpoch` strides an epoch by `slot_bytes * world_size`. `tp_qknorm` strode its phases by a single slot. Each phase writes `num_tokens * kNumGPU` float2 packs, so for larger token counts phase 0 ran into phase 1's slots. title: [Refactor] custom-ar-v2: Share one symmetric workspace per group
summary: > (auto generated by Claude) ## What Before this change, every push/pull kernel family outside the custom all-reduce either borrowed `CustomAllReduceV2`'s planes through a global or allocated its own symmetric memory and semaphores. Sizes and launch widths were coupled across unrelated kernels. This PR gives each process group one symmetric workspace that every family requests a share of. - `symm_workspace.py`: one per-group allocation laid out as `[push slots | pull staging | pull semaphores]` plus the rank-local push `EpochCounter`. title: [Perf] dsa: Pin the indexer logits budget before prefill graph capture
summary: [by Claude Code] Split out of #49472. #49943 already covers that PR's main goal, prefix-hit replay under DCP, so #49472 is closed, and this independent part moves here, rebased on main. ## Motivation The DSA prefill indexer splits its MQA logits and top-k into chunks bounded by a budget: `min(static, free memory x SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_FREE_MEM_FRACTION)`. `Indexer._get_mqa_logits_budget_bytes` measures it once, at the first prefill outside capture, and caches it for the process. With breakable prefill CUDA graphs, that first prefill comes after capture, when the graph pool has already taken its memory: - How much the budget shrinks depends on the size of the graph pool. In the Kimi-K3.1 TP8/DCP8 runs behind #49472, the pool took 9-13 GB of the ~30 GB left after the KV pools. That roughly halved the budget, and long-context passes ran about twice as many logits and top-k chunks as on an eager server. With the 17-bucket list measured below on main, the pool is about 7 GB, and the budget drops by about 20%. - Each rank also measures its own budget. Ranks can then split the same pass differently and launch different numbers of kernels, and the slowest rank holds up the others at the next collective. ## Modifications - `Indexer.pin_mqa_logits_budget(device_index, cpu_group, max_bytes=None)` measures the budget, takes the minimum over `cpu_group` and caches it for the process. With `max_bytes`, it only lowers the pinned budget. - `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` pins the budget over the TP group before capture. After capture, it lowers the budget only if it exceeds half of the free memo

title: [Diffusion] Preserve mapped component weights during low-memory offload
summary: ## Motivation Component offload (`--component-residency <c>=component-offload`, and the legacy `--*-cpu-offload` flags) swapped a component out with `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` — a full device-to-host copy of **immutable** weights into fresh host memory on every single swap-out. Three problems this PR removes: 1. **A wasted D2H copy per swap-out.** Inference never mutates weights. Measured on MiniMax-H3's 9.7 GiB video VAE on an RTX 5090: 4.85 s on the first cycle, 0.37 s per cycle after; now ~0 (one device sync + a pointer rebind). 2. **Unbudgeted, kernel-locked host memory.** `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` allocates a *pinned* destination, entirely behind `HostPinBudget`'s back — 9.7 GiB per offloaded VAE that the kernel can never reclaim, RssAnon never shows, and no accounting ever sees. Pinned offload memory now goes through the budget, and a denial degrades to the existing pageable storage without copying anything. 3. **`keep_checkpoint_mapped` weights were destroyed after one use.** A VAE loaded as mmap views into its safetensors file (so a constrained host keeps those bytes evictable) lost the mapping permanently on the first GPU round trip. The mapping now survives: a mapped weight's host copy *is* its mmap view, never replaced. ## Modifications Five commits: 1. **BCG × offloaded-DiT guard** (`runtime/server_args/server_args.py`). Any explicitly non-resident DiT placement with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` fails at startup validation, next to the other BCG rules: BCG captures the DiT forward, every offload flavor rebinds or frees its weight storag

summary: ## Motivation ROCm (with NPU and XPU) keeps one ViT call per request in chunked prefill; the cross-request batch was excluded on ROCm in #32415 after a CI regression. summary: ## Motivation When a gfx1250 accelerator is split into two partitions, the partitions share its links to the other accelerators, while the link between the two partitions is a separate one. title: [Feat] dllm: Support overlap scheduling for FDFO
summary: This PR enables overlap only for FDFO + LowConfidence. FDFO executes one forward pass and one denoise step per `run_batch()`, requiring frequent scheduling. Sync mode completes multiple denoise steps within one `run_batch()`, amortizing scheduling overhead; overlap is not currently supported for sync mode. # Design ## Asynchronous run_batch() Overlap scheduling requires the scheduler to submit `run_batch()` and continue without waiting for GPU results. Some existing paths frequently synchronize the scheduler with the GPU. These paths need to return GPU tensors first and defer CPU consumption. For example, FDFO's `LowConfidence.step()` updates tokens and computes completion flags directly on GPU tensors, without calling `.tolist()` or reading GPU booleans inside the step. `DllmRunOutput.block_tokens` and `block_done` both remain tensors. ## Dependencies between batches Overlap requires the scheduler to schedule batch N+1 before receiving batch N's results. At that point, the CPU has not processed batch N's results. However, the next forward pass must use the updated block tokens from the previous step, rather than the CPU inputs that have not yet been updated. FutureMap adds `dllm_block_tokens_buf`, which stores a full block of tokens per request slot. After batch N's step, it writes the tokens into the corresponding row. Before its forward pass, N+1 reads that row and replaces its block input. This dependency stays on the GPU without passing through CPU result processing. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] mem_cache: Bound cached sliding windows by their share and batch FULL write-back waits under unified memory
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory`, a hybrid-SWA model's full-attention KV and every window sub-pool share one arena. This is a deliberate high/low-water exception to stop-on-fit, so small successive demands do not each pay a trim. title: [RFC] Elastic KV tail: lend idle co-tenant VRAM to the KV cache and give it back on demand (HIP VMM, ROCm)
summary: ## Motivation On small multi-GPU boxes SGLang often shares its GPUs with something else that is idle most of the time: a diffusion server for pictures or video, a second model, a desktop. Today the KV pool is sized once at startup for the worst case of that co-tenant, so most of the time several GiB per GPU sit unused that could hold prefix cache. This RFC proposes an **elastic KV tail**: a fixed base KV pool, plus an optional tail of extra token slots mapped on demand into the address range right after the base with the GPU virtual-memory API (`hipMemMap` on ROCm; `cuMemMap` is the obvious CUDA counterpart). The tail is grown while the co-tenant is idle and handed back within about a second when it needs the memory. It complements, rather than duplicates, open work in this area: - #48202 (device-neutral VMM backend for DWDP): the tail could sit on the same VmmBackend abstraction. - #48106 (elastic hybrid-SWA pools through kvcached): kvcached does not support ROCm/HIP or TP shrink today, and does not give memory back to another process. - #13581 (elasticmem integration). ## Design (as implemented and tested in our patch series) 1. **Base pool unchanged.** It is sized for the full per-request context. Requests never need the tail, so the context limit doesn't change and a shrink never has to refuse a request for lack of room. 2. **Tail = prefix-cache room only.** The allocator prefers base slots; tail slots are used when the base is full of cached prefixes. title: [Fix] qwen3_coder: Preserve streamed text and tool argument order
summary: ## Motivation Valid Qwen tool output can lose its closing argument delta when streamed through the Anthropic endpoint. The result depends on how the same output is chunked, even when generation finishes normally. `Qwen3CoderDetector` currently groups each increment into one `normal_text` string and one list of tool deltas. This loses their relative order. `OpenAIServingChat` then emits all text before all tool deltas. For example: ```text chunk 1: Before.<tool_call><function=Write><parameter=content>first</parameter> chunk 2: </function></tool_call>Between.<tool_call><function=Write><parameter=content>second</parameter></function></tool_call>After. ``` The first chunk emits `{"content": "first"`. On the second chunk, the existing emitter sends `Between.After.` before the first call's closing `}`. The Anthropic adapter closes that tool block on the text transition, so its client receives incomplete argument JSON. OpenAI clients also observe text in the wrong position, even if they concatenate argument fragments by tool index. Related to #42260 and #42353. The latter buffers formatting whitespace in the Anthropic adapter. This change fixes the earlier loss of ordering and also handles meaningful text between and after tool calls. ## Modifications - Preserve ordered text/tool parts in the Qwen cursor parser, while deriving the existing grouped parser result from that same parsing path. - Carry those parts through `FunctionCallParser` and emit OpenAI SSE in parser order. - Retain existing fallback behavior for other detectors, schema-only parsing without a tools list, and `Json

summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. title: [Perf] scheduler: Track num_held_rows incrementally in prefill batch admission
summary: ## Motivation In `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`) and `SchedulerDllmMixin.process_dllm_incoming_reqs` (`python/sglang/srt/dllm/mixin/scheduler.py`), each iteration of the `for req in self.waiting_queue:` admission loop recomputes: ```python num_held_rows = sum(r.kv.holds_kv for r in adder.can_run_list) ``` Because `adder.can_run_list` is strictly append-only across the prefill admission pass and `r.kv.holds_kv` does not change for already-admitted requests until `ScheduleBatch.init_new` allocates pool rows after the loop completes, rescanning `adder.can_run_list` from index `0` on every candidate request causes $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ `r.kv.holds_kv` evaluations as `can_run_list` grows (e.g., under large `max_running_requests` / chunked-prefill / batched prompt workloads). ## Modifications - Track `num_held_rows` and `num_held_rows_scanned` incrementally in `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw` and `SchedulerDllmMixin.process_dllm_incoming_reqs`, scanning only newly appended entries `adder.can_run_list[num_held_rows_scanned:]` on each iteration (`O(1)` amortized per candidate, `O(N)` total across the pass). - Add `TestHeldRowAdmission.test_incremental_held_rows_avoids_quadratic_rescan` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py` verifying that `r.kv.holds_kv` is read at most once per admitted request while preserving exact admission semantics. ## Benchmark Microbenchmarking the admission loop (`100` prefill scheduling passes): - `N = 1,024` admitted requests: `42.0 ms` $\rightarrow$ `0.26 ms` (**161.5

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] DSA: Fix BF16 TileLang shared memory overflow on SM120
summary: ## Motivation On RTX 5090 (SM120), BF16 TileLang DSA decode with `d_v=512`, a 64-wide RoPE tail, and 8 query heads fails on the first decode step: ```text tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 170048 ``` The device's opt-in shared-memory limit is 101376 bytes per block. The v2 kernel defaults to a 64-row tile; its two BF16 KV buffers alone require `2 * 64 * (512 + 64) * 2 = 147456` bytes, before query and scratch buffers. This reproduces with a standalone kernel call, without model weights or a server. Simply setting `block_I=32` also fails: both producer loops still load four 16-row slices, writing 64 rows into 32-row shared buffers. ## Modifications - Make both v2 KV-loading loops use `BI // 16` and assert 16-row tile alignment. - Select a 32-row tile for CUDA BF16 512+64 attention with at most 16 heads on SM12x. Keep the existing tile selection for other architectures and shapes. - Add a regression test for the public entry point with 8/16 heads and the direct 32-row v2 factory, registered on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `1-gpu-small` (RTX 5090). It uses the validated reproducer's seed, tensors, and masked indices. This extends the existing v2 kernel. The FP8 and ROCm partial/combine paths and the zero-RoPE v1 path keep their existing dispatch. ## Accuracy Tests Standalone reproducer, RTX 5090, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, TileLang 0.1.12: BF16 Q/KV, 512+64 dimensions, one query token, 4096 KV rows, topk=2048, last eight indices masked with -1; FP32 PyTorch attention reference rounded to BF16. title: [Fix] pp: Fix mixed-chunk crash under PP speculative decoding
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #42648. With `--pp-size 2`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC=1`, EAGLE/MTP and `--enable-mixed-chunk`, the server crashes once a long prompt is chunked while another request is decoding: ``` _pp_spec_rebuild_verify_input: AttributeError: 'EagleDraftInput' object has no attribute 'rids' ``` After a prefill round, `_pp_prep_batch_result` only restores the `PPSpecRelayInput` when the batch holds the last chunk of a prompt. The decode rows of a mixed batch on a middle chunk therefore reach their next verify round without a relay. ## Modifications Also set a degenerate relay after a mixed batch (one condition). Not tested: `--speculative-eagle-topk` > 1 and other draft algorithms under PP. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Without `--enable-mixed-chunk`, fix vs main: 190.9 vs 190.3 output tok/s (3 streams). title: [Fix] moe: Tune fused MoE up configs against the down config the server pairs them with
summary: ## Motivation `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` times every candidate config under `override_config(config)`. When an override is set, `try_get_optimal_moe_config` never loads the `_down` config, so the down GEMM runs the candidate config without TMA. The server does not run that pairing. It runs the up GEMM with the tuned config and the down GEMM with the `_down` config file, which on Hopper has `USE_TMA: true` and has its `BLOCK_SIZE_M` aligned to the up config. The tuner therefore optimizes for a pairing that serving never executes, and the config it picks can be slower than the one it replaces. We hit this while retuning GLM-5.3 (`E=257,N=256`, fp8 block [128, 128], TP8) on 8x H20-3e for Triton 3.8.0. The only tuned config was the `triton_3_5_1` one, together with its `_down.json`. Measured on the server's path, the freshly tuned up config was **slower than the old one in 8 of the 11 batch sizes we checked, by 4.8 to 11.2%**. ## Modifications - `override_config(config, down_config=None)`: an optional down-projection config. Without it, behavior is unchanged: the down GEMM reuses `config`, which is what the existing LoRA tests rely on. The context manager now also restores state if the body raises. - `try_get_optimal_moe_config`: under an override, returns the given `down_config`. It goes through the existing `BLOCK_SIZE_M` alignment, the same as a file-loaded down config. - `get_moe_configs(..., reuse_up_config=True)`: new flag. With `False`, a missing `_down` file returns `None` instead of falling back to the up configs. The tuner needs this to tell a real `_down` file apar

title: [Fix] qwen3-asr: chunk long audio and batch uneven-length audio items
summary: ## Motivation Qwen3-ASR serves fine for short clips, but long audio is silently truncated, and the fix (splitting into chunks) exposes a crash in the audio encoder batching. title: [Bug] Graceful shutdown: a request that arrives after the SIGTERM drain sent ShutdownReq is never answered, and the server does not exit until that client disconnects
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On the default HTTP server (one tokenizer process, uvicorn), SIGTERM starts the drain in `TokenizerManager.sigterm_watchdog`. While requests are in flight it keeps admitting new ones; once `rid_to_state` is empty it sends `ShutdownReq` to the schedulers, waits for them to exit with a synchronous `time.sleep(0.1)` loop on the event loop thread (up to 15 s), kills the remaining children and asks uvicorn to stop. A request that reaches the server on a connection it had already accepted, in the seconds between that last drain check and the end of the scheduler wait, is read only when the wait ends. Nothing refuses it at that point: `generate_request` registers it and sends it to a scheduler that has already left its loop, so it is never answered. This unanswered request is what this report is about. It contradicts the Python server's drain semantics as written in #47489: "2. Requests are still admitted, and every admitted request finishes." summary: ## Motivation `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-BF16` is a looped (latent-recurrent) LLM: a shared recurrent block is applied `n_recurrent_loops` times between an input and an output block, so a single checkpoint serves several inference-compute budgets. Its residual stream is nGPT (normalize-and-slerp) rather than RMSNorm+add, and attention interleaves sliding-window and full layers with two rope thetas (1e4 sliding / 1e7 full). vLLM landed a native port in vllm#60149. SGLang already serves looped models (`nanbeige`, `iquest_loopcoder`) with per-loop `RadixAttention` virtual layer ids, but had no nGPT-style model, so Dory could not be served at all.
