title: [Fix] gdn: Honour the fp32 radix track snapshot in Triton extend
summary: ## Motivation `hybrid_linear_attn_backend._track_mamba_state_extend` restores a radix checkpoint whose depth is not on the FLA chunk grid (64 tokens) from the per-chunk `h` tensor. `h` is allocated with the activation dtype and is "already rounded to the activation dtype" — bf16 for a BF16 checkpoint. Snapshot-capable kernels avoid that rounding by writing the chunk-boundary state in fp32 into `track_state`, and `gdn_backend` allocates that buffer only when the extend kernel declares `supports_track_state_snapshot`. All KDA kernels declare it. GDN's Triton kernel declared `supports_packed_decode` and `supports_strided_target_verify_qkv` but not this flag, and `fla/chunk.py` dropped the two arguments on the way to `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` — which already accepts them and asserts fp32. So for GDN with an fp32 state pool, a hit whose cached depth was not a multiple of 64 resumed from a bf16-rounded state. Measured on A100-SXM4-80GB, BF16 `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, TP=1, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, prompt 2934 tokens hitting at 2880 (`2934 % 64 = 54`): | branch | `max|Δlogp|` hit vs flushed cold, before | after | output ids | |---|---:|---:|---| | A | 3.756e-2 | **0.0** | 32/32 equal | | B | 1.802e-1 | **0.0** | 32/32 equal | Controls: aligned donation (prompt 1408 = 22×64) was already bit-exact before the patch, and cold-vs-cold is 0.0 with and without it, so the change is confined to the hit path. Also bit-exact at 8k and 16k prefixes, TP=2, and with Qwen3.5-9B. ## Change - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/chunk.py`: accept `track_stat

title: [Feat] clef: Honor an explicit prefill CUDA graph backend
summary: ## Motivation A Clef checkpoint serves one whole prompt as a single extend and never decodes, so the joint-head hook declares **both** CUDA graph phases disabled. A declared resolution outranks raw CLI input, so `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill` is silently overridden for these checkpoints and the prefill graph is unreachable. `/v1/systemone` therefore runs fully eager: on a short prompt the launch train between ~1000 tiny kernels costs more wall time than the GPU work (A100, clef-flash-int8: 70.9 ms per request, GPU busy 30.7%). The prefill body is graph-eligible: BCG captures the transformer stack and replays the outer tail eagerly, and the `EmbeddingGemma` branch in the same file already uses BCG prefill in embedding mode, so this is not a new contract. Opting the phase in also exposed a bug in the breakable runner, fixed by the first commit of this PR. ## Modifications 1. `prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py` (`load_batch`): the static `ForwardBatch` is rebuilt field by field and the tail then runs eagerly on the replayed hidden states, so the prefill-only readout metadata it consumes must survive the rebuild. Forward `decision_layouts` (a joint schema head raises `the joint schema head did not score this request` -> HTTP 500 without it) and `token_indices_to_pool` (setwise readout; forwarding it keeps the rebuild faithful rather than silently falling back to standard pooling if the runner's guard is ever relaxed -- today that guard keeps setwise batches off the graph). 2. `model_hook.py`: keep disabling the decode phase (nothing to capture), but stop overriding a prefill backend

title: [Fix] qwen3_next: dequantize GGUF weight for shared embedding/head
summary: ## Motivation GGUF-quantized `embed_tokens` / `lm_head` modules keep the packed `qweight` and expose no `.weight`. When a GGUF target is paired with a draft model, speculative decoding hands the target embedding and output head to the draft through `Qwen3NextForCausalLM.get_embed` / `get_embed_and_head` (used by EAGLE3 / NEXTN workers). Those getters dereferenced `.weight`, so with a GGUF target they raised `AttributeError` and the draft could not start. ## Modifications - Add `get_gguf_dequantized_weight(module, dtype)` to `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`: returns `.weight` as-is for an unquantized module, otherwise dequantizes the packed `qweight` once into `dtype` and caches the dense tensor on the module. - Route `Qwen3NextForCausalLM.get_embed` and `get_embed_and_head` through the helper (local import, matching the existing gguf import sites in `qwen3_moe.py` / `deepseek_v4.py`). The unquantized path keeps its exact previous behaviour via the `hasattr(module, "weight")` short-circuit. - Add a CPU-only unit test (`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_gguf_shared_weight.py`) covering the dense pass-through, the dequantize call/args, the per-module cache, and the two getters. ## Accuracy Tests - New unit test: 4 passed (CPU-only, no accelerator). - A100 end-to-end (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B Q4_K_M GGUF target + NEXTN MTP draft): the draft starts (previously failed with AttributeError), accept length ~ 3.2 / accept rate ~ 0.73; GSM8K-100 = 98.0 == non-speculative baseline (two A100 runs gave 97/98; the 1-question spread is MTP-on run-to-run nondeterminism,

title: [Fix] [AMD] utils: Cap integrated-device available memory by the device total
summary: ## Motivation On integrated/unified-memory devices `get_available_gpu_memory()` reports `psutil.virtual_memory().available` instead of the device pool, because `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` on those devices excludes reclaimable cache. That value is not bounded by the device capacity: an APU whose GTT cap is below the host RAM reports more available memory than the device can hold. Measured on Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.4): | quantity | value | |---|---| | `props.total_memory` | 108.0 GiB | | `psutil.virtual_memory().available` | 122.08 GiB | | `get_available_gpu_memory("cuda", 0)` | **122.08 GiB** | The value feeds `pre_model_load_memory` and therefore the KV budget in `_profile_available_bytes` (`rest ~= mem_fraction_static * pre - weights`). `mem_fraction_static` is derived from the device capacity (108 GiB) while `pre` comes from host availability (122 GiB), so the budget is inflated by `mem_fraction_static * 14 GiB` and the pool request exceeds the device. Reproduced with `sglang.launch_server` on Qwen3-0.6B with `--mem-fraction-static 0.95 --attention-backend triton` (decode/prefill CUDA graph disabled). summary: # [Feat] disaggregation: Add optional KV Cache compression to Mooncake P/D Serving ## Motivation Long-context disaggregated serving can transfer large KV caches from prefill to decode, making KV transfer a significant communication bottleneck. summary: ## Motivation The Triton path in `_sparse_attn_v4_paged_prefill_triton` currently launches with a conservative configuration: `block_h = 16`, the AMD MFMA minimum tile, and no `num_stages` argument. These are safe defaults that work across architectures, and the file has no `@triton.autotune`, so they apply uniformly wherever the Triton kernel is selected. On gfx1250 there is meaningful headroom in that choice. The kernel spends most of its time on scattered `tl.load` gathers through `kv_indices`, which benefits from software pipelining, and with `index_n_heads = 64` a larger head tile lets a single CTA cover all heads of a token. Profiling DeepSeek-V4-Flash at ISL 8192 puts this kernel at 9.9% of prefill GPU time and the highest per-call cost in the trace (473 us), so it is worth tuning for this architecture. title: [Feat] radix-cache: Add --system-prompt fixed-prefix optimization for hybrid Mamba models
summary: ## Motivation This optimization targets **offline bulk processing** (batch annotation / enrichment over a document library): a large batch of requests is fired at a static model, **every request is fully independent** — single-turn, no conversation history is ever reused — and **all requests carry the identical fixed system prompt**, often thousands of tokens. In this scenario the system prompt is the *only* content shared across requests, which breaks the assumptions the radix cache normally relies on: - **Full-attention models**: the shared system-prefix KV is reused, but every request's unique suffix is *also* inserted into the radix tree on finish. Since no request is ever seen twice, those suffix entries are pure waste — they occupy KV pages and evict useful entries until the batch ends. - **Hybrid Mamba / linear-attention (SSM) models** are worse: every request holds a running state slot plus ping-pong tracking slots for radix donation, so `max_running_requests` is capped to `max_mamba_cache_size // 3` (ratio 3). Each finished request also donates its per-request suffix state into the tree, evicting the shared system-prefix state it just helped create. When the deployment has a fixed system prompt, all requests can share one chunk-aligned boundary state instead: - warm requests hold **1 running slot** (no ping-pong, no suffix tracking/donation) → the mamba ratio drops from 3 to **1**, i.e. **3x more concurrent requests** on the same state pool; - the per-request suffix KV and mamba state are **freed, not cached** → the radix tree stays tiny (exactly one shared system-

title: [Roadmap] Hybrid State Cache Management for Agentic Workloads (FlashStates)
summary: ## Overview This issue tracks the integration of the FlashStates cache-management methods into SGLang, as a series of small PRs that are easy to review. On a hybrid model (full attention next to Mamba / GDN / KDA layers), a cached prefix can be resumed only at a node that still holds a recurrent state. Today the radix cache evicts KV and states separately, by LRU. On agentic traffic this keeps KV that no state can serve, and drops the state that the next turn of a session needs, so the session prefills again tokens whose KV is still cached. FlashStates manages the two together: 1. **Unit eviction.** A cached state and the KV that only it can serve form one unit, kept or evicted as a whole. KV that no state can serve goes first. 2. **Unit-level GreedyDual-Size (GDS).** Evict the unit whose hits save the least prefill time per byte it holds, with aging, so a unit nobody resumes still leaves the cache. 3. **Last two leaves per session.** A session resumes from its newest state. With states checkpointed at the chunk size (as in vLLM), each session keeps its last two leaf states; its older states go first. These are eviction policies in `UnifiedRadixCache`, so they do not depend on the memory layout. They run in both layouts, in parallel tracks: - **Separate pools** (the default; `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` / `--max-mamba-cache-size` fix the split at startup). The main models will keep this layout while Unified Memory matures, so this track brings the gains to current deployments. Unit eviction does not replace the ratio: it still needs tuning per model. - **Unified Memory** (`-

title: [Fix] tokenizer_manager: Reject prompts that tokenize to zero tokens
summary: ## Motivation One request can take a server down: ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text": "", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 2}}' ``` `GenerateReqInput` rejects an empty `input_ids` list with a 400 (#4481), but a `text` prompt is tokenized later, and on a tokenizer that adds no BOS token (Qwen2.5 here) `""` becomes zero tokens. summary: ## Motivation Cross-rank EPLB rebalancing can fail when expert weights contain `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` scale tensors, such as those used by Humming with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. title: [Fix] [XPU] weight_sync: stage serialized XPU tensors through host shared memory
summary: ## Motivation `Engine.update_weights_from_tensor()` crashes on Intel XPU, so online RL training (GRPO/RLHF through verl and similar trainers) cannot push weights into a colocated engine after each `optimizer.step()`. Inference is unaffected. PyTorch has no XPU tensor IPC: `UntypedStorage` has `_share_cuda_` but no `_share_xpu_`, and `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor` has only CUDA and meta branches ([intel/torch-xpu-ops#1678](https://github.com/intel/torch-xpu-ops/issues/1678)). An XPU tensor falls through to the CPU storage path: ``` File "torch/multiprocessing/reductions.py", in reduce_storage fd, size = storage._share_fd_cpu_() RuntimeError: _share_fd_: only available on CPU ``` Under Ray it fails instead with `AuthenticationError: digest received was wrong`, because fd passing needs an authkey that a trainer actor and an `mp.spawn`-ed scheduler never share. ## Modifications **Transport** (`python/sglang/srt/utils/xpu_tensor_shm.py`). Each serialized XPU tensor is staged through a POSIX shared-memory segment. The producer copies device → host, the payload carries only the segment name (174 B regardless of tensor size), and each scheduler copies host → its own device. There is no fd passing, so no authkey dependency. `posix_fallocate` turns an exhausted `/dev/shm` into `ENOSPC` instead of `SIGBUS`. **Segment lifetime** follows who can observe the readers. Each scheduler reads `payload[tp_rank]`, so a payload has one reader per pipeline stage (DP replicas are already rejected for this API, `tokenizer_control_mixin.py:565`). Stage 0's TP0 replies only after it

title: [Fix] rl: One tensor weight payload per engine rank under pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Motivation `update_weights_from_tensor` sends one CUDA-IPC payload per TP rank and each scheduler rank reads `serialized_named_tensors[tp_rank]`. With `pp_size > 1`, stage 1's rank r opens the same handle as stage 0's rank r: it gets stage 0's parameters, which it does not own and skips, so later stages are never updated. title: [Feature] Receive requests during model forward to overlap DFS KV prefetch
summary: ## Motivation We use the Mooncake direct linker with DFS-backed KV storage. On the synchronous, non-overlap scheduler path, a request arriving during an earlier batch's model call cannot start scheduler-side prefix lookup and DFS prefetch until that call returns. This delays the storage work and leaves more DFS latency exposed before the request can run. We implemented an optional path that receives and prepares eligible requests during the current forward, so their DFS reads can overlap that forward and their queueing time. We have observed improvements on a 64K-context workload and would appreciate feedback on correctness risks and whether this would be suitable for upstreaming. ## Implementation 1. Run the current batch's model call on a single dedicated forward executor, explicitly establishing its device, execution context, and forward stream. The scheduler thread continues to own receive sockets, request handling, and radix-tree operations. 2. While the forward future is active, the scheduler receives ordinary text generation requests, matches their cached prefixes, and submits snapshots of the required KV transfers to background DFS prefetch workers. New requests still go through normal admission in a subsequent scheduling iteration. 3. Use separate CPU/Gloo process groups for ingress/lookup and background prefetch coordination, isolated from the model's groups. Synchronize receive-loop participation across the ranks that share receive broadcasts, including when forward completion times differ. 4. Bound prefetch concurrency and staging capacity. title: [Feat] scheduler: add fixed-batch bounded LPM policy
summary: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48408 ## Motivation LPM falls back to FCFS when the waiting queue exceeds 128 requests to avoid matching and sorting the entire queue. Under KV-cache pressure, this fallback can separate requests that share long prefixes, allowing reusable prefixes to be evicted before they are used again. This PR improves the existing `lpm` policy with three complementary changes: 1. **Bound prefix-matching and sorting work:** operate on a fixed batch of at most 64 requests instead of matching and sorting the entire waiting queue. 2. **Limit cross-batch overtaking:** keep batch membership fixed until its requests leave the waiting queue, so later arrivals cannot continually displace earlier requests. Temporary admission skips can expose one additional fixed fallback batch. 3. **Exploit prefix locality within the batch:** re-match and reorder the remaining members on each scheduling pass, allowing requests to benefit from shared prefixes established by earlier admissions. Queue length alone does not establish whether reordering is worthwhile. With a constrained KV pool, bounded reordering can reduce repeated prefill computation. With a larger pool, FCFS may already preserve useful prefixes, leaving little additional cache benefit while reordering still delays some requests. The ungated results below demonstrate this tradeoff. To target cache competition, this PR activates bounded scheduling only when estimated threatened reuse is at least 1.5 times the KV capacity. Otherwise, it retains the existing FCFS fallback. ## Modifications The change stay

summary: ## Motivation `_validate_prefill_complete` derives the attention-DP width from `dp_size` and `enable_dp_attention`. However, `handle_deprecated_dp_attention` runs before it. So the local width is always 1, and every attention-DP launch with `tp_size > 1` fails with "attention tensor parallelism greater than one". This happens even though attention TP is 1. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] runtime: Blackwell/Rubin serving optimizations for hybrid GDN + QSA + MoE models
summary: ## Motivation These are runtime optimizations for serving with MTP speculative decoding on Blackwell / Rubin, aimed at agentic multi-turn workloads. title: [Perf] [NPU] embeddings: Fuse token remapping and vocabulary mask
summary: ## Motivation Vocabulary-parallel embeddings remap global token IDs to local shard indices and construct an out-of-shard mask before the embedding lookup. On the tested Ascend path, `get_masked_input_and_mask` executes 13 elementwise ATen calls, expanding into 16 device compute kernels, including dtype casts. This introduces launch and host submission overhead for small MTP verify inputs: the tested batch of eight requests produces only 32 token IDs per mapping call. Fuse the remapping and mask computation into one Triton Ascend kernel, preserving the eager implementation’s output contract. ## Modifications - Add `get_masked_input_and_mask_npu` under `sglang.kernels.ops.embeddings`, with lazy registry metadata declaring NPU capability. - Route contiguous NPU `int32` and `int64` inputs through the fused implementation. Preserve the existing path for other devices, unsupported dtypes, and noncontiguous inputs. - Produce local token IDs and the invalid-token mask in one kernel launch. Preserve original-vocabulary offsets, added-vocabulary offsets, padding, and exclusive range boundaries. - Return `int64` mapped IDs and a boolean mask. This preserves the eager reference’s dtype promotion even for `int32` input. - Handle empty inputs without launching a kernel and execute on the current NPU stream. - Add NPU correctness tests and a standalone operator benchmark. Embedding lookup, quantization, masked fill, AllReduce, and Mamba commit/stream dependencies remain unchanged. title: [Frontend] Parallelize long chat prompt encoding
summary: ## Motivation A rendered chat prompt goes through one `tokenizer.encode(text)` call on one thread. At agentic context lengths this is on the TTFT path: encoding a 200k-token prompt took 240 ms before the request reached the scheduler. This is separate from #30771, which moves the work off the asyncio event loop. That fixes who waits; this reduces the work itself. The two compose. ## Modifications `parallel_prompt_encode` cuts a rendered prompt only at boundaries where independently encoded chunk ids concatenate to the original single-call result, then uses the tokenizer backend's `encode_batch` and Rayon pool. Verified intra-text cuts are enabled only for the exact `Split` regex + `ByteLevel` + BPE pipeline used by GLM and Llama-3-style tokenizers. Added-token boundaries remain available where their matching semantics are independent. Unsupported tokenizer pipelines, post-processors that can rewrite sequence ids (including unsafe `Sequence` children), runtime options, or a serial Rayon process fall back to the original `tokenizer.encode`; tests cover each refusal path. Rayon availability is detected from process CPU rather than caller-thread CPU and cached per PID, so cold-start result conversion cannot disable working parallelism and forked children recheck their own pool. Two environment gates are defined in `environ.py`: - `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE` (default on) - `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE_MIN_CHARS` (default 32768) ## Accuracy Tests External validation produced ids identical to `tokenizer.encode` on 117 real agentic prompts (up to 990k tokens) and 3154 edge/fu

title: [Perf] rust-server: Encode only what a chat prompt appends to an earlier prompt
summary: Closes #50501. Related: #49190, #49193, #44374, #41148. ## Motivation A multi-turn chat re-sends the whole conversation on every turn, and the Rust server encodes all of it again. On a long multi-turn agent trace (Gemma-4-31B, 12,880 chat requests, 16.6K prompt tokens on average), encoding takes 99.6% of the frontend's CPU per request, with a p50 of 46 ms. That time is on the TTFT path of every request. More tokenizer threads (#49193) remove queueing during bursts, but they cannot shorten a single encode: with 64 threads, TTFT was the same as with 4. Neither existing reuse mechanism covers this case: - dynamo-tokenizers' L1 prefix cache (the one #41268 enabled in sgl-router) cuts only after special tokens. This client sends the whole history inside one `user` message, so the L1 cache reused 0.17% of tokens. - toktier (#44374) does not cover `rust/sglang-server`, and it excludes Gemma 4 because Gemma 4's tokenizer pipeline has no pre-tokenization boundaries. ## Modifications - `sglang-processor`: `DynamoTokenizer::with_incremental_encode(path, revision, budget_bytes)` attaches an `IncrementalEncoder`. The encoder serves `encode(text, add_special_tokens = false)`, which is the call a rendered chat prompt goes through. - **Admission**, checked at startup from `tokenizer.json`. The tokenizer must be a BPE model whose only normalization is `" "` -> `"▁"`, with no pre-tokenizer split left after it, no post-processor tokens, and no added token containing a space. The vocabulary entries that have a `"▁"` after a non-space are collected; Gemma 4 has exactly one, `>▁</`. A tokenizer

title: [Feat] [AMD] mori: Run MORI EPv2 dispatch/combine on AsyncLL kernels for TBO
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #40666 (MORI EP V2). Two things kept two-batch overlap (TBO) from paying off for DeepSeek-V4 on AMD with MORI EPv2: 1. **Communication occupied the compute units.** MORI's AsyncLL kernels (ROCm/mori#768, merged) split each dispatch/combine into a send and a receive half and move data with the copy engine (`sdma`) or peer stores (`lsa`). This PR lets the EPv2 dispatcher drive them, so one micro-batch computes while the other's transfer drains. Both micro-batches stay on one compute stream. 2. **TBO silently did nothing with DSpark.** DSV4 turned TBO off whenever DSpark captured aux hidden states. This PR captures them per micro-batch, so TBO runs with DSpark. AsyncLL is opt-in through the existing switches (`--deepep-mode low_latency` or `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`); default EPv1/EPv2 behavior is unchanged. **Related MORI PR:** ROCm/mori#892 gives each AsyncLL op its own SDMA queue (opt-in); this PR turns it on when MORI supports it. Without it, results are correct but TBO prefill is about 11% slower. ## Modifications **MORI EPv2 AsyncLL** (`moriep.py`, `moe_hook.py`) - `low_latency` sends in `*_a` and receives in `*_b`; `normal` + SDMA sends and receives back to back. With either switch EPv2 runs AsyncLL instead of falling back to EPv1 (EPv1 only if the MORI build lacks AsyncLL). - fp4 dispatch falls back to MXFP8 (bf16 on gfx1250), combine to bf16, since AsyncLL has no fp4 or quantized-combine kernels. **MORI dispatcher under TBO** - TBO-only transfer settings (comm stream, full receive buffer) apply only to TBO micro-batches, no longer to every forward

title: [Feature] [RFC] Opt-in `toktier` tokenizer backend: exact incremental and chunk-parallel tokenization on the CPU
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Summary We propose an opt-in tokenizer backend, `--tokenizer-backend toktier`. It keeps each session's token sequence between turns and re-encodes only the appended text plus a short tail, and it encodes long stateless requests as parallel chunks on several CPU cores. Everything else lives in the open-source toktier library (https://github.com/asu-idi/toktier). This RFC is the first step of a roadmap that continues with a worker pool, a GPU route and a second PR for the Rust front end. The design and the measurements are in [our paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19801) (arXiv:2610.19801). ### Motivation Agent sessions re-send the whole conversation on every turn. The radix cache already handles this on the model side, but the tokenizer still encodes the full history on one CPU core, so its share of TTFT grows with the context. In our measurements on SGLang v0.5.19, a Qwen3-8B chat turn with a cached 100K-token prefix reaches its first token after about 145 ms, and 93 to 99 ms of that is the Hugging Face encode. title: fix(jit-kernel): exact fallback for fast_topk threshold-bin overflow (#36807)
summary: ## Motivation `radix_select_topk` in `fast_topk.cuh` treats "at most SMEM_INPUT_SIZE candidates in the threshold bin" as a correctness assumption. The coarse fp16 binning (~2 mantissa bits per bin) lets a concentrated row place far more candidates in one bin — 16K at L=30,938 and 34K at L=65,504 for QSA k=512 (reported in #36807 by @mochgolf). Overflowing candidates are dropped *together with* their fused histogram contributions, so the staged subset no longer represents the threshold-bin population and refinement silently selects from a truncated set: wrong top-k, run-to-run unstable, and no error is surfaced since the output still looks like exactly-k valid indices. ## Fix Keep the fast path unchanged. Detect the overflow (`s_num_input[0] > SMEM_INPUT_SIZE`), then refine by rescanning the full row, filtering candidates by the coarse bin plus the refined radix digits selected in previous rounds (`s_prefix_bins`). No API change, no smem layout change, CUDA-graph / PDL safe. The coarse-stage threshold selection itself stays exact: it runs on the full first-pass histogram *before* any staging truncation, and kTopK (512/2048) < SMEM_INPUT_SIZE (4096) makes a post-truncation boundary unreachable. ## Tests - New regression `test_fast_topk_regression.py` (registered CUDA CI): concentrated rows at L=30,938 / 65,504 x k in {512, 2048} **fail on the unpatched source** (8 failed / 2 passed — wrong rows and unstable selections) and **pass with the fix** (10 passed); non-overflow N(0,1) controls unchanged. - **Update (09-28)**: the regression matrix has since been expanded to 33 cases

title: [Fix] function_call: Drain tool calls stranded in the buffer when the stream ends
summary: ## Motivation `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` emits at most one tool-call unit per delta: a tool name with empty parameters, then that call's argument diff, then the next call. When a final delta carries more than one complete tool call (larger `--stream-interval`, multi-token decode steps), the remainder is left stranded in `self._buffer`, and `BaseFormatDetector.finish()` returns an empty result — the trailing calls are silently dropped. The serving-side top-up (`_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args`) only covers argument bytes of the last *tracked* call, so a stranded call is unrecoverable. Reproduced offline with `FunctionCallParser` directly: streaming `<tool_call>{...NYC...}</tool_call><tool_call>{...LA...}</tool_call>` as one delta emits only `[(0, 'get_weather', '')]` — the argument bytes and the second call are lost — while `detect_and_parse` returns both calls. With fine-grained chunks the second call lands complete in the buffer and disappears at flush. The same loss pattern was already fixed per-detector in #31860 (Inkling) and #33901 (GLM-4.7), and is being patched detector-by-detector in #36129/#40994/#41909/#41914. `JsonArrayParser.finish()` already implements the drain pattern; the shared base default does not. ## Modifications - `BaseFormatDetector.finish()`: re-run `parse_streaming_increment("")` until it stops emitting calls (identical to the existing `JsonArrayParser.finish()`), accumulating normal_text and calls. Termination: every call-emitting pass either consumes the completed call from the buffer or flips `current_tool_name_sent`. Detector

title: [Feat] mem_cache: FlashStates integration for hybrid models: unit eviction, GreedyDual-Size, miss attribution, exact checkpoint
summary: ## Motivation A hybrid model (Mamba, gated delta rule) can resume a cached prefix only where a recurrent state is cached. The radix cache's LRU evicts states and KV separately, so it keeps KV that no state can use and drops states that requests need. This PR is the FlashStates integration for SGLang ([paper](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate), [project](https://flashstates.ai), [code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashStates)), ported onto the unified radix cache. `main` already has a state-only, cost-based policy (#50122, `--radix-eviction-policy state_cost`); this PR's `gds` is the unit-level policy beside it. ## Modifications | feature | flag | what it does | | --- | --- | --- | | Unit eviction | `--enable-mamba-unit-eviction` | Keeps and evicts a state together with the KV only it can serve; KV no state can serve goes first. | | Unit-level GreedyDual-Size | `--radix-eviction-policy gds` | Evicts the unit with the lowest prefill time saved per byte (aged); implies unit eviction. | | Cache-miss attribution | `--enable-cache-miss-attribution` | Splits uncached prompt tokens into `new` / `placement` / `dependency` / `capacity` (response `meta_info` and a metric). | | Exact checkpoint | `--enable-mamba-exact-checkpoint` | With `extra_buffer`, caches a finished request's state at its exact end, not the last grid point. | - All flags are off by default. With every flag off, the branch computes exactly what `main` computes, on the default Rust tree core. Turning on an eviction feature switches to the Python tree core. - Unsupported combinations (HiCache and other

title: [Fix] function_call: Stream prose that arrives in the same delta as the first tool call
summary: ## Motivation When the text before the first tool-call marker arrives in the **same streaming delta** as the call itself, `BaseFormatDetector` drops it. The increment starts parsing at `current_text.find(self.bot_token)`, and when the call completes the buffer is reset to the remainder *after* the JSON — the prefix is never emitted as `normal_text`. Multi-token deltas make this the common case, not an edge case: a larger `--stream-interval` (documented as the throughput knob) and speculative decoding / MTP batch several tokens per delta. Reproduced offline with `FunctionCallParser` on current `main`: ```python # one delta: 'Sure! <tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "SF"}}\n</tool_call>' # streaming: normal_text='' <- 'Sure!' silently dropped # detect_and_parse: normal_text='Sure!', one complete call ``` `KimiK2Detector` already drains text before its start token as normal text (`_locate_tool_call_start`); the shared base detector does not, so every detector relying on `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` (e.g. `qwen25`) loses the prose. ## Modifications - `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment`: at the entry of the tool-call branch, if a non-whitespace prefix precedes the **first** `bot_token`, trim it into the result's `normal_text` and process the call in the same increment (single bounded recursion — after the trim, `bot_pos == 0`). - Scoped to `current_tool_id == -1`, so markup between later calls stays suppressed and cannot leak into content. - Whitespace-only prefixes keep the old drop behavior, so constrained pure-JSON output (

title: [Fix] gguf: keep the batched MoE MMQ experts above index 255
summary: ## Motivation `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/quantization/gguf/moe.cuh` still carries the guard inherited from vLLM: ```cuda if (exp_idx > 255) return; ``` That bound only made sense while the Python dispatcher kept wide MoE models on the per-slot kernel. `fused_moe_gguf` no longer has such a check — it selects the batched MMQ kernel purely on `x.shape[0] > 64` and on the two quant types — so a quantised MoE with more than 256 experts takes the batched path and the kernel **drops every expert block above index 255**. The op allocates its output with `torch::empty`, so those blocks are never written and the request keeps decoding on uninitialised memory. Qwen3-Next (512 experts) hits this on any prefill longer than 64 tokens. This is a correctness bug that happens to be invisible below 257 experts, which is why the 128/256-expert MoE models we do test never caught it. ## Modifications * `moe.cuh`: `moe_q` now takes `n_experts` and rejects `exp_idx >= n_experts` instead of `exp_idx > 255`. The `-1` padding sentinel keeps its existing zero-fill branch; `moe_align_block_size` guarantees every other id is a live expert, so the bound is exact rather than a magic constant. * The 10 per-type launchers (`ggml_moe_q4_0_q8_1_cuda` … `ggml_moe_q6_K_q8_1 _cuda`) forward the new argument. * `gguf_kernel.cu`: each dispatch case passes `W.size(0)`, i.e. the same tensor the launcher already uses for `exp_stride`. No Python-side signature, op schema or `sgl_kernel` API change. ## Accuracy Tests A100 80GB PCIe (GPU 3), Q4_K packed weights, 128 tokens × top-2, bf16, comparing the batched kern

title: [Fix] custom-ar-v2: Finalize symmetric workspaces in registration order
summary: ## Motivation `finalize_symm_workspaces()` allocates every symmetric workspace that is still pending, before CUDA graph capture. Each allocation is a collective `symm_mem.rendezvous` on the workspace's group. Since #49382 it walks the groups in sorted-name order, on the assumption that one order shared by all ranks keeps ranks that share several groups from waiting on each other. That assumption does not hold when ranks are members of different sets of groups: - PyTorch numbers the handle exchanges of a symmetric-memory rendezvous with one sequence counter per process, shared by all groups, and peers look each other's handles up under that number. Two ranks can only complete a rendezvous on a group they share if both have done the same number of exchanges before it. - Sorting by name orders each rank's own groups. Where a shared group falls in that order depends on the names of the groups the rank does not share with its peer. Groups created with `use_local_synchronization`, which `parallel_state.py` uses for groups built at a rank offset above 0, get hashed names, so their name order is unrelated to the order they were created in. Take rank 0 in groups `S` and `P`, and rank 1 in groups `S` and `Q`, where `S` is shared and both ranks requested `S` first. If the names sort as `P < S < Q`, rank 0 allocates `P` and then `S`, while rank 1 allocates `S` first. They arrive at `S` with different counters, neither finds the other's handle, and startup hangs until the rendezvous times out. title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] megakernel-binding: state, pool, prefill-graph and draft-step views for hybrid models
summary: ## Motivation A megakernel plugin attaches to SGLang through the existing `install_megakernel` hook and the `MegakernelBinding` / `EagleBinding` views. That contract can already run a dense model's decode. A hybrid model also has linear-attention (GDN) layers, a sparse full-attention backend, hierarchical-cache load-back and MTP speculative decoding, and for those the current contract is missing: - read access to the state the forward uses (KV and state pools per layer, the attention backend's step metadata, the prefill extend data); - a way for the plugin to keep its own recurrent verify state, sized, reset and committed by SGLang at the right points. This PR adds those pieces as a generic interface. It has no model names and no per-operation hooks in model files: when a megakernel covers a step, the plugin runs the whole forward of that step, and SGLang only hands it views and calls it at fixed points. Without a plugin, or when the spec does not cover a step, nothing changes. ## Modifications The PR is standalone on `main`. title: [Fix] scheduler: backport no_grad CUDA graph capture (#43854) to amd_march

title: [Fix] [AMD] sgl-kernel: backport wave32 DSA top-k (#41687) to amd_march
summary: ## Motivation On `amd_march`, the DSA indexer top-k kernels in `include/hip/dsa_topk_coop.cuh` hard-code `kWaveSize = 64`. On RDNA (wave32), every wave-level scan and ballot in them is wrong, so `fast_topk*` / `fast_topk_transform*` / `deepseek_v4_topk*` return wrong indices. On unmodified `amd_march`, `tests/test_topk.py` gives `157 failed, 5 passed` on both gfx1100 (W7900D) and gfx1201 (R9700), for example: ``` E AssertionError: wrong_values=92, max_permit_error=5 ``` `main` already fixed this in #41687. That PR selects `kWaveSize` by arch macro and traps if the launched wavefront size disagrees. title: [Fix] constrained: Keep grammars that allow no token from crashing the server
summary: ## Motivation One constrained-decoding request can take down the whole server. The request only needs a grammar that reaches a state where no token is allowed. Two examples that reach it from the public API: - An OpenAI `response_format` JSON schema whose `$ref` only points back to itself: `{"$defs": {"a": {"$ref": "#/$defs/a"}}, "$ref": "#/$defs/a"}` - The native `ebnf` constraint `root ::= root`, or `root ::= "a" b` with `b ::= b` (the dead state comes after the first token). XGrammar compiles these grammars without an error. In the dead state `fill_next_token_bitmask` writes an all-zero row. Applying that row sets every logit to `-inf`, `softmax` turns the row into NaN, and `torch.multinomial` in the torch top-k/top-p sampler hits a device-side assert: ``` TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel: Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. File ".../srt/layers/sampler.py", line 838, in top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch sampled_index = torch.multinomial(probs_sort, num_samples=1) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered SIGQUIT received. ... kill_process_tree called ``` The scheduler exits and every in-flight and later request fails until the server is restarted. With greedy sampling the same request does not crash. `argmax` over an all `-inf` row returns token 0, the grammar rejects it, and the request is aborted with garbage output ("!!"). Related: #27618 reported that `torch.multinomial` can crash the scheduler, and its notes say no request-level trigger was known. This PR gives one and fi

title: fix(attention): convert flashinfer base-2 LSE to natural log in chunked-prefix MLA merge
summary: ## Motivation `FlashInferMhaChunkKVRunner.forward` feeds the per-layer LSE of MLA chunked-prefix attention into `sgl_kernel.merge_state_v2`. title: O(1) slot allocation in DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()
summary: ## Motivation `DecodeReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py`) has the same free-slot bookkeeping shape as `ReqToTokenPool.alloc()` (fixed in [#32208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32208)), and the same drawback: it selects free request-slots from the **head** of `self.free_slots` and rebuilds the list from the remainder (`self.free_slots = self.free_slots[need_size:]`). CPython slicing always allocates a new list and copies the surviving `PyObject*` pointers, so this line is O(len(free_slots)) — proportional to how many free slots *remain*, not to how many are being allocated (`need_size`). This pool is decode-side-specific to PD disaggregation: unlike plain `ReqToTokenPool`, it also carries slots for requests that are pre-allocated or mid-transfer from the prefill side (`_alloc_size = size + pre_alloc_size + 1`), so at steady state under high concurrency `free_slots` is not just pool-sized but *larger* than the running-request cap, and stays long precisely in the regime PD disaggregation is meant to help (high concurrency headroom, trickle admission per scheduler step). `alloc()` runs once per scheduler step that admits new decode-side requests, on the single-threaded scheduler process that gates GPU dispatch — so this is wasted allocation-dominated CPU cost on every scheduler iteration, worse than the non-PD case because `pre_alloc_size` inflates the pool further. `free()` is already O(1) amortized (`self.free_slots.append(...)`) and is unaffected. ## Modifications - Pop from the **tail** of `free_slots` instead of the head (`sel

title: [Fix] scheduler: Publish KV events on every decode step
summary: ## Motivation With `--kv-events-config`, a KV-aware router (sgl-router, or Dynamo) builds its view of each worker's cache from the BlockStored / BlockRemoved stream. During decode, the scheduler publishes that stream only every `decode_log_interval` steps (40 by default). Blocks inserted when a request finishes, and blocks evicted to make room for decode, reach the router up to 40 steps late, and a follow-up turn that arrives in that window is routed on a stale view. Prefill publishes after every batch, so mixed workers partly hide this. PD decode workers run only decode batches, so they always lag. ## Modifications `report_decode_stats` called `publish_kv_events()` after its periodic early return, so 39 of 40 decode steps skipped it. The call now runs before that return, so every decode step publishes, as every prefill batch already does. On ranks without a publisher it is a no-op, and a step with no events costs one `take_events()` call. ## Accuracy Tests New case in `test/registered/unit/observability/test_forward_pass_metrics.py`: a real `SchedulerKvEventsPublisher` behind the metrics reporter, one queued event, one decode step that is not a log step. - main: `AssertionError: Lists differ: [] != [[<object ...>]]` (nothing published) - this PR: passes (the file: 34 passed) CPU only. I have not measured the effect on a live router. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: one extra queue drain per decode step, on the publishing rank only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribut

title: [Feat] tokenizer: await toktier's worker pool in TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts
summary: ## Motivation With the toktier backend (#44373, which this PR stacks on) the encode still runs in the tokenizer manager's process, on the event loop's thread. One long encode then holds the loop, and a short session append waits behind a whole long request. toktier ships a worker pool for this. With `TOKTIER_SGLANG_SESSION_KEY=contextvar`, keyed requests go to a home worker that holds their session state. Stateless requests (every request in `off` mode, or a long keyless one in `contextvar` mode) enter a shared shortest-first queue, cut into chunks once they reach `TOKTIER_SGLANG_SCHED_CHUNK_MIN_CHARS` characters (131072 by default). In the default `auto` mode each request is a content lookup on a worker chosen from the start of the text, never chunked, with the same ids. A request the pool cannot answer is encoded in process as before. The pool lives in toktier; SGLang needs one hook to await it. The design and the measurements are in [RFC #44374](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44374), roadmap item 2, and in the [Delta Tokenizer paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19801) (arXiv:2610.19801), §4.5 and §4.6. ## Modifications One hunk in `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts`. When the backend is `toktier` and the input is plain text (a string or a list of strings), the method awaits `toktier.integrations.sglang.tokenize_texts_with_pool`, which returns `(input_ids, None)`. With any other input (cross-encoder pairs, EmbeddingGemma, an empty string), or with no pool running, the call returns `None` and the method continues unchanged. title: [Feat] tokenizer: add an opt-in toktier backend (exact per-session repair, chunk-parallel CPU encode)
summary: ## Motivation Agent sessions re-send the whole conversation on every turn. The radix cache handles that on the model side, but the tokenizer still encodes the full history on one CPU core, so its share of TTFT grows with the context. On SGLang v0.5.19, a Qwen3-8B chat turn with a cached 100K-token prefix spends 93 to 99 ms of its 145 ms TTFT in the Hugging Face encode. More cores do not shorten a single encode, and a faster serial encoder still re-encodes the whole history every turn. This PR adds an opt-in backend, `--tokenizer-backend toktier`. It keeps each session's token sequence between turns and re-encodes only the appended text plus a short tail, and it encodes long stateless requests as parallel chunks on several CPU cores. Both paths return exactly the ids the loaded Hugging Face tokenizer returns from scratch, and any request for which the backend cannot establish this goes to that tokenizer unchanged. The design and the measurements are in the RFC and in two papers: [TokTier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29678) (arXiv:2607.29678) and [Delta Tokenizer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19801) (arXiv:2610.19801, which has the SGLang end-to-end results). Design RFC: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44374 (#44374) ## Modifications Three hunks in two files, wired like the `fastokens` branch, plus an optional extra and a unit test. Nothing changes unless the option is given. - `arg_groups/fields/serving.py`: `toktier` as a third `tokenizer_backend` choice. - `managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: `init_tokenizer_and_processor` wraps the loaded tokenizer with `toktier.int

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Key decode-offloaded KV pages by bigrams under EAGLE
summary: ## Motivation With PD disaggregation, `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` and EAGLE / EAGLE3 / MTP, no page the decode instance offloads to L3 is ever hit by a later lookup. The next turn recomputes the generated tokens' KV, and the decode-side writes only cost IO and storage. Under EAGLE the prefill tree keys pages by token bigrams, and so does the storage lookup. The decode offload manager hashed plain tokens, so its keys match no lookup. It also assumed the prefill stored `N // P * P` prompt tokens. A bigram key over N tokens has N - 1 entries, so the prefill stores `(N - 1) // P * P`, and when N is a multiple of the page size one page is written by neither side. ## Modifications - Read `is_eagle` from the speculative algorithm at init, the same expression `kv_cache_builder.py` passes to the prefill tree. Under EAGLE each hashed span carries one lookahead token. - `_prefill_offloaded_len` subtracts one token under EAGLE before page-aligning. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve early TransferInfo across bootstrap room clear
summary: ## Motivation In disaggregated serving with Mooncake, the prefill `bootstrap_thread` (in `MooncakeKVManager.start_prefill_thread`) receives decode-side `TransferInfo` messages over ZMQ asynchronously from the prefill scheduler thread. If Request 2 (`r2`) reuses the same `bootstrap_room` and its decode `TransferInfo` arrives at `bootstrap_thread` before `r1_sender.clear()` runs: 1. `bootstrap_thread` writes `r2`'s `TransferInfo` into `self.transfer_infos[room]` and calls `self.update_status(room, KVPoll.WaitingForInput)`. 2. title: [Fix] inkling2: Ignore the Hub ModelOpt quantization_config stub
summary: ## Motivation On 2026-11-13 the published `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small` and `Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8` checkpoints gained a stub in `config.json`. Its only purpose is to make the Hub count parameters: ```json "quantization_config": {"quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "NVFP4"} // MXFP8 for the MXFP8 checkpoint ``` The real per-tensor precision is still in `hf_quant_config.json` (`quant_method: inkling2`). Every cookbook command now fails at launch on the current checkpoint, in two stages: 1. `ModelConfig.hf_quant_config` is built from the stub. The MegaMoE token-budget check (`mega_moe_needs_token_budget`) sees `FP4` and treats the experts as having no fallback, so the cookbook's `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096` is rejected: `ValueError: ... requires SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK to cover ... required_per_rank=16384`. 2. With the cap raised, quantization detection picks `modelopt_fp4` and the model refuses it: `ValueError: Inkling2 requires its checkpoint precision metadata`. #50585 (for #50583) fixes stage 2 by changing quant-method precedence. `hf_quant_config` still carries the stub, though, so stage 1 still blocks the cookbook command. This PR removes the stub at its source, so every reader of `quantization_config` sees the checkpoint as it was before the Hub edit. ## Modifications - `Inkling2MMConfig.__init__` drops a `quantization_config` whose `quant_method` is `modelopt`. title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Fix Triton cache flooding in aiter backend
summary: # Fix Triton cache flooding in DSA `aiter` backend (`_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel`) ## Summary When serving a DSA model (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x FP8) with the `aiter` prefill/decode kernels: ``` --attention-backend dsa --dsa-prefill-backend aiter --dsa-decode-backend aiter ``` the Triton compilation cache under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/triton/` grows without bound — tens of thousands of kernel directories written during a benchmark sweep. As the cache fills, filesystem operations slow the container down over time. One of the two offending kernels lives in this repo. The issue does **not** reproduce with `--dsa-*-backend tilelang` (never calls this kernel) or with non-DSA models like DeepSeek-R1 (never enters this backend). ## Root cause `_get_valid_kv_indices_kernel` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_kernel.py` declared the batch size as a `tl.constexpr`: ```python @triton.jit def _get_valid_kv_indices_kernel( page_table_ptr, kv_indptr_ptr, kv_indices_ptr, bs: tl.constexpr, # baked into the compiled artifact topk: tl.constexpr, ): ``` Triton bakes each `constexpr` value into a separately compiled artifact, so a new kernel is compiled — and a new cache directory written — for **every distinct batch size** the kernel is launched with. Under continuous batching the decode/extend batch size changes on almost every step, so this recompiles continuously and floods the cache. Worse, `bs` was **never referenced** in the kernel body — the launch grid `(bs,)` already encodes the batch dimension via `tl.program_id(0)`. It was pure dead specialization. The other constex

title: [diffusion] feat: TeaCache coefficient calibration
summary: ## Motivation TeaCache is already implemented in sglang, but it only works for models that ship calibrated polynomial `coefficients` and a `teacache_thresh`. There is no tool in the repo to produce them, so any model without hand-copied upstream coefficients simply cannot use TeaCache — LongCat-Image had none, `Wan2_2_T2V_A14B_SamplingParam` shipped no `teacache_params` at all, and MiniMax-H3 rejected `enable_teacache` outright. This PR adds the missing calibration path, and uses it to enable TeaCache on LongCat-Image (T2I and Edit), Wan2.2-T2V-A14B and MiniMax-H3. On LongCat-Image-Edit this is a ~1.98x denoise speedup that was previously unreachable. Three things blocked doing this cleanly, all fixed here: 1. Calibration needs >=50 diverse prompts to be stable, which is too slow on one GPU, so recording has to be shardable and mergeable across GPUs. 2. MoE dual-transformer models (Wan2.2) need one polynomial per expert; `TeaCacheParams` only had a single shared set. 3. MiniMax-H3 packs video and audio at different timesteps in a single forward, so it has no single-timestep lossless TeaCache contract and simply raised on `enable_teacache`. It needs an opt-in lossy variant rather than the lossless one. **Docs** — `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/teacache.mdx` New "Generating Coefficients (Calibration)" section: what is recorded and fitted, the >=50-diverse-prompt warning, single-GPU and sharded multi-GPU commands, the output format (single vs MoE `high`/`low`), how to wire values into a `SamplingParams` subclass, and how to enable TeaCache at inference. title: [Feat] simulator: Estimate energy from a measured power calibration
summary: ## Motivation The simulator predicts step latency, so it can compare serving configurations on TTFT, TPOT and throughput, but not on energy. The usual shortcut is TDP times time. I measured Qwen3-8B on one H100 (700 W limit), and the shortcut's error depends heavily on load: - At batch 1, decode draws about 422 W, so TDP times time overstates its energy by 1.66x. - At batch 128 and above, it is within 2%. So comparing configurations by energy needs power that follows the batch. This PR adds optional energy estimates from a measured power calibration. It is off unless the simulator config has `predictor.energy`, so existing runs are unchanged. ## Modifications - `time_predictor/energy.py` (new): - `EnergyPredictor` wraps any latency predictor (`aisimulate`, `ml`, `replay`). - Each forward step is charged its phase's calibrated power times its predicted latency. That power is linear in the existing 18 ML batch features (optionally `log1p_`), clipped to [idle, power limit]. - Time between steps on the simulated clock is charged at idle power. The GPU doesn't drop to idle the moment a step ends, so an optional `active_gap` charges the first `max_s` seconds of each gap at its own power. - The calibration is a small JSON file decoded into strict msgspec structs. Unknown fields and feature names are rejected. - `simulation/manager/config.py`: wraps the configured predictor when `predictor.energy.calibration_path` is set, and validates that block. - `simulation/sglang/scheduler.py`: one line after the existing `metrics.update(...)` adds `energy_j_per_output_token`. - New `metrics.j

title: [Fix] marlin: Apply the up projection's own global scale in NVFP4 MoE
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48930. The FP4 Marlin MoE kernel takes one w13 global scale per expert, so `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` gives it the gate's (w1) and drops the up's (w3), with a one-time warning. Every expert whose two scales differ then has its up projection dequantized with the gate's scale. Marlin is the default NVFP4 MoE runner up to Hopper GPUs, and the GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 exports on the Hub have differing gate and up scales in about 70% of their experts (up to 10x). ## Modifications - `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` (Marlin branch): when an expert's w1 and w3 `weight_scale_2` differ, it keeps their ratio, up / gate, per local expert in `layer.w13_up_scale_ratio`. The kernel still gets the gate's scale. Checkpoints whose two scales match get no ratio and run as before. - `MarlinMoeQuantInfo` carries the ratio (`w13_up_scale_ratio`), and the Marlin runner passes it to `fused_marlin_moe` (`w1_up_scale_ratio`), which rescales the up half of the GEMM1 output by each row's expert ratio, in fp32, before the activation. This is exact up to the rounding of the GEMM1 output: a global scale is a per-expert factor on the up projection's output, so nothing is requantized. - The ratio is indexed by the top-k ids the kernel gets, which are local expert ids: with expert parallelism the standard dispatcher has already mapped global ids to local ones (and marked other ranks' experts with -1, which keep a ratio of 1). title: [Feat] hicache: Support Mooncake L3 in buffer_only mode under logical-page KV sharding
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` supports HiCache host offload, but no in-tree storage backend can serve a KV-sharded pool. The storage path addresses whole pages through the logical host indices, while each shard rank holds only its own pages as local rows. #50370 added an extension point for out-of-tree backends; this PR uses it for Mooncake in `buffer_only` mode. ## Modifications - **Own pages only.** `MooncakeStore` reads and writes only this rank's pages of every v1 (KV) and v2 (sidecar, e.g. the DSA indexer) batch, as owner-local host rows. A page another rank owns reports success: the controller already MIN-reduces prefetch completion across the CP and TP groups, so the agreed prefix is where the first rank failed. - **Writers.** Every shard rank is a storage writer; under CP, the first attention-TP rank of each CP rank writes. MLA keys already carry no rank, so any owner can read a page another owner wrote. - **Config checks.** Sharded storage requires `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only`, because only buffer mode draws a hit's host bounce in its chain's owner phase. Mooncake storage under sharding is limited to MLA models, since MHA keys name the TP rank. Launch and runtime attach run the same check, and the DSA sharding check now accepts `buffer_only` with a storage backend. - **Sidecar fence.** `validate_buffer_only_stack` compares a sharded source's sidecars against its owner-local size. Related: #46943 covers Mooncake/file storage in `cache` mode for non-DSA models. ## Accuracy GLM-5.2-NVFP4 PD: prefill TP4 with prefill CP4, KV sharding and HiCach

summary: ## Motivation `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` (logical-page KV sharding on PD prefill workers) rejects `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` at startup, so a prefill-CP deployment cannot combine the larger sharded device cache with direct L3. Any owner can read a page another owner wrote. - **Own pages only.** `DevicePoolGroup.owned_transfers` narrows load and offload transfers to this rank's pages and translates logical slots to owner-local rows. Every shard rank writes its own pages. - **Rank-consistent queues.** A rank that owns none of a request's pages still queues an empty load, so all ranks report the same verdict. It also queues an empty offload behind earlier offloads, so offload results stay in node order. title: [Fix] ollama: Preserve text in streams
summary: ## Motivation With `--incremental-streaming-output`, the tokenizer manager sends only the new text in each chunk. The Ollama `/api/chat` and `/api/generate` routes still treat each chunk as the full reply. They skip as many characters as the previous chunk contained, so parts of the response disappear. Both routes also drop new text from the last chunk. For a reply that ends in one chunk, the client gets no text at all. #17961 reported this last-chunk case earlier and was closed as stale. Fixes #42141. ## Modifications Use the tokenizer manager's output mode in both routes. Pass incremental text through as it is. For cumulative text, keep the existing suffix calculation. If the last chunk has new text, send that text before the usual empty `done: true` event. An empty last chunk still produces just the completion event. ## Accuracy Tests Added CPU tests for both routes and both output modes. They cover an empty last chunk, text in the last chunk, a single chunk, Unicode, empty chunks, and repeated text. The tests use the real handlers and response schemas with a fake tokenizer manager. ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/entrypoints/ollama/test_streaming.py -v pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ollama/serving.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/ollama/test_streaming.py ``` All six test methods passed (24 subcases). title: [Fix] marlin: Decode E4M3 subnormal NVFP4 block scales exactly with bfloat16 activations
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48906. On SM80 to SM9x GPUs SGLang serves NVFP4 linear and MoE layers through FP4 Marlin by default. `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` turns each E4M3 block scale into an S0E5M3 byte (scale * 2^7, 5-bit exponent with bias 15). With bfloat16 activations, `dequant_fp8_scales<nv_bfloat162, kFE4M3fn>` turns that byte into bfloat16 by moving its top bit to the top of the bfloat16 exponent. That is right only when the top bit is 1, i.e. for block scales of 2^-6 or more. Every E4M3 subnormal block scale (2^-9 to 7 * 2^-9) decodes to about 2^-112 of its value, and the weights of its block become 0. The float16 specialization reads the same byte back as the top byte of a half and decodes every scale exactly. E4M3 subnormal block scales occur in real checkpoints: - in normalized ModelOpt exports, in tensors whose largest block scale is near 448. nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 has 165,266 of them, in five tensors whose largest block scales are 320 to 448. They hold 2,236,146 nonzero weights, almost all in layer 0's `q_proj` and `k_proj`. - in checkpoints exported with a global scale of 1, where many block scales are small (#44998). #45031 ports vLLM's host-side power-of-two rescale for the second case. It does not help the first one: when a layer's largest block scale is above 224, the rescale factor is 1, so its subnormal scales stay below 2^-6. It also sets every scale below 2^-6 to zero for float16, which decodes them exactly today. title: [Fix] sampling: Feed the relayed last token to penalizers under the overlap scheduler
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #41124. With the overlap scheduler (the default), frequency, presence and repetition penalties are applied one token late. For output token `i` they count `[prompt[-1]] + output[:i-1]` instead of `output[:i]`. The first decode step penalizes the last prompt token, and every later token is penalized a step late. The issue shows this with logprobs against a float32 HF recompute; `--disable-overlap-schedule` is correct. Cause: `prepare_for_decode` feeds `req.output_ids[-1]` to the penalizers. Under overlap the next batch is prepared before the previous token is processed, so that value trails by one. The real token is only on the device (`future_map`) until `resolve_forward_inputs` gathers it. ## Modifications - Under overlap, `prepare_for_decode` marks the batch (`penalty_update_pending`) instead of feeding the stale token. - `resolve_forward_inputs` feeds the gathered tokens to the penalizers right after the gather, before `copy_for_forward()` snapshots the penalty buffers. - Mixed chunked prefill: the same feed goes to the running decode rows only (`cumulate_output_tokens(row_start=...)`, default 0, so existing callers are unchanged). Those rows line up with the running requests because the scheduler only mixes when no running request has a beam group; a beam tail can follow the request rows only in a plain decode forward, which the decode branch slices off with `[: len(batch.reqs)]`. - The non-overlap path and speculative decoding are unchanged. title: [Fix] scheduler: Reserve only the remaining decode when re-admitting a retracted request
summary: ## Motivation After a decode OOM retraction, a retracted request is re-admitted by re-prefilling its prompt plus the tokens it already generated. Admission then reserves its full `max_new_tokens` of decode headroom again, so those tokens are counted twice. The pass that re-admits it can end with NO_TOKEN, and fresh requests behind it wait for a later pass although the pool has room. With 8000 free tokens, a retracted request (1000 prompt, 3000 generated, `max_new_tokens=4000`) is charged 8001, and a 1500 + 500 request that fits beside it is refused. ## Modifications The gate in `add_one_req` already charges min(max(max_new_tokens - generated, 0), CLIP), the formula of `_swa_new_tokens`. The commits and the other admission paths charged min(max_new_tokens, CLIP). This renames `_swa_new_tokens` to `_remaining_new_tokens` and uses it wherever `PrefillAdder` prices future decode: whole, chunked and ignore_eos admissions and their commits (a chunked request's deferred decode included), the demand-priced selection and commit from #49300 and #48012, the HiCache load-back reshape, dLLM staging on the fixed pool, the running-batch offset, and the priority-preemption demand. Preemption also sizes a newcomer's extend as `origin_input_ids + output_ids` less its prefix. It runs before `init_next_round_input` refreshes the fill ids, so a retracted request's fill ids still stop at its last prefill (from the Codex review). summary: Supersedes #49377, which GitHub closed when its base branch (#49370's head) was deleted after #49370 merged. One channel per CU (256 threads, unroll 32) pushes 2 MB slices through a two-slot FIFO in the next rank's memory, behind 64-bit ready/drained counters. The FIFO and its counters live in an uncached symmetric buffer of their own (`SymmetricBuffer` from #49382, as the hier planes do), allocated only where the table selects `ring_simple`: 4 MB per channel, one channel per CU the device reports. title: [Fix] engine: Release pinned host memory before SIGKILL in Engine.shutdown() to avoid a ~20 s node-wide stall
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache on, `engine.shutdown()` blocks driver calls of every other GPU process on the node for about 20 seconds. On 8-GPU B200 or B300 nodes, many mainstream models need only part of a node, so one node often runs several workers, for example two DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash or GLM-5.3-Flash workers. Each restart, scale-down or rolling update of one worker then stalls the others. In our runs, a neighbor's `nvidia-smi` stalled for 20–23 s on every such stop. Once, a separate server's prefill forward stalled for 21 s and its gateway returned 503. `Engine.shutdown()` SIGKILLs the schedulers through `kill_process_tree`. The kernel then reclaims their `cudaHostRegister`ed host buffers (HiCache host pools, the HiSparse buffer), and while it does, other processes' driver calls block. #28779 added a graceful path for this: `ShutdownReq`, then `release_host_resources`. But only `sigterm_watchdog` uses it, so `launch_server` stops are graceful and `Engine` stops are not. Dynamo's SGLang workers stop through `engine.shutdown()` ([prefill handler](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/90f8ad2fff9dd84a3d0b5ae10d449b29dec9b8bc/components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/prefill_handler.py#L95)). **Reproduction** (3 GPUs, about 450 GB of free host memory). title: [Fix] linker: Wait for external linker loads before breakable replays that capture KDA state reads
summary: ## Motivation A breakable prefill CUDA graph that captures the KDA extend runs the pool accessor's layer wait only at capture time, so a replay must wait for in-flight layer loads explicitly. #45839 added that mechanism (`HiCacheGraphEvents`), including a fallback for CPU-future counters, but `_needs_hicache_event_capture` turns it on only when `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is set. The unified-cache external linker loads layer-wise through the same pool wait hook (`LayerWiseLoadCounter`), and it is mutually exclusive with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`. So with the linker on a KDA model (Kimi-Linear class), the mechanism is never enabled: a replay runs the captured KDA layers without waiting for the linker's load, and only the eager full-attention breaks wait. The KDA layers before the first break read their conv and recurrent state before it lands, and the request silently computes on whatever the state slot held. ## Modifications - `_needs_hicache_event_capture` also returns true when the external linker is enabled. title: [Fix] spec: Fix speculative decoding penalty state under repetition_penalty
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49403. Under `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM` (and EAGLE, which shares the code path) a request that sets `repetition_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty` or `min_new_tokens` produces a different completion than the same request decoded without speculation, on the same weights and the same greedy settings. title: [Feat] scheduler: Add waitable request retirement receipts
summary: ## Motivation `/abort_request` currently returns after sending the cancellation. A generation terminal can also arrive before the scheduler releases the request's resources. Callers that need to hand off work or wait for one request to leave the scheduler cannot use either event as a retirement receipt. This adds an opt-in wait for one captured request instance. The first slice is deliberately limited to single-rank, unified text generation with built-in full-attention caches and static pools. CUDA serving validation now covers that narrow scope; it is out of draft for review, and the API and ownership boundary are the parts that most need a maintainer's call. Tracks #48626. ## Modifications - Preserve the default empty HTTP 200 response and existing prefix/abort-all behavior. Waiting requires an exact RID, a cancellation ID and a bounded timeout. - Carry an opaque request-instance token through the existing IPC path. Retries remain bound to that instance after output cleanup or RID reuse. - Reuse the existing abort and RequestRetirer paths. Send a separate control reply only after the request is finished, all host scheduler steps are processed, request-owned rows/state and cache locks are released, and live scheduler holders are clear. - Bound receipt retention to 256 operations and a five-minute retry window. Timeouts and disconnected waiters leave the shared receipt intact; unknown and unsupported results are idempotent too. A control send that fails keeps its route and is redelivered on later scheduler steps. - Keep the feature disabled by default and reject unsupported

title: [Fix] hicache: Continue eviction after a failed file unlink
summary: ## Motivation With a bounded HiCache file backend, one undeletable oldest cache page prevents eviction of every later page. `_evict_one_lru_locked` restores that entry at the LRU head and returns `stop` on OSError. Every later capacity-constrained write retries the same head and is refused, even when another page can be reclaimed. Reproduction on official main 29bcb74a89: fill a 128-byte cap with two real 64-byte files, inject PermissionError only for the oldest file's unlink, then cache another 64-byte page. The new write returns False and the second, deletable file is never tried. ## Modifications Retain the failed entry and its charged bytes at the end of the eviction queue, returning `skipped` so the existing bounded skip loop can try other victims. A failed unlink contributes zero reclaimed bytes and does not invalidate positive metadata. Update the helper's outcome documentation. Two CPU regressions check: - Selective unlink failure: a later victim is evicted, the new file contains the expected bytes, the failed file and metadata remain, and accounting stays at 128 bytes. - All unlinks fail: the write is refused after trying both candidates, no reservation or byte refund occurs, and a later retry succeeds once unlink is allowed. This changes eviction ordering after an unlink failure. It does not retry forever or assume the failed file was removed. It shares the existing skip budget with pending writes. Scope is one file-backend evictor, not cross-process coordination. ## Accuracy Tests Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA hidden; normal SGLang imports with isolated

title: [Fix] function_call: Process every complete tool call in a streamed chunk
summary: ## Motivation Part of the **Streaming tool calls** item in the 1.0 release tracker (#50045). A streamed chunk can hold a whole tool call or several, with batched detokenization, `--stream-interval` above 1, and speculative decoding. Many detectors handle one step per `parse_streaming_increment` call: they send a tool name or an argument diff, and leave the rest of the chunk in their buffer until the next chunk arrives. When the calls come in the final chunk, the rest is never processed. The end-of-stream flush in `serving_chat` only recovers the trailing arguments of the last call it knows about (#31915). For example, on `main`, a Qwen 2.5 or Llama 3 response whose final chunk holds both calls reaches the client as `get_weather` with empty arguments, and `get_time` is never sent. ## Modifications `FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_chunk` now keeps stepping the detector with no new text until a step returns nothing and leaves the detector's buffer unchanged. Detectors are not changed. In the test from #50609, the loop stops after the chunk is processed for every registered parser, in all three chunking modes. With the per-parser test from #50609 applied, this fixes all 18 cases it marks `one step per chunk (#31915)`, across `qwen25`/`qwen`, `hermes`, `llama3`, `trinity`, `ling3`, `mimo`, `glm45`/`glm`, `glm47`/`flint`, `interns1`, `deepseekv3` and `deepseekv31`. The other 10 expected failures have detector-specific causes, and I'll send separate fixes for them. Whichever of the two PRs lands second will remove the 18 entries from `KNOWN_FAILURES`. #41039 (Qwen 2.5) and #32167

title: [Feat] spec-decoding: Tree verify without per-node state snapshots for GDN layers
summary: Closes #50497. ## Motivation Modern state-of-the-art speculative decoding architectures employ a tree draft structure. Examples include EAGLE-4, DDTree, and Sequoia-based approaches. However, for most models, inference kernels are far from optimized for tree draft verification. While benchmarking Qwen3.8-27B, we profiled the target's verify forward with a chain draft (a straight sequence of predicted tokens) and a tree draft (a tree structure where each branch may have multiple candidates for the continuation token, with a higher probability of at least one candidate being accepted). It turned out that the GDN linear attention layers give the highest overhead. In a tree verify, the GDN kernel writes the recurrent state after every draft node to `intermediate_ssm`. Children start from their parent's snapshot, and the commit step copies the snapshot of the last accepted node. Chain drafts already avoid this under `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`; trees could not. The snapshots are not needed for a tree either: the verify can compute every node's output from the state before the draft, and the commit step can rebuild the state of the accepted branch afterwards. We implemented this approach. Across 11 Qwen models it speeds up the GDN layers of a tree verify by 1.33x to 1.94x and the whole verify forward by 1.11x to 1.24x, leading to up to 1.21x speedup in tokens/s throughput. `intermediate_ssm`, 4.8 to 38 GB depending on the model, is no longer allocated. ## How it works For a draft node `t` with parent `p`, a GDN head computes ``` H_t = a_t * H_p + k_t ⊗ d_t d_t = b_t * (v_t -

title: fix(args): floor the derived mem_fraction_static and validate explicit values
summary: ## Motivation `chunked_prefill_size=-1` is the documented way to disable chunked prefill, but it makes the activation reserve in `handle_gpu_memory_settings` scale with `max_prefill_tokens`: `512 + 16384 * 1.5` MiB before the CUDA-graph and DeepEP terms, which exceeds any device under roughly 25 GiB. The derived `mem_fraction_static` comes out negative and the engine dies at memory profiling with ``` ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=-0.05 ``` for a flag the user never set (issue reporter measured -0.05 on a 24058 MiB RTX 4090; I reproduce -0.026 at 24576 MiB and -0.539 at 16 GiB). The same path triggers for any config whose estimated reserve exceeds the device, e.g. `chunked_prefill_size=32768` on a 24 GiB card derives -1.026. This locks the whole 16/24 GiB class (T4, L4, A10, 3090/4090/5090) out of a documented configuration. ## Fix - Floor the *derived* fraction at 0.5 with a warning that names the estimated reserve, the device size, and how to override with `--mem-fraction-static`. The startup profiler already computes a precise minimum viable fraction and raises with a suggested value when the weights genuinely do not fit, so in that case this converts the misleading negative-fraction failure into an accurate, actionable error, and small models (where the model-agnostic 1.5 MiB/token estimate is far above real activations) get a working engine. - Reject an explicit `--mem-fraction-static` outside (0, 1] in `handle_other_validations`, so a bad explicit value fails at argument parsing instead of deep in the memory

summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #50311 * #50310 * __->__ #50309 * #50308 * #50307 * #50306 ## Motivation When a unified-memory allocation needs room, the relief read every band's free and pending pages on the host (`.tolist()`), then compacted from those lists. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kda: Use 8-row value tiles for the FP32-state packed decode on SM90 and SM10x
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #47893, as discussed in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47893#issuecomment-6619597334. `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` launches its Triton kernel with BV = 32 V rows per program. With an FP32 state on SM90 and SM10x, BV = 8 (4x the programs, 8 state rows each) cuts the kernel time by 9-40% on H20 and 1-25% on B300. BV only sets how the V rows are split across programs, so output and state stay bit-identical. With GLM-5.3-Flash on attention DP8, median ITL drops 1.0-1.2% on H20 and 1.0-1.6% on B300 at concurrency 64-128. Since #47893 this kernel runs for: - safe-gate layers when the fused decode kernel does not take the step. For GLM-5.3-Flash that means 32 or 64 KDA heads per rank (TP2, TP1, attention DP), and on SM90 also 8 or 16 heads from 2048 (token, head) blocks; - layers without the safe gate below batch 8. From batch 8 the CUDA row-streaming kernel takes the shapes it covers; this PR does not touch it. We measured GLM-5.3-Flash shapes only (K = V = 128, 8-64 heads). ## Modifications - `_kda_packed_decode_value_tile()` returns 8 for an FP32 state on compute capability 9.x and 10.x, and 32 otherwise. summary: ## Motivation On Blackwell, MiniMax-M3.1's MXFP8 dense GEMMs (attention projections, shared experts, draft) resolve to the FlashInfer CuTe-DSL backend by default. That backend compiles one kernel per tactic in every new process. In FlashInfer 0.7.x those compiles have no on-disk cache, so a warm restart compiles about 53 kernels per rank, most of them during prefill graph capture, and a cold start about 235 while autotuning.
