title: [Feat] [NPU] moe: Add LPLB with graph-stable dynamic EPLB updates
summary: ## Motivation EPLB changes where expert replicas live. LPLB chooses which replica should process each route in the current batch. SGLang already exposes `--ep-dispatch-algorithm lp`, but its solver and probability dispatcher use CUDA, and the ordinary NPU routing path does not invoke the solver. This PR adds the NPU implementation and connects it to dynamic EPLB. For example, if an expert has a copy on each of two ranks, uniform routing gives both copies the same share of that expert's tokens. That can still leave one rank overloaded by its other experts. LPLB includes that fixed load when choosing the two copies' shares. It preserves the logical experts selected by top-k and their routing weights. The implementation follows SGLang's existing LP formulation and uses [DeepSeek's LPLB](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/LPLB/tree/0490f79452f7ef277e814449600b1b1dd4c663b3) as a reference for the count → solve → replica-dispatch pipeline. The device kernels are implemented in Triton for Ascend. This remains a draft. Device routing and graph tests pass, and a matched full P/D serving pair has completed. LPLB is slower in that long-decode pair; the measurements and next test direction are below. ## Modifications ### Latest revision: reuse fixed inputs and keep dispatch inside NPU The NPU routers now call one entry that counts routes, solves the LP, and selects physical expert IDs. Ordinary, hash, and precomputed top-k paths share this entry. The common CUDA probability-dispatch file is restored to the base version. Placement-dependent matrix columns are written only at initialization

title: [Feat] mem_cache: Add an opt-in state-only, cost-based eviction order for Mamba states (--radix-eviction-policy state_cost)
summary: ## Motivation Resubmitting #49430 as an opt-in, as asked there after #50118 reverted it. `state_cost` is a new value of `--radix-eviction-policy` that nothing picks by default, and the eviction code is the same as in #49430. It was renamed from `gds` in `f5d94e391a`, so `gds` stays free for the unit-level policy of the FlashStates integration in #50233. On a hybrid model (KDA / GDN / Mamba layers next to attention), a cached prefix can only be resumed at a node that still holds a recurrent state. The state pool is much smaller than the KV pool: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2x B200 (TP2, `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.9`) gets 419 state slots next to 2,969,600 KV tokens, and each running request takes 5 of the slots. The Mamba LRU drops one state at a time and keeps its KV, so on agent traffic a session that comes back after a tool call often finds its latest state gone while its KV is still there. It falls back to an older state, or to token 0, and prefills again tokens that were never evicted (#36935 described the same thing). `--radix-eviction-policy state_cost` is a state-only, cost-based eviction order for recurrent states, inspired by FlashStates ([paper](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate), [code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashStates), [project page](https://flashstates.ai)). A state's priority is the eviction watermark at its last use plus the prefill it would take to rebuild it from the nearest shallower state (or from token 0). The lowest goes first and the watermark rises to each victim's priority, so a state nobody resumes still ages out. A state right

title: [CI] [AMD] disaggregation: Disable UCX ROCm dmabuf registration for the NIXL e2e test
summary: ## Motivation Since #49603 moved the ROCm image to UCX 1.24 (`929abbbae`) and NIXL `c656976f`, `test_nixl_transfer_engine_e2e.py::TestNixlTransferEngineAccuracy` fails in `setUpClass` on the MI35x disaggregation runners (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49603#issuecomment-6883830388): - rocm10: the decode scheduler gets `hipErrorOutOfMemory` at `schedule_stream.cuda_stream` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43598237271/job/132457289973)) - rocm724: the prefill scheduler segfaults in `hsa_queue_create` from `CUDAStream::stream()` ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43629835467/job/132553830144)) Both happen at the first HIP stream creation right after NIXL's UCX backend registers the KV cache. UCX 1.24 registers ROCm memory through dmabuf by default (`v1.19.x` did not take this path), and on these runners that leaves the next HIP stream creation failing. This is the same failure this step already works around for Mooncake with `MOONCAKE_DISABLE_HIP_DMABUF=1` ("out of memory on rocm10, segfault on rocm720. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion: Read both TP ranks' partial sums in the epilogue kernel (Z-Image, Qwen-Image-2.1)
summary: ## Motivation On a two-rank TP group every row-parallel layer ends in an all-reduce: each rank pushes its partial sum to the other, the two are added, and the next kernel reads the result back. Profiled on 2xH200 at 1024x1024, that all-reduce is 14-18% of the denoise GPU time for Z-Image-Turbo and Qwen-Image-2.1 TP2, and about 105 us of its ~145 us is the NVLink transfer itself; the GPU is otherwise back to back (97-98% busy). ## Change Each rank's GEMM writes its partial straight into a buffer the peer has mapped (the `mm` / `addmm` that `F.linear` lowers to, with `out=`), publishes a sequence number with a stream memory op (no SMs), and the kernel that used to read the all-reduced tensor reads both partials and adds them as it loads: - **Z-Image**: `rmsnorm_tanh_residual_sum2` = all-reduce -> `rmsnorm_tanh_residual` [-> `rmsnorm_scale`], the same expressions. - **Qwen-Image-2.1**: `residual_gate_add_sum2` = all-reduce -> `residual_gate_add`, each sum and product rounded by its own instruction (a plain cast lets the multiply and add contract into one fma and changes the bytes). The transfer becomes that kernel's loads; the reduce pass and one or two epilogue launches per site are gone. - New `device_communicators/tp_peer_partial.py`: two staging slots alternating per call, peer mapping, publish / wait. Both ranks agree before and after initialization, so a failure on one rank sends both back to the all-reduce. - `RowParallelLinear.partial_into` / `supports_partial_into`: the same GEMM `forward` runs, written into a caller buffer. - Engages on CUDA for a two-rank TP group o

title: [Fix] flashinfer: Guard sliding-window attention in multi-item scoring (--enable-mis)
summary: ## Motivation Mitigates #50596 (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/50596). When `--enable-mis` (`--attention-backend flashinfer`) is enabled on models with Sliding-Window Attention (SWA), `FlashInferAttnBackend` currently forces `window_left = -1` in both planning (`FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.call_begin_forward` via `not multi_item_enabled`) and forward execution (`FlashInferAttnBackend.forward_extend` setting `paged_window_left = -1`). Across all three SWA execution paths supported in SGLang (`SWAKVPool` hybrid SWA, 2-wrapper non-hybrid MHA SWA, and 1-wrapper per-layer `RadixAttention` SWA), any query-item pair with logical span `prefix_len + item_len - 1 > window_left` silently computes unbounded causal full attention and diverges from independent `enable_mis=False` evaluation by up to **3.01 nats** on `token_logprobs` (matching `W = 4096` to `0.000000e+00`). Simply forwarding `window_left >= 0` into `flashinfer==0.7.4` is not a valid fix: `logits_mask_multi_item_scoring` in FlashInfer's `prefill.cuh` checks `kv_idx + window_left < idx_in_original_seq` against the physical packed offset before separating shared-prefix vs. item-local tokens, which would falsely mask out the shared query for later items in the packed sequence even when every individual `(query, item)` fits inside `window_left`. Until FlashInfer supports item-logical SWA, this PR enforces a fail-closed, request-level guard: - Allow `--enable-mis` requests whose every `(query, item)` logical span fits within the model's strictest non-negative SWA window (`max_logical_pos <= window_left`, where

title: [Fix] attention: Triton decode reads wrong KV head for GQA groups > 16 not divisible by 16 (GLM-4-32B breaks)
summary: ## Motivation glm-4-32b-0414 on the triton backend decodes heads 24-31 against kv head 0, so gsm8k drops from ~93% to ~51%; triton is also what sglang picks for an fp8_e5m2 kv cache on hopper. `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` sets `cur_kv_head = cur_head_id // tl.cdiv(kv_group_num, BLOCK_H)` with BLOCK_H = 16, but lays tiles over query heads contiguously (`cur_head = cur_head_id * VALID_BLOCK_H + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)`), so when a group > 16 is not a multiple of 16 (48/2 = 24 on glm-4-32b-0414), tile 1 spans two groups and heads 24-31 read kv head 0. ## Modifications `_grouped_head_tiles` gives every KV head a whole number of 16-head tiles (`kv_head_num * cdiv(kv_group_num, 16)`), and in `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`, only when the group is not a multiple of BLOCK_H, a compile-time branch indexes the tile's heads from its group's start so the last tile of each group is partly filled and masked. Shapes whose group is a multiple of 16 compile to the same code, and `test_decode_attention_gqa_group_above_tile` tests groups 24, 20, 8, 16, and 32. ## Accuracy Tests THUDM/GLM-4-32B-0414 on GSM8K (n = 1,319, greedy, H100, step-by-step prompt): | Flags | Stock | Patched | | --- | --- | --- | | `--attention-backend triton` | 50.87% | 93.48% | | `--attention-backend fa3` | 93.48% | - | | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2` | 49.51% | 92.87% | With sgl-eval's default boxed-answer prompt all arms score lower (30.02% stock, 38.67% fixed, 38.51% FA3) because the model skips reasoning. repro: https://gist.github.com/EvanZhuang/e205b5d8038c23ab414fccb6abdaa22a (`python3 repro.py`). tests: `test_triton_a

title: [Fix] granitemoe: Declare packed_modules_mapping so per-projection quant targets match qkv_proj
summary: ## Motivation `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` fuses `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` into `qkv_proj` but declares no `packed_modules_mapping` (unlike `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM`, and vLLM's `GraniteMoeForCausalLM`). The model loader hands that mapping to the quant config, which uses it to match a fused layer to per-projection targets. Without it, a compressed-tensors checkpoint that gives attention its own scheme fails to load. For example, FP8 attention alongside 4-bit experts, with targets `re:.*self_attn\.(q|k|v|o)_proj$`: ``` ValueError: Unable to find matching target for model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj in the compressed-tensors config ``` Single-scheme checkpoints (`targets: [Linear]`) are unaffected, which is why this hasn't surfaced before. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/granitemoe.py`: declare `packed_modules_mapping` on `GraniteMoeForCausalLM`. - `qkv_proj` ← `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`. - `input_linear` ← `input_linear`: `GraniteMoeShared`'s shared-expert gate+up, which is stored fused (as in `GraniteMoeHybrid`). - `GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM` and `GraniteMoeSWAForCausalLM` inherit it. - `test/registered/unit/models/test_granitemoe_packed_modules.py` (new, CPU), using a mixed-precision compressed-tensors config (FP8 attention, NVFP4 experts): - `qkv_proj` resolves to the attention scheme; - `o_proj` still matches; - without the mapping, the lookup raises the error above; - the two subclasses inherit the mapping. ## Accuracy Tests On H200 (SM90), with this change applied to an earlier SGLang build: GraniteMoE checkpoints with FP8 attention plus NVFP4A16 or MX

title: [Feature] Add `--verify-attention-backend` for speculative target verify
summary: ## Summary - Add `--verify-attention-backend`, a first-class attention backend for speculative target-verify, independent of the prefill / decode / draft backends. ## Background - Target-verify has no attention backend of its own: `--speculative-attention-mode` (`prefill`/`decode`) picks which existing backend serves it, naming a phase rather than a backend. - Its default `prefill` silently routes verify to the prefill backend; with a cpu-seq-lens prefill backend (e.g. flashinfer) that forces a per-step `seq_lens` D2H + host sync in the spec decode loop. ## Changes - Add `--verify-attention-backend`: names the target-verify backend independently. Defaults to following the decode backend — the sync-free path on GPU-plan backends such as `trtllm_mla`. - `HybridAttnBackend` becomes a 3-slot container (prefill / decode / verify). Each slot is built from its own resolved backend string (built once per unique string). `needs_cpu_seq_lens` now ORs only the backends the spec decode loop runs (decode + verify), and the verify backend's CUDA graph is captured when it differs from decode. - Deprecate `--speculative-attention-mode` for verify routing (still the fallback when `--verify-attention-backend` is unset); warn when its default `prefill` silently routes verify to the prefill backend under an explicit attention backend. Backward compatible: `--verify-attention-backend` defaults to `None` and follows the existing `--speculative-attention-mode` routing, so current configs are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x

summary: ## Summary - Default regular decoding, speculative verification and sampling-mask capture to the same top-k-first filtering order (related: #34201). - Add server-wide `--sampling-filter-order`: `top_k_first` (default) keeps top-k, renormalizes, then applies top-p; `joint` intersects both filters against the full distribution, retaining regular decode's former semantics from #1457. - Align the default with [Transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d6c1e71bd717bf092f8293f0c3c9bd4a5ac5401a/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1593), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8fb16ea5a66f0ef362e728f0ff025f2845927fd5/vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py#L494), [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f7b384c1e5c5b2c5b321a4a7cefea04b15b54cb7/common/common.h#L263), [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/fc2f8543e039f9736c8ba576b87e1aeee42d34e1/tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/sampler/ops/flashinfer.py#L131) and [FlashInfer](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/generated/flashinfer.sampling.top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs.html). - **Behavior change:** with probabilities `[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]`, `top_k=2`, `top_p=0.55`, top-k-first yields `[1, 0, 0]`; joint yields `[0.625, 0.375, 0]`. Cross-framework cutoff ties and random streams may still differ. - Preserve full-vocabulary mass for joint speculative filtering and use the Ascend fallback for joint mode. Kernel optimization is separate in #41957. ## Validation - Existing tests passed: 13 sampling-mask, 47 sampling-batch-info, 1 Ascend dispatch, 2 UNO contract and 29 CLI/config checks.

title: [Fix] Report which limit bound `max_running_requests`
summary: ## Summary - `resolve_max_num_reqs` folds several independent bounds into nested `min()` calls and then attributes the outcome to a single hard-coded cause: `"reduced from the requested N to M due to the available KV cache capacity"`. When the hybrid state pool is what bound it (the common case for mamba/GDN models), that message points at the wrong resource - It is also silent whenever the user did not pass `--max-running-requests` — the heuristic ceiling (`token_capacity / context_len * 512`, clamped to `[2048, 4096]`) can be the binding limit with nothing logged - Collect the bounds as data (`ConcurrencyLimit`: value + where it comes from + how to raise it), pick the min, and report the one that actually bound the result — WARNING when the user asked for more than they got, INFO otherwise ## Example Before (hybrid model, state pool binding): ``` max_running_requests was reduced from the requested 74 to 26 (per dp worker) due to the available KV cache capacity. ``` After: ``` max_running_requests reduced from the requested 74 to 26 (per dp worker), bound by mamba_state_pool (max_mamba_cache_size=131 / 5 slots per request); other limits: max_running_requests=74, kv_capacity=399104. To raise it: set --max-mamba-cache-size 370, raise --mamba-full-memory-ratio, or halve the state size with --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16. ``` The remedy carries the concrete value needed for the requested concurrency, so raising the ceiling no longer requires deriving `slots x per-request` by hand. ## Changes - New `mem_cache/concurrency_limit.py`: `ConcurrencyLimit` + `resolve_concurrency_limit` +

title: [Feat] grpc: Advertise api.v1 owning-runtime instance identity
summary: ## Motivation We are separating an independent Rust runtime sidecar from the native SGLang engine into different container images, so we can adopt upstream SGLang images for new-model support without rebuilding the sidecar. Following the unified `api.v1` direction, the two processes communicate through native gRPC and have independent lifetimes. The sidecar needs to distinguish **reconnecting to the same engine** from **connecting to a replacement engine at the same address**. Model, version, topology and startup duration cannot establish this. Without an engine-owned boot identity, a reconnect cannot reliably decide whether cached engine-scoped state still belongs to the current runtime. This PR supplies that identity through existing metadata calls. A sidecar can compare it on reconnect and invalidate or fence state when it changes. Client-side fencing/recovery is a separate integration step; this field does not implement it by itself. ## Modifications - Add opaque UUIDv4 `instance_id` (field 16) to native `api.v1 GetServerInfoResponse` and typed HTTP `/server_info`. - Mint it once at embedded Rust `CoreInner` construction, shared by clones and HTTP/gRPC adapters. Repeated reads, transport reconnects and external sidecar restarts preserve it; a fresh owning runtime gets a new value. - Keep the typed identity authoritative over stale launch snapshots. Do not reuse `PortArgs.instance_id`, which identifies shared IPC/load-snapshot namespaces and may survive worker recovery. - Regenerate Rust/Python bindings and bump `sglang-api-types` to 0.2.0. Scope is the embedded Rust run

title: [Feature][RFC] Preserve measured cache-write usage across PD handoff
summary: ## Checklist - [x] This proposes a serving capability, rather than a general support question. - [x] This issue is written in English. ## Motivation A disaggregated request should be able to report a cache-write measurement made on its prefill worker through the API served by its decode worker. Today the PD handoff carries cached-read information, but not the measured-write state proposed in #46091. That PR deliberately keeps PD writes **unknown**, including when the decode worker's local cache is disabled. This is the correct fallback; a local measured zero would not describe work performed by prefill. This RFC proposes the missing end-to-end capability as a follow-up to #46091. It does not ask to broaden that PR before merge. The useful outcome is the same measured-versus-unknown distinction for disaggregated and colocated serving, with one definition of newly reusable prompt ranges across JSON and terminal streaming usage. This is request usage accounting. A measured write is not an L3 durability acknowledgment, a retention promise, a billing policy, or proof of future cache residency. ## Proposed scope Start with normal bootstrapped dense Python serving, PP1, one request, no session, speculative decoding or external linker, and a cache configuration whose prefill-side measurement has a provable handoff boundary. State the exact supported sender/receiver topology. title: [Perf] spec-decode: Add candidate-pruned DSpark Markov sampling
summary: This PR caches scaled FP32 biases for static Markov candidates and adds a fused greedy walk across all draft positions. Base-logit Top-K is computed once per block; each walk step evaluates the correction for at most K dynamic candidates and gathers the static candidates’ cached biases. The fused walk avoids dense per-step score buffers and scatters while leaving target verification unchanged. On 8× NVIDIA H200 with DP=8, TP=1, Qwen3-4B, K=32 and block size 8, the optimized configuration improves geometric-mean output throughput by 3.6% across 10 datasets. Draft-block latency improves by 1.4–6.7× versus the dense path, including 1.032 → 0.430 ms at batch size 32. Requests terminate naturally at EOS. The recommended configuration pairs --speculative-dspark-markov-topk 32 with SGLANG_DSPARK_USE_GREEDY_DRAFT=1. The sampled candidate path still materializes dense step logits and regressed by 5.6% in the reported control run. Candidate tables occupy 55.6 MiB per rank, including 18.5 MiB of added FP32 bias storage. title: [Bug] inkling2: Generic ModelOpt metadata overrides checkpoint precision config
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest affected branch (`inkling-2-small-support` at `778fb834e7`, PR #50186). - [x] I included environment information and a minimal reproducible demo below. - [x] This is a bug report, written in English. ### Describe the bug Thanks for the Inkling-2-Small support in #50186. The released checkpoint cannot be loaded without overriding its HF config because its two quantization metadata sources are resolved in the wrong order for this model. Explicitly passing `--quantization inkling2` does not provide a usable workaround because the conflicting declaration is still parsed. title: [Feature] EAGLE tree verify without per-node state snapshots for GDN layers
summary:
Modern state-of-the-art speculative decoding architectures employ a tree draft structure. Examples include EAGLE-4, DDTree, and Sequoia-based approaches. However, for most models, inference kernels are far from optimized for tree draft verification. While benchmarking Qwen3.8-27B, it turned out that the tree-vs-chain verification overhead is within the linear attention (GDN) layers, specifically in their memory traffic. The current implementation stores a checkpoint of the recurrent state matrix for every node of the draft, so that the commit step can load the one for the verified branch. Verifying the same 16 draft tokens with 8 requests in the batch takes 17.3 ms as a chain and 24.3 ms as a tree. 6.7 ms of that 7.0 ms gap is in the GDN layers. Chains avoid the snapshots with `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`. Trees cannot: the flag rejects `--speculative-eagle-topk > 1`. Adding no-snapshot logic for tree draft verification would speed up the linear layers by over 60% and the overall verify forward pass by up to 38% for this particular model, assuming the tree reaches the chain's cost in these layers.
Setup and reproduction Qwen3.8-27B on one B300, `nightly-dev-cu13-20261112-2c597c92`, CUDA graphs on, MTP draft, 7.4k-token prompts, greedy, 160 new tokens. Times are GPU time of one target verify forward from the torch profiler (`/start_profile`), median over the verify steps. | | 1 reque

summary: ## Motivation One MiniMax-H3 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps) on one B300 takes about 119 s and keeps the GPU busy 99.8% of the time. title: [Perf] minimax-h3: Fuse the attention gated residual with the norm2 modulation
summary: ## Motivation One MiniMax-H3 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps) on one B300 takes about 119 s and keeps the GPU busy 99.8% of the time. FA4 and the GEMMs account for about 93% of it, at the GPU's 1100 W power cap. This is one of five independent, bit-exact cuts to the small kernels around them (#50387, #50388, #50390, #50391, #50392); each PR stands on its own. After attention, each H3 block wrote the gated residual (`indexed_gate_bf16_`) and then read it back for the fused RMSNorm + AdaLN modulation of the MLP input: two passes over a 37760 x 5376 bf16 tensor. ## Modifications - `indexed_gate_rmsnorm_scale_shift_`: one Triton pass writes the gated residual in place and returns the normed, modulated rows. It uses the same roundings and the residual kernel's reduction layout, so both outputs are bit-identical to the two kernels. - The H3 block uses it when Cache-DiT does not need the block input preserved, the MLP takes bf16 input (not MXFP8) and the fused norm-modulate path is on; otherwise it keeps the two kernels. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_rmsnorm_indexed_scale_shift.py`: the fused kernel against the two-kernel sequence, bit for bit. title: [Perf] mem_cache: Drain external KV offload completions with a deque
summary: ## Motivation Completing external KV-cache offloads currently calls `pending_offloads.pop(0)` for each acknowledgement. Each call shifts the remaining list entries, so draining a backlog incurs quadratic pointer-shifting work. Use a deque to make removal of each completed entry constant-time. This is a bounded CPU bookkeeping optimization. I have not established that large offload backlogs occur in production or that this change improves end-to-end serving performance. ## Modifications - Store `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.pending_offloads` in a deque and drain with `popleft()`. - Preserve FIFO completion, publication callbacks, and lock-release ordering. - Add three regression cases covering partial mixed-success completion and subsequent appends, repeated splits of a non-head offload, and clearing outstanding offloads without duplicate lock releases. - Change existing empty-list assertions to container-independent emptiness checks. Split-node updates still scan the queue and replace the matching entry by index. Deque indexed replacement is linear; this path was already linear because it scans for the matching offload. No model math, device kernels, or transfer semantics change. ## Accuracy Tests - All configured pre-commit checks passed for both changed files, including test-registration validation. - Three dependency-free behavioral smoke tests passed against both the original and patched implementations. title: [Fix] weights: Reject mismatched manifests before distributed broadcasts
summary: ## Motivation **A distributed weight update can report success and advance the policy version even when only part of the requested weights—or none of them—were received.** The ordinary receiver iterates `zip(names, dtypes, shapes)`. Unequal list lengths silently truncate the receive set. The scheduler then loads that prefix, reports success, and records the requested version. For RL rollout synchronization, this can advertise a new policy while some weights still belong to the previous policy. A separate failure occurs when a later dtype, shape or allocation is invalid: the receiver has already posted earlier asynchronous broadcasts before discovering the error, and exits without waiting for those handles. ## Before/after evidence The same CPU probe was run against upstream `4f8b6867534c8a6632845353997555fca857dd63` and this branch. It calls the **actual scheduler, distributed receiver and weight loader**, using a two-weight CPU model and a controlled broadcast boundary. title: [Fix] attention: Widen GDN chunk-state offsets to int64 before multiplying
summary: _Produced by Hyperloom._ ## Motivation `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` (`fla/chunk_delta_h.py`, and its XPU copy) builds its pointer bases as ```python h += ((boh * H + i_h) * V * K).to(tl.int64) v += ((bos * H + i_h) * V).to(tl.int64) ``` The multiply runs in int32 and the cast only widens the result after it has wrapped. One chunk-state slot is `H * V * K` elements (2**19 for H=32, K=V=128 per rank), so once a sequence's `chunk_offsets` entry reaches 4096 the `h` offset passes 2**31 and goes negative: the kernel writes before the chunk-state buffer. At 8192 (offset 2**32) it wraps to 0 and silently overwrites the first sequence's chunk states. Only sequences that are not first in a packed batch are affected (a single request has `bos = boh = 0`). With H=32, K=V=128 per rank the `h` offset overflows once about 262k tokens precede a sequence in the same launch (131k with H=64), which is reachable with a large or disabled `chunked_prefill_size`. The `bos`-based `v/k/w/v_new` offsets overflow at twice that. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/chunk_delta_h.py` and `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/kernels/fla/chunk_delta_h.py`: widen `bos` and `boh` to int64 once, before the products. title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Keep active DP decode ranks out of idle tail replay
summary: ## Motivation In a colocated prefill/decode deployment with DP attention, a single step can run an `EXTEND` batch on one rank and an active `DECODE` batch on another, with both ranks seeing `is_extend_in_batch=True`. When the step selects the eager-prefill decoder tail graph, the decode rank has no prefill tail, so `DecoderReplayTail.plan` routes it through `run_idle`. `run_idle` slices its inputs to zero rows before returning a graph buffer sized for the original nonzero decode batch, corrupting next-token logits and producing repeated or malformed output. We reproduced this on a SGLang `v0.5.23`-based build. The same planner path is present in [upstream `v0.5.23`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/297e54fd105e974cdf401e5b4d20253a22c16f90/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py#L203-L238) and remains reachable for ordinary decode on [`main` at `3825fcd397`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/3825fcd3978ea549a6b41417be21f6973c98e50e/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_replay_tail.py#L203-L240). [#46676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46676) only guards coordinated speculative verify steps via `dp_spec_prefill_coordination_applied`. Ordinary decode does not go through speculative coordination. If a mixed step keeps a live rank in `DECODE` mode and selects the eager-prefill tail graph, that rank can still be routed to `run_idle`. ## Modifications - Piggyback a tail-graph eligibility flag onto the row counts in the existing host collectives (computed after forward-mode reshaping on the TP-MoE path, and by checking for an actual tail or

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] gemma4: write o_proj/down_proj partials straight into the AR-fusion symmetric buffer
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #48563. Each fused all-reduce site (`SGLANG_GEMMA4_AR_FUSION=1`) first copies the `o_proj` / `down_proj` partial sums into its symmetric buffer, because the kernel reads them through NVLink multicast. That is a `[T, 5376]` bf16 copy before every site, twice per layer: 44 MB and ~20 µs per site at a 4096-token chunk on H200, about 12 % of the fused site. This PR has the GEMM write its output into the symmetric buffer directly, so the copy goes away. `RowParallelLinear.forward(output_tensor=...)` already routes to `quant_method.apply_into`, but only `UnquantizedLinearMethod` implements it. Gemma-4 FP8-block checkpoints load through compressed-tensors, so the FP8 path needed the same entry point. ## Modifications - `compressed_tensors.py`: `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod.apply_into` checks the output shape and hands the caller tensor to the scheme's `apply_weights_into`; a scheme without it computes as before and copies. - `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py`: `apply_weights_into` for the W8A8 FP8 schemes. On the block-FP8 DeepGEMM path the GEMM writes the caller tensor; the Triton, CUTLASS and per-tensor/channel paths compute and copy. - `fp8_utils.py` / `fp8_kernel.py`: optional `output=` on `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` and `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_deepgemm`. Used only when it is contiguous bf16 at the GEMM's output dtype; otherwise the result is copied in (the GEMV fallback included). - `gemma4_ar_fusion.py`: `Gemma4ArFusion.partial_out(num_tokens)` returns the buffer the site reads; `_stage` skips the copy when the partial already live

title: [Feat] attention: Add ag_delay_reduce DCP backend for MLA and Triton GQA
summary: ## Motivation Decode context parallelism (DCP) splits each request's KV cache across the `c` ranks of a DCP group. Every attention layer must then merge the ranks' partial outputs. Every existing backend sends the partial outputs themselves: `ag_rs` all-gathers the LSE and reduce-scatters an FP32 output, while `a2a`/`fi_a2a` pack the output and LSE into one exchange. The attention-output payload is `B x heads x head_dim` per layer either way. This PR adds the opt-in `--dcp-comm-backend ag_delay_reduce`. It sends only the LSE, `B x heads` FP32 values, and lets the all-reduce that already follows `o_proj` do the summation. The approach follows PipeSwift (https://github.com/wsjdsg/PipeSwift). ## How it works After local attention, rank `r` holds its partial output `o_r[h]` and log-sum-exp `L_r[h]` for every head `h` of its DCP group (context shard `r`). Then: 1. All-gather the LSE (`[B, H_g]` FP32) within the DCP group. 2. Scale the local partial: `alpha_r[h] = exp(L_r[h] - logsumexp_r' L_r'[h])`, `o_r'[h] = alpha_r[h] * o_r[h]`. This uses the backend's log base and maps empty shards (`-inf` LSE, NaN output) to zero. 3. Keep all `H_g` group heads. Project them with the DCP group's full output weight (plus the MLA V up-projection), which is gathered once at startup. 4. Let the existing attention-TP all-reduce after `o_proj` sum the result. Prefill keeps the original head-sharded merge and the original TP weight shard. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Bound a chunked continuation past decode headroom by free rows
summary: ## Motivation Under KV pressure the scheduler can crash with: ``` RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 3909 tokens. Available full tokens: 3840 (full_available_size=3840 + full_evictable_size_=0) ``` `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` (the budget of plain, non-SWA pools) caps a chunked continuation at `remaining_total`, which also subtracts the decode headroom reserved for running requests. When that goes to zero or below, it returns the full `chunk_limit` so the continuation still makes progress, without checking how many rows are actually free. If the pool is physically short too, the pass admits a chunk that `alloc_for_extend` cannot allocate and the scheduler dies. `SWAPrefillBudget` and `ChainPrefillBudget` already wait in this case. It shows up most readily with `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first`: that policy shrinks the running chunk to admit shorter requests in the same pass, so the chunked request's next continuation often finds the pool already full. It can happen under any policy. ## Modifications - When `remaining_total` leaves no room, the continuation still goes past the decode headroom, but only into the rows free now (`remaining_current`, page-floored). With none free it returns `None`, and the chunked request waits for decode to release memory, as the SWA and chain budgets already do. - `test_prefill_adder.py`: `test_continuation_past_decode_headroom_fits_free_rows`. title: [Feat] serving: Add --clamp-max-new-tokens-to-context to cap max_tokens when the prompt fits
summary: ## Motivation Closes #45841. When the prompt fits the context but prompt + `max_new_tokens` does not, `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request` returns 400. Clients often cannot compute the exact prompt length (it depends on the server's tokenizer and chat template), so a client that sends a fixed `max_tokens` cap, or computes one from an estimated prompt length, gets rejected. The OpenAI API defines `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` as an upper bound, and the scheduler already treats it that way: `init_req_max_new_tokens` clamps it to `max_req_len - input_len - 1` and to the KV budget. The 400 comes only from the frontend check. The only existing switch, `--allow-auto-truncate`, also truncates prompts that are too long, so it cannot be used to get "cap the output, reject an overlong prompt". ## Modifications - New opt-in server flag `--clamp-max-new-tokens-to-context` (`serving` namespace, default off). It is appended at the end of `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`, so existing positional slots don't move. - `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request`: with the flag, a request whose prompt fits but whose `max_new_tokens` overshoots gets `max_new_tokens` capped to `context_len - input_tokens` (reserved tokens included), the same value the `--allow-auto-truncate` branch already sets. Prompts longer than the context still fail with the existing 400. - `OpenAIServingChat._validate_request`: with the flag, a `max_completion_tokens` larger than the whole context is accepted as a cap, mirroring how that check already defers to `--allow-auto-truncate`. - Docs: a row in `server_arguments.m

title: [Test] attention: Guard Muse Spark fused KV store writes
summary: ## Motivation The Muse Spark fused QK norm/RoPE/KV-store test compares the cache with a numerical tolerance and randomly selects slots. That is useful for reduction/RoPE accuracy, but does not explicitly guard repeated padding slot 0, both ends of the writable pool, all-padding calls, or bitwise preservation of untouched storage. A small stray write can fit inside the current 2e-2 / 0.125 tolerance. ## Modifications Add eight cases to the existing CI-registered `test_muse_spark_qk_norm_rope_store.py`: RoPE on/off × BF16/E4M3 cache × mixed/all-padding slots. - Deliberately use slots `[0, capacity - 1, 1, 0, 9]`, or all zeros. - Require untouched K/V cache rows (including slot 0) and the entire strided QKV source allocation, including row padding, to remain byte-identical. - Check live K against the returned BF16 K from the same call, converted to the cache dtype. Keep the existing tolerant comparison with the independent torch norm/RoPE implementation. - Check live V against its raw input, including signed zeros, E4M3 halfway values and ±448/±512 saturation cases. The API requires unity cache scales; no foreign scaling/rounding convention is imposed. No production code changes, no claimed kernel bug or speedup. This strengthens the fused operation's store contract; the standalone `store_cache` tests exercise a different kernel. Overlap review: FlashInfer #7957 already covers paged append output preservation and #4992 covers window/split attention against an FP32 oracle, so those were not duplicated. SGLang's fused implementation already has BF16 rounding before RoPE and FP8

title: [Perf] diffusion: Walk one token's heads per warp in the two-rows QK-norm+RoPE kernel
summary: ## Motivation One MiniMax-H3 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps) on one B300 takes about 119 s and keeps the GPU busy 99.8% of the time. FA4 and the GEMMs account for about 93% of it, at the GPU's 1100 W power cap. This is one of five independent, bit-exact cuts to the small kernels around them (#50387, #50388, #50390, #50391, #50392); each PR stands on its own. The head_dim-128 QK-norm+RoPE kernel gives each warp a pair of rows and redoes the token, head, position and cos/sin loads for every pair. At H3's shape (37760 tokens, 56 heads) it ran at 3.7 TB/s. ## Modifications - Rows are token-major, so with an even head count both rows of a warp share a token. When there are at least as many tokens as resident warps, a warp now walks one token's heads, loads its position, cos/sin and both weights once, and prefetches the next row. - On sm_103 and sm_120 the bf16/fp16 RoPE products and sums run two elements per instruction (`mul/add/sub.rn.*x2`), with the same per-element rounding as the scalar `rotary_mul_rn` path (since #50101 SM100 also takes that scalar path; the packed variant stays on the arches it was measured on). - Per-row arithmetic is unchanged, so the output is bit-identical. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place.py` gains a 24611-token case that exercises the token loop. On B300, on this branch merged with main `6ddfd1380c8f`, it and `test_rope.py` give 1289 passed (1277 on main). - At H3's shape, the outputs are bit-identical to main (same inputs, `torch.equal`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling One idle B300, H3 shape (37760 tokens, 56 heads, r

title: [Fix] deepseek-v3.1: Fix quadratic regex scans in the tool-call parser
summary: ## Motivation `DeepSeekV31Detector` (`deepseekv31`) scans model output with patterns that go quadratic when `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` never arrives: 1. `parse_streaming_increment` runs `re.search(r"<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*)<｜tool▁sep｜>(.*?)(<｜tool▁call▁end｜>|$)")` over the **whole buffer on every chunk**. With repeated `<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>` tokens and no separator, each call retries the greedy scan from every begin token. 2. `detect_and_parse` uses `re.findall(begin.*?end)`, rescanning to the end from every begin token, then a greedy detail pattern per block. | Input | Before | After | |---|---|---| | 130 KB, one streaming call | 9.9 s | ~0 | | 30 KB stream in 64-char (multi-token / MTP) chunks | 0.66 s worst chunk, **84 s total** | 0.1 ms worst chunk | | 130 KB, non-stream | 9.4 s | ~0 | Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time. ## Modifications The three patterns are replaced with linear `find` / `rfind` helpers that return the same groups: - `_iter_call_blocks`: `begin.*?end` spans. - `_search_complete_call`: `begin(.*)sep(.*)end`. The match starts at the first begin, and the greedy groups end at the last end token and at the last separator before it. - `_search_partial_call`: `begin(.*)sep(.*?)(end|$)`. The name group ends at the last separator. The lazy argument group stops at the first end token, else at `$`, which, as in `re`, is end of text or just before a trailing newline. title: [Feat] scheduler: Persist hybrid active requests for fresh-process resume
summary: ## Motivation An active hybrid-model request contains more than a reusable prefix: it also owns Mamba recurrent state, generated tokens/logprobs, and native decoding progress. This draft adds an **opt-in, default-disabled** snapshot path to continue that request in a fresh SGLang process after the source exits, without recomputing its committed history. The supported contract is deliberately bounded: identical model weights/version, source build, TP size, dtype, page/layer geometry, and the same device pair, using trusted shared local storage. Local pool capacity may differ when the actual request allocations fit. Exact sampling-RNG trajectory equivalence, cross-host/weight recovery, crash-atomicity, HA, Trainer integration, and performance are outside this draft's demonstrated scope. ## Modifications - Export Attention KV plus Mamba conv/temporal state at a committed native decoding boundary; require every TP rank's immutable payload and manifest before source-slot release. - Reconstruct a new native request with its token/logprob history, normalized sampling parameters, reasoning/stream progress, and remaining generation budget; validate identity and payload integrity before allocating/importing into fresh slots. - Separate per-request state geometry from local Mamba pool capacity, preserving strict dtype, layer, version, source-build, and TP checks. - Include public export/resume/reference/negative clients, a public-input reproduction guide, and focused CPU storage/request contracts. title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Precompile BF16 sparse MLA splits during warmup
summary: ## Motivation ROCm BF16 sparse MLA selects `inner_iter` from the current query length. The query length itself is dynamic, but `inner_iter` and the corresponding combine group count specialize two TileLang kernels. Normal startup and workload warmup can therefore miss an intermediate split and compile it while serving requests. In a four-node GLM-5.3 TP8/PP4 run, an unseen `inner_iter=4` triggered 64 native builds (partial + combine on 32 workers). Compilation progressed through the four pipeline stages, taking 44.294 seconds from the first stage's start to the last stage's completion and producing large TTFT outliers. ## Modifications - Add a cached helper that prepares both BF16 partial and combine kernels for every split reachable by the existing selector. - Invoke it on the first ROCm BF16 sparse-attention forward, using the actual model dimensions, attention scale, block size, and thread count. Normal server warmup can then populate the variants before serving traffic. - Follow the selector's halving sequence and divisibility check, including padded top-k sizes that are not powers of two. - Add regression coverage for split coverage, cache keys/reuse, numerical results across query lengths, and graph capture/replay. Kernel definitions, attention math, runtime split selection, FP8 paths, and NVIDIA BF16 dispatch are unchanged. This moves compilation work to the first forward; it does not remove that work. If startup warmup is disabled, the first actual forward pays the preparation cost. Persisting `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR` helps subsequent process/container starts. ## Accura

title: [Feat] tracing: Stable span names, full rid, and configured request headers on root spans
summary: ## Motivation A request's trace is hard to find and hard to group: - Root spans are named `Req <first 8 chars of rid>`, and thread spans `Scheduler [TP 0] (host:<id> | pid:<pid>)`. With a per-request or per-process ID in the name, every span gets a unique name, which breaks grouping and aggregation by span name in tracing backends. The IDs are already recorded as attributes. - The `rid` attribute is the rid split on `_`, to drop a worker-ID prefix that multi-tokenizer added to rids (#8964; the split came with #9962). #11295 removed that prefix, so the split now only truncates rids that contain `_`: `req_abc_123` is recorded as `123`, so a request can't be found by its rid. - A root span carries only SGLang's own `rid`. Clients, gateways and load balancers know a request by their own IDs (`x-request-id`, a correlation ID, ...), so finding its trace means correlating timestamps across systems. ## Modifications 1. **Create root spans in one function.** `start_root_span` replaces the identical root-span code in `TraceReqContext` and `TraceReqContextAsync`, so the changes below apply to both sync and async tracing. Pure refactor, no behavior change. 2. **Stable span names; `rid` recorded as is.** - Root spans are named `Req`, or `prefill Req` / `decode Req` under PD disaggregation. - Thread spans are named `<label> [TP n] [PP n] [DP n]`; `host_id` and `pid` stay attributes. - The `rid` attribute is the full rid. 3. **Record configured request headers on root spans.** `SGLANG_TRACE_REQUEST_HEADERS` (comma-separated, case-insensitive) names the request headers to record. title: Support compressed-tensors NVFP4 Marlin with BF16 and DSpark
summary: ## Motivation Compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints currently require the native SM100+ FP4 runner. On SM80-SM90 GPUs, the existing Marlin NVFP4 path is available for ModelOpt checkpoints but is not wired into the compressed-tensors scheme. BF16 models expose a second issue: small E4M3 block scales can underflow when Marlin encodes them through FP16 bit manipulation. In addition, compressed-tensors quantization is not attached to `ParallelLMHead`, and DSpark computes logits through the raw weight tensor, so a quantized `lm_head` is loaded or executed incorrectly. summary: ## What changed This PR adds three per-step histograms. Each batch is sampled by exactly one scheduler rank: attention TP rank 0 and attention CP rank 0 on the final PP stage. That is the same predicate the FPM publisher uses (`_is_forward_pass_metrics_rank()`). With `--enable-dp-attention`, each attention DP group runs its own batch and emits its own series under its `dp_rank` label. - `sglang:forward_pass_duration_seconds`: device-measured time of the batch's own forward segments. When one batch launches several segments (e.g. speculative draft + verify), their times are added. Labels: `phase`, `prefill_tokens_bucket`, `decode_reqs_bucket`. - `sglang:decode_step_latency_seconds`: the same measurement, limited to passes with decode requests. Labels: `phase` (`decode_only` / `mixed`), `co_scheduled_prefill_bucket`, `decode_reqs_bucket`. - `sglang:schedule_to_result_latency_seconds`: wall time from the start of batch selection to the end of result processing. Under overlap it includes the next batch's selection and launch, so it measures an engine step, not forward time. **Attribution under overlap.** `run_batch` stamps each batch with the `[begin, end)` range of device-timer segments it launched (`DeviceTimer.num_started`). Result processing claims exactly that range. `event_loop_overlap` launches n+1 before it processes n, and n+1's forward is never charged to n. A step is skipped if it launched no timed segment, or if one of its segments has not finished. summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary `BlockRemoved` currently reports only the removed block hashes and the storage medium: ```python class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent): block_hashes: list[int] medium: Optional[str] = None ``` This tells a KV-event consumer that blocks disappeared from a tier, but not why they disappeared. As a result, consumers cannot reconstruct the KV-cache lifecycle or attribute cache losses to a specific policy or request lifecycle. ## Why this matters The same `BlockRemoved` event can currently represent very different actions: - capacity-driven LRU eviction; - normal release after a request finishes; - request abort/cancellation; - demotion to a lower storage tier; - an explicit cache clear. These cases have different operational meanings. For example, a cache miss after an `evicted` event indicates capacity pressure, while a miss after a `demoted` event may be recoverable from another storage tier. Without the reason, monitoring and KV-cache analysis have to infer the cause from timing and unrelated scheduler state. This prevents consumers from reliably answering questions such as: - Are prefixes being lost because the GPU KV pool is too small? - How many blocks are truly discarded versus moved to another tier? - Is a lower cache hit rate caused by eviction or by normal request cleanup? ## Current implementation detail `KVC

With that image, any configuration whose automatic `max_running_requests` reaches roughly 4000 crashes at start-up in the dummy decode batch: ``` CUDA Error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS .../flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh 1269 Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault ``` With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the fault is raised at `qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton` (`_forward_trtllm_sparse` → `sparse_attn.py`), not in the FMHA. Operand sizes of the dummy batch: `topk 2051`, page 64 → row stride 2112, one KV head of dim 256 per TP4 rank; `batch × 2112 × 256` exceeds 2^31 for the last rows once the batch is a few thousand rows — 3892 rows worked, 4000 failed in our scans (fp32 and bf16 SSM state alike; the exact first failing batch depends on which rows/columns are written). Casting the offsets to int64 (what #38851 does) makes the same configurations start and serve, and the patched kernel is bitwise equal to the stock kernel below the overflow and to a torch reference gather at batch 4000. How users hit it on the shipped image: `--disable-radix-cache` (needed for fair benchmarks) plus e.g. `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` with `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` or `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` — each raises the automatic `max_ru

title: [Feature] Store DeepSeek-V4.1 C1/C2 Main KV in packed FP4 on Hopper
summary: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation baseline: #38798 DeepSeek-V4.1 already applies E2M1 fake quantization to C1/C2 compressed latents, but the result is dequantized and requantized into the legacy FlashMLA FP8 cache: ```text E2M1 fake quant -> dequantized BF16/FP32 values -> FP8 E4M3 quantization -> legacy FlashMLA page (584 logical bytes per compressed token) ``` This preserves FP4 numerical behavior but not FP4 storage density. This issue proposes a versioned packed layout for **DeepSeek-V4.1 C1/C2 Main KV only**. SWA KV, Indexer KV, V4 C4/C128, and request-scoped C2 pair state remain unchanged. The implementation is split into a correctness-first staged consumer and a later native SM90 mixed-cache consumer. The first two phases provide the persistent KV-capacity gain without requiring an immediate FlashMLA kernel rewrite. ## Scope In scope: - Main KV written by V4.1 ratio-1 and ratio-2 `kv_source_layer_ids` - C1/C2 decode and prefill stores - Memory-pool sizing and typed layout descriptors - Dense/sparse prefill and decode consumers - HiCache and Mooncake/NIXL PD page transfer - Hopper/H20 software E2M1 encode/decode - A future SM100 hardware-conversion specialization Out of scope: - SWA KV layout - FP4 Indexer KV layout - V4 C4/C128 layout - C2 pending-pair ring layout or transfer semantics - Radix-tree logical slot/page indexing ## Current Behavior Th

title: [RFC] FuseEP Integration for MiniMax-M3 Prefill on Ascend NPU
summary: ## 1. Summary This RFC proposes an opt-in Ascend FuseEP path for MiniMax-M3 W8A8 prefill in SGLang. It adds a MiniMax-M3-specific normal-mode operator, DispatchFFNCombineM3, that fuses routed-expert dispatch, the two expert FFN GEMMs, and combine into one EP operation. The existing low-latency FuseEP path remains the decode path. The initial implementation is deliberately narrow: MiniMax-M3, ModelSlim W8A8, hidden size 6144, top-k 4, 128 routed experts, and EP/TP 16 on Ascend NPU. It does not alter the generic DeepEP path, routing algorithm, attention implementation, or model semantics. Reference implementation: - SGLang integration: https://github.com/ClownBin/sglang/commit/2ca0e6cc3bfcb3379926e6261d95cc6dfe9f039c - Ascend kernel and DeepEP adapter: https://github.com/ClownBin/sgl-kernel-npu/commit/87525b7305d449dfc66272465feb856188244092 - Original experiment and launch configuration: https://github.com/ClownBin/sglang/issues/19#issuecomment-5099607728 --- ## 2. Motivation For long prefill, the conventional MoE path exposes separate dispatch, expert-GEMM, and combine phases. In the tested MiniMax-M3 deployment, those boundaries leave observable accelerator idle periods and limit NPU utilization. The data path must also accommodate MiniMax-M3's W8A8 weight layout and SwiGLU variant. FuseEP can eliminate those boundaries by performing dispatch, FFN, and combine in one operator and HCCL EP collective. title: [Feat] ngram: let each request choose which external corpora to draft from
summary: ## Motivation A server can load several external corpora, such as code and legal text. NGRAM currently uses all of them for every request. Unrelated corpora share the draft budget and can reduce the accept length. This PR lets each request choose its corpora. It covers the "User request take in corpus_ids to match" item in #21052. ## Modifications Add `ngram_corpus_ids` to the request's sampling params: ```json {"text": "...", "sampling_params": {"ngram_corpus_ids": ["code"]}} ``` | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | Not set | Use all loaded corpora, as before | | `["a", "b"]` | Use only these corpora | | `[]` | Use the online trie without external corpora | | Unknown ID | Ignore it, since a corpus may have been removed | The external SAM budget is split only among the selected corpora. A request that selects one of two corpora gets the same drafts as a server with only that corpus loaded. The worker stores the selection once per request. It tracks the request itself as well as its ID, so a new request cannot inherit an old selection when it reuses that ID. Later steps of the same request keep their state. The Python API, protobuf schema, and Rust server accept the new field. The field order matches on both sides. ## Accuracy Tests After the update to main (`782b69f`): - **137 CPU tests and 23 subtests passed.** These cover the corpus, request state, worker prompt, Mamba updates, and sampling params. - **21 Rust API tests passed.** `cargo gen-api` reproduced the generated files without changes. - Pre-commit passed with the Rust workspace Clippy hook skipped. title: [Feat] ngram: let each request draft from its own prompt
summary: ## Motivation Code edits, text revisions, and document quotes often repeat parts of the prompt. NGRAM can draft from its online trie and external corpora, but only the last `max_trie_depth` prompt tokens enter the trie. Most of the prompt is unavailable as a draft source. This PR lets each request draft from its own prompt. It covers the "SAM for user request's input" item in #21052 and builds on #44957. ## Modifications Add two server args: | Arg | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `--speculative-ngram-prompt-sam-budget` | `0` (off) | Draft nodes for the request's prompt | | `--speculative-ngram-prompt-sam-max-tokens` | `32768` | Maximum number of recent prompt tokens to index | ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct \ --speculative-algorithm NGRAM --speculative-num-draft-tokens 16 \ --speculative-ngram-prompt-sam-budget 8 ``` The worker builds a suffix automaton (SAM) once for each request. It uses a separate draft budget, so prompt drafts do not take slots from external corpora. Construction runs outside the corpus mutex to avoid a long pause for other requests. The worker tracks the request itself as well as its ID. A new request that reuses an ID gets fresh state and its own prompt SAM. Later decode steps and prefill retries of the same request keep that state. ## Accuracy Tests After the update to main and #44957 (`11e8d91`): - **144 CPU tests and 27 subtests passed.** These cover the corpus, request state, worker prompt, Mamba updates, and sampling params. - **14 argument and docs tests plus 14 subtests passed.** - The AP

title: [Fix] cohere_command4: Strip an echoed think-start and keep same-chunk answers in streaming
summary: ## Motivation `CohereCommand4Detector` gives different results in streaming and non-streaming mode: 1. **Echoed `<|START_THINKING|>`.** The class docstring and `detect_and_parse` handle checkpoints that echo `<|START_THINKING|>` although the chat template already emitted it, and strip it. `parse_streaming_increment` streams it as reasoning, split across deltas. 2. **Answer lost when it arrives in one chunk with `<|END_THINKING|>`.** After emitting the reasoning, `parse_streaming_increment` returns and leaves `<|START_TEXT|>answer<|END_TEXT|>` in the buffer. If the stream ends there, `finish()` drops it because `<|START_TEXT|>` was never seen. Speculative decoding and `stream_interval > 1` deliver such multi-token chunks (as noted in `TestStreamingChunkSizeInvariance`). title: [Fix] tuning_block_wise_kernel: Tune [32, 32] block recipes on CUDA
summary: ## Motivation Part of #50057 (problem 1 only). `tuning_block_wise_kernel.py --block-k 32` could not tune a `[32, 32]` block recipe on CUDA: - `get_configs_compute_bound()` only offered `BLOCK_SIZE_K` 64 and 128. - `tune_on_gpu()` keeps only tiles that divide `--block-k`, so `--block-k 32` left 0 candidates. - `tune()` then printed "Completed tuning" and died on a bare `assert best_config is not None`, writing no config. ## Modifications - New `get_cuda_block_k_tiles(block_k)`: keeps the default `[64, 128]` tiles, and falls back to a 32-wide tile only when no default tile divides the quant group. `get_configs_compute_bound()` takes an optional `block_k` and uses it. - `tune_on_gpu()` raises a `ValueError` naming `--block-k` when the filtered search space is empty, instead of running and failing later. - `tune()` replaces the bare assert with a `RuntimeError` that names the shape and the reason. I did not add 32 to the default list: 32 also divides 128, so the common `[128, 128]` recipe would get 50% more candidates and take 50% longer to tune for no gain. Not addressed here: problem 2 in the issue (timing with the weight resident in L2). title: [Fix] quantization: Correct cache state and latency in block-wise tuner
summary: ## Motivation Refs #50057 (cache/timing portion). `benchmark_config()` warms up and repeatedly benchmarks the same weights without evicting L2. For weights that fit in cache, this can change candidate rankings relative to a larger working set. It also divides by `num_iters * 10`, although each sample executes one matmul, underreporting latency by 10x. ## Modifications - Use Triton's backend-specific benchmark cache buffer and clear it before each start event, excluding eviction work from the timed interval. - Average the actual number of samples and convert milliseconds to microseconds. - Reject nonpositive sample counts before launching work. - Add CPU regressions for timing arithmetic, eviction placement and invalid sample counts. title: [Fix] [AMD] docker: Pin UCX and NIXL commits for ROCm PD disaggregation
summary: ## Motivation The ROCm image builds UCX from `v1.19.x` and NIXL at `c28061f9`. With that pair, NIXL-based prefill/decode disaggregation on ROCm does not work as intended: - NIXL before ai-dynamo/nixl#2371 leaves `ROCM_IPC_MIN_ZCOPY` at its default, so intra-node GPU-to-GPU transfers skip `rocm_ipc` (XGMI) and fall back to a slower path. - The UCX ROCm fixes NIXL relies on are only on UCX master: - openucx/ucx#12150: pick the closest NIC per GPU. - openucx/ucx#12178: register whole ROCm allocations. - openucx/ucx#12228: UCM modules no longer call `ucs_status_string()`. Without it, when the ROCm BISTRO hook fails to install (e.g. with the torch-bundled HSA runtime), loading the UCX NIXL plugin fails with an undefined symbol. title: [Feat] [NPU] dsa: Token shard, every head for this rank's slice of the tokens (2/2)
summary: ﻿> The parent PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42977, DSA indexer query sharding) is merged; this branch is rebased on current main. ## Motivation In NPU DSA prefill, attention TP splits the heads: each rank computes its 1/`attn_tp_size` of the heads for every token. For sparse attention, each rank then reads and dequantizes the top-2048 KV rows for every query. So the KV reads, which dominate sparse attention, are repeated on every rank. This PR swaps the split for the attention core only. Each rank computes every head, but for its own slice of the tokens. The weights stay head-sharded. Only the attention core changes, between the `w_kc` absorb and `w_vc`. This is the same design as vLLM-Ascend's `enable_dsa_cp`. It needs no extra ranks, and unlike upstream prefill CP it works with attention TP > 1. ## Modifications - `dsa_token_shard.py` (new): the plan and the two all-to-alls. After the `w_kc` absorb, one all-to-all turns "my heads, every token" into "every head, my tokens". Sparse attention runs on that slice. A second all-to-all turns it back before `w_vc`. The KV write and the indexer stay full width. - `deepseek_v2.py`: when the flag is on, each DSA layer gets a full-head `RadixAttention` (`attn_mqa_for_dsa_token_shard`). It is keyed on `use_dsa`, not on the Indexer, because a skip-top-k layer has no Indexer but still attends. - `deepseek_v2_attention_mla_npu.py`, `ascend_backend.py`: the token-shard branch of the attention core, and per-rank query and KV lengths for the sparse operator. summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The OpenAI backend in `sgl-model-gateway` drops the upstream `Retry-After` header when proxying chat completion responses. In `OpenAIRouter::route_chat()`, the response is reconstructed from the upstream `reqwest` response. For non-streaming requests, only `Content-Type` is copied. For streaming requests, a new response is created with `text/event-stream`, without preserving `Retry-After`. As a result, an upstream `429 Too Many Requests` or `503 Service Unavailable` response reaches the client without the retry guidance supplied by the provider. This makes it difficult for clients to respect provider-side rate limits and temporary availability constraints when requests pass through the gateway. ### Reproduction Use a mock OpenAI-compatible upstream that: * Returns `test-model` from `GET /v1/models`. * Returns HTTP 429 from `POST /v1/chat/completions`. * Includes `Retry-After: 30` and a valid JSON error body in every response. title: [Fix] spec: Keep chain MTP prefill hidden states under DP attention
summary: ## Motivation Under DP attention, multi-layer EAGLE with a chain MTP draft (`chain_mtp_hidden_states`: `Step3p5MTP`, `InklingForConditionalGenerationMTP`, `GigaChat35ForCausalLMNextN`) builds the prompt's draft KV for every step after the first from zero hidden states. In `MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker._draft_extend_for_prefill`, a chain draft captures hidden states with `CaptureHiddenMode.FULL` and passes `output.logits_output.hidden_states`, one row per prompt token, to the next step. Under DP attention, `ModelRunner.forward` then calls `ForwardBatch.post_forward_mlp_sync_batch`, and its `EAGLE_DRAFT_EXTEND` (non-V2) arm slices `hidden_states` to `[:bs]`, the request count. The next step's `_pad_inputs_to_size` pads the missing rows with zeros. So steps 1..K-1 write the prompt's draft KV from the token embedding alone, with no context. - Step 0 reads the target hidden states and is unaffected. - Draft KV written during decode goes through the `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` arm, which keeps `bs * num_tokens_per_req` rows, and is correct. - Without DP attention, `post_forward_mlp_sync_batch` does not run. Multi-turn workloads, where most of the context arrives through prefill, lose acceptance from the second draft position on. ## Modifications - `ForwardBatch.post_forward_mlp_sync_batch`, `EAGLE_DRAFT_EXTEND` arm: when the batch captures FULL, slice `hidden_states` to `_original_num_tokens`, the token count before MLP-sync padding. Every other capture mode keeps the per-request slice, and `next_token_logits` keeps its per-request slice. - `test_mlp_sync_pad_unpad.py`: a draft-extend batch

title: [Fix] spec: Apply the multi-layer boundary-KV fix to non-hybrid chain MTP drafts
summary: ## Motivation The multi-layer EAGLE boundary-KV fix (`SGLANG_ENABLE_MTP_BOUNDARY_KV_FIX`, on by default, added in #31681) widens each draft-extend window by K - 1 front rows, plus the conv warm-up rows on hybrid models, and re-runs them so the draft KV at already-landed positions is rebuilt from confirmed tokens. `MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker._init_boundary_kv_fix_state` only turns it on when the request pool holds state slots, i.e. on hybrid (mamba / sconv) models. The conv warm-up rows are already gated on the pool on their own (`draft_extend_num_warmup_tokens`). The K - 1 rows come from the chain depth, not from the cache. So a chain draft (`chain_mtp_hidden_states`) on a plain cache never gets the fix, and its startup log never prints `SGLANG_ENABLE_MTP_BOUNDARY_KV_FIX on: draft-extend windows widened by ...`. Of the current chain drafts, `Step3p5MTP` runs on a plain cache. Why the rows matter: in chain MTP, step k at position q embeds the token at q + k + 1. A draft-extend window only covers the K + 1 new positions, so near its end that token is still a draft guess. The next window starts past those positions and never rewrites them. Each round, step k keeps min(k + 1, accept_len) landed positions whose draft KV was built from a token that was later rejected, and the count grows with k. ## Modifications - Gate the fix on `chain_mtp_hidden_states or req_to_token_pool.holds_state_slots`. Hybrid models are unchanged, and the conv warm-up rows stay hybrid-only. - Non-chain drafts on a plain cache (MiMoV2) still skip the fix, as #31681 set up. The guessed-token argument looks

title: [Feat] hicache: Store the MHA L2 host pool as INT8, 1.78x more cached tokens per GB
summary: ## Motivation HiCache stores L1 and L2 in the same dtype, so one byte of host DRAM buys one byte of cached KV. This keeps L1 BF16 for attention and stores L2 as INT8, restoring to BF16 on a hit. Caching policy, radix tree, scheduler and transfer engine are untouched; only the L2 representation changes. For Qwen3-8B at TP=1: 82,944 host bytes/token against 147,456, so a fixed `--hicache-size` holds **1.78x more tokens**. ## Design trade-off Every existing host pool mirrors its device pool's dtype, so the mover stays a byte copy. This one is asymmetric. The JIT mover takes separate strides but a single `element_size`, so a 2048-byte BF16 row cannot be written into a 1152-byte encoded row. Both directions stage through a same-width device buffer: ``` D2H device BF16 -> encode -> staging -> mover -> host arena H2D host arena -> mover -> staging -> decode -> device BF16 ``` That is 1.78x L2 capacity for two device staging buffers and an encode/decode per direction. If the codec cost dominates on some workload, a fused kernel or a mover-side adapter is the fix, and I would rather hear that now than after merge. ## Modifications New: `pool_host/int8_codec.py` (pure tensor logic, no SGLang imports), `pool_host/int8_staging.py` (the staging buffers), `pool_host/mha_int8.py` (`MHATokenToKVPoolHostINT8`), plus unit tests. `pool_host/mha.py`: 7 lines of dispatch in `get_mha_host_pool_cls`. MXFP8 and asymmetric pools keep precedence, since neither is representable in this record. `environ.py` and the env-var docs: two flags. title: [Fix] hicache: Keep write-back admission from promising device KV that eviction cannot free
summary: ## Motivation With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, prefill admission can promise device KV that eviction cannot free, and the scheduler then dies in `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend` with `Prefill out of memory`. Admission budgets with `full_available_size + full_evictable_size` (`mem_cache/prefill_budget.py`). Under write_back, freeing an unbacked device node needs either room in the host tier for its backup, or the drop fallback (`drop_subtree_no_host`), which is declined when any host-only descendant is pinned (storage-backup lock, load-back, prefetch anchor, write-through pending). When the host tier has no reclaimable room, those nodes stay on the device (`write_back: backup failed under host memory pressure but subtree drop declined`) but are still counted as evictable, so admission over-promises. Observed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 x 4 servers, write_back + Mooncake L3, `--hicache-ratio 1.2`, under an agentic multi-turn trace replay: all four TP schedulers raised ``` Prefill out of memory. Try to allocate 12527 tokens. Available full tokens: 242944 (full_available_size=768 + full_evictable_size_=242176) ``` ## Modifications - **Tree cores (Rust and Python):** one read-only post-order walk, `full_write_back_reclaim_classes()`, returns the FULL device tokens that are stuck (blocked, plus the evictable ancestors waiting behind them), need host room, or are droppable, and the host-only tokens eviction can reclaim. The drop-blocking rule is factored out of `drop_subtree_no_host` into one helper both use, so admission and eviction cannot disagree. - **`UnifiedRadixCac

title: [Perf] qwen3.8-flash: Improve HyperConnection performance on SM100
summary: ## Motivation Reduce HyperConnection (HC) kernel launches and intermediate memory traffic in Qwen-3.8-Flash around attention/MLP, without changing the core computation. Fuse Down and Inject, and reuse residual statistics across HC blocks instead of materializing a normalized residual at each block. This patch targets `main` and contains the HC optimization, its necessary framework integration and registered regression tests. The previously merged model support is not part of this patch. ## Modifications - **Fuse Down + Inject.** Fold the learned RMS scale into shared packed weights. Small T uses the custom GEMM epilogue to emit Down/SiLU and FP32 alpha; large T uses branch-batched GEMM with aligned output padding, followed by fused branch reduction, normalization, SiLU and sigmoid. - **Reuse cross-block RMS statistics.** Carry the raw residual and FP32 square sums in `HCSumState`. Down and Up/Mix reconstruct inverse RMS where needed. Initial or invalidated state still requires bootstrap statistics. - **Tune the remaining kernels.** Use register-only alpha output, configuration- sized shared memory, finer Up tiles, warp-shuffle post-processing and vectorized Apply. title: [Perf] muse-spark: EP Marlin tile density uses local expert count
summary: ## Problem Muse Spark uses the local expert count to select the Marlin tile size. With expert parallelism (EP), each GPU receives all token rows. Only some routes use its local experts. The current calculation overestimates the number of routes per expert. It can select a tile that is too large. ## Example For 128 tokens, top-k 8, and 256 experts across eight GPUs: | Calculation | Routes per expert | Selected tile rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Divide by 32 local experts | 32 | 48 | | Divide by 256 total experts | 4 | 8 | This occurs in `_marlin_expert_outputs` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/muse_spark/muse_spark_fp4_moe.py` at commit `b77d7b8573747aee535612413b5deb2fa178f86e`. ## Proposed change Use `global_num_experts` to estimate routes per expert. When EP is disabled, the selected tile sizes stay the same. Fix: #50508.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Skip DSA indexer host transfers with no pages
summary: ## Motivation A HiCache load that carries no DSA indexer pages kills the scheduler with SIGFPE (`Fatal Python error: Floating-point exception`). `DSAIndexerPoolHost._get_indexer_page_indices` passes empty index tensors through unchanged, and `load_to_device_per_layer` hands them to the kvcacheio kernel anyway. `transfer_kv_launcher` in `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/kvcacheio/transfer.cu` then sizes its grid like this: ```cpp const int64_t num_items = src_indices.numel(); // 0 const int64_t items_per_warp = div_up(num_items, block_quota * num_warps_per_block); // 0 const int32_t num_blocks = div_up(num_items, items_per_warp * num_warps_per_block); // (0 + 0 - 1) / 0 ``` That integer division by zero raises SIGFPE in the host process. Every `transfer_kv_per_layer*` and `transfer_kv_all_layer*` op goes through this launcher, so the backup paths have the same gap. The faulting stack, innermost first: - `transfer_kv_per_layer_mla_pf_lf` - `DSAIndexerPoolHost.load_to_device_per_layer` - `HostKVCache.load_to_device_per_layer_physical` - `l2_transfer.py` `submit_host_to_device` - `cache_controller.py` `start_loading` - `UnifiedRadixCache.ready_to_load_host_cache` - the scheduler's `get_new_batch_prefill` Nothing on that path filters out an empty per-pool transfer. We hit this under sustained multi-turn load: a hybrid DSA model, HiCache with the `page_first` layout, the `kernel` IO backend, and an L3 storage backend. It happened on a fork whose DSA host pool code matches main here. It recurred several times, and skipping empty indexer transfers stopped it. We have not reproduced t

title: [Fix] mamba: Warn about prefill checkpoint capacity
summary: ## Motivation Refs #36935. With full-precision device checkpoints taken at every chunk, the Mamba state pool can lose cached prefix states before the corresponding KV tokens are evicted. This startup diagnostic makes that capacity mismatch visible so users can tune the state pool or chunk size when branch-prefix reuse matters. ## Modifications - Estimate checkpoint demand as `ceil(final_KV_tokens / chunked_prefill_size)` and state the workload assumption in the warning: a KV pool filled with chunked prefixes, one state per chunk. Main's new default level 2 policy from #49886 checkpoints forks/end states, so it does not trigger this estimate. Also skip disabled radix caching, capped paths, separate int8 or host-only checkpoint pools, and unified memory. title: [Fix] diffusion: Stop the multi-rank IPC all-to-all leak with one IPC handle per peer
summary: ## Motivation Diffusion servers that use the multi-rank IPC all-to-all (Ulysses > 2, head-group pipeline) leak GPU memory whenever the request geometry changes. On 8x B300 at Ulysses 8, a video DiT whose sequence length differs per request gained about 2 GB of live memory per request and ran out of memory after about 50 requests. Workloads with a few fixed shapes leak slowly. Root cause: `IpcA2AMultiState._share` exported each buffer with a single `reduce_tensor` handle, and all `world - 1` peers opened it. torch keeps one IPC reference count per handle and frees the producer's block only when that count returns to zero. Several consumers releasing one count never bring it back to zero, so no dropped buffer was ever freed: - the `_PipelinePool` dropped when a new plan is built; - staging buffers evicted from the LRU. ## Modifications All changes are in `ipc_a2a_multi.py`: - `_share` exports one handle per peer; each peer opens its own. - `_release_shared()` synchronizes, runs a group barrier and calls `torch.cuda.ipc_collect()`. It runs after a pipeline pool is dropped and after a staging buffer is evicted. Both sites are reached in the same order on every rank, so the old buffers are freed before the new ones are allocated. - `drop_staging()` also calls `torch.cuda.ipc_collect()`. The two-rank `ipc_a2a.py` path has one consumer per handle and is unaffected. ## Accuracy / outputs Unchanged. Outputs are byte-identical before and after the fix: 40/40 and 20/20 mp4 md5 matches on two workloads, with a deterministic baseline confirmed across three runs. ## Benchmarking and vali

title: [Fix] sampling: Reject expensive Python stop regexes
summary: ## Motivation **Impact: one expensive `stop_regex` can stall unrelated requests sharing the same scheduler.** The scheduler runs CPython `re.search` synchronously during decode-result processing. While that search is occupied, the scheduler cannot advance other requests assigned to it. Streaming responses can stop progressing, queued work can accumulate, and otherwise valid requests can hit their client timeouts. This is a host-side scheduling bottleneck; healthy GPUs do not remove it. The small reproduction demonstrates how little generated text is needed to trigger the problem. On base `95999790a4`, a six-character pattern, `(a+)+b`, searching a 28-character synthetic no-match tail exceeded our two-second limit; we terminated the child rather than waiting for completion. **Two seconds is a measured lower bound, not the full stall duration.** These particular patterns have compounding backtracking costs, so longer matching prefixes can become dramatically more expensive. Ordinary regexes do not become pathological merely because a completion is long: the trigger is the combination of an expensive pattern and a suitable output tail. Real generations can readily exceed 28 characters, so small request/pattern byte limits do not adequately address this failure mode. An additional CPU check used the ordinary 28-character English sentence `Please summarize the report.` with `(?:.?){30}Z`.
