title: [Perf] spec: Avoid blocking H2D for MRoPE delta in spec decode
summary: ## Motivation `ForwardBatch.compute_spec_mrope_positions` builds the per-step MRoPE position tensor for multimodal requests by stacking each request's `mrope_position_delta` on host and shipping it to device with `.to(device=device)`. The source (`torch.stack`'s output) is pageable, so PyTorch appends a `cudaStreamSynchronize` to that H2D copy — the driver cannot let the DMA proceed asynchronously because the OS could swap the source page mid-transfer. The host blocks until every kernel already queued on the stream has retired. This function runs every step of speculative decode (both target verify and draft extend call it), so the queued work behind the sync is the whole in-flight draft/verify window. On an MTP (NEXTN) deployment (TP8), this turned an 8-byte copy into a multi-millisecond stall per call — profiling showed two such stalls per decode step (~1.4ms and ~7.7ms), each draining the stream and then starving the GPU while the host re-issued kernels one at a time instead of running ahead on a primed queue. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications Stage the stacked delta tensor through pinned host memory before the H2D, so `non_blocking=True` actually applies (it only takes effect when the source is pinned): ```python stacked = torch.stack(deltas, dim=0) if stacked.device.type != "cpu" or not is_pin_memory_available(device): return stacked.to(device=device) staging = torch.empty(stacked.shape, dtype=stacked.dtype, pin_memory=True) staging.copy_(stacked) return staging.to(device=device, non_blocking=True) ``` CUDA's per-stream orde

Together with paged experts (#42557, #48642, #49195) this serves the full model on a 16 GB card. title: [Perf] [AMD] spec: Skip the vocabulary-wide sort in MTP rejection-sampling verify
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at concurrency 16 spends 2.2 ms of each decode step building dense target probabilities for the MTP verify. ROCm EAGLE/NEXTN with `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` uses rejection sampling by default, so every verify runs a softmax, `top_k_renorm_prob` and `top_p_renorm_prob` over all `bs × num_draft_tokens` rows. On HIP, both renorms run a vocabulary-wide `torch.sort`, and top-p adds a `cumsum`. #46808 makes top-p sort-free, but top-k still sorts. The compact top-k branch (`SGLANG_OPT_SPEC_COMPACT_VERIFY_SAMPLING`) does not help, because it requires rejection sampling to be off. Top-k sampling only ever picks from each row's top-k tokens, so the other ~248k tokens in the vocabulary carry no probability. Qwen3.8 ships `top_k=20` in `generation_config.json`, so every AgentX request sets one. This PR builds the target probabilities for those top-k tokens only, instead of sorting the whole vocabulary, and passes them to the unchanged `chain_speculative_sampling_triton`. The result matches the existing dense path (softmax plus top-k and top-p renorms over the whole vocabulary), ties included. On MI355X the target-probability step goes from 2.74 ms to 0.30 ms at 64 rows, and eager time per decode step goes from 3.34 ms to 1.23 ms. Batches where any request has `top_k` outside 2 to 128 (including no top-k) keep the dense path. #41283 takes the same approach on CUDA with a new chain kernel, but it is CUDA-only and no longer applies to `main`. ## Modifications - `eagle_utils.py`: - New `_sparse_rejection_target_probs` builds the target probabil

title: [AMD][Fix][MiniMax-M3] Choose the aiter FP8 cache mode from the pool's KV scales
summary: ## Motivation `MiniMaxM3Attention._aiter_sparse_qknorm_cache` hardcodes `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3_unit"` for any FP8 main cache. aiter has two FP8 cache modes and they are not interchangeable — both contracts are asserted in `csrc/kernels/fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm.cu`: | mode | scale | scale tensors | |---|---|---| | `fp8_e4m3_unit` | fixed at 1.0 | **refused** — *"fp8_e4m3_unit does not accept k_scale/v_scale tensors"* | | `fp8_e4m3_static` | from the pool | **required**, single-element contiguous fp32 | So the mode has to be chosen from the pool's actual per-tensor scales. title: [Fix] scheduler: Avoid cancellation in dynamic chunk-size prediction
summary: ## Motivation The PP dynamic-prefill chunk-size predictor evaluates the positive root of `A*x**2 + B*x - target_latency = 0` by subtracting `B` from `sqrt(B**2 + 4*A*target_latency)`. Those values can be nearly equal when the linear latency term dominates. Cancellation then changes the predicted chunk before integer conversion and page alignment. For example, with `a=1e-8`, `b=0.01`, `history_len=0`, and base chunk size 2048, the existing target-latency calculation gives a mathematical root of 2048, but the current expression returns approximately `2047.9999999999804`. Both the default smoothing factor 0.75 and factor 1.0 therefore yield **1984** after 64-token page alignment. With `a=1e-20` and `b=1`, cancellation instead produces zero and unnecessarily takes the static fallback. ## Modifications - Rationalize the same positive root to `-2*C / (B + sqrt_discriminant)`. - Preserve the static fallback if the rationalized denominator underflows to zero. - Extend the existing registered CPU test file with six regression methods covering zero-history page boundaries, a nearly linear model, high-precision reference roots (including zero linear coefficient), existing caps/page alignment, and the unready/underflow fallbacks. The fit, target latency, smoothing coefficient, minimum chunk size, context margin, maximum chunk size, and page-alignment policy are unchanged. No new dependency or model/kernel change is introduced. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output or end-to-end inference accuracy test was run. This patch changes numeric chunk-size prediction, not model weights or sampling

Prepending late messages to the root system prompt mutates the prefix on every turn, defeating SGLang's RadixAttention prefix caching and causing severe TTFT regressions across multi-turn agent loops. ### Solution - Updated `spec_supports_inline_system` in `chat_encoding.py` to recognize all verified native encoders (`kimi_k3`, `dsv41`, `dsv4`, `dsv32`, `inkling`) that render conversation turns sequentially in place. - Updated `test_serving_responses.py` parametrization to assert that `dsv32`, `dsv4`, `dsv41`, and `inkling` preserve the prompt prefix and maintain inline placement (`preserve=True`). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #43585635720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43585635720)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #43585635712](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43585635712)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:x: [Run #43585635626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/43585635626)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end --> > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Perf] [Apple] layernorm: Add a Metal RMSNorm for the Torch MPS path
summary: ## Motivation First part of the "direct Metal semantic ops for eager" item in the Apple Silicon roadmap (#32321): RMSNorm on the Torch MPS eager path. SiLU-and-mul follows in a separate PR. Today `RMSNorm` has no MPS path, so on Apple Silicon it runs `forward_native`: an fp32 upcast, `pow`, `mean`, `rsqrt` and two multiplies, each a separate MPS kernel with its own fp32 intermediate. This PR replaces that with one Metal kernel per call. ## Modifications - `fused_op.py`: add an `"mps"` platform key, so `BaseFusedOp` dispatches to `forward_mps` on Apple Silicon. Ops that don't define `forward_mps` still fall back to `forward_native`, so nothing else changes. - `kernels/ops/layernorm/rmsnorm_mps.py` (new): RMSNorm and fused add + RMSNorm, compiled with `torch.mps.compile_shader`. One threadgroup per row. The sum of squares and the residual add are done in fp32, like `forward_native`; only the stores round to the input dtype. Supports fp32, fp16 and bf16. Inputs are never modified; the fused variant returns `(out, x + residual)`. - `layernorm.py`: `RMSNorm.forward_mps` uses the kernel for the plain variant. Everything else goes to `forward_native`: `post_residual_addition`, `var_hidden_size`, `cast_x_before_out_mul`, `fp32_residual`, `override_orig_dtype`, and mismatched dtypes or shapes. - `test_rmsnorm_mps.py` (new, registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mps`): parity against `forward_native` and a dispatch test. ## Accuracy Tests `test_rmsnorm_mps.py` compares against `RMSNorm.forward_native` for fp32/fp16/bf16, with and without residual, on shapes `(1, 7)`, `(3, 64)`, `(5, 1000)`

title: [Perf] HiCache PP-sync drain makes the PP prefill scheduler lock-step across ranks
summary: ## Summary With HiCache enabled on a pipeline-parallel prefill server, every scheduler round on PP rank `r` blocks until PP rank `r+1` has received the previous round's HiCache PP-sync message. PP0's loop therefore cannot run more than one round ahead of PP1's. PP1 is held back by PP2 in the same way, and so on down the pipeline. `--pp-async-batch-depth` is meant to let PP0 run ahead, and this backpressure cancels much of that. PP0's GPU then sits idle while runnable work is queued. ## Mechanism 1. [`check_hicache_events`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py#L3609) calls `_drain_async_work()` at the start of every round. 2. [`_drain_async_work`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py#L354-L364) then `wait()`s on every `isend` from the previous round. 3. Those sends come from [`_pp_sync`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/78185f4b3f565cbe0fec20d71bb5deb372428e80/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py#L379-L400): PP0 sends its ready counts down the pipeline with tag `HICACHE_PP_SYNC`. Each rank `r > 0` posts a blocking `recv` for them from its own `check_hicache_events`. 4. Each send is a CPU tensor on the PP group, so it uses gloo. It completes only once the receiver has posted the matching `recv`. As a result, round `k+1` on PP0 waits until PP1 reaches the HiCache step of its round `k`. Getting there includes PP1's whole tail of round `k-1` (`d2h_wait`, result p

title: [Perf] hicache: Let the PP-sync channel run the pipeline's depth ahead, not one round (#45351)
summary: Fixes #45351. Related: #45357 (hang in the same wait; this does not fix a rank that never posts its recv, see below), #42433 (removes the channel in cache mode on the old bootstrap ring), #28916 (the single-round drain). ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache._pp_sync` posts one gloo `isend` per `_all_reduce` to the next PP rank, and `_drain_async_work` waits on all of the previous round's sends at the start of every `check_hicache_events`. A gloo send completes only when the receiver posts the matching `recv`, and rank r+1 posts it inside its own HiCache step, after its forward launch, result processing and the other PP receives. So rank r's round k+1 cannot start until rank r+1 reached round k's HiCache step: the pipeline runs in lock-step on this channel and `--pp-async-batch-depth` cannot let PP0 run ahead. #45351 measured ~20% of PP0's loop in that wait on a PP8 prefill server with runnable work queued. Measured with the same gloo calls on CPU (torch 2.14.1): `isend()` returns in 0.2 ms, eight back-to-back sends issue in 3 ms, every send completes exactly when the receiver posts its recv, and `Work.is_completed()` never turns true on its own, only `wait()` reports completion. That last point is why the pre-#28916 non-blocking reap never reaped, and why a window has to be counted rather than polled. ## Modifications - `unified_radix_cache.py`: `work_list` becomes `work_rounds`, a deque of per-round send lists. `_bound_async_work` (replacing `_drain_async_work`) opens the new round and waits out the oldest round only while more than `pp_sync_window = pp_size + pp_async_batch_d

title: [Fix] FA3: size k/v descale from query segments in extend and decode
summary: ## Motivation FA3 validates k/v descale batch dimensions against the query segments passed to the same attention call. DP padding can grow the logical forward batch after attention metadata is built. This produces a descale shape mismatch in speculative draft extend and decode. ## Modifications - Derive descale batch size from `cu_seqlens_q.numel() - 1`, falling back to the logical batch size when absent. - Re-expand descales after selecting the extend call's query metadata. - Use the query segment count when preparing decode descales. - Cover mismatched, matching and absent metadata, including a mocked `forward_decode` call with 25 logical rows and 24 query segments. ## Accuracy Tests GPU evidence is from a port onto public release/v0.5.23 (`297e54fd105e974cdf401e5b4d20253a22c16f90`) with the same extend and decode production changes, not a direct GPU run of this PR candidate or current main. 8x H800 80GB, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 with an EAGLE3 draft, FA3 + FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8 attention. Base reproduces the descale exception in draft decode. Patched code completes 1696 load-test requests; a separate diagnostic run observes mismatches in both decode and DRAFT_EXTEND_V2. GSM8K full test split, 1319 problems, sgl-eval 0.1.3, temperature 0, max tokens 2048: | Configuration | Correct / total | Accuracy | |---|---|---| | Base, DP8 attention, no speculation | 1261/1319 | 95.60% | | Patched, DP8 attention + EAGLE3 | 1264/1319 | 95.83% | | Patched, same configuration repeated | 1263/1319 | 95.75% | | Patched, DP8 attention, no speculation | 1264/1319 | 95.83% | | Base, EA

title: [Feat] unified_cache: Support MXFP8 KV caches in the direct external linker
summary: ## Motivation `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` (the long-context recipe for Inkling) fails at startup with `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker`: the direct linker rejects any KV pool with scale buffers. ## Modifications - `_mha_device_pool_entry` packs the MXFP8 K/V UE8M0 scale buffers into the KV page object after the FP8 payload. Only whole aligned pages move and a page's scales are contiguous in both the interleaved (`page_size=128`) and flat layouts, so each scale buffer is viewed as uint8 rows aligned with the payload slots. No new pool names or storage keys. - FP4 scaled KV pools are still rejected. ## Accuracy Inkling (`--revision test`, 1x B200, fa4, page size 128, deterministic inference, Mooncake over RDMA). title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Load layers that match no target as unquantized
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #46335. SGLang cannot build a model from a compressed-tensors checkpoint that leaves a layer out of both `config_groups[*].targets` and `ignore`. llm-compressor writes such checkpoints for experts-only and attention-only quantization. It sets `"ignore": []` and stores every untargeted layer unquantized. SGLang raises on the first of those layers, before it loads any weight: ``` File ".../layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py", line 144, in find_matched_target ValueError: Unable to find matching target for model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz in the compressed-tensors config. ``` The checkpoint that hit this is [`bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/bottlecapai/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) at `df3922b2`. It is a `qwen4_exp` model whose config targets only the routed experts, with NVFP4 weight-only quantization: ```json "config_groups": {"group_0": {"targets": ["re:.*mlp\\.experts\\.\\d+\\.(gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)$"], "input_activations": null, "...": "..."}}, "ignore": [], "sparsity_config": {} ``` A missing `packed_modules_mapping` is not the cause. Qwen4-Exp already maps `in_proj_qkvz` to `in_proj_qkv` and `in_proj_z`, and the config targets neither shard. Today the checkpoint only loads with `--json-model-override-args` replacing the whole `quantization_config`, with `"ignore": ["re:^(?!.*mlp\\.experts).*$"]` added. vLLM has loaded untargeted layers as unquantized since vllm-project/vllm#41965. title: [Feature] [Rust server] Encode only what a multi-turn chat prompt appends to an earlier prompt
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation A multi-turn chat re-sends the whole conversation on every turn. With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, the server renders and encodes all of it again each time, even though almost all of the prompt was encoded on the previous turn. On a long multi-turn agent trace (Gemma-4-31B, 12,880 chat requests, 16.6K prompt tokens on average), replayed offline through the server's own render and encode path: - Encoding takes 99.6% of the frontend's CPU per request. The p50 is 46 ms and the p95 is 74 ms. Template render and JSON parsing together take under 0.2 ms. - That time sits on the TTFT path of every request. More tokenizer threads (#49190, #49193) remove queueing during bursts, but they cannot shorten one encode: on H200 (TP4, c100), 64 tokenizer threads gave the same TTFT as 4. Existing reuse mechanisms don't cover this case: - The L1 prefix cache in dynamo-tokenizers (enabled in sgl-router by #41268) cuts only after special tokens. This client sends the whole history inside one `user` message, so the L1 cache reused 0.17% of tokens. - toktier (#44374) targets the Python tokenizer manager and sgl-router, not `rust/sglang-server`, and it excludes Gemma 4 because Gemma 4's tokenizer pipeline has no pre-tokenization boundaries. **Proposal:** keep recent prompts with their ids and offsets. title: dspark_accept SoftmaxTemp.execute (flashinfer branch) returns NaN rows on GB10 in 6/17 cold starts — cross-ref flashinfer#9486
summary: ### Summary On NVIDIA GB10 (SM 12.1, DGX Spark), in 6 of 17 cold starts of an SGLang v0.5.22 server with speculative decoding (DSPINE plugin, chain/rejection sampling), the FlashInfer branch of `SoftmaxTemp.execute` (`sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py`) returns probability tensors with entire rows NaN from verifiably healthy logits. Consequences: all draft tokens rejected (accept rate 0.00), bonus scan never crosses threshold, output degenerates to the vocab-end token repeated forever, decode drops to ~6 tok/s. `temperature=0` is unaffected (argmax path never calls this softmax). Full evidence chain, in-server probe data and the negative standalone-repro result are in the upstream issue: **https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/9486** ### Two SGLang-side notes beyond the upstream report 1. **Dispatch visibility**: `SoftmaxTemp.execute` prefers `_flashinfer_softmax` (`flashinfer.sampling.softmax`) whenever the import succeeds — the `--sampling-backend` option does not control this softmax at all. This made the failure look like a "sampling backend" issue during triage; it may be worth exposing this dispatch or logging which branch is active, since spec-decode users on non-standard hardware silently depend on it. 2. **Caller-side workaround (deployed, verified on our machine)**: replacing the call in the plugin's `build_dspine_target_probs` with pure `torch.softmax(logits / temperature)` eliminates the failure (17/17 cold boots clean, incl. a 12-boot regression battery over temps 0.3–1.0 / top-p / top-k / min-p / batch 1–3; accept rate stable

title: [MeetUp][NPU] GDN hybrid models (Qwen3.8-27B) crash on Ascend 910B unless --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16
summary: ### Current problem Deploying Qwen3.8-27B (GDN hybrid linear-attention architecture) on Ascend 910B (A2) with default server args starts successfully but crashes on the first request: ``` RuntimeError: FP32 initial_state is only supported on Ascend950 (arch35) ``` Root cause: the SSM states pool defaults to `float32` (`--mamba-ssm-dtype`), and the NPU kernel `torch.ops.npu.chunk_gated_delta_rule` (called from the ascend GDN backend `chunk_gdn` path) does not support FP32 `initial_state` on Ascend 910B (arch32) - only on Ascend950 (arch35). ### Expected behavior The server should either work out-of-the-box on 910B, or fail fast at startup with a clear error message, instead of crashing on the first inference request. ### Suggested fix (any of) 1. Auto-select `bfloat16` SSM dtype on 910B when the model uses GDN/linear attention 2. Add a startup validation that raises a clear error for this combination 3. Document `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` as a mandatory arg for GDN models on 910B (Qwen3.6-27B tutorial & best-practices pages) ### Environment - Image: sglang:cann9.1.0-910b-20261112 - Hardware: Ascend A2 (910B3 x4), TP=4 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B (BF16), also reproduced with Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 - SGLang: main (0.0.0.dev22121+g0fa9ff55f.d20261112) ### Workaround ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server ... --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 ``` Related PR: #50485 (MeetUp practice report with full deployment/tuning details)

title: [NPU][Qwen3.8-27B] Docs: Add A2 (910B3) deployment guidance, 128K prefix-cache best practice, and fix testing instructions
summary: MeetUp task ID: `hw_008615958372123_01` ## 1. Current state / problems found Environment used: SGLang `0.0.0.dev22121+g0fa9ff55f`, CANN 9.1.0, Atlas 800I A2 (910B3) × 4, TP=4. 1. **No Ascend NPU doc page for Qwen3.8-27B.** Only `qwen3_6_27b.mdx` exists. Qwen3.8-27B uses `model_type: qwen3_5`, so users cannot tell from the docs whether it is supported, and must guess that the 3.6-27B guide applies unchanged. 2. **Best practices are A3-only.** Every table targets A3 (2 dies per card, TP=2). title: [Perf] disaggregation: Hold PD decode starts on DP ranks above the fleet-mean running count
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention on a PD decode server, every DP rank's decode step lasts as long as the busiest rank's: ranks pad to the largest batch for the MoE/collective phase. Requests are placed on DP ranks when they arrive, but the per-rank running counts still drift apart as requests finish at different times. On DSv4.1-Flash with DEP16 decode, the busiest rank runs about 1.22x the mean, so every step pays for lanes that most ranks do not have. ## Modifications New server arg `--disaggregation-decode-lane-balance-margin` (int, **default 3, on**; set 0 to disable). It acts only on a PD decode server with DP attention and attention TP/CP size 1. Any other layout keeps the current admission unchanged. Algorithm, per decode scheduling step on each DP rank: 1. Read the per-rank running counts from the last MLP-sync gather. A new `DPRankRows` carrier on `SchedulerDPAttnAdapter` keeps `global_num_tokens`, which in decode is the running batch size (0 for an idle rank). Every rank holds the same list, so no communication is added. 2. Compute `cap = ceil(mean(rows)) + margin`. The rank starts new prebuilt requests only up to `cap - running`, within the existing `max_running_requests` limit. 3. Release past the cap, so total admission is never capped: - by count: if more than 16 startable requests are held on the rank, the excess starts; - by wait: a request that has waited 1 s in the decode waiting queue starts. Requests still waiting on a host-memory restore are not counted. 4. While it acts, each rank logs one line every 60 s: cap range, max/mean of the running counts, held

title: [Fix] watchdog: send SIGQUIT even if diagnostics hang
summary: Fixes #43205 ## Motivation When the scheduler stops making progress, the hard watchdog runs `dump_info()` and `py-spy dump`, then logs the timeout, then sends SIGQUIT. If a diagnostic never returns, the timeout is never logged and SIGQUIT is never sent. The server stays frozen with no error and no restart. We hit this on a DP-attention decode server. One rank's scheduler thread blocked in `stat()` on a stalled NFS mount, the other ranks waited in a collective, and all GPUs sat at 0%. The watchdog fired and started `py-spy dump --native`. That call stats every mapped file, and some of those files were on the same mount, so it went into uninterruptible sleep too. Nothing was logged for the rest of the incident, and the server never restarted. Three more paths in `pyspy_dump_schedulers` can end the same way: - `subprocess.run` has no timeout, so a hung py-spy blocks the watchdog forever. - With a timeout, `TimeoutExpired` is not caught. It reaches `_watchdog_thread`, which logs "watchdog thread crashed" and returns. That leaves no SIGQUIT and no watchdog for the rest of the process's life. - `shell=True` means a timeout kills `sh` instead of py-spy. #43546 fixes the ordering in `watchdog.py`. This PR applies the same ordering, which is why it also closes #43205, and adds the py-spy side. ## Modifications - `watchdog.py`: - Log the timeout first. - Run `dump_info` and the py-spy dump in a daemon thread. Wait for it at most `_DIAGNOSTICS_TIMEOUT_S` (60 s), and catch and log any exception it raises. - Then run `before_crash` and send SIGQUIT as before, however the diagnostics end

title: [Perf] diffusion: Look up the rounded SiLU of the gated activation in a table on sm_10x
summary: ## Motivation One MiniMax-H3 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps) on one B300 takes about 119 s and keeps the GPU busy 99.8% of the time. FA4 and the GEMMs account for about 93% of it, at the GPU's 1100 W power cap. This is one of five independent, bit-exact cuts to the small kernels around them (#50387, #50388, #50390, #50391, #50392); each PR stands on its own. The rounded SiLU-and-mul kernel (SiLU rounded to the activation dtype, then times `up`) spends about 30 instructions per element on `expf` and the IEEE divide. Under the power-capped clock that makes it ALU-bound: 750 us per H3 MLP in serving against 533 us on an idle GPU. ## Modifications - The rounded SiLU of a bf16/fp16 gate depends only on its 16 bits. A 65536-entry table, built once per device and dtype by the same device function (`apply_activation_f32<kSiLU, kFastMath>`, so the same `kFastMath` as the kernel it replaces), holds every value the kernel can produce. - The rounding kernels copy it into shared memory and look the activation up. The multiply by `up` and the final rounding are unchanged, so the bytes are identical. - Enabled on sm_10x, where it was measured, when the 128 KiB shared-memory opt-in is available. Graph capture before the table exists keeps the computed kernel. - Merged with #48942 (FP32 activation functions unified under `kFastMath`): the table kernel takes the struct's `kFastMath`. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_activation.py` adds a check over every gate bit pattern, for bf16 and fp16, in place and out of place. title: [Feat] scheduler: Expose single-iteration API
summary: ## Motivation An in-process RL rollout driver currently has to copy the scheduler's event-loop bodies to advance generation one iteration at a time. This adds a supported single-step entry point for that use case. Addresses #48472. ## Modifications - Add `Scheduler.run_one_iteration()` for the normal and overlap schedulers without receiving tokenizer or RPC input. Callers inject requests separately on the schedule stream and drive the same iterations on every TP rank. - Share the scheduling bodies with the existing continuous loops, initialize the step driver once, and retain pending overlap results across calls. Preserve work submitted on the original schedule stream if initialization replaces it. - Continue internal per-iteration maintenance, including broadcasting timeout aborts to TP ranks, without reading external input. Reject PP, PD/role-switch and MLX modes explicitly. - Scope both scheduler watchdogs to explicit iteration calls, refresh the existing heartbeat before rearming, and preserve caller-owned gaps with overlap work in flight. Add deterministic watchdog regressions, CPU scheduler tests, and a real-model single-GPU comparison. ## Accuracy Tests - CPU scheduler regression suite: **100 passed** and **34 subtests passed**, including a two-process Gloo test for empty/timeout/empty broadcasts, watchdog gap/rearm/stall and exception coverage, queue lifetime, pause, shutdown, and the existing continuous loops. title: [Perf] ngram: Freeze external-corpus SAMs into a compact layout
summary:
Motivation

External corpora for ngram speculative decoding (#21425, #22203) are stored as a SuffixAutomaton in which every state owns a std::unordered_map of transitions plus two sorted child vectors. After finalize() the SAM is read-only, but it kept this build-time layout for the lifetime of the server, costing ~525 bytes of host RAM per corpus token.

At the default --speculative-ngram-external-corpus-max-tokens 10000000 that is ~5.0 GB per scheduler process, and every scheduler running NGRAMWorker builds its own copy (startup corpora load in NGRAMWorker.__init__; HTTP-added corpora are broadcast to every TP rank). TP=8 therefore needs ~40 GB of host RAM for one full-budget corpus. On my 8 GB test machine, loading a default-budget corpus through NgramCorpus was OOM-killed on main; with this PR it fits in 542 MB.

Related roadmap: #21052

Modifications

Only suffix_automaton.{h,cpp} change. There is no change to Ngram, the FFI surface, or Python.

  • finalize() now ends with freeze_(), which copies the automaton into flat arrays and releases the build-time states_:
    • per state (16 B): link_, max_len_, occ_count_ (uint32_t), edge_begin_
    • per edge (16 B): edge_token_ / edge_target_, sorted by token within each state, plus <

title: [Fix] observability: Report a converted decode batch as decode in forward pass metrics
summary: ## Motivation Under DP attention, when one DP rank runs a decode batch while a peer rank runs prefill in the same step, the decode batch is viewed as 1-token extends so that every rank replays the extend graphs (`maybe_convert_decode_to_extend` -> `ScheduleBatch.convert_decode_to_extend`). The batch still only decodes, and the result path already treats it that way (`decoding_reqs`, `prefill_stats = None`). `ForwardPassMetrics` did not: `_build_scheduled_request_metrics` classified the step by its `EXTEND` mode and published every decoding request as a prefill request with zero prefill tokens and no decode requests, for example for a 2-request decode batch: ``` num_prefill_requests: 2, sum_prefill_tokens: 0, sum_prefill_kv_tokens: 64, num_decode_requests: 0, sum_decode_kv_tokens: 0 ``` A consumer of the per-step metrics (the Dynamo planner) then sees decode load disappear and phantom prefill requests on that rank for the step. On main `bd47834099` with 2 DP ranks, 29 of 4,640 published steps were such converted steps, and all 29 were published as prefill. ## Modifications - `_build_scheduled_request_metrics`: a batch in `ForwardMode.EXTEND` with a non-empty `decoding_reqs` is a converted decode batch (a fresh prefill batch never carries `decoding_reqs` outside `MIXED`; `convert_decode_to_extend` sets it to all requests). Such a batch is kept out of the prefill branch and reported through the existing decode branch, from the launch-time `seq_lens_cpu`. The step therefore publishes exactly what it publishes as a plain decode step. Mixed batches and every other mode are untouc

title: [NPU][Docs] W8A8 keeps less KV cache than BF16 at the same `--mem-fraction-static`
summary: ## Environment - SGLang image: `cann9.1.0-910b-20261112` - Hardware: Ascend A2 (910B3) x4, TP4 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B BF16 vs Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8 (ModelSlim quantized, same checkpoint family) - Launch args differ only in the weights path; both use `--mem-fraction-static 0.82` ## What happened The quantized checkpoint is 29 GB against 52 GB for BF16, so I expected the W8A8 run to expose a larger KV cache budget. The opposite happened: | Build | Weights | KV cache capacity reported at startup | | --- | --- | --- | | BF16 | 52 GB | ~2.02M tokens | | W8A8 | 29 GB | ~1.84M tokens | At a fixed `--mem-fraction-static`, the draft model, the quantization scale buffers and the extra workspace all count against the same memory fraction, and the reduction in weight bytes does not translate into extra KV capacity. This is counter-intuitive when sizing `--context-length` for 128K inputs: the quantized build is the one that runs out first. ## Expected The Ascend quantization docs should warn that `--mem-fraction-static` is a fraction of total HBM, not of the free memory after weights, and that W8A8 does not automatically yield more KV cache. A short table like the one above would have saved a debugging cycle.

title: [NPU][Docs] Prefix-cache guidance is contradictory on the Qwen3.6-27B best-practices page
summary: ## Current behavior The Qwen3.6-27B best-practices page lists a 64k+1k / 90% prefix-cache-hit configuration whose launch command keeps prefix caching enabled: ``` --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer (no --disable-radix-cache) ``` while most other configurations on the same page pass: ``` --disable-radix-cache ``` There is no sentence explaining that the flag must stay off for prefix-reuse workloads and is only appropriate for random-input traffic. Anyone copying a benchmark command from one section to another, or tuning a 90% hit-rate case, can silently disable prefix caching and measure a much lower throughput. Page: https://docs.sglang.io/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_6_27b ## Expected behavior Add a short note next to the flag explaining when it must be omitted (prefix-shared / gsp datasets, 90% hit-rate cases) and when it is used (random-input benchmarks, redundant with PD decode). ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the Qwen3.6-27B best-practices page. 2. Compare the 64k+1k prefix90 command with the random-input commands. 3. Add `--disable-radix-cache` to the prefix90 command and rerun with `--dataset-name generated-shared-prefix`: prefix caching is off, so the 90% hit rate the configuration is tuned for cannot be reached. ## Environment image `lmsysorg/sglang:cann9.1.0-910b-20261112`, Atlas A2 910B3 x4, sglang 0.0.0.dev22121+g0fa9ff55f.d20261112

title: [NPU][Docs] Missing model deployment page for Qwen3.8-27B
summary: ## What happened The Ascend model deployment section covers Qwen3 / Qwen3.6 27B-style checkpoints, but there is no page for Qwen3.8-27B. Its architecture differs in ways that change the launch flags: - hybrid linear attention, so `--attention-backend` and the mamba/linear-attention cache flags matter on NPU - NEXTN / MTP head shipped with the checkpoint, exposed through `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` - both BF16 and W8A8 (ModelSlim) variants are published, and the quantized one is not a drop-in replacement for the BF16 flags ## Impact Copying a Qwen3.6-27B command and changing only `--model-path` produces either a startup failure or a silently mis-configured server. I spent a full tuning cycle deriving a working command for 128K input / 1K output. ## Suggestion Add a tutorial + best-practices pair for Qwen3.8-27B (BF16 and W8A8) mirroring the existing Qwen3.6-27B pages, including: - verified launch commands for TP4 on 910B3 - GSM8K results under a stated protocol - the 128K-input / 1K-output throughput point with the TPOT constraint Happy to share the measured commands and numbers if a maintainer wants a starting draft.

title: [Fix] [AMD] QSA: Fit the relative prefill indexer kernel in gfx942 LDS
summary: ## What Caps the K pipeline depth of the request-relative QSA prefill scoring kernel to the device's shared-memory limit on ROCm. On MI300 (gfx942) with bf16 this means two stages instead of three; gfx950 and fp8 keep three. Behaviour on other platforms is unchanged (the new check is behind `is_hip()`). ## Why Since #45791, the MI300 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next nightly fails on all three ROCm lanes ([example job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40552118021/job/122358344976)). The server dies on the first prefill: ``` RuntimeError: Initialization failed: Requested dynamic shared memory 81920 exceeds device limit 65536 for kernel_kernel ... qsa_indexer.py select_prefill_tokens -> mqa.py tilelang_qsa_mqa_prefill_relative ``` The kernel keeps a [128, 128] bf16 Q tile (32 KiB) plus three pipelined [64, 128] K tiles (48 KiB), 80 KiB in total. gfx942 allows 64 KiB of LDS per workgroup. With two stages it needs exactly 64 KiB. The same jobs passed on the nightly before #45791 merged; the MI355 lanes are not affected (160 KiB LDS). ## Notes for the reviewer The stage count is computed from Triton's `max_shared_mem` for the device rather than keyed on the gfx arch, the same way `triton_sparse_mla.py` sizes its KV tile. ## Test plan - [x] `nightly-2-gpu-mi30x-qwen38-flash-next-fp8` (rocm10) on this commit: [passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40637569607/job/122647959804), GSM8K 0.970 (threshold 0.94; 0.973 on the last nightly before #45791) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #406376301

title: [Fix] weight-sync: Add selector to update_weights_from_disk
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #46806. `update_weights_from_disk` always reloads every model runner. Under speculative decoding with a separate draft checkpoint (DFLASH in the issue), the target's `model_path` is therefore also loaded into the draft. The DFLASH loader accepts the target's `model.layers.*` and `model.norm.weight` as its own, so the call reports success, but the acceptance length drops to ~1.0. The tensor and distributed requests already have a `selector` field to avoid this, but the disk request has none, so callers such as RL frameworks doing disk-based refits can't keep the draft out. ## Modifications - `managers/io_struct.py`: add `selector: Optional[Literal["target", "draft", "all"]] = None` to `UpdateWeightFromDiskReqInput`, like the tensor and distributed requests. The HTTP endpoint picks the field up from the struct. - `scheduler_components/weight_updater.py`: `update_weights_from_disk` uses the selector. Without one, the draft is reloaded only when it was loaded from the target's checkpoint (`speculative_draft_model_path` unset or equal to `model_path`, e.g. a bundled MTP layer), so that behavior is unchanged. A draft with its own checkpoint, such as DFLASH, keeps its weights. The cache is still flushed only when the target was reloaded. - `entrypoints/engine.py`: `Engine.update_weights_from_disk` accepts `selector`. - `docs/.../sglang_for_rl.mdx`: add `selector` to the request table and the Engine API signature. This PR doesn't change the DFLASH loader silently skipping names it doesn't recognize. I asked in the issue whether a warning there is wanted. ## Accu

summary: ## Motivation Fixes #44897. With `--ep-dispatch-algorithm fake`, `transform_select_experts_inputs` fills the router logits with noise and replaces the correction bias with zeros, so the simulated routing ignores the bias. On ROCm with aiter, `select_experts` then overwrites that zeroed bias with `topk_config.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)`, a cached cast of the model's real bias. The aiter router picks experts from noise plus the real bias, so the "fake" expert distribution is skewed toward the experts the bias favours. On CUDA the zeroed bias is kept. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: use the cached cast only while `correction_bias` is still `topk_config.correction_bias`. With fake dispatch the bias must be all zeros (bf16 and fp32 bias); with no dispatch info and with `static` dispatch it must still be the config's bias, so normal serving is unchanged. This is independent of #44797, which skips the cast for fp32 biases (#44794). title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Undo the Marlin repack when restoring W4A16 MoE weights for a weight update
summary: ## Motivation For experts-only W4A16 checkpoints on Marlin (the Kimi-K2 INT4 RL layout), `restore_weights_before_loading` only resizes the packed expert tensors back to checkpoint shapes and leaves their bytes in Marlin layout. `end_weight_update` then repacks every MoE layer, so any expert not reloaded in that session is repacked twice: an empty session or a partial refit silently corrupts the model while reporting success. Full refits are fine, which is why this went unnoticed. ## Modifications Restore now inverts the scale permutation and the Marlin tiling in place, one expert at a time, in the same storage so captured CUDA graphs stay valid. It covers symmetric checkpoints without group act-order. Asymmetric and act-order checkpoints keep the old path. Adds a case to `test_compressed_tensors_wna16_moe_reload.py` that fails on main and passes with the fix. ## Accuracy Tests RTX 3090, an experts-only W4A16 checkpoint built from `nm-testing/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat-quantized.w4a16`. On main an empty session changes all 96 expert tensors’ checksums and all 8 prompts diverge at token 0 (3/3), and a partial session (one layer’s `w2` scales) changes the other 95 (2/2). With the fix, empty and partial sessions change 0 tensors, and a one-tensor perturbation changes exactly 1 (3/3). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Restore runs once per weight-update session, not on the inference path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests accor

For decimal 128k, the corresponding targets are `115200 + 12800`, with 1000 output tokens. Generated text can tokenize to different actual lengths. 2. A concurrency cap above the generated request count cannot be exercised. 3. Treating a 90% shared-prefix input ratio as evidence of 90% cache hits, without recorded cached-token counters or a controlled warmup/cache-reset procedure. 4. summary: > Supersedes #38392 (closed unintentionally when its head branch was recreated during a rebase onto latest `main` — same change, rebased, with an extra context-parallel safety gate). The sampler then keeps ranks in sync via `all_reduce(MIN)`, which depends on bitwise-deterministic sampling kernels — the original motivation of the `sampling_info.grammars` special case. Non-entry ranks carry a `PlaceholderGrammarObject` and never compile. (#16874 still compiled lazily on every rank: the grammar backend cache is per-process, so the re-fetch in its move-ready loop was a full re-compile.) 2. **Mask once per step**: only the entry rank computes and applies the grammar vocab mask; other ranks skip `update_regex_vocab_mask` entirely. 3. **Broadcast instead of trust**: when grammars are present, the sampler broadcasts the entry rank's token ids (`group_src=0` over the attention-TP group under DP attention), replacing `all_reduce(MIN)`. ## W

title: [Feat] unified_memory: Support mxfp8 KV cache on the unified memory pool
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-unified-memory` with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` passes every startup check today but cannot work: the unified pool builds a plain `UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool`, which has no scale buffers. The server boots, sizes its pools, and dies on the first forward: ``` AttributeError: 'UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'get_kv_scale_buffer' ``` mxfp8 is the only KV dtype that keeps a slot in two pieces — an fp8 payload and a per-32-element UE8M0 exponent — while the unified pool's premise is one shared byte buffer. This adds the missing half. ## Modification A block-scaled sub-pool sets `scale_block_size` on its `MHASubPoolSpec`. `UnifiedKVPool` allocates each layer's K/V scales as contiguous tensors in the FA4 interleaved shape, outside the shared buffer, and shrinks that buffer by `1/scale_block_size` per scaled sub-pool so the pair stays inside the caller's byte budget. `UnifiedMHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8` binds them and inherits `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8` for the scale read/write path, which already works in the physical loc space this pool hands out. `move_kv_cache` relocates the payload by page envelope and the scales per slot. Two things a reviewer should check: - **The scale tensors must span exactly the paged KV extent.** FA4 keeps only the scale tensor's base pointer and rebuilds its layout by tiling `BlockScaledBasicChunk` over `k_cache`'s shape, then indexes it with the raw page-table value. Nothing asserts the shape, so a mismatch is a silent out-of-bounds read. - **The K/V views carry the fp8 dtype**, not the `uint8` storage alias the unified pool

title: [Feat] rust-server: Serve HTTP/2 (h2c) beside HTTP/1.1 with --enable-http2
summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` the launcher refuses `--enable-http2` (it is listed in `RUST_SERVER_UNSUPPORTED_ARGS`), and the Rust frontend's `/server_info` reports `enable_http2: false` whatever the flag says, because its HTTP listener speaks HTTP/1.1 only. So: - A launch command that asks for HTTP/2 cannot switch to the Rust frontend. - `sgl-router` forwards over cleartext h2c only to a worker whose `/server_info` reports `enable_http2: true`, so it cannot use h2c with an engine on the Rust frontend. ## Modifications The Rust HTTP listener serves HTTP/2 over cleartext (h2c, prior knowledge) beside HTTP/1.1 on the same port when the server is launched with `--enable-http2`, as Python's Granian server does. - **Accept loop.** `axum::serve` exposes no HTTP/2 settings, so the listener runs its own small accept loop (`rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/connections.rs`) on hyper-util's `auto::Builder` and `GracefulShutdown`. It keeps what `axum::serve` did: the graceful drain (stop accepting, let open connections finish their requests, close idle ones), the accept-error handling of `axum::serve::Listener`, the peer's `ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>` on every request, and no timer, so HTTP/1.1 still has no header-read timeout and idle keep-alive connections stay open. A drain that arrives while an accept error is being retried stops the listener at once. - **Protocol.** With the flag, a connection that opens with the HTTP/2 preface is served as h2c; any other connection is served as HTTP/1.1, so plain HTTP/1.1 clients and probes are unaffected. title: [Fix] kimi_k25: Run the vision projection under the caller's grad mode
summary: ## Motivation In `kimi_k25.py`, `mm_projection_auto` is decorated with `@torch.inference_mode()`, so the non-DP branch of `get_image_feature` always returns an inference tensor, regardless of the caller's mode. title: [Fix] scheduler: Answer health probes that are waiting behind other requests
summary: Stacked on #49695; only the top commit is this change. It needs the `poll_storage_prefetches` call that #49649 adds in front of the waiting-queue ranking, so it does not apply to `main` by itself. CI runs on the top of the stack. ## Motivation `/health_generate` sends a one-token probe through the scheduler. A probe that arrives while the scheduler is busy is skipped at intake and acknowledged after the next step, so it never waits on other requests. A probe that arrives at an idle scheduler is admitted and waits in the waiting queue like any other request. If other work arrives before the probe is scheduled, the probe is answered only once it runs. A long prompt admitted ahead of it takes every prefill pass until its last chunk, so the caller's health check times out while the engine is busy with real work. ## Modifications - `Scheduler._ack_waiting_health_checks()` takes the probes out of the waiting queue and acknowledges them through `return_health_check_ipcs`, the signal a probe skipped at intake already uses. - A probe that is alone in the queue with no chunked prefill in flight is left to run: its forward pass is the check. - An acknowledged probe is released the way `_abort_waiting` releases a waiting request, including its sender and metadata buffer on a PD prefill server, but no abort is sent to the tokenizer. - The acknowledgement is the probe's final output, so it is recorded with `record_send(probe, "health_check")`; `RequestRetirer.release` takes the probe out of the waiting queue and records its exit. title: [Perf] hicache: Keep the buffer load-back ownership check from waiting on the GPU at admission
summary: Stacked on #49658. This pull request's own change is its last commit: 2 files. ## Motivation In HiCache buffer mode, `init_load_back` admits a staged storage hit by inserting the loaded prefix and then checking that the rows the tree now publishes for the span are the rows the load-back's host-to-device copy targets. A mismatch means that copy may write into freed slots, so the engine fail-stops. That check was `torch.equal(canonical, device_indices)` on CUDA tensors. It returns a Python bool, so the scheduler thread waits until the GPU has run the comparison, behind everything already queued on the scheduler's stream. In serving that can be the running forward, and the admission then holds the scheduler thread for the rest of it. ## Modifications - Admission still fail-stops, before any H2D runs, on everything the host can decide. It raises the same "HiCache buffer load-back ownership violation" error unless the insert appended the whole span (`insert_result.prefix_len == splice_base`), the match covers the span, and the two index tensors have the same length. - The row comparison is queued on the current stream. Its one-element result is copied into pinned host memory with `async_d2h`, and a CUDA event is recorded after it (`_check_ownership`). title: [Fix] scheduler: Observe finished storage prefetches before shortest-prefill-first ranks, and count staged prefixes as cached
summary: Stacked on #49644: this pull request's own change is its last commit, nine files. ## Motivation `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` orders the waiting queue by uncached work: prompt plus retracted output, minus the matched prefix. It overestimates a request whose prefix comes from HiCache storage (L3), for two reasons: - In buffer mode a fetched span is staged outside the radix tree until admission, so `num_matched_prefix_tokens` does not include it. - A finished storage prefetch is observed only when admission reaches the request (`check_prefetch_progress`). A request still ranked by its unloaded prefix sorts behind shorter work, so admission may never reach it and the completion is never observed. A long prompt whose prefix is almost entirely in storage is then ranked as a long prefill and waits behind requests that need more computation, although its fetch has already finished. ```text waiting queue, shortest-prefill-first, buffer-mode HiCache: A: 4608-token prompt, 512 matched in the tree, storage span staged up to 4600 B: 1024-token prompt, nothing cached before: work(A) = 4096, work(B) = 1024 -> B, A after: work(A) = 8, work(B) = 1024 -> A, B ``` ## Modifications - `BasePrefixCache.staged_storage_prefix_end(handle)` reports the absolute end of a completed storage prefetch held outside the tree, 0 by default. `UnifiedRadixCache` answers from the buffer pipeline's staged prefetches (`BufferModePipeline.staged_prefix_end`). - `SchedulePolicy._shortest_prefill_work` counts the larger of `num_matched_prefix_tokens` and that end as cached. title: [Fix] radix-tree: Clamp SWA tombstone recovery to the protected prefix in the Rust tree core
summary: ## Motivation The Rust tree core could free FULL KV pages that a node still mapped. A request owns FULL pages only from its protected prefix (`prev_prefix_len`) upward; below it, the row it inserts holds the node's own canonical page ids by reference. `SwaComponent::update_component_on_insert_overlap` recovered an SWA-tombstoned node from that row starting at the request's SWA eviction cursor (`swa_evicted_seqlen`), and the cursor can sit below the protected prefix: a read-only FULL prefix match can end strictly inside a node, and a request that has not evicted that far yet has a cursor behind it. The recovery then covered pages the request never owned. They were handed to the free path as if they were the request's duplicates (the swap branch's old FULL ids, or the locked branch's incoming ids) while the node kept mapping them. Once they re-entered the free list, a later allocation could overwrite KV the node was still serving. ``` position 0 16 24 (page size 4, SWA window 8) |-- protected ---|---- own ----| node N [ p0 p1 p2 p3 ] [ p4 p5 ] FULL resident, SWA evicted request row [ p0 p1 p2 p3 ] [ q4 q5 ] p0..p3 borrowed by reference, q4 q5 fresh before: recovery starts at the SWA cursor (8) locked node -> frees "incoming" p2 p3 node still maps p2 p3 => double free unlocked node -> adopts p2 p3, frees "old" p2 p3 => double free after: recovery starts at max(cursor, 16) = 16 only [p4 p5] vs [q4 q5] is reconciled; p0..p3 untouched ``` This is the Rust counterpart of #46700, which made the same change in the Python SWA component and left the Rust tree core's own recovery path

title: [sgl-router] Add an opt-in toktier tokenizer backend (session-delta encoding)
summary: ## Motivation Router tokenization sits on the TTFT path, and every turn re-encodes the full rendered chat. #41268 added `--tokenizer-backend fast` and the L1 prefix cache to cut that work. This PR adds a third backend, opt-in, built on [toktier](https://crates.io/crates/toktier). toktier keeps the transcript of each session, and when a new turn's rendered prompt extends it, toktier re-tokenizes only the appended tail and repairs the BPE boundary exactly. The backend changes how much text is tokenized again and nothing else: on every route the ids are the ones the reference `tokenizers` engine returns for the same text. The method and its measurements are in [Delta Tokenizer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19801) (arXiv:2610.19801, session deltas and segment parallelism on multicore CPUs) and [TokTier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29678) (arXiv:2607.29678, the exactness certificate the crate ships with each tokenizer family). It is a backend and not a cache in front of one because the L1 cache reuses tokens only up to a special-token boundary and re-encodes the tail turn whole, while toktier's session store repairs at any byte position. A turn that appends 400 characters to a 100K-token context therefore tokenizes about 400 characters' worth of text, whether or not a special token happens to sit at the cut. On this branch, a session turn that appends about 400 characters to a 109K-character rendered transcript takes 0.41 ms for Qwen3-8B and 0.39 ms for Llama-3.1-8B, against 22.3 ms and 16.7 ms for the router's `hf` encode of the same prompt. summary: ## Motivation ModelSlim integer W4A8 MoE loads the W2 matrix as a TP-local K shard, but currently allocates and loads all 16 checkpoint `scale_bias` columns on every TP rank. The post-load reduction therefore applies a full-K quantization compensation to a partial-K matrix product. title: [Fix] kda: Fix prefill-graph track copies with a bf16 SSM pool
summary: ## Motivation With `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`, the KDA SSM pool is bf16. `_kda_track_ssm_kernel` (#41105) loads the pool dtype in its mode-1 branch and the fp32 chunk-boundary snapshot in its mode-2 branch, then stores the result. Triton rejects a variable whose type differs between the branches of a runtime `if`, so the kernel fails to compile on a bf16 pool. On GLM-5.3-Flash with breakable prefill CUDA graphs, which capture the KDA extend, this fails server startup during prefill graph capture. ## Modifications - Cast the fp32 snapshot to the pool dtype inside the mode-2 branch, so both branches produce the pool dtype. An fp32 pool is unaffected: the cast is then a no-op. - Add `test_kda_prefill_graph_track.py`. It runs `kda_track_ssm_state` on fp32 and bf16 pools with mode 0, 1 and 2 rows, and compares the pool exactly with a torch reference. ## Accuracy Tests On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) with Triton 3.8.0, the new test passes (2 tests). title: [Perf] glm53-flash: Overlap prefill TP all-reduces across two microbatches
summary: ## Motivation On PCIe GPUs without NVLink, GLM-5.3-Flash prefill at TP4 spends much of its time in tensor-parallel all-reduces. In a profile of a 32K-token prompt (4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, FP8, TP4, 8192-token chunks), NCCL all-reduce was 45% of GPU time: 64 MB per call, 4.2 ms each. Prefill runs one request's chunk through each layer and then waits for that layer's all-reduce, so the GPUs compute nothing while it runs. Splitting the chunk in two lets one half's all-reduce run while the other half computes. In an isolated test of a 4096-row MoE layer, an all-reduce running under the next half's MoE took a layer from 4.78 ms serially to 3.13 ms; the MoE alone took 2.61 ms. ## Modifications - New `prefill_mbo` module, enabled with `SGLANG_PREFILL_MBO=1` (default off). - A single-request extend of at least `SGLANG_PREFILL_MBO_MIN_TOKENS` tokens (default 4096) is split at a 256-aligned absolute position into two child batches. The 256-token alignment keeps KV pages, k-pool groups and KDA chunks of both halves aligned. - Each child batch has its own attention backend instance and metadata. Mamba track fields go to the child that reaches the tracked length. - Each half's attention and FFN partial sums are all-reduced on a side stream, over a dedicated NCCL group created at startup on the TP ranks. title: [Perf] dsv41: Cut encoder SWA bounded-replay window copies from ~4.2 ms to ~0.1 ms per decode step
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-encoder-swa-bounded-replay`, the DeepSeek-V4.1 target keeps each request's SWA state in a `RequestWindow`. Before each attention layer, `buffer` gathers the window history into the workspace. After the layer, `commit` writes the step's tokens back and tags them. Both went through `copy_packed_tokens`, which moved the data and scale rows with tensor indexing, and each layer recomputed the row indices with `torch.where`. That is 72 kernel launches per layer for one gather and one commit, measured with `torch.profiler` in the benchmark below; for the 43 layers of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash that is 3,096 launches per decode step, all inside the decode CUDA graph. ## Modifications - New `sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/request_window.py` with two Triton kernels, registered in the attention kernel inventory: - `gather_window_history` computes each history row's source (`req * capacity + pos % capacity`, or the zero row when masked) and copies its data and scale rows. - `commit_window_tokens` computes each new token's destination (or the sink row), copies the token, and records its position in `tags`. - Both run one program per token and copy int32 words, with the index math inside the kernel. - `window_layout` makes `req` and `pos` contiguous. `.to(torch.int64)` returns an already-int64 view unchanged, and the commit kernel reads these arrays by program id without strides, so before this fix a strided view could select the wrong request rows and write past the state buffer. Both wrappers assert contiguous 1-D index and mask inputs. - `RequestWindow.buffer`

title: [Fix] dspark: Keep output sampling exact under folded draft sampling by storing corrected logits in FP32
summary: ## Motivation With folded draft sampling (`SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING`, on by default when memory allows), `DsparkDraftSampler` draws each draft token in the draft CUDA graph from the Markov-corrected step logits and copies those logits to `corrected_out`. Sampling acceptance later rebuilds the draft distribution q from `corrected_out`. `corrected_out` was allocated in the head dtype: `lm_head.weight.dtype` for a floating-point weight, otherwise the dtype of the first Markov-head parameter (BF16 for a BF16 `lm_head`). The DeepSeek-V4 DSpark Markov head adds an FP32 bias, so its corrected logits are FP32. The token was drawn from the FP32 logits, but rejection sampling used q from a BF16-rounded copy. Rejection sampling then compares the target against a distribution that is not the one the draft token came from, which can bias the output distribution. The eager proposal path keeps the FP32 logits, so the folded and eager paths also used different q. ## Modifications - Allocate `corrected_out` as FP32 and remove `_base_logits_dtype`. FP32 holds BF16/FP16 logits exactly, so heads with BF16 corrected logits get the same values as before. - The free-memory check that decides whether folded sampling is enabled now counts 4 bytes per element. For heads that previously stored 16-bit logits, the buffer grows by `max_bs * gamma * vocab * 2` bytes, where `max_bs` is the largest decode CUDA-graph batch size. That is about 21 MB at max_bs 16, gamma 5, vocab 129,280, and 83 MB at max_bs 64. This can change one decision. For eligible heads in AUTO mode, an initialization-time check en

title: [Feat] glm: Enable compact NoPE KV storage with native FlashInfer
summary: ## Motivation With compact-aware FlashInfer kernels, the same memory budget for GLM NoPE KV rows can hold 24.2% more token slots: each row uses 528 rather than 656 bytes, with the same FP8 values and FP32 scales. That provides more room for long prompts or cached request context without reducing precision. This is the row-capacity gain before allocator padding; other memory pools and configured context limits still apply. This PR makes that capacity available to SGLang by integrating FlashInfer's native GLM NoPE attention backend on SM120 and selecting compact rows when supported. The existing RoPE entry point cannot serve GLM's NoPE query and sparse-candidate geometry. Gabriel Wu’s merged [FlashInfer #5075](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5075) provides the canonical compact payload, runtime row strides and masked-read correction, including my eight-head decode and layout-validation fixes. His subsequent [FlashInfer #5197](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5197) refactors native SM120 execution, runtime dispatch and calibration. Both are merged upstream and first ship in the FlashInfer 0.7.1 release line (0.7.1rc1 and later). No isolated serving speedup is claimed. Related to #36830 for the SM120 native-backend path; this PR does not add SM90 support. ## Dependency The native GLM NoPE path requires FlashInfer 0.7.1 or newer, which is currently published only as release candidates (0.7.1rc1 and later). title: [Fix] dflash: Give the draft a private RoPE module
summary: ## Motivation We observed an illegal memory access in speculative serving with a Qwen3.5-family target and a DSpark draft. The underlying issue affects the DFlash/DSpark attention path when target and draft resolve to the same cached RoPE module and the draft replaces its cache after target CUDA Graph capture. Replay can then read stale storage, producing incorrect results or an illegal memory access. This does not imply that every Qwen3.5 + DFlash/DSpark configuration is affected. `get_rope()` caches `RotaryEmbedding` modules by their arguments. A draft that retains matching partial/M-RoPE configuration from the target can receive the same module in `DFlashAttention`. The complete resolved cache key must match; sharing a `partial_rotary_factor` alone is insufficient. The relevant capture/forward order is: 1. The target's fused QK-norm/RoPE kernel (`fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, Qwen3.5) reads `rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache` (fp32) directly, and that read is captured in the target's CUDA graphs. 2. A subsequent BF16 draft forward takes the CUDA `MRotaryEmbedding` path and calls `_match_cos_sin_cache_dtype()`, replacing `cos_sin_cache` with a bf16 copy. If no other owner retains the old fp32 tensor, its allocation can be released and reused. 3. Target graph replay still uses the captured pointer; it does not re-read the updated Python attribute. Reusing the old allocation can expose incorrect results or an illegal access. Replay may happen to compare equal while the old contents remain intact, which does not make the lifetime safe. The sequence can occur serially in one proc

summary: <!-- PR body starts below --> ## Motivation Mooncake's next-generation transfer engine, **TENT**, can choose a transport per request, spread traffic across NICs by backlog and bandwidth, and isolate foreground and background traffic into separate QP pools. This PR adds it as an **opt-in** backend for the Mooncake PD connector so it can be evaluated. **Classic TE stays the default.** On one node, TENT reduced KV transfer latency under NIC congestion. TTFT did not change much, because prefill compute dominates it. The numbers below are reference data points, not a general performance claim. ## Modifications - **`kv_transfer_engine.py` (new):** a small `KVTransferEngine` interface shared by TE and TENT, plus a `TransferIntent` enum (`FOREGROUND` / `BACKGROUND`). - **`mooncake_transfer_engine.py`:** the TE wrapper implements the interface. `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_TRANSFER_ENGINE` selects `te` (default) or `tent`. title: [Feat] rust-server: Tell a model package's abort hook which requests an abort names
summary: Stacked on #50189; only the top commit (25 files, all under `rust/sglang-server/`) is this change. ## Motivation A package that serves through `Server::start_with_extensions` and keeps its own per-request records has no way to learn which requests a client aborted. An abort by rid reaches the frontend through three entries: the listener's `/abort_request`, the gRPC `Abort`, and, under attention DP, the abort another DP rank's listener relays to `/internal/peer`. A package's HTTP layer sees only the first of them, so it cannot tell a request the client cancelled from one the server ended. ## Modifications - `AbortHook` (`api_server/core/abort_hook.rs`, re-exported from the crate root) is a new extension trait with one method, `named_abort(&self, rid: &str)`. It is installed with a new `abort_hook: Option<Arc<dyn AbortHook>>` argument of `Server::start_with_extensions`, after `generate_validator`, and carried through `RuntimeConfig` and `CoreConfig`. - `CoreHandle::abort`, where every entry converges, calls the hook with the non-empty rid of each abort before the abort ends anything, whether or not the rid selects a live request on that listener. An `abort_all` or an empty rid names no request and does not reach the hook. With no hook installed nothing changes. - The `test-support` feature gains `SchedulerlessServer` (`utils/runtime/test_support.rs`), a whole frontend with no scheduler behind it. title: [Fix] marlin: Load dense group scales and zero points at group boundaries
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #45000. With an FP8 block-quantized checkpoint, the dense Marlin kernel intermittently returns wrong GEMM results, which shows up as wrong greedy tokens. A lagging warp then scales a whole K tile with the wrong group’s scale. Both zero-point loads have the same pattern. vLLM fixed this in vllm-project/vllm#24722 with a `pipe % g == 0` guard, and SGLang’s MoE template already has it for scales. ## Modifications Adds the `pipe % g == 0` guard to the scale load and both zero-point loads in `marlin_template.h`, as in vLLM. title: [Fix] rust-server: Keep the /v1/loads snapshot lock wait off the async workers
summary: ## Motivation The Rust server's `GET /v1/loads` reads the scheduler's load-snapshot file under a shared `flock`, the same lock Python's reader takes. The writer (`ShmLoadSnapshotWriter.write` in `python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py`) holds that lock exclusively for as long as its write takes. The handler opened the file, took the shared lock and read the file inline on a tokio worker, so a poll that has to wait for the writer parks that worker in the syscall. If the writer pauses while it holds the lock, every waiting poll holds one worker, and once all workers of the HTTP runtime are waiting, nothing else the listener serves makes progress until the writer releases the lock. ## Modifications - `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/loads.rs`: the snapshot read and decode (`read_snapshots` + `to_dict`) run in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. The JSON and Prometheus output, the status codes, and the fallback for a missing, mismatched or malformed file are unchanged. A poll still waits for the writer; it no longer holds an async worker while it waits. The `get_loads` latency observation still times the whole read, so it now includes any wait for a blocking-pool thread. - Test `locked_snapshot_does_not_block_workers`: on a two-worker multi-thread runtime, a thread holds the exclusive lock on a snapshot file while two `/v1/loads` calls, one per worker, run next to a ticker task. title: [Fix] model_loader: Return replaced weights to the device after each post-load hook
summary: ## Motivation On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB), gpt-oss-120b does not start on current `main` with default options: ``` Load weight end. elapsed=3.50 s, type=GptOssForCausalLM, quant=mxfp4, avail mem=11.70 GB, mem usage=82.52 GB. ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=0.858. Raise --mem-fraction-static above 0.876 (minimum viable = 1 - available/pre = 0.8756). ... ``` The weights themselves take 66 GB. The other 16 GB sit in the allocator cache, and KV-cache sizing counts them as used. Where they come from: - Since #35180, `device_loading_context` runs each post-load hook inside `stage_module_for_post_load` when the target is not the CPU. Before the hook runs, that context records every registered tensor of the module, including the ones already on the target device, and holds them until it exits. Before #35180 only CPU-resident parameters were recorded. - So when a hook replaces a weight with a re-laid-out copy, the old weight stays allocated for the rest of the hook. The `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` that the hooks call at their end cannot return it. - The old weight is freed only when the context exits, into the allocator cache. Then the next module's hook allocates. Its new weights are larger than the cached blocks and get fresh segments, while smaller tensors are carved out of the cached blocks and pin them. The case above is `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, which `auto` selects for gpt-oss on SM120. `_process_weights_for_sm120_cutlass` rebuilds each layer's experts padded to 128-element tiles. title: [Spec][Ngram] Seed the ngram corpus with each request's rendered tool calls
summary: ## Motivation Part of #21052, not on the list, I proposed it in the thread. NGRAM drafts from what is already in the corpus: tokens that earlier requests produced, plus an external corpus if you loaded one. A tool call's syntax is not in there until some request has already produced it. The prompt has the tool schema as JSON, while the model outputs the actual tool call syntax from its chat template, for example `<tool_call>\n{"name": ...` for Qwen and Hermes. Those are different token sequences. So the first call to each tool on a server still decodes that structure one token at a time, and on a single-user box every call is a first call. Agentic use is a pretty large share of how these models are served now, and agent loops are dominated by tool calls. A harness might expose tens of tools and most of them only get called once per session. I've been getting deep into speculative decoding at work and this is the gap I kept running into. The idea is pretty simple: Render the conversation normally, then render it again with an example assistant tool call appended. The difference between those two renders is the assistant turn the model is about to generate, already in that model's own chat template and its own tokens. Put that into the corpus before the request's first draft. Now instead of decoding the structural part of the tool call one token at a time, the model verifies a bunch of it in one step. The actual argument values are still generated by the model, this only seeds the syntax around them. Nothing is forced. If a seed is wrong it just does not match, so the output

title: [Feat] disaggregation: Make the PD top-logprobs metadata width configurable
summary: ## Motivation In PD disaggregation, prefill sends the first output token's top logprobs to decode through `MetadataBuffers`, whose rows are 128 entries wide: a constructor default that neither `MetadataBuffers` call in `Scheduler.init_disaggregation` overrides. A request with a larger `top_logprobs_num` makes `MetadataBuffers.set_buf` raise in the prefill scheduler: ``` RuntimeError: top_logprobs_num 256 exceeds disaggregation metadata capacity 128. Lower top_logprobs_num or increase the metadata buffer. ``` The scheduler exits on the exception and takes the prefill server down, while a non-disaggregated server serves the same request. No setting increases the buffer. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Keep freeing SWA slots for an unpublished prefill with a pending SWA branch
summary: ## Motivation Under a write-through cache, a disaggregated prefill that is admitted before its bootstrap completes stays unpublished: each chunk goes through `UnifiedRadixCache.advance_unpublished_req`, which frees out-of-window SWA slots without inserting into the tree. When that request's prefix match reported an SWA branch point (`swa_branching_seqlen`), the SWA component caps the cache length at the branch until the branch is inserted, and only a tree insert clears it. The unpublished path never inserts, so the free frontier stays at the branch on every later chunk and the request keeps every SWA slot past it. A prompt that runs past the branch by more than the SWA pool fills the pool and cannot schedule its next chunk. ## Modifications - `UnifiedRadixCache.advance_unpublished_req`: when the request has a pending SWA branch beyond its protected prefix and has reached it, checkpoint the request into the tree up to the branch. This is the insert the published path already does at its first checkpoint past the branch. The request then keeps advancing unpublished, so the frontier follows its own length, and later requests still reuse the branch. - A request with `skip_radix_cache_insert` never inserts, so it drops the branch instead and frees SWA slots the same way. - `test_prefill_send_protection.py`: new `test_unpublished_branch_keeps_releasing_swa` drives a branched unpublished request through the Python and Rust tree cores with an SWA pool smaller than the prompt. title: [Fix] hicache: Refuse a runtime write_back policy under buffer_only host memory
summary: ## Motivation With `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only` the host pool is only a staging buffer: every cached page lives in the storage backend, so there is no host tier for `--hicache-write-policy write_back` to defer writes into. Argument resolution already handles the pair at launch by resolving `write_back` to `write_through`. The runtime storage attach (`StorageAttachment.attach`, which also serves same-backend policy updates) only checks that the policy name is valid. Its existing host-mode check covers a different case: switching a `cache`-mode `write_back` tree to write-through. So on a `buffer_only` server a runtime request can still set `write_back`: - a same-backend policy update applies it and returns success; - a fresh attach applies it before attaching the controller. Once it is applied, hits stop writing through, and an unbacked leaf asks for a backup when it is evicted. In buffer mode that backup is only queued and reports nothing written, so the eviction can take its host-pressure fallback and drop the leaf without storing it (`write_back: KV subtree dropped without backup due to host memory pressure`). A leaf that `write_through` would have stored is then missing from storage for later requests. Cached KV is not corrupted. This consequence comes from reading the eviction path; it was not reproduced on a running server. ## Modifications - `StorageAttachment.attach` refuses `hicache_write_policy="write_back"` when the cache's host memory mode is `buffer_only`, right after the policy-name validation and before any side effect: no policy changes, the contro

title: [Fix] kda: Keep the exact intra-chunk diagonal for short prefills without a gate lower bound
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #39971. On short prefills (B·NT·H ≤ 256), `chunk_kda_fwd` always takes the fused-diagonal path, which splits each diagonal block’s `exp2(g_i − g_j)` into two factors clamped to ±126. Without a gate lower bound, a channel can decay by more than 126 (log2) within 16 tokens, the factors stop cancelling, and keys that should be forgotten are read at near full weight. Error against an fp64 recurrence jumps from 3.0e-3 at a span of 125 to 0.116 at 126. ## Modifications `fuse_diagonal` now also requires `safe_gate`, so ungated short prefills use the exact token-parallel diagonal, as upstream FLA does. Models with a gate lower bound keep the fused path. Adds a steep-decay case to `TestKDAChunkExponentDomain`, which fails on main (24.7% error) and passes with the fix (0.36%). ## Accuracy Tests RTX 4090, rel-L2 against an fp64 recurrence: spans of 126 and above go from 0.116–1.26 to 2.8e-3, and the issue’s per-channel case from 0.179 to 4.0e-3. Gated models (lower_bound −5) are unchanged. `test_kda_kernels.py`: 20 passed with the fix (19 on main plus the new case). The same 2 decode tests fail on both in my environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Ungated short prefills on an RTX 4090 with CUDA graphs: GPU time ranges from −10.8% to +15.7% across 7 shapes, and 5 of the 7 are neutral or faster. title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Compile the HIP FP4 prefill schedule kernels before serving
summary: ## Motivation On AMD GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1 sometimes pauses for 0.4 to 2.8 seconds in the middle of serving. When the caching allocator held stale NaN, 655360 of 655360 outputs were non-finite. The aiter that the v0.5.21 image bundles (`acf8fdf930`) does not have #4919 and is not affected. title: [Bug] FP8 block-quantized checkpoint on SM86 (FP8 Marlin) intermittently gives wrong tokens with the overlap scheduler; exact without it
summary: ## Summary On an RTX 3090, SGLang 0.5.22 serves a 128×128 block-FP8 checkpoint through FP8 Marlin (weight-only; SM86 has no FP8 tensor cores). title: [WIP][TLX][Feat] [AMD] muse-spark: Add TLX MoE backend via vendored tlx.ops.moe
summary: Motivation This is the first step in adding TLX kernel support to SGLang on AMD. The goal is to replace and fuse more of the per-op kernels on gfx950 (MoE first, then GEMM, layernorm and others) with TLX kernels from tlx.ops in facebookexperimental/triton. On stock ROCm Triton, those kernels can run through the uTLX plugin (utlx_plugin, from triton-ext). MoE comes first because it's the largest share of GPU time we measured. We profiled Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B on 8× MI355X (TP8/EP8, aiter attention, MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=flydsl, DFlash speculative decoding) with a long-prompt workload. The routed-expert path took about 24.4% of total GPU time: ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Kernel │ Share of GPU time │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ muse_moe_gate_up_mfma_flydsl │ 13.9% │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ muse_moe_down_mfma_flydsl │ 7.2% │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ _align_small_kernel │ 2.0% │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ muse_moe_finalize_vector_flydsl │ 1.2% │ ├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ _map_local_ids_kernel │ <0.01% │ └─────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` tlx.ops.moe (gfx950) was written for exactly these shapes: K = I = H = 4096, 32 of 256 experts local, top-8, BF16. One call does token-to-expert alignment, the gate/up GEMM with fused SiLU, the down GEMM, and the post-expert RMSNorm with the routing-weighted combine.
