title: [Bugfix] FlashInfer autotune cache dropped every startup under expert parallelism
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #40320. `_autotune_cache_digest` hashes each rank's whole cache file to decide whether the ranks agree. Under expert parallelism each rank tunes a disjoint subset of MoE shapes, so the per-rank tactics legitimately differ — `len(set(digests)) == 1` cannot hold, and the cache is unlinked on every boot. Tactics are then re-drawn from timing noise on each start, so the same configuration gives different throughput across boots. ## Modifications `load_configs` in flashinfer is all-or-nothing: it accepts a per-rank cache file only when its `_metadata` matches the current environment, otherwise it skips the whole file. The cross-rank agreement the entry gate needs is that every rank makes the same load decision under the current environment — not that tactic entries agree. Digest the `(loadable, stamp, env)` triple instead of the file bytes. +7/-3 in `flashinfer_autotune.py`. Two regression tests, both fail before / pass after: - `TestAutotuneCacheDigest::test_disjoint_shape_sets_digest_alike_when_env_matches` — unit-level: two rank caches with the same `_metadata` but disjoint per-shape entries must digest alike. - `TestDropDivergedAutotuneCache::test_disjoint_shape_sets_with_matching_env_are_kept` — integration over a real gloo group and real files: both ranks' caches must survive the gate. Two tests were removed: - `test_diverged_caches_are_dropped_on_every_rank` enforced the byte-equality contract this fix disproves. - `test_key_order_does_not_matter` degrades to a mirror under the new digest and is subsumed by the new disjoint-content test above. title: [Perf] pooler: Avoid rebuilding pooled hidden states before scoring
summary: ## Motivation Setwise and multi-item scoring gather selected hidden-state rows into a contiguous tensor, split it into per-request views, then immediately concatenate the same views before applying the classification head. summary: ## Motivation The Ascend parameter tuning page is the entry point for tuning a deployment that already runs, but it had two problems. title: [Fix] compressed-tensors: Reject WNA16 MoE TP shards that split a scale group
summary: ## Motivation `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoE` shards the w2 scales by narrowing whole scale groups. When a MoE TP shard is not a multiple of `group_size`, each rank gets scales for the wrong K range. Example: `moe_intermediate_size=640`, `group_size=128`, `moe_tp_size=4`. Each rank's down_proj has K = 160 = 128 + 32. `create_weights` builds 160 // 128 = 1 scale group per rank, the generic loader narrows the 5 checkpoint groups by 5 // 4 = 1, and the Triton kernel needs cdiv(160, 128) = 2 groups. Half of the K elements are dequantized with the wrong scale, and the kernel reads past the 1-group tensor for the K tail. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 at `--tp 8 --ep 2` (8× A800) the server dies with `illegal memory access` on every EP1 rank. When the over-read happens to land in mapped memory, long generations degrade into `!!!!`. vLLM rejects this layout at load time (vllm-project/vllm#41161) and tells the user to pick a compatible TP size or use expert parallelism. This PR makes SGLang do the same, so the misconfiguration fails at startup with a clear message. ## Modifications - `compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py`: `create_weights` raises `ValueError` when the w2 scales are sharded per rank and `intermediate_size_per_partition % group_size != 0`. The message gives both sizes and suggests a TP size that keeps whole groups per rank, or expert parallelism. Channel-wise quantization and grouped actorder (which loads the full w2 scales on every rank) are not affected. - New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_wna16_moe_tp_split.py`: - misaligned shards

Proposed title: [RFC] Optimizing Large-Scale MoE Inference with Multi-GPU Partial Expert Offload --> ## Summary We would like to discuss how SGLang should serve large MoE models efficiently when their full expert working set, KV cache, and runtime allocations are close to, or exceed, the HBM capacity of a multi-GPU deployment. The proposed direction is **multi-GPU, partial expert offload**: keep the active working set and a configurable set of resident experts on each GPU, hold the remaining experts in host memory, and bring them to the GPU on demand. Then optimize the complete serving path—native expert kernels, CUDA graphs, transfers, scheduling, and residency selection—without changing the intended model precision or making speculative predictions necessary for correctness. Paged Experts already provides much of the required foundation: host-resident experts, GPU slots, GPU-side decode planning, and host-planned prefill waves. We would prefer to extend this architecture where its contracts fit, rather than introduce an independent offload runtime. This RFC is a discussion of the problem, design choices, and useful optimization directions, not a claim that all the mechanisms below are already supported upstream. ## Motivation: the HBM capacity boundary is a serving problem A model need not be many times larger than GPU memory for offload to matter. summary: ## Motivation When `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` is unset, the prefill CUDA graph ceiling defaults to `--chunked-prefill-size`. MiniMax-M3.1 recipes use a 32768-token chunk, so startup captures 106 breakable prefill graphs; 57 of them sit above 4096 tokens, spaced 512 apart. Prefill steps that large are compute-bound: an 8K-16K-token step takes the same time with or without a graph. The 16K-32K graphs are never replayed at all, because `max_prefill_tokens` caps a step at 16384 tokens. ## Modifications - Replace the MuseGlimmer-only default with a small per-architecture table (`apply_arch_prefill_cuda_graph_max_bs_default`). The cap is per architecture and not global on purpose. Some models, such as Muse MegaMoE with LayerNorm SP, require the capture ceiling to cover the whole chunk, because a larger eager prefill can replace workspaces that the captured graphs hold. ## Accuracy Tests MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4 + DSPARK, B200: | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | GSM8K, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 | 95.0% | 96.0% | | RULER2 at 32768 tokens, 600 samples, greedy, 2 runs | 90.49% / 89.51% | 88.57% / 88.93% | On RULER2 the arms are not bit-identical. title: [Perf] engram: Extend all-to-all lookup to prefill CP
summary: ## Summary Prefill CP currently gathers Engram hash IDs, performs a TP-sharded lookup followed by AllReduce, and then keeps only the token rows belonging to the local CP rank. This materializes and reduces lookup results that the rank subsequently discards. This PR extends the existing DP all-to-all lookup to eligible prefill CP batches. Each rank looks up its owned hash columns and exchanges the results so that each destination receives the complete embeddings for its local tokens. The hash-ID AllGather is unchanged. The implementation reuses the existing lookup, communication, and token-major reorder kernels. ## Changes - Extract the existing DP all-to-all path into a helper with explicit communication group and rank arguments. - Use that helper for uniform, unpadded eager CP batches with at least 64 token rows per rank. - Require identical TP/CP group membership and ordering, evenly distributed hash columns, and per-rank CPU table shards. The number of hash columns must be divisible by the TP size. - Preserve the original lookup for unsupported batches, including small batches, padded tails, and CUDA graph capture. - Normalize signed zero on the new CP path to match the original AllReduce SUM behavior. The optimization requires explicit configuration: ```bash --engram-config '{"placement":"cpu","replication":"none","lookup":"all_to_all"}' ``` The default `auto` selection is unchanged. Existing DP, shared-table, peer-read, and staged-lookup paths retain their behavior. ## Correctness and testing The distributed test covers: - FP8 and MXFP4 tables with non-unit scales. - B

title: [Perf] tokenizer: Skip TokenizersBackend retries when the checkpoint declares that class
summary: ## Motivation In transformers v5, `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` is an alias of `TokenizersBackend`. Both reloads return the same class. They also log a misleading "still TokenizersBackend after retries" warning. `get_tokenizer` runs several times during startup: in the scheduler, in the TP worker's processor, and in each tokenizer worker. For a 200K-vocab tokenizer, each wasted reload costs about 0.6 s. ## Modifications - Skip the `TokenizersBackend` retries when the declared tokenizer class already resolves to `TokenizersBackend`. - Factor the `tokenizer_config.json` read out of `_load_tokenizer_by_declared_class` so both paths share it. - Add a unit test that loads a checkpoint declaring `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` and checks that `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` runs once. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Serving a ModelSlim-quantized Qwen3.5/3.8 checkpoint (main model `W8A8_DYNAMIC`) with MTP speculative decoding on NPU produces a numerically broken draft model: every drafted token is rejected (`accept len: 1.02, accept rate: 0.01`), so the full draft cost is paid for nothing (~15 tok/s vs 56 tok/s on the same 2-card server with a working draft). **Root cause.** - On NPU, `_mtp_quant_config()` forces the MTP draft to `quant_config=None` when `speculative_draft_model_quantization` is unset (`qwen3_5_mtp.py`). - These checkpoints store the MTP **projections** as W8A8: `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` is `int8` (12288, 5120) with a per-row `weight_scale` (12288, 1) and zero `weight_offset`; only norms/`fc` are `FLOAT` (per `quant_model_description.json`). - The loader therefore copies the raw int8 codes into bf16 parameters. Verified via a live weight dump: the 6 MTP projection matrices have `absmax = 128` (the int8 code range) while correctly loaded `mtp.fc.weight` matches the checkpoint value exactly. The draft matmuls then run on garbage matrices and the target rejects every proposed token. This is complementary to #34353: that PR covers checkpoints where **all** `mtp.*` entries are `FLOAT`; here the `mtp.*` projections are quantized, so that branch does not fire. A related loading failure is reporte

title: [Perf] cuda_graph: Run one eager warmup per breakable prefill graph shape
summary: ## Motivation Breakable prefill CUDA graph capture runs every shape eagerly twice before capturing it. The first eager run already pays the shape's JIT compilation, autotuning and lazy allocations, so the second one repeats it for nothing. On a large prefill ladder (106 shapes at `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`), the second run is about 30% of prefill capture time. ## Modifications - `BreakableCudaGraphBackend.capture_one` runs one eager warmup per shape instead of two. The barrier, the precarve measurement and `post_warmup_hook` still run around it. - A comment in `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` that referred to the second warmup is updated. title: [Perf] watermark: Record decode contexts without dynamic CUDA indexing
summary: ## Motivation The ordinary full-vocabulary/large-top-k watermark fallback records selected contexts with `nonzero` and three dynamically sized Boolean gathers. On CUDA these introduce four host synchronization points per decode step. The selected rows and history counts are already on the device. ## Modifications Record ordinary CUDA contexts in one small Triton kernel. Only a selected row with remaining history capacity writes its hash and increments its count; inactive rows do not write, including inactive rows sharing a pool index. Keep the CPU implementation unchanged. Sampling probabilities, sorting, token selection, entropy gating, and the existing finite-top-k and speculative kernels are unchanged. The change adds 56 production lines and three parameterized/test cases to the existing state tests. ## Accuracy Tests Base `5d0de926ad92eb6ec49e67941e278c93ea41772f`; WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB. - The new real `WatermarkState.force` profiler regression fails on the base with **four `aten::nonzero` calls**, and passes after the change with **zero**. The new recording kernel runs once; sorting and cumulative sums remain. - The state and selector files initially report **22 passed, two failed**. Both failures are existing `test_dspark_chain_commits_non_speculative_contexts` variants whose FlashInfer JIT build rejects `--compress-mode=size` under the local CUDA 12.0 compiler. The same two tests fail at the same build step on the clean base. A final focused run excluding those two reports **22 passed, two deselected**; DSPar

title: [Feat] kimi_k3: Serve Kimi-K3.1 on the unified memory pool
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * __->__ #49913 * #49966 * #49912 * #49775 * #49720 * #49719 ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1 (`KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration`) refused `--enable-unified-memory`. It is a KDA hybrid whose MLA layers use DSA sparse attention. The unified pool had no place for the DSA indexer's keys, could not store FP8 latent rows with block scales (the `flashmla_kv` row layout), and the DSA backend read `req_to_token` directly instead of translating the unified pool's virtual ids. This PR serves Kimi-K3.1 from the unified pool with TP, without extra kernel launches compared with the static pools. ## Modifications **Page layout** (on the composite sub-pool of the previous PR) - The configurator declares, for each MLA layer of a DSA model, two full-lifetime parts: - the latent rows: `MLAGeometry` with `row_format=fp8_ds_mla` (656 B: NoPE values, block scales, RoPE; UE8M0 scales for Kimi-K3.1) and `layer_major=True`; - the indexer keys: `IndexKeyGeometry`, one blob per page holding the page's keys, then their scales, as the paged indexer kernels read them. Layers that reuse the previous layer's top-k declare none. - The plan composes both parts into the full sub-pool's units. Each 64-token page holds every layer's 64 latent rows contiguously, then the index blobs, then padding. - Each layer's latent view `(pages, 64, 1, 656)` has a 656-byte token stride and a page-sized block stride, so FlashMLA's sparse kernels read it directly with plain token ids. - Index keys use the index-K page stride support from #49912. title: [Perf] rust-processor: Decode byte-level token pieces without table scans
summary: ## Motivation The Rust frontend decodes GPT-2 byte-level token pieces for each output logprob and each top-logprob alternative. Every remapped character currently reconstructs its inverse mapping by scanning and filtering `0..256`. Ordinary space prefixes, newlines and UTF-8 byte fragments repeatedly take this path. ## Modifications Replace the repeated scan with the three exact inverse ranges. Keep the printable-byte ranges, rejection of other Unicode scalars, tokenizer classification and response behavior unchanged. This adds no table, cache, dependency or shared state. The shared function serves both chat and legacy completion responses. Add a literal 256-byte table fixture through the real `TokenPieces` interface, plus rejected Unicode and range boundaries. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on WSL2 Ubuntu with the workspace's Rust 1.92.0 toolchain, at base `5d0de926ad92eb6ec49e67941e278c93ea41772f`. The relevant Rust code remains unchanged on the newer main inspected before submission. - `cargo +1.92.0 test --locked -p sglang-processor --features openai -- --nocapture`: **80 unit tests and five integration entrypoints pass**. The existing integration runners skip 68 OpenAI cases for two uncached DeepSeek tokenizers, leave token IDs unchecked for 13 uncached renderer snapshots, and report 72 existing known-gap fixture allowances. title: [Refactor] mem_cache: Compose same-lifetime parts into one unified sub-pool
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49913 * __->__ #49966 * #49912 * #49775 * #49720 * #49719 ## Motivation The unified memory pool plans one sub-pool per `(lifetime, allocation unit)` group. It refused a group whose layers declared more than one geometry: "the unified pool lays out one geometry per sub-pool". Payload that shares the KV's lifetime but has a different shape therefore had no generic home. Each such case was handled specially: - the request parts (`_request_group`); - a fused draft's region inside the host entries; - extra parts inside a state geometry. Sparse-attention models, for example, keep indexer keys per page beside their MLA latent rows, with the same lifetime. This PR lets one sub-pool compose several same-lifetime geometries. The next PR in the stack uses it for Kimi-K3.1's index keys. A fused draft's rows can later move onto its per-token parts. ## Modifications - `kv/decl.py`: `kv_layer_decls(full_layer_parts=...)` (`FullLayerParts`) lets full layers declare full-lifetime parts beside their KV. Models that don't use it declare exactly what they did before. - `kv/plan.py`: `_group_parts` keeps, per `(lifetime, unit)` group, its geometries in declaration order (KV first). - A group with one geometry plans exactly as before: same names, specs, entry bytes and chain order. - A group with several geometries, or a geometry laid out only in a unit, gets a `CompositeSubPoolSpec`. `PlannedSubPool.parts` lists its parts, and `geometry`/`layer_ids` stay the KV part's. - Two KV geometries in one group, parts on layers without KV, state or reques

title: [Fix] [NPU] EPLB: preserve NZ storage, reuse TP, and isolate draft capture
summary: ## Summary This PR changes how dynamic EPLB moves expert weights on Ascend. It replaces the existing NZ-to-ND staging round trip with writable views of the model's physical expert storage, reuses the TP device group for EPLB communication, and covers draft recording during NPU graph warmup and capture. These are three separate changes with different reasons: | Change | Problem it addresses | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Move complete expert storage blocks | Converting weights to contiguous ND creates conversion buffers and a separate conversion/copy-back pass. Transposed NZ and packed weights also need their storage layout preserved. | Move the stored bytes, including NZ padding, through the existing updater. Model tensor addresses, dtype, shape and storage format stay intact. | | Reuse the TP device group | Statistics and migration previously use default WORLD, even when NPU inference already has a TP group covering the same ranks. | Use the existing TP group and its HCCL configuration when TP spans WORLD. Warm its communication paths before KV-cache sizing. | | Guard NPU draft graph capture | Some graph callbacks call the model directly and bypass the recording context in `ModelRunner.forward`. | Apply the recorder's existing disable context to draft warmup and capture, so those callbacks do not reset or publish target-expert counts. | The existing single-layer migration algorithm still decides which expert to send, receive or copy locally. This PR supplies the NPU storage views and communication group. It builds on the NPU EPLB support and common recorder lifecycle fix

title: [Fix] spec: Prune the draft branch instead of crashing when the grammar rejects a token
summary: ## Motivation `traverse_tree` (used by DSPARK/DFLASH and other spec-decode paths to build the grammar bitmask over the draft tree) calls `grammar.accept_token()` on every draft token that passed its parent's mask row. The matcher can still reject one — a mask/matcher desync, e.g. a disaggregation retracted-request double-accept — and `XGrammarGrammar.accept_token` raises `ValueError: Tokens not accepted`. That exception was **uncaught**, so it propagated out of the scheduler event loop and **killed the engine**: ``` File ".../speculative/spec_utils.py", line 717, in dfs grammar.accept_token(int(draft_tokens[curr])) File ".../constrained/xgrammar_backend.py", line 103, in accept_token raise ValueError(f"Tokens not accepted: {token} ...") ValueError: Tokens not accepted: 1 # -> "Scheduler hit an exception" -> process exit -> liveness probe fails -> pod recreated ``` Observed on a PD-disaggregated DeepSeek deployment running DSPARK speculative decoding with xgrammar JSON-schema structured output: a single structured-output request takes down the whole decode engine. ## Modifications A grammar-rejected draft token is exactly what speculative decoding already handles — it simply should not be accepted. In `dfs`, on the `ValueError`: - Clear that token in the **parent mask row**, so the verify step will not accept it (the mask now agrees with the matcher). - **Prune** the branch (skip fill / children). The accept failed, so the grammar is still at the parent state and **no rollback is owed** for the node. - Sibling branches keep being verified; the request stays alive and its out

title: [Feat] dsa: Honor the page stride of index-K buffers
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49913 * #49966 * __->__ #49912 * #49775 * #49720 * #49719 ## Motivation The DSA indexer's paged index-K kernels assume the pages of the buffer they are given are packed back to back: page `p` starts at `p * page_bytes`. A pool that keeps each page's index keys inside a larger per-page entry hands out a per-layer view `(num_pages, page_bytes)` whose `stride(0)` is larger than one page's blob. With such a view, `fused_store_index_k_cache`'s wrapper silently copied the destination with `.contiguous()`, so the writes were lost, and the other kernels either refused the view or read the wrong bytes. The unified memory pool needs this for Kimi-K3.1 in the next PR of this stack. ## Modifications Every CUDA writer and reader of index-K pages that Kimi-K3.1 reaches now addresses page `p` at `p * buf.stride(0)`: - `fused_store_index_k_cache` (JIT `fused_store_index_cache.cuh`): the kernel takes the page stride from the tensor. The wrapper no longer copies a non-contiguous destination; it asserts `stride(-1) == 1`. - `fused_k_indexer_norm_rope_store` (`deepseek_v32/indexer_k.cuh`): same change. - `SetKAndS` / `GetKAndS` (Triton): pages are addressed by `stride(0)` instead of the page size, and the setter no longer requires a contiguous buffer. Page offsets are computed in int64; the getter's int32 offset would have overflowed at about 1.8k pages of 1.2 MB. - `store_fp4_index_k_cache` already used `stride(0)`; its offsets are now int64. - The CuTe DSL paged MQA logits kernel takes the block stride from the tensor instead of rejecting a s

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Size a fused draft's KV region in the dtype the draft resolves
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49913 * #49966 * #49912 * __->__ #49775 * #49720 * #49719 ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory`, a speculative draft's KV cache can live in its own region inside the target's pages, and that region may hold a dtype other than the target's. The region was sized with the target's resolved KV dtype standing in for an `auto` draft dtype. The draft runner resolves `auto` from the quant config its loaded model keeps, and several draft classes narrow that config in their constructors. Example: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4` declares an FP8 KV cache, but its MTP head ships in BF16 (`qwen3_5_mtp.py::_mtp_quant_config` returns `None` for serialized NVFP4). The target resolves FP8, and the region is sized FP8. The draft then resolves BF16 and fails to bind: ``` ValueError: Fused draft KV: the draft resolved its KV cache dtype to torch.bfloat16, but its region inside the target's pages holds torch.float8_e4m3fn. Set --speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype explicitly ... ``` The same happens with any explicit `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype auto` whose draft keeps no FP8 KV declaration. ## Modifications - `model_loader/loader.py::built_quant_config`: the quant config a model keeps once built, known before it is built. It is the loader's config (`_get_quantization_config`, which every loader calls), narrowed by the model class's optional `own_quant_config`. - `own_quant_config(hf_config, quant_config)` on every draft class whose kept config differs from the loader's; a class without it keeps the loader's config. title: [Refactor] mem_cache: Keep the KDA speculative ReplaySSM ring in the request sub-pool
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49913 * #49966 * #49912 * #49775 * __->__ #49720 * #49719 ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory`, the KDA speculative ReplaySSM ring was a part of every state slot's entry. Every cached prefix checkpoint carried a ring it never reads (each commit folds the accepted records into the state), and a PD prefill server, which runs no verify, declared a different state entry than its decode peer, so unified KDA speculative ReplaySSM with PD was refused. Building on the request sub-pool of the previous PR, the KDA ring now lives there too. ## Modifications - `mem_cache/kv/decl.py`: every speculative ring is a request part. The decode ring (`--enable-linear-replayssm`) stays in the slot, since it lags the slot's state. - `kda_backend.py`, `spec_utils.py`, `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`: KDA verify and both commit paths index the ring by the rows the forward resolved, never the live request table; a request-scoped ring without resolved rows is an error, not a silent slot write. - `kernels/ops/attention/kda_decode_mtp.py`: the CuTe DSL MTP verify takes an optional `replayssm_ring_indices`. With it, the ring stores use those rows; without it, they use the state slot as before. The fallback to the Triton verify for request-scoped rings is removed. - `kv_cache_configurator.py`: unified KDA speculative ReplaySSM with PD disaggregation is no longer refused: prefill and decode declare the same state entries. ## Tests - New: the KDA ring is request memory and checkpoints no longer carry it (`test_declared_parts.py`); a PD prefill with

title: [Refactor] mem_cache: Keep the GDN speculative ReplaySSM ring in a request sub-pool of unified memory
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49913 * #49966 * #49912 * #49775 * #49720 * __->__ #49719 ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory`, the GDN speculative ReplaySSM ring and its three cursors were allocated outside the unified arena, as fixed rows reserved for every possible request row. That memory could not be shared with KV or state, it was reserved even with few requests running, and it was the last request-scoped payload kept outside the arena. This PR keeps request-scoped payload in a *request sub-pool* of the arena: one unit per bound request row, priced and moved like every other sub-pool, never cached by the prefix tree, never stored on the host or sent to a PD peer. ## Modifications - **Declaration and plan** (`mem_cache/kv/decl.py`, `kv/plan.py`, new `kv/layout/request.py`): `RequestLifetime` joins the lifetimes. A state geometry's `request_parts` form one float `request` sub-pool. `drive_order`, tree slots and PD wire entries exclude it. `RequestPartDecl` and `KVStoragePlan.request_parts` are removed. - **Allocation** (`kv/alloc/chain.py`, `kv/requests.py`): a non-owner `FloatBand` per request sub-pool whose virtual ids are request rows. `RequestTable.alloc_rows` / `free_rows` bind and free the units. A unit is zeroed when handed out and reused only after the forwards that touched it retire, so the per-forward row reset is no longer needed for unified memory. - **Pricing**: `KVDemand.request_rows` is priced in the chain's take and admission, the shared-memory prefill budget and the scheduler's admission sites, PD preallocation and the memory

title: [Fix] vision: Compute SDPA masks on GPU during graph capture
summary: ### Motivation When `VisionSdpaAttention` runs under CUDA/HIP Graph capture with GPU `cu_seqlens`, both sequence-isolation paths copy `cu_seqlens` back to CPU via `.tolist()`: 1. `_maskless_seq_lens` calls `cu_seqlens.tolist()` to split sequences into Python integer lengths for per-sequence unmasked SDPA calls. 2. `generate_patch_attention_mask` calls `tuple(cu_seqlens.cpu().tolist())` to build and cache the boolean mask on CPU. During stream capture, those GPU-to-CPU reads fail with `RuntimeError: Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture`. Caching a static mask before capture would also apply stale boundaries when replaying the graph with updated `cu_seqlens`. ### Modifications Modified `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py`: 1. In `_maskless_seq_lens`, return `None` when `cu_seqlens.is_cuda and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` so captured graphs skip per-sequence Python splitting and use a fixed-shape masked SDPA call. 2. In `generate_patch_attention_mask`, compute the boolean mask directly on device when `cu_seqlens.is_cuda and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`: - `flatten_batch=True`: map token positions to segment IDs via `torch.searchsorted(cu_seqlens, positions, right=True)`, clamp valid tokens to `[cu_seqlens[0], cu_seqlens[-1])`, and broadcast to `[1, s, s]`. - `flatten_batch=False`: compute `cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]` and broadcast to `[bsz, 1, s, s]`. ### Accuracy Tests Verified on AMD Radeon 880M (gfx1150, Torch `2.14.1+rocm7.2`): - Graph capture and multi-boundary replay match explicit-mask reference out

title: [Fix] DSV4: count folded encoder-SWA replay rows in the prefill-graph DP vote
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, the breakable prefill CUDA graph, and decoder- plus encoder-SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4, every DP rank must reach the same graph-or-eager decision for a prefill step. Otherwise one rank replays the graph while another runs the step eagerly, and their collectives no longer match. The DP vote (`_local_prefill_cuda_graph_vote`) asks the backend's `vote_prefill_cuda_graph` whether the late-layer tail of the batch fits the in-graph tail block. That vote reads the raw `batch.extend_lens`. Later, the worker's `fold_encoder_swa_replay` prepends each prefix hit's last SWA window (`replay_len(prefix) = min(prefix, 128)` rows) to its extend. It also shifts the logprob start by the same amount. `can_run_prefill_cuda_graph` then judges this folded batch. The two checks see different lengths. When a batch's raw tail fits the block but its folded tail does not, the rank votes for the graph and then rejects it locally after the DP verdict. The MLP-sync row count already adds these rows (`dp_attn.py`: `num_tokens += folded_replay_rows(local_batch)`), and `replay_len`'s docstring lists its readers. The backend vote was the one reader that missed them. **Trigger.** The tail block holds `max_running_requests * 128` rows. A request's tail normally stays at most one window (128 rows), so the folded tail can only outgrow the block for requests that run their whole extend in the late layers. Those are requests that return prompt logprobs (`logprob_start_len` inside the extend), or requests that return every hidden state (outside DSpark). Each such request gai

title: [Perf] [Apple] activation: Add a Metal SiLU-and-mul for the Torch MPS path
summary: Depends on #47803. Only the last commit is new; please merge #47803 first. I'll rebase this once it lands. ## Motivation Second part of the "direct Metal semantic ops for eager" item in #32321, after RMSNorm in #47803. It needs the `"mps"` dispatch key added there. Today `SiluAndMul` runs `forward_native` on Apple Silicon: a slice, `silu`, and a multiply, each a separate MPS kernel with its own intermediate. This PR does it in one Metal kernel. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/activation/silu_and_mul_mps.py` (new): `silu(x[..., :d]) * x[..., d:]` compiled with `torch.mps.compile_shader`. Computes in fp32 and rounds once on store, like `forward_native`. title: [AMD] Fix cross-layer KV sharing on ROCm: consumers zero the provider's cache
summary: Depends on #47271 — please merge after it. #47271 adds cross-layer KV sharing and correctly threads `save_kv_cache` through `forward_mla.py` (CUDA), but `forward_mla_rocm.py` still hardcodes `save_kv_cache = True` (line 926 on that branch). Without #47271 there is no KV sharing, so the hardcode is harmless and this patch is a no-op — hence stacked rather than standalone. ## Mechanism Mistral-Large-4 has 9 KV-sharing consumer layers (39, 43, …, 71) reading provider layer 35. A consumer drops `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` and passes an all-zero placeholder latent. With `save_kv_cache` forced `True`, every consumer wrote those zeros into layer 35's cache immediately before reading it. Zero K/V give uniform scores, so attention output is exactly 0; `o_proj` has no bias, so the layer collapses to an identity on the residual stream. Net: 10 of 72 attention layers dead in decode (35 plus its 9 consumers), while the MoE stack and the other 62 attention layers stayed intact — fluent text with broken long-range reasoning and arithmetic wrong by small amounts. No error, no warning; the server looked healthy throughout. ## Fix Mirror the CUDA path: read `self.save_kv_cache` and pass it to `attn_mqa(...)` and `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode(...)`, which previously fell through to `RadixAttention.forward`'s default of `True` (`radix_attention.py:120`). ## Reproduction dependencies Measured on `amd/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B-Quark-MXFP4`, which needs **both**: 1. #47271 (the model itself), and 2. a separate commit for Quark MXFP4 checkpoint loading (name mapper, block-FP8 scales) that is not in #47271 — tha

title: [Fix] quantization: Load block-FP8 MoE TP shards that split checkpoint blocks
summary: ## Motivation A block-FP8 MoE layer whose per-rank intermediate size is not a multiple of the checkpoint block is rejected. With 128x128 blocks and `moe_intermediate_size` 640, any TP size without EP hits it (TP2: 320, TP4: 160, TP8: 80 per rank): ``` ValueError: The output_size of gate's and up's weight = 320 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128. ``` - `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`: only the MTP experts are block-FP8, so only the draft layer is affected. The cookbook works around it with the BF16 head from the RadixArk export. - `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`: every MoE layer (48 plus MTP) is affected. With EP (the cookbook's `--tp 4 --ep 4`), experts are not split and nothing changes. ### Why refine the scales instead of padding the shard Padding each shard to whole 128 blocks also works, and touches fewer kernels. But on the official FP8 checkpoint it pads every MoE layer: | MoE TP | shard | padded | routed-expert weights / rank | padding adds / rank | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2 | 320 | 384 | ~56 GiB | ~11 GiB (+20%) | | 4 | 160 | 256 | ~28 GiB | ~17 GiB (+60%) | | 8 | 80 | 128 | ~14 GiB | ~8.5 GiB (+60%) | (Computed from the config, not measured: 48 layers x 512 experts x 3 x 2560 x 640 FP8.) The padded rows also cost compute. Measured on the MTP layer at TP2, a padded layer was 8-23% slower than a refined one on Triton and 4-17% slower on DeepGEMM. Refinement only adds scales. ## Modifications TP splits w13 along N and w2 along K. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug `sigmoid_gate_topk_renorm` accepts `k=5, n_shared_experts=4` through its host-side checks, but the Triton kernel cannot compile for this input. The host checks pass, then compilation fails with a `tl.static_assert` because `next_power_of_2(k)` and `next_power_of_2(k + n_shared_experts)` differ: - `K_POW2 = next_power_of_2(5) = 8` - `A_POW2 = next_power_of_2(5 + 4) = 16` - device assertion: `tl.static_assert(K_POW2 == A_POW2, "epilogue reuses the topk slot axis for the active axis")` The wrapper computes `K_POW2` and `A_POW2` independently when building the launch, but does not validate that they are equal before launching the Triton kernel. The device assertion is therefore only discovered at kernel compilation time. The production shape `k=6, n_shared_experts=2` is not affected because both values are 8. The problem appears when the routed/shared split crosses a power-of-two boundary. Expected behavior: either support `A_POW2 > K_POW2`, or reject the combination in the Python wrapper with a clear `ValueError` before launching Triton. title: [Perf] [AMD] aiter: Quantize unified prefill Q to FP8 when the KV cache is FP8
summary: ## Motivation #38757 routes AITER extend/prefill through `unified_attention`. When the KV cache is FP8, it still passes Q in BF16. AITER then sees a BF16-Q / FP8-KV call, which has two effects: - AITER does not select its tuned FP8-Q / FP8-KV prefill config (ROCm/aiter#5598). - The gfx950 Gluon kernel is not used, because it requires Q and KV to have the same dtype (ROCm/aiter#4614). The unified **decode** path already quantizes Q to FP8 with `scaled_fp8_quant()` and passes the matching `q_descale`. This PR makes prefill do the same. The GQA KV-head-repeat FP8 ASM prefill that used to be part of this PR was split out to a separate PR, linked below once opened. title: [Perf] [AMD] DeepSeek-V4.1: compile the vision encoder's norm, rotary and gated activation
summary: **Stacked on #44918.** Until that merges, this diff includes its commit; the change here is the last two commits only (the compile change and the import fix). ## Motivation The DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder runs its RMSNorms, 2D rotary and SiLU-gated MLP activation in fp32 eager mode, so each of them is several elementwise kernels per layer (32 layers). With #44918 removing the host-side overhead, these launches and the fp32 round trips through memory are a visible share of the encoder's time. ## Modifications - `models/deepseek_v41_vit.py`: `rms_norm`, `apply_rotary` and `silu_and_mul` are wrapped in `torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=get_compiler_backend())`, so each becomes one fused kernel. - `dynamic=True` keeps one graph across image grids; there is no recompile per image size. - `rms_norm` keeps `RMSNorm.forward_native`'s arithmetic (fp32 upcast, `rsqrt`, weight, downcast) and reads the module's weight and epsilon, so checkpoints load unchanged. - On by default; no new server args or env vars. - Import fix: main moved `get_compiler_backend` into `sglang.srt.utils.device` ("utils: Split common.py into topic modules", #48781). title: [Perf] [AMD] fla/gdn: Faster GDN long-prompt prefill on gfx95 (chunk kernels, two-stream chunk scan, no host syncs)
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X, a long Qwen3.8-27B prompt (100k-200k tokens, TP1, 16384-token prefill chunks, 48 GDN layers) spends about 11% of its prefill in the chunked gated delta rule of `fla/`. A profile of a 200k-token request shows costs that do not need to be there: 1. `chunk_fwd_o` launches two programs per (chunk, head) (`BV=64` for V = 128), and both compute the same `q @ k^T` of the chunk. 2. In a breakable prefill CUDA graph the Triton GDN kernel returns a new tensor, which `_linear_attention_with_output_impl` copies into the graph's static output buffer (2 x 201 MB per layer and chunk). 3. `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_intra` zero-fills A before the fused kkt + solve kernel, which writes only the blocks on and below the diagonal. 4. `chunk_h`, the serial recurrence (one program per (head, V block), 192 programs for 48 heads x 4, each walking 256 chunks), is latency-bound and leaves most CUs idle, while the per-chunk kernels before and after it wait for it. 5. Each prefill step has host reads of device tensors (`prepare_chunk_indices` `.tolist()` and index copy, the pipelined scan's `cu_seqlens.tolist()`, `prepare_chunk_offsets` `new_tensor([0])`). Each blocks the CPU until the GPU has drained, so the GPU idles 1.2-1.5 ms at the start of every chunk. The values are all known on the host (`extend_seq_lens_cpu`). The fifth read of the step, in the aiter prefill indices, is not touched here; newer main already removes it. ## Adaptation note This PR was reduced and rebased for review. It now contains 8 commits on top of main `d800cb859e`: the earlier 5-change kernel series

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: Match exclude entries that name a parameter (.weight) by module
summary: ## Motivation `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4` keeps its MTP (next-token prediction) layer in BF16 and lists it in the Quark `exclude` list by parameter name, e.g. `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight`: all 15 `mtp.*` entries end in `.weight`. Exclusion is matched against module names (exact or `re:`), so none of these entries match. Since #39064, `_mtp_quant_config` keeps the Quark config for a draft whose routed experts are not excluded and relies on the per-layer exclusions to keep the BF16 modules BF16; this dense MTP has no experts, so its linears are built as packed MXFP4 parameters and loading the BF16 MTP tensors fails: ``` Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP.load_weights -> load_merged_column_weight: AssertionError (assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape) ``` MTP speculative decoding therefore cannot start on this checkpoint without editing its `config.json`. #36158 (checkpoint probe for MTP quantization) does not cover this case: it asks the checkpoint only when the exclude list names no `mtp.*` layer, and this checkpoint names all of them. title: [Perf] DFLASH: Verify top-k sampled batches on the all-gathered top-k support (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation With TP > 1 and a softcapped lm_head, DFLASH verify finishes the logits all-gather in the worker. For a sampled batch it then: - all-gathers the full fp32 logits of every verify row, `[bs * block, vocab]`; - softcaps them and runs a radix top-k over the whole vocabulary; - scatters the target p and the draft selector's q into vocab-sized tensors; - runs the chain sampler, which scans the whole vocabulary. When the requests sample with a top-k, as many generation configs do by default, only the top-k tokens of a row carry target mass. Almost all of that work reads and writes zeros, and the gather moves the largest tensor of the step across the TP group. With this PR, such a batch is verified on the top-k support alone: - each rank takes the top `next_power_of_2(max_top_k + 16)` logits of its vocab shard. The 16 spare slots hold logits tied with the k-th one; - the ranks all-gather those (value, id) pairs instead of their shards. At TP8 and a 202K vocabulary, that is 1 KB per row from each rank instead of 101 KB; - one Triton kernel softcaps and merges the candidates into each row's exact top-k and argmax. It uses the softcap formula of the dense gather, so the kept values equal the dense row's bit for bit; - one Triton kernel runs the chain accept and the residual resample on that support. It makes the dense path's two uniform draws in the same order. It adapts the top-k chain sampler of #41283 to DFLASH's exactly-k top-k and sparse q. title: [Perf] scheduler: Avoid redundant tree work in dfs-weight scheduling
summary: ## Motivation `--schedule-policy dfs-weight` does CPU work that cannot affect its result: it builds an auxiliary waiting-prefix tree for a deprioritization set that DFS never consumes, and its Python ordering helper traverses every resident cache branch even when the current queue touches only a few of them. ## Modifications - Keep real KV-prefix matching and all request-field updates. Skip auxiliary in-batch prefix matching/insertion only for `DFS_WEIGHT`; LPM, HRRN, and shortest-prefill-first still use their existing deduplication path. Compute the policy guard once per scheduling call and check the existing prefix threshold first inside the loop so warm hits retain their short-circuit path. summary: ## Motivation Deterministic mode refuses AITER decode attention for MLA models (DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1, Kimi K2, Moonlight, ...), so they decode on Triton MLA, the slowest part of their deterministic step. summary: ## Motivation `/v1/audio/transcriptions` sends `text=""`, which reaches the multimodal processor as an empty `input_ids` list. summary: ## Motivation `hyperparameter_tuning.mdx` currently covers offline throughput only. A common issue in online serving is not documented: a long prompt pauses every running request for the full duration of its prefill, because prefill is scheduled first and the chunks of a long prompt run back-to-back by default. The two existing flags that address this, `--enable-mixed-chunk` and `--prefill-decode-interval`, are only described in one line each in the server arguments reference, with no guidance on when to use them. ## Modifications Adds a "Reducing decode stalls for online serving" section to `docs/advanced_features/hyperparameter_tuning.mdx`: - why long prompts stall decoding (prefill-first scheduling, back-to-back chunks, and why smaller chunks do not help) - `--enable-mixed-chunk` and `--prefill-decode-interval`: what each does, measured effect, and cost - guidance on choosing between them ## Accuracy Tests Documentation only; no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No code changes. The numbers in the doc come from the following run. SGLang 0.5.23, 1x A40, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (BF16). Background load: `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 32`. Three 16,048-token prompts with `max_tokens=32` were sent 5 s apart during the run, each with a unique prefix to avoid prefix cache hits. All four configurations were run on the same machine in one session; scheduler logs confirm the long-prompt chunks in each run were prefilled with 32 running requests

title: [Fix] scheduler: Park a chunked prefill continuation when its chunk or KV budget is spent
summary: ## Motivation A chunked prefill continuation is sized by `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens`. When nothing was available, it fell back to the full `chunk_limit` so the continuation could make progress. That fallback assumed two things that do not always hold: - **The chunk limit is positive.** With `--enable-mixed-chunk`, the decode rows are charged to the chunk first (`rem_chunk_tokens -= running_bs`). When more requests are decoding than `chunked_prefill_size`, the limit is negative, and the continuation got a negative chunk: `extend_end < prefix_len`, an empty input slice, and negative extend lengths in the batch. - **The pool holds the chunk.** Running decodes' reserved headroom can drive `remaining_total` negative. The full chunk was then admitted without checking free tokens, and the scheduler crashed in `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend`: ``` RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 16384 tokens. Available full tokens: 3200 (full_available_size=3200 + full_evictable_size_=0) ``` ## Modifications - `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` returns `None` when no chunk tokens are available, so the continuation parks for this pass. This matches `SWAPrefillBudget` and the joint budget, which already park. - A parked continuation admits no one ahead of it: the waiting-queue loop in `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` stops, so no batch carries a chunked request it does not run, or counts it in flight. Before this, only an exhausted chunk budget stopped admission; an exhausted memory budget did not. This also stops priority preemption for t

title: [Perf] kimi-k3.1: Share ViT work across prefill CP ranks
summary: ## Motivation With TP2/PCP2 and singleton attention TP, Kimi's internal image-DP path encodes the same uncached images on both CP ranks. Share whole-image work across the stage-local TP group, then restore complete features in input order before language-model CP sharding. Shared ownership requires agreement on image identities and cache misses. Rank-private cache drift can associate same-shaped features with the wrong image or let only one rank enter a collective. A local allocation failure must also stop peers before they enter feature communication. ## Modifications - Use the stage-local TP group for ownership and feature collectives when image-DP is enabled, CP>1 and attention-DP=1. CP=1 and attention-DP>1 retain existing behavior; PP/EP sizes are not hard-coded. - Compare ordered image identities and miss digests before cache-hit early returns. Recompute the ordered union of misses when caches disagree and discard affected old entries. - Coordinate capturable preprocessing, ViT, allocation and output-processing failures. Allocate the complete all-gather receive buffer inside the guarded local stage, preserving the symmetric-memory allocation context and existing preallocated-output communication backend. The single-image broadcast and implicit attention-TP path retain their existing behavior. - Use CustomTestCase for both CPU entries. Exercise independent Gloo control/payload groups, including receive-buffer allocation failure and subsequent encoding. Use a temporary FileStore rendezvous. - Preserve model math, dtype, load balancing and language-model parallel groups.

title: [Fix] cpu: wire --device cpu to the CPU-engine platform selection
summary: ## Motivation `--device cpu` did not activate the CPU engine. Platform selection and layer-level device dispatch gate on the **`SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE` env var** (`platforms/__init__.py`, `utils/device.py::is_cpu()`), which is independent of the CLI flag. Launching with `--device cpu` but without the env var leaves `is_cpu()` False, so the scheduler believes it is on CPU while the layer-level dispatch believes it is not; model construction then falls into the non-CUDA / non-HIP branch of `rotary_embedding/base.py:143` and crashes with a misleading error: ``` ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm' ``` `vllm` is not even an sglang dependency, so the message sends users down the wrong path. This is reproducible on master `a8ff9948` with `pip install -e ./python` on a GPU-less host (CPU-only, i9-13900K, no AMX). #41727 documents the same env-var-before-imports requirement ("SGLang caches platform detection") for the simulator; this PR wires the documented CLI surface so the env var is no longer a hidden prerequisite. Timing constraints the fix must respect (and does): 1. `is_cpu()` is `@lru_cache` — children forked from the launcher would inherit a cached `False`, so the cache must be cleared **before** scheduler subprocesses are forked. 2. Scheduler subprocesses are plain `mp.Process` (fork on Linux) — the env var must be set in the launcher process before the fork, not just in the child. 3. `current_platform` resolves lazily via module `__getattr__`, so children resolve it after the fork with the var already set. ## Modifications In `handle_cpu_backends` (ServerArgs resol

title: [Feat] flexkv: Support external connector and hybrid restore ownership
summary: ## Problem and resulting behavior Connect SGLang's ordinary prefix cache and DeepSeek V4 split C4/C128/SWA cache to the external FlexKV connector. Lookup and prefetch can run before admission; restore destinations are allocated only after admission and stay owned until checkpoint or row release. This prevents a rank that cannot allocate from leaving its peers inside a restore collective, and prevents rematches or stale cleanup from reclaiming active DMA destinations. This revision merges SGLang main `7b790e1c5f3f2601c3d9c549ad24eaf7ee0d5938`, uses the current lazy-prefix/checkpoint/request-retirement interfaces, and removes the duplicate connector and communication implementation from SGLang. - Ordinary MP restores become tree-owned. Ordinary IP and hybrid MP/IP retain private leases. Row cleanup validates ownership before mutation, applies the restored SWA boundary before freeing, and retires the lease afterwards. Reset fences writers before reclaiming orphaned allocations; stale completions cannot cancel a successor attempt. - With `sync_load_ready`, both adapters vote after allocation/eviction retry and before restore collectives. Failed votes release fresh peer slots and held lookups while preserving existing tree prefixes. This agreement is independent of batching. - Current separate-buffer DSv4 and unified-chain allocators coexist. Tail allocation uses the separate allocator's scalar contract or the chain's named-window mapping, including retry after eviction. title: [Bug] one_batch crashes with --enable-dp-attention: int object has no attribute startswith
summary: ## Describe the bug `sglang.benchmark.one_batch` constructs requests with an integer `rid` (`Req(rid=i, ...)`), although `Req` declares `rid: str`. With DP attention enabled, `prepare_mlp_sync_batch_raw` calls `is_health_check_generate_req`. The helper checks only whether `rid` is not `None` before calling `rid.startswith(HEALTH_CHECK_RID_PREFIX)`, so the first prefill fails with `AttributeError`. ## Reproduction Replace `<model>` with the model path: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch --model <model> \ --tp-size 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --ep-size 4 \ --batch-size 8 --input-len 8192 --output-len 1 ``` Relevant traceback: ```text File ".../benchmark/one_batch.py", in latency_test_run_once next_token_ids, _, batch = model_runner.extend(reqs) File ".../managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py", in <genexpr> and all(is_health_check_generate_req(req) for req in local_batch.reqs) File ".../managers/utils.py", in is_health_check_generate_req return rid is not None and rid.startswith(HEALTH_CHECK_RID_PREFIX) AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith' ``` The same workload was confirmed to complete on the remote H20 system after converting both benchmark request IDs to strings and adding a string-type guard to the helper. ## Environment Reported `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output (package and hardware details): ```text Python: 3.12.16 (main, Oct 26 2026, 14:08:45) [Clang 23.1.3 ] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 1

title: [Test] mem_cache: Skip DSA indexer sharding test below SM 8.9
summary: ## Motivation `TestPageInterleaveIndexer.test_two_gpu` / `test_four_gpu` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_page_sharded_dsa_attention.py` only check the GPU count. On multi-GPU hosts below SM 8.9 (T4, V100, A100, ...) they error instead of skipping, because the DSA indexer K cache stores FP8 E4M3 and Triton can't compile `fp8e4nv` there: ``` triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0: def _set_k_and_s_triton_kernel( ^ ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')") ``` Both `packed` iterations of `_run_indexer` go through `SetKAndS.triton`, so the test can't run at all below SM 8.9. The file is registered in `base-a-test-cpu`, so running that suite on such a host reports a false failure. Upstream CI doesn't hit this: the CPU runners have no GPU, and the CUDA registration targets `4-gpu-b200`. ## Modifications In `TestPageInterleaveIndexer._test_world`, skip when `torch.cuda.get_device_capability() < (8, 9)`. The check runs in the parent process before `mp.spawn`, so no workers start and no process group is created on unsupported GPUs. This mirrors the existing capability gate in `TestShardedDSAAttention` in the same file. The threshold is SM 8.9 rather than `major in (9, 10)` because this path only needs FP8 E4M3, so Ada keeps its coverage. Test-only change, 2 lines. summary: ## Motivation FP16 pooling can return NaNs for zero embeddings because `F.normalize`'s epsilon rounds to zero. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Run the side-stream mHC mix in BF16x3 for Blackwell decode batches
summary: ## Motivation On Blackwell, the mHC mix for 32-4095 rows runs the DeepGEMM TF32 prenorm GEMM. Since #48984 that is the one-pass `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_dual`. In decode, the FFN-side mix runs on the side stream while MegaGate and MegaMoE use the full SM budget. So what it costs is how much it slows them down, not its own runtime. The compensated BF16x3 mix on a 64x64 grid is shorter, and its small CTAs co-reside with MegaMoE's, so it adds less to the decode step. Before this PR, Blackwell used BF16x3 only for 4096-65536 rows. Earlier revisions of this PR targeted a GSM8K loss seen with the old two-call TF32 mix. On current main (with #48984 and sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.7) that loss does not reproduce (see Accuracy), so this PR is now a performance change only. ## Modifications - `_mix_stats_impl`: on SM100/SM103, use the BF16x3 projection for 32-256 rows as well. 257-4095 rows keep the dual TF32 kernel, since the 64x64 grid is slower from 512 rows (see the kernel table). SM107 measures slower with it and keeps the dual TF32 kernel for all rows below 4096; SM12x keeps its split-K partial path. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Time out decode preallocation waits and clear stale lifecycle state
summary: ## Motivation With prefill and decode served by separate workers, a decode request can wait indefinitely before KV-cache allocation because its receive timeout does not start until transfer metadata is sent. Starting the waiting deadline at the first receiver poll lets participating ranks agree on failure before allocation or transfer proceeds. An emptied prefill-only batch also retains its prefill-only flag, and pending health-check signals are returned only one per scheduler pass. This PR clears that stale batch state and drains the pending signals. The chunk-budget admission changes previously included here are removed in favor of #35645, which addresses #35642. That work is maintained by @imReese with regression tests contributed by @Kangwenqiao. ## Modifications - Start the waiting deadline before allocation and report expiry through receiver polling before the existing rank consensus. The preallocation wait is tracked in its own field, so `init_time` still marks metadata publication. Abort notification relies on `init_time` to decide whether to arm deferred KV release, and preallocation-queue cleanup never clears that state, so a request aborted or timed out before publication must not arm it. Metadata submission starts a fresh transfer deadline. - Clear the prefill-only flag when filtering empties a batch. - Return all pending health-check signals in the scheduler pass. ## Accuracy Tests 92 CPU tests and 6 subtests passed across the five changed test files. title: [Fix] mamba: Retry queued prefills when cache capacity may have recovered
summary: ## Motivation A hybrid SSM server can leave requests queued even after Mamba-state capacity becomes available. Once admission marks the running batch as full, the scheduler does not retry while that batch remains unchanged. Cached states can become evictable during that time, so a previous capacity failure is not a valid reason to stop checking. Retrying exposes a second problem. Each admission attempt re-runs the prefix match, and a match that hits a cached Mamba state allocates a per-request slot for the copy-on-write before `PrefillAdder` checks capacity. If no slot can be freed (for example, decode has consumed a shared Mamba/attention pool since the earlier refusal and the remaining cached states are locked), that allocation asserted and terminated the scheduler instead of leaving the request queued. This PR retries admission for hybrid SSM models whose cache supports Mamba state, and makes a failed copy-on-write allocation an ordinary admission refusal. It does not bypass capacity checks or enlarge the pool. ## Modifications - Clear the full-batch admission latch each scheduler round for that configuration, alongside the existing hybrid-SWA and priority-preemption resets. Other configurations retain their existing behavior. - When the Mamba copy-on-write slot cannot be allocated even after eviction, raise a dedicated `MambaCowAllocError` instead of asserting. title: [Fix] Skip cancelled requests in the dynamic batch tokenizer
summary: ## Motivation With the dynamic batch tokenizer enabled, cancelling an `encode()` caller leaves its prompt in the queue. title: [HF3FS] Stop persistence timers on graceful shutdown
summary: ## Motivation With HF3FS metadata persistence enabled, stopping Uvicorn leaves the process waiting for its non-daemon save timer. The timer keeps scheduling its successor, while the registered `atexit` shutdown callback cannot run until those threads finish. A confirmed write after the last periodic save is consequently not flushed on graceful shutdown. ## Modifications - Shut down persistence in `Hf3fsMetadataServer.run()`'s `finally`, including serving errors and `KeyboardInterrupt`. - Fence shutdown and timer rearming with the existing state lock. Cancel and join the timer outside that lock before the final save, so an active periodic writer cannot race the final writer on the same temporary file. - Make shutdown idempotent and avoid joining the current thread. - Add CPU regressions for normal return, serving failure, interruption, a gated active save, repeated shutdown, and disabled persistence. ## Accuracy Tests - Original source: five failing assertions across the new methods/subtests; corrected source: four test methods and three subtests pass. - Actual loopback Uvicorn, metadata HTTP initialize/reserve/confirm, and SIGINT reproduction: before the fix, Uvicorn stopped but the process did not exit and the confirmed write was absent from persistence. After the fix, the process exits successfully and the final confirmed key/page mapping is persisted. - The local source harness executes the repository classes and tests while excluding GPU-heavy backend import initialization. Timers, JSON/filesystem I/O, FastAPI and Uvicorn are real; no GPU or native 3FS storage validatio

title: fix(deepseek_v2): don't coerce unscaled MLA models onto deepseek_yarn
summary: ## Motivation `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` treats a truthy `rope_scaling` as "scaling is configured": ```python # python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py if rope_scaling: rope_scaling["rope_type"] = "deepseek_yarn" ``` That held on transformers v4, where unscaled models had `rope_scaling = None`. On v5, `config.rope_scaling` aliases `rope_parameters` and is **always** populated — for GLM-4.7-Flash: ```python {'rope_theta': 1000000, 'partial_rotary_factor': 1.0, 'rope_type': 'default'} ``` So every unscaled MLA model is now coerced onto the YaRN path and reaches branches expecting keys its config never carried (notably `original_max_position_embeddings`). This repo already recognises the v5 aliasing — `rotary_embedding/factory.py::_get_rope_param` documents it and warns + defaults. That handles the symptom; this PR removes the coercion that makes the fallback necessary. On ROCm the same config is fatal rather than a warning, because aiter's vendored `get_rope` has no equivalent fallback (see ROCm/aiter#4742). ## Modifications Adds `_has_rope_scaling()`, true only when `rope_type`/`type` is neither `None` nor `"default"`, and uses it at the three sites that made the v4 assumption: | Line | Before | | --- | --- | | 1775 | `if rope_scaling:` | | 1887 | `if rope_scaling and rope_scaling.get("apply_yarn_scaling", True):` | | 1891 | `self.use_deepseek_yarn_rope = rope_scaling is not None` | Scope: configs declaring `rope_type="yarn"`/`"deepseek_yarn"` (DeepSeek, Kimi, etc.) are unaffected and still take the YaRN path. Only configs explicitly declaring `default` stop being coerced. Lin

title: [Feature] Interleaved Prefill Pipeline Parallelism for DeepSeek-V4.1: PP4 x CP2 with Two Virtual Stages per Rank
summary: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary Introduce forward-only interleaved pipeline parallelism for DeepSeek-V4.1 Prefill. Each physical PP rank owns two non-contiguous layer chunks: one from the first 20 layers and one from the last 20 layers. This is physical **PP4 x CP2 with virtual pipeline size 2 (VPP2)**, using eight GPUs in total. It is not physical PP8. The proposal separates: 1. Physical ranks and their communication groups. 2. Logical stages and their execution order. 3. Shared KV sources and their producer/consumer ownership. Non-contiguous weight placement alone is insufficient. The design also requires a stage-aware scheduler, mHC state handoff, explicit shared-cache dependencies, and a coordinated cache/PD lifecycle. ## Motivation and Evidence DeepSeek-V4.1's causal encoder-decoder (CED) structure and cross-layer sharing make equal layer counts a poor proxy for equal Prefill cost. Splitting layers 0-19 and 20-39 is semantically possible, but can be poorly balanced, especially with decoder SWA bounded replay: - The early layers process the full uncached extend. - Layer 20 still processes the full extend and produces shared C1 KV and candidate information. - Layers 21-39 can process only the bounded replay tail. - Engram at layers 1 and 14 and source-layer projections add uneven costs. summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues. title: [Bug] SWA branching attaches a later Mamba checkpoint to an earlier prefix
summary: ## Background Branching-point caching saves the shared prefix where requests diverge so later requests can resume there. In a joint Full/SWA/Mamba cache, SWA selects a page-aligned boundary, while Mamba selects a checkpoint-grid-aligned boundary. Inkling uses the MAMBA component to cache short-convolution state. These targets are computed independently. The scheduler tracks Mamba's target, but insertion takes the minimum length requested by all components. KV can be sliced to that length; a checkpoint cannot be sliced into an earlier state. ## Example With page size 1 and checkpoint grid 64: 1. Existing checkpoints are at 64 and 128; a new request shares 96 tokens before diverging. Only checkpoint64 is reusable. 2. SWA proposes branch96. Mamba rounds 96 down to64, which is already cached, so it proposes no new branch. 3. Prefill continues to192 and saves state192. The scheduler does not use SWA's branch96 to choose this checkpoint. 4. Insertion takes `min(96, 192)` and attaches **state192 to key96**. A later request hits96 and resumes from the wrong state. PR #37584 propagated SWA branching into the Rust backend, exposing this mismatch in the shared insertion logic. The example does not require SWA eviction or HiCache. ## Observed impact Reproduced on H200 with the real `thinkingmachines/Inkling` test checkpoint, Rust TreeCore, Triton, page size 1, and Mamba `extra_buffer`, at PR head `bd087fc94fc5f8196a29b40f13f6386d1b79b89e`. title: [Fix] server: require POST for state-changing endpoints
summary: ## Motivation State-changing endpoints currently accept GET as well as POST. An attacker-controlled `image_url` or `video_url` can cause the server to make an HTTP GET to an administrative endpoint. If media fetching can reach that listener and the request passes its authentication checks, the operation can execute before the response is rejected as invalid image/video data. A decoding error does not undo the state change. Require POST for these operations so a URL-only media GET cannot invoke them. This closes the GET-triggered mutation path; destination restrictions and administrative authentication remain separate defenses. Existing clients using GET must switch to POST. title: [Fix] minimax-h3: preserve per-layer AdaLN parameters with Cache-DiT
summary: ## Motivation MiniMax H3 gathers AdaLN parameters for every layer, then indexes them while iterating `model.blocks`. Cache-DiT temporarily replaces that stack during forward with a wrapper that forwards the same kwargs to each original block. The outer loop now has one entry, so every block receives layer 0's modulation parameters. A full-compute Cache-DiT step can therefore differ from the uncached model before any cache reuse occurs. ## Modifications - Give each DiT block its original layer index. - Pass the complete per-step AdaLN tuple through the stack; each real block selects its own parameters. Keep explicit single-block `adaln_params` supported. - Keep the existing batched gather and cache lifecycle. No per-layer cache registration or mutable current-step cache state is introduced. - Add CPU/CUDA regressions for ordinary, shared-kwargs and real Cache-DiT stacks. Compare with an explicit per-layer reference across timestep-plan and width changes, verify actual wrapper execution, and guard the forward pass against host reads. ## Accuracy Tests Native Linux/CUDA validation on NVIDIA H20 (SM90), Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and Cache-DiT 1.5.1: **68 passed**. The seven dispatch cases include constructor coverage plus CPU/CUDA execution of all three stack forms. Every dispatch output matches the explicit per-layer reference exactly (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`). Real Cache-DiT calls execute `CachedBlocks_Pattern_3_4_5`; attention/MLP are deterministic small fixtures in that regression. title: [Fix] hicache: resolve prefetch trailing-window keys before the storage read
summary: ## Motivation With a trailing-window sidecar pool (SWA window, Mamba state) on independent host side pools, a per-rank storage read failure during a prefetch leaves the TP ranks with different storage beliefs, so they enqueue a different number of storage writes afterwards. The backup ack drains are MIN-counted and positional across ranks, so that difference never heals. ``` rank 0: KV read completes rank 1: KV read falls short alloc hit SWA keys = [placeholder x2] SWA keys = [placeholder x2] IO thread KV 2/2 -> _sync_trailing_keys KV 1/2 -> sidecar read skipped SWA keys = [h1, h2], SWA read ok SWA keys stay [placeholder x2] ack reduce agreed (MIN): KV short, swa hits 0 same agreed verdict discard invalidate_beyond([h1, h2], 0) invalidate_beyond([placeholder x2], 0) SWA window beliefs dropped no-op, beliefs kept next insert enqueues a SWA window write enqueues nothing ack drain ack_backup_queue = 1 ack_backup_queue = 0 -> MIN 0, never drained ``` Root cause: the PREFETCH-phase transfer of a trailing-window pool carries placeholder keys (`unified_cache/components/swa.py:1221`, `mamba.py:1142`). On the shared page-envelope host layout the real keys are filled at allocation, on the scheduler thread (`HybridCacheController.alloc_prefetch_host_buffers`). On independent side pools they are filled only by `_page_transfer_sidecar` on the prefetch IO thread, and only on a rank whose own KV read completed. title: [Fix] Gemma 4: skip quantization for ignored fused vision qkv/gate_up layers
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #43342. Loading `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors W4A16) fails during weight post-processing with `gptq_marlin_repack.cuh:311: size_n = 8608 is not divisible by tile_n_size = 64`. The Marlin shape is a symptom. The checkpoint's quantization `ignore` list excludes the vision tower, naming its clippable linears by their inner module, e.g. `model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.linear` and `...mlp.gate_proj.linear`, and stores those weights in bf16. The vision qkv_proj (N = 3456) passes the Marlin shape check, so it would run on uninitialized weights if only the gate_up crash were worked around. title: [Feat] dp-attention: Add prefix_affinity load balancing for routing-key/session affinity
summary: ## TL;DR `prefix_affinity` is an opt-in, routing-key-based affinity policy for single-instance DP attention. It targets multi-turn / agentic workloads where independent sessions share a large system/tools prefix but should not all be routed to the same DP rank. Compared with `round_robin`, it preserves per-session radix-cache locality; compared with first-N-token prefix hashing (#26612), it avoids collapsing all sessions whose distinguishing tokens appear after the shared prefix window. An overload guard lets affinity degrade to load-aware routing when the preferred rank becomes hot. --- ## Motivation Single-instance DP attention (`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size N`) currently offers only `round_robin`, `follow_bootstrap_room`, `total_requests`, and `total_tokens` — **none route by request content**, so under `round_robin` a repeated shared prefix only hits a rank's radix cache about once per `dp_size` requests. This is the known DPA cache-miss problem. The open proposal #26612 (`prefix_match`) addresses the *sequential* case by hashing the first ~4K tokens and routing `hash % dp_size`. This PR covers an adjacent failure mode: for workloads where the first hash window is dominated by a shared system/tools prompt (agentic / OpenCode / Claude-Code-style traffic), first-N-token hashing cannot distinguish sessions. In the worst case, independent sessions with identical leading tokens map to the same DP rank, creating a hotspot. This policy was motivated by our production-like GLM5.2 agentic workload, where many concurrent local-agent sessions share a large system/tools prefix.

title: [Perf] dflash: Side-stream context projection and a one-kernel verify commit
summary: ## Motivation Two independent, opt-in reductions of the DFLASH verify step's critical path: 1. The draft KV write projects the verify hidden states into the draft's context features (`project_target_hidden`), but the worker only reaches it after accept and sampling, which read the logits and not the hidden states. The projection can run concurrently with them. 2. The sampling selector's commit (rank 0's accept lengths and bonus tokens synced to every rank, then the committed block) runs as several small operations per step. ## Modifications - `--speculative-dflash-overlap-ctx-projection`: the projection is issued on a side CUDA stream once the verify step's logits gather is queued, so it runs concurrently with accept and sampling (issued earlier, its GEMM, which fills every SM, can delay the gather's collective on some ranks; see the profile below); the draft KV write joins the side stream and takes the result. The verify step reshapes the hidden states once and hands that tensor to the write; the write takes the side result only for that same tensor and projects any other inline, joining the side stream either way, so the side stream never outlives a buffer the next verify replay may overwrite. Same call on the same input, so the result is unchanged. A capture, an empty input or a failed projection leaves nothing pending and the inline call runs; a failure turns the overlap off for the rest of the run. Off by default: it saves at most ~0.2 % of a verify step, and at one request the difference is within run-to-run noise (see the overlap table below). - `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_EA

summary: ## Motivation run of MiniMax-H3 on MI355X (sglang v0.5.23) takes 118.2 s on 2 GPUs, 36% more GPU-seconds than on 1 GPU (B200: 6%). Two GPUs exchange over a single XGMI link (~57 GB/s), so Ulysses' all-to-all is large next to the layer: even with the head-group pipeline (#47567), the first group's input exchange and the last group's output exchange stay exposed, about 5 ms of a ~46 ms layer on main. Ring attention at degree 2 sends K/V once, overlaps the send with the local chunk's attention, and has no output exchange. `--ring-degree` refused aiter, though, and aiter is the fast exact backend on ROCm. ## Modifications - aiter returns the softmax LSE the ring merge needs: `forward(..., return_softmax_lse=True)` (dense, `[B, H, S]`) and `forward_ring_kv_chunk` (packed, `[H, Tq]`), and declares `supports_ring_rotation()`. The LSE is fp32 natural log (checked against an fp32 reference). - Server args and MiniMax-H3 (pipeline admission and the DiT's ring gate) accept aiter for ring. - `_ring_attention_varlen` takes its stacked K/V pair from the reusable staging buffers instead of allocating a pair per call. A fresh pair stays held for the P2P stream until the GPU reaches it, and with the host hundreds of layers ahead that is one ~1 GB pair per queued layer: H3 at ring 2 ran out of device memory within 4 denoise steps (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`, also reproduced in a standalone loop). This part is backend-independent and leaves the values unchanged. - Docs: the ring-capable backend list. ## Accuracy Tests - Unit (ROCm with aiter): two KV chunks merged with the ring merge

title: [Fix] [AMD] top-k: Avoid shared split workspace races
summary: ## Motivation The ROCm top-k v2 split path uses one persistent scratch workspace per device. Its histogram and counters are reset by the split kernels themselves, so concurrent launches on different streams race the same memory and can leave invalid top-k indices. CUDA/HIP graph capture adds another case: graphs captured on one stream bake the same workspace pointers into their kernel arguments, then may be replayed concurrently on different streams. ## Modifications - Bind the ROCm split workspace to the first eager stream that uses it. Other eager streams fall back to the existing one-block path. - Disable the split path while a stream is being captured, so a shared workspace address is not baked into a graph that can later replay elsewhere. - Add a fresh-process ROCm regression covering both ordinary two-stream execution and two graphs captured on one stream then replayed concurrently. ## Accuracy Tests - Before the fix, the synthetic two-stream fixture produced invalid rows within 3 rounds; the graph-replay fixture produced invalid rows within 3 rounds as well. - After the fix, both fixtures completed 100 rounds with all output indices in range and unique. - The added regression checks 20 ordinary concurrent rounds and 20 concurrent graph-replay rounds. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speedup is claimed. The split optimization remains enabled on its owner eager stream. Non-owner streams and graph capture use the existing correct one-block path. A valid pre-fix concurrent-graph performance comparison is unavailable because its outputs are corrupt. ## Checklist - [ ] Run

title: [Fix] lora: Skip unsupported embeddings when targeting all modules
summary: ## Motivation Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 fail to start with `--lora-target-modules all`: ```text AttributeError: 'Gemma3TextScaledWordEmbedding' object has no attribute 'org_vocab_size' ``` `all` unconditionally adds `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`, even when auto-detection excludes them. Gemma uses a scaled `nn.Embedding` that the embedding LoRA wrapper does not support. Since `lm_head` shares that embedding, adding it as a target triggers conversion to `ParallelLMHead`, which reads the missing `org_vocab_size` attribute. ## Modifications Only add both embedding targets when auto-detection finds a `VocabParallelEmbedding` or `ParallelLMHead`. Supported parallel embeddings keep the same targets, including a tied `lm_head`. For Gemma, `all` selects the supported projections and skips the tied-head conversion. The original embedding, its scaling, and the shared output weights remain in use. No embedding LoRA wrappers are installed; existing checks already skip their LoRA buffer allocation and updates. This fixes startup for projection-only adapters; it does not add Gemma embedding LoRA support. With `all`, an adapter that explicitly lists `embed_tokens` or `lm_head` is rejected by the existing target validation. Add two regression tests: a tied parallel embedding still gets both targets, and a tied plain `nn.Embedding` gets neither. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on current head `59f4e3b1cfcb0be10cae9d7d5ce1ca0d243d655f` on 2026-11-12 after merging upstream main `2f2f186e6fb0dd21981c44663e3ecdc7a110460e`.
