title: [Fix] moe: Make simulated expert routing work on in-kernel routers
summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_SIMULATE_UNIFORM_EXPERTS` and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ROUND_ROBIN_EXPERTS` replace MoE routing with balanced expert sets for benchmarking. They worked by rewriting materialized top-k ids, so routers that pick experts inside the MoE k ernel (bypassed top-k: FlashInfer TRT-LLM, FlashInfer MXFP4, gfx1250 W4A8) silently ignored them. Benchmarks of those backends with the flags set measured the model's real, skewed routing. MiMo-V2 disabled its bypass under simulation to work around this. Simulated sets also ignored `topk_group`, so grouped routers (DeepSeek-V3: 4 of 8 groups) were simulated with expert sets the real router can never produce. ## Modifications **Simulation on in-kernel routers** - On the bypass path, TopK now hands the kernel router logits that select exactly the simulated experts. Targets get `-ln(k-1)` and every other expert gets `-64`, with a zero correction bias. Softmax routers and renormalized sigmoid r outers then weight each target exactly 1/k. A plain sigmoid router weights it 1/k up to the logit's rounding (bf16, k=8: 0.12506). `select_experts` does not re-simulate encoded logits. - gfx1250 W4A8 routes from logits even with STANDARD top-k. It now encodes the already-simulated ids into its logits, so recorded and executed experts agree. - MiMo-V2 keeps its bypass under simulation. - The encode reuses the raw logits buffer when its rows are contiguous. **Grouped routers** - When `topk_group < n_group`, simulated sets stay within `topk_group` groups. - Round-robin numbers tokens per DP shard. Each shard therefore balances groups and EP ranks

title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Run the HIP sparse prefill on the FP8 KV cache
summary: ## Motivation On AMD MI355X GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash keeps part of its attention memory in a compact 8-bit form. Before each long prefill (reading the prompt), it turns those values back into 16-bit numbers and runs a 16-bit attention kernel. This PR lets prefill read the 8-bit values directly with a faster AITER kernel, which cuts the time to first token on long prompts by about 2%. It is off by default. On gfx950 with `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL=1`, `DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` dequantizes the selected SWA and compressed-history rows of the V4 FP8 cache record to BF16 and calls AITER's BF16 `pa_sparse_prefill_opus`. title: [Feat] rust: Add sglang-engine crate with typed config and process
summary: This PR tracks offline sglang.Engine support under the Rust server migration in RFC #23206 (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23206), item 18. The migration moves the offline Engine request front half to Rust, through request submission to the existing Python scheduler. Python continues to own scheduling, model loading and execution, GPU workers, kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, and quantization. This work does not port the scheduler or model runner to Rust. ## Motivation The Rust server already implements parts of SGLang’s request front half, but offline sglang.Engine is not supported with SGLANG_RUST_SERVER. The existing Python Engine remains responsible for its in-process API and request lifecycle. Offline support should reuse the Rust server’s request pipeline and established Rust/Python scheduler boundary. The API must preserve Python Engine behavior while leaving scheduler and GPU execution in Python. ## Runtime boundary Rust owns the offline request lifecycle through: - Engine-facing request conversion, validation, and preprocessing - Tokenization, detokenization, streaming, cancellation, and response conversion - Control request handoff, backpressure, tensor-buffer ownership, and error propagation - Startup, readiness, and lifecycle integration with the Rust request workers The Python scheduler and GPU worker continue to own scheduling and model execution. The Python sglang.Engine entry point may remain as a compatibility interface, delegating request handling to the Rust runtime. ## Migration phases | Phase | Status | Scope | |---|---|---

title: [Kernel] Coalesce the MiniCPM-SALA blockwise get_block_table stores
summary: ## Motivation `get_block_table` builds the per-token sparse block table for MiniCPM-SALA sparse attention. It has two strategies, selected in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/minicpm_sala/get_block_table.py`: the `blockwise` kernel for prefill and the `elementwise` kernel for decode, with blockwise as the automatic fallback whenever the elementwise layout does not apply (`block_size != 64` or `topk % 16 != 0`). The blockwise kernel in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/minicpm_sala/get_block_table.cuh` gave one thread a whole `out_block_table` row and wrote it with `kSparseBlockSize` scalar stores. Row `r` starts at element `r * kSparseBlockSize`, so with `block_size = 64` every thread writes 256 B and **adjacent threads are 256 B apart**: each warp store instruction touches 32 addresses spread over 8 KiB and consumes ~32 sectors to deliver 128 B of useful payload — roughly 8x the memory transactions. Because rows are also contiguous, `topk_idx` is read once per row; the whole cost of the kernel is that strided write. On sm_86 it reached only **15.6 GB/s** while the elementwise variant reached ~120 GB/s, a stable 7.4–7.8x gap across 512–16384 tokens. This is not a deliberately-tuned tradeoff being second-guessed. [#30360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30360) describes the split as *"Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes"*, but its checklist item `[ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results` was left unchecked and the PR text notes end-to-end accuracy "has not yet been recorded," so **the bloc

title: [Fix] scheduler: Make collective_rpc reliable with DP attention
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, multiple attention leaders connect DEALER sockets to the same Engine RPC endpoint. A request can reach a leader whose control list is discarded by the global TP broadcast, leaving the caller waiting indefinitely. When the source leader receives the request, multiple leaders can reply, leaving stale responses for later calls. The original handler also does not consistently report an error from a non-IO rank to the caller. Addresses #50073 for the default DP-attention control path. ## Modifications - Keep the RPC socket on the global TP source leader and reuse the existing control broadcast to deliver requests to all TP ranks, with one response per call. - Allow other leaders to receive tokenizer requests without an RPC socket, including when setting up the idle sleeper. - Agree on the RPC result across the TP CPU group before replying, so errors on non-IO ranks reach the caller. Broadcast error messages as UTF-8 bytes. - Reject `collective_rpc` before sending when DP attention uses local control broadcast, with instructions to use global control broadcast. That mode does not provide a shared TP receive point; synchronous RPC requires coordination with model collectives. This patch does not add per-iteration collectives or silently change the configuration. - Add seven registered CPU regression cases using real two-process Gloo and ZMQ, invoking the actual Scheduler RPC handler. title: [Feat] MLA: Enable combined PCP and DCP for DeepSeek dense MLA
summary: ## Motivation Enable prefill and decode context parallelism together for DeepSeek V2/V3 models using dense MLA. vLLM counts PCP as a separate rank dimension and accepts DCP sizes of 1, PCP, or TP × PCP at the configuration level. SGLang splits its configured TP ranks into PCP and attention TP, and this PR uses the PCP rank membership for DCP. The eight-GPU layout above therefore corresponds to vLLM TP=2, PCP=4, DCP=4. ## Modifications The initial configuration supports single-node eager execution with BF16 KV, one request per prefill batch, and `PCP = DCP > 1` and `TP % PCP == 0`. Prefill supports zigzag and interleave with FA3 on SM90 or FA4 on SM100. Decode uses FlashInfer MLA. ``` SGLang --tp-size 8, PCP = DCP = 4, attention TP = 2 Q head shard 0 Q head shard 1 Persistent KV positions CP/DCP rank 0 GPU 0 <--------> GPU 1 0, 4, 8, ... CP/DCP rank 1 GPU 2 <--------> GPU 3 1, 5, 9, ... CP/DCP rank 2 GPU 4 <--------> GPU 5 2, 6, 10, ... CP/DCP rank 3 GPU 6 <--------> GPU 7 3, 7, 11, ... Rows Attention TP reduction across head shards Columns PCP gathers KV for prefill. DCP merges decode attention via LSE. ``` Prefill builds a temporary KV view in sequence order while keeping the persistent cache sharded. With interleave, Q assignment uses the token’s offset within the current chunk, while KV ownership uses its position in the full sequence. For example, the first token of a chunk starting at position 127 runs its prefill Q on CP rank 0, sees 128 KV entries, and stores its KV on DCP rank 3. title: [Fix] flashinfer-mla: Keep CUDA graph kv_indptr current

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/convrot: Fuse INT8 projection and rounded SwiGLU on SM120
summary: ## Motivation ConvRot INT8 MLPs currently materialize both BF16 projection halves before a separate rounded SwiGLU. On an RTX 5090 D v2, the H3-sized operation at 16,384 rows takes 11.16 ms and peaks at 1,344 MiB of temporary allocations. This change writes the activated output directly: 9.28 ms and 532 MiB, preserving the existing rotation, INT8 values, scale order and BF16 rounding points. ## Modifications - Add a compound `convrot_int8_swiglu` operator for the existing `[gate | up]` weight layout. summary: On MI355X (gfx950), each full-attention layer in decode ran three small kernels before the attention kernel (`vattn_asm`). title: [Feat] mem_cache: Evict Mamba states by GreedyDual-Size (--radix-eviction-policy gds)
summary: ## Motivation On a hybrid model (KDA / GDN / Mamba layers next to attention), a cached prefix can only be resumed at a node that still holds a recurrent state. The state pool is much smaller than the KV pool: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2x B200 (TP2, default pools) gets 419 state slots next to 2,969,600 KV tokens, and each running request takes 5 of the slots. The Mamba LRU drops one state at a time and keeps its KV, so on agent traffic a session that comes back after a tool call often finds its latest state gone while its KV is still there. It falls back to an older state, or to token 0, and prefills again tokens that were never evicted (#36935 described the same thing). This adds `--radix-eviction-policy gds`, GreedyDual-Size over recurrent states, following FlashState ([paper](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate), [project](https://flashstate.ai), [code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashState)). A state's priority is the eviction watermark at its last use plus the prefill it would take to rebuild it from the nearest shallower state (or from token 0). The lowest goes first and the watermark rises to each victim's priority, so a state nobody resumes still ages out. A state right under another one is cheap to rebuild and goes early; the only state of a long session is expensive and stays. `gds` is the default on the hybrid models SGLang lists for the Mamba radix cache (such as Qwen3-Next and GLM-5.3-Flash) when `--radix-eviction-policy` is not given, except with `--enable-session-radix-cache`. title: [Fix] hicache: Register the whole host-pool allocation with Mooncake
summary: ## Motivation Host pools hand out views of a single allocation: MHAHostKVCache exposes k_buffer/v_buffer as kv_buffer[0]/kv_buffer[1], two halves of one mmap. Registration was sized to each view, so the interior view started at a non-hugepage-aligned offset and the first view ended at a length that is not a hugepage multiple. title: [Perf] [AMD] muse-spark: Optimize prefill performance
summary: ## Motivation The Muse Spark extend kernel `_muse_extend_kernel` is VALU-bound. On MI355X the softmax arithmetic sets the pace of each 128-key tile, not the MFMAs and not memory. A sizable part of the remaining VALU work in the hot loop was address math that is the same for every tile, or could be folded at compile time. This PR removes that work. The kernel gets about 9% faster, and Muse Spark prefill TTFT drops by 1.5% to 7.1% at 32K to 256K prompt tokens. ## Modifications All changes are in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/muse_extend_gluon.py`. Tiling, softmax and numerics are unchanged. - **Constexpr KV strides.** The six K and V cache strides are now `gl.constexpr`, so the compiler folds them into the address math. - **Hoisted per-lane KV pointers.** Each lane's offset for KV head, row within the page and head dim is computed once before the loop. A tile only adds `page * stride`, kept in 64 bits because one layer's KV pool can exceed 2 GiB. - **Scalar block-table base.** Tile `j` reads its block-table row with `buffer_load` from the scalar base `bt + j * TILE // PAGE`, so the lane offsets `kr // PAGE` and `vr // PAGE` are loop-invariant. Masks apply only to tiles that can cross the sequence end or the first key of the sliding window. - **Prefetch bound.** The unmasked loop prefetches page ids two tiles ahead without a mask, so it now stops at `interior - 2`. Every unmasked block-table read stays inside the sequence's own entries. Sliding-window layers and page sizes 16 to 128 keep their current behavior. title: [Fix] bench_warm_cache: Count streamed output tokens from meta_info.completion_tokens
summary: ## Motivation `benchmark/hicache/bench_warm_cache.py` can silently under-report **output token throughput** under high concurrency / long streaming requests: some requests finish with HTTP 200 but are recorded as `success` with `output_len == 0`, so `Total generated tokens` ends up an exact multiple of `output_len` short of `completed * output_len` and `output_throughput` is deflated — even though the server actually generated the tokens (engine `gen throughput` logs confirm generation). This is a **benchmark-only** measurement bug; no serving/runtime code is involved. Root cause in `async_request_sglang_generate`: 1. The token count is only updated inside `if "text" in data and data["text"]:`. A request whose chunks never hit that branch (chunk-boundary / cumulative-text handling under load) keeps `output_len == 0` and never reads `meta_info.completion_tokens`. 2. Any HTTP 200 is marked `output.success = True` regardless of whether tokens were received, so 0-token streams are silently counted into the denominator. title: [Fix] scheduler: Answer release_memory_occupation only after every pipeline stage released
summary: ## Motivation Under pipeline parallelism a stage handles a control request before relaying it to the next stage, so the first stage answered `release_memory_occupation` while later stages still held GPU memory. A trainer sharing the GPUs could start allocating too early and OOM. Separately, a rank that was not idle returned from the release handler on its own, while its idle TP peers went on to the group barrier and waited forever. ## Modifications - Each stage folds its release verdict into the earlier stages' and passes it on; a refusal from any stage wins. The verdict sends are waited together with the request relay, since the next stage receives a verdict only after it has the requests. - A first stage that released waits at the end of its iteration for the last stage's reply, then answers the caller. It is idle at that point, with no microbatch in flight. - A first stage that refuses answers at once, and the last stage sends no reply. Later stages need the first stage's next iterations to reach the request, so waiting while busy would freeze the pipeline. - The verdict travels on its own tag, so `point_to_point_pyobj` takes a `tag`. - The idle check is reduced over the TP group before anything is released, so the ranks refuse or release together. A barrier at the end of the handler keeps the verdict from leaving before every TP peer has released. ## Tests Qwen2.5-0.5B with `--enable-memory-saver`, H100: | Layout | Idle release | Concurrent releases while generations run | |---|---|---| | 2 nodes, pp=2, tp=1 | 200 in 57 ms, both nodes released | 3 x 400 in under 10 ms,

summary: ## Motivation `--enable-return-routed-experts` captures each MoE layer's top-k expert ids per token so an RL trainer can replay the rollout's routing. With `--pp-size > 1`, each stage captures only its own layers, and only the first stage keeps a host cache and answers requests. Responses therefore carry the first stage's layers and zeros for every later stage: on `Qwen3-30B-A3B` with `--pp-size 2`, layers 24 to 47 come back all zero, 49.6% of all ids. Each stage merges its own layer columns into the rows it received and sends them on with the hidden states. The TP worker pops them before the forward, so the model and its CUDA graphs never see the key. - The last stage adds the full rows to the output message it already sends back. The first stage writes them into its host cache at the KV slots it recorded at launch and drops the key before forwarding the output on. - Middle prefill chunks keep their output message while capture is on, or their tokens would silently return zeros. Capture is refused with `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC`, whose spec branch does not carry the rows. On T-HEAD SAIL (PPU) three things differ: 1. **Layout.** SAIL's DeepGEMM wants an explicitly padded per-expert `M` (`compute_aligned_M`), rather than the `m_indices`-derived layout the CUDA runner builds. 2. **Entry points.** The SAIL build exposes `*_nopad` grouped GEMMs (`m_grouped_*_gemm_nt_nopad`) instead of the CUDA names. 3. **Quantisation + epilogue.** Activations are quantised in a different order, and the SwiGLU `swiglu_limit` clamp is fused separately (`_swiglu_silu_clamp_mul`). title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/nomas: Fuse VAE QK normalization and MRoPE epilogue
summary: ## Motivation The Nomas PixelUMM VAE computes Q/K mean squares with ATen and then runs three compiled pointwise kernels for normalization and three-axis rotary embedding. Those three kernels are repeated 864 times in the profiled 1280×704×121 decode. This change fuses the pointwise epilogue into one Triton kernel while retaining the ATen reductions, existing chunking and output-copy behavior. It preserves the actual Parameter-backed compiled reference's FP32 multiply/FMA rounding. A per-signature `BitExactFusionGate` verifies the result before retaining the fast path. The existing head-64, autograd/compiler and unsupported-layout paths remain available. The fusion is eligible for BF16 head-128 inputs with rotary sections `(64,32,32)` on SM100+; model performance below is measured on SM103 only. This is independent of [#49308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49308), which changes the DiT mean-square reduction. This branch starts directly from the frozen main and contains no DiT change or new configuration flag. - Main baseline: `5325cfabd757819e2e01bb7eb3b28c5b39b8cec9`. - PR head: `aef7b894a610f6c04fe43d00ea9decca2ab1f718`. - Native vLLM-Omni reference: `725c1c9acd108d9f5248bd937489f19a2c560205`. ## Accuracy and cleanup The exact committed head passes 14 focused operator cases and one model-wrapper test against the actual Parameter-backed compiled reference. The cases cover chunk views with storage offsets and batch gaps, extreme amplitudes, changed inputs during CUDA Graph replay, invalid mean shapes, activation on the real head-128 wrapper and head-64 fallback.

title: [Perf] diffusion/ming: Fuse lossless RMSNorm scale and residual epilogues
summary: ## Motivation Ming's unquantized DiT already uses ordered RMSNorm, but still launches BF16 scale and residual operations after it. This fuses those epilogues into the existing ordered kernel, removing 2,304 pointwise launches per 12-step request while preserving the original intermediate rounding. ## Modifications - Extend the shared ordered kernel with optional scale/residual operands. Preserve FP32 statistics, the cast before learned-weight multiplication, the cast before scaling, and the cast before residual addition. `tanh` remains native. - Add Ming-specific block hooks while keeping Z-Image's default helpers. Eligible CUDA BF16 width-3840 inputs use the existing per-signature bit-exact gate; unsupported layouts, small reductions, quantized blocks and compilation retain their existing expressions. - Reuse the existing kernel during cleanup, add changed-input CUDA graph and actual Dynamo tracing regression coverage, and document the bounded B300 validation scope. No new user flags. ## Accuracy Tests Frozen main: `5325cfabd757819e2e01bb7eb3b28c5b39b8cec9` Final head: `f4f735368259481a04a955e8d6b6699bd849b3fc` Checkpoint: `inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design@c57c49689d12ef7d4e24a170014f1dc43d3ce258`. On the same physical B300, 48 Ming tests and six shared RMSNorm regressions pass. The six epilogue cases cover odd lengths, batch two, strided scale views, changed inputs and CUDA graph replay against the independent native RMSNorm expression. The compile fallback uses `torch.compile(backend="eager", fullgraph=True)` to exercise real Dynamo tracing; this is not an Inductor perf

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] mhc: allow the SM120 decode band on the compensated bf16x3 projection
summary: ## Motivation On sm_120 the hyper-connection mix still runs the split-K partial kernel for 32..256 decode rows, even though `deepseek_v4.py` already builds the bf16 weight triple for SM120 at load time (the pure-Triton branch, `tf32_parts` stays `None`) and `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_bf16x3` takes an M-independent decode grid. #48456 opens that grid for `is_sm100` only, so SM120 is the one Blackwell family that pays for the triple and never uses it below 4096 rows. This is a two-line gate change in `_mix_stats_impl`; nothing new is added to the kernels. ## Measurements 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB (sm_120), PCIe only, single stream. Operators at the checkpoint geometry (`hc_attn_fn` (24, 20480), `hc_mult` 4, hidden 5120, 20 Sinkhorn iterations). CUDA graph with 20 launches captured, median of 7 replays; both arms were built by rewriting only the launcher arguments on the same Triton kernels, so the kernel bodies are byte-identical across arms. µs: | rows | partial path (today on SM120) | bf16x3 decode grid | grid / partial | |------|-------------------------------|--------------------|----------------| | 32 | 11.95 | 9.50 | 0.795 | | 64 | 12.56 | 9.91 | 0.789 | | 128 | 18.92 | 12.76 | 0.675 | | 192 | 25.01 | 12.73 | 0.509 | | 256 | 27.33 | 15.75 | 0.576 | Three independent repeats of each cell moved the ratio by at most 0.003, and the two arms' `pre` / `post` / `comb` differ by 3e-07..9e-07 relative — the same order #45264 reported for its own block-K change. `hc_mix` runs 80 times per forward step (attn and ffn in 40 layers), so at 128 rows the saving is 6.2us x 80 ≈ 0.5ms of GPU time

title: [Fix] deterministic: Size the MQA-logits chunks without free memory
summary: ## Motivation The sparse-attention indexers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4) split their MQA-logits matrix into row chunks, and `mqa_logits_budget_bytes` sizes the chunks from the free GPU memory at that moment. Free memory changes from run to run, so the chunking does too, and the logits kernel's result for a row depends on the chunk size. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the same prompt can then give different tokens from run to run when the server is short of free memory: GLM-5.3-Flash at TP2 with `--mem-fraction-static 0.9` did, with a 32k-token prompt sent twice on its own. This PR sizes the chunks from the static budget alone in deterministic mode, as already happens under CUDA graph capture. Nothing changes with deterministic inference off. If free memory is below the static budget, the allocation can now fail with an out-of-memory error instead of silently changing the results; lowering `--mem-fraction-static` fixes that. **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it fixes the DSA k-pool indexer independently of GLM-5.3. GLM-5.3 needs it, together with the rest of the group; the final PR, #50078, lets GLM-5.3 start in deterministic mode once everything is in. ## Modifications - `mqa_logits_utils.mqa_logits_budget_bytes`: with deterministic inference enabled, the budget is the static one and `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` is not called. The ROCm 2 GiB ceiling still applies. - `test_dsa_mqa_logits_chunking.py`: two CPU tests. Outside deterministic inferenc

title: [Fix] deterministic: Put DSA k-pool prefill chunk ends on the chunked-prefill grid
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, a long prompt's prefill on a DSA k-pool model (GLM-5.3) depends on where the prompt is split into chunks, and batchmates move the split: chunk ends are aligned only to the k-pool size (4 tokens on GLM-5.3), so a 32k-token prompt alone and the same prompt next to other requests are cut at different positions. On MI350X, GLM-5.3 gave the same long prompt different results with different batchmates (long-context check 2 / 6 identical, chunk-boundary check 4 / 8). Aligning to 64 or 2,048 tokens did not help: any change of the split points changes the result. **Impact** - GLM-5.3 (DSA k-pool models) in deterministic mode: a prompt is always split at the same positions, so long prompts give the same result whatever their batchmates. - Only deterministic inference on DSA k-pool models changes, through the existing truncation alignment; no measurable speed cost. - GLM-5.3's `dsa` attention backend is not yet allowed in deterministic mode; #50078 allows it. The results below were taken with the whole group applied. **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it applies to every DSA k-pool model. GLM-5.3 needs it together with the rest of the group; #50078 lets GLM-5.3 start in deterministic mode once everything is in. ## Modifications - `managers/scheduler.py`, `init_dsa_kpool_truncation_align`: in deterministic inference, the truncation alignment becomes the largest multiple of the k-pool alignment that fits the chunked-pr

title: [Fix] deterministic: Deterministic k-pool top-k for the DSA indexer
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3 (DSA with a k-pool indexer) picks the keys each query attends to with a top-k over pooled indexer logits. The fused radix-select kernels behind `topk_from_pooled_history_logits` resolve ties at the selection threshold, and write the selected groups, in `atomicAdd` order. So the same logits can select a different set of keys, in a different order, from run to run, and the sparse attention after it sums in that order. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, GLM-5.3 gave different results for the same 16k-token prompt on two fresh servers: a hash trace put the first difference with equal inputs at this top-k (layer 3), and with only the order fixed the set still differed at a later layer. **Impact** - GLM-5.3 (and other DSA k-pool models) in deterministic mode: the indexer selects the same keys in the same order every time, whatever rows share the call. - Only deterministic inference changes; the fused kernels stay the default. Platform-independent (the change is in Python / PyTorch). - GLM-5.3's `dsa` attention backend is not yet allowed in deterministic mode; #50078 allows it. The results below were taken with the whole group applied. **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it applies to every DSA k-pool model. GLM-5.3 needs it together with the rest of the group; #50078 lets GLM-5.3 start in deterministic mode once everything is in. ## Modifications - `dsa/kpool_fp8_index.py`: in deterministic inference, `topk_from_pooled_history_logits` sele

title: [Fix] [AMD] deterministic: Batch-invariant mHC pre for GLM-5.3 on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3 (and other models with manifold hyper-connections, such as DeepSeek-V4) run "mHC pre" before every attention and MoE block: a per-token RMS over the residual streams, a small GEMM against the mixing weights, Sinkhorn normalisation, and a weighted sum of the streams that becomes the layer input. On ROCm this runs through AITER's `mhc_pre`, which chooses its split-K from the number of tokens in the call. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, a token's layer input therefore changes with its batchmates: on MI350X at GLM-5.3's shape, the rows of every sub-batch call (1 to 2,048 rows) differ from the same rows inside a 4,096-row call, so no deterministic check can pass. The only batch-invariant alternative today is the Torch fallback, which makes deterministic GLM-5.3 unusable: 0.07x of normal-mode throughput at TP4 and 0.13x at TP1 (1k/1k). **Impact** - GLM-5.3 in deterministic mode on gfx950: the mHC layers become batch-invariant at 0.58-0.82x of normal-mode throughput instead of 0.07-0.19x (numbers below). - Only deterministic mode on ROCm changes. Normal mode, other platforms, and models without hyper-connections are unchanged. - GLM-5.3's `dsa` attention backend is not yet allowed in deterministic mode; #50078 allows it. The results below were taken with the whole group applied. **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it also applies to DeepSeek-V4's hyper-connections. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Bound unsharded PD prefill prompts at bootstrap
summary: ## Motivation `max_bootstrap_input_len` returns the raw pool capacity for an unsharded pool, so the P/D bootstrap door lets through any prompt up to `max_total_num_tokens`. `PrefillAdder` prices a fresh request at the prompt plus one handoff token plus one alignment page, and on the stricter `add_one_req_ignore_eos` path (`ignore_eos` with the radix cache disabled, the usual `bench_serving` setup) it also page-rounds the prompt. A prompt within one or two pages of capacity therefore passes the door, is never admitted on an empty pool, and sits `NO_TOKEN` at the head of the waiting queue forever. Nothing downstream drops it, so one such request wedges the prefill worker until the client or router gives up. This predates #46548. The base memory clamp in `init_req_max_new_tokens` returns `max(0, ...)` and never `None`, so the intake abort did not fire for these prompts either; the prefill path then forced the `0` to `1` and the request wedged the same way. Sharded pools (`kv_shard_widening > 1`) already use the strictest-path bound at the door and do not have this problem. ## Modifications - `max_bootstrap_input_len` applies the sharded bound to unsharded pools too: page-rounded prompt, one page per shard, one new token and one spare token must stay below capacity. A longer prompt is rejected at bootstrap with the existing 400 (`exceeds the maximum number of tokens`) and retired through `retire_unadmitted`, the same path sharded pools use. - The scheduler is untouched; PD prefill still budgets the single handoff token before any `match_prefix`, so PP ranks keep deriving identi

title: [CI] ppu: run the nightly test on the image the same night builds
summary: `nightly-test-ppu.yml` carried its own `0 16 * * *` schedule. It started at the same moment as `release-docker-ppu-nightly.yml`, knew nothing about whether the build succeeded, and tested a hardcoded base image plus a fresh `pip install -e` of whatever commit it happened to check out. So the image the nightly builds was never the thing under test. A broken image could pass every case; a good image could fail because the source install had drifted from it. Two independent crons racing on the same clock also meant "which image was actually tested" had no answer after the fact. ## Modifications - **Trigger** — the `schedule` is removed; the workflow now runs on `workflow_run` of `Release Docker Images Nightly (PPU)` (`types: [completed]`). `prepare` only lets through a successful, *scheduled* build on the default branch, so failed builds and the `push=false` debug dispatch cannot start a test line that has nothing to pull. `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` keep working and gain a `test_image` input. - **Image under test** — derived once in `prepare` from the build run's `head_sha` / `head_branch` / `created_at`, using the immutable tag the build already pushed: `<branch>-<UTC date>-cuda13.0.0-sdk2.2.0-<sha7>`. The `:nightly` rolling tag is deliberately not used, so a later build or a re-run cannot change what a given test run measured. - **Modes** — `test_image` non-empty means the pods run on that image; empty means the previous behaviour (fixed base image + source install), so manual debugging is unchanged. - **`PPU_TEST_MODE`** (new, defaults to `source`) — `image` skip

title: [Perf] model_overrides: Default GLM-5.3-Flash to an agentic Mamba pool split
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash splits post-weight memory into a KDA state pool and a KV pool at `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` 0.9 by default. Under agentic multi-turn traffic this leaves the KV pool below the sessions' working set: every session is evicted before its next turn and the prefix-cache hit rate collapses (0.056 below). title: [RFC] Kimi K3 decode: FlashInfer reuse and integration scope
summary: ## Motivation Kimi K3 serving mixes long prefills and cache restoration with repeated decode steps. For single-node B300/SM103, TP8, no-speculation serving, we want to reduce decode latency while preserving KV capacity, recurrent-state ownership, HiCache behavior and public API contracts. An existing candidate brings an opt-in, prepared 93-layer executor with DCP1/DCP8 profiles into SGLang. Before asking maintainers to carry that model-specific implementation, this RFC asks **what is the smallest useful integration to maintain now that FlashInfer supplies a reusable primitive?** The candidate and broader serving context are recorded in [#48510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48510) and [#48626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48626). I suggest qualifying primitive reuse in an existing SGLang consumer first, and landing lifecycle/correctness changes separately where they fix an existing affected path. The full executor would remain a candidate until matched whole-model results and an ownership/CI plan justify it. The proposed integration would be opt-in and use existing engine interfaces. ## Existing FlashInfer work The starting point is yyihuang's merged MLA value-projection and gate primitive, request-length load update, and automatic program selection. yyihuang also authored the initial SGLang adapter incorporated into #48510. The reuse discussion was closed with the `completed` state. The original `MlaValue` implementation is Lee Nau's work, and its source notices remain in the candidate. title: [Fix] batch_invariant_ops: Cap the mean kernel's grid so large outputs launch on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, `torch.mean` runs through `batch_invariant_ops.mean_dim`, which launches one Triton program per output element. ROCm limits a launch to 2^32 threads, so any mean with more than about 16.7M outputs fails with `Triton Error [HIP]: invalid argument`. Models with hyper-connections (GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4) hit this on long prompts: they average the residual over 4 streams, which gives `tokens x hidden` outputs. An 8k-token prefill with hidden size 4096 (33.5M outputs) crashes the server. This PR caps the grid at 2^20 programs and lets each program handle several outputs. Results are bit-identical, and nothing changes for outputs up to 2^20 elements. Only deterministic mode uses this kernel; the failure itself is ROCm-only. **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it fixes any batch-invariant mean above 2^24 outputs (e.g. DeepSeek-V4) independently of GLM-5.3. GLM-5.3 needs it, together with the rest of the group; the final PR, #50078, lets GLM-5.3 start in deterministic mode once everything is in. ## Modifications - `batch_invariant_ops.py`: `mean_dim` launches `min(M * K, 2**20)` programs, and `mean_kernel` loops over its outputs with the unchanged per-element reduction. - `test_batch_invariant_ops.py`: new `TestMeanDim`. A `[8192, 4, 4096]` bf16 mean over dim -2 runs and matches `torch.mean`, and sub-batches of 1 / 7 / 300 / 4,096 rows are bitwise equal to the same rows of the full result. ## Accuracy Tests 1x MI350X,

title: [Fix] deterministic: Batch-invariant Kimi Delta Attention
summary: ## Motivation Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) is the linear attention of Kimi-Linear, Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3's linear-attention layers. It is not deterministic with `--enable-deterministic-inference`: on MI350X, Kimi-Linear gave 2-7 different outputs for 50 identical requests, up to 9 per prompt in the prefix test, and bitwise-identical logprobs in only 10 of 1,275 responses. KDA gives a request different results depending on its batch in four places: - `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` switches to a row-streaming kernel from 8 requests up, which rounds differently from the Triton kernel; - `chunk_kda_fwd` fuses the diagonal blocks and the recompute when the batch's total chunk grid is small (`B * NT * H <= 256`): a 59-token sequence alone takes the fused path and inside a batch the unfused one, and the two round differently; - chunked prefill can split a request off the 64-token chunk grid that `chunk_kda` counts from the sequence start; - on gfx950, KDA prefill first tries a HIP kernel when the gate has a lower bound of -5 and beta is raw (GLM-5.3, Kimi K3). Its launch layout follows the batch's longest sequence, so from about 1,280 tokens on a sequence's rows and final state depend on its batchmates (at GLM-5.3's shape, a 2,606-token sequence differs from row 1,792 on). Kimi-Linear has no gate lower bound and never uses that kernel. **Impact** - Kimi-Linear (and Kimi K3, which runs the same kernels) becomes deterministic; GLM-5.3's linear-attention layers become batch-invariant, one of the changes GLM-5.3 needs in deterministic mode. - Only batch-invariant / deterministic mode

title: [Fix] [AMD] deterministic: Run block-FP8 linears through Triton on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-deterministic-inference` on ROCm, block-scale FP8 checkpoints (Qwen3-FP8, Qwen3.8-FP8, DeepSeek FP8) are not deterministic: `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` runs their linears through AITER, which picks kernels and split-K settings by the number of tokens, so a request's result depends on its batch. On MI350X, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 in deterministic mode gives 2 different outputs for 50 identical requests, up to 6 outputs per prompt in the prefix test, and identical logprobs in only 289 of 1,275 responses; Qwen3-8B-FP8 up to 5 per prompt. SGLang's Triton block-FP8 GEMM uses one tile configuration per weight shape and no split-K, so its result for a row does not depend on the other rows. This PR selects it in deterministic mode on ROCm when the backend is `auto`, the same way deterministic mode already resolves other batch-dependent backends. **Which models this affects.** Every block-scale FP8 checkpoint served on ROCm in deterministic mode: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, Qwen3-8B-FP8 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (tested below), and the DeepSeek FP8 family's dense linears. FP8 MoE experts need the companion change (`rocm-deterministic-fp8-moe-triton`). **Part of #50083 (deterministic inference for GLM-5.3 on MI350X).** This PR does not depend on any other PR in the group and can be merged on its own; it fixes every block-FP8 checkpoint independently of GLM-5.3. GLM-5.3 needs it, together with the rest of the group; the final PR, #50078, lets GLM-5.3 start in deterministic mode once everything is in. ## Modifications - `arg_groups/overrides.py`: new post-process pass `_determinist

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dflash: Batch native context KV writes across draft layers
summary: ## Motivation DFlash already projects and normalizes context K/V across its draft layers, but the generic materializer still calls the pool writer once per layer. The post-verify prefix commit therefore launches one scatter kernel per layer. This change batches those native cache writes into one launch without changing the projection, RMSNorm, or RoPE numerics. Duplicate-work check: #48948 overlaps projection with verify and fuses the acceptance commit; it preserves the layer-wise context KV writes. #47982 introduces checkpoints trained with shared context KV. Neither implements this native cross-layer scatter. DSpark already has a fused norm/RoPE/store path, with a different rounding contract; that path stays intact. ## Modifications - Add a CUDA Triton scatter for native FP16/BF16 stacked K/V. It accepts per-layer physical locations, padded source-layer/cache-row strides, and GPU prefix commit lengths; all address arithmetic uses 64-bit offsets. - Bind the real routed cache buffers after allocation and refresh them whenever the draft pool is rebuilt. Full and sliding-window sub-pools resolve their own locations through the existing router. - Use the stacked writer through the existing DFlash/DFlash2 helper. Quantized, HND, MLA, unsupported layouts/devices, and async-assert instrumentation keep the existing writer. DSpark remains on its existing fused path. - Add kernel regression coverage, pool lifecycle/routing coverage, and a registered benchmark comparing the exact existing ordinary/prefix writers. title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: split large-K bf16 linears on gfx1151
summary: ## Motivation On gfx1151 (Strix Halo / RDNA 3.5) rocBLAS picks a much slower kernel as K grows. The Qwen-Image 2.1 MLP down-projection `[4096, 12288] x [12288, 4096]` (`bf16`, bs=1, 1024x1024) measures **16.3 TFLOP/s**, while the same FLOPs at `K=4096` reach **23.6** and a 3072-wide `K` reaches **29.7 TFLOP/s**. That projection runs in all 32 MLP blocks of every denoising forward, and a torch-profiler capture of the model attributes 72% of denoising GPU time to GEMMs, so the shape gap is directly on the critical path. Splitting `K` into four chunks and accumulating them keeps every GEMM inside the fast K regime: **22.6 TFLOP/s** on the same shape (1.39x). ## Modifications - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/linear.py`: add a K-split path to `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply`, next to the existing platform/shape dispatches (`_use_flydsl_linear` for gfx1250, `_USE_AITER_TGEMM`). Placing it in the quant method means every `RowParallelLinear` / `ColumnParallelLinear` on gfx1151 is covered, with no per-model call-site changes. - The `K/N` chunk copies are built once per layer and cached against `weight.data_ptr()`, so weight load, `.to()` and layerwise offload rebuild them instead of using a stale copy. An in-place copy into the same storage (the post-training weight sync) is the one thing the key cannot observe, so `splitk_linear_chunks` documents the `layer._splitk_chunks` reset it needs. - Eligibility is deliberately narrow: `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_SPLITK_GEMM > 1`, `current_platform.is_gfx1151()`, bf16 x bf16, no bias, 2D weight (the 1D placeholder left by offload falls bac

title: [Fix] deterministic: Run the MoE routing functions eagerly in batch-invariant mode
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode, a token's routed experts must not depend on the server start or on the other tokens in the batch. The routing functions in `layers/moe/topk.py` are wrapped in `torch.compile`. Inductor tunes the generated kernels (block sizes, reduction splits) by timing them on first use, so the summation order of the routing scores can differ between server starts and batch shapes. With it, the selected experts can differ too. On MI350X this made DeepSeek-V2-Lite pass the deterministic checks on some server starts and fail on others (see below). This PR runs these routing functions eagerly in batch-invariant mode and keeps them compiled in normal mode. **Scope.** The change applies on every platform, to models whose routing reaches these Python functions: - DeepSeek-V2-style softmax grouped top-k (`grouped_topk_gpu`), for example DeepSeek-V2 / V2-Lite; - Kimi K2-style biased top-k (`kimi_k2_biased_topk_impl`, `biased_topk_impl`); - DeepSeek-V3-style sigmoid + correction-bias grouped top-k (`biased_grouped_topk_impl`, used for example by DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K3 and GLM-4.5), when no fused routing kernel takes over. Where a fused kernel runs instead, this PR does not change anything. Examples: - `fused_topk_deepseek` and `moe_fused_gate` on CUDA; - AITER's routing kernel on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, which is the case for DeepSeek-V3-style routing on MI300/MI350. DeepSeek-V4 cannot run in deterministic mode yet (its attention backend is refused), so it is not covered here. The failure was reproduced and the fix validated end to end on DeepSeek-V2-Li

title: [Feat] [NPU] attention: support FP8 KV with DSA context parallelism
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.2 on Ascend 950 can store DSA KV in packed FP8. The prefill context parallel and decode context parallel attention branches need readers for that layout. ## Modifications - Reuse the quantized Lightning Indexer for DSA prefill CP with FP8 KV. Each rank uses its local queries and block-table rows to index the full paged K cache with Q and K scales. The existing packed FP8 QSFA consumes those Top-K indices. - Use the A5 packed FP8 KV sparse attention kernel from sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#1007 for DSA DCP. Prefill, decode and NEXTN target verify keep their rank-local page tables and actual KV lengths. The kernel derives each query's selected-key count and returns max/sum for the existing LSE merge. - Use the packed kernel output for empty local Top-K rows. title: [Fix] hisparse: Admit decode prompts against the logical pool
summary: **[Fix] hisparse: Admit decode prompts against the logical pool** Let a HiSparse PD decode engine accept prompts longer than its device KV rows, up to the host-backed logical pool. ## Motivation A HiSparse decode engine has two pools: - **Logical pool:** `size × host_to_device_ratio` rows. It holds every request's full KV in host memory, and index-K is sized to match. - **Device pool:** only `size` rows. These rows hold each request's hot buffer (`device_buffer_size` + 64 per request), not the full prompt. On a PD decode engine, prompt KV arrives over RDMA into the logical pool (`alloc_logical_only`), and decode swaps the top-k rows into the hot buffer. The decode engine never needs a device row for each prompt token. Admission still checks the prompt against the device pool: - `TpModelWorker.get_worker_info` takes `kv_capacity` from `effective_logical_max_total_num_tokens`. Under HiSparse that value is the device row count, so `max_req_input_len` is the device row count, and `validate_input_length` rejects any longer prompt. - `max_new_tokens_for_memory` gets the same device row count as `token_capacity`. A prompt that got past the length check would have its output clipped to 0. #28753 added ModelRunner.max_token_pool_size and applied it to the decode prealloc check, but the front-door limit in get_worker_info and the output budget in max_new_tokens_for_memory still use device rows. This PR applies the same logical capacity to both. On GLM-5.2 with r=16, the decode engine has 147,136 device rows and a 2,354,176-row logical pool. A 256K prompt is rejected with `Input lengt

title: [Fix] qsa: Prefill predicates (correctness claim withdrawn)
summary: ## Draft for maintainer review; correctness claim remains withdrawn ### Status A maintainer reopened this PR on 2026-09-15. The current head includes a merge of `qwen4-main-squashed`; its kernel predicates and tests still do not demonstrate an observable correctness or performance benefit. ### Reassessment of the original claims Rechecking the indexing and public consumer invalidated both the original illegal-memory-access explanation and the later cross-row-contamination explanation. Extra stores remain within their own query row, and the public wrapper masks out-of-window values before returning. The end-to-end tests also passed before this patch; raw pre-mask tests distinguish internal stores, not a public-output defect. ### Related work and historical evidence No fix for #37633 is claimed. Separately, merged #38346 bounds the compression gather for forwards with only 1–3 source rows; it is a different code path. Historical verification on the original H20 deployment was later reported in [the September 16 update](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37638#issuecomment-5695024174), but that evidence supports the independent gather fix, not the predicates proposed here. Serialization or disabling overlap suppressing a short reproduction did not establish a race as root cause. ### Remaining work The branch is retained as a draft for maintainer review and provenance. It is not ready to merge without an independently established correctness or performance motivation. GPU validation and any motivation for retaining these predicates need to be established independently.

title: [Feat] linear-attn: Bole spec-verify for GDN (drop per-draft SSM snapshots)
summary: ## Motivation Speculative target verify on GDN (gated delta rule) hybrid models snapshots the full recurrent state after every draft step into `MambaPool.intermediate_ssm`, so that the commit can copy back the state of the accepted step. The buffer is `(max_running_requests + 1) x num_draft_tokens x state_size_per_layer x num_gdn_layers` and is reserved for the whole lifetime of the server. For Qwen3.8-27B (48 GDN layers, TP2) with DFLASH block 8 it is **3.66 GB per GPU at `--max-running-requests 12`**, taken straight out of the KV pool, and it grows linearly with the concurrency cap. ReplaySSM spec-verify (RFC #28511) removes this buffer for MTP-style verify, but with DSPARK/DFLASH it currently requires a KDA model (`--enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires a KDA model`), so GDN models served with DFLASH (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2) still pay the full snapshot cost. ## Modifications Bole keeps only the low-rank factors of each draft step and rebuilds the accepted state on commit. Starting from the same state `S_0`, the state after `a` steps of the gated delta rule is $$S_a = p_a S_0 + \sum_{j \le a} \frac{p_a}{p_j} k_j u_j^\top$$ where `p` is the cumulative decay, `k_j` the L2-normalized key and `u_j` a correction vector obtained from a `T x T` unit lower-triangular system. Verify stores `p`, `k`, `u` (about `T x 128` values per head instead of `T x 128 x 128`), and the commit writes `S_a` back into the request slot. - `kernels/ops/attention/linear/bole_spec_verify.py` (new): three Triton kernels - `bole_factor_kernel`: per (request, head) cumulative log-

summary: ## Motivation Make **DeepSeek-V4-Flash on A3 work with a non-speculative prefill server (P), a DSPARK6 decode server (D), and the `ascend` transfer backend**. The reported deployment should be able to keep DSPARK disabled on P. The request fails at the P/D handoff because D expects draft state that P never produced. This PR accepts that specific missing component and prevents draft attention from reading the missing prompt history. ### What P, D and draft state mean in this failure In PD serving, P processes the input prompt, and D continues generating the response. To continue the model's computation, D needs intermediate data produced while processing the prompt. KV caches and the model's compressor state are part of that data. With DSPARK enabled, D also runs a **draft path**, which proposes candidate tokens for the **target model** to verify. The target and draft paths have their own cached state. Having the target's prompt state does not mean the draft's prompt state has also been computed. What is missing is the draft's prompt history. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv4: Vectorize RoPE loads in SM100 decode attention
summary:
## Motivation The SM100 SwapAB decode kernel currently uses scalar loads for RoPE. Casting the base pointer to BF16 before adding the element offset lets Triton recognize contiguous accesses and emit 128-bit loads. On SM103, the Q=8 SWA+C2 specialization goes from 64 scalar `LDG.E.U16` instructions to 8 vector `LDG.E.128` instructions. Across Q=1/4/8/16/32, full SwapAB attention latency (partial_gluon + _combine) decreased by 2.6%–4.8% with Triton 3.8.0 and 3.4%–10.3% with Triton 3.9.0. ## Modifications In `_load_v4`, 2 * i produces byte offsets `0, 2, 4, …`, and Triton’s pointer contiguity analysis (AxisInfo) cannot infer unit-stride BF16 access through the later cast. Casting the RoPE base first makes the BF16 stride explicit while preserving the same byte addresses. ```diff - rope_ptr = (base8 + 2 * i).to(bf16_ptr) + rope_ptr = base8.to(bf16_ptr) + i ``` ## Accuracy Tests I tested Q=1/4/8/16/32 across SWA, SWA+C2, and SWA+C1, and outputs are bitwise identical before and after the patch on each Triton version (3.8.0 and 3.9.0). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured full SwapAB decode attention (partial_gluon + _combine) with H=16 and a 4K context. title: [Feat] scheduler: Add UniBoost tail-aware schedule policy with a rank-invariant TP/PP mode
summary: ## Summary This PR adds **UniBoost**, an opt-in tail-aware schedule policy (from *[Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026](https://openreview.net/challenge?redirect=%2Fforum%3Fid%3DV40F5O5N85)). Before each prefill admission pass, the waiting queue is re-sorted by a soft priority. Agentic / RL-rollout serving is **prefill-dominated with heavy tails**: in a production SWE-agent trace we measured (7.6k requests), input length p50 is 11.8k tokens vs output p50 of ~90 (≈100:1), turns append a median of 169 tokens of tool output but p99 = 9.1k (test-log dumps), and per-request work varies by two orders of magnitude. Under FCFS, short or cache-hot prefills routinely wait behind cold 30k-token prompts, inflating P90+ latency exactly in the moderate-overload regime that RL rollout bursts create. `Phi(i) = arrival_i − b_γ(w_i)`, `w_i = α · uncached_tokens_i` where the boost `b_γ(w) = (1/γ)·ln(1/(1−e^{−γw}))` is bounded, decreasing and convex: short / radix-cache-hot requests are pulled forward, long requests decay to their FCFS rank (bounded boost ⇒ **no starvation**), and γ interpolates FCFS (γ→∞) ↔ SJF (γ→0) **without any output-length prediction**. An optional **gamma-Ada** controller adapts γ online from the observed latency tail ratio (t99/t95). On a single rank, sampling and refitting stay off the scheduler critical path: completion recording is an O(1) `deque.append`, the percentile scan + EMA refit run on a daemon thread, and the scheduler only reads the current γ. title: [Perf] DFLASH: Keep an all-sliding-window draft's KV on the target's SWA slots (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation A DFLASH draft allocates one KV row per target token, even when every draft layer is sliding-window and can read only its last window. On a hybrid sliding-window target, that pool is sized like the target's full-attention pool. Most of it holds rows the draft can no longer read, and HiCache mirrors it on the host. With this PR, such a draft's KV lives on the target allocator's SWA slots: - one draft row per target SWA slot; - the target's budget charges the draft per SWA token, and the bytes saved become target KV; - HiCache backs it up as a DRAFT_SWA sidecar of the SWA host pool. The draft window must not exceed the target's, so the target's SWA eviction keeps every slot the draft reads. #40665 covers full-attention targets; this PR covers hybrid sliding-window targets. Related: #36995 and #37180 bound an all-sliding-window draft's KV with a request-private compact layout for PD serving, with radix cache and HiCache off; this PR keeps the draft on the target's SWA slots, with radix cache and HiCache on. ## How to enable ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_DRAFT_KV_ON_SWA=1 # default off ``` Requires: - `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with an all-`sliding_attention` draft; - a hybrid sliding-window target; - `--speculative-draft-attention-backend trtllm_mha`. title: [Fix] HiSparse: use logical PD budgets and abort unsupported retraction
summary: ## Motivation HiSparse PD keeps the full target KV on the host and a sparse working set on the device. Two boundaries need to agree with that design: 1. The accepted prompt length and generation memory budget must use the full logical capacity rather than the smaller physical working set. For example, with 48,000 device slots and 384,000 logical slots, a 65,536-token prompt should not get its 64-token output budget clipped to zero solely because it exceeds 48,000. 2. A genuinely retracted HiSparse PD request cannot currently be restored by the generic decode backup path: its coordinator has released the sparse workspace and there is no complete host-KV/indexer/draft restoration implementation. Calling the unsupported backup path can raise instead of returning a request-level failure. ## Modifications - Use the host-backed logical capacity for HiSparse PD prompt limits, retaining request-table capacity handling and existing hybrid-SWA behavior. - Use `size_full` for the PD decode generation budget, retaining page alignment and reserve slack. Monolithic/prefill behavior and physical pool metrics are unchanged. - Force the existing no-backup path for `HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` during PD retraction, clean up the request and report `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of attempting an unsupported CPU backup or requeuing lost KV state. - Return 503 for a HiSparse last-request OOM as well. title: [Feat] checkpoint: Process checkpoint lifecycle with prepare/status/restore routes
summary: ## Motivation External checkpoint/restore orchestrators, such as ones built on CRIU and `cuda-checkpoint`, need three things from the server: a signal that it is safe to capture, one idempotent call to bring it back after the restore, and a way to prepare at startup, before state that cannot be captured (such as a P/D KV transfer transport) exists. SGLang already has the pieces under `--enable-memory-saver`: `pause_generation`, `release_memory_occupation`, `resume_memory_occupation` and `continue_generation`. This PR sequences them behind three routes, so a prepared server behaves exactly like a server paused with `/pause_generation`. It implements the SGLang side of #44523. The vLLM counterpart is vllm-project/vllm#62570. ## Modifications | API | Behavior | | :-- | :-- | | `POST /checkpoint/prepare?mode=abort\|retract` | Pause generation with `mode`, wait for the scheduler to go idle, then release the KV cache. Returns once started, or 400 with the reason and nothing changed if it cannot prepare now. | | `GET /checkpoint/status` | 200 once prepared, 503 until then, 500 after a failure. | | `POST /checkpoint/restore` | Bring the KV cache back and continue generation, after a restore or in place. Safe to repeat. | | `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` | Prepare before the server is marked Up. | | `Engine.checkpoint_prepare/restore/state` | The same steps in process. | - The routes are `ADMIN_OPTIONAL`, like `/pause_generation`. - Between prepare and restore, the server behaves like a paused one: `/ready` and the `/health` canary report 503, and new requests wait until restore.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fp8: keep K%128!=0 block-fp8 linears on the Triton kernel under the MXFP8 view
summary: ## Motivation On SM12x, a block-fp8 checkpoint (`weight_block_size=[32,32]`, `scale_fmt=ue8m0`) served through the MXFP8 view (`--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass`) silently gets a per-layer slowdown whenever the layer's K is a multiple of 32 but not of 128: no error, no log, just a slower kernel. The per-layer admission check and the kernel choice disagree: - `_prepare_block_fp8_as_mxfp8` admits a layer on `k % 32 == 0` and converts its scales; - `_b12x_or_cutlass_mxfp8_linear` (#45262) then picks `backend = "b12x" if weight.shape[1] % 128 == 0 else "cutlass"`, because b12x cannot take such a K -- it raises `b12x mm_mxfp8 requires the contraction dim K to be a multiple of 128 (one full BK128 tile). Got K=288.` So those layers are handed to CUTLASS MXFP8, which at the decode shapes this view targets is 2.3x to 3.0x slower than the Triton block kernel the layer already had. Reported with measurements in #49789. ## Modifications Make the gate ask the same question the dispatch asks, instead of carrying a looser copy of it: - `fp8_utils.py`: new `block_fp8_mxfp8_can_serve_k(backend, k)` returns `k % 128 == 0` exactly when the route in play is `flashinfer_cutlass` **and** b12x is supported on this device -- the same condition `dispatch_block_fp8_mxfp8_linear` uses to select `_b12x_or_cutlass_mxfp8_linear`. That expression is now shared as `_flashinfer_b12x_supported()` rather than written twice, so the two cannot drift apart again. - `fp8.py`: `_prepare_block_fp8_as_mxfp8` consults it before converting, so the layer keeps its plain `weight_scale_inv` and stays on `w8a8_block

title: [Perf] [AMD] attention: Switch MLA decode to Aiter on gfx1250
summary: ### Motivation On gfx1250, MLA decode runs the Triton kernel. AITER has a faster ASM decode kernel (fp8 Q, fp8 KV). This PR switches decode to it and folds its input preparation into the existing fused RoPE/KV-cache kernel, so no extra kernels are added per layer. ### Changes - **ASM decode path** (opt-in: `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_GFX1250_ASM=1` with `--decode-attention-backend aiter`) - Non-persistent AITER ASM kernel; fp8 KV cache, page size 64. - The KV cache uses the page layout the ASM kernel reads. Prefill and prefix reads go through the pool, so other paths are unaffected. - CUDA-graph compatible. - **Fusion** - The fused RoPE + concat + KV-cache kernel also writes the ASM page layout and emits the fp8, padded Q the kernel takes directly, removing the separate Q quantization and KV-write pass. - With ASM on, the Triton decode page table, its CUDA-graph buffer and the persist MLA metadata are not built; the ASM path builds its own page table. Default behavior (flag off) is unchanged. ### Dependencies - Requires ROCm/aiter#7133 (paged-layout mode for the fused RoPE/KV-cache kernel); keep `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_GFX1250_ASM` off until the aiter pin includes it. - Independent of #48893: prefix reads go through the pool's `get_mla_kv_buffer`, which handles the ASM page layout, so the two PRs can merge in either order. ### Results Kimi-K2-Thinking MXFP4, 8× gfx1250, TP8, input/output 8192/1024, same server args apart from the decode backend: | Concurrency | TPOT (ms) Triton → ASM | Total throughput (tok/s) Triton → ASM | TTFT | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 20.56 → 15.98 (**−22%**) | 1680 →

title: [Perf] kimi-k3: Build the fused routing metadata in a separate 1024-thread PDL kernel
summary: ## Motivation The fused Kimi-K3 routing kernel (#48586) builds the trtllm-gen routing metadata in whichever 224-thread routing CTA finishes last, picked by an atomic counter. That build runs after every routing CTA has finished, in one small CTA, and its cost grows with the row count. At 256 rows it is most of the kernel's time. ## Modifications - **Metadata kernel**: the metadata build moves into a separate 1024-thread, single-CTA kernel launched right after the routing grid and chained with PDL. It waits for the whole routing grid; the routing CTAs already trigger their dependent early. - **Routing CTAs**: they no longer use the last-CTA counter, its fences, or the shared-memory union with the metadata workspace. The `counter` argument and its per-device tensor are removed. - **Padding rows**: the token map's padding rows are set to -1 in one parallel pass before the scatter. Before, each expert's owning thread filled its own tiles' padding. ## Accuracy Tests - **Rig comparison**: for every row count and tile size below, the rig's outputs are bitwise equal to base. This covers ids, weights, the FP8 activations and scales, expert weights, the CTA→expert and mn-limit maps, per-expert counts, CTA and padded-token totals, and the number of padding rows. - **Unit test**: `test_kimi_k3_fused_routing.py` passes on VR. - **`test_kimi_k3_prepared_routing.py`**: fails 12 of 13 on VR with my image both with and without this PR. title: [Perf] diffusion: Run SANA-Video 2.0 anchor attention on BF16 inputs at quality=high
summary: ## Motivation SANA-Video 2.0 promotes the softmax anchor layers' Q/K/V to FP32 before `scaled_dot_product_attention`, following the release config's `fp32_attention: true`. Those tensors are already BF16-valued (RMSNorm and RoPE cast back to the activation dtype), so the upcast adds no information, but it restricts PyTorch to the FP32 memory-efficient kernel: flash attention does not accept FP32 inputs. On a 720p/193-frame request one anchor layer spends 529 ms in `fmha_cutlassF_f32` per forward, and the eight anchor layers are about half of the denoising time. This PR adds a request-gated site, following the SANA-Video 2B `SANA_VIDEO_LINEAR_ATTENTION` pattern: at `quality=high` the anchor layers hand their BF16 Q/K/V to SDPA directly, so flash attention runs with FP32 accumulation for QK^T, softmax and PV. The only precision change is that the probabilities round to BF16 before the PV GEMM. The default `quality=exact` path is unchanged and bit-identical to main. ## Modifications - `sites/sana_video2_softmax_attention_site.py`: `SANA_VIDEO2_SOFTMAX_ATTENTION` (`QualityGatedFusion`) and `try_sana_video2_softmax_attention`, exported through the diffusion kernel facade. - `GatedSoftmaxAttention` marks itself as a site and tries the gated path before the FP32 upcast. - `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS` gains the site at tier `high`. - `SanaVideo2DenoisingStage` mounts and unmounts request-gated fusions at quality changes, like the shared `DenoisingStage` and the Helios stage do. title: [Bug] Native runtime.v1 gRPC reports asynchronous input validation failures as INTERNAL
summary: ## Summary We are separating a Rust sidecar from the engine image and plan to use native gRPC to integrate with an unmodified SGLang image. We want to keep orchestration and engine lifecycles independent, without maintaining an engine fork or parsing engine error-message strings. The current error contract is a significant obstacle to completing that integration: the sidecar cannot reliably tell a rejected client request from an engine failure when both arrive as `INTERNAL`. This affects how we return client errors, decide whether to retry, account for capacity rejection, and isolate actual engine failures. Normal inference can work, but safe error handling remains unresolved. The Python-backed native `sglang.runtime.v1` gRPC bridge loses error classification when request validation fails during asynchronous iteration. A request with an invalid sampling parameter can therefore reach the same `INTERNAL` path as a genuine server failure. This concerns `RuntimeHandle` / `rust/sglang-grpc`, rather than the legacy `--grpc-mode` SMG servicer or the Rust frontend's shared `api.v1` service. ## Version and evidence Source inspected: - Integration target: SGLang v0.5.23, commit `297e54fd105e974cdf401e5b4d20253a22c16f90`. - Main cross-check: `175ab80201868643048cf02f593323872460c91f`; the asynchronous error-to-string path remains present. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When serving Qwen3.5 with the CuTe DSL GDN prefill backend on NVIDIA Blackwell SM100/SM103 GPUs, some long-context prefills can produce non-finite values in the GDN recurrent state and output. The affected code is: ```text python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/linear/gdn_blackwell/kernel_kkt_inv_uw.py ``` The issue is in the Newton–Schulz iterations used to approximate the inverse of the four 16×16 diagonal blocks of: ```text M = I + A ``` The kernel keeps the persistent inverse iterate in FP32 as `Ai_f32`, but converts it to BF16 before each MMA: ```python Ai_bf16.store(Ai_f32.load().to(BFloat16)) ``` The intermediate product `-AiM` is also converted to BF16 before the second MMA. Therefore, although accumulation is FP32, both Newton–Schulz matrix operands are repeatedly truncated to BF16. For an ill-conditioned `I + A`, entries in the inverse iterate can become large. The BF16 rounding error then scales approximately with: ```text cond(I + A) × u_bf16 ``` where `u_bf16 ≈ 2^-8`. The resulting inverse error is propagated by the gated recurrent update. Long contexts process many 64-token internal GDN chunks

title: [Feat] Engram: Serve native tables from Mooncake MNNVL EGM
summary: <!-- PR title: [Feat] engram: Serve native Engram/PLE tables from Mooncake MNNVL EGM --> Add an in-tree adapter for the Mooncake MNNVL EGM row store. After native weight loading and before kernel precompilation, each Engram/PLE shard is republished as an immutable byte table in EGM and its native host backing is released. Hashing, quantization, scales, masking and collectives stay in the model; configure with `--engram-mnnvl-config`. ## Motivation Engram and PLE tables are large, immutable after load, read-only at inference, and read by row id. Keeping one private CPU replica per rank makes them the dominant host-memory block of a deployment and a capacity bottleneck. Fabric-mapped host memory fixes that: a table is materialized once, mapped by every GPU on every node over NVLink, and optionally sharded across supernode peers so each node stores only its shard. This PR is the model-side half: it republishes the tables SGLang already builds into the Mooncake EGM store and routes the existing gather through a byte-fetch op. The storage, allocation, mapping and metadata session live in the companion Mooncake PR [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5406](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/5406) (`[Store] Serve Engram tables from MNNVL EGM host memory`), following roadmap [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4692](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4692) (Stage 3a) and the shape of #46248 (local HiCache Engram) and #47673 (DeepEP remote Engram). title: [Fix] [AMD] scheduler: Keep Muse Spark's scheduler GPU work on the forward stream under monokernel
summary: ## Motivation An AMD monokernel launch (`--enable-amd-monokernel`, sgl-amd-mono) keeps all of its workgroups resident and waiting on each other through device-memory flags. The overlap scheduler issues small kernels on its own `schedule_stream`, and the result readback runs on `copy_stream`. If one of those kernels takes a CU while a monokernel launch is being dispatched, some of the launch's workgroups cannot become resident. The resident ones then wait until the plugin's guard deadline (60 s) stops every rank, and the log shows a GPU memory fault at address `(nil)`. On Muse Spark TP8 with the monokernels on 8x MI355X, this hit about once every 15-60 min at concurrency 1 and 4 on the full AgentX trace set, always in the DFlash2 draft's first launch. A standalone repro replays that launch's CUDA graph and runs one small kernel every 100 ms on a second stream: 4 of 8 GPUs hang within 7 min. The same replays without the second stream ran 200M launches clean. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: on HIP, for Muse Spark with `--enable-amd-monokernel`, `schedule_stream` and `copy_stream` are the forward stream. The host side still overlaps; only the scheduler's GPU work queues behind the forward. Other models, and Muse Spark without the flag, are unchanged. ## Accuracy GSM8K (full 1319 questions), Muse Spark Open TP8 with `--enable-amd-monokernel` on 8x MI355X, `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:muse-spark-open-1027` (carries this change): 0.9750. ## Benchmark NA ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/

title: [Feat] offloader: Let OffloaderV1 offload only the model-declared submodule
summary: ## Motivation Models tell the offloader which submodule of each layer to offload through `offloader_kwargs` (`submodule_accessor`). OffloaderV2 (`--offload-group-size`) honors it, but OffloaderV1 (`--cpu-offload-gb`) ignores it and always offloads whole decoder layers until the budget is used up. Whole-layer offload breaks models that use layer parameters outside the layer's `forward`, which V1's `functional_call` wrapper does not cover. With DeepSeek-V4 (after #49850 adds its `offloader_kwargs`), `--cpu-offload-gb 110` fails while loading, because the mHC parameters were moved to CPU: ``` DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights -> _prewarm_mhc_kernels -> mhc_pre -> tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm NotImplementedError: Could not run 'deep_gemm::tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend ``` (reproduced on main b95f22fcc). For MoE models, offloading only the routed experts is also the better use of the budget: it is what V2 does for DeepSeek, and what vLLM does with `--cpu-offload-params experts`. ## Modifications `layers/offloader.py`, `OffloaderV1`: - `wrap_modules` passes `submodule_accessor(module)` to `maybe_offload_to_cpu` when the model provides an accessor. - `maybe_offload_to_cpu(module, offloaded_submodule=None)` moves only `offloaded_submodule`'s parameters to pinned CPU memory, but keeps the `functional_call` wrapper on `module.forward` (the whole layer). title: [Fix] [AMD] moe: Keep is_shuffled on AITER-shuffled unquantized MoE weights
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm with the AITER MoE runner, `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` shuffles `w13_weight` and `w2_weight` with `aiter.ops.shuffle.shuffle_weight(..., (16, 16))` and stores the result with `copy_or_rebind_param`. `shuffle_weight` marks the tensor it returns with `is_shuffled = True`, but `copy_or_rebind_param` detaches it and copies the data into the existing `Parameter`, so the parameter that reaches `aiter.fused_moe` has no `is_shuffled` attribute. `aiter.fused_moe` reads `is_shuffled` to choose between the `preshuffle_on` and `preshuffle_off` CK 2-stage MoE modules and to accept tuned fMoE configs (it warns that tuned kernels expect preshuffled weights). As a result, unquantized BF16 MoE models always run the `preshuffle_off` path on weights that were shuffled, and tuned configs for these shapes cannot be applied. This is the same issue that #47870 fixes for the compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 MoE path, here in the unquantized path. ## Modifications Set `is_shuffled = True` on `layer.w13_weight` and `layer.w2_weight` right after each `copy_or_rebind_param` call. Weight bytes, dtype and layout are unchanged; only the attribute that `aiter.fused_moe` checks is restored. ## Accuracy Tests MI350X (gfx950, 256 CUs), AITER `2bb5491`. One EP rank of a BF16 MoE layer: 512 experts (256 local via `expert_mask`), top-10, hidden 2560, expert intermediate 640, SiLU, fused gate/up, called through `aiter.fused_moe` exactly as `AiterRunnerCore` does. Because this path reports `is_shuffled=False`, the call now raises: ``` RuntimeError: gfx950 fp8 CK MoE read

title: [Fix] scheduler: Keep the paged intake limit admittable on an empty KV pool
summary: ## Motivation With `page_size > 1`, a prompt can pass intake and then never be admitted, even on an empty KV pool. The request sits at the head of the waiting queue and nothing behind it runs. `TpModelWorker.get_worker_info` bounds requests by `kv_capacity - 1` (then `- 5` for `max_req_input_len`). Admission is stricter: `PrefillAdder` rounds the prompt up to whole pages and reserves one more page (`per_req_token_overhead`, the `+ page_size` in `PrefillBudget.reserve`), and `init_req_max_new_tokens` clamps with the same page. The bound only matters when the KV pool is smaller than the context length, which #42976 now warns about at startup ("long requests will be refused or truncated at serving time"). This is the symptom of #28530. That issue was closed as fixed by #25126, which aligned the `max_new_tokens` clamp; the intake limit was left at `kv_capacity - 1`. #29249 proposed tightening the limit in `validate_input_length` and was closed by the stale bot without review. title: [Fix] hisparse: disambiguate __ffsll for HIP's dual overloads
summary: ## Bug The `hisparse_spec` JIT kernel fails to compile on ROCm, so speculative decoding with `--enable-hisparse` cannot start on AMD GPUs. ## When it happens `first_set_lane()` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/kvcacheio/hisparse_spec.cuh` calls `__ffsll(mask)` with `mask` of type `BallotMask` (`uint64_t`, i.e. `unsigned long` on LP64). HIP provides `__ffsll` overloads for both `unsigned long long` and `long long`; the conversion from `unsigned long` is equally valid for both, so hipcc rejects the call as ambiguous and the module build fails. Reproduced on gfx942 (MI300X). CUDA has a single-signature `__ffsll`, so the same source builds fine there. ## Why it's critical This blocks every HiSparse speculative configuration on ROCm, including the already-supported EAGLE path — not a new feature, an existing one that cannot build. ## Fix Cast the mask to `unsigned long long` to pin the overload, inside the existing `#ifdef USE_ROCM` branch. The CUDA branch is untouched and the modified line is not compiled under nvcc, so there is no behavior change on NVIDIA. ## Verification - The `hisparse_spec` module now builds on gfx942, and a GLM-5.3 TP8 server on 8x MI300X runs HiSparse + speculative decoding with measured accept length 2.88 tokens/round. - No CUDA impact by construction (the change is preprocessor-gated to ROCm). ## Checklist - [x] Fix verified on the affected platform (ROCm build + serving run) - [ ] Unit tests added (N/A: compile fix; covered by the kernel build on CI) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_

summary: ## Motivation The NPU PR test pipeline regressed from ~149 min to 200+ min. summary: ## Motivation Nomas calls its Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE wrapper repeatedly during denoising. The existing wrapper materializes the BF16 input as FP32, squares it, and calls ATen mean before its compiled normalization/rotation epilogue.
