title: [Fix] PD: reject incompatible handshakes without killing decode
summary: A prefill/decode KV or state layout mismatch raises `RuntimeError` during bootstrap. The exception escapes the decode scheduler, terminating the decode workers instead of rejecting the incompatible requests. In an Ascend 910C DeepSeek-V4-Flash deployment, the first request caused all eight decode ranks to exit. Catch these rejections at the pending-handshake boundary. Abort the requests waiting for the incompatible prefill, preserve the original layout error for their responses, clear their retry bookkeeping, and continue processing other peers. Layout validation is unchanged. Validation: - The new mismatch regression errors on the unmodified base and passes with this change. It also covers multiple affected requests, retry cleanup, continued processing of a healthy peer, and propagation of unexpected exceptions. - 39 CPU unit tests passed across decode queue cleanup, speculative KV layouts, and unified state-wire validation. On the NPU host, the existing CPU-only queue fixtures require `_is_npu=False`; the added handshake tests also pass with the NPU flag enabled. - Real Ascend 910C negative case: P without speculative configuration and D with DSPARK produce a four-versus-five state-entry mismatch. With this change, D returned HTTP 500 with the original reason and remained healthy, rather than terminating its scheduler. The paired gateway cancellation fix is #49792. Combined real-service fault injection returned the original mismatch in 14.33 ms (buffered) and 13.04 ms (streaming), observed cancellation of both prefill requests, and recovered correct inference after fault

title: [Fix] [NPU] dsv4: transfer A3 C4 state using peer-local rows
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill/decode disaggregation on A3 (Ascend 910C) returns HTTP 500 when prefill runs without speculation and decode enables DSpark. Prefill (P) must hand off the target model's C4 compressor state so decode (D) can continue from the same history. The reported configuration gives the target C4 compressor an **8-row ring on P and a 16-row ring on D**. The state rows have the same format on both peers, but the old A3 registration groups an entire ring into one transfer item inside `StateType.SWA`: | Buffer | Bytes per row | P item: 8 rows | D item: 16 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | C4 attention compressor state | 8,192 | 65,536 | 131,072 | | C4 indexer compressor state | 2,048 | 16,384 | 32,768 | The Ascend backend uses the shared Mooncake manager's layout validation. It rejects these unequal item strides before the state transfer completes, and the request returns HTTP 500. The hardware transfer tests below use MemFabric SDMA. ## Modifications Register C4 compressor state as **individual rows** under the existing `AscendStateType.DSV4_C4_STATE` component. P and D then independently translate the same logical history positions into their own physical state rows. The attention item stride becomes 8,192 bytes on both peers; the indexer item stride becomes 2,048 bytes on both peers. ### How the A3 row mapping works The A3 EXPLICIT compressor consumes the last `coff * compress_ratio = 2 * 4 = 8` logical history positions, or all available positions for a shorter history. title: [Perf] dsa: bf16 MQA logits for the prefill indexer
summary: ## Motivation The DSA indexer's ragged (prefill) path calls DeepGEMM's `fp8_mqa_logits`, which splits rows evenly across SMs and writes fp32 logits. On long cached contexts the logits kernel and the top-k over its output are a visible part of a Kimi-K3.1 prefill forward. DeepGEMM's legacy entry `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits_legacy` writes bf16 logits from the same FP8 query and keys: half the bytes to write and to read in the top-k, and half the chunk scratch. It also accepts the row schedule from `get_mqa_logits_metadata_legacy`, which balances rows of different key ranges across SMs. ## Modifications Opt-in, CUDA only. With `SGLANG_DSA_INDEXER_BF16_LOGITS=1`, `Indexer._mqa_logits` calls `fp8_mqa_logits_bf16` (legacy entry, schedule, bf16 weights, bf16 logits), and the logits chunk budget doubles. The v2 ragged top-k gets a bf16-score build: `topk_impl.cuh` / `topk_v2.cuh` take a `score_t` (`-DSGL_TOPK_SCORE_BF16`), widen scores to fp32 on load and keep the selection logic; `topk_transform_ragged_v2` picks the build from the score dtype (a separate JIT module, `mode{N}_bf16`). ## Accuracy Tests - Top-2048 overlap with an fp32 reference (`sum_h relu(q_h . k_j) * w_h`) on one real Kimi-K3.1 DSA layer's indexer inputs from a cold 16,384-token prefill: FP8 inputs with fp32 logits (today) 0.9792, with bf16 logits 0.9791. - bf16-score top-k: the same set of selected values as the fp32 build on bf16 inputs, equal to `torch.topk` values. title: [Perf] [XPU] linear: Use torch scaled_mm for MXFP8 linear
summary: ## Motivation MXFP8 (OCP Microscaling with E4M3 elements and block-32 UE8M0 scales) has become the de facto standard for cutting weight memory bandwidth and footprint in models such as DeepSeek-V4 and MiniMax-M3. With PyTorch 2.14+ XPU introducing native hardware acceleration for `torch.nn.functional.scaled_mm(..., ScalingType.BlockWise1x32)`, XPU now natively supports high-throughput block-32 scaled matrix multiplications. summary: # [Feat] paged-experts: a disk tier for experts that do not fit host memory ## Motivation This PR aims at adding a disk-tier to Paged Experts. Paged Experts keeps all E experts of every MoE layer in a pinned host store, so a model whose experts do not fit the host's RAM cannot start. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is a 167 GB checkpoint; its routed experts take 137.1 GiB in the host store's layout. On an RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB with 62 GB of RAM, about 45 GiB of that can be pinned next to the rest of the server, so the model does not run on this machine at all today (its MXFP4 routed experts in an FP8 checkpoint are also not a format Paged Experts pages yet). There is no "before" number to compare against. This PR adds the disk as a third tier behind the GPU slots and the host store. With `--paged-experts-enable-disk`, when the host budget cannot hold every expert, each layer keeps all its experts in its expert cache file (#48642) and only R of them in pinned host rows; an expert the router picks that is only on disk is read into a host row and copied into its slot, also inside a captured decode step, which waits for the read instead of falling back to eager. On the same machine DeepSeek-V4-Flash now serves at 13.8-14.1 tok/s decode with 71 of 256 experts per layer in host memory, TTFT for a natural 1.5k-token prompt is 8.5 s, and GSM8K (200 questions) is 0.975. The first start writes the 137.1 GiB of files once (`load_model` 288.9 s) without the model ever having to fit in RAM; later starts load in 81-82 s. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (112.7 GiB of experts) serves on the same card at 15.0-15

title: [Fix] scheduler: Reject duplicate rid at intake to prevent cross-client token leak
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49903. `rid` is caller-supplied on `/generate`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings`. Each tokenizer worker rejects a duplicate rid only against its own `rid_to_state`, so with `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` two concurrent requests with the same rid can both be accepted when they land on different workers. The scheduler has no duplicate-rid check, so both run — and because `DetokenizeStateTable` is keyed by rid alone, the second request's first output row replaces the first request's live detokenize state. The first client's tokens are then decoded with the second client's header and routed to the second client's tokenizer worker, which appends them to the second client's response (`text` and `output_ids`). Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation SGLang can read activations but cannot write them. `return_hidden_states` is supported end to end, with worked examples for both the server and the engine under `examples/runtime/hidden_states/`. So extracting a steering vector, the difference in mean activations between two prompt conditions, works today. Applying one does not. There is no way to add a vector into the residual stream during the forward pass, and searching the tree for `control_vector` returns nothing. As far as I can tell no issue or PR has ever asked for it, so this is a scoping question rather than a complaint. Steering vectors are used to shift a model's behaviour at inference time without finetuning: refusal and honesty behaviour, hallucination rates, verbosity, persona. The attraction for a serving engine is that the same weights serve every request, the vector is a few hundred kilobytes, and the strength is a per-request knob. The usual alternative, a LoRA per behaviour, costs an adapter per variant and a reload to change it. The reason I am asking before writing anything is that the right answer might be "not in core", and your plugin framework may already be the answer. ### What I am asking 1. title: [Perf] dflash: Fuse the simulated-acceptance overwrite into one kernel
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is a benchmark mode that forces the speculative acceptance length. For DFlash, each verify step runs the real accept first and then overwrites its outputs (accept and commit lengths, bonus token, committed block) with the forced length (`apply_dflash_simulated_acceptance`). That overwrite is simulation-only work, and it was eager: - `fixed` token mode: 4 small launches (`fill_` x 4). - `real-draft-token` mode: 6 launches (fills, zero, slice copies, casts). - On the sampling and selector verify branches, which do not produce the target argmax, `real-draft-token` mode also ran a full-vocabulary argmax over all `bs x block_size` verify rows, then read only one row per request (the row at the forced length). - On the greedy branch the Triton accept already writes `new_seq_lens`; under simulation the caller threw it away and recomputed `prefix_lens + commit_lens` (2 more launches). This PR does that overwrite in one small JIT CUDA kernel and takes the argmax of the forced row only. Outputs are byte-identical to the eager code, including the memory around strided outputs and the CPU RNG state after the call. The real accept is untouched and still runs first, and nothing changes when `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is unset. It follows the rule in #46840 (now in `environ.py`): simulation changes only the accepted length, every operation real serving runs still runs at real cost, and only work that the simulation alone adds may get cheaper. #46840 did the same for the EAGLE simulated bonus sample, which drew over all rows and kept

summary: ## Motivation `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel` runs one program per request, and that program scans the whole vocabulary twice: once to sum the residual distribution and once to walk its CDF. A launch therefore costs about as much at one request as at many, and at small batch the device is nearly idle while a few programs each read hundreds of thousands of entries. With a 202,048-entry vocabulary this final-token pass takes 72-113 us per verify step at batch 1-16 on GB300. ## Modifications - A split path runs the same arithmetic on a (requests x vocabulary tiles) grid. `_split_sum_kernel` repeats the chain walk and reduces one tile; `_split_cdf_kernel` adds the tile sums in tile order to recover the normalizer and the running sum in front of its own tile, then applies the stock tile step. The stock loop takes the first tile with a match and its first matching index, the smallest matching index of the row, so keeping the minimum across tiles with an atomic reproduces the stock token. - The stock kernel is unchanged. title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] moe: Stop DeepGEMM's MLOPart helper once MegaMoE creates its buffer
summary: ## Motivation With `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, every worker keeps DeepGEMM's MLOPart helper tree alive for the whole serving lifetime: the `deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py` helper, an MPS control daemon and an `-mlopart` MPS server. The CUDA driver refuses to checkpoint-lock MPS clients, so MegaMoE workers cannot be captured with CUDA checkpoint, as used by [NVIDIA Snapshot](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/snapshot). This PR stops the helper as soon as DeepGEMM has cached what MegaMoE needs from it. It is the SGLang counterpart of vllm-project/vllm#66015. On B200, DeepGEMM measures it by starting `python -I deep_gemm/utils/mlopart.py`, which runs `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with an `-mlopart` MPS server. The helper allocates memory on each die and sends it to the worker as a POSIX FD, and the worker measures SM-to-die latency. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Avoid wide page-table expansion in chunked prefill
summary: # [AMD] Avoid wide page-table expansion in chunked DSA prefill ## Motivation Long-context DSA prefill splits the logits into row chunks when the full FP32 logits tensor would exceed the memory limit. For example, a 32,768 by 60,000 tensor needs about 7.9 GiB. For each chunk, the PAGED path currently expands the page table with `page_table_1[batch_idx_list]` before selecting top-k entries. This copies every page-table column for every row, even though only the selected top-k indices are needed. ## Modifications - Select the logical top-k indices before reading the page table. - Add a Triton row-map kernel that uses `batch_idx_list` to find the page-table row for each token. - Map only the selected logical indices to physical KV-cache slots. - Read the page-table row stride at runtime so different context lengths do not compile separate Triton modules. At 60,000 tokens with top-k 2,048, this maps about 30 times less page-table data. The decode path is unchanged. [SGLang PR #37889](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37889) handles eligible unchunked rows with the fused top-k v2 kernel. Its chunked fallback still uses the wide page-table expansion. This PR handles that fallback when `batch_idx_list` is present. ## Accuracy Tests The row-map output matches direct PyTorch indexing for: - 3 requests, 17 rows, page-table width 257, and top-k 64; - 16 requests, 32 rows, page-table width 60,003, and top-k 2,048. The tests also check that `batch_idx_list` selects the row-map path. ```bash python3 -m pytest \ test/registered/kernel/attention/test_dsa_prefill_rowmap.py -v ``` ##

summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) has 11 DSA layers with a 512-dimensional latent, no RoPE cache, and a pooled indexer (`index_kpool=4`). The standard GLM SM90 NVFP4 implementation assumes a 64-dimensional RoPE tail and a fixed 2048-token decode table. This draft adds a functional compact-cache path for Flash, while retaining the existing KDA states and FP8 indexer. ## Modifications - Add 288-byte no-RoPE rows: 256 bytes of E2M1 values plus 32 E4M3 block-16 scales. title: [AMD] Prevent DeepSeek-V4 MTP GPU faults during graph replay
summary: ## What broke PR #26383 (`deaba74745d7`) introduced this regression. It changed HIP-Radix target verification to build full metadata early from CPU sequence lengths. Before that change, CUDA Graph target verification built its compression plan from GPU data. After it, fixed-size MTP graph replay accidentally started using the CPU planner. The CPU planner fills a temporary pinned-memory buffer and starts an asynchronous copy to the GPU. CUDA Graph captures that copy for later replay, but the temporary CPU buffer is not kept as graph state. A replay can therefore use stale plan offsets. The C128 write kernel then writes outside its allocation, causing the multi-rank GPU memory fault and scheduler exit `-6`. The later connection failures and `KeyError: answer` happen only because the server has already crashed. PR #30964 later added the GPU planner for ragged target verification, where CPU sequence lengths are unavailable. Its check covered only ragged layouts, so fixed-size MTP graph replay remained on the unsafe path. In short: #26383 introduced the bad graph behavior; #30964 left that fixed-size case uncovered. Failing job: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33538157363/job/99957472899 ## Fix Use the existing GPU planner in the two cases that require it: CUDA Graph replay, and ragged verification without CPU sequence lengths. Fixed-size eager verification keeps the existing CPU planner because it does not replay the temporary host buffer and avoids an extra GPU planning launch. Normal prefill, decode, and draft extension are unchanged. ## Validation ROCm 7.2

title: Fix deterministic DSV4 top-k fallback on ROCm
summary: ### Summary - Fall back to the existing DSV4 Top-K v1 JIT implementation when the packaged ROCm AOT operator is not registered for the active target. - Make that JIT path compile with HIP and fit 64-KiB-LDS devices. - Make ROCm selected-set output deterministic across boundary ties, signed zeroes and coarse-bin overflow while preserving CUDA behavior. - Add a registered AMD test for forced fallback, page mapping, ragged rows, runtime Top-K sizes, overflow, long rows and repeat determinism. ### Why this is needed On an unmodified current SGLang checkout, a native gfx1100 installation whose wheel does not contain the DSV4 AOT operator fails twice: the public Python path raises `AttributeError`, and direct JIT v1 compilation calls the CUDA-only `cudaFuncSetAttribute` and `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` APIs. The launchable ROCm path also needs deterministic handling at the exact selection boundary. Atomic arrival order must not choose among equal scores, signed `-0.0/+0.0` must compare equally, and a coarse FP16 bin larger than the bounded LDS candidate buffer must not be silently clipped. ### Contract DeepSeek-V4 uses `index_topk=512`. SGLang's current API supports runtime `topk in (0, 1024]` and returns an unordered selected set; it does not promise score-sorted output. This change canonicalizes the selected set by logical index on ROCm, which provides a deterministic valid representation without adding a score-order contract. summary: # [diffusion] Sparse attention backends: run the dense path on the dense backend ## Motivation `subblock_sparse_attn` and `sol_attn` are both partial-sparsity schemes: they keep a leading run of denoise steps dense (and, for Sol-Attn, a couple of layers at every step), and only route the rest through their sparse kernel. title: [router] PD: never auto-replay a request that may already be dispatched
summary: ## Motivation Part of the PP-prefill hang fix series — tracking issue #34572. PD dispatch is not idempotent. summary: ## Motivation Part of the PP-prefill hang fix series — tracking issue #34572. In PP disaggregated prefill with HiCache storage prefetch enabled, each stage locally checked `check_prefetch_progress(rid)` when admitting bootstrapped requests. Prefetch completes at different times on different PP stages, so the same request could enter `waiting_queue` on some stages but not on others. No barrier-like collective is inserted into the skewed PP event loop — the same two ring passes are used. - Guarded to `enable_hicache_storage and pp_size > 1`; no behavior change otherwise. - New unit test: `test/registered/unit/managers/test_pp_hicache_prefetch_consensus.py` (readiness skew across stages, late-ready admission, non-storage no-op). title: [MiniMax-M3] Gather-transpose batch KV pages for MSA sparse prefill (Hkv > 1)
summary: ## Motivation `fmha_sm100`'s sparse prefill consumes paged KV in HND layout `[num_pages, Hkv, page_size, D]` and unconditionally calls `.contiguous()` on it. SGLang's MHA pool is slot-major NHD `[max_slots, Hkv, D]`, so `msa_sparse_prefill_main` hands MSA a permuted whole-pool view: - Per-rank **Hkv == 1** (attention-TP >= num_kv_heads): the permuted view is contiguous by construction -> zero-copy. This is why the cost is invisible on TP4. - Per-rank **Hkv > 1** (TP < num_kv_heads, e.g. PP deployments at TP1 -> Hkv=4): the view is non-contiguous, so `.contiguous()` materializes a copy of the *entire per-layer KV pool* on every sparse layer of every prefill forward — with a ~5.7M-slot fp8 pool, ~11.7 GB of traffic per layer per chunk through torch's slow permute-copy path, plus a pool-sized transient allocation each call. ## Modifications - New fused Triton kernel `gather_kv_hnd` (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/common/gather_kv.py`): gathers only the pages referenced by the batch page table from the NHD pool into a compact contiguous HND buffer, transposing on the fly — one read + one write over **batch** KV instead of the whole pool. Dtype-agnostic (bf16/fp8_e4m3) via int32-word reinterpretation; K and V in one launch; ~5-6 TB/s effective on sm103. - `msa_sparse_prefill_main` uses the gathered buffer with an identity page table (`arange`), making MSA's internal `.contiguous()` a no-op. title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 SM120 decode pads q to 64 heads for an SM90 constraint; removing the pad changes greedy output despite the kernel being bit-identical
summary: ### Summary On SM120/121, DeepSeek-V4 decode pads `q` to 64 heads even when the rank owns fewer and FlashInfer has an instance for the real count. Removing the pad is worth **0.50% of a decode step** at TP4 — small, and I would not open a PR for it on its own. What I would like a second opinion on is that removing it **changes greedy output**, which should be impossible if the padded heads are inert. The comment in the padding block says they are not, so this may be known and intentional — but then the constraint is stronger than the one the code cites, and it is worth writing down. ### The padding `srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` (around line 1886): ```python skip_decode_pad = is_sm120_supported() and x.shape[0] > SM120_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS padded_num_heads = (self.n_local_heads if skip_decode_pad else (64 if self.n_local_heads <= 64 else self.n_heads)) ``` with the reason given just below: ``` # FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel only specializes h_q for {64, 128}. ``` That is the SM90 `sgl_kernel` FlashMLA constraint. On the SM120 path the kernel is FlashInfer's `sparse_mla_sm120`, whose `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` carries `{8, 16, 32, 64, 128} x {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024}` and which exports `_decode_dsv4_dispatchable(num_tokens, num_heads, topk, d_qk, page_block_size, extra_topk)` for exactly this question. At `num_attention_heads = 64` and attn-TP 4 each rank owns 16, `(16, 512)` is in the table, so decode attends on 64 heads where 16 would do. Prefill already skips the pad (`x.shape[0] > 64`), so only decode pays. ### Measured cost 4x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP4/EP2, DeepSeek-V

title: PP8 disaggregated prefill has a load-independent ~30 s TTFT floor on Kimi-K3
summary: # Describe the issue A PD-disaggregated Kimi-K3 deployment exhibits a large, load-independent TTFT floor when the prefill node uses pipeline parallelism. Our PP8 configuration was based on the topology and guidance in the LMSYS post [SGLang and Miles Add Day-0 Support for Kimi K3](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support). The post reports that, for 8K prefill on 2×4 GB300 GPUs, PP8×TP1 reaches 1.45–1.72× the prefill capacity of TEP8 and has lower TTFT after the low-concurrency crossover. However, it does not provide the absolute TTFT values or the detailed TTFT measurement methodology. We are trying to determine whether the behavior below comes from a difference in workload or configuration, or from an unexpected PP control-path latency. With the prefill node configured as `pp_size=8, tp_size=1`, TTFT p50 is **31.1 s**. On the same two nodes, with the same replay workload and closed-loop concurrency, a `tp_size=8` prefill baseline has a TTFT p50 of **2.33 s**. The PP8 result is therefore about **13.4x slower**. This does not look like capacity saturation. During the PP8 run: - Prefill uncached throughput was only 1.1–1.6 K tok/s. - The prefill waiting queue was only 1–12 requests across all eight PP ranks. - The decode node had only 1–4 running requests. - TTFT p50 nevertheless remained between 30 and 33 s for the entire run. ## Expected behavior At low load, `pp_size=8` on the disaggregated prefill node should not add a load-independent ~30 s TTFT floor. We expect PP to improve or preserve prefill capacity without making latency-sensitive online traffic

title: [PP + HiCache] HiCache Consistency Fix Plan
summary: # PP HiCache Consistency for Disaggregated Prefill — PR Plan ## Background ### Motivation In agentic and long-context reasoning scenarios, requests frequently share long prefixes (system prompts, tool definitions, multi-turn history) that can span tens of thousands of tokens. Recomputing these shared prefixes for every request is prohibitively expensive. SGLang's **HiCache** addresses this with a 3-level KV cache hierarchy — **L1** (GPU device memory) → **L2** (CPU host memory) → **L3** (external distributed storage, e.g. Mooncake) — enabling prefix reuse across requests and even across restarts via persistent storage. Meanwhile, large models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3 with 60 layers) require **Pipeline Parallelism (PP)** to split layers across multiple GPU groups, combined with **disaggregated prefill** where prefill and decode run on separate server pools. This PP + HiCache + disaggregated prefill stack is critical for production agentic workloads: it maximizes both throughput (via disaggregation) and cache hit rates (via L3 persistence) on large models. However, combining PP with L3 storage introduces a class of consistency bugs that do not exist in simpler configurations. Understanding why requires examining the cache hierarchy level by level. ### Why L3 Storage Breaks PP Consistency In PP mode, each rank runs an independent scheduler with its own radix tree. The key question is: why does adding L3 cause divergence when L1 and L2 alone do not? **L1-only + PP (no HiCache)**: Both ranks receive the same requests in the same order via P2P. `match_prefix` operates on the device radi

title: [Perf] dsa: Stage the DCP top-k merge push in smem and fall back in registers for up to two ranks
summary: ## Motivation The DCP top-k merge (#48588) pushed each rank's 384 candidates with multimem stores straight from `compact()`. `compact()` gives each thread its own contiguous run of output slots, so a warp's stores land scattered: every 8-byte store becomes its own NVLink packet, fanned out to every rank. On Vera Rubin at DCP8 across two nodes, most of the kernel's time went to this push. ## Modifications - **Coalesced push**: the row's candidates are staged in shared memory, then pushed with warp-coalesced multimem stores. title: [Feature] Share GPU memory between the KV pool and the mamba/linear-attention state pool instead of a static split
summary: ### Motivation For hybrid linear-attention models (GDN, KDA, Mamba), SGLang splits the cache memory at startup into a KV pool and a state pool, by `--mamba-full-memory-ratio` (or a pinned `--max-mamba-cache-size`). The split stays fixed for the server's lifetime. With the radix cache, each running request needs several state slots (3 in the default setup, more with speculative decoding), so concurrency is capped at `max_mamba_cache_size // slots per request`, whatever room the KV pool has. Long-context workloads need a small state pool and a big KV pool. Short, high-concurrency workloads need the opposite. A split that suits one starves the other, and a server that sees both (bash99's comment on #33004) can't be sized well. Two RL workloads on the same model, hardware and engine settings needed opposite splits. title: [AMD][ROCm] Add optional device-resident ordering-edge runtime build (rocm-systems#11212)
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, cross-stream / hipgraph dependency polls default to host-visible memory and cross PCIe. With `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES > 4` this manifests as a low-concurrency decode regression. [ROCm/rocm-systems#11212](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/11212) adds device-resident ordering edges (`hsa_amd_signal_create_v2` + `HSA_AMD_SIGNAL_CREATE_DEVICE_MEM_VALUE_WORD` in ROCr, plus the CLR side that names a device-resident ordering-edge value word on cross-queue barrier deps) so those polls come from device-local VRAM instead. vLLM adopted the same mitigation in [vllm-project/vllm#55099](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55099). ## What this PR adds An **optional, opt-in** `docker/rocm-ordering-edge.Dockerfile` layered on top of an existing SGLang ROCm image. title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: fuse compress+norm+rope, emit bpreshuffle scale natively, keep kv_score in bf16
summary: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4 decode a good part of each attention layer goes to kernels that only move or re-lay-out data rather than compute anything. Three of them run on every layer of every step: 1. On CSA layers (`compress_ratio` 4) compress, norm and rope are three separate launches. Each is 4-8 us, which is small enough that dispatch rather than the work sets the cost. 2. The fp8 quant path writes its scale tensor in one layout and then a second kernel transposes it into the layout the bpreshuffle GEMM actually wants — 152 extra launches per decode step. 3. The compressor takes fp32, so the bf16 `wkv_gate` output is widened by a separate elementwise copy before it can be consumed — 92 extra launches per decode step. None of these carry information the surrounding kernels don't already have, so each can be folded into its neighbour without changing the math. ## Modifications Three independent optimisations, each behind its own env gate. **`SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE`** — new `fused_compress4_norm_rope.cuh` folds compress, norm and rope into a single kernel for CSA layers. The fused kernel maps one token per 64-lane wavefront rather than two; that takes it from 85 to 47 VGPRs and lifts occupancy from 5 to 8 waves/SIMD, which is what makes the fused kernel actually cheaper than the three it replaces instead of merely equal to them. **`SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE`** — the quant kernel writes the scale tensor directly in the physical layout bpreshuffle wants (column-major in M), so the separate transpose pass is not needed. **`SGLANG_OPT_KV_SCORE_BF16`** —

summary: ## Motivation On NVIDIA Blackwell SM100 (B200), ModelOpt NVFP4 (`w4a4`, `E2M1` 2x-packed weights/activations with `E4M3` 16-element block scales and per-tensor FP32 `alpha`) dense MLP layers (`LlamaMLP`, `Qwen2MLP`, `Qwen3MLP`) and Mixture-of-Experts (`MoE`) grouped GEMM workloads incur extra kernel launch, global memory round-trip, and tensormap update overhead when executing unfused `gate_up_proj -> SiluAndMul`, non-persistent large-M GEMMs, or unfused `GEMM1 + SwiGLU + scaled_fp4_grouped_quantize + GEMM2` MoE pipelines. This PR adds four warp-specialized Blackwell SM100 CuTe DSL NVFP4 operator modules under `sglang.kernels.ops.gemm` and `sglang.kernels.ops.moe` and integrates them with `DualGemm`, `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod`, and `flashinfer_cutedsl_moe`: 1. **`gemm.nvfp4_dual_gemm_swiglu` (`cutedsl_nvfp4_dual_gemm.py`)**: - Fuses `C = silu(alpha * (A @ B1.T)) * (alpha * (A @ B2.T))` into a single 2-CTA (`256x128x256`, cluster `(2, 1)`, 5-stage) or 1-CTA (`128x128x256` / `128x64x256`) `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::mxf4nvf4` kernel. - Concatenates `sB1` and `sB2` along the N-mode in SMEM so a single `256x256` 2-CTA UMMA computes both gate and up accumulators simultaneously into 512 TMEM columns, cutting `sA` SMEM-to-UMMA descriptor traffic and `SFA` S2T copies (`tcgen05.cp`) in half. - Balances `MUFU.RCP` (`1/4` of pairs) with 2-step `FMA` Newton-Raphson refinement (`3/4` of pairs) in the SwiGLU epilogue. - **1.52x** faster than the strongest `cuBLASLt 13.0` baseline (`Concat[B1;B2]` `torch._scaled_mm` + compiled SwiGLU) in PDL-safe mode, and **2.57x** faster in fast mode

summary: ## Motivation On a hybrid model with `--enable-unified-memory`, a speculative draft whose layers carry recurrent state (for example Inkling-Small's MTP head) stores that state inside each of the target's state slots, so every slot gets wider. title: [Fix] [CPU] kvcache: Validate indices range in store_cache_cpu
summary: ## Motivation `store_cache_cpu` hands the caller-supplied `indices` tensor straight to `store_cache_kernel_impl`, which uses each element as a row index into both KV pools: `k_cache + idx * kc_stride` and `v_cache + idx * vc_stride`, then copies a full row through `copy_stub`. Nothing on this path checks that the index lies inside the pool. The kernel even receives `num_pages` as a parameter and never reads it. An index equal to or past the page count is a deterministic out-of-bounds write one or more rows past the pool end; a negative index writes before the buffer. Under AddressSanitizer, a batch whose third index equals the page count aborts with `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE` inside the row copy performed by `copy_stub`, and the only front-side numeric range check in the production caller is a debug-gated probe that returns immediately unless an opt-in environment variable is set (the caller does validate the physical-location marker of its write locations, but nothing on the default path checks that the numeric index is inside the pool), so the valid range is known to the caller but never enforced where the write happens. ## Modifications * `store_cache_cpu` (`python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/kvcache.cpp`) now validates the whole batch inside the index-type dispatch, before any row pointer is formed and outside the OpenMP region (throwing inside a `at::parallel_for` worker is not safe). summary: This is component 2 of the DFlash adaptive-verification series. Original implementation and component-only review: https://github.com/jianc99/sglang/pull/2. Integration and full-system results: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46182. Updated onto upstream `main` (6a319e7b). All applicable pre-commit checks passed on this branch. title: [Fix] mamba: Never autotune the SSD chunk scan into a config that computes a wrong result
summary: ## Motivation `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`'s autotuner chooses by measured time, and some of its configs do not compute the right answer: on bounded Mamba2 prefill inputs they return non-finite values, or a result that changes between two identical runs. The autotune key is the same in every process, so which config wins is decided by benchmark timing. A server's prefill output then depends on a measurement rather than on its request: the same flags and the same prompts produce correct output in one process and NaN logits in the next. title: [Perf] unified-memory: Stage a fused draft's draft-extend metadata once per draft cycle
summary: ## Motivation A multi-layer EAGLE draft replays one CUDA graph per draft step. When the draft is fused into the unified pool (`--enable-unified-memory`), its FlashAttention backend translates KV ids and so could neither record its draft-extend metadata in the graph nor stage it: every step's replay rebuilt the metadata eagerly first. The steps of a chain extend the same window, so all of those rebuilds produced the same tables: lengths, prefix sums, the translated full and sliding-window page tables, and the sliding-window write ids. In a traced Inkling-Small MTP run on fa4 (TP 8, SM90), the unified pool's draft-extend host time per cycle was twice the default pool's. ## Modifications - A translating FlashAttention backend now stages the draft-extend metadata once per cycle from the cycle's plan (`layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py`). One launch fills the lengths and prefix sums; the page tables come from the plan's read table, which the first step backend builds in place and the others copy; the sliding-window write ids come from the plan, as before. A backend whose reads stay virtual has no plan table to stage from, so it reports no staging support. - The multi-layer runner stages through an explicit `stage_draft_extend_metadata` entry (`layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py`), which Inkling's short-conv wrapper now exposes too (`layers/attention/linear/inkling_sconv_backend.py`). - With staging available, these drafts can take the single combined draft graph, as on the default pool (unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_SINGLE_CG_DRAFT=0`). - On a translating pool the chain stag

title: [Fix] Falcon-H1: run the Mamba2 extend as a graph break in breakable prefill graphs
summary: ## Motivation Falcon-H1's decoder layer calls the Mamba2 backend inline, so a breakable prefill CUDA-graph capture records the Mamba2 extend inside a captured segment. Every replay then reuses the capture-time batch's state slots and chunk metadata rather than the batch being served, with three consequences: - the request's own Mamba state is never written; - the first generated token differs from an eager prefill, and on longer prompts the logits are NaN; - a single server can fault on its first request. On an H20 with `--enable-unified-memory` and the breakable prefill graph on, a server without this change fails with an illegal memory access on its first replay, before serving anything. In a two-role PD run the prefill role serves one request and then dies the same way, leaving the rest of the batch unsent. NemotronH and RadixLinearAttention already route this call through an eager break for the same reason. ## Modifications - `models/falcon_h1.py`: route the Mamba2 extend through an eager break that reads the forward batch live at replay. title: [Fix] unified-memory: Realize the reclaim certificate that relief opens on the tri-pool
summary: ## Motivation On a Mamba + sliding-window model under `--enable-unified-memory`, a decode step could retract a request while the prefix cache held many evictable tokens. The tri-pool chain's decode capacity check calls `ensure_capacity`, then evicts from the tree with `float_reclaim_satisfied` as the stop predicate: the tree skips eviction while the reclaim certificate (the END flushes, or a FLOAT high-side target) says the allocation can already be realized. `ensure_capacity` tries the END and FLOAT certificates once, and when neither holds it falls back to `relieve_for_alloc`. Relief flushes the ENDs and moves FLOAT pages, which can open a FLOAT certificate that was closed when it was checked, while still leaving the allocation short. `ensure_capacity` then returned False without realizing it; the eviction predicate held, so nothing was evicted, and the check failed with the cache full of evictable entries. ## Modifications `ensure_capacity` (`mem_cache/kv/alloc/interim.py`, `_FloatChainPolicy`) now realizes the END or FLOAT certificate once more after a relief that falls short, through one helper, `_realize_token_certificate`, shared with the first attempt. title: [Perf] [AMD] scheduler: Prefill the partial chunk of a long prompt first
summary: ## Motivation With chunked prefill a long prompt runs as whole chunks and then the part that does not fill one. Attention over that short last chunk has the whole prompt as context but under-fills the GPU. On MI355X, AITER's hd256 FP8 prefill kernel runs 24 x ceil(rows / 512) workgroups for Qwen3.8-27B, one per CU at a time, so its time goes in whole waves of 256 workgroups. At 114k tokens of context: 512-5120 rows take 3.9-5.4 ms (one wave), 5632-10752 rows ~10 ms (two), 11264-16384 rows 16-17.8 ms (three). A 1748-token last chunk (a 100k-token prompt with 16384-token chunks) is one wave on 96 of 256 CUs (3.9 ms, vs 1.9 ms at a full chunk's rate per row); a 5364-token one (120k) is a full wave plus 8 workgroups (8.0 ms, vs 5.4 ms for 5120 rows). Run first, the same short chunk attends only to itself and costs almost nothing. ## Modifications - `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFILL_REMAINDER_FIRST=1` (off by default): when a request needs chunking, `PrefillAdder` takes the part of it that does not fill a whole chunk first, rounded up to the page size, `truncation_align_size` and the mamba cut grid, and the rest as whole chunks (the last one short by at most the rounding). Requests that fit whole, or whose length is a multiple of the chunk size, are unchanged. Both admission paths do this: `add_one_req` and the path `ignore_eos` requests take without a radix cache (`add_one_req_ignore_eos`). - The budget a remainder-first chunk leaves can admit requests that fit whole. A second request that needs chunking is not admitted into the same batch (`AddReqResult.OTHER`): the scheduler continues

summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, two of the GDN kernels that run in every decode step leave performance unused: - `_fused_qkvzba_causal_conv1d_update_contiguous_kernel` launches 8 warps per 256-feature block. On 64-lane wavefronts that is 512 lanes for 256 features, so every feature is held twice. It also reloads two state values after the output store. - `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel` streams the whole fp32 recurrent state through the caches. At TP1 that is about 3 MB per request per GDN layer, so roughly 100-800 MB per layer per decode step at batch 32-256. It does the same operations in the same order as the contiguous kernel. The only difference is that it keeps the shifted state values from its first loads instead of reloading them; each lane is the only one touching those elements. title: [Fix] spec: Greedy requests keep the argmax prefill draft under rejection sampling
summary: ## Motivation With rejection sampling on (`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, enabled by default for EAGLE topk 1 on ROCm, where there is no tree-sampling verify kernel), `EagleDraftWorker._draft_extend_for_prefill` draws the first draft token of every request with `fast_sample` from `softmax(logits / T)`. `SamplingParams` turns temperature 0 into temperature 1.0 with top_k 1, so a greedy request's first draft token is sampled at T = 1 instead of taken as the argmax. Every later draft step (`draft_forward`, `_draft_extend_for_decode`) goes through `sample_draft_proposal`, which proposes the argmax for top_k == 1 rows. Greedy output should not depend on the sampler state. The draft distribution passed to the verify is the same `softmax(logits / T)` as before. One call per prefill batch, as before. title: [Perf] gdn: Prefill in place on an envelope-strided state pool
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory` and the page-major layout, the GDN state pool pitches each slot wider than its state, so `conv_states` and `ssm_states` are strided views. `GDNAttnBackend.forward_extend` gathered every prefill's conv and recurrent states into packed copies, ran the kernels on them with identity indices, and scattered both back: two gathers, an arange and two scatters per GDN layer per prefill batch, whatever the batch's length (the `TODO(ch-wan)` in that code). Two of the kernels that round trip protected already address slots by the pool's stride: - GDN prefill reaches the Triton causal conv on CUDA and ROCm (a transposed input with host lengths), which takes every conv-state stride and offsets slots in int64; KDA hands its strided pool to the same kernel. - FlashInfer's GDN prefill gathers each sequence's state by index and writes it back with `index_copy_`, so on a strided pool it ran a second gather and scatter on top of ours. The Triton chunk kernel does not: `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` steps slots by `initial_state.stride(0)`, but its entry point, `ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction.forward`, is wrapped in FLA's `input_guard`, which makes every tensor argument contiguous. On a strided pool it would read the right states and write the final ones into a discarded copy. ## Modifications - `LinearAttnKernelBase.extend_honors_slot_pitch` (default False): the kernel's `extend()` reads and writes each slot's state at the pool's own slot pitch. `FlashInferGDNKernel` sets it; `TritonGDNKernel` sets it False explicitly; other kernels keep the default. -

title: [Fix] scheduler: Reap HiCache events while the engine is paused
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache on (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`, default `write_through`), an RL weight sync runs `pause_generation(mode="retract")`, then `update_weights_from_disk(flush_cache=True)`. The update returns `success=False`: "Weights were updated, but the cache was not flushed because requests are still running or queued. Retract or finish them, then call /flush_cache." The requests are already retracted, and `/flush_cache` fails on every paused iteration, so the only way out is `continue_generation`, which serves the new weights over the old weights' cache. The blocker is not the requests: #40779's paused gate already ignores the requeued ones. It is a HiCache write-through still in `ongoing_write_through` and, with an L3 backend, the prefetch the retract requeue starts for a request with 256 or more uncached tokens. Only `check_hicache_events` retires them, and it runs from the batch getters and `process_decode_queue`, which every paused branch skips. #43758 turned the old assert into this message: the update fails cleanly but cannot succeed while paused. ## Modifications All seven paused branches call `_record_scheduler_state_for_paused_engine()` on each iteration. It now first calls `_process_hicache_events(should_retry_storage_prefetch=False)`: pending acks are reaped before the idle/active record, and no new L3 attempt starts. PD decode reaps only with the decode radix cache, as `process_decode_queue` does. No loop body changes. Considered and rejected: a blocking drain at pause entry, as #30899 and #43282 do. It cannot retire the prefetch the requeue issues

title: [Fix] dsv4/topk_v2: Move the cluster kernels' top-k buffer to dynamic shared memory
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation `topk_v2.cuh` is the JIT-compiled top-k behind `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk`: the top-k of the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention indexer, also used by the GLM k-pool indexer (`topk_transform_kpool_v2`). The cause is two cluster kernels, `topk_small_batch_cluster_kernel` and `topk_candidates_cluster_kernel`. Each declares two static shared-memory buffers: `impl::TopKCluster<C>::Smem`, the cluster selection's scratch (41.6 to 47.2 KiB for cluster size C = 2 to 16), and `int32_t s_topk_indices[kMaxTopK]`, an 8 KiB buffer that stages the selected indices. title: [Fix] ngram: Isolate the speculative corpus by cache namespace
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49626. With `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM`, `NGRAMWorker` keeps one shared `NgramCorpus` per scheduler process. Every request's recent prompt and output tokens are inserted into that trie, and every request drafts from it. `cache_salt` and `extra_key` (including the LoRA id) never reach the corpus. Under default greedy verification, a second tenant that steers its output to a known prefix can draft another tenant's continuation and read the exact match length from `meta_info.spec_num_correct_drafts`. `cache_salt` is the documented per-tenant isolation knob for SGLang's other cache tiers, but it did not apply here. ## Modifications - Derive a per-request XOR mask from `storage_namespace_seed(extra_key, cache_salt)`, the same namespace used by HiCache L3 and related storage paths. - Apply that mask to windows in `NgramCorpus.batch_put` / `batch_get`, and decode draft tokens back before they leave the corpus. - Unnamespaced requests (both `extra_key` and `cache_salt` unset) keep mask `0`, so existing behavior is unchanged. - `NGRAMWorker` passes the request's namespace on the put and get paths. - CPU unit tests cover the original report (cross-salt leak of secret tokens and accept-length oracle), same-namespace matching, LoRA `extra_key` isolation, mixed batches, and the worker wiring. Note: a namespaced request will also not match tokens from an operator-loaded external ngram corpus, because that corpus is stored unnamespaced. I think that is the safer default; I can follow up if we'd rather keep the public external corpus visible across namespaces. ## A

summary: ## Summary This PR is adapted from vLLM PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726. Recall is **exact by construction**. With the per-row affine $b(x) = \lfloor (x - o) \cdot \delta^{-1} \rfloor$ (code: `origin` $= o$, `inv_delta` $= \delta^{-1}$) over negated scores $x = -\text{score}$ (bucket 0 = best), the scan emits exactly $\{\, j : b(x_j) \le \text{th} \,\}$, and every refresh recomputes $\text{th}$ from counts of genuine row elements — so it only ever *tightens* while staying above $b(x_{(k)})$, the bucket of the true k-th best score: $$\text{th}_0 \ge \text{th}_1 \ge \cdots \ge b\big(x_{(k)}\big) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{ j : b(x_j) \le \text{th}_t \} \supseteq \text{top-}k \text{at every } t$$ A stale threshold therefore admits extra candidates but never drops one, and `select` trims the superset exactly. In B200, GLM-5.2 tensors, Q=8192, topk=2048, **1.09–1.25×** over dense logits + top-k at 256K–1M contexts, with **8–32 GB of transient logits memory removed**. title: [Fix] openai: Reject assistant tool calls without a function name (HTTP 500 -> 400)
summary: [by Claude Code] Original authors: @nvpohanh ## Motivation A chat request can carry a conversation history in which an assistant tool call has no function name. title: [Spec] Enable split-KV EAGLE verify on CUDA for the Triton backend
summary: ## Motivation `verify_splitkv_fwd` (the flash-decode style EAGLE target-verify kernel for the Triton backend) is currently gated behind `is_gfx95_supported()`, so it only runs on AMD MI35x. On CUDA the Triton backend's target-verify falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`, whose grid is `(bs, head_num, cdiv(max_len_extend, BLOCK_M))`. At `topk=1` with 4 draft tokens that is **one program per (seq, head)** that walks the whole prefix serially in `BLOCK_N` steps — for a 24-head model, 24 programs vs. the `num_kv_splits=8` × 24 = 192 the regular decode kernel uses for the same prefix. The consequence is that verify cost grows linearly with prefix length and speculative decoding becomes **slower than no-spec beyond ~32k context**, even with a healthy accept length. On a 27B hybrid-GDN model at 128k we measured decode dropping from 31 tok/s (no spec) to 10 tok/s (NEXTN), which is easy to misattribute to the SSM state handling. The kernel itself is already NV-safe (HIP-only launch kwargs are gated on `is_hip()` inside `verify_splitkv.py`, and its own docstring says so), and `test_verify_splitkv.py` is registered on the CUDA CI lane. This PR simply drops the gfx95 gate. `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPLITKV_VERIFY=0` remains as the opt-out. ### Why the gate is gfx95-only today The gate is historical, not technical. In #27382 the kernel originally shipped with **no platform gate**; the NVIDIA CI lane then failed (`test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, `KeyError: Keyword argument waves_per_eu was specified but unrecognised`) because the AMD-only Triton launch hints were passed unconditionally. summary: Stacked on #49370 (#49365 has merged); review only the last five commits. ## Motivation On MI450 (gfx1250), carv2's 2shot_push sends almost the whole tensor across the fabric twice, and the per-vector kernel waits after every scoped store. Above a few MB it loses to RCCL, so large all-reduces (prefill chunks, large-batch decode) fell back to RCCL. This PR adds two gfx1250-only paths so carv2 can take every size up to 4 GB at TP2-8, and tunes the size table for both kernel-argument modes, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0` (the cookbook's) and `=1`. One channel per CU (256 threads, unroll 32) pushes 2 MB slices through a two-slot FIFO in the next rank's memory, behind 64-bit ready/drained counters. The FIFO and its counters live in the same uncached symmetric workspace as the push and pull planes: still one allocation, one rendezvous, and one buffer to release. The ring region is only allocated where the table selects `ring_simple`, about 384 MB per rank at 96 CUs. title: [Perf] attention: Support attention sinks in the split-KV EAGLE verify kernel (gpt-oss)
summary: ## Motivation On the Triton attention backend, EAGLE target verification runs through `extend_attention_fwd`. That is the prefill kernel: one program per (sequence, head) walks the whole prefix serially. `verify_splitkv_fwd` (#27382) replaces it at `topk == 1` with a split-KV (flash-decode) kernel. Two things keep that kernel from serving gpt-oss on NVIDIA: 1. The backend enables it only on AMD gfx95. 2. `can_handle()` rejects attention sinks, and gpt-oss has sinks in every layer. This matters most on NVIDIA SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50xx), where Triton is the default attention backend for gpt-oss. - A torch profile of gpt-oss-120b + `nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-v3` at TP2, batch 1, 8K context: each of the 18 full-attention layers spends ~301 µs in `_fwd_kernel` per verify step, which is 5.4 ms of a 13.9 ms speculative step. - The drafter accepts about half its tokens (accept length ~2.1–2.2 at 2 draft tokens), yet decoding with it was slower than without it. On a closed-loop benchmark with 7.5K-token code prompts, median TPOT at batch 1 was 6.1 ms with the drafter against 4.9 ms without. This PR adds sink support to the split-KV verify kernel. So that it can be reviewed, tested and merged on its own, it also carries the gate change from #39316 as its first commit, with @rluisr as co-author. If #39316 merges first, I will rebase and that commit drops out. ## Modifications Four commits: 1. **Enable split-KV EAGLE verify on CUDA** (based on #39316). `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py` gates `use_verify_splitkv` on `_is_cuda or is_gfx95_supported()`

title: [Feat] diffusion: [sglang-miles] Stop a rollout at a requested step inside the rollout controller
summary: Supersedes #45230: zhihengy's three commits are kept first with their authorship, the rework commits sit on top. #45230 itself is left untouched. ## Motivation radixark/miles_diffusion#331 (DMD2 few-step rollout) asks the engine to stop a rollout at denoising step `i`: run steps `0..i`, send step `i` straight to the terminal sigma, and return `x_i`'s x0 prediction after `i + 1` DiT forwards. #45230 implemented the stop by truncating the sigma grid inside each model's timestep-preparation stage (the base stage and MiniMax H3) and guarding in `prepare_rollout_if_enabled`. That puts a second per-model rollout hookup next to the controller builder, which the rollout framework already treats as the single model-side hookup, and it rewrote the grid of the stage-local scheduler that serving requests share. ## Modifications - `FlowRolloutController` owns the rollout's denoising schedule. It takes the model's full sigma grid and the loop's timesteps from its builder (exactly one sigma past the timesteps), fixes `sigma_max` from the full grid (a stop at step 0 draws the same first-step noise as the full rollout), and `stop_at(i)` keeps `sigmas[:i+1] + [terminal]` and `timesteps[:i+1]`. It steps on its own grid: `transition()` takes `next_sigma` from `self.sigmas[step_index + 1]`, so the scheduler's grid stays whole. `truncate_rollout_sigmas` moves into the controller module. - `rollout_hooks`: the default builder passes `sigmas=scheduler.sigmas` and `timesteps=batch.timesteps` (the loop's published timesteps; Krea-2 feeds its DiT raw sigmas between 0 and 1, not `scheduler.timesteps`)

title: [Fix] lora: [sglang-miles] Keep kv_b_proj adapters off the MHA cached-prefix paths
summary: ## Motivation The DeepSeek/Kimi MHA prefill paths that attend a cached prefix (`forward_mha.py`: `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha`, its packed variant, `_fused_prefix_extend_attn_mha`, `forward_normal_prepare` under `mha_one_shot`) re-project the cached latent through `kv_b_proj` on **prefix rows**. With `kv_b_proj` wrapped by `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, that call runs the LoRA kernels with the forward batch's `LoRABatchInfo`, i.e. the **extend-token** segments. `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` sizes its grid from `max_len × bs` and walks `seg_indptr`/`seg_lens` without looking at `x.shape[0]`: | prefix rows vs. extend tokens | effect | |---|---| | fewer | reads/writes past `x` / `output` / `base_output` → sticky `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`, surfaced at the next launch (`flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:1338` in `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`) | | more | the delta lands on the wrong rows → silently wrong prefix K/V | Only the absorbed MLA path adds the `kv_b_proj` delta per token (`deepseek_mla_correction.apply_q_correction` / `apply_v_correction`). On `trtllm_mla` every extend goes `MHA_CHUNKED_KV` unless `disable_chunked_prefix_cache` is set, so on Blackwell every prefix hit of a `kv_b_proj` adapter takes the broken path; on `fa3`/`flashinfer` it needs ≥ `SGLANG_CHUNKED_PREFIX_CACHE_THRESHOLD` (8192) cached tokens (silent corruption, no crash). With the flag, `trtllm_mla` falls back to the flashinfer MLA implementation for prefix-hit extends (`trtllm_mla_backend.init_forward_metadata`), which is why this is a flag-level rule and not a dispatch-only one. title: [Feat] disaggregation: Support DSA cache layer split with the NIXL transfer backend
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split` is currently limited to the mooncake transfer backend; `model_hook.py` notes that nixl/mori support "will be added later by the community". This PR adds nixl. The shared PD code already does what layer split needs, independent of the backend: the decode pulls from every prefill CP rank, each rank registers only the layers it owns (`prefill_start_layer`), and only the last rank registers the draft's entries. What NIXL lacks is one mapping. Its prepared KV path pairs source and destination entries by position when `pp_size == 1` and neither peer publishes layer ids, and the DSA pool publishes none. A layer split rank would therefore write its layers into the first layers of the decode pool, with no error. ```text decode KV entries: [ L0 ................................ L77 | draft ] CP rank r owns: [ Ls ..... title: [Perf] mrope: Upload M-RoPE decode deltas without blocking the host
summary: ## Motivation `ForwardBatch._compute_mrope_positions_decode` uploads the per-request M-RoPE deltas with `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` from pageable host memory. It runs in `ForwardBatch.init_new` on every decode step that has a multimodal request. - A pageable host-to-device copy can make the host wait for GPU work already queued on the stream. On MI355X, a standalone check on unpatched code queues a long `torch.cuda._sleep` and calls the function: it returns only after the queued work finishes. - Other per-step uploads already use the `async_h2d` helper (#41659). title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: FP8 quantize-dequantize the attention output before wo_a for V4.1-Flash-1017
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017's reference code (`inference/model.py` in the checkpoint) rounds the attention output `o` to FP8 and back before the `wo_a` einsum. The rounding uses `act_quant(o, 32, "ue8m0", ..., inplace=True)`: blocks of 32 values along each group's row, with power-of-two scales. The reference does this in the attention and in the DSpark draft's attention: ```python # wo_a is block-diagonal over groups (each projects only its own heads), hence einsum not # Linear. convert.py dequantizes it to bf16; quantize/dequantize o before einsum. ``` The checkpoint's weights expect the rounded `o`. SGLang's bf16 `wo_a` path skips the step. That is the path 1017 takes: its `weight_block_size` is `[32, 32]`, so `wo_a_fp8_gemm_enabled` is false and `wo_a` is dequantized at load. On 1017 the step changes `o` by 1.8 to 2.6% (relative). ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/o_fp8_qdq.py` (new): an in-place Triton FP8 (e4m3) quantize-dequantize. - Matches the reference: amax floored at 1e-4, scale `2^ceil(log2(amax / 448))`, clamp to ±448, round to e4m3, multiply back. - Uses the hardware e4m3 conversion on sm89 and newer. - Older GPUs get an fp32 emulation of the same rounding: round half to even onto the e4m3 grid, signed zero kept. - `deepseek_v4.py` (`MQALayer`) and `deepseek_v4_dspark.py` (`DSparkAttention`): apply the step on the bf16 `wo_a` path when `SGLANG_DSV4_O_FP8_QDQ_BLOCK` is set. - `environ.py`: two switches. - `SGLANG_DSV4_O_FP8_QDQ_BLOCK` (default 0, off). - `SGLANG_DSV4_O_FP8_QDQ_EMULATE` forces the emulated path, for checking

The whole request then leaves the token path: sgl-router forwards it to the worker as text, and sglang-server serves it through `chat.rs` instead of the lowered path. The gate was added with the lowering in #42999, when the renderers did not dump `defer_loading` yet. The templates that read the flag hide the tool as Python's do, and the parity fixtures' deferred-tool cases match SGLang. The gate was never relaxed. summary: | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Status** | Draft | | **Authors** | TBD | | **Created** | 2026-06-29 | | **RFC doc** | `docs/rfcs/kv-events-hicache-l3-storage-backend.md` (local draft) | | **Related** | [Mooncake RFC #1527](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1527), [Mooncake RFC #1403](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1403), [Dynamo #8912](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/8912), [Dynamo KV Events docs](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kv-managers/kv-events-for-custom-engines), [SGLang HiCache design](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/advanced_features/hicache_design.md) | --- ## Motivation SGLang exposes **KV cache events** so cache-aware routers (e.g. `sgl-router` with the ZMQ cache-aware policy) can index which prefix blocks each worker holds and route requests accordingly. Today this pipeline covers: | Tier | SGLang medium | Event source | | --- | --- | --- | | L1 (GPU HBM) | `GPU` | Radix cache insert / load-back | | L2 (host pinned) | `CPU_PINNED` | HiCache write-through DMA ack | | L3 (distributed storage) | `EXTERNAL` | **Not emitted today** | When HiCache is configured with an L3 storage backend such as **Mooncake**, KV pages are written from host memory to the distributed pool after L2 backup completes. Routers and external indexers (Dynamo KV router, Mooncake standalone indexer) cannot see these blocks unless the engine or the storage backend publishes events for them. This gap breaks end-to-end cache-aware routing in deployments where: - Multiple workers share a Mooncake pool and any worker may prefetch from L3.

title: [Fix] diffusion: Bound VRAM during resident FP8 weight loading
summary: ## Motivation With online FP8 or MXFP8 and a resident DiT, startup can run out of VRAM before quantizing the first layer. title: [Fix] simulator: exclude predictor query time from offline cpu_overhead
summary: Fixes #39042 ## Problem In OFFLINE simulation mode, `C_SchedulerHook` calls the inference-time predictor (`INFERENCE_PREDICTOR.predict_infer_time`), which blocks the host thread. The query cost was accumulated into `TOTAL_PREDICTOR_TIME_COST` for reporting, but `last_real_time_ts` was not advanced by it. Since OFFLINE mode advances no wall clock on its own, the next `cpu_overhead = max(now - last_real_time_ts - blocked_l2_wall_dur, 0.0)` included the predictor query duration, inflating the simulated clock. This caused up to ~41% TTFT error for short prompts — the predictor query time was counted as scheduler CPU overhead instead of simulation work (see #39042 for the measured breakdown). BLOCKING mode was unaffected: `time.sleep(abs(predicted_latency))` plus `set_last_real_time_ts(now)` already advances the real clock past the query. ## Fix In the OFFLINE `else` branch, advance `last_real_time_ts` by `predictor_time_cost` so the query time is excluded from the subsequent `cpu_overhead` computation. The extracted `predictor_time_cost` is reused for both the `TOTAL_PREDICTOR_TIME_COST` accumulator and the timestamp advance. ## Tests Two focused unit tests in `test_simulation_offline_blocking.py` using a virtual clock (no real sleeps, no GPU, no model): - `test_predictor_cost_excluded_from_cpu_overhead` (parametrized OFFLINE/BLOCKING): asserts `cpu_overhead` per iteration equals only the non-predictor CPU work (gap + run + process = 0.09s), regardless of a 0.3s predictor query, in both modes. - `test_offline_token_latency_independent_of_predictor_query_duration`: sweeps predic

title: [Fix] scheduler: Reserve member rows of beam leaders admitted in the same prefill
summary: ## Motivation With beam search, the scheduler can crash with this assertion when a beam request shares a prefill with other requests and req-to-token rows are scarce: ``` AssertionError: Beam member spawn needs 2 req-to-token slots but only 1 are free; the admission gate (get_num_allocatable_reqs) must reserve them. ``` How it happens: 1. A `beam_width=k` leader takes one req-to-token row at admission. It spawns its `k-1` member rows later, at its prefill relay. 2. `get_num_allocatable_reqs` subtracts `pending_member_rows(running_batch)`, which covers groups that are already running. It does not cover leaders already admitted to the prefill being built (`adder.can_run_list`). 3. A later candidate in the same pass then fits into rows the leader has promised to its members. When the leader's prefill relays, `_spawn_member_rows` finds too few free rows and the assertion takes the scheduler down. Example: with 3 free rows, a `beam_width=3` leader is admitted (it needs 3 rows in total), then a plain request is admitted too, because the gate still sees 3 free rows for 2 requests. The rows only bind when the running batch is near `max_running_requests`, so this shows up under load. ## Modifications - `BeamCoordinator.pending_member_rows_of(reqs)`: the existing `pending_member_rows(batch)` over a request list. `pending_member_rows` now calls it. - `get_num_allocatable_reqs` takes `admitted_reqs` and also subtracts their pending member rows from the row budget. The admission loop passes `can_run_list`. - `test_scheduler_held_row_admission.py`: its coordinator stub gains `pending_mem

title: [Feat] [NPU] ascend_bench: config-driven benchmark sweeps with SLA gating
summary: ## Summary `ascend_bench` is a self-contained sweep tool that automates launch → warm up → benchmark → verify → rank for SGLang deployments, with first-class support for Ascend NPU hosts. One YAML file describes the whole sweep: server argument grid, workload grid, SLA thresholds, and repeat policy. It was built to establish reproducible NPU performance baselines and to support regression verification (hiascend community task "[SGLang] sglang 自动化基准测试能力建设", issue #1103), but the core is hardware-agnostic: `asc_bench/` imports neither `torch` nor `sglang` (enforced by a unit test), and all NPU awareness is isolated in a single module (`asc_bench/npu.py`). ## What it does - **Config-driven sweeps** — cartesian product over `server.axes` and `workload.axes`; every YAML key is a literal `sglang.launch_server` / `sglang.bench_serving` CLI flag. Validation aggregates all errors and rejects Ascend-unsafe configs up front (e.g. `--cuda-graph-bs` > 10 entries → graph-capture stream-conflict crash 507000). - **Hard HBM gate** — after each cell the server process group is killed and `npu-smi info` is polled until per-device HBM is back within a budget of the pre-run baseline; stragglers are SIGKILLed and the cell is flagged `failed_hbm` instead of poisoning the sweep with phantom OOMs. - **SLA filtering + variance-gated ranking** — cells violating any percentile threshold are eliminated; survivors are ranked by output throughput (TPOT p99 tiebreak); repeats report mean ± std and cells with CV above `cv_max` are marked unrankable. - **Accuracy smoke gate** — optional per-cell gsm8k run

title: [Fix] [AMD] kv-cache: Reject unsupported FP8 E5M2 requests
summary: ## Motivation On HIP, an explicit `fp8_e5m2` KV cache request currently resolves to the platform's E4M3 `fp8_dtype`. The requested FP8 format is silently changed, including when selected through the draft KV cache override. Reject this unsupported configuration with an actionable error rather than silently substituting another format. Related validation in #18625 concerns FlashAttention 3; this change addresses the HIP dtype resolver and target/draft argument validation. ## Modifications - Reject `fp8_e5m2` in HIP cache compatibility checks for both `--kv-cache-dtype` and `--speculative-draft-kv-cache-dtype`, suggesting `fp8_e4m3` instead. - Add the same rejection in the runtime resolver after applying any draft override. - Add CPU regressions for rejection, supported HIP formats, draft override precedence, and preservation of E5M2 resolution on non-HIP platforms. ## Accuracy Tests ```sh PYTHONPATH=python HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_dtype.py \ test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py \ -k 'TestHipKvCacheDtype or TestKvCacheDtype' -q ``` Focused result: **6 passed, 11 subtests passed**. Before the fix, five target/draft rejection cases failed because no error was raised. The complete KV dtype, fused-draft placement, and server-argument suites now pass: **417 passed, 293 subtests passed**. Earlier local import failures were resolved by installing the missing dependencies. An original-versus-fixed resolver matrix covered **31,104 combinations**: **29,952 identical outcomes** and **1,152 intentional HIP E5M2 rejec

title: [Refactor] scheduler: Remove the remaining direct request-list edits
summary: Follows #49677. The functions the ratchet still allowed to edit a request list directly now go through `move` or the retirer, and the ratchet allows none. The final picture: ```text move(reqs, dst) new req ------------------------> [ list A ] ---+ | ^ | release / abort / move | | move | retire_unadmitted / v | | abort_retracted [ list B ] ---+---------------------> ended | a release that raised -------+-- abandon ----------> ended (frees nothing; raises in CI) [ DEFERRED ] ---- settle_output ----> output sent (released before it) req.owner_list names the one list a request is in (#49623). ``` | Exit | When | Gives back | |---|---|---| | `release` | a request ends | its KV, row and buffers | | `abort`, `retire_unadmitted` | a request is aborted, or refused at intake | the same, through `release`, after sending the abort | | `abort_retracted` | a retracted request is not requeued | the rest; the retraction freed the KV | | `abandon` (new) | a release raised before taking the request out | nothing; logged, and raised in CI | | `settle_output` (new) | a released request's deferred output is sent or aborted | nothing; its release did | | Check | Where | Catches | |---|---|---| | Ratchet | `test_request_list.py` | any direct list edit or `owner_list` write outside `request_list.py` and `request_retirer.py`, in the source and the test trees (tests go through `move` and one shared retirer double) | | Second list | `_join`, always on | a request joining a list while still in another | | Ended but unlisted | CI idle check | a kept request in no list that never sent its output or exit

title: [Feat] unified-memory: Keep a fused draft through HiCache
summary: Stacked on #46381 ([Feat] unified-memory: Fuse MLA drafts into MLA hosts); only the last commit is new here. ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory`, a fused draft's KV lives in the target's entries, so HiCache has to keep those rows together with the target's. #45700 does this for a fused DFLASH draft on a hybrid sliding-window target: the target's L2 page envelopes copy whole pages, draft parts included, so the draft needs no host pool of its own. The check verifies, at registration, that every draft pool shares the target's unified buffer and that both host envelopes are page envelopes. A DFLASH draft keeps its full-attention-only rule. - On a Mamba host the host pool copies rows layer by layer. title: [Perf] unified-memory: Clear Mamba slots without a host sync
summary: Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. It no longer stacks on #46379 or #46378, both closed. ## Motivation `UnifiedMambaPool.clear_slots` (whole entries) and `UnifiedDraftMambaPool.clear_slots` (a fused draft's state block) zeroed slots as `view[idx] = 0`. With device indices that is `index_put_` with a 0-dim host value, which copies the value to the device from pageable memory: a `cudaMemcpyAsync` plus a `cudaStreamSynchronize` per view. A fused draft clears its block after every prefill's draft extend, once per draft runner and state view. Inkling-Small's MTP draft fuses 8 runners of 6 conv state streams each, so every admitting forward stalled the scheduler about 48 times, and serving traces on the unified pool showed about four times the default pool's stream synchronizes, nearly all of them here. ## Modifications - Both clears now zero with `index_fill_` (a device-side scalar fill; indices cast to int64 where they are not already), which writes the same bytes: strided views, whole-entry uint8 rows, int32 and duplicate indices, and an empty temporal stream behave as before (`mem_cache/unified_memory_pool.py`, `mem_cache/unified_draft_pool.py`). The slot siblings' own resets are unchanged. The default `MambaPool` already zeroes without a host value. Test (CUDA), `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_handout_zeroing.py`: `TestMambaSlotClearStaysOnDevice` clears a fused host and draft state pool under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`, which raises on a synchronizing operation, and checks the cleared and the spared slots. title: [Fix] trtllm_mha: Pack the plan's page tables on the graphs-off path
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory`, trtllm_mha's graphs-off forwards read the iteration's translated page tables from its `IterationIds` plan. FlashInfer's XQA decode and fmha_v2 prefill are handed only the table's data pointer and take its row length from its width (`max_seq_len = width * page_size` for XQA, `block_tables.shape[1]` for fmha_v2); they ignore its strides. The plan's table is packed when a graphs-off read is the first to build it. When an earlier reader in the same iteration is a captured CUDA graph, the table is built inside that graph's capture-stable buffer. If the batch's host-side sequence lengths make the table narrower than the buffer, the plan's table is a column view of a wider tensor. One plan serves a speculative iteration's draft steps, verify and draft extend, so graph-backed drafting followed by an eager draft extend reads such a view. Today that read stops on the assert that the tables are packed ("trtllm_mha reads its page tables as packed rows, but the plan's table is a strided view of a wider buffer"). This is reachable in serving: on SM90, Qwen3.5-9B with NEXTN on `--attention-backend trtllm_mha`, the non-overlap scheduler and `SGLANG_DISABLE_DRAFT_EXTEND_CUDA_GRAPH=1` stops on that assert on every unified-memory server. Under the overlap scheduler the draft plan carries no host-side lengths, so its table keeps the captured width and the assert does not fire. ## Modifications - The graphs-off path in `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` now packs both of its tables, full-attention and sliding-window, with `.contiguous()`: a copy only when the pl

title: [Fix] flashinfer: Read a replayed draft extend's whole sliding window
summary: ## Motivation An EAGLE draft extend writes `num_tokens_per_req` rows per request, the accepted ones first, and each row attends over its own sliding window. Planned eagerly, FlashInfer's window wrapper starts its read a window before the first of those rows. Replayed from a CUDA graph, the draft extend plans without prefix lengths, and `update_sliding_window` derived them as `seq_lens - num_accept_tokens`, as if only the accepted rows were queries. The read then started up to `num_tokens_per_req - num_accept_tokens` tokens too late: once a sequence is longer than the window plus the accepted tokens, accepted row j lost up to `num_tokens_per_req - num_accept_tokens - j` of the earliest keys in its window. This hits a draft with sliding-window layers (for example an EAGLE3 draft run with `--speculative-draft-window-size`) on FlashInfer with draft-extend CUDA graphs on, on any KV pool. The draft's proposals change; the target still verifies every token. This PR used to carry wider FlashInfer and TRTLLM MHA window support and backend allow-list changes. Upstream's unified-memory rewrite absorbed those, and this one replay fix is what remains. ## Modifications A draft-extend input now plans the window from `seq_lens - num_tokens_per_req`, the read its eager plan makes (`layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py`). Tests: - CPU, `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_draft_extend_window.py`: a graph replay and an eager plan of the same draft extend read the same window for every row (lengths [12, 5, 12] for a window of 8 and four rows per request); on main the replay

title: [Fix] triton: Size a captured draft extend by the runner's width
summary: ## Motivation The multi-layer EAGLE draft-extend CUDA graph (`--enable-multi-layer-eagle`) lays out each request's draft tokens plus its boundary-KV front rows (`speculative_num_steps - 1` plus the conv warmup rows; 4 + 5 = 9 rows per request for Inkling-Small at 3 steps) and stamps that width on `spec_info.num_tokens_per_req`. The Triton attention backend's captured draft extend ignored it: `_update_draft_extend_buffers` strided `qo_indptr` by `num_draft_tokens`, and the captured metadata took the same number as `max_extend_len`, so every request after the first was read at the wrong rows. The output stays correct, because verification rejects the bad drafts, but the drafts degrade: with CUDA graphs on, an Inkling-Small MTP head on Triton accepts 1.51 tokens per step instead of about 2.92, on both the default and the unified-memory pool. With CUDA graphs off, and on the FlashAttention backends, the width is read from the batch and is right. ## Modifications - New `TritonAttnBackend._draft_extend_num_tokens_per_req`: the stamped `spec_info.num_tokens_per_req` when it is set (positive), else the previous rule (`num_draft_tokens` for the V2 draft extend, `speculative_num_steps + 1` otherwise), as the target-verify width already does. - `_update_draft_extend_buffers` (the `qo_indptr` filled before replay) and the captured draft-extend metadata (`max_extend_len`) both take the width from it. - A graph replays only when the batch's stamped width equals its captured one, and the plain EAGLE draft-extend graph captures exactly `num_draft_tokens`, so nothing else changes. title: [Fix] unified-memory: Refuse an MXFP8 KV cache at boot
summary: ## Motivation `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` (SM100 and newer) stores the KV cache as fp8 rows plus a scale factor per 32-element block. The default pool keeps both in `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, and the FA4 MXFP8 attention path reads the scales from the pool. The unified memory pool (`--enable-unified-memory`) builds only the fp8 rows: `MHAView` leaves `k_scale_buffer` and `v_scale_buffer` as `None`. So the combination passes the boot checks and has no scale buffers for the kernel to read. The FP4 KV cache already refuses `--enable-unified-memory` at boot for the same reason (`handle_kv4_compatibility`). ## Modifications - `handle_mxfp8_kv_cache_compatibility` (`arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`) now raises a `ValueError` when `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` is combined with `--enable-unified-memory`, after its existing SM100 check. The message names the flag and the reason. MXFP8 without unified memory is unchanged. Test (CPU), `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: `TestMXFP8KVCacheCompatibility::test_mxfp8_rejects_unified_memory` overrides the platform to SM100 and checks that mxfp8 alone resolves and that mxfp8 with `--enable-unified-memory` raises. It fails on main and passes with this PR. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: the change refuses a configuration while resolving server arguments. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable.
