title: [Fix] mla: Attend each draft step's own tokens on flashinfer_mla, flashmla and trtllm_mla
summary: ## Motivation An EAGLE chain draft writes step i's token at the committed length plus i, and `draft_forward` passes every step the same committed `seq_lens`. So each step of a multi-step draft backend has to read the committed prefix plus its own i + 1 draft tokens, as fa3 (`speculative_step_id`) and triton already do. Three MLA backends read fewer: - FlashMLA and TRT-LLM MLA (and cutedsl_mla, which inherits from it) gave the kernel the committed length. FlashMLA's block table could also stop a page short. - FlashInfer MLA's multi-step backend packs the right indices, but neither path planned them. The eager decode never passed the step its `spec_info`, so it packed and planned the committed prefix again. Graph replay planned host lengths and offsets from the committed `seq_lens_cpu`, so each request's window was short and every later request's segment started at the wrong place in the packed indices. So every draft step left out its own token and the earlier steps' drafts. The target still verifies every draft token, so outputs stay valid; this corrects the draft's attention window. It does not raise acceptance: see Accuracy Tests. ## Modifications - The draft step id now lives on the FlashInfer MLA backend, which the other three subclass, and their multi-step backends give each step backend its id. - A draft step's decode adds its tokens to the key lengths, the scheduler metadata, the block-table width and FlashInfer's host plan; FlashInfer's eager step plans the indices its multi-step backend packed. This covers the eager path and CUDA graph replay, including the DCP rep

title: [Fix] eplb: Reject expert distribution record calls when the recorder is disabled
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #42071. Without `--expert-distribution-recorder-mode`, `/start_expert_distribution_record`, `/stop_expert_distribution_record` and `/dump_expert_distribution_record` reach the noop recorder, which raises inside the scheduler's event loop. The scheduler dies and takes the server with it. ## Modifications - `Scheduler.expert_distribution_handle` returns `success=False` with a message when the recorder mode is unset, instead of calling the noop recorder. The check runs in the scheduler because the mode can be resolved at startup (e.g. `--enable-eplb` sets `stat`), and it is the same check `ExpertDistributionRecorder.init_new` uses. - `ExpertDistributionReqOutput` gains `success` and `message`; the defaults keep the old shape. - The tokenizer merges per-DP-rank replies; any failed rank fails the request. - The HTTP routes return 400 with the message. - `Engine.start/stop/dump_expert_distribution_record` now raise `RuntimeError` when the recorder is disabled. Before, the call crashed the server. ## Tests `test/registered/unit/managers/test_expert_distribution_control.py` (CPU). It is a separate file because it imports the scheduler and the HTTP server, which `test_tokenizer_control_mixin.py` avoids. title: [Feature] [Intel] weight-cache: Support the weight cache daemon on Intel XPU
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation # [Feature] [Intel] weight-cache: Support the weight cache daemon on Intel XPU ### Motivation The weight cache daemon ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)) holds post-quantized weights in GPU memory and hands them to a restarting engine over IPC. This cuts weight load from minutes to under a second. Today the daemon runs only on CUDA and ROCm. On Intel XPU it is rejected at startup, and lifting that check is not enough: its IPC transport cannot share an XPU tensor between processes. **Request:** support `--weight-cache-mode daemon|client` with `--device xpu`, with the same guarantees as on CUDA. Attaching should take under a second, and the weights should match a disk load byte for byte. This issue is the XPU part of the roadmap in [#33522](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33522). Intel will implement and validate it on Arc Pro B60 (Battlemage) and Crescent Island. title: [Bug] DeepSeek chunked-prefix prefill merges base-2 LSE into a natural-log merge_state_v2 (silent accuracy loss on every prefix-cache hit)
summary: ### Summary On the DeepSeek MLA chunked-prefix prefill path, the per-chunk log-sum-exp values produced by the ragged attention kernels are in **base 2**, while `merge_state_v2` (and the Triton fallback) combine them with a **natural-log** formula. Nothing converts in between, so every prefix-cache hit merges the chunks with the wrong weights: the long cached prefix is over-weighted by 2^(0.4427·Δ) relative to the new tokens. This is silent — no error, no warning, plausible-looking output — and on Blackwell it is on by default, because `trtllm_mla` is the auto-selected backend for `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` on sm100 and it takes the chunk-and-merge path on *every* extend with a non-empty prefix. ### Where - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py`, `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha()`: calls `merge_state(output, lse, accum_output, accum_lse, ...)` with the LSE exactly as the backend returned it. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/merge_state.py` → `sgl_kernel.merge_state_v2`, else `merge_state_triton`. The Triton kernel is explicit about the convention it assumes: `out_se = tl.exp(p_lse) + tl.exp(s_lse)`, `out_lse = tl.log(out_se) + max_lse`. - No backend converts on the way out: `grep -n "log2\|1.4427\|LOG2E" python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py` is empty. Verified on `main` at `2d25767`, and reproduced at runtime on 0.5.15.post1 and 0.5.19. vLLM hits the same kernels and converts per backend, which is presumably why it does not show the problem: `log2_lse_to_ln` (defined in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py`) is app

title: [Perf] [AMD] MiniMax-M3: Remove small kernel launches from the sparse KV cache write

The profiled decode step is 9.2% shorter, output throughput is 1.9% to 8.0% higher at concurrency 4–64, and GSM8K is unchanged (mean 0.978 in both arms). ## Modifications - **A. title: [Feat] [Intel] diffusion: Run ConvRot INT8 linears on native sgl-kernel-xpu ops
summary: ## Motivation On Intel XPU, `convrot_int8` (both online and serialized Comfy ConvRot INT8) currently runs through `comfy_kitchen`. On XPU that path launches 44–50 kernels per linear. sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#589 adds two native BMG ops: `convrot_rotate_quantize` (H256 rotation + per-row INT8 quantization) and `convrot_int8_linear_prequant` (INT8 GEMM with fused scaling and bias). This PR makes SGLang dispatch to them. On MiniMax-H3, the INT8 linears run about 3.5x faster and end-to-end latency drops by 24–28%. Depends on sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#589. Bump the `sglang-kernel-xpu` pin in `pyproject_xpu.toml` after that kernel is released. If an older kernel is installed, loading fails with a rebuild hint. ## Modifications - New `xpu` backend for `convrot_int8`, implemented as `ConvRotInt8XpuLinearMethod`. Each linear calls the two native ops. It is used for online quantization, for serialized Comfy ConvRot INT8 checkpoints, and for the INT8 layers of mixed NVFP4/INT8 checkpoints. - With `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CONVROT_INT8_BACKEND=auto` on XPU, the backend resolves to `xpu`. `jit` and `comfy_kitchen` are refused on XPU, so there is no silent fallback. title: [Tracking] Pipeline parallelism x speculative decoding (EAGLE/MTP): converge prefill gate PRs, make the path model-agnostic, decide decode design
summary: ## Motivation Pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding are still gated off against each other, but the pieces to lift the gate have been landing and are now in flight from several authors with overlapping scope. This issue tracks the work so the remaining PRs can converge on one design instead of a per-model allowlist. Concrete use case: PD-disaggregated serving of large hybrid MoE models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 / DeepSeek / GLM) where the prefill role runs PP (e.g. PP4 for the InferenceMAX AgentX recipe) and the decode role uses MTP. Today the prefill role only starts with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1` to skip the assertion, or with one of the model-specific gate PRs below. ## What is already model-agnostic (merged) Since #35758 the prefill-side runtime does not depend on the model: - The draft worker is created only on the last PP stage (`EAGLEWorkerV2._hosts_draft`); other stages return proxy tensors so scheduler dispatch stays rank-uniform. - `scheduler_pp_mixin` carries the draft output (`draft_topk_p`, `draft_topk_index`, `draft_hidden_states`) along the PP ring and rebinds it as `batch.spec_info` on stage 0 so the PD result contains it. ## What is still model-specific today **1. Last-stage draft embedding (the only hard dependency).** `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` calls `target.get_embed_and_head()`. On the last stage `embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` for most targets (`deepseek_v2`, `llama`, `glm4_moe`, ...), so `.weight` raises. Two different fixes exist: - Qwen3.5 (#37471, merged): the draft keeps its own embedding and `qwen3_5_mtp.load_weights` loads it from the target

title: [Refactor] scheduler: Add the guards for aborting a request on receipt
summary: Aborting a request on receipt will finish it, release what it holds and take it out of its list at once, even while a launched step still carries it. This adds the CPU-side guards that needs: - **MLX overlap loop**: a chained decode launches only if every request of the pending step is still in `running_reqs`, so a request taken out since the launch never runs again on a released row. Today every such request is still running here: an abort only marks it, and a finish breaks the chain first. - **Session close**: a turn holding media counts as a reader while it is unfinished or a launched step still carries it (`inflight_steps > 0`). - **dLLM results**: `process_batch_result_dllm` asserts overlap scheduling is off. It commits every row without a membership check, so no step may be in flight when a request leaves; dLLM already turns overlap off. The PD prefill result processor and `ScheduleBatch.filter_batch` keep their `is_aborted` / `finished()` checks: an abort on receipt still finishes the request, so those checks hold until the flags themselves go. No behavior change, except: - Under overlap scheduling, closing a session right after a turn with media finished, while a launched step still carries that turn, now defers the close until that step is processed and the next session reap runs (about a second at most). Until then the session id cannot be reopened, as with a close deferred by an unfinished turn. Tests: `test_no_chain_after_a_request_left_running` (MLX) and `test_close_waits_for_a_finished_reader_a_step_still_carries` (session) fail on main; the MLX and dLLM fixtu

title: [Bug] SM12x: block-fp8-as-MXFP8 gate (k%32) is looser than b12x dispatch (K%128); K%128!=0 layers regress silently

title: [Feat] kv-cache: Observability and Logging capabilities enhancement for HiCache
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This PR addresses the remaining observability gap identified in #35808. Currently, when a cache read fails, operators cannot distinguish between: - **"Data not present"** (capacity eviction / cache miss) - **"Data present but read failed"** (transfer error / corruption) `UnifiedRadixCache` records some prefetch outcomes internally, but the default collector does not export them. A `batch_exists` hit followed by a failed `batch_get*` is only logged—not exposed as a metric[reference:5]. This makes it difficult to diagnose whether cache hit rate degradation is caused by capacity pressure or underlying transfer failures. This PR closes this gap by: 1. **Adding Prometheus counters** for cross-tier transfer failures (L1→L2, L2→L3, and reverse), with bounded `op` and `result` labels for low-cardinality classification. 2. **Adding structured logs** containing `rid` (request ID) to trace a single request's KV cache flow across the entire L1 GPU → L2 Host → L3 Storage hierarchy, aligned with the proposal in #35808[reference:6]. title: [Feat] [AMD] mori: MORI EPv2 AsyncLL dispatch/combine, with shared experts overlapped under SBO
summary: ## Motivation MORI EPv2 currently runs only its native dispatch/combine, which finishes the whole transfer inside one call, so nothing can run while tokens move. MORI's AsyncLL kernels (ROCm/mori#768) split each transfer into a send and a receive half, and with `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1` move the tokens on the copy engine instead of CUs. This PR drives those kernels from SGLang and uses them for single-batch overlap (`--enable-single-batch-overlap`). On AMD, SBO runs the shared experts in the dispatcher's dispatch hook, between `dispatch_a` and `dispatch_b`. With the send in `dispatch_a` and the receive in `dispatch_b`, the shared experts now overlap the transfer. title: [Feat] kimi-k3: add video support via frame sampling
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 and K3.1 support video natively: MoonViT carries temporal position embeddings and pools `temporal_merge_kernel_size` frames into one frame's tokens, and the checkpoint's `preprocessor_config.json` ships the video sampling keys. This PR adds video input for Kimi-K3/K3.1 through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses APIs. Videos are sampled into timestamped 4-frame chunks and served through the existing image path. ## Modifications - **Chat encoding:** each `video_url` part gets an ordered media slot, so images and videos keep their prompt order. title: [Fix] [AMD] custom_all_reduce: skip IPC setup on ROCm when it cannot be selected
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` only selects the custom all-reduce when the GPUs are fully connected by XGMI or the deterministic 1-stage kernel is enabled. Without either, `__init__` still allocates the meta/data buffers and exports IPC handles, although the result is never used. That setup fails when `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`: `self.buffer` comes from the caching allocator, so it is VMM-backed (`hipMemCreate`/`hipMemMap`), and `hipIpcGetMemHandle` on it returns `invalid argument`. `CUDACHECK` then calls `exit()`, so the process dies during distributed init. The SGLang Diffusion CI cases for MiniMax-H3 set this allocator option. Observed with SGLang Diffusion, MiniMax-H3 t2va, TP2 on two PCIe Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201): ``` Failed: Cuda error .../csrc/allreduce/custom_all_reduce.hip:152 'invalid argument' ``` Single-GPU check of the failing call (`sgl_kernel.allreduce.get_meta_buffer_ipc_handle`): | buffer | `hipIpcGetMemHandle` | |---|---| | `hipMalloc` / `hipExtMallocWithFlags` (default, fine-grained, uncached, contiguous) | ok | | `torch.empty`, `expandable_segments:False` | ok | | `torch.empty`, `expandable_segments:True` | `invalid argument` | ## Modifications - `CustomAllreduce.__init__`: on ROCm, when the GPUs are not fully XGMI-connected and the deterministic implementation is off, return early as disabled. `should_custom_ar()` returns `False` in this case anyway, so the selected all-reduce (RCCL) does not change; only the unused IPC setup is skipped. - New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_

title: [Doc] hicache: Document buffer_only anchor-lock cap and DP-attention scaling of schedule conservativeness
summary: ## Motivation Two knobs that matter a lot when serving long-context agentic traffic with DP attention and HiCache `buffer_only` are not explained in the docs. We had to read the code to understand both while benchmarking GLM-5.3 W4AFP8 on 8×H200 (Dynamo router, HiCache + Mooncake L3, context up to 300k tokens): 1. **`--schedule-conservativeness` is multiplied by 0.3 when DP attention is on** (`arg_groups/parallel_hook.py`, `_handle_data_parallelism`). The default 1.0 therefore runs as 0.3, and the guidance in `hyperparameter_tuning.mdx` ("decrease to 0.3", "increase to 1.3") reads differently for DP-attention deployments. We only noticed after reading the code; we now pass 3.33 so that the resolved value in the `server_args` log is 0.999. 2. **`SGLANG_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK_CAP`** (default 0.5) bounds the device tokens pinned by staged L3 prefetches in `buffer_only` mode. It is documented only by a comment in `environ.py`, and `buffer_only` itself has no section in `hicache_best_practices.mdx`. title: [Fix] [AMD] minimax: Run the gfx950 Gluon sparse prefill with several KV heads per rank
summary: ## Motivation The fastest MiniMax-M3.1 prefill layout on MI355X is pipeline parallel at TP1: PP4 x TP1 gives each GPU 15 whole layers and no per-layer all-reduce, and it is the prefill side of PD (#49753, #49767). Each rank then holds all 4 KV heads, but the gfx950 Gluon sparse prefill only takes one KV head per rank, which is what TP4 gives. With several KV heads on a rank: - the NVFP4 KV, which is the default under DSpark and therefore on a DSpark PD prefill, raises `NotImplementedError: NVFP4 KV sparse prefill runs only on the gfx950 Gluon path (...)`. The server dies at startup, during the prefill CUDA graph capture (reproduced with the cookbook's MI355X command at `--tp 2`). - an fp8 KV warns and falls back to the Triton sparse prefill, about 2x slower per layer. The gate is the KV head count per rank, so TP below 4 and attention DP, which the M3.1 ROCm override also accepts, hit it the same way. ## Modifications - `gluon_sparse_prefill` takes several KV heads per rank. It runs them head by head, each over its GQA group of q heads, as the existing single-head prefill on a strided one-head view of the pool. One KV head per rank (TP4) takes the unchanged path. - On the pair kernel the forward metadata is built once per layer. Each head reads its q slice and writes its O slice in place, or its slice of the fp8 O and scales for the `o_proj`. The new `pair_sparse_prefill_into` takes those caller-owned views, and `pair_sparse_prefill` now wraps it. - NVFP4 page rows give each head a view of its own payload and scales. title: [Perf] attention: Let SM12x FA4 split KV outside the architecture decode policy
summary: ## Motivation On SM12x every FA4 call outside the architecture-owned decode policy runs with `num_splits=1`. With radix caching most extends are a few dozen new tokens over a long cached prefix, so a full-attention layer launches q-tiles x kv-heads CTAs (one request, one KV head) and reads the whole prefix serially. title: [Fix] attention: Return zeros instead of NaN from merge_state_v2 when both states are empty
summary: ## Motivation The Triton path is covered by #48796; this fixes the CUDA kernel. `merge_state_v2` (`kernels/aot/csrc/attention/merge_attn_states.cu`) combines two partial attention states using their log-sum-exp values. When a token is empty on both sides (both LSEs `-inf`, or `+inf`, which the kernel maps to `-inf`), `max_lse` is `-inf`, `-inf - (-inf)` makes both scales NaN, and the kernel writes NaN to the output and LSE. On sglang-kernel 0.4.10 (NVIDIA L4), a both-empty token gives NaN in every output element. vLLM carries the same kernel and fixed this case in #28181. SGLang callers work around empty KV in places (e.g. #22688 for trtllm MLA chunked prefill), but the kernel itself still returns NaN. #48796 (open) rewrites the Triton `merge_state` with the same both-empty behaviour; no open PR I found touches `merge_attn_states.cu`. ## Modifications - `merge_attn_states.cu`: for a both-empty token, write zeros to the output and keep its LSE at `-inf`, so a later merge still sees an empty state. The kernel returns early for that case; other tokens are untouched. - Zeros match an empty softmax, vLLM's Triton (#49294) and torch fallback paths, and #48796's Triton kernel. vLLM's CUDA kernel (#28181) copies `prefix_output` instead (zeros whenever the caller zeroed it); easy to switch if you prefer that. - Test: `test_merge_state_v2_both_empty` in `kernels/aot/tests/test_merge_state_v2.py` runs `merge_state_v2` (float32, float16, bfloat16) on a batch with two both-empty tokens (one via `+inf`) and checks no NaN, zeros and `-inf` LSE on those tokens, and the torch reference on t

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Fuse MXFP8 quant into the small MoE sort
summary: ## Motivation While DeepSeek-V4.1 writes tokens, every MoE (mixture-of-experts) layer runs two small GPU jobs one after the other: one sorts the tokens by expert, and the next one compresses them to 8-bit numbers. This PR does both in one job. Each output token then comes 1.5 to 2.6% faster at 1 to 32 users. No other open PR is needed. In decode, AITER's MoE sorts the routed tokens and, with fp8 activations, quantizes the stage-1 input to MXFP8. Main fuses that quant into the small MoE sort only when `hidden % 2048 == 0`, and its bitonic sort kernel (#44004) runs only without the quant, so DeepSeek-V4.1 (hidden 5120, E 385, top 7) runs two launches in every MoE layer. This PR fuses them for hidden sizes that are multiples of 1024, with bitwise tests against AITER. ## Modifications - `moe_sorting_small.py`: the `fused_moe` gate passes the activations to the sort when `hidden % 1024 == 0` (was 2048), and the bitonic kernel also writes the quant (fp8 rows and e8m0 scales, with AITER's layout and math). For DeepSeek-V4.1 (E 385 = 384 routed + 1 fused shared expert, top 7), the sort and the quant become one launch up to 36 rows. - Below 512 experts, the quant path takes the bitonic kernel above 32 pairs. From 512 experts on, it keeps main's kernels: at Qwen3.5's E 513 / top 11, the bitonic kernel with the quant was 4.7 to 5.2% slower at 3 to 5 rows. - `test_moe_sorting_small.py`: E 385 / top 7 sorting, quant bytes and scales bitwise against AITER at hidden 5120, the 36 / 37-row cutoff, and a new `test_fused_moe_a8w4_stage1_matches_aiter`: AITER `fused_moe` at DeepSeek-V4.1's TP4

title: [Feat] [NPU] weight-cache: Add NPU weight cache support
summary: ## Motivation The weight cache (`--weight-cache-mode=daemon|client`) shares preloaded weights with serving engines through zero-copy IPC, but it was gated as CUDA-alike only: the daemon rejected anything that failed `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()`, because CUDA IPC relies on torch's `_share_cuda_` handle export. title: [Fix] scheduler: Skip a chunked prefill when the KV pool holds no free page
summary: ## Motivation A server started with `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` dies with `RuntimeError: Out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.` once the KV pool is fully locked while a chunked prefill is in progress. We hit it on three of four one-minute windows of the Mooncake tool-and-agent trace (Kimi production traffic, FAST'25) replayed against Qwen3-8B on one A100 with `--max-total-tokens 160000`. `fcfs` and `lpm` did not pack the pool that tightly in the same runs. A chunked prefill holds KV that is only released when the whole prefill finishes, so a continuing chunk has to run even when the pass budget is negative. The budget is negative in two different situations. Usually the running requests' decode headroom (`total_offset`) exceeds the free pool, and the chunk may borrow from it because that memory exists. Sometimes the pool is physically full: every slot locked by running requests and by the chunk's own earlier chunks, nothing free, nothing evictable. `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` returned the full chunk size in both cases. In the second one `prepare_for_extend` asked `alloc_token_slots` for tokens the pool did not hold, eviction found nothing, and the scheduler process raised: ``` Out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 1 tokens. Available full tokens: 0 (full_available_size=0 + full_evictable_size_=0) ``` (`_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` -> `prepare_for_extend` -> `alloc_for_extend` -> `alloc_token_slots`) ## Modifications - `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` (the single-pool budget): when the pass budget is spent, the chu

title: [Fix] scheduler: Fire priority preemption when KV runs out, and keep retracted KV behind a flag
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-priority-scheduling` documents preemption: a request whose priority exceeds a running request's by more than `--priority-scheduling-preemption-threshold` is meant to preempt it. The admission loop in `Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw` tries preemption in one situation only, when the running batch has reached its request cap. When the request does not fit because KV memory has run out, which `PrefillAdder.add_one_req` reports as `AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN`, the loop stops. On a server with the default request cap, memory is what runs out, so a higher-priority request waits behind lower-priority running requests until they finish, and the flag only orders the queue. We found this on the first run of a priority-based scheduler on Qwen3-8B: priorities changed every step and nothing was ever preempted. The second change answers the TODO in `release_req`, "for preempted requests, we may want to insert into the tree". When a request is retracted or preempted, everything beyond its cached prompt prefix is freed, and its decoded tokens are recomputed when it comes back. `--preempt-keep-kv` inserts the request's KV, decoded tokens included, into the radix tree before its row is released, so the request resumes with a one-token prefill. Off by default. ## Modifications - Preemption on NO_TOKEN. After `add_one_req` returns NO_TOKEN for a request that was not admitted, with preemption enabled, the scheduler calls `adder.preempt_to_schedule(req)`; if that released enough, it drops what the first prefix match staged (`_drop_unadmitted_match`, as the loop does for a

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add a skip-join MLFQ policy with cache-aware placement and a prefill gate
summary: ## Motivation SGLang runs a prefill batch of waiting requests before the running batch's next decode step, and the scheduling policy only orders the waiting queue: it decides which prompt is prefilled next, not whether a prefill runs now. Under agent-style traffic, long prompts with short answers and many returning turns, that step model pauses every running request for every newcomer's prefill. On an A100 a fresh 50k-token prompt is seven chunks of 0.6 to 2.9 s each, about 6.8 s back to back, while a decode step takes 40 ms; a 30-token tool-call answer that needs 1.2 s of decode spends most of its life waiting for other requests' prefills. Measured under fcfs on the Mooncake tool-and-agent trace (Kimi production traffic, FAST'25), the mean time per output token was 646 ms against a 40 ms step: each decode step waited fifteen times its own compute. No queue order fixes that: fcfs, lpm, shortest-prefill-first and an MLFQ without a gate landed within 4% of each other on this trace. `--schedule-policy sj-mlfq` is FastServe's skip-join multi-level feedback queue (Wu et al., arXiv:2305.05920) adapted to a prefix-caching engine, with the one decision SGLang's step model allows: whether a prefill starts now. A request joins the queue level its predicted first iteration fits, priced from the uncached suffix it must prefill on top of its cached prefix, not from the whole prompt (cache-aware placement). summary: Follows #49623. A request list now changes membership through two doors only; every other edit is private. ```text move(reqs, dst) retirer new req ------------------> [ list A ] -----------------> ended | ^ release / abort / move | | move retire_unadmitted / v | abort_retracted [ list B ] -----------------> ended req.owner_list names the one list a request is in (#49623). ``` - **In, or between lists: `move`.** `ReqList.join` becomes `_join`. - **Out: the retirer.** Each exit takes the request out of its list, so the call sites that left a list themselves (PD failure and transfer exits, a prebuilt batch, a KV checksum mismatch, the chunked and uOCR aborts) drop that edit, and `ReqList.take` goes. - **The rest is private**: `_leave`, `_drop_all`, `_leave_finished`; `replace` becomes `reorder`, which raises if the requests change. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Fail parked prefill requests when their decode goes away
summary: Related: #43699 (KVCache liveness). Follows up #40703. ## Motivation With `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete`, a request keeps its KV on prefill until decode is ready for it: 1. Decode sends `BOOTSTRAP(room, ip, port)` to prefill. 2. Prefill runs the request and sends `WaitingForInput` to decode over its ZMQ status socket. 3. When decode has free KV, it sends destinations; prefill transfers the KV and frees it. If decode dies between 2 and 3, prefill never notices, because liveness is only checked from decode to prefill. The parked requests hold their KV until `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` (default 300 s) fires, and prefill accepts almost no new work meanwhile. The status socket's monitor sees the disconnect within about 1 ms, but it is only read on the next send to that decode, and nothing is sent while its requests are parked. Separately, if decode is already dead at the first connect, the socket reports `EVENT_CLOSED`, which the monitor did not watch. The readiness message then sits in a socket that never delivers. The timeout cannot be tuned around this. A short one fails requests that are legitimately waiting for a busy but healthy decode (second table below); a long one strands KV for minutes when decode dies. This PR does not depend on the timeout: it reacts to the lost connection itself. ## Results Two nodes, one prefill and one decode instance (TP 1 each), Mooncake over RDMA, `deepseek-moe-16b-chat`, `sglang-router` 0.3.2, main at 286e018. 128 requests (3000 input and 1000 output tokens) are sent at once. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] flashinfer: Pass uniform_q_len to the target-verify plan for EAGLE speculative decoding
summary: ## Motivation EAGLE target verify gives every request exactly `num_tokens_per_req` (= `draft_token_num`) query rows: `EagleVerifyInput` builds `qo_indptr` as a constant-stride arange. FlashInfer's FA2 CUDA-graph planner cannot see that from the ragged CSR alone, so it sizes its query tile for the worst case (`total_rows - bs + 1` rows per request). For a typical verify batch (32 q-heads, TP8, 4 draft tokens) that means running a 64-row tile on a 16-packed-row problem. Capture fixes the verify kernel's query tile from the hint, so every plan through a captured verify wrapper must carry the same hint: the hint is passed on both plan paths, the real `plan()` and the `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHINFER_VERIFY_HOST_PLAN` sync-free replay (`fast_prefill_plan`, which previously pinned the argument to 0). **Requires a FlashInfer pin with the `plan(uniform_q_len=...)` keyword (>= 0.7.2.post1); `main` already pins

title: [Fix] flexkv: Isolate FlexKV KV by the request's cache namespace
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49624. The FlexKV integration sent FlexKV only token ids on lookup, store and prefetch. FlexKV matches by token-id prefix, so KV stored under one `(extra_key, cache_salt)` was returned to a request with a different tenant salt, a different LoRA adapter, or none. The loaded node was then stamped with the caller's namespace in the local radix tree. title: [RFC] scheduler: UniBoost, a starvation-bounded schedule policy (#48076-#48079)
summary: ## Motivation Under overload, the existing policies trade fairness for work differently, and none gives a wait bound. `fcfs` bounds waits but ignores work; `lpm` and `shortest-prefill-first` favor cheap requests and can starve large ones; `hrrn` ages by waited tokens. On agentic workloads (long shared contexts, heavy-tailed outputs) we see a long TTFT tail of requests that wait minutes. UniBoost (*Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026, https://yl3469.github.io/uniboost-icml26/#cite) is a prediction-free policy with one knob. Requests are served in ascending `phi(r) = A(r) - b_gamma(q(u(r)))`: arrival minus a bounded boost for small uncached work. No boost exceeds `b_gamma(k)`, so a newcomer can only overtake requests that arrived less than that long ago. ## Proposal Four stacked PRs. Everything is opt-in and off by default, so existing policies are untouched. 1. #48076: `--schedule-policy uniboost` with fixed gamma (token or wall clock). 2. #48077: gamma-Ada from the paper, `--uniboost-adaptive-gamma`. gamma adapts online from the response-time tail (t99 - t95), floored by a max-jump bound. 3. #48078: wait bounds under prefix sharing. Dedup followers sort right behind their leader instead of last, and a commit gate avoids recomputing a prefix that a sibling is about to commit. 4. #48079: decode time-slicing, `--uniboost-preempt-wait-s`; this one is our extension, not in the paper. When a first-token waiter has starved for N seconds and does not fit in memory, the longest-running decodes are released into the radix cache. They resume from cac

Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Typical SGLang cache tiers namespace KV by `(extra_key, cache_salt)`, for example the device radix tree, the HiCache L3 storage keys (`storage_namespace_seed`, `mem_cache/utils.py:102-116`), and the LMCache. The extra_key carries the LoRA id, and cache_salt carries the tenant salt and, for multimodal requests. But the FlexKV integration somehow sends FlexKV **only the token ids** on all three paths: lookup, store and prefetch. FlexKV matches by token-id prefix, so KV stored under one namespace is returned to any request with the same tokens under any other namespace. From then on, the foreign KV sits in the caller's own namespace in the local radix tree. FlexKV is documented as shared across DP ranks and instances (`storage/flexkv/README.md:245,295-297`), so the store is the place where tenants and adapters meet, risky. **Impact:** 1. **Cross-salt prefix oracle.** Tenant B, under its own salt, sends a candidate prefix. title: [Fix] hicache: retain prefetched host pages until admission
summary: ## Motivation Fixes [#49221](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/49221). This PR is stacked on [#48848](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48848); the benchmarks below use that prerequisite as the baseline. In cache mode, a completed L3 prefetch inserts pages into the host radix tree before request admission but does not retain an eviction reference. Under L2 pressure, a later prefetch can evict those pages before load-back. The request then gets a partial hit or miss at admission despite the earlier storage hit, causing redundant prefill and increasing `cache_admission_shortfall`. ## Modifications - Pin completed prefetches in the host radix tree until prefill admission or decode load-back finishes. Also release the pin on request abort and storage teardown. - Queue confirmed storage hits in FIFO order during transient host-capacity pressure, but only when an independent in-flight operation can release capacity. Fall back if the hit cannot fit or no such operation exists. Waiting prefetch policies perform the storage lookup before applying this backpressure. - In disaggregated prefill, fall back instead of waiting for capacity pinned by another completed prefetch that has not been admitted. That request may itself be waiting for decode capacity, so waiting could create a cross-side wait cycle. The fallback may recompute under pressure. - Check operation identity before revoking a queued prefetch, so a stale operation cannot cancel a newer prefetch that reuses the same request handle. - Add regressions for admission, eviction pressure, abort, decode load-ba

title: [Fix] HiCache: Wait for decode prefetch before publishing prefix length
summary: ## Motivation Fixes [#48802](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48802). In PD disaggregation, decode uses `decode_prefix_len` to tell prefill which KV prefix it can reuse locally. Prefill transfers only the remaining suffix. With HiCache enabled, decode currently counts an L3 lookup hit toward this length before the prefix has actually been restored to the L2 host cache. If the subsequent prefetch fails because L2 is full, neither side supplies the skipped KV: prefill has already excluded it from the transfer, and decode cannot restore it locally. The request then fails with `HiCache load-back failed`. In the reproducer, decode published a 6,144-token reuse prefix but restored zero tokens. This change waits for the L3 prefetch outcome, then determines the reusable prefix from the resident L1/L2 cache. If the prefetch fails, prefill transfers the missing KV and the request can complete. The issue reproduces on [10be18dcfc](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/10be18dcfc466a2171b4892de214909a328ff737), which includes [#48421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48421). That PR rejects partial L3 allocations for hybrid models, but decode can still publish the reuse length before the allocation outcome is known. ## Modifications - Keep registered or ticketed L3 prefetches in the preallocation queue until they settle. Rematch the resident L1/L2 prefix and recheck admission capacity before publishing P-to-D transfer metadata. The rematch does not query L3 again. - Retain the existing host allocation and eviction logic. Publish only the usable prefix lengt

title: [Fix] [AMD] disaggregation: Pair MoRI DSA state across PP prefill stages
summary: ## Motivation PD over MoRI breaks as soon as the prefill server runs a DSA model with PP > 1. title: [Bug] Qwen4-Exp PLE: BF16 n-gram shards are cast to FP8 with a unit scale when the checkpoint's config sets ple_embedding_dtype (primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4)
summary: ### Describe the bug `primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (about 6.7k downloads last month) has `text_config.ple_embedding_dtype: "float8_e4m3fn"` in its `config.json`, keeps `*.ple.*` out of quantization in its `ignore` list, and stores all 128 `ngram_embedding.shard_*` tensors in BF16 with no scale tensor. `_ple_table_is_fp8` returns `True` from the config field, so the n-gram table is built in FP8 with `weight_scale` a buffer of ones, and the loader casts the BF16 rows into it. The only sign is one warning: ``` PLE checkpoint shards are torch.bfloat16 but the embedding storage is fp8 (ple_embedding_dtype / fp8 quant config); downcasting is lossy ``` On 65,536 real rows of `layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding.shard_0.weight` (`[2500012, 160]`), the unit-scale FP8 cast gives: | | value | |---|---| | relative error of the table | 7.6% | | nonzero values that become 0 | 10.2% | | median absolute value | 0.0048 (below FP8 E4M3's smallest normal value, 2^-6) | | largest absolute value | 0.051 | | relative error with one per-tensor scale (amax / 448) instead of 1.0 | 2.8% | Among the 15 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints I checked, this is the only one whose config asks for FP8 n-gram storage while its shards are BF16. The others either ship FP8 shards (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `RadixArk/...-NVFP4`, `dealignai/...` x2, `jpezzulli/...`), leave `ple_embedding_dtype` unset with BF16 shards (`Inferact/...`, `RedHatAI/...`, `davetha/...`), or use `nvfp4`. `ple_embedding_dtype` is also the setting the offload path tells users to set for FP8 storage, so I did not change it

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fp8: Add Triton block-fp8 GEMM configs for RTX PRO 5000 [128, 128]
summary: ## Motivation On SM120 (consumer Blackwell, here 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB) the dense block-FP8 GEMMs run through the Triton `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul` kernel: DeepGEMM is not used for these layers because `should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0()` returns False for `get_device_sm() == 120` (see the comment there: "SM120 routes dense block-FP8 GEMMs to CUTLASS/Triton (fp32 scales); only the grouped MoE GEMM consumes DeepGEMM layouts there"). At decode batch 32 the kernel family accounts for 32.5% of GPU busy time in a 24-step torch-profiler window, which is why the default tile choice is worth fixing. ## Changes Six new config files

title: [Perf] Persistent lazy eviction heaps for the unified radix cache full component
summary: ## Motivation `FullComponent._evict_device_start` rebuilds the eviction heap from every evictable leaf on each walk (`list` + `heapify`, O(L)), and the host walk does the same. Once the KV pool is full, that runs on every scheduler step: at ~41k leaves it costs 70-77 ms per evict and takes 95% of the scheduler thread, and throughput drops 87-92%. This PR keeps one lazy heap per leaf set across walks instead, with eviction order unchanged. SGLang-Omni hit the same rebuild first and harder (short zero-hit audio requests keep the pool saturated on a host-bound scheduler; ASR throughput fell 92%) and carries the same construction on the classic tree in sgl-project/sglang-omni#1724; this PR moves it to where every dense model runs. ## Modifications - **Persistent leaf heaps** (`unified_cache/components/full_component.py`): one lazy min-heap each for the device and host leaf sets, entries `(key, seq, node)`. A pop drops entries whose node left the set and re-pushes entries whose key moved; a heap is rebuilt only when stale entries exceed `max(1024, 4 x leaves)`. - **Push hook** (`unified_cache/unified_tree_core.py`): `_update_evictable_leaf_sets` calls `on_evictable_leaf_added` when a node enters a leaf set. That is the single add site, so every evictable leaf always has a live entry. - **Tests** (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_evict_heap.py`, `1-gpu-small`): eviction order equals the previous per-walk rebuild on randomized insert / match / lock / evict traces (3 seeds); heap size stays within the compaction bound and drains after a full evict. summary: ## Motivation Fast-dVLM (NVlabs/Fast-dLLM) serves a Qwen2.5-VL-3B checkpoint converted to block diffusion through a vendored SGLang fork. This PR moves its MDM decoding mode (HierarchyBlock) onto the current dLLM interfaces, with the block-level radix cache from #18724 left on and no new caching mechanism. Text prompts only for now. The algorithm denoises sub-blocks left to right with bidirectional attention inside the block, then writes the block's KV with one causal forward. The KV left in the cache and reused through the radix tree matches an autoregressive pass over the same tokens. The causal pass also predicts the first token of the request's next block. Fast-dLLM v2 (#22156) adds a HierarchyBlock in the same file. Any forward over fully resolved blocks runs causally, so the final KV write and the next-token prediction are one pass. The first token after a prompt tail is also predicted by a causal forward. title: [Fix] dsa: Rebuild draft page table after DP-attention padding
summary: ## Bug On an eager DSA draft decode under DP attention, the backend plans its metadata before the batch is padded to the global DP size. The planned `metadata.page_table_1` then has fewer rows than the padded `topk_indices`, so the decode path either asserts or gathers from stale rows. ## Fix When `metadata.page_table_1` has a different row count from the padded `topk_indices`, rebuild it from `req_to_token` for the padded batch. Dummy padded rows get a valid one-column row; their `topk` is all `-1`, so the gather stays inert. ## Verification - Added `test_dsa_padded_draft_page_table.py`: - rebuild extends to the padded rows and maps the real rows correctly - rebuild preserves the planned width when it is wider than the max sequence length - Both tests pass. - Full `pre-commit run --files` passes. - No e2e claim is made here: the earlier e2e in #48081 covered both the DSA and scheduler halves; the scheduler half has been removed after review, so that run does not apply to this reduced PR. ## Scope This PR now contains only the DSA-side fix from #48081. The scheduler half was removed after review because it was not on the PD decode path and would have crashed non-PD HiSparse + EAGLE. The missing-DSA-seed investigation on the prefill side remains a separate follow-up.

summary: ## Motivation Speed up RoPE on Cambricon MLU by routing `RotaryEmbedding` to FlagTree's Cambricon Triton RoPE kernel (`triton.ops.apply_rotary`) instead of the PyTorch-native fallback. ## Modifications - Add MLU backend detection (`is_mlu()` from main) and route `RotaryEmbedding` to `forward_mlu` on MLU, skipping the CUDA/vLLM fallback kernel. - `forward_mlu` uses FlagTree's **padded** API (`cu_seqlens=None`): Q and K are viewed as one `(1, num_tokens, heads, rotary_dim)` sequence and rotated **in place**. title: [Feat] spec: add per-request speculative decoding opt-out with mixed-batch support (#47797)
summary: ## Summary and final contract Implements per-request speculative-decoding opt-out for EAGLE, EAGLE3, and STANDALONE, including mixed batches. Related RFC: #47797. `SamplingParams.disable_speculative_decoding=True` means **one target-root token committed per decode iteration**. The opted-out row independently uses the ordinary target sampler; draft proposals are not accepted. Draft prefill, proposal, and extend work **continues**, including when every row opts out, to preserve the configured execution layout and draft KV state. This is deliberately narrower than the RFC's zero-draft-work request. It is not a target-only performance baseline or a promise of bitwise-identical sequences across separately configured servers. Maintainer agreement on this contract remains necessary. ## Changes - Propagate opt-out masks and host flags through batch construction, filtering, merging, and empty batches. - Sample and replace the target-root token, then truncate acceptance counts and index sentinels. Exclude deliberate zero draft acceptance from adaptive accuracy feedback. - Reject unsupported algorithms and custom logit processors. title: [RFC] Define per-request speculative decoding opt-out execution semantics
summary: ## Motivation Resume the design discussion from #30263 and draft #30264, both closed by inactivity automation. GitHub rejected reopening the original issue. Current main (`a52ee805`) still has no request-level `disable_speculative_decoding` field or consumer. Per-request speculative statistics (including #34814) do not provide an opt-out. The original draft only transported an unenforced flag. I do not propose restoring that API as a working feature without implementing its execution semantics. ## Proposed scope and alternatives 1. Group opt-out requests into non-speculative scheduler batches, preserving ordering, streaming and KV-cache ownership across batch transitions. This makes mixed request behavior explicit but adds scheduling and execution-path complexity. 2. Use an explicit steps-zero runtime state for batches containing opt-out requests. This could reuse adaptive speculative runtime machinery, but needs a defined mixed-batch policy and correctly matched attention/CUDA-graph state. Changing only the request flag or branching inside the worker is insufficient. `EAGLEWorkerV2` still has a `speculative_num_steps == 0` path, and `adaptive_spec_params.py` manages runtime transitions. These are investigation points, not proof that a per-request switch is safe. ## Acceptance criteria before a mergeable PR - Opted-out requests execute no draft-model work and match the non-speculative target output for deterministic sampling. - Default requests retain existing behavior; specify what happens when both types share a batch. - Test eager and CUDA-graph execution, streaming/canc

title: [Fix] scheduler: Free a chunked prefill's out-of-window SWA slots before sizing its next chunk
summary: ## Motivation On a hybrid-SWA model served with `--disable-radix-cache`, when the SWA pool is sized by `SWARequestCapPoolConfigurator`, a long prompt's chunks shrink after the second one. On MiMo-V2.6-Flash (window 128, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 1`, overlap on) the SWA pool is 8,451 tokens, and a 127,852-token prompt ran as 2 × 4,096 and then 258 and 3,968 alternating: 60 forwards instead of 32. On current `main`, gpt-oss-20b (window 128, page size 64, SWA pool 8,640) runs a 33,644-token prompt as 4096, 4096, then 384 and 3968 alternating, ending with 3308: 14 forwards instead of 9 (the reviewer's run on one B200). The cause is ordering. `PrefillAdder.add_chunked_req` sizes a continuing chunk from `SWAPrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens`, which is the SWA pool's free count. At that point the previous chunks' out-of-window rows are still held: `ScheduleBatch.maybe_evict_swa` retires them only later, in `alloc_for_extend`, once the chunk is placed. `compute_swa_request_cap` already assumes those rows are gone by then. Under overlap it budgets two chunks plus one window (`chunks_in_flight = 2`), which is what is live when chunk N+1 is placed while chunk N runs, once everything before chunk N's window has been retired. Without overlap it budgets one chunk, and the old order shrinks chunks there too (4096, 258, 3968, …; see the unit test). With a pool below two chunks plus a window, the same order stops the request for good: under overlap the first two chunks are both held when the third is sized, nothing fits, `add_chunked_req` returns the request

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] flash-attn: FA4 SM90 FP8 e4m3 KV cache for head_dim 256 and 512 (Gemma-4)
summary: ## Motivation Since #44399, `--attention-backend fa3` runs Gemma-4's 10 full-attention layers (head_dim 512) on FA4. FA4 has no FP8 KV path on SM90, so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` is rejected at init, although FA3 already reads FP8 KV on the 50 sliding-window layers (head_dim 256). The sliding-window layers also run on FA4 whenever a batch carries image tokens, including the VLM startup warm-up, so FA4 needs FP8 KV at both head dims. This PR lets FA4's SM90 forward read an FP8 e4m3 KV cache at head_dim 256 and 512. Gemma-4 can then serve with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on H100/H200, which doubles both KV pools. ## Modifications - **Kernel** (`flash_fwd_sm90.py`, `named_barrier.py`, `utils.py`): K/V tiles are loaded as fp8 into a staging buffer and cast to fp16 in shared memory by the MMA warpgroups. The K/V descales fold into the softmax scale and the output scale. At head_dim 512 each warpgroup casts its half of V; at head_dim 256 all MMA threads cast the whole of V behind one barrier. One pipeline stage when FP8 KV is on. - **Interface** (`interface.py`): bf16/fp16 Q with fp8 e4m3 K/V on SM90 selects this path, and the Q/K/V dtypes join the compile key. Unsupported cases raise `NotImplementedError`: e5m2, head_dim other than 256 or 512, non-paged KV, `qv`, `rel_bias`, block sparsity, `mma_pv_is_rs=False`. bf16 Q is narrowed to fp16 in-kernel, so |q| above 65504 overflows; Gemma-4's QK-norm keeps Q far below that. - **Backend** (`flashattention_backend.py`): the `fa3` backend accepts an `fp8_e4m3` cache when it upgrades layers to FA4. title: [Fix] moe: Validate the scale grid and use logical K for even_Ks in the GPTQ/AWQ Triton MoE kernel
summary: ## Motivation `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` has two K-tail problems when the per-rank K is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K`: 1. **Packed int4 weights are loaded without a mask.** #48556 fixes this with the same one-line change, which this PR also contains (the hunk is byte-identical, so either order merges cleanly). 2. **Scales are read past the end of an incomplete grid.** The kernel picks scale group `k // group_size`. If a caller's grid has fewer than `cdiv(K, group_size)` groups, the K tail reads the next row's scales, and on the last row it reads past the scale tensor. A mask cannot fix this, because those K positions hold real data. compressed-tensors WNA16 builds such a grid today: at `moe_intermediate_size=640`, `moe_tp_size=4` (K=160 per rank) it creates `160 // 128 = 1` group while the kernel needs 2. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 (compressed-tensors, group 128), 8× A800, `--tp 8 --ep 2 --moe-runner-backend triton`, every EP1 rank dies with `illegal memory access` during CUDA graph capture, and with `--disable-cuda-graph` it dies on the first prefill. **Masking only the B load does not stop the crash**: the scale over-read still faults. This path is the default in two places: compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE always uses `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` on ROCm, and selects it automatically on SM100/SM103 (`compressed_tensors.py:1003-1033`). ## Modifications - Mask the B load with the existing K mask (same as #48556). - Before launch, require `B_scale.shape[2]` (and `B_zp.shape[2]`) to equal `cdiv(K, group_size)`; otherwise raise `ValueError` instead of reading out of bou

title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM5: Add opt-in W8A16 KDA decode projections on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation Depends on #38764. With the #38764 PTPC selector enabled, GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode still runs the first-stage `[qkv | beta | f_a | g_a]` projection as a fused BF16 GEMM, and that GEMM reads the full BF16 weight on every decode step. #38764 already keeps a per-channel FP8 copy of the same weight for prefill. This change adds an opt-in W8A16 decode path that reads that existing FP8 weight with BF16 activations. Beta's rows are packed into the same FP8 weight, so one decode GEMM produces qkv, beta, and f/g. No second quantized copy is stored, and no activation quantization runs on the decode path. The decode GEMM reduces its split-K partials inside the same launch. ## Modifications - Add the default-off `SGLANG_OPT_GLM53_KDA_W8A16_DECODE` selector and reject it unless `SGLANG_OPT_GLM53_KDA_PTPC_MODULES` is also set. - Add `sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.gfx95_a16w8_preshuffle`, a gfx950 Triton GEMM with BF16 activations against the (16, 16)-preshuffled per-channel FP8 PTPC weight. It is used for decode token counts covered by the tuned table (`M<=64`), reuses the weight as a zero-copy view, and applies the existing per-row scale once to each reduced tile. - Reduce split-K partials in the GEMM. The last CTA of each output tile sums the partials in split order and writes BF16, so there is no separate reduce launch and results do not depend on CTA arrival order. Splits of a tile share a program id modulo 8, so gfx950's round-robin dispatch places them on one XCD and the hand-off stays in one L2 behind a relaxed device-scope counter. title: [Perf] kda: Reuse one int64 cu_seqlens per batch in FlashInfer prefill to avoid per-layer host sync
summary: ## Motivation FlashInfer's CuTe DSL KDA prefill (`recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")`) reads `cu_seqlens` back to the host to plan its routes. It skips that read only when it gets the same int64 tensor object as on the previous call (`kda_chunked_bt16._cu_seqlens_contents`). Our KDA backend passed `query_start_loc` as int32. FlashInfer recasts any int32 `cu_seqlens` to a new int64 tensor on every call (`kda_prefill_cute.py`), so the cached read was never reused and, on routes that read `cu_seqlens`, **every KDA layer did a blocking device-to-host copy**. The host stalled until the GPU stream drained, once per layer. GLM-5.3-Flash has 34 KDA layers, and FlashInfer prefill is its default KDA prefill backend on SM100/SM103 (the model has a lower-bound gate). ## Modifications - `ForwardMetadata` gains `query_start_loc_int64`. `KDAAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata` builds it once per extend forward, only when the extend kernel sets the new `uses_int64_query_start_loc` class flag. Today only `FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel` sets it. - `forward_extend` passes it through, and `FlashInferKDAPrefillKernel` hands it to FlashInfer as `cu_seqlens`. Every KDA layer of a forward therefore gets the same tensor object, so only the first layer reads `cu_seqlens` back to the host. - No numerics change: the kernel receives the same offsets, in the same int64 dtype FlashInfer converted them to before. ## Accuracy Tests The kernel inputs are unchanged apart from reusing one int64 tensor, so this change has no accuracy effect. `test/registered/attention/test_kda_prefill_flashinfer.py` passes on GB300

summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash MTP 5/1/6 decode runs 6 `sm100_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` kernels per step, 2 in each gap between the verify, draft-extend and draft graphs. GLM-5.3 runs 3. title: [GLM-5.3-Flash] Fuse the FFN mHC post into the next layer's attention pre
summary: ## Summary At decode batch sizes, GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries are small, latency-bound launches. The attention -> FFN boundary inside a layer is already fused (`hc_ffn_post_pre`); this does the same for the layer -> layer boundary. - Each layer's FFN `hc_post` is deferred. Its coefficients stay on the layer's `MHCState` until the next layer's attention read fuses them with that layer's `hc_pre` (`hc_attn_post_pre`). - It reuses the existing post+pre fusion path and its 16-token cap. Larger batches fall back to the unfused post, then pre. - The last layer still writes back and contracts the streams itself. - It is gated by the existing `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE`, and off under PP > 1, TBO and `--enable-attn-tp-input-scattered`. - The rejections of attention-CP and MoE-CP gathers, and of input-scattered attention under CP, now key on any non-plain FFN update, so they also cover the deferred one. - `hc_ffn_post_pre` and `hc_attn_post_pre` share one helper. ## Results GLM-5.3-Flash on 4x GB300, TP4. Before is main; single runs. GSM8K: 97.50% before, 97.65% after. title: [Perf] [AMD] Qwen3.5: enable fused GDN decode unpack + Conv1D for ROCm platform
summary: Qwen3.5 uses a type of layer called GDN (a linear-attention layer). On AMD GPUs, every GDN layer ran two small GPU kernels in a row during decode. This PR combines them into one. Nothing changes for NVIDIA GPUs. ## Motivation Decode is the step where the model writes its answer one token at a time. In each GDN layer, the model needs to do two small jobs before the main computation: | Kernel | What it does | |---|---| | `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous` | Splits one big packed tensor into the separate pieces the layer needs | | `causal_conv1d_update` | Updates a small saved state and applies a short convolution | Together they took 10.5 µs per layer. Each one does very little work, so most of that time is not real computation. It is the cost of starting a kernel and waiting for it to finish. SGLang already has a single fused kernel that does both jobs, but only for NVIDIA GPUs. summary: ## Motivation Serving benchmarks already report aggregate end-to-end latency statistics, but detailed output does not retain the underlying per-request latency values. Aggregates alone cannot recover custom percentiles, evaluate a different latency target after a run, or correlate slow requests with their input/output lengths. title: [Hardening] Log why the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm path falls back instead of discarding it
summary: Two handlers on the fused all-reduce path catch `Exception` and drop it, so a permanent fallback to a slower path — or a silent `None` — is indistinguishable from the fast path having been chosen. `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: ```python if hasattr(ca_comm, "fused_allreduce_rmsnorm"): try: return ca_comm.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(input_, residual_inp_, weight_, eps) except Exception: # Fall back to custom_fused_ar_rms path below. pass ``` and, a few hundred lines later: ```python try: return ca_comm.custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant(...) except Exception: return None ``` Why this matters in practice: the communicator behind these calls validates operand layout and raises when it cannot express one. That exception is the diagnostic — it names which operand and which layout — and both handlers throw it away. The result is a run that is quietly on the unfused path for every layer of every forward, with nothing in the log to say so and no way to tell it apart from a configuration where the fusion was never requested. Someone measuring the fusion's benefit can then measure zero and conclude the fusion does not help, when in fact it never ran. The change keeps the fallback behaviour exactly as it is — this is not a behaviour change and not a bid to make these paths fatal — and only stops the reason being lost: warned once per process with the exception attached, so a fallback is visible in the log while remaining a fallback. It follows the pattern already in the tree for this exact situation rather than adding a helper: a module-level `_..._warned` flag with a

title: Feat/router session stats
summary: # feat(sgl-router): per-session turn-timing statistics (measurement-only) ## Summary sgl-router today records **global** TTFT and request-duration histograms (`server/metrics.rs`) but nothing **per session**. This PR adds an opt-in, measurement-only collector that records, for every session, the four key instants of each turn and reports the per-session timing. It is purely observational: it **collects and reports** timing, it does **not** change routing, scheduling, or eviction. Disabled by default → all hooks are cheap no-ops; zero overhead when off. ## Motivation Per-session timing is the signal needed to reason about a session's **prefill/decode arrival cadence** — how busy vs. idle (client thinking / tool time) a session is over its turns. The global histograms can't express this because they aggregate across sessions and requests. Exposing it at the router (which already sees every turn and streams every response) is the natural place. ## Design framework For each session (identified by the sticky routing key, e.g. `x-session-id`) the router stamps **four instants per turn**, all reusing instrumentation points that already exist on the request path — no extra network calls, no new hot-path work: ``` client turn sgl-router (chat handler) ─────────── ───────────────────────── POST /v1/chat/completions ─────► t_recv = request received [handler entry] (route / tokenize; retries here counted) t_dispatch = forwarded to worker [dispatch site] first SSE token ◄───── t_first = first streamed token [TTFT first-byte hook] …stream… │ stream end ◄───── t_end = last token / stream

title: [Refactor] custom-ar-v2: Single-word push epoch and consume-style pull semaphores
summary: > (auto generated by Claude) > (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent) Supersedes #48217, moved to an in-repo branch so follow-up PRs can stack on it. ## What Simplifies the synchronization state shared by the CustomAllReduceV2 push/pull planes and every kernel that borrows them, so that resource sizes no longer depend on launch widths. - Push plane: the per-block phase counter array is replaced by one u64 `EpochCounter`. Each grid participant does one fire-and-forget `red.add` at exit (participant 0 adds `2^32 - (N - 1)`, the others add 1), so any grid size advances the phase exactly once. All "bumper" / cleanup blocks that flipped unused counters are removed, and push kernels may launch any grid size. - Pull plane: `Semaphore` keeps one arrival counter per ordering class (relaxed / release). title: [Fix] watchdog: Let py-spy attach to watched processes in CI
summary: ## Motivation When a server hangs in CI, the watchdog and the crash path call `py-spy dump` to record where it's stuck. On the NVIDIA runners, every one of those dumps fails: ``` Pyspy failed (py-spy dump --native --pid 2020632). Error: Error: Permission denied (os error 13) Pyspy failed (py-spy dump --native --pid 325233). Error: Error: Failed to copy Py_Version ... Permission denied (os error 13) ``` Across 18 recent jobs on 5090 (`sm1`-`sm4`), B300 (`di-tor5`) and H100 (`computable-d`, `novita`) runners, about 250 py-spy attempts all failed, with no successes. So every hang leaves no stack. For example, the `test_disaggregation_basic.py` prefill servers that never became healthy on 11-06 ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42128580169/job/127658193873)) left nothing to debug with. **Cause (inferred; I haven't read the runners' sysctl):** the containers don't have `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`, and under Yama `ptrace_scope=1` (the Ubuntu default) a process may then ptrace only its own descendants. A same-user dump would succeed under `ptrace_scope=0`, so the errors point to `ptrace_scope` being 1 or higher. (The AMD and XPU container scripts in this repo add `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE`; the NVIDIA runner containers are set up elsewhere.) SGLang starts py-spy in two places, `python/sglang/srt/utils/cudacore_pyspy_dump_utils.py:70`: - **`WatchdogRaw`** runs it as a **child** of the process it dumps (its own PID). - **`TokenizerManager`'s crash dump** runs it as a **sibling** of the schedulers it dumps. Neither is a descendant relationship, so the kernel refuses both. ##

title: [Bug] Encoder-decoder KV cache: shared boundary page is double-freed when page_size > 1
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug For encoder-decoder models (Whisper, Llama-3.2-Vision / `mllama`, `MossVL`, any `config.is_encoder_decoder`), the encoder is prepended to the request as a single contiguous block of `num_image_tokens` KV tokens, so a request's `req_to_token` row is `[encoder region | decoder region]`. Decode-time allocation, however, derives its paged arithmetic from the **encoder-stripped** `seq_lens`: `alloc_for_decode` (`mem_cache/allocation.py:531-561`) reads `last_loc = req_to_token[req_pool_indices, seq_lens - 1]` and lets `alloc_decode_kernel` decide "does this step need a new page?" from `seq_lens % page_size`, while the *write* position is `encoder_lens + seq_lens`. At `page_size > 1` those two disagree by `encoder_len`, so every decode token is handed `encoder_slot[seq_len - 1] + 1` — a slot that **aliases the encoder region** — and new pages are taken at the wrong row positions. The row therefore stops satisfying `row[j] == page[j // page_size] * page_size + (j % page_size)`. title: [Bug] Chunked Prefill + Radix Insert race corrupts KV pages (QSA, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
summary: ## Chunked Prefill + Radix Insert race produces persistent KV cache corruption (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / QSA) ### Summary A race condition between chunked-prefill KV-page insertion into the Radix Cache and pool page deallocation (retract/abort) produces silently corrupted KV pages. Once cached in the Radix tree, every subsequent request matching the same prefix immediately reads garbage attention data, causing an impossible-token loop (token ID `248319` = OOV/never-trained lm_head row) on the very first decode step. ### Symptoms - First decode token after prefill is always the impossible token `248319` (tokenizer length = 248077, lm_head = 248320) - `num_correct_drafts = 0`, `accept_len = 1` — the target model independently produces the bad token on its first forward - The corrupted KV slot range is identical across repeated requests with the same prefix - `flush_cache` resolves the issue temporarily (evicts the corrupt radix prefix) - Re-appears at the same prefix once the corruption is re-triggered ### Hardware/Software - **Hardware:** 1× DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB, SM121) - **Model:** `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (180B MoE, QSA sparse attention) - **Serving:** SGLang with QSA KDA kernel + SM121 Triton fallback decode - **KV cache dtype:** auto (NVFP4) - **Speculative decoding:** EAGLE, 3 steps, topk=1, 4 draft tokens - **Chunked prefill:** 2048 tokens/chunk - **Page size:** 64 (compressed QSA full//ratio addressing) - **Context length:** 262144, mem_fraction_static=0.79 - **Attention:** prefill=triton, decode=trtllm_mha - **Mamba radix cache strategy:** extra_buffer ###

title: [Roadmap] Quantization Modifications
summary: ### 1. Quantization refactor ### Background #### Scheme structure Currently, quantization methods are mostly implemented in 2 ways: with schemes structure, like `compressed_tensors` and `quark`, and without, like `modelslim` for NPU or `AWQ`. While foregoing scheme structure can be ok if we only load 1 format, having ability to load many of them without specific logic will overload `get_quant_method` function. Overall, the more quant methods get supported, the bigger each respective file gets. #### Weight loading and inference The weight creation and inference code is currently implemented in the same class, but same inference code can be utilized by different frameworks. ### Motivation #### Support more scheme structures The key improvement of following the scheme structure is that it is much easier to **maintain** and **update**, allowing for **easier implementation and review process**. Below is the example of proposed scheme structure change: #### Split weight loading and inference Quant config, weight creation and kernel call logic should be clearly separated to allow different frameworks to use the same kernel if it fits. This will avoid code duplication and thus increase **code readability** and avoid circular imports. Our end goal is to create a **unified and simpler structure** for quantization functionality

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Gather 16 local Engram rows per program on SM103 and SM107
summary: ## Motivation `engram_gather`'s local kernel (`_engram_gather_kernel`) runs one Triton program per looked-up row. Each program is a chain of dependent loads (id, then payload and scales) ending in a 512-byte store. In a DeepSeek-V4.1 DP prefill a forward makes two such calls of `ranks x tokens x 24` rows: 3.1M programs at 32K tokens per rank on 4 ranks. Per-program latency, not bandwidth, bounds the kernel. On 4x VR200 at 32K tokens per rank each call took 1.67 ms, about 1.5% of the forward. The peer-read kernel (`_engram_gather_peer_kernel`, #46180) already runs 8 rows per program. This PR batches rows the same way for the local gather, 16 per program. On `main` the local gather runs for the lookups that are not peer reads: all-reduce, reduce-scatter and all-to-all lookups, host-table placement, and TP groups that span nodes. ## Modifications - `_engram_gather_kernel` takes `ROWS` rows per program as a 2-D `[ROWS, DIM]` tile through the existing `_dequant_rows`, with a ragged last program masked. The MXFP4 decode, the destination permutation (`sort_ids`) and the shard bounds stay as they were. Values are bitwise those of one row per program. - `_gather_rows_per_program()` picks 16 on SM103 and SM107, where it was measured. Other GPUs keep one row per program: the grid and per-program work there are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests The change is bitwise; no model-level accuracy run is needed. - VR200 (SM107), this branch against `main`'s kernel: 8 and 16 rows per program equal `main`'s one-row kernel bit for bit (bf16 outputs compared as int16). title: [Feat] hicache: Add a direct_kernel IO backend on page_row for MLA/DSA pools
summary: > Written with Claude Code. ## Motivation HiCache's `direct` IO backend moves `page_first_direct` pages with the copy engine. Before each transfer it syncs the token-slot indices to the CPU and builds one copy descriptor per (page, layer). For an MLA model with a DSA indexer (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V3.2) that host-side work dominates each transfer: about 0.5 us of CPU issue per page and layer, paid on every load-back and write-back. The scheduler does this work before it launches the forward, so the GPU waits through it. In a profiled GLM-5.2 agentic-coding replay with PP4 prefill on GB300, one request (119 new tokens on a 372,855-token cached prefix) loaded 4.5 GB from and wrote 4.5 GB back to the host pool on each PP stage. With `direct`, each stage spent 199-229 ms before its forward kernels started, while the GPU was otherwise idle. About 140 ms of that went to issuing the copies (`cudaMemcpyBatchAsync`), during which the copy engines were busy for only about 50 ms. The four stages handle the request one after another, so it spent about 0.85 s in cache handling against 80-130 ms of forward per stage. When prefill is the bottleneck, this host time caps prefill throughput. In the serving A/B below, a busy prefill worker computed 12% more tokens per second with `direct_kernel`, and about 30% more on batches with cached prefixes above 128k tokens. Median TTFT dropped 15-21%. ## Modifications The PR has four commits. title: [Perf] R3: Gather DeepEP routed-expert ids once per forward (3/3)
summary: ## Why? With a scattered MoE a2a backend (DeepEP), each attention-TP rank holds a slice of the tokens. So capture all-gathered every MoE layer's ids inside the forward: one small collective per layer, on every rank, between top-k and dispatch. ```text Before (one forward, attn-TP 4, L MoE layers) After layer 1: top-k → all-gather → device buffer layer 1: top-k → local buffer layer 2: top-k → all-gather → device buffer layer 2: top-k → local buffer ... ... layer L: top-k → all-gather → device buffer layer L: top-k → local buffer → 1 all-gather, all layers = L collectives on every rank = 1 collective ``` ## What? - Each rank writes its own tokens' ids to a local buffer. At this rank's last routed layer, `capture()` all-gathers every layer in one call: the output rank receives into its device buffer, the other ranks into a scratch buffer they ignore. Ranks hold equal, rank-ordered shares, so rows land in the order the per-layer all-gather produced. - The all-gather runs inside the forward and takes its size from the captured rows, so CUDA graphs record it with the shapes they replay. - The last routed layer is the highest `TopK.layer_id` with capture enabled on this rank (each pipeline stage finds its own), computed once in `create()`. A capture past it raises, and so does a layer whose row count differs from the first routed layer's. The per-layer all-gather stays when there is no such layer (models that call `capture()` directly), under decoder SWA bounded replay (late layers run on fewer rows), and under two-batch overlap (two sub-batches interleave their layers; #48666 pla

summary: - **`move(items, src, dst, at=)`** is the one way a request changes its owner list: it checks every request is in `src`, joins `dst`, then leaves `src`; `src=None` means a request entering its first list. `at=` inserts before a position, which replaces `prepend`; every list's `join` takes it and a keyed list rejects it. `items` may be the destination's wrappers (`req_of` maps an item back to its request). - **The side that hands requests on is `move_<what>(dst)`**: `move_bootstrapped`, `move_preallocated`, `move_transferred` / `move_transferred_with_outcomes`, `move_resumed` (was `resume_retracted_reqs`), and HiSparse `move_ready_reqs`. - **A destination keeps its add verb and takes `src`**: `_add_request_to_queue(req, *, src=None)`, the PD queues' `add`, uOCR `park` / `enqueue`, `hold_rebootstrap`, `admit_request_into_staging`, dLLM `add_waiting_reqs`. - **A request finished on its way between lists leaves through the retirer**: `RequestRetirer.abort`, `retire_unadmitted` and `abort_retracted` take `src` and take the request out of it, so a door refusal (priority, queue limit, KV capacity, an intake reject) and the retract, queue-eviction and unschedulable aborts leave their list in the same call that finishes them. - **Each scheduler path is now one move**: admission (waiting -> chunked slot or `prefill_launched`, at admission instead of at launch, so `_join_prefill_launched` goes), the merge (`prefill_launched` -> running), PD decode prebuilt (waiting -> running), HiSparse staging, grammar ready, preemption, decode retraction, the pause retract, uOCR released, PD held re

summary: ## Motivation With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, every ordinary MHA KV write on main still converts eagerly in `set_kv_buffer`: `div_` on K and on V, a cast of each, then the store. title: [Fix] hicache: settle storage backups at the rank-agreed written prefix
summary: ## Motivation Addresses the storage-write leg of #39444. A HiCache storage backup is written in 128-page batches. When a batch fails, `HiCacheController._page_backup` stops and the operation is acked with `completed_tokens` short of the request (`python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py:1513-1533` on `b50d439494`). The tree's ack drain then treated the operation as complete: in buffer mode `BufferModePipeline.finish_storage_write_ack` fed existence beliefs for every key of the write and freed the staging; in cache mode `_drain_backup` released the node's host lock. The unwritten tail was believed stored, nothing re-wrote it, and a later prefetch of that prefix stopped at the failed batch. Issue #39444 describes this on both host memory modes. Why the fix has to be rank-agreed: backup submission and acks have no collective of their own; the drain pairs operations by position across ranks after a MIN of the ack-queue sizes (`_sync_hicache_ready_counts` / `_drain_queue`), and the write-through trigger reads each rank's own tree state. A storage write can fail on one rank only (each rank writes its own KV shard; with replicated MLA KV only the writer rank writes at all). If every rank settled from its own `completed_tokens`, their beliefs would differ, the write-through trigger would fire on some ranks and not others, and the positional ack pairing would desync for good. Scope, chosen deliberately small: this is a hit-rate problem, not a reliability one, so the PR does one thing. title: [Fix] [XPU] graph: Retain capture inputs and reset graphs in FullXPUGraphBackend
summary: ## Motivation In SGLang, device graphs capture and record raw GPU virtual addresses rather than retaining Python object references. During graph capture (e.g., under data parallelism where dummy batches instantiate capture-only metadata tensors such as `global_num_tokens_gpu`), these temporary tensors must be preserved across the graph's lifetime to prevent Python GC from collecting them. If collected, the PyTorch caching allocator may reassign their underlying memory while the graph actively replays, resulting in dangling pointers, silent memory corruption, or illegal memory access errors. While `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` tracks and retains `capture_inputs`, `FullXPUGraphBackend` previously accepted the `capture_inputs` parameter in `capture_one()` but omitted storing it. Additionally, captured graphs were not explicitly reset upon backend `cleanup()`. ## Modifications 1. **Retain Capture Inputs in `FullXPUGraphBackend`** (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/graph_runner/xpu_full_graph_backend.py`): - Initialized `self._capture_inputs: Dict[Any, Any] = {}` in `__init__`. - Stored `self._capture_inputs[shape_key] = capture_inputs` in `capture_one()` so that capture-time tensor lifetimes are preserved across the backend lifecycle. - Cleared `self._capture_inputs.clear()` in `cleanup()`. 2. **Explicitly Reset Graphs upon Cleanup** (`xpu_full_graph_backend.py`): - Called `graph.reset()` on all captured `XPUGraph` instances during `cleanup()` to ensure allocated memory pool segments are cleanly released back to the driver. ## Accuracy Tests - **XPU Graph Metadata & Capture
