title: [Doc] server_args: --mem-fraction-static is a fraction of free memory at startup
summary: ## Motivation The tuning guide defines ``` mem_fraction_static = (model weights + KV cache pool) / GPU memory capacity ``` and the `--mem-fraction-static` help text says "the fraction of the memory". The code doesn't use the GPU's capacity. `KVCacheConfigurator._profile_available_bytes` sizes the pool as ``` KV budget = free memory after weights load - pre_model_load_memory * (1 - mem_fraction_static) ``` where `pre_model_load_memory` is the free memory measured just before this server loads its weights (`distributed/bootstrap.py: measure_pre_model_load_memory`). So weights + KV cache come to about `mem_fraction_static * (GPU memory free at startup)`. On a dedicated GPU, free memory and capacity are close, so the formula looks right. On a GPU shared with another process, such as a second server on the same card, they are not. A value tuned on an empty GPU then gives a much smaller pool than the guide predicts. It can also fail with `Not enough memory` even though the guide's arithmetic says it fits. We took a server down that way while relaunching it next to a running one. ## Measurement `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.7`, one H200 (143 GB). Same GPU and command, first idle, then with another process holding 70 GiB: | | GPU free before launch | Server's footprint | Footprint / free | KV cache (`#tokens`) | |---|---|---|---|---| | idle GPU | 142,727 MiB | 101,163 MiB | **0.709** | 49.9 GB (4,357,464) | | 70 GiB held by another process | 70,524 MiB | 50,138 MiB | **0.711** | 23.9 GB (2,087,654) | Footprint = `nvidia-smi` used after the server is up, minus used b

title: [Fix] [AMD] deepseek: Restore fused block-scale FP8 projections on gfx950 and fix the MHA_ONE_SHOT KV reload
summary: ## Motivation On AMD MI355X GPUs, FP8 models such as DeepSeek-V3.2 miss SGLang's faster fused FP8 kernels. The check that turns them on looks for the wrong weight name, so it never fires. This PR fixes the check, which makes decoding 1.4 to 2.2% faster on DeepSeek-V3.2. It also fixes a crash that the faster path would otherwise cause on requests that reuse a cached prompt prefix. On gfx950, the DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V3.1 and GLM-5.1-FP8 checkpoints store block scales as `weight_scale_inv`, but `_is_block_scale_fp8` looks only for `weight_scale`, so the fused FP8 projection paths (`fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` before `q_b_proj` and `kv_b_proj`, `fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant` before `o_proj`, and the fused RMSNorm + FP8 quant at the attention input) are never selected. Once they are, an `MHA_ONE_SHOT` prefix reload passes `kv_b_proj` a quantized tensor that covers only the new tokens, and the server crashes, so the two fixes must land together. The reload fix and its CPU test come from #41408 by @salexspb, carried here as the first commit under their name, so one PR covers the bug. ## Modifications - **Detection** (`deepseek_common/utils.py`, `_is_block_scale_fp8`; `deepseek_v2.py`, `_detect_gfx95_quant_format`): accept `weight_scale` or `weight_scale_inv`, and require FP8 weights, a 2-D scale and a K-block of 128; per-channel and group-32 MXFP8 scales stay rejected. Both sites need the fix. title: [Fix] scheduler: pause generation in abort mode to ensure idle release
summary: Closes #44840 ## Motivation `pause_generation(mode="abort")` can return before the scheduler has freed the KV of every request, so a `release_memory_occupation` (or `flush_cache`) sent right after it is refused. Since #48757 this is an error instead of a scheduler crash, but the pause still does not leave the engine idle. Repro: with `--enable-memory-saver`, disconnect a streamed `/generate`, then immediately call `/pause_generation {"mode": "abort"}` and `/release_memory_occupation`. 1. The disconnect makes the tokenizer send an `AbortReq` for the request and lets its handler exit. 2. Abort mode never reached the scheduler: the tokenizer sent `abort_all` and returned once `model_update_lock` had no handler left. The disconnected request's handler was already gone, so this returned at once. 3. In the scheduler, `abort_request` only requests the finish (`request_finish(FINISH_ABORT())`); a running request frees its KV at its next step. The release arrives before that step, sees a non-empty `running_batch`, and is refused. ## Modifications - `scheduler.py`: `pause_generation` accepts `mode="abort"` and runs the retract path: it drains the in-flight overlap result and retracts every request holding KV, freeing it, into the waiting queue. - `tokenizer_manager.py`: abort mode sends the pause to the scheduler before `_abort_all_until_unlocked()`. Both go over the same socket, so the scheduler pauses first, the `abort_all` then drops the retracted requests from the waiting queue, and a later `release_memory_occupation` finds the engine idle. - `multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: the route

title: [Fix] hicache: keep the storage ack sequence on backend failures, stop workers in lockstep, fail the rank when a worker dies
summary: ## Motivation HiCache's four storage worker threads (prefetch query, prefetch IO, prefetch sync, backup) are started per rank in `HiCacheController._start_storage_threads` and nothing watched them. This PR is hardening for three situations that recent features opened up; none of them has a field report, and the symptom of the first is a silent freeze, which is why. 1. An exception could escape a worker and nobody noticed. The classic cache-mode transfer loop has nothing that can raise outside its inner per-batch guard, but the hybrid path (#20457 and its follow-ups) added call sites in front of and around it: the unified host layout lease taken around the whole transfer (poisoned on acquire, raising on release), the trailing sidecar chain (`_sync_trailing_keys`, `_resolve_sidecar_nonkv_derived_pool_transfers`) before the sidecar ack, and the trace initialisation of #37976 on dequeue. `prefetch_io_aux_func` ran `_page_transfer` under `try/finally` with no `except`, so an exception at one of those sites published the final ack and killed the thread. From then on the hit path kept allocating host bounces that only this thread's acks free: the host pool filled, hits parked forever, and under the default `timeout` policy requests kept being admitted with no L3 benefit; under `wait_complete` they never admitted. No log line said why, and on the hybrid controller the skipped sidecar ack also desynchronised this rank's ack sequence from its peers'. The response chosen here is to crash the rank: an escaping exception stays a rare event, keeping the worker alive by inventing the miss

summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #49312 * #49311 * #49310 * #49309 * #49301 * __->__ #49300 * #49299 ## Motivation Sub-pools of the unified pool share one byte arena, and a request's demand mixes per-token units (tokens, window rows) with per-request units (state slots) in proportions that differ by request. title: [Fix] cp: Embed the full sequence when a CP hook returns no embeddings
summary: ## Motivation `EagerRunner._execute_extend_cp` has two branches that disagree about who embeds. The branch **without** a `prepare_cp_inputs` hook embeds the full layout itself and only then shards: ```python input_embeds = kwargs.get("input_embeds") if input_embeds is None: input_embeds = model.get_input_embeddings()(forward_batch.input_ids) ``` The branch **with** the hook trusts whatever the model returned. A model that only prepares positions/metadata and returns `None` embeddings (a text-only extend is the common case) leaves `input_embeds` unset, and `cp_shard_model_inputs` still hands the model the rank-local token shard. Embedding that shard is not a local operation: CP splits tokens across ranks, so the ids a rank holds are unrelated to the ones its peers hold, while `VocabParallelEmbedding.forward` ends in a tensor-parallel all-reduce (`vocab_parallel_embedding.py`). The all-reduce then sums embeddings of **different tokens** into every row, and the rank computes the whole layer stack on corrupted hidden states. What makes this expensive to diagnose is that it is partial: multimodal batches stay correct because their embeddings are produced over the full sequence before the shard, so only pure-text requests come back wrong — and not as an error. They come back as fluent garbage of the right length and grammatical shape with the wrong content. We hit it while porting a vision+CP model onto v0.5.23: images answered correctly, every text answer was nonsense; turning prefill CP off restored correct output, which is what pointed at the embedding stage. ## Modifications

summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49368. DeepSeek-V2/V2.5 checkpoints with static per-tensor FP8 scales in compressed-tensors format (e.g. `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V2.5-1210-FP8`) fail to load: ``` AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([1]) ... loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([2]) ``` `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with a single per-tensor scale. When the loader fuses `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, it special-cases only 0-d scale pairs (and keeps `q_a_proj`'s scale, which is wrong when the two differ) and concatenates everything else. compressed-tensors stores per-tensor scales as `[1]`, so `weight_scale` / `input_scale` become `[2]`. ## Modifications In `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin.do_load_weights`: - A `weight_scale` / `input_scale` pair with one element each (0-d or `[1]`) loads `max(q_a, kv_a)` into the fused layer. - When the two weight scales differ, the fused FP8 weight rows of the projection with the smaller scale are rescaled to the max once loading finishes. title: [Feat] spec: Add EXTERNAL speculative decoding algorithm
summary: A new speculative decoding mode where the draft model runs in a separate process over a ZMQ wire protocol. SGLang handles verification, KV cache, and scheduling, while the external drafter produces the draft tokens. - ExternalWorker: chain verification using the existing mask-driven path - Wire contract (msgspec.msgpack): language-agnostic, no SGLang imports - Transport interface: abstract + ZMQ implementation - TP > 1: rank 0 receives drafts, broadcasts to other ranks - 23 unit tests (contract, transport, server_args guards, enum) <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation SGLang's existing speculative decoding modes (EAGLE, NGRAM, DFLASH, etc.) all run the drafter inside the same worker as the target model, on shared GPUs and out of the same memory pool. This works well when the drafter is a small neural network that fits alongside the target, but it rules out drafters that run on different hardware (custom accelerators, CPUs, FPGAs) or in a separate process with their own runtime. This PR adds a new `EXTERNAL` speculative decoding algorithm where the draft model runs in a separate process that SGLang does not own. SGLang keeps the target model, KV cache, verification, sampling, and scheduling. The external process owns the draft model entirely: weights, KV cache, compute. The only thing crossing the boundary is token IDs and control signals. ##

title: [RFC] Disaggregated request preprocessing
summary:
### Motivation Before a model runs, the serving system often needs to know what the request will look like to the model: - A router places and sizes work before a request reaches a GPU: how long the request is, whether its prefix is already cached, and whether its media is already processed. - A disaggregated pipeline prepares a request once and hands the model the tokens, instead of re-tokenizing at each hop. For both cases, the prepared request has to match what the model actually runs. When it does not, cache lookups can miss and token counts can be wrong (#26555, #27386, [llm-d-router#1072](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1072)). This proposal exposes that request view before execution, so routing and model servers do not rely on approximations. ### Proposal

The goal is to expose the same preprocessing path used by SGLang inference as a lightweight standalone service that returns the prepared generate request without running the model. In particular, this should: - Run as a CPU-light preprocessing-only server. - Share the exact preprocessing logic used by normal SGLang inference endpoints. - Return a generate request, not just raw token IDs, with the metadata needed for tokens-in/tokens-out. - Include multimodal hashes and related metadata in the tokenize/preprocess output, so encoder-disaggregated setups can route and reuse MM encoder work consistently. **Before and after:** Today, chat and completions requests can b

title: [Fix] attention: Keep sigmoid(beta) in fp32 in GDN/KDA decode kernels
summary: The GDN packed decode kernel and the GDN/KDA linear-replay decode kernel rounded sigmoid(beta) through the activation dtype: beta_val = tl.sigmoid(b_val).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) The rounded beta feeds the delta-rule update of the persistent SSM state, so the rounding error enters the state once per decode step and accumulates with context length: state rel-L2 reaches 1.4e-3 after 1000 decode steps, vs 1e-7 with the round-trip removed. The failure is silent (outputs stay well-formed, per-op tolerances stay green). The same line was fixed in vLLM in vllm-project/vllm#53877 (the packed decode kernel originated there; sglang#20627 imported it pre-fix) but was never ported. title: [Perf] hicache: Enable async ready-count sync by default
summary: Adapt based on @nvrohanv 's draft. ## Motivation With `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, the scheduler calls `check_hicache_events` every step. It counts each rank's completed write-back (D→H) and load-back (H→D) acks and MIN-all-reduces the counts over the attention-TP CPU group. That way every rank consumes the same acks and the radix trees stay identical. The all-reduce is a **blocking gloo collective on the critical path of every step, decode included**. The overlap scheduler hides it while the GPU step is long. Once the GPU step is short, as with fast decode kernels or small or sparse models at low concurrency, the CPU loop becomes the critical path. That one collective then adds directly to every decode step. ## Modifications Async ready-count sync, **on by default**. `--disable-hicache-async-ready-sync` restores the blocking per-step sync, which is what stock main does, for example when debugging. In the results below, **flag on** is this PR's default and **flag off** is `--disable-hicache-async-ready-sync`, which is identical to stock main. The data was collected while the flag was still opt-in; the code paths are the same. - The ready-count all-reduce is issued with `async_op=True` on a **dedicated gloo group** in step N and consumed in step N+1. - Safety rests on two invariants: 1. Acks complete in queue order, and queues only grow at the tail. So a prefix that was ready on every rank in step N is still ready in step N+1. 2. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation DSpark proposes a block of γ draft tokens in one parallel forward. It then corrects them with a serial Markov walk. At step k: ``` logits_k = base_k + W2 · W1[x_{k-1}] (rank 256, full vocabulary) x_k = argmax or sample of logits_k ``` The folded draft graph runs this walk as γ separate steps. Each step is a bf16 GEMM that re-reads all of W2 from HBM (78 MB at Qwen3's 151,936-token vocabulary), followed by `MarkovSampleStep`. On an H100 at γ = 7 the walk costs 269 µs per round at bs = 1 and 453 µs at bs = 64; at γ = 16 and bs = 1 it costs 608 µs. This PR adds an opt-in replacement for that walk, for every draft graph bucket up to bs = 64: - one persistent cooperative launch runs all γ steps; - an int8 copy of W2 is spread over the SMs: each keeps most of its share in shared memory and streams the rest from L2; - the bias is computed with exact int32 tensor-core dot products; - each step's tokens are chosen across all SMs with one atomic `{key, count}` exchange per request. Results: - The walk alone runs 3.3-6.5x faster than the default walk (table below). - End to end, client output throughput rises by 1.2-9.0% on six real target / drafter pairs (table below). - Greedy outputs are unchanged. summary: # [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Route radix4 on bf16 with the cached bias, drop the per-call cast Branch: `kimi_k3_rocm_radix4_avoid_extra_dtype_conversion` (one commit on `main`). ## Motivation `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK=1` (off by default) opts Kimi-K3 on ROCm into the radix4 router. This pull request makes bf16 the routing precision under that flag: radix4 routes on the bf16 router logits against a cached bf16 copy of the correction bias. That removes an elementwise kernel that ran before the router in every MoE layer, casting the `[num_tokens, 896]` logits to fp32, so the radix4 path launches only the router kernel. Kimi-K3 holds `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32, and `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` currently matches the logits to it before either router runs: ```python if correction_bias.dtype == torch.float32: route_logits = gating_output.to(torch.float32) route_bias = correction_bias ``` The radix4 kernel accepts bf16 scores with a bf16 bias and widens both to fp32 in-register, so on its path the cast costs a launch per layer per forward. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: - `select_experts`: when the bias is fp32, aiter is in use, and `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK` is set, it fetches `TopKConfig.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)` and passes it down as `radix4_bias`. That copy is built once, lazily, and keyed on the bias's `data_ptr` and `_version`, so a weight reload rebuilds it and nothing is cast per call. title: [Feat] [NPU] dsa: Shard indexer prefill queries across attention TP (1/2)
summary: ## Motivation On Ascend, the DSA indexer is the most expensive part of long-context prefill, and every attention-TP rank runs all of it. Each rank scores every query against every key, so the O(n²) work is repeated `attn_tp_size` times. On GLM-5.2, Ascend A3, a single 1M-token prefill, the indexer is most of TTFT: about 83%, inferred from the speed-up below. A single-die probe of the indexer operator alone measured 61%. Every rank already holds the full index-K. So only the queries need to be split, and the work divides by `attn_tp_size` with no change to the KV layout and no extra KV memory. ## Modifications - `dsa_npu_indexer.py`: in prefill, each attention-TP rank scores `1/attn_tp_size` of the indexer queries. The top-k indices are then all-gathered over attention TP, so every rank still ends with the top-k for every token. - The rank also projects only its own rows through `wq_b` and the query rotary. A Linear acts on each row alone, so this gives the same rows as projecting everything and slicing. Only for neox-style rotary. - `dsa_token_shard_layout.py` (new): the row plan. Rows are split `ceil(T / attn_tp_size)` per rank, and the query tensor may be padded to a multiple of `attn_tp_size`. - The gate turns it off at attention TP 1, for decode and speculative passes (only plain and mixed extend shard), for prefill CP, when the attention input is scattered, and when the query tensor's width is outside `[real tokens, rows * attn_tp_size]`. - `SGLANG_NPU_ENABLE_DSA_INDEXER_QUERY_SHARDING`, **default on**. title: [Fix] cuda-graph: Pause automatic GC during CUDA graph capture
summary: ## Motivation `freeze_gc` wraps CUDA graph capture unless `--enable-cudagraph-gc` is set. It collects once and freezes the surviving objects, but leaves automatic collection running. Objects allocated inside the capture loop, for example by `torch.compile` warmup and autotuning before each batch size, can therefore be collected while a stream is capturing. When one of them is a kernel whose finalizer unloads its GPU module, the unload is rejected on the capturing stream (error 900) and the capture is invalidated (error 901). Two finalizers do this: - Triton's `CompiledKernel.__del__`. Whether a collection lands inside a capture depends on allocation counts, so the failure is intermittent: the same command can capture cleanly on one run and crash on the next. ## Modifications - `freeze_gc` calls `gc.disable()` after `gc.freeze()`. title: [Fix] gemma4: Honor OOT attention defaults
summary: ## Motivation SGLang's generic attention-backend resolution lets an out-of-tree platform provide its default through `SRTPlatform.get_default_attention_backend()`. title: [Perf] [CPU] graph: Move SWA index translation into Intel AMX attention kernels and prune masked prefix loads
summary: ## Motivation In the existing CPU Intel AMX attention backend, sliding-window attention (SWA) layers perform dynamic slicing and gathering in Python (`_swa_kv_indices`): ```python rows = req_to_token[req_pool_indices, : int(seq_lens.max())] translated = self.runner_ids.ids_in(IdSpaceKind.SLIDING_WINDOW, rows) ``` This introduces several critical performance and stability bottlenecks: 1. **CPU Graph (`torch.compile`) Recompilations**: `int(seq_lens.max())` converts a dynamic tensor scalar into a Python `int`, establishing a strict TorchDynamo value guard. During autoregressive decoding where `seq_lens` increments every step, this guard fails on every iteration, triggering continuous recompilation and breaking graph execution. 2. **Host-Side Allocation Overhead**: Creating transient 2D tensors and `arange` indices on every step in the Python hot path causes allocator lock contention and CPU cache pollution. 3. **Redundant Gathering of Expired Tokens**: Slicing up to `seq_lens.max()` gathers and translates tokens that have already slid out of the sliding window. 4. **Pointer Stability for Graph Replay**: CPU graph capture bakes the underlying `data_ptr` of write-location tensors into the compiled graph; re-allocating new tensors during replay risks stale pointer dereferencing. This PR moves full-to-SWA index mapping into the C++ attention kernels, prunes out-of-window prefix computations during extend attention, and ensures static memory pointer stability during CPU graph capture and replay. ## Modifications 1. **In-Kernel SWA Index Translation (`csrc/cpu/`)**: - Extended `dec

title: [Fix] [AMD] quark: do not declare the MiniMax-M3 TP8 MoE pad to CK-Tile
summary: ## Motivation MiniMax-M3 on TP8 falls into repetitive loops in normal mode (AIME25 0/30). Answers start fine, then repeat one line until the 32,768-token cap. - At TP8 each GPU holds 384 of the expert's 512 intermediate columns, so the weights are zero-padded from 384 to 512. - AITER's CK-Tile SwiGLU stage-1 kernel returns wrong output at decode batch sizes when it is told about that padding. - The padding is zeros, so the fix is to stop declaring it on this path: SwiGLU-OAI passes `intermediate_pad=0` and keeps the padded weights. - Result: AIME25 24/30 and 26/30, GSM8K 95.83%, one-request decode 202 tok/s vs 203 stock. - This fix is only that SGLang change. It runs on the AITER build already in the image. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/3862 is a closed transformers import error and is not used here. The same kernel idea was proposed in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3862 and closed without merging. title: [Doc] forward-hooks: Say that hooks don't run under CUDA graphs
summary: Fixes #45317 ## Motivation The forward hooks page says hooks are attached in `ModelRunner.initialize` and "run on every forward pass". That's not what happens. Hooks are registered **after** CUDA graph capture (`finalize_cuda_graph_capture`), and CUDA graph replay never runs Python hooks. With default settings on CUDA, decode and prefill both use CUDA graphs, so a hook can silently never run. In #45317, a hook on `model.layers.14` of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (v0.5.21, NVIDIA L4) ran **0 times** for a 128-token request with default settings. It ran **128 times** with CUDA graphs disabled. ## Modifications Docs only: `docs/docs/advanced_features/forward_hooks.mdx`. - Fix the intro line: hooks are attached after CUDA graph capture and don't run on graph replay. - "Hook lifecycle": replace the old `ModelRunner.initialize()` snippet with the real registration code from `finalize_cuda_graph_capture`. - Key points: say hooks run only on the eager path. - New section **"Hooks and CUDA graphs"**: why hooks don't run, and how to make them run on every step (`--disable-decode-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph`, or the engine kwargs `disable_decode_cuda_graph=True, disable_prefill_cuda_graph=True`). It also notes that this lowers throughput. - Summary: same correction. No code changes. A startup warning when `forward_hooks` are set while CUDA graphs are on could be a follow-up PR. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable (docs only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable (docs only). For context, #45317 has the throughput cost of disabling CUDA graphs on an L4. ## Checklist - [x] Form

title: [Perf] dsv4: Enable overlap scheduling for online C128 MTP
summary: Follow up of #30365. ## Problem The experimental online C128 MTP target-verify path added in #26471 still uses the host prefill planner. #30365 removed the sequence-length D2H dependency from the other DSV4 speculative paths, but intentionally preserved the CPU path for online C128 MTP. That path requires CPU sequence lengths and a pinned plan buffer, introducing a D2H synchronization on every verify step and preventing it from working with the overlap scheduler. ## Solution - Add a single fixed-shape CUDA kernel to the online C128 C++ planner for MTP target verification. It emits the `CompressPlan` records and does the request-to-state-slot finalization in the same launch. - Read int64 device sequence lengths and request-pool indices directly, without a host round trip. - Use the MTP bound of at most 8 draft tokens to emit at most one close-chunk plan and one trailing-partial plan per request. - Mask inactive padded requests with the runtime active batch size, including zero-active/idle replay, so CUDA graphs cannot reuse stale compression plans. - Keep target-verify sequence lengths and compression metadata on device, remove the pinned CPU plan buffer, and remove the separate Triton planner. ### Planner equivalence The CUDA kernel emits the native `CompressPlan` records for the MTP target-verify subset and finalizes them to state slots in the same launch. title: [Feat] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: Avoid padded PLE prefill activations
summary: ## Summary This PR fixes Qwen3.8/Qwen4Exp PLE prefill temporary activation amplification for mixed-length batches. The current PLE short-conv prefill path materializes packed tokens as a dense tensor: ```text [num_requests, max_query_length, ple_channels] ``` This means short requests are padded to the longest request in the batch. For skewed mixed-length batches, the temporary activation memory scales with: ```text num_requests × max_query_length × ple_channels ``` instead of: ```text sum(query_lengths) × ple_channels ``` This can allocate several GiB of temporary tensors and cause OOM even when KV cache utilization is still low. This PR adds a packed varlen Triton path for ordinary PLE prefill so short-conv memory and compute scale with the actual scheduled tokens. ### Nsight Systems serving trace To verify that the packed kernel is selected in the serving path, we profiled a single HTTP batched request containing four sequences: ```text query lengths = [8192, 1, 1, 1], new sequences = 4, new tokens = 8195, cached tokens = 0 ``` The following traces compare the same TP rank and GPU. summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug For diffusion/video generation workloads, the Prometheus metric: `sglang:diffusion_num_queue_reqs` does not immediately reflect all requests that are already accepted by the HTTP server and waiting for execution. When the Scheduler is executing a long-running diffusion request, subsequent requests can remain pending between `AsyncSchedulerClient` and the Scheduler's ZMQ receiver. These requests are not counted until the Scheduler returns to `recv_reqs()` and inserts them into `waiting_queue`. As a result, the queue metric may remain at zero, or report a value lower than the number of requests actually waiting from the client's perspective. ### Reproduction 1. Start an SGLang diffusion/video generation service with metrics enabled. 2. Configure the service to execute one generation request at a time. 3. Submit one long-running video generation request. 4. While the first request is running, submit three additional requests. 5. Query /metrics immediately: curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/metrics | grep diffusion_num ### Environment Environment - SGLang commit: b2616cabbf - Runtime: SGLang multimodal/diffusion -

title: [Tracking] Predictable long-context agent serving: APIs, cache usage, and resource lifetime
summary: ## Motivation An agent reuses a long system/document prefix across turns, sends both cold and warm requests, sometimes includes images or video, and may cancel an interrupted turn before continuing. Clients use Python Chat, Responses, or Messages. To operate this workload, they need consistent input/tool semantics and usage, bounded work at each stage, and a clear distinction between cancellation accepted, generation finished, and resources released. **The goal is predictable request behavior under this mixed workload, with enough accounting and tracing to explain latency and capacity.** K3 is one motivating deployment; most of the API, scheduler, and lifetime changes have broader uses. This issue connects the existing patches and records their boundaries. summary: Closes #49519. ## Motivation With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, a text prompt sent to `/generate` is encoded without `<bos>` for tokenizers that rely on `add_bos_token`, such as Gemma 4. The Python frontend adds it. On Gemma 4, `few_shot_gsm8k` (raw `/generate`) drops from 0.940 on Python to 0.797 on Rust. Details are in #49519. title: fix(quantization): per-stream Marlin workspaces to prevent cross-stream CTA deadlock under PD-Multiplexing
summary: Fixes #37904 ## Part 1 — prerequisite: repair stale Scheduler fields (PDMux cannot start on current main) `multiplexing_mixin.py` still reads `self.gpu_id` / `self.tp_size`, fields that no longer exist on `Scheduler` (they moved to `ParallelState`). PDMux raises in `initialize_stream_groups` before the model loads. Replaced with `self.ps.gpu_id` / `self.ps.tp_size`, matching the pattern used elsewhere in `scheduler.py`. ## Part 2 — the deadlock fix Under `--enable-pdmux`, the decode forward and the split-prefill slice of the **same layer** run concurrently on two green-context streams. Marlin kernels use `workspace` as a cross-CTA lock array (`barrier_acquire` waits for exact counter equality) and assume every launch touching one workspace is serialized on a single stream. Sharing one per-layer workspace lets both launches corrupt the barrier counters and a CTA spins forever — the scheduler hangs in `decode_stream.synchronize()` at 99% SM, and the watchdog never fires. Repro and device-side evidence (cuda-gdb naming the spinning Marlin kernel, py-spy stacks, measured before/after): #37904. Three helpers in `marlin_utils`, wired through **every** remaining consumer of a shared per-layer workspace (FP8-Marlin dense prepare, NVFP4/MXFP4 prepares, modelopt FP8/FP4 branches, compressed-tensors w8a16_fp8 / wNa16 dense + MoE; the classic MarlinConfig method and `prepare_moe_fp8_layer_for_marlin` were removed from main after this fix was prepared, and `moe_runner/marlin.py` already allocates per-call workspaces — both intentionally untouched): - `marlin_stream_workspaces_enabled()`

title: [Perf] [NPU] sampling: threshold top-k/top-p renormalization instead of a full-vocabulary scatter
summary: ## Motivation `top_{k,p}_renorm_prob` keeps the top-k / nucleus entries in the sorted space and then scatters them back to their original token positions: ```python torch.zeros_like(probs).scatter_(-1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted_probs) ``` On Ascend NPU that random write over the full vocabulary dominates the operator: measured at ~85% of its cost, ~3.1 ms for a 4 x 154880 block on 910B. Speculative verify runs this operator on every verify step, so the write lands on the decode critical path. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_threshold.py`: after the sorted mask, read the smallest kept *unrenormalized* probability as the pivot and keep every entry `probs >= pivot`. The pivot lives on the same scale as `probs`, so the kept set is the one the scatter form writes back; the row is renormalized once at the end. Only aten ops (`sort`, `cumsum`, `masked_fill`, `sum`), no scatter. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm.py`: the NPU entry of the per-platform table resolves to the threshold module instead of `sgl_kernel_npu.sample`. title: [Feat] observability: Expose HiSparse device and host cache metrics
summary: ## Motivation HiSparse maintains two KV cache tiers with different capacity domains: - a bounded device working set - a larger host KV pool The generic KV cache metrics cannot accurately represent both tiers. For example, with `host_to_device_ratio=3`, an idle decode instance may report 66.67% through `sglang:token_usage`, because the host-expanded logical capacity is compared with device allocator availability. HiSparse already calculates device and host occupancy separately, but these values are not exposed through Prometheus. ## Modifications Expose the following HiSparse-specific Prometheus metrics: - `sglang:hisparse_device_used_tokens` - `sglang:hisparse_device_total_tokens` - `sglang:hisparse_device_token_usage` - `sglang:hisparse_host_used_tokens` - `sglang:hisparse_host_total_tokens` - `sglang:hisparse_host_token_usage` The metrics are registered only when HiSparse is enabled. This change preserves the existing generic KV cache metrics for backward compatibility. Added unit tests covering: - coordinator-to-observer capacity propagation - zero usage for idle device and host pools - correct usage for partially occupied pools - omission of HiSparse metrics when HiSparse is disabled ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only exposes observability metrics and does not modify model execution or outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. summary: ## Problem With the default overlap scheduler and `--enable-return-routed-experts`, DSpark rollouts return all-zero or stale routed-expert IDs for generated tokens. Target verification computes them, but `TargetVerifyResult` and the final `GenerationBatchResult` drop the deferred capture outputs, so the scheduler never copies them to the host. With routing replay in RL (Miles R3), the trainer replays these IDs, so generated tokens are trained through expert 0 instead of the experts the rollout actually used. ## Change Forward the routed-expert, indexer top-k and KV-version capture outputs from target verification to the generation result, as the EAGLE and DFLASH paths already do. ## Validation On a 43-layer DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 RL rollout on 32 MI355X GPUs, 1,651,456 of 1,654,253 generated positions per layer had all-zero experts before this change; after it, every generated position returns six distinct, in-range experts. The first training step's routing-replay mismatch dropped from 1,935/2,176 tokens to 22/2,176, in line with 23/2,176 without speculative decoding. title: fix(sm120): fall back to Triton per call when FlashInfer lacks the prefill shape
summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND` picks one sparse-MLA implementation for the whole process, and the default `flashinfer` backend has a fixed prefill instantiation envelope in C++ (`sparse_mla_prefill_dispatch`): * single cache: `topk ∈ {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024, 2048}` * dual cache (hierarchical candidate pool, DSV4 only): `topk == 128` and `extra_page_block_size ∈ {64, 2}` Outside that envelope the C++ returns `false` and **aborts the engine**: ``` tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (ok) is false: Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=8 topk=128 page_block_size=64 topk_extra=512 extra_page_block_size=128 ``` DeepSeek-V4.1's hierarchical candidate pool pages its extra KV cache at 128 (and 256) tokens, so serving that model on SM120 currently requires the global `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton`, which gives up FlashInfer for *every* call — including the decode and single-cache shapes FlashInfer handles well. ## Modifications * Add `_flashinfer_covers(q, indices, extra_k_cache, extra_indices)`, a predicate mirroring the C++ prefill envelope (decode short-circuits to `True`; the decode dispatch table already covers the `(num_heads, topk)` pairs this model uses). * In `flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120`, when the default backend is `flashinfer` and the shape is outside the envelope, log once per call at `info` and route **that call** to the existing Triton implementation. * No change when the backend is explicitly `triton`/`torch`, and no change for shapes FlashInfer covers. Companion change: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5121 instantia

title: [Fix] openai: Validate sampling bounds and preserve chat output limits
summary: ## Motivation Several invalid sampling values pass request parsing and only fail later, in serving or in the scheduler. Chat output-limit handling also used `max_completion_tokens or max_tokens`, so an explicit `0` fell back to the legacy limit. Observed on a live server (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, vocab size 151936): - A huge `n` is rejected only after the request has been expanded `n` times: `/generate` with `n=3,000,000` took ~113 s and grew server memory by ~18 GB before returning 400. On `main`, `n=300,000` did not complete within 15 minutes and server memory passed 90 GB. `n=0` was not rejected with a clear message. - `top_logprobs` above the vocab size (for example 200000) kills the server, because `torch.topk` fails past the vocab size. A list or negative `top_logprobs_num` garbles a batch. A request with logprobs off can crash it too: its count is not checked, but the scheduler takes `topk` over every request's count when any request in the same prefill batch wants logprobs. - A large `logit_bias` overflows to `inf` in the float32 bias tensor, or after the sampler divides by a temperature below 1, and NaNs the softmax. title: [Bug] ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: layers with an unsupported quant_algo (FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN) are built unquantized and load FP8 codes as BF16 values
summary: ### Describe the bug `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` builds a linear layer with the method of its per-layer `quant_algo` (`FP8`, `FP8_PB_WO`/`FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`, `MXFP8`, `NVFP4`, `W4A16_NVFP4`) and returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for any other algorithm. `from_config` does not check the algorithms either. So a mixed-precision checkpoint with a layer kind SGLang has no branch for loads without an error: the layer is built in BF16, the stored FP8 codes are copied in as if they were BF16 values, and the per-channel `weight_scale` is skipped (only a `Parameter ...weight_scale not found in params_dict` log line). `AEON-7/Qwen3.8-27B-AEON-ULTIMATE-UNCENSORED-NVFP4-MIXED` (ModelOpt 0.46.0, about 10k downloads last month) stores 232 attention projections as `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` and 168 MLP projections as `NVFP4`. On SGLang the attention projections are `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. For layer 0's `linear_attn.out_proj`, loaded with its real weight and scale, the output on random BF16 inputs reaches 41728 against 60.9 for the dequantized reference (relative error about 6.6e3). vLLM builds the same layer with `ModelOptLinearMethod` and matches the reference (relative error 0.026). ### Reproduction ```python from sglang.srt.layers.linear import LinearBase from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig cfg = ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.from_config({ "quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "MIXED_PRECISION", "ignore": [], "quantized_layers": { "model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj": {"quant_algo": "FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN"}, "

title: [Feat] deepseek-v4: Rebuild the evicted SWA window on a cache hit instead of prefilling again
summary: ## Motivation - DeepSeek-V4 keeps two kinds of KV for a cached prefix: the full KV (compressed entries and indexer keys) and a smaller sliding-window (SWA) KV. Under memory pressure the SWA KV of an idle prefix is evicted first. - On main, a request that reuses such a prefix gets no cache hit. It prefills the whole prefix again even though the full KV is still on the GPU. - This PR rebuilds the SWA KV instead. It replays only the last tokens of the prefix (5,632 for V4-Flash) and reads everything older from the cached full KV. - On a 120K-token prompt the request after an eviction takes 0.21 s instead of 2.21 s. - This is a smaller take on #31713 by @jellysnack. The replay length and the "at least twice the replay length" threshold come from that PR. ## Modifications - New server flag `--enable-swa-recompute`, off by default. - Replay length: `ceil_align(ceil_align(W, page) + (L - 1) * W, page)` for window `W` and `L` layers. Layer `l` needs window rows built from layer `l - 1`, one window further back each time, so only the last window of the replay is exact and only that window is kept. - Cache side (`unified_cache/swa_recompute.py`): - A match reports how many full-KV tokens a replay would make reusable. Prefixes that would save less than twice the replay length are prefilled again as before. - When the request is admitted, fresh SWA rows are bound to the replayed tokens and the last window is attached to the tree. The other rows are scratch and are freed after the forward. The bind runs right before the admission is committed, after the last exit. If it fails, the reque

title: [Speculative] Derive the DSpark verify-budget cost table at CUDA graph capture
summary: Co-authored-by: Weiwei Zhang (@jerrynlp) ## Summary Under `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact` and without `--speculative-dspark-sps-table-path`, DSpark's verify-budget scheduler runs on the **uninitialized (flat) SPS table**, and under it the scheduler's `argmax` is provably pinned to verify-all: present, wired, and mathematically unable to trim. **This PR makes that configuration fast**, by measuring the real capacity curve from the CUDA graphs that capture has *already recorded* and installing it into the additive cost model SGLang already defines, so the scheduler starts making the decisions it was written to make. **What the planner maximises — `theta = tau_star × sps` — and the additive cost model that supplies the step time behind it both already exist upstream, and neither changes here.** This fills in the table they were written for, and adds one guard (`min_predicted_gain`, default 0.0, so a table loaded from disk still gets a plain argmax). A pinned `--speculative-dspark-sps-table-path` keeps precedence. It is opt-in via `SGLANG_DSPARK_ENABLE_CAPTURE_DERIVED_SPS=1`, and every new code path is gated on a table this PR measured itself, so with the variable unset the engine behaves exactly as it does today. - **Performance** (H200, compact ragged verify): Qwen3-14B tp1 **+14.4%** at concurrency 48 and **+24.1%** at 64; Qwen3-8B tp1 **+8.3%** and **+5.6%**. summary: ## Motivation Related to #48963. summary: ## Motivation On Kimi-K3, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` is the useful serving configuration: it halves the KDA state pool (6.9 GiB vs 13.8 GiB per rank at 900 slots) and that memory goes to MLA KV, which is what actually limits concurrency at long context. The fused KDA decode path does not run on a BF16 pool on NVIDIA. In `models/kimi_k3.py` the fused FlashInfer consumer (#48859) is armed only when ```python if (mamba.linear_attn_decode_backend == "flashinfer" and ssm_is_fp32 # <- hard gate and spec is none and sm in ((10, 0), (10, 3))): layer._k3_flashinfer_fused_decode = prepare_fused_kda_decode(...) ``` so a BF16 pool never prepares the adapter and decode takes the recurrent path instead. title: [Fix] dsv4: Fix draft-extend CUDA graph padding and WAR ordering
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30853. Enabling DSV4 draft-extend CUDA graphs exposes two correctness issues: 1. Graph-bucket padding uses seq_len=1. When the captured draft width is 4, uniform-width expansion produces causal lengths [-2, -1, 0, 1], and therefore negative positions and invalid attention metadata for padded rows. 2. DSV4 translates out_cache_loc through the live full-to-SWA mapping inside the captured graph. The runner currently publishes the scheduler WAR read-done event before replay, so the schedule stream may overwrite shared mapping state while replay is still reading it. ## Changes - Clamp DSV4 uniform-width causal lengths to 1, keeping padding on reserved slot 0 while leaving valid requests unchanged. - Add an explicit AttentionBackend capability for replay-time shared-buffer reads. - Defer the draft-extend WAR read-done event until after replay only for DSV4; other backends retain the pre-replay fast path. - Add focused CPU tests for padding metadata and both event-order modes. This follows the same padded-row underflow diagnosis fixed for DSA in #30378. title: [Perf] linker: Load DSpark draft KV with the last transfer layers
summary: ## Motivation The direct linker maps sidecar draft depth `i` to transfer layer `i` (#48125). With grouped layer loads (#45106), all five M3.1 DSpark draft layers fall in the first layer group. Target layer 0 waits on that group before it can start. summary: ## Motivation `TransferReady` holds two events: the page indices from the scheduler stream, and the forward that may still use the destination slots (#45580). title: [Perf] model_loader: Stage weight copies to the GPU through pinned memory
summary: ## Motivation Weight loaders copy slices of memory-mapped safetensors tensors to the GPU with `Tensor.copy_`. The source is pageable memory. On MI355X, measured inside the SGLang ROCm container: - a pageable host-to-device copy from the page cache runs at 7-8 GB/s regardless of chunk size and torch thread count, and a strided slice (the row-parallel w2 shard of `_load_w2`) at 2.0 GB/s with one torch thread; - a copy from pinned memory to the GPU runs at 57 GB/s; - a single-threaded CPU memcpy from the page cache into pinned memory runs at 97 GB/s. Staging the large copies through pinned buffers shortens the load, provided the CPU gather into pinned memory has more than one thread. `ModelRunner.load_model` calls `torch.set_num_threads(1)` before loading, and with one torch thread staging gave nothing (prototype numbers below). title: [Perf] linker: Build every Mooncake layer group's range reads before the forward fence
summary: Stacked on #49462 and #49463; only the last commit is new. ## Motivation After #49463, `MooncakeDirectLinker.load_layer_wise` resolves slot locations before the forward fence, but it still builds each layer group's range reads after the fence, one group at a time: `get_prepared_layers_range_meta`, `tolist`, and the per-thread split. That Python runs on the load thread while the I/O threads are already executing the earlier groups' range gets, and the two contend for the GIL: - For the same batch and the same amount of data per layer, a single range-get call took 2.15 ms p50 while the load thread was still submitting, and 1.40 ms after submission ended (1.45x slower at p50, 2.5x at p90). - Group 0's first call started 3.9 ms p50 / 39 ms p90 after its submit. - So the read tail of group 0, which forward layer 0 waits on, gets longer. This was the main source of the GPU idle time the linker adds to a prefill step: in nsys, 81% of that idle time fell between group 0's submit and its reads landing. The range metadata depends only on the slot locations, which are already known before the fence. ## Modifications - `load_layer_wise` builds every group's range reads (metadata plus per-thread split) right after the slot locations resolve, before the forward fence. title: [Fix] linker: Cover published prefetch KV with its request's session
summary: ## Motivation In the external linker's `prefetch` load mode, a queued request's KV is read from the store and published into the radix tree before admission. With `--enable-session-radix-cache`, a session ref is registered only when the request finishes. Until then the published nodes hold no session ref, so session-aware eviction drops them before older session-covered KV. The request then recomputes a prefix it had just prefetched. ## Modifications - `_ExternalCachePrefetch` keeps the request. - `_finish_prefetch` registers the published leaf with the request's session right after the insert. It calls `session_refs.register_session_ref`, which already handles a disabled session cache, streaming sessions, closed sessions and stale generations. - When the request finishes, its usual registration moves the session coverage to the deeper leaf. No second ref is taken. ## Accuracy Tests Not affected. Only eviction order changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling MiniMax-M3.1 NVFP4 + DSpark, 1P2D on 3x8 B300, Mooncake direct linker in prefetch mode, 640-session multi-turn agentic replay. title: [Perf] linker: Complete landed Mooncake layer groups between submits
summary: ## Motivation `MooncakeDirectLinker.load_layer_wise` submits the range gets of every layer group before it waits on any of them. Layers complete only in the wait loop that follows. The forward blocks in `wait_until(0)` until group 0 completes, so layer 0 waits for the load thread to build and submit the last group's range metadata, even when group 0's reads have already landed. ## Modifications - After each group submit, the load thread completes groups whose reads have all landed. It checks in order from the first group not yet completed and stops at the first group with a read in flight. - After the last submit, it waits on the remaining groups as before. - Groups still complete in order: `_broadcast_loaded_layers` sends all layers up to a waited one and assumes they have landed. - If a check reaches a group with a failed read, the batch fails there and later groups are not submitted. The failure path (cancel and drain submitted reads, then `fail`) and the get session end are unchanged. A group that lands during a submit is completed when that submit ends, so one slow submit can still delay layer 0. Completing groups from the I/O threads would avoid that, but it resolves layer futures from several threads and races with `LayerWiseLoadCounter.fail` and `reset`. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model outputs. Layers are published only after their reads land, in the same order as before. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a layer-0 latency cleanup. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] gdn: deferred-fold ReplaySSM target verify on FlashInfer u-cache kernels
summary: ## Motivation With a bf16 SSM state, `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` folds the GDN state on every verify step. `spec_utils.py` passes `fold_every_commit = temporal.dtype != torch.float32`, so the cursor kernel marks every row that accepted a token as "flush". The ring never carries history across steps, and one all-layer commit kernel reads and writes the full recurrent state every step. On B200 (TP1, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, NEXTN 3/4) that commit costs 2.3 / 4.7 / 10.2 / 21 ms per decode step at B = 64 / 128 / 256 / 512. This PR adds a separate, **off-by-default** GDN target-verify path, `--enable-gdn-replayssm-ucache`. It uses the FlashInfer u-cache ReplaySSM kernels (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6791): - Each GDN layer keeps a checkpoint state plus a 32-slot ring of `(k̂, u, g)` records per state slot. - One verify launch per layer computes the draft outputs from the checkpoint plus the live window and appends the new records. - The window is folded into the checkpoint, inside the same launch, only for rows whose window is full (`hist_len >= 16 - T + 1`, about one step in five). There are no per-draft state snapshots and no per-step state commit. The existing `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` and Q38 megakernel / fused-glue paths are untouched; the new path uses its own tensors, so their gates stay false. ## Modifications - **Flag and guards** (`arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`, `attention_hook.py`, `pipeline.py`, `resolution_hooks.py`): `--enable-gdn-replayssm-ucache`, off by default. - Requires: a GDN hybrid model (not KDA), SM100, SM103 or SM107 (SM103 runs the SM100 build),

title: [Feat] kda: run the Kimi-K3 fused FlashInfer decode on a BF16 SSM state (NVIDIA SM100/103)
summary: ## Motivation On Kimi-K3, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` is the useful serving configuration: it halves the KDA state pool (6.9 GiB vs 13.8 GiB per rank at 900 slots) and that memory goes to MLA KV, which is what actually limits concurrency at long context. The fused KDA decode path does not run on a BF16 pool on NVIDIA. In `models/kimi_k3.py` the fused FlashInfer consumer (#48859) is armed only when ```python if (mamba.linear_attn_decode_backend == "flashinfer" and ssm_is_fp32 # <- hard gate and spec is none and sm in ((10, 0), (10, 3))): layer._k3_flashinfer_fused_decode = prepare_fused_kda_decode(...) ``` so a BF16 pool never prepares the adapter and decode takes the recurrent path instead. On the AMD side the equivalent work already exists (#41794 runs the fused KDA decode with a BF16 state), so this is a parity gap rather than a new capability. This matters because the KDA decode step is a measurable part of the step: on 8x B300, TP8/DCP8, 12 heads per rank, 65,536-token decode, the KDA kernels are ~4.6 ms of a ~60 ms step (ncu: low occupancy, ~12.5%, latency bound), and the fused kernel is the only path that can shorten it. ## What we hit With a BF16 pool and `--linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer` on v0.5.23, the fused consumer is not prepared (gate above), and the fallback FlashInfer recurrent kernel rejects the safe gate: ``` NotImplementedError: lower_bound (safe gate) is only supported by TritonKDAKernel; got FlashInferKDAKernel. ``` That hard `isinstance(..., TritonKDAKernel)` check is pre-#41121; on main the capability-based selection should let the FlashInfer

title: [Feat][PoC] beam_search: Add paged KV support and item-catalog constraints for GR
summary: ## Motivation This PR presents a **proof of concept (POC)** for generative recommendation (GR) beam search with larger KV pages (page_size > 1), context KV reuse, and optional item-catalog constraints. It establishes the storage layout and attention integration needed to explore potential kernel-performance improvements with larger pages. title: [Perf] [AMD] batch-invariant: Segmented split-K bf16 matmul for gfx950
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode, SGLang runs every bf16 linear layer through a batch-invariant Triton matmul. At decode sizes (a few to a few hundred tokens) that kernel launches only a few programs and leaves most of an MI350X idle, so the decode GEMMs are one of the largest remaining costs of deterministic mode on gfx950. This PR adds a segmented split-K matmul for bf16 on gfx950: K is split into 4 fixed segments that are summed in a fixed order at every batch size, and at small batch sizes the segments run in separate programs, so decode GEMMs use 4 times as many programs. A token's result still does not depend on its batch. **Impact** - Deterministic-mode throughput on MI350X: Qwen3-8B +12% (1k/1k), +12% (4k/512), +3% (8k/1k); Qwen3.8-27B +12% / +14%; Phi-4 +14% / +14% / +5%. Batch invariance and accuracy unchanged (tables below). - Only `--enable-deterministic-inference` on gfx950 with bf16 models changes. Normal mode, MI300 (gfx942), NVIDIA, and fp16 / fp32 matmuls are unchanged. - The reduction order changes, so deterministic-mode outputs on gfx950 differ in the last bits from before this PR, as with any change of the batch-invariant kernel. Design note: the kernel never software-pipelines the loop over segments within one program (`num_stages` 1 there). With pipelining, some K values were not run-to-run deterministic on MI350X (seen only with 2 segments; cause not understood), and a unit test keeps it off. ## Modifications - `batch_invariant_ops.py`: - `_segmented_matmul_kernel` (Triton): per output tile, sums 4 fixed K segments in order; `SPLIT` runs one segmen

title: [Perf] mem_cache: Reclaim a branch's last SWA window last in unified eviction
summary: ## Motivation - To continue from a cached prefix, the server needs the SWA KV of the last `sliding_window` tokens of that prefix. Older SWA KV on the same path is no longer needed. - When the SWA pool is full, the unified cache frees SWA KV in plain LRU order. An idle conversation is the least recently used, so its last window is freed before the old windows that active conversations leave behind on every turn. - When the idle conversation comes back, only the shared system prompt is a cache hit. The rest is prefilled again, even though its full KV is still cached. - #35515 by @QAQEthan fixes this in `swa_radix_cache.py`, but that file is no longer on main. This PR brings the same idea to the unified cache, for both the Python core and the Rust core. ## Modifications - A node counts as the end of a branch when a leaf or a fork lies less than one window of live SWA tokens below it. These nodes hold the windows that a later request needs. - `_evict_device_next_node` now skips these nodes on its first pass. If it reaches the end of the LRU list and it skipped some nodes, it starts again from the oldest entry and frees them in LRU order. So eviction still succeeds wherever it succeeded before. - The same change is made in `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/swa.rs`. `ComponentState` gets two new flags to track the two passes. - A `joint_lru` eviction walk (#46827) picks each SWA victim itself, so it turns the skipping off. title: [Fix] moe_topk_sum: fold rows past CUDA's 65535 gridDim.y into gridDim.z
summary: ## Motivation `moe_topk_sum` (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/topk_sum.cuh`) launches one block row per token on `gridDim.y`: ```cpp dim3 grid((n_vecs + kThreads - 1) / kThreads, M); ``` CUDA caps `gridDim.y` at 65535. With attention data parallelism the MoE layer reduces the tokens of every DP rank in one call, so when all ranks run a full chunked prefill at the same time, `M` reaches `dp_size x per-rank chunk` and the launch fails: ``` tvm.error.InternalError: Failed at .../kernels/jit/csrc/moe/topk_sum.cuh:99: CUDA error: invalid argument ``` All DP schedulers die at once; the HTTP server stays up, so requests simply stop being served. Reproduced with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x H200 on v0.5.23, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --enable-dp-lm-head --moe-runner-backend marlin --chunked-prefill-size 65536` (16384 per rank, so 4 x 16384 = 65536 rows), under a multi-turn agentic load. Lowering the per-rank chunk so that the sum stays below 65536 avoids it. `main` @ 1be97a0a63 has the same launch code: since #48605 the kernel also applies a `scale` and unrolls the topk loop, and the block width is a parameter, but the grid is still `(x, M)`. This is the same failure as #34822 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, H100, marlin, DP attention). This PR revives that fix by @ZhenshengWu (closed without review) and adds a unit test. ## Modifications - `TopkSumParams` carries `M`; the kernel reads its row as `blockIdx.y + blockIdx.z * gridDim.y` and returns for padding rows. The padding rows return before `PDLWaitPrimary`, the same way the existing `v >= n_vecs` early return does. - The launcher splits `M`

title: [Fix] [AMD] attention: size the Lean decode KV tile to the device LDS budget
summary: ## Motivation `--attention-backend triton` cannot start on gfx1151. The Lean decode kernel is captured for batch >= 16 and stages only the K tile in LDS, but on HIP head dim 128 was always given `BLOCK_N = 128`, i.e. `num_stages * BLOCK_N * head_dim * 2 = 2 * 128 * 128 * 2 = 65536` B plus the compiler's own scratch. That is 66560 B against the 64 KiB shared memory per workgroup of gfx1151 (RDNA3.5), so graph capture raises `OutOfResources: shared memory Required 66560, Hardware limit 65536` and no request is served. `torch_native` is the only backend left, and it is 8-16x slower than the Triton decode kernels on this part. ## Modifications - `_lean_decode_block_n` picks the largest tile whose staged K tile fits the device's shared-memory budget, instead of hard-coding `BLOCK_N = 128` on HIP. title: fix(memory): skip speculative Mamba verify budget on PD prefill
summary: ## Motivation PD prefill workers do not execute `TARGET_VERIFY`. #34191 already made their hybrid request pool skip verify-only per-draft Mamba/GDN state, but the memory sizing path still charged that state whenever speculative decoding was enabled. title: [Perf] Keep RadixKey prefix matching on the array('q') memcmp path
summary: ### Motivation The radix-tree prefix match (`RadixKey.match`) runs for every request that enters the scheduler (`match_prefix_for_req`) and for every prefill insert traversal (`_insert_helper`). Its inner loop compares exponentially growing slices of the two token-id sequences, so the **container type** of `token_ids` dominates the per-call cost: - `array('q')` slice compare is a C-level `memcmp` (fast); - `list[int]` slice compare copies references and boxes every `PyLong` — measured up to **~15x slower** on long shared prefixes. Two concrete issues motivated this PR: 1. `HiRadixCache._concat_split_chain` (backup/restore path) rebuilds a `RadixKey` from plain lists, dropping the restored key onto the slow slice-compare path; 2. `RadixKey.match` asserted `type(t0) is type(t1)`, so a plain-list query key compared against an array-backed tree node (or vice versa) **crashed** even when the contents were identical. This PR keeps the hot path on `array('q')` and makes mixed container inputs safe. ### Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` — `RadixKey.match`: when the two sides' containers disagree, convert the `list` side to `array('q')` so matching proceeds on the memcmp path and the `type is type` assert no longer trips on a list query key vs an array-backed tree node. An eager convert of *both* sides is deliberately avoided: `array("q", list)` costs O(n) per call and is **more** expensive than the list slice compare it would replace, so the convert is limited to the mixed-type case. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py` — `_concat_split_chain`

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] quantization: Write SM90 UE8M0 activation scales in DeepGEMM's MN-major layout to skip its transpose

title: [Perf] hicache: Run the host->device load-back enqueue on a loader thread (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation Closes #38470 `HiCacheController.start_loading` submits the whole host->device load-back burst inline on the scheduler thread. With `--hicache-io-backend direct` and the `page_first_direct` layout every per-layer `load_to_device_per_layer` builds a batched-copy descriptor on the CPU (~2.4 ms per layer in our profile), so one burst on a 78-layer model with two host pools keeps the scheduler thread busy for ~375 ms. By the time the batch is built and the forward launches, every copy has already landed and the layer-wise pipeline (`LayerDoneCounter.wait_until` in the attention layers) overlaps ~0.04 % of the copy time. This PR adds `SGLANG_ENABLE_HICACHE_ASYNC_LOAD_ENQUEUE` (default off). With it on, `start_loading` only does the producer-slot hand-out and `start_event.record()` on the scheduler thread, then hands the index move, the per-layer enqueue and the ack to a single FIFO daemon thread (`hicache-load-enqueue`). With it off the call sequence is byte-for-byte the previous one (the unit test asserts the exact stream/event sequence). ## Modifications **Rebased onto current main (2026-11-10).** Main changed the load path around this feature in several places, so this is a re-port rather than a mechanical rebase, and it touches two files the previous revision did not (`l2_transfer.py`, `hicache_graph_events.py`). title: [HiSparse] Fix copy_cache_planned_kernel grid sizing for prefetch replay
summary: ## Motivation `copy_cache_planned_kernel` (introduced in #34329, HiSparse shared-index/IndexShare prefetch) replays a shared-index anchor's recorded miss plan into each skip layer's device buffer on a side stream. It launches with a small, batch-size-independent grid (`num_blocks=4`) and round-robins all requests' misses across that fixed set of warps. This works well at low batch size / low miss counts (the kernel's comment cites a 183us -> 29us H200 microbenchmark at bs=100 with 2 misses/req), but the total (request, miss) work grows with batch size while the grid does not. As batch size and per-request miss counts increase, the copy kernel's own wall time grows faster than the compute it's supposed to overlap. Because skip layers block on an event recorded after this kernel finishes, the anchor's compute stream ends up waiting on it — the prefetch's win shrinks and, past a few dozen concurrent requests, inverts into a regression relative to disabling prefetch entirely. ## Modifications Switch the grid to one block per request (`num_blocks=num_reqs`), the same convention `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` already uses for the anchor's own swap-in. Each block now only handles its own request's miss list (round-robin across the block's warps), instead of a global round-robin over a fixed warp count. Parallelism now scales with the batch instead of sitting behind a fixed grid size. Files changed: - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/hisparse.cuh`: `copy_cache_planned_kernel` rewritten to one-block-per-request scheduling. - `python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py`:

summary: ## Motivation `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()` overestimates the capacity needed before paged prefill allocation as: ```python extend_num_tokens + batch_size * page_size ``` This ignores free slots in each request's existing partial tail page and can evict reusable prefixes even when the allocation already fits. title: [Fix] moe: Fix illegal memory access in the W4A16/W8A16 Triton MoE kernel (unmasked K tail)
summary: ## Motivation Weight-only quantized MoE models (W4A16 / W8A16) that run on the Triton MoE path can crash with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`. An AutoRound W4A16 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at TP 4 hits it on its first decode step, every time. The cause is a weight load without its K mask; this PR adds the mask. **Cause.** When K is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` builds `k_mask` and applies it to the activation, scale and zero-point loads, but not to the weight load: ```python b = tl.load(b_ptrs) ``` So the last K tile reads past the end of every weight row. On the last row of the last expert, it reads past the end of the weight tensor. The extra values are multiplied by a scale that is masked to zero, so the results are correct whenever the read does not fault. `fused_moe_kernel` already masks the same load. **Who runs this kernel.** - `--quantization moe_wna16`, for GPTQ and AWQ checkpoints. - AWQ and AutoRound MoE layers that Marlin cannot take, for example without Marlin support on the platform, or with a per-rank intermediate size that is not a multiple of max(64, group size). So the irregular shapes, the ones most likely to leave a partial K tile, are the ones that fall back here. - Compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE through `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE`: always on ROCm, by default on SM100/SM103 for symmetric INT4 with group 32 or 128, and elsewhere with `--moe-runner-backend triton`. **When it reads out of bounds.** Whenever the per-rank K is not a multiple of the `BLOCK_SIZE_K` in use. title: [Perf] moe/paged-experts: decide block-wide and skip empty page-ins
summary: ## Motivation Paged experts is what lets a MoE larger than one GPU decode on one card: every decode step runs a residency decision per MoE layer (48.76 calls/step for a 48-layer model) and a page-in gather whose plan is empty most of the time. title: [Fix] hicache: vote the prefetch timeout once per tick, not per admission poll
summary: ## Motivation Under `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout` (the default) the per-request deadline verdict is agreed by a collective issued from inside the admission loop: `check_prefetch_progress` calls `_can_terminate_prefetch`, which on main does one `_all_reduce(MAX)` per call (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py:2480-2490` on `1ad0149814`). The scheduler issues that call once per waiting request with a live prefetch per scheduling pass (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4543` on `b50d439494`), and the loop's exits around it (`batch_is_full` from `get_num_allocatable_reqs`, `scheduler.py:4406-4411` and `4528-4540` on `b50d439494`) are evaluated by each rank on its own. That is the shape reported in #30760 (TP=4, no PP): one rank examined one more candidate than its peers before its own `batch_is_full` tripped, called the collective one more time, and waited in it forever while the others had moved on to `recv_requests`. #44614 centralized the per-request budget (`_StoragePrefetchWait`, started at the first blocked poll, `_prefetch_deadline_expired`, `_mark_prefetch_deadline_expired`) but left the vote in the poll; #36425 had moved the vote into `_can_terminate_prefetch`; #33029 and #44340 (both closed, not merged) proposed a once-per-tick vote, and this PR reuses that part of #44340. This PR removes the per-poll collective that #30760 reported and makes the remaining rank-consistency premise (every rank polls the same requests) fail loud in the same tick on every rank instead of hanging. title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM5: Use Triton sparse attention for GLM-5.3 on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash uses BF16 sparse MLA with a 512-wide absorbed query/KV row, no RoPE tail, and a 2,051-column K-pool page table. The existing gfx950 path pads it to 2,112 columns and sends it through TileLang for both prefill and decode. This change removes zero-width RoPE operations at compile time and lets the existing HIP default select Triton for the validated GLM-5.3 prefill and decode geometry. Explicit TileLang selection remains TileLang; unsupported K-pool/Triton geometry is rejected during backend initialization. Inside the same geometry, the new `aiter_sparse_mla` DSA backend routes the batch sizes where AITER's Gluon `sparse_mla_fwd` is faster to AITER and keeps Triton elsewhere. It is selected explicitly with `--dsa-prefill-backend aiter_sparse_mla --dsa-decode-backend aiter_sparse_mla`. Its measured gains depend on the BF16 gather fix in [ROCm/aiter#6276](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6276), merged in AITER as `9fd025ef`; AITER builds without it remain correct. ## Modifications - Compile out zero-width query/KV RoPE fragments and their dot products in the Triton sparse prefill and graph-safe split-K decode kernels. - Enable Triton for gfx950 BF16 GLM-5.3 sparse attention with 16 local heads at TP4 and 8 local heads at TP8. - Consume the natural K-pool top-k 2,051 and existing absorbed query views without TileLang's padding or `q_all` copies. - Use the single-pass Triton path for prefill and the reusable-workspace split-K path for decode. - Keep explicit TileLang selection as a true TileLang path and validate K-pool/Triton geometry at initializat

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add SLA-constrained dynamic batching for decode phase optimization
summary: Replaces #28477, which was automatically closed by the stale bot on Sep 22, 2026. The work is still relevant, so this PR resubmits the changes, rebased and re-adapted onto the current `main`. > Note: the original PR was written against the monolithic `server_args.py`. Since then `main` moved server arguments into `arg_groups/fields/` and reworked scheduler internals (`get_new_batch_prefill` now returns `NextBatchPlan`, `get_num_allocatable_reqs` has a new signature, and `get_parallel()` replaces `self.ps`). This branch is rebuilt as a single commit on top of current `main`, with the SLA feature re-applied to the new architecture so it merges cleanly. ## Motivation Static batching treats max batch size as a fixed hyper-parameter, which cannot adapt to varying workload intensity. This leads to either GPU underutilization (low load) or SLA violations (high load). This PR implements the SLA-constrained dynamic batching algorithm from Pang et al., "Optimizing LLM Inference Throughput via Memory-aware and SLA-constrained Dynamic Batching" (arXiv:2503.05248). It dynamically adjusts the decode batch size search space [b_low, b_high] based on real-time inter-token latency (ITL) feedback, keeping latency within the target SLA range [D_SLA - epsilon_D, D_SLA + epsilon_D]. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: online SLA-constrained dynamic batching algorithm with latency history tracking, adaptive bound updates, and memory guardrails. title: [Fix] gemm: Order the CuTe DSL kernels' TMEM release after the epilogue's tcgen05.ld
summary: ## Motivation Three CuTe DSL GEMM kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/` release TMEM through a two-round mbarrier (`bar_tmem_alloc` or `tmem_ready`, 160 arrivals = 32 MMA + 128 EPILOG): round 0 publishes the TMEM allocation, round 1 says the epilogue has read the accumulator. The MMA warp makes its round-0 arrival after `alloc_tmem`, runs the K-loop, makes its round-1 arrival, waits with `mbarrier_wait(bar, 1)` and deallocates. It never waits for round 0. If an EPILOG warp has not yet made its first arrival when the MMA warp arrives the second time, that arrival counts toward round 0, round 0 stays open, and the parity-1 wait returns immediately: parity 1 then names the barrier's "immediately preceding phase", which is complete by definition (PTX ISA, [`mbarrier.test_wait` / `mbarrier.try_wait`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#parallel-synchronization-and-communication-instructions-mbarrier-test-wait-try-wait)). `tcgen05.dealloc` then runs before the epilogue's `tcgen05.ld`. In the 2-CTA tactics the non-leader CTA's MMA warp skips the K-loop (`if is_leader:`), so its two arrivals are back to back and the race is against the EPILOG warps' first few instructions. This is the same race that flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6786 reported and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7443 fixed in FlashInfer's split-K kernel. The three SGLang kernels still have the original sequence: - `cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py` (TGV BF16 GEMM, a copy of FlashInfer's `tgv_gemm_cute_ext.py`; the upstream fix is flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8787, this PR applies the identical change so the two files

title: [Perf] [Apple] mps: Encode and prefill the next Unlimited-OCR v2 window under the current decode
summary: ## Motivation Part (c) of the Unlimited-OCR v2 MPS work split in review. It builds on #47921 (part (a), running the model on MPS): its own changes are the commit "Encode and prefill the next Unlimited-OCR v2 window under the current decode" and a test move, and everything else comes from #47921. I will rebase it once #47921 merges. With `--uocr-doc-split`, the serving layer sends window `i+1` while window `i` decodes. On CUDA, the scheduler parks it and encodes its pages on a side stream under the current decode (`EarlyEmbeddings.encode_ahead`). MPS has no side stream: Torch uses one command queue per process. So in (a) the next window's pages are encoded at its prefill, and its new page is prefilled at the window boundary with nothing left to decode. With three gundam pages on the M5 below, the stream stops for 1.4 s at the first window boundary. The review of #47921 asked for this without the side vision process, which held its own copy of the weights and so put model state outside the Torch `ModelRunner`. This PR does the work inside the scheduler process, with the model's own modules, between forwards: - the parked window's pages are encoded in short slices after decode steps; - once they are encoded, the window's new pages are prefilled in chunks while its predecessor still decodes. ## Modifications **Vision encoder in slices** (`models/unlimited_ocr_v2.py`) - `get_image_feature_steps(items)`: the encoder behind `get_image_feature` as a generator.
