title: [Fix] [NPU] dsv4: Use explicit compressor state on Ascend 950
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 on Ascend 950 uses a request-local compressor state bank. A radix-cache hit can reuse the prefix's SWA pages under a different request slot. Using explicit state locations lets the resumed compressor find the C4 history associated with those pages. ## Modifications - Use the shared explicit state table and `torch.ops.npu.compressor` on Ascend 950. Build the table for eager execution and refresh it in place for NPU graph replay. - Resolve C4 state through each worker's SWA pages. Keep Ascend 950 prefill/decode (PD) transfers row-granular so peers with different MTP ring sizes can pair the same logical positions. - Replace request-bank tests with explicit graph-replay and C4 PD mapping coverage. **Kernel dependency.** Build and install the Ascend 950 kernel from https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/989 before using this backend. The paired kernel changes the `cache_mode=2` table from a vector of bank IDs to a two-dimensional table of physical state rows. ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling performance with change performance baseline 8k1k : performance with change

title: [Feat] [Intel] monokernel: --enable-xpu-monokernel, the Intel XPU backend of the monokernel binding
summary: # [Feat] [Intel] monokernel: --enable-xpu-monokernel, the Intel XPU backend of the monokernel binding ## Motivation sgl-kernel-xpu adds decode "mono" kernels for Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 MoE (35B-A3B, block-FP8) at TP2 on two Intel Xe2 GPUs. Each decoder layer of a decode or MTP target-verify step runs as one persistent kernel (GatedDeltaNet or full attention, then the MoE with the shared expert), and both tensor-parallel all-reduces run inside the kernel through mailboxes in the peer GPU's memory. The MTP drafter's draft decode steps and its draft extend step (the verified positions) run on the same kind of kernels. The kernels come with an SGLang plugin, `sgl_kernel.monokernel`, which implements the existing monokernel contract: the one behind `--enable-amd-monokernel` and the MSA plugin. This PR exposes that plugin as the `xpu` backend of the shared binding behind a new opt-in flag, `--enable-xpu-monokernel`. It contains no Intel-specific model code. All XPU platform logic (device and model checks, memory budget, wait deadline, fail-stop) stays in the plugin, following the rule that platform switches live in the kernel package and SGLang keeps one interface. On two Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs (TP2, BF16), decode TPOT improves 2.0x over the base at one request (1K context: 10.96 -> 5.30 ms; 32K: 11.65 -> 5.66 ms). With MTP the speedup is 1.4x to 5.4x. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged. Depends on sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#614 (the kernels and the plugin). **Merge order:** #614 first, then an sgl-kernel-xpu release that contains it, then this PR; it stays a draft until then. title: [Perf] flashinfer-megamoe: Add an optional decode workspace
summary: ## Motivation Found while adding Beam (#44747), split out of #45256 at review because it is not specific to Beam. MegaMoE's per-call cost scales with workspace capacity. title: [HiCache] Batch direct DMA transfers and overlap safe restores
summary: HiCache's direct path plans and submits transfers per layer, and restores wait for the previous forward even when their destination pages are safe. Move copy planning into native code, batch transfers by logical layer block, and add opt-in overlap with the previous forward. - Keep fused Mamba slot clear/copy working with page-major views and reuse `page_first_direct` for BF16/MXFP8 host storage. - Plan and coalesce indexed copies in C++, cache stable layout metadata, and batch copies across supported static KV, SWA, Mamba, and draft pools. Preserve existing paths for other pools and runtimes. - Add `--hicache-load-block-layers` (default `1`). Completion covers payloads, scales, and auxiliary pools; Mamba follows its mapped logical layers. Supported Inkling CUDA graphs use persistent block-wait events. - Add `--hicache-restore-backward-overlap` (default off). Allocators track reuse of recently freed pages; those restores retain the forward fence. Existing WAR ordering protects metadata, and Mamba request slots use forward-stream copy-on-write. The six commits separate layout support, native planning, block waits, draft/scales ordering, pooled submission, and backward overlap. On a synthetic GB300 BF16 KV transfer (512 MiB, 32 layers, 4 layers/block), median restore CPU submission was **1.924 → 1.391 ms**. title: [Fix] sampling: Refresh is_all_greedy / is_any_greedy when filter_batch removes rows
summary: ## Motivation `SamplingBatchInfo.is_all_greedy` and `is_any_greedy` are computed only in `from_schedule_batch`, from each request's `top_k <= 1`. `merge_batch` combines them (`is_all_greedy &= other.is_all_greedy`, `is_any_greedy |= other.is_any_greedy`), but `filter_batch` never recomputes them. It slices `temperatures` / `top_ps` / `top_ks` / `min_ps` / `sampling_seed` and leaves both flags alone. So when one non-greedy request is merged into a running decode batch of greedy requests, `is_all_greedy` becomes `False` and stays `False` for the rest of that batch's life. That holds even after the non-greedy request finishes and `filter_batch` removes it. Every remaining greedy request then takes the sampling path until the batch fully drains: - `layers/sampler.py`: the `is_all_greedy` argmax fast path is skipped in favour of top-k/top-p sampling. - Speculative verify: for example, `eagle_utils._verify_uses_greedy` and `dspark_components/dspark_verify.py`, where the fused-argmax `AcceptGreedy` path falls back to `SoftmaxTemp` + rejection sampling. The same applies to the `is_all_greedy` branches in the dflash / uno / eagle-v2 workers and the greedy CUDA-graph variant in `eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner`. `is_any_greedy` goes stale the same way in the other direction: it stays `True` after the last greedy row leaves. Outputs stay correct, because a greedy row on the sampling path still ends up at its argmax. The cost is speed. With DSpark speculative decoding, after a single sampling request had passed through the batch, we measured decode steps about 37% longer for a batch-1 gr

summary: ## Motivation External linker lookups cannot currently report pending separately from a completed miss. title: [Fix] scheduler: Wait for idle before completing abort-mode pause
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #44745. title: fix: include Mamba pressure in hybrid SSM load reporting
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid SSM engines have two independent capacity constraints: the Full KV cache and the Mamba state cache. The existing metrics path reports cache pressure using `max(full_token_usage, mamba_usage)`, while `/v1/loads` reports only `full_token_usage`. When the Mamba state cache is the bottleneck, these two interfaces therefore expose inconsistent load information, and `/v1/loads` underestimates the engine's effective resource pressure. `/v1/loads` is intended to provide load information for load balancing, monitoring, and capacity planning. A router or load balancer that consumes its `token_usage` field may treat a Mamba-constrained engine as having more available capacity than it actually has, potentially resulting in suboptimal or imbalanced request routing. This change aligns `/v1/loads` with the metrics path by reporting the bottleneck-aware value `max(full_token_usage, mamba_usage)`. It preserves `full_num_used` as the absolute token count because Mamba occupancy is measured in request slots rather than KV tokens. ## Modifications - For hybrid SSM pools, report token usage as `max(full_token_usage, mamba_usage)`. - Keep `full_num_used` as the absolute token count because Mamba occupancy is measured in request slots rather than KV tokens. - Add unit tests covering: - Mamba usage being higher than Full KV usage. - Full KV usage being higher than Mamba usage. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. title: [Feature] Token-aware admission cap (--max-inflight-prefill-tokens)
summary: The admission knobs we have today (`--max-running-requests`, `--max-queued-requests`) are count-based. They can't tell a 4k prompt from a 500k one. So when a burst of long-context requests lands, the server admits them by count, over-commits prefill memory, and OOM-crashes instead of shedding. On a GLM-5.2-FP8 tp8/dp8 run, 8 concurrent 500k-token prompts take the whole server down (every request net-fails). This adds a token-aware bound: `--max-inflight-prefill-tokens N`. The tokenizer manager sits in front of the workers (one per server, before requests are dispatched to the DP ranks), so it's the right place to bound total work before anything is scheduled. A new request is rejected up front when the prompt tokens already in flight plus this request would exceed `N`. The one subtle part is the accounting. The charge is recorded on the request's `ReqState` inside `_validate_one_request`, which runs synchronously (no `await`), so the read of the in-flight total and the charge are atomic against other in-flight requests. That matters under a concurrent burst: if you compute the in-flight total lazily, 8 requests that arrive together all read an empty total and all get admitted (I hit exactly this and watched it still OOM). Charging synchronously fixes it. The charge is released for free when the request finishes and leaves `rid_to_state`, so there's no separate counter to leak on aborts or disconnects. Default is unset, which is a no-op: the `is not None` guard short-circuits, zero overhead. When set, the only added cost is an int sum over in-flight requests at admission tim

title: [HiCache] Bulk/staging reload fast-path for contiguous host runs
summary: When an evicted prefix is reloaded from the host KV tier, the transfer runs the per-token kernel (`transfer_kv_per_layer_mla`) at ~4.3 GB/s no matter how the bytes are laid out, because it pays a per-token indexing cost for every token. The host pool makes that worse: it hands out free slot ids first-fit and appends freed ids on free, so after a few fill/evict cycles a re-admitted prefix lands on a scrambled set of host offsets. So the reload is a fine-grained scatter/gather. Two changes turn that reload into a large contiguous copy: 1. The host slot allocator hands out a contiguous run whenever one is free, so a prefix's KV occupies a contiguous host region. Capacity and the success/failure set are identical to the stock allocator (it only returns None when there isn't enough total free, same as before), and when the pool is too fragmented for one run it falls back to gathering the largest runs first. So the slots handed out are always valid, distinct and in range; only the packing changes. 2. A reload fast-path in `load_to_device_per_layer`. When the host run for a layer is one ascending unit-stride run, it moves the slab in one shot instead of the per-token gather: if the device target slots are also one run, a single `copy_`; if the device slots are scattered (the device pool allocator does not pack them), it copies the contiguous host slab into a contiguous device staging buffer once and places the rows at their real slots with an on-device `index_copy_`. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation With an explicit `--hicache-ratio` or `--hicache-size`, HiCache auto-sizing is off (`hicache_host_memory_fraction` resolves to `None`) and `auto_size_hicache` yields without a budget scope. summary: ## Motivation With an FP8 KV cache, `--enable-mixed-chunk` kills the DSA backend on the first mixed batch when the prefill backend is `flashmla_sparse`, `flashmla_sparse_q8` or `triton_sparse_mla`. The rest of the stack already treats such a batch as an extend-shaped batch (its decode rows are one-token extends with a full prefix), which is exactly how the gap surfaces: - The eager runner runs a mixed batch as EXTEND (`eager_runner.execute` rewrites the mode), so without a prefill CUDA graph the backend never sees MIXED and nothing fails. - The prefill CUDA graph runner (breakable, the CUDA default) builds the attention metadata from the real MIXED batch and replays the EXTEND-captured graphs, whose in-graph ops see a static batch with mode EXTEND. The metadata is therefore prepared for PAGED and has no `topk_indices_offset`, while the in-graph indexer asks for the RAGGED transform: ``` RuntimeError: RAGGED topk_transform requires topk_indices_offset; expected extend-without-speculative metadata. ``` - Runs that hand MIXED straight to `forward_extend` (context parallel, NPU) take the PAGED path and the bf16-only kernel receives the packed FP8 pool: ``` RuntimeError: kv must have dtype torch::kBFloat16 # flashmla_sparse, flashmla_sparse_q8 TypeError: sparse_mla_prefill needs a bf16 KV cache, got torch.float8_e4m3fn # triton_sparse_mla ``` The gap was pointed out by @ch-wan in the review o

summary: ### Summary `XGrammarGrammar.rollback()` in `python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py` rebuilds a full list slice on every call. title: [Feature] Batched asynchronous Engram host-row prefetch
summary: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 introduces two large, immutable Engram tables. SGLang can keep these tables in host memory with: ```bash SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 ``` This reduces HBM usage substantially, but every Engram lookup then performs sparse reads from pinned host memory. The current optional prefetch path: ```bash SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_KV_PREFETCH=1 ``` launches the layer-14 Engram lookup and WKV projection on a side CUDA stream and overlaps them with layers 0-13. However, it is currently enabled only when all of the following are true: - CUDA execution; - pipeline parallel size is 1; - DP attention is disabled; - the model is text-only; - the host table uses the shared layout; - the WKV projection uses the FlashInfer CuTeDSL MXFP8 backend; - the forward is normal decode with exactly one token. The FlashInfer CuTeDSL MXFP8 backend requires Blackwell. H20 is SM90 and uses the block-FP8 fallback for the DeepSeek-V4.1 32x32 dense weights, so the final backend check prevents prefetch from being enabled even when the host table is shared and pinned. For batch sizes greater than one, simply removing the `hash_ids.shape[0] == 1` check is undesirable. The layer-14 WKV projection is a large dense GEMM. Running it concurrently with layers 0-13 can compete for SM and HBM resources and may reduce throughput.

title: [RFC] First-Class, Versioned KV Hint Envelope for SGLang
summary: ## Motivation [#27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574) proposes programmatic KV-cache management for agentic workloads: an orchestrator has trajectory-level context that a single engine cannot infer, while SGLang retains ownership of scheduling, cache allocation, eviction, transfer, and failure handling. This issue scopes the API boundary needed to carry that intent into SGLang. It does not define a global cache policy or commit SGLang to execute every possible action. Router-driven KV experiments can use ad-hoc request fields and backend-specific metadata. That is useful scaffolding, but it is not a durable interface for an orchestrator, scheduler, HiCache, or storage backend. title: [HiCache] Fix SWA over-admission of host load-backs that crashes the scheduler
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache on a hybrid sliding-window (SWA) model, prefill admission can accept a host load-back that the SWA pool cannot serve. `alloc_for_extend` then raises and the scheduler dies; every later request fails: ``` alloc_for_extend -> alloc_token_slots: RuntimeError: Out of memory. Try to lower your batch size. Try to allocate 2318 tokens. Available full tokens: 7949 (full_available_size=4137 + full_evictable_size_=3812) Available swa: 2270 (available_size=2270 + component_evictable_size_=0) ``` `PrefillAdder.add_one_req` selects the request while only its device match (`req.last_node`) is pinned. After `init_load_back`, the request's sliding-window lock is anchored at `req.best_match_node`, and that window can cover device-resident SWA past `last_node`. Selection counted that SWA as evictable, and nothing charged it: `swa_host_hit_length` covers only the host-only part of the window. `add_one_req` already pins `best_match_node` around `memory_budget.prepare_load_back(...)`. `SharedSWAPrefillBudget` (unified memory) implements that hook, but `SWAPrefillBudget`, used by the separate FULL/SWA pools and the Mamba tri-pool, inherits the base no-op. So on the default allocator nothing checks SWA with the window pinned. Observed with Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (window 1024) on one RTX 5090, at 28 concurrent multi-turn chat sessions, on a build of `main` from 2026-09-21 (a9871012ac). title: [Perf] [AMD] quark: Compile each layer_quant_config pattern once
summary: ## Motivation `QuarkConfig._find_matched_config` walks `layer_quant_config` with `fnmatch.fnmatch(layer_name, name_pattern)` once per layer. On Python 3.10, `fnmatch._compile_pattern` is `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=256)`; Python 3.11 raised it to 32768. AMD's GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 checkpoint lists 924 `layer_quant_config` patterns, so each walk evicts every compiled pattern before it is reused and every lookup recompiles all of them: 49.8 ms per lookup. The full GLM-5.3 Quark MXFP4 checkpoint lists 439 patterns, which also exceeds 256 (3.5 ms per full walk). title: [Perf] [XPU] quantization: Run block-FP8 linears weight-only (W8A16) on Xe2
summary: ## Motivation Block-FP8 checkpoints (128x128 weight scales, e.g. Qwen3-32B-FP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8) run their linears on XPU in two steps. First `per_token_group_quant_fp8` quantizes the activation. Then `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` calls `scaled_mm` (oneDNN). At decode sizes that path streams the fp8 weight at only 175-350 GB/s on Arc Pro B70; the bf16 GEMM reaches 510-590 GB/s. So Qwen3-32B-FP8 decodes no faster than bf16, even though it reads half the bytes. Xe2 has no FP8 math, so fp8 activations buy nothing. The win is bandwidth: keep the activation in bf16 and stream the fp8 weight once. ## Dependency The fused GEMM is `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20`, added in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#587. sglang currently pins sgl-kernel-xpu 0.5.0, which does not have it. - This PR detects the op (`has_xpu_w8a16_gemm`). The weight is dequantized to bf16 by a small Triton kernel (one program per 128x128 scale block, edge blocks masked) and multiplied with `F.linear`. title: [Fix] speculative: Apply repetition penalty per draft position in EAGLE verify
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49403. Under EAGLE-family speculative decoding the repetition penalty is applied in a relaxed way: the penalizer sees one token per verify step (`req.output_ids[-1]`), and one penalty row is broadcast to every draft position. With `repetition_penalty != 1` (common, since sglang applies `generation_config.json` defaults) greedy speculative output therefore differs from non-speculative output. On 1,500 prompts at `repetition_penalty=1.05` it changes the judged score on 7.7 % of prompts against 0.4 % run-to-run noise; with this PR, 1.1 %. Related: #45233 (draft that bundles exact NEXTN penalties with a CORAL overlay, without GPU validation; its author marked it stale); #48901 / #46752 (the same class of issue for DFLASH/DSPARK, which have their own verify path; this PR does not touch it). ## Modifications - `speculative/spec_repetition_penalty.py` (new): `SpecRepetitionState`, a bool table of seen tokens per request-pool row, kept on the GPU and touched only on the forward stream (no host syncs; works with the overlap scheduler). - Verify row `j` of a request is penalized by the table plus `cand[0..j]` (the root and the earlier drafts of the block). For chain drafts (`topk == 1`) this matches non-speculative decoding without overlap token for token; for trees only the committed history is exact. - After verify, the root and the correct drafts are added from `predict[accept_index]`, which every rank shares. title: [Bug] EAGLE/EAGLE3 verify applies repetition_penalty to only one token per step, so speculative output differs from non-speculative decoding
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug With `repetition_penalty != 1`, EAGLE-family speculative decoding (EAGLE, EAGLE3, STANDALONE, NEXTN, multi-layer EAGLE) produces different greedy output than plain decoding of the same model. Two places in the spec path apply the penalty in a relaxed way (the code comments call it "a relaxed version of penalties for speculative decoding"): 1. **Most committed tokens are never penalized.** `eagle_prepare_for_decode` feeds the penalizer `req.output_ids[-1]` once per verify step (`ScheduleBatch.cumulate_penalty_output_tokens`). With an accept length of ~3.5, roughly 70 % of the committed tokens never enter the penalty. 2. **One penalty row is broadcast to every draft position.** `eagle_sample` applies `repeat_interleave(acc_scaling_penalties, draft_token_num)`, so draft `j` is verified without the penalty for drafts `0..j-1` of the same block. At temperature 0 both change the target's verification logits relative to non-speculative decoding, so the accepted tokens differ. This affects any model whose `generation_config.json` sets `repetition_penalty`, since the chat endpoint applies it by default. Measured

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qsa: split-K sparse decode kernel for fp8 KV
summary: ## Motivation QSA decode and MTP target verify in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4_exp`) attend each query row to 2,051 selected positions (512 compressed blocks of 4 tokens plus a 3-token tail). On SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), the backend prepares them with `fused_kv_prepare`: it stores the new KV, expands the blocks and packs the selected K/V of every row into a page-strided scratch. FlashInfer's `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` then reads that scratch. On SM120 the scratch is bf16 even when the KV pool is `fp8_e4m3`, the setting every NVIDIA recipe in the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook pins. The pack therefore writes and re-reads twice the bytes the attention needs, and at 32 or more query rows it is about 4x the cost of the attention itself. This PR adds a JIT CUDA kernel that reads the selected fp8 K/V rows straight from the KV pool through `req_to_token`. It computes the attention in one split-K pass with no gather and no scratch. It is opt-in behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_SPARSE_DECODE_CUDA`. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/attention/qsa_sparse_decode.cuh` (new, JIT; no `sglang-kernel` release needed): - **Split kernel.** One CTA per (query row, KV head, split), 8 splits, 4 warps. 32-column blocks are loaded through a 2-3 stage `cp.async` pipeline. `q k^T` and `p v` run on bf16 `m16n8k16` tensor cores with an online softmax, and the kernel writes unnormalized partials. title: [Fix] RL: Fix crash when returning routed experts under DCP or KV sharding
summary: ## Why? With `--enable-return-routed-experts`, sglang saves each token's routed experts in a CPU buffer, one row per KV slot. The buffer is sized for one GPU's KV pool. With DCP (decode context parallel) or KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`), KV slot numbers cover every GPU's pool. Slots past the first GPU's pool have no row, so the server crashes. ```text Example: DCP 4, each GPU's KV pool holds 64 tokens KV slots 0 ──────────────────────────────── 271 (4 GPUs' pools) buffer before 0 ──── 67 (1 GPU's pool) └─ slot 68 → IndexError → server crashes buffer after 0 ──────────────────────────────── 271 ``` We hit this on Kimi-K3 with DCP16 during RL, about 20 minutes into the run. ## What? - Make the buffer cover every KV slot the allocator can hand out: - no DCP, no KV sharding: unchanged - DCP: every DCP rank's pool - KV sharding: every shard's pool - Only one function changes: `RunnerIds.capture_token_capacity`. The indexer top-k buffer uses it too, so it gets the same fix. - The int16 buffer option that used to be in this PR is now #47833. ## Verification? A new unit test fills the KV pool and checks that the buffer has exactly one row per slot: ```text case largest slot rows before rows after no DCP 67 68 68 DCP 4 271 68 ✗ 272 KV sharding 4 271 68 ✗ 272 (observed, CPU) ``` ## Test? - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_runner_ids.py::test_capture_capacity_covers_widened_allocator_ids`: **observed** passing on CPU. It **observed** failing on `main` for the DCP and KV-sharding cases. - All 19 tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_runner_ids.py`: **observed**

title: [Feat] scheduler: log host-device syncs by stage and call site
summary: ## Motivation When a serving engine is host-bound, one stray host-device sync in the scheduler path (an `.item()`, a `.tolist()` of a device tensor, a pageable `torch.tensor(..., device="cuda")`) makes the host wait for the GPU queue to drain, so it can no longer launch ahead. The scheduler already exports wall time per stage (`sglang:scheduler_stage_seconds_total`, #37636, #42025), but nothing says **where** the host blocks or **how often per step**. torch's sync debug mode can report every sync, but its warnings are deduplicated per location and carry no step context, so they cannot answer "how many syncs does one decode step or one extend cost, and from which call sites?" This PR adds an opt-in census: with `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET` set, the scheduler counts every sync torch reports under the scheduler stage it ran in, the forward mode of the batch being launched or processed, and its Python call site. It writes one JSON record per interval, together with the number of launched batches per forward mode. Syncs per decode step or per extend then follow by division. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/observability/scheduler_host_sync_logger.py` (new): `SchedulerHostSyncLogger`. On the first launched batch it calls `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")`, adds an `"always"` filter for the sync warning, and installs a `warnings.showwarning` hook that counts each sync under `(stage, forward_mode, call_site)`. title: [Feat] qwen4: --ple-offload-token-embedding keeps embed_tokens in host memory
summary: ## Motivation On a single 96 GB RTX PRO 6000, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` leaves only a few GB for the KV cache once its weights are resident, so serving is KV-bound. That holds even with `--ple-offload-embedding` moving the 47.7 GiB PLE n-gram table to host memory (the cookbook cells run 78k–170k-token pools). The token embedding (`embed_tokens`, 248,320 x 2,560 BF16 = 1.27 GB) still sits on the GPU. It is only read row-by-row: one gather per input token. That is exactly the access pattern the existing zero-copy PLE gather kernel serves from pinned host memory. ## Modifications - New opt-in server arg `--ple-offload-token-embedding` (default off), next to `--ple-offload-embedding` in `ExecOffload`. The table is always page-locked host memory, whatever `--ple-offload-backend` is, and on unified-memory devices (e.g. GB10) the flag frees nothing; the help text and the docs row say so. It is plumbed into the Qwen4-Exp text config like the other PLE offload settings, and is rejected for non-Qwen4-Exp models and together with `--cpu-offload-gb` / `--offload-group-size`, like `--ple-offload-embedding`. - `Qwen4ExpModel._build_embed_tokens`: with the flag, the embedding is built on the meta device and wrapped in the existing `Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding`, so its table is allocated only in pinned host memory and never on the GPU. Rows are gathered by the existing Triton kernel (bitwise-equal rows, CUDA-graph safe). title: [Perf] [XPU] distributed: Default oneCCL to its Arc all-reduce on Arc GPUs
summary: ## Motivation At small batch, decode issues one tensor-parallel all-reduce per attention block and one per MLP/MoE block: 129 per step for Qwen3-32B and 94 for Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4. Their latency is a fixed part of every step. On Arc Pro B70 (4 cards over PCIe), oneCCL's default SYCL all-reduce takes 17-26 us per call at decode sizes. Its Arc-specific algorithm (`CCL_SYCL_ALLREDUCE_ARC=1`) takes 15-16 us, and it is equally fast at prefill sizes. ## Modifications - `distributed/bootstrap.py`: new `_set_xpu_ccl_defaults()`, called in `init_parallel_runtime` on XPU before the first communicator is created. - When the device name contains `Arc`, it does `os.environ.setdefault("CCL_SYCL_ALLREDUCE_ARC", "1")`, so a value the user sets still wins. - Other Intel GPUs are left alone. - Setting the variable in-process takes effect: oneCCL reads it when the first communicator is created, and the per-call latency drops as shown below. ## Accuracy Tests Only the all-reduce algorithm changes. Like any switch of all-reduce algorithm, the summation order can change, so outputs are not bit-identical across the two settings. oneCCL runs are not bit-reproducible on this setup to begin with. title: [Perf] [XPU] qwen3: Fuse q/k RMSNorm and RoPE on XPU
summary: ## Motivation On XPU, every Qwen3 dense layer runs the q RMSNorm, the k RMSNorm and RoPE as three kernel launches. Qwen3-MoE already replaces them with one in-place launch, sgl-kernel-xpu's `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`, under `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope`, which is on by default on XPU. Qwen3 dense (`Qwen3Attention`) never took that path. ## Modifications - `models/qwen3.py`: new `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_xpu`, decided once in `Qwen3Attention.__init__`. When it is set, `forward_prepare_native` calls `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` on the strided q/k views of `qkv`, normalizing and rotating them in place. This is the same call Qwen3-MoE makes. - The fused path is used only when all of these hold; otherwise the unfused path runs unchanged: - the device is XPU, - `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` is set, - RL on-policy mode is off (it needs the FP32 norm), - the rotary embedding is not mrope, - the head dim is 64, 128 or 256, - q_norm and k_norm use the same eps, - the dtype is bf16. - `test/registered/xpu/test_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope_xpu.py`: the existing test checks the fused call against the model's unfused path. It now also covers the per-rank head counts of Qwen3-32B at TP4 (16 q / 2 kv heads), in addition to Qwen3-30B-A3B's (8 / 1). ## Accuracy Tests - `test_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope_xpu.py`: 32 passed on Arc Pro B70, with sgl-kernel-xpu 0.4.0 and 0.5.0. The cases include YaRN scaling, partial rotary, neox and non-neox, and 1 and 257 tokens. - GSM8K on Qwen3-32B, TP4: 94.31% before, 94.77% after. Same within sampling noise. Settings: sgl-eval, full 1319 questions, temperature 0.7

title: [Fix] [XPU] benchmark: Run the fused MoE Triton tuner on XPU
summary: ## Motivation `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py` fails on XPU before it benchmarks the first config: - It hard-codes CUDA: `torch.cuda.synchronize`, `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`, `torch.cuda.Event`, and a `"cuda"` cache-flush tensor. - It uses Ray's global GPU id as the local device ordinal. Ray already isolates one card per worker, so on XPU that ordinal is out of range, as it is on ROCm. The sibling `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py` already uses the device-generic APIs. ## Modifications - `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`: - Synchronize, capture the graph and create events through `torch.get_device_module()`, with `torch.xpu.XPUGraph` on XPU. - Allocate the L2-flush buffer on the current device. - Seed through the device module. - Use device ordinal 0 on XPU, as on ROCm. - CUDA behavior is unchanged: every call resolves to `torch.cuda`. - `README.md`: new "Intel XPU" section. Ray only registers Intel GPUs as `GPU` resources when `dpctl` is installed (it is part of the `ray` extra in `pyproject_xpu.toml`). Cards are selected with `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`. ## Accuracy Tests Benchmark tooling only; no runtime code changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The tuner now runs end to end on Arc Pro B70; it was used to tune Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP4 for batch sizes 1-32. title: [Feat] mamba: Allow skipping per-draft intermediate SSM state
summary: ## Motivation Speculative verify on hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5/3.6, KDA, ...) allocates `intermediate_ssm` in `MambaPool`: one recurrent-state snapshot per draft token per request, so rejected drafts can roll back by copying the last accepted snapshot. It is the largest piece of speculative scratch; for a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-style GDN model with 4 draft tokens it is hundreds of MiB per request, and `KVCacheConfigurator` takes it out of the mamba budget. A linear-attention backend that implements its own rollback never reads that buffer. Today the only way to skip it is `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, which is tied to ReplaySSM. This PR exposes the skip directly, so such a backend can turn off the allocation and its budget reservation without enabling ReplaySSM. ## Modifications - `KVCacheConfigurator.allocate_intermediate_ssm: bool = True`, forwarded to `MambaPool` through `HybridReqToTokenPool` and the disaggregated `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool`. `UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool` accepts it for signature parity and, like the other spec flags there, does not forward it. - `MambaPool` skips `intermediate_ssm` when the flag is false, using the same branch ReplaySSM already uses. Conv intermediate windows are still allocated (conv rollback reads them). - `_handle_max_mamba_cache` reserves intermediate memory only when the buffer is allocated (`reserve_intermediate_ssm`), for all three sizing paths. - Default `True` keeps current behavior everywhere. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: no kernel or model forward change, and the default leaves every code pat

title: [Feat] qsa: host offload of the QSA K/V with a per-request GPU hot cache (1/N)
summary: ## Motivation Qwen4-Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, `qwen4_exp`) decodes with QSA sparse attention: each query row attends to at most 512 compressed blocks (2,048 tokens) per QSA layer. The full-attention K/V of every token still stays on the GPU. On `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` that is 24,576 B/token in BF16 (12 QSA layers × 2 KV heads × 256 × K+V), against 768 B/token for the GPU-resident compressed index. On one 96 GB RTX PRO 6000, `main` at `--mem-fraction-static 0.93` has a KV pool of 306,624-307,456 tokens. At 61K-token prompts that is 4 concurrent sessions: a long-context, many-session deployment is KV-bound long before it is compute-bound. This PR keeps the full K/V of the QSA layers in pinned host memory and keeps per request only a bounded GPU cache of the blocks the indexer selects. Upstream's HiSparse solves the same problem for DSA, DeepSeek V4 and MiniMax M3, but it requires `--disable-radix-cache`: host rows and device slots belong to one request. Here host rows are indexed by the logical KV slot (the allocator index in `req_to_token`), so a radix prefix shared by many requests shares its host rows, and the radix cache, chunked prefill and the indexer are unchanged. **Series.** This PR stands alone: it is a complete, exact feature behind an off-by-default flag. PR 2/N, the fused CUDA-graph-safe resolve (Triton), builds on it, becomes the default on CUDA and must merge after it. Possible follow-ups, not part of this series yet: offloading the MTP draft layers' K/V, and a prefill that gathers only the context rows the top-k reads. ## Modifications - **`mem_cache/

title: Fix compressed-tensors asymmetric WNA16 MoE: zero-point transpose and converter
summary: ## What this fixes A compressed-tensors W4A16 **MoE** checkpoint whose experts carry `weight_zero_point` does not serve correctly on SGLang. There are **two independent defects** in one scheme, and both are needed — either alone is not sufficient. **1. Loader** (`fused_moe_triton/layer.py`). Both `FusedMoE` weight-loader sites transpose every expert tensor for the `CompressedTensorsWNA16*` methods *except* names containing `"zero"`. The checkpoint's zero points are stored N-first and the scheme's buffers are K-first, so that exclusion sends them in with the wrong layout. Removing it makes the checkpoint load at all. **2. Converter** (`compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py`, `marlin_utils.py`). The MoE scheme converts expert zero points with `moe_awq_to_marlin_zero_points`, which applies AWQ's `undo_interleave` permutation (`argsort([0, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3, 5, 7])`). Compressed-tensors checkpoints carry no AWQ interleaving, so that step **injects** a channel permutation. This PR adds `moe_packed_to_marlin_zero_points` — unpack, then the Marlin permutation, applied per expert. **The strongest evidence that (2) is the right formula is in this repository:** SGLang's own **dense** path (`compressed_tensors_wNa16.py`) already does `marlin_zero_points(unpack_cols(x.t(), ...))`, with no `undo_interleave`. The new MoE helper is that same formula per expert. vLLM's MoE path uses the packed/GPTQ converter, not the AWQ one. Fixing only (1) turns a loud failure into a silent one: the checkpoint loads and generates fluent text with corrupted zero points. ## Validation Qwen3.6-35B-A3B asym: **276/300

title: [Perf] kv-cache: Amortize L1 eviction under sustained pressure
summary: ## Motivation When the device (L1) KV pool remains saturated, the allocator currently evicts only the exact token shortfall required by each allocation. Under sustained prefill traffic, this produces many small eviction cycles. Each cycle synchronously rebuilds and scans the radix-cache eviction heap on the scheduler thread. Once `kv_available_tokens` reaches zero, repeated eviction work stalls the scheduler, introduces pipeline backpressure, and causes a persistent throughput drop even though allocations continue to succeed. The effect is especially severe for short-input workloads: short requests create allocation and radix-cache activity more frequently while providing less GPU computation over which to amortize the synchronous CPU work. The paged free-list optimization in #37146 reduces release-side metadata overhead, but it does not reduce the number of radix-cache eviction cycles. Profiling shows that the remaining bottleneck is repeated synchronous eviction-heap work. ## Modifications - Add the opt-in environment variable `SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS`. - When an allocation first encounters pressure, evict the current shortfall plus a bounded reserve. - Cap the optional reserve by the number of currently evictable tokens, so headroom cannot turn an otherwise satis

title: [Refactor] custom-ar-v2: Single-word push epoch and consume-style pull semaphores
summary: > (auto generated by Claude) > (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent) ## What Simplifies the synchronization state shared by the CustomAllReduceV2 push/pull planes and every kernel that borrows them, so that resource sizes no longer depend on launch widths. - Push plane: the per-block phase counter array is replaced by one u64 `EpochCounter`. Each grid participant does one fire-and-forget `red.add` at exit (participant 0 adds `2^32 - (N - 1)`, the others add 1), so any grid size advances the phase exactly once. All "bumper" / cleanup blocks that flipped unused counters are removed, and push kernels may launch any grid size. - Pull plane: `Semaphore` keeps one arrival counter per ordering class (relaxed / release). Separate counters make the release/acquire barrier well-defined under the PTX memory model even when a peer's next-round arrival lands first. - `PushPlane` takes a `default_blocks` launch width; `PullPlane` has `capacity` (allocated as `max(num_sm, num_pull_blocks)`) and `default_blocks`. - Migrated kernels: custom AR (push/pull), all_reduce_fusion, beam, tp_qknorm, nvlink_comm, K3 ar_fusion / sp_collective / gemm_ag / attn_res fused TMA, Muse Spark all-gather kernels and the CuTe DSL finalize all-reduce. ## Validation - 2x B300: test_custom_all_reduce, test_all_reduce_resi

summary: ## Why? - `--enable-return-routed-experts` keeps every token's routed expert ids in a device buffer and a pinned host cache, and returns them in the response, all as int32. - The ids are small. title: [Perf] kda: shorten the MTP verify phase-1 critical path (-11% at N=32, -12% at N=64 on VR)
summary: ## Motivation In the KDA MTP verify kernel (`kda_decode_mtp.py`), the conv precompute (phase 1) sits on the critical path ahead of the block barrier. A dose that removes only the q/k/g producer loop saves 18–19% of the kernel at the K3.1 production shape (H=12, num_spec=7, ring + fused output norm, N=32/64). The SASS (sm_107a) shows why: - Each q/k/g producer step issued its `x`/`g`/`beta` loads *after* the previous step's `intermediate_conv_*` / ReplaySSM ring stores, and consumed them right away. ptxas cannot move a plain load above a store it cannot prove does not alias, so every step paid a full global-load latency (two for the q/k windows). - Each step was its own basic block, because of the per-step `if p1_job == ...` / `if i_t < T_LOOP` branches. As a result, a warp's 4 independent token chains (conv → SiLU → 5-shuffle L2 norm) ran strictly back to back. ## Modifications - **One straight-line block per job.** The `p1_job` branch is hoisted outside the producer-step loop. The `i_t < T_LOOP` guard is dropped at compile time when `T_LOOP % P1_JOB_WARPS == 0`, since `p1_par < P1_JOB_WARPS` makes it always true then. ptxas can now interleave the token chains. This applies on both block widths. - **Invariant loads on the narrow block.** The phase-1 inputs (`x_q`, `x_k`, `g`, `beta`, output-norm gate) are read-only for the kernel's lifetime. On the narrow block (256 threads, 2 blocks/SM) they are loaded with `CopyG2ROp(invariant=True)` (`ld.global.nc`), so ptxas may schedule them ahead of the scratch/ring stores. title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve strong identities across VLM caches
summary: ## Motivation Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state. This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim. ## Modifications - Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host. - Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress. - Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality. - Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented. - Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors. - Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs. The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #4

title: [Fix] moe: Refresh cached correction bias after in-place weight updates
summary: ## Motivation `TopKConfig.correction_bias_for_dtype` caches `e_score_correction_bias` cast to the activation dtype. The cache key includes the parameter's `_version`, which is the mechanism the existing comment relies on to drop a copy taken before weights are loaded. That check does not fire for the writes RL actually uses. Weight loaders and the RL weight update path write through `param.data.copy_()`, and a write through `.data` does not bump `_version`. The cached BF16 bias built during warmup therefore stays in place for the rest of the process. With dummy-load startup, warmup runs on random weights, so every later routing decision uses a correction bias of about `±1e-3` instead of the real values (about 5 per expert on GLM-5.3-Flash). Weight sync replaces the parameter and the weight checker never sees the cache, because it is not a registered tensor. This affected every RL run on the ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash branch, including MI355X, not only MI300X. It is not an AMD kernel bug. Any in-place weight update that writes `e_score_correction_bias` through `.data` leaves the cache stale, on CUDA as well as HIP. ## Modifications The lookup path is unchanged from main: a cache hit returns the cached tensor without a copy. Following review, the refresh now happens when weights are loaded, not on every decode step. - `TopKConfig.refresh_correction_bias_cache()` copies the current bias into the existing cached tensor and re-keys it. title: [Fix] [AMD] tilelang: Zero masked KV loads in the BF16 sparse MLA decode kernel
summary: ## Motivation On HIP, `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` is used for both prefill and decode. For invalid (`-1`) top-k indices it loaded KV row 0 and relied on a `-inf` score mask. Padded CUDA-graph rows write their K/V into row 0 (`out_cache_loc` padding is 0). Once row 0 held a non-finite value, `-inf + q·k` and `0 * v` became NaN for every later request. With BF16 KV and decode CUDA graphs, the server was correct until the first decode batch whose size had no captured graph (for example 3 requests replayed in the batch-size-4 graph). After that, every request returned the right first token followed by `!!!!...` and `None` logprobs until the server restarted. Eager decode and FP8 KV were not affected. `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1` did not help. This showed up on GLM-5.3-Flash BF16 RL rollout on MI355X and is independent of the model: any BF16 sparse-MLA decode that uses this kernel and CUDA graphs can poison the server. ## Modifications In `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial`, masked slots now load zeros instead of row 0, in both the main and tail parts. The score mask is unchanged. The FP8 kernel (`sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial_fp8`) has the same load pattern and is not changed here. ## Accuracy Tests On a fresh MI355X server with BF16 KV and decode CUDA graphs, padded batches of 3 and 5 were correct, and so was every request afterward. title: [Fix] hicache: Restore sub-window SWA L3 hits under a mid-tree anchor
summary: ## Motivation An L3 hit shorter than one sliding window, under a mid-tree anchor, is dropped in both host-memory modes. It is the usual hit when a reader holds a prefix on device and another writer stored its continuation, e.g. a PD decode offloading its output KV. End to end (PD with decode KV offload, hybrid SWA + Mamba model, window 512, page 128; a 512-token prompt whose decode wrote KV up to 768), the next turn's prefill reuse: | prefill host memory | before | after | |---|---|---| | `cache` (`write_back`) | 512 (its own prompt; the 256 stored tokens are dropped) | 768 | | `buffer_only` | 512 (the lookup is declined) | 768 | Every turn's logprobs match a no-cache reference (max drift 4.4e-16). Run on a fork carrying this change. ## Modifications - **Cache mode** (Python and Rust tree cores): `SWAComponent.prepare_prefetch` stages `min(span, window)` pages at any anchor, and the SWA prefetch commit no longer drops a short window under a non-root anchor. The window head is the anchor path's own SWA; the match validator (`create_match_validator`) accepts a boundary only after a full contiguous SWA window, so a short window whose head is gone never matches. - **Buffer mode**: remove the full-window lookup minimum (`resolve_prefetch_threshold`). A staged hold pins FULL, not SWA, so the head of a staged short window can be evicted while it waits (the concern behind #39283); admission now refetches when this pass's joint match no longer reaches the window's start. ## Accuracy Tests No kernel or forward change. | test | before | after | |---|---|---| | `test_hicache_l3_prefetc

title: [Fix] hicache: Reject incomplete NIXL cache files before reading
summary: ## Motivation Refs #45563. A failed NIXL write can leave an empty or truncated cache file. The current lookup treats any existing file as a hit, and NIXL 1.4.0 can report a short read as successful. This lets a restore publish incomplete KV or sidecar data. The issue reports incorrect DSA outputs after restoring empty indexer files. Lookup checks alone are insufficient: hybrid restores using `assume_stored` can skip lookup. Validate the requested byte count at the shared read entrypoint before starting a transfer. ## Modifications - Treat empty FILE objects as lookup misses. - Reject FILE reads when any file is missing or smaller than its corresponding host buffer. Reuse the existing transfer sizes, including unequal Mamba component sizes; allow larger files for alignment padding. A rejected transfer leaves its destination unchanged and uses the existing failure propagation. - Extend the existing POSIX tests with real truncated files for KV copy/zero-copy, indexer copy, and Mamba zero-copy paths. Cover empty, one-byte-short, complete, and padded files. The production change adds 19 lines, with no new configuration or cached metadata. OBJ and write paths retain their existing behavior. This addresses the unsafe restore part of #45563; write alignment and batch chunking are separate work tracked by #35231, #42491, #36524, and #37690. title: [Perf] [AMD] mori: Read MORI EPv2 AsyncLL segmented receive in place, skipping the receive copy
summary: > **Draft, stacked on #44492.** This branch contains #44492's commits; review only the last commit, `MORI EPv2 AsyncLL: read the segmented receive layout in place`. It also needs ROCm/mori#918 (AsyncLL segmented receive layout), which is still in review, so the MORI-side API (`async_ll_recv_layout`, `segment_stride`) may change. I will rebase onto main once #44492 merges and update this PR to the final #918 API. ## Motivation With #44492, MORI EPv2 AsyncLL moves the dispatch tokens by SDMA into a landing buffer and then copies the received rows into a compact buffer for the MoE. ROCm/mori#918 adds a segmented receive layout: the landing buffer is one fixed-stride segment per source rank, so the expert can read it in place. This PR uses that layout for single-node prefill, which removes the receive-side copy. The SDMA transfer from the sender into the landing buffer is unchanged. ## Modifications All changes are in `layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py`, plus a comment in `moe_runner/aiter.py`: - **Opt-in by MORI capability, no new flag.** `init_mori_epv2_op` sets `async_ll_recv_layout="auto"` for single-node SDMA AsyncLL with bf16 or mxfp8 dispatch, and only if the installed MORI has that config field. With `auto`, MORI builds the segmented layout only when the op config supports it. Older MORI builds, multi-node (internode) ops and other dispatch dtypes keep the compact receive. - **One stride per dispatch, the same on every rank.** `_segmented_stride()` derives the per-source stride from the gathered DP rows (`_dispatch_sender_rows`, split over the attention TP ranks). title: Feature request: extension points for externally defined models (registration of runtime classes, attention lookup, attention kernels, sampler logprobs)
summary: Running a model defined outside SGLang (built at runtime, with its own attention kernels and logprob computation) needs four private touchpoints today: 1. **Registration.** `ModelRegistry.register(package_name)` imports a package; a class built at runtime can only be registered by writing `ModelRegistry.models[arch] = cls`. Request: `ModelRegistry.register_class(arch, cls)`. 2. **Attention-layer lookup.** Some components (e.g. breakable prefill CUDA graphs) find each layer's `RadixAttention` by attribute path (`layers[i].attention.attn` among others). A model with a different module tree must alias the module at one of those paths. Request: let the model expose its attention modules, e.g. a `get_attention_layers()` method. 3. **Attention kernels.** To use a custom varlen/paged attention kernel with `FlashAttentionBackend`'s metadata, we subclass it and override the private `_init_flash_attention_functions` hook. Request: a public way to supply the kernel functions to the FA backend. 4. **Sampler logprobs.** To return logprobs computed by the caller's code (so a trainer and the generator share one logprob path), we patch `Sampler.forward`. Request: a hook to override the logprob computation. Seen at sglang commit 851642ade7.

title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: compile the FP4 indexer prefill schedule kernels at startup
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm the DeepSeek-V4 FP4 indexer builds its prefill schedule per forward, outside the CUDA graph (`build_prefill_schedule`). summary: ## Motivation `torch.cuda.Stream.wait_stream()` currently records a newly constructed lazy event on every call: ```python self.wait_event(stream.record_event()) ``` That materializes as `cudaEventCreateWithFlags -> cudaEventRecord -> cudaStreamWaitEvent -> cudaEventDestroy`. title: [Fix] dsa: Cap the MQA-logits budget by host memory on integrated GPUs
summary: ## Motivation Refs #36941. The first half of that issue (the kpool path never calling the logits guard) was fixed by #40854. Part of what remains is the report from unified-memory machines: the fp32 MQA-logits budget comes out too large, and only `SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_FREE_MEM_FRACTION=0.01` avoided host OOM. This PR covers the ROCm integrated case (gfx1151). On an integrated GPU, device memory is host memory, but `mqa_logits_budget_bytes` caps the budget only by `torch.cuda.mem_get_info`. On ROCm gfx1151 (Strix Halo, `is_integrated=1`) that free figure does not move when the host takes memory: | step | `mem_get_info` free | host `MemAvailable` | |---|---|---| | idle | 108.0 GiB | 120.8 GiB | | 8 GiB device allocation | 99.9 | 112.5 | | freed (kept by the caching allocator) | 99.9 | 112.5 | | plus 24 GiB on the CPU | **99.9** | **87.7** | So the cap never tightens as the host fills up. On top of that, `Indexer._get_mqa_logits_budget_bytes` caches the budget per device at the first prefill, so even a correct measurement goes stale. SGLang already handles this at startup: `get_available_gpu_memory` uses `psutil.virtual_memory().available` when `props.is_integrated`. ## Modifications - `mqa_logits_utils.py`: new `mqa_logits_cap_by_host_memory`. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Reuse a failed unified PD transfer's pages only on proof its engine stopped
summary: This PR is part of a stack. ## Motivation Under unified memory a failed or aborted PD transfer's pages could be reused, or moved over, while its engine still touched them: - Prefill counted a send of a room that failed or was cleared as done at once. Mooncake drops a batch that timed out with its transfer possibly still running (freeBatchID refuses a busy batch), so the engine could keep reading source pages that already held another request's KV. - Decode counted a failed receive as done at its release timeout, or at once with deferred release disabled, and freed its destination at that timeout, under a late write from a prefill whose transfer kept running. - The page ledger did not protect a freed page from a transfer still recorded on it: a request's row release released its transfers, a page freed through the normal free path joined the free list as a plain hole (only vacated fences order a take), and a pool clear reset every fence. ## Modifications This PR has three commits. **Reuse a failed transfer's pages only on proof its engine stopped.** A timeout or failure now aborts the request; only proof of a transfer's end lets its pages be reused. The proof: a send is done only on the transfer worker's report on it, delivered to the send's own record even after its room was cleared or started anew. The worker reports a chunk it skips, and a send whose submitted transfer failed is reported unsettled and is never done. A failed receive is done only once no peer was sent its destination or every peer acknowledged its drain. Unified memory with PD requires SGLANG_DISAGGREGATIO

title: [Fix] modelopt_fp4: skip swizzled blockscales the marlin runner never reads
summary: ## What `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.create_weights()` allocates an fp8 copy of *every* expert blockscale in the swizzled layout (`*_blockscale_swizzled`). Three consumers read that copy: the FlashInfer Cutlass path, the CuteDSL path, and TRTLLM. **The marlin MoE runner never reads it.** `process_weights_after_loading()` returns right after `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin(layer)` (`modelopt_quant.py:2757`), i.e. before the Cutlass branch that would compute the swizzle, and the runner reads `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` through `get_marlin_quant_info()`. So on the marlin path the copy is pure waste, and because the function returns early there is nothing that could ever free it. ## Change Materialise the swizzled copy only when the selected backend consumes it — i.e. skip it for `marlin`, `flashinfer_megamoe`, `flashinfer_trtllm_moe`, and for `AUTO`. `AUTO` is resolved later in `process_weights_after_loading()`; the backends that do want the copy (Cutlass / CuteDSL) recompute and bind it there anyway via `alias_or_bind_derived_param`, so skipping the eager allocation is safe. Note `create_weights()` runs before the backend is resolved on this stack, which is why the existing condition could not catch marlin. ## Measurement Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, TP=2 on 2xL20 (47.45 GiB/card), `--mem-fraction-static 0.97`, CUDA graph on: | item | before | after | |---|---|---| | model footprint | 44.75 GB/card | **41.27 GB/card** (-3.48 GiB, -7.8 %) | | max_total_num_tokens | 240,192 | **547,072** | | KV pool | 0.54 GiB | 6.26 GiB | | decode (greedy, 5,157-token prompt) | 95.

title: [Feature] flashinfer: Split the extend into ragged and paged passes under full prefill CUDA graphs with an FP8 KV cache
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation Under `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill full`, `FlashInferAttnBackend` plans plain EXTEND with `use_ragged=False` (`init_forward_metadata_out_graph`). Every chunk then attends to its own new tokens through the paged kernel, reading their K/V back from the KV cache. The eager path, which breakable prefill graphs also take for attention, splits the work: the new tokens attend to themselves in the ragged kernel on the chunk's own K/V, the cached prefix goes through the paged kernel, and `merge_state` combines the two. With an FP8 KV cache this has two effects: - **Numerics.** The full graph sees the new tokens' K/V after FP8 rounding; eager and breakable see them in BF16. So full and breakable cannot agree on such a model, even where every other kernel is the same. - **Speed at head_dim 256.** The FP8 paged kernel is the slower of the two there. summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #48014 * #48013 * #48012 * #48011 * #48010 * __->__ #48009 ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory`, a PD node kept every band of the shared KV arena in place while any PD transfer might be in flight: the scheduler registered one pin source over every sub-pool (`disagg_transfers_in_flight`), true while a prefill send was queued or still sending a chunk, or while a decode destination was published, receiving or offloading. Under steady PD load the pool therefore never compacted and floats never moved, and the predicate had to be read again on every capacity query, since its answer changes with no write to the pool. A PD transfer addresses device rows by physical id from the moment the ids are translated for a send, or published to the peer for a receive, until its engine is done with them. title: Fix/encdec decode paged alloc row offset
summary: ## Motivation For encoder-decoder models the encoder KV is prepended to the request's req_to_token row, so decoder position L lives at row position encoder_len + L. `alloc_for_decode` already accounts for that when writing (locs = encoder_lens + seq_lens) but not when computing the paged allocation: last_loc was read at `row[seq_len - 1]` and the new-page decision used the encoder-stripped seq_len. At page_size > 1 that makes `last_loc + 1` resolve to `row[L]` -- the slot already held by encoder position `L` -- so the row stops satisfying `row[j] == page[j // page_size] * page_size + (j % page_size)`. The paged free path relies on that invariant: free_segment() samples one page representative every page_size row entries, so an aliased row makes it name the same physical page twice and `available_size()` grows by one page per request until the idle pool-leak invariant aborts the scheduler. ## Modifications Use the row length (encoder_lens + seq_lens) for last_loc, for the seq_lens handed to alloc_decode, and for the CPU mirror feeding `get_num_new_pages`. `page_size == 1` takes the non-paged branch before any of this runs, so default CUDA behaviour is unchanged, as is every non-encoder-decoder model. ## Accuracy Tests Added: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_encdec_paged_kv_page_accounting.py` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #42605192461](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42605192461)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #42605192386

title: [Fix] flashinfer: Pass logits_soft_cap at plan time so gemma-2 and grok are capped
summary: ﻿## Motivation Fixes #33915. Related: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#1193. The FlashInfer attention backend never applies `logit_cap`. Since flashinfer >= 0.2, `use_logits_soft_cap` is compile-time state that `plan()`/`begin_forward()` bakes into the selected kernel module; the deprecated per-call `forward()`/`forward_return_lse()` still accepts a `logits_soft_cap` argument but the value only reaches a kernel that was planned with capping enabled. sglang passed the cap exclusively at forward() time and never at any of the plan call sites, so every model with a nonzero `logit_cap` ran uncapped on the default backend: - gemma-2 family: `logit_cap = config.attn_logit_softcapping` (50.0) - grok: `logit_cap = max(getattr(config, "attn_logit_softcapping", 30.0), 0.0)` (gemma-3 / gemma-4 / gemma-3n pass `logit_cap=0.0` and are unaffected.) The triton backend applies the cap, so the two backends disagreed on the same checkpoint. The ragged prefill wrapper dropped `window_left` by the same mechanism. Main fixed that in #46214, so after the rebase onto main this PR covers only the cap. Verified against the pinned flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 wheel: `plan()` selects the module with `logits_soft_cap > 0` and `forward()` stores the per-call values that `run()` passes to the kernel, so the plan-time argument enables the feature and the existing per-layer forward() arguments keep choosing the values: ``` 1 cap at plan(): vs capped 0.999999 | vs uncapped 0.593908 2 cap at legacy forward() only: vs capped 0.593905 | vs uncapped 1.000000 <- the bug 3 cap at plan and forward: vs capped 0.999999 | vs unc

title: [Bug] Breakable prefill CUDA graph: short prefills padded to a capture bucket give different logprobs than eager (Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, hybrid GDN, v0.5.23)
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When I run SGLang v0.5.23 with the breakable prefill CUDA graph and `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 32`, short prefills give different logprobs than they do in eager mode. The breakable prefill CUDA graph (BCG) is the default prefill backend on CUDA. The difference only shows up when the number of new tokens is not exactly a capture bucket size, so the prefill gets padded up to the next bucket. The gap is much larger than float noise. In one case, the first token `L` has a probability of 0.4814 with the graph and 0.2902 in eager mode. Short extends on top of a radix-cache hit are affected in the same way. With 64 cached tokens and 18 new tokens, one prompt gives 0.4850 with the graph and 0.6005 in eager mode. This means ordinary multi-turn traffic can hit the bug, not just very short prompts. Prefills whose new-token count lands exactly on a bucket (16 or 20 tokens) match eager mode to 4 decimal places. The prefills of 36 to 40 tokens that I tested also match, because anything over 32 tokens runs eagerly on both servers. I expected a padded replay to match eager mode up to float noise. title: [Fix] [AMD] dflash: Sample-verify temperature > 0 drafts on ROCm instead of falling back to greedy
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, `verify_sampling` resolves no `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` (the CUDA kernel is built on FlashInfer), so every DFLASH request with temperature > 0 is verified by greedy argmax ("DFLASH non-greedy verification is unavailable on this build/device; falling back to greedy argmax verification"). The served distribution is then not the requested one. DFlash proposals are a linear chain (`topk == 1`), which collapses the general tree verifier into something cheap to write in Triton. This PR adds that verifier for ROCm, plus a fused fast path on the top-k support that removes the host syncs the dense path needs. Related: #34140 adds a general Triton tree verifier for ROCm (EAGLE and DFLASH). This PR is DFLASH-only and narrower: it binds only inside `dflash_utils.py`, so EAGLE's tree verification is untouched, and the fused path covers the common top-k sampling configuration without materialising anything vocab-sized. Happy to rebase onto or fold into #34140 if reviewers prefer one path. ## Modifications 1. **`kernels/ops/speculative/dflash_chain_sampling.py`** (new): `chain_speculative_sampling_target_only`, with the CUDA operator's keyword signature. On a chain, `retrive_next_sibling` is always -1 and `prob_acc` resets on every acceptance, so the accept test at level j is local (`coin[j-1] <= tps_j / threshold_acc or tps_j >= threshold_single`) and the walk is a gather plus a leading-run count. title: [Fix] minimax-m3: Support pipeline parallelism in PD disaggregation
summary: ## Summary This PR enables MiniMax-M3 pipeline parallelism under PD disaggregation with the Mooncake transfer backend. It fixes two MiniMax-M3 PP blockers: 1. MiniMax sparse index state registration did not preserve global sparse layer IDs, so Mooncake could not safely map `index_k` transfer entries across pipeline stages. 2. Decode CUDA Graph capture built PP proxy tensors with global token shapes even when the PP boundary tensor layout was already scattered by attention TP, causing hidden/residual shape mismatches during CUDA Graph replay. With this PR, MiniMax-M3 can run symmetric PP disaggregated serving such as `TP4/PP2/EP4` on both Prefill and Decode nodes, while keeping Decode CUDA Graph enabled. ## Motivation MiniMax-M3 has sparse attention states in addition to the standard KV cache. These sparse states are stored in `index_k_pool` and only correspond to a subset of model layers. Before this PR, pipeline parallelism was explicitly blocked for MiniMax sparse index transfer because each PP stage only sees a local sparse-index list. Without the original global layer IDs, the disaggregation backend cannot know whether source and destination sparse-index entries refer to the same model layer. After fixing sparse-index transfer, Decode CUDA Graph exposed another issue. In PP + EP / scattered-layout cases, CUDA Graph dummy `PPProxyTensors` were constructed using the global token count, while the actual hidden states had already been scattered by attention TP. title: [Feat] sampling: Honor per-request sampling_seed without deterministic inference
summary: ## Motivation Part 1 of #48474. Today a request's `sampling_seed` is honored only under `--enable-deterministic-inference`. That flag also overrides aten matmuls and reductions process-wide with SGLang's batch-invariant kernels, and changes attention backends, chunk alignment and the sampler's softmax path. A caller that only wants reproducible sampling, or that brings its own model, kernels and batch invariance (e.g. an RL trainer embedding SGLang), has to turn all of that on, then monkeypatch `ModelRunner.maybe_enable_batch_invariant_mode` to undo the kernel overrides. Outside the flag the seed is dropped silently, including the OpenAI `seed` field, which maps to `sampling_seed`. vLLM honors per-request seeds without a flag: each request has a seed (random if unset), and a batch with an explicit seed skips the fused FlashInfer sampler for one that takes per-row seeds. This PR does the same in SGLang, reusing its existing hash-based seeded sampler (`multinomial_with_seed`). ## Modifications - `SamplingBatchInfo`: - Outside deterministic mode, a batch builds `sampling_seed` when a request sets `sampling_seed`. Its other rows get random filler seeds, so they stay random. The filler seeds come from a dedicated `random.Random`, not the global `random`: TP ranks sample independently (no token sync by default), every rank builds the same batches, but the global `random` also serves rank-specific callers such as tracing, which would desync the ranks' filler seeds. - A new CPU list, `explicit_sampling_seeds`, tracks which rows set their own seed. `filter_batch` drops the seeds onc

title: [Fix] Confidential-Computing: enable Flashinfer all-reduce fusion
summary: ## Motivation Under NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC), FlashInfer AllReduce + Residual + RMSNorm fusion was effectively off. FlashInfer's usual VMM `SymmDeviceMemory` workspace cannot be allocated under CC, so SGLang's preflight failed and fusion fell back to the normal all-reduce. FlashInfer [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3993](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3993) (in 0.7.0 and later; SGLang pins 0.7.2) allocates the TRTLLM workspace with torch symmetric memory under CC instead. This PR lets SGLang run the multicast-free `trtllm` backend under CC, and keeps backend selection and the workspace preflight safe there. ## Modifications All in `layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` and `arg_groups/overrides.py`, gated on `is_confidential_compute()`: - **`cc(fix): enable FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion under Confidential Computing`**: `_resolve_backend` forces `trtllm` under CC and raises on an explicit `mnnvl` or `cutedsl` request or on multi-node, which need NVLink multicast. - **`cc: choose only fusion backends Confidential Computing can run`**: under CC, the fusion auto-enable turns on `trtllm` for single-node systems only, and leaves multi-node and MiMo (`cutedsl`) off. Before, those defaults crashed at startup instead of falling back. An explicit incompatible request still raises in `_resolve_backend`. - **`cc: keep the AR-fusion preflight vote under Confidential Computing`**: the preflight's cross-rank vote now also runs under CC, so a rank that cannot allocate stops every rank before FlashInfer's workspace rendezvous instead of hanging startup. title: [Fix] lora: Bound expert_id against num_experts in fused MoE LoRA kernel
summary: ## Motivation `_fused_moe_lora_kernel` reads `expert_id` from `expert_ids_ptr` and guards only against the `-1` sentinel, then indexes the stacked LoRA weights with it: ```python if expert_id == -1: return ... b_ptrs = ( cur_b_ptr + lora_id * stride_bl + expert_id * stride_be + offs_k[:, None] * stride_bk + offs_bn[None, :] * stride_bn ) ``` `num_experts` is passed into the kernel (derived as `lora_a_stacked[0].shape[1]` in `_fused_moe_lora`) but is never read in the kernel body, so `expert_id` has no upper bound. ### The out-of-range id is produced deliberately With shared-experts fusion, the fused shared expert is appended to the routed set and given an id past the routed range. In `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/hash_topk.py`, the last `topk_ids` column is assigned: ```python topk_ids[:, -1] = torch.randint( low=self.num_experts, high=self.num_experts + self.num_fused_shared_experts, ... ) ``` So with one fused shared expert, `topk_ids` contains exactly `num_experts`, while `lora_a_stacked` only covers `0 .. num_experts - 1`. `_moe_runner_fusion_disable` in `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py` auto-sets `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` for the `flashinfer_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_trtllm`, `experimental_sgl_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` runners. The Triton runner is not among them, so this kernel is reachable with fusion active. ### The failure is silent cross-adapter contamination For `lora_a_stacked[0]` of shape `(max_loras, num_experts, max_lora_rank, K)`: ``` stride_bl = stride(0) = num_experts * max_lora_rank * K stride_be = stride(1) = max_lora_rank * K

title: [Perf] rust-server: Size the tokenizer pool from the frontend cores
summary: Closes #49190. ## Motivation The Rust server sizes its tokenizer pool from `--tokenizer-worker-num`, which defaults to 1. As a result, a single thread, `tokenizer-0`, renders the chat template and encodes every request. The Python frontend uses the same flag value but still encodes on a thread pool, so it doesn't have this limit. With long multi-turn prompts, that one thread saturates. Requests then wait in front of the scheduler, and the Rust frontend's tail latency gets worse than Python's. Full measurements are in #49190: Gemma4-31B FP8, TP4 on H200, agentic replay with mean ISL of about 16.7k tokens. A short summary: | | Python | Rust, 1 thread (today) | Rust, 4 threads | Rust, 8 threads | |---|---|---|---|---| | c100 TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | 208 / 1097 | 215 / 1182 | 173 / 1052 | 172 / 1030 | | c100 queue wait p99 (ms) | 218 | 430 | 181 | 180 | | c128 TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | 319 / 1492 | 328 / 1619 | 283 / 1291 | not run | | c128 queue wait p99 (ms) | 231 | 648 | 186 | not run | Queue wait is measured from the client send to the scheduler's `entry_time`. ITL and throughput were the same in all runs. 8 threads gave the same results as 4 (the busiest tokenizer thread was about 8% of a core), so 4 is past the saturation point for this workload; heavier workloads can still raise the flag. ## Modifications - Add `RuntimeConfig::tokenizer_thread_num()` (Rust), which returns `max(tokenizer_worker_num, frontend_cores / 2)`, where `frontend_cores` is the shared core set that Python's `_partition_cores` pins the frontend to. - The runtime sizes the tokenizer pool with this value. title: [Perf] mooncake: Group and parallelize direct linker layer-wise loads
summary: ## Motivation The Mooncake direct linker loads an L3 hit with one synchronous `batch_get_into_multi_buffer_ranges` call per layer per pool, on a single thread. Each ranged op costs roughly 3 us serialized, so a DSA page-layer (a 72 KB KV range plus an 8 KB indexer range) moves at about 12-14 GB/s per rank, well below the NIC line rate. With a short new suffix on a long cached prefix (the common multi-turn / agentic shape) the load cannot hide behind compute, so it is directly on TTFT. A standalone Mooncake microbenchmark with the GLM-5.2 page geometry (64K tokens, 6.6 GB, one GPU and its PIX NIC) shows where the time goes: | read pattern | time | GB/s | |---|---|---| | one call per layer (current) | 454 ms | 14.5 | | one call per layer, keys split over 4 threads | 188 ms | 35.0 | | one call per page (all layers), 8 threads | 137 ms | 47.8 | Concurrency is the main lever; reading several layers of a page per call adds more on top. ## Modifications - `load_layer_wise` reads `linker_load_layer_group` layers per call (default 8) and splits each call's keys over `linker_load_threads` workers (default 4).
