title: [Bug] Inkling: fused attention prologue stores CUDA-graph padding rows into KV slot 0 → NaN logits (`probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0`)
summary: ## Describe the bug With Inkling (NVFP4) the prefill CUDA graph backend defaults to `full`. The fused attention-prologue extend kernel (`inkling_attn_prologue_extend_kernel` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/inkling/inkling_attn_prologue_fused.cuh`) stores K/V for every token in its launch grid, including the padding tokens of the captured graph bucket. Padding tokens get `out_cache_loc = 0` (the prefill graph buffer registry zero-fills the padded tail: `build_prefill_registry` in `cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py`, `PaddingPolicy.ZERO`), and their rows are stale static-buffer data, sometimes non-finite, so they are written into KV slot 0. Slot 0 is later read by sliding-window attention when the KV page size is below 128 (the default on H200 with FA4 is page size 1). The masked score is 0, but `0 * NaN` is NaN, so the logits row becomes NaN. - `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0`: `torch.multinomial` asserts, the scheduler exits on every rank. - Default `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=1`: no crash; affected requests silently return token id 0 (`!`) with NaN logprobs. - B200 is affected too: FA4 forces page size 128 on sm100 (`_fa4_page_constraint`), which hides the read; with page size 1 B200 crashes the same way. ## Reproduction Environment: 1x H200, `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-cu130`, checkpoint `thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4` revision `test` (small test checkpoint, fits one GPU). ```bash huggingface-cli download thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4 --revision test --local-dir /tmp/inkling-test SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0 sglang serve --model-path /tmp/inkling-test \ --served-model-n

title: [Fix] inkling: Skip KV stores for CUDA-graph padding tokens in the fused attn prologue
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #46572. With Inkling, prefill runs under the full CUDA graph by default. The fused attention-prologue extend kernel stores K/V for every token in its launch grid, which under graph replay is the padded bucket. Padding tokens (`t >= cu[B]`) get `out_cache_loc = 0` from the prefill graph buffer registry and carry stale, sometimes non-finite, rows, so they are written into KV slot 0. Sliding-window attention can later read slot 0 (KV page size below 128, the default on H200 with FA4), which turns the logits row into NaN: `torch.multinomial` asserts with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_GUMBEL_SAMPLE=0`, and with the default sampler affected requests silently return token 0 with NaN logprobs. Details and a standalone reproducer are in #46572. ## Modifications - `inkling_attn_prologue_fused.cuh`: add the real sequence count `B` to `AttnPrologueExtendParams` and skip the KV store in `inkling_attn_prologue_extend_kernel` for tokens at or beyond `cu[B]`. Real tokens are stored exactly as before; the `out` / `k_out` / `v_out` writes for padding rows (the graph's own scratch outputs) are unchanged. `B` is already computed in the launcher (`cache_indices.size(0)`), and `cu` has `B + 1` entries. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_inkling_attn_prologue_extend_pad.py`: new kernel unit test. It fills the padded tail of `qkvr` with NaN, maps padding tokens to slot 0 as the graph runner does, and checks that slot 0 and every other unused slot stay untouched while real tokens are stored bit-identically to the kernel's own `k_out` / `v_out` and are finite (`num_pad` 1 and 8). ##

title: [Fix] attention: Order the fp8 paged MQA logits kernel's TMEM dealloc after every math warp's tcgen05.ld
summary: ## Motivation `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/cutedsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.py` frees its accumulator TMEM without ordering the other math warps' reads before the free. Math warps 0-7 (two warp groups of 128 threads) read the UMMA accumulators with `tcgen05.ld`. Math warp 0 is the allocator: at the end of the kernel it runs `tmem.relinquish_alloc_permit()` and `tmem.free(tmem_ptr)`, which is `tcgen05.dealloc` issued by warp 0 alone (`cutlass.utils.TmemAllocator.free` has no CTA barrier for a 1-CTA kernel). Nothing orders the last `tcgen05.ld` of warps 1-7 before that dealloc: - each warp's `fence_view_async_tmem_load` (`tcgen05.wait::ld`) only waits for its own loads; - the UMMA pipelines' `consumer_release` arrivals are waited on by the UMMA warp, never by math warp 0, and each pipeline's consumer group is one warp group (128 threads), so warp group 0 learns nothing about warp group 1; - there is no `cute.arch.barrier`, named barrier or mbarrier wait between the last load of warps 1-7 and warp 0's free. So the kernel deallocates columns that warp group 1 may still be loading from. The CuTe DSL's own `examples/blackwell/dense_gemm.py` does `cute.arch.barrier()` right before `dealloc_tmem` for this reason. `tcgen05.dealloc` does not clear TMEM, so the stale loads return the right data as long as nobody re-allocates the columns in between. With the shipped launch (384 threads x 168 registers, >128 KB smem) one CTA fits per SM and no other kernel can take the freed columns before this CTA exits, so the output is correct today. title: [Perf] [AMD] decode-attention: Skip the CDNA launch hints on RDNA3/3.5/4 for GQA decode
summary: ## Motivation Since #42092, RDNA defaults to the Triton attention backend. Its grouped decode kernel (`_decode_grouped_att_m_fwd`) applies MI300-tuned launch hints on every HIP GPU: `waves_per_eu=1`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`, `kpack=2`, with 4 warps (from #3255). On RDNA3.5 (gfx1151, Strix Halo; wave32; the other RDNA generations are also wave32 with no MFMA): - `waves_per_eu=1` lets the compiler use 246 VGPRs per wave, so 5 waves fit per SIMD. Without it, 156 VGPRs and 9 waves. - `matrix_instr_nonkdim` and `kpack` produce identical code on RDNA. ROCm/aiter#5917 drops `kpack` from its gfx1151/gfx1201 configs for the same reason, extending the gfx1100 cleanup in ROCm/aiter#5217. GQA decode at batch is limited by how many KV loads are in flight, so with these hints the kernel reads the KV cache 1.4-2.7x slower once ~8+ requests are running. ROCm/aiter#2402 reaches the same conclusion for its unified attention on RDNA: `waves_per_eu` 8 on gfx1151, against 2 on CDNA. ## Modifications On RDNA3, RDNA3.5 and RDNA4 (gfx110x, gfx115x, gfx120x), `_rdna_grouped_num_warps` drops the hints and uses 2 warps. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation While profiling Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid GDN + full attention, M-RoPE) on 4x Intel Arc Pro B70 with the decode XPU graph enabled, we found that multimodal requests decode about 0.5 ms/token slower than text-only requests with the same context length. The GPU kernel time per step is the same in both cases, so the gap comes from host-side work outside the graph replay. There are two sources of overhead: 1. **M-RoPE decode positions are rebuilt on the host every step.** `_compute_mrope_positions_decode` collects one Python int per request and calls `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every decode step. On an in-order queue, this blocking H2D copy waits for the previous step to finish, so the overlap scheduler cannot prepare batch N+1 while batch N is running. Text-only requests do not take this path, which is why only multimodal decode is affected. 2. **The XPU fused GDN decode fills a mask in every layer.** `XpuGDNAttnBackend.forward_fused_gdn` allocates `torch.ones(bs, dtype=torch.bool)` in every linear-attention layer. This mask is constant, but it is recorded into the decode graph, so every replay launches one fill kernel per GDN layer (48 per step for Qwen3.8-27B). ## Modifications - **`MultimodalInputs` / `ForwardBatch`:** - Add `MultimodalInputs.get_mrope_position_delta_on_device()`. title: [Perf] [NPU] gdn: Enable direct state-pool I/O for prefill
summary: ## Motivation A shared-prefix hit may require temporal CoW to turn a read-only cached state into a request-owned destination. Ordinary chunk continuation generally keeps using the request's own state slot and does not require that CoW. Both paths still gather the initial state into a temporary contiguous tensor and scatter the returned final state back into the pool, adding state-sized temporary allocations, data movement, and host dispatch overhead. This PR connects the NPU GDN backend to indexed pool I/O: the operator reads the initial state from its source slot and writes the final state directly to the request's destination slot. Eligible shared-prefix prefills can omit temporal CoW, while eligible cached and continuation prefills avoid the temporary gather/scatter. The recurrence, state precision, and chunk-local `h` used by `fwd_o` are preserved. Companion kernel PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/970 The kernel PR is required to **enable** the new path, but is not a merge-time hard dependency. With an older kernel, operator detection disables pool I/O and preserves the legacy CoW/operator path. ## Modifications ### Source and destination state lifecycle - Track prefill source slots independently from request-owned destination slots. - Translate source and destination indices to physical pool slots and normalize them to contiguous int32 tensors. - Allow requests sharing a cached prefix to read the same source slot while writing separate destinations. - Preserve fresh-request zero initialization and existing destination-slot ownership. - Keep convol

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
summary: ## Motivation `SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel. Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call): | S | strided | dense | gain | |---|---|---|---| | 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x | | 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x | | 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x | | 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x | | 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** | The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS. ## Modifications - Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**. - The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change. - Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check. - The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch. ## Accuracy Tests - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layou

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: add a Triton dense attention prefill path for gfx1151
summary: ## Motivation `SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a **non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5, Ryzen AI MAX 395) that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same `attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens, versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost. ## What this adds * `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4 warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA, `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores). * A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN` (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`, `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on SDPA. ## Numbers (gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=12

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k2.5: Fuse MLA projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write
summary: ## Motivation In Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 graph decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA key projection, RoPE and KV-cache write run as separate launches on the critical path, even though they share operands. AITER's `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` does all three in one launch. #38340 already added this fusion for FP8 `w_kc` (`fused_fp8_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, DSA path). This PR adds MXFP4 `w_kc` as a second branch of that same structure rather than a parallel path. ## Modifications | Piece in `forward_mla_rocm.py` | FP8 `w_kc` (#38340, unchanged) | MXFP4 `w_kc` (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Gate `_can_fuse_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` | shared terms + TileLang/Triton DSA backend | shared terms + `_can_fuse_mxfp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` | | Kernel in `_fused_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` | `fused_fp8_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` | `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` | | Call site in core | DSA branch | aiter-backend branch | - Shared gate terms: gfx95 + AITER, kill-switch on, no DCP, has RoPE, no deep-gemm BMM, no LoRA on `kv_b_proj`. The gate then dispatches on `w_kc.dtype`. - MXFP4 terms: fuse only during CUDA-graph capture of AITER-backend decode with at most 256 tokens, at head dims the kernel tiles, without DSA or DCP; eager decode and larger captured batches keep the split path. - With an FP8 KV cache, fused Q is not bit-identical to split Q (about 1% of the absorbed values move by one FP8 step); the KV-cache bytes match. - The FP8 and MXFP4 fused writers share one KV-target helper, which maps HiSparse slots like the split path. - One `fuse_bmm_rope_cache` flag in prepare cover

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k2.5: Fuse shared-expert append into AITER grouped topk
summary: ## Motivation - Kimi-K2.5 routes with grouped top-k: 8 routed experts plus 1 fused shared expert. - On ROCm/AITER with one expert-parallel rank, the shared expert's ID and weight are appended after grouped top-k by a separate `fused_append_shared_experts` launch in every MoE layer. - That launch sits on the latency-critical decode path and only writes constants, so it can be removed. ## Modifications - New fast path `srt/layers/moe/aiter_topk.py`, tried first by `select_experts` on ROCm/AITER. - One persistent `[height, routed_k + n_shared]` weight/ID buffer per routing config, with the shared columns pre-filled once. AITER `biased_grouped_topk` writes the routed columns through strided views, so no append launch runs. - Buffers live in the runtime context (`get_buffer`): - Height = max(chunked-prefill size, `max_prefill_tokens`), floored at 8192 and capped at 131072 rows. - Cost: `layers x height x (routed_k + n_shared) x 8 B`, e.g. about 71 MB for 60 layers at 16384 rows. - Never allocated inside a CUDA-graph capture; that call takes the ordinary path. - Same kernel inputs as the ordinary path: an fp32 correction bias routes in fp32 (shared helper `aiter_grouped_topk_route_inputs`). - KT's `mask_cpu_expert_ids` now masks out of place, so it cannot overwrite the persistent shared column. - No new env var or flag. Fallbacks (the existing routing + append path runs): | Condition | Reason | |---|---| | Not grouped top-k, no correction bias, or no fused shared expert | nothing to fuse | | `moe_ep_size != 1` or per-rank shared slots (DeepEP/MegaMoE) | shared IDs are per rank |

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Unregister a failed staging room before releasing its KV
summary: ## Problem When a PD decode transfer fails and is not held for deferred release, `pop_transferred_with_outcomes` releases the request (which clears `req.kv.req_pool_idx`) before it unregisters the request's staging room. With the default `SGLANG_PLB_SCATTER_DEFER=0`, the KV manager's receive thread scatters arriving chunks itself, so it can scatter a pending chunk for the still-registered room in that window. `_scatter_region` then indexes `req_to_token[None, start:end]`, which selects whole rows of other requests, and writes the failed request's chunk into live requests' KV. The deferred path (`_do_release`) already unregisters before it releases. With `SGLANG_PLB_SCATTER_DEFER=1` the scatter runs on the scheduler thread and cannot interleave. ## Fix - The immediate-release branch unregisters the staging room before the release, the same order as `_do_release`. - `_unregister_staging_room` replaces the three copies of the registered-room check. ## Tests - `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`: a failed staging transfer released at once unregisters its room before the release. The test fails on main with the order reversed. - A CPU reproduction with the real `DecodeStagingHandler`, `ReqToTokenPool` and torch scatter path, forcing the interleaving with a thread, showed a live request's K overwritten by the failed request's staged chunk on main. - `test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py` and `test_staging_draft_kv_slots.py` pass locally. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #4255301784

title: [Bug] ignore_eos requests finish early when their grammar terminates
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug A request sent with `ignore_eos=true` stops early if it is grammar-constrained (`regex`, `json_schema`, `ebnf`, or a grammar the server attaches, such as the `glm47` tool-call grammar). It finishes with `finish_reason: stop` as soon as the grammar reaches its terminal state, instead of running to `max_new_tokens`. `ignore_eos` exists mostly for benchmarking with a fixed output length, so this silently shortens outputs and skews throughput numbers. In a fixed-length serving benchmark with `ignore_eos` and the `glm47` tool-call grammar (speculative decoding on), 250 of 1,382 requests (18%) returned at least 5% fewer tokens than requested, and the mean output length dropped from 1,096 to 724 tokens compared with an earlier build that did not attach the grammar. Per-case GPU measurements are in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43003#issuecomment-6101767131. **Cause.** `Req.update_finish_state` finishes a request whenever its grammar is terminated, without checking `ignore_eos` ([`schedule_batch.py` L1492-L1494 at 5a2645d](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5a2645deba2f9e8514f69e3ba287d03f45

title: [Fix] rust_extensions: Include C++ flags in the TreeCore build cache key
summary: ## Motivation The TreeCore build configuration preserves inherited CXXFLAGS for torch-sys, but the local extension-cache fingerprint does not include them. After one build is cached, changing those flags can silently return the old binary. The loader takes the cache-hit path before Cargo runs, so Cargo's build-input tracking cannot detect the change. ## Modifications Include the final effective CXXFLAGS string in the Torch build fingerprint. This separates both cached extension artifacts and Cargo target directories when the C++ flags change. Add a regression to the existing registered Rust-extension test file. Changed flags must load a newly built artifact; repeated identical flags must reuse it. This intentionally invalidates existing local Torch-extension cache entries. A source-checkout move may also trigger a conservative rebuild because the effective flags include the compatibility header's absolute path. Bundled wheel loading is unchanged. Generic build-environment selection and other compiler variables are outside this change's scope. ## Accuracy Tests - Existing registered Rust-extension file: 16 tests pass. - The same file with the new regression on pristine main 75d7c3ba83ff7519a3d9e673dde144b154dcd654: 15 existing tests pass; the new regression fails because the -O0 artifact is reused for -O3 -march=native. - Separate native-library probe: three loads request compile-time values 1, 2 and 2. The baseline returns 1, 1 and 1 from one build. The fix returns 1, 2 and 2 from two builds. The final native probe uses real crate discovery, toolchain probes, Cargo, cc-rs C

title: [Fix] flashinfer: Apply the sliding window in ragged prefill for hybrid-SWA models
summary: ## Motivation On `--attention-backend flashinfer`, a hybrid sliding-window/full model's sliding layers attend past their window during ragged prefill. FlashInfer selects the kernel module at plan time: `window_left >= 0` picks the variant with the sliding mask compiled in, and a `window_left` passed only to `forward` has no effect on a module planned without it. Main plans one ragged wrapper, shared by sliding and full layers, without the window. On SM100 there is a second cause: for the head dims it serves, that wrapper uses CUTLASS, whose ragged attention ignores the window even when it is planned. This is unchanged in FlashInfer 0.7.3, which main now pins: `fmha_varlen`, the CUTLASS ragged path, still builds its module with `use_sliding_window=False`. A ragged wrapper planned with `window_left=511` on B300 (FlashInfer 0.7.2, lengths [1500, 700], 12 q heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16), max absolute error against an fp32 reference: | Backend | vs windowed reference | vs full-attention reference | |---|---:|---:| | CUTLASS | 0.390 | 0.0081 | | FA2 | 0.0084 | 0.466 | This was found while adding Beam (#44747) and is split out of #45256 at review. It affects every hybrid-SWA model that takes ragged prefill on this backend, not only Beam. Multimodal models, multi-item scoring, deterministic inference and `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_PAGED` use the paged path instead. ## Modifications Merged with main after the FlashInfer 0.7.3 bump (#48468), where a sliding-window read is a `WindowRead`. - Each wrapper (sliding/full, or decoder/cross-attention) gets its own ragged prefill plan i

title: [Perf] quantization: Speed up Hopper group32 FP8 quantization with FP32 scales
summary: ## Motivation The row-major FP32 power-of-two scale path uses `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2` on the baseline. This PR routes the matching contiguous BF16 group32 case on Hopper to the existing trait-driven kernel. Both kernels use two lanes per group. For `[8192, 5120]`, the launch changes from 32 threads and 16 groups per CTA to 256 threads and 128 groups per CTA, reducing the observed grid from 81,920 to 10,240 CTAs. The trait-driven kernel also uses packed BF16 pairs for the local absmax and power-of-two scaling. Six interleaved baseline/candidate H200 server restarts show median **8K TTFT falling 2.21% at c1 and 2.31% at c2**; the constructed real-text workload improves 2.86%. The cold-L2 kernel measurement is **100.257 → 31.761 μs (3.16×)**. The serving results include the complete dispatch and validation path. This builds on #26766's fused rounding; it does not remove another scale-rounding launch. Related #46838 targets column-major FP32 scales for DeepGEMM, whereas this change targets row-major group32. ## Changes and review fixes - Separate power-of-two rounding (`kUe8m0`) from packed storage (`kPackedScale`). Preserve existing packed, sorted, masked and fused-activation specializations, including the external fused route+quant trait consumer. - Route supplied contiguous FP32 power-of-two scales for flat BF16 group32 through the Hopper trait kernel. Normalize singleton strides using a view of the same storage. Automatic packed-scale allocation is unchanged. - Validate each tensor once in the trait FP32-scale launcher, allowing 16B-aligned output row strides. Limit

title: [Perf] DSpark: reduce compact verify execution overhead
summary: ## Motivation Compact DSpark verify currently packs target inputs into temporary tensors, copies them into CUDA Graph buffers, and expands packed logits and hidden states back to fixed-stride tensors for acceptance and draft KV commits. This adds work around the target forward even when its token budget is smaller. This PR extracts the execution-overhead optimizations into an opt-in change on top of main. It does not change the planner, cost estimates, token budgets, graph capture tiers, or static/compact routing policy. ## Modifications - `SGLANG_DSPARK_COMPACT_DIRECT_INPUTS=1`: fuse input packing into the graph's input/position/cache-location buffers; skip exact-alias copies and duplicate layout staging. - `SGLANG_DSPARK_COMPACT_NATIVE_ACCEPT=1`: accept greedy requests directly from packed rows and commit packed target hidden states to draft KV, avoiding the dense logits/hidden scatter. Preserve legacy zero-padding and cap-trim semantics. - `SGLANG_DSPARK_COMPACT_POST_FOLD=1`: with native accept, also perform Engram history updates and FutureMap publication in the graph. Only the small candidate-token matrix is reconstructed for Engram. All three flags default to false. Unsupported KV pools, eager execution, sampling, grammar/logits adjustments, logprobs, watermarking, and diagnostics that require strided logits retain the existing fallback. KV-pool capability lookup is deferred until graph warmup/capture because the draft pool is not initialized when the epilogue is constructed. ## Accuracy Tests On this PR branch: - 45 differential cases passed with `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`

title: [Fix] speculative: Support --speculative-token-map with a vocab-sharded target lm_head (TP>1)
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #42397. `--speculative-token-map` (reduced "hot" draft vocab) crashes at `--tp-size > 1`. `init_lm_head` in `eagle_worker_v2.py` indexes the shared target lm_head with **global** vocab ids. Under vocab-parallel TP each rank only holds `vocab / tp` rows, so this either: - reads out of bounds, giving a device-side assert in `vectorized_gather_kernel`, or - silently picks the wrong rows on rank ≥ 1. #42424 makes this fail fast. This PR makes it work instead. If #42424 lands first, its guard can be dropped. ## Modifications New `slice_hot_token_head(hot_token_id, target_lm_head)`. It is pure index math, run once at init. 1. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Enable Decode Context Parallel (DCP) for MLA models on the aiter attention backend (AMD ROCm, gfx950). DCP shards the KV cache across ranks along the sequence dimension using round-robin (global-position) assignment, so each rank only stores and attends over `1/W` of the context during decode. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Keep one zeroed MegaAttention packed-query buffer instead of zeroing it per layer
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation On SM100/SM103 (B200/B300), DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash can run attention through FlashMLA MegaAttention (`--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega`, FP8 KV cache), whose kernels take the query packed as `(tokens, 32, padded_heads, 16)` with the heads padded to 64. With attention TP > 1 each GPU holds fewer heads (16 of 64 at TP4), and `pack_query` rebuilt the packed tensor in each of the 40 attention layers: a zero-fill of the whole padded tensor, three quarters of it padding at TP4, then a copy of the real heads. This PR gives the MegaAttention backend one packed-query buffer, zeroed once when it is first used and never reallocated. Each layer writes only its real heads into a row slice of it, and nothing writes the padding, so it stays zero. Its size is fixed at startup from the largest forward the server bounds there: a prefill chunk, a CUDA-graph bucket, or a decode or verify batch. Eager forwards, captured CUDA graphs and the decoder tail graphs (CUDA graphs of the late layers that eager prefill chunks replay) pack into this one buffer, so its address never changes. A forward with more rows, such as a long prompt with chunked prefill disabled, packs into fresh zeros as on main and leaves the buffer as it is. The packed values are bitwise identical and no kernel changes. On current main, MegaAttention is the default in PD prefill and decode servers and in aggregated servers without attention TP; aggregated servers with attention TP > 1 default to `flashmla` since #46263 and use this path with `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega`. **Impact** - **Accuracy:

title: [Fix] Mamba slot admission for the classic hybrid pool: gate the scheduler, never assert the engine
summary: ## Description **Symptom**: on hybrid-SSM models (Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.8 GDN family) with the classic `HybridReqToTokenPool` (i.e. **without** `--enable-unified-memory`), two concurrent long requests deterministically crash the scheduler: ``` AssertionError: Can not alloc mamba cache .../unified_cache/components/mamba.py:509: _alloc_mamba_slot ``` Repro on a 27B GDN model, `--max-mamba-cache-size 10` (auto-sized): fire two ~90K-token requests concurrently → dead. Two ~30K requests with `mamba_track_interval=64` → also dead. The assert kills every in-flight request on the engine; nothing else dies gracefully. **Root cause**: the scheduler *does* have a mamba-slot admission ledger (`PrefillAdder.rem_mamba_slots`, `schedule_policy.py`), but it is gated on `isinstance(token_to_kv_pool_allocator, UnifiedMamba*Allocator)` — it only fires for the **unified memory pool**. With the classic hybrid pool, `mamba_allocator` is a separate free-list the ledger never sees, so admission checks nothing. Meanwhile each new mamba request really costs **3 slots** (`MAMBA_STATE_PER_REQ_PREFIX_CACHE`: 2 ping-pong + 1 running — the constant `alloc_req_slots` reserves with), plus one donated checkpoint per cache boundary. Two long requests ≈ 10+ slot demand against a 10-slot pool; the ledger admits both; the first donation with no evictable slot left asserts. The gap is even acknowledged in-place: the FIXME in `_mamba_gap_budget_for_req` says *"if over-admission crashes under pressure, make this more conservative (e.g. multiply by `MAMBA_STATE_PER_REQ_PREFIX_CACHE`)"* — this PR does exactly that, for

title: [Fix] minicpm5: Recover malformed parameter boundaries
summary: ## Motivation When a complete MiniCPM5 function block omits a parameter's `</param>`, the XML fallback can consume the next parameter as part of the previous value or drop a required argument. Under concurrent load, requests recompute prefixes that were already in L3, and `storage_prefetch_unfulfilled_tokens_total{reason="cache_admission_shortfall"}` increases. On GLM-5.3-Flash, 32 requests with 6,100 input tokens each hit 188,416 cached tokens when sent serially. At concurrency 16, the same requests hit 64,768 cached tokens, while the rank-0 shortfall counter increased by 88,320 tokens. This counter includes repeated prefetch attempts, so it is not a count of unique recomputed tokens. The suspected cause is a lifetime gap: L3 completion inserts host pages without retaining an eviction reference until admission, allowing another prefetch to evict them before load-back. Related: [#47481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/47481) reports a hit-rate drop under L2/L3 pressure. title: [Fix] metrics: Handle process CPU clock resets after restore
summary: ## Motivation After CRIU restore, the process CPU clock can be below the scheduler's saved accounting baseline. The resulting negative delta causes the Prometheus counter to raise `ValueError`, terminating the restored scheduler when metrics are enabled. Without a time namespace, restoring on a host with less uptime also moves the monotonic clock backwards. Scheduler time accounting then stalls until the clock catches up, and stage metrics accumulate negative wall time that crashes the same way when drained. ## Modifications - Count the restored CPU clock reading as CPU time since restore instead of a negative delta, so the counter never decrements. - Flush buffered idle and stage totals before rebasing scheduler time accounting when the monotonic clock moves below the last sample. - Preserve the active stage and reset the forward-occupancy window. - Drop backwards spans in `SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder` so drained totals stay non-negative. title: [Fix] multimodal: Compact CPU tensor views before inline transport
summary:
## Motivation Large multi-image requests can block the tokenizer event loop while preparing a message for the scheduler when multimodal features travel inline as CPU tensors (`nnodes > 1`, or fallback after SHM allocation fails). `get_new_expanded_mm_items()` splits a batched feature tensor into per-image views. A view can be contiguous while still retaining the entire batch's storage. PyTorch's pickle reducer serializes that storage for each distinct view, so the payload grows quadratically with the number of images. For 96 images at 1024 x 1024, the processed float32 features occupy 2.25 GiB in total. Each image view contains 24 MiB of useful data but references the same 2.25 GiB storage. Pickling one view produces about 2.25 GiB; serializing all 96 would contribute about 216 GiB of storage data. In the serving reproduction, `send_pyobj()` did not return before tokenizer RSS reached the 128 GiB experiment limit, and `/model_info` timed out. The 216 GiB figure is a storage-size estimate, not a completed wire transfer. The measured 8-image request expands 192 MiB of features into a 1.50 GiB ZMQ message. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Image preprocessing
96 images: one 2.25 GiB CPU storage"] --> B["Split into 96 Tensor views
24 MiB logical data each
Each still references the full 2.25 GiB storage"] B --> C{"Feature transport"} C -->|"SHM succeeds"| D["Copy each image's valid bytes into SHM
ZMQ carries SHM descriptors"] D --> S["Scheduler and TP ranks
obtain image features"] C -->|"CPU inline: multiple nodes or SHM fallback"| E{"At the send boundary"} E -->|"B

title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: Capture decoder-tail graphs at startup, never on a step a DP rank skips
summary: ## Motivation A DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill server can hang on its first busy prefill steps after startup. This happens with DP attention (attention TP 1), `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, and decoder SWA bounded replay. Every DP rank stops. After 300 s, DeepGEMM's MegaMoE grid-sync timeout traps and the GPUs report Xid 43. A restart doesn't help: the next cold start can hang the same way. How it happens: 1. With MegaMoE and no DP gather in the graph, `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` lets each DP rank replay the prefill-graph bucket of its own token count. 2. The decoder replay tail (#45059, #45107) takes one of two forms, depending on the bucket: - In buckets of at least `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MIN_PREFILL_TOKENS` (2048), it runs as an eager break, `_tail_layers_in_prefill_graph`. The break replays row-bucket graphs of its own. - In smaller buckets, the tail layers, MegaMoE included, are recorded inline in the prefill graph. 3. The break captures a missing row-bucket graph on first use. `RowBucketGraphRunner._record` calls `tp_group.barrier()` before it captures. 4. Take a step where one rank's bucket is at least 2048 and another's is below 2048: - The first rank waits in the gloo barrier. - The second rank has already launched MegaMoE and waits in its grid sync for the first. - Neither can move. #45881 guards one variant of this: an idle rank, which never reaches the break. title: [Fix] modelopt: Defer serialized CUTLASS NVFP4 scale layouts until loading
summary: Reopened from #40682, which was closed by mistake on 22 September; its review history is still there. Serialized CUTLASS NVFP4 models swizzle uninitialized expert scales during construction, then rebuild those layouts after loading. Those duplicate buffers can make a checkpoint fail before its weights are read. MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL on TP2/EP2 RTX PRO 6000 reaches the 95 GiB device limit during audio-encoder construction; the redundant MoE scale buffers account for 8.8125 GiB per rank. Defer the derived layouts for serialized CUTLASS checkpoints, as the TRTLLM and MegaMoE paths already do. The normal post-load code creates and aliases the populated scales. The online quantization allocation path stays intact. Validation: five remote CPU tests cover cold allocation, online initialization, post-load values, reloads, and non-gated padding. With this change, the same complete MiMo NVFP4 artifact loads and serves on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards, including sampled bring-up, cached conversation and bounded-context checks. No weight or activation precision is changed. The separate MiMo packed-module mapping fix used by that mixed checkpoint is #42450. Duplicate preflight on 2026-09-22 applies cleanly to upstream 264da633191d. Inspected #38216: it changes FP4 dispatch and per-token all-gather scales, not construction-time derived buffers. Rebased onto upstream `f2385314b2b3` on 2026-10-04. title: [Fix] hicache: Budget deduplicated host pools by physical ownership
summary: ## Motivation With the MLA/DSA host dedup integration in #44536, only the source rank allocates the target host payload. The per-rank split introduced by #35540 still gives that source only 1/8 of the usable host memory on TP8, rejecting valid explicit cache sizes and unnecessarily reducing the automatically selected ratio. **Dependency:** this draft is stacked on #44536 at `261559ba6b6d2d58ef65a19173ddd565e5dd052e`. The fix is the final commit, `5dd2784eb5eb0e54b49e1294f529242364b22fa7` ([fix-only diff](https://github.com/HZY-Wade/sglang/compare/261559ba6b6d2d58ef65a19173ddd565e5dd052e...5dd2784eb5eb0e54b49e1294f529242364b22fa7)). The preceding integration commit is unchanged. Merge the dependency first; this PR must then be rebased if that dependency is squash-merged. ## Modifications - Use the same dedup eligibility gate for sizing and pool construction. - Before constructing pools, gather each rank's physical host-mirror byte estimate and available headroom. Distribute each host's budget by those estimates, using the minimum headroom reported by its co-located ranks. The collective occurs once before pool construction, where different PP pool counts cannot change its ordering. - Count target MLA/DSA payload only on source ranks while retaining draft sidecars on every rank. Multiple dedup groups and PP stages share their host budget; hosts containing only dummy peers need no target payload budget. - Apply the resulting budget scope to both explicit sizes and automatic sizing. MLA KV, DSA indexer and draft allocations book the same snapshot. Keep the cgroup limit, 10 GiB

title: feat(jit): support native MUSA compilation
summary: ## Overview This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path. The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and `--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries. HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback. MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly; SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache fingerprints the selected compiler path and version. Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through `stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on [yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132), currently a fork Draft. JIT compilation remains in SGLang. title: [Feat] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Add full mono decode
summary: ## What this does #43497 added the front mono kernel, K1, for DeepSeek-V4.1 decode on MI355X. It runs on 30 of the 40 backbone layers. Attention still runs through the normal SGLang kernels, followed by a separate fused FFN launch. This PR completes the path: 1. K1 runs on all 40 backbone layers. 2. The existing sparse-attention indexer runs between K1 and K2 on the layers that need it. 3. K2 runs attention, the output projections, and the FFN in one kernel. The path is opt-in with `SGLANG_ROCM_MONO_K2=1`, which also requires the existing mono decode and K1 flags. It handles decode and DSpark target-verify steps with 48 rows or fewer. Larger steps and draft layers stay on the normal path. ## Why Without K2, SGLang only uses the front half of the mono path. It returns to the normal attention kernels and then launches the FFN kernel separately. K2 removes those launches from the decode path and keeps the work inside the fused kernel. ## Performance The baseline is the #43497 image at `d4708ad`: K1 on 30 layers, normal attention, and the separate FFN launch. The PR image has K1 and K2 on all 40 layers. title: [Bugfix] Link JIT modules against the pip CUDA runtime
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation SGLang's TVM-FFI JIT path can link against the wrong CUDA runtime when CUDA is provided by NVIDIA's pip packages. In the failing layout, TVM-FFI resolved `CUDA_HOME` to the pip CUDA package, but searched `CUDA_HOME/lib64` while that package exposed only a versioned `libcudart.so.13` under `CUDA_HOME/lib`. The linker then fell through to the system CUDA installation and produced a JIT module with a `libcudart.so.11.0` dependency. Loading that module in a CUDA 13 process caused `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` in the activation kernel. This issue was discovered independently while validating an unrelated inference report. ## Modifications - Detect a versioned-only CUDA runtime layout before invoking TVM-FFI. - Create a cache-local compatibility `CUDA_HOME` that exposes the selected runtime as `lib64/libcudart.so`, without modifying the CUDA installation. - Add the selected runtime identity to the JIT build-directory key so an existing module linked against another runtime is not reused. - Preserve standard CUDA layouts and the existing ROCm/Windows behavior. - Add CPU unit coverage for both the versioned pip layout and the standard `lib64/libcudart.so` layout. ## Accuracy Tests Validation was run on a node with 2x RTX 3090 (SM 8.6), the pip CUDA 13 runtime, NVCC 13.0.88, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, and TVM-FF

title: perf: Remove redundant D2D copy in layer-split broadcast
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> In disaggregated prefill with DSA cache layer split, _broadcast_tensor_from_owner performs a full D2D copy from kv_buffer[local_idx] to remote_kv_buffer on the owner rank before NCCL broadcast. This copy is unnecessary — NCCL broadcast allows each rank to use a different send/recv buffer address as long as numel, dtype, and device match. The copy is serial with the broadcast, delaying its start. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> All changes in python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py: 1. _broadcast_tensor_from_owner: Owner broadcasts src_tensor (kv_buffer[local_idx]) directly instead of copying to remote_kv_buffer first. Non-owner still receives into remote_kv_buffer as before. 2. _get_broadcastable_kv_buffer: Owner returns kv_buffer[local_idx] instead of remote_kv_buffer. summary: ## Motivation gpt-oss emits a preamble before calling a tool: an assistant message on the `commentary` channel with no recipient. `/v1/responses` crashes on it. `parse_output_message` assumes every commentary message is a tool call: ```python elif message.channel == "commentary": if message.recipient.startswith("functions."): # recipient is None ``` ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith' ``` Nothing filters this — `_make_response_output_items_with_harmony` runs `parse_output_message` over every generated message, and that call is outside `responses_full_generator`'s try/except. For non-streaming requests it lands in the catch-all in `create_responses`, which defaults to 400 `invalid_request_error`, so the client gets told its own request was bad: ```json {"error": {"message": "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'", "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": 400}} ``` That's probably why nobody's reported it — it looks like a client-side mistake. Chat Completions already handles this fine. `harmony_parser` treats `commentary` as user-visible content, and `test_parse_commentary_then_final` asserts it comes out as a `"normal"` event rather than reasoning. summary: ## Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at [https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions). Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ## Motivation ### Use case Multi-tenant serving where prefix caching is per-tenant and opt-in: - Tenants that opt in send their own `cache_salt`, so only they can hit their KV. - Tenants that opt out must leave nothing reusable behind. Today the only supported way is a random `cache_salt` per request. Why a tenant opts out: - Contracts and regulations (GDPR, sector rules for health, finance, public sector) often require that prompt content not be retained beyond the request. A prefix cache entry is a derived copy of the prompt. Cached KV can be used to recover the prompt tokens, so "not stored" has to mean "not inserted", not "inserted under a key nobody else knows". - Shared prefix caches leak prompt content through timing: a hit is measurably faster than a miss. `cache_salt` closes the cross-tenant case, but a tenant with strict threat models does not want its prompts in any shared structure at all, including the host tier of HiCache. A random salt isolates the KV but does not stop the insert. Every opt-out request still puts a full-length, never-hittable branch into the radix tree: 1. It occupies pool memory as evictable garbage until LRU reaches it, displacing opt-in tenants' real prefixes and lowering their hit rate. 2. title: [Feature] Enforce attention metadata consistency after post-plan padding
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary SGLang can change a `ForwardBatch`'s shape after attention metadata has already been planned: ```text plan metadata for shape R -> mark metadata ready -> DP / attention-TP padding changes the batch to shape M -> skip metadata initialization -> run the backend ``` Here, `R` is the planned query-token count and `M >= R` is the final physical count. This is not automatically incorrect: a backend may safely ignore rows `[R:M)` or may pad its own metadata. The generic risk is that SGLang does not enforce either behavior. A backend can receive a larger query than the metadata plan covers. ## Current behavior The eager speculative draft path plans metadata before `ModelRunner` and marks it ready ([source](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/52fecfdf0908dca24f4c6799ff5967125cc4110e/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_common.py#L194-L208)): ```python if not batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and not can_run_decode_cuda_graph: draft_model_runner.attn_backend.init_forward_metadata(forward_batch) forward_batch.mark_forward_metadata_ready() ``` `ModelRunner` applies eager DP / MLP-sync padding afterward ([source](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/52fecfdf0908dca24f4c6799ff5967125cc4110e/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L1784-L1798)): ```python self._prepare_eager_forward_batch(forward_batch

title: [Feature] Expose multimodal preprocessing latency metrics (media download / load / processor) in Prometheus
summary: ### Motivation In the default (co-located) deployment, all multimodal input handling — downloading media from URLs, base64/PIL/video/audio decoding, and the HF processor call — happens in the tokenizer manager / HTTP server process **before** the request ever reaches the scheduler. Today this time is completely invisible in Prometheus: - Scheduler metrics (`sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds`, `sglang:e2e_request_latency_seconds`, queue stats, etc.) only start counting after tokenization + mm processing, so mm preprocessing time is silently absorbed into what looks like queueing overhead / TTFT. - The only mm-related latency metrics are `sglang:encoder_*` (e.g. `sglang:encoder_preprocess_seconds`), which cover only the **disaggregated encoder service**, not the standard tokenizer-manager path (`BaseMultimodalProcessor._load_single_item` / `load_mm_data` / `process_mm_data`). As a result, when a multimodal request is slow, operators cannot tell whether the time went to (a) network download of media, (b) CPU-bound media decode (PIL/video frames/audio), or (c) the HF processor. In production we have hit exactly this: truncated/slow media downloads from object storage, and heavy video frame sampling, both surface only as "slow requests" with no per-stage breakdown. ### Proposed feature Record Prometheus metrics in the tokenizer manager process (multiprocess mode already aggregates them into `/metrics`), gated on `--enable-metrics`: - `sglang:mm_media_download_seconds{modality}` — HTTP(S) media fetch latency per item - `sglang:mm_media_download_bytes{modality}` — downloaded size

title: supports_fp8() always True; _apply_fallback_scaled_mm still calls torch._scaled_mm (no escape on SM<89)
summary: ## Summary `CudaPlatform.supports_fp8()` always returns **`True`**, while `cutlass_fp8_supported()` is correctly **False** on GPUs without FP8 tensor cores (e.g. Turing sm_75). `torch._scaled_mm` requires CC ≥ 8.9 / 9.0. title: HYV4 (Hunyuan-V4) with an all-to-all MoE backend silently computes 1 token in attn_tp_size

No error is raised, the server is healthy, and throughput is *higher* than the correct arm, so nothing short of a logprob comparison catches it. `--moe-a2a-backend deepep` is one of the toggles shipped in the docs Playground for this model (`docs/src/snippets/configs/tencent/hy4-preview.jsx:187`). ### Why `require_attn_tp_gather()` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:3879`) returns True on "an a2a backend is set" alone (or `moe_dense_tp_size is not None`), so the scheduler derives `num_token_non_padded` as this attn-TP rank's *sequence shard* (`forward_batch_info.py:259`, `tokens_per_rank = num_tokens_per_dp // attn_tp_size`). That contract holds for models whose `LayerCommunicator` hands the MoE the scattered shard. `models/hunyuan_v4.py` has no `LayerCommunicator` at all: it uses `hc_attn_layer`/`hc_mlp_layer`, its attention TP is head-parallel only (`hunyuan_v4.py:358-359`, `:383-384`) with no sequence scatter, and it calls `self.mlp(hidden_states, forward_batch)` on the **full padded width** on every rank (`:606-607`). `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_deepep` then passes that shard-local `num_token_non_padded` to `self.topk()` for a full-width batch, and every row at or past it gets `topk_ids = -1`, i.e. contributes nothing. ### Evidence Measured on 8x B300, `--tp 8 --ep 8`, a 5-token prompt padded to 8, so `tokens_per_rank == 1`

summary: Two CI-only additions to the exit ledger, gated on `SGLANG_ENABLE_RUNNING_REQS_CHECK` (on in CI, off in production). title: [Fix] torch_native_llama: load checkpoint tensors and KV-cache scales
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48917. Fixes #49202. With the default load format, `TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM.load_weights` collected the parameters of the root module only, so `TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM` and `TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM` loaded no checkpoint tensor and kept their initial values, with no error. Their attention was also built without `quant_config` and the loader had no rule for KV-cache scale names, so a checkpoint's FP8 KV-cache scales could not load even then. Phi-3 checkpoints store fused `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` tensors, which the TorchNative weight loaders could not take. Once tensors load, a checkpoint that stores its linear layers quantized is misread instead (#49202): the TorchNative classes build plain `torch.nn.Linear` layers (their quantization goes through torchao after loading), so FP8 or packed codes load into the BF16 weights as numbers and `weight_scale` / `input_scale` are skipped. Such a checkpoint is now refused at load. ## Modifications - `load_weights` loads into the whole model (`recurse=True`); `load_weights_to_module` keeps `recurse=False` for `LayeredModelLoader`. - `LlamaAttention` passes `quant_config` (and its prefix) to `RadixAttention`. - `load_weights_to_module` maps KV-cache scale names with `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` before the q/k/v_proj -> qkv_proj rename, as `llama.py` does. It maps them against the scale parameters of the whole model, because `LayeredModelLoader` fills one submodule at a time. - `qkv_proj_weight_loader` and `gate_up_proj_weight_loader` take a fused tensor without a shard id and split it into its parts, as

On a PCIe-only node this exit is on the prefill critical path: with Nsight Systems I measured communication at about half of prefill GPU time on 4x H200 NVL (no NVLink), with no overlap. ## Modifications - Remove `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` and `Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP` from `_AR_ARCHITECTURES`, so `auto` resolves to the framework default `rs+rsv`. - Update the two cases in `test_model_overrides.py::TestBoundaryReductionDefaults` that pinned the old default. `--boundary-reduction ar` keeps the old behaviour. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, 4x H200 NVL (PCIe, same NUMA node), `--tp 4 --ep-size 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention`, nightly `858073e4` with #48824 applied so the prefill graph can stay on. | | `ar` | `rs` | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (200 questions, 32 threads) | 97.5% | 96.5% | | Questions right in only one arm | 2 | 0 (exact McNemar p = 0.5) | | Same config, two passes, prompt logprobs | identical | identical | | `ar` vs `rs` prompt logprobs, 6198 token

title: [Fix] scheduler: Finish rejected requests and offloaded releases through the request retirer
summary: Several paths ended a request without `RequestRetirer`, so they skipped what the retirer releases. They now all go through it. - **Requests rejected before they are queued** finish through `RequestRetirer.retire_unadmitted`, which already served the PD unadmitted reject as `Scheduler.retire_unadmitted_request` and now lives in the retirer (it takes `stream_output`): - the PD decode door's KV-capacity reject (`DecodePreallocQueue._check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity`) and the PD prefill one (`PrefillBootstrapQueue._check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity`); - the sampling-mask, beam and missing-bootstrap-room rejects in `handle_generate_request`; - the EPD encoder failure reported by the request receiver, which now takes the `RequestRetirer` and is built after it. title: [AMD] Fused qk rmsnorm bf16 for amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm targets with a BF16 DeepSeek model, the MLA QK layernorm path falls through to the PyTorch sequential fallback instead of using aiter's fused kernel. The BF16 fused branch in forward_mla.py was gated by _use_aiter and not _use_aiter_gfx95, which correctly excludes gfx950 from the FP8/MXFP4 quantized paths but incorrectly also excludes it from the BF16 fused path. This PR fixes the condition so the fused BF16 kernel is used on all AITER-enabled ROCm targets (gfx942, gfx950). ## Technical Details The condition in forward_mla.py is changed from _use_aiter and not _use_aiter_gfx95 to elif _use_aiter:, making the fused layernorm branch fire on all AITER-enabled targets when model weights are not in a quantized format (FP8/MXFP4). alt_stream is always None on ROCm/HIP, so the fused path is always reachable on those targets. The fused op is fused_qk_rmsnorm from aiter.ops.fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant, backed by csrc/kernels/fused_qk_norm.cu. This kernel already supports both fp16 and bf16 natively via a clean 2D-grid design (Q and K blocks run in parallel on separate CUs) — no new aiter kernel is required. ## Accuracy Tests Before the change: GSM8K 0.928 After the change: GSM8K 0.935 ## Speed Tests and Profiling In terms of `Decode batch ... gen throughput (token/s)`: Before the change 90.12; after the change 90.84, for a large configuration ISL/OSL=128000/64000. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests

title: [Rust server] Tokenization runs on a single thread by default and becomes the tail-latency bottleneck for long prompts
summary: ### Summary With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, every request is tokenized on one thread, `tokenizer-0`, because `--tokenizer-worker-num` defaults to 1 and `spawn_pool("tokenizer", ...)` in `rust/sglang-server/src/utils/runtime.rs` takes that value as is. With long multi-turn prompts, that thread saturates. Requests then queue in front of the scheduler, and the Rust frontend's tail latency ends up worse than the Python frontend's. The Python frontend spreads the same work over a thread pool. Setting `--tokenizer-worker-num 4` removes the bottleneck. title: [Fix] mamba: Preserve completed checkpoints across overlap gaps
summary: ## Motivation Non-lazy `extra_buffer` checkpointing can overwrite a completed Mamba/KDA checkpoint after a prefill gap under overlap scheduling. The next decode destination normally rotates in anticipation of a boundary. When that rotation is missed, processing the completed boundary records its slot and length but can leave the next write destination pointing at the same slot. A later boundary then overwrites the state while cache insertion still uses the earlier length. On GLM-5.3-Flash, this produced a checkpoint tagged as length 11520 whose contents were actually the state at 11776, causing large logprob errors on prefix-cache hits. Read-only state snapshots confirmed this identity on all eight ranks: the initial 11520 checkpoint was correct, but the later restored checkpoint matched the 11776 state instead. ## Modifications - After processing a completed non-lazy checkpoint, set the next destination to the other slot through `TrackingAdvance(next_position=...)`. Preserve the completed and previous checkpoint metadata. - Derive that destination from the completed batch's slot snapshot, so an already-performed anticipatory rotation is not reversed. Do this after the existing prefix-cache update, which also handles the zero-lookahead path. - Extend the existing CPU regression suite with six deterministic cases: a missed anticipatory rotation, an already-rotated overlap case, and zero lookahead, each in both slot directions. The test runs the real result handler and write/keep-slot selection, then models a later device write and checks that the completed checkpoint survive

title: [Fix] [NPU] attention: Run page_size<16 models on the reference attention path
summary: # [Fix] [NPU] attention: Run `page_size < 16` models on the reference attention path ## Motivation Two Ascend 950 (A5) failure modes abort inside a fused op or a kernel assert for models that do not use a standard KV page granularity. Both surface as an opaque `161001` / `EZ1009` at the first decode step instead of as an unsupported-configuration check. 1. **Paged attention needs `block_size` in `[16, 512]`, as a multiple of 16.** A caller that keeps `page_size=1` (e.g. a frame-level KV cache for a streaming speech tower) gets `Parameter block_size of FusedInferAttentionScore has incorrect value 1`. The file already carries torch-reference branches for the shapes the fused op cannot serve — they were just unreachable by page size. 2. **`chunk_gated_delta_rule` asserts a dtype match.** The kernel checks `chunk_state.dtype == initial_state.dtype`, but `chunk_state` is allocated from `k` (model dtype) while the recurrent state is fp32: `RuntimeError: chunk_state dtype must match initial_state`. ## Modifications - `hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py` - derive `use_native_sdpa` from the page size (`page_size % 16 != 0 or not 16 <= page_size <= 512`), next to the existing Gemma2 special case that sets the same flag; - add the flag to the decode branch that selects the fused op, so those page sizes reach the torch-reference branch that was already there; - `forward_decode_graph` defers to eager `forward_decode` in that case, because the reference attention reads shapes on the host, which graph capture forbids. - `hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_gdn_backend.py`

title: Post-hoc Req.finished_len mutation desyncs pool accounting — invariant checker fires with negative residue (undocumented contract)
summary: # post-hoc `Req.finished_len` mutation desyncs pool accounting (invariant checker fires with negative residue) (2026-10-15, 49 min outage) on a 4× DGX Spark (GB10/SM120) TP4 deployment of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark speculative decoding. ## Summary `Req.finished_len` has an implicit contract: it may only be set **inside** `update_finish_state`'s own flow (stop-string/regex via `_locate_str_stop_finished_len`, `_cap_finished_len_at_max_new_tokens`). Engine-side consumers correctly honor it (e.g. `BatchResultProcessor._visible_output_len`, speculative sampling-mask row drops "past finished_len, as output_ids is trimmed there"). But nothing prevents an extension from shrinking `finished_len` **after** the step's bookkeeping has run on the longer length. title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Share compressed-key reads across the four verify rows of a request on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at concurrency 16 spends 2.0 ms of each decode step in the QSA indexer's decode scoring (`tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode`). With MTP (4 draft tokens), the four verify rows of a request read the same compressed keys four times, once per row. On ROCm, each row also pads its 4 indexer heads to the 16 columns MFMA needs, so three quarters of each MFMA is zero padding. AgentX contexts are long (about 106k tokens per request), so each row scores about 26k compressed keys per layer. #46631 adds a TileLang kernel that scores the four verify rows of a request from one key load, but enables it on SM107 only. On gfx950, 4 rows × 4 heads fill the 16-wide MFMA exactly, so the same kernel also removes the head padding. This PR enables the grouped kernel on gfx950 and launches it over the page table on ROCm. The logits are bit-identical to the per-row kernel. At 64 verify rows and 26k keys, the kernel goes from 220.3 µs (main) to 37.9 µs, and from 63.3 µs to 37.9 µs against #48649, which speeds up the per-row kernel on ROCm. Depends on #46631, and edits its grouped kernel (launch only). Only the last two commits are new; the branch also merges `main`. I will merge `main` again once #46631 lands. Overlap with #48649: both PRs change `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode` on ROCm, so they conflict in text. They are complementary in behavior: #48649 speeds up every decode row, and this PR handles MTP verify rows. #48649 makes the indexer project Q padded to 16 heads; this PR accepts that layout, so the grouped path stays on when both land. See the comment below. ## Motivation On a PD decode server, a request within `--num-reserved-decode-tokens` (default 512) of the decode KV pool size passes every intake check and then never fits, even when the pool is empty. The decode server stalls until the requests time out or are aborted. This case does not need a long prompt: a 64-token prompt that has generated close to its limit is enough. summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #48014 * #48013 * #48012 * #48011 * #48010 * #48009 * __->__ #48008 * #48007 * #48006 * #48852 ## Motivation Under `--enable-unified-memory`, the bands of the shared KV arena reuse freed pages and move live pages (compaction of an end, a float making room for its neighbour) while forwards and host copies may still read or write them. title: [Perf] mem_cache: Defer reuse of freed unified pages instead of waiting on every free
summary: This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom): * #48014 * #48013 * #48012 * #48011 * #48010 * #48009 * #48008 * #48007 * #48006 * __->__ #48852 ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory` and the overlap scheduler, the forward launched before a result is processed (N+1) can still use the pages of a request that this result ends. It reads them through its prepared page table, and it writes the request's next slot. A unified pool writes a freed page from the schedule stream when it hands the page out (zeroing) or compacts into it. The schedule stream is not ordered after N+1. On `main` this is handled by #48496 (which replaced #48450's wait on every lazy free). Freed physical pages are held, keyed by a forward event, and settled once that event has fired (`_settle_freed` reads `event.query()`). A take that needs them orders its writers after the forward through a reuse fence; zeroing moves to the forward stream; PD publication waits on reuse fences. Which pages are free therefore depends on rank-local event timing, so TP ranks can choose different pages. This PR replaces that mechanism. It frees at once and delays only the physical reuse, deciding from logical progress only: - The ids, the virtual-to-physical entries and the request rows are released immediately. The scheduler's write-after-read barrier (`Scheduler._apply_war_barrier`) already orders these schedule-stream writes after N+1's shared reads. - The freed physical pages stay pending until N+1's result is processed. They count as free in every capacity check. A take that needs them before then settles them first: i

title: [Fix] multimodal: Clear the embedding cache in Scheduler.flush_cache
summary: Clears the multimodal embedding cache when the scheduler flushes its caches. Before this, a server whose weights were updated kept answering an image it had seen before with the embeddings of the old vision encoder. #36468 by @yuanlehome proposed the same change first. This pull request adds a regression test in the existing flush test file and checks the fix on nine models (images, video and audio) against fresh servers, bitwise. Happy to work with the author on either pull request, or for the maintainers to merge whichever they prefer. ## Motivation The scheduler keeps the vision encoder's output for an image or a video in `mm_schedule.embedding_cache`, keyed by a hash of the input. `Scheduler.flush_cache()` resets the radix cache, the KV pools and the grammar cache, but not this cache, and nothing else clears it. `update_weights_from_disk`, `update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_distributed` and `update_weights_from_ipc` all end in `flush_cache()`. So do `/flush_cache` and `release_memory_occupation` when it releases the KV cache. After a weight update the radix cache is empty, but an image the server has seen before still gets the old encoder's embeddings, and the model answers it as if the vision weights had not changed. A new image already gets the new ones. The cache is on by default for most VLMs (`SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB`, 100 MiB). Qwen3-VL on large Hopper GPUs and `--rl-on-policy-target` turn it off unless the variable is set. The memory is not returned either: `flush_cache()` empties the allocator cache while the cached tensors are still referenced.

summary: # [Feat] paged-experts: keep experts on disk so later starts skip loading them ## Motivation This PR shortens the start of Paged Experts and lays the groundwork for models whose experts do not fit in RAM. On an RTX 5070 Ti with 62 GB of RAM, `load_model` takes 34 s for Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, 53 s for Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 and 121 s for Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4 (with #48082). This PR keeps the result on disk. With `--paged-experts-enable-disk`, the first start writes each paged layer's experts to a file in the host store's layout, and later starts read the files back with direct I/O instead of loading and repacking every expert again. title: [Feature] Share a prompt's KV among requests admitted in the same prefill batch
summary: ### Motivation Requests that share a prompt and are admitted in one prefill batch each compute the whole prompt: the radix cache inserts a request's KV only after its prefill result is processed (`checkpoint_kv_cache` in `process_batch_result_prefill`), so `PrefillAdder` matches the second and later requests against a tree that does not have the first request's prompt yet. This is the common case for RL rollouts (GRPO-style groups: N samples of one prompt, sent as N requests so each has its own session / routing), and for any client that fans out samples of one prompt as separate requests. `lpm`'s in-batch prefix caching (`_compute_prefix_matches`) only moves the duplicates to the tail of the waiting queue; when the prefill budget fits them they still join the same batch. It is also unavailable with priority scheduling, which only allows `fcfs` / `lof`. SGLang's own parallel sampling (`n > 1`) works around this in `TokenizerManager` by sending a `max_new_tokens=0` request per prompt and waiting for it before sending the n samples. For comparison, vLLM registers a request's to-be-computed full blocks in its prefix cache when it allocates them at scheduling time (`KVCacheManager.allocate_slots` -> `coordinator.cache_blocks(request, num_computed + num_new)`), so a later request in the same step hits blocks that the earlier one writes in the same forward (each layer writes KV before its attention reads it). title: [Fix] mamba: Keep the decode-track ping-pong parity under overlap interleavings
summary: ## Motivation With `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` and the overlap scheduler, a hybrid (GDN / Mamba) request can hand the radix tree a decode checkpoint that holds the wrong state. A later turn that hits it restores the state at `end` under the label `end - interval`, and every token it decodes is conditioned on that wrong state. Nothing errors; outputs are silently off. We found it through a bitwise rollout-vs-trainer log-prob check on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B multi-turn RL (page size 128, `--mamba-track-interval 128`). In each affected case the previous turn ended exactly on a 128-token boundary, and the next turn hit the cache at `end - 128`. The decode-track ping-pong index `mamba_next_track_idx` is toggled from two views of one boundary step `s`: - at the result of step `s - 1`, when step `s` was already launched (lookahead 1), via `mamba_track_mask_next_cpu`; - at the result of step `s`, when nothing was launched since (lookahead 0), via `mamba_track_mask_cpu`. Lookahead is 1 only when the next batch the overlap loop launched was the decode batch. So a non-decode batch (a prefill, or an idle step) right after step `s` gives both views, a double flip. One right after step `s - 1` gives neither, so no flip happens. Either way the next boundary forward writes the slot that holds the latest checkpoint. While the request keeps decoding, that boundary's own result relabels the slot, so nothing goes wrong. summary: ## Motivation Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44810. A DeepSeek-V4 BF16 checkpoint carries no `quantization_config`. title: [Fix] unquant: Keep BF16 low-M autotune calls bias-free so TP ranks stay in sync

title: [Perf] disaggregation: Send replicated KV heads from one prefill rank
summary: ## Motivation When a model has fewer KV heads than the prefill attention TP size, several prefill ranks hold an identical copy of the same head. In the Mooncake heterogeneous-TP path every one of those ranks writes its copy into the same decode buffer. With one KV head and prefill attention TP8 → decode TP1, each decode rank receives 8x the logical KV bytes. The slice path also posts one RDMA descriptor per token slot, so long prompts pay for both the duplicate writes and the descriptor count. ## Modifications - `should_send_kv_replica` in `disaggregation/common/utils.py` elects one writer inside each group of prefill ranks that map to the same decode rank and hold the same head. - The election hashes the shared bootstrap room with BLAKE2b, so every chunk and every PP stage agrees on the writer. - The hash spreads load across replicas. Raw room bits can correlate with DP routing, so they are not used directly. - Mooncake slice path (`send_kvcache_slice`): non-elected ranks skip the write. - Mooncake staging path: - Prefill writer offsets, decode staging allocation and decode scatter all use one compact slot per distinct head: `staging_writer_ranks` / `staging_writer_slot`, and `compute_staging_layout(..., deduplicate=)`. - A single per-backend switch, `BaseKVManager.deduplicate_kv_staging`, keeps the three in agreement. Mooncake enables it; NIXL keeps the current layout. - Whole-page fast path (`_can_send_whole_kv_pages`): when both sides hold at most one KV head per rank, page byte layouts match and unified memory is off, the elected rank sends whole pages with `send_kvcac

title: [Fix] multimodal: Decode images on CPU when the PIL image processor is used
summary: ## Motivation When the server runs with `--disable-fast-image-processor` or `--image-processor-backend pil`, image preprocessing happens on the CPU. However, `BaseMultimodalProcessor.gpu_image_decode` still defaults to `True`, so on a CUDA host `load_image()` decodes every JPEG with nvJPEG (`torchvision.io.decode_jpeg(..., device="cuda")`) inside the tokenizer process. The slow image processor works on host arrays, so the decoded tensor is copied straight back to the CPU afterward. In this mode, the GPU decode adds cost without doing anything useful. The first JPEG creates a CUDA context in the tokenizer process, and that context stays alive for as long as the process runs. On an RTX 5090, `nvidia-smi` showed the tokenizer process using 596 MiB next to the scheduler. On a single GPU with little free memory, that amount can decide whether a feature fits at all. In my case, it was the difference that let MTP speculative decoding fit at 262k context. The first image request after startup also has to wait for the lazy torchvision load (which a code comment estimates at about 1 s) and for the CUDA context to be created. The flag is read in two different places. `_load_single_item` is a classmethod that reads `cls.gpu_image_decode`, while the artifact decode path and the preprocess fingerprint read `self.gpu_image_decode`. Because of that, setting the flag only on the instance would not reach the io-worker loader. ## Modifications - `BaseMultimodalProcessor.gpu_image_decode` now defaults to `None`, which means "auto". - `__init__` resolves the value on the instance right after th

title: [Perf] longcat-image: Reuse timestep conditioning for serial CFG
summary: LongCat-Image computes the same timestep conditioning for both serial CFG branches. For a 50-step request, its 40 AdaLN projections run 4,000 times and the timestep embedder runs 100 times. Prepare each timestep once, run each layer's original one-row projection across those timesteps, and reuse the results during denoising. This keeps the existing BF16 operators and rounding; it does not turn them into a batched GEMM. The cache belongs to `DENOISING_LOOP_STATE` and is released when the denoising loop ends. It is limited to single-sample eager serial CFG with sequence-parallel degree 1. CPU, gradients, compilation, CUDA Graph capture/BCG, CFG parallelism, sequence parallelism, layerwise offload and wrapped projection modules retain their original computation. title: [Fix] dsa: Isolate masked KV rows in FP8 TileLang attention
summary: ## Motivation Invalid (`-1`) sparse indices in `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial_fp8` map to KV row 0. Masking the attention score does not isolate that row: a NaN in it can propagate through both QK (`-inf + NaN`) and PV (`0 * NaN`), corrupting otherwise valid outputs and generation logprobs. This was reproduced on GLM-5.3-Flash with FP8 KV and TileLang DSA on H20, with both PP1 and PP2, including a plain-main deployment without EPLB. A direct operator reproduction changed only padding KV row 0 from zero to NaN and changed the output from finite to 196608 NaN elements. This is a correctness fix; it does not require changing the deployment's CUDA Graph, overlap, or speculative decoding settings. Related prior work: #44541 applies the same masked-load isolation to the BF16 kernel and explicitly leaves the FP8 kernel unchanged. This PR covers that FP8 gap. #36207 tracks producer-side writes to reserved KV row 0; this consumer-side fix does not depend on row 0 remaining finite and does not claim to resolve every writer path. The FlashInfer masked-gather fix discussed in #42440 concerns a different backend. ## Modifications - Zero invalid KV rows before the FP8 kernel's QK and PV matrix multiplications, including the optional RoPE tail. Keep the existing score mask and valid KV values unchanged. - Add poisoned-padding regressions for 256+0, 512+0, and 512+64 geometries, eager and CUDA Graph execution, and all-masked outputs remaining zero. ## Validation | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Poisoned-padding regression before the fix | Failed for all three geometries | | Full existing

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kda: Skip the row-streaming packed decode kernel on SM90 and SM10x
summary: ## Motivation `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode()` sends KDA decode steps without the safe gate (`lower_bound is None`) to the JIT row-streaming CUDA kernel `kda_packed_decode` from batch 8 up. The kernel and this dispatch came with the Kimi K3 kernel port (#32890), which left speed measurements to a later runtime integration. #47893 brought the safe-gate layers to this function on CUDA but kept them on the Triton kernel, which is faster than the row-streaming kernel at GLM-5.3-Flash's 8-32 heads per rank on H200 and B200. The layers without the safe gate still take the row-streaming kernel.
