summary: ### Checklist - [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug With `--encoder-only --enable-mm-global-cache` and encoder TP greater than one, every encoder rank creates an embedding storage backend and an `EmbeddingCacheController`. Each controller allocates and registers its own vision/audio host pools and starts an I/O thread. However, the current encoder pipeline uses rank 0 for cache existence checks, prefetch, host-pool staging, cache-hit loading, output assembly, and insertion. Other encoder ranks participate in hit/fallback mask broadcasts and forward computation for misses; they do not receive or read cached embedding data. The nonzero-rank pools are therefore unused pinned CPU allocations in this supported path. The default budget is 4 GiB per controller, independently of TP size. For one TP=8 encoder instance, the source implies approximately 32 GiB of total pool allocation while only rank 0's approximately 4 GiB is used. The estimated redundant allocation is approximately 28 GiB, subject to page rounding. title: [Perf] pd: Send NIXL KV chunks without a host sync on the scheduler thread
summary: ## Motivation #45492 took the device-to-host copy of a prefill KV send's page indices off the scheduler thread, but only for senders that declare `supports_host_tensor_indices`, which only the Mooncake sender did. The NIXL sender still ran the blocking `kv_to_page_indices` copy on the schedule stream, which waits behind the in-flight forward, so every NIXL chunk send stalled the scheduler thread until the forward had finished. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`: - `NixlKVSender` declares `supports_host_tensor_indices = True`. - `NixlKVManager.add_transfer_request` forwards `indices_event` into the queued `TransferKVChunk`. - `transfer_worker` waits on `indices_event` after the early-send wait and converts the host tensor to numpy before descriptors are built, as the Mooncake worker does. Unit test: `test_host_page_indices_are_read_after_their_copy_lands` in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_backend_basic.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: the pages transferred are unchanged, only the thread that waits for their index copy moves. ## Speed Tests and Profiling TODO ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations)

title: [Bug] NVFP4 Marlin path (default on SM80-SM90) decodes E4M3 subnormal block scales as 0 with bfloat16 activations
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On SM80 to SM9x GPUs (A100, L40S, H100, H200, H20, ...), SGLang serves NVFP4 linear layers through the FP4 Marlin path by default (`initialize_fp4_gemm_config` picks `marlin` there), and NVFP4 MoE layers through the Marlin fallback. `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` stores each E4M3 block scale as an S0E5M3 byte (scale * 2^7, 5-bit exponent with bias 15). With bfloat16 activations, `dequant_fp8_scales<nv_bfloat162, kFE4M3fn>` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/marlin/dequant.h` builds the bfloat16 exponent from the top bit of that byte. That is right only when the top bit is 1, i.e. for block scales of 2^-6 or more. Every smaller scale, i.e. every E4M3 subnormal (2^-9 to 7 * 2^-9), decodes to about 2^-112 of its value, so the 16 weights of its block become 0. With float16 activations the same bytes decode exactly. E4M3 subnormal block scales occur in real checkpoints: - in normalized ModelOpt exports, in tensors whose largest block scale is near 448. nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 has 165,266 of them, in five tensors whose largest block scales are 320 to 448: 162,143 in `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_

title: [Perf] linear-attn: Skip the verify row mask when PP spec decoding is off
summary: ## Motivation This is a performance change: the GDN, KDA and `qwen4_exp` target-verify paths build a per-row validity mask on every verify pass that only PP speculative decoding reads, and this PR skips it when PP spec decoding is off, worth **-1.1% to -1.3% median TPOT** at 8k/1k concurrency 1 and 2 (-0.35% geomean over 14 serving shapes) with NEXTN MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8. `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices` reads `valid` only when `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` is set. Otherwise it returns the positional scratch rows and drops the mask, yet the callers still evaluate `cache_indices[: n] >= 0` (GDN, KDA) or `batch.lengths.ne(0)` (`qwen4_exp`) first, and the comparison is captured into the verify CUDA graph. On Qwen3.8 that is 69 `compare_scalar_kernel<int>` launches per verify step, one per GDN layer. ## Modifications Each in-tree caller passes `None` instead of the mask unless `pp_spec_stable_rows_enabled()` is true, which is what the NVIDIA megakernel binding already does. The selector is unchanged, so its output is the same with PP spec decoding on or off, and out-of-tree callers that pass a tensor keep working. ## Accuracy Tests With PP spec decoding off the mask was never read, so the change cannot alter outputs. GSM8K, full test set (1314 questions, the other 5 are the few-shot prompt), `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 2048`, thinking off, same node and server args as the speed test below: | | main | this PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K | 0.9711 | 0.9741 | The 4-question difference is run-to-run noise. title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] DSA: Add FlashInfer GVR V2 top-k backend
summary: ## Motivation DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, Mistral Large 4) run an indexer top-k (K=2048) in every sparse-attention layer on every decode step, and with the default `sgl-kernel` top-k its cost grows with context length. FlashInfer's GVR V2 top-k did not grow with context in our measurements, which matters for the 1M-token contexts of models such as GLM-5.2/5.3 and Mistral Large 4. Measured on Mistral Large 4 (44 DSA layers of 72; model support is not in `main` yet), a default top-k call takes 15.8 us at 128K context and 24.0 us at 960K, while GVR V2 with the fused page lookup takes ~11-14 us. This PR adds it as an opt-in backend for long-context decode: ``` --dsa-topk-backend flashinfer_gvr2 ``` It covers plain decode and speculative verify / draft extend on SM100/103/107 with top-k 512/1024/2048. Prefill keeps `sgl-kernel`. The default backend is unchanged. ## Modifications - **New `flashinfer_gvr2` DSA top-k backend** (`dsa_topk_backend.py`, `dsa_backend.py`, CLI choices for target and draft workers). Shapes GVR V2 does not implement (prefill) fall back to `sgl-kernel` with all arguments passed through. title: [Feat] gemma4: per-layer attention backend
summary: ## Motivation Gemma-4-31B has two kinds of attention layer: - 50 sliding-window layers with head_dim 256; - 10 full-attention layers with head_dim 512. FA3 cannot run head_dim 512, so on SM90 the whole model runs on `fa4` today. On the 256-dim layers, FA3 is faster than FA4 for small-batch decode. This PR lets Gemma-4 run with `--attention-backend fa3`. The 256-dim layers stay on FA3 and the 512-dim layers run on FA4. ## Modifications - `FlashAttentionBackend._ver_for(layer)` picks the kernel per layer. On the `fa3` backend it returns FA4 when `max(head_dim, v_head_dim) > 256` or the batch has image masks (FA4-only). Otherwise it returns the backend's own version. MLA and the `fa4` backend are unchanged. - Every kernel call and FA4-only guard in `forward_extend` and `forward_decode` uses this per-layer `ver` in place of `self.fa_impl_ver`. - When FA4 layers are present, init rejects a KV cache that is not BF16 and the embedding no-KV-cache path (`fa_skip_kv_cache`), and skips the FA3 scheduler-metadata precompute, which FA3 cannot size for head_dim 512. - `fa3` is added to Gemma-4's accepted backends. Usage: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block \ --attention-backend fa3 ``` ## Accuracy GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, parallel 8, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. title: [Fix] hicache: Stop L3 prefetch at the match key limit
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation With hierarchical cache enabled and an L3 storage backend, a request whose prefix is already stored can still end up with `#cached-token: 0` right after a successful prefetch: HiCache prefetch success ... completed=227840 matched=0 loaded=227840 occupied=0 Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 227864, #cached-token: 0, ... The prefetched data was paid for (RDMA read) and then silently dropped, and the entire prompt was re-prefilled. This happens for hybrid SWA models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4: `page_size=256`, `sliding_window=128`, `swa_gates_prefix_match=True`) when the L3 prefetch span overruns the radix match key: - Match key: `_req_radix_key` caps the key at `L - swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()`, so page-aligned matching ends at `E_match = floor((L - W) / P) * P`. - L3 prefetch: `_prefetch_kvcache` used `req._compute_max_prefix_len(...) = L - 1`, so the page-aligned span ends at `E_pre = floor((L - 1) / P) * P`. For `L mod P = r`, `E_pre > E_match` exactly when `1 <= r <= W - 1` (~49.6% of all prompt lengths for `P=256, W=128`) and the page `[E_match, E_match + P)` is present in L3. For a prefetched span, the only SWA host window is committed to the span's last page, whose position assumes the span end. title: [Perf] [AMD] DeepSeek-V4.1: Token-sharded prefill attention under attention TP
summary: ## Motivation Under attention TP, DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill on ROCm runs the ratio-1/2 indexer for every token on every rank (the indexer is replicated), and each rank's sparse attention gathers the top-k KV rows of every token for its few heads. ## Modifications Behind `SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_SHARD_Q` (default off), each attention-TP rank attends a share of the prefill tokens with every head: - `dsv4/shard_q.py`: zigzag split (each request is cut into `2 * tp` chunks; rank `r` takes chunks `r` and `2 * tp - 1 - r`, which balances causal work) and two padded all-to-alls: the query `[T, H / tp, D] -> [T_rank, H, D]` before attention, and the output back to `[T, H / tp, D]` before `wo_a`. - HIP backend: the prefill metadata's query fields are narrowed to the rank's tokens (`apply_cp_reindex(local_index=...)`). The cache-write fields stay global, so the SWA store and the compressors still write every token. The indexer scores only the rank's rows and keeps its top-k local; the OPUS chunk cache uses the rank's rows per request. - Model: full `attn_sink`, the rank's positions for the in-kernel inverse RoPE. - `rowgroup_prefill_query_start_loc` keys its cache on the per-request split too, since a request can have no rows on a rank. Applies to eager `EXTEND` with attention TP > 1, no CP, `aiter_sparse`, at least 1024 tokens and no DP padding. Under decoder SWA bounded replay the tail layers keep their head-sharded path. ## Status Prototype; not yet run on GPU, accuracy and performance to follow. Checked on CPU: the split against a brute-force reference; the all-to-all round trip at TP 2/4/8

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Re-land the JIT moe_finalize_fuse_shared with the shared row read after the PDL wait

title: [Fix] scheduler: Match arrival prefixes on every PP stage
summary: With pipeline parallelism, HiCache L3 storage, and `buffer_only` host memory, only the first stage matched a request's prefix on arrival. If grammar compilation delayed enqueueing, this could leave cache LRU state different across stages and cause subsequent evictions to produce different prefix lengths. This PR matches the arrival prefix on every pipeline stage before grammar waiting, while keeping prefetch ticket creation on the first stage. A focused regression test reproduces the prefix mismatch caused by asymmetric Mamba checkpoint eviction and checks that arrival matching preserves the same checkpoint across stages. The arrival hook now checks `controller.pp_prefetch_command_group` directly after a null-controller check, so eligibility follows the initialized ticket channel without `getattr` or duplicate mode/PP-size gates. The regression fixture also covers a disabled channel. Six isolated controller/rank cases and commit lint checks passed; GPU regressions were not rerun for this follow-up. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #42148338975](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42148338975)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #42148338960](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42148338960)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #42148338968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42148338968)<!

summary: ## Motivation Stacked on #44660 (ROCm kv-shard with aiter and MoRI): only the last commit is new; please review after #44660. title: [Feat] [AMD] diffusion: Add MXFP6 and A6W4 online GEMM quantization
summary: ## Motivation Currently on gfx950 the two quantization options for ROCm are MXFP4 and FP8. This PR adds the middleground - MXFP6 and A6W4. They are the compromise between the two, both in speed and accuracy. ## Modifications - `runtime/layers/quantization/aiter_packed_mx.py`: shared base for both formats. - `runtime/layers/quantization/mxfp6.py`: `Mxfp6Config` / `Mxfp6LinearMethod`, weights and activations via `quant_mxfp6_gemm`, product via `gemm_a6w6`. - `runtime/layers/quantization/a6w4.py`: `A6W4Config` / `A6W4LinearMethod`, weights via `quant_mxfp4_gemm`, activations via `quant_mxfp6_gemm`, product via `gemm_a6w4`. - Each format wraps its activation quant plus GEMM in one functional custom op (`direct_register_custom_op`) so the layer stays `torch.compile` compatible. - Registered `mxfp6` and `a6w4` in the quantization registry and in the four online-quant sites (`transformer_load_utils`, `comfyui_checkpoints/spec`, `text_encoder_loader`, `--quantization` help). Both honour `--quantization-ignored-layers`. ## Accuracy Tests Relative error against an fp32 reference, measured on gfx950 at Wan2.2-A14B layer shapes (hidden 5120, ffn 13824, M=9450). summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, MiniMax-M3 on MI350X at TP4 gives different outputs for the same prompt depending on its batch and on whether part of it came from the radix cache: the prefix test returns many different outputs per prompt, and `radix_cache` fails. summary: ## Motivation The legacy DFlash draft cache scales linearly with target KV capacity. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Make the KV checksum digest each state component's own transfer payload
summary: ## Motivation `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` is meant to digest exactly the bytes the PD transfer moved: prefill digests what it sends, decode digests what it received, and a mismatch aborts the request (and raises in CI). On main the two digests cover different bytes than the transfer does, in four ways. A correct transfer can therefore be reported as corrupted, and a corrupted one can pass. 1. **State rows are not the ones the transfer used.** `state_indices_for_request` derives a single index tensor by inspecting the pool (mamba row, window pages, or token pages). `KvChecksumComputer` then applies that one tensor to every buffer of every state component. The transfer instead addresses each component with its own payload (`resume_units` window units, DSA tail rows, SWA-ring rows, request-state rows, ...). Wherever a component's payload differs from the shared tensor, the digest reads rows the transfer never wrote. 2. **DeepSeek-V4 has no state indices at all.** For `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` the function returns `None` while state buffers are registered, which trips the assert. That is why #48292 rejects the flag for DeepSeek-V4. 3. **Decode verifies the wrong range for a rebootstrapped request.** Decode digests `[cache_protected_len, len(origin_input_ids))`. A rebootstrap's prefill input is `origin_input_ids + output_ids[:-1]`, and prefill digests that whole range, so every rebootstrap with more than one kept output fails verification. title: [AMD][Kernel] Add a K-only store_cache and use it for the MiniMax index-K pool
summary: ## Motivation `MHATokenToKOnlyPool.set_k_buffer` — the MiniMax sparse index-K cache — writes with an elementwise `self.k_buffer[layer_id][loc] = cache_k`, which lowers to `index_put_`. The JIT `store_cache` kernel already exists for exactly this shape of write and is faster, but it has no K-only form: both `store_cache` and `can_use_store_cache` take a K **and** a V tensor. title: [Feat] weight_update: Let platforms serve weight transports through /plugin_weight_update
summary: ## Motivation Port of sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1866 to main, so the two trees stay the same. A platform that receives RL weight updates by its own transport (first user: a TPU trainer sending weights over ICI) needs code on every TP rank inside the weight-update session. Today that means a request type, an HTTP route, a tokenizer communicator and a scheduler branch in core per transport, which the plugin migration is meant to stop. ## Modifications A weight update has two halves. The **receive half** is the transport: get the bucket's tensors onto this rank, over ICI, p2p/RDMA, shared memory, disk, or a DMA engine. The **load half** is policy: the weight-cache and derived-weight guards, the draft runner, the session's `post_load_weights` decision, flush, and the version. This PR makes the receive half pluggable and keeps the load half in core, so a transport cannot be less safe than `/update_weights_from_distributed`, and load-side features reach every transport when they land here. ```python SRTPlatform.get_weight_update_handlers() -> {name: handler} # {} by default handler(context, payload) -> [(name, tensor), ...] # receive one bucket on this TP rank context: runners [(role, ModelRunner)], tp_rank, tp_size, state # state: per-rank, kept across calls POST /plugin_weight_update {handler, payload, flush_cache, abort_all_requests, weight_version, selector, torch_empty_cache} -> {success, message, received_tensor_counts} ``` - **Tokenizer:** the same path as `update_weights_from_distributed`: data-parallel check, `abort_all_requests`, the pause-aware writer lock, one reply

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Use a spill-free BF16 tile for the triton sparse-MLA split-K decode on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation The triton sparse-MLA split-K decode on gfx950 runs a BF16 KV cache with a 16 x 64 tile that spills registers, because the only gfx950 tile tuning in the file is reserved for FP8 KV; this PR gives BF16 KV a spill-free tile and widens the head tile where the grid still covers the device. `triton_sparse_mla_decode_splitk` hardcodes `BLOCK_H = 16` and takes `BLOCK_K` from the LDS budget, 64 for BF16 KV on a 160 KiB gfx950 CU. `_gfx950_sparse_mla_decode_tile_config` sits behind `optimize_gfx950_fp8`, so a BF16 DSA decode (GLM-5.2/5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the ROCm default `--dsa-decode-backend triton` and `--kv-cache-dtype auto`) holds a 64 x 576 BF16 KV tile in registers for both dots. On MI355X the fused kernel compiles to: | | n_spills | n_regs | LDS | |---|---:|---:|---:| | main (`BLOCK_H=16, BLOCK_K=64`) | 15 | 512 | 72 KiB | | this PR (`BLOCK_H=32, BLOCK_K=32`) | 0 | 484 | 36 KiB | ## Modifications `_sparse_mla_decode_tile_shape()` picks the split-K decode tile. For BF16 KV at least 512 wide on gfx950: - `BLOCK_K = min(block_k, 32)`: spill-free, and half the LDS, so a second workgroup fits per CU. - `BLOCK_H = 32` when `H % 32 == 0` and `bs * (H // 32) >= num_cu`. The wider head tile gathers each selected KV row once per 32 heads instead of 16 but halves the head-block count, so it is taken only where the halved grid still fills the device; below one wave, forcing it costs up to 38 %. `H % 32 == 0` keeps `h_padded` as today, so the shared reduce kernel and the split-K workspace are unchanged. - FP8, non-gfx950 and narrow-KV callers get `(16, block_k)`,

title: [Perf] mhc: halve the DeepGEMM prenorm slices when the grid overflows one wave
summary: ## Motivation `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` always splits K into 16 slices. Its two `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` calls launch `ceil(m / 64) x 16` CTAs, and each CTA's shared-memory footprint allows one CTA per SM. During DeepSeek-V4.1 decode at 256 requests per rank with 3 draft tokens (m = 1024 rows), that is 256 CTAs: more than one wave. The grid runs on `hc_stats_stream` beside MegaMoE, and its second wave holds SMs that the main-path kernels need. ## Modifications - `_hc_mix_deepgemm_slices(m)`: 16 slices when `ceil(m / 64) * 16` CTAs fit in one wave, otherwise 8. The reduce/sinkhorn kernel already takes `NUM_SLICES=slices`, so both stages stay consistent. - 8 is the floor. Error against an fp64 reference grows about linearly with K per slice. 8 slices doubles the 16-slice error, 4 quadruples it, and 2 is 8x. - The `bf16x3` path keeps `_HC_MIX_COMPENSATED_SLICES`. ## Accuracy Max abs error vs fp64 over pre/post/comb, hidden 7168 (K = 28672), relative to the 16-slice error at the same m: | slices | m = 32 | 1024 | 4095 | |---|---|---|---| | 8 | 1.9x | 1.9x | 1.9x | | 4 | 4.8x | 3.4x | 3.9x | | 2 | 9.0x | 6.5x | 8.0x | hidden 4096 follows the same pattern. ## Benchmark Standalone `hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm` time, 8 slices / 16 slices (CUDA graph, ABBA): | m | hidden 4096 | hidden 7168 | grid at 16 slices | |---|---|---|---| | 64 | 1.16 | 1.33 | one wave | | 576 | 1.12 | 1.26 | one wave | | 1024 | 0.76 | 0.80 | > one wave | | 2048 | 0.77 | 0.83 | > one wave | | 4095 | 0.82 | 0.90 | > one wave | | 131072 | 0.75 | 0.86 | > one wave | 16 slices wins while the grid fits one

title: [Fix] Respect an explicit SGLANG_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_SIZE

title: [Doc] [NVIDIA] cookbook: Recommend the CuTe DSL all-reduce fusion backend for GLM-5.2 GB300 TP4 low latency
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation In every GLM-5.2 decoder layer, the attention output and the MLP output (an MoE in 75 of the 78 layers) are each summed across the tensor-parallel ranks (an all-reduce), added to the residual and normalized (RMSNorm). All-reduce fusion runs these three steps as one kernel. On one Blackwell node at TP4, SGLang turns it on by itself with `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend auto`, which resolves to FlashInfer's `mnnvl` backend (MNNVL is multi-node NVLink; these kernels exchange data over the NVLink fabric). That fusion covers batches of up to 2048 tokens; larger prefill chunks fall back to an NCCL all-reduce and a separate RMSNorm. The opt-in `cutedsl` backend uses FlashInfer kernels written in CuTe DSL (CUTLASS's Python kernel language) over the same fabric. It fuses batches up to `--max-prefill-tokens` (8192 in this deployment) and, for batches of up to 192 tokens, also folds in the MoE finalize (the weighted sum of the selected experts' outputs) and the shared-expert add. This PR adds a Configuration Tips bullet to the GLM-5.2 cookbook that recommends `cutedsl` for one deployment: GB300 NVFP4, aggregated TP4, concurrency 1 (c1), a point of the page's Agentic Long-Context section. That section lists commands measured with AgentX, SemiAnalysis InferenceX's agentic-coding benchmark, which replays recorded multi-turn coding-agent sessions against the server. The bullet gives the measured effect, the builds the flag needs (those with #45565, which raised the default prefill CUDA-graph size for MLA models from 2048 tokens to min(8192, chunked-pre

title: [Feat] kimi-k3.1: DSA decode context parallelism runtime

summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug These models build `RadixAttention` without `quant_config`, so attention gets no KV-cache method and no `k_scale`/`v_scale`. title: [Fix] hicache: Do not count staged-prefetch deferrals while KV awaits a PD transfer
summary: ## Motivation In HiCache buffer mode a staged L3 prefix must fit in GPU KV at admission. When admission fails on the token budget and nothing is running, `PrefillAdder._defer_staged_for_capacity_if_idle` counts the scheduler pass as a deferral, and after `max_staged_admission_defers` passes the buffer pipeline drops the staged copy so the request recomputes its prefix. On a disaggregated prefill engine that count is wrong: finished prefills keep their KV until the decode side has pulled it (`Scheduler.disagg_prefill_transfer_queue`). While those transfers hold the pool, the running batch is empty, so every scheduler pass looks idle to the adder, the deferral budget is spent while the transfers are still in flight, and the staged prefix is dropped although the transfers free the memory shortly afterwards. The request then recomputes the whole prefix it already had in L3. ```text PD prefill engine, buffer-mode HiCache: pool: [ KV of finished prefills, awaiting decode transfer ........ ][free] staged L3 prefix needs more than [free] -> NO_TOKEN running batch empty -> "idle" -> defers += 1 ... repeated every pass until defers == max_staged_admission_defers staged copy dropped -> transfers complete -> prefix recomputed from scratch ``` ## Modifications - `PrefillAdder` takes a new keyword `kv_awaiting_transfer: bool = False`. The scheduler passes `bool(self.disagg_prefill_transfer_queue)`. - `_defer_staged_for_capacity_if_idle` returns without counting a deferral while `kv_awaiting_transfer` is set, exactly as it already does while `can_run_list` or the running batch is non-empt

title: [MiniMax-M3] Fix PP tc_piecewise position padding
summary: ## Motivation MiniMax-M3 fails during pipeline-parallel prefill when using the `tc_piecewise` CUDA Graph backend together with fused QKNorm/RoPE. After a hidden state is forwarded to a later PP stage, its token dimension contains only the actual local tokens, while `positions` may still retain the tail padding of the CUDA Graph bucket. For example: ```text hidden_states.shape[0] = 3372 positions.shape[0] = 3584 ``` Passing tensors with these inconsistent token dimensions to the fused QKNorm/RoPE kernel causes a shape mismatch. ## Changes Trim tail-padded `positions` to the PP-local hidden-state token count before calling the MiniMax fused QKNorm/RoPE kernels. The normalization is applied only when: - the prefill CUDA Graph backend is `tc_piecewise`; and - fused QKNorm/RoPE or grouped fused QKNorm/RoPE is enabled. ```python if positions.shape[0] > hidden_states.shape[0]: positions = positions[: hidden_states.shape[0]] ``` ## Scope This change is intentionally limited to the MiniMax-M3 fused QKNorm/RoPE prefill path. It does not affect: - decode; - non-`tc_piecewise` prefill; - non-fused QKNorm/RoPE paths; - the NPU-specific forward path; - other model implementations; - requests where `positions` and `hidden_states` already have matching lengths. ## Why trimming is correct The extra entries are tail padding introduced by the CUDA Graph bucket and do not correspond to real hidden states on the current PP stage. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] glm5: Route small-M BF16 GEMMs to FlashInfer warp split-K with PDL on SM107
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation On SM107 (Vera Rubin NVL72), GLM-5 TP4 decode with EAGLE runs its dense BF16 GEMMs on 1 to 20 tokens per step: o_proj, fused_qkv_a, the DSA indexer's fused wk + weights_proj, and the shared expert's gate_up and down. Today they go to the CuTe DSL TGV kernel, to cuBLAS (for the shared expert and the indexer often a split-K GEMM plus a separate reduce kernel), or, for fused_qkv_a at M <= 16, to SGLang's fused_a JIT kernel. At these sizes each GEMM takes a few microseconds and mostly streams weights, so how much of its start-up overlaps the previous kernel matters as much as the kernel body. FlashInfer's warp split-K BF16 GEMM, which main already runs for its Muse Spark keys in `_BF16_WARP_SPLITK_TUNED_TACTICS`, launches with PDL (programmatic dependent launch): it starts while the previous kernel is still finishing, issues its weight loads, and waits for the previous kernel only before it reads the activations. With PDL it is faster per call than the current route at all of these shapes; without PDL it is slower than TGV at o_proj (tables below). title: [Perf] mem_cache: Defer unified KV recycling until forward completion
summary: ## Motivation #48450 prevents an overlapping forward from reading recycled KV pages, but waits on that forward during every lazy free. Defer physical-page recycling until the recorded forward completes so request cleanup can proceed without adding that stream dependency. ## Modifications - Keep freed physical-page tensors grouped by their own `forward_done` event. Poll completion when freeing, allocating or flushing; completed groups return to the free list without a wait. title: [Bug] PD + Mooncake: different DSA backends on prefill and decode silently corrupt the decode KV ("Requested address ... not found")
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug In PD disaggregation, a DSA model picks its FP8 KV layout per role from that role's DSA backend ([`calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4387a94cf218ba870474d7a2a40a632bc4975798/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py#L3350-L3357)): - a prefill with `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv` gets 656 B/token per layer; - a decode with the default `trtllm` backend gets 576 B/token per layer. The Mooncake sender writes each decode page at `dst_ptr + page * item_len` using the **prefill's** `item_len` ([`_send_kvcache_generic`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4387a94cf218ba870474d7a2a40a632bc4975798/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py#L1200-L1203)). The decode's `dst_kv_item_len(s)` arrive at registration, but they are compared only under `--enable-unified-memory`. As a result: - every transfer writes the wrong bytes at the wrong offset, so GSM8K through PD scores 0 even when no transfer fails; - blocks in the top ~12% of a decode pool overrun the layer buffer. Mooncake then logs `nvlink_transport.cpp:1153 Requested address ... not found!` and the request fails. It is not specific to DEP: a PP prefill with the same flags fails the same way. NIXL addresses the destination

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Reject a decode peer whose KV page stride differs at Mooncake registration
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48230. - The Mooncake sender writes decode pages at `dst_ptr + page * item_len` using the prefill's `item_len`. When the roles allocate different KV layouts, every transfer silently corrupts the decode KV, and pages near the end of the pool overrun the layer buffer (`Requested address ... not found`). - One way to hit it is a DSA model whose prefill and decode use different DSA backends (656 B/token with `flashmla_*`, 576 B/token with `trtllm`). Another is a different `--kv-cache-dtype` on each role (#19355). - The decode already sends its `dst_kv_item_lens` at registration, but nothing compares them outside `--enable-unified-memory`. ## Modifications - `MooncakeKVManager._kv_layout_mismatch`: at peer registration, compares the prefill KV item lengths with the decode's, pairing entries as the sender does. MLA and layer-id pools reuse the PP-aware `_state_stride_mismatch` that already guards the state buffers. Plain MHA pools at the same attn TP compare K and V per layer through `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp`. On a mismatch, the peer goes into `state_layout_rejections`, so every request to that peer fails with one clear reason (both lengths, the page size, and the likely cause) and no bytes are written. Ascend inherits the check. - The check is skipped where the stride differs by design or is checked elsewhere: TP-sliced MHA, DCP relayout, and unified memory (`_validate_envelope_kv_layout`). It is also skipped for a PP1 MHA peer whose entry count differs from ours (a decode-only draft KV). There is no opt-out flag, the same as the existing state-layout check.

Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary This RFC proposes an optional KV compression path for Prefill-to-Decode transfer over Mooncake RDMA. SGLang would manage layout preparation, bounded buffers, transfer metadata, and asynchronous completion through a small internal interface for compression backends. title: [Fix] nixl: release transfer worker when room is aborted mid-wait
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #44369. In PD disaggregation with the NIXL backend, aborting a request after its KV transfer handles were submitted did not bound the prefill transfer worker's wait when a handle stayed healthy but non-terminal (`PROC`): `NixlKVManager._await_handles()` only arms its settle deadline after an `ERR` is observed, so with every handle `PROC` the deadline stays `None` and the wait is unbounded. The abort notification marks the room `Failed` and registers the deferred ACK target, but it neither wakes a worker already inside `_await_handles()` nor drains the room's `_staging_outstanding` count — so the deferred abort ACK never fires and the worker thread never returns to its queue. With the default `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=4`, four such aborted rooms can exhaust all prefill transfer workers. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` - `_await_handles()` now accepts an optional `room` and returns `(settled, any_failed, aborted)`. When the room is marked `Failed` while polling (e.g. a decode-side abort notification landed after the batch was submitted), the wait ends immediately with `aborted=True` instead of spinning forever on healthy non-terminal handles. The exception-path call site passes no room, so its already-bounded (`failure_seen=True`) behavior is unchanged. - `transfer_worker()` handles the aborted wait: it releases the chunk's staging count (guarded by the existing `staging_counted` flag, mirroring the failure path) and fires the deferred abort ACK via `_maybe_ack_drained_abort()`, then continues with the next chunk.

title: [Perf] radix cache: each eviction rebuilds a heap over all evictable leaves
summary: ### Describe the bug Once the KV pool is full of unreferenced cached prefixes, every allocation that needs room evicts. Each eviction rebuilds a heap over all evictable device leaves, in Python: ```python # python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/full.py:207-215 def _evict_device_start(self, request_cnt: int) -> None: ... self._evict_device_heap = [ (self.session_ref_eviction_strategy(n), n) for n in self.tree_core.evictable_device_leaves ] heapq.heapify(self._evict_device_heap) ``` That makes each `evict_for_alloc` call O(number of evictable leaves), even when it frees only a few pages. With a large tree, decode steps that need new pages pay several milliseconds each. `RadixCache.evict` (`radix_cache.py:557`) has the same pattern. ### Measurements Qwen3-0.6B, TP 2, 2x GB300, SGLang `851642ade7`, scheduler driven in-process (one scheduler iteration per step). A sequence of benchmark workloads fills the pool with cached prefixes. title: [Bug] EPLB statistics include empty draft records during speculative decoding
summary: ### The problem EPLB uses recent expert counts to decide where the **target model's** experts should live. With DSpark, the target and draft runners share this recorder. A draft forward adds an empty record to the target's history, even though the draft model already disables its counting hooks. **The problem is still present in main at `b147f4aa1092b6f5b206f50d8dd3f84f8c48aa98`, fetched on November 5.** I traced the current call path and reproduced the empty appends using that revision's Python recording code on CPU. The real-service heatmaps below were collected separately on October 31. The practical effect is that draft records use up space intended for target observations. In our service capture, a 200-entry slice held **100 target records and 100 empty draft records**. Excluding draft recording gave **200 target records**, with speculative decoding still running. ### Why this happens There are two separate operations: counting expert assignments during a forward, and saving the resulting count table when the forward ends. The existing draft guard stops the first operation, but not the second. ```text Target forward: reset counters -> count target routes -> save a target record Draft forward: reset counters -> counting is disabled -> save an empty record ``` The draft model's `disable_this_region()` is inside the outer recording context. By the time it runs, the recorder has already reset the counters. When the model returns, the outer context collects those zero counters and appends them anyway. title: [Fix] [NPU] Support CPU weight offload with pinned host memory
summary: ## Motivation `cpu_offload_gb` reduces device memory usage by keeping part of the model weights in CPU memory and copying them back to the device for computation. This PR enables that path for NPU inference with graph capture by allocating pinned CPU storage for the offloaded weights. `OffloaderV1` currently chooses pinned storage solely through `is_pin_memory_available()`, which returns `False` on the evaluated NPU stack. The resulting pageable CPU storage causes the weight copy back to NPU to fail during graph capture. Requesting pinned storage at allocation time allows the existing CPU-to-NPU transfer to run in the tested graph path. ## Modifications In `OffloaderV1.maybe_offload_to_cpu`, request pinned CPU storage when the parameter's original device is NPU: ```diff - pin_memory = is_pin_memory_available() + pin_memory = is_pin_memory_available() or device.type == "npu" ``` This applies the allocation policy in the shared offloader, where the CPU storage is created. Weights are still copied back to NPU by the existing forward wrapper. Other devices continue to use the platform's pinned-memory decision. Add three policy tests covering NPU pinning, the existing non-NPU policy, and the zero-budget/CPU-resident cases. They execute the actual `OffloaderV1` class with mocked allocations, so they can run without an NPU. ## Validation On main at `d0a75654368a`, the policy tests pass with the patch (**3 passed**). Against the unpatched main implementation, the NPU pinning case fails because the allocation receives `pin_memory=False`. Existing device validation used Qwen3-ASR-0.6

title: [Feat] all-reduce: host-staged all-reduce for two GPUs without peer access
summary: **Problem.** On consumer cards (no NVLink, no PCIe P2P — `nvidia-smi topo` says `SYS`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce` is required) NCCL uses its SHM transport. Its kernels read host memory over PCIe a cache line at a time: on two RTX 5070 Ti (PCIe 4.0 x16, 26 GB/s per direction measured) a 20 MB all-reduce — `[2048, 5120]` bf16, one TP=2 prefill chunk — takes 10.9 ms, 1.9 GB/s, under `NCCL_PROTO=LL`, `Simple` and `LL128` alike. A 2048-token prefill chunk of a 64-layer model does 128 of them: 733 ms of an 802 ms step in the torch profiler. `NCCL_SHM_USE_CUDA_MEMCPY=1` brings the 20 MB case to 12.5 GB/s but doubles the latency of the 10 KB decode all-reduces (39 -> 81 µs, 130 per token), so it costs decode. **Change.** An opt-in communicator (`SGLANG_HOST_STAGED_ALLREDUCE=1`) for messages of at least `SGLANG_HOST_STAGED_ALLREDUCE_MIN_BYTES` (1 MiB) outside CUDA-graph capture; smaller messages and captured graphs keep the existing path, so decode is untouched. Two ranks share a `/dev/shm` file (rank 0 names it, the gloo group carries the name at init), registered Portable|Mapped. Slots are double-buffered with a "read back" counter guarding reuse. title: [Perf] GGUF: use MMQ from 2 rows for very large matrices (e.g. lm_head)
summary: ## Motivation `fused_mul_mat_gguf` dispatches standard / K-quant GGUF matmuls to MMVQ (`ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8`) when `x.shape[0] <= mmvq_safe`, with `mmvq_safe = 2` for matrices with more than 5120 output rows. MMVQ launches one grid row per input row, so its cost is linear in the number of input rows, while MMQ (`ggml_mul_mat_a8`) has a fixed cost that a very large matrix amortizes. For a large-vocab lm_head this makes the 2-row case (e.g. the verify window of one-step speculative decoding) almost twice as slow as it needs to be. So the existing rule is right for ordinary layers, and the change is a threshold on output rows. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`: add a module-level constant `MMVQ_SINGLE_ROW_ABOVE = 32768`. title: [Perf] GGUF: dequantize + dense GEMM for large batches instead of MMQ
summary: ## Motivation `fused_mul_mat_gguf` sends standard and K-quant GGUF matmuls to MMQ (`ggml_mul_mat_a8`) for every batch larger than the MMVQ cutoff. MMQ's time grows linearly with the number of input rows. A prefill chunk has thousands of rows, so the GGUF linear layers become the bottleneck there. The other option is to dequantize the weight once and run a dense bf16 GEMM, the path that I-Matrix types already take. That option has a mostly fixed cost, the dequantization, which even a small batch amortizes. title: [Fix] GGUF: IQ3_S codebook and q8_1 block sums
summary: ## Motivation Two accuracy bugs in SGLang's GGUF CUDA kernels. Both slipped past the existing tests, whose element-wise tolerances are loose (`atol=1e-2, rtol=4e-2` for dequant, bf16 `rtol=3e1` for MMVQ and `1e4` for MMQ). 1. **IQ3_S is computed from the wrong codebook.** `dequantize_block_iq3_s` and `vec_dot_iq3_s_q8_1` look up the 3-bit codes in `iq3xs_grid` and scale each block by `d * (0.5 + s) * 0.5`. That pair belongs to a pre-release IQ3_S format. The released format, which llama.cpp writes and gguf-py reads, uses `iq3s_grid` with `d * (1 + 2s)`. 2. **The q8_1 block sums do not match the quantized activations.** `quantize_q8_1` stores the sum of the *unquantized* inputs in `ds.y`. The kernels use that sum to apply a per-block weight offset or minimum: Q4_0's -8, Q5_0's -16, IQ1_S's delta, and the Q4_K / Q5_K minimums in MMQ. Only the sum of the values that were actually multiplied cancels exactly. With the unquantized sum, the rounding error of the activations stays in the result, multiplied by the offset. Relative L2 against an fp32 product with gguf-py's dequantized weights, measured on the `Isotr0py/test-gguf-sample` files (RTX 5070 Ti, sm_120, `randn` bf16 activations; MMVQ uses 7 tokens and MMQ uses 300): | kernel | type | main | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `ggml_dequantize` (fp32) | IQ3_S | 1.4e-2 | 0 | | `ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8` (MMVQ) | IQ3_S | 1.6e-2 | 5.8e-3 | | MMVQ | Q4_0 / Q5_0 / IQ1_S | 1.5e-2 / 1.5e-2 / 1.1e-2 | 5.7e-3 / 5.8e-3 / 5.9e-3 | | `ggml_mul_mat_a8` (MMQ) | Q4_K / Q5_K / Q4_0 | 1.3e-2 / 1.3e-2 / 1.4e-2 | 5.7e-3 / 5.7e-3 / 5.7e-3 | | all kernels

title: [Perf] GGUF: llama.cpp's int8 tensor-core MMQ behind ggml_mul_mat_a8
summary: ## Motivation On CUDA, `ggml_mul_mat_a8` is the dp4a MMQ that vLLM copied from llama.cpp in 2024 (b2899). Since then llama.cpp's MMQ has moved to int8 tensor-core `mma` instructions, stream-k scheduling and kernels for the i-quants. At prefill sizes, SGLang's GGUF linear layers are now **8-15x slower** than llama.cpp on the same GPU. The i-quants (IQ2_*, IQ3_*, IQ4_*, IQ1_S) have no MMQ at all here: they dequantize the whole weight to bf16 on every call. Low-bit GGUF releases of large MoE models are now common: IQ2/IQ3/IQ4 experts, with Q4_K/Q6_K dense layers. This PR replaces the CUDA implementation behind `ggml_mul_mat_a8` with llama.cpp's current MMQ and extends MMQ to every GGUF weight type, IQ1_M included (llama.cpp has no IQ1_M MMQ; the third commit adds a tile loader for it). title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: score the torch indexer chunk in place
summary: ## Motivation The torch indexer of DeepSeek-V4.1 (the path GPUs without DeepGEMM's paged MQA logits take, e.g. SM12x) scores a prefill in chunks of a bf16 `[rows, 64 heads, keys]` product capped at `_TORCH_SCORE_BUDGET_BYTES` (1 GiB). `scores()` then did `(s.relu() * weights.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1)`: `relu()` and the multiply each allocated another tensor of the chunk's size, so a chunk peaked at 3 GiB. On 12-16 GB cards that is the largest transient of a long prefill, and it is where the prefill runs out of memory. ## Modifications - `dsv41_sparse.py`, `DeepseekV41Indexer.scores()`: `relu_()` and `mul_()` on the einsum's own output, then the same `sum(dim=1).float()`. The einsum returns a fresh tensor and `scores()` has one caller (`_score_chunks`), so nothing else sees it. - `v41_indexer/scoring.py`: the budget's comment no longer says transients run ~3x the cap. ## Accuracy Tests Same operations in the same order. title: [Fix] moe: scale the KT routed output once when the top-k already folds the factor
summary: ## Motivation Since #44993, `TopK` folds `routed_scaling_factor` into the top-k weights whenever the layer's quant method reports `fuse_routed_scaling_factor_in_topk`. `KTEPWrapperMethod` forwards unknown attributes to its GPU method through `__getattr__`, and the MXFP4 methods (`mxfp4_flashinfer_cutlass_moe`, `mxfp4_marlin_moe`, `mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`) report `True`. So under KTransformers the top-k weights already carry the factor. `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream` still multiply the routed output by `routed_scaling_factor` unconditionally whenever the quant method is `KTEPWrapperMethod`. The routed experts were therefore scaled twice. On DeepSeek-V4.1 (`routed_scaling_factor` 1.5) they came out at 2.25x instead of 1.5x, on every layer. ## Modifications The KT branch of that condition now scales only when the top-k has not already folded the factor (`not self.routed_scaling_factor_fused_in_topk`). Both sites are changed. GPU methods that do not fuse the factor keep the single multiply they had before. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (1017 checkpoint), KTransformers hybrid MoE on 2x RTX 5070 Ti (TP2) with AVX2 MXFP4 CPU experts. - **Reference.** Teacher-forced log-probs on 24 x 480-token pieces (11,496 scored tokens) from the checkpoint's own `inference/model.py`, streamed one layer at a time. - **Layer 0.** I dumped piece 0's MoE pieces on both sides from the same input. - The routing and the top-k weights are identical, and the weights already sum to 1.5 per token. - The shared expert matches within 0.2%. - The KT routed output

title: [Feat] deepseek-v4.1: the V4.1 KV cache layouts on SM120 / SM121
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 defines two KV cache layouts. The checkpoint's own `inference/model.py` and DeepSeek's DeepInfer (`V41_FORMAT`) agree on both: - **Window/SWA KV:** all 512 values, RoPE part included, in e4m3 blocks of 32 with UE8M0 scales. - **Ratio-1/2 compressed KV:** e2m1 blocks of 16 with e4m3 scales. SGLang already has both layouts as `KVLayout.V41` and `V41_FP4`, and its writers support them. However, `select_dsv4_kv_layout` allows them only on SM100. SM120 / SM121 (RTX 50, RTX PRO Blackwell, DGX Spark) therefore always run the V4 layout, which keeps RoPE in bf16 and uses FP8 blocks of 64. FlashInfer 0.7.2 already ships SM120 kernels that read both V4.1 caches (`kv_scale_format="ue8m0_g32"`, `extra_kv_fp4`). ## Modifications - `select_dsv4_kv_layout`: return V41 on SM12x when `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT=v41` and `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer` (the default backend). The default layout stays `v4`, so nothing changes unless the variable is set. - `flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120`: a 528-byte main cache goes to FlashInfer's `SparseMLASm120Wrapper`, with: - `kv_scale_format="ue8m0_g32"`; - `extra_kv_fp4` set for a 288-byte extra cache; - one wrapper per (extra format, device). The cache is read in place: FlashInfer takes the page size at run time, so the 256 → 64 page split the V4 path needs is skipped. - `SGLANG_SM120_V41_PRECISION`, default `bf16`, selects FlashInfer's full-BF16 route: bf16 Q and P, exact on-chip dequantization, and fp32 softmax and merge, as the reference computes. `default` selects FlashInfer's MXFP8 route. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4

title: [Fix] mimo: Keep tool calls with nullable schemas, overflowing numbers, or batched stream chunks
summary:
## Motivation `MiMoDetector` (`--tool-call-parser mimo`) drops tool calls in three cases: 1. **A parameter schema uses a `type` list, e.g. `{"type": ["string", "null"]}`.** `_get_param_type` returns the list, and `_convert_param_value` calls `.startswith` on it, which raises `AttributeError`. In the non-streaming path, `serving_chat` catches the exception and returns the whole `<tool_call>` block as plain content, so the call is lost. OpenAI strict-mode schemas and many MCP tools use this form. `anyOf` schemas (`Optional[int]`) don't crash, but they fall back to `"string"`, so `5` comes back as `"5"`. 2. **The model emits a number that overflows, e.g. `1e400`.** `int(float("1e400"))` raises `OverflowError`, which is not in the `except` tuple. The call is lost the same way. 3. **One streaming chunk contains more than one complete `<tool_call>` block** (MTP, `--stream-interval > 1`, parallel tool calls). `parse_streaming_increment` handles only the first block. The rest stays in the buffer and is lost if no further chunk arrives. MiMo doesn't override `finish()`, so nothing flushes it at stream end. Repro (CPU only): ```python from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.mimo_detector import MiMoDetector tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="search", parameters={ "type": "object", "properties": {"site": {"type": ["string", "null"]}}}))] text = "<tool_call>
<function=search>
<parameter=site>github.com</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>" MiMoDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools) # AttributeError: 'list

title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Rebuild derived weights in place on weight updates
summary: ## Motivation Fixes the CUDA graph address drift issue during RL weight updates for Kimi-K3 and related models. During online weight updates (e.g., RL training), derived tensors (like `w_kc`, `w_vc`, `_bfa_w`, `_front_w`) were re-allocated with new memory addresses. Because these tensors are captured by CUDA graphs, the graphs continued reading stale data from the old addresses, leading to severe accuracy crashes. This PR implements the RFC guideline (in-place updates for graph-visible derived state) to fix this. ## Modifications 1. **`attn_residual.py`**: Extracted the cache product calculation into `_cw_product` and added `refresh_cw`. This uses `bind_or_assign` to safely update both `bf16` and `fp32` caches in-place during weight loads. 2. **`kimi_k3.py`**: - Replaced direct assignments with `bind_or_assign` for derived tensors (`w_kc`, `w_vc`, `_bfa_w`, `_bfa_f_b_w`) in `post_load_weights` and `_merge_bfa_weights`. - Added early returns in `_merge_front_weights` and `_merge_bfa_weights` to skip redundant `torch.cat` for view-based merges. - Updated `_prepare_fused_decode` to refresh the tuple of tensors in-place. - Stripped `nn.Parameter` to `.data` for `_bfa_f_b_w` to avoid hidden address rebindings. 3. **`kimi_linear.py`, `kimi_k25_eagle3.py`, `minicpm3.py`**: Applied the same `bind_or_assign` fix for `w_kc` / `w_vc` to keep the Kimi family consistent. 4. **Test Added**: Added `test/registered/e2e/rl/test_kimi_k3_weight_update.py` to assert that all derived tensors maintain their `data_ptr()` and correct values after bucketed weight updates. ## Accuracy Tests - **Loca

title: [Feat] moe: hot-replace fixed-capacity Qwen4 experts through native Engine
summary: ## Motivation A native Engine started with a physical expert profile should be able to change the retained expert set between requests without restarting its workers or reallocating its expert slots. This draft adds fixed-capacity replacement from the original BF16 checkpoint. Depends on #48694. The branch includes that startup-profile implementation until the dependency lands. Compatible metadata and cached dispatch views update in place. Expert tensor shapes/addresses stay fixed. A failed write restores the original rows/maps. summary: An existing MoE checkpoint can be served with a calibrated subset of routed experts by passing `--moe-expert-profile`. The model allocates weights only for retained physical slots, while its router keeps the original logical expert IDs. This lets deployments evaluate and use different expert profiles without rewriting a checkpoint for each profile. For example, given a model with eight routed experts per layer, this profile stores four experts per layer and preserves the specified slot order: ```json {"num_experts": 8, "keep": [[7, 1, 5, 3], [6, 2, 4, 0]]} ``` ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path MODEL_PATH \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --moe-runner-backend triton \ --moe-expert-profile profile.json ``` The resolver validates the profile against the model before workers start and serializes its contents into the resolved configuration. Each router masks absent logical experts before its existing Top-K selection. Existing expert-location metadata maps retained logical IDs to compact physical slots, and the weight loader skips experts with no slot. The token Top-K and routing normalization stay as configured by the model. Physical weight allocation uses the retained count. Shared experts execute separately. The first implementation accepts unquantized BF16 Qwen3-MoE and Qwen4Exp checkpoints with Triton MoE and no expert parallelism or A2A. summary: ## Motivation In multi-turn multimodal agent conversations, historical images are often resubmitted with the conversation context on each turn. summary: ## Environment sgl-router v0.2.4 (`sgl_model_gateway`), PD disaggregation mode (`--pd-disaggregation`, 1 prefill + 1 decode), sglang main nightly `b94ac87e`. ## Symptom After a burst of client-side timeouts/aborts (e.g. a benchmark tool cancelling slow requests, or a genuine transient hang on the workers), the router's circuit breaker for the **prefill** worker opens. From then on, for `/v1/chat/completions`: - the request is still dispatched to the **decode** worker (bootstrap room gets allocated, decode waits for KV), - but is **never dispatched to prefill** (no POST ever reaches it), - so decode waits for KV that will never arrive; the client times out; decode logs `KVTransferError(...): Aborted by AbortReq` — which feeds the breaker again. The result is a stable "fake dead" state that looks exactly like a KV-transfer failure on the workers (we spent hours chasing mooncake before finding `Circuit breaker state transition: open -> half_open` in router logs with no subsequent `-> closed`). `docker restart` of the router instantly fixes everything. ## Expected behavior When the prefill leg is broken open, the router should fail the request fast (503) rather than half-dispatching it to decode. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. When this pool evicts the trailing SWA pages while the FULL prefix survives, the prefix cannot be reused directly and may fall back to cold prefill. title: [HiCache] Feed existence beliefs only for the storage-written prefix
summary: ## Motivation When a buffer-mode storage backup fails partway (`_page_backup` hits a `batch_set` failure and `break`s), `finish_storage_write_ack` still marks the **entire** snapshot as present in L3 — including pages the backend never wrote. Those pages get a stale-positive existence belief with no self-heal: `covers_all` skips their re-write forever, and recompute re-stages the same content hashes the belief already covers, so they are recomputed on every access. Unlike a normal stale positive (bounded to "one cold recompute" per the `StorageExistenceCache` docstring), the data never reached L3, so the belief never heals. Trigger is production-common (connection blip, disk full, network error) and silent (warning only). Affects the buffer-mode backup ack path that the sidecar-borrow paths from #37424 flow through. ## Modifications - `pipeline.py` `finish_storage_write_ack`: add a `successful_tokens` param and feed beliefs only for `hash_values[:successful_tokens // page_size]` — the prefix the write actually persisted. `None` keeps full-span behavior. - `unified_radix_cache.py` `_drain_backup`: all-reduce `completed_tokens` (`MIN`) on the rank-synced drain so every rank feeds identical (pessimistic) beliefs — preserving the original TP-determinism intent. Mirrors the existing `_reduce_prefetch_ack` pattern. The detach/shutdown local drain (`n_backup is None`) passes `None` (beliefs cleared on that path). No change on the happy path (all pages written → full span). ## Accuracy Tests N/A — cache bookkeeping change, does not affect model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [HiSparse] Support dynamic hisparse to reduce small-batch swap overhead
summary: ## Summary This PR adds dynamic HiSparse residency to avoid unnecessary performance regression in small-batch decode. Before this change, once a request entered HiSparse, its KV cache was backed up to host and the device-side KV was still cut down to `device_buffer_size`. This static behavior is useful when HBM is under pressure, but it is too aggressive for small batches. In small-batch scenarios, there is often enough spare HBM to keep the full device KV resident, so forcing every HiSparse request into the shortened device-buffer mode makes decode unnecessarily slower. With dynamic HiSparse, a request still gets host backup after entering HiSparse, but its full device KV is preserved by default. Only when the device KV allocator is under pressure do we demote resident requests to the traditional HiSparse swap mode and shrink their device cache to `device_buffer_size`.This keeps the memory-saving behavior of HiSparse for large batches, while avoiding the small-batch regression when HBM capacity is still available. Regarding the CUDA Graph, since it was unclear at what batch size HBM space insufficiency would occur, a dual-path CUDA Graph strategy was adopted. ## Benefits Single-node benchmark, 8K input / 128 output: | Mode | TPOT | TPOT excl. first ITL | |---|---:|---:| | no HiSparse | 28.41 ms | 24.29 ms | | Static HiSparse | 39.68 ms | 31.99 ms | | Dynamic HiSparse | 30.74 ms | 25.01 ms | Dynamic HiSparse recovers **8.95 ms** TPOT over static HiSparse, about **79.4%** of the static-to-native gap. summary: Stacked on #44884; this PR contains only the exact comparison-rank lookup follow-up. ## Motivation The fused greedy-verification logits reduction still computes FP32 softcap for every vocabulary element. BF16 has only 65,536 bit patterns, so build exact comparison ranks through the existing native FP32 softcap once and reduce those ranks instead. summary: ## Motivation The current implementation stores a SWA cache for each page in the L3. This leads to high memory consumption in L3. title: [Hicache]Fix non-blocking HiCache storage prefetch misses
summary: ## Motivation HiCache storage prefetch currently registers a request as an ongoing prefetch before the storage hit query finishes. In L3-miss-dominated workloads, this can make the scheduler wait on storage prefetch progress even when there is no data to load from storage. This is especially visible on Qwen3.5 workloads with Mamba sidecar pools, because the old path may allocate host KV/Mamba buffers before knowing whether storage has matching pages. When the storage query misses, those buffers are immediately released, adding unnecessary resource churn and TTFT tail latency. ## Modifications - Add `ack_prefetch_queue` to separate storage hit query completion from actual prefetch transfer enqueueing. - Track storage-hit queries in `pending_prefetch` instead of `ongoing_prefetch`. - Do not allocate host KV or Mamba buffers during the storage query phase. - Promote a pending query to `ongoing_prefetch` only after storage reports enough hit pages. - Let the scheduler continue immediately for pending storage queries. If the request no longer needs prefetch, mark the query terminated and revoke it. - Keep the actual storage prefetch transfer path unchanged for real storage hits. ## Accuracy Tests N/A. This PR only changes HiCache storage prefetch scheduling and resource allocation behavior. It does not modify model forward computation or output semantics. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on a Qwen3.5 workload where L1/L2 cache covers most hits and L3 storage queries are miss-dominated. title: [HiCache]handle TP-replicated hybrid cache backups per pool
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A hybrid model may use multiple cache pools with different tensor-parallel backup requirements. A concrete example is Ling-2.6-flash, which adopts a 1:7 hybrid architecture combining MLA and Lightning Linear Attention. In SGLang, the MLA layers use an MLA KV pool, while the recurrent states of the linear-attention layers are managed through a Mamba pool. These two pools have different TP semantics: - The MLA KV cache is replicated across TP ranks, so only TP rank 0 needs to back it up. - The Mamba pool contains rank-local linear-attention states, so every TP rank must back it up. Both pools are managed by the same HybridCacheController. However, the existing controller-level backup_skip applies to the entire backup operation and cannot distinguish between them. For Ling-2.6-flash, enabling backup_skip for the MLA pool also skips the Mamba pool on non-zero TP ranks, causing rank-local linear-attention states to be missed. Disabling it causes every TP rank to write the replicated MLA cache, introducing redundant storage writes. title: [Bugfix] Do not finish on grammar termination when ignore_eos is set
summary: ## What changes Constrained requests sent with `ignore_eos=true` no longer stop when their grammar terminates. Before this change they finished at the grammar's stop token (usually an EOS token) instead of running to `max_new_tokens`; after it, decoding continues unconstrained until `max_new_tokens` or a stop string, the same as for EOS and stop tokens. Requests without `ignore_eos` are unchanged. ## Problem `Req.update_finish_state` finishes a request as soon as its grammar is terminated, without checking `ignore_eos`: ```python if self.grammar is not None and self.grammar.is_terminated(): self.finished_reason = FINISH_MATCHED_TOKEN(matched=self.output_ids[-1]) return ``` The token-based check just above it (`_check_token_based_finish`) returns early under `ignore_eos`, but this grammar check does not. summary: ## Motivation SGLang publishes scheduler KV usage periodically during decode. title: [PP] Carry TP-sharded flag in proxy-tensor metadata to fix #30015
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #30015. When a model runs with both pipeline parallelism (`pp>1`) and tensor parallelism (`tp>1`), `GroupCoordinator.send_tensor_dict` applies its send-slice + all-gather-on-receive optimization to **every** tensor in the proxy dict. That optimization is only lossless for tensors that are **replicated** across the all-gather (attention-TP) group: each rank's `1/tp` slice is then a genuine piece of the whole. For a **TP-sharded** tensor each rank holds *different* data, so the receiver reassembles slices from different ranks into a wrong-but-plausible tensor. No error is raised — the output is just silently wrong. Every in-tree transformer only puts replicated tensors (`hidden_states`, `residual`) into `PPProxyTensors`, which is why this has stayed latent. It bites linear/recurrent models that must carry a per-rank activation across a stage boundary: in the RWKV-7 case that surfaced it, layer 0's `v_first` (a per-head-group shard) came out byte-identical-but-wrong on the receiving stage, and greedy decoding diverged deterministically at a fixed token (repro + analysis in #30015). This is the same root cause #30058 addresses; this PR is an alternative that I think is a little more robust and also wires it through end to end (see below). ## Modifications The transfer needs to know which proxy keys are sharded (send whole) vs replicated (safe to slice/all-gather). title: [Fix] HiCache: reclaim redundant host mirrors after storage backup (write_through host-pool starvation)
summary: ## Motivation Under `--hicache-write-policy write_through` with a storage backend (`--hicache-storage-backend mooncake` etc.), the host (L2) pool deadlocks whenever it is smaller than the device pool, silently starving the storage tier. Three code facts combine into this: 1. **Every inserted node immediately pins a host mirror** — `write_backup()` allocates host slots for every node that enters the device radix cache (threshold 1 under `write_through`). 2. **The backup ack never frees the slot** — `_drain_backup()` only calls `entry.release_host()`, which decrements `host_ref_counter`; the memory stays attached to `node.host_value`. 3. **The only reclaimer refuses device-resident nodes** — `evict_host()` guards with `if not x.evicted: continue`, so a mirror can only be reclaimed after the *device* copy is evicted. The in-band rescue inside `write_backup()` (`evict_host` then retry) is a no-op for the same reason. Under sustained load the device pool stays full, so pinned-mirror demand approaches the full device pool size. With `hicache_size` below device KV capacity the host pool fills with irreclaimable mirrors, and **both** staging (`hicache_write_rejected_tokens_total{reason="host_alloc_failed"}`) and storage prefetch (same reason, `stage="storage_prefetch"`) are rejected wholesale — storage starves in both directions. The default `hicache_ratio 2.0` hides the bug by capping mirror demand at half the pool, at the cost of a device-pool-sized slice of host DRAM that is permanently pinned and never reused. title: [Kernel] Skip invalid-index stores in DeepSeek-V4 fused KV cache store kernels
summary: ## Motivation `fused_store_flashmla_cache` and `fused_store_indexer_cache` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/store.cuh` compute `page = index >> kPageBits` and store unconditionally. The kernel's own comment says "always load the value from input (don't store if invalid)" — but the *don't store* half was never implemented, and unlike the generic pool kernel these kernels have no bounds check at all. Invalid indices can reach these kernels through two documented paths: 1. **CUDA-graph padding rows carry `out_cache_loc = 0`** — the pool's reserved slot. `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.clear()` starts free pages at 1, and the SWA page LUT maps 0 → 0, precisely so that padding writes have a harmless sink. But that only holds if nothing *reads* slot 0 back: the fused kernels silently store undefined padding K/V into it, and page-table padding points partially-valid tiles at the same page, so the garbage is read back before masking. 2. **The SWA page LUT deliberately ends with a live `-1` ("no page") entry.** Unguarded, `page` goes negative and the store becomes an out-of-bounds write *before* the cache base — silent memory corruption of whatever tensor happens to precede the pool. This is the same defect class as #32477 (merged), which added the reserved-index skip to the generic `store_cache` kernel. ## Modifications Both kernels now compute `const bool store_valid = index > 0;` and wrap only the final stores in it: - The guard wraps the stores instead of early-returning, so `PDLTriggerSecondary` still fires for every block/warp and the `warp::reduce_max` reductions s

title: [DLLM] Add GFusion and EBSampling
summary: ## Motivation This PR adds support for a new diffusion LLM (dLLM) model and a new dLLM decoding algorithm. **GFusion** (`ai-sage/GFusion-10B-A1.8B`) is a Mixture-of-Experts diffusion language model built on the DeepSeek-V3 **MLA** architecture (10B total / 1.8B active parameters). Since it reuses DeepSeek-V3's MLA blocks and weight layout, the model itself is a thin subclass. The real change is adapting the MLA attention backends to run the DLLM_EXTEND (bidirectional block-decode) forward mode. **EBSampling** (entropy-bounded sampling) is a new, model-agnostic dLLM decoding algorithm. Instead of revealing tokens whose confidence exceeds a fixed threshold (as `LowConfidence` does), it reveals the lowest-entropy masked token in each block and then keeps revealing tokens while the running cumulative-entropy prefix stays within a budget `gamma`. This lets it commit more tokens per forward pass at matched output quality. ## Modifications **New model** — `models/gfusion.py`: `GFusionForDiffusionLM`, a `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` subclass that reuses MLA, only flipping attention to `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` and setting `return_full_logits=True`. `dllm/config.py` registers the GFusion arch defaults (`block_size=32`, `mask_id=128170`). **New dLLM algorithm** — `dllm/algorithm/eb_sampling.py`: `EBSampling` suppresses the mask token before argmax/entropy, then reveals the prefix of lowest-entropy masked tokens whose cumulative entropy stays within `gamma` (vectorized, `gamma=0.15` default). **`DLLM_EXTEND` for the MLA attention backends** — previously only flashinfer handled dLLM exten

title: [CI] [AMD] nightly-disagg: Install the checkout's runtime deps over the image
summary: ## What The MI355X disagg launcher now installs the checked-out sglang together with its torch-free runtime deps (`sglang[runtime_base]`). Previously it used `--no-deps`. ## Why The nightly overlays main's source on the newest published image. With `--no-deps`, a runtime dependency added to main after the image was built never gets installed. #47120 (merged 11-04 12:48 UTC) added a hard `import blake3` in `srt/multimodal/cache/digest.py`. The 11-05 nightly ran on image `v0.5.23-rocm10-mi35x-20261104`, which predates that change, and all 35 jobs died at server startup with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'blake3'`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41966044506 A newer image clears this particular failure. The same failure returns whenever a dependency lands between an image build and the next nightly. ## Notes for the reviewer - `runtime_base` is the torch-free subset in `pyproject_other.toml`. pip's default `only-if-needed` strategy leaves satisfied packages alone, so the image's torch, aiter and other ROCm builds are untouched. Only missing packages, or ones whose pin moved on main, get installed. - One side effect: when main bumps a pin in `runtime_base` (e.g. `transformers==`), the run now uses main's version rather than the image's. title: [Fix] rust-server: bound and fail fast rust warmup
summary: Follow-up to #43004 addressing its review. - **Bound the warmup inside `warm_up`** ([review](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43004#discussion_r4213344109)). `warm_up` now takes a `timeout` that covers admission and the whole response stream, like `probe_health(timeout)`. The caller still resolves `SGLANG_WARMUP_TIMEOUT` (default 600 s, 1800 s for PD). title: [Perf] qsa: 64 CTAs per row for the mid-batch indexer decode
summary: ## Motivation `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode` (the QSA indexer's decode scoring) launches a fixed number of CTAs per query row. A row's CTAs stride over its 64-key groups, so each CTA scores about `groups / ctas` of them back to back. `_decode_ctas_per_row` picks the count for about four waves: - 256 CTAs per row below `4 * SMs / 16` rows; - 16 between `4 * SMs / 16` and `4 * SMs` rows; - 1 above. On a 152-SM GPU the middle level covers 38-607 rows, which is the usual batch range for long-context decode and MTP verify. There, 16 CTAs per row leave each CTA a long serial walk at long contexts. With an 85K context, one CTA scores about 20 groups in sequence. The grid is large enough, but each CTA's serial work dominates. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/mqa.py`: `_decode_ctas_per_row` keeps the row thresholds and the 256 / 1 levels and raises the middle level from 16 to 64. The levels stay three values, so the number of TileLang specializations is unchanged. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa_indexer.py`: - `test_decode_ctas_per_row_by_row_count` pins the rule on a 152-SM device; - `test_tilelang_mqa_decode_ctas_per_row_bitwise` (bf16 and fp8 cache) checks that the logits are bit-identical at every level. title: [Fix] scheduler: Do not request input logprobs again when re-prefilling a retracted request
summary: ## Motivation A retracted request asks its re-prefill for input logprobs it already has. A `return_logprob=True` request without `logprob_start_len` (output logprobs only, the default RL rollout shape) gets `logprob_start_len = len(origin_input_ids)` at intake, so its first prefill scores no input positions. When the request is retracted (KV pool full in `retract_decode`, or `pause_generation(mode="retract")` during a weight sync), it re-prefills prompt + generated tokens. `logprob_start_len` still points at the prompt end, so `compute_extend_logprob_start_len` asks for input logprobs over every generated token: - The logits processor computes full-vocab logits for those rows (`extend_return_logprob` becomes True). - Their target ids are padding (0), because `extend_input_logprob_token_ids` reads only `origin_input_ids`. - `add_input_logprob_return_values` then drops them ("The input logprob has been already computed. It only happens upon retract."). The output logprobs already returned stay on the req and are never recomputed. So the work is pure waste, and it grows with response length (e.g. ~3.5k generated tokens × vocab per retracted RL sample). On a backend that cannot serve input logprobs, the request is fatal: on sglang-torchtpu the compiled forward rejects it, and every retraction under `return_logprob` traffic killed the engine (fixed there in sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1836). ## Modifications - `compute_extend_logprob_start_len` takes `input_logprobs_finalized`.
