title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qsa: JIT CUDA kernel for the indexer decode scoring
summary: ## Motivation The QSA indexer of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4_exp`) scores every compressed key of every decode and verify row once per layer (`qsa_mqa_decode`). On long contexts this decode scoring is memory-bound: each row streams its request's compressed keys, and the TileLang kernel reloads them for every row and synchronizes the CTA several times per 64-key group. This PR adds a JIT CUDA kernel that writes **the same logits, bit for bit**, but moves the data more efficiently. Model outputs do not change. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/attention/qsa_mqa_decode.cuh` (new, JIT): every logit runs the instructions the TileLang decode kernel emits, in the same order (`mma.sync.m16n8k16` bf16→fp32 over head_dim 128 in ascending k, `max(·, 0)`, the same head-sum order, division by the scale under fast math). Only the data movement changes: - the query rows that share a page-table row are staged in shared memory once per CTA; - each CTA strides over many 64-key groups of its request with double-buffered `cp.async` page gathers; - verify rows of one request (`rows_per_request`) reuse one load of each key group, and a group needs two CTA barriers instead of one per row plus one. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/qsa_mqa_decode.py` (new): the JIT loader and `qsa_mqa_decode_logits`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/mqa.py`: - `cuda_qsa_mqa_decode` (same signature and logits contract as `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode`) and `use_cuda_qsa_mqa_decode` (coverage check); - `qsa_mqa_decode` tries the CUDA kernel first. It covers bf16 scoring with at most 8 query

title: [Bug] FP8 KV cache scales are silently dropped when loading Qwen3-MoE / Qwen2 / Mixtral and every layer falls back to scale 1.0
summary: ## Describe the bug When a checkpoint carries FP8 KV cache scales as tensors, the hand-written weight loaders of `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, and `MixtralForCausalLM` drop them. `process_weights_after_loading` then sees both scales still at their initial -1.0 and resets them to 1.0. ```python # python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py, current main elif layer.k_scale <= 0.0 and layer.v_scale <= 0.0: # If no scales were loaded (both scales are invalid non-positive # values), use the default value of 1.0 k_scale = 1.0 v_scale = 1.0 ``` Every attention layer therefore dequantizes its FP8 cache with a unit scale, and the per-layer error equals the calibrated scale. Outputs stay finite, nothing is raised, and the error is invisible to tensor-level checks. Three scale namings are affected. llm-compressor stores the scales under the fused projection name, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale` (the layout reported in vllm-project/vllm#25047). ModelOpt stores them per projection, for example `model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale`. The deprecated single `.kv_scale` tensor is lost as well, while the model registers the scales at `self_attn.attn.k_scale` and `self_attn.attn.v_scale`. ### Mechanism The loaders run their `stacked_params_mapping` loop before the params lookup, and the mapping is a substring replace. ```python # python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py, current main for param_name, weight_name, shard_id in stacked_params_mapping: # 1186 if weight_name not in name: continue ... name = name.replace(weight_name, param_name) # 1198 ...

title: [Fix] attention: do not apply KV-cache scales to a BF16 KV cache in FlashInfer and Triton
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48747. A checkpoint's KV-cache scales stay on the attention layer whatever the KV cache dtype is. The KV pool divides K/V by them only when it casts them to another dtype, so a BF16 cache holds them unscaled. FlashInfer and Triton still applied the scales when reading the cache, so attention over a BF16 cache used K and V multiplied by the calibration scales and decoding produced garbage. This happens with `--kv-cache-dtype bf16`, and with the default `auto` for `quant_method: fp8` checkpoints with `kv_cache_scheme: "static"` and for Quark checkpoints with a `kv_cache_group`: `auto` gives them a BF16 cache while their scales are still loaded. FlashInfer is the default MHA backend on Ampere, Ada and SM120 GPUs, so these checkpoints give wrong output there with default flags. ## Modifications - `flashinfer_backend.py`: a `_kv_read_scales` helper passes `k_scale` / `v_scale` to the paged prefill and decode wrappers only when the cache dtype differs from the query dtype, which mirrors the pool's write. It replaces the three direct uses of `layer.k_scale_float` / `layer.v_scale_float`. - `triton_backend.py`: a `_kv_descales` helper returns `1.0, 1.0` for a cache in the query dtype and replaces the four copies of the descale selection. Triton's MLA path divides K by its scale itself before storing it, so MLA keeps the scales. - An FP8 cache is unchanged in both backends. trtllm_mha, aiter, flashmla and trtllm_mla already apply the scales only to an FP8 cache, and FA3 gives the right output with a BF16 cache in the runs below, so those backends are not touched

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Publish a yielded optimistic prefill's KV under a write-through cache
summary: ## Motivation An optimistic prefill request yields when its prefill finishes before its decode peer has bootstrapped: the scheduler releases its KV and requeues it for a retry. `optimistic_release_and_requeue` checkpoints the KV the request computed into the radix tree before the release, so the retry matches that prefix instead of recomputing it. Under a write-through HiCache that checkpoint was skipped. Pending-bootstrap KV is kept request-owned under write-through (#38978) so that the decode bootstrap path never waits on a host/L3 backup, and the release path inherited the same condition. A yielded request has no bootstrap to delay, though, so skipping the checkpoint only dropped everything it had computed beyond its already published prefix: once the device copy was evicted, the retry recomputed the whole prompt. ## Modifications - `optimistic_release_and_requeue` now checkpoints the request's KV into the tree unconditionally before releasing it. Under write-through the insert backs the KV up, the released slots become evictable tree pages, and the retry's storage baseline (`storage_prefetch_last_match_len`) covers the whole computed prefix, so an evicted prefix is looked up in L3 once before it is recomputed. - Only the write-through branch changes; the non-write-through path already checkpointed. Mamba caches are unaffected: write-through optimistic prefill does not run with them (`advance_unpublished_req` asserts no Mamba). The extra work per yield is the write-through backup of KV that a bootstrapped request would back up anyway. - New unit test `TestOptimisticPrefi

title: [Perf] eager-runner: size the input registry by the prefill limit
summary: ## Motivation The `EagerRunner` builds one fixed-size input registry at startup. Its token-axis slots (`input_ids`, `positions`, `out_cache_loc` int64 and `mrope_positions` 3 x int64: 48 bytes per token) are sized to `max(max_total_num_tokens, chunked_prefill_size)`, the whole KV pool. An eager pass carries one prefill batch, bounded by the chunk / `max_prefill_tokens`, or a decode-shaped batch, so almost all of that memory is never written. The waste scales with the KV pool: a small model on a large GPU has a multi-million-token pool and wastes hundreds of MB of device memory that activations and CUDA graphs could use. ## Modifications - `model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py`: - The registry is sized by the prefill limit: `max(chunked_prefill_size (or the PP dynamic-chunking ceiling), min(max_total_num_tokens, max_prefill_tokens), max_bs * tokens_per_req)`. It is never larger than before. - `load_batch` regrows it when a batch is larger (e.g. chunked prefill disabled and a long prompt). The regrown registry is the next power of two, capped at the old pool-based size, and is built outside the process-wide input-buffer pool. The first regrow does not free the startup registry: it stays in that pool, whose slots the CUDA-graph runners share. Each later regrow frees the previous regrown registry. - `model_executor/cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py`: `build_eager_registry(share_pool=...)` (default `True`, unchanged for every existing caller). - Test: `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_eager_runner_input_registry.py` (CPU) covers four cases: - a large pool does not si

title: [Refactor] scheduler: Release retracted, paused and chunked-aborted requests through RequestRetirer
summary: Retraction (decode memory pressure and pause in retract mode) and the pending chunked-prefill abort released their requests by hand: `ScheduleBatch.release_req` backed up and freed the KV itself, and the requests a retraction could not requeue were only sent an abort, with no cache-side cleanup. They now go through `RequestRetirer`, on top of the `abort` / `release` API of the previous PR. - Add `RequestRetirer.retract(req, *, offload_kv)`: releases a request a retraction requeues, without checkpointing it: HiSparse rows, then the KV backup where the KV is restored rather than recomputed (PD decode), then KV and mamba state. Returns whether the request can be resumed. `ScheduleBatch.release_req`, `retract_decode`, `retract_all` and `PrefillAdder` take the retirer instead of the pools and the HiSparse coordinator. - Add `RequestRetirer.abort_retracted(req, *, reason)`: ends a request a retraction released but cannot requeue, and tells the tokenizer once. It detaches the request (multimodal inputs, streaming session, uOCR), abandons its cache attempt and retires its beam group. It does not finish the request in place, since a step launched before the retraction may still carry it. `retract_decode`'s unrequeueable requests and the pause-retract unresumable requests use it. - The pending chunked-prefill abort ends the request through `abort` (after stopping the PD prefill sender), instead of a `release` plus a separate abort send. - The allowlist of direct `release_kv_cache` / `_detach` callers in `test_request_retirer.py` drops `ScheduleBatch.release_req`. title: [Perf] deepseek_v4: call the current DeepGEMM paged MQA API for DSv4.1 decode
summary: ## Motivation #48424 bumped sgl-deep-gemm to 0.2.6. In 0.2.6 the SM100 paged MQA API is varlen-only. The DSv4.1 low-ratio (c1/c2) indexers still called it with the 0.2.3 signature (positional `clean_logits` + `logits_dtype`) and built the schedule without `indices`, so DeepGEMM's shim routed every decode call to the frozen legacy kernel. In the DSv4.1 decode benchmark on VR that made paged MQA logits +20% per call at bs64 and +30% at bs256 against the Oct 30 stack. ## Modifications - `PagedIndexerMetadata` builds the varlen schedule (one row per token, per-row lengths, request ids as `indices`) on SM100 with bf16 index weights and at least 96 query rows. Below that the legacy kernel stays: it is faster at bs8-16. - `paged_logits_args` passes the per-row layout and `indices` to `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`. The schedule is per chunk when the forward is row-chunked. - The c4 indexer, sglang's JIT schedule and non-SM100 keep the legacy call. summary: issue:https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39700 base pr: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40179 ## Summary DeepSeek V4.1 consumer layers can share the same compressed KV storage, but sparse prefill currently dequantizes that storage into a BF16 workspace on every layer. Reuse the dequantized compressed KV within a forward to avoid repeated reads, dequantization, and workspace writes. ## Changes - Limit reuse to CP sparse BF16 prefill with compression ratios 1 and 2. - Keep separate workspaces per compression ratio. - Track validity by source layer and workspace address within the per-forward gather cache. - Refresh on producer execution, source changes, workspace reallocation, or a new forward. - Continue updating SWA and top-k inputs for every layer. title: [Refactor] scheduler: Release every PD disaggregation exit through RequestRetirer
summary: PD disaggregation exits (prefill transfer success and failure, aborted prefill results, bootstrap failures, and the decode transfer, deferred-release, prealloc-failure and checksum-mismatch paths) each released their request by hand, with different subsets of the cleanup steps. They now go through `RequestRetirer`, whose API is cut to two verbs, split by who reports the request: - `abort(req)` (was `abort_queued`): ends a request no launched step carries, tells the tokenizer once, and ends in `release`. - `release(req, *, checkpoint)`: gives back what an ended request holds; the caller finishes and streams it. An aborted request is first detached: its multimodal inputs, its streaming-session in-flight flag and its uOCR reuse state are dropped, its cache attempt is abandoned unless the KV is checkpointed (the cache's store then settles it, as on a normal finish), and its beam group leaves the live set. Then its KV backup, HiSparse rows, KV and mamba state go. It replaces `release_finished`, `release_aborted` and the separate free step. The detach (was `release_aborted_request`) is now the retirer's private `_detach`, run only inside `release`: an aborted request cannot be released without being detached, and no caller detaches on its own. A logical abort only marks the request; the exit that releases it detaches it. - Add `release_prefill_sender(req, *, abort_sender)` on the prefill mixin (replacing `release_aborted_prefill_waiting_req`): clears the pending chunk send, optionally aborts the sender (best effort, logged on failure), frees the metadata buffer and clears `pendin

title: Add Agentic-Aware Tail-Optimized LRU eviction to the unified radix cache
summary: ## Motivation Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU, [NeurIPS 25](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15152)) keeps only as much of a conversation cached as its next prefill needs to stay under a TTFT SLO budget, and frees the rest of the tail before falling back to recency order, so newer requests can be admitted. On agentic traces the tail is what a plain LRU protects at the expense of every other conversation's tail latency by up to 43%. The policy is opt-in and off by default; `lru` remains the default and its code path is unchanged. ## Modifications ``` --radix-eviction-policy tlru --tlru-threshold N # xi, in tokens --tlru-next-prompt-estimate M # Q_hat, in tokens ``` Concretely: a conversation or agentic turn with history length `L` whose next prompt is expected to add `Q_hat` tokens only needs `L + Q_hat - xi` tokens resident to keep its next prefill inside a TTFT budget `xi`. Everything past that point is "TEL-safe" — evicting it cannot worsen tail latency, because the recompute it causes still fits the budget. T-LRU frees those tokens first (phase 1) and continues in plain recency order once they run out (phase 2). Implemented as a priority function rather than a second eviction pass: a TEL-safe node reports as infinitely old, so the existing device and host eviction drivers produce both of the paper's phases unchanged. ```python budget = max(node.convo_length + self.next_prompt_estimate - self.threshold, 0) cached_without_this_node = node.depth -

title: [Fix] speculative: Reject grammar requests with DSpark and TP>1 to prevent deadlock
summary: Fixes #41449 ### Description When running with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and Tensor Parallelism (`tp_size > 1`), batching a grammar-constrained request currently causes a silent multi-GPU deadlock. This occurs because grammar-masked verification diverges across ranks, leaving mismatched collective sizes that cause the GPUs to spin indefinitely. This PR implements the suggested fail-fast workaround by rejecting grammar requests at the `TokenizerManager` level if DSpark and TP > 1 are both active. Instead of hanging the entire cluster, the server will now immediately throw a clean `ValueError` HTTP 400 back to the client, preserving cluster availability while maintaining full throughput for non-grammar requests. title: [Fix] openai: Report the raw byte for SentencePiece byte-fallback pieces in chat logprobs
summary: ## Motivation #38604 made Chat logprob `bytes` lossless for byte-level BPE tokenizers by recovering bytes from the token id. It deliberately left SentencePiece tokenizers (Gemma, Mistral, ...) on the display-text fallback, so that `é` is not turned into `[233]`. That fallback is wrong for one kind of SentencePiece token: **byte-fallback pieces** `<0x00>`..`<0xFF>`. A tokenizer with `byte_fallback` uses them for any character that is missing from its vocab, one piece per UTF-8 byte. The ASCII pieces `<0x00>`..`<0x7F>` decode to their own character and already report the right byte. A non-ASCII piece `<0x80>`..`<0xFF>`, decoded on its own, is U+FFFD, so today each such token reports `bytes=[239, 191, 189]`, and so does every `top_logprobs` entry that is one. Clients that rebuild text from `bytes` (as the OpenAI API intends) get `���` instead of the character. Repro on main e838360ffd with the `unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-NVFP4` tokenizer (`GemmaTokenizer`, not byte-level). This is CPU-only and calls `OpenAIServingChat._build_token_logprobs_from_raw` on the engine-style `(logprob, id, tokenizer.decode([id]))` triples: | text | pieces | `bytes` before | `bytes` after | |---|---|---|---| | `ฃ` (U+0E03) | `<0xE0><0xB8><0x83>` | `[239,191,189]` x3 | `[224] [184] [131]` | | `ฦ` (U+0E26) | `<0xE0><0xB8><0xA6>` | `[239,191,189]` x3 | `[224] [184] [166]` | | `🫨` (U+1FAE8) | `<0xF0><0x9F><0xAB><0xA8>` | `[239,191,189]` x4 | `[240] [159] [171] [168]` | | `𠮷` (U+20BB7) | `<0xF0><0xA0><0xAE><0xB7>` | `[239,191,189]` x4 | `[240] [160] [174] [183]` | | `ไทย é` | `ไทย`, `▁é` | `[224,185,132,...]`

title: [Fix] spec: sample from the target when the rejection residual is empty in TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #42528. `TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly` draws coins from `[0, 1)` and, after rejecting a draft, samples the bonus/replacement token from the residual `relu(target - draft)`. The residual can be **empty**: every token the target gives mass to was a rejected draft (the kernel copies `target` into `draft` for each rejected token, so `q - p == 0` there). The easiest way to hit this in practice is a renormalized one-token nucleus (`top_k` + `top_p`): its probability is `1 - 2^-24`, not `1.0`, and `torch.rand` returns exactly `1 - 2^-24` with probability `2^-24`. The half-open CDF test (`coin < prob_acc`, #35798) then rejects the only token with target mass, `sum(relu(q - p)) == 0`, `u == 0`, no bucket is ever selected and the fallback emits token id `d - 1` — a token with zero target probability. With MTP on a 248k vocabulary this shows up as a rare garbage token (id `vocab_size - 1`) in the middle of a generation. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh` (shared device header, so the CUDA/ROCm JIT launchers and the MUSA AOT build all pick it up): also accumulate `sum(q)` in the first pass; when `sum(relu(q - p))` is not `> 0`, sample from the target distribution itself (`u = coin * sum(q)`, buckets from `q`). The acceptance test is unchanged, so #35798's semantics (half-open CDF, no zero-mass drafts) are preserved. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`: add `upper-endpoint-empty-residual` — target `[0, 1 - 2^-24, 0]`, draft token 1, coin `1 - 2^-24`: the draft is rejecte

title: [Fix] diffusion/realtime: Close the connection with 1011 when generation fails
summary: ## Motivation When the realtime generate loop fails, the client cannot tell the failure from a dropped network connection. `_generate_loop` reports the failure with an `error` message and stops. `generate()` then closes the socket only when the session reached `max_chunks`. Otherwise it returns without a close frame, and the client sees an abnormal closure (1006). #48345 noted this and left it out of scope. Measured over a real socket (uvicorn + a `websockets` client). The generate loop is replaced by one that sends a chunk, then reports `error during generate loop: scheduler failed` and stops, as the real loop does on a scheduler error: | | Client receives | Close | |---|---|---| | `main` | chunk, `error` | 1006 (no close frame) | | This PR | chunk, `error` | 1011 `generation failed` | ## Modifications - When the generate task has finished without reaching `max_chunks`, `generate()` closes with 1011 `generation failed`. 1011 is the RFC 6455 code for a server that hit an unexpected condition. If the client has already gone, `_close_realtime_websocket` ignores the failed close, as it already does for the `max_chunks` case. - New case `test_generate_closes_with_an_error_code_when_generation_fails`. It drives `generate()` over a real Starlette `WebSocket`. On `main` the server's messages end after the `error`, with no `websocket.close`. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model code or outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Only the end of a failed session changes. summary: ## Motivation Fixes #48482. When the `Scheduler` runs in-process with `--skip-tokenizer-init`, a caller that wants per-request timing (time in the wait queue, time to first token, prefill and decode times, number of retractions) gets it in `RequestOutputStats.time_stats` only with `enable_metrics`, which also starts the Prometheus collectors. Without it, the only option is reading `Req.time_stats` and `Req.retraction_count` off the scheduler's request objects directly, which relies on private fields. title: [Fix] hicache: validate decode L3 hits and preserve transferred Mamba state
summary: ## Motivation Fixes [#48601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48601). For hybrid models, Decode can report an L3 KV hit even when the prefix has no matching Mamba checkpoint. The subsequent prefetch cannot restore that prefix, causing the request to return HTTP 500. During host-to-device restore, a prefix checkpoint can also overwrite the full-prompt Mamba state received from Prefill. If the local copy finishes after the P/D transfer, Decode starts from the wrong state. ## Modifications - Reuse the prefetch transfer builder when probing Decode L3 hits, checking Mamba checkpoints and required sidecars, including the indexer, together with KV pages. - Intersect checkpoint endpoints across attention ranks. For example, ranks with endpoints `{4, 8}` and `{4, 6}` must select `4`; taking the minimum of their longest hits would incorrectly select `6`. - Restore cache-owned checkpoints without copying them into the Decode request's Mamba slot. Prefill keeps its existing request-state restore behavior. ## Accuracy Tests The storage regressions cover missing Mamba checkpoints, reuse of an earlier checkpoint, differing rank checkpoint sets, and missing or partial indexer data. A separate load-back regression writes the simulated P/D state before the local restore, then checks that the request state is preserved and the cache-owned checkpoint is restored. Both regressions fail without their respective fixes and pass with them. title: [Perf] [NPU] chunked-prefill: KV cache pruning for extra-long context
summary: ## Motivation Prefilling ~1M-token prompts is the dominant cost for extra-long-context serving: with 64K chunked prefill, every middle chunk attends over the whole already-prefilled prefix, so prefill time grows ~linearly in the number of chunks (≈6.3 min TTFT for a 983040-token prompt on 2x Ascend 910B4 for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-1M). For such long prompts, most of the old KV cache has a negligible effect on output quality (verified below with RULER @ 983040 tokens). This PR keeps a bounded-size KV cache during chunked prefill instead of the full prefix, and uses a small re-prefilled "guiding tail" (default 128 tokens, a copy of the last tokens of the full prompt) as a query for detecting the most important KV positions. Result: ~1.5x faster TTFT at 1M context with no meaningful accuracy regression. The feature is off by default, opt-in via a new server flag, and currently implemented for Ascend NPU (FIA attention) with batch size 1. ## Modifications - **New server flag `--kv-cache-pruning-config`** (`arg_groups/fields/model.py`, default `None`): - a digit — treated as the maximal allowed retained KV cache size in tokens (page-aligned); - Throws at startup unless `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1` (the initial implementation is Ascend FIA only); designed for batch size 1 (asserted). - **New `srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/kv_cache_compression.py`**: code to calculate attention statistics and make prune least usable positions in KV cache with a "young" guard that always keeps the most recent tokens. title: [Bug] TBO can change deterministic prefill outputs and drop speculative auxiliary hidden states
summary: Two correctness issues were found in Two-Batch Overlap (TBO, `--enable-two-batch-overlap`). ### 1. Incorrect prefill offsets **Finding:** TBO slices token buffers into microbatches but leaves `extend_start_loc` parent-relative. **Impact:** The second microbatch can read incorrect KV slots or access out of bounds in deterministic Triton prefill. Real HTTP inference with a pretrained Qwen3-0.6B fixture converted to identical MoE experts produced different tokens in **4/8 requests** compared with TBO disabled. **Fix:** Rebase each child's `extend_start_loc` to its sliced token buffers. All 8 requests then matched the reference exactly, including output-token and top-5 logprobs. ### 2. Missing auxiliary hidden states **Finding:** TBO's staged layer execution bypasses the auxiliary capture points in ordinary forwards. **Impact:** EAGLE3 can fail when unpacking target outputs; mixed ordinary/staged execution can return incomplete features. **Fix:** Capture at the same attention boundary, collect snapshots per microbatch, then merge by layer and parent token order, excluding padding. Preserve ordinary-layer and terminal captures. Fixed EAGLE3 inference matched the TBO-off control; auxiliary features also matched bitwise on tiny Qwen3-MoE, DeepSeek and MiMo models. Reproduced on `1305b1830a`, with 2× H100, BF16, TP2 / attention-DP2 / EP2, DeepEP normal and Triton attention. CUDA graphs were disabled. EAGLE3 used step=3; DFlash validation covered target feature capture only. Proposed fix: #48659.

title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Fix garbage decode output with unified attention at page size 1 under CUDA graph
summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` on a dense (non-sliding-window) model at the default page size 1, decode produces garbage output when CUDA graph is on. The first token (from prefill) is correct and every decoded token after it is wrong: with greedy sampling, `"The capital of France is"` continues as `" a ( ( ( ( ( ..."` instead of `" a city of romance, art, fashion, and cuisine. Paris is a must"`. GSM8K drops to 0.00. Nothing rejects this configuration, so it fails silently. In `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata`, the unified-attention page table is copied into the captured `cuda_graph_page_table` only for sliding-window pools or `page_size > 1`. At page size 1 nothing is copied, so `unified_attention` reads an all-zero page table. Sliding-window models and Qwen3-VL (which gets page size 16 from its model override) are not affected. The non-CUDA-graph path builds the page table directly and is not affected either. The SHUFFLE 5D KV layout, the other decode path that reads this page table, requires a page size divisible by 8 (BF16 KV) or 16 (FP8 KV), so it never runs at page size 1. The AMD CI tests and cookbook recipes that enable unified attention all set `--page-size 16` or `64`, so page size 1 had no coverage. ## Modifications - `aiter_backend.py`: copy the page table for every non-sliding-window configuration. `_transform_table_1_to_real` is the identity at page size 1, so the `page_size > 1` condition only skipped the copy. - New AMD CI test `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_unified_attention_page_size_1.py`: GSM8K on `DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST` wit

title: [Perf] attention: Enable tensor descriptors in the Triton extend-attention kernel
summary: Supersedes #29639 (auto-closed as a stale draft; rebased onto current `main`). ## Motivation Triton's [tensor descriptors][td] let a kernel describe a tile by its shape and strides instead of computing a tensor of per-element pointers. title: [RFC] MoE routing simulator for prefill imbalance profiling: balanced reference and GPU-faithful replay
summary: ## Motivation We would like to follow up on #20307 with a narrowly scoped, opt-in profiling workflow: **compare production routing with a controlled synthetic routing reference inside the real serving pipeline, before investing in routing or load-balancing changes.** While investigating DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill on a single 8-GPU B300 node (TP8/DP8, MegaMoE), we found that several effects were easy to conflate: - logical expert popularity from the learned router; - physical placement / replica dispatch; - grouped-GEMM block rounding and padding; - rank-level stragglers; - All-to-All dispatch/combine cost; - request-supply / arrival gaps outside the MoE kernels. A balanced grouped-GEMM microbenchmark can isolate one kernel property, but it cannot establish how much **end-to-end serving latency** is actually caused by routing imbalance. Conversely, a lower expert-count CV does not imply lower GPU work if the backend rounds each expert workload to tile/block boundaries. This proposal therefore treats balanced routing as a **counterfactual measurement tool**, not as a production optimization. It does not change default routing, claim quality preservation, or imply that any observed synthetic gain can be recovered by EPLB or routing-bias changes. --- ## Related work and analytical framing | Reference | Mechanism / result | Relevant lesson for this RFC | | --- | --- | --- | | [TensorRT-LLM Perfect Router](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/04cefe271daceb491dbdacb0fcd8f1a174c10c16/docs/source/developer-guide/perf-analysis.md#moe-expert-load-balance-analysis-perfect-router)

title: [RFC] [XPU] paged-experts: Intel XPU support with Lookahead Expert Scheduling (LES) and an SSD tier for iGPU, single-GPU MoE offload
summary: **TL;DR.** Paged Experts (#42557) gave SGLang its core: - expert slots on the GPU, - all experts in pinned host memory, - device-side residency, and - a `topk_ids → slot` rewrite, so MoE kernels stay unchanged. This RFC proposes opt-in follow-ups that plug into the seams #42557 added, **enabled on `--device xpu` only**. The mechanisms come from our POC prototype on Intel GPUs. We reshaped them to fit Paged Experts' existing contracts: 1. **Intel XPU** as a Paged Experts device: Arc Pro B-series dGPU and Panther Lake iGPU, single GPU, with the INT4 / FP8 formats SGLang's XPU MoE path already supports. - **dGPU: VRAM ↔ pinned host.** This is today's Paged Experts contract unchanged: every expert in the pinned host store, slots in VRAM. What the dGPU gains: - **It runs at all.** Paged Experts does not run on XPU today, and FP8 35B-A3B does not fit on a 32 GB B70. - **Fewer synchronous gathers.** A miss is a synchronous gather on the critical path. title: [Fix] models: Pass HF sliding windows to RadixAttention without the query
summary: ## Motivation `RadixAttention.sliding_window_size` is the number of keys a query may see before itself: fa3 uses `window_size=(sliding_window_size, 0)`, and the triton extend and torch_native masks keep `k_pos >= q_pos - sliding_window_size`. An HF config's `sliding_window` counts the query too (`kv_idx > q_idx - sliding_window` in `transformers.masking_utils`), which is why Gemma 2/3, EXAONE 4, OLMo 2 and gpt-oss pass `config.sliding_window - 1`. These layers pass the HF value through unchanged: - `commandr.py` (Cohere2: Command R7B, Command A) - `cohere2_moe.py` - `gemma3n_causal.py` (its `get_attention_sliding_window_size` already returns `sliding_window - 1`, so its layers also disagree with the window the runner and SWA pool use) - `step3p5.py` (Step-3.5-Flash, window 512) - `transformers.py` (the Transformers fallback backend, so every HF model with sliding layers served through it) The reference modeling code of all of these builds its mask with `create_sliding_window_causal_mask(config.sliding_window)`. In SGLang their sliding layers attend to one key more than the checkpoint's window on every backend that applies the per-layer window (triton extend, fa3, trtllm_mha), so outputs drift from the reference once a sequence passes the window. EXAONE-MoE (`exaone_moe.py`) and MiMo-V2 (`mimo_v2.py`, `mimo_v2_nextn.py`) have the same off-by-one. #43555 and #43678 already fix them, so they are left out of this PR. Minimal repro: a tiny random-weight Cohere2 with `sliding_window=16`, scored teacher-forced in SGLang (triton backend) and in HF (eager, fp32). Run on an RTX 2060

summary: ## Motivation I fixed a batch-order dependency in automatic truncation. Normalized batch requests can share their sampling dictionary, so shortening one request's `max_new_tokens` also shortens later requests that still fit the context window. ## Modifications I copy the sampling dictionary only when applying a request-specific truncation. These CPU checks use the repository's `maybe_stub_sgl_kernel` helper for unavailable kernel imports. Tokenization, request normalization, validation, and sampling-parameter conversion are real; no GPU inference or model-accuracy benchmark was run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance benchmark was run. The new dictionary allocation occurs only when automatic truncation changes a request's budget; model and kernel execution are unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Applicable pre-commit hooks pass. - [x] The regression fails before the fix and passes afterward. - [x] Existing request semantics are preserved; no public API documentation change is needed. - [ ] GPU accuracy and speed benchmarks were not run. title: [Perf] beam: Pack q/k/v/gate into one projection for FP8 checkpoints
summary: ## Motivation Beam's attention projects q/k/v and the output gate from the same hidden states. BF16 checkpoints already run that as one packed `qkv_gate_proj` GEMM. FP8 checkpoints run `qkv_proj` and `gate_proj` separately, so each layer quantizes the same input to FP8 twice and launches two small GEMMs. At decode sizes those calls are launch-bound, so the second pair costs about as much as the first. FP8 is the only quantized Beam recipe on H200, and also a B300/GB300 recipe. Beam roadmap: #45370. ## Modifications - `BeamAttention` builds the packed `qkv_gate_proj` with the quant config for FP8 checkpoints. FP8_DYNAMIC is per-channel weights plus per-token activations, so the four shards' weights and scales concatenate along N and one per-token quant feeds all of them. - It packs only when the scheme targets the `Linear` class (as the Beam FP8 checkpoint does, so the packed name always resolves) and the ignore list leaves both `qkv_proj` and `gate_proj` quantized, the same check main runs for those two layers. Anything else keeps the split path, as do NVFP4 checkpoints, whose attention is BF16. Packing BF16 shards changes cuBLAS's kernel choice at small M on B300 (not bitwise equal to the split pair), so that can follow once it has an accuracy run. Replicated KV (attention TP > 8) is unchanged. - `BeamForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping` gets `qkv_gate_proj -> q/k/v/gate_proj`, so the quant config resolves the packed name through its checkpoint shards. - Loading needs no change: `load_weights` already routes `self_attn.{q,k,v,gate}_proj.*` to `qkv_gate_proj` when that param

title: [Fix] [NPU] adapt --speculative-dspark-align-verify-tokens-to-graph-tier on Ascend
summary: ## Motivation `--speculative-dspark-align-verify-tokens-to-graph-tier` has both halves in tree already: the planner side (pad every request up to the cuda-graph tier, budget the verify tokens with the SPS table) and the CUDA replay of those tiers. The DSV4 target-verify graph baked its q layout from`bs * draft_width` , so any graph tier whose slots did not each span a full draft row fed the fused compressor a`ropeSin` table of the wrong length and graph capture died. title: [Perf] paged-experts: load experts without a staging copy
summary: # [Perf] paged-experts: load experts without a staging copy ## Motivation This PR aims to reduce memory footprint while loading checkpoints. Paged Experts (#42557) keeps every expert in a pinned host store. Today a start first loads every expert into a pageable staging copy in the checkpoint layout, then fills the store from it K experts at a time (on the Marlin runner — GPTQ, AWQ, MXFP4, NVFP4, compressed-tensors W4A16 — through the repack). The staging copy is as large as the store, and while loading, both are in RAM at once, next to the checkpoint's page cache. So a start needs host memory for every expert twice. Paged Experts exists to serve models whose experts don't fit in VRAM from host RAM, and the staging copy halves which models that is: a model whose experts fit in RAM once but not twice cannot start without swapping heavily, and is killed on a host without enough swap. For example, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4 on an RTX 5070 Ti with 62 GB of RAM: - the staging copy takes 44 GB, - 19-26 GB go to swap during the start, - `load_model` takes 177-352 s, depending on how much it swaps, - after the start, 3.4-3.5 GB of the server process stay in swap, which raises TTFT. This PR removes the staging copy: the expert loads replay K experts at a time from the mapped checkpoint, straight into the store (or the repack). On the same machine, Qwen3-Next loads in 125-128 s without swapping, and TTFT p50 drops from 220-231 ms to 192 ms. Models whose experts fit in RAM twice don't gain from it; their start is 1-2 s slower. ## Modifications - **Loads wait** (`store.py`: `Expe

summary: ## Motivation In `NGRAMWorker._prepare_for_speculative_decoding` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`), `USE_FULL_MASK = True` is unconditionally hardcoded. On every speculative verify step, `NGRAMWorker` constructs a full-sequence mask of shape `(bs, draft_token_num, seq_len_i + draft_token_num)` on the GPU: 1. Pre-allocates `bs` separate `torch.ones((draft_token_num, seq_len_i), device=self.device)` tensors in default `torch.float32` (4 bytes/element). 2. summary: ## Motivation Gemma-4 31B with the frozen-KV MTP draft (`google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant`, NEXTN) on `--attention-backend fa4` crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` on long prompts, and the draft's accept length collapses to about 1.01 before the crash. Cause: Gemma-4 31B is a hybrid SWA model (10 full + 50 sliding-window layers, window 1024; full pool 505,587 slots, SWA pool 46,161 slots). The page table holds full-pool ids, which SWA layers must translate through `full_to_swa_index_mapping`. summary: ## Motivation With `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup cpu_tensor`, a retracted PD decode request copies its KV to CPU and frees its slots. On resume it gets new slots, and the backup is written into them. Only the target KV pool is backed up. EAGLE/EAGLE3, multi-layer EAGLE, DFLASH and DSPARK drafts that do not share the target pool keep their own KV tensors, indexed by the same token slots. Once another request reuses the freed slots, the resumed request's draft reads that request's KV. Drafts then come from the wrong context, so the acceptance rate drops. Output stays correct, because the target verifies every draft token. The `host_pool` backend already moves draft KV through its pool transfers. `cpu_tensor` does not. ## Modifications - `BaseSpecWorker.retraction_draft_pools()` returns the draft KV pools that a target-slot backup can carry: MHA pools with tensors of their own, indexed by the target's token slots. It skips: - fused drafts and drafts that write into the target pool, since the target backup already holds their KV; - pools shared by several draft runners, which are backed up once; - MLA pools, whose `get_cpu_copy` maps token ids to this DCP rank's rows; - the page-major MHA layout, which has no CPU copy. - `DFlashWorkerV2` returns no pools when it uses the compact draft cache. That cache has its own request->token table, so its rows are not the target's slots. - `Scheduler.init_memory_pools` registers these pools on the target allocator when the backend resolves to `cpu_tensor`. - `Req.offload_kv_cache` and `load_kv_cache` copy every registered pool

title: [Ops][Feature] Enable static & super kernel under PIECEWISE cudagraph mode
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE is the default cudagraph mode, but the static / super kernel flags were force-disabled for it, and the static kernel sym_range only covered decode batch sizes — so prefill-shaped pieces never got compiled. title: [Feature] BigTensorLoader snapshot fast-restore via a shared weight-state kernel

summary: ## Description Port of vLLM #58737 to vllm-ascend. `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s "align" branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request. As PyTorch ops this expands to **seven eager kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor** — a single element per op in a one-request decode — so almost all of its cost is launch overhead, not work. title: [BugFix] Fix Mooncake SWA prefill handoff at N-1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mooncake PD replays the final prompt token on Decode. For sliding-window caches, computing the entire prompt on Prefill can retire a page that Decode still needs for that replay. With prompt length 1023, window 512 and block size 128, the page containing position 511 can be discarded before Decode computes position 1022. A successful transfer cannot recover data from a page that has already been recycled. Detect `SlidingWindowSpec` in the expanded cache groups and reuse the existing N-1 handoff: Prefill leaves the final prompt token to Decode, and remote-hit accounting and published lengths use the same handoff position. Decode keeps its original prompt. Compressed-cache and Mamba behavior, the single-token guard and idempotent truncation remain intact. This is a standalone Mooncake fix based on upstream main `f85f77a98df5`; it does not depend on the Step5 model PR. Regression coverage includes pure SWA, Full+SWA, uniform SWA and a synthetic Step5-shaped mixed cache, using cache specs rather than model-name checks. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Fixes incorrect PD continuation caused by premature sliding-window page eviction at prompt/block boundaries. No new configuration is required. ### How was this patch tested? **Main-based source: CPU regression and static checks** - The same frozen source snapshot passed **454 tests on each of two hosts**, with vLLM 0.33.0, CPU PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch-npu 2.10.0.post7. title: [Attention][Feature] Enable PCP decode request sharding for GLM-5.3-Flash
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? GLM-5.3-Flash currently replicates decode requests across PCP ranks. This PR uses the upstream Model Runner V2 decode ownership policy when PCP > 1 and DCP = 1, assigning each request, including speculative target verification, to one rank round-robin within the batch. KDA gathers inputs in global request order so every rank advances its recurrent-state shard, including when a request changes owner or a rank has no live requests. title: [BugFix][Worker] Explain MC2 profiling failures caused by a small HCCL_BUFFSIZE
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On A2/A3 with plain MC2, `profile_run` runs a dummy MC2 dispatch to reserve the HCCL window before the standard profile run. When `HCCL_BUFFSIZE` is smaller than the window the dummy needs, the dispatch kernel asserts inside the device, but operators are asynchronous: startup dies later with an opaque `vector core exception` (error code 507035) blamed on an unrelated operator. All ranks fail, and nothing in the traceback points at `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`. This PR covers the whole MC2-enabled profiling path — the MC2 dummy and the standard profile run that follows, including its final synchronize — and, when a `RuntimeError` carries one of the device signatures that actually reach `str(exc)` (`507035`, `vector core exception`, `fftsplus aivector error`), re-raises an error that names the likely cause, the configured `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, the dummy's token count, and the `ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` diagnostic. The kernel assert text (`HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP is too SMALL`, `realWinSize >= minWinSize`) is written to device stdout and never reaches the exception, so it is not used as a marker. The hint says "device-side vector-core failure (for example, error code 507035)" rather than quoting one specific form, and is worded "MC2 profiling failed" because the dummy itself does not synchronize; the async error can surface at the profile sync. Production decode trace (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W4A8 TP8/EP8, bs=2): `aclnnTransposeBatchMatMul` 40 calls/step x \~50.6 us = **2.03 ms/step** (\~10% of the 5.3 us/call HBM floor of the 8.4 MB bf16 weight). title: [BugFix][PCP] Reuse profile budget for prefill MC2 capacity
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? PCP startup profiling uses a local token budget, but prefill MC2/MegaMoe capacity still starts from the global scheduler budget. Extract the calculation into `utils.get_pcp_profile_num_tokens` and reuse it from `profile_run` and the prefill branch of `set_mc2_tokens_capacity`. The helper reserves replicated rows first, shards the remaining token budget by PCP, and adds two rounding tokens per request for DualChunkSwap. With B scheduled tokens, R requests and PCP size P, it uses C = min(B, R * L), then min(B, C + ceil((B - C) / P) + 2 * R). Without DCP, L is the decode query length, covering both replicated decodes and uneven whole-request decode sharding. With DCP, L also covers short prefills selected by the upstream empty-chunk predicate, whose maximum length is (2 * P - 1)^2. Block/context drafters retain the global budget. title: [RFC]: MoonEP redundant-expert load balancing for inference prefill
summary: ## Motivation ### Problem: MoE prefill is compute-imbalanced Expert-parallel MoE places each expert on exactly one rank. Every token is routed to its top-K experts, so a rank's work is set by how many routed rows land on the experts it owns. Real traffic is not uniform: in the workloads below the per-layer peak-to-average ratio (PAR, max expert load / mean expert load) is 1.7 on average for Qwen3-30B-A3B and reaches 2.53 on the hottest layer. Two effects follow: 1. The hot expert's owner rank runs a longer grouped GEMM while the other ranks idle. All-to-all and MC2 move the rows but cannot split the compute, so they do not fix the straggler. 2. With data parallelism, ranks advance in lockstep. A slow prefill rank stalls the whole DP step, which shows up directly as TTFT tail latency and, in a mixed prefill/decode run, as decode bubbles. ### Why EPLB is not sufficient here EPLB rebalances expert *placement*. In the comparison run below EPLB was configured with `num_redundant_experts: 0`, `eplb_policy_type: 2`, heat collection every 40 steps, algorithm execution every 20 steps, and heat collection in all stages. With zero redundant experts, EPLB can only move a hot expert (and its hotspot) from one rank to another; it cannot create a second copy to split that expert's rows across ranks. Measured against base, the EPLB effect is small and inconsistent across models (wall −1.6% to +3.7% prefill-only, −1.2% to +0.6% PD mix): | model | prefill-only wall | PD-mix wall | | :--- | ---: | ---: | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | +3.7% | +0.6% | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | +2.3% | −0.03% | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B

title: [BugFix][MRv2] Preserve NZ expert weights with eager CPU prefetch
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Before this fix, GLM-5.1 W8A8C8 could fail at startup with `EZ1001` on A3 when MRv2 ran in eager mode with explicit CPU weight prefetch. Quantization post-processing produced `FRACTAL_NZ` expert weights. The upstream offloader bound those parameters to ND buffers, and the fused expert kernel rejected that layout. The W8A8 MoE implementation directly casts `w13_weight` and `w2_weight` to NZ during `process_weights_after_loading()` because `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant` requires NZ weights on this path. These casts bypass `maybe_trans_nz()`, so setting `weight_nz_mode=0` still produces NZ expert weights. The offloader therefore needs to preserve the layout required by the expert kernel. [W8A8 MoE weight processing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/9f791f2952d504bfe0b06708041394c005b2f6c3/vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/w8a8_dynamic.py#L279-L286) With `enforce_eager=True` and `offload_backend="prefetch"`, MRv2 now reuses MRv1's `AscendPrefetchOffloader`. It detects NZ weights during post-processing, prepares NZ static buffers, and binds the corresponding parameters to those buffers. This reuses the existing prefetch scheduling and Ascend layout handling. The runner constructs and registers the offloader inside `torch_cuda_wrapper()` so its `torch.cuda.Stream()` call creates an NPU copy stream. The eager restriction comes from the prefetch copy itself. CPU backing storage is ND, so copying these weights into an NZ buffer requires ND-to-NZ conversion. title: [Performance] Write DSpark SWA draft indices straight into persistent buffers
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The DeepSeek-V4.1 draft path (DSpark, speculative decoding) rebuilds its non-causal SWA sparse indices on **every decode step**. Per decode step this removes 2 × `torch.empty` and 2 × full-tensor `copy_` from the metadata-builder hot path. On the profiled decode loop these four host ops accounted for \~40-60 µs/step of pure dispatch and allocation cost (see microbenchmark below); at small batch sizes the draft metadata builder is host-bound, so the saving lands directly on the critical path. This PR brings the V4.1 builder in line with that established protocol — the V4.1 builder went through a separate logical-index kernel that still rebuilds temporaries and copies. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? A narrowly scoped change in DeepSeek V4.1 would exclude DSpark from the MTP buffer condition: ```diff - needs_mtp_hidden_states = spec_config is not None and ( - spec_config.use_eagle() or spec_config.uses_draft_model() + needs_mtp_hidden_states = ( + spec_config is not None + and not spec_config.use_dspark() + and (spec_config.use_eagle() or spec_config.uses_draft_model()) ) ``` This preserves the traditional MTP path for other consumers and leaves the shared meaning of `use_eagle()` unchanged. A capability-based condition may be preferable if maintainers want to address auxiliary-state methods more broadly. ### Why this matters For BF16, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `hc_mult=4`, and `hidden_size=5120`, `_mtp_hidden_buffer` has shape `[16384, 20480]` and occupies **640 MiB per rank**. title: [Feature] Add int8 quantized all-reduce for large bf16 TP collectives on Atlas A2
summary: ## What does this PR do? Adds an **opt-in int8 quantized all-reduce** for large bf16 TP collectives on Atlas A2 (910B series, A3-ready), halving the communication volume of the bandwidth-bound prefill all-reduces (attention output projection / MoE output reduction). ## Motivation & context On HCCS-interconnected Atlas A2 TP deployments, prefill-stage bf16 all-reduces dominate the non-overlapped communication time (~16% of stage time for Qwen3.6-35B TP=4 with 16k-token batches; 81 all-reduces per 16k-token forward pass, 64 MiB each at ~33 GB/s effective algorithm bandwidth). ## Design (final) 1. **Per-channel symmetric scale with an integer-safe exact bound** — no clamp kernel: `max_q = 127 // world_size`, `scale[c] = global_amax(channel c) / max_q`. `|x| <= amax` implies `|x/scale| <= max_q`, and rounding a value that is already `<= max_q` cannot exceed it, so every rank stays within `+/-max_q` and the `ws`-way int8 sum is bounded by `ws * max_q <= 127` for **any** input distribution (same-sign worst case included). title: [Performance] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 mHC boundaries and overlap coefficient computation on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On vLLM-Ascend main, the boundary between two DeepSeek V4.1 sublayers runs `HcPost`, `HcPreV3`, and RMSNorm in sequence. `HcPreV3` both collapses the four residual streams using the incoming `pre_mix` and computes three new coefficients (`pre`, `post`, and `comb`). Coefficient computation takes up a substantial part of HcPreV3’s runtime and Attention and MoE can start before these three sets of coefficients are ready, since they’re only used in later steps. This PR makes the following changes to speed up this process: - **Split `HcPreV3` work.** Add `HcPreCoefficients`, a coefficient-only Ascend C operator that reuses the native projection, row partitioning, and coefficient computation. The full `HcPreV3` path remains available for fallback and for boundaries that cannot be fused. - **Fuse input preparation.** One Triton kernel combines `HcPost`, the four-way residual collapse, and RMSNorm. - **Overlap coefficient computation.** In a full decode graph, the auxiliary stream starts coefficient computation once the updated residual is ready. The main stream can start attention or MoE as soon as its input is ready and waits at the next coefficient consumer. Outside full graph execution, eligible fused boundaries compute coefficients on the main stream. The split and overlap design follows [vLLM #59802](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59802), which implemented the same scheduling idea for ROCm. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Fusion + overlap is enabled by default for eligible DeepSeek V4.1 batches on A2

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MooncakeConnectorV2 (producer side) releases the KV blocks of a completed transfer only from `Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished`, which core calls in `update_from_output` under `if kv_connector_output:`. **The gate is closed on the producer, not just on idle steps.** For this connector the P-side worker never produces a non-empty `KVConnectorOutput`: | field | why it is empty on P | | --- | --- | | `finished_sending` / `finished_recving` | `get_transfer_results` returns the receiving thread's results, and that thread exists only on the decode role | | `kv_connector_stats` | `record_transfer` in `stats.py` has no caller in the connector | | `kv_cache_events` / `kv_connector_worker_meta` | base-class defaults, not overridden by V2 | `is_empty()` is always true, `with_kv_conn_output_only` compacts it away, and the hook never runs. title: [Performance][A3][A5] Speed up packed DCP attention output combine
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The shared DCP attention path merges partial outputs from separate K/V shards, including an optional local result in split MLA attention. For BF16 head scatter, this PR decodes each packed LSE once per output row and reuses the rank weights across all features. Runtime and warmup launch one Triton kernel. The device profile supplies a compile-time row mode. A3 processes one row at a time because multirow loads can lower to nested scalar loops. A5 processes eight rows per tile to improve memory throughput. Each program owns a contiguous interval. The same selection applies at every row count. The optimized path accepts `D <= 512`, output-only combine and unit local feature stride when a local output is present. Other supported layouts and dtypes use the existing scalar path. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Packed DCP attention output combine is faster on the target A3 and A5 shapes. Callers use the existing API. The result includes the optional local contribution once, masks outputs with nonfinite LSE and returns zeros for all-invalid rows. ### How was this patch tested? **Device-kernel performance.** The public wrapper ran on the same device with the same inputs for each comparison. title: [Performance][Model] Tile Qwen4Exp HC gate mix on Ascend A2/A3/A5
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR adds an eight-row Triton tile for Qwen4Exp HyperConnection `gate_mix`. The existing one-row kernel remains the fallback. The row-block kernel processes an `8 x 512` tile, reduces the launched-program count by up to 8x, and preserves the original FP32 accumulation order. The dispatch threshold is based on the integrated wrapper, not the kernel alone: - A2/A3: row-block starts at 2048 rows. - A5: row-block starts at 1024 rows. At 1024 rows the direct kernel is faster on all three devices, but host-side output allocation and custom-op dispatch dominate on A2/A3. A5 crosses over earlier and benefits from the row-block path at 1024 rows. The shared `8 x 512` tile is close to the best measured per-device tile at 1024 rows: - A2: `8 x 512` is `80.00 us`; the best measured `4 x 512` variant is `78.86 us`, a 1.45% difference. - A5: `8 x 512` is `14.63 us`; the best measured `32 x 128` variant is `14.57 us`, a 0.41% difference. `512` divides the production `group_dim=2560` exactly, preserves column alignment, and keeps one shared tile instead of adding per-device tuning. One hoisted mask is reused for all stream loads and the output store, including production-aligned and tail widths. The implementation also handles column tails, combined row/column tails, and element offsets beyond `INT32_MAX`. The normal prefill path remains int32. No environment variable or user configuration is added. ### Operator integration - Public wrapper: `hc_gate_mix(x, gate, hc_count)` - Registered custom op: `qwen4_exp_ascend_hc_gate_mix` - Production caller

title: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Sweep expired Mooncake delayed-free entries from the sending thread
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Lease expiry on the Mooncake V2 producer is enforced by `_retrieve_expired_requests_locked`, but main only drives it from two places: | driver | when it stops working | | --- | --- | | `get_and_clear_finished_requests` (scheduler hook) | the hook only runs while the engine steps, and for `MooncakeConnectorV2` the producer-side worker output is empty on every step, so the hook's call site is never reached | | `_handle_heartbeat` | only renews or reaps the IDs D still tracks; once D has removed the request from its roster (D crash, abort, permanently lost DONE) the entry is never looked at again | Both miss the same class of entries: present in the producer's ledger but no longer mentioned by D. The lease bound then means nothing and the ledger grows until restart. This PR adds a third driver that cannot go away: the sending thread's 1s `zmq.Again` recv timeout calls the same existing sweep. It reuses `_retrieve_expired_requests_locked` and the existing `_log_lease_finish` outside the lock, so the expiry rule and its logging stay in one place. **Scope (important):** the sweeper only *archives*. It moves expired entries from the lease ledgers into `finished_requests`, where a later scheduler drain releases the blocks; it never frees blocks itself and never drains the queue. So this is a lease-accounting and observability hardening, not the memory release fix - block release is the idle-step drain in #21918, or real worker output. title: [Feature]: Add node-local direct UVA for shared MXFP8 Engram tables across independent A5 instances
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch We run four independently launched DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill instances on one Ascend A5 host, each with DP2 × PCP2 × TP1. With `cpu_offload=true` and `dp_shared_memory=true`, workers within each instance share a host Engram table. Each independent instance still loads its own copy because it has a separate process group. The two Engram layers in our MXFP8/E8M0 checkpoint require 188.83 GiB of host backing. Four instance-local copies would require approximately 755.33 GiB. One node-local copy would save approximately 566.50 GiB (75%) of Engram table backing. We propose an opt-in, node-local Host UVA mode for `shared_engram`: - A persistent CPU owner loads the original MXFP8 codes and E8M0 scales once. Workers validate the checkpoint identity and table layout, then attach to the published table generation. - The owner passes shared-memory FDs over a Unix socket. Other tensors in the same safetensors shard continue to load normally. - A prefill instance can attach after the owner is ready. Workers synchronize outstanding device reads before unregistering their mappings and releasing their leases. ### Alternatives - Use instance-local `dp_shared_memory`. This already shares the table within each DP × PCP group and requires one backing allocation per independently launched instance. - Use the A2/A5 HIXL b

title: [RFC]: Support native FP8 per-block (128x128) weights
summary: ### Motivation. More and more models are now published directly in FP8: `config.json` carries `quant_method: "fp8"` together with `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`, e.g. [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8](https://modelscope.cn/models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8), [zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash), and the multimodal/MoE variants of the DeepSeek/GLM families. Such a checkpoint stores every quantized matrix as one `float8_e4m3fn` weight plus one `float32` scale per 128x128 tile (`weight_scale_inv`). vLLM Ascend currently has a single execution path: after loading, the block scales are expanded into the model dtype (`resolve_block_scales`) and re-quantized to MXFP8 (one E8M0 scale per 32 elements along the reduction dim), then handed to the MXFP8 branch of `npu_quant_matmul` / `npu_grouped_matmul`. That path works and keeps weights at one byte per element, but it has three problems: 1. **The numbers are no longer the checkpoint's.** Dequantizing to bf16 and re-quantizing to MXFP8 is two lossy roundings, and an E8M0 scale can only be a power of two, so it cannot represent the checkpoint's float32 block scale. title: [Bug]: Ling routed experts can use the wrong SwiGLU limit on Ascend
summary: ### Your current environment - Ascend baseline `80a705e62778bee2d49ffa72becf557961f7c181`. - Upstream vLLM `v0.33.0` (`4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`) and `ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe`. - Local CPU reproduction on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.10 and PyTorch 2.14.0. NPU operators were mocked. ### 🐛 Describe the bug On vLLM `v0.33.0`, Ling routed experts with a configured `expert_swiglu_limit_list` entry request `silu`. That path clamps the gate before SiLU, which differs from the clamp-after-SiLU behavior used by [upstream vLLM #65088](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65088). `ba15685` selects `swiglustep` upstream. Ascend's standard MoE and W8A8 MXFP8 `SWIGLUSTEP` paths still use a fixed limit of `7.0` on the unchanged baseline. A CPU probe on the unchanged Ascend baseline with `v0.33.0` returned `15.71222` for `gate=8`, `up=6`, and a configured limit of `4`. The expected output is `16`. The order difference can be reproduced without model weights: ```python from math import exp gate, up, limit = 8.0, 6.0, 4.0 up = min(max(up, -limit), limit) def silu(x): return x / (1 + exp(-x)) print(f'{silu(min(gate, limit)) * up:.5f}') # 15.71222 print(f'{min(silu(gate), limit) * up:.5f}') # 16.00000 ``` Layers with the same MoE shape can also share communication state, so the executing layer's limit can be replaced by another layer's limit. The local fused MC2 path on A3 uses a shared pre-SiLU limit. A configured limit on the target or an MTP draft therefore needs the regular MoE path.

title: [BugFix][EPLB] Make DYNAMIC_EPLB / EXPERT_MAP_RECORD env parsing case-insensitive
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The two EPLB gate variables are parsed inconsistently in the same predicate (`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`, `EplbConfig._validate_config`): ```python assert ( os.getenv("DYNAMIC_EPLB", "false").lower() in ("true", "1") or os.getenv("EXPERT_MAP_RECORD", "false") == "true" ), "The environment variable DYNAMIC_EPLB or EXPERT_MAP_RECORD of the EPLB must be set to true." ``` `DYNAMIC_EPLB` accepts `true` / `TRUE` / `True` / `1`; `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD` only accepts the exact lowercase `"true"`. This is a one-line behavioural fix: parse `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD` with the same `.lower() in ("true", "1")` comparison the sibling variable already uses, and keep the two expressions readable by naming them. Every value previously accepted is still accepted; `True`, `TRUE` and `1` now enable the EPLB paths instead of failing. ### Scope note: `envs.py` `AGENTS.md` asks for environment variables to be read through `vllm_ascend/envs.py`. title: [Performance] Fuse DSA V4.1 slot-mapping 2D/flat computation into one Triton kernel
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? The DSA V4.1 attention-metadata builder launches per-KV-cache-group slot-mapping 2D/flat computation as ~13 eager aclnn operators (GeScalar, ClampMin, DivMods, Remainder, SWhere, ViewCopy) every step. This change fuses those device operations into one Triton kernel (compute_slot_mapping_2d) that computes validity, block/offset division, selection and the three buffer writes in a single launch, reusing the existing persistent buffers. Metadata preparation remains outside model graphs. The fused kernel runs for both prefill and decode forwards (the metadata build executes on every forward step), so host-side launch overhead is cut across the whole serving path. The fused kernel: - accumulates RMSNorm in FP32 and preserves the BF16 rounding boundary before RoPE; - implements the existing adjacent-pair interleaved partial RoPE convention; - uses the cache tensor's real block/row/feature strides; - skips negative [block, offset] coordinates used by invalid slots and graph padding; - launches on the caller's current stream, preserving the existing overlap between the KV branch and Wq_b GEMM; - retains the original three-operator path for unsupported inputs. Selection is limited to Triton-enabled A2 (910B), BF16 NPU WKV/cache tensors, DeepSeek V4.1's 512-wide standard SWA cache, compatible 2-D slot mappings, RMSNorm without a loaded bias, and at most 8192 rows. A3, replicated PCP cache writes requiring a global row gather, A5 packed caches, unsupported layouts/dtypes, larger batches, Long KV, C1/C2 compressor, and indexer cache writes remain unchanged. The fused path reduces the SWA preparation region from three kernels to one while avoiding the normalized KV intermediate and its subsequent RoPE/scatter global-memory traffic. WKV GEMM is intentionally left separate. ### Performance #### End-to-end serving After resolving the upstream conflicts, we reran th

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On Ascend A2, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash prepares cache slot mappings and attention/indexer metadata before replaying the decode graph. title: [WeightTransfer][BugFix] Preserve the expert map during layerwise reload
summary: Replaces #20397 as a non-draft PR. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Ascend registers `expert_ids_per_ep_rank` as a non-persistent buffer for its inference-side expert routing. The checkpoint/weight sender does not supply this buffer, but layerwise reload includes it in the module's expected weight count and replaces it with a meta tensor. Consequently, receiving all real weights is not enough to complete the module: received tensors remain in `loaded_weights` instead of being released module by module. The locally generated routing map also loses its storage during reload initialization. Register only this buffer in the existing MoE platform patch: - `SKIP_LOAD_TENSORS`: do not wait for it when determining module completion. - `SKIP_TENSORS`: retain the existing tensor during meta replacement. The existing non-persistent buffer registration and sleep/wake restoration remain in use. The additions mutate the existing upstream sets in place, preserving references held by the layerwise loader. They are idempotent process-local initialization before model loading, not per-request mutations. The patch registry documents replacing this workaround with a per-buffer upstream reload policy when available. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Live MoE weight updates can complete each module without waiting for the inference-generated expert map, avoiding retained incoming weights across completed modules and preserving the routing map. The changes address these correctness issues: - Index Mamba pre-copy and postprocess operations by persistent request slots, preventing reordered batches from accessing another request's convolution or SSM state. - Rebuild the Mamba alignment context during KV-cache initialization, including after profiling, and avoid duplicate dimension-first convolution copies across tiles. - Collect ReplaySSM tracker tensors after model-state initialization so scheduler block copies retain the final tensor references. - Materialize contiguous PLE convolution inputs

title: [RFC]: Support Inkling 2 Small DSpark speculative decoding on Ascend MRV2
summary: ### Motivation. Inkling 2 Small ships a DSpark drafter in its checkpoint. Upstream vLLM #67325 loads it from `mtp_config` and `mtp.safetensors`, collects inputs to selected target layers, and lets each draft layer mix those features. This RFC tracks bringing the Inkling 2 Small speculative-decoding path to Ascend MRV2. ### Proposed Change. 1. Adapt the target feature collection and draft loading contract alongside the base Inkling 2 Small model work. Register the Inkling2 DSpark architecture and speculator on Ascend, and load the bundled draft with `method=dspark` and `num_speculative_tokens=7`. 2. Preserve raw target features for per-draft-layer mixing and context KV construction. Build the recurrent head's context from the last committed target position after rejection sampling. Bring up NPU eager execution before ACL graph capture, preserving the checkpoint's anchor-plus-seven block layout. 3. Adapt the recurrent Markov head for greedy and probabilistic drafting, including logits rounding and draft-cache contents. Share the target's normalized embedding and LM head, and rebuild derived folded weights in place after target weight replacement. 4. Validate acceptance, output quality and latency with the released checkpoints. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [BugFix][PD] Fix MooncakeHybridConnector KV registration for sparse-indexer hybrid models (GLM-5.3-Flash)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With PD disaggregation (`MooncakeHybridConnector`), **GLM-5.3-Flash** (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) produces garbled output on the decode node, while the prefill and decode instances each work correctly when used standalone. **Root cause** GLM-5.3-Flash combines MLA, a compressed sparse indexer (`index_topk`) and recurrent (mamba) state. Since `patch_mamba_config` aligns these caches into shared padded pages ("Setting attention block size to 1152 tokens to align MLA, recurrent-state, and compressed indexer cache pages"), the connector has to register KV caches per physical page. But `register_kv_caches` only takes the shared-page path (`_reconstruct_shared_pages`) when the model config has `compress_ratios` (DeepSeek-V4). GLM-5.3-Flash has no `compress_ratios`, so it falls into the per-view `use_mamba` branch: - empty placeholder views (`numel() == 0`) register `data_ptr() == 0` as base addresses; - the block stride is taken from each view instead of the page stride; - `addr_group_idx` stays empty, so every group's block ids are applied to every address. On the decode side, adxl rejects the read: ``` CheckTransferOpDescs: ErrorNo: 103900 local addr of desc can not be null. Failed to TransferSync, remote_engine:...:20011, operation:read, op_descs size:180 ``` The exception is caught and only logged in `_handle_request`, so the request still proceeds and decode generates from an empty KV cache. The result is garbled text (`External prefix cache hit rate: 92.3%` while nothing was actually transferred). Routing the model to the sha

title: [Performance][Worker] Reuse V2 attention metadata across cache groups and batch GDN state writes
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On Model Runner V2, a hybrid model builds one attention metadata object per cache group on every step. The batch-level fields (`seq_lens`, `query_start_loc`, masks, `max_query_len`, ...) are identical for all groups of the same spec; only the physical block table and the recurrent state indices differ. Qwen3.5-9B keeps its original 38 cache groups, and a compatible 24-GDN-group batch currently performs one common build plus 23 physical-state refreshes. This PR makes that sharing explicit and removes the remaining per-group cost: - Reuse a bounded metadata template across compatible groups. Dense groups key on `(kv_cache_spec, decode_threshold, causal)`; GDN groups key on `(kv_cache_spec, builder type)`. `update_block_table()` shallow-copies the template and replaces only the group-local block table / state view. - Skip common-metadata construction entirely for single-builder GDN groups once a template exists in the same step, instead of building it and then reusing. - Record whether reuse happened during capture (`_gdn_reuse_at_capture`) and force the same decision on replay, raising instead of silently taking the other path. - Replace per-group `copy_`/`fill_` of GDN state indices with a single guarded int32 NPU kernel into graph-owned buffers, plus Triton helpers for aligned state indices and cached pure-decode layout materialization. - Stay compatible with vLLM #58737, which derives `num_reqs` from the block table and asserts that `seq_lens` has the same number of rows; Ascend's `unpadded()` intentionally keeps padded block-table r

title: [Performance] Reuse paged SFA for BF16 HiSparse prefill
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Reuse the existing paged sparse flash attention path for unquantized HiSparse prefill with RoPE. The current path expands every query's selected tokens into its own KV workspace. Queries attending to overlapping positions read and copy the same cached rows repeatedly. Split the staged KV pages into contiguous latent and RoPE tensors once per prefill layer call. Pass the logical Top-K indices, staged block table and prefill-only sequence lengths to the existing paged SFA. This uses the regular causal prefill indexer contract. Decode rows, graph-capture inputs and padded inputs retain their existing path. This PR targets main and can merge independently of #21892. #21892 adds PCP functional support and was included in the configuration below to exercise the BF16 optimization with PCP2. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Reduced BF16 HiSparse prefill latency for long-context RoPE models. No configuration changes. ### How was this patch tested? Ascend 950, GLM5.3, both main KV and indexer BF16, TP4/PCP2/EP8, MTP3 and decode graphs. Same inputs with 24,576 prompt tokens and 4,096 output tokens per request. Both variants used HiSparse. The on-device experiment used Ascend `64dd8404` plus the BF16 PCP functional patch from #21892, with only the prefill logic toggled. title: [BugFix][Mamba] Avoid grouped Conv2D in NPU causal convolution
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #22241. On the reported 8 x Ascend 910B4 system (A2, CANN 9.2.1), serving LiquidAI/d1-3B with vLLM 0.32.0 exits the engine on the first request. title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Support DCP replicated indexer in layerwise connector
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Support fully DCP-replicated SFA indexer caches in MooncakeLayerwiseConnector while preserving the existing main-KV DCP mapping. Select one redundant prefill sender per destination and transfer the indexer blocks incrementally as chunks complete, including destinations with no main-KV blocks for short prompts. Normalize component block-size scales by each side's DCP replication factor so different P/D DCP sizes can use matching kernel block sizes. Preserve decode prefix-cache hits before request computed-token state is updated, and count the union of main-KV and indexer senders over the uncached suffix for completion notifications. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Layerwise transfer can handle fully replicated SFA indexer caches alongside DCP-sharded main KV, including different P/D DCP sizes, prefix-cache hits, and indexer-only final chunks. Indexer layouts without full DCP replication retain the existing mapping path. Main and indexer components must still share a KV cache group with compatible normalized kernel block sizes. ### How was this patch tested? - Added unit coverage for replicated-indexer registration, per-destination sender selection, the non-replicated fallback, prefix-hit propagation and completion counts, chunk progression, short prompts with indexer-only destinations, request-key preservation, and address generation with different P/D DCP sizes. - Passed Ruff lint and format checks on both changed files. - Passed Python syntax compilation and Git diff whitespace checks. - Unit tests and Ascen
