title: [Feature] Fuse GatingTopK with EPLB expert mapping
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With ModelRunnerV2 EPLB, expert selection writes logical expert IDs before a separate Map kernel reads them and produces physical IDs. This change adds an optional `expert_replica_routing_table` input to `moe_gating_top_k_hash`, allowing supported routes to map the final IDs before they leave on-chip memory. The router automatically selects fusion on supported A3/A5 hardware for ungrouped `sqrtsoftplus` routing. It reuses the existing periodic EPLB table, including the AllGather table when applicable, and skips the subsequent standalone Map. Weights are computed using logical IDs before the output IDs are mapped. The router inherits upstream `_select_experts` unchanged. An internal `_use_gating_top_k_with_map` switch is resolved once at the first routing call, after EPLB/capture setup and using the actual hidden size. The existing Ascend mapping hook only reads this fixed choice; it does not reset or consume per-call state. `_can_fuse_gating_map` checks eligibility once, while `_get_gating_map_table` reads the current ordinary/AllGather table on every nonempty fused call. Missing tables raise instead of returning unmapped IDs. The original parent-fallback condition is preserved; eligibility is resolved for the fixed model routing configuration. The router retains the existing nonempty-input expectation: the reviewed ModelRunnerV2 target paths skip zero batches or provide dummy/padded tokens before routing. This PR does not add standalone zero-row TopK support. Model routing configuration, including logical-ID capture, must be finalize

title: [BugFix][Attention] Fix GLM DFlash2 FA3 HND caches and target graph warmup
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Standalone follow-up to #21850, rebased onto main at `8cd3c3762`. Prerequisite #20167 is now merged; this PR contains only the focused follow-up increment, not its prerequisite commits. With a GLM MLA/SFA target and an eager DFlash2 draft, the draft needs a multi-head HND cache and its own FA3 metadata. Previously, target attention initialization also constructed metadata for the eager draft. Native FA3 scheduler work could then be initialized during target graph warmup or deferred until the first real idle-draft forward. The observed failure blocked the native task queue while `PackedCuLast` waited for a scalar read. This PR enables the existing optional FA3 backend for eligible local GLM DFlash2 drafts, preserves physical HND caches, and separates eager draft initialization from target graph execution: - `platform.py`: admit the supported local eager GLM DFlash2 draft, including the `dflash_head` loader tag, under a distributed target topology. Keep hardware, local PCP/DCP, draft-KV dtype and fallback guards. - `attention/flash_attention_v3.py`: honor HND/LBHNC physical cache writes and expose zero-copy logical FA3 views. Initialize the eager DFlash native scheduler during draft metadata-builder initialization, before runtime metadata builds, and retain its inputs/results until initialization completes. These synchronization barriers run once per device/operator contract, outside capture and per-step metadata construction. - `patch/worker/patch_model_runner.py`: use the existing `init_attn_backend(active_layer_names=...)` extension

title: [RFC]: Add KV Pool environment validation and fixed-SLO capacity search tools
summary: ### Motivation. KV Pool deployment involves multiple hardware, runtime, network, storage, and software dependencies. Users often discover environment problems only when the service starts or when KV Pool initialization fails. A standardized preflight check would improve deployment reliability, simplify troubleshooting, and provide consistent evidence for issue triage. Performance validation has a similar gap. Fixed-concurrency or fixed-request-rate benchmarks do not directly answer whether a deployment can sustain a target latency SLO, or what maximum concurrency and throughput it can support under that SLO. We propose adding two opt-in utilities to vLLM-Ascend: 1. A KV Pool environment checker for deployment validation and diagnostics. 2. A fixed-SLO capacity search tool for performance validation and capacity planning. ### Proposed Change. ### Common Principles Both utilities will be command-line tools intended for operators and developers. They will be opt-in and will not affect normal inference behavior or add import-time side effects. Proposed location: vllm_ascend/examples/ ├── kvpool_envcheck/ └── slo_search/ The changes will be submitted as two PRs: - PR1: Add a KV Pool environment checker that validates the hardware, runtime, networking, storage, and software dependencies required for deployment. - PR2: Add a fixed-SLO capacity search tool that identifies the maximum sustainable concurrency and throughput under configurable TTFT and/or TPOT latency constraints. ### 1. KV Pool Environment Checker #### Requirement Validate whether a target environment is ready for KV

title: [Bugfix] Keep all SWA layers when V4.1 cache groups are uneven
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `group_cache_specs()` in `vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/cache_config.py` transposes the per-tuple SWA layer columns with `zip(*swa_columns)`. `zip` silently truncates to the shortest column, so when the SWA layers do not divide evenly across the KV source tuples, the tail layers are silently dropped. A reduced 15-layer backbone over 4 KV sources distributes the SWA layers as `[4, 4, 4, 3]`; `zip` emits only 3 groups and drops layers 12/13/14, so the reduced checkpoint fails to start with `AssertionError: Some layers are not assigned to any group`. This PR replaces `zip` with `itertools.zip_longest` and filters out the `None` padding, keeping every SWA layer. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No user-facing API/interface change. Bug fix only: reduced-layer DeepSeek V4.1 checkpoints now start instead of raising an assertion. ### How was this patch tested? - Added `test_uneven_swa_columns_are_not_truncated` in `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_cache.py`, which builds a 15-layer / 4-KV-source spec set and asserts all 15 SWA layers are retained. Verified on NPU (Atlas 800 A2): with the fix the grouping is `[8, 3, 4, 4, 4, 3]` (15 SWA layers kept); without the fix the same input yields only 12. - End-to-end: a 15-layer reduced checkpoint (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w8a8-N15`) loads and serves with this change, which previously failed with the assertion above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba15685ab7f4f5fbed8630bbb7441f8837e76fbe

title: [Feature] Decoder Append-Prefill for Agentic Scenario Prefiller Offloading
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Agentic workloads often have long inputs—tens of thousands of tokens from user and system prompts—but short outputs, such as tool-call instructions of around a hundred tokens. In P/D-disaggregated serving, this imbalance concentrates pressure on Prefiller instances. Even when multiple Prefillers serve one Decoder (nP1D), a fixed P/D ratio cannot dynamically adjust prefill capacity to fluctuating request rates, leaving Prefillers vulnerable to sharp load increases and queueing during request bursts. Successive turns in an agentic session often extend the same conversation history, so the Decoder that served an earlier turn may still hold a reusable prefix in its KV cache. This creates an opportunity to attempt prefill for a follow-up request on that Decoder, reusing the cached prefix and computing the uncached suffix to reduce Prefiller load. This PR introduces Decoder Append-Prefill to support this approach, with a fallback to the Prefiller when no usable local prefix remains. - Add `decoder_append_prefill_proxy_server.py` to route subsequent requests from the same session to its owner Decoder instance and owner DP rank. - Check actual local KV-cache hits in the Scheduler before admitting Decoder-local prefill. If no usable local prefix remains, reject the local attempt before generating output so the proxy can retry through the Prefiller and the normal P/D path. Otherwise, reuse the prefix and perform append-prefill on the Decoder. - Enable append-prefill admission through `scheduler_config.decoder_append_prefill_enable` in each Deco

title: [Refactor][Feature] Remove compress attention manager for DeepSeek V4
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR attempts to remove the Ascend special `CompressAttentionManager` for deepseek V4. DeepSeek V4 compressed MLA has two distinct block-size domains: - The logical raw-token span used by the scheduler, prefix hashing, allocation, and KV connectors. - The physical compressed page size used by Ascend cache tensors and kernels. Previously, vLLM-Ascend exposed the physical size as `KVCacheSpec.block_size` and used a custom `CompressAttentionManager` to multiply or divide token counts by `compress_ratio`. This duplicated upstream cache-manager behavior and required compression-specific adjustments throughout the scheduler, workers, prefix cache, and connectors. This PR aligns compressed MLA scheduling with the upstream vLLM contract while preserving the Ascend-specific physical cache layout. The main changes are: - Expose compressed MLA block sizes in logical raw-token units: - C4: `block_size = physical_block_size * 4` - C128: `block_size = physical_block_size * 128` - `storage_block_size = physical_block_size` - Keep `--block-size` as the Ascend physical tuning knob supporting 32, 64, and 128. - For example, physical block size 128 produces C4 logical size 512 and C128 logical size 16384. - Register compressed MLA specs with upstream `FullAttentionManager` and remove `CompressAttentionManager`. - Use logical block sizes for: - scheduler allocation and admission limits - prefix hashes and cache-hit boundaries - block-table sizing - AscendStore and Mooncake keys - P/D and context-parallel raw-token coverage - Use physical storage block

title: [Feature][Refator] Decouple the allocation of SFA kv and indexer cache
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR allocate SFA MLA and indexer caches through separate KV cache specs while keeping Ascend-specific physical tensor layout and binding. We add a cache-only indexer metadata backend so split indexer cache groups do not construct SFA attention metadata. In our earlier implementation, the allocation of physical indexer cache tensor is along with normal SFA kv cache, i.e. : ``` layers.0.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor, dsa_k_tensor) layers.1.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor, dsa_k_tensor) layers.2.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor, dsa_k_tensor) ... ``` **proposed change** This PR follows the design in vLLM. We introduce a new **AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec** for SFA indexer cache alone. AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec and AscendMLAAttentionSpec are grouped into a UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs. Now the allocation is like: ``` layers.0.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor) layers.0.self_attn.indexer.k_cache --> AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec --> dsa_k_tensor # Full indexer layer layers.1.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor) layers.1.self_attn.indexer.k_cache --> AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec --> dsa_k_tensor # Full indexer layer layers.2.self_attn.attn --> AscendMLAAttentionSpec --> (raw_k_tensor, raw_v_tensor) layers.2.self_attn # Sharing indexer, no physical indexer allocation ... ``` In terms of saving indexer cache, this PR takes the same effects as #11065 .

title: [Bugfix] Ensure full range load of kv pool when enabling prefill layerwise offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR fixes the following 2 bugs when enabling layerwise prefill offload: 1. #16947 introduces a special mechanism for optimize KV pool: a block's all-rank presence is cached per (group, block_hash) with a 30s TTL and a 200k-entry cap, and a cached miss short-circuits the whole group with zero RPCs. This is reasonable for ordinary layerwise kvpool, but causes trouble when enabling layerwise reuse for prefill offload in cases that some requests hit prefix cache. The key difference is that: - Ordinary layerwise AscendStore still assumes that every layer has its own device cache tensor. So hit blocks from device and kvpool are essentially different. The hit blocks from device can be safely retrieved, while the missed blocks from kvpool can be recomputed by model forward. - However, when enabling layerwise reuse, the cache tensors are sharing a small number of buffers (for example 3). So "hitting blocks from device" still needs to be retrieved from kvpool. And if these blocks are missed, there is no recomputation guaranteed. In conclustion, this PR proposes to disable this mechanism for layerwise offload. The behavior of ordinary layerwise kvpool is kept unchanged. 2. Layerwise offload introduces independent layers and shared buffer layers. When we set independent layers to be layer 0, we cannot simply share the metadata across all layers as they might have different load ranges. Thus this PR also proposes to dispatch the share metadata build between these two components. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? ### How was

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix an uninitialized residual-mass read when Model Runner V2 uses block verification with draft logits on `releases/v0.32.0rc`. This specific double exclusion is limited to the v0.32 integration: v0.31 lacks the grid-dependent guard, while v0.33 and current main use explicit bonus-row detection. No changes to those branches are needed for this issue. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Block verification with draft logits now computes the final required residual row correctly. No API, configuration, or default changes are introduced. title: [Feature] Add fault tolerance with retry and MC2 scale-down on Ascend NPU
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In DP+EP (Data Parallelism + Expert Parallelism) MoE deployments, a dead DP rank makes the EP all2all on surviving ranks block indefinitely, hanging the whole cluster. Upstream vLLM introduced a fault-tolerance framework (vllm-project/vllm#44428) that detects the fault, aborts in-flight requests and lets an external orchestrator trigger coordinated recovery, but Ascend NPU needs its own backend. This PR provides the complete Ascend NPU fault-tolerance backend in two layers: 1. **Retry-based recovery for transient faults** (foundation). Reuses the upstream `GPUWorkerSentinel` flow (clean worker state + DP-group re-initialization on retry) and adds the NPU-specific pieces upstream cannot cover: aborts hung NPU communication ops via `torch.npu.npu.set_op_timeout_ms` (new `ft_communication_abort_timeout` ascend config) and applies the CPU distributed timeout to DP-sync process groups, so peer failures surface as exceptions instead of hanging. 2. **Scale-down recovery for MC2** (this PR's focus). When a rank is confirmed dead, retry alone cannot recover - survivors keep routing MoE tokens to the dead EP rank and the all2all keeps failing. This mirrors the upstream GPU `scale_down` flow while adapting the mask, routing and weight layers to Ascend's MC2 all2all backend: - `npu_communicator`: turns the no-op MC2 all2all manager into the owner of the dead-rank mask, encoded as the MC2 `elastic_info` tensor (flag, dense EP size, shared/physical expert counts plus orig-to-dense and dense-to-orig rank tables), rebuilt in place so captured graphs

title: [BugFix][Mamba] Derive attention block size from K+V page to fix mamba slot padding
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The attention block size is derived from the K-only page size (`attn_single_token_k_page_size`) while the downstream padding uses the K+V page size (`attn_token_page_size`) — the two sides are inconsistent. Historical context: the K-only derivation was deliberately introduced in #6887, where K and SSM shared one contiguous tensor (`[k, ssm]`), so aligning the K page with the SSM block was the right constraint for that layout. The three-tensor layout has since been superseded by the unified `page_size_padded` mechanism (the attention page is padded up to the mamba padded page), so the K-only derivation no longer matches the layout it was designed for. Note that the 310P path (`patch_mamba_config_310.py`) already derives from the K+V page via `FullAttentionSpec`. For hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) the inconsistency: - doubles the block size (2048 vs 1024), coarsening the prefix cache reuse granularity - pads the mamba slot to ~2x what it actually needs, wasting KV cache This PR derives the attention block size from the K+V page size, making the padding exactly ssm+conv (zero waste) with no precision impact. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No API or interface changes. The derived block size for hybrid models changes (2048 -> 1024 for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), improving KV cache efficiency. ### How was this patch tested? title: [BugFix][P/D] Surface missing prompt-token details in the PD proxy
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? PD deployments report a 0% KV cache hit rate in EvalScope while the prefiller logs show real prefix-cache hits. The reporting path is: 1. The PD proxy asks the prefiller for a non-streaming completion and reads `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. 2. It overwrites the decoder's `usage` with that value, because in PD the decoder counts the KV it receives from the prefiller as cached and its own count is inflated. 3. vLLM only fills `usage.prompt_tokens_details` when the server runs with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, and it also drops the field when the prefiller had zero cache hits. Since #13040 (v0.27) the proxy always reports the prefiller value; before that it left the decoder value untouched, which is why older releases could show a non-zero hit rate without the flag. This PR keeps the cold-cache semantics but makes the degradation visible and documents the required flags: - Warn once when a prefiller response has no cached-token count, pointing at `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`. - Document the reporting path, the decode-side usage requirement (`stream_options.include_usage` or `--enable-force-include-usage`), and a curl check in the EvalScope guide. - Add `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` to the GLM-5.3-Flash PD Prefill examples (A2 and A3). ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [BugFix][Model] Honor the physical page stride for Qwen4 QSA raw keys
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The Qwen4Exp MRV2 planner sizes a shared raw-key region using its largest per-layer page. A narrower 2048-byte view in a 2240-byte region currently fails initialization with `Qwen4 hybrid page mismatch: view=2048, region=2240`. Accept raw-key payloads that fit and address each physical block with the planner's `block_stride`. Compressed-key page matching remains strict, and oversized raw payloads remain rejected. Related raw-stride work: #21634, #21635, #21654. The actual trigger was reproduced on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8-MXFP, two Ascend950DT nodes with8 NPUs each, TP4 x DP2 + EP, MooncakeConnectorV2, MRV2, `--language-model-only` and MTP3. title: [Feature] Add TopKPerRow aclnn operator (ragged per-row top-k)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [BugFix] Warm eager DeepSeek V4.1 attention before DP serving
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? An eager DeepSeek V4.1 DP worker can finish its first real prefill and then compile an uncached CANNBotDSL QLI variant on its first idle step. Temporary pre-MoE hooks synchronize the device and the EP CPU group, so a faster compiler cannot move its rank into the expert collective before its peers. The hooks are removed on both success and failure. The large pass uses the existing balanced-routing profile context; the idle pass retains the normal idle behavior and both preserve persistent ring state. The change is limited to eager DeepSeek V4.1 on hardware with the packaged cache ABI, DP > 1 and expert parallelism. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Each read drains the NPU queue. The audio tower runs while other requests are decoding on the same engine, so every one of those stalls them too. There is a second cost that is specific to Ascend: device lengths leave `cu_seqlens` on the NPU, and `AscendMMEncoderAttention._maybe_compute_cu_seqlens` ends with ```python return cu_seqlens.cpu() ``` so a device `cu_seqlens` is copied back **once per encoder layer**. Built on the host it is already there and that call costs nothing. This PR patches `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder.forward` and `Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration._process_audio_input` with versions that keep the lengths, the padding mask and `cu_seqlens` on the host, and gather the valid rows with `index_select` on host-built indices copied up by `async_tensor_h2d`. The computation, the shapes and the results are unchanged. **Relationship to vLLM.** This is the change merged on vLLM `main` as [vllm-project/vllm#68099](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68099), currently being backported to vLLM `relea

title: [Performance] Compose fine-grained embedding & LM head TP with standard tensor parallelism
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fine-grained TP shards vocabulary weights along the **data-parallel axis**. When stacked on standard `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, the embedding and LM head knobs used to replace the standard TP sharding with an equal-size fine-grained shard, so every TP rank kept a replicated copy of its slice — a `tensor_parallel_size`-fold redundancy in per-card weight memory and per-step weight reads. Both knobs now **compose** with standard TP: the vocabulary is sharded over the combined `finegrained_size × tensor_parallel_size` grid (`shard_rank = tp_rank * finegrained_size + fg_rank`, the linearization PCP_X_TP already uses), and one TP collective afterwards completes the vocabulary result — an all-gather for the LM head, an all-reduce for the embedding. The padding granularity is raised to `lcm(padding_size, shard_count)`. With `tensor_parallel_size == 1` the behavior is unchanged. For example, with 8 ranks (`dp=4 × tp=2`, `lmhead_tp=4`): | global rank | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **old** shard (`lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | | **new** shard (`tp.rank * 4 + lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 4 | 1 | 5 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 7 | - Draft-model heads resolve through the same plan; the DFlash2 candidate exchange appends the same TP all-gather so its Top-K union spans all composed shards. - `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/Fine_grained_TP.md` documents composing instead of replacing. ### Measured results (single-node stacked deployment) Atlas 900 A3 (16 NPUs), MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-W8A8, DP4 × TP4 / EP16, DSpark s

If maintainers would rather see this > on `main` first and cherry-picked back, say so and I will retarget it. Three changes that together make Qwen3-ASR serving on Ascend substantially faster. The tower's attention is varlen `cu_seqlens`, and the layer reads those back to the host (`actual_seq_lengths`), so it cannot be captured as a full graph and would need one graph per distinct shape. The patch re-implements the layer attention as batched FIA with a boolean attention mask, places each attention window into a fixed-width grid row, and captures the encoder layers and head once per window-count bin. One graph per bin then serves an audio of any length, and the mask is a tensor input so its values are re-read on each replay. This code is **Ascend-SACT's**, published as a patch against vllm-ascend v0.23.0 at https://gitcode.com/Ascend-SACT/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B with no upstream pull request. It is contributed here **with its authors' permission**, with its Huawei copyright kept and the repository's Apache-2.0 header added. The first commit is that code as published , so what came from them and what we changed is visible in the history.

title: [Feature][Engram] Shard shared host tables across A2/A3/A5 owners
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Distribute one immutable DeepSeek Engram table across static owners on A2, A3 and A5. Independent serving instances retain their own TP layouts and request state, while each owner stores only its assigned rows. This reduces the table capacity required on one host; it does not further reduce aggregate table bytes compared with a shared single owner. This is the combined follow-up to merged #19528 and #20612, and incorporates the static sharding scope from #21245. It uses the merged backends rather than introducing the old A3 native-VMM stack. Qwen PLE remains separate in #21638. - **A3:** owners join one MemFabric group and contribute rank-local shards to one packed BM object. Logical tensor regions are GiB-aligned so lookup chunks cannot straddle independent mappings. Per-layer clients share the process mapping with reference counting and retain owner leases until their device access is retired. - **A2/A5:** one HIXL engine and registered receive buffer fetch rows from the ordered owners. Requests are partitioned by row range, dequantized, and restored to their original positions. Owner requests are sequential; no speedup is claimed. - Validate checkpoint identity, shard order/ranges, layouts and A3 group membership. Reject new access once teardown starts while allowing failed cleanup to be retried. Missing or failed owners do not trigger transparent failover or automatic lease reclamation. ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? Yes. Owners accept `--shard-index` and `--shard-count`; consumers use `shared_engram.endpoints`

title: [RFC]: Shared-PCP for Ascend: owner-sharded PCP KV with CANN VMM peer mapping
summary: # [RFC]: Shared-PCP for Ascend: owner-sharded PCP KV with CANN VMM peer mapping ## Motivation. Prefill context parallelism (PCP) on vLLM Ascend partitions a long prompt across ranks. Each rank computes and writes only its own token chunks, but the KV cache is currently allocated as a complete replicated slot on every PCP rank. The attention kernel already consumes the same logical layout on every rank, so most of that replication is not required for the prefill computation itself. It costs HBM proportional to the PCP degree and directly reduces the headroom available for weights, activations, and `max_num_batched_tokens`. Upstream vLLM RFC [#50127](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50127) defines the Shared-CP semantic model: a logical cross-rank object with explicit physical ownership, stable local and peer views, a declared consumer layout, and an explicit publication and lifetime contract. This RFC is the Ascend application of that contract to PCP KV. It is not a new context-parallel algorithm and does not change PCP or DCP rank topology. The goal is to remove avoidable KV replication in prefill while keeping the existing attention path, block-id semantics, and rollback behavior intact. This work is separate from orthogonal PCP/DCP composition ([#12622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/12622)), request-sharded draft execution ([#21632](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21632)), and Engram host-memory placement ([#19970](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19970)). ## Proposed Change. ### Opt-in behavior and fall

title: [BugFix][MoE] Require prefill coordination when the recompute scheduler is enabled
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On a PD-disaggregated decode node with `recompute_scheduler_enable=true`, the recompute scheduler can admit local prefill chunks whose token count exceeds the MC2 capacity even though decode itself fits. `should_skip_allreduce_across_dp_group` let the recompute flag bypass the prefill/cudagraph precondition entirely, so each DP rank used its local token count: some selected MC2 and others AllToAll (and FULL vs NONE graph modes). The ranks then entered different collectives, which can hang stream synchronization. The skip is only safe when the whole runnable input range maps to one communication method and one graph mode. Keep the existing `prefill_must_use_mc2 and uniform_cudagraph_mode` precondition for every skip; the recompute flag no longer bypasses it. This matches the analysis in #22002: local tokens `[18, 384]` with a 192-token MC2 capacity must coordinate. Fixes #22002 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes, as a correctness fix: PD decode deployments with `recompute_scheduler_enable=true` no longer skip DP metadata coordination when local prefill can cross the MC2 capacity, avoiding stream-synchronization timeouts. Deployments whose runnable range already fits MC2 and uses one graph mode keep the skip. ### How was this patch tested? - New CPU unit test `test_recompute_scheduler_does_not_bypass_prefill_coordination` in `tests/ut/test_utils.py`. title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add HCCL batch-sharded DSpark sampling for DeepSeek V4.1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR introduces an HCCL-based batch-sharded sampling implementation for DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark on Ascend NPU. The implementation extends the existing upstream batch-sharded sampling infrastructure to the Ascend DSpark speculative decoding path, enabling request-level sharding of both target-side sampling and DSpark draft sampling. #### Motivation Under tensor parallelism (TP), each rank computes a local vocabulary shard. The upstream batch-sharded sampling design avoids materializing full-vocabulary target logits on every rank by using local logits computation and All-to-All communication. However, DSpark draft generation has an additional sequential Markov chain sampling process. Replicating this process across TP ranks introduces redundant sampling computation. This PR extends request-level sharding to DSpark draft generation on Ascend, allowing each TP rank to independently execute the Markov chain sampling process for its assigned requests. #### Background and Related Work This implementation builds upon the following upstream work: - [vLLM #50465](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50465): Introduces batch-sharded sampling for Model Runner V2. It shards target sampling inputs and logits across TP ranks, using `compute_logits_local` and All-to-All communication to avoid redundant full-vocabulary logits materialization. - [vLLM #63554](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63554): Introduces batch-sharded draft logits caching, reducing per-rank draft logits cache allocation. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [Performance] Cache fusion compilation results to reduce warm-start latency

title: [Performance][Attention] Optimize fused_sparse_attention_overlap kernel on A3
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The `fused_sparse_attention_overlap` operator (poolingSFA) uses KV offload, but the current kernel is not fully optimized: the H2D communication takes a long time, communication and computation are not well overlapped, and the hardware resources are not fully utilized. This PR optimizes the kernel on the arch22 (A3 / ascend910_93) path: - **Row-partition parallelism**: set `workerCount = GetBlockNum() * 2` so every AIV subcore joins `RunAllCoreSelectionUpdate` (plan=off, bs>24: **-19% ~ -42%** on the selection-update path). - **Pair-sort**: sort hit pairs by slot number so the paired-copy stride is always positive (copy issue count **-33%**). - **Writeback path**: skip transposition re-derivation (4 GM scalar reads), read back only tokens actually written, and scan one pair at a time. - **UB direct write**: flush update entries to the selection cache while data is still in UB; collect-always + full-batch zero-window mask; `directWrittenWindowMask_` lets the writeback path skip windows already handled (hit ratio 0-70%: **+10% ~ +12%**). - **Windowed two-phase MergeKv main loop** with branch-free batch plan decode (Phase A single-array scheme). - **Idle-core helper mechanism**: idle cores assist MergeKv via done/credit handshake rings placed in an independent workspace area (`+2*actCoreNum*64*8*4` bytes in tiling); supports plan/LRU paths and update-writeback sharing, gated to full coverage (bs<=12); SyncAll narrowed to helper launches with per-launch handshake zeroing. title: [RFC]: Add a process watchdog for stalled-process diagnosis in vllm-ascend
summary: ### Motivation. vllm-ascend serves LLMs from several long-lived processes: the engine core (including one per DP rank), the multiproc workers, and the shared-memory IPC channels between them. When one of these processes stalls — a deadlock, an NCCL/IPC hang, an infinite loop, or a driver hang — there is often no crash: no exception, no error log, and no core dump. The service just stops making progress, and the only available remediation is a manual restart, which destroys the evidence needed to find the root cause. Operators are left with a "hung" service and no diagnostic information about where its threads were blocked. The goal of this RFC is a passive, low-overhead liveness monitor per process: whenever a process fails to make progress for a configurable timeout, it automatically dumps the stacks of all its threads to a log file, giving an actionable snapshot of where the process is stuck. The mechanism must: - have no performance impact on the hot paths (a single atomic write per feed), - not false-trigger when a process is legitimately idle (waiting for input or for IPC data must count as "alive"), - produce stack dumps that are easy to correlate with the process's own log files. ### Proposed Change. ## 1. Core watchdog primitive: `vllm_ascend/common/utils/watch_dog.py` A process-local singleton `WatchDog` (obtained via `get_watch_dog()`) with: - `setup(name, timeout=300, check_interval=10)` — configures the per-process identity and the liveness contract. Defaults: 300 s timeout, 10 s check interval. The name ("engine" / "worker" / ...) identifies the process role. -

title: [Performance][DSv4.1] Avoid full-capacity MTP hidden-state copies under compile
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With DeepSeek V4.1 + MTP/DSpark under `compilation_config.mode=3`, the model writes its persistent MTP hidden-state buffer with a slice in-place copy inside `forward()`: ```python num_tokens = hidden_states.shape[0] self._mtp_hidden_buffer[:num_tokens].copy_(hidden_states.flatten(1)) ``` The buffer is sized for the **prefill** capacity (`max_num_batched_tokens * hc_mult * hidden_size` = `[32768, 20480]` bf16 = 1.25 GiB), while a decode step only writes the active rows (24 in the measured workload). AOT functionalization must expose that mutation as a graph product, so the slice write becomes a `slice_scatter` over the whole allocation plus a copy-back: **two full-capacity TensorMove kernels per target replay = 2.5 GiB of D2D traffic**, i.e. moving 2.5 GiB to preserve ~0.94 MiB of state. At ~1.46 TB/s this is already ~90 % of the device HBM peak, so it is pure bandwidth waste. This PR treats the buffer as graph-external state, the same way KV caches and other `no_compile_layers` entries are treated: - register the buffer in `compilation_config.static_forward_context` under a unique key (duplicate keys raise, so a silent overwrite is impossible); - perform the prefix write together with the existing `hc_collapse` inside one `direct_register_custom_op(..., mutates_args=[], fake_impl=..., dispatch_key="PrivateUse1")` that looks the buffer up through `get_forward_context().no_compile_layers[key]` at execution time; - return the collapse result from the op, so the state update stays on the model's output dependency path and cannot be DCE'd

title: [Feature][Proxy] Add group-balanced sticky prefix affinity
summary: Follow-up to #19708. ### What this PR does / why we need it? #19708 added opt-in prefill session affinity using stateless rendezvous hashing. This improves prefix-cache locality, but two cases remain: 1. Requests with the same reusable leading prompt but different suffixes can produce different fallback affinity keys. 2. Rendezvous hashing does not account for the number of distinct affinity groups already assigned to each healthy prefiller. This PR adds opt-in group-balanced sticky prefix affinity to the disaggregated P/D proxy while preserving the existing default behavior. #### Code design - `--prefill-affinity-policy {rendezvous,group-balanced}` selects the routing policy. The default `rendezvous` policy remains stateless and compatible with #19708. - `--prefill-affinity-prefix-chars N` optionally limits only the first user message's string content or first structured text part when constructing the fallback identity. The limit is measured in Python characters, not tokens; `0` retains the full content. - Identity precedence remains `X-Session-Id` > nonempty request `user` > first-user-message fallback. Explicit identities are not truncated, and the request sent to the model is not modified. - The fallback identity still includes the model and preceding system/developer messages, and uses canonical JSON plus SHA-256. The group-balanced policy maintains two indexes in `SharedProxyScheduler`: ```text affinity key -> prefiller endpoint prefiller endpoint -> set[affinity key] ``` Under the scheduler lock: 1. A retained assignment remains sticky while its prefiller is healthy

It validates the physical topology before exposing the replicated query view. Other drafts, threads and invalid configurations retain upstream validation. No upstream vLLM source files are changed. - Copy the prepared draft's device sequence lengths to the CPU with blocking `copy_`, including DCP>1. This uses rejection-corrected lengths rather than the target CPU upper bound plus draft width. title: [Feature] Support Qwen4-Exp batch-invariant execution on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen4-Exp can produce different attention outputs for the same request when its batch companions or physical KV page allocation change. In batch-invariant mode, select the CANN v8 non-split GBSA schedule and pack selected KV blocks in a stable logical order before calling the existing CANN operator. Process at most 32 query rows per packing chunk to bound temporary storage. Declare batch-invariance capability for the QSA/PLE auxiliary cache backends and the Ascend fused GDN backend. Reuse the existing QSA backend alias for release/main compatibility. With effective EP enabled, select AlltoAll consistently across token counts; without effective EP, retain AllGather. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Adds Qwen4-Exp support for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on Ascend. The GBSA path requires the CANN v8 metadata layout and rejects unknown layouts before mutation. Disabling split-KV scheduling reduces available parallelism and packing adds memory traffic; no throughput improvement is claimed. The QSA/PLE capability patches retain upstream backend class identity and are installed when the Ascend model module loads. They can be removed once equivalent capability handling is available upstream. The metadata-layout validation set is worker-local, stores only validated device identities, and assumes the loaded CANN library is fixed for that worker's lifetime. ### How was this patch tested? - Added 34 CPU GBSA cases covering metadata validation/non-split scheduling, FP16/BF16 packing, noncontiguous input strides, partial/empty sele

title: [Performance] Avoid repeated block_hash_to_str conversion in _alloc_gvas_for_save

title: [Feature][Profiler] Add layerwise receive queue profiling
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add an opt-in profiler for the layerwise receive queue to investigate head-of-line (HOL) blocking in Ascend Store. Each task is associated with its request, layer and group. The timeline separates queue residence, save CPU/NPU waits, gate condition/NPU waits, metadata construction and backend calls. Readiness samples identify cases where a blocked head has a follower whose dependencies are all satisfied. The patch also adds trace analysis, a serving benchmark and usage documentation. Measurements cover Memcache GVA and Mooncake key-based transfers, buffer reuse, independent layers, shared-buffer counts, prefetch depths, and concurrency 1/4. Across Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Qwen3-1.7B and SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, the investigation found no repeatable HOL opportunity. The recommendation is to retain FIFO. Addresses #14149; related to #9079. Ascend community task: https://www.hiascend.com/activities/task-center/details/2acb7e4a8e0a440bbaadffcb30814be2?menu=guide ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/21323.yaml`. Users can enable profiling through `kv_connector_extra_config`: - `layerwise_trace_path`: output prefix; profiling is disabled when omitted. - `layerwise_trace_capacity`: maximum retained events and task probes, default 100000. - `layerwise_trace_interval_ms`: readiness sampling interval, default 1 ms. Snapshots are written every five seconds and at connector shutdown. FIFO scheduling remains unchanged. When disabled, the profiler creates no observer thread, records no events

The implementations already differ in vocabulary masking. Upstream bounds candidate IDs by the draft selector vocabulary. Gather across PCP first and TP second. Candidate gathering continues to exchange local TopK scores and token IDs. 3. Delegate Ascend DFlash2 candidate selection to the shared processor once the paired vLLM version includes the hook. Keep the selector vocabulary bound, output multiplier, soft cap, and unquantized LM head requirement. ## Validation 1. title: [BugFix] Enable layerwise KV save hooks for DeepSeek V4.1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 executes attention through its dedicated `dsa_v41_forward` custom operator. The Push connector resolves the cache name to the physical layer and its associated caches, allowing eligible KV transfers to start during the forward pass. This is the model-side follow-up to #20940. The connector must initialize the current step's producer send state before the model forward. The NPU validation below used a local pre-forward initialization adjustment in the connector/vLLM runner; that adjustment is a separate integration dependency and is not included in this model-hook PR. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Existing connector metadata guards continue to skip dummy/profiling calls without attention metadata. ### How was this patch tested? - The updated regression test calls the custom operator's Python implementation and the real save helper. title: [Doc][BugFix] Raise global_segment_size example to 30GB in KV Cache Pool guide
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The `mooncake.json` configuration example in the KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store) guide (`docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.md`) starts from `"global_segment_size": "1GB"`. This PR raises the documented example value to `30GB`, a safe starting default that keeps the guide's configuration usable out of the box. title: [Feature][Observability] Add router replay state metrics for RL
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds `rl:routed_experts_state{state}`, a `basic`-level 0/1 gauge for MoE router replay (routed-experts capture) in RL rollouts. Three states: - `enabled`: `aux_output_config.enable_return_routed_experts` is on. - `ready`: the auxiliary-output data plane is resolved after KV cache init, so capture can start. - `capturing`: the capture hook has run at least once in this process. The three states separate "configured" from "wired" from "actually capturing", so a rollout that enables router replay but never captures routing decisions is visible on the dashboard. Where each state is reported: - `enabled` / `ready`: around the AuxOutput connector setup in `initialize_kv_cache`. `enabled` is written before the data plane is built and `ready` after it succeeds, so a failed setup stays at `enabled=1, ready=0`. - `capturing`: in the existing `RoutedExpertsCapturer.capture` patch. `capture` runs once per MoE layer per step, so the state is latched after the first call instead of being recorded on the hot path. `ready` carries no `rank` label: the TP owner rank builds the buffer, but every rank reports the same stage, so several ranks writing the same gauge cannot disagree. The `handlers` package imports the optional `ms_service_metric` framework at module scope, so both imports are guarded with `try/except ImportError`; router replay keeps working when the metrics framework is not installed. title: [RFC]: Support Online Quantization (load-time weight quantization)
summary: ### Motivation. Upstream vLLM supports online quantization: any BF16/FP16 checkpoint can be quantized at load time with `--quantization fp8_per_channel`, without pre-quantized weights and without calibration data. Upstream reuses its layerwise meta-device loader, so only one layer is BF16-resident at a time and the weight memory drops from 2 to 1 byte per parameter. Currently, vLLM-Ascend also supports some online quantization features: for example, #14852 added support for re-quantizing to MXFP8, and #21817 built upon this to add support for Native FP8; #21987 introduced online quantization from BF16 to MXFP8 for RL scenarios; and #17107 added operator support for online quantization without providing end-to-end capabilities (that PR was ultimately rejected, with the maintainers noting there were no immediate plans to support it). Now, I believe it is time to start aligning our online quantization capabilities and user interfaces with upstream to prevent the two from gradually diverging. vLLM-Ascend supports none of it, through three independent failures: 1. No online name is listed in `NPUPlatform.supported_quantization`, so `--quantization fp8_per_channel` is rejected by `verify_quantization()`. 2. All Ascend linear layers call `quant_config.get_quant_method()` directly from `AscendLinearBase.__init__`, bypassing upstream `resolve_quant_method()`. A pure BF16 model crashes inside CUDA kernel selection; a checkpoint that already carries quantization metadata is silently left in BF16 — no error, no speedup, which is the worse failure mode. 3. Upstream's `_engram_head_shard_weight_loader()` consumes the tensor (`narrow(0, engram_vocab_start, param.shape[0])`, then `param.data.copy_`). Those two hooks live on `WeightTransferEngine` — the trainer class only sends — so this is the side that runs the loader. summary: **What this PR does / why we need it?** Cloze-style requests (`echo=True, max_tokens=0, logprobs=N`) cannot be served correctly by the PD two-hop pipeline: 1. The decode hop receives `max_tokens=0`, which is not a valid generation request; its response cannot carry the echo logprob rows. 2. Backfilling prefill-side rows onto that malformed response misaligns per-token values, which silently corrupts close-probability comparisons (winogrande-style cloze scoring). This PR short-circuits cloze requests to the prefill pool: - `_is_cloze_request()` detects `echo=True + max_tokens==0 + logprobs>0 + prompt + non-stream`; - `build_cloze_request()` rewrites it to `max_tokens=1/min_tokens=1 + prompt_logprobs=N` (vLLM rejects 0) with cross-pool KV transfer disabled; - `handle_cloze_shortcut()` serves it from the prefill pool and `strip_sampled_row()` trims the single forced-sampled token so the reply matches native echo semantics (text rebuilt from remaining tokens, `completion_tokens=0`, finish reason normalized); - scheduling uses `reserve_prefill_kv` paired with `release_prefill_kv` so the active-request counter is unaffected. **Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?** Yes: `echo+max_tokens=0` requests now return correct, aligned logprobs instead of corrupt rows. All other requests keep the existing two-hop path. **How was this patch tested?** On-device PD deployment (TeleChat4-1T, 4P+4D, Ascend 910C): - winogrande cloze logprob evaluation through the proxy (1267 samples): 73.3 (misaligned) -> 76.8 / 76.6 across two runs, matching the 76.6 non-PD baseline; direct-pool refer

summary: Remove the v0.24.0-era monkeypatch of get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank. The patch tolerated a pre-sharded ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var, but that is not the upstream contract after vllm#45026: vLLM slices the un-sharded env (or the full --device-ids list) per DP rank itself. The patch silently turned device misconfiguration into a successful-looking startup and replaced upstream error context with a raw IndexError. - Delete vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_dp_device_ids.py and its registration and documentation entry. - tests/e2e/conftest.py: pass the full un-sharded device_ids list for every executor backend in _run_vllm_runner_dp_worker, so vLLM's per-rank slicing never relies on the env var offset. The Ray branch still pre-slices ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES per DP rank because each DP worker starts its own local Ray instance, which must only see its own NPUs; otherwise independent Ray instances can bind two ranks to the same physical NPU (HCCL EI0015). The full device_ids is passed alongside, so the pre-sharded env needs no patch. Migration: - Affected: application-level DP that pre-shards ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES per rank without passing --device-ids. title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Support KV-sharing layers in MooncakeConnectorV2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A model can let a layer read another layer's KV cache instead of keeping its own, by giving it `kv_sharing_target_layer_name` (upstream examples: Gemma 3n and Gemma 4). Such a *borrower* gets no KV cache spec and no `kv_cache_tensors` entry, so it owns no blocks. The model runner still binds it to its owner's cache (`kv_caches[borrower] = kv_caches[owner]`) and passes that binding to `register_kv_caches`. MooncakeConnectorV2 treated it as an unconfigured layer, so neither a prefill nor a decode instance of such a model could start: ValueError: KV caches contain layers absent from kv_cache_tensors: [...] The owner's blocks are all the KV a borrower reads, so transferring the owner already transfers everything the borrower needs. This PR makes the connector aware of owners and borrowers, rather than special-casing borrowers at the end of registration. **Changes** - New `vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/kv_sharing.py`. It doesn't depend on Mooncake, so other connectors can reuse it: - `get_kv_sharing_targets(vllm_config)` reads the declarations from every layer in the static forward context, not only `Attention`, so MLA layers are covered. - `KVCacheLayerTopology.build(owner_layers, kv_caches, sharing_targets)` splits the registered layers into owners (in `kv_cache_tensors` order) and a read-only borrower → owner map, and validates every borrower. - `MooncakeBaseConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches` builds the topology before publishing anything, then publishes `topology.owner_layers` only. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark on a ModelSlim W8A8_MXFP8 checkpoint (`quant_method: ascend`) built `main_proj` as BF16, so the draft loader failed on `main_proj.scale`. DSA `wo_a` also needs an ND weight of `[n_local_groups, hidden, o_lora_rank]` for `npu_transpose_quant_batchmatmul`. This change keeps that quantized contract and the DSA layout: - Read `quant_method` from the draft checkpoint `quantization_config`. When the checkpoint does not set it, use `vllm_config.quant_config.get_name()`. - Pass `vllm_config.quant_config` into `main_proj` when packed-cache ops are available and the method is `fp8` or `ascend`. - Register the module as `mtp.0.main_proj` so per-layer quant descriptions match the checkpoint name. - Set `wo_a.dsa_wo_a_3d_layout`. W8A8_MXFP8 post-processing then stores the 3D weight and scale, and skips NZ conversion when `skip_weight_nz_conversion` is set. `restore_weights_for_rl_loading` folds a 3D `wo_a` back to the checkpoint shape before an RL reload. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [MRV2][Misc] Expose ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT to diagnose Qwen3.6 prefill overhead
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? CANN caches at most `ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT` compiled operator descriptors per worker process (default `10000`). Model Runner V2 captures the target and the speculative prefill/decode graphs separately, so it browses a larger operator/shape working set: on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (TP=2, MTP=3, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) one worker was observed holding about **9945 entries** right after startup, one warmup away from the default ceiling. Once the cache is full the executor stops reusing descriptors and recomputes tiling and workspace on the host for every call, which a profile shows as `aclnn*GetWorkspaceSize` / `*_Tiling` host time while NPU time stays flat (#21741). This PR makes the knob visible and diagnosable rather than claiming a fix: - register `ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT` in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` so it appears in the generated env-var page; - log a one-shot startup advisory when speculative decoding with ACL Graph is configured without it; - document the profile signature and the before/after procedure in the FAQ; - cover the advisory with unit tests. The variable is not set automatically because CANN reads it when the ACLNN executor is created, which happens before `check_and_update_config` runs. Scope note: in our own A/B runs on v0.30.0 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8, TP=2, MTP=3, 12-wave prefill at 2048 and 8192 tokens) raising the limit did not change the measured wave time beyond run-to-run noise. title: [Performance][LoRA][MoE] Skip idle LoRA routing on TP AllGather
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? In a deployment with LoRA enabled, a request batch may consist entirely of base-model requests and contain no adapter tokens. For non-quantized MoE, the current code still performs LoRA routing restoration and w13 delta injection whenever a `lora_context` exists, even when the batch has no LoRA work. These calls are not free: routing recovery builds the inverse permutation and gathers expert and adapter IDs, while w13 delta injection launches the fused MoE LoRA kernel. Because this work recurs in every MoE layer, a base-model-only batch still pays routing, kernel-launch, and LoRA application overhead in a LoRA-enabled server. For pure-TP AllGather, `has_lora() == False` is a complete local description of the AllGather input: no DP, PCP, or SP rank can introduce adapter tokens from another rank. This PR therefore skips both operations for that idle batch. It does not skip the base MoE GMM, AllGather itself, or any model forward work. This isolation is the performance source: the measured gain comes from removing repeated idle LoRA side-work, with LoRA-disabled execution providing the upper bound. This PR does not change communication context publication. This PR only optimizes pure-TP, non-quantized `MoECommType.ALLGATHER` batches. The fast path requires `ep_size=1`, `dp_size=1`, `pcp_size=1`, and `is_sequence_parallel=False`: 1. When `apply_gmm1()` is in AllGather mode and `has_lora() == False`, it does not restore LoRA routing and does not inject the w13 delta. 2. `forward_impl()` preserves the existing communication context publicati

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Derive the sorted DCP in-group rank in Mooncake Push
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #22129. The decode attention kernel assigns KV stripes by its `dcp_group.rank_in_group`. Push derived that rank as `(tp * PCP + pcp) % DCP`, which is only correct while a DCP group stays inside one TP rank's segment. Upstream vLLM builds one DCP group per segment of `dcp_size` consecutive (TP, PCP) positions; since [vllm@25e9f7b3f2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/25e9f7b3f2) `GroupCoordinator` receives those members sorted by global rank (`pcp * tp_size + tp`). Once a group spans TP ranks (`DCP > PCP`), the PCP and TP ranks interleave, the derived rank points at the wrong decode worker, and the transfer reports success while corrupting two stripes. ## Fix - `_get_remote_dcp_rank()` derives the rank from the destination topology exactly the way upstream builds the group: the segment starts at `lin - lin % dcp_size` with `lin = tp * pcp_size + pcp`, and the rank is the number of members whose in-replica global rank (`member % pcp_size * tp_size + member // pcp_size`) is lower. - `_dcp_groups_sorted()` (a small cached detector) checks whether the installed vLLM sorts the member list, so builds that predate vllm@25e9f7b3f2 (vLLM v0.33.0 and the pinned 2026-11-06 main) keep the legacy TP-major order and behave exactly as before. - The transfer protocol is untouched (no handshake metadata, no mixed-version rejection), so a patched prefill engine paired with an older decode engine stays safe. ## Scope This fixes the FullAttention/MLA push primary path only. Mamba and the pull direction still derive ranks from the TP-major rank; they are tracked in #22

title: [Test][Kernel] Cover GDN fwd_h recurrent state I/O across chunk boundaries
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` writes the GDN recurrent state in three places: it loads `initial_state`, stores the running state of every chunk into `h`, and stores the final state. The kernel keeps the state in hard-coded `[128, 64]` fp32 registers and relies on masked loads and `make_block_ptr(..., boundary_check=...)` stores when `K` or `V` is smaller than the tile. The existing Triton tests (`tests/e2e/nightly/.../triton/test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` and `.../test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h_vllm.py`) only compare the attention output and the `v_new` buffer; `final_state` is never checked. That is why the following failure stays silent on triton-ascend: for `K = V = 32` (any v-head dim below the 128x64 tile), the attention output of a single-chunk sequence is bit-exact, but the state that is stored or loaded is wrong, so multi-chunk prefill, chunked-prefill tails and decode hand-off all continue from a corrupted state. This PR adds the missing regression coverage. The expected state is derived without an external reference, so the test is independent of the `_310p` torch implementation: * for a two-chunk sequence, `h[0]` must be the (zero) initial state and `h[1]` must equal the final state of the first chunk run on its own; * replaying the second chunk with that state as `initial_state` must reproduce the final state of the full two-chunk sequence. title: [RFC]: Residency-aware QSA prefill offload for PP and asymmetric P/D DCP
summary: ### Motivation. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next combines QSA attention/indexer caches with recurrent GDN/Mamba state. Rotating prefill layers through shared HBM buffers can increase logical cache capacity, but a cold-prefix long request still needs its own previous prefill chunks. Zero cross-request prefix hits therefore do not imply zero external history reads. This RFC proposes **residency-aware history restoration for QSA prefill offload**, building on the existing layerwise pool and model-reuse work rather than introducing another connector or storage protocol. The integration target is PD + PP + producer-side DCP + prefill KV offload + MemCache layerwise pooling. The immediate motivation is a measured capacity/performance tradeoff in a field prototype; the proposed general policy has not been implemented or validated on current main. #### Evidence from the field prototype, 2026-11-18 Two Ascend 950DT hosts, eight NPUs per side; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A8 MXFP; TP4/PP2/DP1 on both sides, 24+24 main layers; P DCP2 and D DCP1; block/interleave 512; MTP disabled; P eager/async and D FULL_DECODE_ONLY/synchronous. The prototype used vLLM base `4ba787e` and vLLM-Ascend base `9005a22a`, plus local integration changes. These are base revisions, **not a complete published patch identity**. summary: ## 背景 需要系统验证 DeepSeek V3.2 在 Model Runner V2（MRV2）上的精度与性能，并以 Model Runner V1（MRV1）为基准，确保重构不引入功能或性能回归。 本 issue 由 @wisdom1710 认领，用于跟踪测试配置、真机数据、回归用例及后续问题修复。 ## 验收范围 ### 1. 可复现配置 - 在 `tests/e2e` 或 nightly 增加 DeepSeek V3.2 的可复现配置。 - 记录模型 revision、硬件、CANN / torch / torch_npu / vLLM / vLLM-Ascend 版本、TP / DP / EP、图模式及完整命令。 ### 2. 精度与功能对比 - MRV2 / MRV1 覆盖 greedy、non-greedy、短长中英文及代码 prompt、logprob。 - 固定随机种子时，token / 采样结果满足仓库既有精度规则。 - MTP 投机解码 acceptance rate 对比：记录 MRV2 / MRV1 各步接受长度分布及平均接受 token 数。 - 输出分布对比：在同一 prompt 集上记录 top-k logits 重合度与 KL 散度，作为 token 一致之外的辅助判据。 - 验证模型特有输出可正确解析。 ### 3. 性能对比 - 同配置覆盖多 batch size / sequence length。 - 不同 `num_speculative_tokens`（1 / 3 / 5）下的性能曲线。 - 记录 prefill / decode 吞吐、TTFT、TPOT、端到端延迟，以及设备 HBM 占用对比。 - MRV2 不得有未解释回退；发现差异须修复或提交关联 issue。 ### 4. 特性组合与回归 - 覆盖 MoE / MLA、长上下文、MTP，以及模型实际支持的量化和并行配置的代表性组合与异常 / 边界。 - 提交精度数据表、性能原始数据、结论和新增回归用例。 - 确认现有 MRV1 和其他模型无回归。 ## 环境基线与机器需求 首选基线为 `vllm-ascend/DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8`，采用官方单机 A3 部署形态，覆盖 DP2 + TP8 + EP + MTP + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`，并在相同配置下切换 MRV1 / MRV2。 需要申请 **1 台独占 Atlas 800I A3，16 × 64GB NPU（总 HBM 1TB）**；建议主机内存不少于 1TB，本地可用磁盘不少于 2TB（建议 4TB NVMe）。该任务不默认包含 PD 分离，因此暂不需要四台 A3；若后续增加 PD 分离或未量化全量模型场景，再单独评估多机资源。 ## 当前进展 - 已核对官方 DeepSeek V3.2 部署文档：W8A8 支持单台 16 卡 A3。 - 已确认现有 nightly 测试矩阵使用 `linux-aarch64-a3-800i-16` 运行 `DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8.yaml`。 - 已完成任务 issue / PR 查重，未发现同一验收范围的现有 issue。 - 下一步：先提交可复现的 MRV1 / MRV2 回归测试框架；真机资源到位后补齐精度、性能数据并处理差异。 ## 参考 - DeepSeek V3.2 部署文档：https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/zh-cn/v0.23.0rc1/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V3.2.html - 同类 MRV2 对比任务：#13742（其测试维度可参考；模型为 DeepSeek-3.1、版本不同期，结论不直接复用） ## 关联

title: [Performance][PCP] Overlap local Q projection with global cache preparation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DSA PCP prefill currently runs three things serially per layer: gather/restore the hidden states, prepare the replicated caches (global collectives), and only then compute the local Q prolog. The Q prolog only reads local inputs and weights, so it can be issued on the auxiliary stream while the caller stream performs the unchanged collectives, hiding the Q cost behind communication. This PR enables that overlap for PCP prefill on the existing DSA multistream switch. No new configuration option is added: - `_prepare_caches_and_query` replaces `_prepare_caches_before_attention`: it prepares the caches and optionally returns the Q intermediates produced by this invocation. The base `AscendDSAImpl` implementation returns `(False, None)`, so non-PCP behavior is untouched. - `AscendDSAPCPImpl.__init__` maps the inherited `multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap` value into `pcp_q_projection_overlap` and then sets the inherited flag to `False`, because PCP has already prepared the replicated caches before local attention and must not start a second cache-update overlap on the base path. - `AscendDSAPCPImpl._prepare_caches_and_query` issues `_mla_prolog_single_stream` on the existing overlap stream (`dsv4_dsa_overlap_stream()`) for layers whose PCP metadata has a global prefill and whose local query shard is nonempty. Every collective stays on the caller stream in its original order, empty local shards still join all collectives and skip the Q prolog, and the Q stream is joined in a `finally` block so a failure cannot leave an unsynchronized stream. - `

title: [Feature][Model] Enable compact SP replay for DeepSeek V4.1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Enable DeepSeek V4.1 decoder bounded replay with MRV2 sequence parallelism on main. For a 4,096-token prefill retaining 128 rows at TP8, the late decoder runs on 16 rows per rank. The CPU planner sweeps retained request intervals and original SP shard boundaries in `O(num_requests + TP)` to compute the exchange splits. It reuses the ordered device row buffer already written by the replay metadata kernel: each original rank owns a contiguous slice, and subtracting that rank's shard start produces local indices. No token-by-token CPU expansion or second row-index H2D upload is needed. The device subtraction still allocates its result. Each rank selects its retained local hidden states and pre-mix, packs their original bytes into a shared int8 payload, and exchanges it with one AlltoAllV. The inverse exchange returns both outputs to their original owners with one more AlltoAllV. Packing performs no numerical dtype conversion; decoded outputs retain their original dtype and contiguous layout. Discarded rows and synthetic padding are not sent. Routing IDs are selected directly from the runner's replicated input IDs, including for hash/vision routing. The original full padding mask is retained for local selection and MC2, preserving masked rows within query spans. Neither metadata tensor needs a collective. Per compact SP replica, this reduces the replay-boundary communication from six AlltoAllV plus one AllGather under sharded padding to **two AlltoAllV and zero metadata AllGather**. title: [BugFix][Worker] Preserve padded V1 attention cache page strides
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Target: releases/v0.30.0, based on 972cd38e7e5e5f7f60e6af2ffb56f93f4d787be2. Model Runner V1 can receive a combined attention allocation whose physical pages are individually padded for a shared hybrid cache. Its fallback removes padding from the whole allocation, then builds contiguous K/V views. Those views no longer preserve the relationship between scheduler block IDs and physical pages: writing one logical cache block can modify a different shared page. title: [Performance][SpecDecode] Reuse DSpark metadata during FULL graph replay
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DSpark can build matching draft attention metadata twice within one proposal: once through the upstream proposal path and again when Ascend prepares the FULL graph replay. The second build repeats host metadata construction and the device-to-host sequence-length readback. This PR reuses matching GQA FULL-graph metadata within the current proposal. Reuse requires matching request counts, padded token counts, query boundaries, speculative step and causality. The previous cache is restored on both normal and exceptional exits, preventing metadata from being reused across proposals. DCP, explicit local sequence lengths, non-GQA and non-FULL paths retain their existing behavior. Absent metadata is not cached. Cache hits eliminate the redundant device-to-host sequence-length readback and its associated synchronization and runtime overhead during replay metadata preparation. This reduces CPU–NPU data transfers and can shorten NPU idle gaps by allowing subsequent draft work to be submitted earlier. The first exact sequence-length readback remains. Related work: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46849 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Performance only. No new APIs, configuration options or environment variables are introduced. Model weights, sampling probabilities and attention kernels are unchanged. The optimization reduces duplicate metadata construction and sequence-length readbacks. It does not change the computational work or communication volumes of the model

title: [Performance][Model] Reuse DeepSeek V4.1 routing input IDs across DP/PCP
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In DeepSeek V4.1, every MoE layer prepares identical routing `input_ids` via `all_gather_input_ids()`, followed by INT64 casting and `-1` sentinel normalization. This introduces redundant collective communication and tensor preparation overhead across layers. This PR caches and reuses the prepared routing `input_ids` across MoE layers within the same execution segment. - **Lazy Producer & Buffer Sharing:** The first eligible MoE layer performs the standard `all_gather_input_ids()` and normalization (preserving exact SP/DP/PCP row ordering and padding) into a model-owned buffer with a fixed memory address. Subsequent layers in the same segment reuse this buffer directly, ensuring compatibility with both eager execution and graph capture (ACLGraph). - **Segment Isolation (Normal vs. Replay):** Separate buffers and producers are maintained for the normal decoder prefix and the decoder replay tail, as replay token compaction alters DP row counts. - **Scope & Fallback:** Reuse applies to the runtime `ALLGATHER` communication path. Non-`ALLGATHER` paths and concurrent microbatching safely fall back to per-layer preparation. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. This is an internal performance optimization with no new CLI arguments or environment variables. ### How was this patch tested? #### 1. title: [Performance][SpecDecode] Fix DFlash context tile width to avoid per-bucket Triton recompilation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #20334. `prepare_dflash_inputs_triton()` derived the kernel tile width from the per-step batch shape: ```python max_ctx_per_worker = triton.cdiv(max_target_query_len, workers_per_req) block_size_kernel = min(_MAX_CONTEXT_BLOCK_SIZE, triton.next_power_of_2(max(2, max_ctx_per_worker))) ``` `BLOCK_SIZE` is a `tl.constexpr`, so this turns every distinct tile width (2/4/8/16/32/64/128/256) into a separate Triton specialization. `max_target_query_len` varies with the batch composition on every scheduler step, so during serving the kernel crosses buckets and **Triton recompiles the kernel for every newly seen width, blocking the host for 2.3–3.4 s per first encounter** — while the kernel itself runs in ~10–20 µs. On a Kimi-K3 1P1D deployment this showed up as a bubble between the main model and the DSpark pipeline on the prefill side (#20334), and the first-hit-window P99 TTFT carried ~4.2 s attributable to this kernel (service-level A/B in the issue). This PR fixes the width to the constant `_MAX_CONTEXT_BLOCK_SIZE` (256), which is safe because `workers_for_context = cdiv(max_target_query_len, _MAX_CONTEXT_BLOCK_SIZE)` and `workers_per_req >= workers_for_context`, so every worker's context partition fits in a single masked tile of `_MAX_CONTEXT_BLOCK_SIZE` lanes; lanes beyond the partition are masked off. Note the upstream GPU reference implementation (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`) also uses a fixed constant (`BLOCK_SIZE = 128`); 128 alone would not be safe here because the Ascend context path covers each work

title: [BugFix] Drain async KV loads during wait-mode pauses
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #20466 by adapting [vLLM #60572](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60572) to the Ascend Recompute, DyntraLB and Balance schedulers. title: [Performance]: Fuse multi-group slot mapping into a single 2D-grid Triton kernel with pre-cached params
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Replacement of pr #13340 ### 1. Fused 2D-grid slot-mapping kernel (`ops/triton/slot_mapping.py`) - New `compute_slot_mapping_fused_kernel` uses a 2D grid `(num_reqs + 1, num_groups)`. - Each program handles exactly one `(req_idx, group_idx)` pair, so all KV cache groups execute concurrently within a single launch. - Per-group parameters are accessed through pre-built pointer arrays (`block_table.data_ptr()`, `slot_mapping.data_ptr()`, `block_size`, ...), using the pointer-indirection pattern already used by `batch_memcpy`. - Computation inside the normal path is byte-for-byte identical to the original single-group `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel`. ### 2. Zero-copy param pre-caching (`worker/block_table.py`) - `MultiGroupBlockTable._build_fused_params()` builds the 6 per-group parameter tensors **once** during `__init__`. - These values (`data_ptr`, `stride`, `block_size`, ...) are static after construction, so they are reused on every step — eliminating the ~5ms per-call tensor construction entirely. ### 3. Strategy dispatch & fallbacks - `compute_slot_mapping` now prefers: fused kernel → multi-stream parallel launch → original sequential loop. - Falls back to sequential when DCP is active or Triton is unavailable. Gain: the compute_slot_mapping time from 2.13ms to 0.55ms - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ba07e4a48fc951300d97eb506217dd530583dea3

title: [Performance][Patch] Skip no-op staged-write flushes in Sampler and BlockTables
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The model-runner-v2 staged-write architecture flushes runtime metadata on every `execute_model` step. Two of these flushes run unconditionally even when nothing was staged: 1. `Sampler.apply_staged_writes()` is called on every step, but every sampler sub-state (sampling params, logit bias, bad words, penalties, logprobs, thinking budget, trace replay) stages data only inside its `add_request`, which is only invoked when a new request is scheduled. On steps without new requests each flush still issues ~15 `copy_to_uva` calls. 2. `BlockTables.apply_staged_writes()` calls `num_blocks.copy_to_uva()` unconditionally, although `num_blocks.np` is written only in `append_block_ids`. On platforms with mapped pinned host memory each `copy_to_uva` is a cheap CPU-side memcpy. UVA on Ascend requires PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_mem_register:True. but on the fallback path (triton-ascend 3.2.2 disable the uva feature) every one of them is a real H2D copy with per-call launch overhead. A decode step without new requests or new blocks therefore pays ~15 wasted H2D copies per step. This PR gates both flushes with dirty flags, following the same pattern upstream already uses in `ThinkingBudgetState._budget_dirty`: - `Sampler.add_request` sets a `_has_staged_writes` flag; `apply_staged_writes` returns early when the flag is clear. - `append_block_ids` sets a `_num_blocks_dirty` flag; the instance-level `num_blocks.copy_to_uva` becomes a no-op when the flag is clear. Upstream method bodies are wrapped, not duplicated, so the patch survives upstream refac

title: [Performance] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 VL embed_input_ids to remove per-step copies
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Profiling the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp deployment (`dsv4-vision-exp`) showed ~4ms of copy operations inside `embed_input_ids` on every scheduler step. The cause was that the sentinel-replacement path re-executed avoidable copies per forward: 1. `torch.stack([...]).to(inputs_embeds.dtype)` — the four `image_*` parameters are float32 while embeddings are bf16, so every step re-stacked and re-cast the sentinel vectors. 2. `sentinel_mask & ~is_multimodal.to(input_ids.device)` — `is_multimodal` lives on CPU in this stack, so every step performed an H2D copy of the mask plus a device AND. This exclusion is unnecessary: positions flagged `is_multimodal` are always overwritten afterwards by `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, so the table value written there is dead anyway. 3. `torch.where(...)` allocated a fresh full `seq_len x hidden` tensor per step on top of the `table[idx]` gather. Changes: - Cache the stacked sentinel table in the embedding dtype (`_get_sentinel_table`), built once per model instance and reused for the process lifetime. - Drop the redundant `& ~is_multimodal` exclusion and its per-step H2D copy (safe because `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` overwrites those positions afterwards). - Write the sentinel replacement in place via `torch.where(..., out=inputs_embeds)`, removing one full-sequence allocation per step. After the change, `embed_input_ids` takes ~785us (down from ~4ms+), with the remaining cost being the inherent `table[idx]` gather + `where` memory traffic. benchmark result: origin: ============ Serving Benchmark R

title: [Performance] Reuse head-first QKV storage in GDN prefill to eliminate redundant copies
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Supersedes #21739 and targets `main`. The GDN prefill convolution can expose Q, K and V as sequence-first `[B, T, H, D]` views of contiguous head-first `[B, H, T, D]` storage. The base adaptor currently copies each tensor into sequence-first order, then copies each back into head-first order for ChunkGDN. This round trip costs six layout copies. The adaptor converts each input to a head-first view and packs it only if needed. Dense head-first inputs reuse their storage. A token slice with gaps is packed directly in the layout ChunkGDN consumes. Q and K are normalized over the same final dimension `D`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Eligible prefill inputs automatically skip the six copies on the base device adaptor. No configuration change is required. ### How was this patch tested? On A3, a 2,048-token prefill slice (17 leading tokens removed, 8 Q/K heads, 24 V heads, head dimension 128, BF16) produced elementwise-identical outputs and final recurrent states against the previous PR head (`a04482cce`). Across 24 profiled calls per version, the mean summed Q/K/V copy-kernel time fell from **110.04 to 24.46 µs**: three AsStrided plus three Transpose kernels became three Slice kernels. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `#16292` protected the legacy AscendC recurrent GDN kernel by adding a local per-sequence cap and a width gate in `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`: ```python _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS = 8 use_upstream_recurrent = ... or ( spec_state_indices_tensor.ndim == 2 and spec_state_indices_tensor.shape[1] > _MAX_RECURRENT_GDN_TOKENS ) ``` That number describes the *installed fla_npu OPP*, not this repository. Since fla_npu `#1070` the arch22/arch35 kernel consumes a sequence in windows and has no per-sequence cap, but nothing connects the Python constant to the kernel that is actually installed. Two silent failures follow from a version bump: * bump fla_npu and leave the code alone → `k >= 8` keeps going to the strided Triton kernel forever, with no error and no gain from the new kernel; * delete the cap before the wheel ships it (or delete only half of it) → a 9-token window reaches the single-window kernel, which returns without writing output: the request produces garbage instead of an error. This PR adds a CPU-only tripwire that reads the operator that is installed and fails when the code and the kernel disagree, naming the exact edit: * classify the OPP from what the wheel installs: an `arch22/`/`arch35/` directory means the window-loop kernel (no cap); otherwise the root header's `MAX_MTP = N` is the legacy fixed window. Vendors are visited in the order `opp/vendors/config.ini` declares, so an overlaid tree cannot describe the kernel that does not run. title: [BugFix] Resolve exact Mamba terminal block for async saves
summary: ## Summary - publish the execution-time Mamba circular-slot view from the Ascend model runner - resolve each request's terminal Mamba state to its exact physical block ID before asynchronous AscendStore save - carry the resolved ID in request metadata and use it for the terminal checkpoint without scanning neighboring slots - forward this metadata only through vLLM Ascend connectors; standard vLLM is unchanged ## Problem For hybrid Attention/Mamba models, the retention mask identifies a logical terminal checkpoint, while Mamba execution uses circular state slots.
