title: [Feature]: Add a synchronization hook for indexer cache loading before sparse top-k execution
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Motivation: We encountered accuracy degradation on long-context evaluation datasets when serving GLM-5.2 with vLLM 0.27.1 on two H100 nodes using UCM layerwise external KV cache loading. Our investigation indicated that the indexer could consume its cache before loading had completed. Moving cache loading and completion waits one layer earlier in the connector restored accuracy on the affected workload. This motivates a supported synchronization point before indexer cache consumption, allowing connectors to wait when the data is actually needed. Current limitation: The KV connector API exposes wait_for_layer_load(layer_name), which is invoked from attention-layer execution through maybe_transfer_kv_layer. In the sparse-attention path we investigated, indexer computation and top-k selection occur before the corresponding attention-layer wait hook. Therefore, waiting at that hook does not protect earlier indexer cache reads. The execution order can be: 1. The connector submits the cache load for layer L. 2. Layer L's indexer reads its cache and computes top-k. 3. The attention hook calls wait_for_layer_load(L). 4. Attention executes. If loading has not completed by step 2, the wait in step 3 is too late for the indexer. Registering an indexer cache as an AttentionLayerBase does not itself provide a runtime wait point. For example, DeepseekV32IndexerCache is used for cache specification and binding, while the actual indexer computation executes elsewhere. Proposed feature: Provide a supported synchronization hook before indexer execution

title: [Refactor]Adopt vLLM pluggable kv-cache-dtype mechanism for KV cache
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR adopts the pluggable KV cache dtype mechanism introduced in vLLM (>= releases/v0.33.0). title: [Feature] Support prefill KVPP in Mooncake Push
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Enable prefill-side KVPP with `MooncakePushConnector` for supported non-hybrid MLA/SFA models, including GLM-5.3 W8A8C8. Push previously chose a producer replica by destination rank. With KVPP, that rank can lack the layer's persistent cache, leaving a decode worker with missing data even after all producer ranks report DONE. Reuse the owner map from cache registration. A target layer's persistent owner writes that layer to each decode worker that has it. Replicated MTP caches still select one producer per destination. Decode keeps KVPP disabled. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Set `"enable_kvpp": true` on the prefill node when both nodes use `MooncakePushConnector`. Decode leaves KVPP disabled. Prefill uses DCP=1 when KVPP is enabled. Decode can use the existing Push DCP path with compatible cache layouts. ### How was this patch tested? - **Local CPU/mock** — Used the workspace's existing `vllm-ascend/.venv`, the base branch's pinned vLLM source (`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`), and a temporary dependency overlay for Transformers 5.20.2, huggingface-hub 1.33.0 and tokenizers 0.23.3. title: [BugFix][StructuredOutput] Drop the stale outlines accept_tokens override
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_structured_output.py` wraps `OutlinesGrammar.accept_tokens` and returns `True` as soon as `guide.is_finished()`. That short-circuit predates upstream's own terminal handling: `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_outlines.py` already truncates at EOS, latches `_is_terminated` and keeps `num_processed_tokens` in sync (present in both the verified main and the v0.33.0 tag). With the wrapper in place the grammar never records the terminal token, so the scheduler's speculative rollback asks the guide to roll back more steps than it advanced: ``` ValueError: Cannot roll back 2 step(s): only 1 states stored (max_rollback = 8). ``` It also leaves `is_terminated()` False, so a finished request never reports termination. These are the failures reported in #21974. The fix drops the override and lets the upstream implementation own termination accounting. Upstream's residual behaviour (mask allows only EOS in a final state, EOS is stripped and handled explicitly) covers the case the wrapper was written for. Fixes #21974 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes: it fixes a crash in structured output generation with the `outlines` backend when speculative decoding rolls back tokens after the grammar completed. Release note fragment added separately. ### How was this patch tested? title: [Feature] Bidirectional KV transfer for Mooncake P/D connector (D-to-P KV reuse in multi-turn sessions)
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it Enables **bidirectional KV transfer** in the Mooncake P/D connector for multi-turn dialogue scenarios. After a decode request finishes, the Decode node delay-releases its KV blocks and advertises a content-addressed hash chain. On the next turn of the same conversation, the Prefill node walks its prompt hash chain against the Decode node's chain to find the exact token-alignment boundary, pulls the matched KV blocks via Mooncake, and only prefills the unmatched tail — eliminating the redundant re-prefill of the shared conversation context. **Key components:** 1. **Hash-chain alignment**: sha256-chained per-block hashes (128-token blocks, matching the physical attention-group block size) computed identically on D and P. Longest common chain prefix = exact token-alignment boundary; mismatch safely falls back. 2. **Stateful-model safety**: hybrid models (MambaSpec groups) hold one end-of-sequence state snapshot; a full-sequence alignment gate (tail hash + exact length) restricts pulls to verified boundaries. Attention-only models keep partial pulls. 3. **P-side pull path**: MooncakePullConnectorWorker/Scheduler on kv_producer nodes start recving threads and execute D-to-P Mooncake reads; stale remote blocks are dropped by `remote_blocks_expiry_time` before each pull. 4. **Memory lifecycle**: 3-tier management — proactive expiry sweep every 30s from the sending-thread idle tick, LRU eviction of oldest delayed blocks, and a `decoder_kv_block_budget` cap (default 20% of pool). title: [BugFix] fix sleep mode bug of deepseekv4.1 and add dsv41 ipc e2e test
summary: # [BugFix] fix sleep mode bug of deepseekv4.1 ## What this PR does / why we need it? With --engram-config {"cpu_offload": true} the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables live in registered host memory and the gather kernel reads them over UVA. vLLM's layerwise reload — the path a checkpoint reload and every RL weight update finish through (finalize_layerwise_reload) — parks a layer's tensors on the meta device and materializes them again on the device. For an offloaded table that is a full per-rank device allocation: 22.89 GiB for a 384M x 256 BF16 table over 8 ranks (183 GiB per table at the released size). It cannot fit next to the weights a level-2 sleep keeps resident, so both paths die with torch.OutOfMemoryError. This PR makes the reload host-offload aware and adds the E2E lane that exercises it. #### 1. Host-offload aware layerwise reload — `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_offload_reload.py` (new) The reload's call site resolves the helper through the `layerwise` module (`layerwise.materialize_layer`), so rebinding only `meta.materialize_layer` would leave the upstream implementation in place. Both names are rebound, together with `layerwise._copy_and_restore_kernel_tensors`: * a parameter that carries a host range is rebuilt **on that range**, not with `torch.empty_strided` on the device; * the range is left in place instead of being copied back out of a device copy, so an update written into the table is the update the lookup kernel reads; * parameters without a host range take the upstream path unchanged. Both hooks are upstream internals, so `install()` is defensive: a vLLM

title: [Performance] Skip QSA CPU length sync for Ascend builder
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with MTP can skip the per-decode-step CPU sequence-length synchronization when every metadata consumer accepts the optimistic CPU upper bound and uses rejection-corrected lengths on device. The capability guard already allows the upstream `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder`, but the Ascend runtime instantiates `AscendQSAMetadataBuilder`. Because the guard intentionally uses an exact type allowlist, the Ascend builder misses the fast path and falls back to `num_computed_tokens_event.synchronize()` on every decode step. Profiling shows that this host synchronization breaks asynchronous submission and creates bubbles between decode steps. This PR: - adds the audited `AscendQSAMetadataBuilder` to the exact allowlist for `AscendQSABackend`; - keeps conservative fallbacks for unknown builders/backends, DCP, PCP, sparse KV offload, and real-time/interleaved multimodal inputs; - updates the positive regression fixture to use the actual Ascend builder; - retains an explicit compatibility test for the upstream builder. This is the `main` counterpart of #21589, which targets `releases/v0.32.0rc`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. It removes an unnecessary per-step host synchronization for the supported Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Ascend QSA + MTP path, improving pure-decode throughput and latency without changing the API or configuration. ### How was this patch tested? Latest-main validation: - rebased onto vLLM Ascend `main` at `1f49be4c3`; - `git diff --check`; - `python -m compileall` for the changed implementation

title: [BugFix] Fix Qwen4Exp MTP position cache for long context
summary: ## What this PR does Fixes the long-context MTP position-cache mismatch for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on the main branch while keeping the behavior change scoped to the Qwen4Exp model implementation. When the target model is started with `--max-model-len 1010000` and YaRN overrides, the nested `Qwen4ExpMTP` draft config can still retain `max_position_embeddings=262144`. During long-context graph replay this undersizes the MTP rotary position cache and can lead to out-of-bounds device access, Ascend error 507011, and `EngineDeadError`. ## Implementation - Align the Qwen4Exp MTP draft position-cache capacity with the target `max_model_len` before the upstream draft config and rotary embeddings are constructed. - Apply the adjustment only when the draft architecture contains `Qwen4ExpMTP`. - Grow only a draft using default RoPE; do not copy the target model's YaRN parameters into the draft. - Never shrink an already larger draft cache. - Leave non-Qwen4Exp architectures and non-default draft RoPE configurations unchanged. The runtime change is contained in `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/mtp.py`. No shared worker or speculator module is modified. ## Tests Added Qwen4Exp-specific unit coverage for: - long-context cache growth from 262144 to 1010000 - target YaRN parameters not being copied to the draft - non-default draft RoPE being left unchanged - larger draft caches not being shrunk - other architectures being ignored - alignment occurring before upstream draft-config construction The same model-scoped logic passed 8 targeted unit tests and an A5 end-to-end regression on the release

summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? This PR adds MC2 (matmul-collective) fusion for dense sequence parallelism on the Qwen3.5 family. PR #20756 must be merged first. title: [Performance][DSpark] Fuse V4.1 context KV preparation across draft layers
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark already merges the context WKV projection across draft layers, but the projected KV still goes through per-layer RMSNorm, partial RoPE, and paged SWA cache writes. This PR fuses that post-WKV work for 2–4 eligible draft layers into one Triton launch. The kernel preserves FP32 RMSNorm accumulation, the BF16 rounding boundary before interleaved partial RoPE, and each layer's independent cache stride and slot mapping. The optimized variant limits the RoPE gather to the 64 rotary dimensions and writes the NoPE and RoPE slices directly to paged cache. The existing merged WKV GEMM and RoPE lookup are unchanged. The fused path is attempted by default for 2–4 active draft layers with standard BF16 paged SWA caches on supported A2/A3 layouts and at most 4096 context tokens per invocation. The guard rejects unsupported layouts, packed caches, and RMSNorm configurations with a loaded bias; these cases, single active layers, and larger batches use the original per-layer path. There is no environment-variable switch in the current PR. ### Performance #### Post-WKV KV preparation microbenchmark Measured on an Ascend server using median NPU Event time per call. The measurement covers RMSNorm, partial RoPE, and cache writes across the draft layers; it excludes the merged WKV GEMM, RoPE lookup, and other serving work. title: [Perf][KV Transfer] Avoid full-prompt rehashing after Mooncake V2 truncation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mooncake V2 truncates the final P-side prompt token after `Request` has already hashed the full prompt. The current `clear()` + `update_block_hashes()` preserves correctness, but hashes the entire prompt again on the scheduler path. With an effective request hash block size of 2, a 128K prompt has about 65K hashes, including when most of the prompt is already in the prefix cache. Preserve hashes whose complete dependency windows still fit in the shortened request, and discard only the invalid suffix. This uses the resolved `KVCacheConfig.hash_block_size` and `num_hash_lookahead_tokens`, rather than assuming the CLI/physical KV block size is the request hash granularity. - Delegate to `Request.truncate_block_hashes()` when available. - Backport the same tail-truncation operation for the current verified core pin, which predates that API; clear the prompt-embedding hash memo as the upstream primitive does. - Keep `update_block_hashes()` to fill a missing suffix, and retain the existing full-rebuild fallback when the resolved geometry is unavailable. - Preserve the existing token truncation, producer guard, idempotency marker, and KV handoff behavior. Related to #21437: its description explicitly proposes migrating truncation sites to the upstream primitive to avoid full-prompt rehashing. This PR implements that performance follow-up for the **Mooncake V2 base scheduler**. #21437's hybrid/layerwise changes remain a separate scope. title: [Feature] Add dynamic token deferral, state restoration and rebatching for MoE decoding
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? this PR introduces dynamic token deferral and rebatching for MoE decoding on Ascend, initially targeting Qwen3-MoE on Ascend A3. During expert-parallel decoding, uneven token routing can create imbalanced expert workloads and increase step latency. This implementation uses expert load information to defer selected decode tokens at MoE layer boundaries, allowing the remaining tokens to continue. Deferred tokens retain their intermediate states and resume at the corresponding layer in a subsequent iteration. The goal is to reduce per-step expert workload and communication pressure while preserving the progress of deferred requests. The main changes include: - **Load-aware token deferral:** Introduce device-side token selection and compaction before MoE dispatch, updating routing information and the active-token mask together. - **State preservation and resumption:** Save and restore hidden states, residuals, top-k expert IDs and weights, and request mappings for deferred tokens. - **Attention metadata updates:** Keep positions, slot mappings, sequence lengths, and block tables aligned with the active batch as tokens are deferred and restored. - **Runner and scheduler coordination:** Update request bookkeeping, computed-token counts, and output mappings so that only completed decode work advances request outputs. - **ACL Graph integration:** Use preallocated state buffers and device-side runtime controls to accommodate changes in the active token set during graph capture and replay. This is an initial implementation based on vLLM v0.27.0

title: [Performance][Attention] Parallelize SFA indexer queries within PCP groups
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #21039. title: [Feature][Model] Add Mistral Large 4 support on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mistral Large 4 is not in a vLLM release yet, it lives in draft PR vllm-project/vllm#64534. This adds the Ascend model adapter, registered only where the upstream package exists, so nothing changes on builds without it. Much of the model needs no work here. Upstream gates its hand-fused Triton kernels on `is_rocm()`, so on Ascend the torch reference paths already run, and scalable softmax is correct through `SSMaxScaling`'s own fallback without a new kernel. MLA, the DSA indexer, the shared-indexer schedule, NoPE, YaRN and the FP8 block-scaled checkpoint are all carried by paths we already ship, and the backend selector resolves this config to `AscendSFABackend` unpatched. What does not carry over is everything that assumes q-LoRA. **The query path.** `AscendSFAImpl` reaches for `fused_qkv_a_proj` and `q_a_layernorm` to split a q-LoRA latent; Mistral has neither and projects Q straight from the hidden states. So `AscendMistralMLAAttention` builds the outer MLA modules itself and hands them to `AscendMultiHeadLatentAttention`, and the impl gains a Mistral query branch: project, apply SSMax, then absorb NoPE. SSMax is a per-token/per-head scalar, so applying it before absorption is the same number as scaling the absorbed lane after. NoPE layers project only the 192-wide query and append the model's zero RoPE lane. Because the whole preprocess now lives in the impl, the model's `forward` hands over positions and hidden states and nothing else — the projections, the top-k read and the output projection are all inside. summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it Enables DSpark speculative decoding under PCP+DCP topology by gathering compact KV history for prefill and keeping the draft's DCP KV addressing. title: [Feature] Add history and request-state pool planning interfaces
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Token history and bounded request state have different capacity requirements. History grows with processed tokens, while sliding-window and compressor state is sized by active requests. Planning both through a single block count ties fixed-state storage to history capacity. This PR adds the planning and budgeting interfaces for RFC #21324: - Immutable pool descriptors with allocation units (`token_block` / `request_slot`), physical capacities, and explicit cache-group ownership. - Per-worker accounting for `fixed state + workspace + history blocks × history page bytes`. - Capacity resolution that checks minimum admission requirements and explicit block-count overrides against the full budget. Reserved/null IDs are included in physical capacities exactly once. - Validation of pool IDs, group ownership/coverage, and invalid capacity or byte counts. Worker plans can be rebuilt with an agreed history capacity without subtracting fixed reservations twice. The current Core-owned `KVCacheConfigBuilder` flow resolves `num_blocks` using proportional per-block accounting. A fixed reservation cannot be represented by inflating that per-block cost. These interfaces are therefore separate from `KVCacheConfig`; they provide a CPU-testable foundation for the subsequent Core/MRV2 integration without changing the active builder. The design document describes the contracts, a small allocation example, and the integration boundary. title: [RFC]: Sharing and sharding Engram/PLE tables across instances
summary: Related vLLM RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64002 ## Motivation DeepSeek V4.1 Engram tables / PLE tables can consume substantial host memory. Host offloading reduces HBM usage, but independently launched model instances may still load separate copies of the same immutable tables. This is especially relevant to prefill/decode deployments, where multiple instances serve the same model and may use different parallel configurations. We propose separating **table ownership and physical placement** from **the instances performing lookups**: - **Sharing:** independent instances use one logical copy of the tables. - **Sharding:** multiple owners hold different parts of that logical copy, distributing host-memory consumption across nodes. For example, a 3P1D deployment could share one logical table across all four instances. With four owners, each node could hold approximately one quarter of the table: ```text One logical Engram table ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐ │ shard 0 │ shard 1 │ shard 2 │ shard 3 │ │ owner P0 │ owner P1 │ owner P2 │ owner D │ └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘ ▲ ▲ ▲ ▲ └──── shared by P0, P1, P2 and D ────┘ ``` Sharding distributes the capacity of the shared table across hosts. It does not further reduce total table capacity compared with a single shared owner. ## Design A table owner loads and publishes an immutable table or shard. title: [Bugfix]Rope does not recover after waking up from sleep mode (L2)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix incorrect outputs after `sleep(level=2)` + `reload_weights` + `wake_up` for models using the MLA/MTP RoPE path (`AscendRotaryEmbedding`). **Root cause.** `_record_cos_and_sin_cache_interleaved()` derives two detached tensors (`_cos_cache` / `_sin_cache`, `cos_sin_cache.view(-1, 2, hd).repeat(1, 1, 2).chunk(2, dim=1)`) and caches them in **module-level globals** in `vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py`. Because `.repeat()` materializes real storage, they are allocated inside `NPUWorker.load_model()`'s `CaMemAllocator.use_memory_pool(tag="weights")` scope, so they land in the `weights` pool. But: - they are not `nn.Parameter`/`nn.Buffer`, so `NPUWorker.sleep`'s level-2 CPU backup (`model.named_buffers()`) cannot see them, and `reload_weights` does not restore them either (`vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py:250`, `:286`); - `allocator.sleep(offload_tags=())` (level 2) passes an empty tuple, so nothing in the pool is offloaded — every allocation is `unmap_and_release`d with no CPU backup (`vllm_ascend/device_allocator/camem.py:209-222`), so their physical pages are released and `wake_up()`'s `create_and_map()` only remaps the VA, it does not restore contents; - the cache guard is `if _cos_cache is not None: return`, which is independent of content, so the tables are **never rebuilt**. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Feature]: Compose fine-grained embedding/LM head TP with standard TP — remove the TP-fold weight redundancy in stacked deployments
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `finegrained_tp_config` allows the embedding and LM head knobs to be stacked on standard `tensor_parallel_size > 1` (no `tp == 1` restriction; the feature guide's Scenario 1 is exactly such a stacked example). However, in stacked deployments these two modules shard the vocabulary **only** by the fine-grained group: the standard TP sharding is replaced rather than composed, so every TP rank keeps a replicated copy of its fine-grained slice (`vocab / finegrained_size` per rank) and the TP columns repeat the same sharded GEMM. This leaves a full `tensor_parallel_size`-fold redundancy in both per-card weight memory and per-step weight reads. For DeepSeek-R1-W8A8 with `dp=4 × tp=4` (`lmhead_tp = embedding_tp = 4`), the LM head alone reads ~232 MB of weights per decode step per card; with a composed `finegrained_size × tp_size` grid (16 shards) that drops to ~58 MB (−75%), and per-card LM-head weight memory drops by ~174 MB — the embedding improves by the same factor. Proposal: compose the two grids into one flat sharding (`shard_rank = tp_rank * finegrained_size + fg_rank`, `TP`-outer / fine-grained-inner — the same linearization the PCP path already uses), keep the token exchange on the fine-grained group, and complete the vocabulary result with one TP collective afterwards (an all-gather for the LM head, an all-reduce for the embedding). Raise the padding granularity to `lcm(padding_size, shard_count)` so the padded vocabulary always divides evenly. title: [Performance][MRV2] Reuse V4.1 SWA replay visible lengths
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 bounded replay rebuilds the same per-token SWA visible lengths for multiple SWA groups. Reuse the result in the existing batch-local `common_v41_batch_metadata` dictionary, reducing 20 identical group computations to one. For request `r`, query offset `j`, sequence length `S`, query length `Q`, window `W` and replay floor `R`, the helper computes: ```text p = S - Q + j visible_len = p - max(0, p - W + 1, R) + 1 ``` `query_start_loc` defines request partitions; `seq_lens`, `replay_start` and `num_actual_tokens` define the positions, lower bounds and output range. These inputs are fixed within each shared batch dictionary. The cache key therefore only needs the window and a replay-specific namespace: ```python cache_key = f"replay-swa-visible-lens:w{window_size}" ``` This follows the [existing A5 causal SWA cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/b4a065a85c0e27e921d72e8aca4b9a4f63dd9260/vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v41.py#L1284-L1297), which uses `a5-causal-swa:w{window_size}` in the same dictionary. The replay result uses its own prefix because its visible lengths also depend on the replay floor. It reuses the dictionary and lookup pattern, rather than the ordinary SWA result tensor. Each metadata build creates a fresh batch dictionary. Decoder replay groups share request coordinates and replay floors; the [first SWA layer with a different encoder replay floor already uses an independent dictionary](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/b4a065a85c0e27e921d72e8aca4b9a4f63dd9260/vllm_ascend/models/de

title: [Feature]: Extend HiSparse KV offloading to Ascend A2/A3
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch #### Summary Extend the existing A5 HiSparse implementation to Ascend A2/A3, reusing the shared vLLM HiSparse framework and providing an arch22 operator implementation with native INT8 KV cache support. The goal is to make sparse KV offloading available across A2/A3 deployments while preserving the existing A5 behavior and minimizing hardware-specific changes in the framework. #### Motivation Long-context inference places increasing pressure on device memory. Sparse attention reduces the number of KV entries accessed during decoding, but retaining the complete KV cache on the device still limits context capacity and concurrency. HiSparse provides a way to keep backing KV data in host memory and make the selected entries available on the device for attention. Extending this capability to A2/A3 would: • Reduce device-memory pressure from long-context KV caches. • Enable more flexible trade-offs between device cache capacity, supported context length, and concurrency. • Bring the existing HiSparse framework to a broader installed hardware base. • Avoid maintaining separate scheduling, cache-management, and offloading implementations for each hardware generation. These are intended benefits; achievable capacity and performance gains must be established through hardware validation. #### Proposed implementation • Reuse the A5 foundation: retain the shared HiSparse lifecycle, request-state management, host backing storage, residency resolution interface, and refill workflow. • Support native quantized caches: use INT8 KV payloads and INT8 In

title: [Feature][Model] Support GLM-5.3-Flash DCP and PCP+DCP on A3/A5
summary: **CPU and static checks are recorded below. A3/A5 operator execution, HCCL graph replay, full-model accuracy and performance validation remain pending.** ## What this PR does / why we need it GLM-5.3-Flash's pooled indexer currently rejects DCP. This change adds owner-local KPool selection and routes its main MLA attention through the shared DCP implementation, allowing token-history caches to be distributed within TP or jointly across PCP and TP. The candidate transport follows #20883, while preserving GLM's own scoring formula: reduce the head-weighted query, score complete pools without ReLU, select pools globally, then expand them into token IDs and append the visible incomplete tail. - Shard the main MLA cache and completed KPool keys using the same token ownership. Each rank exchanges fixed-width candidate IDs/scores; it does not gather the indexer's token-history cache. - Preserve global token IDs in shared Top-K buffers. Main SFA gathers query heads, remaps selected IDs to local KV positions, and merges partial attention outputs using softmax statistics. - Reduce local indexer heads in FP32 before PCP communication, preserving BF16 head-weight rounding and the existing FP8 query quantization/dequantization order. Gather one weighted query in global request order instead of separate multi-head queries and weights, then restore local rows after selection and main-attention output merging. Support DCP=PCP and DCP=TP*PCP, including TP2/PCP2/DCP4. - Backport the final SFA-only correction from #21380: preserve global request prefill classification for PCP lookahead shards

title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Preserve DeepSeek V4 DSpark heads during weight loading
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #17094. DeepSeek V4 DSpark maps both target and MTP-specific head/embed/HC checkpoint keys to the same parameters. If `mtp.2.head.weight` arrives before the target `head.weight`, the latter silently overwrites the trained draft head. Unordered shard completion can therefore collapse acceptance while requests still succeed. This change gives MTP-specific parameters priority independently of loading order: - Track the five head/embed/HC destination names already loaded from `mtp.*`. - Skip subsequent target fallbacks for those parameters; allow later MTP weights to replace earlier fallbacks. - Preserve standalone and partial-MTP fallback behavior and the existing rotation guards, without buffering checkpoint tensors. The September 7 W8A8 checkpoint's `optional: {}` exposes the target head/embed fallback path. This is a loader correctness fix, not a change to checkpoint metadata, the forward path, or acceptance rules. The issue contains a tiny checkpoint-free reproducer, the checkpoint comparison, and the regression history (#13506). ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes: checkpoints containing dedicated MTP heads consistently use those heads regardless of shard order, restoring speculative acceptance. There are no new flags or API changes. Target weights remain fallbacks when the corresponding MTP weights are absent. ### How was this patch tested? - Added `tests/ut/model_executor/test_dspark_head_loading.py`: **262 passed**, covering explicit target-first/draft-first order, 128 seeded shuffles, rotation present/

title: feat: quantize the draft model's shared LM head copy online
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds online quantization for **the draft model's copy of the shared target LM head** (EAGLE3/MTP spec decode), building directly on #21706 (online *target* LM head quantization for Model Runner V2). It validates the option, resolves the hardware format, registers the Ascend LM head schemes under internal `"int8"`/`"mxfp8"` keys in the upstream `_LM_HEAD_METHODS` table (lazy factories wrapped in `AscendEmbeddingMethod`), and assigns the resolved format to the upstream `SpeculativeConfig.draft_lm_head_quantization` field **for the draft loading window only** (the field is validated at construction and only accepts the platform formats). title: Fix Engram host registration on CANN driver 26.1.1
summary: ## What this PR does DeepSeek V4.1 (an Engram model) fails to start on CANN driver 26.1.1: the single-shot `aclrtHostRegisterV2` of the full Engram host table (~91.5 GiB) exceeds the driver's new per-call cap (~5.8 GiB) and returns rc=207001. This PR registers the host range in chunks no larger than 5 GiB, aligned to the kernel `CHUNK_ROWS` granularity so each device pointer in `self.ptrs` maps to exactly one registered chunk, in both `HostUvaBuffer` and `SharedUvaBuffer`. `close()` unregisters each chunk and keeps the remainder for retry on failure. Fixes #21566 ## Root cause CANN 26.1.1 caps one `aclrtHostRegisterV2` call at ~5.8 GiB. Verified Engram tables register cleanly (no rc=207001). Note: chunking works around the per-call cap. title: [Feature][WeightTransfer] Add bounded large-parameter HCCL updates
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A parameter larger than `packed_buffer_size_bytes` currently produces an oversized packed HCCL collective and another owning input on the receiver. With a 2 GiB parameter and a 128 MiB bucket, the existing path broadcasts 2 GiB in one collective. This change adds `packed_transfer_mode="bounded"` to split it across capacity-limited collectives while preserving native `load_weights()` and the existing START/UPDATE/FINISH transaction. - Share deterministic byte planning between sender and receiver; no full-size source packing copy is required. - Reconstruct independent, aligned parameter storage. Complete small inputs share loader calls within the same storage budget; at most one parameter is incomplete. Loaders may retain or modify their inputs. - Bound transport-held tensor storage by `K * B + Lmax`. When the payload is smaller than a bucket, receive slots shrink and their unused budget can hold complete inputs. Model/source weights, loader retention and layer rebuilding, runtime workspaces, allocator rounding and reserved memory are separate. - Reuse session-owned streams across updates, wait before copying/reusing each slot, and drain submitted work on errors. One slot is serial; two permit the next receive to overlap current reconstruction/loading. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. `HCCLTrainerInitInfo(packed=True, packed_transfer_mode="bounded", ...)` selects the new protocol. `legacy` remains the default. Mode, bucket capacity and slot count are fixed at initialization. Both peers must support bounded mode;

Ascend-side encoder graph capture is a separate feature; until it exists, running the multimodal encoder eagerly is the supported configuration. After the change the same command reports the new error immediately. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes: a configuration that used to hang now fails fast with an actionable message. title: [BugFix] Keep the scheduling cursor correct on PRIORITY preemption
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [Feature] Support bilateral DCP in MooncakePushConnector
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `MooncakePushConnector` currently rejects DCP greater than one. Enable independent P/D DCP sizes for MLA KV transfer, including different DCP sizes on the two peers (for example, P TP8/DCP4 to D TP8/DCP2). For each layer, intersect the current chunk's ready token interval with both peers' DCP stripes, then translate the resulting blocks through each peer's local block table. Select one complete P DCP replica group for each D worker, so all required source shards contribute without duplicate writes from other replicas. Preserve per-layer events, intermediate-chunk alignment, final partial blocks, empty-stripe progress, and DONE accounting from every P worker. Resolve replicated indexer caches independently on each peer. SWA/circular caches retain their existing layouts. Reject unsupported topologies and misaligned interleaves before issuing their writes. This follows the now-merged #20940. The PR contains the DCP adaptation, tests and documentation only; it does not change the proxy protocol, model hooks, or the runner's initialization sequence. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Users can enable `--decode-context-parallel-size` on P, D, or both with `MooncakePushConnector` for MLA caches. Both sides must use PCP=1, and each DCP size must divide that side's TP size. The peers must have equal kernel block sizes; DCP interleaves must align to kernel blocks and divide their respective logical page sizes. title: [Performance][MoE] Eliminate All2AllV dispatch split host sync
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV._preprocess` currently blocks the host twice per MoE dispatch: - `torch.repeat_interleave(..., num_global_tokens_per_local_expert.ravel())` infers its output length from device values, causing an implicit D2H copy and stream synchronization. - The single-local-expert path calls `torch.npu.synchronize()`. This PR keeps the split accounting on device and defers host access: - Reuses pinned CPU staging buffers for the two split D2H copies. - Guards both copies with one NPU event instead of synchronizing in `_preprocess`. - Enqueues `npu_moe_token_permute` before waiting on that event. - Copies the split values after the event so returned numpy metadata does not alias the reusable staging buffers. - Passes an explicit `output_size` to `repeat_interleave`. - Removes the full-device synchronization from the single-local-expert path. No environment variable, public API, or user configuration is added. The `MoEAllToAllCombineMetadata` contract is unchanged. This implementation also addresses the pinned-staging race discussed in #17670. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. All2AllV MoE dispatch no longer performs synchronous split D2H copies or the single-local-expert full-device synchronization. A3 measurements show a 7.9% reduction in host dispatch time and a 0.63% reduction in 8K-prefill TTFT. A release note fragment is included. ### How was this patch tested? ## Tested revisions | Revision | Purpose | |---|---| | `4b3bd7ebe51094f3afa5288bb7a3316d12d3154e` | Current upstream/main base | | `9

title: [BugFix] Tile wide BF16 DequantSituQuant rows within UB capacity
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? BF16 `dequant_situ_quant` currently allocates UB buffers for a whole input row. Wide rows fail Host Tiling's capacity check before the kernel runs: inputs of width 33792 and 67584 require 355872 and 710688 bytes respectively with a reported UB budget of 196352 bytes. Select an aligned BF16 column tile from the available UB capacity and allocate input, intermediate, and output buffers for that tile. Read corresponding columns from both gate/up halves. For rows spanning multiple tiles, first compute the whole-row absolute maximum, then recompute each tile and quantize with the same row-wide scale. Small rows retain a single-pass path; the INT32 path retains its whole-row capacity check. Add 25 parameterized regression cases covering narrow/alignment boundaries, the observed UB tile boundary, wide rows and tails, multiple rows, activation direction, zero input, and grouped row counts. A maximum in the last column checks that quantization uses a whole-row scale rather than separate per-tile scales. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. BF16 wide rows that exceed the whole-row UB budget can execute using bounded tiles, preserving the existing INT8 output and per-row FP32 scale interface. Bugfix release-note fragment: `release_notes/fragments/21724.yaml`. ### How was this patch tested? **Main + PR hardware validation completed on November 12–13, 2026:** - Tested vLLM-Ascend main `3f1de8b04de8feab92587439b24e2cbf67133720` plus this PR head `b1abd5765614311f7d3a89b2526cd620d169f363`, integrated as `6870729aa1c2dc384bc894de

title: [Feature] Bidirectional KV transfer for Mooncake P/D connector (D-to-P KV reuse in multi-turn sessions)
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it Enables **bidirectional KV transfer** in the Mooncake P/D connector for multi-turn dialogue scenarios. After a decode request finishes, the Decode node delay-releases its KV blocks and advertises a content-addressed hash chain. On the next turn of the same conversation, the Prefill node walks its prompt hash chain against the Decode node's chain to find the exact token-alignment boundary, pulls the matched KV blocks via Mooncake, and only prefills the unmatched tail—eliminating the redundant re-prefill of the shared conversation context. **Key components:** 1. **Hash-chain alignment**: sha256-chained per-block hashes (128-token blocks, matching physical KV block size) computed identically on D (over prompt+output) and P (over next prompt). Longest common chain prefix = exact token-alignment boundary; mismatch safely falls back to conservative bounds or full re-prefill. 2. **Stateful-model safety**: Hybrid models (Qwen3.5 HMA with MambaSpec groups) hold one end-of-sequence state snapshot per request—a partial-prefix pull would produce wrong initial state. A full-sequence alignment gate (tail hash + exact length) restricts pulls to verified boundaries for such models; attention-only models keep partial pulls. 3. **P-side pull path**: `MooncakePullConnectorWorker` on the kv_producer node starts a receiving thread and executes D-to-P Mooncake reads (previously gated on `is_kv_consumer` only). 4. **Streaming kv_transfer_params backport (PR #40186)**: Captures the Decode node's bidir metadata from streaming responses by wrapping `RequestOutpu

title: [Performance]: Avoid full-capacity MTP hidden-state copies when DeepSeek V4.1 runs compiled (mode=3)
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance With DeepSeek V4.1 + MTP/DSpark and `compilation_config.mode=3`, the model writes its persistent MTP hidden-state buffer with a slice in-place copy inside `forward()`: ```python # vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/model.py (main) num_tokens = hidden_states.shape[0] self._mtp_hidden_buffer[:num_tokens].copy_(hidden_states.flatten(1)) ``` The buffer is sized for the *prefill* capacity, not for decode: ```python self._mtp_hidden_buffer = torch.empty( vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens, # 32768 self.hc_mult * config.hidden_size, # 4 * 5120 = 20480 dtype=vllm_config.model_config.dtype, # bf16 ) ``` so it is `[32768, 20480]` bf16 = 1.25 GiB, while a decode step only writes the 24 active rows. Under `mode=3`, AOT functionalization must expose the mutated buffer as a graph product, so the slice write is rewritten into `slice_scatter` over the whole capacity allocation plus a copy-back. That is **two full-capacity TensorMove kernels per target replay = 2.5 GiB of D2D traffic**, i.e. moving 2.5 GiB to preserve ~0.94 MiB of useful state. Proposal: treat the buffer as graph-external state (the same way KV caches and other `no_compile_layers` entries are treated) and perform the write together with the existing `hc_collapse` in a custom op: - register the buffer in `vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context` under a unique key; - fetch it at execution time via `get_forward_context().no_compile_layers[key]`; - `direct_register_custom_op(..., mutates_args=[], fake_impl=..., dispatch_key="PrivateUse1")` where the op writes the

title: [BugFix] Validate layerwise prefetch before backend initialization
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Layerwise prefetch configuration was parsed differently by the GVA planner and block-key worker. Values such as `2.0` could be silently converted to an integer, and some invalid configurations were discovered only after backend creation. Share a strict positive-integer/decimal-string parser across the connector, scheduler, worker and cache planner. Reject invalid prefetch values, unsupported layerwise backends/data planes, and GVA-only reuse options on Mooncake before clients or transfer threads are created. Add a common implementation support matrix and parameter contract, update the overview/specialized guides and Chinese catalogs, and remove stale translated Memcache/Prefill-only, non-CP and single-group claims. Addresses the configuration/documentation portion of #14144. **Draft:** maintainer confirmation of the release matrix and representative real-backend, model and multi-card validation remain required. The matrix describes current implementation paths; its entries are not newly certified by descriptor tests. Related overlapping work: #21755. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Booleans, floats (including `2.0`), explicit null, empty/non-decimal strings, zero and negative prefetch values now fail early with a parameter-specific `ValueError`. Positive integers and decimal strings, including `"003"` and `"+3"`, retain their exact value. Mooncake rejects GVA-only buffer options rather than ignoring them. title: mxfp8/fp8 KV cache: arbitrary-slot indexed reads return corrupted data (paged sequential access is correct)
summary: ## Environment - Hardware: Ascend 950DT (aarch64) - Image: quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5 (CANN 9.2.1, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, Python 3.12) - Model: Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8, --kv-cache-dtype mxfp8 ## Bug With an mxfp8 KV cache, reading rows back by **arbitrary slot indices** (gather by a slot-id tensor) returns corrupted values, while the paged attention kernel reading the same cache sequentially is correct. This breaks any sparse-attention / retrieval read path that gathers selected slots by index (e.g. LSA-style top-k reads). ## Repro A minimal repro used during our sparse-attention port (single layer, rows written via `reshape_and_cache`, then gathered by slot tensor): 1. Write known K/V rows into the mxfp8 caches via `reshape_and_cache` (slots 0..N-1). 2. `gathered = key_cache[slot_ids]` with a shuffled `slot_ids` int64 tensor. 3. Compare `gathered` against the original rows. Observed: gathered values are wrong (bit-level corruption of the quantized payload). Reading the same rows sequentially (`key_cache[0:N]`) is correct. Repeating the same experiment with a bf16 cache gives exact matches, so the index-read corruption is specific to the quantized (fp8/mxfp8) cache tensors, not to our indexing code. ## Workaround Keep a separate bf16 mirror of the (pre-quantization) K/V rows, written at cache-write time, and gather from the mirror instead of the quantized caches. This restores correctness but doubles memory for those layers (~4 GB extra for 16 layers at 65536 rows on this model). ## Ask Confirm whether indexed/gathered reads on quantized KV cache tensor

title: [BugFix][GLM] Align LI C8 cache pages for tail rows and FP32 scales
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? GLM-Next shares a physical page class between pooled indexer keys and compressor-tail state. Choosing only the largest unpadded page can leave a partial tail row or misalign FP32 scale planes after the scheduler page is split into kernel pages. title: [Bug]: Graph padding rows are dispatched to experts in Ascend MC2 decode
summary: ### Your current environment This is a retrospective bug-tracking issue for the fix merged in #20242, not a new reproduction run. Environment recorded in that PR: - Atlas 800I A3, single node. - Kimi-K3 W4A8, a 48-layer truncated checkpoint, TP16 / EP16, DSpark k=7, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, FlashComm1. - DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark W4A8 on 4 cards for the draft-model symptom. - vLLM main: vllm-project/vllm@24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58. - Full `collect_env.py` output is not attached; exact CANN and torch_npu versions are not asserted here. ### Describe the bug In FULL decode graphs every step is padded up to a captured batch size. On Ascend, the MC2 and FusedMC2 MoE paths dispatched those graph padding rows to experts as if they were real tokens, even with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` enabled, which is the upstream default. The padding rows all carry the same input, so they route to the same experts, and in MC2 those experts sit on one rank. That rank becomes the straggler of every MoE layer, and the other ranks wait for it inside `MoeDistributeCombineV2`. A second symptom shows up as soon as MC2 honours `is_padding`: the Ascend Triton replacement `prepare_dflash_inputs_triton` never wrote `is_padding`, so after draft graph capture the buffer stayed all `True`. An MoE draft such as the DeepSeek-V4 DSpark MTP layer then treats every row as padding in FULL replay. #### Expected behavior With `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1`, rows that the runner marks in `is_padding` are not dispatched to experts, as on GPU after vllm-project/vllm#56079 and vllm-project/vllm#46428. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add an experimental, opt-in Ascend KDA RecoverSSM path for Kimi K3 and K3.1 speculative decoding. Verification keeps the recurrent checkpoint unchanged and writes request-indexed records; after sampling, the accepted state and convolution history are committed. title: [Performance][v0.32.0rc] Reuse head-first QKV storage in GDN prefill to eliminate redundant copies
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The GDN prefill convolution can expose Q, K and V as sequence-first `[B, T, H, D]` views of contiguous head-first `[B, H, T, D]` storage. The base adaptor currently copies each tensor into sequence-first order, then copies each back into head-first order for ChunkGDN. This round trip costs six layout copies. When all three head-first views are contiguous, the adaptor reuses their storage. It L2-normalizes Q and K along the same final dimension `D` and passes V directly to ChunkGDN. Token slices that leave gaps between heads follow the existing packing path. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Eligible prefill inputs automatically skip the six copies on the base device adaptor. No configuration change is required. ### How was this patch tested? #### Operator and serial-request performance On Ascend A3 (W8A8, TP8, DP1), a rank-0 trace of a 16,435-token prefill showed **6 → 0 QKV copy kernels in each of 180 GDN windows** across 36 layers, eliminating **20.37 ms of summed copy-kernel time** on that rank. With profiling disabled, median TTFT for serial requests of the same length fell from **2,278.90 to 2,245.56 ms (−1.46%)**, with 20 requests per variant. #### Serving performance We ran each workload once per variant on Ascend A3 with W4A8 weights, using the same inputs and target request rate. A is the original implementation and B enables the optimization. The table covers all measured requests. title: [Performance] Use a plain tensor add for the MoE tail combine
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MoE layers with both shared and routed experts merge the two outputs once per layer at the end of the block. The combine is currently a single-element multi-tensor add: ```python result = torch._foreach_add([shared_output], [fused_output])[0] ``` Both operands are ordinary activation tensors, so this is an elementwise add. On Ascend the `_foreach_add` form still enters the multi-tensor dispatch and launches a dedicated `ForeachAddList` kernel per MoE layer. That launch has a fixed cost (~17us on Atlas 910B) which is independent of the tensor size, and a one-element tensor list gets no vectorization benefit from the foreach path. On a 45-layer MoE model this is ~0.75ms of pure launch overhead on **every decode step**, i.e. directly on the token-to-token critical path. This PR adds an opt-in switch, `additional_config.enable_moe_tail_plain_add`, that performs the same combine with a plain tensor add: ```python result = shared_output + fused_output ``` The arithmetic is unchanged (same dtype, same operand order, elementwise add), so the output is bit-identical; only the kernel performing the sum changes and one op launch per MoE layer disappears. The combine was extracted into `AscendMoERunner._combine_shared_and_routed_output` so both branches can be unit-tested. The default is `false`, and when it is off the original `torch._foreach_add` path runs unchanged. The flag is read once in `AscendMoERunner.__init__` and cached on the instance, so the hot path does not re-read the config and no graph recompilation happens mid-run. Runners cons

title: [Performance] Replace padding-mask fills with a single output writeback for GLM5.3-Flash
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Decode runs on a graph-captured batch whose token count is padded to a fixed capacity, so every KDA layer and every SFA layer has to zero the rows that no request owns. On `releases/v0.31.0rc` this is still done by building a mask and applying it element-wise over the whole `[1, tokens, heads, head_dim]` activation — `arange` → `cast` → `less` → `logical_not` → `masked_fill` — once per layer per decode step. The KDA spec-verify path pays a second copy for the same reason: in steady state `spec_token_indx` is `arange(num_actual_tokens)`, so the `index_copy_` into the layer buffer is an identity scatter, preceded by another full `masked_fill` inside `recurrent_kda`. This PR reuses the recurrent output writeback the pure-decode path already relies on: one Triton kernel walks the captured buffer once, copies the rows `cu_seqlens` marks valid and stores zeros everywhere else — padding is cleared as a by-product of a copy that has to happen anyway. - **KDA** (`vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/kda.py`): when a spec-verify step carries no non-spec tokens, `recurrent_kda` writes straight into the captured buffer (`output_buffer=core_attn_out`) and the identity `index_copy_` is skipped. The `masked_fill` inside `recurrent_kda` is skipped as well, since the writeback has already zeroed the padding rows. - **SFA NoPE** (`vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py`): the `arange`/`cast`/`less`/`logical_not`/`masked_fill` chain is replaced by a single `write_recurrent_output` launch over the same tensor. title: [Feature]: Support native data-parallel serving on Ascend 310P
summary: ### The feature, motivation and pitch Enable native, single-host data-parallel serving with the 310P v2 model runner, including DP=2 / TP=2 on four visible NPUs. The existing runner rejects DP; enabling it also requires correct worker device mapping, per-replica HCCL host-port allocation, subgroup broadcast roots, and world-control-group initialization. For MoE models without expert parallelism, each DP replica should be a complete model replica with expert weights sharded only over its TP group. This avoids cross-DP device collectives in the MoE forward path, which exhausted graph-capture event resources in the environment described in PR #21997. The trade-off is increased per-device weight memory and reduced KV capacity; no universal performance improvement is claimed. ### Alternatives Run multiple independent TP services and route requests externally, or use a single larger TP deployment. These do not provide the same native DP configuration and coordination. ### Additional context Implementation and submitted validation report: #21997. Scope: single-host 310P v2 native DP; preserve existing PP/CP/EP restrictions. Ray, multi-node, MTP and LoRA combinations require separate validation. Acceptance checks include rank/device-list handling, bounded and nonoverlapping configured port ranges, subgroup root mapping, CPU broadcast delegation, startup and graph capture, request correctness, and disclosure of memory/performance trade-offs. Historical hardware measurements and outstanding validation are described in the PR; this issue does not claim additional test execution.

title: [Feature][Model][v0.32.0rc] Enable compact SP replay and fix compiled replay for DeepSeek V4.1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? SP currently disables DeepSeek V4.1 decoder bounded replay. This change enables the MRV2 path with PCP size 1 by computing an original-to-compact SP plan for each eligible eager prefill. Each rank selects its locally retained rows before a variable-size all-to-all, then the late decoder layers run on balanced compact shards. Padding is created at the destination; the inverse exchange restores the retained outputs to their original SP owners. For a 4,096-token prefill retaining 128 rows at TP8, the replay-boundary conversion exchanges only those 128 valid rows and executes 16 rows per rank. This is a payload/layout example, not a measured performance claim. The existing final model output gather is unchanged. Non-SP bounded replay also previously reused the full-batch path traced while `rows` was `None`. This change applies the same outer runtime dispatch to SP and non-SP: active replay calls the raw backbone forward, while ordinary decode keeps the complete compiled model. The compiled layer loop never reads mutable replay context. The plan also preserves decode and prompt-logprob query spans, coordinates with untrimmed or idle DP replicas, and handles both layouts of the MoE padding mask. The ordinary warmup/decode path traces every layer in the main model loop. Only an active replay batch (including an untrimmed DP peer) enters the raw backbone forward, so it can use the current layout and attention/DP context without specializing a compiled graph on mutable replay state. There is no opaque custom op around the decoder tail. ### Doe

title: [Feature][SpecDecode] Support GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? GLM-5.3-Flash could not start DFlash2 speculative decoding because the target did not expose the required Eagle3 auxiliary hidden-state interface. This PR adds the GLM-5.3-Flash target-side integration for DFlash2: - exposes target auxiliary hidden states through `EagleModelMixin`, including deferred mHC residual completion before sequence-parallel gathering; - allocates isolated scheduler groups and backing tensors for speculative sliding-window KV caches; - accepts the wrapped multimodal target embedding key in the shared QuaRot draft-weight alignment path; - skips QK-Norm+RoPE fusion for no-RoPE MLA models; - applies the existing speculative device-length policy to `glm5_next_text`. This PR does not add DFlash2 graph support itself. Current main supports full ACLGraph for ordinary DFlash2 when the target uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and the nested draft `enforce_eager` is unset or `false`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Performance][Quantization] Use QuantMatmul for W4A8 dynamic Linear
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The integer `W4A8_DYNAMIC` Linear implementation currently expresses an ordinary projection as a single-group `npu_grouped_matmul`. title: [RFC]: Pooling feature combined with PCP and DCP
summary: ### Motivation. The pooling feature has been supported in vLLM Ascend. By enabling this feature, requests can be stored in the cache pool at the block granularity level. When encountering duplicate requests, there is no need to recompute the KV cache. The pooling feature works in conjunction with PCP and DCP functions; by enabling PCP and DCP for long-sequence requests, it can save storage space for the KV cache. This combination allows the supported context length to increase exponentially or by a high multiple under limited hardware resources. ### Proposed Change. In the pooling feature, the put and get operations in KVCache are performed based on keys. In the code without the CP feature, we distinguished keys by TP dimension, so that each card uploads and retrieves all blocks of a single request. However, for CP scenarios, it is necessary to distinguish between PCP rank and DCP rank to ensure that each card reports the corresponding KVCache correctly. Therefore, we have modified the pooling keys. Setting PCP and DCP causes the block size to become the original block size multiplied by pcp_size and dcp_size, which increases the block size. As a result, the corresponding hit logic for pooling needs to be adjusted to ensure that tokens are matched according to the new block size. The figure below shows the PCP2, TP4, and DCP1 scenarios, with a total of 1912 input tokens and a block storage scenario where the model head is 4. For PCP and DCP scenarios, DP cannot be enabled, and it must be ensured that TP/KV heads >= DCP_size.

title: [Bug]: Adler32 request-ID collisions cause stale KV reuse in fused-overlap sparse offload
summary: ## Summary With sparse KV offload and `use_fused_overlap=true`, two distinct request IDs with the same Adler32 value can be treated as the same resident-cache owner. The new request preferentially reuses the previous request's physical row, skips request-change invalidation, and treats the previous request's prefix KV as resident hits. A controlled single-NPU experiment confirmed that values left in those historical resident slots are consumed by the next request's attention. title: [Attention][BugFix] Use request incarnation IDs for sparse KV offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adler32 collisions can make a new sparse-offload request match a previous resident-cache owner. Assign each local request incarnation a positive int64 owner without reuse within an allocation cycle. The V2 model state owns the registry; target and MTP draft metadata share it. Request-state removal retires the string mapping, while temporary absence from a scheduled batch preserves the incarnation. Real requests, padding (0), empty rows (-1), and dummy/capture rows (<= -2) have disjoint identities. Missing or non-string active IDs fail before metadata publication. At counter wrap, drain outstanding device work, invalidate native and fallback resident-owner markers in place, and reserve owners live at wrap for the next allocation cycle. Existing buffers, copy shapes, planner/kernel ABI, and same-owner prefix reuse are preserved. Normal decoding adds no device synchronization. Only counter wrap performs two device synchronizations and makes resident KV cold; later planning reloads selected KV from the unchanged CPU full-KV pool. No new configuration, collective, or scheduling round is introduced. Fixes #20904. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Different requests and later incarnations of the same request ID no longer inherit resident-prefix hits because of an identity collision. Deploy through a normal worker restart. V2 preemption removes local request state, so resume creates a new owner. This conservatively loses historical resident-prefix hits that might otherwise survive. title: [RFC]: KV cache layout combining all layers per block
summary: ### Motivation. title: [Performance] replay rejection sampling kernels from one ACL graph
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? On Model Runner V2 speculative decoding, every decode step runs `rejection_sample` — four Triton kernels (block stats, probabilistic rejection, resample, categorical finalize) — plus `get_num_sampled_and_rejected`. Profiling on Ascend 910B showed the device side takes only ~110-170 us while the Python/host side costs ~1.98 ms per call: each triton-ascend dispatch carries ~100-300 us of fixed host cost (argument binding, launch-key computation, run-time tiling), and the four kernels launch serially on the critical path. This PR removes that host overhead with two combined changes: 1. **Compile-time launch shapes** — shape-related scalars that are constant for a given model/speculative config become `tl.constexpr`, so triton-ascend resolves the tiling at compile time. 2. **One ACL graph replay** — the four plain-path kernels are captured once into a dedicated ACL graph and replayed with a single dispatch per step. Sampling results are bit-identical: same kernels, same inputs, same RNG (seed/position live in device buffers). ## Implementation ### 1. `tl.constexpr` launch shapes - `_compute_block_stats_kernel`: a same-signature wrapper around the upstream `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` declaring `vocab_size` and `num_speculative_steps` as `tl.constexpr`. title: [Feature][KV Pool] Add MLA KV pool read deduplication
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Refs #14140. This PR implements MLA KV Pool read deduplication for the non-layerwise `start_load_kv` path. When the MLA KV cache is replicated across TP ranks and `put_step == tp_size`, each rank reads a disjoint subset of block keys from the AscendStore backend. The implementation then selects a direct P2P cache write for few-view layouts or one all-gather payload exchange for multi-view layouts. The new path is enabled only when all of the following hold: - MLA model; - TP > 1 and `put_step == tp_size`; - DCP and PCP are both 1; - not TP mismatch; - not layerwise transfer; - not KVPP; - no recurrent `align_state` group. Unsupported layouts retain the legacy full-read path. Both synchronous `start_load_kv` and the asynchronous receive thread are covered. The implementation adds: - byte tensor views for KV cache transfer ranges; - contiguous TP shards with layer-major view coalescing; - direct P2P cache writes when a shard has very few coalesced views; - one all-gather payload exchange for multi-layer layouts; - batched `_foreach_copy_` pack/copyback for the all-gather path; - a Gloo reduction for the small P2P status bitmap; - local-shard copyback eliminated because the backend already populated it; - conservative legacy fallback when replicated KV is too small to amortize collective and copy overhead; - unit coverage for TP=2/4/8 sharding, async dispatch, and initialization guards. Following review feedback, the Python object collectives were removed. The final path batches adjacent views and copies, skips the local shard copyback,

title: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Merge pending KV reformat groups instead of overwriting the per-shard stash
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? PD disaggregation with the mooncake p2p connector (`MooncakeConnectorV1`) can run the decode side with a smaller TP size than the prefill side. Attention groups of one shard then become transfer-complete in **different** pull tasks: single-pull indexer/MLA groups finish on their first pull, the multi-pull GQA draft group on its last. `_stash_pending_reformat` replaced the per-`(request_id, shard_idx)` bucket on every call, so a later call silently dropped the groups stashed earlier. Dropped groups were never reformatted; their KV was consumed cross-rank interleaved — corrupting the GQA draft group's KV and collapsing speculative acceptance on recycled blocks, while target output stayed correct. Root cause, dose–response and the two-state repro signature are in #20367. This PR touches the V1 connector only (V2, `kv_p2p/mooncake/`, has no pull-then-reformat stash at all): 1. `_stash_pending_reformat` merges arriving groups into the per-shard bucket, de-duplicated by attention group index, so every group is reformatted once. 2. Merging lets one bucket hold groups with different `num_group_pulls`, while the non-hybrid reformat path requires a uniform pull count for the batch (`_apply_kv_cache_reformat` raises `RuntimeError` otherwise). Therefore `_reformat_pending_kv_caches` now dispatches **one reformat per pull count** instead of one per shard. ### How was this patch tested? `test_reformat_pending_kv_caches_dispatches_mixed_pull_bucket` drives the **real** consumer on a mixed-pull bucket (`_reformat_pending_kv_caches` → `_apply_kv_cache

title: [BugFix][Scheduler] Fix async prefill admission after long cache hits
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix async prefill admission for recycling KV-cache groups after a long local or remote cache hit. Requests can exhaust the shared physical block pool while every request waits for enough capacity to resume its next prefill chunk. The observed state was running=0, waiting=16, with prompt and generation counters frozen even though KV receive completions had arrived. The upstream admission path caps the logical block-table end before subtracting the existing logical table length. Sliding-window and chunked-local tables retain NULL placeholders for evicted prefix blocks, so a long NULL prefix can reduce the reservation to zero. For example, with block size 2, 102400 cached tokens, and a 113484-token prompt, a table with 51196 NULL entries and four live blocks incorrectly reserves zero instead of the 5542 additional physical blocks needed. For first-time admission, apply the recycling cap after the skipped prefix, preserving capacity estimates for long local and remote cache hits. For requests with a nonempty `req_to_blocks` table, reserve `min(uncapped_need, max(0, cap - exclusive_held_blocks))`. Count only non-NULL blocks with `ref_cnt == 1`: releasing a shared block does not return a slot to the physical pool. Scan the live suffix back to the first NULL, using actual held blocks even when prefix caching is disabled and `num_cached_block` has no entry. title: [Refactor][Sleep] Remove unused sleep-persistent CaMem tag
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Removes the unused sleep-mode workaround from #10775. #10775 kept the DSA Hadamard matrix alive across sleep by tagging it `sleep_persistent` and skipping that tag in `CaMemAllocator.sleep()` / `wake_up()`. Two later changes make that path dead: - #16096 enters the `kv_cache` allocation context only around backing KV cache allocation, so persistent metadata no longer inherits the `kv_cache` tag. - #13352 registers Hadamard matrices with `get_or_register_attention_buffer()`, so their device memory is owned by the attention modules instead of a CaMem tag. Nothing on main sets or reads `sleep_persistent_tag`, and `use_allocation_tag()` has no callers. This PR deletes the tag, the sleep/wake skips, and that context manager. Every allocation now follows the existing `offload_tags` path. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. The sleep/wake API is unchanged, and no allocation uses the removed tag. ### How was this patch tested? - Regression tests in `tests/ut/device_allocator/test_camem.py`: an allocation tagged `sleep_persistent` is released by `sleep()` and restored by `wake_up()`. - `uvx ruff@0.14.0 check` and `uvx ruff@0.14.0 format --check` pass on the changed files. - `sleep()` / `wake_up()` were executed with CPU torch and mocked memcpy/unmap. The old tag is released and restored, and ordinary offload/discard behavior is unchanged. - Full `pytest` and NPU sleep/wake e2e were not run here (no vLLM install and no Ascend device). - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e9

title: [BugFix][Attention] Avoid FIA copies of shared hybrid KV cache pages

Expose the existing storage through contiguous zero-copy views and remap logical block IDs by the physical page stride (e.g. b -> 2b for interleaved K/V). Preserve shared-page ownership, the original write-side views, and KV allocation size. title: [Doc][Model] Add LocateAnything-3B decoupled deployment tutorial
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds a model tutorial for **LocateAnything-3B** (`docs/source/tutorials/models/LocateAnything-3B.md`) plus one row in the multimodal support matrix, documenting the **decoupled (encoder-disaggregated)** deployment that is actually required by this model. LocateAnything-3B = MoonViT vision tower + Qwen2-2B LM + MTP head. Its MTP is a custom "6-token window + `handle_pattern`" rule-based decoder, which vLLM does not implement, so the whole model cannot be served inside vLLM. The working pattern, validated end-to-end on Atlas 800 A2 (910B3): - vision tower + projector + `embed_tokens` run in a client process on an Ascend NPU, - the Qwen2 language model runs in vLLM Ascend and receives pre-computed embeddings through `--enable-prompt-embeds`, - decoding falls back to plain autoregressive generation. The client and the LM server can share **one NPU** (about 22 GB of HBM in total, with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`) or use separate NPUs for lower latency and higher throughput. Why this is worth documenting rather than leaving to users: 1. **`--enable-prompt-embeds` is confirmed working on Ascend**, and there is currently no documentation of it in a multimodal context. title: [RFC]: Worker-local KV Trace for Ascend Model Runner V2
summary: ### Motivation. KV-cache address errors can appear as incorrect generation, cross-request interference, or device failures far from the code that constructed the address metadata. A capacity check alone cannot detect two valid slots being swapped between requests. Debugging needs a comparison between the scheduler's declared request/block mapping and the final address plan handed to the model runner. This RFC proposes **opt-in, worker-local KV Trace for Ascend Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**. It reconstructs request bindings from native `SchedulerOutput` messages and checks the final per-cache-group slot mappings, read block tables, and sequence lengths. It also records public KV-transfer boundaries to help correlate a failure. Implementation: [PR #17833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17833). The design/source baseline below is [`11ba7b73079bda403be5c795f1d6d9c1a43045d4`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/11ba7b73079bda403be5c795f1d6d9c1a43045d4). The follow-up support items in section 6.1 extend that initial scope. Upstream design discussion: [vllm RFC #66942](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66942). That proposal includes request/block history across scheduler, allocator, and runner boundaries. summary: ## Motivation. title: [Performance][Model] Fuse the dense-SP boundary collectives into their GEMMs (MC2, stacked on dense SP)
summary: Stacked on #20756 (dense sequence parallelism for the Qwen3.5 family) — merge after it. Only the last commit is unique to this PR. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Dense SP replaces each per-layer TP all-reduce with a reduce-scatter + all-gather pair around the layer boundary. This PR fuses those two boundary collectives into their GEMMs for prefill-sized batches on unquantized (BF16/FP16) checkpoints, using the `torch_npu` MC2 fused kernels: - **Column side — `npu_all_gather_base_mm`** (`DenseSpAllGatherMmOp` on `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`): the sequence all-gather is folded into the GEMM, so the gathered activation is never materialized and the communication overlaps the matmul. - **Row side — `npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base`** (`DenseSpMmReduceScatterOp` on `o_proj` / GDN `out_proj` / `down_proj`): the TP partial sums are reduced and scattered in one kernel, so neither the partial output nor a separate collective is materialized. The ops are installed as the projections' custom ops at layer init (the same mechanism as `KimiOProjMMReduceScatterOp`); the decoder layer then skips its own gather / reduce-scatter for layers whose boundary projections took them, and the patched attention trims the padded full-token rows the fused column op returns back to the real token count. The GDN in-projections deliberately keep the decoder-level gather (it feeds several consumers inside the mixer core); their `out_proj` still fuses. title: [RFC]: Introduce Per-Model Capability Matrices and Standardized Deployment Examples
summary: ### Motivation. **Background** The current vLLM-Ascend repository provides deployment examples organized primarily by deployment scenarios, such as: - Single-GPU inference (e.g., for DeepSeek, Qwen) - Multi-GPU inference - Prompt/Decode (PD) co-located deployment - PD-separated deployment While these scenario-based examples offer basic guidance for getting started, they are becoming increasingly insufficient as the number of supported models grows rapidly (e.g., Llama, Baichuan, ChatGLM, InternLM, Yi, Phi, etc.). The current approach—structuring both documentation and code samples around deployment scenarios rather than models—has revealed several key challenges. **Problem Statement** 1. High incidence of deployment-related issues According to support data from the vLLM-Ascend team over the past two months, over 50% of user-reported issues are deployment-related. Many stem from users attempting unsupported configurations due to a lack of clear guidance. 2. Unclear model capabilities Users often cannot easily determine which features a given model supports on Ascend, such as: - Multi-GPU inference - Continuous batching - PD-separated execution - LoRA / multi-LoRA - Speculative decoding Without explicit documentation, users resort to trial-and-error or source code inspection—increasing friction and onboarding time. 3. Poor scalability and maintainability of examples The current “scenario × model” example structure leads to combinatorial explosion as new models and features are added. This makes documentation hard to maintain and increases the risk of inconsistencies or omissi

title: [RFC]: Support for KV Cache Storage in Decode Phase
summary: ### Motivation. **Background**: In inference clusters utilizing KV Pool, sufficient capacity exists to store large volumes of KV cache. This enables preserving KV cache computed by D-instances, thereby reducing redundant KV cache computations. Another key value: KV cache persistence by D-instances directly facilitates multi-turn dialogues. **Current State**: In existing KV pool implementations, P-instances store KV cache into the pool via put operations after computation, while D-instances only retrieve KV cache from the pool (though P-nodes also use get operations to obtain prefix cache). ### Proposed Change. **Solution:** Enable D-instances to possess KV cache storage capability while minimizing modifications to the KV cache logic layer and scheduler workflow. With reference to the diagram below, specific steps: 1 The scheduler dispatches requests to workers normally, consistent with existing procedures. 2 After completing forward computation, blocks exhibit two states: - 2.1 When computed tokens in a block don't form complete chunks divisible by block_size (e.g., 128), proceed to step 3.2. - 2.2 When blocks form complete chunks, proceed to step 3.1. 3 Determine whether blocks require preservation after model forward computation: - 3.1 If storage is required, put the complete-block data into KV Pool. The number of stored blocks scales linearly with layer size. - 3.2 Proceed with post-forward processing operations. 4 After synchronizing all request operations, return results to the scheduler.

title: [RFC] Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend
summary: # RFC: Sleep-mode tensor ownership and recovery on Ascend ## Summary vLLM Ascend sleep mode currently assigns an allocation tag according to the active `CaMemAllocator` pool. That tag controls whether an allocation is host-backed, discarded, or kept mapped across sleep/wake. It does not describe the semantic lifetime of every tensor that shares the allocation scope. This RFC proposes a semantic ownership contract for persistent NPU tensors and a narrower `kv_cache` allocation boundary. Its primary objective is to ensure that a tensor that is needed after wake-up is never silently discarded merely because it was created while the KV-cache pool was active. This is the Ascend counterpart of the upstream vLLM RFC [Sleep Mode Tensor Ownership and Recovery](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53343). It builds on the targeted fixes already merged for DSA Hadamard matrices and the ALLTOALL expert-ID map in vLLM Ascend PR #13352. ## Motivation `CaMemAllocator` records one tag per underlying allocation. In the current worker path, `Worker.initialize_from_config()` enters `use_memory_pool(tag="kv_cache")` around the complete `model_runner.initialize_kv_cache()` call. This operation does more than allocate cache backing storage. Depending on the runner and configuration, it also creates or binds attention backends, input-batch state, speculative decoding state, KV-transfer registrations, sparse-KV state, KVPP runtime state, and ACL-graph-related metadata.
