title: [Performance] Cache loaded Gemma RMSNorm unit-offset weights
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Gemma RMSNorm residual paths, the A5 RMSNorm adaptor, and fused Q/K normalization currently recompute `1 + weight` on each invocation. The cache preserves the original parameter-dtype rounding and leaves checkpoint parameters unchanged. It is a nonpersistent buffer, refreshed in place on weight reload so captured graphs keep its storage. Native layerwise reload restores parameters before re-registering the original buffers; a module-local `register_buffer` override refreshes the effective weight at that point because upstream skips copying derived nonpersistent buffers. Meta staging and unprepared caches are excluded. No forward-time validation or global reload patch is added. PyTorch state-dict loads (including `assign=True`) refresh it, and dtype/device conversion recomputes it in the destination dtype. Grad-enabled execution retains the original differentiable addition. Unprepared receivers/loaders retain runtime computation. Native Gemma kernels continue to receive raw weights. There is no batch-size, token-count, or output-history-length threshold. Each Norm allocates one additional weight-sized buffer (4 KiB for 2048 BF16 elements). No model-runner behavior or environment variable is added. title: [BugFix] Read quantized checkpoint indexes for RFork model state
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Before RFork registers a model, `_get_checkpoint_weight_names` reads the checkpoint weight names to restore model state such as MTP/DSpark head ownership. It only looked for the index file that vLLM's `DefaultModelLoader` reports (`model.safetensors.index.json`, or `consolidated.safetensors.index.json` for Mistral-format checkpoints). Quantized checkpoints ship `quant_model_weights.safetensors.index.json` instead, so for most quantized models the index was never found and RFork opened the header of every selected shard. This change keeps the default index as the first choice. When it is missing, RFork looks at the other `*.safetensors.index.json` files in the same folder: - it uses one only when it is the only distinct index whose `weight_map` references exactly the shard files the default loader selected; identical copies count as one; - differing indexes over the same shards are ambiguous, so RFork reads the shard headers instead of picking one by file name; - an index that references other shards is ignored, and unreadable or malformed candidates are skipped; - the folder is escaped before globbing, so folders such as `model[AWQ]` still find their index. A malformed default index still raises `ValueError`, so it keeps falling back to the default loader. The draft checkpoint metadata FAQ in the RFork guide and its zh_CN translation now describe this lookup order. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Feature][KVCache] Support PCP with KVPP layer sharding in Mooncake layerwise pooling
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds PCP support to KVPP layer sharding in Mooncake block-key layerwise KV pooling. Before this change `MooncakeBackend.bind_layerwise_keys` rejected `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1` together with `enable_kvpp`. KVPP shards the persistent target caches by layer across the TP x PCP replica domain, so each layer is persisted by exactly one owner (`kvpp_rank = pcp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`). Attention groups are not PCP-sharded: after #20835 they share one key across PCP ranks and only PCP rank 0 saves a replica. That is correct for replicated caches, but not for KVPP, where owners on every PCP rank own different layer shards. This PR therefore: - Removes the PCP + KVPP bind rejection. - Counts every KVPP owner in the layerwise hit check (`kvpp_size`) instead of the non-KVPP saving-head count, which is one for MLA/SFA. - Lets every KVPP owner persist its layer shard, bypassing the PCP replica save deduplication; otherwise owners on PCP ranks greater than zero would never write. - Fails closed when an owner would persist no target layer, because the all-owner hit check could then never succeed. - Uses the PCP-aware PP layer-partition stride when projecting the layerwise topology namespace (the vLLM rank layout is DP x PP x PCP x TP). - Updates the KVPP, Mooncake layerwise, hybrid attention, and context parallel guides, and adds `release_notes/fragments/21253.yaml`. No key-builder change is needed: after #20835, non-PCP-sharded attention groups carry no PCP suffix, and the KVPP writer coordinate (`kvpp_rank`) already distinguishes owner

title: [Feature][KV Pool] Support DCP for Mooncake layerwise KV pooling
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mooncake block-key layerwise KV pooling rejects decode context parallelism (`decode_context_parallel_size > 1`) at key-binding time. This PR adds standalone DCP support (`prefill_context_parallel_size=1`): each DCP rank owns its own block-key objects and PUT/GET sessions, keys append `@dcp_size:<N>@dcp_rank:<R>` while DCP=1 keys remain byte-identical, and a prefix block is reported as a hit only when every PP stage and DCP rank has committed its objects. The change also hardens the DCP path so the worker key space, scheduler-side hit check and save leader cannot disagree: - share the DCP rank mapping `(tp_rank * pcp_size + pcp_rank) % dcp_size` and fail closed if the worker's DCP group rank does not match it; - reject cache groups that vLLM does not shard across DCP (sliding-window, recurrent/align-state, circular-buffer, any group without `dcp_sharded`); - fail closed when `put_step < decode_context_parallel_size`; - reject mixed cache-group block sizes whose smallest value does not divide the others, and reject an explicit `prefix_match_unit` with DCP (vLLM v0.33.0 expresses it in DCP-scaled hash units); - document the constraints in the layerwise, hybrid and context-parallel guides and mark KV Cache Pool x Decode Context Parallel as partial in the support matrix. Related prior art: #19361 added PCP to the same data plane, and #16498 added DCP sharding to the Memcache GVA layerwise data plane. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. `use_layerwise=true` with standalone DCP is now accepted for Mooncake block-key poo

title: [BugFix] Allow non-root users to load operator libraries
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Operator packages installed as root can leave vendor directories and libraries inaccessible to non-root users, causing missing-operator errors. Use `--install-for-all` in the existing custom Transformer and batch-invariant installation commands so their artifacts receive readable permissions before packaging and caching. The csrc cache key includes these installation scripts, so the change invalidates the previous artifact cache. Pass `--install-for-all` to the existing `mfcli kernel install` commands for A2, A3 and A5. MemFabric's installer then publishes its kernel package and configuration with read access for all users. Existing directory permissions are not rewritten. No post-install recursive chmod or separate permission-fix script is introduced; ownership and the default container user remain unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Non-root inference processes can access these operator packages without deployment-specific ownership changes. CANN environment initialization is unchanged; deployments must supply an initialized environment to the non-root service. title: [BugFix][MRV2] Copy idx_mapping as int32 so thinking-budget kernels compile with dspark
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes the `_thinking_budget_kernel` compilation failure reported in #20000, where a single request carrying a thinking-token budget crashes **all** TP workers as soon as `dspark` speculative decoding is enabled: ``` triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 51:8 AssertionError('initial value for `last_start` is of type int32, but the then block redefines it as int64') ``` Root cause is a dtype leak in the MRV2 Ascend runner: 1. `batch_req_state.idx_mapping_np` is `np.intp` (int64 on a 64-bit host), and `async_copy_to_gpu` (`vllm.utils.torch_utils.async_tensor_h2d`) infers the dtype from the numpy array when `dtype` is not given, so `idx_mapping` came out as int64. 2. In the speculative-decoding branch, upstream `expand_idx_mapping()` allocates `expanded_local_pos` with `idx_mapping.new_empty(...)`, inheriting int64 instead of int32. 3. `_thinking_budget_kernel` then computes `effective_len = total_len (int32) + local_pos (int64)`, so the `tl.range` induction variable is int64, and `last_start = i` inside `if start_match:` redefines the int32 live-in as int64 — Triton's then/else type assert fires at compile time. Upstream's CUDA runner passes the dtype explicitly (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, `async_tensor_h2d(idx_mapping_np, device=self.device, dtype=torch.int32)`), and the non-draft branch here already uses `torch.zeros(..., dtype=torch.int32)`, which is why plain decode and non-speculative serving are unaffected. Passing `dtype=torch.int32` keeps the Ascend runner in sync with upstream and makes the kernel's int32 live-i

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `rope_forward_triton_siso(qk, cos, sin)` calculates padding from the default `rope_dim=-1` before inferring the actual rotary dimension. title: [Bugfix] Avoid out-of-bounds slice in _swiglu_quant_kernel tail block
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #21472. The quant loop in `_swiglu_quant_kernel` steps by `COL_BLOCK_SIZE` over `HALF_COLS`, but `extract_slice` always takes a fixed `COL_BLOCK_SIZE` elements. When `HALF_COLS` is not a multiple of `COL_BLOCK_SIZE`, the final iteration slices past the end of `out`. The store `mask` kept the results correct, but the out-of-range lanes were still sliced and computed, and on Ascend they read past the UB allocation into the neighbouring live buffer. `swiglu_quant` passes `HALF_COLS = h // 2` with a hard-coded `COL_BLOCK_SIZE = 1536`, so this is the common case rather than an edge case: | hidden size `h` | `HALF_COLS` | `HALF_COLS % 1536` | affected | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 4096 | 2048 | 512 | yes | | 14336 | 7168 | 1024 | yes | | 2048 | 1024 | 1024 | yes | | 6144 | 3072 | 0 | no | This PR processes whole tiles and the compile-time remainder separately. `TAIL_COLS` is a `tl.constexpr`, so the tail disappears at compile time when the width divides evenly. For `h = 4096` the generated TTIR goes from one dynamic-offset `[1536]` slice of a 2048-element value to two static slices, `[0] [1536]` and `[1536] [512]`. Neither store needs a mask any more, since every lane is inside the row by construction. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No change in results — outputs and scales are bit-identical to the current implementation in every case checked. The observable effect is lower kernel latency on shapes that have a tail. [Details and CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21261#issuecomment-6895759083). ### What this PR does / why we need it? Refs #20759. STAIR currently averages chronological bins before scoring a candidate. Alternating expert hot spots can cancel inside each bin, making a worse placement look better. Keep one row per recorded step through the existing EPLB load reduction. The CPU planner still uses chronological bins for candidate search. It checks the winning placement against the current layout on the same uncompressed window and rejects it if predicted mean or P95 max-to-average rank load increases. Hysteresis and the reported before/after ratios use the same stepwise score. A rejected layer keeps its existing map, identity sources and previous hysteresis anchor. This changes the payload at a rebalance boundary from one row per bin to one row per recorded step. It reuses the existing collective and adds no per-step communication. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. STAIR can skip expert transfers that passed the binned check but regress the stepwise score. No new setting is required. The existing `load_window_bins` setting still bounds the candidate search. ### How was this patch tested? - vLLM-Ascend base `28e9e97`, vLLM verified revision `24

title: [RFC]: Deprecate and Sunset Dynamic Chunk Size Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP)
summary: ### Motivation. Dynamic Chunked Pipeline Parallel (CPP) was originally introduced in vLLM Ascend to address the pipeline bubble problem in Pipeline Parallelism (PP) + Chunked Prefill scenarios. For dense attention models (such as standard GQA and dense MLA models), the Self-Attention mechanism exhibits $O(n^2)$ computational complexity. Under fixed chunk sizes, processing later chunks with longer historical prefixes takes progressively longer ($T_1 < T_2 < T_3 < \dots$), causing stage imbalance and pipeline bubbles. Dynamic chunk CPP uses profiling data (sampling 64 chunk sizes during engine startup) to fit a quadratic latency model ($f(l) = a \cdot l^2 + b \cdot l + c$) with online calibration, dynamically shrinking chunk sizes as the prefix grows to equalize per-chunk latency across pipeline stages. However, recent model architecture evolution and production requirements make this feature obsolete: 1. **Shift towards Sparse and Linear Attention Models**: Current mainstream LLMs have predominantly transitioned from dense attention to sparse architectures (e.g., DeepSeek V3/V4 with sparse attention, SFA, MoE) and linear attention / hybrid models (e.g., Kimi K3/K3.1, GLM-5.x, GLA, Mamba-hybrid). In these models, the quadratic self-attention cost is no longer dominant or has been converted to $O(1)$ / $O(n)$ state updates. The quadratic latency model does not hold, and dynamic chunk adjustments yield negligible or no throughput/latency gains. 2. **Lack of Real Production Benefit**: In practice, modern production deployments rely heavily on Prefill/Decode (P/D) disaggregation

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Don't pin mamba speculative scratch blocks on save
summary: Backport of #16329 to `releases/v0.27.1rc`. ## Problem `touch_sending_mamba_blocks` pins every non-null block of the mamba group's block table for async sends — including the trailing speculative scratch blocks. After vllm PR #51358, `_relocate_speculative_block` requires speculative blocks to be exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`) to relocate them in place; the pin deposit here makes the allocator's zero-ref check fail and crashes in `allocate_new_blocks` at chunk boundaries (observed as NPU crashes on hybrid-attention + MTP + mamba align-mode deployments). ## Fix Trim the last `num_speculative_blocks` slots before touching, so the speculative tail is never pinned. title: [BugFix][MoE] Mask graph padding rows in Ascend MC2 dispatch
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In FULL decode graphs every step is padded up to a captured size. The padding rows all carry the same input, so they route to the same experts, and in MC2 those experts sit on one rank. That rank becomes the straggler of every MoE layer: in our Kimi-K3 profile its GroupedMatmul takes 491 us per layer against about 330 us elsewhere, and the other 15 ranks wait for it inside `MoeDistributeCombineV2`. This is the decode-side counterpart of the problem upstream fixed in vllm-project/vllm#56079 and vllm-project/vllm#46428. The existing MC2 mask cannot catch these rows. `mc2_mask` is built in the platform forward-context hook from the token count **after** graph padding, so it masks SP padding and DP-alignment padding but marks graph padding rows as valid. Rebuilding it from the real token count inside the hook would not work either: with FULL graphs the hook runs after `graph.replay()` has been launched (`aclgraph_utils.py` `_graph_relay`), so the replayed graph would read the previous step's mask. This PR makes two changes on Model Runner V2: 1. **The runner fills `is_padding`.** `_prepare_inputs_impl` never wrote `input_buffers.is_padding`, so after graph capture the buffer stayed all `True` and every reader of `forward_context.is_padding` saw real tokens as padding. It now rewrites the buffer for each real batch, the same four lines as upstream `prepare_inputs`. The write happens before graph replay, so captured graphs read the current step's value. 2. **MC2 masks the rows marked in `is_padding`.** `PrepareAndFinalizeWithMC2.prepare` de

title: [Feature] Overlap the SFA indexer q projection with pre-processing on two streams
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In the SFA attention decode forward, the indexer pre-processing is made of two independent strands that are currently issued back-to-back on the current stream: - **k strand**: `wk_weights_proj` (AIC) → k norm + RoPE (AIV) → k c8 quant (AIV) - **q strand**: `quantize(q_c)` (AIV) → `wq_b` quant matmul (AIC) Both strands have a cube phase and a vector phase, but they are executed serially, so each engine idles while the other one works. The q strand is therefore fully exposed on the critical path even though it is independent of the k strand and could run concurrently. This PR adds the `multistream_sfa_indexer_overlap` additional config key (default **off**). When enabled, the q strand is issued on `attention_calculation_stream()` and interleaved with the k strand, so the AIC and AIV units stay busy at the same time. ### How it works The two strands are interleaved with four `wait_stream()` synchronization points: 1. `aux.wait_stream(main)` → aux quantizes `q_c` (AIV) while main runs `wk_weights_proj` (AIC); 2. after the main cube phase, `aux.wait_stream(main)` → aux runs the `wq_b` quant matmul (AIC) while main runs the k vector part (AIV); 3. `main.wait_stream(aux)` once, right before the k c8 quantization — i.e. main only waits when the indexer kernel actually needs `q_li`. ```text main: |-- wk_weights_proj (AIC) --|-- k norm + RoPE + c8 quant (AIV) --|wait|--> indexer aux: |-- quantize(q_c) (AIV) -----|-- wq_b quant matmul (AIC) --------| ``` `forward` hands the precomputed `q_li` to `indexer_select_post_process(q_li=...)`, which th

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Backport the wide speculative GDN window dispatch to `releases/v0.32.0rc`. The AscendC recurrent kernel accepts at most eight tokens per sequence. title: [BugFix][310P] fix performance degrade issue with MTP for Qwen3.5-2B on the 310P
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On Ascend **310P**, enabling MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=1`) for **Qwen3.5-2B-W8A8** can make ais_bench synthetic decode **slower** than MTP-off (higher TPOT / lower output throughput), while larger models such as Qwen3.5-9B still benefit from MTP on the same stack. **Root cause:** MTP=1 does ≥2 FULL ACLGraph replays per step (target SpecDecoding verify + draft). title: [Performance][Kernel] Share exact radix sorting across BF16 and FP32 candidate packing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Replace the FP32 compare/exchange sort in fused candidate packing with the stable radix implementation shared by BF16 and FP32. The shared operator is called by the context-parallel sharded indexer through `pack_local_candidates`; this change optimizes candidate preparation before merging, without adding a model-specific entry point. Inputs are INT32 local token IDs and BF16/FP32 scores with shape `[T, 1, K]`. The fused path uses **K = 2048** and returns INT32 `[T, K, 2]` pairs containing the global token ID and the FP32 score payload. Candidates are ordered by score descending, then token ID ascending. The implementation uses one inline least-significant-digit radix loop: - Valid local token IDs use a fixed **20-bit** field. - Each pass sorts `digit * 2048 + position`. The 11-bit position tag preserves the order established by earlier passes, leaving 13 digit bits within FP32's 24-bit significand. - BF16 uses 16 score-key bits and three passes; FP32 uses all 32 score-key bits and four passes. - Scores and IDs follow the same permutation after every pass. Signed zeros compare equal while retaining their original payloads; FP32 scores are not rounded to BF16. Remove the per-row maximum-ID reduction, short/full ID-width selection, and large-ID radix fallback. Keep the comparison helper used by merge kernels. Existing workload-based fused dispatch and the separate sorting/packing path for other workloads remain in place. The operator document and release note are included. title: [Performance][Model] Add fused split_qkv_index_rmsnorm_rope kernel for MiniMax-M3 sparse prepare
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? - The MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention prepare stage (`_sparse_prepare`) is currently implemented as a chain of independent operators: `narrow`/`split` × 5, `npu_rms_norm` × 4, `npu_rotary_embedding` × 2, and `clamp`(+`cast → fp8`) × 4. - That is 11+ separate kernel launches, with every intermediate result written back to global memory and re-read by the next operator, costing ~42ms per prepare stage. - This PR adds a fused Triton kernel, `qkv_index_rmsnorm_rope`, which performs split + Gemma RMSNorm + NeoX RoPE + FP8 clamp/cast in a single launch: ```concat [q | k | v | index_q | index_k] → Python: cos_sin_cache[positions] (1 aclnnIndex, deterministic) → Triton kernel (single pass): split (by offset load) + Gemma RMSNorm (tl.sum reduction) + NeoX RoPE (vectorized cos/sin) + clamp ±448 + cast → fp8 → q/k/v/index_q/index_k ``` The intermediates stay in UB/registers, so GM traffic drops from ~8× to ~1× the input size, and the prepare-stage latency drops from ~42 us to ~10us. ### Key implementation notes - **Determinism.** cos/sin rows are gathered in Python via `cos_sin_cache[positions]` (one `aclnnIndex`) and the kernel reads them by contiguous offset. The earlier in-kernel scalar gather (`get_element` + `insert_slice` loop) is non-deterministic on Ascend Triton: scalar indirect-address loads are scheduled unstably under concurrent memory traffic, producing ULP-level differences that diverge greedy-sampling output. See the determinism note in the kernel docstring for the ablation evidence. - **FP8.** The kernel fuses `clamp(±448) → e4m3` fo

title: [Feature][Model] Add MiniMax-M3 Union attention with runtime D8 routing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Integrate MiniMax-M3 UnionSparseGen and GBSA exactMask on supported Ascend 950 geometry for BF16/FP16 and E4M3 KV caches. Union preserves each query's selected KV blocks using the exact mask. If the optional matched CANN extensions cannot load, the model uses the existing native attention path. Union is enabled by default. `minimax_m3_union_d8_threshold_pct` in `--additional-config` defaults to `100`: this path does not load the policy module, compute D8 routing, launch native attention, or merge branch outputs. With a threshold below `100`, each sparse layer and local selector head routes each request's aligned eight-query group from its **current actual block selections**, including on graph replay. D8 is the distinct-block union size divided by `8 * topk_blocks`; the final short group uses its actual query count. A group exceeding the threshold uses native attention (Q-gather-KV in prefill); equality selects Union. There is no calibration file or startup routing table, and selection-dependent values stay on device without a host scalar read. Top-k and selector behavior are unchanged. Runtime policy supplies disjoint selections to two attention entry points and merges their outputs. Both entry points still launch; Union preprocessing, device routing, schedule generation, and merging add overhead. This implementation does not claim a performance gain for a lower threshold. Native decode schedules are rebuilt from routed counts to avoid stale metadata. ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? Yes. Supported MiniMax-M3 config

title: [Test][DCP] Qwen3.5 DCP 功能测试（decode context parallelism）
summary: ## 背景 vllm-ascend 支持 DCP（Decode Context Parallelism），用于长序列 decode 阶段的并行加速（head-sharding 机制，见 `platform.py` 的 `decode_context_parallel_size` 约束）。需验证 DCP 在 **Qwen3.5** 上的功能正确性，确保长序列推理可用。 ## 任务 对 **Qwen3.5** 进行 DCP 功能测试，验证 decode context parallel 在该模型上的功能可用性。 - 模型：Qwen3.5 - 功能：DCP（decode context parallelism） - 配置：`--decode-context-parallel-size N` - attention 类型：GQA（dense / A3B MoE） ## 验收标准 ### 1. 功能正确性 - DCP 开启后模型能正常推理（不报错、不崩溃、不死锁） - 不同 CP size（2/4/8）下功能正常 - 不同序列长度（4K/16K/64K）下功能正常 - 不同 TP size 与 CP size 组合下功能正常 ### 2. 精度一致性 - DCP 开启 vs 关闭，输出 token 序列一致性（greedy `temperature=0` + non-greedy `temperature>0`） - 多组 prompt 覆盖（短/长/中英文/代码） - 精度无回归（与 DCP=1 基准对比） ### 3. 叠加场景（若适用） - DCP + 投机解码（MTP/Eagle3/DSpark）叠加功能正常 - DCP + chunked prefill 叠加功能正常 ### 4. 交付件 - 测试报告（功能矩阵 + 精度数据 + 通过/失败判定） - 可复现测试脚本（提交到 `tests/`） - 若发现功能问题，提 follow-up issue 并关联本 issue ## 环境约定 - vllm-ascend：最新 main - 硬件：Ascend NPU（多卡，CP size <= 卡数） - 关联任务池：#9079 - 验收人：@王盈聪 ## 重点关注 - DCP 是 head-sharding（`platform.py` 约束：`num_q_per_kv % dcp_size == 0`，`max_dcp_size = TP // kv_heads`） - Qwen3.5 的 attention 类型（GQA（dense / A3B MoE））决定 DCP 路径： - GQA -> `attention_cp.py`（AscendAttentionDCPImpl） - MLA -> `mla_cp.py` - prefill CP（PCP）ascend 不支持（`platform.py:339` 明确），仅 decode CP - DCP + spec decode 叠加见 `enable_sfa_dcp_replicated_indexer`（SFA sparse index 复制） ## 任务周期 - 发布：2026-08-10 - 回收：2026-09-30

title: [Performance][PCP] Run MoE TopK before PCP all-gather
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The AllGather MoE path gathers full router logits across PCP ranks before running TopK on every rank. Token-local routing can run before this collective, reducing duplicated TopK work and replacing the full-logit communication with selected expert weights and ids. Compute logical routes on each PCP shard, then gather hidden states and packed TopK weights/ids. Apply capture callbacks, EPLB mapping and layer postprocessing after gather to preserve their original token-row ordering. Keep the existing DP padding/gather stage and PCP/DP finalization order. The optimization supports combined DP and PCP configurations without requiring `dp_size == 1`. Shared-expert handling, forced routing, dynamic load collection, upstream V2 EPLB accounting and LoRA context cleanup remain in the existing execution flow. The implemented path requires AllGather communication, PCP > 1, no MoE sequence parallelism, and a router supporting token-local routing. Hash/vision routers that internally gather `input_ids` and arbitrary custom routers retain the existing path. A separate 1,024-token performance policy retains the existing path for small shards; this policy needs hardware retuning for other workloads. This PR contains only the MoE routing/communication changes, their regression tests. The ND weight-cache optimization is tracked separately in #21662. Both PRs target `main` and can be merged independently. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [BugFix][Quantization] Reject native block FP8 on unsupported devices
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Native block-wise FP8 checkpoints use an FP8 execution path only on Ascend 950. On A2/A3, the linear and MoE schemes instead expanded checkpoint weights to the model dtype and selected unquantized GEMM, silently doubling weight storage and increasing load-time peak memory. This change rejects the unsupported native block-FP8 path at scheme construction, before vLLM config lookup or weight-buffer allocation, with guidance to use a BF16 checkpoint or a supported ModelSlim/LLM-Compressor checkpoint. Ascend 950 MXFP8 execution and its shape-specific dense fallback remain unchanged. Fixes #21157 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Native block-wise FP8 checkpoints now fail early with an actionable error on non-950 devices instead of silently running as BF16. This applies to A2/A3 and other non-950 devices using this checkpoint format, including Qwen native FP8 checkpoints. ### How was this patch tested? - Added linear and MoE constructor regression tests. Both new tests failed before the fix with “NotImplementedError not raised” and pass after the fix; each asserts the failure occurs before vLLM config lookup and weight allocation. - On an actual Atlas 800T A2 host (8 x 910B3, `npu-smi` 25.5.1), ran both scheme constructors against the patched main source. title: [Feature][Engram] Share A2/A5 host tables across P/D instances via RDMA
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Independent DeepSeek V4.1 prefill and decode instances otherwise retain separate host Engram tables. This opt-in A2/A5 backend keeps one immutable table in an owner process and fetches selected rows over HIXL. On A5 it uses the UB endpoint and supports FP8 checkpoint rows. The owner gathers quantized rows into registered host staging; consumers transfer them to bounded device buffers and dequantize them on the NPU. Existing TP/DP exchanges and the P/D KV connector remain in place. The owner may be co-located with a model instance; it is a separate process and the co-located instance also reads through HIXL. Batched lookups combine small requests from both Engram layers, while large requests and unsupported owners use the per-layer path. The consumer requires per-tensor checkpoint filtering before materialization. The companion loader work is included in draft [vLLM #64395](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64395), including multithreaded lazy loading and secondary sources. Its CUDA transport is separate from the Ascend HIXL backend; the draft still needs human review and H20/CUDA validation of its merged source. A separately tested [current-main loader candidate](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/feat/a2-engram-loader-current) is retained for comparison; it is not an additional PR. This is a follow-up to the merged A3 shared-table implementation [#19528](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19528), which builds on [#16689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16689). title: [Bug]: Native FP8 checkpoints silently run as BF16 on A2/A3, which have no FP8 matmul
summary: ## Your current environment <details> <summary>The output of `python collect_env.py`</summary> ```text vLLM Ascend: main @ ac6405d9e Hardware: Ascend A2 (910B) / A3 (910C) Model: any native FP8 checkpoint, e.g. Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash ``` </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug `vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/fp8_block.py` serves native block-wise FP8 checkpoints (`"quant_method": "fp8"` plus a `weight_block_size`). Only Ascend 950 has an FP8 execution path for them, but the file decides that by falling back to BF16 instead of reporting it: ```python # fp8_block.py:180 / :270 self.mxfp8_method = AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicLinearMethod() if is_950() else None ``` With `mxfp8_method is None`, `process_weights_after_loading` dequantizes the whole FP8 weight into the model dtype with `resolve_block_scales(...)` and serves it through the unquantized GEMM (`:226-228`, `:247-249`); the MoE scheme does the same via `_resolve_experts` / `bf16_method` / `quant_type = QuantType.NONE`. So on A2/A3 an "FP8" model silently runs as a BF16 model, with no error. This is not reasonable: - A2/A3 have no FP8 matmul, so there is nothing to fall back to. The rewrite buys no throughput and doubles the weight footprint (fp8 is 1 byte, bf16 is 2), which is exactly what breaks the "a 27B FP8 checkpoint fits on one card" property the scheme is built around. Peak memory during load is worse still, since the dense copy is materialized while the FP8 weight and `weight_scale_inv` are still alive. - The degradation is invisible. The only trace is one `logger.info_once` saying block-wise fp8

title: [BugFix][Quantization] Reject native FP8 checkpoints on non-950 devices
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A native block-wise FP8 checkpoint (`"quant_method": "fp8"` with a `weight_block_size`) can only be executed on hardware that has an FP8 matmul. On Ascend A2/A3 the block-wise FP8 scheme therefore used to rewrite the checkpoint into the model dtype while loading and serve an unquantized GEMM instead: the weights doubled in size compared with the BF16 release, the arithmetic no longer matched what the checkpoint describes, and the only trace of it was a single info log. Atlas 300I DUO behaves the same way. The MXFP8 path that actually consumes FP8 was, and remains, Ascend 950 only. Fixes: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21157 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Loading a native block-wise FP8 checkpoint on Ascend A2/A3 or Atlas 300I DUO now fails at startup ### How was this patch tested? - `pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py` - the per-device format matrices now assert that all profiles declare `BF16`/`FP16`/`INT8`, that only A5 adds `FP8_E4M3`/`HIF8`/`MXFP8`/`MXFP4`, and that `supports_weight_format()` agrees with `native_weight_formats`. - `pytest tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_fp8_block.py` --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values, off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). title: [BugFix][Recipes] Fix Ascend recipe TP/DP configuration
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Problem In `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph mode, every decode step updates all 36 captured FIA graph tasks individually on the host: ```python torch.npu.graph_task_update_begin(update_stream, handle) torch_npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score.out(..., actual_seq_lengths_kv=seq_lens_list, ...) torch.npu.graph_task_update_end(update_stream) event.record(update_stream) ``` The Host-side FIA update costs **~198 μs per layer — ~7.13 ms per decode step for 36 layers** — the largest single Host block of the decode step. title: [BugFix][Attention] Honor EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec in Ascend attention metadata
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen3.5-family hybrid models run bidirectional full-attention layers when `is_causal=False`. vLLM marks those layers `ENCODER_ONLY` and the model runner creates an `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` group that keeps no KV cache. On GPU, the backend dispatches `ENCODER_ONLY` to `_forward_encoder_attention(causal=False)`. The Ascend metadata builder instead always uses `common_attn_metadata.causal`, which is built as `True`, so encoder-only layers execute causally on NPU. This change computes a group-local causal flag that also requires the KV cache spec not to be `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec`, and uses it for both the attention mask and `AscendMetadata.causal`. The shared metadata is not mutated, so causal layers in the same batch keep their semantics. ### When does this trigger? Only when the model config sets `is_causal=False`, i.e. bidirectional full-attention deployments such as two-way or retrieval inference. In the default causal mode no `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` group is created, so regular generation deployments are unaffected and all existing `FullAttentionSpec` / `CrossAttentionSpec` paths keep their current behavior. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. ### How was this patch tested? - UT: `test_build` covers `FullAttentionSpec` / `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` with `causal=True/False` and asserts the shared metadata is unchanged. - E2E: encoder-only correctness is parameterized over `common_causal` and uses `EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` with `runner_type="pooling"`. The `common_causal=True` case fails before this fix. -

summary: Fixes #21251 ## Problem The Ascend rewrite of `initialize_kv_cache` (`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_model_runner.py`, adapted from upstream ced6857afa) builds `BlockTables` without `sliding_window_reach`. title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Release retained prefill KV when a hybrid decode request finishes before receive dispatch
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In PD disaggregation with `MooncakeHybridConnector`, when a decode-side request finishes in the D scheduler (abort, pre-admission rejection, preemption) before its KV receive is dispatched to the worker, the connector sends no completion notification to the prefill node. The P node then retains the request's KV blocks until the delayed-free timeout (`VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, 480 seconds by default) expires and force-frees them ("Force freed expired request ... (480 seconds)"). Under sustained load with large prompts this strand KV blocks on P for 8 minutes per aborted request and crowds out prefill capacity. This ports the MooncakeConnectorV1 cleanup to the hybrid connector: - `request_finished_all_groups()` now enqueues (or replaces) a notification-only empty receive when a `do_remote_prefill` request finishes, or when its receive is still pending in `_reqs_need_recv`. The worker skips the data transfer for empty block IDs (existing behavior) but still sends the DONE signal in its completion path (existing behavior), so P releases its retained blocks immediately. - Receives carry `awaiting_kvs` (`num_external_tokens > 0`) so the D-side completion path can distinguish real receive completions from notification-only tasks; the latter only clean up local worker tracking and do not report a normal receive completion to the scheduler. - Already-dispatched transfers keep their existing completion path (no early DONE), so in-flight reads are untouched. title: [RFC]: Separate pools for history pages and request state in hybrid KV caches
summary: ### Motivation. In DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, historical KV and sparse index data grow with the number of processed tokens. Sliding-window attention (SWA) retains the most recent 128 tokens, and the compressor maintains bounded intermediate state. History capacity therefore depends primarily on context length, while the capacity needed for SWA and compressor state depends primarily on the number of active requests. In the tested vLLM-Ascend baseline, one shared block ID indexes the same page number in four physical slots. The page stride of each slot is set by its largest payload. In one of these slots, either the SWA or compressor page needs 128 KiB, while historical KV and its index need only 72.125 KiB. When the block is assigned to history, the stride remains 128 KiB, leaving 55.875 KiB of padding. ```text Same physical slot, 128 KiB page stride History use [ History KV + index 72.125 KiB ][ Padding 55.875 KiB ] State use [ SWA or compressor state 128 KiB ] ``` Across the four slots, a block ID assigned to history occupies 528.25 KiB, including 167.625 KiB of padding (**31.73%**). This is the padding fraction of a shared block used for history. The overhead grows as longer contexts allocate more history blocks, even at the same number of active requests. ### Proposed Change. Implementation: [PR #12 — Separate history and request-state pools with explicit planning](https://github.com/immengzi/vllm-ascend/pull/12). title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Add heartbeat leases to MooncakeConnectorV2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MooncakeConnectorV2 currently releases producer KV after a fixed timeout even when a decoder is still waiting to consume it. title: [Performance] Use plain NZ matmul for DSA o_proj wo_a with a single local group
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek-V4(-V4.1) DSA o\_proj low-rank projection `wo_a` is always dispatched to `npu_transpose_batchmatmul` on a 3D weight of shape `[n_local_groups, hidden_size, o_lora_rank]`. When all o\_groups land on the current TP rank (`n_local_groups == 1`, e.g. TP >= o\_groups — TP8 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), the batched-transpose path degenerates to a plain linear but still pays a large fixed kernel cost at decode batch sizes (M << N). Profiling DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W4A8 TP8/EP8 decode (bs=2), per decode step: - `aclnnTransposeBatchMatMul`: 40 calls/step x \~50.6 us = **2.03 ms/step** (\~10% of the 5.3 us/call HBM floor of the 8.4 MB bf16 weight) - a plain 2D matmul on the same weight in NZ format measures \~17 us/call in an op-level microbench; `MatMulCommon` of the same shape runs at \~14 us in the production trace This PR dispatches `_wo_a_bmm` to the standard `unquantized_gemm` 2D matmul when `n_local_groups == 1`, and keeps the bf16 `wo_a` weight 2D in NZ format through the unquantized linear method (`skip_weight_nz_conversion` is now only set for the grouped path). The grouped path (`n_local_groups > 1`) and quantized (fp8/int8) wo\_a layouts are unchanged. title: [BugFix][DSpark][EPLB] Fix V4.1 draft expert loading and registration
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark has two EPLB integration bugs: 1. Draft MoE discovery does not set `num_moe_layers`, so MRv2 EPLB cannot reliably register the draft model. 2. The checkpoint loader builds its expert mapping with zero redundant experts even when the draft has redundant physical slots. The loader can therefore place the wrong logical expert weights in those slots or leave slots uninitialized. This PR sets `num_moe_layers` from the discovered local MoE layers and passes the draft's actual `num_redundant_experts` into the checkpoint mapping helper. Expert weight loading then uses the same physical layout as runtime routing. Fixes #21608. ### Relationship to other PRs - **#21168:** the corresponding fix for DeepSeek V4, already merged. V4.1 has a separate DSpark implementation and needs this change independently. - **#21316:** a separate Gloo/NZ weight-transfer fix required by the FP4 migration smoke tests below. It is not included in this PR. This PR changes V4.1 DSpark registration/loading, regression tests and a release note. EPLB scheduling and migration-policy optimizations are tracked separately in #21608. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. V4.1 DSpark can register its local draft MoE layers with EPLB and load weights according to the configured redundant-expert layout. Zero-redundancy loading behavior is preserved. ### How was this patch tested? **Regression tests** - 19 focused tests passed on the development container. title: [Performance][Spec Decode] Fuse add and argmax for Dspark on Ascend V2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DSpArk sequential greedy drafting selects each draft token from the sum of base logits and the Markov-head bias. The existing path materializes this sum and then reads it again for argmax. This PR adds an opt-in fused add and two-stage argmax implementation for Ascend NPUs in Model Runner V2. It avoids materializing the full summed-logits tensor during supported greedy sampling steps. The implementation: - Splits the vocabulary into blocks of 4096 elements. - Loads base logits and Markov bias, performs source-dtype addition, and computes each block’s maximum value and corresponding index in the first kernel. - Reduces the partial results and writes the selected draft-token ID in the second kernel. - Uses standard `tl.max` and `tl.min` reductions. - Allocates temporary reduction buffers during speculator initialization and reuses them across sequential steps. - Preserves draft-to-target vocabulary mapping and the independent confidence-head path. The kernel supports matching FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs with unit vocabulary stride, including non-contiguous row layouts. It preserves source-dtype addition rounding, first-index tie breaking, NaN handling, and positive/negative infinity handling. Probabilistic sampling, top-k drafting, acceptance-estimator consumers, and models with output-logit transforms or custom sequential sampling methods retain the existing sampling path. Unsupported tensor configurations also fall back to the existing path. ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? Yes. It introduces an optional `additional_

title: [Bug][Model] mm_device_do_normalize device-side preprocessing breaks train-inference logprob parity for Qwen3.5-VL on 950DT (v0.30.0, from #16996/#18443)
summary: ### Summary Since v0.30.0, Qwen3.5-VL image preprocessing (resize / patchify / rescale+normalize) is offloaded to the NPU worker (#16996 on main, #18443 on the release branch), on by default via `mm_device_do_normalize`. In an RL training loop (verl GRPO) on Ascend 950DT with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in BF16, this path breaks the parity between rollout logprobs and training-side recomputed logprobs: the mean per-token logprob mismatch grows 3.5x (0.0138 -> 0.048) and greedy eval accuracy drops ~3 points. title: [RFC] Standardizing how dynamic KV-cache quantization is enabled
summary: ## Background Model parameter counts and context lengths keep growing, so KV-cache quantization is being adopted in more and more scenarios and is attracting more and more development effort. However, different developers currently implement it in different ways — in particular, **there is no agreed standard for how dynamic KV-cache quantization should be enabled at launch time**. This RFC is to align on a single standard launch path for dynamic KV-cache quantization in vLLM-Ascend, and to collect feedback before we codify it in code and docs. ## Current status KV-cache quantization in practice falls into two categories: **static** and **dynamic**. ### Static quantization The `scale`/`offset` used to quantize the KV cache must be calibrated offline at weight-quantization time and stored inside the checkpoint. They are loaded together with the weights and consumed by the KV-cache quantization path during inference. Consequences: - The quantization toolchain **must** be involved and the weights must be regenerated. - Taking W4A8C8 as an example, `W4A8C8` and `W4A8` are two *different* checkpoints. A user who wants to enable the C8 feature has to switch to a different set of weights. ### Dynamic quantization The KV cache is quantized at runtime based on the actual values, and the `scale` is generated online — it does not depend on the checkpoint. In theory, a user only needs to add **one CLI flag** to enable the C8 feature. The caveat is that C8 is lossy. title: [BugFix][Sampler] Apply top-p to the top-k truncated distribution
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? `_apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch` softmaxed the full vocabulary once and then reused that pre-cut distribution for the top-p cut. Top-p must instead be applied to the distribution **truncated by top-k**. Because the reused distribution still carries the mass that top-k just discarded (`S_k <= 1`), the `1 - p` percentile was taken over the wrong mass. Two consequences whenever both samplers are enabled (`k < vocab_size` and `p < 1`): 1. The retained set is larger than upstream's, so sampling behaves as if `p` were higher than requested. With `S_k > p` the effective threshold is `p' = 1 - (1 - p) / S_k`. 2. Once `S_k <= p`, the discarded mass already fills the `1 - p` budget, the cumulative sum never reaches the cutoff, and **top-p degrades to a no-op** — only top-k remains. The fix sorts the logits first, cuts top-k on the sorted logits, then re-normalizes before accumulating for top-p, matching `apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch` in vLLM. The pure top-k path (`p is None`) no longer pays for an unused full-vocabulary softmax either. ### Scope Three entry points all converge on this function, so all three are affected: - V1 main path: `AscendTopKTopPSampler.forward_native` - MRv2: `patch_triton.py` redirects upstream's `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` to `apply_top_k_top_p_npu`, which delegates here - Speculative decoding: same redirection ### Evidence `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` already matches upstream exactly, which confirms this was an implementation divergence rather than an intentional NPU semantic. title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Fix packed cross-chunk readiness and buffer lifetime
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Packed HCCL layerwise reload can retain owning clones from an earlier chunk and read them on a later slot stream. Slot-local waits do not establish cross-chunk readiness or protect clone storage while deferred reads remain pending. Keep Ascend's local packed producer/consumer loops and the HCCL engine inheritance already present in main. Record an NPU event **after each loader callback** and wait for it before the next chunk's unpack/load work. Record each owning clone on all supported slot streams and the caller stream before invoking the loader; the tracking helper drops its temporary references before the callback. Join existing caller-stream work onto all slots, retain native HCCL packing/receive boundaries and failure drains, and document additional-stream caller contracts. No per-chunk post-load host barrier is added. Use main's HCCL-specific metadata cache/session reset and its repeated-update tests for main/release compatibility. IPC behavior is unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Fixes packed HCCL cross-chunk readiness and storage lifetime. No new public API or configuration. ### How was this patch tested? Author validation on Ascend 910C, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Port the existing V1 pre-admission cleanup from `releases/v0.26.0rc` to MooncakeHybridConnector on the same release branch. title: [BugFix][PD] Route hybrid KV transfer through cache entries for prefill-side PP > 1
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? PD disaggregation with a **pipeline-parallel prefill instance** (`prefill.pp_size > 1`) using `MooncakeHybridConnector` silently produces garbage decode output on every request (hybrid-attention models, e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash). No errors are logged and the external cache hit rate looks healthy, which makes it look like a model/serving problem rather than a connector bug. Root cause: each PP stage builds its **own** `kv_cache_tensors`, so the config-level tensor tables have different layer composition on the two sides. Measured on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (block_size 32, PP=2): The consumer pairs whole tensors (positionally, and after #14549 by stage slicing) and copies whole blocks between them: real KV bytes land at wrong **layer-composition offsets** — values look sane, attention reads the wrong layers. title: [Performance][Kernel] Materialise contiguous RoPE derived cos/sin caches
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `_record_cos_and_sin_cache_interleaved` publishes the derived cos/sin lookup tables as **strided views** (row stride `2*hidden_dim`) into the `[max_seq, 2, hidden_dim]` staging copy built by `view().repeat(1,1,2).chunk(2)`. `aclnnIndex` cannot gather from a strided source in place, so every `get_cos_and_sin_mla` lookup first **materialises the whole table with a row-major copy** (`aclnnIndex_SliceAiCore_Slice`, `[1048576, 128] -> [1048576, 64]` in the profile) before selecting the few rows it actually needs. With the 1M-row caches GLM-5.3 builds, that is ~366 us for each of cos and sin per lookup (~740 us per call), ~10 calls per decode step — **~7.6 ms of a 108 ms decode step (~7%) spent rewriting a table that never changes after load**. This PR materialises the pair once, at record time: ```diff - _cos_cache = cos_cache.squeeze(1) - _sin_cache = sin_cache.squeeze(1) + _cos_cache = cos_cache.squeeze(1).contiguous() + _sin_cache = sin_cache.squeeze(1).contiguous() ``` - **Values are bit-identical** — `contiguous()` is a pure copy; verified with whole-table `torch.equal` on hardware. - **Steady-state memory is unchanged**: the same-size contiguous pair replaces the staging copy the strided views used to pin. The only transient is the pair being built while the staging copy is still alive — once, during weight load, before ACL graph capture. - Runs once at load; `owner.register_buffer` keeps holding the very same tensor objects, so the RFC #16558 ownership contract documented in the docstring is preserved. - Every per-step lookup degrad

title: [Performance][DSv4] Shard prefill indexer rows across TP ranks
summary: ## What On pure-TP deployments every rank runs the C4 lightning indexer over **all** prefill rows with identical (replicated) indexer projections — the scoring work is duplicated `tensor_parallel_size`-fold. This PR gives each rank a contiguous, cost-balanced slice of the prefill rows: each rank scores and selects TopK only for its slice, and the final int32 TopK indices are gathered back into global row order. Cache writes stay replicated and untouched. ## Design - **Cost-balanced contiguous split** (`balanced_prefill_row_shard`): row cost is the number of compressed keys the row scores, `((seq_len - query_len + 1) + row) // 4`; equal-cost boundaries via `searchsorted` on the cumulative cost, with `>=1 row per rank` clamping. Contiguity keeps request order intact and makes every kernel-side extent derivable (no per-token positions plumbing). - **Decline floors**: batches below `512 rows/rank`, below `16 Mi` cumulative scoring cost, or whose padded gather (`tp * max slice`) exceeds `2x` the batch rows keep the replicated path. Under `max_num_batched_tokens` chunking, real chunks are `mnbt - spec_reserve` rows (8186 at the 8192/7 deployment), so the row floor must stay below that; a fresh prompt's first chunk still declines on the cost floor. - **Exchange workspace**: one module-level `(scratch, gather)` pair shared by all layers and the MTP draft, reserved at Indexer builder `__init__` so the memory profile accounts for it: `36 MiB` per card at TP8 / mnbt 8192 / topk 512 (2x-capacity gather bound) instead of 144 MiB unbounded. The gather is a padded `all_gather_into_tensor`

title: [RFC]: Support Mamba2 ReplaySSM speculative decoding with Triton on Ascend
summary: ## Motivation Mamba2 speculative decoding can write a full recurrent state for each candidate position. With a replay capacity of `B = replayssm_buffer_len` and a verification window of at most `T = 1 + num_speculative_tokens`, the upstream speculative ring has `B + T` rows. Verify replays the previously accepted inputs, writes a checkpoint when replay plus the current window would exceed capacity, then appends the new candidates. title: [RFC]: Evaluate deferred KDA RecoverSSM for GLM-5.3-Flash on Ascend
summary: ## Motivation Ascend's GLM KDA RecoverSSM path verifies a speculative window, then compacts the convolution history and commits the accepted SSM state after sampling. The verify and commit stages each read the recurrent checkpoint. Deferring the SSM update to the next verification step can remove one checkpoint read for requests that can carry a pending replay forward. Reading the convolution history at the accepted-token offset can also avoid a separate compaction pass for those requests. The existing immediate path provides the baseline for evaluating these changes on Ascend. title: [BugFix][MRV2] Refresh the padding mask on every real batch
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? What this PR does / why we need it? The returned mask is sized to num_tokens_after_padding rows while retaining its persistent storage address, leaving TP padding and rank-local slicing to the model-level SP helpers. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [BugFix][Qwen4] Support multi-head QSA cache stores
summary: ## Summary - extend the Qwen4Exp Triton QSA cache-store kernel to address the cache head dimension explicitly - accept cache rows shaped as `[tokens, heads, width]` while preserving the existing single-head convenience path - validate row/cache head compatibility and cover multi-head stores in the unit test ## Problem `qsa_store_cache_rows` previously required `[pages, page_size, 1, width]` caches and flattened the row head dimension. title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6 long-context prefill is ~36% slower on Model Runner V2: the blocking seq-len sync removes stream overlap
summary: ## Summary On Atlas 800T A3, Qwen3.6-27B W8A8 with TP=2, Model Runner V2 needs **+36% wall time** for a ~200k-token prefill while executing **the same operators, the same number of times, at the same speed** as Model Runner V1 (+0.4% NPU time, +2.4% host ACL time). Per-stream accounting shows the difference is **idle time on the compute stream**: both runners spend ~41.3 s executing kernels, but V2 accumulates **23.2 s of idle instead of 6.1 s**, i.e. V2 loses ~17 s of allreduce/compute overlap. The blocking wait is in `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py::_update_seq_lens_cpu()`, which calls `num_computed_tokens_event.synchronize()` whenever a speculator (MTP) is configured, and can only be skipped for the Kimi model classes. title: perf: reduce per-step metadata H2D/D2D copies in the decode path
summary: ## Summary Single-request GDN decode on Ascend 910B4 is host-bound (NPU busy only ~42%), and per-step host time is dominated by many small H2D/D2D copies (~35-72us each). This PR removes or packs most of them: 1. `copy_snapshot_to_gpu` / `commit_block_table`: persistent pinned staging instead of a fresh `clone().pin_memory()` per call; `commit_block_table` additionally gets a dirty flag so steady-state decode skips the staging copy + H2D entirely (a class-level generation counter, bumped on every commit and on `clear()`, lets consumers skip redundant derived-data copies safely). 2. `AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder`: reuse `common_attn_metadata.query_start_loc` instead of re-uploading `query_start_loc_cpu` (the removed line had its own TODO acknowledging the redundancy). 3. GDN metadata builders: the padded `query_start_loc` row and `actual_seq_lengths` are fully known on CPU — build them in pinned staging and ship one H2D each instead of per-group D2D launches. All GDN group builders receive identical inputs per step, so destination buffers are shared class-wide (device/capacity guarded) and writes are deduplicated with a CPU-side content compare. 4. Model runner: per-step metadata buffers (`prev_positions`, `req_indices`, `query_pos`, `mrope_positions`, `num_scheduled_tokens`, `num_computed_tokens`, `gdn_query_start_loc`) are rebound onto two dtype-packed pinned staging + device tensors, so a step issues **one H2D per dtype** via `_flush_packed_h2d` instead of one launch per buffer. Also skips a redundant full-buffer `query_start_loc` upload when no padding rows were writte

title: [RFC]: Defer SSM checkpoint writeback across speculative decoding steps on Ascend
summary: ## Motivation Ascend’s GLM KDA and Qwen GDN RecoverSSM already avoid storing a full SSM state for every candidate token. After sampling, they replay the accepted prefix and write back the resulting checkpoint each step. That still produces a full-state write on every speculative decoding round. Upstream Mamba2 ReplaySSM demonstrates another option. It keeps accepted updates in a bounded ring across decode steps and writes back the full state when required. This RFC proposes testing whether the same writeback policy reduces HBM traffic and TPOT for Ascend KDA and GDN, where the update records and replay kernels differ. [Upstream ReplaySSM #55688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55688) · [Ascend Qwen GDN RecoverSSM #20485](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20485) ## Proposed Change 1. **Keep a checkpoint and a bounded history of accepted updates.** During verify, use the checkpoint and pending history to reconstruct the starting SSM state. After sampling, retain only the accepted prefix of the new records. Track the oldest pending record and the pending count per live state slot. 2. **Materialize the full state when needed.** Flush before the history runs out of room. For later prefix caching and P/D support, materialize the exact boundary state before publishing or transferring it. Keep convolution state on its existing commit path in the first prototype. 3. **Prototype behind an opt-in on MRV2.** Start with one model and colocated decode without prefix caching. Use the existing per-step commit as the baseline and fallback. Extend to the second model

title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B batched MTP is not batch-invariant: identical prompts diverge at index 10-22
summary: ## Summary With more than one sequence in a scheduler batch and MTP speculative decoding enabled, two identical prompts can produce **different final token sequences**, on Model Runner V1 as well as on Model Runner V2. The first divergent token is not fixed: it has been observed anywhere between index 10 and index 22 depending on the run. Since the two copies are in the same batch, this is a per-sequence state/scheduling effect, not a numerical difference between the two runners. A frozen golden for a batch>1 case therefore cannot exist: it would fail on the next run. title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B batched MTP is not batch-invariant: identical prompts in one batch diverge (MRV1 and MRV2)
summary: ## Summary On Atlas 800T A3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8 with `qwen3_5_mtp` and two concurrent prompts is not reproducible within either MRV1 or MRV2. Both runners exceed the decode tolerance on the second prompt and both eventually diverge on token identity; on the first prompt the pre-divergence same-token delta stays within tolerance on both runners. title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B prefill TTFT regression: host ACLNN workspace/tiling is not reused
summary: ## Summary On Atlas 800T A3, with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8, TP=2, MTP=3 and ACL Graph enabled, the MRV2 model runner is **25.4% slower than MRV1 on prefill TTFT** for `batch=4, prompt_len=2048, max_tokens=1`. title: [BugFix] Sync SWA block IDs before KV Pool prefill saves
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? During chunked prefill, vLLM replaces released SWA request blocks with null blocks. KV Pool's request tracker previously only appended new block IDs, so a later save could associate an old key with a recycled physical slot when that key was missing remotely. This PR refreshes SWA block IDs from vLLM's current request block table before building each running request's save metadata. Released positions become block ID 0 and are skipped by the store thread. The non-layerwise save path now drains its queue in `wait_for_save()` before the next chunk can reuse source slots. SWA block pinning from the earlier revision is removed; existing Mamba retention remains. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. KV Pool no longer PUTs released SWA slots under old keys. Draining each save batch can increase prefill latency; this has not been benchmarked. ### How was this patch tested? - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, Python AST parsing, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files. - A focused unit test checks that a released SWA position is replaced with block ID 0 from the current request table. - Unit tests and NPU serving were not run locally; this macOS workspace cannot run torch/torch_npu-dependent code. - `bash format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` is not installed in this worktree. ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Released SWA positions become null, and null block IDs are skipped by the store thread. - [x] **Regression test**: Current request table replaces a stale SWA

title: [BugFix][v0.30.0] Sync SWA block IDs before KV Pool prefill saves
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Backport the final net changes of #20853 (head `b1a0e9b664bd3d2b17a0413949010c4e1d6eee29`) to `releases/v0.30.0`. During chunked prefill, vLLM retires old SWA blocks and replaces their request-table entries with null blocks. KV Pool's tracker can retain an old physical block ID and later publish that slot's current contents under a historical key when the key is absent remotely. Refresh cacheable SWA/RSWA group IDs from the current `KVCacheManager` request table before building running-request metadata, and skip nonpositive block IDs in the bulk PUT path. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [BugFix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Fix FP8 adaptation: ignored_layers prefix mismatch silently quantizes layers the checkpoint left unquantized
summary: ## What this fixes Fixes #20860. GLM-5.3-Flash's native FP8 checkpoint lists ~1150 layers in `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert` using a flat module-prefix (e.g. `model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.wq_b`). vLLM loads this model as a nested `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` wrapper, whose real prefix for that layer is `language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.wq_b`. `AscendFp8Config.get_quant_method()`'s exact-match check never matches any of these entries, so layers the checkpoint explicitly left unquantized — several with no `weight_scale_inv` at all — are silently FP8-quantized instead. No error, no warning. Concretely, this makes the KeyPool sparse-indexer's query projection (`wq_b`) produce exactly-zero query vectors at every indexer layer, collapsing its top-k token selection into a frozen, query-independent set. See #20860 for the full live evidence and benchmark impact (AIME2026 40% → 93.3%, GPQA-Diamond 62.1% → 89.4% with this fix). ## The fix `AscendFp8Config` retries the skip check with `match_mode="suffix"` only if the configured mode already failed, and logs a one-time warning when that's what matched. This is additive only: - No behavior change for any checkpoint whose exact match already succeeds (which is every checkpoint this code path has correctly served so far). - Can't exempt a layer that has no corresponding `ignored_layers` entry in any form. - Scoped to `AscendFp8Config` only. ## User-facing change Yes. GLM-5.3-Flash native FP8 honors checkpoint-excluded layers under nested model wrappers. Release note: `release_notes/fragments/20861.ya

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Expand each KV group by its own physical block size in Mooncake P2P
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `MooncakeConnectorScheduler` emits the KV block size in the P2P transfer metadata from `cache_config.block_size`. On hybrid (Mamba / linear-attention) models the logical scheduler block size can legitimately be smaller than the physical KV block size of the attention groups: the KV-cache group specs are resolved at runtime per layer (a sliding-window draft layer of a speculative drafter keeps the kernel-limited 128-token block while all other groups use 1024 tokens). `EngineCore` then collapses `cache_config.block_size` to the minimum across groups, which is synced back to the API server. The metadata then describes block ids counted in 1024-token physical blocks as if they were counted in 128-token blocks. The scalar is equally wrong in the opposite regime: under Mamba-aligned hybrid layouts `cache_config.block_size` is the LCM across groups (e.g. 1536), so a 128-token sliding-window draft group next to 1536-token full-attention groups is sized from the 1536 scalar, and the receiver's kernel size and packing for that group are both wrong. title: [Performance][Ops] Split fused qkvz projection into separate qkv and z linears in GDN
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In `vllm_ascend/ops/gdn.py`, `AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward` previously computed the fused `qkvz` input projection and then split the output tensor into `mixed_qkv` and `z`. For the non-interleaved GQA layout used by Qwen3.5 (`gqa_interleaved_layout=False`), this PR adds a fast path that splits the projection weight up front and computes the two parts with independent `torch.nn.functional.linear` calls: ```python qkv_size = (self.key_dim * 2 + self.value_dim) // self.tp_size z_size = self.value_dim // self.tp_size use_weight_split = ( getattr(self, "quant_config", None) is None and isinstance( getattr(self.in_proj_qkvz, "quant_method", None), UnquantizedLinearMethod, ) ) if use_weight_split: qkvz_weight = self.in_proj_qkvz.weight mixed_qkv = torch.nn.functional.linear( hidden_states, qkvz_weight[:qkv_size] ) z = torch.nn.functional.linear( hidden_states, qkvz_weight[qkv_size:] ) else: mixed_qkvz, _ = self.in_proj_qkvz(hidden_states) mixed_qkv, z = mixed_qkvz.split([qkv_size, z_size], dim=-1) ``` The weight-split path is restricted to genuinely unquantized models. Quantized models continue to use the projection module's normal `forward` path before splitting the result. This guard is required for the quantized Qwen3.5 regression identified during review. ModelSlim checkpoints can leave Qwen3.5 GDN projections marked as `FLOAT` while quantizing surrounding MoE layers as `W8A8_DYNAMIC`. title: [BugFix][EPLB] Rebuild Gloo NZ receives with the destination's cast parameters
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Roadmap #20602 item 5. FRACTAL_NZ is not a single physical layout: `npu_format_cast` derives the C0 tiling from `customize_dtype`/`input_dtype`, so a weight cast with them reports a C0 variant. A W4A8MXFP expert weight is cast with `customize_dtype=float8_e4m3fn` and `input_dtype=float4_e2m1fn_x2`, and reports `FRACTAL_NZ_C0_16` (50), not `FRACTAL_NZ` (29). title: [v0.30.0][Performance][Model] Fuse the dense-SP boundary collectives into their GEMMs (MC2)
summary: Backport of the dense-SP MC2 fusion to `releases/v0.30.0`, on top of the dense sequence parallelism landed in #19001. Main-branch counterpart: #20934 (stacked on #20756). ### What this PR does / why we need it? Dense SP replaces each per-layer TP all-reduce with a reduce-scatter + all-gather pair around the layer boundary. This PR fuses those two boundary collectives into their GEMMs for prefill-sized batches on unquantized (BF16/FP16) checkpoints, using the `torch_npu` MC2 fused kernels: - **Column side — `npu_all_gather_base_mm`** (`DenseSpAllGatherMmOp` on `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`): the sequence all-gather is folded into the GEMM, so the gathered activation is never materialized and the communication overlaps the matmul. - **Row side — `npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base`** (`DenseSpMmReduceScatterOp` on `o_proj` / GDN `out_proj` / `down_proj`): the TP partial sums are reduced and scattered in one kernel, so neither the partial output nor a separate collective is materialized. The GDN in-projections deliberately keep the decoder-level gather (it feeds several consumers inside the mixer core); their `out_proj` still fuses. title: [Performance][Model] Fuse matmul+allreduce for Qwen3.5 row-parallel linears on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Under TP, every row-parallel linear in Qwen3.5 (attention `o_proj`, MLP `down_proj`, GDN `out_proj`) runs a matmul followed by an all-reduce: the all-reduce (reduce-scatter + all-gather on the ring) makes the activation cross the HCCL link twice, and the two kernels execute serially — the all-reduce can only start after the matmul fully completes. This PR fuses both steps into one CANN kernel — `aclnnMatmulAllReduce` (`torch_npu.npu_mm_all_reduce_base`) — so communication overlaps the matmul tail and the activation crosses the interconnect once, halving interconnect traffic per layer. Implementation (single new file `qwen3_5_mc2.py` + an 11-line registration): - The fused op is wrapped in a custom op (`direct_register_custom_op` + fake impl) for torch.compile opacity. The ACL-graph capture guard lives **inside the op impl** because dynamo specializes outer Python guards away at compile time; during capture (GLOBAL/MAX modes) it falls back to stock matmul+allreduce — the MC2 comm-resource allocation uses a synchronous memcpy prohibited under capture (EE1016). - `_AscendMC2Mixin.__init__` installs the fused path **instance-level**: only this model's own `RowParallelLinear` modules with `reduce_results=True` get their `forward` swapped (`types.MethodType`); the global class, other models and LoRA are untouched. - Eligibility per call: `reduce_results ∧ TP>1 ∧ M>1000 (prefill-sized) ∧ bias-free ∧ UnquantizedLinearMethod`. title: [Performance][Quantization] Fuse add-rms-norm-bias with dynamic quant
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `AscendRMSNorm` always calls `npu_add_rms_norm_bias` when a residual is present, including checkpoints with no norm bias. W8A8 dynamic linear then calls `npu_dynamic_quant(dst_type=torch.int8)`. The norm-quant fusion pass already rewrites `npu_add_rms_norm` + `npu_dynamic_quant`, and `npu_add_rms_norm_bias` only when a real bias tensor is present. The common no-bias sequence never matched, so those two kernels stayed separate. This registers patterns for `npu_add_rms_norm_bias` (bias `None` or a real bias) followed by `npu_dynamic_quant`, with and without an explicit `dst_type=torch.int8`, and replaces them with `npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_quant`. Fusion still runs only when `fuse_norm_quant` is enabled (the default) and the hardware profile supports graph norm-quant fusion. On a successful match the compile log prints `Replaced N norm-quant patterns`. This is a compile-time fusion. Eager execution is unchanged. FP8 / MX dynamic quant is not part of this replacement. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? W8A8 dynamic models compiled with norm-quant fusion use `npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_quant` instead of `npu_add_rms_norm_bias` plus `npu_dynamic_quant` on the residual RMSNorm path. title: [Misc][Ops] Fix a bug inside a triton operator fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR fixes an Ascend Triton compilation failure in `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel`, which can be triggered by Qwen3.5 in some decoding cases. The previous implementation handled invalid initial state indices by: 1. mapping negative `h0_indices` to `0`, 2. loading from `h0_source`, 3. then using `tl.where` to discard the loaded value when the original index was invalid. Although the logic is correct, this creates a more complex IR pattern involving `tl.load`, `tl.zeros_like`, and post-load `tl.where`. On Ascend Triton, this can trigger an MLIR lowering failure during kernel compilation. This PR moves the validity condition directly into the `tl.load` mask: ```python idx = tl.load(h0_indices + i_n) tmp0 = tl.where(idx < 0, 0, idx) p_h0 = h0_source + tmp0 * HV * K * V + i_hv * K * V + o_k[:, None] * V + o_v[None, :] value0 = tl.load(p_h0, mask=mask_h & (idx >= 0), other=0).to(tl.float32) b_h += value0 - vLLM version: v0.20.2 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/9090368b650896bf5fc990c921df7eb4c20355a5

title: [CI][Feature] Accelerate csrc compilation with Scheduled ninja incremental build
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Introduces a **ninja-based incremental build cache** (`csrc/build`) that is shared by all CI workflows compiling vllm-ascend from source. It replaces the old hash-based exact-match cache (`CSRC_HASH` → `vllm-ascend-build-v1`) which had a near-zero hit rate on PRs — a single line change in any csrc file invalidated the entire cache and triggered a full recompilation. **Single producer, multiple consumers:** A new scheduled workflow (`schedule_cache_csrc_build.yaml`, daily at 02:00 UTC+8) is the sole producer. It dynamically reads the Dockerfile list and release branches from `schedule_image_build_and_push.yaml`, extracts the CANN image tag from each Dockerfile's `FROM` line at runtime, and compiles with ninja for **2 branches × 6 Dockerfiles × 2 architectures = 24 cache variants**. The resulting `csrc/build` directory is saved to GitHub Actions cache. Consumers (`_selected_tests.yaml`, `_schedule_image_build.yaml`, and 8 Dockerfiles) simply restore `csrc/build` before compilation — CMake + ninja auto-detect changed files and rebuild only the diff. **Commit history (oldest first):** | Commit | Description | |--------|-------------| | `8e003976` | Rewrite `csrc/build.sh` / `build_aclnn.sh` / cmake rules to support ninja | | `c512b37d` | Fix `build_aclnn.sh` bug; add initial ninja cache to `_e2e_test.yaml` | | `d7fa8ee0` | **Major refactor:** unify key format, remove hash cache, `_schedule_image_build` consumer | | `de9b0987` | Fix `build_aclnn.sh` moe dispatch; enhance ninja cache in E2E | | `8f4782cd` | Resolve merge conflicts; clean up

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The Chat Completions / Completions PD proxy treats each HTTP byte chunk as a complete JSON response or SSE event. Prefill KV release remains tied to the first raw response bytes. Related: #13040 (existing accounting), #17715 (Messages/Responses framing in a separate protocol path), #21637 (missing Prefill detail warnings). title: [PD][Feature] Add opt-in bounded reads for Mooncake hybrid KV transfer
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Concurrent pull-mode KV reads can overrun a Decode receiver even when average link bandwidth is sufficient. This adds opt-in byte/descriptor batching and per-receiver FIFO admission around the two synchronous reads in `MooncakeHybridConnector`. The default byte limit is zero and preserves the original call/concurrency. An enabled read splits large descriptors at aligned offsets, preserves exact tails, and rejoins the FIFO between batches. Negative returns or exceptions stop that request's remaining batches and release admission. Interrupted waiters remove only their own queue token; they cannot release another active reader. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Two documented `kv_connector_extra_config` fields on Decode: ```json {"kv_read_batch_bytes": 262144, "kv_read_batch_descriptors": 128} ``` Bytes must be zero or a positive multiple of 256; descriptor count is a positive integer. Defaults preserve existing behavior. Small batches can add call overhead; 256 KiB is a measured setting, not a universal recommendation. Limits are per receiver, not a host/link bandwidth cap. No collective/QoS/PFC/ECN/driver/switch changes, fixed-rate throttle or new environment variable. `release_notes/fragments/20491.yaml` is included. Request-failure propagation in #20488 is independent. ### How was this patch tested? **Main synchronization, 2026-11-12:** `ecb7ba34df4a5a22f2fc8dee62d001ef7d165e96` is linearly rebased onto Ascend main `a4971912ceaf3e775425a793369de32a93aa13ba`. title: [Performance] Add QLI candidate skip fast path (mode 4) for QuantLightningIndexerV2
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #19910. `QuantLightningIndexerV2` in `candidate_mode=2` (consumer) computes scores for the full 2048-wide tile and only *masks* out-of-candidate scores right before the sort, so the AIV `SortAll(2048) + MergeSort` cascade spends ~99% of `aiv_time` sorting entries that can never win top-k (see profiling data in the issue). This PR adds `CANDIDATE_MODE_CONSUMER_SKIP = 4`: consumer layers compactly gather scores/positions of **candidate blocks only** and sort the compacted 64-aligned length S instead of the full tile: - `BuildCandidateCompact()` reuses the existing `CountGE` binary search to locate the per-tile candidate range `[hi, lo)`, gathers score/pos pairs via in-pipeline `Adds(+0)` int32 copies (bit-exact, MTE-pipeline-safe), and fixes the mixed tail block with an entry-index-driven 64-wide vector mask chain (no scalar `SetValue`, no data-value dependence) - `ProcessVec1` routes mode4 to `SortAll(S) + MergeSort` on the compact buffer; mode2 path is untouched - Host-side validation (`tiling.cpp` / `torch_adpt.h`) accepts mode 4 with the same consumer-input constraints as mode 2 - Gated by `VLLM_ASCEND_QLI_CANDIDATE_SKIP` in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` (**default off = mode 2**, one env var to roll out/roll back) Mathematical equivalence: top-k positions always lie inside candidate blocks (mode1 pins the tail block). summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it?
