The ordinary SFA indexer registers its own Ascend cache owner, including quantized dtype, scales, DCP replication and runtime ownership. The worker collects those specs without looking up the paired implementation by layer name. Upstream cache-role and grouping metadata are retained. 2. **Logical dimensions and physical bytes are separate.** MRV2 keeps the logical `head_size` and uses `state_content_bytes` for packed storage, including indexer scales. Allocation, views and KVPP consume the physical component width explicitly. Existing legacy specs without an explicit byte count retain their physical width convention. 3. **Cross-layer padding belongs to planning.** Collection returns each owner's demand; the planner aligns pages before grouping. GLM-Next main/KDA and indexer/tail page classes, QSA descriptor-native alignment and contiguous K/V segment constraints remain in their existing planning paths. title: [Feature][Quantization] LeapQuant recurrent-state int8 quantization for GDN/KDA on A3
summary: Implements the pure torch-npu milestone of the LeapQuant RFC #21097. ## Motivation LeapQuant ([arXiv 2609.38166](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166)) quantizes the **recurrent state** of hybrid linear-attention models online, during inference: the GDN/KDA state of Qwen3.5 and Kimi linear-attention layers is kept full precision inside a `window`-token span and re-encoded at each window boundary as a small fp16 low-rank compensator plus int8 residual codes. Error is injected once per window instead of once per decode step, so it stays bounded over long contexts instead of accumulating geometrically, while most of the state pool drops to one byte per element. No modified checkpoint or offline step is needed. ## What this PR adds - `vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/mamba_state/leapquant/` — state ops (fixed seeded start basis, two-pass MGS subspace iteration, fp16 low-rank compensators `q`/`u`, int8 residual codes with per-K/per-V scales) and the runtime row-flush glue (due-row selection from `seq_lens % window == 0`, slot-index gather/scatter through the compiled KDA state-copy plan, a CPU fallback, or triton gather/scatter). - `leapquant_config` in `additional_config` (`enabled` / `window` / `compensator_tokens` / `bits`) with startup validation: A3-only; rejects speculative decoding, aligned Mamba cache mode, C8 KV quantization, KV connectors, and FULL graph mode. - Flush hooks after the recurrent update in `ops/gdn.py` (Qwen3.5 GDN) and after the prefill scatter in `ops/kimi_kda.py` (Kimi KDA), driven by `leapquant_seq_lens` attached in `ops/gdn_attn_builder.py`. - Docs: `lea

title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Support the UCM prefetch handle in PD disaggregation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In PD-disaggregated deployments, the KV-block handle a connector produces at request finish is currently dropped on the streaming path, so clients that consume chunks incrementally (e.g. a router that later prefetches those blocks on a decode node) never receive it. It is also impossible to combine `kv_transfer_params` when more than one sub-connector produces them: the HMA path in `AscendMultiConnector` raises as soon as a second sub-connector returns a non-empty dict. This PR closes both gaps: 1. `AscendMultiConnector.request_finished_all_groups()` now merges `kv_transfer_params` from every sub-connector key by key instead of rejecting the second producer. A genuine key clash still raises `RuntimeError`, so silent overwrites are impossible. 2. `MooncakeConnector` forwards the connector-provided `hash_keys` from the scheduler-side `kv_transfer_params` into the final response on the decode node (`do_remote_decode=False`, finished request). Non-empty `hash_keys` there mark a request that was proxy-forwarded for remote prefill. 3. `UCMConnectorV1` can now expose a prefetch entry point: once the worker KV caches are registered, an optional per-rank HTTP prefetch server is started (`prefetch_http.enable`, disabled by default), with `prefetch()` bridging to the UCM store's `prefetch_data()`. 4. A new platform patch, `patch_kv_transfer_params_streaming`, injects `kv_transfer_params` into the last SSE chunk before `data: [DONE]`. title: [BugFix][KVPool] Propagate transfer-thread device-binding startup failures
summary: Fixes #20975 ### What this PR does / why we need it? If a KV transfer thread raises from backend device binding, it exits before setting its readiness event or recording a fatal error. The pool worker waits on that event without a timeout, so initialization cannot complete or report the original exception. Catch backend device-binding exceptions into the existing `_fatal_error` channel, always signal `ready_event` in `finally`, and return without entering the request loop on failure. Call `raise_if_failed()` immediately after each readiness wait in both the bulk and layerwise workers. Merged [#19101](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19101) handles queued-transfer/request-loop failures and shutdown, but device binding remains outside that guarded loop. Open [#19193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19193) publishes a different class's Mooncake scheduler ZMQ startup errors. Closed [#19651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19651) changes tests only and checks successful startup, not a `set_device()` exception. The inspected diffs do not cover this readiness gap. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. KV pool initialization now reports transfer-thread device-binding failures instead of waiting indefinitely for a startup signal. Release note: [`release_notes/fragments/20986.yaml`](https://github.com/wangjianyuweg/vllm-ascend/blob/fd0d4339304de627dc2374150ec508f6efd1b448/release_notes/fragments/20986.yaml). ### How was this patch tested? title: [BugFix][Model] Fix GLM5Next MTP compressed-tensors quantization mapping
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix GLM-5.3-Flash MTP startup with mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoints, including the AutoRound MXFP4 export. The text-only MTP drafter can inherit the target's quantization configuration after its layer names have been mapped to `language_model.model.*`. Expose the same draft configuration through `set_current_vllm_config` while constructing the predictor, since quantization scheme constructors also consult the active configuration. The target configuration remains unchanged. Other quantization methods retain their existing path. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Affected GLM-5.3-Flash compressed-tensors MTP drafts can initialize and load their packed MXFP4 expert weights with the intended high-precision exclusions. title: [BugFix][Platform] Fix silent token corruption with V1 model runner + pipeline parallelism + MTP
summary: Fixes #14207. ### What this PR does / why we need it With `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (V1 runner) + `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` + MTP speculative decoding, output tokens are silently corrupted. This is the same failure reported in #17149, which added a fail-fast guard that rejects the combination. This PR fixes the underlying paths instead of rejecting it, so `V1 runner + PP>1 + MTP` becomes usable on Ascend. Three separate defects have to be fixed together; fixing any subset still produces divergent output: 1. **Draft tokens never reach the scheduler.** `patch_pp_mtp` skips `EngineCore.post_step` under PP, and the V1 runner builds `ModelRunnerOutput` without ever populating `spec_token_ids`. The scheduler therefore receives no drafts and `spec_decode_num_drafts` stays 0 — speculation is silently disabled. Note this failure mode is *invisibly "correct"*: PP2 output matches PP1 exactly, because PP2 is simply not speculating. A `drafts > 0` assertion is required for any test of this combination. 2. **Accepted-token count is stale on non-final stages.** Non-final PP stages do not sample, so the number of drafts accepted by the previous verify step is not available locally. Without it, the hybrid GDN/Mamba recurrent state drifts: at the same step the final stage had `acc=[4]` while rank 0 still held `acc=[1]`. 3. **The batch queue lets the scheduler run ahead.** With a batch queue, a request is advanced before the previous verify output is consumed, so draft writeback lands on mutated `Request` state (same direction as upstream vllm-project/vllm#61326). ### How this PR fixes

title: [BugFix][Worker] Clear stale block ids left by move_row/add_row in block table
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Block-table rows are consumed by **request-derived lengths** — FIA reads the columns covered by `kv_len`, the Triton `compute_slot_mapping` kernel walks the flat GPU buffer, GDN/mamba state paths gather state indices — not by `num_blocks_per_row`. Two row-update paths leave previously-valid block ids beyond a row's live region, which get dereferenced after those blocks have been freed and reallocated. In hybrid models (attention + mamba/GDN groups) all block-table groups recycle ids through one LIFO free stack, so the stale id frequently points at another group's live data; under dense KV layout (KV pool and mamba state pool aliasing one unified pool) this corrupts mamba recurrent state, and every later request that hits the affected prefix produces garbled output or immediate EOS. Fixes: - **`move_row`**: clear the vacated source row (mirrors the fix already applied upstream in vllm-project/vllm#49757, which this fork had not merged) **and** the target-row tail left by a shrinking move. - **`add_row`**: when a row is rebuilt shorter than its previous content (a request landing on a recycled row slot), clear the tail beyond the new live region. `append_row` is growth-only and needs no change once the two shrinking paths are fixed. Production evidence (v0.30.x, hybrid GDN model, prefix caching on, 2× Ascend 910B): 12/12 deterministic garbled outputs on prefix-hit requests with bitwise-identical signatures across both devices; 410 operator-level parameter dumps trace the corruption to stale block-table cells consumed via slot-mapping/FI

title: [Performance][GLM] Reuse device offsets for short-prefill recurrent KDA

title: [Feature] Mask EOS sampled inside the think block (Qwen3-class reasoning models)
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen3.8-class models occasionally sample their end-of-turn token inside the `think` block: the request stops with `finish_reason=stop`, the whole answer is parked in `reasoning_content`, and `content` is left empty. Agent harnesses (e.g. tau2-bench) read this as an empty reply and the run crashes. Upstream tracks this as vllm-project/vllm#55420 (the `reasoning_eos_policy` PR #55562 was closed unmerged); with MTP/speculative decoding the mid-think EOS can also be drafted and accepted, silently terminating the turn. This PR carries the mask sketched in the #55420 discussion as an **opt-in**, covering both model runners: - **V1 runner**: `ThinkingEosMaskStateHolder` (`vllm_ascend/sample/thinking_eos_mask.py`) extends the stock `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder`, created from `NPUInputBatch`. title: [Feature] Add experimental whole-request Mooncake push connector
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it` The non-layerwise Mooncake Pull proxy submits D after P returns. D allocation and transfer preparation therefore add to the post-prefill handoff. title: [Bugfix][Worker] Preserve request-accepted counts across scheduling p…
summary: Fixes #20677 ## 问题 async 调度 + hybrid GDN（mamba_cache_mode="align"）+ MTP 组合下，defer_block_free 产生的调度暂停会丢失请求的 accepted 计数，下一次 forward 读错 mamba 状态槽， 静默污染生成（复读环 / 乱码），全程不报错。完整根因分析与证据见 #20677。 ## 根因（摘要） - align 模式下 accepted 计数即"请求已结算 recurrent 状态所在槽"的地址 （slot = state_idx + accepted − 1），由 FLA/GDN 内核与 mamba precopy 消费； - 该计数只存在于按 batch 行号索引的临时量中：postprocess 按刚执行完那批的行序 D2H，下一步经 prev_req_id_to_index 认领重排，映射缺项缺省为 1； - defer_block_free 在分配失败且 victim 仍在飞时放弃抢占，产生"暂停"：未调度 请求被移出 InputBatch（连带删除 prev 映射条目），而其 mamba 状态块与 mamba_state_idx 按请求 ID 存活； - 请求回来时按新请求发布 accepted=1，真状态仍停在暂停前的槽位，forward 从槽 0 读到缺失至多 num_spec 个已接受 token 的旧状态，并被随后的 precopy 归并洗白。 ## 修改内容（vllm_ascend/worker/v1/model_runner.py） - 新增按请求 ID 的两份元数据：`_mamba_accepted_by_request`（每请求最近一次 结算的计数）、`_mamba_pending_accepted_rows`（postprocess D2H 提交时的 req→row 快照，消费一次）； - `_update_states` 开头按 finished/preempted/resumed/new 四类生命周期事件 失效两份数据（防旧生命周期的 pending D2H 回填脏值）； - `_update_states_after_model_execute` 在提交 D2H 前记录 req→row 快照； - `_sync_num_accepted_tokens` 在 event 同步后先收割全部 pending 行（含本批 未调度的请求），再按当前批行序发布； - 门控 `_use_mamba_accepted_state_cache()`：async + speculative + hybrid + need_accepted_tokens + num_spec_tokens > 0 + mamba "align"；其余配置与原 实现逐位一致。 ## 验证 - CPU 元数据回归：对修改后源码提取方法直接驱动，覆盖连续步/部分暂停/整批 空步/多步暂停/生命周期失效/req_id 复用/门控关闭（零行为变化）； - 真实 NPU 内核对照：仅计数错误即改变 FLA GDN 输出（0.375 / 0.125 / 归位后 恢复 0.375）。 ## 影响范围 仅 V1 model runner。V2 按请求状态槽存计数、且不在未调度时移除请求，不受影响； 非 MTP / 非 hybrid / 非 align / 非 async 配置走门控旁路，零行为变化。 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

title: [Performance][DSv4.1] Shard the Engram wkv projection across TP ranks
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Port of upstream vLLM PR vllm-project/vllm#58678 to vLLM Ascend. This PR builds `wkv` as a `ColumnParallelLinear` with `gather_output=True`: - Each TP rank computes only `out_features / TP` output columns and one all-gather restores the full `kv` tensor, so the downstream gate (`fused_engram_gate` / `engram_gate`) is unchanged. - Under sequence parallelism the token dimension is already sharded, so the layer's `use_sequence_parallel` flag is passed through `disable_tp` to keep the projection replicated there (correctness requires it; see the fallback path below). - With TP=1 the layer degrades to a plain linear; behavior is unchanged. Measured on 8× Ascend NPUs (TP8 + EP, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w4a8, DSpark, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, sequence parallelism disabled): output token throughput +1.84%, mean TPOT -2.04%, mean E2EL -1.80%, mean TTFT -0.87%. The wkv matmul kernel drops from 260 µs to 45 µs (-82.7%), while the added all-gather costs 4 µs on device. Upstream reported similar gains on 8×H20 (TTFT -3.5% ~ -4.2%, decode throughput +1.5% ~ +4.0%). Weight memory: each rank now stores `1/TP` of the wkv weights (~0.13 GiB/GPU for the w4a8 checkpoint at TP8), which goes back to the KV cache. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [BugFix][Core] Bound the KV-pool lookup RPC with a deadline, versioned errors and socket recovery
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #14147. The scheduler asks the worker, over a ZMQ REQ/REP socket inside the same instance, whether the external AscendStore KV pool already holds a prefix. Three things were wrong with that call: 1. **The wait was unbounded.** The client blocked on `recv()` forever, so a worker that died mid-request stalled scheduling instead of degrading. 2. **The reply could not express failure.** The server answered with a bare 4-byte integer, so "zero hits" and "the worker blew up" were the same wire value, and any decode error on the reply path was indistinguishable from a miss. 3. **The server loop had no per-request boundary.** One malformed frame or one backend exception could end the serving thread, after which every lookup in the process timed out against a dead peer. This change bounds the wait, gives the reply a versioned envelope, and puts an exception boundary around each request on both ends. **1. One deadline per `lookup()` (new `lookup_rpc_timeout_ms`, default 5000 ms)** One wall-clock budget is started before the first frame is sent and is the only budget the rest of the call may spend: `send` takes from it, `recv` is given the remainder (never a fresh full timeout), and response decoding and validation are also covered by it. `0` and negative values are rejected at construction rather than meaning "wait forever" -- the config key is validated in `validate_timeout_ms()` before any socket is opened, and so is a positive value too large to honour, because the socket option itself is 32-bit (`_MAX_SOCKOPT_MS = 2**31 - 1`). **2. title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Add heartbeat leases to MooncakeConnectorV2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A request admitted to D's scheduler can wait for a decode slot or KV transfer longer than P's delay-free timeout. P can then release and reuse its KV blocks before D finishes reading them, causing transfer failures or incorrect output. Add renewable KV leases to `MooncakeConnectorV2`: - Register outstanding remote KV in the existing scheduler `on_new_request()` hook, before allocation. A dedicated D control thread continues renewal while the scheduler/model execution waits, until aggregated worker receive completion. Aborted in-flight reads retain their lease until worker completion. - Batch request IDs by producer over the existing scheduler ZMQ control endpoint, with at most 512 IDs per packet and one unacknowledged packet per peer. Nonblocking I/O and per-peer ACK timeouts isolate unavailable producers. Idle connectors wait on an event. - On P, use two expiry-ordered `OrderedDict` queues for initial and renewed leases. Registration, renewal and completion take average O(1) per request; expiry collection takes O(expired requests + 1), avoiding a full scan each scheduler step. Late heartbeats cannot revive expired requests. Unsent batches survive periodic refreshes and drain before the next snapshot is encoded. Per-peer connection setup failures close any partially created socket and retry that endpoint without terminating the control thread. Lease lookup consults the renewed queue only after an initial-queue miss. The documentation multiplication sign is corrected. Tracking begins at scheduler admission. Requests still in EngineCore

title: [Bugfix][SpecDecode] Drop padded query_start_loc entries from drafter sampling indices
summary: ### What this PR does The drafter derives the per-request sampling indices from `query_start_loc`: ```python token_indices_to_sample = common_attn_metadata.query_start_loc[1:] - 1 ``` `query_start_loc` is **padded before the drafter runs**: * `_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia()` appends one extra entry equal to the padded token count whenever `query_start_loc[num_reqs] < num_tokens_padded` (`num_reqs_padded += 1`); * the cross-DP token padding raises `num_tokens_padded` to the maximum over DP ranks, so a rank that owns fewer tokens gets a *larger* padded count. Those appended entries describe **no real request**: their query length is zero and their "last token" index is `num_tokens_padded - 1`, which is larger than the number of tokens actually forwarded. The index then reaches the gather ```python sample_hidden_states = last_hidden_states[token_indices_to_sample] ``` which lowers to `aclnnIndex`. Its index-range kernel (`IndexCheck`) aborts the vector core, the worker process dies, and in PD-disaggregated deployments the whole prefill/decode group is torn down. ### Reproduced on hardware Atlas 800I A3 super-node, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=2 / DP=16, `num_speculative_tokens=5`, dspark: ``` Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 8187 exceeds bounds 8184! index_check.h:130 void IndexCheckKernel<int>::ProcessScalar(...) Vector Core kernel execution failed, retCode=0x31. ``` The device dump of the same failure contains an index tensor of exactly `[8183, 8187]` for a batch of 8184 forwarded tokens — the extra `8187` is the padded `query_start_loc` tail (8188) minus one. title: [Performance] Optimize QLI candidate masks and Top512 tile merges on A2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? QLI candidate consumers build each tile's membership mask by repeatedly computing distances from every tile block to each candidate. This change optimizes the existing arch22 `candidate_mode=2` path: - Initialize a block mask and clear the slots for candidates inside the tile, then expand each block to eight token positions. Preserve the existing candidate sorting, binary-search bounds and scalar/vector fences. - For consumer `topk=512`, merge only the first `min(tile_length, 512)` entries of each sorted tile into the upstream adaptive Top-K accumulator. `TopK(A ∪ B) = TopK(TopK(A) ∪ TopK(B))`, so a sorted tile's entries after Top512 cannot affect the final Top512. The adaptive UB buffers, workspace layout, cross-core merge widths and Level-0 vector dispatch from #20303 are retained. title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Use prepared DSpark KV lengths for MLA DCP
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Its first extra KV token contained an Inf, and NaNs propagated into the merged draft attention output. The fix copies only real requests into an int32 CPU vector, leaves padded requests at zero, and applies the existing maximum model length limit. It runs in the metadata hook before draft forward/FULL graph replay, outside graph capture. GQA, non-DCP, and other draft attention architectures retain their existing paths; the outer target metadata preparation is unchanged. This is a correctness fix with a blocking device-to-host length copy. In FULL mode the metadata hook can be called twice per draft step. The synchronization cost has not been benchmarked; a future exact-length CPU mirror could avoid it without reintroducing optimistic lengths. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Performance][MRV2] Skip seq-lens D2H sync for device-native backends under spec decoding via consumer-declared requirement

title: [v0.32.0rc][Attention][BugFix] Retain MiniMax DSpark graph FlashAttn
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Setting `speculative_config.enforce_eager=false` for native MiniMax M3.1 DSpark currently makes `_validate_minimax_dspark_flash_attn` reject CANN FlashAttn and fall back to FIA. That backend switch caused a measurable graph-mode regression. Remove only the eager requirement. The existing CANN graph path already captures device sequence lengths and tiling and replays persistent device buffers. Keep the A5 capability gate, live draft-loader tag, native/prepared architecture checks, MiniMax target type, PP/PCP/DCP=1, decoder / FP16-BF16 / unquantized-KV requirements and adaptive-verification / unsupported-feature guards. No kernel, graph replay or fusion implementation changes. Extend the selector regression tests to require CANN FlashAttn in both eager and graph modes for both native/prepared architecture names, and run all rejection cases in both modes. Existing Qwen3 DSpark and GLM DFlash2 selection stays unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Eligible A5 MiniMax M3.1 DSpark drafts retain CANN FlashAttn when graph execution is enabled, avoiding the unintended FIA fallback. ### How was this patch tested? - Base: `releases/v0.32.0rc@9d0e0491e`. - CPU production-function tests: **140 passed**: `python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/ut/attention tests/ut/attention/test_minimax_dspark_integration.py tests/ut/attention/test_minimax_ecosystem_fa3.py -q`. These execute production bodies with dependency stubs. The new graph positives reproduce the bug: four fail before the patch, while eager positives pass; all pass

title: [BugFix][Model] Revert MiniMax-M3 A3 TopK fusion for nightly validation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Temporarily revert #18294 to isolate the MiniMax-M3-W8A8-A3 nightly regression. The failing nightly job checked out `06d7a24415c1e0467f7f6912fd9eceb79571f0a7`, where GPQA fell to 51.52 and the NPU worker later crashed. A prior rerun based on `9f9da5562089280a7f01c3d03e855b258e372807` passed GPQA at 90.40 and TextVQA at 71.11. This branch contains only the #18294 revert, based on the failing job's actual checkout. It is intended for an A/B CI run; the result will determine whether #18294 caused the regression. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. It restores the previous MiniMax-M3 A3 index TopK path for validation. ### How was this patch tested? - `git diff --check` passed. - Python syntax parsing passed for the MiniMax-M3 and MSA modules. - NPU validation pending: run `MiniMax-M3-W8A8-A3` on A3 560T and compare GPQA, TextVQA, and NPU errors with the failed job. title: [Feature] Add reuse-prioritized LRU for sparse KV offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds an optional reuse-prioritized LRU policy for sparse KV offload, based directly on `releases/v0.26.0rc`. The existing policy places newly loaded entries after all surviving non-hit entries. Scans of one-time accesses can therefore evict previously reused KV. The new policy resets resident hits to age zero, inserts newly loaded entries at a configurable probation age, and uses free slots before evicting the oldest non-hit entries. Unaccessed resident entries age with saturation. The CPU C++ planner merges slot/age entries in linear time without sorting or moving physical KV. It reuses the existing miss-only H2D and resident attention paths. The default policy remains `lru`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Adds two options to `sparse_kv_offload_config`: | Option | Accepted values | Default | |---|---|---| | `eviction_policy` | `lru`, `reuse_prioritized_lru` | `lru` | | `probation_age` | Integer in `[0, 2147483646]`; used by the new policy | `4` | Add these fields to an existing sparse KV offload configuration: ```json { "eviction_policy": "reuse_prioritized_lru", "probation_age": 4 } ``` ### How was this patch tested? - Added `tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/test_lru_resident.py`, which compiles the production CPU planner definitions verbatim without torch/ACL dependencies. title: [BugFix][Quantization] Use FP32 scales for W8A8 grouped matmul
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A2 W8A8 grouped matmul can fail in `aclnnGroupedMatmulWeightNz` because the current GMM1/GMM2 paths pass FP16 scales. title: [RFC]: Request-sharded DFlash2 candidate generation under PCP on MRV2
summary: ### Motivation. DFlash2 currently repeats candidate generation across PCP ranks when used with the replicated draft path on Model Runner V2. This RFC proposes request-level sharding of that work, primarily to improve multi-request throughput. Related correctness prerequisite: #21630, which enables the replicated DFlash path with PCP and fixes draft capacity, synchronization, and vocabulary-sharded candidate selection. This RFC is a separate performance proposal; it does not expand that PR's scope. The distinction between target and draft execution matters: - PCP splits prefill token work. Some target decode/verification paths can also distribute requests across PCP ranks; that behavior is model/configuration-dependent. - After restoring the global inputs required by the replicated DFlash2 draft, each participating PCP rank on the last PP stage independently generates drafts for the global request batch. This is replicated draft computation, not TP across those ranks. - For 32 requests and PCP=8, that means eight ranks each generate candidates for all 32 requests. title: [Bug][EPLB] DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark misses draft MoE registration and redundant expert mapping
summary: ## Description DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark does not register its draft MoE layers for EPLB, and its checkpoint loader builds the expert mapping with zero redundant experts even when the physical layout has replicas. title: [Feature][Attention] Support quant_mode=5 pseudo-quant for MTP decode in C8 backend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `AscendC8AttentionBackendImpl` (INT8 KV cache, e.g. ModelSlim C8-quantized Qwen3-style dense models) has no correct fast path for MTP / speculative decoding: - The V2 model runner reports speculative decoding as `ChunkedPrefill`, and multi-token queries (1 + num_speculative_tokens per request) classify as decodes. The existing BNSD fast paths assume exactly one query token per request, so they mis-slice query rows against KV batch rows. - The generic fallback gathers and dequantizes the whole paged INT8 KV into dense float before TND attention, which is correct but slow. This PR routes the multi-token-query decode segment through `torch_npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` with `quant_mode=5` (KV pseudo-quantization): TND layout, paged INT8 KV handed to the operator directly via the NZ 5D view + block table, per-channel antiquant scales, causal mask with `sparse_mode=3`. When the installed torch_npu rejects `quant_mode=5` for this combination, the path degrades to a decode-scoped gather+dequant TND fallback (warn once, sticky per impl instance). The single-token BNSD fast path and ACL graph capture behavior are unchanged. Under ACL graph capture the multi-token-query decode segment is **explicitly rejected** for now, at both capture and replay time: the C8 branch of `full_graph_fia` raises before baking the one-query-row BNSD call, and `FIAParamProvider.resolve` (flagged `is_c8_bnsd`) rejects replays that arrive with MTP-shaped metadata. title: [Performance][ModelRunner] Issue num_computed_tokens D2H before RecoverSSM commit in MRV2 postprocessing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The `num_computed_tokens` D2H snapshot only depends on the `post_update` kernel, but it was issued after `model_state.postprocess_state`, whose `wait_stream` snapshot also covered the RecoverSSM commit kernels. The CPU consumer in `_update_seq_lens_cpu` therefore blocked until the commit drained, serializing the commit against the next step's input preparation. This PR issues the copy before `postprocess_state` by temporarily wrapping `model_state.postprocess_state`, so the commit stays out of the copy's wait set and overlaps the next step's input preparation. A fallback tail call keeps the snapshot issued on paths where `postprocess_state` does not run. The early copy is safe without a post-copy write barrier: staged request-state GPU writes only touch newly added requests' slots, while the snapshot consumer reads only `scheduled_cached_reqs` slots; the last writer of those slots is `post_update`, which `wait_stream` already orders the copy after. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes, measurable performance improvement for GDN hybrid + speculative decoding on MRV2 (numbers below). No API or configuration changes. ### How was this patch tested? Verified on A5 with Qwen3.x GDN hybrid + MTP: the ~40ms per-step idle gap after the draft section disappeared and steady-state decode TPS at 72-way concurrency recovered from 24 to ~30. title: [Test][BugFix] Align bisect dependencies with hardware Dockerfiles
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The nightly bisect tool previously adapted dependencies from a partial set of version and requirement files. On A3, that led it to fetch `torch-npu` from a slow or unreachable package source and misclassify environment setup failures as model regressions. This change reads each candidate's hardware-specific base Dockerfile (A2, A3, 310P, or A5), its matching nightly Dockerfile, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, and `requirements-nightly.txt`. The bisect tool uses the selected build recipe to switch vLLM, vLLM Ascend, nightly dependencies, Dockerfile-installed wheels, flash-attention-npu, and AISBench in build order. It rejects CANN image changes and unsupported Dockerfile build-step changes as environment errors. The new single-node `--mock-tests` mode performs the same checkout, version adaptation, dependency installation, and rebuild steps as a real trial, then simulates only the pytest verdict. Mock runs use separate state and reports, mark every verdict as simulated, and do not claim a first bad commit. Per-round logs record the requested Dockerfile pairing and installed vLLM/torch-npu versions before and after preparation. The PyTorch CPU extra index remains as specified by the Dockerfile; a reachable Huawei Cloud PyPI mirror is used as the primary index for isolated build dependencies. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Performance] Skip QSA CPU length sync for Ascend builder
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with MTP can skip the per-decode-step CPU sequence-length synchronization when every metadata consumer accepts the optimistic CPU upper bound and uses rejection-corrected lengths on device. The capability guard already allows the upstream `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder`, but the Ascend runtime instantiates `AscendQSAMetadataBuilder`. Because the guard intentionally uses an exact type allowlist, the Ascend builder misses the fast path and falls back to `num_computed_tokens_event.synchronize()` on every decode step. Profiling shows this host synchronization breaks asynchronous submission and creates bubbles between decode steps. This PR: - adds the audited `AscendQSAMetadataBuilder` to the exact allowlist for `AscendQSABackend`; - keeps all conservative fallbacks for unknown builders/backends, DCP, PCP, sparse KV offload, and real-time/interleaved multimodal inputs; - updates the positive regression fixture to use the actual Ascend builder; - retains an explicit compatibility test for the upstream builder. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. It removes an unnecessary per-step host synchronization for the supported Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Ascend QSA + MTP path, improving pure-decode throughput and latency without changing the API or configuration. title: [Attention][Feature] B1 paged verify for Gemma4 512-dim MTP verify on MRv2 (FIA-v2 BNSD)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Model Runner V2 has no path for the Gemma4-style head_dim=512 MTP verify step: FIA TND rejects head_dim=512, and the V2 capture metadata is never labeled `SpecDecoding`, so the PA capture gate does not fire either. This PR adds a dedicated, per-layer backend that captures the verify step as `npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2` BNSD paged ops (`sparse_mode=0`, per-sequence block table, explicit `[B, 1, k+1, W]` bool mask), so V2 can run MTP k=3 with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and the hybrid KV cache manager enabled. - New `vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v2_b1.py`: B1 backend/impl/builder, BNSD (`[2, blocks, Hkv, block, D]`) KV cache for the 512-dim layers, an all-visible placeholder mask at capture time with the real mask rebound on every graph update, and a per-layer `FIAPagedVerifyParamProvider`. - `platform.py`: `_want_b1_paged_verify()` selects the backend per layer — Model Runner V2 + speculative decoding + decoder self-attention + `head_dim == 512` + no sliding window; MLA/sparse/compress/PCP/DCP/ KV-connector/sink, adaptive verification and A5 keep the stock backend. - `attention/utils.py`: the B1 layers get private contiguous K/V buffers (the shared block-interleaved view is rejected by the FIA-v2 paged op), plus the shared one-query-per-row re-lay helper used by both attention lanes. - `device/utils.py`: normalize BNSD/HND cache views before the dense prefill KV gather. - `envs.py`: `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_B1_PAGED_VERIFY` (default 1, `0` opts out). - `worker/v2/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py`: per-layer graph-update param

title: perf(glm5next): replicate the input embedding to skip its mask and all-reduce
summary: Add a VLLM_ASCEND_GLM_REPLICATED_EMBED switch that keeps the GLM input embedding table unsharded. The input embedding currently always uses VocabParallelEmbedding, which shards the table over TP and so does three things on every lookup: - gather the N requested rows: 104 us at chunk 15232, and independent of how wide the table is - zero every row whose token id falls outside this rank's shard: 594 us of MaskedFill - all-reduce the result: ~1.75 ms, since a 119 MiB bf16 activation is 178 MiB/rank of ring traffic at the ~107 GB/s measured on this machine Only the gather is inherent to a lookup; the mask and the all-reduce exist purely because the table is split, and splitting does not make the gather any cheaper. There are four lookups per forward, the main model plus the three MTP draft steps, which share this module because llm_base_proposer deletes the draft model's own table and points it here. Replicating once therefore removes four masks and four all-reduces, about 9.4 ms per chunk-15232 forward. Replicate the table behind the switch and keep the sharded path as the default. The table costs 1210 MiB per rank instead of 302.5 MiB, so +907 MiB at TP4, and arming logs a warning naming that cost. lm_head stays vocab-parallel: it is a GEMM over a weight of the same 154880 x 4096 shape, where splitting the work does pay off. The two sides are separate tensors here because GLM-5.3-Flash sets tie_word_embeddings=False, which is what lets the input side be replicated on its own. title: perf(glm5next): fuse KDA projections with AllGather and ReduceScatter
summary: Add opt-in communication-compute fusion for the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA input and output projections during sequence-parallel prefill. The current decoder gathers token shards before the merged KDA input projection, then reduce-scatters the output projection results. These separate collectives serialize communication and matrix multiplication. Fuse the two pairs independently: - input projection: use npu_all_gather_base_mm and avoid materializing the gathered hidden states when they have no other consumer - output projection: use npu_quant_mm_reduce_scatter with sum reduction and return the local token shard directly Measured on Atlas A3, TP4, 34 KDA layers, medians over 544-2720 calls per point with an identical chunk mix, us per layer per call: output projection fused 82.0 + 0.0603*N unfused 86.0 + 0.0863*N fused is faster at every measured chunk, -21% to -28% input projection fused 283.3 + 0.1823*N unfused 124.3 + 0.2047*N break-even near N = 7100; per layer, chunk 15232 gains 173.9 us while chunk 4352 loses 23.2 us and chunk 1420 loses 157.5 us The input fusion carries a 3.5x larger fixed cost than the output one because MC2 splits its GEMM into world_size sub-GEMMs of shard_rows each: at chunk 1420 that is four M=355 GEMMs in place of one M=1420 GEMM, well below the cube's efficient M. The output fusion keeps the full M and chunks only the reduce_scatter. Hence the asymmetric default minimum token counts, 8192 for input and 1024 for output, each overridable through its own environment variable. title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE position preparation when PCP is enabled
summary: Add support for PCP-MROPE positions in input preparation. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Background: PCP breaks the assumption underlying RopeState.prepare_positions(). Prefill Context Parallel (PCP) splits a long prefill request across multiple ranks. The original RopeState.prepare_positions() assumes a 1:1 mapping between rank-local rows and global requests — i.e., each request's scheduled tokens form one contiguous local segment, and the local row index maps directly to a global offset. For standard 1D RoPE this holds. For M-RoPE models, positions are 3D (Temporal, Height, Width) tensors, and correctness depends on each local token retaining its exact global offset within the multimodal sequence. PCP violates this in two ways. First, a request is fragmented into non-contiguous rank-local pieces, so local row index no longer corresponds to a contiguous global span. Second, positions may be non-monotonic across ranks, so per-request positions cannot be concatenated in order. Under these conditions the original path reconstructs M-RoPE positions from the wrong global offsets. The damage is most severe for image inputs, where spatial H/W coordinates become misaligned with the visual tokens they index. Impacted model scope. The affected class is precisely: models that (a) use M-RoPE and (b) run with prefill_context_parallel_size > 1 under ModelRunner V2. Concretely this includes: Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL (native M-RoPE) Qwen3-VL (the validation target of this PR; vLLM's MRoPE state explicitly covers Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5) GLM-4.6V (documented M-RoPE consumer) MiniCPM-V-4.7

title: [Bug] Engram host registration fails on CANN driver 26.1.1 (aclrtHostRegisterV2 rc=207001)
summary: # [Bug] Engram host registration fails on CANN driver 26.1.1 (aclrtHostRegisterV2 rc=207001) ## Environment - vllm-ascend: v0.30.0 (commit c09d3e20b) - CANN driver: 26.1.1 - Hardware: 16x Ascend 910B (64 GiB HBM/card) - Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w8a8 (Engram model) - Parallel: TP8 x DP2, Engram `cpu_offload=true` ## Symptom Model fails to start. Engram table registration aborts with: ``` RuntimeError: aclrtHostRegisterV2 failed: rc=207001 size=<~91.5 GiB> ``` Each rank cannot bring up the Engram embedding tables, engine init fails. ## Root cause `vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/engram/npu.py` registers the entire Engram host range in a single `aclrtHostRegisterV2` call in both `HostUvaBuffer` and `SharedUvaBuffer`. On CANN 26.1.1 this call rejects ranges above ~5.8 GiB (returns rc=207001). The DeepSeek V4.1 Engram tables are ~91.5 GiB each, so a single registration is far above the new limit. Older CANN drivers did not enforce this per-call cap, so the current code works there but breaks on 26.1.1. ## Fix Register the host range in chunks no larger than 5 GiB, aligned to the kernel `CHUNK_ROWS` granularity so each device pointer in `self.ptrs` maps to exactly one registered chunk. `close()` unregisters each chunk and keeps the remainder for retry on failure. title: [Contribution] 任务 #6：MooncakeConnector handshake 端口动态分配
summary: **在提交新问题之前，请确保您已经在社区中搜索过相关问题，并使用了社区中提供的资源/工具后，仍未找到满意的解决方式。** ### 📚 任务问题描述 ## 任务描述 该任务拆分自 #9079，任务 ID：#6。 当前 `mooncake_connector.py` 中 handshake 端口通过 `handshake_port = side_channel_port + device_index` 固定推导，其中 `device_index = pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank + pcp_rank * prefill_tp_size`。该方式依赖静态端口范围，容易在多实例、多节点复用、残留进程、端口被占用等场景发生冲突。本任务需要将 MooncakeConnector handshake 监听端口改为动态选择可用端口，并通过 metadata/side channel/握手机制确保 P 节点和 D 节点都能拿到正确的对端端口，避免端口冲突且不影响现有 KV cache 传输功能。 ## 验收标准 1. MooncakeConnector 不再依赖固定 `side_channel_port + device_index` 作为唯一 handshake 监听端口。 2. 每个 rank 可动态选择本机可用端口，且同节点多 rank、多实例启动时不冲突。 3. P 节点和 D 节点能通过 handshake metadata 或现有 side channel 正确交换并使用对端实际监听端口。 4. PD 分离普通 Mooncake KV 传输功能不回退，prefill/decode 多 DP/TP 场景可正常建立连接并传输 KV cache。 5. 端口申请、释放、异常清理逻辑可靠，进程异常退出后不会影响下次启动。 6. 补充 UT/e2e 或最小复现用例，覆盖端口被占用、多 rank 动态分配、P/D 端口同步正确性。 ## 对接人 @jyoung6652 ## 认领状态 待认领 ### 建议的替代/修复方案 请根据任务描述提交实现、测试或文档 PR，并在 PR 中关联本 issue 与 #9079；如实现过程中发现任务边界、使用指导或现有行为存在不合理之处，请同步补充说明和最小复现。 欢迎加入社区，感谢您对社区的贡献 🎉!

title: [BugFix][Model] Re-pack Kimi K3.1 Pro KDA conv weight after layerwise reload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The Kimi K3.1 Pro KDA layer (`AscendKimiK3DeltaAttention`) registers `ascend_conv1d_weight`, a derived parameter that converts the checkpoint's FP32 `[3C, 1, W]` conv weight into the activation-dtype `[W, 3C]` layout consumed by `fla_npu`'s `causal_conv1d`. It is absent from checkpoints and is produced only by `_pack_conv_weights()`. Today that pack runs only from the wrapper installed on `conv1d.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading`. A layerwise reload (`sleep(level=2)` -> `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` -> `collective_rpc reload_weights` -> `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`) re-materializes the layer from the kernel tensors saved by `initialize_layerwise_reload()`. The checkpoint has no entry for the derived parameter, and without a layer-level hook the layer is not treated as a deferred attention layer, so nothing re-derives the packed weight after the conv weight is placed. KDA then runs with stale data and produces NaN logits; requests with `logprobs` fail with `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`. This PR gives the layer its own `process_weights_after_loading` hook. This makes `is_deferred_attention_layer()` true, so the layer is finalized after all other layers and the derived weight is rebuilt from the freshly loaded `conv1d.weight`. vLLM v0.33.0 and the vLLM main commit currently tested by this repo call the hook with `model_config.dtype` from `_finalize_attention_layer()`; newer vLLM main calls it no-arg from `finalize_model_weights()`. title: [RFC]: Provision shared draft embeddings on the target's last PP stage
summary: ## Motivation With pipeline parallelism (PP), the target normally loads its input embedding on the first stage, while the draft runs on the last stage. A draft that reuses the target embedding needs that weight to be available locally before draft initialization attempts to share it. Ascend DSpark currently handles this in two places. `patch_dspark.py` skips the upstream sharing check when the target embedding is missing and the draft exposes `post_process()`. Later, `align_draft_weights()` may reopen the target checkpoint and load an unrotated embedding into the draft. The first step assumes the draft will supply the missing embedding. The second can reload it even when a usable target embedding is already present. [Sharing override](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/2b938127ad3a469d2c5dfa9100f2171f7c26584e/vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_dspark.py#L54-L94) · [Draft reload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/2b938127ad3a469d2c5dfa9100f2171f7c26584e/vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dspark.py#L41-L73) ## Proposed Change Make the target responsible for providing shared embedding weights on the last PP stage. Start with Ascend Kimi K3 and DSpark drafts that may reuse the target embedding. During target construction, create a `VocabParallelEmbedding` on the last stage when the existing layer is `PPMissingLayer` and the configured draft may need to share it. Use the target's normal checkpoint loader to load the TP vocab shard. The upstream draft loader can then share the loaded module directly. title: [RFC]: MoE expert offloading on Ascend
summary: > Draft for review, 2026-11-10. Intended repository: `vllm-project/vllm-ascend`. ## Motivation Large MoE checkpoints can exceed a single NPU's memory capacity even though each token uses only a subset of routed experts. Keeping every layer's complete expert inventory on the device makes expert weights a capacity constraint alongside KV cache and activations. We propose an opt-in expert offload path that keeps the expert inventory in host memory and loads router-selected experts into device slots for native MoE computation. The initial implementation preserves routing decisions, routing weights, and checkpoint expert weights. It targets single-device inference on Ascend 950PR/950DT with Model Runner V2 (MRV2), including decode ACL Graph replay. [PR #18604](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18604) provides the initial implementation under review. This RFC describes the expert offload foundation and leaves room for incremental optimizations. ## Proposed Change ### Initial scope and configuration The initial implementation offloads target routed-expert weights and their associated quantization tensors. Attention, shared experts, and draft experts retain their native execution paths. title: [Platform][Doc] Add sunset deprecation warnings and documentation for dynamic chunk CPP and GQA DCP (v0.32)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR introduces sunset deprecation warnings and documentation updates for two features that are entering the sunset process in v0.32.0: 1. **Dynamic chunk size Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP)**: - Deprecation rationale: Dense models with long sequences previously leveraged quadratic dynamic chunk profiling to reduce pipeline bubbles. With the shift towards sparse (MoE/SFA) and linear attention models, this feature provides negligible benefits while incurring high scheduling and profiling maintenance costs. Tracked in RFC [#21304](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21304). - Emits a runtime deprecation warning when `profiling_chunk_config.enabled` is detected during engine config validation and scheduler initialization. 2. **Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) for GQA models**: - Deprecation rationale: GQA models naturally shard KV heads across TP ranks and rarely require multi-node KV sequence-sharding. In speculative decoding setups with target DCP, GQA draft models maintain native TP head sharding without needing DCP. Maintaining specialized GQA DCP metadata, All-to-All communication, and LSE combine paths imposes disproportionate maintenance overhead. Tracked in RFC [#21305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/21305). - Emits a runtime deprecation warning when `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` is configured for GQA models. (Note: DCP for MLA and SFA models remains fully supported). 3. **Documentation & Release Notes**: - Added sunset announcements in `docs/source/user_guide/release_notes.md` under

title: [BugFix] Reuse upstream MLA context packing and workspace sizing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MLA chunked prefill currently divides workspace equally among requests with cached context. When the per-request share is smaller than one cache block, rounding it down produces a zero-sized chunk. Requiring workspace to scale with `max_num_reqs * block_size` avoids that case by increasing memory use. Reuse upstream `plan_mla_context_chunks` to pack contexts into bounded workspace chunks instead. Reuse `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.determine_chunked_prefill_workspace_size` for sizing. Keep per-request offsets for DCP cache reorganization, account for DCP padding, and map global PCP plans to local fragments. For example, eight history requests can share a 256-token workspace with 128-token blocks by processing multiple chunks, even though an equal share would be only 32 tokens. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. MLA workspace no longer needs a `max_num_reqs * block_size` lower bound. It follows upstream sizing and only needs to fit one aligned chunk. ### How was this patch tested? - `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python3 -m pytest tests/ut/attention/test_mla_pcp_dcp.py -q`: **61 passed**. Regression coverage includes many requests, mixed context lengths, PCP mapping, and DCP rank-local offsets. - A3, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, TP=1, eager, BF16: **full GSM8K test set (1,319 questions)**. Both baseline `b87b0d881` and target `fbc066c7c` scored **509/1,319 (38.59%)**; every generated token sequence matched. - Fixed 5-shot training examples (seed 1234), greedy decoding, model seed 0, max output 512 tokens. - `max_model_len=409

title: [BugFix] Bound MLA prefill npu_attention_update inputs with 16-way staged merging
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In `vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py` (`_compute_prefill_context`), MLA chunked prefill accumulated query prefix `(output, LSE)` pairs alongside all historical chunks into one `torch_npu.npu_attention_update` call. When prefill spans 16 or more historical chunks (`>= 17` total pairs), the call exceeds the 16-input limit of native CANN `npu_attention_update` and fails with error `161002`. This PR bounds every `npu_attention_update` call in `_compute_prefill_context` to at most 16 pairs using staged merging. Prefill without historical context directly returns the original query attention result, while 2 to 15 pairs retain the direct native update path. When 16 pairs accumulate, `merge_prefill_chunks` in `vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py` merges them into one accumulated FP32 pair via fused Triton LSE preparation and native update. Exact flush boundaries (16, 31, 46, ... total pairs) return the accumulated output directly; residual groups merge once at loop completion. In `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/attention_update.py`, intermediate LSEs are normalized with explicit pointer arguments, maintaining relative LSE against a separate row anchor to prevent precision loss at large common offsets (+1000) without host synchronization. For ordinary finite model inputs, actual query slicing and causal self-key visibility ensure the current causal prefix starts with finite LSE. Kernel runtime `ROWS` with `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=['ROWS'])` allows compiled kernel reuse across batch sizes, while `COUNT` and `HAS_ANCHOR` remain bounded specializations.

title: [BugFix][Quantization] Handle empty W4A8 expert batches
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? An expert-parallel rank can legitimately receive zero routed tokens. W4A8's unfused GMM1/GMM2 hooks currently pass the resulting empty per-token scale to native grouped matmul. On Ascend 950, this raises `perTokenScale must not be null` (161002) instead of returning an empty result. Return an empty BF16 tensor with the projection's output width before quantization/GMM. Resolve widths through the existing weight accessor, covering stacked and expert-list storage. The nonempty computation is unchanged; the guard reads tensor shape metadata without device synchronization. This is independent of serving configuration, DCP, and speculative decoding. A two-rank PyTorch/HCCL reproduction, with every token routed to rank 0, gives a successful `[128,256]` input on rank 0 and the same native error for `[0,256]` on rank 1. No vLLM engine or launch configuration is involved. The repository regression also reproduces the failure directly on main `484cd036c923aba3d51d24e45ee89817a020d9da`, without the GQA/DCP adaptation. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [BugFix] Integrate KDA state-copy with shared Triton warmup
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Integrate prepared KDA state-copy launchers with the current Ascend Triton JIT warmup framework. Both model runners register metadata-only compile keys after cache binding, and the worker invokes shared `kernel_warmup` before model dummy runs and ACL graph capture. `StateCopyJitKernel` derives from `AscendTritonJitKernel` and uses `TritonWarmupTensor` inputs: four fused gather/scatter and INT32/INT64 keys per worker layout, or one byte-copy fallback key. Registry compilation caches the completed executor and its constexpr ABI constants. Serving uses that executor without JIT or signature inspection after warmup. The existing `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` setting controls precompilation; disabling it permits first-use compilation through the framework cache. Cache initialization allocates no warmup tensors and launches no copies. This retains compatibility with compiled launchers that retain constexpr argument slots. State-copy compilation runs serially because ABI inspection requires completed compiled objects. Worker layouts share kernel owners while layer bindings remain distinct. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Fixes prepared Kimi K3 state-copy launcher compatibility and routes compilation through shared JIT warmup. No new flags or environment variables. ### How was this patch tested? - **Local focused CPU regression: 43 passed.** Uses the real paired vLLM registry/helper and Ascend wrapper, with device JIT/context and platform/rank discovery stubbed. title: [BugFix] Preserve K3 token shards after fused O-projection
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Kimi K3 attention residuals apply sequence-parallel ReduceScatter twice when the fused O-projection already returns a token shard. Skip the decoder ReduceScatter in that case, retaining it for the unfused path. This also applies without DCP or speculative decoding. The v0.30.0 release branch retained this guard from #17270. The newer-version path introduced in #17870 omitted it; #18229 subsequently removed the older path. This restores the original token-sharding contract. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Fixes attention-residual shape errors with fused O-projection on Ascend A5. title: [BugFix][Worker][v0.30.0] Preserve DSA-CP Top-K indices across PP
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix GLM-5.2 IndexShare across pipeline stages when DSA-CP is enabled. title: [Performance] Overlap V4.1 DSA-CP gathers
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it DeepSeek V4.1 DSA-CP with sequence-parallel MoE previously used an activation all-gather before attention, an attention-output all-to-all, and an output reduce-scatter. This PR keeps the query input sequence-sharded and asynchronously gathers hidden states only for replicated KV/cache work. For batches containing prefill requests on either A3 or A5, it asynchronously all-gathers the full O-projection weights, projects the local tokens with an ordinary matmul, and skips the attention-output all-to-all and model-level reduce-scatter. For pure decode batches, it exchanges tokens with all-to-all, applies the local O projection, and reduce-scatters the result. Empty-query ranks still participate in the required collectives. The change also fixes token-origin handling for sparse-index selection and applies KV RoPE to the actual token count rather than rank padding. The `enable_dsa_v41_cp_comm_optimization` and `enable_dsa_v41_cp_full_o_proj` settings allow independent validation of the V4.1 paths. The test-only `skip_engram_for_testing` setting defaults to `false`; it permits validation with the available W8A8 checkpoint, which omits Engram weights. ## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? The OpenAI API is unchanged. The new V4.1 configuration settings above control the communication path; `skip_engram_for_testing` must be explicitly enabled and changes model semantics. ## How was this patch tested? - Related unit tests: 160 passed. Repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. - A3 single-host validation with Engram ex

title: [BugFix] Record prefix cache stats in BalanceScheduler
summary: This is an earlier PR fix. #15745 Co-authored-by @mashuiping ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #15744 Fixes #20211 `BalanceScheduler` forks `Scheduler.schedule()`, but it only records local prefix-cache statistics on the mamba + connector fast path. For full-attention models (Qwen3, DeepSeek, GLM, …) the branch never runs, so `vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total` and `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` stay at zero even with prefix caching enabled, and the reported prefix-cache hit rate is meaningless. title: [Performance][Ops] Add SwiGLU graph fusion pass
summary: ## Why Some model paths write the SwiGLU activation with raw aten ops instead of going through `AscendSiluAndMul` / `npu_swiglu`. For example `DeepseekV4VisionMLP.forward`: ```python gate, up = self.w1(x).chunk(2, dim=-1) return self.w2(F.silu(gate) * up) ``` This keeps the `chunk -> silu -> mul` sequence as separate graph ops, with intermediate tensor round-trips that a single fused `npu_swiglu` call avoids. ## What Add a new FX graph fusion pass (`vllm_ascend/compilation/passes/swiglu_fusion_pass.py`) that matches the bare `chunk(2, dim=-1) -> F.silu(gate) * up` pattern and rewrites it into a single `torch_npu.npu_swiglu(x)` call, mirroring the existing `muls_add` / `norm_quant` / `qknorm_rope` / `mm_reduce_scatter` passes. - New `SwigluFusionPattern(BasePattern)` + `SwigluFusionPass(VllmInductorPass)`. - Gated by a new `fuse_swiglu` config (`ascend_config.py`, default `True`) and a new `GRAPH_SWIGLU_FUSION` hardware capability (`hardware_profile.py`, enabled for A2/A3 via `_STANDARD_CAPABILITIES`). - Wired into `GraphFusionPassManager.configure`. - New test `tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/compile/test_swiglu_fusion.py` covering operator presence/absence before/after the pass plus numerical equivalence. ## Design notes - The pattern is written with the high-level `F.silu` op. The pattern matcher traces the pattern function with the same decomposition table as the target graph, so `F.silu` decomposes identically on both sides and the structures line up across dtypes. title: [BugFix] Restore has_sync_kv_loads bookkeeping in the copied schedulers
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Restores the `has_sync_kv_loads` bookkeeping that upstream vLLM's `Scheduler.schedule()` performs, in the two vLLM-Ascend copies of that method that had dropped it: - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py` (`BalanceScheduler`) - `vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py` (`DyntraLBScheduler`) Without the flag, `SchedulerOutput.has_sync_kv_loads` keeps its default `False` value. The worker derives `start_after_forward = not scheduler_output.has_sync_kv_loads` from it, so `start_load_kv()` was deferred until **after** the forward pass even when the current forward needs KV cache that an external connector loads synchronously (`load_kv_async=False`). With layerwise external KV loading the per-layer `wait_for_layer_load()` then returns early, the model reads KV cache that was never restored, and the output is corrupted. Both copies now mirror upstream vLLM exactly: - initialize `has_sync_kv_loads = False` per scheduling step; - set it to `True` when a request is admitted with `num_external_computed_tokens > 0` on the synchronous path (upstream's comment `load_kv_async is False here` applies to the same branch); - propagate it into `SchedulerOutput`. `DyntraLBScheduler` keeps the file's existing `_scheduler_output_supports(...)` guard, because it also supports vLLM releases whose `SchedulerOutput` has no such field (`v0.26.0`). `BalanceScheduler` targets the pinned vLLM release tag (`v0.32.0`), which always carries the field, so it passes it directly — the same way `vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py` and `vllm_ascend/c

title: [Performance] Add experimental V2 MTP greedy verification
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds an opt-in Model Runner V2 MTP greedy verification path that uses blockwise target argmax and per-request greedy verification to choose accepted, replacement, and bonus tokens. It is gated by `VLLM_ASCEND_EXPERIMENT_GREEDY_VERIFY=1` (default off). Non-MTP, non-greedy, watermark, synthetic, block, FLy, entropy verification, and narrower draft-vocabulary cases fall back to the existing implementation. The patch wraps the upstream rejection sampler and should eventually be replaced by a backend-dispatched implementation if the experiment proves worthwhile. This is a draft: correctness and performance on NPU, compatibility with the exact upstream vLLM revision, and edge cases must be verified before review for merge. It is an experiment on target-side greedy verification; it does not establish that the MTP-to-next-verify device idle gap is reduced. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. It adds a default-off experimental environment variable. The release-note fragment is `release_notes/fragments/21524.yaml`. ### How was this patch tested? - Passed Python syntax compilation for the changed implementation and test files and `git diff --cached --check` on the community branch. - Added mocked unit tests for dispatch/fallback/idempotency and NPU differential tests for variable-length requests, rejection, bonus, placeholders, ties, NaN/Inf and vocabulary block boundaries. title: [Performance] Overlap PCP prefill communication and reduce KDA output collectives
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? PCP prefill needs to exchange main-KV and KPool inputs across ranks. Waiting for these AllGathers before running independent query projections leaves communication on the critical path. KDA also reduces the full output on every PCP rank before selecting only that rank's token rows. This PR reduces those exposed waits and redundant output communication: - **Main-KV overlap:** launch the PCP AllGather before MLA query projections and wait when the gathered values are needed for the cache write. Use one `exec_kv` path for immediate and deferred completion, with DCP slot selection in one entry point. Offload accepts the same signature while completing its existing cache writes and CPU commits synchronously. Keep the send buffers alive until communication completes. - **KPool overlap and gather ordering:** start the hidden-state AllGather before MLA/indexer query computation and restore token order at the KPool consumer. Keep contiguous send buffers alive until the consumer waits for completion. In native SFA preprocessing, enqueue main-KV and KPool gathers before output-projection weight/scale gathers, whose results are consumed later. - **KDA ReduceScatter:** pack output rows by PCP ownership and replace AllReduce followed by local row selection with ReduceScatter, so each rank receives its own reduced rows. Preserve the existing SP and other fallback paths. The changes preserve token ordering, padding, replicated decode prefixes, cache-write semantics, and graph-owned output buffers. title: [Feature][Sample] Add Triton apply_top_k_top_p fused op for sampling
summary: ## What A Triton implementation of top-k/top-p filtering for the sampler, opt-in via `--additional-config '{"enable_triton_apply_topk_topp": true}'` (default `false`). Two entry points: - `apply_top_k_top_p` — masked logits, bit-exact with `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` (`torch.equal` on fp32/bf16/fp16) - `fused_topk_topp_softmax` — same filtering with the final softmax folded into the kernel, returns fp32 probs directly; this is the branch the sampler uses when logprobs are not requested Both take the per-request `[B]` k/p tensors from `_get_topk_topp_constraints()` as-is. The CANN op forces a `.item()` on that tensor (host sync on every decode step); this op doesn't. ## How it works The host does the sort once (`torch.sort`, ascending, stable) and the kernel only works on the sorted row. Because the input is ascending, both the top-k mask (`s >= topk_value`) and the top-p mask (`cumsum > 1 - p`) are suffix-monotone, so the kept set collapses to a single scalar boundary `m = max(m_p, m_k)` per row. The kernel then only scatters the surviving suffix (~k elements) into a pre-filled output — the non-surviving positions are one contiguous block write instead of V random stores. I used a scalar boundary rather than a cumsum-derived boolean vector as the scatter mask on purpose: triton-ascend 3.2.2 miscompiles that pattern (the store collapses to a few elements). The `v >= m` comparison mask sidesteps it. ![kernel flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/kernel_flow.png) Two kernel paths: rows up to the single-pass block size load the r

title: [Feature]: MXFP8 KV cache: per-query indexed (top-k) attention reads from the PA_NZ packet layout
summary: Follow-up to #21285 (triaged as feature request). Use case: sparse attention (LSA/QSA) reads on Qwen3.8-27B full-attention layers (16 of 64) on 950DT, CANN 9.2.1, vllm-ascend v0.30.0-a5, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. What we'd want the feature request to capture, per @kunpengW-code's questions: **Selection granularity: block-level.** - QSA indexer: keys are 4-token blocks (mean-pooled); each query selects the top 512 closed blocks (~2048 keys) plus its own open block. - LSA indexer: keys are clustered into buckets (bucket_cap ~16 keys); each query picks top-p buckets and expands them to a top-k key list (~1024-2048 keys), plus a window (512) and sink (64). - The per-query keep set is therefore a sorted list of absolute key positions (or block lists), disjoint per query, changing every step. **Indices into the kernel, not gathered tensors.** Yes - that would sidestep the whole problem. The selection produces per-query block/key indices per layer per step; feeding them to the attention kernel as per-query block lists (paged-attention `block_table` semantics, or a gather-indices input) is exactly the shape we want. Today we cannot express that on the mxfp8 cache: the PA_NZ packet buffer ([K | K_scale | V | V_scale] per 512-token block, NZ strided views, E8M0 scales in separate views) has no supported indexed-read or scatter-indices API, so we fall back to a per-layer bf16 mirror pool plus a compact-cache rebuild around `atb::_npu_paged_attention_v2`. **Frequency.** Every forward step, every full-attention layer (16/64): per-token at decode, per-chunk at prefill. **Perf budget.** K

title: [Performance][MRV2] Optimize _penalties_kernel vocab grid to cut scalar overhead
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `apply_penalties` launches `_penalties_kernel` on a 2-D grid `(num_tokens, vocab_grid_size)`, where the second axis was sized as: ```python vocab_grid_size = min(num_vocab_blocks, 65535 // num_tokens) ``` With Qwen3's vocabulary (151936) and `BLOCK_SIZE = 4096` there are 38 vocab blocks, and `65535 // num_tokens >= 38` for every `num_tokens <= 1724`. The expression therefore evaluates to **38 at every batch size we actually serve**, i.e. one program per vocab block, and the grid-stride loop inside the kernel never iterates. Each program pays the per-program cost once for a single block of work. That cost is not bandwidth. The kernel is **scalar-bound on A2**: profiling `glm-5.3-flash-w8a8` with `AiCMetrics.PipeUtilization`, a representative launch at logits `[8, 154880]` spends 83 % of its vector-core time in the scalar pipe and 11 % in the vector pipe. Running a fixed shape in fp32 instead of bf16 moves 1.5× the bytes and costs **+0.15 %** time, which rules out bandwidth. The scalar unit also dispatches to every other pipe, so per-program scalar work serialises everything behind it. This PR replaces the 2-D grid with a 1-D grid of `get_vectorcore_num()` programs, each owning a contiguous range of the flattened `(token, vocab_tile)` work space. The number of programs no longer depends on the batch size or the vocabulary, and no helper is needed to choose it. Here is the same launch before and after. `[8, 154880]` means `num_vocab_blocks = 38`, so the old rule launched 304 programs and the new one launches 48: | kernel_details metric |

title: [BugFix] Defer accepted-token sync for async Mamba decode
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Async speculative decode with hybrid/Mamba models currently waits for the previous step's accepted-token D2H snapshot early in `_prepare_inputs`. Profiling a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next pure-decode workload showed that this host synchronization serializes next-step input preparation with the previous step's sampling/post-processing and contributes to a 5–7 ms device idle gap between decode iterations. This change: - keeps the accepted-token counts used by the next forward in a dedicated NPU buffer; - computes the current request-order counts on device from `valid_sampled_token_count_gpu`; - defers the previous step's D2H event synchronization until Mamba align preprocessing actually needs the CPU snapshot; - preserves the existing CPU snapshot/remapping semantics and keeps the non-async/non-align paths unchanged. The separate buffer is required because the original buffer is also the destination of the previous step's asynchronous D2H snapshot. Reusing it for the next forward would introduce a read/write race. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Users running async speculative decode with `mamba_cache_mode=align` should avoid the unnecessary early synchronization between decode iterations. Release-note fragment `release_notes/fragments/21520.yaml` is included. ### How was this patch tested? title: [Feature][MRV2] Support LM head TP with probabilistic draft sampling
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Enable LM head TP together with `draft_sample_method="probabilistic"` in Model Runner V2. title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Keep Mooncake buffer registration across level-1 sleep
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #21165. `NPUWorker.sleep()` unconditionally unregisters the Mooncake transfer-engine buffers, while `wake_up()` only re-registers them when the wake covers the KV cache: ```python # sleep() global_te.unregister_buffer() # always allocator.sleep(offload_tags=("weights",) if level == 1 else tuple()) # wake_up() allocator.wake_up(tags=tags) if tags is None or "kv_cache" in tags: global_te.reregister_buffer() ``` A level-1 sleep only offloads the weights pool, so the KV cache stays resident and its registrations are still valid. Unregistering them anyway makes the legal sequence `sleep(level=1)` → `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` unrecoverable: the weights-only wake skips `reregister_buffer()`, and nothing else re-registers until the next engine startup. From then on every Mooncake P2P transfer involving that worker fails (Ascend Direct `unregister_memory` also disconnects peers). This PR only unregisters for `level >= 2`, where the KV cache is actually offloaded/unmapped, and keeps the existing `kv_cache`-wake re-registration path. Partial-wake semantics for level 2 are unchanged: a weights-only wake keeps the buffers unregistered, and the subsequent `kv_cache` wake restores them exactly once. ## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change? No API change. RL-style sleep/wake workloads that use `sleep(level=1)` followed by a weights-only `wake_up()` keep their Mooncake KV-cache registration instead of silently losing it. ## How was this patch tested? - Extended `tests/ut/worker/test_sleep_parameter_retention.py`: - level-1 sleep + weigh

Two independent blockers: 1. **Missing target-side aux interface.** For `method="dflash"` the MRV2 runner enables `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs` and expects the target to implement the shared Eagle3-style auxiliary hidden-state interface. Support using upstream vLLM's `MooncakeStoreConnector` on Ascend through an optional worker compatibility patch for legacy Fabric initialization and NPU transfer-thread device binding. **Depends on [vllm-project/vllm#66271](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66271).** That companion change supplies extensible Store configuration, the `_setup_store` hook, logical KV layouts, and device-generic events. Those portable changes stay in vLLM; this PR contains the Ascend-specific lifecycle adaptation. The companion must be available before enabling this integration. For affected Fabric deployments before HDK 26.1, constructing the Store transport during worker setup creates device resources before cache registration and graph capture. The patch defers transport setup until serving, leaves explicit KV-buffer registration to Fabric, and returns a cold cache miss before initialization. This keeps the first lookup RPC from creating the transport. The implementation: - Preserves the upstream Store configuration defaults and validates that Fabric memory uses `protocol="ascend"`. - Serializes first-time Store initialization, binds each calling thread to the owning NPU, and handles setup failure and idempotent close. - Binds send/receive threads before their first request, including before event synchronization or transport I/O. - Installs replacements only on explicit opt-in during worker patch loading. title: [BugFix][MoE] Guard fused MC2 capacity and MegaMoe dispatch modes
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add capacity checks around the fused MC2 `dispatch_ffn_combine` path and validate CANN MegaMoe dispatch quantization modes against the selected hardware profile. For the operator path, a configured output capacity smaller than the received expert-token load can drop work. The patch increases the configured capacity using a prefill-load heuristic, checks the reported received-token count after execution when the conservative bound cannot exclude saturation, and clones the routing indices before passing them to the operator. Current implementation at `fe603d6968417951b4770688f9a1af0cbafe4c5a`: - Cache `max_num_batched_tokens // tensor_parallel_size` from the construction-time vLLM configuration, or zero when no configuration context exists. - Compute the operator capacity as `max(mega_moe_max_tokens, max(1, prefill_tokens_per_rank * experts_per_token * 8))`. The factor eight is a workload-derived heuristic, not a proven upper bound for all routing distributions. - Reuse `_init_mega_moe_symm_buffer`: prefill/PD-mixed nodes use this capacity clamped to the existing absolute receive bound; the decode-only sizing path is unchanged. The peer buffer and operator capacity therefore need not be numerically equal. - Skip the received-token synchronization when `num_tokens * topk * ep_world_size < capacity`; otherwise read the reported count and raise when it is **greater than or equal to** capacity. Equality is treated conservatively by this implementation; it is not itself proof that tokens were discarded. - Clone `topk_ids` before the fused op

title: [Ops][BugFix] Zero-init fused MC2 combine output to avoid uninitialized HBM
summary: ### What `FusedMC2CommImpl.fused_experts` allocates the `dispatch_ffn_combine` output with `torch.empty_like(...)` (`vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py`, the `enable_fused_mc2 == 1` branch). The fused op does **not** necessarily write every row of `out`: when expert routing leaves a local expert with zero tokens the per-expert GMM is skipped, and rows beyond the routed / under-filled count are never touched. Those rows are then consumed downstream (combine reduction → `compute_logits`) as **uninitialized HBM**, surfacing as NaN / garbage / malformed-`<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` first-step logits. This switches the allocation to `torch.zeros_like(...)` so any row the kernel does not write is a deterministic zero. Zero is also the mathematically correct identity for the combine (a token with no expert contribution sums to 0), so this is a correctness fix, not merely a guard. ### Why This is one of the source-identified contributors to #9170 ("DeepSeek-V4 W8A8 Concurrency Failure: Output Corruption and Malformed begin_of_sentence"). The corruption is intermittent because the device allocator sometimes hands back already-zeroed pages — consistent with the issue's "concurrency-dependent" framing. The trigger (a local expert receiving zero tokens, or a per-rank token count below the AIC core count) is a function of batch size / routing distribution, **not** of speculative decoding, so it is reachable in plain high-concurrency decode/prefill. ### Cost A single memset of the `[num_tokens, hidden]` output buffer per fused-MC2 call — negligible relative to the grouped matmul + a

title: [Feature][MoE] Fuse the shared expert into the A5 MegaMoe operator for W4A4 MXFP4 (enable_fused_mc2=3)
summary: ## What Fuse the shared expert into the A5 CANN MegaMoe operator (`enable_fused_mc2=3`), extending #17654 with W4A4 MXFP4 support and fixing activation-enum handling. ## Why With `enable_fused_mc2=2`, the shared expert runs as a separate GMM1+activation+GMM2 forward alongside the MegaMoe routed path. `enable_fused_mc2=3` folds the shared expert into the MegaMoe kernel so its weights travel with the routed weights and the extra kernels disappear. #17654 implemented this for W8A8 MXFP checkpoints only; W4A4 MXFP4 models (e.g. GLM-5.3-W4A4C8-MXFP4) silently fell back to the separate shared-expert forward. Three additional gaps found while enabling it for W4A4: 1. The routed-activation guard compared the `MoEActivation` enum via `str(...)`, which renders as `MoEActivation.SILU` and never matches `"silu"`, so fusion was disabled even for standard SiLU models. Because the operator applies a single global activation to the shared experts, the guard was then generalized to a "same activation function" check: equal activation type plus equal activation params (see How). 2. Packed-FP4 shared weights need the same layout rebuild as the routed experts: `w1` cast to `FRACTAL_NZ`, `w2` rebuilt as `FRACTAL_NZ_C0_32` on an fp8 carrier from the packed fp4 buffer, and the byte-stored E8M0 scales viewed as `float8_e8m0fnu`. 3. An unbounded shared `SiluAndMul` was unconditionally accepted even when the routed swiglu carries a `swiglu_limit` clamp, which would silently change shared-expert numerics under fusion. ## How - `shared_experts.py`: accept `QuantType.W4A4MXFP` in the fusion gate; in th
