title: [Feature][SpecDecode] Support sliding-window KV cache for draft models on MRV2 (draft_kv_window)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR adds `additional_config["draft_kv_window"]` for Model Runner V2 target-dependent speculative decoding. It bounds supported EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP draft attention to the most recent `W` tokens instead of retaining draft KV for `max_model_len`. The default is `None`, preserving the existing behavior. Target-model verification continues to use the full target KV cache. The draft window has two required halves: - **Storage:** draft `FullAttentionSpec` becomes upstream `SlidingWindowSpec`; out-of-window blocks are released, and `gather_block_tables()` masks entries below the visible range. Draft KV per request changes from O(`max_model_len`) to O(`W`). - **Compute:** draft FIA receives the matching compile-time sliding-window band, so it never reads nulled out-of-window entries. `extra_retained_tokens=num_speculative_tokens` keeps the speculative re-prefill step alive. Other implementation details: - Forward upstream `BlockTables.sliding_window_reach` through `AscendBlockTables`, including compatibility with lanes that do not declare the argument. - Allow compatible target full-attention and draft sliding-window groups to share dense KV backing without the previous per-layer budget scaling failure. - Validate the window and speculative method at startup. Unsupported 310P, DCP, specialized MTP variants, MLA drafts, and Kimi K3/DSpark mixed grouping fail explicitly. - Validate Qwen3-8B EAGLE3 short-prompt no-op behavior, long-prompt eviction, and concurrent block reuse; the test-only files are not retained in the final PR diff. ### CANN 9.

title: [RFC]: Migrate Engram Host UVA to MemFabric GVA across A2/A3/A5
summary: ## Motivation This RFC proposes migrating **Engram host offload** from Host UVA to MemFabric GVA as the default backend across A2, A3, and A5. MemFabric hybrid packages are already in the default vLLM-Ascend requirements; the current `main` pin is 1.2.0, while 1.3.0 is now available on all Ascend platform. This proposal is therefore an architecture and backend-unification effort, and it does not assume a performance improvement. There are two relevant implementation references with different data planes: - [#19528](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19528) uses MemFabric BM GVA for A3 owner-backed tables and reports cross-server validation on A3. - [#20171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20171) adds A5 single-node row-sharded GVA using a SHARED pool and `entry_gather`, with fixed HBM staging for graph replay. It is an implementation reference for A5, not evidence of A5 cross-node support. title: [Performance]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 910B4: async scheduling improves decode but can worsen short-burst TTFT
summary: ## Proposal to improve performance We run **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W8A8 on four Ascend 910B4 NPUs, with TP4, expert parallelism and no speculative decoding**. Native async scheduling made decode much faster, but TTFT became slower and less consistent in some four-request cold-KV bursts. We tried a small change to EngineCore's prefill admission timing. Later runs looked better, although the first patched runs were still slow. The measurements and patch are below. Is there a recommended Model Runner V2 / async configuration for this A2 + Qwen4Exp + PLE CPU-offload setup at 1–4 concurrent requests? We would also like to discuss whether EngineCore should sometimes consume the pending batch result before scheduling more prefill work. We suspect the current ordering can split a burst into separate prefill batches, but have not traced that sequence yet. If a core change is needed, Ascend testing of the existing upstream proposals would help us avoid maintaining a separate patch. These results come from Ascend. We have not checked whether the same behavior occurs on other backends. ## Report of performance regression ### Controlled configurations The three configurations use the same four devices, checkpoint, tokenizer, image and numerical operators. title: [BugFix][v0.32.0rc] Use configured block size for DeepSeek V4.1 SWA cache
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Cherry-pick of #21243 to the `releases/v0.32.0rc` branch. `AscendDeepseekV41SWACache` currently remaps `cache_config.block_size` through `DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES`: ```python block_size = DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[cache_config.block_size][0][1] ``` The V4.1 SWA cache should use the configured block size directly instead of going through the DeepSeek V4 block-size table. This PR removes the table lookup: ```python block_size = cache_config.block_size ``` For the previously supported 32/64/128 values, behavior is unchanged because the table mapped them to themselves. The change lets the V4.1 cache honor the configured block size and avoids a bare `KeyError` for values outside the table. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [Bug]: `_swiglu_quant_kernel` tail block slices past the end of `out` when `HALF_COLS % COL_BLOCK_SIZE != 0`
summary: ## Where `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/activation/swiglu_quant.py`, the quant loop in `_swiglu_quant_kernel`: ```python for col_blk_idx in range(0, HALF_COLS, COL_BLOCK_SIZE): tmp_out = extract_slice(out, offsets=(col_blk_idx,), sizes=(COL_BLOCK_SIZE,), strides=(1,)) ... mask = (col_blk_idx + tl.arange(0, COL_BLOCK_SIZE)) < HALF_COLS tl.store(out_ptr + o_offsets, tmp_out.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask) ``` ## Problem The loop steps by `COL_BLOCK_SIZE` over `HALF_COLS`, but `extract_slice` always takes a fixed `COL_BLOCK_SIZE` elements. The `mask` is applied only to `tl.store`, so the tail iteration still slices and computes a full block. When `HALF_COLS` is not a multiple of `COL_BLOCK_SIZE`, the last iteration slices past the end of `out`. The same happens whenever `HALF_COLS < COL_BLOCK_SIZE`. `swiglu_quant` calls the kernel with `HALF_COLS = h // 2` and a hard-coded `COL_BLOCK_SIZE = 1536`, so this is the common case rather than an edge case: | hidden size `h` | `HALF_COLS` | `HALF_COLS % 1536` | affected | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 4096 | 2048 | 512 | yes | | 14336 | 7168 | 1024 | yes | | 2048 | 1024 | 1024 | yes | | 6144 | 3072 | 0 | no | For `h = 4096` the second iteration requests elements `[1536, 3072)` of a 2048-element value. This is visible in the generated TTIR as a fixed-size slice at a dynamic offset: ```mlir %tmp_out = tensor.extract_slice %out[%off] [1536] [1] : tensor<2048xf32> to tensor<1536xf32> ``` On Ascend910B3 the lowered code reads real memory for those lanes: the slice taken from the second half of the row runs past the end of its UB allocat

title: [Refactor][AscendStore] Run AscendStore KV cache services in an independent multiprocess server
summary: Implements the direction of #14143: move the KV transfer hot path (key building, buffer scheduling, I/O submission) out of the engine process so it no longer contends for the forward path's GIL. ### What this PR does / why we need it? AscendStore's Scheduler/Worker services currently run inside the vLLM engine process as daemon threads coordinated by queues and events. This PR adds an opt-in multiprocess mode where they run in a dedicated KV cache server process, decoupling the cache service lifecycle from engine lifetime and letting multiple engine instances attach to one external pool service. - `mp/rpc`: ZMQ transport layer — framing, routing, deadlines, per-lane execution, server health and shutdown. Owns transport-level errors only; carries no KVCache semantics. - `mp/service`: service lifecycle — sessions, heartbeat-driven leases, expiry cleanup, forced-shutdown reporting. - `mp/kv_cache`: business layer — wire protocol, client, server and manager (Lookup / Store / Retrieve orchestration and degradation policy compatible with in-process AscendStore), registration, scheduler view; pool scheduler/worker reuse the in-process `KVPoolScheduler` / `KVPoolWorker` semantics via inheritance; Mooncake / Memcache / YuanRong backend adapters own their own resource lifecycle; NPU IPC path for cross-process buffer sharing. - `AscendStoreMPConnector`: translates vLLM v1 scheduler/worker callbacks into MP client operations. Connector registration routes `AscendStoreConnector` / `MooncakeConnectorStoreV1` to the MP class when `VLLM_ASCEND_STORE_MULTIPROCESS=1`; default `0` keeps in-pr

title: [BugFix] Preserve mixed-precision Kimi MLA output gates
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fix a mixed-precision weight-loading regression exposed by the vLLM 0.33 Kimi MLA gate fusion. For quantized Q/KV with a FLOAT gate, the fused layer therefore allocates INT8 storage for all three shards. The real upstream weight loader silently casts BF16 gate weights into INT8, while the gate's quantization scale/offset shards have no checkpoint values. The shape fix in [d0e83d582](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/d0e83d582fcce76bb578e0dbf48866e569a0f163), merged with #20627, corrected output splitting but did not cover this allocation/loading mismatch. - Keep differently quantized MLA output gates separate from the replicated Q/KV projection. - Load standalone verifier and MTP gate parameters before the upstream fused-shard remapping, preserving TP slicing, scale loading and loaded-name tracking. - Validate all three quantization descriptions only for actual three-shard projections. Preserve all-FLOAT/uniform-quant fusion, nongated draft projections and existing KDA mappings. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. ModelSlim Kimi checkpoints with mixed MLA projection/gate precision retain the gate's checkpoint dtype and values instead of silently corrupting them. The public [Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8 description](https://modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8/resolve/master/quant_model_description.json) has W8A8_DYNAMIC Q/

title: [Bug]: enable_reduce_sample returns incorrect vocabulary IDs for greedy requests in mixed batches
summary: ### Your current environment The issue was reproduced with vLLM-Ascend built from source at `fb00c6b`, together with vLLM at the CI-pinned commit `b2f6858`. Key output from `python collect_env.py` in the same test environment: ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (aarch64) Python: 3.12.13 PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu torch-npu: 2.10.0.post4 CANN: 9.1.0 npu-smi: 25.5.2 NPU: Ascend910; 1 and 2 NPUs used to test TP1 and TP2, respectively ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug With `enable_reduce_sample` enabled during speculative decoding, a batch containing both greedy-sampling and random-sampling requests can cause the greedy requests to return positions in the reordered candidate tensor instead of the corresponding vocabulary token IDs. This produces incorrect output tokens and also affects draft-token acceptance and rejection. A component-level reproducer uses two requests with entirely finite target logits. Each row is: ```python [-8., -3., -2., -1., 0., 9., 1., 2.] ``` The maximum corresponds to vocabulary token ID **5**. The first request has temperature `0`; the second has temperature `0` or `0.7`. title: [BugFix] Fix DecodeBenchConnector FP8 KV cache filling on Ascend NPUs

The cache remains FP8 after the fix. This PR builds on the FP8 encoding and startup-fill support introduced in [vllm-project/vllm#58472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58472). It addresses a separate compatibility issue: the current implementations still create or write FP8 tensors through operators unavailable on the tested NPU stack. Preserve upstream finite-range clamping, output dtypes, block selection and non-FP8 behavior. Constant fills encode one CPU scalar and allocate the fill buffer on the destination device; random startup fills use bounded row chunks. Select the adapted worker for FP8-only configurations as well as circular-cache configurations. This branch is based on **[vllm-project/vllm-ascend#20659](https://gi

title: [BugFix] Fix DecodeBenchConnector handling of Ascend circular KV caches
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DecodeBenchConnector recognizes circular caches only through the upstream `CircularBufferSpec` class. Ascend's `AscendIndexerKPoolTailSpec` instead derives from `SlidingWindowSpec` and declares circular semantics through `is_circular`. Its block size is ring capacity, and its manager allocates one block per request. Treating a 7-entry ring as ordinary historical KV makes a 5999-token dummy prefill require 857 blocks and fail the allocation assertion. **Failure reproduced on 950DT** GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8, single-node TP8/DP1 with EP, FP8 KV, MTP3, and a fixed 6000-input/1000-output workload failed during the first C1 warmup. The historical environment was vLLM `0.30.0+empty`, vLLM Ascend `0.30.0rc2`, and CANN 9.2.0. The original installed DecodeBenchConnector was enabled with `fill_mean=0.015` and `fill_std=0.0`. ```text AssertionError: DecodeBenchConnector block range exceeds allocated blocks: request=cmpl-bench-12c27c7d-0-0-8de42a08, group=1, range=[0, 857), allocated=1 ``` Group 1 was `AscendIndexerKPoolTailSpec` with ring capacity 7 and one allocated block. The CPU regression reproduces this exact 857-versus-1 failure before exercising the adapter. **Additional full-model validation** A full-model GLM-5.3-Flash run on 950DT completed 1,792 requests with 6,000 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens each, with no failures. This run combined the circular-cache fix with separate FP8-write and tuple/list isolation fixes, so its results cannot be attributed to this PR alone. Independent validation of this patch is listed below. Register

title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Add heartbeat leases to MooncakeConnectorV2
summary: Development continues in the original PR #21425, which includes the duplicate-DONE fix. The `mooncake-v2-heartbeat-leases` branch remains available for fetching. ### What this PR does / why we need it? MooncakeConnectorV2 currently releases producer KV after a fixed timeout even when a decoder is still waiting to consume it. Add renewable heartbeat leases so scheduler-admitted decode requests can retain producer KV while waiting for scheduling or completing a transfer, provided renewals arrive before expiry. D tracks requests from scheduler admission and sends batched heartbeats through a dedicated thread to P's existing scheduler control endpoint. P tracks initial and renewed leases using its local monotonic clock and expiry-ordered queues. Aggregated receive completion stops renewal and sends the completion notification. Late heartbeats do not revive expired leases. Based on the heartbeat implementation in #20192, with unconditional heartbeats and a 120-second default initial lease. This PR contains one commit and preserves the upstream remote-prefill completion handling. It replaces #21425 to move the source branch to `mooncake-v2-heartbeat-leases`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. MooncakeConnectorV2 uses heartbeat leases in place of the fixed 480-second timeout. No heartbeat enable flag is required. title: [RFC]: Tree Speculative Decoding
summary: ## Motivation. Tree-based speculative decoding has attracted considerable attention in recent years. It can substantially increase the acceptance length and yields pronounced speedups in latency-sensitive settings. We have therefore undertaken an exploratory implementation of tree speculative decoding on vLLM-Ascend. This RFC presents the progress to date and the plan for subsequent work. This RFC is organized into two parts. 1. Upstream integration — Merge support for tree speculative decoding into vLLM. 2. Ascend operator optimization — Optimize the vLLM-Ascend operators used by tree speculative decoding. ## Architecture The implementation resides entirely in vLLM-Ascend Model Runner V2 and does not depend on an upstream vLLM tree-speculative path. ### Tree construction One parallel draft feeds three schemes: - **DFlash.** Depth-wise logits are expanded into a tree, with no per-parent redraft. - **DSpark.** The tree grows level by level. Each parent is scored in its own context. - **Domino.** A wide candidate tree on the DFlash draft is pruned to the node budget, then rescored by a prefix correction head. ### Data flow Tree state is written to `req_states` and copied onto `AscendInputBatch` for verification. The proposer returns a flat token list. title: [Ops][BugFix] Clamp Engram lookback offsets to fix masked-lane OOB (aivec 507035)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #21392 `_gather_lookback_kernel` (Engram lookback, MRV2) computes `pos = num_computed - 1 - offs`, which is negative for fresh requests (`num_computed == 0`). title: [BugFix][Kernel] Fix W4A8 combine token accounting
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `CombineV2` in `dispatch_ffn_combine_w4_a8` compares `maxOutputSize`, a logical-token capacity, with `preSrcExpertSum`, an offset accumulated after doubling W4A8 rows. This can truncate valid expert tokens even when their total fits the configured capacity. It can also make Combine's tile scheduling disagree with GMM2, producing corrupted outputs that may propagate to logits and cause empty visible responses. For example, a logical prefix of 32,604 tokens and another expert with 5,850 tokens fit within a capacity of 65,536. The old check uses the expanded prefix of 65,208 and retains only 328 of those 5,850 tokens. Track logical capacity with `preSrcTokenSum`, incremented before row expansion. Preserve `preSrcExpertSum` for the expanded-row offsets. The regression test uses deterministic nonzero INT4 projections and checks a sufficient capacity against a larger reference capacity. A different input first overwrites the shared output buffer so missing writes cannot accidentally reuse the reference result. It covers stacked/tensor-list weights, inactive tokens, a safe control, a partially truncated group, exact capacity, and spare capacity. Related work: #9814 and #17343 address caller-side capacity sizing/guards. This fixes an internal units mismatch when the configured logical capacity is already sufficient. The open-PR search and related diffs did not reveal the same fix. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Corrects W4A8 fused MoE outputs that can become invalid or cause empty responses. No public API or configu

title: [Performance][Model] Skip padded DSV4.1 expert routes by default
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DSV4.1 pads token rows for graph replay and sequence parallelism. On the AllGather MoE path, routing those rows to local experts adds work to the grouped GEMMs. This change filters padding after the router selects experts. Hash routing uses the existing per-layer input-ID AllGather. - Model Runner V2 prepares one TP-aligned routing mask for the target model. Each graph replay refreshes its captured buffer with the current batch's valid token count, including when a prompt tail hits a decode graph. Eager decode and mixed batches also use the mask. - Pure prefill dispatched to eager skips both the mask update and the per-layer expert-ID rewrite, including when SP alignment adds padding. - After top-k, each EP rank maps padding rows to an expert outside its local range. InitRouting then excludes those routes from the local expert counts consumed by the grouped GEMMs. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? The existing `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` switch defaults to `1`. Set it to `0` to disable this filtering. It applies to DSV4.1 target inference on fixed AllGather with model-level SP, EP, TP > 1, DP/PCP/PP/DCP = 1 and linear expert placement. The eligibility check excludes microbatching, EPLB, mixed placement and adaptive verification. ### How was this patch tested? - 124 isolated CPU cases passed locally with production callables and mocked device operators. They cover eager prefill, eager mixed batches, prompt tails on FULL and PIECEWISE graphs, captured mask storage, per-layer Hash ID gathering and per-rank expert counts. -

summary: <details> <summary>The output of `python collect_env.py`</summary> ```text vLLM Ascend Version: 0.19.1rc2.dev3296+gb04f258fa vLLM Version: 0.32.0+empty PyTorch version: 2.10.0+cpu torch_npu version: 2.10.0.post7 CANN version: 9.2.1 Hardware: Ascend 950DT (A5) Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (native FP8, weight_block_size=[32,32], expert_dtype=fp4, num_attention_heads=64) ``` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug `AscendDSAV41AttentionMetadataBuilder._build_smla_metadata` (`vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v41.py`) already computes the TP-sharded local head count a few lines above: ```python n_local_heads = int( kwargs.get( "num_query_heads", int(_config_value(text_config, "num_attention_heads")) // self.vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size, ) ) ``` but the A5 packed-cache branch never uses it — it passes a hardcoded `num_heads_q=64` to `mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla_metadata`: ```python value = self._device_backend.mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla_metadata( length_rows, length_rows, cu_seqlens_q=common.query_start_loc[: req.num_reqs + 1].int().contiguous(), num_heads_q=64, num_heads_kv=1, head_dim=512, ... ) ``` At `tensor_parallel_size=1` this is invisible, since `n_local_heads` happens to equal 64 too. At `tensor_parallel_size>1` the real per-rank head count is lower (e.g. 8 at TP=8 for this 64-head model), but the kernel is still told "64", and rejects the mismatch. The sibling `dsa_v1.py` builder (the non-V4.1 DSA path) already passes `num_heads_q=n_local_heads` for the equivalent call, so this looks like a straightforward oversight introduced with the initial V4.1 A5 suppo

Yes. The three affected paths now honor the upstream configuration: | CLI setting | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Omitted | `None` (dense) | Upstream default `0` | | `0` | `None` (dense) | `0` | | Positive interval | `None` (dense) | Configured interval | | `None` | `None` (dense) | `None` (dense) | For sliding-window/Mamba groups, `0` retains the checkpoints needed for prompt replay, positive values additionally retain periodic checkpoints, and `None` retains reachable checkpoints densely. title: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Make DSpark draft ACL-graph capture correct for multi-request batches
summary: ## What this fixes The DSpark draft path is hard-disabled for ACL graph capture: ```python # DSpark runs eager only (Ascend cudagraph unsupported on this path). self.use_cuda_graph = False ``` When that path is exercised (draft graph enabled), three defects make multi-request decode fail or produce wrong draft rows: 1. **Batch contract mismatch.** The draft graph is captured with `q = num_query_per_req` rows per request, but dispatch is bucketed by `uniform_decode_query_len` (`q + 1`). With enough requests the dispatcher returns a bucket that is one request short (40 -> 42 gives 7 < 8, 35 -> 36 gives 6 < 7) and `model_runner_v1._pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` trips `assert num_reqs <= num_reqs_padded`. Repro: C=32 always, C<=16 never. 2. **Replay-buffer address drift.** `target_positions` and the CP local-length tensor are allocated per step, so the captured graph keeps reading stale addresses. 3. **Metadata ordering loss.** Draft metadata producers are enqueued through a Python-side wait that is not replayed inside the graph, so producer/consumer ordering is lost after capture. ## What this PR does - Build the draft batch descriptor from `num_query_per_req` and pad draft requests explicitly; keep the target descriptor only as the graph cache key. - Keep replay inputs in persistent, caller-owned buffers and refresh them in place, clearing the tail when the batch shrinks. - Enqueue metadata producers on the consumer stream before graph replay (device-side ordering, no host synchronize). - Gate all of the above behind the existing `dspark` method contract, DP=1 / DCP=1 / PCP=1

summary: ### Motivation. 孵化中心创新课题评审，因为最后的成果要合入vLLM-Ascend，专家建议社区对指标和场景提提意见。 ### Proposed Change. 1. 页感知的 KV Cache 稀疏方法研究  针对大模型推理过程中 KV Cache 随序列增长导致的内存爆炸问题，提出一种基于页级别管理的动态稀疏化算法。  层次化聚类映射： 不再简单地按 Token 权重剔除，而是通过分析不同 KV 页（Page）内部的注意力分布特征，利用聚类算法识别“活跃页”与“冗余页”。  页级卸载与重构策略： 在大页配置下，通过轻量级预测器实时识别不活跃页，并将其动态卸载至内存或进行低比特压缩，从而在保证模型推理精度（精度损失 < 10%）的前提下，显著降低显存峰值。 2. 硬件友好的昇腾页感知内存友好加速算子实现  针对昇腾 DaVinci 架构对连续访存的严格要求，开发高性能定制化算子。  算子融合与流水线并行： 将稀疏矩阵压缩指令与高性能密集计算内核（Cube Unit）深度结合，设计支持非规整页访问的专用 TILING 策略。  自适应计算映射： 针对页感知稀疏后的非连续特征，通过硬件感知的地址映射技术，实现稀疏操作在 NPU 内部的流水线并行，消除存储气泡。 3. 轻量级 vLLM 系统集成与端到端优化  将上述方法集成至适配昇腾生态的轻量级 vLLM 框架中。  精细化调度引擎： 结合动态资源管理，在推理过程中根据当前算力环境自动调节稀疏比例。  端到端加速： 目标实现在长序列推理场景下，页感知内存友好算子实现 >4 倍加速，端到端推理效率提升 2 倍，为大规模国产化稀疏推理提供可落地的方案。 ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_

title: [BugFix] Restore PCP prefill classification only for SFA attention
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With PCP8, one remaining prompt token plus five speculative lookahead positions can produce shards starting beyond the prompt boundary. These shards are locally classified as decode although their request is globally prefilling. For SFA attention and its indexer, that can make only some ranks skip prefill KV collectives. Do not enable graph execution previously rejected for another reason. Pure decode batches and non-SFA configurations retain their existing behavior. The predicate covers GLM KPool SFA and excludes dense attention and compressed DSA. The correction stays in the existing PCP finalization hook. title: [KV Transfer][BugFix] Drain Mooncake worker resources during shutdown
summary: Fixes #20974 ### What this PR does / why we need it? The public Mooncake connector shutdown hook only forwards to its scheduler. For a worker-role connector, it returns while the pull receiver is still blocked in its request queue, retaining the receiver and its executor/transfer-engine references. Forward connector shutdown to its worker. The pull receiver closes request admission under a short lock, places a FIFO stop sentinel after already accepted work, joins the receiver, then closes its executor with `wait=True`. New nonempty submissions are rejected once stopping begins. The join uses a 30-second warning interval so a slow drain is visible; it keeps waiting and retains ownership until completion. This is **not a 30-second teardown deadline** and does not cancel running native I/O. The worker clears its receiver reference only after successful cleanup. Repeated sequential shutdown is safe, failed cleanup remains retryable, and the executor is released even if the receiver never started. The base worker supplies a default no-op hook for implementations without asynchronous work. One existing scheduler test fixture that bypasses `__init__` now initializes `connector_worker = None`. This follows the pinned upstream [shutdown contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py#L446). Returning early via `executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` would not cancel already running transfers. No early-return teardown mode is added: aborting accepted requests also needs an e

title: [BugFix][MRV2] Fix residual grid for stochastic block verification
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Align the Ascend MRV2 residual-mass launch grid with native vLLM in both supported core lanes. The original v0.32.0 launch could leave a residual row unwritten and accept drafts with zero target probability; the rebased patch uses the native `num_logits` grid with the current v0.33.0 and main kernel signatures. **Original v0.32.0 failure** The earlier launch used `num_logits - 1`, while the imported kernel also excludes its final program through `logit_idx + 1 >= tl.num_programs(0)`. For one request with K=5, there are six logit rows and residual rows 1–4 are required. Launching five programs makes row 4 return before its store. Block verification then reads `local_residual_mass[4, :]` to decide whether to retain the four-token prefix. The workspace comes from `new_empty`, so this decision depends on the previous contents of that allocation. A NaN residual selects `h = 1` in the threshold calculation and can incorrectly retain all four drafts. **Fix and invariant** Change the two launch expressions to `(num_logits, vocab_num_blocks)` and leave first/bonus-row handling to the kernel. Every residual row consumed by block verification must be written before it is read. The regression uses disjoint target/draft distributions and fills the workspace with NaN to expose the missing write deterministically: a target supported only on token 0 must reject token-1 drafts. **Upstream relationship** Ascend #19138 introduced MRV2 block verification using the upstream kernels. The grid-dependent guard is present in vLLM 0.32.0 after vllm-project/vll

title: [Attention][BugFix] Ensure ENCODER_ONLY layers in pooling models bypass causal path
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `AscendAttentionBackendImpl.forward` chose the bidirectional pooling path from `attn_metadata.causal` alone. `ENCODER_ONLY` layers of hybrid models (Gated DeltaNet + full attention, e.g. the Qwen3.5-based Decision 3.0 / D3 checkpoints) reach the backend with `causal=True`, because they do not go through the `EncoderOnlyAttention` wrapper that clears the flag. These layers therefore silently ran causal attention even though the model sets `config.is_causal = False`. This PR also routes layers whose `attn_type` is `ENCODER_ONLY` to `_forward_encoder_attention`, which is what upstream backends do for such layers regardless of `metadata.causal`. - `DECODER` layers are unchanged. - Models whose encoder-only layers already receive `causal=False` (e.g. BERT-style models through `EncoderOnlyAttention`) take the same branch as before. - Generation models are unchanged (`model_runner_type` is not `"pooling"`). **Prefill context parallelism (PCP) is not supported for `ENCODER_ONLY` attention.** The encoder attention path attends over rank-local K/V only. Unlike the KV-cache write, it never gathers the other PCP ranks' tokens (encoder-only layers have no KV cache). Pooling models default to the V1 model runner, which already rejects PCP, but `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` can force V2 and bypass that check, which would silently give wrong results. This PR therefore fails at model construction with `NotImplementedError` for `ENCODER_ONLY` attention when `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`, and documents the limitation in the context parallel guide.

title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Reuse upstream packed HCCL flow with Ascend cross-chunk ordering

No global monkey-patching. - Order each later chunk after the preceding loader callback's slot-stream work with an NPU event recorded **after** that callback. Protect each owning clone on all slot streams and the caller stream before passing it to the loader. - Join already-submitted caller work onto the slots. Other producer/callback streams must establish the dependencies documented in the helper contracts. - Keep the conservative native HCCL submission/receive boundaries, Ascend's byte-clone unpack contract, validation and exception cleanup. There is no per-chunk post-load host barrier. - Preserve upstream's per-model parameter metadata cache and clear it on reinitialization. Without this, the upstream trainer omits unchanged metadata on update2, the Ascend receiver returns without receiving, and the trainer hangs in HCCL. - Add repeated model/graph reload coverage and unit tests for ordering, lifetime tracking, metadata reuse, device binding and failure paths. title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Size nested MTP draft position cache
summary: ## What this PR does Fixes long-context MTP startup/runtime failures for models whose text configuration is nested under `hf_text_config` (for example Qwen3.8-style configs). The vLLM revision currently pinned by vLLM Ascend tries to size the MTP draft position cache from the top-level `hf_config`. For nested text configs, the draft cache can therefore remain at its native positional limit while the target accepts a much longer context, which can lead to out-of-bounds rotary-cache access and engine termination. This change adds an Ascend MTP compatibility path that: - reads the draft's nested `hf_text_config`; - expands only `max_position_embeddings`, and only for cache-only RoPE types that are safe to extend; - synchronizes the draft `max_model_len` only after that safe expansion succeeds; - deliberately does **not** copy the target YaRN parameters into the draft, so it does not alter the draft rotary frequencies or multiply its cache footprint. ## Scope and upstream status This is a backend-specific temporary compatibility fix for the vLLM revision currently pinned by vLLM Ascend, not a claim that the global root cause lives in the Ascend plugin. title: [BugFix][v0.32.0rc] Align MTP draft RoPE config for long context
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR safely expands the nested MTP draft model's positional cache before constructing its runtime config. Dict-style `hf_overrides` are applied only to the target model in vLLM. For a long-context target using YaRN, the MTP draft can therefore retain the checkpoint's original `max_position_embeddings=262144` and build a `(262144, 64)` RoPE cache, while draft graph replay receives target positions around 1M. On Ascend this causes an out-of-bounds device access (error 507011) and kills the decode engine. The failure was confirmed from device addresses: the fault address offset from the draft RoPE cache base was exactly `1,008,000 * 64 * 2` bytes. The fix applies vLLM's cache-only safety rule to the nested draft `hf_text_config`, which the pinned vLLM release currently misses: - it does **not** copy the target's YaRN parameters into the draft; - it raises the draft `max_position_embeddings` and runtime `max_model_len` only when the draft's own RoPE type is safe to resize (`default`, `linear`, `llama3`, `ntk`, or `proportional`); - unsafe RoPE types such as YaRN remain unchanged. This keeps the target's YaRN behavior and the draft's rotary frequencies unchanged while ensuring that a plain-MRoPE MTP draft has enough cache rows for the target positions. The compatibility path can be removed after vllm-project/vllm#63432 is available in the pinned vLLM version. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [RFC]: Deprecate and Sunset Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) for GQA Models
summary: ### Motivation. Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) was designed to partition the KV cache along the sequence length dimension across ranks, mitigating per-device KV cache memory bottlenecks during decode. For Grouped Query Attention (GQA), `vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/attention_cp.py` implemented specialized GQA DCP metadata builders (`AscendAttentionDCPMetadataBuilder`) and execution implementations (`AscendAttentionDCPImpl`), which perform query head all-to-all gather, local attention against local KV shards, and output/LSE combination via `fused_dcp_lse_combine`. However, the continued maintenance of DCP for GQA models has become unjustified: 1. **GQA KV Heads are Already Sharded by TP**: In GQA architectures, the number of KV heads is naturally small (e.g., 4 or 8 KV heads). These KV heads are already sharded across Tensor Parallelism (TP) ranks (e.g., TP=4 or TP=8 leaves only 1 KV head per rank). Overlaying DCP onto GQA requires strict divisibility constraints (`TP % DCP == 0` and KV head divisibility), leaving very little flexibility or scenario space where DCP is practically beneficial. 2. **Current Mainstream Models Rarely Use Standard GQA for Long Contexts**: Frontier long-context models have broadly transitioned to Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), Sparse Attention (SFA), or Linear Attention architectures. Pure GQA models are rarely deployed with context lengths that require sequence-sharded KV cache over multiple nodes/devices. 3. **High Maintenance and Code Complexity Overhead**: The GQA DCP path introduces substantial complexity: - Dedicated all-to-al

title: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Pass full-capacity group metadata buffers to store_kv_block
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The group metadata buffers (`group_len`, `group_key_idx`, `group_key_cache_idx`) are token-level descriptors produced by `store_kv_block_metadata` from the slot_mapping. A prefill chunk of N tokens across B blocks yields up to B groups (one per block-run of consecutive slots), which is a token-dimension quantity. They were incorrectly sliced to the REQUEST dimension when passed into the attention metadata (introduced in #11865): ```text model_runner_v1.py: group_len.gpu[:num_reqs_padded] llm_base_proposer.py: group_len.gpu[:num_reqs] ``` With `c8_enable_reshape_optim` enabled, the `store_kv_block` kernel reads the group descriptors from this sliced view and only writes indexer KV for the visible groups. For a typical prefill chunk (16384 tokens, 128 blocks), only `num_reqs` groups (e.g. 1-8) out of ~128 are visible, so the indexer KV for the remaining ~120 blocks is never written and stays zero/stale. The corrupted indexer KV is transferred to the decode node where the top-k selection attends a wrong token subset. The single-layer MTP draft is hypersensitive to this (acceptance rate collapses) while the 78-layer greedy target absorbs it (outputs look correct), making the bug hard to spot from correctness checks alone. Fix: pass the full-capacity buffers (`max_num_batched_tokens`) without slicing. The `store_kv_block_metadata` kernel already zero-fills unused entries, and the `store_kv_block` kernel already skips `group_len <= 0`, so the full buffer is safe and correct. This also gives graph capture a fixed tensor shape, which is more

title: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Make DSpark draft ACL-graph capture correct for multi-request batches
summary: ## What this fixes The DSpark draft path is hard-disabled for ACL graph capture: ```python # DSpark runs eager only (Ascend cudagraph unsupported on this path). self.use_cuda_graph = False ``` When that path is exercised (draft graph enabled), three defects make multi-request decode fail or produce wrong draft rows: 1. **Batch contract mismatch.** The draft graph is captured with `q = num_query_per_req` rows per request, but dispatch is bucketed by `uniform_decode_query_len` (`q + 1`). With enough requests the dispatcher returns a bucket that is one request short (40 -> 42 gives 7 < 8, 35 -> 36 gives 6 < 7) and `model_runner_v1._pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` trips `assert num_reqs <= num_reqs_padded`. Repro: C=32 always, C<=16 never. 2. **Replay-buffer address drift.** `target_positions` and the CP local-length tensor are allocated per step, so the captured graph keeps reading stale addresses. 3. **Metadata ordering loss.** Draft metadata producers are enqueued through a Python-side wait that is not replayed inside the graph, so producer/consumer ordering is lost after capture. ## What this PR does - Build the draft batch descriptor from `num_query_per_req` and pad draft requests explicitly; keep the target descriptor only as the graph cache key. - Keep replay inputs in persistent, caller-owned buffers and refresh them in place, clearing the tail when the batch shrinks. - Enqueue metadata producers on the consumer stream before graph replay (device-side ordering, no host synchronize). - Gate all of the above behind the existing `dspark` method contract, DP=1 / DCP=1 / PCP=1

title: --async-scheduling has no effect on Ascend (silently ignored) - measured identical throughput
summary: ## Environment - Hardware: Ascend 950DT (aarch64), DP=7 TP=1, max-num-seqs 32 - Image: ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5 (CANN 9.2.1, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7) - Model: Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8, MTP k=3, block verify enabled ## Observation We are hunting host-side scheduling overhead in decode-bound serving. Instrumented `EngineCore.step/step_with_batch_queue` (perf_counter around schedule/submit/wait/update) shows the EngineCore side is nearly idle: sched ≈ 0.85 ms, submit ≈ 0.12 ms, update ≈ 0.3 ms per step, while ~84 ms/step is spent blocking on worker response — i.e. the host gap lives inside the worker's execute_model call chain, and scheduler/execution overlap would be the natural lever. `--async-scheduling` exists in vLLM and `SchedulerConfig.async_scheduling` is accepted on this build, but: 1. Adding the flag changes nothing measurable: 3-run benchmark mean 5281 tok/s vs 5384 baseline (within run variance), accept length and TPOT identical. 2. No log line acknowledges the flag being unsupported/disabled on the Ascend platform. ## Ask Either wire async scheduling through the Ascend model runner (it looks like the NPUModelRunner path does not implement the hooks it needs), or emit an explicit warning that it is a no-op on this platform, so users don't benchmark under a false assumption.

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Isolate multi-group bulk load failures per request
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #18794 A bulk GET can restore one KV cache group while leaving another incomplete. Flat block IDs cannot safely identify the affected hybrid request because IDs overlap across groups. A synchronous request can already be RUNNING when the failure is discovered. Keep non-layerwise external cache hits with multiple physical groups in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until loading completes. Successful loads become eligible for a later model step; failed, missing or malformed results fail the affected request through the existing load-failure policy. Healthy requests continue. The scheduler, worker and connector share this admission decision. Completion handling preserves cancellation bookkeeping and worker quorum; Mamba copy ordering follows the waiting mode. A defensive exception remains if a synchronous multi-group failure lacks proof that its request is waiting. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Multi-group bulk external hits wait before model execution, including with `load_async=false`. GET still executes synchronously in that configuration. Single-group and layerwise admission behavior is unchanged. The default `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` returns an error for the affected request; hybrid recomputation remains unsupported. The extra admission step has been measured in the controlled single-NPU fixture described below; production-model performance remains unmeasured. title: [BugFix] Correct draft-graph batch contract and replay-buffer ownership
summary: # PR draft Title: fix(spec_decode): correct draft-graph batch contract and replay-buffer ownership ## Problem With DSpark speculative decoding and ACL graph capture, multi-request decode batches can crash or produce wrong draft rows because the draft path reused the target batch descriptor (q + 1 rows per request) while the draft graph is captured with q rows per request. Two related lifetime issues also break graph replay: - `target_positions` and the CP local-length tensor are re-created per step, so the captured graph keeps reading stale addresses. - Draft metadata producers are enqueued through a Python-side wait that is not replayed inside the graph, so producer/consumer ordering is lost after capture. ## Fix 1. Build the draft batch descriptor from `num_query_per_req` (per-request draft rows) and pad draft requests explicitly; keep the target descriptor only as the graph key. 2. Keep replay inputs in persistent buffers owned by the builder and refresh them in place, clearing the tail when the batch shrinks. 3. The shared GLM-5.3-Flash PD launcher always executes role templates with `--data-parallel-rank`, including when `--dp-size 1` is selected. Document the filtering and the requirement to put each option on its own line. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Documentation only. No runtime library changes or release note fragment. ### How was this patch tested? - Extracted and executed the documented Python launcher from this release branch with actual Bash child processes and a mock role template. title: [Refactor] Consolidate SFA PCP execution
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? SFA distributes PCP behavior across a separate implementation class and composes PCP+DCP through multiple inheritance. PCP continues to use `ParallelOProjection`. - DCP and PCP+DCP use one DCP subclass, which inherits PCP behavior and owns DCP initialization, slot selection, query/KV gathers, sparse-index remapping and LSE output merging. DCP metadata/context types and both builders remain in `sfa_cp.py`. - Remove `AscendSFAPCPImpl`, `AscendSFAPCPDCPImpl`, both resolvers and `SFAForwardContext`. Two native-forward hooks preserve communication timing: decode Q gather starts before packed KV writes; prefill/mixed KV gather starts after writes and before indexer selection. - Preserve native/fused PCP cache handling, C8/TQ layouts, physical PCP handling for replicated drafts, and sleep-mode buffer ownership. - Reuse the metadata builder's stable local slot view for PROLOG_V3 PCP decode without KV gather, preserving one cached int64 conversion across layers. Inline DCP-only initialization in the DCP constructor, with its body and ordering unchanged. - Retain main #20512's packed PCP cache fix in the shared `_store_packed_kv_cache()`: expanded slots must match the gathered, deduplicated decode/prefill payload. title: [Bugfix][Sample] Preserve logprob precision for common logit offsets
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Preserve token-logprob precision when logits have a large common offset by subtracting the row maximum before the log-normalization term: `logits - max_val - lse`. For 32,000 equal FP32 logits of `1e8`, the existing kernel returns `-8` instead of `-log(32000)`, approximately `-10.37349118`. Subtracting `lse` from the large logits first loses normalization precision. The corrected order matches vLLM's core token-logprob implementation. The patch adds 12 deterministic regression cases covering FP32, FP16, BF16, offsets of +/-10000, and single/multiple vocabulary blocks. References use CPU FP64 normalization of the already-quantized input. The tests are in the Model Runner V2 PR test directory. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Token log probabilities retain normalization precision for finite logits with large common offsets. The API and output layout are unchanged. Includes `release_notes/fragments/20376.yaml`. ### How was this patch tested? For current head `672efb1f4e53d858101c71652fd3e7960c0d272e`, [CI run #42481971467](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/42481971467) passed pre-commit and both CPU matrices: vLLM `v0.32.0` and verified main `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`. DCO and both documentation builds also passed. The [official targeted A2 workflow](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41064109224) passed against vLLM `v0.32.0` and verified main `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542` for head `b413c6e2579b291c1e5884dba80489398df95692`. title: [Feature] Fuse sequence collective into dense SP GEMMs for Qwen3.5
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Dense sequence parallelism (FlashComm switch, Qwen3.5 dense family) now fuses the sequence all-gather into the column GEMMs (`torch_npu.npu_all_gather_base_mm`) and the reduce-scatter into the row GEMMs (`torch_npu.npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base`) for unquantized batches at TP size 2/4/8, overlapping the boundary communication with the matmuls. title: [BugFix][Sampling] Fix greedy token IDs in mixed batches
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #16396. With `enable_reduce_sample=True`, the rejection sampler passes reordered logits to `greedy_sample` when greedy and random requests share a speculative batch. `greedy_sample` assumes the columns still follow the local vocabulary order. For logits `[-8, -3, -2, -1, 0, 9, 1, 2]`, the mixed TP1 path returns candidate position 0 instead of vocabulary ID 5. It incorrectly accepts draft token 0 and rejects draft token 5. Compute greedy IDs after logits processors and before `apply_sampling_constraints`, then pass them to `rejection_sample`. This keeps processor masks effective and preserves the original argmax tie-break before top-k truncation. The two greedy all-gathers now run before candidate gathering. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Fixes incorrect tokens and draft acceptance for greedy requests batched with random requests. No serving API or configuration changes. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on Ascend `9d9b9ed` with its paired vLLM `a97dacb`: ```bash TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest -sv tests/ut/sample/ ``` Applying only the test changes gives **32 passed, 8 failed**. With the fix, **40 passed**. The 16 new cases cover pure-greedy/mixed batches, masks, ties, acceptance/rejection, and a random row whose expected result differs from greedy sampling. Native TP1 and TP2 checks passed all 16 cases per rank; the original code failed the 8 mixed cases. These use real HCCL and rejection kernels with fixed bonus and random inputs. Python 3.12, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4

title: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Normalize layerwise producer prompts before prefix lookup
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Normalize hybrid PD producer prompts in the existing `on_new_request` hook, before the scheduler queries the local prefix cache. The cache-matching callback then keeps the request length unchanged. Previously, a repeated prompt could first match all but its last token locally and then lose that final token inside connector matching. The cached-token count could cover the entire shortened producer prompt, triggering `assert num_new_tokens > 0`. The change is independent of prefill offload and uses cache capabilities and transfer direction, with no model-name or sequence-length special cases. The shared scheduler is unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Existing final-token handoff and single-token behavior are preserved. ### How was this patch tested? - Regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it; cover admission timing, repeated callbacks, cache-block boundaries, consumers and non-hybrid requests. - Main-based connector tests: `python -m pytest -q --import-mode=importlib tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_layerwise_connector.py` (69 passed). title: [BugFix][v0.32] Preserve KDA rollback state for zero-draft and shortened MTP decodes
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Backport of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20773 to `releases/v0.32.0rc`. Fixes silent recurrent-state corruption when an MTP decode has zero scheduled drafts or a shortened verification query. - `AscendMambaHybridModelState.prepare_attn` previously classified a row as speculative only with positive drafts and `scheduled == drafts + 1`. A zero-draft/shortened decode could become `-1` (non-speculative). `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build` also demoted an entire zero-draft batch. That discards the rollback state-table convention: the previous accepted count selects `state_indices[accepted - 1]`, so reading the normal first slot can use a stale state and corrupt subsequent hidden states and sampling without a runtime error. - Keep rollback-capable decode rows, including explicit zero drafts, on the speculative path; preserve their previous acceptance and full state table. Prefill remains distinguished by `-1`. - **Native KDA companion: https://github.com/flashserve/flash-linear-attention-npu/pull/1049.** Native `recurrent_kda` additionally rejects `previous_accepted > current_query_length`, even when it is within the 2-D state-table width, and returns without writing output/state. For the native FLA KDA path that guard must also be fixed; this Ascend patch alone does not resolve the combined failure. With RecoverSSM enabled, speculative verification uses Triton `kda_recoverssm_verify` plus its commit path and bypasses this guard; that route does not require the native fix for this defect; a separate original-FLA r

title: [BugFix][Attention] Serialize GLM CANN operator package initialization
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Concurrent GLM-5.3-Flash workers can lose Torch JIT build locks when initializing CANN operators in a shared cache. Serialize package import and native `key_pool` / `pool_key_indexer` preloads with an atomic marker in the resolved Torch build directory. Serialized compilation can also leave some ranks outside the subsequent MC2 HCCL initialization window. After initialization, MoE workers rendezvous on their CPU EP group, outside the cache lock, before constructing the following MoE layers. Release counterpart: #18982. Refs #15665 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? CANN compilation completes during backend initialization, and MoE peers finish this initialization before proceeding together. Lock acquisition waits up to 30 minutes and never removes an occupied marker automatically. A killed initializer can leave a marker; the timeout explains when manual cleanup is safe. ### How was this patch tested? - Focused KPool, metadata, cache and MTP suite on the release counterpart: 151 CPU/mock tests passed. The existing fork regression covers unavailable advisory locking, first operator use, and MoE synchronization outside the lock; the timeout regression preserves an occupied marker. - Real complete backend-module and CANN initialization with a real four-rank Gloo group: a controlled late rank causes the previous implementation to fail its subsequent collective (0/4); the updated main and release implementations each pass (4/4). title: [BugFix] Settle DeepSeek V4.1 KV cache block size
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 uses the same 32/64/128 KV-cache block-size table as DeepSeek V4, but `refresh_block_size()` only recognizes `model_type == "deepseek_v4"`. V4.1 therefore falls through to the generic block-size policy, whose behavior depends on whether prefix caching / chunked prefill are enabled. **When prefix caching or chunked prefill is enabled:** the generic policy rewrites every block size other than 128 to 128. For V4.1 this means: - an explicit `--block-size 32` or `--block-size 64` is silently ignored and the cache is built with 128; - an unsupported size (for example 16 or 256) is also promoted to 128 by the generic rule rather than being handled by the V4.1-specific fallback policy. The result is that the requested cache geometry is not honored and V4.1 does not apply its own block-size normalization policy. **When both prefix caching and chunked prefill are disabled:** the generic rewrite is skipped. Supported 32/64 values remain valid, but unsupported values are left untouched (apart from the xlite >128 adjustment). A size such as 16 can then reach `DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[cache_config.block_size]` while the V4.1 cache spec is being built and raise `KeyError`, because that table only contains 32/64/128. The failure mode simply moves from "silently rewritten" to "crash later". In class `AscendDeepseekV41SWACache`: The line `block_size = DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[cache_config.block_size][0][1]` restricts `block_size` to only take values in `[32, 64, 128]`. title: [BugFix] Preserve GLM-Next shared-pool KV budget

title: [Performance]: Avoid unused origin allocation in MX SwiGLU quantization
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance `npu_swiglu_group_quant` allocates a full BF16/FP16 `y_origin` tensor even with `quant_mode=2` and `output_origin=False`. The routed MXFP4 MoE path discards this output, and the MX kernel does not consume its pointer. For a BF16 input of shape `[196608, 4608]`, the unused `[196608, 2304]` output occupies **864 MiB**. We found this while tracing allocator retries during long-prefill serving. It adds avoidable memory pressure even though no extra origin computation is performed. The allocation is in [the Native factory](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/40b3842d367daa86e5eaf38573d42b36e3790d41/csrc/torch_binding.cpp#L1905); [Meta](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/40b3842d367daa86e5eaf38573d42b36e3790d41/csrc/torch_binding_meta.cpp#L1332) mirrors it. The affected factory and binding are unchanged from the hardware-tested base `3b715ff78066`. A possible fix is to return an empty tensor for this unrequested MX output and update Native/Meta together, preserving the requested-origin and other quantization paths. This changes the third output's shape to `(0,)`, so that contract should be documented. ### Report of performance regression Minimal allocation reproduction on an A5 environment with the native binding built: ```python import importlib import torch import torch_npu from vllm_ascend.utils import bootstrap_custom_op_env bootstrap_custom_op_env() if not hasattr(torch.ops._C_ascend, "npu_swiglu_group_quant"): importlib.import_module("vllm_ascend.vllm_ascend_C") x = torch.randn(128, 4608, dtype=torch.bfloat16, d

title: [BugFix] Keep PP decode fenced until in-flight tokens complete
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With Model Runner V1, PP and async scheduling, the scheduler can queue the final prefill chunk before consuming the preceding chunk's result. That earlier completion clears the request's decode fence while the final chunk still has tokens in flight. Decode can then be queued before the first sampled token is available to the first pipeline stage. Clear the fence after the request's in-flight token count reaches zero. Intermediate chunks and independent requests can still overlap. The change applies when speculative decoding is disabled as well. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. It fixes incorrect generated output in this PP path when an intermediate prefill completion precedes the final prefill completion. ### How was this patch tested? - Added a regression in tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_pp_mtp.py. It schedules two prefill chunks, completes the earlier chunk first, and verifies that the fence stays set until the final completion. - Replayed the regression with a CPU scheduler double. The old implementation fails while two tokens are still in flight. The patched implementation passes. - Ruff 0.14.0 lint and format checks passed for both modified Python files. - Python compilation and git diff --check passed. Upstream CI will exercise the full supported test environments. Review should focus on the ordering between the base scheduler's in-flight accounting and the wrapper's fence release. Revert this change to restore the previous behavior. ### Checklist - [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage - [x] Regression

title: [RFC]: Support GDN RecoverSSM for Speculative Decoding on Ascend
summary: ### Motivation. This RFC proposes extending RecoverSSM to Gated DeltaNet (GDN) on Ascend Model Runner V2 (MRV2). During speculative decoding, the target model needs to verify multiple draft tokens while maintaining recurrent states. The conventional approach may retain intermediate SSM states for each speculative position, increasing Mamba/SSM cache consumption as the speculative window grows. RecoverSSM addresses this by maintaining a single recurrent-state checkpoint and reconstructing the accepted state after rejection sampling. The existing KDA RecoverSSM work provides a reference for the verify/commit lifecycle. However, GDN has different recurrent-state update equations and requires dedicated recovery operators. The goal is to reduce recurrent-state cache consumption for GDN-based models without compromising speculative decoding correctness. Proposed Change ### Proposed Change. ### 1. Extend the RecoverSSM Lifecycle to GDN Reuse the existing RecoverSSM architecture and MRV2 post-sampling commit lifecycle. The proposed execution flow is: ```text Persistent GDN State | v Speculative Verification (K+1 tokens) | |-- Compute target outputs |-- Record intermediate recovery data |-- Preserve the persistent checkpoint | v Rejection Sampling | |-- Determine accepted prefix |-- Include the leading target token | v GDN RecoverSSM Commit | |-- Reconstruct accepted recurrent state |-- Compact convolution history | v Updated Persistent GDN State ``` During verification, the persistent recurrent checkpoint must not be overwritten by speculative states that may later be rejected. title: [BugFix][KVOffload] Offload only prefix-cacheable KV cache groups
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `AscendOffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches()` builds `CanonicalKVCaches.group_data_refs` by iterating over **every** entry of `kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups`, while the scheduler only emits `GPULoadStoreSpec.group_sizes` / `block_indices` for the groups returned by `get_offloading_group_ids()` (i.e. `kv_cache_config.prefix_cacheable_group_ids`, or the HiSparse indexer groups when `hisparse_host_num_blocks` is set). `SingleDirectionNPUOffloadingHandler` consumes both sequences positionally: assert len(group_sizes) == len(self.kv_cache_groups_data_refs) ... for group_size, block_idx, group_data_refs in zip( group_sizes, block_indices, self.kv_cache_groups_data_refs ): So on any hybrid cache layout that contains a group which is not eligible for offloading — e.g. a `CircularBufferSpec` state/scratch group, or an SWA group under bounded replay — the worker registers more groups than the scheduler addresses. The outcome is either an immediate `AssertionError` inside `native/cpu_npu.py`, or, when only the *order* diverges, D2H/H2D copies that silently target the tensors of the wrong group. This PR filters both registration loops through `get_offloading_group_ids()` and preserves the order of the returned tuple. That is exactly what upstream `OffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches()` has done since vllm-project/vllm#57145 ("[kv_offload] Skip scratch groups"); the Ascend native connector is a forked copy of that worker, so it never picked the fix up even though the vLLM version it pins already requires the filtered set. title: [BugFix][Model] Fix A5 BF16 GBSA softmax precision

title: [Performance] Fuse QSA compressed-key normalization and cache store
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? QSA compressed Indexer keys currently pass through group pooling, a first-position tensor, rotary gathering, RMSNorm/MRoPE and a separate cache store. Add a specialization of the existing group-compression kernel that normalizes, rotates and stores directly into the strided compressed-key cache, without allocating those intermediate tensors. Keep the BF16 pooling/normalization/product rounding boundaries and the original slot masking. Group-first MRoPE positions can come from the current chunk or the old position ring. title: [Feature]: Support Pooling Model Full Graph Capture
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Feature Proposal Enable full graph (CUDAGraph/TorchGraph) capture for models with pooling layers on Ascend NPU. Previously, forcing full graph mode on pooling models resulted in error `507011` during replay. This PR resolves the underlying issues related to graph keys, sequence length persistence, and tensor reference management to allow successful graph construction and replay for pooling models. ### Motivation The current vLLM Ascend implementation restricts full graph capture for pooling models due to several technical hurdles: 1. **Graph Capture Failure:** Forcing `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` on pooling models triggers error `507011` during the replay phase. 2. **Key Management Issues:** The graph capture mechanism relies on keys that are not padded tokens, leading to mismatches during replay. 3. **Persistence Issues:** Variables like `qsl` (query sequence lengths) and `seq_len` are not persistent across graph captures, causing state inconsistency. 4. **Reference Lifetime:** Tensors captured in the graph are treated as weak references, which can lead to garbage collection before the graph is replayed. Enabling full graph capture for pooling models is critical for maximizing inference throughput on Ascend NPU, as pooling models (often used in embedding tasks or vision-language models) are common in production workloads. ### Problem Statement - **Specific Problem:** When users attempt to run pooling models with `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`, the system fails with error `507011` during the replay phase of graph capture. - **Root Causes:** - The k

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR implements the Decode sparse KV cache offloading proposed in [vllm-project/vllm#48203](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48203) using Mooncake as the host memory and transfer backend. Long-context inference can require KV cache capacity beyond available HBM. For DSA models such as GLM5.2, sparse attention accesses only the top-k tokens selected by the Indexer. This permits the full Main KV cache to reside in host DRAM, with the Indexer cache and hot top-k buffers retained in HBM. This PR enables Mooncake-backed DSA sparse KV offload for Decode through Mooncake host allocation, integration with the fused-overlap operator, and P/D transfer support in `MooncakeConnectorV1`. The Connector transfers Main KV from Prefill HBM directly to Decode host DRAM (RD2H) and Indexer KV to Decode HBM (D2D). This PR depends on [#15642](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/15642), which provides the fused-overlap operator for DSA sparse KV offload and its framework integration. **1. Mooncake host allocation** - Introduce a backend-neutral `HostKVAllocator` interface and `MooncakeHostPool`, while retaining `memfabric` as the default backend. - Allocate Decode Main KV through `mooncake.shared_segment` using Ascend VMM, with 1-GiB-aligned address reservations. TP rank 0 owns the allocation; peers map the same physical host memory using their own local addresses. - Validate local view layouts and manage allocation cleanup. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Apply the GLM5Next input-normalization fix to `releases/v0.32.0rc`. The model inherits `supports_mm_device_do_normalize=True`, so vLLM skips CPU rescaling/normalization and supplies raw pixels. title: [BugFix][Model] Restore GLM5Next device-side normalization
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? GLM5Next inherits `supports_mm_device_do_normalize=True` from its parent. vLLM therefore supplies raw pixels instead of rescaling and normalizing them on the CPU. The Ascend-specific vision tower did not install or call the input normalizer: it only cast the pixels before patch embedding. Pass `build_mm_input_norm(self.model_config)` to the custom vision tower and apply it once, before patch embedding. This reuses vLLM's processor-derived normalization and its Ascend implementation. title: [Contribution] 任务 #2：[Arch/Perf] 传输路径改 IPC，消除 GIL 瓶颈
summary: ## 背景 `ascend_store` 的 save/load 当前通过进程内 daemon 线程完成（`KVCacheStore*Sending/RecvingThread`），主线程与 send/recv 线程之间用 `queue.Queue` + `threading.Event` 协作。每进程最多 1 个 send 线程 + 1 个 recv 线程（`_start_kv_transfer_threads` 在三种模式间二选一）。部分热路径在 Python 层执行：`PoolKey.to_string`、`_handle_stored_request` 内 addrs/sizes 构建、key 生成器循环，与 forward 的 Python 层代码共享同一进程的 GIL。 随着多 rank 并行传输、独立崩溃隔离、NPU stream/event 跨进程协作等需求出现，单进程多线程架构在扩展性上存在瓶颈。 相关代码路径：`vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store`。 ## 任务 将传输路径由"进程内多线程 + queue.Queue"改造为"独立传输子进程 + IPC"，使 key 构建、buffer 调度、I/O 提交在独立子进程执行，不再与 worker 主进程共享 GIL。 * 范围：三种传输模式（非 layerwise / key layerwise / GVA layerwise） * 改造范围较大，建议分阶段推进，阶段划分与方法由开发者自定 ## 验收标准 ### 1. 功能正确性 * 三种传输模式功能与改造前一致 * greedy / non-greedy 输出一致（精度无回归） * 子进程异常不拖垮 worker 主进程，且能被重启或降级回进程内线程模式 ### 2. 性能验证 * 附改造前后对比数据：吞吐 / 延迟 / key 构建 CPU 占比 / IPC 开销 ### 3. 交付件 * 设计文档（含方案选型、风险清单、回退预案） * 原型对比报告 * PR + 设计说明 + 单测（覆盖子进程启停、异常恢复、跨进程 buffer 共享、IPC 通道断连） ## 环境约定 - vllm-ascend：最新 main - 硬件：Ascend NPU（注明型号 + 卡数 + TP/CP/PP 配置） - 关联任务池：#9079 - 验收人：@赵鹏博 ## 重点关注 * NPU KV cache buffer 跨进程共享是核心难点 * layerwise 模式的 NPU Event 跨进程语义需重新设计（`AttentionComputeStartGate`） * 需保留降级路径，平台不支持或子进程启动失败时能回退到进程内线程模式 ## 任务周期 * 发布：2026-08-12 * 回收：2026-10-31（长线任务，分阶段交付）

title: [Contribution] [Perf][MRV2] compute_token_logprobs 算子性能优化
summary: ## 背景 MRV2（Model Runner V2）采样路径中，`compute_token_logprobs` 负责对采样 token 计算 log-softmax 概率。Ascend 侧实现位于 `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/logprob.py`，通过 `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_triton.py` 替换 vllm-core 的 GPU 版本（`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logprob.py`）。 当前实现为 Triton kernel `_topk_log_softmax_kernel`：每个 request 启动一个 program，以固定 `BLOCK_SIZE=12944` 分块遍历整个词表，两趟计算（max + sum exp）得到 log-softmax，再 gather 指定 token_ids 的 logprob。配套的 `compute_topk_logprobs` 中 `_ranks_kernel` 计算 token rank（遍历词表统计 logits > 选中值的个数）。 存在以下可优化点： - `BLOCK_SIZE=12944` 硬编码，对不同词表大小 / batch shape 非最优； - log-softmax 两趟遍历词表，未使用 online softmax 融合； - `_ranks_kernel` 用 int32 累加 `(logits > x)` 的逐块比较，长词表下开销大； - `multibuffer=False`、grid `(batch_size,)` 未充分利用 NPU 向量核。 ## 任务 优化 `compute_token_logprobs` / `compute_topk_logprobs` 在 Ascend NPU 上的性能。 - 路径：`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/logprob.py` - 方向（由开发者结合 NPU profiling 自定）：online softmax 单趟融合、BLOCK_SIZE 自适应、rank 计算并行化、向量核利用率提升 ## 验收标准 ### 1. 精度对比（前后） - 优化前后 `compute_token_logprobs` / `compute_topk_logprobs` 输出在相同输入下一致（logprob 数值误差 ≤ 1e-5，token_ranks 完全一致）； - 与 vllm-core GPU 基线（`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logprob.py`）输出对齐（误差 ≤ 1e-5）； - 开启 logprob 的端到端推理输出 token 序列与优化前一致（greedy + non-greedy）。 ### 2. 性能对比（前后） - 单算子 profiling：优化前后 kernel 延迟对比（多组 batch_size / num_logprobs / vocab_size）； - NPU profiler 时间线对比（kernel 数量、向量核利用率）； - 端到端：开启 logprob 场景下 decode 吞吐 / 延迟对比。 ### 3. 交付件 - PR + 设计说明 + 精度对比表 + 性能数据曲线 + 单测 ## 环境约定 - vllm-ascend：最新 main - 硬件：Ascend NPU（注明型号 + 卡数 + TP 配置） - 关联任务池：#9079 - 验收人：@chengduxiaowu ## 重点关注 - logprob 为采样/排序关键路径，精度必须严格对齐，不得改变采样结果； - 大词表（如 15w+）场景是主要

title: [Contribution] [Perf][MRV2] apply_penalties 算子性能优化
summary: ## 背景 MRV2 采样路径中，`apply_penalties` 对 logits 施加 repetition / frequency / presence 惩罚。Ascend 侧实现位于 `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/penalties.py`，经 `patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_triton.py` 替换 vllm-core GPU 版本。 当前实现为 Triton kernel `_penalties_kernel`，grid `(num_tokens, num_blocks)`，`BLOCK_SIZE=4096` 分块遍历词表。kernel 内对每个 token 有一段顺序循环 `for prev_pos in tl.range(pos)` 累加前序 draft token 的 bin count（O(pos) 每程序），再施加三类惩罚。受限于 "NPU 不支持链式 or" 做了 `use_penalty = use_penalty or ...` 拆分。 存在以下可优化点： - `for prev_pos in tl.range(pos)` 顺序累加 draft token 计数，长序列 / 多 draft token 下串行开销大； - `BLOCK_SIZE=4096` 固定； - 早期返回（无惩罚）逻辑可进一步减少无效 launch。 ## 任务 优化 `apply_penalties` 在 Ascend NPU 上的性能。 - 路径：`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/penalties.py`（`_penalties_kernel` / `apply_penalties`） - 方向：消除 / 并行化 draft token 计数顺序循环、BLOCK_SIZE 自适应、减少无效 launch ## 验收标准 ### 1. 精度对比（前后） - 优化前后施加惩罚后的 logits 在相同输入下一致（数值误差 ≤ 1e-5）； - 与 vllm-core GPU 基线对齐； - 开启各惩罚组合（rep / freq / pres 及混合）的端到端输出与优化前一致（greedy + non-greedy）。 ### 2. 性能对比（前后） - 单算子 profiling：优化前后 kernel 延迟（多组 num_tokens / vocab_size / pos 长度）； - NPU profiler 时间线对比； - 端到端：开启惩罚场景下 decode 延迟对比。 ### 3. 交付件 - PR + 设计说明 + 精度对比表 + 性能数据 + 单测 ## 环境约定 - vllm-ascend：最新 main - 硬件：Ascend NPU（注明型号 + 卡数 + TP 配置） - 关联任务池：#9079 - 验收人：@chengduxiaowu ## 重点关注 - rep/freq/pres 各组合须与 GPU 基线逐位对齐； - 顺序循环消除后须保证 draft token bin count 结果一致。 ## 任务周期 * 发布：2026-08-12 * 回收：2026-10-31

title: [Contribution] [Perf][MRV2] bincount 算子性能优化
summary: ## 背景 MRV2 采样路径中，`bincount` 构建 prompt 的二进制 bitmask（`prompt_bin_mask`，标记 prompt 中出现过的 token）与输出 token 计数（`output_bin_counts`），供 `apply_penalties` 使用。Ascend 侧实现位于 `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/penalties.py`。 当前实现为 Triton kernel `_bincount_kernel`，grid `(num_tokens, num_blocks)`，`BLOCK_SIZE=1024`。kernel 通过 `tl.atomic_or` 写 bitmask（token_id // 32 为字索引，token_id % 32 为位），通过 `tl.atomic_add` 累加 output_bin_counts。两个原子操作在高并发下存在竞争。 存在以下可优化点： - `atomic_or`（bitmask）与 `atomic_add`（counts）原子操作竞争； - `BLOCK_SIZE=1024` 固定； - 每个 token 独立遍历 prompt，重复扫描可合并。 ## 任务 优化 `bincount` 在 Ascend NPU 上的性能。 - 路径：`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/penalties.py`（`_bincount_kernel` / `bincount`） - 方向：降低原子竞争（分块规约 / 私有副本合并）、BLOCK_SIZE 自适应、减少重复扫描 ## 验收标准 ### 1. 精度对比（前后） - 优化前后 `prompt_bin_mask` 与 `output_bin_counts` 在相同输入下完全一致（bitmask 位级一致、counts 整数一致）； - 与 vllm-core GPU 基线对齐； - 端到端（bincount + apply_penalties 联动）输出与优化前一致。 ### 2. 性能对比（前后） - 单算子 profiling：优化前后 kernel 延迟（多组 num_tokens / prompt_len / prefill_len）； - NPU profiler 时间线（原子操作开销）； - 端到端：开启惩罚场景下 decode 延迟对比。 ### 3. 交付件 - PR + 设计说明 + 精度对比表 + 性能数据 + 单测 ## 环境约定 - vllm-ascend：最新 main - 硬件：Ascend NPU（注明型号 + 卡数 + TP 配置） - 关联任务池：#9079 - 验收人：@chengduxiaowu ## 重点关注 - bitmask 为位级语义，优化不得改变任一位； - 原子规约合并后须保证 counts 正确。 ## 任务周期 * 发布：2026-08-12 * 回收：2026-10-31

title: [BugFix] Align Mamba checkpoint drop with the Ascend cache lookup policy

If an explicitly marked Mamba group still drops a checkpoint on write, its checkpoint boundary can disagree with the split boundary, preventing a common hybrid-cache hit. title: [Ops][Feature] Optimize Ascend PLE short conv with SD layout and spec kernel
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR is the follow-up to the Ascend PLE short-convolution work already merged for prefill (#20344), decode (#20643) and block-size tuning (#20697). Those changes kept the conv-state cache in the backend (DS) layout and still routed speculative (MTP) decode through the upstream `ple_conv`. This PR completes the optimization by keeping the conv-state in the SD layout (`[slot, window, channel]`, channel innermost) end-to-end and adding a Triton kernel for speculative decode. Concretely: 1. **Keep SD layout end-to-end, removing the per-call transpose.** Upstream canonicalizes the cache to the DS layout (`[slot, channel, window]`) before dispatch. On Ascend the Triton kernels are designed for channel-innermost access, so that transpose is wasted work and adds a full cache re-layout to the decode hot path. The vLLM-Ascend wrapper `_wrap_ple_short_conv` now replaces the upstream `Qwen4ExpPLELayer._short_conv` entirely: it canonicalizes the cache to SD (via `is_conv_state_dim_first()`), applies the same `state_capacity` validation/slicing, and dispatches directly to `_short_conv_dilated_dispatch`, whose `ple_conv` is bound to the Ascend kernels. title: [Bug] HCCL Error 19 during DeepSeek-V4-Flash initialization: Fixed by configuring loopback interface inside Docker container / 单机部署 HCCL Error 19 解决方案
summary: ### Your current environment # [Bug] HCCL Error 19 during DeepSeek-V4-Flash initialization: Fixed by configuring loopback interface inside Docker container / 单机部署 HCCL Error 19 解决方案 ## English ### Environment - Hardware: Ascend Atlas A3, single-node, 8 NPUs - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (W8A8) - Docker image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0` - Parallelism: TP8, EP8, DP1 - Docker network: `--net=host` - Network environment: Physically disconnected from external networks ### Problem During model initialization, after EP expert mapping and while initializing the W8A8 MoE quantization module, the worker crashed with: ```text RuntimeError: createHcclCommOrigin: ../torch_npu/csrc/distributed/ProcessGroupHCCL.cpp:3101 HCCL function error: hcclGetRootInfo(&hcclID), error code is 19 (call network api fail) ERR02200 DIST call hccl api failed ``` The failure occurred at: ```text vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/ w8a8_dynamic.py:169 backend.get_hccl_comm_name(local_rank) ``` ### Investigation The following approaches did not resolve the issue: 1. Connecting the physical network interface. 2. Setting `HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo` on the Docker host without passing it into the container. 3. Using Docker `--net=host` alone. The issue persisted with HCCL error code 19. ### Working Solution **Set the HCCL loopback interface inside the Docker container, before starting vLLM:** ```bash export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="lo" unset HCCL_IF_IP export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo vllm serve /data/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel ``` Alt

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Port V1 abort cleanup to MooncakeHybridConnector
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? When a decode request finishes before MooncakeHybridConnector dispatches its KV receive metadata, the connector does not notify the prefill node. P can retain the request's KV blocks until the delayed-free timeout (480 seconds by default). Port the existing MooncakeConnectorV1 cleanup to the hybrid connector: enqueue a notification-only empty receive from the request-finished hook, skip the data read, and send the existing DONE notification to P. Carry V1's awaiting_kvs/report_completion handling so notification-only tasks do not report a normal D-side receive completion. Keep already-dispatched transfers on their existing completion path. This is an interim connector-level fix. It does not cover cancellation before the D request reaches EngineCore. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Hybrid PD requests that reach the scheduler and finish before receive dispatch can notify P to release retained KV without waiting for the abort timeout. No new configuration or protocol is introduced. ### How was this patch tested? Extended worker tests to check notification-only completion, producer tracker cleanup without expiry, and propagation through both receive branches.
