title: [Kernel] Tune small-M block-FP8 Triton configs for NVIDIA L20
summary: ## Overview Add five NVIDIA L20 block-FP8 Triton configuration tables for small-M decode and numerical coverage in the existing kernel suite. Smaller M tiles reduce the wasted row computation of the generic BM64 configuration; N tiles and pipeline stages are selected per shape. This reuses the existing device/shape lookup. Kernel math and backend selection are unchanged. M1–32 uses the tuned entries; the M33 anchor preserves generic parameters for larger M. The tables apply only to matching L20/Triton shapes with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`. The tested Auto configuration selects Marlin, so these results do not establish an Auto-path speedup or superiority over Marlin. ## Claims On L20 TP1 with explicit Triton, the five tables improve 27B block-FP8 output throughput by 5.61%–29.85% across the measured 512/2048-token workloads at concurrency 1 and 8. The comparison uses stock Triton as its baseline. ## Validation **November 20 main rebase.** Base `efffc2a0bccb0d16f906fc0738835269fe3302e7`, PR head `0d13ffcc3ca16c94744c380a7ee51414795392d6`. title: [Quantization] Keep E8M0 scale bytes when loading into uint8 params
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item L6). Builds on #65235 (P1, load plan). MX scale parameters (compressed-tensors MXFP4/MXFP8, ModelOpt MXFP8, Quark OCP-MX, INC MXFP4/MXFP8) are `uint8`, and their loaders end in `copy_weight_`. When the source is `float8_e8m0fnu`, `copy_` converts it by value (2^(b-127) cast to an integer), which stores wrong scales. Under the load plan the same copy is a cast, so the name falls back, and the fallback stores the same wrong bytes. With this PR, `copy_weight_` copies between any two different **byte containers** as bytes (`src.view(dst.dtype)`). The parameter then holds the sent bytes, and because the load plan sees a view, the names are direct. The load plan also makes copy-time casts between real value formats direct (for example a BF16 checkpoint into an FP32 or `float8_e4m3fn` parameter): the planned copy replays the loader's by-value conversion into a destination in the parameter's dtype. Same-width integer casts (`int8` ↔ `uint8`) are byte copies there. This part is taken from #67836 by @aoshen02 and co-authored. - **Byte containers:** `uint8`, `int8`, `float8_e8m0fnu`, `float4_e2m1fn_x2`. They hold raw bytes, scales or packed data, so the bytes are the value. - **Covered pairs include:** - E8M0 scales into `uint8` params, and the reverse (a U8 checkpoint into Fp8's `float8_e8m0fnu` block scales); - `int8` ↔ `uint8`, e.g. DeepSeek-V4/V4.1-Flash I8 routed experts into Mxfp4MoEMethod's `uint8` params. `copy_` already gave the same bytes. title: [Feature][PP] Add bounded activation send buffering
summary: ## Overview Add opt-in bounded activation-send buffering for fixed-partition pipeline parallelism. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Report async EPLB worker failures to fault tolerance instead of stalling
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #66144. With `--enable-fault-tolerance`, an async EPLB worker exception is now reported to fault tolerance (FT) instead of silently stopping EPLB. ## Claims - Under FT, an exception in the async EPLB worker makes `step()` raise on every rank, through the #62009 path. Before, it raised nowhere: EPLB stopped for good and the engine stayed HEALTHY. - The worker thread still stays alive, so a `retry` can resume EPLB. `scale_down` redistributes the experts and then disables rebalancing (`eep_eplb_suppressed`). If no recovery arrives, the engine raises the original error and exits after `engine_recovery_timeout_sec` (existing FT behavior, not run end to end here). - `reset_eplb_async_state()` first waits for the worker to finish the cycle it is in, then clears the error, so recovery never resets the state or rebuilds the groups under a running cycle. A peer's worker blocked in a collective ends within `cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`; if the wait times out, the `retry` fails and can be sent again. The reset clears `rebalanced` before it changes the reset epoch, so a cycle that starts during the reset transfers nothing. - Docs: the fault-tolerance section of `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md` says an async EPLB worker error is a fault, and that `retry` resumes rebalancing unless an earlier `scale_down` disabled it. ## Validation - Unit tests in `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`. title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Compose ShardQ with the candidate-only indexer prefill
summary: I measured the candidate-path deployment (#65656) on 8xH20 with TP8: it takes 82.9 s at 1M tokens, and adding the V4.1 ShardQ prefill takes it to 49.9 s (-39.8%). Dense scoring with ShardQ is 51.5 s, so the combination keeps the candidate default and is 3.0% faster at 1M. ## Overview #65656 made the candidate-only indexer the SM90 default: the indexer scores candidate blocks instead of dense logits. It is faster, but at 1M tokens the indexer MQA logits are still 40.5% of GPU kernel time, and candidate-only is only 1.6% faster than dense-only prefill (82.9 vs 84.3 s), so the long-context prefill bottleneck remains. ShardQ token-shards the V4.1 sparse-MLA prefill: each TP rank takes a zigzag slice of the step's prefill tokens and runs the indexer and the sparse attention for those rows with all heads, with all-to-alls moving Q in and the output out. summary: ## Overview Currently, llm-d's precise KV-aware routing suffers from the fact it must hash incoming requests itself. title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Engram pool: split Engram tables across engines over NVLink or RDMA
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds `vllm/distributed/engram_pool/`, a pool of read-only tables split by rows over every GPU of a group of engines. Rows move over NVLink, or over RDMA from HBM or host memory. DeepSeek V4.1's cross-engine peer group (#66552) now runs on it and gains `peer_group_transport: nvlink | rdma`. Same goal as RFC #64002, #64395, #57023 and #64082 (one copy of the Engram tables shared across engines), different approach: no owner host or process, no native dependency (verbs through ctypes), NVLink and RDMA from HBM or host memory, and fetches fully capturable in CUDA graphs. Tracking issue: #57448. ## Design - **NVLink:** every GPU maps every shard (cuMem FABRIC); a fetch is one gather kernel. - **RDMA:** the owner's NIC gathers rows, ~15 rows (one packet) per RDMA WRITE, so fetches are not bound by the NIC's READ message rate. The requester's GPU writes the WRs and posts the request itself (mlx5 WQE + doorbell); a per-GPU owner proxy process posts them on its NIC. Each QP's last chain ends with a READ and a fenced flag WRITE, and the consumer kernel waits on the flags. A fetch is 2 kernels, with no host sync. - **Engines sharing NICs:** another engine's prefill could fill every owner QP and delay decode fetches (P/D in one group). `peer_group_rdma_inflight` (default 8) bounds prefill-sized gathers in flight per NIC. - **Host shards:** placed on the GPU's NUMA node. title: [Feature]: Transformers backend: gpt-oss experts are never fused, and MXFP4 raises NotImplementedError
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `--model-impl transformers` cannot serve `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4). It raises at construction: ``` NotImplementedError: Transformers modeling backend does not support MXFP4 quantization yet. ``` Removing that guard alone does not help: the model then fails in weight loading. The guard hides three separate gaps (reproduced on an A10G, Marlin MXFP4 backend, base `c5db9bd35f`): 1. **Experts are never fused.** `MoEMixin.recursive_replace` treats an experts module as packed only if all of its parameters are 3-D. gpt-oss experts also carry 2-D biases (`gate_up_proj_bias`, `down_proj_bias`), so the check fails and the HF experts stay in place. 2. **The checkpoint layout doesn't match `FusedMoE`.** gpt-oss ships `gate_up_proj_{blocks,scales,bias}` and `down_proj_{blocks,scales,bias}` with gate and up **interleaved**. The generic expert loader splits a fused `gate_up` tensor into halves (`chunk(2, dim=1)`), which would scramble them, and has no mapping for the `blocks`/`scales`/`bias` names. The blocks also need flattening to the `(E, N, K // 2)` shape `FusedMoE` expects. Native `gpt_oss.py` bypasses the generic loader for the same reason. 3. **Padded kernels return strided views.** Marlin MXFP4 pads `hidden_size`, and the `transformers_moe_forward` custom op then returns a non-contiguous view. I have a working patch (3 files, +93/−5) and will open a PR for it right after filing this. It supports gpt-oss MXFP4 at TP=1 / EP=1 and raises a clear `NotImplementedError` for TP>1 or EP>1. ### Alternatives Editing the shared `RoutedExperts.load_we

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Drop PCP padding-only rows from FlashMLA sparse FP8 decode metadata
summary: ## Overview With `--prefill-context-parallel-size > 1` (PCP) and the FlashMLA sparse FP8 KV cache (`fp8_ds_mla`), a decode step can crash and deadlock the engine when at least one PCP rank owns no decode request. PCP decode sharding assigns each decode request to a single PCP rank; the other ranks keep a zero-token collective placeholder row. The local batch is padded to the largest rank's token count, so on a FULL-cudagraph replay `num_actual_tokens` is the padded count (e.g. 1) while `query_start_loc` is all zeros. The FP8 separate prefill/decode metadata builder then computes `decode_query_len = 0` and `num_decode_tokens = 1`, and the pre-fix code fails at `assert decode_query_len > 0` (or divides by zero) on those ranks. The rank that owns the decode keeps going and enters the PCP collectives, so the workers deadlock and the engine core dies after the RPC timeout. I drop decode metadata for a batch whose rows carry no query token and make the FP8 forward return zeros for padding-only rows so every PCP rank still reaches the collectives. ## Claims - Fixes the crash and deadlock: a decode step where at least one PCP rank owns no request no longer asserts in the FP8 separate prefill/decode metadata builder, and every rank still reaches the PCP collectives. - No behavior change for batches where every PCP rank owns a token, for non-PCP batches, or for DCP (DCP>1 disables PCP decode sharding, so a padding-only rank cannot occur). - Adds regression coverage for the decode-row helper, the metadata builder, and the forward early return. ## Validation I validated on GLM-5.3 W4AF

title: [Bugfix] Keep the deferred MoE all-reduce on the naive AgRs path
summary: I hit this while running GLM-5.3 W4AFP8 (deepseek_v32) with expert parallelism and prefill context parallelism. title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: MXFP4 MoE on native routes and column-sharded at TP prefill, via AITER's two-stage API
summary: ## Overview Muse Spark normalizes each expert's output before the top-k weighted sum, so its MoE must return the unweighted per-route outputs `[T, top_k, H]`. On ROCm the MXFP4 experts get them by repeating the normed input `top_k` (8) times and calling AITER `fused_moe` with one route per row, and at TP > 1 every route's partial sums over all `H` columns are then reduce-scattered before the norm. This PR runs the experts through AITER's two-stage MoE API (ROCm/aiter#7135): - **Native routes.** One input row per token, on the `[T, top_k]` routes; stage 2 writes each route to its own row (`per_slot`). The kernels are the ones AITER selects for today's repeated-input call (`config_shape`), so the route outputs are bitwise identical. - **Column-sharded stage 2 at TP prefill.** For eager batches of ≥ 1024 tokens, the MXFP4 stage-1 output and its scales are all-gathered along the intermediate dim and stage 2 runs against this rank's `H / tp` output rows of `w2`. The norm then needs only a `[T, top_k]` sum-of-squares all-reduce and an all-gather of the finalized columns, instead of a `[T, top_k, H]` reduce-scatter. It replaces #63290 (native routes) and #63263 (column-sharded down projection), which reached into AITER internals (`_fused_moe_impl` with `_metadata_transform` and `_stage2_override`) and could not be combined. With the public API both are one code path. #63290 and #63263 are closed in favour of this PR. **Dependency.** Needs ROCm/aiter#7135, merged on 2026-11-18 (`ca7cfa1c3`) and not yet in an AITER release; vLLM's ROCm images use AITER 0.1.29. title: [RFC]: A top-level --lm-head-config for the draft and verify lm_head, with per-arch defaults
summary: Add one engine flag, `--lm-head-config`, that configures the target's (verify) lm_head and the drafter's copy of it, with an `auto` default resolved per arch. It replaces today's separate knobs: `draft_lm_head_quantization` in the speculative config and `lm_head` patterns in `quantization_config.targets`. ## Motivation On bandwidth-limited GPUs the drafter's full-vocabulary lm_head is the largest kernel in a draft step. A Qwen3.8-Flash-Next head is 248k x 2560 in BF16 (about 1.27 GB), and an MTP drafter reads it k times per step. The target still verifies with its own head, so a cheaper draft head can only change the acceptance length, never the output. Measured with #67236 on 1x DGX Spark (GB10, 273 GB/s), MTP k=3, SPEED-Bench qualitative, greedy, same-node pairs, BF16 head vs NVFP4 draft copy: | Model | Decode c=1 | AL c=1 | GSM8K (256) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 | 39.76 to 45.90 tok/s (+15.4%) | 2.668 to 2.636 | 247 / 247 | | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (BF16 head) | 66.46 to 91.85 tok/s (+38.2%) | 2.849 to 2.842 | 247 / 243 | Two levers act on this head (quantize it, or read fewer rows), and each new lever and drafter adds its own key. Users cannot tell which combination is right for their GPU and drafter. title: [Bugfix] kv_offload: fallback for memfd_create on standalone Python
summary: ## Overview Fixes #68625 by providing a multi-tier fallback for `memfd_create` when running on Python distributions without `os.memfd_create` (such as `uv`-managed `python-build-standalone`). ## Claims - Fixes `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'memfd_create'` when initializing CPU KV offload with multiple segments on standalone Python builds. - Provides fallback sequence: `os.memfd_create` -> `libc.memfd_create` via ctypes -> `libc.syscall` via ctypes -> anonymous shared `mmap(-1)`. ## Validation - Added unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`: - `test_create_memfd_fallback_when_os_missing` - `test_segmented_region_initializes_without_os_memfd_create` - `test_segmented_region_fallback_to_anonymous_mmap` - Verified code formatting and linting with `ruff check` and `ruff format`. ## Details Python standalone builds (e.g., from `uv` / `python-build-standalone`) are compiled against older glibc sysroots where `HAVE_MEMFD_CREATE` is not defined, so Python's `os` module omits `memfd_create`. When CPU KV offloading initializes a segmented region (`len(self._segments) > 1`), `SharedOffloadRegion` called `os.memfd_create` directly to create the reservation, failing with `AttributeError`. The host Linux kernel (>= 3.17) and libc (>= 2.27) almost universally support `memfd_create`. This change introduces `_create_memfd`: 1. First uses `os.memfd_create` if present. 2. Falls back to calling `libc.memfd_create` directly via ctypes. 3. Falls back to issuing the Linux system call (`sys_num` for x86_64, aarch64, riscv64, etc.) via `libc.syscall`. 4.

title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Generalize cache registration and payload layouts
summary: ## Overview Generalize MooncakeStore's rank-local cache registration to describe logical tensor components instead of relying on their allocation layout. This supports offset and strided views, grouped kernel blocks, and multiple components while preserving compact descriptors for adjacent regions. ## Claims - Describe each group's live bytes with separate addresses, strides, and transfer lengths. Skip empty components and remove covered aliases without copying neighboring components or padding. - Preserve component order and coalesce adjacent regions only when their strides and registered storage bounds match and the combined span fits within a block stride. - Use one registration path for device and host-resident groups, register each backing storage once when the Store owns registration, and stop startup if registration fails. Preserve shared PD TransferEngine registration ownership. - Use `torch.Event` and extensible configuration/setup methods; support documented environment overrides for the Store master and segment size. No hardware-specific branches are added. ## Validation ### Current revision: main sync and grouping reuse Commit `d01caf4ef8370fe1a2283ed3cee52b2c2e0eaa60` merges upstream main `700af4612915fe008fe1e0d8c97de23c57e3a1ac`. Rank-local registration now calls `group_kernel_blocks()` inside the layout; the worker groups only for other layouts. Upstream Store service/result validation and shared PD TransferEngine ownership are retained. No new skip or tolerance relaxation was added. Purpose

title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Offer the coarse prompt-end checkpoint to KV connectors

title: [Attention][FlashInfer] DiffusionGemma: mixed causal/bidirectional attention on TRTLLM-Gen, default for text-only SM100/SM103
summary: ## Overview DiffusionGemma batches mix causal requests (prompt and commit) with bidirectional requests (denoise). On SM100-family GPUs, vLLM had no fast backend for these batches: - FlashInfer rejected the model. - The default backend, FA4, fails at startup because its per-request causal mask is SM90-only. So B200 users had to pass `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`. This PR runs the mixed batches on FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen and makes that the default for text-only serving (`--language-model-only`) on SM100-family GPUs. It needs https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4905 (VariableWindow FMHA), which is in FlashInfer 0.7.3 and later (vLLM pins 0.7.4). **Scope:** SM100 family, text-only serving. Hopper and multimodal serving keep their current backend choice. ## Claims - **Perf:** 1.10–1.45× (BF16 KV) and 1.15–1.54× (FP8 KV) output tokens/s per GPU over `TRITON_ATTN` with BF16 KV, on 1×B200 at concurrency 1–8. - **Accuracy:** GPQA-Diamond scores 68.69 (BF16 KV) and 69.67 (FP8 KV), against 69.95 for `TRITON_ATTN`. - **Default:** `vllm serve <diffusiongemma> --language-model-only` now selects FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen on SM100 with no attention flag. Before this PR it failed to start. ## Validation Model `nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`, 1×B200, TP1, on `main` at `7dadcb647e` with FlashInfer 0.7.4 and vLLM's default block size. **Perf.** aiperf with SPEED-Bench 1K-throughput prompts: 32 requests per concurrency level, ISL ≈ 1.2K, OSL ≈ 3.1K, prefix caching off. Each cell is output tokens/s per GPU / per user, the mean of 3 runs. The per-GPU speedup is in parentheses.

title: [Bugfix][KDA] Fix fused_recurrent_kda output shape and 2D state-index strides in FLA recurrent kernels
summary: ## Overview Fixes #68415. Fixes #68416. Two bugs in the vendored FLA recurrent kernels, one commit each, plus a docstring-only commit. 1. `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` allocated its output with `torch.empty_like(k)`, but the recurrent kernel writes `HV` heads of width `V`. When `k` and `v` differ in head count or width, the output has the key shape, and when the value side is larger the kernel writes past it. The first commit allocates the output from `v`, keeping `k`'s dtype. 2. `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` and `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` pass `stride_indices_tok` to the kernel, but it loads the initial-state and final-state slots with `ssm_state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_seq + i_t`. A 2D index table whose token stride is not 1 therefore selects the wrong slots. The second commit multiplies the token index by `stride_indices_tok` in those four loads, the same change as fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1414. `fused_recurrent_kda` launches the same kernel and gets this fix too. Both are direct-operator bugs, and I have not found a serving path that hits them. `bailing_moe_v3.py`, the in-tree caller of this `fused_recurrent_kda`, passes `k` and `v` with the same head count and width. The GDN metadata builder (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`) makes the 2D spec-decode tables as unit-step slices of the block table, so their token stride is 1. ## Claims - `fused_recurrent_kda` returns an output with `v.shape`, for example `[1, 4, 1, 32]` for key width 64 and value width 32 (it was `[1, 4, 1, 64]`), and `[1, 4, 2, 32]` when `v` has two heads and `k` one.

title: [Feature][Sampling] Add native GPU output no-repeat n-gram masking
summary: ## Purpose Add an output-only no-repeat n-gram GPU logits-processor plug-in for Model Runner V2. The implementation scans the existing persistent GPU token history with one batched Triton kernel, avoiding the per-request Python processor's model-runner fallback. The processor is loaded through the existing custom logits-processor path with the FQCN `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.no_repeat_ngram:NoRepeatNGramState`; it is not registered in the built-in sampler list. It is available offline through `SamplingParams.extra_args` and online through `vllm_xargs`. It accepts: - `no_repeat_ngram_size`, with `ngram_size` as an OCR-integration compatibility alias; - `window_size`, which bounds the recent output-token history searched; - `whitelist_token_ids`, which keeps OCR grounding/control tokens available. Prompt tokens are deliberately excluded. Reused request slots are reset, invalid or out-of-vocabulary values fail closed, and speculative decoding is rejected when the plug-in is initialized. The DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, and multi-image OCR examples now load this GPU plug-in instead of registering the legacy per-request processor. For exact compatibility, the `ngram_size=1` alias preserves the legacy processor's no-op behavior, while canonical `no_repeat_ngram_size=1` retains standard unigram blocking semantics. ## Related work / duplicate check - #56497 provides the Model Runner V2 logits-processor lifecycle and request-state interface. title: [Perf][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graphs for the Qwen3-Omni / Qwen3-ASR audio tower

title: [Bugfix][Quantization][Model] Apply the quantization checkpoint mapper in the DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP loaders
summary: ## Overview Fixes #68627. An MTP head is loaded as a standalone draft model: `DefaultModelLoader` calls its hand-written `load_weights` directly, so `AutoWeightsLoader` — the only place that applies a quantization config's checkpoint mappers — never runs. title: [Model] Bidirectional spans on Gemma 4's sliding-window layers, without the window
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview #67710 applies bidirectional spans on full-attention layers only, and refuses a checkpoint that lists `sliding_attention` in `bidirectional_span_layer_types`. A window kept on the sliding-window layers would cut a span longer than the window. With this PR, a Gemma 4 checkpoint can list `sliding_attention` in `bidirectional_span_layer_types`, alone or with `full_attention`. vLLM then builds those sliding-window layers without a window, for every request on the checkpoint, and spans apply on them as on full-attention layers. The change is in the config check and in `Gemma4Attention`. The per-attention-group routing of #67709 and #67710 already gives the listed layers the spans and no image ranges, so nothing else in the engine changes. On Gemma 4 E2B and E4B, at TP=1 and TP=2, served answers match a transformers reference that applies the spans with no window. The cost is KV memory. On Gemma 4 31B, a token beyond the stock 1,024-token window costs 11 times as much KV memory as in the stock layout. Section 7 of RFC #67334 gives two consistent definitions of a span on a sliding-window layer, and this PR implements (a), in which a listed layer has no window. The branch also carries #67709 and #67710, and only the last commit, 252fd4cbf0, belongs to this PR. ## Claims - `bidirectional_span_layer_types` accepts `full_attention` and `sliding_attention`, alone or together. title: [Feature][Core] Request-level bidirectional attention spans
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview A token in a bidirectional attention span depends on the span's later tokens as well as its earlier ones. Serving spans therefore takes more than an attention mask, because a prefill chunk can't end inside a span, and a cached KV block is valid only for the spans it was computed under. This PR lets a request carry such spans, which are sorted and disjoint `[start, end)` ranges of the prompt whose tokens attend to each other in both directions on the layers that apply them, while everything else stays causal. A checkpoint declares those layer types in its text config, and Gemma 4 applies spans on its full-attention layers. On `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` with spans declared through `hf_overrides`, served next-token distributions match a transformers reference built from the same masks at span lengths of 64, 1,024 and 2,048 tokens, with prefix caching and chunked prefill on. This PR is the core part of RFC #67334. It has the engine, offline `TokensPrompt` support and Gemma 4, and #67711 adds the `bidirectional_spans` field to the OpenAI-compatible APIs. The branch also carries #67709. The last three commits belong to this PR: the feature, a tighter TP=2 check in the pooling test, and a refusal of spans whose multimodal items don't fit the encoder cache together. ## Claims - A Gemma 4 checkpoint that declares spans is served with them, both offline and when the code that renders a prompt sets spans on the engine input, multimodal inputs included. title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #68725. When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks. That ordering is the bug: - A host prefix hit needs the GPU indexer blocks; a copy only speeds up a hit that also finds them. - A long request leaves about 1 indexer block and several resident copies per page. - Later requests' copies therefore outlive earlier prefixes' indexer blocks, and re-sent prompts miss far below host-pool capacity. The fix adds a retained tier to `BlockPool`, a second free queue. Copies that no live request reads go there, and allocation now takes uncached free blocks first, then retained blocks, then prefix-cached blocks. With no retained blocks, `get_new_blocks` takes the existing path unchanged. Alternative considered: putting copies at the queue head. It also fixes the loss, but every copy dies at the next allocation, so copy reuse drops to zero. In a 10k-block simulation: | Re-send lag | main | head | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | 2 requests | 4720 | 0 | 4720 | | 10 requests | 4400 | 0 | 3494 | ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse pytest tests/v1/core/ ``` `test_hisparse_finished_copies_do_not_evict_older_prefix` fails on main and passes here. ## Test Result **Unit tests** - HiSparse tests pass. - `tests/v1/core/` has the same set of failures as main. title: [Bugfix][MLA] Prevent SM90 sparse MLA planner work-list overflow
summary: ## Overview Large sparse MQA steps can exceed FlashInfer 0.7.4's 16,384-work-item SM90 planner limit. Split the rows across independent plans, then reserve those plans before the engine determines how much GPU memory it can use for KV. This revision is `7111c2f5`, based on `0ae7032d`, and retains Simon Veitner's four review commits. ## Changes - Bound the rows per plan using `8192 // ceil(num_heads / 64)`. Partially filled plans can select the 64-head tile. Apply each chunk's global row offset to KV lengths and allocate the tail for the remaining rows. - Use the same plan/run loop for one chunk and for several. The chunks share a 128 MiB float workspace and keep their own indices and integer-plan buffers. The backend handles this independently of scheduler chunked prefill. - Once the worker knows its KV layout and layer groups, prepare each configured chunk with one valid row before KV sizing. FlashInfer materializes device and pinned host storage on the first plan. Reuse those GPU buffers for graph profiling, warmup and serving. Each microbatch gets private mutable state. title: [Rust Frontend][EPD] Token-level EPD handoff over gRPC Generate
summary: ## Motivation EPD (encoder disaggregation) runs the multimodal encoder on separate instances (E) and hands its output to the prefill/decode instances. Besides the embeddings, which the EC connector moves, P/D needs the expanded prompt, each item's placeholder range and identity, and a few CPU-side kwargs that the model still reads when it skips the encoder (for example Qwen's `image_grid_thw` for M-RoPE). Today the only EPD path in vLLM is chat-level. The example proxy sends E a chat request, E's EC connector echoes the model's metadata as JSON inside `ec_transfer_params`, and the proxy rewrites each image into a metadata-only `image_embeds` part for PD. PD then renders the chat again and rebuilds every placeholder from that metadata with per-model rules. The layout is computed twice, the metadata takes a lossy MessagePack → JSON → tensor round trip, and internal handoff fields live on a user-facing API. The token-level interface already has the right shape for this: `GenerateRequest.media` accepts engine-ready `PreprocessedMediaFeatures` (MessagePack `kwargs`) that a version-compatible frontend produced and the caller carries opaquely. Two pieces were missing for EPD. E's reply did not return the layout, and a consumer could not accept features that carry no encoder input. This PR adds those two pieces for gRPC `Generate`, so a router that renders prompts itself can run E → P/PD (→ D) without any instance re-deriving the layout. E's output and P/D's input are the same message, and the router never parses kwargs or applies model rules. ## What this PR does - **First commit:

title: [RFC] [DSV4.1] [Engram]: Share immutable host-backed Engram tables across independent instances
summary: ## Motivation: Engram host offload alone is not enough. * Engram host offload saves accelerator memory, but independently launched serving instances can still keep separate copies of the same large immutable tables. * This is particularly expensive for prefill/decode deployments with different TP layouts. Sharing inside one instance's DP group does not eliminate these cross-instance copies. * Additionally, when deployed with KVcache Pool (such as Mooncake), DRAM fragments will lead to engine OOM. We propose separating **table ownership and physical placement** from **the instances that perform lookups**. A persistent owner publishes one table generation. Independent workers attach the head ranges they need and run lookup kernels against device-accessible mappings of that backing. Selected rows and model activations remain local to each worker. ## Tracking PRs ### vLLM - [ ] [#64082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64082), cross-instance shared host tables. - [ ] [#64395](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64395), GPU-initiated RDMA GET for Engram sharing. - [x] [#66552](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66552), cross-engine GPU table sharding. - [ ] [#67539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67539), Engram pool over NVLink or RDMA. - [ ] [#68684](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68684), Qwen FP8 PLE sharing over NVLink and RDMA (draft). - [ ] [#68685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68685), Grace EGM backing for NVLink Engram pool shards (draft). ### vLLM-Ascend - [ ] [#21246](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pu

title: [RFC]: Optional weight staging and trainer-managed pause for weight transfer engines
summary: ### Motivation. Some weight sync strategies need more from the weight transfer API than it offers today. They split an update into **fetching** the new weights (slow, safe while serving) and **applying** them (faster, needs a pause): - **ModelExpress** already splits its client into `stage_weight()` (for example S3 delta download and decode) and `apply_weight()`. Its vLLM backend has to call both inside `update_weights`, while paused. - **vime disk-delta** patches vLLM with a `pull_weights` worker RPC so it can fetch to local NVMe before pausing. - **CoreWeave's RL rollouts** (built on ModelExpress S3-delta) run a separate background prefetcher process for the same reason. - **humans&** (on SGLang) reports a ~220 ms pause out of a ~4 s sync by decoding into pinned host memory while rollout continues. vLLM can't express this today. Pause/resume is entirely up to the caller, and no engine-side call is promised to be safe while serving: every weight-sync RPC runs inline on the EngineCore busy loop and each worker's main loop, so even an "unpaused" call stalls generation. The in-tree engines don't need the split, since their transfers are fast enough to fit inside the pause. This RFC proposes one optional, engine-side staging step that is guaranteed to overlap with generation, and moving pause/resume into the trainer-side `send_weights` so each backend pauses only for the apply. title: [Bugfix] Don't re-append default custom ops on every `replace()`
summary: Update: a second commit (1a21913) widens the fix after a review pass. It adds `CompilationConfig.enable_custom_op_by_default()`, uses it for the `quant_fp8` default and in the ROCm platform defaults, which had the same problem, and deletes the duplicate `quant_fp8` block in `__post_init__`. The sections below describe both commits. ## Overview `VllmConfig.__post_init__` writes default custom ops into `compilation_config.custom_ops`, and `replace()` re-runs it on a copy that shares the same `CompilationConfig`. Those writes weren't idempotent. The blocked-FP8 `+quant_fp8` default was appended on every run, from two identical blocks, and on ROCm `apply_config_platform_defaults` appended `+sparse_attn_indexer` (and, depending on the AITER and batch-invariance settings, `+quant_fp8` and `+rms_norm`) again on every run. So the compile hash of a config changed every time it was copied. This PR adds `CompilationConfig.enable_custom_op_by_default(op)`, which enables `op` unless `custom_ops` already enables or disables it. The `quant_fp8` default and all five ROCm defaults use it, and the second `quant_fp8` block is gone. ## Claims - For a blocked-FP8 config, `compile_factors()` is the same before and after `replace()`, for the copy and for the original. - `flashinfer_autotune_cache_hash` returns the same name every time it is called on a runner. - The same holds on ROCm, where the platform defaults now go through the same method. title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Fix MiniCPM5XMLToolParser streaming tag leaks and dropped blocks
summary: ## Purpose `MiniCPM5XMLToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` leaks raw XML into `content` and drops tool calls when a delta does not line up with tag boundaries: 1. **Split `<function` tag leaks.** When a chunk ends inside `<function` (e.g. `<` or `<functio`), the fast path emits it as content and advances `_processed_len`, so the next chunk no longer sees `<function` and the whole block streams as plain text. The existing `test_extract_tool_calls_streaming_single` shows this: the raw `<function ...>...</function` block ends up in `other_content`. 2. **Early returns drop content.** The loop returns on the first prose gap or right after the first complete block, so the rest of a delta that carries prose plus several blocks is lost. This happens with `--stream-interval > 1` and with speculative decoding. ## Changes - Hold back a possible `<function` prefix with `partial_tag_overlap` instead of emitting it as content. - Process every complete `<function>...</function>` block and the prose between them in one pass, then handle the remainder once: an unfinished block is held until it closes or generation ends. - Emit a tool call only after `_parse_function_block` accepts the completed block. A rejected block (e.g. missing a required parameter) is returned as content and never opens a call with non-JSON arguments, for every chunk split. - `DelegatingParser.finalize_generation` calls `finish_streaming` on a non-engine tool parser, so text held back as a possible prefix (`<`, `<fun`, `<function later.`) is flushed when `parse_delta(..., finished=True)`. ## Test Plan ```bash pyte

title: [Feature][Core] Size prefill chunks from a step-time budget.
summary: ## Overview Add an opt-in scheduler that sizes each prefill chunk from a measured step-time budget instead of a fixed token cap. Enable it with `--scheduler-cls prefill_budget.scheduler.TimeBudgetScheduler` and `async_scheduling=False`. ## Claims - After a short warmup, the scheduler fits `cost(q, c) = a q² + b q c + g q + d` from completed steps on the current GPU and chooses the largest chunk `q` whose predicted time stays within the budget. - On one GPU with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct`, a 60 ms budget held the median step at 55.0 ms (p90 62.6 ms) while a fixed 1024-token chunk in the same prefix range took 80.0 ms (p90 84.4 ms). - The chunk shrank as the prefix grew: median 704 tokens in the first half of the budget phase, 576 in the second. ## Validation Single GPU, eager mode, prefix caching off, async scheduling off, `max_num_seqs=1`. ```bash python -m prefill_budget.bench \ --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct \ --budget-ms 60 \ --warmup-steps 4 \ --prompt-tokens 8000 \ --max-model-len 8192 ``` result of the run: fixed : steps=6 c=2048..7168 q median=1024 step_ms median=80.0 p90=84.4 budget: steps=10 c=1920..7680 q median=640 step_ms median=55.0 p90=62.6 budget median step 55.0 ms, target 60.0 ms budget chunk median early=704 late=576 chunk shrank as the prefix grew ## Details --- <details> vLLM's scheduler already caps a prefill with long_prefill_token_threshold. This subclass only replaces that cap. The first warmup chunks are forced through a spread of sizes so the fit sees both short and long chunks. The step time is the gap from the end of one schedule() to the start

title: [ROCm] gfx950: use aiter.mqa_logits for the sparse indexer prefill
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On gfx950, this PR enables AITER's shape-dispatched `aiter.mqa_logits` ([ROCm/aiter#6185](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6185)) for the sparse indexer prefill logits (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`). AITER picks the Triton/Gluon or FlyDSL kernel per shape from its tuned table, so vLLM no longer needs a change each time the best prefill kernel moves (as [#59280](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59280) did for FlyDSL). This is an enablement change, not an end-to-end speedup: GLM-5.3 throughput and accuracy are unchanged within noise, and 128k c1 TTFT is +1.9% (below). The AITER that vLLM pins (v0.1.29, [#66596](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66596)) includes [ROCm/aiter#6185](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6185), so this path is live on main. ## Claims - gfx950 + AITER: the prefill indexer logits go through `aiter.mqa_logits`. - Tuned for GLM-5; other shapes keep Triton/Gluon. title: [ROCm] Use aiter.paged_mqa_logits for the sparse indexer decode logits
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On ROCm, this PR enables AITER's shape-dispatched `aiter.paged_mqa_logits` ([ROCm/aiter#6140](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6140)) for the sparse indexer decode logits (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`). title: [Attention] Run SM90 FP8-KV attention on FA4 native FP8
summary: ## Overview On SM90 with an FP8 KV cache, this PR runs attention on FA4's native FP8 forward from vllm-project/flash-attention#206, which computes attention on E4M3 Q/K/V with FP8 WGMMA: - **FA3 → FA4 upgrade.** `get_flash_attn_version` upgrades FA3 to FA4 on SM90 when the KV cache is FP8 E4M3 and FA4 supports the head size: 64, 96, 128, 192 or 256, with the same V head size, no softcap and no batch invariance. An explicitly set `flash_attn_version` is kept. - **Gemma4 on FA4 for all layers.** With an FP8 KV cache on SM90, `main` runs Gemma4's sliding-window layers on FA3 and its full-attention layers on FA4. This PR uses FA4 for all layers, as Gemma4 already does in other configurations: - **Sliding-window layers (head dim 256)** quantize Q to FP8, as FA3 does, and run FA4's native FP8 forward. - **Full-attention layers (head dim 512)** keep `main`'s FA4 FP8-KV path with BF16 Q. The FlashAttention pin is bumped once vllm-project/flash-attention#206 merges. ## Claims - **Faster.** On gemma-4-31B-it-FP8 on H200, output throughput is 1.20x `main` on the `8k-in-1k-out` benchmark of [`gemma_4_31b_it_h200`](https://github.com/vllm-project/perf-eval/blob/main/workloads/gemma_4_31b_it_h200.yaml). `main` runs with its pinned FlashAttention commit, and this PR with vllm-project/flash-attention#206, which is based on that same commit. - **Accuracy-neutral.** GPQA Diamond, AIME 2025, MMLU-Pro and GSM8k all match `main` and BF16 within noise. ## Validation **Serving.** The `8k-in-1k-out` benchmark of [`gemma_4_31b_it_h200`](https://github.com/vllm-project/perf-eval/blob/main/workloads/

title: [ROCm][Qwen3.8-Flash-Next] Specialized decode: MTP verify steps
summary: ## Overview **Stacked on #65188** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next `--monokernel` decode at 1-192 rows), on its head `294644b81e`; until it merges the compare view shows its commits too. title: [Feat] [AMD] ultraquant: Add MTP verify decode
summary: ## Purpose UltraQuant decode already ships. MTP verification did not reach it: on current `main` the TurboQuant metadata builder opts out of spec-as-decode, so a k-token verify is classified as a prefill and never enters the UltraQuant decode kernel. This PR keeps an MTP verify on the UltraQuant decode path and scores it with the shipping FlyDSL kernel. - Width 1 is today's single-token decode. - Widths 2–8 are the same kernel, compiled as the four-wave schedule in `ultraquant_decode_hd256.py`. One read of each KV tile scores the verify. Qwen3.8-27B is query group 6. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B at TP=4 is query group 8 per rank. Both are head size 256 with MTP k=5, so a verify step is 6 tokens. - A width outside 2–8, or a batch that is not eligible, falls back to one single-token launch per verify token. There is no environment variable and no second kernel file. The wide path is the default when the query length is in 2–8. The 4-bit cache format is unchanged: FP4 E2M1 codes, UE8M0 per-group scales, Hadamard-rotated keys. See [UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20474). ## Design - `UltraQuantMetadataBuilder` subclasses `TurboQuantMetadataBuilder` and opts into spec-as-decode. A pure verify batch stays a decode: `is_prefill` is set from whether any request is a prefill, not from `max_query_len > 1`. - `num_verify_tokens` comes from `max_query_len`. A ragged batch such as `[2, 4]` is not collapsed to one width. Each request is masked with `query_start_loc`. - `build_ultraquant_decode_hd256_module` takes `num_verify_tokens`. Width 1 compile

title: [ROCm][Perf][Mistral] Overlap MLA cache write and query prep with the indexer for Mistral Large 4
summary: ## Overview This ports the `mqa_q_prepared` overlap from the NVIDIA ML4 attention (#64534) to `mistral/amd/attention.py`. The KV-cache write, W_UK absorption and FP8 query quant now run on the main stream while the indexer runs on the aux stream, instead of after the join. The ROCm sparse backend takes a bf16 `(ql_nope, q_pe)` tuple and quantizes it inside `forward_mqa`. So this also adds a small `MLAAttentionImpl.prepare_mqa_query` hook, which lets `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` do its concat+quant early. Without the hook, the quant stays after the join and the gain is less than half. title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3] Select the whole-layer mono decode with --monokernel and remove mono/envs.py
summary: ## Purpose The ROCm MiniMax-M3 mono decode (#64111) and DSpark drafter kernels (#65386) were switched on by model-specific env vars in `mono/envs.py`. Every other monokernel uses `--monokernel` (equivalently `additional_config: {"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}`), including the MiniMax-M3 FFN-only decode (#62712). This removes `envs.py`. `--monokernel` now runs every MiniMax-M3 monokernel the deployment fits: - Decode: the whole-layer mono decode if it fits (MXFP8 attention as in M3.1, FP8 KV and indexer caches, the AITER sparse PA path, 256 CUs, no weight transfer), otherwise the FFN-only decode (BF16 attention, as in M3). - Draft: the DSpark drafter kernels (7-token DSpark, TP4). - If none fit, startup fails and lists every reason. The whole-layer conditions are checked at startup, so a deployment that can't run it falls through to the next kernel instead of silently running the stock path after warmup. title: [HiSparse] Batch owner bookkeeping when unpinning pages
summary: ## Purpose Cut the HiSparse coordinator's per-block Python work when a request's resident pages are unpinned. Importing a long multi-turn prefix in P/D, as in #65888, adopts the GPU copies of about 1,250 pages × 20 resident groups, then unpins them on the next step. Unpinning built one owner `set` and one `(request, page)` tuple per block, about 50k long-lived objects per import. On 8×B200 with #65888, that's about 12 ms of a 17.7 ms `schedule()` step, plus full-GC spikes of up to 76 ms. Changes, all in `vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`: - `_owners` maps a block to a tuple of owners. A page's blocks share one 1-tuple, so a single-owner block (the common case) costs no allocation. - `_unpin_pages` finds null pages once per column and updates page state once per page. Release order is unchanged: page-major, tail first. - The block-reuse watcher is bound once. Each unpin used to pass a new bound method, which `BlockPool` keeps per block. - `_discard_owner` replaces the per-call `set.discard` in `_lose_page` and `free`. No behaviour change. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_stats.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py ``` CPU micro-benchmark at real size (1,250 pages × 20 resident groups, real coordinator and block pool), this PR vs `main`. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] gfx1250 W4A4 MoE: fused silu + fused quant + preshuffled weights
summary: ## Purpose On gfx1250, the AITER W4A4 MoE path (`--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_mxfp4`, `AiterW4A4ExpertsMonolithic`) runs SILU models such as DeepSeek-V4 through four kernels per MoE layer: GEMM1 with a bf16 output, `fused_clamp_act_mul`, a separate `mxfp4_quant` of the intermediate, then GEMM2. It also forces routing off TDM and gathers the input rows before GEMM1. This PR runs SILU through the fused path AITER already provides for SWIGLUOAI, and always uses preshuffled weights: - **Fused epilogue:** GEMM1 applies SiLU (with the clamp) in its epilogue and writes MXFP4 directly (`apply_swiglu=True, out_mx_quant=True`). Nothing runs between the two MoE GEMMs. - **Routing and gather:** routing keeps TDM on, and GEMM1 gathers rows itself (`gather_indx`) instead of a separate pre-gather. - **Preshuffled weights:** SILU weights are always preshuffled into the WMMA 16x16 tile order (`preshuffle_weights=True`). This is faster, and it also fixes correctness: with non-preshuffled weights, the gluon `moe_gemm_a4w4` kernel returns intermittent garbage on identical inputs at some tile configs (details below). The preshuffled kernel never did in our tests. On DeepSeek-V4 this restores gsm8k accuracy on gfx1250. Code changes: - `oracle/mxfp4.py`: in the `AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_MXFP4` weight prep, SILU joins SWIGLUOAI in the gate/up row interleave, which the fused epilogue reads. This is the only change to `convert_gpt_oss_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format`. - `experts/aiter_mxfp4_w4a4_moe.py`: - `AiterW4A4ExpertsMonolithic.__init__` sets `preshuffle_weights` for SILU. - The new `process_w

title: [Performance]: Tiny-window SlidingWindowSpec conv state dominates per-request KV accounting via the in-flight admission reserve
summary: ## Summary Hybrid models that expose per-token short-conv state as a tiny-window `SlidingWindowSpec` (Inkling: `sliding_window = block_size = kernel_size = 4`) are charged an admission reserve of `cdiv(window - 1 + max_in_flight_tokens, block_size) + 1` blocks per request per KV cache group. With async scheduling, `max_in_flight_tokens = 2 * max_num_batched_tokens`; at the `vllm serve` default on this hardware class (16,384 batched tokens on >=160 GiB GPUs; smaller GPUs default lower) that is 8,194 blocks per conv group per request, and across Inkling's 6 conv groups it is 84% of all per-request blocks. The charge covers dtype-pinned bf16 state and is independent of `kv_cache_dtype`, so it mutes the capacity gain of any KV compression: fp8 KV cache halves every attention KV byte but the pool capacity figure improves only +8.6% at defaults (versus +73% at 1M `max_model_len` with 2,048-token chunks, same memory). The numbers below were reproduced exactly through vLLM's own `get_kv_cache_configs` / `get_kv_cache_capacity`: the reconstruction matches both servers' logged token counts to the token and their logged concurrency figures, with a single scanned free parameter (`available_memory`, which the server logs rounded to 0.01 GiB). ## Environment - vLLM v0.28.0 (release), PyTorch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1 - 1x host with 8x B200 (SM100, 183 GB); two independent 4-GPU servers, TP4: `kv_cache_dtype=auto` (bf16) and `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` - Model: Inkling-Small (in-tree, `vllm/models/inkling`), 276B total / 12B active MoE, 42 layers (35 sliding-window-512 + 7 global attention), one scon

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] Use AITER tuned GEMM for the Router GEMM on gfx1250
summary: ## Purpose On gfx1250, `GateLinear` sends the BF16 MoE router GEMM to `torch.mm(x, w.T, out_dtype=torch.float32)`, which runs on hipBLASLt. At router shapes the hipBLASLt kernel it picks takes 0.45–0.85 ms per call at any M. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro (61 MoE layers) that adds about 49 ms to every decode step. This PR sends gfx1250 through the dispatch gfx950 already uses. title: [Frontend] [Core] Streaming session API supporting infinite continuous video inputs
summary: ## Purpose Complete bounded streaming sessions for RFC #51948, combining the KV eviction primitive, retention/consolidation core (#53871, #53876), and session frontend in one PR. The implementation targets Model Runner V2 and reuses the streaming-input lifecycle fixes already merged into main. Long-running sessions retain the task prompt and a bounded window of frames and replies. Old KV is evicted while the request stays alive; retained context is rebuilt and replayed before positions overflow. Rebuilding removes fragments and replies belonging to discarded frames while preserving per-frame text. The frontend is gated behind `--enable-streaming`, off by default. Sessions also close on client disconnect and engine error. The session layer is a thin adapter over `AsyncLLM.generate(stream)`. summary: ## Purpose Fix #49122 — `rhymes-ai/Aria` (`AriaForConditionalGeneration`) generates incoherent garbage at `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, with coherence degrading proportionally to TP size (coherent at TP=1, partially degraded at TP=2, fully garbage at TP=4). **Root cause: the shared-experts output is all-reduced twice.** `AriaTextMoELayer` passes its shared-experts `LlamaMLP` into `FusedMoE(shared_experts=...)`. The `MoERunner` contract is that it performs the tensor-parallel reduction itself, exactly once (see the note in `moe_runner.py` — either the combine kernel reduces `fused_output` and the runner then all-reduces `shared_output` separately in `_maybe_reduce_shared_expert_output`, or neither is reduced and the runner all-reduces `shared_output + fused_output` in `_maybe_reduce_final_output`). The shared-experts module must therefore return **unreduced per-rank partial sums**. Aria constructed `LlamaMLP` without `reduce_results=False`, so its `RowParallelLinear` down-projection all-reduced its output first, and the runner reduced it again — scaling the shared-expert contribution by `tp_size`. This is invisible at TP=1 (all-reduce over one rank is the identity) and corrupts the residual stream progressively as TP grows, exactly matching the symptom table in the issue. Every other in-tree model that passes `shared_experts` to `FusedMoE` already constructs it with `reduce_results=False`: `deepseek_v2`, `glm4_moe`, `ernie45_moe`, `bailing_moe`, `bailing_moe_linear`, `hunyuan_v1`, `afmoe`, `exaone_moe`, and `cohere2_moe` (via its MLP's default). title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950 device length aware top-k split policy for k=2048
summary: This fixes #55327. The change generalizes `topKPerRowDecodeGfx950DeviceLengthAware` to work with different values of k, and adds `gfx950TopK2048ActiveBlocks`. The grid still only depends on `numRows`, so graph capture stays stable, and the number of splits is now determined on device per row, ensuring that there are at least 2048 real indices in each split. Rows under 4096 can be processed by a single block, skipping the merge step. GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 use `index_topk` 2048, which goes through the generic path on gfx950 and has 10 splits. In the merge step, all 20480 candidates are processed by a single block for each row. For rows with fewer active tokens this can lead to significant overhead. With this PR, the number of candidates per row in the merge step will be reduced to between 0 and 12288, a 70 percent reduction in the median case. I also added two new tests for gfx950 and k 2048, to make sure we're covering the different numbers of splits and graph capture and replay. I've checked this with a CPU model on all 35 shapes mentioned in the issue, and the result is an exact match with exact top-k for all of them. The kernel compiles fine for gfx950, and I'll provide timings on MI355X in this PR. AI-disclosure: Drafted with tooling. Planned, tested, checked and finalised by me.

title: [Bug]: CUTLASS 3.x scaled_mm ignores leading strides of sliced tensors
summary: ### Your current environment ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H800 PCIe (SM90) - Driver: 580.82.07 - CUDA runtime/toolkit: 13.0 - Python: 3.12 - PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 - Released build: official vLLM 0.28.0 wheel - Source build: vLLM main at `a69e75b9b6d6a26d90b6790e2eb75b3419a47c16` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary `torch.ops._C.cutlass_scaled_mm` silently returns incorrect results on the CUTLASS 3.x path when otherwise-valid A, B, or output tensors have a padded leading dimension. The operator entry point accepts these layouts: it requires `a.stride(1) == 1`, `b.stride(0) == 1`, and `c.stride(1) == 1`, but does not require tightly packed leading dimensions. However, the C3x caller reconstructs packed strides from tensor shapes and discards the tensors' actual leading strides. I reproduced this on both the official vLLM 0.28.0 wheel and main at commit `a69e75b9b6d6a26d90b6790e2eb75b3419a47c16`, on an NVIDIA H800 (SM90). This is a correctness issue rather than a tolerance issue: separate A-only, B-only, and output-only padding controls each produce about 8.1% mismatched elements. A minimal fix that passes the actual leading dimensions to CUTLASS reduces all five cases below to zero mismatches. ## Reproduction The reproducer creates 512x512 views backed by 1024x1024 allocations: ```python import torch torch.manual_seed(0) def to_int8(x): return torch.round(x.clamp(-128, 127)).to(torch.int8) whole_a = to_int8(torch.randn((1024, 1024), device="cuda") * 5) whole_b = to_int8(torch.randn((1024, 1024), device="cuda").t() * 5) a = whole_a[:512, :512] # stride (1024, 1) b = whole_b[:512

summary: ## Overview Preserve in-flight prefill reservations when HiSparse uses spare GPU blocks to bring historical KV pages back from the host after an async import. ## Details The scheduler reserves enough blocks for in-flight prefills when it admits an async KV load. This is a budget check. The reserved capacity still appears in the GPU pool's free-block count. Later, when the worker reports that the import has finished, `_promote_imported_pages` checks the free count against the HiSparse transition watermark alone. title: [NIXL] Bound the READ descriptor runs each pull worker posts per step
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Add an opt-in `max_read_runs_per_step` option to `kv_connector_extra_config`. It bounds how much NIXL READ work each pull (decode) worker posts per engine step. Posting a READ is synchronous on the model-execution thread. With data parallelism, one rank posting a long-prompt READ makes every rank wait at the next DP synchronization. Related, complementary work: #45211 and #57987 (READ lifecycle off the forward thread), #61638 (completion polling off-thread), #55841 (contiguous KV block runs), #66970 / #60851 (whole-row descriptors), #65639 (same-host stream-ordered CUDA IPC pulls), ai-dynamo/nixl#2618 (UCX SGL for multi-descriptor READs). No open PR limits how much READ work a step posts. The PRs above move posting to another thread or cut the number of runs; they do not split a READ across steps. ## Claims - On a DP8 decode instance fed by a DP2 prefill instance (agentic multi-turn replay at concurrency 224), `max_read_runs_per_step=1000` cuts mean ITL from 8.79 ms to 2.24 ms (p99 39.1 → 2.79 ms) and raises output throughput by 24.5 % (2,603 → 3,242 tok/s). Mean TTFT is no worse (23.9 → 21.7 s). - Default `0` keeps the current behaviour: every READ is posted whole as soon as it is ready. - A sliced READ notifies the prefiller once, after its last slice completes. The same deferred-notification path is already used for split DRAM/VRAM reads. A failed slice stops the remaining slices and suppresses the notification. ## Validation **Unit tests** at commit `f4c0f7051`. The PR's Python sources were run over a main `8ca766326` CUDA build

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Skip GPU restores for cancelled KV imports
summary: ## Overview Skip HiSparse host-to-device restores when an external KV receive completes after its request has been cancelled. A successful receive can still publish the completed host prefix. ## Details Cancellation removes the request from the HiSparse connector's live-request map. Its landing blocks stay allocated until the outstanding receive completes. Previously, a successful receive acknowledgment caused the coordinator to schedule the tail restore and promote eligible historical pages even after the request had been removed. Those transfers pinned GPU blocks until another worker acknowledgment, although the request could no longer consume the restored KV. At receive completion, use the connector's existing live-request map to decide whether to schedule restores. For a cancelled request, advance the GPU-copy indexing cursor past the imported prefix. This lets host prefix publication proceed without advertising a GPU landing block that the worker never filled. If a restore was already submitted before cancellation, its endpoints remain pinned until the worker acknowledges completion. ## Claims A CPU reproduction using the scheduler, MultiConnector and three HiSparse resident groups produced the following results on successful receive completion. | Request state at receive completion | Base | This change | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Live request, restores queued | 4 | 4 | | Cancelled request, restores queued | 4 | 0 | | Cancelled request, GPU block references held by these restores | 12 | 0 | Both fixes can land independently. title: [Perf][Attention] Run PrefixLM steps as FlashAttention 4 varlen rows on Hopper
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On Hopper, prefill steps that apply PrefixLM ranges are slow. These ranges are multimodal items, or the bidirectional spans added in #67710. #67710 serves span layers with the `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` composite, whose Triton PrefixLM kernel costs 8.6 to 9.9 times causal attention on an 8K prefill. title: [Perf][V2] Pool AsyncOutput's D2H copy events instead of creating them every step
summary: ## Overview Pool the CUDA events that the V2 model runner's `AsyncOutput` creates every step to order and complete its D2H copy. #39115 fixed a race from reusing one copy event across steps by creating a new event every step, and noted the events could be pooled later if needed. This PR is that pool. It is safe against the same race because an event pair goes back to the pool only after `get_output()` has synchronized on it. Why it matters: these are driver calls on the execute-model thread. When another thread in the process holds the CUDA driver lock for a long time, for example a KV connector posting many CUDA IPC copies from a background thread, these calls wait behind it. With data parallelism, every rank then waits for the late rank. Related: - #39115: the per-step events this replaces. - #57987, #45211: move NIXL READ posting to a background thread. That is the setting where this contention appears. No open PR pools these events. The closest, #54422, makes multiproc workers release their last output sooner and does not touch the copy events. ## Claims - After warm-up, the V2 async-output path no longer creates or destroys CUDA events each step. The pool holds one (ready, copy) pair per output in flight. - Ordering is unchanged. The copy stream waits on an event recorded on the main stream, which is what `Stream.wait_stream()` did with a temporary event. - No event is re-recorded while anything still waits on it, so the #39115 race cannot come back. - Under Confidential Computing the pool is off, and the old path is used unchanged. - On main with #57987's background r

title: [RFC]: Decode states at prefix-match boundaries for hybrid prefix caching (FlashStates)
summary: ### Motivation. Hybrid models (full attention next to Mamba / GDN / KDA layers) can resume a cached prefix only where a recurrent state is cached. In agentic traffic each turn's prompt is the previous prompt plus the model's output plus a tool result, so the best place to resume is as close as possible to where the previous request stopped. Today the prompt keeps its state at the last `prefix_match_unit` boundary before the prompt end. For decode, since #67053 `main` keeps the state at the latest block boundary that decode crossed and caches it when the request is freed; this is on by default (`prefix_cache_retention_interval` 0 or positive). Blocks are large (hundreds to thousands of tokens), so a turn whose output does not cross a block boundary still resumes at the end of its prompt, and every turn recomputes the tokens between its last cached state and the previous end. Example (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8, block and `prefix_match_unit` 576 tokens, 8 sessions x 5 turns, outputs of 5-162 tokens): with block-aligned states only, every later turn resumed 61-673 tokens before the end of the previous request. With `prefix_match_unit` set to 32 and a decode state at its last boundary, the gap would be less than 32 tokens by construction. This is one piece of FlashStates ([code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashStates)), which we, its authors, would like to upstream as small PRs. ### Proposed Change. title: [HiSparse] Offload the indexer by default and split host_pool_gib with it
summary: Related to #68725. ## What changes When HiSparse runs with prefix caching (the default), vLLM now also offloads the indexer cache to CPU. Before, cached prefixes were lost after a few prompts of other traffic, however large `host_pool_gib` was. A prefix hit needs the indexer cache too, and that cache only lived on the GPU, where it was evicted quickly ([root cause](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68725#issuecomment-7013589195)). title: [HiSparse] Store one copy of the offloaded indexer across TP ranks
summary: ## What changes With HiSparse and an `OffloadingConnector` (which offloads only the indexer cache) on a single node with TP > 1, the CPU tier now stores **one** copy of the indexer cache shared by all TP ranks, instead of one copy per rank. The bytes are identical on every rank, so at TP4 this cuts the tier's host memory by 4× for the same capacity. Why it happened: the shared-copy layout requires every KV cache group to be TP-replicated. HiSparse's resident and hot GPU page groups are raw pages with no TP metadata, so the check always failed. Those groups are never offloaded, so the check now looks only at the groups that are. Example config that is affected: ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[ {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}, {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":4294967296}}]}}' ``` Before, the 4 GiB tier held 1 GiB worth of blocks (four copies). After, it holds the full 4 GiB. ## Validation `test_hisparse_indexer_tier_is_single_copy_under_tp` fails on `main` and passes here: ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py ``` On 4×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4), with this change applied together with #68771, the indexer tier was a single shared region: `Created mmap file /dev/shm/vllm_offload_<engine>.mmap (4.05 GB)`. title: [Perf][Attention] Let Gemma 4 full-attention layers opt out of multimodal PrefixLM ranges
summary: ## Overview On Gemma 4 with `use_bidirectional_attention="vision"`, the full-attention layers are causal, but they run on the Triton child of the composite attention backend on every prefill step with image or video tokens (#65513). title: [Kernel] Scale KDA sigmoid-gating V-tile with batch at low concurrency
summary: `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` launches grid (NK, NV, N*HV) with NV = V/BV and caps BV at 32 unconditionally. For Kimi-K3 at tp=8 (HV=12, K=V=128) that is 4*N*12 workgroups -- only 48 at batch 1, i.e. 0.19 per CU on a 256-CU MI355X, so roughly 81% of the GPU is idle. A narrower tile makes more programs and buys occupancy, at the cost of re-loading the full 128-wide q/k in each one. That trade is positive only while the launch is starved, so cap BV by 8*N as well. min(32, 8*N) reproduces the current cap exactly for N >= 4, so this is a no-op outside the starved regime. Measured on MI355X (torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0), Kimi-K3 tp=8, CUDA-graph replay time, against the current BV=32 with #54103 applied: C1 decode (T=1) 3.185 -> 2.830 us -11.1% (BV=8) C1 spec (T=4) 7.810 -> 6.529 us -16.4% (BV=8) C2 decode (T=1) 3.308 -> 3.068 us -7.3% (BV=16) C2 spec (T=4) 8.292 -> 7.332 us -11.6% (BV=16) C4 and above 0.0% (BV=32, unchanged) Verified numerically against BV=32 over C1/C2/C4/C8 x decode/spec x 3 seeds x BV in {4,8,16,64}, comparing both the attention output and the mutated recurrent state: 0 failures, worst relative deviation 3.8e-04, most configs bit-exact. num_stages and waves_per_eu were swept over the same grid and are inert for this kernel (all values within 0.3% and 0.7% respectively), so BV is the only dimension that moves it.

summary: ## Overview Since #67335, `allocate_token_bitmask` pins the structured-output bitmask, and #68484 removed the unpinned fallback. title: [RFC]: Upstream the vLLM gaps that Hugging Face TRL works around
summary: ### Motivation Hugging Face TRL runs vLLM for rollouts in two modes. In colocate mode, vLLM runs inside the trainer process via `external_launcher`. In server mode, TRL runs `vllm serve` and syncs weights over NCCL. TRL has already retired most of its vLLM-specific code: `trl vllm-serve` now just execs upstream `vllm serve`. Four workarounds remain, all four reproduced on vLLM main (see Reproductions), and each covers a gap that other colocated or server-mode RL frameworks hit too. This RFC proposes fixing them in vLLM so TRL (and others) can delete the workarounds. Audit baseline: TRL [`211381b`](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/tree/211381b68a890af237222d5ef246eb4b5757341d), vLLM main [`4ae5147`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/4ae51478154cbc4e2fc8aa7d664ddbc0b249102c). title: [Model Loader] Enable the EP weight filter by default and skip non-local expert scales
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Enable the EP weight filter (`--enable-ep-weight-filter`) by default; `--no-enable-ep-weight-filter` turns it off. Also skip other ranks' per-expert **block scales**, and fall back to loading every expert when the model's MoE layout doesn't match what the filter assumes. Under expert parallelism each rank only needs its own experts. Without the filter, every rank still creates a tensor for every expert weight in the checkpoint and passes it through the model's `load_weights`, only for `FusedMoE` to discard the non-local ones. The filter skips them up front. This PR has three commits: 1. **Default on** (`vllm/config/parallel.py`, +3/−2). 2. **Skip non-local block scales** (`ep_weight_filter.py`, +5/−4; test +5/−4). Other ranks' tensors ending in `.weight_scale`, `.weight_scale_inv` or `.scale` are now skipped like their weights. Per-expert **scalars** are still read on every rank: `input_scale`, `weight_scale_2` and the `*_global_scale` names, which some backends reduce over all experts. 3. **Layout guard** (`default_loader.py`, +13). The filter derives one set of local expert ids from `model_config.get_num_experts()`. If the model doesn't have exactly one `RoutedExperts` per layer with that many experts, the filter now turns itself off with a warning. **History.** The filter landed on by default in #37136 and was made opt-in two days later (#37351), alongside #37322, which fixed its two accuracy bugs: - **EPLB:** redundant expert slots were starved, and GSM8K dropped to ~0.08. #37322 disabled the filter under EPLB; #64187 later made

title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't let later image requests overtake a request deferred for encoder limits
summary: ## Overview Fixes #67292. With chunked prefill off and async scheduling, a multimodal request that the scheduler defers whole for encoder cache or budget limits (#65399) can be skipped indefinitely, while later requests with fewer images take the encoder cache space it needs. With this PR, once the scheduler defers a request this way, it admits no later request that needs encoder output in that step, as long as the deferred request's images fit the configured encoder cache at once. In the issue's repro, the 4-image request is then scheduled whole at step 2, where before it was not scheduled in 50 steps. ## Claims - Under FCFS, with chunked prefill off and async scheduling or pipeline parallelism, a request deferred for encoder limits is no longer overtaken by later requests that need encoder output, provided the embeddings of all its images add up to no more than the configured encoder cache size. It is scheduled whole once the steps in flight at the deferral have been processed, with one exception described in Details. - In the scheduler-only repro from #67292, with `AsyncScheduler` and chunked prefill off, the 4-image request is scheduled whole at step 2. Before this change it was not scheduled in 50 steps. - On `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` served with chunked prefill off and async scheduling under a sustained one-image load, base completed none of the 4-image requests within 30 s in any of its saturated runs, and the first version of this change completed all of them, with a median time to first token of 0.45 to 1.36 s. title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep AITER MLA split metadata alive for CUDA graph replay
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, `aiter.mla.get_meta_param` is a `functools.lru_cache` (default 128 entries) that returns a device tensor, `num_kv_splits_indptr`. A CUDA graph captured around `mla_decode_fwd` keeps only that tensor's address, and the cache entry is its only owner. Once enough new batch shapes evict the entry, the memory is reused and every replay of that graph reads garbage split offsets: decode output silently turns to gibberish while prefill stays correct. This PR holds a reference to every tensor handed out while a graph is being captured. This is a stopgap for ROCm/aiter#5193. The proper fix is ROCm/aiter#5194 (open); vLLM pins AITER v0.1.27, which still has the cache. The workaround switches itself off once AITER stops caching the tensor. ## Claims - Fixes silent decode corruption on long-running ROCm servers whenever AITER MLA decode runs inside CUDA graphs and `mla_decode_fwd` derives its own split metadata: the sparse MLA backend (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) always, and by code reading the dense backend when it runs without persistent metadata. - GSM8K on `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` (8x MI355X, TP8) scores 93.5–93.7% in both compiled and no-compile graph modes with the fix. Without it, runs scored 75–94% because the corruption started at a random point 25–37 minutes in. - Memory stays bounded: only tensors handed out during capture are kept, about one per captured batch size. ## Validation **Regression test** (new, in the AMD CI step that already runs this file): capture `rocm_aiter_ops.mla_decode_fwd` in a graph, clear AITER's cache, reuse the freed memory, replay,

title: [RFC]: Resource bound for the `/tokenize` endpoint
summary: ### Motivation. `/tokenize` is a vLLM-specific endpoint. Its request models currently build tokenization parameters with `max_total_tokens=None`: ```python TokenizeParams( max_total_tokens=None, ... ) ``` `VLLM_HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` limits the serialized body (default 32 MiB), but in an isolated test an approximately 18 MiB synthetic prompt tokenized to 4,404,015 tokens, so a body within that limit can still expand to millions of tokens. We investigated an API-server availability incident and believe this path is a plausible contributor, but the evidence is partly indirect: - The exact production request body was not retained, and per-write historical thread IDs were not retained, so the triggering request and the write-lock holder cannot be identified. - A tokenizer worker was observed blocked in `do_user_addr_fault -> rwsem_down_read_slowpath -> down_read`. Its stack matched `TokenizersBackend._encode_plus` and the list comprehension in Transformers' `_encode_plus`, which builds a Python token list. - A register value at that point (`RDX=0x2001f68` = 33,562,472) equals the pointer-array size of a Python 3.12 list with 4,195,309 elements (appending one more element grows it to 37,757,824 bytes). This is consistent with, but does not prove, a multi-million-element token list being built. - During the same period the API server stopped serving health, metrics, logs, and requests for about 9 minutes 34 seconds; the container stayed running, with no restart and no OOM kill.
