title: [ROCm][Muse Spark] Decode MoE on native routes
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> Two commits, reviewable one at a time: (1) the decode MoE on native routes; (2) one launch for the sort and the stage-1 MXFP4 quant up to 512 tokens. ## Purpose At decode batch sizes a Muse Spark MoE layer on ROCm is mostly small launches, and the AITER path repeats each token's row `top_k` times before the experts. On gfx950 with EP AITER MXFP4 experts, `MuseSparkMoE.forward` now hands MoE calls of up to 2048 tokens (decode and spec-decode verify steps, and prefill chunks of up to 2048 tokens) to a model-local path (`amd/decode_moe.py`) that runs the whole layer on the layer's own weights: - one Triton kernel for the router split-K reduce, top-k routing and pre-expert RMSNorm (one row per token); - the experts on the native `[T, top_k]` routes (T rows instead of `T * top_k`) with kernels already in released AITER, then the fused post-expert finalize; - the layer's all-reduce, or #63085's reduce-scatter on token-sharded steps. Commit 2: up to 512 tokens, the two sorting kernels and the stage-1 MXFP4 quant become one Triton launch, built on AITER's Triton MXFP4 helpers. Every other configuration and size runs the existing code unchanged, as does any shape whose AITER config this path cannot launch. On by default, no new option: the output matches the existing path's, the collectives are the same, and it is faster at every size it takes (below). `--moe-backend` cannot switch it off: the Muse Spark ROCm checkpoint only starts with `auto` (its BF16 edge-layer experts need `auto`/`triton`, its MXFP4 experts an AITER MXFP4 backend). ## Results MI355X

title: [Bugfix][FA4] Warm the SplitKV combine kernel for the layer's query heads
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview vLLM's dense JIT warmup for FlashAttention 4 (FA4), registered for Gemma 4 checkpoints, compiles the SplitKV combine kernel of the SM90 head-size-512 forward for one query head. FA4 keys that kernel on the number of heads, so the warmed kernel matches no layer, and the first split-KV call for each head count and split bucket compiles the combine while serving. This PR adds the layer's query heads to the warmup's compile key and compiles the combine for them. On H100 with stock Gemma 4 in the default CUDA graph mode, the first request that adds 64 tokens to a cached 32K-token prompt takes 0.074 s instead of 0.534 s on E2B, and 0.069 s instead of 0.507 s on 12B. ## Claims - On H100 with stock `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and `google/gemma-4-12B-it` in the default CUDA graph mode, the first request that adds 64 tokens to a cached 32K-token prompt takes 0.534 s on main and 0.074 s with this PR on E2B, and 0.507 s and 0.069 s on 12B. The next such request takes 0.051 to 0.061 s on both builds. - On main, that first request adds one kernel to FA4's combine cache, at head size 512 with the layer's 8 (E2B) or 16 (12B) query heads. With this PR it adds none. Neither build compiles a forward kernel in these requests. - A fresh 32K-token prompt doesn't split the keys and takes the same time on both builds (0.441 and 0.435 s on E2B, 1.651 and 1.661 s on 12B). - The JIT warmup took 9.84 s on main and 10.06 s with this PR on E2B, and 11.71 s and 11.10 s on 12B. ## Validation All runs are on H100 80GB with main `c02ebf136e`, torch 2.14.0+cu130 and flas

title: [RFC][Prototype] Snapshot post-processed model weights to skip checkpoint loading on restart
summary: ## [RFC][Prototype] Snapshot post-processed model weights to skip checkpoint loading on restart ### Purpose On restart, vLLM re-reads the safetensors checkpoint and re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` even when nothing changed. This draft adds an opt-in snapshot of the post-processed model state. The first start saves it; later starts build the model with dummy weights (same structure) and copy the saved bytes back with O_DIRECT reads, skipping checkpoint parsing and weight conversion. ### Usage | Env var | Meaning | |---|---| | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_DIR` | Enables the feature; one snapshot file per rank in this directory. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_AUDIT=1` | After a restore, log live CUDA storages the snapshot did not cover (state a model keeps outside module attributes). | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_SKIP_FUNCS` | Comma-separated `module:function` list of pure, expensive weight-preparation functions whose output the snapshot overwrites; skipped on restore (see below). Empty by default. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_CLEAR=1` | Delete this rank's snapshot files in the directory (all keys) and load normally without saving. One-shot: applies on every start while set. | | `VLLM_WEIGHT_SNAPSHOT_REBUILD=1` | Delete this rank's snapshot for the current key, load normally and save a fresh one. One-shot like CLEAR; mutually exclusive with it. | The file key is built from the settings that shape the post-processed weights: checkpoint identity (HF `repo@commit` plus a `config.json` digest, or weight file names/sizes for local directories), dtype, quantization, hf_overrides, KV cache dtyp

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Add __syncwarp before the lane-0 stores in the fused KDA decode block reductions
summary: ## Overview In `csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu`, the two pairwise block reductions let lane 0 of warp 0 overwrite `scratch[0]` and `scratch[1]` right after the warp reads the per-warp partials from the same buffer. Lane 1 reads `scratch[1]`, and nothing orders that read before lane 0's store. This PR adds one `__syncwarp()` before the stores in each function. TensorRT-LLM made the same change to the same two functions in its copy of this kernel ([NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19830](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19830)). ## Claims - Removes an intra-warp shared-memory race in `block_reduce_sum2_for` and `block_reduce_sum2_active_for`. compute-sanitizer racecheck reports it on main and reports no hazards with this change. - Outputs do not change: they are bitwise identical before and after on B200. - No measurable latency change. The fix adds one `WARPSYNC` instruction per kernel. ## Validation Setup: one B200, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0, compute-sanitizer 2025.3.1. vLLM at 3d81a51 with `_C_stable_libtorch` built from source (`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0`, Release), without and with this patch. The other extensions come from the precompiled wheel. | Check | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | racecheck on `test_fused_kda_decode_correctness` (command below) | 2400 warnings, 0 errors | 0 hazards | | `test_fused_kda_decode_correctness`, native backend | 10 passed | 10 passed | | `fused_kda_decode` outputs (`out`, `conv_state`, `state`), 12 parameter sets × 3 seeds | | bitwise identical to main, 36/36 | | fused kernel latency, `benchmark_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py --graph`

title: [RFC]: Store the Gemma 4 global-layer KV cache once (attention_k_eq_v): 37.5% fewer global KV values, read by the stock attention kernel
summary: ### Motivation. **TL;DR.** Gemma 4's global layers compute the value from the key, but vLLM still caches both. I propose storing one 640-value row per head and token instead of 1,024 values, which the existing attention kernel reads through two overlapping views. In a prototype this cut the decode KV memory per request by 1.34x to 1.40x and raised decode tokens per step by 1.24x to 1.38x. I would like your guidance on the KV spec, the page plan and the query transform before I open a PR. The Gemma 4 technical report (arXiv 2607.02770) states that the global layers reuse the keys as the values, which cuts the global KV cache by up to 37.5%. vLLM does not get this saving today: it stores a full K and a full V in these layers (1,024 values per KV head and token). In the global (full-attention) layers of Gemma 4 31B and 26B-A4B, `attention_k_eq_v=True`. These layers have no V projection: - V = RMSNorm(W_k x), with no learned weight. - K = rope_p(w * V), where w is the k_norm weight. p-RoPE (p = 0.25) rotates 128 of the 512 dims of each head (dims 0 to 63 and 256 to 319). - So K equals w * V on the 384 unrotated dims. Only the 128 rotated dims differ, because their rotation depends on the position. On main today, `gemma4.py` loads `k_proj` into both the K and the V shards of `qkv_proj` (`k_eq_v_shards`), computes V = v_norm(the duplicate K), and passes separate K and V tensors to `Attention`, so the cache holds both. I describe the method and my measurements in a preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23035. The prototype code and the raw records are at https://github.com/Kushagra

title: [KV Cache] Allow mixed page sizes in a layer-compact KV layout (for Nemotron Shortcut)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Nemotron Shortcut ([#68198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68198)) needs a layer-compact KV cache layout with mixed page sizes. Its SDSA indexer cache joins its core's KV cache group, so that group mixes page sizes, and the SDSA core supports only `LBHNC`. `validate_kv_cache_layout` refuses this today, although `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places it correctly. This PR relaxes the check. No model on `main` hits it. No other model is affected: the check only got looser and the placement order did not change, so every configuration accepted on `main` is accepted with the same layout. Why layer-outer, when Kimi-K3 and Qwen4-exp, which also mix linear-attention layers with an indexer cache, use block-outer packing: the SDSA core reads each layer's pages as one pool of token rows, so the layer dim must stay outermost with dense pages. Block-outer packing would also put the model under NIXL's limits for packed layouts (the pull connector refuses them with PP, and PP push needs MLA). ## Claims - A model with more than one KV cache group and mixed page sizes can use a layer-compact layout (`LBHNC`, `LBNHC`) when the layers that overlay each other have the same block stride. Groupings whose overlaid layers differ are still refused with the same error; single-group models, uniform page sizes and block-outer layouts behave as before. ## Validation **Reproducer** (CPU only): <details><summary>repro_kv_layout.py</summary> ```python from unittest.mock import MagicMock import torch from vllm.config import CacheConfig from vllm.v1.co

title: [ROCm] Share the AITER IPC all-gather helper; use it for the DCP group

title: [RFC]: Bidirectional attention spans, set per request
summary: ### Motivation. Several decoder models are now trained with a PrefixLM-style mask such that some token ranges of the prompt attend to each other in both directions, and the rest of the prompt is causal. vLLM applies such ranges today to images and videos (`mm_req_doc_ranges` in `CommonAttentionMetadata`; FlashAttention 4 support with #42175, FlexAttention with #27938; since #65996, per request in `DefaultModelState.mm_prefix_ranges`). Models that need ranges over text, or over a whole state that holds images, build them out of tree or model by model, including the following: - #66722, which carries #62584, serves Decision 3.0 `prefix_bidir` (vllm-sr/d3-turbo, a Qwen3.5 hybrid). A prompt is a state block, media included, and a question block, each bidirectional within itself on the full-attention layers. `D3Strategy` sends the state block's size in `PoolingParams.extra_kwargs`, and a model state writes the two blocks into `mm_prefix_ranges`. Chunked prefill and prefix caching stay off. - #63114 serves Base Labs mammoth-1 and elephant-1 (Qwen3.5) with a block-bidirectional mask, two ranges per request, with its own `PrefixLMScheduler` (cache hits capped at the prefix end, the rest of the prompt prefilled in one step, client salts moved into a prefix namespace). - RFC #64267 builds a state cache for Decision 3.0 on top of both. - #63033 makes PaliGemma's whole prompt one bidirectional block, with chunked prefill and prefix caching off. - #65268 (draft) reads a shared prefix and several candidates in one forward, for encoder-only models. - Strands Decider's Gemma 4 decision mod

title: [ROCm] Fix MiniMax-M3 sparse PA KV block count
summary: ## Overview MiniMax-M3 LBHNC interleaves K and V inside each block, so the V cache view has fewer rows than K. No block-table page id addresses them (max id is `127 * 16 + 7 = 2039`). - The trim stays inside `_run_gluon_decode`, so `_sides_are_packed` and `minimax_m3_sparse_block_page_stride` still see the original shapes and keep a block page stride of 16. ## Validation Reproduced on MiniMax-M3 with the AITER sparse paged-attention decode path. title: [ROCm][DSA] Enable the DCP global-key indexer prefill by default
summary: Stacked on #68758. ## Overview Enable the ROCm DCP global-key indexer prefill by default. `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_GLOBAL_KEY_PREFILL=0` keeps the per-rank candidate merge. The row-sharded scoring (`VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_ROWSHARD_PREFILL`) stays opt-in and is *not* flipped here: it grows the indexer logits workspace by the DCP world size, which needs a default of its own before it can be on for everyone. ## Why this default is safe - **It is the exact path, not a heuristic.** With `compress_ratio == 1` and no candidate blocks the merge path keeps at most `topk_tokens` candidates per rank and merges them, so a token just outside one rank's cut cannot be recovered. The global-key path scores every row against the whole key set, so its top-k is the true one. Enabling it cannot lower accuracy relative to the merge it replaces. - **It moves far less data.** DCP4, 32k-token chunk, 2048 query rows, 20 iterations on MI355X: | path | per chunk | payload | |---|---|---| | candidate merge (pack, all-gather, merge) | 1.19 ms | 128.0 MiB | | global-key (pack, all-gather, restore) | 0.10 ms | 4.1 MiB | - **Pack/restore is byte-exact.** `test_global_key_prefill_restores_global_token_order` (in #68758) round-trips every token's key and FP32 scale into global order for DCP 2/4 and interleave 1/16. - **Already the served default on MI355X.** The published AgentX preset in `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro.yaml` sets this flag to 1. - **Scoped.** Only fires for `compress_ratio == 1`, no candidate blocks, block-flat (`"NORMAL"`) indexer cache, 3-D indexer cache, DCP > 1 on ROCm. title: [Perf][MoE] Select full-warp top-k rows with redux.sync and keep selections in registers (SM80+)
summary: ## Overview `topkGating` (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu`) gives each row to one full warp when the row is wide enough (512 experts, 256 experts with 16-bit logits, 128-512 experts with fp32 logits). For each of the k selections it runs a 5-stage shuffle butterfly with 3 dependent shuffles per stage, then lane 0 stores the selection and later re-reads the weights to scale them. For those rows, without a correction bias, this PR selects each expert with two `redux.sync` reductions (`__reduce_max_sync` on the score key, then `__reduce_min_sync` on the expert among the lanes that hold the max), keeps selection i in the registers of lane i, rescans only in the winning lane, and writes the row once at the end. The output is bitwise equal to `main`: the same experts, the same order, the same lowest-index tie rule and the same weight bits. The register-resident output path is from @Gin-Sin (#64731, co-author); the SM80+ `redux.sync` selection scope is from this PR. #64731 will be closed in favour of this PR. ## Claims - **Same output:** bitwise equal to `main` (ids, weights as bits, token-expert indices) in every case run on A100, including tie-heavy, all-equal and NaN/Inf rows. - **Faster on SM80+:** E 512 top-10 softmax on A100: 0.59-0.68x of `main`'s time at 1-256 tokens, 0.71-0.76x at 1,024-4,096 tokens. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Tile whole kernel rows of groups to persist logical block for drafter blocks
summary: ## Overview Claude and I hit this while benchmarking P/D for Kimi K3 with its DSpark draft model on GB300. Every engine that loaded `NixlConnector` died at startup in `register_kv_caches`, on every topology we tried, including a plain 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 with no DCP. The cause seems to be a mismatch between two layers of vLLM: - The model runner picks a kernel block size for each KV cache group, but `NixlConnectorWorker` picks one physical/logical block ratio and applies it to every layer. - When one group keeps the full logical block as a single row, NIXL cannot split that group's cache into the blocks it expects. Claude proposes that we should register each such row as `ratio` byte pages, and makes the handshake refuse a peer whose rows are laid out differently. This means we just outright reject mismatches, which might be wrong for DP -> TP (I haven't tested this extensively, and I'm currently working on it). Seems like #63997 (Gemma 4) has the same root cause. #64067 fixes it for contiguous views and #59586 for MLA groups but doesn't seem to address Kimi K3's draft group, given that it is a non-MLA group whose rows are padded. _Note that this also might just be K3-specific, so I haven't tested with other models just yet_. ## Claims - Kimi K3 with the DSpark draft on `FLASH_ATTN` now starts and serves P/D over `NixlConnector`. On main and on nightly `7c3a9302` every engine asserts before it accepts a single request. - The draft KV arrives intact. Over 2180 transfers (3.65 TB), decode saw 0 failures and a spec-decode acceptance rate of 0.163, at or above the 0.158-0.160 we me

title: [Bugfix] Reduce sparse-MLA + indexer workspace bounds on SM_120 (consumer Blackwell)
summary: ## Problem PR #41834 lands first-class SM_120 (consumer Blackwell) support for DeepSeek-V4 via Triton sparse-MLA. The workspace bounds in `indexer.py` and `flashmla_sparse.py` were sized for H200 (140 GiB per GPU) headroom. On 95 GiB consumer Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000 Workstation, RTX 5090) the workspace overflows the cumem budget by ~14 GiB, surfacing as a misleading "allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs)" OOM — the user can't shrink it via `--max-cudagraph-capture-size`, `cudagraph_mode`, `--enforce-eager`, or any other documented knob. ## Fix Arch-gate three workspace bounds via `current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)`: 1. **`indexer.py`** — workspace multiplier `40 → 8`. `split_indexer_prefill_chunks` already enforces `M * N * 4 ≤ bound`, so a smaller bound simply yields more chunk passes per prefill. No correctness change. 2. **`flashmla_sparse.py`** — workspace multiplier `5 → 2`. `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache` iterates rows at a time; smaller workspace just holds fewer rows per chunk. 3. **`sparse_indexer_max_logits_bytes()`** default `256 MB → 96 MB`. Same chunking path enforces the bound. All three are no-ops on H100 / H200 / H800 / B100 / B200 — only `SM_120` devices take the new bounds. ## Dependency on #41834 This PR is built on top of **jasl:codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable** (the head of #41834). The three hunks here only make sense in combination with #41834's SM12x enablement (they reference functions/imports added by #41834). Best landed after #41834 merges — or rolled into #41834 directly if the author prefers. ## Testing Live productio

title: [Bugfix][Core] Redo prompt logprobs for requests resumed after reset_prefix_cache
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61490. Active `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` exposed two opposite redo-state errors: resuming before a dropped output arrived could leave prompt-logprob rows unwritten, while resetting after a complete output was emitted could recompute and append a duplicate block. This PR arms redo at drop-mode preemption only when complete prompt logprobs have not already been emitted. The recompute marker persists until prompt logprobs are produced, and a separate output-emitted marker prevents an unnecessary second prefill from appending `N - 1` rows after the original `N` rows. ## Claims - A resume no longer has to wait for dropped output to arrive before redo is armed. Prefix hits cannot silently turn into unwritten prompt-logprobs rows on that first resume. - Once complete prompt logprobs are attached to an `EngineCoreOutput`, a later reset does not request another copy. The output processor therefore does not receive the duplicate `N - 1` scored rows observed in the independent GPU reruns. - Current MRV2 sends new and resumed requests through the same new-request path, which re-registers the prompt-logprobs requirement without the removed V1-only redo directive. Requests without prompt logprobs do not arm the redo path. - Completion formatting keeps one logprob row per prompt token, including explicit placeholders for missing rows and truncation of extra rows. summary: ## Purpose `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (the first sparse MLA choice on Hopper for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash) has no HiSparse path. Requires a ROCm build with the `_rocm_C` RDNA3 MXFP4 op (#60413). ## Follow-up Use the `gemm` vs `fallback` gap to decide on a fused dequant-G

title: [Bugfix][Core] Align streamed token ids with stop-buffered text
summary: ## Overview Streamed outputs of requests with stop strings send token ids that are ahead of their text: the detokenizer holds back the last `max(len(stop)) - 1` chars, but not the tokens they decode from. Parsers that match markers by token id then misparse reasoning and tool calls. This PR holds back text at token boundaries, and sends each output's `token_ids`, `logprobs` and `sampling_mask` for exactly the tokens its text covers. Fixes #51641 ## Claims - In streaming, every output's `token_ids` decode to its `text`, also when stop strings hold text back. `logprobs` and `sampling_mask` stay aligned with `token_ids`. Holds for `DELTA` and `CUMULATIVE` outputs, and for multi-token steps (i.e. speculative decoding). - This fixes, for streaming requests with `stop` and `include_stop_str_in_output=False`: - Tool call arguments corrupted by engine-based parser that matches markers by token id. With Qwen3 + `hermes`, `{"cmd": "echo hi"}` streams as `{"cmd": "echo hi"}}`. With GLM-4.7, the arguments are lost. - Reasoning split at the wrong place by legacy parsers (#51641). With `deepseek_r1`, reasoning is cut at `…saf` and content starts with `/think>`. - No parser changes, so every parser gets aligned input. Requests without stop strings, or with `include_stop_str_in_output=True`, hold nothing back and are unchanged. - Text is still held back as before: no part of a stop string is streamed before it is matched. title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Align the fused gate shard to its block-FP8 weight scales
summary: ## Purpose Fix silently wrong dequantization of the Kimi-K3 output-gate projection when the attention projections are block-FP8 (e.g. ModelOpt `FP8_PB_WO` checkpoints such as `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4`, or any `Fp8Config` with `weight_block_size`). `KimiK3MergedQKVGateLinear` fuses `q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `g_proj` into one `[q_a | kv_a | gate]` weight. The merged loader writes shard *i*'s weight rows from `sum(previous rows)`, but its block scales from `ceil(sum(previous rows) / 128)` (`adjust_block_scale_shard`). Kimi-K3's latents are `1536 + 576 = 2112` rows, which is not a multiple of 128: | | starts at row | block | |---|---|---| | gate weight rows | 2112 | inside block 16 | | gate scale blocks | 2176 | block 17 | So every gate weight row `r` is dequantized with the scale of block `r // 128`, which belongs to the gate block it should use for only half of its rows: **64 of every 128 gate rows (768 per rank at TP8, 6144 at TP1) use a neighbouring block's scale** (kv_a's last block or the previous gate block). The existing `FP8_PB_WO` partial-block handling pads only the end of the matrix, so it does not cover this interior misalignment. The model still loads and serves, and gsm8k stays near the reference, so this is easy to miss. But on real checkpoint weights, the gate outputs differ from the dequantized checkpoint by up to 60–161% (max relative error per channel at M=8000), while q_a and kv_a are within BF16 rounding. ## Change - `KimiK3MergedQKVGateLinear` resolves the row height of its weight-scale blocks from the quant config (`_weight_block_rows`: ModelOpt

title: [Kernel][torch.compile] CUDA fused QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache write (fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache on FlashAttention)
summary: ## Purpose The partial NeoX RoPE fix this fusion needs landed on `main` in #68386. This branch was originally stacked on #57681, which is now closed. The CUDA KV-cache fusion can proceed independently. CUDA counterpart of the ROCm `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` pass (#42749 / #42755): fuse Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + the paged KV-cache write into one launch on the FlashAttention backend. Today the CUDA path runs `fused_qk_norm_rope` (which writes the rotated Q/K back into `qkv`) and then `reshape_and_cache_flash`, which reads K and V back out of `qkv` only to scatter them into the cache. The new kernel keeps K/V in registers and stores them to `q_out`/`k_out` and to the cache directly, so K/V are never re-read. This fills the "QK Norm + RoPE + Cache" CUDA gap in #36066. ## Changes - `csrc/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`: `WRITE_CACHE` template variant of both kernels (1-head and N-token-heads). In that mode `qkv` is read-only, Q/K land in contiguous `q_out`/`k_out`, K/V are scattered into the (possibly strided) flash-layout cache via `slot_mapping`; V heads get their own warps. Tokens beyond `slot_mapping.size(0)` or with slot `-1` are normalised/rotated but not cached, matching `reshape_and_cache_flash`. All stores happen before the PDL trigger. The existing `fused_qk_norm_rope` entry is unchanged in behaviour (same kernel, `WRITE_CACHE=false`). - New op `_C.fused_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` (+ `vllm._custom_ops` wrapper). - `FlashAttentionImpl.fused_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_supported()` / `do_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_update()`: enabled for `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`, decoder layers, `head_size ∈ {64,1

title: [Rust Frontend] Serve /generative_scoring
summary: ## Overview The Rust frontend answers `POST /generative_scoring` with a 501. title: [Qwen4Exp] PLE disk offload
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'` for Qwen4Exp. The PLE n-gram table stays in the checkpoint files, and each step reads only its rows on the host. On DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 loads with 27.0 GiB less memory. Decode is within 3.5% of the resident table, and GSM8K is unchanged. This carries forward @Trosfy's design from #58815 (their commits are kept, co-authored). It is rebased onto the NVFP4 PLE tables from #56273 and renamed `disk_offload` to pair with `cpu_offload`. ## Claims - **Memory:** no table in GPU or pinned host memory, and no copy in an offload directory. Recently read rows sit in the OS page cache, which the kernel can reclaim. The page cache does fill up over a long session (ids are hashed, so there is no locality), but the kernel reclaims it on demand without hurting decode; the cost of a cold table is in TTFT (below). Use it with the checkpoint on local NVMe: on network storage a cold prefill is 2 to 4.5x slower. On unified-memory Spark, `cpu_offload` does not help, because pinned memory comes out of the same pool as the weights and the KV cache. - **Formats:** BF16, FP8 and NVFP4. Rows are read in checkpoint format and decoded on the GPU with the existing PLE kernel. - **CUDA graphs:** the forward reads fixed device buffers, so graphs replay unchanged. - **Cost:** decode within 3.5% at c=1/4/8, and about 11% higher TTFT. ## Validation Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (`local-inference-lab@6c01ac3`), one GB10, both arms in one job on the same node. MTP n=3, FP8 KV (6 GiB), prefix caching off. |

title: [Hisparse] Support HiSparse for QSA
summary: ## Summary Add HiSparse support for NVIDIA QSA. Main K/V can be offloaded to host; indexer keys, raw-key rings and GDN state stay on GPU. ## Design QSA reuses the existing HiSparse planner and index-group runtime shared with DSA. Sparse-role fields (cache_role, topk_buffer_width, and is_index_group_leader) now live on AttentionSpec, extending sparse-role metadata from MLA to full K/V attention independently of whether HiSparse is enabled (QSA falls back to its normal backend when HiSparse is off). Each TP rank manages a private host pool; host_pool_gib budgets unique KV heads per replica, while padding and replicated heads still consume physical memory. Fused QSA prepare writes to the resident cache. During decode, the shared resolver maps logical selections to resident/hot physical KV rows (refilling hot-cache misses from host) before BF16/FP8 split-K attention: QSA logical selections -> HiSparse resolver -> physical KV rows -> BF16/FP8 QSA split-K attention - **Prefill & split-K:** Prefill reads resident KV directly or via shared staging; split-K honors the backing cache's actual block stride (including padding). - **MTP & prefix caching:** Target and draft layers reuse logical selections while keeping separate physical-index buffers for CUDA graph replay. Prefix reuse is limited to whole scheduler pages. - **Warmup:** Covers physical-index decode; BF16 split-K no longer recompiles when the cache-pool block count changes. title: [Feature]: Async CP for PCP + DCP prefill: prefetch the next layer's KV and indexer K behind the current layer's compute
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **Pitch.** Asynchronous context parallelism ("async CP") for PCP + DCP prefill of DSA models: run each layer's context-parallel gathers off the main stream, behind the previous layer's compute, instead of synchronously right before the attention that needs them. The data that is already in the sharded KV cache before the step does not depend on the current layer's output, so layer l+1's share of it can be fetched while layer l computes. **Motivation.** Under PCP + DCP each rank stores one DCP shard of the KV cache. During `flashmla_sparse` prefill of a DeepSeek V3.2-style (DSA) model, every layer all-gathers the KV of the whole context right before its attention. Every indexer layer also all-gathers its indexer K, and the current chunk's new KV and indexer K rows are gathered as well. All of these gathers run on the main stream, and the first two grow with context length. **How much this costs.** For a 1M-token prompt prefilled in chunks of 16384 tokens, these gathers take about 29 ms of a ~210 ms step (about 14%), all on the main stream with nothing overlapping them: | Gather on the main stream (one prefill step at 1M context) | ms | |---|---:| | Whole-context KV all-gather (every layer) | 24.7 | | New KV + indexer K rows of the current chunk | 3.0 | | Indexer K all-gather (indexer layers) | 1.5 | | **Total** | **29.2** | The KV all-gather grows linearly with the context, while DSA keeps the attention itself cheap, so its share of the step grows with context length. title: [Bugfix] Reject token-major layout for nvfp4 KV cache
summary: ## Problem `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` silently corrupts the KV cache under a token-major layout (BLNHC/LBNHC). Fixes #61225. The nvfp4 writer (`reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_dispatch`) derives data/scale strides for a side-contiguous `[data | scale]` page packing that only holds for head-major pages. Under a token-major layout it writes fp4 data and block scales to the wrong bytes, and the reader reads the garbage back — every K/V write (and its block scales) lands in the wrong location. No exception, no crash; just incoherent output at every context length. ## Fix Reject token-major layouts at the shared writer instead of silently corrupting, matching the head-major restriction already applied on SM100 (`FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts`) and the `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` workaround. - `csrc/nvfp4_kv_cache_kernels.cu`: fail with a clear error when the cache is not head-major. - `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py`: stop exercising the now-unsupported NHD layout for nvfp4. ## Notes The alternative of making the writer (and `nvfp4_split_data_scale`) support token-major is out of scope here: token-major interleaves data and scale per head, so the data and scale views alias, and a coordinated writer+reader repacking is required. A hard error avoids the silent-corruption failure mode. ## Testing Not run on this machine (no Blackwell GPU). The change is a guard plus test skips; existing SM100 head-major nvfp4 paths are unchanged.

summary: ## Purpose On XPU, `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` always returns False, so the FA backend never quantizes the query to FP8 even with an FP8 KV cache. Xe3p kernels in vllm-xpu-kernels (>= 0.1.17) can run full-FP8 attention (FP8 Q/K/V, `q_scale` fused in the kernel), while Xe2 kernels cannot. This PR adds `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` (`bool | None`, default unset) to control it: | `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` | Device | FP8 query | |---|---|---| | `1` | any XPU | on | | `0` | any XPU | off | | unset | Xe3p (`torch.ops._xpu_C.is_xe3p_arch()`) | on | | unset | other XPU (e.g. BMG), or op missing | off (unchanged) | Implementation: `XPUPlatform.support_fp8_query()` resolves the value, and `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` calls it on XPU. Other platforms are unchanged (still True). Limitation: the Xe3p full-FP8 kernels currently only support head_size 128 (and Q/K/V of the same FP8 type), so models with another head size fail on Xe3p when the FP8 KV cache is on; set `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0` for those until the kernels are extended. ## Test Plan On an Xe3p GPU, serve a model with FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) and check the query is quantized; compare with `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0`. On a non-Xe3p XPU the default stays off. Not yet run on hardware.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA][DCP] gfx942: run causal DCP verify on AITER single-token asm decode
summary: ## Purpose On gfx942, causal DCP verify (qlen > 1) currently runs on Triton segmented MLA where it fits in LDS, and on the generic Triton split-KV decode otherwise (#58555). This PR runs gfx942 verify on AITER's non-persistent single-token asm decode whenever gfx942 ships a kernel for the DCP-gathered head count, which covers Kimi-K3 (96) and DeepSeek-V3 (128). Each verify token becomes one qlen-1 row with its own causal KV window, the row view that #58555 already builds. * New route `ASM_ROWS`, checked before TRITON and SEGMENTED on gfx942. Counts with no kernel (above 128) never reach AITER, which would otherwise abort; they take the fallback above. * KV splits per row: `min(cdiv(CUs, 2*rows), max_kv_len // 128, 64)`, floor 2. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Fix heterogeneous-TP WRITE of NVFP4 KV pages and replicated indexer caches
summary: ## Overview MoRIIO's heterogeneous-TP WRITE (prefill TP != decode TP) cannot serve MiniMax-M3 today, for two independent reasons. This PR fixes both: 1. **NVFP4 KV pages** (`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on ROCm): the WRITE cuts the page into per-head slots as if each KV head's bytes were contiguous, but the ROCm page stores all heads' FP4 data before all heads' block scales on each K/V side. A decode instance with a smaller TP than prefill (e.g. TP4 -> TP1) receives scrambled KV and generates garbage. This PR slices those pages by their real layout, and refuses any other packed NVFP4 page instead of mis-slicing it. 2. **Replicated indexer key cache**: MiniMax-M3's lightning-indexer keys live in an MLA-type cache (one vector per token, identical on every TP rank) inside a GQA model. The per-layer WRITE mapping sizes it by the model's KV heads, so with prefill TP > decode TP (and fewer prefill ranks than KV heads, e.g. TP4 -> TP2) it tries to slice it by head and every request fails with `MoRIIOError: Heterogeneous-TP WRITE of layer ...indexer... needs a KV head layout on both sides`. This PR maps such a layer like an MLA latent: copied whole, by one prefill rank per decode rank on fan-in and to every decode rank on fan-out. ## Claims - Prefill TP != decode TP over MoRIIO WRITE with an NVFP4 KV cache on ROCm (MiniMax-M3) now lands every KV byte where the decode kernels read it; before, the decoder output was garbage. - A packed NVFP4 page MoRIIO cannot slice (e.g. laid out by KV head, `kv_head_major_slots=True`) now fails with a clear `ValueError` instead of silently writing the w

title: [Bug][Watermarking]: `deduplicate_contexts="all"` misses repeats across the prompt boundary under speculative decoding
summary: ### Describe the bug With `deduplicate_contexts="all"`, a token is sampled without the watermark when its context (the previous `context_width` tokens) already occurred earlier in the prompt or the output. Under speculative decoding this check misses contexts whose earlier occurrence starts in the prompt and ends in the output. Those tokens are watermarked, while non-speculative decoding samples them without the watermark, so the two paths can produce different text. The default `single_turn` and `none` are not affected. ### Example Take `context_width=2` and count one token per word. The prompt ends with `... say it twice: bye`. The model has answered `bye` so far, and the drafter proposes `bye` again. | Position | 0 (prompt) | 1 (output) | 2 (draft) | 3 (next token) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Token | `bye` | `bye` | `bye` | ? | The token at position 3 has context `(bye, bye)` from positions 1-2. - **Non-speculative decoding** with mode `all` searches the prompt too. It finds `(bye, bye)` at positions 0-1, the last prompt word followed by the first output word. The context is a repeat, so the token is sampled without the watermark. - **Speculative decoding** checks the n-grams that end at the last committed token or at a draft through the contexts of the earlier rows in the same verification block. The earlier row stores its context as `(-1, bye)`, because context positions inside the prompt are written as -1. `(bye, bye)` does not match `(-1, bye)`, so the token is watermarked. title: [Spec Decode] Optimize DSpine draft operators and candidate retrieval
summary: Follow-up to vllm-project/vllm#67094. ### Motivation Every DSpine draft round runs adjacent causal injection in each draft layer and last-write refinement across candidate pairs. Both paths use several separate PyTorch operations that write intermediate tensors. Fusing these operations reduces kernel launches and memory traffic while retaining the existing transition scoring and verification. In a batch-8 CUDA graph profile with the fused operators, candidate retrieval still took 2.40 ms out of 7.49 ms per round. The full-vocabulary BF16 projection accounted for 2.17 ms. An optional FP8 head speeds up the vocabulary scan, and fused BF16 rescoring avoids materializing the shortlisted weight rows. ### Summary - Fuse adjacent causal injection and last-write refinement with Triton. Preserve the BF16 cast boundaries and the full FP32 transition score table. - Reuse `draft_lm_head_quantization: "fp8"` for optional FP8 candidate retrieval at TP=1. Retrieve 128 candidates and rescore them with the original BF16 head. Keep the existing BF16 retrieval as the default. - Fuse shortlist rescoring to avoid materializing the gathered weight tensor. FP8 retrieval and fused rescoring are separate commits. ### Validation The benchmark used Qwen3.8-27B BF16 with the Tencent DSpine b16 draft on one H20 with TP=1, CUDA graphs, and adaptive verification disabled. The table reports median draft proposal latency in ms per round. Reproduced identically on: 1. `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.34.0` 2. `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7c3a9302f5ac2441ad199134129e973d22a46797` 3. nightly + `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_decoder_replay":false}'` (still segfaults → the crash is in the speculator's own graph capture path, not decoder replay) Hardware: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0. **Workaround:** `--enforce-eager` serves cleanly and correctness is preserved (bit-identical battery outputs), but the MoE target loses its graph speedups — short-prompt throughput drops ~3x vs a TF-based baseline, which makes the drafter a net loss on short-prompt workloads. **Also tried, no effect:** dropping the draft's `attention_backend` FLASHINFER override; `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (irrelevant to the crash). title: [Spec Decode] Add option to disable extract_hidden_states decode drafts
summary: ## Summary - `disable_extract_hidden_states_decode_drafts=True` schedules no decode drafts. It sets the existing dynamic SD schedule to K=0 for all batch sizes (`[(1, 1, 0)]`), with no scheduler or model runner changes (about 45 non-test lines). - It raises a clear error for MoE models with data parallelism, alongside another schedule, or with another method, instead of silently falling back to drafts. Dense models with data parallelism keep the K=0 schedule, matching #67005. - Fixes the speculator docstring that said these drafts are always accepted. - #65250 measured a 37.4% to 39.1% saturation throughput loss from these drafts, and −0.03% to 2.56% with the same K=0 schedule (L4, Qwen3-4B, v0.30.0). I did not re-measure on this branch. ## Why the drafts aren't needed The draft is the token that was just sampled (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py:117`), and the next step feeds `[last_sampled, draft]` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py:456-472`), so it is accepted only when the model repeats a token. `propose()` saves hidden states for every scheduled row without using the draft (`:130-156`). With K=0, each input position is still scheduled once and saved at its own slot. ## Gap in the test model `PredictableLlamaModel`, used by the existing extraction test, writes the same value to every position of a layer, so a hidden state saved at the wrong position still passes. Shifting the K=0 save by one position did pass. I added a test-only subclass, `PositionalPredictableLlamaForCausalLM`, whose saved layers output `32 * layer + position`, and the new tes

title: [Rust Frontend] Add /v1/messages (Anthropic Messages API) + x-api-key auth
summary: ## Why Stock Anthropic-protocol clients — Claude Code, the official Python SDK, agent CLIs — cannot complete a single request against the Rust frontend today. The API key they send is rejected (fixed by the first commit), and there is no `/v1/messages` route at all (fixed by the second). This PR makes the Rust frontend usable by these clients out of the box. ## What's in it (two commits, reviewable separately) **1. Accept `x-api-key` as an alternative auth header** (+28) Anthropic clients send `x-api-key` by default; the key is accepted and verified with the same constant-time comparison as the Bearer path. Refs #51572 (reported against the Python frontend; this is the Rust frontend side). **2. Add `/v1/messages` route module** (+1149/−26) - `routes/anthropic.rs` — non-streaming + SSE streaming handlers, `count_tokens` - `routes/anthropic/{types,convert}.rs` — Anthropic↔OpenAI conversion; `tool_use`/`tool_result` round-trips (content optional per spec); image blocks inside `tool_result`; `thinking.budget_tokens` → reasoning effort; `metadata` and unknown-field tolerance - reasoning-effort fallback — when the model's chat template rejects the client's default effort (Claude Code hardcodes `high`; e.g. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next accepts only `xhigh`/`medium`/`low`), retry once with the engine default instead of returning 400 - Adaptations for current main: `resolve_request_context` now returns `Result` (wrapped at both call sites); `SpecDecodingStats` gains `#[serde(default)]` on `num_verified_tokens(_per_pos)` — frontend builds from source currently fail to decode EngineCore outputs

title: [KV Connector] [Mooncake] Fix Mooncake Store lookups after cached L1 prefixes
summary: ## Overview Pass the confirmed local prefix into Mooncake Store lookups so a missing Store copy of an L1 block does not hide a complete L2 suffix. Related: [#48230](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48230), which skips lookup when L1 already covers the entire usable prefix, and this change handles a partial L1 prefix followed by an external suffix. ## Claims - A Store hole entirely inside a confirmed, aligned FullAttention L1 prefix no longer prevents reuse of a complete external suffix. title: [Quantization] Lower peak memory of online requantization, support block-FP8 to MXFP4
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Disclosure AI assistance was used. title: [Bug]: TP=1 silent engine wedge on Qwen3.8 GDN-hybrid MoE (MTP4, NVFP4-KV, FlashInfer, SM120) — frozen generation counter, running>0 waiting=0, health 200, no self-recovery on v0.27.2rc1.dev77
summary: ### 🐛 Describe the bug Silent engine wedge on a **TP=1** deployment of a Qwen3.8-27B GDN-hybrid MoE (abliterated community build of Qwen3.8-27B, MTP spec decode) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120). Matches the family reported in #40926 (TP=1 repro by @nichdiekuh) and #53130. **Signature (identical across three separate incidents, 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-23):** - `vllm:generation_tokens_total` frozen across 60s+ samples - `vllm:num_requests_running = 10`, `vllm:num_requests_waiting = 0` — requests stuck "Running", never complete - `nvidia-smi`: GPU util 100% (reporting), power draw at idle level (~26-138W of a 600W part) — the GPU spins on nothing - `/health` returns 200 the whole time; no exception, no traceback in logs - Engine never self-recovers; only `docker restart` clears it - Trigger appears to be a burst of ~10 simultaneous requests landing on the engine (seen both times) **Related but distinct:** in the 48h window around the silent wedges, the same deployment also crashed loudly **16 times** with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` at `gpu_model_runner.py get_output → torch/cuda/streams.py synchronize`, producing `EngineDeadError`. The silent wedge produces zero errors — it is a distinct failure mode of the same runtime. ### To Reproduce ```bash vllm serve <Qwen3.8-27B GDN-hybrid NVFP4 artifact> \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}' \ --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --attention-backend FLASHINFER \ --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.50 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-pref

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Kimi-K3: don't bake the fused decode MLA path into PIECEWISE graphs
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, Kimi-K3 bakes the decode-only fused MLA path into PIECEWISE CUDA graphs at capture time, so every later replay runs decode kernels on prefill/mixed tokens; with `max_cudagraph_capture_size=1024` the first request crashes or hangs. This PR skips the fused path inside PIECEWISE graphs and warms the skinny-GEMM workspace in `allocate_kv_cache` for every KV cache allocation path, which the unfused path then needs before capture. No existing PR covers this (searched open PRs for "kimi k3 piecewise", "fused decode cudagraph", "aiter_mla piecewise", "wvSplitKrc", "kimi k3 cudagraph" on 2026-11-09). ## Claims - Kimi-K3 (AITER MLA, TP8, MI355X/MI350X) at `max_cudagraph_capture_size=1024`: main crashes or hangs on its first request; this PR serves correctly. ## Validation Kimi-K3, TP8 on 8x MI350X (gfx950), same image for every leg of sections 1 and 2: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432`. This PR applied over the nightly image by bind-mounting the two changed files (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py`, `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`) into the container; main is the same image with those two files left stock. ### 1. Main vs. this PR, same image, same flags Server command (identical on both sides; only whether the two fix files are bind-mounted differ): <details> <summary>serve command + env</summary> ``` docker run --rm \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --ipc host --network host \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 128g \ -v /mnt/data/hf/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ -e VLLM_RO

title: [Feature]: dual_key_gumbel watermarking for DFlash2 drafters
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `dual_key_gumbel` watermarking currently rejects DFlash2 drafters (`supports_watermarking = False` in `dflash2/config.py`). DFlash2 is the fastest drafter for models such as Qwen3.8-27B, so watermarked deployments have to fall back to MTP or DSpark. DFlash2's verification side already works, because it writes the realized candidate scores into `draft_logits`. Only the candidate walk needs to sample with key-A Philox Gumbel noise. I have a PR ready for this. ### Alternatives Use MTP or DSpark with watermarking. On H100 that is 12–34% slower than DFlash2 (numbers in the PR). ### Additional context Follows #59554 (DFlash watermarking). LiLiCorr stays unsupported. Related: #56105. This issue was written with the help of Claude.

title: [Perf] Select split-KV for long-context width-9 Triton verification
summary: ## Overview For fixed-width speculative decoding, a target can verify eight proposed tokens plus the current token in one forward pass. At this query width of nine, the Triton target currently uses 2D attention even when a long KV history leaves too little parallel work on the GPU. This draft captures a second FULL decode graph for eligible shapes and selects it when an active request’s host-side KV-length upper bound reaches 2048. The original graph serves all-short batches. The **Q-block budget is unchanged**. On the measured 32 Q / 8 KV heads, head dimension 128 configuration, each request needs three Q blocks. With a budget of 16, five requests fit (15 blocks) and six exceed it (18). The check uses the padded graph shape. Eager execution, variable-width verification, draft graphs and other verification widths keep their existing behavior. ## Claims and limitations One H100 SXM 80 GB, TP1, BF16. The comparison in this table uses the submitted code and its unmodified parent on the same GPU. Each cell is the median of four measured batches after one warmup, one independent engine start per arm. Throughput counts output tokens over wall time including prefill. TPOT is first-to-last streamed token time divided by 127, reported separately for short and long requests. | Target + draft | Batch of five (prompt tokens) | Output tok/s, base → draft PR | Change | Short TPOT (ms) | Long TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3-4B + DFlash2 | 5 × 256 | 1830.6 → 1851.6 | +1.1% | 2.11 → 2.11 | — | | Qwen3-4B + DFlash2 | 3 × 256 + 2 × 4096 | 768.9 → 1033.5 | +34.4% | 4.66 → 3.0

title: [Perf] Replay the rejection-sampling kernels as a single CUDA graph
summary: ## Problem Speculative-decode verification calls `rejection_sample`, which per decode step dispatches four Triton kernels (local logits stats, rejection, resample, insert-resampled) and allocates ~10 intermediate tensors. On smaller GPUs the host-side dispatch and allocation overhead is a meaningful fraction of every verify step, and decode steps run back-to-back under concurrency, so the cost is paid on every step of every request. ## Approach `RejectionSamplerGraph` (new file `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_graph.py`) captures the four kernels into a single CUDA graph and replays them per step: - Capture happens once, at the first eligible verification step (in practice the startup warmup), at the maximum verify-batch geometry `max_num_reqs x (num_speculative_tokens + 1)` logits rows. - Per step, the live tensors are copied into static input buffers, and a small metadata-pack kernel replaces eight `copy_`/`fill_` dispatches with one launch. The padded tail is filled so padded requests become no-ops inside the graph: `cu_num_logits` repeats the total (empty row ranges), index mappings point padded rows at state slot 0, and the padded tail of `expanded_local_pos` is zeroed so padded rows (and the live row that closes each range) take the stats kernel's existing early return, matching the eager path's masked lookahead. Padded-lane results are discarded. - The step then replays the graph and returns views into static output buffers. - Output-buffer reuse follows the same contract as the existing graph-static `sampled_token_ids`: consumers complete their read

title: [RFC]: Replicate selected blocks across TP ranks for tensor parallelism over slow inter-node links
summary: ### Motivation Tensor parallelism across nodes linked by commodity Ethernet (25 GbE RoCE between workstations or DGX Spark-class boxes) pays one all-reduce per block per step. At decode batch sizes that all-reduce is latency-bound: we measured about 66 us for TP4 and 36-40 us for TP2 over 25 GbE at batch 1 (inside a CUDA graph), against 2-3 us on one PCIe node. That is the same order as reading a mixer's weights from HBM, so for some blocks it is cheaper to keep the block whole on every rank (replicate it) and skip its all-reduce than to shard it. Replicating a block costs each rank (1 - 1/TP) x W extra bytes of resident weights and of reads per step, and saves one all-reduce. With weight bandwidth BW and all-reduce time t_AR(T) for a step of T tokens, it pays when (1 - 1/TP) x W / BW < t_AR(T). Prefill matters: under steady load each prompt is prefilled inside other requests' decode steps, and those steps carry multi-MB all-reduces, which is why replication gains most at high concurrency. ### Proposal 1. **Per-model opt-in replication of selected blocks** (attention, linear-attention/Mamba mixers, FFN), built on `disable_tp=True` for the block's linear layers and skipping the block's all-reduce. Each model declares which blocks can be replicated; MoE experts, embeddings and lm_head stay sharded. The model PRs below do this behind experimental environment flags, one per model, to gather evidence before proposing a common interface. 2. **Cold planning (knapsack).** Which blocks to replicate is a multiple-choice knapsack: each block chooses sharded or replicated, the value is

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Pack the decode sparse-MLA ragged top-k in one launch from the MXFP4 indexer's row bounds
summary: ## Overview On gfx950 with the MXFP4 sparse indexer and no `--monokernel`, every DeepSeek-V4.1 index layer converts its decode top-k into the ragged form sparse MLA reads: global slot ids, indptr and lengths. Main builds it in 4 launches per index layer: a count kernel, a zero fill, a cumsum and a pack. This PR builds it in 1. Each row's length is `min(topk, row_len)`, where `row_len` is the bound the indexer's top-k already ran over, so the count and the scan are not needed. Over the 8 index layers this removes 24 of the 32 launches per decode step, with identical output. It runs on the layouts that decode without `--monokernel`: DEP8 (C128 and up), 2x TP4+EP4 (C64), and TP2 steps of more than 48 rows (C32). Since #66047, a TP>1 decode step of 64 or more rows narrows the indexer's `decode_row_lens` to the rank's own shard. The PR therefore keeps the whole step's bounds in `decode_step_row_lens`, set before the narrowing. Every rank's top-k rows are all-gathered before the pack runs, so the bounds of the whole step are the right ones. Part of a series that trims the DSv4.1 sparse-indexer launch overhead on MI355X, after #63888: #67363, #67364, #67366, #67367 and #67368. This PR is independent of the others. ## Performance vs main Setup: - Base: stock `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2`, AITER 0.1.29. Every file this PR touches, and the indexer ops it reads, is identical to main 2c1fc9b3d3 (this PR's base). The md5s inside the containers matched. - This PR: the same image with the PR's two Python files mounted over it. - Hardware and model: MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1

With PCP=8, a 1-2 token prefill step leaves 6-7 of the 8 ranks with no row of that prefill. That happens in practice when a KV connector (for example LMCache) loads every prompt token except the last one, so the step schedules a single-token prefill. title: [Distributed] Opt-in FP16 partial sums for tensor-parallel row-parallel layers
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With tensor parallelism every row-parallel layer (`o_proj`, `down_proj`, linear-attention `out_proj`) rounds its per-rank partial sum to BF16 before the all-reduce, while a single GPU rounds the full sum once. The extra rounding is small on average but explodes where the two halves cancel, which is frequent: on real Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-14B activations at TP=2, outputs whose error exceeds 1% of the row's RMS occur **4.75x / 5.53x as often as on one GPU**. Converting the BF16 partials to FP32 before the all-reduce (#50972) cannot help at TP=2: the rounding has already happened, and the result is bit-identical. This PR adds `VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS=1` (off by default): the row-parallel GEMM writes its partial sum in FP16 (8x finer than BF16, same bytes on the wire), the all-reduce runs in FP16, and the output is rounded to BF16 once, after the sum, as on one GPU; an exact power-of-two prescale (2^-2 by default) keeps partial sums far from the FP16 range limit. The large-error events return to the single-GPU level, and the BF16 output gets measurably closer to an FP32 reference than both TP=2 today and TP=1. The cost is up to ~1% in throughput, plus a higher activation peak in the unquantized path (see Tradeoffs). **Not a duplicate of #50972.** That PR upcasts the BF16 partial sums to FP32 before the all-reduce; at TP=2 this is bit-identical to today (`bf16(a) + bf16(b)` is exact in FP32), because the extra rounding happens earlier, when each rank's GEMM writes BF16. This PR changes the precision of the partial sums themselves. Related:

title: [Spec Decode] Exclude invalid draft logits from the acceptance estimator
summary: ## Overview Malformed draft logits can enter the online acceptance estimator as calibration observations and distort acceptance estimates for subsequent valid drafts. This change hardens the online estimator by excluding undefined draft distributions (a NaN or +inf logit, or every logit -inf) from the fit and assigns them zero confidence, deprioritizing their verification. Related: #68164, #66673, #57533 (see Details). ## Claims - Rows containing a NaN or +inf after temperature scaling, or containing only -inf, store feature 0, confidence 0, and `valid = False`. They contribute nothing to the IRLS statistics (`info`, `grad`, `counts`), even if admitted for verification. - Valid rows retain the existing scoring behavior, including one-hot distributions with a feature clamped to `+MAX_LOG_ODDS`. title: [Qwen3.5] FP16 partial sums for the deferred row-parallel all-reduces
summary: ## Overview This is a follow-up to #61888 and is stacked on it: the diff specific to this PR is 28e9e006 plus the `main` merges (through #61888's branch) and the docstring commit on top of it, and I'll rebase once #61888 lands. #61888 adds an opt-in flag (`VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS`) that makes tensor-parallel row-parallel layers exchange their partial sums in FP16 instead of BF16, so the result is rounded once, as on a single GPU. Since #64723, Qwen3.5 on NVIDIA no longer all-reduces inside those layers: it defers the all-reduce to the next norm. The flag therefore never reaches them. On Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 at TP=2, flag on and flag off give identical logprobs. This PR makes the deferred path carry FP16 partial sums too, on GPUs where that all-reduce isn't fused into the norm by FlashInfer (anything but SM90/SM100-class). The norm that receives the sum undoes the 2^-k prescale itself. For the quantized case this happens inside the existing Triton norm kernel, so there's no extra launch, and the result is bit-identical to unscaling first. On the 27B, decode at batch 1 is 0.7% slower with the flag. A simpler version that kept the all-reduce in the layers cost 3.3%, because this path runs without torch.compile and the unscale became a separate kernel in every layer. With the flag off, or on SM90/SM100, nothing changes. <details> <summary>How it works, tests and numbers</summary> **Change** - `deferred_fp16_partial_sums()` (context manager in `linear.py`): row-parallel layers built inside it with `reduce_results=False` write FP16 partial sums when their kernel can, under the sam

title: [Bugfix] deepseek_v32: honor the decoder's deferred MoE all-reduce on the naive all2all path
summary: ## Summary Every deepseek_v32-NVIDIA decoder builds its MoE with `reduce_results=False` and performs the all-reduce itself in the next layer's `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`. When the MoE runs the naive all-gather/reduce-scatter all2all container (EP on, TP>1, prefill CP>1), the build-time formula in `fused_moe/layer.py` also clears `skip_final_all_reduce`, so the runner all-reduces as well. Every MoE layer's output then enters the residual stream scaled by `tp_size`. Serving `nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` in that shape silently returns garbage (GSM8K 0.00 on 0.31.0 and 0.32.0; mechanism and full measurements in #62945). This adds a module-level helper in the NVIDIA decoder, `_defer_moe_allreduce(moe_cfg)`, called once after the MoE build, which restores `skip_final_all_reduce=True` on exactly that path (`use_ag_rs_all2all_kernels and not is_sequence_parallel`). The AMD variant already defers decoder-side the same way for its non-MoRI backends (`deepseek_v32/amd/model.py:86-94`). Nothing else changes: no-all2all layouts already defer, self-reducing combines (DeepEP, MoRI, NIXL, MoonEP, both NVLink pairs, passthrough) return the output reduced and stay protected by the runner's coexist assertion, and sequence parallel owns its own reduction. The deeper fix, making the `layer.py` formula consult `output_is_reduced()` and the caller's `reduce_results` so no decoder-side override is needed, is a good follow-up discussion; this change is kept minimal and inside what was measured. The MoRI-style `zero_mlp_output` covers the self-reducing corner at TP>1 (AMD precedent, unmeasured here). ## Te

title: [Perf] tokenizer_manager: Drop the prompt token list once a single request is dispatched
summary: ## Motivation `GenerateReqInput.input_ids` stays a Python `list[int]` for the whole request, because `ReqState.obj` holds the request until it finishes. With long agentic prompts (0.5-1M tokens) at high concurrency, the tokenizer manager process holds tens of millions of list elements in the young GC generations. Every gen0/gen1 collection walks all of them, about 8-9 ns per element, so the process stalls for 0.2-0.5 s per collection. Clients see these stalls as mid-stream gaps in the token stream. A PD decode gateway hits this hardest: it serves the full prompt of every in-flight request for the whole length of its decode. ## Modifications - `TokenizerManager.generate_request`, single-request path: after `_send_one_request`, `obj.input_ids` is set to `None`, so the prompt list is freed by refcount instead of living in the young GC generations until the request finishes. The scheduler already has its own `array('q')` copy. - The release is skipped while something reads `obj.input_ids` after dispatch: request logging at `--log-requests-level` 2 or 3, `--export-metrics-to-file`, request dumps (`dump_requests_folder`) and crash dumps (`--crash-dump-folder`). These keep the original list, so their output, dump loading and multimodal requests are unchanged; such deployments keep today's GC behavior. - Nothing else reads `obj.input_ids` after dispatch (the OpenAI chat path reads it only before dispatch; batch requests are unchanged). - Request and crash dumps can be turned on at runtime (`/configure_logging`). title: [Perf] [AMD] triton: Scale KV cache writes out of place and drop the extend K/V clones
summary: ## Motivation `TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend` clones K and V before every scaled KV write only because the MHA pools' `set_kv_buffer` divides the caller's `cache_k`/`cache_v` by the scale in place; this PR makes the pools scale out of place and drops the two clones, removing two full K/V copies per extend call with identical KV cache bytes. The clone runs for non-MLA triton extend whenever `layer.k_scale` is set, which FP8/Quark/ModelOpt checkpoints do (1.0 when they ship no KV scale), so it also runs with the default bf16 KV cache. On ROCm the default MHA backend is aiter, so with default flags only MiniMax-M3 reaches it (its override selects triton on HIP), on dense layers 0-2 of 60. The saving there is 2-20 us per call. Other models reach it with `--attention-backend triton` and a quantized checkpoint. Related: #42181 (closed, unmerged) removed the clones by dividing on the triton side and leaving the pool in place. That also divides when the KV cache is bf16, where the pool skips scaling: in the micro below it is 13-61% slower than main on that case, and it changes the stored KV when the layer scale is not 1. #31652 (open) fuses the FP8 store on CUDA sm89+ but keeps the eager `div_` and the clones. ## Modifications - `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer`, `MHATokenToKVPoolFP4.set_kv_buffer`, `MHAView.set_kv_buffer` and the eager fallback of `_set_mha_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` use `torch.div(x, scale, out=torch.empty_like(x))` instead of `x.div_(scale)`. `out=` keeps the input dtype, so aiter's shape-[1] fp32 scale does not promote bf16 to fp32 and the result matches `div_`.

One launch checks shard membership, maps original and added vocabulary IDs, reads the local weight rows, and writes zeros for out-of-shard tokens. The existing TP AllReduce combines shard outputs. The standalone Ascend token-remapping kernel covers lookups that still use the separate gather path. The token-remapping work follows sgl-project/sglang#48050. - Fuse page-table construction for fixed-width `TARGET_VERIFY` graph replay on the Kimi K3.1 target and the supported DFlash2 MLA draft. title: [Fix] speculative: Prevent draft deadlock under DP attention when the DSA seed is missing
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention and EAGLE/NEXTN (topk 1) on a DSA model whose draft seeds its sparse attention from the draft extend (`seed_dsa_topk_from_draft_extend`, IndexShare), the decode server deadlocks on the first decode round whose batch has no seed. In PD disaggregation with a target-only prefill server every request arrives unseeded, and so does the PD warm-up request, so a decode server started with `--enable-dp-attention` never becomes healthy. `EAGLEWorkerV2.draft()` drops the draft CUDA graph (eager draft) when `draft_input.dsa_topk_indices is None`. The check is per rank, so under DP attention it is true only on the rank that holds the new request. The draft's MoE collectives span all attention-DP ranks: that rank drafts eagerly while its peers replay the draft graph and move on to target verify, and the collectives no longer pair up. Stacks on the hang: DP0 inside the eager NextN forward (`moe_fused_gate`), DP1-3 in target-verify metadata, all host threads in `cuModuleLoadData` behind NCCL kernels that never complete. ## Modifications Under DP attention (`get_parallel().enable_dp_attention`), skip this fallback so every rank replays the draft graph. The draft graph runner already zero-fills a missing seed (`buffers.dsa_seed_topk[:raw_bs].zero_()`), so that round's draft is rejected by verify and the next draft extend publishes a real seed. Without DP attention nothing changes. - Scope: DP attention + EAGLE/NEXTN + a DSA model with draft-extend seeding + a decode batch without a seed + a CUDA-graph-eligible decode. title: [Fix] distributed: Give the attention-TP subgroup a PyNCCL communicator under attention DP
summary: ## Motivation Without attention DP, the attention-TP group is the TP group, which has a PyNCCL communicator. With attention DP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a separate attention-TP subgroup with `use_pynccl=SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP or enable_symm_mem`, normally false. The override dates from the first attention-DP group; token-id sync now runs on the torch process group and does not use it. The other derived groups (`dcp`, `attn_cp`, `shared_experts_tp`) take the default, which is PyNCCL on. So under attention DP with attention TP above 1, collectives that need PyNCCL on the attention-TP group (`all_gatherv`, `reduce_scatterv`, the PyNCCL broadcast under graph capture) are unavailable, and callers that check for the communicator silently fall back. One observed case is the DSA indexer. For prefill extends of at least `tp_split_min_rows` rows it splits its logits and top-k rows across the attention-TP group and gathers the top-k back with `all_gatherv`; `_indexer_tp_split` returns `None` when the group has no PyNCCL, so every rank scores every row. Kimi-K3.1 prefill on GB300, AgentX traces, torch traces of rank 0 over the same 10 s window, per forward: | | TP8/DCP8 | attn DP 2 x (TP8, DCP8), replica 0 | |---|---:|---:| | `sm100_mqa_logits` (indexer logits) | 13.5 ms, 96 calls | 111 ms, 216 calls | | `topk_ragged` | 4.6 ms | 41 ms | | Forward | 0.42 s | 0.59 s | | Server log "rows split across attn-TP (tp=8)" | yes | no | ## Modifications - The attention-TP subgroup built under attention DP now takes the default `use_pynccl`, like the `dcp`, `attn_cp` and `shared_expert

summary: ## Motivation The nightly NPU case `qwen3.6-27b W8A8 1p in3k5/out1k5 GPQA` (`test/registered/npu/accuracy/qwen3_6_27b/test_npu_qwen3_6_27b_w8a8_1p_in3k5_out1k5_50ms_gpqa.py`, part of `nightly-acc-test-2-npu-a3`) fails on Ascend A3 with a host-side OOM: - `torch.OutOfMemoryError`: `NPU error code is: 207001`, raised by torch_npu's `CachingHostAllocator` when the pinned host memory cache is exhausted. - The pytest process is then killed with exit code 137 while the host memory allocated through `aclrtMallocHost` keeps growing (pinned memory is not accounted in the container cgroup without kmem accounting). Root cause on the test side: 3.5k-token prompts combined with a high concurrency cap (`--max-running-requests 64`) keep many small pinned int64 index tensors alive per in-flight request. `torch_npu`'s `CachingHostAllocator` never returns cached pinned blocks to the OS, so pinned host memory grows until it is exhausted. title: [Feat] scheduler: Keep a reserve of KV and state slots for cached prefixes (--prefill-cache-reserve)
summary: ## Motivation On multi-turn agent traffic the prefix cache collapses once the sessions' contexts no longer fit next to the running requests. GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2x B200 (TP2, the 0.9 split that was its default before #50018: 2,969,600 KV tokens, 419 state slots) with coding-agent sessions of about 75K tokens, `lru`: the hit rate is 0.91 at 16 sessions, 0.43 at 40 and 0 at 64. At 64 sessions 58 running requests hold 98% of the KV pool. A session that steps out for a tool call leaves its KV evictable, the next prefill takes it, and the session comes back to a full recompute. The extra prefill keeps decode waiting, so requests hold their KV longer and the next round loses more. The eviction order can't fix this: on the same setup (runs on #49430's branch, where `lru` is main's policy and the policy was still called `gds`; #49430 was reverted in #50118 and is now the opt-in `state_cost` in #50122) `lru` and `gds` both had a 0 hit rate at 64 sessions, since almost nothing is left to choose from. `--enable-session-radix-cache` (#29173) only evicts unreferenced KV first; with every session still open all of it is referenced, so I did not expect it to help and did not measure it. Admission can: a request that reuses little of the cache should wait for running requests to finish rather than take the room other sessions are about to come back to. This adds `--prefill-cache-reserve R` (off by default). title: [Fix] [XPU] graph: Retain capture inputs and reset graphs in FullXPUGraphBackend
summary: ## Motivation In SGLang, device graphs capture and record raw GPU virtual addresses rather than retaining Python object references. During graph capture (e.g., under data parallelism where dummy batches instantiate capture-only metadata tensors such as `global_num_tokens_gpu`), these temporary tensors must be preserved across the graph's lifetime to prevent Python GC from collecting them. If collected, the PyTorch caching allocator may reassign their underlying memory while the graph actively replays, resulting in dangling pointers, silent memory corruption, or illegal memory access errors. While `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` tracks and retains `capture_inputs`, `FullXPUGraphBackend` previously accepted the `capture_inputs` parameter in `capture_one()` but omitted storing it. Additionally, captured graphs were not explicitly reset upon backend `cleanup()`. ## Modifications 1. **Retain Capture Inputs in `FullXPUGraphBackend`** (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/graph_runner/xpu_full_graph_backend.py`): - Initialized `self._capture_inputs: Dict[Any, Any] = {}` in `__init__`. - Stored `self._capture_inputs[shape_key] = capture_inputs` in `capture_one()` so that capture-time tensor lifetimes are preserved across the backend lifecycle. - Cleared `self._capture_inputs.clear()` in `cleanup()`. 2. **Explicitly Reset Graphs upon Cleanup** (`xpu_full_graph_backend.py`): - Called `graph.reset()` on all captured `XPUGraph` instances during `cleanup()` to ensure allocated memory pool segments are cleanly released back to the driver. ## Accuracy Tests - **XPU Graph Metadata & Capture

This PR uses it, and lets the slice GEMM store straight into the plane (peer-store epilogue) so only FlashInfer's consumer runs. It also enables the path on SM107 and up to 1024 tokens at TP4. Depends on flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9732; the FlashInfer pin needs a release that includes it. ## Modifications - `muse_spark_gemm_ag.py`: - `gemm_ag_norm_fp4_quant` runs the peer-store GEMM, then `all_gather_rmsnorm_fp4_quantize(None, ..., num_tokens=m)`. - If the GEMM has no peer-store epilogue, it runs `gemm_local` and the op publishes the slice. - The FlashInfer workspace is built on the lease's push plane, one per (lease, width), and compiled for each eps on first use (warmup). - `unquant.py`: `bf16_gemm_peer_store` runs the split-K / warp split-K / low-latency GEMM and tactic that `bf16_gemm_dispatch` would run, stored into the push plane. title: [Fix] spec: DSpark simulated acceptance draws the stop-row bonus from the rejection residual (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation Benchmarks pin speculative acceptance with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected` and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token`. Under these settings, DSpark commits: - the sampled draft chain at the forced positions; - one bonus token at the stop row. That bonus is currently a plain draw from the target distribution p. A real rejection at that row would resample from the residual max(p − q, 0), which excludes the draft's proposal at its draft probability. With the plain draw, the stop token can re-pick exactly what the draft proposed. On long generations the committed text then collapses into short repeated phrases. In a DSV4.1-Flash DEP4 decode run at 136 requests per rank, OSL 2000-6000, AL 2.90, temperature 1.0, about 60 streams per arm, measured as the zlib compression ratio of the last 4000 characters of each response: | setting | streams in tight loops (ratio < 0.05) | ratio p50 | |---|---:|---:| | simulated acceptance, plain stop-row bonus (today) | 13-22% | 0.45-0.46 | | real verification (no simulation) | 0% | 0.47 | | simulated acceptance, residual stop-row bonus (this PR) | 0% | 0.54 | Two control checks: - Forcing an argmax draft (`SGLANG_DSPARK_USE_GREEDY_DRAFT=1`) raises the loop share to 61%, so the default draft does sample. - Drawing a per-request accepted length instead of one length per step only lowers the loop share to 10%. A longer model context, such as GLM-5.3's 1048576, is capped by default, and a longer `--context-length` is rejected at startup. - The reserve formula in `allocation_sizing.py` moved into pure functions, so the cap and the allocator share it. title: [Perf] [AMD] quantization/fp8: Use the CK bpreshuffle GEMM for dense block-FP8 on gfx942
summary: ## Motivation On MI300X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP8) runs its dense block-FP8 linears through aiter's CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`, which has been the gfx942 default since #43815. gfx95 already preshuffles these weights at load and calls `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, but gfx942 doesn't. At decode sizes the two CK kernels are about the same, but at prefill sizes the plain CK kernel is no faster than Triton, while bpreshuffle is 4-5x faster. This PR brings the same preshuffle + bpreshuffle path to gfx942. It doesn't add a new environment variable. Instead, it follows the existing `SGLANG_AITER_GFX942_BLOCKSCALE_USE_CK` switch, so it's on by default, and setting the switch to `0` still falls back to Triton as before. On 8x MI300X it gives +7-11% throughput and 16-19% lower TTFT at concurrency 16-32 on 8k/1k, and +3.5-4.5% throughput on AgentX. ## Modifications - `fp8.py`: on gfx942 with the CK path on, preshuffle dense block-FP8 weights at load, same as gfx95. Only layers with `N % 64 == 0` are preshuffled, which the CK bpreshuffle instances need. - `fp8_utils.py`: a weight preshuffled at load takes `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` with the column-major scale. Other layers are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi30x-20261020`. The CK and Triton rows use the image's own, older SGLang (before #43815). | Config | Strict-match | Flexible-extract | |---|---:|---:| | Triton, TP8 | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | 0.9636 | | CK, TP8 | 0.9712 ± 0.0046 | 0.9659 | | This PR, TP8 | 0.9666 ± 0.0049 | 0.9629

title: [Feat] [AMD] mori: Add the AMD_GEM custom memory pool for KV caches on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation amdgpu-dkms counts `hipMalloc` memory that a NIC pins twice in the KFD allocation limit: - on 30.x, for dma-buf registrations (the only kind on hosts without peer memory, such as VMs); - on 31.10 – 31.60, for every registration. See ROCm/mori#721. MoRI registers the whole KV pool, which takes most of `--mem-fraction-static`. Once the registered size exceeds the VRAM left after allocating it, every later device allocation of the server fails. With PD over MoRI, every decode rank dies with `Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 209` at the first request. Models with small weights per GPU, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, hit this at any usual fraction. No public amdgpu-dkms release has the driver fix. This PR is the MoRI counterpart of the `AMD_GEM` pool that @llying-001 proposed for Mooncake in #50938 (with kvcache-ai/Mooncake#5583, #5584 and #5587). The idea and design come from her work: keeping KV caches in amdgpu GEM BOs imported into HIP, pinning each one with a one-page dma-buf MR, and registering them only through their dma-buf. Many thanks to @llying-001 for working this out. **Draft:** - It should follow #50938, so that the two backends' `AMD_GEM` pools stay consistent. - It needs ROCm/mori#1051, which adds `mori.io.HipGemAllocator`. ## Modifications - `SGLANG_MORI_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=AMD_GEM`: `maybe_init_custom_mem_pool` returns a `torch.cuda.MemPool` backed by `mori.io.HipGemAllocator`. - KFD counts its amdgpu GEM BOs once, and mori registers them through their own dma-buf. - Every KV pool that goes through `maybe_init_custom_mem_pool` uses it, including the DSV4 pools
