title: [Feat] [AMD] linear-attn: Add FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
summary: ## Motivation AITER ships fused FlyDSL implementations of the GDN prepare stages and the K5 state scan for AMD gfx95. Qwen3.5-397B has 45 Gated DeltaNet layers, and at TP4 each rank runs them with 4 key heads, 16 value heads and K=V=128. On those shapes the FlyDSL path runs a prefill batch 1.4-1.74x faster than SGLang's Triton GDN prefill. This PR exposes that path as an opt-in prefill backend: ```bash --linear-attn-prefill-backend flydsl ``` Decode and speculative verification stay on Triton. The backend requires gfx95 and is rejected with deterministic inference or multi-item scoring. It also serves batches that track Mamba state for the radix cache, so it stays active with radix cache on (e.g. AgentX). It falls back to Triton for unsupported input/state shapes, mixed batches, and graph-planned paths. ## Modifications - Register `flydsl` in the linear-attention backend enum and CLI choices. - Add `FlyDSLGDNKernel`, which runs AITER's FlyDSL prepare, FlyDSL K5 state scan, and output stages. - Calls the stages directly instead of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk`, which only returns `(o, final_state)`. Radix-cache Mamba tracking needs the per-chunk states `h`, so the adapter keeps them. - Uses SGLang's native `[N, H, V, K]` state pool with indexed in-place updates, reuses the caller-provided output buffer, and remaps DP-attention padding indices to the pool's padding slot once per batch. - `use_exp2=True` (FlyDSL's fused prepare owns the gate cumsum). Recurrent state follows `--mamba-ssm-dtype`; per-chunk snapshots are bf16. - Requires AITER with the `gated_delta_net` module

summary: ## Motivation In an eager prefill or extend forward, a TP MoE layer of GLM-5-Next runs three steps: - the AITER fused MoE for the routed experts; - the shared expert (separate GEMMs, or one more expert slot when fused); - the TP all-reduce. The expert-parallel AMD MegaMoE path (`--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`) is not touched here. This PR adds `--enable-aiter-mega-moe-tp` (default off). With it, eager extend forwards of 1 to 4096 tokens make one MegaMoE-TP call per MoE layer. Scope: - Models: `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (e.g. `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) with MXFP4 experts on the AITER MoE runner; with the option on, any other model is refused at load. - Not reached: the GLM-5 NextN draft model, the other `DeepseekV2MoE` hosts, CUDA and CPU. - Platform: ROCm, `gfx950`, TP 2 to 8 on one node. - Measured at TP 2 in both shared-expert layouts: - unfused (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`): main's TP 2 configuration, since on HIP main fuses the shared expert only at TP 4 and TP 8; - fused: with #46578, which admits fusion at TP 2. - AITER: ROCm 10 images that ship the HIP runtime in both `_rocm_sdk_core` and `_rocm_sdk_devel` need an AITER build with ROCm/aiter#6398. - SGLang's `gfx950-rocm1000` image pins `285579b6`, before it; #50759 moves the pin past it. - With an older AITER, its loader maps a second HIP runtime beside torch's, `hipIpcGetMemHandle` rejects torch's allocation, and loading fails with

title: [Feat] openai: Support DSV4.1 dynamic tools in Responses and Messages
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4.1 loads tools during a conversation. Responses clients use `tool_search` / `tool_search_output`; Messages clients use `defer_loading`, `tool_reference` and `tool_addition`. Bridging these requests through Chat Completions loses the discovered schemas and their positions, so the model does not see the `### Updated Tool Schemas` block at the point where the tool becomes available. ## Modifications Native rendering is selected only for DSV4.1 requests that use these capabilities. Other models and ordinary Chat Completions, Responses and Messages requests keep their existing paths. - Convert the original Responses or Messages body once with `deepseek-recipe`, obtaining prompt ids, ordered image inputs and the tools callable after the history from the same `Conversation`. - Inject the prepared prompt into the shared Chat serving path for grammar, stop handling, scheduling, streaming and output parsing. There is no parallel request hierarchy or second prompt conversion. - Preserve thinking/effort settings, strict tool schemas, named/required tool choice and loaded-tool filtering. The response store remains optional; clients can replay complete input histories without it. Responses: - Support client-executed `tool_search`, typed `tool_search_call` output and streaming events, `tool_search_output` history and response-store replay. - Support function and namespace discovery, `apply_patch` custom-tool discovery, and top-level deferred declarations loaded by a search result. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dspark: Stage draft DP-MoE token counts through persistent buffers
summary: ## Motivation Under DP-MoE sync, `DraftBlockProposer._fill_dp_moe_sync_metadata` builds two fresh pinned `torch.tensor`s each decode step and copies them H2D: the draft's `global_num_tokens_gpu` and `global_num_tokens_for_logprob_gpu`. The draft ForwardBatch also gets a fresh `global_num_token_non_padded` H2D twice, once when it is built and once in the fill. summary: This PR is the second of three PRs split from sgl-project/sglang#38658. It enables `load_mode=prefetch` under pipeline parallelism and can be merged independently of the flush fix. ## Summary The linker reuses HiCache’s request-arrival hook and `pp_prefetch_ticketed` marker. PP0 issues tickets in arrival order, and each stage binds the ticket to its local request. The linker manages its own reservations, reads, and publication. title: [Fix] mamba: isolate one sequence's non-finite input from others in the same chunk
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51108. The SSD chunk-state and chunk-scan kernels zero out another sequence's contribution to a dot product by multiplying it by a clean 0.0. But `0 * inf` (and `0 * nan`) is still `nan` under IEEE 754, regardless of which operand supplied the zero. If one sequence's x or B tensor has a non-finite value, it silently leaks through `tl.dot` into every other sequence sharing the chunk — including their cached SSM state, which then stays wrong for all later decode steps. ## Modifications Sanitize x and B right after loading in both `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` and `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, replacing non-finite elements with 0 before they reach any multiply or dot. `v - v` is 0 for finite v and nan for +-inf/nan — the same idiom already used in this codebase's `fla/route.py` for nan handling. This only changes behavior when a non-finite value is present; output is bit-identical for ordinary finite inputs (checked with and without `seq_idx` batching). Added a regression test (`test_mamba_chunk_scan_isolates_nonfinite_request`) via the public `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` API, reproducing the issue exactly. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on an RTX 4090: - New test fails on unpatched code (30/30 non-finite outputs, non-finite final state) and passes with this fix. - Full existing `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` suite (371 cases) still passes. - Bit-identical output and final state on normal finite inputs, patched vs. unpatched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `mamba_chunk_scan_combined`, median ms/iter over 50 iters, warmed up, RTX 4090: | config | unpatched | patched | delta | |---

title: [Fix] gemm: Use int64 row offsets in block-scaled FP8/INT8 matmuls
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51098. The block-scaled FP8 and INT8 Triton matmuls compute `offs_am * stride_am` and `stride_cm * offs_cm` with int32 row offsets. Once `M * K` (A) or `M * N` (C) reaches 2^31 elements, the offsets wrap and the kernels read A and write C out of bounds. Example reach from the issue: Qwen3-32B-FP8 at TP1, gate_up projection (N = 51,200), from about 41.9k tokens in one forward. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py` and `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/int8_kernel.py`: `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, its Hopper and gfx1250 variants, and `_w8a8_block_int8_matmul` take a `USE_INT64_OFFSETS` constexpr that promotes `offs_am` and `offs_cm` to int64. The launchers set it only when A or C has at least 2^31 elements, so every other shape compiles the original int32 kernel unchanged. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: the same for the group offset in `_per_token_group_quant_int8` (the FP8 quantizers already use int64 here), set only when the input has at least 2^31 elements. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_block_matmul_large_m.py`: regression tests with M = 2^15 + 1 and a 2^16-wide dimension, so the last row starts past 2^31 elements: FP8 with rows of A past 2^31, FP8 with rows of C past 2^31, and INT8 through `apply_w8a8_block_int8_linear` (quantization plus matmul). title: [Fix] model_loader: Split checkpoint prefetch among each node's own ranks
summary: ## Motivation `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` splits the checkpoint's shards among a node's ranks, so that the node reads each shard once and the ranks' mmap loads hit the page cache. On multiple nodes, the split is wrong: - The split strides by `world_group.local_size or launch_world_size`. - On GPU, `LOCAL_SIZE` is never set, so the stride is the whole world size (`tp * pp`), while the offset `local_rank` is the GPU index. - With 4 nodes of 4 GPUs, every node prefetches the shards whose index `i` satisfies `i % 16 < 4`: the same quarter on every node. - The other three quarters are never prefetched on any node and are read through page faults during loading. ## Modifications The split now uses the number of ranks per node, `launch_world_size // nnodes` when `LOCAL_SIZE` is unset, and this rank's position on its node, `rank % ranks_per_node`. Ranks are numbered node by node. No option is added. Prefetch itself stays opt-in; #50342 (on by default) and #37806 (automatic on network filesystems) propose enabling it, and either would hit this bug on every multi-node run. ## Accuracy Tests Prefetch never changes which weights are loaded. title: [Feat] hicache: Release the host KV pool with the KV cache
summary: ## Motivation `release_memory_occupation(tags=["kv_cache"])` pauses the device KV pool and flushes the radix tree, but the HiCache host mirror keeps every page of host DRAM it allocated. An engine that offloads its KV cache between steps — the RL flow that swaps weights and caches while training — therefore holds the full host pool for no benefit. Measured on Ascend 910 with Qwen3-0.6B and `--hicache-size 8`: after a release of `kv_cache`, the 8 GB host pool was still resident, and only came back after the process dropped it manually (`torch_npu` host statistics: `allocated_bytes.current` stayed at 8 GiB after `del` + `gc`). ## Modifications New flag `--release-hicache` (default off, so existing deployments are unchanged). When it is set, the host pool follows the device KV cache: - `HostKVCache.release_memory_occupation()` / `resume_memory_occupation()`: release drops the payload buffers and every view or pointer table derived from them, empties the allocator state so no slot can be handed out from freed memory, and returns the pages to the OS; resume re-checks the host budget, re-allocates the pool and rebuilds the derived state. title: [Fix] [NPU] memory_saver: Forward positional graph arguments to the TMS adapter
summary: ## Motivation `TorchMemorySaverAdapter.cuda_graph()` only accepted keyword arguments, but the NPU graph runner captures decode graphs by passing the graph handle positionally: ```python # python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_cudagraph_backend.py graph_ctx = partial(self._memory_saver_adapter.cuda_graph, tag=GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH) ... graph_ctx(graph, pool=self._pool, stream=self._capture_stream, auto_dispatch_capture=True) ``` With pauseable graphs enabled (`--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH=1`), the engine therefore died on the first captured shape: ``` TypeError: _TorchMemorySaverAdapterReal.cuda_graph() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given ``` That path is what RL serving uses when it offloads KV cache and weights between training steps, so pauseable NPU graphs were unusable. ## Companion PR This is one half of a two-repo fix. sglang hands the graph handle and `auto_dispatch_capture=True` to the adapter; the NPU build of `torch_memory_saver` has to accept and forward both. That half is **sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#1069**. Neither PR is useful on its own, and they are meant to land together: | this PR | sgl-kernel-npu#1069 | decode-graph capture | | --- | --- | --- | | no | yes | `TypeError: _TorchMemorySaverAdapterReal.cuda_graph() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given` | | yes | no | `TypeError: TorchMemorySaver.cuda_graph() got an unexpected keyword argument 'auto_dispatch_capture'` | | yes | yes | capture succeeds, server serves and offloads | If they cannot land in the same window, merging this one first

title: [Perf] [AMD] qsa: Score decode rows with a grouped Triton kernel on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, the QSA indexer of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores the compressed keys of every decode, target-verify and draft-extend row with `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode`. In an MI355X trace of AgentX at concurrency 48 (NEXTN MTP with 4 draft tokens, so a verify step holds 44 requests x 4 rows = 176 rows), the call takes 0.693 ms per QSA layer: 8.3 ms of a 41.3 ms decode iteration across the 12 QSA layers. It reads the keys at about 0.5 TB/s, for two reasons: - Each draft row of a request reads the request's compressed keys again, although a request's rows share its page-table row and differ only in length, so a verify step moves 4x the key bytes it needs. - ROCm MFMA needs a 16-wide N dimension, so the 4 index heads are padded with 12 zero heads (`head_alignment = 16 if is_hip()`) and three quarters of the MFMA work multiplies zeros. ## Modifications Scope: ROCm only. CUDA, XPU, and the TileLang and torch kernels are unchanged. - `kernels/ops/attention/qsa_mqa_decode_triton.py` (new): a Triton paged decode scoring kernel with the contract of `tilelang_qsa_mqa_decode` for bf16 operands, `min_scored_len` included (rows at most that long are not scored and logits past each row's length are left unset, as `fast_topk` with k = 512 expects). A program scores `rows_per_group` consecutive rows that share one page-table row against a split of their keys: it loads each key tile once for the group, and the group's rows x heads form the N dimension of one dot (4 draft rows x 4 heads = 16 columns, no zero heads). The grid is (groups, splits) with about 11 programs per CU. `can_use_qsa_

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] megakernel-binding: Skip the Protocol check in megakernel_can_run_graph without a tensor entry
summary: ## Motivation `megakernel_can_run_graph` runs on every decode step, from `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.can_run_graph`. Since #48414 it calls `_decode_entry_kind`, which runs `isinstance(built, SupportsDecodeTensorEntry)`. `SupportsDecodeTensorEntry` is a `runtime_checkable` Protocol. When a build does not implement it, as with DeepSeek-V4.1, the check fails, and a failing runtime Protocol check walks the protocol members with `inspect.getattr_static`. That is host time on every decode step. Megakernel decode steps right after a prefill are host-bound, so it lengthens them. ## Modifications `megakernel_can_run_graph` returns `True` before the Protocol check when the installed megakernel has no tensor entry. The result is the same as before. The installer sets `tensor_entry` whenever `_decode_entry_kind(built)` is non-zero (the `if tensor_entry is None and _decode_entry_kind(built)` branch in `binding.py`), and `_tensor_entry` returns an adapter or raises. So a `None` tensor entry implies decode entry kind 0, for which the function already returned `True`. Builds with a tensor entry keep the existing check and dispatch. `megakernel_configure_aux` already tests `installed.tensor_entry is not None` the same way. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy run: the change is host-side dispatch only and returns the same value for every installed build (see above). ## Speed Tests and Profiling cProfile of the scheduler on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark (TP8 + EP2 on two GB300 trays, megakernel on, concurrency 1), 1500 decode `run_batch` calls, before this change: | frame | cumulative time per decode

title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3.1: Post a chunk's MoRI KV and state writes in one batch_write
summary: ## Motivation The prefill's MoRI sender calls `engine.batch_write` once per layer and once per state tensor, each with its own `allocate_transfer_uid`. For Kimi-K3.1 a request's last chunk is about 190 writes, so about 380 pybind calls, each releasing and retaking the GIL on a shard worker while the scheduler thread launches the next forward. Follow-up to #51000. ## Modifications - `SGLANG_OPT_MORI_COALESCE_TRANSFERS` (default off, prefill only): queue a chunk's KV and state writes and post them in one `batch_write`, one entry and transfer ID per buffer pair. The writes themselves are unchanged, so the decode side needs nothing. - If that `batch_write` raises, entries it already posted have no status to drain, so with deferred decode KV release the room is never acked and the decode waits out its release timeout. - KDA state blocks go through `_submit_batch_transfer_plan` so they are coalesced too. Aux is sent after all targets' KV and state, in both modes. ## Accuracy Tests Model outputs are not affected: the same RDMA writes are posted, in fewer calls. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Coalesced call vs the per-layer calls (15 writes: MLA, draft, KDA, DSA; local one-off check) | identical entries, same order | | `test_coalesced_post_failure_never_acks` (new) | passes; fails with the room poisoning removed | | `base-a-test-cpu`, run locally | same results as main | ## Speed Tests and Profiling CPU model of a Kimi-K3.1 last-chunk submission (191 writes): the real `MoriKVManager` sender over a stub engine whose calls release the GIL. No RDMA, and no isolated end-to-end A/B.

summary: ## Motivation #43463 bounds the decode indexer's work by the context length, but at the batch sizes we serve (112–256 verify rows) it launches 16 CTAs per row, so each CTA walks 1/16 of a long context serially. With MTP, the four verify rows of a request also read the same compressed keys four times. title: [Fix] scheduler: Free prefill KV before admitting instead of raising "Prefill out of memory"
summary: ## Motivation - Fixes #50790. With HiCache `write_back` and a full host pool, `evictable_size()` counts device KV that eviction cannot free. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qwen3.8: Fuse MoE finalize with the shared-expert gate
summary: ## Motivation In Qwen3.8's NVFP4 MoE block, the routed-expert finalize kernel and the shared-expert sigmoid gate + add run as two serial, latency-bound kernels on the critical path (~12.7 µs + 2.7 µs per layer at 256 tokens). ## Modifications - Use the existing deferred-finalize output (`do_finalize=False`) and add one Triton kernel that does the top-k weighted gather-sum, the sigmoid gate and the shared-expert add. - The kernel keeps the same FP32 accumulation order over k, rounds the routed sum to BF16 first, and reduces the gate with the same block size as the existing gate kernel, so the output is bitwise identical. - Enabled by default for the measured shape (CUDA, BF16, hidden 2560, top-10); other shapes and FP32 expert weights keep the existing path. - Tests: bitwise vs the unfused pair over production shapes with padded expert maps and strided GEMM output, CUDA graph replay, and the FP32 fallback. ## Accuracy Tests Bitwise identical to the unfused finalize + gate/add for 1–8192 tokens with synthetic weights, and with the real FlashInfer NVFP4 MoE at 64/256/384/1024 tokens. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All numbers: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on one Rubin (VR200) GPU, TP1, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN MTP (3 steps, 4 draft tokens), CUDA graphs on. - MoE tail per layer: 12.7 → 3.4 µs; full MoE layer in a CUDA graph at 256 tokens: 172.7 → 162.3 µs. - Decode step (concurrency 64, 8K, same node): 18.22 → 17.65 ms (−3.1%); repeated baseline 18.24 ms. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_

title: [Fix] dsv41: Build MegaGate row masks inside the decoder replay-tail graph capture
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51478. With MegaGate on and EPLB off, the decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs inside a serving forward, after two eager warm-ups of the same layers on a copy of the same batch. The per-forward row-mask cache from #46071 hands the warm-ups' eager masks to the capture, so the mask build is never recorded in the graph. Every replay then reads a valid-row mask computed for the step that captured the graph. Real rows past that count are routed as padding in the tail layers, and prompts whose tail runs from a graph (≤ 2048 tokens here) drift. ## Modifications - `layers/moe/mega_gate.py::_gate_row_masks`: the cache key gains `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`. A capture builds its own masks inside the graph, and the layers it captures still share them; eager forwards behave as before. The query runs only when the per-forward cache is active. - `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: a CPU test that runs an eager build and a capturing build in one forward scope and checks that the capture does not reuse the eager mask. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on 2× GB300, upstream `34dfaccc57` (the code path is unchanged on current `main`); config and method in #51478. Top-1 agreement with a MegaGate-off reference over 50 real text prompts, at positions where the reference's top-1 margin is above 1 nat: | arm | all prompts | ≤ 2048 tokens | > 2048 tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:| | MegaGate on, 3 independent boots | 96.64% / 96.77% / 96.78% | 69.7% | 99.4% | | MegaGate on + fix | 99.41% | 99.3% |

title: [RFC] HiCache: Size and stage for unified memory (GB10 / DGX Spark)
summary: On GB10 the GPU and CPU share one memory pool, so HiCache's L2 host tier holds no memory that the GPU pool doesn't also compete for. Measured on one DGX Spark (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, GPU KV capped at 512k tokens, 64 sessions x 6 rounds): | Arm | TTFT p50 / p99 | Hit rate | Peak page cache | |---|---|---|---| | GPU only | 6.4 / 20.6 s | 3.2% | - | | GPU + L2, same total budget | 6.4 / 20.7 s | 1.5% | - | | L3 NVMe, NIXL POSIX O_DIRECT, 4 GB `buffer_only` | 2.1 / 4.1 s | 71.4% | 29.2 GiB | | L3 NVMe, buffered `file` | 2.1 / 3.9 s | 71.4% | 65.8 GiB | Default auto-sizing gives L2 391k tokens against 3.65M on the device, and the server warns that L2 is less effective. Detection: on GB10 `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).is_integrated` (`CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_INTEGRATED`) is 1. A Grace-coupled discrete GPU such as GB200 also reports `PAGEABLE_MEMORY_ACCESS_USES_HOST_PAGE_TABLES = 1`, so that attribute cannot tell them apart. Allocating 8 GiB on the GB10 GPU lowered host `MemAvailable` by 8.13 GiB, and `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` reported 70 GiB free while the host reported 114 GiB available. Proposal, when the GPU shares memory with the host: 1. With an L3 backend, default `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only` and a small staging buffer instead of auto-sizing L2. 2. Without one, warn that L2 trades against GPU KV instead of adding to it. 3. Default file-based L3 to O_DIRECT, because page cache competes with GPU memory. 4. Log the detection, so it can be overridden. We'll send PRs and test them on Spark. Is this direction welcome, and is there already work on it?

title: [Fix] weight_update: Rebuild each CUDA-IPC tensor once for the target and draft runners
summary: ## Motivation `update_weights_from_tensor` deserializes the payload once in `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager`, then hands the same `LocalSerializedTensor` entries to every selected runner. Each runner's `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor` calls `_unwrap_tensor`, and `LocalSerializedTensor.get()` deserializes again, so with a speculative draft every producer CUDA-IPC handle is opened once per runner. title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Exchange K/V over device IPC instead of two NCCL all-gathers in 2-rank K/V-gather SP
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** `USPAttention._forward_with_kv_gather` calls `_gather_sharded_sequence` twice per attention layer, once for K and once for V. Those two `all_gather_into_tensor` calls are the only collectives in a FLUX.2 denoising step, and they are slow out of proportion to the bytes they move: on a gfx1250 socket a 25 MB/rank all-gather takes 446 us, an effective 56 GB/s, while a device copy of the same bytes takes 9.8 us. In a 2-step FLUX.2 trace the 432 RCCL kernels account for 219 ms of 1183 ms of GPU time, 18.5% of the step, to move data between two ranks that already have peer access to each other's memory. **Where it shows up** Any two-rank K/V-gather SP group pays this, on any device where the collective is slower than a peer-to-peer copy, and for any model that takes that path -- it is a property of the SP mode, not of FLUX.2. It is most visible when the two ranks are partitions of one socket, because the collective is then moving bytes that never had to leave the device. It reproduces on FLUX.2-dev at 720p with `--num-gpus 2` (`sp_degree=2`, `kv_gather_degree=2`) on two gfx1250 partitions; a single-GPU run has no SP group and is unaffected. The fix below is gated to ROCm and off by default, so no other platform changes behavior. **How to fix** Exchange the bytes the way the hardware already allows, and use a collective only for the ordering it is actually needed for: each rank copies K and V into a staging buffer the peer has mapped over device IPC, a one-element `all_gather_into_tensor` orders the two streams, and each rank reads the peer's half

A ranker only orders the queue: it reads requests and their prefix matches, and declares a match plan (`NoMatch`, `FullMatch`, `HeadWindowMatch`) plus a few hooks. summary: ## Motivation Closes #43196. A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside `load_weights`, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files. title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: Capture decoder-tail graphs at startup, never on a step a DP rank skips
summary: ## Motivation A DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill server can hang on its first busy prefill steps after startup. This happens with DP attention (attention TP 1), `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`, and decoder SWA bounded replay. Every DP rank stops. After 300 s, DeepGEMM's MegaMoE grid-sync timeout traps and the GPUs report Xid 43. A restart doesn't help: the next cold start can hang the same way. How it happens: 1. With MegaMoE and no DP gather in the graph, `prefill_graph_tolerates_sum_len()` lets each DP rank replay the prefill-graph bucket of its own token count. 2. The decoder replay tail (#45059, #45107) takes one of two forms, depending on the bucket: - In buckets of at least `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODER_TAIL_GRAPH_MIN_PREFILL_TOKENS` (2048), it runs as an eager break, `_tail_layers_in_prefill_graph`. The break replays row-bucket graphs of its own. - In smaller buckets, the tail layers, MegaMoE included, are recorded inline in the prefill graph. 3. The break captures a missing row-bucket graph on first use. `RowBucketGraphRunner._record` calls `tp_group.barrier()` before it captures. 4. Take a step where one rank's bucket is at least 2048 and another's is below 2048: - The first rank waits in the gloo barrier. - The second rank has already launched MegaMoE and waits in its grid sync for the first. - Neither can move. #45881 guards one variant of this: an idle rank, which never reaches the break. summary: ## Motivation D1 of #50943 (load-diff). A loader that hands a loaded model to another process must carry everything loading left in the model, not only its named parameters and buffers. title: [Feat] diffusion: Add expert parallelism for MoE DiTs
summary: ## Motivation MoE DiTs are growing, and SP shards activations but not experts: every rank still stores all routed experts. This PR adds expert parallelism (EP) to SGLang Diffusion, with LingBot-Video MoE (128 routed experts) as the first supported model. On 2×H100, EP2 cuts peak memory by 26.2 GB/GPU (43%) for 12% more latency. ## Modifications Two commits: 1. **Fix LingBot SP.** LingBot under SP produced wrong output before this PR (RoPE positions restarted at zero on every rank, and replicated text was gathered as distinct shards). It now shards video tokens inside the DiT, slices global RoPE positions per rank, and passes text as `num_replicated_suffix`. 81 frames are no longer rounded to 85. EP depends on this. 2. **Add EP.** `--ep-size`, a per-pipeline capability gate, expert-sharded checkpoint loading, and a fixed-capacity dispatcher. **Design decision: EP reuses the SP group (`ep_size == sp_degree`).** SP already gives every rank the same token count, so dispatch is one equal-split all-to-all with static shapes and no host sync. summary: [`ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826`](https://huggingface.co/ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-10B-A1.8B-0826) (`DeepseekV3BidirectionalModel`) is a DeepSeek-V3 backbone with bidirectional attention and normalized mean pooling: 26 layers, hidden size 1536, MLA attention, 64 routed experts with top-4 routing. It cannot be served today: 1. **No native implementation.** SGLang falls back to the Transformers backend, which treats the MLA layers as plain multi-head attention. The first request then fails while writing the MLA KV cache: `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (84352) must match the existing size (42) at non-singleton dimension 1. A bidirectional model must see its whole input in one pass: - with chunked prefill, the first chunk never attends to later tokens, and mean pooling covers only the last chunk; - with a radix-cache hit, the reused prefix KV was computed in another request's context. On Intel XPU, a 6,001-token input reached the absorbed-MLA prefill path on its second chunk. title: [Perf] Mamba2 _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel compiles during serving on NemotronH, stalling the first large prefills
summary: On a fresh server, the first large prefill bursts of NemotronH models log, on every TP rank: ``` Triton kernel '_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel' took 1.45 s to compile after serving started. Serving-time compilation can stall the engine; pre-compile it during engine init. ``` It compiles 2–3 times per rank (new specializations as prefill shapes grow), 2.5–3.6 s in total per rank, in every configuration I ran: Nemotron 3 Nano BF16 and Nano Omni BF16, TP4, on H100 and on GB200, with AllReduce fusion on or off, on `main` and on branches. Only compiles over the 1 s warning threshold are logged, so the real serving-time compile cost is somewhat higher. `py-spy` also caught `_chunk_state_fwd`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd` and the fused-MoE Triton kernel compiling during the first c=128 burst. This is one of the reasons the first high-concurrency run on a cold server is slower than later ones (on GB200 at c=128, a 256-prompt warmup took about 38 s against about 11 s once warm, for every arm, base included). Fix: pre-compile the Mamba2 chunked-scan kernels during engine init for the prefill shapes the server can produce (chunked prefill size, page size), as `precompile_rmsnorm` and friends do for their kernels.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Do not cache window-evicted KV in pure-SWA checkpoint
summary: ## Motivation For an all-sliding-window model without a prefill-aware window floor (`req.kv.window_evict_floor == 0`), `RadixCache.checkpoint`, which `PureSWARadixCache` uses, inserts the whole request row into the tree when the request finishes. During decode, `retire_window_rows` has already returned the slots between `cache_protected_len` and the window cursor to the allocator, so the tree takes ownership of free slots: - the allocator hands those slots to other requests while the tree still serves them, so a later prefix match reads another request's KV; - evicting the node frees them a second time, which puts duplicates on the free list. With one 4-token request, window 2 and eviction interval 1, after eight decode steps on main `b6d4389a`: ``` slots of positions [4, 8) already went back to the allocator: [5, 6, 7, 8] tree now caches 11 tokens of a, slots [1, ..., 11] slots both in the tree and on the free list: [5, 6, 7, 8] allocator: available 25 + tree evictable 11 = 36 of 32 request b was given tree-owned slots: [5, 6, 7] ``` This is the fix from #31486 by @v-code01, which was closed for inactivity without a review. The checkpoint code has been refactored since, so this applies the same boundary to the current `checkpoint` and adds a regression test. @v-code01 is credited as co-author. Reachability: the path needs a pure-SWA cache (no full-attention layers on the runner) and no prefill-aware floor. Unlimited-OCR uses `PureSWARadixCache`. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Snapshot host memory before any rank builds explicit-size HiCache pools
summary: ## Motivation With an explicit `--hicache-size` or `--hicache-ratio`, each HiCache host pool checks its allocation against the host memory free when that pool is built, divided by the number of ranks on the host (`host_memory_budget_plain_hugetlb`). The ranks on a host build their pools at the same time. A rank that reaches its check after its node mates have allocated therefore gets a share that their pools have already shrunk. Whether startup succeeds depends on the order the ranks run in, not on how much memory the host has. Example: a node runs 4 ranks, and each rank builds KV (60 GB), Mamba (72 GB) and DSA indexer (14 GB) host pools. That is ~146 GB per rank and ~583 GB per node, on nodes with ~699 GiB available. In one launch, a rank reached its Mamba check after its node mates had built most of their pools. It saw 240 GiB free, got a (240 - 10) GiB / 4 = 57.5 GiB (61.7 GB) share, below its 72 GB Mamba pool, and failed with `Not enough host memory available`, although the node had room. The same config passed in a launch where all 4 ranks checked before any of them had allocated. The auto-size path (neither flag set) does not have this race. It samples the budget, runs an all-reduce over the world group before building any pool, and books every pool against that one snapshot through `host_memory_budget_scope`. ## Modifications - `auto_size_hicache`: for explicit sizes, sample the budget, call a barrier on the world CPU group so no rank allocates before every rank has sampled, then book the rank's pools against that snapshot. title: [Fix] [XPU] compressed-tensors: Support W8A8 int8 on XPU and quantize Whisper MLP linears.
summary: ## Motivation `RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w8a8` is a compressed-tensors W8A8 int8 checkpoint: per-channel symmetric int8 weights, dynamic per-token symmetric int8 activations, `targets: [Linear]`, `ignore: []`. It cannot be served on Intel XPU, and once the load is unblocked it produces garbage output. There are four separate issues, and each one hides the next: 1. **No XPU kernel path.** `CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8` calls `sgl_kernel.int8_scaled_mm`, which sgl-kernel-xpu does not provide, so the scheme cannot load on XPU. title: [Fix] pd: Agree on requested abort vs error across PP and attention CP ranks
summary: Stacked on #47618. Only the last two commits belong to this PR; the earlier ones are #47618 and will drop out once it merges. ## Motivation With PP (or attention TP/CP) prefill in PD disaggregation, the release of an inflight transfer is agreed across ranks, but the *classification* of a failed transfer is still decided locally. When a request is aborted (client `AbortReq` or a decode-side abort), only the rank that saw the abort records an abort reason. A stage that finished its own transfer has no failure reason, so it concludes the same request as a transfer error and returns a 500 for a request the client aborted, while other stages finish it as an abort. ## Modifications - `disaggregation/common/conn.py`: `record_failure` replicates whether a stage's failure was a requested abort to PP0 through `PPConsensusStore`, before the Failed status on the same ordered channel; keys are cleaned up with the room. - `disaggregation/utils.py`: `TransferOutcome` and the PP / attention TP-CP outcome polls. PP0 forwards polls together with the terminal outcome, merged as ERROR < ABORT < SUCCESS: an error on any rank outranks an abort on another, and an abort is reported only if every failed rank recorded one. The same classification applies across attention TP/CP ranks without PP. - `disaggregation/prefill.py`: the inflight failure handler uses the agreed classification (abort → abort finish, not counted as a failure; error → 500) instead of the local exception. - `disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py`: record the decode-side abort reason, as NIXL already does. - Tests: `test_pp_prefill_rel

title: [Perf] kv-shard: Free sharded KV pages without a host sync
summary: Stacked on #47578. Only the last commit belongs to this PR; the first one is #47578 and will drop out once it merges. ## Motivation Under logical-page KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`), `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` returns each freed page to its owner class. `free_segment` derives the owners from the freed locs and splits the pages per class with `torch.unique` or a `bincount` whose counts go back to the host through `.tolist()`. That read waits on the scheduler stream, which can be queued behind an in-flight forward, so every request release and every eviction stalls the scheduler. The owner of position-page `P` on a chain is `(rotation_base + P) % N`, and the scheduler already knows the request's rotation base on the host, so the split can be computed without touching the device. ## Modifications - `free_segment`, `free_segments`, and the storage `free_units` / `free_token_rows` take an optional `rotation_base`. With it, `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` computes each class on the host: page `k` of the segment belongs to class `(rotation_base + start_pos // page_size + k) % N`, its pages are the stride slice `page_ids[k::N]`, and its count is closed-form. Grouped frees collect the slices per class and merge each class once at `free_group_end`. Debug mode still checks the host phase against the loc-derived owners. Without a rotation base the old path is unchanged. - Callers that free a request's row or tree values pass the base: - `release_kv_cache` and the overallocated-tail release pass `req.kv_rotation_base` through `free_kv_row` / `free_kv_row_segments`. - Tree n

title: [Fix] pd: Release PP prefill transfers via PP0 decision once every stage concludes
summary: ## Motivation With a pipeline-parallel prefill server in PD disaggregation, every PP stage must release an inflight request at the same step. Main does this with a ring consensus over the PP group (#47045 made the concluded outcome agree across stages). #45085 (WIP, @stepinto) replaces the ring with a simpler scheme: PP0 reads every stage's transfer status through `PPConsensusStore` and forwards its decision. Taken alone, that scheme releases too early. PP0 decides from `min()` over the stage statuses, so a Failed on one stage releases the request on every stage while another stage is still Transferring; that stage then frees KV pages and the metadata slot its transfer worker still reads. The staging Success hold (outstanding staging chunks, worker cleanup under `prefill_complete`) is also local to each stage, so PP0 only applies its own. This PR carries #45085 rebased onto current main (authorship preserved; happy to rebase onto it if it lands first) and makes the PP0 decision wait for every stage. The abort-vs-error classification that was previously part of this PR is now a separate PR stacked on this one: #51720. ## Modifications - `[Refactor]` (from #45085, @stepinto): PP0 polls every stage's status via `PPConsensusStore` and forwards the decision, replacing the ring consensus. A transfer that failed on any stage stays Failed, keeping the behavior of #47045. Separate P2P tags for the bootstrap and inflight PP syncs. - `[Fix]` A stage other than PP0 no longer polls its own senders, so a transfer it releases would skip the sender's conclusion side effects (trace finish,

title: [Perf] kv-shard: Batch PageInterleave allocator pops and frees per batch
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` is on the scheduler's critical path for every prefill batch and every KV release. Today its cost grows with the batch: - `alloc_extend` loops over requests and launches several small device ops per request: an `arange`/scatter for each owner class, plus offset math and a `cat`. - `free()` selects each owner class with a boolean mask, which costs one host sync per class. - `free_segment()` falls back to `free()`, so it runs a `torch.unique` and gets no benefit from the base class's stride-based fast path. ## Modifications All changes are in `mem_cache/allocator/page_interleave.py`. Allocation results are identical to the current implementation: the same pages, in the same order. - **`alloc_extend`** - Reads the host lengths once as Python ints. - Each owner class pops its whole-batch need in a single slice. - A numpy host plan maps every output row to a (popped page, in-page offset) pair. The device work is one H2D copy, one gather, and one multiply-add, so the number of device ops no longer depends on batch size. - The plan's H2D copy goes through a reused pinned buffer. A CUDA event makes sure the buffer is only reused after its previous copy has completed. - **Free path** - `free()` now goes through a shared `_free_pages()`. - `_free_pages()` computes per-class counts with `scatter_add_` and a single `.tolist()`, then does a stable argsort/split by owner. That is one host sync instead of one per class. - **`free_segment()`** - Now has a stride-based implementation: the start must be page-aligne

title: [Fix] pd: Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots
summary: ## Motivation On the PD **decode** side, `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` sizes the hybrid Mamba / linear-attention **speculative** scratch (`intermediate_ssm`, `intermediate_conv_window`, and the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv / N-gram scratch) by `size + pre_alloc_size`, where `pre_alloc_size = disaggregation_decode_extra_slots` reserves extra `req_to_token` slots for in-transfer (being-received-from-prefill) requests. In-transfer requests are not in the running batch and never enter `target_verify`, so they never need a scratch row. What the scratch does need is a row for every row of a verify batch **after padding**: eager warmup and MLP sync pad the batch to the attention TP (and CP) width, and CUDA graphs to their batch-size alignment. GDN and KDA verify read the scratch through `build_verify_intermediate_state_indices`, which maps every padded row onto the padding row. Other writers index it by batch position: the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv tape and N-gram commit, LFM2's short-conv tape (`arange(bs)`), and the lightning `seg_la` verify (`arange(cache_indices.shape[0])`). They fit today only because the in-transfer rows happen to cover the padding. With `--disaggregation-decode-extra-slots 0`, or more than 32 requests per worker (where the default is 0), a padded verify batch overruns the PLE scratch on main too. The in-transfer rows are not budgeted either. By default a decode server runs with the radix cache disabled, and `_handle_max_mamba_cache` then reserves verify scratch for `max_running_requests // attn_dp_size + 1` rows, while the pool allocates `size + pre_alloc_si

title: [Feat] [NPU] dcp: Switch MLA and DSA to token sharding
summary: ## Motivation Switch NPU MLA and DSA target attention KV from page ownership to token ownership, including P/D transfer. With DCP2, rank 0 owns tokens 0, 2, 4 and rank 1 owns tokens 1, 3, 5. Keep ordinary NPU DSA index-K/scales and draft KV replicated. Token ownership produces many short source segments. Gather each destination rank's attention KV into a continuous NPU buffer before transfer, using the existing common DCP pack/send flow. ## Modifications - Use token ownership for target writes, rank-local lengths, DSA Top-K remapping, speculative visibility, and MLA prefix reconstruction. Covers ordinary MLA, Kimi K3 hybrid MLA, and ordinary DSA. - Register NPU index-K and optional scales as independent `StateType.DSA` entries, including draft indexer buffers when present. Preserve global slots and copy complete indexer pages to every decode DCP rank. Publish layer IDs for PP/draft pairing. - Keep layout, state, and pack adaptation in `hardware_backend/npu/`. The new NPU pack buffer uses the NPU allocator and a row-tiled Triton kernel, caching pointer/width/stride metadata. Allocate one buffer per send worker using common capacity sizing and retain the existing small-buffer fallback. - Reuse common address planning, packing offsets, transport submission, and synchronization. The common pack helper only selects an optional buffer-specific copier; GPU buffers continue to use the existing GPU gather. Preserve the Prefill-ready event and gather completion ordering. - Enable this flow for both Mooncake and Ascend NPU managers. `disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py` remains unchanged

title: [Perf] cosmos3: optimize Sim-Bimanual kv cache management
summary: Motivation Cosmos3 Nano Sim-Bimanual repeatedly concatenates text, history, and current KV during inference, and rebuilds history after each clean-frame commit. This adds memory traffic, allocation overhead, and temporary KV copies, especially with full history. Related issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48144 ## Modifications - Reuse request-local, per-layer `[text | history | current]` KV buffers across denoising steps. Only clean frames commit history. - Preallocate full-history capacity for each request and reject requests exceeding the configured history limit. - Preserve sliding-window sink/recent retention using one scratch buffer sized for a single layer's recent-window K/V (**48.125 MiB total** in this benchmark), reused across all 36 layers. Full history requires no scratch storage. Overlap compaction with subsequent computation through per-layer CUDA events, with stream cleanup on normal and exceptional exits. ## Accuracy Tests - Both full and sliding modes produce **bit-identical BF16 latents and all 901 decoded RGB frames** compared with the original KV implementation. - Targeted unit suites: **217 tests and 116 subtests passed**. title: [Feat] [CPU] quantization: Add per-token FP8 quantization with AVX10.2 runtime dispatch
summary: replace #41064. ## Motivation Add per-token BF16-to-FP8 E4M3FN activation quantization on x86 CPUs. title: [Fix] gdn: Stop torch.compile from cloning the state and KV pools
summary: Title: [Fix] gdn: Stop torch.compile from cloning the state and KV pools ## Motivation Fixes #51651. With `--enable-torch-compile`, Qwen3.5-9B never starts: decode CUDA graph capture runs out of memory at bs=32. Inductor clones SGLang's caches before writing them: - **GDN state.** `mamba2_layer_cache(layer_id)` slices the all-layers pool inside the compiled graph, and the packed decode kernel (a user Triton kernel) writes that slice. Inductor then clones the pool from its start through that slice: k + 1 layers' worth for GDN layer k, on every call. On an A100 80GB the 7th layer's clone (6.96 GiB) does not fit. The conv state gets the same clone from the fused conv update. - **KV cache.** `k_buffer[i]` and `v_buffer[i]` are views of one shared allocation, made once at start-up. `store_cache` writes both, and Inductor clones the whole allocation (3.39 GiB per layer here) before the write. Both reduce to a few lines with no SGLang, on torch 2.14.1 / Triton 3.8.0. Largest buffer in the generated code for a `(24, 509, 64)` tensor: | Case | Largest buffer | |---|---| | user Triton kernel writes `cache[5]`, slice taken inside the compiled fn | 6 slices (a clone of `cache[:6]`) | | same, slice made outside and passed in | none | | same launch wrapped in a custom op with `mutates_args` | none | | custom op writes two views of one tensor made outside (like K and V) | the whole tensor | | same op, both views sliced inside the compiled fn | none | Reproduction scripts and logs: https://github.com/Aagam-Bothara/rigtune/tree/main/benchmarks/sessions/2026-11/modal-sglang-compile-oom ## Mo

title: [Perf] Foundry: adding the adapter of foundry to enable fast CUDA graph save/load
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation [Foundry](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry) persists CUDA graphs across restarts. The first start (`save`) archives the captured graphs, their kernels and the device-memory layout. Later starts (`load`) rebuild the graphs from the archive instead of capturing them, so an engine that spends 40-120 s capturing 128 decode graphs per rank is serving within a few seconds of the eager engine. Foundry hooks the CUDA driver (an `LD_PRELOAD` library, like `torch_memory_saver`) and needs SGLang to call it at a few points of the engine bring-up. This PR adds it the way SGLang integrates `torch_memory_saver`: an optional dependency behind an adapter that is a no-op unless the feature is enabled, a server argument, and explicit one-line call sites. The call sites pass only the values Foundry needs (the loaded model, the draft-worker flag, the resolved pool config, the prefill request slots), never a runner or backend object. It replaces the plugin approach of #41791, which maintainers considered unsuitable for an extension that needs runtime call sites. Outside the configurations Foundry supports, the engine starts natively and says why (see Modifications, 3). ## Modifications Eleven commits on `main` (`cbbc6b67f4`), 37 files, +1863 / -51. Three groups: **1. Pre-capture state is built explicitly, on every start (

title: [Fix] server-args: Floor the derived mem_fraction_static and validate explicit values
summary: ## Motivation `chunked_prefill_size=-1` is the documented way to disable chunked prefill, but it makes the activation reserve in `handle_gpu_memory_settings` scale with `max_prefill_tokens`: `512 + 16384 * 1.5` MiB before the CUDA-graph and DeepEP terms, which exceeds any device under roughly 25 GiB. The derived `mem_fraction_static` comes out negative and the engine dies at memory profiling with ``` ValueError: Loaded weights leave no GPU memory for the KV cache under --mem-fraction-static=-0.05 ``` for a flag the user never set (issue reporter measured -0.05 on a 24058 MiB RTX 4090; I reproduce -0.026 at 24576 MiB and -0.539 at 16 GiB). The same path triggers for any config whose estimated reserve exceeds the device, e.g. `chunked_prefill_size=32768` on a 24 GiB card derives -1.026. This locks the whole 16/24 GiB class (T4, L4, A10, 3090/4090/5090) out of a documented configuration. ## Fix - Floor the *derived* fraction at 0.5 with a warning that names the estimated reserve, the device size, and how to override with `--mem-fraction-static`. The startup profiler already computes a precise minimum viable fraction and raises with a suggested value when the weights genuinely do not fit, so in that case this converts the misleading negative-fraction failure into an accurate, actionable error, and small models (where the model-agnostic 1.5 MiB/token estimate is far above real activations) get a working engine. - Reject an explicit `--mem-fraction-static` outside (0, 1] in `handle_other_validations`, so a bad explicit value fails at argument parsing instead of deep in the memory

title: [Fix] entrypoints: validate sampling bounds in OpenAI request models
summary: ## Motivation SGLang 1.0 requires malformed requests to fail with a 4xx response instead of reaching the scheduler or crashing the server (release checklist issue #50045). Two open issues remain visible at the request-model boundary: - **#41482** — `top_k`, `logprobs`, and `n` were not fully bounded by the OpenAI-compatible request models. - **#41466** — a `session_params` value of the wrong type used to reach attribute access far from the request boundary instead of failing validation. Most of the work is already in `main`: `n` is bounded to `1..128` through `OPENAI_MAX_N`, chat `top_logprobs` and `temperature` have lower bounds, and serving checks cap `logprobs`/`top_logprobs` at the vocabulary size. This PR closes the remaining gaps without duplicating those checks or imposing limits that SGLang deliberately does not enforce. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`: - Add a shared `TopK` annotated type that accepts `-1` (disable top-k) or any value `>= 1`, matching `SamplingParams.verify()`. - Apply it to `CompletionRequest.top_k`, `ChatCompletionRequest.top_k`, and `ResponsesRequest.top_k`. Values such as `0` or `-2` now fail at request parsing instead of later in the sampling pipeline; accepted requests are unchanged. - Add `ge=0` to `CompletionRequest.logprobs` (previously only checked at serving time). - Add `ge=0` to `ResponsesRequest.top_logprobs` (previously `-1` was silently coerced to `0`). No upper bounds are added: - `n` already uses `OPENAI_MAX_N = 128` plus `SGLANG_MAX_BATCH_REQS_PER_HTTP_REQ`. - Chat/completions `top_logprobs`/`l

title: [Fix] qwen2_moe: Replicate the shared expert under DWDP
summary: ## Motivation Under DWDP (#29778), sparse MoE runs on DP-local tokens and each rank computes its own tokens' routed experts in full, so nothing sums the MoE output over TP: `post_experts_output_is_complete()` is True and `reduce_moe_output` skips its all-reduce, and in Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8, which leave that sum to the layer boundary, the boundary also takes the output as complete (`is_moe_input_scattered_across_dp_ranks()`). `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` replicates its shared expert only for the a2a backends. Under DWDP the shared expert stays TP-sharded with an unreduced down projection, so each rank adds 1/TP of the shared expert's output for its own tokens, and nothing sums the shards. Shared-expert fusion is wrong under DWDP too: DWDP prefetches only the routed experts, and the fused shared slot's routing weight is pre-scaled by 1/ep_size for the post-experts all-reduce that DWDP skips. title: [Bug] Sleep mode does not restore plain tensor attributes: only parameters and buffers survive release/resume
summary: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug `sleep`/`release_memory_occupation(tags=["weights"])` discards the contents of the weights region; `resume_memory_occupation` then remaps the same virtual addresses to freshly committed (zero-filled) pages. Only two kinds of state are restored: - **parameters** — refilled by the following weight update, and - **registered buffers** — refilled by `_export_static_state` / `_import_static_state`. A third kind is **not** restored: **plain tensor attributes** — tensors held directly on modules, inside lists/dicts on modules, or on non-`nn.Module` helper objects attached to modules (MoE dispatchers, quantization helpers, ...). They are allocated in the weights region, and after resume they silently read zeros at a stable virtual address, so captured graphs keep replaying against corrupted state. This is one class with several concrete manifestations across the ecosystem: - #47147 — `RMSNorm(has_weight=False).weight` (used as `embed_norm` / `qk_norm` in Muse Glimmer): the weight comes back as zeros, hidden states are multiplied by zero, every logit becomes equal, and sampling fails with `Sampling support exceed

title: [Perf] linker: Remove superseded Mamba states from the external store
summary: ## Motivation A hybrid (Mamba) model writes one Mamba state per radix node that holds a checkpoint. At the default `--hybrid-cache-checkpoints-level 2` (#49886) that is each fork point and each request end, so in multi-turn traffic every turn's end state goes to the external store. The per-path cap then frees the previous turn's checkpoint from the device, but by design not its other copies (`_evict_excess_path_states`: "Full KV and any existing host backup are retained"), and the linker has no delete path. The store keeps one state per turn while only the newest on a path can be restored without recompute. Measured on Kimi-K3.1 prefill, attention DP 16 on 16 GB300 GPUs, AgentX agentic traces, Mooncake direct linker. Bytes actually put to the store, per rank: | Pool | Written | Share | Per new token | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mamba (KDA state, fp32, 0.42 GiB each) | 90.3 GiB | 59% | 24.8 KB | | KV | 50.3 GiB | 33% | 13.8 KB | | DSA indexer | 11.5 GiB | 8% | 3.2 KB | One state is written per about 18K new tokens. With a 2.73 TB store the run hit the eviction watermark minutes into the measured window, after which restorable KV history is evicted alongside superseded states. ## Modifications - When the linker offloads a node that carries a Mamba state, it walks the node's root-to-node path (`collect_path_info`, `get_prefix_hash_values`) and selects the Mamba keys of ancestors that have exactly one child and whose state this rank wrote. - The direct linker removes those keys with `batch_remove` after the new state's put succeeds, so a path never loses its newest state. title: [Fix] linker: Renew external store leases on device-cache hits
summary: ## Motivation The unified-cache external linker looks up only the pages past the device-cache hit: `match()` builds its store lookup from `tail_hashes`, which starts at `device_hit_len`. A prefix that a rank keeps serving from its device cache therefore never touches the store, and the store's leases on that prefix lapse while the conversation is still active. That matters once the store is full. Mooncake's memory eviction (`EvictNamespaceMemory`) takes every object whose lease has expired, rotates the list to a random start, and evicts the target count; objects with a live lease are skipped. A store lookup renews leases (`BatchExistKey` grants a read lease per key, `--default_kv_lease_ttl`). So pages of an active conversation that one rank serves from its device cache are eligible for eviction from the moment their write lease expires. Restoring a prefix needs it contiguous from page 0, so one evicted page truncates the hit when the conversation next lands on another attention-DP rank. ## Modifications - In `match()`, once per request, read the device-hit prefix's page hashes from the tree (`get_prefix_hash_values`) and submit a store lookup over them to one background thread. The existence check renews each key's lease. - The scheduler thread never waits on it; a failed lookup is logged and dropped. No data is written or moved. ## Expected effect and limits Measured on Kimi-K3.1 prefill, attention DP 16 on 16 GB300 GPUs, AgentX agentic traces, least-loaded routing, one 2.73 TB Mooncake store, 60 s lease, 2% eviction per round: | | Value | |---|---| | Store reaches the 95%

title: [Roadmap] Prefill-Decode Disaggregation Roadmap (2026 Q4)
summary: ## Motivation Prefill-Decode Disaggregation is now the default way people run SGLang at scale, and over the last two quarters we have made it work with almost every model family, every parallel strategy (TP/PP/CP/DCP/DP-attention), HiCache, and speculative decoding (see the Q2 roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21703 for the history). The cost of that is visible in the code: three transfer backends that each carry their own copy of the protocol, a KVCache lifecycle that is only correct because of a long list of patches, and a decode side that still reserves every destination slot in HBM up front. So for Q4 the theme is less "support one more combination" and more "make the thing we already have correct, memory-efficient, and better coordinated with the router": 1. One protocol layer, per-backend transport (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510). 2. KVCache liveness as an invariant, not a patch series. 3. Pre-allocate decode KV slots in HiCache / host memory instead of VRAM, and move the KV into VRAM once the transfer is done. 4. Router/engine coordination for agentic prefix reuse. ## Shared-protocol unification Tracker: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510, RFC: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861 @jambow0320 @livingshade Mooncake / NIXL / Mori each implement bootstrap, room lifecycle, chunk orchestration, timeout, heartbeat, abort, and failure handling in their own `conn.py`. title: [Feat] hicache: Forward request-scoped KV hints to storage backends
summary: ## Motivation #38891 added a versioned `kv_hints` envelope to generation requests. `GenerateReqInput` documents that it is "passed through untouched to the HiCache storage backends", but today it stops at `Req.kv_hints`: no storage backend can see it. This PR completes that path, so a HiCache storage backend can use an orchestrator's hint when it looks up and reads pages. For example, an orchestrator that routes a request to one worker can tell that worker's storage backend which of the request's blocks another worker has already published, so the backend can fetch those blocks instead of the worker recomputing them. The first consumer is the KVCR storage backend in #45647, which will be rebased onto this API. No in-tree backend uses hints yet, and the hook is opt-in, so nothing changes for existing backends. Hints are stated in terms of the block hashes that SGLang publishes in KV events. For requests isolated by `cache_salt` or by an `extra_key` such as a LoRA adapter, those event IDs differ from the HiCache storage keys. A backend cannot convert between them without reproducing the scheduler's hash chain, so this PR also gives the backend that mapping. ## Modifications A storage backend opts in by overriding `HiCacheStorage.consumes_kv_hints()` to return `True`. For such a backend, HiCache storage lookups (`batch_exists`, `batch_exists_v2`) and reads (`batch_get_v1`, `batch_get_v2`) for a request whose `kv_hints` contains at least one action receive one or two entries in `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info`: - `kv_hints`: the request's `KvHintsEnvelope`. - `storage_key_t

title: [Feat] flashinfer-autotune: Persist single-rank tactics in FlashInfer's managed v2 store
summary: ## Motivation Since #43927, SGLang selects tactics with FlashInfer's autotune v2 (`autotune_v2`, including the default-tactic race). It still persists them through the v1 per-rank JSON files (`load_configs`/`save_configs`). This PR moves persistence for single-rank servers to FlashInfer's managed v2 store. FlashInfer's v2 design expects frameworks to adopt that store before v2 becomes the default. Its graduation gate is "vLLM and SGLang migrated and released". vLLM did the single-rank part in vllm-project/vllm#55671. This revives the migration in #42108 by @Kangyan-Zhou. That PR was closed once its original cold-L2 motivation was fixed in v1 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5705). Its design of one store per process, shared by the target and the draft, carries over here, and so does its partial-cache restart test. What changes for a single-rank server: - **Per-entry publish.** Each winner is published atomically as its own entry, as soon as it is tuned. A crash mid-tuning keeps what was already tuned. v1 writes the whole file only at the end. - **Per-entry misses.** A missing, corrupt or stale entry is a miss for that entry alone; it is retuned and republished. v1 accepts or rejects the whole file by its metadata stamp. - **FlashInfer owns invalidation by environment:** FlashInfer, CUDA, cuBLAS, cuDNN and CuTe-DSL versions, plus the GPU. - **One store for target and draft, loaded at warmup start.** On v1 warm restarts, draft-model lookups made before the draft's JSON was loaded got FlashInfer's default tactic first. title: [Feat] profiler: Emit the forward step span as an NVTX range
summary: ## Motivation SGLang labels every forward pass with a descriptive span, `step[EXTEND bs=8 toks=4096]`, `step[DECODE bs=48]`, `step[VERIFY bs=48]`, `step[DRAFT bs=1]`, built by `build_step_span_name`. Today that span only reaches the torch profiler. The `profile_range` call in `ModelRunner.forward` does not pass `nvtx_enabled`, so in an Nsight Systems trace every step is just `scheduler.run_batch` and there is no way to tell prefill from decode, or to read the batch size, without guessing from kernel names. Guessing breaks with DP attention, where ranks do different work inside the same step. title: [Fix] custom-ar-v2: Build the communicator during CUDA graph capture
summary: ## Motivation With FlashInfer AllReduce fusion on, which is the default for NemotronH at TP>1, the first large burst of traffic after startup stalls every TP rank for about 7.5 s on H100. `CustomAllReduceV2.obj` is a `cached_property`. Building it loads the `communicator` JIT module, which on a cold JIT cache means an nvcc compile. With fusion off, the captured decode graphs run their all-reduces through this class, so the compile happens during CUDA graph capture at startup. With fusion on, the captured layers use the fused all-reduce, and nothing builds the communicator until the first eager all-reduce that needs it. That happens mid-serving: here, the embedding all-reduce of a large prefill. One rank compiles while the other three wait on the JIT build lock. `py-spy` stacks of all four schedulers during the stall: ``` _build_lock (sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/loader.py) load_jit (sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/loader.py) _init_communicator (sglang/kernels/ops/communication/all_reduce.py) WorkspaceLease.get_communicator (symm_workspace.py) CustomAllReduceV2.obj (custom_all_reduce_v2.py) CustomAllReduceV2.custom_all_reduce (custom_all_reduce_v2.py) ... VocabParallelEmbedding.forward (vocab_parallel_embedding.py) ``` This is likely the "c=128 drop with fusion on" reported in #50021. ## Modifications - `custom_all_reduce_v2.py`: `capture()` builds `self.obj` before capturing. `GroupCoordinator.graph_capture()` enters it on every rank at startup, so the communicator is ready before serving, whatever the captured graphs use. summary: ## Motivation `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` bounds its sliding window by a shard **count**: `num_threads + 1` shards are in flight, so peak host RAM is about `(num_threads + 2) x shard size`. summary: ## Motivation FlashInfer 0.7.4, already pinned on main, ships batch-invariant GEMMs. A call with `batch_invariant=True` returns the same bits for a row whatever batch it is in, and FlashInfer guarantees that tile config, grid, SM count and autotuning never change those bits. This PR is the first and smallest step toward using them in SGLang: BF16 only, through `mm_bf16`. In deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`), SGLang's aten `mm`/`addmm` overrides call `matmul_persistent`. On Blackwell that function runs DeepGEMM's deterministic `bf16_gemm_nn` or a Triton persistent kernel. RL trainers that call `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` go through the same function, so a change here reaches rollout and training together. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/batch_invariant_ops/batch_invariant_ops.py`: `matmul_persistent` first sends eligible calls to `flashinfer.mm_bf16(a, b, backend="auto", batch_invariant=True)`. A call is eligible when all of these hold: - The GPU is SM100, SM103 or SM107, as reported by FlashInfer's `is_supported_device`, and FlashInfer 0.7.4+ imports. If it doesn't, the call falls back silently to today's path. - `a`, `b` and the output are all bf16, with K and N divisible by 8. - The weight is row-major (K, N) or the transpose of a row-major (N, K), with a 16-byte-aligned base. title: [Fix] dspark: Stabilize blockwise rejection sampling under logit shifts
summary: ## Motivation At temperature 1, take draft logits `[-inf, 0, 0, -inf]` and target logits `[-inf, 16, 16, -inf]`. Both assign probability ½ to tokens 1 and 2. A proposal of token 1 must be accepted. With server seed 0 and step counter 620191, the blockwise verifier rejects it and resamples token 0, which has zero target probability. This counter gives the first row an acceptance coin one FP32 step below 1. Two roundings affect this decision. Adding the log of the centered sum to the row maximum loses precision when the maximum is large. And even with identical, unshifted logits, adding a near-zero `log(u)` to `log(q)` can round back to `log(q)`, causing a false rejection. A related issue affects the bonus and one-hot residual draws: adding Gumbel noise to large uncentered scores can round distinct draws to a tie. ## Modifications Keep the maximum and the log of the centered sum separate through acceptance and residual sampling. Compare `log(u) < log(p) - log(q)` in both Triton and the Torch reference. Reuse the last verified row's statistics on rejection. For the bonus row, compute only the target maximum and center the Gumbel race by the same value across all vocabulary blocks. The verifier still uses four kernels and does not materialize vocabulary-sized probability tensors. ## Accuracy Tests ```sh python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_blockwise_rejection.py -k 'not routes' ``` On an RTX A6000 (PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Triton 3.5.1), all five new CUDA cases fail on upstream main at `401d0c7929` and pass with the patch. title: [Perf] paged-experts: optionally fuse copying missing experts with MoE kernels (Triton and Marlin)
summary: Any feedback is highly welcome! I'm a PhD student working on serving performance, but I'm new to contributing to sglang and open-source repositories in general. Please let me know if I've missed anything obvious! ## Motivation Paged Experts copies every missing expert into its GPU slot before the MoE kernel starts. That makes every expert wait for every transfer: resident experts cannot start until all copies finish, and each missing expert waits for the others to arrive. Fusing the host reads into the MoE kernel removes that dependency, so the GPU pipelines computation with transfers. This matters more as CPU-GPU interconnects get faster, as with NVLink-C2C on GH200, GB200/GB300 and (upcoming) Vera Rubin. ## Design Our goal is to extend the existing MoE kernels (Triton and Marlin) to pipeline loading missing experts alongside computing resident experts, without unnecessary dependencies between them. The host copies are variants of the existing Triton `fused_moe_kernel` and Marlin MoE kernel, chosen through their existing entry points; no other implementation in SGLang pages experts in from inside a MoE kernel. The kernel has to use as much of the interconnect bandwidth as it can for the whole launch, without taking every SM, so resident experts keep progressing. - How the kernel knows which experts to read from host memory: each layer has K GPU slots, and routed entries normally carry a slot id 0 to K − 1. title: [Fix] qwen4: Align fused verify state rows with PP commit
summary: ## Motivation With pipeline-parallel speculative decoding enabled, Qwen4 fused short-conv verify writes intermediate windows by batch position, while commit reads them by request-pool row. This can commit stale or zero state. Padding must also use reserved row 0: request rows 1 through `pool_size` are live. Addresses the Qwen4 path in #51107 and the padding/mask issues raised in review. ## Modifications - Pass explicit intermediate-state row indices to fused verify; retain batch-position indexing when PP speculative decoding is disabled. - Compute `valid_rows` and PP intermediate row indices once in `_prepare_ple_batch`. title: [Feat] speculative: Insert bounded prompt tail on extend in NGRAMWorker
summary: ## Motivation Part of the N-gram Speculative Decoding Roadmap (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21052). Currently, `NGRAMWorker._update_ngram_corpus` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`) is only called after `TARGET_VERIFY` steps and carries a `FIXME`: ```python # FIXME: Whether to insert 'extend' into the cache or not, after testing, # there is not much difference, so we will not insert it for now. ``` As a result, when a new request completes its prefill (`EXTEND`) phase and enters its first `DECODE` step, the N-gram Trie has **zero tokens from the current request's prompt** (except the last `max_trie_depth = 18` query suffix). In long-context chat, RAG, summarization, and structured JSON planning workloads, entities, identifiers, and schema keys that appear earlier in the prompt cannot be drafted until they have already been generated once by the model. Inserting an entire 32k–64k prompt into the Trie on `EXTEND` would incur O(L * max_trie_depth) CPU insertion overhead. However, inserting a **bounded tail window** (`NGRAM_EXTEND_PROMPT_WINDOW = 1024` tokens) of each completed request's unpadded prompt + output asynchronously on `EXTEND` takes only `~0.18 ms` (bs=1) to `~0.54 ms` (bs=8) on the scheduler thread, while the background C++ `insertWorker` overlaps with the GPU forward pass and captures the most relevant recent context, instructions, and entity names for immediate drafting on step 1. ## Modifications 1. **`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`**: - On `ForwardMode.EXTEND` completion in `forward_batch_generation`, asynchronously

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Bound and price hybrid SWA + Mamba window retention when checkpoints stall
summary: ## Motivation Some models mix sliding-window attention with Mamba-style recurrent state. In the unified radix cache, retirement keeps the window rows behind each request's latest state checkpoint (`swa_retain_floor`). Admission (`request_demand`) prices that retention on the assumption that a checkpoint is taken every `checkpoint_interval` rows, and its TODO names two cases where that assumption fails: - **(A) Lazy tracking finds no second tracking slot at a boundary.** The old checkpoint stays as the retention floor, and the request keeps more and more window rows behind it. - **(B) A checkpoint publication finds no replacement state slot.** `MambaComponent.prepare_for_caching_req` returns 0, and retirement then gets the frontier of an empty insert key (`-1`), so it retires nothing. Two more callers skip a boundary the same way: a speculative crossing whose tracking plan is `-1`, and a decode row that rides a mixed chunked-prefill forward. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Carry running requests' window growth across admission passes
summary: ## Motivation With unified memory and sliding-window sub-pools, admission must leave room for the window KV that already-running requests will still write. - Each admission pass builds a fresh prefill budget, and running requests carry only their remaining full-attention token estimate into it (`min(max_new - output, CLIP) * new_token_ratio`). - `ChainPrefillBudget.reserve` charges a newly admitted request's window commitment only in the pass that admits it. - From the next pass on, nothing charges the window rows a decoding request still adds. Its private decode window regrows to about `window + retention` beside the prompt window the tree keeps. - Later passes can therefore admit work into that room. When the arena fills, requests are retracted and recomputed. ## Modifications The change touches 3 files (+45/−6). It removes no interface and adds no tests. - `mem_cache/kv/alloc/demand.py`: - A new `DemandPurpose.RUNNING` prices what a running request may still add: the same clip and new-token ratio as the full-token remainder, no prompt, and no prefill retirement lag. - A new `DemandRule.prefills` field (default `True`) carries the "no prompt" rule. - Existing purposes get identical inputs. - `mem_cache/prefill_budget.py`: - `PrefillBudget.reserve_running_windows` is a no-op for static and SWA budgets. - `ChainPrefillBudget.reserve_running_windows` prices the request through the shared `request_demand`, credits the rows past its tree-owned prefix (`window_dead_lo`) as held, and adds the result to `window_offsets`, the whole-request pending window demand. - This pass's forw

title: [Test] sgl-router: Run the e2e suite on 4-gpu-h100 with a PD dp-aware 2P+2D test
summary: The router e2e job runs on the `2-gpu-h100` label, the same 16 runners that serve every `base-b-test-2-gpu-large` partition of the main suite. Yesterday's utilization report shows a 153-minute average queue there against 72 minutes on `4-gpu-h100`, and the last six router e2e runs were all cancelled by a newer push before a runner picked them up. - **Runner.** The e2e job moves to `4-gpu-h100`. `SGL_ROUTER_E2E_MIN_GPUS=4` makes the session fail on a smaller allotment: `GPUAllocator.acquire` skips a test that asks for more cards than it has, and a skipped multi-GPU test leaves the run green. - **PD dp-aware test** (`chat_completions/test_pd_dp_aware.py`), using the two extra cards: a dp2 prefill on GPUs 0-1 and a dp2 decode on GPUs 2-3 behind the router in PD mode with `--dp-aware`. Each worker's `/metrics` labels `sglang:num_requests_total` with the scheduler's `dp_rank`, so the tests read which rank served from the engine rather than the router: 1. eight concurrent requests complete through PD and reach both prefill ranks and both decode ranks; 2. after a prompt's KV events reach the router, eight repeats all return to the prefill rank that cached it (by load alone, a 1-in-256 accident); 3. while one decode rank streams a 400-token reply, a new request lands on the other decode rank. - **Infra.** `Router.start_pd` / `start_regular` take `extra_args`.
