title: [Fix] dspark: Prevent Philox rounding from selecting a masked token
summary: ## Motivation With logits `[-inf, 0]` and temperature 1, DSpark's Markov sampler can return token 0. Both the Torch and Triton implementations do this with the draft key for server seed 0, row 0, step 0 and counter 4,757,896. Token 1 draws the Philox word `0xffffff9f`. Converting that word to FP32 rounds it to 2³², so the uniform becomes exactly 1. Its exponential noise is infinite and its score ties the masked token at `-inf`. The sharded verifier uses the same transform for its bonus draw. At counter 1,781,785 it accepts the sole supported draft token and then returns the masked token as its bonus. ## Modifications Compute the smaller of the uniform midpoint and its complement by folding the integer word before converting it to FP32. For the lower half, use `-log1p(-u)`. For the upper half, evaluate `-log(1-u)` from the directly computed complement. Both endpoints give finite, positive noise. The CUDA C++ sampler already uses this [integer folding technique](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/08f10090c76294a458c7b307e1ba97bd7ff1654e/python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/sampling.cuh#L66-L73). The draft and sharded bonus Triton paths share the conversion. The Torch reference uses the same midpoint convention. The Philox keys, counters and word order are unchanged. Seeded token choices can change when the corrected upper-half noise changes a winner. ## Accuracy Tests ```sh python test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dspark_markov_sample.py -v ``` On the base revision, the two new regressions reproduced token 0 for the CPU and CUDA draft paths and for

title: [Feat] pd: Add decode-side prompt-tail computation and first-token sampling
summary: ## Motivation Refs #50547. PD currently requires prefill to run the LM head and provide the first sampled token, even when request sampling state belongs on decode. Add an opt-in dense-attention slice: with the same `--disaggregation-decode-tail-tokens W` on both roles, prefill sends KV for `[0, max(0, N-W))` and skips LM-head computation and sampling. Decode extends the remaining prompt in its already allocated slots and samples the first output token. Short prompts use a metadata-only handoff. The default value zero retains the existing path. ## Modifications - Use one transfer boundary for sender registration (clamping negative `transfer_input_len - decode_prefix_len` deltas to zero), actual sends, checksum coverage, lazy staging prefetch (`min(upto_tokens, req.extend_end)`), and decode commitment. Retain the last transfer page until readiness metadata is published, including warmed-prefix and chunked-prefill cases. - Admit real tail extends within request and token budgets after filtering finished requests from `running_batch` (resetting `batch_is_full` when rows finish) so back-to-back overlap tail batches do not leak finished 1-token requests; clear `pd_tail_extend` on transition/merge/decode preparation so subsequent decode steps do not re-enter the tail-merge branch. When priority scheduling is enabled, use the existing decode admission policy before selecting the tail batch; retain the existing decode transition and finish handling. title: [Feat] linker: support pipeline parallelism in linker
summary: ## Motivation Support pipeline parallelism (PP) in both `layer_wise` and `prefetch` modes of the unified cache external linker. Each rank queries its own storage shard, so backends only need to answer local lookups. The pipeline then agrees on a prefix that every stage can restore. ## Layer-wise loading PP0 issues a ticket with the request key and its local prefix position. Each rank queries the external store for the missing suffix and reports the page boundaries it can restore. A downstream stage can start its lookup before the request arrives. If its local device-cache prefix ends at a different position, it rechecks the suffix from its own pinned prefix. The ranks select the longest common boundary and use it during admission. Each stage then follows the existing layer-wise path, loading only its own layers into slots owned by the request. The restored KV enters the radix tree through the normal request insertion path. ## Prefetch and PP coordination Prefetch reuses HiCache’s ordered ticket broadcast and scheduler readiness relay. PP0 issues tickets in request order, and every rank queries its local backend. 1. PP0 sends its local hit upper bound through the readiness relay. Each stage reserves device slots up to that bound while slower local lookups can still be in flight. 2. Each rank builds a mask of the page boundaries its local query can restore and removes boundaries beyond its **actual reservation**. A single PP `MIN` all-reduce intersects these masks. title: [Fix] logging: Bound token-ID decoding in partial request logs

title: [Feat] observability: Log stats lines for idle steps on PD prefill and decode workers
summary: ## Motivation TL;DR make post-processing of log lines be more accurate by inserting log lines even when server is idle. This is controlled by `SGLANG_LOG_IDLE_BATCH_STATS`, off by default which maintains previous behavior. Without idle logs, stats that can vary within the idle time (e.g., #transfer-req) is not visible. Furthermore, it is not possible to infer how large a time window a log line covers. Before PR: After PR: PD prefill and decode workers log a `Prefill batch` / `Decode batch` line only for forwards that do work. A worker with no forward to run, or such an attention-DP rank, prints nothing, though it can be in either of two states: 1. **Idle**: no requests exist. 2. **Blocked**: requests exist but wait on something other than compute. With the defaults (`early` decode allocation, no optimistic prefill), prefill starts a request only after decode has reserved KV cache for it. While the decode KV pool is full, new requests wait in the prefill bootstrap queue and the prefill worker has nothing to run. title: [Perf] dspark: Fold the static verify epilogue's commits into the accept tail and trim the verify-to-draft glue
summary: ## Motivation At batch 1, a DSpark decode step on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash replays two CUDA graphs, the target verify and then the draft, with a little eager work between them. Several small launches on that path sit on the critical path. All of them run whatever the sampling temperature: - **The static verify graph's epilogue.** The verify graph always records the greedy epilogue. On a sampled step it runs with its commit gate at 0, before the sampling-accept graph replays the real accept and commits. After the fused accept tail, that epilogue still issues up to four serial launches: the engram history commit, two `index_put` scatters of the FutureMap relay (new seq lens and bonus), and the deferred draft KV staging. - **The verify ids copy.** The draft graph's tail writes `[anchor | draft tokens]` into the draft sampler's `verify_ids`, and the verify replay then copies them into the verify graph's `input_ids` slot. - **The relay resolve.** The overlap scheduler resolves the relay with two index gathers. The second one, for the bonus tokens, runs on the forward stream behind the previous step's draft. All three changes copy the same integer values that the separate launches copy, so the results are bitwise identical. None of them adds a switch: each is gated only by the feature it builds on. ## Modifications - **Commit tail in the fused accept tail.** When the fused greedy accept tail serves the batch size, `run_static` passes the relay scatter, the engram history commit and the deferred draft KV staging to that tail. `static_accept_tail` takes the relay tables and a `CommitTai

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dp-attention: Route the padding rows of the TP-MoE gather to no expert
summary: ## Motivation With attention DP and TP MoE on CUDA, the MoE input of a decode step is a MAX_LEN gather: every DP rank contributes a slot of the same length, and the rows past its real requests are padding. The decode CUDA graph always uses this layout, and an idle rank still replays one fabricated row. The router sends the padding rows to experts like real tokens, so every MoE layer loads those experts' weights. Since #46225 this costs more on hybrid models. Before it, the unpacked KDA/GDN decode left the padding rows' output unwritten. On GLM-5.3-Flash, six or seven of the seven padding rows of a one-request step then selected exactly experts 0-7 in every MoE layer, which is what the router does with NaN scores (it ranks NaN as -1e30 and breaks ties toward the lowest id). #46225 zeroes that output, which is the right fix for correctness, and the padding rows now route like real tokens. With one request on 8×H20 (attention DP8, main 552e16968b), the expert-distribution recorder counts 64 selections and 35 distinct experts per MoE layer per decode step; with this PR, the real row's 8. On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 zeroes the padding rows before the gather (#43077). Zeroed rows still route, to the experts with the largest correction bias. title: [Feat] sgl-router: Route DeepSeek image chats by prefix cache
summary: Standalone: this PR no longer depends on #46562. It carries the one piece of that PR the router needs (`EncodedPrompt` and `ChatFormatter::encode_multimodal_request` in `sglang-processor`, 145 lines, three files) as its own commit, rebased on current `main`. Everything else is `sgl-router/`. ## Motivation Cache-aware routing finds a prompt's cached prefix by hashing the router's own tokenization of the request and matching it against the block hashes engines publish as KV events. For DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1, the router renders chats through `sglang-processor`, whose text-only path refuses images (`image input is not supported for this model`). The router then falls back to hashing the raw message text. Those hashes never match the engine's blocks, so every chat that carries an image is routed as if nothing were cached. In agent workloads an image (a screenshot, a `read_image` result) stays in the history for the rest of the conversation, so all its later turns scatter across workers and re-prefill context that another worker already holds. Two things are missing on the routing side: 1. **The router never renders image chats.** `encode_chat` calls `encode_request`, which refuses images. 2. **Rendering alone stops at the first image.** The engine turns each image into token ids derived from its preprocessed pixels (`pad_value`), which the router does not reproduce. KV events can therefore confirm an image chat only up to its first image. Past that point every worker holding the shared prefix (system prompt, tools, early turns) ties, and the tie is broken by load. ## Modifications

title: [Perf] kimi-k3.1: Sequence-parallel layer tail for large eager prefill batches
summary: ## Motivation Original design and implementation by @nvpohanh. On a Kimi-K3.1 prefill with plain-TP attention (no attention DP or CP) and no EP all-to-all MoE backend, every TP rank repeats the row-wise part of each layer on all rows of the batch: the attention-residual bank reads, the residual adds, the latent RMSNorm, the latent up_proj and the tail add. The o_proj and MoE sums are full all-reduces. ## Modifications A sequence-parallel layer tail for large eager prefill batches. From the first MoE layer on, each TP rank keeps only its 1/tp of the rows (the batch is padded to a multiple of 2 * tp; pad rows are zero and dropped by every gather). Per layer: - bank read for the attention input on the local rows, then an all-gather of the normed attention input; - attention (MLA with DCP, or KDA), unchanged; - reduce-scatter of o_proj's TP partial with the residual add fused; - bank read for the FFN input on the local rows, then an all-gather for the MoE; - the fused MoE front and the routed experts, unchanged; the shared experts on the side stream end in a reduce-scatter instead of an all-reduce; - reduce-scatter of the routed latent sum, then the latent RMSNorm, up_proj and tail add on the local rows. DFLASH aux-hidden-state captures and the final norm run on the local rows and are gathered into owned storage. The collectives are K3's NVLS pull reduce-scatter and multicast direct all-gather on the TP group's CustomAllReduceV2, in BF16, with an NCCL fallback. summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-mixed-chunk` (#36933), running DSPARK requests are folded into prefill steps, but there each running request only decodes its pending token: 1 token per step instead of the ~4.8 a normal DSPARK verify step yields. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Route the DCP prefill by its wire bytes
summary: ## Motivation A DSA DCP prefill can be served two ways: **owned** all-gathers Q, attends the slots this rank owns, and LSE-merges the head partials back through an a2a; **gathered** all-gathers the cached prefix KV latents once and attends them with this rank's local heads, with no merge. Neither wins everywhere. Owned pays per extend token and head, gathered pays per cached prefix token, and the crossing between them is a property of the data layout, not of the model. This PR derives it from the running configuration and routes each extend batch accordingly. Builds on #47180 (Q replication + project-before-merge) and #44322, both merged. ## Modifications Per extend token and gathered head, owned puts a partial plus its packed LSE on the wire. Per cached prefix token, gathered puts one latent on the wire. Both collectives move the same `(W-1)/W` of their volume over the same fabric, so the group width and the bandwidth cancel: ``` crossover = (partial_width + lse_pack) * itemsize(partial_dtype) / (latent * itemsize(kv_dtype)) gathered when sum(extend_prefix_lens) < crossover * gathered_heads * extend_num_tokens ``` `latent = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`; `partial_width` is `v_head_dim` when the partials are projected before the merge, `kv_lora_rank` otherwise. A query all-gather adds one latent in the KV dtype to the numerator, which is exactly the denominator — so **not replicating `q_b_proj` adds exactly 1.0, for every model and dtype.** `dcp_gathered_prefill_crossover()` evaluates this once at backend construction and logs it. title: [Feature] Support partial-page prefix reuse in RadixCache
summary: ## Motivation SGLang's paged RadixCache keeps radix-tree ownership page aligned. Before this change, when the logical longest common prefix ended inside a page, only the page-aligned portion was reused and up to `page_size - 1` already-computed tokens were sent through model forward again. This issue is negligible at `page_size=1`, but becomes increasingly relevant with larger physical page sizes such as 16, 32, and 64. With larger practical page sizes such as 16, 32, and 64, treating the physical page boundary as the only logical reuse boundary can discard a meaningful amount of already-computed work. At those sizes, treating the physical page boundary as the only logical reuse boundary can discard a meaningful amount of already-computed work. If the divergence position is uniformly distributed within a page, the average missed reuse is `(page_size - 1) / 2`: 7.5, 15.5, and 31.5 tokens for page sizes 16, 32, and 64 respectively. The page boundary should therefore remain the radix tree's physical ownership boundary, but it is no longer always the best logical prefix-reuse boundary. This PR experimentally reuses those partial-page KV entries without changing the page-aligned radix-tree structure or ownership model. The matched KV entries are copied into a new request-private physical page, allowing the allocator to continue writing into the remainder of that page. The feature is disabled by default and initially targets the ordinary CUDA FULL-attention Python RadixCache path. ## Modifications 1. title: Bound DSpark rejection sampling workspace
summary: ## Motivation DSpark's non-greedy verification path materializes full-vocabulary probability tensors for rejection sampling: - draft probabilities: [B, gamma_rows, V] - target probabilities: [B, verify_num_draft_tokens, V] - probability dtype: FP32 The simultaneous workspace therefore scales as: B x (gamma_rows + verify_num_draft_tokens) x V x 4 bytes For Qwen3-8B (V=151,936) and DSpark block7, this workspace becomes the dominant peak-memory allocation at large batches. In local RTX PRO 6000 pressure tests, the original path did not complete reliably at B=3072 and B=4096 and reported CUDA illegal memory access. This PR bounds the probability workspace by splitting verification at request boundaries. This is related to [vLLM #48630](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48630), which bounds rejection-sampling workspace for large batches. This PR targets SGLang DSpark specifically, reuses the existing rejection sampler, and does not change the acceptance rule. ## Design ### Request-boundary chunked verification The batch is divided into request-aligned chunks. Each chunk independently constructs draft probabilities and invokes the existing rejection sampler. A request is never split across chunks, so its candidate tokens, target logits, sampling metadata, and cutoff lengths remain aligned. The original full-batch path is retained when the estimated workspace fits the available memory. Chunking is therefore only used when the configured budget or current memory pressure requires it. ### Workspace-aware planner The planner estimates the simultaneous FP32 draft/target probab

title: Fix EnvField.override() leaking the env var when the with body raises
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Problem EnvField.override() is a @contextmanager that temporarily sets an env var and restores it on exit. The restore logic sits after yield with no try/finally: When the with body raises, contextlib.contextmanager throws the exception into the generator at the yield point. Because there is no try/finally, the code after yield is skipped, so the env var is never restored and permanently leaks into os.environ for the rest of the process. Impact Any code that does with envs.X.override(...): <raises> permanently contaminates the process environment. title: Drop null `required`/`properties` in tool schema normalization
summary: ## Motivation Closes #35242. When a tool is served through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `serving_chat` validates each tool's `parameters` with `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` (after running the `normalize_json_schema_types` compatibility pass). Some client SDKs emit `"required": null` (and `"properties": null`) for a tool that has no required fields / no properties, instead of omitting the keyword. JSON Schema requires `required` to be an array and `properties` to be an object, so `check_schema` raises `SchemaError: None is not of type 'array'` and the entire request fails with: ``` 400 Tool 17 function has invalid 'parameters' schema: None is not of type 'array' ``` `required: null` is semantically equivalent to omitting `required` ("no required fields"), so rejecting it breaks real clients for no semantic gain. This was reported in #35242 with qwen3.8-27b. ## Modifications `normalize_json_schema_types` (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/utils.py`) is already the documented compatibility layer whose job is to keep otherwise-usable tool schemas validating (it rewrites DB/ORM type aliases such as `varchar` -> `string`). This PR extends it to drop `required` / `properties` when their value is `null`, at every schema level the walker already visits: ```python for key in ("required", "properties"): if key in schema and schema[key] is None: del schema[key] ``` Scope is deliberately limited to `required` and `properties` (the two container-typed keywords SDKs most commonly null out) rather than a blanket "strip all null keywords", which could mask genuine schema mistakes. title: [Fix] spec: Keep the post-verify graphs' outputs out of the shared graph pool
summary: ## Motivation `_PostVerifyGraphs` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_post_verify_graphs.py`, behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`) double-buffers each key: rounds alternate between two capture slots, so round N's outputs (`predict`, `accept_lens`, `accept_index`, `new_seq_lens`, `bonus_tokens`, the draft-extend inputs, `commit_steps`) stay valid while round N+1 is launched. The reader at risk is the scheduler's device-to-host copy of `predict` / `accept_lens`. It runs on `copy_stream`, or, under Confidential Computing, on `AsyncD2HCopyWorker`'s own thread and stream. Nothing orders it against round N+1's post-verify replay. The other readers are ordered before that replay today: `run()` joins the previous side-stream commit first, and the relay is stream-ordered. They would be exposed only if a later change deferred them. Every capture, of every key and both slots, goes into **one graph pool** (`self._pool`). A capture's temporaries are freed back to that pool when the capture ends, and PyTorch **may** place a later capture's tensors in those freed blocks, including the tensors the later graph keeps as outputs. Every **replay of the earlier graph rewrites its temporaries, and may overwrite the later graph's outputs**. So the two slots are not disjoint in memory: - slot 1's outputs can sit in slot 0's scratch, so round N+1 (slot 0) overwrites round N's (slot 1) results; - the same happens across keys: B7's outputs, captured after B8, can sit in B8's scratch, so a B8 replay overwrites a held B7 round (the batch growing by one). **Observed on main b2cc023:**

title: [Feat] rust-server: A grpc.health.v1 inference service covering every DP rank on the node
summary: ## Motivation With the Rust `sglang.api.v1` server (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) and attention DP, each DP leader on a node runs its own api.v1 listener on `--grpc-port + offset`. A kubelet gRPC probe targets one port, so today it sees one rank. A hung rank on another port goes unnoticed, and with attention DP one hung rank stalls the whole group. ## Modifications - The node's first api.v1 listener (port offset 0) now also serves `grpc.health.v1`. summary: ## Motivation Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors: - A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal request. - Every `trace_ctx.abort(abort_info=...)` sets the thread span's status to ERROR, whether the request hit a server fault, was rejected as invalid, or was aborted by its caller. A sampler or alert that keys on error spans counts every bad request and every client disconnect as a server failure. - A request that fails in the tokenizer before reaching the scheduler (invalid input, a LoRA or encoder error) never has its trace ended. With sync tracing its root span is never exported, so rejected requests don't appear in traces at all. ## Modifications 1. **Thread spans are errors only for server faults.** Each abort that has an HTTP status passes it in `abort_info["status_code"]`, matching the status the client gets: - scheduler: 503 when it refuses a request as unavailable (e.g. the queue is full), and the `FINISH_ABORT`'s own status when retiring an unadmitted or chunked request (e.g. 400 for a bad sampling mask or a prompt over the PD KV capacity); - PD prefill: 500 on KV transfer or bootstrap failure, and the sampling-mask reason's status. A request aborted while its KV sender holds it ends through the same failure path; its span gets no status. - EPD encoder: 504 on timeout, otherwise `MMError.code` or the worker's error code, falling back to 500. title: [KDA] Fused intra-chunk prefill path (`chunk_kda_fwd_intra(fuse_diagonal=True)`) collapses for strong per-channel decays because of the ±126 clamp in the exp2 factorization
summary: ## Summary `chunk_kda_fwd` selects `chunk_kda_fwd_intra(fuse_diagonal=True, fuse_recompute=True)` whenever `B * NT * H <= 256` (i.e. for every short prefill). Inside `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused` the diagonal sub-blocks factorize `exp2(g_i - g_j) = exp2(g_i - g_n) * exp2(g_n - g_j)` and clamp both factors: ```python b_gm0 = tl.clamp(b_g0 - b_gn0[None, :], -126.0, 126.0) b_gq0 = tl.where(m_tc0[:, None], exp2(b_gm0), 0.0) b_gk0 = tl.where(m_tc0[:, None], exp2(-b_gm0), 0.0) ``` When a channel decays by more than 2^126 inside a 16-token sub-block, the clamped factors no longer cancel and the block's `exp2(g_i - g_j)` is effectively replaced by `exp2(0)`: keys that should have been forgotten are read at full weight. Kimi Linear's gates are mild enough not to trigger this; models with sharper per-channel decays do (our model: cumulative log2 decays inside a 64-token chunk down to -485, `exp(A_log)` up to 72). ## Measurements (H200, Triton kernels from main @ 2026-08-03, one real layer's q/k/v/gate/beta, T = 298) rel-L2 of the chunk output vs an fp32 torch recurrence on identical inputs: | path | rel-L2 | |---|---| | `chunk_kda` heuristic (fused intra, small grid) | 1.52e-1 | | `chunk_kda` with the token-parallel (unfused) intra path | 2.37e-3 | | vLLM's fla port `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (same inputs) | 2.32e-3 | End to end (40-layer hybrid model, per-layer comparison against the HF implementation): the first KDA layer is 15 % off with the fused path and 0.23 % with the unfused one; prompt top-1 agreement 95.3 % vs 97.0 % (the HF fla-vs-torch reference pair itself ag

title: [Bug] humming MoE runner picks tuning config with a 4x-inflated shape under EP, and the obvious EP-aware fix regresses serving
summary: ### Describe the bug `estimate_local_valid_shape_m()` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py` returns `topk_ids.nelement()` when no `expected_m` is given (~line 204, carries `# TODO: update for EP and DP`, introduced in #23754). Under EP this counts the global routed elements. `local_expert_mapping` keeps the tensor shape unchanged and writes -1 for non-local experts, so `nelement()` = M_global x top_k, while each rank's GEMM only touches ~1/ep_size of those rows. The value only drives kernel config selection: the Python block-size ladder in `_prepare_indexed_gemm_kwargs` and the humming launcher's variant lookup (`find_kernel_launch_data` in launcher.cpp). title: [Fix] mem_cache: Preserve hybrid prefill numerical consistency
summary: ## Motivation With FP32 GDN states and BF16 activations, unaligned prefix-cache snapshots currently pass through a BF16 chunk-state buffer. Copying it into an FP32 cache cannot recover the discarded precision, so a prefix hit resumes from a rounded state. Downstream integration: [sglang-omni#3234](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/3234) carries this fix alongside a pinned upstream GDN graph runtime. Stacked [sglang-omni#3235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/3235) enables Drama3 prompt-only prefix caching and depends on this fix to restore FP32 checkpoints without BF16 rounding. ## Modification **Before (default Triton prefill)** ```text GDN at a tracked chunk boundary FP32 recurrent state `--> BF16 chunk buffer h --> chunk_fwd_o --> prefill output `--> FP32 cache slot (already rounded to BF16) Full attention cached prefix KV (pool) + new suffix KV (input tensors) `--> two-stage extend attention ``` **After (Drama3 opts in to each path independently)** ```text GDN with --enable-gdn-fp32-snapshots FP32 recurrent state |--> BF16 chunk buffer h ---------> chunk_fwd_o --> prefill output `--> extra FP32 snapshot buffer --> FP32 cache slot (selected boundary only) Full attention with use_unified_prefill=True cached prefix KV + new suffix KV --> one index list into the KV pool `--> unified one-stage extend attention ``` FP32 snapshot export defaults to off and supports eager and captured Triton prefill with an FP32 state pool and FP16/BF16 activations. ## Cache-hit numerical parity In a controlled H200 Drama3 c16 diagnostic, each cache hit was compared

title: [Fix] diffusion: Reserve mmap and activation headroom in host pin budget (#51188)
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Closes #51188 On memory-constrained hosts or containers (e.g., an RTX 4090 24 GB GPU in a container capped at 32 GiB host RAM via cgroup v2), running diffusion models with layerwise offload (such as `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`) causes the scheduler worker process to be OOM-killed during synthetic server warmup. ### Root Causes 1. **Aggressive Host Pin Budget Over-allocates Pinned Storage**: In `host_memory_budget.py`, `HOST_RESERVE_FRACTION` was set to `0.05` (5%) with `MIN_HOST_RESERVE_BYTES = 2 * GIB_BYTES`. Following PR #48418 (which counted reclaimable page cache as available memory under a cgroup cap), `HostPinBudget` calculated ~15.48 GiB of spendable budget in a 32 GiB cgroup and pinned 12 of 50 DiT layers (~14.43 GiB) into unevictable `memfd`/shmem (`sglang-pinned-store`). Because unpinned components stream from disk via `mmap` (DiT ~37.5 GB, text encoder ~46.9 GB, plus VAE), converting all available memory into unevictable shmem left zero page cache headroom for `mmap` page faults and dynamic activations, triggering an unrecoverable cgroup `oom_kill 1`. 2. **Server Fails Open on Worker Death**: In `http_server.py`, when synthetic warmup failed due to the scheduler worker being SIGKILLed by the cgroup OOM killer, the server logged `"Synthetic server warmup failed; continuing startup"`, set `warmup_done`

title: [Feat] [AMD] muse-spark: Run fbtriton's gfx950 qk_norm_rope_kv_cache, rmsnorm_gate and paged_attention_decode behind opt-in switches (paged decode needs uTLX)
summary: ## Motivation fbtriton's `tlx.ops` ([facebookexperimental/triton](https://github.com/facebookexperimental/triton)) has three landed gfx950 kernels with a call site in ROCm Muse Spark: - `qk_norm_rope_kv_cache`: QK norm, RoPE and the FP8 paged KV-cache store in one launch. - `rmsnorm_gate`: the attention output's per-head RMSNorm times sigmoid gate. - `paged_attention_decode`: one-token paged decode attention with an FP8 KV cache, with the output RMSNorm x sigmoid gate applied in its split-K reduce. The first two are plain Triton and run on stock ROCm Triton. **`paged_attention_decode` uses TLX primitives (`triton.language.extra.tlx`), so `SGLANG_USE_TLX_PAGED_DECODE` needs Triton with the uTLX plugin, i.e. SGLang's `BUILD_UTLX=1` ROCm image** (or fbtriton's Triton). The other two switches need neither. All three kernels are vendored unmodified and wired in behind opt-in switches, off by default. On the sliding-window layers, the decode kernel replaces a path that is slow above 8 rows: the FP8 query quant, aiter's gluon `unified_attention` (about 45 µs per window layer at any batch, because it walks the whole page table) and a separate norm-gate launch. End to end this takes 10.3% off TPOT at 16 concurrent requests. It is independent of #50354 (vendored TLX `mm` / `moe` / `norm_residual_norm` / `router_gemm`): the decode kernel uses no `llvm_cl_opts`, intra-wave stages or fbtriton knobs, so it does not need #50354's runtime helper. Shared paths are kept identical, so whichever lands second rebases trivially: - `kernels/tlx_ops/` layout - the vendored `qk_norm_rope_kv_cache`

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Build the ROCm batched-Conv2D VAE input in one Triton pass
summary: ## Motivation **What** Build the NHWC input of the ROCm Conv3d-to-batched-Conv2D VAE path with one Triton kernel instead of `cat -> F.pad -> unfold -> copy_`, cutting Wan2.2 720p VAE decode from 8.64 s to 7.38 s. **Why** For each causal 3x3x3 conv, the gfx1250 NHWC branch of `_conv3d_as_batched_conv2d` materializes a full padded fp32 copy (cat with the feature cache, then `F.pad`) and then gathers the Kt temporal taps into `[N, T_out, Hp, Wp, Kt, C]` bf16 with a 6-D strided `copy_`. aten runs that gather at ~1.4 TB/s (3.1 ms per call at 96 ch 720p). These copies took 1.66 s of the 6.6 s VAE kernel time. The new kernel reads `cache_x` and `x` directly, resolves the frame source and row validity per program, zero-fills the padding and casts once. title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen: Fuse GDN prefill FP8 quants and gating
summary: ## Motivation Stacked on #51023 (its commit is the first of this branch). On ROCm, a GDN layer's prefill with Quark per-channel FP8 linears and per-token activations (`QuarkW8A8Fp8`) quantizes the same BF16 layer input twice, once inside `in_proj_qkvz` and once inside `in_proj_ba`; writes the gated RMSNorm's BF16 output and reads it back to quantize it for `out_proj`; and computes the gates (`fused_gdn_gating`) with one single-warp program per token and 8 heads. #51023 fuses the norm and the quant for decode-sized batches (at most 256 tokens, contiguous `z`); the prefill path, where `z` is a strided view of the projection, keeps two launches. title: [Feat] tracing: Record detokenizer time on root spans
summary: ## Motivation Time spent in the detokenizer is invisible in traces. It sits between the scheduler's spans and the tokenizer's, so it shows up as unexplained latency between them. ## Modifications - With tracing on (`--enable-trace`), `DetokenizerManager.handle_batch_token_id_out` times each batch it handles, from the start of decoding (beam-search and standard) until the output is built, and sends the duration in a new `BatchStrOutput.detokenize_duration` field. The field is `None` when tracing is off. - `TokenizerManager._handle_batch_output` adds the duration to every request in the batch, and `set_finished_time` puts two attributes on the root span: - `detokenize.total_seconds`: summed time of the batches that carried the request (each request waits for its whole batch); - `detokenize.batches`: number of those batches. - Multi-tokenizer routing copies the per-batch duration into every sub-batch: `detokenize_duration` is in `_NOT_SPLIT_FIELDS`, and `_handle_output_by_index` and `_handle_output_by_indices` copy it explicitly; the generic split would otherwise call `len()` on the float and fail. Root-span attributes rather than a span per batch keep the span count unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling With tracing off, the duration isn't sent, so the cost is one `perf_counter` read and a few branches. Measured with `timeit` (Xeon 8375C, Python 3.11): | Where | Cost, tracing off | | --- | --- | | Detokenizer, per batch | ~55 ns | | Tokenizer, per batch | ~30-70 ns | | Tokenizer, per request | ~3 ns

title: [Feat] tracing: Record why requests failed, and mark only server faults as errors (OLD)
summary: ## Motivation Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors: - A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal request. - Every `trace_ctx.abort(abort_info=...)` sets the thread span's status to ERROR, whether the request hit a server fault, was rejected as invalid, or was aborted by its caller. A sampler or alert that keys on error spans counts every bad request and every client disconnect as a server failure. - A request that fails in the tokenizer before reaching the scheduler (invalid input, a LoRA or encoder error) never has its trace ended. With sync tracing its root span is never exported, so rejected requests don't appear in traces at all. ## Modifications 1. **Thread spans are errors only for server faults.** Each abort that has an HTTP status passes it in `abort_info["status_code"]`, matching the status the client gets: - scheduler: 400 for a missing bootstrap room or a bad sampling mask, 503 when the queue is full, and the `FINISH_ABORT`'s own status when retiring an unadmitted or chunked request; - PD prefill: 400 over KV capacity, 500 on KV transfer or bootstrap failure, and the sampling-mask reason's status; - EPD encoder: 504 on timeout, otherwise `MMError.code` or the worker's error code, falling back to 500. An aborted thread span is marked ERROR only for a 5xx, as the OpenTelemetry HTTP conventions do for server spans. Attributes whose value is None are left out instead of being exported as empty

title: [Perf] [H20] fp8-gemm: Take the swapAB kernel for small-M block FP8 GEMM on H20
summary: ## Motivation On SM90, `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` resolves to plain DeepGEMM (`_dispatch_auto_backend` → `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`). DeepGEMM's default kernel is shaped for large M, but in decode the M dimension *is* the batch size: every decode step runs 60+ block-FP8 GEMMs with `1 <= M <= 32`, and that kernel leaves most of its tile empty at those sizes. Whether that empty tile **costs** anything depends on how much compute the part has per byte of weights it streams, and on H20 it costs a lot. H20 is Hopper silicon cut down to 78 SMs against 132 on H100/H200, so it has roughly a third of their compute while giving up only ~15% of their bandwidth. Narrow-M block-FP8 GEMM on H20 is therefore compute-bound: the redundant MMA work, not the ~27 GB weight stream, is what sets the inter-token time. That is the part this PR targets, and the measurement below shows the effect is absent on an H200 — so the change is scoped to H20 rather than to SM90 as a whole. `flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` is one entry point over **two** DeepGEMM kernels — `fp8_gemm_kernel_swapAB` for `M < 32` and `fp8_gemm_kernel` above it. #32843 already confined `flashinfer_deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` to exactly the `1 <= M < 32` band and delegates every other M (including `M == 0` on idle ranks) back to DeepGEMM, so that callable is a strict superset of what `auto` selects today. It is reachable only by naming `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` explicitly, which leaves the single-request decode of a mainstream FP8 model at roughly 60% of what it reaches

title: [Fix] sampling: Prevent truncated speculative masks in mixed top-k batches
summary: ## Motivation Speculative sampling-mask capture can silently export an incomplete distribution when bounded top-k requests share a verify batch with whole-vocabulary requests. For example, with K=64 and 72 tied logits, the bounded-only path selects exactly 64 tokens. Adding an unbounded row selects the dense renormalization path, which can retain all 72 ties. Capture then exports 64 columns, with total probability 64/72, while reporting OK. ## Modifications - Keep bounded rows on the existing exact-K verification path in mixed bounded/unbounded batches. Preserve the unbounded rows' full-vocabulary probabilities and current joint top-k/top-p semantics. - Cache the bounded top-k upper bound on SamplingBatchInfo, including construction, filtering/refresh, and merging, so the overlap path needs no new device-to-host scalar synchronization. - Inspect one extra support column during speculative capture and report OVERFLOW if exporting K columns would discard positive mass. Preserve greedy point-mass capture and INVALID status precedence. - Add regression tests for cutoff ties, row order, top-p, host metadata lifecycle, legacy metadata, greedy capture, and overflow with or without support logprobs. ## Accuracy Tests Based on upstream main at `51ccc1f6994530b2f16ed1160e728c13a4c0b283`. summary: ## Motivation A breakable prefill CUDA graph that captures the KDA extend runs the pool accessor's layer wait only at capture time, so a replay must wait for in-flight layer loads explicitly. #45839 added that mechanism (`HiCacheGraphEvents`), including a fallback for CPU-future counters, but `_needs_hicache_event_capture` turns it on only when `--enable-hierarchical-cache` is set. The unified-cache external linker loads layer-wise through the same pool wait hook (`LayerWiseLoadCounter`), and it is mutually exclusive with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`. The KDA layers before the first break read their conv and recurrent state before it lands, and the request silently computes on whatever the state slot held. ## Modifications - `_needs_hicache_event_capture` also returns true when the external linker is enabled. title: [Fix] pd: Keep a transfer Success terminal when a client abort lands late
summary: ## Motivation A client abort in the prefill transfer queue can land after the transfer worker wrote `Success` but before the scheduler polled. `update_status` wrote `Failed` over the `Success`, and `abort()` set its own result to `Failed`. Under `prefill_complete`, decode had not been told `Success` yet, so it received `Failed` for KV that had already landed. Under early, prefill released the KV without caching it and the client got a 500. ## Modifications `Success` is terminal like `Failed`, `update_status` checks and writes under the lock, and `abort()` returns early when the room is already `Success`. An abort after the transfer finished is the router's cancel, not a failed transfer. `conclude_transfer` takes `counts_self`, so a chunk the worker has not yet uncounted does not make its own Success provisional. Mooncake passes it; Mori passes it under deferred release; NIXL uncounts first and needs nothing. For review: - On prefill, `Success` is final once no chunk is pending; a `Failed` from an outstanding deferred chunk still replaces it. Decode keeps main's rule and accepts a late `Failed` from prefill, since only prefill knows whether chunks are outstanding. - Traced and tested on Mooncake staging; Mori counts the concluding chunk only under deferred release; NIXL uncounts before it concludes. Both are covered by unit tests on CPU and untested on hardware. - After an early return, the request stays in the transfer queue and the next poll takes the Success branch: `release(checkpoint=True)`, then `clear()`, which drops the abort's failure record. The `abort_sender` path

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add UniBoost tail-aware schedule policy with a rank-invariant TP/PP mode
summary: ## Summary This PR adds **UniBoost**, an opt-in tail-aware schedule policy (from *[Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026](https://openreview.net/challenge?redirect=%2Fforum%3Fid%3DV40F5O5N85)). Before each prefill admission pass, the waiting queue is re-sorted by a soft priority. Agentic / RL-rollout serving is **prefill-dominated with heavy tails**: in a production SWE-agent trace we measured (7.6k requests), input length p50 is 11.8k tokens vs output p50 of ~90 (≈100:1), turns append a median of 169 tokens of tool output but p99 = 9.1k (test-log dumps), and per-request work varies by two orders of magnitude. Under FCFS, short or cache-hot prefills routinely wait behind cold 30k-token prompts, inflating P90+ latency exactly in the moderate-overload regime that RL rollout bursts create. `Phi(i) = arrival_i − b_γ(w_i)`, `w_i = α · uncached_tokens_i` where the boost `b_γ(w) = (1/γ)·ln(1/(1−e^{−γw}))` is bounded, decreasing and convex: short / radix-cache-hot requests are pulled forward, long requests decay to their FCFS rank (bounded boost ⇒ **no starvation**), and γ interpolates FCFS (γ→∞) ↔ SJF (γ→0) **without any output-length prediction**. An optional **gamma-Ada** controller adapts γ online from the observed latency tail ratio (t99/t95): each ended request appends one latency (O(1)), and every 256 latencies a synchronous refit runs a percentile scan over at most 2,000 samples plus one EMA step. With `tp_size > 1` or `pp_size > 1`, the policy uses only inputs that are identical on every rank (below), so every rank admits the same batch. **

title: [Fix] scheduler: Make collective_rpc reliable with DP attention
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, multiple attention leaders connect DEALER sockets to the same Engine RPC endpoint. A request can reach a leader whose control list is discarded by the global TP broadcast, leaving the caller waiting indefinitely. When the source leader receives the request, multiple leaders can reply, leaving stale responses for later calls. The original handler also does not consistently report an error from a non-IO rank to the caller. Addresses #50073 for the default DP-attention control path. ## Modifications - Keep the RPC socket on the global TP source leader and reuse the existing control broadcast to deliver requests to all TP ranks, with one response per call. - Allow other leaders to receive tokenizer requests without an RPC socket, including when setting up the idle sleeper. - Agree on the RPC result across the TP CPU group before replying, so errors on non-IO ranks reach the caller. Broadcast error messages as UTF-8 bytes. - Reject `collective_rpc` before sending when DP attention uses local control broadcast, with instructions to use global control broadcast. That mode does not provide a shared TP receive point; synchronous RPC requires coordination with model collectives. This patch does not add per-iteration collectives or silently change the configuration. - Add seven registered CPU regression cases using real two-process Gloo and ZMQ, invoking the actual Scheduler RPC handler. Coverage includes repeated calls, unique responses, non-source errors, empty/UTF-8 errors, unknown methods, and recovery. The same regression fails on the unmodified b

title: [Fix] [Intel] disaggregation: Compute Mooncake transfer addresses in uint64
summary: [Fix] [Intel] disaggregation: Compute Mooncake transfer addresses in uint64 ## Motivation On Intel XPU, two Mooncake transfer paths kill the prefill transfer thread the first time they run: ``` File ".../disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py", line 2036, in process_layer_tp_aware src_page_base_addrs = src_layer_ptr + prefill_page_indices * src_kv_item_len OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long RuntimeError: Transfer thread failed because of Python int too large to convert to C long. Prefill instance with bootstrap_port=21500 is dead. ``` Both add page or row offsets to a layer base pointer in int64 numpy arrays. Level Zero device pointers have bit 63 set (for example `torch.empty(..., device="xpu").data_ptr() == 0xffff80ac0bc00000`), so they don't fit in int64. CUDA pointers do fit, which is why this only shows on XPU. The two paths: - `send_kvcache_slice`, the heterogeneous-TP head-slice path. It runs when prefill and decode split KV heads differently, e.g. GQA prefill CP (attention TP 1) into decode TP 2. Hit on 4x Arc Pro B60. - `send_kvcache_dcp`, the sliced draft-KV path (`process_sliced_draft`). It runs for decode context parallel with a draft model. Reproduced in a unit test. ## Modifications - Compute the addresses in both paths in `np.uint64`: page and row indices, per-token and head-slice offsets, and layer base pointers. The NIXL connector already does the same for this reason (`nixl/conn.py`, `_pack_stride_descs`). - Every operand is non-negative and the result is a device address, so the values are unchanged on CUDA. - Add `test_sliced_draft_address

title: [Feat] qwen4-exp: Add the per-token PLE lookup (ple_embedding_mode="per_token")
summary: ## Motivation [`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-TokenPLE-AWQ-UINT4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-TokenPLE-AWQ-UINT4) replaces the hashed n-gram PLE table (95 GiB in bf16) by a table with one row per token id (`[248320, 2560]`, 1.2 GiB). [AMD's write-up](https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/artificial-intelligence/quark-qwen-ple/README.html) presents it for a Ryzen AI Halo device with 128 GB of unified memory; my machine is a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with 128 GB. The checkpoint's config has `text_config.ple_embedding_mode: "per_token"` and the table is stored as `...ple.ple_embedding.per_token_table.weight`. SGLang does not read the field: `Qwen4ExpPLELayer` always builds the n-gram embedding, sized from the n-gram settings of the config. With the MoE scheme of the first PR alone, the engine on this machine (110 GiB of GTT) stops during model construction with `torch.OutOfMemoryError: HIP out of memory`, 104.5 GiB allocated: the n-gram table is built (16 heads of about 20 M rows, 160 wide, bf16: about 95 GiB) and the expert weights no longer fit. That error was seen once, on an earlier revision; a second attempt on a later revision did not terminate and had to be stopped (on unified memory the allocation starves the host), so I did not repeat it. vLLM has the same feature open as vllm-project/vllm#64369, and this PR follows its design (same config field and values, table name, clamping and single-PLE-layer limit), adapted to SGLang's PLE batch and loader. This is the second of the two PRs proposed in #51359. ## Modifications - `configs/qwen4_exp.py`: `ple_embedding_mode`

title: [Feat] [AMD] quark: Run packed UINT4 W4A16 MoE experts on the Triton WNA16 kernel (gfx115x)
summary: ## Motivation Quark exports weight-only 4-bit MoE checkpoints as packed integers, for example AMD's [`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-TokenPLE-AWQ-UINT4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-TokenPLE-AWQ-UINT4): `quant_method: quark`, `weight_format: real_quantized`, `pack_method: reorder`, expert weights `dtype: uint4`, `qscheme: per_group`, `group_size: 128`, `symmetric: false`, no activation quantization. The kernel this checkpoint needs is already here: the Triton WNA16 MoE kernel that `moe_wna16.py` uses for AWQ and GPTQ takes 4-bit weights with per-group scales and zero points, and Quark's `reorder` packing is AutoAWQ's nibble order. What is missing is a Quark scheme that converts the checkpoint's tensors to that kernel's layout. This is the first of the two PRs proposed in #51359. Related work I found while checking for duplicates: the `strix/optimizations` branch of clintg6's fork has a Quark INT4 MoE scheme on the same Triton kernel (`QuarkW4A16Int4MoE`, commit [`fd0e7c9fde`](https://github.com/clintg6/sglang/commit/fd0e7c9fde3593eff7ed4c1aff3169f9eefc89ae)) that, as far as I can see, has not been submitted (the linear `QuarkW4A16Int4` from the branch's earlier commit came in, in adapted form, through #47695). It is selected for `dtype: int4` and raises for asymmetric weights, noting that the zero points would have to reach

title: [Feat] sampling: Honor per-request sampling_seed without deterministic inference
summary: Part 1 of #48474. ## Motivation A request's `sampling_seed` (the OpenAI `seed`) is honored only under `--enable-deterministic-inference`; otherwise it is dropped without notice. That flag also replaces kernels process-wide, so a caller who only wants reproducible sampling has to take all of it. ## Modifications - Outside deterministic mode, a batch that holds a seeded, non-greedy request samples with the torch seeded sampler, whose draw is a hash of seed and position and does not depend on the batch slot. The batch's other rows get filler seeds from a dedicated RNG that is identical across TP ranks, so they stay random. When the last seeded row leaves, the batch returns to the fast samplers. A greedy row never draws, so its seed does not count. - With `n` > 1, sample 0 keeps the request's seed and sample i uses `seed + i * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` (wrapping int64), so the samples differ and each is reproducible. `SamplingParams.for_sample` does this in the Python tokenizer manager and in the Rust server's chat and completions fan-outs, and tests in both pin the same values. This also applies in deterministic mode, where the n samples of a seeded request used to be n copies; `n` = 1 is unchanged. - Speculative decoding (its draft graphs have seed buffers only in deterministic mode) and MLX keep ignoring the seed outside deterministic mode, and now warn once. - Drop the assert against min-p with a seed: Gumbel-max is invariant to scaling a row, so min-p's unnormalized weights draw what the renormalized distribution draws. - Document `sampling_seed` in the sampling parameters page.

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] cosmos3: Fix multi-node execution
summary: # [Fix] diffusion/cosmos3: Fix multi-node CFG-parallel FSDP desyncs and auto_tune GPU probing ## Motivation Serving a Cosmos3 checkpoint that only fits with FSDP sharded across nodes (`--use-fsdp-inference --cfg-parallel-size 2 --ulysses-degree 4 --nnodes 2`) hits three independent bugs: 1. **Startup fails on multi-node launches.** `auto_tune` probes `num_gpus` device ids on every node, but `num_gpus` is the total across nodes: `AssertionError: Invalid device id`. 2. **T2I returns a corrupted image, then the server hangs.** The default T2I `guidance_interval` turns CFG off partway through the request. During CFG-split steps each CFG rank caches only its own UND K/V entry, so at the first no-CFG step one rank misses its cache and reruns the UND layers. Under FSDP that issues all-gathers the other ranks never match: the collectives pair the wrong layers (equal shard sizes, so NCCL does not error), one node returns an image built from mixed-layer weights, and the other node hangs until the NCCL watchdog fires. Every later request then hangs as well. 3. **Transfer with control-CFG + text CFG desyncs the same way.** Three CFG branches on two ranks give one rank two forwards and the other one, so the ranks issue different numbers of FSDP all-gathers. ## Modifications - `auto_tune.py`: probe `num_gpus // nnodes` local GPUs. - `Cosmos3DenoisingStage._denoise_once`: track each step's CFG split mode (`"control"`, `"text"` or none) and call `transformer.reset_cache()` on every rank when it changes, so all ranks recompute the UND prefix in the same step. Costs one extra UND pass per mo

title: [Fix] dsa: Make metadata kernel batch size a runtime arg to avoid per-bs Triton recompiles
summary: ## Motivation Three Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py` declare the batch size as `bs: tl.constexpr`. The batch size changes from one step to the next: - `_fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata_kernel` Because `bs` is a `tl.constexpr`, Triton specializes on it and compiles and caches a separate kernel for every batch size it sees. These kernels are not called during CUDA-graph capture. They run when a graph's metadata is filled on replay, with `bs` set to the padded graph batch size. So on main, the first decode step at each new padded batch size JIT-compiles up to three kernels inside the serving loop, and the Triton cache gets one entry per kernel per captured size. These kernels only use `bs` as a runtime bound: `offs_b < bs`, `row < bs`, `tl.range(0, bs)`, and `expanded_size = bs * next_n`. The compile-time tile shapes already come from `BLOCK_BS = next_power_of_2(bs)` and `BLOCK_EXPANDED`, so `bs` itself does not need to be a `constexpr`. For the same reason, `bs` is also added to each kernel's existing `do_not_specialize` list. Otherwise Triton's divisible-by-16 integer specialization would still compile a separate variant for batch sizes like 16, 32 or 48. This is the same bug as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33506, which @amd-mvarjoka fixed in another file. This PR applies that fix to the file below. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py`: removed `tl.constexpr` from `bs` in all three kernels. `bs` stays in e

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Tune the gfx1250 TDM GEMM tile and write FLUX.2 attention straight into the output projection's input
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** Two things on the FLUX.2 denoise path on gfx1250. The TDM GEMM #51155 routes to still runs on its untuned tile, which leaves most of its headroom on the table: 2x4 waves with `group_m 4`, and an M that ends on a few leftover rows pays a whole 256-row tile for them. And `Flux2ParallelSelfAttention` writes its attention output to HBM, then copies all of it again into the output projection's input, because the attention backend has no way to write through to a strided destination. **Where it shows up** Any gfx1250 running FLUX.2 with an aiter that ships the TDM GEMM (merged as ROCm/aiter#7851). The numbers below are 2x TP1 - one independent job on each DPX half of one package, which is the loaded case the opt-in flag was hedging against, and the case where the two halves share a socket power cap so wasted memory traffic costs the most. **How to fix** Retune the TDM tile to 2x2 waves with `group_m 8` and give a short leftover-row remainder its own launch; then implement the existing `forward_into` backend hook for AITER so the attention kernel writes straight into the output projection's input instead of being copied there. ## Modifications - `runtime/layers/linear.py`: the TDM tile is now 2x2 waves / `group_m 8` / `interleave`, and an M that ends on at most 16 leftover rows sends those rows in their own small launch instead of paying a whole 256-row tile for them. - `runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`: implement the existing `forward_into` hook for `AITerImpl` through the FlyDSL BSHD kernel's `out=`, which `aiter.flash_attn_func` does

title: [Fix] mem-cache: Retain SWA behind the replay-trimmed prefix frontier
summary: ## Motivation SWA matching excludes `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens(req)` before page alignment, but out-of-window eviction currently retains the window behind the untrimmed frontier. At some alignments it frees a page needed behind the actual match boundary. An otherwise reusable Full-KV prefix then falls back to an older SWA checkpoint and unnecessarily re-prefills almost an entire 8K chunk. With 256-token pages, a 128-token window/replay guard and a 32,576-token prefix, the old frontier frees through position 32,256. The matched prefix needs the preceding window too; retaining through 32,000 avoids that fallback. A 32,448-token prefix is the unaffected alignment control. ## Modifications - Pass the existing replay-tail policy through the KV-storage `advance` API from both scheduler allocation and unified-cache checkpoints. Both the arena and static storage implementations forward it to the shared SWA helper. - Retain the window behind the earlier, aligned replay boundary when prefix sharing is enabled. Keep the replay guard and attention kernels unchanged. - Preserve checkpoint floors, previously freed cursors, and the no-replay and no-prefix-sharing policies. - Add nine CPU-registered regressions executing the real helper, including an alignment sweep and the two caller policies. title: [Perf] diffusion/flux3: Keep static streams across steps under CFG parallel
summary: ## Motivation A FLUX.3 request reuses the work of the streams whose tokens and timestep stay fixed across denoising steps (text and reference tokens: input embedding, the mode blocks, their modulation and position tables) through `Packed.static`. With `--enable-cfg-parallel` that reuse never happened: - the gate in `Flux3ImageDenoiseStage` excluded `enable_cfg_parallel`, and - `_CFGParallelModel` slices its branch out of the packed CFG pair on every step, so even with the gate open the DiT would get a fresh, empty `StaticStreams` each step. So on two GPUs every step recomputed the text stream on both ranks. ## Modifications - `_CFGParallelModel` keeps one `StaticStreams` per branch for the request (the wrapper is built per request) and attaches it to the per-step slice. - The static-stream gate no longer excludes CFG parallel. The other conditions (no flow map, no CUDA graph, no compile, no layerwise offload, no sequential CFG, `can_reuse_mode_blocks()`) are unchanged. ## Accuracy Reuse is the same computation done once instead of every step. Checked end to end on 2 GPUs with CFG parallel, main against this branch, three requests (1024x1024 and 768x1344, two prompts, three seeds): the returned image bytes have the same md5 in every case. ## Benchmark FLUX.3 Klein Base, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 3.5, 2x B300, `--enable-cfg-parallel --performance-mode speed`, single request end to end (client wall clock, median of 5 requests after warmup, fresh server per arm, arms mirrored A B B A on one machine): | | round 1 | round 2 | |---|---:|---:| | main | 2.046 s | 2.048 s | | this PR

title: [Fix] diffusion: Align Krea-2 request sizes to the 16-pixel patch grid
summary: ## Motivation On a default `sglang serve --model-path krea/Krea-2-Turbo` server, `/v1/images/generations` with `"size": "1920x1080"` or `"1000x1000"` returns HTTP 500 with the body `Internal Server Error`. The server log shows why: ``` einops.EinopsError: Error while processing rearrange-reduction pattern "b c (h ph) (w pw) -> b (h w) (c ph pw)". Shape mismatch, can't divide axis of length 135 in chunks of 2 ``` `Krea2BeforeDenoisingStage` builds the latent at `height // 8` x `width // 8` and splits it into 2x2 patches ([krea2.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8f44124e6010351daffbd5c1d1754b3fa05d2c6c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/krea2.py#L122-L140)), so a latent side that is odd (1080 / 8 = 135, 1000 / 8 = 125) cannot be split. Nothing aligns the requested size before the request reaches it ([Krea2SamplingParams](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8f44124e6010351daffbd5c1d1754b3fa05d2c6c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/sample/krea2.py)). A size such as 854x480 already works on main, because 854 // 8 = 106 is even and the output is 848x480. ## Modifications - `Krea2SamplingParams` rounds width and height down to multiples of 16 (VAE 8 x patch 2, read from the pipeline config; at least 16) after the request's sampling params are resolved, and for synthetic warmup requests, and logs a warning, as #49714 (Z-Image) and #50114 (Cosmos3) do. It applies only to `Krea2PipelineConfig`. Sizes that were already multiples of 16 are unchanged, and 854x480 still gives 848x480, now with a warning. - `test_krea2.p

title: [Fix] mooncake: Keep a per-request error from killing the prefill transfer worker
summary: ## Motivation Each Mooncake prefill rank shards rooms over `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` queues (default 4), one transfer worker thread each, keyed by the sum of the decode session ports. When sending one chunk raised, `transfer_worker` failed that room and then raised `Transfer thread failed ... is dead`, and the thread exited. Nothing drains that queue afterwards. Every later request hashed onto it waits out the waiting timeout (300 s) and aborts. Meanwhile the other queues keep producing output, so `/health_generate` keeps returning 200 and nothing restarts the server. We hit this with a multimodal request whose image-token count differed between prefill and decode. The request length's parity decides the length of a positional state component, so `maybe_send_extra` raised `state index length mismatch` for that one request. The exception killed one worker. A quarter of that rank's later requests then failed at the timeout until the server was restarted by hand. The same length disagreement, with equal parity, went through the KV path. There it logged `len(chunked_dst_kv_indice) = X, len(kv_chunk.prefill_kv_indices) = Y`, truncated the send, and reported success. ## Modifications **The worker survives a per-request error** (`mooncake/conn.py`) - An exception while processing one chunk fails only that room. The room's failure is recorded, it is marked Failed, and its drained-abort ack is withheld because a write may still be in flight. Decode is notified (`conclude_failure`) so it does not wait out its own timeout. The error is logged at ERROR with the traceback, and

title: [Fix] moe/tuning: Tune NemotronH's non-gated relu2 MoE with its real shape
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51627. The fused MoE tuners assume every MoE is gated: `calculate_shard_intermediate_size` returns `2 * intermediate_size // moe_tp_size`, the tuners build `w1` with that many rows and run `fused_moe` with the default gated SiLU. NemotronH's experts are non-gated relu2 (`is_gated=False` in `nemotron_h.py`), so its configs were tuned on an up projection twice the real size, with a different activation. The config file name was already right (`N = w2.shape[2]`), so the wrong-shape configs were saved under the correct name. ## Modifications - `common_utils.py`: new `get_moe_activation(architecture, config)` returns `(activation, is_gated)`: `(config.mlp_hidden_act, False)` for `NemotronHForCausalLM`, `("silu", True)` otherwise. `calculate_shard_intermediate_size` takes `is_gated` (w1 rows are `intermediate / tp` when not gated), `get_model_config` returns `activation` and `is_gated`, and `get_config_filename` takes `is_gated` so `N` stays `w2.shape[2]`. - `tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`: `benchmark_config`, `BenchmarkWorker.benchmark` and `tune` take `activation` and `is_gated` (defaults keep the current behavior). `w2`, its int4 packing and its block-scale tiles use the activation output size, and `fused_moe` runs with `MoeRunnerConfig(activation=..., is_gated=...)`. - `tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py`: the same `is_gated` sizing for `w2`, the down-projection input (`intermediate_cache2`) and the saved file name. This tuner times the up and down GEMMs separately, so no activation is involved. Gated models are unchanged: every new parameter defaults to the gat

title: [Perf] [AMD] Kimi-K3: fuse o_proj all-reduce with the attention-residual aggregation on ROCm
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm TP8, Kimi-K3 finishes every attention block with o_proj's all-reduce, the pending residual add and the MLP-side attention-residual aggregation (score, softmax, mix, RMSNorm) as separate launches. At decode sizes the aggregation is per-CU bound, so fusing it behind the all-reduce only pays off if the aggregation is spread across CUs, and that needs a cross-CTA reduction of the score/norm statistics. The all-reduce already has a cross-GPU barrier in the middle, so the statistics ride that barrier. ## Modifications - `kernels/jit/csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ar_agg_hip.cuh`, `kernels/ops/communication/k3_ar_agg_hip.py`: o_proj all-reduce (AITER 2-stage summation order) + residual add + aggregation + norm in one launch on AITER's custom all-reduce, TP8, up to 64 tokens. The all-reduced row and the bank snapshot are bit-identical to the unfused path; the normalized output matches up to rare 1-ulp bf16 flips. - `kernels/jit/csrc/kimi_k3/attn_res_smallm.cuh`, `kernels/ops/attention/attn_res_smallm_hip.py`: single-launch HIP aggregation for up to 128 tokens; `_aggregate_hip` uses it there and keeps the Triton kernel above. - `layers/attn_residual.py`: `AttnResidual.forward_ar_fused`, which returns None when the fused kernel does not take the batch. - `models/kimi_k3.py`: on ROCm TP8, when main's `k3_ar_fusion` is off, the decoder layer adds a `ReadoutFusion` for the attention-TP sum that calls `forward_ar_fused`. Every other case keeps the existing path. - `layers/communication/k3_logits_gather.py`: logits all-gather on ROCm. This PR used to be stacked on #46652/#46653 a

title: [Perf] [AMD] scheduler: DP prefill coalescer mode for the prefill delayer (1/5)
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, the prefill delayer lets one rank prefill while the others decode, so the gathered MoE runs unbalanced prefill steps. A coalescer mode holds prefill until all ranks have work and enough tokens to fill the chunk. ## Modifications - New `--prefill-delayer-mode coalesce` (default `legacy`, unchanged). It negotiates once per scheduler pass with one 6-int all_gather, after the waiting queue is ranked. - After any DP rank prefilled, hold prefill for `--prefill-decode-interval` passes while decode exists. Then wait until every rank has prefill work and the group's pending tokens fill `--prefill-delayer-fill-ratio` of the chunk, bounded by stall / TTFT / partial-prefill / KV-pressure releases. - The decision is a pure function with unit tests (`test_prefill_delayer_coalesce.py`). - Fix `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_GATHER_FP8` on ROCm: quantize with the triton group-quant kernel. The default path ends in a CUDA-only JIT kernel. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP2 on 2x MI355X, coalesce + fp8 DP gather): 0.911. ## Speed Tests and Profiling DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DEP2 on 2x MI355X, agentic trace at concurrency 128, same hour, GPUs swapped: legacy 229,469 -> coalesce 235,185 tok/s (+2.5%; +2.2% in the other order). ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update doc

title: [Fix] spec: Clear moe_dense_tp_size for a draft narrowed to plain TP
summary: ## Motivation `patch_tensor_parallel_group` narrows a speculative draft to plain TP on its group, with one attention DP rank. It did not reset `moe_dense_tp_size`. So with `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` under DP attention, the draft's dense layers still took the DP dense-FFN row layout. On MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with a DSpark draft (`--tp-size 8 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-dense-tp-size 1`), startup failed during the draft's CUDA graph capture with `ValueError: input tensor must be the same size as output size times world size` in the attention-TP reduce-scatter. ## Modifications `patch_tensor_parallel_group(..., owns_attention=True)` also overrides `moe_dense_tp_size=None` for the draft. ## Accuracy Tests On our MiniMax-M3.1 branch with this fix, the DEP8 config above with `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` started and gave GSM8K 95.53% (1319 questions, sampled, seed 42). title: [Perf] [AMD] Kimi-K3: fuse the KDA gated o_norm into the o_proj GEMM on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 target verify on MI355X runs the KDA gated output RMSNorm and the o_proj GEMM as two launches at decode sizes (M <= 8 rows per layer). Fusing the norm into the GEMM prologue saves a launch and an activation round trip on every KDA layer. ## Modifications - `kernels/jit/csrc/kimi_k3/norm_gemm_hip.cuh`, `kernels/ops/gemm/k3_norm_gemm.py`: a HIP kernel that applies the gated o_norm (sigmoid gate, per-head RMSNorm, bf16 weight) in the prologue of the o_proj GEMM, for 1 <= M <= 16, head_dim 128, K = 12 x 128 (K3 TP8). The normalized operand is bit-identical to `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`, and the output differs from the unfused pair only by GEMM summation order. - `models/kimi_k3.py`: `KimiK3DeltaAttention` takes the fused path in target verify on ROCm when the o_proj is an unquantized bf16 TP-partial linear with no bias and the backend did not already fold the norm. Every other case keeps the existing two-step path. This PR used to carry Triton KDA verify changes too. Main's gfx950 HIP chain verify (#50998) now covers those shapes, so they were dropped. ## Accuracy and performance - `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_k3_norm_gemm.py` compares against the unfused norm + GEMM on MI35x. - 1x MI355X, CUDA graph replay, K3 TP8 shapes (N=7168, K=1536): fused vs `FusedRMSNormGated` + main's bf16 GEMM, identical outputs. | M | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | unfused (us) | 6.7 | 7.1 | 7.2 | 7.3 | 7.7 | | fused (us) | 6.5 | 6.6 | 6.6 | 7.0 | 8.0 | The model only takes the fused path up to M = 8. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Late

title: [Perf] [AMD] Kimi-K3: fused MoE routing, sort, quant and epilogue
summary: ## Motivation At K3 decode batch sizes, MoE routing, sorting, activation quant and the shared-expert epilogue were separate small launches, and launch-bound. ## Modifications - **Generic sorter hook.** `moe_sorting_small.py` stays model-agnostic. It exposes `SortExtension`, a hook for the sort AITER runs inside `fused_moe`, scoped with the `sort_extension(...)` context manager. With no extension set, behavior is unchanged. - **K3 plan in a `k3_*` module.** `k3_sort_plan.py` holds `K3SortPlan(SortExtension)`: the route-state handoff and the deferred shared-expert GEMM. K3 uses AITER's current rows (ROCm/aiter#6464). Gates are on shapes and gfx950, not on the model name. Kimi-K3.1 has the same MoE shapes at TP8 (896 experts, top-k 16, hidden 3584, per-rank intermediate 384, SiTU beta 4 / linear beta 25), so these paths apply to it too. title: [Fix] multimodal: bound image preprocessing GPU memory; reject decompression bombs
summary: ## Motivation Kimi GPU image preprocessing runs in the tokenizer process on GPU 0, alongside TP rank 0's static pools. - A many-image request batched every same-size image into one fp32 tensor. A 48-image request exhausted GPU 0 and returned a 500 CUDA OOM. - The tokenizer's caching allocator kept that peak reserved on GPU 0 after the request finished. - PIL's `DecompressionBombError` surfaced as a 500. ## Modifications - Each NaViT size group is processed in sub-batches of at most 512 MiB (`_GPU_PREPROCESS_CHUNK_BYTES`). - Tokenizer-side Kimi preprocessing releases the GPU cache only when free cached memory (reserved minus allocated) exceeds 1 GiB, so small requests skip it. Model-side deferred preprocessing does not release. - Sources above 4096x4096 are resized on the CPU with the same antialiased bicubic kernel. `max_gpu_resize_pixels` is a required keyword argument, so every caller states its cap. - On a tokenizer-side GPU OOM, Kimi-K3 serves the request through its CPU processor. - `DecompressionBombError` maps to the existing "Could not decode image" `ValueError`, which returns a 400. ## Accuracy Tests - `test_kimi_k3_gpu_preprocess.py` and `test_mm_process_config.py` pass on CPU. The 2 `midashenglm` failures in the same suite also fail on `main`. - On MI355X, `test_kimi_gpu_resize_parity.py` passes: the CPU fallback stays within 1 pixel level of the GPU resize. - 48-image requests on MI355X give the same output chunked and unchunked: | Images | Unchunked peak | Chunked peak | |---|---|---| | 48 x 3024x4032 | 10.85 GiB | 5.40 GiB | | 48 x 4000x6000 | 18.68 GiB | 5.22

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] mega_moe: Opt-in FlashInfer SM107 MegaMoE for the W4A4 MXFP4 layers
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation On Vera Rubin (SM107), prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe --enable-w4a4-mxfp4-megamoe` spends most of its GPU time in DeepGEMM's MXFP4 x MXFP4 MegaMoE. FlashInfer has a native SM107 CuTe DSL MegaMoE with the same numerics, E2M1 with per-32 E8M0 scales on both operands (`Sm107_Mxfp4_Mxfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7944). At DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's DEP2 prefill shapes it is 17-24% faster per layer than DeepGEMM pre-dispatch + MegaMoE. This PR adds it as an opt-in backend for the `mxf4xmxf4` layers. It uses FlashInfer's canonical prequantized weight transform, and SGLang keeps one copy of the expert weights. On this branch, cold prefill throughput rises 3.0% with FlashInfer 0.7.5 and 4.3% with FlashInfer main. In an end-to-end PD run it raised prefill throughput per prefill GPU by 4.0% (below). ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_moe.py`, active only with `SGLANG_OPT_MEGA_MOE_MXFP4_FLASHINFER=1` and only for `mxf4xmxf4` layers: - **Weights.** `build_mega_moe_experts_weights` hands the packed E2M1 weights and E8M0 scales to FlashInfer's `preprocess_mega_weights` and builds a `MoEEpMegaLayer` on the MoE EP group. FlashInfer's transformed tensors are expert-major, and each expert's slice is one gapless block. The four routed-expert parameters become `(E_local, bytes)` uint8 views of those tensors, so SGLang's own copies are freed and EPLB rebalancing moves the kernel's weights in place. - **Forward.** `run_mega_routed_experts` sends these layers to FlashInfer with int32 top-k ids

title: [Perf] Triton MoE is 5–8× slower than flashinfer_cutlass for Nemotron 3 Nano FP8 at TP8 on H100
summary: The default on Hopper is `flashinfer_cutlass`, so default users don't hit this. With `--moe-runner-backend triton`, Nemotron 3 Nano FP8 (ModelOpt per-tensor FP8) at TP8 on 8×H100 decodes 5–8× slower: step time 3.1 → 19.8 ms at batch 16, and 5.7 → 41.3 ms at batch 128. GSM8K is unchanged (91.0 vs 92.0). A standalone kernel benchmark at the shard shape (E=128, N=232, K=2688) gives Triton/cutlass ratios of 4.5–23×. No tuned `fp8_w8a8` config exists for E=128,N=232 on H100, so this is likely the default-config fallback. Not root-caused.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Pick the plain Ulysses exchange's transport by payload

title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: Keep gfx12xx off the slow hipBLASLt linear+GELU epilogue
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** `_input_independent_ok` in `fused_linear_gelu_site.py` gates the `torch._addmm_activation` linear+GELU epilogue behind `current_arch().is_sm_at_least(12)`. `is_sm_at_least` is implemented on `CudaArch` only; `HipArch` does not override it, so the `DeviceArch` base returns False for every non-NVIDIA device. On gfx1250 the guard therefore never fires, the epilogue is mounted, and hipBLASLt dispatches it to a Tensile `Cijk_...MT32x16x32` kernel that takes ~257 ms per call where the unfused GEMM takes ~17 ms. title: [Feature] Enhancing api.v1 gRPC control plane and operability

title: [Fix] disaggregation: wait for the prefill forward before sending KV chunks under PP
summary: ## Motivation On a disaggregated prefill server with pipeline parallelism, `process_prefill_chunk` sends the KV of a chunked request's non-final chunk at the start of the next scheduler iteration. At that point the chunk's forward has only been launched on `forward_stream`, and the PP event loop does not wait for it before the page indices are handed to the KV sender. With the default PP comm path and the default `--pp-async-batch-depth 0`, this happens to be safe. After launching a batch, each stage issues a P2P send for it (proxy tensors on non-last stages, outputs on the last stage) that makes the schedule stream wait on that forward's event. The page-index copy in `send_kv_chunk` is issued on that stream after the wait, so it completes only after the forward: v0.5.22 blocks on it with `.cpu()`, and on main the Mooncake transfer worker synchronizes on its `indices_event`. Three settings break this ordering: - `--pp-async-batch-depth N` with N > 0: the last stage sends the outputs of the micro-batch launched N iterations earlier, before it launches the current one, so what holds its scheduler back now refers to that older forward. The last stage hands each non-final chunk to the KV sender while the chunk's forward is still running. - `SGLANG_PP_COMM_OVERLAP=1`: the wait is issued on the dedicated PP comm stream instead, so on the non-last stages nothing orders the KV read after the forward anymore. - `SGLANG_PP_SKIP_PURE_CHUNKED_OUTPUT_COMM=1`: the last stage skips the output send for a batch that holds a single non-final chunk, and the wait goes with it. #47074 reports t
