title: [Perf] [AMD] Qwen3.8: Serve QSA decode with AITER's fused FlyDSL sparse decode on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, Qwen3.8 QSA decode and speculative verify run the sparse attention as two passes: 1. a Triton gather copies each row's selected KV (up to 2051 positions) into packed scratch; 2. a Triton decode runs one program per (row, KV head). At decode batch sizes that is an extra round trip through the selected KV, and most of the GPU sits idle. At 32k context with MTP on one MI355X, QSA attention takes about 9.4% of decode GPU time, roughly 120 µs per layer call. AITER now has a fused FlyDSL kernel for gfx950: `aiter.ops.flydsl.qsa_sparse_decode` [(AITER PR](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6670)). It reads the selected KV straight from the pool through `req_to_token` and splits each row's selection across CTAs. This PR serves QSA decode and verify with it. ## Modifications - `QwenSparseAttnBackend.forward_decode` → `_forward_paged_attention` takes the fused kernel first on HIP when `can_use_flydsl_qsa_sparse_decode` accepts the operands: gfx950, bf16 q, bf16 or fp8 KV, head_dim 256, GQA group ≤ 16. That covers decode, target verify and draft extend, since each query row is its own length-one query. Everything else falls through to the existing path unchanged. - **Split count:** `recommended_num_splits` sets the KV split count per batch size, so it is fixed for each captured CUDA graph. - **Workspace:** sized once at the captured maximum with `workspace_partials`, because graphs keep raw pointers to it. title: [Perf] scheduler: Skip external store probes when ranking the waiting queue
summary: ## Motivation With `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first`, every scheduling pass re-matches the whole waiting queue to rank it. With the unified-cache external linker, each of those matches also runs a synchronous lookup in the external KV store for every uncached page. Once the queue grows to a few hundred long-context requests, a pass spends most of its time on remote lookups and prefill throughput collapses while the GPUs sit idle. ## Modifications - Ranking matches only the device and host tree (`MatchPrefixParams.probe_external=False`). Admission still re-matches each request it takes, external probe included, so loads from the store are unchanged. - Past `WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX` waiting requests, a ranking pass refreshes only never-matched requests plus a rotating window of matched ones, so its cost is O(window) instead of O(queue x context). - Ranking reuses the incrementally kept fill ids instead of concatenating input and output ids per request. ## Accuracy GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples, T=1.0): 0.965 before, 0.970 after. ## Benchmark DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300, DP-attention 2 + EP2, DSPARK, Mooncake external linker over RDMA, multi-turn long-context replay with live outputs; output tokens/min per GPU, 0 errors: | Concurrency | main | this PR | gain | |---|---|---|---| | 128 | 151,750 | 157,543 | 1.04x | | 256 | 63,500 | 173,500 | 2.7x | | 512 | 34,788 | 177,900 | 5.1x | Prefix hit rate is unchanged (0.97). title: [Perf] [AMD] hyperconnection: Add a Triton prefill path for gated HC sites
summary: ## Motivation On gfx950, a gated hyper-connection (HC) site with a per-branch norm runs a grouped norm that writes a BF16 normed residual, then a mix and `hc_combine` that read it. Up to 128 rows (its `_MAX_ROWS`) the mix is AITER's FlyDSL mix where it is installed; above, it is unfused: hipBLASLt GEMMs and TorchInductor kernels. Prefill, speculative-verify and draft-extend batches take this path at every site. For batches of more than 48 rows, this PR adds an opt-in path that never writes the normed residual: the norm's `(1 + w)` is folded into the down and inject weights, so one GEMM over the HC branches reads the raw residual, and each branch's `rstd` scales its output. Up to 512 rows (a verify pass of 13 to 128 requests at 4 rows each, or a short prefill chunk) that GEMM is a split-K Triton kernel; above, `torch.bmm`. On one MI355X, a site's mix + combine takes 25-40 % less time than the unfused path with TorchInductor's defaults and 36-51 % less with the image's max-autotune setting (129 to 16,384 rows). At 129 to 512 rows the split-K kernel takes up to 11 % more off the `torch.bmm` version of this path, and above 512 rows it changes nothing. At 49 to 128 rows, timed in chains of 48 sites, a site takes 33-47 % less time than on the FlyDSL mix path. Related work: - #40552 (closed) and its FlashInfer successor #50538 (open) apply the same scheme on NVIDIA SM100, and also carry the square sums from one block to the next. This PR does not carry them. - #48648 fuses the norm and inject into the FlyDSL mix for batches up to 128 rows, and also hands the combine the inject log

title: [Fix] rl: One tensor weight payload per engine rank under pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Motivation `update_weights_from_tensor` sends one CUDA-IPC payload per TP rank and each scheduler rank reads `serialized_named_tensors[tp_rank]`. With `pp_size > 1`, stage 1's rank r opens the same handle as stage 0's rank r: it gets stage 0's parameters, which it does not own and skips, so later stages are never updated. Two consumers on one IPC handle also break producer-side refcounting (#8203 saw it as OOM). ## Modifications Payloads are now one per engine rank in world-rank order: producers emit `tp_size * pp_size` copies and each rank reads entry `tp_size * pp_rank + tp_rank`. summary: ## Motivation With DP attention and the gathered MoE on HIP, each rank all-gathers bf16 hidden states. title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM5: Fuse KPool Hadamard and FP8 quant on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash uses `IndexerKPool`, so the non-pooled indexer optimization in #30715 does not apply to it. Its query path separately launches Hadamard rotation and FP8 quantization in every DSA layer; dual-stream decode also launches two elementwise operations to apply the head-gate scale. This ports that fusion to `IndexerKPool`. The intended benefit is fewer kernel launches and one fewer BF16 intermediate round-trip, not an end-to-end throughput claim. Component launch profile on MI355X/gfx950: | path | fusion off | fusion on | |---|---:|---:| | prefill | 2 launches | 1 launch | | dual-stream decode | 4 launches | 1 launch | ## Modifications - Add `fused_hadamard_act_quant`, a Triton kernel combining the query-side Walsh-Hadamard transform and block FP8 quantization. - Preserve the production BF16 materialization boundary inside the fused kernel so `ue8m0` scales match the two-pass path exactly. - Fold `weights * q_scale * softmax_scale` into the fused kernel when dual-stream decode has precomputed head-gate weights. - Wire the kernel only into `IndexerKPool`; the non-pooled `Indexer` remains unchanged. - Keep the existing path as the default and fallback. The fused path requires `SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_HADAMARD_QUANT=1`, ROCm gfx950, a power-of-two head dimension, and `head_dim == block_size`. - Add gfx950 tests covering GLM-5.3-Flash geometry `(M, 32, 128)`, `M={1,64,4096,16384}`, two seeds, `ue8m0` and unrounded scales, production two-pass parity, folded weights, finite outputs, and CUDA graph replay. ## Accuracy Tests Full GLM-5.3-Flash Quark MXFP4 GSM8K on snap

summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA layers use the safe gate (`lower_bound`), so on ROCm their decode skips the packed decode path. title: [diffusion] Serve the LLaDA-Image Turbo FP8 checkpoint on one GPU
summary: ## Motivation inclusionAI publishes a pre-quantized FP8 checkpoint of LLaDA-Image Turbo, `inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8`. sglang refuses it at startup today. With this PR it serves on one GPU from its own quantization metadata, with lower latency and about 18.6 GiB less device memory than BF16 Turbo at matching quality. It follows the BF16 LLaDA-Image support of #37907. ## Modifications - The DiT loads its FP8 weights through the native FP8 linear method from the checkpoint's `quantization_config`. Only serialized FP8 weights in 128x128 blocks with dynamic activation scales are accepted, and any other declared quantization fails at startup with the declared config named. - The FP8 DiT stays resident on the GPU when the automatic memory policy would offload it. An explicit transformer offload fails at startup with the flags named. - The text encoder's `llada_fp8_experts` metadata maps to a standard FP8 config that quantizes only the routed experts. Attention, shared experts, and the dense MLPs keep their BF16 weights. - The LLaDA2 loader expands the fused per-expert block scales into `weight_scale_inv`. Every other tensor keeps its name, and none of the 96 public LLaDA2 repositories checked carries the fused scale names, so they load as before. - The FP8 Base checkpoint `inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-FP8` stays refused at startup, with a message that points to BF16 Base (see Accuracy Tests). - The `--quantization` refusal now points to the Turbo FP8 checkpoint. ## Reproduction ```bash sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8 --revision 664a975e4b4980fb750fd4

summary: ## Motivation ModelSlim checks the quantization scheme before it builds a fused layer. For QKV, it used to require a description for each of Q, K, and V. This catches incomplete descriptions and helps avoid choosing the wrong scheme for the layer. Gemma 4 shares K and V in some text layers. For example, layer 5 in the Eco-Tech MXFP4 checkpoints lists `q_proj.weight` and `k_proj.weight` as `W8A8_MXFP8`. The loader uses K for V too, so the checkpoint has no separate `v_proj.weight` entry. ModelSlim raised an error before the loader reached that layer. ## Modifications When a packed layer has descriptions for only some of its parts, log the missing keys and use the scheme from the parts that are present. In the Gemma example, Q and K agree on MXFP8. Conflicting schemes and ambiguous whole-layer and split descriptions still raise an error. ## Accuracy Tests All 16 CPU tests in `test_modelslim_mapping.py` passed. We checked metadata from two checkpoints on ModelScope: - [Eco-Tech/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w4a4-mxfp4](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w4a4-mxfp4) - [Eco-Tech/gemma-4-31B-it-w4a4-mxfp4](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/gemma-4-31B-it-w4a4-mxfp4) All 15 shared K/V text layers select MXFP8. The other 75 text QKV layers select MXFP8 without a missing-key warning. End-to-end accuracy is untested. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The change runs during layer setup. No inference speed benchmark was run. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html

title: [Feat] [AMD] tlx: Add the vendored gfx950 TLX GEMM and Muse MoE kernels on stock Triton via uTLX

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsa: Fuse the FP4 indexer key store and head gate
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-fp4-indexer`, Kimi-K3.1 decode TPOT is about 1.0-1.3% (roughly 0.1 ms per token) above the FP8 indexer at every context length (numbers in #51450, now merged). The FP4 decode step runs more small kernels per DSA layer than FP8: the key is quantized and stored by two kernels, and the BF16 head gate is scaled by three elementwise ops. ## Modifications - `store_fp4_index_k_cache`: below 4096 tokens, one kernel quantizes each key row and writes it to its page. Larger batches keep the batched quantize kernel followed by the store. - `indexer_head_gate`: one kernel for the BF16 head-gate scaling of an indexer whose query carries no scale; `Fp4Indexer._fused_q_quant` uses it. Per DSA layer and decode step this takes the FP4 path from 6 kernels to 3 (FP8 runs 2). The query quantize stays a separate kernel inside the scoring call. The store change also applies to the DeepSeek V4 pool, which shares the kernel. ## Results Kimi-K3.1 on 2x GB300 trays, TP8 / DCP8, `--enable-fp4-indexer`, single request, four launches alternating unfused and fused on the same nodes (median of 6 runs of 256 tokens per launch): | TPOT (ms) | unfused | fused | delta | |---|---|---|---| | ctx 132K | 9.746 / 9.771 | 9.652 / 9.658 | -1.1% | | ctx 33K | 9.551 / 9.563 | 9.473 / 9.470 | -0.9% | | ctx 2K | 9.577 / 9.596 | 9.497 / 9.507 | -0.9% | TTFT is unchanged (cold 131K 5.37 s on all arms). GSM8K 200 on a fused arm: 99.0%. Kernel tests pass on GB300. Not measured: concurrency, and DeepSeek V4 perf with the fused store. Details in the comment below. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ###

title: [Fix] dsa: Attend the sharded indexer's local slots in trtllm / prims_ts DCP decode
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1 under decode context parallelism produces garbage with `--dsa-decode-backend prims_ts` or `trtllm`: GSM8K drops from ~0.97 to ~0.03 and answers mix in other requests' content. `flashmla_kv` (the default) is unaffected, so `test_kimi_k31_b300.py` stays green. The InferenceX Kimi-K3.1 GB300 recipes serve with `prims_ts`, so every disagg point broke when moving from the Kimi-K3.1 Day-0 image to a main nightly (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261118-ecd3d75a`). Root cause: a semantic merge conflict between two PRs that are each correct on their own base. They touch different lines, so they merged cleanly. - sgl-project/sglang#49106 (opened before the next PR merged) added sharded DCP decode (`dcp_partial`) to `_forward_trtllm`, which both `trtllm` and `prims_ts` go through. On its base the indexer returned global slots (`dcp_global_topk`), so it localized them with `localize_dcp_page_table`. That remap treats its input as interleaved global slots, keeps `slot % dcp_size == dcp_rank`, and maps those to `slot // dcp_size`. - sgl-project/sglang#48895 merged first and moved localization into the indexer: `dcp_local_topk` returns this rank's compacted local KV slots and writes their counts to `metadata.dcp_topk_length`. It updated the only consumer that existed then, `flashmla_kv`, to take them as-is. After both merged, `_forward_trtllm` localizes slots that are already local. That keeps about 1/dcp_size of the selected keys and points them at unrelated KV entries. The Day-0 branch localized only once, with `dcp_localize_compact` at this point in the back

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Run mla_v_absorb on the transposed w_vc that DeepSeek-style loaders keep
summary: ## Motivation `mla_v_absorb` (#50997) replaces hipBLASLt's `torch.bmm` for MLA's v absorb at decode-sized batches, and #51000 calls it from `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` under `--enable-amd-monokernel`. `covered()` requires a contiguous `w_vc`, but Kimi-K3.1 and DFLASH's MLA draft load `w_vc` as `w_vc.contiguous().transpose(1, 2)`, which is not contiguous. So the kernel never runs: on Kimi-K3.1-Pro TP8 decode, all 29 v absorbs per step (24 target layers and 5 draft layers) still go to hipBLASLt (`Cijk_..._MT128x32x128`, 7.9 µs each). ## Modifications - The kernel takes `w_vc`'s K and N strides. `covered()` accepts a unit-stride K axis (the transposed layout the loaders keep) or a unit-stride N axis (contiguous). - Tile: one 512-wide K step, 16-column blocks, 2 warps. A sweep over both layouts at 1-64 tokens puts it within 4% of each case's best. - `test_mla_v_absorb.py`: both layouts at 1, 6, 8 and 64 tokens against an fp32 bmm, plus the inputs `covered()` rejects. The transposed cases fail on `main`. ## Accuracy Tests Kimi-K3.1-Pro, 8x MI355X, #51000's head (`afe367c955`; `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` and `mla_v_absorb.py` are unchanged on `main`), sgl-amd-mono with sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#160, `--enable-amd-monokernel`, DFLASH with 8 draft tokens, GSM8K 1319 (`few_shot_gsm8k`): | | Accuracy | |---|---| | before | 0.967 | | this PR | 0.964 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling Kernel, gfx950, per call inside a CUDA graph cycling 29 weights: | tokens | `torch.bmm` today (transposed `w_vc`) | this PR (transposed) | before, contiguous `w_vc` | this PR (contiguous) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 6.30 µs

title: [Fix] marlin: Prevent scale underflow in NVFP4 fallback on SM80-SM90 (#44998)
summary: fixes #44998 when running nvfp4 on pre-blackwell gpus with marlin, checkpoints that have small block scales (like weight_scale_2 = 1.0 from modelopt, probec, or llm-compressor) underflow during bf16 dequantization. the marlin packing does `(scales * 2^7).view(int16) << 1` which assumes `scales * 2^7 >= 2`. with small scales, the top bit is unset and bf16 exponent widening causes the weights to dequantize to zero, corrupting output. ported the fix from vllm #34577: - added `_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor` to upscale small block scales by a power of 2 so `scales * 2^7 >= 2` - clamped subnormals (`scales < 2`) to zero to prevent bit corruptions - compensated by dividing `weight_global_scale` by `scale_factor` - unified the scale factor across experts in `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin` - added unit tests covering scale factor computation, dense/moe scale adjustment, and underflow prevention <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->⊘ **Skipped** -- add the `run-ci` label to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->⊘ **Skipped** -- add the `run-ci` label to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->⊘ **Skipped** -- add the `run-ci` label to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end --> > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. title: [Perf] dp-attention: Symmetric-memory push for attention-TP2 all-gather / reduce-scatter with MegaMoE
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention over TP2 pairs and the MegaMoE a2a backend (e.g. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash at `--tp-size 8 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend megamoe`), every layer does an attention-TP all-gather and reduce-scatter of a few hundred decode rows over NCCL. At these sizes NCCL's fixed cost dominates. ## Modifications - New `layers/attn_tp_push_comm.py`: a symmetric-memory push for the TP2 attention group. Each rank writes the peer's rows into the peer's buffer, then runs one GPU barrier. Each op kind has two buffer generations: a slot is rewritten two ops later, after a barrier that follows its last read. The peer store is an elementwise kernel (`bitwise_or(x, 0)` on int16 views). On B300, `copy_` into peer-mapped memory takes the driver's peer memcpy and cost about 15 us more per call. - `dp_attention.attn_tp_all_gather_into_tensor` / `attn_tp_reduce_scatter_tensor` try the push first. The DP gather and the reduce-scatter paths now go through these two helpers instead of calling the group directly. Anything the push does not take falls back to NCCL: 2D bf16 rows of the model hidden size, up to 4096 gathered rows, are taken; everything else is not. - Enabled at `init_layer_runtime` only when the attention-TP group has 2 ranks and is narrower than TP, the a2a backend is `megamoe`, and CUDA is available. MegaMoE synchronizes every EP rank each layer, which orders slot reuse across forwards. The comm object lives in a `get_resources()` slot. - New env var `SGLANG_OPT_ATTN_TP2_PUSH_COMM` (default on); `=0` keeps NCCL. ## Accuracy Tests On our MiniMax-M3.

title: [Perf] dspark: Split the eager verify accept over a TP2 group, keep verify logits as vocab shards

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] minimax-m3.1: Overlap the routed-input NVFP4 quant with the router GEMM
summary: ## Motivation In MiniMax-M3.1 decode under CUDA graphs, the shared experts run on the main stream while the router GEMM, top-k and routed experts run on the alt stream. The routed experts then quantize their input to per-token NVFP4 at the start of the TRTLLM-Gen MoE call, which serializes after the router. That quant only depends on the hidden states, so it can run on the main stream while the router GEMM runs on the alt stream. ## Modifications - `moe_runner/flashinfer_trtllm.py`: the per-token NVFP4 input quant moves into `quantize_nvfp4_per_token_input`, which returns an `Nvfp4PerTokenInputPreQuant`. `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4` uses `dispatch_output.hidden_states_pre_quant` when it holds one (and the hidden dim is not padded), otherwise it quantizes as before. - `models/minimax_m3.py`: `MiniMaxM3MoE.router_quant_overlap` is set for `MiniMaxM3Nvfp4Config` on Blackwell with no MoE a2a and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`. In the graph-captured dual-stream path, the main stream quantizes and records an event; the alt stream runs the router and top-k, waits on the event, and passes the result to the experts as `pre_quant_input` (the existing `FusedMoE` plumbing that sets `hidden_states_pre_quant`). - `test_minimax_m31_model.py`: the deferred-finalize mock takes the new `pre_quant_input` keyword. The quant is the same call on the same input, so outputs do not change. There is no switch; the path applies whenever its conditions hold. Eager, breakable-graph and prefill paths are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Not run on this branch; it was only import- and lint-check

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] minimax-m3.1: Context-parallel MSA-v1 decode indexer at attention TP2
summary: ## Motivation MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (NVFP4, MSA-v1 Q8KV4 index cache) is served at attention TP2. The decode indexer is replicated: both ranks score all four index heads over the whole context, so at long context it costs the same per rank as at TP1. This PR splits the pages over the two ranks. title: [Perf] paged-experts: pre-copy the next layer's predicted experts beside compute
summary: # [Perf] paged-experts: pre-copy the next layer's predicted experts beside compute ## Motivation In a captured Paged Experts decode step, a MoE layer copies its missing experts into GPU slots only after the layer has routed, so every page-in sits on the critical path. title: [Fix] dsa: Isolate masked KV rows in FP8 TileLang attention
summary: ## Motivation Invalid (`-1`) sparse indices in `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial_fp8` map to KV row 0. Masking the attention score does not isolate that row: a NaN in it can propagate through both QK (`-inf + NaN`) and PV (`0 * NaN`), corrupting otherwise valid outputs and generation logprobs. This was reproduced on GLM-5.3-Flash with FP8 KV and TileLang DSA on H20, with both PP1 and PP2, including a plain-main deployment without EPLB. A direct operator reproduction changed only padding KV row 0 from zero to NaN and changed the output from finite to 196608 NaN elements. This is a correctness fix; it does not require changing the deployment's CUDA Graph, overlap, or speculative decoding settings. Related prior work: #44541 applies the same masked-load isolation to the BF16 kernel and explicitly leaves the FP8 kernel unchanged. summary: ## Motivation `Indexer._indexer_tp_split` is called by every participating DSA layer. Its host-only row partition currently materializes several tensors of length `q_offset` (including two repeat-interleaves and a cumulative sum) even for a single request. This fixed cost matters for short extends over cached context, and grows with the number of new query rows. Within a request that cost is an arithmetic series (with a flat head for the existing minimum-cost clamp). - Locate each target cost in the request prefix sums and invert the local cumulative cost using integer square root. This returns exactly the same right-side cut as the original per-row `searchsorted`; no floating-point rounding. - Preserve the uniform fallback for inconsistent length metadata and the original nonempty-rank clamping. title: [Roadmap] CUDA Graph Persistence with Foundry
summary: ## Overview This issue tracks CUDA graph persistence in SGLang: `--cuda-graph-persistence save` captures the graphs as usual and writes them, with the memory layout they reference, to an archive; `--cuda-graph-persistence load` restores them from the archive instead of capturing. It is opt-in and built on [Foundry](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry) (`pip install "sglang[foundry]"`, package `foundry-core`). A restored start skips the per-shape warmup and capture. On 2x H100 the capture loops of a `load` take 6 to 16 % of the native ones in the per-commit tests (decode graphs), and outputs match the native engine. The first integration is in review. The next steps are to loosen the dependency coupling, move the remaining initialization changes into SGLang for transparency, remove the two separate initialization paths the integration introduces, and widen what can be persisted. **References:** - Integration PR: #42254 - Foundry roadmap: https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry/issues/49 - Documentation: `docs/advanced_features/cuda_graph_persistence` (lands with #42254) ## Roadmap ### 1. Dependency and packaging - [ ] `foundry-core` on the LibTorch stable ABI: one wheel for every torch >= 2.14 and every CPython. A torch bump in SGLang then no longer needs a new `foundry-core`, and the tests can drop the torch-pin skip. - [ ] Require `foundry-core>=0.1.0` once it is released. ### 2. Initial integration - [ ] `--cuda-graph-persistence {save,load}` with the Foundry adapter, call sites, docs and e2e tests: #42254 - Decode graphs on the full backend, full prefill graphs, TP / E

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Opt-in single-pass Triton top-k for long-context decode rows
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, DSA decode and MTP verify run their top-2048 + page transform through the top-k v2 kernel. At long contexts with 72 or more rows per rank, v2 takes 113 to 127 us per call on MI355X. This PR adds a single-pass Triton/Gluon selector that takes 58 to 82 us there, 1.5x to 1.9x faster. It is opt-in via `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_TRITON=1` because it is slower than v2 at short contexts; see the table below. ## Modifications - **New `kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_topk_transform.py`**: three launches whose shape depends only on the row count (CUDA-graph safe). - `est`: per row, samples about 8192 logits and bit-searches a threshold that leaves about 2 x topk elements above it. Rounding down admits more candidates, but a biased sample can still overestimate the full-row threshold; the selector handles candidate underflow explicitly. - `collect`: one pass over the logits on a persistent grid; keys at or above the threshold go to a per-row candidate buffer of 8192 entries. - `select`: the exact k-th largest key among the candidates, then exactly min(L, topk) slots through the compact page table (`real_page_table`, page_size 64). This is the table the v2 decode graph keeps, so it needs no page_size=1 table. - **Exact fallback.** If a row has fewer than min(L, topk) candidates or overflows the 8192-entry buffer, `select` takes the k-th largest key over the whole row and emits from it. This path is slow and rare, but it keeps the result an exact top-k for any input. - **Dispatch** (`dsa_topk_backend.topk_transform`): this path is used, instead of v2, for decode-shaped PAG

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] kvcache: Gate fused FP8 prefix-valid commit kernel on SM89+
summary: Motivation set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8 (added by #40785) fuses FP8 KV-cache quantization into the prefix-valid commit kernel used by DFLASH speculative decoding. It compiles fp8e4nv inside a Triton kernel, which only works on SM89+ (Ada / Hopper). On SM86 (Ampere, e.g. RTX 3090) the Triton codegen rejects fp8e4nv: ValueError: type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5'). The dispatch in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid only checks the KV cache dtype and the resolved K/V scales — it does not inspect the compute capability — so an SM86 box is sent straight into the fused kernel and crashes on startup. The pre-#40785 eager path (PyTorch-layer quantization + the generic byte-copy Triton kernel) is left untouched below the fused branch, so the fix is to fall back to it on pre-SM89 GPUs. This is the prefix-valid writer specifically. #31652 gates the ordinary set_kv_buffer FP8 stores on SM89+ but leaves the prefix-valid dispatch ungated, and #42982 (SM89 NaN-saturation) does not add a capability guard either. title: [Feat] dsv41: Support encoder-only prefill for PD disaggregation

title: [Fix] hicache: Move NIXL pages that are not whole O_DIRECT blocks
summary: ## Motivation Refs #45563. With a NIXL file plugin and O_DIRECT on (the default), every transfer's address and length must be whole 4 KiB blocks. title: [Fix] cuda-graph: Pack prefill aux hidden states into one runner-owned buffer

The same flags without a draft, or with EAGLE (MTP), start normally. These drafts read the target's hidden states from 5 layers; for the 32,768-token shape one set is 5 × 32768 × 5120 × 2 B = 1.68 GB. That PR established the idea and the file: time the all-reduce backends and write the best one per message size to a JSON table. It kept to four backends, derived the sizes from the model config, timed eager calls only, and ran from a `--allreduce` flag on the auto-tune main flow. What is kept from it is the shape of the output and the place in the tree. What is new here is a second timing mode for CUDA graphs, a selection file that names who competes, cross-rank agreement before entering any collective, and the synchronisation needed to keep eight ranks from wedging in a timing loop. The entry point is a standalone torchrun module that starts no server and loads no model. Which all-reduce backend is fastest depends on the message size, the hardware, and whether the call is replayed from a CUDA graph. New all-reduce implementations keep landing (another custom all-reduce, another QuickReduce codec, FlyDSL INT4), and the only way to know where each one wins is to time them against each other on the machine before a model is started. The tuner is the tool for that: it opens the kernels the selection names, times them at the sizes you list, and writes the winner per size. ## Workflow Commands, example output for each mode, and the stack-dump guide are in `python/sglang/auto_tune/README.md`. summary: ## Motivation On Hopper, Inkling-2-Small decode returns garbage once requests are batched, unless the server runs with a page size that is a multiple of the decode tile (the cookbook's `--page-size 128`). [concurrency 16] The user wants ★★★ The user response follows.The user wants coral 0The ocean covers about the ocean is ... ``` Nothing warns or fails. A lone request usually gets contiguous slots. summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, a model that fuses RoPE with its KV write corrupts the unified KV arena's reserved padding slot. Slot 0 is the padding sink: graph padding rows write their dummy K and V there, and masked page-table entries read that page back. The fused HIP writer stores to whatever destination it is handed, including slot 0, so the sink stops being zero. This PR skips the reserved destination and writes through the physical locations the attention backend already computed. title: [Fix] bench: retry a lost request and abort a stalled run
summary: ## Motivation `sglang-bench` (the Rust client) intermittently records `error sending request` under high concurrency. Printing the error source chain shows the connection dies while the request is in flight: error sending request for url (...) <- client error (SendRequest) <- connection closed before message completed error sending request for url (...) <- client error (SendRequest) <- connection error <- Connection reset by peer (os error 104) The client keeps an idle connection for 90 s (reqwest's default). SGLang's HTTP server closes an idle keep-alive connection 5 s after a response completes (`SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`, the timer uvicorn arms in `on_response_complete`), and a request written at that boundary is closed without an answer. This is tracked upstream as uvicorn discussion #3258 (measured on v0.54.0; main a99c1b7 has the same handler): the timer closes the connection even when the next request has already arrived, and hyper does not resend a request it has written. Reproduced against this server with a raw-socket harness (5 s keep-alive, 32 connections x 5 rounds): writes 10, 5 or 2 ms before the deadline were all served (160/160 each), while writes at the deadline lost the connection every time (32/32 closed, no silent waits). Separately, a run can stop making progress altogether: a request that never completes keeps the run alive until that request's six-hour timeout and reports nothing at all. title: [Fix] deepseek_v4: floor amax before the division in the V4.1 fp8 KV scale
summary: ## Motivation The V4.1 fp8 KV store (`store_row_fp8`) and its pure-torch reference floor the scale quotient, `2^ceil(log2(max(amax / 448, 1e-4)))`, so the smallest scale is 2^-13. DeepSeek's `act_quant` (`scale_fmt="ue8m0"`) floors `amax` first, `max(amax, 1e-4) / 448`, so its smallest scale is 2^-22. summary: ## What changes With synchronous EPLB, the forward thread submits expert transfers and writes the received weights into place before returning to inference. `--enable-eplb --eplb-async-rebalance` lets Ascend stage one layer on a worker while subsequent forwards use its current placement. The option is experimental and defaults to off. ## Moving one layer The worker uses the existing expert-to-peer mapping, batch boundaries and `torch.distributed.batch_isend_irecv` on a dedicated HCCL process group. title: [NPU] [Roadmap] SGLang Diffusion Integration with MindIE-SD
summary: ## Background SGLang Diffusion already supports RainFusion, adaptive block sparse, and Laser attention on Ascend. Extending sparse attention and quantized FA requires ongoing kernel development, integration, and maintenance. Maintaining these paths ourselves means bringing the required kernels and bindings into `sgl-kernel-npu`, as is currently done with the `attentions` module, and keeping them compatible with new CANN releases and Ascend devices. This duplicates work across inference frameworks and increases the effort needed to adopt new optimizations and fixes. [MindIE-SD](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD) is a diffusion acceleration framework that provides optimized attention implementations and public APIs for sparse and quantized execution. Reusing these APIs can reduce duplicated kernel maintenance and shorten the path to adopting performance improvements in SGLang. vLLM-Omni also integrates MindIE-SD, providing a precedent for sharing this acceleration layer across inference frameworks. This roadmap starts with attention backends, with potential extensions to other MindIE-SD optimizations. SGLang remains responsible for model execution, scheduling, and parallelism; MindIE-SD supplies optimized execution APIs. The integration boundary and configuration design are discussed in [RFC #48582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48582). ## Motivation Provide a maintainable way to adopt MindIE-SD optimizations in SGLang Diffusion, reducing duplicated kernel development and enabling faster adoption of performance improvements on Ascend. title: [Fix] [AMD] scheduler: Retire a stashed chunk's window rows behind its forward
summary: With `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1` and the WAR barrier off (its default on ROCm), wait for the launched forward before retiring a stashed prefill chunk's out-of-window SWA rows. ## Motivation Stashing a prefill chunk retires its out-of-window SWA rows and clears their full -> SWA mapping on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler that chunk's forward is still running, and the aiter unified-attention path resolves the mapping in every sliding layer's KV store, so the later layers store those tokens at the padding slot and read stale rows. title: [Fix] scheduler: let a client abort yield to the stop or length cap of its step
summary: ## Motivation `Req.update_finish_state` applies a pending abort before it checks the step's own stop token, stop string and length cap. When the step that commits a client abort (`/abort_request`) also reached EOS or `max_new_tokens`, the request finishes as an abort with every committed token. With speculative decoding one step commits several tokens, so the output can carry tokens after the EOS or past `max_new_tokens`. Clients that abort requests and keep the partial outputs then receive tokens past a stop. Related: open #44874 caps aborted speculative output at `max_new_tokens` and keeps the abort reason. This PR covers stop tokens and stop strings too, and reports the step's own finish (`stop` / `length`) for client aborts only; aborts that carry a status code (intake rejections, timeouts, the 499 case in #44874) keep their reason, so the two do not conflict in behavior. ## Modifications - `Req.update_finish_state`: a client abort (`FINISH_ABORT` with no status code) yields to the stop token, stop string or length cap reached in the same step, which then trims the output as usual. Aborts with a status code keep their reason. - Visible to clients: a request aborted with `/abort_request` (or by a session abort) in the step where it reaches a stop token, a stop string or `max_new_tokens` now returns `finish_reason` `stop` or `length` instead of `abort`, with the output trimmed at the stop or the cap. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_finish_length_speculative.py` (CPU), 5 new cases: EOS, stop string and length cap in the abort step win and trim; an abort without a ste

summary: ## Motivation Z-Image folds RoPE into its QK-norm call only on CUDA, or on any platform when the RoPE table is the batched 3D form that carries explicit positions. That 3D table is built in exactly one place, under `len(input_images) > 1 and get_sp_world_size() == 1`, so the common Z-Image configurations never produce it. On ROCm every attention in those configurations therefore runs QK-norm over Q and K and then a separate `RotaryEmbedding` call, one extra kernel per step per block for each of the image, caption, and unified streams. title: [Fix] metrics: Add MLA/MoE-aware FLOPs and fix device-timer prefill TFLOPS estimation in the MFU estimator
summary: ## Motivation `_init_estimated_perf_constants()` in `metrics_reporter.py` applied the generic dense/GQA linear-layer formula to every model, regardless of architecture. Two gaps this causes: - **MLA models** (DeepSeek-V2/V3, MiniCPM3, DeepSeek-VL2, Kimi-VL) have a structurally different attention shape: Q is optionally low-rank compressed (`q_lora_rank`), and K/V are jointly down-projected into one shared latent per token (`kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`) rather than per-head K/V like GQA. Reusing the generic formula (with the padded kernel-layout `head_dim`, e.g. 256) overstates both linear-projection FLOPs and, especially, KV-cache/weight-read bytes -- directly undercutting the bandwidth-bound regime MLA is designed to shrink. - **MoE models** were charged dense `intermediate_size` FFN cost per token, not scaled by how many experts actually activate (`num_experts_per_tok` + shared experts), understating MLP FLOPs/bytes by roughly that multiplier. This is depended on by `fix/hybrid-mamba-mfu-flops-overcount` (#48326)'s `num_attn_layers`/`num_mlp_layers` layer-type split, so this PR is stacked on that one and should be reviewed/merged after it (or rebased if it lands first). A second, smaller fix in the same file: `query_forward_active` (which drives the `forward_overlap` label on `scheduler_stage_seconds_total`) was gated on `self.scheduler.device == "cuda"`, silently disabling it on every non-CUDA backend even though `DeviceTimer`/`_TimingInterval` only use `torch.get_device_module()` + `Event.query()`, both device-agnostic. ### `est. prefill TFLOPS/s` can report physic

summary: ## Motivation A continuation can repeat prefill for a prompt tail that the previous request already computed. summary: ## Motivation Under DP attention every DP rank publishes its own `ForwardPassMetrics` (FPM) stream, one message per step, and a consumer (the Dynamo planner) combines the ranks of one worker. Nothing in a message says which step it belongs to: `counter_id` is a per-rank publisher sequence that also advances on heartbeats. A consumer that reads "the latest message of each rank" can therefore combine rows of different steps, or a measured row with an idle heartbeat. In the validation runs below, that latest-per-rank view held rows of different steps for 2.6% to 8.9% of busy time with 2 DP ranks and 7.9% to 16.5% with 4 (the ranks' messages for one step arrive 0.06 to 2 ms apart at p50 and up to 66 ms apart at worst). This PR adds an optional `iteration_id` to `ForwardPassMetrics`. For a step that the attention-DP ranks launch together, every rank's message carries the same id, so a consumer can group messages by `(worker_id, iteration_id)` and use a set once every rank reported it. ## Modifications - `ForwardPassMetrics.iteration_id: Optional[int] = None`, appended last. `FPM_VERSION` stays 1: a message is a msgpack map keyed by field name (the struct sets neither `array_like` nor `forbid_unknown_fields`), so a consumer built before the field ignores it. summary: ## Motivation Z-Image has 30 attention heads, which do not divide evenly across Ulysses degree 8. Its spatial SP planner also rounds each local image shard to a multiple of 32, even when the complete image already meets the model's 32-token alignment. At 1088x1920 this adds 32 attention-visible image tokens that the single-device reference does not require. The main transformer stack additionally treats caption tokens as a replicated suffix in every block. This PR adds model-local head padding, a guarded global-alignment path, and joint image/caption sequence sharding for native eager Ulysses inference. It preserves existing spatial token ownership and reconstruction while avoiding per-block replicated-caption handling on eligible requests. ## Modifications - Pad Q/K/V with zero-valued heads when the head count does not divide the Ulysses group size, and remove them again before the output projection. Z-Image has 30 heads, so Ulysses degree 8 otherwise fails at the first all-to-all. Only the layers that really exchange heads pad: the context refiner attends over replicated caption tokens on one rank, and a run that selects the K/V-gather exchange keeps every head local, so neither of them pays for padding. - Shard the caption together with the image instead of replicating it. title: [Perf] scheduler: Scale the prefill/decode interval with the waiting backlog
summary: ## Motivation `--prefill-decode-interval N` runs N decode rounds after every prefill batch to protect inter-token latency. title: [Test] [AMD] deterministic: Check AITER paged decode batch invariance on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation Deterministic inference needs batch-invariant decode attention: a request's output must not depend on how many other requests share its batch, or how long they are. On gfx950, the AITER attention backend decodes non-MLA models with AITER's `paged_attention_ragged`. That kernel splits each request's KV cache into fixed 256-token partitions, so its result for one request does not depend on its batchmates. Nothing tests that, though. An AITER update that changed it, for example by choosing the number of partitions from the batch, would make outputs batch-dependent without any test failing. This adds a small kernel-level test to the MI35x per-PR suite. It pins that property, so a regression shows up in CI at the AITER bump that causes it, instead of as non-reproducible outputs later. #44489 proposes allowing AITER decode attention in deterministic mode on gfx950 on the strength of this property. This test is useful with or without it and does not depend on it. Impact: test only. No runtime code changes. Adds about 35 s to the `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite. summary: Stacked on #49462 and #49463; only the last commit is new. ## Motivation After #49463, `MooncakeDirectLinker.load_layer_wise` resolves slot locations before the forward fence, but it still builds each layer group's range reads after the fence, one group at a time: `get_prepared_layers_range_meta`, `tolist`, and the per-thread split. summary: ## Motivation `MooncakeDirectLinker.load_layer_wise` submits the range gets of every layer group before it waits on any of them. Layers complete only in the wait loop that follows. title: [Perf] DFLASH: Verify top-k sampled batches on the all-gathered top-k support (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation This continues #46080 by @nbommi19, rebased onto current main with the review feedback on that PR applied. The original commits are kept. With TP > 1 and a softcapped lm_head, DFLASH verify finishes the logits all-gather in the worker. For a sampled batch it all-gathers the full fp32 logits of every verify row (`[bs * block, vocab]`), runs a top-k over the whole vocabulary, scatters the target p and the draft selector's q into vocab-sized tensors, and runs the chain sampler over the whole vocabulary. When requests sample with a top-k (Muse-Spark-Open's generation config uses top_k 64), only the top-k tokens of a row carry target mass. With `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_SPARSE_VERIFY` on, such a batch is verified on the top-k support alone: - each rank takes the top `next_power_of_2(max_top_k + 16)` logits of its vocab shard; the 16 spare slots hold logits tied with the k-th one; - the ranks all-gather those (value, id) pairs instead of their shards (at TP8 and a 202K vocabulary, 1 KB per row from each rank instead of 101 KB); - one Triton kernel softcaps and merges the candidates into each row's exact top-k and argmax, with the softcap formula of the dense gather; - one Triton kernel runs the chain accept and the residual resample on that support, with the dense path's two uniform draws in the same order. A batch the support cannot reproduce keeps the dense path: max top_k above 64 (top_k -1 included), top-p, min-p, any logit adjustment (penalties, logit bias, custom logit processor, grammar), logprobs, sampling-mask capture, block verification and padded vocab shards. title: [Fix] hicache: Preserve storage prefetch results through admission
summary: ## Motivation HiCache cache-mode storage hits can be lost at two admission boundaries: 1. A capacity-limited prefetch has no active operation yet, so admission may treat the deferred lookup as a miss and cancel it. 2. The original TP2 reproduction used independent 45,056-token L3 prefixes, 50,000-token inputs and 1,000-token outputs. A same-request trace showed capacity rejection, no-operation admission, retry cancellation and zero cached tokens with zero prefetch wait. A regression fails on upstream base `9304abb5321dcf27b28235d53060ecc1438df0f5`. ## Changes and provenance - Preserve pre-query capacity deferrals as explicit waiters, with retry/cancellation and rank-agreed timeout handling. - Retain completed host-cache spans until admission hands ownership to load-back, including abort and teardown cleanup. - Keep pending storage hits under allocation backpressure and account for admission capacity, including PD prefill wait-cycle handling. - Complete PD decode storage lookup before advertising a reusable prefix to prefill, rematch before admission, and transfer/release host references during restore and cancellation. - Settle pending decode prefetches before FIFO admission can stop on a capacity-constrained queue head, then recompute current capacity budgets. - Adapt the dependency stack to the current request-list ownership API. title: [Fix] grpc: Allow --tokenizer-worker-num > 1 with --grpc-port in Rust-server mode
summary: ## Context (TL;DR) - **Report:** a Dynamo deployment of SGLang behind Dynamo's gRPC sidecar could not raise `--tokenizer-worker-num` above 1, because `--grpc-port` refuses it. title: [Fix] [AMD] dflash: Keep the draft KV on full-attention slots under PD disaggregation
summary: On PD prefill and decode servers, keep the DFLASH draft KV pool on full-attention slots instead of the target's sliding-window ids, which the KV transfer does not address. ## Motivation This issue only affects ROCm. On other platforms, `dflash_draft_kv_follows_target_swa` returns `False` at the `_is_hip` check, so the draft pool already uses the full-attention slots that PD transfers address. On ROCm, `SGLANG_ROCM_ENABLE_DFLASH_SWA_DRAFT_KV` (on by default) sizes a compact DFLASH draft pool per sliding-window token and indexes it with the target's SWA ids. Accepted tokens ... title: [Fix] encoder: Abort waiting requests before draining embeddings in the same tick
summary: ## Motivation In `Scheduler.ingest_requests()`, `self.request_receiver.recv_requests()` runs `self.mm_receiver.process_waiting_requests(recv_reqs)` before `self.process_input_requests(recv_reqs)` dispatches `AbortReq` to `Scheduler.abort_request()`. Inside `MMReceiverBase._process_waiting_requests()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encoder/receiver.py`): 1. The initial loop over `recv_reqs` appends `AbortReq` directly to `new_recv_reqs` without calling `self.abort_waiting_requests(recv_req)` (and places any newly arrived multimodal `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` into `self.waiting_list`). 2. Right after that loop, `_drain_scheduler_embeddings()` and `waiting_req._try_recv_mm_data()` run. If the target waiting request finishes receiving its embeddings in the same scheduler tick, it transitions to `WaitingMMRequestStatus.SUCCESS`, leaves `self.waiting_list`, and is appended to `new_recv_reqs` **behind** the `AbortReq`. 3. When `Scheduler.process_input_requests(new_recv_reqs)` then runs, it processes `AbortReq` first -- at which point the request is already gone from `mm_receiver.waiting_list` and not yet in `waiting_queue` or `running_batch` -- so the abort is dropped. The request right behind it is then added to `waiting_queue` as a new request. Impact: the abort is silently ignored. The request runs a full prefill and decode on the language-only server and finishes normally instead of with `FINISH_ABORT`: a disconnected client's request keeps using GPU time and KV until it completes, and an explicit or timeout abort does not take effect. It triggers when the `AbortReq` land

title: [RFC] Asymmetric P/D deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash
summary: ## Summary This RFC proposes an asymmetric Prefill/Decode deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash. For a prompt of length `N` and replay window `W = 128`: - The **Prefill worker** processes only the prefix `[0, N-W)` and produces its KV cache. - The **Decode worker** receives that prefix KV and processes the final prompt window `[N-W, N)` as a bounded prefill/replay. - Decode then samples the first output token and continues normal speculative decoding with per-request `q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens`. The key property is that Decode does not need separate encoder and decoder workloads. Every layer sees the same token count in a given step: ```text first Decode step: L0-L39 process W prompt tokens later Decode steps: L0-L39 process 1 + num_spec_tokens tokens per request ``` ```text P: prompt tokens [0, N-W) -> prefix KV | v D: prompt tokens [N-W, N) -> first output token D: generated tokens -> normal decode / speculative verify ``` The Prefill worker only needs the causal encoder and the decoder's first KV-producing projection path. The Decode worker keeps the full model. The main goal is to remove almost half of the model weights from each Prefill replica. A secondary goal is to avoid running a separate, low-density late-decoder workload on Prefill. Decode remains architecturally simple: its first step is a bounded prefill through the full model, followed by normal decode steps through the same full model. ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash has 40 transformer layers, a sliding-window size of 128, and shared compressed-KV source layers at 2, 8, 14, and 20. With the current decoder b

title: [AMD][Kimi-K3] Route radix4 on bf16 with the cached bias, drop the pe…
summary: # [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3: Route radix4 on bf16 with the cached bias, drop the per-call cast Branch: `kimi_k3_rocm_radix4_avoid_extra_dtype_conversion` (one commit on `main`). ## Motivation `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK=1` (off by default) opts Kimi-K3 on ROCm into the radix4 router. This pull request makes bf16 the routing precision under that flag: radix4 routes on the bf16 router logits against a cached bf16 copy of the correction bias. That removes an elementwise kernel that ran before the router in every MoE layer, casting the `[num_tokens, 896]` logits to fp32, so the radix4 path launches only the router kernel. Kimi-K3 holds `e_score_correction_bias` in fp32, and `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` currently matches the logits to it before either router runs: ```python if correction_bias.dtype == torch.float32: route_logits = gating_output.to(torch.float32) route_bias = correction_bias ``` The radix4 kernel accepts bf16 scores with a bf16 bias and widens both to fp32 in-register, so on its path the cast costs a launch per layer per forward. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: - `select_experts`: when the bias is fp32, aiter is in use, and `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK` is set, it fetches `TopKConfig.correction_bias_for_dtype(router_logits.dtype)` and passes it down as `radix4_bias`. That copy is built once, lazily, and keyed on the bias's `data_ptr` and `_version`, so a weight reload rebuilds it and nothing is cast per call. Only the layer's own bias is cached; a substituted bias (for example a dynamic expert bias) still takes the uncached path. - `biased_grouped_topk_gpu`

title: [Feat] hicache: Add a direct_kernel IO backend on page_row for MLA/DSA pools
summary: > Written with Claude Code. ## Motivation HiCache's `direct` IO backend moves `page_first_direct` pages with the copy engine. Before each transfer it syncs the token-slot indices to the CPU and builds one copy descriptor per (page, layer). For an MLA model with a DSA indexer (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V3.2) that host-side work dominates each transfer: about 0.5 us of CPU issue per page and layer, paid on every load-back and write-back. The scheduler does this work before it launches the forward, so the GPU waits through it. In a profiled GLM-5.2 agentic-coding replay with PP4 prefill on GB300, one request (119 new tokens on a 372,855-token cached prefix) loaded 4.5 GB from and wrote 4.5 GB back to the host pool on each PP stage. With `direct`, each stage spent 199-229 ms before its forward kernels started, while the GPU was otherwise idle. About 140 ms of that went to issuing the copies (`cudaMemcpyBatchAsync`), during which the copy engines were busy for only about 50 ms. The four stages handle the request one after another, so it spent about 0.85 s in cache handling against 80-130 ms of forward per stage. When prefill is the bottleneck, this host time caps prefill throughput. In the serving A/B below, a busy prefill worker computed 12% more tokens per second with `direct_kernel`, and about 30% more on batches with cached prefixes above 128k tokens. Median TTFT dropped 15-21%. ## Modifications The PR has four commits. title: [Fix] scheduler: Count the unprefilled part of a chunked request in total_tokens load
summary: ## Motivation With `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the smallest `num_total_tokens`. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens", but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill. That request holds KV only for the chunks it has already run, and it is in neither the running batch nor the waiting queue. So a rank that has just started a 64K-token prompt reports only about one chunk of load, and new requests keep going to it. We saw this on 2×H20 with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP=2, `--attn-dp-size 2`, FA3, FP8 KV, and `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` (4096 per rank). The traffic was 30 short requests (1024 in / 96 out) plus one 32K and one 64K prompt. When the 32K prompt arrived first, both long prompts went to different ranks as expected. The rank prefilling the 64K prompt then also received 24 of the 30 short requests, which gave a 38,912 / 90,112 input-token split. When the 64K prompt arrived first, the bug was not triggered and the split was 68,608 / 60,416. `SchedulerLoadInquirer._get_num_pending_tokens()` already adds the chunked request's `seqlen - prefix_len`; `num_total_tokens` did not. ## Modifications - `load_inquirer.py`: add the chunked request's remaining tokens (`seqlen - prefix_len`) to `num_total_tokens`, and so also to `num_active_tokens`. The prefix it has already run is counted in `num_used_tokens`, as before. - `test_load_inquirer.py`: two unit tests for `get_loads()`, with and without a chunked request. The new chunked case fails on main (`300 != 340`) and passes with this

title: [FlashInfer] Persist autotune results in the autotune_v2 managed store
summary: ## Motivation FlashInfer autotune persistence never pays off for ops that profile under a non-default measurement policy. The trtllm-gen FP4 MoE (`flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) profiles with cold L2, and the v1 JSON files written by `save_configs` record no per-entry policy. So while tuning, `AutoTuner.search_cache` skips every file entry for that op, and every boot re-profiles it from scratch, even when the file holds the exact keys. On a B300 Kimi-K3 deployment that is about 4 minutes of startup per pod, with a fully seeded, matching cache on disk. FlashInfer's `autotune_v2` managed store is the fix path. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5495 records each entry's profiling policy in that store, so a cold-L2 winner is reused on the next boot. The v1 file path stays gated by design. This PR moves sglang onto `autotune_v2` so it picks that up. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py` - **One store per rank, attached once per process** (`attach_flashinfer_autotune_store`). - `autotune_v2` attaches its store for the whole process, and the last attach wins. Serving then reads tuned winners from that store's partition. - So the target, extend, draft and PCIe-IPC tuning passes all have to tune into a single store that is attached before the first of them runs. - Root: `$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/flashinfer/autotune/managed/<key>/rank_tp{}_pp{}_dp{}`. FlashInfer adds its own environment namespace below it (library versions, GPU). - **Cross-rank agreement gate rebuilt over the store** (`_agree_on_autotune_store`). Same contract as before: a store

summary: ## Motivation Small invariant follow-up to #47476 and #49195: When an explicit `--paged-experts-num-resident` is passed, `disk_tier.host_rows()` enforces both `num_slots <= rows` and `num_slots <= _MAX_TIER_SLOTS` (`1024`, the single-block thread bound in `paged_experts_tiered_plan`). summary: On ROCm, GDN packed decode can call AITER's `flydsl_gdr_decode` instead of the Triton packed kernel. ReplaySSM decode stays on Triton. - Q, K, and V are strided views of the post-conv `mixed_qkv` row. Nothing is copied into separate Q/K/V tensors. - A launch the kernel does not cover logs once and falls back to Triton. The adapter also stays on Triton when `flydsl_gdr_decode` is missing or does not zero padding rows. summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, `AiterAttnBackend.forward_extend` routes **every plain extend (prefill)** through the Triton `unified_attention` kernel: ```python if self.use_triton_unified_attention: # unified_attention has no head_dim cap; route extend through it # so Gemma-4's 512-wide full-attention layers don't hit the CK # `head dimension at most 256` assert. return self._forward_extend_unified(...) ``` The comment says the route exists for Gemma-4's 512-wide heads, but the condition does not check the head dim. title: [Fix] spec: Greedy requests keep the argmax prefill draft under rejection sampling
summary: ## Motivation With rejection sampling on (`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, enabled by default for EAGLE topk 1 on ROCm, where there is no tree-sampling verify kernel), `EagleDraftWorker._draft_extend_for_prefill` draws the first draft token of every request with `fast_sample` from `softmax(logits / T)`. `SamplingParams` turns temperature 0 into temperature 1.0 with top_k 1, so a greedy request's first draft token is sampled at T = 1 instead of taken as the argmax. Every later draft step (`draft_forward`, `_draft_extend_for_decode`) goes through `sample_draft_proposal`, which proposes the argmax for top_k == 1 rows. summary: ## [Feat] Use Weight Cache only for the target model during speculative decoding ### Motivation and changes The Weight Cache Daemon publishes target weights, but its configuration applies to the whole service. summary: ## Motivation On the Python TreeCore, `FullComponent._evict_device_start` builds a heap over every evictable device leaf on every eviction call and throws it away afterwards; `drive_host_eviction` does the same for host leaves. That is O(#leaves) per call however few tokens are evicted (#48623 reports it on GB300). Since #39627 the default core is Rust, so this helps the configs that run the Python core: session radix cache, joint_lru, KV-cache sharding, several window slots, NPU / XPU / MLX, and installs without the Rust extension. joint_lru's `start_joint_eviction` rebuild is out of scope. ## Modifications `_LazyLeafHeap` in `unified_tree_core.py`, one persistent heap per leaf set, created in `reset()`. - An entry's key is a lower bound of the node's current key and is re-read at pop: a key that grew is pushed back, a node that left the set is dropped. - Only writes that can lower a key call the heap. They are listed in the `_touch_full_eviction_key` docstring: access stamps under `mru`, the suffix in `_split_node`, the joint_lru restore, Full `session_ref` decrements. - Leaving the leaf set does nothing and re-entering is a dict lookup, so lock / unlock and LRU touches never push. - No O(#leaves) pass. Past `2 * tracked + 64` entries the heap is retired and each later push moves 8 entries over; a walk pops from both. - Walks keep main's order: the device walk only sees mid-walk entrants through the explicit parent push (#46930), the host walk takes new host leaves at once (#47126). - A nested host eviction can decrement `session_ref` in the middle of a device walk. title: [Feat] DeepSeek-V4.1: Add encoder-language disaggregation
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash carries a ViT tower that is tiny next to the 286 GB of language weights, but on memory-constrained accelerators that is not the right comparison. The tower is replicated on every TP rank, so colocating it costs ~0.82 GB of weights per GPU plus its preprocessing and forward workspace — measured ~1.6 GB per GPU on this deployment. Moving the tower to a dedicated encoder server returns that HBM to the KV pool, lets the ViT be scaled separately from the language model, and keeps vision compute off the MoE prefill path. SGLang already supports this split (Encoder–Prefill–Decode disaggregation), but `--encoder-only` and `--language-only` rejected `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` in the model whitelist, so V4.1 could not be deployed that way. ## Modifications - `srt/arg_groups/pd_disaggregation_hook.py`: accept `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` in the encoder-disaggregation whitelist and mention DeepSeek-V4 in the rejection message. - `srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`: - `encoder_only` builds only the ViT/aligner and loads only vision weights, skipping the language model, lm_head and per-layer expert bookkeeping. - `language_only` skips the tower in `__init__`. - `supports_visual_inputs` decouples "has a local vision tower" from "consumes image inputs". In language-only mode precomputed embeddings must still be injected and `MM_PAD_SHIFT` sentinels must still be mapped back to `image_token_id`, otherwise Engram masking and visual MoE routing see the image as plain text. - `preprocess_mm_for_encoder` patchifies raw images into per-item ViT inputs (CPU or GPU preprocessing)

title: [Bug] quantization: drop dead 'marlin' --quantization CLI choice
summary: ## Summary Fixes #32250. `--quantization marlin` was accepted by the CLI (it was in `QUANTIZATION_CHOICES`) but has no entry in `QUANTIZATION_METHODS`: the bare W4A16 `marlin` method was superseded by `gptq_marlin` / `awq_marlin`, so `get_quantization_config("marlin")` raises `Invalid quantization method: marlin` at model load. summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation On AMD with the default `aiter` attention backend, EAGLE/MTP `target_verify` for non-MLA models runs on the legacy Triton `extend_attention_fwd`. That kernel has no split-KV: each request's long paged KV is walked by one program, so at agentic context lengths it runs far below HBM bandwidth. The faster `unified_attention` verify path from #23146 already exists, but it is only taken when `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`. That variable also moves prefill and decode to Triton `unified_attention`. With one-token KV pages (the default) that makes 16k-token prefill chunks over long contexts tens of times slower on MI300X. With `--page-size 16` the variable is usable, and the InferenceX MI325X Qwen3.5 recipe sets it, but prefill and decode then leave the aiter kernels, which costs TTFT and throughput (397B table below). This PR is the target-verify half of decoupling the EAGLE paths from that variable. #40872 (approved) is the draft_extend half; the two are independent and merge cleanly together. The #40872 thread already points at this gap: with #40872 alone, NEXTN decode on Qwen3.5 drops below no-spec decode at ~11k context, and the cause is target verify still on `extend_attention_fwd` (554 us per call at 11k vs 14 us on `unified_attention`). summary: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. title: [Feat] [Intel] pp: Support long-context pipeline parallelism on Intel XPU
summary: ## Motivation Pipeline parallelism has run on Intel XPU since #23645, but the long-context path in the [PP guide](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/advanced_features/pipeline_parallelism) had never been validated there. On eight Arc Pro B60 cards it showed three bugs, and there was no XPU PP test: 1. **Dynamic chunking breaks the server it profiles.** At startup PP0 runs 128 prefill probes, the largest at 1.25x `--chunked-prefill-size`. The allocator keeps that peak cached, so oneCCL and Level Zero, which allocate outside PyTorch, run short of memory: - Large probe that succeeds (16K initial chunk, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`): the first PP transfer hangs in `isend` (PP4), or fails with `xccl: onecclCommInitRank failed with code 11` (PP2). The server never becomes healthy. - Probe that runs out of memory (12K initial chunk, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`): the server logs `Dynamic chunking will be disabled`, then the first forward dies with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. The documented fallback never happens. title: [Feat] disaggregation: Support prefill_complete with a pipeline-parallel prefill and send its Success from the transfer worker
summary: ## Motivation TL;DR This PR enables prefill_complete in #40703 for PP prefill as well. For a high throughput GLM5.2 server, prefill_complete on PP scheduler reduces ~70% of reserved requests on decode. Furthermore, we change how we send the kv-transfer completion signal under prefill_complete, improving TTFT by 1 to 2 iterations of prefill model forwards. This improves prefill_complete for overlap scheduler slightly, and is quite crucial for prefill_complete for PP scheduler to be useful. `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` (#40703) makes PD (prefill/decode) disaggregated decode reserve a request's KV (key-value cache) slots only after prefill finishes, instead of at bootstrap. It helps most when prefills are long, and long-context prefill is often served with PP (pipeline parallelism). This PR lets the policy run with a PP prefill, and removes the TTFT (time to first token) cost that releasing a request through the PP stages would otherwise add. **PP prefill.** Today the policy cannot start on a PP prefill: 1. `_validate_prefill_complete` rejects `pp_size != 1` on both roles. 2. `handle_other_validations` resolves `--optimistic-prefill-attempts` to 0 whenever `pp_size > 1`, and `prefill_complete` requires optimistic prefill. 3. The decode receiver fails any room whose prefill peer has `pp_size != 1`. Removing these checks is not enough. Each PP stage runs its own scheduler, and the stages must make identical scheduling decisions. title: [Fix] [AMD] GLM-5.3-Flash: Keep the MoE correction bias fp32
summary: ## Summary On MI355X with aiter, GLM-5.3-Flash picks MoE experts with a rounded bias. The checkpoint stores each layer's 288 expert correction biases in fp32, within a band about 0.4 wide. With FP8/Quark weights, `MoEGate` stores them in bf16, which steps 0.03–0.06 there; CUDA keeps fp32. 59% of real tokens then change their top-8. This PR keeps the stored bias fp32 for GLM-5.3-Flash. Since #44797, aiter routes an fp32 bias with fp32 logits, so the routing code needs no change. How the cast swaps an expert, illustrative values: | | Expert A | Expert B | Chosen expert (higher val) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | fp32 bias | 7.410 | 7.420 | | | Sigmoid score | 0.300 | 0.295 | | | Score + fp32 bias | 7.710 | **7.715** | B | | bf16 bias | 7.40625 | 7.40625 | | | Score + bf16 bias | **7.70625** | 7.70125 | A | ## Scope MI355X (gfx95) with aiter and FP8 / compressed_tensors / Quark weights, the only case where `MoEGate` downcasts the bias. The change keys on `model_type == "glm5_next_text"`, so only GLM-5.3-Flash moves. GLM-5.2 already keeps fp32 through `is_glm_moe_dsa`; other models keep the bf16 bias. `topk.py` is not touched. CUDA is untouched. title: [Perf] dllm: Run several denoise forwards per scheduled FDFO round
summary: ## Motivation Under FDFO, one scheduler round is one denoise forward. Everything the round does around that forward — committing resolved blocks, admitting waiting requests, processing results, rebuilding the batch — is paid once per forward. dLLM also disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so that host work is exposed directly as device idle rather than hidden behind the next forward. At large batch this is a real share of the step: the forward itself is the only part that scales with the model, while the round overhead is roughly fixed. ## Modifications `SGLANG_DLLM_FDFO_STEPS_PER_ROUND` (new, default `1` = today's behavior) makes a round issue N denoise forwards instead of one. The batch is frozen for the inner steps: rows that resolve mid-round freeze themselves inside the step, and commits, admissions and result processing all happen once at the end of the round. The per-round host work is therefore amortized over N forwards. Two hooks are added to `DllmAlgorithm` so an algorithm can keep its per-request state in batched device tensors for the whole round (`fdfo_batched_begin` / `fdfo_batched_step` / `fdfo_batched_all_finished`), which is what makes an inner step cost no host gather/scatter. `JointThreshold` implements them; an algorithm that returns `None` from `fdfo_batched_begin` gets a plain loop with the same semantics, which is the path non-NPU dLLM runs today. The round still exits early once every row has resolved, so a short round does not issue no-op forwards. That probe costs one scalar s

title: [Feat] [AMD] moe: Fuse GLM-5.2 routing with the AITER MoE sort
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, every GLM-5.2 MoE layer runs four small kernels between the router GEMM and the first expert GEMM: upcast the bf16 logits to fp32, aiter `biased_grouped_topk`, append the fused shared expert, and aiter `moe_sorting` (which also zeroes the `fused_moe` output). At decode and MTP-verify sizes these take about 21 µs per layer, and they run in all 78 target layers plus every draft step. This PR does all of that in one JIT kernel, `glm_route_sort`. It routes, appends the shared expert, writes the exact sort `fused_moe` would compute under the EP expert mask, and zeroes the output buffer. The sort is handed to aiter's `fused_moe` as a presort, so it skips `moe_sorting`. Per call, this drops from 21.1 µs to 7.7 µs. **Result** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4/EP4, MI355X, AgentX; baseline = same stack with the env off): | Conc | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | P90 TTFT (s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 158.7 → **173.4** (+9.3%) | 6,845 → 6,794 (−0.7%) | 0.794 → 0.805 | 5.28 → **4.88** (−7.5%) | | 8 | 113.9 → **117.6** (+3.2%) | 11,734 → 11,857 (+1.0%) | 0.744 → 0.750 | 6.84 → **6.24** (−8.8%) | Decode gets 7–9% faster at both concurrencies. Throughput and TTFT move within run-to-run noise (about 3%), as expected for a decode-only change at low concurrency. title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM-5.3-Flash: Small-M MoE kernel and sort-fused MXFP4 quant for decode
summary: ## Summary At small decode batches, the routed experts of a GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 MoE layer take **five** kernels. A sort groups tokens by expert, and each of the two expert GEMMs needs an FP4 quant first. The sort and the two quants cost half as much as the GEMMs. Both changes are on by default: 1. SGLang already has a gfx950 small-batch MoE kernel. It reads BF16 activations directly, so it needs no sort and no quant. GLM-5.3-Flash now uses it. 2. For somewhat larger batches, the sort also writes the first FP4 quant, bit-exact with aiter. title: [Fix] constrained: bound the compiled-grammar cache by host memory (LRU) to stop RSS growth with per-request schemas
summary: ## Motivation `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` is a plain `dict` that is never evicted. Each compiled grammar (xgrammar / outlines / llguidance) holds per-vocabulary token tables; with a 150k-token vocabulary we measured **+250–380 MB of scheduler RSS per previously-unseen `json_schema`**. Agent frameworks commonly embed per-call values (enums, defaults, descriptions) inside the schema, so every request is a cache miss and the scheduler grows until the host runs out of RAM. Fixes #45077. ## Changes - `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` becomes an LRU `OrderedDict` bounded by a fixed host-memory budget, `BaseGrammarBackend.DEFAULT_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES` (1 GiB). title: [Fix] json-schema: Add depth and state bounds validation
summary: This fix addresses the security vulnerability where deeply nested or complex JSON schemas could cause CPU thread hanging and DoS via unbounded DFA/NFA state compilation. Changes: 1. Added validate_schema_depth() and validate_schema_bounds() functions in json_schema_validation.py 2. Added JSONSchemaDepthExceeded and JSONSchemaStateExplosion exception classes 3. Integrated validation into all three grammar backends (xgrammar, outlines, llguidance) 4. Added comprehensive unit tests for the new validation The validation enforces: - Maximum schema nesting depth of 16 - Maximum estimated DFA states of 10,000 This prevents adversarial schemas from causing DoS by state space explosion. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. title: [Perf] scheduler: Skip SWA admission only during global capacity exhaustion
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid SWA admission needs to retry as running decode releases capacity. Retrying when the full KV pool is globally exhausted repeats queue matching and external-cache lookups that cannot admit any candidate. ## Modifications Cache an admission refusal only for non-CP budgets with no remaining current full-pool capacity. Poll storage-prefetch completions before this gate. Resume admission as soon as capacity becomes positive. Candidate-specific refusals (including window pressure and future-token reservations), CP padding, and joint-pool budgets retry every round. Priority preemption, an empty running batch, and chunk continuation retain their progress paths. This deliberately narrows the optimization: a shorter request, a better prefix hit, or reduced decode reservations may permit admission without physical capacity growth, so those cases must not reuse a capacity-only refusal. ## Validation - CPU checks executing the actual scheduler gate and budget methods passed: reservation improvement, candidate replacement/prefix changes, global exhaustion/release, completion polling, CP/joint-pool fallback, preemption, chunk continuation, and empty batches. - Updated the existing prefill-adder regression to distinguish candidate-specific refusals from global exhaustion. - Full registered tests and GPU/model validation were not run locally because the required runtime dependencies are unavailable. - No new performance measurements are claimed. Earlier measurements of the broader gate do not establish performance of this narrowed implementation. <!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [Perf] hicache: optional minimum tokens per write_back allocation-driven eviction
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache `write_back`, an allocation-driven device eviction waits once for the forward running on the device (the write fence) before its victims' copies to the host pool complete. The allocator asks only for its shortfall, so a busy prefill server evicts many small batches and pays that wait each time. On post-#46930 `main`, @xiezhq-hermann measured the remaining single wait per walk as most of the eviction time (28% of scheduler wall time at 80 req/s, 46% at saturation, 87-91% of it that wait; see the review below). ## Modifications - `environ.py`: `SGLANG_HICACHE_WRITE_BACK_MIN_EVICT_TOKENS` (`EnvInt`, default 0 = off): the minimum Full KV tokens one write_back allocation-driven eviction frees. - `unified_radix_cache.py` `evict_pool_shortfalls` (where prefill and decode capacity, HiCache load-back and PD decode preallocation evictions converge since #48012): under write_back, when `0 < token shortfall < value`, the token shortfall is raised to the value and the token entry of the `demand` handed to `_evict` by the same amount. Raising the demand matters: the walk stops at the first victim after which its pool can serve the demand, so raising only the token count would free nothing extra. `_write_back_batch_tokens` then takes the whole floor as one batch behind one wait. The cheap shortfall check runs before reading `is_write_back`, so a disabled floor never reaches it. - Scope: Full KV only.
