title: [Performance] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 mHC boundaries and overlap coefficient computation on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On vLLM-Ascend main, the boundary between two DeepSeek V4.1 sublayers runs `HcPost`, `HcPreV3`, and RMSNorm in sequence. `HcPreV3` both collapses the four residual streams using the incoming `pre_mix` and computes three new coefficients (`pre`, `post`, and `comb`). Coefficient computation takes up a substantial part of HcPreV3’s runtime and Attention and MoE can start before these three sets of coefficients are ready, since they’re only used in later steps. This PR makes the following changes to speed up this process: - **Split `HcPreV3` work.** Add `HcPreCoefficients`, a coefficient-only Ascend C operator that reuses the native projection, row partitioning, and coefficient computation. The full `HcPreV3` path remains available for fallback and for boundaries that cannot be fused. - **Fuse input preparation.** One Triton kernel combines `HcPost`, the four-way residual collapse, and RMSNorm. - **Overlap coefficient computation.** In a full decode graph, the auxiliary stream starts coefficient computation once the updated residual is ready. The main stream can start attention or MoE as soon as its input is ready and waits at the next coefficient consumer. Outside full graph execution, eligible fused boundaries compute coefficients on the main stream. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 currently publishes indexer K through separate RMSNorm, partial RoPE, dynamic INT8 quantization, and K/scale cache scatter operations. Its ratio-2 compressor also normalizes pooled output in a separate operation. These intermediate operations add kernel launches and global-memory traffic to the compressed-source path. This PR introduces two Triton epilogue fusions: - **Indexer K publication:** fuse RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, per-token INT8 quantization, and direct writes to the paged K and FP16 scale caches. The `wk` projection remains a separate GEMM. - **C2 pooling:** optionally apply RMSNorm inside the token-aligned pooling kernel, preserving the BF16 pooling-output boundary before normalization. FP32 ring-state updates retain their existing ordering. The indexer kernel preserves the BF16 boundary between RMSNorm and RoPE, quantizes using an FP32 scale, and stores the dequantization scale in FP16. It respects physical cache strides and skips invalid physical slots. Valid output slots must remain unique. The fused indexer path targets ordinary A2/A3 INT8 caches. A5 packed/folded cache publication and indexer Norm with a loaded bias retain the existing path. The C2 compressor also retains separate normalization when its Norm has a loaded bias, so that the bias is applied. The intended benefit is fewer launches and intermediate memory accesses. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fine-grained TP shards vocabulary weights along the **data-parallel axis**. The previous `AscendMLAImpl.update_graph_params()` path rebuilt captured FIA calls from parallel parameter, handle, and event lists, so updates depended on the order of attention layers. - Registers each `npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2.out` call as a graph task during capture. The task retains its operation arguments and output tensors, removing the MLA-specific graph parameter bookkeeping. - Adds `MLAParamProvider` to resolve runtime parameters from the current layer's decode metadata. It pads target KV lengths, builds EAGLE target query lengths, and supplies draft query lengths, KV lengths, and block tables, including trimming the draft block table when padded batches are disabled. - Uses `get_capture_resource()` to allocate and reuse the FIA workspace across captures. The speculative decoders are updated to pass MLA FIA sequence-length and block-table parameters in the new form. Related design: #13058; earlier `UpdatableGraph` work: #16798. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. This changes the internal MLA graph capture and replay path without changing public APIs, configuration, or defaults. ### How was this patch tested? - Pre-commit, CPU unit tests against vLLM main and v0.33.0, and DCO/title checks passed. - `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_v1.py` covers target KV padding, EAGLE query lengths, and draft block-table trimming. `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_fp8_decode_layout.py` checks registered FIA task

title: [Feature] Fuse GatingTopK with EPLB expert mapping
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With ModelRunnerV2 EPLB, expert selection writes logical expert IDs before a separate Map kernel reads them and produces physical IDs. This change adds an optional `expert_replica_routing_table` input to `moe_gating_top_k_hash`, allowing supported routes to map the final IDs before they leave on-chip memory. The router automatically selects fusion on supported A3/A5 hardware for ungrouped `sqrtsoftplus` routing. It reuses the existing periodic EPLB table, including the AllGather table when applicable, and skips the subsequent standalone Map. Weights are computed using logical IDs before the output IDs are mapped. The router inherits upstream `_select_experts` unchanged. An internal `_use_gating_top_k_with_map` switch is resolved once at the first routing call, after EPLB/capture setup and using the actual hidden size. The existing Ascend mapping hook only reads this fixed choice; it does not reset or consume per-call state. `_can_fuse_gating_map` checks eligibility once, while `_get_gating_map_table` reads the current ordinary/AllGather table on every nonempty fused call. Missing tables raise instead of returning unmapped IDs. The original parent-fallback condition is preserved; eligibility is resolved for the fixed model routing configuration. The router retains the existing nonempty-input expectation: the reviewed ModelRunnerV2 target paths skip zero batches or provide dummy/padded tokens before routing. This PR does not add standalone zero-row TopK support. Model routing configuration, including logical-ID capture, must be finalize

title: [Performance][A3][A5] Speed up packed DCP attention output combine
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The shared DCP attention path merges partial outputs from separate K/V shards, including an optional local result in split MLA attention. For BF16 head scatter, this PR decodes each packed LSE once per output row and reuses the rank weights across all features. Runtime and warmup launch one Triton kernel. The device profile supplies a compile-time row mode. A3 processes one row at a time because multirow loads can lower to nested scalar loops. A5 processes eight rows per tile to improve memory throughput. Each program owns a contiguous interval. The same selection applies at every row count. The optimized path accepts `D <= 512`, output-only combine and unit local feature stride when a local output is present. Other supported layouts and dtypes use the existing scalar path. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Packed DCP attention output combine is faster on the target A3 and A5 shapes. Callers use the existing API. The result includes the optional local contribution once, masks outputs with nonfinite LSE and returns zeros for all-invalid rows. ### How was this patch tested? **Device-kernel performance.** The public wrapper ran on the same device with the same inputs for each comparison. The table gives mean kernel duration from two interleaved `msprof op` captures per side against fixed main `6385299e`. title: [Feature][KV Transfer] Support KV-sharing layers in MooncakeConnectorV2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A layer that reads another layer's KV cache declares `kv_sharing_target_layer_name`. It owns no blocks, so it has no `kv_cache_tensors` entry, but the model runner still registers it with the connector, bound to its owner's cache. MooncakeConnectorV2 rejected such a layer at registration: ``` ValueError: KV caches contain layers absent from kv_cache_tensors: [...] ``` So prefill and decode instances of models with cross-layer KV sharing (for example Mistral Large 4) could not start with MooncakeConnectorV2. `register_kv_caches` now validates these extra layers before registering any memory. The implementation follows #22468. - An extra layer is accepted only if it declares a target in the static forward context, the target is a configured layer, and the layer is bound to the same cache as its target (same device, address, dtype, shape and stride for every tensor). - Undeclared extra layers are still rejected with the original error. Bindings to a different cache, missing owners and chained targets are rejected. - Accepted layers publish nothing of their own. Transfer metadata and registered memory are identical to the owner-only case: the owner's blocks are transferred once, and the sharing layer reads them through its binding. - KV sharing combined with KV parallelism (KVPP) is rejected with an explicit error before KVPP rank mapping. Supporting that combination is left for a follow-up. The handshake format, scheduler, pull/push address calculation and transfer-engine calls are unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing

title: [BugFix][v0.32.0rc] Backport V4.1 DSpark layer capture fix (#22122)
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Backport #22122 (`f29d21cdd82007d04b6fbf86778a538ec31e1a4a`) to `releases/v0.32.0rc`. DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark's MRV2 resolver preserves the checkpoint's zero-based target layer IDs, but the target model compared them against `layer_idx + 1`. For example, `[37, 38, 39]` captured inputs to layers `[36, 37, 38]`, and selecting layer `0` captured nothing. Use the zero-based comparison in regular forward and decoder replay. This release calls `AscendDecoderReplayLayers` directly, so the backport keeps that implementation and does not introduce main's newer replay custom op or its auxiliary-output count. The release's V1 DSpark fallback also added `1` to V4.1 checkpoint IDs. Align that fallback with the corrected target using the existing V4.1 identification helper before unwrapping the configuration. This covers the released composite schema (`model_type="deepseek_v41"`, `text_config.model_type="deepseek_v41_text"`) and flattened configurations. Without this release-specific adaptation, V1 would request `[38, 39, 40]` from a 40-layer model and capture only two of the three required auxiliary states. V4 and GQA DSpark retain their existing `+1` semantics. The regression tests exercise the actual target forward, replay wrapper, V1/V2 resolvers and public text/multimodal setters. They cover empty selections, layer `0`, `[37, 38, 39]`, IDs at the replay boundary, compacted and full batches, regular SP capture, nested/flattened V1 V4.1 configurations, and unchanged V4/GQA resolution. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Fixed

title: [BugFix] Honor per-layer SwiGLU limits in Ascend MoE
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Ling routed experts need to apply each layer's configured SwiGLU gate limit after SiLU. This PR adapts the upstream fix to Ascend. title: [BugFix] Allow DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark MXFP8 main_proj and DSA wo_a layouts
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This change keeps the quantized `main_proj` contract and adds a ModelSlim MXFP8 linear method for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1: - Read `quant_method` from the draft checkpoint `quantization_config`. When the checkpoint does not set it, use `vllm_config.quant_config.get_name()`. - Pass `vllm_config.quant_config` into `main_proj` when packed-cache ops are available and the method is `fp8` or `ascend`. - Register the module as `mtp.0.main_proj` so per-layer quant descriptions match the checkpoint name. - Register `AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicAscendV1LinearMethod` as `("W8A8_MXFP8", "ds_linear")`. With `--quantization ascend`, every quantized linear on DeepSeek V4 or V4.1 uses `ds_linear`; the registered ModelSlim scheme is `W8A8_MXFP8`. Other models stay on `linear`. Other layers use the shared 2D MXFP8 post-processing. - Set `weight_switch_output_gather_specs` to gather dim 0, matching `ds_linear`, so PCP full-weight prefill reconstructs the `wo_a` groups. title: [Ops][Feature] Fused Triton Qwen vision QKV, RoPE, and FIA padding
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR fuses QKV layout extraction, Q/K RoPE and head-dimension padding into one Triton producer for the Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3.5-VL vision-attention FIA path. It removes the separate PyTorch preprocessing and padding operations before `npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. It also avoids full-pool copies when FIA reads eligible block-interleaved Qwen3.5 hybrid KV caches, using zero-copy read aliases while preserving the existing cache writers and shared KV/Mamba page ownership. - Restricts the specialized path to contiguous BF16 tensors with eight Q/K/V heads and head dimension 72; - Accepts packed multi-sequence `cu_seqlens` for multi-image, multi-frame video and window-attention inputs; - Primes and caches host FIA sequence boundaries once per vision forward group, avoiding repeated device-to-host conversion across attention layers; - Records fused-path hit rate and fallback reasons with periodic statistics logging; - Launches only the vector cores needed for the token tiles in the fused producer; - Provides launch A/B knobs for vector-core mode, token tile size, Q/K store mode and output allocation mode; - Allocates Q/K/V outputs from one contiguous buffer and exposes non-overlapping views to reduce allocator calls; - Keeps all model integration in `vllm_ascend/patch/worker` instead of changing `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py` in the vLLM repository; - Preserves the existing generic Qwen vision-attention path as the fallback; - Feeds the fused padded Q/K/V tensors directly to FIA. title: [Performance][GDN] Overlap Qwen input projections on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen GDN runs two independent input projections, in_proj_qkvz and in_proj_ba, on the same stream. This PR adapts [vLLM #64425](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64425) to Ascend. During eligible ACLGraph captures, it runs BA on an auxiliary NPU stream while QKVZ runs on the main stream. The auxiliary stream waits for the input to be ready, and the main stream waits for BA before downstream GDN operations consume the results. Both projections use the existing weights, operators, and output layouts. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Set gdn_projection_overlap_max_tokens in --additional-config to opt in. It defaults to 0, which preserves serial execution. A positive value caps the number of input rows after graph padding. The optimization applies to eligible unquantized BF16 projections in FULL or FULL_DECODE_ONLY ACLGraph mode with compilation disabled. ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-9B \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --additional-config '{"gdn_projection_overlap_max_tokens":64}' ``` 64 is a trial threshold. The release note is in release_notes/fragments/21037.yaml. ### How was this patch tested? Local checks: Seven host unit tests passed, covering stream dependencies, tensor lifetimes, threshold boundaries, and serial fallback. title: [Feature][PCP] Align short-prefill dispatch across attention backends
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? When a request has an existing computed prefix and only one new prompt token to process, it can still be in the prefill lifecycle. Under PCP, partitioning that request as prefill while attention runs it as decode can make request ownership, graph dispatch, and attention metadata disagree. This PR classifies eligible one-token prompt tails as decode work before PCP graph dispatch. The classification excludes speculative draft tokens and applies when `PCP > 1`, `DCP == 1`, and decode-request sharding is enabled. - Preserves the original lifecycle flags for prompt preparation and sampling. Dispatch, partitioning, and attention metadata apply the same explicit host masks through `apply_prefill_as_decode_mask`. - Returns the original batch when no request qualifies. For batches with an override, the runner publishes the dispatch mask after FlashMLA finalizes request order, so dispatch sizing and graph eligibility use the same request layout as partitioning. - Makes FlashMLA consume the effective phase directly from attention metadata. MLA honors that phase under PCP, so a genuine prefill fragment stays on the prefill path even when its rank-local query has one token. - Uses the same effective phase for DeepSeek V4.1 C2 compressor sends and ring updates. Request ownership and slot mapping reuse the paired vLLM PCP implementation. - Extends CPU regression coverage for indirect FLA imports through Kimi during model discovery. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Feature] QLI v2: candidate-driven execution, QSLI metadata operator, and arch22 performance optimizations
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [Feature] BigTensorLoader snapshot fast-restore via a shared weight-state kernel
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Two tightly-related pieces: ### 1. `--load-format bigtensorloader`: snapshot fast-restore Restarting a vLLM Ascend instance re-parses safetensors, re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` (quantization repacking, NZ layout conversion, MLA impl construction) and re-allocates final device buffers — a large, repetitive cost for every restart of the same model. This loader caches **each rank's final post-process device weights** (one blob file + one JSON manifest) after the first fresh load, and on subsequent starts restores them via mmap + batched H2D, skipping parsing/repacking/conversion entirely. Measured on Ascend 910B: **2x–7.7x faster `load_model`** across dense bf16, W8A8-quantized, multimodal and MoE+MLA models, with byte-identical serving outputs. Correctness-first design: - **Container capture**: list/dict-held tensors (quant scales, MLA impl carriers) are enumerated through the module graph and restored via chained installs with tuple sealing — no silently-skipped containers, dotted dict keys safe (`[{"a": ...}, {"i": ...}, {"k": ...}]` labeled access chains). - **Alias dedup**: tied weights are persisted once (`alias_of`, nbytes=0) and re-share storage on restore. - **Install-time validation**: schema v3 gate, per-run fingerprint match, blob bounds checks, per-tensor spot hashes — tampering is caught even in size-only verify mode. - **Fallback semantics**: a failed restore never kills startup — the stale snapshot is deleted, the instance falls back to a fresh load and re-saves. ### 2. summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Fix layerwise callback indexing for shared KV under pipeline parallelism
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A shared-source KV cache can register cache views for a layer that runs on an earlier pipeline stage. For example, with a 24+16 split of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, stage 1 holds a mirror of layer 20 and runs decoder layers 24 through 39. The layerwise worker receives 16 forward hooks on that stage. Counting model-wide layer IDs or giving the mirror its own hook can leave the final save wait scheduled after the last forward hook. Use the local stage bounds when registering shared-source cache views. Associate incoming mirrors with the first local hook so their historical prefix rows are available there. The last executing layer reaches the existing final-save wait. PP1 and the fallback for older layer-index APIs retain their previous behavior. The change is confined to the KV pool. It introduces no model-specific layer IDs or prefetch settings. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. With shared-source models and producer-side pipeline parallelism, layerwise Memcache transfers now follow the actual layer execution order and finish at the final local layer. ### How was this patch tested? - Ran `python3 -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store` on the standalone patch. 1058 passed and 12 skipped. The new regression fails against the unpatched base (40 callback slots for 20 local layers). - Added unit coverage for 20+20, 24+16, and 14+26. It checks the HBM buffer addresses scheduled by the first load, the full request's transfer targets, and one final-save wait at the last local hook. A separate in-memory byte round trip

title: [Feature][MoE] Add opt-in DSpark expert-pool routing for single-device expert offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Offloading some MoE expert weights to CPU memory makes it possible to serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a single Ascend 950PR or 950DT device ([#18604](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18604)). During inference, the NPU can stall while waiting for selected expert weights to arrive from CPU memory, making host-to-device transfers a performance bottleneck. This PR limits how many distinct experts are activated in each DSpark verification step. summary: ## Summary Speculative decoding with `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` on the **V1 model runner** silently corrupts generated tokens. This PR fails fast at config validation and steers users to the V2 model runner, which runs the same combination correctly. ## Evidence (A3, Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8, greedy) | Config | Result | | --- | --- | | MRV1 + TP2×PP2 + MTP3, graphs + async | ❌ corrupted | | MRV1 + TP2×PP2 + MTP3, eager, no async | ❌ byte-identical corrupted output | | MRV1 + TP2×PP2 + MTP1, eager | ❌ same divergence point | | MRV1 + TP2×PP2, no speculation | ✅ correct | | MRV1 + TP4 + MTP3 (no PP) | ✅ correct | | MRV2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) + TP2×PP2 + MTP3 | ✅ correct | The corruption is deterministic across all modes, so it is a logic bug, not a race. Token-level tracing shows the mechanism: the drafter emits the correct tokens (its drafts match the non-speculative greedy continuation exactly), the scheduler schedules the real draft tokens, but the **target model conditions on the KV of rejected draft tokens from the previous verify step** — at the first divergence the target's argmax literally returns the previously rejected draft token. Rollback of rejected-draft KV is broken for this combination on the V1 runner. title: [BugFix][Worker] Explain MC2 profiling failures caused by a small HCCL_BUFFSIZE
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On A2/A3 with plain MC2, `profile_run` runs a dummy MC2 dispatch to reserve the HCCL window before the standard profile run. When `HCCL_BUFFSIZE` is smaller than the window the dummy needs, the dispatch kernel asserts inside the device, but operators are asynchronous: startup dies later with an opaque `vector core exception` (error code 507035) blamed on an unrelated operator. All ranks fail, and nothing in the traceback points at `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`. This PR covers the whole MC2-enabled profiling path — the MC2 dummy and the standard profile run that follows, including its final synchronize — and, when a `RuntimeError` carries one of the device signatures that actually reach `str(exc)` (`507035`, `vector core exception`, `fftsplus aivector error`), re-raises an error that names the likely cause, the configured `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, the dummy's token count, and the `ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` diagnostic. The kernel assert text (`HCCL_BUFFSIZE_EP is too SMALL`, `realWinSize >= minWinSize`) is written to device stdout and never reaches the exception, so it is not used as a marker. The hint says "device-side vector-core failure (for example, error code 507035)" rather than quoting one specific form, and is worded "MC2 profiling failed" because the dummy itself does not synchronize; the async error can surface at the profile sync. Other `RuntimeError`s pass through unchanged, and the original exception is chained. Fixes #21756 ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes: the startup error for this failure mode becomes actionable. Succe

title: [Feature][Performance] Support InternLM2-20B-Chat and dispatch scaled RoPE variants to the NPU kernel
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `InternLM2ForCausalLM` runs on the existing upstream vLLM path, but its checkpoint sets `rope_scaling = {"type": "dynamic", "factor": 2.0}`, which resolves to `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding`. That class was missing from `REGISTERED_ASCEND_OPS`, so every decoder layer silently fell back to `forward_native` — no log line, no error, just slower. The same gap affects three other scaled RoPE types. They all share a property: the only thing they change is how the cos/sin cache is computed at init; the forward itself is inherited from `RotaryEmbedding`. So a single mixin (`_AscendScaledRopeMixin`) can route them all to the fused NPU kernel safely: | `rope_scaling.type` | upstream class | models | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dynamic` + `factor` | `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding` | InternLM2, InternLM2.5 | `forward_native` | NPU kernel | | `dynamic` + `alpha` | `DynamicNTKAlphaRotaryEmbedding` | Hunyuan | `forward_native` | NPU kernel | | `ntk` | `NTKScalingRotaryEmbedding` | — | `forward_native` | NPU kernel | | `llama3` | `Llama3RotaryEmbedding` | Llama 3.1+ | `forward_native` | NPU kernel | Three variants are intentionally left out: - `longrope` / `fope`: they override the forward, not just the cache. - `linear`: indexes into the cache via the `offsets` arg, which `rope_forward_oot` rejects. title: [Feature][PP] Add standalone activation send buffering on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add opt-in bounded activation-send buffering for fixed-partition pipeline parallelism, implemented entirely in vLLM Ascend using the existing vLLM PP communication interfaces. Each non-last PP worker copies its intermediate tensors into an independent send slot and posts communication on a separate stream. Subsequent forwards can reuse the model output storage while earlier sends remain in flight. A slot is recycled only after its sends complete, and a full ring applies backpressure. The implementation includes the buffer, runtime integration, configuration validation, documentation, and regression tests in the Ascend repository. It requires no model-specific changes or modified vLLM core package. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Configure the number of activation-send slots per non-last PP worker with: ```bash --additional-config '{"pp_send_buffer_size":5}' ``` The default is `0`. Slots are reserved during initialization using `max_num_batched_tokens`, and their persistent memory is deducted from the KV cache budget. Additional slots consume NPU memory and introduce an activation copy per send. The feature uses fixed layer partitions and has no PP=2 or single-output-token requirement. Existing model/platform requirements for chunked prefill, speculative decoding and graph execution still apply. Sleep mode, external launcher, and sequence/context parallel configurations are rejected. ### How was this patch tested? title: [MRV2] Qwen3.6 prefill: host-side ACLNN workspace/tiling overhead grows with the operator working set
summary: ## Summary On Model Runner V2 with speculative decoding and ACL Graph, the host side of a prefill wave costs more than on Model Runner V1: the NPU executes the same operators at the same speed, but `aclnn*GetWorkspaceSize` / `*_Tiling` calls occupy the host dispatch loop and the wave takes longer. The CANN ACLNN operator-descriptor cache is the mechanism that makes this visible: single-operator descriptors are cached per thread up to `ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT` (default `10000`), with a separate process-wide pool for large fused operators. Model Runner V2 keeps the target and the speculative prefill/decode graphs separately, and a Qwen3.6 worker was observed holding **~9945 descriptor entries in aggregate** right after startup. title: [Misc][MRV2] Expose ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT to diagnose Qwen3.6 prefill overhead
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? CANN keeps single-operator ACLNN descriptors in a per-thread cache whose ceiling is `ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT` (default `10000`), and keeps a separate process-wide pool for large fused operators. Model Runner V2 captures the target and the speculative prefill/decode graphs separately, so it browses a larger operator/shape working set: on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (TP=2, MTP=3, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) a worker was observed holding about **9945 descriptor entries in aggregate** right after startup. That count is worker-wide, so it does not by itself show that a thread reached the per-thread ceiling; saturation is a hypothesis that a profile has to confirm. When a cache does fill, the executor stops reusing descriptors and recomputes tiling and workspace on the host for every call, which a profile shows as `aclnn*GetWorkspaceSize` / `*_Tiling` host time while NPU time stays flat (#21741). summary: ## Summary Add an opt-in INT8 CSA cache path for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Atlas A3. The path packs the MLA KV cache into the 608-byte record consumed by `mixed_quant_sparse_flash_mla(quant_mode=1)` and uses that operator for CSA layers instead of the BF16 `npu_sparse_flash_mla` fallback. The default path is unchanged. The new path is enabled with `--kv-cache-dtype int8` on A3 devices with native INT8 sparse support. ## Switch semantics `--kv-cache-dtype int8` is a global KV cache dtype, but only the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4.1 use the packed INT8 record. On A3 the platform hook therefore: 1. records the opt-in on the engine's HF config (`_a3_int8_csa`), and 2. resets `cache_config.cache_dtype` to `auto`. title: [RFC]: Sleep Mode Upstream Alignment
summary: > **Status:** Draft > **Target:** vLLM Ascend main; vLLM 0.33.0 and main > **Related:** vLLM RFC #34303 (pluggable sleep-mode backend), vLLM #66010 (level-2 discards only parameters) > **Owner:** TBD ## Summary vLLM Ascend currently implements sleep mode with a private worker path (`NPUWorker.sleep` / `wake_up`) that talks to `CaMemAllocator` directly. Upstream vLLM now dispatches sleep through a pluggable `SleepModeBackend`, and level-2 sleep discards only parameter allocations through a `discardable` set. The two implementations have diverged enough that Ascend misses upstream behavior (runtime state preservation, selective discard, `release_kv_cache_memory`) and duplicates worker logic. This RFC aligns Ascend with the upstream dispatch model in four workstreams: 1. integrate `SleepModeBackend`; 2. integrate `discardable` parameters for level-2 sleep; 3. implement selective `discard(tags)`; 4. add the missing release coverage for runtime state, workspace scratch, and ACL graph memory. The public sleep API and configuration stay unchanged: `--enable-sleep-mode` alone must keep working, with `"cumem"` selecting the Ascend implementation. ## Goals - One dispatch path: engine → executor → worker → `SleepModeBackend` → `CaMemAllocator`, matching upstream control flow. - Level-2 sleep discards only what the weight update rewrites; other state is backed up or left resident. - Support `LLM.release_kv_cache_memory()` through `SleepModeBackend.discard`. - Cover the state upstream already covers: `runtime`, `workspace`, and `cudagraph` allocations, not only `weights` and `kv_cache`.

title: [Performance][KV Pool] Automatically right-size layerwise Memcache GVA objects
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In mixed prefill/decode serving (`kv_both`), the original layerwise Memcache GVA allocation rule uses the full model's layer count to set a minimum object capacity. When a KV cache group registers only a subset of those layers, each pooled object can reserve a large unused tail. For new objects, use the transfer start offset plus the total length of the registered KV segments as the allocation size when the worker can establish the object's complete access range. This includes pipeline stages with independent object keys, even when their transfers start at a nonzero offset. Full- and partial-key allocations and the transfer builder use the same layout. Copy lengths, transfer offsets, and cache keys stay the same. Disaggregated prefill/decode deployments (`kv_producer` and `kv_consumer`) and layouts where the worker cannot establish the complete object range continue to use the original allocation rule. Existing objects retain their allocated size while they remain in the pool. This change uses the GVA data-plane strategy introduced by #21314. ## Detailed changes - **`layerwise/pool_worker.py`** builds a per-group layout after KV buffers are registered. Each layout records the allocation size and the existing transfer start offset. For supported Memcache GVA groups in `kv_both` mode, the worker validates that the layer boundaries cover all registered segments and sizes the object to `start_offset + sum(segment_lengths)`. title: [Misc] Add logs for KV-exhaustion recompute in PD disaggregated serving
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? When the decode (D) node cannot allocate KV blocks, the request is aborted and sent back to the prefill (P) node for another prefill ("recompute"). This path is almost silent today: the client sees a normal completion, and the only signal is `stop_reason="recomputed"` observed by the proxy. Correlating a recompute across the three hops (scheduler decision -> KV connector handoff -> proxy retry) is currently guesswork, which makes production timeouts and throughput regressions hard to triage. This PR adds five targeted log points, all using lazy `%` formatting and an existing logger (no new env vars, no new config keys): - `RecomputeScheduler._finish_recomputed_request` (INFO): request parked for recompute, with `request_id` and `client_index`. - `RecomputeScheduler.schedule` preempt branch (DEBUG): blocked request id, preempted (victim) request id, and scheduler step. - `MooncakeConnectorScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens` (DEBUG): adds `request_id` next to computed tokens and `kv_transfer_params`. - `MooncakeConnectorScheduler.request_finished` (DEBUG): adds `request_id` to the delayed-free decision, with request status and transfer params. - Proxy `handle_completions_impl` retry branch (INFO): `request_id`, retry count, generated tokens, and `max_tokens` before/after the retry. Only the recompute event itself and the proxy retry are logged at INFO; they are rare, so normal serving logs stay quiet. No control flow, API or behavior change. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. The change only adds log statements.

title: [BugFix] Honor ascend_log_path from API server startup
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? During API server startup, the Ascend platform opens its log file before initializing the process-wide Ascend configuration. Looking up that configuration at that point silently selects the default log directory. Workers already have the configuration when they open their log files, so a single deployment can end up with logs in two places. The platform extracts `ascend_log_path` from the launch configuration and passes the directory to the file logger before platform validation. When the option is omitted, the platform passes `None` and the file logger selects its default directory. The worker calls the logger with no arguments and reads the path from its initialized Ascend configuration. Calling the worker entry point before initialization now surfaces the configuration error. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [Bug] mega_moe_max_tokens=6144 (previous default) hard-crashes with HCCL 507057 on first prefill (A3, EP16, Kimi-K3)
summary: ### Environment - Hardware: Atlas 800I A3 (910_93), 16 NPUs, supernode deployment - Deployment: Kimi-K3 (W4A8, reduced-layer variant, 13 MoE layers) TP16 = EP16, PD-separated prefill node, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, MoE `topk=16` - Software: vLLM 0.27.1 + vLLM-Ascend megamoe integration branch (0.27.1-based), CANN 9.2.0, cann_ops_transformer_custom mega-moe wheel - The failure lives in the CANN MegaMoe op / HCCL layer, so it is expected to reproduce on any base using the same wheel (current `main` not re-tested, see "Scope" below) ### Symptom With `mega_moe_max_tokens=6144` (the default in the 0.27.1-era megamoe integration), the service **hard-crashes on the first long-prefill request**: ``` Worker_TP6 SUSPECT REMOTE ERROR 507057 ``` All in-flight requests fail (30/30 in the repro), the engine dies. This is not recoverable. ### Root cause analysis `mega_moe_max_tokens` is not a tuning knob — it is passed to the CANN MegaMoe op as `max_recv_token_num` and participates in the **collective symmetric-memory handshake** (`moe_comm_method.py`, `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe` path): it declares "the maximum number of tokens this rank may receive after MoE dispatch". The value must be identical on all EP ranks, and must be >= the actual per-rank received token count. The actual received count is deterministic under load: ``` prefill chunk = 8192 tokens/step dispatch replication (topk) = 16 global token-expert pairs = 8192 x 16 = 131072 balanced per-rank receive (EP16) = 131072 / 16 = 8192 tokens ``` So **even with perfectly balanced expert load, every rank receives ~8192 tokens

title: [Feature][Observability] Report RL lifecycle and router-replay state metrics
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Adds RL metrics for `NPUWorker` lifecycle and for router-replay (routed-experts capture) state, all at the `basic` level. **Commit 1 - lifecycle durations** - `lifecycle:sleep:duration_ms` - wall clock of `NPUWorker.sleep` - `lifecycle:sleep:freed_gb` - memory released by `NPUWorker.sleep` - `lifecycle:wake:duration_ms` - wall clock of `NPUWorker.wake_up` - `lifecycle:update_weights:duration_ms` - wall clock of `NPUWorker.update_weights` The three durations are symbol hooks declared in `config/rl_lifecycle_metrics.yaml`, so no business logic is edited. `NPUWorker.sleep` returns `None` and measures the freed memory internally, so `freed_gb` is reported from the worker through `record_sleep_freed_gb`, labeled with the sleep level. **Commit 2 - router-replay state** - `rl:routed_experts_state{state}` - 0/1 gauge with states `enabled` (aux-output config turns capture on), `ready` (aux-output data plane resolved after KV cache init) and `capturing` (capture hook ran at least once in this process) This one is not a symbol hook: the states are reported from the code that owns each transition (`patch/worker/patch_model_runner.py` and `patch/worker/patch_routed_experts_capture.py`). `capture` runs once per MoE layer per step, so the `capturing` state is latched after the first call to keep the hot path free of metric overhead. Builds on the metric level gating merged in #19776. Recording is gated by the process-local level; these specs stay at `basic` because they fire once per lifecycle event or once per process rather than once per step. ###

title: Kvtc offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? KVTC compresses offloaded KV-cache blocks to reduce host memory usage and CPU↔NPU transfer volume on prefix-cache hits. This PR adds KVTC to Ascend Model Runner V2. [KVTC paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01815) · [Related SGLang RFC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30417) - The scheduler manages separate raw and compressed CPU pools. It stores sink and trailing window blocks raw, prefers raw copies on prefix hits, and recomputes a protected suffix if its raw copy is missing. - The worker uses calibrated PCA projections, optional grouped quantization, and batched DMA. Four Ascend C operators gather and restore K/V blocks, including inverse and forward RoPE for keys. - The calibration tool fits PCA bases and quantization layouts offline using KV-cache dumps. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Users can opt in through `--kv-transfer-config` by selecting `AscendKVTCOffloadConnector` from `vllm_ascend.kvtc.kvtc_offload_connector`. The connector takes a calibration checkpoint matching the model and TP configuration. Its options include K/V compression ratios, quantization, and raw sink and window block counts. The current scope is one uniform BF16 full-attention cache group with tensor parallelism and PP=1. ### How was this patch tested? **Setup.** Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct on two Ascend 910B3 NPUs, TP=2, vLLM 0.33.0, and CANN 9.2.1. title: [Performance][Model] Reuse DeepSeek V4.1 routing input IDs across DP/PCP
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In DeepSeek V4.1, every MoE layer prepares identical routing `input_ids` via `all_gather_input_ids()`, followed by INT64 casting and `-1` sentinel normalization. This introduces redundant collective communication and tensor preparation overhead across layers. This PR caches and reuses the prepared routing `input_ids` across MoE layers within the same execution segment. - **Lazy Producer & Buffer Sharing:** The first eligible MoE layer performs the standard `all_gather_input_ids()` and normalization (preserving exact SP/DP/PCP row ordering and padding) into a model-owned buffer with a fixed memory address. Subsequent layers in the same segment reuse this buffer directly, ensuring compatibility with both eager execution and graph capture (ACLGraph). - **Segment Isolation (Normal vs. Replay):** Separate buffers and producers are maintained for the normal decoder prefix and the decoder replay tail, as replay token compaction alters DP row counts. - **Allocation & Scope:** At model initialization, reuse the runtime MoE policy at the largest supported padded batch and allocate buffers only if `ALLGATHER` is reachable. For example, A3 with an EP group larger than one skips allocation, while A2 can still allocate when small batches use MC2 and larger batches use `ALLGATHER`. At runtime, other communication paths and concurrent microbatches continue to prepare IDs per layer. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. This is an internal performance optimization with no new CLI arguments or environment variables. ### How was this

title: [Performance][MRV2] Reuse V4.1 SWA replay visible lengths
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 bounded replay rebuilds the same per-token SWA visible lengths for multiple SWA groups. Reuse the result in the existing batch-local `common_v41_batch_metadata` dictionary, reducing 20 identical group computations to one. For request `r`, query offset `j`, sequence length `S`, query length `Q`, window `W` and replay floor `R`, the helper computes: ```text p = S - Q + j visible_len = p - max(0, p - W + 1, R) + 1 ``` `query_start_loc` defines request partitions; `seq_lens`, `replay_start` and `num_actual_tokens` define the positions, lower bounds and output range. These inputs are fixed within each shared batch dictionary. The cache key therefore only needs the window and a replay-specific namespace: ```python cache_key = f"replay-swa-visible-lens:w{window_size}" ``` This follows the [existing A5 causal SWA cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/b4a065a85c0e27e921d72e8aca4b9a4f63dd9260/vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v41.py#L1284-L1297), which uses `a5-causal-swa:w{window_size}` in the same dictionary. The replay result uses its own prefix because its visible lengths also depend on the replay floor. It reuses the dictionary and lookup pattern, rather than the ordinary SWA result tensor. Each metadata build creates a fresh batch dictionary. Decoder replay groups share request coordinates and replay floors; the [first SWA layer with a different encoder replay floor already uses an independent dictionary](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/b4a065a85c0e27e921d72e8aca4b9a4f63dd9260/vllm_ascend/models/de

title: [BugFix][PCP] Compact decoder replay across PCP ranks on prefix hits
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #22416. With prefill context parallelism (`PCP > 1`), prefix caching and `--swa-bounded-replay`, a cache hit can return an immediate EOS (`token_ids=[1]`) instead of the expected continuation. Cold prefills and PCP=1 hits are fine. Root cause: `DecoderReplayState._pcp_kept_lengths` decides whether the compact decoder replay saves rows by comparing the **global** kept row count with the **PCP rank-local** padded token extent: ```python num_padded = int(global_kept.sum()) # 128 if num_padded >= batch.num_tokens_after_padding: # 30 on PCP8 return None ``` A prefix hit schedules the hit's last replay window plus the uncached tail, and PCP spreads that query across ranks (e.g. 234 tokens -> 24-30 rows per rank on PCP8). The global window (128) is therefore larger than the local padded width (30), so the function returns `None`, the compact replay is skipped, and layers 21-39 run in the ordinary PCP main pass with the scheduler's replay floor instead of the compact replay floor. Cold prefills (local width ~1246) and PCP=1 hits (local width 234) take the compact replay, which is why only PCP>1 hits break. This PR removes the rank-local comparison. Compaction is a global decision: if any request is trimmed, the PCP branch compacts, the same rule the non-PCP path uses (`requires_compaction`). The rank-local padded width is not a valid proxy for it. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. This is a correctness fix for an existing opt-in feature (`swa_bounded_replay` with `PCP > 1`). Prefix caching off and PCP=1 are inert:

title: [BugFix][EPLB] Make DYNAMIC_EPLB / EXPERT_MAP_RECORD env parsing case-insensitive
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The two EPLB gate variables are parsed inconsistently in the same predicate (`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`, `EplbConfig._validate_config`): ```python assert ( os.getenv("DYNAMIC_EPLB", "false").lower() in ("true", "1") or os.getenv("EXPERT_MAP_RECORD", "false") == "true" ), "The environment variable DYNAMIC_EPLB or EXPERT_MAP_RECORD of the EPLB must be set to true." ``` `DYNAMIC_EPLB` accepts `true` / `TRUE` / `True` / `1`; `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD` only accepts the exact lowercase `"true"`. A user who writes `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD=True` (Pythonic) or `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD=1` (numeric-truthy) gets an assertion failure that says the variable "must be set to true" — while the variable *is* set to a true value. The same asymmetry appears in `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py`, so `patch_multiproc_executor` was silently skipped for the same spellings. This is a one-line behavioural fix: parse `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD` with the same `.lower() in ("true", "1")` comparison the sibling variable already uses, and keep the two expressions readable by naming them. Every value previously accepted is still accepted; `True`, `TRUE` and `1` now enable the EPLB paths instead of failing. ### Scope note: `envs.py` `AGENTS.md` asks for environment variables to be read through `vllm_ascend/envs.py`. This PR deliberately keeps the change to the existing `os.getenv` call sites rather than migrating both variables into the central module: the goal here is to fix the inconsistency, and the surrounding function already reads environment variables directly. title: [Performance][Model] Reuse Qwen4Exp HC block output across streams
summary: Depends on #21901. Qwen4Exp `hc_combine_norm` currently launches one program per `(row, HC stream)`. Every program loads the same row of `block_output`, so the production four-stream layout reads that row four times. This PR adds an A3 row-wise variant for per-branch norm weights at 512 rows and above. One program loads `block_output` once and walks the HC streams in the original order. It preserves the BF16 combine-materialization boundary and FP32 RMSNorm reduction order. Shared weights, smaller batches, and other hardware profiles keep the legacy kernel. The upstream NVIDIA implementation also uses the per-`(row, stream)` schedule and does not provide an Ascend row-wise implementation to reuse. No CLI option, environment variable, or additional-config key is added; the 512-row value is an internal A3 hardware-profile threshold based on measured crossover. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Qwen4Exp long-prefill HC execution on A3 is faster. Public APIs and configuration are unchanged. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [Feature] Opt-in owner-sharded PCP KV cache for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on A3
summary: # What / why PCP ranks currently keep and write a full physical copy of the shared KV slot, even though a prefill token belongs to exactly one rank. This adds an **opt-in owner-sharded placement** for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash prefill on A3: the KV cache is backed by a CANN VMM slab whose 2 MiB physical chunks are split `1 / pcp_size` per rank, while every rank maps the complete logical address range. The stock attention kernel keeps addressing the same cache tensor; only the physical footprint changes. This is the **OB3** and **OB3 + capacity** scope only. # Scope - A3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, **prefill PCP only**. Decode remains replicated and unchanged. - Default-off: `VLLM_ASCEND_PCP_KV_SHARING=replicated` by default; every other switch defaults off. - If any rank cannot map the owner slab, the group falls back collectively to a replicated allocation (`OWNER_CAPACITY` is the exception: it fails closed). - No upstream vLLM changes are required. Related RFC: vllm-project/vllm#50127. ## What is in the PR 1. **Local prefill KV writes** from rank-local hidden states, opt-in and only active with a mapped owner slab. SWA has one entry per token and no cross-chunk state, so the local write is exact and skips the KV-row all-gather. The compressed source planes keep the gathered global write unless explicitly opted in, and never write locally while the index plane is replicated. 2. **Owner VMM slab**: 2 MiB chunk split, `1 / pcp_size` physical bytes per rank, full virtual range on every rank. title: [BugFix][KVTransfer] Sweep expired Mooncake delayed-free entries from the sending thread
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Lease expiry on the Mooncake V2 producer is enforced by `_retrieve_expired_requests_locked`, but main only drives it from two places: | driver | when it stops working | | --- | --- | | `get_and_clear_finished_requests` (scheduler hook) | the hook only runs while the engine steps, and for `MooncakeConnectorV2` the producer-side worker output is empty on every step, so the hook's call site is never reached | | `_handle_heartbeat` | only renews or reaps the IDs D still tracks; once D has removed the request from its roster (D crash, abort, permanently lost DONE) the entry is never looked at again | Both miss the same class of entries: present in the producer's ledger but no longer mentioned by D. The lease bound then means nothing and the ledger grows until restart. This adds a third driver that cannot go away: the sending thread's 1s `zmq.Again` recv timeout runs the same existing sweep. It reuses `_retrieve_expired_requests_locked` (the ledger consolidated by #18957 - this PR adds no ledger) and keeps the expiry rule in one place. **Scope:** the sweeper only *archives*. It moves expired entries from the lease ledgers into `finished_requests`, where a later scheduler drain releases the blocks; it never frees blocks itself and never drains the queue. So this is lease-accounting and observability hardening, not the memory-release fix - block release is #21918's idle-step drain, a real worker output, or a future PR-C that frees after confirming D is dead. ### Design points **Bounded lock hold per tick.** `SWEEP_BATCH_SIZE = 256` caps entri

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Ordinary KDA state commit reconstructs accepted speculative updates for each layer. title: [Ops][Feature] Enable static & super kernel under PIECEWISE cudagraph mode
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE is the default cudagraph mode, but the static / super kernel flags were force-disabled for it, and the static kernel sym_range only covered decode batch sizes — so prefill-shaped pieces never got compiled. Two coupled changes: platform.py — _setup_compile_backend used to force-disable enable_npugraph_ex / enable_static_kernel / enable_super_kernel in additional_config under PIECEWISE. npugraph_ex compiles each piece with force_eager=True and can carry the static/super kernel passes per piece, so the force-off is unnecessary; keep the user's ascend_compilation_config flags untouched. compiler_interface.py — the static kernel sym_range was always _compute_decode_cudagraph_batch_sizes(...), which is capped at max_num_seqs: prefill token counts (e.g. 1024..8192, the cudagraph capture sizes) never enter the compile set. title: [Performance][Model] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 SWA KV cache preparation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 currently prepares SWA KV with three consecutive operators after the WKV projection: RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, and paged-cache scatter. This PR replaces that chain with one A2 (910B) Triton kernel that consumes the raw BF16 WKV output and writes the normalized/rotated rows directly to their physical SWA cache coordinates. The fused kernel: - accumulates RMSNorm in FP32 and preserves the BF16 rounding boundary before RoPE; - implements the existing adjacent-pair interleaved partial RoPE convention; - uses the cache tensor's real block/row/feature strides; - skips negative [block, offset] coordinates used by invalid slots and graph padding; - launches on the caller's current stream, preserving the existing overlap between the KV branch and Wq_b GEMM; - retains the original three-operator path for unsupported inputs. Selection is limited to Triton-enabled A2 (910B), BF16 NPU WKV/cache tensors, DeepSeek V4.1's 512-wide standard SWA cache, compatible 2-D slot mappings, RMSNorm without a loaded bias, and at most 8192 rows. A3, replicated PCP cache writes requiring a global row gather, A5 packed caches, unsupported layouts/dtypes, larger batches, Long KV, C1/C2 compressor, and indexer cache writes remain unchanged. The fused path reduces the SWA preparation region from three kernels to one while avoiding the normalized KV intermediate and its subsequent RoPE/scatter global-memory traffic. summary: ## Summary The Atlas A2 (non-arch35) preMix path of `npu_hc_pre_v3` is ~1.5x slower than the non-premix path at large token counts. title: [Performance][Qwen4Exp] Fuse QSA preparation paths
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Continue the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) QSA preparation optimizations from #21957 on this branch. The implementation originates from #20943, #20944 and #20947; original authorship, contributor attribution and DCO sign-offs are retained. Original implementation credit: `kk_1999` and `Lethobenthos20`. This PR reduces kernel-launch overhead and intermediate tensor traffic at four preparation points: 1. **Indexer query:** move position clamping and sin/cos gathering into the existing RMSNorm + MRoPE kernel. 2. **Compressed Indexer keys:** fuse pooling, RMSNorm, MRoPE and compressed-key cache writes. title: [Feature] Decoder Append-Prefill for Agentic Scenario Prefiller Offloading
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Agentic workloads often have long inputs—tens of thousands of tokens from user and system prompts—but short outputs, such as tool-call instructions of around a hundred tokens. In P/D-disaggregated serving, this imbalance concentrates pressure on Prefiller instances. Even when multiple Prefillers serve one Decoder (nP1D), a fixed P/D ratio cannot dynamically adjust prefill capacity to fluctuating request rates, leaving Prefillers vulnerable to sharp load increases and queueing during request bursts. Successive turns in an agentic session often extend the same conversation history, so the Decoder that served an earlier turn may still hold a reusable prefix in its KV cache. This creates an opportunity to attempt prefill for a follow-up request on that Decoder, reusing the cached prefix and computing the uncached suffix to reduce Prefiller load. This PR introduces Decoder Append-Prefill to support this approach, with a fallback to the Prefiller when no usable local prefix remains. - Add `decoder_append_prefill_proxy_server.py` to route subsequent requests from the same session to its owner Decoder instance and owner DP rank. - Check actual local KV-cache hits in the Scheduler before admitting Decoder-local prefill. If no usable local prefix remains, reject the local attempt before generating output so the proxy can retry through the Prefiller and the normal P/D path. Otherwise, reuse the prefix and perform append-prefill on the Decoder. - Enable append-prefill admission through `scheduler_config.decoder_append_prefill_enable` in each Deco

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The shared DCP sharded indexer merges packed (global ID, score) candidates into an exact owner-local Top-K prefix. For sorted, owner-sharded inputs with a valid local rank and `local_k == topk == 2048`, the kernel caches per-peer bounds between pivots. It uses descending score and ascending ID to resolve ties and pads unused output slots with -1. The public wrapper selects the scan from group size alone. One rank uses the serial specialization. summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? title: [v0.31.0][Ops][Feature] Add short-sequence dense FIA branch for Qwen3.8 QSA attention
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的 QSA 层（12/48 层）当前在 Ascend 上固定走 GBSA 稀疏内核：Lightning Indexer 选 top-k 压缩块 → `npu_generic_block_sparse_attention` 只算选中块。 **短序列场景下这套流程是浪费的**：索引器的 token 预算 K=2048（微块 r=4），当 step 内所有请求的 KV 长度 ≤ 2048 时，top-k 选择会覆盖全部压缩块——稀疏注意力退化为全注意力，索引打分、topk 排序、GBSA 的稀疏元数据开销全部白付。 本 PR 为 QSA 增加短序列稠密分支：条件满足时跳过 GBSA，用 `torch_npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score`（TND + paged block_table）直接在**同一份 QSA 主 K/V cache** 上做全注意力。 ### 实现要点 - **门控**：`max_seq_len <= token_topk（2048，可用 VLLM_ASCEND_QSA_SHORTSEQ_MAX_LEN 覆盖）` 且非 CUDA graph capture 时走稠密分支；否则回退 GBSA，行为与现状一致 - **无需 attention mask**：每 token 一行 TND，逐行可见长度 = `min(logical_position + 1, seq_len)`，复现索引器的因果规则（910B3 实测：TND 的 `actual_seq_lengths_kv` 语义是每行自身可见长度，不是文档描述的累加和——per-row 值误差 0.007，cumsum 值误差 1.46） - **页表逐 token 聚合**：`block_table[token_to_req]`，K/V cache 兼容 `[blocks, page, nkv, head]` / `[blocks, nkv, page, head]` 两种存储布局（与 GBSA 适配层一致） - **索引器不停**：side cache（raw key 环 + 压缩组）照常更新，请求后续变长时无缝切回 GBSA，不需要任何重建 - **零拷贝**：q/k/v 输入无 drift；`block_size` 取自 cache 页轴（128 对齐，满足算子 [16,1024] 的 16 倍数约束） ### 开关 ```bash export VLLM_ASCEND_QSA_SHORTSEQ_FIA=1 # 默认开；0 恢复纯 GBSA export VLLM_ASCEND_QSA_SHORTSEQ_MAX_LEN=2048 # 可选阈值覆盖；0=自动=索引器预算 ``` ## Note on dependencies 本 PR 基于 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 支持链（QSA owner / GBSA adapter / Lightning Indexer，随 #16981 谱系一起 review）。上游 main 尚未包含 `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/`，为使本 PR 可独立编译运行，commit 中一并提供这些依赖模块（`vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/*`、`ops/gbsa*.py`、`ops/triton/qwen4_exp/*`）。短序列分支本身的核心 diff 是 `qsa_fia.py`（新增）+ `qsa.py`（gate + 分支）+ 单测。 ## Does this PR introduce any user-facing chan

summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 currently uses `use_eagle()` to decide whether to allocate the full HC hidden-state buffer. That predicate includes DSpark, even though DSpark consumes the selected auxiliary hidden states through its own storage. Serving with DSpark therefore reserves an unused `[max_num_batched_tokens, hc_mult * hidden_size]` buffer and copies into it on each target forward. With SP enabled, its presence also selects the full-HC/pre-mix gather path. Exclude DSpark at the V4.1 allocation condition. The existing buffer-free forward path then handles collapse/gather, while MTP, Eagle/Eagle3, DFlash and regular draft-model conditions remain unchanged. No runner, shared `use_eagle()` semantics, or automatic-KV accounting changes are included. Target: `releases/v0.32.0rc`. Related #16621 concerns DeepSeek V4 forward/runner operations; this change fixes V4.1 allocation itself. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. DSpark leaves more device memory available for KV cache and avoids the unused HC copy. No configuration changes are required. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Follow-up to #22183, with @bowgneo credited as co-author. This PR fixes two issues: 1. **Incorrect layer ranges in layerwise pooling when PP and PCP are both enabled.** In vLLM v0.33 without the upstream fix from [vllm-project/vllm#65539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65539), the PP rank calculation ignores the PCP dimension. As a result, the pool's layer offset and layer count can differ from those of the actual PP stage. This PR uses the rank from the actual PP process group to determine the layer range and fix external prefix cache reuse. 2. **Incomplete draft KV handling for DFlash/DFlash2 layerwise pooling.** Draft KV is updated after the target forward, so target-layer callbacks alone cannot complete its transfers. One number cannot fit all TP degrees: the break-even payload is strongly TP-dependent, because the bf16 HCCS bandwidth grows with the group size while the fixed cost of the int8 path (`absmax`, 8 KiB fp32 `amax` all-reduce, quantize, dequantize) does not.
