title: [Kernel][ROCm] Partition the cached-context scan for short-query attention (spec-decode verify)
summary: ## Purpose `context_attention_fwd` launches `_fwd_kernel` with a grid of `(batch, head, cdiv(max_input_len, BLOCK_M))`. When the query is short but the cached context is long, that third dimension collapses to **1**, and each program scans the entire context serially. Speculative decoding makes this the common case rather than an edge case. Every decode step has `query_len = num_speculative_tokens + 1`, so `max_query_len > 1` routes the step here instead of to the paged-decode kernels — a 9-token verify against 100K of context runs on one program per head. This adds a specialised route for exactly that shape: the cached context is split across programs which accumulate an unnormalised softmax numerator with its running max and denominator, and a reducer combines the partials and then applies the current chunk in a single tile (valid because the route is gated on `query_len <= VERIFY_MAX_Q`). `_fwd_kernel` is untouched, so ordinary prefill is unaffected, and the route declines when alibi, sinks, sliding window, fp8 output, f32 queries, or cache-sourced current-chunk KV are in play. ### Two load-bearing details about the sizing **The grid must not be sized from the runtime `max_seq_len`.** Both `RocmAttentionMetadataBuilder` and `TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder` set `seq_lens` to 1 in `build_for_cudagraph_capture()`, and both declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`. A grid derived from it is therefore captured at ~1 partition and then **silently truncates the tail of every long sequence at replay** — wrong results, not a slowdown. The available parameters belonging to fc (ColumnParallelLinear) are: {'fc.weight_packed', 'fc.weight_scale', 'fc.weight_shape'} ``` The target model itself loads fine; only the drafter fails. ### Root cause In `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` builds `self.fc` with the target's `quant_config` unless: 1. the quant method is `modelopt_fp4` (workaround from #38650), or 2. `hf_config.quantization_config.dynamic` contains a `-:` pattern matching `mtp` (GPTQ-style exclusion). title: [Docs] Explain how to measure prefix cache effectiveness
summary: ## Purpose The Automatic Prefix Caching guide explains where APC helps, but does not currently tell operators how to measure cache effectiveness or distinguish token reuse from end-to-end performance gains. This change: - documents the token units of `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` and `vllm:prefix_cache_hits`; - adds a PromQL example for aggregate token hit ratio; - describes how to control request order, concurrency, and initial cache state for comparisons; - recommends reporting TTFT, latency, and throughput alongside hit ratio; - clarifies that decode, scheduling, eviction, routing, and block alignment can make a high hit ratio differ from the observed speedup; and - corrects the metric overview so both counter descriptions explicitly say tokens. This guidance is informed by an isolated prefix-cache experiment in which a 94.59% full-block token hit ratio produced only a 5.7%–6.2% throughput improvement for a short agentic workload at concurrency 64. title: [Bugfix] Do not FULL-capture spec-decode batches in TurboQuant attention backend
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #52475: MTP speculative decoding with any `turboquant_*` KV cache dtype silently collapses into repetition, and `num_speculative_tokens: 1` kills the engine with an illegal memory access. Root cause: `TurboQuantMetadataBuilder` declares `_cudagraph_support = UNIFORM_BATCH` while also declaring `supports_spec_as_decode=False`. Those two declarations are contradictory under speculative decoding: 1. `UNIFORM_BATCH` tells the runner it may FULL-capture uniform batches, explicitly including spec-decode verify batches whose query_len is `1 + num_speculative_tokens` (see the `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` docstring). `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` classifies these batches by query length alone and does not consult `supports_spec_as_decode`. 2. But because `supports_spec_as_decode=False` sets `reorder_batch_threshold=1`, the TurboQuant forward routes every batch with `max_query_len > 1` through its per-request Python prefill loop (`_prefill_attention`). That loop iterates over CPU-resident metadata (`query_start_loc_cpu.tolist()`, `seq_lens_cpu.tolist()`), so it is not graph-capturable: capture bakes in the dummy metadata from `build_for_cudagraph_capture`, which fills `seq_lens` with 1. With query_len 4 and seq_len 1, `cached_len = seq_len - q_len` is negative and the synthetic seq_lens slice `_arange_cache[cached_len + 1 : seq_len + 1]` is empty, so the captured graph performs no attention at all. title: [Feature]: Close the remaining DeepGEMM (and other kernel-library) runtime-JIT gaps in kernel warmup
summary: ### Closing Remaining Gap of Deepgemm kernel The main issue and motivation for this is we found **Silent JIT compile** during production workloads, and for VLLM users, there are no easy way to tell if kernel cache is missed or not. The common failure we saw in the real time is related to the "shared memory broadcast" where the system is doing the JIT compilation, taking really long time. it's about **external kernel libraries that JIT-compile in their own runtime, DeepGEMM first.** Their kernels are only partly covered by warmup and not visible to `jit_monitor`. Any model that reaches one of those uncovered entry points can still compile on live requests, even if it passes `--jit-monitor-mode error`. **Goals:** 1. Every DeepGEMM entry point vLLM calls is either warmed, or its JIT compiles are visible to `jit_monitor`. 2. The same treatment for other libraries that JIT outside the hooks `jit_monitor` already has. **Related Impacts.** DeepGEMM compiles a new kernel with nvcc whenever it meets an M (tokens per step) that maps to a tile config it hasn't built yet, and it logs nothing while doing so. Two things make this worse: - **Under DP + EP every rank waits for the rank that is compiling.** - **A step with enough compile time exceeds `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s).** The engine logs `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`, then `EngineDeadError`, and the server exits. `/health` still returns 200, so traffic keeps routing to the stuck pod. title: [Bugfix] Exclude the compilation peak from memory profiling
summary: ## Purpose Closes #54122. On a cold start `torch.compile` and Inductor autotuning run inside `profile_run()`, which sits inside the `memory_profiling()` window. With AOT compile, `decorators.py` already splits the two phases into separate `with` blocks, and `monitor_profiling_run()` asserts compilation is finished before the profiling forward begins, but nothing clears the allocator high-water mark between them. Compilation's temporaries are freed before that forward, so `transient_peak_headroom` counts them as activation memory and the KV cache shrinks until the compile cache is warm. This drops the high-water mark when compilation finishes. Clearing the counter alone would also discard a peak recorded earlier in the same window, since `profile_run()` runs the multimodal encoder before the backbone compiles, so the pre-compilation value is carried over and folded back in. Without AOT (`VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE=0` or `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`) the compile and the first profiling forward run in the same `monitor_torch_compile` block, so the two peaks can't be told apart there. That block passes `discard_peak=False` and keeps the current behavior. ## Test plan 1x H100 80GB, `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, nightly wheel `3b33a845c` with the patch overlaid. Cold means `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` and `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` wiped, warm means the same boot repeated. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Load redundant experts from stacked checkpoints
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #67054. With `--enable-eplb` and `num_redundant_experts > 0`, a checkpoint that stores the experts as one stacked tensor only fills the logical experts. The redundant experts are never written, and EPLB sends tokens to them from the first step, so accuracy drops with no error. Checkpoints with one tensor per expert already get them through the expert mapping, so nothing changes there. title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Support FP8 KV cache for NoPE sparse MLA
summary: ## Summary - Route rope-free (NoPE) sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton kernels for every KV-cache dtype. Routing now depends only on geometry (`head_size == kv_lora_rank`) and workload, not on `kv_cache_dtype`. - Add per-tensor-scaled FP8 KV support to both Triton kernels: the ragged prefill kernel, and the split-K decode kernel from #58584. KV is upcast through BF16 in registers. K and V are the same latent row, so the scale is folded in once into the QK scale and once into the accumulator, never per tile. - Keep Q in model dtype on the Triton route. The AITER asm route and the `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` opt-in still quantize Q to FP8. - Use 64-bit query-row offsets in the ragged prefill kernel, so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic. - Preserve custom MLA geometry and the FP8 cache dtype in the attention benchmark harness. ## Problem AITER's precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. On main, FP8 NoPE requests reach the AITER path, whose 576-element assumption can read past the cache row and cause a ROCm GPU memory fault, so GLM-5.3-Flash cannot serve with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. The Triton ragged and split-K paths already handle the NoPE geometry for BF16. This PR makes their routing geometry-based, adds scaled FP8 KV dequantization, and skips FP8-quantizing Q on that path. ## Duplicate-work check No open PR addresses ROCm NoPE FP8 sparse-attention KV rows. #39168 overlaps the ROCm ops file but changes t

title: [RL] Sharded RDT on the load plan
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item **E1**). This PR moves the sharded RDT weight-transfer engine onto the load plan (`plan_loads`, `get_boxes`/`get_dest`) and direct reload. It deletes everything the plan subsumes and redesigns the trainer/worker protocol around boxes and flat buckets. Not a duplicate: E1 is unclaimed in the tracker. The layerwise RDT path it replaces landed earlier; this PR deletes that path rather than adding a second one. ## Design Every RL step resends all weights from a sharded trainer to vLLM workers. The load plan already knows where each weight lands, so RDT uses the plan rather than its own bake. - **Chosen:** flat buckets. The producer packs each bucket into a NIXL-registered arena once, and the same worker of every deployment pulls that one block into its own registered arena. This keeps the pull count and memory bounded (~231 pulls per 235B sync). - **Rejected:** - keeping the bake and only looking up destinations in the plan (two sources of truth); - one Ray return per tensor (thousands of calls at ~1.2 ms each, with unbounded serving memory); - packing ahead on the sender (measured slower: it contends for the GIL with Ray's return path); - raw NIXL without Ray (it would reimplement Ray's lifecycle and error handling; Ray's costs are listed in Follow-ups instead). - **Costs:** the arenas sit outside `gpu_memory_utilization`, and the first sync plans for 18–21 s on 235B (see Known limitations). ## What changes **Deleted** - The bake: `sharded_rdt_fake.py` (`FakeRDTTensor`, op chains, `BakeSink`, `_Scatter`), recording stamps, the dry-run re

title: [Feature]: Integrate CFT counted-write MoE all-to-all kernel
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Summary Integrate the CFT counted-write MoE all-to-all kernel introduced in [TensorRT-LLM PR #17647](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17647) into vLLM through FlashInfer. ## Background The kernel adds a Compute Fabric Transport (CFT) path for MoE dispatch and combine communication. It uses CUDA Logical Endpoints and `fabric.try_put.counted` operations to write directly into peer receive buffers over the NVLink fabric. A Logical Endpoint is a CUDA transport object representing a resource reachable over the NVLink fabric. Peers address its bound memory using an endpoint ID and offset rather than a mapped remote pointer. ## What is a counted write? A counted write transfers data to a remote Logical Endpoint while atomically incrementing a destination-side counter by the number of bytes delivered. The receiver waits until the counter reaches the expected byte count before consuming the data. This combines data transfer and arrival notification to reduce nvlink latency, avoiding a separate fence-and-flag handshake between the sender and receiver. In throughput cases, because the counter adds to bytes transferred, it could lead to perf regressions. ## Integration plan 1. @bobboli will first integrate the kernel into [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer). 2. After the kernel is available through FlashInfer, vLLM should integrate it through the FlashInfer backend. 3. vLLM should detect the required capabilities at runtime and fall back to the existing MoE all-to-all path when they are unavailable. ## Requirem

title: [HiSparse] Support DFly speculative decoding on HY4
summary: ## Purpose Make HiSparse work with DFly speculative decoding on HY4 / HY4 Flash. Stacked on #69026 (HiSparse support for HY4 Flash); review only the commits above it. Three bugs blocked HiSparse + DFly: 1. **KV-sharing readers with a wider top-k** (`vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py`). DFly draft layers alias target layers. Their top-k is 2176 (history + causal query block), above the target's 2048. Binding them to the owner's hot buffer kept the reader's own `region_stride`, so the resolver rejected it with `region_stride must match the LRU size`. The reader now adopts the owner's `region_stride` and `lru_init`. It also raises if its union bound exceeds the owner's `device_buffer_size`. 2. **DFly draft KV writes** (`vllm/models/hy_v4/nvidia/dfly_speculator.py`). The draft wrote query slots into a private slot-mapping buffer. HiSparse's `write_target` reads the slot mapping bound from `BlockTables`, so draft KV landed in the target's slots. DFly now writes into `block_tables.slot_mappings` and builds metadata from it. The model guard also accepts `HiSparseConnector`; other KV connectors are still rejected. 3. **Resolver output not front-packed** (`csrc/hisparse_kernels.cu`). `hisparse_resolve_residency` wrote attention indices at their original column, but returned `valid_counts` that FlashMLA uses as `topk_length`, which processes only the leftmost `topk_length` columns. DFly rows have holes (clipped history before the query block), so valid query rows past the count were dropped. summary: ## Purpose Fixes #56992. Compressed-tensors checkpoints with a `kv_cache_scheme` currently change the KV cache dtype from `auto` to `fp8` during `Attention` initialization. title: [RFC]: [Spec decode] KV-cache pool collapse when a draft model introduces a new cache spec type (hybrid GDN + DFlash): diagnosis, mitigation dead-ends, and a working dedicated-draft-pool POC
summary: ### Motivation. The unified hybrid KV-cache pool assumes that all attention layers can be grouped by their KV-cache spec type and that **every request draws blocks from every group**. This assumption breaks when a speculative-decoding draft model registers attention layers whose spec type no target layer has: the draft's spec type fragments grouping, inflates per-request block demand, and the scheduler's usable KV pool collapses — even though the draft itself needs very little memory. We hit this end-to-end with a real deployment: a 27B hybrid model (48 linear-attention/GDN layers + 16 full-attention layers) served with a DFlash draft (`num_speculative_tokens=7`) whose 5 attention layers are sliding-window (window 2048, non-causal). title: [Perf] SM90 FP8 scaled_mm: 64x256 tiles for M just above a multiple of 256
summary: ## Overview `cutlass_scaled_mm` for FP8 with per-token activation scales and per-channel weight scales (the `Fp8LinearOp` path on Hopper) uses one config for every M in (128, 8192): 128x128x128 tiles in a 2x1x1 cluster. The cluster pairs two 128-row tiles, so when M is just above a multiple of 256 most of the last 256 rows are padding: - with an odd number of 128-row tiles (0 < M % 256 <= 128), the partner CTA of the last cluster runs the full mainloop on zero rows (it still has to load its half of the multicast B tile); - with 128 < M % 256 <= 192, the last 128-row tile is at least half padding. As a result M = 272 takes 2-3x longer than M = 256 and up to 1.8x longer than M = 512 (twice the work). The same step repeats above every multiple of 256. Chunked prefill and mixed decode + prefill batches land on such M values all the time (the last chunk of a prompt, a few decode rows plus a chunk). This PR adds one config, 64x256x128 tiles without clustering, for M in (128, 1024] with 0 < M % 256 <= 192, which caps the padding at 63 rows. Every other M keeps the current config, so multiples of 256 and all M > 1024 run exactly the same kernel as today. ## Claims - **Kernel time, H200, five GEMM shapes:** the changed M values run 1.42x faster on geomean (min 0.99x, max 2.47x, 50 points); the unchanged ones are within run-to-run noise (geomean 1.00x). - **Root cause, Nsight Compute:** at M = 272 the current config does exactly the tensor-core work of M = 512 and reads the weight 1.65 times from DRAM; the new config does 0.62 of it and reads the weight about once (table below). - **

title: [CI][ROCm] Transcendental, reduction and MFMA bounds for specialized decode (T1 of #68016)
summary: ## TL;DR A GPU computes `exp`, `1/x`, `1/sqrt(x)` and matrix products approximately, so every test of them needs a tolerance. The usual shortcut is to run the kernel once and call what it printed acceptable — which proves nothing, because the run *defined* passing. Every bound here is derived **before** the kernel runs, from AMD's documented instruction accuracy or from the arithmetic itself, and is written next to the assertion that uses it. 34 new tests, green on both target boards. ``` measured tolerance this PR ────────────────── ─────── kernel ──run──> 0.00037 ISA §12.8 ─┐ │ accumulator ┼─> bound ─┐ └──> assert err < 0.0004 helper src ─┘ │ │ kernel ─┴─> compare a later regression to │ 0.00039 still passes err > bound => the kernel is wrong ``` Completes tier T1 of #68016 for the AMD monokernels: #67135 covered the helpers with a closed form and asserted them bit-exact; this adds the ones that cannot be bit-exact — the hardware transcendentals, the wave reductions and the MFMAs. T1 reaches into this model's internals on purpose, because comparing a monokernel against vLLM's own ops cannot localise a bug: both sides reach for the same helpers, and a shared bug cancels. title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Prefetch the whole checkpoint into every node's page cache
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Safetensors prefetch (`--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`, or the automatic prefetch on NFS/Lustre) splits the checkpoint shards by **global** rank. The page cache is per node, so on a multi-node deployment each node warms only `1/num_nodes` of the shards, and its ranks then read the rest cold through the loader. This PR splits the shards among the ranks of **each node**, so every node prefetches the whole checkpoint. This affects any deployment whose world group spans nodes with prefetch active: - TP or PP across nodes (`--nnodes`, or Ray); - DP/EP across nodes, because `init_distributed_environment` folds the DP rank into the global rank. Related: #51339 (extends auto-prefetch to VirtioFS), #49324 (prefetch in the multi-thread loader; it calls `_prefetch_all_checkpoints`, so it inherits this fix), #57973, and the earlier prefetch and read-order work in #40068, #41499, #42837. Follow-ups: #68490 (stacked on this PR: EP-aware prefetch plus a per-node RAM gate) and #68491 (enable the EP weight filter by default). ## Claims - Each node now prefetches every shard. title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #68725. When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks. That ordering is the bug: - A host prefix hit needs the GPU indexer blocks; a copy only speeds up a hit that also finds them. - A long request leaves about 1 indexer block and several resident copies per page. - Later requests' copies therefore outlive earlier prefixes' indexer blocks, and re-sent prompts miss far below host-pool capacity. The fix adds a retained tier to `BlockPool`, a second free queue. Copies that no live request reads go there, and allocation now takes uncached free blocks first, then retained blocks, then prefix-cached blocks. With no retained blocks, `get_new_blocks` takes the existing path unchanged. Alternative considered: putting copies at the queue head. It also fixes the loss, but every copy dies at the next allocation, so copy reuse drops to zero. In a 10k-block simulation: | Re-send lag | main | head | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | 2 requests | 4720 | 0 | 4720 | | 10 requests | 4400 | 0 | 3494 | ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse pytest tests/v1/core/ ``` `test_hisparse_finished_copies_do_not_evict_older_prefix` fails on main and passes here. ## Test Result **Unit tests** - HiSparse tests pass. - `tests/v1/core/` has the same set of failures as main. title: [Core] Prefill hold without data parallelism
summary: ## Overview Builds on #66927: every commit here except the last is #66927's (`e90610c76a`), and this PR's change is the last commit, `dc6a44ee0a` (`[Core] Prefill hold: hold without data parallelism too`); review only that one. It makes `--prefill-hold-ttft-target` work without data parallelism, and on the independent DP ranks of a dense model, which #66927 rejects. This PR merges after #66927 and will be rebased onto `main` once #66927 lands. ## Claims - Without DP attention + EP, the scheduler updates the hold from its own row before each step, as #66927's DP state sync does between steps, and applies the decision in that same step. - Under #66927's 3-parameter NNLS + Online Ski-Rental model (`F + a * M + b * S`), a single rank has `M == S`: `_Cost3D` reduces to 2D (`F + a * M`), `a_waste` vanishes, and Online Ski-Rental amortizes the fixed mixed-step overhead `F`. This commit adds `has_2d` ratio-preserving rescaling (mirroring `has_3d`) so sustained full-budget batches on a single rank preserve the learned `(F, a)` split instead of collapsing `a * M` into `F`. - DP attention + EP is unchanged. Each gate has a bar (a pass/fail threshold). The bar is a tolerance, or the drift between the reference's own repeated passes (its rerun noise) if the noise is more permissive. For the NLL change and the KL estimate, more permissive means higher; for top-1 agreement, lower. title: [Model][Gemma4] Fuse post-attention residual add into pre-FFN RMSNorm
summary: ### Purpose The Gemma4 decoder layer wrote the post-attention residual as a standalone add: ```python hidden_states = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states) hidden_states = hidden_states + residual # separate elementwise add kernel residual = hidden_states hidden_states = self.pre_feedforward_layernorm(hidden_states) ``` That add lowers to its own kernel every layer (`triton_poi_fused_add_*` in a torch-compile trace; a standalone elementwise pass otherwise). This PR folds it into the following norm using `RMSNorm`'s two-argument add-then-norm form: ```python hidden_states = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states) hidden_states, residual = self.pre_feedforward_layernorm(hidden_states, residual) ``` `RMSNorm.forward(x, residual)` dispatches to `fused_add_rms_norm`, which performs the residual add and the normalization in one op. This is the exact residual-threading pattern `gemma3` and `llama` already use. On ROCm (CK-tile / aiter RMSNorm) this removes one standalone add kernel per decoder layer; on other backends it removes the separate add node from the graph. Primarily this is a redundant-kernel cleanup that aligns Gemma4 with the gemma3/llama residual-threading pattern. The measurable upside is concentrated in short-input decode — the long tail of chat interactions, where inputs start as very short sentences and the fixed per-pass kernel overhead is a larger fraction of each step; at large ISL the saved time is negligible against the prefill GEMMs (see Serving benchmark). ### Why this is numerically equivalent (not an approximation) `fused_add_rms_norm` (`vllm/

title: [ROCm] Warm the AITER FA extend kernels from the attention backend
summary: ## Summary Register the two `ROCM_AITER_FA` extend kernels from the attention backend's metadata builder, through `JitWarmupRegistry`, so they build at startup instead of on the first chunked-prefill continuation or prefix-cache hit. ## Motivation A fresh prompt runs one causal varlen call without the LSE. A chunked continuation or prefix-cache hit runs `extend_forward`, which makes a causal call for the new tokens and a noncausal call per gathered context chunk, both returning the LSE. AITER builds each of those modules on first use, so the first request that takes the extend path stalls for about 45 s per module. The study of which kernels each ROCm attention backend misses, and where a warmup can be registered, is in [#68022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68022). ## Changes - Register `AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel` from the `ROCM_AITER_FA` metadata builder, with two keys: causal with sinks, and noncausal without sinks. It uses the same `VllmJitKernel` / `JitWarmupRegistry` mechanism as FA4. - Sliding-window layers register nothing. Their extend path runs the same LSE-free call as a fresh prompt. - The warmup passes `min_seqlen_q=0`, the same literal the serving calls pass. AITER names the module after a zero value. - The warmup query is 16 tokens, because AITER treats a one-token query as decode and drops `causal`. - The registry deduplicates identical layers. summary: ## Overview Let a KV connector request and receive each step's intermediate (EAGLE-3 auxiliary) and final hidden states after sampling without storing them in the KV cache. title: [Perf][Kernel] Triton attention: split only the sliding window across 3D decode segments
summary: ## Purpose On the 3D (split-KV) decode path, `kernel_unified_attention` cuts each sequence into `NUM_SEGMENTS_PER_SEQ` (16) segments over all of `[0, seq_len)`, and only then clips each segment to the sliding-window tile range. Once the context is well past the window, the window's tiles land in one or two segments. The other programs return at once, and one program per (sequence, KV head) does all the work. For Gemma 4 31B's sliding layers (window 1024) at a 32K context, 1 of the 16 segments is active. This PR splits `[window start, seq_len)` instead, whenever the kernel prunes its tile loop to the window: - A new `@triton.jit` helper, `compute_3d_segments`, returns the first tile to split and the tiles per segment. The attention kernel (early exit, and loop bounds through `compute_tile_loop_bounds`) and `reduce_segments` (which segments to combine) both call it, so they cannot disagree. - The wrapper sets a new constexpr, `WINDOW_SEGMENTS`, on 3D launches with a sliding window. R-SWA and unclamped prefix-LM ranges are excluded: keys before the window stay visible there, and `compute_tile_loop_bounds` does not prune them either. Chunked attention (its chunks lie inside the window) and Gemma 4's window-clamped image ranges are included. With the flag off, the helper computes the split with the old expressions. That covers full attention, R-SWA, prefix-LM, and the int4 and turboquant kernels, which reuse `reduce_segments` with its defaults. The attention kernel then compiles to the same PTX as on main, and outputs are bit-identical. With the flag on, outputs differ from main

title: [KV Offload] Support pipeline parallelism in the canonical layout
summary: ## Overview The OffloadingConnector's `canonical_layout` fails at startup with pipeline parallelism today. This PR makes it work with PP, so engines with different PP sizes, TP sizes and layer partitions share KV through secondary tiers. Depends on #67998, whose commits are merged into this branch; please review the commits that are not in #67998. ## Claims - `canonical_layout` works with PP, including non-default layer partitions (`VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION`). title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Honor apply_router_weight_on_input in MoE LoRA
summary: ## Purpose With `apply_router_weight_on_input` (top-1 routing, e.g. Llama4), `prepare()` multiplies the MoE input by the routing weight and the base GEMMs skip the weight on the output. The MoE LoRA path did not follow that contract, in two places, on every LoRA-capable experts class: 1. **W13 LoRA input missing the weight.** The modular kernel stashed the unscaled `hidden_states` as `lora_ctx.original_hidden_states`, which the W13 LoRA reads (Triton experts on a single rank, quantized TRTLLM path). Fix: stash the input scaled the same way prepare scales it. 2. **W2 LoRA delta weighted a second time.** `apply_w2_lora` always multiplied the delta by `topk_weights` (`add_lora_w2` hardcodes `mul_routed_weight=True`). Fix: `apply_w2_lora(..., mul_routed_weight=...)`; the Triton, Marlin and OAI Triton experts pass `not apply_router_weight_on_input`. Inside, unit weights are used rather than passing `False` to the op, because the op's `mul_routed_weight` also selects the W2 row mapping. The TRTLLM LoRA experts also passed the weights to FlashInfer's fused MoE finalize, which has no such switch; they now use unit weights when the flag is set (as `DeepGemmExperts` does). The two errors sit on either side of the activation, so they do not cancel. ## Test Plan New `tests/lora/test_moe_lora_router_weight_on_input.py`: modular kernel (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular` + `TritonExperts`, BF16) with a real `PunicaWrapperGPU` LoRA context, top-1. title: [HiSparse] Add hisparse_config.host_pool_gib to configure HiSparse with indexer offloading
summary: Related to #68725. ## What changes New option: `hisparse_config.host_pool_gib` turns on HiSparse without writing HiSparse's connectors into `--kv-transfer-config`: ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --attention-config.hisparse_config.host_pool_gib 64 ``` vLLM sets up the connectors itself: - `HiSparseConnector`. - With prefix caching (the default), an `OffloadingConnector` for the indexer cache. For GLM-5.3 that's 60.2 GiB of HiSparse pool and 3.8 GiB of indexer cache. title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 native linear: 128x128x128 two-stage tile for short-K large prefill on gfx950

title: [HiSparse] Store one copy of the offloaded indexer across TP ranks
summary: ## What changes With HiSparse and an `OffloadingConnector` (which offloads only the indexer cache) on a single node with TP > 1, the CPU tier now stores **one** copy of the indexer cache shared by all TP ranks, instead of one copy per rank. The bytes are identical on every rank, so at TP4 this cuts the tier's host memory by 4× for the same capacity. Why it happened: the shared-copy layout requires every KV cache group to be TP-replicated. HiSparse's resident and hot GPU page groups are raw pages with no TP metadata, so the check always failed. Those groups are never offloaded, so the check now looks only at the groups that are. Example config that is affected: ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[ {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}, {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":4294967296}}]}}' ``` Before, the 4 GiB tier held 1 GiB worth of blocks (four copies). After, it holds the full 4 GiB. #68771 adds `hisparse_config.host_pool_gib`, which splits one budget between the HiSparse pool and this tier. Whichever of the two PRs lands second will make that split count the tier's actual number of copies. ## Validation `test_hisparse_indexer_tier_is_single_copy_under_tp` fails on `main` and passes here: ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py ``` On 4×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4), with t

Without the env var, the ROCm sparse MLA backend now sends KV caches larger than 4 GiB to vLLM's Triton sparse kernels instead of AITER's asm decode kernel, which is correct but slower. title: [Bugfix][Model] Inkling 2: fit k_group_partials in SM12x shared memory
summary: Fixes the first point of #69012. From 2048 tokens `k_group_partials` launches the TMA kernel with 128x128 tiles over 4 stages, which needs 196,868 B of shared memory. SM12x allows 101,376 B per block, so the engine dies in warmup unless `max_num_batched_tokens` < 2048. The unsplit non-TMA path has the same problem at 4 stages. On devices under 128 KiB of shared memory this uses 2 stages and 64-wide N tiles (both paths). Only pipelining and the output column split change, so the per-element K accumulation order is the same. Hopper/SM100 are untouched. GB10 (sm_121), main at c78f57f7, `tests/models/inkling2/test_moe.py` with the module gate widened to family 120 locally: - main: 11 failed / 39 passed (10 of them shared-memory `OutOfResources`, 147,456 to 196,868 B) - this PR: 1 failed / 49 passed The one left is `test_routing_quantizes_tokens_into_their_rows[200-nvfp4]`, a packed-fp4 mismatch that fails the same way on main, so unrelated. I left the test gate alone because of it; can widen it here if you want.

title: [ROCm][Model][Perf] Fold the k_out dequant and fp8 query quant into the QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache fusion for ROCM_AITER_FA, ROCM_ATTN, and ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
summary: ## Overview This PR depends on: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6808, which has already made it into the most recently pinned aiter release for vLLM (0.1.29). When this fusion and FP8 KV-Cache are active, there's an extra dequantize op (shown below) after the fused kernel to convert `k_out` from FP8 back to BF16 so the downstream attn pieces (ROCM_ATTN & ROCM_AITER_FA) can consume it properly. ```bash def convert_fp8( output: torch.Tensor, input: torch.Tensor, scale: float = 1.0, kv_dtype: str = "fp8" ) -> None: torch.ops._C_cache_ops.convert_fp8(output, input, scale, kv_dtype) ``` This extra small op launch overhead can be saved by folding the conversion portion back into the fused kernel, as it already has an option to output k_out in BF16 when FP8 KV Cache is active. We take `k_out` via `k_out_unquantized`. As for the FP8 query quant, it follows the same idea; we fold the FP8 quantization portion back into the fused kernel. `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` consumes quantized q_out_fp8; we're only able to fold the extra quantize op if the method is `per_tensor` and one corner case of `per-head` (if we have only one local KV head, we'd only need 1 scale). If we have more than 1 local KV head, it falls back to an extra ` static_scaled_fp8_quant` launch to take care of the quantization. To be able to fold all query quantization cases back into the fused kernel, this requires further kernel-side changes within AITER; it needs to take in a scale tensor of size [num_kv_heads] and have the kernel pick the scale for each Q head. I digress; this could be a favorable follow-up PR later

title: [Perf][Core] Pack the consumed audio of streaming sessions
summary: ## Overview Stacked on #68539: only the last commit, 6201477, is new here. A streaming input session keeps the feature of every audio chunk, so that it can replay them after a preemption. Each kept feature is about 15 objects that the cyclic GC tracks, across the scheduler and the workers. A full collection therefore gets slower the longer a session runs. This PR packs the features of the chunks that have been consumed into arrays and a few byte buffers, so each one leaves no tracked objects behind. This is a proof of concept, opened as a draft. It has no end-to-end serving benchmark yet. Non-test file changes: +392 -12 ## Claims - In a 20-minute session (15000 chunks of 80 ms), tracked objects added per consumed chunk drop from 15.09 to 0.09, scheduler and worker combined. - Preemption replay is unchanged: a session rebuilt after a preemption gets all its features back, and re-encodes them if their encoder outputs were evicted. ## Validation Tests were run on 6201477, on CPU (macOS, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): ``` pytest tests/multimodal/test_packed_features.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py tests/v1/worker/cpu/test_cpu_encoder_cache.py --durations=0 ... 0.66s call multimodal/test_packed_features.py::test_tracked_objects_do_not_grow_with_packed_features 0.14s call v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::test_session_packs_consumed_features_and_replays_them[True] 0.13s call v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::test_session_packs_consumed_features_and_replays_them[False] FAILED tests/v1/streaming_

title: [Bugfix][Core] Evict idle streaming sessions when KV blocks run out
summary: Fixes a scheduler deadlock with streaming input sessions, found while reviewing #68539. It affects `main` today and #68539 as well. #### Problem Streaming sessions keep their KV blocks outside `running`: - while parked between chunks (`WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`), and - while waiting in `kv_holding_waiting` for their next chunk to be admitted. These sessions can never be freed: - Preemption victims come only from `running`, so these sessions are never preempted (`_preempt_request` asserts `RUNNING`). - A waiting request that cannot get blocks just ends the waiting loop (`if new_blocks is None: ... break`) and preempts nothing. - `_reserve_parked` reserves blocks only for async KV-connector loads, and the watermark only applies to new admissions. So if such sessions hold all KV blocks and each next chunk needs one more block, nothing is running and no step frees a block. The scheduler then stalls forever with no error. #### Fix When a waiting request cannot get blocks and nothing is running, `_evict_idle_sessions` frees the KV cache of streaming sessions outside `running`, parked ones first, until the blocked request would fit: - **Choice:** parked sessions first (they need nothing until their next chunk), then sessions waiting with KV. It stops once the free blocks plus the blocks it has released cover an upper bound of the blocked request's needs, taken from `coordinator.get_num_blocks_to_allocate` without prefix-cache hits. - **Shared release path:** `_preempt_request` is split into `_release_request_state`, which frees the blocks, encoder cache, aux-output state, and in-

title: [RFC]: Shared JSON Schema structure for structured-output checks and transformations
summary: This RFC describes the target design. Illustrative interfaces below are not implemented APIs. ## Motivation The core problem is that vLLM's pre-compilation JSON Schema checks and configuration-driven transformations lack a shared schema-aware structural model. Several recurse through arbitrary dictionaries and lists, so they can mistake property names or literal JSON values for schema keywords, or treat an unreferenced `$defs` entry as an active constraint. Some type-specific checks also require an explicit `type`, although JSON Schema assertions can apply without one. Patching these cases one walker at a time is whack-a-mole: the next keyword or consumer can repeat the same mistake. These consumers need one shared account of schema boundaries, reference reachability, and type applicability. Concrete motivating cases include: - A property named `patternProperties`, or the same key inside `const`, incorrectly triggers the [Guidance feature gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L50-L73) ([bug #58694](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58694)). - With `disable_additional_properties=True`, the [Guidance transformation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L37-L48) inserts `additionalProperties: false` into an object inside `const`, changing the allowed value ([bug #58695](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58695)). - String assertions can bypass xgrammar checks when `type` i

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Tune the GatedDeltaNet Triton prefill kernels on gfx942
summary: ## Purpose The Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill walks each sequence's chunks in order, so the kernel grid and the MFMA tile shape are all that decide how much of the GPU its five Triton kernels fill. title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FlashInfer's plan() staging buffer pageable
summary: ## Purpose Fixes a race where FlashInfer can overwrite a CPU planning buffer before the GPU has finished reading the previous plan. With MTP speculative decoding, the GPU can then use the wrong scheduling data and crash or hang. This addresses the staging-buffer race reported in #40756. The change replaces FlashInfer's pinned CPU staging buffer with ordinary, pageable CPU memory when vLLM creates an attention wrapper. This lets CUDA stage the source data before the next plan reuses the buffer. It covers decode, prefill and DCP child wrappers (cascade attention, which this originally also covered, was removed upstream in #61126), and adds a regression test for both eager and CUDA graph decode. ### Why it is needed Repeated draft steps can plan the same wrapper before its previous GPU copy runs. A `seq_lens.cpu()` wait masks that overlap in the recorded main baseline, but the performance change in #57352 removes the wait for drafting. This fix protects the planning buffer independently of that wait. The fused drafting path in #58371 does not cover the native FlashInfer path that re-plans each step. ### Why this is not a duplicate Rechecked #40756 and open PR searches for the issue, `_pin_memory_int_workspace_buffer` and FlashInfer planning. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Fold the consumer remap into top-512
summary: ## Overview On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 sparse indexer has 4 candidate-consumer index layers (24/28/32/36). Each picks the top-512 from the candidate pool's compact scores, then a second Triton launch, `_remap_compact_topk`, maps each picked pool slot to its context position. This PR adds a ROCm op, `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode_remap`: the existing gfx950 top-512 kernel with an index map in its final store, so it writes the context positions directly. The consumers use it when k = 512 and the step has fewer than 128 decode rows (a prefill launch goes by its own rows), which removes 4 launches per decode step. It also skips the `-1` fill on all decode rows, whichever top-k kernel runs. #63888 skipped it only where vLLM's top-k runs (fewer than 128 decode rows in the step, k < 2048), so at 128 or more step rows and at k >= 2048 this removes the remaining fills (one launch per index layer, 8 per DeepSeek-V4.1 step) unless prefill or padding rows follow the decode rows. Both halves are exact: the fused op stores the same index sets, and every top-k path writes every slot. On TP-sharded steps both decisions follow #66047's step rows (the whole step's decode rows, not the rank's slice), so all ranks and FULL-graph replays take the same branch. ROCm/gfx950-only. End to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP8 and TP4), that saving (4.7-5.0 us per C1 step in the microbench, about 0.11% of the 4.3 ms TP8 C1 step) is below the server-to-server noise: no step-time change is resolved in either direction, and long-context accuracy is unchanged. ## Performance vs main Setup: MI355X (gf

title: [Perf] Load saved FlashInfer tactics before DS4.1F TP4 decode warmup
summary: ## Overview FlashInfer benchmarks several kernel tactics for an operation and input shape, then saves the winner in a per-rank table. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s TP4 low-latency decode starts that search inside `load_model`. On a warm restart all four tables can already be on disk. The normal warmup reads them after `load_model`, so the decode has already paid to find the same winners again. Moving the read earlier on its own can still miss. In one reproduction, the early key used a KV block size of 64 and the saved table used the backend’s resolved size of 128. This patch resolves the block size first, finds the right table for each rank and loads the saved tactics **before** specialized decode warmup. Shapes with a saved choice can reuse it. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Bound the acceptance estimator's refit step on saturated predictions
summary: ## Overview Limit each refit of the online acceptance estimator to a change of 2 in any predicted acceptance logit. When a confident draft is rejected, its residual can stay large even as its curvature approaches zero. A single large, finite Newton update can then _distort the acceptance estimates that adaptive verification uses to decide which drafts to keep_. When the estimator's predictions saturate, those rejections can trigger oversized Newton steps and cause adaptive verification to _trim_ useful drafts. This behavior can happen in all the situations where the draft model is overly confident, such as repetitive text (e.g. editing tasks, copying workload). As shown in the validation section, in such cases, the adaptive verification can lead to _degraded_ throughput. On a synthetic repetition and copying workload, the baseline verified **70.5%** of drafts and delivered **2,001 tokens/sec**, a **19.7% throughput penalty** compared with verifying every draft. That pattern is consistent with the saturation failure reproduced in simulation. This fix caps the change in any predicted acceptance logit at **2 per refit**. On the same workload, the fix verified **91.6%** of drafts, increased mean acceptance length from **10.73 to 12.92**, and delivered **2,395 tokens/sec** (**+19.7%** over the baseline). ## Claims - For any clamped feature `|f| ≤ 40` and draft position, one refit moves the acceptance logit by at most 2, up to fp32 rounding. - On a simulated stream with feature 40 and 80% acceptance, the bounded refit reaches a logit of 1.34 after 12 refits, close to the target o

title: [Bugfix][Core] Budget the GPU memory held by prompt embeddings
summary: ## Overview Workers copy each request's `prompt_embeds` to the GPU when it is added and kept them until it finished. Memory profiling never counted these tensors, so they came out of the headroom after the KV cache and grew with every running long-prompt request . >[!IMPORTANT] Long multi-turn `prompt_embeds` traffic at high concurrency could run the GPU out of memory. With `--enable-prompt-embeds`, a fixed amount of GPU memory, (`max_model_len + max_num_batched_tokens`) rows of the model's embedding width, is set aside from the KV cache at startup. title: [Frontend] Support cross-machine snapshot (step 1: portable attachments)
summary: # Purpose This PR extends the snapshot feature ([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51360](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51360)) from inplace checkpoint/restore to cross-machine checkpoint/restore. The goal is fast startup for auto-scaling scenarios. ## WHAT Making snapshots work across machines requires solving at least the following problems: * Package all intermediate files generated during vllm startup, such as the triton jit cache. Some of these files are currently open/mapped by vllm; others may be used later. They must be carried over to the new machine, so the process can still find them after restore. * Support cuda device map. GPU device uuids change on the new container, so we need to tell cuda-checkpoint how the old uuids map to the new ones. * Handle ip changes. The new container gets a different ip. Any TCP connections recorded in the snapshot must be re-established on the new ip, and any connections vllm makes afterwards must use the new ip as well. * Avoid pid conflicts. In the new container, running the vllm snapshot restore cli imports libraries such as cuBLAS, which can start threads before criu restore runs. Those threads may occupy pids that criu restore needs. Nothing currently prevents this conflict; a solution is needed, for example setting `kernel.ns_last_pid`. This PR is the first step: it packages the intermediate files so they can travel with the snapshot, and introduces the following: 1. A new `--portable` flag. It marks the snapshot as portable, i.e. for cross-machine use. Making this explicit keeps inplace checkpoint/restore

title: [CPU] Support heterogeneous memory (DDR + HBM) NUMA nodes via hwloc
summary: ## Purpose Follow up to #65677, On CPUs with heterogeneous memory, vLLM currently recognizes only one NUMA node per CPU core, which can be selected with `CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODES`. On CPUs configured with SNC4 (sub-NUMA clustering) and containing two memory tiers DDR and HBM (Intel Xeon Max, SiPearl's Rhea1), the DDR nodes are attached to CPU cores, while the HBM nodes are CPU-less and have no cores assigned. `lscpu` does not report this layout, so it is only visible through `lstopo`/`hwloc-ls`. As a result, vLLM CPU workers cannot be placed on HBM memory nodes, and users cannot benefit from the higher memory bandwidth of HBM. This PR adds an hwloc-based topology path that: - parses `hwloc-ls --of xml` and maps each core to every NUMA node attached to it, including CPU-less HBM nodes, instead of a single node per core - lets users assign their own memory nodes to each vLLM CPU worker via `<CPU_VISIBLE_MEMORY_NODE>`, including HBM nodes - falls back to the existing `lscpu` path, which stays the default. hwloc is used only when the env var is set and `hwloc-ls` is installed, so there is no behavior change otherwise - works with `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` set to either `auto` or explicit core lists - picks an alternative memory node for a core when its default node is not in the allowed set, and stores the chosen node on the worker. Memory availability checks, error messages and KV cache sizing now use the node actually selected rather than the core's default node `hwloc-ls` becomes an optional dependency, needed only for this feature. ## Test Plan - Manual runs on <CPU model

title: [ROCm][Perf][Mistral] Mistral Large 4 specialized decode on gfx942 (MI325X) at TP8
summary: ## Overview Ports the Mistral Large 4 specialized decode (the FlyDSL MonoKernel decode from #64534, following RFC #60904) from gfx950 at TP4 to gfx942 (MI300X / MI325X) at TP8, where the block-FP8 checkpoint fits at about 125 GB a GPU. It stays opt-in, as on gfx950: `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`. - **Overlaps #58710.** The AITER sparse-MLA metadata builder copies `seq_lens` from the device every decode step, which waits for the previous step and stalls async scheduling. #58710 fixes that for every case, with slack for speculative decoding and tests. This PR carries only the non-speculative part (10 lines in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`): without speculation, the host upper bound `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is exact, so the builder reads it instead. Whichever lands first, the other drops or rebases this hunk. All numbers below were measured with it, for the baseline and this PR alike. Without it, the specialized decode's TPOT was about 9% higher at one request, measured on an earlier build. ## Claims - On 8× MI325X at TP8 (block-FP8 checkpoint, FP8 KV cache), pure decode steps of 1, 2, 4 or 8 requests run each layer as one persistent kernel launch: the dense layer 0 and the MoE layers 1-71. - TPOT at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 concurrent requests drops from 13.49 / 14.29 / 15.89 / 18.70 ms to 4.20 / 5.25 / 7.49 / 12.15 ms, which is 3.2× / 2.7× / 2.1× / 1.5× lower (main: 14.00 / 14.83 / 16.48 / 19.16 ms). - GSM8K is unchanged: 96.74% strict / 97.27% flexible, against 96.51% / 97.12% with vLLM's decode. - gfx950 is unchanged: every gfx942 change is gated on

summary: ## Overview Experimental, disabled-by-default prompt-time admission for #62574. title: [Metrics] Add vllm:kv_admission_reserved_blocks gauge
summary: Adds a per-engine Prometheus gauge, `vllm:kv_admission_reserved_blocks{kind}`, for the free KV cache blocks the scheduler holds back from admissions: the watermark, and the reserve for in-flight prefills applied to async KV load admissions. ## Overview `allocate_slots` refuses an admission unless the request's blocks fit within the free blocks minus two reserves: - **watermark** (`--watermark`): headroom kept free when admitting waiting/preempted requests while others are running; - **in-flight load reserve**: an async KV load holds its blocks for the whole transfer and can't be preempted, so the scheduler admits one only if it leaves free the blocks the in-flight prefills still need (`_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()`, passed as `reserved_blocks`). Neither is exported. On a dashboard, `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` can show free blocks while waiting requests, especially P/D decode loads, are still refused. This gauge shows how much of the free pool is held back, so `free - reserved` is the capacity admissions actually see. ## Claims - `vllm:kv_admission_reserved_blocks{kind="watermark"}` reports `KVCacheManager.watermark_blocks` while requests are running, and 0 otherwise, matching when `allocate_slots` applies it (`has_scheduled_reqs`). - `vllm:kv_admission_reserved_blocks{kind="inflight_load"}` reports the reserve an async KV load admission currently faces: the blocks in-flight prefills still need plus the spec decode step blocks, the same `reserved_blocks` value the scheduler passes to `allocate_slots`. It is 0 without a KV connector, since there are no async loads to ga

title: [Quant] Keep uncalibrated KV scales at 1.0 under dummy loading
summary: ## Purpose With `load_format=dummy`, the compressed-tensors `q/k/v_scale` placeholders were filled with random values, which post-load processing then used as live scales: an fp8 KV cache is quantized with garbage scales until real scales are loaded. Checkpoints without KV scales never provide them, so a "dummy start, then load the real weights" flow (RL weight sync, reload) keeps the garbage for good. Give the placeholders dummy value 1.0, and keep the `-1.0` sentinel of `KVCacheScaleParameter`, so `BaseKVCacheMethod` still falls back to 1.0 exactly as in a real load that finds no scale. This only changes the compressed-tensors path; I did not check the other quantization methods. Context: verl works around this with a startup patch plus `reset_uncalibrated_kv_cache_scales` ([code](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/453954b3/verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py)). Tracking: #68777. ## Test Plan / Result RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, dummy start + weight sync: GSM8K 0.91/0.92 vs real load 0.915 (GB200). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [ROCm][CI] Run the MI355 spec decode sharded sampling test nightly only to reduce queue backlog
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview This PR reduces the backlog on the `amd_mi355_2` Buildkite queue. Its agents are busy almost every hour, and jobs wait for them. With the two AR-RMS fusion steps now nightly-only (#65940), `:amd: (MI355) Distributed DP Basic` is the largest per-PR consumer of the queue. This PR moves the step's least stable and second-slowest test, `v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py`, to a new optional MI355 step, `:amd: (MI355) [Nightly] Batch-Sharded Sampling (Spec Decode)`. ## Claims - Saves an estimated 54 agent-hours a week on `amd_mi355_2`, about 2.8% of its load: - Each MI355 DP Basic run is 5.3 minutes shorter: 13.9 + 12.6 planned minutes over 2 shards, against 15.0 + 16.8 today. - The test was behind 58 of the step's 64 automatic retries from Nov 2 to 9, and all 23 builds whose last attempt failed (16 PR builds, 7 on `main`). - MI355 DP Basic keeps the other five L4 commands, including `v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py`, so batch-sharded sampling is still checked on ROCm on every PR. - The spec decode test still runs on MI355 in the daily full CI build (`NIGHTLY=1`), and any PR can run it from "Run more jobs". The L4 step is unchanged. ## Validation **The `amd_mi355_2` backlog.** Hourly snapshots from Nov 5, 14:00 to Nov 12, 14:00 UTC (169 hours), from `https://ci.vllm.ai/api/metrics?hours=168&queue=<queue>`: | Queue | Most agents seen | Hours with every agent busy | Most jobs waiting for an agent | Hours with 10+ jobs waiting | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `amd_mi355_2` | 33 | 165 of 169 | 50 (Nov 9, 16:00) | 19 | | `

title: [Perf][MoE] Add opt-in per-token FP8 dispatch for Humming
summary: ## Overview Humming indexed experts currently quantize per-token FP8 activations after AgRs gathers FP16/BF16 inputs . This PR adds an opt-in path that quantizes on the source rank, transports FP8 activations and FP32 scales, and lets the receiving experts reuse them, solve #68894. Related work: #51332 covers Humming block-FP8 dispatch, #30014 moves FlashInfer FP4 quantization before AllGather, and #61962 targets MXFP8 dispatch with AMD/AITER and MoRI. This PR addresses Humming’s per-token FP8 path with AgRs. ## Claims - Adds default-off per-token FP8 dispatch for indexed Humming, using its existing quantizer and AgRs scale transport. - Uses the same pre-dispatch quantization path in eager execution and CUDA Graph capture/replay. - Reuses AgRs topology handling instead of imposing a separate TP/PCP/DP/SP whitelist. - Improves observed long-input throughput by **4.08% on two L20 GPUs** and **7.42% on four L20 GPUs**. Small graph workloads can regress, so the option remains disabled by default. ## Validation Baseline and candidate use Python source at `d9d7e9434f2dfca94a424deedca44a36d673ce0a`, Humming 0.1.20, and the same official native artifacts from `aefea5c8e00c47032cda6d0b75704f6cd0a7c66d`. This is a nearby-wheel native overlay, not an exact-source full CUDA build. The native build closure and runtime identities were checked for compatibility. ### Correctness and execution coverage - Two-GPU DP2 and PCP2 kernel tests cover BF16/FP16, tiny and empty inputs, uneven ranks, alignment, exact FP8 bytes/scales/routes, and actual graph capture/replay. - Ordinary Humming post-lo

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Skip weights for shared indexer layers
summary: ## Overview Fixes #68919 by skipping checkpoint indexer weights for shared-top-k layers that do not instantiate an indexer. The fix covers both ROCm and CUDA DeepSeek-V3.2 loaders. ## Claims - Prevents `KeyError` when loading checkpoints with `index_topk_freq > 1`. - Preserves normal loading for layers that own an indexer. - Adds a real `LLM` loading regression test for AMD and NVIDIA CI. ## Validation ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_deepseek_v32_indexer_loading.py \ --collect-only -q ``` ```text tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_deepseek_v32_indexer_loading.py::test_loads_checkpoint_weights_for_shared_indexer_layers 1 test collected in 0.02s ``` The following checks also passed: ```bash git diff --check .venv/bin/python -m py_compile \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_deepseek_v32_indexer_loading.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/model.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py ``` Full execution requires CUDA/ROCm and is delegated to the H100 and MI300 CI jobs added by this PR. The loaders now collect the indexer prefixes actually present in `named_parameters()` and skip checkpoint weights for absent prefixes, matching the existing generic DeepSeek loader behavior introduced in #46600. Its modules keep their checkpoint names, and only the classifier runs in `head_dtype`. This replaces per-model head code, and covers heads an FX trace can't (DeBERTa's `ContextPooler`, DistilBERT's inline ReLU). - **Heads are probed at init**: a copy of the head runs on CPU with random weights. title: [RFC]: Rank-local host backing and SM120 DCP for HiSparse
summary: ## Motivation We have implemented and open-sourced Kitepond, a tiered KV cache manager for vLLM. Its vLLM 0.34.0 compatibility build already serves GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 with HiSparse and DCP8 enabled together, plus MTP (multi-token prediction) speculative decoding, on eight RTX 6000D GPUs. We propose upstreaming the reusable support as two independent patches, so that this support can live upstream rather than in a Kitepond fork and other cache managers can use native vLLM interfaces. [Kitepond source](https://github.com/deepagent-ltd/Kitepond) · [Compatibility code](https://github.com/deepagent-ltd/Kitepond/tree/e1df6c23a42e0ecec59da0c285116a54b181a50e/compat/vllm-v034) · [DCP8 launch example](https://github.com/deepagent-ltd/Kitepond/blob/e1df6c23a42e0ecec59da0c285116a54b181a50e/examples/serve_glm53_flash_nvfp4_dcp8.sh) Upstream vLLM 0.34.0's configuration guard rejects HiSparse combined with DCP; our compatibility build carries the two patches below. On the supported SM120 path, DCP distributes a request's KV along the sequence dimension, and HiSparse lets each GPU retain a smaller working set and recall selected historical KV from host RAM. We also need a host memory lease (external backing) that lets an external provider supply rank-local storage while vLLM owns CUDA registration, synchronization, and teardown. On the Kitepond compatibility build, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 with TP8/EP8/DCP8 at 90% GPU memory utilization used 0.976 GiB of GPU KV memory per 1M tokens in aggregate across the eight GPUs, versus 6.304 GiB with DCP8 alone (HiSparse disabled) — an 84.5% reduction in

title: [Perf][Core] Send workers only uncached prompt-embeds rows
summary:
>[!important] **Depends on #68215. This branch contains #68215's commits. I'll rebase onto main once #68215 merges.** ## Overview A request's `prompt_embeds` were sent to the workers and uploaded to the GPU in full, including rows whose positions were already computed, such as prefix-cache hits. Those rows are never read. ## Claims - `NewRequestData` now carries only the rows from `num_computed_tokens` on, and their token-id flags, with the offset as `prompt_embeds_offset` - The worker kernel reads row `num_computed - offset`. The scheduler reserves only the rows sent against `--max-num-prompt-embeds-tokens`, and checks the fit after the prefix-cache lookup. With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a failed load can roll a running request back without re-sending it, so every row is still sent. ## Validation ---

summary: ### What happens Every GLM-5.3 start on 8x MI325X with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` logs ``` WARNING [compilation.py:1466] Cudagraph mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE requires piecewise capture, but the loaded model provides neither a compiled submodule nor breakable CUDA graphs. title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Warm up the SSD kernels on a prefill-sized sequence
summary: ### Purpose Warm up the Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels on up to 32 chunks instead of one, so the autotuned tile suits real prefills. Extends the warmup added in #39822. Related: #60801 (tensor-descriptor path for the same kernels), whose reproducible results depend on this fix. No other PR does this (searched open and merged PRs for SSD, warmup and autotune; #48363 warms other kernels). The Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels are autotuned on their first call: the one-chunk `MambaMixer2._warmup_ssd_kernels` during the profile run. The autotune keys have no sequence-length term, so that pick is reused for every later prefill (and cached on disk with `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=1`). On one chunk many tiles tie within noise; on a real prefill the grid is `nchunks` times larger and tiles differ by multiples. Which tile wins the tie is random per start, so a start can lock in a slow one. This PR warms up on `clamp(projected_states.shape[0] // chunk_size, 1, 32)` chunks. The profile run has `max_num_batched_tokens` rows, so Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (chunk size 256) warms up on 32 chunks by default. ### Results Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16, TP=1. Each sample is a fresh server start; picks are scored against a timing of all tiles at 4x2048. | GPU | warmup | starts with a state / scan tile >1.05x slower than best | | --- | --- | --- | | H200 | 1 chunk (before) | 24/30 (up to 1.55x) / 4/30 (up to 1.45x) | | H200 | 32 chunks | 0/30 / 0/30 | | B200 | 1 chunk (before) | 28/30 (up to 1.61x) / 12/30 (up to 1.53x) | | B200 | 32 chunks | 0/30 / 0/30 | | Arc Pro B70 | 1 chunk (before) | bad tile in 10/12 emulated starts

title: [Bug]: GDN decode hangs — host thread blocked inside CUDA driver call (cuModuleLoadData / cuLaunchKernel) in the triton GDN launch path on RTX 3090 / Windows (WDDM)
summary: Summary On RTX 3090 (SM86, Windows, WDDM — TCC is not available on GeForce), serving a Qwen3.5 GDN hybrid model, the engine core hangs non-deterministically (~1 per 15 h of continuous serving, 3 occurrences so far). The EngineCore main thread is blocked inside a CUDA driver call on the triton kernel launch path of the GDN linear attention kernels — while the GPU keeps spinning at 100% util / ~1% memory bandwidth. Two different launch-path sites have been captured: 1. First-launch site — triton/compiler/compiler.py:479 in _init_handles (i.e. blocked in cuModuleLoadData-style module load), ~5 min after instance boot, on the first launch of fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update. 2. Steady-state site — triton/backends/nvidia/driver.py:351 in __call__ (the C launcher call → cuLaunchKernel), on an instance that had been serving for 15.4 h, so this is not limited to the JIT/warmup window. An automatic supervisor restarts the engine; recovery takes ~91–102 s. Because the hang point is the driver submission path rather than Python-level code, we suspect either (a) a previously-launched GDN triton kernel wedged on-device, back-pressuring subsequent submissions on the same stream under WDDM, or (b) a driver-level wedge. The GPU forensics (100% util, SM ≈1965 MHz, mem_util 1–2%, power ≈208–210 W) fit a kernel stuck in a compute loop with no memory traffic. title: [Bugfix] Guard Conch W4A16 preconditions and pad non-tile-multiple outputs
summary: ## Overview `--linear-backend conch` dies at the first forward pass on `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16`: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x30a2bea0) on address 0x7e69a4600000. Reason: Unknown. ``` 48 of the model's layers are fused `in_proj_ba` projections with `N=96`. Conch's W4A16 kernel loads the weight block and the per-group scales in 64-column tiles with no bounds mask, so the second tile covers columns 96-127: **128 B of packed weight and 64 B of scales per row past the end of the buffer**. This PR handles those shapes in vLLM's Conch wrapper: a `K` the kernel cannot address is refused, and `N` is padded up to the kernel's tile width. title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Frontend — Separating Online Serving from Engine
summary: ### Motivation. This RFC is a follow-up to [RFC #22817 (Disaggregated Everything - Token In <> Token Out API Server)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22817), which proposed disaggregating tokenization and enabling a token-in / token-out API server. It builds upon https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22880. Based on discussions in `#sig-frontend`, I propose a two-phase approach to achieve disaggregation. The key goals are: - **GPU-less deployment of frontend**: Allow preprocessing (tokenization, MM input processing) and postprocessing (detokenization, tool call parsing, reasoning parsing) to run without GPU. - **Disaggregated tokenization**: Support use cases such as llm-d, Dynamo, and custom frontends that need to leverage vLLM's preprocessing logic without running the full inference engine. - **Tokens-in / tokens-out engine**: Make the engine a pure token-in / token-out service, decoupled from request preprocessing. ### Proposed Change. We propose a two-phase disaggregation approach, introducing new CLI subcommands instead of [adding flags ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33000)to the existing `vllm serve`. ### Phase 1: `vllm online` | `vllm engine` The first step is to separate `vllm online` (frontend) from `vllm engine` (GPU inference). Communication between `vllm online` and `vllm engine` is via In-proc (default, co-located) or RPC (disaggregated). This achieves the first level of disaggregation: the online serving layer can run without GPU, handling all preprocessing and postprocessing, while the engine runs on GPU for inference only. When

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate MNNVL buffer setup on multicast support
summary: Fixes #68916. ## Problem CustomAllreduce construction calls torch symmetric memory empty() and rendezvous() on every CUDA device during group init, without the capability gate that SymmMemCommunicator already applies to the same API (the "Device capability 8.9 not supported" line in the issue is that gate). On GPUs without multicast, e.g. L20, the call can never produce a usable buffer: rendezvous returns multicast_ptr == 0 and the result is discarded. The rendezvous is a collective over the group store and has a known host-level crash on 2-rank gloo groups (pytorch/pytorch#203740). Since #58623, VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT no longer auto-disables custom all-reduce, which exposes this init path on TP=2/DP=2 setups like the one in the issue. ## Fix Skip the symmetric-memory buffer setup when no rank in the group has multicast support, using the same collective capability check the cross-node path already uses (_all_ranks_true + _has_local_multicast_support). On Hopper/Blackwell groups nothing changes; on older GPUs we no longer run a 96MB VMM allocation plus a cross-process rendezvous that is immediately thrown away. title: [RFC][XPU] Enable HiSparse on Intel XPU

title: [ROCm][DSv41] MegaMoE improvements for DEP8
summary: ## Motivation AITER MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has scope for improvement: - **No overlap between dispatch and GEMM1.** A rank cannot tell whether more tokens will arrive for an expert, so it waits for every rank's dispatch to finish before computing. - **No overlap between GEMM1 and GEMM2.** The two run as separate stages. - **Kernel selection.** A4W4 ran generic configs that are not tuned for this shape. title: [CPU][Sampler] Triton top-k/top-p kernel for x86 CPU
summary: ## Overview Adds a Triton top-k/top-p masking kernel for x86 CPU (triton-cpu). After #66792 removes the old Triton kernel, x86 drops to the sorting PyTorch fallback, while Model Runner V2 aims to keep the sampler on Triton kernels. **Depends on #66792**, and stacks on its head. Until that PR merges, this diff also shows its commits; only the last two commits belong to this PR. The #66792 kernel is built around `tl.sort`, which triton-cpu can't compile at this size: a 4096-element sort ran for over 7 minutes. So this PR takes the shared helpers from `topk_topp_triton.py` (`Key`, `cached_launch`, the row and mass helpers) and uses three launches: - a per-split pass computes group maxima and FP64 exp sums; - a per-row select bounds the top n by group maxima and cuts them exactly with a radix select; - a per-split fill applies the mask. The sampler dispatches to it on CPU after the GPU branch, and the model runner registers its JIT warmups on CPU. Top-p alone with a very flat distribution falls back to a full-row select, which is the slow case but still faster than the PyTorch fallback. ## Claims - x86 CPU with FP32 logits and a vocab under 2^20 runs top-k, top-p and top-k+top-p on Triton instead of the PyTorch fallback. title: [CPU][Zen] Give the int8 MoE experts slack for the in-place reorder
summary: ZenDNN reorders int8 MoE expert weights in place only when each expert has room for the `N * 4` byte compensation row that follows it. `process_weights_after_loading` leaves them packed back-to-back, so it falls back to duplicating every expert instead. zentorch exposes the fix as an op, `zentorch_preprocess_weights` which re-allocates an `[E, N, K]` int8 weight with slack after each expert. The op is merged on the zentorch plugin's main branch but is not in a released build yet, so on the pinned `2.14.0.1` this path is inert. `has_zentorch_op` returns `False` and the hook returns before touching a weight. It will reach the public package in an upcoming release. ## Validation Unit coverage added to `tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py`, which the `CPU-Kernel Tests` Buildkite job already collects: ``` $ pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py 11 passed ``` ### What the padding buys Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8, 40 MoE layers, 256 experts, 32 cores per arm on one socket each. title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid temporary Qwen3.5 MTP vocab allocations
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #53887. Each table is `vocab_size x hidden_size`; for `Qwen3.8-27B` (248320 x 5120, BF16) that is ~2425 MiB each, ~4850 MiB of throwaway memory at load time. That is enough to OOM a target that fits without MTP, as reported on 24 GB cards (RTX 3090, L4) in the issue. This PR stops building and loading both tables when the drafter would discard them: - **`lm_head`**: never built or loaded. title: [Rust Frontend] Stream Muse tool-call arguments
summary: ## Overview The Rust Muse unified parser buffers each ATEM block until `</atem:function_calls>`, so a tool call produces no deltas until the whole block has been generated. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Skip zeroing READ destinations and wait for their pending copies
summary: ## Overview With a mixed-precision KV cache (e.g. DeepSeek-V4) and async scheduling, MoRIIO READ mode can lose prompt KV it has already received, as the model runner zeroes new blocks on the compute stream and nothing orders MoRI's writes after that. This PR leaves the blocks that a READ overwrites in full out of that zeroing, and makes the decode worker wait for the compute stream before its first read only when that stream still has block copies queued for the step's READ destinations. ## Claims - READ destinations are not zeroed, and received KV is written only after the compute stream has finished copying into the destination blocks. - That fixes the accuracy drop. On MI355X with MoRIIO READ over xGMI and async scheduling, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (P TP4 → D TP4) goes from 0.600 / 0.644 on main to 0.954 / 0.954 in GSM8K (strict-match / flexible-extract), against 0.955 / 0.955 without a connector. Qwen3-32B with an fp8 KV cache and layer 0 kept in bf16 (P TP1 → D TP1) goes from 0.056 / 0.064 to 0.923 / 0.905 over xGMI and from 0.036 / 0.036 to 0.934 / 0.918 over RDMA, against 0.927 / 0.918 without a connector. - READ steps do not wait for zeroing. A step waits in two cases only, when a block copy or a hybrid Mamba state copy on the compute stream writes into a READ destination. The wait is a host sync with the compute stream, so under async scheduling such a step also waits for the previous step’s forward and loses the overlap. The READ steps of a mixed-precision model do not wait, and in the 8k/512 benchmark below throughput, TTFT, TPOT and ITL stay within 0.3% of main. At 16k

title: [ROCm][DCP] Opt-in DCP optimizations: global-key indexer prefill, AITER all-gather (stacked on #65685)
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview **ROCm DCP optimizations split out of #65685 (opt-in): the global-key indexer prefill and the AITER all-gather for the DCP group.** Stacked on #65685: until it merges, the diff against `main` includes it. **Review only `k31...k31-dsa-global-key`** (+704 −1 in 6 files): commits 78319b321a and 1c8b8bacae. Not a duplicate: the code comes from #65685, which drops it in fdf599c9f1. #63859 adds ROCm DCP for `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` in general; #54394 shards indexer rows across TP ranks on CUDA. Neither gathers the index keys across DCP ranks. ## Claims With DCP > 1 on ROCm, the base indexer prefill in #65685 scores each rank's key shard and merges the per-rank top-k candidates. This PR adds: - **Global-key prefill** (`VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_GLOBAL_KEY_PREFILL`, default 1): all-gather every rank's FP8 index keys once per prefill chunk (`gather_global_indexer_keys`) and take the top-k over the whole context, so no candidate merge is needed. - **Row-sharded scoring** (`VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_ROWSHARD_PREFILL`, default 1): each rank scores 1/dcp of the chunk's query rows, and the selections are all-gathered once per layer. The chunk planner's logits budget grows by `dcp_world_size` to match. - **Global row bounds**: `DeepseekV32IndexerPrefillChunkMetadata.global_cu_seqlen_ks/ke`, the row bounds in the request's key space, built by running the existing metadata kernel once more with one rank. They are only built on ROCm with DCP > 1 and no PCP. - `VLLM_ROCM_DSA_DCP_PAD_KEY_GATHER` (default 0) pads the key all-gather to a 16-byte multiple for the AITER IP

title: [Feature][EPLB] Run async policy computation in a persistent subprocess
summary: ## Overview Run async EPLB policy computation in a persistent CPU subprocess so it executes outside the inference worker's Python GIL. This is the standard path when `use_async` is `true` (the existing default); synchronous EPLB and profiling keep their original in-process policy calls. This remains a feasibility draft. Historical H20 A/B runs on `584b4ab` measured 5.37% higher steady-state throughput for the Qwen short-prefill workload and 58.0% lower TTFT P99 for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P-side workload at a fixed request rate. ## Claims - Only policy computation moves to the child. Load aggregation, D2H, migration scheduling, expert transfers, and mapping commits keep their existing execution paths. - Fixed CPU load snapshots produce exactly the same placements as the direct policy, including old-slot retention and custom stats fields. Extension tests verify that async policy calls execute in a different PID. - One child is reused per worker, including daemonic executor workers. Policy exceptions, child death, and timeouts surface as async errors; close reaps the child. ## Validation Local macOS CPU validation of the tree committed as `584b4abce5e01a5d459a143275122a7b65a8aaed`: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_algo.py tests/distributed/test_eplb_extension_hooks.py tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py -q ``` ```text 89 passed, 7 skipped in 44.99s ``` The skips are existing accelerator conditions; no skips were added.
