title: [Core][Mamba] Remove mamba_cache_mode
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Removes `mamba_cache_mode`. Since the `"all"` mode was removed (#58997, #60043), it can only be `"align"` (prefix caching on) or `"none"` (off), so Mamba code now reads `cache_config.enable_prefix_caching` directly. The `--mamba-cache-mode` flag was already a deprecated no-op scheduled for removal in v0.34.0 (#64838); it is removed here too. ## Behavior changes `"align"` was set once, by `MambaModelConfig` in `try_verify_and_update_config`, so it also meant "this model has Mamba layers" and stayed set if prefix caching was turned off later. - Every replaced check is in Mamba-only code (Mamba layers, their metadata builders, `MambaManager`, `MambaHybridModelState`) or guarded by `has_mamba_layers`, a `MambaSpec` or `is_hybrid`, so it still applies to Mamba models only. The one model-agnostic check, chunked MM input in `VllmConfig`, is now guarded by `is_hybrid`. - Two places still turn prefix caching off after that point: batch invariance on TRITON_MLA (at `Attention`/`MLAAttention` init) and MLA on a CPU without AMX. Hybrid models used to keep the `"align"` layout there with caching off; they now raise and ask for `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, since switching the layout that late would leave `mamba_block_size` at the attention block size.

title: [Feature]: Async CP for PCP + DCP prefill: prefetch the next layer's KV and indexer K behind the current layer's compute
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch **Pitch.** Asynchronous context parallelism ("async CP") for PCP + DCP prefill of DSA models: run each layer's context-parallel gathers off the main stream, behind the previous layer's compute, instead of synchronously right before the attention that needs them. The data that is already in the sharded KV cache before the step does not depend on the current layer's output, so layer l+1's share of it can be fetched while layer l computes. **Motivation.** Under PCP + DCP each rank stores one DCP shard of the KV cache. During `flashmla_sparse` prefill of a DeepSeek V3.2-style (DSA) model, every layer all-gathers the KV of the whole context right before its attention. Every indexer layer also all-gathers its indexer K, and the current chunk's new KV and indexer K rows are gathered as well. All of these gathers run on the main stream, and the first two grow with context length. **How much this costs.** For a 1M-token prompt prefilled in chunks of 16384 tokens, these gathers take about 29 ms of a ~210 ms step (about 14%), all on the main stream with nothing overlapping them: | Gather on the main stream (one prefill step at 1M context) | ms | |---|---:| | Whole-context KV all-gather (every layer) | 24.7 | | New KV + indexer K rows of the current chunk | 3.0 | | Indexer K all-gather (indexer layers) | 1.5 | | **Total** | **29.2** | The KV all-gather grows linearly with the context, while DSA keeps the attention itself cheap, so its share of the step grows with context length. title: [RFC]: Eager-mode Sequence Parallelism (SP) with Fused GEMM-Collective (AG+GEMM / GEMM+RS)
summary: ### Motivation. [#42770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42770) moves vLLM away from full-graph `torch.compile` fusion passes toward fusions expressed directly in eager/model code. [#43224](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43224) tracks the concrete porting work for that effort and leaves two explicit open questions unanswered: 1. **Sequence Parallelism (SP)** — "We should decide whether to keep an SP path at all in the manual-fusion world." 2. **GEMM-collective fusion** — "Not sure if this is possible to port to manual fusion." [#60517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60517) has since removed the `torch.compile`-based SP and GEMM-collective fusion passes entirely, so today there is neither SP nor GEMM-collective fusion in the compile-free world. This RFC proposes an eager-mode answer to both open questions: - **Yes, keep SP** — expressed as a property of the model's own forward pass, not a compiler pass. - **Yes, GEMM-collective fusion is portable** — as a *fused GEMM-collective* (AG+GEMM / GEMM+RS), an opportunistic behavior of the same mechanism, which degrades gracefully to plain SP when it isn't available. **RFC Draft design:** https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yKH678I3_rcm6_IQzEbbMaGOwdDPS7Ri9YGLlutP5Bs/edit?tab=t.0 ### Proposed Change. ### Why SP needs a communication/GEMM boundary TP duplicates token-wise work like norms and residual adds. title: [RFC]: Bounded-memory video sessions — KV retention for long-running streaming-input requests
summary: ### Motivation. Continuous video understanding - a model that watches a live camera and emits a short reply per frame for hours (captioning, alerting, counting objects over time) - has no good shape in vLLM today. Each frame's reply has to be produced *in the context of the frames before it*, and with request-at-a-time serving the only way to supply that context is to resend it. That leaves two options, and both fail: - **One request per frame carrying the history.** Every frame re-uploads and re-processes everything the model has already seen. Work per frame grows with the age of the stream; the feed falls behind within minutes. Bounding the resent window caps the growth but pays a full window prefill on every frame. - **One long-lived request that never ends.** Two resources then grow without bound: GPU memory, since everything the model has seen stays resident for the life of the request (video is token-hungry - an hour at 2 fps is on the order of a million tokens of context); and sequence length, since the stream crosses the model's trained horizon within minutes to hours and output quality degrades past it. **vLLM already has the mechanism the second option needs.** Streaming input (#28973), introduced to power the realtime audio API and described in [Streaming Requests & Realtime API in vLLM](https://blog.vllm.ai/2026/01/31/streaming-requests-realtime-api.html), keeps one long-lived request alive while input arrives in chunks: context stays live in GPU memory between chunks, so appending a chunk costs only that chunk. title: [Bugfix][MoE] Decouple DeepEP low-latency dispatch size from max_num_batched_tokens
summary: ## Overview `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` crashes at startup whenever `--max-num-batched-tokens` is set above a few hundred. This happens with an ordinary prefill-friendly config such as `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. The cause is that the per-rank dispatch capacity of the DeepEP LL buffers is taken directly from `max_num_batched_tokens`. This PR decouples the two: the LL buffers are sized for a fixed number of tokens per rank, and larger forward passes are split into several dispatch rounds that stay in sync across the DP ranks. Related: #57894 / #57915 (draft). That PR adds a fail-fast error for the same 32 GiB limit, but the config still cannot run. This PR makes the config run. ## Claims - DP8xEP8 `deepep_low_latency` with `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` now starts and serves correctly with no `NVSHMEM_*` env tuning. Before this PR it crashed in `deep_ep.Buffer.__init__`. - The memory used by the LL RDMA buffer and the batched-expert workspaces no longer grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`. - A clear `ValueError` is raised when a user-set `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` is too small. Previously this was a bare `AssertionError` deep inside DeepEP. - No behavior change for the default LL config: when `max_num_batched_tokens` is not set it already defaults to 256, so no chunking happens and the buffer size is unchanged. - No behavior change for other all2all backends. Chunking only triggers when a rank's batch exceeds `prepare_finalize.max_num_tokens_per_rank()`. Other prepare/finalize implementations report `max_num_batched_tokens` or `None` there, so they never trigger it.

title: [Kernel] Tune small-M block-FP8 Triton configs for NVIDIA L20
summary: ## Overview Add five NVIDIA L20 block-FP8 Triton configuration tables for small-M decode and numerical coverage in the existing kernel suite. Smaller M tiles reduce the wasted row computation of the generic BM64 configuration; N tiles and pipeline stages are selected per shape. This reuses the existing device/shape lookup. The tables apply only to matching L20/Triton shapes with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`. The earlier Auto check selected Marlin. The serving measurements cover explicit Triton. ## Claims On L20 TP1 with explicit Triton, the five tables improve 27B block-FP8 output throughput by 6.8%–34.3% versus stock Triton in the official nightly runs. title: [Feat] debug_utils: Tag non-intrusive dumps with an optional tags dict
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50087. Under DSPARK speculative decoding, the draft model's block forward borrows `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY` to reuse the verify-style attention metadata and the decode CUDA graph. The target model's verify forward uses the same mode. So when the non-intrusive dumper is on, draft and target dumps carry identical tags and cannot be told apart, and dumps of the same tensor from the two runners collide in the comparator. Which model a forward belongs to is a property of the runner, not of the forward, so `forward_mode` is the wrong place to encode it. ## Modifications - `register_non_intrusive_dumper(model, *, tags=None)` accepts an optional dict of tags and attaches it to every dump the hooks emit (both core fields and, in `all` mode, the prefixed module dumps). The tags are bound at registration, so two models in one process keep their own tags even when their forwards interleave. - `ModelRunner` passes `{"runner": "draft"}` or `{"runner": "target"}` (from `is_draft_worker`) only when speculative decoding is on. Without speculative decoding, and when no tags are given, dump names are unchanged. - The dumper itself stays unaware of speculative decoding: the tags are an opaque dict. - Tag names are checked when the dumper is registered. A non-string name raises `TypeError`. A name that is a `dump()` argument, `recompute_status`, or an existing `set_ctx` key raises `ValueError`; before, such a tag raised a `TypeError` on the first dump, inside the forward. A `set_ctx` call made after registration that reuses a tag's name still collides. - The draft/target

title: [Fix] mem_cache: Restore request padding after KV resume
summary: ## Motivation `req_to_token` maps request/token positions to KV-cache locations. Row 0 is initialized to zero and reserved for dummy requests used to pad a CUDA graph batch; real requests use the other rows. With memory saver enabled, releasing `kv_cache` unbacks this table along with the KV allocations. Resuming remaps the memory without preserving its previous contents, but the padding row is not initialized again. Newly admitted real requests populate their own rows, while row 0 can remain uninitialized. A subsequent padded graph replay can read that row while building the attention page table, even though the padded request's output is discarded. An uninitialized entry can point to an unrelated or out-of-range KV page. For example, in the FlashMLA page-table builder with page size 64, an entry of 6400 would select page 100 instead of the reserved padding page 0. Depending on the backend and the resulting index, this can cause a device memory access error or incorrect inference output; it may also appear to work if the remapped bytes happen to be zero. A targeted H20 test detected uninitialized reads after resume, even though the remapped bytes happened to be zero. Separate model inference did not show incorrect output. The test configuration and fix validation are described below. ## Modifications Restore the padding row to zero after KV memory resumes. Add a CPU regression test that simulates nonzero data after resume and checks that real request rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - CPU: `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_sched

title: Decouple per-request sampling seeds from `enable_deterministic_inference`'s kernel overrides; allow ignoring the generation config's EOS ids
summary: Two scheduler options are bundled with behavior we need to turn off: 1. Per-request `sampling_seed` is honored only with `enable_deterministic_inference`. That flag also calls `ModelRunner.maybe_enable_batch_invariant_mode`, which overrides aten matmuls and reductions process-wide with SGLang's batch-invariant kernels. A caller that brings its own model and kernels (and its own batch-invariance) wants seeded sampling without the global overrides, so we monkeypatch `maybe_enable_batch_invariant_mode` to a no-op. Request: a separate option for seeded sampling, or a way to opt out of the kernel overrides. 2. The scheduler adds `model_config.hf_eos_token_id` (from the checkpoint's generation config) to every request's stop tokens. `ignore_eos=True` also disables the request's own `stop_token_ids`, so a caller that wants its stop list to be the only stops clears `hf_eos_token_id`. Request: a server arg (or sampling param) to not add the generation config's EOS ids. Seen at sglang commit 851642ade7.

title: SGLang 1.0 Release Tracker
summary: SGLang 1.0 is a stability release. The work focuses on hardening existing functionality, replacing silent configuration changes with errors that name the setting, and defining a compatibility policy for the 1.x series. Upgrading from 0.5.x may require changes; see [Upgrade notes](#upgrade-notes). This issue tracks progress toward the release, and the sections below are kept current. ## What SGLang offers These capabilities are available in 0.5.x. 1.0 makes them more reliable; apart from the models under New model support, it does not add new ones. ### Performance - Overlap scheduling and multi-stream execution - CUDA graph support, including breakable and full-graph capture - Rust implementations of the radix tree, the router, and an experimental frontend server - A runtime built around prefix sharing - Speculative decoding ### Production serving - Aggregated and prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated serving - Parallelism support: TP, DP, EP, PP, DCP, PCP, and SP - HiCache, Linker, and HiSparse - Unified memory ### Multimodal generation - SGLang Diffusion in the same package and CLI, with native pipelines for image, video, 3D, world, and action models - Composable multi-GPU parallelism: CFG, TP, sequence parallelism, and DP - Request-level quality tiers - Component residency and layerwise offload, from consumer GPUs to multi-GPU servers - OpenAI-compatible image and video API, a Python SDK, and a ComfyUI plugin ### Multiple platform support - NVIDIA (Hopper, Blackwell, Grace Blackwell, Vera Rubin), AMD Instinct, Intel Xeon and XPU, Ascend NPU, PPU, and MUSA ## Release principle

title: [Feat] scheduler: Load-scaled class boundary and token budget for shortest-prefill-first
summary: ## Motivation `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` serves the shortest uncached prompt first. At normal load that lowers mean time to first token, but under sustained short traffic every new short prompt passes a waiting long one, so the long one can wait for a very long time. The policy also fills every prefill batch to the chunked prefill size even when the queue is nearly empty, so a short prompt that arrives mid-batch waits for a whole chunk. This PR adds an opt-in mode that scales both behaviours with the engine's prefill backlog `B`: the uncached tokens of the waiting requests plus what a continuing chunked prefill still has left, per DP attention rank. `B` is recomputed on every pass from the prefix matches the sort already uses, so every TP rank computes the same values. ## Modifications - **Class boundary.** `N(B) = C * 2 ** (-max(0, B - B0) / (K * C))`, where `C` is the chunked prefill size per DP attention rank and `B0` the decay start. Requests with fewer than `N` uncached tokens go first, shortest first, and may join a continuing chunk. Requests at or above `N` follow in arrival order and never join one: the chunk reservation for joiners and admission beside a continuing chunk both stop at the first of them. Up to `B0` the boundary is `C`; beyond it the boundary halves every `K` chunks of backlog, so under overload the order tends to first-come-first-served. - **Token budget.** `Q(B) = r * C * 2 ** (B / (D * C))` caps the prefill tokens of each batch, rounded down to the page size and the chunk alignment (at least one of them), with no cap once `Q` reache

title: [Perf] scheduler: Skip external store probes when ranking the waiting queue
summary: ## Motivation With the unified-cache external linker, `match_prefix` on a request also looks up the external KV store for its uncached pages: a synchronous remote lookup plus an all-reduce across the attention group. Cache-aware ranking (`shortest-prefill-first` in particular, which has no queue-length cutoff) re-matches the whole waiting queue every scheduling pass, so a queue of a few hundred long-context requests turns each pass into hundreds of remote lookups and collectives, and prefill throughput collapses while the GPUs sit idle. Ranking still has to see those external hits: shortest-prefill-first orders by uncached work, and the waiting-queue load metrics report uncached tokens. ## Modifications - Ranking looks up the external store once per request and keeps the restorable prefix end (`Req.external_hit_end`). Later passes match only the local tree and count `max(local hit, external_hit_end)` as cached, so ranking and the uncached-token metrics keep counting external hits. A retraction clears the cached end. - Admission still re-matches each request it takes with a fresh lookup, so what is loaded from the store is decided exactly as before. - `probes_external_store()` says whether a tree's match looks up an external store (a sync-mode linker outside PD decode). Only those trees cache the hit; a HiCache host hit stays a fresh local match. The match path uses the same check. - Past `WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX` waiting requests, a shortest-prefill-first pass refreshes only never-matched requests plus a rotating window of matched ones. - Ranking reuses the increment

title: [Fix] diffusion: Prevent silent server warmup failures
summary: ## Motivation 1. PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28127 introduced `fail_open=server_args.warmup_resolutions is None`, which silently ignores server warmup failures unless `warmup_resolutions` is explicitly specified. As a result, warmup errors can go unnoticed, allowing CI to pass and the server to be marked ready despite failed warmup generation. The proposed behavior ensures that a server running synthetic warmup is not marked ready when warmup generation fails. title: [Refactor] scheduler: Split SchedulePolicy into per-policy rankers and SchedulePlanner
summary: Scope: this PR separates four owners in the scheduler's prefill path, with no behavior change: the policy choice (an enum), the ordering rule (a read-only ranker per policy), the runtime state and the per-pass plan (`SchedulePlanner`, run before admission), and the budget (`PrefillAdder` and its prefill budget, which receive the chunk limit as a number). It leaves open the ranker interface (per-request keys or whole-queue orders) and how the bounded-LPM batch reaches admission; later PRs settle those, each touching a ranker module or `schedule_planner.py` alone. - `SchedulePolicy` is now an enum of the `--schedule-policy` choices (`schedule_policies/policy.py`), merging `CacheAwarePolicy` and `CacheAgnosticPolicy`. Whether a policy needs the prefix cache now follows from its ranker's match plan, so a matching policy falls back to FCFS without a cache, as before. - Each policy is a ranker class in `managers/schedule_policies/`, on `BaseRanker`: the cache-agnostic FCFS, LOF, random, and routing-key rankers share `cache_agnostic.py`; `lpm`, `dfs_weight`, `hrrn`, `shortest_prefill`, and `uniboost` have a module each. A ranker only orders the queue: it reads requests and their prefix matches, declares a match plan (`NoMatch`, `FullMatch`, `HeadWindowMatch`), and writes no request or tree state. - The bounded-LPM admission state for long LPM queues moves into `BoundedLpmAdmission` (`schedule_policies/bounded_lpm.py`). - The former `SchedulePolicy` class becomes the scheduler component `SchedulePlanner` (`scheduler_components/schedule_planner.py`), held as `Scheduler.schedule_plan

title: [Doc] [NVIDIA] qwen3: Add 16 GB consumer GPU (SM89) config tip to the cookbook
summary: ## Motivation The Qwen3 cookbook covers datacenter GPUs, Intel Arc, and Xeon, but has no guidance for 16 GB consumer cards, where the default KV pool is the main limit. This was discussed in #46804, where measuring and adding a 3.2 config-tip bullet was suggested as the low-friction route. ## Modifications Adds one bullet to section 3.2 (Configuration Tips) of `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.mdx`: - On a 16 GB card, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` with default flags gets a ~16K-token KV pool, compared with a 40,960-token default context. - `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` doubles the pool. The bullet gives the measured TTFT/TPOT trade-off and the GSM8K comparison, so readers can judge the accuracy cost. - The scheduler reserves KV based on `max_tokens`, clipped at `SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION` (default 4096). It covers the client cap and the server-side env var. - It links the open pip-install issues on recent toolchains. The command generator (`qwen3-deployment.jsx`) is unchanged. The FP8 KV flag is lossy, so it lives only in the tip and not in a generated cell. The command in the bullet uses `sglang serve`. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3, using Qwen3's recommended non-thinking settings (sgl-eval has no Qwen3 preset): `sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-examples 200 --n-repeats 3 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --max-tokens 4096 --seed 0` | config | pass@1 (3 repeats) | std | majority@3 | |-|-|-|-| | default (BF16 KV) | 0.955 | 0.015 | 0.963 | | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 0.938 | 0.008 |

title: [Fix] jit: Link libcudart from the pip CUDA toolkit layout
summary: base_link_flags() always linked `-L$CUDA_HOME/lib64 -lcudart`. The pip CUDA wheels (site-packages/nvidia/cu13) ship lib/libcudart.so.13 with no lib64/ and no unversioned libcudart.so, so every JIT module with device code failed to link there with `cannot find -lcudart`. Look in lib64/ then lib/, and link the versioned soname by name when the unversioned link is missing. title: [Feat] rust-server: Honor --tokenizer-backend fastokens
summary: ## Motivation Rust-server mode (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) refuses `--tokenizer-backend fastokens` at startup. The Python frontend and sgl-router (`--tokenizer-backend fast`, #46251) honor it, and `dynamo-tokenizers`' `FastTokenizer` is already a dependency of the Rust server. On long multi-turn chats, encoding is nearly all of the Rust frontend's CPU time per request (see #50501). fastokens removes most of it without a cache and without per-rank state, so this is a simpler route than the incremental encode of #50455, which I am putting on hold. ## Modifications - Wire `--tokenizer-backend fastokens` to the Rust tokenizer workers. The loader builds fastokens 0.3.6 from Hugging Face's effective added-token set, including the checkpoint config's matching flags and IDs. - Use the fast encoder with BOS/EOS post-processing for plain text and keep Hugging Face for decoding. Segmented prompts keep Dynamo's control-token checks. - Fall back to Hugging Face if fastokens cannot load the checkpoint or encode the input. A BPE tokenizer without an UNK ID or full byte coverage uses Hugging Face to preserve token IDs around unknown characters. - Keep the native tiktoken checkpoint path. Log when DeepSeek V4/V4.1 chat uses its recipe tokenizer. Set `FASTOKENS_BPE_THREADS=1` for embedded Rust frontend startup by default so the tokenizer workers control encode concurrency. ## Accuracy Tests - Added regression coverage for `single_word` and normalized added tokens, checkpoint config token IDs, out-of-vocabulary BPE, complete byte fallback, BOS post-processing, native tiktoken, and segmented prom

title: [Perf] [AMD] deepseek-v4.1: Reuse the low-ratio identity extend fill across the layers of a ratio
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, every DeepSeek-V4.1 low-ratio index-source layer clears and re-fills its ratio's sparse index buffers in `low_ratio_index_topk_hip_extend`, although on an all-identity prefill the fill is the same for every layer of that ratio; this PR does it once per ratio per forward and lets the later layers reuse it. title: [Feat] api.v1: Add opt-in administrative Shutdown RPC
summary: ## Motivation A separate runtime sidecar using native `api.v1` needs to request engine shutdown without a shared PID namespace. #38075 tracks this operability gap. A closed Generate stream or an RPC acknowledgement must not be mistaken for scheduler retirement or process exit. **A central part of this PR is adding P/D support to the existing native Rust graceful-drain path.** The Shutdown RPC reuses the existing SIGTERM lifecycle. For supported P/D configurations, a normal drain additionally waits for frontend pipeline work, every scheduler request queue, and owned KV-transfer work to settle. This is why the change touches the Rust request/drain core, Python Scheduler, and KV-transfer lifecycle. ## Changes - Implement `SglangService.Shutdown` and generate the Rust/Python bindings with the repository generator; bump `sglang-api-types` to 0.3.0. - Require explicit `SGLANG_ENABLE_NATIVE_SHUTDOWN_RPC=1`, a nonempty `--admin-api-key` bearer credential, and the expected `GetServerInfo.instance_id`. The inference key does not grant this administrative operation. - Enter the existing native SIGTERM drain, including listener close, parent-supervisor notification and scheduler teardown. Refuse before mutation unless the launcher installed that ownership path. Keep unified single-node, single-DP serving without DP attention, and add per-engine prefill/decode shutdown for the bounded P/D configuration below. - Authenticate the listener-close notification with Linux `SCM_CREDENTIALS` and the launcher's registered listener PID list. title: SGLang: stop_regex passes validation but a 24-byte pattern causes MemoryError that escapes the safety net and kills the scheduler
summary: The findings reported here were generated by an LLM-driven automated security audit system (an academic research project at Nankai University, AOSP Lab), and this report was drafted with AI assistance and then reviewed by the reporters. All dynamic evidence quoted below is captured verbatim from actual test runs. ## Summary A 24-byte regex in the `stop_regex` request parameter passes all existing validation (256-byte limit, 32-count limit, `sre_parse.parse` succeeds) but causes Python's `re.search` to allocate about 1.8 GB of memory and raise `MemoryError`. This exception escapes the `except (re.error, RecursionError)` safety net in `_check_str_based_finish` and reaches the scheduler's top-level handler, which sends SIGQUIT and terminates the entire scheduler process. A single unauthenticated request kills the server. ## Affected versions Tested against SGLang v0.5.23 (`schedule_batch.py:1940-1941`). On the current main branch (2026-11-21) the safety net still only catches `re.error` and `RecursionError`, and the `stop_regex` length limit is unchanged at 256 bytes. ## Preconditions - The attacker can reach the SGLang HTTP server port. In the default deployment no `api_key` is configured and `/generate` is unauthenticated. - No special server flags required. ## Root cause The pattern `(?:(?:a*){65535}){65535}` uses nested bounded repetition to force Python's regex engine to allocate a large internal state table. title: SGLang: multimodal chunking parameters have no upper bound, enabling CPU and memory exhaustion from a single request
summary: The findings reported here were generated by an LLM-driven automated security audit system (an academic research project at Nankai University, AOSP Lab), and this report was drafted with AI assistance and then reviewed by the reporters. All dynamic evidence quoted below is captured verbatim from actual test runs. ## Summary The `/generate` endpoint accepts `max_dynamic_patch` and related multimodal chunking parameters (`image_max_dynamic_patch`, `video_max_dynamic_patch`) as plain `Optional[int]` with no upper bound. The InternVL processor's `dynamic_preprocess` function uses these values in a triple-nested loop whose iteration count grows as O(max_num^2). A single unauthenticated request with `max_dynamic_patch=200` takes about 10 seconds of CPU time (versus about 1 second at the default of 12), and larger values grow quadratically. ## Affected versions Tested against SGLang v0.5.23. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark-open: Fuse all-reduce + Norm
summary: ## Motivation 1. Muse Spark's attention boundary runs the o_proj all-reduce (CustomAllReduceV2 push) and then the post-norm + gated residual + pre-norm kernel: two launches and a round trip of the reduced row through HBM. 2. This PR's first version fused them with an SGLang JIT kernel; reviewers asked for the kernel to live in FlashInfer and for SGLang only to call it. 3. The kernel is now FlashInfer's `all_reduce_gated_residual_next_rmsnorm` (FI #9820 (AR+dual-norm), on FI #9732 (push plane)), run on CustomAllReduceV2's push plane. In the 1-shot range (M * TP <= 128) o_proj's peer-store GEMM stores every rank's partial straight into the plane and the kernel only gathers; when the GEMM for the shape has no peer-store epilogue, the kernel publishes the partial itself (published 1-shot). Above that range it runs 2-shot. ## Modifications - `muse_spark_all_reduce_norm_residual.py`: builds one FlashInfer workspace per (communicator, hidden size) on the communicator's push plane (`PushPlane`: this rank's slots, the multicast address, the epoch counter, 4-byte atoms, every rank's slot base) and calls the FlashInfer op with the norm's (cluster size, threads) and an explicit `use_oneshot`. The JIT kernel, its `.cuh`, and the `norm_residual.cuh` / `all_gather_norm_residual.cuh` refactor are dropped. - The launch policy (1-shot or 2-shot, slot bytes, cluster size, threads, the measured SM107 TP4 M = 48 override) is resolved once per shape and shared by the support check, `push_applicable` and the call. `FusedAllReducePostNormResidualPreNorm.__call__` calls the FlashInfer op directly.

title: [Fix] kernels: Fix CuTe DSL GDN dtypes/strides and vectorize decode kernel
summary: ## Motivation CuTe DSL kernel launches do not perform runtime dtype or stride validation on passed PyTorch tensors. In `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/cutedsl_gdn.py`, `_get_compiled_kernel` previously compiled against synthetic dummy tensors with hardcoded `float32` state, `bfloat16` `dt_bias`, `int32` indices, and contiguous state layouts. Whenever runtime inputs deviated from those hardcoded assumptions, the kernel silently corrupted memory or misread bit representations: 1. **BF16 / FP16 state pools (silent 2× OOB corruption + NaNs)**: Passing a 2-byte state pool (`--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` or `float16`) executed 4-byte FP32 loads/stores, overwriting adjacent pool slots and producing NaNs. 2. **FP32 `dt_bias` (silent bit reinterpretation)**: Passing an FP32 `dt_bias` (e.g., `Qwen3.5-9B` / `Qwen3.5-27B` checkpoints where `dt_bias` is FP32) caused the compiled BF16 kernel to reinterpret every FP32 element as two BF16 values. 3. **`int64` `initial_state_indices` (silent index corruption)**: Passing `torch.int64` indices caused the compiled `int32` kernel to read the upper 32 bits (zeros) on odd requests, corrupting slot 0. 4. **Envelope-strided state pools & non-contiguous `a`/`b` views**: Pools with padded slot stride `stride(0) > HV * V * K` (such as radix/hybrid mamba envelopes) and non-contiguous `a`/`b` views (e.g., `mixed_ba.split` in `Qwen3.5-27B`) were not compiled or normalized against their actual strides. In addition, `cutedsl_gdn.py` maintained four nearly identical shared-memory-staged kernels (`1,528` lines) with two `__syncthreads()` barriers per K-ti

title: [Fix] attention: Read the sliding-window tree mask at the window's columns in the unified extend kernel
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51096. On a sliding-window layer, `_fwd_kernel_unified` read the speculative tree mask with the rail length as the row stride and the rail index as the column. Mask rows are full length (`seq_len + num_draft`) and the rail holds only the last `min(seq_len, window)` prefix keys, so for `seq_len > window` drafts attended to drafts that were not their ancestors. For `seq_len <= window` the result was already correct. ## Modifications - Read the mask with row stride `cur_seq_kv_len + cur_window_start` and column origin `cur_window_start`, as `_fwd_kernel` does with `window_kv_offset`. Without a sliding window `cur_window_start` is 0, so other layers are unchanged. - Add `test_unified_sliding_window_tree_mask_matches_reference`, which compares the kernel with a torch reference at prefix lengths 56, 64, 65 and 199 (window 64). ## Accuracy Tests RTX 4090, torch 2.10.0+cu128, Triton 3.6.0, on upstream `1ed3e1d04b` plus this commit (same new-test results on `981becd7af` and `145647c55f`): - The new test passes at all four lengths. With the kernel change reverted it fails at 65 and 199 (13% and 23% of output elements wrong, max abs diff 0.33). - Existing `test_unified_sliding_window_chunked_matches_unchunked` and `test_build_unified_kv_indices` pass. - Existing `test_extend_attention_unified_vs_regular` is intermittent here: it failed on `D=80` in three of four runs (once with this change reverted) and passed in the latest. title: [Feat] [MLU] attention: Add GQA and MLA support
summary: ## Motivation Add GQA and MLA attention support for MLU through SGLang's shared attention and KV-cache interfaces. ## Modifications - Add the MLU MHA attention backend. - Support causal prefill, cached-prefix prefill, decode, and mixed batches. - Support sliding-window attention and explicit LSE returns. - Use paged HND KV storage with shared cache allocation and management. - Add the MLU MLA attention backend. - Support BF16 latent attention for prefill, decode, and mixed batches. - Support dense MHA prefill, including one-shot and chunked-prefix paths. - Support LSE returns and shared attention state merging. - Add an MLA KV pool and a Triton gather kernel, used by the model's one-shot and chunked-prefix paths. - Integrate both backends with the shared runtime. - Preserve model-specific attention backend defaults when resolving MLU defaults. - Preserve MLU mixed mode in the eager runner and use `mixed_prefill_reqs` to distinguish prefill and decode requests. - Support eager DP attention padding for both MHA and MLA backends. - Share forward metadata construction and prepare batch-dependent data once per forward. - Support explicit Triton backend selection with the shared NHD MHA KV pool. - Resolve the default MHA cache layout from the selected backend, preserve explicit environment settings, and reject incompatible configurations. - Add tests for attention correctness, routing, KV-cache operations, mixed-batch boundaries, and platform configuration. Depends on #50116 for explicit HND KV-cache layout support. ## Known Limitations - Eager execution only; MLU graph execution

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe/mlp: Fuse SiLU-and-mul with blockwise FP8 quant in Triton MoE and Qwen2MoeMLP

title: [Fix] scheduler: Hold a capped chunk's unfinished rest in the prefill budget
summary: ## Motivation Under `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` and `uniboost`, the scheduler caps a resumed chunked request's next chunk (`chunked_req_limit`) so that shorter waiting requests join the same pass. The memory budget charged only the chunk that runs now, so the requests admitted after it could take the KV the chunk's unfinished rest needs. On the next pass the continuation then finds no room and parks (since #44823; before it, `Prefill out of memory`), so a chunked request can stall between its own chunks for whole passes. The admission paths already pass the unfinished rest to `memory_budget.reserve()` (`unfinished_input_len`, `deferred_max_new_tokens`), but only `ChainPrefillBudget` charged it; `PrefillBudget` and `SWAPrefillBudget` dropped it. ## Modifications - `PrefillBudget.reserve(..., commit_unfinished=False)`: when set, the page-ceiled rest plus its deferred decode headroom goes to `total_offset` only; later passes allocate it, so `current_offset` is unchanged. - `SWAPrefillBudget.reserve`: the FULL pool commits the whole rest; a window pool commits the window peak of one more chunk (`swa_tokens`), not the whole rest. On a pure-SWA pool, where `total_offset` counts the window pool, the total takes that amount too. A per-request SWA ring already owns its slot and takes nothing. - `ChainPrefillBudget` already commits whole requests; the flag changes nothing there. - `PrefillAdder._add_chunked_req` sets the flag when a chunk is cut short while `chunked_req_limit` is set. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] kernels: Fuse SiLU-and-mul with dynamic per-token FP8 quantization
summary: ## Motivation In dynamic per-token FP8 inference (`--quantization fp8`), every SwiGLU MLP layer executes `silu_and_mul` followed by `per_token_quant_fp8` as two separate kernels. This materializes an intermediate `[M, I]` BF16/FP16 activation tensor in HBM (write in `silu_and_mul` + 2× read in `per_token_quant_fp8` for max-reduction and quantization) and adds an extra kernel launch per layer. Existing `DenseSiluAndMulQuant` fusion on CUDA only covered SM100 128-element block-FP8 (`TP=1`, decode-only). title: [Fix] disaggregation: Clamp routed_experts_start_len to prompt length on PD decode

title: [Fix] model_loader: Wire SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION into DefaultModelLoader and quantize in-place on device
summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION=1` (opt-in, default `False` — zero impact on default GPU loading) is intended to allow online quantization (e.g., loading a 27B/32B BF16 checkpoint with `--quantization fp8` onto a 48 GB GPU where full BF16 weights do not fit in VRAM) by initializing weights on CPU and quantizing module-by-module on the target device. title: [Perf] diffusion: Shorten a multi-GPU server's startup (lazy PyNccl, shared DiT copy, early peer access, held NVML)
summary: ## Motivation A single-node multi-GPU server spends a good part of its launch-to-healthy time on host work that every rank repeats, and on setup that sits on the critical path only because of where it runs. title: [Feat] embedding: Add Cohere-compatible /v2/embed API
summary: ## Motivation Add Cohere-compatible `POST /v2/embed`, following vLLM v0.32.0's embedding contract through SGLang's existing inference and pooling pipeline. ## Modifications - Support text, image and mixed-input adaptation, task prefixes, truncation, output dimensions, and float/base64/binary/ubinary formats. - Serialize successful responses with `model_dump_json(exclude_none=True)` and `Response`, bypassing dictionary conversion and Python JSON encoding. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Route the DCP prefill by its wire bytes
summary: ## Motivation A DSA DCP prefill can be served two ways: **owned** all-gathers Q, attends the slots this rank owns, and LSE-merges the head partials back through an a2a; **gathered** all-gathers the cached prefix KV latents once and attends them with this rank's local heads, with no merge. Neither wins everywhere. Owned pays per extend token and head, gathered pays per cached prefix token, and the crossing between them is a property of the data layout, not of the model. This PR derives it from the running configuration and routes each extend batch accordingly. Builds on #47180 (Q replication + project-before-merge) and #44322, both merged. ## Modifications Per extend token and gathered head, owned puts a partial plus its packed LSE on the wire. Per cached prefix token, gathered puts one latent on the wire. Both collectives move the same `(W-1)/W` of their volume over the same fabric, so the group width and the bandwidth cancel: ``` crossover = (partial_width + lse_pack) * itemsize(partial_dtype) / (latent * itemsize(kv_dtype)) gathered when sum(extend_prefix_lens) < crossover * gathered_heads * extend_num_tokens ``` `latent = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`; `partial_width` is `v_head_dim` when the partials are projected before the merge, `kv_lora_rank` otherwise. A query all-gather adds one latent in the KV dtype to the numerator, which is exactly the denominator — so **not replicating `q_b_proj` adds exactly 1.0, for every model and dtype.** `dcp_gathered_prefill_crossover()` evaluates this once at backend construction and logs it. title: [Feat] [NPU] dcp: Switch MLA and DSA to token sharding
summary: ## Motivation Switch NPU MLA and DSA target attention KV from page ownership to token ownership, including P/D transfer. With DCP2, rank 0 owns tokens 0, 2, 4 and rank 1 owns tokens 1, 3, 5. Preserve the Prefill-ready event and gather completion ordering. - Enable this flow for both Mooncake and Ascend NPU managers. `disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py` remains unchanged

title: [Fix] mamba: isolate one sequence's non-finite input from others in the same chunk
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51108. The SSD kernels zero another sequence's contribution to a dot product by multiplying it by a clean 0.0. But `0 * inf` (and `0 * nan`) is `nan` under IEEE 754. If one request's x, B or carried state is non-finite, it leaks through `tl.dot` into every other request that shares the chunk, including their cached SSM state, which then stays wrong for all later decode steps. ## Modifications Four changes in three files. Each removes another request's rows with a select, not by a multiply: - `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`: a chunk's state belongs to the sequence at its last position. The x and B rows of every other sequence are zeroed (`tl.where` on `seq_idx_k == seq_idx_last`). The owning sequence's rows are untouched, so its own non-finite input still shows up in its state. For a chunk of a single sequence this is a no-op. - `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, carried state: `prev_states` belongs to `seq_idx_prev`. After the dot, the rows of any other sequence are selected to 0 (`tl.where(seq_idx_m == seq_idx_prev, ...)`). The owning sequence's rows keep a non-finite carried state. Not applied with initial states: there each program covers one sequence, so nothing is shared. - `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, x: in a chunk that straddles a sequence boundary, non-finite elements of x are replaced by 0 before `tl.dot(cb, x)` (`v - v` is 0 for finite v and nan for +-inf/nan). Single-sequence chunks are skipped. - `_state_passing_fwd_kernel`: the carried state is selected (`tl.where`) at a sequence boundary instead of multiplied by a zero scale. title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Run the BigVGAN vocoder's convolutions in MIOpen's summation orders from Triton
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, MIOpen serves the FP32 convolutions of the BigVGAN vocoder (the MiniMax-H3 audio decode) with slow solvers: - The dilated conv1d calls of the residual blocks (dilation 3 and 5, 8-512 channels, 3-11 taps) run on the naive solver, which accumulates in FP64 at 4-5 ms a call: about 0.28 s of a 5 s request's audio decode, on every GPU count. - The alias-free up/down-sampling filters are depthwise conv_transpose1d / conv1d calls (12 taps, stride 2, 8-512 channels). Per shape MIOpen picks the naive solver (FP64 sum, up to 0.7 ms a call), im2col + an FP32 GEMM (0.9 ms), or a K=1 GEMM + col2im (0.35-0.48 ms). Each of these solvers has a fixed summation order, so a kernel that sums in the same order returns the same bytes. ## Modifications - New `kernels/ops/diffusion/conv/`: - `conv1d_fp64acc`: sums `x * w` in FP64, input channel outer and tap inner, skipping padded taps, and rounds once. Products of FP32 values are exact in FP64, so repeating the order repeats the sum. - `conv1d_depthwise_fma`: one FP32 FMA per tap, taps ascending (the im2col + GEMM order). - `conv_transpose1d_depthwise`: the naive backward-data order (FP64, taps ascending) or the GEMM + col2im order (FP32 products added with the taps descending). - `minimax_h3_audio_vae/bigvgan.py`: on ROCm, dilated FP32 convs of `AMPBlock1` go through `conv1d_fp64acc` behind a per-shape `BitExactFusionGate`. Undilated convs take a faster FP32 solver and stay on MIOpen. - `vaes/alias_free.py`: on ROCm, each filter shape runs the eager conv at its first sight (outside compile tracing and graph capture) and ad

title: [Bug] PD disaggregation (NIXL): a decode request that reuses a live `bootstrap_room` gets the other request's output with HTTP 200 (follow-up to #40125)
summary: # Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. # Describe the bug This is a follow-up to #40125. That issue has the same root cause and the same trigger: a client sends a `bootstrap_room` that another request is using, directly to the prefill and decode servers. #40125 was closed by the stale bot, and its fix PR #40185 was closed unmerged by the idle-PR bot. No maintainer declined either one. This issue adds three facts that #40125 does not have: 1. #40125 says "No confidentiality/integrity impact observed" and records only the status and the time of each request. We checked the text. The duplicate request's HTTP 200 carries **the other request's output**. 2. This is on the NIXL transfer backend. #40125 tested Mooncake. 3. title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] inkling: Fit small-M grouped GEMM in SM120 shared memory
summary: ## Motivation Inkling doesn't start on SM120 GPUs (RTX 50 series, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). The server dies while capturing decode CUDA graphs: ``` File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/moe/inkling_moe.py", line 998, in grouped_gemm_triton _grouped_gemm_kernel[grid]( triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 110592, Hardware limit: 101376. ``` The small-M grouped GEMM config (used for decode, up to 6144 routed tokens) runs with `num_stages=4`. With 16x128x128 bf16 tiles, Triton keeps 3 stage buffers in shared memory: 3 x 36,864 B = 110,592 B. SM120 only allows 101,376 B per block. This was already fixed for SM121 (GB10 / DGX Spark) in [#33108](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33108). Other GPUs are unchanged. - `test_moe_preprocess.py`: also register the test on the `1-gpu-small` (RTX 5090) runner, the same way `test_convrot_int8.py` does. title: [Perf] [AMD] quantization/fp8: Use the CK bpreshuffle GEMM for dense block-FP8 on gfx942
summary: ## Motivation On MI300X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP8) runs its dense block-FP8 linears through aiter's CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`, which has been the gfx942 default since #43815. gfx95 already preshuffles these weights at load and calls `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, but gfx942 doesn't. title: [Fix] pd: Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots
summary: ## Motivation On the PD **decode** side, `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` sizes the hybrid Mamba / linear-attention **speculative** scratch (`intermediate_ssm`, `intermediate_conv_window`, and the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv / N-gram scratch) by `size + pre_alloc_size`, where `pre_alloc_size = disaggregation_decode_extra_slots` reserves extra `req_to_token` slots for in-transfer (being-received-from-prefill) requests. In-transfer requests are not in the running batch and never enter `target_verify`, so they never need a scratch row. What the scratch does need is a row for every row of a verify batch **after padding**: eager warmup and MLP sync pad the batch to the attention TP (and CP) width, and CUDA graphs to their batch-size alignment. GDN and KDA verify read the scratch through `build_verify_intermediate_state_indices`, which maps every padded row onto the padding row. Other writers index it by batch position: the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv tape and N-gram commit, LFM2's short-conv tape (`arange(bs)`), and the lightning `seg_la` verify (`arange(cache_indices.shape[0])`). They fit today only because the in-transfer rows happen to cover the padding. With `--disaggregation-decode-extra-slots 0`, or more than 32 requests per worker (where the default is 0), a padded verify batch overruns the PLE scratch on main too. The in-transfer rows are not budgeted either. title: [Perf] diffusion: Memoize MiniMax-H3 block AdaLN projections per timestep set
summary: ## Motivation Every MiniMax-H3 block computes its AdaLN parameters with a 2688 x 96768 BF16 projection: 50 weight-bandwidth-bound GEMVs per DiT step, 520 MB read each. The projection's only input is the step's time embedding, and requests that share a schedule run the same timesteps (a few-step release such as Pika-H3-Flex has a single schedule), so after the first request of a schedule each later one recomputes values the process already produced. The AdaLN cache modes (`--minimax-h3-adaln-online`, `--minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path`) remove this work by pruning `adaln_proj`, but they need unquantized native weights and reject adapters that carry AdaLN LoRA deltas. A server outside those constraints pays the GEMVs on every step. ## Modifications - `MiniMaxH3DiTModel._adaln_memo_params`: with resident projections and no tensor parallelism, a step's block AdaLN parameters come from a memo keyed by the bit patterns of the step's unique timesteps (plus the input's shape, dtype and device). At most 32 entries per transformer, least recently used out first. A miss runs the same `project_local` as before and keeps its outputs. - The memo is rebuilt when an `adaln_proj` weight is rebound or the conditioning weights epoch advances. Weight updates and LoRA merges write weights in place, and an unmerged LoRA changes the projection without touching the weight; all of them already advance that epoch. - Unchanged paths, never memoized: both AdaLN cache modes, TP > 1 (the batched all-gather), `torch.compile`, CUDA graph capture, Cache-DiT, layerwise offload, and non-CUDA devices. summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 low-ratio indexer writes the rows of identity prefill requests one request at a time, about eight tiny device ops each, so its launch count grows with the batch; this PR writes a whole run of identity requests with a fixed number of launches. A prefill request whose compressed context fits `index_topk` selects all of its visible compressed positions, so `fill_identity_requests` writes its rows without scoring. title: [Fix] diffusion: Fail the request whose Ulysses peer wait expired, and bound the head-group pipeline's waits
summary: ## Motivation Two gaps in how the multi-rank copy-engine transport (`ipc_a2a_multi`) handles a rank that stops answering: 1. **The plain exchange serves the request that timed out.** Its `spin_wait` gives up after `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) and the exchange returns incomplete data, but the timeout word is only read at the start of the next request. The request that computed on incomplete data finishes and its output is returned; the request after it fails instead. 2. **The head-group pipeline has no timeout at all.** `pipelined_attention` waits for its peers with `cuStreamWaitValue32`. It reports an expiry that no denoising stage did (a stage outside the denoiser role, such as Cosmos 3's denoising stage), so that request fails too instead of the one after it. - The error is `IpcPeerTimeoutError`. title: [Feat] scheduler: Allow lpm with priority scheduling
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-priority-scheduling` only works with `--schedule-policy fcfs` or `lof`; startup rejects every other policy. A deployment that serves several priority classes therefore has to give up prefix-cache-aware ordering. That costs the most when many requests of the same class wait at once, for example agentic multi-turn sessions with 100k-token contexts. FCFS then admits requests of one class in arrival order, they evict each other's prefixes, and every miss is paid back as recomputed prefill. This PR allows `lpm` with priority scheduling. Requests are ordered by priority first, then by longest cached prefix within a priority. ## Modifications - `validation_hook.py`: `lpm` is accepted with `--enable-priority-scheduling`. - `SchedulePolicy._sort_lpm_with_priority`: - sorts the queue by (priority, arrival); - prefix-matches only the first `WAITING_QUEUE_PREFIX_MATCH_MAX` (128) requests in that order and re-sorts them by (priority, in-batch duplicate, longest prefix); - leaves the tail in (priority, arrival) order. Plain `lpm` drops to unsorted FCFS above 128 waiting requests, but with priority the class order holds for the whole queue. - The tail gets the same handling as the tail of a bounded batch: a fast-match init, and the FCFS prefix refresh before the head is matched. - Bounded LPM (#48409) is turned off when priority scheduling is on. Its fixed batch commits the head of the queue, so a new higher-priority request could wait behind committed lower-priority members. title: [Feat] scheduler: Add waitable request retirement receipts
summary: ## Motivation Accepting a cancellation does not mean the request has left the scheduler: its terminal output can precede resource release. Callers handing off work need a separate retirement acknowledgement. The api.v1 integration in #50042 consumes this contract. Adds an opt-in receipt for one captured request instance. Tracks #48626 and replaces #48624, preserving its implementation and review history. ## Modifications - Keep ordinary `/abort_request` behavior unchanged. Waiting requires an exact RID, a cancellation ID and a bounded timeout. - Bind retries to the captured instance, including after output cleanup or public RID reuse. Retain completed and pending cancellation-ID bindings for the full five-minute retry window. At capacity, reject new operations rather than forgetting existing bindings; retry failed control replies. - Confirm retirement only after terminal handling, launched scheduler steps, request-owned allocations/cache locks and live scheduler holders have drained. A retraction abort follows the same fences. - Separate scheduler target identity from IPC reply correlation with an append-only optional `target_rid`, retaining the legacy HTTP layout/fallback. This prepares the shared core wire contract for #50042 without enabling native retirement execution in this PR. - Limit this slice to single-rank unified text generation with built-in full-attention caches, static pools and Python TreeCore. Unsupported owners are rejected before cancellation; Rust HTTP ingress rejects waiting before local abort or peer relay. | Result | HTTP | Caller action | | --- | ---

summary: - Under local control broadcast (`--enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast`, and the Rust server's per-rank listeners), each attention-DP group received a control request in its own step, so groups applied a weight update or a memory release in different steps. #51641 scoped the handlers' barriers and gathers to the group to avoid the deadlock that caused; this change aligns the groups instead. - Each control request gets a number: the DP controller numbers what it sends, and on the Rust server DP rank 0's listener gives the number to whichever listener fans the request out, over a new internal route, `/internal/control_seq` (same auth level as `/internal/peer`). title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Speed up the MiniMax-H3 video VAE decode on ROCm (gfx950)
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm the MiniMax-H3 video VAE decoder (a 36-block ViT, 32 heads of 64, 1797 tokens per tile) leaves three things on slow paths: - **Attention.** torch's fused SDPA corrupts this decoder on gfx950, so the ViT attention runs an FP32 math replica (#47570): two FP32 GEMMs and an FP32 softmax per `[1, 32, 1797, 64]` call, 7056 calls per 5 s request. - **The decoder fast path.** The quality-gated fast path (batched tile decode, fused residual-add RMSNorm) is installed only from the CUDA platform, so on ROCm every tile runs its own decoder forward. The fused norms were kept off ROCm (#43350) because they decoded to NaN there: their PTX `mul.rn` has no HIP lowering. - **The QK norm.** The affine-free per-head RMSNorm (64 wide) goes through aten's `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel<half, float, rms_norm>`: one 256-thread block per row, after a `.contiguous()` copy of the strided q/k chunk, 45 us a call and 14112 calls per 1-GPU request (0.64 s). The NeoX rope then makes it three launches and four passes over q and k per attention block. ## Modifications - `minimax_h3_video_vae/attention.py`: on gfx950, half-precision inputs on the GPU go to aiter's flash kernel (`aiter.flash_attn_func`), the fused FP32-accumulating class that CUDA's SDPA uses for the same call. FP32 inputs and CPU inputs keep the math replica. The attention module is shared with the MiniMax-H3-Image decoder, which takes the same kernel. - `norm/aten_rms_norm_rocm_triton.py` (new), `aten_rms_norm_rocm`: a replica of ROCm aten's affine-free RMSNorm for FP16/BF16 rows of 64, 128 or 256. summary: Addresses #50443 (the server-side part, suggestion 1). ## Motivation When the KV cache pool is smaller than the context window, a request's `max_new_tokens` is lowered to fit the pool with no log, and the output ends early as an ordinary `"length"` finish. summary: Groundwork for #50943: B1 (owners initialize like engines) and B2 (the cache daemon loader). ## Motivation Three bugs on the weight-cache path (`--weight-cache-mode client` / `daemon`): 1. **A weight-cache engine never reaches the weight-cache loader for a pre-quantized ModelOpt checkpoint.** `get_model_loader` takes the ModelOpt branch before the `IPC_CACHE` branch, and the ModelOpt branch exempts only `RUNAI_STREAMER` and `REMOTE_INSTANCE`. title: [Fix] speculative: Exact sampling penalties and min_new_tokens in DFlash and DSpark verify
summary: ## Motivation DFlash and DSpark verify ignore `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `repetition_penalty` and `min_new_tokens`. Nothing counts the tokens they commit in the penalty tables, and verify reads `acc_linear_penalties`, a field that `SamplingBatchInfo` does not have. So a request with `min_new_tokens` can stop early, and a request with a repetition penalty gets the same logits as one without. This PR counts every committed token and penalizes each verify row as decoding one token at a time would. The results are bitwise equal to non-speculative decoding. ### Penalties in a verify block In each step of chain speculative decoding, the draft model proposes $K$ tokens $d_1, \dots, d_K$. The target model then runs once over $K + 1$ tokens: the anchor $a$ (the token sampled last in the previous step) followed by the drafts. Row 0 of the target's output predicts the token after $a$ and row $j$ the token after $d_j$. Verify accepts drafts from left to right while they agree with these rows, then samples a bonus token from the first row that disagrees, or from row $K$. Row $j$ is used only when $d_1, \dots, d_j$ are accepted, and then the output so far ends with $a, d_1, \dots, d_j$. So the penalties of row $j$ must count $d_1, \dots, d_j$ in addition to the earlier output and $a$: | Row | Predicts the token after | Output that its penalties count | |---|---|---| | 0 | $a$ | earlier output, $a$ | | 1 | $d_1$ | earlier output, $a$, $d_1$ | | $j$ | $d_j$ | earlier output, $a$, $d_1, \dots, d_j$ | For example, with the drafts "the cat sat", row 3 predicts the word after "sa

title: [Bug] HiCache backup of oversized request evicts all host-cached prefixes before giving up
summary: ## Summary When HiCache is enabled with a host pool smaller than the device pool (`--hicache-ratio 0.5`), `_execute_kv_backup` evicts all host-only evictable prefixes when a backup request exceeds the entire host pool. The eviction cannot make room because the pool is too small for the backup, so the function returns None after the damage is done. Other requests whose prefixes were evicted lose their L2 cache hits and must recompute. **What:** `_execute_kv_backup` calls `evict_host(needed)` without checking whether `needed` can ever fit the host pool capacity. **Where:** `unified_radix_cache.py:2283-2295`, function `_execute_kv_backup`. **Who/when:** Any client whose prompt backup exceeds the host pool, on a server where HiCache is enabled with `--hicache-ratio` less than 1.0 (e.g. 0.5). With the default configuration (neither `--hicache-ratio` nor `--hicache-size` set), [`hicache_auto_size.py:144`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/1f2d76c79d/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_auto_size.py#L144) computes `ratio = min(requested, budget*(1-slack)/device_bytes)` with no floor above zero; `all_reduce MIN` at lines 149-153 can shrink the ratio further across ranks. On a memory-tight host or cgroup the default config can therefore give a host pool smaller than one request's backup. Selective policy: an oversized prompt sent twice (the second hit triggers the backup attempt). Default write-through: a prompt that first pushes existing guards off device. **Expected:** Eviction only when it can make room. An oversized backup should be skipped without side effects. **Actual

title: [Perf] kimi-k3: Order shared-expert side-stream frees on the current stream
summary: ## Motivation Under `_sbo_shared_overlap`, `KimiK3MoE` runs the shared experts on `alt_stream` and releases their input and output with `record_stream`. A `record_stream` free completes only once the GPU reaches it, and in prefill the host runs many layers ahead, so every queued layer's shared-expert blocks stay reserved in the caching allocator. On Kimi-K3.1 prefill (GB300, shared experts TP4) this left about 6 GB per GPU reserved but unusable, and it kept growing over the first 10 minutes of load. ## Modifications - The CUDA overlap path no longer calls `record_stream` on the shared input or output. title: [Perf] diffusion: Quantize and LANCZOS-resize MiniMax-H3 image output on the GPU
summary: ## Motivation When a MiniMax-H3-Image request is smaller than `min_generation_area`, the DiT generates on a larger canvas (e.g. 2720x1536 for a 1344x768 request) and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` resizes the decoded image back with Pillow LANCZOS. It costs about 110 ms of a ~148 ms decode stage (the VAE decode itself is ~35 ms), i.e. ~16% of a C1 request, and nothing overlaps with it. summary: ## Motivation CI tests measure a lot (TTFT, throughput, GSM8K/MMMU accuracy, spec accept length, nightly one-batch benchmarks) but print it as text for people, each kit in its own shape, so tracking any number over time means one log parser per kit. summary: The DSA indexer host pool hard-codes `can_use_jit = False`, so its layer_first `load_to_device_per_layer` always runs the AOT `transfer_kv_per_layer_mla`, even though the MLA KV right next to it already goes through the JIT kernel. This sets `can_use_jit` from `can_use_hicache_jit_kernel` on the index page stride (each index page is one row for the transfer kernels) and calls `transfer_hicache_one_layer_mla` with `element_dim=indexer_page_stride_size` when the gate passes, AOT otherwise. No host sync, no allocator change. The per-layer indexer backup still uses the AOT call, I can switch it in a follow-up. title: [Perf] scheduler: Freeze the GC heap every N batches on a busy scheduler (default off)
summary: ## Motivation `GCFreezer` (#50883) freezes the scheduler heap only after the scheduler has been idle for `--gc-freeze-on-idle-secs`, and that freeze starts with a full collection. A PD prefill scheduler under sustained load is never idle, so its heap is never frozen. Every generation-2 collection then walks the whole long-lived heap and stalls the scheduler loop. Under pipeline parallelism, one stage's stall holds up the whole pipeline. ## Modifications - `--gc-freeze-after-batches N` (default `0`, off). Once the scheduler has launched N forward batches, `GCFreezer.on_batch` collects generations 0 and 1 and calls `gc.freeze()`. - `--gc-freeze-every-batches M` (default `0`). Also freezes every M batches the same way, so objects that became long-lived since are frozen too. - Full pass: frozen objects are never cycle-collected, so every N batches after the first freeze, a freeze unfreezes the heap and runs one full `gc.collect()` before freezing. This also happens with `M = 0`. - It bounds the cyclic garbage kept frozen, at the cost of one full-collection pause per N batches. N is therefore both the first-freeze point and the full-pass period, so a small N means frequent full pauses; the help says so. - It logs the number of unreachable objects it collected and its duration, and can trigger the `--gc-warning-threshold-secs` warning. - It does not use `refreeze_gc()`, which runs three full collections. - The schedule is a pure function of the batch count, so ranks that launch the same batches freeze and run full passes on the same batches. - Each rank counts its own launched ba

title: [Fix] pd: Release PP prefill transfers via PP0 decision once every stage concludes
summary: ## Motivation With a pipeline-parallel prefill server in PD disaggregation, every PP stage must release an inflight request at the same step. Main does this with a ring consensus over the PP group (#47045 made the concluded outcome agree across stages). #45085 (WIP, @stepinto) replaces the ring with a simpler scheme: PP0 reads every stage's transfer status through `PPConsensusStore` and forwards its decision. Taken alone, that scheme releases too early. PP0 decides from `min()` over the stage statuses, so a Failed on one stage releases the request on every stage while another stage is still Transferring; that stage then frees KV pages and the metadata slot its transfer worker still reads. The staging Success hold (outstanding staging chunks, worker cleanup under `prefill_complete`) is also local to each stage, so PP0 only applies its own. This PR carries #45085 rebased onto current main (authorship preserved; happy to rebase onto it if it lands first) and makes the PP0 decision wait for every stage. The abort-vs-error classification that was previously part of this PR is now a separate PR stacked on this one: #51720. ## Modifications - `[Refactor]` (from #45085, @stepinto): PP0 polls every stage's status via `PPConsensusStore` and forwards the decision, replacing the ring consensus. A transfer that failed on any stage stays Failed, keeping the behavior of #47045. title: [Perf] dsa: Avoid per-row CPU allocations in indexer TP split planning
summary: ## Motivation `Indexer._indexer_tp_split` is called by every participating DSA layer. Its host-only row partition currently materializes several tensors of length `q_offset` (including two repeat-interleaves and a cumulative sum) even for a single request. This fixed cost matters for short extends over cached context, and grows with the number of new query rows. This is independent of the short-extend threshold and logits kernel choices in #49870 and rank-local gather offsets in #51533. No split admission threshold, device kernel, collective, or attention layout is changed. ## Modifications - Accumulate the KV-length cost by request, instead of expanding every query row. Within a request that cost is an arithmetic series (with a flat head for the existing minimum-cost clamp). - Locate each target cost in the request prefix sums and invert the local cumulative cost using integer square root. This returns exactly the same right-side cut as the original per-row `searchsorted`; no floating-point rounding. - Preserve the uniform fallback for inconsistent length metadata and the original nonempty-rank clamping. title: [Fix] moe: Make biased top-k symbolic-shape safe
summary: The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic. For routing scores shaped `[T, E]` and a shared correction bias shaped `[E]`, the intended operation is: ```text [T, E] + [1, E] ``` The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic expert width: `correction_bias.view(-1, num_experts)` When `num_experts` is symbolic, Dynamo represents the inferred leading dimension as `correction_bias.numel() // num_experts`. Fake-tensor tracing cannot always prove that this expression is 1, causing a shape assertion or broadcasting failure before inference starts. This affects the generic PyTorch fallback and is not specific to a particular hardware backend. The same pattern exists in both `biased_topk_impl` and `biased_grouped_topk_impl`. The helpers also support per-token correction biases shaped `[T, E]`, so always reshaping the bias to `[1, E]` would not be correct. ## Modifications - Add a private _add_correction_bias helper that preserves both supported bias layouts: - Shared bias [E] is explicitly expanded to [1, E]. - Per-token bias [T, E] remains unchanged. - Use the helper in both biased_topk_impl and biased_grouped_topk_impl. - Add a CPU regression test that: - Marks the routing dimensions as unbacked. - Keeps the model correction-bias width static. - Compiles both helpers with backend="eager", dynamic=True, and fullgraph=True. - Compares compiled outputs against eager outputs, including expert IDs, weights, dtypes, and normalization. title: [Perf] linker: Load DSpark draft KV with the last transfer layers
summary: ## Motivation The direct linker maps sidecar draft depth `i` to transfer layer `i` (#48125). With grouped layer loads (#45106), all five M3.1 DSpark draft layers fall in the first layer group. Target layer 0 waits on that group before it can start. A draft deeper than the target's transfer layers is rejected. - The Mamba builder computes its layer count before adding the sidecar entries, and includes the sidecar depth in it. - New `UnifiedCacheLinker.draft_layer_counter()` returns an `OffsetLayerCounter`. title: [Fix] dsa: Align DP token counts to attention TP in cal_padded_tokens
summary: ## Motivation `cal_padded_tokens` predicts how many q rows DSA attention will see after `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`, and the FlashMLA metadata (`num_splits`) is sized from that count. It skips the first step of `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`: rounding each DP rank's token count up to `attn_tp_size`. When metadata is planned after MLP sync, the counts are already aligned, so nothing goes wrong. But the eager multi-step draft decode plans before MLP sync. With attn-DP 2 × attn-TP 4 and 5 / 4 draft requests, q is padded to 8 rows while the metadata is planned for 5, and FlashMLA fails with `num_splits must have shape (b+1)`. This can happen whenever draft decode runs eagerly, for example with the decode CUDA graph disabled (it fails in warmup) or on a rank with more requests than `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. Only `attn_tp_size > 1` is affected. On main, #48712 avoids the crash in the `flashmla_kv` and `trtllm` paths by trimming q to the planned rows. This PR fixes the planned count itself. Related: #30296. #30642 proposed the same alignment earlier; its branch has since diverged from main. ## Modifications - `cal_padded_tokens`: align each rank's count to `attn_tp_size` before choosing the padding mode and the row count, in the same order as `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`. Counts that are already aligned do not change. - Unit test in `test_dsa_backend_dp_padding.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Single node: GLM-5.3 W4AFP8, 8×H20, attn-DP 2 (attn-TP 4), EAGLE (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), FP8 KV (`flashmla_kv`). title: [Perf] scheduler: Send a finished request's last output before its prefix-cache insert and free its prompt ids after the next dispatch
summary: ## Motivation At the end of every streamed response, two pieces of host work that grow with the prompt length run between the request's last output token and the end of its response stream: 1. **Scheduler: the prefix-cache insert runs before the final chunk is sent.** `process_batch_result_decode` releases a request that finishes in the step (`request_retirer.release` -> `release_kv_cache`, which checkpoints the whole sequence into the radix tree) inside its per-request loop, and only then calls `stream_output`. So the final chunk of every response waits for the insert. 2. **TokenizerManager: the prompt's token-id list is freed before the stream ends.** A prompt given as token ids (the chat-completions path, `/generate` with `input_ids`, or a frontend that tokenizes itself) is a Python list holding one int object per token. Its last references are the request's generator frames, so it is freed when `generate_request` returns: after the final output was yielded, but before the caller ends its response. That costs about 10 ns per token. title: [Fix] moe: make FusedMoE out of place by default (dual-stream shared-expert race)
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51990. Many MoE blocks overlap the shared experts with the routed experts in decode CUDA graphs, using a second stream, and both branches read the MoE input. The triton MoE runner is in place by default (`FusedMoE(inplace=True)`, `MoeRunnerConfig.inplace = True`), so `fused_experts` writes the routed output over that input. Nothing orders the shared branch's read before that write. The audit in #51990 finds 17 model files exposed (DeepseekV2MoE and its users, the GLM-4 MoE blocks, Hunyuan-V3, Kimi-Linear, the Bailing MoE blocks, EXAONE-MoE, LLaDA2, MiniMax-M3, Sarvam-MoE, Llama 4, Nemotron-H). #31870 fixed only the LoRA wrapper; #10352 fixed only Qwen2-MoE. On DeepseekV2MoE, a probe measured 0.01-0.1% of graph replays racing (about 20% of the eager capture warm-up calls). A racy read takes the routed output as the shared experts' input. The values stay finite, so the race is silent. ## Modifications - `FusedMoE.__init__` and `MoeRunnerConfig` default `inplace` to `False`. In place becomes an opt-in, for callers whose input nothing else reads. - `DeepseekV2MoE` opts back in when it does not overlap the shared experts (`alt_stream is None` or fused shared experts). That keeps today's memory behaviour there, including deep_gemm's eager input disposal. - Callers that already pass `inplace` keep their choice (qwen2_moe, cohere2_moe, inkling, deepseek, dbrx, xverse_moe, afmoe). - New CPU test `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_fused_moe_inplace_default.py` asserts both defaults. title: perf(mamba): defer device free-list merging until allocation needs released slots
summary: ## Motivation `MambaSlotAllocator.free()` currently rebuilds the complete device free-list on every release: ```python self.free_slots = torch.cat((self.free_slots, free_index)) ``` The cost is proportional to the current free-list size, rather than the number of slots being released. During request turnover, releasing one request can therefore allocate and copy a large device tensor on the scheduler bookkeeping path. The host pool already uses a lazy free-list release design: record released chunks first, keep them in the available-size accounting, and merge them only when the primary free-list cannot satisfy an allocation. title: [Scheduler] Gate and batch request generation tracking for DSpark
summary: ## Motivation `req_generation` prevents DSpark's delayed confidence relay from associating confidence from an old request with a new request that reuses the same request-pool slot. However, it is currently incremented unconditionally for every newly allocated request, even though non-DSpark serving modes never consume it. Batched admission also performs one CPU Torch scalar operation per new request. This adds unnecessary overhead to the scheduler admission path of every request. ## Modifications - Make request-generation tracking opt-in in `ReqToTokenPool` and `DecodeReqToTokenPool`. - Enable tracking from `ModelRunner` only when the speculative algorithm is DSpark. - Keep the scalar update for single-request DSpark admission. - Use one vectorized operation for batched DSpark admission. - Share the generation-update implementation between the regular and disaggregated decode request pools. - Keep the `req_generation` tensor in every pool to preserve the existing request-pool interface. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not change model forward computation, sampling, or output tensors. Non-DSpark serving does not consume `req_generation`. For DSpark, tracking remains enabled and preserves the existing slot-reuse semantics. A randomized allocation/free/chunked-prefill trace produced identical generation states between the baseline and the updated DSpark path. A slot-reuse experiment also verified that delayed confidence is accepted for the same request generation and rejected after the slot is reassigned to a new request. title: [Bug] Dual-stream MoE blocks read the MoE input on one stream while the in-place triton runner overwrites it on the other
summary: ### Checklist - [x] Searched issues and PRs. Related, not duplicates: - #31870 fixed only the LoRA-wrapper half. - #25279 is the same overwrite in eager `forward_normal` only. - #29142 / #29463 / #30460 moved the routed experts to the main stream and issued them first. Their analysis was about `dispose_tensor` and stream explosion, not a data write. - #10344 / #10352 fixed the same race in Qwen2-MoE only. - #46461 is the same class of bug in HunyuanImage-3 (eager ordering). - #49881 / #46225 / #47013 are a different NaN path with the same symptom on GLM-5.3-Flash; this report reproduces with both fixes applied. - [x] Present in v0.5.23 and in main at 46a931ccf (2026-11-21). ### Describe the bug Many MoE blocks overlap the shared experts with the routed experts in decode CUDA graphs, using a second stream. Both branches read the MoE input `hidden_states`. The triton MoE runner is in place by default: - `FusedMoE(..., inplace: bool = True)` (`srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:356`; main `:399`) and `MoeRunnerConfig.inplace = True` (`moe_runner/base.py:57`). - `fused_experts` then sets `out_hidden_states = hidden_states` (`srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:619-620`). The routed branch therefore writes its sum over the tensor the shared branch is still reading, and nothing orders the read before the write: a write-after-read race across streams. A post-fork `hidden_states.clone()` on the reading stream does not help, because the clone is itself an unordered read.
