summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation On the Marlin path, `MuseSpark1xFp4Experts` picks `block_size_m` from the mean number of routes per local expert, `num_tokens * topk / num_local_experts`. Under EP this counts every route in the batch against this rank's experts; with 256 experts over EP8 the true mean per local expert is 8x smaller. At 128 tokens (topk 8, 32 local experts) the rule picks 48-row blocks, and at 256 tokens 64-row blocks. (hariappi noted the same overestimate in their Open Kernel Challenge repo.) Using the exact mean doesn't fix it, because routing is skewed: a few hot experts take most of a small batch's routes. At 128 tokens the exact mean selects 8-row blocks, so the hot experts run several blocks each and re-read their weights. What measured fastest on H200 is to keep the current rule and cap the result at 16 rows while the estimate is at most 64 routes per local expert. Prefill sizes are unaffected (753 and 16,384 tokens keep 64). Whole decoder layer on one H200 at TP8/EP8 sizes, with routing from the model (`muse_decode_layer` problem of the Muse Spark Open Kernel Challenge), against stock in the same run: | tokens | 8-row blocks (exact mean) | 16-row blocks (cap) | stock | |---|---|---|---| | 128 (16 users x 8 verify tokens) | 0.94-0.95x | 1.13-1.19x | 48-row blocks | | 256 (32 users x 8 verify tokens) | — | routed experts 1.32x | 64

title: [Feat] hicache: Forward request-scoped KV hints to storage backends
summary: ## Motivation #38891 added a versioned `kv_hints` envelope to generation requests. `GenerateReqInput` documents that it is "passed through untouched to the HiCache storage backends", but today it stops at `Req.kv_hints`: no storage backend can see it. This PR completes that path, so a HiCache storage backend can use an orchestrator's hint when it looks up and reads pages. For example, an orchestrator that routes a request to one worker can tell that worker's storage backend which of the request's blocks another worker has already published, so the backend can fetch those blocks instead of the worker recomputing them. The first consumer is the KVCR storage backend in #45647, which will be rebased onto this API. No in-tree backend uses hints yet, and the hook is opt-in, so nothing changes for existing backends. Hints are stated in terms of the block hashes that SGLang publishes in KV events. For requests isolated by `cache_salt` or by an `extra_key` such as a LoRA adapter, those event IDs differ from the HiCache storage keys. A backend cannot convert between them without reproducing the scheduler's hash chain, so this PR also gives the backend that mapping. ## Modifications A storage backend opts in by overriding `HiCacheStorage.consumes_kv_hints()` to return `True`. title: [Feature] Token-aware admission cap (--max-inflight-prefill-tokens)
summary: The admission knobs we have today (`--max-running-requests`, `--max-queued-requests`) are count-based. They can't tell a 4k prompt from a 500k one. So when a burst of long-context requests lands, the server admits them by count, over-commits prefill memory, and OOM-crashes instead of shedding. On a GLM-5.2-FP8 tp8/dp8 run, 8 concurrent 500k-token prompts take the whole server down (every request net-fails). This adds a token-aware bound: `--max-inflight-prefill-tokens N`. The tokenizer manager sits in front of the workers (one per server, before requests are dispatched to the DP ranks), so it's the right place to bound total work before anything is scheduled. A new request is rejected up front when the prompt tokens already in flight plus this request would exceed `N`. The one subtle part is the accounting. The charge is recorded on the request's `ReqState` inside `_validate_one_request`, which runs synchronously (no `await`), so the read of the in-flight total and the charge are atomic against other in-flight requests. That matters under a concurrent burst: if you compute the in-flight total lazily, 8 requests that arrive together all read an empty total and all get admitted (I hit exactly this and watched it still OOM). Charging synchronously fixes it. The charge is released for free when the request finishes and leaves `rid_to_state`, so there's no separate counter to leak on aborts or disconnects. Default is unset, which is a no-op: the `is not None` guard short-circuits, zero overhead. When set, the only added cost is an int sum over in-flight requests at admission tim

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Exchange K/V over device IPC instead of two NCCL all-gathers in 2-rank K/V-gather SP
summary: ## Motivation **What goes wrong** `USPAttention._forward_with_kv_gather` calls `_gather_sharded_sequence` twice per attention layer, once for K and once for V. Those two `all_gather_into_tensor` calls are the only collectives in a FLUX.2 denoising step, and they are slow out of proportion to the bytes they move: on a gfx1250 socket a 25 MB/rank all-gather takes 446 us, an effective 56 GB/s, while a device copy of the same bytes takes 9.8 us. In a 2-step FLUX.2 trace the 432 RCCL kernels account for 219 ms of 1183 ms of GPU time, 18.5% of the step, to move data between two ranks that already have peer access to each other's memory. **Where it shows up** Any two-rank K/V-gather SP group pays this, on any device where the collective is slower than a peer-to-peer copy, and for any model that takes that path -- it is a property of the SP mode, not of FLUX.2. It is most visible when the two ranks are partitions of one socket, because the collective is then moving bytes that never had to leave the device. It reproduces on FLUX.2-dev at 720p with `--num-gpus 2` (`sp_degree=2`, `kv_gather_degree=2`) on two gfx1250 partitions; a single-GPU run has no SP group and is unaffected. The fix below is gated to ROCm and off by default, so no other platform changes behavior. **How to fix** Exchange the bytes the way the hardware already allows, and use a collective only for the ordering it is actually needed for: each rank copies K and V into a staging buffer the peer has mapped over device IPC, a one-element `all_gather_into_tensor` orders the two streams, and each rank reads the peer's half

title: [Fix] attn-tp: Run prefill-graph replays unscattered
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-attn-tp-input-scattered` and TP > 1, prefill graph replay can feed unreduced embeddings into a graph captured with full embeddings. Capture calls `layer_model.forward` directly, outside `AttnTpContext.maybe_input_scattered`, so the captured body expects the unscattered layout. Replay calls the model's eager outer `forward`, which opens `maybe_input_scattered`. The eager `VocabParallelEmbedding.forward` then skips its all-reduce, and the vocab-shard partial sums are copied into the graph's static `input_embeds` slot. This requires all of the following: - The model calls `AttnTpContext.init_context` and `allow_input_scattered` is True. This excludes `speculative_algorithm == "EAGLE3"`. - Its forward opens `maybe_input_scattered` around an eager embedding that fills `input_embeds` from outside the graph. The slot is registered for `model_config.is_multimodal` models or an EAGLE3 breakable draft. - A breakable or full prefill graph is used. This is the default on CUDA, subject to the multimodal allowlist. From code inspection on `b2cc023f` and `21dae9b1`, only `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (GLM-5.3-Flash) meets all of these conditions. The GPU results below use a shrunk public config with seeded random weights. summary: ## Motivation `--enable-unified-memory` already supports PD disaggregation, but `handle_unified_memory_pool` rejects PD + speculative decoding over Mooncake (`kv_cache_hook.py`). Serving a hybrid-SWA target with a DFLASH draft (e.g. Muse-Spark-Open + DFlash2) under unified memory therefore cannot run disaggregated. Three things block it: 1. The unified arena is allocated with `torch.empty`/VMM, which multi-node NVLink Mooncake transfers cannot register; every KV transfer fails (`KVTransferError`) unless the arena comes from Mooncake's custom memory pool. 2. A DFLASH draft whose layers are all sliding-window is still placed on the full-length band, costing capacity it never reads. 3. The Mooncake send path builds a Python list per contiguous run (`group_concurrent_contiguous`). Unified-memory pages are rarely contiguous, so every send allocates one small list per page; at production concurrency this drives frequent full GC passes on the prefill scheduler. This addresses the roadmap item "Support PD disaggregation with speculative decoding" in #49944. ## Modifications - `arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`: admit unified memory + PD + speculative decoding over Mooncake **for DFLASH on CUDA only**; other algorithms and platforms keep the existing refusal. - `mem_cache/kv/memory/arena.py`: on CUDA, when `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL` selects a pool, allocate the arena from that pool so Mooncake can register it. title: [Perf] [H20] fp8-gemm: Take the swapAB kernel for small-M block FP8 GEMM on H20
summary: ## Motivation On SM90, `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` resolves to plain DeepGEMM (`_dispatch_auto_backend` → `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`). DeepGEMM's default kernel is shaped for large M, but in decode the M dimension *is* the batch size: every decode step runs 60+ block-FP8 GEMMs with `1 <= M <= 32`, and that kernel leaves most of its tile empty at those sizes. Whether that empty tile **costs** anything depends on how much compute the part has per byte of weights it streams, and on H20 it costs a lot. H20 is Hopper silicon cut down to 78 SMs against 132 on H100/H200, so it has roughly a third of their compute while giving up only ~15% of their bandwidth. Narrow-M block-FP8 GEMM on H20 is therefore compute-bound: the redundant MMA work, not the ~27 GB weight stream, is what sets the inter-token time. That is the part this PR targets, and the measurement below shows the effect is absent on an H200 — so the change is scoped to H20 rather than to SM90 as a whole. `flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` is one entry point over **two** DeepGEMM kernels — `fp8_gemm_kernel_swapAB` for `M < 32` and `fp8_gemm_kernel` above it. #32843 already confined `flashinfer_deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` to exactly the `1 <= M < 32` band and delegates every other M (including `M == 0` on idle ranks) back to DeepGEMM, so that callable is a strict superset of what `auto` selects today. It is reachable only by naming `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` explicitly, which leaves the single-request decode of a mainstream FP8 model at roughly 60% of what it reaches

title: [Feat] [PPU] monokernels: Add the T-Head SAIL monokernel backend
summary: ## Motivation We want PPU to run mega kernels too, starting with Qwen3.8-Flash. The goal is that, over time, more models run on mega kernels on PPU and get the performance they should. Today each vendor wires up its mega kernel on its own. NVIDIA has its own binding, AMD's monokernel lives inside its vendor module, and there is no shared entry point. Adding PPU would mean a third copy, or having PPU import someone else's module, and neither belongs in main. So this PR lifts the common monokernel runtime into a vendor-neutral module. PPU only adds its own binding and the `--enable-t-head-monokernel` flag, and the `sgl-t-head-mega` plugin then registers, gets selected, and gets validated the same way as the other backends. It also adds a guard so that two mega kernel backends selected at once fail at startup instead of letting import order decide. title: [Fix] spec: DSpark simulated acceptance draws the stop-row bonus from the rejection residual (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation Benchmarks pin speculative acceptance with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected` and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token`. Under these settings, DSpark commits: - the sampled draft chain at the forced positions; - one bonus token at the stop row. That bonus is currently a plain draw from the target distribution p. A real rejection at that row would resample from the residual max(p − q, 0), which excludes the draft's proposal at its draft probability. With the plain draw, the stop token can re-pick exactly what the draft proposed. On long generations the committed text then collapses into short repeated phrases. summary: ## Summary Enable SGLang's public JIT backend to compile and load kernels on MUSA with `mcc`, while delegating generic CUDA-to-MUSA runtime aliases to Torchada's `cuda_compat` headers. title: [Perf] [AMD] kimi-k3.1: Run decode GEMMs from a per-M kernel table and merge the MLA input projections
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1's TP8 DFLASH verify runs every dense GEMM at M = 5 × graph batch size, where hipBLASLt's heuristic and AITER's padded-M rows pick kernels by shape class, not by the exact M. Separately, q_a + kv_a, the output gate and the DSA indexer's [wk | weights_proj] all read the MLA input but run as three GEMMs. Follow-up to #51000. ## Modifications - **Exact-M decode GEMM table.** A bf16 GEMM whose exact (M, N, K, output dtype) has a row in `SGLANG_ROCM_DECODE_GEMM_TABLE` runs that row's hipBLASLt solution or FlyDSL tile (`unquant_hip.decode_gemm`); every other shape keeps its route. Kimi-K3.1's gfx950 defaults point it at a 149-row MI355X TP8 table for verify M = 360-800, on servers that verify drafts (a speculative algorithm, not the prefill role). - **Preload.** The table's kernels are loaded at model load, before the KV cache is sized, which costs 8.2% of the KV tokens per rank in the run below. The table only changes which kernel runs a GEMM and the front merges GEMMs over the same input, so outputs differ by float rounding. | Check | Result | |---|---| | 149 table rows against an fp32 reference, 8 GPUs, random bf16 inputs | 149 of 149 rows usable; max relative error 1.1e-2 with the table, 6.

title: [Fix] logging: Bound token-ID decoding in partial request logs
summary: ## Problem With `--log-requests-level 2` (the default), native token-ID requests still decode every input token after the received record is formatted, and batched requests decode every row (`python/sglang/srt/observability/request_logger.py`, `log_received_request`). The decoded result is then assigned back to the real request's `text`, so enabling logging mutates the object later used by tokenization and multimodal processing. title: [Fix] speculative: Prune quantized lm_head rows for --speculative-token-map
summary: ## Motivation `--speculative-token-map` crashes at startup when the target `lm_head` is quantized. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` prunes the shared head with `head.data[self.hot_token_id]`, which assumes a dense `[vocab, hidden]` weight. A per-channel FP8 `lm_head` (compressed-tensors W8A8, e.g. `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4-Fast`) is stored as `[hidden, vocab]` column-major with a `[vocab, 1]` `weight_scale`, so the slice indexes the hidden dim with vocab ids. Even when the indexing happens to be in range, the draft would get an FP8 weight without its scale or quant method. Repro on `main` (1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4-Fast \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-token-map hot_24576.pt --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 ``` ``` File ".../speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 422, in init_lm_head head.data = head.data[self.hot_token_id] torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.68 GiB. ``` On v0.5.22, with more free memory, the same line raised a device-side index assert instead. ## Modifications - `spec_utils.prune_quantized_lm_head`: returns a copy of the target `lm_head` restricted to the hot rows. It selects the vocab dim of the weight (the dim that is not `hidden_size`) and of a per-channel `weight_scale`, keeps the original weight layout, quant method and `logical_widths`, and leaves the target module untouched. title: SGLang: max_new_tokens and n have no server-side upper bounds, so one request can monopolize the scheduler
summary: We previously submitted a private GitHub Security Advisory for this issue: [GHSA-74p5-rgj8-w57v](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/security/advisories/GHSA-74p5-rgj8-w57v). Please review the private advisory. ## Summary Two generation parameters are unbounded on the server side: `sampling_params.max_new_tokens` (capped only by the model context length, which is a functional limit, not a safety limit; `SGLANG_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_LIMIT` defaults to None) and `sampling_params.n` (no cap at all). We verified end to end that a single unauthenticated request can expand into thousands of scheduled sub-requests and that generation-budget attacks slow other users' requests by 7.4 times.

title: SGLang: stop_regex is evaluated on the scheduler thread, so a crafted regex blocks all decoding for minutes
summary: We previously submitted a private GitHub Security Advisory for this issue: [GHSA-m7xv-579r-jpwr](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/security/advisories/GHSA-m7xv-579r-jpwr). Please review the private advisory. ## Summary The `stop_regex` request parameter is matched with Python's `re` module on the scheduler's main thread during decoding. A regex with catastrophic backtracking blocks the scheduler and stops all request processing. We verified end to end that a single unauthenticated request with the regex `(?:[^b]+)+b` stopped all decode batches for 8 minutes and 25 seconds on a default deployment.

title: [Fix] mem_cache: charge PD decode pre-allocated slots in the mamba memory budget
summary: Fixes #48837 ## Motivation On PD-disaggregation **decode** servers for hybrid mamba models (GLM-5.3-Flash + EAGLE), the profiled mamba budget in `_handle_max_mamba_cache` charges `K+1` main slots and `(K+1) * draft_tokens` intermediate entries, while the decode pools actually allocate `(size + disaggregation_decode_extra_slots) * slots_per_req` main slots and `(size + pre_alloc + 1) * draft_tokens` intermediate entries (the `extra_slots` flag auto-defaults to `per_worker * 2` when `per_worker <= 32`). The inflated remaining budget oversizes the KV pool and startup dies with a CUDA OOM while building the pools. title: [Feat] diffusion: Add expert parallelism for MoE DiTs
summary: ## Motivation MoE DiTs are growing, and SP shards activations but not experts: every rank still stores all routed experts. This PR adds expert parallelism (EP) to SGLang Diffusion, with LingBot-Video MoE (128 routed experts) as the first supported model. On 2×H100, EP2 cuts peak memory by 26.2 GB/GPU (43%) for 12% more latency. ## Modifications Two commits: 1. **Fix LingBot SP.** LingBot under SP produced wrong output before this PR (RoPE positions restarted at zero on every rank, and replicated text was gathered as distinct shards). It now shards video tokens inside the DiT, slices global RoPE positions per rank, and passes text as `num_replicated_suffix`. 81 frames are no longer rounded to 85. EP depends on this. 2. **Add EP.** `--ep-size`, a per-pipeline capability gate, expert-sharded checkpoint loading, and a fixed-capacity dispatcher. **Design decision: EP reuses the SP group (`ep_size == sp_degree`).** SP already gives every rank the same token count, so dispatch is one equal-split all-to-all with static shapes and no host sync. Non-local routes carry a `-1` expert ID and are masked; partials are reduced in FP32 by the existing `moe_fused_mul_sum`. | Alternative considered | Result | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | Replicated tokens (no SP) | 1711 vs 1245 ms/step | Keep SP; replication duplicates attention | | Variable-split Torch dispatcher | 1133 vs 1051 ms/step, ~20× more variance | Fixed capacity; no per-block host sync | | Eager / compiled reducer | 3.64 / 1.07 vs 0.211 ms | Reuse `moe_fused_mul_sum` | ## Scope and scaling - Qualified: EP2/SP2, single-node CUDA

title: [Fix] gemma4: Reject malformed vision features before scheduling
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51828. Refs #26751 and #51822. A Gemma 4 request with grayscale/RGBA patch width, missing positions, or incompatible position shapes currently reaches ViT and can terminate the scheduler along with unrelated requests. Normalizing JPEG decoding removes one trigger, but does not contain malformed processor outputs from other paths. ## Changes Reject these recoverable input-shape failures at the request receiver, before batching or entering vision collectives: - Check image/video patch width against `3 * patch_size**2` and validate the corresponding position tensor shapes. PP relays the failure marker before scheduling. - Inspect CUDA IPC/VMM shape metadata without reconstructing features just for validation, and release rejected transport proxies before replacing the payload with its failure marker. The new logic is restricted to Gemma 4 multimodal admission. Text-only requests and other models retain their existing gating. This prevents input-shape errors before execution; it does not catch arbitrary encoder/kernel exceptions or attempt recovery from a corrupted CUDA context. #36724 addresses malformed encoder outputs at a different stage. title: [Fix] spec: Run an auto-dtype draft model in the target's dtype
summary: - With `--dtype auto`, a draft model resolved its dtype from its own checkpoint config. title: [Fix] pd: Wait for the forward before transferring intermediate PP prefill chunks
summary: ## Motivation With PP in PD disaggregation, the schedule stream may only wait for the launched forward's shared reads (the read-done fast path, e.g. `trtllm_mha` extend), not for its KV writes. Without overlap, the PP prefill loop sends the previous chunk of a chunked request from `process_prefill_chunk` while the forward that computes that chunk can still be running, so the KV transfer can read KV that is not written yet. The early cached-prefix send has the same gap under PP, since it only records a forward event under overlap. Affected: PD prefill with `--pp-size > 1`, multi-chunk requests, and an attention backend that publishes read-done. Backends that do not publish read-done are unaffected. ## Modifications - `disaggregation/prefill.py`: add `_wait_enqueued_forwards_before_send`, which records an event on the forward stream into the sender's `_early_send_wait_event`, the mechanism the early cached-prefix send already uses under overlap. The transfer worker waits on it before reading source KV, so the scheduler thread does not block. It is used for every intermediate-chunk send under PP and for the early cached-prefix send under PP as well as overlap. summary: ## Motivation Sol-Attn is block-sparse attention that recovers the skipped KV blocks from pooled (mean) K and V under the same softmax, so a skipped block costs its higher-order terms instead of all of its mass. title: [Feature] Add per-request skip_detokenize option to sglang.api.v1.GenerateRequest
summary: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation In `rust/sglang-server`, `--skip-tokenizer-init` controls server detokenization globally at startup (`DetokenizerBackend::Skip` vs `Dynamo`). On a standard pool, `sglang.api.v1.SglangService/Generate` detokenizes every output chunk into `text` alongside `output_ids`. Token clients consume `output_ids` only, so server detokenization wastes CPU for them. Conversely, a `--skip-tokenizer-init` pool cannot serve text-output requests, which forces operators to maintain separate worker pools. Even on dedicated token-output pools, `--skip-tokenizer-init` disables scheduler features that depend on the vocabulary. Without a loaded tokenizer, the scheduler leaves `grammar_backend` unset and aborts `json_schema`, `regex`, `ebnf`, and `structural_tag` requests with `400`. title: [Fix] model_loader: Split checkpoint prefetch among each node's own ranks
summary: ## Motivation `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` splits the checkpoint's shards among a node's ranks, so that the node reads each shard once and the ranks' mmap loads hit the page cache. On multiple nodes, the split is wrong: - The split strides by `world_group.local_size or launch_world_size`. - On GPU, `LOCAL_SIZE` is never set, so the stride is the whole world size (`tp * pp`), while the offset `local_rank` is the GPU index. - With 4 nodes of 4 GPUs, every node prefetches the shards whose index `i` satisfies `i % 16 < 4`: the same quarter on every node. - The other three quarters are never prefetched on any node and are read through page faults during loading. ## Modifications The split now uses the number of ranks per node, `launch_world_size // nnodes` when `LOCAL_SIZE` is unset, and this rank's position on its node, `rank % ranks_per_node`. Ranks are numbered node by node. No option is added. Prefetch itself stays opt-in; #50342 (on by default) and #37806 (automatic on network filesystems) propose enabling it, and either would hit this bug on every multi-node run. ## Accuracy Tests Prefetch never changes which weights are loaded. title: [Fix] dsv41: Build MegaGate row masks inside the decoder replay-tail graph capture
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51478. With MegaGate on and EPLB off, the decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs inside a serving forward, after two eager warm-ups of the same layers on a copy of the same batch. The per-forward row-mask cache from #46071 hands the warm-ups' eager masks to the capture, so the mask build is never recorded in the graph. Every replay then reads a valid-row mask computed for the step that captured the graph. Real rows past that count are routed as padding in the tail layers, and prompts whose tail runs from a graph (≤ 2048 tokens here) drift. ## Modifications - `layers/moe/mega_gate.py::_gate_row_masks`: the cache key gains `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`. A capture builds its own masks inside the graph, and the layers it captures still share them; eager forwards behave as before. The query runs only when the per-forward cache is active. - `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`: a CPU test that runs an eager build and a capturing build in one forward scope and checks that the capture does not reuse the eager mask. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on 2× GB300, upstream `34dfaccc57` (the code path is unchanged on current `main`); config and method in #51478. Top-1 agreement with a MegaGate-off reference over 50 real text prompts, at positions where the reference's top-1 margin is above 1 nat: | arm | all prompts | ≤ 2048 tokens | > 2048 tokens | |---|---:|---:|---:| | MegaGate on, 3 independent boots | 96.64% / 96.77% / 96.78% | 69.7% | 99.4% | | MegaGate on + fix | 99.41% | 99.3% |

title: [Feat] [AMD] linear-attn: Add FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
summary: ## Motivation AITER ships fused FlyDSL implementations of the GDN prepare stages and the K5 state scan for AMD gfx95. Qwen3.5-397B has 45 Gated DeltaNet layers, and at TP4 each rank runs them with 4 key heads, 16 value heads and K=V=128. On those shapes the FlyDSL path runs a prefill batch 1.4-1.74x faster than SGLang's Triton GDN prefill. This PR exposes that path as an opt-in prefill backend: ```bash --linear-attn-prefill-backend flydsl ``` Decode and speculative verification stay on Triton. The backend requires gfx95 and is rejected with deterministic inference or multi-item scoring. It also serves batches that track Mamba state for the radix cache, so it stays active with radix cache on (e.g. AgentX). It falls back to Triton for unsupported input/state shapes, mixed batches, and graph-planned paths. ## Modifications - Register `flydsl` in the linear-attention backend enum and CLI choices. - Add `FlyDSLGDNKernel`, which runs AITER's FlyDSL prepare, FlyDSL K5 state scan, and output stages. - Calls the stages directly instead of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk`, which only returns `(o, final_state)`. title: [HiCache] Do not shrink full L3 prefetch hits to available host capacity
summary: ## Motivation In cache mode, a full L3 storage hit can currently be silently shortened to the L2 host pool's currently available capacity. The store reports a complete prefix, but the request later sees only a partial storage hit. For example, a controlled Qwen3-4B / H20 run reported `16010 / 16010` pages from Mooncake `batch_exists()`, but the L2 allocator could only stage 2,551 tokens. The old fallback allocated that shorter prefix and returned `cached_tokens=2551`, making the result look like a partial L3 hit even though the L3 objects were complete. ## Modifications - Remove the cache-mode fallback that allocates a shorter page-aligned prefix when the full L3 hit cannot be staged in L2. - Keep the existing `host_capacity` path: finish the prefetch with zero fulfilled tokens, revoke it, and expose the deferred/unfulfilled metrics. - Add a CPU regression proving that a complete storage hit is not shortened to the available host capacity and does not enter the transfer queue. This is intentionally a correctness fix, not a full-restore optimization. A later optimization can reclaim host values only after their L3 copies are confirmed, or defer the full staging until capacity is available. ## Accuracy Tests Model accuracy evaluation is not applicable because model computation is unchanged. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py` — 9 passed. - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py` — 17 passed, 1 existing skip. - `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k storage` — 41 passed, 24 existing skips. - Controlled Moo

title: [Feat] scheduler: Keep a reserve of KV and state slots for cached prefixes (--prefill-cache-reserve)
summary: ## Motivation On multi-turn agent traffic the prefix cache collapses once the sessions' contexts no longer fit next to the running requests. GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2x B200 (TP2, the 0.9 split that was its default before #50018: 2,969,600 KV tokens, 419 state slots) with coding-agent sessions of about 75K tokens, `lru`: the hit rate is 0.91 at 16 sessions, 0.43 at 40 and 0 at 64. At 64 sessions 58 running requests hold 98% of the KV pool. A session that steps out for a tool call leaves its KV evictable, the next prefill takes it, and the session comes back to a full recompute. The extra prefill keeps decode waiting, so requests hold their KV longer and the next round loses more. The eviction order can't fix this: on the same setup (runs on #49430's branch, where `lru` is main's policy and the policy was still called `gds`; #49430 was reverted in #50118 and is now the opt-in `state_cost` in #50122) `lru` and `gds` both had a 0 hit rate at 64 sessions, since almost nothing is left to choose from. `--enable-session-radix-cache` (#29173) only evicts unreferenced KV first; with every session still open all of it is referenced, so I did not expect it to help and did not measure it. Admission can: a request that reuses little of the cache should wait for running requests to finish rather than take the room other sessions are about to come back to. This adds `--prefill-cache-reserve R` (off by default). summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation RFC #39963: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, layers 21-39 own only a 128-token SWA window, so a PD prefill server needs only layers 0-19 plus the KV producers of layer 20 (the boundary `kv_source`). This implements the RFC's split, the same semantics TRT-LLM shipped in NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19727: prefill stops `128` tokens short of the prompt end, and decode runs those last tokens as an ordinary extend. title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Raise the small MoE sort's pair limit from 256 to 1024
summary: ## Motivation The small MoE sort (#36559, #44004, #42498) is limited to 256 (token, expert) pairs, so it turns off at 32 decode tokens with top 8. Speculative decoding reaches that limit quickly. A DFLASH verify step has 8 tokens per request, so at top 8 it covers only 4 requests (256 pairs); 8 requests need 512 pairs and 16 requests 1024. Past the limit every MoE layer goes back to aiter's two-kernel sort followed by a separate stage-1 quant launch. The 256 limit was set in #36559 without a stated reason, and #41900/#44004 benchmarked only up to 256 pairs. Measured above it, the sort is still faster than aiter's sort plus quant at every point up to 1024 pairs, and slower from 1536 on (tables below). This PR raises the limit to 1024. On one MI355X, the MoE layer gets 2 to 5 % faster between 257 and about 900 pairs, and is unchanged at and above 1024. In serving MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL with DFLASH, throughput rises 1.3 % with 8 concurrent requests and is unchanged with 16 (same-node A/B below). Why the crossover sits there: the sort (the bitonic kernel from #44004, with #42498's fused quant) runs in one CTA over `next_pow2(pairs)` lanes, so its time steps up at each power of two: 5.3 us up to 256 pairs, 7.3 to 7.6 us up to 512, and 10 us up to 1024. At 1536 pairs it pads to 2048 lanes and takes 18 us. aiter's sort plus quant grows only from 9.5 to 11.7 us between 256 and 1024 pairs (masked, block 32). title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Support the EP expert mask in the small MoE sort
summary: ## Motivation Under expert parallelism, every decode step hands the MoE sort and the stage-1 MXFP8 quant back to aiter, because the small MoE sort turns itself off whenever aiter passes an expert mask, and EP always passes one. In detail: #44004 and #42498 replace aiter's MoE sort and the separate stage-1 MXFP8 quant with one small Triton launch, but `_small_sort_supported` returns False when `expert_mask` is set. title: [Feat] model-loader: Add model-aware checkpoint shard selection for Qwen MTP
summary: ## Motivation Closes #43196. A main model and its MTP draft can share a checkpoint while requiring different weights. Existing model implementations usually filter unused tensors inside `load_weights`, after the Default Loader iterator or prefetcher has started processing files. On whole-file paths, an unnecessary shard may already have been read into memory before the model discards its tensors. Following [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152), this PR extracts existing model-owned selection rules into a reusable interface and excludes wholly unused shards before weight-payload reads and prefetch. This avoids unnecessary reads, memory copies, and tensor iteration. The same need arose in [ModelExpress #805](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/issues/805). Keeping the rules in SGLang lets native loaders and downstream integrations share one implementation, instead of requiring MX to duplicate architecture-specific checkpoint naming rules and keep them synchronized with upstream changes. ## Modifications 1. **Model-owned weight selection.** Add an optional `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` hook. It receives a raw checkpoint tensor name and returns `True` when the model does not use that weight. Pre-read selection and `load_weights` share the same rule, preserving shared weights and pipeline-parallel embedding requirements. 2. **Select files before Default Loader reads.** Pass the rule through `Source.is_unused_weight`, inspect safetensors headers, and retain a shard whenever it contains at least one required tensor. title: [Perf] scheduler: Add SGLANG_DISABLE_THP to turn off transparent huge pages
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With transparent huge pages (THP) on, two kernel paths can stop a thread for a long time: - The first write into an eligible region allocates and zeroes a whole huge page in the faulting thread. - khugepaged collapses small pages into huge ones while it holds the process's mmap lock for writing. Every page fault in the process waits behind it. On kernels with 64K base pages, as on Arm servers such as NVIDIA Vera, a PMD huge page is 512 MB, so either path takes tens of milliseconds. With DP attention, every rank then waits at the next gather. We hit this in decode schedulers serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PD disaggregation on Vera Rubin. Decode ran on 32 attention-DP ranks, on a 64K-page 7.0 kernel with THP `enabled=madvise`, `defrag=madvise`. - Every decode scheduler held four 1 GB `MAP_NORESERVE` anonymous regions marked `MADV_HUGEPAGE`, from a native allocator in the process that we did not identify. Each rank had 0.5-2.5 GB of `AnonHugePages`, growing during the run. - A stack sampler caught scheduler main threads asleep ~30 ms in `lock_mm_and_find_vma`, i.e. a page fault waiting on the mmap lock. - All 32 ranks then waited at the next gather: 10-13 all-rank stalls of ~57 ms per minute. The kernel setting is the system-wide fix, but it needs root and also changes every other process on the node. `prctl(PR_SET_THP_DISABLE)` is per process, needs no privileges, and also covers regions marked `MADV_HUGEPAGE`. ## Modifications - New `SGLANG_DISABLE_THP` (default `false`). summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation `AuxDataCodec.deserialize_data_to_buffer` writes aux data received over TCP into the aux buffer with `(c_byte * n).from_address(dst)[:] = data`. A ctypes slice assignment converts every byte to a Python int and holds the GIL for the whole copy. In a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash PD deployment, the decode thread of the KV receiver held the GIL for 45-57 ms about twice a minute. The deployment used DP attention with 32 decode ranks, and Mooncake with its custom NVLink memory pool, so aux data arrives over TCP. The scheduler thread on that rank waited for the GIL, and every DP rank waited for it at the next step's sync. title: [Fix] weight-update: Keep fused-pair halves across chunked weight-update calls
summary: Addresses #51430. Supersedes #51419 and #38298; their authors are co-authors. - DeepSeek-family fused pairs (`q_a_proj` + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`; the block-fp8 indexer `wk` and `weights_proj` weight + scale into `wk_weights_proj`) were held in locals of one `load_weights` call, so in a chunked session (`update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_distributed`, `plugin_weight_update`) a pair split across two chunks lost its first half and the fused parameter silently kept its old values. title: [Feat] linker: support pipeline parallelism in layer-wise mode
summary: This is the third of three PRs split from sgl-project/sglang#38658. It targets `sgl-project/sglang:main` and depends on the external linker PP prefetch PR (part 2). While part 2 is pending, the Files changed tab includes both sets of changes. To review only the layer-wise changes, open commit `c902f023e0a` in the Commits tab. ## Summary Enable `load_mode=layer_wise` under pipeline parallelism. The ticket establishes a common restore boundary before prefill admission, including when one stage already has the prefix in its device cache and another must read it from storage. `match` and `load_back` consume the ticket’s reservation. `PrefillAdder` charges only for the KV and state slots the request still needs. When reads finish, ranks vote on success per request row. Failed request IDs travel through the existing PP forward and output paths so every stage retires the same failed requests while unaffected rows continue. For chunked prefill, the scheduler holds the chunk until the result is known. Disaggregated prefill also waits before sending that chunk’s KV to decode. ## Testing - 407 tests and 368 subtests passed across 18 test files on a pod with two H20-3e GPUs, including two-rank Gloo tests. - Covered asymmetric device-cache hits, reservation accounting during admission, per-row load failures, chunk retirement, and disaggregated prefill. - `pre-commit run --all-files` passed. - DeepSeek-V4-Flash HTTP end-to-end testing is pending on this branch. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contri

title: [Feat] linker: support pipeline parallelism in prefetch mode
summary: This is the second of three PRs split from sgl-project/sglang#38658. It targets `sgl-project/sglang:main` and can be merged independently of the PP flush fix. ## Summary Enable `load_mode=prefetch` under pipeline parallelism. The linker reuses HiCache’s request-arrival hook and `pp_prefetch_ticketed` marker. PP0 issues tickets in arrival order, and each stage binds the ticket to its local request. The linker manages its own reservations, reads, and publication. Each rank queries its local backend and reserves destination space. It marks the page boundaries that its backend can restore and its reservation can hold. A single PP `MIN` all-reduce intersects these masks and selects the longest prefix every rank can restore. This combines hit and allocation agreement in one vote, including when ranks report different hit lengths or one rank runs out of space. Read completion uses a separate acknowledgement. Once every rank confirms success, the linker publishes KV into the radix tree before admission. Failed or cancelled reads release their private slots after outstanding writes finish. ## Testing - 185 tests and 135 subtests passed across five test files on an H20-3e pod, including two-rank Gloo tests. - Covered unequal hit lengths, insufficient reservation capacity, delayed followers, failed reads, cancellation, and recovery. - `pre-commit run --all-files` passed. - DeepSeek-V4-Flash HTTP end-to-end testing is pending on this branch. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#

title: [Perf] [AMD] batch-invariant: Faster small-M launch for the segmented bf16 matmul on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode on gfx950, bf16 linear layers run through the segmented batch-invariant matmul (#45599). At decode batch sizes (M up to 64) its launch uses narrow 64-column tiles with 2 pipeline stages, and its final reduction (the step that adds the K segments) uses 4,096-element blocks. At these sizes that leaves much of an MI350X idle, and decode GEMMs are still one of the largest costs of deterministic mode. This PR tunes only the launch for M <= 64: 128-column tiles with 3 stages, and 1,024-element reduction blocks. Launch parameters cannot change the result: the K segments and the order in which they are added are fixed, so every launch gives the same bits. **Impact** - Deterministic-mode throughput on MI350X, 1k/1k, single request: Qwen3-8B +9.9% (TP1) and +10.5% (TP4), phi-4 +9.3%, Qwen3.8-27B +6.3%. At concurrency 16-64: +1.4% to +10.8% (tables below). - Outputs are bitwise the same as before this PR: the same tokens and log-probabilities. - Only `--enable-deterministic-inference` on gfx950 with bf16 linears at M <= 64 and N >= 1,024 changes. Normal mode, other GPUs, larger M and N < 1,024 are unchanged. ## Modifications - `batch_invariant_ops.py`, `_segmented_matmul_launch(M, N)`, for every N >= 1,024: - M <= 32: 32 x 128 tiles, 4 warps, 3 stages (was 32 x 64, 4 warps, 2 stages); - M <= 64: 64 x 128 tiles, 8 warps, 3 stages (was 64 x 64, 4 warps, 2 stages). Chosen from 10 candidate launches timed on MI350X over 22 bf16 linear shapes (Qwen3-8B, phi-4, Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, gpt-oss-20b, Llama 3.1 8B, a 24B Mistral model and the Qwen3-8B LM

title: [Bug] Gemma 4 Triton image masks make full-attention layers bidirectional
summary: ### Describe the bug On current main (`d215bb3b8c`), Gemma 4 image prefill with the Triton attention backend passes the same bidirectional image mask to both sliding-window and full-attention decoder layers. Full-attention image rows can consequently attend to future image tokens. Gemma 4 requires causal full attention; only sliding-window layers receive the same-image bidirectional overlay. This is also explicit in Transformers 5.19.0's `create_masks_for_vision_model` in `transformers/models/gemma4/modeling_gemma4.py`. ### Reproduction CPU metadata/dispatch replay (no model weights required): 1. Construct a two-request EXTEND batch, each with seven image tokens at offsets `(0, 6)`. 2. Call `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.prepare_attn_masks` with `use_bidirectional_attention="vision"` and a Triton backend. 3. Dispatch `TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend` for sliding, full, and sliding layers, recording the mask at the attention-kernel boundary. Repeat with deterministic inference enabled. Both Triton paths pass the all-true 7x7 image mask to the full layer. Expected: full layers get no custom mask and use causal attention; sliding layers retain the image mask. With zero attention scores and values `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]`, the erroneous full-layer first-row average is 3 instead of 0. The regression and a fix are being submitted together. This is a CPU mask/dispatch regression, not a full-model accuracy measurement. ### Scope The earlier PR #32303 identified the same layer-scoping problem and was closed without merging. title: [RFC] Prefill sequence parallelism with replicated MoE for small-TP long-prompt prefill (Qwen3.5 MoE)
summary: > **Revised 2026-10-13.** The first version proposed context-parallel prefill (contiguous token sharding with an affine GDN state hand-off). Measurements, summarized below, show that at small TP the gain comes from **replicating the MoE and running prefill sequence-parallel**, not from CP. CP is dropped. Implementation: #44034. ## TL;DR For long-prompt prefill on a small TP group (e.g. TP2), add `--moe-replicate-tp`: - every rank holds all experts; - a prefill keeps each rank's tokens through the MoE, which then needs no collective; - attention and linear attention keep their TP heads, with an all-gather in and a reduce-scatter out. On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 2×B200, 60K-token prompts, TTFT goes from **420 to 384 ms (−8.6%)** on main, with GSM8K unchanged. The cost is full expert memory per GPU and slower decode, so the flag targets prefill instances. ## 1. Where TP prefill time goes (first principles) Per layer, TP prefill does two all-reduces of `[L, hidden]`: after attention or GDN, and after the MoE. At 60K tokens on TP2 they cost ~45 ms of pure transfer. Pairing the NCCL kernels of both ranks shows only 5–10 ms of that is skew. A sparse MoE with small active parameters (A3B) has little compute per token, so this communication is a large share of the prefill. To remove a collective, a layer must either keep the tokens on their rank or replicate the weights: | strategy | attention / GDN | MoE | collectives per layer | |---|---|---|---| | TP | TP heads | TP experts | 2 all-reduce | | collocated CP (#39062) | CP (K/V gather) | TP experts: all-gather + reduce-scatter | ≈ 2 all-red

title: [Feature] --moe-replicate-tp: replicated MoE with prefill sequence parallelism (Qwen3.5 MoE)
summary: ## Motivation Implements the design in #43820 (revised). For long-prompt prefill on a small TP group, TP pays two costs that grow with the prompt and do not shrink with the TP size: - the all-reduce of the attention / linear-attention output; - the all-reduce of the MoE output. Sequence parallelism alone does not remove them: with TP-sharded experts, the MoE still needs an all-gather plus a reduce-scatter, which moves the same bytes. Replicating the experts does remove them. Each rank keeps its own tokens through the MoE, so the MoE needs no collective at all, and only the attention side keeps one all-gather / reduce-scatter pair. For Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 2 GPUs, full BF16 experts fit in memory (~63 GB per GPU), and the MoE all-reduce was ~half of the prefill communication. ## Modifications New flag `--moe-replicate-tp` (Qwen3.5 MoE only). It also allows `moe_dp_size == tp_size` without CP. - **`layers/moe/utils.py`**: `moe_replicated_over_tp()`. The MoE output is complete, so its all-reduce and the fused all-reduce with the next layer are skipped. - **`models/qwen2_moe.py`**: the shared expert is replicated too (`parallel_group="replicated"`). title: [Perf] kv-shard: Free sharded KV pages without a host sync
summary: Stacked on #47578. Only the last commit belongs to this PR; the first one is #47578 and will drop out once it merges. ## Motivation Under logical-page KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`), `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` returns each freed page to its owner class. `free_segment` derives the owners from the freed locs and splits the pages per class with `torch.unique` or a `bincount` whose counts go back to the host through `.tolist()`. That read waits on the scheduler stream, which can be queued behind an in-flight forward, so every request release and every eviction stalls the scheduler. The owner of position-page `P` on a chain is `(rotation_base + P) % N`, and the scheduler already knows the request's rotation base on the host, so the split can be computed without touching the device. ## Modifications - `free_segment`, `free_segments`, and the storage `free_units` / `free_token_rows` take an optional `rotation_base`. With it, `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` computes each class on the host: page `k` of the segment belongs to class `(rotation_base + start_pos // page_size + k) % N`, its pages are the stride slice `page_ids[k::N]`, and its count is closed-form. Grouped frees collect the slices per class and merge each class once at `free_group_end`. Debug mode still checks the host phase against the loc-derived owners. Without a rotation base the old path is unchanged. - Callers that free a request's row or tree values pass the base: - `release_kv_cache` and the overallocated-tail release pass `req.kv_rotation_base` through `free_kv_row` / `free_kv_row_segments`. - Tree n

title: [Fix] pd: Agree on requested abort vs error across PP and attention CP ranks
summary: Stacked on #47618. Only the last two commits belong to this PR; the earlier ones are #47618 and will drop out once it merges. ## Motivation With PP (or attention TP/CP) prefill in PD disaggregation, the release of an inflight transfer is agreed across ranks, but the *classification* of a failed transfer is still decided locally. When a request is aborted (client `AbortReq` or a decode-side abort), only the rank that saw the abort records an abort reason. A stage that finished its own transfer has no failure reason, so it concludes the same request as a transfer error and returns a 500 for a request the client aborted, while other stages finish it as an abort. ## Modifications - `disaggregation/common/conn.py`: `record_failure` replicates whether a stage's failure was a requested abort to PP0 through `PPConsensusStore`, before the Failed status on the same ordered channel; keys are cleaned up with the room. - `disaggregation/utils.py`: `TransferOutcome` and the PP / attention TP-CP outcome polls. PP0 forwards polls together with the terminal outcome, merged as ERROR < ABORT < SUCCESS: an error on any rank outranks an abort on another, and an abort is reported only if every failed rank recorded one. The same classification applies across attention TP/CP ranks without PP. - `disaggregation/prefill.py`: the inflight failure handler uses the agreed classification (abort → abort finish, not counted as a failure; error → 500) instead of the local exception. - `disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py`: record the decode-side abort reason, as NIXL already does. - Tests: `test_pp_prefill_rel

title: [Fix] kernels/quantization: Use int64 row offsets in the int8 quant kernels
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51104. `_per_token_quant_int8` computed `row_id * stride_x` and `row_id * stride_xq` from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`, and `_per_token_group_quant_int8` did the same with `g_id * y_stride`. For inputs with at least 2^31 elements the product wraps to a negative offset and the kernels read and write before the tensors. The fp8 siblings already use `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` for this case. Activation quantization of W8A8-INT8 linear layers and the channel-wise int8 fused MoE reach this path. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: widen `row_id` (`_per_token_quant_int8`) and `g_id` (`_per_token_group_quant_int8`) to int64. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_int8_kernel.py`: new `TestInt8QuantLargeInputOffsets` (CUDA, skipped below about 10 GB of free GPU memory). It asserts the per-row scales equal `value / 127` and that the last 16 rows, which sit past 2^31 elements, quantize exactly like the early rows with the same value. It compares against equal-value rows instead of a fixed code because the group kernel truncates, so some rows give 126 instead of 127. title: [Fix] mem_cache: Preserve hybrid prefill numerical consistency
summary: ## Motivation With FP32 GDN states and BF16 activations, unaligned prefix-cache snapshots currently pass through a BF16 chunk-state buffer. Copying it into an FP32 cache cannot recover the discarded precision, so a prefix hit resumes from a rounded state. title: [Perf] [AMD] carv2: SPX-specific gfx1250 table for TP2/TP4
summary: # [AMD] carv2: SPX-specific gfx1250 table for TP2/TP4 ## Motivation The gfx1250 rows in the carv2 config table were tuned on DPX nodes, where each partition has 96 CUs. We recently brought up an MI455X node in SPX mode (one 256-CU partition per GPU, 4 GPUs), and carv2 turned out to be slower than RCCL there in a couple of size ranges, which is the opposite of what we want from a custom all-reduce. Here's what we saw on current `main` (graph mode, µs, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1`): | TP | size | carv2 (main) | RCCL | what carv2 picks | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2 | 2 MB | 20.1 | 14.9 | 2shot_push | | 2 | 4 MB | 24.1 | 12.8 | 2shot_push | | 4 | 1.5 MB | 21.1 | 20.0 | 2shot_push | | 4 | 24 MB | 67.1 | 46.4 | ring_simple | | 4 | 48 MB, late rank | 102.8 | 100.4 | ring_simple | Above the 16 MB 2shot threshold, TP2 and TP4 go to `ring_simple`. The unrolled 2shot keeps beating RCCL all the way to 64 MB, but with the default 16 MB `max_size` a 2shot slot (`2 × nbytes / world_size`) only fits 16 MB at TP2 and 32 MB at TP4. title: [Feat] observability: Log stats lines for idle steps on PD prefill and decode workers
summary: ## Motivation TL;DR make post-processing of log lines be more accurate by inserting log lines even when server is idle. This is controlled by `SGLANG_LOG_IDLE_BATCH_STATS`, off by default which maintains previous behavior. Without idle logs, stats that can vary within the idle time (e.g., #transfer-req) is not visible. Furthermore, it is not possible to infer how large a time window a log line covers. Before PR: After PR: PD prefill and decode workers log a `Prefill batch` / `Decode batch` line only for forwards that do work. A worker with no forward to run, or such an attention-DP rank, prints nothing, though it can be in either of two states: 1. **Idle**: no requests exist. 2. **Blocked**: requests exist but wait on something other than compute. With the defaults (`early` decode allocation, no optimistic prefill), prefill starts a request only after decode has reserved KV cache for it. While the decode KV pool is full, new requests wait in the prefill bootstrap queue and the prefill worker has nothing to run. Such waiting is worth observing because acting on it pays off. `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` (#40703) reserves decode KV only after prefill, so requests compute instead of waiting for a decode slot; #45337 extends it to PP prefill and reports lar

This PR adds a FlyDSL kernel that does the conv and the gated delta rule in one launch and writes the ReplaySSM rings. 8 lanes share each state column and add their parts with three DPP adds, so the state stays in registers. For GLM-5.3-Flash's TP4 shape it is faster than the HIP kernel from 6 requests up, so that shape now tries FlyDSL first. | KDA verify, gfx950 + ReplaySSM | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 (16 heads, 6 draft tokens) | HIP `kda_chain_verify_gfx950` | FlyDSL `kda_verify_gfx950_flydsl` | | Other shapes (Kimi-K3.1, …) | HIP `kda_chain_verify_gfx950` | HIP `kda_chain_verify_gfx950` | ## Scope gfx950 (MI355X) KDA target verify with ReplaySSM and 6 or 8 draft tokens, when FlyDSL imports. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dp-attention: Route the padding rows of the TP-MoE gather to no expert
summary: ## Motivation With attention DP and TP MoE on CUDA, the MoE input of a decode step is a MAX_LEN gather: every DP rank contributes a slot of the same length, and the rows past its real requests are padding. The decode CUDA graph always uses this layout, and an idle rank still replays one fabricated row. The router sends the padding rows to experts like real tokens, so every MoE layer loads those experts' weights. Since #46225 this costs more on hybrid models. Before it, the unpacked KDA/GDN decode left the padding rows' output unwritten. On GLM-5.3-Flash, six or seven of the seven padding rows of a one-request step then selected exactly experts 0-7 in every MoE layer, which is what the router does with NaN scores (it ranks NaN as -1e30 and breaks ties toward the lowest id). #46225 zeroes that output, which is the right fix for correctness, and the padding rows now route like real tokens. With one request on 8×H20 (attention DP8, main 552e16968b), the expert-distribution recorder counts 64 selections and 35 distinct experts per MoE layer per decode step; with this PR, the real row's 8. On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 zeroes the padding rows before the gather (#43077). Zeroed rows still route, to the experts with the largest correction bias. This PR keeps them out of routing on CUDA. `SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE` (#31888, off by default) drops the same rows from the dispatch, but only with EP: it runs in the standard dispatcher after the local expert mapping, which exists only when `moe_ep_size > 1`. summary: ## Motivation Fixes #50130; part of #49944 ("Ensure safe page reuse after failed or timed-out PD transfers"). A Mooncake `batch_get_into` receipt is the number of bytes actually read for a key: positive on success, negative on error. A partially served object — e.g. a page a crashed writer only half published — still yields a positive but SHORT receipt. summary: ## Motivation FlashInfer 0.7.4, already pinned on main, ships batch-invariant GEMMs. A call with `batch_invariant=True` returns the same bits for a row whatever batch it is in, and FlashInfer guarantees that tile config, grid, SM count and autotuning never change those bits. This PR is the first and smallest step toward using them in SGLang: BF16 only, through `mm_bf16`. In deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`), SGLang's aten `mm`/`addmm` overrides call `matmul_persistent`. On Blackwell that function runs DeepGEMM's deterministic `bf16_gemm_nn` or a Triton persistent kernel. RL trainers that call `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` go through the same function, so a change here reaches rollout and training together. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/batch_invariant_ops/batch_invariant_ops.py`: `matmul_persistent` first sends eligible calls to `flashinfer.mm_bf16(a, b, backend="auto", batch_invariant=True)`. A call is eligible when all of these hold: - The GPU is SM100, SM103 or SM107, as reported by FlashInfer's `is_supported_device`, and FlashInfer 0.7.4+ imports. If it doesn't, the call falls back silently to today's path. - `a`, `b` and the output are all bf16, with K and N divisible by 8. - The weight is row-major (K, N) or the transpose of a row-major (N, K), with a 16-byte-aligned base. Eligibility depends only on the device, the dtypes and the weight, never on M. Switching providers with the batch size would break batch invariance even though each provider is invariant on its own. summary: ## Motivation Part of the N-gram Speculative Decoding Roadmap (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21052). Currently, `NGRAMWorker._update_ngram_corpus` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`) is only called after `TARGET_VERIFY` steps and carries a `FIXME`: ```python # FIXME: Whether to insert 'extend' into the cache or not, after testing, # there is not much difference, so we will not insert it for now. ``` As a result, when a new request completes its prefill (`EXTEND`) phase and enters its first `DECODE` step, the N-gram Trie has **zero tokens from the current request's prompt** (except the last `max_trie_depth = 18` query suffix). In long-context chat, RAG, summarization, and structured JSON planning workloads, entities, identifiers, and schema keys that appear earlier in the prompt cannot be drafted until they have already been generated once by the model. title: [Feat] linker: support pipeline parallelism in linker
summary: ## Motivation Support pipeline parallelism (PP) in both `layer_wise` and `prefetch` modes of the unified cache external linker. Each rank queries its own storage shard, so backends only need to answer local lookups. The pipeline then agrees on a prefix that every stage can restore. ## Layer-wise loading PP0 issues a ticket with the request key and its local prefix position. Each rank queries the external store for the missing suffix and reports the page boundaries it can restore. A downstream stage can start its lookup before the request arrives. If its local device-cache prefix ends at a different position, it rechecks the suffix from its own pinned prefix. The ranks select the longest common boundary and use it during admission. Each stage then follows the existing layer-wise path, loading only its own layers into slots owned by the request. The restored KV enters the radix tree through the normal request insertion path. ## Prefetch and PP coordination Prefetch reuses HiCache’s ordered ticket broadcast and scheduler readiness relay. PP0 issues tickets in request order, and every rank queries its local backend. 1. PP0 sends its local hit upper bound through the readiness relay. Each stage reserves device slots up to that bound while slower local lookups can still be in flight. 2. Each rank builds a mask of the page boundaries its local query can restore and removes boundaries beyond its **actual reservation**. A single PP `MIN` all-reduce intersects these masks. title: [Perf] [AMD] hyperconnection: Add a Triton prefill path for gated HC sites
summary: ## Motivation On gfx950, a gated hyper-connection (HC) site with a per-branch norm runs a grouped norm that writes a BF16 normed residual, then a mix and `hc_combine` that read it. summary: ## Motivation **What** Mount the `FUSED_LINEAR_GELU` quality site on gfx1250 with a backend that keeps the FlyDSL GEMM and replaces aten's GELU with one bit-exact Triton launch, so the Wan2.2 FFN GELU stops taking 2.3 ms per block. **Why** `_input_independent_ok` rejects every arch >= 12.0 to keep the cuBLASLt epilogue off SM120, and gfx1250 reports 12.5, so the site never mounted on MI450. The FFN then runs `F.gelu(approximate="tanh")` on the [90000, 13824] bf16 intermediate: its byte offsets pass 2**31, so TensorIterator splits it into two launches that each reach only ~2.2 TB/s (1164 + 1131 us per block). hipBLASLt has no tuned gfx1250 kernels, so the cuBLASLt-style `_addmm_activation` is not an option; the gfx1250 backend runs `apply_unquantized_linear` (FlyDSL) and then the new kernel in place. title: [Fix] scheduler: Count the unprefilled part of a chunked request in total_tokens load
summary: ## Motivation With `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the smallest `num_total_tokens`. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens", but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill. That request holds KV only for the chunks it has already run, and it is in neither the running batch nor the waiting queue. So a rank that has just started a 64K-token prompt reports only about one chunk of load, and new requests keep going to it. We saw this on 2×H20 with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP=2, `--attn-dp-size 2`, FA3, FP8 KV, and `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` (4096 per rank). The rank prefilling the 64K prompt then also received 24 of the 30 short requests, which gave a 38,912 / 90,112 input-token split. When the 64K prompt arrived first, the bug was not triggered and the split was 68,608 / 60,416. `SchedulerLoadInquirer._get_num_pending_tokens()` already adds the chunked request's `seqlen - prefix_len`; `num_total_tokens` did not. ## Modifications - `load_inquirer.py`: add the chunked request's remaining tokens (`seqlen - prefix_len`) to `num_total_tokens`, and so also to `num_active_tokens`. title: [Perf] dllm: Run several denoise forwards per scheduled FDFO round
summary: ## Motivation Under FDFO, one scheduler round is one denoise forward. Everything the round does around that forward — committing resolved blocks, admitting waiting requests, processing results, rebuilding the batch — is paid once per forward. dLLM also disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so that host work is exposed directly as device idle rather than hidden behind the next forward. At large batch this is a real share of the step: the forward itself is the only part that scales with the model, while the round overhead is roughly fixed. ## Modifications `SGLANG_DLLM_FDFO_STEPS_PER_ROUND` (new, default `1` = today's behavior) makes a round issue N denoise forwards instead of one. The batch is frozen for the inner steps: rows that resolve mid-round freeze themselves inside the step, and commits, admissions and result processing all happen once at the end of the round. The per-round host work is therefore amortized over N forwards. Two hooks are added to `DllmAlgorithm` so an algorithm can keep its per-request state in batched device tensors for the whole round (`fdfo_batched_begin` / `fdfo_batched_step` / `fdfo_batched_all_finished`), which is what makes an inner step cost no host gather/scatter. `JointThreshold` implements them; an algorithm that returns `None` from `fdfo_batched_begin` gets a plain loop with the same semantics, which is the path non-NPU dLLM runs today. summary: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. title: [Fix] constrained: bound the compiled-grammar cache by host memory (LRU) to stop RSS growth with per-request schemas
summary: ## Motivation `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` is a plain `dict` that is never evicted. Each rank picks its variant from its own longest sequence, and an idle rank always picks sparse. Under DP attention the ranks replay their graphs in lockstep, and the collectives captured inside them pair up across ranks. Some of these collectives register their graph's input buffers (aiter all-gather / reduce-scatter / custom all-reduce). Pinning every rank to one variant removed all of them, which confirmed the cause. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? title: [BugFix][Scheduler] Keep the scheduling cursor correct on PRIORITY preemption
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #22017. The Ascend schedulers are copies of upstream vLLM's `Scheduler.schedule()`. When a running request cannot allocate its KV blocks under `SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY`, the lowest-priority request is preempted and removed from `self.running`. `self.running.remove(victim)` shifts every request behind the victim one slot to the left, so the `req_index` loop cursor has to move back with it. The copies only corrected the cursor when the victim had *already been scheduled* in the current step (`victim in scheduled_running_reqs`). A victim that was skipped earlier in the same step — for example a request with `num_new_tokens == 0` (deferred prefill, a decode-staggered request, or a request that hit its max length) — is **not** in `scheduled_running_reqs`, so the cursor was never moved back. Every running request behind the victim was then silently skipped for the rest of that step: the requests keep their KV blocks but produce no token, and the token budget of the step is silently under-used. summary: ## 这个 PR 做了什么 FLA/KDA 的 varlen 回退路径（没有传入 prebuilt chunk 元数据时）在每次 kernel launch 前调用 `prepare_chunk_indices()`，它的实现里有一句 `.tolist()`： ```python indices = torch.cat([torch.arange(n) for n in triton.cdiv(prepare_lens(cu_seqlens), chunk_size).tolist()]) ``` `cu_seqlens` 在设备上，所以这是**一次 device→host 同步**，带来两个后果： 1. eager 下每个 kernel launch 都会打断 NPU 流水（GDN prefill 每层 6 个 kernel）； 2. **ACLGraph 图捕获期间禁止 host 同步**，这些路径因此无法进图模式。 本 PR 新增 `prepare_chunk_indices_dev()`，用**纯设备端算子**构造同一份 `[total_chunks, 2]` 的 `(seq_id, chunk_in_seq)` 张量，并把 FLA/KDA 里全部回退调用点切到它（12 个调用点，FLA 7 个 + KDA 7 个中的 12 处，见文末清单）。 ### 行数为什么要用上界 行数必须在 host 侧可见（grid 大小、临时 buffer 分配），所以不能用精确值 `sum(ceil(len_s / chunk_size))`，而用形状推出的上界： ```python total_chunks = total_tokens // chunk_size + num_seqs ``` 因为 `sum(ceil(l_s / CS)) <= sum(l_s / CS + 1) = T/CS + N`，所以该上界恒不小于真实行数，最多多出 `N` 行（对齐长度时正好多 `N` 行，平均每序列 1 行）。 多出来的**phantom 行**是安全的：它们的 `seq_id` 被夹到 0，而 `chunk_in_seq` 越过序列 0 的末尾， 于是 kernel 里由 `cu_seqlens` 导出的 token offset 全部越界、mask 全假，不写任何数据；grid 只是 多跑几个全空 program。已逐个 kernel 核对过遮罩方式： | kernel | 遮罩方式 | phantom 行行为 | | --- | --- | --- | | `chunk_local_cumsum` | store `boundary_check=(0,)` + `cu_seqlens` mask | 不写 | | `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt` | `A` store `boundary_check=(0,1)` | 不写 | | `solve_tril`（merge / large block） | 显式 `store_mask` | 不写 | | `recompute_w_u` | `w`/`u` store mask | 不写 | | `fwd_h`（blockdim64 / kda 版） | `chunk_offsets` + 每 chunk 的 `T_` 上界 | 不写，见下 | `fwd_h` 是唯一用 `len(chunk_indices)` 做分配的地方（`h = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, K, V)`、 `h_update = k.new_empty(B, NT + N, ...)`），上界只会让它多分配几行；`h` / `h_update` 的写入位置由 `chunk_offsets` / `up

title: [Performance] Vectorise the A3 HiSparse resolver union and merge the emit pass
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On Ascend A3 (arch 220) the HiSparse resolver falls back to its scalar path as soon as one selected token is cold. One AI core owns a whole request group and walks its 4 x 2048 tokens three times — union, miss ordering, publish — translating every token on each pass with two page-table loads. At the production shape that is ~3.4 ms per call, 47.6% of the decode iteration span, with only 0.4% of it overlapping compute. The cost is instruction count, not bandwidth: one scalar access on A3 costs ~20 ns whether it hits UB or GM, and the request needs ~86k of them. Vectorising the data movement does nothing by itself (moving the page tables into UB measured 6.6% and 8.2% *slower*); the win comes from issuing far fewer instructions. This PR ports three changes onto the aclnn-resident kernel. All of them live in `csrc/attention/hisparse_resolve_residency/op_kernel/arch22/hisparse_resolver_kernel.h`; no other product file changes. 1. **Translate once.** The union pass stores each cold host id into the output buffer (which is not written until publish), so the miss-ordering and publish passes read it back instead of re-reading the page tables. Page-table scalar loads drop 3x. 2. **Vectorise what is independent.** Both page rows are DMA'd into UB once per request; each 256-token tile is then translated with `Gather`/`Shift`/`Compare`/`Select` and compacted with `GatherMask`, so only real cold tokens reach the serial hash insert. title: [BugFix][Worker] Validate KV cache sizing when free NPU memory is unchanged
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Refs #18343. The NPU worker compares free memory before model loading and after profiling. Equal readings can be consistent when model weights fit within memory already reserved by PyTorch. They can also occur when a device or virtualization layer fails to report a new reservation. In the latter case, the derived non-PyTorch memory delta can cancel the weight cost and inflate the KV cache budget. This change accepts equal free-memory snapshots when device totals and PyTorch reservations agree, new live allocations fit in the reported initial reserve, and the computed budget accounts for those allocations. Inconsistent readings raise an actionable error that points to the existing `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` option for users who know a safe budget. Increased free memory raises an explicit error with the before and after readings. The change is scoped to the generic NPU worker. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Startup can proceed when unchanged free-memory readings are consistent with the measured allocations. When automatic sizing cannot establish a budget, the startup error explains how to set a known-safe per-worker budget. The FAQ and release note describe this behavior. ### How was this patch tested? - `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main bash format.sh ci` passed. - An isolated CPU harness ran the seven cases in `tests/ut/worker/test_worker_multi_instance.py` using the worker method and profiling code from both aligned vLLM versions. title: [Performance][Kernel] Halve BF16 candidate exchange for sharded Kimi Top-K
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Kimi's sharded indexer gathers 2048 candidates per row from every DCP rank. For owner-local output, each rank already knows which peer produced a candidate. When the configured model length guarantees all owner-local IDs fit in 16 bits, pack the local ID and the original BF16 score into one INT32. The owner-prefix merge consumes those words directly and resolves equal scores by interleave block and rank. This halves the AllGather payload. At 128 rows and DCP8, the gathered buffer falls from 16 MiB to 8 MiB per rank. The fused pack also tags each radix digit and its lane with a positive normal FP32 bit pattern. The native value sort can carry 19 digit bits per pass. At K2048, BF16 takes two passes and FP32 takes three. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Kimi's BF16 owner-local DCP Top-K exchange is faster on Ascend 950DT. The existing model-length bound and shared topology select the wire format at the graph boundary. FP32, global output, other Top-K sizes and larger or unknown local capacities use the full-width exchange. Both formats preserve the public INT32 token IDs, including ties and padding. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on Ascend 950DT with CANN 9.2.1, PyTorch 2.10, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7 and Triton-Ascend 3.6.0.post2. The baseline transport module in the runtime matches the PR base. The eight-rank numbers cover the full pack, HCCL AllGather and owner-prefix merge. The inputs are synthetic BF16 scores and unique IDs sampled from each rank's visible prefix, with K2048 and interleave 768. - At 16,3

title: [BugFix] Apply expert gate in quantized shared expert paths
summary: ## What this PR does Apply the optional model-specific `expert_gate` after the quantized shared-expert fast paths for W8A8, W4A8, and W4A8MXFP. The non-quantized path applies this gate in `part2()`, but the quantized fast paths bypass `part2()`. As a result, models that use the optional shared-expert gate, such as Qwen3-Next, can produce incorrectly scaled shared-expert outputs and corrupted generation results. ## Root cause The expected shared-expert computation is: ```python gate_out, _ = self.layer.expert_gate(hidden_states) shared_out = F.sigmoid(gate_out) * shared_out ``` The quantized fast paths execute the gate/up projection, activation, and down projection directly, bypassing `part2()` where this gate is normally applied. ## Changes - Preserve the original shared-expert input before the quantized path overwrites `hidden_states`. - Apply `expert_gate` after the W8A8, W4A8, and W4A8MXFP fast paths. - Keep other quantization types unchanged because they fall back to `part2()` and already apply the gate. - Add a W8A8 regression test that verifies: - `expert_gate` receives the original shared-expert input. - A zero gate logit scales the output by `sigmoid(0) = 0.5`. ## Validation Test environment: ```text vLLM: 0.26.0 System fingerprint: vllm-0.26.0-1bb1d043 Model: qwen36-gptq-w8a8 Quantization: GPTQ W8A8 ``` The following request was used before and after applying the fix: ```bash curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8327/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "qwen36-gptq-w8a8", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "请用简洁的语言介绍一下人工智能。" } ],

title: [Feature][Attention] Add B1 paged verify for Gemma4 512-dim MTP verify
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This is a rebased and adapted continuation of #20125 on current main, where Model Runner V1 has been removed. The Gemma4 target runs its MTP verify step with k+1 queries per request on head_dim=512 global-attention layers. On A2/A3, FIA TND rejects head_dim=512 and the MRV2 capture metadata never emits SpecDecoding, so neither the TND nor the PagedAttention capture path can serve this geometry. This PR adds a per-layer backend that keeps the former B1 op contract: - Hkv-major paged K/V cache and npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2 BNSD paged ops with a per-sequence block table; - explicit [B, 1, k+1, W] bool causal mask and sparse_mode=0; - capture-time placeholder mask rebound per replay; - FULL-cudagraph PA row expansion for 512-dim layers. Selection is limited to MTP decoder layers with head_dim=512 and no sliding window, and stays off for MLA/sparse/PCP/DCP/connectors/sinks/adaptive verification; never on A5. The backend is opt-in: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_B1_PAGED_VERIFY=1 (default 0). Credits: original implementation by Wu Meng in #20125. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes: new environment variable VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_B1_PAGED_VERIFY (default 0). title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Trim stale Mooncake prefill hashes without rehashing the prefix
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Addresses the Hybrid connector portion of #21166. When the prefill producer drops the last prompt token, any block hash covering that token becomes stale. The Hybrid connector could retain that hash. Mooncake V1 rebuilt the entire prefix. After #22167, V2 still did so on vLLM versions earlier than 0.34 when the native truncation method was unavailable. These three scheduler paths now trim hashes before the local prefix lookup using the engine-resolved hash block size and the configured hash lookahead. V2 Pull and Push inherit the same change. Each scheduler calls `Request.truncate_block_hashes()` when the method is callable. For vLLM versions earlier than 0.34 that lack it, a shared fallback trims the invalid suffix in place and clears the prompt-embedding hash cache. The existing one-token and rescheduling guards still apply. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [Refactor][Attention] Simplify FA3 config and layout contracts after #22159
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Follow-up cleanup of #22159, which is already merged. This PR contains only the subsequent FA3 configuration/lifecycle simplification, not the original GLM DFlash2 feature changes. FA3 now consumes the engine-resolved cache layout explicitly. `_uses_hnd_kv_cache(config)` reads `get_resolved_kv_cache_layout()` directly; the static shape entry point obtains the current initialization config, while runtime cache writes and attention reads keep using the allocation config bound to each Impl by the metadata builder. The constructor therefore uses `get_current_vllm_config()` and completes scheduler initialization directly, rather than silently skipping it for missing config/NPU checks.
