title: [Performance][Ops] Cache decode GDN attention metadata across steps
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Ref #20607. `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` is invoked once per GDN KV-cache group on every decode step. On hybrid (linear attention) models, rebuilding the same `GDNAttentionMetadata` for every group is a significant part of the host-side step time whenever the batch composition is stable. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 (48 GDN + 16 full attention layers, TP8 on 910B4, MTP spec4 speculative decoding) the builder costs ~4.7 ms per decode step for its 3 GDN KV groups, i.e. ~22% of the ~21 ms step, and the decode step is host bound in that configuration. All host inputs of a pure-decode step only change when a sequence advances into a new KV block or when the set of requests changes. The built metadata can therefore be cached across steps and only the accepted-token counts (the only value that advances every step) are refreshed in place. Prefill steps drop the cache. The cache key covers the request identity, the batch shape, the query start locations, the derived sequence-length facts the builder consumes (zero-length graph-padding rows, "sequence has state", KV block index), the prefill mask and the per-request draft-token counts. title: [Performance][Model] Reuse Qwen4Exp HC block output across streams
summary: This is a follow-up optimization built on our existing #21901 work. No external AscendC package or Torch extension is required. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen4Exp `hc_combine_norm` currently launches one program per `(row, HC stream)`. Every program loads the same row of `block_output`, so the production four-stream layout reads that row four times. This PR adds an A3 row-wise variant for per-branch norm weights at 512 rows and above. One program loads `block_output` once and walks the HC streams in the original order. It preserves the BF16 combine-materialization boundary and FP32 RMSNorm reduction order. Shared weights, smaller batches, and other hardware profiles keep the legacy kernel. The row-wise variant selects INT64 row addressing only when an input or output offset exceeds INT32_MAX; ordinary shapes retain INT32 addressing and the legacy launch is unchanged. The upstream NVIDIA implementation also uses the per-`(row, stream)` schedule and does not provide an Ascend row-wise implementation to reuse. No CLI option, environment variable, or additional-config key is added; the 512-row value is an internal A3 hardware-profile threshold based on measured crossover. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Qwen4Exp long-prefill HC execution on A3 is faster. Public APIs and configuration are unchanged. title: [BugFix] Keep the scheduling cursor correct on PRIORITY preemption
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Two vendored copies of the upstream vLLM v1 scheduler loop pre-empt a running request under `SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY` by removing it from `self.running` without correcting the `req_index` loop cursor, so every running request that follows the victim in `self.running` is silently skipped for the rest of that scheduling step. The affected copies are: - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py` (`BalanceScheduler`, used when `enable_balance_scheduling` is on) - `vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py` (`DyntraLBScheduler`, used when DyntraLB is on) Both removed the victim with `self.running.remove(preempted_req)` and only corrected the cursor when the victim happened to be *scheduled* in the current step: ```python self.running.remove(preempted_req) if preempted_req in scheduled_running_reqs: ... req_index -= 1 ``` `self.running.remove(victim)` shifts every request behind the victim one slot to the left. title: [Bug][PD] MooncakeHybridConnector pairs KV addresses by position without validating entry counts, silently dropping consumer layers the producer never registered (DSpark P/D asymmetry)
summary: ## Your current environment ```text vllm-ascend: v0.30.0rc2 (tag) vLLM: v0.30.0 model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash topology: 1P1D, MooncakeHybridConnector ``` Note: this report is derived from source analysis of `v0.30.0rc2` and has **not** been reproduced on hardware, so no `collect_env.py` output is attached. All line numbers refer to tag `v0.30.0rc2`. ## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary `MooncakeHybridConnector` exchanges only a **flat address list** during the handshake: the metadata carries neither layer names nor any speculative-configuration identity. At transfer time the worker pairs local and remote entries positionally with `zip` and never checks that both sides registered the same number of entries. Consequently, when the decode engine registers more KV entries than the prefill engine — typically because decode runs DSpark while prefill does not — the extra entries are silently skipped, or, if the address ordering interleaves them, the whole positional mapping shifts. Neither case raises an error or emits a warning. ### Configuration that triggers it Both engines use `MooncakeHybridConnector` with the parameters from `docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` sections 5.2.2 / 5.2.3, except that the speculative configuration is asymmetric: ```bash # Prefill: no --speculative-config --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeHybridConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer",...}' # Decode: DSpark enabled --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}' --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeHybridConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",...}' ```

title: [RFC]: Support lookahead block hashes in AscendStoreConnector for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching
summary: ### Motivation Upstream vLLM migrated core prefix caching and in-tree KV connectors to **lookahead block hashes** (`vllm-project/vllm#61589`, `#64096`, `#65448`) and recently removed the legacy EAGLE trailing-block drop fallback altogether (`vllm-project/vllm#66234`). In `vllm-ascend`, `AscendStoreConnector.supports_lookahead_block_hashes()` (`vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/ascend_store_connector.py`) currently hardcodes `return False` because `AscendStore`'s external coordinator still retains trailing EAGLE-block dropping and does not propagate `num_hash_lookahead_tokens` through its lookup/store masks. As a result: 1. title: [RFC]: Support tail-only KV backing and target padding avoidance for sliding-window DFlash/DSpark drafts on Ascend MRV2
summary: ### Motivation Upstream vLLM recently introduced two key memory optimizations for sliding-window DFlash/DSpark speculative decoding on Model Runner V2: 1. **Tail-only drafter KV backing (`vllm-project/vllm#64109`, related to `vllm-project/vllm#59117`)**: A DFlash or DSpark drafter's context KV is projected from target hidden states and draft attention only attends past the last target token. `DFlashSlidingWindowManager` backs only the required trailing window `[T - tail_tokens, ...)` and caps per-request admission reservations so they stop scaling with prefill chunk size. 2. **Avoid sizing target KV cache groups from draft-only SWA buckets (`vllm-project/vllm#68533`)**: Keeps draft-only sliding-window buckets out of uniform-page-size group sizing so target full-attention layers do not suffer unnecessary padding layers (eliminating ~20% per-token full-attention KV overhead on hybrid Muse Spark models). title: [BugFix] Match KDA RecoverSSM L2 normalization to native RecurrentKDA on A5
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The pinned A5 FLA RecurrentKDA operator normalizes nonzero query and key vectors by their L2 norm. RecoverSSM added `1e-6` to the squared norm, which shrank small vectors and caused speculative verification outputs and committed states to diverge from native RecurrentKDA. Use the same normalization rule for verification and both state-commit kernels. On A5, guard the zero squared norm before taking its reciprocal square root so a zero vector stays zero. On A3, keep the existing `1e-6` epsilon. The kernel selects the rule at compile time from the device type. Recheck this choice when upgrading A5 FLA to a version that adds an epsilon. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. On Ascend A5, Kimi KDA speculative decoding with RecoverSSM now matches native RecurrentKDA for small query and key vectors. The fix applies automatically. ### How was this patch tested? title: [Performance] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel on Ascend
summary: ## Description Port of vLLM #58737 to vllm-ascend. `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s "align" branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request. As PyTorch ops this expands to **seven eager kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor** - one element per op at one-request decode - so the cost is launch overhead, not work. Both Ascend call sites (the GDN attention metadata builder, run by every Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-Next GDN model each step, and the GLM RecoverSSM metadata builder) are host-side builders executing **every step, outside any captured graph**, at any batch size. The upstream kernel cannot be inherited: vLLM gates it with `if not block_table.is_cuda`, so NPU always falls back to the seven-op expression **regardless of the vLLM version**. This PR ships the same kernel for triton-ascend (NPU-only) and swaps the two call sites. Equivalence vs the expression was probed bit-exact (8/8 shapes) before implementation; the outputs are integer block IDs (exact-compare category), so model-level outputs are unchanged by construction. ## Performance ### 910B probe (triton-ascend 3.6.0, per call) Device ~370 -> ~215 us (**-42%**), host ~247 -> ~121 us (**-51%**); flat across 1..512 rows - the win is per-launch, per-step. ### E2E on 910B (Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8, MTP5, TP4) Arms = base tree vs this PR, alternating with cold restarts. Concurrency 1, five independent pairs, zero flips, B faster in all: ITL **-0.112 / -0.168 / -0.245 ms (-0.7 / -1.0 / -1.4%)**; aisbench TPOT 17.3 -> 17.1 ms, E2E latency -1.0%. title: [Feature]: Add model-load lifecycle hooks for worker extensions
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch The public `worker_extension_cls` mechanism can add collective RPC methods, but extensions cannot override `load_model` because it conflicts with the worker's existing method. This leaves no supported extension callback between device/model-runner initialization and weight loading. Please support these optional instance methods on configured worker extensions: ```python def before_load_model(self, *, load_dummy_weights: bool) -> None: ... def after_load_model(self, *, load_dummy_weights: bool) -> None: ... ``` The before callback should run after device initialization and before the normal worker loader. The after callback should run only after the whole worker loader succeeds. A before-callback exception should prevent loading; a loader exception should skip the after callback; callback exceptions should propagate as startup failures. These callbacks let extensions prepare loading resources and inspect or initialize model-dependent state after weights become available, without copying the worker's loader or changing request execution. Normal Ascend loading should preserve `NPUWorker.load_model()`'s no-argument signature and pass `load_dummy_weights=False` to the callbacks. Explicit dummy-weight loading should remain conditional on the worker supporting it. The upstream proposal is [vllm-project/vllm#68936](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68936), which addresses [vllm-project/vllm#68573](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68573). title: [BugFix][Ops] Retire eager packaged MLA stream uses on Ascend A5
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The packaged CannBotDSL MLA call records the query and attention output on the submission stream. In eager execution these records can delay buffer reuse and increase memory pressure. After submitting the kernel, record and wait on a device event on that stream, then retire the recorded uses of `q` and `attn_out`. The cleanup is gated to eager execution. When those buffers stay pending across layers, new allocations can exhaust the available pool and trigger the allocator's retry path. That path synchronizes the device and reclaims cached blocks before retrying. [TorchNPU allocator retry path](https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/v26.2.0-pytorch2.10.0/torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/NPUCachingAllocator.cpp#L1309-L1324) Split out from #21727 for independent review and validation. The packaged MLA hunk also appears in the broader fused epilogue integration in #21826. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Reduces peak temporary NPU memory awaiting reuse during eager DeepSeek V4.1 packaged MLA on Ascend A5. In the original long-prefill DeepInfer MegaMoE diagnostic, the reduction was about 6 GB and allocation retries fell from four to zero. ### How was this patch tested? - **11 CPU unit tests passed** on Linux AArch64 with Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`, pytest 8.4.2 and vLLM `c410543d9ffff03f5f66c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`. title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Ignore EOS on the truncated prefill sample
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MooncakeConnectorV1 drops the last prompt token on the prefill side so the decoder can recompute it (the N-1 handoff). The prefill engine then samples a one-token placeholder solely to drive the KV handoff. If that placeholder sample lands on EOS, the request finishes `STOPPED` before the connector's `request_finished` path can run. The conductor short-circuits on `"stop"` and returns empty content to the client; no KV transfer is started. Set `ignore_eos` and clear the EOS id on the truncated P-side request, so the placeholder sample always takes the length-based stop and the handoff runs. The placeholder token is discarded (the first real token comes from decode), so there is no semantic loss. This is a rebase of the internal 0.32 fix `fad89020d` (original author shangyan.wq), which was observed on DSV4.1 PD deployments. It is distinct from #20788: that PR avoids the compression-triggered truncation in the Hybrid connector; V1 still needs truncation for the N-1 handoff, so it needs this guard when truncation is used. Related: #20999 (P-side first token EOS in PD), #20788 (Hybrid draft), #21437 (Hybrid stale prefill hashes). ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Prefill requests whose placeholder sample would hit EOS now complete the KV handoff instead of returning an empty response. ### How was this patch tested? - `ruff check` on both changed files: passed. - `python3 -m py_compile` on both changed files: passed. - Extended the existing `test_prefill_truncation_preserves_payload_and_is_idempotent` parametrized t

title: [Performance][Model] Tile Qwen4Exp HC gate mix on Ascend A2/A3/A5
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR adds an eight-row Triton tile for Qwen4Exp HyperConnection `gate_mix`. The existing one-row kernel remains the fallback. The row-block kernel processes an `8 x 512` tile, reduces the launched-program count by up to 8x, and preserves the original FP32 accumulation order. The dispatch threshold is based on the integrated wrapper, not the kernel alone: - A2/A3: row-block starts at 2048 rows. - A5: row-block starts at 1024 rows. At 1024 rows the direct kernel is faster on all three devices, but host-side output allocation and custom-op dispatch dominate on A2/A3. A5 crosses over earlier and benefits from the row-block path at 1024 rows. The shared `8 x 512` tile is close to the best measured per-device tile at 1024 rows: - A2: `8 x 512` is `80.00 us`; the best measured `4 x 512` variant is `78.86 us`, a 1.45% difference. - A5: `8 x 512` is `14.63 us`; the best measured `32 x 128` variant is `14.57 us`, a 0.41% difference. `512` divides the production `group_dim=2560` exactly, preserves column alignment, and keeps one shared tile instead of adding per-device tuning. One hoisted mask is reused for all stream loads and the output store, including production-aligned and tail widths. The implementation also handles column tails, combined row/column tails, and element offsets beyond `INT32_MAX`. The normal prefill path remains int32. No environment variable or user configuration is added. ### Operator integration - Public wrapper: `hc_gate_mix(x, gate, hc_count)` - Registered custom op: `qwen4_exp_ascend_hc_gate_mix` - Production caller

title: [Refactor][MRV2] Reuse unified KV cache allocation for Kimi K3
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it Port the Kimi K3 MRV2 changes onto the merged #21083 allocator (`e0ea2e623`). MRV2 models whose text config reports `kimi_linear` now use descriptor offsets and strides to build their cache views from the shared backing. - KDA uses the state shapes and dtypes in `MambaSpec` and keeps manager-block indexing. - The MLA layer publishes the component widths and the layout selected by the implementation. FIA keeps its NoPE/RoPE tuple and FlashMLA keeps its fused Tensor. For a 1:2 split, adjacent manager pages allow a fixed kernel-slot stride. - `kimi_linear` uses the same allocator dispatch as DeepSeek V4/V4.1. Block-outer 1:2 layouts are rejected because their kernel slots do not have a uniform stride. KV transfer, KVPP, speculative decoding, ReplaySSM, and K3.1 variants still need compatibility validation. title: [Feature][XLite] Support MTP accepted state pages on widened hybrid state tables
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Enables MTP (speculative decoding) on the xlite hybrid path (GLM-5.3-Flash family). All changes are confined to `vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py`. Under MTP, the hybrid mamba allocator hands out multi-column state tables `[rows, W]` (`W = num_spec + 1`): column 0 is the live page, column `j` is the state-after page of verify-span token `j`. The xlite kernels (external GVirt extension) consume a different, widened descriptor layout, so the tables must be rewritten each step — without this, hybrid xlite cannot run with MTP at all (states would commit to wrong pages: the conv rolling window would drift across pages whenever acceptance varies between steps, and per-token snapshot pages would be lost). title: [Feature][WeightTransfer] Add bounded large-parameter HCCL updates
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? A parameter larger than `packed_buffer_size_bytes` currently produces an oversized packed HCCL collective and another owning input on the receiver. With a 2 GiB parameter and a 128 MiB bucket, the existing path broadcasts 2 GiB in one collective. This change adds `packed_transfer_mode="bounded"` to split it across capacity-limited collectives while preserving native `load_weights()` and the existing START/UPDATE/FINISH transaction. - Share deterministic byte planning between sender and receiver; no full-size source packing copy is required. - Reconstruct independent, aligned parameter storage. Complete small inputs share loader calls within the same storage budget; at most one parameter is incomplete. Loaders may retain or modify their inputs. - Bound transport-held tensor storage by `K * B + Lmax`. When the payload is smaller than a bucket, receive slots shrink and their unused budget can hold complete inputs. Model/source weights, loader retention and layer rebuilding, runtime workspaces, allocator rounding and reserved memory are separate. - Reuse session-owned streams across updates, wait before copying/reusing each slot, and drain submitted work on errors. One slot is serial; two permit the next receive to overlap current reconstruction/loading. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. `HCCLTrainerInitInfo(packed=True, packed_transfer_mode="bounded", ...)` selects the new protocol. `legacy` remains the default. Mode, bucket capacity and slot count are fixed at initialization. Both peers must support bounded mode;

This PR leverages the upstream `Request.truncate_block_hashes()` API to preserve valid prefix hashes and recompute only the affected suffix, avoiding unnecessary full-prompt rehashing. In the previous NPU A/B benchmark (128K input / 1K output, concurrency 32), this optimization improved output throughput by **11.31%**, reduced mean P-side queue time by **18.1%**, and reduced mean TTFT by **18.4%**. These performance results are from the original implementation in #21857; no new NPU benchmark was performed for this revision. Related to #21437: its description explicitly proposes migrating truncation sites to the upstream primitive to avoid full-prompt rehashing. This PR implements that performance follow-up for the **Mooncake V2 base scheduler**. #21437's hybrid/layerwise changes remain a separate scope. The correctness rebuild was introduced by #20213; the upstream primitive comes from [vLLM #64096](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64096). title: [Performance][KV Transfer] Vectorize Mooncake V2 pull address construction
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mooncake V2 builds Python lists for every singleton block and every contiguous run, then loops over those groups for each layer to construct transfer descriptors. Both grouping forms are built even when a layout only uses one. This change stores run starts and lengths as NumPy arrays and vectorizes address construction. It prepares groups on demand, caching each `(request_id, coalesce)` representation within a spec/bucket call for reuse across layers. Padded or partial-head layouts skip contiguous-run preparation; mixed layouts can prepare both representations once each. A single transfer range uses scalar arithmetic. The READ interface still receives Python integer lists. The existing byte-contiguity predicates, transfer order, head offsets and independent P/D strides are preserved. No Mooncake array API or version upgrade is required. Block mapping, request scheduling, failure/completion handling and Mamba's separate address path are unchanged. This PR is based on main and is independent of #20903 (per-request submission and pool configuration). ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No configuration changes. The intended benefit is lower CPU descriptor preparation overhead for Mooncake V2 pulls with many transfer ranges. title: [Feature][MoE] Add opt-in DSpark expert-pool routing for single-device expert offload
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Offloading some MoE expert weights to CPU memory makes it possible to serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a single Ascend 950PR or 950DT device ([#18604](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18604)). During inference, the NPU can stall while waiting for selected expert weights to arrive from CPU memory, making host-to-device transfers a performance bottleneck. title: [Performance][EPLB] Optimize expert mapping and load recording
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In Model Runner V2, EPLB maps each token’s top-k logical expert IDs to physical experts and records how many tokens each local expert processed. On main, the map kernel uses a fixed tile of 256 assignments for both decode and prefill, and the record kernel handles all local experts in one Triton program. This PR selects the map tile size from the number of assignments. Small decode batches can spread work across more cores, while large prefills process more assignments per tile. The kernel specializes on top-k and keeps the assignment count dynamic, so batches within a tile size can reuse a compiled variant. For load recording, each program handles up to 256 local experts, allowing larger expert sets to run across multiple programs. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Against main, median map speedup was **3.29× on A3** and **1.25× on A5** across 28 sampled shapes. With `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` enabled, the V2 MoE factory registers map variants during startup for EPLB-enabled routers. [Release note](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/a70663a0c16003864f5aade65313dec75d9d981c/release_notes/fragments/17579.yaml) ### How was this patch tested? #### Operator results against main The map and record kernels were validated at `b7ac9d60` with CANN 9.2.1 and Triton Ascend 3.6.0. Map and record integer outputs matched the CPU reference exactly in eager execution and Graph replay. Map speedups below summarize the 28 per-shape main/PR graph latency ratios. title: [Feature]: Compose fine-grained embedding/LM head TP with standard TP — remove the TP-fold weight redundancy in stacked deployments
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `finegrained_tp_config` allows the embedding and LM head knobs to be stacked on standard `tensor_parallel_size > 1` (no `tp == 1` restriction; the feature guide's Scenario 1 is exactly such a stacked example). However, in stacked deployments these two modules shard the vocabulary **only** by the fine-grained group: the standard TP sharding is replaced rather than composed, so every TP rank keeps a replicated copy of its fine-grained slice (`vocab / finegrained_size` per rank) and the TP columns repeat the same sharded GEMM. This leaves a full `tensor_parallel_size`-fold redundancy in both per-card weight memory and per-step weight reads. For DeepSeek-R1-W8A8 with `dp=4 × tp=4` (`lmhead_tp = embedding_tp = 4`), the LM head alone reads ~232 MB of weights per decode step per card; with a composed `finegrained_size × tp_size` grid (16 shards) that drops to ~58 MB (−75%), and per-card LM-head weight memory drops by ~174 MB — the embedding improves by the same factor. Proposal: compose the two grids into one flat sharding (`shard_rank = tp_rank * finegrained_size + fg_rank`, `TP`-outer / fine-grained-inner — the same linearization the PCP path already uses), keep the token exchange on the fine-grained group, and complete the vocabulary result with one TP collective afterwards (an all-gather for the LM head, an all-reduce for the embedding). Raise the padding granularity to `lcm(padding_size, shard_count)` so the padded vocabulary always divides evenly. title: [Performance] Compose fine-grained embedding & LM head TP with standard tensor parallelism
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fine-grained TP shards vocabulary weights along the **data-parallel axis**. When stacked on standard `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, the embedding and LM head knobs used to replace the standard TP sharding with an equal-size fine-grained shard, so every TP rank kept a replicated copy of its slice — a `tensor_parallel_size`-fold redundancy in per-card weight memory and per-step weight reads. Both knobs now **compose** with standard TP: the vocabulary is sharded over the combined `finegrained_size × tensor_parallel_size` grid (`shard_rank = tp_rank * finegrained_size + fg_rank`, the linearization PCP_X_TP already uses), and one TP collective afterwards completes the vocabulary result — an all-gather for the LM head, an all-reduce for the embedding. The padding granularity is raised to `lcm(padding_size, shard_count)`. With `tensor_parallel_size == 1` the behavior is unchanged. For example, with 8 ranks (`dp=4 × tp=2`, `lmhead_tp=4`): | global rank | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **old** shard (`lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | | **new** shard (`tp.rank * 4 + lhtp.rank`) | 0 | 4 | 1 | 5 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 7 | - Draft-model heads resolve through the same plan; the DFlash2 candidate exchange appends the same TP all-gather so its Top-K union spans all composed shards. - `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/Fine_grained_TP.md` documents composing instead of replacing. ### Measured results (single-node stacked deployment) Atlas 900 A3 (16 NPUs), MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-W8A8, DP4 × TP4 / EP16, DSpark s

title: [Performance] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 indexer weights projection overlap
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR optimizes **DeepSeek V4.1 Indexer weights projection scheduling** by adjusting the synchronization point between the main and auxiliary NPU streams. Previously, the main stream waited for `weights_done` immediately after Query RoPE. This introduced unnecessary serialization: the independent FP32 input cast could not overlap with the auxiliary weights projection, and query quantization was also delayed. title: [BugFix][Multimodal] Cap encoder ACL graph frame slots by token budget
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Encoder ACL graphs currently use the global frame limit for every token budget. When video is enabled and that limit exceeds a graph's budget, Qwen capture layouts perform unnecessary padded-frame work: for example, a 128-token graph receives 1,000 frame slots. title: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
summary: Mixture of Block Attention (MoBA) reduces long-context computation by selecting key-value (KV) blocks for each query. FlashMoBA implements MoBA efficiently but retains a fixed Top-k budget and query-centric schedule. Fixed Top-k applies one budget across different score distributions and couples routing to task granularity; query-range ownership fragments K/V reuse when several ranges select the same column. We present LightningMoBA, which co-designs selection and execution through dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining. Dynamic routing thresholds MoBA's per-query block scores and directly emits variable-cardinality sparse metadata. KV-centric ownership groups selected rows by (query head, KV block) column, splits high-fanout columns into bounded tasks, and reuses each task's loaded KV tile. On Hopper, pipelining overlaps regular K/V transfers and irregular query gathers with Tensor Core computation. Together, these mechanisms decouple retention from GPU scheduling granularity. At matched Top-16 retention across five checkpoints, LightningMoBA accelerates end-to-end generation by 1.20 to 1.60x while raising mean RULER score from 74.42 to 75.28.

title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent settings (best 95.2%). The System 1 agent filled 97.0% of 6,056 stated argument values. No System 1 call contained invented content, against 5.5-19.7% of LLM calls. The System 1 Agents framework is freely available as open-source software at https://github.com/eltzanis/SystemOneAgents.

title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid (>250times dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension (d to d+K) with d/(d+K) norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential (+254,-256) tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed {+,-,times} circuits in constant TC^0 depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, N=1{,}728; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic (N=1{,}200, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, le 0.036%) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, le 0.057%) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
summary: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.

title: [Spec Decode] Support anchor-first (sample_from_anchor) DFlash/DFlash2 drafts

Two parts of #54154 are no longer needed on main: - **V1-runner rejection:** the V1 GPU model runner has been removed, and only the V2 runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu`) runs DFlash. - **Scheduler drafting-slot tweak in `SpeculativeConfig`:** main now delegates this to `SpeculatorConfig.max_num_new_slots_for_drafting`. title: [Bugfix][Tool Calling] Preserve leading content when Jamba tool calls share start delta (#69213)
summary: ## Problem When streaming with Jamba tool parser (`--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser jamba`), any text arriving in the same delta as the `<tool_calls>` opening tag was dropped. As described in #69213, this occurs whenever a delta holds several tokens—such as with `stream_interval > 1`, during speculative decoding, or when the output collector batches output deltas. The parser skipped emitting the leading content and immediately switched to parsing tool calls, resulting in lost user-facing reasoning or conversational text preceding the tool invocation. ## Solution Partition `delta_text` on `self.tool_calls_start_token` when the opener is encountered. If there is leading text before `<tool_calls>`: 1. Recursively call `extract_tool_calls_streaming` for the remainder starting with `<tool_calls>`. 2. Prepend the leading content to the emitted delta, or return `DeltaMessage(content=leading)` if tool call extraction is not yet ready. ## Verification - Added regression test `test_extract_tool_calls_streaming_content_in_tool_start_delta` in `tests/tool_parsers/test_jamba_tool_parser.py`. - Negative proof: confirmed prior to patch, `content == 'Let'` instead of `'Let me check. '` (lost `' me check. '`). - Positive proof: with fix applied, `content == 'Let me check. '` and tool call `get_current_weather` is extracted cleanly. - Validated with `ruff check` (all checks passed) and `ruff format --check` (2 files verified). Fixes #69213.

title: [RFC]: support n sampling requests to eliminate redundant prefill computation and memory
summary: ### Motivation. Background: the `n` sampling parameter allows generating multiple different responses for a single prompt. The original implementation immediately splits an `n>1` request into `n` separate child requests at the entry point. It causes severe resource waste especialy in **PD Disaggregation** scenarios. The problems with immediate splitting in PD disaggregation: 1. **Redundant Prefill Computation**: The same prompt is computed `n` times on the Prefill instance 2. **Memory Waste**: Each child request independently allocates KV cache, storing `n` copies of identical prefill KV 3. **Network Transfer Overhead**: The same KV cache is transferred `n` times from P-side to D-side Even with Prefix Caching enabled, the original approach still has significant limitations: - Prefix caching operates at the Block level; only complete blocks can be cached and reused - Network transfer remains `n` copies of complete KV cache in PD disaggregation Goals: - Eliminate redundant prefill computation for `n>1` requests in both PD disaggregation and PD colocated scenarios - Reduce memory footprint by sharing prefill KV cache among child requests - Minimize network transfer overhead in PD disaggregation scenarios - Maintain backward compatibility with existing API interfaces ### Proposed Change. Implement a **delayed split** strategy: defer the splitting of `n>1` requests until after prefill completion, allowing all child requests to share the prefill KV cache. #### Architecture Overview **Entry Point Decision** (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py`): - D-side (KV consumer): Immediate split a

title: [WIP][Spec Decode] Drafter early exit in a CUDA graph WHILE node
summary: Autoregressive drafters (MTP, EAGLE) can stop drafting on the GPU without a host sync, so async scheduling is preserved. With VLLM_DYN_DRAFT set, the captured FULL decode graph runs draft steps 1..k-1 inside one CUDA graph WHILE node; a Triton kernel decides after each step whether the batch's expected gain from the next draft position (from the acceptance estimator's confidences) clears a threshold that adaptive verification derives from its cost model each step ("cost"), or never stops ("full"). Adaptive verification still admits as many drafts as the CPU budgeted, since the CPU-built batch layout depends on it; admitted drafts at positions the drafter skipped are verified as placeholders through the invalid-draft path, so outputs are unchanged, and the acceptance estimator is graded only on drafted positions. title: [Perf][Kernel] Mamba2 SSD chunk_scan: launch all heads of a chunk together
summary: Fixes #69206 ## Overview _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel puts chunks on grid axis 1 and heads on grid axis 2, so the GPU runs every chunk of head 0, then every chunk of head 1, and so on. Each chunk's 256 x 256 fp32 CB block (from _bmm_chunk_fwd) is read by every head of its group. While the CB blocks of all chunks in one call fit in L2 this costs nothing; once they do not (on an RTX 4060 Ti with 32 MB of L2, past about 16k tokens per call), every head re-reads them from DRAM and the kernel's time per token jumps. This PR swaps the two grid axes, so all heads of a chunk run together and share its CB block while it is in L2. Two lines plus a comment; the work per program is unchanged, and outputs and final states are bit-identical. ## When it matters With chunked prefill off, every long prompt goes through the SSD op in one call, so any prompt above about 16-24k tokens hits the cliff; this is the main case the PR helps. With chunked prefill on, the cliff depends on the total number of prefill tokens in one SSD call, not on prompt length (1 x 32768, 4 x 8192 and 16 x 2048 behave the same). vLLM's default token budget per step (engine/arg_utils.py) is 2048 for vllm serve and 8192 for offline LLM on most GPUs including A100, 8192 / 16384 on H100 and H200, and 16384 for both on GPUs with at least 160 GB. Default settings on the GPUs measured here therefore stay below the cliff and see no change; it applies when the budget is raised above about 16k tokens. ## Claims - SSD op, RTX 4060 Ti, current main: **2.2x** faster at 32k tokens per call, 1.34-1.37x at 24k, 1.03-1.07x at 8-16k, and no

title: [Perf][Attention] Vectorize per-token-head KV tile loads in Triton attention
summary: ## Overview The Triton attention kernels read per-token-head KV caches (`int4_per_token_head`, `int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`) one byte per load instruction. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Dequantize directly-consumed block-FP8 weights before Marlin repacks them
summary: ## What this fixes On devices without FP8 hardware (SM 8.x / A100 / A800) the FP8 quant method selects Marlin. Marlin's `process_weights_after_loading` repacks `layer.weight` into an opaque layout and rewrites the block scales (folding an exponent bias into them). That is fine for layers that go through `apply_weights()`, but some layers are consumed **directly**: DeepSeek-V4's `o_proj` sets `layer.is_bmm = True` and reads `layer.weight` together with its block scales in a fused FP8 einsum. With Marlin selected it reads packed integers as FP8 and the model emits garbage. title: [Metrics] Add `vllm:kv_cache_token_usage_perc`
summary: ## Purpose `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` counts blocks. That is the right unit for scheduling — blocks are the allocation unit — but it is not the right unit for judging how much of the KV cache actually holds keys and values. A block holding one token is indistinguishable from a full one, so with short prompts the reported figure can be nearly double the real occupancy, and an operator has no way to see it. Concretely, on `facebook/opt-125m` with `--block-size 16` and a saturating stream of 17-token prompts, the existing gauge reads a median of **66.7%** while only **36.5%** of the token slots hold anything — a 30-point gap that is invisible today. With 400-token prompts on the same server the two agree to within 1.2 points, so the gap is a property of the workload shape, not a constant tax. That distinction is actionable: it is exactly the number you need to decide whether lowering `--block-size` is worth it. Today the only way to get it is to reconstruct it offline. This is closely related to the motivation in #45702, which notes that a coarse block size "hurts prompts whose reusable boundaries are not multiples of the [...] block size, such as chat turns, tool-call boundaries, and agentic traces." Those are the same workload shapes where this gap is largest. That RFC is about *hit granularity*; this PR is about making the *memory* cost of block granularity observable. ## Approach A new gauge `vllm:kv_cache_token_usage_perc`, computed alongside the existing one in `Scheduler.make_stats`, from `KVCacheManager.token_usage(self.running)`. title: [Performance]: Mamba2 _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel slows down about 2x past 16k-24k tokens per call because its launch order defeats L2 reuse
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance I found this while measuring the cost per token of Mamba2 SSD prefill at different token budgets. The cost per token is flat up to about 16k tokens in one SSD call and then jumps. Almost all of the jump is in _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel; the other SSD kernels scale linearly. The cause seems to be the kernel's launch order. In ssd_chunk_scan.py the program ids are pid_c = program_id(axis=1) and pid_h = program_id(axis=2) (lines 248 and 249), and the grid is (tiles, nchunks, nheads) (line 572). The GPU therefore runs every chunk of head 0, then every chunk of head 1, and so on. Each chunk's 256 x 256 fp32 CB block from _bmm_chunk_fwd (ssd_combined.py, line 129) is read by every head of its group. That is 256 KB per chunk, so once a call has more than about 128 chunks (32 MB, the L2 of an RTX 4060 Ti, at 32k tokens), the CB blocks no longer fit in L2 and every head reads them again from DRAM. Proposed fix: swap the two grid axes, so that all heads of a chunk run together and share its CB block while it is in L2. It is a two-line change; the work per program is unchanged and outputs are bit-identical. I have a fix and will link the pull request in a comment below. Measured improvements (full tables, tests and method in the PR): - SSD op on an RTX 4060 Ti, current main: 2.2x faster at 32k tokens per call and 1.34x to 1.37x at 24k; 1.03x to 1.07x at 8k to 16k; no change for short multi-prompt splits. - SSD op on an A100, current main: 1.41x to 1.45x at 32k to 64k tokens per call, 1.23x at 24k, 1.00x to 1.03x up to 16k. - End to end, Granite-4.0-H-35

title: [Performance]: Mamba2 SSD prefill cost grows with the number of short prompts in a step, not with tokens (about 20x for the same 2,048 tokens)
summary: ### Proposal to improve performance I found this while measuring how Mamba2 prefill time in vLLM depends on how a step's tokens are split into prompts. In packed (varlen) prefill, vLLM never lets an SSD chunk cross a sequence boundary, so a step full of short prompts becomes many short chunks. The SSD op then costs far more for the same number of tokens: on current main, 2,048 tokens given as 256 prompts of 8 tokens take about 20 times longer than one 2,048-token prompt. Two parts of the Triton SSD path still pay full-chunk cost for each short chunk: 1. _chunk_scan_fwd_kernel launches cdiv(chunk_size, BLOCK_SIZE_M) M-blocks for every chunk. For an 8-token chunk with chunk_size 256 and BLOCK_SIZE_M 64, three of the four M-blocks cover rows past the chunk end: they load the previous-state tile, do the masked math and store nothing. chunk_size_limit is computed (ssd_chunk_scan.py, line 289) but not used to skip them. 2. For a sequence that fits in one chunk, _chunk_state_fwd writes an fp32 state for the chunk (ssd_chunk_state.py, lines 338 and 347), _state_passing_fwd reads it back, writes it again in the state dtype (ssd_state_passing.py, line 105) and then writes the final state into the cache (line 122). That final state is just exp(dA_cs_last) * initial_state + chunk_state, which _chunk_state_fwd already has. Proposed fix: return early from M-blocks past the chunk end, and, when the caller passes a state cache (final_states_out) and does not ask for every chunk's state, write a single-chunk sequence's final state directly from _chunk_state_fwd and skip it in _state_passing

summary: ## Overview The Ripple parser (added in #65745) has no `arg_value_extender`. Every streamed delta inside a tool call therefore re-runs `_ripple_arg_converter` and `ParserEngine._safe_arg_prefix` over the whole call so far, so streaming one tool call costs O(N^2) CPU in the API server. This PR adds an extender for open string values of the `arguments` object, which is the same approach #62334 proposes for Granite and the one Qwen3, GLM-4.7, MiniMax M2 and DeepSeek V3.2/V4 already use. ## Claims - Streaming a Ripple tool call with a long string argument becomes linear in the argument length. On a 4k-token argument the streaming parse goes from 97.9 s to 0.92 s on the same machine. - Arguments without long strings (numbers, many short keys) stream no slower than main. The follow-up commit 58c10266e6 sets `arg_structural_chars`, so a delta outside an open string value that carries no JSON structure skips the conversion. On about 8k characters streamed one character per delta, `{"data": [0, 1, 2, ...]}` takes 6.4 s against 13.5 s on main, and the long string case keeps its win. - The streamed arguments, content and reasoning are identical to main at every delta (checked by a randomized differential run and by the new tests). ## Validation Benchmark through the server's streaming step (`ChatStreamProcessor.step`, one Qwen3 token per delta, `--tool-call-parser ripple --reasoning-parser ripple`), one `write_file` call whose `content` argument grows. The script checks that the concatenated streamed arguments decode to the expected JSON. | tokens in the call | main | this PR | |---|-

title: [Bug]: Triton fp32 -> FP8 (e4m3) casts round twice on SM89 (Ada): FP8 KV cache and NVFP4 emulation store values one e4m3 step off
summary: ### Your current environment ```text GPU: NVIDIA L4 (compute capability 8.9), driver 595.112.07 OS: Linux-7.0.0-1017-aws-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 Python: 3.14.10 vLLM: main c32251b5d1 (0.34.0rc1.dev1129+gc32251b5d, precompiled install) torch: 2.14.0+cu132 (CUDA runtime 13.2) triton: 3.8.0 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug On SM89 (Ada: L4, L40S, RTX 40xx), a Triton cast from fp32 to `tl.float8e4nv` rounds twice, so about 0.4% of fp32 inputs end up one e4m3 step away from the round-to-nearest-even result. For example 3.1259 is stored as 3.0; torch and SM90+ give 3.25. This affects every vLLM Triton kernel that quantizes an fp32 value to e4m3 on these GPUs, including the FP8 KV cache store of `TRITON_ATTN`. **Cause.** Triton 3.8.0 (what vLLM's CUDA build gets with torch 2.14.0) uses the direct PTX conversion only from SM90. The TTGIR asks for `rtne`, but on SM89 the PTX is: ``` tt.fp_to_fp %x, rounding = rtne : tensor<...xf32> -> tensor<...xf8E4M3FN> cvt.rz.f16.f32 %rs1, %r1; # truncate to fp16 cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f16x2 %rs3, %r3; # then round to nearest even ``` A value just past an e4m3 tie (within one fp16 ulp, away from zero) is truncated onto the tie, and the tie then goes to the even neighbour. Inputs that are exact in fp16 (so bf16 and fp16 values) and exact ties convert correctly. Compiling the same kernel for `sm_90`, `sm_100` and `sm_120` gives a single `cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32`, so only SM89 is affected. The condition is in `ElementwiseOpToLLVM.cpp`: v3.8.0 has `computeCapability >= 90`, v3.9.0 changed it to `>= 89` for e4m3. The 3.9.0 source was read, not run. **Rep

title: [Bugfix] Fix GQA head-tile mapping in Triton decode attention
summary: Fixes #68413. Port of the already-merged SGLang fix (sgl-project/sglang#47802) to vLLM. ## Problem `decode_attention_fwd` assigns the wrong KV head to some query heads when the GQA group size (query heads per KV head) is greater than `BLOCK_H = 16` and not a multiple of it, with at least two KV heads. This is the head layout of GLM-4-32B-0414 (48 query heads, 2 KV heads, group 24). The launcher creates `cdiv(head_num, min(16, group))` head tiles. A tile covers 16 consecutive query heads, but the KV head is `tile // cdiv(group, 16)`. With group 24, tile 1 covers heads 16-31 yet is assigned wholly to KV head 0; heads 24-31 should read KV head 1. ## Fix 1. Give each KV head a whole number of head tiles: launch `num_kv_heads * cdiv(group, BLOCK_H)` tiles. 2. In `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1`, when `group % BLOCK_H != 0`, reindex tile-local heads from the group start (`cur_head = cur_kv_head * group + head_in_group`) and mask heads past the group end. This leaves groups that are multiples of 16, groups smaller than 16, MHA, and MLA paths unchanged. ## Test `test_decode_attention_gqa_group_above_tile` covers `(H_Q, H_KV)` of `(48, 2)`, `(40, 2)`, `(16, 2)`, `(32, 2)`, `(64, 2)` against a `repeat_interleave` PyTorch reference. ## Validation Kaggle CPU with Triton interpreter enabled; `Req_to_tokens` passed as a real block table; max abs error vs PyTorch reference: | H_Q | H_KV | group | before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 48 | 2 | 24 | 1.510e+00 | 4.172e-07 | | 40 | 2 | 20 | 1.417e+00 | 5.960e-07 | | 16 | 2 | 8 | 7.153e-07 | 7.153e-07 | | 32 | 2 | 16 | 4.470e-07 | 4.470e-0

title: [Bugfix] Fix Marlin MoE W13 scale permutation under tensor parallelism
summary: ## Purpose Two-line fix. Marlin MoE weight prep (`int_wna16.py`) permutes the W13 scales with `size_k=intermediate_size_per_partition`, but W13's K is the hidden size. title: [Core] Add gap-tolerant prefix cache reuse
summary: ## Summary Add gap-tolerant prefix cache reuse: when a middle block in a cached prefix is evicted, the matching blocks on both sides of the gap can still be reused, rather than discarding all subsequent blocks. ## Motivation Traditional prefix caching requires continuous match from the start — if any middle block is evicted, all subsequent blocks become unusable. This wastes significant KV cache, especially in long-context scenarios where partial evictions are common. ## Implementation - Add `enable_gap_tolerant_reuse` config flag (env: VLLM_GAP_TOLERANT_PREFIX_REUSE) - Detect secondary gap hits after the contiguous prefix match - Pin gap-hit blocks until they are grafted or discarded - Release pinning when requests abort or complete ## Testing - Added unit test `test_gap_tolerant_prefix_reuse` covering: - Normal gap hit flow - Gap hit after middle block eviction - Request abort → gap hits discarded → ref counts released

title: [CI][Bugfix] Precompute Gemma3n sparsity quantiles before inference
summary: ## Root Cause The CI failure was exposed by [vllm-project/vllm#60648](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60648) (`8f8f6c8fc8`), which added Gemma3n Omni generation coverage through the Transformers backend with `enforce_eager=True`. It exposed a pre-existing synchronization issue in HF's `Gemma3nTextMLP._gaussian_topk`, rather than introducing an incorrect sparsity formula. For layers with nonzero activation sparsity, HF creates a CUDA tensor from the constant sparsity value and reconstructs its Gaussian quantile on every forward pass. This performs a host/device transfer inside inference. CI enables `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, introduced by [vllm-project/vllm#43107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43107), so the otherwise functional eager path raises `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`. Pre-merge coverage did not require this combination: the new Omni generation test belongs to the optional extended multimodal nightly job. The introducing PR reported local Gemma3n/HF logprob parity, but did not document running it with GPU synchronization checks enabled. Output parity alone does not detect this synchronization issue. The fix precomputes the constant quantile during Transformers-backend initialization and stores it in a nonpersistent buffer. The forward pass retains HF's formula and dtype conversion but no longer creates the constant on the device. This removes the synchronization rather than disabling the check; the PR reports nine bit-exact MLP cases and a real-backend eager generation parity test with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. ## Ov

title: KV transfer scheduler frees blocks unconditionally in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` — assert crash reproduced with LMCacheMPConnector; in-flight transfers are not cancelled after request abort
summary: ### Summary `Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` frees the KV-transfer block set of a request **unconditionally for both directions** (`finished_sending` and `finished_recving`), with no per-direction accounting and no check that no in-flight transfer is still targeting those blocks: - vLLM **v0.30.0**: `scheduler.py:2998-3025` - vLLM **v0.33.0**: `scheduler.py:3556-3582` (unchanged behavior; we verified the installed wheel at runtime, SHA-256 `d76cc222…e501a`) The KVConnector base contract (`kv_connector/v1/base.py:377-403, 582-601`) says blocks should not be freed until the connector returns the request from `get_finished()`. In practice each connector has to enforce that discipline by its own bookkeeping. When a connector reports a completion for one direction while a transfer in the other direction is still in flight, the scheduler frees the blocks, the blocks get reused by a new request, and the in-flight DMA continues to write into them. Depending on ordering, this either (a) crashes later with the known `assert req_id in self.requests` when the late completion arrives, or (b) **silently writes one request's KV into blocks now owned by another request**. ### New runtime evidence: in-flight transfers are NOT cancelled on abort We built a deterministic harness against vLLM 0.30.0 + LMCache v0.5.6rc1 (`LMCacheMPConnector`, `kv_role=kv_both`, MP server CPU storage, single Tesla T4, TP1) — the same configuration family as #60986 — and measured what actually happens after an abort: - 19.5k-token sessions, 6 concurrent resumes, abort

title: [Perf][Attention] Enable ShardQ for SM90 FlashInfer NoPE sparse MLA prefill
summary: ## Purpose On Hopper, GLM-5.3-Flash uses the FlashInfer FA3 sparse MLA backend. With TP8, the existing head-sharded path scores the same long-prefill query rows on all eight ranks. This PR connects that backend to the token split and collectives already merged in #63956. Each rank scores its own prefill rows and attends them with all heads. The existing decode path continues to partition by head. The backend opts in for NoPE with non-FP8 KV, under the existing ShardQ eligibility and length checks. BF16 KV was tested. As fast as ~40GB/s for a single modern NIC. GPU Direct Storage (4): Offers the best theoretical performance of local files. Triggered via ioctl for GDS or P2P based IO, with limited applicable scenarios. Direct IO (1): NVMe direct I/O. Requires block size alignment and cannot be shared across processes. Page Cache MMAP (3): File memory mapping. Not ideal for KV Cache workloads (due to linear memory growth). Page Cache Copy From/To User (2): Has the lowest performance, yet delivers the best general compatibility. title: [Model][Perf] Overlap mixed GDN decode and prefill recurrent kernels
summary: ## Summary Overlap the already-separated non-spec GDN recurrent decode update with the FlashInfer prefill chunk scan in mixed Qwen GDN batches. The path is opt-in through `VLLM_GDN_DECODE_PREFILL_OVERLAP=1` and remains fail-closed unless all of the following hold: - CUDA-like platform; - FlashInfer GDN prefill backend; - `mamba_cache_mode="none"`, which provides one private state slot per request; - mixed non-spec decode + prefill batch; - at least 4096 prefill tokens. The existing serial decode-then-prefill route remains unchanged for feature-off, small, pure, speculative, non-FlashInfer, non-CUDA, and prefix-cache-mode cases. ## Implementation - Prepare FlashInfer-only dtype/layout conversions before the stream fork. - Launch the FlashInfer chunk scan first on one shared GDN auxiliary stream. - Launch recurrent decode on the current stream and join before state/output use. - Reuse streams and CUDA events created during layer initialization. - Preserve decode-first output order and disjoint SSM-state updates. title: [Feature]: Add DFly speculative decoding and D-Cut support（Related to issue 50245）
summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ## Motivation We would like to propose adding DFly speculative decoding support to vLLM, together with D-Cut, a dynamic draft pruning method for speculative decoding. DFly is the main speculative decoding method in this proposal. Existing DFlash/DSpark-style paths are treated as baselines or compatibility foundations. The primary goal is to make DFly usable in vLLM's standard serving stack and improve its runtime efficiency with D-Cut. ## Feature overview This proposal focuses on two main features: ### 1. DFly speculative decoding DFly is a speculative decoding method that uses a draft model to generate candidate tokens for the target model to verify. The proposed integration adds support for running DFly-style draft models inside vLLM, including: - recognizing DFly draft model architectures - registering the DFly draft model implementation - routing DFly through the speculative decoding runtime - supporting the required draft-token transport and verification flow - keeping compatibility with existing speculative decoding infrastructure The expected result is that users can serve target models with a DFly draft model through normal vLLM APIs, without relying on an external or out-of-tree runtime. ### 2. D-Cut dynamic draft pruning D-Cut is a dynamic pruning strategy for speculative decoding. Instead of always verifying a fixed number of draft tokens, D-Cut chooses how many draft tokens to keep for each request based on draft confidence and runtime cost. This helps avoid wasting verification compute on low-confidence draft tokens. At a

summary: ## Purpose Fix two initialization failures when serving a model with `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4`, particularly on NVIDIA Ampere GPUs. ### 1. title: [PD] Emit inactive KV blocks for decode affinity
summary: Publish GPU block inactivity when the last request reference is released so external schedulers can maintain accurate decode load signals. ## Purpose Add a new KV cache event, `BlockInactive`, so external PD schedulers can track when a GPU prefix-cached block is no longer actively referenced. Today, KV event consumers can observe `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved`, but cannot reliably detect that the last request released a block while it may still remain in the prefix cache. Without a refcount-zero signal, decode-affinity load accounting (`active_blocks`) tends to only increase or needs fragile heuristics. This PR: - Adds `BlockInactive` to `KVEventBatch`, emitted from `BlockPool.free_blocks()` when `ref_cnt` drops to 0 for a hashed GPU block (`medium=MEDIUM_GPU`). - Publishes it through the existing KV event path (`take_events()` / ZMQ). No new scheduler-loop wiring. - Gates emission for Prefill-only instances: `kv_role == "kv_producer"` still emits `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved`, but does **not** emit `BlockInactive`, so Prefill frees do not pollute decode load signals. - Decode (`kv_consumer`), union (`kv_both`), and non-PD setups continue to emit Inactive via `KVTransferConfig.should_emit_block_inactive` (`kv_role != "kv_producer"`). Related issue: #50730 ## Test Plan pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \ -k "free_blocks_emits_block_inactive or free_blocks_skips_block_inactive or kv_transfer_should_emit_block_inactive" \ -q Coverage: free_blocks emits BlockInactive when enable_block_inactive_events=True. Prefill-style gate (enable_block_inactive_events=False) sti

title: [Spec Decode][Perf] Optimize DSpark Markov head with addmm
summary: ## Purpose DSpark produces the base logits for all speculative positions in one LM-head call, then applies the dense Markov projection sequentially for each draft step. The existing path launches a projection and a separate elementwise add for every step. This PR makes the DSpark sample layout step-major, so each step owns a contiguous `[request, vocab]` base-logits slice, and adds the Markov bias with: ```python base_logits.addmm_(markov_embed, weight.t()) ``` The beta=1 GEMM writes directly into the LM-head output after its final read. This removes the separate add kernel without allocating an out-of-place result. The fast path is limited to NVIDIA CUDA, an unquantized replicated Markov head, compatible dtypes, contiguous logits, unit logit scale, and no soft cap. All other configurations keep the existing non-mutating path. The fixed `max_num_reqs` step stride also keeps the layout valid when full CUDA Graphs pad the request batch. DFlash remains request-major. ### Duplicate-work check I searched open vLLM PRs for DSpark, Markov head, addmm, in-place, and step-major changes. I did not find another PR implementing this dense step-major/in-place path. - #49969 is an opt-in top-k Markov projection that restricts the candidate rows. This PR keeps the exact dense projection and optimizes its memory and kernel sequence. The approaches are conceptually complementary, although they touch two of the same files and may need a rebase if both land. - #50424 adds quantization plumbing to the Markov head; this PR deliberately falls back for quantized heads. - #47584 adds an opt-in FP8

title: [RFC]: Unify the Tensor Type for Device-Pointer Storage to `torch.uint64`
summary: ### Motivation. In vLLM, several kernels accept `Tensor` objects whose elements are not ordinary numeric values but raw device pointers (i.e., `data_ptr()` of other tensors). These pointer tensors are used for batch memory copies, grouped operations (e.g., MoE where each expert has its own pointer array), attention block-table lookups, and cross-GPU IPC workspaces. Device pointers are semantically unsigned 64-bit values (`CUdeviceptr` / `uintptr_t`). However, the current vLLM codebase exhibits three inconsistent storage practices, one of which is clearly problematic: 1. **Unconditional use of `torch.int64`** — problematic. Assigning an unsigned address (`data_ptr()`) to a `torch.int64` tensor triggers `ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long` when the address exceeds `2^63-1`. title: [RFC]: Complete Model Runner V2 pipeline parallelism: scheduling, speculative decoding, and PP-first DP/EP topology
summary: ### Motivation. > [!NOTE] > This RFC expands the original request-admission proposal into an end-to-end plan for Model Runner V2 (MRV2) pipeline-parallel feature composition. The original proposal remains Workstream A below, with its prototype in #50410. MRV2 pipeline parallelism (PP) already overlaps multiple batches to reduce pipeline bubbles (#42187). With asynchronous scheduling, it keeps `pp_size + 1` batch slots in flight, while a decode request becomes eligible again after a `pp_size`-step cadence. title: [Frontend] Support repetition_detection as a server-side default
summary: ## Purpose Enable `repetition_detection` as a **server-side default sampling parameter**. vLLM already ships the detector (`check_sequence_repetition` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/utils.py`, terminating with `FinishReason.REPETITION`) and exposes it per-request in the OpenAI API — but there is no way for an operator to turn it on for a whole deployment: the `get_diff_sampling_param` allowlist silently drops it from `--generation-config` / `--override-generation-config`, and the OpenAI protocols never fell back to `default_sampling_params` for it. **Motivating failure:** on a `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` deployment, requests with large context (~240K tokens) degenerated into emitting a single repeated token on every step, never sampling EOS, and ran to `max_tokens` — keeping the server saturated for ~19 hours. A server-side repetition default would have terminated these requests within a few dozen tokens, containing the incident automatically. Today the only lever is asking every client to pass the parameter on every request. With this PR, an operator sets it once: ```bash vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --override-generation-config '{"repetition_detection": {"max_pattern_size": 8, "min_count": 4}}' ``` and every request that doesn't specify its own `repetition_detection` is guarded; requests can still override or disable it per-request. title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pass FlashInfer metadata in the Qwen3-Omni audio encoder
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview With `--mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER`, `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` (and any model using `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder`) fails at engine startup with `assert max_seqlen is not None` in the FlashInfer ViT wrapper. Non-FlashInfer backends keep the host-side `max_seqlen` path from #68099. ## Validation DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, aarch64), current `main` (after #68831), torch 2.14.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.4. title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Match multimodal token counts to the processor for Unlimited-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR, MiniCPM-V 4.6 and MiniCPM-OCR
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Four multimodal models disagree with their HF processor on token counts or options. Separate commits per model: - **Unlimited-OCR / -2:** placeholders assume the default `max_crops` (32 / 16), so a request with a lower `max_crops` fails, and with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` it kills the engine core. Placeholders now use the processor's `num_image_tokens`, as #68127 did for DeepSeek-OCR. - **DeepSeek-OCR / -2:** the square profiling dummy tiles as 2x2, while tall pages tile up to `max_crops`. The dummy is now one column of `max_crops` tiles. - **MiniCPM-V 4.6:** the inherited canvas assumes equal-cost slices; 4.6's token count doesn't, so ordinary images exceed the budget (720 vs 648) and a 16-frame video is rejected at defaults. 4.6 now profiles its own worst case, profiling and processing share an aspect bound (images 200:1 as in other vLLM processors, video frames 50:1), and video honors a request-level or `videos_kwargs` `max_slice_nums` like images do. Follow-up from #67111. - **MiniCPM-OCR:** video frames were given upsize options no released Transformers has (5.21 to 5.23 only declare `small_image_upsize`), so every video failed and the engine doesn't start with default limits. Frames now pin `small_image_upsize="always"`, images forward the real option, and OCR profiles the 4.6 worst-case canvas at `"always"`, the maximum of every upsize mode. ## Claims - **Unlimited-OCR.** A request-level `max_crops` below 32 / 16 works. title: [Bugfix] Emit Nemotron diffusion prompt logprobs before denoising
summary: ## Root Cause The failure was introduced by [vllm-project/vllm#58387](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58387) (`3aeca630d8`), which added Nemotron diffusion support. Unlike autoregressive generation, diffusion finishes prefill without emitting a token, while the shared prompt-logprobs worker returns completed scores immediately. This violates the scheduler's existing assumption that completed prompt scores accompany token output, triggering the assertion even in the PP=1 reference run. Pre-merge coverage missed this combination: the new Nemotron tests exercised generated-token logprobs, while the per-PR PP-equivalence subset excluded Nemotron. The full architecture sweep, configured as an optional nightly job, requests prompt logprobs and exposed the scheduler contract mismatch. The scheduler change retains these scores until the first token-bearing output, preserving the existing output and TTFT semantics. The change belongs at this shared output boundary, where prompt scores and sampled tokens are combined, rather than changing diffusion's prefill or denoising behavior. ## Overview Fix the `NemotronLabsDiffusionModel` PP-equivalence failure in [Buildkite 104867](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104867/list). The scheduler assertion occurs during the PP=1 reference run. ## Claims Emit completed prompt logprobs even when diffusion prefill produces no generated tokens, keeping the request active for denoising. Only the scheduler, one end-to-end test, and documentation change. ## Validation Base: `0bf9c07376`. Tested the patch before committing it as `757c51c8ec`

title: [Perf][Inkling2-Mini] Improve small M GEMM on 5090 (sm120)
summary: ## Overview Three decode-time improvements to Inkling2's SM12x low-M (M <= 16) BF16 GEMM from #69028 (`ops/gemv.py`, now `ops/ll_gemm_sm120.py` as `sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm`): 1. **Split-K for narrow outputs.** When there are too few column tiles to fill the GPU, the kernel splits K, deterministically. The short-conv projection (N=32) now uses it instead of `F.linear`: **up to 7.1×** faster. 2. **Batched GEMM for the loop blend.** A 3D weight runs a batched matmul, replacing the blend's two `torch.bmm` calls: **up to 5.1×** faster. 3. **Fused q/k/v projection.** `qkv_bmm` computes q, k and v, each from its own input, in one launch instead of three: **1.2×** faster. End to end on RTX 5090, decode steps are **6.5–7.5% faster** (`vllm bench serve`, DSpark). title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Use W8A16 for the fp8 draft lm_head on GPUs without FP8 GEMMs
summary: ## Purpose `draft_lm_head_quantization: "fp8"` fails at startup on GPUs without FP8 GEMMs (SM80/SM86: A100, A10, RTX 3090): ``` ValueError: FP8 PTPC online quant requires a kernel that honors per-token activation quantization; MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel is W8A16 weight-only. title: [Mamba] Add FlashInfer FP16 GDN ReplaySSM for Qwen3.5 and Qwen4
summary: ## Overview Adds FlashInfer ReplaySSM to Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) Gated DeltaNet (GDN), extending the shared lifecycle from #55688. ReplaySSM stores a recurrent checkpoint and compact replay buffers instead of a full recurrent-state copy for each speculative token. This PR uses the released FlashInfer kernels. Related Triton integrations are #62004, #64699, and #56466. ## Claims - Supports standard decoding and MTP with up to seven draft tokens through `--use-replayssm`. - Supports prefix caching with Mamba cache mode `align`, plus decoding without prefix caching in mode `none`. - Requires FlashInfer 0.7.3, SM100-class GPUs, and FP16 recurrent state. Model activations remain BF16. ## Validation **Direct comparison with Triton ReplaySSM (November 9–10, 2026).** Both backends use Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 on one GB300, TP1, a 256-request limit, and CUDA graphs. title: [Bugfix][Core] Widen EAGLE periodic SWA tails so a diverging sibling keeps its prefix-cache hit
summary: ## Summary Fixes #64808 (fix option B from the issue): with EAGLE spec decoding and a positive `--prefix-cache-retention-interval`, a request sharing a long prefix falls back a whole retention interval (16384 -> 8192 cached tokens in the reporter's repro) instead of hitting the cached segment tail. ## Root cause `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask` places each periodic segment tail so its right edge sits on the aligned boundary block (the EAGLE peek block, `shift=1`). A sibling that diverges right after a segment boundary cannot use that peek block, so its sliding-window hit lands one block lower — and those blocks were never cached. The shared-prefix junction path already handles the same situation by appending `shared_prefix_boundary - block_size` as an extra reachable boundary; the periodic-segment path had no equivalent. ## Change In the periodic-segment branch of `SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`, widen each tail by one block on the low side under EAGLE (`tail_need = need + 1`). This only ever caches additional blocks (dense caching is the safe fallback), never drops a reachable block. The non-EAGLE path, the reachable-boundary tails, and the final-partial-segment branch are unchanged. Cost: one extra cached block per periodic checkpoint, matching the reporter's measurement for option B (per-request hits 0/16256/16256/16256 instead of 0/8192/16256/16256). ## Tests New regression test `test_swa_reachable_block_mask_eagle_periodic_tail_widens_by_one` plus updated EAGLE expectations in `test_swa_reachable_block_mask_final_partial_segment` (its old expecta

title: [Kernel][Perf] Do not split rows no longer than k in `top_k_per_row_decode`
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview When the logits are at least 200,000 wide, `top_k_per_row_decode` spends about 120 µs on a decode row no longer than k, although the result is just the row's own indices. In a small batch, a row of 2–4K tokens takes about 50 µs. The call ends with its slowest row, so one such short row slows the whole batch. This PR lets rows no longer than k skip the split and the merge, which brings them to about 5 µs. This matters for Mistral Large 4 on MI325X, which uses this kernel at its default 262,144 context with k = 2048: - A request takes this path while its prompt plus generated tokens are at most 2,048. On main such requests decode more slowly than 8K-token ones (19.2 vs 15.9 ms per output token at concurrency 1). With this PR they take 14.1 ms. - Long requests batched with a short one pay the same penalty. With 32 rows spread over 1K–64K tokens, a call takes 160 µs on main, more than 32 rows of 254–262K tokens (104 µs), and 85 µs with this PR (Gaussian logits; 191 → 162 µs with clustered ones). Over the 44 indexer layers that is 1.3–3.3 ms per decode step for every request in the batch. This is computed from kernel times and was not measured end to end. - If every request is longer than 2,048 tokens, nothing changes: with 8K-token inputs the serving results match main within 0.5%. An earlier version of this PR also carried a fix for strided logits. That fix is now #69176, and the two PRs are independent. ## Claims - Calls on rows no longer than k drop from 43–142 µs to 5–10 µs on MI325X, at k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048} and widths of 262,144 a

title: [Bugfix] Exclude the compilation peak from memory profiling
summary: ## Purpose Closes #54122. On a cold start `torch.compile` and Inductor autotuning run inside `profile_run()`, which sits inside the `memory_profiling()` window. With AOT compile, `decorators.py` already splits the two phases into separate `with` blocks, and `monitor_profiling_run()` asserts compilation is finished before the profiling forward begins, but nothing clears the allocator high-water mark between them. Compilation's temporaries are freed before that forward, so `transient_peak_headroom` counts them as activation memory and the KV cache shrinks until the compile cache is warm. This drops the high-water mark when compilation finishes. Clearing the counter alone would also discard a peak recorded earlier in the same window, since `profile_run()` runs the multimodal encoder before the backbone compiles, so the pre-compilation value is carried over and folded back in. Without AOT (`VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE=0` or `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`) the compile and the first profiling forward run in the same `monitor_torch_compile` block, so the two peaks can't be told apart there. That block passes `discard_peak=False` and keeps the current behavior. ## Test plan 1x H100 80GB, `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, nightly wheel `3b33a845c` with the patch overlaid. title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Record the load window by logical expert
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #60685. EPLB records load per physical expert. When step_interval < window_size, part of the window still holds load recorded under the old map, and the next rearrange counts it for the expert that now sits at that physical index. This PR records load by logical expert instead. `eplb_map_and_record` already has the logical id, so the `atomic_add` now goes to the logical id rather than the physical index. `expert_load_pass` and the window have logical width, so old steps stay with the right expert after the map changes, and rearrange only sums the window. No extra kernel or scatter is added. The PR also removes `expert_load_pass_buffer`, `last_expert_load` and `use_last_expert_load`. The number of logical experts does not change when Elastic EP scales, so the window stays valid across a scale and the scale rearrange uses it directly. `log_balancedness` needs per rank load, so the same kernel also records physical counts into a new `physical_load_pass` when `log_balancedness` is on. The window never reads these counts, and they are cleared in the same `step` as the logical pass, so each logged value comes from one forward under one map. With `log_balancedness` off the buffer is not allocated and Triton compiles the second `atomic_add` out. The MegaMoE kernels share this helper, so they get the same recording. No open PR fixes this. #49700 only clears the window on an elastic EP topology change, and #64485 changes when rearrangements run, not how the window is recorded. ## Test Plan The first round is on H100, on main at `24a49203ee` with this PR on top. title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Wire Gemma-4 MoE layers into EPLB
summary: ## Purpose `--enable-eplb` has no effect on Gemma-4 MoE models (for example `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`).
