This PR: - passes `enable_eplb` and `num_redundant_experts` from the parallel config to Gemma-4's `FusedMoEFactory`, as `qwen3_moe.py` does. - takes the physical and local expert counts from the first MoE layer's `moe_config`. With `num_redundant_experts > 0` this needs #69062. Gemma-4 checkpoints store the experts as fused tensors, and #69062 makes that loader fill the redundant experts too. No existing issue or PR covers the Gemma-4 part. ## Test Plan Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, EP=4 (DP=4, TP=1, DeepEP high-throughput) on 4xH100, `--enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"window_size": 40, "step_interval": 40, "num_redundant_experts": 16, "log_balancedness": true}'`. - Before: EPLB logs zero load at every step. - After: EPLB logs nonzero load and rearranges experts. - Accuracy with EPLB (GSM8K, HellaSwag, MMLU, chat template) matches the run without EPLB, which shows that the redundant copies hold the right weights. summary: ## Overview `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` returns wrong indices for logits at least 200,000 wide with `stride(1) != 1`, on every platform. This sends such logits to the unsplit radix kernel, which handles strides correctly. Split out of #65427, which is now stacked on this PR. ## Claims - Fixes wrong indices for strided logits at least 200,000 wide. At k = 512, rows of 100,003 and 262,144 logits got only 244 and 257 of their 512 indices inside the row, and at k = 2048 only 996 and 1,005 of 2,048. - Contiguous logits run the same kernels as before on every platform, so in-tree callers see no change in behavior or performance. - The new regression test fails on main and passes with this PR. ## Validation MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, HIP 7.15. This PR is commit `08aab072df` on main `0bf9c07376`. Both arms use the same Python tree and differ only in `_C_stable_libtorch`, built from each commit. New test only, with this PR's test file against each kernel: ```bash pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k strided_logits -v --durations=0 ``` | kernel | result | |---|---| | main | `2 failed, 979 deselected, 17 warnings in 2.26s` | | this PR | `2 passed, 979 deselected, 17 warnings in 1.65s` (calls: 0.57 s for k = 512, < 0.01 s for k = 2048) | <details> <summary>Raw output: main fails</summary> ``` E AssertionError: assert False E + where False = <built-in method equal of type object at 0x7566ff78af60>(tensor([511, 512, 244, 257], device='cuda:0'), tensor([511, 512, 512, 512], device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.int32)) tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py:531: Assert

title: [RFC]: [Rust Frontend] Speech-to-text APIs (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`)
summary: ### Motivation. Roadmap item in #44280 (🧭): *"Speech-to-text APIs: `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations`"*. I'd like to take this item; this is the design discussion the 🧭 marker asks for. The Rust frontend registers no route for either path (they appear only in `TRACKED_HANDLERS` in `rust/src/server/src/middleware/load.rs`), so an ASR model served with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` returns 404 where the Python frontend serves them. Most of the hard parts already exist on the Rust side: - Audio decoding, resampling and Whisper-style log-mel features run in Rust through `llm-multimodal` (Symphonia with an ffmpeg fallback; `Qwen3AudioProcessor`), and chat audio inputs already use them. - `llm-multimodal` has `registry::transcription::TranscriptionFamily` (`sanitize_prompt`, `assistant_prefill`, `parse_transcript`), with Qwen3-ASR registered. vLLM does not use it yet. Missing pieces: multipart parsing, a supported-tasks gate, the speech-to-text request and response contract, long-audio chunking, and encoder-decoder lowering for Whisper. ### Proposed Change. Two stages, so the first lands without engine co-design: 1. **Contract and generic pipeline, serving decoder-only ASR families the Rust multimodal stack already processes (Qwen3-ASR).** No engine changes. 2. **Whisper (encoder-decoder).** Needs a Whisper feature extractor in `llm-multimodal` and an encoder-decoder lowering path in vLLM. This is the co-design point. Out of scope until the Python contract settles, tracked against #25750: Realtime (#53452), diarized output, VAD (#46126), word timestamps (#47664)

title: [Attention][DCP] Add opt-in FlashInfer fused DCP A2A + LSE combine for MLA
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Adds opt-in `--dcp-comm-backend flashinfer_a2a_fused` for MLA. The per-layer DCP output exchange and LSE merge then run as one FlashInfer kernel, `decode_cp_a2a_lse_reduce` from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6483. Today that is an all-gather plus a reduce-scatter with `ag_rs`, or four kernels with the opt-in `a2a`. `ag_rs` is the default unless a model selects `a2a`. This stays a draft until a FlashInfer release includes flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6483 (vLLM pins 0.7.4). It replaces #61922, which targeted the older FlashInfer API. ## Claims - **NCCL symmetric-memory backend.** The flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6483 kernel reads peer buffers and synchronizes through NCCL's device API (NCCL window, LSA pointers). Its workspace therefore has to be PyTorch symmetric memory on the NCCL backend. FlashInfer's other comm kernels do not need this. PyTorch fixes the backend once per process, so with `flashinfer_a2a_fused` the worker selects NCCL before anything allocates. Under the NCCL backend: - rendezvous goes through the group's NCCL communicator, so each group creates it up front (about 0.5 GiB per GPU per group); - symm-mem all-reduce and the custom all-reduce MNNVL buffers rendezvous on the device group instead of Gloo, so they stay enabled. On main they silently turn off under `TORCH_SYMMMEM=NCCL`. Defaults and the CUDA backend are unchanged. The backend alone does not change speed: `a2a` on the NCCL backend is within 0.4% end to end. - **Performance** on 8x H100, TP8/DCP8, CUDA graphs, batch 1. title: [Perf][Models] Keep cu_seqlens on CPU for non-flash Qwen VL encoder attention
summary: ## Purpose Ports the spirit of huggingface/transformers#47703 ("Fix D2H sync in Qwen VL vision encoder") into vLLM for the remaining real sync point. The `TORCH_SDPA` multimodal-encoder attention backend splits the packed vision sequence per block using Python sizes derived from `cu_seqlens`. Because every Qwen VL vision tower previously moved `cu_seqlens` to GPU unconditionally, the per-block `.tolist()` in `vit_torch_sdpa_wrapper` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py:277`) forced a device-to-host sync on every attention layer of every eager forward. `grid_thw` is host metadata to begin with, so this change keeps `cu_seqlens` (and `cu_window_seqlens` for Qwen2.5-VL) on CPU when the SDPA backend is selected, eliminating those syncs. Kernel backends (FlashAttention / Triton / FlashInfer) still receive the GPU tensor and are unchanged. The other two sync classes HF #47703 targeted were already mitigated in vLLM (`grid_thw` stays CPU host metadata via `keep_on_cpu`, `max_seqlen` is kept on CPU per #37139, and the mrope position path is CPU/numpy), so they are intentionally not touched here. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Searched `vllm-project/vllm` for open PRs matching "D2H", "Qwen VL", and vision-encoder sync fixes (e.g. #37139, #37239, #37316, #42850). None address the non-flash/SDPA encoder `cu_seqlens` D2H sync. title: [Perf][MM] Use varlen attention in MiniCPM-V vision encoder
summary: ## Overview This PR replaces masked SDPA with variable-length attention for padded batches in MiniCPM-V’s eager vision encoder. MiniCPM-V/O batches image slices with different patch counts by padding them to a common length and using masked PyTorch SDPA. In a timing-only test on MiniCPM-V 4.6 with 500 synthetic prompts and 8 images per prompt (mixed 448×448 and 336×672), setting attention_mask=None switched the encoder to batched MMEncoderAttention. Mean encoder forward time fell by 15.5% with padding still in place, pointing to the attention path is an opportunity for optimization. This PR uses variable-length MMEncoderAttention for padded batches in the eager vision encoder. It packs valid patches and uses cu_seqlens to keep attention within each slice. ## Claims ### Results - On the mixed-resolution `vllm bench mm-processor` workload, mean `encoder_forward_ms` decreased by 26.5% for MiniCPM-V 4.0 and 15.6% for MiniCPM-V 4.6. - ChartQA relaxed accuracy changed by −0.16 and +0.48 percentage points, respectively. Both changes were smaller than the reported standard errors. ### Changes - Attention goes through `MMEncoderAttention` with `cu_seqlens` / `max_seqlen`, e.g. `flash_attn_varlen_func` on the FlashAttention backend. Backend-specific metadata is prepared with the existing `MMEncoderAttention` helpers (`maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`, `compute_max_seqlen`, `maybe_compute_seq_lens`), the same way as Qwen-VL. - Valid patch tokens are packed into a single sequence `(1, N, D)`, and `cu_seqlens` marks the slice boundaries (block-diagonal attention). - Outputs are unpacked back

title: [Bugfix][RL] Release extensible KV cache allocator cap during sleep
summary: ## Overview Level 1 and level 2 sleep, and `release_kv_cache_memory()`, release the extensible KV cache's physical pages but left PyTorch's process-wide caching-allocator cap in place. Colocated code could not allocate the memory sleep had just freed. This lifts that cap while the pages are released and restores it when the KV cache is recommitted. TRL-1 in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68777. ## Claims - While the engine is asleep, or after `release_kv_cache_memory()`, colocated allocations are no longer bounded by the extensible KV cache's allocator cap. - `wake_up()` and `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])` restore the same cap after the pages are mapped again. A weights-only wake leaves the cap lifted. - Engines that do not sleep, and engines without an extensible KV cache, keep the previous behavior. - No open PR addresses TRL-1. Nearby sleep changes (#63546, #58066, #59130) cover failed-sleep recovery, backup preparation, and telemetry. ## Validation On main, the new sleep tests fail because sleep does not change the allocator fraction (`assert [] == [1.0]`): 3 failed in 6.86s. With this change (`15974fa223e24a4ce8f4f476be84bbfc383f3b50`): ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q -p no:cacheprovider \ tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_freeing_the_cache_lifts_the_torch_memory_cap \ tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_sleep_lifts_and_wake_restores_the_torch_memory_cap \ tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_lifting_an_unset_allocator_cap_is_a_no_op \ tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_allocator_cap

The Rubin build docs now warn about ptxas 13.5.37 and give a `docker run` option that keeps Triton on the ptxas-blackwell 13.4 this wheel bundles. The images themselves don't change which ptxas Triton uses. This also removes the PyTorch/Triton requirement conflict reported in #64761. ## Claims - `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt` pins `torch==2.16.0.dev20261116+cu135` from the cu135 nightly index. torch's CUDA runtime wheels move to 13.5 with it (`cuda-toolkit` 13.4.1 → 13.5.0, `nvidia-cuda-runtime` 13.4.49 → 13.5.37). - PyTorch publishes no cu135 torchvision or torchaudio yet. title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Yield once per engine step in the AsyncLLM output handler
summary: ## Overview `AsyncLLM`'s output handler now yields to the event loop once per engine step. title: [ROCM][KVConnector][MoRIIO] Add WRITE-mode consumer timeout
summary: ## Purpose Fixes the decode-side hang in #59114 and the consumer half of ROCm/mori#655. In MoRIIO WRITE mode, a request whose prefill dies after the decode allocated its blocks waits in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until the client gives up, with nothing logged and `/health` at 200. This adds `write_recv_timeout`, a per-request timer on the decode scheduler that fails the request at the deadline instead. It complements ROCm/mori#670 (merged), which fails the producer-side transfer on a QP error but still tells decode nothing. **Set `write_recv_timeout` below your client timeout.** A client abort stops the timer, so with the 540 s default and #59114's 400 s client the client still gives up first, as on `main`. A dead prefill's KV blocks stay held either way (see Scope). Config: `kv_connector_extra_config["write_recv_timeout"]` (seconds, default 540, finite and > 0, validated at startup). Documented in `docs/features/moriio_connector_usage.md`. Not a duplicate: the other open MoRIIO timeout PRs cover the prefill side (#51301, #56465) or the handshake (#63856). ## Scope: this fails the request, it does not free the blocks RDMA writes are one-sided, so a passed deadline does not prove the producer's NIC has stopped; releasing a block could let a late write corrupt another request. Blocks stay held until a real `finished_recving` (lifecycle split in #59382): a timed-out request keeps its transfer mapping, so a late `write_done` (a slow producer) still frees its blocks. For Whisper this is the bottleneck before the encoder even starts. 2. **[#62352](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62352)** — `WhisperEncoder.forward` runs a per-item Python loop over `gelu(conv1) → gelu(conv2) → transpose → +embed_positions`, one CUDA launch per audio clip. Fields whose names land in the set skip the model-dtype cast (they are still moved to CPU). Demonstrated by PR #60352 for Voxtral, needed here to keep Whispers fp32 PCM round-trip safe. ### B. Whisper log-mel on the GPU worker (closes #62355) - `WhisperMultiModalProcessor._get_hf_mm_inputs` no longer runs the HF extractor. title: [Spec Decode][Attention] Enable fused multi-step draft decode for FlashInfer XQA on SM12x
summary: ## Overview In Model Runner V2, when `num_speculative_tokens > 1` and every draft attention group sets `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`, `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` executes all `K - 1` draft decode steps after the first token via `_run_fused_multi_step_decode`—replaying them inside a single fused CUDA graph in `FULL` mode (with metadata built once at capture) or from one host metadata build per `propose()` in eager mode ([#46849](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46849), [#58463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463)). title: [Core] Admit KV-ready requests before token scheduling in arrival order
summary: ## Overview Separate admission into `running` from first worker dispatch so a request that waited for remote KV can regain precedence over later running requests before they consume the step's token budget. The relative order of existing running requests is unchanged. - Admission consumes no tokens. title: [Model] Add masked_token_ids to never sample given tokens
summary: ## Purpose Some token ids must never be sampled: the `lm_head` rows past the tokenizer (padding, so the logits exist but decode to nothing; see #13175) and, for multimodal models, placeholder tokens that are meaningless without their media. Today the only options are per-request `allowed_token_ids` (very slow with a large allow-list) or patching `compute_logits`, which RL frameworks do (e.g. verl, [`monkey_patch_compute_logits`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/453954b3/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py#L117-L145), added in verl-project/verl#7038). RL makes this worse than plain inference: training perturbs the untrained rows and a sampled OOV token feeds back into the policy. This adds an engine-level `--masked-token-ids` (`ModelConfig.masked_token_ids`): - The model runner (`GPUModelRunner.sample()` and the standalone CPU runner) sets those logits to `-inf` once, on the full-vocab target logits, after the batch-sharded all-to-all and before the grammar bitmask and the sampler. Draft heads with their own vocab and TP-sharded logits are not touched. - Draft tokens that hit a masked id are always rejected by the lossless rejection samplers, since the target gives them probability 0. The lossy methods (`synthetic`, `fly`) can accept draft tokens regardless of the target logits, so they are rejected at config time. - The ids are validated against the vocab size at startup. - Prompt logprobs are unaffected. title: [ROCm][Perf][MoE] Keep a 32-column BF16 intermediate pad for AITER on CDNA3
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Summary On CDNA3, vLLM now passes AITER the 32-column intermediate pad of an unquantized MoE instead of rounding it down to 0, so AITER's gfx942 BF16 FlyDSL decode kernels skip the zero tail (ROCm/aiter#8411). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 at TP4 has 160 intermediate columns per rank, stored as 192, and today every expert computes and reads the 32 zero columns at the end of each Gate/Up half and of Down's K. Skipping them makes the MoE 8–13% faster from 1 to 256 tokens. On 4× MI325X, TP4, MTP-3: * up to 5.3% more output throughput (1K input, concurrency 8) * 4–5% lower median ITL at concurrency 8 and 32, including 32K input * GSM8K, RULER NIAH at 32K and 128K, and GPQA-Diamond within noise of main and the published scores Draft until vLLM's AITER pin contains ROCm/aiter#8411. ## What changed * `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py`: `aiter_moe_pads` takes `skip_bf16_tail` and then rounds an undoubled intermediate pad to 32 instead of 64. `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` sets it for unquantized weights on CDNA3 (`get_cdna_version() == 3`). CK still rounds the pad down to 64 itself. * `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`: new `test_aiter_moe_pads_skip_bf16_tail`: at TP4 the 32-column pad passes through; at TP1 it stays doubled and 64-wide. The file runs in the existing AMD kernels step. On MI325X with ROCm/aiter#8411: 92 passed, 5 skipped. ## Gating No flag or environment variable. title: [Performance]: Fused CUDA GDN MTP decode kernel stores a full recurrent state per draft token
summary: ### Summary The fused CUDA GDN MTP decode op (`fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp`, `csrc/libtorch_stable/gdn/fused_gdn_decode_kernel.cu`), which is the default spec-decode path on CUDA, still stores a full recurrent state for every token of a spec-decode step. #61434 and #64325 defer these stores for the two Triton kernels; the CUDA kernel has no equivalent yet. On a DGX Spark the per-token stores cost 6.8% of the decode step at batch 4 with three draft tokens. ### Environment - DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 24 MB L2, ~252 GB/s measured read bandwidth), CUDA 13.0 - vLLM 0.31.0 (also checked on 0.34.0), CUDA graphs, `--no-async-scheduling` - Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, `--speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'`, FP32 SSM state, no prefix caching ### What the stores cost With three draft tokens the kernel stores 4 x 3.15 MB (48 value heads x 128 x 128 x fp32) per layer per request; the next step reads only the slot of the last accepted position. 1. **Batch 1.** The stores fit in L2 and the write-back lands on the next GEMM. `linear_attn.out_proj` takes 194 us per launch while `self_attn.o_proj`, the same CUTLASS FP8 kernel on a same-shaped weight, takes 149 us. In isolation both take 147 us; writing N MB right before the GEMM reproduces the gap (0/4/8/12/24 MB -> 147/169/187/198/213 us). 2. **Batch 4.** The stores are 50 MB per layer, twice the L2, and the GDN kernel itself becomes write-bound (268 us). title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Generalize cache registration and payload layouts
summary: ## Overview Generalize MooncakeStore's rank-local cache registration to describe logical tensor components instead of assuming that each layer occupies an entire allocation page. This supports offset and strided views, grouped kernel blocks, and multiple components, while retaining compact transfers for adjacent regions and allocator-verified padding. ## Changes - Describe each group's regions with independent addresses, block strides, and transfer lengths. Skip empty components, deduplicate identical regions in input order, and coalesce adjacent regions only within compatible registered storage. Containment-based alias deduplication is intentionally removed. - Reuse upstream `group_kernel_blocks()` in the rank-local layout. Other layouts continue receiving manager-block views from the worker; TP-shared layout contracts remain unchanged. - When `KVCacheSpec` and `KVCacheTensor` metadata match a complete padded layer view, construct a zero-copy transfer view spanning its internal kernel-page padding. Validate the full shape, dtype, offsets, strides, and allocation bounds. Components, slices, and unverified views keep precise region descriptors. Normalize identical KV-sharing views together, including aliases that precede their allocated target. - Validate that chunks start at a manager-block boundary, satisfy hash-block alignment, and have `0 < span <= block_size`; broadcast region lengths instead of multiplying by a block count that must be one. - Remove unused layout setters and `ChunkedTokenDatabase` wrappers. Tests register real CPU tensors through `register_kv_caches()`

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Tune the GatedDeltaNet Triton prefill kernels on gfx942
summary: ## Purpose The Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill walks each sequence's chunks in order, so the kernel grid and the MFMA tile shape are all that decide how much of the GPU its five Triton kernels fill. On gfx942 those kernels autotune over a stock config list that is not tuned for CDNA3: the `num_stages=3` entries cannot launch at all, and the picks among the rest use a wider MFMA tile than the hardware prefers. This PR adds gfx942 config lists for the five kernels, chosen per launch from the input size, with no kernel body changes. The KDA prefill (Kimi-K3, GLM-5-Next and others) shares two of the five kernels, so it changes also. Builds on #41446 by @zobinHuang and @BoruiXu; their commit keeps its authorship. ## Claims - GDN prefill layer, bf16, 10 shapes on MI325X: 1.366x geomean, 0.996x to 1.662x. - KDA prefill, 6 shapes on MI325X: 1.095x geomean, 1.025x to 1.209x. - Nine of ten GDN shapes improve. 16/48 at 1024 tokens is at parity, 0.996x; at that length the layer is launch-overhead bound and the two rounds landed on either side of 1.0. - Serving `Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` at TP1 on MI325X: median TTFT 1.7% to 19.0% lower on all seven shapes, median ITL within 0.1%, total throughput 0.1% to 2.0% higher. - GSM8K 5-shot and GPQA diamond 0-shot: every delta is within one standard error of main. - On by default on gfx942; other targets keep the stock lists and keys. With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` Qwen GDN resolves to `aiter_flydsl` on gfx942, so the GDN rows apply with AITER off; KDA and OLMo Hybrid use these kernels either way. title: [Feature][RL] Per-request opt-out from auxiliary outputs
summary: ## Summary Adds a per-request `SamplingParams.return_aux_outputs` flag (default `true`). A request that sets it to `false` gets no RL auxiliary outputs: no routed experts (neither recorded nor retained) and no sampling mask. Logprobs keep following `logprobs`, `logprob_token_ids` and `prompt_logprobs`, since a client can already turn those off per request. RL inference servers record these outputs for every request, but some requests never use them, such as evals that run next to rollouts. Recording has to stay on for the rollouts, so the opt-out is per request. Original work by @hallerite; generalized from routed experts to all auxiliary outputs by @aoshen02. ## Behavior - Works on `SamplingParams` and on `/inference/v1/generate` (inside `sampling_params`), in the Python and Rust frontends. The OpenAI routes do not expose it. - On a server that records routed experts, an opted-out request's blocks have no recorded routing, so it gets its own prefix-cache salt. When aux outputs are enabled, `EngineCore.preprocess_add_request` derives the salt with `aux_output_cache_salt`: a reserved prefix followed by a JSON object of the salt's parts. A client salt that starts with the prefix is wrapped the same way, so no client salt can produce another request's salt. The engine hashes every request whose salt it changed, since frontend prompt hashes lack it. - Opted-out requests skip routed-expert retention for KV tiers (#62591) and are not capped by it. - Routing capture and sampling-mask computation still run for the whole batch; the opt-out skips per-request recording, retention, and

title: [ROCm][Perf] wvSplitK: packed bf16 dot on gfx950
summary: ## Overview Two changes, one idea: the `YTILE 3/4` rows of the `wvSplitK` tile table only pay off when `sml_` takes them (`M % tile == 0`); when `M % tile != 0` the shape routes to the fragmented `hf_` tile, which loses to `sml_` at `YTILE 2` for every dtype — so those shapes now fall back to `YTILE 2` on wave64. title: [Kernel] Avoid runtime alignment specialization in Triton MoE
summary: ## Summary Avoid Triton alignment specialization for `EM` and `num_valid_tokens` in `fused_moe_kernel`. Both values are determined by runtime token routing, so a route alignment not seen during engine profiling can otherwise compile a new kernel variant on the first production request. The kernel math and launch configuration are unchanged. This only makes those two scalar arguments alignment-generic. ## Prior work / duplicate check This revives and credits the core idea from #11057 / #11056, which was automatically closed as stale in 2025 without review and no longer applies cleanly to current `main`. I found no active PR implementing the same change. Compared with that closed PR, this submission ports the change to the current kernel shape, adds a focused regression test, and supplies RTX 5090 production-shape correctness, compilation-cardinality, and first-request measurements. A read-only pre-submission check also found no changes to either touched path on current `main` and a clean merge-tree. ## Why On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 with TP2+EP on RTX 5090, an unseen route shape compiled `fused_moe_kernel` during inference even though its block configuration and algorithm matched the profiled variant. Marking the runtime route sizes as non-specialized-on-alignment removed that compile event. ## Validation The RTX 5090 measurements below are historical results at the recorded September revisions. - Qwen3.6 local fused-MoE production shape (`E128`, `topk=8`, `N=512`, `K=2048`): 11/11 route-size cases produced identical output hashes. - Production-shape kernel p50 geomean: 1.0016x

title: [Kernel][MoE] Run Kimi-K3.1 SiTU routed experts in SM90 DeepGEMM Mega MoE
summary: ## Overview `MEGA_MOE_MXFP4_SM90` advertised only SwiGLU, so `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on Hopper rejected Kimi K3.1's SiTU activation while constructing the experts: ``` NotImplementedError: DeepGEMM MegaMoE mxfp4 experts support ['swiglu'], not 'situ'. ``` SM100's `MEGA_MOE_MXFP4` already accepts `situ`, and the only thing that makes the SM90 variant distinct is its hidden-state staging (FP8 with one FP32 scale per 128, versus SM100's packed per-32 UE8M0). That staging is a property of the dispatch path and is independent of the L1 epilogue activation. Accept SiTU there too. The second half of this change is a capability probe. SM90 SiTU support lives in the DeepGEMM kernel, not in vLLM, so simply widening the frozenset would move the failure downstream: an installed DeepGEMM without the SM90 SiTU branch rejects it in its C++ host code (`DG_HOST_ASSERT(activation != "situ")`), which surfaces as an opaque launch error. `deep_gemm_supports_sm90_situ()` probes for the `situ_beta` parameter that [DeepGEMM#62](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/62) adds to `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, following the same signature-probing pattern this file already uses in `_kernel_fuses_shared_experts`. The probe is false on the DeepGEMM revision pinned in `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` today, so construction raises a clear `NotImplementedError` naming the missing kernel. **This PR does not change behavior on the current pin**; it takes effect once DeepGEMM#62 is merged and the pin is bumped. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose At small batch the Muse Spark DSpark draft is weight-bandwidth bound: each draft step reads the context projection `fc`, the five decoder layers, the vocab-sharded `lm_head` and, once per sequential round, the Markov head `markov_w2` (207 MB in BF16 per rank). title: [Bugfix][DP] Fail fast when the data parallel RPC port is already in use
summary: ## Overview Detect the data parallel RPC port conflict **before** the engine binds it, and report the process that holds the port. The rank 0 frontend binds `tcp://<master ip>:<rpc port>` for the data parallel startup handshake. When a previous engine hangs or exits abnormally, that stale process keeps the port (and the accelerator devices) alive, so starting an engine again in the same container fails immediately with a bare: ```text zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use (addr='tcp://<node-ip>:29550') ``` The bind happens in the frontend process, so the error carries no hint about the stale process that has to be stopped — the operator only sees a zmq traceback and has to hunt the process down by hand. With this PR the engine fails during startup with an actionable error: ```text The data parallel RPC port 10.99.48.128:29550 is already in use by PID 1234 (python). ``` Related: #65096 (proposal 2 of 4). Reported from the Ascend plugin: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#20339. ## Claims - A deployment whose data parallel RPC port is held by another process now fails during startup with an error that names the port, the holder PID and the recovery steps, instead of failing later with a bare `zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use`. - The check never fires on a deployment that does not bind the endpoint: it only runs when the data parallel engines are **not** all local (upstream then uses the local IPC transport instead of the TCP handshake address), and only for the **rank 0 frontend** (the other ranks connect to the master instead of binding the address). - The reported proc

title: [Bugfix] Fill missing NVFP4 MoE activation scales, reject missing weight scales
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview Fixes #45212; #51525 reports the same failure on another checkpoint. ModelOpt leaves out an expert's `input_scale` when calibration routes no tokens to it, and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` allocated the per-expert scales with `torch.empty`, so those experts kept whatever the allocator left there. Backends that reduce the scales to one layer maximum usually hide this; `VLLM_CUTLASS` reads them per expert and returns empty completions. The scales now start as NaN. A missing activation scale takes the layer's largest calibrated one, with one warning per layer, on every backend that reads activation scales. A missing weight scale, or a layer with no calibrated activation scale, still fails the load. Earlier versions of this PR rejected such checkpoints, which is what @taking-lying-flat and @AubinGil preferred here: fail by default (@taking-lying-flat suggested a fill only as an opt-in). I changed it to fill by default, with no switch back to the hard failure. The warning names every filled expert, and the filled checkpoint scores at the Marlin level on every backend tried (below). title: [Bugfix][LoRA][MoE] Use int64 token offsets in MoE-LoRA Triton kernels
summary: ## Purpose The MoE-LoRA Triton kernels compute output/input row addresses as `offs_token * stride`, where `offs_token` is loaded from the int32 `sorted_token_ids` (or built from `pid_m`). Once `num_tokens * top_k * N >= 2**31` the product wraps in int32 and the kernel writes outside the output tensor (illegal memory access, or silent corruption). With MoE LoRA enabled this is reachable in a single prefill step, e.g. ~37K tokens for DeepSeek-V3/Kimi-K2 shapes or ~65K tokens for Qwen3-235B, including the profile run when `max_num_batched_tokens` is large. The base `fused_moe` kernel already casts `offs_token` to int64 for exactly this reason (`fused_moe.py`: "stride_cm * offs_token can exceed int32 for large token counts"); the LoRA kernels were missing the cast. Changes: - `fused_moe_lora_op.py`: cast `offs_token` to int64 in `_fused_moe_lora_one_shot_kernel` and in `_get_token_offs` (used by the legacy `fully_sharded` kernel for both `stride_am` and `stride_cm`). - `fused_moe_lora_fp8_op.py`: same fix in its own copy of `_get_token_offs`. - `trtllm_lora_moe.py`: promote the row/token and permuted indices to int64 in `_unpermute_activation_kernel` and `_finalize_lora_kernel`, which have the same `row * stride` pattern with `num_tokens * top_k` rows. - Add `do_not_specialize=["num_valid_tokens", "stride_tl_", "stride_el"]` to the one-shot kernel, matching the legacy kernel, so per-step scalars do not cause runtime recompiles. Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs/issues (`fused_moe_lora int64`, `moe lora offs_token overflow`, `LoRA MoE int32 overflow`) and found nothing addres

title: [Spec Decode] Reload in-checkpoint draft weights on reload_weights
summary: ## Purpose A disk `reload_weights` with an MTP draft never reloads the draft's own weights. `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) reloads only `get_model()`, and `on_target_weights_replaced` only refreshes the draft's derived values, so draft-only tensors (e.g. `mtp.*`) stay at their cold-start values after an RL weight update. Fix: when the draft ships in the target's checkpoint, reload it from the same path. The draft reloads first, inside `draft_context()`, so the target wins on the shared embedding and lm_head. Iterator-based updates and `prefill_context_kv_only` are skipped. Also fixes the level-2 sleep warning text in `gpu_worker.py`. ## Test Plan Qwen3.8-27B + MTP, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, `weight_transfer_config={"backend":"nccl"}`: reload weights from disk, then compare all parameters against a freshly started engine and compare greedy outputs. ## Test Result | | tensors differing from fresh engine | tokens | max \|dlogprob\| | |---|---|---|---| | main (468d10ae51) | 12/743 (all draft tensors) | - | - | | this PR | 0/743 | equal | 0 | One independent review round (different model) done; findings applied. ## Known gaps A draft at a different path is not reloaded: runai / `model_weights`, and MiniMax-M3 DSpark at `<target>/dspark`. ## Duplicate check Searched open PRs. Related, not duplicates: #52487 reloads the configured draft checkpoint on the no-argument level-2 sleep wake path (explicit `weights_path` does not reload the draft there); #60139 adds a separate `reload_draft_weights` RPC for hot-swapping a separately trained draft.

title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] DeepSeek V3/V3.1: keep content that shares a delta with the tool call start tokens
summary: ## Overview With `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v3` or `deepseek_v31`, streaming drops the text that arrives in the same delta as `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>`. For example, if `" you."` and both start tokens come in one delta, the client gets `Let me check the weather for` instead of `Let me check the weather for you.`. Multi-token deltas are normal with `--stream-interval > 1` and speculative decoding. Non-streaming, and streaming one token per delta, are not affected. The delta that contains the start tokens goes to the "starting a new tool call" branch, which sets `text_portion = None` and returns only the tool name (or `None`), so the text before the start token is lost. This PR splits that text off before the existing parsing runs and attaches it to the returned delta as `content`. Related, different code paths: #67078 (V3 argument tail truncated at the call end), #58806, #59589, #67491 (V3.1). ## Claims - Text before a DeepSeek V3/V3.1 tool call streams in full, however the tokens are grouped into deltas. - Tool calls and non-streaming output are unchanged. ## Validation CPU only (WSL2, Python 3.12), main `664dfcd`, this PR `3ed203d`. title: [KV Offload][FS] Opt-in per-block CRC32C checksums
summary: ## Purpose Implements item 1 of #54363. The FS tier catches a truncated block (short read) but not one whose bytes changed at the same size, e.g. bit rot; such a block is loaded as KV silently. New tier option `checksum_blocks` (default `false`), using the xattr approach preferred in the #54363 discussion: * **Store:** the block's CRC32C is set as xattr `user.vllm.kv_crc32c` on the temp file, before the rename. * **Load:** verified after the read. A checksum verification failure removes the file and fails the load with `EBADMSG` through the existing `num_succeeded` partial-keep path, with `checksum_failed` set on the exception. The FS tier counts it in `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_checksum_failures` (no `tier` label) and publishes it via `get_stats()`. An `EBADMSG` from the filesystem itself (as ext4/xfs report metadata checksum errors) is not flagged, so it fails the load without removing the file or being counted. * **Backward compatible:** a block with no recorded checksum still loads, so the option can be enabled on an existing cache. For the same reason `FileMapper.fields` is not bumped, unlike the RFC text: the file contents do not change, so there is no cold start. * **xattrs unavailable at `root_dir`:** the tier fails at startup (see the design decision below). * Implemented in both `csrc/fs_io.cpp` (SSE4.2, table fallback) and the Python fallback in `fs/io.py`. title: [Doc]: Distinguish the KV-cache concurrency estimate from SLA capacity
summary: ### 📚 The doc issue The [Benchmark CLI guide, Load Pattern Control Parameters](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/benchmarking/cli/#load-pattern-control-parameters) recommends using the startup-reported maximum concurrency as an SLA limit. That startup value estimates KV-cache capacity at the configured context length. The server scheduler and the benchmark client impose separate limits, and latency and error targets require workload measurements. In one historical serving run, the engine reported **83.04×** at a 102,400-token context limit and was configured with `--max-num-seqs 24`. The long-prompt sweep reached a **client cap of 8 outstanding requests**, using 98,304 input tokens as its calibration target and an output cap of 256 tokens. All 16 requests at that test point completed. That point establishes coverage of the synthetic workload at C8. The run did not establish a production SLA or maximum sustainable concurrency. ### Suggest a potential alternative/fix Distinguish the following in the guidance: - **KV-cache estimate:** use the startup-reported value as a memory-sizing input. - **Scheduler limit:** `--max-num-seqs` caps the number of sequences processed per engine iteration. - **Client limit:** `vllm bench serve --max-concurrency` caps outstanding requests on the benchmark client. - **SLA validation:** sweep load within the intended operating range for a representative arrival pattern, token-length distribution, and cache conditions. summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose With an FP8 KV cache, `ROCM_AITER_FA` computes extend attention (chunked prefill over a cached prefix) by gathering and dequantizing the prefix to BF16 in chunks, running CK per chunk and merging by LSE. For long prefixes this dominates the prefill step. This PR makes `ROCM_AITER_FA` honor the existing `AttentionConfig.use_prefill_query_quantization` flag (today used by MLA backends). title: [ROCm] Use aiter.paged_mqa_logits for the sparse indexer decode logits
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On ROCm, this PR enables AITER's shape-dispatched `aiter.paged_mqa_logits` ([ROCm/aiter#6140](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6140)) for the sparse indexer decode logits (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`). AITER picks the Gluon or FlyDSL kernel and its launch knobs per shape from its tuned table, so tuning changes ship with AITER and need no vLLM change. Shapes AITER has no tuned row for get the same Gluon `ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2` call as today. This is an enablement change, not an end-to-end speedup: GLM-5.3 end to end is unchanged within noise. This follows review feedback on [#59422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59422). The AITER that vLLM pins (v0.1.29.post1 with FlyDSL 0.5.0, [#67959](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67959)) includes aiter#6140, so this path is live on main. ## Claims - Same output: `calc_diff` about 1e-10 vs the Gluon call. - End to end (GLM-5.3 MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, no MTP and MTP 1, 3 and 5): throughput, TTFT, TPOT and accuracy unchanged within noise; rerun outlier points flip sign between runs. - End to end on MI325X (gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4): throughput, TPOT and accuracy unchanged within noise. AITER has no gfx942 rows, so the dispatched call is today's Gluon call. - Tuned for GLM-5; other shapes keep Gluon with today's knobs. AITER's table has rows only for gfx950, 256 CUs, 32 index heads, head_dim 128, KV block 64, preshuffled cache, next_n 1-8. Shapes without a row get AITER's default, which is the same Gluon `ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2` call as today. - GLM-5 / 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.3

title: [ROCm] gfx950: use aiter.mqa_logits for the sparse indexer prefill
summary: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Overview On CDNA4 and later (gfx950 today), this PR enables AITER's shape-dispatched `aiter.mqa_logits` ([ROCm/aiter#6185](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6185)) for the sparse indexer prefill logits (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`). AITER picks the Triton/Gluon or FlyDSL kernel per shape from its tuned table, so vLLM no longer needs a change each time the best prefill kernel moves (as [#59280](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59280) did for FlyDSL). This is an enablement change, not an end-to-end speedup: GLM-5.3 throughput and accuracy are unchanged within noise, and 128k c1 TTFT is +1.9% (below). The AITER that vLLM pins (v0.1.29.post1, [#67959](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67959)) includes [ROCm/aiter#6185](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6185), so this path is live on main. ## Claims - CDNA4 and later + AITER: the prefill indexer logits go through `aiter.mqa_logits`. gfx1250 has no tuned rows yet, so AITER [falls back to the same Triton kernel](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/v0.1.29.post1/aiter/mqa_logits.py#L50) as today. - Tuned for GLM-5; other shapes keep Triton/Gluon. The AITER table (v0.1.29) has rows only for gfx950, 256 CUs, 32 index heads, head dim 128. On that key every shape gets a tuned row; shapes shorter than every row use the smallest one (FlyDSL). Shapes off that key run the same Triton/Gluon kernel as today: - GLM-5 / 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3 and their MTP (32 index heads): tuned rows. - DeepSeek-V3.2 and its MTP (64 index heads): Triton/Gluon, unchanged. - GLM-5 Next (16 index heads, padded to 32): GLM-5

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Explain why Marlin MoE rejects a config
summary: ## Purpose Serving a group-quantized WNA16 MoE checkpoint at a tensor-parallel size that splits the intermediate size into a non-whole number of quantization groups currently fails with a bare `AssertionError` and no message at all: ```python # vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py if self.is_marlin: assert check_moe_marlin_supports_config( self.moe, self.group_size, allow_tile_padding=True ) ``` Concretely: a model with `moe_intermediate_size = 640` and `group_size = 128` works at TP=1 and dies at TP=2 (640 → 320, and `320 % 128 != 0`). The operator is told nothing — not the rule, not the two numbers involved, and not the way out. It is easy to misread as a Marlin build or hardware problem. The backend-oracle path is only marginally better: `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py` returns the generic string `"Marlin not supported for this layer"` for every distinct reason. There is a second, subtler problem. The `allow_tile_padding=True` branch still requires `intermediate_size_per_partition % group_size == 0`, so padding does **not** rescue a group-size violation — correctly, because a scale group straddling a TP shard boundary is a correctness issue, not a tile-alignment one, and zero-padding cannot fix it. The code has always behaved this way but never said so, which makes `allow_tile_padding` read as more permissive than it is. ## Proposed change Add `explain_moe_marlin_unsupported()`, which returns `None` when a config is supported and otherwise a message naming the rule, the

summary: ## Overview Follow up on #56842 by checking the padded sinc kernel dimensions before calling torchaudio. ## Claims - Apply the existing element limit to the full filter shape, including its padding. - Verify the approximated rate pair before constructing or caching the resampler. - Preserve the normal resampling path and its filter settings. ## Validation On macOS arm64 with matching PyTorch and torchaudio 2.11.0 CPU wheels: ```text python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/multimodal/test_audio.py -k 'checks_padded_kernel or matches_torchaudio' # Base 78f20a5a34 with the new tests: 2 failed, 114 deselected, 1 warning in 3.18s # The padded-kernel guard did not raise and the element count differed from torchaudio's kernel shape. python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/multimodal/test_audio.py # Fix c372b2094c: 116 passed, 9 warnings in 14.92s ``` The local run excludes the shared conftest because its unrelated Dynamo fixture requires a newer PyTorch. title: [Kernel][Fusion] Fuse GELU-tanh+Mul with NVFP4 quantization (Gemma 2/3/4)
summary: ## Purpose Gemma 2/3/4 use `gelu_pytorch_tanh` in their gated MLPs. summary: ## Summary An ECCPUConnector NIXL consumer treats `ec_transfer_params` as the producer address and then trusts that peer's `XferAck.src_block_indices`. title: [Security] Widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
summary: ## Summary - Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32` - Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension - Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels ## Affected kernels | Kernel | File | Risk | |---|---|---| | `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC | | `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path | | `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High | | `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate | | AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) | ## Root cause CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens. ## Fix pattern ```cpp // Before (32-bit overflow) scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size; // After (64-bit safe) const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x; scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size; ``` For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change. ## Test plan - [x] Pr

title: [Perf] kimi-k3: Ship cached images as encoded bytes instead of re-decoding them
summary: ## Motivation Multi-turn clients resend every earlier image on each turn. title: [Refactor] sampling: Run sampling-stage adjustments through one ordered pipeline
summary: Stacked on #52170. ## Motivation The order in which a non-speculative sampling step adjusts its logits was spread over three places: `ModelRunner._preprocess_logits` (grammar mask build, then `SamplingBatchInfo.apply_logits_bias`, which applied penalties, the grammar mask, and logit_bias), `ModelRunner.sample` (watermark, sampler call, commits), and `Sampler.forward` (custom logit processors and NaN sanitize). title: [Fix] mem_cache: Restore request padding after KV resume
summary: ## Motivation `req_to_token` maps request/token positions to KV-cache locations. Row 0 is initialized to zero and reserved for dummy requests used to pad a CUDA graph batch; real requests use the other rows. With memory saver enabled, releasing `kv_cache` unbacks this table along with the KV allocations. Resuming remaps the memory without preserving its previous contents, but the padding row is not initialized again. Newly admitted real requests populate their own rows, while row 0 can remain uninitialized. A subsequent padded graph replay can read that row while building the attention page table, even though the padded request's output is discarded. An uninitialized entry can point to an unrelated or out-of-range KV page. For example, in the FlashMLA page-table builder with page size 64, an entry of 6400 would select page 100 instead of the reserved padding page 0. Depending on the backend and the resulting index, this can cause a device memory access error or incorrect inference output; it may also appear to work if the remapped bytes happen to be zero. A targeted H20 test detected uninitialized reads after resume, even though the remapped bytes happened to be zero. Separate model inference did not show incorrect output. The test configuration and fix validation are described below. ## Modifications Restore the padding row to zero after KV memory resumes. Add a CPU regression test that simulates nonzero data after resume and checks that real request rows are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - CPU: `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_sched

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Settle the in-flight decode result before a PD decode retraction
summary: ## Motivation With overlap scheduling, a PD decode worker can retract a request while the previous decode step's result is still queued. The retraction backs up the request's device state and requeues the request. On resume, the backup is restored and the request decodes from `output_ids`. By the time the backup is taken, the device state has already taken the in-flight step, but `output_ids` has not. Result processing skips retracted requests, so the in-flight step never reaches `output_ids`. The backup and `output_ids` end up one step apart: - **Speculative decoding:** the in-flight verify commits its whole accepted block into KV and draft state. Those tokens never reach `output_ids`, so the resumed request skips tokens or ends early. - **Recurrent state** (Mamba / GDN / KDA): a request has one slot that is updated in place, so the backup holds the state after the in-flight step. On resume the last token is fed again and the state advances twice. For a pure-attention model without speculative decoding this is already correct: the offload covers `[:seqlen - 1]`, and the resumed step recomputes the last position. `_reqs_finishing_inflight` already skips a retraction when the queued result finishes requests, but it does not settle the result. ## Modifications - `Scheduler._settle_pd_decode_inflight` runs only when a PD decode step under overlap is about to retract, whether from memory pressure or `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT`. It: - processes the queued results; - clears `last_batch` so the overlap loop does not process them again; - returns whether anything was settled. - `update_r

title: [Fix] multimodal: Fall back to CPU reliably when image preprocessing runs out of GPU memory
summary: ## Motivation Split from #52228, which now covers only stall detection. We serve a multimodal hybrid model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8, TP4/EP4) on 4x H200. Image requests sometimes fail with 500 on a CUDA OOM: the tokenizer process runs the fast image processor on `cuda:{base_gpu_id}`, which it shares with TP rank 0. On our server the scheduler held 135 of 139.8 GiB on GPU 0, and `torch.cat` in the HF Qwen2-VL image processor failed to allocate 1.3 GiB. `QwenVLImageProcessor` already retries on CPU, but: - the retry runs inside the `except` block, whose traceback keeps the failed attempt's GPU tensors alive, so `empty_cache()` frees nothing and the CPU retry runs with that memory still held; - it catches only `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError`, not an OOM raised as `RuntimeError` / `torch.AcceleratorError` by a CUDA call; - with the auto worker count on CUDA (1), preprocessing runs inline on the tokenizer's event loop, so a slow request, including a CPU fallback, blocks every other request and `/health`. ## Modifications - `process_mm_data` and the Qwen-VL chunked path retry on CPU after leaving the `except` block, and treat any `RuntimeError` whose message contains "out of memory" as an OOM (`is_cuda_out_of_memory` in `serving_preprocessing.py`). This is on by default; it changes behavior only after a GPU OOM. - `SGLANG_MM_GPU_PREPROCESS_RESERVE_MB` (default `0`, off): when the GPU has less free memory (device free plus this process's cached-but-unused blocks) than the estimated need plus the reserve, preprocessing goes straight to the CPU (`route_preprocessing_by_free_memory`). title: [Fix] [AMD] JIT: Port per-token group FP8 quantization v2 to ROCm
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fails to start on gfx942 with ROCm. During decode CUDA graph capture, it calls `per_token_group_quant_8bit_v2`. That kernel includes the CUDA-only `cuda_fp8.h`, so hipcc fails and the server exits before serving a request. The kernel is generic, so this also fixes other models that reach the same FP8 quantization path. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is the model verified here. On gfx942, the kernel also uses the wrong FP8 range. It scales values as though FP8 can represent up to 448, but gfx942 only supports up to 224. This can produce incorrect quantized values and scales. title: [Perf] [AMD] carv2: SPX-specific gfx1250 table for TP2/TP4
summary: # [AMD] carv2: SPX-specific gfx1250 table for TP2/TP4 ## Motivation The gfx1250 rows in the carv2 config table were tuned on DPX nodes, where each partition has 96 CUs. We recently brought up an MI455X node in SPX mode (one 256-CU partition per GPU, 4 GPUs), and carv2 turned out to be slower than RCCL there in a couple of size ranges, which is the opposite of what we want from a custom all-reduce. Here's what we saw on current `main` (graph mode, µs, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1`): | TP | size | carv2 (main) | RCCL | what carv2 picks | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2 | 2 MB | 20.1 | 14.9 | 2shot_push | | 2 | 4 MB | 24.1 | 12.8 | 2shot_push | | 4 | 1.5 MB | 21.1 | 20.0 | 2shot_push | | 4 | 24 MB | 67.1 | 46.4 | ring_simple | | 4 | 48 MB, late rank | 102.8 | 100.4 | ring_simple | Above the 16 MB 2shot threshold, TP2 and TP4 go to `ring_simple`. It streams through its own FIFOs, so `max_size` doesn't bound it, and carv2 takes every size instead of handing large ones to RCCL. There are two separate problems: 1. **TP2 2–6 MB.** Below the 8 MB cutoff for the unrolled 2shot kernel, TP2 uses the per-vector 2shot kernel, which is slow on a 256-CU part. Running 1shot with a full-CU grid is much faster in this range. For example, 4 MB takes 9.8 µs vs 24.1 µs today. 2. **TP4 above 16 MB.** `ring_simple` loses to RCCL on SPX. The unrolled 2shot keeps beating RCCL all the way to 64 MB, but with the default 16 MB `max_size` a 2shot slot (`2 × nbytes / world_size`) only fits 16 MB at TP2 and 32 MB at TP4. title: [Perf] diffusion/ltx-2.3: Reuse the cond pass's prefix blocks for the STG pass
summary: ## Motivation LTX-2.3 runs four guidance passes per denoising step: cond, neg, STG-perturbed and modality. The perturbed pass takes the cond pass's text, mask, latents and timesteps, and differs only by skipping self-attention in its STG blocks (block 28 by default). Blocks 0–27 therefore compute the same rows for both passes, so about 28/192 of the stage-1 DiT work is repeated. ## Modifications - `LTX2VideoTransformer3DModel.forward` takes two new arguments: - `ltx2_stg_capture_block` also returns the inputs of block K. - `ltx2_stg_resume_block`, with those inputs, starts the forward at block K. - Both take and return plain tensors, so both calls can be captured as breakable CUDA graphs. - LTX-2 denoising stage. When the perturbed pass differs from cond only by its STG blocks: - The per-pass path (`quality="exact"` one-stage) resumes each perturbed row from its cond row. - The batched path runs cond, neg and modality in one call, then runs the perturbed pass from block K. Splitting the batch changes its size, which can move GEMM and attention rounding, so this path is enabled only from `quality="lossless"` up; `exact` keeps the single batched forward. - Prefix sharing is off under CFG parallel, cache-dit and layerwise DiT offload. - New unit test (CPU): a resumed STG pass is `torch.equal` to a full STG pass, and capturing leaves the cond output unchanged. ## Benchmark H100 80GB, `sglang generate --model-path Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, default 768×512, 121 frames, seed 42, warm runs. title: [Fix] gdn: Stop torch.compile from cloning the state and KV pools
summary: Title: [Fix] gdn: Stop torch.compile from cloning the state and KV pools ## Motivation Fixes #51651. With `--enable-torch-compile`, Qwen3.5-9B never starts: decode CUDA graph capture runs out of memory at bs=32. Inductor clones SGLang's caches before writing them: - **GDN state.** `mamba2_layer_cache(layer_id)` slices the all-layers pool inside the compiled graph, and the packed decode kernel (a user Triton kernel) writes that slice. Inductor then clones the pool from its start through that slice: k + 1 layers' worth for GDN layer k, on every call. On an A100 80GB the 7th layer's clone (6.96 GiB) does not fit. The conv state gets the same clone from the fused conv update. - **KV cache.** `k_buffer[i]` and `v_buffer[i]` are views of one shared allocation, made once at start-up. `store_cache` writes both, and Inductor clones the whole allocation (3.39 GiB per layer here) before the write. Both reduce to a few lines with no SGLang, on torch 2.14.1 / Triton 3.8.0. Largest buffer in the generated code for a `(24, 509, 64)` tensor: | Case | Largest buffer | |---|---| | user Triton kernel writes `cache[5]`, slice taken inside the compiled fn | 6 slices (a clone of `cache[:6]`) | | same, slice made outside and passed in | none | | same launch wrapped in a custom op with `mutates_args` | none | | custom op writes two views of one tensor made outside (like K and V) | the whole tensor | | same op, both views sliced inside the compiled fn | none | Reproduction scripts and logs: https://github.com/Aagam-Bothara/rigtune/tree/main/benchmarks/sessions/2026-11/modal-sglang-compile-oom ## Mo

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Run mla_v_absorb on the transposed w_vc that DeepSeek-style loaders keep
summary: ## Motivation `mla_v_absorb` (#50997) replaces hipBLASLt's `torch.bmm` for MLA's v absorb at decode-sized batches, and #51000 calls it from `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` under `--enable-amd-monokernel`. `covered()` requires a contiguous `w_vc`, but Kimi-K3.1 and DFLASH's MLA draft load `w_vc` as `w_vc.contiguous().transpose(1, 2)`, which is not contiguous. Retain consumed event handles in a bounded deque so they can be released on the forward thread, avoiding off-thread CUDA context creation when a sampled wrapper frame outlives the call. 3. Event retirement and allocation changes affect shared paths, whose performance on other model and topology combinations remains unmeasured. title: [Feat] spec/dflash: Add opt-in prompt lookup that drafts from a request's own tokens
summary: ## Motivation Agentic and coding requests copy long spans of their own context: file contents, tool output, code written earlier in the conversation. A DFLASH drafter often misses these spans, while an exact lookup in the request's own tokens finds them. This PR adds an opt-in prompt lookup to DFLASH v2. When a request's last tokens repeat an earlier span of its own prompt or output, the tokens that followed that span replace the drafter's tokens in that request's verify block. The target still verifies every committed token. Unlike `--speculative-algorithm NGRAM`, which drafts from a host-side n-gram cache instead of a draft model, this keeps the DFLASH drafter and replaces its block on the device only where a long match exists. title: [Diffusion] Preserve mapped component weights during low-memory offload
summary: ## Motivation Component offload (`--component-residency <c>=component-offload`, and the legacy `--*-cpu-offload` flags) swapped a component out with `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` — a full device-to-host copy of **immutable** weights into fresh host memory on every single swap-out. Three problems this PR removes: 1. **A wasted D2H copy per swap-out.** Inference never mutates weights. Measured on MiniMax-H3's 9.7 GiB video VAE on an RTX 5090: 4.85 s on the first cycle, 0.37 s per cycle after; now ~0 (one device sync + a pointer rebind). 2. **Unbudgeted, kernel-locked host memory.** `module.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` allocates a *pinned* destination, entirely behind `HostPinBudget`'s back — 9.7 GiB per offloaded VAE that the kernel can never reclaim, RssAnon never shows, and no accounting ever sees. Pinned offload memory now goes through the budget, and a denial degrades to the existing pageable storage without copying anything. 3. **`keep_checkpoint_mapped` weights were destroyed after one use.** A VAE loaded as mmap views into its safetensors file (so a constrained host keeps those bytes evictable) lost the mapping permanently on the first GPU round trip. The mapping now survives: a mapped weight's host copy *is* its mmap view, never replaced. ## Modifications Five commits: 1. **BCG × offloaded-DiT guard** (`runtime/server_args/server_args.py`). Any explicitly non-resident DiT placement with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` fails at startup validation, next to the other BCG rules: BCG captures the DiT forward, every offload flavor rebinds or frees its weight storag

title: [Perf] DFLASH: Verify top-k sampled batches on the all-gathered top-k support (opt-in)
summary: ## Motivation This continues #46080 by @nbommi19, rebased onto current main with the review feedback on that PR applied. The original commits are kept. With TP > 1 and a softcapped lm_head, DFLASH verify finishes the logits all-gather in the worker. For a sampled batch it all-gathers the full fp32 logits of every verify row (`[bs * block, vocab]`), runs a top-k over the whole vocabulary, scatters the target p and the draft selector's q into vocab-sized tensors, and runs the chain sampler over the whole vocabulary. When requests sample with a top-k (Muse-Spark-Open's generation config uses top_k 64), only the top-k tokens of a row carry target mass. With `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_SPARSE_VERIFY` on, such a batch is verified on the top-k support alone: - each rank takes the top `next_power_of_2(max_top_k + 16)` logits of its vocab shard; the 16 spare slots hold logits tied with the k-th one; - the ranks all-gather those (value, id) pairs instead of their shards (at TP8 and a 202K vocabulary, 1 KB per row from each rank instead of 101 KB); - one Triton kernel softcaps and merges the candidates into each row's exact top-k and argmax, with the softcap formula of the dense gather; - one Triton kernel runs the chain accept and the residual resample on that support, with the dense path's two uniform draws in the same order. A batch the support cannot reproduce keeps the dense path: max top_k above 64 (top_k -1 included), top-p, min-p, any logit adjustment (penalties, logit bias, custom logit processor, grammar), logprobs, sampling-mask capture, block verification and padded vocab shards. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Back up separate draft KV pools in PD CPU retraction
summary: ## Motivation With `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup cpu_tensor`, a retracted PD decode request copies its KV to CPU and frees its slots. On resume it gets new slots, and the backup is written into them. Only the target KV pool is backed up. EAGLE/EAGLE3, multi-layer EAGLE, DFLASH and DSPARK drafts that do not share the target pool keep their own KV tensors, indexed by the same token slots. Once another request reuses the freed slots, the resumed request's draft reads that request's KV. Drafts then come from the wrong context, so the acceptance rate drops. Output stays correct, because the target verifies every draft token. It skips fused drafts and drafts sharing the target pool, deduplicates shared pools, and marks separate draft pools without CPU copy support (`PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4`) so `backup_kv_cache(..., "cpu_tensor")` returns `False` instead of resuming on stale draft KV. - `Scheduler.init_memory_pools` registers these pools on the target allocator when the backend resolves to `cpu_tensor`. - `Req.offload_kv_cache` and `load_kv_cache` copy every registered pool with the target KV. title: [Perf] disaggregation: Vectorize staging gather/scatter for aligned KV buffers
summary: ## Motivation The staging gather/scatter kernels read KV buffer addresses from a pointer table on the device. Triton cannot infer alignment from a loaded pointer, so the KV side is lowered to scalar loads and stores. In the PTX for the current kernels, the payload moves one element at a time, and the fused scatter kernel also uses 8 KB of shared memory that the vectorized version does not need. The KV buffers are 16-byte aligned in practice. The kernel just has no way to know. ## Modifications - Add an `ALIGNED_16` specialization to the gather and scatter kernels. When it is on, the row bases get a `tl.multiple_of(..., 16)` hint and Triton emits vector loads and stores. For scatter, the hint covers the fused and persistent kernels; the per-page scatter kernel keeps generic addressing. - Check the KV buffers once when Mooncake or NIXL registers them (`kv_buffers_preserve_16_byte_alignment`, called from `build_staging_kv_buffer_info`). The result is stored with the buffer info, so transfers do not rescan the buffer list. - On each transfer, only the staging buffer address is checked (`_can_use_aligned_staging_copy`), because it can start at any ring offset. The strides and head offsets come from the buffer shape, so the registration check covers them. If any check fails, the transfer uses the generic kernel, same as today. summary: ## Motivation A HiCache load-back enqueues every layer's host-to-device copy before the forward starts. Streams share a small number of hardware queues (`CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, 8 in SGLang), and a breakable prefill CUDA graph replays each segment on its own stream. title: [Fix] disaggregation: Don't count a request-aborted prefill KV send as a transfer failure
summary: ## Motivation In PD disaggregation, a prefill request whose KV send is in flight sits in the prefill transfer queue. A request abort (for example a client disconnect, or the router closing the prefill stream once decode has the KV) reaches `_abort_prefill_transfer`, which aborts the request's KV sender. The sender then reports the transfer as failed. The shared sender abort (`CommonKVSender.abort`, used by the mooncake, nixl, mori and ascend backends) marks the room failed, notifies decode, and turns an already-concluded success into a failure. `handle_inflight_transfer_failure` treats that failure like any other: - it logs `Prefill transfer failed ...` as a warning; - it increments `num_transfer_failed_reqs`. On a PD deployment where the prefill stream is closed after every handoff, this turns routine aborts into a steady stream of transfer-failure warnings, and a transfer-failure count that rises with traffic rather than with real faults. The abort itself is already counted, by the tokenizer, when it sends the AbortReq. ## Modifications - `Req.disagg_transfer_aborted` (default `False`) records that a request abort ended the in-flight KV send. - `_abort_prefill_transfer` sets it when the `AbortReq` carries no `abort_message`. - Scheduler timeout aborts carry one, so they stay transfer failures, as before. - Every rank receives the same `AbortReq`, so every rank marks the request alike. - `handle_inflight_transfer_failure` logs a marked failure at debug and skips `increment_transfer_failed_reqs`. - The response is unchanged: the same message with a 500. - Retirement and the

title: [Perf] custom-all-reduce: Map each peer graph-input allocation once at registration
summary: ## Motivation `VmmGraphInputManager.register_graph_inputs` gives every rank a local mapping of each peer's CUDA-graph-input memory. With expandable segments a captured tensor can cross allocation boundaries, so its peer mapping has to be contiguous. The current code builds one reserved span per distinct tuple of allocations an input covers, and imports and maps every allocation of that tuple again for each such tuple. Graph inputs overlap heavily on the same allocations, so the number of imports and mappings grows with the number of distinct input tuples rather than with the number of allocations, and a peer's memory ends up imported and mapped many times over. Every import and map is a driver call that serializes on the driver lock, so registration gets slow, and so does anything else that goes through the driver while the mappings pile up. With many graph inputs per rank this dominated CUDA graph capture time. ## Modifications - `register_graph_inputs` maps a peer's allocations in runs that keep the peer's layout: one reserved VA range per run of allocations adjacent in the peer's address space, each allocation imported and mapped once at its original relative offset. An input's chunks are adjacent by construction, so its peer address is the run address of its first chunk plus the input offset; no per-input span is reserved or mapped any more. - New helper `adjacent_runs` groups `(base_ptr, alloc_size)` allocations into address-ordered runs that break at every gap. - Registration raises if an input's chunks turn out not to be adjacent on a peer, instead of handing out a w

When the profiler stops with rounds still in a window, those sends are waited after `stop()` has freed the event storage, and the late end callbacks write into freed host memory. title: [Fix] hicache: fold page-layout tag into HiCacheFile key suffix
summary: ## Motivation Two sglang servers pointing at the same `--hicache-storage-backend file` directory silently reuse each other's KV pages any time the key does not distinguish the page layout. The original bug was reported in #51045 — the same writer→reader flow was shown to return garbage text under HTTP 200 when the reader's `--dtype` differed from the writer's. fp16 and bf16 pages are the same size, so nothing rejects the stale key at read time. #38362 fixed the dtype half of this by folding the logical KV dtype into the storage namespace (via `storage_model_name`). The remaining gap on main is layout: - `HiCacheStorageConfig.is_page_first_layout` describes the byte order *within* a page, - the file backend's `config_suffix` does not include it, - `hicache_storage.py`'s TODO comment already says "_Other layout differences still need extra_backend_tag_", and while simm / mooncake / umbp / npu_memcache honor that key today, `HiCacheFile` does not. Any two servers that share `SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR` — one with `--dtype fp16`, one with `--dtype bf16` is the flavour the issue covers — will run into this again the moment a layout-altering change is made (page-first vs not, or any other backend-specific byte format, for example a future FP8 KV layout change that reuses the same logical dtype tag). The reader proceeds to apply KV values written under a different layout, returning HTTP 200 with corrupt text, exactly like the report. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py`: fold the layout tag and the user-supplied `extra_backend_tag` into th

title: [Feat] hicache: Add unified Engram store and support Qwen4-Exp
summary: ## Motivation Add a **unified Engram store abstraction to HiCache**, and support **Qwen4-Exp as its first model integration**. HiCache provides a common interface for storing and looking up immutable Engram tables. Models supply row IDs and interpret the returned bytes, while storage backends handle table ownership and data access. This separates model computation from the storage implementation and gives Engram integrations a shared storage contract. This PR introduces the HiCache abstraction, implements a local backend using [Mooncake EngramStore](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4701), and connects Qwen4-Exp PLE N-gram tables to it. The storage interface is model-independent; Qwen4-Exp is the only model integrated and validated in this PR. This supersedes #44521. ## Modifications - **Add the HiCache Engram store interface.** `HiCacheEngramStorage` defines `initialize(rows)`, `lookup(ids)`, and `close()` for immutable byte-row tables. It is defined at the end of `hicache_storage.py`, with row-based semantics independent of the existing KV interface. `sglang.srt.mem_cache.engram.create_storage` creates row storage within the Engram module, independently of a KV cache or host KV pool. - **Add the Mooncake backend.** `MooncakeEngramStorage` implements the HiCache interface over Mooncake EngramStore, including owned local snapshots and CUDA stream-ordered lookup. The embedding adapter uses the HiCache storage contract. - **Support Qwen4-Exp.** Route its PLE N-gram embedding construction through the shared adapter. title: [Feat] dsa: Packed verify for DFLASH compact mode on Kimi K3.1
summary: ## Motivation Main's DFLASH worker can plan a verify length per request and run a packed ("compact") verify since #46190. On Kimi K3.1 it refuses `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact` at startup, because the `dsa` attention backend does not support packed verify. This PR adds that support for `flashmla_kv` with DCP 1. On K3.1 that means passing `--dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv` on Blackwell GPUs, where the default is `prims_ts`; the cookbook's DCP 8 cells and ROCm still refuse compact at startup. It builds on #46190 and does not repeat it. The assumption it removes: DSA's verify metadata expects every request to have the same number of query rows. Compact verify packs a different number from each request. Lengths `[2, 5, 1]` give eight rows with boundaries `[0, 2, 7, 8]`, and reshaping them as `[requests, next_n]` loses which request each row belongs to and how many keys it may see. Whether compact helps K3.1 is not known yet. On Qwen3.8, #46190 measured it ahead of static only at its highest concurrency, and slower below c64. **Since the previous revision.** Merging main (`681f1b5893`) replaced this branch's copies of the worker, planner, relay, mRoPE and profiler changes with #46190's. `c5b4786b43` deletes the `attention.fused_dsa_ragged_query_rows` kernel, its zero-length rows and the `_forward_flashmla_kv` output mask. The existing extend kernel already computes per-row lengths, owners and page tables for requests of different widths, so a second kernel for the same job is not needed. ## Modifications ### 1. title: [Perf] multimodal: Token-bucketed ViT CUDA graphs for Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5
summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` keys ViT graphs on the exact `(seq_len, cu_seqlens)` layout, so with mixed image sizes almost every batch captures a new graph with its own memory pool. On Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5 with 1–4 mixed-size images per request, the server runs out of GPU memory at concurrency 8, so the graph path is not usable in real serving today. Part of the ViT-overhead item in #43314. ## Modifications - New `ViTBucketedCudaGraphRunner`: one graph per token bucket (256–4096 pre-merge tokens by default, `SGLANG_VIT_CUDA_GRAPH_TOKEN_BUCKETS`). All buckets are captured once on the first image, largest first, in one private pool and capture stream. Each batch is padded to the smallest bucket that holds it and replayed once; larger batches run eagerly. - `cu_seqlens` has a fixed length per bucket (empty sequences fill the tail) and is rewritten on every replay. Padding rows form their own 64-token sequences, so they never attend to real tokens and their attention cost stays linear. - The Qwen3-VL vision tower (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Omni vision) uses it on the `fa3` backend; other backends and models keep the existing runner. Eager and graph paths share `_forward_blocks`. - The bucketed path keeps the compiled rotary kernel (every bucket is warmed up before capture), so outputs are bit-identical to eager. Replay returns a copy, so the embedding cache never aliases the graph output buffer (the issue #43315 fixes for the existing runner). ## Accuracy Tests In-server check, 1×H100: every vision batch was rerun eagerly with the graph env off and compared

title: [Perf] Kimi-K3.1: keep the breakable prefill CUDA graph on by default on CUDA
summary: ## Motivation Kimi-K3.1 prefills eagerly by default. The breakable prefill CUDA graph is switched off for it by two default rules in `disable_breakable_cudagraph_if_incompatible`: "KDA hybrid linear attention" (every KDA model except GLM-5.3 Flash) and "decode context parallel (dcp_size > 1)". An eager prefill pass costs 200-300 ms for a few hundred new tokens, and every running request waits for it. With a speculative-decoding server at 48 concurrent short requests, prefill was 42-47% of scheduler wall time. The capture path itself is already there: `kda_prefill_graph.py` captures the KDA extend, the prefill graph runner plans the DCP gather at capture and replay (#38943), and Kimi-K3.1 is on the multimodal breakable-graph allowlist. Passing `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` explicitly works today; this PR proposes making that the default for Kimi-K3.1 on CUDA. Opened as a draft: the question for maintainers is whether the validation below is enough to flip the default, or whether it should stay opt-in. ## Modifications - `arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py`: exempt Kimi-K3.1 on CUDA (`is_kimi_k31(...) and not is_hip()`) from the KDA rule and from the DCP rule. ROCm is left as is (not validated here). An explicit `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill` or `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` still takes precedence, as before. title: [Fix] multimodal: Remove unnecessary pin_memory() in CPU video decoding and preprocessing
summary: ## Motivation `VideoDecoderWrapper.get_frames_as_tensor()` / `_parallel_decode()`, `qwen_vl_media_processing.preprocess_video_sync()`, and `ernie45_vl.preprocess_video()` unconditionally call `.pin_memory()` on CPU-decoded video frame tensors whenever the host is not running on a CPU-only engine (`not is_cpu()`). This causes **both** a permanent host RAM leak and silent GPU 0 VRAM consumption (including HTTP 500 `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` failures), plus wasted CPU decode latency, while providing zero H2D transfer benefit to any caller in the codebase. ### Trigger Paths #### 1. summary: ## Motivation TeaCache is already implemented in sglang, but it only works for models that ship calibrated polynomial `coefficients` and a `teacache_thresh`. MoE dual-transformer models (Wan2.2) need one polynomial per expert; `TeaCacheParams` only had a single shared set. 3.
