title: [Fix] disaggregation: Bind a bootstrap room to the request that claims it
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51980. The same root cause is behind #40125. The prefill server files every decode destination for a `bootstrap_room` under that room, and the transfer worker sends the room's KV to whatever is filed there (`nixl/conn.py` and `mooncake/conn.py` bootstrap threads). Nothing checks that a destination belongs to the prefill server's own request. When a client sends a request with a room that another request is using, two things can go wrong: - a decode request on that room receives the other request's KV and returns the other request's output with HTTP 200, while the owner's decode request waits until `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` (the issue); - a second prefill request on that room sends its KV into the owner's decode request, which then returns text from the other prompt (see the `dup_prefill` row below). Rejecting only the second registration of a room does not prevent the first case. In the issue's order, the other request registers first. ## Modifications Prefill and decode compute a fingerprint of the inputs whose KV one transfer carries. A room belongs to the one live prefill sender that claims it, and only destinations and ABORTs with that request's fingerprint act on the room. - `kv_transfer_fingerprint()` (`disaggregation/utils.py`) is a 64-bit BLAKE2b digest of the prompt ids, the LoRA adapter name, `input_embeds` and positional embedding overrides. title: [Fix] kernels/quantization: Use int64 row offsets in the per-token int8 quant kernel
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51104. `_per_token_quant_int8` computed `row_id * stride_x` and `row_id * stride_xq` from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`. For inputs with at least 2^31 elements the product wraps to a negative offset and the kernel reads and writes before the tensors. The fp8 siblings already use int64 here, and #51148 fixed the same wrap in `_per_token_group_quant_int8`. Activation quantization of W8A8-INT8 linear layers and the channel-wise int8 fused MoE reach this path. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: `_per_token_quant_int8` takes the `USE_INT64_OFFSETS` constexpr that #51148 introduced for the group kernel. The launcher sets it only when `x.numel() >= 2**31`, and only then is `row_id` widened to int64. Every smaller input compiles the original int32 kernel, so the shapes served in practice run exactly the code on `main`. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_int8_kernel.py`: new `TestInt8QuantLargeInputOffsets` (CUDA, skipped below about 10 GB of free GPU memory). It quantizes an fp16 input of 83890 x 25600 (2,147,584,000 elements, just past 2^31) whose row `r` holds the constant `r % 100 + 1`, with both per-token kernels. It asserts the per-row scales equal `value / 127` and that the last 16 rows, which sit past 2^31 elements, quantize exactly like the early rows with the same value. It compares against equal-value rows instead of a fixed code because the group kernel truncates, so some rows give 126 instead of 127. title: [Doc] cookbook: Correct the GLM-5.3-Flash note on prefill CP with PD disaggregation
summary: ## Motivation The GLM-5.3-Flash cookbook says prefill CP and PD disaggregation cannot be combined (§3.5) and that selecting a PD role disables prefill CP (§3.6). The Playground's CP chip and PD note give the same reason, and the PD note adds that CP/TP group sharing cannot transfer the KDA state between PD workers. Since #43774 and #49089, the server accepts prefill CP on a PD prefill worker that runs over Mooncake with EP, DP and PP at 1, with native MTP (top-k 1), DFlash2 or no speculative decoding (`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/cp_tp_group_sharing_hook.py`). The prefill worker's CP rank r transfers as TP rank r, including its KDA state shard, and the decode worker serves plain TP. `test/registered/e2e/disaggregation/test_glm53_cp_bcg_dflash.py` covers CP4 prefill to TP4 decode with DFlash2 and with MTP. ## Modifications - §3.5: replace "Prefill CP and PD disaggregation cannot be enabled together" with a pointer to §3.6. - §3.6: say that the Playground removes the CP flags for PD roles because it does not generate this combination yet, and list the conditions and flags for running CP on the prefill worker by hand. - `glm-5.3-flash.jsx`: reword the CP chip's disable reason and the PD note to match. The Playground's behavior does not change, and no generated command changes. Letting it emit CP for a PD prefill worker would also need EP gating for PD prefill, so I left that out. title: [Feat] rust-server: Fall back to the Python MM processor
summary: ## Motivation With `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, the Rust server handles HTTP, tokenization and multimodal preprocessing inside the scheduler process. Its multimodal preprocessing is a Rust pipeline that exists only for the Qwen-VL family. Any other multimodal model fails at launch, so it cannot use the Rust server. This PR serves such a model with SGLang's existing Python multimodal processor, called from the Rust server's multimodal worker threads. Qwen-VL models keep the Rust pipeline by default, at the same speed as on main (see Speed Tests). The environment variable `SGLANG_FORCE_PYTHON_MM_PROCESSOR=1` selects the Python processor for them too. The open items are listed at the end. ![The launch gate starts the Rust MM worker pool with a PyO3 adapter; each worker calls SGLang's Python multimodal processor, and its pickled output rides the request ring to the drain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnanPrash/sglang/0e63b4702c89ff21661b1342555a3a3065f2aa77/sgl-py-mm-fallback-architecture.png) ## Startup command The command does not change. title: [Feat] mem_cache: Evict a Mamba state together with the KV only it serves (unit eviction)
summary: ## Motivation On a hybrid model (Mamba, gated delta rule), a cached prefix can be resumed only at a node that holds a recurrent state. The radix cache evicts states and KV separately by LRU, so under memory pressure it keeps full-attention KV that no state can serve and evicts states that the next turn of a conversation resumes from. This PR adds unit eviction from FlashStates ([paper](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.flashstate), [code](https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FlashStates), [project page](https://flashstates.ai)), the "Unit eviction" item of the roadmap #50700. ## Modifications `--enable-mamba-unit-eviction` (off by default): - A cached Mamba state and the full-attention KV that only it can serve form a unit: when the state is evicted, that KV is freed with it. - KV that no state can serve is evicted before any other KV. - The bookkeeping lives in `unified_cache/unit_eviction.py`: per-node counts of the states at or below each node, updated when a state appears or goes, so no eviction decision walks a subtree. With the flag off, the cache behaves exactly as on `main`. With it on, the Python radix-tree core is used (selected automatically). The flag is refused with `--disable-radix-cache`, a registered `--radix-cache-backend`, `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (for now) and on a model without Mamba states. The flag is documented in `server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests Unit eviction changes which cached prefixes stay on the GPU, not what the model computes. - GSM8K on every benchmark server below, on a boot with the same server arguments just before each run: 200

summary: ## Motivation A page-striped HiCache host tier for aggregated DeepSeek-V4 (`--hicache-host-shard stripe`). DSv4 decodes with head-TP, so every rank must keep the full device KV, and device-side KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, #30501) does not apply. title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Feed encoder-only decode tails through DSpark verify steps
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation Stacked on #45265 (encoder-only prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1 PD). Until that merges, this diff also contains its two commits; the change here is the last commit, `50bc63b0ef`. In #45265 the prefill server stops 128 tokens short of the prompt end. Decode then runs those last tokens (the "tail") through all 40 layers before it samples the first token. #45265 runs each tail as an extend step that alternates with decode steps. With decode DP attention every rank joins that step, so a steady stream of new requests costs every running request extra steps. At c160 the tail extends raised decode ITL p50 from 11.0 to 15.8 ms. This PR runs the tail inside the speculative verify steps that decode performs anyway: - A transferred request joins the running batch with its KV at the tail start. - Each DSpark verify step feeds the request's next 6 prompt tokens as forced drafts. Their logits rows are one-hot, so the normal accept takes exactly those tokens. - A 128-token tail therefore rides about 22 verify steps instead of separate extend steps. - Late layers floor their sliding window at the tail start, so each tail row attends to the same keys as in the extend. - Prompt tokens never reach the output or the speculative metrics. The path is behind `SGLANG_DSV41_FUSED_TAIL=1` (default off). Without it, #45265's extend path is unchanged. **Impact** - **Accuracy:** GPQA diamond (`sgl-eval`): split with fused tails 90.6% (358/395) vs stock PD + prefill HiCache 91.9% (362/394), within the ~2-point standard error. GSM8K (400 questions): fused 0.900, stock 0.900. - **

summary: ## Motivation With trace level 1, a level-2 DP dispatch slice is filtered out. The current early return also discards `thread_finish_flag=True`, so a serialized request context can retain its thread span after dispatch has completed. Its destructor may then report normal completion as an unclosed span. Request completion also ends children using a fresh clock reading instead of the supplied end timestamp. The async path has the same early return and must still notify the exporter when a filtered slice completes a thread. This patch separates lifecycle completion from the decision to record a slice. title: Fix MTP draft embed/lm_head dedup running after KV pool sizing
summary: ## 📌 Summary Fixes an MTP (NEXTN) memory-accounting bug where ~2.5GB of VRAM on a 27B-class model was permanently left unused after startup, because the draft model's `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` dedup ran **after** the KV cache pool had already been sized. ## 🔍 Problem With `--speculative-algo NEXTN` (MTP draft, e.g. Qwen3.5/3.8), the draft model initially owns its own `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`. `EagleWorkerV2.init_lm_head()` shares the target model's tensors with the draft (`set_embed_and_head` / `set_lm_head_from_target`), deleting the draft-side duplicates and calling `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`. However, `init_token_map()` / `init_lm_head()` were only called from `alloc_memory_pool()`, which the scheduler invokes **after** `init_target_memory_pool()` has already computed the KV budget from current free memory. The freed ~2.5GB was therefore invisible to the sizing pass and stayed idle until the next process restart: ``` Load weight end ... type=Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, mem usage=28.39 GB Load weight end ... type=Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP, mem usage=5.18 GB <- includes ~2.5GB dup embed/lm_head KV Cache VA upper bound ... #tokens: 273K ``` ## ✅ Solution Move `init_token_map()` and `init_lm_head()` from `alloc_memory_pool()` to the end of `EagleWorkerV2.__init__`, i.e. before the scheduler sizes the main KV pool. Both calls only depend on state already set earlier in `__init__` (`target_worker`, `draft_runner`, `speculative_algorithm`); `hot_token_id` is itself assigned *inside* `init_token_map()`, so nothing breaks. ## 📊 Measured effect RTX 4090D 48GB, Qwen3.5-27B fp8

title: [NPU] Keep DeepSeek router GEMM output in fp32
summary: ## Motivation DeepSeek MoE router logits should preserve FP32 precision before expert selection. On NPU, the existing fallback uses `F.linear` with BF16 activations and weights, which writes the router logits in BF16. The downstream NPU top-k path converts those logits to FP32, but that post-hoc conversion cannot recover the mantissa bits already lost during BF16 writeback. This affects all three NPU execution paths in `MoEGate.forward`: - regular routing - prefill context-parallel routing - deterministic inference Fixes #34861 ## Modifications - Keep the authoritative `MoEGate.weight` parameter in FP32 on NPU. Checkpoint loading and runtime weight updates continue to write into the same live parameter, avoiding a stale derived cache. - Add a shared NPU FP32 router projection: `F.linear(hidden_states.float(), weight_fp32)`. - Route regular, prefill context-parallel, and deterministic NPU execution through the shared projection. - Preserve the existing CUDA, ROCm/aiter, CPU, and XPU dispatch paths. - Do not change NPU top-k, correction bias, grouped routing, checkpoint format, or public APIs. Keeping the live NPU gate weight in FP32 avoids converting the entire router weight on every forward pass. It increases persistent gate storage by two bytes per weight element compared with BF16. ## Accuracy Tests ### CPU CI-compatible tests Environment: - Python 3.11.15 - PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu Command: ```bash python -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v2_npu_router.py -v ``` Results: - New focused test `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v2_npu_router.py`: 7 passed

title: [Perf] gemma4: Replay the audio encoder from frame-bucket CUDA graphs
summary: ## Motivation Gemma 4 E2B/E4B encode audio with a 12-layer conformer that runs eagerly, one clip at a time. Its local attention is assembled from many small fp32 ops, so one 3–5 s clip takes about 22 ms on an H100, almost all of it launch overhead. Prefill batches rarely hold more than one new audio request, so on ASR traffic the tower sets TTFT and caps throughput. ## Modifications - **CUDA graphs:** a single clip replays a CUDA graph captured for the next 128-frame bucket, up to 30.72 s of audio. - All 24 buckets are captured on the first clip, largest first, into one private pool. On E4B this takes 1.7 s. - The extra frames are padding, masked the same way the processor's own padding is. The valid output frames do not change. - Longer clips, batches of more than one clip, and TP > 1 run eagerly. - `SGLANG_GEMMA4_AUDIO_CUDA_GRAPH=0` turns this off. - **Batching:** `get_audio_feature` encodes every clip of a batch in one tower pass and takes the valid frames with one boolean index, instead of one tower pass and one index per clip. ## Accuracy Tests The graph output is bit-identical to an eager pass over the same padded input: 153 of 153 encoder calls in a serving run compared with `torch.equal`. Padding changes the GEMM shapes, so bf16 rounding differs from an unpadded pass. WER does not move: | LibriSpeech test-clean (≤30 s), `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | WER main | WER this PR | Identical transcripts | |---|---|---|---| | concurrency 1 (64 clips) | 2.81% | 2.81% | 63/64 | | concurrency 8 (384 clips) | 2.61% | 2.64% | 375/384 | | concurrency 32 (384 clips) | 2.60% | 2.62% | 3

title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] kvcache: Gate fused FP8 prefix-valid commit kernel on SM89+
summary: Motivation set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8 (added by #40785) fuses FP8 KV-cache quantization into the prefix-valid commit kernel used by DFLASH speculative decoding. It compiles fp8e4nv inside a Triton kernel, which only works on SM89+ (Ada / Hopper). On SM86 (Ampere, e.g. RTX 3090) the Triton codegen rejects fp8e4nv: ValueError: type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5'). The dispatch in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid only checks the KV cache dtype and the resolved K/V scales — it does not inspect the compute capability — so an SM86 box is sent straight into the fused kernel and crashes on startup. The pre-#40785 eager path (PyTorch-layer quantization + the generic byte-copy Triton kernel) is left untouched below the fused branch, so the fix is to fall back to it on pre-SM89 GPUs. This is the prefix-valid writer specifically. #31652 gates the ordinary set_kv_buffer FP8 stores on SM89+ but leaves the prefix-valid dispatch ungated, and #42982 (SM89 NaN-saturation) does not add a capability guard either. Modifications - Add a module-level _FP8_FUSED_OK that is True only on CUDA SM89+ (torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (8, 9)). - Add and _FP8_FUSED_OK to the fused-branch condition in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid, so pre-SM89 GPUs take the existing eager-quantization fallback (the pre-#40785 path) instead of the fused fp8e4nv kernel. SM89+ keeps the fused fast path unchanged; SM86 / SM80 and other pre-SM89 arches fall back to eager quantization, which is exactly what worked before #407

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Speed up the MiniMax-H3 video VAE decode on ROCm (gfx950)
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm the MiniMax-H3 video VAE decoder (a 36-block ViT, 32 heads of 64, 1797 tokens per tile) leaves three things on slow paths: - **Attention.** torch's fused SDPA corrupts this decoder on gfx950, so the ViT attention runs an FP32 math replica (#47570): two FP32 GEMMs and an FP32 softmax per `[1, 32, 1797, 64]` call, 7056 calls per 5 s request. - **The decoder fast path.** The quality-gated fast path (batched tile decode, fused residual-add RMSNorm) is installed only from the CUDA platform, so on ROCm every tile runs its own decoder forward. The fused norms were kept off ROCm (#43350) because they decoded to NaN there: their PTX `mul.rn` has no HIP lowering. - **The QK norm.** The affine-free per-head RMSNorm (64 wide) goes through aten's `vectorized_layer_norm_kernel<half, float, rms_norm>`: one 256-thread block per row, after a `.contiguous()` copy of the strided q/k chunk, 45 us a call and 14112 calls per 1-GPU request (0.64 s). The NeoX rope then makes it three launches and four passes over q and k per attention block. ## Modifications - `minimax_h3_video_vae/attention.py`: on gfx950, half-precision inputs on the GPU go to aiter's flash kernel (`aiter.flash_attn_func`), the fused FP32-accumulating class that CUDA's SDPA uses for the same call. FP32 inputs and CPU inputs keep the math replica. The attention module is shared with the MiniMax-H3-Image decoder, which takes the same kernel. - `norm/aten_rms_norm_rocm_triton.py` (new), `aten_rms_norm_rocm`: a replica of ROCm aten's affine-free RMSNorm for FP16/BF16 rows of 64, 128 or 256. It keeps that kernel

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Assemble a MiniMax-H3 VAE window's tiles in one kernel
summary: ## Motivation The tiled decode of the MiniMax-H3 VAE blends, crops and copies every decoded tile into the canvas with about eight small launches a tile (~225 for a 28-tile window), and they run between two tile groups' forwards. This PR replaces the first commit of #52052. The other two commits of #52052 (the `Normalize` constants built once, and starting each window's tile gather before assembling the last) were dropped: measured on main with #52051 applied, they did not help (numbers below). ## Modifications - `layout/h3_vae_tile_assemble_triton.py` (new), `h3_vae_assemble_tiles` (Triton): the eager chain's FP32 arithmetic per canvas pixel in one launch. Each pixel takes the vertical blend with the tile above, then the horizontal blend with the tile to the left, both neighbours as decoded, each blend as two products and one add without FMA (`enable_fp_fusion=False`). Per-axis index and weight tables are built once per layout. Where an overlap is wider than the part of the next tile that is kept (latent tiles of a tiled encode), only the kept rows are blended, as the eager chain does after cropping. - `klvae.py`: `AutoencoderKL._assemble_tiles` mounts the kernel on ROCm only, behind a per-layout first-sight check against the eager chain (`BitExactFusionGate`). The eager chain stays as `_assemble_tiles_eager`, and CUDA returns to it before anything else, so the CUDA decode is main's. title: [Perf] diffusion: Pipeline the MiniMax-H3 VAE decode windows
summary: > Stacked on #52051 (`perf/minimax-h3-audio-decode-beside-tiles`): the gather below starts from that PR's ownership-list gather, and the hand-off rotation changes its audio-rank hand-off. Only the last three commits are new here. ## Motivation Every decode rank decoded a temporal window's tiles, waited on their NCCL all-gather, and assembled the window before it started the next window's tiles. The assembly alone is about eight small launches a tile (~225 for a 28-tile window) between two tile groups' forwards, so each window paid its gather, the wait for the slowest rank and the assembly on the critical path. On ROCm the streamed decode also blocked the host once per tile group in torchvision's `Normalize` (in a rank-0 trace of a 5 s request on 8x MI355X, `hipMemcpyWithStream` under `normalize`). ## Modifications Three commits. 1. **One-kernel tile assembly** (`[AMD]`). `h3_vae_assemble_tiles` (Triton, `layout/h3_vae_tile_assemble_triton.py`) runs the eager chain's FP32 arithmetic per canvas pixel in one launch: the vertical blend with the tile above, then the horizontal blend with the tile to the left, both neighbours as decoded, each as two products and one add without FMA (`enable_fp_fusion=False`). `klvae._assemble_tiles` mounts it behind a per-layout first-sight check against the eager chain (`BitExactFusionGate`), which stays as `_assemble_tiles_eager`. Exported and registered with the other MiniMax-H3 VAE output kernels and listed in the kernels README. title: [Feat] dflash: Support Domino transformer corrector heads
summary: ## Motivation Some DFlash checkpoints use a transformer corrector to condition each proposal on earlier picks in the block and a short window of target states. SGLang already supports their draft backbone. This adds the missing conditional head. ## Modifications - Load `DFlash2DominoDraftModel` through the existing DFlash weight loader when the checkpoint selects `conditional_head="transformer"`. - Reuse the target context projection and DFlash ring indexing. Prefill populates the window, and verification appends the committed prefix of each block. A prefix-cache hit starts the window at the first newly computed token. - Run the corrector eagerly with greedy proposals. The existing target verifier handles greedy and sampled requests. The launch interface stays the same. ## Accuracy tests The CPU tests compare incremental corrector states and token IDs with a full-block teacher-forced reference. summary: # Weight Loader RFC Claude assisted, I took a pass, and most of the suggestions seem reaonsable. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the fault is attributed to **sglang's own Triton fused-MoE kernel on the unquantized (draft-model) MoE path** — not to any FlashInfer MegaMOE kernel: ``` srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py forward_impl -> run_moe_core srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:1008 apply srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:1110 forward_cuda srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton.py:129 run srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:620 _fused_moe_kernel_sequence kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:1004 invoke_fused_moe_kernel triton/runtime/jit.py -> <illegal memory access> ``` So this looks less like a MegaMOE kernel defect and more like a state/config conflict between the two MoE backends coexisting in one server: the main model runs MegaMOE while the EAGLE draft model runs the unquantized Triton fused-MoE runner, and the draft path faults. Note `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` is not in `validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model`'s `validated_architectures`; we added it locally in order to evaluate MegaMOE (see Reproduction). title: [Roadmap] Unified Hybrid Radix Cache Refactor
summary: Blog: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-11-unified-radix-cache/ ## Motivation The current radix cache implementations (RadixCache, MambaRadixCache, SWARadixCache, etc.) share a large amount of logic but are maintained as separate, diverged copies. This leads to code duplication, inconsistent behavior, and high maintenance burden when extending cache functionality to new model types (e.g., hybrid linear models, sliding window attention models). The goal of this refactor is to unify the hybrid radix cache hierarchy around a common base interface, making it easier to: - Add new cache variants without duplicating logic - Ensure consistency across all cache implementations - Enable future extensions (e.g., HiCache, PD disaggregation, new model architectures) @hzh0425 @yizhang2077 @pansicheng @ispobock ## Progress ### Stage 0: Unify Radix Tree Interface - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17142 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17397 @yizhang2077 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17401 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17852 @pansicheng - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18147 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19427 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19429 @hzh0425 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20330 @pansicheng - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20590 @hzh0425 ### Stage 1: Support Unified HybridRadixTree V2 - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21206 @hzh0425 @ispobock @yizhang2077 @pansicheng - [x] Move UnifiedRadixTree into the main

Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Motivation The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's sizing formula prices the GDN state pool as the binding constraint on consumer GPUs: *"the GDN state pool (sets the concurrency ceiling)"*, with `state/slot = 153.9 MB` at float32. On a 32GB RTX 5090 at the default sizing, a bfloat16 state pool pins the ceiling the way the cookbook warns about — the server logs *"max_running_requests is capped to 7 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=36, 5 state slots per request)"*. title: Prefill CUDA graph reserves ~1.8 GB and starves quantized-KV long-context prefill on small cards (no auto-disable rule looks at free VRAM)
summary: ## Summary On a small-VRAM card, the prefill CUDA graph and a length-proportional KV dequant workspace compete for the same memory, and nothing in the resolution path notices. The result is not an OOM — the server starts fine and then stalls at long context while still reporting 100% GPU utilisation. Disabling the prefill graph took 96K prefill from **202 to 893 tok/s (4.4x)** on our setup, and made short prompts **4-7% faster** as well. This is not a bug in the prefill graph. It is a resolution gap: **no auto-disable rule considers free VRAM.** ## Setup - Qwen3.8-27B (dense hybrid SSM: 48 linear-attn + 16 full-attn layers), 2-bit weights - Quantized KV cache (INT2, via the OSCAR path in #32129 — but the mechanism applies to any KV recipe that dequantizes a prefix) - 2x RTX 5070 12 GB (sm_120), TP2, WSL2 - sglang 0.5.19, torch 2.13.0+cu129 - `--chunked-prefill-size 4096 --attention-backend triton` ## What happens 0.5.19 captures the prefill graph over **51 token shapes** (4096 down to 4) and holds **1.81 GB**. A quantized KV cache has to materialise the cached prefix back to model dtype before attention, and that transient scales with **sequence length** — roughly 337 MB + 5.58 MB per 1K tokens here, so ~873 MB at 96K. With 12 GB per card there is not room for both. title: [Fix] speculative: Exact sampling penalties and min_new_tokens in DFlash and DSpark verify
summary: ## Motivation DFlash and DSpark verify ignore `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `repetition_penalty` and `min_new_tokens`. Nothing counts the tokens they commit in the penalty tables, and verify reads `acc_linear_penalties`, a field that `SamplingBatchInfo` does not have. So a request with `min_new_tokens` can stop early, and a request with a repetition penalty gets the same logits as one without. This PR counts every committed token and penalizes each verify row as decoding one token at a time would. The results are bitwise equal to non-speculative decoding. ### Penalties in a verify block In each step of chain speculative decoding, the draft model proposes $K$ tokens $d_1, \dots, d_K$. The target model then runs once over $K + 1$ tokens: the anchor $a$ (the token sampled last in the previous step) followed by the drafts. Row 0 of the target's output predicts the token after $a$ and row $j$ the token after $d_j$. Verify accepts drafts from left to right while they agree with these rows, then samples a bonus token from the first row that disagrees, or from row $K$. Row $j$ is used only when $d_1, \dots, d_j$ are accepted, and then the output so far ends with $a, d_1, \dots, d_j$. So the penalties of row $j$ must count $d_1, \dots, d_j$ in addition to the earlier output and $a$: | Row | Predicts the token after | Output that its penalties count | |---|---|---| | 0 | $a$ | earlier output, $a$ | | 1 | $d_1$ | earlier output, $a$, $d_1$ | | $j$ | $d_j$ | earlier output, $a$, $d_1, \dots, d_j$ | For example, with the drafts "the cat sat", row 3 predicts the word after "sa

title: [Fix] sglang-server: Order cross-DP weight updates through DP rank 0's listener
summary: Part of #51333 (item 2): with the Rust server at dp_size > 1, two cross-rank weight updates sent to two listeners at the same time deadlock. ## Summary Before: each origin holds its own update lock across the fan-out, and its peer relay waits for the other listener's lock. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C1 as client 1 participant L0 as listener (rank 0) participant L1 as listener (rank 1) participant C2 as client 2 C1->>L0: update_weights_from_disk Note over L0: takes rank 0's update lock C2->>L1: update_weights_from_disk Note over L1: takes rank 1's update lock L0->>L1: peer relay (waits for rank 1's lock) L1->>L0: peer relay (waits for rank 0's lock) Note over L0,L1: circular wait: both listeners stay in update hold ``` After: DP rank 0's listener is the coordinator. Every cross-rank weight update (`update_weights_from_disk`, `begin_weight_update`, `end_weight_update`, over HTTP or gRPC) runs there, so both schedulers apply the updates in one order. ```diff cross-rank weight update arrives at any listener (the origin) - hold_for_update (origin's own update lock) - fan_out to every peer + origin is rank 0 -> coordinate + origin is rank k -> POST /internal/weight_update to rank 0 (takes no update lock) + +coordinate (rank 0 only; any other listener answers 421) + spawned, so a client disconnect cannot stop a half-sent update + abort own generations, then abort_peers(abort_all) + hold_for_update (rank 0's update lock; later updates queue FIFO) + fan_out_within(peers, 30 min per peer) + release ``` The 30 min deadline is arbitrary and generous; the origin waits 31 min

title: [Perf] [AMD] muse-spark: Faster FP8 joint router/pooler GEMM for decode and verify
summary: ## Motivation On MI355X, `_joint_fp8_partial` (the FP8 joint router/pooler front in `router_pooler_topk.py`) runs once per MoE layer in every Muse Spark decode / verify step. Each call reads about 42 MB of weights from HBM (FP8 pooler `[4096, 8192]` plus the BF16 high / low router rows `[512, 8192]`), and it reached about 2 TB/s at 40 rows. At TP8 / concurrency 28 that is about 60 calls x ~21 us per verify step. ## Modifications The kernel change is confined to `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/router_pooler_topk.py`: `_joint_fp8_partial`, its `FP8_JOINT` launch table, and the launch in `joint_router_pooler_topk_fp8`. The products (FP8 x FP8 and BF16 x BF16), the FP32 accumulation and the SK = 4 split are unchanged. - **Wider pooler tiles.** 128 output columns per program, so the activation is re-staged fewer times. Above 128 rows the M tile is 256 rows, so no weight is streamed twice per call. - **Separate router tile.** The BF16 router rows get their own narrower tile (`BN_R`), plus an `R_MS` row split above 128 rows, so router programs no longer finish last. - **XCD-aware program-id remap.** Each of the 8 XCDs gets one or two K slices instead of all four, which cuts per-XCD L2 traffic for the activation. The remap is a bijection onto `(pn, pk)`, so the partials are bitwise identical to the current kernel. - **Rules over M.** Row buckets plus `_xcd_map(m)` thresholds; nothing is keyed to specific row counts. title: [Fix] encoder: Abort waiting requests before draining embeddings in the same tick
summary: ## Motivation In `Scheduler.ingest_requests()`, `self.request_receiver.recv_requests()` runs `self.mm_receiver.process_waiting_requests(recv_reqs)` before `self.process_input_requests(recv_reqs)` dispatches `AbortReq` to `Scheduler.abort_request()`. Inside `MMReceiverBase._process_waiting_requests()` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encoder/receiver.py`): 1. The initial loop over `recv_reqs` appends `AbortReq` directly to `new_recv_reqs` without calling `self.abort_waiting_requests(recv_req)` (and places any newly arrived multimodal `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` into `self.waiting_list`). 2. Right after that loop, `_drain_scheduler_embeddings()` and `waiting_req._try_recv_mm_data()` run. If the target waiting request finishes receiving its embeddings in the same scheduler tick, it transitions to `WaitingMMRequestStatus.SUCCESS`, leaves `self.waiting_list`, and is appended to `new_recv_reqs` **behind** the `AbortReq`. 3. When `Scheduler.process_input_requests(new_recv_reqs)` then runs, it processes `AbortReq` first -- at which point the request is already gone from `mm_receiver.waiting_list` and not yet in `waiting_queue` or `running_batch` -- so the abort is dropped. The request right behind it is then added to `waiting_queue` as a new request. Impact: the abort is silently ignored. The request runs a full prefill and decode on the language-only server and finishes normally instead of with `FINISH_ABORT`: a disconnected client's request keeps using GPU time and KV until it completes, and an explicit or timeout abort does not take effect. It triggers when the `AbortReq` land

summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #52035. Speculative verify scores several draft positions of a request in one forward, but every verify row of a request got the same penalty: the request's history as of the start of the block. summary: ## Motivation `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_MHC_PREFILL` already selects single-pass Mega-mHC prefill on SM100 (DeepGEMM). title: [Perf] mem_cache: Cut unified-memory relocation cost once the pool fills
summary: ## Motivation With `--enable-unified-memory`, the sliding-window band sits between the Mamba-state band and the full-attention band. Once the pool fills, nearly every allocation relocates it, and on `main` each relocation is expensive: - Slack between bands is split by expected growth in pages. A Mamba state is 32 MB and a window token is 12 KB, so the gap beside the states gets too little room and the window is pushed again and again while the pool fills. - Each relocation walks every page of the window's span on the host: about 290 ms for a 1.2 million-page window at page size 1. At page size 1 this costs 38% of throughput in the run below. Chains whose bands share one page size get the same plans as before. - `FloatBand.relocate_into` walks only the pages that leave the block and the free pages, not the whole span. title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deep_select: Opt-in multi-wave cluster top-k for long-tailed rows
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation DeepSelect's bf16 top-k sends a batch to a cluster kernel only when the batch fits in one wave of some cluster tier. A larger batch goes to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. That kernel runs every row at once, so its time is set by the longest row in the batch. The DeepSeek-V4.1 decode indexer hits this case. With DSpark (6 verify rows per request) and 40 requests per rank, each index layer runs a top-512 over 240 rows. On a Vera Rubin GPU (SM107, 212 SMs) the widest one-wave tier is the 2-CTA cluster with 106 rows, so all 240 rows go to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. Agentic decode batches mix very different context lengths: in the samples below, the longest row is 2.6-6.3x the mean row. The cluster kernel already launches one cluster per row, and the hardware starts the next row's cluster as an earlier one retires. Run over several waves, its time follows the total row length instead of the longest row. ## Modifications - New opt-in env `SGLANG_DEEP_SELECT_MULTIWAVE=1`. It sends bf16 top-k batches with more rows than every one-wave tier, and at most `_MULTIWAVE_MAX_ROWS` = 512 rows, to the cluster tier with the most rows per wave (the 2-CTA tier on SM107), which then runs over several waves. Batches that fit a one-wave tier, short rows (`vocab_size <= 16384`) and every other dtype or signature dispatch exactly as before. - Off by default: on uniform row lengths the one-CTA-per-row kernel wins (numbers below), so whether it pays depends on the workload's context mix. - `_precompile` reads the env once per signature and passes that tier's module to `_C

title: [Perf] deterministic: Launch a fixed number of Triton decode blocks for large split budgets
summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode, Triton decode attention gets much slower than in normal mode as the batch grows: on MI350X, gpt-oss-20b reaches 0.33x of normal-mode throughput at 64 concurrent requests and 0.21x at 256. The cause is the split budget. For batch invariance, deterministic mode fixes the decode split size at 256 tokens and sizes the budget for the longest possible request (512 splits for gpt-oss's 131k context). The kernels launch one block per split of that budget, so for a 1k-2k-token request about 99% of the blocks do no work, and the waste grows with the batch. This PR lets the grouped decode kernel run fewer blocks than splits, each block looping over the request's own splits: enough blocks to cover the GPU, and at least 32 per request and head tile. In deterministic mode the merge also stops at the request's split count instead of walking the empty tail. Every split is computed and merged in the same order as before. **Impact** - Deterministic gpt-oss-20b: 0.33x / 0.21x -> 0.63x / 0.50x of normal mode at 64 / 256 requests; gpt-oss-120b +63% / 2.1x. Any model on Triton decode attention in deterministic mode benefits, more with a longer context limit. - Normal mode is bitwise unchanged, including MLA with its core-count-sized split budget: checked against main on MI350X for MLA and GQA shapes at batch 1-64, at 0.98-1.05x main's kernel time. In deterministic mode GQA results are bitwise the same as today; on MLA shapes the merge's early stop can move them by a few ULP, and they stay batch-invariant. ## Modifications - `decode_attention.py`, `_fwd_groupe

title: [Perf] DSv4.1 on Hopper: stabilize mixed-prefill TTFT and small-batch decode latency

A typical request might reuse a long document prefix, extend it with a differently shaped input, and then decode in a small batch. Both the first token and subsequent tokens matter. A large persistent prefix cache is not itself a solution if a new prefill shape pays another JIT compilation or a low-batch decode step pays avoidable communication/epilogue launches. The goal of this issue is **stable time-to-first-token across mixed prefill shapes and lower cache-hot small-batch decode latency on Hopper, without regressing supported context, correctness, cache behavior or loaded throughput**. The sum of synchronized first-use layout calls decreased from 6.02 to 2.16 s and from 6.33 to 2.58 s in reverse order; warm isolated query geometric-mean ratios were 1.006x and 0.987x. title: [Fix] scheduler: sync grammar before launching mixed step under overlap spec decoding
summary: ## Summary Fixes a grammar-desync gap for MIXED steps under overlap speculative decoding (EAGLE/EAGLE3/STANDALONE/DFLASH-family algorithms). This PR **supersedes #42401** — same root cause and test design (thanks @giuliotosato for the original analysis), retargeted at the decision point introduced by #47716 (`is_disable_overlap_for_batch` no longer exists). ## Root cause - A `ForwardMode.MIXED` batch satisfies `is_extend()`, so spec workers run it as a plain prefill (`_forward_prefill_batch`) whose grammar mask is built from `req.grammar` — **no `verify()` barrier**. - For decode steps this is irrelevant: the barrier inside `verify()` advances the grammar FSM over the still-queued previous result. - If the previous batch's result is still in `result_queue` when the mixed batch launches, the mixed batch's decode rows mask under a grammar FSM **one token behind**, and `accept_token` rejects the token they sample → `finish_reason: abort` (HTTP 500 to the client). - #47716 moved the "process last result early" decision *before* planning the next batch and replaced the old `need_grammar_sync` logic with `last_batch.grammar_needs_sync()`, which only covers **non**-overlap algorithms — leaving exactly this gap. ## The fix `should_process_last_batch_early` (scheduler.py, +22 lines): when the pending result came from a grammar-carrying spec batch of a grammar-overlap-capable algorithm and prefill work is pending (waiting queue or chunked request — a pre-plan proxy for the next step mixing decodes with a prefill), process the result before launching. summary: A full Engine refit of a server with an EAGLE3 draft kills the server, and `begin_weight_update(selector="target")` cannot prevent it: tensor, distributed and plugin loads read their own request `selector`, which defaults to `"all"` and which the `Engine` update calls never set, so target tensors keep reaching the draft. title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Run the BigVGAN vocoder's convolutions in MIOpen's summation orders from Triton
summary: ## Motivation On ROCm, MIOpen serves the FP32 convolutions of the BigVGAN vocoder (the MiniMax-H3 audio decode) with slow solvers: - The dilated conv1d calls of the residual blocks (dilation 3 and 5, 8-512 channels, 3-11 taps) run on the naive solver, which accumulates in FP64 at 4-5 ms a call: about 0.28 s of a 5 s request's audio decode, on every GPU count. - The alias-free up/down-sampling filters are depthwise conv_transpose1d / conv1d calls (12 taps, stride 2, 8-512 channels). Per shape MIOpen picks the naive solver (FP64 sum, up to 0.7 ms a call), im2col + an FP32 GEMM (0.9 ms), or a K=1 GEMM + col2im (0.35-0.48 ms). Each of these solvers has a fixed summation order, so a kernel that sums in the same order returns the same bytes. ## Modifications - New `kernels/ops/diffusion/conv/`: - `conv1d_fp64acc`: sums `x * w` in FP64, input channel outer and tap inner, skipping padded taps, and rounds once. title: [Fix] diffusion: Fail the request whose Ulysses peer wait expired, and bound the head-group pipeline's waits
summary: ## Motivation Two gaps in how the multi-rank copy-engine transport (`ipc_a2a_multi`) handles a rank that stops answering: 1. **The plain exchange serves the request that timed out.** Its `spin_wait` gives up after `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_IPC_A2A_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) and the exchange returns incomplete data, but the timeout word is only read at the start of the next request. The request that computed on incomplete data finishes and its output is returned; the request after it fails instead. 2. **The head-group pipeline has no timeout at all.** `pipelined_attention` waits for its peers with `cuStreamWaitValue32`. A stuck peer holds every rank for good, and nothing names the rank or the path. ## Modifications Commit 1, the request that timed out fails and the server says so: - After every denoising stage the executor runs `IpcA2AMultiState.check_timeout` (one `all_gather` of an int32 per rank), before the decode stage encodes anything. The check is a group collective, so both executors run it where every rank arrives and not inside the stage: a denoising stage can run on the main rank alone (LTX-2's second stage under CFG parallel) while the transport is up over every rank, and a check that only the main rank reached would wait for the others for good. - The check at the start of the next request moves to the end of the forward, on every rank. It reports an expiry that no denoising stage did (a stage outside the denoiser role, such as Cosmos 3's denoising stage), so that request fails too instead of the one after it. - The error is `IpcPeerTimeoutError`. title: [Perf] diffusion/qwen-image: Batch the two CFG branches into one forward when the DiT streams
summary: ## Motivation When the Qwen-Image DiT (38 GiB in BF16) does not fit on the GPU and layerwise offload streams it from host memory, each denoising step runs the DiT twice, once per CFG branch, and so copies every streamed layer twice. The copies dominate: in a torch profile of 10 serial steps with 24 GiB free, host-to-device copies were busy 99.4 % of each pass, and 99.7 % of the kernel time ran under a copy. Running both branches as one batch-2 forward copies the weights once per step and roughly halves request time. #20434 batched the CFG branches for Qwen-Image and was closed. title: num_matched_prefix_tokens stays 0 for cache-agnostic policies (fcfs, lof, random, routing-key)
summary: # Issue: `num_matched_prefix_tokens` stays 0 for cache-agnostic policies - load snapshots and cache-hit reporting read zero reuse ## Summary With `--schedule-policy fcfs` (and the other cache-agnostic policies: `lof`, `random`, `routing-key`), `Req.num_matched_prefix_tokens` stays at 0 for the request's whole lifetime, even though the request does reuse cached prefixes. Every consumer of the field then reads zero reuse. ## Root cause 2 facts combine: 1. `SchedulePolicy.calc_priority` only populates `num_matched_prefix_tokens` at sort time for cache-agnostic policies when `tree_cache.supports_fast_match_prefix()` is true - which is false for the current radix implementations - so the field is never set there (`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_policy.py`). 2. `Req.init_next_round_input` runs the real admission-time re-match (`tree_cache.match_prefix(...)`) and unpacks `prefix_indices` / `host_hit_length`, but never records the match length into `num_matched_prefix_tokens` - the field keeps its init value 0 (and its retraction reset value 0). So the scheduler reuses cached prefixes correctly at admission (behavior is fine), but the bookkeeping field stays 0. ## Impact - `SchedulerLoadInquirer.get_num_waiting_uncached_tokens` computes `req.seqlen - req.num_matched_prefix_tokens` whenever `waiting_queue_prefix_matched()` is true => The uncached waiting-token estimate counts full input lengths, i.e. load snapshots overestimate pending prefill work for cache-agnostic policies. - Any observability or reporting that reads per-request matched tokens for these policies reads 0. ##

title: [Perf] scheduler: Look up the external store once per request when ranking the waiting queue
summary: ## Motivation With the unified-cache external linker, `match_prefix` on a request also looks up the external KV store for its uncached pages: a synchronous remote lookup plus an all-reduce across the attention group. Cache-aware ranking (`shortest-prefill-first` in particular, which has no queue-length cutoff) re-matches the whole waiting queue every scheduling pass, so a queue of a few hundred long-context requests turns each pass into hundreds of remote lookups and collectives, and prefill throughput collapses while the GPUs sit idle. Ranking still has to see those external hits: shortest-prefill-first orders by uncached work, and the waiting-queue load metrics report uncached tokens. ## Modifications - Ranking looks up the external store once per request and keeps the restorable prefix end (`Req.external_hit_end`). Later passes match only the local tree and count `max(local hit, external_hit_end)` as cached, so ranking and the uncached-token metrics keep counting external hits. A retraction clears the cached end. - Admission still re-matches each request it takes with a fresh lookup, so what is loaded from the store is decided exactly as before. - `probes_external_store()` says whether a tree's match looks up an external store (a sync-mode linker outside PD decode). Only those trees cache the hit; a HiCache host hit stays a fresh local match. The match path uses the same check. Every attention-TP rank ranks the same queue in the same order, so the requests that still need a lookup, and with them the all-reduce count, are identical across ranks. Without an external store

title: [Feat] platforms: Let OOT platforms provide breakable graph backends (3/3)
summary: ## Motivation SGLang lets users choose a graph backend independently for decode and prefill. Both phases can select `breakable`, where one model forward is captured as multiple device-graph segments separated by operations that run eagerly. Today, selecting `breakable` always constructs SGLang's built-in `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`. An out-of-tree platform can provide a full decode graph backend, but it has no equivalent way to provide its own breakable graph implementation. The platform must patch SGLang or inherit CUDA-specific code, even when it already supports segmented graph capture on its device. This is the final PR in a three-part series: 1. [PR 1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49402) introduced the device-neutral `BaseGraphBackend` and `BaseBreakableGraphBackend` contracts. 2. [PR 2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49457) decouples `eager_on_graph` from private CUDA/XPU capture state through a device-neutral recorder contract. 3. This PR adds the platform hook and resolver routing that allow an OOT platform to supply a breakable backend for decode, prefill, or both. Together, the three changes separate responsibilities cleanly: core SGLang owns graph policy and runner behavior, while the platform owns device-specific graph capture and replay. ## Behavior changes Built-in platform behavior does not change. The new hook returns `None` by default, which keeps the existing `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` path. An OOT platform may now return a `BaseBreakableGraphBackend` subclass for either phase. title: [Perf] diffusion: Memoize MiniMax-H3 block AdaLN projections per timestep set
summary: ## Motivation Every MiniMax-H3 block computes its AdaLN parameters with a 2688 x 96768 BF16 projection: 50 weight-bandwidth-bound GEMVs per DiT step, 520 MB read each. The projection's only input is the step's time embedding, and requests that share a schedule run the same timesteps (a few-step release such as Pika-H3-Flex has a single schedule), so after the first request of a schedule each later one recomputes values the process already produced. The AdaLN cache modes (`--minimax-h3-adaln-online`, `--minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path`) remove this work by pruning `adaln_proj`, but they need unquantized native weights and reject adapters that carry AdaLN LoRA deltas. A server outside those constraints pays the GEMVs on every step. ## Modifications - `MiniMaxH3DiTModel._adaln_memo_params`: with resident projections and no tensor parallelism, a step's block AdaLN parameters come from a memo keyed by the bit patterns of the step's unique timesteps (plus the input's shape, dtype and device). At most 32 entries per transformer, least recently used out first. A miss runs the same `project_local` as before and keeps its outputs. - The memo is rebuilt when an `adaln_proj` weight is rebound or the conditioning weights epoch advances. Weight updates and LoRA merges write weights in place, and an unmerged LoRA changes the projection without touching the weight; all of them already advance that epoch. - Unchanged paths, never memoized: both AdaLN cache modes, TP > 1 (the batched all-gather), `torch.compile`, CUDA graph capture, Cache-DiT, layerwise offload, and non-CUDA devices. title: [Perf] diffusion: Quantize and LANCZOS-resize MiniMax-H3 image output on the GPU
summary: ## Motivation When a MiniMax-H3-Image request is smaller than `min_generation_area`, the DiT generates on a larger canvas (e.g. 2720x1536 for a 1344x768 request) and `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` resizes the decoded image back with Pillow LANCZOS. title: [Feat] scheduler: Add opt-in reasoning-effort KV budgets
summary: ## Motivation Running requests currently share the scheduler's new-token ratio regardless of reasoning effort. This adds an opt-in way to use effort tiers when budgeting their future decode growth during prefill admission. Related to #42915. This PR implements a separate **KV admission-budget** capability; it does not implement the RFC's DP routing or retraction-victim policies and should not close that RFC. ## Modifications Add `--reasoning-effort-kv-budget {off,scaled,adaptive}`, defaulting to `off`: - **off:** retain existing admission behavior. - **scaled:** multiply the initial reservation by a tier-specific factor and divide the accumulated global ratio decay by that factor. Higher tiers reserve more and decay more slowly; lower tiers reserve less and decay faster. Simply multiplying the current ratio would not provide the intended decay behavior. - **adaptive:** use the mean of recent completed output lengths for the request's tier. The difference between that mean (capped by the request limit) and generated length scales the accumulated decay. Normalization uses the existing clipped admission demand, so large `max_new_tokens` values do not collapse all tiers onto the same fastest-decay setting. Requests that outlive the mean recover a ratio of 1 rather than losing their reservation. Chat Completions forwards recognized effort metadata after template/default normalization. summary: ## Motivation in speculative decoding, multiple draft tokens get committed to output_ids before finish checks run. when a request gets aborted mid-run via to_finish, update_finish_state sets finished_reason and returns early without setting finished_len or checking length boundaries. because finished_len stayed none, output_ids_through_stop returned the raw output_ids including the overshot speculative tokens, so completion_tokens exceeded max_new_tokens on aborted requests (issue #44839). ## Modifications clamps finished_len to max_new_tokens inside the to_finish handler when output_ids meets or exceeds the cap, and ensures output_ids_through_stop and the output streamer never emit past max_new_tokens. added unit tests covering speculative aborts both over and under the token cap in test_finish_length_speculative.py. ## Checklist - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #39210363171](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39210363171)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #39210363104](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39210363104)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:x: [Run #39210363105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39210363105)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] attention/fa4: Skip the hd256 KV copy on SM90 for strided paged caches
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #52079. `flash_attn_varlen_func` makes Q/K/V contiguous on every head-dim-256 call (#33436). The workaround exists for the dedicated hd256 kernel that `interface.py` selects on other architectures (`use_dedicated_hd256_kernel`), which builds its K/V layout from the shapes alone. On SM90 the hd256 path is `FlashAttentionForwardSm90`, which reads the real strides of the tensors it is given. For a dense paged cache `.contiguous()` is a no-op. With `--enable-unified-memory`, one token slot of the pool holds the K/V of several layers, so a layer's cache is an `as_strided` view whose token stride is the whole slot. Every FA4 hd256 call on SM90 then copies the layer's entire paged K and V cache, however few tokens the batch reads, and allocates two cache-sized buffers that a CUDA graph capture has to reserve. ## Modifications - `flash_attention_v4.py`: add `_uses_dedicated_hd256_kernel()` (cached, mirrors `use_dedicated_hd256_kernel` in `interface.py`) and keep the hd256 `.contiguous()` workaround only when it is true. The copy is skipped on SM90 only; the existing TODO stays. - `test_flash_attention_4.py` (`TestFlashAttention4SM90`): `test_hd256_strided_paged_kv_read_in_place` builds an fp8 hd256 paged cache as a strided view into a 4-layer pool, and checks that the output equals a dense copy bit for bit and that the call allocates less than a quarter of one K copy. ## Accuracy Tests Kernel level (H200): strided view vs dense copy of the same cache, fp8 KV, page 64, window 1023. | batch | context | bit-identical | max abs diff | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 9216 |

title: [Fix] attention: Honor an explicit --triton-attention-num-kv-splits on ROCm and MLA
summary: _Produced by Hyperloom._ ## Motivation `--triton-attention-num-kv-splits` is not always the cap the Triton decode backend runs with: - On ROCm, `handle_amd_specifics` declares `triton_attention_num_kv_splits=16` on every launch, and a resolution declaration takes precedence over the raw input. `--triton-attention-num-kv-splits 32` (or `8`) on MI300X/MI355X still publishes 16. - On MLA models, `TritonAttnBackend` raises the configured value with `_mla_decode_kv_splits_cap` (`max(configured, min(next_pow2(CUs), next_pow2(ctx / 32)))`), so an explicit 8 on a full MI355X with 32k context becomes 256, and with `SGLANG_TRITON_DECODE_ATTN_STATIC_KV_SPLITS` every sequence runs 256 splits. - A count of 0 is accepted and reaches `get_num_kv_splits_triton`, which divides by the zero cap. ## Modifications - `triton_attention_num_kv_splits` stays `Optional[int] = None` with no fallback, so the published config tells an unset flag from an explicit value. - `handle_amd_specifics` no longer declares 16. The gfx942 MLA pin to 256 still applies to every value, since a larger buffer faults in ROCm graph replay. - New resolution step `validate_triton_attention_num_kv_splits` rejects counts below 1 (whitelisted in `resolution_hooks.py` like the neighboring validators). - Help text and the `server_arguments.mdx` row

title: [Fix] gemma4: Make DFlash drafts work on a Gemma-4 target
summary: ## Motivation Related: #52080, which was measured with this change applied. Two independent problems keep a DFlash draft (e.g. `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.dflash2`) from running correctly on a Gemma-4 target. 1. **Crash in `candidate_topk` with a tied, replicated `lm_head`.** Gemma-4 ties `lm_head` to `model.embed_tokens`, a plain `nn.Embedding` (`Gemma3TextScaledWordEmbedding`) that holds the whole vocabulary on every TP rank. `candidate_topk` assumes a `VocabParallelEmbedding` head (`org_vocab_size` at TP1, `shard_indices` + all-gather at TP>1). A DFlash2 selector draft therefore crashes while capturing the draft decode graph: `'Gemma3TextScaledWordEmbedding' object has no attribute 'shard_indices'`. 2. **Draft inputs scaled by `sqrt(hidden_size)`.** The DFlash draft has no embedding of its own; the worker embeds the block (bonus + mask tokens) with the target's `get_input_embeddings()`. On Gemma-4 that module multiplies by `embed_scale = sqrt(hidden_size)` in `forward` (sqrt(5376) ≈ 73.3 on the 31B). The draft is trained on the raw table (SpecForge `TargetEmbeddingsAndHead` is a plain `nn.Embedding`; vLLM feeds the raw `VocabParallelEmbedding` and applies the normalizer only in `Gemma4Model.embed_input_ids`), so every draft layer sees inputs about 73x too large and acceptance length drops sharply. ## Modifications - `models/dflash.py`: when the head is an `nn.Embedding` (full vocabulary on each rank), `candidate_topk` takes the top-k over the full local logits and skips the all-gather. `VocabParallelEmbedding` heads are unchanged. - `models/gemma4_causal.py`, `mo

title: [Fix] parser: Route reasoning prefixes consistently across stream chunks
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #35083. Thanks to @tancheng33 for the detailed report and the earlier #35085 attempt, which was closed without merging after inactivity. title: [Fix] hicache: Agree on write-through backups across pipeline stages
summary: ## Why this fails In ordinary pipeline-parallel serving, a HiCache write-through backup can reserve host slots on one stage while another stage runs out. The next cache poll relays PP0's number of ready writes. Each follower takes that many entries from its own FIFO. Once an enqueue succeeds on only one stage, the same queue position can refer to different prefixes. [Upstream completion loop](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9b4b6b6d163c31d234e770eac9f484bd469822a3/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py#L4409-L4416) A two-stage regression submits prefixes A, B, and C. A fits everywhere, B fits on only one stage, and C fits everywhere once the temporary reservation is released. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P0 as PP0 participant P1 as PP1 Note over P0,P1: A completed on both stages P0->>P0: B cannot reserve host slots P1->>P1: B reserves slots and queues a copy P0->>P0: C reserves slots and queues a copy P1->>P1: C reserves slots and queues a copy P0->>P1: One write is ready P0->>P0: Settle C P1->>P1: Settle B at the head of its FIFO ``` Reversing which stage misses B exposes the second symptom. PP0 announces B and PP1 pops an empty queue. Both outcomes were reproduced against upstream `b959096ecf` with storage disabled. [Upstream reproduction](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28429#issuecomment-7063351912) ## What changes The ordinary PP scheduler collects write-through intents and pins their device paths until the cache poll. It rebuilds the parent-first spans after any radix split. The stages compare logical prefix identities, in

title: [Fix] kernels/lora: Use int64 token row offsets in the csgmv shrink and expand kernels
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51099. The chunked-SGMV (csgmv) LoRA kernels load each token's physical row from the int32 `permutation` and multiply it by the row stride: `s_offset_physical * x_stride_0` / `* output_stride_0` in the shrink kernel (plain and split-K) and `* output_stride_0` in the expand kernel. When `row * stride >= 2^31` the int32 product wraps, so the kernels read (shrink) and read/write (expand) before the tensors. The Triton LoRA backend already widens the same index to int64 in `kernel_utils.py`. One forward of about `2^31 / K` tokens reaches this, e.g. a long unchunked prefill. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/lora/dense/chunked_sgmv_shrink.py` and `chunked_sgmv_expand.py`: widen `s_offset_physical` to int64 right after the `tl.load` (three kernels: shrink, split-K shrink, expand). - `test/registered/kernels/ops/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph.py`: three CUDA regression tests, skipped below about 10 GB of free GPU memory. The shrink test (with and without `split_k=2`) uses the shape from the issue, `x` of 65538 x 32768 fp16 with the last physical row at offset 2,147,516,416, and expects the last row to be 16 values of 32.0. The expand test writes into a 65538 x 32768 fp16 base output and expects the last row to be all 1.0. They are added to the existing csgmv test file in the same subsystem. ## Accuracy Tests No model output changes for inputs below 2^31 elements: the offset arithmetic is unchanged there. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA L4, 24 GB (compute capability 8.9, sm89), driver 595.112.07 (CUDA 13.2) | | Host | RunPod container, Ubuntu 24.

title: [Feat] kimi-k3: Shared-expert TP across attention-DP ranks
summary: ## Motivation Under attention DP with attention TP 1 (e.g. Kimi-K3.1 ADP8), `--shared-experts-tp-size` must divide attention TP x CP, so the shared experts are replicated: 22.64 GiB per rank on K3.1. summary: ## Motivation Rust-server mode (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) refuses `--tokenizer-backend fastokens` at startup. title: [Fix] embedding: Keep the trailing [SEP] on auto-truncation and accumulate MEAN pooling in fp32
summary: Split out of the XPU model-enabling PR #35304 so these shared changes are reviewed on their own. title: [Fix] pd: Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots
summary: ## Motivation On the PD **decode** side, `HybridMambaDecodeReqToTokenPool` sizes the hybrid Mamba / linear-attention **speculative** scratch (`intermediate_ssm`, `intermediate_conv_window`, and the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv / N-gram scratch) by `size + pre_alloc_size`, where `pre_alloc_size = disaggregation_decode_extra_slots` reserves extra `req_to_token` slots for in-transfer (being-received-from-prefill) requests. In-transfer requests are not in the running batch and never enter `target_verify`, so they never need a scratch row. What the scratch does need is a row for every row of a verify batch **after padding**: eager warmup and MLP sync pad the batch to the attention TP (and CP) width, and CUDA graphs to their batch-size alignment. GDN and KDA verify read the scratch through `build_verify_intermediate_state_indices`, which maps every padded row onto the padding row. Other writers index it by batch position: the Qwen4-Exp PLE short-conv tape and N-gram commit, LFM2's short-conv tape (`arange(bs)`), and the lightning `seg_la` verify (`arange(cache_indices.shape[0])`). They fit today only because the in-transfer rows happen to cover the padding. With `--disaggregation-decode-extra-slots 0`, or more than 32 requests per worker (where the default is 0), a padded verify batch overruns the PLE scratch on main too. The in-transfer rows are not budgeted either. By default a decode server runs with the radix cache disabled, and `_handle_max_mamba_cache` then reserves verify scratch for `max_running_requests // attn_dp_size + 1` rows, while the pool allocates `size + pre_alloc_si

title: SGLang: /get_weights_by_name materializes the full weight tensor before truncation, enabling memory exhaustion from a single request
summary: ## Summary The `/get_weights_by_name` endpoint calls `.tolist()` on the full weight tensor before slicing to `truncate_size`. Even with the default `truncate_size=100`, the entire matrix is materialized as a Python list first. On a Llama-70B-scale model, a single weight matrix (`down_proj.weight`, shape `[4096, 11008]`, about 45M floats) produces about 1 GB of Python float objects. The endpoint is `ADMIN_OPTIONAL` and unauthenticated in the default deployment. ## Affected versions Tested against SGLang v0.5.23 (`llama.py:884`). The `.tolist()[:truncate_size]` expression is unchanged on the current main branch (2026-11-21). ## Preconditions - The attacker can reach the SGLang HTTP server port. In the default deployment no `api_key` or `admin_api_key` is configured, and the endpoint is `ADMIN_OPTIONAL` (open). - The served model implements `get_weights_by_name` (llama, granite, opt, exaone4, embedding_gemma2, and others). - No special server flags required. ## Root cause In `llama.py:884` (and equivalent implementations in other model files): ```python # llama.py:884 (v0.5.23) weights[name] = weight.cpu().to(torch.float32).numpy().tolist()[:truncate_size] ``` Python evaluates `.tolist()` before `[:truncate_size]`. The full tensor is converted to a Python list of floats first, then truncated. The intermediate list is proportional to the full tensor size, not to `truncate_size`. ## PoC Executed by an independent curl client against a real SGLang v0.5.23 HTTP server (default flags, CPU, no api_key, test model with `hidden_size=512, intermediate_size=14336, 1 layer`): 1. Send `PO

title: [Perf] paged-experts: pre-copy the next layer's predicted experts beside compute
summary: # [Perf] paged-experts: pre-copy the next layer's predicted experts beside compute ## Motivation In a captured Paged Experts decode step, a MoE layer copies its missing experts into GPU slots only after the layer has routed, so every page-in sits on the critical path. On Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-NVFP4 on an RTX 5070 Ti (about 100 of 512 experts per layer resident), a single-request step pages in about 62 experts, 2.4 ms of a 10.2 ms step. Related: #46520 (@wyc55069407): pre-copying the next layer's predicted experts is the look-ahead idea discussed there, here on the RAM tier. ## Modifications - **Pre-copy** (`precopy.py`, new): after a MoE layer's gather, a side stream applies the next MoE layer's router to this layer's input (one GEMV). The plan kernel then takes the next layer's top-k by softmax probability. Up to 3 of those experts that are in none of the next layer's slots get its least recently used slots, never one holding a predicted expert. title: [Fix] paged-experts: Cap auto K at the disk tier plan kernel limit
summary: ## Motivation Small invariant follow-up to #47476 and #49195: When an explicit `--paged-experts-num-resident` is passed, `disk_tier.host_rows()` enforces both `num_slots <= rows` and `num_slots <= _MAX_TIER_SLOTS` (`1024`, the single-block thread bound in `paged_experts_tiered_plan`). title: [Feat] glm5_next: Support LayerNorm sequence parallelism
summary: ## Motivation With TP attention every rank runs GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC (`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`, `mhc_post`, the `hc_prenorm` GEMM) on all token rows, since the residual stream is replicated. On the 8x H200 TP8 proxy below that is 81 ms of rank 0's 651 ms of GPU time for a 128K cold prefill, the same work on all 8 ranks. `--enable-layernorm-sp` already keeps the residual on 1/tp of the rows for Qwen3, Qwen4Exp and Muse. mHC only mixes the `hc_mult` streams of one token, and `residual/mhc.py` declares the same update facts as the gated residual Qwen4Exp runs under SP, so the boundary needs no change. What's missing is the GLM decoder layer running attention and the FFN on gathered rows. I also tried `--enable-attn-tp-input-scattered`, since GLM's forward goes through `maybe_input_scattered`. With the default breakable prefill graphs it doesn't change the mHC work: on a 2x H200 TP2 proxy (main 424fa3c8b7), 32K cold prefill, mHC was 20.14 ms by default and 20.09 ms with it, GPU busy 296.4 / 296.8 ms. This is for the TP-attention cells. With DP attention each rank already does mHC only for its own requests; I didn't compare against DP attention. ## Modifications - `Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward`: under SP, attention (KDA and MLA/DSA) and the FFN run through `run_replicated_token_rows` on the gathered rows and hand back this rank's rows. KDA, the DSA indexer and the MoE see exactly the sequence rows (`total_rows=positions.shape[-1]`). - MLA reads its QKV latent from the attention inputs the boundary cached on this rank's rows, so the SP closure points them at the gathered rows.

title: [Perf] diffusion: Fuse ordered mean-square reductions in Nomas VAE
summary: # Fuse the ordered mean-square reduction in Nomas VAE Nomas VAE currently materializes FP32 squares before reducing them. This change reuses the existing ordered mean-square operator for contiguous width 4096 and head-64 views, including either half of packed head-128 Q/K tensors. It removes 722 intermediate square launches per 49-frame generation while preserving ATen's reduction order and the existing normalization rounding. Unsupported layouts keep the original implementation through the existing per-signature `BitExactFusionGate`. Main baseline: `0745bfe49b855ae48e0c1ef3305362b8e0c78a03`. Final PR head: `37999f7ab31809bd8a9f3cabee3fa50c54f179d6`. vLLM-Omni baseline: `aa2968e858a718989332a61ad40758024cb4a3a5`. Pre-cleanup candidate: `fbfb89d4c73ae6adc1d2d769af4a34a4cd881541`. ## End-to-end measurements One **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition**, 97887 MiB, SM120, driver 595.84; physical GPU0 UUID `GPU-1565b45e-a702-2015-9776-61f68c36fd59`. The task's maximum budget is two GPUs, connected through SYS without NVLink; all performance measurements below use the same single GPU. The supplemental Ulysses2 correctness checks use both physical GPUs. These are current-machine results. Native SGLang backend, resident BF16 weights, lossless quality, 1280×704, 49 frames at 24 FPS, 8 denoising steps, CFG1, flow shift5, CPU seed42, batch1/concurrency1. Short and long structured prompts are fixed in [the input manifest](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/9473cba216404611937d488804a56682f83882e7/inputs/nomas-native-workloads01.json). title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] mem_cache: Keep the fp8 KV cache for DFLASH fa4 drafts on SM90
summary: ## Motivation Related: #52080 (FA4 hd256 copy on SM90 for the same unified-memory setup). `configure_kv_cache_dtype` overrides the KV cache dtype of a DFLASH draft worker on the `fa4` draft backend: - Whenever the requested KV dtype differs from the model dtype, the draft's KV cache is set to the compute dtype (bf16). - The override comes from #29218. At that time FA4 required `K.dtype == Q.dtype`, so a draft could not read an fp8 cache. #46965 changed that: FA4 on SM90 can now read an fp8 e4m3 paged KV cache. - Q stays unquantized (fp16/bf16), and K/V are cast in-kernel (`fp8_kv_dequant` in `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`). - `FlashAttentionBackend` enables this through `fa4_casts_fp8_kv`, for head_dim 256/512 on MHA layers. - #46965 did not update the DFLASH override. With unified memory, the draft region fused into the target's window sub-pool sizes from this dtype. Example: Gemma-4-31B with a 5-layer DFLASH draft (8 KV heads, head_dim 256, TP2): - fp8, as on fa3 and triton: 20,480 B/token. - bf16, as forced on fa4: 40,960 B/token. Two places answered "can FA4 read this fp8 cache?" independently, and only one was updated. title: [Perf] [AMD] aiter: Run EAGLE target verify on unified_attention by default on gfx942
summary: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation On AMD with the default `aiter` attention backend, EAGLE/MTP `target_verify` for non-MLA models runs on the legacy Triton `extend_attention_fwd`. That kernel has no split-KV: each request's long paged KV is walked by one program, so at agentic context lengths it runs far below HBM bandwidth. The faster `unified_attention` verify path from #23146 already exists, but it is only taken when `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`. That variable also moves prefill and decode to Triton `unified_attention`. With one-token KV pages (the default) that makes 16k-token prefill chunks over long contexts tens of times slower on MI300X. With `--page-size 16` the variable is usable, and the InferenceX MI325X Qwen3.5 recipe sets it, but prefill and decode then leave the aiter kernels, which costs TTFT and throughput (397B table below). This PR is the target-verify half of decoupling the EAGLE paths from that variable. #40872 (approved) is the draft_extend half; the two are independent and merge cleanly together. The #40872 thread already points at this gap: with #40872 alone, NEXTN decode on Qwen3.5 drops below no-spec decode at ~11k context, and the cause is target verify still on `extend_attention_fwd` (554 us per call at 11k vs 14 us on `unified_attention`). title: [Perf] [H20] fp8-gemm: Take the swapAB kernel for small-M block FP8 GEMM on H20
summary: ## Motivation On SM90, `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` resolves to plain DeepGEMM (`_dispatch_auto_backend` → `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`). DeepGEMM's default kernel is shaped for large M, but in decode the M dimension *is* the batch size: every decode step runs 60+ block-FP8 GEMMs with `1 <= M <= 32`, and that kernel leaves most of its tile empty at those sizes. Whether that empty tile **costs** anything depends on how much compute the part has per byte of weights it streams, and on H20 it costs a lot. H20 is Hopper silicon cut down to 78 SMs against 132 on H100/H200, so it has roughly a third of their compute while giving up only ~15% of their bandwidth. Narrow-M block-FP8 GEMM on H20 is therefore compute-bound: the redundant MMA work, not the ~27 GB weight stream, is what sets the inter-token time. That is the part this PR targets, and the measurement below shows the effect is absent on an H200 — so the change is scoped to H20 rather than to SM90 as a whole. `flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` is one entry point over **two** DeepGEMM kernels — `fp8_gemm_kernel_swapAB` for `M < 32` and `fp8_gemm_kernel` above it. #32843 already confined `flashinfer_deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` to exactly the `1 <= M < 32` band and delegates every other M (including `M == 0` on idle ranks) back to DeepGEMM, so that callable is a strict superset of what `auto` selects today. It is reachable only by naming `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` explicitly, which leaves the single-request decode of a mainstream FP8 model at roughly 60% of what it reaches

title: [Fix] diffusion: Align Krea-2 request sizes to the 16-pixel patch grid
summary: ## Motivation On a default `sglang serve --model-path krea/Krea-2-Turbo` server, `/v1/images/generations` with `"size": "1920x1080"` or `"1000x1000"` returns HTTP 500 with the body `Internal Server Error`. The server log shows why: ``` einops.EinopsError: Error while processing rearrange-reduction pattern "b c (h ph) (w pw) -> b (h w) (c ph pw)". Shape mismatch, can't divide axis of length 135 in chunks of 2 ``` `Krea2BeforeDenoisingStage` builds the latent at `height // 8` x `width // 8` and splits it into 2x2 patches ([krea2.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8f44124e6010351daffbd5c1d1754b3fa05d2c6c/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/krea2.py#L122-L140)), so a latent side that is odd (1080 / 8 = 135, 1000 / 8 = 125) cannot be split. A size such as 854x480 already works on main, because 854 // 8 = 106 is even and the output is 848x480. ## Modifications - `Krea2SamplingParams` rounds width and height down to multiples of 16 (VAE 8 x patch 2, read from the pipeline config; at least 16) after the request's sampling params are resolved, and for synthetic warmup requests, and logs a warning, as #49714 (Z-Image) and #50114 (Cosmos3) do.
