title: [Feat] diffusion: Integrate FlashInfer Ulysses for Wan and MiniMax H3
summary: ## Motivation Wan and MiniMax H3 currently use SGLang's built-in Ulysses collectives and IPC pipelines. This adds an explicit option to run their ordinary, unquantized BF16/FP16 Ulysses exchange through FlashInfer's public `UlyssesCommunicator`, preserving the selected attention compute backend. ## Modifications The shared adapter handles `scatter_heads` / `gather_heads` and fused QKV exchange (`scatter_qkv_head_chunk` when exposed by FlashInfer; head-interleaved `scatter_heads` otherwise). It supports Wan's 4D and H3's packed 3D tensors, the legacy fixed-layout path, and uniform-length varlen exchanges. H3 keeps its existing strided Q/K/V views. Communicators retain only the current geometry for each process group, device, dtype and operation. QKV input and output have separate slots. Shape changes collectively close the old communicator before constructing a replacement; failed initialization is not cached. There is no lifetime limit on sequence geometries. Teardown closes the remaining contexts before the process groups are destroyed. Registered PCIe outputs are copied out so later exchanges cannot overwrite live operands. This uses no Sage Ulysses or low-precision QKV quantization. The option takes precedence over SGLang's IPC head-group pipelines. CPU/ROCm, autograd, compile/capture, and uneven sequence shards retain their existing transport. Default behavior is unchanged. ### Usage Set these identically on every rank, alongside the usual `--ulysses-degree` option: ```bash export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_ULYSSES=1 export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_ULYSSES_BACKEND=a

title: [Fix] dsa: Make metadata kernel batch size a runtime arg to avoid per-bs Triton recompiles
summary: ## Motivation Three Triton kernels in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py` declare the batch size as `bs: tl.constexpr`. The batch size changes from one step to the next: - `_fused_dsa_decode_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata_kernel` - `_fused_dsa_draft_extend_metadata_kernel` Because `bs` is a `tl.constexpr`, Triton specializes on it and compiles and caches a separate kernel for every batch size it sees. These kernels are not called during CUDA-graph capture. They run when a graph's metadata is filled on replay, with `bs` set to the padded graph batch size. So on main, the first decode step at each new padded batch size JIT-compiles up to three kernels inside the serving loop, and the Triton cache gets one entry per kernel per captured size. These kernels only use `bs` as a runtime bound: `offs_b < bs`, `row < bs`, `tl.range(0, bs)`, and `expanded_size = bs * next_n`. The compile-time tile shapes already come from `BLOCK_BS = next_power_of_2(bs)` and `BLOCK_EXPANDED`, so `bs` itself does not need to be a `constexpr`. For the same reason, `bs` is also added to each kernel's existing `do_not_specialize` list. Otherwise Triton's divisible-by-16 integer specialization would still compile a separate variant for batch sizes like 16, 32 or 48. This is the same bug as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33506, which @amd-mvarjoka fixed in another file. This PR applies that fix to the file below. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/metadata.py`: removed `tl.constexpr` from `bs` in all three kernels. `bs` stays in e

title: [Bug] Unbounded compiled-grammar cache in BaseGrammarBackend leaks host memory with per-request JSON schemas
summary: ### Checklist - [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version (the cache code is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-10-19). - [x] 3. Environment info and a minimal reproducible script are included below. - [x] 4. This is a bug report, not a question. - [x] 5. Written in English. ## Describe the bug `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` (`python/sglang/srt/constrained/base_grammar_backend.py`) is a plain `dict` with no size limit, and the xgrammar backend creates `GrammarCompiler(tokenizer_info=tokenizer_info)` with xgrammar's default unbounded internal cache. Every request whose `response_format.json_schema` (or regex / EBNF) has not been seen before adds one compiled grammar to both caches, and nothing ever evicts it while the server is up. Only `/flush_cache` clears it, and `/flush_cache` is refused unless the scheduler is completely idle. title: [Fix] constrained: bound the compiled-grammar cache by host memory (LRU) to stop RSS growth with per-request schemas
summary: ## Motivation `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` is a plain `dict` that is never evicted. Each compiled grammar (xgrammar / outlines / llguidance) holds per-vocabulary token tables; with a 150k-token vocabulary we measured **+250–380 MB of scheduler RSS per previously-unseen `json_schema`**. Agent frameworks commonly embed per-call values (enums, defaults, descriptions) inside the schema, so every request is a cache miss and the scheduler grows until the host runs out of RAM. In production (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, `--dp-size 4`, 4× H100 NVL, 128 GB RAM + 61 GB swap, SGLang 0.5.10.post1) one client with ~1,250 distinct schemas/day drove each scheduler from 3.5 GB to 35 GB in 11 days; RAM and swap filled and the server stalled for 25 minutes. `/flush_cache` clears the cache but is refused unless the server is fully idle, so it is not a mitigation under load. The cache code is unchanged on `main`. Fixes #45077. ## Changes - `BaseGrammarBackend.cache` becomes an LRU `OrderedDict` bounded by a fixed host-memory budget, `BaseGrammarBackend.DEFAULT_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES` (1 GiB). There is no server flag for it (review feedback: the bound is an implementation detail); backends and tests can still pass `cache_limit_bytes` to the constructor, and `<= 0` there disables the bound. Each entry is charged `BaseGrammarObject.memory_size_bytes()` plus the UTF-8 length of its key: xgrammar reports `CompiledGrammar.memory_size_bytes`, `InvalidGrammarObject` is charged the length of its error message (failed compilations stay cached but cannot accumulate for free), and backends without a size API (outlines,

title: [Fix] weight_update: Rebuild each CUDA-IPC tensor once for the target and draft runners
summary: ## Motivation `update_weights_from_tensor` deserializes the payload once in `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager`, then hands the same `LocalSerializedTensor` entries to every selected runner. Each runner's `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor` calls `_unwrap_tensor`, and `LocalSerializedTensor.get()` deserializes again, so with a speculative draft every producer CUDA-IPC handle is opened once per runner. Similar problem with #17870. We hit it in colocated RL with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and its NEXTN MTP head (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk=1), TP=4: the first weight sync OOMed when the KV cache was resumed, because exported blocks stayed alive on the trainer side. ## Modifications - `model_runner_components/weight_updater.py`: add `unwrap_local_serialized_tensors`, which rebuilds each `LocalSerializedTensor` once on the deployment TP rank and current device, the same values each runner would pick. Payloads without `LocalSerializedTensor` are returned unchanged. - `scheduler_components/weight_updater.py`: call it after `deserialize_own_rank` and before the runner loop, so the target and draft runners share the rebuilt tensors. `flattened_bucket` payloads are dicts the runners unpack themselves and are left as is. `_unwrap_tensor` in the runner is a no-op on tensors that are already materialized, so the runner path is unchanged. - `test_weight_update_tensor_rank.py` (CPU): with a target and a draft runner, each IPC entry is rebuilt exactly once and both runners load it (fails on main with `get` called 2 times). - `test/registered/rl/test_update_weights_from_tensor_spec.py` (GPU, Qwen3.5-4B +

title: [Feat] speculative: Insert bounded prompt tail on extend in NGRAMWorker
summary: ## Motivation Part of the N-gram Speculative Decoding Roadmap (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21052). Currently, `NGRAMWorker._update_ngram_corpus` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`) is only called after `TARGET_VERIFY` steps and carries a `FIXME`: ```python # FIXME: Whether to insert 'extend' into the cache or not, after testing, # there is not much difference, so we will not insert it for now. ``` As a result, when a new request completes its prefill (`EXTEND`) phase and enters its first `DECODE` step, the N-gram Trie has **zero tokens from the current request's prompt** (except the last `max_trie_depth = 18` query suffix). In long-context chat, RAG, summarization, and structured JSON planning workloads, entities, identifiers, and schema keys that appear earlier in the prompt cannot be drafted until they have already been generated once by the model. Inserting an entire 32k–64k prompt into the Trie on `EXTEND` would incur O(L * max_trie_depth) CPU insertion overhead. However, inserting a **bounded tail window** (`NGRAM_EXTEND_PROMPT_WINDOW = 1024` tokens) of each completed request's unpadded prompt + output asynchronously on `EXTEND` takes only `~0.18 ms` (bs=1) to `~0.54 ms` (bs=8) on the scheduler thread, while the background C++ `insertWorker` overlaps with the GPU forward pass and captures the most relevant recent context, instructions, and entity names for immediate drafting on step 1. ## Modifications 1. **`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`**: - On `ForwardMode.EXTEND` completion in `forward_batch_generation`, asynchronously

title: [Fix] scheduler: Count the unprefilled part of a chunked request in total_tokens load
summary: ## Motivation With `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the smallest `num_total_tokens`. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens", but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill. That request holds KV only for the chunks it has already run, and it is in neither the running batch nor the waiting queue. So a rank that has just started a 64K-token prompt reports only about one chunk of load, and new requests keep going to it. We saw this on 2×H20 with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP=2, `--attn-dp-size 2`, FA3, FP8 KV, and `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` (4096 per rank). The traffic was 30 short requests (1024 in / 96 out) plus one 32K and one 64K prompt. When the 32K prompt arrived first, both long prompts went to different ranks as expected. The rank prefilling the 64K prompt then also received 24 of the 30 short requests, which gave a 38,912 / 90,112 input-token split. When the 64K prompt arrived first, the bug was not triggered and the split was 68,608 / 60,416. `SchedulerLoadInquirer._get_num_pending_tokens()` already adds the chunked request's `seqlen - prefix_len`; `num_total_tokens` did not. ## Modifications - `load_inquirer.py`: add the chunked request's remaining tokens (`seqlen - prefix_len`) to `num_total_tokens`, and so also to `num_active_tokens`. The prefix it has already run is counted in `num_used_tokens`, as before. - `test_load_inquirer.py`: two unit tests for `get_loads()`, with and without a chunked request. The new chunked case fails on main (`300 != 340`) and passes with this

title: [Bug] `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_triton`: row offset wraps for inputs with >= 2^31 elements
summary: ### Describe the bug `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul` computes `a_ptrs = A + offs_am * stride_am + ...` and `c_ptrs = C + stride_cm * offs_cm + ...` with int32 `offs_am` and `offs_cm` ([fp8_kernel.py#L99-L102](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py#L99-L102), [fp8_kernel.py#L136-L138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py#L136-L138)). The unrolled variant has the same lines ([fp8_kernel.py#L192-L195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py#L192-L195), [fp8_kernel.py#L248-L250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py#L248-L250)), and so does `_w8a8_block_int8_matmul` ([int8_kernel.py#L63-L66](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/int8_kernel.py#L63-L66), [int8_kernel.py#L94-L96](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/int8_kernel.py#L94-L96)). When `M * K >= 2^31` (or `M * N` for the output), the offsets wrap, and the kernel reads and writes outside A and C. `scaled_mm_kernel` in the same file already uses int64 offsets for this reason ([fp8_kernel.py#L760-L772](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b2cc023f23e14e6482490238968e018573847d0c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_ke

title: [Fix] gemm: Use int64 row offsets in block-scaled FP8/INT8 matmuls
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51098. The block-scaled FP8 and INT8 Triton matmuls compute `offs_am * stride_am` and `stride_cm * offs_cm` with int32 row offsets. Once `M * K` (A) or `M * N` (C) reaches 2^31 elements, the offsets wrap and the kernels read A and write C out of bounds. Example reach from the issue: Qwen3-32B-FP8 at TP1, gate_up projection (N = 51,200), from about 41.9k tokens in one forward. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_kernel.py` and `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/int8_kernel.py`: `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, its Hopper and gfx1250 variants, and `_w8a8_block_int8_matmul` take a `USE_INT64_OFFSETS` constexpr that promotes `offs_am` and `offs_cm` to int64. The launchers set it only when A or C has at least 2^31 elements, so every other shape compiles the original int32 kernel unchanged. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: the same for the group offset in `_per_token_group_quant_int8` (the FP8 quantizers already use int64 here), set only when the input has at least 2^31 elements. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_block_matmul_large_m.py`: regression tests with M = 2^15 + 1 and a 2^16-wide dimension, so the last row starts past 2^31 elements: FP8 with rows of A past 2^31, FP8 with rows of C past 2^31, and INT8 through `apply_w8a8_block_int8_linear` (quantization plus matmul). Inputs use exact encodings. ## Accuracy Tests Run on an NVIDIA L4 on top of the `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image, with this branch's `python/` on `PYTHONPATH`: | Test | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | FP8, rows of A past 2^31 | error | pass | | F

title: [Bug][HiCache] HiRadixCache.writing_check can TP-deadlock; root cause is divergent write_backup / load_back enqueue decisions
summary: ## Summary `HiRadixCache.writing_check()` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py`) still short-circuits before its `all_reduce` when the local `ongoing_write_through` is empty: ```python # NOTE: all ranks has the same ongoing_write_through, can skip sync if empty if len(self.ongoing_write_through) == 0: return ``` This is the same anti-pattern fixed for `UnifiedRadixCache` in #27489 (merged) and reported for `HiMambaRadixCache` in #26921 / #26923. `HiRadixCache` — the **default** hierarchical-cache implementation for non-hybrid models (selected by `--enable-hierarchical-cache` unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE` or the experimental C++ tree is set) — was never patched. `loading_check()` in the same file is already unconditional; only `writing_check()` keeps the early return. I want to (a) close that gap with a minimal sibling fix (PR attached), and (b) put the actual root cause on record. As #27489's own description notes, and as @xiezhq-hermann pointed out on #26923, making the `all_reduce` unconditional removes the hard deadlock but does **not** stop the underlying divergence. ## Why the early return is unsafe — the divergence source The comment assumes every rank holds an identical `ongoing_write_through`. title: [Fix] spec: sample from the target when the rejection residual is empty in TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #42528. `TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly` draws coins from `[0, 1)` and, after rejecting a draft, samples the bonus/replacement token from the residual `relu(target - draft)`. The residual can be **empty**: every token the target gives mass to was a rejected draft (the kernel copies `target` into `draft` for each rejected token, so `q - p == 0` there). The easiest way to hit this in practice is a renormalized one-token nucleus (`top_k` + `top_p`): its probability is `1 - 2^-24`, not `1.0`, and `torch.rand` returns exactly `1 - 2^-24` with probability `2^-24`. The half-open CDF test (`coin < prob_acc`, #35798) then rejects the only token with target mass, `sum(relu(q - p)) == 0`, `u == 0`, no bucket is ever selected and the fallback emits token id `d - 1` — a token with zero target probability. With MTP on a 248k vocabulary this shows up as a rare garbage token (id `vocab_size - 1`) in the middle of a generation. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh` (shared device header, so the CUDA/ROCm JIT launchers and the MUSA AOT build all pick it up): also accumulate `sum(q)` in the first pass; when `sum(relu(q - p))` is not `> 0`, sample from the target distribution itself (`u = coin * sum(q)`, buckets from `q`). The acceptance test is unchanged, so #35798's semantics (half-open CDF, no zero-mass drafts) are preserved. - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`: add `upper-endpoint-empty-residual` — target `[0, 1 - 2^-24, 0]`, draft token 1, coin `1 - 2^-24`: the draft is rejecte

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] dsa: GLM-5 decode context parallelism on SM90
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5 DSA supports DCP only through the replicated index-K path, which needs the SM100 `trtllm` kernels. On SM90 (H100, H200) `--dcp-size` therefore does not work for GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3. With DCP4, a 16-GPU PP4 × TP4 deployment holds nearly 4× the KV tokens, 5.0M instead of 1.3M. ## Modifications - On SM90, GLM-5 DSA opts into the token-sharded index-K layout that Kimi-K3.1 already uses (`glm_dsa_shards_index_k`). SM100/SM103 keeps the replicated path. - In that mode, unset `--dsa-prefill-backend`, `--dsa-decode-backend` and `--kv-cache-dtype` resolve to `flashmla_sparse_q8`, `flashmla_kv` and `fp8_e4m3` instead of the `trtllm` defaults. The context length is capped so that table fits: 2^20 rounded down to a whole allocator page, minus the allocator's speculative reserve. At DCP4 that is 1048572 without a draft and 1048309 with 5 MTP steps and 6 draft tokens. A longer model context, such as GLM-5.3's 1048576, is capped by default, and a longer `--context-length` is rejected at startup. - The reserve formula in `allocation_sizing.py` moved into pure functions, so the cap and the allocator share it. title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Route the DCP prefill by its wire bytes
summary: ## Motivation A DSA DCP prefill can be served two ways: **owned** all-gathers Q, attends the slots this rank owns, and LSE-merges the head partials back through an a2a; **gathered** all-gathers the cached prefix KV latents once and attends them with this rank's local heads, with no merge. Neither wins everywhere. Owned pays per extend token and head, gathered pays per cached prefix token, and the crossing between them is a property of the data layout, not of the model. This PR derives it from the running configuration and routes each extend batch accordingly. Builds on #47180 (Q replication + project-before-merge) and #44322, both merged. ## Modifications Per extend token and gathered head, owned puts a partial plus its packed LSE on the wire. Per cached prefix token, gathered puts one latent on the wire. Both collectives move the same `(W-1)/W` of their volume over the same fabric, so the group width and the bandwidth cancel: ``` crossover = (partial_width + lse_pack) * itemsize(partial_dtype) / (latent * itemsize(kv_dtype)) gathered when sum(extend_prefix_lens) < crossover * gathered_heads * extend_num_tokens ``` `latent = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim`; `partial_width` is `v_head_dim` when the partials are projected before the merge, `kv_lora_rank` otherwise. A query all-gather adds one latent in the KV dtype to the numerator, which is exactly the denominator — so **not replicating `q_b_proj` adds exactly 1.0, for every model and dtype.** `dcp_gathered_prefill_crossover()` evaluates this once at backend construction and logs it. title: [Fix] [AMD] attention: preserve DCP LSE through prefill graph wrappers
summary: ## Motivation ROCm DCP MLA attention returns an `(output, LSE)` pair, but its two call sites in `forward_mla_rocm.py` did not mark that return shape for the prefill graph attention wrapper. With breakable prefill graphs, `RadixAttention._eager_attention` then treats the pair as a tensor and fails with `AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'data_ptr'`. The CUDA path (`forward_mla.py`) already passes `return_lse=True`. Adding the caller keyword alone is not enough: neither DCP-capable ROCm backend accepted it. The DSA backend and `AiterAttnBackend` both raised `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'return_lse'`. For aiter, that would have broken every DCP decode and target-verify step, even without prefill graphs. Supersedes #51856. ## Modifications - `forward_mla_rocm.py`: pass `return_lse=True` at both ROCm DCP MLA call sites. One goes through the DSA backend, the other through the aiter backend. - `dsa_backend.py` and `aiter_backend.py`: accept `return_lse: bool = False` in `forward_extend` and `forward_decode`. The function bodies and GPU kernels are unchanged, because the DCP branches already return `(output, LSE)`; the keyword only tells the prefill graph wrapper what to expect. - Tests: - `test_radix_attention.py`: the capture/replay test now also covers LSE requested by keyword while `mha_return_lse` is unset, which is the DCP case. - New `test_aiter_dcp_return_lse.py` (CPU): aiter DCP decode and target-verify dispatch through `backend.forward(..., return_lse=True)` and return the pair. title: [Feat] scheduler: Load-scaled class boundary and token budget for shortest-prefill-first
summary: ## Motivation `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` serves the shortest uncached prompt first. At normal load that lowers mean time to first token, but under sustained short traffic every new short prompt passes a waiting long one, so the long one can wait for a very long time. The policy also fills every prefill batch to the chunked prefill size even when the queue is nearly empty, so a short prompt that arrives mid-batch waits for a whole chunk. This PR adds an opt-in mode that scales both behaviours with the engine's prefill backlog `B`: the uncached tokens of the waiting requests plus what a continuing chunked prefill still has left, per DP attention rank. `B` is recomputed on every pass from the prefix matches the sort already uses, so every TP rank computes the same values. ## Modifications - **Class boundary.** `N(B) = C * 2 ** (-max(0, B - B0) / (K * C))`, where `C` is the chunked prefill size per DP attention rank and `B0` the decay start. Requests with fewer than `N` uncached tokens go first, shortest first, and may join a continuing chunk. Requests at or above `N` follow in arrival order and never join one: the chunk reservation for joiners and admission beside a continuing chunk both stop at the first of them. Up to `B0` the boundary is `C`; beyond it the boundary halves every `K` chunks of backlog, so under overload the order tends to first-come-first-served. - **Token budget.** `Q(B) = r * C * 2 ** (B / (D * C))` caps the prefill tokens of each batch, rounded down to the page size and the chunk alignment (at least one of them), with no cap once `Q` reache

title: [Fix] weight_cache: Destroy the daemon's NCCL communicators before serving
summary: A fix to the weight cache daemon: destroy its NCCL communicators before it serves. ## Motivation A weight cache daemon loads the model under process groups of its own, laid out like the engine's. A group of more than one rank creates a PyNccl communicator when it is built and connects it with a warm-up all-reduce, for the collectives of a forward pass. A daemon never runs one. PyNccl has no teardown of its own (`GroupCoordinator.destroy()` only drops the object), so every daemon kept its NCCL communicators, and their buffers, for as long as it served. The engines on the same GPUs size their KV cache on the memory that is left. On B200 this is 630 MiB per GPU at TP2, TP4 and TP8 in the runs below (measured: the daemon's GPU memory once it is ready, with and without this change). #7465 and vllm-project/vllm#19465 proposed destroying the communicator in `PyNcclCommunicator.__del__`; neither was merged, and the vLLM review pointed out that garbage-collection order is not reliable for a call that the other ranks must also make. This PR does not change PyNccl or the engine. It destroys the communicators only in the daemon, at one point that every rank reaches: after loading and the export, before serving. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/weight_cache/daemon.py`: - `destroy_nccl_communicators()`: goes through the registered groups (`parallel_state._groups`) in registration order, which model-parallel initialization makes the same on every rank. title: [Feat] [NPU] dsa: Shard DFlash Verify indexer requests in graphs
summary: ## Motivation On Ascend, every attention TP rank runs the BF16 DSA indexer over the same target Verify queries. With TP16, 16 requests, and five DFlash Verify rows per request, each rank scores 80 queries against its replicated index-K cache. MLA still needs all 80 rows of Top-K because its heads are split across TP ranks. The request split reduces the costly indexer scan. It adds a Top-K collective on the path to sparse attention. In our eager prototype, rank arrival skew erased the scoring savings. In a fixed-batch NPU graph the ranks reach the collective much closer together. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_NPU_DSA_VERIFY_REQUEST_SHARD`, off by default. For fixed-width DFlash target Verify graphs with BF16 index-K, each attention TP rank scores contiguous whole requests. With TP16 in the example above, it scores five rows. A rank-ordered all-gather restores the full query layout for the existing sparse attention call. - Update a persistent valid-request mask before graph replay using the live batch size. Padded requests get safe indexer inputs and their Top-K rows are set to `-1` before the collective. Graphs with incompatible batch sizes continue to use the existing path. - For attention DP, keep the indexer all-gather inside each attention TP group. On Ascend, allow `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_TP_AUX_FC` when the worker has narrowed its draft TP group to a single attention-DP shard. The FC split and all-reduce already exist in main and remain independently selectable. - Add CPU coverage for rank ordering, KV lengths and ineligible shapes. Document both opt-ins. ## Accuracy Tests

title: [Fix] dp-attention: Take single-node control-plane ports from a free block
summary: ## Motivation With DP attention, `PortArgs.init_new` derives five control-plane ports (tokenizer, detokenizer, metrics, scheduler input, load collector) from `--port + 233`. Two servers on one host whose `--port` values are close derive overlapping blocks. The common case is a PD pair on one node: prefill on `--port 30000` takes ports in 30234–30239, so a decode on `--port 30001` or `30002` (whose blocks start at 30234 and 30235) waits 30 s and exits. With the decode on 30002: ``` ValueError: dist_init_port at 30235 is not available in 30 seconds. dist_init_port is used by a process already. process.name()='sglang' ... '--port', '30002'] ... pid=18 ``` The message names the decode server itself as the owner. The real owner is the prefill server in another container: psutil reports `pid=None` for a socket held by a process in another PID namespace, and `psutil.Process(None)` is the calling process. On a single node without `--dist-init-addr`, nothing outside the server derives these ports, so they do not need to come from `--port`. This picks up the approach of #30833 by @luccafong (closed as a stale draft) on current main, with them as co-author of the first commit. ## Modifications - `PortArgs.init_new`, single node, no `--dist-init-addr`: the launcher takes the block from the new `get_free_port_block`. It looks for consecutive free ports in 22000–29999, skipping every configured `--*-port` value and the NCCL port. - It prefers the part of that range below the kernel ephemeral range, like the existing `nccl_port` allocator, so no outbound connection can take a port before

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] dsa: Add an opt-in NVFP4 MLA KV cache for prims_ts (--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla)
summary: Add an opt-in KV cache dtype for the `prims_ts` DSA backend: with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` the DSA MLA cache stores each token as a 352 B NVFP4 record (FlashInfer Prims-TS `"nvfp4.fp8rope"` format, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7410) instead of a 576 B raw-FP8 row. Nothing changes unless the flag is passed. ## Motivation In PD serving of DSA models (Kimi-K3.1), the prefill pool's KV capacity limits how many cached prefixes stay on GPU; misses are reloaded from the HiCache host tier or recomputed. The MLA rows are most of a DSA layer's KV bytes: - Raw FP8: 576 B MLA + 132 B index-K = 708 B/token/layer. - NVFP4 record: 352 B MLA + 132 B index-K = 484 B/token/layer. So the same memory holds **1.46x more KV tokens on GPU** (1.64x in the HiCache host tier, which stores only the MLA rows). On Kimi-K3.1 GB300 serving this raises the GPU prefix-cache hit by about 13 points and cuts TTFT, with unchanged GSM8K (see below). The NVFP4 attention kernel is dequant-bound and somewhat slower than raw FP8 per call, which is why the dtype is opt-in rather than a default. ## Modifications **Record layout** (352 B/token/layer): `[0, 256)` the 512 NoPE values as E2M1, two per byte; `[256, 320)` the 64 RoPE values as unscaled E4M3; `[320, 352)` 32 E4M3 block-16 scales, block `b` at `320 + 8*(b%4) + b//4`. Block scale `e4m3(max(amax16 / 6, 2^-9))`, no global scale. **Interface and validation** - New `--kv-cache-dtype` choice `nvfp4_ds_mla`, separate from the existing `nvfp4` (`float4_e2m1fn_x2` pool) recipe. It resolves to `float8_e4m3fn` elements and E4M3 queries, so FP8 dtype checks keep hold

title: [Perf] linker: Load DSpark draft KV with the last transfer layers
summary: ## Motivation The direct linker maps sidecar draft depth `i` to transfer layer `i` (#48125). title: [Fix] hicache: Move NIXL pages that are not whole O_DIRECT blocks
summary: ## Motivation Refs #45563. With a NIXL file plugin and O_DIRECT on (the default), every transfer's address and length must be whole 4 KiB blocks. DSA models' host pages are not: GLM-5.x has 3,316,736 B KV pages and 667,392 B indexer pages. Such a pool fails `is_stride_page_aligned(4096)` and falls back to copy mode. Copy mode's staging slots are exactly one page long, so the kernel refuses (EINVAL) every transfer and NIXL leaves empty files behind. The L3 then either never produces a usable hit or, with older NIXL, restores all-zero KV. ## Modifications **Copy mode (any layout, any pool).** Under O_DIRECT, each staging slot is padded to whole 4 KiB blocks. The view keeps the allocation's CUDA host-registration ranges, so `destroy()` still unregisters them. - **Who decides:** `get_storage_page_align(layout, allocator_type)` asks the backend. title: [Feature] KVarN: KV-cache compression for hybrid linear-attention models
summary: ## Motivation Hybrid linear-attention models (GDN/Mamba + full-attention) like Qwen 3.5 and Kimi-Linear have O(n) linear-attention layers but still retain O(n²) full-attention layers whose KV cache dominates GPU memory at long contexts. This limits the practical context length on commodity GPUs (e.g. 24 GB RTX 3090). KVarN compresses the full-attention KV cache to int4 (~8x reduction vs BF16), enabling long-context inference within bounded GPU memory. ## Modifications ### Core design **Quantization pipeline**: Per-tile Hadamard rotation → Sinkhorn variance normalization → 4-bit packing with per-group scales. The decode kernel fuses dequant with QK^T and attention. **HiCache integration**: KVarN stores raw int4 tiles in the host memory pool (~2.7 KB/token) without dequant/requant, enabling transparent offloading of long conversation history. title: [Fix] [AMD] dsa: Reuse one buffer for the FlyDSL prefill indexer logits
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.2-FP8 on 8x MI355X with attention DP 8 crashes when 8 prompts of 500k tokens come in at once: on main all 8 requests fail after ~254 s with a HIP runtime abort. With this change and the aiter one below, all 8 are served in 340 s and prefill speed doesnt change. This is the crash behind #34011, which I closed after finding the real cause. The cause is the prefill indexer logits. On gfx950 `ragged_mqa_logits` gets them from aiter's FlyDSL `fp8_mqa_logits`, which allocates a new `[rows, keys]` fp32 tensor on every call. Each chunk of a long prefill sees more keys, so each call wants a slightly bigger block than the last one (2048 rows x 235k keys is about 1.8 GiB, the next chunk wants 16 MiB more). The caching allocator cant reuse the freed smaller blocks for that and keeps them. In the crash run torch's reserved memory reached 271-279 GiB per GPU while live tensors stayed at ~167 GiB. MI355X has 288 GB of HBM per GPU, and the HIP runtime needs some free device memory outside torch's cache for its own allocations, so it aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. `expandable_segments` isnt supported on ROCm and `garbage_collection_threshold:0.8` didnt help. ## Modifications - `dsa_indexer_hip.ragged_mqa_logits` passes `out=` from one buffer per device and stream. The buffer only grows, and then at least 2x, so a long prefill takes a handful of growth steps instead of a new block per chunk. The view uses the kernel's own row pitch (keys rounded up to 256), so the layout the top-k reads is the same as before. - It needs the aiter `out=` from https://gith

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsa: Fuse KPool query Hadamard and FP8 gate quantization on SM120
summary: ## Motivation Part of the Q4 kernel/quantization optimization roadmap (#42473) and GLM-5.3 on SM120 tracking (#51550). In dual-stream decode and target verify, query preparation launches a Hadamard transform, `act_quant`, and head-gate scaling separately. The intermediate BF16 query and per-head quantization scales need not be written back to memory. This PR fuses the three operations into one CUDA kernel. It is complementary to the separate fused logits/top-k work in #49098. ## Modifications - Reuse the existing 128-point warp Hadamard and FP8/UE8M0 helpers. Register the operator and extend the existing indexer fusion accuracy test; add a reproducible benchmark. ## Accuracy Tests RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120), PyTorch 2.14.1 + CUDA 13.0: - The four new registered cases (0, 1, 32, 1,024 tokens) pass on the exact final source. title: [Feat] sampling: Count penalty history right after sampling in a per-request pool
summary: ## Motivation Sampling penalties need each request's output history. On main that history lives in per-batch penalizer tables: the scheduler fills them from the host `output_ids` in `prepare_for_decode`, which lags one step under overlap, and filters and merges them on the schedule stream while a forward may still read them. Exact speculative penalties (the next PR) need the history current at verify and owned by the device. This PR counts each committed token right after sampling, on the sampling stream, into a per-request pool; the scheduler only hands out and frees penalty indices and builds each step's params. ## Modifications - `sampling/penalties.py`: `PenaltyStatusPool`, one per scheduler. It holds an int32 per-token count table plus output lengths, with one row per request that uses a penalty; the request holds its row's penalty index (`Req.penalty_index`), and a step carries the penalty indices it was built with. `StepPenalties` holds a step's params and builds the `[bs, vocab]` additive and scaling tables from the pool. The penalizer orchestrator and its four penalizers are removed. - **Rows**: - A request gets a penalty index at its first extend admission (`alloc`), and the row is reset and replayed from `output_ids` at every extend admission (`reset_history`) (prefill, every chunk, retraction readmission, PD decode prebuilt). This also wipes a discarded chunk sample. - A row is freed at request exit in `RequestRetirer`; a retraction keeps its row. - The tables are dropped when no row is live. - **Streams**: host calls only queue device writes. title: [Feat] linear-attn: Bole spec-verify for GDN (drop per-draft SSM snapshots)
summary: ## Motivation Speculative target verify on GDN (gated delta rule) hybrid models snapshots the full recurrent state after every draft step into `MambaPool.intermediate_ssm`, so that the commit can copy back the state of the accepted step. The buffer is `(max_running_requests + 1) x num_draft_tokens x state_size_per_layer x num_gdn_layers` and is reserved for the whole lifetime of the server. For Qwen3.8-27B (48 GDN layers, TP2) with DFLASH block 8 it is **3.66 GB per GPU at `--max-running-requests 12`**, taken straight out of the KV pool, and it grows linearly with the concurrency cap. ReplaySSM spec-verify (RFC #28511) removes this buffer for MTP-style verify, but with DSPARK/DFLASH it currently requires a KDA model (`--enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires a KDA model`), so GDN models served with DFLASH (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2) still pay the full snapshot cost. ## Modifications Bole keeps only the low-rank factors of each draft step and rebuilds the accepted state on commit. Starting from the same state `S_0`, the state after `a` steps of the gated delta rule is $$S_a = p_a S_0 + \sum_{j \le a} \frac{p_a}{p_j} k_j u_j^\top$$ where `p` is the cumulative decay, `k_j` the L2-normalized key and `u_j` a correction vector obtained from a `T x T` unit lower-triangular system. Verify stores `p`, `k`, `u` (about `T x 128` values per head instead of `T x 128 x 128`), and the commit writes `S_a` back into the request slot. - `kernels/ops/attention/linear/bole_spec_verify.py` (new): three Triton kernels - `bole_factor_kernel`: per (request, head) cumulative log-

title: [Perf] scheduler: Send a finished request's last output before its prefix-cache insert and free its prompt ids after the next dispatch
summary: ## Motivation At the end of every streamed response, two pieces of host work that grow with the prompt length run between the request's last output token and the end of its response stream: 1. **Scheduler: the prefix-cache insert runs before the final chunk is sent.** `process_batch_result_decode` releases a request that finishes in the step (`request_retirer.release` -> `release_kv_cache`, which checkpoints the whole sequence into the radix tree) inside its per-request loop, and only then calls `stream_output`. So the final chunk of every response waits for the insert. 2. **TokenizerManager: the prompt's token-id list is freed before the stream ends.** A prompt given as token ids (the chat-completions path, `/generate` with `input_ids`, or a frontend that tokenizes itself) is a Python list holding one int object per token. Its last references are the request's generator frames, so it is freed when `generate_request` returns: after the final output was yielded, but before the caller ends its response. That costs about 10 ns per token. summary: ## Motivation The prefill delayer's queue trigger (`--prefill-delayer-queue-min-ratio`, #23189) should hold prefill until the queue reaches `running_req * ratio` or `--prefill-delayer-max-delay-ms` elapses, but on main it ends its own delay in three ways; this PR removes all three. 1. **The threshold collapses toward the queue.** Without `--prefill-max-requests` it is capped by the `max_prefill_bs` high-watermark, which delayed passes feed with the waiting-queue length (#34284). #35191 fixed this only when a request limit is set. 2. **A queue-only delay consumes the one-shot `skip_first_delayer` bypass** meant for the slot trigger's first `merge_batch`. 3. **The default `max_delay_passes` (#32880) also bounds queue delays**, so 30 passes end them long before the 5000 ms default. ## Modifications - The threshold is `running_req * ratio`, capped only by a configured `--prefill-max-requests`. - `skip_first_delayer` is consumed only when the slot condition holds. - Queue-triggered delays are bounded by `max_delay_ms` (TP0 decides it since #42625), and by `--prefill-delayer-max-delay-passes` only when it is set. title: [Fix] json-schema: Add depth and state bounds validation
summary: This fix addresses the security vulnerability where deeply nested or complex JSON schemas could cause CPU thread hanging and DoS via unbounded DFA/NFA state compilation. Changes: 1. Added validate_schema_depth() and validate_schema_bounds() functions in json_schema_validation.py 2. Added JSONSchemaDepthExceeded and JSONSchemaStateExplosion exception classes 3. Integrated validation into all three grammar backends (xgrammar, outlines, llguidance) 4. Added comprehensive unit tests for the new validation The validation enforces: - Maximum schema nesting depth of 16 - Maximum estimated DFA states of 10,000 This prevents adversarial schemas from causing DoS by state space explosion. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This PR addresses a security vulnerability (Issue #39125) where deeply nested or cyclically referencing JSON schemas (depth > 16 or high branching factor) could cause the Grammar DFA/NFA state compiler to attempt unbounded state space compilation. title: [BugFix][Worker] Preserve measured non-KV memory when sizing the KV cache
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fixes #22448. The regular Ascend worker replaces vLLM Core's measured non-KV memory total with a sum of weight memory, non-Torch growth, and incremental Torch peak. A persistent allocation made after weight measurement and before profiling cancels out of the incremental peak, leaving the automatic KV budget and the startup suggestion too large. The issue records this on Ascend 910C (A3) with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash BF16. Use the Core profiler's total for the regular worker's automatic KV sizing and reuse it in startup suggestions before adding the measured ACL graph memory and existing buffer. Both vLLM CI pins expose the same total. This uses the standard worker path shared by MRV1 and MRV2, including Qwen deployments. The 310P worker's inherited suggestion keeps its existing calculation. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Automatic KV capacity and startup recommendations account for model-runner allocations retained outside weight loading. ### How was this patch tested? - Ran 12 targeted tests in a source-isolated unittest harness with the actual worker methods and mocked profiling dependencies. Both regressions failed before the fix and all 12 tests passed afterward. They cover automatic sizing, persisted startup suggestions including graph memory, and existing multi-instance cases. - On one Ascend 910B3 (A2), CANN 9.2.1, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and torch-npu 2.10.0.post7, ran the worker's profiling method against real NPU allocations with the vLLM v0.33.0 profiler and the repository's Torch accelerator bindings. title: [Feature] Add fused W4A4 INT4 MoE "mega" kernel for Qwen3.x-MoE (Ascend 910B)
summary: ## What Adds a single-launch **W4A4** (INT4 weight × INT4 activation) fused MoE expert kernel for Qwen3.x-MoE on Ascend 910B, exposed as a new `("W4A4_DYNAMIC", "moe")` quantization scheme. One MIX kernel runs the whole routed-expert path — block-diagonal Hadamard → INT4 quant + routing scatter → INT4 `gate_up` → SwiGLU + INT4 requant → INT4 `down` → unpermute/top-k combine — replacing the vendor's multi-launch `torch_npu` `npu_*` op chain, with cube matmuls overlapped against the vector stages. ## Why MoE decode serving on 910B is HBM-bandwidth bound. The standard vllm-ascend W4A4 path ("vendor" throughout this PR) already shrinks the routed-expert weights 4×, but it assembles the expert path from a chain of **separate `torch_npu` `npu_*` op launches** — `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` → `npu_dynamic_quant` → `npu_grouped_matmul` (`gate_up`) → `npu_swiglu` → `npu_dynamic_quant` → `npu_grouped_matmul` (`down`) → `npu_moe_token_unpermute` — each paying dispatch + cross-core sync overhead and round-tripping the activations through HBM between ops. (So everywhere this PR says "vendor", it means that stock chain built from `torch_npu` builtins — no custom kernel.) This kernel folds that whole chain into **one MIX launch**, with the cube matmuls overlapped against the vector stages, so the intermediate activations never leave on-chip memory. The payoff is twofold: - **vs. standard vllm-ascend W4A4 (same checkpoint, same accuracy):** the fused kernel is the headline win — **1.46× higher decode throughput** purely from removing the per-op dispatch/sync/HBM-round-trip overhead. title: [Feature][KV Pool] Support hybrid load failure recompute
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR is a follow-up to #9701 and ports the hybrid failed-block handling from #7476. For hybrid KV cache layouts, one backend load failure can invalidate peer KV blocks that correspond to the same token span across different KV cache groups. This PR records those peer block IDs together so `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"` can rewind and recompute all affected hybrid blocks instead of only the single group that reported the failed backend key. It also removes the temporary hybrid rejection for `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Hybrid models can now use KV load failure policy `recompute` instead of failing fast at config validation. ### Validation vLLM version: v0.23.0 vLLM main: vllm-project/vllm@967c5c3bc38891f4465d3f4e99917ed837bb3833 - vLLM version: v0.23.0 - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/967c5c3bc38891f4465d3f4e99917ed837bb3833

title: [Feature] Support Container Snapshot and Restore (GRUS) on Ascend NPU
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This pull request aims at implement the container snapshot function for vllm-driven infer service. It proposes that adding two lifecycle interfaces to the inference engine: `/suspend`, `/resume`, to support state saving and restoration based on Container Snapshot. 1. Suspend (snapshot save phase) During container checkpointing, the container snapshot framework triggers the inference engine’s suspend interface to converge the runtime state into a consistent snapshot point. This includes: (1) Device-side state persistence Persist the device-side runtime state required for inference recovery, including device memory state, KV cache, and execution context. (2) Model weight checkpointing Export model weights from the device and persist them to host-side storage or memory for later restoration. 2. Resume (snapshot restore phase) During container restoration, the container snapshot framework triggers the inference engine’s resume interface to restore a runnable instance from the snapshot state. This includes: (1) Communication group reconstruction Destroy and reinitialize distributed communication groups and runtime communication contexts to ensure consistency. (2) Model weight restoration (host → device) Load model weights from the host side and transfer them back to device memory. (3) Graph-mode recovery (if enabled) Re-perform graph capture in graph mode. title: [RFC]: Reuse HiSparse prefixes with AscendStore in colocated serving
summary: ### Motivation. An agent often sends the same long system prompt and conversation history on successive requests. If the prefix has left the worker's local cache, the next request has to run Prefill over that history again. HiSparse helps the *running* request fit more KV by keeping historical main KV in local DDR and fetching selected rows for Decode. AscendStore provides a way to reuse KV *across* requests. [Ascend HiSparse RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19293) We propose composing the two connectors on a single Ascend A5 node that runs both Prefill and Decode. A GLM-5.3 request should be able to restore a previously saved prefix, compute its new suffix, and continue decoding with the existing HiSparse attention path. [HiSparse foundation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20926) · [Implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/21924) ### Proposed Change. #### A prefix shared by two requests ```text Request 1 [ shared prefix ] [ first question ] Prefill produces KV AscendStore saves complete prefix blocks to the external pool (PUT) Request 2 [ shared prefix ] [ next question ] Local prefix miss, external pool hit AscendStore restores matching blocks to DDR and NPU (GET) │ ▼ Prefill computes the remaining tokens HiSparse serves Decode with Resident, Hot and Host Source KV ``` AscendStore moves **whole prefix blocks** between the worker and the pool. Inside each Decode step, HiSparse selects **individual KV rows** and fetches missing rows from local DDR. A pool hit restores the state needed for that selection. ####

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Trim stale Mooncake prefill hashes without rehashing the prefix
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Addresses the Hybrid connector portion of #21166. When the prefill producer drops the last prompt token, any block hash covering that token becomes stale. The Hybrid connector could retain that hash. Mooncake V1 rebuilt the entire prefix. After #22167, V2 still did so on vLLM versions earlier than 0.34 when the native truncation method was unavailable. These three scheduler paths now trim hashes before the local prefix lookup using the engine-resolved hash block size and the configured hash lookahead. V2 Pull and Push inherit the same change. Each scheduler calls `Request.truncate_block_hashes()` when the method is callable. For vLLM versions earlier than 0.34 that lack it, a shared fallback trims the invalid suffix in place and clears the prompt-embedding hash cache. The existing one-token and rescheduling guards still apply. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Hybrid uses the shortened prompt for prefix reuse, and long text prompts avoid the full-prefix hash pass during producer admission. ### How was this patch tested? - Added a V2 connector regression using the vLLM request and block hasher. It compares the result with an independently hashed shortened request and checks that reentry makes zero hasher calls. Two cases cover the hash boundary: an embedding prompt loses one hash when a lookahead token is removed, and a text prompt keeps all complete hashes when a partial tail is removed. title: [Performance][Model] Reuse Qwen4Exp HC block output across streams
summary: This is a follow-up optimization built on our existing #21901 work. No external AscendC package or Torch extension is required. ### What this PR does / why we need it? Qwen4Exp `hc_combine_norm` currently launches one program per `(row, HC stream)`. Every program loads the same row of `block_output`, so the production four-stream layout reads that row four times. This model-specific operator returns the combined and normalized tensors and is installed into the Qwen4Exp model's upstream HC call path. This PR adds an A3 row-wise variant for per-branch norm weights at 512 rows and above. One program loads `block_output` once and walks the HC streams in the original order. It preserves the BF16 combine-materialization boundary and FP32 RMSNorm reduction order. Shared weights, smaller batches, and other hardware profiles keep the legacy kernel. The row-wise variant selects INT64 row addressing only when an input or output offset exceeds INT32_MAX; ordinary shapes retain INT32 addressing and the legacy launch is unchanged. The upstream NVIDIA implementation also uses the per-`(row, stream)` schedule and does not provide an Ascend row-wise implementation to reuse. No CLI option, environment variable, or additional-config key is added; the 512-row value is an internal A3 hardware-profile threshold based on measured crossover. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. Qwen4Exp long-prefill HC execution on A3 is faster. Public APIs and configuration are unchanged. A release-note fragment is included with the mechanism and measured scenario. ### How was this patch test

title: [Performance][GDN] Preserve warm prefill checkpoints in dedicated pages on MRV2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Enable Model Runner V2 to consume an explicit Mamba checkpoint block ID and export the GDN state into a dedicated page during an existing model forward. The Ascend fused prefill path runs the recurrence on both sides of the checkpoint and retains the intermediate convolution window and recurrent state for later prefix hits. This also covers short warm continuations where the checkpoint has no writable column in the ordinary Mamba block table. PR #22728 runs the native recurrence with existing block-table destinations and has a policy that can skip a first-seen tail. This draft focuses on preserving a reusable checkpoint in those short continuations. The supporting Core prototype is based on the verified vLLM pin and is available at https://github.com/Dwight2458/vllm/tree/perf/mamba-private-prefill-checkpoint. Direct worker propagation is needed because the generic block-table metadata provides no destination for a page outside that table. The long-term path is a shared Core allocation and metadata interface. AI assistance was used in preparing this draft. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? With the experimental `gdn_internal_prefill_checkpoints` option enabled and a paired Core that supplies dedicated checkpoint pages, eligible warm GDN prefills can keep their new checkpoint in one model forward. The dedicated path is gated on Model Runner V2 with speculative decoding disabled. title: [Feature] Opt-in owner-sharded PCP KV cache for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on A3
summary: # What / why PCP ranks currently keep and write a full physical copy of the shared KV slot, even though a prefill token belongs to exactly one rank. This adds an **opt-in owner-sharded placement** for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash prefill on A3: the KV cache is backed by a CANN VMM slab whose 2 MiB physical chunks are split `1 / pcp_size` per rank, while every rank maps the complete logical address range. The stock attention kernel keeps addressing the same cache tensor; only the physical footprint changes. This PR validates the **owner + local KV write + long-KV/SWA staging + replicated index** profile, with optional **capacity**. # Scope - A3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, **prefill PCP only**. Decode remains replicated and unchanged. - Default-off: `additional_config.pcp_config.kv_sharing` defaults to `"replicated"`; every other switch defaults off. - If any rank cannot map the owner slab, the group falls back collectively to a replicated allocation (`pcp_config.owner_capacity` is the exception: it fails closed). - No upstream vLLM changes are required. Related RFC: vllm-project/vllm#50127. ## What is in the PR 1. **Local prefill KV writes** from rank-local hidden states, opt-in and only active with a mapped owner slab. SWA has one entry per token and no cross-chunk state, so the local write is exact and skips the KV-row all-gather. title: [Performance][Ops] Cache decode GDN attention metadata across steps
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Ref #20607. `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` is invoked once per GDN KV-cache group on every decode step. On hybrid (linear attention) models, rebuilding the same `GDNAttentionMetadata` for every group is a significant part of the host-side step time whenever the batch composition is stable. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 (48 GDN + 16 full attention layers, TP8 on 910B4, MTP spec4 speculative decoding) the builder costs ~4.7 ms per decode step for its 3 GDN KV groups, i.e. ~22% of the ~21 ms step, and the decode step is host bound in that configuration. All host inputs of a pure-decode step only change when a sequence advances into a new KV block or when the set of requests changes. The built metadata can therefore be cached across steps and only the accepted-token counts (the only value that advances every step) are refreshed in place. Prefill steps drop the cache. The cache key covers the request identity, the batch shape, the query start locations, the derived sequence-length facts the builder consumes (zero-length graph-padding rows, "sequence has state", KV block index), the prefill mask and the per-request draft-token counts. title: [BugFix] Skip MRV2 Engram lookback reads for padded rows
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? MRV2 launches one lookback program per row of a persistent window sized to `max_num_seqs`. The request-to-slot mapping contains only the active requests for the current step. When a batch shrinks, the old kernel still forms a pointer beyond that mapping for each padding row and passes it to a masked scalar load. Branch on the row before computing any input address. Active rows gather the most recent tokens from their mapped slot using the device count and the history row stride. Padding rows write `-1` across their output. Both paths share the final masked store, so the next forward sees a refreshed window after requests leave or slots are reused. Refs #21392. The reported 910B3 fault was a negative token-history offset on v0.30. Current main already clamps that offset. This PR covers the distinct mapping boundary on partial batches and adds regression coverage for both cases. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? The output contract, configuration, persistent buffer and launch grid are preserved. This is an internal MRV2 address-safety change. The active slot and history-count invariants come from the runner. Delayed PP sampling uses a separate mapping. ### How was this patch tested? - Ran the new address tests against the original and changed kernel bodies using the paired vLLM CPU Triton decorator and NumPy operations. Baseline `c64ace678d12` had 2 failures on padding rows and 8 passes. The candidate passed all 10. On Windows these focused tests used isolated imports. title: Engine wedge (idle, no traceback) when verl bypass_mode requests calculate_log_probs on TP8 long-context
summary: ## Summary With verl's `algorithm.rollout_correction.bypass_mode=True` + `rollout.calculate_log_probs=True`, the vllm-ascend V1 engine (TP8, `max_model_len=32768`) wedges during the generation long tail. Full symptoms: - generation stalls with a partial finish count (e.g. 473/512 sequences finished) - NPUs drop to idle power (~400 W/card), no kernel activity - no traceback on any rank, engine unresponsive Reproduced 3× after excluding HBM leak / host-level orphan processes as causes. Suspect: the logprobs collection path for TP8 + 32k context in the vllm-ascend V1 engine (a large gather across TP ranks during the decode tail). ## Env - Ascend 950DT (8×96 GB), vllm-ascend V1 engine, TP8 - verl 0.10.0.dev async rollout driving the engine ## Workaround None found. We abandoned `bypass_mode` (its saving was only ~400 s/step anyway), but the wedge looks like a real hang bug in the logprobs path. Happy to provide more config details or a minimal repro script if useful.

title: [Feature] Route the DSA indexer per_row top-k to the TopKPerRow operator
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? vLLM's sparse-attention indexer selects its decode top-k kernel per call in `vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py`: ```python if not self._cooperative_constraints(logits, topk_tokens, num_rows): return "cooperative" if self._is_cuda and topk_tokens in (512, 1024, 2048): return "persistent" return "per_row" ``` `cooperative` and `persistent` both require CUDA, so on NPU every DSA-indexer model lands on `per_row`, and `SparseIndexerTopk._per_row` then calls `vllm._custom_ops.top_k_per_row_decode`, which dispatches to `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode`. That operator only exists in vLLM's CUDA extension, so on Ascend the indexer stage raises -- and #21917's TopKPerRow operator has no consumer. This PR rebinds the two `vllm._custom_ops` entry points onto `torch.ops._C_ascend.top_k_per_row_prefill` / `.top_k_per_row_decode`. The wrappers take the same eight positional arguments as vLLM's, matching the Ascend schemas in `csrc/torch_binding.cpp`, so every call site is unchanged; `stride0`/`stride1` are accepted and unused because the Ascend operator derives the row width from the tensor. The indexer looks the names up on the module at call time, so no vLLM source is modified and no import-order requirement beyond "before the first indexer forward" is introduced. Every path through vLLM's `SparseIndexerTopk` -- including an explicit `kernel_config.sparse_indexer_topk_backend="per_row"` -- then reaches the AscendC kernel instead of a CUDA-only attribute. **The Ascend operator is resolved per call, not once at import.** `torch.ops._C_asc

title: [RFC]: Reuse HiSparse prefixes with AscendStore in colocated serving
summary: Working draft for a community RFC Issue. The proposal below uses the repository RFC template. ## Motivation An agent often sends the same long system prompt and conversation history on successive requests. If the prefix has left the worker's local cache, the next request has to run Prefill over that history again. HiSparse helps the *running* request fit more KV by keeping historical main KV in local DDR and fetching selected rows for Decode. AscendStore provides a way to reuse KV *across* requests. title: [Performance][Spec Decode] Fuse add and argmax for Dspark on Ascend V2
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DSpArk sequential greedy drafting selects each draft token from the sum of base logits and the Markov-head bias. The existing path materializes this sum and then reads it again for argmax. This PR adds an opt-in fused add and two-stage argmax implementation for Ascend NPUs in Model Runner V2. It avoids materializing the full summed-logits tensor during supported greedy sampling steps. The implementation: - Splits the vocabulary into blocks of 4096 elements. - Loads base logits and Markov bias, performs source-dtype addition, and computes each block’s maximum value and corresponding index in the first kernel. - Reduces the partial results and writes the selected draft-token ID in the second kernel. - Uses standard `tl.max` and `tl.min` reductions. - Allocates temporary reduction buffers during speculator initialization and reuses them across sequential steps. - Preserves draft-to-target vocabulary mapping and the independent confidence-head path. The kernel supports matching FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs with unit vocabulary stride, including non-contiguous row layouts. It preserves source-dtype addition rounding, first-index tie breaking, NaN handling, and positive/negative infinity handling. Probabilistic sampling, top-k drafting, acceptance-estimator consumers, and models with output-logit transforms or custom sequential sampling methods retain the existing sampling path. title: [Performance][MoE] Eliminate host-bound sync in AlltoAllv dispatch preprocess
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? `TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV._preprocess` blocked the host twice on every MoE dispatch: 1. `torch.repeat_interleave(self.expert_ids_per_ep_rank, num_global_tokens_per_local_expert.ravel())` derives its output length from device-side repeats, which ATen implements via an implicit `repeats.sum().item()` — a D2H copy plus a stream sync. Because the router histogram, the EP all_gather and the split D2H copies are all queued ahead of it, the host stalls until the entire backlog drains (production profiles showed ~15 ms per call, with only ~66 us of actual kernel work), and the device idles behind the all_gather while waiting for the host to wake up and enqueue the following kernels. 2. The `num_local_experts == 1` branch fell back to a full `torch.npu.synchronize()`. **Key rule (the general principle this PR follows):** once the host needs to *read* a device-side value (an explicit `.item()`, or implicitly to derive an output length), it must wait in place for every op already queued ahead of it on the device. Two consequences follow: (1) the host-side `torch.repeat_interleave` appears extremely slow — its wall time is mostly blocking on device work that was enqueued earlier and has not drained yet; (2) once the device queue does drain, the `.item()` D2H sync plus the wait for the host to issue new ops leaves a device-side bubble. With enough host-side work in between, the whole step turns host-bound and produces fast/slow (staggered) ranks. title: [Performance][LoRA][MoE] Skip idle LoRA routing on TP AllGather
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? In a deployment with LoRA enabled, a request batch may consist entirely of base-model requests and contain no adapter tokens. For non-quantized MoE, the current code still performs LoRA routing restoration and w13 delta injection whenever a `lora_context` exists, even when the batch has no LoRA work. These calls are not free: routing recovery builds the inverse permutation and gathers expert and adapter IDs, while w13 delta injection launches the fused MoE LoRA kernel. Because this work recurs in every MoE layer, a base-model-only batch still pays routing, kernel-launch, and LoRA application overhead in a LoRA-enabled server. For pure-TP AllGather, `has_lora() == False` is a complete local description of the AllGather input: no DP, PCP, or SP rank can introduce adapter tokens from another rank. This PR therefore skips both operations for that idle batch. It does not skip the base MoE GMM, AllGather itself, or any model forward work. This isolation is the performance source: the measured gain comes from removing repeated idle LoRA side-work, with LoRA-disabled execution providing the upper bound. This PR does not change communication context publication. This PR only optimizes pure-TP, non-quantized `MoECommType.ALLGATHER` batches. The fast path requires `ep_size=1`, `dp_size=1`, `pcp_size=1`, and `is_sequence_parallel=False`: 1. title: [BugFix][Worker] Validate KV cache sizing when free NPU memory is unchanged
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Refs #18343. The NPU worker compares free memory before model loading and after profiling. Equal readings can be consistent when model weights fit within memory already reserved by PyTorch. They can also occur when a device or virtualization layer fails to report a new reservation. In the latter case, the derived non-PyTorch memory delta can cancel the weight cost and inflate the KV cache budget. On the generic worker with HiSparse disabled, this change accepts equal free-memory snapshots when device totals and PyTorch reservations agree, new live allocations fit in the reported initial reserve, and the computed budget accounts for those allocations. Inconsistent readings raise an actionable error that points to the existing `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` option for users who know a safe budget. Increased free memory raises an explicit error with the before and after readings. HiSparse requires a decrease in free memory for automatic sizing. Equal readings leave only transient headroom in the upstream non-KV total, which can omit retained allocations. On 310P EP (dedicated HBM), an equal reading requires the allocator to account for retained allocations in existing reserves. The worker subtracts retained bytes and transient peak headroom before halving the budget for workspace. On 310P RC (shared memory), the comparison uses host available memory for both snapshots and the existing budget calculation uses host occupancy. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? title: [Performance][Scheduler] Cap mixed-batch decodes and drain deferred requests
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? When prefill and decode requests share a step on Ascend, a large decode population can make the mixed step expensive and leave fewer opportunities for decode-only execution. This draft adds an opt-in cap on the number of decode requests in a step that may carry prefill. When the cap defers decode requests, the following step holds regular prefill work so runnable decodes can advance within the existing token and KV-cache budgets. The Ascend platform selects a scheduler subclass for this policy. It applies the cap before KV-slot allocation through the paired vLLM scheduler's token-selection hook and uses the existing prefill throttle for the drain step. Upstream allocation, preemption, and async bookkeeping remain in use. The drain also covers a prefill that turns out to be blocked after the cap has deferred a decode. A queued prefill participates in the cap decision only when a running slot is available. Related work in #14054 addresses prefill admission for pipeline parallelism. This proposal targets decode admission in colocated Ascend mixed batches. AI assistance was used in the implementation and tests. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. The policy is disabled by default. For colocated serving with FCFS, DP=PP=1 and local KV, it can be enabled through Ascend additional config: ```sh --additional-config '{"scheduler_config":{"max_num_decode_seqs_in_mixed_batch":2}}' ``` The configuration is independent of the prefix match unit. title: [Performance][MoE] Pipeline prefill expert offload and reuse resident weights
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With exact expert offload enabled, prefill currently reloads every expert from host memory into one shared full-layer pool and waits for each transfer batch. This change reuses resident expert weights through device-to-device copies, coalesces contiguous physical copies within each source allocation, and prefetches the next layer into a second reusable pool. Load-completion and last-reader events protect both pools. Before decode can update resident slots, pending prefetches are drained; on returning to prefill, pending graph callbacks are fenced once before reading residency. Captured decode graphs therefore do not disable the prefill pipeline. Failed transfers invalidate the affected pool, and failed MoE execution does not launch the next prefetch. Batch-phase handling uses the existing `expert_offload_utils.prepare_batch` extension point; no additional model-runner hook or model-specific branch is introduced. Decode capacity overflow retains the synchronous full-layer fallback, and native expert layouts, routing, and target/draft separation are preserved. The existing uniform-decode graph capacity filtering is unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. When `expert_offload_config.enabled` is true on Ascend 950 (A5), prefill and mixed batches use two full-layer expert buffers. This reserves **one additional complete expert layer**, including weights, scales, and native padding, compared with the previous single-buffer implementation. Both pools are included in model memory accounting before KV-cache sizing.

title: [Performance] Vectorise the A3 HiSparse resolver union and merge the emit pass
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On Ascend A3 (arch 220) the HiSparse resolver falls back to its scalar path as soon as one selected token is cold. One AI core owns a whole request group and walks its 4 x 2048 tokens three times — union, miss ordering, publish — translating every token on each pass with two page-table loads. At the production shape that is ~3.4 ms per call, 47.6% of the decode iteration span, with only 0.4% of it overlapping compute. The cost is instruction count, not bandwidth: one scalar access on A3 costs ~20 ns whether it hits UB or GM, and the request needs ~86k of them. Vectorising the data movement does nothing by itself (moving the page tables into UB measured 6.6% and 8.2% *slower*); the win comes from issuing far fewer instructions. This PR ports three changes onto the aclnn-resident kernel. All of them live in `csrc/attention/hisparse_resolve_residency/op_kernel/arch22/hisparse_resolver_kernel.h`; no other product file changes. 1. **Translate once.** The union pass stores each cold host id into the output buffer (which is not written until publish), so the miss-ordering and publish passes read it back instead of re-reading the page tables. Page-table scalar loads drop 3x. 2. **Vectorise what is independent.** Both page rows are DMA'd into UB once per request; each 256-token tile is then translated with `Gather`/`Shift`/`Compare`/`Select` and compacted with `GatherMask`, so only real cold tokens reach the serial hash insert. title: [Performance] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 indexer K cache writes and C2 RMSNorm
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 currently publishes indexer K through separate RMSNorm, partial RoPE, dynamic INT8 quantization, and K/scale cache scatter operations. Its ratio-2 compressor also normalizes pooled output in a separate operation. These intermediate operations add kernel launches and global-memory traffic to the compressed-source path. This PR introduces two Triton epilogue fusions: - **Indexer K publication:** fuse RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, per-token INT8 quantization, and direct writes to the paged K and FP16 scale caches. The `wk` projection remains a separate GEMM. - **C2 pooling:** optionally apply RMSNorm inside the token-aligned pooling kernel, preserving the BF16 pooling-output boundary before normalization. FP32 ring-state updates retain their existing ordering. The indexer kernel preserves the BF16 boundary between RMSNorm and RoPE, quantizes using an FP32 scale, and stores the dequantization scale in FP16. It respects physical cache strides and skips invalid physical slots. Valid output slots must remain unique. The fused indexer path targets ordinary A2/A3 INT8 caches. A5 packed/folded cache publication and indexer Norm with a loaded bias retain the existing path. The C2 compressor also retains separate normalization when its Norm has a loaded bias, so that the bias is applied. The intended benefit is fewer launches and intermediate memory accesses. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [RFC]: Partial-block prefix caching as the default path for every KV cache group
summary: ### Motivation. - Groups in a hybrid model want different block sizes. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS storage rank derivation with pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Overview `HF3FSKVConnector` uses the TP rank alone as its storage rank. With pipeline parallelism, workers of different stages that share a TP rank write the same data file (`hf3fs_vllm_data_file_<rank>`) and register as the same metadata rank, although they hold different layers. This PR lets a request name a namespace: its routed experts are written once to a shared Mooncake object store, one immutable object per KV span, and the final output lists the keys instead of the rows. Any process that can reach the store reads them. Requests without a namespace keep the inline behavior, unchanged. Object delivery works with the default configuration on full-attention, sliding-window hybrid, Mamba/linear-attention hybrid and loop models, with speculative decoding and with an external KV tier (support matrix below). This PR is self-contained on `main`. It composes with #62920 (per-reque

title: [Kernel] Allow steering the unquantized linear backend independently
summary: ## Purpose `--linear-backend` is consumed by two selectors: the quantized kernel picker in `model_executor/kernels/linear`, and `dispatch_unquantized_gemm` for unquantized layers. Setting it to reach the second also redirects the first, which on a mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint was a net loss in our measurements even though the unquantized layers themselves improved. ## Changes Adds `--unquantized-linear-backend` / `KernelConfig.unquantized_linear_backend`, which overrides the backend for `UnquantizedLinearMethod` only. title: [Metrics][SpecDecode] Add draft-logits NaN statistics aligned with the verifier's read set
summary: ## What does this PR do? Extend the sampler NaN statistics to the **draft logits**, restricted to the read set of the speculative-decoding verifier. The existing probe (`VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` -> `get_num_nans`, reported per request as `num_nans_in_logits`) only covers the target side; this PR adds `get_num_draft_nans` and plumbs `num_draft_nans` alongside `num_nans` through the existing chain (`SamplerOutput` -> `ModelRunnerOutput` -> `EngineCoreOutput.num_draft_nans_in_logits`), gated by the same flag. ## Why is it needed? With speculative decoding, an acceptance collapse can come from either side: the target verification logits or the draft proposals. The current statistics are blind to the draft side, so a production failure cannot be attributed -- a real incident on DeepSeek V4.

title: [RL][Weight Transfer] Add sparse_disk backend for sparse deltas through storage
summary: ## Overview Adds `sparse_disk`, a weight transfer backend for sparse weight deltas published through storage, for trainers that cannot share an NCCL group with inference or that feed many replicas. title: [Core] Add cache_salt_start_idx for divergence-point prefix-cache salting
summary: ## [Core] Divergence-point prefix-cache salting: `cache_salt_start_idx` ### Motivation `cache_salt` today is all-or-nothing. A salted request isolates its **entire** block-hash chain, so two tenants on the same deployment never share a single cached block — even when their prompts begin with the same thousands of tokens (shared system prompts, RAG preambles, agent scaffolds). That is the all-or-nothing tradeoff documented in "Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference" ([arXiv:2608.09225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09225)), which proposes salting only from the point where prompts diverge. title: [Bugfix] Exclude the compilation peak from memory profiling
summary: ## Purpose Closes #54122. On a cold start `torch.compile` and Inductor autotuning run inside `profile_run()`, which sits inside the `memory_profiling()` window. With AOT compile, `decorators.py` already splits the two phases into separate `with` blocks, and `monitor_profiling_run()` asserts compilation is finished before the profiling forward begins, but nothing clears the allocator high-water mark between them. Compilation's temporaries are freed before that forward, so `transient_peak_headroom` counts them as activation memory and the KV cache shrinks until the compile cache is warm. This drops the high-water mark when compilation finishes.
