title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] gfx942 large-step MoE for decode steps above the mono limit
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under `--monokernel` on gfx942 runs decode steps of up to 42 rows (7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts) in the mono decode layer (#60731, #67540), and larger steps fall back to vLLM's MoE, which reads every routed expert's weights once per pass of rows. This PR runs the MoE block of 43- to 256-row decode steps as a grouped GEMM over groups of 16 picks of one expert (the design of #65421 for gfx950, here in FlyDSL for gfx942), so each expert's weights are read once per 16 picks. title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Grouped QSA indexer scorer for MTP verify rows
summary: ## Purpose With MTP, every decode request sends 1 + k query rows to the QSA indexer, and they all score the same compressed keys. The current kernels score each row on its own, so each key tile is loaded 1 + k times. This PR adds a grouped kernel for verify batches. One program takes the rows of one request, loads each key tile once, scores all rows and index heads with one `tl.dot`, then sums the heads with a second small dot. Scores differ from the tiled kernel only in the order of the fp32 sums. It is used only when the batch has no prefill rows and every decode request has the same row count (2 to 8), with bf16 or fp16 keys. title: [Feature][Quantization]: Add 2-bit Kitty KV quantization with dynamic precision boosting.
summary: # tl;dr This PR adds support for Kitty KV-cache quantization to vLLM through `--kv-cache-dtype kitty` and a dedicated attention backend. Kitty reduces KV-cache memory usage by quantizing values and most key channels to 2 bits, while dynamically boosting selected key channels to 4 bits. It retains attention sink tokens and recent tokens in the model's original precision to help preserve accuracy during long-context generation. The implementation is based on the [original Kitty paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18643) and the authors' [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Summer-Summer/Kitty). To test it out, serve one of the following models: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --kv-cache-dtype kitty vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B --kv-cache-dtype kitty vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --kv-cache-dty

title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #68725. When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks. That ordering is the bug: - A host prefix hit needs the GPU indexer blocks; a copy only speeds up a hit that also finds them. - A long request leaves about 1 indexer block and several resident copies per page. - Later requests' copies therefore outlive earlier prefixes' indexer blocks, and re-sent prompts miss far below host-pool capacity. The fix adds a retained tier to `BlockPool`, a second free queue. title: [Perf][Spec Decode] DSpark: run the Markov walk in one kernel with int8 W2 on chip (Hopper)
summary: ## Overview DSpark walks its draft block left to right: each step adds `W2 @ W1[prev]` to the base logits (W2 is V x 256) and then takes the argmax or a sample. Today every draft token is a full-vocab GEMV, an add and a sampler, and W2 (78 MB in bf16 at V = 151936) is read from HBM again on every step. This adds `dspark_markov_quantization="int8"` to the speculative config. With it, sm_90 runs the whole walk in one cooperative kernel. W2 is quantized to int8 with one fp32 scale per row, most of it stays in shared memory across all SMs and the rest streams from L2, and the per-step argmax across CTAs goes through one atomic {key, count} pair. title: [Bug]: Triton fp32 -> FP8 (e4m3) casts round twice on SM89 (Ada): FP8 KV cache and NVFP4 emulation store values one e4m3 step off
summary: ### 🐛 Describe the bug On SM89 (Ada: L4, L40S, RTX 40xx), a Triton cast from fp32 to `tl.float8e4nv` rounds twice, so about 0.4% of fp32 inputs end up one e4m3 step away from the round-to-nearest-even result. For example 3.1259 is stored as 3.0; torch and SM90+ give 3.25. This affects every vLLM Triton kernel that quantizes an fp32 value to e4m3 on these GPUs, including the FP8 KV cache store of `TRITON_ATTN`. **Cause.** Triton 3.8.0 (what vLLM's CUDA build gets with torch 2.14.0) uses the direct PTX conversion only from SM90. title: [Bugfix] Fall back from DeepGEMM on SM12x when nvcc is older than 13.0
summary: ## Overview DeepGEMM's SM120 kernels refuse to compile below CUDA 13. vLLM, however, only requires nvcc 12.9 before it selects DeepGEMM (#60438). So on SM12x GPUs (RTX 50, RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark) with a CUDA 12.9 toolkit, block FP8 models abort engine init. This PR raises the nvcc floor to 13.0 on the 12.x family, so that selection falls back the same way #60438 does on Hopper. ## Claims - Block FP8 models now load and serve on SM12x with nvcc 12.9. title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
summary: ### Motivation. Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side. Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. title: [Metrics] Add `vllm:kv_cache_token_usage_perc`
summary: ## Purpose `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` counts blocks. That is the right unit for scheduling — blocks are the allocation unit — but it is not the right unit for judging how much of the KV cache actually holds keys and values. A block holding one token is indistinguishable from a full one, so with short prompts the reported figure can be nearly double the real occupancy, and an operator has no way to see it. Concretely, on `facebook/opt-125m` with `--block-size 16` and a saturating stream of 17-token prompts, the existing gauge reads a median of **66.7%** while only **36.5%** of the token slots hold anything — a 30-point gap that is invisible today. With 400-token prompts on the same server the two agree to within 1.2 points, so the gap is a property of the workload shape, not a constant tax.

title: [Perf][Inkling2-Mini] Improve small M GEMM on 5090 (sm120)
summary: ## Overview Three decode-time improvements to Inkling2's SM12x low-M (M <= 16) BF16 GEMM from #69028 (`ops/gemv.py`, now `ops/ll_gemm_sm120.py` as `sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm`): 1. **Split-K for narrow outputs.** When there are too few column tiles to fill the GPU, the kernel splits K, deterministically. The short-conv projection (N=32) now uses it instead of `F.linear`: **up to 7.1×** faster. 2. **Batched GEMM for the loop blend.** A 3D weight runs a batched matmul, replacing the blend's two `torch.bmm` calls: **up to 5.1×** faster. 3. **Fused q/k/v projection.** `qkv_bmm` computes q, k and v, each from its own input, in one launch instead of three: **1.2×** faster. End to end on RTX 5090, decode steps are **6.5–7.5% faster** (`vllm bench serve`, DSpark). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used. ##

title: [Kernel][Perf] Do not split rows no longer than k in `top_k_per_row_decode`
summary: ## Overview When the logits are at least 200,000 wide, `top_k_per_row_decode` spends about 120 µs on a decode row no longer than k, although the result is just the row's own indices. In a small batch, a row of 2–4K tokens takes about 50 µs. The call ends with its slowest row, so one such short row slows the whole batch. This PR lets rows no longer than k skip the split and the merge, which brings them to about 5 µs. This matters for Mistral Large 4 on MI325X, which uses this kernel at its default 262,144 context with k = 2048: - A request takes this path while its prompt plus generated tokens are at most 2,048. title: [RFC]: Scheduler-owned persistent state, initially for cache-aware streaming RNN-T ASR
summary: ## Motivation. This RFC proposes support for stateful, cache-aware streaming RNN-T models such as [NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 ASR](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b), requested in [Issue #47455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47455). These models process potentially indefinite audio streams, so they need to carry acoustic and decoder state between chunks without letting memory grow with the recording. That state includes encoder attention and convolution caches, predictor state, and decoding progress. To support these models, vLLM needs to preserve each session’s GPU state while batching computation across ready sessions and returning incremental results through its existing serving system. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix handshake metadata key collision across PCP ranks
summary: ## Overview Fix KV connector handshake failures when using `MultiConnector` with PCP > 1 and DCP = 1. Workers with the same PP and TP ranks report metadata under the same key, so one PCP rank’s report can overwrite another’s before `MultiConnector` distributes the metadata to its sub-connectors. This can discard NIXL’s handshake metadata and cause P/D requests to fail. This PR preserves each worker’s metadata using `(pp_rank, pcp_rank, tp_rank)` keys, then splits the reports by sub-connector before converting them to the existing handshake keys. title: [Roadmap] Rust Frontend Feature Parity
summary: ## Motivation The Rust frontend has landed in the vLLM repository as a drop-in alternative to the Python API server process. It is enabled through `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and uses the existing vLLM engine/core boundary. The Rust frontend is still experimental and not yet feature-complete relative to the Python frontend. This roadmap prioritizes user value and the Rust frontend's architectural goals over blanket 1:1 parity with the Python frontend. title: [RFC]: UltraQuant: the scale constant c = 0.156 is MSE-optimal before the UE8M0 snap, not after; c ≈ 0.2 cuts KV-quantization KL by 40–56% at no cost
summary: ### Motivation. `ultraquant_4bit` picks each group's UE8M0 scale as ``` s_raw = c * absmax(group) # c = 0.156 (DEFAULT_CONSTANT_C, vllm/v1/attention/ops/ultraquant/format.py) s = 2^round(log2(s_raw)) # UE8M0 snap ``` The constant is documented as "MSE-optimal; `s_raw = c * absmax`, then UE8M0-snapped". That holds before the snap. c = 0.156 minimizes the E2M1 reconstruction error for a **continuous** scale s = c·absmax. But the stored scale is the snapped power of two. Snapping moves absmax/s anywhere within a factor √2, and erring toward clipping costs more than erring toward coarseness. So for the snapped scale the MSE optimum moves up, to **c ≈ 0.19–0.20**. At c = 0.156, about a third more reconstruction error is left on the table, on synthetic data and on real K/V alike. For reference,

title: [Bugfix] Keep KV-cache scale defaults under dummy loading
summary: ## Purpose With `load_format=dummy`, the dummy loader writes random values into the attention KV-cache scales. A checkpoint without KV-cache scales never overwrites them, so after a dummy start and a weight sync (the usual RL startup) the engine still differs from a real start. summary: ## Purpose EAGLE-style speculation (including MTP) cannot reuse the KV of the last matched block: the drafter runs one token ahead of the verified prefix, so `KVCacheCoordinator` drops one drop-unit off every affected group's prefix-cache hit. title: [Bugfix][Model] Reuse CUDA segments when loading Inkling expert weights
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #51205. The NVIDIA Inkling w13 loader dropped the previous CUDA scratch tensor before allocating the next one. While `GPUWorker.load_model()` applies `max_split_size_mb=20`, this leaves fully free 20 MiB allocator segments that cannot satisfy the next smaller upload. CUDA reserved memory therefore grows while allocated memory remains flat, which can exhaust lower-memory GPUs or livelock the loader in allocator retries. This change chains the CPU `narrow()` view and `.to(param.device)` operation so the previous CUDA tensor remains alive until the next allocation completes. The tensor layout and destination copies are unchanged. Thanks to @brocktice for documenting the allocator interaction and suggested fix in [this issue comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues

title: [RFC]: LoRA adapter support for DFlash speculative decoding draft models
summary: ### Motivation. vLLM supports serving many LoRA adapters over a single base target model, but speculative decoding still requires a separate, fully-trained draft model per domain. When serving many domains, this is expensive: each domain needs its own drafter (e.g. 0.8B) held in memory, with corresponding I/O cost to load and swap. This RFC proposes applying LoRA adapters to the DFlash drafter, so a single base drafter can be specialized per-domain via small adapters instead of full drafters. In our experiments an R64 adapter is ~28x smaller than the 0.8B drafter it replaces, substantially reducing memory footprint and I/O latency when serving many domains, while keeping drafter quality within ~2% of a fully-trained per-domain drafter (measured by acceptance length behavior). title: [Bug]: Triton MoE and block-FP8 GEMMs mishandle the K tile — an out-of-bounds weight read, and wrong scales when a tile spans two quantization groups
summary: ## Summary Two Triton GEMMs used by quantized MoE serving get the K tile wrong, and in both cases a sibling code path already does it correctly. 1. **`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` reads the packed weights out of bounds.** The kernel builds `k_mask` whenever `K` is not a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and applies it to the scale load and to *both* zero-point loads, but the weight load itself is unmasked, so the last K iteration reads past the end of the weight tensor. The sibling `fused_moe_kernel` masks the identical load. The numbers that come back are multiplied by a scale that *is* masked to zero, so the arithmetic result is unaffected — this is a memory-safety bug, not a numerical one. 2. **`w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` can pick one scale for a tile that spans several quantization groups.**

title: [Performance][ROCm] gfx1100 long-prefill: unified attention BLOCK_M=16 default leaves ~2x on the table; BLOCK_M=64 gives 1.1-1.3x TTFT on latest main
summary: ## Summary On RDNA3 (gfx1100 / RX 7900 XTX), the unified Triton attention kernel (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py`, TRITON_ATTN backend) is configured with `BLOCK_M=16` for every GQA model with `num_queries_per_kv <= 16`. For long prefill (8k tokens) this leaves the kernel at roughly half its achievable throughput. Raising the query block to `BLOCK_M=64` (`BLOCK_Q=8` for `nq_per_kv=7`, `BLOCK_Q=16` for `nq_per_kv=4`) improves prefill TTFT by **1.1-1.3x** across 4 models and 3 quantization regimes on latest main, with bitwise-identical outputs and no decode regression. ## Data (in=8192, same-process interleaved A/B, min of 2 reps, greedy first-token correctness) | Model | Quant | nq/kv | wall baseline (BLOCK_M=16) | wall BQ=8 | speedup | correctness | |---|---|---:|---:|-

summary: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Currently `LoRARequest.lora_scale` is fixed at request creation and baked into the CUDA graph / kernel as a scalar. This prevents: - same-adapter requests in one batch from using different strengths; - adjusting LoRA strength mid-generation. title: [Core] Make the shm message-queue busy-wait window configurable
summary: ## Purpose `SpinCondition` busy-waits for `busy_loop_s` after each read before parking on its zmq notification socket, hardcoded to `1`. This makes that window configurable via `VLLM_SHM_BROADCAST_BUSY_LOOP_S` and **keeps the default at `1`**, so behaviour is unchanged for every existing deployment. The right value is a property of the hardware, not of vLLM. On a discrete-GPU server the current default is a good trade: a spinning core is thermal noise and the saved wake-up is free latency. On packages where the CPU and GPU share one power and thermal budget, it is not — the core held at max clock is taken out of the GPU's headroom. summary: ### Motivation. Two related changes are proposed for KV connector save paths: 1. summary: # [RFC]: Internal State Checkpoints for Mamba Align Mode ## Motivation. `mamba_cache_mode="align"` stores recurrent states at reusable Mamba block boundaries. title: [ROCm][Perf] Tune Triton W4A16 dense GEMM tiles for gfx90a (104 CUs)
summary: ## Purpose — why this change exists The Triton W4A16 dense GEMM's tile table routes gfx90a into its **MI300 branch, tuned for 304 CUs**. An MI210 has 104. At decode widths that starves the card: with `BLOCK_N=64`, a narrow-N layer launches only **80–96 workgroups onto 104 CUs** — fewer than one per CU — while the SMs sit idle. Shrinking `BLOCK_N` for the gfx90a narrow shapes raises that to 320–384 workgroups and lets the card actually fill. This is the same class of issue as any large-SI tile table being reused for a small-SI part: the dispatch is legal, so nothing fails — the kernel just runs at a fraction of the achievable rate and nobody notices. ## Measured (2× AMD MI210, gfx90a, wall clock over the production `triton_w4a16_gemm`) | shape | M | stock | tuned | speedup | |---|---|---|--

title: [Kernel][ROCm] Partition the cached-context scan for short-query attention (spec-decode verify)
summary: ## Purpose `context_attention_fwd` launches `_fwd_kernel` with a grid of `(batch, head, cdiv(max_input_len, BLOCK_M))`. When the query is short but the cached context is long, that third dimension collapses to **1**, and each program scans the entire context serially. title: [RFC]: [Spec decode] KV-cache pool collapse when a draft model introduces a new cache spec type (hybrid GDN + DFlash): diagnosis, mitigation dead-ends, and a working dedicated-draft-pool POC
summary: ### Motivation. The unified hybrid KV-cache pool assumes that all attention layers can be grouped by their KV-cache spec type and that **every request draws blocks from every group**. This assumption breaks when a speculative-decoding draft model registers attention layers whose spec type no target layer has: the draft's spec type fragments grouping, inflates per-request block demand, and the scheduler's usable KV pool collapses — even though the draft itself needs very little memory. We hit this end-to-end with a real deployment: a 27B hybrid model (48 linear-attention/GDN layers + 16 full-attention layers) served with a DFlash draft (`num_speculative_tokens=7`) whose 5 attention layers are sliding-window (window 2048, non-causal). title: [Bugfix][Prefix Caching] Keep hybrid evictions on a prefix every KV cache group can hit
summary: ## Overview A hybrid prefix hit needs every KV cache group, but a finished request's blocks enter the LRU free queue one group at a time, so pool pressure evicts one group's head while the other groups' blocks stay cached and can never be hit. title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Dequantize ModelOpt 4-D FP8 block scales in DequantLinearMethod
summary: ## Overview `DequantLinearMethod` (#66118) runs a projection that the checkpoint stores in FP8 in BF16. title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Inkling: zero CUDA-graph padding rows in decode attention
summary: ## Overview With `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs, Inkling on ROCm can hit a GPU memory fault in `fused_moe_kernel` once a few requests decode concurrently (`--enforce-eager` avoids it). Decode graphs are replayed at fixed batch sizes, so 3 live requests run in the batch-4 graph with one padding row. That row has `cache_seqlens` 0 and belongs to no request, but its attention output flows through the residual into the MoE gate, and two paths can leave NaN there. A NaN gate logit can make top-k return an index past the routed experts. Related: #61413 (open) moves this code to `inkling/common/`; both bugs are still in its version, and we are happy to rebase onto it or have it fold this in. ## Claims - Split-KV decode: `_split_kv_stage2` combines zero splits for an empty row and stores `acc / ro

title: [HiSparse] Store one copy of the offloaded indexer across TP ranks
summary: ## What changes With HiSparse and an `OffloadingConnector` (which offloads only the indexer cache) on a single node with TP > 1, the CPU tier now stores **one** copy of the indexer cache shared by all TP ranks, instead of one copy per rank. The bytes are identical on every rank, so at TP4 this cuts the tier's host memory by 4× for the same capacity. Why it happened: the shared-copy layout requires every KV cache group to be TP-replicated. HiSparse's resident and hot GPU page groups are raw pages with no TP metadata, so the check always failed. Those groups are never offloaded, so the check now looks only at the groups that are. title: [RFC]: Fault-tolerant sharded RDT weight sync: continue on surviving inference engines
summary: ### Motivation. With the sharded RDT weight-transfer backend (as redesigned on the load plan in #68038, part of #64418), one failed inference engine fails the weight sync for every engine. An engine crash fails the round within seconds. A lost RPC fails it only after the 300 s HTTP timeout or stall watchdog. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Stop P/D transfers short of the last prompt token
summary: ## Purpose P/D decode recomputes the last prompt token. NIXL and Mooncake load all N prompt tokens and the scheduler then rewinds one token, but by then every group was laid out for position N. For a sliding window, prefill and decode both drop the block holding position N - W whenever N % block_size == block_size - 1, so the recomputed token N - 1 attends to the null block. With a zeroed null block this silently perturbs one window position for 1/block_size of requests; on DeepSeek-V4.1, whose null block is not zero, it corrupts the output (NaN logits at 1023/4095/8191 tokens, reported in #59197). title: [Quantization] Keep E8M0 scale bytes when loading into uint8 params
summary: ## Purpose Part of #64418 (tracker item L6). Builds on #65235 (P1, load plan). MX scale parameters (compressed-tensors MXFP4/MXFP8, ModelOpt MXFP8, Quark OCP-MX, INC MXFP4/MXFP8) are `uint8`, and their loaders end in `copy_weight_`. When the source is `float8_e8m0fnu`, `copy_` converts it by value (2^(b-127) cast to an integer), which stores wrong scales. Under the load plan the same copy is a cast, so the name falls back, and the fallback stores the same wrong bytes. With this PR, `copy_weight_` copies between any two different **byte containers** as bytes (`src.view(dst.dtype)`). The parameter then holds the sent bytes, and because the load plan sees a view, the names are direct. title: [RFC]: Data integrity and I/O liveness for the filesystem KV offload tier
summary: ### Motivation. title: [Perf][V2] Pool AsyncOutput's D2H copy events instead of creating them every step
summary: ## Overview Pool the CUDA events that the V2 model runner's `AsyncOutput` creates every step to order and complete its D2H copy. #39115 fixed a race from reusing one copy event across steps by creating a new event every step, and noted the events could be pooled later if needed. This PR is that pool. It is safe against the same race because an event pair goes back to the pool only after `get_output()` has synchronized on it. Why it matters: these are driver calls on the execute-model thread. When another thread in the process holds the CUDA driver lock for a long time, for example a KV connector posting many CUDA IPC copies from a background thread, these calls wait behind it. summary: ## Motivation DSA-style sparse attention (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4.1) selects the top-k keys for each prefill row from indexer scores over all visible keys. title: [RFC] feat(scheduler): implement Shortest Remaining Prefill First (SRPF) policy with starvation aging
summary: ### Summary Implements Shortest Remaining Prefill First (SRPF) scheduling with dynamic starvation aging in the v1 engine core. In mixed workloads, heavy prompt ingestion (e.g. multi-turn context or RAG prompts with 7k+ tokens) causes head-of-line (HoL) blocking under FCFS: long prefills are chunked across consecutive iterations, forcing short interactive requests arriving behind them to queue for seconds. title: [ROCm][DSA] Enable the DCP global-key indexer prefill by default

title: [Perf][MoE] Select full-warp top-k rows with redux.sync and keep selections in registers (SM80+)
summary: ## Overview `topkGating` (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu`) gives each row to one full warp when the row is wide enough (512 experts, 256 experts with 16-bit logits, 128-512 experts with fp32 logits). For each of the k selections it runs a 5-stage shuffle butterfly with 3 dependent shuffles per stage, then lane 0 stores the selection and later re-reads the weights to scale them. title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Tile whole kernel rows of groups to persist logical block for drafter blocks
summary: ## Overview Claude and I hit this while benchmarking P/D for Kimi K3 with its DSpark draft model on GB300. Every engine that loaded `NixlConnector` died at startup in `register_kv_caches`, on every topology we tried, including a plain 1P1D TP4 -> TP4 with no DCP. summary: ## Overview Related: #60844. title: [Bugfix][Core] Redo prompt logprobs for requests resumed after reset_prefix_cache
summary: ## Overview Fixes #61490. Active `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` exposed two opposite redo-state errors: resuming before a dropped output arrived could leave prompt-logprob rows unwritten, while resetting after a complete output was emitted could recompute and append a duplicate block. title: [Spec Decode] Fix Dspark adaptive verification cost model
summary: ## Summary Adaptive verification picks, every step, the draft budget `b` that maximises ``` expected accepted tokens(b) / step cost(b) step cost(b) = drafter cost + base + (price of b draft slots) ``` The argmax depends only on how the slot price compares with the base. title: [RFC]: Replicate selected blocks across TP ranks for tensor parallelism over slow inter-node links
summary: ### Motivation Tensor parallelism across nodes linked by commodity Ethernet (25 GbE RoCE between workstations or DGX Spark-class boxes) pays one all-reduce per block per step. At decode batch sizes that all-reduce is latency-bound: we measured about 66 us for TP4 and 36-40 us for TP2 over 25 GbE at batch 1 (inside a CUDA graph), against 2-3 us on one PCIe node. That is the same order as reading a mixer's weights from HBM, so for some blocks it is cheaper to keep the block whole on every rank (replicate it) and skip its all-reduce than to shard it. Replicating a block costs each rank (1 - 1/TP) x W extra bytes of resident weights and of reads per step, and saves one all-reduce. title: [Bug] [Diffusion] Host pin budget OOM-kills MiniMax-H3 on a 24 GB GPU + 32 GB host; server still reports ready and returns 503
summary: ### Describe the bug On an RTX 4090 (24 GB) with host memory capped at 32 GiB, the default MiniMax-H3 command dies during the synthetic server warmup. The cookbook 24 GB recipe dies the same way. What happens: - The scheduler worker is OOM-killed by the cgroup (`memory.events: oom_kill 1`). - The server logs `Synthetic server warmup failed; continuing startup`, then serves `/v1/models` normally. - Every `POST /v1/videos` returns `503 Service Unavailable`. Nothing in the log says the worker was OOM-killed. At the moment of the kill, the cgroup held about 12–14 GiB anon plus **19.5–19.6 GiB shmem**, which is the full 32 GiB. The shmem is the layerwise-offload pinned store: `layerwise_offload._shared_storage` → `memfd_create("sglang-pinned-store")`. Without swap the kernel cannot reclaim it.

title: [Fix] qwen4-exp: Scale BF16 PLE shards before FP8 storage
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #49493. When a checkpoint sets `ple_embedding_dtype="float8_e4m3fn"` but stores BF16 PLE shards, the loader casts them to FP8 with scale=1. title: [Bug] bootstrap_room fan-out wraps in the Rust worker but not in Python (io_struct) — mixed PD legs can disagree on the rendezvous room near i64::MAX
summary: ## Summary When a scalar `bootstrap_room` is fanned out over a batch, the Rust worker and the Python worker use different arithmetic: the Rust worker fans out with `wrapping_add` (i64 wrap-around), while Python uses arbitrary-precision addition (never wraps). For rooms near `i64::MAX` the two frontends therefore derive **different room values for the same request**, which breaks the documented PD rendezvous contract ("both legs receive the same `bootstrap_room`") in deployments that mix a Rust-server leg with a Python leg. summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With DP attention, every scheduler gathers with all the others once per step (the MLP-sync gather), so a pause on any one rank stalls every rank at the next gather. title: [Bug] dsv41: Candidate graph variants can differ across attention-DP ranks (decode and DSpark verify)
summary: ## Problem Under DP attention the ranks replay their CUDA/HIP graphs in lockstep, and some collectives captured in them (custom all-reduce, aiter all-gather / reduce-scatter) register that graph's input buffers. If two ranks replay different graph variants in the same step, a rank reads its peer's buffer from the other graph, which holds stale data. `Dsv41CandidateGraphVariants` (DeepSeek-V4.1, SM100+ and gfx95) still selects from each rank's own lengths: - Decode: ranks holding different requests can pick different candidates; an idle rank has no lengths and takes `candidate_filtered`. - DSpark target verify: busy ranks select from their committed lengths plus `verify_extra_tokens`. title: [Bug] radix_eviction_policy=priority ignores --schedule-low-priority-values-first, evicting highest-priority prefixes first
summary: ### Describe the bug `--radix-eviction-policy priority` always evicts the prefix with the **smallest** `node.priority` first, regardless of the priority direction set by `--schedule-low-priority-values-first`. Under that flag (lower value = higher priority), the eviction order is inverted: the prefixes of the **highest-priority** requests are evicted first. Every other priority consumer honors the direction flag: | Consumer | Direction handling | |---|---| | Waiting-queue sorting (`schedule_policy.py`) | ✅ `priority_sign` | | PD decode queue sorting (`disaggregation/decode.py`) | ✅ `priority_sign` | | Queue-limit eviction (`scheduler.py` `_abort_on_queued_limit`) | ✅ `direction` | | KV retraction `retraction_policy=priority` (`schedule_batch.py`) | ✅ `-priority_sign` (incl. None sentinel)

title: [Fix] marlin: keep one block per SM in the MoE kernel
summary: Fixes #44999. ## Motivation `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` intermittently returns wrong rows on pre-Hopper GPUs. Reported by #44999 on sm86; reproduced here on sm89 (RTX 4090) with synthetic AWQ W4A16 MoE weights (E=128, K=2048, N=768, group 128, topk 8): 4-6% of probe launches differ from the majority output, 3-4 of 64 tokens are wrong (|delta| up to 5.0) and every other row is bit-identical. The Triton WNA16 path is exact, which is how the report distinguishes it from a numerics issue. `determine_exec_config()` sizes the launch by an occupancy estimate (`allow_count`), so the kernel can run two or three blocks per SM. The split-K reduction chains those blocks through a global lock array (`barrier_acquire`/`barrier_release`), and that chain is only correct with a single resident block per SM. ##

title: [Fix] attention: Keep shared-KV verify split partials in FP32
summary: ## Motivation The shared-KV verify kernel in `verify_mla.py` stores each split's partial output (`Att_Out`) in BF16 and merges the splits afterwards. When the splits cancel each other out, the true result is a small residual, and the rounding before the merge can be as large as that residual. summary: ## Motivation In deterministic mode, Triton decode attention gets much slower than in normal mode as the batch grows: on MI350X, gpt-oss-20b reaches 0.33x of normal-mode throughput at 64 concurrent requests and 0.21x at 256. title: [Feat] scheduler: Allow lpm with priority scheduling
summary: ## Motivation `--enable-priority-scheduling` only works with `--schedule-policy fcfs` or `lof`; startup rejects every other policy. A deployment that serves several priority classes therefore has to give up prefix-cache-aware ordering. That costs the most when many requests of the same class wait at once, for example agentic multi-turn sessions with 100k-token contexts. FCFS then admits requests of one class in arrival order, they evict each other's prefixes, and every miss is paid back as recomputed prefill. This PR allows `lpm` with priority scheduling. Requests are ordered by priority first, then by longest cached prefix within a priority. ## Modifications - `validation_hook.py`: `lpm` is accepted with `--enable-priority-scheduling`. - `SchedulePolicy._sort_lpm_with_priority`: - sorts t

title: [Perf] hicache: Fence write_back eviction copies on the forward stream instead of blocking the scheduler
summary: ## Motivation With HiCache `write_back`, the device eviction walk backs its victims up to host and then blocks the scheduler on `Event.synchronize()` for those D2H copies before it demotes the victims. The copies are fenced behind the in-flight forward (`write_fence_stream`), so on a busy prefill server the scheduler cannot finish building the next batch until the current forward ends. title: [Feat] [Apple] mps: Add eager Gated DeltaNet support for Qwen3.5
summary: ## Motivation Our goal is to serve Qwen3.5 and newer models such as Qwen4 on Apple Silicon through SGLang’s Torch-owned MLX backend. In this design, Torch owns the model weights and per-request state. MLX runs batches that the compiled runner can handle, while eager Torch MPS handles cases such as multi-request prefill or extending a cached prefix. Qwen3.5 interleaves full attention with Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers. Without an eager MPS implementation of GDN, a request that takes the eager path cannot finish its forward pass. This PR fills that gap for dense Qwen3.5 text generation and provides the fallback needed when we add compiled GDN support on top of #42938. ## Modifications - Implement causal convolution and gated delta recurrence in Metal. Its private decode window regrows to about `window + retention` beside the prompt window the tree keeps. - Later passes can therefore admit work into that room. title: [Fix] diffusion: Prevent silent server warmup failures
summary: ## Motivation 1. PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28127 introduced `fail_open=server_args.warmup_resolutions is None`, which silently ignores server warmup failures unless `warmup_resolutions` is explicitly specified. As a result, warmup errors can go unnoticed, allowing CI to pass and the server to be marked ready despite failed warmup generation. The proposed behavior ensures that a server running synthetic warmup is not marked ready when warmup generation fails. Users can still bypass synthetic server warmup with `--warmup-mode off` or use `--warmup-mode request`. 2. This issue was exposed by a recent change that switched MiniMax-H3 to the shared `RMSNorm` custom op on NPU. Unlike `torch.nn.RMSNorm`, this implementation stores epsilon in `variance_epsilon` instead of `eps`.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Settle the in-flight decode result before a PD decode retraction
summary: ## Motivation With overlap scheduling, a PD decode worker can retract a request while the previous decode step's result is still queued. The retraction backs up the request's device state and requeues the request. On resume, the backup is restored and the request decodes from `output_ids`. By the time the backup is taken, the device state has already taken the in-flight step, but `output_ids` has not. Result processing skips retracted requests, so the in-flight step never reaches `output_ids`. The backup and `output_ids` end up one step apart: - **Speculative decoding:** the in-flight verify commits its whole accepted block into KV and draft state. title: [Fix] speculative: Exact sampling penalties and min_new_tokens in DFlash and DSpark verify
summary: ## Motivation DFlash and DSpark verify ignore `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `repetition_penalty` and `min_new_tokens`. Nothing counts the tokens they commit in the penalty tables, and verify reads `acc_linear_penalties`, a field that `SamplingBatchInfo` does not have. So a request with `min_new_tokens` can stop early, and a request with a repetition penalty gets the same logits as one without. This PR counts every committed token and penalizes each verify row as decoding one token at a time would. The results are bitwise equal to non-speculative decoding. ### Penalties in a verify block In each step of chain speculative decoding, the draft model proposes $K$ tokens $d_1, \dots, d_K$. title: [Feat] speculative: Apply exact per-row sampling penalties in verify
summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #52035. Speculative verify scores several draft positions of a request in one forward, but every verify row of a request got the same penalty: the request's history as of the start of the block. A row at draft depth `d` therefore missed the draft tokens before it on its own path, and `min_new_tokens` was off by `d`. With the history now in a per-request device pool, exactness only needs the same formula applied over the pool counts plus each row's ancestor tokens. This replaces #51903: it covers EAGLE trees and NGRAM as well as DFlash and DSpark, it is exact on every device, and it costs less per step. ## Modifications - **Verify kernel** `sampling.verify_penalties` (JIT, CUDA sm_80+), in `kernels/jit/csrc/sampling/verify_penalties.cuh`. - **Semantics:** verify r

summary: ## Motivation Related to #51188 (not a full fix). title: SGLang: stop_regex is evaluated on the scheduler thread, so a crafted regex blocks all decoding for minutes
summary: We previously submitted a private GitHub Security Advisory for this issue: [GHSA-m7xv-579r-jpwr](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/security/advisories/GHSA-m7xv-579r-jpwr). summary: ## Motivation The Rust server's detokenizer shards decode every stream through dynamo-tokenizers' `DecodeStream`, which on each step re-decodes all ids since its last complete text and moves its offsets only when the text grew and does not end in U+FFFD. title: [Feat] logprob: Let a request choose its prompt logprob candidates in place of the top-k
summary: ## Motivation A request that asks for input (prompt) logprobs with `top_logprobs_num = K` gets, at every prompt position, the K most likely tokens. Some consumers of prompt logprobs want a different set of K candidates per position, for example K tokens drawn from the model's next-token distribution at that position, or K tokens fixed by the caller. The choice depends on the logits of the position, so it has to be made where the prompt logprobs are computed, inside `InputLogprobProcessor`, where the row of logits exists; after the forward only the top K is left. This PR adds that hook. It contains no selector: the stock `InputLogprobProcessor` raises `NotImplementedError` when a request carries one, and nothing in this PR sets one, so every request computes exactly what it computed before.

title: [Fix] rl: One tensor weight payload per engine rank under pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Motivation `update_weights_from_tensor` sends one CUDA-IPC payload per TP rank and each scheduler rank reads `serialized_named_tensors[tp_rank]`. With `pp_size > 1`, stage 1's rank r opens the same handle as stage 0's rank r: it gets stage 0's parameters, which it does not own and skips, so later stages are never updated. Two consumers on one IPC handle also break producer-side refcounting (#8203 saw it as OOM). ## Modifications Payloads are now one per engine rank in world-rank order: producers emit `tp_size * pp_size` copies and each rank reads entry `tp_size * pp_rank + tp_rank`. title: [Refactor] graph: Decouple eager_on_graph from CUDA capture (2/3)
summary: ## Motivation SGLang's breakable graph path captures a model forward as a sequence of device graph segments separated by operations that must run eagerly. Model and attention code marks those boundaries with `@eager_on_graph`. At each boundary, SGLang finishes the current captured segment, preserves the eager call's inputs and outputs, records the callback for replay, and starts the next segment. Today, `eager_on_graph` performs those steps by reaching directly into private `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` state. It calls CUDA/XPU-specific segment methods, appends callbacks through `capture.cuda_graph._break_fns`, and applies the current CUDA/XPU tensor-retention policy itself. summary: ## Motivation `GenerateReqInput.input_ids` stays a Python `list[int]` for the whole request, because `ReqState.obj` holds the request until it finishes. summary: ## Motivation #35573 enabled the fused QK-norm and QK-norm+RoPE paths on ROCm, but the kernels behind them still don't build on all models. `elementwise/qknorm.cuh` fails outright, and `diffusion/qknorm_rope.cuh` fails for neox instantiations. In the tail layers, real rows are routed as padding, so they get no routed experts. Cause: 1. `mega_gate_forward_scope` puts a per-forward dict on the `ForwardBatch`, and `_gate_row_masks` caches the valid-row mask (`arange(rows) < num_token_non_padded`) and the image mask in it, keyed by `(rows, id(bound), id(image_input_ids))` ([mega_gate.py#L145-L169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/33a03ba42ee4c6036d75c22e71b9bb8600c79355/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/mega_gate.py#L145-L169)). 2. `RowBucketGraphRunner` captures the tail graphs inside a live forward. The capture batch is a `copy.copy` of the forward batch

title: [Fix] dsv41: Build MegaGate row masks inside the decoder replay-tail graph capture
summary: ## Motivation Fixes #51478. With MegaGate on and EPLB off, the decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs inside a serving forward, after two eager warm-ups of the same layers on a copy of the same batch. The per-forward row-mask cache from #46071 hands the warm-ups' eager masks to the capture, so the mask build is never recorded in the graph. Every replay then reads a valid-row mask computed for the step that captured the graph. Real rows past that count are routed as padding in the tail layers, and prompts whose tail runs from a graph (≤ 2048 tokens here) drift. ## Modifications - `layers/moe/mega_gate.py::_gate_row_masks`: the cache key gains `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`. A capture builds its own masks inside the graph, and the layers it captures still share them;

title: [Perf] Triton MoE is 5–8× slower than flashinfer_cutlass for Nemotron 3 Nano FP8 at TP8 on H100
summary: The default on Hopper is `flashinfer_cutlass`, so default users don't hit this. With `--moe-runner-backend triton`, Nemotron 3 Nano FP8 (ModelOpt per-tensor FP8) at TP8 on 8×H100 decodes 5–8× slower: step time 3.1 → 19.8 ms at batch 16, and 5.7 → 41.3 ms at batch 128. title: [Perf] scheduler: Add SGLANG_DISABLE_THP to turn off transparent huge pages
summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation With transparent huge pages (THP) on, two kernel paths can stop a thread for a long time: - The first write into an eligible region allocates and zeroes a whole huge page in the faulting thread. - khugepaged collapses small pages into huge ones while it holds the process's mmap lock for writing. Every page fault in the process waits behind it. On kernels with 64K base pages, as on Arm servers such as NVIDIA Vera, a PMD huge page is 512 MB, so either path takes tens of milliseconds. With DP attention, every rank then waits at the next gather. We hit this in decode schedulers serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with PD disaggregation on Vera Rubin. title: [Feature] --moe-replicate-tp: replicated MoE with prefill sequence parallelism (Qwen3.5 MoE)
summary: ## Motivation Implements the design in #43820 (revised). For long-prompt prefill on a small TP group, TP pays two costs that grow with the prompt and do not shrink with the TP size: - the all-reduce of the attention / linear-attention output; - the all-reduce of the MoE output. Sequence parallelism alone does not remove them: with TP-sharded experts, the MoE still needs an all-gather plus a reduce-scatter, which moves the same bytes. Replicating the experts does remove them. Each rank keeps its own tokens through the MoE, so the MoE needs no collective at all, and only the attention side keeps one all-gather / reduce-scatter pair. For Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 2 GPUs, full BF16 experts fit in memory (~63 GB per GPU), and the MoE all-reduce was ~half of the prefill communication. ## Modifications

title: [Fix] dspark: Stabilize blockwise rejection sampling under logit shifts
summary: ## Motivation At temperature 1, take draft logits `[-inf, 0, 0, -inf]` and target logits `[-inf, 16, 16, -inf]`. Both assign probability ½ to tokens 1 and 2. title: [Feat] tracing: Record why requests failed, and mark only server faults as errors (OLD)
summary: ## Motivation Traces don't tell a failed request from a normal one, and they mark the wrong things as errors: - A request's root span shows that it finished, but not whether it failed or why: an overloaded server, a rejected prompt and a client abort all look like a normal request. - Every `trace_ctx.abort(abort_info=...)` sets the thread span's status to ERROR, whether the request hit a server fault, was rejected as invalid, or was aborted by its caller. A sampler or alert that keys on error spans counts every bad request and every client disconnect as a server failure. - A request that fails in the tokenizer before reaching the scheduler (invalid input, a LoRA or encoder error) never has its trace ended. With sync tracing its root span is never exported, so rejected requests don't appear

title: [Feat] scheduler: Add UniBoost tail-aware schedule policy with a rank-invariant TP/PP mode
summary: ## Summary This PR adds **UniBoost**, an opt-in tail-aware schedule policy (from *[Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference*, ICML 2026](https://openreview.net/challenge?redirect=%2Fforum%3Fid%3DV40F5O5N85)). Before each prefill admission pass, the waiting queue is re-sorted by a soft priority. Agentic / RL-rollout serving is **prefill-dominated with heavy tails**: in a production SWE-agent trace we measured (7.6k requests), input length p50 is 11.8k tokens vs output p50 of ~90 (≈100:1), turns append a median of 169 tokens of tool output but p99 = 9.1k (test-log dumps), and per-request work varies by two orders of magnitude. title: [Fix] mooncake: Keep a per-request error from killing the prefill transfer worker
summary: ## Motivation Each Mooncake prefill rank shards rooms over `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE` queues (default 4), one transfer worker thread each, keyed by the sum of the decode session ports. When sending one chunk raised, `transfer_worker` failed that room and then raised `Transfer thread failed ... is dead`, and the thread exited. Nothing drains that queue afterwards. Every later request hashed onto it waits out the waiting timeout (300 s) and aborts. Meanwhile the other queues keep producing output, so `/health_generate` keeps returning 200 and nothing restarts the server. We hit this with a multimodal request whose image-token count differed between prefill and decode. title: [Fix] scoring: Correct GDN delimiter state and empty MIS readouts
summary: ## Motivation Multi-item scoring should process each item as an independent continuation of the shared query. This is the behavior requested in [#31969](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31969) and enabled for Qwen3.5 GDN layers by [#33922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33922). The GDN item segments still include their synthetic starting delimiters. Full attention masks those delimiters out, but GDN convolution and recurrent updates consume them before the real item: ```text Packed input: Q | D0 | I1 | D1 | I2 | D2 Current: query-ending state -> D_i -> I_i Expected: query-ending state -> I_i ``` Changing a packing-only delimiter can therefore change an item's score. This follow-up excludes that delimiter from real-item GDN state updates without changing the Score AP

title: [Fix] disaggregation: wait for the prefill forward before sending KV chunks under PP
summary: ## Motivation On a disaggregated prefill server with pipeline parallelism, `process_prefill_chunk` sends the KV of a chunked request's non-final chunk at the start of the next scheduler iteration. At that point the chunk's forward has only been launched on `forward_stream`, and the PP event loop does not wait for it before the page indices are handed to the KV sender. With the default PP comm path and the default `--pp-async-batch-depth 0`, this happens to be safe. summary: ## Motivation With Mamba `extra_buffer` caching and overlap scheduling, the next decode/verify batch can capture `req_to_token` before the previous prefill result publishes its cache insertion. Its query path separately launches Hadamard rotation and FP8 quantization in every DSA layer; dual-stream decode also launches two elementwise operations to apply the head-gate scale. This ports that fusion to `IndexerKPool`. The intended benefit is fewer kernel launches and one fewer BF16 intermediate round-trip, not an end-to-end throughput claim. Component launch profile on MI355X/gfx950: | path | fusion off | fusion on | |---|---:|---:| | prefill | 2 launches | 1 launch | | dual-stream decode | 4 launches | 1 launch | ## Modifications - Add `fused_hadamard_act_quant`, a Triton kernel combining the query-side Walsh-Hadamard transform and block FP8 quantization. - Prese

title: [Perf] [AMD] GLM5: Row-streaming KDA packed decode on gfx950
summary: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA layers use the safe gate (`lower_bound`), so on ROCm their decode skips the packed decode path. It runs `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`, which holds a `[BV, K]` FP32 state tile per program. The recurrent state update is bandwidth-bound on that FP32 state, and this kernel reaches only about 5 TB/s of in-place state traffic on MI355X at decode batch sizes. This change adds a gfx950 Triton kernel that streams the FP32 state in row chunks per (request, head, row group), and routes GLM-5.3's safe-gate layers to the packed decode path on gfx950. CUDA already uses its own row-streaming kernel in this dispatcher; other HIP targets keep their current path. ## Modifications - Add `kda_packed_decode_rowstream`, a gfx950 Triton row-streaming KDA decode kernel

title: [Fix] dsa: Isolate masked KV rows in FP8 TileLang attention
summary: ## Motivation Invalid (`-1`) sparse indices in `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial_fp8` map to KV row 0. Masking the attention score does not isolate that row: a NaN in it can propagate through both QK (`-inf + NaN`) and PV (`0 * NaN`), corrupting otherwise valid outputs and generation logprobs. This was reproduced on GLM-5.3-Flash with FP8 KV and TileLang DSA on H20, with both PP1 and PP2, including a plain-main deployment without EPLB. A direct operator reproduction changed only padding KV row 0 from zero to NaN and changed the output from finite to 196608 NaN elements. This is a correctness fix; it does not require changing the deployment's CUDA Graph, overlap, or speculative decoding settings. summary: ## Motivation `--prefill-decode-interval N` runs N decode rounds after every prefill batch to protect inter-token latency. title: [RFC] Asymmetric P/D deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash
summary: ## Summary This RFC proposes an asymmetric Prefill/Decode deployment for DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash. For a prompt of length `N` and replay window `W = 128`: - The **Prefill worker** processes only the prefix `[0, N-W)` and produces its KV cache. - The **Decode worker** receives that prefix KV and processes the final prompt window `[N-W, N)` as a bounded prefill/replay. - Decode then samples the first output token and continues normal speculative decoding with per-request `q_len = 1 + num_spec_tokens`. The key property is that Decode does not need separate encoder and decoder workloads. summary: ## Motivation Fixes #40320. `_autotune_cache_digest` hashes each rank's whole cache file to decide whether the ranks agree. title: [BugFix] Preserve the DeepSeek-V4.1 MoE cursor during bounded replay
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On a single Ascend A5 node serving prefill and decode together, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GSM8K accuracy rose from **75.22% to 97.38% (+22.16 percentage points)** with this fix. These are three-round means among completed answers. Counting all scheduled questions, the correct-answer share rose from **2,905/3,957 (73.41%) to 3,833/3,957 (96.87%)**. With `fast_moe_cold_start`, each MoE dispatch advances the cursor in the current forward context. Bounded replay creates a new context with a cursor of zero, so in the captured Flash runs decoder layers 21–39 used expert weights from layers 0–18. title: [Performance][MoE] Pipeline prefill expert offload and reuse resident weights
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? With exact expert offload enabled, prefill currently reloads every expert from host memory into one shared full-layer pool and waits for each transfer batch. This change reuses resident expert weights through device-to-device copies, coalesces contiguous physical copies within each source allocation, and prefetches the next layer into a second reusable pool. Load-completion and last-reader events protect both pools. Before decode can update resident slots, pending prefetches are drained; on returning to prefill, pending graph callbacks are fenced once before reading residency. Captured decode graphs therefore do not disable the prefill pipeline. Failed transfers invalidate the affected pool, and failed MoE execution does not launch the next prefetch.

title: [Performance][Model] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 SWA KV cache preparation
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? DeepSeek V4.1 currently prepares SWA KV with three consecutive operators after the WKV projection: RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, and paged-cache scatter. title: [Feature] BigTensorLoader snapshot fast-restore via a shared weight-state kernel
summary: ## What this PR does / why we need it? Two tightly-related pieces: ### 1. `--load-format bigtensorloader`: snapshot fast-restore Restarting a vLLM Ascend instance re-parses safetensors, re-runs `process_weights_after_loading` (quantization repacking, NZ layout conversion, MLA impl construction) and re-allocates final device buffers — a large, repetitive cost for every restart of the same model. title: [Feature][PP] Add standalone activation send buffering on Ascend
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Add opt-in bounded activation-send buffering for fixed-partition pipeline parallelism, implemented entirely in vLLM Ascend using the existing vLLM PP communication interfaces. Each non-last PP worker copies its intermediate tensors into an independent send slot and posts communication on a separate stream. Subsequent forwards can reuse the model output storage while earlier sends remain in flight. A slot is recycled only after its sends complete, and a full ring applies backpressure. The implementation includes the buffer, runtime integration, configuration validation, documentation, and regression tests in the Ascend repository. It requires no model-specific changes or modified vLLM core package. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

title: [Feature] Decoder Append-Prefill for Agentic Scenario Prefiller Offloading
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Agentic workloads often have long inputs—tens of thousands of tokens from user and system prompts—but short outputs, such as tool-call instructions of around a hundred tokens. In P/D-disaggregated serving, this imbalance concentrates pressure on Prefiller instances. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Mooncake PD replays the final prompt token on Decode. title: [bug]:[v0.26][Qwen3.8 Flash-Next] AscendStore misreads 768-token request hashes as 8-token hashes
summary: ### 🐛 Describe the bug The engine resolves `Request.block_hashes` using prefix-participating groups and produces 768-token hashes. AscendStore scheduler/worker independently choose `min(original_block_size)` across all physical groups, including a non-participating 8-token raw ring. Self-rollout training stops the gradient at this cache, and Self Gradient Forcing (SGF) restores it, but applies it to the same weights that generate the current segment. We find that writing and generating are different roles: in a pretrained generator the written KV already differs from the KV used for denoising, and on shared weights the gradient from future reads is negatively aligned with the gradient of generation. title: Hindsight Forcing: Learning Better History from the Future in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
summary: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables real-time streaming generation, with each generated chunk serving as historical context for subsequent generation. To avoid the memory explosion of backpropagation through time, previous self-rollout methods typically truncate cross-chunk gradients or detach historical latents. As a result, earlier denoising computations receive no downstream feedback through the generated history on how to synthesize frames that facilitate subsequent generation, leading to visual drift and structural collapse as rollouts extend. To address this limitation, we propose Hindsight Forcing, which allows historical chunks to learn directly from future outcomes by decoupling forward generation from backward credit assignment via a latent straight-through bridge. title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable
summary: Prior KV cache compression schemes empirically demonstrate that the prompt cache can be dropped or summarised during decoding with little accuracy loss, indicating that it is partly redundant. We ask when and what kind of redundancy, i.e., at which layers, after how many decoding steps, and in what form can the prompt span KV cache be replaced without breaking the task. A controlled splice intervention swept over layers and decoding steps shows this redundancy is about form rather than content. Replacing the upper layer prompt span KV cache with KV cache from a chat template scaffold with empty user content or filler tokens recovers near clean accuracy, while zeroing the entire prompt KV collapses accuracy. title: Do VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) reason about long videos over hundreds to thousands of tokens. Every decoding step re-reads the key-value (KV) cache of the entire video. Must the model keep looking while it reasons? In LookAway, the model first writes timestamped notes on what the question needs and then puts the video away. Once the notes close, the inference engine hides the video's KV cache for the rest of the response. Across both hybrid and pure-attention VLMs, dependence on the video is concentrated early in the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, writing notes preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step. title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
summary: AI coding agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) interleave multi-step LLM inference with tool execution, creating a workload different from chatbots. We present the first production-scale characterization of coding agents using sampled GitHub Copilot traces from June-July 2026, comprising 7.4M users, 819M conversations, 5.7B LLM calls, and 946T tokens. Our analysis reveals distinctive workload properties with unique systems implications: e.g., sparse user-initiated turns unfold into autonomous agent loops with nearly 1:1 coupling between LLM calls and tool execution; parallel LLM calls are rare but exist in turns that trigger subagents; KV cache hit rates average 90% within a turn, but fall to 52% across turn boundaries and to 6% after model switches; workflows and user behavio

title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
summary: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.

title: CarrierKV: An Edge LLM Accelerator with Positional Carrier Decomposition for Low-Bit KV Cache
summary: Long-context decoding on edge devices is limited by DRAM, because every generated token reads the whole, growing KV cache. 4-bit block-scaled formats such as NVFP4 reduce this traffic but degrade accuracy: on Qwen3-4B, NVFP4 lowers 32K RULER (seven tasks) from 92.6 to 79.4, and a Hadamard rotation lowers it further to 57.7. We observe that most of the key energy is a positional carrier, one per-head vector that rotary position embedding (RoPE) rotates with position. In NVFP4, it sets the shared scale of most key blocks and lowers the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio of the content by about 5 dB, nearly one bit, yet it depends only on that vector and the position. title: Aggron: Aggressive Compression of Agentic KV Caches during Head-of-Line Stalls in the Request Queue
summary: LLM agents run long, multi-turn programs whose contexts grow at every step, and serving them is limited by KV cache capacity. To alleviate this limitation, systems use context compression techniques, which typically wait until the KV cache crosses a large threshold and then summarize large spans of history at once, either in the background while the agent progresses or on the critical path. These summarizations can be done using the same model running on the same engine, or using the same or a different model running on extra hardware. When running on the same engine, summarization competes with the requests being served for both compute and memory capacity. title: Approximating Softmax in Pretrained LLMs: Model Sensitivity and Kernel Acceleration
summary: On NVIDIA Blackwell B200, tensor-core throughput outpaces special-function exponential throughput by more than two orders of magnitude, exposing exponential evaluation in fused attention kernels. A pretrained Transformer, however, may not need it evaluated accurately at every element. We characterize what a pretrained model does need by approximating softmax at inference in ten frozen decoder-only models (0.5B-72B). The number of positions the softmax map assigns probability to and within-row resolution can be cut substantially, yet uniform weighting of the same positions is damaging. Where a fixed resolution budget is placed matters as much as its size, with resolution near the row maximum consistently favored. title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. title: Weave: Routing-Adaptive Runtime Warp Scheduling for MoE Megakernels
summary: The Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture is widely used in mainstream large language models. Under expert parallelism (EP), state-of-the-art systems fuse each MoE layer into a persistent megakernel for high performance. By the nature of EP, each GPU's communication and computation volumes vary with the routing result. title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
summary: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
summary: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K < T passes over a deep context cache. title: [Performance][EPLB] Skip unchanged layers in async transfer cycles
summary: ## Summary - Skip async EPLB weight transfers for layers whose physical-to-logical expert mapping is unchanged. - Mark the final changed layer explicitly so a cycle no longer depends on the model's physical last layer. - Publish a no-transfer completion result when every layer is unchanged, preserving the existing cross-rank/main-thread acknowledgement path. Fixes #51791. ## Root cause and impact The async worker previously iterated over every MoE layer after rebalancing. Even when a layer's mapping was unchanged, it still performed the coordinated stop check, entered `transfer_layer()`, synchronized the CUDA stream, published a result, and waited for acknowledgement. Sparse mapping changes therefore cost `O(L)` layer handshakes instead of `O(K)`, where `K` is the number of changed layers.

title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
summary: ## Purpose Fixes #68725. When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. The fix adds a retained tier to `BlockPool`, a second free queue. title: Fix non-deterministic greedy decoding across repeated generate() calls
summary: ## Summary Fixes vllm-project/vllm#61319 cuBLAS may use split-K GEMM algorithms whose partial-result reduction order depends on GPU thread scheduling. title: [Core][Scheduler] Add opt-in aging to cache-aware admission
summary: ## Overview `--cache-aware-admission-window` (#54625) lets waiting requests with a cached prefix go ahead of requests that would have to compute theirs. Nothing limits how often a request can be passed, so an older request with no cached prefix can be bypassed again and again by newer cache-warm requests for as long as they keep arriving. This PR adds the optional `--cache-aware-admission-max-wait-ms`. It defaults to `0` (disabled), which keeps current scheduling behavior. With a positive value, a request in the window that has waited that long can no longer be passed by cached peers, and expired requests are admitted in the order the scheduler received them. Related: #54625 (merged; introduced the window), #53277 (cache-aware waiting QoS). This PR is independent of #66331 (see Details). #

title: [RFC]: Progressive block handoff for NIXL Push
summary: ### Motivation. `NixlPushConnector` currently starts transferring a remote-prefill request's KV cache after the producer finishes the request. title: [ROCm][Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Shard the kpool indexer prefill across TP
summary: ## Overview On ROCm, every TP rank of GLM-5.3-Flash runs the k-pool indexer over the whole prefill. This splits the indexer's tokens across ranks with the existing ShardQ zigzag split, so each rank scores 1/TP of the prompt with balanced causal work, then the ranks all-gather the selected pool ids. Sparse attention stays head-sharded. Pool ids are what makes this cheap. A row selects `index_topk / index_kpool` = 512 pools and expands them to 2051 token ids, so exchanging pools instead of tokens moves a quarter of the data; narrowing them to int16 where they fit moves an eighth. Supersedes #60601, which implemented the same idea on `PrefillRowShard` and `balanced_prefill_row_shard`, which #63956 removed in favour of ShardQ. The pool-id exchange was publicly proposed by @jin-amd in https://g

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] gfx942 large-step MoE for decode steps above the mono limit
summary: ## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under `--monokernel` on gfx942 runs decode steps of up to 42 rows (7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts) in the mono decode layer (#60731, #67540), and larger steps fall back to vLLM's MoE, which reads every routed expert's weights once per pass of rows. This PR runs the MoE block of 43- to 256-row decode steps as a grouped GEMM over groups of 16 picks of one expert (the design of #65421 for gfx950, here in FlyDSL for gfx942), so each expert's weights are read once per 16 picks. The router, the TP all-reduce and every path without `--monokernel` stay as they are. ## Claims - MI325X TP4, AgentX c20: P90 interactivity 79.2 -> 86.9 tok/s/user (+9.6%), and 80.6 -> 87.1 (+8.1%) in a second run on the same node, against `--monokernel` without this PR on the same image.

title: [Perf][Kernel] AWQ: vectorize the output store in dequantize_weights
summary: ## Overview The CUDA `awq_dequantize` kernel ([`dequantize_weights`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e2b672312328d3f95980f5b82869f7937194fd62/csrc/quantization/awq/gemm_kernels.cu#L352-L409)) wrote each thread's 8 dequantized halves as 8 scalar 2-byte stores. title: [Bugfix][Core] Budget the GPU memory held by prompt embeddings
summary: ## Overview Workers copy each request's `prompt_embeds` to the GPU when it is added and kept them until it finished. Memory profiling never counted these tensors, so they came out of the headroom after the KV cache and grew with every running long-prompt request, unbudgeted and unbounded in concurrency. >[!IMPORTANT] Long multi-turn `prompt_embeds` traffic at high concurrency could run the GPU out of memory. title: [Bugfix][DeepEPv2] Fix ElasticBuffer over-allocated by sp_size× under sequence parallelism
summary: ## Overview With sequence parallelism (TP>1, DP>1, EP), each EP rank only dispatches a `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, sp_size)` shard. It also caps the per-step dispatch bound at the buffer capacity. Follows #57210, which bounded the dispatch by `sp_size` but left the buffer sizing unchanged. Related: #57440. ## Claims - Frees **~2.7 GiB per GPU** (ElasticBuffer 3.56 → 0.89 GiB) for KV cache on Kimi-K3 TP4×DP4×EP16 (B200). The saving is `(1 − 1/sp_size)` of the buffer and grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`. - Fixes a latent overflow. title: [ROCm][Kernel] Tune the GatedDeltaNet Triton prefill kernels on gfx942
summary: ## Purpose The Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill walks each sequence's chunks in order, so the kernel grid and the MFMA tile shape are all that decide how much of the GPU its five Triton kernels fill. title: [Perf][DiffusionGemma] Canvas packing + canvas swap: up to 10x lower short-request latency under load
summary: ## Overview Every DiffusionGemma request gets the full served canvas (256 tokens, about two paragraphs). Each denoising step computes and budgets all 256 positions, whether the reply is 14 tokens or 250, so under load short replies queue behind work that is mostly padding. When the scheduler preempts a request mid-block, the half-denoised canvas is discarded and the block restarts from noise. This PR adds two opt-in mechanisms to the MRV2 runner. Both are off by default. - **Canvas packing** (`VLLM_DIFFUSION_PACK_SPANS`): two requests share one canvas. A per-sequence span mask in Triton unified attention keeps each request's queries off the other's keys. title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS storage rank derivation with pipeline parallelism
summary: ## Overview `HF3FSKVConnector` uses the TP rank alone as its storage rank. With pipeline parallelism, workers of different stages that share a TP rank write the same data file (`hf3fs_vllm_data_file_<rank>`) and register as the same metadata rank, although they hold different layers. KV loaded back from HF3FS then contains another stage's layers and the outputs are garbage. title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1/K2 for every compress ratio at TP2
summary: ## Overview DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode (`--monokernel`, gfx950, TP2) takes #63027's tuned K1/K2 only on the compress-ratio-2 layers, although none of the tuned paths reads the ratio, so the two window-only layers and the twenty ratio-1 layers (22 of 40) still run the generic code. This PR drops the ratio condition from `MonoBuild.tuned`, so every target layer at TP2 takes the tuned builds. The FFN launch is built with ratio 0 on the generic scratch layout and relied on that condition to stay generic; a new `MonoBuild.ffn` field keeps it generic. **Result vs main:** the ratio-0/1 layers are 7.6-11.8% faster at 6-48 rows with bit-identical outputs. On the recipe's TP2 serving points, total throughput is up 4.2-5.8% at concurrency 1, 4.6% at 8 and 2.5% at 32, unchanged at 64 and at TP4.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] DSpark: run the Markov walk in one kernel with int8 W2 on chip (Hopper)
summary: ## Overview DSpark walks its draft block left to right: each step adds `W2 @ W1[prev]` to the base logits (W2 is V x 256) and then takes the argmax or a sample. Today every draft token is a full-vocab GEMV, an add and a sampler, and W2 (78 MB in bf16 at V = 151936) is read from HBM again on every step. This adds `dspark_markov_quantization="int8"` to the speculative config. With it, sm_90 runs the whole walk in one cooperative kernel. W2 is quantized to int8 with one fp32 scale per row, most of it stays in shared memory across all SMs and the rest streams from L2, and the per-step argmax across CTAs goes through one atomic {key, count} pair. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Check pointer alignment before vectorizing activation kernels
summary: ## Overview The activation launchers in `csrc/activation_kernels.cu` (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`, `fatrelu_and_mul`, `gelu_fast`, ...) pick the 128/256-bit vector path from the row width alone. A contiguous input or output whose data pointer is not vector-aligned, such as a view at an odd storage offset, passes that check and then fails with `CUDA error: misaligned address`, which leaves the CUDA context unusable. This PR also checks both data pointers and falls back to the existing scalar path when either is unaligned. ## Claims - Inputs or outputs at an unaligned storage offset now produce correct results instead of a sticky CUDA error, for all ops built on the three launch macros. - Aligned tensors take the same vector path as before: on Qwen3-8B, GSM8K scores m

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Ignore KV cache dtype for encoder-only backend selection
summary: ## Purpose Fix embedding / encoder-only serving when a global `--kv-cache-dtype` is set (e.g. `bfloat16`). `EncoderOnlyAttention` does not allocate a KV cache (`get_kv_cache_spec` returns `None`), but it still passed `cache_config.cache_dtype` into `get_attn_backend()`. title: [Kernel][Perf] Do not split rows no longer than k in `top_k_per_row_decode`
summary: ## Overview When the logits are at least 200,000 wide, `top_k_per_row_decode` spends about 120 µs on a decode row no longer than k, although the result is just the row's own indices.
