title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Fold the consumer remap into top-512
summary: ## Overview On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 sparse indexer has 4 candidate-consumer index layers (24/28/32/36). Each picks the top-512 from the candidate pool's compact scores, then a second Triton launch, `_remap_compact_topk`, maps each picked pool slot to its context position. This PR adds a ROCm op, `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode_remap`: the existing gfx950 top-512 kernel with an index map in its final store, so it writes the context positions directly. The consumers use it when k = 512 and the step has fewer than 128 decode rows (a prefill launch goes by its own rows), which removes 4 launches per decode step. It also skips the `-1` fill on all decode rows, whichever top-k kernel runs. #63888 skipped it only where vLLM's top-k runs (fewer than 128 decode rows in the step, k < 204

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Keep few-row gfx950 top-512 calls in one block up to 36K
summary: ## Overview On gfx950 (MI355X), `top_k_per_row_decode` with topK = 512 and at most 32 rows splits every row longer than 16K positions into 8 blocks (more above 128K) and merges their candidates in a second kernel. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode at low concurrency takes this path on every step: DSpark k=6 gives 7 rows per request, and indexer layers 2/8/14/20 each make one full-width top-512 call per step (rows of about half the context for layers 2/8/14, the full context for layer 20). For rows of up to about 36K, the split plus merge is slower than one block. This PR keeps rows of 16K-36K in one block when no row of the call is longer than 36K. A call with any longer row splits exactly as on main. - **Device:** the split kernel and the merge kernel make the same decision from the same inputs.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Fold the decode RoPE + KV-cache write into the AITER fused decode query
summary: ## Overview On ROCm with AITER MLA and an fp8 KV cache, each MLA decode layer runs `concat_and_cache_mla_rope_fused` (RoPE of q_pe/k_pe + the fp8 KV-cache write) before the fused decode query kernel from #64560. This PR moves that work into the same kernel: on pure-decode steps, `forward_impl` calls AITER's `fused_bf16_bmm_rope_cat_quant_pad_cache_mla` (ROCm/aiter#7458) instead of `fused_bf16_bmm_cat_quant_pad_mla`, and the RoPE + KV-cache op skips its HIP launch. Depends on ROCm/aiter#7458; without it, the tuned-config check returns false and the #64560 path runs unchanged. ## Claims - Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, against #64560: output throughput **+0.8% to +2.6%**, mean TPOT **−0.8% to −2.6%** across 1k/1k (concurrency 16/64/128) and 1k/8k (concurrency 64). - Decode step with 64 tokens

title: [Perf][Gemma4] Run attention and FFN only for logit rows in the last KV-producing layer
summary: ## Overview Under `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill`, Gemma 4 still runs its last KV-producing layer in full for every prompt token, although prompt tokens only need that layer's K/V. title: [RL] Deliver routed experts through shared objects under namespaces
summary: ## Summary RL rollouts with long multi-turn trajectories return routed experts (R3) for every position, and turns and GRPO samples recompute or re-send the same prefix rows again and again. Object delivery works with the default configuration on full-attention, sliding-window hybrid, Mamba/linear-attention hybrid and loop models, with speculative decoding and with an external KV tier (support matrix below). title: [Perf][UMBP] Ask the other ranks only about objects the first rank holds
summary: ## Overview A hash-granular UMBP lookup asks every rank about its own copy of every probed object, although callers only use whether all ranks hold an object and most probed positions hold nothing. On an 8-rank Kimi K3 deployment a long prompt sends tens of thousands of keys per lookup, and in embedded mode the scheduler asks the ranks' lookup sockets one after another, so a synchronous lookup blocks scheduling for the sum. Ask the first rank about every object, then the other ranks only about the objects it holds. Keep each object's own key count, since a TP-replicated group stores one key per object where the other groups store one per rank. title: [RFC]: Pluggable KV cache eviction policy for hybrid models
summary: ### Motivation. A hybrid prefix hit at position P needs every KV cache group to resume at P: full attention (FA) needs blocks `[0, P)`, sliding window (SWA) needs the window ending at P, Mamba/GDN needs the state at P. vLLM never evicts with that unit in mind. Eviction is decided implicitly by the order blocks enter one shared LRU free queue, so every fix for hybrid hit rate today is another hard-coded reordering of that queue. Open work that tries to fix this one order at a time: - #48435: Gemma-4 (SWA hybrid) prefix reuse collapsed to zero at about 25% pool occupancy. It was closed by retention (#43447, default 0 on main since #52216), which decides *which* SWA blocks keep a hash. summary: ## Overview `FullAttentionManager.find_longest_cache_hit` calls `BlockPool.get_cached_block` once per prompt block until the first miss. title: [RL][Weight Transfer] Add sparse_disk backend for sparse deltas through storage
summary: ## Overview Adds `sparse_disk`, a weight transfer backend for sparse weight deltas published through storage, for trainers that cannot share an NCCL group with inference or that feed many replicas. The trainer publishes each version's patches as one file. Every inference worker keeps its part of the checkpoint in host memory, laid out as its load plan writes it. In an update, the worker applies the new files to that copy and copies its whole part into the model, so every update is a full direct reload through the load plan, with post-load processing rerun. ## Claims - Sparse updates without an NCCL group between trainer and inference; every replica reads the same patch files. - No new loading pattern: each update runs `start_reload`, writes every tensor through the load plan's destinations

title: [Security] Add hash collision defense for prefix cache with non-crypto hashes
summary: When using non-cryptographic hash algorithms (xxhash/xxhash_cbor) for prefix caching, hash collisions can cause cache poisoning where a request receives incorrect KV cache data from an unrelated prompt. Add insertion-time content verification that stores a token fingerprint alongside each cached block and rejects colliding insertions with a warning. The defense is automatically enabled when the configured hash algorithm is xxhash or xxhash_cbor, with zero overhead on the default sha256 path.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Default fill-in DSpark drafts to block_size - 1 tokens
summary: ## Overview When `num_speculative_tokens` is not set, vLLM takes it from the DSpark checkpoint's `block_size`. title: [Security] Keep live MoRIIO transfer IDs bound to the first owner
summary: ## Summary MoRIIO stored `transfer_id` → `request_id` with last-write-wins semantics. If two overlapping requests presented the same `transfer_id`, the later request stole the mapping, so the first request's completion was reported as `finished_sending` for the later request and the scheduler freed that request's live KV blocks. title: [Security] Hold MoRIIO deferred-send blocks until a finished_sending ACK
summary: ## Summary In MoRIIO READ (and other delay-free) producer mode, `update_connector_output` treated a missing `finished_sending` ACK as permission to free KV blocks after `defer_timeout`. The scheduler then returned those blocks to the pool while a consumer READ could still reference them, so a later request could reuse the same physical blocks. This change keeps the blocks allocated until a real ACK arrives. Timed-out consumer reads now send the same release notify as a failed transfer so the producer can still free after the consumer has abandoned the read. A lost ACK path is fail-closed on purpose: deferred entries and transfer-id mappings stay until a real ACK, so a late ACK can still free and the scheduler never returns those blocks to the pool. title: [RFC]: Replicate selected blocks across TP ranks for tensor parallelism over slow inter-node links
summary: ### Motivation Tensor parallelism across nodes linked by commodity Ethernet (25 GbE RoCE between workstations or DGX Spark-class boxes) pays one all-reduce per block per step. At decode batch sizes that all-reduce is latency-bound: we measured about 66 us for TP4 and 36-40 us for TP2 over 25 GbE at batch 1 (inside a CUDA graph), against 2-3 us on one PCIe node. That is the same order as reading a mixer's weights from HBM, so for some blocks it is cheaper to keep the block whole on every rank (replicate it) and skip its all-reduce than to shard it. Replicating a block costs each rank (1 - 1/TP) x W extra bytes of resident weights and of reads per step, and saves one all-reduce. title: [Perf][PCP] Give short prefills whole to one rank
summary: ## Purpose Under prefill context parallel without DCP, a prefill is cut into `2 * pcp_world_size` chunks, and every rank attends its two chunks against the rest of the request as context. A 1k-token prompt at PCP 8 becomes 16 chunks of 64 tokens, each attended against up to 960 context tokens that the rank gathers from the cache, projects to K/V and concatenates, every layer. For short prompts that context pass costs more than the attention. New option `--pcp-whole-prefill-max-tokens N` (default 0 = off): prefills of at most N scheduled tokens are handed out whole, one per rank at a time and longest first, so every rank gets the same number and none needs a context pass. title: [Fix] attention: Keep shared-KV verify split partials in FP32
summary: ## Motivation The shared-KV verify kernel in `verify_mla.py` stores each split's partial output (`Att_Out`) in BF16 and merges the splits afterwards. When the splits cancel each other out, the true result is a small residual, and the rounding before the merge can be as large as that residual. Minimal repro: uniform attention over a prefix whose V values sum to 1.75, so the exact output is 1.75/n. At head_dim 256 the kernel returns 0. With real Gemma-4 Q/K/V I get 0.0530 where the FP64 reference is 0.0763. The per-head split-KV verify kernel and Triton's split-KV decode both keep their partials in FP32. This PR does the same here. ## Changes - `Att_Out` scratch is FP32. Q/K/V, output and LSE dtypes are unchanged, as are dispatch and tiling. - New regression test in `test_verify_shared_kv.py

title: [Perf] kv-shard: Free sharded KV pages without a host sync

title: [Fix] diffusion: keep TP/Ulysses head shards on the unsharded torch SDPA kernel
summary: ## Motivation PyTorch's flash SDPA forward picks split-KV when `batch * heads * ceil(query_len / 128)` is below 80% of the SM count (`num_splits_heuristic` in ATen's `flash_api.cpp`). Split-KV reorders the softmax sums. Tensor parallelism and Ulysses both reduce the number of heads each rank attends over. At short sequence lengths, that can push a head shard onto the split kernel while the unsharded layer stays unsplit. The result is that `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` runs differ between parallel and single-GPU execution even at the attention-operator level. The default backends do not depend on the head count, and are unaffected: - sm100: cuDNN SDPA. Measured on B200: head shards are bit-identical. - sm90: sgl FA3, which runs with `num_splits=1`. summary: ## Motivation `HummingRunnerCore.prepare_buffers` runs on every Humming MoE forward. It calls `get_buffer_metas` twice: once inside `_workspace_shapes` to size the two workspaces, then again to slice them. It also applies `view(dtype)` and `[:numel]` to every buffer, even when the dtype already matches the workspace and the buffer covers the whole workspace. This is host-only work. When the forward runs eagerly (CUDA graph disabled, batches outside the captured sizes, or the eager pieces of a piecewise graph), it adds up across MoE layers. Each decode step of Qwen3-30B-A3B, for example, runs 48 MoE layers. ## Modifications - Compute the buffer metas once and derive the workspace sizes and the per-buffer layout in a single pass. title: [Fix] marlin: keep one block per SM in the MoE kernel
summary: Fixes #44999. ## Motivation `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` intermittently returns wrong rows on pre-Hopper GPUs. Reported by #44999 on sm86; reproduced here on sm89 (RTX 4090) with synthetic AWQ W4A16 MoE weights (E=128, K=2048, N=768, group 128, topk 8): 4-6% of probe launches differ from the majority output, 3-4 of 64 tokens are wrong (|delta| up to 5.0) and every other row is bit-identical. The Triton WNA16 path is exact, which is how the report distinguishes it from a numerics issue. `determine_exec_config()` sizes the launch by an occupancy estimate (`allow_count`), so the kernel can run two or three blocks per SM. The split-K reduction chains those blocks through a global lock array (`barrier_acquire`/`barrier_release`), and that chain is only correct with a single resident block per SM. ##

title: [Fix] scheduler: Publish Mamba prefill cache updates before preparing the next batch
summary: ## Motivation With Mamba `extra_buffer` caching and overlap scheduling, the next decode/verify batch can capture `req_to_token` before the previous prefill result publishes its cache insertion. title: [Feature] Incremental chat-prompt processing: stop re-tokenizing the whole history on every turn
summary: ## Problem A multi-turn chat request re-sends the entire conversation. On every turn `OpenAIServingChat` re-renders the chat template over all messages and re-encodes the full rendered prompt, on the TokenizerManager's event loop, before the request reaches the scheduler. Prefix caching already makes the *prefill* of the repeated history nearly free, but this CPU work still grows with every turn and becomes the part of time to first token that grows with history. summary: ## Motivation Muse Spark NVFP4 checkpoints currently only run with EP equal to TP (TP4/EP4, TP8/EP8); `--ep-size 1` is rejected. summary: ## Summary We would like to discuss how SGLang should serve large MoE models efficiently when their full expert working set, KV cache, and runtime allocations are close to, or exceed, the HBM capacity of a multi-GPU deployment. Each group stores one 8-bit index into a 256-entry codebook, equivalent to two payload bits per component. Values are rotated and quantized to four scalar levels, packed as INT2. title: [Feature] Multistream overlap of SFA indexer q projection with pre-processing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? In the SFA attention decode forward, the indexer pre-processing is made of two independent strands that are currently issued back-to-back on the current stream: - **k strand**: `wk_weights_proj` (AIC) → k norm + RoPE (AIV) → k c8 quant (AIV) - **q strand**: `quantize(q_c)` (AIV) → `wq_b` quant matmul (AIC) Both strands have a cube phase and a vector phase, but they are executed serially, so each engine idles while the other one works. The q strand is therefore fully exposed on the critical path even though it is independent of the k strand and could run concurrently. title: [Performance][Attention] Reduce strided MLA cache slot indexing
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Strided MLA history reads currently build per-token request IDs and use advanced indexing to construct cache slots. For one to eight requests, this proposal constructs slots on device; one- and two-request batches reuse a physical page lookup across each page. Other shapes and unsupported metadata retain the current PyTorch path, and the existing KV copy is unchanged. The wrapper checks request lengths and first/last page indices with PyTorch indexing, then consumes the checked page values in the Triton kernels. This keeps checks on device, preserves negative indexing for valid metadata, and avoids silently treating an invalid page as a padded slot. Empty requests, strided metadata, integer overflow and graph replay are covered by tests. Related: #19

title: [BugFix] Avoid reserving DSpark draft slots in the recompute scheduler
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? When paired with older vLLM versions, `RecomputeScheduler` reserves `K - 1` additional input slots per DSpark request. DSpark drafts in a separate forward pass, so these slots unnecessarily consume the target batch's token budget. With seven speculative tokens, an eight-token decode step consumes 14 budget slots, preventing a batch of 32 such requests from fitting within `max_num_batched_tokens=400`. Use zero additional target-input slots for DSpark, matching current vLLM behavior, while preserving the upstream reservation for other drafting methods. The change applies to both running requests and waiting-request admission, including the async scheduler. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Yes. title: [Performance][GDN] Overlap Qwen input projections on Ascend

title: [Performance] Publish A3 FSA KV plans via shared DDR and Notify
summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Fused sparse attention with KV offload shares a plan across tensor-parallel ranks. On Ascend A3, the device planner calculates the plan from the runtime geometry. In `notify` mode, TP0 writes it to shared host DDR and signals READY. Each peer publishes it to its local FSA buffers and signals ACK before TP0 can reuse the shared payload. The change integrates planning with V2 target and draft graph capture, replay, and retirement. It reserves each rank's persistent planner HBM before sizing the KV cache. Single-token graphs captured without speculation skip the per-reuse-layer KV writeback broadcast. summary: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The int8 quantized all-reduce added in #19000 is gated by a payload threshold, `min_numel`, and ships with a single default of `16777216` elements (32 MiB of bf16 payload). title: PISA: Piecewise Sparse Attention Is Wiser for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
summary: Diffusion Transformers are fundamental for visual generation, but their efficiency is bottlenecked by the quadratic complexity of self-attention. title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
summary: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by the memory demands of the key-value (KV) cache, whose size scales linearly with context length. title: On-Policy Codec Distillation for Efficient All-in-One Video Generation
summary: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely new is exactly the problem that classical video codecs have long solved. Thus, we first introduce a codec-based token pruning method that discards redundant tokens. title: Time Series Foundation Models on the Edge
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast zero-shot with accuracy exceeding that of task-specific models, and the smaller ones fit on edge devices. title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
summary: We introduce TiRex-2, a recurrent xLSTM-based time series foundation model that generalizes the univariate TiRex to multivariate forecasting with both past and future covariates. summary: Modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) benefit from chain-of-thought prompting and test-time scaling, but these gains often come with prohibitive inference cost due to large visual contexts and long decoding chains. Existing methods typically optimize one axis at a time, leaving the joint allocation of compute across these axes underexplored. summary: Autoregressive video generators produce videos block by block from historical context. title: Cascade: Exploiting SLO-Aware latency budget for fair and high goodput LLM inference serving
summary: The reasoning and agentic capabilities of LLMs have expanded the range of applications they support, from short interactive exchanges to long, prefix-heavy requests. This headroom must cover not only execution, but also scheduling and preemption delays and the cost of retrieving KV state from deeper memory tiers. title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
summary: KV cache compression is essential for efficient long-context inference. title: Language Models Act on Hidden Valence
summary: Language models describe some internal states as good and others as bad. But whether models have a stake in them is an open question. Simply asking models is unlikely to be informative. title: Gossamer: A Utility-Driven Architecture for Constant-Budget KV Cache Compression in Reasoning LLMs
summary: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to complex reasoning tasks, yet their inference efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the rapid growth of the KV cache. As reasoning contexts extend to hundreds of thousands of tokens, the key-value (KV) cache becomes the dominant contributor to both memory footprint and bandwidth demand, tightly coupling computation with memory utilization and thereby limiting scalability. Existing compression methods, such as quantization and eviction, alleviate capacity pressure but remain purely algorithmic, often introducing additional passes and compute overhead that reduce system efficiency. This paper presents Gossamer, a KV cache compression architecture for reasoning LLMs that bridges the algorithm--system--hardware gap.

title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair

title: RES: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models with Rolling Entropy Sampling
summary: A diffusion language sampler makes two choices for every position in its denoising window: where the next token comes from, and when the position is committed to the KV cache. title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent

summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. title: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect - KV Cache Management for AI Agents
summary: LLM agents alternate between inference and tool execution, repeatedly reusing their growing context across calls.
